body.text:
sphuṭārthā
abhidharmakośavyākhyā
body.translated_text:
<s>Sphuṭārthā</s> (Clear Meaning)
Commentary on the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>

body.text: I
body.translated_text: I

body.text: (dhātunirdeśo nāma prathamaṃ kośasthānam)
body.translated_text: (The chapter on elements (<s>dhātu-nirdeśa</s>), the first section of the <s>Kośa</s>)

body.text: Tib. 1b
body.translated_text: Tib. 1b

body.text: namo mārabalapramathanāya.
body.translated_text: Homage to the Crusher of <s>Māra</s>'s forces.

children.translated_text: He who, of great power, tamed by wisdom and <s>samādhi</s>,
having torn apart the cage made of birth,
to that supreme elephant among teachers, I bow my head.
He who, performing the work of the teacher of ultimate truth, as if performing the teacher's work in the world —

children.text: yaṃ buddhimatām agryaṃ dvitīyam iva buddham ity āhuḥ. ||
children.translated_text: whom the wise call the foremost, like a second <s>Buddha</s>.
By him, named <s>Vasubandhu</s>, who will be the ultimate kinsman of the world,
this guide to the <s>Abhidharma</s> was composed, called the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>.
For this jewel of a treatise, drawn from the ocean of the <s>Abhidharma-bhāṣya</s>,
this commentary has been made by me, rightly named <s>Sphuṭārthā</s> (Clear Meaning).
The explanation of word-meanings that was well-accomplished by commentators such as <s>Guṇamati</s>, <s>Vasumitra</s>, and others —

children.text: sukṛtā [Tib. 2a] sābhimatā me likhitā ca tathāyam artha iti. ||
children.translated_text: [Tib. 2a] that is approved by me, and this meaning has been written accordingly.

children.text: siddhāntārthāpasṛtā kvacitkvacid yā tu taiḥ kṛtā vyākhyā |
children.translated_text: But wherever commentary that departs from the intended meaning of the established doctrine was made by them —

children.text: tām udbhāvya yathāvad vihiteha mayānyathā vyākhyā. ||
children.translated_text: that having been brought to light, a different commentary has been made here by me, as is proper.
Those who have labored in the <s>Abhidharma-vibhāṣā</s> and in the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s> —

children.text: pravicāryatām iyaṃ tair vyākhyā yuktā na vā yuktā. ||
children.translated_text: let this commentary be examined by them, [to determine] whether it is correct or not.

children.text: yuktā ced grāhyeyaṃ na eed apohyānyathā vidhātavyā |
children.translated_text: If correct, let this be accepted; if not, let it be rejected and [the matter] be arranged otherwise.

children.text: na hi viṣame 'rthe skhalituṃ na saṃbhaven mādṛśāṃ buddhiḥ. ||
children.translated_text: For it is not impossible that the intellect of those like me should stumble on a difficult topic.

children.text:
yaḥ sarvathā sarvahatāndhakāraḥ
saṃsārapaṃkāj jagad ujjahāra
tasmai namaskṛtya yathārthaśāstre
śāstraṃ pravakṣyāmy abhidharmakośam.
children.translated_text:
He who has completely destroyed all darkness in every way,
who lifted the world from the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s> —
having bowed to that teacher of truth,
I shall expound the treatise, the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>.

body.text: ity asya ślokasyārthaṃ vivṛṇvāna ācārya āha. śātraṃ praṇetukāmaḥ svasya
body.translated_text: Explaining the meaning of this verse, the <s>Ācārya</s> (<s>Vasubandhu</s>) said: Wishing to compose the treatise, he began with a salutation preceded by a declaration of his own

body.text:
śāstur māhātmyajñāpanārthaṃ guṇākhyānapūrvakaṃ tasmai namaskāram ārabhata iti. śāstram abhidharmakośaṃ praṇetukāmaḥ kartukāmaḥ svasya ṣāstur ātmīyasya śāstuḥ. sa hi bhagavān ācāryasyātmīyaḥ śāstā. tacchāsanapratipannatvāt. [Tib. 2b] tena vā śāstrā mahākaruṇāparatantreṇa sakalo lokaḥ svatvena parigṛhītaḥ. tasmād ācāryasyāpi svatvena gṛhītasya sa bhagavān svaḥ śāstā bhavati. māhātmyajñāpanārtham iti. mahātmatvaṃ māhātmyaṃ svaparārthapratipattisampat tajjñāpanārthaṃ tadavabodhārtham. guṇākhyānapūrvakaṃ guṇakathanapūrvakaṃ tasmai namaskāram ārabhate tasmai praṇāmaṃ
karotīty arthaḥ. atītakālatvād ārabdhavān iti vaktavye vartamānakāle padaprayogo 'dyāpi namaskārārambhābhiprāyāt. śiṣyaparaṃparayā vā namaskārāraṃbhāvirāmāt. śabdaśāstre 'pīdṛśa eva śabdaprayogo dṛśyate. atha śabdānuśāsanam. athety ayaṃ śabdo 'dhikārārthaḥ prayujyata iti. guṇākhyānamātreṇa māhātmyāvabodho na namaskāreṇeti cet. na. tasya tatsūcakatvāt. namaskāreṇa hi māhātmyaṃ sūcyate. atha vā guṇākhyānenaiva māhātmyaṃ jñāpyate na namaskāreṇa. namaskārārambhas tu svapuṇyaprasavārtham. sadācāranuvṛttipradarśanārthaṃ vā. kṛtābhimatadevatāpūjāstutinamaskārā hi santaḥ kriyām ārabhanta iti satām ācārāt. tatra māhātmyajñāpanaṃ kimartham ity ācakṣmahe. tadgauravotpādanārtham. gauravotpādanaṃ punas tatpravacanasatkṛtyaśravaṇārtham. satkṛtyaśravaṇaṃ krameṇa śrutacintābhāvanāmayaprajñotpādanārtham. tadutpād
anaṃ kleśaprahāṇārtham. tat punaḥ sarvaduḥkhopaśamalakṣaṇanirvāṇaprāpaṇārtham [Tib. 3a] iti prayojananiṣṭhā. māhātmyajñāpanaṃ tv ekam ācāryeṇa prayojanam uktaṃ sākṣātprayojanatvāt. taditarāṇi tv abhyūhituṃ śakyānīti noktāni. ya iti buddhaṃ bhagavaṃtam adhikṛtyāheti. sāmānyaśabdo 'pi yacchabdo vihitaviśeṣaṇatvāt viśeṣavṛttir bhavati. tadyathā ya eṣāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ gauraḥ śukravāsāḥ sa evaśarmeti. tadvad ihāpi.
body.translated_text: teacher's greatness. [That is:] Wishing to compose the treatise — the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s> — that is, wishing to create it, for the purpose of making known the greatness of his own teacher — 'his own teacher' meaning the teacher who belongs to him personally. For the Blessed One is indeed the <s>Ācārya</s>'s own teacher, because he follows His teaching. [Tib. 2b] Or, because the Teacher, who is impelled by great compassion, has embraced the entire world as his own, therefore too the Blessed One is the personal teacher of the <s>Ācārya</s>, who has been embraced as his own. 'For the purpose of making known the greatness' means: greatness (<s>māhātmya</s>) is the excellence of accomplishment for one's own and others' benefit; 'making known' means 'for the purpose of understanding that.' 'Preceded by a declaration of qualities' means preceded by a recounting of virtues — he begins a salutation to him, meaning he makes a prostration to him. Although the past tense should be used since it is a past action — 'he began' — the present tense is employed because the intention is that the commencement of salutation [continues] even now; or because, through the succession of disciples, the commencement of salutation never ceases. In the science of grammar too, just such a usage of words is seen: 'Now, the teaching of words (<s>śabdānuśāsana</s>)' — where 'now' (<s>atha</s>) is used in the sense of a topic-introduction. [Objection:] Greatness is understood merely through the declaration of qualities, not through salutation. [Reply:] No, because [salutation] is indicative of that. For greatness is indicated by salutation. Alternatively, greatness is indeed made known by the declaration of qualities alone, not by salutation. The commencement of salutation, however, is for the purpose of generating one's own merit, or for the purpose of demonstrating conformity to good conduct. For the virtuous, having performed worship, praise, and salutation to their chosen deity, then commence an activity — [this is] from the conduct of the virtuous. Now, what is the purpose of making known the greatness? We explain: For the purpose of generating reverence toward him. And the generation of reverence is for the purpose of respectfully listening to his proclamation. Respectful listening is for the purpose of gradually generating wisdom born of hearing, reflection, and meditation. The generation of that is for the purpose of abandoning the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>). And that, in turn, is for the purpose of attaining <s>nirvāṇa</s>, characterized by the pacification of all suffering [Tib. 3a] — this is the ultimate purpose. The <s>Ācārya</s> stated only one purpose — 'making known the greatness' — because it is the direct purpose; the others can be inferred, so they were not stated. 'Who' (<s>yaḥ</s>) — this is said with reference to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One. The word 'who' (<s>yat</s>), though a general term, functions with specific reference because [specific] qualifiers have been provided. Just as [in the expression] 'whichever of these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> is fair and wears white garments, he is Evaśarman.' So too here.

children.text:
yaḥ sarvathā sarvahatāndhakāraḥ
saṃsārapaṅkāj jagad ujjahāra
tasmai namaskṛtyeti
children.translated_text:
'Who has completely destroyed all darkness in every way,
who lifted the world from the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s> —
having bowed to that one' —

body.text: buddha eva bhagavati yacchabdo vartate. na hi buddhād anya evaṃ guṇaviśiṣṭaḥ saṃbhavatīti ato vyācaṣṭe. ya iti buddhaṃ bhagavantam adhikṛtyāheti. buddha iti kartari ktavidhānaṃ. buddher vikasanād buddhaḥ. vibuddha ity arthaḥ. vibuddhaṃ padmam iti yathā. atha yāvidyānidrādvayāpagamād buddhaḥ prabuddha ity arthaḥ. prabuddhapuruṣa iti yathā. karmakartari ktavidhānam
body.translated_text: The word 'who' refers to the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> alone. For no one other than the <s>Buddha</s> could possess such distinguished qualities. Therefore he explains: 'Who' is said with reference to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One. '<s>Buddha</s>' — the <s>kta</s> suffix is in the agent sense (<s>kartari</s>). <s>Buddha</s> means 'awakened' because of the blossoming of intelligence — it means 'fully opened,' as [one says] 'a fully opened lotus.' Or, <s>Buddha</s> means 'awakened' because of the departure of the twofold sleep of ignorance — it means 'one who has awakened,' as [one says] 'an awakened person.' Others say the <s>kta</s> suffix is in the agent-object sense (<s>karmakartari</s>).

body.text: ity apare. svayaṃ budhyata iti buddha ity arthaḥ. karmaṇy api ktavidhānam apy adoṣaṃ paśyāmaḥ. sarvaguṇasaṃpatsaṃpannatayā sarvadoṣavinirmuktatayā ca buddhair anyair vā buddho jñāta ity arthaḥ. bhagavantam iti dvitīyapadopādānam anādarasaṃbhāvanānivṛttyarthaṃ. nirupapadānām abhidhānānāṃ hi loke anādaro dṛśyate. evadatta iti. vinayavibhāṣākārās tu catuṣkoṭikāṃ kurvanti. asti buddho na bhagavān. pratyekabuddhaḥ svayaṃbhutvād buddha iti śakyate vaktum. na tu bhagavān. aparipūrṇadānādisaṃbhāratvāt. yo hi māhātmyavān sa bhagavān ucyate. asti bhagavān na buddhaḥ. caramabhaviko bodhisattvaḥ paripūrṇadānādipāramitatvāt [Tib. 3b] anabhisaṃbuddhatvāc ca. asty ubhayathā buddho bhagavān. asti nobhayathā etān ākārān sthāpayitveti. ato buddhaṃ bhagavantam ity ubhayaviśeṣaṇam. hatam asyāndhakāram anena veti hatāndhakāraḥ. ṣaṣṭhībahuvrīhau mārgeṇa hatam iti kartṛbhūto mārgo adhyāhāryaḥ. tṛtīyābahuvrīhau tu mārgeṇeti karaṇam adhyāhāryam. apara āha. vigrahadvayapradarśanaṃ hana hiṃsāgatyor iti hantyarthadvayaparigrahārtham. yadā hatam asyāndhakāram iti vigraham. tadā gatyartho hantir gṛhyate. gatam asyāndhakāram ity arthaḥ. yadā punas tṛtīyābahuvrīhiḥ. tadā hiṃsārtho hantir gṛhyate. hiṃsitam anenāndhakāram ity arthaḥ. evam uttarayoḥ padayor aikapadyaṃ kṛtvā paścāt saptamītatpuruṣaṃ karoti. sarvasmin hatāndhakāraḥ sarvahatāndhakāra iti. tathā ca sati hataśabdo 'tra na pūrvaṃ nipatati. saptamīsamāsas tv iha kena lakṣaṇena bhavatīti cintyam. saptamī śauṇḍair iti samāsaḥ. hatāndhakāraśabdaḥ śauṇdādiṣu paṭhyate. śauṇḍādīnām ākṛtīkṛtatvāt tatrāsyānupraveśo 'vagantavyaḥ. saptamīti yogavibhāgād vā. utsargeṇa vā samāsaḥ. saha supeti sub iti vartamāne subantaṃ subantena saha samasyate. yatreṣṭam iti akṛtalakṣaṇo vā tatpuruṣo mayūravyaṃsakādiṣu draṣṭavya ity anena vā katham upasarjanībhūtam andhakāraṃ sarvasminn ity anenabhisaṃbadhyate. satyaṃ nāndhakāram anenabhisaṃbadhyate. andhakāraghātas tv anenābhisaṃbadhyate. yena hy andhakāraghātena yogād bhagavān hatāndhakāraḥ. sa tasyāndhakāraghātaḥ sarvādhāro 'vagantavyaḥ. yathā akṣeṣu dhūrta iti. yena dhaurtyalakṣaṇena guṇena yogāt. asau dhūrtaḥ so 'kṣādhāraḥ. evam ihāpy avagantavyam. anyathāpi ceha saṃbhavantaṃ samāsaṃ paśyāmaḥ. sarvasmin hataṃ sarvahatam. sarveṇa prakāreṇa sarvahataṃ sarvathā sarvahatam. sarvathā sarvahatam asyāndhakāram anena veti sarvathā sarvahatāndhakāraḥ. evaṃ hataśabdasyāndhakāreṇa sāmānādhikaraṇyam
body.translated_text: The meaning is: 'one who awakens by himself.' We also see no fault in taking the <s>kta</s> suffix in the object sense (<s>karmaṇi</s>) — the meaning being: 'known (<s>buddha</s>) by other <s>Buddhas</s> or others,' because he is endowed with the perfection of all qualities and is free from all faults. 'The Blessed One' — the addition of this second word is for the purpose of preventing disrespect. For in the world, disrespect is seen toward names without epithets, as [when one simply says] '<s>Devadatta</s>.' However, the authors of the <s>Vinaya-vibhāṣā</s> construct a fourfold classification: (1) There is a <s>Buddha</s> who is not a Blessed One — a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, for he can be called '<s>Buddha</s>' because of being self-arisen, but not 'Blessed One' because his accumulations of giving, etc. are not complete; for one who possesses greatness is called 'Blessed One.' (2) There is a Blessed One who is not a <s>Buddha</s> — a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence, because his perfections of giving, etc. are complete, [Tib. 3b] but because he has not yet attained perfect awakening. (3) There is one who is both <s>Buddha</s> and Blessed One. (4) There is one who is neither — setting aside these [previous] types. Therefore '<s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One' serves as a double qualifier. 'Whose darkness has been destroyed' (<s>hatāndhakāra</s>) — whose darkness has been destroyed by him. In the possessive compound with the sixth case (<s>ṣaṣṭhī-bahuvrīhi</s>), 'destroyed by the path' — the path as agent must be supplied. In the instrumental compound (<s>tṛtīyā-bahuvrīhi</s>), 'by the path' as instrument must be supplied. Another says: The showing of two analyses is for the purpose of including both meanings of the root <s>han</s> — 'to go' and 'to destroy.' When the analysis is 'whose darkness has been destroyed (<s>hata</s>),' the root <s>han</s> is taken in the sense of going — the meaning is 'whose darkness has departed.' But when it is an instrumental compound, the root <s>han</s> is taken in the sense of destroying — the meaning is 'darkness destroyed by him.' Thus, making a single word of the two subsequent words, he then forms a locative <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound: 'in all [respects], whose darkness is destroyed' = <s>sarvahatāndhakāra</s>. And in that case, the word <s>hata</s> does not function as the first member here. But the question arises: by what rule does the locative compound occur here? [Answer:] The compound is like <s>śauṇḍaiḥ</s> (with the seventh case). The word <s>hatāndhakāra</s> is listed among the <s>śauṇḍādi</s> [group]. Since the <s>śauṇḍādi</s> group is treated as an open class (<s>ākṛtikṛta</s>), its inclusion there is to be understood. Or, by separation of the rule applying to the seventh case. Or, the compound is by the general rule: since <s>sup</s> ('case-ending') is current in the rule 'together with <s>sup</s>' (<s>saha supā</s>), a case-inflected word is compounded with another case-inflected word, wherever desired. Or, the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> is of the undefined type, to be understood from the <s>mayūravyaṃsakādi</s> [examples]. But then how does 'darkness,' which has become subordinate, connect with 'in all'? True — 'darkness' is not directly connected with 'in all'; but the destruction of darkness is connected with it. For by whatever destruction of darkness the Blessed One is called 'one whose darkness is destroyed,' that destruction of darkness is to be understood as having 'all' as its domain. Just as [in] 'a cheat at dice' (<s>akṣeṣu dhūrtaḥ</s>) — by whatever quality characterized as cheating he is a cheat, that [quality] has dice as its domain. So too here it should be understood. Moreover, we see another possible compound here: 'destroyed in all' = <s>sarvahata</s>; 'destroyed in all by every means' = <s>sarvathā sarvahata</s>; 'whose darkness has been thus destroyed' or 'by whom it has been destroyed' = <s>sarvathā sarvahatāndhakāra</s>. In this way, the word <s>hata</s> is in co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) with 'darkness.'

body.text:
. na ca pūrvanipāta iti. sarveṇa prakāreṇeti kliṣṭākliṣṭāndhakāravigamataḥ. sarvasmin jñeye dvādaśāyatanalakṣaṇe. sarvaṃ sarvam iti brāhmaṇa yāvad eva dvādaśāyatanānīti sūtre vacanāt. kim atra śārvaraṃ tamo 'ndhakāraśabdenocyate. nety āha. ajñānaṃ hi bhūtārthadarśanapratibandhād andhakāram ity avagantavyam. andhakāraśabdo hi naiśe tamasi prasiddhaḥ. andham iva janaṃ karotīti andhakāraḥ. sadbhūtaghaṭapaṭādirūpadarśanapratibandhāt. tatsādharmyāt ajñānam [Tib. 4a] apy andhakārākhyaṃ labhate. bhūtārthaduḥkhādisatyadarśanapratibandhāt. tac ceti tad ajñānam. pratipakśalābheneti āryamārgalābhena. vipakṣaḥ kleśaḥ vipakṣapratighātāya pakṣaḥ pratipakṣa iti kṛtvā. atha vā jñānaṃ anāsravam ajñānapratipakṣaḥ tasya lābhena. atyantaṃ sarvathā sarvatra jñeye puṇaranutpattidhamatvāt hatam asamudācāraprahāṇīkṛtam ity arthaḥ. ato 'sāv iti bhagavān. pratyekabuddhaśrāvakā apy abhyarhitavāt pratyekabuddhaśabdaḥ pūrvanipātaḥ. kāmam ity anujñāyām. na tu sarvatheti. akliṣṭasaṃmohānatyantavigamāt. nanu ca sarvaṃ sāsravavastu śrāvakapratyekabuddhānām api buddhavat prahīṇam. kim idam ueyate. kliṣṭasaṃmohasya teṣām atyantavigama iti. tathā hy uktam. nāham ekadharmam apy anabhijñāya aparijñāya duḥkhasyāntakriyāṃ vadāmīti. tathā nāham ekadharmam apy aparijñāyāprahāya duḥkhasyāntakriyāṃ vadāmīti. tasmāc chrāvakapratyekabuddhānām api tad akliṣṭam ajñānaṃ cakṣurādivac chandarāgaprahāṇāt prahīṇam eva. anyathā hi śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ duḥkhāntakriyā na bhavet. satam asty etad evam. prahīṇam eva teṣāṃ kliṣṭavad akliṣṭam apy ajñānaṃ. tat tu teṣāṃ cakṣurādivat prahīṇam api samudācarati. buddhasya tu prahīṇaṃ san na samudācarati. ata eva ca viśeṣitaṃ punaranutpattidharmatvāt hatam [Tib. 4b] iti. anyathā tat sarvathā sarvatra jñeye prahīṇam ity evāvakṣyat. ye tu vyācakṣate śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ kliṣṭasaṃmohamātravigamāt saṃkleśavinivṛttir iti. tad apavyākhyānam eṣāṃ yathoktam iti pratyācakṣyate. tathā hy eṣām iti vistaraḥ.
tathā hīti yasmād ity arthaḥ. atha vā tatheti yathā na sarvathā tatheti. hiśabdo hetau. eṣām iti śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ. buddhadharmeṣv āveṇikādiṣu. ativiprakṛṣṭadeśakāleṣu cārtheṣu ativiprakṛṣṭadeśeṣu ativiprakṛṣṭakāleṣu ca. anantaprabhedeṣu cābuddhadharmasvabhāveṣv api rūpādiṣv artheṣu. bhavaty evākliṣṭam ajñānaṃ samudācaraty eva tad ity arthaḥ. tatra ye buddhadharmā āveṇikādayaḥ. teṣu svabhāvaparamasūkṣmagambhīratvād buddhād anyeṣām ajñānam. yathoktaṃ. jānīṣe
body.translated_text:
. And there is no prior placement [of the word]. 'In every manner' means by the removal of both afflicted and non-afflicted darkness. 'In all that is to be known,' characterized by the twelve sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>). Because it is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'Everything is everything, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, insofar as there are the twelve sense-bases.' Is the nocturnal darkness meant by the word 'darkness' here? No, he says. For ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) should be understood as 'darkness' because it obstructs the vision of reality. The word 'darkness' is well-known in the sense of nocturnal gloom. It is called 'darkness' (<s>andhakāra</s>) because it makes people as if blind — by obstructing the seeing of real forms such as pots, cloths, and so forth. By analogy with that, ignorance also obtains the designation 'darkness' — because it obstructs the seeing of the truths of reality, suffering, and so forth. 'And that' means that ignorance. 'By obtaining the antidote' means by obtaining the noble path (<s>āryamārga</s>). The adversary is defilement (<s>kleśa</s>); the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) is what opposes the adversary. Or, uncontaminated knowledge (<s>anāsrava jñāna</s>) is the antidote to ignorance; by obtaining that. 'Completely' means in every way, regarding all that is to be known — because of the nature of non-arising again — 'destroyed' means made abandoned through non-occurrence. Therefore that one, the Blessed One. Even <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s> are honored, yet the word '<s>Pratyekabuddha</s>' has prior placement [before <s>Śrāvaka</s>]. '<s>Kāmam</s>' is used in the sense of permission. 'But not in every way' — because the non-afflicted delusion is not completely removed. But surely all contaminated things are abandoned by <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> just as by the <s>Buddha</s>. Why then is it said that there is complete removal of afflicted delusion for them? For it is stated: 'I do not declare the making of an end of suffering without having fully known even a single <s>dharma</s>.' Likewise: 'I do not declare the making of an end of suffering without having fully known and abandoned even a single <s>dharma</s>.' Therefore, for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> too, that non-afflicted ignorance is indeed abandoned — like the eye-faculty and so forth — through the abandonment of desire and attachment (<s>chandarāga</s>). Otherwise, the making of an end of suffering would not occur for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. That is true, it is so. The non-afflicted ignorance, like the afflicted, is indeed abandoned for them. But for them, though abandoned, it still occurs — like the eye-faculty and so forth. For the <s>Buddha</s>, however, once abandoned, it does not occur again. And for this very reason the distinction is stated: 'because of the nature of non-arising again, destroyed.' Otherwise, it would have simply stated: 'abandoned in every way regarding all that is to be known.' Those who explain that for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, the turning away from defilement occurs merely through the removal of afflicted delusion — that is a misinterpretation; it is rejected as stated. For of these — and so on in detail.
'For thus' (<s>tathā hi</s>) means 'because.' Alternatively, 'thus' (<s>tathā</s>) means 'in such a way that it is not in every way.' The particle <s>hi</s> indicates reason. 'Of these' means of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Regarding the <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas, the unique qualities (<s>āveṇika</s>) and so forth. 'And regarding things in extremely remote places and times' — in extremely remote places and in extremely remote times. 'And regarding things of infinite variety' — even regarding things like form and so forth whose nature is not the <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas. Indeed there is non-afflicted ignorance — it indeed occurs. Therein, regarding the <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas, the unique qualities and so forth — because their intrinsic nature is supremely subtle and profound, those other than the <s>Buddha</s> have ignorance regarding them. As stated: 'Do you know, [

body.text: tvaṃ śāriputra tathāgatasya śīlaskandhaṃ samādhiskandhaṃ prajñāskandhaṃ vimuktiskandhaṃ vimuktijñānadarśanaskandham iti bhagavatā pṛṣṭena sthaviraśāradvatīputreṇoktam. no hīdaṃ bhagavann iti. ye tv anye 'rthā rūpiṇaḥ paramāṇusaṃcitāḥ. te ativiprakṛṣṭadeśā yadi bhavanti. ye 'py avijñaptyarūpiṇaḥ. te 'pi yady ativiprakṛṣṭadeśādhāratvāt ativiprakṛṣṭadeśā bhavanti. teṣv api teṣām ajñānam anekalokadhātvantaritadeśatvāt. śrūyate hi sthaviramaudgalyāyanasya ativiprakṛṣṭadeśamārīcīlokadhātujātasvamātṛdeśaparijñānam. ativiprakṛṣtakāleṣv apy atīteṣu anāgateṣu vā teṣv artheṣv atibahukalpāntarāntaritavināśaprādurbhāvatvāt [Tib. 5a] teṣāṃ bhavaty evājñānam. śrūyate hi sthaviraśāriputreṇa mokṣabhāgīyakuśalamūlādarśanāt pravrajyāpekṣapuruṣapratyākhyānam. bhagavatā tu tasya mokṣabhāgīyaṃ dṛṣṭam uktaṃ ca
body.translated_text: O <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata's</s> aggregate of morality, aggregate of concentration, aggregate of wisdom, aggregate of liberation, aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation?' When asked by the Blessed One, the Elder <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (Śāriputra) replied: 'No indeed, Blessed One.' Those other things that are material, composed of atoms — if they are in extremely remote places, [there is ignorance]. Those that are non-manifest and formless — if they too are in extremely remote places because their support is extremely remote, regarding those too, they have ignorance, because many world-realms intervene. For it is heard that the Elder <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> had knowledge of his own mother's location in the world-realm of <s>Mārīci</s>, an extremely remote place. Regarding things in extremely remote times too — whether past or future — because their destruction and manifestation are separated by extremely many aeons, they indeed have ignorance. For it is heard that the Elder <s>Śāriputra</s> rejected a man seeking ordination because he did not see [in him] the roots of virtue pertaining to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya kuśalamūla</s>). But the Blessed One saw his liberation-pertaining [root] and said:

body.text:
mokṣabījam ahaṃ hy asya susūkṣmam upalakṣaye
dhātupāṣāṇavivare nilīnam iva kāṃcanam
body.translated_text: 'For I perceive his seed of liberation, extremely subtle, hidden like gold in a crevice of a stone of the elements.'

body.text: iti. sa ca puruṣaḥ pravrājita iti. anantaprabhedeṣv iti. dhātugatiyonyupapattyādiprabhede durbodheṣv artheṣu. teṣām ajñānaṃ bhavaty eva. tathā hy āha.
body.translated_text: And that man was ordained. 'Of infinite variety' — regarding things that are difficult to understand, being of varied types such as elements, destinies, modes of birth, and forms of existence. They indeed have ignorance regarding those. For thus it is said:

body.text:
sarvākāraṃ kāraṇam ekasya mayūracandrakasyāpi
nāsarvajñair jñeyaṃ sarvajñabalaṃ hi tajjñānam
body.translated_text: 'The cause in every aspect even of a single peacock's tail-eye is not knowable by those who are not omniscient — for the knowledge of that is the power of omniscience.'

body.text: iti. tāny etāni catvāry ajñānakāraṇāni bhavanti. teṣāṃ kvacid ekaṃ kvacid dve kvacit trīṇi kvacit catvāsrīti saṃbhavato yojyāni. ity ātmahitapratipattisampad iti vistaraḥ. ātmahitāya pratipattiḥ ātmahitapratipattiḥ. ātmahitapratipatteḥ sampat ātmahitapratipattisampat phalaniṣpattir ity arthaḥ. sā ceyaṃ saṃpat jñānaprahāṇasaṃpatsvabhāvā veditavyā. parahitapratipattisaṃpad api tathaiva carcanīyā. apare vyācakṣate. ātmahitapratipattir ātmahitapratipādanam. ātmahitopagraha ity arthaḥ. tasyāḥ sampat ātmahitapratipattisampat. evaṃ parahitapratipattisaṃpad api vyākhyeyā. sā punaḥ sarvaduḥkhopaśamanirvāṇapariprāpaṇasvabhāvā.
body.translated_text: These are the four causes of ignorance. Among them, sometimes one, sometimes two, sometimes three, sometimes all four may be applicable according to possibility. Thus, 'the perfection of the practice for one's own benefit' — and so forth in detail. The practice for one's own benefit is <s>ātmahitapratipattiḥ</s>; the perfection of that practice is <s>ātmahitapratipattisampat</s> — meaning the accomplishment of the result. And this perfection should be understood as having the nature of the perfection of knowledge and abandonment. The perfection of the practice for others' benefit should be analyzed in the same way. Others explain: <s>ātmahitapratipattiḥ</s> is the communication of one's own benefit, meaning the support of one's own welfare; the perfection of that is <s>ātmahitapratipattisampat</s>. The perfection of the practice for others' benefit should be explained similarly. That [latter] has the nature of bringing about <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the cessation of all suffering.

children.translated_text: 'He lifted the world from the mud of <s>saṃsāra</s>' —

body.text: vacanāt. saṃsaraṇaṃ saṃsāra [Tib. 5b] ājavaṃjavībhāvaḥ janmamaraṇaparaṃparety arthaḥ. atha vā saṃsaranty asmin sattvā iti saṃsāras traidhātukam. saṃsāraḥ paṅka iva saṃsārapaṅkaḥ paṃkasādharmyāt. ata āha. saṃsāro hi jagadāsaṅgasthānatvād duruttaratvāc ca paṅkabhūta iti. paṅko hi loke avasādātmakatvāt āsaṅgasya sthānam. ata eva ca duruttaraḥ. caṃcalatvād vā parāśrayottaraṇīyatvād
body.translated_text: because of this statement. <s>Saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) — the rushing succession of birth and death. Or, '<s>saṃsāra</s>' is the three realms, because beings transmigrate in it. <s>Saṃsāra</s> is like mud, hence '<s>saṃsāra</s>-mud' — because of its similarity to mud. Therefore he says: <s>Saṃsāra</s> is like mud for the world, because it is a place of attachment and because it is difficult to cross. For mud in the world is a place of attachment because of its nature of sinking. And for that very reason it is difficult to cross — either because of its instability, or because it can only be crossed with others' help.

body.text: vā duruttaraḥ. saṃsāro 'pi hi tṛṣṇābhiṣyanditatvād āsaṅgasthānam. duruttaraś ca tasmād eva dṛṣṭivicikitsāvispanditena. buddhāpāśrayottaraṇīyatvena vā duruttaraḥ. tatrāvamagnaṃ tādātmyanupraveśataḥ samudāyāvayavarūpato vā. jagat sattvalokam atrāṇam anākrandam anukampamānaḥ karuṇāyamāno bhagavān saddharmadeśanāhastapradānaiḥ. saddharmadeśanā eva hastāḥ. teṣāṃ pradānāni. uttāraṇīyabahutvād bahuvacanaṃ. tair yathābhavyaṃ abhyuddhṛtavān. yathābhavyam iti anucyamānam api gamyate loke tathā dṛṣṭatvāt. tadyathā brāhmaṇān ānīya bhojayāmāsety ukte. ye tatra bhojayituṃ śaktā grāme nagare vā saṃnihitāh. tān eva bhojayāmāseti gamyate. sarvalokabrāhmaṇānāṃ bhojayitum aśakyatvāt. evam ihāpi yo jano bhavyo 'bhyuddhartum. tam evabhyuddhṛtavān iti. ato yathābhavyam iti vyācaṣṭe.
body.translated_text: Similarly, <s>saṃsāra</s> too is a place of attachment because it is moistened by craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). And it is difficult to cross — for that very reason, because of the agitation of [wrong] views and doubt. Or it is difficult to cross because it can only be crossed with the help of the <s>Buddha</s>. Therein 'submerged' — through identification with it or in the form of the aggregate and its parts. 'The world' means the world of beings — unprotected, without anyone to cry out to — the Blessed One, having compassion, out of great mercy, through the giving of the hands of the teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s> — the teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s> itself constitutes the hands; 'their giving' — the plural is used because of the multiplicity of those to be rescued — by those [hands], according to their capacity (<s>yathābhavya</s>), he lifted them up. 'According to their capacity' — even without being stated, this is understood, because it is seen thus in the world. Just as when it is said 'having brought <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, he fed [them]' — it is understood that he fed only those who were able to eat and were present in the village or town, because it is impossible to feed all <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in the world. Similarly here too, whatever person is capable of being lifted up — him alone he lifted up. Therefore he explains: 'according to their capacity.'

body.text: śirasā praṇipatya kriyāspadībhūtatvān namaḥśabdasya praṇipatyārtho namaskṛtyaśabdo bhavati. praṇipātaś ca loke śirasā pratīta iti śirasety āha. vāṅmanonamaskāro 'pi atranuktasiddho guṇākhyānapūrvakatvāt manaskarmapūrvakatvāc ca kāyakarmaṇaḥ. tasmai iti kiṃlakṣaṇeyaṃ caturthī. atra bahavo vyākhyānakārā muhyanti. ācāryaguṇamatis tacchiṣyaś cācāryavasumitra āhatuḥ. namaḥśabdayoge caturthī. namaḥsvastisvāhāsvadhālaṃvaṣaḍyogāc ceti. tad etad ayuktam. svatantrasya namaḥśabdasya yoge sā caturthī bhavati. asvatantraś cāyaṃ namaḥśabdaḥ kriyāspadībhūtatvāt. ata eva cānenaivācāryeṇa vyākhyāyuktau
body.translated_text: having bowed down with the head. Because the word <s>namaḥ</s> has become the basis of the action [of bowing], the word <s>namaskṛtya</s> means 'having bowed down.' And bowing is understood in the world as [done] with the head — hence he says 'with the head.' Homage by speech and mind is also established here without being stated, because bodily action is preceded by the recounting of virtues and by mental action. 'To him' — in what sense is this dative? Here many commentators are confused. The teacher <s>Guṇamati</s> and his pupil, the teacher <s>Vasumitra</s>, said: the dative is used in connection with the word <s>namaḥ</s>, [citing the rule]: 'the dative is used in connection with <s>namaḥ</s>, <s>svasti</s>, <s>svāhā</s>, <s>svadhā</s>, <s>alam</s>, and <s>vaṣaṭ</s>.' But this is incorrect. That dative applies when the word <s>namaḥ</s> is independent. But here the word <s>namaḥ</s> is not independent, having become the basis of an action [i.e., compounded with <s>kṛtya</s>]. And for this very reason, by this same teacher [Vasubandhu], in the <s>Vyākhyāyukti</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Having paid homage with the head to the Sage' —

body.text: karmalakṣaṇā dvitīyā prayuktā. tasmān na namaḥśabdayoge caturthīti. dvitīyāyāḥ sthāne caturthī prayuktety apare. tad idam eṣām icchāmātram. na hi lakṣaṇam asyāstīti. kena tarhīyaṃ caturthī. saṃpradānalakṣaṇeyaṃ caturthīti vyācakṣmahe. kathaṃ saṃpradānasaṃjñā. karmaṇā yam abhipraiti. sa saṃpradānam iti. cūrṇikāreṇa karmaśabda ubhayathā varṇyate. pāribhāṣikaṃ karma laukikaṃ ceti. tatra yadā kartur īpsitatamaṃ karmeti pāribhāṣikaṃ karmāśrīyate. tadā kartur īpsitatamena yam abhipraiti. sa saṃpradānasaṃjño bhavati. brāhmaṇāya gāṃ prayacchatīti. etat siddhaṃ bhavati. yadā tu karma kriyeti laukikaṃ karmāśrīyate. tadā kriyayā yam abhipraiti. sa saṃpradānasaṃjño bhavatīti. tad etat siddhaṃ bhavati. yuddhāya saṃnahyati. patye śeta iti. saṃnahanakriyayā yuddham abhipraiti kartā. śayanakriyayā patim iti.
body.translated_text: the accusative, characterizing the object, is employed. Therefore, the dative is not [required] in connection with the word <s>namaḥ</s>. Others [say] the dative is used in place of the accusative. But this is merely their wish; there is no rule for this. By what then is this dative [justified]? We explain: this dative has the characteristic of the recipient (<s>saṃpradāna</s>). How does the designation 'recipient' apply? 'That which the action aims at is the recipient.' The commentator (<s>cūrṇikāra</s>) explains the word 'action' (<s>karma</s>) in two ways — technical and ordinary. When the technical [definition] is relied upon — 'the object most desired by the agent is the <s>karma</s>' — then that which the agent aims at with the most desired object becomes designated as the recipient. 'He gives a cow to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' — this is established. But when the ordinary [definition] is relied upon — '<s>karma</s> means action' — then that which the action aims at becomes designated as the recipient. And this is established: 'He arms himself for battle,' 'She lies with [her] husband.' The agent aims at battle through the action of arming; at the husband through the action of lying.

body.text: yuddhādīnām sampradānasaṃjñā siddhā bhavati. tathehapi namaskārakriyayā śāstāram abhipraiti ācāryaḥ. tasmāc chāstari saṃpradānasaṃjñā. saṃpradānasaṃjñāyāṃ satyāṃ saṃpradāne caturthī 'ti caturthī bhavati. evaṃ ca kṛtvā
body.translated_text: The designation of recipient for 'battle' and the like is thus established. Similarly here too, the teacher aims at the Master through the action of paying homage. Therefore, the designation of recipient applies to the Master. When the designation of recipient is established, the dative [follows from the rule]: 'the dative in the case of the recipient.' Thus, doing so:

children.text:
pūrvaṃ praṇamya vadatāṃ pravarāya śāstre. |
pramāṇabhūtāya jagaddhitaiṣiṇe
praṇamya śāstre sugatāya tāyina. |
children.translated_text:
'First bowing to the foremost of speakers, to the Master,
To the one who has become an authority, who desires the welfare of the world,
Bowing to the Master, the <s>Sugata</s>, the Protector —'

body.text: ityevamādīni kāvyaśāstrāntaroktāni śabdarūpāṇi sunītāni bhavanti. yadi tarhi saṃpradānasaṃjñaiveṣyate.
body.translated_text: such expressions found in other poetic and scientific works are well-formed. But if the designation of recipient is preferred,

children.translated_text: 'Having paid homage with the head to the Sage' —

body.text: atra dvitīyā na prāpnoti. naiṣa doṣaḥ. vivakṣātaḥ kārakāṇi bhavanti. yadā karmavivakṣā. tadā dvitīyā. yadā saṃpradānavivakṣā. tadā caturthī 'ti ubhayam api siddhaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: here the accusative would not be obtained. This is no fault. For grammatical relations (<s>kāraka</s>) are determined by the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>). When the object is intended, the accusative [is used]; when the recipient is intended, the dative — thus both are established.

body.text: Tib. 5b
body.translated_text: Tib. 5b

body.text: yathārthaśāstra
body.translated_text: 'The treatise true to its subject matter' —

body.text: iti. śāstr iti auṇādikaḥ śabdaḥ. tṛntṛcau śaṃsikṣādibhyaḥ saṃjñāyāṃ cāniṭāv iti tṛnpratyayānto 'niṭ śāsteti bhavati. nanu ca saṃjñāyāṃ śāsteti bhavati. na ceyaṃ saṃjñā. saṃjñaiveyam. dvividhā hi saṃjñā viśeṣasaṃjñā sāmānyasaṃjñā ca. viśeṣasanjñā evadatto yajñadatta iti. sāmānyasaṃjñā mātāpitetyevamādikā. mātrādayo 'pi hi tatra saṃjñāyām eva nipātyante. naptṛneṣṭṛtvaṣṭṛhotṛpotṛbhrātṛjāmātṛmātṛpitṛduhitṛ iti. tena yathā sarvāsāṃ mātṝṇām iyaṃ saṃjñā māteti. sarveṣāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ piteti. evaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca śāstṝṇām iyaṃ saṃjñā śāsteti. sa tu śāstā dvividho bhavati. ayathārtho yathārthaś ca. [Tib. 6a] ayathārthaś ca pūraṇādiḥ. yathārthaś ca tathāgata iti. ato viśinaṣṭi yathārtham aviparītaṃ śāstīti yathārthaśāstā. etac ca viśeṣaṇaṃ parahitapratipattyupāyasūcanārtham. ata evāha. parahitapratipattyupāyam asyāviṣkarotītyevamādi. na tv ṛddhivarapradānaprabhāveneti prabhāvaśabdaḥ pratyekam abhisaṃbadhyate. ṛddhiprabhāvena varapradānaprabhāveneti. ṛddhiprabhāvas tadyathā viṣṇor viśvarūpasaṃdarśanam. varapradānaprabhāvas tadyathā maheśvaro varaṃ prayacchatīti pravādaḥ. atha vā tripado dvaṃdvaḥ. ṛddhiś ca varapradānaṃ ca prabhāvaś ceti. prabhāvaḥ śaktiviśeṣaḥ. nanu ca buddhā api kadācit ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vineyānām upadarśayanti. asty etad evam. api tv āvarjanamātraṃ tu teṣāṃ. anuśāsanīprātihāryeṇa tu rāgādipratipakṣabhāvanākrameṇa saṃsārottaraṇaṃ bhavati. kiṃ kariṣyatīti praśnaḥ.
body.translated_text: Thus. '<s>Śāstṛ</s>' (teacher) is a word formed by <s>Uṇādi</s> suffixes. [The rule] '<s>tṛn</s> and <s>tṛc</s> [are added to roots] <s>śaṃs</s>, <s>ikṣ</s>, and so forth, and in a designation — both without <s>iṭ</s>' — thus the word ending in the <s>tṛn</s> suffix, without <s>iṭ</s>, becomes '<s>śāstā</s>.' But [one might object:] '<s>śāstā</s>' occurs only in a designation, and this is not a designation. [Reply:] This is indeed a designation. For designation is of two kinds: specific designation and general designation. A specific designation is like '<s>Devadatta</s>' or '<s>Yajñadatta</s>.' A general designation is like 'mother,' 'father,' and so on. For 'mother' and the rest are also listed there under 'in a designation': '<s>naptṛ</s>, <s>neṣṭṛ</s>, <s>tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>hotṛ</s>, <s>potṛ</s>, <s>bhrātṛ</s>, <s>jāmātṛ</s>, <s>mātṛ</s>, <s>pitṛ</s>, <s>duhitṛ</s>.' Therefore, just as the designation for all mothers is 'mother,' and for all fathers is 'father,' so for all teachers the designation is '<s>śāstā</s>.' But that teacher is of two kinds: the one who teaches what is not the true meaning, and the one who teaches the true meaning. The one who teaches what is not true is <s>Pūraṇa</s> and others [i.e., the six heretical teachers]. The one who teaches the true meaning is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore he specifies: one who teaches the true meaning — who teaches correctly and without error — is a 'true teacher.' And this qualifier is for the purpose of indicating the means of benefiting others. Hence he says, 'He reveals to them the means of practice for the benefit of others,' and so on. Not through the power of supernatural feats or the power of granting boons — the word '<s>prabhāva</s>' (power) is connected with each separately: 'through the power of supernatural feats and through the power of granting boons.' The power of supernatural feats is, for example, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s displaying of the universal form. The power of granting boons is, for example, the tradition that <s>Maheśvara</s> grants boons. Alternatively, it is a three-membered <s>dvandva</s> compound: 'supernatural feats, granting of boons, and power.' '<s>Prabhāva</s>' [means] a special capacity. But [one might object:] <s>Buddhas</s> too sometimes display the miracle of supernatural feats to those to be trained. This is so. However, that is merely for the purpose of attracting them. But through the miracle of instruction — through the systematic cultivation of antidotes to passion and the rest — there comes the crossing over <s>saṃsāra</s>. 'What will he do?' is the question.

body.text: ktvāvidheḥ kriyāntarapekṣatvāt. samānakartṛkayor hi pūrvakāle ktvāvidhir bhavati.
body.translated_text: because the <s>ktvā</s> construction requires another action [by the same agent]. For the <s>ktvā</s> construction occurs with the earlier [of two actions] having the same agent.

body.text: arthaviśeṣābhidyotako nāmasamūhaḥ śāstraṃ. kṣaṇikatvāt samuhānupapattir iti cet. na. tadgrāhakabuddhirūpasamūhakalpanāt. śiṣyaśāsanāc chāstram iti. [Tib. 6b] kiṃ śāstram iti kiṃ nāmadheyam ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: A collection of words that illuminates a particular meaning is a '<s>śāstra</s>' (treatise). If [one objects that] a collection is impossible because [words are] momentary — no, because [a collection] is imputed on the basis of the cognitions that grasp them, which have the form of a collection. [Or:] Because it instructs disciples, it is a '<s>śāstra</s>.' What treatise? — the meaning is: what is its name?

body.text: (I.2ab)
body.translated_text: (I.2ab)

body.text: ity asya nirvacanaṃ vakṣyate. āstāṃ tāvad etat.
body.translated_text: its etymological analysis will be stated. Let this be set aside for now.

body.text:
avayavārthāvabodhapūrvakaḥ samudāyārthāvabodhaḥ ity avayavārthaṃ tāvat
pṛcchati. ko 'yam abhidharmo nāmeti. 1.
body.translated_text: Since the understanding of the compound meaning is preceded by the understanding of the component meanings, he first asks about the component meaning: 'What is this thing called <s>abhidharma</s>?' 1.

body.text: iti. dharmapravicayakāle prajñā pradhānam iti mukhyavṛttyā prajñāgrahaṇam.
body.translated_text: — Thus. Since at the time of discerning <s>dharmas</s>, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is primary, the word '<s>prajñā</s>' is used in its primary sense.

body.text: anāsravā. malānām āsravaparyāyatvāt.
body.translated_text: [means] undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>). Because defilements (<s>malas</s>) are synonymous with outflows (<s>āsravas</s>).

body.text: saparivārā. rājñā samaṃ carann api bhṛtyo rājānucara ity ucyate. tadanuvṛttikāritvāt. tathehāpi samakālaṃ caranto 'pi tatsahabhuvo dharmā anucarā evocyante. ke punas te. cittacaittāḥ anāsravasaṃvaro jātyādayaś ca cittaviprayuktā iti. nanu ca cittaṃ caittebhyaḥ pradhānam. tathā hi cittasya ime citte vā bhavāś caittā iti. tena prajñaiva cittasya parivāro 'rhati. na tu cittaṃ prajñāyāḥ caitasikatvāt asty etat. api tu dharmapravicayakāle prajñā caittasyāpi sarvasya kalāpasya rājāyate. kvacit kaścid dharmaḥ prādhānyam āskandati. tadyathā abhisaṃpratyayakāle śraddhetyevamādi. anāsravaḥ pañcaskandhaka iti. anāsravasaṃvaras tasmin kalāpe rūpaskandhaḥ. yā vedanā. sa vedanāskandhaḥ. yā saṃjñā. sa saṃjñāskandhaḥ. cetanādijātyādayaḥ saṃskāraskandhaḥ. [Tib. 7a] vijñānaṃ cātra vijñānaskandhaḥ. eṣa tāvad iti. tāvacchabdaḥ kramārthaḥ. pāramārthika iti. paramārtha eva pāramārthikaḥ. paramārthe vā bhavaḥ pāramārthikaḥ. paramārthena vā dīvyati caratīti vā pāramārthikaḥ. sāṃketikas tu sāṃvyavahārikaḥ.
body.translated_text: [means] with its attendants. Just as a servant who accompanies the king is called the king's 'attendant' because he acts in conformity with him, so here too, <s>dharmas</s> that arise simultaneously — the concomitant <s>dharmas</s> — are called 'attendants.' What are they? The mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caittas</s>), the undefiled restraint (<s>anāsrava-saṃvara</s>), and birth (<s>jāti</s>) and other mind-dissociated [formations]. But [one might object:] mind is primary over the mental factors. For mental factors are 'those that belong to mind' (<s>citta</s>) or 'those that exist in mind' (<s>caitta</s>). Therefore wisdom should be the retinue of mind, not mind the retinue of wisdom, since [wisdom] is a mental factor. This is so. However, at the time of discerning <s>dharmas</s>, wisdom assumes sovereignty over even the entire aggregate of mental [factors]. At different times, different <s>dharmas</s> assume primacy — for example, at the time of conviction, faith [is primary], and so on. 'The undefiled five-aggregate [collection]' — the undefiled restraint in that aggregate is the form-aggregate. The feeling [therein] is the feeling-aggregate. The perception [therein] is the perception-aggregate. Volition and the rest, birth and the rest — [these constitute] the formations-aggregate. And consciousness therein is the consciousness-aggregate. 'This, for now' — the word 'for now' (<s>tāvat</s>) indicates sequence. 'Ultimate' (<s>pāramārthika</s>) — [means] what is the ultimate reality itself, or what exists in the ultimate reality, or what functions through or moves in the ultimate reality. 'Conventional' (<s>sāṃketika</s>) means 'transactional.'

children.translated_text: 'And that which [leads] to the attainment of that' —

body.text: prajñā sānucarā so 'bhidharma iti cātrādhikṛtam. tasyā anāsravāyāḥ prajñāyāḥ prāptyarthaṃ sākṣāt pāraṃparyeṇa vā yā śrutamayī cintāmayī ca bhāvanāmayī ca prajñā sāsravā yā copapattipratilambhikā sānucarā. sāpi sāṃketiko 'bhidharmaḥ. tatra śrutaprayogajā śrutamayī. yuktinidhyānaprayogajā cintāmayī.
body.translated_text: thus wisdom with its retinue is <s>abhidharma</s> — this is what is being discussed here. For the purpose of attaining that undefiled wisdom — directly or indirectly — the wisdom born of hearing, born of reflection, and born of meditation, which is defiled (<s>sāsrava</s>), and that which is obtained at birth, with its retinue — this too is conventional <s>abhidharma</s>. Therein: that born of the effort of hearing is 'born of hearing.' That born of the effort of rational investigation is 'born of reflection.'

body.text: bhāvanāprayogajā bhāvanāmayī. upapattipratilambhajā upapattipratilambhikā. upapattipratilambho 'syāstīti. ata iniṭhanāv iti ṭhanvidhānān na vṛddhiḥ. śrutacintāmayy upapattipratilambhikā bhāvanāmayī cārūpyāvacarī catuḥskandhako 'bhidharmaḥ anuparivartakarūpabhāvāt. rūpāvacarī tu dhyānasaṃvarasadbhāvāt paṃcaskandhako 'bhidharmaḥ.
body.translated_text: That born of the effort of meditation is 'born of meditation.' That obtained at birth is 'obtained at birth' — 'one who has obtained at birth' — hence by the rule '<s>iniṭhanau</s>' the <s>ṭhan</s> suffix is applied, without <s>vṛddhi</s>. The wisdom born of hearing and reflection, that obtained at birth, and the one born of meditation in the formless realm — these constitute a four-aggregate <s>abhidharma</s>, because of the absence of concomitant form. But in the form realm, because of the existence of <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint, it is a five-aggregate <s>abhidharma</s>.

body.text: iti abhidharmaśāstram abhipretaṃ. tat tu sānucaraṃ na sānucaram iti vyākhyābhedaḥ. kecit tāvat acittacaitasikakalāparūpatvāt.
body.translated_text: refers to the <s>Abhidharma</s> treatise. Whether that [treatise] is 'with retinue' or 'without retinue' — this is a difference in interpretation. Some, since it does not have the nature of an aggregate of mind and mental factors,

body.text: iti nānuvartayanti. jātyādisaṃbhavāt kecid anuvartayanti. ekaskandhako hy asāv abhidharmaḥ. dviskandhako vā. tasya ca jātyādayaḥ santīti. anye tu vyācakṣate śāstram iti [Tib. 7b] jñānaprasthānaṃ. tasya śarīrabhūtasya ṣaṭ pādāḥ. prakaraṇapādaḥ vijñānakāyaḥ harmaskandhaḥ prajñaptiśāstraṃ hātukāyaḥ saṃgītiparyāya ity atas tad api śāstraṃ sānucaram eva pāraṃparyeṇa pāramārthikābhidharmaprāptaye sāṃketiko 'bhidharma ity ucyate. upapattipratilambhikā hi prajñā śāstraśravaṇāt tadartham anusarati. tasyāḥ śrutamayī śrutamayyāś cintāmayī cintāmayyāḥ sāsravā bhāvanāmayī tasyā anāsravā prajñā jāyata iti anukramaḥ. tad ayam iti. tad iti vākyopanyāse. ayam iti svalakṣaṇadhāraṇatvena niruktaḥ pāramārthikaḥ sāṃketiko 'bhidharmaḥ. praramārthadharmam iti. paramasya jñānasyārthaḥ paramārthaḥ. paramo vārthaḥ paramārthaḥ sarvadharmāgratvāt paramārthaḥ. paramārthaś cāsau dharmaś ca paramārthadharmaḥ. dharmalakṣaṇaṃ veti. svasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ khakkhaṭalakṣaṇaḥ pṛthivīdhātur anityaṃ duḥkham ityevamādi. tat pratyabhimukhaḥ pratilambhāya prativedhāya avabodhāya vā abhimukho dharmaḥ abhidharmaḥ. kugatiprādaya iti tatpuruṣasamāsaḥ. nanu ca lakṣaṇenābhipratī ābhimukhya iti avyayībhāvaḥ prāpnoti. yadā hy abhir lakṣaṇena saha samasyate. tadāvyayībhāvaḥ. tadyathā abhyagni śalabhāḥ patanti. śalabhapatanaṃ agninā lakṣyate. so 'gnir asya lakṣaṇaṃ. na tv ayaṃ dharmo 'nyasya lakṣaṇam. kiṃ tarhi. lakṣyaḥ. svayam evābhimukhyāt. śāstrākhyo 'pi sāṃketiko 'bhidharmaḥ prāpaṇāyābhidyotanāya vā nirvāṇaṃ dharmalakṣaṇaṃ vā praty upaniṣadbhāvenābhimukhaḥ. kimaṃga pāramārthika ity atas tatpuruṣasamāsenābhidharma iti siddhaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: do not carry over [this qualifier]. Some carry it over, because of the occurrence of birth and other [formations]. For that <s>abhidharma</s> consists of one aggregate, or two aggregates. And it has birth and the rest. Others, however, explain: 'the treatise' means the <s>Jñānaprasthāna</s>. Its six 'feet' [subsidiary texts] are: the <s>Prakaraṇapāda</s>, the <s>Vijñānakāya</s>, the <s>Dharmaskandha</s>, the <s>Prajñaptiśāstra</s>, the <s>Dhātukāya</s>, and the <s>Saṃgītiparyāya</s>. Therefore that treatise too is indeed 'with retinue.' It is called conventional <s>abhidharma</s> because it [leads] indirectly to the attainment of ultimate <s>abhidharma</s>. For the wisdom obtained at birth follows the meaning of that treatise through hearing it. From that [arises] the wisdom born of hearing; from that, the wisdom born of reflection; from that, defiled wisdom born of meditation; from that, undefiled wisdom is born — this is the sequence. 'This, then' — '<s>tat</s>' introduces the statement. '<s>Ayam</s>' refers to this [<s>abhidharma</s>], explained as ultimate and conventional by defining its specific characteristics. 'The ultimate <s>dharma</s>' — the object of the supreme knowledge is the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>). Or, the supreme object is the ultimate, because it is the foremost of all <s>dharmas</s>. The ultimate which is also a <s>dharma</s> is 'ultimate <s>dharma</s>.' 'Or the characteristic of <s>dharmas</s>' — the specific and general characteristics: the earth element characterized by hardness, [or] 'impermanent,' 'suffering,' and so on. That which faces toward, [which is] for the attainment of, for the penetration of, or for the comprehension of that — [such] a <s>dharma</s> facing [the ultimate] is <s>abhidharma</s>. '<s>Kugatiprāda</s>' and similar — [this is] a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound. But [one might object:] when '<s>abhi</s>' means 'facing toward,' along with the characteristic, an <s>avyayībhāva</s> [compound] should result. For when '<s>abhi</s>' is compounded with the characteristic, it becomes an <s>avyayībhāva</s> — for example, '<s>abhyagni</s>': 'Moths fall toward the fire' — the fall of the moths is characterized by the fire; that fire is its characteristic. But this <s>dharma</s> is not the characteristic of another — rather, it is what is characterized, by its own facing toward [the ultimate]. The treatise-named conventional <s>abhidharma</s> too faces toward — for leading to or illuminating — <s>Nirvāṇa</s> or the characteristic of <s>dharmas</s>, by being a proximate condition. How much more the ultimate [<s>abhidharma</s>]! Therefore, through the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound, '<s>abhidharma</s>' is established.

body.text: (I.2cd) ukto 'bhidharma iti. svabhāvaprabhedanirvacanato avayavārtho 'vabuddhaḥ.
body.translated_text: (I.2cd) '<s>Abhidharma</s> has been stated' — thus. Through its intrinsic nature, classification, and etymology, the component meaning has been understood.

body.text: samudāyārthas tu na tāvad ity ataḥ samudāyārthaṃ pṛcchati. idaṃ tu śāstraṃ katham abhidharmakośam iti.
body.translated_text: But the compound meaning has not yet [been stated] — therefore he asks about the compound meaning: 'But how is this treatise [called] <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>?'

children.translated_text: 'Of that, in terms of meaning, in this [treatise]' —

body.text: iti. tasyābhidharmasaṃjñakasya śāstrasyānantaroktatvāt grahaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Of that' refers to the treatise designated as <s>Abhidharma</s>, since it was just mentioned.

body.text: iti na vyañjanata iti. arthato 'yam
body.translated_text: meaning: not in terms of verbal expression. In terms of meaning, this

body.text: Tib. 8a
body.translated_text: is not complete. Therefore '<s>yathāpradhānam</s>' ('according to what is primary') — [this is]

body.text: na sākalyena. tasmād yathāpradhānam ity avyayībhāvaḥ. antarbhūtaḥ praviṣṭa iti. etac chāstraṃ madīyaṃ tasyārthasya kośasthānīyaṃ bhavati. kośasadṛśaṃ. etasminn arthe ṣaṣṭhītatpuruṣasamāsaḥ. abhidharmasya kośo 'bhidharmakośa iti. yatra hy asiḥ praviśati. sa tasya kośaḥ. atha vā so 'bhidharmo jñānaprasthānādir etasya madīyasya śāstrasyāśrayabhūtaḥ. tato hy ārṣād abhidharmād etan madīyaṃ śāstraṃ nirākṛṣṭam. arthata ity adhikṛtam. ataḥ sa evāsyābhidharmaḥ kośa iti. etasminn arthe bahuvrīhisamāsaḥ. abhidharmaḥ kośo 'syeti abhidarmakośaḥ. yato hy asir nirākṛṣyate. sa tasya kośa iti. etac chāstram abhidharmakośam iti. samudāyārtho 'py asyāvagamita iti sūcayati.
body.translated_text: an <s>avyayībhāva</s> [compound]. '[The meaning] has entered, has been included.' This treatise of mine serves as a receptacle (<s>kośa</s>) for that meaning — it resembles a sheath. In this sense, [it is] a genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound: 'the sheath of <s>abhidharma</s> is <s>abhidharmakośa</s>.' For that into which a sword enters is its sheath. Alternatively, that <s>abhidharma</s> — the <s>Jñānaprasthāna</s> and the rest — serves as the basis of this treatise of mine. For from that authoritative <s>abhidharma</s>, this treatise of mine was drawn out — 'in terms of meaning,' as stated. Therefore that [authoritative <s>abhidharma</s>] itself is the <s>kośa</s> (source-sheath) of this [treatise]. In this sense, [it is] a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound: 'that whose <s>abhidharma</s> is [its] <s>kośa</s> is <s>abhidharmakośa</s>.' For that from which a sword is drawn is its sheath. 'This treatise is <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>' — he indicates that the compound meaning too has been conveyed.

body.text: (I.3) kimarthaṃ punar abhidharmopadeśaḥ kiṃ prayojanam ity arthaḥ. saprayojanasya hi śāstrasya pratyāsaḥ sādhur bhavet. na niḥprayojanasya. kena cāyaṃ prathamata upadiṣṭaḥ. kena cāyam abhidharma ādito deśitaḥ. āptopadiṣṭasya hi śāstrasya pratyāso 'rharūpaḥ syād ity abhiprāyaḥ. prathamata iti viśeṣaṇam. bhadantakātyāyanīputrādīnāṃ piṇḍīkaraṇena paścād upadeśasya siddhatvāt. prathamata upadeśe hi vivādaḥ. yata iti vistaraḥ. yataḥ kāraṇāt. ācāryaḥ śāstrakāraḥ. abhidharmakośaṃ pratyāsaśāstraṃ vaktuṃ praṇetum ādriyate. ādaram karotīty arthaḥ. evaṃ kṛte praśnadvaye abhidharmaśāstrasya saprayojanatām āptopadeśatāṃ ca pradarśayann āha. 2.
body.translated_text: (I.3) Now, what is the purpose of the <s>abhidharma</s> teaching — what is its aim? This is the meaning. For the undertaking of a treatise with a purpose would be proper, not [that] of one without purpose. And by whom was this first taught? By whom was this <s>abhidharma</s> originally expounded? For the undertaking of a treatise taught by an authoritative person would be fitting — this is the intent. 'First' is a qualifier, since the later teaching through compilation by the venerable <s>Kātyāyanīputra</s> and others is already established. The dispute concerns who taught it first. 'Since' — the elaboration. 'Since' means 'for this reason.' The master, the author of the treatise, undertakes — makes an effort — to compose the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>, the treatise worthy of undertaking. In having done so, showing both that the <s>abhidharma</s> treatise has a purpose and that it was taught by an authoritative person, he says: [verse] 2.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: thus, the elaboration.

body.text: Tib. 8b
body.translated_text: Tib. 8b

body.text: yato
body.translated_text: 'Since' —

body.text: vinā dharmapravicayena rūpaṃ vedanā anityaṃ duḥkham ityevamākāreṇa.
body.translated_text: without the discernment of <s>dharmas</s> — form, feeling, [and so on, examined] in the aspect of 'impermanent,' 'suffering,' and so forth —

children.translated_text: 'there is no means for the subsiding of defilements' —

body.text: anya iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. sa eva tu kleśopaśamābhyupāya iti arthād āpannaṃ bhavati. tadyathā nāhāreṇa vinā prāṇasaṃdhāraṇopāya ity ukte sa evāhāraḥ prāṇasaṃdhāraṇopāya ity arthād āpannaṃ bhavati. tadvad etat. yadi kleśopaśamo
body.translated_text: 'other [than this]' is the completion of the sentence. That this [discernment] itself is the means for the subsiding of defilements is implicitly established. Just as when one says 'without food there is no means for the sustaining of life,' it is implicitly established that food itself is the means for sustaining life — so too here. If there were no subsiding of defilements,

body.text: na syāt kiṃ syād iti. ata āha.
body.translated_text: what would happen? Hence he says:

children.translated_text: 'And through defilements, the world wanders in the ocean of existence' —

body.text: iti. anena kleśopaśamasyāvaśyakartavyatāṃ darśayati. bhavaḥ saṃsāra ity ekārthaḥ. bhava evārṇavo bhavārṇavaḥ. majjanasthānasādharmyāt samudrakalpo bhavaḥ. etasmin bhavārṇave atra. pratyakṣīkṛtapañcopādānaskandhalakṣaṇavyatiriktabhavapratiṣedhārtham atragrahaṇam. atra loko bhramati tādātmyāvasthānāt. tādātmyavasthānato 'pi hi adhikaraṇanirdeśo dṛśyate. tadyathā anyapādapānupayogena palāśeṣv ārāmaḥ sthita iti. vṛttau tu hetvarthatāṃ tṛtīyāyāḥ sūcayatā hetumaṇṇicā hetvartha uktaḥ. kleśāś ca lokaṃ bhramayantīti. ata ity uddiṣṭahetupratyāmnāyaḥ. yata evam. ata uddiṣṭo 'bhidharma ity arthaḥ. dharmapravicayaḥ kleśopaśamopāyo nānyo dharma ity abhidharmopadeśakaḥ saṃbandha ity ata uktaṃ
body.translated_text: Thus. By this, he shows that the pacification of afflictions is something that must necessarily be done. '<s>Bhava</s>' and '<s>saṃsāra</s>' are synonymous. '<s>Bhava</s> itself is the <s>arṇava</s> (ocean)' — [this is] the compound <s>bhavārṇava</s> (ocean of existence). Existence is like an ocean, by analogy with a place of drowning. 'In this ocean of existence' — 'here' (<s>atra</s>). The word 'here' is for the purpose of negating existence as something apart from the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging) whose characteristics have been made directly perceptible. Here the world wanders, due to abiding in identity with [the aggregates]. For even from the condition of identity, a locative designation is seen — just as [one says] 'the park stands among the <s>palāśa</s> trees,' without [the park] being anything other than those trees. But in the <s>Vṛtti</s> (auto-commentary), by indicating that the third case has a causal meaning, the instrumental word is said to have a causal sense — 'because afflictions cause the world to wander.' 'Therefore' (<s>ataḥ</s>) is a resumption of the previously stated reason — 'since it is so.' 'Therefore the <s>Abhidharma</s> has been taught' — this is the meaning. '<s>Dharmapravicaya</s>' (analysis of <s>dharmas</s>) is the means of pacifying afflictions; there is no other <s>dharma</s> [that serves this purpose]' — this states the connection as the teacher of <s>Abhidharma</s>. Hence it is said:

body.text: iti. sa eva hetus taddhetuḥ. tasya tasmād vā
body.translated_text: — that very reason is 'that reason' (<s>taddhetuḥ</s>). 'Of that' or 'from that' —

body.text:
iti. tasya dharmapravicayasyārthe 'bhidharmopadeśahetuko dharmapravicayaḥ.
kathaṃ nāme dharmapravicayaḥ syād ity abhidharma upadiṣṭaḥ śāstrā buddhena. [Tib. 9a] ata eva. na hi vinābhidharmopadeśena śiṣyaḥ śakto dharmān pravicayitum iti.
body.translated_text:
— for the sake of that <s>dharmapravicaya</s>, [the] <s>Abhidharma</s> was taught as the cause of <s>dharmapravicaya</s>.
How indeed could <s>dharmapravicaya</s> be [achieved]? — for this purpose, the <s>Abhidharma</s> was taught by the Teacher, the <s>Buddha</s>. [Tib. 9a] For that very reason. For without the teaching of <s>Abhidharma</s>, a disciple is not able to analyze <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: iti vader niṣṭhāyāṃ kṛtasaṃprasāraṇasyaitad rūpam. na tu iṇa utpūrvas yārthāyogāt. udita ity uktaḥ upadiṣṭa ity ekārthaḥ.
body.translated_text: this is the form of the root <s>vad</s> (to speak) when <s>saṃprasāraṇa</s> [vowel replacement] has been applied at the completion [of the verbal action]. It is not <s>iṇ</s> with the preverb <s>ut</s>, because the meaning would not connect. '<s>Udita</s>' means 'spoken,' synonymous with 'taught' (<s>upadiṣṭa</s>).

body.text: kilaśabdaḥ parābhiprāyaṃ dyotayati. ābhidhārmikāṇām etan mataṃ. na tv asmākaṃ sautrāntikānām iti bhāvaḥ. śrūyante hy abhidharmaśāstrāṇāṃ kartāraḥ. tadyathā jñānaprasthānasya āryakātyāyanīputraḥ kartā. prakaraṇapādasya sthaviravasumitraḥ. vijñānakāyasya sthaviradevaśarmā. harmaskandhasya āryaśāriputraḥ. prajñaptiśāstrasya āryamaudgalyāyanaḥ. hātukāyasya pūrṇaḥ. saṃgītiparyāyasya mahākauṣṭhilaḥ. kaḥ sautrāntikārthaḥ. ye sūtraprāmāṇikā na śāstraprāmāṇikāḥ. te sautrāntikāḥ. yadi na śāstraprāmāṇikāḥ kathaṃ teṣāṃ piṭakatrayavyavasthā. sūtrapiṭako vinayapiṭako 'bhidharmapiṭaka iti. sūtre 'pi hy abhidharmapiṭakaḥ paṭhyate. traipiṭako bhikṣur iti naiṣa doṣaḥ. sūtraviśeṣā eva hy arthaviniścayādayo 'bhidharmasaṃjñāḥ
body.translated_text: The word <s>kila</s> indicates another's view. This is the position of the <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> (Abhidharma specialists), but not of us, the <s>Sautrāntikas</s> — this is the implication. For the authors of the <s>Abhidharma</s> treatises are known: the author of the <s>Jñānaprasthāna</s> is the Noble <s>Kātyāyanīputra</s>; of the <s>Prakaraṇapāda</s>, the Elder <s>Vasumitra</s>; of the <s>Vijñānakāya</s>, the Elder <s>Devaśarman</s>; of the <s>Dharmaskandha</s>, the Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>; of the <s>Prajñaptiśāstra</s>, the Noble <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>; of the <s>Dhātukāya</s>, <s>Pūrṇa</s>; of the <s>Saṃgītiparyāya</s>, <s>Mahākauṣṭhila</s>. What is the <s>Sautrāntika</s> position? Those who regard the <s>sūtras</s> as authoritative but not the [independent] treatises — they are <s>Sautrāntikas</s>. If they do not regard the treatises as authoritative, how is the threefold <s>Piṭaka</s>-classification established for them — <s>Sūtra-piṭaka</s>, <s>Vinaya-piṭaka</s>, <s>Abhidharma-piṭaka</s>? For even in the <s>sūtras</s>, the <s>Abhidharma-piṭaka</s> is recited — '[he is] a <s>traipiṭaka</s> (master of the three <s>Piṭakas</s>) monk.' There is no fault. For certain special <s>sūtras</s> themselves — the <s>Arthaviniścaya</s> and the like — bear the designation '<s>Abhidharma</s>'

body.text: yeṣu dharmalakṣaṇaṃ varṇyate. etadāśaṅkānivṛttyartham āhuḥ. sa tu prakīrṇa ukto bhagavateti vistaraḥ. yathā sthaviraharmatrātena udānā
body.translated_text: , those in which the characteristics of <s>dharmas</s> are described. To remove this doubt, they say: 'But that was spoken by the Blessed One in a scattered manner' — and so on in detail. Just as, by the Elder <s>Dharmatrāta</s>, the <s>Udānas</s> —

body.text: ityevamādikā vineyavaśāt tatratatra sūtra uktā vargīkṛtā ekasthīkṛtāḥ. evam abhidharmo 'pi dharmalakṣaṇopadeśasvarūpo vineyavaśāt tatratatra bhagavatoktaḥ [Tib. 9b] sthavirakātyāyanīputraprabhṛtibhir jñānaprasthānādiṣu piṇḍīkṛtya sthāpita iti āhur vaibhāṣikāḥ. vibhāṣayā dīvyanti caranti vā vaibhāṣikāḥ. vibhāṣāṃ vā vidanti vaibhāṣikāḥ. ukthādiprakṣepāṭ ṭhak. 3.
body.translated_text: and so forth, spoken in various <s>sūtras</s> according to [the needs of] those to be trained, were classified and collected into one place — so too the <s>Abhidharma</s>, whose essence is the teaching of the characteristics of <s>dharmas</s>, spoken by the Blessed One in various [places] according to [the needs of] those to be trained, [Tib. 9b] was compiled and established in the <s>Jñānaprasthāna</s> and other [texts] by the Elder <s>Kātyāyanīputra</s> and others — thus say the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>. '<s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>' — they shine (<s>dīvyanti</s>) through the <s>Vibhāṣā</s>, or they practice (<s>caranti</s>) through it. Or, they know (<s>vidanti</s>) the <s>Vibhāṣā</s>, [hence] '<s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>.' The suffix <s>ṭhak</s> [is applied] by analogy with the inclusion of <s>uktha</s> and similar [words]. 3.

children.translated_text: '<s>Dharmas</s> with outflows and without outflows' (<s>sāsravānāsravā dharmāḥ</s>) —

body.text: iti. saha āsravaiḥ sāsravāḥ. na santy āsravā eṣv iti anāsravāḥ. sāsravāś cānāsravāś ceti samāsaḥ. svasāmānyalakṣaṇadhāraṇād dharmaḥ. eṣa sarvadharmāṇāṃ samāsanirdeśa iti. etāvanto dharmā yad uta sāsravāś cānāsravāś ca. naitadvyatiriktā dharmāḥ santi. tasmād āha sarvadharmāṇām iti. samāsanirdeśa iti saṃkṣepanirdeśaḥ. vistaranirdeśas tu paścād ā śāstraparisamāpter bhaviṣyati anye 'pi samāsanirdeśāḥ santi. saṃskṛtā asaṃskṛtā rūpyarūpiṇaḥ sanidarśanānidarśanā ityevamādayaḥ. kimartham ayam eva samāsanirdeśa uktaḥ. kasminn ukte na paryanuyogaḥ. atha vā sāṃkleśikavyāvadānikapakṣapradarśanārthaṃ tadarthatvāc chāstrasya. tatpakṣadvayāvabodho hi saṃkleśapakṣam apahāya vyavadānapakṣāsevanān niḥśreyasāvāptir bhavet.
body.translated_text: 'Together with outflows' (<s>āsravas</s>) = '<s>sāsrava</s>.' 'There are no outflows in them' = '<s>anāsrava</s>.' '<s>Sāsrava</s> and <s>anāsrava</s>' — [this is] a compound. '<s>Dharma</s>' [means that which] holds (<s>dhāraṇa</s>) its own and general characteristics. 'This is the summary statement of all <s>dharmas</s>' — [i.e.,] <s>dharmas</s> are exactly this much, namely <s>sāsrava</s> and <s>anāsrava</s>; there are no <s>dharmas</s> beyond these. Therefore he says 'of all <s>dharmas</s>.' 'Summary statement' means 'concise statement.' The detailed statement will come later, up to the completion of the treatise. There are other summary statements too: 'conditioned and unconditioned,' 'material and immaterial,' 'with-demonstration and without-demonstration,' and so on. For what purpose is this very summary statement given? [Because] when this is stated, there is no further objection. Or alternatively, [it is] for the purpose of showing the sides of affliction and purification, since the treatise is for that purpose. For through understanding both sides — abandoning the side of affliction and cultivating the side of purification — the attainment of the highest good would be [achieved].

children.translated_text:
'Conditioned [dharmas], excluding the path,
are with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>)' —

body.text: iti saṃskṛtā eva nāsaṃskṛtāḥ. hetupratyayajanitā rūpādayaḥ saṃskṛtāḥ. kiṃ sarve. nety āha.
body.translated_text: [that is,] conditioned only, not unconditioned. Those produced from causes and conditions — forms and the rest — are conditioned. Are all [conditioned dharmas sāsrava]? No, he says:

body.text: mārgasatyena varjitāḥ. mārgasatyasya saṃskṛtatvāt prasaṅga ity ata evaṃ viśinaṣṭi. etad uktaṃ bvhavati. mārgasatyaṃ varjayitvā sarve saṃskṛtāḥ [Tib. 10a] sāsravā iti. kathaṃ punas te sāsravāḥ. yady āsravasaṃprayogāt kliṣṭā eva cittacaittāḥ sāsravāḥ syuḥ. nānye. athāsravasahotpādād ekasyāṃ saṃtatau samudācaratkleśasya sattvasya yathāsaṃbhavaṃ pañcopādānaskandhāḥ sāsravāḥ syuḥ. nāsamudācaratkleśasya. nāpi bāhyā dharmāḥ. athāsravāṇāṃ ye āśrayāḥ. te sāsravā iti. ṣaḍ evāyatanāni ādhyātmikāni sāsravāṇi syuḥ. athāsravāṇām ālambanāni sāsravāṇi. nirodhamārgasatyam api sāsravaṃ prāpnoti. ūrdhvā ca bhūmir ūrdhvabhūmyālambanair āsravaiḥ sāsravā syād ity ata āha.
body.translated_text: excluded by the truth of the path. Since the truth of the path is itself conditioned, [to avoid] the unwanted consequence [that the path too would be sāsrava], he makes this distinction. What has been said is this: excluding the truth of the path, all conditioned [dharmas] [Tib. 10a] are <s>sāsrava</s>. But how are they <s>sāsrava</s>? If [it is] through association with outflows, then only defiled mind and mental factors would be <s>sāsrava</s>, not others. If [it is] through co-arising with outflows, then in one continuum, for a being in whom afflictions are active, the five aggregates of clinging would be <s>sāsrava</s> as appropriate, but not for one in whom afflictions are not active, nor would external <s>dharmas</s> [be sāsrava]. If [it is that] those which are the bases (<s>āśraya</s>) of outflows are <s>sāsrava</s>, then only the six internal sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>) would be <s>sāsrava</s>. If the objects (<s>ālambana</s>) of outflows are <s>sāsrava</s>, then the truths of cessation and the path too would be <s>sāsrava</s>. And a higher plane, through outflows that take a higher plane as object, would be <s>sāsrava</s>. Therefore he says:

body.text: iti. tasmāt sāsravā iti pūrvam evādhyāhāryas tasmācchabdaḥ. anuśerata iti puṣṭiṃ labhanta ity arthaḥ. pratiṣṭhāṃ labhanta ity artho vā. puṣṭilābhe pratiṣṭhālābhe vā te rāgādayaḥ saṃtāyante. apare vyācakṣate. yathānuśete mamāyam āhāra iti pathyo 'nuguṇībhavatīty arthaḥ. tathā rāgādayo 'pi teṣu dharmeṣu anuśerate. anuguṇībhavantīty arthaḥ. rāgādyabhiṣyanditakarmanirvartitā hi sāsravā dharmāḥ.
body.translated_text: Therefore [they are] <s>sāsrava</s> — the word 'therefore' must be supplied from earlier. 'Lie dormant' (<s>anuśerate</s>) means 'gain nourishment' — this is the meaning. Or, 'gain a foothold' — this is the meaning. When they gain nourishment or a foothold, those [outflows such as] attachment and the rest proliferate. Others explain: Just as [one says] 'food lies dormant [i.e., agrees] with me' — meaning it is suitable, it becomes agreeable — so too attachment and the rest 'lie dormant' in those <s>dharmas</s>, meaning they become agreeable [to them]. For <s>sāsrava dharmas</s> are produced by <s>karma</s> that has been irrigated by attachment and the rest.

children.translated_text: 'The diversity of the world is born of <s>karma</s>' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. pratyayānuguṇyenānuśerate puṣṭiṃ labhanta ity anuśayāḥ. anuśerate anuguṇā vartante pratyayā eṣv iti vā [Tib. 10b] anuśayāḥ. anuśayanaṃ caiṣām ālambanataḥ saṃprayogato vā draṣṭavyaṃ. guṇamatis tv ācārya iha vyācaṣṭe. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ yat sarvadharmeṣv āsravāṇām ālambanībhavatsu saṃskṛtā eva mārgavarjitāḥ sāsravā ucyante iti. sarvadharmāḥ sāsravāṇām ālambanam ity anabhidhārmikīyam etat. ākāśapratisaṃkhyānirodhayor āsravānālambanatvāt. ṣaḍ eva hy anuśayā anāsravālambanāḥ paṭhyante. te ca nirodhamārgālambanā evā.
body.translated_text: so it is said. They are called <s>anuśayas</s> (dormant tendencies) because, being agreeable to conditions, they lie dormant [and] gain nourishment. Or, '<s>anuśayas</s>' [because] conditions that lie dormant — that are agreeable — in these [dharmas]. [Tib. 10b] And their dormancy should be understood as [operating] through objects or through association. But the <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Guṇamati</s> explains here [as follows]: What is the reason that, when all <s>dharmas</s> serve as objects of the outflows, only conditioned [dharmas] excluding the path are called '<s>sāsrava</s>'? 'All <s>dharmas</s> are objects of the outflows' — this is not in accordance with <s>Abhidharma</s>. For space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) are not objects of outflows. For only six <s>anuśayas</s> are listed as having non-<s>āsrava</s> objects. And those are precisely [the ones] having cessation and the path as objects.

children.text:
mithyādṛgvimatī tābhyāṃ yuktāvidyātha kevalā
nirodhamārgadṛggheyāḥ ṣaḍ anāsravagocarā
children.translated_text:
'Wrong view, doubt, and the ignorance connected with those two, and [ignorance] by itself —
those to be abandoned by insight into cessation and the path: [these] six have a non-outflow domain' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. tasmān na sulikhitam etad iti paśyāmaḥ. kāmam iti yady apīty arthaḥ. atha vā kāmam iti nipāto 'bhyupagamārthaḥ. abhyupagamyata eva nirodhamārgasatyālambanā api āsravā upajāyanta ity arthaḥ. tatra nirodhamārgasatyayoḥ. anuśayanirdeśa eva jñāpayiṣyāma iti.
body.translated_text: so it is said. Therefore we consider that this [assertion that all dharmas are objects of outflows] is not well-written. '<s>Kāmam</s>' means 'even if' — this is the meaning. Or, the particle <s>kāmam</s> has the sense of concession: it is conceded that outflows do arise that take the truths of cessation and the path as objects — this is the meaning. Regarding this, [he says:] 'We shall explain in the very exposition of dormant tendencies regarding the truths of cessation and the path.'

children.translated_text: 'Non-outflow [dharmas] and [dharmas of] the higher plane [are not sāsrava], because of non-acceptance and because of being the opponent' —

body.text: ity atra. yad dhi vastv ātmadṛṣṭitṛṣṇābhyāṃ svīkṛtaṃ bhavati. tatrānye 'py anuśayā anuśayitum utsahante. ārdra iva paṭe rajāṃsi saṃsthātuṃ. na caivam anāsravam. nāpy ūrdhvā bhūmiḥ. ato na tadālambanās teṣv anuśerate. vipakṣabhūtau ca nirvāṇamārgau tadālambanānāṃ kleśānām. ūrdhvā ca bhūmir adharāṇām. ato 'pi na teṣu pratiṣṭhāṃ labhante. tapta ivopale talāni pādānām iti. 4.
body.translated_text: In this regard: whatever object is appropriated by self-view (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) and craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), in that, other dormant tendencies too are able to lie dormant — just as dust settles on a damp cloth. But [this is] not so for the non-outflow [dharmas]. Nor for the higher plane. Therefore the outflows that take them as objects do not lie dormant in them. And <s>nirvāṇa</s> and the path are the opponents of the afflictions that take them as objects; and the higher plane [is the opponent] of the lower [afflictions]. For this reason too, [the outflows] do not gain a foothold in them — like the soles of feet on a heated stone. 4.

body.text: Tib. 11a
body.translated_text: Tib. 11a

body.text: anāsravā mārgasatyaṃ trividhaṃ capy asaṃskṛtam
body.translated_text: 'Non-outflow [dharmas are]: the truth of the path, and the threefold unconditioned' —

body.text: ity arthāpattisiddhatvāt na sūtrayitavyam etad iti evaṃ codye ācāryaguṇamatis tāvad āha. vaktavyam evedaṃ. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. dvividho hi mārgo laukiko lokottaraś ca. ato viśeṣārthaṃ punar abhidhīyate. ata eva cātra mārgasatyagrahaṇam.
body.translated_text: Since this is established by implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>), it need not be stated as a <s>sūtra</s> — in response to this objection, the <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Guṇamati</s> first says: This must indeed be stated. What is the reason? For the path is twofold — worldly and supramundane. Therefore, for the purpose of specifying [which], it is stated again. And for this very reason, the term 'truth of the path' is used here

body.text: prasiddhaṃ cārthāpattyā gamyate nāprasiddhaṃ. aprasiddhaṃ cāsaṃskṛtam iti. apare vyācakṣate. tṛtīyarāśyāśaṃkānivṛttyartham arthāpattisiddham apy etat punar ucyate. yathā hi tisro vedanā bhavanti. sukhā duḥkhā aduḥkhāsukhā ceti. evaṃ dharmā api saṃbhāvyeran. sāsravā anāsravāḥ sāsravānāsravāś ceti. atha vā naiva sāsravā nānāsravaś ceti. tena ye 'rthāpattyā nirastāḥ. kiṃ te 'nāsravā eva utāho sāsravānāsravā eva. āhosvin nobhayatheti saṃdihyeta. asti hi sāsravānāsravatvavikalpāvakāśaḥ. katham iti. vaibhāṣikaprakriyā tāvad
body.translated_text: . Moreover, what is well-known is understood by implication, not what is unknown. And the unconditioned is unknown. Others explain: For the purpose of removing the doubt about a third category, even though established by implication, this is stated again. Just as there are three types of feeling — pleasant, painful, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant — so too <s>dharmas</s> might be conceived as: <s>sāsrava</s>, <s>anāsrava</s>, and both <s>sāsrava</s> and <s>anāsrava</s>; or alternatively, neither <s>sāsrava</s> nor <s>anāsrava</s>. Then, regarding those [dharmas] that are eliminated by implication — are they exclusively <s>anāsrava</s>? Or are they both <s>sāsrava</s> and <s>anāsrava</s>? Or neither? — one might doubt. For there is scope for the distinction of being both <s>sāsrava</s> and <s>anāsrava</s>. How so? According to the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> system, to begin with —

children.translated_text: 'In two ways: [dharmas] with dormant tendencies are defiled; non-defiled [dharmas] are [sāsrava] through [the operation of] the dormant-tendency-producers' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. ye cakṣurādayo bāhyā vā rūpādayo 'kliṣṭāḥ. te 'nuśayānair evāsravaiḥ sāsravā nānanuśayānaiḥ. prahīṇais tair ananuśayānair āsravair na sāsravāḥ. aprahīṇais tv antataḥ parasaṃtānagatair api sāsravā [Tib. 11b] eveti. dārṣṭāntikaprakriyayāpi ca cakṣurādayo arhatsaṃtānagatā bāhyāś ca rūpādayo anāsravāḥ. āsravāṇām anāśrayatvāt. sāsravāś ca te āsravāṇām apratipakṣatvād iti. pāryāyikaṃ sāsravānāsravatvaṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ kalpyata iti saṃdehaḥ. tatsaṃdehavinivṛttyartham idam ucyate.
body.translated_text: so it is said. The eye and other [internal āyatanas], or external forms and the like, that are non-defiled — they are <s>sāsrava</s> through those very outflows that are their dormant-tendency-producers, not through [outflows] that are not dormant-tendency-producers. When those [dormant-tendency-producing outflows] are abandoned, [the dharmas] are not <s>sāsrava</s> through outflows that are not dormant-tendency-producers. But when [those outflows are] not abandoned — even if they exist in another's continuum — [the dharmas] are <s>sāsrava</s>. [Tib. 11b] And according to the <s>Dārṣṭāntika</s> system too, the eye and other [internal āyatanas] belonging to an <s>Arhat</s>'s continuum, and external forms and the like, are <s>anāsrava</s> — because they are not the basis of outflows. And they are <s>sāsrava</s> — because they are not the opponent of outflows. Thus, a figurative (<s>pāryāyika</s>) state of being both <s>sāsrava</s> and <s>anāsrava</s> can be conceived for the eye and the rest — hence the doubt. For the purpose of removing that doubt, this is stated:

children.translated_text: 'Non-outflow [dharmas are]: the truth of the path, and the threefold unconditioned' —

body.text: iti. niṣparyāyam anāsravā evāmī na sāsravā yathoktam iti punarvacanam. te tarhy arhaccakṣurādayo vaibhāṣikaiḥ kva pakṣe nikṣeptavyāḥ. kiṃ sāsravapakṣe athānāsravapakṣe iti. sāsravapakṣa iti ta āhuḥ kathaṃ prahīṇair āsravais te sāsravā vyavasthāpyante. yeṣv āsravā anuśerate anuśayitavanto anuśayiṣyante vā. te sāsravāḥ. traikālikārthavivakṣayāpi hi loke vartamānākāle prayogo dṛśyate. yaḥ prajā rakṣati. sa rājeti. yo 'pi rakṣitavān yo 'pi rakṣiṣyati. sa cāpi rājeti gamyata eveti. ata evaṃ vyākhyāyate. atha vā yady api te prahīṇair āsravair na sāsravāḥ. aprahīṇais tu aparimitair āsravair antataḥ parasaṃtānagatair api sāsravā eva bhavanti. nanu ca samāsanirdeśād eva
body.translated_text: These are exclusively <s>anāsrava</s>, not <s>sāsrava</s>, as has been stated — [this is] the restatement. Then, in which category should the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> place the eye, etc. of an <s>Arhat</s> — in the <s>sāsrava</s> category or the <s>anāsrava</s> category? In the <s>sāsrava</s> category — they say. How are they established as <s>sāsrava</s> through outflows that have been abandoned? Those in which outflows lie dormant, have lain dormant, or will lie dormant — those are <s>sāsrava</s>. For we see in the world that usage in the present tense [extends] even to three-temporal meaning — 'He who protects the people is a king' — and one who has protected or will protect is also understood to be a king. Therefore it is explained thus. Or alternatively, even if they are not <s>sāsrava</s> through the abandoned outflows, they are <s>sāsrava</s> through the unlimited outflows that have not been abandoned — even those belonging to another's continuum.
