body.text: iti tṛtīyarāśyaprasaṃgaḥ. [Tib. 12a] na. tatraikaśeṣanirdeśasaṃbhavāt. sāsravāś cānāsravāś ca sāsravānāsravāś ceti. sāsravānāsravā iti ekaśeṣaḥ. asarūpāṇām apy ekaśeṣa iṣyate. guṇo yaṅlukor iti yathā. apare punar āhuḥ. arthāpattyā siddham evaitat. spaṣṭīkaraṇārthaṃ tu prapaṃca ucyate. tadyathā viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyeṇa bahulam ity anenaiva sarvasiddham. pūrvakālaikasarvajaratpurāṇanavakevalāḥ samānādhikaraṇenetyevamādiprapaṃca ucyate. tadvad
body.translated_text: Thus, there is no [unwanted] entailment of a third category. [Tib. 12a] No — because there the <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (single-remainder) construction is possible: '<s>sāsravāś ca anāsravāś ca</s> = <s>sāsravānāsravāḥ</s>' (with-outflows and without-outflows). The <s>ekaśeṣa</s> is accepted even for dissimilar [words], as [in the grammatical rule] '<s>guṇo yaṅlukoḥ</s>.' Others however say: This is already established by presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>). The elaboration is stated merely for clarification. Just as [the rule] 'the qualifier [agrees] with the qualified, generally' establishes everything, yet elaborations are stated such as 'former, simultaneous, single, old, ancient, new, sole — with a co-referent [term].' So too

body.text: etat. katamaṃ trividham asaṃskṛtam ity apratītatvāt pṛcchati. trividhagrahaṇaṃ iyattāvadhāraṇārtham. santi hi kecid ekam evāsaṃskṛtaṃ nirvāṇam ity āhur yathā vātsīputrīyāḥ. paramāṇvādayo bahavo asaṃskṛtā iti vaiśesikāḥ. tanmatapratiṣedhārtham iyattāvadhāraṇam. katamau dvāv iti. pratisaṃkhyāpratisaṃkhyānirodhāv eva pṛcchati. nākāśam. ākāśasya loke prasiddhatvāt.
body.translated_text: this [elaboration]. 'What is the threefold unconditioned?' — he asks because it is not [yet] understood. The use of 'threefold' is for the purpose of determining the exact number. For some say there is only one unconditioned, namely <s>nirvāṇa</s> — like the <s>Vātsīputrīyas</s>. And the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> [say] that atoms and the like are many unconditioned [entities]. The determination of exact number is for the purpose of refuting those views. 'What are the two?' — he asks specifically about the cessation through analytical and non-analytical knowledge. Not about space (<s>ākāśa</s>), because space is well-known in the world.

body.text: iti tatreti nirdhāraṇe. vākyopanyāse vā. avakāśaṃ dadātīti ākāśam iti nirvacanam. bhṛśam asyāntaḥ kāśante bhāvā ity ākāśam ity apare.
body.translated_text: 'therein' is used in the sense of determination; or in the sense of introducing a statement. 'It gives room' — therefore [it is called] <s>ākāśa</s> (space) — this is the etymological derivation. Others [say]: 'In it, things shine (<s>kāśante</s>) intensely (<s>bhṛśam</s>)' — therefore [it is called] <s>ākāśa</s>.

body.text: anāvaraṇam. kartṛsādhanaṃ karmasādhanaṃ vā. yo dharmo 'nyān dharmān nāvṛṇoti anyair vā nāvriyate. tad anāvaraṇasvabhāvaṃ ākāśam. tad apratyakṣaviṣayatvāt anyadharmānāvṛtyā anumīyate. na tv āvaraṇābhāvamātram. ata eva ca vyākhyāyate. yatra rūpasya gatir iti. yadi yan nāvṛṇoti nāvriyate vā. tad ākāśam. apratighā api cittādayaḥ saṃskārās tathaiveti [Tib. 12b] ākāśaṃ prāpnuvanti. na prāpnuvanti. pareṣām āvaraṇabhāvāt. ṛddhimanto hi cittacaittabalena pareṣāṃ gatiṃ cittādīnāṃ vibadhnanti. pratisaṃkhyā-apratisaṃkhyānirodhau tarhi avibandhakatvād ākāśaṃ prāpnutaḥ. na. tayoḥ saṃyogadravyānutpattidharmāṇāṃ saṃyogaprāptiniyatarodhabhūtatvena utpattivighnarodhabhūtatvena cāvaraṇabhūtatvāt. atha vā yasyānāvaraṇam eva lakṣaṇaṃ nānyal lakṣaṇaṃ. tad ākāśaṃ. tayoś cānyalakṣaṇam astīti na tau nirodhāv ākāśaṃ prāpnutaḥ. asarvagataṃ tarhy ākāśaṃ anityaṃ vā prāpnoti. āvaraṇābhāve bhāvāt. tadbhāve cābhāvāt. kuḍyādiṣu hy anyasya rūpasyāvaraṇaṃ bhavatīti. atrākāśalakṣaṇābhāvāt ākāśabhāvaprasaṃgaḥ. kuḍyādyapagame ca punas tad bhavatīti anityaṃ prāpnoti. nānityaṃ prāpnoti. tatrāpi kuḍyādyavakāśadānād ākāśam asty eva. yadi hi tatrākāśaṃ na syāt tasyaiva kuḍyāder anavakāśatvād avasthānaṃ na syāt. yat tu tatra rūpāntarasyānavasthānam. tat kuḍyādyāvaraṇān nākāśābhāvāt. uktaṃ hi bhagavatā. pṛthivī bho gautama kutra pratiṣṭhitā. pṛthivī brāhmaṇa apmaṇḍale pratiṣṭhitā. apmaṇḍalaṃ bho gautama kva pratiṣṭhitaṃ. vāyau pratiṣṭhitam. vāyur bho gautama kva pratiṣṭhitaḥ. ākāśe pratiṣṭhitaḥ. ākāśaṃ bho gautama kutra pratiṣṭhitam. atisarasi mahābrāhmaṇātisarasi mahābrāhmaṇa. ākāśaṃ brāhmaṇāpratiṣṭhitaṃ anālambanam iti vistaraḥ. tasmād asty ākāśam iti vaibhāṣikāḥ. 5.
body.translated_text: means non-covering (<s>anāvaraṇa</s>). It can be taken either as an agent-derivation or an object-derivation. That <s>dharma</s> which neither obstructs other <s>dharmas</s> nor is obstructed by others — that which has the intrinsic nature of non-obstruction is space. Since it is not an object of direct perception, it is inferred through [its property of] non-obstruction of other <s>dharmas</s>. But it is not merely the absence of obstruction. And for this reason it is explained: 'Where form has passage.' If whatever neither obstructs nor is obstructed is space, then non-resistant (<s>apratigha</s>) conditioned things like mind, etc. would also [Tib. 12b] turn out to be space. They do not [qualify as space], because of the existence of obstruction for others [by them]. For those with supernatural powers obstruct the movement of others' minds, etc., through the power of mind and mental factors. [Objection:] Then analytical cessation and non-analytical cessation, since they do not obstruct, should turn out to be space. [Reply:] No, because those two have the nature of obstruction — being invariably the blocking of the connection-attainment of the substances of connection, and being the blocking of the arising [of dharmas that would otherwise arise]. Alternatively, that whose characteristic is solely non-obstruction, with no other characteristic, is space. And since those two cessations have another characteristic, they do not turn out to be space. [Objection:] Then space turns out to be either non-omnipresent or impermanent — existing where there is absence of obstruction, and not existing where obstruction is present. For in walls, etc., there is obstruction of other form — so space's characteristic would be absent there, entailing the absence of space. And when the wall, etc. is removed, it [space] would come into being again — so it turns out to be impermanent. [Reply:] It does not turn out to be impermanent, because even there, in the wall, etc., space exists, since it gives room to the wall, etc. For if space did not exist there, the wall itself, having no room, could not be situated. But the fact that other forms cannot be situated there is due to the obstruction by the wall, etc., not due to the absence of space. For the Blessed One said: 'O <s>Gautama</s>, where is the earth established? O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the earth is established on the water-sphere. O <s>Gautama</s>, where is the water-sphere established? It is established on the wind. O <s>Gautama</s>, where is the wind established? It is established in space. O <s>Gautama</s>, where is space established? You go too far, great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, you go too far, great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! Space, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is unestablished, without support' — and so on in detail. Therefore, space exists — so say the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>. [Sūtra] 5.

body.text: Tib. 13a
body.translated_text: Tib. 13a

body.text: yo visaṃyoga iti viśeṣeṇānityatānirodho 'pratisaṃkhyānirodhaś ca vyudastau bhavataḥ. na hi visaṃyogalakṣaṇau tau nirodhau. visaṃyuktir visaṃyogaḥ kleśavisaṃyuktilakṣaṇaḥ. saṃyogaprāptiniyatarodhabhūto vā yo dharmaḥ. sa pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. duḥkḥādīnām āryasatyānām iti viśeṣaṇaparisatyādyākārā. kiṃ tarhi. uttarādharabhūmiśāntādyudārādyākārā. prajñāviśeṣa iti. viśeṣagrahaṇaṃ kleśaprahāṇānantaryamārgaprajñāgrahaṇārtham. tena prajñāviśeṣeṇa prāpyo nirodha iti pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. madhyapadalopaṃ kṛtveti. śākapārthivādīnām upasaṃkhyānam. śākapriyāḥ pārthivāḥ śākapārthivā itīṣṭyā madhyapadalopaḥ. yadi pratisaṃkhyā anāsravaiva prajñā gṛhyeta laukikamārgaprāpyo nirodho na gṛhīta ity avyāpilakṣaṇaṃ prāpnoti. nāvyāpi. sarvo hi traidhātukasāsravavastunirodho 'nāsravayā prāpyate. na sa nirodho 'sti. yo laukikyaiva prajñayā prāpyate nānāsravayeti. kiṃ laukikyā prajñayā prayojanam. yo hi laukikena mārgeṇa kaścin nirodhaḥ prāpyate. sa eva punar lokottareṇa prāpyata eveti. lokottaraiva prajñā tatra na laukikī. dravyasan pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ satyacatuṣṭayanirdeśanirdiṣṭatvān [Tib. 13b] mārgasatyavad iti vaibhāṣikāḥ.
body.translated_text: 'That which is disjunction' — by this specification, the cessation of impermanence (<s>anityatā-nirodha</s>) and non-analytical cessation are excluded. For those two cessations do not have the characteristic of disjunction. Disjunction (<s>visaṃyoga</s>) is dis-junction, characterized by dis-junction from afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). Or, that <s>dharma</s> which is invariably the blocking of the attainment of connection — that is analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s>). 'Of the noble truths such as suffering, etc.' — the qualification does not [refer to] aspects such as the truth of suffering. Rather, [it refers to] aspects such as 'superior/inferior ground,' 'peaceful/gross,' etc. 'Distinguished insight' (<s>prajñā-viśeṣa</s>) — the word 'distinguished' is for the purpose of including [specifically] the insight of the uninterrupted path that abandons afflictions. The cessation attained through that distinguished insight is analytical cessation. '[This is formed] by elision of the middle word' (<s>madhyapadalopa</s>) — this is to be enumerated among [compounds] like <s>śākapārthiva</s>. '<s>Śākapārthiva</s>' means kings fond of vegetables — the middle word is elided by convention. If analytical knowledge were taken as exclusively supramundane (<s>anāsrava</s>) insight, then the cessation attained by the mundane path would not be included, resulting in an under-inclusive definition. [Reply:] It is not under-inclusive. For every cessation of defiled (<s>sāsrava</s>) conditioned things of the three realms is attained by supramundane [insight]. There is no cessation that is attained only by mundane insight and not by supramundane [insight]. Then what is the purpose of mundane insight? For whatever cessation is attained by the mundane path, that very [cessation] is subsequently attained by the supramundane path as well. Thus the supramundane insight alone [is operative] there, not the mundane. Analytical cessation is a real entity (<s>dravyasat</s>), because it is taught in the exposition of the four truths, [Tib. 13b] like the truth of the path — so say the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>.

body.text: iti nānety arthaḥ. yāvanti hi saṃyogadravyāṇīti. saṃyuktiḥ saṃyogaḥ. saṃyogāya dravyāṇi saṃyogadravyāṇi. saṃprayujyante teṣv iti vā saṃyogāḥ. saṃyogāś ca te dravyāṇi ceti saṃyogadravyāṇi. sāsravadravyāṇīti yāvad uktaṃ bhavati. sāsravaṃ hi dravyaṃ stambhasthānīyaṃ saṃprayojanaṃ rajjusthānīyaṃ pudgalas tu balīvardasthānīya iti bhagavatoktam. anyatheti yady eka ity arthaḥ. sarvakleśanirodhasākṣātkriyeti. samudayādidarśanabhāvanāheyakleśanirodhaprāptir ity arthaḥ. śeṣapratipakṣabhāvanā vaiyarthyam iti. śeṣakleśasamudayādidarśanabhāvanāprahātavyātmakapratipakṣamārgotpādanaṃ niṣprayojanam ity arthaḥ. yat tarhy uktaṃ asabhāgo nirodha iti. kvoktaṃ. sūtre. pūrvabhartrā viśākhena gṛhapatinā pṛṣṭayā harmadinnayā bhikṣuṇyoktaṃ. kiṃ sabhāga ārye nirodhaḥ. asabhāga āyuṣman viśākheti. apratisadṛśo nirodha ity artham abhisamīkṣya pṛcchati. asya ko 'rtha iti. bahutve hi sati pratisadṛśo 'nyo bhaved iti parasyabhiprāyaḥ. nāsya kaścit sabhāgahetur iti. sabhāgahetuḥ sabhāga ity eko 'rtho hetuśabdalopāt. dṛśyante hi padeṣu padaikadeśān prayuṃjānā vākyeṣu ca vākyaikadeśān. tadyathā satyabhāmā
body.translated_text: means 'variously.' 'As many as are the substances of connection' — conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is [the same as] being conjoined (<s>saṃyukti</s>); the substances for conjunction are 'connection-substances'; or 'connections' are [things] with which [defilements] are conjoined, and those are substances, hence 'connection-substances.' What is meant is: 'defiled substances' (<s>sāsrava-dravyāṇi</s>). For the Blessed One said: a defiled substance is like a post, the connecting [defilement] is like a rope, and the person is like a bull. 'Otherwise' means 'if it were one.' 'Direct realization of the cessation of all afflictions' — the meaning is: attainment of the cessation of afflictions to be abandoned by seeing the truth of origination, etc. and by meditation. 'The cultivation of the remaining antidotes would be purposeless' — the meaning is: the production of the antidote paths — those belonging to the nature of [what is] to be abandoned by seeing the truth of origination, etc. and by meditation — for the remaining afflictions would be without purpose. As for what was said, 'cessation is dissimilar' — where was this said? In a <s>sūtra</s>. The nun <s>Dharmadinnā</s>, questioned by the householder <s>Viśākha</s>, her former husband, said: 'Is cessation similar, Noble Lady?' 'It is dissimilar, Venerable <s>Viśākha</s>.' He asks, considering the meaning to be: 'cessation is without counterpart.' What is its meaning? For if [cessation] were multiple, there could be another similar [cessation] — this is the other's intent. 'It has no similar cause' — '<s>sabhāgahetu</s> (similar cause) = <s>sabhāga</s> (similar)' — this is one meaning, from the ellipsis of the word 'cause.' For indeed, people are seen using parts of words for [whole] words and parts of sentences for [whole] sentences. Just as '<s>Satyabhāmā</s>'

body.text: bhāmā evadatto attaḥ praviśa piṇḍīṃ praviśa tarpaṇam [Tib. 14a] iti. nityaḥ khalu pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. tasya kiṃ sabhāgahetunā prayojanam iti. asabhāgahetur asabhāgaḥ. nāsti sabhāgo 'syeti asabhāgo bahuvrīhisamāsaḥ. nāsau kasyacid iti. nāsau pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ kasyacid anyasya dharmasya sabhāgahetur iti adhikṛtam. kiṃ kāraṇam. saṃskṛta eveti sabhāgahetur iṣyate. tatra na sabhāgo asabhāga iti tatpuruṣaḥ. na tu nāsya kaścid sabhāgo 'stīti. na tv asya nirodhasya kaścid anyo nirodhaḥ sadṛśo na bhavatīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: [is shortened to] '<s>Bhāmā</s>,' '<s>Devadatta</s>' to '<s>Datta</s>,' 'enter the [begging-]round' to 'enter the offering' [Tib. 14a], and so on. Analytical cessation is indeed permanent; what use would it have for a similar cause? 'Dissimilar cause = dissimilar' — '<s>asabhāga</s>' is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound: 'that which has no similar [thing].' 'It [is not a similar cause] of anything' — this analytical cessation is not a similar cause of any other <s>dharma</s>. This is the subject under discussion. What is the reason? 'Because a similar cause is accepted only for conditioned [dharmas].' There, '<s>na sabhāga</s> = <s>asabhāga</s>' is a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> [compound]. But it does not [mean] 'there is nothing similar to this cessation' — it does not mean that there is no other cessation resembling this cessation.

children.translated_text: 'Another cessation — the complete obstruction of arising — [is attained] without analytical [knowledge].'

body.text: anāgatānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ utpādasyātyantaṃ vighnaḥ atyantavighnaḥ atyantaniyatarodhaḥ.
body.translated_text: The complete obstruction of the arising of future <s>dharmas</s> — complete obstruction means an absolutely determined blocking.

body.text: iti apratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. sa hi pratisaṃkhyānirodhāt anantaroktāt anyaḥ.
body.translated_text: means non-analytical cessation (<s>apratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s>). For it is other than the analytical cessation just mentioned.

body.text: prasajyapratiṣedhe ayam akāraḥ. na pratisaṃkhyayā prāpya ity arthaḥ. atha vā paryudāse. pratisaṃkhyāyā yad anyat pratyayavaikalyam. sāpratisaṃkhyā. tayā prāpyo nirodho 'pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. madhyapadalopāt. ayuktam etat. pratyayavaikalyaṃ hy abhāvaḥ. katham abhāvena sa nirodhaḥ prāpyata iti. aupacārikatvād adoṣaḥ. atha vāpratisaṃkhyānirodha iti na pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. apratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ pratisaṃkhyānirodhād anyatvamātram evocyate. na tu pratyayavaikalyasya vyāpāra iti. utpādagrahaṇam anityatānirodhavyudāsārthaṃ. [Tib. 14b] anityatānirodho dharmasthiter atyantavighno na dharmotpādasya. atyantagrahaṇaṃ asaṃjñinirodhasamāpattyāsaṃjñikavyudāsārthaṃ. tāni hy anāgatānāṃ cittacaittānām utpādavighnaḥ. na tv atyantaṃ tāvatkālikatvāt tadvighnabhāvasya. yathaikarūpavyāsaktacakṣurmanasa iti vistaraḥ yathety udāharaṇakathanaṃ. yathaikasmin nīlarūpe vyāsaktaṃ cakṣur manaś ca yasya. sa ekarūpavyāsaktacakṣurmanāḥ. tasya. yāni rūpāntarāṇi gṛhyamāṇāt nīlād anyāni nīlāntarapītalohitāvadātādīni varṇarūpāṇi saṃsthānarūpāṇi ca śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāni ca sarvāṇi atyayante pratyutpannam adhvānaṃ atikrāmanti. atītam adhvānaṃ pratipadyanta ity arthaḥ. tadālambanair iti. tāni nīlantarādīni anantaroktāni ālambanāni eṣāṃ. te tadālambanāh. ke. paṃca vijñānakāyāḥ. taiḥ. na ṣakyam utpattum iti bhāvasādhanam etat. na hi te samarthā iti vistaraḥ. na hi te paṃca vijñānakāyā atītaṃ viṣayaṃ svālambanam api śaktā grahītuṃ. vartamānālambanatvāt paṃcānāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ. athānyad idānīṃ nīlantarādikaṃ vartamānam
body.translated_text: This <s>a</s>-prefix is a <s>prasajya-pratiṣedha</s> (simple negation). The meaning is: 'not attained through analytical [knowledge].' Alternatively, [it is] a <s>paryudāsa</s> (implicative negation): that which is other than analytical knowledge — namely, the deficiency of conditions — is non-analysis (<s>apratisaṃkhyā</s>); the cessation attained through that is 'non-analytical cessation' — [formed] by middle-word elision. [Objection:] This is improper, for the deficiency of conditions is a non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>); how can that cessation be attained through a non-existence? [Reply:] There is no fault, because of its figurative usage. Alternatively, '<s>apratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s>' means 'not analytical cessation' — only the mere otherness from analytical cessation is expressed; the functioning of the deficiency of conditions [is not implied]. The use of the word 'arising' is for the purpose of excluding the cessation of impermanence (<s>anityatā-nirodha</s>). [Tib. 14b] For the cessation of impermanence is the complete obstruction of the persistence of <s>dharmas</s>, not of the arising of <s>dharmas</s>. The use of 'complete' (<s>atyanta</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the cessation of unconscious perception (<s>asaṃjñi-nirodha-samāpatti</s>) and the unconscious state (<s>āsaṃjñika</s>). For those are an obstruction to the arising of future minds and mental factors, but not a complete [obstruction], because their obstruction is temporary. 'Just as when the eye and mind are engaged with one form' — and so on in detail. 'Just as' introduces an illustration. Just as one whose eye and mind are engaged with a single blue form — for him, the other forms that are different from the blue being perceived — other blues, yellows, reds, whites, and other color-forms and shape-forms, as well as sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles — all pass beyond the present time-period, that is, they enter the past time-period. 'With those [forms] as objects' — those other [things] just mentioned, such as other blues, etc., are the objects of these [consciousnesses]; those [consciousnesses] have those as objects. Which ones? The five consciousness-groups. They [= the five consciousness-groups] — 'cannot arise' — this is an expression of [the impossibility of their] coming into being. 'For they are not capable' — and so on in detail. For those five consciousness-groups are not able to apprehend a past object, even their own object, because the five consciousness-groups have [only] present objects. Now, if another present [form] — another blue, etc. —

body.text: ālambya kasmān notpadyante. na śakyam evaṃ bhavituṃ. sarvadharmāṇāṃ catuṣke niyatatvāt. hetau phala āśraya ālambane ceti. yasya vijñānasya yad ālambanaṃ. tad eva [Tib. 15a] tasyālambanaṃ bhavet. bhaven nānyad iti. ālmbanapratyayavaikalyāt te paṃca vijñānakāyā na punar utpadyante. ata āha. sa teṣāṃ apratisaṃkhyānirodha iti vistaraḥ. teṣāṃ paṃcānāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ pratyayavaikalyāt prāpyate ālambanapratyayavaikalyāt. caturbhir eva hi pratyayair hetusamanantarālambanādhipatipratyayaiś cittacaittā utpadyamānā utpadyante. teṣām anyataravaikalye 'pi anutpattiḥ. samanantarapratyayavaikalyād ity apare. samanantarapratyayo hi tadānīṃ cittacaittalakṣaṇa ekasyaiva tasya nīlavijñānasya utpattāv avakāśaṃ dadāti. netareṣāṃ nīlantarādivijñānānāṃ. yugapadvijñānotpattyasambhavāt. udāharaṇamātraṃ caitat. evaṃ kṣāntilābhyādīnāṃ paṃcānām api āpāyikānāṃ anāgatānāṃ skandhānāṃ tadutpattiviruddhapratyayasaṃmukhībhāvena pratyayavaikalyāt apratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ prāpyate ity udāhāryaṃ. apratisaṃkhyānirodham eva cābhisaṃdhāya srotaāpannaṃ pudgalam adhikṛtyoktaṃ bhagavatā niruddhā asya narakās tiryaṃcaḥ pretā iti. tad evaṃjātīyakānāṃ anāgatānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratyayavaikalyāt. pratisaṃkhyām antareṇa utpādasya niyatarodhabhūto yo dharmaḥ. so 'pratisaṃkhyānirodha ity ucyate. na hi pratyayavaikalyamātrād atyantaṃ tadanutpattir upapadyate. punas tajjātīyapratyayasāṃnidhye tadutpattiprasaṃgāt. ko hi tadā tadutpattau vibandhaḥ syād iti vaibhāṣikāḥ. [Tib. 15b] catuṣkoṭikaṃ cātreti vistaraḥ. atra pratisaṃkhyāpratisaṃkhyānirodhalakṣaṇanirdeśe catuṣkoṭikaṃ catuṣprakāraṃ praśnavisarjanaṃ. kim arthaṃ. vyutpādanārthaṃ. tadyathātītapratyutpannotpattidharmāṇāṃ sāsravāṇāṃ iti. sāsravatvāt pratisaṃkhyānirodha eva labhyate. atītapratyutpannānām utpādasya kṛtatvāt. utpattidharmāṇāṃ cāvaśyaṃbhāvāt. nāpratisaṃkhyānirodho labhyate. utpādātyantavighnalakṣaṇo hy apratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. tadyathānutpattidharmāṇāṃ anāsravasaṃskṛtānām iti. atyantavighnitotpādatvād eṣām anutpattidharmatvaṃ. ataś ca teṣām apratisaṃkhyānirodho labhyate. tadyathā ṣaḍbhūmikānām anāgamyadhyānāntaradhyānabhūmikānāṃ śraddhānusārimārgāṇām ekasmiṃ saṃmukhībhūte śeṣāṇāṃ paṃcānām apratisaṃkhyānirodho labhyate. na tu pratisaṃkhyānirodho 'nāsravatvāt. na hi nirdoṣaṃ prahāṇārhaṃ bhavati. anutpattidharmagrahaṇaṃ atītapratyutpannotpattidharmanirāsārthaṃ. anāsravagrahaṇaṃ sāsravanirāsārthaṃ. saṃskṛtagrahaṇam asaṃskṛtanirāsārthaṃ. asaṃskṛtam api hi svabhāvato [Tib. 16a] 'nutpattidharmakaṃ. atas tatprasaṃgo mā bhūd iti tad viśeṣaṇaṃ. keṣāṃcid
body.translated_text: relying on [that object], why do they not arise? It cannot be so, because all <s>dharmas</s> are determined in the fourfold [system of conditions] — namely, in cause, in result, in support, and in object-condition. Whatever object belongs to a given consciousness, that alone would be its object-condition, and nothing else. Due to the deficiency of the object-condition (<s>ālambanapratyaya</s>), those five consciousness-groups do not arise again. Therefore he said: 'That is the cessation through non-deliberation (<s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) of those' — in detail. Of those five consciousness-groups, it is obtained due to the deficiency of conditions — [specifically] the deficiency of the object-condition. For mind and mental factors arise when arising through four conditions only — cause-condition, immediately-antecedent condition, object-condition, and dominant condition. Even when one of these is deficient, there is non-arising. 'Due to deficiency of the immediately-antecedent condition' — according to others. For the immediately-antecedent condition at that time gives room for the arising of only that single blue-cognition, not for the arising of other cognitions such as blue-[cognition] and so forth. Because the simultaneous arising of [multiple] cognitions is impossible. And this is merely an illustration. Likewise, for those who have obtained <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance) and so forth — for the five kinds of future <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) pertaining to the lower realms — <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (cessation through non-deliberation) is obtained due to the deficiency of conditions through the confrontation with conditions opposed to their arising — this should be illustrated. And it is with reference to <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> alone that the Blessed One said, regarding the <s>Srotaāpanna</s> (stream-enterer) individual: 'Destroyed for him are the hells, animal [realms], and hungry ghost [realms].' Thus, for such <s>dharmas</s> belonging to the future, due to the deficiency of conditions — that <s>dharma</s> which, apart from deliberation (<s>pratisaṃkhyā</s>), constitutes a definite obstruction to arising — that is called <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>. For the permanent non-arising of those [dharmas] cannot be established merely from the deficiency of conditions, since when conditions of that same type are again present, there would be the unwanted consequence of their arising. For what obstruction to their arising would there be then? — thus [say] the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>. [Tib. 15b] 'And here the fourfold classification' — in detail. Here, in the exposition defining <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> and <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>, the fourfold classification is a fourfold question-and-answer. For what purpose? For the purpose of elucidation. 'Such as past, present, and those with the nature of arising, which are with-outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>)' — because of being with-outflows, only <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is obtained. Because the arising of the past and present has already occurred, and because the arising of those with the nature of arising is inevitable, <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is not obtained. For <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is characterized by the permanent obstruction of arising. 'Such as those with the nature of non-arising, which are without-outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>) and conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>)' — because the arising of these has been permanently obstructed, they have the nature of non-arising. Therefore, for them, <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is obtained. For example, of the six-level [dharmas] — those belonging to the <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary access), the inter-<s>dhyāna</s>, and the <s>dhyāna</s> levels — when one of the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> (faith-follower) paths has come to confrontation, for the remaining five, <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is obtained. But <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is not, because they are without-outflows. For what is faultless is not fit for abandonment. The term 'with the nature of non-arising' is for the purpose of excluding the past, present, and those with the nature of arising. The term 'without-outflows' is for the purpose of excluding those with-outflows. The term 'conditioned' is for the purpose of excluding the unconditioned. For the unconditioned too is by its own nature [Tib. 16a] with the nature of non-arising. To prevent the unwanted extension to that, it is a qualifier. According to some

body.text:
evaṃ pāṭhaḥ. tadyathā anutpattidharmāṇām anāsravāṇām iti.
teṣāṃ katham asaṃskṛtānāṃ grahaṇaprasaṃgo na bhavati. yeṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratisaṃkhyānirodho 'pratisaṃkhyānirodhaś ca saṃbhavati. teṣām adhikāraḥ. na cāsaṃskṛtānāṃ tau nirodhau saṃbhavataḥ. utpādātyantavighno hy apratisaṃkhyānirodho na cāsaṃskṛtānām utpādo 'sti. kiṃ canutpattidharmāṇām iti paryudāsena nañsamāsaḥ. utpattidharmebhyo ye 'nye tatsadṛśā dharmāḥ. te 'nutpattidharmāṇaḥ. ke ca tatsadṛśāḥ. saṃskṛtā eva nāsaṃskṛtā iti. aprasaṃgo 'saṃskṛtānām iti bruvate. santi yeṣām ubhayam iti pratisaṃkhyānirodhaś ca apratisaṃkhyānirodhaś ca. tadyathā sāsravāṇām iti vistaraḥ. sāsravatvād eṣaḥ pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ prāpyate. anutpattidharmatvād apratisaṃkhyānirodho 'pi prāpyate. yadā tadānayoḥ prāptir abhiprīyate nāvaśyam anayor yugapatprāptir bhavati. keṣāṃcid dhi pūrvaṃ pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ prāpyate. paścād apratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. tadyathārhata ekarūpavyāsaktacakṣurmanasas tadanyarūpādyālambanānāṃ paṃcānāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ. keṣāṃcit pūrvam apratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ prāpyate. paścāt pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. tadyathā kṣāntilābhino 'pāyagatīnāṃ. [Tib. 16b] keṣāṃcid yugapat. tadyathā dṛṣṭiprāptasyādhimātrādhimātrakleṣapratipakṣodaye teṣāṃ adhimātrāṇām anāgatānāṃ kleśānāṃ pratisaṃkhyānirodhaś cāpratisaṃkhyānirodhaś ca yugapat prāpyate. evam anyeṣām api saṃbhavato yojyaṃ. tadyathātītapratyutpannotpattidharmaṇāṃ anāsravāṇām iti. atītādīnām eṣām utpādasya vighnayitum aśakyatvāt apratisaṃkhyānirodho na labhyate. anāsravatvāc caiṣāṃ pratisaṃkhyānirodho 'pi na labhyate. asaṃskṛtānāṃ tūtpādābhāvāt nāpratisaṃkhyānirodho 'sti. utpādātyantavighno hi apratisaṃkhyānirodha ity uktaṃ prāk. anāsravatvāc ca pratisaṃkhyānirodho 'pi nāsti. 6.
body.translated_text:
the reading is: 'Such as those with the nature of non-arising, which are without-outflows.'
How is there no unwanted extension of grasping the unconditioned for them? [Answer:] The topic concerns those <s>dharmas</s> for which <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> and <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> are possible. And for the unconditioned, those two cessations are not possible. For <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is the permanent obstruction of arising, and there is no arising for the unconditioned. Furthermore, 'with the nature of non-arising' — the negative compound (<s>nañsamāsa</s>) is by way of exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>). Those <s>dharmas</s> which are other than those with the nature of arising but similar to them — those are 'with the nature of non-arising.' And which are similar to them? Only the conditioned, not the unconditioned — thus there is no unwanted extension to the unconditioned, they say. 'There are some for which both [obtain]' — both <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> and <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>. 'Such as those with-outflows' — in detail. Because of being with-outflows, <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is obtained for these. Because of having the nature of non-arising, <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> too is obtained. When the obtaining of both of these is intended, the two are not necessarily obtained simultaneously. For some, <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is obtained first and <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> afterward — for example, for an <s>Arhat</s> whose eye and mind are engaged with one [type of] form, [regarding] the five consciousness-groups having other forms and so forth as their objects. For some, <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is obtained first and <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> afterward — for example, for one who has obtained <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance), regarding the lower destinies. [Tib. 16b] For some, [both are obtained] simultaneously — for example, for one who has attained [the path of] seeing (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>), upon the arising of the antidote to the most intense of the most intense afflictions, both <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> and <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> of those most intense future afflictions are obtained simultaneously. Likewise, the application to other possible cases should be made. 'Such as past, present, and those with the nature of arising, which are without-outflows' — because the arising of these past and so forth cannot be obstructed, <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is not obtained. And because they are without-outflows, <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> too is not obtained. As for the unconditioned, because there is no arising, there is no <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>. For it has been previously stated that <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is the permanent obstruction of arising. And because they are without-outflows, there is no <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> either. [Section] 6.

yad uktaṃ
body.translated_text:
(I.7) Thus, because there is little to be said about the unconditioned, having completed the questions about it beforehand, wishing to expound the conditioned, he raises a preliminary introduction.
What was stated —

children.translated_text: 'The conditioned, excluding the path, are with-outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>)'

body.text: iti. katame te saṃskṛtā iti.
body.translated_text: — what are those conditioned [dharmas]?

body.text: punaḥśabdaḥ prabhedāntarapradarśanārtha uktaḥ pūrvaprabhedaḥ sāsravānāsravā iti. ayaṃ tu punaḥprabheda iti.asaṃskṛtanirdeśena vyavahitatvāt. punaḥ saṃskṛtagrahaṇaṃ asaṃskṛtanirāsārthaṃ.
body.translated_text: The word 'again' (<s>punaḥ</s>) is used for the purpose of showing another classification. The previous classification was 'with-outflows and without-outflows.' But this is another classification — hence 'again.' Because of the intervening exposition of the unconditioned, the word 'conditioned' is taken again for the purpose of excluding the unconditioned.

body.text: iti. tacchabdaḥ pūrvaprakṛtāpekṣaḥ. ke ca pūrvaprakṛtāḥ. avarjitāś ca ye sāsravāḥ. varjitāś ca ye mārgasatyasvabhāvāḥ. ubhaye 'py apekṣitāḥ. kathaṃ gamyate.
body.translated_text: — the word 'those' (<s>tat</s>) refers back to what was previously mentioned. And what was previously mentioned? Both those with-outflows that are not excluded, and those excluded [ones] that have the nature of the truth of the path — both are referred to. How is this understood?

children.translated_text: 'Those with-outflows are the aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandhas</s>)' —

body.text: iti anāsravebhyaḥ sāsravaniṣkarṣavacanāt. yad
body.translated_text: by this statement extracting the with-outflows from the without-outflows. And

body.text: Tib. 17a
body.translated_text: Tib. 17a

body.text: rūpādiskandhapaṃcakaṃ
body.translated_text: the fivefold [classification into] form and so forth —

body.text: vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇaṃ. te 'mī saṃskṛtā draṣṭavyāḥ. anyonyam eṣāṃ saṃgrahaḥ. rūpādigrahaṇaṃ śīlādiskandhanirāsārthaṃ. anye 'pi hi paṃca skandhās santi. śīlaskandhaḥ samādhiskandhaḥ prajñāskandho vimuktiskandhaḥ vimuktijñānadarśanaskandhaś ceti. skandhagrahaṇaṃ rūpādiviṣayanirāsārthaṃ. sametya saṃbhūyeti paryāyāv etau. atha vā sametya samāgamyānyonyam apekṣyety arthaḥ. saṃbhūya saṃjanyety evaṃ saṃśabdasyārthaṃ darśayati. na hy ekapratyayajanitam iti. sarvālpapratyayatve 'pi avaśyaṃ dvau pratyayau staḥ.
body.translated_text: with the characteristics to be stated [below]. These are to be understood as conditioned. Among these, each includes the others. The inclusion of 'form and so forth' is for the purpose of excluding the [five] aggregates [beginning with] morality and so on. For there are also five other aggregates: the aggregate of morality (<s>śīlaskandha</s>), the aggregate of concentration (<s>samādhiskandha</s>), the aggregate of wisdom (<s>prajñāskandha</s>), the aggregate of liberation (<s>vimuktiskandha</s>), and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation (<s>vimuktijñānadarśanaskandha</s>). The term 'aggregates' is for the purpose of excluding the objects [such as] form, etc. 'Having come together' (<s>sametya</s>) and 'having assembled' (<s>saṃbhūya</s>) — these two are synonyms. Or, '<s>sametya</s>' means 'having come together, having mutually depended on one another' — this is the meaning. '<s>Saṃbhūya</s>' means 'having been produced together' — thus he shows the meaning of the prefix '<s>saṃ</s>.' For it is not produced by a single condition. Even in the case of the fewest conditions, there are necessarily at least two conditions.

children.translated_text:

the others are born from two' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. dugdhavad iti. saṃskṛtaśabdasya niṣṭḥāntatvāt niṣṭhāntaśabdenaiva dṛṣṭāntaṃ darśayati. dugdhavad iti dugdhaṃ nāma kṣīraṃ. yat stanān niṣkāsitaṃ tad dugdham iti nyāyyaṃ. yat tu niṣkāsiṣyate. yac ca naiva niṣkāsiṣyate dhenustham eva vartate. tad dugdham iti na prāptaṃ. ucyate ca loke dugdham iti. evam ihāpi ye saṃskariṣyante utpattidharmāṇo 'nāgatā ye 'pi na saṃskariṣyante anutpattidharmāṇaḥ. te 'pi saṃskṛtā ity ucyante. tajjātīyatvāt svalakṣaṇasādṛśyatvāt.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated. 'Like milk' — because the word '<s>saṃskṛta</s>' (conditioned) has a past participial form, he illustrates with an example using a past participial word itself. 'Like milk' — '<s>dugdha</s>' (milk) is the same as <s>kṣīra</s> (milk). That which has been drawn from the udder — that is properly called '<s>dugdha</s>' (the drawn/milked). But that which will be drawn and that which will never be drawn — which remains in the cow — calling that '<s>dugdha</s>' is not proper. Yet in the world it is called '<s>dugdha</s>' (milk). Likewise here too, those future [dharmas] with the nature of arising that will be conditioned, and those with the nature of non-arising that will not be conditioned — they too are called '<s>saṃskṛta</s>' (conditioned), because they are of the same type, because of similarity in intrinsic characteristics.

body.text: vistaraḥ. sarvābhidharmaḥ sūtrārthaḥ sūtranikaṣaḥ [Tib. 17b] sūtravyākhyānam iti sūtroktānām api adhvādīnāṃ skandhaparyāyarūpāṇāṃ iha vacanaṃ gatagacchadgamiṣyadbhāvād iti. lokaprasiddham adhvānam apekṣyāyam adhvā vyākhyātaḥ. tathā hi loke kathyate. ayam adhvā grāmaṃ gato 'yam adhvā gacchati ayam adhvā gamiṣyatīti. evam ihāpi gato 'dhvā yo 'tītaḥ gacchati yo vartamānaḥ gamiṣyati yo 'nāgata iti. adyante 'nityatayeti vādhvāna ity adhikṛtaṃ. nairuktaṃ vidhānam apekṣyāyam artho darśitaḥ. adyante
body.translated_text: in detail. All <s>Abhidharma</s> is the meaning of the <s>sūtras</s>, a touchstone of the <s>sūtras</s>, [Tib. 17b] an explanation of the <s>sūtras</s> — thus the statement here of the time-periods and so on, which are synonyms for the aggregates mentioned in the <s>sūtras</s>, having the forms of what has gone, is going, and will go. This time-period (<s>adhvan</s>) is explained with reference to the time-period commonly known in the world. For in the world it is said: 'This road (<s>adhvan</s>) has gone to the village; this road is going; this road will go.' Likewise here too, the road that has gone is the past; that which is going is the present; that which will go is the future. 'They are consumed by impermanence' — or, '<s>adhvāna</s>' (time-periods) is the topic under discussion. This meaning is shown with reference to the etymological procedure. They are consumed

body.text: anityatayā bhakṣyanta iti adhvāna iti saṃskṛtā evādhvaśabdena bhagavatā deśitāḥ.
body.translated_text: by impermanence, hence [they are called] '<s>adhvānas</s>' (time-periods) — thus the conditioned alone have been taught by the Blessed One with the word '<s>adhvan</s>' (time-period).

body.text: śabdenāpi ta eva saṃskṛtā bhagavatā deśitāḥ. trīṇīmāni bhikṣavaḥ kathāvastūni acaturthāny apaṃcamāni yāny āśrityāryāḥ kathāṃ kathayantaḥ kathayanti. katamāni trīṇi. atītaṃ kathāvastu anāgataṃ kathāvastu pratyutpannam iti. kathā vākyam iti vistaraḥ. kathā vākyaṃ varṇātmakaḥ śabda ity arthaḥ. tasyā vastu nāmaviṣaya ity arthaḥ. nāmnā punar artho 'bhidheyaḥ. tathā hi vakṣyati. vāṇ nāmni pravartate. nāmārthaṃ dyotayatīti. yadi nāmaiva kathāvastu nāma ca saṃskāraskandhaikadeśa eveti kathaṃ kṛtvā kathāvastuśabdena saṃskṛtā evoktā ity ata āha. sārthakavastugrahaṇāt tu saṃskṛtaṃ kathāvastūcyate iti. anyathā hīti vistaraḥ. yadi sārthakaṃ vastu na gṛhyeta prakaraṇagrantho virudhyate. kathāvastūny [Tib. 18a] aṣṭādaśabhir dhātubhiḥ saṃgṛhītānīti. kayā punar yuktyā sārthakaṃ vastu gṛhyate. dvividhaḥ kathāyā viṣayaḥ. sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa ca. sākṣādviṣayo nāma. pāramparyeṇārthaḥ. sa hi svaviṣayabhūtasya nāmno viṣaya iti. atas tasyāpi viṣayo vyavasthāpyate. asaṃskṛtaṃ kasmān na kathāvastutvenoktaṃ. adhvapatitasya nāmno 'nadhvapatitena sahārthāyogāt. viṣayo hetur iti vā arthadvayavācakavastuśabdaparigrahād vā. yad dhi kathāyā viṣayo hetupratyayaś ca bhavati. tat kathāvastu. asaṃskṛtaṃ tu na hetupratyayaḥ kathāyā iti na kathāvastu. atha vā atītādīnāṃ saṃskṛtānām atibahurūpatvenākhyānakaraṇayogyatvāt. evaṃ caivaṃ ca īpaṃkaras tathāgato 'bhūt. evaṃ caivaṃ ca maitreyas tathāgato bhaviṣyati. evaṃ caivaṃ ca rājā kapphiṇo bhavatīty ataḥ saṃskṛtā eva kathāvastutvenoktā nāsaṃskṛtāḥ. sarvasya saṃskṛtasya nirvāṇam iti nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇaṃ. yady evaṃ sāsravasya tad astīti bhavati sāsravasya sanissāratvayogaḥ. mārgasatyasya tu kathaṃ. kolopamaṃ dharmaparyāyam ājānadbhir dharmā api prahātavyāḥ prāg evādharmā iti mārgasatyasyāpi niḥsaraṇaṃ kalpata eveti. sarva eva saṃskṛtāḥ saniḥsārā bhavanti.
body.translated_text: By the word [<s>saṃskṛta</s>] too, it is those very conditioned things that were taught by the Blessed One. 'There are, O monks, three topics of discourse (<s>kathāvastu</s>) — not four, not five — relying on which the noble ones speak when they speak. What are the three? The past is a topic of discourse, the future is a topic of discourse, the present [is a topic of discourse].' 'Discourse (<s>kathā</s>) is a statement (<s>vākya</s>)' — and so forth in detail. Discourse is a statement, meaning a word (<s>śabda</s>) whose nature is phonemes. Its 'object' (<s>vastu</s>) means its referent. And the referent is what is denoted by the name. For it will be stated: 'Speech operates on names; names illuminate the referent.' If the name alone is the topic of discourse, and name is only a part of the aggregate of formations (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>), then how is it that by the word 'topic of discourse,' only conditioned things are referred to? Therefore he says: 'Because [the word <s>vastu</s>] grasps the referent together with meaning, the conditioned is called a topic of discourse.' Otherwise — and so forth in detail. If the referent with meaning were not grasped, the treatise's [own] passage would be contradicted — 'topics of discourse are included in the eighteen elements (<s>dhātu</s>).' But by what reasoning is the referent with meaning grasped? The object of discourse is twofold: direct and indirect. The direct object is the name; indirectly, the [real] object — for that is the object of the name which is [discourse's] own object. Therefore the [real] object too is established [as included]. Why is the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) not stated as being a topic of discourse? Because the name, which falls within the three times, cannot be connected in meaning with what does not fall within the three times. Or because 'object' (<s>viṣaya</s>) and 'cause' (<s>hetu</s>) — the word <s>vastu</s> encompasses both meanings. For what is both an object and a causal condition of discourse, that is a topic of discourse. But the unconditioned is not a causal condition of discourse, hence it is not a topic of discourse. Or, because conditioned things of the past and so forth, being of extremely many forms, are suitable for narration: 'In such and such a way was the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>; in such and such a way will be the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Maitreya</s>; in such and such a way is King <s>Kapphiṇa</s>' — therefore only conditioned things are stated as topics of discourse, not unconditioned. '<s>Nirvāṇa</s> of all that is conditioned' means <s>Nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>). If so, that applies to the contaminated — the connection of the contaminated with having an escape would be established. But how about the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>)? For those who understand the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the raft simile, even <s>dharmas</s> [i.e., the path] are to be abandoned, let alone non-<s>dharmas</s> — thus an escape is fitting for the truth of the path too. Therefore, all conditioned things indeed have an escape.

body.text: iti. vasanty asmin prāk kāryāṇi paścāt tata utpattir iti. vastu hetur ity arthaḥ. sa eṣām astīti savastukāḥ. pravacane hi vastuśabdaḥ paṃcasv artheṣu dṛśyate. svabhāve [Tib. 18b] ālambane saṃyojanīye hetau parigrahe ca. svabhāve tāvat. yad vastu pratilabdhaṃ. samanvāgataḥ sa tena vastuneti tena svabhāveneti gamyate
body.translated_text: The word means: things previously subsist in it, and afterward production [occurs] from that. '<s>Vastu</s>' means 'cause.' 'They have that' — hence <s>savastukāḥ</s> ('those having a [causal] basis'). In the teaching, the word <s>vastu</s> is seen in five senses: intrinsic nature, object, what is liable to attachment (<s>saṃyojanīya</s>), cause, and possession. Regarding intrinsic nature first: 'whatever entity is obtained — he is endowed with that entity' — thus by 'intrinsic nature'...

body.text: . ālambane. jñeyā dharmāḥ katame. āha. sarvadharmā jñānena jñeyā yathāvastu yathālambanam ity arthaḥ. saṃyojanīye. yasmiṃ vastuni anunayasaṃyojanena saṃyuktaḥ. pratighasaṃyojanenāpi tasminn iti. hetau. savastukā dharmāḥ katame. sarvasaṃskṛtā dharmā iti. parigrahe. kṣetravastugṛhavastu-āpaṇavastudhanavastuparigrahaṃ prahāya tataḥ prativirato bhavatīti. iha hetau vastuśabdo veditavyaḥ hetuvacanaḥ. kileti. kilaśabdaḥ paramataṃ darśayati. svamataṃ tv asya lakṣyate. savastukāḥ sasvabhāvāḥ saṃskṛtāḥ. asaṃskṛtās tv avastukāḥ prajñaptisattvād iti.
body.translated_text: . Regarding 'object': 'What <s>dharmas</s> are to be known? He says: all <s>dharmas</s> are to be known by knowledge — as they really are, as they are the object.' Regarding 'what is liable to attachment': 'the entity regarding which one is bound by the fetter of attachment — and also by the fetter of aversion toward that.' Regarding 'cause': 'What <s>dharmas</s> have a [causal] basis? All conditioned <s>dharmas</s>.' Regarding 'possession': 'field-property, house-property, shop-property...'

body.text: (I.8) ta eva punaḥ saṃskṛtā iti. ye sāsravā anāsravāḥ pūrvam uktā iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: (I.8) 'Those very conditioned things again' — this shows that those which were previously stated as contaminated and uncontaminated [are the same].

children.translated_text: 'Those that are contaminated are the aggregates of clinging' (<s>upādānaskandha</s>) —

body.text: iti. teṣām ity atrāhāryaṃ. kiṃ siddham iti. yad arthāpannaṃ. tad vicārayati. upādānaskandhādayaḥ sūtreṣūktāḥ. teneha te vyākhyāyante. sarvo 'bhidharmaḥ sūtrārtha iti vistareṇa uktam etat. tatsaṃbhūtatuād upādānaskandhā iti. upādānasaṃbhūtāḥ skandhā upādānaskandhāḥ. madhyapadalopāt. yathā tṛṇasaṃbhūto 'gnis tṛṇāgniḥ. [Tib. 19a] tuṣasaṃbhūto 'gnis tuṣāgnir iti. upādānānāṃ skandhā upādānaskandhā iti ṣaṣṭhīsamāsenaiva madhyapadalopam akṛtvā anye sādhayanti. evaṃ ca nidarśayanti. yathā tṛṇānām agnis tṛṇāgnir iti yuktaṃ. ye sattvasaṃkhyātāḥ. te upādānaskandhāḥ kleśābhiṣyanditakarmahetukatvāt. bāhyās tu bhāvāḥ katham upādānaskandhāḥ. te 'py upādānanirvṛttāḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Of them' — this must be supplied. 'What is established?' — that which is implied. He examines that. The <s>upādānaskandhas</s> and so forth are stated in the <s>Sūtras</s>; therefore they are explained here. 'All <s>Abhidharma</s> is the meaning of the <s>Sūtras</s>' — this has been stated in detail. 'Because of being produced from them (<s>upādāna</s>), [they are called] <s>upādānaskandhas</s>' — aggregates produced from clinging are <s>upādānaskandhas</s>, with elision of the middle word. Just as grass-born [fire]...

children.translated_text: 'The variety of the world is born of <s>karma</s>' —

body.text: iti siddhāntāt. tadvidheyatvād vā rājapuruṣavad iti. yathā rājño vidheyaḥ puruṣo rājapuruṣaḥ. evam upādānāṃ vidheyāḥ skandhāḥ. tadvaśenālambanagatyantarapravṛtteḥ. upādānāni vā tebhyaḥ saṃbhavantīti. arthakathanamātram etat. padāni tv evaṃ vaktavyāni. upādānāṃ saṃbhavā hetavo vā skandhā upādānaskandhāḥ puṣpaphalavṛkṣavat. yathā puṣpāṇāṃ phalānāṃ vā saṃbhavo hetur vā vṛkṣaḥ. puṣpavṛkṣaḥ phalavṛkṣa iti vā. tadvat. arhatskandhā api pārasāṃtānikopādānavidheyā vikriyotpādanāt. tebhyo 'pi pārasāṃtānikāni upādānāni saṃbhavantīti aviruddham eṣām upādānaskandhatvaṃ. raṇā hi kleśāḥ ātmaparavyābādhanād iti. ye hy ātmānaṃ parāṃś ca vyābādhante. te raṇā yuddhānīty arthaḥ. tathaiva ca kleśā [Tib. 19b] iti raṇā ucyante. tadanuśayitatvād iti. tair anuśayitā upasevitā ity arthaḥ. atha vā
body.translated_text: from this established doctrine. Or because they are subject to them [clingings], like a king's servant. Just as a servant subject to the king is a 'king's man,' so aggregates subject to the clingings [are <s>upādānaskandhas</s>] — because they operate toward different objects and destinies under their control. Or the clingings arise from them — this is merely a statement of meaning. But the words should be stated thus: the aggregates that are the arising or causes of the clingings are <s>upādānaskandhas</s>...

body.text: 'nuśayinaḥ kṛtāḥ tair anuśayitāḥ. tadbhāvas tadanuśayitatvaṃ. tasmāt. tadanuśayitatvāt. atha vā teṣām anuśayitatvaṃ. tasmāt. saraṇāḥ sāsravavat. sāsravatve yad vyākhyānaṃ. tad evāsya vaktavyaṃ. āryāṇāṃ pratikūlatvāt duḥkham iti. saṃskāraduḥkhatayā āryāṇāṃ tat pratikūlaṃ. samudety asmād duḥkham iti samudaya iti. hetubhūtāḥ skandhāḥ samudayaḥ. phalabhūtāḥ skandhā duḥkham iti varṇayanti. lujyata iti loka iti. asminn eva rohitāśva vyāmamātre kalevare lokaṃ prajñapayāmi lokasamudayaṃ ceti sūtraṃ. lujyate pralujyate tasmāl loka iti ca bhagavataivoktaṃ. lujyate vinaśyatīty arthaḥ. lujir iha gṛhīto na lokaḥ. nairuktena tu vidhānena gakārasya sthāne kakāraḥ kṛtaḥ. tasmāl loka iti bhavati. dṛṣṭir asmiṃs tiṣṭhatīti. ye kecid bhikṣava ātmata ātmīyataś ca samanupaśyanti. ta imān eva paṃcopādānaskandhān ātmata ātmīyataś ca samanupaśyantīti vacanād upādānaskandhā dṛṣṭisthānaṃ bhavatīti. bhava iti sāsravā eva dharmāḥ bhavaśabdenoktāḥ. bhavaḥ katamaḥ. paṃcopādānaskandhā iti vacanād. ete ca duḥkhādayaḥ śabdā mārgasatye 'pi prasajyante. mārgasatyam api hi saṃskāraduḥkhatayā duḥkhaṃ. [Tib. 20a] samanantarapratyayādibhāvena cāsmāt sāsravaṃ vastu samudeti. lujyate ca. dṛṣṭiś ca tad ālambate. bhavati ca tad utpadyate ity arthaḥ. naiṣa doṣaḥ. rūḍhiṃ hy apekṣate śabdapravṛttiḥ. ye dharmāḥ saṃskāraduḥkhatayā āryānām pratikūlā duḥkhā virodhinaḥ tadutpādakāḥ prasiddhāḥ dṛṣṭipuṣṭijanakaḥ. anādimati ca saṃsāre vinaśyanti bhavanti. teṣv evāmī duḥkhādaya āryaiḥ saṃketitā na mārgasatye. tasmāt sāsravā eva dharmā duḥkhaśabdādyabhidheyā bhavanti nānāsravāḥ. na hi gacchatīti gaur ity ukte sarvo gantā gaur ity ucyate. tasmāt sūktaṃ duḥkhaṃ samudaya ityevamādi. 8.
body.translated_text: — made to have underlying tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>); they are underlain by those [tendencies]. The state of that is being underlain by them. 'Therefore, because of being underlain by them.' Or, 'their being underlain' — therefore. '<s>Saraṇa</s>' [is explained] like <s>sāsrava</s> ('contaminated'). The explanation given for 'contaminated' should be stated for this as well. 'Suffering because it is disagreeable to the noble ones' — through suffering of formations (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>), it is disagreeable to the noble ones. 'From this, suffering arises' (<s>samudaya</s>) —

body.text: (I.9ab)
body.translated_text: (I.9ab)

body.text: iti rūpaskandhaḥ.
body.translated_text: means the form-aggregate (<s>rūpaskandha</s>).

body.text: manaindriyavyudāsārthaṃ.
body.translated_text: for the purpose of excluding the mind-faculty.

body.text: viṣayāḥ aryante jñāyanta ity arthaḥ. punaḥ
body.translated_text: means referents (<s>viṣaya</s>) — they are 'reached' (known), hence <s>artha</s>. Again,

body.text: grahaṇaṃ dharmāyatanaviṣayanirāsārthaṃ.
body.translated_text: this specification is for the purpose of excluding the <s>dharma</s>-sense-base object.

body.text: (I.9cd)
body.translated_text: (I.9cd)

body.text: iti. tacchabdo 'rthān apekṣate. teṣv artheṣu teṣāṃ vā vijñānāni tadvijñānāni.
body.translated_text: The word 'those' (<s>tad</s>) refers to the objects. The cognitions of those objects, or cognitions belonging to them — those are 'their cognitions' (<s>tadvijñāna</s>).

body.text: teṣām āśrayās tadvijñānāśrayāḥ.
body.translated_text: The bases of those [cognitions] are 'the bases of those cognitions.'

body.text: iti. rūpāṇi ca tāni prasādāś ca ta iti rūpaprasādāḥ. anena viśeṣaṇena manaindriyaṃ nirastaṃ bhavati. mano 'pi hi tadvijñānāśrayaḥ.
body.translated_text: They are forms (<s>rūpa</s>) and they are transparencies (<s>prasāda</s>) — hence 'material transparencies.' By this qualifier, the mind-faculty is excluded. For the mind too is a base of those cognitions.

body.text: iti siddhāntāt. [anuśayitās te.] na tu mano rūpasvabhāvam ity ato nirastaṃ. rūpagrahaṇaṃ [Tib. 20b] tv iha śraddhāprasādanirāsārthaṃ. tadvijñānāśrayā ity anena viśeṣaṇena śraddhāyā aprasaṃga iti cet. na. bahuvrīhikalpanāyāṃ tatprasaṃgasaṃbhavāt. rūpagrahaṇe tu bahuvrīhikalpanā nivartate. na hi rūpamayo 'sti prasādo yasya tadvijñānāny āśrayatvena kalperan. prasādagrahaṇaṃ punar indriyagrāhyavastuvyatiriktarūpaprasādaviśeṣajñāpanārthaṃ. vaibhāṣikā hi bruvate. bhūtavikāraviśeṣā evendriyāṇīti. pravacane tu naivaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. rūpādiviṣayavyatiriktāni acchāni atīndriyāṇi svavijñānānumeyāni indriyāṇi yeṣāṃ cakṣurādīni adhiṣṭhānāni dṛśyante.
body.translated_text: from the established doctrine. [They are underlain by them.] But the mind is not of material nature — hence it is excluded for that reason. The word 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>) here is for the purpose of excluding the transparency of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). [Objection:] 'The bases of those cognitions' — by this qualifier, faith would not be applicable. [Reply:] No, because in construing it as a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, such applicability is possible. But with the word 'form,' the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> construal is prevented. For form is not...

body.text: iti ca viśeṣaṇam anyonyalakṣaṇasāṃkaryanivṛttyarthaṃ. yadi hi rūpaprasādāś cakṣurādaya ity etāvad avakṣyat. cakṣur api śrotrādi vā cakṣuḥ. yatas tv evaṃ viśeṣyate. rūpavijñānāśrayo yo rūpaprasādaḥ. tac cakṣur iti. ato lakṣaṇasāṃkaryaṃ na bhavati. na hi śrotram anyad vā indriyaṃ rūpavijñānasyāśrayaḥ. evaṃ yāvat spraṣṭavyavijñānāśrayo yo rūpaprasādaḥ. tat kāyendriyam iti vaktavyaṃ. yathoktaṃ bhagavateti. etad vyākhyānaṃ sūtrānugatam ity abhiprāyaḥ. katham iti. ādhyātmikam iti vijñānāśraya ity arthaḥ. ātmaśabdo hi cittam ātmety upacaryata iti vakṣyate. ātmani adhi adhyātmam. adhyātmam eva ādhyātmikaṃ. [Tib. 21a] ātmani cittalakṣaṇe kartavye hetur ity ayam artha ādhyātmikaśabdenocyate. vijñānāśraya iti yāvad uktaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: this qualifier also serves to prevent the confusion of characteristics with one another. For if only 'material transparencies are the eye and so forth' were stated, the eye could be [confused with] the ear, etc. But when qualified thus — 'the material transparency that is the base of visual cognition is the eye' — confusion of characteristics does not arise. For the ear or any other faculty is not the base of visual cognition.

children.text:
atha vā yānīti vistaraḥ. atha vā
tac-
children.translated_text: Or 'which' (<s>yāni</s>) — and so forth in detail. Or —

body.text: chabdena indriyāṇy abhisaṃbadhyante. cakṣurvijñānaṃ śrotravijñānam ityevamādi pravacanaprasiddham etat. na tu rūpavijñānaṃ śabdavijñānam iti. loke tu kadācid evaṃ bhavet. tasmād idaṃ vyākhyānāntaram āśrīyate. tasmād āha. evaṃ ca kṛtvā prakaraṇagrantho 'py anuvṛtta iti vistaraḥ. katham ihāsiddham asiddhena sādhyate. cakṣur eva hy asiddhaṃ. tadasiddhau cakṣurvijñānam apy asiddhaṃ. kathaṃ tat tena tadāśrayatayā sādhyate. siddhā
body.translated_text: by the word [in the compound], the sense-faculties are connected. 'Eye-consciousness,' 'ear-consciousness,' and so on — this is well-known in the scriptures. Not 'form-consciousness' or 'sound-consciousness.' In ordinary usage, however, this might sometimes occur. Therefore the alternative interpretation is adopted. Hence he says, 'Having done so, the <s>Prakaraṇa</s> text too follows' — thus the elaboration. How is something unestablished being proved by [another] unestablished thing? For the eye itself is unestablished. If that is unestablished, eye-consciousness too is unestablished. How then is it [the eye] proved by that [consciousness], as being its support? [Reply:]

body.text: evaite paṃca vijñānaviśeṣāḥ. parasparaviśeṣopalakṣaṇārthaṃ tu vayam etaiś cakṣurādibhis tān viśeṣayanto darśayāmaḥ. etad uktaṃ bhavati. etasya prathamasyaikasya svasaṃvedyasya vjñānaviśeṣasya ya āśrayo rūpaprasādaḥ. tac cakṣurindriyaṃ. evaṃ yāvad etasya paṃcamasya svasaṃvedyasya vijñānaviśeṣasya ya āśrayo rūpaprasādaḥ. tat kāyendriyam iti. nāsiddhenāsiddhasya sādhanaṃ.
body.translated_text: These five specific types of consciousness are indeed established [through direct experience]. But we show them as distinguished by those [terms] — 'eye' and so forth — for the purpose of marking their mutual distinctiveness. What is being said is this: the material sensitivity (<s>rūpa-prasāda</s>) that is the support of this first specific type of consciousness, knowable by itself [alone] — that is the eye sense-faculty. Likewise, the material sensitivity that is the support of this fifth specific type of consciousness, knowable by itself — that is the body sense-faculty. Thus, it is not the proving of something unestablished by something unestablished.

body.text: cakṣuṣo 'rtho varṇasaṃsthānabhedād dviḥprakāraḥ. lokapratītatvāt tasya svalakṣaṇaṃ anuktvā prabheda eva kathyate. varṇaś caturvidho nīlādir iti. nīlalohitapītāvadātā varṇāḥ. tadbhedā anya iti abhrādayaḥ. apare vyācakṣate. tadbhedā anya iti nīlādivarṇacatuṣṭayasaṃparkaviśeṣāt [Tib. 21b] kākāṇḍavarṇādayo 'pi jāyante. na kevalam abhrādya iti. saṃsthānam ākṛtiviśeṣaḥ. punas tad evāntargaṇikena bhedena bhidyate.
body.translated_text: The object of the eye is of two kinds, due to the distinction between color and shape. Since [form] is commonly understood in the world, its specific characteristic is not stated — only its subdivisions are explained. 'Color is of four kinds: blue and so on' — the colors are blue, red, yellow, and white. 'Others are subdivisions of those' — clouds and the rest. Others explain: 'Others are subdivisions of those' means that from the specific mixing of the four colors — blue and so on — crow-wing color and the rest are also produced, not just clouds and so on. 'Shape' (<s>saṃsthāna</s>) is a specific type of configuration. This is further divided by an internal classification.

body.text: tadyathā nīlapītādi. saṃsthānam aṣṭavidhaṃ dīrghādivisātāntaṃ. śeṣo dvādaśavidho varṇa iti viṃśatidhā. nabhaś caikavarṇam iti. yad dūrato vaiḍūryabhittyākāraṃ dṛśyate. vṛttaṃ vartulaṃ. parimaṇḍalaṃ cakralaṃ. unnataṃ sthūlādirūpaṃ. avanataṃ nimnarūpaṃ. yatra rūpāṇāṃ darśanam iti vacanaṃ chāyāndhakārayor nānākaraṇapradarśanārthaṃ. na vipaṃcitaṃ na vibhaktam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: Namely: blue, yellow, and so on. Shape is of eight kinds, from 'long' through 'even.' The remaining twelve are color — thus, twenty. 'And the sky is of one color' — that which from a distance appears like a <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) wall. 'Round' (<s>vṛtta</s>) means circular. 'Globular' (<s>parimaṇḍala</s>) means wheel-shaped. 'Elevated' means thick-bodied form and so on. 'Depressed' means sunken form. The statement 'where there is the perception of forms' — this is for the purpose of showing the difference between shadow and darkness [and other forms]. 'Not detailed' means not divided — this is the meaning.

body.text: idam iha vicāryate. yadi nīlādivarṇacatuṣṭayabhedā eva abhrādayo na tadvyatiriktā bhavanti. yatheha kākāṇḍādivarṇā noktāḥ. tathābhrādayo 'pi na vaktavyā iti. naitad vyākhyānakārair vicāritaṃ. śakyaṃ tv evaṃ bhaṇituṃ. māyārūpasadṛśatvāt nīlādibhedabhūtā api te abhrādayaḥ pṛthag uktāḥ. tathā hi te dūrato bhittaya iva lakṣyante abhyāsagamane tu na dṛśyante. mā kasyacid evaṃ bhūt. naitat kiṃcid asti. vimatir vā. kim asty etat. uta bhrāntimātram iti. tadviparyāsasaṃśayanivṛttyartham ime abhrādaya uktāḥ. saṃty evāmī rūpāyatanasvabhāvā iti. dīrghādīnāṃ pradeśa iti. dīrghādivisātānta [Tib. 22a] pradeśa ity arthaḥ. kataro 'sau pradeśa ity āha. kāyavijñaptisvabhāva iti. kāyavijñaptir hi kadācid dīrghā kadācid dhrasvā kadācid yāvad visāteti. kīdṛśī punaḥ sāvagantavyā. tad ālambanacittasamutthāpitaṃ yat kāyakarma. akāyakarmasvabhāvaṃ tu dīrghādivisātāntaṃ nirastaṃ boddhavyaṃ. asty ubhayathā. pariśiṣṭam iti. yan nirastaṃ dīrghādi. abhradhūmarajomahikāś ca.
body.translated_text: This is examined here: if clouds and so on are merely subdivisions of the four colors — blue and so on — and not distinct from them, then just as crow-wing color and the rest are not [separately] stated here, so too clouds and the rest should not be stated. This has not been examined by the commentators. But it is possible to say: because they resemble illusory forms, clouds and so on, though being subdivisions of blue and the rest, are stated separately. For they appear from a distance as if they were walls, but when approached closely they are not seen. Lest someone think 'this is nothing at all,' or have doubt 'does this exist, or is it mere illusion?' — to remove that error and doubt, these clouds and the rest are stated: 'These indeed have the nature of the form sense-base.' 'The locus of long and so on' — the meaning is: the locus of [shapes] from long through even. What is that locus? He says: 'the nature of bodily expression.' For bodily expression is sometimes long, sometimes short, sometimes even. But of what kind is it to be understood? That bodily action which is generated by a mind having that [shape] as its object. But [shape that is] long and so on which is not of the nature of bodily action should be understood as excluded [from this]. It exists in both ways. 'The remainder' — the long and so on which is excluded, and clouds, smoke, dust, and mist.

body.text: dṛśyate hi nīlādīnāṃ dīrghādipariccheda iti. nīlapītalohitāvadātacchāyāndhakārāṇāṃ dīrghādisaṃsthānagrahaṇaṃ. tasmād eṣām api tṛtīyāyāṃ koṭyām antarbhāva ity abhiprāyaḥ. kathaṃ punar ekaṃ dravyam ubhayathā vidyata iti. katham ekaṃ dravyaṃ varṇasaṃsthānātmakaṃ bhavati. varṇarūpād dhi saṃsthānarūpaṃ dravyāntaram iti vaḥ siddhāntaḥ. ubhayasya tatra prajñānāt. varṇasaṃsthānasya tatra grahaṇāt. jñānārtho hy eṣa vidir na sattārtha iti. vida jñāna ity etasya dhātor lugvikaraṇasya etad rūpaṃ vidyata iti. na tu vida sattāyām ity etasya dhātoḥ śyanvikaraṇasyaitad rūpam ity arthaḥ. jñānaṃ tatrobhayākāraṃ pravartate. na dravyaṃ ekam ubhayalakṣaṇam iti vaibhāṣikaparihāraḥ. kāyavijñaptāv api tarhi prasaṃga ity ācāryaḥ. na hi kāyavijñaptau gṛhyamānāyāṃ varṇagrahaṇaṃ na pravartate. vaibhāṣikāṇām ayam abhiprāyaḥ. nīlādigrahaṇam ātapālokagrahaṇaṃ vā saṃsthānanirapekṣaṃ pravartate. kāyavijñaptigrahaṇaṃ tu varṇanirapekṣaṃ. pariśiṣṭarūpāyatanagrahaṇaṃ [Tib. 22b] tu varṇasaṃsthānāpekṣaṃ pravartata iti. sautrāntikapākṣikas tu ayam ācāryo nainam arthaṃ prayacchati. na hi cākṣuṣam etat saṃsthānagrahaṇaṃ. mānasaṃ tv etat parikalpitaṃ. varṇasaṃniveśaviśeṣa eva hi saṃsthānaṃ. na saṃsthānaṃ nāma dravyaṃ kiṃcid asti. varṇāgrahaṇe saṃsthānagrahaṇābhāvāt. etac ca karmakośasthāne parīkṣiṣyate.
body.translated_text: For the delimitation of long and so on is seen in blue and so on — the apprehension of the shape 'long' and so forth of blue, yellow, red, white, shadow, and darkness. Therefore, the intent is that these too are included in the third category [i.e., neither purely color nor purely shape, but apprehended in connection with both]. But how can a single substance exist in both ways? How can a single substance have the nature of both color and shape? For shape-form is a different substance from color-form — this is your [the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>'] established position. [Reply:] Because both are cognized there — because both color and shape are apprehended there. The word '<s>vid</s>' here has the meaning of knowledge, not of existence. That is, it is the form of the root '<s>vid</s>' meaning 'to know,' with the elision of the <s>vikaraṇa</s>, [giving] '<s>vidyate</s>' — not the form of the root '<s>vid</s>' meaning 'to exist,' with the <s>śyan</s> <s>vikaraṇa</s>. The cognition there operates with both aspects — it is not that a single substance has both characteristics. This is the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> response. 'The same consequence would apply to bodily expression as well' — says the master [<s>Vasubandhu</s>]. For when bodily expression is being apprehended, the apprehension of color too is not absent. This is the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> intent: the apprehension of blue and so on, or the apprehension of sunlight and lamplight, operates independently of shape. But the apprehension of bodily expression operates independently of color. The apprehension of the remaining form sense-base, however, operates dependent on both color and shape. But the master, siding with the <s>Sautrāntikas</s>, does not accept this position. For this apprehension of shape is not visual — rather, it is mental, imagined. For shape is merely a specific arrangement of colors — there is no substance called 'shape.' Because in the absence of color-apprehension, there is no apprehension of shape. And this will be examined in the section on <s>karma</s>.

body.text: sattvāsattvākhyaś ceti. vāgvijñaptiśabdas tadvyatiriktaś cety arthaḥ. sattvāsattvasaṃkhyātaś ceti kecit paṭhanti. ayam eva ca ihārtho 'bhipretaḥ. yadi hi sattvāsattvasaṃtānaja iti ayam artho 'bhipreto bhavet. sattvākhyo vāgvijñaptiśabdo 'sattvākhyo 'nya iti evaṃ vakṣyamāṇakaṃ vivaraṇaṃ niḥprayojanam eva. tasmāt sattvāsattvākhyaś ceti pāṭhaḥ sphuṭaḥ paṭhitavyaḥ. upāttamahābhūtahetuka iti. pratyutpannānīndriyāvinirbhāgāni bhūtāny upāttāni. anyāni anupāttāni. upāttāni mahābhūtāni hetur asyeti upāttamahābhūtahetukaḥ. yathā hastavācchabda iti. yadi sattvasaṃtānaja ity abhipretaḥ. bāhyo 'pi hi nirmito mānuṣākāro hastavācchabdaṃ kuryāt. sa cānupāttamahābhūtahetukasvabhāvo 'vagantavya indriyavinirbhāgavartitvāt. sa ca mānuṣīm api vācaṃ nirmātṛvaśād bhāṣet. vakṣyati hy
body.translated_text: 'Designated as produced by sentient and non-sentient [beings]' — thus. The meaning is: the sound of vocal expression, and that which is distinct from it. Some read '<s>sattvāsattvasaṃkhyāta</s>' ('counted as sentient and non-sentient'). The intended meaning here is the same. For if the meaning intended were '<s>sattvāsattvasaṃtānaja</s>' ('born from the continuum of sentient and non-sentient beings'), the forthcoming explanation 'the sound designated as sentient is vocal expression; the other is designated as non-sentient' would be purposeless. Therefore, the reading '<s>sattvāsattvākhya</s>' ('designated as sentient and non-sentient') is clear and should be adopted. 'Caused by appropriated great elements' — the elements that are present, inseparable from the sense-faculties — these are 'appropriated.' Others are 'unappropriated.' 'Appropriated great elements are the cause of this' — [thus] 'caused by appropriated great elements.' 'Like the sound of clapping hands' — if '<s>sattvasaṃtānaja</s>' were intended, even an externally created form resembling a human being could produce the sound of hand-clapping. And that should be understood as having the nature of being caused by unappropriated great elements, since it operates apart from sense-faculties. And that [created being] might even speak human speech at the creator's will. For it will be stated:

children.text:
ekasya bhāṣamāṇasya bhāṣante sarvanirmitāḥ.
ekasya tūṣṇīṃbhūtasya sarve tūṣṇīṃbhavanti te.
children.translated_text: 'When one [creator] speaks, all the created beings speak; when one falls silent, all of them become silent.'

body.text: tasya ca bāhyanirmitaśabdasya anupāttamahābhūtahetuka ity atra grahaṇaṃ. yathā vāyuvanaspatinadīśabda [Tib. 23a] iti. yathāśabdasyodāharaṇārthatvāt.
body.translated_text: And the externally created sound — its inclusion is under 'caused by unappropriated great elements.' 'Like the sounds of wind, trees, and rivers' — the word 'like' is for the purpose of giving examples.

body.text: sattvākhyo vāgvijñaptisabdo 'sattvākhyo 'nya iti. sattvam ācaṣṭe sattvākhyaḥ. vāgvijñaptiśabdena hi sattvo 'yam iti vijñāyate. taṃ vāgvijñaptiśabdaṃ varjayitvā anyaḥ śabdo hastaśabdo 'pi yāvad asattvākhya eva. kim aṃga asattvasaṃtānaja iti vyākhyātaṃ bhavati. tad evam upāttamahābhūtahetukaḥ sattvākhyaś cāsattvākhyaś ca bhavati. anupāttamahābhūtahetuko 'pi nirmitaśabdo vāgvijñaptisvabhāvaḥ sattvākhyaḥ. tasyaiva hastaśabdo vāyuvanaspatyādiśabdaś cāsattvākhya iti. caturvidhaḥ śabdo manojñāmanojñabhedāt punar aṣṭavidho bhavati. yathaiko varṇaparamāṇur iti. na bhūtacatuṣkadvayam upādāya vartate śadbaḥ. upādāyarūpatvāt. varṇaparamāṇuvad iti bhāvaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'That designated as sentient is vocal expression sound; the other is designated as non-sentient' — thus. 'Designated as sentient' — it designates a sentient being. For through the sound of vocal expression, one recognizes 'this is a sentient being.' Excluding that vocal expression sound, any other sound — even the sound of hand-clapping — is designated as non-sentient. How much more what is born from a non-sentient continuum. Thus, sound caused by appropriated great elements is both designated as sentient and as non-sentient. Sound caused by unappropriated great elements — the created sound having the nature of vocal expression — is designated as sentient. The hand-clapping sound of that same [unappropriated category], and the sound of wind, trees, and so on — is designated as non-sentient. The fourfold sound becomes eightfold by the further division into pleasant and unpleasant. 'Just as a single color-atom' — sound does not operate by depending on two sets of four great elements. Because it is a derived form — the idea is: just as a color-atom [depends on only one set].

body.text: ṣaṇmūlajātim adhikṛtyaivam uktaṃ. rasaṣaṭkasya anyonyasamparkaviśeṣāt tv atibahuprakārā rasāḥ saṃbhavanti. ekakadvikatrikacatuṣkapaṃcakaṣaṭkasamparkayogād dhi carake triṣaṣṭī rasā upadiṣṭāḥ.
body.translated_text: This is said with reference to the six basic types. But from the specific mixing of the six tastes with each other, very many types of tastes are possible. For in the <s>Caraka</s> [medical treatise], sixty-three tastes are taught through the mixing of one, two, three, four, five, and six [basic tastes].

body.text: sugandhadurgandhayoḥ samaviṣamagandhatvād iti. anutkaṭotkaṭagandhatvād ity arthaḥ. asmin pakṣe dvividho gandha iṣṭaḥ. trividhas tu śāstra iti. samagaṃdho 'nyas tṛtīya ity arthaḥ. [Tib. 23b] apare punar vyācakṣate. samagandha iti tayor evaikadeśa iti sa evārtho bhavati. śabdamātraṃ tu bhidyate.
body.translated_text: 'Of pleasant and unpleasant scent — because of even and uneven scent' — the meaning is: because of subdued and strong scent. On this view, scent is accepted as twofold. 'But threefold in the treatise' — the meaning is: even scent is a third [type], distinct [from pleasant and unpleasant]. Others, however, explain: 'even scent' is a subdivision of those two [pleasant and unpleasant] themselves — so the meaning is the same, but only the wording differs.

body.text: śītam uṣmābhilāṣakṛd iti. saṃbhavaṃ praty evam ucyate. yo dharma uṣmābhilāṣaṃ kuryāt. tac chītaṃ nāmopādāyarūpaṃ. grīṣme yady api tan na kuryāt tajjātīyatvāt tu śītam eva tad avagantavyaṃ. kāraṇe kāryopacārād iti. attumicchā jighatsā caitasiko dharmaḥ. tasya kāraṇaṃ. antar udare kāyendriyeṇa yaḥ spṛśyate. sā jighatsā nāmopādāyarūpaṃ. yathā
body.translated_text: 'Cold is that which produces a desire for warmth' — thus it is said with reference to [its] possible [effect]. Whatever <s>dharma</s> would produce a desire for warmth — that derived form is called 'cold.' Even if in summer it does not produce that [desire], it should be understood as cold because it belongs to that class. 'By the figurative transfer of the effect to the cause' — hunger (<s>jighatsā</s>), the desire to eat, is a mental <s>dharma</s>. Its cause — what is touched by the body sense-faculty inside the belly — that derived form is called 'hunger.' Just as

body.text: ityādi abhyudayaniḥśreyasasukhakāraṇatvāt buddhotpādasya sa sukham ity ucyate. tadvat. evaṃ pipāsāpi vaktavyā. saṃcitāni punas tulyanta iti sūkṣmagurutvasadbhāvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. atrānumānaṃ. sagurutvaṃ rūpāvacaraṃ vastrādi. ādhārādheyabhāvāt. kuṇḍabadaravad iti. anugrāhakaṃ kilāstīti. kilaśabdo vaibhāṣikamatadyotanārthaṃ. svamataṃ tu samādhir evātrānugrāhakaḥ. kim atra śītena parikalpiteneti. yadā tatprakāravyavaccheda iti. yadā nīlādiprakāranimittābhogaḥ. evaṃ śrotrādivijñānam iti. ya eṣa bahuvidhaḥ śabda uktaḥ. tatra kadācid ekena dravyeṇa śrotravijñānam utpadyate yadā tatprakāravyavacchedo bhavati. kadācid bahubhir yadā na vyavacchedaḥ. tadyathā [Tib. 24a] tūryaśabdasamūham anekākāratāramandratādiśabdarūpaṃ śṛṇvataḥ. evaṃ ghrāṇajihvāvijñāne api svaviṣaye yojye. kāyavijñānaṃ tu
body.translated_text: and so on — because the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is a cause of happiness in terms of both worldly prosperity and the highest good, it is called 'happiness.' Similarly [with hunger]. Thirst is also to be explained in the same way. 'And the accumulated [atoms] are again weighed' — the intent is: because of the existence of subtle heaviness. Here is an inference: that which has heaviness is form-realm [matter], such as cloth and the like — because of the relation of support and supported, like a pot and a jujube. 'There is supposedly a facilitating [factor]' — the word 'supposedly' (<s>kila</s>) is for indicating the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> view. But his own view is that <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) alone is the facilitating [factor] here — what need for a posited 'cold'? 'When there is the delimitation of that type' — when there is the intentional attention to the sign of a [specific] type such as blue and so on. 'Likewise ear-consciousness and so on' — this manifold sound that has been described — sometimes ear-consciousness arises from a single substance, when there is delimitation of that type; sometimes from many [substances], when there is no delimitation — for example, when hearing a mass of musical sounds having many aspects such as loud and soft tones. Likewise, nose-consciousness and tongue-consciousness are also to be applied to their respective objects. But body-consciousness —

body.text: paraṃ paṃcabhir iti. kathaṃ. kadācid ekena dravyeṇotpadyate yadā tatprakāravyavacchedo bhavati. kadācid dvābhyāṃ yāvat paṃcabhir yadā na vyavacchedaḥ. ekena ca ślakṣṇatvādineti. kim atra kāraṇaṃ. karkaśatvādīnām anyabhūtacatuṣkāśritatvāt. nanu caivam iti vistaraḥ. yathā cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvākāyavijñānālambanāny abhisamasya manovijñānaṃ gṛhṇātīti kṛtvā sāmānyalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ tad vyavasthāpyate. tathā nīlapītalohitāvadātālambanānāṃ caturṇāṃ cakṣurvijñānānāṃ tāni catvāri bahutarāṇi cālambanāny abhisamasya cakṣurvijñānam ekaṃ gṛhṇātīti sāmānyalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ tat prāpnoti. rūpāyatanasāmānyalakṣaṇam asyālambanam iti kṛtvā. tathā śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyavijñānāny api svaviṣayeṣu yojyāni. āyatanasvalakṣaṇaṃ pratīti. svaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ. āyatanānāṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ āyatanasvalakṣaṇaṃ. cakṣurvijñānavijñeyatvādi. rūpāyatanatvādi vā. tat praty ete paṃca vijñānakāyāḥ svalakṣaṇaviṣayā iṣyante pravacane. na dravyasvalakṣaṇaṃ prati svalakṣaṇaviṣayā iṣyante iti prakṛtaṃ. dravyāṇāṃ nīlādikānāṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ nīlādyākāracakṣurvijñānādivijñeyatvaṃ. [Tib. 24b] nīlākārādi vā. na tat praty ete paṃca vijñānakāyāḥ svalakṣaṇaviṣayā iṣyaṃte ity adoṣaḥ. yugapadviṣayasaṃprāptāv iti. kāyajihvendriyayor yugapadviṣayasaṃprāptiḥ saṃbhavati. dvayoś ca vijñānayor yugapatpravṛttir na saṃbhavati. ataḥ pṛcchati. katarad vijñānaṃ pūrvam utpadyata iti. yasya viṣayaḥ paṭīyān. yadi kāyendriyasya viṣayaḥ paṭutaraḥ kāyavijñānaṃ pūrvam utpadyate. atha jihvendriyasya viṣayaḥ paṭīyān jihvāvijñānaṃ pūrvam utpadyate. samaprāpte tu viṣaye tulya ity arthaḥ. jihvāvijñānaṃ pūrvam utpadyate. kasmāt. bhoktukāmatāvarjitatvāt saṃtateḥ. bhojanecchāpravaṇatvāt ātmabhāvasyety arthaḥ. pūrvaṃ jihvāvijñānam utpadyata iti vacanāt paścāt kāyavijñānam utpatsyata ity arthād uktaṃ bhavati. tenātra vicāryate. kiṃ yo 'sau jihvāviṣayakṣaṇena saha prāptaḥ kāyaviṣayaksaṇa āsīt. tatra tat kāyavijñānam utpadyate. āhosvid anyasmin kāyavijñānaviṣayakṣaṇa iti. anyasminn ity āha. katham ālambananiyamo na bhidyate. naiṣa doṣaḥ. yat tadviṣayālaṃbanaṃ vijñānaṃ. tad apratisaṃkhyānirodhaniruddhaṃ. anyat tu tatsadṛśaṃ kāyavijñānam utpadyata iti. ataḥ paścāt tad utpadyate ity ucyate jātisāmānyenaikatvopacārāt.
body.translated_text: at most by five — how so? Sometimes it arises by one substance (<s>dravya</s>), when the exclusion of that particular variety occurs. Sometimes by two, up to five, when there is no exclusion. And 'by one, such as smoothness' — what is the reason here? Because roughness and the rest are dependent on the set of four [great elements] belonging to another [atomic aggregate]. 'But is this not so?' — in detail. Just as <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness) grasps by subsuming the objects of eye-, ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness — and thereby it is established as having a general characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object — likewise, since a single eye-consciousness grasps by subsuming the four and more objects of the four eye-consciousnesses that have blue, yellow, red, and white as their objects, it would follow that it has a general characteristic as its object — namely, the general characteristic of the form sense-base (<s>rūpāyatana</s>) would be its object. Similarly, ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousnesses should be applied to their own objects. 'With reference to the intrinsic characteristic of the sense-base' — the intrinsic characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is one's own characteristic; the intrinsic characteristic of the sense-bases is the intrinsic characteristic belonging to the sense-bases — namely, being cognizable by eye-consciousness, etc., or being a form sense-base, etc. The five consciousness-groups are held in the teaching to have intrinsic characteristics as their object with reference to that, not with reference to the intrinsic characteristic of substances. The intrinsic characteristic of substances such as blue, etc. is the cognizability by eye-consciousness and so on through the form of blue, etc. [Tib. 24b] Or it is the blue-form, etc. The five consciousness-groups are not held to have intrinsic characteristics as their objects with reference to that — thus there is no fault. 'When the sense-objects are simultaneously encountered' — it is possible for the body-faculty and tongue-faculty to simultaneously encounter their objects. But the simultaneous operation of two consciousnesses is not possible. Therefore he asks: 'Which consciousness arises first?' That whose object is more acute. If the object of the body-faculty is more acute, body-consciousness arises first. If the object of the tongue-faculty is more acute, tongue-consciousness arises first. But when the objects are encountered equally — this is the meaning: tongue-consciousness arises first. Why? Because the mental continuum is inclined by the desire to eat. Because the personal existence is disposed toward the desire for food — this is the meaning. From the statement that tongue-consciousness arises first, it is implicitly stated that body-consciousness will arise afterward. Therefore, here is investigated: Was the moment of body-object that was encountered together with the moment of tongue-object [still present at the time of body-consciousness]?

body.text: (I.11) anekakathāprapaṃcavyavahitatvāt naṣṭa ivāvijñapter uddeśadhikāra iti. ata idam upanyasyati. uktāḥ paṃcendriyārthā yathā ca teṣāṃ grahaṇam iti. kadācid ekena dravyeṇa cakṣurvijñānam utpadyata ityevamādinā. [Tib. 25a] teṣāṃ tu grahaṇam iti karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī. avijñaptir idānīṃ vaktavyeti.
body.translated_text: (I.11) Because [the topic] has been interrupted by the extensive discussion of many topics, the section on the exposition of <s>avijñapti</s> (non-informative [matter]) was as if lost. Therefore he presents this: 'The five sense-faculties' objects have been stated, and how they are grasped' — by such statements as 'sometimes eye-consciousness arises from one substance,' etc. [Tib. 25a] 'Their grasping' — the sixth case is in the object sense (<s>karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī</s>). Now <s>avijñapti</s> is to be discussed.

children.text: rūpaṃ paṃcendriyāṇy arthāḥ paṃcāvijñaptir eva cety
children.translated_text: 'Form [consists of] the five sense-faculties, [their] five objects, and <s>avijñapti</s> alone' —

body.text: avijñaptir evāvaśiṣyate. tasyā lakṣaṇanirdeśāvasara iti vaktavyā.
body.translated_text: <s>Avijñapti</s> alone remains [to be discussed]. Since this is the occasion for the exposition defining its characteristics, it must be discussed.

children.translated_text: 'Of one whose [mind] is distracted or without mind' —
