body.text: kecid evaṃ vṛttiṃ paṭhanti. asmiṃ pāṭhe evaṃ sūtravigrahaḥ. vikṣiptaṃ nāsti vā cittam asyeti vikṣiptācittakaḥ. atha vā vikṣiptaṃ cittaṃ nāsti vā cittam asyeti vikṣiptācittakaḥ. ekasya cittaśabdasya lopaḥ. kecid evaṃ paṭhanti. vikṣiptasyeti. asmin pāṭhe uttarapadadvayasya bahuvrīhiṃ kṛtvā paścād evaṃ vigrahaḥ. vikṣiptaś cācittakaś ca vikṣiptācittakaḥ. vikṣiptaḥ pudgalaḥ vikṣiptacitta ity arthaḥ. vikṣiptacittasyeti tadanyacittasyāpīti avikṣiptacittād anyacittasyety arthaḥ. tadyathā kuśalāyā avijñapteḥ samutthāpakaṃ cittaṃ kuśalaṃ. tadanyacitto 'kuśalāvyākṛtacittaḥ. sa iha vikṣiptacitto 'bhipretaḥ. akuśalāyās tv avijñapter akuśalaṃ cittaṃ samutthāpakaṃ. tadanyacittaḥ kuśalāvyākṛtacittaḥ. sa cāpi vikṣiptacitto veditavyaḥ. tasya. tadanyacittasyāpi. acittakasyāpīti asaṃjñinirodhasamāpattisamāpannasyāpi. apiśabdenāvikṣiptasacittakasyāpīti vijñāyata [Tib. 25b] iti. etatpudgaladvayavyatiriktasya tṛtīyasyāpy arthaḥ. yo 'nubandha iti pravāha iti. yo dharmo nityapravāhayukta ity arthaḥ. pravāhena pravāhī nirdiśyate pravāhopalakṣyatvāt. atha vā anubadhnātīti anubandhaḥ. pravāha iti ca vyākhyāpadaṃ kṛtabahuvrīhikaṃ. pravṛttaḥ prakṛṣṭo vā vāho 'syeti pravāho dharmaḥ. sa eva nirdiśyate. na tat srotaḥ. kuśalākuśala iti. kuśalākuṣala evety avadhāraṇaṃ. avyākṛto nastīty arthaḥ. etena cakṣurādayo vyadastā veditavyāḥ. prāptipravāho 'py asti īdṛśa iti. tatprāptir api vikṣiptāvikṣiptacittasyāpi pravāhiṇī kuśalākuśalaiva ceti tadviśeṣaṇārtham ucyate. mahābhūtāny upādāyeti. mahābhūtahetuka ity arthaḥ. yathendhanam upādāyāgnir bhavatīty ukte. indhanahetuko 'gnir iti gamyate. jananādihetubhāvād iti.
body.translated_text: Some read the text thus. In this reading, the analysis of the <s>sūtra</s> is as follows: 'One for whom the mind is distracted or there is no mind — that is <s>vikṣiptācittaka</s>.' Or, 'the mind is distracted, or there is no mind — for whom this is so — that is <s>vikṣiptācittaka</s>.' One occurrence of the word 'mind' (<s>citta</s>) is elided. Some read it thus: '<s>vikṣiptasya</s>' ('of one who is distracted'). In this reading, having made a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound of the two latter words, then thus...

children.translated_text: 'From generation, from support, from location, from sustaining, and from nourishing' —

body.text: jananahetus tebhya utpatteḥ. niśrayahetur jātasya bhūtānuvidhāyitvād ācāryādiniśrayavat. pratiṣṭhāhetur ādhārabhāvāt citrakuḍyavat. upastambhahetur anucchedahetutvāt. upabṛṃhaṇahetur vṛddhihetutvāt. katamāny mahābhūtāny upādāya. kim āśrayamahābhūtāni. utāho niśrayamahābhūtāni. āśrayamahābhūtānīty āhuḥ. tannāmakaraṇajñāpanārtha iti. yasmād rūpakriyāsvabhāvāpi satī [Tib. 26a] vijñaptivat paraṃ na vijñāpayati. tasmād avijñaptir
body.translated_text: The cause of generation — because of arising from them. The cause of support (<s>niśraya</s>) — because what has arisen conforms to the [great] elements, like dependence on a teacher, etc. The cause of establishment (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) — because of being a basis, like a wall for a painting. The cause of sustaining (<s>upastambha</s>) — because of being a cause of non-destruction. The cause of nourishing (<s>upabṛṃhaṇa</s>) — because of being a cause of growth. 'Depending on which great elements?' — Does this mean the great elements as support (<s>āśraya</s>), or the great elements as basis (<s>niśraya</s>)? It means the great elements as support — he says:

body.text: ity arthaḥ. rūpakriyāsvabhāvāpīty ubhayaviśāṣaṇaṃ. kim arthaṃ. yad dhi vastu rūpasvabhāvam eva na kṛiyāsvabhāvaṃ. tan na paraṃ gamayati. tadyathā cakṣurādayaḥ. yad api kriyāsvabhāvam eva na rūpasvabhāvaṃ. tad api paraṃ na gamayati. tadyathā cetanā. yat tūbhayasvabhāvaṃ. tat paraṃ gamayati. tadyathā vijñaptiḥ. vijñaptir hi svasamutthāpakaṃ cittaṃ kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtaṃ saumyaṃ krūram anubhayam iti vā paraṃ vijñāpayati. tena vijñaptivad iti viparītadṛṣṭāntaprayogaḥ.
body.translated_text: — this is the meaning. 'Having the nature of both form and action' — this is a qualifier of both [kinds]. For what purpose? For that which has the nature of form only, not the nature of action, does not convey [information] to another — such as the eye and other [sense-faculties]. And that which has the nature of action only, not the nature of form, also does not convey [information] to another — such as <s>cetanā</s> (volition). But that which has the nature of both — that conveys to another — such as...

body.text: samāsatas tv iti vistaraḥ. śiṣyasukhāvabodhārthaṃ saṃkṣepato vākyena tad avijñaptirūpaṃ darśayaty ācāryaḥ. vijñaptisamādhisaṃbhūtaṃ kuśalākuśalaṃ rūpam avijñaptir iti. yathāsaṃbhavam etat yojyaṃ. kāyavākvijñaptisaṃbhūtaṃ kuśalaṃ prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ naivasaṃvaranāsaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ ca. akuśalaṃ punar asaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ naivasaṃvaranāsaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ ca. samādhisaṃbhūtaṃ tu kuśalam eva. tad dvividhaṃ. sāsravasamādhisaṃbhūtaṃ dhyānasaṃvarasvabhāvaṃ. anāsravasamādhisaṃbhūtaṃ anāsravasaṃvarasvabhāvaṃ. upādāyarūpasvabhāvaṃ ca. na cittacaitasikādisvabhāvam [Tib. 26b] ity avagantavyaṃ. nanu caivaṃ vijñaptir api avijñaptiḥ prāpnoti. sāpi uttarā sabhāgahetubhūtapūrvavijñaptisaṃbhūtā. kuśalākuśalam evety avadhāraṇāt vijñaptāv aprasaṃgaḥ. vijñaptir hy avyākrtāpi saṃbhavati. ata eva divyaṃ cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ca samādhisaṃbhūtam api sat vijñaptijaṃ ca vipākarūpaṃ nāvijñaptiḥ prasajatīti.
body.translated_text: 'In brief' — in detail. For the easy understanding of students, the <s>Ācārya</s> shows that <s>avijñapti</s>-form briefly in a sentence. '<s>Avijñapti</s> is wholesome or unwholesome form born from informative action (<s>vijñapti</s>) and from concentration (<s>samādhi</s>).' This should be applied as appropriate. That born from bodily and vocal informative action which is wholesome — included in the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) and in [the category of] neither-restraint-nor-non-restraint. The unwholesome —

body.text: atrācāryasaṃghabhadra idam avijñaptilakṣaṇasūtraṃ dūṣayati.
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> criticizes this <s>sūtra</s> defining <s>avijñapti</s>.

children.text:
nyūnaṃ śāstrāpetaṃ hānir atasyāḥ prasajyate tattvaṃ
apiśabdādhikavacanaṃ viśeṣyaṃ aviśeṣitaṃ cātra.
children.translated_text:
'[The definition is] deficient; it departs from the treatise; a loss of that [avijñapti] would follow;
the word <s>api</s> ('also') is an additional word; the qualified [term] is unqualified here.'

body.text: anubandho hi pravāhas tenaiva vyākhātaḥ. na cādyaḥ kṣaṇaḥ pravāho mā bhūd atiprasaṃgaḥ. tasmāt tasyātra lakṣaṇenāsty avarodha iti nyūnaṃ pravāhasya cādravyatvāt adravyam avijñaptir iti śāstrāpetaṃ. samāhitāyāś ca nāsti vikṣiptacittācittakasyānubandha iti sā cāvijñaptir na prasajyata iti hāniḥ. avikṣiptacittakasya tadanubandhān naiṣa doṣa iti cet. śubhāśubhāyā vijñapter avijñaptilakṣaṇaprasaṃga ity atasyāḥ prasajyate tattvaṃ. acittakasyāpīti cāpiśabdavaiyarthyaṃ pūrveṇaiva kṛtatvāt. vikṣiptacittakasyāpīti anena hi sarvasacittakāvasthāgrahaṇaṃ. kā punar anyā avasthā. yā dvitīyenāpiśabdena saṃgṛhyeteti apiśabdādhikavacanaṃ. acittakaṃ cādhikṛtya śubho [Tib. 27a] 'vijñaptyanubandho viśeṣaṇīyaḥ. na ca vyākhyāne 'pi viśeṣita iti viśeṣyam aviśeṣitam.
body.translated_text: For the continuum (<s>anubandha</s>) is indeed the stream (<s>pravāha</s>), and that has been explained by him [in that way]. And the first moment is not the stream — lest there be over-extension. Therefore, the definition obstructs [the first moment] — hence it is 'deficient.' And because the stream is not a substance (<s>dravya</s>), '<s>avijñapti</s> is not a substance' — hence it 'departs from the treatise.' And because for one in concentration, there is no continuum for one whose mind is distracted or without mind, that <s>avijñapti</s> [born from concentration] would not follow — hence 'loss.' [The objection about the word] '<s>avikṣ[ipta]</s>'...

body.text: idaṃ cāparaṃ viśeṣyam aviśeṣitam apratighaṃ rūpam iti. evam anekadoṣaduṣtatvāt na saṃbaddham etal laksaṇam iti. atra brūmaḥ. yat tāvad uktaṃ nyūnaṃ pravāhasyāvijñaptyupadeśād ādyaḥ kṣaṇo nāvijñaptiḥ syād iti. idaṃ tāvad asau praṣṭavyaḥ. ko 'yaṃ pravāho nāma. bahuṣu kṣaṇeṣu pravāha ity ākhyā. yady evaṃ ādyo 'pi kṣaṇaḥ pravāhaḥ sidhyati. prathamakṣaṇaprabhṛtibahuṣu kṣaṇeṣu pravāha iti kṛtvā. tathā hy utsāt taḍāgād vā nirgacchatām udakānām ādyodakāvayavaprabhṛtiṣu pravāhasaṃjñeti. nāsty avyāpitā lakṣaṇasya. yadā cānubadhnātīti anubandha ity acpratyayāntena padena dravyam eva nirdiśyate. tadā nyūnatāśaṃkāpi nāsti. ata eva śāstrāpetatādoṣo 'pi parihṛto bhavati. athāpy anubaṃdhanam anubaṃdha iti sroto 'bhidhīyate. tathāpy adoṣo rūpādhikārāt. pravāhavartitvāt tu pravāhaśabdena pradarśyate. samāhitāyā apy avijñapter agrahaṇaṃ na bhavati. sāpi hi yady api vikṣiptacittācittakasaṃtānaṃ nānubadhnātīti avikṣiptakasacittasaṃtānaṃ tv anubadhnāty eva. avijñaptijātisāmānyena tu vikṣiptācittakasyāpi yo 'nubandhaḥ. sāvijñaptir iti ucyate. yat punar etad uktaṃ. avikṣiptacittakasya tadanubandhān naiṣa doṣa iti ced iti. yady avikṣiptacittasya [Tib. 27b] kevalasya yo 'nubandhaḥ. sāpy avijñaptir iti samāhitāyā avijñaptes tyāgo na bhavatīti bravīṣi. vijñaptir api kuśalākuśalā tathaiva bhavatīty avijñaptis te prāpnotīti. sa cāpy adoṣaḥ śubhāśubha evety avadhāraṇāt. vijñaptir hy avyākṛtāpi saṃbhavatīti. na vijñaptir avijñaptiḥ prasajyate. atha vā prakarṣagater eṣa prasaṃgo na bhaviṣyati. prakarṣeṇa hi yo 'nubandhaḥ. saivāvijñaptiḥ. na ca vijñaptir avijñaptivat prakarṣeṇānubadhnātīti. avijñaptyanirodhe 'pi tannirodhadarśanāt. yad apy uktam. apiśabdādhikavacanam iti. tad apy ayuktam uktaṃ. tathā hy eka eveha sūtre paṭhito 'piśabdaḥ. vṛttau tu tena pudgaladvayena tadarthaḥ sambadhyata iti dviḥ punaḥ paṭhitaḥ. tenaikena sūtrapaṭhitenāpiśabdena vikṣiptaviparītam avikṣiptam acittakaviparītaṃ ca tam eva sacittakaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pudgalam avijñaptyāśrayaṃ bruvann ācāryaḥ svanāmoktaṃ vikṣiptācittakapudgaladvayaṃ jātisāmānyenāvijñaptyāśrayaṃ pradarśayan vijñapticittacaittebhyo 'rthāntarabhūtām avijñaptim ācaṣṭe. traya eva hi pudgalā bhavanti vijñapticittavisabhāgacitto vijñapticittasabhāgacitto acittakaś ca. tatra vijñapticittavisabhāgacitto vikṣiptacitta ihābhipretaḥ. tasya sā vākkāyavijñaptir [Tib. 28a] niruddhā bhavati. acittakasya tu cittacaittā api niruddhā iti. tatra vijñapteś cittacaitasikakalāpāc cārthāntarabhūteyam avijñaptiḥ. yata ebhyo 'nubandhinītvena viśiṣyate. tam evārthaṃ darśayann āha.
body.translated_text: And this is another objection: the object of qualification is left unqualified — [namely,] 'non-resistant form.' Thus, because it is vitiated by many faults, this definition is not valid. To this we say: First, as to the objection that it is too narrow because 'the first moment would not be <s>avijñapti</s> since the instruction [uses the term] stream (<s>pravāha</s>)' — one should first ask: what is this so-called 'stream'? 'Stream' is the designation for many moments. If so, the first moment too qualifies as a stream, since 'stream' applies to the many moments beginning from the first moment. For just as the designation 'stream' applies to the [successive] water-portions starting from the first water-portion issuing from a spring or a reservoir — so the definition is not under-inclusive. And when [the text says] 'follows' (<s>anubadhnāti</s>), meaning 'continuation' (<s>anubandha</s>) — using a word with the <s>ac</s>-suffix — it designates a real entity (<s>dravya</s>) itself, so there is not even a suspicion of under-inclusiveness. For this very reason, the fault of departing from the treatise is also avoided. And even if 'continuation' (<s>anubandha</s>) means 'the process of following' and designates a stream — even so, there is no fault, because of the context of form (<s>rūpa</s>). But because it operates in a stream, it is indicated by the word 'stream.' There is no non-inclusion of the <s>avijñapti</s> [arising from] meditative concentration either. For although that [<s>avijñapti</s> from concentration] does not follow the continuum of one with a distracted mind or one without mind, it does follow the continuum of one without distraction and with mind. But by the generic class of <s>avijñapti</s>, the continuation even of one with distracted or no mind is called '<s>avijñapti</s>.' And as to the further objection: 'If there is no fault because it follows the continuum of one without distracted mind' [Tib. 27b] — if you say that only the continuation of one without distracted mind is also <s>avijñapti</s>, such that there is no abandonment of the <s>avijñapti</s> from concentration — then <s>vijñapti</s> (manifest action) too, being likewise wholesome or unwholesome, would turn out to be <s>avijñapti</s> for you. But that too is not a fault, because of the restrictive specification 'only wholesome or unwholesome' — since <s>vijñapti</s> can also be morally indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>), <s>vijñapti</s> does not turn out to be <s>avijñapti</s>. Alternatively, this unwanted consequence will not arise because of the intensity of continuation. For that which follows with intensity is <s>avijñapti</s> itself, and <s>vijñapti</s> does not follow with intensity like <s>avijñapti</s>. 'Even when <s>avijñapti</s> has not ceased' — because the cessation of that is observed [separately]. And as to the objection regarding 'the word <s>api</s> being superfluous' — that too is improperly stated. For only one <s>api</s> particle is read in this <s>sūtra</s>. But in the commentary, its meaning connects with two [types of] persons, and so it is read twice. Thus, by the single <s>api</s> particle read in the <s>sūtra</s>,

children.translated_text: 'even of one with distracted mind or without mind' —

body.text: avikṣiptacittasyāvijñaptir vartata iti nātiśayaḥ. vijñaptir api hi tasya vartate. vikṣiptacittasyāpi tu vartata ity atiṣayaḥ. vijñaptir hi tasya nāsti. avijñaptis tv anubandhinīti vijñapter viśiṣyate. tathā vikṣiptacittakasyāvijñaptir vartata iti nātiśayaḥ. cittacaittā api hi tasya vartanta eva. acittakasyāpi tu vartate iti atiśayaḥ. tasya hi cittacaittā niruddhāḥ. avijñaptis tv anubandhinīti cittacaittebhyo viśiṣyate. tad evaṃ dharmāntaraviśeṣaṇārthaṃ avikṣiptacitto vikṣiptācittakatṛtīyabhūtas tenaikenāpy apiśabdenābhidhīyate. ata eva cāpiśabdenāvikṣiptasacittakasyāpīty uktam ācāryeṇa. tṛtīyabhūtatvāt. itarathā hy apiśabdenāvikṣiptacittakasyāpīty evāvakṣyat sacittakasyāpīti vā. tadyathā trayo loke manuṣyāḥ. eko dhanavān itarāv api dhanamātravantau. tāv abhisamīkṣya viṣṇumitrasya dhanam astīty ekenokte dvitīyo vaktā bhavet. evadattayajñadattayor [Tib. 28b] api dhanam astīti. apiśabdena viṣṇumitrasyāpy astīti. evadattayajñadattagatena dvaitam ivāpannenāpiśabdena sa eva viṣṇumitro lakṣyate na tv avasṛjyate ity arthaḥ. tena nātrāpiśabdo 'dhika eva. tadvad ihāpi draṣṭavyaṃ. yat punar etad uktaṃ. acittakaṃ cādhikṛtya śubho 'vijñaptyanubandho viśeṣaṇīya iti. tad api na kiṃcit. avijñaptijātim adhikṛtyaital lakṣaṇaṃ praṇītaṃ. sā cāvijñaptijātir acittakasya bhavatīti etāvad vivakṣitaṃ. kim anena viśeṣitena. tvadīye 'py avijñaptilakṣaṇe śubho 'vijñaptyanubandho acittakam adhikṛtya na viśeṣitaḥ.
body.translated_text: That <s>avijñapti</s> operates for one without distracted mind is not extraordinary, since <s>vijñapti</s> too operates for him. But that it also operates for one with distracted mind — this is extraordinary.

children.text:
kṛte 'pi visabhāge 'pi citte cittātyaye ca yat
vyākṛtāpratighaṃ rūpaṃ sā hy avijñaptir iṣyata
children.translated_text: 'That morally determinate, non-resistant form which [exists even] when the mind is changed, when it is of a dissimilar class, and when there is no mind — that is considered <s>avijñapti</s>'

body.text: iti. eṣā ca vijñaptisaṃbhūtā kuśalaivāvijñaptir acittakasya saṃbhavatīti caturthe kośasthāne jñāpayiṣyate. yac cāpratigham iti aviśeṣitam iti. tad api paścād darśayiṣyāmaḥ.
body.translated_text: — this <s>avijñapti</s>, produced from <s>vijñapti</s>, being wholesome alone, occurs for one without mind — this will be explained in the fourth section of the <s>Kośa</s>. And regarding

body.text: ity atra. daśaiva dhātavaḥ sapratighā ity avadhāraṇāt. avijñaptir dharmadhātuparipaṭhitā. sā tv apratigheti setsyati. tasmād idam āsmākīnam evam adoṣaduṣṭam avijñaptilakṣaṇam iti. tad evāstu.
body.translated_text: here, by the restriction 'only the ten elements are resistant,' <s>avijñapti</s>, which is enumerated under the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> (element of phenomena), will be established as non-resistant.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. dhātugrahaṇaṃ varṇasaṃsthānātmakapṛthivyādinirāsārthaṃ. svalakṣaṇopādāyarūpadhāraṇād [Tib. 29a] dhātava iti. kāṭhinyādisvalakṣaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: and so on in detail. The use of the word 'element' (<s>dhātu</s>) is for the purpose of excluding earth, etc. that consists of color and shape. 'Elements' because they hold (<s>dhāraṇa</s>) their own characteristics [Tib. 29a] as derivative form (<s>upādāya-rūpa</s>).

body.text: cakṣurādyupādāyarūpaṃ ca dadhātīti dhātavaḥ. aṣṭādaśadhātavas tu svasāmānyalakṣaṇadhāraṇāt. gotrārtho vā dhātvarthaḥ dhāraṇārtham anapeksya. ṣaḍdhādhātudeśanāyāṃ punarbhavabījārtho vā dhātvarthaḥ bhavaṃ puṣṇantīti kṛtvā. mahattvam eṣāṃ sarvānyarūpāśrayatvenaudārikatvād iti. sarvopādāyarūpāśrayatvena mahattvād ity arthaḥ. tadudbhūtavṛttiṣv iti. tair mahābhūtair udbhūtā vyaktā vṛttir dhṛtyādikā yeṣu. ta ime tadudbhūtavṛttayaḥ pṛthivyaptejovāyuskandhāḥ. teṣu. eṣāṃ mahābhūtānāṃ mahāsaṃniveśatvān mahāracanatvāt bhūtaṃ tanvantīti bhūtāni.
body.translated_text: They are 'elements' because they hold derivative form such as the eye, etc. But the eighteen elements [are called so] because they hold both their own and general characteristics. Alternatively, the meaning of 'element' (<s>dhātu</s>) is 'lineage' (<s>gotra</s>).

children.translated_text: 'Established through functions such as holding, etc.' —

body.text: iti. dhṛtyādikarmanirdeśaḥ pṛthivyādiṣu śeṣānumānārthaṃ. upalādike hi pṛthivīdravye saṃgrahapaktivyūhanadarśanāc cheṣāṇāṃ jalatejovāyūnām astitvam anumīyate. apsu nausaṃdhāraṇoṣṇateraṇakarmadarśanāt pṛthivītejovāyūnām astitvaṃ. agnijvālāyāṃ sthairyasampiṇḍanacalanadarśanāt pṛthivyudakavāyūnām astitvaṃ. vāyau saṃdhāraṇaśītoṣṇasparśadarśanāt pṛthivyaptejasām astitvam iti vaibhāṣikāḥ. vyūhanaṃ punar vṛddhiḥ prasarpaṇaṃ veti. vṛddhiḥ sambandhādhikaśarīraṃkurādyavayavotpattiḥ. prasarpaṇaṃ śarīrādīnāṃ prabandhena deśantarotpattiḥ.
body.translated_text: The indication of functions such as holding, etc. for earth, etc. is for the purpose of inferring the remaining [elements]. For in material substances like stone, etc. belonging to earth, the functions of cohesion, maturation, and arrangement of the remaining [elements] are observed.

body.text: svabhāvābhidhāne 'pi bhāvapratyayaḥ. uṣṇa eva uṣṇateti. [Tib. 29b] deśantarotpādanāt pradīperaṇavad iti. kṣaṇikānāṃ nāsti deśāntaragamanaṃ yatraivotpattiḥ. tatraiva vināśaḥ. tenaivam ucyate. deśāntarotpādanasvabhāvā bhūtasrotasa īraṇā. kṣaṇikatvāt. pradīpavat. kṣaṇikāni ca bhūtāni. rūpatvāt. pradīpavat. pradīpaś ca kṣaṇikaḥ prasiddha ity udāharaṇaṃ. karmaṇāsya svabhāvo 'bhivyakta iti. īraṇākarmaṇā laghutvaṃ viśiṣyate. yad īraṇātmakaṃ laghutvaṃ. sa vāyudhātur iti. laghusamudīraṇo vāyudhātuḥ. laghv eva tu yat. tad upādāyarūpaṃ.
body.translated_text: even though it expresses an intrinsic nature, the <s>bhāva</s>-suffix is [used merely to form the abstract noun]: 'heat' means simply 'the hot one.' [Tib. 29b] 'Because it produces [fire] in another location, like a lamp or a fan' — for momentary [entities], there is no [actual movement].

body.text: (I.13) pravacane pṛthivīdhātvādayaḥ pṛthivyādayaś coktā ity ataḥ pṛcchati. kaḥ punar eṣāṃ viśeṣa iti.
body.translated_text: (I.13) 'In the [Buddha's] teaching, the earth-element, etc. and earth, etc. have been mentioned' — therefore he asks: 'What then is the distinction between them?'

body.text: lokasaṃvyavahāreṇa. vātyeti vātānāṃ samūho vātyā. brāhmaṇādibhyo yann iti samūhārthe yanpratyayaḥ. strītvāc cāppratyayaḥ.
body.translated_text: means 'by worldly convention.' '<s>Vātyā</s>' (windstorm) is a collective mass of winds. The <s>yan</s>-suffix is in the sense of collectivity, from [words like] '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>, etc.' And the <s>āp</s>-suffix is because of feminine gender.

body.text: tathā hy arthavargīyeṣūktam iti. arthavargīyāṇi sūtrāṇi kṣudrake paṭhante.
body.translated_text: 'For it is stated in the <s>Arthavargīya</s> [sūtras]' — the <s>Arthavargīya</s> sūtras are recited in the <s>Kṣudraka</s> [collection].

body.text: teṣūktaṃ.
body.translated_text: In those it is stated:

children.translated_text: 'For him who is desiring' (<s>tasya cet kāmayānasya</s>) —

body.text: vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: and so on in detail.

body.text: dehinaḥ
body.translated_text: means 'for the embodied being.'

children.translated_text: 'Who is desiring' means 'in whom desire has arisen.'

body.text: yadi
body.translated_text: 'If' —

body.text: viṣayā
body.translated_text: means 'sense-objects.'

body.text: na sampadyante.
body.translated_text: means 'do not come to fruition.'

children.translated_text: 'He is afflicted (<s>rūpyate</s>) as if pierced by an arrow.'

body.text: bādhyata ity arthaḥ. bādhanārthaparicchinnenānena rūpyateśabdena rūpyate rūpyata iti bhikṣava ity atra sūtre rūpyateśabdo bādhanārtha eva paricchidyate. śalyaviddhaḥ kāmayānaś ca [Tib. 30a] duḥkhavedayitṛtvād bādhyata iti yuktaṃ. rūpaṃ tu kathaṃ bādhyate. ata āha. vipariṇāmotpādaneti. vikriyotpādanety arthaḥ. tathā cehārthe sati
body.translated_text: The meaning is: 'he is tormented.' By this word <s>rūpyate</s>, determined in the sense of tormenting, [<s>Vasubandhu</s> explains] the word <s>rūpyate</s> in the <s>sūtra</s> 'It is tormented (<s>rūpyate</s>), O monks' —

children.translated_text: 'Afflicted as if pierced by an arrow' —

body.text: ity atrāpi yadi vikriyata ity artho gṛhyate. sutarām artho yujyate. pratighāta iti. svadeśe parasyotpattipratibandhaḥ. paramāṇurūpaṃ tarhīti. dravyaparamāṇurūpaṃ na rūpaṃ prāpnoti. kasmāt. arūpaṇāt. niravayavatve sati arūpaṇād ity abhiprāyaḥ. pakṣadvaye 'py etac codyam upanyastaṃ. bādhanarūpaṇe pratighātarūpaṇe ca dravyaparamāṇur niravayavatvān na śakyate rūpayitum iti. na vai paramāṇurūpam ekaṃ pṛthagbhūtam astīti. ekam iti grahaṇaṃ dravyaparamāṇusaṃdarśanārthaṃ. pṛthagbhūtam asaṃghātastham ity arthaḥ. tad īdṛg nāsti. saṃghātasthaṃ nityaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: here too, if the meaning 'it is altered' is taken, the point is all the more valid. '<s>Pratigḥāta</s>' (resistance/obstruction) means: the obstruction of the arising of another [entity] in its own location.

children.translated_text: 'In the desire [realm], there are eight material [substances], excluding sound' —

body.text: ityādivacanāt saṃghātasthaṃ tad rūpyata eveti. arthād etad abhīṣṭaṃ bhavati. tad dravyaparamāṇurūpaṃ saṃghātasthaṃ rūpyate bādhyate pratihanyate ca. atītānāgataṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. atītānāgatam adeśatvān na rūpyate na bādhyate nāpi pratihanyate. tad apīti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 30b] tad api rūpitam ity atītabādhanapratighātanārthena. rūpayiṣyamāṇam ity utpattidharmakam anāgataṃ. tenaivārthadvayena. tajjātīyaṃ cety utpattidharmakajātīyam anutpattidharmakam
body.translated_text: From statements such as this, [we understand that] it is form (<s>rūpa</s>) precisely as it exists in an aggregate (<s>saṃghāta</s>). This is the intended [meaning] by implication. That which is the substance-atomic form (<s>dravyaparamāṇurūpa</s>), existing in an aggregate, is altered (<s>rūpyate</s>), obstructed (<s>bādhyate</s>), and resisted (<s>pratihanyate</s>). 'What about past and future [form]?' — this is the elaboration. Past and future [form], being without location, is not altered, not obstructed, and not resisted. 'That too' — this is the elaboration. [Tib. 30b] 'That too was altered' means in the sense of past obstruction and resistance. 'That which will be altered' means future [form] that has the nature of arising — with those same two meanings. 'And of the same kind' means future [form] without the nature of arising, which is of the same kind as [form] with the nature of arising

body.text: anāgataṃ. iṃdhanavat. yad apīddhaṃ yad apīndhiṣyamāṇaṃ tajjātīyaṃ ca. tad apīndhanam. tajjātīyaṃ punar indhanaṃ yad indhanārthe kalpitam aprāpyaivāgnim aṃtarā naṃkṣyati. avijñaptis tarhi na rūpaṃ prāpnoti. kasmāt. apratighatvāt. apratighatvena hi sā na bādhyate nāpi pratihanyate. sāpi vijñaptirūpaṇād iti vistaraḥ. vijñaptir avijñaptisamutthāpikā. tasyāḥ sapratighāyā rūpaṇāt avijñaptir api rūpyate. yathā chāyāsamutthāpakasya vṛkṣasya pracalanāt chāyā pracalati. tadvat. nāvikārād iti. anena pratijñādoṣa udgrāhyate. pareṇa hy evaṃ pratijñātaṃ. svasamutthāpakavikārānuvidhāyinī avijñaptiḥ. samutthāpyatvāt. vṛkṣachāyāvad iti. seyaṃ pūrvābhyupagamavirodhinī pratijñā. abhyupagato hi vijñapter vikāre 'pi avijñapter avikāraḥ. tathā hy aṃjaliṃ bhaṃktvā kapotaṃ kurvataḥ kāyavijñaptir vikriyata ity abhyupagamyate na tv avijñaptiḥ. tasmād asādhanam etat. vijñaptinivṛttau vāvijñaptinivṛttiḥ syād [Tib. 31a] ity anena dharmiviśeṣaviparyayo 'py asyāḥ pratijñāyā udgrāhyate. yadi vṛkṣachāyādharma iṣyate vṛkṣanivṛttau chāyānivṛttir dṛṣṭeti. tadvat syāt. atra kaścin nāvikārād iti na samyag etad uktam iti dūṣayati. vikriyata evāvijñaptir vijñaptivikāre sati. mṛdumadhyādhimātratve hi vijñapter mṛdumadhyādhimātratā bhavaty avijñapter iti. tad etad ayuktaṃ. kasmāt. utpattir evāvijñapter evaṃ bhavati. mṛdur madhyādhimātrā vā. na tu vikāraḥ. utpannasya hi dharmasya punaranyathotpādanaṃ vikāraḥ. tac ca rūpaṇam abhipretam. āśrayabhūtarūpaṇād iti apara iti. vṛddhācāryavasubandhuḥ. bhūtagrahaṇam āśrayabhūtapradarśanārthaṃ. ataś cetaraḥ prasaṃjayati. evaṃ tarhi cakṣurvijñānādīnām apīti vistaraḥ. cakṣurādyāśrayarūpaṇāt tadvijñānānām api rūpatvaprasaṃgaḥ. viṣamo 'yam upanyāsa iti. vṛddhācāryavasubandhudeśīyaḥ kaścit pariharati. avijñaptir hīti vistaraḥ. chāyā vṛkṣam upaśliṣṭāśritya vartate. prabhāpi maṇiṃ tathaiva. utpattinimittamātraṃ tāni teṣām iti. nopaśliṣṭānīti bhāvaḥ. tam itaraḥ itaraḥ. pratyāha. idaṃ tāvad avaibhāṣikīyam iti vistaraḥ. naitad vaibhāṣikamataṃ. vaibhāṣikamataṃ tu chāyā varṇaparamāṇuḥ svabhūtacatuṣkam āśritya vartate [Tib. 31b] na vṛkṣaṃ. tathā prabhā varṇaparamāṇuḥ svabhūtacatuṣkam āśritya vartate na maṇiṃ. pṛthagdravyatvāt. ity evam anāśrayakāraṇatvān maṇivṛkṣayoḥ na mahābhūtavijñaptivat upaśliṣṭe chāyāprabhe iti asāmānyaṃ dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayoḥ. saty api ca tadāśritatva iti vistaraḥ. athāpi pāraṃparyeṇa tadāśritatvam abhyupagamyate. chāyā svabhūtāśritā. tāni tu bhūtāni vṛkṣam āśritāni. prabhāpi svabhūtāśritā. tāni tu bhūtāni maṇim āśritāni. tadanuvidhāyitvāt. tathāpy asāmānyaṃ.
body.translated_text: . Like fuel. Whatever has been burned, whatever will be burned, and whatever is of the same kind — that too is fuel. 'Of the same kind' here means fuel that was designated for the purpose of fuel but will perish without ever reaching fire. [Objection:] Then <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifestation) should not be form. Why? Because it is non-resistant (<s>apratigha</s>). For by being non-resistant, it is not obstructed nor resisted. 'That too, because of the alteration by <s>vijñapti</s> (manifestation)' — this is the elaboration. <s>Vijñapti</s> is the originator of <s>avijñapti</s>. Because of the alteration of that [vijñapti] which is resistant, <s>avijñapti</s> too is altered. Just as a shadow moves from the moving of the tree that produces the shadow — similarly. 'Not from transformation' — by this, a flaw in the thesis is pointed out. For the opponent has made this thesis: '<s>Avijñapti</s> follows the transformations of its own originator, because it is produced [by it], like the shadow of a tree.' But this thesis contradicts the earlier concession. For it is conceded that even when <s>vijñapti</s> transforms, <s>avijñapti</s> does not transform. Thus, when one who has folded his hands [in añjali] then makes [the gesture of] a pigeon, the bodily <s>vijñapti</s> transforms — this is conceded — but not the <s>avijñapti</s>. Therefore this [argument] fails to prove [its point]. 'Or, when <s>vijñapti</s> ceases, <s>avijñapti</s> should cease' [Tib. 31a] — by this, a reversal of the subject-property (<s>dharmiviśeṣaviparyaya</s>) of this thesis is also pointed out. If the property of being like a tree's shadow is accepted, then just as when the tree ceases, the shadow is seen to cease, similarly [avijñapti should cease when vijñapti ceases]. Here, someone objects: 'Not from transformation' — this is not correctly stated, [they say,] because <s>avijñapti</s> does indeed transform when <s>vijñapti</s> transforms. For when <s>vijñapti</s> [varies in] mild, medium, and intense [degrees], <s>avijñapti</s> also becomes mild, medium, and intense. But this is unjustified. Why? Because it is only the arising of <s>avijñapti</s> that occurs in this way — mild, medium, or intense — not a transformation. For a <s>dharma</s> that has arisen [cannot] again

body.text: niruddheṣv apy avijñaptyāśrayeṣu mahābhūteṣu tasyā anirodhābhyupagamād iti.
body.translated_text: even when the material elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>) that are the basis of <s>avijñapti</s> have ceased, [the Vaibhāṣikas] accept the non-cessation of that [avijñapti].

children.translated_text: 'From the [next] moment onward, <s>avijñapti</s> arises from [elements of] the desire[-realm], obtained, past, and element-born' —

body.text: siddhāntāt. tasmān na bhavaty eṣa parihāra iti. ya ukto 'bhūd avijñaptir hi chāyeva vṛkṣam iti vistareṇa.
body.translated_text: this is from established doctrine. Therefore, this resolution does not hold — the one that was stated, [namely] '<s>avijñapti</s> is like a shadow to a tree' — and so on in detail.

body.text: anye punar atra parihāram āhur iti. ayam evācāryas tan mataṃ samarthayann āha. āśrayo bhedaṃ gata iti. dvividha ity arthaḥ. kaścid rūpyate cakṣurādiḥ sapratighatvāt. kaścin na rūpyate. manaḥ. viparyayāt. tasmād asamānaḥ prasaṃga iti. cakṣurvijñānādīnām apy āśrayabhūtarūpaṇād rūpatvaprasaṃga iti. rūpaṇād rūpam ity āśrayarūpaṇād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Others, however, offer this resolution here' — the same <s>Ācārya</s>, setting forth their view, says: 'The basis has undergone division' — meaning it is twofold. Some [bases] are altered — the eye and the rest — because of being resistant. Some are not altered — the mind — because of the opposite. Therefore the analogy is not the same. [Objection:] The eye-consciousness and the rest, too, because the form that is their basis is altered, should [themselves] be form. [Reply:] Form

body.text: atra codayanti. vijñaptisaṃbhūtāyā avijñapter evaṃ parikareṇa rūpatvaṃ bhavad bhavet. samādhisaṃbhūtāyās tu kathaṃ rūpatvam iti. tajjātīyatvāt tad api rūpaṃ. [Tib. 32a] kiṃ punas tajjātīyatvaṃ. mahābhūtāny upādāyeti bhāvaḥ. teṣām upādāyarūpajananādihetubhūtatvād iti.
body.translated_text: Here they raise an objection: For <s>avijñapti</s> originating from <s>vijñapti</s>, [its] being form may perhaps [be established] through such an elaborate procedure. But for <s>avijñapti</s> originating from <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), how is it form? [Reply:] Because it is of the same kind, that too is form. [Tib. 32a] What then is 'being of the same kind'? It means 'in dependence on the great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>)' — this is the implication. Because those [great elements] serve as the cause for producing derived form (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>) and the like.

children.translated_text: 'The sense-faculties and their objects — those very [dharmas]' —

body.text: bhagavato vineyavaśāt tisro deśanāḥ skandhāyatanadhātudeśanāḥ. tāsu ca ye skandheṣu deśitā dharmāḥ. ta eva āyatanadhātuṣu deśitāḥ. asaṃskṛtās tv atra kevalam atiriktāḥ. sarvaś cābhidharmaḥ sūtravyākhyānaṃ. ata idam uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: According to those to be trained, the Blessed One gave three teachings: the <s>skandha</s> (aggregate), <s>āyatana</s> (sense-base), and <s>dhātu</s> (element) teachings. And the <s>dharmas</s> that were taught in [the context of] the <s>skandhas</s> — those very ones were taught in the <s>āyatanas</s> and <s>dhātus</s>. Only the unconditioned [dharmas] are additionally [included] here. And all <s>Abhidharma</s> is an explanation of the <s>sūtras</s>. Therefore this is said:

children.translated_text: 'The sense-faculties and their objects — those very [dharmas]' —

body.text: vistaraḥ. lāghavikaś cāyam ācāryo vedanādiskandhalakṣaṇam anuktvaiva lāghavena rūpaskandhasvabhāvān dharmān āyatanadhātuṣu darśayati. indriyāṇi ca indriyārthāś ca
body.translated_text: this is the elaboration. And this <s>Ācārya</s>, favoring brevity, without even stating the characteristics of the feeling-aggregate and the rest, concisely shows the <s>dharmas</s> that are the nature of the form-aggregate in the <s>āyatanas</s> and <s>dhātus</s>. 'The sense-faculties and the objects of the sense-faculties' —

body.text: viśeṣaṇam anyendriyanirāsārthaṃ anyārthanirāsārthaṃ ca. āyatanavyavasthāyāṃ tu yathāsaṃkhyena daśāyatanāni cakṣurāyatanaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ yāvat kāyāyatanaṃ spraṣṭavyāyatanam iti. dhātuvyavasthāyāṃ ta eva daśa dhātavaḥ cakṣurdhātū rūpadhātur yāvat kāyadhātuḥ spraṣṭavyadhātur iti.
body.translated_text: [this] qualifying [word] is for the purpose of excluding other sense-faculties and other objects. In the <s>āyatana</s> classification, by the method of enumeration, [there are] ten <s>āyatanas</s>: the eye <s>āyatana</s>, the form <s>āyatana</s>, up to the body <s>āyatana</s> and the tangible <s>āyatana</s>. In the <s>dhātu</s> classification, those very ten [become] <s>dhātus</s>: the eye <s>dhātu</s>, the form <s>dhātu</s>, up to the body <s>dhātu</s> and the tangible <s>dhātu</s>.

body.text: (I.14cd, 15) ukto rūpaskandhas tasya cāyatanadhātuvyavasthānam iti. na sakalasya rūpaskandhasyāyatanadhātuvyavasthānam uktaṃ. avijñaptirūpasya vakṣyamāṇatvāt. katham idam ucyate. uktam iti. bāhuliko nirdeśaḥ. bāhulyena rūpaskandhasyāyatanadhātuvyavasthānam uktam ity arthaḥ. katipayamudgagulikāsambhave 'pi māṣarāśivyapadeśavat.
body.translated_text: (I.14cd, 15) 'The form-aggregate has been stated, and its <s>āyatana</s> and <s>dhātu</s> classification' — not the entire form-aggregate's <s>āyatana</s>-<s>dhātu</s> classification has been stated, because <s>avijñapti</s>-form is yet to be explained. How then is 'stated' said? It is a statement in terms of the majority. The <s>āyatana</s>-<s>dhātu</s> classification of the form-aggregate has been stated for the most part — this is the meaning. Like a few <s>mudga</s>-bean pellets [missing from a heap does not negate the description of the heap].

body.text: trividho 'nubhava iti. [Tib. 32b] anubhūtir anubhava upabhogaḥ. kasya. cittasya pudgalasya vā. sa ca trividhaḥ. sukho duḥkho 'duḥkhāsukhaś ca.
body.translated_text: 'Experience (<s>anubhava</s>) is threefold' — [Tib. 32b] <s>Anubhūti</s>, <s>anubhava</s>, <s>upabhoga</s> [are synonyms]. Of what? Of the mind, or of the person. And it is threefold: pleasant, painful, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant.

body.text: vastuno hlādaparitāpatadubhayavinirmuktasvarūpasākṣātkaraṇasvabhāvaḥ. anubhūyate vānena viṣaya ity anubhavaḥ. anubhavatīti vānubhavaḥ. kāyacittopacayāpacayatadubhayavinirmuktāvasthāpravṛttaś caiasikaviśeṣaḥ sparśānubhava ity apare. anur lakṣaṇe sparśacihnaḥ. sparśanimittānubhava ity arthaḥ. sa vedanāskandhaḥ. nimittodgrahaṇātmiketi. nimittaṃ vastuno avasthāviśeṣo nīlatvādi. tasyodgrahaṇaṃ paricchedaḥ. tadātmikā tatsvabhāvā. duḥkhādīty ādiśabdena lohitādīnāṃ grahaṇam. asau saṃjñāskandhaḥ. yadi paricchedātmikā saṃjñā tatsaṃprayoge nimittam udgṛhṇantīti paṃcāpi vijñānakāyā vikalpakāḥ syuḥ. na syuḥ. na hi paṃcavijñānasaṃprayoginī saṃjñāpaṭvī. manovijñānakāyasaṃprayoginī tu paṭvīti tad eva vikalpakam uktaṃ. ṣaṭ saṃjñākāyā vedanāvad iti. yathā cakṣuḥsaṃsparśajā vedaneti vistareṇoktaṃ. tathā cakṣuḥsaṃsparśajā saṃjñeti vistareṇa vaktavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: Its nature is the direct realization of the intrinsic nature of an object as agreeable, disagreeable, or free from both. Or, '<s>anubhava</s>' because the object is experienced (<s>anubhūyate</s>) by it. Or, '<s>anubhava</s>' because it experiences (<s>anubhavati</s>). Others [define it as:] a specific mental factor operating in the state of increase, decrease, or freedom from both, of body and mind — [that is] contact-experience (<s>sparśānubhava</s>). <s>Anu</s> [means] 'mark' — marked by contact. The meaning is: experience [that follows] the sign of contact. That is <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) —

body.text: iti. caturbhyaḥ skandhebhyaḥ skandhādhikārāt. rūpaskandhādibhyas [Tib. 33a] tribhya uktebhyo vijñānaskandhāc coddiṣṭavakṣyamāṇakāc caturbhyo 'nye saṃskārāḥ saṃskāraskandhaḥ. sūtre ṣaṭ cetanākāyā ity uktam iti. saṃskāraskandhaḥ katamaḥ. ṣaṭ cetanākāyā iti. abhisaṃskaraṇe pradhāneti. evaṃ caivaṃ ca syām ity abhisaṃskaraṇe pradhānā. karma hetur upapattaya iti vacanāt. chandaprāptyādayas tu cetanānuvidhāyitvāt tadākārahetubhāvānuvidhānataḥ saṃskāraskandha eva veditavyāḥ. tad evaṃ sati saṃskaraṇe pravṛtto dharmarāśiḥ saṃskāra ity uktaṃ bhavati. apare punar āhuḥ. saṃskṛtābhisaṃskaraṇe cetanāyāḥ prādhānyam uktam. ataḥ sūtre cetanāgrahaṇaṃ. saṃprayuktaviprayuktasaṃskṛtadharmasaṃgraheṇa tu prādhānyād ayam eva skandhaḥ saṃskāraskandha uktaḥ. saṃskṛtarāśir iti kṛtvā. saṃskṛtam abhisaṃskarotīti bhāvinyā saṃjñayā anāgataṃ skandhapaṃcakaṃ saṃskṛtam ity uktam. anyathā hīti vistaraḥ. yadi yathāsūtranirdeśaṃ cetanaiva kevalā saṃskāraskandha iṣyate nānye. śeṣāṇāṃ chandādīnāṃ caitasikānāṃ prāptyādīnāṃ ca cittaviprayuktānāṃ skandhāsaṃgrahāt. rūpādiṣu skandheṣu rūpaṇādilakṣaṇābhāvenāsaṃgrahāt. saṃskāraskandhe caivaṃ. sūtre yathārutagrahaṇenāsaṃgrahāt. iti skandheṣv asaṃgrahād duḥkhasamudayasatyatvaṃ na syāt. iti parijñāprahāṇe na syātāṃ. [Tib. 33b] parijñā duḥkhasya prahāṇaṃ samudayasya. anabhijñāya laukikena mārgeṇa aparijñāya lokottareṇa. atha vānabhijñāya darśanamārgeṇa aparijñāya bhāvanāmārgeṇā. evam aprahāyety uktam iti sūtrāntaraṃ. naham ekadharmam
body.translated_text: other than the four <s>skandhas</s> — because we are in the topic of <s>skandhas</s>. Other than the three [already] stated — the form-aggregate and the rest — [Tib. 33a] and other than the consciousness-aggregate, which has been indicated and will be explained: [these are] the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — the <s>saṃskāra</s>-aggregate. In the <s>sūtra</s>, 'the six bodies of <s>cetanā</s> (volition)' is stated — [meaning:] 'What is the <s>saṃskāra</s>-aggregate? The six bodies of <s>cetanā</s>.' Because [volition] is predominant in the act of conditioning (<s>abhisaṃskaraṇa</s>). And thus and thus it would be —

body.text: api aparijñāyāprahāya duḥkhasyāntakriyāṃ vadāmīti. duḥkhanirodhaṃ vadāmīty arthaḥ. nanu cākāśāpratisaṃkhyānirodhau lokottareṇa mārgeṇa na parijñāyete. atha ca duḥkhasyāntakriyeṣyate. saṃkleśavastvabhisaṃdhivacanāt. sautrāntikadarśanena ca prajñaptisattvād adoṣaḥ. na hi tau saṃkleśavastū. kim anayoḥ parijñeyatvena. nirodhamārgasatye api tarhi na saṃkleśavastū iti na parijñeye syātāṃ. duḥkhasamudayasatyasaṃbandhasadbhāvāt tayoḥ parijñeyatvaṃ vyavasthāpyate. tathā hi yogina evaṃ vicārayanti. asya sahetukasya duḥkhasya ko nirodhaḥ. kena copāyena sa nirodhaḥ prāpyata iti. nirodhamārgasatye api parijānanti. na tv ākāśāpratisaṃkhyānirodhayor duḥkhena sambandha iti na tau parijānanti. prayogāvasthāyāṃ tu laukikena jñānena tāv api sāmānyarupeṇa sarvadharmā anātmāna iti bhāvayanti.
body.translated_text: ...'I do not declare the making of an end of suffering without having fully known and abandoned [even a single <s>dharma</s>].' 'I declare the cessation of suffering' — this is the meaning. But surely space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and non-analytical cessation (<s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) are not fully known by the supramundane path. And yet the making of an end of suffering is desired. [Reply:] Because the statement is made with reference to the objects of defilement (<s>saṃkleśavastu</s>). And from the <s>Sautrāntika</s> viewpoint, because they are merely designations, there is no fault — for those two are not objects of defilement. 'What then is the point of their being fully known?' The truths of cessation and the path too are not objects of defilement, so they too should not need to be fully known. [Reply:] The full-knowability of those two is established because of the existence of their connection with the truths of suffering and origination. For practitioners deliberate thus: 'What is the cessation of this suffering that has a cause? And by what method is that cessation attained?' — thus they fully know the truths of cessation and the path as well. But space and non-analytical cessation have no connection with suffering — hence they are not fully known. In the preparatory stage, however, through mundane knowledge, those too are contemplated in a general way: 'all <s>dharmas</s> are non-self.'

body.text: iti. āyatanaṃ ca dhātuś cāyatanadhātū. dharmaś cāsāv āyatanadhātuś ca dharmāyatanadhātuḥ. tadākhyā eṣāṃ ta ime
body.translated_text: 'Sense-base' (<s>āyatana</s>) and 'element' (<s>dhātu</s>) [form the compound] 'sense-base-and-element.' '<s>Dharma</s>' and [it is also] 'sense-base-and-element' — hence '<s>dharma</s>-sense-base-and-element.' Their designation is that — hence these are

body.text: ke. vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāraskandhāḥ.
body.translated_text: Which ones? The feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, and formations aggregate,

body.text: iti. sahāvijñaptyā sahāsaṃskṛtaiś cākāśādibhiḥ. [Tib. 34a] āyatanadeśanāyāṃ dharmāyatanam iti. dhātudeśanāyāṃ ca dharmadhātur iti. sapta dravyāṇīti. avijñaptir vedanāskandhaḥ saṃjñāskandhaḥ saṃskāraskandhaḥ ākāśaṃ pratisaṃkhyānirodho 'pratisaṃkhyānirodhaś ceti.
body.translated_text: together with non-manifest [form] (<s>avijñapti</s>) and together with the unconditioned — space and so forth. In the teaching of sense-bases, [this is called] '<s>dharmāyatana</s>' (the <s>dharma</s> sense-base). And in the teaching of elements, '<s>dharmadhātu</s>' (the <s>dharma</s> element). 'Seven substantial entities' — non-manifest [form], the feeling aggregate, the perception aggregate, the formations aggregate, space, analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>), and non-analytical cessation (<s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>).

body.text: iti. vijñānaskandhaḥ prativijñaptir ity arthaḥ skandhādhikārāt. pratir vīpsārthaḥ. viṣayaṃviṣayaṃ pratīty arthaḥ. upalabdhir vastumātragrahaṇaṃ. vedanādayas tu caitasā viśeṣā viśeṣagrahaṇarūpāḥ. ṣaḍ vijñānakāyā iti ṣaḍ vijñānasamūhāḥ.
body.translated_text: meaning the consciousness aggregate is discernment — because the context is [that of] the aggregates. The prefix '<s>prati</s>' has the sense of distribution — meaning 'with respect to each object.' 'Apprehension' (<s>upalabdhi</s>) is the grasping of the mere entity. Feeling and the others are mental factors — particular [functions] having the nature of grasping particulars. 'Six groups of consciousness' means six collections of consciousness.

body.text: iti. ṣaḍ vijñānadhātavo yāthāsaṃkhyena yaś cakṣurvijñānaṃ. sa cakṣurvijñānadhātuḥ. evaṃ yāvat yan manovijñānaṃ. sa manovijñānadhātuḥ. samastāni tv etāni ṣaṭ manodhātur iti veditavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: The six consciousness-elements, in corresponding order: that which is visual consciousness — that is the visual-consciousness element. And so on up to: that which is mental consciousness — that is the mental-consciousness element. But all these six together should be understood as the mind-element (<s>manodhātu</s>).

children.text: ṣaṇṇām anantarātītaṃ vijñānaṃ yad dhi. tan mana
children.translated_text: 'Of the six, whatever consciousness has just passed — that is mind (<s>manas</s>)' —

body.text: iti.
iti nirdhāraṇe ṣaṣṭhī. teṣām eva madhye nānyad ity arthaḥ. anantaragrahaṇam
body.translated_text: the sixth case-ending here is partitive — meaning 'among them alone and no other.' The word 'immediately preceding' (<s>anantara</s>)

body.text: anyavijñānavyavahitanivṛttyarthaṃ. yad dhi yasyānantaram anyavijñānāvyavahitaṃ. [Tib. 34b] tat tasyāśrayaḥ. vyavahitaṃ tu na tasyāśrayaḥ. anyasyāsāv āśrayaḥ. yasya tadavyavahitaṃ. ata evācittikāvasthāyāṃ cirātītam api samāpattipraveśacittaṃ vyutthānacittasyāśrayo bhavati. vijñānāntarāvyavadhānāt. atītagrahaṇaṃ pratyutpannanirāsārthaṃ. manovijñānaṃ hi āśrayi tasyām avasthāyāṃ pratyutapannaṃ. atas tad atītam iṣyate. tad eva caitad ucyate.
body.translated_text: is for the purpose of excluding [consciousness] that is separated by another consciousness. For what immediately follows without being separated by another consciousness — that is the base [of the next consciousness]. But what is separated is not its base — it is the base of another, [namely] of that for which it is unseparated. For this very reason, even in a mindless state (<s>acittikāvasthā</s>), consciousness that entered the attainment [of cessation], though long past, becomes the base of the emergence-consciousness — because there is no intervening [other] consciousness. The word 'past' (<s>atīta</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the present. For in that state [of mindlessness], mental consciousness is a base; [but the relevant one] in that state is present. Therefore it is desired [to specify it as] past. And this very [point] is stated:

children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of establishing the base of the sixth [consciousness]' —

body.text: iti. vijñānagrahanaṃ vedanādyanantarātītanivṛttyarthaṃ.
body.translated_text: The word 'consciousness' (<s>vijñāna</s>) is for the purpose of excluding feeling and the others that are immediately past.

body.text: iti jātinirdeśān na vīpsāprayogaḥ. vṛttau tu dravyapadārthābhidhitsayā vīpsāprayogaḥ. yadyat samanantaraniruddhaṃ vijñānaṃ tattan manodhātur iti. tadyathā sa eveti vistaraḥ. tadyathā sa eva putro 'nyasya pitrākhyāṃ labhate. tad eva phalam anyasya bījākhyāṃ. tathehāpi sa eva cakṣurādivijñānadhātur anyasyāśraya iti manodhātvākhyāṃ labhate.
body.translated_text: because it is a statement of genus (<s>jāti</s>), the distributive construction is not applied. But in the commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>), intending to express individual substantial entities, the distributive construction is applied: 'Whatever consciousness has ceased immediately before — that is the mind-element.' For example — and so forth in detail. For example, the same son obtains the designation 'father' in relation to another. The same fruit obtains the designation 'seed' in relation to another. Similarly here too, the same visual-consciousness element and so forth obtains the designation 'mind-element' in relation to another as being its base.

body.text: (I.17cd) saptadaśa dhātavo bhavanti dvādaśa veti. ya eva ṣaḍvijñānadhātavaḥ. sa eva manodhātuḥ. ya eva ca manodhātuḥ. ta eva ca ṣaḍvijñānadhātava iti itaretarāntarbhāve yadi ṣaḍvijñānadhātavo gṛhyeran nārtho manodhātuneti saptadaśa dhātavo bhavanti. yadi manodhātur gṛhyeta nārthaḥ sāḍvijñānadhātubhir iti dvādaśa dhātavo bhavanti.
body.translated_text: (I.17cd) 'There are seventeen elements or twelve.' Those very six consciousness-elements are the mind-element, and the mind-element itself is the six consciousness-elements — if, through mutual inclusion, the six consciousness-elements were grasped, there would be no need for the mind-element — [hence] there are seventeen elements. If the mind-element were grasped, there would be no need for the six consciousness-elements — [hence] there are twelve elements.

children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of establishing the base of the sixth' —

body.text: iti. paṃcānāṃ vijñānadhātūnāṃ āśrayaprasiddhir nāṃgīkriyate cakṣurādisvāśrayasaṃbhavāt. manovijñānāśrayo nāstīti tadāśrayaprasiddhyarthaṃ [Tib. 35a] manodhātur vyavasthāpyate. āśrayādiṣaṭkavyavasthānenāṣṭādaśa dhātavo bhavanti. āśrayaṣaṭkaṃ cakṣurādimanontaṃ. āśritaṣaṭkaṃ cakṣurvijñānādimanovijñānāntaṃ. ālambanaṣaṭkaṃ rūpādidharmāntam iti. yogācāradarśanena tu ṣaḍvijñānavyatirikto 'py asti manodhātuḥ. tāmraparṇīyā api hṛdayavastu manovijñānadhātor āśrayaṃ kalpayanti. tac cārūpyadhātāv api vidyata iti varṇayanti. ārūpyadhātāv api hi teṣāṃ rūpam abhipretaṃ. ārūpya iti ec īṣadarthe āṅ āpiṃgalavad iti. caramaṃ cittam iti. nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇakāle. na mano bhaviṣyatīti. na manodhātur bhaviṣyatīty arthaḥ. na hi tad astīti. notpadyata ity arthaḥ. na. tasyāpi manobhāveneti vistaraḥ. naitad evaṃ. kasmāt. tasyāpi caramacittasya manobhāvenāśrayatvenāvasthitatvāt. anyakāraṇavaikalyād iti. paunarbhavikakarmakleśakāraṇavaikalyāt. nottaravijñānasaṃbhūtir iti. na punarbhavapratisaṃdhivijñānam ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: The establishment of a base for the five consciousness-elements is not accepted [as a problem], because the eye and other own-bases exist for them. [But] there is no base for mental consciousness — hence, for the purpose of establishing its base, the mind-element is posited. Through the arrangement of the sixfold base, supported, and object, there are eighteen elements. The sixfold base: eye through mind. The sixfold supported: visual consciousness through mental consciousness. The sixfold object: form through <s>dharmas</s>. But according to the <s>Yogācāra</s> view, there exists a mind-element distinct from the six consciousnesses. The <s>Tāmraparṇīyas</s> [i.e., Theravādins] also posit a 'heart-substance' (<s>hṛdayavastu</s>) as the base of mental-consciousness element. And they assert that it exists even in the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>). For they accept form even in the formless realm — [explaining that] <s>ārūpya</s> [means] 'with minimal form,' the prefix <s>ā</s> being in the sense of 'slightly,' like <s>āpiṅgala</s> ('slightly tawny'). 'The final consciousness' — at the time of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> without remainder. 'Mind will not exist' — meaning the mind-element will not exist. 'For that does not exist' — meaning it does not arise. [Objection:] No — because even that [would have] the nature of mind — and so forth in detail. This is not so. Why? Because even that final consciousness stands as a base through being mind. [The non-arising] is due to the absence of other conditions — namely, the absence of <s>karma</s> and defilement conditions for renewed existence. 'There is no arising of a subsequent consciousness' — the intended meaning is: there is no rebirth-linking consciousness of renewed existence.

body.text: idam iha vicāryate. uktam etat. āśrayāśritālambanaṣaṭkavyavasthānād aṣṭādaśa dhātavo bhavantīti. āśritaṣaṭkaṃ tāvad vyavasthāpyate. cakṣurvijñānadhātur yāvan manovijñānadhātur iti. kim asyāśritaṣaṭkasya yathāsaṃkhyaṃ āśrayaṣatkaṃ vyavasthāpyate. cakṣurvijñānadhātor āśrayaś cakṣurdhātur [Tib. 35b] yāvan manovijñanadhātor manodhātur āśraya iti. om ity āha. yadā tarhi cakṣus tatsabhāgaṃ bhavati. tat kasyāśrayaḥ. na kasyacit. kathaṃ tarhīdam uktaṃ. cakṣurvijñānadhātoś cakṣurdhātur āśraya ityādi. āśraya eva cakṣuḥ. yas tu kiṃcidanāśrayas tatsabhāgaṃ cakṣuḥ. tad api tajjātīyatvāt cakṣurdhātutvena vyavasthāpyata eva. evaṃ yāvat kāyadhātur vaktavyaḥ. manodhātur api kiṃ manovijñānadhātor evāśrayaḥ. nety āha. cakṣurvijñānadhātvādīnām api hi sa āśraya iṣyate. tathā hi vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: This is examined here. It has been stated that through the arrangement of the sixfold base, supported, and object, there are eighteen elements. First the sixfold supported is established: the visual-consciousness element up to the mental-consciousness element. Is the sixfold base established in corresponding order for this sixfold supported — the eye-element as the base of the visual-consciousness element, up to the mind-element as the base of the mental-consciousness element? He says: Yes. But when the eye is in its homogeneous state (<s>tatsabhāga</s>), of what is it the base? Of nothing. Then how was this stated: 'The eye-element is the base of the visual-consciousness element'? [Reply:] The eye is indeed a base; but the eye in its homogeneous state [i.e., not currently supporting consciousness] is not a base of anything — yet even that, being of the same type, is established as being of the eye-element. Similarly up to the body-element should be explained. Is the mind-element the base of the mental-consciousness element alone? He says: No — for it is accepted as the base of the visual-consciousness element and the others too. For it will be stated:

children.translated_text: 'The base of the last [mental consciousness] is past; and [the base] of the five [sense-consciousnesses] is co-arisen with them' —

body.text: iti. kiṃ tarhīdam uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: Then why was this stated:

children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of establishing the base of the sixth, the elements are remembered as eighteen' —

body.text: iti. nānyeṣām āśrayaḥ sa iti kṛtvā ṣaṣṭhāśrayaprasiddhir na bhavati. ṣaṣṭhasyāpy ayam āśrayo bhavati saṃbhavataḥ. ālambanaṣaṭkam api. cakṣurvijñānadhātor ālambanaṃ rūpadhātur yāvan manovijñānadhātor dharmadhātur ālambanam iti. tad idaṃ vicāryate. kiṃ yathā cakṣurvijñānadhātor yāvanti rūpāṇi ālambanaṃ. sa rūpadhātuḥ. evaṃ yāvat kāyavijñānadhātor yāvanti spraṣṭavyāny ālambnaṃ. sa spraṣṭavyadhātuḥ. evaṃ manovijñānadhator yāvanto dharmā ālambanaṃ. sa dharmadhātur iti. atra sthavira āha. sarvadharmasvabhāvo dharmadhātur aṣṭādaśadhātusvabhāva ity arthaḥ. katham asyādhyātmikabāhyadhātuvyavasthā sidhyati. cakṣurādayo hi dvādaśādhyātmikā iṣyante. ṣaḍ bāhyā iti. [Tib. 36a] yadi hi te 'pi dharmadhātāv antarbhāvyeran sāṃkaryaṃ prāpnoti. sthavira āha. pāryāyikam eṣām ādhyātmikabāhyatvaṃ. vijñānānām āśrayās te cakṣurādaya ity ādhyātmikāḥ. manovijñānaviṣayatvāt tu bāhyā iti. tad evaṃ necchanti vaibhāṣikāḥ. sūtravirodhāt. evaṃ hi sūtra uktaṃ. dharmā bhikṣo bāhyam āyatanam ekādaśabhir āyatanair asaṃgṛhītam anidarśanam apratigham iti. tasmāt saptadravyako dharmadhātur eṣṭavyaḥ. avijñaptivedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāraskandhākāśapratisaṃkhyānirodhapratiṣaṃkhyānirodhasvabhāvatvāt. aparipūrṇas tarhi manovijñānadhātor ālambananirdeśaḥ. na ca cakṣurvijñānādīnām aparipūrṇa alambananirdeśa iṣyate. asty etad evaṃ. kiṃ tu cakṣurādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇām āśrayatvena nirdeśāc cakṣurvijñānādīnāṃ cāśritatvena rūpādīnāṃ ca paṃcānāṃ paṃcavijñānakāyālambananirdeśān
body.translated_text: It is not the case that [the mind-element] is the base of no others, such that establishing the base of the sixth is not achieved — it is also a base of the sixth, among its [various functions]. The sixfold object too — the form-element is the object of the visual-consciousness element, up to the <s>dharma</s>-element is the object of the mental-consciousness element. This is examined: Is [the correspondence] such that however many forms are the object of the visual-consciousness element, that is the form-element, and so on up to however many tangibles are the object of the body-consciousness element, that is the tangible-element, and however many <s>dharmas</s> are the object of the mental-consciousness element, that is the <s>dharma</s>-element? Here the Elder [<s>Saṃghabhadra</s>] says: 'The intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s> is the <s>dharma</s>-element' — meaning [it has] the nature of the eighteen elements. [Objection:] How then is the establishment of internal and external elements achieved? For the eye and so forth — the twelve — are accepted as internal, and six as external. If those too were included in the <s>dharma</s>-element, confusion would result. The Elder says: Their internal-ness and external-ness is figurative. Those — the eye and so forth — being bases of consciousness, are 'internal.' But being objects of mental consciousness, they are 'external.' But the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> do not accept this, because it contradicts the <s>Sūtra</s>. For it is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: '<s>Dharmas</s>, O monk, are the external sense-base, not included in the eleven sense-bases, non-indicative, non-resistant.' Therefore, the <s>dharma</s>-element should be accepted as having seven substantial entities — being of the nature of non-manifest [form], feeling aggregate, perception aggregate, formations aggregate, space, analytical cessation, and non-analytical cessation. [Objection:] Then the indication of the object of the mental-consciousness element is incomplete. And an incomplete indication of the object of the visual consciousness and the others is not accepted. [Reply:] This is so. But because the eye and so forth, the six, are indicated as bases, and the visual consciousness and the others as supported, and form and the other five as objects of the five sense-consciousness groups —

body.text: na teśāṃ manovijñānaviṣayatve 'pi dharmadhātau prakṣepa iti varṇayanti.
body.translated_text: even though they are also objects of mental consciousness, they are not thrown into the <s>dharma</s>-element — thus [the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>] explain.

children.translated_text: 'But in summary, one should know the complete inclusion' —

body.text: iti. āyatanādibhir api sarvasaṃgrahaḥ. na tu samāsataḥ. kiṃ tarhi. vistarataḥ. ayaṃ tu deśanātrayān niṣkṛṣya samāsata uktaḥ. rūpaskandhena rūpaskandhaḥ saṃgṛhīto daśa cendriyārthasvabhāvāny āyatanāni dhātavaś ca. dharmāyatanadhātvekadeśaś cāvijñaptiḥ. [Tib. 36b] manaāyatanena vijñānaskandhaḥ. tad eva ca manaāyatanaṃ saptacittadhātavaś ca saṃgṛhītāḥ. dharmadhātunā vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāraskandhāḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ dharmāyatanaṃ dharmadhātuś ca. avijñaptir iha dviḥ saṃgṛhītā. tadyathā cakṣurindriyam iti. cakṣurindriyaṃ vedanādiskandhaśrotrādyāyatanadhātunirodhasatyamārgasatyasvabhāvena viyuktaṃ. ata etad uktaṃ. cakṣurindriyaṃ rūpaskandhena cakṣurāyatanadhātubhyāṃ duḥkhasamudayasatyābhyāṃ ca saṃgṛhītaṃ tatsvabhāvatvāt. nānyaiḥ skandhādibhis tadbhāvaviyuktatvād iti. mahatātrālpakaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ. na tu mahad alpakena. katham iti. rūpaskandho mahān sarvarūpasaṃgrāhakatvāt. cakṣurindriyam alpakaṃ rūpaskandhaikadeśatvāt. rūpaskandhena cakṣurindriyaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ. na tu cakṣurindriyeṇa rūpaskandhaḥ. cakṣurindriyavyatiriktarūpaskandhasadbhāvāt. tadyathā hastipadena pakṣipadaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ. na tu pakṣipadena hastipadaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ. tadvat. samena tu samam anyonyaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ. tadyathā cakṣurindriyaṃ cakṣurāyatanena. cakṣurāyatanam api cakṣurindriyeṇety ayam abhidharmanayo veditavyaḥ. yathā saṃgrahavastubhiḥ parṣadām iti. catvāri saṃgrahavastūni. dānaṃ priyavāditā arthacaryā samānārthatā ca. catasraḥ parṣadab bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ. [tip. 37a] tais tāsāṃ saṃgrahaḥ. sa tu kādācitkaḥ. kadācidbhavaḥ kādācitkaḥ. kadācid āsāṃ dīyate priyaṃ cocyate. na ce saṃgraha iti. sāṃketikaḥ sāṃvyavahārikaḥ. svabhāvasaṃgrahas tu pāramārthika ity uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: Thus. Through <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) and other [categories] too, there is a comprehensive inclusion — but not in brief; rather, in detail. Here, however, extracting from the three [types of] exposition, it is stated in brief. By the form-aggregate, the form-aggregate is included, and the ten <s>āyatanas</s> and <s>dhātus</s> whose nature is that of sense-faculties and their objects, and <s>avijñapti</s> as a portion of the <s>dharma-āyatana</s> and <s>dharma-dhātu</s>. By the mind-<s>āyatana</s>, the consciousness-aggregate [is included]; and that same mind-<s>āyatana</s> and seven consciousness-<s>dhātus</s> are included. By the <s>dharma-dhātu</s>, the feeling, perception, and formations aggregates are included, and the <s>dharma-āyatana</s> and <s>dharma-dhātu</s>. <s>Avijñapti</s> is included twice here. For example, the eye sense-faculty: the eye sense-faculty is disjoined from the nature of the feeling aggregate and others, the ear <s>āyatana</s> and other <s>dhātus</s>, and the truths of cessation and the path. Hence this is said: the eye sense-faculty is included by the form-aggregate, the eye <s>āyatana</s> and eye <s>dhātu</s>, and the truths of suffering and origination, because it has their nature — not by the other aggregates and so on, because it is disjoined from their nature. The larger includes the smaller, but not the larger by the smaller. How? The form-aggregate is large because it includes all form. The eye sense-faculty is small because it is only a portion of the form-aggregate. The eye sense-faculty is included by the form-aggregate, but not the form-aggregate by the eye sense-faculty, because the form-aggregate apart from the eye sense-faculty exists [as well]. Just as a bird's footprint is included by an elephant's footprint, but not an elephant's footprint by a bird's footprint — so too here. But equals include each other mutually. For example, the eye sense-faculty [is included] by the eye <s>āyatana</s>, and the eye <s>āyatana</s> by the eye sense-faculty — this <s>abhidharma</s> principle should be understood. 'Just as assemblies by means of the factors of attraction' — the four factors of attraction are: generosity, affectionate speech, beneficial conduct, and impartiality. The four assemblies are: monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers. The attraction of those [assemblies] by these [factors] is occasional — occurring at some times. Sometimes giving is made or kind words are spoken [to them, but] this is not [the same as their essential] inclusion. [That is merely] conventional, transactional. But inclusion by intrinsic nature is ultimate — thus it is said.

children.translated_text: 'By the commonality of birth, object, and consciousness — there is unity of element, even though there are two of the eye and the rest' —

body.text: ity arthād etad uktaṃ bhavati. jātyādibhedād yathāsaṃbhavaṃ dhātubhedavyavasthānaṃ. na tv adhiṣṭhānabhedād iti. tatra cakṣurdhātvādīnām anyonyaṃ jātigocaravijñānabhedo bhavati. rūpadhātvādīnāṃ jātivijñānabhedaḥ. vijñānadhātūnāṃ jātigocarabhedaḥ. manovijñānasyāpi hi dharmadhātur asādhāraṇo gocaraḥ. evaṃ śrotraghrāṇayor api yojyam iti. jātisāmānyam ubhayoḥ śrotrasvabhāvatvāt. gocarasāmānyam ubhayoḥ śabdaviṣayatvāt.
body.translated_text: the meaning of this is as follows: the establishment of the distinction of elements is according to the distinction of birth and so on, as applicable — not according to the distinction of support-bases. Therein, for the eye <s>dhātu</s> and the rest, there is a mutual distinction of birth, object, and consciousness. For the form <s>dhātu</s> and the rest, a distinction of birth and consciousness. For the consciousness <s>dhātus</s>, a distinction of birth and object. For even mind-consciousness has the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> as its unshared object. This same [analysis] should be applied to the ear and nose as well. Commonality of birth — because both [ears] have the nature of the ear. Commonality of object — because both have sound as their object.

body.text: vijñānasāmānyam ubhayor ekaśrotravijñānāśrayatvāt. tasmād eka eva śrotradhātuḥ. evaṃ ghrāṇasyāpi yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: Commonality of consciousness — because both are the support of one and the same ear-consciousness. Therefore there is only one ear <s>dhātu</s>. The same analysis should be applied to the nose as well.

body.text: (I.19cd) kāryāntarābhāvāt tarhi dvayānutpattiprasaṃgaḥ syād ity ata āha.
body.translated_text: (I.19cd) If there is no other effect [requiring two], then the non-arising of both would follow — hence he says:

children.translated_text: 'But the arising of two is for the sake of beauty' —

body.text: iti. ekacakṣuḥśrotrādhiṣṭhānaikanāsikābilasaṃbhavān mahad vairūpyaṃ syād ity ekasya cakṣuḥśrotrādhiṣṭhānasya ekasya ca nāsikābilasya saṃbhavān mahad vairūpyaṃ syāt. nanu coṣṭramārjārolūkaprabhṛtīnāṃ cakṣurādidvayodbhave 'pi na bhavaty āśrayaśobhā. jātyantarāpekṣayā [Tib. 37b] na teṣām āśrayaśobhā. svajātyapeksayā tu yasya cakṣurādidvayam asti. tasya tasyāṃ svajātāv āśrayaśobhā. yasya nāsti. tasya vairūpyam iti. adūṣyam etat. ācāryasaṃghabhadras tv asya sūtrasyārthaṃ vivavre. śobhārtham ity ādhipatyārtham ity arthaḥ. ādhipatyasaṃpanno hi loke śobhatīty apadiśyate. yeṣāṃ cendriyāṇāṃ amūny adhiṣṭhānāni. teṣāṃ pariśuddhadarśanaśravaṇaghrāṇāyādhipatyaṃ syāt. na hi yathā dvābhyāṃ cakṣurbhyāṃ pariśuddhaṃ darśanaṃ bhavati tathaikena. evam itarayor api. evaṃ caiṣām indriyatvaṃ hīyeta. tadartham etad uktaṃ syād iti. sphuṭopalabdhyartham ity arthaḥ. ihāpi śakyam evaṃ vaktum. ekam eva parisphuṭopalabdhyāśrayabhūtaṃ vistīrṇaṃ karmaṇotpādyatāṃ. kim āśrayavicchedeneti. vibhāṣāyāṃ tu likhitam etat pakṣadvayaṃ. śobhārthaṃ dvayodbhava ity eko vyaktyartham ity apara iti. alaṃ prasaṃgena. nanu ca karmavaśāt indriyadvayotpattiḥ. kim anyad evocyate śobhārthaṃ vyaktyarthaṃ ceti. karmavaśād evātrendriyadvayodbhava uktaḥ. katham iti. evaṃ vibhaktāvayavāśrayeṇānādikālābhyastaḥ śobhābhimānaḥ sattvānāṃ pravartate. atas tadabhilāṣapūrvakeṇa sphuṭopalabdhyabhilāṣapūrvakeṇa ca karmaṇā tad indriyadvayam [Tib. 38a] abhinirvartamānaṃ śobhārthaṃ vyaktyarthaṃ codbhavatīty ucyate.
body.translated_text: thus. Were there to be one support-base for the eye and ear, and one nostril — there would be great disfigurement. From the occurrence of one support-base for the eye and ear and one nostril, great disfigurement would result. But [one might object:] even for camels, cats, owls, and the like, though there is the arising of two eyes and the rest, there is no beauty of the support-body. [Reply:] Relative to another species, there is no beauty of their support-body. But relative to their own species, for one who has two eyes and the rest, there is beauty of the support-body within that species; for one who does not have them, there is disfigurement. This cannot be faulted. <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s>, however, explained the meaning of this <s>sūtra</s> [differently]: 'For the sake of beauty' means 'for the sake of mastery' — for one endowed with mastery is described in the world as being 'beautiful.' And for those sense-faculties whose support-bases are these [paired organs], there would be mastery of pure seeing, hearing, and smelling. For seeing is not as pure with one eye as with two. Likewise for the other two. And thus, their character as sense-faculties would be diminished. This is stated for that purpose, meaning: 'for the sake of clear perception.' Even here, one could say: let a single [organ], being broad, serve as the support of clear perception, produced by <s>karma</s> — why should there be a separation of supports? In the <s>Vibhāṣā</s>, however, both positions are recorded: 'The arising of two is for beauty' — one [view]; 'for clarity' — another. Enough of this digression. But [one might ask:] the arising of two sense-faculties is due to <s>karma</s>; why is something else stated — 'for beauty' and 'for clarity'? [Reply:] The arising of two sense-faculties is indeed said to be due to <s>karma</s>. How? The pride in beauty, practiced since beginningless time, of beings having support-bodies with divided parts, operates [as motivation]. Therefore, through <s>karma</s> preceded by the desire for that [beauty] and the desire for clear perception, those two sense-faculties come into being — and are said to arise 'for beauty' and 'for clarity.'

children.translated_text: 'The meanings of aggregate, heap, door, and lineage [are respectively:] <s>skandha</s>, <s>āyatana</s>, <s>dhātu</s>' —

body.text: iti. yathākramaṃ rāśiḥ āyadvāraṃ gotraṃ cārtha eṣāṃ. ta ime rāśyāyadvāragotrārthāḥ. ke. skandhāyatanadhātuśabdāḥ. atha vā rāśyāyadvāragotraśabdānām arthāḥ. ke. skandhāyatanadhātavaḥ. sūtre vacanāt. sūtre rāśyarthaḥ skandhārtha iti. rāśer yo 'rthaḥ. sa skandhasyārthaḥ. taṃ sūtreṇa darśayati. yat kiṃcid rūpam atītānāgatapratyutpannam iti vistaraḥ. aikadhyam iti. ekadhaivaikadhyaṃ. anityatāniruddham iti. anityatayā saṃskṛtalakṣaṇena
body.translated_text: thus. In order: heap, door, and lineage are the meanings of these [terms]. These are [the words] '<s>skandha</s>, <s>āyatana</s>, <s>dhātu</s>.' Alternatively, the meanings of the words 'heap,' 'door,' and 'lineage' are what? <s>Skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s>. [This is known] from the <s>sūtra</s>. In the <s>sūtra</s>, [it says] 'the meaning of heap is the meaning of <s>skandha</s>.' That which is the meaning of 'heap' — that is the meaning of <s>skandha</s>. He shows this through the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Whatever form — past, future, or present' — thus in detail. '<s>Aikadhyam</s>' means 'into one single [group].' 'Ceased through impermanence' — the meaning is: ceased by impermanence, i.e., by the conditioned characteristic.

body.text: niruddham ity arthaḥ. anityatāgrahaṇaṃ anyanirodhanirāsārthaṃ. paṃcavidho hi nirodhaṃ. lakṣaṇanirodhaḥ samāpattinirodha upapattinirodhaḥ pratisaṃkhyānirodho 'pratisaṃkhyānirodhaś ca. tad yady atītaṃ rūpaṃ niruddham ity eva brūyāt. aviśeṣitatvāt samāpattinirodhādīnām api prasaṃgaḥ syāt. na ca tair atītārthateṣyate. samāpattinirodho hy anāgatānām eva cittacaittānām. upapattinirodho 'py eṣām eva. pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ sāsravāṇām eva. apratisaṃkhyānirodho 'py anutpattidharmāṇām evānāgatānāṃ. tasmāl [Tib. 38b] lakṣaṇanirodhagrahaṇārtham idam anityatāgrahaṇaṃ. anāgatam anutpannam iti. pratyutpannatām asaṃprāptaṃ. pratyutpannam utpannāniruddham iti. utpannagrahaṇam anāgataviśeṣaṇārthaṃ. aniruddhagrahaṇam atītaviśeṣaṇārthaṃ. anāgataṃ yady apy aniruddhaṃ na tūtpannam. atītam api yady apy utpannaṃ na tv aniruddham iti. ādhyātmikaṃ svāsāṃtānikam iti. cakṣurādikaṃ rūpādikaṃ ca. bāhyam anyad iti. tad eva pārasāṃtānikam asattvasaṃkhyātaṃ ca. āyatanato veti. ādhyātmikaṃ cakṣurādipaṃcakaṃ svaparasaṃtatipatitaṃ.
body.translated_text: The use of the word 'impermanence' (<s>anityatā</s>) is for the purpose of excluding other [types of] cessation. For cessation is fivefold: cessation by characteristic, cessation by attainment, cessation by [change of] birth, cessation by analytical knowledge (<s>pratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s>), and cessation not by analytical knowledge (<s>apratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s>). If one were to say merely that past form 'has ceased,' without specifying, the consequence would extend to cessation by attainment and the rest as well — but 'past' is not intended by those. For cessation by attainment is only of future mind and mental factors. Cessation by [change of] birth is also only of these. Cessation by analytical knowledge is only of defiled [<s>dharmas</s>]. And cessation not by analytical knowledge is only of future [<s>dharmas</s>] that will never arise. Therefore, the word 'impermanence' is [used] for the purpose of indicating cessation by characteristic. 'Future' means 'not yet arisen' — not having attained the state of being present. 'Present' means 'arisen and not [yet] ceased.' The word 'arisen' is for distinguishing from the future; the word 'not ceased' is for distinguishing from the past. The future, although not ceased, is not arisen. The past, although arisen, is not un-ceased. 'Internal' means 'belonging to one's own continuum' — the eye and other [sense-faculties], and form and other [objects]. 'External is the other' — that which belongs to another's continuum and that designated as non-sentient. 'Or from the standpoint of <s>āyatanas</s>' — the internal is the group of five beginning with the eye, belonging to one's own and others' continuums.

body.text: iti vacanāt. bāhyam anyad rūpādikaṃ viṣayapaṃcakaṃ svaparasaṃtatipatitam. asattvasaṃkhyātaṃ cāvijñaptiś ca. bāhyāyatanasvabhāvam iti kṛtvā. audārikaṃ sapratigham iti. paramāṇusaṃcayasvabhāvaṃ. sūkṣmam apratighaṃ. avijñaptirūpaṃ. āpekṣikaṃ veti. apekṣayā vā audārikaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ca bhavati. tadyathā likṣām apekṣya audārikī yūkā. yūkām apekṣya sukṣmā likṣeti. tad evaṃ sati sapratigham eva audārikaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ bhavati. apratighaṃ tu sūkṣmam evāsaṃcitatvāt. āpekṣikatvād asiddham iti. saiva sūkṣmā likṣā vātāyanarajo 'pekṣya audārikī. saiva ca audārikī yūkām apekṣya sūkṣmeti avyavasthitam audārikasūkṣmatvaṃ pārāpāravat. kathaṃ hi nāma. audārikaṃ sūkṣmaṃ bhavati sūkṣmaṃ ca audārikam iti. na. apekṣābhedād [Tib. 39a] iti. apekṣayā bhedo 'pekṣābhedaḥ. tasmān nāsiddhaṃ. yad evāpekṣya audārikaṃ na jātu tad apekṣya sūkṣmaṃ. na kadācit tad evāpekṣyam ity arthaḥ. pitṛputravad iti. tadyathā evadattasya putro yajñadattaḥ. yajñadattasya putro viṣṇumitraḥ. sa yajñadatto viṣṇumitram apekṣya pitā. evadattam apekṣya putraḥ. na cāpekṣikatvād asya pitṛputrabhāvo na sidhyati. apekṣābhedāt. na hi sa yajñadattas tam eva viṣṇumitram apekṣya putraḥ. nāpi tam eva devadattam apekṣya
body.translated_text: because of this statement [in the <s>sūtra</s>]. 'The external is the other' — the group of five beginning with form and other objects, belonging to one's own and others' continuums; and that designated as non-sentient, and <s>avijñapti</s> — because it has the nature of an external <s>āyatana</s>. 'Gross is what has resistance' — that whose nature is an aggregate of atoms. 'Subtle is what lacks resistance' — <s>avijñapti</s>-form. 'Or it is relative' — or, grossness and subtlety exist relatively. For example: a louse is gross relative to a nit; a nit is subtle relative to a louse. Thus, only what has resistance can be both gross and subtle; but what lacks resistance is always subtle only, because it is not aggregated. 'Because of the relativity, it is unestablished' — [one might object:] that very subtle nit, relative to a dust-mote in a sunbeam, is gross; and that very gross louse, relative to a nit, is subtle — so grossness and subtlety are not fixed, like [the relative positions of] the near and far shores. How indeed can the gross be subtle and the subtle be gross? [Reply:] No [fault] — because of difference in the [term of] reference. 'Difference of reference' means difference depending on what is referred to. Therefore it is not unestablished. What something is gross relative to — it is never subtle relative to that same thing; it is never the same referent — this is the meaning. 'Like father and son' — for example, <s>Devadatta</s>'s son is <s>Yajñadatta</s>; <s>Yajñadatta</s>'s son is <s>Viṣṇumitra</s>. That <s>Yajñadatta</s>, relative to <s>Viṣṇumitra</s>, is a father; relative to <s>Devadatta</s>, a son. And it is not that, because of relativity, his status as father and son is not established — because of difference in the referent. For that <s>Yajñadatta</s> is not a son relative to that same <s>Viṣṇumitra</s>; nor is he a father relative to that same <s>Devadatta</s>.

body.text: piteti. tadvat. hīnaṃ kliṣṭaṃ sadbhis tyaktam iti kṛtvā. praṇītam akliṣṭaṃ kleśadūṣitatvāt. dūram atītānāgataṃ saṃtānapracyutatvāt tadasaṃprāptatvāc ca. antikaṃ pratyutpannaṃ saṃtānasaṃnihitatvāt. evaṃ yāvad vijñānam iti. yā kācid vedanā atītānāgatapratyutpannā ādhyātmikī vā bāhyā vā audārikā vā sūkṣmā yā vā dūre yā vā antike tāṃ sarvām aikadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya vedanāskandha iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati. evaṃ yāvad vijñānaṃ vaktavyaṃ. yāvat sarvam aikadhyam abhisaṃkṣipya vijñānaskandha iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchatīti. atītāditvam eṣāṃ vedanādīnāṃ yathā rūpasya. ayaṃ tu viśeṣo vedanādīnāṃ. audārikaṃ paṃcendriyāśrayaṃ vedanādicatuṣkaṃ. amūrtatvāt avagatam audārikatvaṃ [Tib. 39b] nāsti. sūkṣaṃ mānasam āśrayasyāpy amūrtatvāt. bhūmito veti. audārikaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ca vedanādikaṃ. audārikī kāmāvacarī vedanā. sūkṣmā prathamadhyānabhūmikā. audārikī prathamadhyānabhūmikā. sūkṣmā dvitīyadhyānabhūmikā. evaṃ yāvad audārikī ākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmikā. sūkṣmā bhavāgrabhūmiketi. yathā vedanā. evaṃ yāvad vijñānaṃ vaktavyaṃ. bhadanta iti sthaviraḥ. kaścit sautrāntikas tannāmā vā. bhagavadviśeṣas tv āha. sthaviraharmatāto 'sāv iti. atra vayaṃ brūmaḥ. yadi harmatrāto 'tītānāgatāstitvavādī. sa iti na sautrāntiko na ārṣṭāntika ity arthaḥ. tathā hi vakṣyati. bhāvānyatviko bhadantaharmatrātaḥ. sa kilāha. dharmasyādhvasu pravartamānasya bhāvānyathātvaṃ bhavati na dravyasyānyathātvam iti. sautrāntikadarśanāvalaṃbī cāyaṃ bhadanto vibhāṣāyāṃ likhitaḥ. bhadanta āhetyevamādi. bhadantaharmatrāto 'pi svanāmnaiva vibhāṣāyāṃ likhitaḥ. bhadantaharmatrāta āhetyevamadi. tena lakṣyate bhadantaharmatrātād anyo 'yaṃ sautrāntikaḥ kaścit sthaviro bhikṣur iti. paṃcendriyagrāhyam iti rūpādipaṃcakaṃ. sūkṣmam anyac cakṣurādipaṃcakaṃ. avijñaptiś ca. manāpam iti. mana āpnotīti manaāpaṃ manojñam ity arthaḥ. punaḥsaṃdhikaraṇaṃ cātra draṣṭavyaṃ. pūrvatrāsiddham iti īṣadarthena ñaparigrahāt kiṃcit siddham ity ekasavarṇadīrghatvaṃ. dūram adṛśyadeśam iti. ādhāradeśaṃ āśrayādhāradeśaṃ [Tib. 40a] cādhikṛtya. draṣṭuṃ śakyo dṛśyaḥ. dṛśyo deśo 'syeti dṛśyadeśaṃ dṛśyādhāradeśaṃ. dṛśyāśrayādhāradeśaṃ vā. tadyathā kuṇḍe badaraṃ. cakṣurādi vā. tad antikaṃ. adṛśyadeśaṃ tu tadviparītaṃ dūraṃ. dūram adṛśyam iti noktaṃ. āsannam api hi kiṃcid atisūkṣmatvān na dṛśyate. na ca tad dūram iṣyate. dṛśyadeśatvāt. kimarthaṃ punar evaṃ bhadantena vyākhyāyate. atītādīnāṃ svaśabdenābhihitatvāt. anyathā hi punaruktadoṣaḥ syāt. dūrāntikatvaṃ tu teṣām āśrayavaśād
body.translated_text: 'father' — likewise. [That is called] 'inferior' (hīna) because it is defiled and abandoned by the good. 'Superior' (praṇīta) because it is undefiled — because of being tainted by defilements. 'Distant' (dūra) is the past and future — because of having fallen from the [mental] continuum, and because of not having been attained in it. 'Near' (antika) is the present — because of being proximate to the continuum. 'Thus up to consciousness' — whatever feeling, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, distant or near — having subsumed all of that into one, it goes under the designation 'feeling aggregate' (<s>vedanāskandha</s>). Likewise up to consciousness, it should be stated: up to having subsumed all into one, it goes under the designation 'consciousness aggregate' (<s>vijñānaskandha</s>). The pastness, etc. of these — feeling and the rest — is like that of form. But there is this distinction for feeling, etc.: gross is the set of four beginning with feeling that has the five sense-faculties as its support. Because they are immaterial, [Tib. 39b] grossness as understood [for form] does not apply. Subtle is that which has the mental [faculty] as support, because the support too is immaterial. 'Or by level' — gross and subtle feeling, etc. Gross is feeling belonging to the desire-realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>). Subtle is that belonging to the level of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Gross is that of the first <s>dhyāna</s> level. Subtle is that of the second <s>dhyāna</s> level. Thus up to: gross is that of the level of the base of nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>). Subtle is that of the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). As with feeling, so up to consciousness it should be stated. '<s>Bhadanta</s>' means 'elder' (<s>sthavira</s>). A certain <s>Sautrāntika</s>, or one of that name. But the distinguished <s>Bhagavat</s> [commentator] says: 'That is <s>Sthavira Harmatrāta</s>.' Here we say: if <s>Harmatrāta</s> holds the doctrine of the existence of past and future, then he is not a <s>Sautrāntika</s>, nor an <s>Ārṣṭāntika</s> — this is the meaning. For it will be stated: '<s>Bhadanta Harmatrāta</s> holds the view of change of state (<s>bhāvānyathātva</s>).' He reportedly said: 'When a <s>dharma</s> operates in the time-periods, there is an alteration of state but not an alteration of substance.' And this <s>Bhadanta</s> is recorded in the <s>Vibhāṣā</s> as one who relies on the <s>Sautrāntika</s> view — '<s>Bhadanta</s> says,' etc. <s>Bhadanta Harmatrāta</s> too is recorded in the <s>Vibhāṣā</s> by his own name — '<s>Bhadanta Harmatrāta</s> says,' etc. From this it is observed that this <s>Sautrāntika</s> <s>Bhadanta</s> is someone different from <s>Bhadanta Harmatrāta</s> — a certain elder monk. 'Graspable by the five [sense-]faculties' refers to the five [objects] beginning with form. 'Subtle' refers to the other five [dhātus] beginning with the eye [sense-faculty] and also <s>avijñapti</s>. '<s>Manāpa</s>' (agreeable) — it reaches (āpnoti) the mind (manas), hence manāpa, meaning 'mentally pleasant.' And here a re-compounding is to be understood. 'Not fully established in the preceding' — because of the acceptance of the particle ña in a slight sense, [something is] partially established — hence the vowel lengthening. 'Distant [means those] in an invisible location' — with reference to the location of the substratum, the location of the support-substratum. [Tib. 40a] 'Capable of being seen' = dṛśya; 'whose location is visible' = dṛśyadeśa; meaning 'whose substratum-location is visible,' or 'whose support-substratum-location is visible.'
