body.translated_text: the space element [contributes] by providing room. For this very reason, the designation '<s>dhātu</s>' (element) applies to them: 'they hold (<s>dadhati</s>) the conception (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>) — therefore they are elements.' But undefiled <s>dharmas</s> are not so —

body.text: iti. kim idaṃ nidarśanaṃ nāma. yena viśeṣeṇa yogāt tad vastu tathā nidarśayituṃ śakyate. sa viśeṣo nidarśanam ity ucyate. vacanena parasya cakṣurvijñānām utpannaṃ vā nidarśanaṃ. tena saha vartate sanidarśana eko rūpadhātur atrāṣṭādaśasu dhātuṣu. rūpadhātur evaikaḥ sanidarśana ity avadhāraṇād uktaṃ bhavati. anidarśanāḥ śeṣā iti. anena cāsya sanidarśanatvena prādhānyam uktam iti. na punaruktadoṣaprasaṃga iti tatsiddheḥ. ete ca sanidarśanatvādayaḥ prabhedāḥ prāyeṇa sūtroktā eva pradarśyante. [Tib. 53b] tathā hi sūtra uktaṃ. cakṣur bhikṣo ādhyātmikam āyatanaṃ. catvāri mahābhūtāny upādāya rūpaprasādaḥ rūpy anidarśanaṃ sapratighaṃ. yāvat kāyo bhikṣo ādhyātmikam āyatanaṃ pūrvavat. mano bhikṣo ādhyātmikam āyatanaṃ arūpy anidarśanam apratighaṃ. rūpāṇi bhikṣo bāhyam āyatanaṃ. catvāri mahābhūtāny upādāya rūpi sanidarśanaṃ sapratighaṃ. śabdā hi bhikṣo bāhyam āyatanaṃ. catvāri mahābhūtāny upādāya rūpy anidarśanaṃ sapratighaṃ. yāvat spraṣṭavyāni bhikṣo bāhyam āyatanaṃ. catvāri mahābhūtāni catvāri ca mahābhūtāny upādāya rūpy anidarśanaṃ sapratighaṃ. dharmā bhikṣo bāhyam āyatanaṃ. ekādaśabhir āyatanair asaṃgṛhītaṃ arūpy anidarśanam apratigham iti. ete ca prabhedā dhātūnām eva ā prathamakośasthānaparisamāpteḥ kathyante. rūpavijñānavibhāgatvāt.
body.translated_text: thus. What is this 'indication' (<s>nidarśana</s>)? That distinguishing feature by virtue of which that thing can be shown as such — that feature is called 'indication.'

children.translated_text: 'The ten that have form are resistant' —

body.text:
iti. rūpigrahaṇam arūpinirāsārthaṃ. rūpaṇaṃ rūpaṃ. tad eṣām astīti rūpiṇaḥ. daśeti cakṣurdhātvādayaḥ paṃca tadviṣayadhātavaś ca paṃca ceti. dharmadhātor nirāsaḥ kathaṃ kṛtaḥ. sa cāpi hi rūpīti śakyate vaktuṃ. tatrāvijñaptirūpasadbhāvāt. rūpiṇa evety avadhāraṇāt tannirāsaḥ kṛto bhavati. ye hi dhātavo rūpisvabhāvā eva te grahītavyāḥ. dharmadhātus tu rūpyarūpisvabhāva [Tib. 54a] iti. svadeśe parasyotpattipratibandha iti vistaraḥ. yatraikaṃ sapratighaṃ vastu. tatra dvitīyasyotpattir na bhavati.
yathā hasto haste 'bhyāhataḥ pratihanyate. upale vā. hasto hastasthāne upalasthāne vā notpadyate. upalo 'pi. tayor hastopalayoḥ sthāne upalo 'pi notpadyate. jale pratihanyata iti. jale svaviṣaye pravartata ity arthaḥ. prāyeṇa manuṣyāṇām
body.translated_text: thus. The word 'having form' (<s>rūpin</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the formless. '<s>Rūpaṇa</s>' (that which is molded) is form (<s>rūpa</s>); those which have that are '<s>rūpin</s>' (having form). 'Ten' means the five beginning with the eye <s>dhātu</s> and the five object-<s>dhātus</s>.

body.text: iti prāyagrahaṇaṃ kaivartādinivṛttyarthaṃ. asti nobhayatreti. garbhe niyatamṛtyūnāṃ. etān ākārān iti. etāṃ prakārān ity arthaḥ. titīlā jatunyaḥ. mārjārādīnām ity ādigrahaṇena cauramanuṣyādīnāṃ vyāghrādīnāṃ ca grahaṇaṃ. yasmiṃ yasya kāritraṃ. sa tasya viṣaya iti. kāritraṃ puruṣakāraḥ. cakṣuḥśrotrādīnāṃ rūpaśabdādiṣv ālocanaśravaṇādikāritraṃ. tac ca svacittacaittān praty āśrayabhāvaviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyaṃ. yac cittacaittair gṛhyate daṇḍāvaṣṭambhanayogena. tad ālambanaṃ rūpādi. tad evaṃ sati cittacaittānām evālambanaṃ. viṣayaḥ punaś cakṣurādīnām api na kevalaṃ cittacaittānāṃ. tasmāt pareṇāpravṛtter iti. yo hi loke yataḥ pareṇa na pravartate. sa tatra pratihanyate kāṣṭhe kuḍye vā. tathā cakṣurādi viṣayāt pareṇa na kāritraṃ karoti. viṣaya eva tu karoti tasmāt tatra pratihanyata ity ucyate. [Tib. 54b] nipāto vātra pratighāta iti vistaraḥ. atra viṣaye nipatanaṃ nipātaḥ. yā svaviṣaye pravṛttiḥ. kāritram ity arthaḥ. tad ihāvaraṇapratighāteneti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: the word 'generally' (<s>prāya</s>) is for the purpose of excluding fishermen and the like. 'There is [exception] in neither [case]' — for those with certain death in the womb. 'These aspects' means 'these types' —

body.text: atrāvaraṇapratighātena te daśa dhātavaḥ sapratighā abhipretāḥ. tatra viṣayālambanapratighātābhyāṃ cittacaittānām api sapratighatvaprasaṃgāt catuṣkoṭikaḥ praśnaś catuṣkoṇaś catuḥprakāra ity arthaḥ. paścātpādaka iti. yadi praśnasya paścādbhāgaṃ gṛhītvā visarjanāyottiṣṭhate sa paścātpādakaḥ. yadi pūrvaṃ bhāgaṃ gṛhītvā sa pūrvapādakaḥ. viṣayapratighātenāpi ta iti cittacaittāḥ. te hi viṣayapratighātenālambanapratighātena ca sapratighāḥ. paṃcendriyāṇi nālambanapratighātena sapratighāny anālambanatvāt.
body.translated_text: here, those ten <s>dhātus</s> are intended as resistant in terms of obstruction-resistance (<s>āvaraṇa-pratighāta</s>). Therein, through object-resistance and object-support-resistance, even mind and mental factors would have resistance.

children.translated_text: 'Where, for a mind about to arise' —

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. yatrāśraye ālambane ca utpattukāmasya manasaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus, the elaboration. [The mind] desiring to arise in that support and with that object —

body.text: 'nutpattiḥ
body.translated_text: [means] non-arising —

body.text: antarāvaraṇena.
body.translated_text: through interposing an obstruction.

children.translated_text: That itself is what is resistant.

body.text: tenāntarāvaraṇalakṣaṇena pratighena sapratighatvāt. svadeśe parasyotpattipratibandhanalakṣaṇena pratighātena sapratighatvād ity apare. kiṃ punas tat. paṃcendriyapaṃcaviṣayadhātusvabhāvaṃ.
body.translated_text: Because it is resistant (<s>sapratigha</s>) through the resistance characterized by intervening obstruction; or, as others say, because it is resistant through the resistance characterized by the obstruction of the arising of another in its own location. What then is that [which is resistant]? That which has the nature of the five sense-faculty and five sense-object elements.

children.translated_text: 'By the opposite, the non-resistant is accepted.'

body.text: yatrotpitsor manasaḥ pratighāto na śakyate paraiḥ kartuṃ yathā manodhātor dharmadhātoś ca manovijñānotpattau [Tib. 55a] antarāvaraṇaṃ na śakyate paraiḥ kartuṃ. ataḥ saptacittadhātudharmadharmadhātusvabhāvam apratigham iti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: Where the resistance of mind that wishes to arise cannot be caused by others — for example, intervening obstruction cannot be made by others for the arising of the mind-element from the <s>dharma</s>-element and the mental consciousness [Tib. 55a] — therefore, it is established that what has the nature of the seven mind-elements and the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> is non-resistant.

body.text: iti. avyākṛtā evāṣṭāv ity avadhāraṇaṃ. kuśalākuśalabhāvenāvyākaraṇāt avyākṛtāḥ. ye kuśalākuśalavyatiriktāḥ. ta evāvyākṛtā ihābhipretāḥ. na tu kuśalāḥ akuśalāvyākṛtāvyākaraṇāt. nāpy akuśalāḥ kuśalāvyākṛtāvyākaraṇāt. kuśalākuśalānāṃ kuśalākuśalabhāvena vyākṛtatvāt. saṃketarūḍhyapekṣā hi śabdapravṛttiḥ.
body.translated_text: This is a restriction: 'only eight are morally indeterminate.' 'Indeterminate' (<s>avyākṛta</s>) because they are not determined as either wholesome or unwholesome. Those that are distinct from wholesome and unwholesome — those alone are intended here as 'indeterminate.' Not the wholesome, because they are not determined as unwholesome or indeterminate. Nor the unwholesome, because they are not determined as wholesome or indeterminate. For the wholesome and unwholesome are determined in their wholesome and unwholesome nature. The functioning of words depends on convention and established usage.

body.text: iti. dhātava ity adhikṛtaṃ. traidhaivānye naikadhā na dvidheti avadhāraṇaṃ. alobhādisaṃprayuktāḥ kuśalā iti vistaraḥ. alobhadveṣamohahryapatrapāsaṃprayuktāḥ saptacittadhātavaḥ kuśalāḥ. lobhadveṣamohāhrīanapatrāpyasaṃprayuktā akuśalāḥ. kutsitāc chalitā gatā apakrāntā iti kuśalāḥ. prajñā vā kuśa iva tīkṣṇeti kuśaḥ. taṃ lānti ādadata ity kuśalaḥ. tadviparītā akuśalāḥ. anye tv alobhādilobhādyasaṃprayuktā avyākṛtāḥ. dharmadhātur iti vistaraḥ. alobhādisvabhāvo [Tib. 55b] yo 'yam uktaḥ. alobhādisaṃprayukto vedanādiḥ. alobhādisamuttho viprayuktaḥ. prātijātyādiḥ. avijñaptiś ca. pratisaṃkhyānirodhaś cāpara iti caturvidhaḥ kuśalaḥ. dharmadhātur lobhādisvabhāvasaṃprayuktasamuttho 'kuśalaḥ. anyo 'vyākṛto yo nālobhādisvabhāvasaṃprayuktasamutthaḥ. nāpi lobhādisvabhāvasaṃprayuktasamutthaḥ. ākāśam apratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. teṣāṃ ca yathāśaṃbhavaṃ prāptijātyādayaḥ. eṣo 'vyākṛto dharmadhātuḥ. tadanyāv avyākṛtāv iti. tābhyāṃ kuśalākuśalacittasamutthābhyāṃ rūpaśabdadhātubhyām anyau rūpaśabdadhātū avyākṛtacittasamutthau kāyavāgvijñaptisaṃgṛhītau vijñaptyasaṃgṛhītau cāvyākṛtau.
body.translated_text: 'Elements' is the topic under discussion. 'The others are precisely threefold — not one-fold, not two-fold' — this is the restriction. 'Those conjoined with non-greed, etc. are wholesome' — and so on in detail. The seven mind-elements conjoined with non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion, conscience (<s>hrī</s>), and shame (<s>apatrapā</s>) are wholesome. Those conjoined with greed, hatred, delusion, shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), and recklessness (<s>anapatrāpya</s>) are unwholesome. '<s>Kuśala</s>' (wholesome) means: 'those that have departed, moved away, gone away from what is censurable (<s>kutsita</s>).' Or, insight (<s>prajñā</s>) is <s>kuśa</s> because it is sharp like <s>kuśa</s>-grass; that which takes (<s>lāti</s>) that [insight] is <s>kuśala</s>. The opposite of that is unwholesome. Others — those not conjoined with non-greed, etc. or with greed, etc. — are indeterminate. 'The <s>dharma-dhātu</s>' — and so on in detail. [Tib. 55b] What was stated as having the nature of non-greed, etc.; what is conjoined with non-greed, etc. — feeling, etc.; what is produced by non-greed, etc. and is dissociated — such as the [factor of] birth, etc.; and <s>avijñapti</s>; and analytical cessation as another [type] — thus the wholesome <s>dharma-dhātu</s> is fourfold. The <s>dharma-dhātu</s> that has the nature of greed, etc., or is conjoined with or produced by them, is unwholesome. What is other and indeterminate is what does not have the nature of non-greed, etc. nor is conjoined with or produced by them, and likewise does not have the nature of greed, etc. nor is conjoined with or produced by them — [namely,] space and non-analytical cessation, and their respective [factors of] attainment, birth, etc. as applicable. This is the indeterminate <s>dharma-dhātu</s>. 'The other two [that are] indeterminate' — the form-element and sound-element other than those two [that are wholesome and unwholesome] — i.e., those not produced by wholesome or unwholesome mind —

body.text: iti. kāmadhātvāptāḥ sarva evety avadhāryate. aṣṭādaśadhātutvamātrasaṃgrahāt. na tu pratyekaṃ sākalyataḥ. tata āha.
body.translated_text: This is a restriction: 'all are obtained in the desire-realm.' Because [the desire-realm] encompasses all eighteen elements. But not that each [element exists there] in its totality —

body.text: tayoḥ kavaḍīkārāhāratvād iti. tayor gandharasayoḥ. gandho 'pi hi kavaḍīkārāhāraḥ sūkṣmaḥ. tatrābhāvaprasaṃga iti. tatra rūpadhātau spraṣṭavyadhātor abhāvaprasaṃgaḥ kavaḍīkārāhāratvāt.
body.translated_text: 'Because those two are morsel-food' (<s>kavaḍīkārāhāra</s>) — 'those two' means smell and taste. For smell too is morsel-food, [though] subtle. [The reason for] their absence there —

children.translated_text: 'Morsel-food exists in the desire [realm] with three sense-bases as its nature' —

body.text: Tib. 56
body.translated_text: Tib. 56

body.text: iti siddhāntāt. gandharasayor apy eṣa prasaṃga iti. yau nāhārasvabhāvau. tau tatra syātām ity arthaḥ. asti tu spraṣṭavyasyeti. kiṃ. paribhoga indriyāśrayabhāvena ādhārabhāvena prāvaraṇabhāvena ca. anye punar āhur iti bhadantaśrīlātaḥ. praśrabdhisahagateneti. praśrabdhisahotpannena kāyakarmaṇyatāsahagatenety arthaḥ. atrācāryo bhadantaśrīlātamatam anādṛtya vaibhāṣikamataṃ sāvakāśaṃ dṛṣṭvā viniścayam ārabhate. evaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. vaibhāṣikair arthata etat pratijñātaṃ. na sto rūpadhātau gandharasau. niḥprayojanatvāt. strīpuruṣendriyaviṣayavad iti. taṃ pakṣam ācāryo dūṣayati. duṣṭo 'yaṃ pakṣaḥ. dharmiviśeṣaviparyayāpakṣālatvāt. rūpadhātugandharasākhyo hi dharmī vidyamānasvagrāhako 'bhipretaḥ. tasyāvidyamānasvagrāhakatvaṃ prāpnoti. yathā hi strīpuruṣendriyaviṣayo niḥprayojanatvena avidyamānasvagrāhako bhavati. tathā gandharasākhyo 'pi viṣayaḥ prāpnoti. sphuṭam apy anumānam asti. yenaiṣa dharmiviśeṣaviparyayo vyajyate. na sto rūpadhātau ghrāṇajihvendriye niḥprayojanaviṣayatvāt. puruṣendriyavad iti. vaibhāṣikadeśīyaḥ kaścit pratividhatte. asti prayojanam iti vistaraḥ. tābhyāṃ ghrāṇajihvendriyābhyāṃ [Tib. 56b] vinā śarīraśobhaiva na syāt vāgvijñaptiś ca. anena dṛṣṭabādhena prasaṃgaṃ nivartayati. anumānaṃ hy atra dṛṣṭaṃ bādhate. kiṃ ity ucyate. sto rūpadhātau ghrāṇajihvendriye. saprayojanatvāt. cakṣurindriyavad iti. ācārya āha. yady etat prayojanam iti vistaraḥ. adhiṣṭhānenaivāśrayaśobhā vacanaṃ ca bhavati nendriyeṇeti saprayojanatvasya hetor asiddhatāṃ darśayati. vaibhāśikadeśīya āha. nānindriyam adhiṣṭhānam iti vistaraḥ. na rūpadhātau saṃbhavaty anindriyaṃ ghrāṇajihvendriyādhiṣṭhānam. indriyādhiṣṭhānatvāt. puruṣendriyādhiṣṭhānavad iti. etena saprayojanatvasya siddhatāṃ sthāpayati. ācārya āha. yuktas tadasaṃbhava iti vistaraḥ. yuktas tatra puruṣendriyādhiṣṭhānasyāsaṃbhavo niḥprayojanatvāt. ghrāṇajihvendriyādhiṣṭhānānaṃ tv āśrayaśobhābhivyāhāra prayojanatvāt saprayojanaṃ. ato 'sya vināpīndriyeṇa yuktaḥ saṃbhavaḥ. sādhanaṃ tatrocyate. saṃbhavati rūpadhātāv anindriyaṃ ghrāṇajihvendriyādhiṣṭhānaṃ. saprayojanatvāt. cakṣurindriyādhiṣṭhānavad iti. anena tām eva saprayojanatvasyāsiddhatāṃ vyavasthāpayati. evam atra saprayojanatvavādini vaibhāṣikadeśīye kasmiṃścin niṣiddhe yad etad ādāv uktaṃ. evaṃ tarhi ghrāṇajihvendriyayor apy abhāvaprasaṃgaḥ niḥprayojanatvād iti taddūṣaṇābhāsatāṃ darśayanto vaibhāṣikā āhuḥ. niḥprayojanāpīti vistaraḥ. yathā garbhe [Tib. 57a] niyatamṛtyūnāṃ niḥprayojanābhinirvṛttiḥ.
body.translated_text: This is from the established doctrine. 'This unwanted consequence would apply to smell and taste too' — those two, which are not of the nature of food, could [also] exist there.

body.text:
na hi teṣāṃ rūpadarśanādir bhavati. evaṃ rūpadhātau ghrāṇajihvendriyābhinirvṛttir niḥprayojanāpi bhaviṣyatīti. tena na sto rūpadhātau ghrāṇajihvendriye. niḥprayojanatvāt. puruṣendriyavad iti niḥprayojanatvam anaikāntikaṃ pradarśyate. ācārya āha. syān nāma niḥprayojaneti vistaraḥ. bhaven niḥprayojanendriyābhinirvṛttiḥ. na tu nirhetukā saṃskṛtānāṃ sahetukatvāt. yaś ca viṣayād vitṛṣṇaḥ. sa niyatam indriyād apīti. anena hetvabhāvaḥ pradarśyate. tataś caivaṃ sādhanam ucyate. na sto rūpadhātau ghrāṇajihvendriye. nirhetukatvāt. nirhetukāṃkuravat puruṣendriyavad vā. puruṣendriyam api vā kiṃ nirvartata ity ācārya eva vikalpaṃ vāhayati. ko 'bhiprāyaḥ. yadi niḥprayojanā hetum antareṇāpi vā ghrāṇajihvendriyayor utpattiḥ puruṣendriyam api vā na nirvartate. vaibhāṣikānāṃ hy ayaṃ pakṣaḥ. saghrāṇajihvendriyo rūpadhātusattvasaṃtānaḥ. rūpiprāṇitvāt. kāmāvacarasattvasaṃtānavad iti. ācāryas tu puruṣendriyam api kiṃ na nirvartata ity anena tasya pakṣasya dharmiviśeṣaviparyayaṃ darśayati. avidyamānapuruṣendriyo rūpadhātusattvasaṃtāno dharmī. tasya viparyayo vidyamānapuruṣendriyatvam iti. vaibhāṣikāḥ [Tib. 57b] pariharaṃty
aśobhākaratvād itil. katham iti. na rūpadhātau puruṣendriyam asti. aśobhākaratvāt. kāṇakuṇṭhatvavat. tadanumānabādhanān na viparyety asmākam eṣā pratijñā. yadi dṛṣṭaṃ na bādhata iti naiyāyikasiddhāntād ity abhiprāyaḥ. ācārya āha. kośagatavastiguhyānāṃ kiṃ na śobhate. vastau guhyaṃ vastiguhyaṃ. vastir yena tat puruṣendriyaṃ veṣṭitaṃ. guhyaṃ puruṣendriyaṃ. kośo yatra tad vastiguhyaṃ tiṣṭhati. kośagataṃ vastiguhyaṃ. yeṣāṃ ta ime kośagatavastiguhyāḥ. teṣāṃ kiṃ na śobhate śobhata evety arthaḥ. anenāśobhākaratvam asiddhaṃ darśayati. na ca prayojanavaśād utpattir iti vistaraḥ. vaibhāṣikair aśobhākaratvād iti bruvadbhir arthāpattyaitat pratijñātaṃ bhavati. prayojanavaśotpādyaṃ puruṣendriyam iti. sa ca pakṣo 'numānabādhito dharmisvarūpaviparyayāpakṣālatvāt. katham iti. ucyate. na prayojanavaśotpādyaṃ puruṣendriyaṃ. svakāraṇotpādyatvāt. kāṇakuṇṭhatvavat. vaibhāṣikā āhuḥ. sūtraṃ tarhi virudhyata iti vistaraḥ. yo 'yam avidyamānaghrāṇajihvendriyo rūpadhātusattvasaṃtāna iti pakṣaḥ. sa sāpakṣālaḥ. prākpakṣavirodhāt. [Tib. 58a] tathā hi bhagavatā rūpāvacarāḥ sattvā avikalā ahīnendriyā iti uktāḥ. kāṇakuṇṭhatvābhāvatvāt. ahīnendriyāś cakṣurādibhir ahīnatvāt. ācārya āha. yāni tatreti vistaraḥ. yāni tatra rūpadhātau ghrāṇendriyādirahitāni cakṣurādīni tair ahīnendriyā iti sūtrārthaparigrahād avirodhaḥ. evaṃ tu varṇayanti vaibhāṣikāḥ. sta eveti vistaraḥ. bhavata. eva tatra
body.translated_text: For those [beings of the form-realm] do not have the seeing of form, etc. [through smell and taste]. Thus, even though the production of nose and tongue faculties in the form-realm would also be purposeless,

body.text: rūpadhātau ghrāṇajihvendriye na tu gandharasau. ātmabhāvamukhena hi svasaṃtānamukhena ṣaḍāyatane cakṣurādike tṛṣṇāsamudācārḥ prāṇināṃ pravartate. tadabhiṣyanditaṃ ca karmeti. sahetuke rūpadhātau ghrāṇajihvendriye. tataś ca sahetukatvāt. sta eva te rūpadhātau. sahetukāṃkurādivad iti. anena ca na sto rūpadhātau ghrāṇajihvendriye nirhetukatvād iti yat sādhanam uktaṃ. tad asiddham iti pratipādayanti. puruṣendriye tu maithunasparśamukhena. kiṃ. tṛṣṇāsamudācāra iti prakṛtaṃ. maithunasparśavītarāgāś ca rūpāvacarāḥ sattvāḥ. tasmāt tasmāt tatra na tṛṣṇāpūrvakaṃ karma bhavati. tasmād ahetukatvāt. tatra puruṣendriyaṃ nāsti nirhetukāṃkurādivad iti siddhaṃ rūpadhātau caturdaśaiva dhātava iti.
body.translated_text: in the form-realm there are nose and tongue faculties, but not smell and taste. For [the production of the six sense-bases occurs] by way of the body (<s>ātmabhāva</s>) — that is, by way of one's own continuum — the six sense-bases

body.text: iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: and so on in detail.

children.translated_text: The mind-element, <s>dharma</s>-element, and mental consciousness element —

body.text: Tib. 58b
body.translated_text: By the restrictive [particle]

body.text: evārūpyāptā ity avadhāraṇād anye dhātavo na santīty uktaṃ bhavati. yasmād rūpavītarāgānāṃ tatropapattiḥ. ato daśa rūpasvabhāvā dhātavaś cakṣurādayaḥ paṃca rūpādayaś cāpi paṃca na santi. tadāśrayālambanāś ca paṃca vijñānadhātavo na santīti. te cakṣurādayo rūpādayaś ca yathākramam āśrayā ālambanāni ca yeṣāṃ. ta ime tadāśrayālambanāḥ. āśrayāṇāṃ cakṣurādīnām ālambanānāṃ ca rūpādīnāṃ abhāvāt te 'pi cakṣurvijñānādidhātavas tatra na santi.
body.translated_text: 'only the formless realm is attained,' it is stated that other elements do not exist [there]. Because those free from attachment to form are reborn there, therefore the ten elements with the nature of form — the five [beginning with] the eye and the five [beginning with] form — do not exist [there]. And the five consciousness-elements whose bases and objects are those [material elements] do not exist either. Those [five consciousness-elements] whose bases are the eye and so forth and whose objects are form and so forth, respectively — they are 'those whose bases and objects are those.' Because of the absence of the bases — the eye and so forth — and the objects — form and so forth — those visual-consciousness elements and the rest do not exist there.

body.text: iti. eta eva trayaḥ sāsravānāsravā ity avadhāraṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: The restrictive [sense] is: these three alone are contaminated and uncontaminated.

body.text: iti. kim artham idam ucyate. nanv eta eva trayaḥ sāsravānāsravā ity avadhāraṇāt. śeṣāḥ sāsravā iti siddhaṃ. na siddhaṃ. kathaṃ. śeṣāṃ sāsravā evānāsravā eva vā syur ity āśaṃkāḥ. tannivṛttyartham idam ucyate. śeṣāḥ sāsravā eveti.
body.translated_text: For what purpose is this stated? Surely, from the restriction that these three alone are contaminated and uncontaminated, it is already established that the rest are contaminated. [Reply:] It is not established. How so? Because there might be doubt whether the rest are exclusively contaminated or exclusively uncontaminated. To remove that [doubt], this is stated: 'The rest are exclusively contaminated.'

children.translated_text: 'The five consciousness-elements indeed have [both] applied thought and sustained thought' —

body.text: iti. savitarkasavicārā eveti hiśabdo 'vadhāraṇe.
body.translated_text: The particle <s>hi</s> ('indeed') is restrictive — meaning: they have applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>) exclusively.

children.translated_text: 'The last three are of three kinds' —

body.text: iti. antyā eva triprakārā ity avadhāraṇaṃ. anyatra vitarkavicārābhyām iti. vitarkavicārau saṃprayuktakadharmadhātusvabhāvau tayor atra grahaṇaprasaṃga iti parivarjyete. [Tib. 59a] vitarko hi dvitīyaprakārāntare 'ntarbhaviṣyati. vicāro 'pi dhyānāntarajas tṛtīye prakāre 'ntarbhavati. tadanyas tu
body.translated_text: The restriction is: the last ones alone are of three kinds. 'Except for applied thought and sustained thought' — applied thought and sustained thought, whose nature is the associated <s>dharma</s>-element, are excluded here because [otherwise] their inclusion [in the element being classified] would follow. For applied thought will be included in the second variety. And sustained thought, belonging to the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>...

body.text: triṣv api prakāreṣu nāntarbhavatīti vakṣyati. te ete manodhātvādayaḥ saṃprayuktadharmadhātuparyantāḥ kāmadhātau prathame ca dhyāne sasāmantake maule savitarkāḥ savicārāḥ vitarkavicārasaṃprayogāt. ata eva dhyānāntare 'vitarkā vitarkābhāvāt. vicāramātrā vicārasaṃprayogāt. ata eva dvitīyāt prabhṛti yāvad bhavāgraṃ tayor abhāvād avitarkā avicārāḥ. sarvaś cāsaṃprayukto dharmadhātur iti. yathāsaṃbhavaṃ traidhātukarūpacittaviprayuktā asaṃskṛtāś ca dhyānāntare ca vicāraḥ avitarko. vitarkābhāvāt. avicāro dvitīyavicārābhāvāt. vicāra eṣu triṣu prakāreṣu nāntarbhavatīti. kāmadhātuprathamadhyānabhūmiko vicāraḥ prathame tāvat prakāre nāntarbhavati. savitarkaḥ savicāra iti. sa hi savitarkaḥ saṃbhavati na tu savicāro vicārasaṃprayogāt. dvitīye 'pi nāntarbhavati. avitarko vicāramātra iti. vitarkasaṃprayogāt. dvitīyavicārābhāvāc ca. tṛtīye 'pi nāntarbhavati. avitarkaḥ avicāra iti. sa hi yady api avicāro dvitīyavicārābhāvāt. na tv avitarko [Tib. 59b] vitarkasaṃprayogāt. sa kathaṃ vaktavya ity ata āha. avicāro vitarkamātra iti. dvitīyavicārābhāvāt avicāraḥ. vitarkasaṃprayogāt vitarkamātraḥ. ata eveti. yasmāt savitarkasavicārāṇāṃ bhūmau vicāra eva caturthaḥ prakāro bhavati. avicāro vitarkamātra iti.
body.translated_text: ...is not included in any of the three varieties — as will be stated. These — the mind-element and the others, including the associated <s>dharma</s>-element — in the desire realm and in the first <s>dhyāna</s> together with its preparatory [stage], [both] foundational, have applied thought and sustained thought, because they are associated with applied thought and sustained thought. For this very reason, in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, they are without applied thought — because of the absence of applied thought — and have sustained thought only.

body.text: iti. śesā daśa rūpiṇo dhātava uktāḥ. te 'vitarkā vicāramātrā vā avitarkā avicārāḥ syur iti āśaṃkāyām avadhārya tadubhayavarjitā eva śeṣā avitarkā avicārā evety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: The rest — the ten material elements that were mentioned. They are without applied thought and [the doubt whether they] might have sustained thought only, or might be without applied thought and without sustained thought — [to remove this,] having restricted: 'the rest are devoid of both' — meaning the rest are exclusively without applied thought and without sustained thought.

body.text: (I.32) katham avikalpakā ity ucyanta iti. cakṣurvijñānasamaṃgī nīlaṃ vijānāti nohati nīlam iti vacanāt. trividhaḥ kila vikalpa iti. kilaśabdaḥ paramatadyotanārthaḥ. svābhiprāyas tu cetanāprajñāviśeṣa eva vitarka iti na svabhāvavikalpo 'nyo dharmo 'stīti. tathā hy anena paṃcaskandhaka uktaṃ. vitarkaḥ katamaḥ. paryeṣako manojalpaḥ cetanāprajñāviśeṣaḥ yā cittasyaudārikatā. vicāraḥ katamaḥ. pratyavekṣako manojalpas tathaiva yā cittasya sūkṣmatā. anabhyūhāvasthāyāṃ cetanā abhyūhāvasthāyāṃ prajñeti vyavasthāpyate. tad eṣāṃ svabhāvavikalpo 'stīti. tad iti vākyopanyāse nipātas tasmādarthe vā. svabhāvenaiva [Tib. 60a] vikalpa audārikalakṣaṇatvāt. svabhāvavikalpo vitarkaḥ. sa eṣāṃ paṃcānāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ saṃprayogato 'sti tasmāt savikalpā uktāḥ. netarāv abhinirūpaṇānusmaraṇavikalpāv eṣāṃ staḥ. tasmād avikalpakā ucyante. yathā ekapādako 'śvaḥ apādaka iti. pādatraye cchinne ekasminn api pāde saty
body.translated_text: (I.32) 'How are they said to be non-conceptual?' Because it is stated: 'One who possesses visual consciousness cognizes blue; [but] he does not think "blue."' 'Conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) is said to be threefold' — the particle <s>kila</s> ('it is said') is for indicating the other's position. But his [Vasubandhu's] own view is that applied thought is exclusively a particular [kind of] volition and wisdom — hence there is no other <s>dharma</s> that is inherent conceptualization...

body.text: apādaka ity ucyate. tadvad ekavikalpā avikalpakā iti. sā hy abhinirūpaṇāvikalpa iti. sā mānasy asamāhitā prajñā śrutacintāmayy upapattipratilaṃbhikā ca. sā hi manasi bhavā mānasī. vyagrā vividhāgrā vyagrā vividhālambanety arthaḥ. vigatapradhānā vā muhurmuhur ālambanāntarāśrayaṇāt. vyagrā kasmād abhinirūpaṇāvikalpa ity ucyate. tatratatrālambane nāmāpekṣayābhipravṛtteḥ. rūpaṃ vedanā anityaṃ duḥkham ityādyabhinirūpaṇāc ca. samāhitā tu bhāvanāmayī nāmanapekṣyālambane pravartata iti. naiṣābhinirūpaṇāvikalpa ity ucyate. mānasy eva sarvā smṛtir iti. samāhitā cāsamāhitā ca. sā kila nāmānapekṣā anubhūtārthamātrālambanā pravartate. smṛtiḥ katamā. cetaso 'bhilāṣa iti lakṣaṇāt. paṃcavijñānakāyasaṃprayuktā tu nānubhūtārthābhilāṣapravṛtteti [Tib. 60b] nānusmaraṇavikalpa itīṣyate.
body.translated_text: ...is said to be 'supportless.' Likewise, 'those with a single [type of] conceptualization are non-conceptual.' For that [type] is the conceptualization of examination (<s>abhinirūpaṇāvikalpa</s>). That is the mental wisdom — unabsorbed, born of hearing and reflection, and [the wisdom] obtained at birth. That which exists in the mind is 'mental' (<s>mānasī</s>). 'Distracted' (<s>vyagrā</s>) — having diverse [objects as] primary [focus], meaning having diverse objects. Or, 'devoid of a primary [focus]'...

body.text: ity ubhayāvadhāraṇaṃ. saptaiva sālambanāḥ sālambanā eva ca sapteti.
body.translated_text: This is a double restriction: only seven have objects, and those that have objects are only seven.

body.text: sālambanam iti. uktavyatirekeṇedam ucyate. atrāpy ubhayāvadhāraṇaṃ. dharmārdham eva sālambanaṃ. sālambanam eva ca dharmārdham iti. yasmāc ca saptaiva sālambanā dharmārdhaṃ caiva sālambanam iti avadhāraṇam asti tasmāc ccheṣā rūpiṇo dhātavo dharmadhātupradeśaś cāsaṃyukto 'nālambanā iti siddham ity uktaṃ. tathā hy anavadhāraṇe hy ayam artho na sidhyet.
body.translated_text: has objects. This is stated by exclusion of what was [already] mentioned. Here too there is a double restriction: only half of the <s>dharma</s> [element] has objects, and that which has objects is only half of the <s>dharma</s> [element]. And because there is the restriction that only seven have objects and only half of the <s>dharma</s> [element] has objects, therefore the remaining material elements [and] the <s>dharma</s>-element...

body.text: iti navānupāttā evety avadhāraṇaṃ. aṣṭamasyārdhena sārdham iti. saheti yāvat.
body.translated_text: The restriction is: nine are exclusively unappropriated. 'Together with half of the eighth' — [meaning] 'with.'

body.text: iti. te ca sapta cittadhātavo dharmadhātuś ca yasyārdhaṃ sālambanam uktaṃ. aṣṭagrahaṇaṃ sakaladharmadhātugrahaṇārthaṃ. mā dharmadhātvardhāgrahaṇaṃ vijñāyīti.
body.translated_text: And those seven mind-elements (<s>cittadhātu</s>) and the <s>dharma</s>-element, of which half was said to have objects. The word 'eight' is for grasping the entire <s>dharma</s>-element — lest half of the <s>dharma</s>-element not be grasped.

body.text: iti navānupāttā ity uktāḥ.
body.translated_text: are the nine said to be unappropriated.

children.text: cakṣurādayaḥ paṃca śabdavarjyāś ca rūpādayaś catvāra iti nava te dvidhaiva. upāttānupāttā ity arthaḥ. na tūpāttā eveti. etadarthaṃ ca.
children.translated_text: The five [beginning with] the eye, and the four [beginning with] form excluding sound — [these] nine are exclusively twofold — meaning appropriated and unappropriated. Not exclusively appropriated — and for this purpose:

body.text: punaḥ sūtritaṃ. anugrahopaghātābhyām anyonyānuvidhānād [Tib. 61a] iti. cakṣurdhātvādīnām anugrahopaghātābhyām aṃjanādipāṇighātādilakṣaṇābhyāṃ
body.translated_text: is stated again. 'Because of mutual conformity through benefit and harm' — of the eye-element and so forth, through benefit and harm characterized by [the application of] collyrium and the like, and by the striking of the hand and so forth

body.text: cittacaittānām anugrahopaghātau bhavataḥ. cittacaittānāṃ cānugrahopaghātābhyāṃ saumanasyadaurmanasyalakṣaṇābhyāṃ cakṣurdhātvādīnām anugrahopaghātau bhavataḥ. atas te cittacaittair adhiṣṭhānabhāvenopagṛhītā ucyante svīkṛtā ity arthaḥ. yal loke sacetanam iti sajīvam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: benefit and harm of mind and mental factors occur. And through benefit and harm of mind and mental factors, characterized by mental pleasure and mental displeasure, benefit and harm of the eye-element and so forth occur. Therefore, those [sense-faculties], supported by mind and mental factors in the mode of a foundation, are said to be 'appropriated' — meaning 'made one's own.' As in the world, if...

body.text: ity ubhayāvadhāraṇaṃ. spraṣṭavyam eva dvividhaṃ dvividham eva spraṣṭavyam eveti.
body.translated_text: This is a double restriction: only the tangible is twofold, and the twofold is only the tangible.

body.text: ity atrāpy ubhayāvadhāraṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: Here too there is a double restriction.

children.translated_text: 'And a part of the <s>dharma</s>-element is derived' —

body.text: ity atrāpy ubhayāvadhāraṇaṃ. yasmāc caite ubhayāvadhāritāḥ. tasmāc cheṣāḥ sapta cittadhātavo dharmadhātuś cāvijñaptivarjyo nobhayatheti siddhaṃ. bhūtānāṃ catuṣkakhakkhaṭādilakṣaṇāvadhāraṇād iti. catuṣkāvadhāraṇāt pṛthivyaptejovāyudhātavaḥ spraṣṭavyadhātau catvāri bhūtāni. ślakṣṇatvādayas tatra cakṣurādayaś ca na bhūtāni. khakkhaṭādilakṣaṇāvadhāraṇāc ca pṛthivyaptejovāyudhātuṣv anye dharmāś cakṣurādayo nāntarbhāvaṃ gacchanti. kathaṃ. catvāri mahābhūtāni pṛthivīdhātur [Tib. 61b] abdhātus tejodhātur vāyudhātuḥ. pṛthivīdhātuḥ katamaḥ khakkhaṭatvam iti vistaraḥ. teṣāṃ ca spraṣṭavyatvād iti. teṣāṃ ca khakkhaṭatvādīnāṃ spraṣṭavyatvāt. yasmāt tāni spraṣṭavyāni. varṇādayas tu draṣṭavyāḥ śrotavyā ghrātavyāḥ svādayitavyāḥ. kathaṃ gamyate spraṣṭavyāni tānīti. ata āha. na hi kāṭhinyādīni cakṣurādibhir gṛhyante. kiṃ tarhi. kāyendriyeṇaivety ato 'vagamyate spraṣṭavyāni tānīti. syān mataṃ te 'pi varṇādayaḥ spraṣṭavyā ity ata āha. nāpi varṇādayaḥ kāyendriyeṇa. kiṃ. gṛhyanta iti prakṛtaṃ. uktaṃ ca sūtra iti vistaraḥ. aparasminn api sūtre spaṣṭam ādarśitaṃ. katham iti vistareṇa yāvad idam uktaṃ. spraṣṭavyāni bhikṣo bāhyam āyatanaṃ catvāri mahābhūtāni catvāri mahābhūtāny upādāya rūpy anidarśanaṃ sapratigham iti. śeṣaṃ cakṣurādyāyatanaṃ na bhūtānīti spaṣṭam ādarśitaṃ. yat tarhi sūtra uktam iti vistaraḥ. yac cakṣuṣi māṃsapiṇḍe khakkhaṭakharagataṃ kharaprakāra ity arthaḥ. cakṣurindriyaṃ khakkhaṭasvabhāvam iti matvā codayanti. tenāvinirbhāgavartino māṃsapiṇḍasyaiṣa upadeśa iti. tena cakṣurindriyeṇāvinirbhāgavartino 'dhiṣṭhānasya etad vacanaṃ. bhavati hi cakṣuradhiṣṭhāne 'pi cakṣurupacāraḥ. ata eva māṃsapiṇḍa iti grahaṇaṃ. anyathā cakṣuṣīty evāvakṣyat yadīndriyam eveṣyate. [Tib. 62a] ṣaḍdhātur ayaṃ
body.translated_text: Here too there is a double restriction. And because these have been doubly restricted, therefore it is established that the remaining seven mind-elements and the <s>dharma</s>-element excluding non-manifest [form] are neither [great element nor derived]. 'Because of the restriction that the characteristics of the great elements are the four [beginning with] hardness and so forth' — because of the restriction to four, the earth, water, fire, and wind elements [are included in] the tangible...

body.text:
bhikṣo puruṣa iti vistaraḥ. garbhāvakrāntisūtre kalalādyavasthāyām iti bhūtamātropadeśān na bhautikam astīti codyam āśaṃkyāha. mūlasattvadravyasaṃdarśānārtham iti. mūlasya sattvadravyasya saṃdarśanārtham eva. pṛthivīdhātvādayaś catvāro mūlasattvaṃ. paṃcānāṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ sparśāyatanānāṃ tata utpatteḥ. manodhātur api mūlasattvaṃ manaḥsparśāyatanasya tata utpatteḥ. atha vā caturṇāṃ pṛthivīdhātvādīnām upādāyarūpāśrayatvāt. vijñānadhātoś ca caitasikānām āśrayatvāt ta eva mūlasattvaṃ. kathaṃ gamyate. punaḥ ṣaṭsparśāyatanavacanāt. tattraiva sūtre paścād uktaṃ. ṣaṭ sparśāyatanānīti cakṣuḥsprarśāyatanaṃ yāvan manaḥsparśāyatanam iti. ato vijñāyate mūlasattvadravyasaṃdarśanārthatvāt ṣaḍdhātur ayaṃ bhikṣo puruṣa iti vacanaṃ. na tu bhūtamātratvād iti. nanu ca yathā vijñānadhātor avyatiriktam api manaḥsparśāyatanaṃ punar ucyate. evaṃ cakṣurādīny api caturdhātvavyatiriktāni punar ucyerann iti. ato na punaḥ ṣaṭsparśāyatanavacanena tadvyatiriktabhautikāstitvasiddhiḥ. naitad evaṃ. yadi hi pṛthivīdhātvādaya eva sparśāyatanāni abhaviṣyan bhūtāny eva sparśāyatanānīty evāvakṣyat. na tv evaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. cakṣuḥsparśāyatanaṃ yāvan manaḥsparśāyatanam iti. ato 'vagamyate. pṛthivīdhātvādivyatiriktāni cakṣurādīnīti. [Tib. 62b] vijñānadhātus tu cakṣurādisparśāyatanavacanānuṣaṃgena punar ucyate. sparśāyatanam iti ko 'rthaḥ. sparśasya caitasikasyāśraya ity arthaḥ. cittabhāvaprasaṃgāc ceti. yadi ṣaḍdhātur ayaṃ bhikṣo puruṣa iti yathābhūtam eva dravyāṇi gṛhyeran nānyāni tadāśritāni dravyāṇi. tenaitat prāptaṃ. vijñānadhātumātragrahaṇāt. atra caitasikānāṃ tadāśritānām agrahaṇaprasaṃgaḥ. iṣṭatvād adoṣa iti cet. na. sapakṣālatvād asya pakṣasya. sāpakṣālo hy ayaṃ pakṣaḥ. cittaviśeṣā eva caitasikā iti svasiddhāntavirodhāt. tenāha. na ca yuktaṃ cittam eva caittā ity abhyupagantuṃ. kasmāt. saṃjñā vedanā ca caitasika eṣa dharmaś cittaniśrita iti sūtravacanāt. sādhanaṃ cātropatiṣṭhate. cittād arthāntarabhūte saṃjñāvedane. skandhadeśanāyāṃ pṛthag deśitatvāt. rūpaskandhavad iti. atha vā svāśrayād arthāntarabhūte saṃjñāvedane. tadāśritatvāt. yat svāśrayāśritaṃ tat svāśrayād arthāntarabhūtaṃ. tadyathā kuḍyāśritaṃ citraṃ. sarāgādicittavacanāc ceti. sarāgaṃ cittaṃ sarāgaṃ cittam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. vigatarāgaṃ cittaṃ vigatarāgaṃ cittaṃ iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti.
sadveṣaṃ cittaṃ sadveṣaṃ cittam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 63a] atra
body.translated_text: O monk, a person' — thus in detail. In the <s>Garbhāvakrānti-sūtra</s>, regarding the <s>kalala</s> (embryonic) stage and so forth — anticipating the objection that from the teaching of elements alone, derived form does not exist — he says: 'For the purpose of showing the fundamental substance of a living being.' It is for the purpose of showing just the fundamental substance of a sentient being. The four — earth element and the rest — are the fundamental substance, since the five sense-bases beginning with the eye arise from them. The mind element too is a fundamental substance, since the mind-contact sense-base arises from it. Alternatively, because the four beginning with the earth element are the support of derived form, and because the consciousness element is the support of mental factors — these same are the fundamental substance. How is this understood? From the subsequent mention of the six contact sense-bases. For in that same <s>sūtra</s>, it is later stated: 'Six contact sense-bases — the eye-contact sense-base through to the mind-contact sense-base.' Therefore it is understood that the statement 'This person, O monk, consists of six elements' is for the purpose of showing the fundamental substance — not because [a person consists of] mere elements. But [one might object:] just as the mind-contact sense-base, though not distinct from the consciousness element, is mentioned again, so too the eye and other [sense-faculties], not being distinct from the four elements, might be mentioned again. Therefore, the subsequent mention of six contact sense-bases does not establish the existence of derived [forms] distinct from [the elements]. [Reply:] This is not so. For if the earth element and the rest themselves were the contact sense-bases, it would have been stated 'the elements themselves are the contact sense-bases.' But it is not so stated. Rather: 'The eye-contact sense-base through to the mind-contact sense-base.' Therefore it is understood that the eye and the rest are distinct from the earth element and the rest. But the consciousness element is mentioned again in connection with the mention of the eye and other contact sense-bases. What is the meaning of 'contact sense-base'? It means 'the support of contact, a mental factor.' 'And because the absurd consequence of [mental factors being merely] states of mind would follow' — if in 'This person, O monk, consists of six elements' only the substances as such were grasped and no other substances dependent on them, then this would follow: from the grasping of consciousness element alone, there would be the unwanted consequence of not grasping the mental factors dependent on it. If [one says] there is no fault because [their exclusion] is desired — no, because this position has a deficiency. For this position has a deficiency — it contradicts your own established doctrine that mental factors are merely differentiations of mind. Therefore he says: 'And it is not proper to accept that mental factors are just mind.' Why? [Because of the <s>sūtra</s> statement:] 'Perception and feeling are mental factors; this <s>dharma</s> is dependent on mind' — thus from the <s>sūtra</s> statement —

body.text: sādhanaṃ. sarāgaṃ cittam iti cittarāgayoḥ parasparato 'rthāntaratvaṃ. sahayoganirdiṣṭatvāt. saputraś caitra iti sahayoganirdiṣṭacaitraputravad iti.
body.translated_text: — the proof. 'Mind with passion' — mind and passion are mutually distinct entities, because they are indicated as co-occurring. Just as in '<s>Caitra</s> with his son,' <s>Caitra</s> and the son indicated as co-occurring [are distinct].

body.text: paramāṇusaṃcayasvabhāvā daśaivety arthaḥ. anye tu dhātavo 'smād avadhāraṇān na saṃcitā iti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: The meaning is: only ten have the nature of an aggregate of atoms. Other <s>dhātus</s> are established as not aggregated, from this restriction.

body.text: (I.35) tulayatīti kasya dhātor etad rūpaṃ. tathā hi tula unmāna ity asya dhātos tolayatīti rūpaṃ bhavati. naiṣa doṣaḥ. tulāṃ karoti tulayatīti prātipadikadhātor etad rūpam iṣyate. karmaṇi ca tulya iti rūpaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: (I.35) '<s>Tulayati</s>' (weighs/burns) — of which element is this the form [of the verb]? For the form '<s>tolayati</s>' comes from the root '<s>tula</s> [meaning] measurement.' [Reply:] This is no fault. 'He makes a balance — <s>tulayati</s>' — thus by denominative derivation.

body.text: iti rūpādikaṃ śabdavarjyaṃ. paraśudārvādisaṃjñakam iti. paraśvādisaṃjñakaṃ chinatti dārvādisaṃjñākaṃ chidyate. saṃbhavaṃ praty evam ucyate. kadācit paraśvādisaṃjñakaṃ chidyate. dārvādisaṃjñakam api cchinatti. saṃbandhotpādina iti vistaraḥ. saṃbandhenāvibhāgenotpattuṃ śīlam asyeti saṃbandhotpādi. saṃghātasroto rūpādisaṃghātasaṃtāna ity arthaḥ. tasya vibhaktotpādanaṃ vibhaktajananaṃ yat sa chedaḥ. kṣaṇikānāṃ hi bhāvānāṃ vināpi paraśvādinā cchedo bhavaty eva. saṃtānanirodhas tu paraśvādineti. paraśvādikaṃ chinattīty ucyate. kāraṇasāmagrīviśeṣavaśād vikāryaviśeṣotpattir bhavati. tatra dhātucatuṣṭayam avacchinatti chidyate vety avadhāryate. tathāvadhāraṇāc cānye dhātavo nobhayatheti siddhaṃ. ata eva cāha. na kāyendriyādīni chidyanta iti vistaraḥ. atra na cakṣurindriyādīnīti vaktavye kasmāt kāyendriyādīnīti vacanaṃ. yasmāt kāyendriye parisphuṭaś chedo bhavati yadi bhaved ity ataḥ [Tib. 63b] kāyendriyapurassarāṇīndriyāṇi kathyante. niravaśesāṃgacchede sarvāṃgapratyaṃgacchede. tadadvaidhīkaraṇāt teṣāṃ kāyendriyādīnāṃ advaidhīkaraṇāt. kathaṃ punar gamyate tadadvaidhīkaraṇam iti. ataḥ punar āha. na hīndriyāṇi dvidhā bhavanti chinnasyāṃgasya kāyād apagatasya nirindriyatvāt. idam api kathaṃ gamyate. nirindriyaṃ tad aṃgaṃ yac chinnaṃ kāyād apagatam iti. yasmāt tat pratītya spraṣṭavyādikaṃ ca kāyādivijñānānupapattiḥ. kathaṃ tarhi chinnena punar lagnena nāsikāgreṇa kāyavijñānotpattiḥ. nāsikāmūlasaṃbandhena punaḥ kāyendriyotpatter adoṣaḥ. katham iha gṛhagodhikādīnāṃ pucchāni chinnāni spandante yadi tatra kāyendriyaṃ nāsti. vāyadhātor eṣa vikāro naitat kāyendriyasya karmety avagantavyaṃ. na cāpi chindanti maṇiprabhāvad acchatvāt. yathā maṇiprabhā na chinatti acchatvāt. tadvad indriyāṇi.
body.translated_text: thus, form and the rest, excluding sound. 'Designated as axe, wood, and so on' — what is designated as 'axe' and the like cuts; what is designated as 'wood' and the like is cut. This is said with reference to possibility. Sometimes the axe —

body.text: ity evaṃśabdena tad eva bāhyaṃ dhātucatuṣṭayaṃ tathātvena pradarśyate. kāṣṭhādīnām agnikṛto vikāro dāhaḥ. ca cendriyānāṃ na bhavati maṇiprabhāvad acchatvāt. na hi tāni kāṣṭhādivac carmādivad vā vikriyante. kiṃ tarhi. tatsaṃbandhāt pravāhachedo bhavati. tulādibhūtaṃ ca tad eva dhātucatuṣṭayaṃ tulayati nendriyāṇi tathaivācchatvāt. amūrtānāṃ tu dhātūnām amūrtatvād eva chedādyasaṃbhava iti. teṣāṃ chedādi na cintyate. na śabda uccheditvād iti. [Tib. 64a] kiṃ. chinatti chidyate dahyate tulyati vāpravāhavartitvāt.
body.translated_text: thus, the word 'likewise' (<s>evam</s>) shows that same external group of four elements in that manner. The modification produced by fire of wood and the like is burning. 'But [this] does not [happen] to the sense-faculties, because of the power of gems' — [fire] does not [burn them], being impeded —

children.translated_text: 'There is dispute [over whether] the burner and what is balanced [are the same elements]' —

body.text: ity uttaratrāpīdam anuvartate na śabda uccheditvād iti. tad eva dhātucatuṣṭayaṃ dāhakaṃ tulyaṃ ceti. agnikṣārādi dāhakaṃ. samastasyātra dhātucatuṣṭayasya bhasmādivikārahetutvāt. lavaṇādi tulyaṃ. tatrāpi samastasya tulāvanatihetutvād ity ekeṣām abhiprāyaḥ. tejodhātūr eva dagdhā gurutvam eva ca tulyam iti. tejodhātur evāgnijvālādigata udbhūtavṛttir dahati. pṛthivīdhātvādīnām udbhūtasvavṛttitve 'py adāhakatvadarśanāt. gurutvam eva copādāyarūpam udbhūtavṛtti tulyate. ātapādiṣu laghudravyeṣu rūpādīnām udbhūtavṛttitve 'py atulyatvadarśanāt.
body.translated_text: thus, and this applies further on as well: 'not sound, because it is cut off.' That same group of four elements is both the burner and the balanced. Fire, alkali, and so on are the burners. Of the entire group of four elements here —

body.text: iti. paṃcagrahaṇaṃ manonivṛttyarthaṃ. adhyātmagrahaṇaṃ rūpādinivṛttyarthaṃ. vipākajaupacayikā eva paṃcādhyātmikā na naiṣyandikā ity avadhāraṇaṃ. kasmāt. tadvyatiriktaniṣyandābhāvāt. vipākajā aupacayikāś ca yady api naiṣyandikā bhavanti.
body.translated_text: thus. The mention of 'five' is for the purpose of excluding mind. The mention of 'internal' is for the purpose of excluding form and the rest [as objects]. 'Only the five internal [sense-faculties] are retributive or growth-based, not outflow' — this is a restriction. Why?

children.translated_text: 'An outflow is similar to its cause' —

body.text: iti kṛtvā. te tu vipākajaupacayikatvenaiva saṃgṛhītatvāt. na naiṣyandikā iti gṛhyante. ye tu svahetusadṛśā na ca vipākajā na caupacayikāḥ. ta iha naiṣyandikā [Tib. 64b] abhipretāḥ. na caivaṃvidhāś cakṣurādayo bhavanti. kiṃ tarhi vipākajā vā aupacayikā vā bhavantīty ata evam ucyate. tadvyatiriktaniṣyandābhāvād iti. kathaṃ punar jñāyate naiṣyandikās te na santīti. mṛtasyānanuvṛtteḥ. na hi rūpādivan mṛtasya cakṣurdhātvādayo 'nuvartante. vipākahetor jātā iti. vipākasya phalasya hetur vipākahetuḥ. vipākahetor jātā vipākajāḥ. madhyapadalopāt hetuśabdalopāt gorathavat. yathā gobhir yukto ratho goratha iti. phalakālaprāptaṃ vā karmeti. vipākaphalotpattyanantarakṣaṇāvastham ity arthaḥ. vipacyata iti vipākaḥ. karmakartari ghañ. vipākāj jātā vipākajāḥ. phalaṃ tu vipaktir eveti vipāka iti. bhāve ghañ. bhavatu vā hetau phalopacāra iti vistaraḥ. avipākasvabhāvo 'pi karmalakṣaṇo hetm vipāka ity
body.translated_text: because of this. But since they [the five internal sense-faculties] are already included as retributive or growth-based, they are not taken as outflow. Those which are similar to their own causes but are neither retributive nor growth-based — those are taken here as outflow.

body.text: ucyate. tadutpādakatvāt. yathā phale hetūpucāra iti vistaraḥ. ṣaḍ imāni sparśāyatanāni cakṣurādīni paurāṇaṃ karma purāṇe janmani bhavaṃ purāṇam eva vā paurāṇaṃ karma. tāni sparśāyatanāni apaurāṇakarmasvabhāvāny api paurāṇaṃ karmety ucyaṃte. tajjātatvāt. evam iha viparyayopacāro draṣṭavyaḥ. āhārasaṃskārasvapnasamādhiviśeṣair upacitā aupacayikā iti. viśeṣaśabdaḥ pratyekam abhisaṃbadhyate. tatrāhārasvapnau loke pratītau. saṃskāro 'bhyaṃgasnānānuvāsanādisvabhāvḥ. [Tib. 65a] samādhiś cittaikāgratālakṣaṇaḥ. samīpe caya upacayaḥ. upacaye bhavā aupacayikāḥ sainikavat. upacayā eva vā aupacayikāḥ vainayikavat. svārthe taddhitavidhānāt. brahmacaryeṇa cety eke iti. brahmacāriṇām upaśāntendriyāṇāṃ śarīropacayadarśanāt. anupaghātamātraṃ tu tena syād iti. abrahmacaryeṇa śarīrāpacayaḥ. brahmacaryeṇa tu śarīrāpacayo na bhavati. tasmād āha. anupayghātamātraṃ tu tena brahmacaryeṇa syāt nopacayaḥ. upacayas tv āhārādibhir eva. kasmāt tarhi pravrajitānāṃ keṣāṃcic charīrāpacayo bhavati. kāmaparidāhādiyogād asau bhavet. pratiprākāra ivārakṣeti. upacayasaṃtāno vipākasaṃtānasya parivāryāvasthānenārakṣā. śabda aupacayika ity anupacitakāyasya śabdasauṣṭhavādarśanāt. icchātaḥ pravṛtter iti. śabdo me syād iti icchayā śabdaḥ pravartate. anicchayā na pravartate. vipākajaś ca dharmo 'nicchato 'pi pravartate. tasmān na vipākajaḥ śabdaḥ. sādhanaṃ cātrocyate. na vipākajaḥ śabdaḥ. icchātaḥ pravṛtteḥ. yoniśomanasikāracaitasikavat. yat tu vipākajaṃ. na tasyecchayā pravṛttiḥ. tadyathā cakṣurindriyasyeti. yat tarhīti vistaraḥ. anena svasiddhāntaviruddhatāṃ pratijñāyā udgrāhayati. tṛtīyāsau paraṃparety eka iti vistaraḥ. bhūtāni pāruṣyavirateḥ karmapathasya kaṇṭhe vipākasvabhāvāni [Tib. 65b] nirvartante. tebhyaḥ śabdaḥ. dvitīye 'pi pakṣe karmebhyo vipākajāni bhūtāni. tebhya aupacayikāni āhāropacayataḥ samādhyupacayato vā bhūtāntarāṇi. tebhyo naiṣyandikāni pūrvabhūtavyatiriktāny āgantukāni bhūtāni. tebhyaḥ śabda iti. paraṃparābhinirvartanaṃ tv abhisaṃdhāya pāruṣyavirater brahmasvaratā nirvartata ity uktaṃ. anena svasiddhāntaviruddhatā tasyāḥ pratijñāyāḥ parihriyate. yadi śabdavad yuktivirodhaḥ syād iti. śabda icchātaḥ pravartata iti vipākayuktivirodhāt na vipākaja uktaḥ. tad yadi tadvac chārīriky api vedanā icchātaḥ pravartate na vipākajā syāt. na tv icchātaḥ sā pravartate. kiṃ tarhi. anicchayāpi sā pravartate. cakṣurādivat. tasmād vipākajeti yujyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. kīdṛśī punaḥ sā. yā sukhaduḥkhapratyayopasaṃhāram antareṇāpi pravartate. naiṣyandikāḥ sabhāgasarvatragahetujanitā iti. sabhāgasarvatragahetubhir eva janitā na vipākahetuneti avadhāraṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: It is called [thus] because it produces that. As [the term] 'cause' is applied figuratively to the effect — and so on in detail. 'These six contact-bases — the eye, etc. — are old <s>karma</s>' — <s>karma</s> from a former birth is 'old'; or [<s>karma</s>] that occurred in a former [birth] is itself 'old.' Those contact-bases, even though they do not have old <s>karma</s> as their intrinsic nature, are called 'old <s>karma</s>' because they are born from it. Thus, here one should see a figurative usage by transposition. 'Nourished by food, formations, sleep, and <s>samādhi</s> — [these are called] <s>aupacayika</s> (accrued)' — the word 'special' (<s>viśeṣa</s>) connects with each separately. Of these, food and sleep are well-known in the world. 'Formation' (<s>saṃskāra</s>) here has the nature of anointing, bathing, therapeutic oiling, etc. [Tib. 65a] '<s>Samādhi</s>' is characterized by one-pointedness of mind. '<s>Upacaya</s>' means accrual in proximity. Those that exist in accrual are '<s>aupacayika</s>' — like 'military' (<s>sainika</s>). Or, the accruals themselves are '<s>aupacayika</s>' — like '<s>vainayika</s>' (relating to the <s>Vinaya</s>), since the <s>taddhita</s> suffix is used in its own sense. 'And through celibacy, say some' — because one sees bodily accrual in celibates (<s>brahmacārin</s>) whose faculties have become calm. 'But that would only be non-deterioration' — sexual indulgence causes bodily deterioration; celibacy, however, does not cause bodily deterioration. Therefore he says: 'But through celibacy there would only be non-deterioration, not [actual] accrual.' Accrual, however, is [caused] by food, etc. alone. Why then does bodily deterioration occur for some renunciants? That would be due to the burning of desire, etc. 'Like a rampart serving as a guard' — the continuum of accrual is the guarding of the continuum of maturation by surrounding and maintaining it. 'Sound is <s>aupacayika</s>' — because one does not see beauty of voice in one whose body is not accrued. 'Because it operates from desire' — sound operates from the desire 'let me have a sound'; it does not operate without desire. But a maturation-born (<s>vipākaja</s>) <s>dharma</s> operates even without desire. Therefore, sound is not maturation-born. And the proof is stated here: Sound is not maturation-born because it operates from desire — like mental factors [born from] proper attention. But what is maturation-born — that does not operate by desire, just as the eye-faculty [does not]. 'But then' — and so on in detail. By this, he shows the contradiction with one's own established doctrine. 'That is the third, [related] by indirect causation' — and so on. The great elements, having the nature of maturation, are produced in the throat due to non-abstention from harsh speech, which is a path of action. [Tib. 65b] From those [great elements], sound [arises]. In the second position too: the great elements, being maturation-born from <s>karma</s>, [produce further elements]; from those, other great elements [arise as] accrued through food-accrual or <s>samādhi</s>-accrual, which are <s>aupacayika</s>; from those, adventitious great elements different from the previous ones, which are outflow (<s>naiṣyandika</s>); from those, sound [arises]. But it is said 'the <s>Brahma</s>-voice arises from non-abstention from harsh speech' with the intention of indirect production. By this, the contradiction with one's own established doctrine in that thesis is resolved. 'If, like sound, there were a contradiction with reasoning' — sound was said not to be maturation-born because of the reasoning-contradiction that 'sound operates from desire.' If, similarly, bodily feeling too operates from desire, it would not be maturation-born. But that does not operate from desire. Rather, it operates even without desire — like the eye-faculty, etc. Therefore, it is proper [to say it is] maturation-born — this is the intent. What kind then is that [feeling]? 'That which operates even without the conjunction of conditions for pleasure and pain.' '<s>Naiṣyandika</s>' (outflow) means 'produced by <s>sabhāga</s> (similar) and <s>sarvatraga</s> (universal) causes' — the restriction is: produced only by similar and universal causes, not by the maturation cause.

body.text:
vipākajā vipākahetujanitā iti. vipākahetunā janitā eva na tu vipākahetunaiva janitā ity avadhāraṇaṃ. sabhāgahetunāpi janitā vipākajā bhavanti. tatra cāṣṭāv apratighā naiṣyandikā
vipākajā evety avadhāryate. na hi et [Tib. 66a] aupacayikāḥ saṃcayābhāvāt. aparamāṇusaṃcayasvabhāvatvād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: '<s>Vipākaja</s>' (maturation-born) means 'produced by the maturation cause' — the restriction is: produced by the maturation cause, but not by the maturation cause alone. Those produced also by the similar cause are maturation-born. And of these, 'the eight non-resistant [dhātus] that are outflow or maturation-born' [Tib. 66a] — this is a restriction. For these are not <s>aupacayika</s>, because of the absence of accumulation — the meaning is: because they do not have the nature of atomic accumulation.

body.text: iti. tridhānya evety avadhāryate. tartra vipākajā indriyāvinirbhāgina eva.
body.translated_text: This is a restriction: 'the others are precisely threefold.' Of these, the maturation-born are only those not distinguished [as separate] from the faculties.

children.translated_text: 'Maturation is an indeterminate <s>dharma</s> belonging to beings' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. naiṣyandikaupacayikās tu indriyavinirbhāgino 'pi. kathaṃ punar gamyate. indriyavinirbhāgino 'pi naiṣyandikāḥ santīti. mṛtasyāpi tadanuvṛttidarśanāt. na hy asattvasaṃkhyātā vipākajā iṣyante.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. But the outflow and accrued [types] may also be distinguished from the faculties. How is it known that there are outflow [types] distinguished from the faculties? Because their continuation is observed even in the deceased. For maturation-born [dharmas] are not accepted as belonging to a non-being.

body.text: iti. eka eva dravyavān ity avadhāraṇaṃ. sāratvād dravyam ity avināśāt. kṣaṇam ekam anaiṣyandikā bhavantīti. kṣaṇam ekam asabhāgahetunirvartitāḥ. pūrvakṣaṇānāsravābhāvāt kṣaṇikā na tu kṣaṇāntaravināśina ity ayam artho 'bhipretaḥ. anyathā hi paścimā eva dhātavaḥ kṣaṇikā ity avadhāraṇāt taditareṣāṃ dhātūnām akṣaṇikatvaprasaṃgaḥ. kathaṃ punar duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāntikalāpe manodhātur manovijñānadhātuś ca yugapad bhavataḥ. na hi vijñānadvayasamavadhānam iṣyate. nocyate yugapat tau bhavata iti. kiṃ tarhi. ekam atra vijñānaṃ dhātudvayatvena vyavasthāpyate. nāmadvayena kathyate ity arthaḥ. tena vyācaṣṭe duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāntisaṃprayuktaṃ cittaṃ manodhātur manovijñānadhātuś ceti. [Tib. 66b] śeṣās tatsahabhuvo dharmadhātur iti. tatra kṣāntikalāpe cittād anye dharmāḥ śeṣāḥ. tadsahabhuvas tayā kṣāntyā sahabhuvaḥ. tadyathā anāsravasaṃvaro rūpaṃ vedanāsaṃjñācetanādayaḥ saṃprayuktāḥ. teṣāṃ ca prāptijātyādayo dharmadhātur iti.
body.translated_text: This is a restriction: 'only one is substantial.' '<s>Dravya</s>' (substance) [is so called] because of being essential (<s>sāra</s>) — because of non-destruction. 'For one moment they are non-outflow' — for one moment they are not produced by the similar cause, because in the preceding moment there was no undefiled [<s>dharma</s>]. 'Momentary' does not mean 'perishing in the next moment' — this is the intended meaning. For otherwise, since only the final elements would be momentary — by the restriction — the other elements would turn out to be non-momentary. How then can the mind-element and the mental-consciousness element co-exist simultaneously in the assemblage of the insight-patience of the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering? For the co-occurrence of two consciousnesses is not accepted. [Reply:] It is not said that those two exist simultaneously. Rather, a single consciousness here is established as two elements. The meaning is: it is described by two names. Therefore he explains: 'The mind conjoined with the insight-patience of the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering is both the mind-element and the mental-consciousness element.' [Tib. 66b] 'The rest, co-existing with that, are the <s>dharma-dhātu</s>' — 'the rest' means the <s>dharmas</s> other than mind in the <s>kṣānti</s>-assemblage; 'co-existing with that' means co-existing with that <s>kṣānti</s> — namely, the undefiled restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) [as] form, feeling, perception, volition, etc. that are conjoined, and their attainment, birth, etc. — [all these are] the <s>dharma-dhātu</s>.

body.text: (I.37cd) samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhata iti. prāptim alabdhapūrvāṃ labhata ity arthaḥ. cakṣurvijñānadhātunāpi sa iti. kiṃ. samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhata ity adhikṛtaṃ.
body.translated_text: (I.37cd) 'Obtains possession' — the meaning is: obtains an attainment (<s>prāpti</s>) not previously obtained. 'By the eye-consciousness element too, he' — what? [He] 'obtains possession' — this is the topic under discussion.

body.text: ity anena prathamadvitīye koṭyau darśite.
body.translated_text: by this, the first and second alternatives are shown.

body.text: anena tṛtīyā koṭir darśitā. caturthī tu uktanirmukteti sugamatvān na darśitā.
body.translated_text: by this, the third alternative is shown. The fourth, however, is 'other than those stated' — since it is easy [to understand], it is not shown.

body.text: śabdena vā sāpy uktā. apṛthag asaha ceti. kāmadhātau krameṇa cakṣurindriyaṃ pratilabhamāna iti. kāmadhātau sthitaḥ pudgalaḥ krameṇa kalalādikrameṇa
body.translated_text: by the particle 'and,' that [fourth alternative] too is stated — 'not separately and not together.' 'A person situated in the desire-realm, gradually obtaining the eye-faculty' — a person situated in the desire-realm, gradually — in the sequence of <s>kalala</s> (embryonic stages), etc.

body.text: mṛtyukrameṇa vā. cakṣurindriyaṃ. kiṃpratisaṃyuktaṃ. kiṃ kāmadhātāv eva. nety ucyate. aviśeṣeṇa kāmapratisaṃyuktaṃ vā rūpapratisaṃyuktaṃ vā pratilabhamānaḥ. kalalādyavasthāyāṃ tathā krameṇa maraṇasyācakṣuṣmanmaraṇasya ca kāle cakṣurdhātunā asamanvāgataḥ. kalalādyavasthāyāṃ tathā maraṇāvasthāyāṃ vā tadabhāvāt. ṣaḍāyatanotpattyavasthāyāṃ bhavasyāntarāle vā tenedānīṃ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. na tu cakṣurvijñānadhātunā asamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. yasmād asau kuśalakliṣṭenātītānāgatena samanvāgata eva pūrvam antarābhavapratisaṃdhikāle. viprakṛtāvasthā hy eṣādhikriyate na pratilabdhavatpratilapsyamānāvasthā. cakṣurvijñānadhātuneti [Tib. 67a] vistaraḥ. dvitīyādidhyānopapannas tatra tasya cakṣurvijñānadhātor abhāvāt tena pūrvam asamanvāgata idānīṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikam anivṛtāvyākṛtasvabhāvaṃ saṃmukhīkurvāṇaḥ. tena cakṣurvijñānadhātunā samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. na tu cakṣurdhātunā asamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. pratilabdhavatsamanvāgatatvāt. tatpracyutaś cādhastād upapadyamāna iti. dvitīyādidhyānapracyuto 'dhastāt prathame dhyāne kāmadhātau copapadyamānaś cakṣurvijñānadhātunā asamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. antarābhavapratisaṃdhāne kuśalakliṣṭena atītānāgatena. na tu cakṣurdhātunā asamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. pratilabdhavatsamanvāgatatvāt. syād ubhayeneti vistaraḥ. ārūpyadhātucyuta ubhābhyāṃ cakṣurdhātucakṣurvijñānadhātubhyāṃ pūrvam asamanvāgataḥ. antarābhavapratisaṃdhyavasthāyām eva cakṣurdhātunotpādābhimukhena cakṣurvijñānadhātunā kuśalakliṣṭenātītānāgatena samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. avikalendriyā hy antarābhavikāḥ. nobhayena etān ākārān sthāpayitveti. koṭītrayoktān dharmaprakārān tyaktvety arthaḥ. ārūpyadhātucyutas tatraivotpadyamāno nobhābhyām asamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. asamanvāgatatvaṃ tatrāsti na tu samanvāgamapratilambhaḥ. dvitīyādidhyānopapannaś ca cakṣurvijñānam asaṃmukhīkurvāṇo nobhābhyām asamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. kathaṃ. cakṣurdhātunā yady api samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate na tu cakṣurdhātunāsāv asamanvāgataḥ. cakṣurvijñānadhātunā yady apy asau asamanvāgato na tu samanvāgamaṃ [Tib. 67b] pratilabhate tadasaṃmukhīkurvāṇatvāt. cakṣuṣmān kāmadhātusthaḥ sakṛnmaraṇāt antarābhavapratisaṃdhau
body.translated_text: or in the sequence of death. The eye-faculty — bound to what? Bound to the desire-realm alone? No, it is said. Without distinction — obtaining [the eye-faculty] whether bound to the desire-realm or bound to the form-realm. In the <s>kalala</s> stage and likewise, at the time of death or of death without the eye-faculty, one is without possession of the eye-element — in the <s>kalala</s> stage or likewise in the death-stage, because of its absence there. In the stage of the arising of the six sense-bases, or in the intermediate [existence], one now obtains possession of it. But one does not obtain possession of the eye-consciousness element [for the first time], because one was already in possession of it — the wholesome and defiled [types], past and future — previously, at the time of intermediate existence and of conception (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>). For the state being referred to is the unactualized state, not the state of one who has already obtained or will obtain [it]. 'By the eye-consciousness element' [Tib. 67a] — and so on in detail. One reborn in the second <s>dhyāna</s> and above — because of the absence of eye-consciousness there — was previously without possession of it. Now, making present the eye-consciousness belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, which is of unobstructed-indeterminate nature, one obtains possession of the eye-consciousness element. But one does not [first] obtain possession of the eye-element, because one already possessed it. 'And one who has fallen from that, being reborn below' — one who has fallen from the second <s>dhyāna</s> and above, being reborn below in the first <s>dhyāna</s> or the desire-realm, obtains possession of the eye-consciousness element [for the first time] — at the intermediate existence and conception, [in its] wholesome and defiled [forms], past and future. But one does not [first] obtain possession of the eye-element, because one already possessed it. 'There may be [obtaining of] both' — and so on in detail. One who has fallen from the formless realm — previously without possession of both the eye-element and the eye-consciousness element. At the very stage of intermediate existence and conception, one obtains possession of the eye-element (about to arise) and the eye-consciousness element — the wholesome and defiled [types], past and future. For beings in intermediate existence have complete faculties. 'Not of both' — setting aside these [previously described] types. The meaning is: excluding the three alternatives described as types of <s>dharma</s>. One who has fallen from the formless realm and is reborn right there — does not obtain possession of both, despite being without possession, because there is no obtaining of possession there. And one reborn in the second <s>dhyāna</s> and above who does not make present the eye-consciousness — does not obtain possession of both, despite being without possession. How? [Tib. 67b] Although one obtains possession of the eye-element, one was not without possession of the eye-element [before]. Although one is without possession of the eye-consciousness element, one does not obtain [new] possession of it, because one is not making it present. 'One possessing eyes, situated in the desire-realm, [having undergone] a single death, at the intermediate existence and conception'

body.text: nobhābhyām asamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. tābhyāṃ samanvāgatatvāt. yaś cakṣurdhātunā samanvāgataś cakṣurvijñānadhātunāpi sa iti.
body.translated_text: does not obtain possession of either, since one was already in possession of both. 'And one who possesses the eye-element possesses the eye-consciousness element too.'

body.text:
anenaiva sūtreṇedam api catuḥkoṭikaṃ vartayati. lābho hi pratilambhaḥ. prāptimātre 'pi vivakṣayā kadācid bhavati. prathame catuḥkoṭike pratilambho 'dhikṛto dvitīye tu prāptimātraṃ. prathamā koṭir iti vistaraḥ. dvitīyādidhyānopapanno 'vāśyaṃ cakṣurdhātunā samanvāgata indriyair avikalatvāt. cakṣurvijñānadhātunātrāsamanvāgataḥ. tatrābhāvāt. prathamadhyānabhūmikasya cakṣurvijñānasyāsaṃmukhīkriyamāṇatvāt. kāmadhātāv alabdhavihīnacakṣur iti. alabdhaṃ vihīnaṃ vā cakṣur asyālabdhavihīnacakṣuḥ. alabdhacakṣuḥ kalalādyavasthaḥ. vihīnacakṣur vinaṣṭacakṣuḥ. sa kāmadhātau cakṣurvijñānadhātunā antarābhavapratisaṃdhau pratilabdhena kuśalakliṣṭena samanvāgataḥ. na cakṣurdhātunā tasyābhāvāt. labdhāvihīnacakṣur iti. labdham avihīnaṃ cakṣur asya labdhāvihīnacakṣuḥ. sa kāmadhātau cakṣurdhātunā cakṣurvijñānadhātunā ca tathā pūrvaṃ pratilabdhenedānīṃ tv anena cāvyākṛtena samanvāgataḥ. prathamadhyānopapannaś ca tenobhayena samanvāgataḥ. svabhūmikasya tatrāvaśyam astitvāt parabhūmikasya cakṣuṣaḥ sambhavāt. dvitīyādidhyānopapannaś ca paśyan. prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ [Tib. 68a] cakṣurvijñānaṃ saṃmukhīkurvāṇa ity arthaḥ. sa cāpy avaśyam anenobhayena samanvāgataḥ. caturthy etān ākārān sthāpayitveti. ārūpyopapannaḥ.
yathāyogam abhyūhitavyāv iti. yaś cakṣurdhātunā asmanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate rūpadhātunāpi saḥ. yo vā rūpadhātunā cakṣurdhātunāpi saḥ. cakṣurdhāturūpadhātvoḥ syāt
body.translated_text:
By this very sūtra, he also runs this fourfold classification. For 'lābha' means 'obtaining' (pratilambha). Sometimes it refers to mere acquisition too, by intention. In the first fourfold classification, 'obtaining' (pratilambha) is the topic; in the second, mere 'acquisition.' 'The first alternative' — in detail. One born in the second and higher <s>dhyānas</s> is necessarily endowed (<s>samanvāgata</s>) with the eye-element, because the sense-faculties are not deficient. [But] he is not endowed with the eye-consciousness-element here, because of its absence there. Because eye-consciousness belonging to the level of the first <s>dhyāna</s> is not being brought to confrontation. 'One in the desire-realm who has not-obtained or lost the eye' — 'one who has a not-obtained or lost eye' (alabdhavīhīṇacakṣus). 'Not-obtained eye' means one in the stage of <s>kalala</s>, etc. (embryonic stages). 'Lost eye' means one whose eye has been destroyed. He, in the desire-realm, is endowed with the eye-consciousness-element obtained at the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>) or reconnection (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>) — wholesome or defiled. But not with the eye-element, because of its absence. 'One who has obtained and not lost the eye' — 'one whose eye has been obtained and not lost.' He, in the desire-realm, is endowed with both the eye-element and the eye-consciousness-element — previously obtained and also with the present morally indeterminate one. And one born in the first <s>dhyāna</s> is endowed with both — because what belongs to one's own level necessarily exists there, and because an eye belonging to another level is possible. And one born in the second and higher <s>dhyānas</s> who is seeing — meaning, who is bringing to confrontation [Tib. 68a] eye-consciousness belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> level. He too is necessarily endowed with both. 'Setting aside these aspects for the fourth' — one born in the formless realm.
'Should be inferred by proper application' — whoever obtains endowment with the eye-element also [obtains endowment] with the form-element. Or whoever [obtains endowment] with the form-element, also with the eye-element. Of the eye-element and form-element, there may be

body.text: pṛthak tāvat. syāc cakṣurdhātunā samanvāgataḥ. na rūpadhātunā. kāmadhātau krameṇa cakṣurindriyaṃ pratilabhamānaḥ. syād rūpadhātunā na cakṣurdhātuneti iyaṃ koṭir nāsti.
body.translated_text: First, separately: one may be endowed with the eye-element but not with the form-element — one in the desire-realm who is gradually obtaining the eye-faculty. One may [be endowed] with the form-element but not with the eye-element — this alternative does not exist.

body.text: syāt ubhayenāsamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. ārūpyadhātoś cyuto rūpadhātau kāmadhātau copapadyamānaḥ. nobhayena etān ākārān sthāpayitvā. yaś cakṣurdhātusamanvāgato rūpadhātunāpi sa iti pūrvapādakaḥ. yas tāvac cakṣurdhātunā samanvāgato rūpadhātunāpi saḥ. syāt rūpadhātunā na cakṣurdhātunā kalalādyavasthāsv alabdhacakṣur labdhavihīnacakṣuś ca.
body.translated_text: One not endowed with both may obtain endowment — one who, having fallen from the formless realm, is being reborn in the form-realm or the desire-realm. Not with both [not obtaining] — setting aside these aspects. 'Whoever is endowed with the eye-element is also [endowed] with the form-element' — this is the first clause. First: whoever is endowed with the eye-element is also [endowed] with the form-element. One may [be endowed] with the form-element but not the eye-element — one who has not obtained the eye in the embryonic stages, and one who has obtained but lost the eye.

body.text: yaś cakṣurvijñānadhātunā asamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate rūpadhātunāpi saḥ. yo vā rūpadhātunāsamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate cakṣurvijñānadhātunāpi saḥ. tathaiva tayoḥ syāt
body.translated_text: Whoever, not endowed with the eye-consciousness-element, obtains endowment, is also [endowed] with the form-element. Or whoever, not endowed with the form-element, obtains endowment, is also [endowed] with the eye-consciousness-element. Likewise of those two, there may be

body.text: pṛthak tāvat. syāc cakṣurvijñānadhātunā na rūpadhātunā. dvitīyādidhyānopapannaś cakṣurvijñānaṃ saṃmukhīkurvāṇaḥ. syād rūpadhātunā na cakṣurvijñānadhātunā. [Tib. 68b] ārūpyadhātoś cyuto dvitīyādiṣu dhyāneṣūpapadyamānaḥ.
body.translated_text: First, separately: one may [obtain endowment] with the eye-consciousness-element but not with the form-element — one born in the second and higher <s>dhyānas</s> who is bringing eye-consciousness to confrontation. One may [obtain] with the form-element but not the eye-consciousness-element — [Tib. 68b] one who, having fallen from the formless realm, is being reborn in the second and higher <s>dhyānas</s>.

body.text: syād ubhavenāsamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamaṃ pratilabhate. ārūpyadhātucyutaḥ kāmadhātau brahmaloke copapadyamānaḥ. nobhayena. etān ākārān sthāpayitvā. yaś cakṣurvijñānadhātunā samanvāgato rūpadhātunāpi saḥ. yo vā rūpadhātunā cakṣurvijñānadhātunāpi saḥ. pūrvapādakaḥ. yas tāvac cakṣurvijñānadhātunā samanvāgato rūpadhātunāpi saḥ. syād rūpadhātunā na cakṣurvijñānadhātunāpi. dvitīyādidhyānopapannaś cakṣurvijñānam asaṃmukhīkurvāṇaḥ. yathā ceyaṃ cakṣurvijñānarūpadhātūnāṃ pratilambhasamanvāgamacintā. tathā śrotravijñānaśabdadhātvādīnām api pratilambhasamanvāgamacintā kartavyā. śrotravijñānadhātvoḥ syāt
body.translated_text: One not endowed with both may obtain endowment — one who, having fallen from the formless realm, is being reborn in the desire-realm or the <s>Brahmaloka</s>. Not with both — setting aside these aspects. 'Whoever is endowed with the eye-consciousness-element is also [endowed] with the form-element. Or whoever [is endowed] with the form-element is also [endowed] with the eye-consciousness-element.' This is the first clause. First: whoever is endowed with the eye-consciousness-element is also [endowed] with the form-element. One may [be endowed] with the form-element but not the eye-consciousness-element — one born in the second and higher <s>dhyānas</s> who is not bringing eye-consciousness to confrontation. And just as this deliberation about the obtaining and endowment of eye-consciousness and form-elements [is conducted], so too should the deliberation about the obtaining and endowment of ear-consciousness and sound-elements, etc., be conducted. 'Of the ear-consciousness element and the sound element, there may be

body.text: ādi.
body.translated_text: and so on.

body.text: iti. ubhayāvadhāraṇam. avadhāraṇād eva cānye rūpādayo bāhyā iti siddhaṃ. ātmany adhy adhyātmaṃ. adhy ātmānam iti vā adhyātmaṃ. adhyātmam eva ādhyātmikāḥ. adhyātme vā bhavāḥ ādhyātmikāḥ. ahaṃkārasaṃniśrayatvāc cittam ātmety upacaryata ity ahaṃkārasaṃniśraya ātmety ātmavādinaḥ saṃkalpayanti. cittaṃ cāhaṃkārasaṃniśraya ity ātmety upacaryate. katham ity āha.
body.translated_text: this is a restriction on both. Because of the restriction itself, it is established that the other [dhātus] — form, etc. — are external. '<s>Adhyatma</s>' means 'pertaining to the self' (adhy ātman). Or, '<s>adhy ātmānam</s>' (concerning the self) = <s>adhyātma</s>. Those that are <s>adhyātma</s> itself are <s>ādhyatmika</s>. Or, those that exist in the <s>adhyātma</s> are <s>ādhyatmika</s>. Because it is the locus of the notion of 'I,' the mind is figuratively called the 'self' — thus those who hold the doctrine of the self conceive: 'the locus of the notion of I is the self.' And the mind is the locus of the notion of I — hence it is figuratively called 'self.' How? He says:

children.text: ātmanā hi sudāntena svargaṃ prāpnoti paṇḍita
children.translated_text: 'For the wise one attains heaven by means of a well-trained self' —

body.text: ity uktaṃ gāthāyāṃ. kathaṃ punar gamyate cittam ātmaśabdenocyata iti. tata āha. cittasya cānyatra damanam uktaṃ bhagavateti. anyatra gāthāyām uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus it is said in a verse. But how is it understood that the word 'self' refers to the mind? Therefore he says: 'And the taming of the mind is stated by the Blessed One elsewhere.' Elsewhere, in a verse, it is stated:

body.text: Tib. 69a
body.translated_text: Tib. 69a

body.text:
cittasya damanaṃ sādhu cittaṃ dāntaṃ sukhāvaham
iti. tenāyam arthaḥ. ātmani cittīkārye ātmānaṃ vā cittam adhikṛtya ye dharmāḥ pratyāsannabhāvāt āśrayabhāvena vartante. te ādhyātmikāḥ. ye tu viṣayabhāvena vartante. te bāhyā iti. kaḥ punaḥ pratyāsannabhāvaḥ. yena vijñānaṃ tadvikāram anuvidhatte. cakṣurādiṣv eva hi vijñānaṃ lakṣyate na rūpādiṣv
body.translated_text:
'The taming of the mind is good; a tamed mind brings happiness.'
Thus this is the meaning: those <s>dharmas</s> that, with reference to the self — i.e., the mind — or concerning the self, i.e., the mind, function in the capacity of support due to proximity — those are 'internal' (<s>ādhyatmika</s>). But those that function in the capacity of object — those are 'external' (<s>bāhya</s>). What then is this 'proximity'? That by which consciousness conforms to the modifications of that [support]. For consciousness is observed [to operate] in the eye, etc. alone, not in form, etc.

body.text: iti. tathā hi cittam indriyasambaddhe śarīradeśe paricchidyate na viṣayadeśa iti. evaṃ tarhi ṣaḍ vijñānadhātava iti vistaraḥ. iha paṃca tāvad vijñānadhātavo vartamānā eva gṛhyante. indriyaviṣayasamānakālatvāt. vartanānaviṣayā hi paṃca vijñānakāyāḥ manovijñādhātur api vartamāna eveha vyavasthāpyate. yasmā manodhātur asyāśrayo 'nantarātīto vyavasthāpyate. kālabhedād eva hi manidhātumanovijñānadhātvoḥ pṛthagvyavasthānaṃ. tasmāt ta ādhyātmikā na prāpnuvanti. na hy ete manodhātutvam aprāptā atītatvam aprāptāś cittasyāśrayībhavanti. yadā tadā ta eva te bhavantīti lakṣaṇaṃ nātivartanta iti. kim anena vākyena sādhitaṃ. idam anena sādhitaṃ. vartamānānām apy eṣām āśrayabhāvo bhaviṣyatīti bhaviṣyadāśrayabhāvenādhyātmikatvaṃ bhavatīti. yadi vānāgatapratyutpannasyeti vistaraḥ. atīte 'dhvani yan manodhātulakṣaṇaṃ. tad anāgatapratyutpannayor apy adhvanor asty evety abhiprāyaḥ. na hi lakṣaṇasyādhvasu [Tib.69b] vyabhicāro 'sti. na hi svabhāvaparityāgo 'stīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: For thus, the mind is delimited to the bodily region connected with a sense-faculty, not to the region of the object. 'Then, the six consciousness-elements' — in detail. Here, the five consciousness-elements are first grasped as present only, because they are simultaneous with [their] sense-faculties and objects. For the five consciousness-groups have only present objects. The mental-consciousness element too is established here as present only. Because the mind-element, its support, is established as immediately past. For the separate establishment of the mind-element and the mental-consciousness element is precisely due to the difference in time-period. Therefore, they would not qualify as 'internal.' But [the reply is:] these, not having attained the status of mind-element, not having attained pastness, do not become the support of consciousness. When they do [become the support], then they become those very [mind-elements] — thus they do not transgress the defining characteristic. What has been established by this statement? This has been established: even for these present [consciousnesses], the capacity of being a support will exist — thus internality is established by virtue of their future support-capacity. Or, 'if of the future and present' — in detail. The characteristic of the mind-element in the past time-period — that exists also in the future and present time-periods — this is the intent. For there is no deviation of the characteristic across the time-periods. [Tib. 69b] The meaning is: there is no abandonment of intrinsic nature.

body.text: iti. dharmasaṃjñakaḥ sabhāga evety avadhāryate. yo hi viṣayo yasya vijñānasya niyata iti. tadyathā cakṣurvijñānasya rūpaṃ niyato viṣayo yāvan manovijñānasya dharmāḥ. yadi tatra tac cakṣurvijñānam utpannam utpattidharmi vā. yāvad yadi tatra manovijñanam utpannam utpattidharmi vā. sa viṣayaḥ sabhāga ity ucyate. tasya ca svabhāvasahabhūnirmuktā iti. svabhāvena sahabhūbhiś ca nirmuktāḥ svabhāvasahabhūnirmuktāḥ. sarvadharmās tasya vijñānasyālambanaṃ. na svabhāvaḥ. svātmani vṛttivirodhāt. na hi tad evāṃgulyagraṃ tenaivāṃgulyagreṇa spṛśyate. na saivāsidhārā tayaivāsidhārayā chidyate. na sahabhuvaḥ. saṃprayuktā viprayuktā vā. atisaṃnikṛṣṭatvāt. na hy akṣistham aṃjanaṃ tena gṛhyate. sa punaś cittakṣaṇo 'nyasya cittakṣaṇasya ālambanam iti. ye pūrvasmin kṣaṇe svabhāvasahabhuvo dharmā nālambitā abhūvan. te 'py ālambitā iti dvayoḥ kṣaṇayoḥ sarvadharmā ālaṃbanaṃ bhavanti. tasmād dharmadhātur nityaṃ sabhāgaḥ. dharmadhātur hi niyato manasa eva.
body.translated_text: it is restricted that the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> designated as <s>dharma</s> is <s>sabhāga</s> alone. For the object of a given consciousness is determined [as its sabhāga]. For example, form is the determined object of eye-consciousness, up to <s>dharmas</s> as [the determined object] of mental consciousness. If, with respect to that [object], that eye-consciousness has arisen or has the nature of arising — up to: if, with respect to that [object], mental consciousness has arisen or has the nature of arising — that object is called <s>sabhāga</s> (homogeneous). And 'excluding its own nature and co-existents' — those excluding its own nature and co-existents are 'svabhāvasahabhūnirmuktā.' All <s>dharmas</s> are the object of that consciousness — except its own nature, because of the impossibility of operating on itself. For the same fingertip is not touched by that very fingertip; the same sword-edge is not cut by that very sword-edge. Nor [are] its co-existents [its objects] — whether associated or dissociated — because of extreme proximity. For collyrium placed in the eye is not grasped by it. But that mind-moment is the object of another mind-moment. Those <s>dharmas</s> which in the preceding moment were co-existents of its own nature and were not objectified — they too become objectified — thus, [over] both moments, all <s>dharmas</s> become objects. Therefore, the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> is always <s>sabhāga</s>. For the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> is determined as [the object] of the mind alone.

body.text: caśabdena sabhāgāś ceti. śeṣā eva sabhāgatatsabhāgā ity avadhāryate. nanu ca dharmadhātur [Tib. 70a] eva sabhāga evety avadhāraṇe śeṣā na sabhāgā iti sabhāgatatsabhāgāḥ setsyanti. na setsyanti. yady api na sabhāgā eveti bhaveyuḥ.
body.translated_text: By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), [we understand] 'and they are <s>sabhāga</s> too.' It is restricted that the rest are precisely <s>sabhāga</s> and <s>tatsabhāga</s>. [Objection:] But since the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> [Tib. 70a] alone is restricted as <s>sabhāga</s> alone, the rest, not being <s>sabhāga</s>, would be established as <s>sabhāga</s>-and-<s>tatsabhāga</s>. [Reply:] They would not be established [that way]. Even though they might not be '<s>sabhāga</s> alone,'

body.text: tatsabhāgā eveti tu saṃbhaveyuḥ. tannivṛttyartham idam ārabhyate. sabhāgatatsabhāgā eva śeṣāḥ. na tu sabhāgā eva nāpi tatsabhāgā eveti.
body.translated_text: they might be '<s>tatsabhāga</s> alone.' To prevent that, this is undertaken: the rest are <s>sabhāga</s>-and-<s>tatsabhāga</s> alone — not <s>sabhāga</s> alone, nor <s>tatsabhāga</s> alone.
