children.translated_text: 'That which does not perform its own function' —

body.text: sa tatsabhāga iti saṃbandhanīyaṃ
body.translated_text: should be connected as: 'that is <s>tatsabhāga</s>'

body.text: anantaroktatvāt. uktaṃ bhavati. yaḥ svakarmakṛt sa sabhāga iti. asvakarmakṛd eva tatsabhāgas tatsabhāga eva vāsvakarmakṛd ity avadhāraṇe 'rthāpattyā svakarmakṛt sabhāga iti. rūpāṇy apaśyad iti. adrākṣīd iti vaktavyaṃ. evaṃ hy adyatanātītaṃ hyastanātītaṃ ca parigṛhītaṃ bhavati. anyathā hy avyāpi lakṣaṇaṃ syāt. athaivam eva pāṭha udāharaṇamātraṃ tad draṣṭavyāṃ. adyatanātītam api vaktavyaṃ. evaṃ yāvan manaḥ svena viṣayakāritreṇa vaktavyam iti. svena viṣayapuruṣakāreṇa vaktavyaṃ. katham iti. yena śrotreṇa śabdān aśṛṇot śṛṇoti śroṣyati vā. tad ucyate sabhāgaṃ śrotram iti sarvaṃ. vijñānasamāyuktam asamāyuktaṃ ceti vijñānasambaddham asambaddhaṃ cety arthaḥ. yad ekasya cakṣuḥ sabhāgaṃ tad [Tib. 70b] sarveṣāṃ kiṃ. sabhāgam iti vartate evaṃ tadsabhāgam apīti. yad ekasya cakṣus tadsabhāgaṃ. tat sarveṣāṃ tatsabhāgam ity arthaḥ. prāptagrahaṇād iti. gandhādayaḥ. ye evadattena ghrāṇādīndriyaprāptā gṛhyante. na te yajñadattena gṛhyante. svaghrāṇādikapraviṣṭatvāt. ity asādhāraṇatvād eṣāṃ cakṣurādivad atideśo nyāyyaḥ. ya ekasya gandhaḥ sabhāgaḥ. sa sarveṣām. evaṃ tatsabhāgo 'pīti vaktavyaṃ. na tu vaktavyaṃ yathā rūpam evaṃ gandhādaya iti. asti hy eṣa saṃbhavo ya eva gandhādaya ekasya ghrāṇādivijñānam utpādayeyuḥ. ta evānyeṣām apīti. yadi te evadattaghrāṇādīndriyaprāptā bhaveyur evadattasya vijñānam utpādayeyuḥ. atha yajñadattaghrāṇādīndriyaprāptā yajñadattasya vijñānam utpādayeyur ity arthaḥ. atha vā ta evānyeṣām apīti. tatrāntargatasūkṣmakrimiprabhṛtīnām api vijñānam utpādayeyuḥ. na tasyaiva evadattasya yasya ghrāṇādīndriyaprāptās te gandhādaya iti. indriyaviṣayavijñānānām anyonyabhajanam iti. āśrayaviṣayāśrayibhāvenānyonyābhimukhyena pravṛttiḥ. tathā hīndriyadhātavo vijñānadhātūn āśrayabhāvena yathāyogaṃ bhajante. sevanta ity arthaḥ. viṣayadhātūṃś ca viṣayibhāvena. tathā viṣayadhātavaḥ svendriyadhātūn viṣayabhāvena bhajante. vijñānadhātūṃs tu viṣayabhāvena ālambanabhāvena vā bhajante. tathā [Tib. 71a] vijñānadhātavaḥ svendriyadhātūnām āśrayibhāvena bhajante. viṣayadhātūṃś ca viṣayibhāvenālambakabhāvena vā bhajanta. ity anyonyabhajanaṃ bhāgaḥ. bhāve ghañ. kāritrabhajanaṃ vā bhāgaḥ. kāritraṃ
body.translated_text: because it was stated immediately [before]. It has been stated: 'That which performs its own function is <s>sabhāga</s> (homogeneous).' That which does not perform its own function is <s>tatsabhāga</s> (similar to the homogeneous); or, that which is only <s>tatsabhāga</s> does not perform its own function — through restriction, [the converse is established] by implication: [that which] performs its own function is <s>sabhāga</s>. 'Was seeing forms' — one should say <s>adrākṣīt</s> ('has seen'). For in this way, both today's past and yesterday's past are included. Otherwise, the definition would be non-pervasive. Or, if the reading is precisely thus, it should be understood as merely an illustration — and the today's-past should also be stated. Likewise, up to: the mind (<s>manas</s>) should be stated with its own object-function. 'With its own object-function' means with its own active exertion toward the object. How? 'Whatever ear with which one heard sounds, hears, or will hear — that is called the homogeneous ear' — and so on for all. 'Conjoined or not conjoined with consciousness' means connected or not connected with consciousness — this is the meaning. 'Is what is <s>sabhāga</s> for one person [Tib. 70b] also [sabhāga] for all?' — [the answer] continues: 'Similarly with <s>tatsabhāga</s> too.' The meaning is: whatever eye of one [person] is <s>tatsabhāga</s>, that is <s>tatsabhāga</s> for all. 'Because of [the argument from] proximate grasping' — smells and the like. Those smells that are grasped by <s>Devadatta</s> through having reached his nose-faculty and the rest — those are not grasped by <s>Yajñadatta</s>, because [the objects] have entered [Devadatta's] own nose, etc. Therefore, because of their being non-shared, the extension [of the <s>sabhāga</s>/<s>tatsabhāga</s> distinction] to them is justified, just as for the eye and the rest. Whatever smell is <s>sabhāga</s> for one person — that is [sabhāga] for all. Similarly, <s>tatsabhāga</s> should also be stated. But one should not say 'just as with form, so too with smells and the rest.' For this possibility exists: the very smells and the rest that would produce nose-consciousness and the rest for one person [could produce them] for others too — if they were to reach <s>Devadatta</s>'s nose-faculty and the rest, they would produce <s>Devadatta</s>'s consciousness; and if they were to reach <s>Yajñadatta</s>'s nose-faculty and the rest, they would produce <s>Yajñadatta</s>'s consciousness — this is the meaning. Or, 'for others too' means they would produce consciousness even for subtle worms and such that are inside [the body] — not [only] for that very <s>Devadatta</s> whose nose-faculty and the rest those smells and the rest have reached. 'The mutual sharing of sense-faculties, objects, and consciousnesses' — [means] functioning in mutual orientation as basis, object, and basis-dependent. For the sense-faculty elements share the consciousness elements as their basis — they serve them, is the meaning — and the object elements as that which has objects [i.e., that to which objects pertain]. Similarly, the object elements share their own sense-faculty elements as objects, and share the consciousness elements as objects, or as the condition of support. Similarly, [Tib. 71a] the consciousness elements share their own sense-faculty elements as that which is the basis-dependent, and share the object elements as that which pertains to objects, or as that which provides support. Thus, mutual sharing is <s>bhāga</s> ('portion,' 'sharing'). The <s>ghañ</s> suffix is in the sense of 'state.' Or, <s>bhāga</s> is the sharing of function. The function

body.text: cakṣurādīnāṃ darśanādi. vijñānadhātūnāṃ vijñātṛtvaṃ. viṣayadhātūnāṃ tadviṣayālambanabhāvaḥ. tasya kāritrasya bhajanaṃ kāritrabhajanaṃ. sa eṣām astīty arthaḥ. pradarśanamātram etat. vigrahas tv evaṃ kartavyaḥ. saha bhāgena vartante sabhāgā iti. samāno vā bhāga eṣāṃ eṣāṃ ta ime sabhāgāḥ. samānārthasya sahaśabdasya sabhāva ādiṣṭaḥ. sparśasamānakāryatvād vā. kiṃ. sabhāgā iti prakṛtam. atra karmaṇi ghañ. bhajyata iti bhāgaḥ. vigrahas tu pūrvavat. sparśaś caitasikaḥ. eṣām indriyaviṣayavijñānānāṃ samānaṃ kāryaṃ. cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpāṇi ca utpadyate cakṣurvijñānaṃ. trayāṇāṃ saṃnipātaḥ sparśa ityādivacanāt. ye punar asabhāgā iti vistaraḥ. ye punar anye cakṣurādaya ittham asabhāgāḥ. teṣāṃ sabhāgānām uktalakṣaṇānāṃ sabhāgāḥ sadṛśāḥ. te tatsabhāgāḥ. teṣāṃ tair vā sabhāgās te tatsabhāgāḥ. tulyārthe hy atra sabhāgaśabdo gṛhyate.
body.translated_text: of the eye and the rest is seeing and so forth; of the consciousness elements, the state of being cognizers; of the object elements, the state of being their objects or supports. The sharing of that function is 'function-sharing' — the meaning is: 'they have that.' This is merely an illustration. But the analysis should be made thus: 'They exist together with a share — [hence they are] <s>sabhāga</s> (homogeneous).' Or, their share is equal — those are <s>sabhāga</s>. The word <s>saha</s> in the sense of 'equal' is prescribed [to become] <s>sa</s>-. Or, because they have the same effect as contact (<s>sparśa</s>). What? '<s>Sabhāga</s>' is the topic under discussion. Here the <s>ghañ</s> suffix is in the objective sense (<s>karmaṇi</s>). 'That which is shared is <s>bhāga</s>.' The analysis is as before. Contact is a mental factor. These — sense-faculties, objects, and consciousnesses — have a common effect: 'Dependent on the eye and forms, visual consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact' — because of such statements. 'But those which are <s>asabhāga</s> (non-homogeneous)' — this is the elaboration. But those other [instances of] the eye and the rest that are <s>asabhāga</s> in this way — [they are] similar to those <s>sabhāga</s> [ones] whose characteristics have been stated. They are <s>tatsabhāga</s>. 'Similar to those' or 'similar through those' — they are <s>tatsabhāga</s>. For the word <s>sabhāga</s> is here taken in the sense of 'equal.'

body.text: (I.39) darśanaheyā iti. darśanaṃ prathamataḥ satyadarśanam anāsravaṃ paṃcadaśacittakṣaṇasaṃgṛhītaṃ. bhāvanā tad eva punaḥpunardarśanaṃ. laukikaṃ vā samāhitaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvanā.
body.translated_text: (I.39) 'To be abandoned by insight (<s>darśana</s>)' — <s>darśana</s> means the first seeing of the truths, the non-outflow [wisdom] comprising fifteen mind-moments. <s>Bhāvanā</s> (cultivation) is the repeated seeing of that same [truth]. Or, mundane concentrated knowledge is <s>bhāvanā</s>.

children.translated_text: 'Ten are to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), and five [more]' —

body.text: rūpiṇo dhātavo daśa paṃca ca tadvijñānadhātava iti. [Tib. 71b] kathaṃ punar etad gamyate. eta eva ta iti.
body.translated_text: the ten material elements and the five corresponding consciousness elements. [Tib. 71b] But how is this understood? 'These very ones are those' —

body.text: vacanāt. antyatrayāt anye paṃcadaśa dhātava eva ta ucyanta iti. te bhāvanāheyā evety avadhāryante. triprakārā iti. darśanaheyā bhāvanāheyā aheyāś cety arthaḥ. eta eva tridhā aṣṭāśītyanuśayās tatsahabhuva iti. dhātuprakārākārabhinnāḥ satkāyadṛṣṭyādayo 'nuśayās tatsahabhuvo vijñānavedanādayaḥ saṃprayuktāḥ asaṃprayuktāni ca tallakṣaṇānulakṣaṇāni. tatprāptayaś ca sānucarā iti. tacchabdena anuśayādayaḥ saṃbadhyante. teṣām anuśayānāṃ tatsahabhuvāṃ ca prāptayas tatprāptayaḥ. yady apy anuśayasahabhuvo bhavanti. na tu sarvāḥ. kāścid dhi prāptayo 'nuśayādisahabhuvo bhavanti yāḥ sahajāḥ. kāścit tu pūrvaṃ paścāc ca tebhyo bhavanty ataḥ pṛthak prāptigrahaṇaṃ. sānucarā iti grahaṇena anuprāptayas tallakṣaṇāni ca saṃgṛhyante. śeṣāḥ sāsravā bhāvanāheyā iti. eta eva trayo 'ntyā dhātavo ye śeṣā darśanaheyebhyo 'nye sāsravāḥ. te bhāvanāheyāḥ. ke punas te. daśānuśayās tatsahabhuvas tatprāptayaś ca sānucarāḥ. kuśalasāsravāḥ. anivṛtāvyākṛtāś ca saṃskārāḥ. avijñaptirūpaṃ ca sāsravaṃ sānucaraṃ. [Tib. 72a] anāsravā aheyā iti mārgasatyāsaṃskṛtasvabhāvāḥ. nanu cānyad apīti vistaraḥ. pṛthagjanatvam anivṛtāvyākṛtasaṃskārasvabhāvatvād bhāvanāheyamadhyagatam. apāyasaṃvartanīyaṃ ca
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Other than the last three, the fifteen elements are called 'those' — and they are determined as 'to be abandoned by cultivation only.' 'Threefold' — meaning to be abandoned by insight, to be abandoned by cultivation, and not to be abandoned. 'These very [last three] are threefold — the eighty-eight <s>anuśayas</s> (dormant tendencies) and their co-existents.' The <s>anuśayas</s> beginning with the view of a self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), distinguished by element, type, and aspect; their co-existents — consciousness, feeling, and the rest that are associated [with them]; and the dissociated [dharmas] that are their characteristics and sub-characteristics; and the acquisitions of those — 'together with their retinue.' By the word 'that' (<s>tad</s>), the <s>anuśayas</s> and the rest are connected. The acquisitions of those <s>anuśayas</s> and their co-existents are 'their acquisitions.' Although there are co-existents of the <s>anuśayas</s>, not all [acquisitions are co-existents] — for some acquisitions are co-existents of the <s>anuśayas</s> and the rest, being co-arisen; but some arise before or after them — hence the separate mention of 'acquisitions.' By the phrase 'together with their retinue,' sub-acquisitions and their characteristics are included. 'The remaining <s>sāsrava</s> [dharmas] are to be abandoned by cultivation' — the very same three last elements that are other than those to be abandoned by insight and are <s>sāsrava</s> — they are to be abandoned by cultivation. What are those? The ten <s>anuśayas</s>, their co-existents, and their acquisitions together with their retinue; wholesome <s>sāsrava</s> [dharmas]; and unobstructed indeterminate formations; and <s>sāsrava avijñapti</s>-form together with its retinue. [Tib. 72a] 'Non-outflow [dharmas] are not to be abandoned' — those having the nature of the truth of the path and the unconditioned. [Objection:] 'But isn't there also [something else]?' — this is the elaboration. The state of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjanaatva</s>), being of the nature of an unobstructed indeterminate formation, falls within [the category of dharmas] to be abandoned by cultivation. And <s>karma</s> of body and speech leading to the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>), being of the nature of form, is also said to be abandoned by cultivation. For this reason the <s>Vātsīputrīyas</s> raise an objection: Because of being opposed to the Noble Path — the state of ordinary personhood does not exist when the Noble Path arises. And when <s>karma</s> destined for the lower realms exists, the Noble Path does not arise. And when the Noble Path arises, <s>karma</s> destined for the lower realms does not arise. Therefore, like the view of a self-existing body and the rest, both of those are to be abandoned by insight — so they argue. To refute this, [the topic] was stated briefly. But for the purpose of easy understanding, it is stated again:

body.text: kāyavākkarma rūpasvabhāvatvād bhāvanāheyam uktam. ity ataś codayanti vātsīputrīyāḥ. āryamārgavirodhitvād iti. pṛthagjanatvam āryamārgotpāde na bhavati. niyate cāpāyike karmaṇi sati āryamārgo notpadyate. āryamārgotpāde ca saty āpāyikaṃ karma notpadyate. tasmāt satkāyadṛṣṭyādivat tad ubhayaṃ darśanaheyam iti varṇayanti. tatpratiṣedhārtham uktam apy etad abhisaṃkṣepeṇa. sukhapratipattyarthaṃ punar ucyate.
body.translated_text: [empty]

children.text: na dṛṣṭiheyam akliṣṭaṃ na rūpaṃ nāpy aṣaṣṭhajaṃ.
children.translated_text: 'What is undefiled is not to be abandoned by insight; nor is form; nor what is born of the sixth [i.e., the five sense-consciousnesses].'

body.text: dṛṣṭir darśanam. akliṣṭam anivṛtavyākṛtaṃ kuśalaṃ vā na darśanaheyaṃ. rūpaṃ tu kliṣṭam api na darśanaheyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Insight' (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) means seeing [the truths] (<s>darśana</s>). What is undefiled — unobstructed indeterminate or wholesome — is not to be abandoned by insight. And form (<s>rūpa</s>), even if defiled, is not to be abandoned by insight.

children.translated_text: 'Born of the [first five, not the] sixth' —

body.text: paṃcendriyajaṃ paṃcavijñānaṃ tad arūpaṃ kliṣṭam api san na darśanaheyaṃ. ato 'nyat tu darśanaheyaṃ saṃbhavati yathoktam. akliṣṭāvyākṛtaṃ ca pṛthagjanatvaṃ samucchinnakuśalamūlavītarāgāṇām api tatsamanvāgamād iti. samucchinnakuśalamūlāḥ kuśalair dharmair asamanvāgatā iṣṭāḥ. pṛthagjanatvena tu samanvāgatāḥ. [Tib. 72b] yasmāt te pṛthagjanā iṣyante. tasmān na kuśalaṃ pṛthagjanatvaṃ. kliṣṭam api tan na bhavati. vītarāgānām api tena samanvāgamāt. kliṣṭasya hi vastunaḥ svabhāvaprahāṇam iṣyate. prāptichedaḥ prahāṇam ity arthaḥ. tad yadi pṛthagjanatvaṃ kliṣṭaṃ syāt laukikavītarāgāṇāṃ tasya prāpticheda iti tenasamanvāgamaḥ syāt. iṣyate ca teṣāṃ tena samanvāgamaḥ. tathā hi te laukikavītarāgāḥ pṛthagjanā eveṣyante. akliṣṭavyākṛtatvaikatve 'doṣaḥ. chandarāgaprahāṇaṃ akliṣṭasyeṣyate. tadālambanakleśaprāpticheda ity arthaḥ. na tu tadātmīyaprāpticheda iṣyate. tathā hy uktaṃ bhagavatā yo bhikṣavo rūpe chandarāgaḥ. taṃ prajahīta. evaṃ vas tad rūpaṃ prahīṇaṃ bhavatīti vistaraḥ. tasmād akliṣṭāvyākṛtaṃ pṛthagjanatvaṃ teṣāṃ prahīṇam api cakṣurādivat samudācarati. atas tena samanvāgamo bhavati. kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ. akliṣṭavyākṛtatvāt pṛthagjanatvaṃ na darśanaprahātavyaṃ. rūpatvāc ca kāyavākkarma ity āha. satyeṣv avipratipatteḥ. akleśaduṣṭatvāt pṛthagjanatvaṃ na duḥkhādiṣu satyeṣu vipratipadyate. na viparītarūpeṇa pravartata ity arthaḥ. anālambakatvāc ca. kāyavākkarmāpy anālambakatvād eva na vipratipadyate. tasmāt tad ubhayaṃ na darśanaheyaṃ. ayaṃ ca satyeṣv avipratipatter [Tib. 73a] iti hetur aṣaṣṭhaje 'py anuvartayitavyaḥ. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntau pṛthagjanatvaprasaṃgāc ceti. ayam upacayahetuḥ pṛthagjanatvasyaiva darśanaheyatvanivṛttyartham ucyate kāyavākkarmaṇo 'nabhisaṃbandhāt. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntau pṛthagjanatvaprāptiś chidyate
body.translated_text: [i.e.,] the five consciousnesses born of the five sense-faculties — those, being non-form, even though defiled, are not to be abandoned by insight. What is other than these, however, can be to be abandoned by insight, as has been stated. 'And the state of ordinary personhood, being undefiled indeterminate, [is not to be abandoned by insight] because even those who have cut off wholesome roots and those free from desire are endowed with it.' Those who have cut off wholesome roots are accepted as not endowed with wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, yet they are endowed with the state of ordinary personhood. [Tib. 72b] Since they are accepted as ordinary persons, therefore the state of ordinary personhood is not wholesome. Nor is it defiled — because even those free from desire are endowed with it. For it is accepted that the natural abandonment of a defiled entity [occurs] — 'the cutting off of acquisition is abandonment,' is the meaning. If the state of ordinary personhood were defiled, for those who have attained worldly freedom from desire, there would be a cutting off of its acquisition and thus non-endowment with it. But endowment with it is accepted for them. For indeed, those worldly beings free from desire are accepted as ordinary persons. 'There is no fault in the [state's] being one with the undefiled indeterminate.' The abandonment of desire-and-attachment for the undefiled is accepted [as follows]: the cutting off of the acquisition of the affliction that has it as object — this is the meaning. But the cutting off of the acquisition belonging to itself is not accepted. For thus the Blessed One said: 'Whatever desire-and-attachment there is toward form, O monks — abandon that. Thus form will be abandoned for you' — and so on in detail. Therefore, the state of ordinary personhood, being undefiled indeterminate, continues to operate for those [Arhats], even though abandoned, like the eye and the rest. Hence there is endowment with it. What then is the reason? Because of being undefiled indeterminate, the state of ordinary personhood is not to be abandoned by insight; and because of being form, bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> [is not] — he says: 'Because of non-confusion regarding the truths.' Being not corrupted by afflictions, the state of ordinary personhood is not confused regarding the truths of suffering and the rest — meaning it does not function in a distorted manner. And because of being non-objective. Bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> too, precisely because of being non-objective, is not confused [regarding the truths]. Therefore, both of those are not to be abandoned by insight. And this reason — 'because of non-confusion regarding the truths' — [Tib. 73a] should also be applied to [what is] born of the [first five, not the] sixth. '[Objection:] And because in the [moment of] insight-tolerance (<s>kṣānti</s>) regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering, the state of ordinary personhood would follow.' This additional reason is stated only for the purpose of precluding the state of ordinary personhood from being abandoned by insight — not in connection with bodily and vocal <s>karma</s>. In the [moment of] insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering, the acquisition of the state of ordinary personhood is cut off

body.text: . na tu chinnā tatpraheyakleśaprāptivat.
body.translated_text: . But it is not 'cut off' [in the manner that] the acquisition of the afflictions to be abandoned by that [insight is cut off].

children.translated_text: 'But the path, as it ceases, abandons the obstruction of that' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. duḥkhe dharmajñāne tu tatprāptiś chinnā. tena tatprāptisadbhāvāt duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntyavasthāyāṃ sa pudgalaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ syāt. na cāsau tasyām avasthāyāṃ pṛthagjana iti śakyate vyavasthāpayitum adhigatāryamārgatvāt. tathā hi pṛthagjanatvaṃ katamad. āryadharmāṇām alābha iti pṛthagjanatvalakṣaṇaṃ. sa cāryadharmāṇāṃ lābhenālābho vyāvartate. tasmād ārya evāsāv iti. idaṃ tāvat bhavanto vaibhāṣikāḥ praṣṭavyāḥ. tat pṛthgjanatvaṃ kiṃ bhāvanāmārgapratilambhād eva prahīyate. nety ucyate. tat pṛthagjanatvaṃ navabhaumikaṃ kāmāvacaraṃ yāvat bhāvāgrikaṃ. tac cākliṣṭaṃ. tena pratibhūmibhūminavamakleśaprakāraprahāṇāvasthāyāṃ prahīyate. sarvaṃ hy akliṣṭaṃ sāsravaṃ navama eva vimuktimārge prahīyate. yady evam avītarāgāvasthāyām āryaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ syāt. na. pṛthagjanatvasya vihīnatvāt. [Tib. 73b] duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣānteḥ prabhṛti hi tad vihīnam eva. na tu prahīṇaṃ. kaḥ punar vihānaprahāṇayor viśeṣa iti. vihānaṃ prāptichede vyavasthāpitaṃ. prahāṇaṃ tu pratipakṣalābhe vyavasthāpitaṃ. tasmāt prāptichedāt tena pṛthagjanatvenāsamanvāgamāt tasyām avasthāyām ārya eva bhavati. na pṛthagjana ity adoṣa eṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. But in the [moment of the] <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering, its acquisition is [truly] cut off. Therefore, because of the existence of the acquisition of that [state] at the stage of the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering, that person would be an ordinary person. But one cannot establish that person as an ordinary person at that stage, because the Noble Path has been attained. For thus: 'What is the state of ordinary personhood? The non-attainment of Noble <s>dharmas</s>' — this is the definition of ordinary personhood. And that non-attainment is reversed by the attainment of Noble <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore, that [person] is indeed a Noble One. Now, the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> should be asked this: Is the state of ordinary personhood abandoned only upon the attainment of the cultivation-path (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>)? No, it is said. That state of ordinary personhood has nine levels — from the desire-realm up to the peak of existence. And it is undefiled. Therefore, it is abandoned at the stage of abandoning the ninth type of affliction on each level successively. For all undefiled <s>sāsrava</s> [dharmas] are abandoned only at the ninth liberation-path. If so, at the stage of not being free from desire, the Noble One would be an ordinary person. No — because the state of ordinary personhood is 'diminished.' [Tib. 73b] From the [moment of] insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering onward, it is diminished, but not abandoned. What then is the difference between 'diminished' and 'abandoned'? 'Diminished' is established [as the point] where the acquisition is cut off. 'Abandoned' is established [as the point] where the antidote is attained. Therefore, because of the cutting off of the acquisition, and because of non-endowment with the state of ordinary personhood, at that stage [the person] is indeed a Noble One, not an ordinary person — hence there is no fault.

children.text: cakṣuś ca dharmadhātoś ca pradeśo dṛṣṭir
children.translated_text: 'The eye and a portion of the <s>dharma</s>-element — [these are] view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>)' —

body.text: iti. cakṣur eva dharmadhātupradeśa eva dṛṣṭir ity avadhāryate. satkāyadṛṣṭyādiketi. satkāyadṛṣṭir antagrāhadṛṣṭir mithyādṛṣṭir dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśaś ceti. śaikṣasyānāsraveti prajñety adhikṛtaṃ. aśaikṣasyāśaikṣīti. aśaikṣasyānāsravā prajñā aśaikṣī. kṣayānutpādajñānavarjyeti vaktavyaṃ. vakṣyati hi
body.translated_text: It is restrictively determined that the eye alone and a portion of the <s>dharma</s>-element alone are view. 'The view of a self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and so forth' — the view of a self-existing body, the view of grasping at extremes (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), adherence to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>), and adherence to rules and vows (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>). 'Of the trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>), the uncontaminated wisdom' — this has been discussed. 'Of the adept (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), the adept's [wisdom]' — the uncontaminated wisdom of the adept is the adept's [wisdom]. It should be stated: 'excluding the knowledge of destruction and of non-arising.' For it will be stated:

children.translated_text: 'The knowledge of destruction and non-arising is not view' —

body.text: iti. sameghāmegheti vistareṇa yāvat kliṣṭākliṣṭalaukikīśaikṣyaśaikṣībhir dṛṣṭibhir dharmadarśanam iti. loke bhavā laukikī. kliṣṭā cāklṣṭā ca kliṣṭākliṣṭe. kliṣṭākliṣṭe cāsau laukikī ca. kliṣṭākliṣṭalaukikī. kliṣṭākliṣṭalaukikī ca śaikṣī cāśaikṣī ca kliṣṭākliṣṭalaukikīśaikṣyaśaikṣyaḥ. tābhir dharmadarśanaṃ. kīdṛśam ity āha. sameghāmegharātriṃdivarūpadarśanavad iti. yathā [Tib. 74a] sameghāyāṃ rātrau rūpadarśanaṃ. evaṃ kliṣṭayā laukikyā satkāyadṛṣṭyādikayā dṛṣṭyā dharmadarśanaṃ. avyaktataram ity arthaḥ. yathā tasyām eva rātrau ameghāyāṃ rūpadarśanaṃ. evam akliṣṭayā laukikyā dṛṣṭyā dharmadarśanaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Like [seeing during] cloudy and clear [weather]' — and so on in detail, up to: '<s>dharma</s>-seeing through afflicted, non-afflicted, worldly, trainee, and adept views.' 'Worldly' means 'belonging to the world.' Both afflicted and non-afflicted are the afflicted-and-non-afflicted [pair]. It is afflicted-and-non-afflicted, and it is also worldly — hence 'afflicted-and-non-afflicted-worldly.' [These] together with trainee and adept [are] the afflicted-and-non-afflicted-worldly-trainee-and-adept [views]. By those, <s>dharma</s>-seeing [occurs]. 'Of what kind?' he says: 'Like seeing forms on cloudy and clear nights and days.' Just as seeing forms on a cloudy night — so is <s>dharma</s>-seeing through the afflicted, worldly view of the body and so forth — meaning very indistinct. Just as seeing forms on a cloudless night — so is <s>dharma</s>-seeing through non-afflicted, worldly view.

body.text: avyaktam ity arthaḥ. yathā sameghe divase rūpadarśanaṃ. evaṃ śaikṣyā dṛṣtyā dharmadarśanaṃ. vyaktaṃ na tv atyarthaṃ. yathā punar ameghe divase rūpadarśanaṃ. evam aśaikṣyā dṛṣṭyā dharmadarṣanam. atyarthaṃ vyaktam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: Meaning indistinct. Just as seeing forms on a cloudy day — so is <s>dharma</s>-seeing through the trainee's view — distinct but not exceedingly so. Just as seeing forms on a cloudless day — so is <s>dharma</s>-seeing through the adept's view — meaning exceedingly distinct.

body.text: iti asaṃtīraṇāt. saṃtīraṇaṃ punar viṣayopanidhyānapūrvakaṃ niścayākarṣaṇaṃ. ata eva cānyāpīti vistaraḥ. ata evāsaṃtīraṇād anyāpi mānasī kliṣṭā rāgādisaṃprayuktā akliṣṭā vā kṣayānutpādajñānānivṛtāvyākṛtā prajñā na dṛṣṭiḥ. rūpālocanārtheneti. cakṣur na saṃtīrakatvena dṛṣṭiḥ. kiṃ tarhi. rūpālocanārthena. prajñā tu saṃtīrakatveneti darśitaṃ bhavati. anyavijñānasamaṃgina iti. anyavijñānasaṃmukhīhāvinaḥ pudgalasyānyavijñānavyāsaktasyety arthaḥ. paśyec cakṣurindriyaṃ viṣayādisāṃnidhyāt. yasya tu cakṣurvijñānaṃ paśyatīti pakṣaḥ. tasya tadvijñānāsaṃbhavād adoṣaḥ. tad eva cakṣurāśritaṃ vijñānaṃ paśyatīty astv iti. darśanasya tadbhāve bhāvāt tadabhāve cābhāvāt.
body.translated_text: means because of non-investigation (<s>asaṃtīraṇa</s>). And investigation is the drawing of a definitive conclusion preceded by close attention to the object. 'For this very reason, other [wisdoms] also' — and so forth in detail. For this very reason — because of non-investigation — other mental wisdoms too, whether afflicted (associated with attachment and so forth) or non-afflicted (non-specified, not covered by the knowledge of destruction and non-arising), are not view. 'For the purpose of seeing form (<s>rūpālocana</s>)' — the eye is not view in the sense of being an investigator; rather, for the purpose of seeing [i.e., encountering] form. But wisdom [is view] in the sense of being an investigator — this has been shown. 'Of one possessing another consciousness' — of a person facing another consciousness, meaning a person engaged with another consciousness. 'The eye-faculty would see, because of the proximity of the object and so forth.' But for one whose position is that visual consciousness sees — because of the impossibility of that consciousness [in this case], there is no fault. 'It is the consciousness based on the eye alone that sees' — let it be so. Because seeing exists when that [consciousness] exists, and does not exist when it does not exist.

children.translated_text: 'It is said that a concealed form is not seen, because...' —

body.text: Tib. 74b
body.translated_text: The particle <s>kila</s> ('it is said') indicates the opponent's view. 'Because of its [consciousness's]

body.text: iti kilaśabdaḥ paramatau. tasyāpratighatvād iti. vijñānam amūrtiṃ kuḍyādīny atikramyāpi paśyet. vijñānavādy āha. naiva hy āvṛte cakṣurvijñānam utpadyate ity anābhāsagatatvāt viṣayasyety abhiprāyaḥ. kiṃ khalu notpadyata ity apratighatvāt kuḍyādīni vyatibhidya kuḍyādyavyavahita iva viṣaye vijñānam utpatsyata iti bhāvaḥ. yasya tv iti. yasya mama vaibhāṣikasya pakṣaḥ cakṣuḥ paśyatīti. tasya mama cakṣuṣaḥ sapratighatvāt vyavahite kuḍyādibhir vṛttyabhāvaḥ. tasya cakṣuṣa ālocanavṛttyabhāvaḥ. vijñānaṃ tarhi vaibhāṣikasya vyavahite 'pi prāpnotīti codyam antarnītam āśaṃkya sa eva vaibhāṣikaḥ punar āha. vijñānasyāpy anutpattir iti. yathaiva cakṣuṣo vyavahite vṛttyabhāvo yujyate vijñānasyāpy anutpattir vijñānavṛttyabhāva āśrayeṇa sahaikaviṣayapravṛttatvāt yujyate. ya eva hi cakṣuṣo vyavahito 'rtho viṣayaḥ syāt. sa eva vijñānasyeti yuktā vijñānasyāpy anutpattiḥ. tava tu vijñānavādino 'pratighatvād vijñānasya vyavahite vijñānam utpadyeta. na tūtpadyate. tasmāc cakṣuḥ paśyati na vijñānam iti siddhaṃ. evaṃ vijñānavādini pratiṣiddhe tatpakṣam ācāryo gṛhītvāha. kiṃ nu vai cakṣuḥ prāptaviṣayam iti vistaraḥ. yathā kāyendriyaṃ prāptaviṣayaṃ kuḍyādivyavahitaṃ [Tib. 75a] viṣayaṃ na gṛhṇāti. kuḍyādipratighātāt. tataḥ pareṇa pravartitum alahamānatvāt. kim evaṃ cakṣuḥ prāptaviṣayaṃ kuḍyādipratighātena pratihataṃ sat tataḥ pareṇa gantum alabhamānaṃ
body.translated_text: non-resistance' — consciousness, being immaterial, would see even beyond walls and so forth. The proponent of consciousness says: 'Visual consciousness does not arise when [the object is] concealed' — meaning because the object has not come into the range of illumination. [The opponent asks:] 'Why indeed does it not arise? Because of non-resistance, it should arise with respect to an object unobstructed by walls and so forth, as if penetrating the walls.' [The response of] one whose position is 'the eye sees' — of me, the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>: because the eye has resistance (<s>sapratigha</s>), when obstructed by walls and so forth, there is no operation — no seeing-operation of the eye. [The objection:] 'But consciousness would then reach even what is obstructed, for the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>' — anticipating this internal objection, that same <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says again: 'There is also non-arising of consciousness' — just as the non-operation of the eye when obstructed is fitting, the non-arising of consciousness — the non-operation of consciousness — is also fitting, because consciousness operates on the same object together with its base. For whatever object would be beyond the reach of the eye — that same [object] is beyond consciousness too. Therefore the non-arising of consciousness too is fitting. But for you, the proponent of consciousness, because consciousness is non-resistant, consciousness should arise regarding an obstructed [object] — yet it does not arise. Therefore, 'the eye sees, not consciousness' — this is established. Having thus refuted the proponent of consciousness, the <s>Ācārya</s> [Vasubandhu], taking up that [opponent's] position, says: 'Does the eye indeed perceive a contacted object?' — and so forth in detail. Just as the body-faculty, which perceives a contacted object, does not apprehend an object obstructed by walls and so forth — because of being blocked by walls and so forth, because of being unable to proceed beyond them — does the eye likewise, as one that perceives a contacted object, being blocked by walls and so forth, being unable to go beyond them,

body.text:
taṃ kuḍyādivyavahitaṃ viṣayaṃ na gṛhṇātīti. naitad yujyate. tasmāt sapratighatvāt āvṛtaṃ cakṣur na paśyed iti na vaktavyaṃ. kācābhrapaṭalasphaṭikāṃbubhiś cāntaritaṃ kathaṃ dṛśyata iti. kācenābhrapaṭalena sphaṭikenāmbunā cāntaritaṃ vyavahitaṃ rūpaṃ kathaṃ dṛśyate. sapratighatvād dhi kuḍyādivyavahitavat kācādivyavahitaṃ cakṣur na paśyet tac ca paśyatīti siddhāntaḥ. yatrālokasyāpratibandha iti. āloke hi sati viṣaya ābhāsagato bhavatīti vijñānotpattisaṃbhavaḥ. evaṃ hi vijñānakāraṇaṃ paṭhyate. cakṣurindriyam anupahataṃ bhavati. viṣaya ābhāsagato bhavati. tajjaś ca manasāraḥ pratyupasthito bhavatīty ata āvṛte rūpe kācādibhis tatrotpadyate eva cakṣurvijñānaṃ yatra tu pratibandho 'kācādisvabhāvaiḥ kuḍyādibhis tamasvadbhiḥ tatrāvṛte notpadyate. kiṃ. cakṣur vijñānam iti. anutpannatvād āvṛtaṃ nekṣata iti. yat tvayā kiṃ khalu notpadyata iti anutpattau kāraṇaṃ pṛṣṭam idaṃ tatkāraṇam iti brūmaḥ. yat tarhi sūtra uktam iti vistaraḥ. cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā na nimittagrāhī bhavati nānuvyaṃjanagrāhīti viṣtaraḥ. yasmāc cakṣuḥ paśyati. tasmāt pudgalaś cakṣuṣā paśyatīty abhiprāyaḥ. ācāryaḥ prāha. tenāśrayeṇeti [Tib. 75b] ayam atrābhisaṃdhiḥ. cakṣur aśrityety evātrābhisaṃdhiḥ. cakṣuṣā āśrayeṇa vijñānena dṛṣṭvety arthaḥ. kathaṃ jñāyata ity āha. yathā manasā dharmān vijñāyeti. manasā āśrayeṇa vijñānena vijñāyeti bhavati. na hy anantarātītaṃ mano dharmān vijānāti. vartamānāvasthāyāṃ hi vijñānaṃ kāritraṃ karoti. āśritakarma vā āśrayasyopacaryata iti. āśritasya vijñānasya karma darśanam āśrayasya cakṣuṣa upacaryate. vijñāne paśyati sati cakṣuḥ paśyatīty upacāraḥ. yathā maṃcāḥ krośaṃtīti. yathā maṃcastheṣu puruṣeṣu krośatsu maṃcāḥ krośantīty upacāraḥ. tadvat. yathā ca sūtra uktam iti vistaraḥ. vaibhāṣikāṇām apy ayaṃ pakṣaḥ. na cakṣur vijānāti. kiṃ tarhi. vijñānaṃ vijānātīti. atha coktaṃ cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇi kāntānīti. tatrāśritakarma āśrayasyopacaryata iti avaśyaṃ pratipattavyaṃ. dvāraṃ yāvad eva rūpāṇāṃ darśanāyeti. dvāram iva dvāraṃ hetur āśraya iti abhiprāyaḥ. anenāgamena tenāśrayeṇeti yo 'rtha uktaḥ. tam eva samarthayati. tena cakṣuṣā dvāreṇa vijñānaṃ paśyatīti. darśane tatra dvārākhyeti. cakṣur brāhmaṇa dvāraṃ yāvad eva rūpāṇāṃ dārśanāyety atra. na hy etad yujyate darśanaṃ rūpāṇāṃ darśanāyeti. atrāvācakatvān naitad yujyata ity [Tib. 76a] abhiprāyaḥ. yadi darśanaṃ karaṇaṃ dṛśyate 'neneti darśanam iti. kartari vā lyuṭ paśyatīti darśanam iti.
darśanāyeti ca bhāvasādhanaṃ. dṛṣṭir darśanaṃ tasmai darśanāyeti. katham
body.translated_text: not apprehend the object obstructed by walls and so forth? This is not reasonable. Therefore, it should not be said that, because [the eye] has resistance, it does not see when concealed. 'And how is [what is] concealed by glass, a layer of clouds, crystal, or water seen?' A form concealed — that is, obstructed — by glass, a layer of clouds, crystal, or water — how is it seen? For, because [the eye] has resistance, just as it should not see what is obstructed by walls and so forth, so it should not see what is obstructed by glass and so forth — yet it does see: this is the established [fact]. 'Where there is no obstruction of light' — when there is light, the object comes into the range of illumination, and so the arising of consciousness is possible. For the condition of the arising of consciousness is thus taught: 'The eye-faculty is unimpaired; the object has come into the range [of illumination]; and the mind-attention born from that [eye] is present.' Therefore, when form is concealed by glass and so forth, visual consciousness does arise there — for light is not obstructed there. But where there is obstruction by things not of the nature of glass and so forth — by walls and so forth that possess darkness — when [the form is] concealed there, it does not arise. What? Visual consciousness. 'Because it has not arisen, the concealed is not seen.' [The opponent:] 'But what you asked — "Why indeed does it not arise?" — asking for the reason for non-arising: this is that reason,' we say. 'But then what was stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>' — and so forth in detail: 'Having seen forms with the eye, he is not a grasper of signs, nor a grasper of secondary characteristics' — and so forth in detail. Since the eye sees, therefore the person sees with the eye — this is the intent. The <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'By that base' — this is the purport here: 'relying on the eye' — this alone is the purport here. 'Having seen with the eye — [that is,] the base — by means of consciousness' — this is the meaning. 'How is this known?' he says: 'Just as [it is said:] "having cognized <s>dharmas</s> with the mind."' 'With the mind — the base — by means of consciousness, having cognized' — this is [the meaning]. For it is not the immediately-past mind that cognizes <s>dharmas</s> — for consciousness performs its function in the present state. Or, 'the action of the supported is figuratively attributed to the base.' The action of the supported consciousness — seeing — is figuratively attributed to the base, the eye. When consciousness sees, the eye is [figuratively] said to see — this is the figurative usage. Just as 'the platforms cry out' — just as when men standing on platforms cry out, the figurative expression is 'the platforms cry out.' Similarly here. And as it is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s> — and so forth in detail. Even for the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>, this is [their] position: the eye does not cognize; rather, consciousness cognizes. And yet it has been said: 'Forms are cognizable by the eye, pleasing...' — there, 'the action of the supported is figuratively attributed to the base' must necessarily be accepted. 'It is merely a door for seeing forms' — a door is like a door, [i.e.,] a cause, a base — this is the intent. By this scriptural authority, the meaning stated by 'by that base' is reinforced: 'consciousness sees through that eye, which is the door.' 'There, the designation "door" for seeing' — 'The eye, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is merely a door for seeing forms' — in this [passage]. For it is not reasonable [to say:] 'Seeing [is a door] for seeing [i.e., redundant use].' The meaning is: because it would be non-expressive [i.e., tautological], this is not reasonable. If seeing [means] instrument — 'seeing' because one sees by means of it — or [if] the suffix <s>lyuṭ</s> is in the agent sense — 'that which sees is seeing' — then 'for seeing' would be a verbal noun — 'vision is seeing; for that — for seeing.' How is

body.text: etad yujyate. yasmāc cakṣurvyatiriktaṃ darśanaṃ nāsti. ālocanam iti cet. na. vijñānāvyatiriktatvāt vijñānam eva hy ālocanaṃ. nāto 'nyat paśyāmaḥ. yadi tu cakṣurdvāraṃ vivaraṃ rūpāṇāṃ darśanāya vijñānāyety artho gṛhyeta tad yujyate. tadyathā kācit prajñā paśyaty apy ucyata iti. paśyatīty apy ucyata iti itiśabdo 'trādhyāhāryaḥ. anenopanyāsena darśanavijñānayor anarthāntarabhāva iti darśayati. kā punar asau yā prajñaivam ucyate. yā darśanātmikoktā.
body.translated_text: this reasonable? Because there is no seeing apart from the eye [under that interpretation]. [Objection:] 'It means looking (<s>ālocana</s>).' [Reply:] No, because it is not different from consciousness — for looking is indeed consciousness itself. We do not see anything else [that it could mean]. But if the meaning were taken as: 'The eye is a door — an opening — for seeing forms, [that is,] for consciousness' — that would be reasonable. 'Just as a certain wisdom is also said to "see"' — 'is also said to see' — the particle <s>iti</s> here is to be supplied. By this illustration, he shows that seeing and consciousness are not different things. 'And which is that wisdom that is thus spoken of?' That which has been described as having the nature of view.

children.translated_text: 'The other [wisdom] is noble wisdom in both ways' —

body.text: iti. tasyaivaṃ jānata evaṃ paśyata iti sūtre 'pi vacanāt. kiṃcid iti vacanān na sarvaṃ vijñānaṃ paśyatīty uktaṃ bhavati. cakṣurvijñānaṃ hi paśyatīty ucyate. na tu śrotrādivijñānam iti. kānyā dṛṣṭikriyeti. yasyopalambhakatvaṃ. tasya darśanaṃ yujyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. tad etad acodyam iti vistaraḥ. yadi vijñānaṃ vijānāti. kartṛbhūtasya vijñānasya kānyā vijñānakriyeti vaktavyam iti tulyaṃ codyam āpadyate. na ca tatra kartṛkriyābhedaḥ. na kartur vijñānasya kriyāyāś ca vijñānalakṣaṇāyā bhedo 'nyatvam asti. bhavati ca kartṛkriyāsambandhavyapadeśaḥ. vijñānaṃ vijānātīti. [Tib. 76b] tadvad ihāpi bhavet. cakṣuḥ paśyatīti acodyam etat. cakṣurvijñānaṃ darśanam ity apare. tasyāśrayabhāvāc cakṣuḥ paśyatīty ucyate. yathā nādasyāśrayabhāvāt ghaṇṭā nadatīty ucyate. [vijñānaṃ tarhi kasyāśrayabhāvād rūpaṃ vijānātīty āha.] vijñānasyāśrayabhāvād iti. cakṣurvijñānasyāśrayabhāvād ity arthaḥ. tad vijñānaṃ darśanam iti rūḍhaṃ loke iti. darśanam iti loke rūḍhaṃ na tu vijñānam iti rūḍhaṃ. kathaṃ gamyata ity āha. tathā hi tasminn utpanne rūpaṃ dṛṣṭam ity ucyate na vijñātam iti. vibhāṣāyām apy ucyata iti. sa evartho 'bhidhīyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. cakṣuḥsaṃprāptaṃ cakṣurābhāsagataṃ. vijñānaṃ tu sāṃnidhya mātreṇeti. nāśrayabhāvayogeneti darśayati. yathā sūryo divasakara iti. yathā yathā sāṃnidhyamātreṇa sūryo divasaṃ karotīty ucyate. tathā vijñānaṃ vijānātīty ucyate. kasmāt. loke tathā siddhatvāt. nirvyāpāraṃ hīdaṃ iti vistaraḥ. nirvyāparam iti nirīham. anena hi kartur arthāntarabhūtāṃ vā kriyāṃ pratiṣedhati. dharmamātram iti. svataṃtrasya kartuḥ pratiṣedhaṃ karoti. hetuphalamātraṃ ceti. asaty api kartari hetuphalayoḥ kāryakāraṇam arthatvaṃ darśayati. tatra chandata upacārāḥ kriyante yad vastu vyavahārāṃgaṃ teneha vyavahārārthasaṃsiddhyartham asad api sadrūpeṇa parikalpya [Tib. 77a] kartṛkriyādivyavasthāṇaṃ kriyate. cakṣuḥ paśyati vijñānaṃ vijānātīty
body.translated_text: Thus. Because in the <s>sūtra</s> too it is stated: 'for one who thus knows and thus sees.' From the word 'something' (<s>kiṃcit</s>), it is said that not all consciousness sees — for eye-consciousness is said to 'see,' but not ear-consciousness and the rest. 'What other seeing-action [is there]?' — the intent is: it is fitting that [seeing] belongs to that which has the character of apprehending. 'This is not a valid objection' — thus the elaboration. If consciousness cognizes, then the same objection would apply: 'What other cognizing-action is there for consciousness, which is the agent?' But there [in that case], there is no distinction between agent and action — there is no difference, no otherness, between consciousness as agent and the action characterized as consciousness. And yet there is the designation of agent-action relation: 'consciousness cognizes.' Likewise here too, [one can say:] 'the eye sees' — this is not a valid objection. 'Eye-consciousness is seeing' — say others. 'Because of the relationship of support, the eye is said to see' — just as a bell is said to 'ring' because of the support-relationship to the sound. [If one asks:] 'Because of whose support-relationship does consciousness cognize form?' — he says: 'Because of the support-relationship of consciousness' — meaning because of the support-relationship of eye-consciousness. 'That consciousness is "seeing" — this is established usage in the world.' 'Seeing' (<s>darśana</s>) is established usage in the world, but not 'cognizing' (<s>vijñāna</s>). How is this known? He says: 'For when it [consciousness] has arisen, it is said "form was seen," not "cognized."' 'In the <s>Vibhāṣā</s> too it is stated' — the intent is that the same meaning is expressed [there]. 'Arrived at the eye' — having come within the eye's field. 'But consciousness, by mere proximity' — he shows that it is not through the relation of support. 'Just as the sun is called "day-maker"' — just as the sun is said to 'make the day' by mere proximity, so consciousness is said to 'cognize.' Why? Because it is thus established in the world. 'For this is without activity' — thus the elaboration. 'Without activity' means without effort. By this, he denies either an action that is something other than the agent. '<s>Dharma</s>-mere' — he denies an independent agent. 'And merely cause and effect' — he shows that even without an agent, cause and effect have functional reality. 'Therein, by convention, figurative usages are made' — whatever entity serves as a component of conventional usage, here for the purpose of achieving the aim of conventional usage, even what does not [truly] exist is conceptually constructed in the guise of what exists, and the establishment of agent, action, and so forth is made — 'the eye sees,' 'consciousness cognizes,' and so on.

body.text: evamādi. nātrābhiniveṣṭavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: and so on. One should not cling to these [expressions].

children.translated_text: 'A being is different relative to the future' —

body.text: ityādi janapadaniruktiṃ nabhiniviśeteti. janapadas tatra niyatā niścitā coktir janapadaniruktiḥ. tāṃ nābhiniviśeta. tasmād atreyaṃ niruktir iti. na vā sarvām evārthavatīṃ niruktiṃ kalpayet. saṃjñāṃ ca lokasya nābhidhāved iti. ātmā jīva ity evamādikāṃ saṃjñāṃ lokasya nādhyāropayet. abhūtasamāropeṇāsty ātmā śarīrādivyatirikta iti gacched ity arthaḥ. atha vā saṃjñāṃ ca lokasya nābhidhāven nātisaret. arthābāvāt saṃjñāpi nāstīti na kalpayed ity arthaḥ. atisaraṇam atikramaṇam ity eko 'rthaḥ.
body.translated_text: and so on — [this relates to:] 'one should not cling to local etymologies.' The established and fixed usage of a region is 'local etymology' (<s>janapada-nirukti</s>). One should not cling to it — [thinking] 'therefore this is the [only correct] etymology.' Nor should one regard every etymology as meaningful. 'And one should not violate the conventions of the world' — one should not impose on the world such designations as 'self,' 'soul,' and the like. The meaning is: one should not, by false superimposition, come to [believe that] there is a self distinct from the body and so on. Alternatively: 'One should not violate the conventions of the world' — should not transgress them. The meaning is: one should not conceptualize that, because the referent does not exist, the convention too does not exist. 'Transgression' and 'overstepping' are one and the same meaning.

body.text: apiśabdād ekenāpi nātra niyamaḥ. dvayor vivṛtayoḥ parriśuddhataraṃ darśanam iti. uktaṃ bhavati naikatarānyathībhāvād iti. unmīlitārdhanimīlitayor akṣṇoḥ ekatarasyānyathībhāvād dvayor ekatarad yady anyathībhavati. yadi yad unmīlitaṃ. tad ardhanimīlitaṃ kriyet sarvanimīlitaṃ vā. yac cārdhanimīlitaṃ. yadi tat sarvanimīlitaṃ kriyet sarvonmīlitaṃ vā. tadā dvicandradarśanaṃ na bhavati. ato 'vagamyate dvayor api cakṣuṣor atra vijñānotpattau vyāpāro 'stīti. deśapratiṣṭhitatvāt rūpavad iti viparītadṛṣṭāntaḥ. yathā rūpasya deśapratiṣṭhitatvāt āśrayavicchedād [Tib. 77b] vicchedo bhavati. naivaṃ vijñānasya. na hi vijñānaṃ ca nāśrayavicchedād vicchedo bhavati.
body.translated_text: from the word 'too' (<s>api</s>), [it follows that] even by one alone there is no restriction here. 'When both are open, there is purer seeing' — thus it is said. 'Not from the alteration of one alone' — of the two eyes, one open and one half-closed: if one of the two is altered — if the one that is open is made half-closed or fully closed, or if the one that is half-closed is made fully closed or fully opened — then the seeing of two moons does not occur. Therefore it is understood that both eyes have an operative role in the arising of consciousness here. 'Because of being located in a place, like form' — this is a counter-example. Just as form, because of being located in a place, is interrupted when the support is interrupted — consciousness is not like that. For consciousness is not interrupted just because the support is interrupted.

body.text: (I.42cd) tathā hi dūrād rūpaṃ paśyatīti. yatra rūpaṃ dṛśyate. na tatra tadgrāhakaṃ cakṣurindriyam asti. tatra pramāṇānupalabhyamānatvāt. tatrāvidyamānadevadattādivat. yathā cakṣuḥ. evaṃ śrotram api vaktavyaṃ. itara āha. svaviṣayadeśaprāpti cakṣuḥśrotram. indriyatvāt. ghrāṇendriyādivat. anenānumānena tatra pramāṇānupalabhyamānatvaṃ hetum asiddhaṃ darśayati. ācārya āha. sati ca prāptaviṣayatva iti vistaraḥ. yadi prāptaviṣayaṃ cakṣuḥśrotraṃ kalpyeta divyaṃ cakṣuḥśrotram iha manuṣyeṣu dhyāyināṃ nopajāyet. yadi hi cakṣuḥśrotram api viprakṛṣṭadeśasthaṃ vyavahitaṃ ca kuḍyādibhir yathāyogaṃ rūpaṃ śabdaṃ gṛhṇīyāt. evam asya divyatvaṃ saṃbhavet. tac ca prāptaviṣayatve na syāt. ghrāṇādivat. yathā ghrāṇajihvākāyāḥ prāptaviṣayatvāt divyā dhyāyināṃ nopajāyeran. tadvat. anena svaviṣayadeśaprāpitvapakṣasya dharmiviśeṣaviparyayāpakṣālatvaṃ darśayati. saṃbhavaddivyatve hi cakṣuḥśrotre dharmī. asaṃbhavaddivyatvabhāvo viśeṣaviparyayaḥ. sa prāpnotīti
body.translated_text: (I.42cd) For indeed one sees form from a distance. Where form is seen — there the eye sense-faculty that grasps it does not exist, because no valid means of knowledge apprehends it there — just as <s>Devadatta</s>, who is not present there, and so on. Just as the eye, so too the ear should be stated [as not reaching its object]. The other [party, i.e., the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>] says: 'The eye and ear reach the location of their respective objects — because they are sense-faculties, like the nose sense-faculty and others.' By this inference, he shows that the reason 'not being apprehended by any valid means of knowledge there' is unestablished. The master [<s>Vasubandhu</s>] says: 'But if [they] reached their objects' — thus the elaboration. If the eye and ear were posited as reaching their objects, the divine eye and ear would not arise for meditators among human beings. For if the eye and ear, even when situated in a distant location, could respectively grasp form and sound that are obstructed by walls and the like, thus their divine character would be possible. But that would not obtain if they reached their objects — like the nose and the rest. Just as nose, tongue, and body, because they reach their objects, do not become divine for meditators — likewise. By this, he shows that the position of [the sense-faculties] reaching the location of their objects has the deficiency of contradiction with a special instance of the subject (<s>dharmi</s>). For the eye and ear, whose divine character is possible, are the subject. The impossibility of divine character is the special-instance contradiction. 'It reaches' —

body.text: doṣaḥ anena doṣeṇānumānatvāt. tatpramāṇānupalabhyamānatvaṃ siddhaṃ vyavasthāpayati. tasmād aprāptaviṣayaṃ cakṣuḥśrotraṃ. yady aprāptaviṣayaṃ cakṣur iti vistaraḥ. āsannenātidūrasthena tiraskṛtena vā tulyā tadaprāptir iti [Tib. 78a] tatra darśanaṃ prasaṃjayati. kim idaṃ parasya sādhanam uta dūṣaṇam iti. yadi tāvad evaṃ sādhanam atidūraṃ tiraskṛtaṃ cakṣuḥśrotreṇa gṛhyate. aprāptatvāt. āsannaviṣayavad iti. tadasādhanaṃ hetoḥ svayam aniścitatvāt. pūrvābhyupagamavirodhād vā. atha dūṣaṇaṃ sarvaprāptagrāhakatvaṃ cakṣuḥśrotralakṣaṇasya dharmiṇaḥ prasajyate. tad adūṣaṇam anumānabādhanāt. katham ity āha. kathaṃ tāvad ayaskānto na sarvam aprāptam ayaḥ karṣayatīti praśnamukhenāyaskāntanidarśanam upanyasya sarvāprāptagrāhakatvaṃ cakṣuḥśrotrasya sādhayati. na sarvāprāptagrāhakaṃ cakṣuḥśrotraṃ. sarvāprāptagrahaṇaśaktihīnatvāt. ayaskāntavat. ayaskānto hy aprāptam ayo gṛhṇāti karṣatīty arthaḥ. na ca sarvam aprāptaṃ gṛhṇāti. tadvac cakṣuḥśrotraṃ. prāptaviṣayatve 'pi caitat samānam iti. nātidūratiraskṛto viṣayaś cakṣuḥśrotreṇa gṛhyate. grahaṇāyogyatvāt. saṃprāptāṃjanadaśalākāvat. atha vā na sarvasvagrāhyagrāhi cakṣuḥśrotram. indriyasvābhāvyāt. ghrāṇendriyādivat. ghrāṇādīnāṃ hi prāpto viṣayo na tu sarvaḥ. sahabhūgandhādyagrahaṇāt. ghrāṇādisahabhūni hi gandharasaspraṣṭavyāni ghrāṇādibhir na gṛhyante. śaktir hīndriyāṇām īdṛśīti. manas tv arūpitvād iti. prāptatvaṃ mūrtānām eva vyavasthāpyeta nāmūrtānām iti. mano 'prāptaviṣayam [Tib. 78b] iti na vicāraḥ kriyate.
body.translated_text: — is the fault. Because of this fault in the inference, he establishes that [the reason] 'not being apprehended by any valid means of knowledge there' is proven. Therefore the eye and ear do not reach their objects. 'But if the eye does not reach its object' — thus the elaboration. Whether [the object is] nearby, extremely distant, or concealed — its non-reaching [by the eye] is equal — so [the opponent] presses the consequence that [the eye] would see there [too]. Is this the opponent's proof or a refutation? If it is a proof: 'The extremely distant and the concealed are grasped by the eye and ear, because they are not reached — just as a nearby object' — this proof is invalid because the reason is itself not established [as invariably connected]. Or because it contradicts the prior admission [that only nearby objects are seen]. If it is a refutation: the resistance-character of the subject, the eye and ear, [would entail that they] grasp everything that is not reached — this too is not a valid refutation, because it is blocked by an inference. How? He says: 'Just as a lodestone does not attract all iron that it has not reached' — thus, by posing the question and presenting the lodestone example, he establishes that the eye and ear do not grasp everything not reached. The eye and ear do not grasp everything not reached — because they lack the power to grasp everything not reached — like a lodestone. For a lodestone grasps iron that it has not reached — that is, it attracts it — but it does not grasp all un-reached [iron]. Likewise the eye and ear. 'Even if they reached their objects, the same [problem] would apply' — the extremely distant and concealed objects are not grasped by the eye and ear — because they are unsuitable for grasping, like a collyrium-stick that has arrived [at the eye but cannot see distant objects]. Alternatively: the eye and ear do not grasp everything that is their own graspable — because of the nature of the sense-faculties, like the nose sense-faculty and the rest. For the nose and the rest have objects that are reached, but not all [objects] — because they do not grasp scent and the rest that are concomitant [with their own body]. For the scent, taste, and tangibles concomitant with the nose and the rest are not grasped by the nose and the rest. Such is the capacity of the sense-faculties. 'But mind, being formless' — the reaching [of objects] would be established only for material [entities], not for immaterial ones — so no inquiry is made [regarding mind's] having un-reached objects.

body.text: prāptaviṣayam eva trayam iti iṣṭāvadhāraṇārtham ārambhaḥ. anyathā hi prāptāprāptaviṣayam ity api saṃbhāvyeta. nirucchvāsasya gandhāgrahaṇād iti. yad ucchvāsena sardhaṃ sūkṣmaṃ bhūtacatuṣkaṃ ghrāṇam āgataṃ. tasya gandho ghrāṇena ghrāyate. vāyau gandhāntaram utpannam ity apare. miśṛībhaveyur ekadeśībhaveyuḥ. athaikadeśena. kiṃ. spṛśeyur iti vartate. kathaṃ śabdābhiniṣpattir iti. yadi na spṛśanti. anabhighāte śabdābhiniṣpattir na prāpnotīty abhiprāyaḥ. ata eveti kāśmīrāḥ. yadi hi spṛśeyuḥ. hasto haste 'bhyāhataḥ sajjeta jatuneva jatvantaraṃ. kathaṃ citaṃ pratyāhataṃ na viśīryata iti. anyonyam aspṛśatāṃ paramāṇūnāṃ saṃghātaḥ pratyāhataḥ pāṇyādibhiḥ kathaṃ na viśīryate. tad evaiṣāṃ nirantaratvaṃ yan madhye nāsti kiṃcid ity ālokādi madhye nāstīti nirantaratvam eṣāṃ vyavasthāpyate. tad eva ca prāptatvaṃ nānyatheti. api
body.translated_text: The statement 'three exclusively grasp reached objects' is for the purpose of confirming the desired restriction. For otherwise, [one might suppose] 'they grasp both reached and un-reached objects.' 'Because one without breathing does not grasp smell' — the subtle group of four elements that arrives at the nose together with the in-breath — the smell of that [group] is smelled by the nose. 'Others [say:] a different smell arises in the wind' — [this means:] they would mix, they would become united. 'But [what if they touch] with one part [only]?' — 'what [then]?' 'They would touch' — this is to be supplied. 'How does sound come about?' — if they do not touch, [then] without contact, the production of sound would not obtain — this is the intent. 'Hence' — [say] the <s>Kāśmīras</s>. For if they touched, the hand struck against the hand would stick [to it] like lac stuck to other lac. 'How is the aggregated [structure] not destroyed when struck?' — the aggregate of atoms that do not touch each other mutually — when struck by the hands and the like, how is it not destroyed? 'Their very contiguity is that there is nothing in between' — that there is no light or the like in between — this is established as their contiguity. And that itself is [what is meant by] their 'reaching' — not anything else.

body.text: khalv iti. api cety arthaḥ. saṃghātāḥ sāvayavatvāt spṛśantīty adoṣaḥ. yo 'sau doṣa ukto yadi sarvātmanā spṛśeyur miśrībhaveyur dravyāṇy athaikadeśena sāvayavāḥ prasajyerann iti. kāraṇaṃ pratīti. yasya yādṛśaṃ kāraṇaṃ. tasya tat kāraṇaṃ. spṛṣṭam aspṛṣṭaṃ vā pratīty āha. kadācid iti vistaraḥ. spṛṣṭahetukam iti. spṛṣṭam anyonyaṃ hetur asya spṛṣṭahetukaṃ. evam aspṛṣṭahetukaṃ. [Tib. 79a] yadā viśīryata iti. tadyathā śuṣkā mṛc cūrṇīkriyamāṇā. yadā cayaṃ gacchatīti. tadyathā himaṃ. tad dhi pūrvaṃ sūkṣmaṃ paścān mahad bhavati. cayavatāṃ caya iti. tadyathā mṛtpiṇḍadvayasaṃnipāte. uttarakṣaṇāvasthānaṃ syād iti. utpadya spṛṣṭiyogāt. nirantare tu spṛṣṭasaṃjñeti bhadantaḥ. bhadantamataṃ caiṣṭavyam iti. vaibhāṣikamataṃ kasmān naiṣṭavyaṃ. nanu vaibhāṣikair apy evam uktaṃ. tad evaiṣāṃ nirantaratvaṃ yan madhye nāsti kiṃcid iti. asty evam. sāvakāśaṃ tu tad vacanam. yan madhye nāsti kiṃcid iti bruvāṇā vaibhāṣikā madhye ālokādi necchanti. anyaparamāṇupraveśānavakāśaṃ tu na bruvate. anyathā hi sāntarāṇāṃ paramāṇūnāṃ śūnyeṣv antareṣu gatiḥ kena pratibadhyeta gatimata iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. ayaṃ cāparo doṣaḥ. na ca paramāṇubhyo 'nye saṃghātāḥ yathā vaibhāṣikāḥ kalpayanti. ta eva te saṃghātāḥ paramāṇavaḥ spṛśyante. yathā rūpyanta iti. saṃghātā eva naika ity arthaḥ. yadi ca paramāṇor iti vistaraḥ. paramāṇvapariniṣpattiṃ vaktukāmaḥ ācāryo vicārayati. yadi paramāṇor ekasya pūrvādidigbhāgabhedaḥ kalpyeta spṛṣṭasyānyonyam aspṛṣṭasya vā sāvayavatvaprasaṃgaḥ. na cet. kim. digbhāgabheda iti vartate. spṛṣṭasyāpy aprasaṃgaḥ. kasya. sāvayavatvasya. [Tib. 79b] atra sādhanam. na niravayavaḥ paramāṇuḥ. digbhāgabhedavattvāt. māṣarāśivad iti. tad etad digbhāgabhedavattvaṃ necchanti vaibhāṣikāḥ. digbhāgabhedo hi saṃghātarūpāṇām eva kalpyate. evaṃ ca varṇayanti. dharmataiveyaṃ yat sapratighānāṃ bhinnadeśatvaṃ. teṣāṃ nairantaryeṇāvasthānāt abhinnadeśatvaṃ mā bhūd iti sāntarāṇām api sapratighatvena gatiḥ pratibadhyata iti.
body.translated_text: 'Indeed' (<s>khalu</s>) — means 'moreover' (<s>api ca</s>). 'Aggregates, being composite, touch [each other]' — [so there is] no fault. The fault that was stated was: 'if they touch with their whole being, they would merge and substances [would be lost]; if with a part, they would turn out to have parts.' 'Depending on the cause' — for whatever [entity], whatever kind of cause [obtains], that is its cause — whether touching or not touching [another], he says: 'Sometimes' — and so on in detail. 'Having a touched cause' (<s>spṛṣṭahetuka</s>) — mutually touched is the cause of this, [hence] 'having a touched cause.' Similarly, 'having an untouched cause.' [Tib. 79a] 'When it disintegrates' — for example, dry clay being pulverized. 'When it undergoes accrual' — for example, snow, for it is first small and afterwards becomes large. 'Accrual of things undergoing accrual' — for example, when two lumps of clay come together. 'There would be an establishment in the next moment' — having arisen, through the conjunction of contact. 'But the Venerable [Vasumitra says that] for what is without interval, [there is] the designation of contact' — and the Venerable's view is to be preferred. Why should the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> view not be preferred? Have not the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> too said this: 'their being without interval means that there is nothing in between'? That is so. But that statement allows [for space]. The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>, saying 'there is nothing in between,' do not accept light, etc. in between; but they do not say there is no room for the entry of another atom. For otherwise, since atoms have gaps between them, what would obstruct the movement through the empty gaps [of something] that has movement? — this is the remainder of the sentence. And this is another fault: aggregates are not [entities] different from atoms, as the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> conceive. Those very aggregates are atoms that are touched — as they are altered. The meaning is: aggregates alone, not one [individual atom]. 'And if the atom' — and so on in detail. Wishing to state the non-ultimacy of the atom, the <s>Ācārya</s> investigates: If directional parts — east, etc. — were conceived for a single atom, whether touching another or not, the unwanted consequence of having parts [would follow]. If not — what [follows]? 'Directional parts' is to be supplied. [Then] even for one touching [another], the unwanted consequence does not follow. Of what? Of having parts. [Tib. 79b] Here the proof [is]: the atom is not partless, because it has directional parts — like a heap of beans. This [argument about] having directional parts the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> do not accept. For directional parts are conceived only for composite forms. And they explain thus: it is simply the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>) that resistant [entities] have different locations. Since they stand without interval, their having different locations does not entail [that they are not in contact] — 'lest their having no different location [follow]' — even for those with gaps between them, movement is obstructed by their resistance.

body.text: (I.43ab) āśuvṛttyā ca parvatādīnām alātacakrādivad iti. ātmaparimāṇatulyasyaivārthasya grahaṇa iṣyamāṇe kathaṃ parvatādīnāṃ mahatāṃ sakṛd iva grahaṇaṃ lakṣyate na krameṇety āśaṃkya yuktiṃ tathā grahaṇe kathayati. āśuvṛttyā cetyādi. yathā alātacakrādigrahaṇaṃ krameṇa vartamānaṃ sakṛd iva lakṣyate. tathā parvatanadīśabdādigrahaṇam āśuvṛttyā bhavatīti. āhosvit tulyātulyasyeti. drākṣāphalādidarśane tulyasya. vālāgraparvatādidarśane atulyasyety abhiprāyaḥ. unmiṣitamātreṇeti na kramadarśananyāyena. evaṃ śrotreṇeti
body.translated_text: (I.43ab) 'And because of rapid operation, [the perception of] mountains, etc. [arises] like a whirling firebrand,' etc. When it is accepted that only an object equal to one's own size is perceived, since the perception of large things like mountains, etc. appears to be all at once and not in sequence — anticipating this [objection], he states the reasoning for such perception: 'And because of rapid operation' and so on. Just as the perception of a whirling firebrand, etc., though proceeding sequentially, appears to be all at once, so the perception of mountains, rivers, sounds, etc. occurs through rapid operation. 'Or, of equal and unequal' — in seeing grapes and the like, [it perceives objects] equal [to itself]; in seeing a hair-tip, a mountain, etc., [it perceives objects] unequal — this is the intent. 'Merely by the opening of the eyes' — not by the method of sequential seeing. 'Similarly with the ear' —

body.text: vistaraḥ. kadācid alpīyāṃso yadā maśakaśabdaṃ śṛṇoti. kadācit samāḥ yadā śrotraparamāṇusamapramāṇaṃ kasyacic chabdaṃ śṛṇoti. kadācid bhūyāṃso yadā meghaśabdaṃ śṛṇotīti. ajājīpuṣpavad avasthitāḥ kālajīrakapuṣpavad avasthitāḥ ekatalāvasthitā ity arthaḥ. bhūrjābhyantarāvasthitā iti karṇābhyantare yad bhūrjapattravarṇākāraṃ. tad bhūrjam iveti bhūrjaṃ. tadabhyaṃtare 'vasthitāḥ śrotrendriyaparamāṇavaḥ. [Tib. 80a] ghāṭābhyantare ghāṭā nāsāpuṭī. mālāvad avasthitānīti. maṇḍalena samapaṃktyāvasthitānīti. vālāgramātraṃ kileti. āgamasūcanārthaḥ kilaśabdaḥ. asphuṭam avyāptaṃ. sa kileti karmasāmarthyād evāviśaraṇaṃ syād iti. kilaśabdena aruciṃ sūcayati. saṃcitāśrayālambanatvād iti saṃcitāśrayatvāt saṃcitālambanatvāc ca.
body.translated_text: and so on in detail. 'Sometimes fewer' — when one hears the sound of a mosquito. 'Sometimes equal' — when one hears the sound of something equal in size to the ear-atoms. 'Sometimes more' — when one hears the sound of thunder. 'Arranged like cumin flowers' — means arranged like the flowers of the <s>kālajīraka</s> (cumin) plant — situated on a single level. 'Situated inside the <s>bhūrja</s> (birch)' — inside the ear, that which resembles a birch-bark leaf in color and shape — that is called '<s>bhūrja</s>' as if it were birch-bark; the atoms of the ear-faculty are situated inside that. [Tib. 80a] 'Inside the <s>ghāṭā</s>' — <s>ghāṭā</s> means the nostril-cavity. 'Arranged like a garland' — means arranged in a circle, in even rows. 'Merely the tip of a hair, reportedly' (<s>kila</s>) — the word <s>kila</s> is for indicating a scriptural [source]. 'Unclear, not established.' 'That, reportedly' — [means] it would be non-extension through the power of <s>karma</s> alone. With the word <s>kila</s>, he indicates his dissatisfaction. 'Because of having an accumulated support and object' — because of having an accumulated support and because of having an accumulated object.

children.translated_text: 'The support of the last [consciousness] is past' —

body.text: iti. atīta evety avadhāraṇaṃ. ata evocyata iti. yasmāt paṃca vijñānakāyā indriyadvayāśrayāḥ. cakṣurādīndriyāśrayā manaindriyāśrayāś ca. tasmāc catuḥkoṭika uttiṣṭhate. prathamā koṭiś cakṣur iti. cakṣurvijñānasya cakṣur āśrayabhāvena na samanantarapratyayabhāvena. na hi cakṣuś cittacaittasvabhāvaṃ.
body.translated_text: This is a restriction: 'past only.' 'Therefore it is said' — because the five consciousness-groups have a twofold support — the eye-faculty, etc. as support, and the mind-faculty as support — a fourfold classification arises. The first alternative is 'the eye' — the eye for eye-consciousness in the capacity of support, not in the capacity of the immediately antecedent condition. For the eye is not of the nature of mind and mental factors.

children.translated_text: 'Non-final mind and mental factors that have arisen are the immediately antecedent [condition]' —

body.text: iti ca samanantarapratyayalakṣaṇaṃ. dvitīyā koṭiḥ samanantarātītaś caitasiko dharmadhātus tasya samanantarabhāvena. ṣaḍ eva hy āśrayā vijñānasyeṣyante cakṣurādayo manaḥparyantā nānye. tṛtīyā samanantarātītaṃ manaḥ. ubhayalakṣaṇayuktatvāt. caturthī uktanirmuktā dharmāḥ. koṭitrayamuktā viprayuktā asaṃskṛtādayaḥ. [Tib. 80b] evaṃ yāvat kāyavijñānasya svam indriyaṃ vaktavyam iti. yaḥ śrotravijñānasyāśrayabhāvena. samantarapratyayabhāvenāpi sa. tasyeti catuḥkoṭikaḥ. prathamā koṭiḥ śrotraṃ. dvitīyā samanantarātītaś caitasiko dharmadhātuḥ. tṛtīyā samanantarātītaṃ manaḥ. caturthī koṭir uktanirmuktā dharmā. ity evam api vaktavyaṃ. manovijñānasya pūrvapādaka iti. yo manovijñānasyāśrayabhāvena. samanantarapratyayabhāvenāpi sa. tasyeti pūrvapādakaḥ. yas tāvad āśrayabhāvena. samanantarapratyayabhāvenāpi sa iti. manas tāvad avaśyam asau samanantarapratyayaḥ. syāt samanantarapratyayabhāvena nāśrayabhāvena. samanantarātītaś caitasiko dharmadhātur acakṣurādyāśrayaṣaṭsvabhāvatvāt.
body.translated_text: this is the characteristic of the immediately antecedent condition. The second alternative: the immediately past mental-factor <s>dharma-dhātu</s> — for it, [the relationship is] in the capacity of immediately antecedent [condition]. For only six supports of consciousness are accepted — the eye, etc. up to the mind — and no others. The third [alternative]: the immediately past mind — because it possesses both characteristics. The fourth: <s>dharmas</s> other than those stated — those excluded from the three alternatives: dissociated [factors], the unconditioned, etc. [Tib. 80b] And so on, up to: for body-consciousness, one should state its own faculty. [Similarly:] 'That which, for ear-consciousness, [functions] in the capacity of support — does it also [function] in the capacity of immediately antecedent condition? For that' — [this is] a fourfold classification. First alternative: the ear. Second: the immediately past mental-factor <s>dharma-dhātu</s>. Third: the immediately past mind. Fourth: <s>dharmas</s> other than those stated. And so too it should be stated: 'The preceding [condition] of mental consciousness' — that which, for mental consciousness, [functions] in the capacity of support — does it also [function] in the capacity of immediately antecedent condition? For that — this is the preceding [condition]. Now, that which [functions] in the capacity of support — does it also [function] in the capacity of immediately antecedent condition? The mind is necessarily that immediately antecedent condition. But [the question is:] could something [function] in the capacity of immediately antecedent condition but not in the capacity of support? [Yes:] the immediately past mental-factor <s>dharma-dhātu</s>, because it does not have the nature of the six [supports] such as the eye, etc.

children.translated_text: 'Because of being modified by the modifications of those [faculties]' —

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. teṣāṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ vikāras tadvikāraḥ. tadvikāreṇa vikāras tadvikāravikāraḥ. sa eṣām astīti tadvikāravikārīṇi vijñānāni. tadbhāvas
body.translated_text: and so on in detail. The modification of those — the eye, etc. — is 'their modification.' A modification by their modification is 'the modification by their modification.' That [property] exists in these [consciousnesses] — hence the consciousnesses are 'modified by the modifications of those.' Their possession of that [property]

body.text: tadvikāravikāritvam. tasmāt. cakṣurādaya evaiṣām āśrayā ity avadhāryate. anugrahopaghātapaṭumandatānuvidhānād iti. cakṣurādīnāṃ aṃjanādibhir anugrahaṃ reṇvādibhiś copaghātaṃ cakṣurādivijñānāny anuvidadhate. sasukhotpādāt saduḥkhotpādāc ca. yathākramaṃ paṭumandatāṃ ca teṣām anuvidadhate. [Tib. 81a] paṭumandatotpādād ato 'vagamyate. cakṣurādivikāreṇa vijñānavikāro bhavatīti. nanu ca paṭuni rūpe paṭucakṣurvijñānam utpadyamānaṃ dṛśyate. mande maṃdam iti. [teṣāṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ.] yady api rūpasya paṭumaṃdate cakṣurvijñānam anuvidadhīta. vidhurāvasthayos tu cakṣūrūpayoś cakṣuravasthām eva cakṣurvijñānam anuvidhatte. na rūpavasthāṃ. tathā hi cakṣuṣi anugṛhīte rūpe copahate tadvītarāgāṇāṃ madhyasthānāṃ ca cakṣurvijñānam avikāram utpadyate. na tu saduḥkham utpadyate. rūpe punar anugṛhīte 'parityakte cakṣuṣi copahate kāmalavyādhinā timiropaghātena vā pītadarśanaṃ bhrāntaṃ keśoṇḍukādidarśanaṃ vā pravartate. tathā paṭuni rūpe jarayā mande cakṣuṣi mandaṃ cakṣurvijñānam utpadyate. evaṃ mande rūpe cakṣur yady atipaṭu bhavet paṭu cakṣurvijñānam utpadyate. tathā hi jātisvabhāvena paṭuni gṛdhracakṣuṣi mande 'pi śavarūpe anekayojanaviprakṛṣṭe 'pi cakṣurvijñānam utpadyate. ity evaṃ śrotrādīny api yojyāni.
body.translated_text: is 'being modified by the modifications of those.' Therefore — it is restricted that the eye, etc. alone are the supports of these [consciousnesses]. 'Because they conform to the benefiting, harming, sharpness, and dullness [of the faculties]' — eye-consciousness, etc. conform to the benefiting of the eye, etc. through collyrium, etc. and to the harming through dust, etc. And from the arising of pleasure and the arising of pain, respectively, they also conform to their sharpness and dullness. [Tib. 81a] From the arising of sharpness and dullness, it is understood that consciousness is modified by the modification of the eye, etc. [Objection:] But is it not seen that sharp eye-consciousness arises when form is sharp, and dull when [form is] dull? [Reply:] Although eye-consciousness may conform to the sharpness and dullness of form, when the eye and form are in different states, eye-consciousness conforms to the state of the eye alone, not to the state of form. For when the eye is well-functioning and form is impaired, for those free from desire and for neutral [persons], eye-consciousness arises unmodified — it does not arise with pain. But when form is intact and unimpaired and the eye is impaired by jaundice-disease or afflicted by cataracts, there arises a distorted perception of yellow, or a mistaken perception of hair-nets, etc. Similarly, when form is sharp but the eye is weakened by old age, dull eye-consciousness arises. And when form is dull, if the eye is exceedingly sharp, sharp eye-consciousness arises. For when the vulture's eye, which is sharp by its natural constitution, [perceives] even dull forms of corpses at a distance of many <s>yojanas</s>, eye-consciousness arises. Thus, for the ear, etc. too, the same reasoning should be applied.

body.text: ata āśrayabhāvāt. asādhāraṇatvāc ca. āśrayabhāvo vyākhyāta iti na taṃ praty ādriyate. asādhāraṇatvam eva tu vyācakṣāṇa āha. katham asādhāraṇatvam ityādi. anyacakṣurvijñānasyāpīti. anyasaṃtānavijñānasyāpīty arthaḥ. tair [Tib. 81b] eva nirdiśyata iti. cakṣurādibhiś cakṣurvijñānaṃ yāvan manovijñānaṃ. na rūpādibhiḥ rūpavijñānaṃ yāvad dharmavijñānaṃ. yathā bherīśabdo yavāṃkura iti. asādhāraṇatvāt tābhyāṃ bherīyavābhyāṃ yathā nirdeśo loke bherīśabdo yavāṃkura iti na tu daṇḍaśabdaḥ kṣetrāṃkura iti vā. daṇḍo hi paṭahādiśabdasyāpi kāraṇībhavet. kṣetraṃ ca śāligodhūmāṃkurasyāpīti sādhāraṇatvāt na tābhyāṃ nirdeśaḥ kriyate. asādhāraṇābhyāṃ tu bherīyavābhyāṃ nirdeśaḥ. tadvad ihāpi draṣṭavyam. api khalu cakṣur iva vijñānam ubhayoḥ sattvasaṃkhyātatvāt. rūpaṃ tv asattvasaṃkhyātam api. cakṣuṣā vijñānaṃ cakṣurvijñānam. tasya kāraṇabhāvāt. cakṣuṣi vijñānaṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ. sukhaduḥkhavedanāsaṃprayuktasya vijnānasya cakṣuranugrahopaghātapravṛttatvāt. cakṣuṣo vijñānaṃ cakṣurvijñānam. asādhāraṇatvena tataḥ pravṛtteḥ. cakṣuṣo vijñānaṃ cakṣurvijñānam. sattvasaṃkhyātasyaiva svāmibhāvāt. cakṣuṣi vijñānaṃ cakṣurvijñānam. tatsaṃprayoginyāḥ sukhāyā duḥkhāyā vā
body.translated_text: 'Therefore' means because of the capacity of support. 'And because of being non-common.' The support-capacity has been explained, so he does not attend to it. But explaining only the non-common character, he says: 'How is there non-commonness?' and so on. 'Even of another eye-consciousness' — means even of the consciousness of another continuum. 'They are designated by those [faculties]' [Tib. 81b] — by the eye, etc., [one designates] eye-consciousness up to mental consciousness — not by form, etc. [one designates] 'form-consciousness' up to '<s>dharma</s>-consciousness.' 'Just as a drum-sound, a barley-sprout' — because of non-commonness, the designation is made by those non-common [causes] — the drum, barley — as in the world: 'drum-sound,' 'barley-sprout' — but not 'stick-sound' or 'field-sprout.' For the stick could also be a cause of the sound of a <s>paṭaha</s>-drum, etc.; and the field could also [produce] rice and wheat sprouts — so because of commonness, designation is not made by those. But by the non-common [causes] — the drum and barley — designation [is made]. So too it should be seen here. Moreover, the eye is like consciousness — because both belong to beings. But form may be not belonging to beings. 'Eye-consciousness' (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>) — consciousness of the eye, because of its being a cause. Or, consciousness in the eye, because the consciousness connected with pleasure and pain-feeling operates in relation to the eye's benefiting and harming. Or, consciousness from the eye, because it operates from it by non-commonness. Or, consciousness of the eye, because only what belongs to beings has the status of an owner. Or, consciousness in the eye, because the pleasant or painful

body.text: vedanāyāś cakṣuṣy eva paricchidyamānatvāt. evaṃ śrotrādiṣu yojyam. tad evaṃ cakṣurādibhir eva vijñānanirdeśo yujyate na rūpādibhiḥ. evaṃ tṛtīyacaturthadhyānabhūmikena cakṣuṣā tadbhūmikādharabhūmikāni rūpāṇi paśyato [Tib. 82a] yojayitavyam iti. tasyaiva kāmadhātūpapannasya yojayitavyam. evaṃ tṛtīyādidhyānacakṣuṣā yojyam iti. tasyaiva prathamadhyānopapannasya tṛtīyacaturthadhyānacakṣuṣā paśyato yojyam.
body.translated_text: feeling conjoined with it is delimited to the eye alone. Thus the same reasoning should be applied for the ear, etc. Therefore, the designation of consciousness by the eye, etc. is proper — not by form, etc. 'Thus, for one who sees forms of that ground and lower grounds with the eye belonging to the third and fourth <s>dhyāna</s> [Tib. 82a] — [the same reasoning] should be applied' — this should be applied for that very person born in the desire-realm. 'Similarly, [seeing] with the eye of the third and higher <s>dhyānas</s> should be applied' — this should be applied for that very person born in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, seeing with the eye of the third and fourth <s>dhyānas</s>.

children.translated_text: 'Not lower than the body is the eye' —

body.text: iti. adharabhūmikam ity arthaḥ. svabhūmikam ūrdhvabhūmikaṃ cābhyanujñātaṃ bhavati. paṃcabhūmikāni hi kāyacakṣūrūpāṇi. kāyaḥ śarīraṃ. etāni kāyādīni paṃcabhūmikāni. kāmāvacarāṇi prathamadhyānabhūmikāni yāvac caturthadhyānabhūmikāny ārūpyadhātāv abhāvāt. dvibhūmikaṃ cakṣurvijñānam iti. kāmāvacaraṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ ca. tayor vitarkavicārasadbhāvāc cakṣurvijñānasya cāvaśyaṃ savitarkavicāratvāt.
body.translated_text: means 'not of a lower ground.' [The eye] of one's own ground and of a higher ground is permitted. For the body, eye, and form [exist on] five grounds. 'Body' means the physical body. These — the body, etc. — [exist on] five grounds: belonging to the desire-realm, the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground — because of their absence in the formless realm. 'Eye-consciousness is of two grounds' — belonging to the desire-realm and the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. Because <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application) exist in those two [grounds], and eye-consciousness is necessarily accompanied by <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>.

children.translated_text: 'Form of a higher [ground] is not [perceived] by the eye' —

body.text: iti. nordhvabhūmikaṃ rūpaṃ cakṣuṣo viṣayo bhavati. ūrdhvabhūmikasya rūpasya sūkṣmatvāt. svabhūmikam adharabhūmikaṃ cābhyanujñātaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: Form of a higher level is not the object of the eye. Because form of a higher level is subtle. Form of one's own level and of a lower level is accepted.

body.text: kim. ūrdhvaṃ na cakṣuṣa iti prakṛtaṃ. kāmāvacarasya cakṣuṣo 'dharabhūmikasya prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ na bhavati. svabhūmikam adharabhūmikaṃ vābhyanujñātaṃ bhavati. kāmāvacarasya cakṣuṣaḥ svabhūmikaṃ kāmāvacaram eva cakṣurvijñānaṃ bhavati. prathamadhyānabhūmikasya cakṣuṣaḥ prathamadhyānabhūmikam eva cakṣurvijñānaṃ bhavati. kāmāvacaraṃ tu cakṣurvijñānam asya na bhavati. nanu coktam adharabhūmikam abhyanujñātam iti. satyam uktam etat. [Tib. 82b] kiṃ tu. asaty ātmīye adharabhūmikam iṣyate. na satīti. dvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānacakṣuṣo hy asaty ātmīye prathamadhyānabhūmikam evādharaṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ bhavati. na tu kāmāvacaraṃ paramanihīnatvāt. saṃbhavatas tv evam uktam adharabhūmikam abhyanujñātam iti. asyety anantaroktasya cakṣurvijñānasyeti. cakṣurvijñānajāteḥ rūpaṃ sarvato viṣayaḥ. saṃbhavatas tu yojyam. kāmāvacarasya cakṣurvijñānasya svabhūmikam eva rūpam. prathamadhyānabhūmikasya tu prathamadhyānabhūmikacakṣurāśrayasya cakṣurvijñānasya svabhūmikam adharabhūmikaṃ ca rūpaṃ viṣayaḥ. caturthadhyānabhūmikacakṣurāśrayasya tu caturthadhyānabhūmikaṃ rūpaṃ tataś cādharabhūmikaṃ sarvaṃ viṣayaḥ. evaṃ yāvat dvitīyadhyānabhūmikacakṣurāśrayasya dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ tataś
body.translated_text: What? 'Of the eye, upward, not' — this is the topic. Eye-consciousness belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> level does not arise for an eye belonging to a lower level of the desire-realm. [Consciousness] of one's own level or of a lower level is accepted. For an eye of the desire-realm, only desire-realm eye-consciousness arises. For an eye of the first <s>dhyāna</s> level, only first-<s>dhyāna</s>-level eye-consciousness arises. But desire-realm eye-consciousness does not arise for it. [Objection:] But was it not said 'of a lower level is accepted'? True, that was said.
