[Tib. 82b] However, 'lower level' is accepted when one's own [level consciousness] does not exist, not when it does. For an eye of the second, third, or fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, when one's own [level consciousness] does not exist, only the first <s>dhyāna</s>-level — the lower — eye-consciousness arises. But not desire-realm [consciousness], because of its extreme inferiority. But 'of a lower level is accepted' is stated with reference to what is possible. 'Of this' means 'of the eye-consciousness just mentioned.' Form of that class of eye-consciousness is its object everywhere. But the application should be made with reference to what is possible. For desire-realm eye-consciousness, only form of its own level is [the object]. For first-<s>dhyāna</s>-level eye-consciousness having its support in a first-<s>dhyāna</s>-level eye, form of its own level and of a lower level is its object. For [eye-consciousness] having its support in a fourth-<s>dhyāna</s>-level eye, fourth-<s>dhyāna</s>-level form and all form below it is its object. Likewise, up to: for [eye-consciousness] having its support in a second-<s>dhyāna</s>-level eye, second-<s>dhyāna</s>-level

body.text: cādharabhūmikaṃ rūpaṃ viṣayaḥ. evaṃ cakṣurvijñānajāter ūrdhvam adhaḥ svabhūmau ca rūpaṃ viṣayo bhavati. kāyasya cobhe rūpavijñāne sarvato bhavata iti. kāmāvacarasya kāyasya śarīrasya svabhūmikordhvabhūmike rūpavijñāne bhavataḥ. prathamadhyānabhūmikasya kāyasya prathamadhyānabhūmikam eva vijñānam. rūpaṃ tu svordhvādharabhūmikam. yathā svāśrayaṃ cakṣuḥ. dvitīyādidhyānabhūmikasya kāyasya vijñānam adharabhūmikam eva prathamadhyānabhūmikam evety arthaḥ. rūpaṃ tu dvitīyatṛtīyadhyānabhūmikasya kāyasya svordhvādharabhūmikaṃ [Tib. 83a] yathā svāśrayaṃ cakṣuḥ. caturthadhyānabhūmikasya kāyasya rūpaṃ svādharabhūmikam. tata ūrdhvaṃ rūpabhāvāt.
body.translated_text: and lower-level form is its object. Thus, for the class of eye-consciousness, form above, below, and on its own level is its object. 'And for the body, both — form and consciousness — come from everywhere' — for a desire-realm body (physical frame), both form and consciousness of its own level and of a higher level arise. For a first-<s>dhyāna</s>-level body, only first-<s>dhyāna</s>-level consciousness [arises]. But form of its own, higher, and lower levels [is its object] — just as the eye supported by it. For a body of the second and higher <s>dhyānas</s>, only consciousness of a lower level — meaning, of the first <s>dhyāna</s> level alone — [arises]. But form of a second-or-third-<s>dhyāna</s>-level body [Tib. 83a] is of its own, higher, and lower levels — just as the eye supported by it. For a fourth-<s>dhyāna</s>-level body, form is of its own and lower levels — because there is no form above that.

body.text: iti. yathā cakṣur uktam. tathā śrotraṃ vyākhyātavyam. katham ity āha. yatra kāye sthitaḥ śrotreṇa śabdān śṛṇoti. kiṃ tāni kāyaśrotraśabdavijñānāny ekabhūmikāny eva bhavanti. āhosvid anyabhūmikāny api. āha. sarveṣāṃ bhedaḥ. kāmadhātūpapannasya svena śrotreṇa svāṃ śabdāṃ śṛṇvataḥ sarvaṃ svabhūmikaṃ bhavatīti vistareṇa anayā diśātra grantho vaktavyaḥ. yāvad ayaṃ tu niyamaḥ.
body.translated_text: just as the eye has been stated, so the ear should be explained. How? He says: 'Where one, situated in [a certain] body, hears sounds with the ear.' Are the body, ear, sound, and consciousness [all] of one level alone? Or can they be of different levels? He says: 'There is variation among all [of them].' For one born in the desire-realm, hearing his own sounds with his own ear, everything is of one's own level — and so on in detail. The passage should be stated in this direction. Up to: but this is the restriction:

children.text:
na kāyasyādharaṃ śrotram ūrdhvaṃ śabdo na ca śruter
vijñānaṃ cāsya śabdas tu kāyasyobhe ca sarvata
children.translated_text:
'The ear is not of a lower level than the body; sound is not of a higher level than the ear;
nor is consciousness of a higher level; but sound is [available] from everywhere for both body [and ear].'

body.text: iti vistareṇa yojyaṃ. katham iti.
body.translated_text: And the application should be made in detail. How?

children.translated_text: 'The ear is not of a lower level than the body.'

body.text: paṃcabhūmikā hi kāyaśrotraśabdāḥ kāmāvacarā yāvac caturthadhyānabhūmikāḥ. dvibhūmikaṃ ṣrotravijñānaṃ kāmāvacaraṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ ca. tatra yadbhūmikaḥ kāyaḥ. tadbhūmikam ūrdhvabhūmikaṃ vā śrotraṃ bhavati. na tv adharabhūmikam. yadbhūmikaṃ śrotraṃ. tadbhūmiko 'dharabhūmiko vāsya śabdo viṣayo bhavati.
body.translated_text: For body, ear, and sound span five levels — from the desire-realm up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> level. Ear-consciousness spans two levels — the desire-realm and the first <s>dhyāna</s> level. Therein, whichever level the body belongs to, the ear belongs to that level or a higher level, but not a lower level. Whichever level the ear belongs to, sound of that level or a lower level is its object.

children.translated_text: 'Sound is not of a higher level than the ear.'

body.text: na hi kadācid ūrdhvabhūmikaḥ śabdo 'dharabhūmikena śrotreṇa śrotuṃ śakyate.
body.translated_text: For at no time can sound of a higher level be heard by an ear of a lower level.

body.text: ūrdhvaṃ na śrotrasya śabdavat.
body.translated_text: is not of a higher level than the ear, just like sound.

children.text: asya śabdas tu kāyasyobhe ca sarvataḥ.
children.translated_text: 'But for this [ear-consciousness], sound, and for the body, both — from everywhere.'

body.text: asyeti anantaroktasya śrotravijñānasya śabdaḥ sarvato viṣaya ūrdhvam adhaḥ svabhūmau ca. kāyasya cobhe śabdavijñāne sarvato bhavata iti.
body.translated_text: 'Of this' means: sound is the object of the ear-consciousness just mentioned from everywhere — above, below, and on its own level. 'And for the body, both — sound and consciousness — come from everywhere.'

body.text: iti. yathā cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ vā niyamitaṃ na kāyasyādharaṃ cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ vety evamādinā. naivaṃ niyamitaṃ manaḥ. ata evāha. paṃcabhūmike 'pi kāye sarvabhūmikāni manaādīni bhavantīti [Tib. 83b] manodharmamanovijñānāni sarvabhūmikāni kāmāvacarāṇi yāvad bhāvāgrikāṇi. tadyathā kāmadhātūpapanno yadi kāmāvacarān manaso 'nantaraṃ kāmāvacaram eva kāmāvacaradharmālambanaṃ manovijñānam utpādayati. sarvāṇi kāmāvacarāṇi. yadi prathamadhyānabhūmikād yāvad bhavāgrabhūmikād upapattikāle samāpattikāle vā saṃbhavataḥ kāmāvacaraṃ tathaiva manovijñānam utpādayati. manas tatastyam. śeṣāni kāmāvacarāṇi. atha tatraiva tadvijñānam utpādayati. dharmās tv ālambanaṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikā yāvad bhavāgrabhūmikāḥ. dharmās tatastyāḥ. śeṣāṇi pūrvavat. evaṃ prathamadhyānopapanno yāvad bhavāgropapanno yathāyogaṃ vaktavyaḥ.
body.translated_text: just as the eye or ear is restricted — 'the eye is not of a lower level than the body,' 'the ear is not,' etc. — the mind is not so restricted. Therefore he says: 'Even for a body of five levels, mind and the rest are of all levels' [Tib. 83b] — the mind-element, <s>dharma</s>-element, and mental-consciousness are of all levels — from the desire-realm up to the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). For example, one born in the desire-realm: if, from a desire-realm mind, one produces another desire-realm mental consciousness with desire-realm <s>dharmas</s> as its object, all are desire-realm. If, from a first-<s>dhyāna</s>-level [mind] up to a summit-of-existence-level [mind], at the time of rebirth or attainment, where possible, one produces desire-realm mental consciousness likewise, the mind belongs to that [level]. The rest are desire-realm. But if one produces that consciousness right there [on that level], the <s>dharmas</s> as object are of the first <s>dhyāna</s> level up to the summit of existence. The <s>dharmas</s> belong to that [level]. The rest are as before. Likewise, one born in the first <s>dhyāna</s> up to one born at the summit of existence should be stated as appropriate.

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

children.text: cakṣuś ca dharmadhātoś ca pradeśo dṛṣṭir
children.translated_text: '<s>Dṛṣṭi</s> (seeing) is the eye and a portion of the <s>dharma-dhātu</s>' —

body.text: ity etad ādhikārikam. atha yatra kāye sthitaś cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi paśyatīty evamādir ayam ānuṣaṃgikaḥ prasaṃgaḥ. darśanasambandhād āgatatvāt.
body.translated_text: this is the principal topic. But 'where one, situated in [a certain] body, sees forms with the eye' — etc. — this is the incidental discussion, because it arose in connection with the topic of seeing.

children.translated_text: 'The five external [dhātus] are cognizable by two [types of consciousness]' —

body.text: iti. paṃcagrahaṇaṃ dharmadhātunirākaraṇārtham. bāhyagrahaṇaṃ cakṣurādinirāsārtham. bāhyā eva paṃca dvivijñeyā ity avadhāraṇād anye trayodaśa dhātava ekavijñānavijñeyā iti siddham. paṃcavijñānakāyānām aviṣayatvāt.
body.translated_text: the term 'five' is for the purpose of excluding the <s>dharma-dhātu</s>. The term 'external' is for the purpose of excluding the eye, etc. By the restriction 'only the five external ones are cognizable by two,' it is established that the other thirteen <s>dhātus</s> are cognizable by one consciousness only — because they are not the object of the five consciousness-groups.

body.text: iti. asaṃskṛtā eva nityā ity avadhāraṇam. adhvasaṃcārābhāvāt nityāḥ.
body.translated_text: the restriction is: 'only the unconditioned are permanent.' Because of the absence of passage through the time-periods, they are permanent.

children.text: dharmārdha indriyaṃ ye ca [Tib. 84a] dvādaśādhyātmikāḥ smṛtā
children.translated_text: 'Half of the <s>dharma</s> [-<s>dhātu</s>] is a faculty, and those [Tib. 84a] twelve [that are] remembered as internal' —

body.text: iti. dhātava ity adhikāraḥ. dvāviṃśatīndriyāṇy uktāni sūtra iti. atha jātiśroṇo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ. upasaṃkramya bahagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisāryaikante nyaṣīdat. ekāntaniṣaṇṇo jātiśroṇo brāhmaṇo bhagavantam idam avocat. indriyāṇīndriyāṇīti bho gautama ucyante. kati bho gautama indriyāṇi. kiyatā cendriyāṇāṃ saṃgraho bhavati. dvāviṃśatir imāni brāhmaṇa indriyāṇi. katamāni dvāviṃśatiḥ. cakṣurindriyaṃ śrotrendriyaṃ ghrāṇendriyaṃ jihvendriyaṃ kāyendriyaṃ manaindriyaṃ strīndriyaṃ puruṣendriyaṃ jīvitendriyaṃ sukhendriyaṃ duḥkhendriyaṃ saumanasyendriyaṃ daurmanasyendriyam upekṣendriyaṃ
body.translated_text: <s>dhātus</s> is the governing topic. 'Twenty-two faculties (<s>indriyas</s>) are stated in the <s>sūtra</s>' — thus: <s>Jātiśroṇa</s> the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> approached the Blessed One and, having approached, exchanged with the Blessed One various polite and agreeable words of conversation. Having sat down to one side, <s>Jātiśroṇa</s> the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said to the Blessed One: 'Faculties, faculties,' it is said, O <s>Gautama</s>. How many faculties are there, O <s>Gautama</s>? And what is the classification of the faculties? 'There are, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, twenty-two faculties. What twenty-two? The eye-faculty, ear-faculty, nose-faculty, tongue-faculty, body-faculty, mind-faculty, female faculty, male faculty, life-faculty, pleasure-faculty, pain-faculty, joy-faculty, displeasure-faculty, equanimity-faculty,

body.text: śraddhendriyaṃ vīryendriyaṃ smṛtīndriyaṃ samādhīndriyaṃ prajñendriyam anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyam ājñendriyam ājñātāvīndriyam. itīmāni brāhmaṇa dvāviṃśatir indriyāṇi. iyatā indriyāṇām indriyasaṃgraho bhavati. atha jātiśroṇo brāhmaṇo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrānta iti.
body.translated_text: faith-faculty, energy-faculty, mindfulness-faculty, concentration-faculty, wisdom-faculty, the faculty of 'I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown' (<s>anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriya</s>), the faculty of knowledge (<s>ājñendriya</s>), and the faculty of one who has known (<s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>). These, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, are the twenty-two faculties. To this extent is the classification of faculties.' Then <s>Jātiśroṇa</s> the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having rejoiced in and approved of the Blessed One's words, departed from the Blessed One's presence.

body.text: iti dharmadhātvekadeśa ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: means 'a portion of the <s>dharma-dhātu</s>.'

body.text: iti napuṃsakanirdeśena kecit paṭhanti. teṣāṃ pāṭhe ardhadharma iti samapravibhāgaḥ prāpnoti. ardhaṃ napuṃsakam iti lakṣaṇāt. ardhapippalīti yathā. atha napuṃsakaliṃgo 'py ardhaśabda ekadeśārthe vartate tadaivaṃ samāsaḥ kriyate. dharmaś cāsāv ardhaṃ ca dharmārdham. dharme vārdhaṃ dharmārdham iti. ābhidhārmikās tu ṣaḍāyatanavyavasthām anādṛtyeti. cakṣurāyatanaṃ yāvat kāyāyatanaṃ [Tib. 84b] manaāyatanam iti ṣaḍāyatanam iti ṣaḍāyatanavyavasthāṃ yuktarūpām anādṛtya jīvitendriyānantaraṃ manaindriyaṃ paṭhanti. sālambanatvāt. vedanendriyādīni hi sālambanāni anantaraṃ paṭhanti. jīvitendriyādīny ekādaśeti. jīvitendriyaṃ vedanendriyāṇi paṃca śraddhādīni ceti. trayāṇāṃ ca bhāga iti. ājñāsyāmīndriyādīnāṃ navadravyātmakānāṃ. manaindriyaṃ muktvānyāny aṣṭau dravyāṇi dharmadhātvekadeśaḥ. cakṣurādayaḥ paṃca svanāmoktā iti. paṃca cakṣurādayo dhātavaḥ paṃcendriyāṇi cakṣurindriyaṃ yāvat kāyendriyaṃ. strīpuruṣendriye ca kāyendriyaikadeśa eveti. paṃca cakṣurādidhātavaḥ saptendriyāṇi bhavanti. sapta cittadhātavo manaindriyam iti. evaṃ dvādaśādhyātmikā dhātavo 'ṣṭāv indriyāṇi bhavantīti. dvādaśādhyātmikā dhātava eva dharmārdha eva cendriyam iti avadhāraṇāt paṃca dhātavo rūpādayas tadanyadharmadhātupradeśo nendriyam iti siddham.
body.translated_text: some read it in the neuter form. In their reading, 'half-<s>dharma</s>' (<s>ardhadharma</s>) would result in an equal division — because of the rule 'half is neuter' — as in '<s>ardhapippalī</s>' (half a peppercorn). But if the word '<s>ardha</s>' in the neuter also operates in the sense of 'a portion,' then the compound is formed thus: '<s>dharma</s> and <s>ardha</s> (portion)' = <s>dharmārdha</s> [a karmadhāraya]; or, '<s>ardha</s> (portion) in <s>dharma</s>' = <s>dharmārdha</s> [a tatpuruṣa]. But the <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> (Abhidharma scholars), disregarding the arrangement of the six sense-bases [in the sūtra] — [Tib. 84b] namely, eye sense-base up to body sense-base, then mind sense-base — [instead] read the mind-faculty immediately after the life-faculty, because of having objects (<s>sālambana</s>). For the feeling-faculties, etc. that have objects are read immediately after [the mind-faculty]. 'The eleven beginning with the life-faculty' — the life-faculty, the five feeling-faculties, and the [five] beginning with faith, etc. 'And a portion of the three' — of the three faculties beginning with the 'I-shall-come-to-know' faculty, which consist of nine substances. Excluding the mind-faculty, the other eight substances are a portion of the <s>dharma-dhātu</s>. 'The five beginning with the eye are designated by their own names.' The five <s>dhātus</s> beginning with the eye are five faculties — the eye-faculty up to the body-faculty. And the female and male faculties are only portions of the body-faculty. Thus the five <s>dhātus</s> beginning with the eye are seven faculties. 'The seven mind-<s>dhātus</s> are the mind-faculty.' Thus, the twelve internal <s>dhātus</s> are eight faculties. By the restriction 'only the twelve internal <s>dhātus</s> and only a portion of the <s>dharma</s>[-<s>dhātu</s>] are faculties,' it is established that the five <s>dhātus</s> beginning with form, and the other portion of the <s>dharma-dhātu</s>, are not faculties.

body.text: ācāryayaśomitrakṛtau sphuṭārthāyām abhidharmakośavyākhyāyāṃ dhātunirdeśo nāma prathamaṃ kośasthānam.
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sphutārthā</s>, the Commentary on the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s> composed by <s>Ācārya Yaśomitra</s>, [this concludes] the first section of the <s>Kośa</s>, entitled 'The Exposition of Elements' (<s>dhātu-nirdeśa</s>).

II
(indriyanirdeśo nāma dvitīyaṃ kośasthānam)
body.translated_text:
II
(The second section of the <s>Kośa</s>, entitled 'The Exposition of Faculties' (<s>indriya-nirdeśa</s>))

body.text: (II.1) uktānīndriyāṇīti. prathamasya dvitīyasya ca kośasthānasya sambandhopanipātatāṃ darśayann āha. uktānīndriyāṇīti. prathamakośasthānāvasāne yasmād
body.translated_text: (II.1) 'The faculties have been stated' — showing the connection between the first and second sections of the <s>Kośa</s>, he says: 'The faculties have been stated.' Since, at the conclusion of the first section of the <s>Kośa</s>,

body.text: ity uktam. tasmād idam āyātam iti sambandhaḥ. [Tib. 85a] kaḥ punar indriyārtha iti. vaiyākaraṇair anyathā indriyaśabdārthavyutpattiḥ kṛteti. ataḥ praśnayati. kaḥ punar indriyārtha iti. idi paramaiśvarye iti paṭhyate. tasya dhātor indantītīndriyāṇīti rūpaṃ draṣṭavyam. kathaṃ kṛtvā. indantīti indrāṇi rapratyaya auṇādikaḥ. indrāṇy evendriyāṇīti svārthe ghastaddhitaḥ. atha vā indantītīndriyam. bahutvāt tu bahuvacanena kṛto nirdeśa indantītīndriyāṇīti. tasmāt indantīty asya śabdasya indriyam ity ādeśaḥ. katham. avarṇasya rabhāvaḥ tiśabdasya ceyādeśaḥ. tena nairuktena vidhānena indriyam iti bhavati. tadyathā kuñjara iti. vaiyākaraṇair hi kuñjo 'syāstīti kuñjara iti matvarthīyena kuñjaraśabdo vyutpādyate. nairuktais tu tad anādṛtya kuñjaraḥ kuñjacāritvād iti nairuktena nyāyena sādhyate. tadvad ihāpi draṣṭavyam. yadi hi vaiyākaraṇanayena indrasya liṅgam indriyam iti vyutpādyeta. ādhipatyārtha indriyārtho hīyetādhipatyārthaś ceṣyate. tasmād ittham indriyaśabdasya vyutpattir naiṣṭavyeti. dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca viṣamaparivarjanād iti. dṛṣṭvā śvabhrādi śrutvā ca vyāghrādirutam. śvabhrādivyāghrādirutaviṣamaparivarjanāt. sasaṃprayogayor iti sacaitasikayoḥ. rūpadarśanaśabdaśravaṇayoś ceti. cakṣuḥ paśyati śrotraṃ śṛṇotītyādi vaibhāṣikāṇāṃ siddhāntaḥ. tenālambanaviśeṣalakṣaṇayor darśanaśravaṇayor asādhāraṇakāraṇatve cakṣuḥśrotrayor ādhipatyam.
body.translated_text: Thus it has been stated. Therefore the connection is: 'from this it has come.' [Tib. 85a] 'What then is the meaning of <s>indriya</s> (faculty)?' — The grammarians (<s>vaiyākaraṇa</s>) have given a different etymological derivation of the word <s>indriya</s>; therefore he raises the question: 'What then is the meaning of <s>indriya</s>?' The root '<s>idi</s>' is taught in the sense of supreme sovereignty (<s>paramaiśvarya</s>). The form should be understood as: '<s>indanti</s> (they exercise sovereignty), therefore they are <s>indriyāṇi</s>.' How so? '<s>Indanti</s>' — hence '<s>indrāṇi</s>,' with the <s>ra</s>-suffix being an <s>auṇādika</s> formation. '<s>Indrāṇi</s> are themselves <s>indriyāṇi</s>' — the <s>gha</s> <s>taddhita</s> suffix is used in its reflexive sense. Alternatively, '<s>indanti</s>' — hence '<s>indriyam</s>.' But the plural expression '<s>indanti</s> — hence <s>indriyāṇi</s>' is made because of their multiplicity. Therefore, '<s>indriyam</s>' is a substitution for the word '<s>indanti</s>.' How? The <s>a</s>-vowel undergoes replacement by <s>ra</s>, and the syllable <s>ti</s> is replaced by <s>iya</s>. By that <s>nairukta</s> (etymological) method, the form '<s>indriyam</s>' is obtained. Just as with the word '<s>kuñjara</s>' (elephant): the grammarians derive the word '<s>kuñjara</s>' by the possessive suffix — '<s>kuñja</s> (thicket) exists for it, hence <s>kuñjara</s>.' But the etymologists (<s>nairuktāḥ</s>), disregarding that, derive it by the <s>nairukta</s> method: '<s>kuñjara</s> because it moves in thickets (<s>kuñjacāritvāt</s>).' The same should be understood here as well. For if one were to derive <s>indriya</s> by the grammarians' method — '<s>indriyam</s>' as the mark of <s>Indra</s>' — then the meaning of <s>indriya</s> as sovereignty (<s>ādhipatya</s>) would be lost, and sovereignty is the desired meaning. Therefore, the derivation of the word <s>indriya</s> should be done in this way. 'By having seen and heard, one avoids danger' — having seen pits and the like, and having heard the sounds of tigers and the like, one avoids the danger of pits, tigers, and the like. 'Of the two together with their associates' means of the two together with their mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>). 'And of seeing form and hearing sound' — 'The eye sees, the ear hears' — this is the established position of the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>. Therefore, in the distinctive apprehension of objects (<s>ālambana</s>) — i.e., seeing and hearing — the eye and ear have sovereignty as the uncommon cause.

body.text: ātmabhāvaśobhāyāṃ pūrvavad [Tib. 85b] iti. aghrāṇādīnāṃ sattvānām akāntarūpatvāt. akāntātmabhāvatvād ity arthaḥ. taiḥ kavaḍīkārāhāraparibhogād iti. tair ghrāṇādibhis tatparibhogād iti. kathaṃ gandhasya kavadīkārāhāratvam. nāsikayor gandhagrāsavyavacchedena kavaḍīkaraṇāt. kathaṃ spraṣṭavyasya kavaḍīkārāhāratvam. kāyena snānābhyaṅgādikaspraṣṭavyasya romakūpamukhagrāsavyavacchedena kavaḍīkaraṇāt.
body.translated_text: 'In the beauty of one's bodily existence, as before' [Tib. 85b] — because beings without smell-faculty and the rest have unattractive forms; meaning: because they have unattractive bodily existence. 'Because of the enjoyment of morsel-food (<s>kavaḍīkārāhāra</s>) by those [faculties]' — because of the enjoyment of that [food] by the smell-faculty and the rest. How is smell a morsel-food (<s>kavaḍīkārāhāra</s>)? Because of the making-into-morsels through the delineation of smell-portions at the two nostrils. How is the tangible a morsel-food? Because of the making-into-morsels through the delineation of tangible portions at the openings of the hair-pores by the body, [in cases such as] bathing, anointing, and the like.

body.text: kilaśabdaḥ paramatadyotane. svamatam asya paścād vakṣyate.
body.translated_text: The word <s>kila</s> indicates another's view. His own view will be stated later.

body.text: iti pratyekam abhisambandhaḥ. sattvabhedaḥ strīpuruṣa iti. strīty eko nikāyasabhāgaḥ. puruṣa ity aparaḥ. tayor bhedaḥ. sattvavikalpa iti stanādeḥ saṃsthānasya svarasyācārasya cānyathātvaṃ viśeṣa ity arthaḥ. saṃkleśavyavadānayor ity apara iti pūrvācāryaḥ. na sattvabhedavikalpayoḥ. antareṇāpi puruṣendriyaṃ rūpāvacarāṇāṃ vikalpasiddheḥ. vikalpakṛtaś ca sattvabheda ity abhiprāyaḥ. tadviyuktavikalānām iti. viyuktāś ca te vikalāś ca viyuktavikalāḥ. tābhyāṃ strīpuruṣendriyābhyāṃ viyuktavikalās tadviyuktavikalāḥ. ke. ṣaṇḍhapaṇḍakobhayavyañjanāḥ. tadviyuktāḥ ṣaṇḍhapaṇḍakāḥ. teṣāṃ strīpuruṣendriyābhāvāt. ṣaṇḍhapaṇḍakānāṃ [Tib. 86a] punaḥ kaḥ prativiśeṣaḥ. ṣaṇḍhakāḥ svabhāvato niḥstrīpuruṣendriyāḥ. paṇḍakā upakrameṇopahatendriyāḥ. vinaye tu paṇḍakā eva paṃca paṭhyaṃte. prakṛtipaṇḍakaḥ. īrṣyāpaṇḍakaḥ. pakṣapaṇḍakaḥ. āsekapaṇḍakaḥ. lūnapaṇḍakaś ceti. tatra prakṛtipaṇḍakaḥ ṣaṇḍha ihābhipretaḥ. yasya hi prakṛtyā vyañjanaṃ nāsti. sa prakṛtipaṇḍakaḥ. śeṣā iha paṇḍakā iṣyante. lūnapaṇḍako hi tāvad indriyacchedāt indriyavikala iti sphuṭa eṣaḥ. pakṣapaṇḍakādayas tv indriyākarmaṇyatvena tadvikalā eva. indriyakarmaṇyatvakāle 'pi tadvikalā iti vyavasthāpyanta eva. tadindriyakarmaṇyatvasya puruṣasukhaviśeṣājanakatvāt prasavājanakatvāc ca. indriyasadbhāvāśaṃkānivṛttyartham eva ceha ṣaṇḍhapaṇḍakā iti pṛthakpāṭhaḥ. anyathā hi vinayavad ihāpy abhidharme paṇḍakā ity eva paṭhyeran. ubhayavyañjanās tadvikalāḥ. sthānabhraṃśavaikalyād alpasukhahetutvavaikalyāc ca. apare vyācakṣate. tadviyuktāḥ ṣaṇḍhāḥ. tadvikalāḥ paṇḍakāḥ. upakramavaikalyāt. ubhayavyañjanāś ca tadvikalāḥ. sthānabhraṃśavaikalyāt. alpasukhahetutvavaikalyāc ceti. teṣām asaṃvarādīni na bhavanti.
body.translated_text: the connection is to be made separately [with each]. 'The differentiation of beings is female and male' — '<s>strī</s>' (female) is one type of class-homogeneity (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>); '<s>puruṣa</s>' (male) is another. Their differentiation [is meant]. 'Variation of beings' means that the difference in bodily configuration such as breasts and so forth, in voice, and in conduct is the distinguishing characteristic — this is the meaning. 'In defilement and purification — another [view]' is that of earlier masters (<s>pūrvācārya</s>). Not of the differentiation and variation of beings. Because even without the male faculty, the variation of <s>Rūpāvacara</s> (form-realm) beings is established. And the differentiation of beings is produced by variation — this is the intent. 'Of those separated from and deficient in those' — those who are separated (<s>viyukta</s>) and deficient (<s>vikala</s>) are <s>viyuktavikala</s>; those who are separated from and deficient in those two — the female and male faculties — are <s>tadviyuktavikala</s>. Who are they? <s>Ṣaṇḍhas</s> (eunuchs by nature), <s>paṇḍakas</s> (eunuchs by intervention), and those with both characteristics (<s>ubhayavyañjana</s>). The <s>tadviyukta</s> (separated from those) are the <s>ṣaṇḍhas</s> and <s>paṇḍakas</s>, because they lack the female and male faculties. [Tib. 86a] What then is the distinction between <s>ṣaṇḍhas</s> and <s>paṇḍakas</s>? <s>Ṣaṇḍhas</s> are by nature without the female or male faculty. <s>Paṇḍakas</s> have their faculty impaired by intervention. But in the <s>Vinaya</s>, five types of <s>paṇḍakas</s> are enumerated: the natural <s>paṇḍaka</s> (<s>prakṛtipaṇḍaka</s>), the jealousy-<s>paṇḍaka</s> (<s>īrṣyāpaṇḍaka</s>), the half-month <s>paṇḍaka</s> (<s>pakṣapaṇḍaka</s>), the voyeur <s>paṇḍaka</s> (<s>āsekapaṇḍaka</s>), and the castrated <s>paṇḍaka</s> (<s>lūnapaṇḍaka</s>). Among these, the natural <s>paṇḍaka</s> is what is here intended as a <s>ṣaṇḍha</s> — for the one who by nature lacks the characteristic mark is the natural <s>paṇḍaka</s>. The rest are here considered <s>paṇḍakas</s>. The castrated <s>paṇḍaka</s> is clearly deficient in faculty due to the cutting of the organ. The half-month <s>paṇḍaka</s> and the others are deficient in those [faculties] due to the incapacity of the faculty. Even at the time of faculty-capacity, they are established as deficient in those [faculties], because that faculty-capacity does not produce the distinctive pleasure of a man nor does it produce offspring. The separate enumeration of <s>ṣaṇḍhas</s> and <s>paṇḍakas</s> here is precisely for the purpose of removing the doubt about the existence of the faculty. Otherwise, as in the <s>Vinaya</s>, here too in the <s>Abhidharma</s>, they would be enumerated simply as '<s>paṇḍakas</s>.' Those with both characteristics are deficient in those — because of the deficiency of positional displacement and because of the deficiency of being a cause of only slight pleasure. Others explain: the <s>tadviyukta</s> are <s>ṣaṇḍhas</s>; the <s>tadvikala</s> are <s>paṇḍakas</s>, due to deficiency by intervention; and those with both characteristics are <s>tadvikala</s>, due to deficiency of positional displacement and deficiency of being a cause of only slight pleasure. For them, <s>asaṃvara</s> (non-restraint) and the rest do not exist.

children.text:
nṛṇām asaṃvaro hitvā ṣaṇḍhapaṇḍadvidhākṛtīn.
ānantaryaṃ ṣaṇḍhādīnāṃ tu neṣyate
alpopakāryalajjitvāt.
[Tib. 86b] chinatti strī pumān dṛṣṭicarita
children.translated_text:
'Non-restraint exists for humans, excluding <s>ṣaṇḍhas</s>, <s>paṇḍakas</s>, and those of dual form.
But <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous acts) are not accepted for <s>ṣaṇḍhas</s> and the rest,
because of being of little benefit and lacking shame.
[Tib. 86b] A woman or man cuts off view and conduct' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. strīpuruṣāṇāṃ tu tāni bhavanti. ataḥ saṃkleśe ādhipatyaṃ strīpuruṣendriyayoḥ. saṃvaraphalaprāptivairāgyāṇi ceti. saṃvaras trividhaḥ prātimokṣasaṃvaro dhyānasaṃvaro 'nāsravasaṃvaraś ca. teṣām eko 'pi saṃvaro na bhavati kim aṅga sarvaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated. But for women and men, those [restraints] do exist. Therefore, in defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>), the female and male faculties have sovereignty. 'And restraint, fruit-attainment, and dispassion' — restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) is threefold: <s>prātimokṣa</s>-restraint, <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint, and non-outflow (<s>anāsrava</s>) restraint. Not even one of these restraints exists [for them], let alone all. (

body.text: iti vacanāt. ata eva ca srotaāpattyādiphalaprāptiḥ kāmādivairāgyaṃ ca teṣāṃ na saṃbhavati. strīpuruṣāṇāṃ tu bhavatīti. ato vyavadāne 'pi strīpuruśendriyayor ādhipatyam iti. nikāyasabhāgasambandhasaṃdhāraṇayor iti. jīvitendriyasya nikāyasabhāgotpattau. nikāyasabhāgasambandhe tasyādhipatyaṃ vyavasthāpyate. nikāyasabhāgasaṃdhāraṇe cādhipatyam. jīvitendriyavaśena tadūrdhvamavasthānāt. manaindriyasya punarbhavasambandha iti. kliṣṭena punarbhavasambandhāt. jīvitendriyād asya ko viśeṣaḥ. jīvitendriyasya antarābhava eva sambandhanam. manaindriyasya tūpapattibhave 'pi. samānakālaṃ ca jīvitendriyaṃ nikāyasabhāgena tatsambandhanaṃ karoti. manaindriyaṃ tu bhinnakālam api punarbhave tatsambandhanaṃ karoti. vaśibhāvānuvartana iti. cittasya vaśibhāvam anuvartate loko dharmo vā yathoktam. cittenāyaṃ loko nīyata iti vistaraḥ. gāthāyām apy uktam.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated. And for this very reason, the attainment of the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpatti</s>) and so forth, and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) from desire and so forth, are not possible for them. But for women and men they do exist. Therefore, in purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) too, the female and male faculties have sovereignty. 'In the connection and sustaining of class-homogeneity (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>)' — the sovereignty of the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>) is established with respect to the arising of class-homogeneity and the connection with class-homogeneity; and sovereignty in the sustaining of class-homogeneity [is established] because of the continued existence of that [class-homogeneity] by virtue of the life-faculty. As for the mind-faculty (<s>manaindriya</s>), the connection to renewed existence (<s>punarbhava</s>) — [is established] because the afflicted [mind] connects to renewed existence. What is the difference between this and the life-faculty? The life-faculty's connecting pertains only to the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>), whereas the mind-faculty's [connecting pertains] also to the existence of rebirth (<s>upapattibhava</s>). Moreover, the life-faculty produces the connection with class-homogeneity simultaneously, whereas the mind-faculty produces the connection to renewed existence even at different times. 'Conformity to mastery (<s>vaśibhāva</s>)' — the world or the <s>dharma</s> conforms to the mastery of the mind, as has been stated: 'This world is led by the mind' — and so on in detail. And it has been stated in a verse:

children.text:
cittena nīyate lokaś cittena parikṛṣyate
ekadharmasya cittasya [Tib. 87a] sarvadharmā vaśānugā
children.translated_text:
'The world is led by the mind, the world is dragged by the mind;
of this one <s>dharma</s>, the mind, [Tib. 87a] all <s>dharmas</s> follow the control.'

body.text: iti. rāgādīnāṃ tadanuśāyitvād iti. teṣu sukḥādiṣu anuśāyituṃ śīlam eṣām ālambanataḥ saṃprayogato vā. ta ime tadanuśāyino rāgādayaḥ. tadbhāvas tadanuśāyitvam. tasmād iti. yathoktaṃ sukhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ rāgo 'nuśete. duḥkhāyāṃ dvesaḥ. aduḥkhasukhāyāṃ moha iti. tair hi vyavadāyata iti. tair viśudhyatīty arthaḥ. tad evaṃ kleśaviśuddhāv eśāṃ śraddhādīnām ādhipatyam uktaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: Thus. 'Because of the latent tendency of attachment and the rest toward those [feelings]' — it is the disposition of these [attachment and the rest] to lie latent (<s>anuśayitum</s>) in those [feelings of] pleasure and so forth, either as object or as association. These are the attachment and the rest that have latent tendency toward those — their state is 'having latent tendency toward those.' Therefore — as has been stated: 'In pleasant feeling, attachment lies latent; in painful [feeling], aversion [lies latent]; in neither-painful-nor-pleasant [feeling], delusion [lies latent].' 'For by those one is purified' — means: by those one becomes pure. Thus, the sovereignty of faith and the rest in the purification from afflictions has been stated.

body.text: vyavadāne 'pi sukhādīnām ādhipatyam ity apara iti. na kevalaṃ saṃkleśe sukhādīnām ādhipatyaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. vyavadāne 'pīty apiśabdasyārthaḥ. ābhidhārmikāḥ kecid evam āhuḥ. vyavadāne 'pi teṣām ādhipatyam astīti āgamam
body.translated_text: 'In purification too, the sovereignty of pleasure and the rest — [is the view of] another' — not only do pleasure and the rest have sovereignty in defilement; but in purification too — this is the meaning of the word 'too' (<s>api</s>). Some <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> say thus: 'There is sovereignty of those [feelings] in purification too,' and they adduce scripture

body.text: ānayanti. yasmāt sukhitasya cittaṃ samādhīyata ity uktaṃ sūtre. duḥkhopaniṣac chraddhā. duḥkham upaniṣad asyāḥ. seyaṃ śraddhā duḥkhopaniṣat. duḥkhahetukety arthaḥ. duḥkhe sati kasyacid dharme ratnatraye vā śraddhā jāyate. pravrajyāṃ vābhilaṣati. ṣaṇ ṇaiṣkramyāśritāḥ saumanasyādaya iti. ṣaṇ ṇaiṣkramyāśritāni saumanasyāni. ṣaṇ ṇaiṣkramyāśritāni daurmanasyāni. ṣaṇ ṇaiṣkramyāśritā upekṣāḥ. [Tib. 87b] naiṣkramyaṃ sāsravo 'nāsravo mārgaḥ. dhātoḥ saṃsārād vā niṣkramaṇaṃ vairāgyam ity apare. yathoktaṃ sūtre. cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇi pratītyotpadyate saumanasyaṃ naiṣkramyāśritaṃ naiṣkramyālambanam ity arthaḥ. naiṣkramyānukūlam iti vā. evaṃ yāvan manaḥ pratītya dharmāṃś ca utpadyate saumanasyaṃ naiṣkramyāśritam iti. tathā cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇi pratītya utpadyate daurmanasyaṃ naiṣkramyāśritam. evaṃ yāvan manaḥ. tathā cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇi pratītyotpadyate upekṣā naiṣkramyāśritā. evaṃ yāvan manaḥ. naiṣkramyaṃ prāpsyāmīti kasyacit saumanasyam. na naiṣkramyāya mayā yatnaḥ kriyate iti kasyacid daurmanasyam. kasyacit pratisaṃkhyāyopekṣā teṣu rūpādiṣu bhavati.
body.translated_text: : 'Because the mind of one who is happy becomes concentrated' — thus it is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>. 'Faith has suffering as its proximate cause' (<s>duḥkhopaniṣat</s>) — suffering is the proximate cause of this [faith]; this faith has suffering as its proximate cause; meaning: having suffering as its cause. When suffering exists, faith arises in some <s>dharma</s> or in the Three Jewels, or one desires renunciation (<s>pravrajyā</s>). 'The six [feelings] based on renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>) — <s>saumanasya</s> and the rest' — six <s>saumanasyas</s> (mental pleasures) based on renunciation, six <s>daurmanasyas</s> (mental displeasures) based on renunciation, six <s>upekṣās</s> (equanimities) based on renunciation. [Tib. 87b] <s>Naiṣkramya</s> (renunciation) is the outflow-possessing and outflow-free path. Or, going forth from the elements or from <s>saṃsāra</s> is renunciation, i.e., dispassion — according to others. As stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'Dependent on forms cognizable by the eye, there arises mental pleasure based on renunciation' — meaning: having renunciation as its object. Or: 'in conformity with renunciation.' Similarly, up to: 'Dependent on the mind and <s>dharmas</s>, there arises mental pleasure based on renunciation.' Likewise: 'Dependent on forms cognizable by the eye, there arises mental displeasure based on renunciation.' Similarly up to the mind. Likewise: 'Dependent on forms cognizable by the eye, there arises equanimity based on renunciation.' Similarly up to the mind. For someone, mental pleasure arises [thinking]: 'I shall attain renunciation.' For someone, mental displeasure arises [thinking]: 'I have not made effort toward renunciation.' For someone, reflective equanimity toward those forms and so forth arises.

body.text: (II.2-4) apare punar āhur iti sautrāntikāḥ. vijñāya viṣamaparihārād iti. vijñānena viṣamaparihāraḥ kriyate. na cakṣuḥśrotreṇety abhiprāyaḥ. nāpi vijñānād anyad rūpadarśanaṃ śabdaśravaṇaṃ vāstīti. na rūpadarśanaśabdaśravaṇaṃ grahaṇavyatiriktaṃ vicāryamāṇaṃ labhyate. grahaṇaṃ ca vijñānam eveti nānyad bhavati. tasmāc cakṣuḥśrotravijñānayoḥ sasaṃprayogayor utpattau yad ādhipatyam uktam. tad eva tad bhavati. nānyatrādhipatyam etad [Tib. 88a] ity abhiprāyaḥ. manasaḥ punaḥ sarvārthopalabdhāv iti.
body.translated_text: (II.2-4) 'Others, however, say' — the <s>Sautrāntikas</s>. 'By cognizing, one avoids danger' — it is by consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) that the avoidance of danger is accomplished, not by the eye or ear — this is the intent. 'Nor is there any seeing of form or hearing of sound apart from consciousness' — upon investigation, no seeing of form or hearing of sound distinct from apprehension is found. And apprehension is consciousness itself — hence there is nothing else. Therefore, the sovereignty that was stated for the arising of the two — eye-consciousness and ear-consciousness — together with their associates, that alone is that [sovereignty]. 'There is no sovereignty elsewhere' — [Tib. 88a] this is the intent. 'But for the mind, in the apprehension of all objects' —

children.translated_text: 'Because of sovereignty in the apprehension of its own object' —

body.text: ity eva siddhe manasaḥ sarvārthopalabdhāv iti vacanaṃ dharmadhātor asarvadharmasvabhāvatvāt. vyākhyātaṃ caitat purastāt. nanu cārthānām apy atrādhipatyam iti. dvayaṃ pratītya vijñānasyotpattir iti vacanāt. adhikaṃ hi prabhutvam ādhipatyam iti. adhikaḥ prabhur adhipatis tadbhāva ādhipatyam iti. sarvarūpopalabdhau sāmānyakāraṇatvād iti. nīlapītādisarvarūpopalabdhau ekarūpasya cakṣuṣaḥ karaṇatvāt. na tu rūpasyaikarūpasya nīlapītadisarvarūpopalabdhau kāraṇatvam. na hi nīlarūpaṃ pītarūpopalabdhau kāraṇaṃ bhavati. tatpaṭumandatādyanuvidhānāc copalabdher iti. yasmād upalabdhiś cakṣurādipaṭumandatām anuvidhatte. tadyathā paṭuni cakṣuṣi paṭvī tadupalabdhiḥ. mande mandeti. ādiśabdena akuśalakuśalasavedanāvedanānuvidhānaṃ.
body.translated_text: since this alone is already established, the statement 'in the apprehension of all objects by the mind' is because the <s>dharma-dhātu</s> does not have the nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. And this has been explained before. 'But surely objects too have sovereignty here' — because of the statement: 'Dependent on the dyad [of faculty and object], consciousness arises.' For sovereignty means superior power (<s>prabhutvam</s>). 'Superior' (<s>adhika</s>) is the overlord (<s>adhipati</s>); the state of that is sovereignty (<s>ādhipatyam</s>). 'Because of being a general cause for the apprehension of all forms' — because the one eye is the instrument for the apprehension of all forms — blue, yellow, and the rest — but a single form, being of one kind, is not the cause for the apprehension of all forms — blue, yellow, and the rest. For a blue form is not the cause for the apprehension of a yellow form. 'And because apprehension conforms to the sharpness, dullness, and so forth of that [faculty]' — because apprehension conforms to the sharpness and dullness of the eye and the rest. For example, when the eye is sharp, the apprehension based on it is sharp; when dull, [it is] dull. By the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), [we understand] the conformity to unwholesome, wholesome, with-feeling, and without-feeling [states].

body.text: akuśale manasy akuśalopalabdhiḥ. kuśale kuśalā. savedane savedanā. avedane 'vedaneti. na rūpasya paṭumandatādy anuvidhatte upalabdhiḥ. tenāha. tadviparyayād iti. tasmāc cakṣurādīnām adhikam aiśvaryaṃ [Tib. 88b] na rūpādīnām.
body.translated_text: When the mind is unwholesome, the apprehension is unwholesome; when wholesome, [it is] wholesome; when with feeling, [it is] with feeling; when without feeling, [it is] without feeling. Apprehension does not conform to the sharpness, dullness, and so forth of the object. Therefore he says: 'And from the opposite [being the case for objects].' Therefore, the eye and the rest have superior sovereignty — not forms and the rest.

children.translated_text: 'The female and male faculties [arise] from the body' —

body.text: iti. atra sādhanam. kāyendriyasvabhāvaṃ strīpuruṣendriyam. spraṣṭavyavijñānajanakatvāt. astrīpuruṣendriyasvabhāvakāyendriyavat. vaidharmyeṇa cakṣurindriyavat. stryākṛtisvaraceṣṭābhiprāyā iti. stryabhiprāyapuruṣābhiprāyayor viparyayeṇa. tad evaṃ sati sattvavikalpa eva strīpuruṣendriyayor ādhipatyam. nikāyasabhāgasthitau jīvitendriyasyādhipatyam. na tu vaibhāṣikavat nikāyasabhāgasambandhe. tatra manasa evādhipatyāt. saṃkleśe vedanānām iti. atra vaibhāṣikaiḥ sārdham aikamatyam. tathā hi tair iti vistaraḥ. tathā hi taiḥ śraddhādibhiḥ kleśāś ca viṣkaṃbhyante laukikamārgagatair mārgaś cāvāhyate nirvedhabhāgīyādigataiḥ. tad evaṃ vyavadānasaṃbhāre śraddhādīnāṃ pratyekam ādhipatyam uktaṃ bhavati. na hy avimuktacittasyāsti parinirvāṇam iti. ājñātāvīndriyaṃ kṣayajñānādy anāsravam indriyaṃ. tad eva ca vimuktaṃ kleśavimuktyā saṃtānavimuktyā ca. tatprāptasya nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇaṃ bhavati. tasmād ājñātāvīndriyasya nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa ādhipatyaṃ vyavasthāpyate. dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāraṃ pratīti [Tib.89a] vistaraḥ. dṛṣṭo dharmo dṛṣṭadharmaḥ. dṛṣṭajanmety arthaḥ. sukho vihāraḥ sukhavihāraḥ. dṛṣṭadharme sukhavihāraḥ dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāraḥ. taṃ praty ājñātāvīndriyasyādhipatyam. vimuktiprītisukhapratisaṃvedanād iti. vimuktiḥ kleśaprahāṇam. prītiḥ saumanasyam. sukhaṃ praśrabdhisukham. vimuktyā prītisukhasya pratisaṃvedanaṃ vimuktiprītisukhapratisaṃvedanam. tasmād iti. tad uktaṃ bhavati. vimuktiprītisukhapratisaṃvedanam eva dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra iti.
body.translated_text: Thus. Here the proof [is as follows]: the female and male faculties have the nature of the body-faculty, because they produce tactile consciousness — like the body-faculty that does not have the nature of the female or male faculty. By dissimilarity, like the eye-faculty. 'The appearance, voice, conduct, and inclination of a woman' — with the reverse for [those of] a man. This being so, the dominion of the female and male faculties is precisely over the differentiation of beings. The life-faculty has dominion over the duration of the <s>nikāyasabhāga</s> (class-homogeneity). But not, as the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> [hold], over the connection with the <s>nikāyasabhāga</s> — for therein, the mind alone has dominion. 'In defilement, the feelings [have dominion]' — here there is agreement with the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>. 'For thus, by those' — and so on in detail. For by those [faculties] — faith and the rest — afflictions are suppressed when [they are] in the mundane path, and the [supramundane] path is brought in when [they are] in the [stages of] the aids to penetration and so forth. Thus, the individual dominion of faith and the rest in the equipment for purification has been stated. 'For there is no <s>parinirvāṇa</s> for one whose mind is not liberated.' The <s>ājñātāvīndriya</s> (the faculty of the one who has fully known) is a non-outflow faculty such as the knowledge of destruction and the like. And that very [faculty] is 'liberated' — through liberation from afflictions and through liberation of the continuum. For one who has attained that, there is <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder. Therefore, the dominion of the <s>ājñātāvīndriya</s> is established as [pertaining to] <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder. 'With regard to the pleasant abiding in the present life' — [Tib. 89a] and so on in detail. 'The present life' (<s>dṛṣṭadharma</s>) means 'the dharma that is seen' — meaning 'the present birth.' 'Pleasant abiding' (<s>sukhavihāra</s>) is an abiding in happiness. 'Pleasant abiding in the present life' (<s>dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra</s>) is pleasant abiding in the present life. The <s>ājñātāvīndriya</s> has dominion with regard to that. 'Because of the experiencing of the happiness of the joy of liberation' — liberation is the abandonment of afflictions; joy (<s>prīti</s>) is mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>); happiness (<s>sukha</s>) is the happiness of tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>). The experiencing of the happiness of joy through liberation is 'the experiencing of the happiness of the joy of liberation.' Therefore — what has been said is this: the experiencing of the happiness of the joy of liberation is itself the pleasant abiding in the present life.

body.text: (II.5) vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthānām api cendriyatvam upasaṃkhyātavyam iti. sāṃkhyāś cakṣurindriyādivyatiriktāni vāgindriyādīni kalpayanti. vāgindriyaṃ yena vacanaṃ kriyate. pāṇīndriyaṃ yena kiṃcid dravyam ādīyate. pādendriyaṃ yena viharaṇaṃ kriyate. caṃkramaṇam ity arthaḥ. pāyvindriyaṃ yena purīṣotsargaḥ kriyate. upasthendriyaṃ kāyendriyaikadeśavyatiriktaṃ yenānandaḥ sukhaviśeṣaḥ prāpyate. na khalūpasaṃkhyātavyam avidyādīnām indriyatvam. yenārthena bhagavatā dvāviṃśatir indriyāṇy uktāni. tatrāvidyādīnām ayogāt. ko 'sāv artha ity āha.
body.translated_text: (II.5) 'The faculties of speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals should also be counted' — the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> postulate faculties of speech and the rest that are distinct from the eye-faculty and the rest. The speech-faculty is that by which utterance is made; the hand-faculty is that by which an object is grasped;

children.translated_text: 'The basis of mind and its differentiation' —

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. cittasyāśrayas tadāśrayasya vikalpaḥ
body.translated_text: this is the elaboration. The basis of mind — the differentiation of that basis.

body.text: vyavadāna-
body.translated_text: purifica-

body.text: etac ca ṣaḍāyatanaṃ maulaṃ sattvadravyam [Tib. 89b] iti. taditareṣāṃ tadāśritatvāt. tathā hi ṣaḍindriyādhipatyasaṃbhūtam indriyādhiṣṭhānam. ṣaḍ vā viṣayā vijñānakāyāś ca. tad etad api sattvadravyam iṣyate na tu maulam. na hy adhiṣṭhānādyādhipatyasaṃbhūtaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam iti. vyavadānasaṃbharaṇaṃ paṃcabhir iti śraddhādibhiḥ. vyavadānaṃ tribhir iti. anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyādibhiḥ.
body.translated_text: 'And this sixfold sense-base is the primary substance of a being' [Tib. 89b] — because the others depend on it. For the station of the faculties arises from the dominion of the six faculties. Or, the six objects and the consciousness-groups [also constitute the substance of a being]. This too is accepted as the substance of a being.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. pravṛttipakṣaṃ nivṛttipakṣaṃ cādhikṛtyocyate.
body.translated_text: this is the elaboration. [This] is stated with reference to both the activity-side and the cessation-side.

body.text: saṃsārasyāśraya utpattiḥ
body.translated_text: the basis [for] the arising of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence),

body.text: nivṛtter api nirvāṇasyāśraya utpattiḥ sthitir upabhogaś ca. etāvatā ca puruṣārthaparisamāptir iti. nirarthikā tadanyendriyaprajñaptiḥ. bhavatām api puruṣārthaparisamāptiḥ paṭhyate. tasya śabdādyupalabdhir ādir guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhir anta iti. tatra ṣaḍāyatanaṃ mūlasattvadravyabhūtaṃ saṃsaratīti pravṛtter āśrayaḥ. utpattiḥ strīpuruṣendriye iti. utpadyate 'syā ity utpattiḥ. kasmād ity āha. tata utpatteḥ. kasya. ṣaḍāyatanasya. manaḥkāyendriyayoḥ sākṣāt tābhyām utpatteḥ. cakṣurādīnāṃ caturṇāṃ krameṇotpatteḥ. sthitir jīvitendriyeṇa ṣaḍāyatanāvasthānāt. upabhogo vedanābhiḥ sukhādibhiḥ. śraddhādayo hi nivṛtter āśraya iti. śraddhādīnāṃ pratiṣṭhābhūtatvāt. ājñāsyāmīndriyaṃ prabhava ity ādibhavaḥ prathamato 'nāsravotpatteḥ. [Tib. 90a] sthitir ājñendriyaṃ prābandhikatvāt. upabhoga ājñātāvīndriyeṇeti. tena vimuktiprītisukhapratisaṃvedanāt. ata etāvanty evendriyāṇīti nāvidyādīnām indriyatvam iṣṭam ity arthaḥ. ata eva caiṣāṃ eṣo 'nukrama iti. cakṣurindriyaṃ yāvad ājñātāvīndriyam iti pravṛttinivṛttyor āśrayādibhāvāt. vācas tu nendriyatvam. vacane śikṣāviśeṣāpekṣatvāt. jātamātro hi bālako vinaiva śikṣayā cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi paśyati. na tv evaṃ vacanaṃ karoti. tasmād indriyadharmātikrāntatvāt. na vāg indriyaṃ bhavitum arhati. jihvendriyādhiṣṭhānasyaiva tu etat karma vacanam
body.translated_text: 'Of cessation too — the basis [for] the arising, duration, and enjoyment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And with this much, the complete fulfillment of human purposes [is achieved].' Therefore, the designation of any other faculties is purposeless. '[Objection:] For you too, the complete fulfillment of human purposes is recited.' His perception of sound and the rest

body.text: iti. pāṇipādasya cādānaviharaṇād ananyatvād iti. pāṇir eva hy anyathānyatra cotpanna ādānam ucyate. pāda eva cānyathānyatra cotpanno viharaṇam iti. karmābhāvāt. svātmani ca vṛttivirodhāt. na pāṇipādasyendriyatvam. uragaprabhṛtīnām iti. sarpādīnāṃ pāṇipādaṃ nāsti. atha ca teṣām ādānaviharaṇaṃ bhavati na pāṇipādasyendriyatvam. teṣām apy asti sūkṣmam iti cet. na. sādhyatvāt. pāyor api nendriyatvam utsarga ity aśucyutsarge. gurudravyasya yasya kasyacid ākāśe chidre sarvatra pāyusthānād anyatrāpi patanāt. gurudravyasya gurutvād evaṃ svayaṃ patanaṃ nendriyakṛtam. vāyunā ca tatpreraṇād iti. vāyunā tasya guror aśucidravyasya preraṇā. [Tib. 90b] vāyor eva tat karma syān na pāyvindriyasya. tadanupalabdheḥ. upasthasyāpi nendriyatvaṃ ānanda iti. kāyendriyaikadeśastrīpuruṣendriyavyatiriktakalpitasya upasthasya nendriyatvam ānande. kāyendriyaikadeśabhūtastrīpuruṣendriyakṛtaṃ hi tat. kliṣṭaṃ saukhyam iti vākyarthaḥ. kaṇṭhadantākṣivartmāṅguliparvanām apīti vistaraḥ. yadi yathoktāt kāraṇāt etāvanty evendriyāṇīti neṣyate. kaṇṭhasyābhyavaharaṇe. dantasya carvaṇe. akṣivartmana unmeṣanimeṣe. parvaṇaḥ asthisaṃdhisaṃkocavikāsakriyāyām indriyatvaṃ prasajyeta. sarvasya vā kāraṇabhūtasyeti vistaraḥ. sarvasya vā kāraṇabhūtasya bījādeḥ svasyāṃ kriyāyāṃ svakāryakriyāyām aṅkurādilakṣaṇāyām indriyatvaṃ prasajyetety adhikṛtam. yadi yasya yatra puruṣakāro 'sti. tasya tatrendriyatvam iṣyate. sa ca niyamahetuḥ pūrvokto neṣyate. tasmād ayuktaṃ vāgādīnām indriyatvam.
body.translated_text: — 'And because grasping and locomotion are non-different from the hand and foot.' For the hand itself, arising differently and elsewhere, is called 'grasping'; and the foot itself, arising differently and elsewhere, is called 'locomotion.' [This is] because of the non-existence of [a separate] action, and because of the contradiction of functioning upon one's own self. Not the hand and foot

body.text: (II.7, 8) tatra cakṣurādīnām iti vistaraḥ. tatreti vākyopanyāse. kṛto nirdeśa iti.
body.translated_text: (II.7, 8) 'Of the eye and the rest therein' — this is the elaboration. 'Therein' is for introducing the sentence. 'The exposition has been made' —

children.text:
tadvijñānāśrayā rūpaprasādāś cakṣurādayaḥ.
kāyāt strīpuruṣendriye.
vijñānaṃ prativijñaptir
children.translated_text:
'The transparencies of form that are the bases of their [respective] consciousnesses are the eye and the rest.
The female and male faculties are [derived] from the body.
Consciousness is discrimination' —

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

children.text:
jīvitendriyasyeti.
āyur jīvitam ādhāra ūṣmavijñānayor hi ya
children.translated_text:
'Of the life-faculty' —
'Life is the sustainer — that which is the support of warmth and consciousness' —

body.text: ity atra. śraddhādīnāṃ caitteṣv iti.
body.translated_text: in this context. 'Of faith and the rest, among the mental factors' —

body.text: ity atra pradeśe. nanu ca vedanāyā api kṛto nirdeśaḥ caitteṣu ca kariṣyate
body.translated_text: in this passage. [Objection:] 'But the exposition of feeling has also been made among the mental factors, and will be made [again]' —

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: vacanāt. [Tib. 91a] satyaṃ sāmānyaṃ rūpaṃ vedanāyā uktaṃ vakṣyate ca. viśeṣavibhāgarūpaṃ tv iha vivakṣitam iti sukhādīnāṃ kartavyo nirdeśa ity āha. ājñāsyāmīndriyādīnāṃ tarhi na kartavyo yasmān manaso lakṣaṇam uktam. śraddhādīnāṃ caitteṣu kariṣyate. sukhasaumanasyopekṣāṇām iha kriyate. eṣām api kartavya eva. yasmān navadravyasvabhāvatvam eṣāṃ darśayitavyam. etasyāṃ cāvasthāyām etāṇi nava dravyāṇy anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyākhyāṃ labhante. etasyām avasthāyām ājñendriyākhyām etasyām ājñātāvīndriyākhyāṃ labhanta iti. sa eṣām avasthāviśeṣo darśayitavya ity ataḥ sūktam etat. sukhādīnām ājñāsyāmīndriyādīnāṃ ca kartavya iti.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. [Tib. 91a] True — the general form of feeling has been stated and will be stated. But what is intended here is the specific differentiation-form — therefore the exposition of happiness and the rest must be made — he says. 'Then should not the exposition of the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s> and the rest also be made?' — since those of the mind

body.text: asāteti sātānivṛttyartham. kāyikīti mānasīnivṛttyartham. tatra kāyāś cakṣurādayaḥ paṃca paramāṇusaṃcayātmakatvāt. tatra kāye bhavā kāyena vā āśrayeṇa saha caratīti kāyikī. yā upaghātikā paṃcendriyāśrayā vedanā. tat
body.translated_text: 'Unpleasant' (<s>asātā</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the pleasant. 'Bodily' (<s>kāyikī</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the mental. Therein, the 'body' (<s>kāya</s>) [refers to] the five [sense-faculties] beginning with the eye, because they have the nature of an accumulation of atoms. [A feeling that] arises in that body, or that moves together with the body as its basis — [that is] 'bodily.' That which is injurious, having the five sense-faculties as its basis —

body.text: ity avagantavyam.
body.translated_text: this is to be understood.

body.text: atrendriyam ity anuvartate. kāyikīti ca.
body.translated_text: here, 'faculty' continues [from the previous verse]. And 'bodily' [also continues].

body.text: grahaṇam asātānivṛttyartham. tad etad uktaṃ bhavati. tat sukhendriyaṃ. yānugrāhikā paṃcendriyā vedaneti.
body.translated_text: [this] word is for the purpose of excluding the unpleasant. What has been said is this: that is the happiness-faculty — the feeling that is beneficial, having the five sense-faculties [as its basis].

children.text: dhyāne tṛtīye tu [Tib. 91b] caitasī sā sukhendriyam
children.translated_text: 'But in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, [Tib. 91b] the mental [pleasant feeling] is the happiness-faculty' —

body.text: iti. tṛtīye tu dhyāne caitasy api sātā vedanā sukhendriyam iti vyavasthāpyate. kasmāc caitasy eva sātā tatra gṛhyate na kāyikīti. ata āha. na hi tatra kāyikī vedanāsti. pañcavijñānakāyābhāvād iti. tṛtīye dhyāne kasmāt sā na saumanasyendriyam. ata āha. tṛtīye tu dhyāne prītivītarāgatvāt. sukhenendriyam eva sā. na saumanasyendriyam. sātatvād dhi sukham ucyate. na prītir asaṃpraharṣākāratvāt. tathā hi sūtra uktam. prīter virāgād upekṣako viharatīti vistareṇa yāvat smṛtimān sukhavihārī tṛtīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharatīti. saumanasyād anyā prītir iti cet. ata āha. prītir hi saumanasyam iti.
body.translated_text: In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, however, even the pleasant mental feeling is established as the happiness-faculty. Why is only the pleasant mental [feeling] grasped there, and not the bodily? To this he says: 'For bodily feeling does not exist there, because of the absence of the five consciousness-groups.' In the third

children.translated_text: 'The unpleasant mental [feeling], on the other hand, is displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>)' —

body.text: iti. upaghātikā caitasikī vedanā daurmanasyam.
body.translated_text: the injurious mental feeling is displeasure.

body.text: upekṣendriyaṃ tu yā madhyā vedanā. naivasātāsātety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: the equanimity-faculty is the neutral feeling — meaning neither pleasant nor unpleasant.

body.text: ubhayāvayavāv asyā ubhayī. kāyikī caitasikīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Of both kinds' means it has parts of both. 'Bodily and mental' — this is the meaning.

body.text: iti. abhinirūpaṇāvikalpabhāvād ity arthaḥ. prāyeṇeti grahaṇaṃ samādhijavipākajaprītisukhaparivarjanārtham. na tu kāyikam iti. na tu kāyikaṃ sukhaduḥkhaṃ vikalpanād utpadyate. kiṃkāraṇam ity āha. viṣayavaśād arhatām apy utpatter iti. prahīṇapriyāpriyavikalpānām apy arhatāṃ viṣayavaśenaiva kāyikasukhaduḥkhotpādāt. [Tib. 92a] atas tayor indriyatvena bheda iti. tayoḥ kāyikacaitasikayoḥ sukhayor duḥkhayoś ca indriyatvena bhedaḥ pṛthaktvaṃ sukhendriyaṃ saumanasyendriyaṃ duḥkhendriyaṃ daurmanasyendriyam iti. upekṣā tu svarasenaivānabhisaṃskāreṇāvikalpayata evānabhinirūpayata evotpadyate kāyikī caitasikī vā vipākajā naiṣyandikī vā. tasmād ekam indriyaṃ kriyate indriyatvenābhedaḥ upekṣendriyam iti. anyathā ca kāyikam iti vistaraḥ. anyenānubhavarūpaviśeṣeṇa kāyikaṃ sukham anugṛhṇāti. anyena caitasikaṃ. sthiraṃ hi kāyikam. asthiraṃ hi caitasikam. evaṃ duḥkham anyenānubhavarūpaviśeṣeṇa kāyikam upahanti. anyena caitasikam iti. upekṣāyāṃ naiṣa vikalpa iti. eṣa svarūpaviśeṣalakṣaṇo vikalpo nāsti. ata upekṣaṇaṃ praty upekṣākriyāṃ prati. avikalpanāt asvabhāvaviśeṣād abhedaḥ.
body.translated_text: Thus. The meaning is: because of the absence of the conceptualization of examination. The word 'generally' (<s>prāyeṇa</s>) is for the purpose of excluding pleasure-joy born of concentration and retribution. 'But not bodily' — bodily pleasure and pain do not arise from conceptualization. Why? He says: 'Because [they] arise even for <s>Arhats</s>, due to the object' — because bodily pleasure and pain arise solely due to the object even for <s>Arhats</s> who have abandoned the conceptualization of pleasant and unpleasant. Therefore, their distinction as [separate] faculties — of the bodily and mental, of pleasure and pain — [is established as:] the pleasure-faculty, the mental-pleasure-faculty, the pain-faculty, and the mental-displeasure-faculty. But equanimity arises spontaneously, without deliberation, without conceptualizing, without examining — whether bodily or mental, whether retributive or outflow. Therefore one [single] faculty is made — there is no distinction in terms of being a faculty — [it is called] the equanimity-faculty. 'And otherwise, bodily' — thus the elaboration. Bodily pleasure supports by one particular mode of experience, and mental [pleasure] by another. For bodily [pleasure] is stable, and mental [pleasure] is unstable. Likewise, bodily pain afflicts by one particular mode of experience, and mental [pain] by another. 'In equanimity, this distinction does not [apply]' — this distinction characterized by a difference in essential nature does not exist. Therefore, with respect to equanimizing — with respect to the action of equanimity — because of non-conceptualization, because of no difference in essential nature, there is no distinction.

children.translated_text: 'The path of seeing, cultivation, and beyond-training' —

body.text: iti. dṛg darśanam. dṛśo bhāvanāyā aśaikṣasya ca panthā
body.translated_text: thus. '<s>Dṛg</s>' means seeing. The path of seeing, of cultivation, and of one beyond training —

children.translated_text: [is] 'the path of seeing, cultivation, and beyond-training.'

body.text: tasminn eva mārgatraye yāni manaḥsukhasaumanasyopekṣāśraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñākhyāni nava dravyāṇi. tāni darśanamārge anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyaṃ bhāvanāmārge ājñendriyam aśaikṣamārge ājñātāvīndriyam iti vyavasthāpyante. anyonyam apekṣyamāṇāni tāni nava dravyāṇi tattan nāma labhante. [Tib. 92b] naveti ca kalāpāntarāpekṣayaivam uktam. na tv ekasmiṃś cittakalāpe nava dravyāṇi bhavanti. sukhasaumanasyopekṣendriyāṇām ekatarasyaiva bhāvāt. yadi hi sa mārgo 'nāgamyadhyānāntaracaturthadhyānākāśavijñānākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmikaḥ. tatropekṣendriyam eva. na sukhasaumanasyendriye. yadi prathamadvitīyadhyānabhūmikaḥ. tatra saumanasyendriyam eva. yadi tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikaḥ. tatra sukhendriyam eva nānyad iti. anājñātam ājñātuṃ pravṛtta iti. anājñātaṃ satyacatuṣṭayam ājñātuṃ
body.translated_text: On that very threefold path, the nine substances called: mind, pleasure, mental-pleasure, equanimity, faith, vigor, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom — these, on the path of seeing, are the <s>anājñātam-ājñāsyāmīndriya</s> (the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown'); on the path of cultivation, the <s>ājñendriya</s> (the faculty of perfect knowledge); on the path of no-more-training, the <s>ājñātāvīndriya</s> (the faculty of one who has fully known).

body.text: vedituṃ pravṛttaḥ ājñāsyāmīti prārabdhaḥ. tasyendriyam anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyaṃ. aluksamāsaḥ. ākhyātapratirūpakaś cāyam ājñāsyāmīti śabdaḥ. bhāvanāmārge nāsty apūrvam ājñeyaṃ tad eva tu satyacatuṣṭayam ājānāti śeṣānuśayaprahāṇārthaṃ bhāvanāheyakleśaprahāṇārtham. tasyājñasya pudgalasyendriyam ājñendriyam. ājñam evendriyam iti vā. aśaikṣamārge tv ājñātam ity avagamaḥ ājñātāva iti. arthakathanamātram etat. śabdavigrahas tv evaṃ kartavyaḥ. ājñātam ity āva ājñātāvaḥ. avateḥ ghañi rūpam etad āva iti. so 'syāstīti matvarthīyaḥ ājñātāvī. ājñātam avituṃ śīlam asyeti veti tācchīliko ṇiniḥ. tathābhūtasyendriyam iti. tathābhūtasya pudgalasyendriyam. ājñātāvina ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: having set forth to know, having undertaken [the resolve] 'I shall know' — its faculty is the <s>anājñātam-ājñāsyāmīndriya</s>. This is a <s>aluk</s>-compound. And the word '<s>ājñāsyāmi</s>' (I shall know) resembles a finite verb form. On the path of cultivation, there is nothing new to be known; rather, that very fourfold truth

body.text: iti. amalam eva trayam ity avadhāryate. nanu cāyam anāsravasāsravaprakārabheda ukto dhātunirdeśe.
body.translated_text: thus. It is determined that only the three are stainless. But [one might object:] this classification of defiled and undefiled types was stated in the exposition of <s>dhātus</s>:

body.text: Tib. 93a
body.translated_text: Tib. 93a

body.text: anāsravā mārgasatyam
body.translated_text: 'Undefiled is the truth of the path' —

body.text: iti. tathā
body.translated_text: thus. And likewise:

children.text: sāsravānāsravā ete trayaḥ śeṣās tu sāsravā
children.translated_text: 'These three are both defiled and undefiled; the rest are defiled' —

body.text: ityādivacanāt. satyam ukto 'yam evamādiḥ prakārabhedaḥ. sa tu sāmānyarūpeṇokto na bhedarūpeṇa. ataḥ śiṣyasukhapratipattyartham ayam evamādiprakārabhedaḥ pratipadarūpeṇa punar abhidhīyata ity evam avagantavyam. dvidhā naveti na sūtrayitavyam. ekāntānāsravasāsravanirdhāraṇād eva hi dvidhā naveti siddheḥ. yadi hy etāni navaikantenānāsravāṇi syuḥ. ekāntānāsraveṣv ājñāsyāmīndriyādiṣu paṭhyeran. tathaikāntasāsravāṇi syuḥ. ekāntasāsraveṣu rūpīndriyajīvitaduḥkhadaurmanasyeṣu paṭhyeran. na caivam. ato nava dvidheti siddham. asty etad evam. matāntaranivṛttyarthaṃ tu punar idam ucyate
body.translated_text: and so on — from such statements. True, this and similar type-classification has been stated. But it was stated in a general form, not in a detailed form. Therefore, for the easy understanding of students, this and similar type-classification is stated again in a detailed, item-by-item form — this should be understood.

body.text: dvidhaiva nava. nānāsravāṇi yathaike kathayanti. tatsiddhaye cāgamam ānayanti. yasyemānīti vistaraḥ. sarveṇa sarvāṇi na santīti. sarveṇa prakāreṇa mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedena. sarvāṇīti pañcāpi na santīty arthaḥ. pṛthagjanapakṣāvasthitaṃ vadāmīti vacanāt. arthād uktaṃ bhavati. yasyemāni santi sa ārya iti. nedaṃ jñāpakam. teṣām anāsravatvam adhikṛtyety ācāryaḥ. tathā hy [Tib. 93b] āryapudgalavyavasthānaṃ kṛtvā yasyemānīty āheti. katham.
body.translated_text: Only nine are twofold — [some among them] are not undefiled, as some claim. And to establish that, they adduce scripture: 'For one who has these' — thus the elaboration. 'Not all in every [way]' — not in every manner, by the classification of mild, middling, and intense. 'All' [refers to] the five —

body.text: pañcemāni bhikṣava indriyāṇi. katamāni pañca. śraddhendriyaṃ yāvat prajñendriyaṃ eṣāṃ paṃcānām indriyāṇāṃ tīkṣṇatvāt paripūrṇatvād arhan bhavati. tatas tanutarair mṛdutarair anāgāmī bhavati. tatas tanutarair mṛdutaraiḥ sakṛdāgāmī. tatas tanutarair mṛdutaraiḥ sakṛdāgāmī. tatas tanutarair mṛdutaraiḥ srotaāpannaḥ. tato 'pi tanutarair mṛdutarair dharmānusārī. tatas tanutarair mṛdutaraiḥ śraddhānusārī. iti hi bhikṣava indriyapāramitāṃ pratītya phalapāramitā prajñāyate. phalapāramitāṃ pratītya pudgalapāramitā prajñāyate. yasyemāni pañcendriyāṇi sarveṇa sarvāṇi na santi. tam ahaṃ bāhyaṃ pṛthagjanapakṣāvasthitaṃ vadāmīti. tad evam āryapudgalavyavasthānaṃ kṛtvā yasyemānīty āha bhagavān iti. pṛthagjano vā dvividha iti. ābhyantarakaś ca bāhyakaś ca. asamucchinnakuśalamūla ābhyantarako bauddhasaṃgṛhītatvāt. samucchinnakuśalamūlas tu bāhyakas tadviparyayāt. ata eva ca bāhyam iti viśeṣaṇam. itarathā hi pṛthagjanapakṣāvasthitaṃ vadāmīty evāvakṣyat. uktaṃ ca sūtra iti. atha bhagavato 'cirābhisaṃbuddhasyaitad abhavat. adhigato me dharmo gambhīro gambhīrāvabhāso durdarśo duravabodho 'tarkyo 'tarkāvacaraḥ sūkṣmo [Tib. 94a] nipuṇaḥ paṇḍitavijñavedanīyaḥ. taṃ cāhaṃ pareṣām āvedayeyam. taṃ ca pare na vijānīyuḥ. sa mama syād vighātaḥ. syāt klamathaḥ. syāc cetaso 'nudayaḥ. yan nv aham ekākī araṇye pravaṇe dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāratāyogam anuyukto vihareyam. atha brahmaṇaḥ sahāpater brahmaloke sthitasyaitad abhavat. naśyati batāyaṃ lokaḥ. praṇaśyati batāyaṃ lokaḥ. yatredānīṃ kadācit karhicit tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā loke utpadyante. tadyathā udumbarapuṣpam. tasya cādya bhagavato 'lpotsukavihāritāyāṃ cittaṃ krāmati na dharmadeśanāyām. yan nv ahaṃ gatvādhyeṣayeyam. atha brahmā sahāpatiḥ tadyathā balavān puruṣaḥ sammiṃjitaṃ bāhuṃ prasārayet. prasāritaṃ vā sammiṃjayet. evam eva brahmā sahāpatiḥ brahmaloke 'ntarhito bhagavataḥ purastāt pratyasthāt. atha brahmā tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthām abhāṣata.
body.translated_text: 'O monks, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faith-faculty through to the wisdom-faculty. Because of the sharpness and completeness of these five faculties, one becomes an <s>Arhat</s>. Because of [their being] thinner and milder, one becomes a non-returner. Because of [their being even] thinner and milder [than that]' —

children.text:
prādurbabhūva magadheṣu pūrvaṃ
dharmo hy aśuddhaḥ samalānubaddhaḥ.
apāvṛṇīṣva amṛtasya dvāraṃ
vadasva dharmaṃ virajaṃ niraṃgaṇam.
children.translated_text: 'In <s>Magadha</s> there appeared formerly a <s>dharma</s> that was impure, tainted by defilements. Open the door of the deathless! Speak the <s>Dharma</s> that is stainless and free from corruption.'

body.text: atha bhagavān tasyāṃ velāyām ime gāthe abhāṣat.
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: kṛcchreṇa me adhigato brahman khilāṃ pravidālya.
children.translated_text: 'With difficulty have I attained [this], O <s>Brahmā</s>, having broken through the barrenness.'

children.text:
bhavarāgaparītaiś ca nāyaṃ dharmaḥ susaṃbudhaḥ.
pratisrotopamaṃ mārgaṃ gabhīram atidurdṛśaṃ
na drakṣyante rāgaraktās tamaḥskandhena cāvṛtāḥ.
children.translated_text: 'And those beset by attachment to existence will not easily comprehend this <s>Dharma</s>. They will not see the path that goes against the stream, deep and extremely hard to see — those blinded by passion, shrouded in a mass of darkness.'

body.text: brahmāvocat. santi bhadanta [Tib. 94b] sattvā loke jātā loke vṛddhās tīkṣṇendriyā api madhyendriyā api mṛdvindriyā apīty apravartita eva dharmacakra iti vistaraḥ. indriyāṇi śraddhādīni. yais te bhavyā uktāḥ. yasmād apravartite 'pi dharmacakre santi tīkṣṇendriyā ityādy uktam. tasmāt santy eva sāsravāṇi śraddhādīnīti. sadevakāl lokād iti vistaraḥ. na tāvad aham asmāt sadevakāl lokāt samārakāt sabrahmakāt saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ sadevamānuṣāyā mukto niḥsṛto visaṃyukto viprayukto viparyāsāpagatena cetasā bahulaṃ vyahārṣam iti vistaravacanam. na cānāsravāṇām eṣa parīkṣāprakāra iti. na hy anāsravāṇām āsvāda ādīnavo niḥsaraṇaṃ vā yujyate.
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> said: 'Venerable Sir, there are beings in the world, born in the world, grown in the world — with sharp faculties, with middling faculties, with mild faculties too' — thus, even before the turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel — the elaboration. The faculties are faith and the rest. By which those [beings] are capable —

body.text: (II.10) arhann iti. nānāgāmī. kleśavimuktasaṃtānatvāt. ṛddhimān iti prāptābhijñaḥ. cetovaśitvaṃ prāpta iti. asamayavimuktaḥ. jīvitapariṣkāram iti. jīvitāya pariṣkāras tadanuguṇatvāt. dattvā tat praṇidhāyeti. tad āyuḥ praṇidhāya cetasi kṛtvety arthaḥ. katham ity āha. yan me bhogavipākaṃ karma. tad āyurvipākaṃ bhavatv iti. prāntakoṭikam iti.
body.translated_text: (II.10) '<s>Arhat</s>' — not [merely] a non-returner. Because his continuum is liberated from defilements. 'Possessing supernatural powers' — one who has attained the <s>abhijñās</s> (direct knowledges). 'Having attained mastery of mind' — [means] one liberated at a non-fixed time. 'Preparation of the life[-span]' — preparation for [extending] life, because it is conducive to that [life-extension]. Having given [that preparation], [he makes] the aspiration —

body.text: iti lakṣaṇam asya vakṣyate. cittam utpādayati vācaṃ ca bhāṣata iti. cittavācāv api tatsiddhaye kuryāt naikakāraṇasādhyaṃ hi kāryaṃ. tad anena [Tib. 95a] vipāka eva jīvitendriyam iti darśayati. yan me bhogavipākaṃ karma. tad āyurvipākadāyi bhavatv iti. dhyānabhāvanābalaṃ tu tasyākarṣakam iti.
body.translated_text: thus, its characteristic will be stated [later]. 'He generates the mind and utters the speech' — he should perform both mind and speech for the accomplishment of that, for an effect is not accomplished by a single cause alone. By this, he shows that the life-faculty is exclusively retributive. 'That which for me' —

body.text: vipākoccheṣaṃ vipacyata iti. akālamaraṇenāparisamāptaphalasya tyaktasya janmāntarakarmaṇo bhāvanābalena vipākoccheṣam ākṛṣya pratisaṃvedayate. teṣāṃ tādṛśa iti teṣāṃ yoginām.
body.translated_text: 'The remainder of retribution ripens' — through the power of meditation, one draws in and experiences the remainder of retribution of <s>karma</s> from another life that was abandoned [before its fruit was] fully completed due to untimely death. 'Of those, such [is the case]' — of those yogins.

body.text: pūrvakarmajaṃ sthitikālāvedham iti. pūrvasmin janmani karma pūrvakarma. tato jātaḥ pūrvakarmajaḥ. sthitir indriyamahābhūtānāṃ pravāhaḥ. sthiteḥ kālaḥ sthitikālaḥ. tasyāvedha ākṣepaḥ. sthitikālāvedhaḥ. tāvatsaṃsārakṣaṇānubandhasāmartham ākṣepaḥ. tena hy asau sthitikāla āvidhyate. taṃ pūrvakarmajaṃ sthitikālāvedham indriyamahābhūtānāṃ vyāvartayanti yognaḥ. apūrvaṃ ca samādhijam āgantukam ākṣipanti.
body.translated_text: 'Born from previous <s>karma</s>, the impulsion of the duration-period' — <s>karma</s> in a previous birth is 'previous <s>karma</s>.' Born from that is 'born from previous karma.' 'Duration' is the stream of the faculties and great elements. The 'period of duration' (<s>sthitikāla</s>) is the period of that [duration]. Its 'impulsion' (<s>āvedha</s>) is its projection. 'The impulsion of the duration-period' — [it is] the projection with the power to continue the series of <s>saṃsāra</s>-moments for that long. For by that [previous karma], this duration-period is impelled. That impulsion of the duration-period born from previous <s>karma</s> — <s>yogins</s> (meditators) reverse [it] for the faculties and great elements, and they project a new, adventitious one born from <s>samādhi</s> (concentration).

body.text: praśnāt praśnāntaram upajāyata iti. atha yad arhan bhikṣur āyuḥsaṃskārān sthāpayati. taj jīvitendriyaṃ kasya vipāka ity asmāt praśnāt kimartham āyuḥsaṃskārān adhitiṣṭhantīti praśnāntaram. parahitārthaṃ śāsanasthityarthaṃ ceti. parahitārthaṃ buddhā bhagavantaḥ. śāsanasthityartham eva śrāvakaḥ. rogādibhūtaṃ cātmabhāvam iti. rogagaṇḍaśalyādibhūtaṃ triduḥkhatāyogāt. kva kasya ceti. kvety asya praśnavisarjanaṃ manuṣyeṣv eva [Tib. 95b] triṣu dvīpeṣv iti. kasyety asya visarjanaṃ strīpuruṣayor asamayavimuktasyārhataḥ prāntakoṭidhyānalābhina iti. tasya hīti vistaraḥ. samādhau ca vaśitvaṃ prāntakoṭikadhyānalābhinaḥ tīkṣṇendriyatvāt. kleśaiś cānupastabdhā saṃtatir niravaśeṣakleśaprahāṇāt. dṛṣṭiprāptasya yady api samādhau vaśitvam asti. na tu tasya kleśair anupastabdhā saṃtatiḥ. samayavimuktasya yady api kleśair anupastabdhā saṃtatiḥ. na tu samādhau vaśitvam. asamayavimuktasya tūbhayam asti.
body.translated_text: 'From one question arises another question' — from the question 'When an <s>Arhat</s> monk extends life-formations, whose maturation is that life-faculty?' arises the further question 'For what purpose do they sustain life-formations?' 'For the benefit of others and for the continuance of the teaching' — for the benefit of others, the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones [do so]. For the continuance of the teaching alone, the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples) [do so]. 'And their bodily existence afflicted by disease, etc.' — afflicted by disease, boils, thorns, etc. — because of being subject to the three types of suffering. 'Where and for whom?' — the answer to 'where?' is: 'among humans only, [Tib. 95b] in three continents.' The answer to 'for whom?' is: 'for a man or woman who is an <s>Arhat</s>, a non-time-liberated one, who has obtained the border-peak <s>dhyāna</s>.' 'For he' — in detail. For one who has obtained the border-peak <s>dhyāna</s> has mastery in <s>samādhi</s>, because of possessing sharp faculties. And his continuum is not propped up by defilements, because of the complete abandonment of all defilements. For one who has attained through views (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>), although there is mastery in <s>samādhi</s>, the continuum is propped up by defilements. For the time-liberated one (<s>samayavimukta</s>), although the continuum is not propped up by defilements, there is no mastery in <s>samādhi</s>. But the non-time-liberated one (<s>asamayavimukta</s>) possesses both.

body.text: bahuvacanam iti. jīvitasaṃskārān iti yad vacanaṃ. tad bahuvacanam. kasmād ity āha. bahūnām iti vistaraḥ. bahūnāṃ saṃtānavartināṃ jīvitasaṃskārāṇām utsarjanādhiṣṭhānāt. na hy ekasya kṣaṇasya utsarjane 'dhiṣṭhāne vā proyojanam asti. pravāheṇa parakāryābhiniṣpādanāt. ekasya ca kṣaṇasyāpīḍākaratvāt. na ca kālantarasthāvaram iti. kālāntarasthānaśīlaṃ kālāntarasthāvaram akṣaṇikam. tac caitad āyur dravyaṃ na bhavatīti dyotanārthaṃ bahuvacanam ity eke. bahuṣv eva saṃskāreṣv iti sautrāntikānām ayaṃ pakṣaḥ. ekasminn api kṣaṇe bahavas te saṃskārāḥ. yeṣv āyur iti prajñaptiḥ. naikam āyur nāma dravyam asti. te ca saṃskārāḥ paṃcaskandhasvabhāvāś catuḥskandhasvabhāvā vā draṣṭavyāḥ. anyathā hi naiva saṃskāragrahaṇam akariṣyata. evaṃ tu vaktavyam abhaviṣyat. bhagavān jīvitāny adhiṣṭhāya āyūṃṣy utsṛṣṭavān iti maraṇavaśitvajñāpanārtham iti. maraṇe [Tib. 96a] vaśitvam astīti. traimāsyam eva nordhvam iti. trayo māsāḥ samāhṛtās trimāsam. trimāsam eva traimāsyam atra kālādhvanor atyantasaṃyoge dvitīyā bhavati. nordhvaṃ traimāsyād vineyakāryābhāvāt. subhadrāvasānatvāt buddhakāryasya. tasyāpi saṃpādanārtham iti pratijñātasaṃpādanārtham. anyathā vacanamātraṃ syād iti. kalpāvaśeṣaḥ. kalpa ekaḥ sakalaḥ kalpādhikaḥ kalpaḥ sātireka ity arthaḥ. skandhamaraṇamārayor
body.translated_text: 'The plural' — the expression 'life-formations' is in the plural. Why? He says: 'Of many' — in detail. Because of the releasing and sustaining of many life-formations existing in the continuum. For there is no purpose in the releasing or sustaining of a single moment. Because the accomplishment of benefit for others occurs through the stream. And because a single moment is not oppressive. 'And not something enduring over time' — 'enduring over time' means 'accustomed to remaining over time,' i.e., non-momentary. And this life-span is not such a substance — the plural is used for this purpose of illumination, say some. 'In many formations indeed' — this is the <s>Sautrāntika</s> position. Even in a single moment, those formations are many, with respect to which the designation 'life-span' [is applied]. There is no single substance called 'life-span.' And those formations should be understood as having the nature of five aggregates or four aggregates. Otherwise, the term 'formations' (<s>saṃskāra</s>) would not have been used at all. Rather, it would have been stated thus: 'The Blessed One, having sustained the life-spans, released the life-spans.' 'For the purpose of demonstrating mastery over death' — that there is mastery over death. 'Only for three months, not more' — three months combined is 'three-month' (<s>trimāsa</s>); 'three-month' itself is <s>traimāsya</s>; here the second case [accusative] is used in the sense of total connection with time and path. Not more than three months, because of the absence of those to be trained [after that]. Because the Buddha's work ends with <s>Subhadra</s>. 'For the purpose of accomplishing that too' — for the purpose of accomplishing what was promised. Otherwise it would be mere words. 'The remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>' — one <s>kalpa</s>, complete, more than a <s>kalpa</s>, i.e., with a surplus — this is the meaning. 'Of the aggregates and of death, [the two types of] <s>māra</s>'

body.text: iti. catvāro mārāḥ devaputramāraḥ kleśamāraḥ skandhamāraḥ maraṇamāraś ca. tatra prathame yāme devaputramāro nirjitaḥ. dvitīye yāme divyena cakṣuṣā vyavalokya tṛtīye yāme kleśamāro nirjitaḥ. vaiśālyāṃ tu traimāsyaṃ jīvitasaṃskārān adhiṣṭhāya āyuḥsaṃskārān utsṛṣṭavān. skandhamāranirjayārtham utsṛṣṭāḥ skandhāḥ. teṣūtsṛṣṭeṣu martavyaṃ syāt. ato maraṇamāranirjayārtham adhiṣṭhitā iti vaibhāṣikāḥ.
body.translated_text: — there are four <s>māras</s>: the <s>devaputra-māra</s> (divine māra), the <s>kleśa-māra</s> (defilement-māra), the <s>skandha-māra</s> (aggregate-māra), and the <s>maraṇa-māra</s> (death-māra). Of these, in the first watch, the <s>devaputra-māra</s> was conquered. In the second watch, having surveyed with the divine eye, in the third watch the <s>kleśa-māra</s> was conquered. But at <s>Vaiśālī</s>, having sustained the life-formations for three months, he released the life-formations — for the purpose of conquering the <s>skandha-māra</s>, the aggregates were released. Once those were released, death would ensue. Therefore, for the purpose of conquering the <s>maraṇa-māra</s>, [life was] sustained — thus [say] the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>.

body.text: niṣṭhitam ānuṣaṃgikaṃ yat praśnāt praśnāntaram upajātaṃ.
body.translated_text: The incidental [discussion] is completed — what arose as a further question from a question.

body.text: dvedhaiva dvādaśa evety avadhāryate.
body.translated_text: the restriction is: 'in two ways only, twelve only.'

body.text: chraddhādikād ājñātāvīndriyaparyantāt.
body.translated_text: from faith, etc. up to the faculty of one who has fully known (<s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>).

body.text: jīvitendriyād ekantavipākād anyāni dvādaśendriyāṇi vipākaś cāvipākaś ca. tatra cakṣurādīni puruṣendriyāvasānāni sapta svapnādyabhinirvṛttāny aupacayikāny avipākaḥ. [Tib. 96b] manoduḥkhasukham iti vistaraḥ. yāni manaādīni kuśalakliṣṭāni tāny avipākaḥ. yāni ca yathāyogam airyāpathikaśailpasthānikanairmāṇikasvabhāvāny avyākṛtāni tāny avipākaḥ. yathāyogam iti viśeṣaṇam. airyāpathikādīnāṃ mānasatvena duḥkhendriyasaṃbhavāt sukhasaumanasyayoś ca kvacid asaṃbhavāt. tatra kāmadhātāv airyāpathikaṃ manaindriyaṃ tatsaṃprayukte ca saumanasyopekṣendriye avipākaḥ. rūpadhātāv airyāpathikaṃ manaindriyam avipākaḥ. vedanendriyaṃ ca tatsaṃprayuktaṃ yathābhūmi. nairmāṇikaṃ pañcabhūmikam. tatra copekṣendriyam evāvipākaḥ. airyāpathikaśailpasthānikanairmāṇikāni nityam upekṣendriyeṇa saṃprayuktānīti bhadantānantavarmā. śeṣāṇi vipāka iti. kuśalakliṣṭairyāpathikaśailpasthānikanairmāṇikasvabhāvebhyo manaindriyādibhyo 'nyāni manaindriyādīni vipākajāni vipākaḥ. śeṣāṇy avipāka iti siddham iti. jīvitendriyaṃ dvādaśa cakṣurādīni hitvā tadavadhāraṇād eva śeṣāṇy avipāka iti siddham. katamāni punas tāni. daurmanasyendriyaṃ na vipākaḥ kuśalākuśalatvāt. tathā hi vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: other than the life-faculty, which is exclusively maturation, the twelve faculties are both maturation and non-maturation. Of these, the seven beginning with the eye up to the male faculty — when produced through sleep, etc., as accretionary (<s>aupacayika</s>) — are non-maturation. [Tib. 96b] 'The mind, pain, pleasure' — in detail. The mind, etc. that are wholesome or defiled — those are non-maturation. And those that have, as appropriate, the nature of deportment, craft, construction, or transformation, [being] morally indeterminate — those are non-maturation. 'As appropriate' is a qualifier — because deportment, etc., being mental, [allow for] the possibility of the pain-faculty, and because there may be no occurrence of pleasure and joy in some cases. In the desire-realm, the deportment-mind-faculty and the joy and equanimity faculties conjoined with it are non-maturation. In the form-realm, the deportment-mind-faculty is non-maturation, and the feeling-faculty conjoined with it, according to the level. The transformation-type spans five levels.
