And therein, only the equanimity-faculty is non-maturation. 'The deportment, craft, construction, and transformation [types] are always conjoined with the equanimity-faculty' — thus <s>Bhadanta Anantavarman</s>. 'The rest are maturation' — the mind-faculty, etc. other than the wholesome, defiled, deportment, craft, construction, and transformation types — those mind-faculties, etc. that are maturation-born are 'maturation.' 'The rest are non-maturation' — this is established. Excluding the life-faculty and the twelve beginning with the eye, by the restriction on those [twelve], the rest are non-maturation — this is established. What then are those? The displeasure-faculty is not maturation, because it is wholesome or unwholesome. For it will be stated:

body.text: iti. śraddhādy
body.translated_text: thus. 'The group of eight beginning with faith' —

body.text: ity avipākaḥ.
body.translated_text: is non-maturation.

body.text: Tib. 97a
body.translated_text: Tib. 97a

body.text: vipāko 'vyākṛto dharmaḥ. sattvākhya
body.translated_text: 'Maturation is an indeterminate <s>dharma</s> belonging to beings' —

body.text: iti vipākalakṣaṇābhāvāt.
body.translated_text: because of the absence of the characteristic of maturation.

body.text: yadi daurmanasyendriyaṃ na vipāka ity anenāgamavirodhaṃ darśayati. saṃprayogavedanīyatām adhikṛtyeti. vedanīyaṃ vedanā. daurmanasyaṃ vedanīyam asminn iti daurmanasyavedanīyaṃ karma. saumanasyopekṣāvedanīye apīti. saṃprayogamātravacanād daurmanasyavat saumanasyopekṣe api na vipākaḥ prāpṇuta iti parasyābhiprāyaḥ. saṃprayoge 'pi na doṣo vipāke 'pīti. saumanasyaṃ vedanīyam asmin saumanasyavedanīyaṃ karma. tathā saumanasyaṃ vipākatvena vedanīyam asya saumanasyavedanīyaṃ karmeti. agatyā hy etad evaṃ gamyeteti. yadi daurmanasyaṃ yuktyā paricchinnaṃ na vipāka iti. tata evam agatyākhyāyeta saṃprayogavedanīyatām adhikṛtyoktam iti. tenāha kā punar atra yuktir daurmanasyaṃ na vipāka iti. atha vā agatyā hy etad evaṃ gamyeta. kvacit saṃprayogavedanīyatā. kvacid vipākavedanīyateti. brūyās tvaṃ sarvatraiva tarhi saṃprayogavedanīyateti. ata etad antarābhiprāyam abhisamīkṣyāha. kā punar atra yuktir daurmanasyaṃ na vipāka iti. daurmanasyaṃ hīty [Tib. 97b] aniṣṭacintanādikaiḥ parikalpaviśeṣair utpādyate ca [vyutpādyate ca] vyupaśāmyate ca. saumanasyam apy evam iti. parikalpaviśeṣair iṣṭacintanādibhir utpādyate ca vyupaśāmyate ca. vītarāgādīnāṃ tarhīti. yasmād vītarāgādīnāṃ daurmanasyaṃ vyāvartate. na hi cakṣurādiko vipākabhūto vītarāgādīnāṃ vyāvartate. daurmanasyaṃ tu vyāvartate. vacanād daurmanasyena kāmavītarāgo 'samanvāgata iti. sūtre 'py uktaṃ. avītarāgasya dviśalyā vedanoktā kāyikaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratisaṃvedayate caitasikaṃ ca daurmanasyam iti. vacanāt vītarāgasya ca ekaśalyā kāyikam eva duḥkhaṃ pratisaṃvedayata iti. saumanasyam apy eṣām iti vistaraḥ. vītarāgāṇām avyākṛtaṃ vipākarūpaṃ saumanasyaṃ kīdṛśaṃ syāt. samāpattisaṃgṛhītaṃ teṣāṃ saumanasyaṃ saṃbhavati. tac ca kuśalatvān na vipākaḥ. ato vaktavyam. kīdṛśaṃ teṣāṃ saumanasyaṃ vipāka iti. yādṛśaṃ tādṛśam astv iti. aparicchidyamānam api tad asty eveti darśayati. tasyāsti vipākāvakāśo na daurmanasyasya. sarvathāpy asamudācārāt samāpattyavasthāyām apy asamāpattyavasthāyām apīty ato na vipāka iti siddham. manaindriyam ubhayor ubhayasyeti. ubhayoḥ sugatidurgatyoḥ ubhayasya kuśalākuśalasya. vipāka ity adhikāraḥ. idam utsṛṣṭaṃ jīvitendriyāṣṭamāni sugatau kuśalasya [Tib. 98a] vipāka iti. tatra katham ubhayavyaṃjanam asādhusammataṃ kuśalasya vipāka ity āha. sugatāv ubhayavyaṃjanasyākuśalena tatsthānapratilaṃbha iti. sthānam asya bhraṣṭam. ato 'syākuśalena
body.translated_text: 'If the displeasure-faculty is not maturation' — by this he shows the contradiction with scripture. 'With reference to the feeling to be experienced in conjunction' — '<s>vedanīya</s>' is feeling; '<s>daurmanasya</s>-feeling-to-be-experienced in this' = <s>daurmanasyavedanīya</s> <s>karma</s>. 'Since pleasure and equanimity feeling-to-be-experienced [karmas] too [exist]' — the opponent's intent is: since the statement mentions only 'conjunction' (<s>saṃprayoga</s>), just like displeasure, pleasure and equanimity too would not be maturation. '[Even] in conjunction, there is no fault — in maturation too' — 'pleasure to be experienced in this' = <s>saumanasyavedanīya</s> <s>karma</s>. Likewise, 'pleasure to be experienced as maturation in this' = <s>saumanasyavedanīya</s> <s>karma</s>. 'For this must inevitably be understood thus' — if displeasure is determined by reasoning to be non-maturation, then inevitably it must be explained thus: 'It was said with reference to the feeling to be experienced in conjunction.' Therefore he says: 'But what then is the reasoning that displeasure is not maturation?' Or, 'this must inevitably be understood' — [sometimes] it is feeling-to-be-experienced in conjunction; [sometimes] feeling-to-be-experienced as maturation. You might say: 'Then everywhere it would be feeling-to-be-experienced in conjunction.' Therefore, having examined this underlying intent, he says: 'But what is the reasoning that displeasure is not maturation?' 'For displeasure' — [Tib. 97b] it is produced and suppressed by particular imaginative constructions such as thinking of the undesirable, etc. 'Joy too is like this' — it is produced and suppressed by particular imaginative constructions such as thinking of the desirable, etc. 'Then, for the passion-free, etc.' — since displeasure is excluded for the passion-free, etc. For maturation-born [dharmas] like the eye, etc. are not excluded for the passion-free, etc. But displeasure is excluded — by the statement 'one free from desire is not endowed with displeasure.' In the <s>sūtra</s> too it is said: 'For one not free from passion, two darts of feeling are stated: one experiences bodily pain and also mental displeasure.' By the statement, for one free from passion, one dart — one experiences bodily pain only. 'Joy too, for them' — in detail. What kind of morally indeterminate, maturation-type joy would there be for the passion-free? Concentration-included joy is possible for them, but that is wholesome, not maturation. Therefore it must be stated: what kind of joy is maturation for them? 'Whatever kind — let it exist as such' — he shows that even though it cannot be determined, it certainly exists. 'There is room for maturation of that, but not of displeasure' — because displeasure does not occur at all, in any way, whether in the state of attainment or the state of non-attainment — therefore it is not maturation. This is established. 'The mind-faculty is of both, in both' — 'of both' means of both good destiny and bad destiny; 'in both' means of both wholesome and unwholesome. 'Maturation' is the governing topic. 'This is excluded: the life-faculty, the eight [beginning with faith], and in the good destiny, maturation of the wholesome [Tib. 98a].' Therein, how is the dual-sex (<s>ubhayavyāñjana</s>), which is not approved as wholesome maturation, [maturation] of the wholesome? He says: 'In the good destiny, the dual-sex obtains its position through unwholesome [karma].' Its position has fallen [from the normal]. Therefore, its

body.text: pratilaṃbho viprayukto dharmaḥ. ubhayaṃ tu vyaṃjanaṃ kuśalasyaiva vipāka ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: acquisition through unwholesome [<s>karma</s>] is a dissociated <s>dharma</s>. But the dual sex-organ itself is maturation of wholesome [karma] only — this is the intent.

children.text: iti. tad ekaṃ savipākam evety arthaḥ. tenāha. tuśabda evakārārtho bhinnakramaś ceti. bhinnasthāna ity arthaḥ. tad ekaṃ savipākaṃ tv iti hi kramo na bhinnaḥ syāt. ślokabandhānuguṇyena tv evam uktam. na hi tad avyākṛtam iti. savipākam evety avadhāraṇe yuktiṃ darśayati. dve hi vastunī avipāke iṣyete. avyākṛtam anāsravaṃ ca. vikalpaviśeṣotpādyatvān na tad avyākṛtam. asamāhitatvāc ca nānāsravam. avyākṛtaṃ hi pūtibījavan na vipākadānāya samartham. anāsravaṃ tu tṛṣṇānabhiṣyanditatvān nālaṃ vipākadānāyānabhiṣyanditasārabījavat. pāriśeṣyād akuśalaṃ vā tad bhavet kuśalasāsravaṃ vā. ataḥ savipākam eva nāsty avipākaṃ daurmanasyam.
children.translated_text: the meaning is: that one is with-maturation only. Therefore he says: 'The word <s>tu</s> (but) has the meaning of <s>eva</s> (only), and the sequence is split.' 'Split position' is the meaning. For 'that one is with-maturation, but (<s>tu</s>)' would be the unsplit sequence. But it is stated thus because of metrical convenience. 'For it is not morally indeterminate' — he shows the reasoning for the restriction 'with-maturation only.' For two things are accepted as non-maturation: the morally indeterminate and the undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>). Because it is produced by particular imaginative constructions, it is not morally indeterminate. And because it does not [arise] in concentration, it is not undefiled. For the morally indeterminate, like a rotten seed, is not capable of giving maturation. And the undefiled, because it is not moistened by craving, is not capable of giving maturation — like an unmoistered essential seed. By elimination, it would be either unwholesome or wholesome-with-outflow. Therefore it is with-maturation only — there is no displeasure that is without-maturation.

body.text: daśaiva dvidhā dvidhaiva ca daśety avadhāraṇam. dvidheti savipākāvipākāni.
body.translated_text: the restriction is: 'only ten are twofold, and twofold only.' 'Twofold' means with-maturation and without-maturation.

body.text: Tib. 98b
body.translated_text: Tib. 98b

body.text: mano 'nyavittiśraddhādīni ceti.
body.translated_text: 'The mind, the other feelings, and faith, etc.' —

body.text: manaś ca anyavittayaś ca śraddhādīni ceti. vittir vedanā. anyagrahaṇena daurmanasyavarjitaṃ gṛhyate daurmanasyasyoktatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'the mind, and the other feelings, and faith, etc.' 'Feeling' (<s>vitti</s>) is sensation (<s>vedanā</s>). By the word 'other,' what is grasped excludes displeasure, since displeasure has been [already] discussed.

body.text: śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñā. gṛhyanta ity adhikṛtam anyad avipākam iti. yathoktadaurmanasyādyavadhāraṇāt. jīvitaṃ rūpāṇi ca saptendriyāṇy ājñāsyāmīndriyādīni ca trīṇy avipākānīti siddham avyākṛtatvāt anāsravatvāc ca yathākramam.
body.translated_text: faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. 'Are grasped' is the governing topic — '[the rest are] without-maturation.' By the [above] restriction on displeasure, etc. The life-faculty, the seven form-faculties, and the three faculties beginning with the 'I-shall-come-to-know' faculty are without-maturation — this is established — because of being morally indeterminate and undefiled, respectively.

body.text: iti. aṣṭakaṃ kuśalam evety avadhāraṇam.
body.translated_text: This is a restriction: 'the eight-[fold group] is wholesome only.'

body.text: iti. dvidhaiva daurmanasyaṃ daurmanasyam eva dvidhety avadhāraṇaṃ. dvidheti kuśalaṃ cākuśalaṃ ca. anyad api dvaidham asti. kūśalaṃ cāvyākṛtaṃ ca akuśalaṃ cāvyākṛtaṃ ceti. tat katham idam avadhāryate. kuśalaṃ cākuśalaṃ ceti. vyākhyānato viśeṣapratipattiḥ. atha vā daurmanasyaṃ savipākam eveti nirdhāritam. tasmād idam eva dvaidhaṃ bhavati nānyat.
body.translated_text: This is a restriction: 'displeasure is precisely twofold, and it is displeasure alone [that is] twofold.' 'Twofold' means wholesome and unwholesome. Other twofold [divisions] also exist — wholesome and indeterminate, unwholesome and indeterminate. Then how is this restriction determined — 'wholesome and unwholesome'? The specific understanding [comes] from the commentary. Alternatively, it has been determined that displeasure has maturation results only. Therefore, only this twofold [division] obtains, not another.

body.text: iti daurmanasyavarjyaṃ vedanācatuṣṭayaṃ tasyoktatvāt.
body.translated_text: means the four feelings excluding displeasure, since that [displeasure] has already been stated.

body.text: tredheti.
body.translated_text: 'Is threefold' —

body.text: kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtāni. trayaḥ prakārās tredhā. dvitryoś ca dhamuñ. edhāc ceti
body.translated_text: wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. Three kinds [constitute] 'threefold.' For the [numbers] two and three, the suffix <s>dhamun</s> [is added], and '<s>edha</s>' also.

body.text: tredhety edhāśabdavyutpattiḥ. alobhādisaṃprayuktāni kuśalāni. lobhādisaṃprayuktāny akuśalāni. ato 'nyāny [Tib. 99a] avyākṛtāni.
body.translated_text: 'Threefold' — this is the derivation from the word <s>edhā</s>. Those conjoined with non-greed, etc. are wholesome. Those conjoined with greed, etc. are unwholesome. Those other than these [Tib. 99a] are indeterminate.

body.text: jīvitāṣṭamam anyad ekadhaivety avadhāryate. avyākṛtam evety arthaḥ. etadarthaṃ ca punar asya karaṇam. anyathā hy akuśalam eva kuśalāvyākṛtam evākuśalāvyākṛtam eva vā tat saṃbhāvyate. tasmād abhīpsitaikadhātvaprasiddhyarthaṃ punar ucyate. yasyaikadhātvaṃ saṃbhavati. tad bhavati. kiṃ ca saṃbhavaty avyākṛtatvam iti.
body.translated_text: This is a restriction: 'the other — the eighth, namely the life-[faculty] — is one-fold only.' The meaning is: 'indeterminate only.' And the purpose of this additional statement [is as follows]: otherwise, it could be imagined that it is either unwholesome only, wholesome-and-indeterminate only, or unwholesome-and-indeterminate only. Therefore, to establish the desired one-fold character, it is stated again. What one-fold character is possible? — indeterminate-ness.

children.translated_text: 'Obtained in the desire-realm, excluding the undefiled' —

body.text: amalam eva hitvā kāmāptaṃ bhavati. tad dhy apratisaṃyuktam eveti. adhātupatitam evety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Excluding the undefiled alone, [the rest] are obtained in the desire-realm.' For that [undefiled faculty] is exclusively unconnected [with any realm] — the meaning is: it falls outside the realms.

children.translated_text: 'Obtained in the form-realm: the female and male faculties' —

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. strī ca pumāṃś ca strīpumāṃsau. samāsānte vidhir anitya iti paribhāṣayā samāsānto na bhavati. tayor indriye strīpumindriye.
body.translated_text: and so on in detail. '<s>Strī</s>' (woman) and '<s>puman</s>' (man) [together form] '<s>strīpumāṃsau</s>.' By the grammatical rule 'the suffix is not invariable at the end of a compound,' there is no suffix at the compound's end. Their faculties are the female and male faculties.

body.text: duḥkhavedanāsvabhāve indriye duḥkhadaurmanasye ity arthaḥ. te strīpumindriye duḥkhadaurmanasye amalāṃ cehānuvartamānaṃ hitvā. śeṣaṃ rūpāptam indriyaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: means the faculties whose nature is painful feeling — the suffering and displeasure faculties. Those — the female and male faculties, the suffering and displeasure faculties, and the undefiled [faculty] carried over from above — excluding these, the rest of the faculties are obtained in the form-realm.

body.text: kvocyanta iti pṛṣṭe sūtraṃ darśayati. asthānam anavakāśa iti vistaraḥ. atra sūtra ity abhiprāyaḥ. anyaḥ puruṣabhāvo 'sti. yaḥ kāmadhātau puruṣāṇāṃ bhavatīti. stanādisaṃsthānasvarācārānyathātvam. duḥkhendriyaṃ nāstīti. āśrayasyācchatvāt tad abhighātajaṃ nāsti. akuśalabhāvāc ca vipākajaṃ ca nāsti. daurmanasyendriyaṃ nāsti śamathasnigdhasaṃtānatvād iti. yasmāc ca śamathena samādhinā [Tib. 99b] pratighavigamāt. raukṣyaṃ saṃtāne nāsti. tasmād daurmanasyendriyaṃ nāsti. āghātavastvabhāvāc ceti. āghātaḥ kopaḥ. tasya vastu viṣayaḥ āghātavastu. nava cāghātavastūni. anarthaṃ me akārṣīt karoti kariṣyati cety āghātavastutrayam. mitrasya me anartham akārṣīt karoti kariṣyatīty aparam āghātavastutrayam. amitrasya me artham akārṣīt karoti kariṣyati cety aparam āghātavastutrayam iti. eṣāṃ navānām āghātavastūnām abhāvāt viṣayakṛtam api daurmanasyaṃ nāsti. na kevalaṃ hetukṛtaṃ nastīti darśayati. hetukṛtaṃ hi tad yat svasaṃtānapratighakṛtam. pratyayakṛtaṃ ca tad yan navāghātavastukṛtam iti.
body.translated_text: When asked 'where are they stated?', he shows the <s>sūtra</s>. 'It is impossible, there is no occasion' — and so on in detail. The intent is: in this <s>sūtra</s>. 'There is another male condition' — which belongs to males in the desire-realm. [This refers to] the difference in the configuration of breasts, etc., voice, and conduct. 'The suffering-faculty does not exist [there]' — because of the transparency of the body-support, that [suffering-faculty] born from physical injury does not exist [in the form-realm]. And because of the absence of unwholesome [dharmas], the maturation-born [suffering-faculty] also does not exist. 'The displeasure-faculty does not exist [there], because the continuum is moistened by <s>śamatha</s>' — because through the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>śamatha</s>, [Tib. 99b] by the departure of aversion, there is no roughness in the continuum. Therefore the displeasure-faculty does not exist. 'And because of the absence of objects of hostility' — hostility (<s>āghāta</s>) means anger. Its object is the 'object of hostility.' There are nine objects of hostility: 'he caused me harm, he is causing me harm, he will cause me harm' — this is one triad of hostility-objects. 'He caused harm to my friend, he is causing harm, he will cause harm' — this is another triad. 'He benefited my enemy, he is benefiting, he will benefit' — this is another triad. Because of the absence of these nine hostility-objects, even displeasure caused by objects does not exist — not only that caused by the [internal] cause is absent. For that [displeasure] which is caused by the cause means that which is produced by aversion in one's own continuum. And that which is caused by the condition means that which is produced by the nine hostility-objects.

children.translated_text: 'And excluding the pleasant and the material [faculties]' —

body.text: caśabdena pūrvoktam anukṛṣyate. tenāha. strīpumindriye duḥkhe cāmalaṃ ca hitveti vartata iti.
body.translated_text: By the word 'and,' what was previously stated is carried forward. Therefore he says: 'the female and male faculties, the suffering, and the undefiled — excluding [these]' is to be supplied.

body.text: iti. sukhavedanāsvabhāve sukhasaumanasyendriye. rūpīndriyaṃ cakṣurādi.
body.translated_text: means the faculties whose nature is pleasant feeling — the pleasure and joy faculties. 'Material faculty' means the eye, etc.

body.text: (II.14) vittitrayaṃ sukhasaumanasyopekṣā iti. sukhendriyaṃ yat tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ darśanaheyānuśayasaṃprayuktaṃ. tad darśanaheyam. tatraiva ato 'nyat sāsravam. pañcavijñānakāyikaṃ ca kāmāvacaram. prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ ca trivijñānakāyikaṃ bhāvanāprahātavyam. anāsravaṃ tu sukhendriyam aheyam. [Tib. 100a] saumanasyaṃ darśanaheyasaṃprayuktaṃ darśanaheyam. ato 'nyat sāsravaṃ bhāvanāheyam. anāsravam aheyam. upekṣendriyaṃ tu sarvagam iti sugamam.
body.translated_text: (II.14) The triad of feelings is pleasure, joy, and equanimity. The pleasure-faculty belonging to the third <s>dhyāna</s> ground, conjoined with defilements to be abandoned by seeing — that is to be abandoned by seeing. Other than that, what is defiled there, and what belongs to the five consciousness-groups in the desire-realm, and what belongs to the three consciousness-groups at the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground — [these are] to be abandoned by cultivation. But the undefiled pleasure-faculty is not to be abandoned. [Tib. 100a] Joy, conjoined with [defilements] to be abandoned by seeing, is to be abandoned by seeing. Other than that, what is defiled is to be abandoned by cultivation. What is undefiled is not to be abandoned. The equanimity-faculty, however, pervades all [categories] — so it is easy [to understand].

children.translated_text: 'The displeasured-one's [displeasure] is twofold in what is to be abandoned' —

body.text: daurmanasyayogād durmanaskaḥ. tadbhāvo durmanaskatā. daurmanasyam ity arthaḥ. yasya guṇasya hi bhāvād dravye śabdaniveṣaḥ. tadabhidhāne tvatalāv iti lakṣaṇāt. tad darśanaheyasaṃprayuktaṃ darśanaheyam. ato 'nyad bhāvanāheyam. nāheyam asamāhitatvāt.
body.translated_text: '<s>Durmanaskaḥ</s>' means one who has displeasure; his state is '<s>durmanaskatā</s>' — meaning displeasure. For the designation of a substance is made by that quality whose existence [characterizes it] — by the grammatical rule 'the <s>tva</s> and <s>tal</s> suffixes [are used] in designating that.' That [displeasure], conjoined with [defilements] to be abandoned by seeing, is to be abandoned by seeing. Other than that is to be abandoned by cultivation. It is never 'not to be abandoned,' because of its being a non-concentrated [state].

children.translated_text: 'In the desire [realm], two maturation [faculties] are first obtained' —

body.text: iti. kāmapradhānatvāt kāmadhātuḥ kāma iti nirdiśyata iti vakṣyate. aṇḍajajarāyujasaṃsvedajais sattvaiḥ kāmadhātāv ādau prathamato dve indriye vipākātmake labhyete. kāyendriyaṃ jīvitendriyaṃ ca. kasmāt. pratisaṃdhikāle manaupekṣendriyayor avaśyaṃ kliṣṭatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'The desire-realm is called <s>kāma</s> because desire is predominant [there]' — this will be explained later. 'For beings born from eggs, wombs, and moisture, two faculties of the maturation nature are obtained first — initially — in the desire-realm.' The body-faculty and the life-faculty. Why? 'Because at the moment of conception (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>), the mind and equanimity faculties are necessarily defiled.'

children.translated_text: 'Rebirth-existence is defiled by all afflictions belonging to its own ground' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. cakṣurādīnāṃ ca tasyām avasthāyām avidyamānatvāt.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. And because the eye, etc. do not exist at that stage.

body.text: iti apavādaḥ. aviśeṣitatvād dhy upapādukair api tathaiva dve eva labhyeyātām iti prasaṃgaḥ. tasmād ayaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ. kim upapādukais te dve naiva labhyete. labhyete na tu dve eva. tenāha
body.translated_text: this is the exception. For, because no distinction was made, the unwanted consequence would follow that for those born spontaneously too, only two [faculties] would be obtained in the same way. Therefore, this negation. Do those born spontaneously never obtain those two? They do obtain them, but not only two. Therefore he says:

body.text: vistaraḥ. [Tib. 100b] yady avyañjanā bhavanti. yady avidyamānastrīpuruṣendriyāḥ. yathā prāthamakalpikā iti.
body.translated_text: and so on in detail. [Tib. 100b] If they are without sexual characteristics — if they lack the female and male faculties — as, for example, the beings of the first cosmic age.

children.translated_text: 'The beings born at the beginning of a cosmic age were previously like form-realm beings' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. katamāni ṣaṭ. cakṣurādīni pañca jīvitaṃ ca ṣaṣṭham iti. yathā devādiṣv iti. ādiśabdena nārakādayo 'pi gṛhyante. antarābhavopapattibhavapratisaṃdhyavasthāyāṃ
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Which six? The five beginning with the eye, and the life-faculty as the sixth. 'As among the gods, etc.' — by the word 'etc.,' hell-beings, etc. are also included. At the stage of conception in the intermediate existence and the existence of rebirth,

body.text: tāni prathamato labhyante. kiṃ punar ubhayavyañjanā apy upapādukā bhavantīti. nihīnobhayavyañjanotpattiḥ. viśiṣṭā copapādukā yoniḥ. katham anayoḥ samāyoga iti codanābhiprāyaḥ. rūpapradhānatvād rupāṇīti rūpadhātur nirdiśyate. rūpapradhānatvād iti. rūpāṇāṃ svacchatvād bhāsvaratvād ity arthaḥ. atha vā na kāmaguṇapradhāno rūpadhātuḥ. kiṃ tarhi. rūpamātrapradhānaḥ. nāpy ārūpyadhātuvad arūpapradhāna iti. sūtre 'py uktam iti. sūtre 'py evaṃ dṛṣṭam. na madupajñam evaitad iti darśayati. ye 'pi te śāntā vimokṣā atikramya rūpāṇy ārūpyāḥ. te 'py anityā adhruvā anāśvāśikā vipariṇāmadharmāṇa iti vistaraḥ. avyañjanair upapādukair iti prāthamakalpikaiḥ. samāpattitaś ca paratvād iti. yasmāt pūrvaṃ rūpasamāpattiḥ. paścād ārūpyasamāpattiḥ. tasmād rūpadhātor uttara ārūpyadhātuḥ. upapattitaś ca pradhānataratvād iti. yasmāc copapattitaḥ pradhānataraḥ [Tib. 101a] rūpadhātor ārūpyadhātuḥ. bahūni kalpasahasrāṇi tatrātipraśānto vipāko bhavati. ato 'py asāv uttaro na tūpapattideśataḥ.
body.translated_text: those [faculties] are obtained first. 'But are there also spontaneously born beings with both sexual characteristics?' — the objection's intent is: the arising of both sexual characteristics is inferior, and spontaneous birth is a superior form of birth — how can these two coincide? 'The form-realm is called <s>rūpa</s> because form is predominant' — the form-realm is referred to as '<s>rūpa</s>.' 'Because form is predominant' — meaning because the forms [there] are transparent and radiant. Alternatively, the form-realm is not [characterized by] the predominance of sense-pleasures; rather, it is [characterized by] the predominance of form alone. Nor is it [characterized by] the predominance of formlessness, as the formless realm [is]. 'It is also said in the <s>sūtra</s>' — it is also seen in the <s>sūtra</s> — he shows: 'this is not merely my own assertion.' 'Those peaceful liberations which, transcending forms, are formless — they too are impermanent, unstable, unreliable, of a nature to change' — and so on in detail. 'By the spontaneously born without sexual characteristics' — means by the beings of the first cosmic age. 'And from the attainments, because of being higher' — because first comes the form-realm attainment, then the formless attainment, the formless realm is higher than the form-realm. 'And from the perspective of rebirth, because of being more eminent' — because from the perspective of rebirth, the formless realm is more eminent [Tib. 101a] than the form-realm — for many thousands of cosmic ages, the maturation there is extremely peaceful. For this reason too, that [formless realm] is higher — but not from the perspective of the location of rebirth.

body.text: iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of this statement.

body.text: iti. mriyamāṇa ārūpyadhātāv etāny eva trīṇīndriyāṇi nirodhayati. sāpavādaṃ caitad veditavyam.
body.translated_text: One dying in the formless realm ceases these very three faculties. And this should be understood with exceptions.

body.text: vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of this statement.

body.text: iti. rūpadhātāv aṣṭāv etāny eva. saha pañcabhiś cakṣurādibhir nirodhayet. sakṛtsamagrendriyamaraṇāt. ata evāha. sarve hy upapādukāḥ samagrendriyā upapadyante mriyante ceti.
body.translated_text: In the form-realm, these very eight. Together with the five beginning with the eye, one would cease [them]. Because of dying with all faculties simultaneously. For this reason he says: 'All spontaneously born beings are reborn with complete faculties and die [with complete faculties].'

children.translated_text: 'In the desire [realm], ten, nine, or eight' —

body.text: ubhayavyañjano daśendriyāṇi nirodhayati. yadi samagrapañcendriyo bhavati. ekavyañjano nava. avyañjano 'ṣṭau. yadi tu vikalendriyo 'ndho badhiro vā bhavati. tadā tad indriyaṃ parihāryam. sāpavādaṃ caitat sarvakāmadhātāv eva veditavyam. tad apavādam āha.
body.translated_text: One with both sexual characteristics ceases ten faculties — if one has complete five sense-faculties. One with one sexual characteristic [ceases] nine. One without sexual characteristics [ceases] eight. But if one has deficient faculties — being blind or deaf — then that faculty should be subtracted. And all of this should be understood with exceptions, only in the desire-realm. He states the exception:

body.text: na hy eṣāṃ pṛthagnirodha iti. na hy eṣāṃ kāmadhātāv anyonyaṃ virahayya nirodho 'stīty abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'For these do not cease separately' — the intent is: these [faculties] in the desire-realm do not cease separating from one another.

body.text: sarvasya pūrvoktasya maraṇavidher
body.translated_text: This is the exception to the entire death-procedure stated earlier —

children.translated_text: 'The dying one ceases in the formless [realm]: the life and mind [faculties]' —

body.text: ity evamāder apavādaḥ. trividhaṃ hi maraṇacittaṃ saṃbhavati. kliṣṭam avyākṛtaṃ kuśalaṃ ca. [Tib. 101b] tatra kliṣṭāvyākṛtacittasyotsarganyāyena maraṇavidhir uktaḥ. kuśalacittasya tu maraṇe śraddhādayaḥ pañcādhikāḥ prakṣeptavyāḥ. eṣāṃ hi śraddhādīnāṃ kuśale cetasy avaśyaṃ bhāvaḥ. tena yatra trīṇy uktāni tatrāṣṭau. yatrāṣṭau tatra trayodaśa. yatra daśa tatra pañcadaśa. yatra nava tatra caturdaśa. yatra punar aṣṭau tatra trayodaśa. yatra catvāri tatra naveti vistareṇa gaṇanīyam. rūpārūpyadhātvoṛ nāsti kramamaraṇam.
body.translated_text: and so on — this is the exception. For there are three possible types of death-consciousness: defiled, indeterminate, and wholesome. [Tib. 101b] Of these, for one dying with a defiled or indeterminate mind, the death-procedure has been stated according to the general rule. But for one dying with a wholesome mind, five additional [faculties] — faith, etc. — should be added. For these — faith, etc. — necessarily exist in a wholesome mind. Therefore, where three were stated, there are eight; where eight, there are thirteen; where ten, there are fifteen; where nine, there are fourteen; where again eight, there are thirteen; where four, there are nine — and so on, to be counted in detail. In the form and formless realms, there is no sequential death.

body.text: (II.17) indriyaprakaraṇe sarva indriyadharmā vicāryanta iti. indriyaprakaraṇe iha kriyamāṇe. sarva indriyadharmā indriyāvasthāviśeṣāḥ kāritraviśeṣā vā vicāryanta ity eke vyācakṣate. apare tu vyācakṣate. indriyaprakaraṇe indriyaskandhake sarva indriyadharmā avasthāviśeṣāḥ kāritraviśeṣā vā vicāryante. tenehāpi te vicāryante. tatpratyāsatvāt asya śāstrasyety abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: (II.17) 'In the section on faculties, all properties of faculties are investigated.' In the section on faculties being undertaken here, all properties of faculties — special states of faculties, or special functions — are investigated. So some explain. Others explain: in the section on faculties — in the <s>skandhaka</s> (canonical chapter) on faculties — all properties of faculties — special states or special functions — are investigated. Therefore, here too they are investigated, because of this treatise's proximity to that [canonical chapter] — this is the intent.

children.translated_text: 'The attainment of the two final fruits through nine' —

body.text: iti. navabhir indriyair āptir
body.translated_text: The attainment through nine faculties

body.text: kasya.
body.translated_text: Of what?

body.text: ante bhave antye. antye phale antyaphale. tayoḥ. ke punar antye. srotaāpattiphalaṃ arhattvaphalaṃ ca. yathā daṇḍasya dvāv antau bhavataḥ. evaṃ paṅktyavasthitānāṃ caturṇāṃ phalānāṃ srotaāpattiphalam arhattvaphalaṃ cānte bhavataḥ. sakṛdāgāmiphalam anāgāmiphalaṃ ca madhye bhavataḥ. tayor antyayoḥ phalayor navabhir evendriyaiḥ prāptiḥ. katamair navabhir ity āha. śraddhādibhir ājñātāvīndriyavarjyair [Tib. 102a] manaupekṣendriyābhyāṃ ceti. navabhir iti. tatraivam abhisamayakramaḥ. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ. duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ. duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ. duḥkhe 'nvayajñānaṃ. samudaye dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ. samudaye dharmajñānaṃ. samudaye 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ. samudaye 'nvayajñānaṃ. nirodhe dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ. nirodhe dharmajñānaṃ. nirodhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ. nirodhe 'nvayajñānaṃ. mārge dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ. mārge dharmajñānaṃ. mārge 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ. mārge 'nvayajñānam. iti ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇā abhisamaya ity ucyante. tatra duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntir yāvan mārge 'nvayajñānakṣāntir iti pañcadaśa
body.translated_text: 'In the last existence' — in the final [existence]. 'In the last fruit' — in the final fruit. 'Of those two.' What then are the last [fruits]? The fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>) and the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> (<s>arhattvaphala</s>). Just as a staff has two ends, so too of the four fruits arrayed in a row, the fruit of stream-entry and the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> are at the ends; the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>) and the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>) are in the middle. The attainment of those two last fruits is by nine faculties only. Which nine? He says: the five [beginning with] faith and the rest, excluding the <s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>, [Tib. 102a] and the mind- and equanimity-faculties — [these are] nine. Therein, the order of <s>abhisamaya</s> (realization) is as follows: insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering; <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering; insight-tolerance regarding the subsequent knowledge of suffering; subsequent knowledge of suffering; insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of origination; <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of origination; insight-tolerance regarding the subsequent knowledge of origination; subsequent knowledge of origination; insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of cessation; <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of cessation; insight-tolerance regarding the subsequent knowledge of cessation; subsequent knowledge of cessation; insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of the path; <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of the path; insight-tolerance regarding the subsequent knowledge of the path; subsequent knowledge of the path. Thus the sixteen moments are called <s>abhisamaya</s> (realization). Of these, from the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering up to the insight-tolerance regarding the subsequent knowledge of the path — fifteen

body.text: kṣaṇā darśanamārgaḥ.
body.translated_text: moments constitute the path of insight (<s>darśanamārga</s>).

children.translated_text: 'The path of insight is for one who sees the previously unseen — [consisting of] fifteen moments therein' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. tac cājñāsyāmīndriyam ity ucyate. mārge 'nvayajñānaṃ tu ṣoḍaśaḥ sa bhāvanāmārgaḥ. tataḥ prabhṛtyā vajropamasamādher yāvān anāsravo mārgaḥ sarvo 'sau bhāvanāmārgaḥ. tac cājñendriyam ity ucyate. kṣayajñānāt prabhṛti sarvo 'nāsravo mārgo 'śaikṣamārgaḥ. tac cājñātāvīndriyam ity ucyate. tatra srotaāpattiphalaṃ mārge 'nvayajñānakṣāntyavasthāyāṃ prāpyate. śraddhādīni cātra pañcendiyāṇi avaśyaṃ bhavanti. tasyā avasthāyāḥ kuśalatvāt. ājñāsyāmīndriyasvabhāvā cāsau mārge 'nvayajñānakṣāntir vartamānā. manaindriyaṃ ca tatsaṃprayuktaṃ bhavati. upekṣendriyaṃ cāvaśyaṃ anāgamyāśrayatvāt. [Tib. 102b] anāgamyasya ca upekṣendriyasaṃprayuktatvāt. mārge 'nvayajñānaṃ tu asyām avasthāyām ājñendriyasvabhāvam utpādābhimukhaṃ vartate. tena śraddhādibhiḥ pañcabhir ājñāsyāmīndriyeṇājñendriyeṇa manaupekṣendriyābhyāṃ ceti tatphalaṃ navabhiḥ prāpyate. ubhābhyāṃ hi tasya prāptir iti. ānantaryamārgeṇājñāsyāmīndriyasvabhāvena vimuktimārgeṇa cājñendriyasvabhāvena tasya prāptiḥ. visaṃyogaprāpter āvāhakasaṃniśrayatvāt yathākramaṃ. tasyā visaṃyogaprāter ānantaryamārgasyāvāhakatvāt. janakatvāt. vimuktimārgasya ca tasyāḥ saṃmniśrayatvāt. ādhāratvād ity arthaḥ. dvābhyāṃ cauraniṣkāsanakapāṭapidhānavat. yathā hi dvayor manuṣyayoḥ ekena cauro niṣkāsyate. dvitīyenāsya kapāṭaṃ pidhīyate. tathānantaryamārgeṇa visaṃyogaprāptir āvāhyate kleśaprāptim ādāya nirodhāt. vimuktimārgeṇādhāryate. visaṃyogaprāptisahotpādāt. arhattvasya punaḥ śraddhādibhir ājñāsyāmīndriyavarjyair iti. vajropamasamādhyavasthāyām arhattvaphalaṃ prāpyate. śraddhādīni manaindriyaṃ ca pūrvavat. vajropamasamādhikalāpas tasyām avasthāyām ānantaryamārga ājñendriyasvabhāvo vartamānaḥ. sukhasaumanasyopekṣendriyāṇāṃ cānyatamat. yadi tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ niśrityārhattvaṃ prāpyate. sukhendriyaṃ tatra vartamānaṃ. [Tib. 103a] atha prathamaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānaṃ niśritya tatra saumanasyendriyaṃ. athānāgamyadhyānāntaracaturthadhyānākāśavijñānākiṃcanyāyatanānāṃ anyatamaṃ niśritya tatropekṣendriyaṃ vartamānaṃ. kṣayajñānakalāpas tu asyām avasthāyāṃ vimuktimārga ājñātāvīndriyasvabhāva utpādābhimukho bhavati. tena śraddhādibhiḥ paṃcabhir ājñendriyeṇājñātāvīndriyeṇa manaindriyeṇa sukhasaumanasyopekṣendriyāṇāṃ cānyatameneti tatphalaṃ navabhiḥ prāpyate. ānantaryavimuktimārgābhyāṃ
body.translated_text: because of this statement. And that is called the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s> (the faculty of 'I shall come to know'). But the subsequent knowledge of the path, the sixteenth [moment], is the cultivation-path (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>). From that point onward, up to the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s> (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>), whatever is the non-outflow path — all of that is the cultivation-path. And that is called the <s>ājñendriya</s> (the faculty of knowing). From the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) onward, the entire non-outflow path is the path of no-more-learning (<s>aśaikṣamārga</s>). And that is called the <s>ājñātāvīndriya</s> (the faculty of one who has fully known). Therein, the fruit of stream-entry is attained at the stage of the insight-tolerance regarding the subsequent knowledge of the path. And the five faculties [beginning with] faith necessarily exist at that [moment], because that stage is wholesome. That insight-tolerance regarding the subsequent knowledge of the path, being present, has the nature of the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s>. And the mind-faculty is associated with it. And the equanimity-faculty necessarily [exists], because the basis is the preliminary concentration (<s>anāgamya</s>). [Tib. 102b] And because the preliminary concentration is associated with the equanimity-faculty. But the subsequent knowledge of the path, at this stage, has the nature of the <s>ājñendriya</s> and is facing arising. Therefore, the attainment of that fruit [is] by nine [faculties]: the five [beginning with] faith, the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s>, the <s>ājñendriya</s>, and the mind- and equanimity-faculties. 'For its attainment [is] by both' — by the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), which has the nature of the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s>, and by the liberation-path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>), which has the nature of the <s>ājñendriya</s> — [thus] its attainment [occurs]. Because [these two paths are respectively] the conveyor and the support of the disconnection-acquisition (<s>visaṃyogaprāpti</s>), in that order. Because the uninterrupted path is the conveyor of that disconnection-acquisition — the generator. And because the liberation-path is the support of that — the holder, is the meaning. 'By two, like the expelling of a thief and the closing of the door.' Just as, of two men, one expels the thief and the second closes the door for him — so too, by the uninterrupted path, the disconnection-acquisition is conveyed, through the cessation of the affliction-acquisition; and by the liberation-path, it is sustained — through co-arising with the disconnection-acquisition. As for [the attainment of] <s>Arhatship</s>: 'by [the faculties beginning with] faith and the rest, excluding the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s>.' At the stage of the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s>, the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> is attained. Faith and the rest and the mind-faculty [exist] as before. The assemblage of the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s> at that stage — the uninterrupted path — is present, having the nature of the <s>ājñendriya</s>. And one of the happiness-, mental-pleasure-, or equanimity-faculties [exists]. If <s>Arhatship</s> is attained based on the third <s>dhyāna</s>, the happiness-faculty is present there. [Tib. 103a] If based on the first or second <s>dhyāna</s>, the mental-pleasure faculty [is present there]. If based on any one of the preliminary concentration, the <s>dhyānāntara</s> (inter-<s>dhyāna</s>), the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, or the sphere of nothingness, the equanimity-faculty is present there. But the assemblage of the knowledge of destruction at this stage — the liberation-path — has the nature of the <s>ājñātāvīndriya</s> and faces arising. Therefore, the attainment of that fruit [is] by nine [faculties]: the five [beginning with] faith, the <s>ājñendriya</s>, the <s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>, the mind-faculty, and one of the happiness-, mental-pleasure-, or equanimity-faculties. 'Its attainment [is] by the uninterrupted and liberation paths'

body.text: tatprāptir iti pūrvavad vyākhyānaṃ.
body.translated_text: — the explanation is as before.

children.translated_text: 'By seven, eight, or nine — for the two [middle fruits]' —

body.text: prāptir iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. pratyekam iti vistaraḥ. sakṛdāgāmiphalasya saptabhir aṣṭābhir navabhir vā prāptiḥ. evam anāgāmiphalasya. tat pratipādayann āha. sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ tāvad yady ānupūrvakaḥ prāpṇoti sa ca laukikena mārgeṇeti. laukiko mārgaḥ śāntādyudārādyākāraḥ.
body.translated_text: 'attainment' is the sentence-completion. 'Each [respectively]' — this is the elaboration. The attainment of the fruit of once-returning [is] by seven, eight, or nine [faculties]. Similarly for the fruit of non-returning. Explaining that, he says: 'First, the fruit of once-returning — if one attains it gradually, and by the mundane path.' The mundane path has aspects such as 'peaceful' and the like, or 'gross' and the like.

children.translated_text: 'Having aspects such as "peaceful" and "gross," directed to higher and lower [realms]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. tenottarāṃ bhūmiṃ śāntataḥ praṇītataḥ niḥsaraṇataś ceha yogī paśyati. adharām audārikato duḥkhilataḥ sthūlabhittikataś ca paśyati. sa cāyaṃ catuḥprakāro varṇyate. prayogamārga ānantaryamārgo vimuktimārgo viśeṣamārgaś ca. tatra prayogamārgo yata ānantaryamārga utpadyate. sa punar yena kleśān prajahāti. vimuktimārgo [Tib. 103b] 'py ānantaryamārgād anantaram utpadyate. kleśaprahāṇaprāpter ādhārakaḥ. viśeṣamārgas tata uccaṃ viśiṣṭo mārgaḥ. tena mārgeṇa navaprakārāḥ kleśāḥ praheyāḥ. adhimātrādhimātro 'dhimātramadhyo 'dhimātramṛduḥ madhyādhimātro madhyamadhyo madhyamṛduḥ mṛdvadhimātro mṛdumadhyo mṛdumṛduś ceti. tad yadi pṛthagjanaḥ prajahāti darśanabhāvanāheyān kleśān miśrīkṛtya tena mṛdumadhyādhimātrādibhedena navadhā kṛtvā prajahāti. mṛdumṛdubhyām ānantaryavimuktimārgābhyām adhimātrādhimātraṃ kleśaprakāraṃ prajahāti. evaṃ yāvad adhimātrādhimātrābhyām ānantaryavimuktimārgābhyāṃ mṛdumṛdukleśaprakāraṃ prajahāti. āryas tu bhāvanāheyān eva kleśāṃs tathaiva navadhā kṛtvā prajahāti. darśanaheyānāṃ darśanamārgeṇa prākprahīṇatvāt. lokottaras tu bhāvanāmārgas tathaiva ṣoḍaśākāraḥ. anityādyākārabhedāt. sa cāpi tathaiva prayogādimārgabhedāc caturbhedaḥ. ihāpi mṛdumṛdubhyām ānantaryavimuktimārgābhyām adhimātrādhimātraṃ kleśaprakāraṃ prajahāti. evaṃ yāvad adhimātrādhimātrābhyām ānantaryavimuktimārgābhyāṃ mṛdumṛdukleśaprakāraṃ prajahāti. eṣa laukikalokottarayor mārgayor diṅmātranirdeśaḥ. tat sakṛdāgāmiphalam ānupūrvakeṇa vā labhyeta bhūyovītarāgeṇa vā. tatrānupūrviko yaḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāpya kramāt sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnoti. [Tib. 104a] kaś cāsau. yaḥ sakalabandhana ekaprakārādyupalikhito vā yadi na ṣaṣṭhaprakāropalikhito niyāmam avakrāmati. ṣoḍaśe cittakṣaṇe sa srotaāpanno bhavati. sa bhāvanāheyasyaikasya yāvat ṣaṣṭhasyaiva vā prakārasya prahāṇāya śamathacaritatvāt laukikam api mārgam utpādayati. sa ṣaṣṭhaprakāre prahīṇe sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnoti. tasya phalasya saptabhir indriyaiḥ prāptiḥ śraddhādibhiḥ
body.translated_text: because of this statement. By that [mundane path], the practitioner here sees the higher plane as peaceful, excellent, and as an escape; and sees the lower [plane] as gross, afflicted, and coarse-walled. This [path] is described as fourfold: the preparatory path (<s>prayogamārga</s>), the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), the liberation path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>), and the path of distinction (<s>viśeṣamārga</s>). Therein, the preparatory path [is that] from which the uninterrupted path arises; and that [uninterrupted path] is that by which one abandons afflictions. The liberation path [Tib. 103b] also arises immediately after the uninterrupted path — it is the support of the acquisition of affliction-abandonment. The path of distinction is the distinguished path [rising] higher from that. By that path, nine types of afflictions are to be abandoned: intense-intense, intense-medium, intense-mild, medium-intense, medium-medium, medium-mild, mild-intense, mild-medium, and mild-mild. If an ordinary person abandons [them], he abandons afflictions to be abandoned by insight and by cultivation combined — making them ninefold by the division into mild, medium, intense, and so forth. By the mild-mild pair of uninterrupted and liberation paths, he abandons the intense-intense type of affliction. And so on, up to: by the intense-intense pair of uninterrupted and liberation paths, he abandons the mild-mild type of affliction. But a Noble One abandons only afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation — making them ninefold in the same way — because those to be abandoned by insight have been previously abandoned by the insight-path. The supramundane cultivation-path also has sixteen aspects in the same way — by the distinction of aspects such as 'impermanent' and the rest. And it too is fourfold in the same way — by the distinction of preparatory and other paths. Here too, by the mild-mild pair of uninterrupted and liberation paths, one abandons the intense-intense type of affliction. And so on, up to: by the intense-intense pair of uninterrupted and liberation paths, one abandons the mild-mild type of affliction. This is a brief indication of the direction regarding both the mundane and supramundane paths. Now, the fruit of once-returning may be obtained either gradually or by one who has further [attained] freedom from desire. Therein, the gradual one [is he who], having attained the fruit of stream-entry, attains the fruit of once-returning in sequence. [Tib. 104a] And who is he? One who has complete bondage, or one who has been partially freed from one type up to [no more than] the sixth type, [and who] enters the certainty [of the Noble Path without having abandoned the sixth type]. At the sixteenth mind-moment, he becomes a stream-enterer. He then generates even the mundane path for the abandonment of one type — up to the sixth type only — of [afflictions] to be abandoned by cultivation, because of being inclined toward <s>śamatha</s> (calm). When the sixth type is abandoned, he attains the fruit of once-returning. The attainment of that fruit [is] by seven faculties: [the five beginning with] faith

body.text:
paṃcabhir manaindriyeṇa upekṣendriyeṇa ca saptamenānāgamyanirśrayatvāt. atha lokottareṇe mārgeṇa tasyāṣṭābhir indriyaiḥ prāptiḥ. tair evājñendriyeṇa cāṣṭhamena. tany eva hi śraddhādīni saptendriyāṇi ājñendriyākhyāṃ labhante. anāsravatvāt. atha bhūyovītarāga iti. yo laukikena mārgeṇa pṛthagjanāvasthāyāṃ ṣaṭprakāropalikhito 'bhūt. sa bhūyovītarāga ity ucyate. bhūyasā prakāreṇa vītarāga iti kṛtvā. sa yadi sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnoti. kathaṃ sa prāpnoti iti. abhisamayakrameṇa pūrvoktena mārge 'nvayajñānakṣāntyavasthāyāṃ prāpnoti. tasya navabhir yathaiva srotaāpattiphalasya. śraddhādibhir ājñātāvīndriyavarjyaiḥ. manaupekṣendriyābhyāṃ ceti pūrvavat vyākhyānaṃ. ayaṃ hi srotaāpattiphalaṃ aprāpyaiva ṣoḍaśe kṣaṇe sakṛdāgāmī bhavati. anāgāmiphalaṃ yady ānupūrvakaḥ prāpnotīti. ihānupūrvako [Tib. 104b] yaḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ ca prāpya anāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnoti. yo vā bhūyovītarāgo bhūtvā srotaāpattiphalam alabdhvaiva sakṛdāgāmiphalam eva ca labdhvānāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnoti. sa ca yadi laukikena mārgeṇa prāpnoti. tasya saptabhir indriyaiḥ prāptiḥ. yathā sakṛdāgāmiphalasyānupūrvikīyasyety abhipretaṃ. śraddhādibhiḥ paṃcabhir manaupekṣendriyābhyāṃ cety arthaḥ. atha lokottareṇa mārgeṇa tasyāṣṭābhis tathaiveti. yathā sakṛdāgāmiphalasyaivāṣṭābhir ity arthaḥ. ājñendriyam aṣṭamaṃ bhavatīti. atha vītarāga iti. kāmadhātumātravītarāgo laukikena mārgeṇa navame prakāre prahīṇe prathamād api vā dhyānād yāvad ākiṃcanyād api vā viṭarāgo yo 'nāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnoti. tasya navabhiḥ prāptiḥ. yathā srotaāpattiphalasya. srotaāpattiphalasya hi darśanamārgeṇa prāptiḥ. asya ca darśanamārgeṇaiva prāptir iti tulyatvam. ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ. sakhasaumanasyopekṣendriyāṇām anyatamaṃ bhavati. niśrayaviśeṣād iti. yadi tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ niśritya niyāmam avakrāmati. sukhendriyaṃ tatra bhavati. atha prathamadvitīye dhyāne niśritya saumanasyendriyaṃ tatra bhavati. athānāgamyadhyānāntaracaturthadhyānānām anyatamaṃ niśritya upekṣendriyaṃ tatra bhavatīti. [Tib. 105a] yadāpy ayam ānupūrvika
iti vistaraḥ. yadāpy ayam adhigatapūrvaphala ānupūrvikas tīkṣṇendriyaḥ. sa navame vimuktimārge dhyānaṃ praviśati maulaṃ laukikena mārgeṇa tadāpy aṣṭābhir indriyair anāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnoti. tatra mauladhyānasaṃgṛhīto vimuktimārgo bhavati. tatra ca saumanasyendriyaṃ. ānantaryamārgas tv anāgamyasaṃgṛhīta eva. yadi na pṛaviśati tatra copekṣendriyam eva nānyathā. tasya prāptir aṣṭābhiḥ śraddhādibhiḥ paṃcabhir manaupekṣāsaumanasyendriyaiś ceti. ubhābhyāṃ ca tasya prāptir iti. ānantaryavimuktimārgābhyāṃ.
body.translated_text: with five — the mind-faculty, the equanimity-faculty, and with the seventh [faculty] — because of not having <s>Ānāgamya</s> as a support. But when entering by the supramundane path, the attainment [is] through eight faculties — those same [seven] with the <s>ājñendriya</s> (faculty of perfect knowledge) as the eighth. For those same seven faculties beginning with faith —

body.text: cauraniṣkāsanakapāṭapidhānavad iti vyākhyātam etat. atha lokottareṇa praviśatīti. sa eva ānupūrvikas tīkṣṇendriyo veditavyo 'dhikārānuvṛtteḥ. tasya navabhir indriyaiḥ prāptis tair evedānīm uktair indriyaiḥ. ājñendriyeṇa ca navamena. tāny eva hi indriyāṇi anāsravatvād ājñendriyākhyāṃ labhante. idam iha codyate. kasmād ānupūrvika evam ukto na punar vītarāgapūrvī. na hi vītarāgapūrvī anāgamyaniśrayeṇa darśanamārgam utpādya ṣoḍaśe cittakṣaṇe maulaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ praviśati. tatrādhigate 'nādarāt. ānupūrviko hi mauladhyānarthī tasyānadhigatapūrvatvāt. tasmād asti saṃbhavo yad asau maulam eva praviśati. vītarāgapūrvī tu catuḥsatyadarśanaṃ prati kṛtādaro na dhyānaṃ pratīti [Tib. 105b] na tatra ṣoḍaśe cittakṣaṇe maulaṃ dhyānaṃ praviśatīty abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: this has been explained as 'like expelling a thief and closing the door.' But when [one] enters by the supramundane [path] — that same [practitioner] following the gradual [approach] should be understood as one with sharp faculties, because of the continuity of the topic. His attainment is through nine faculties — those very faculties just stated, plus —

children.translated_text: 'Nine [faculties lead to] the attainment of the last two fruits' —

body.text: ity uktaṃ. tad virodhayati yat tarhi abhidharma uktaṃ. jñānaprasthāne. katibhir indriyair arhattvaṃ prāpnotīti. āha. ekādaśabhir iti. tat kathaṃ na virudhyata ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus it has been stated. He raises a contradiction to that: 'But what is stated in the <s>Abhidharma</s> — in the <s>Jñānaprasthāna</s>: "By how many faculties does one attain <s>Arhatship</s>?" [The answer is:] "By eleven."' The intent is: how is there no contradiction?

body.text: iti. kasyacid evaikasya pudgalasya saṃbhavo na sarvasya saṃbhavaḥ. yo hi mṛdvindriyaḥ parihāya parihāya sukhasaumanasyopekṣābhiḥ niśrayaviśeṣāt pāryāyikībhir arhattvaṃ prāpnuyāt. taṃ praty evam uktaṃ. ekādaśabhir iti. na tu saṃbhavo 'sti sakhasaumanasyopekṣāṇāṃ ekasmiṃ kāle samavadhānam ity arthaḥ. cittacaittānām ekaikadravyotpatteḥ. yo hi kaścin mṛdvindriyaḥ pudgalo 'nāgamyaṃ anyaṃ vopekṣendriyaniśrayaṃ niśritya arhattvaṃ prāpnuyāt. tasya tatprāptir upekṣendriyeṇa. tataḥ punar api parihīyate. tataḥ prathamaṃ dvitīyaṃ vā dhyānaṃ niśritya punar arhattvaṃ prāpnuyāt. tasya tatprāptiḥ saumanasyendriyeṇa. tataḥ punar api parihīyate. tataḥ sa tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ niśritya punar arhattvaṃ prāpnuyāt. tasya tatprāptiḥ sukhendriyeṇa iti. pratyekaṃ tatra phalaprāptau avaśyaṃ navaivendriyāṇi vyāpriyante. śraddhādīni paṃca manaājñātāvīndriyāṇi sukhasaumanasyopekṣendriyāṇāṃ cānyatamad iti. punaḥpunaḥ prāptes tad ekādaśabhir ity uktaṃ. katham anāgāmino 'py eṣa prasaṃgo [Tib. 106a] na bhavatīti. kasmāt tatra śāstre 'rhatvaphalam eva ekādaśabhiḥ prāpnotīty uktaṃ. na tūktam anāgāmiphalam apīti. na hy asau parihīṇaḥ kadācit sukhendriyeṇa prāpnotīti. asāv anāgāmī tṛtīyadhyānordhvabhūmilābhāt parihīṇo bhavati. ūrdhvabhūmer eva parihīṇo bhavati. nasāv
body.translated_text: thus. The possibility is for one particular individual only, not for all. For one who has mild faculties, declining again and again, would attain <s>Arhatship</s> through pleasure, mental-pleasure, and equanimity — which are alternating due to the distinction of support — it is stated thus with respect to that [individual].

body.text: anāgāmiphalāt parihīṇa ity ucyate. evaṃ yāvat. dvitīyadhyānāt. yadā tu prathamāt parihīṇo bhavati. tadānāgāmiphalāt parihīṇa ity ucyate. paṃcāvarabhāgīyaprahāṇād dhi anāgāmiphalaṃ vyavasthāpyate. yadā ca sa kāmavairāgyāt parihīṇaḥ. tadā tṛtīyaṃ dhyānam asya nāsti. tat kathaṃ sukhendriyeṇānāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnuyāt. tata āha. na hy asau parihīṇaḥ kadācit sukhendriyeṇa prāpnotīti. kiṃ. saumanasyendriyeṇa prāpnuyāt. yata evaṃ sukhendriyasyaiva pratiṣedhaḥ. prāpnuyāt yadi navame vimuktimārge maulaṃ dhyānaṃ praviśet. naitad asti. yo hi parihīṇo bhavet. sa mṛdvindriyaḥ. yaś ca mṛdvindriyaḥ. sa na śaknoti navame vimuktimārge maulaṃ dhyānaṃ praveṣṭuṃ. tīkṣṇendriyas tu śaknoti. indriyasaṃcārasya duṣkaratvāt. asty etat. kiṃ tu yady asau mṛdvindriya ānupūrviko 'nāgāmiphalaṃ prāpya tataś ca parihīṇo bhūtvā indriyasaṃcāraṃ kuryāt. indriyasaṃcāreṇa ca tīkṣṇendriyo bhūtvā pūrvakeṇaiva krameṇānāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnuvan yadi navame vimuktimārge maulaṃ [Tib. 106b] praviśet. tasya tadānāgāmiphalaprāptir aṣṭābhir navabhir vā bhavati. śraddhādibhiḥ paṃcabhir manaindriyeṇa upekṣendriyeṇa cānantaryamārgasaṃgṛhītena saumanasyendriyeṇa ca mauladhyānavimuktimārgasaṃgṛhīteneti. lokottareṇa cen maulaṃ dhyānaṃ praviśet. ebhiś cāṣṭābhir ājñendyiyeṇa ca navamenety avagantavyaṃ. tasmāt sūktaṃ. na hy asau parihīṇaḥ kadācit sukhendriyeṇa prāpnotīti. vītarāgapūrvī tarhy ekādaśabhis tat prāpnuyāt. kathaṃ. yo mṛdvindriyaḥ pudgalas tṛtīyadhyānalābhī tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ niśritya niyāmam avakrāmet. sa ṣoḍaśe cittakṣaṇe anāgāmī bhavati. sā tatphalaprāptiḥ. sukhendriyeṇa śraddhādibhiḥ paṃcabhir manaājñāsyāmīndriyājñendriyaiś ceti. sa tato 'nāgāmiphalāt parihīṇa indriyottāpanena tīkṣṇendriyam ātmānaṃ kṛtvā anāgamyaniśrayeṇaivānāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnuvan navame vimuktimārge maulaṃ praviśet. tasya tatphalaprāptiḥ pūrvavad upekṣendriyeṇa saumanasyendriyeṇa ca śraddhādibhiś cāpi paṃcabhir manaindriyeṇa cāṣṭamena lokottaramārgatvāt ājñendriyeṇāpi navameneti. evaṃ dvayoḥ kālayor ekādaśabhir indriyais sa pudgalas tad anāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnuyād iti. tatas tat pratiṣedhārtham idam āha. na ca vītarāgapūrvī parihīyate. tadvairāgyasya dvimāryaprāpaṇād iti. na ca kāmavītarāgaḥ kenacin niśrayeṇa niyāmam [Tib. 107a] avakrāntaḥ parihīyate. kasmāt. tadvairāgyasya kāmavairāgyasya dvimārgaprāpaṇāt. laukikalokottaramārgaprāpaṇāt. iha phalaṃ dvividhaṃ. saṃskṛtam asaṃskṛtaṃ ca.
body.translated_text: one is said to have 'declined from the fruit of non-returning.' Likewise [declining] successively as far as [declining] from the second <s>dhyāna</s>. But when one declines from the first [<s>dhyāna</s>], then one is said to have 'declined from the fruit of non-returning.' For the fruit of non-returning is established through the abandonment of the five lower fetters. That which —

body.text: iti vacanāt. tatra yad asaṃskṛtaṃ visaṃyogalakṣaṇam anāgāmiphalaṃ. tat
body.translated_text: from this statement. Therein, the unconditioned fruit of non-returning, characterized by liberation (<s>visaṃyoga</s>) —

body.text: pūrvaṃ laukikena mārgeṇa prāptaṃ. niyāmāvakrāntau ca lokottareṇa mārgeṇa punas tat prāptaṃ. dvividhā hi tasya prāptiḥ. laukikī lokottarā ca. tasmāt sthiraṃ tad vairāgyaṃ. tasmād ato na parihīyate. nanu ca
body.translated_text: was first attained by the mundane path. And upon entering the fixed course [of certainty], it was again attained by the supramundane path. For its attainment is twofold: mundane and supramundane. Therefore that dispassion is stable. Therefore, from that [fruit] one does not decline. Not —

children.translated_text: 'There is no loss of the fruit, [only] from the earlier [attainments].'

body.text: darśanaheyānām avastukatvād ity etad api kāraṇāntaram asti. kasmāt tad iha noktam ity etad api vaktavyaṃ. api khalu para evaṃ brūyāt. mā bhūd darśanaheyakleśavairāgyaparihāṇiḥ. bhāvanāheyakleśamātravairāgyaparihāṇis tu kasmād asya parihīṇakasya na bhavet. paṃcāvarabhāgīyaprahāṇād dhi anāgāmiphalaṃ bhavati. tatra ca satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ śīlavrataparāmarśo vicikitsā ca darśanaheyāḥ. kāmacchando vyāpādaś ca bhāvanāheyau. tayoś ca tasya vītarāgapūrviṇo 'bhisamayānte ṣoḍaśe cittakṣaṇe prahāṇasya laukikena mārgeṇa prāptasya tatsāmarthyāt punar anāsravā prāptir bhavati. anāsravagotrāṇāṃ labdhatvāt. [Tib. 107b] anāsravaṃ hi navamavimuktimārgasvabhāvaṃ saṃskṛtam anagāmiphalam asaṃskṛtaṃ ca kāmacchandādiprahāṇaṃ tasyām avasthāyāṃ labhyate. tasmād idam eva kāraṇam uktaṃ. āryeṇa tad vairāgyasya dvimārgaprāpaṇād iti. kāmacchandādiprahāṇasya dvimārgaprāpaṇād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: Because those abandoned by the path of seeing are without real substance — this too is another reason. Why is it not stated here? This too should be explained. Moreover, the other [school] —

children.translated_text: 'One endowed with equanimity, life, and mind is necessarily possessed of three' —

body.text: iti. upekṣayā jīvitena manasā vā yukto 'nvito 'vaśyaṃ trayeṇa samanvāgataḥ tenaivopekṣājīvitamanaḥsvabhāvena. na hy eṣām anyonyena rinā samanvāgama iti. yadaikasya samanvāgamaḥ. tadetarayor api samanvāgamaḥ. tenaiṣāṃ samanvāgamavyavasthānaṃ kriyate. cakṣurādīnāṃ tu na kriyate. tasmād āha. cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvendriyair iti vistaraḥ. cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvendriyair ārūpyadhātūpapanno na samanvāgata ity atra kāyendriyāgrahaṇaṃ. kāmadhātau ca yenāpratilabdhavihīnānīty asyopacayārthasya cakṣurādiṣv eva saṃbhavān na kāyendriye. anyathā hi rūpibhir indriyair ārūpyopapanno na samanvāgata ity evocyate. apratilabdhāni kalalādyavasthāyāṃ. vihīnāni labdhavināśād andhatvādyavasthāyāṃ kramamaraṇe vā. pṛthagjanā na samanvgāgatā iti viśeṣaṇaṃ. āryasyāvaśyaṃ samanvāgatatvāt. na hi tasya bhūmisaṃcāreṇa anāsravasukhādityāgaḥ. daurmanasyena kāmavītarāga iti. ihastho dhātvantarastho vā pṛthagjano vāryo [Tib. 108a] vā na samanvāgataḥ. pṛthagjanaphalasthā iti. phalasthāḥ srotaāpannādayo 'bhisamayānte vihīnatvāt. tenānājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyeṇāsamanvāgatāḥ. ājñendriyeṇa darśanamārgasthā
body.translated_text: thus. 'Endowed with equanimity, life, or mind' means 'necessarily possessed of three' — possessed of those three themselves whose nature is equanimity, life, and mind. For these [three] —

body.text: aprāptatvād asamanvāgatāḥ. aśaikṣamārgasthāḥ phalaprāptau vihīnatvāt asamanvāgatāḥ. apratiṣiddhāsv avasthāsu yathoktasamanvāgamo veditavya iti. yā apratiṣiddhā avasthāś cakṣurādibhir indriyaiḥ samanvāgamaṃ prati. tāsv avasthāsu yadyad indriyam uktaṃ. taistaiḥ samanvāgato veditavya ity arthaḥ. tadyathā kāmadhātāv apratilabdhavihīnāvasthāṃ hitvā cakṣurādhibhir jihvāntaiḥ samanvāgataḥ. kāyendriyeṇa kāmarūpadhātūpapannaḥ samanvāgata ityādi.
body.translated_text: because they are not attained, [they are] not possessed. Those on the path of no-more-training, because of being deficient regarding the attainment of the fruit, are not possessed [of certain faculties]. In the states that are not prohibited, as stated —

body.text:
iti. yukta iti vartate. avaśyam iti ca. saṃkhyānukramavivakṣāyāṃ tu tadanantaraṃ tair ity evānantaraṃ sukhādigrahaṇaṃ. sukhendriyeṇa samanvāgata iti. caturthadhyānārūpyadhātūpapannaṃ pṛthagjanaṃ muktvā sarvaḥ sukhendriyeṇa samanvāgataḥ. tasyānyair nāvaśyaṃ samanvāgataḥ. cakṣurādibhir jihvendriyāntair ārūpyadhātau kāmadhātau ca apratilabdhavihīnāvasthāyām asamanvāgamaḥ. kāyendriyeṇa ca ārūpyadhātau. strīpuruṣendriyābhyāṃ rūpārūpyadhātvoś ca. kāmadhātau ca alabdhavihīnāvasthāyāṃ. duḥkhendriyeṇa rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ. saumanasyendriyeṇa pṛthagjanas tṛtīyadhyānopapannaḥ. [Tib. 108b] daurmanasyendriyeṇa kāmavītarāgāvasthāyāṃ. śraddhādibhiḥ paṃcabhiḥ samucchinnakuśalamūlāvasthāyāṃ. ājñāsyāmīndriyeṇa pṛthagjanaphalasthāvasthāyāṃ. ājñendriyeṇa pṛthagjanadarśanamārgasthāśaikṣāvasthāyāṃ.
ājñātāvīndriyeṇa pṛthagjanaśaikṣāvasthāyāṃ asamanvāgata iti. yaḥ kāyendriyeṇa so 'pi caturbhir iti. kāmadhātūpapannaḥ kāyendriyeṇa samanvāgatas tasya. nānyair avaśyaṃ samanvāgamaḥ. cakṣurādibhiḥ kāmādhātāv alabdhavihīnāvasthāyām asamanvāgamaḥ. strīpuruṣendriyābhyām etasyām evāvasthāyāṃ rūpadhātau cāsamanvāgamaḥ. duḥkhena cāsminn eva. sukhena ca pṛthagjanasya caturthadhyānopapattāv asamanvāgamaḥ. saumanasyena pṛthagjanas tṛtīyacaturthadhyānopapanno 'samanvāgataḥ. daurmanasyena śraddhādibhiś cānyaiḥ pūrvavad asamanvāgamo vaktavyaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Endowed' is to be supplied. And 'necessarily.' When the enumeration and sequence are intended, then immediately after those [three], 'with those' — and immediately after, the mention of pleasure and the rest. [One who has] pleasure —

children.translated_text: 'With five — one who has eye and the rest' —

body.text: iti. cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvāvān ity arthaḥ. tena ceti. tena cakṣuṣā. cakṣuṣi saty avaśyaṃ kāyendriyaṃ. na tu śrotrādīni. kāmadhātāv alabdhavihīnatvasaṃbhavāt. strīpuruṣendriyādīnāṃ pūrvavad vyabhicāro vaktavyaḥ. evaṃ śrotraghrāṇajihvendriyair iti. yaḥ śrotrendriyeṇa. so 'vaśyaṃ paṃcabhir upekṣājīvitamanaḥkāyais tena cety evaṃ sarvaṃ neyaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. The meaning is: one who has the eye, ear, nose, and tongue. 'And by that' — by that eye. When the eye exists, the body-faculty necessarily [exists]. But not necessarily the ear and the rest.

body.text: kiṃ. paṃcabhir [Tib. 109a] avaśyaṃ samanvāgata ity adhikṛtaṃ. cakṣurādiṣv eva saumanasyaṃ kasmān na prakṣiptaṃ. anyasthānapāṭhāt. tathā hy ādiśabdena prakṣepa ākulaḥ syāt. dvitīyadhyānajas tṛtīyālābhī katamena sukhendriyeṇa samanvāgata iti. sukhendriyaṃ kāmadhātau paṃcavijñānakāyikaṃ. prathame ca dhyāne trivijñānakāyikam asti. tṛtīye tu dhyāne mānasaṃ. ato dvitīyadhyānajo nādhareṇa sukhendriyeṇa samanvāgataḥ. tasya bhūmisaṃcāreṇa tyaktatvāt. na ṭṛtīyadhyānabhūmikena tasyālābhitvād iti matvā codayati. katamena sukhendriyeṇa samanvāgata iti. āha. kliṣṭena tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikeneti. sarve hy adharabhūmyupapannāḥ sattvā uparibhūmikenāprahīṇena kliṣṭena samanvāgatā iti siddhāntaḥ. śeṣendriyavyabhicāraḥ pūrvavad vaktavyaḥ.
body.translated_text: what? 'Is necessarily possessed of five' — this is what is under discussion. Why is mental pleasure not included among the eye and the rest? Because it is situated elsewhere —

children.translated_text: 'But one who has pain — with seven' —

body.text: iti. kāmadhātūpapanno hy eṣa. tasmād avaśyaṃ kāyendriyeṇa caturbhiś ca vedanendriyair iti. daurmanasyavarjyaiḥ. tadvītarāgāvasthāyāṃ daurmanasyaṃ vyabhicarati. manojīvitendriye ca staḥ. ity avaśyaṃ saptabhir indriyaiḥ samanvāgataḥ. śeṣendriyavyabhicāras tu pūrvavad vācyaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. For this one is born in the desire realm. Therefore necessarily [endowed] with the body-faculty and the four feeling-faculties — excluding mental displeasure. Without that [mental displeasure] —

children.translated_text: 'One who has the female faculty and the rest — with eight and so on' —

body.text: iti. strīpuruṣadaurmanasyaśraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñendriyavān ity arthaḥ. jīvitamanaḥsukhaduḥkhasaumanasyopekṣendriyāṇām uktatvāt. ājñātāvīndriyādīnāṃ ca trayāṇāṃ vakṣyamāṇatvāt. [Tib. 109b] eṣām evāṣṭānām indriyāṇāṃ grahaṇaṃ bhavati. yaḥ strīndriyeṇa samanvāgata iti. sa kāmadhātūpapanna eva strīndriyavattvāt. ataḥ so 'vaśyam aṣṭābhir indriyaiḥ samanvāgataḥ. katamair ity āha. taiś ca saptabhiḥ strīndriyeṇa ceti. kāyajīvitamanobhiś caturbhiś ca vedanendriyair iti saptabhiḥ strīndriyeṇa cāṣṭamena. śeṣair aniyamaḥ. yathoktaṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ vaikalyasaṃbhavād ityādibhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ. strīndriyavat puruṣendriyavān api vaktavyaḥ. daurmanasyavān api kāmopapannaḥ kāmavītarāga iti tathaiva taiḥ saptabhir daurmanasyena ca. śraddhāvān api traidhātukaḥ sattva iti taiḥ paṃcabhiḥ śraddhādibhir avinābhāvibhir upekṣājīvitamanobhiś ca samanvāgataḥ. śeṣair aniyamaḥ pūrvavat. yathā śraddhāvān evaṃ yāvat prajñāvān. ājñāte indriyam ājñātendriyam iti. ājñāta eva indriyaṃ ājñātendriyaṃ. niravaśeṣājñāta indriyam ity arthaḥ. ājñendriyam api hi ājñāta indriyaṃ na tu niravaśeṣe sāvaśeṣatvāt praheyasya. atha vā padaikadeśagrahaṇena ājñātāvī pudgala ājñāta ity ucyate. tasyendriyaṃ ājñātendriyam iti. ya ājñendriyeṇa so 'vaśyam ekādaśabhir iti. ājñendriyavān phalasthaḥ
body.translated_text: thus. The meaning is: one who has the female, male, mental-displeasure, faith, vigor, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom faculties. [Together with] the life, mind, pleasure, pain, mental-pleasure, and equanimity faculties —

body.text: śaikṣaḥ triṣv api dhātuṣu bhavati. sa caturthadhyānārūpyopapannaḥ kathaṃ sukhasaumanasyendriyābhyāṃ samanvāgataḥ. [Tib. 110a] yasmād āryaḥ kāmavairāgye 'vaśyaṃ saumanasyendriyaṃ pratilabhate. dvitīyadhyānavairāgye ca sukhendriyaṃ. te ca bhūmisaṃcāre 'pi na tyajyete. tathā hi vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: a learner exists in all three realms. How then is one born in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> or in the formless realm possessed of the pleasure and mental-pleasure faculties?

children.text:
bhūmisaṃcārahānibhyāṃ dhyānāptaṃ tyajyate śubhaṃ
tathārūpyāptam. āryaṃ tu phalāptyuttaptihānibhir
children.translated_text: 'Through change of level and decline, the wholesome [faculties] attained in <s>dhyāna</s> are abandoned; likewise those attained in the formless [realm]. But the noble [faculties are abandoned] through fruit-attainment, arising, and decline' —

body.text: iti. phalaprāptīndriyottāpane 'pi yady api te pratipannakamārgamṛdvindriyamārgasaṃgṛhīte tyajyete. tathāpy apare phalasthatīkṣṇendriyamārgasvabhāve labhyete. tasmāt tābhyāṃ sukhasaumanasyābhyāṃ bhūmisaṃcāre 'pi aparityaktābhyāṃ caturthadhyānārūpyopapanno 'pi āryaḥ samanvāgata eva bhavati. śeṣaiḥ pūrvavad aniyamaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Even though in the case of fruit-attainment and faculty-arising, the path-of-the-practitioner and the path-of-mild-faculties by which they were included are abandoned, nevertheless others at the fruit-stage —

children.translated_text: 'One endowed with the <s>ājñāsyāmi</s>-faculty is possessed of thirteen' —

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. ājñāsyāmīndriyasamanvāgataḥ kāmāvacaraḥ sattvaḥ kāmadhātāv evājñāsyāmīndriyotpādanāt.
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration. A being in the desire realm who is possessed of the <s>ājñāsyāmi</s>-faculty [is so] because the <s>ājñāsyāmi</s>-faculty is produced only in the desire realm.

children.text: asaṃvegād iha vidhā tatra niṣṭheti vācanād
children.translated_text: 'Because of lack of urgency here; and because of the statement that the culmination is there' —

body.text: iti. tasmād avaśyaṃ kāyendriyam asyāsti. catasro vedanā daurmanasyavarjyāḥ tasya vītarāgāvasthāyāṃ vyabhicārāt. tatrāvaśyam iti vartate. trayodaśabhir ebhir indriyair avaśyam eva samanvāgata ity avadhāryate. na tu trayodaśabhir eveti. śeṣair aniyamaḥ. andhādiṣv api darśanamārgasaṃbhavāt. strīpuruṣendriyayor vaikalye kathaṃ darśanamārgotpattiḥ. strīpuruṣendriyaviyuktavikalānāṃ hi saṃvaraphalaprāptivairāgyāṇi [Tib. 110b] na santīti. kecit tāvad āhuḥ. pratilabdhasaṃvarāṇāṃ phalaprāptir bhavati. dvivyaṃjanodayād dhi prātimokṣasamvaratyāgo bhavati. na tadvaikalyāt. kramamaraṇād vā strīpuruṣendriye nirodhe 'py abhyastanirvedhabhāgīyasya darśanamārgotpattir bhavati. apare punar āhuḥ. pudgalasāmānyam ihādhikriyate. naikatraivendriyair āvaśyakasamanvāgamavyabhicārāv ucyete. katham.
body.translated_text: Thus. Therefore, the body-faculty necessarily exists for this [being]. The four feelings excluding mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) — because of the deviation [of mental displeasure] in his state of freedom from desire. There, 'necessarily' applies — it is determined that one is necessarily endowed with these thirteen faculties, but not with thirteen only. There is no fixed rule regarding the remaining [faculties]. Because the path of insight (<s>darśanamārga</s>) is possible even for the blind and the like. [Objection:] When there is deficiency in the female and male faculties, how can the path of insight arise? For it has been said that restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>), fruit-attainment, and dispassion [Tib. 110b] do not exist for those separated from and deficient in the female and male faculties. Some, for their part, say: for those who have already obtained restraint, fruit-attainment is possible. For the abandonment of <s>prātimokṣa</s>-restraint occurs from the arising of dual sexual characteristics, not from the deficiency of those [faculties]. Or, even when the female and male faculties have ceased through sequential death, the path of insight can arise for one who has cultivated the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (aids to penetration). Others, however, say: the general class of persons (<s>pudgalasāmānya</s>) is the subject here. The necessary endowment and deviation with [these] faculties are not stated with reference to a single [individual] alone. How?

children.translated_text: 'One endowed with equanimity, life, and mind is necessarily endowed with three' —

body.text: iti yāvat. upekṣāsamanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ kāmadhātūpapanno vā yāvad bhavāgropapanno vā sarvo 'sāv avaśyaṃ trayeṇa samanvāgataḥ. cakṣurādivyabhicāras tu saṃbhavato na sarvatra. kaścid eva hi rūpibhir indriyair asamanvāgato ya ārūpyadhātūpapannaḥ. na tu yo rūpadhātūpapannaḥ. vistareṇa yāvat kaścid eva śraddhādibhir asamanvāgato yaḥ samucchinnakuśalamūlaḥ. na tu sa eva ārūpyadhātūpapannaḥ. tasthehāpi yāvān ājñāsyāmīndriyopetaḥ sarvo 'sāv ebhir yathoktais trayodaśabhir indriyair avaśyaṃ samanvāgataḥ. vyabhicāras tu saṃbhavataḥ
body.translated_text: thus and so on. A person endowed with equanimity — whether born in the desire-realm or up to the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) — any such [person] is necessarily endowed with three. But the deviation regarding the eye and the rest is possible, [occurring] not everywhere [but] in some [cases]. For only some are not endowed with material faculties — namely, those born in the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>), but not those born in the form-realm. In detail, up to: only some are not endowed with faith and the rest — namely, those whose wholesome roots are cut off, but not that same [person when] born in the formless realm. Here too, as far as one endowed with the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s> (the faculty of 'I shall come to know'), every such [person] is necessarily endowed with these stated thirteen faculties. But the deviation

body.text: kasyacid eva. tathā hi kasyacic cakṣurindriyeṇāsamanvāgamo yo 'ndhaḥ. kasyacic chrotrendriyeṇa yo badhiraḥ. evaṃ ghrāṇādibhiḥ. yāvat kasyacit strīndriyeṇa yaḥ puruṣaḥ. kasyacit puruṣendriyeṇa yā strī. kasyacid daurmanasyena yo vītarāgaḥ. ity evam evāvagantavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: is only for some. For thus, some are not endowed with the eye-faculty — one who is blind; some with the ear-faculty — one who is deaf; similarly with the smell-faculty and the rest; up to: some [are not endowed] with the female faculty — one who is male; some with the male faculty — one who is female; some with mental displeasure — one who is free from desire. Thus it should be understood.

children.translated_text: 'One without wholesome [roots], with the fewest, [is endowed] with eight' —

body.text: iti ekaḥ pudgalaḥ. sarvebhyo 'lpair [Tib. 111a] yaḥ samanvāgataḥ. sa kiyadbhir alpaiḥ samanvāgata ity āha. niḥśubho yaḥ samucchinnakuśalamūlaḥ. sa ca kāmadhātāv eva.
body.translated_text: this is one [type of] person. One who is endowed with the fewest of all — [Tib. 111a] how many faculties at minimum is he endowed with? He says: one without wholesome [roots] (<s>niḥśubha</s>) — one whose wholesome roots are cut off. And this [occurs] only in the desire-realm.

children.translated_text: 'A woman or man cuts off view and conduct' —

body.text: iti. kāmavairāgyaṃ cātra na saṃbhavati. tasmād asya paṃcāpi vedanendriyāṇi santi. kāyendriyaṃ ca jīvitamanasī ca sta eva sarvatra. cakṣurādīni tu na santi. kramamaraṇāvasthāyāṃ andhatvādyavasthāyāṃ ca teṣām abhāvāt. vcdayata iti kṛtveti kartari kvip. vedanaṃ vā vid iti bhāvasādhana auṇādikaḥ kvip. jñāpakaṃ darśayati. yathā saṃpadanaṃ saṃpad iti.
body.translated_text: thus. And dispassion from desire is not possible here. Therefore, this [person] has all five feeling-faculties. And the body-faculty, life-faculty, and mind-faculty exist everywhere. But the eye-faculty and the rest do not exist — because of their absence in the state of sequential death and in the state of being blind and the like. '<s>Vedayata</s>' — meaning 'because one feels' — the <s>kvip</s> suffix is in the agent sense. Or, '<s>vedana</s>' — '<s>vid</s>' — the <s>kvip</s> suffix is an <s>auṇādika</s> formation in the sense of the action itself. He shows the indicator: just as '<s>saṃpadana</s>' [becomes] '<s>saṃpad</s>.'

body.text: iti saṃkhyāmātraṃ tathāśabdena saṃbadhyate. ekāntakuśalatvāt śraddhādīni śubhagrahaṇena gṛhyanta iti. śubhāny eva nākuśalāvyākṛtāni yāni tāni śubhānīty arthaḥ. ājñāsyāmīndriyādīnām api grahaṇaprasaṃga iti. tāny api ekāntakuśalāni. tasmāt tadgrahaṇaprasaṃga iti. na. aṣṭādhikārād iti.
body.translated_text: only the number is connected by the word 'likewise.' 'Because of being exclusively wholesome, faith and the rest are included by the term "wholesome" (<s>śubha</s>)' — they are wholesome only, not unwholesome or indeterminate — those are what is meant by 'wholesome.' [Objection:] 'There would be the inclusion of the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s> and the rest as well' — for those too are exclusively wholesome; therefore, there would be the inclusion of those. [Reply:] No. 'Because the topic is [one endowed with] eight' —

body.text: ity etasmāt.
body.translated_text: from this [statement].

body.text: aṣṭābhir ity ājñāsyāmīndriyādīnāṃ nirāsaḥ kṛto bhavati. aṣṭaśabdena kṛtāvadhitvāt. bālādhikārāc ceti. bālo 'trādhikriyate.
body.translated_text: the exclusion of the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s> and the rest has been made [by the word] 'eight.' Because a limit has been set by the word 'eight.' 'And because the topic concerns a fool (<s>bāla</s>)' — a fool is the subject here.

body.text: iti vacanāt. [Tib. 111b] ājñāsyāmīndriyādyabhāve ca pṛthagjano bhavati. pṛthagjanatvaṃ katamat. āryadharmāṇām alābha iti vacanāt. tasmāt teṣv anāsraveṣu aprasaṃga iti.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. [Tib. 111b] And in the absence of the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s> and the rest, one is an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). 'What is the state of being an ordinary person? The non-attainment of Noble <s>dharmas</s>' — because of this statement. Therefore, there is no inclusion of those non-outflow [faculties].

body.text: (II.22) dvivyaṃjano yaḥ samagrendriya iti. dvivyaṃjano 'pi hi samagracakṣurādikaḥ. evam ekānnaviṃśatyā samanvāgato nānyathā. ājñātāvīndriyaṃ dvayoś cānyatarad iti. rāgitvād ājñātāvīndriyaṃ ekāntena varjayitavyaṃ. āryasya cājñāsyāmīndriyājñendriyābhyām avaśyaṃ paryāyeṇa samanvāgamāt. yadājñāsyāmīndriyaṃ. na tadājñendriyaṃ. yadājñendriyaṃ. na tadājñāsyāmīndriyaṃ.
body.translated_text: (II.22) 'One with both sexual characteristics who has complete faculties' — for even one with both sexual characteristics can have complete eye-faculties and the rest. Thus, one is endowed with nineteen, not otherwise. 'The <s>ājñātāvīndriya</s> and one of the other two' — because of being with attachment (<s>rāgin</s>), the <s>ājñātāvīndriya</s> must be excluded without exception. And because a Noble One is necessarily endowed in alternation with the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s> and the <s>ājñendriya</s>: when one has the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s>, one does not have the <s>ājñendriya</s>; when one has the <s>ājñendriya</s>, one does not have the <s>ājñāsyāmīndriya</s>.

body.text: ukta indriyāṇāṃ dhātuprabhedaprasaṃgenāgatānāṃ vistareṇa prabhcda iti. aṣṭādaśānāṃ dhātūnāṃ katīndriyaṃ kati nendriyam iti dhātuprabhedaprasaṃgena.
body.translated_text: It has been stated that the detailed classification of the faculties that have come up in connection with the classification of elements [is complete]. 'Of the eighteen elements, how many are faculties and how many are not faculties?' — in connection with the classification of elements.

children.text: dharmārdham indriyaṃ ye ca dvādaśādhyātmikāḥ smṛtā
children.translated_text: 'Half of the <s>dharma</s>[-element] is faculty, and the twelve that are called internal' —

body.text: iti. indriyāṇi āgatāni. teṣāṃ prabhedaḥ
body.translated_text: thus the faculties have been presented. Their classification —

body.text: ity evamādivistareṇoktaḥ.
body.translated_text: and so on — has been stated in detail.

body.text: (II.23) kim ete saṃskṛtā dharmā iti. ye te skandhadhātvāyatanatvenābhihitāḥ pūrvaṃ. yathā bhinnalakṣaṇā iti. rūpyate iti rūpaṃ. anubhavo vedanā. nimittodgrahaṇaṃ saṃjñetyādi. saṃskṛtagrahaṇam utpattimattvāt. utāho niyatasahotpādā api. kecit santīti. santi hi kecit sahotpādā na tu niyatasahotpādāḥ. yathā cakṣurādisahotpādāḥ. tadvijñānādayaḥ cakṣurādīnāṃ sabhāgatatsabhāgabhāvāt. tasmād evaṃ pṛcchati. sarva ime dharmāḥ [Tib. 112a] paṃca bhavaṃtīti. paṃcavastukanayena evaṃ sarvadharmasaṃgraho vyavasthāpyate. rūpādikalāpamukhena dharmanirdeśaḥ. sukhapratipattyarthaṃ. tatrāsaṃskṛtaṃ naivotpadyata iti. na tat prati sahotpādaniyamaś cintyate. sarvasūkṣmo rūpasaṃghātaḥ paramāṇur iti. saṃghātaparamāṇur na dravyaparamāṇuḥ. yatra hi pūrvaparabhāgo nāsti. tat sarvarūpāpacitaṃ dravyaṃ dravyaparamāṇur itīṣyate. tasmād viśinaṣṭi saṃghātaḥ paramāṇur iti.
body.translated_text: (II.23) 'Are these conditioned <s>dharmas</s>?' — those that were previously described as <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>. 'How they differ in characteristics' — '<s>rūpa</s>' (form) because it is impinged upon (<s>rūpyate</s>); feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) is experience; perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) is the apprehension of signs — and so on. 'The term "conditioned" [is used] because of having origination.' Or else, are some necessarily co-arisen as well? 'Some are' — for some are co-arisen but not necessarily co-arisen, such as those co-arisen with the eye and the rest. The consciousnesses and the rest [co-arisen] with the eye and the rest — because the eye and the rest have the states of <s>sabhāga</s> and <s>tatsabhāga</s>. Therefore he asks thus. 'All these <s>dharmas</s> [Tib. 112a] are fivefold' — by the method of five categories, the collection of all <s>dharmas</s> is thus established. The teaching of <s>dharmas</s> through the groupings of form and the rest [is] for the purpose of easy understanding. Therein, 'the unconditioned does not arise at all' — therefore no rule of co-arising is considered with respect to it. 'The smallest aggregate of form is a <s>paramāṇu</s> (atom)' — this is an aggregate-atom, not a substance-atom. For that which has no prior or posterior part — that [substance] stripped of all form is considered to be a substance-atom. Therefore he specifies: 'an aggregate-atom.'

children.translated_text: 'In the desire [realm], eight substances [compose] the soundless [atom]' —

body.text: iti. kāmadhātau yadā śabdo 'tra notpadyate. tadā niyatam aṣṭadravyaka eva bhavati nāto nyūnadravyakaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. In the desire-realm, when sound does not arise therein, [the atom] necessarily consists of exactly eight substances, not fewer.

body.text: iti. aparam indriyam asminn ity aparendriyaḥ. cakṣurādimān ity arthaḥ. yatra hi cakṣuḥ śrotrādi vā tatra kāyendriyeṇa bhavitavyaṃ tatpratibaddhavṛttitvāc cakṣurādīnāṃ. saśabdāḥ punar ete paramāṇava ity aṣṭadravyakādayaḥ saṃghātaparamāṇavaḥ saśabdā utpadyamānā yathākramaṃ nava daśaikādaśadravyakā utpadyante. yo 'ṣṭadravyakaḥ. sa navadravyakaḥ. yo navadravyakaḥ. sa daśadravyakaḥ. yo daśadravyakaḥ. sa ekādaśadravyaka iti. asti hīndriyavinirbhāgī śabdo 'pīti. indriyād vinirbhaktuṃ yo na śakyate. sa indriyāvinirbhāgī śabdaḥ. indriyāpṛthagvartīty arthaḥ. avinirbhogīti kecid bhuji paṭhanti.
body.translated_text: meaning: 'in which there is an additional faculty' — that is, one possessing the eye-faculty and the rest.
