For wherever the eye or the ear and so forth exist, the body-faculty must also be there, because the eye and the rest function in dependence upon it. But when these aggregate-atoms arise with sound, the eight-substance [atoms] and the rest become, in order, nine-, ten-, and eleven-substance [atoms]. An eight-substance [atom] becomes nine-substance; a nine-substance [atom] becomes ten-substance; a ten-substance [atom] becomes eleven-substance. 'For there is also sound that is inseparable from faculty' — sound that cannot be separated from a faculty is sound inseparable from faculty, meaning: sound that does not occur apart from a faculty. Some read '<s>avinirbhogī</s>' with the root <s>bhuj</s>.

body.text: katham avinirbhāge bhūtānāṃ kaścid eva saṃghātaḥ kaṭhina ityādi. kaṭhinaḥ pṛthivīdhātuḥ. dravo [Tib. 112b] 'bdhātuḥ. uṣṇas tejodhātuḥ. samudīraṇā
body.translated_text: 'How, despite non-separation of the elements, is a particular aggregate hard?' and so on. That which is hard is the earth-element. That which is fluid [Tib. 112b] is the water-element. That which is hot is the fire-element. That which is impelling

body.text: vāyudhātuḥ. tulyabhūtasadbhāvāt tulyarūpais tatsaṃghātair bhavitavyam ity abhiprāyaḥ. yad yatra paṭutamam iti vistaraḥ. yad dravyaṃ pṛthivyādilakṣaṇaṃ. yatra saṃghāte paṭutamaṃ sphuṭatamaṃ prabhāvataḥ śaktito na tu dravyataḥ udbhūtam utpannaṃ. tasya tatropalabdhiḥ. tasya dravyasya tatra saṃghāta upalabdhir grahaṇaṃ. sūcītūlīkulāpasparśavat. tatra sūcyo lohamayyaḥ pratītā loke. tūlyo vīraṇādipuṣpamūladaṇḍāḥ. yāḥ siṃkā iti prākṛtapratītāḥ. tāsāṃ sūcīnāṃ tūlīnāṃ ca kalāpaḥ. tasya sparśaḥ sūcītūlīkalāpasparśaḥ. tasya copalabdhiḥ. tasya paṭutamasya prabhāvata udbhūtasya bhūtasyeti. tatra tasyeveti. anena lakṣaṇena vatiḥ. etad uktaṃ bhavati. yathā tulye 'pi sūcīnāṃ tūlīnāṃ kalāpasadbhāve tīkṣṇatvāt sūcīnām eva sparśo vyaktam upalabhyate. na tūlīnām atīkṣṇatvāt. tathā kvacid eva saṃghāte kāṣṭhādike kaṭhinam upalabhyate. kvacid dravaḥ pānīye. kvacid uṣṇo 'gnau. kvacit samudīraṇā vāyau. na ca tatratatra saṃghāte catvāri mahābhūtāni na santi. saktulavaṇacūrṇarasavac ca. saktucūrṇānāṃ lavaṇacūrṇānāṃ ca yathā rasasyopalabdhiḥ. lavaṇacūrṇarasa eva vyaktam upalabhyate. na tu saktucūrṇarasaḥ. tadvad ihāpīti. saṃgrahadhṛtipaktivyūhanād iti. saṃgrahakarmaṇābdhātor astitvaṃ gamyate kāṣṭhādike. anyathā pāṃsumuṣṭivat tad viśīryate. yadi tatrābdhātur na syāt. dhṛtikarmaṇāpsu nauprabhṛtīnāṃ [Tib. 113a] pṛthivīdhātor astitvaṃ gamyate. paktikarmaṇā tejodhātor astitvaṃ gamyate. yadi hi tan na syāt kāṣṭhādikaṃ na pūtībhavet. vyūhanakarmaṇā vāyudhātor astitvaṃ gamyate. prasarpaṇaṃ hi tasya na syād vṛddhir vā yadi vāyudhātus tatra na syāt. evam anyatrāpi yojyaṃ. pratyayalābhe ca satīti vistaraḥ. pratyayānām agnyādīnāṃ lābhe sati kaṭhinādīnāṃ ca dravaṇādibhāvāt. dravaṇaghanatvādibhāvāt. tadyathāgnibhūte sati kkaṭhinasya lohasya dravaṇaṃ. tena jñāyate lohe 'bdhātur astīti. tathā dravasya śaityādipratyayalābhe kāṭhinyaṃ. tena jñāyate pṛthivīdhātor atrāstitvam iti. tathā kaṭhinasaṃgharṣād auṣṇyam upalabhyate. tena tejodhātor atrāstitvaṃ gamyate. iti evaṃ saṃbhavato 'nyatrāpi yojyaṃ. apsu śaityātiśayād auṣṇyaṃ gamyate ity apara iti bhadantaśrīlātaḥ. yasmād āpaḥ śītāḥ śītatarāḥ śītatamāś ca upalabhyante. tato jñāyate tejasas tatrānyataratamotpatteḥ śaityātiśayaḥ. tena ca tatra tejo 'stīti gamyate.
body.translated_text: is the wind-element. The intent is: because of the equal existence of the elements, those aggregates should consist of equal forms. 'Whatever is most acute therein' — and so on in detail. Whatever substance has the characteristic of earth and the rest — whatever in a given aggregate is most acute, most manifest, in terms of potency and capacity (not in terms of substance) — that is apprehended therein. That substance is apprehended in that aggregate. 'Like the contact of a bundle of needles and soft fibers.' Therein, needles are understood in the world as made of iron. Soft fibers are the flower-stalks of <s>vīraṇa</s> grass and the like — what are known in the vernacular as '<s>siṃkā</s>' (reed-stalks). A bundle of those needles and soft fibers — the contact of that is the contact of a bundle of needles and soft fibers. And the apprehension of that — of that [element] which is most acute, which has become manifest through potency — 'therein, of that alone' — by this characteristic is the analogy. What has been stated is this: just as, even when there is equal existence of needles and soft fibers in a bundle, only the contact of the needles is clearly apprehended because of their sharpness — not that of the soft fibers, because they are not sharp — so too, in some aggregate such as wood and the like, hardness is apprehended; in some, fluidity — in water; in some, heat — in fire; in some, impelling — in wind. And it is not the case that the four great elements do not exist in each of those aggregates. 'And like the taste of a mixture of barley-flour and salt-powder.' Just as, of the flavors of barley-powder and salt-powder, only the flavor of the salt-powder is clearly apprehended, but not the flavor of the barley-powder — so too here. 'From the functions of cohesion, sustaining, maturing, and dispersing' — from the function of cohesion, the existence of the water-element is inferred in wood and the like; otherwise, like a handful of dust, it would disintegrate — if the water-element were not there. From the function of sustaining, the existence of the earth-element is inferred in water — [as evidenced by] boats and the like [floating on it]. [Tib. 113a] From the function of maturing, the existence of the fire-element is inferred; for if it were not there, wood and the like would not decay. From the function of dispersing, the existence of the wind-element is inferred; for the spreading out or growth of that [substance] would not occur if the wind-element were not there. The same should be applied elsewhere as well. 'And when the appropriate conditions are obtained' — and so on in detail. When conditions such as fire and the like are obtained, the hard and the like undergo liquefaction and the like — liquefaction, solidification, and the like. For example, when fire is present, hard iron undergoes liquefaction; from this it is known that the water-element exists in iron. Likewise, when a liquid obtains conditions such as cold and the like, [it undergoes] hardening; from this it is known that the earth-element exists there. Likewise, from the friction of hard [substances], heat is apprehended; from this the existence of the fire-element there is inferred. Thus, the same should be applied elsewhere as is possible. 'In water, heat is inferred from the excess of cold — [this is the view of] another,' namely the Venerable <s>Śrīlāta</s>. Because waters are found to be cold, colder, and coldest — from this it is known that the excess of cold is due to the lesser or greater arising of fire there. And from this, the existence of fire there is inferred.

body.text: avyatibhede 'pīti vistaraḥ. taṃ matam ācāryo dūṣayati. yathā na ca
body.translated_text: 'Even despite non-intermixture' — and so on in detail. The <s>Ācārya</s> (<s>Vasubandhu</s>) criticizes that view. 'Just as not'

body.text: śabdasya dravyāntareṇa vyatibhedo miśrībhāvo 'sti atiśayaś ca bhavati svabhāvabhedāt paṭuḥ śabdaḥ paṭutaraḥ paṭutama iti. evam ihāpi bhavet. yathā ca vedanāyā na kenacid dravyāntareṇa vyatibhedo bhavatīti [Tib. 113b] svabhāvabhedāt tāratamyenātiśayaḥ. tathehapīti. nānena tejo'stitvaṃ gamyate. tā eva hy āpaḥ kāścic chītāḥ kāścic chītatarāḥ kāścic chītatamā iti. bījatas teṣu teṣāṃ bhāvo na svarūpata ity apara iti sautrāntikāḥ. bījataḥ śaktitaḥ sāmarthyata ity arthaḥ. na svarūpato na dravyata ity arthaḥ. śaktir eva hi nānāvidhāsti yayā yogibhir adhimokṣaviśeṣeṇa suvarṇadhātū rūpyadhātus tāmradhātur ity evamādayo dhātavaḥ kriyante. kasmād ity āha. saṃty asmiṃ dāruskandhe vividhā dhātava iti vacanāt. dhātuśaktayo hi tatraivaṃ bhagavatoktāḥ. na hi tatrātibahūnāṃ suvarṇarūpyādīnāṃ svarūpato 'vakāśo 'stīti.
body.translated_text: There is intermixture (<s>vyatibheda</s>), a blending, of sound with another substance, and there is gradation due to difference in intrinsic nature — a sharp sound, a sharper sound, the sharpest sound. Thus it should be here as well. And just as there is no intermixture of feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) with any other substance, [Tib. 113b] yet there is gradation by degree due to difference in intrinsic nature — so too here. By this, the existence of fire-element (<s>tejas</s>) is not established. For those very waters (<s>āpas</s>) — some are cold, some colder, some coldest. The <s>Sautrāntikas</s> say: their existence in those [elements] is by seed (<s>bīja</s>), not by intrinsic nature. 'By seed' means by capacity, by power — this is the meaning. 'Not by intrinsic nature' means not by substance — this is the meaning. For capacity itself is of various kinds, by which <s>yogins</s>, through special resolve (<s>adhimokṣa</s>), transform gold-ore, silver-ore, copper-ore, and such minerals. Why? He says: because of the statement 'In this log of wood there exist various minerals.' For thus the Blessed One declared the mineral-capacities therein. For there is no room for the intrinsic existence of the many gold, silver, and other [substances] therein.

body.text: kathaṃ vāyau varṇasadbhāva iti vaibhāṣikān evaṃ codayanti.
body.translated_text: Thus they challenge the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>: how is there the real existence of color (<s>varṇa</s>) in wind (<s>vāyu</s>)?

children.translated_text: In the Desire Realm, [atoms are] eight-substance (<s>aṣṭadravyaka</s>) —

body.text: iti niyame kathaṃ vāyau varṇo 'stīti nirdhāryate. na hi kathaṃcit tatra varṇa upalabhyate. śraddhānīya eṣo 'rtho nānumānīya iti vaibhāṣikāḥ. paramāptair ayam ukto 'rtha iti pratyetavyo nārtho 'numānasādhya ity abhiprāyaḥ. saṃsargato gandhagrahaṇād veti. asti vānumānam iti darśayati. gandhavatā tu dravyeṇa vāyoḥ saṃparkād gandha upalabhyate. sa ca gandho varṇaṃ na vyabhicarati. yatra hi gandhaḥ. tatra varṇena bhavitavyam iti. atra ca sādhanavacanaṃ. varṇavān vāyur gandhavattvāj [Tib. 114a] jātipuṣpavad iti.
body.translated_text: given this rule, how is it determined that color exists in wind? For color is not perceived there in any way. The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> say: this matter is to be accepted on faith, not through inference. The intent is: this meaning was stated by supremely authoritative persons, so it should be accepted — the matter is not to be established by inference. 'Or from the apprehension of smell through contact' — he shows that there is indeed an inference. When wind comes into contact with a substance possessing smell, smell is perceived. And that smell does not deviate from color. For wherever there is smell, there color must be. And here the statement of proof: 'Wind possesses color, because it possesses smell, [Tib. 114a] like a jasmine flower.'

body.text: rūpadhātau gandharasayor abhāva ukta iti.
body.translated_text: The absence of smell and taste in the Form Realm (<s>Rūpadhātu</s>) has been stated.

children.translated_text: 'Without smell, taste, olfactory, gustatory, and consciousness elements' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. tena tatratyāḥ paramāṇavaḥ ṣaṭsaptāṣṭā dravyakā iti. tatratyās tatra bhavāḥ. tatratyāḥ paramāṇavaḥ saṃghātaparamāṇavo 'dhikṛtāḥ. ya ihāṣṭadravyaka ukto nirindriyo 'śabdaḥ. sa tatra saḍdravyakaḥ. yo navadravyakaḥ kāyendriyā. sa saptadravyakaḥ. yo dasadravyako 'parendriyaḥ. so 'ṣṭadravyakaḥ. saśabdakāḥ punar ete saptāṣṭanavadravyakā ity avagantavyaṃ. uktarūpatvān na punar ucyanta iti. uktakalpatvān na punaḥ sūtryanta ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Therefore the atoms there are six-, seven-, or eight-substance. 'There' means existing there. The atoms there — the aggregate-atoms — are the subject. What here was called eight-substance without sense-faculty and without sound, that there is six-substance. What was nine-substance with the body-faculty, that is seven-substance. What was ten-substance with another faculty, that is eight-substance. With sound, these should be understood as seven-, eight-, and nine-substance respectively. 'Because of having been stated in the manner already described, they are not stated again' — the meaning is: because their pattern has already been taught, they are not formulated again in the <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: kiṃ punar atra dravyam eva dravyam iti vistaraḥ. mukhyavṛttyā yad dravyaṃ yasya svalakṣaṇam asti. tad dravyaṃ gṛhyate. āhosvid āyatanaṃ dravyam ity adhikṛtaṃ. āyatanam api hi dravyam iti śakyate vaktuṃ sāmānyaviśeṣalakṣaṇasadbhāvāt. kiṃ cātaḥ. kaś cāto doṣa ity arthaḥ. yadi dravyam eva dravyaṃ gṛhyate. yadi rūpaparyantalakṣaṇaṃ pṛthivyādiparamāṇudravyaṃ
body.translated_text: Now what exactly is 'substance' (<s>dravya</s>) here? — this is the elaboration. In the primary sense, that which has its own characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is substance — that substance is taken. Or is it that 'sense-base' (<s>āyatana</s>) is designated as substance? For a sense-base too can be called substance, because of possessing both general and particular characteristics. What follows from this? What fault results? — this is the meaning. If substance in the strict sense is taken as substance — if the substance of atoms of earth and so forth, which has the characteristic ending in visible form (<s>rūpa</s>),

body.text: gṛhyate. atyalpam idam ucyate. aṣṭadravyaka ityādi. saṃsthānagurutvalaghutvaślakṣṇatvakarkaśatvaśītajighatsāpipāsānāṃ saṃbhavato dravyāntarāṇāṃ kvacitkvacit sadbhāvāt. tathā ca sati yo 'ṣṭadravyakaḥ. sa navadravyako yāvac caturdaśadravyaka ity aṣṭadravyakaniyamo bhidyate. evaṃ navadravyakādiṣu yojyaṃ. evaṃrūpadhātāv [Tib. 114b] api ṣaṭsaptāṣṭadravyaniyamabhedo vaktavyaḥ. caturdravyako hi vaktavya iti. yasmād bhūtāny api pṛthivyādīni spraṣṭavyāyatanaṃ.
body.translated_text: is taken — then too little is said by 'eight-substance' and so forth. Because of the actual presence, in various cases, of additional substances such as shape (<s>saṃsthāna</s>), heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>), lightness (<s>laghutva</s>), smoothness (<s>ślakṣṇatva</s>), roughness (<s>karkaśatva</s>), cold (<s>śīta</s>), hunger (<s>jighatsā</s>), and thirst (<s>pipāsā</s>). And that being so, what is eight-substance would become nine-substance, up to fourteen-substance — thus the rule of eight-substance is broken. The same should be applied to nine-substance and so on. Similarly, [Tib. 114b] the breaking of the rule of six-, seven-, and eight-substance in the Form Realm must be stated. For it should be stated as four-substance, since the elements (<s>bhūta</s>s) — earth and so forth — are themselves the tangible sense-base.

body.text: iti vacanāt. tasmāt kāme caturdravyako 'śabdaḥ. rūpaṃ gandho rasaḥ spraṣṭavyam iti. saśabdas tu paṃcadravyaka iti vaktavyaṃ. yad āśrayabhūtam iti. pṛthivyādīni catvāri. yad āśrayibhūtam iti. rūpaṃ gandho rasaḥ spraṣṭvyaikadeśaś ca. tad evaṃ saṃsthānasya rūpe 'ntarbhāvāt. gurutvādīnāṃ ca spraṣṭavya iti. nātyalpam idam ucyate. nāpy atibahu. āśrayabhūtānāṃ spraṣṭavyāyatanān niḥkṛṣya caturdhā nirdeśāt. evam api bhūyānsīti vistaraḥ. yad bhūtacatuṣkam āśraya ekasyopādāyarūpasya nīlasya pītasya vā. na tad evānyasyopādāyarūpasya gandhasya rasasya vāśrayaḥ. kiṃ tarhi. anyad eva bhūtacatuṣkaṃ tasyāśraya iti vaibhāṣikasiddhāntaḥ. tatra punar jātidravyam iti. bhūtacatuṣkajātir atra gṛhyate. yā hy ekasya bhūtacatuṣkasya jātiḥ. tām anyāni bhūtacatuṣkāni nātikrāmanti. evaṃ vikalpena vaktum iti. kiṃcid atra dravyam eva dravyaṃ gṛhyate yad āśrayabhūtaṃ. kiṃcid atrāyatanadravyaṃ gṛhyate yad āśrayibhūtaṃ. yac caitad āśrayabhūtaṃ. taj jātyā gṛhyata iti. chandato hi vācāṃ pravṛttiḥ. arthas tu parīkṣya iti. chandata icchātaḥ saṃkṣepavistaravidhānānuvidhāyinyo vācaḥ pravartante. arthas tu tāsāṃ parīkṣyaḥ. kim evaṃ niyatasahotpādāni [Tib. 115a] tāni bhavanti. na bhavantīti. yogācāracittās tu saṃghātāvasthāne bhūtānāṃ bhautikānāṃ ca niyamaṃ varṇayanti. katham iti. ucyate. asti samudāya ekabhautikas tadyathā śuṣko mṛtpiṇḍaḥ. asti dvibhautikaḥ sa evārdraḥ. asti tribhautikaḥ sa evoṣṇaḥ. asti yāvat sarvabhautikaḥ sa evārdra uṣṇaś ca mṛtpiṇḍo gamanāvasthāyām iti. upādāyarūpe 'pi yad upādāyarūpaṃ yasmin samudāye upalabhyate. tat tatrāstīti veditavyaṃ. asti samudāya ekopādāyarūpikaḥ. tadyathā prabhā. asti dvyupādāyarūpikaḥ. tadyathā saśabdagandho vāyuḥ. tryupādāyarūpikaḥ. tadyathā dhūmaḥ. tasya rūpagandhaspraṣṭavyaviśeṣaprabhāvitatvāt. spraṣṭavyaviśeṣaḥ punar atra laghutvaṃ veditavyaṃ. caturupādāyarūpikaḥ. tadyathā guḍapiṇḍaḥ. paṃcopādāyarūpikaḥ. tadyathā sa eva saśabdaḥ. ity evamādy api
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Therefore in the Desire Realm, [a unit] without sound is four-substance: visible form, smell, taste, and tangible. With sound, it should be stated as five-substance. 'That which is the support' — the four [elements], earth and so forth. 'That which is the supported' — visible form, smell, taste, and a portion of the tangible. Thus, since shape is included in visible form, and heaviness and the rest in the tangible — neither too little is said nor too much. Because the tangible sense-base, which is the support, is separated and taught in four ways. 'Even so, there are more' — this is the elaboration. The four-element group that is the support of one derived form (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>) — of blue or yellow — that same [group] is not the support of another derived form such as smell or taste. Rather, a different four-element group is its support — this is the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> doctrine. There, 'class-substance' (<s>jātidravya</s>) — the class (<s>jāti</s>) of the four-element group is taken here. For the class of one four-element group is not transcended by other four-element groups. Thus it is to be stated alternatively: some substance here is taken as substance proper — that which is the support; some substance here is taken as sense-base substance — that which is the supported. And that which is the support is taken by class. For speech proceeds according to the speaker's wish (<s>chandas</s>), but the meaning must be examined. 'According to wish' means according to inclination — speech proceeds in conformity with the arrangement of brevity and elaboration; but the meaning of those [statements] must be examined. Are they necessarily co-arisen in this way? [Tib. 115a] No, they are not. But the <s>Yogācāras</s> describe the rule for the co-existence of elements and derived forms in the aggregate state. How? It is said: there is an aggregate with one derived form, such as a dry clay ball. There is one with two derived forms — that same [clay ball] when moist. There is one with three — that same when heated. There is one up to all derived forms — that same moist and heated clay ball in a state of movement. Regarding derived form too, whatever derived form is perceived in whatever aggregate — that should be understood as existing therein. There is an aggregate with one derived form, such as radiance (<s>prabhā</s>). There is one with two derived forms, such as wind with sound and smell. One with three, such as smoke — because it is pervaded by specific visible form, smell, and tangible qualities. The specific tangible quality here should be understood as lightness. One with four derived forms, such as a lump of raw sugar (<s>guḍa</s>). One with five, such as that same [lump] with sound. And so on

body.text: vaktavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: should be stated.

body.text: (II.24ab) śeṣāṇāṃ vaktavya iti cittacaittānāṃ viprayuktānāṃ ca.
body.translated_text: (II.24ab) 'Of the remaining' — meaning: of mind and mental factors, and of those dissociated from mind (<s>viprayukta</s>), it should be stated.

body.text: iti. na cittaṃ caittair vinā utpadyate. nāpi caittā vinā cittenety avadhāryate. na tu sarvaṃ cittaṃ sarvacaittaniyatasahotpādaṃ. nāpi sarvacaittāḥ sarvacittaniyatasahotpādā iti.
body.translated_text: thus. It is determined that mind does not arise without mental factors, nor do mental factors arise without mind. But not every mind necessarily co-arises with all mental factors, nor do all mental factors necessarily co-arise with every mind.

body.text: Tib. 115b
body.translated_text: Tib. 115b

body.text: sarvaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇair
body.translated_text: 'All with the conditioned characteristics' —

body.text: iti. saṃskṛtalakṣaṇair yad yuktaṃ. tat sarvaṃ taiḥ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇair jātyādibhir avaśyaṃ sahotpadyate. kiṃ punas tad ity āha. yatkiṃcid utpadyate rūpaṃ cittaṃ caitasikāś cittaviprayuktāś ceti. pūrvam eva hy asaṃskṛtaṃ bahiṣkṛtaṃ. tatrāsaṃskṛtaṃ naivotpadyate iti vacanāt. vikalpārtho vāśabda iti. kiṃcit prāptyā sahotpadyate yat sattvasaṃkhyātaṃ. kiṃcin na yad asattvasaṃkhyātam iti vikalpaḥ. pratisaṃkhyāpratisaṃkhyānirodhayor yady api prāptir asti na tu tāv utpadyete iti na tayor grahaṇaṃ. sahotpādananiyamo hy ayam ārambha iti. asattvasaṃkhyātasya prāptir nāstīti kim atra kāraṇaṃ. sarvasattvasādhāraṇatvāt. sahajayaiva ca prāptyā prāptyā prāptimān sahotpadyate. na pūrvapaścātkālajayety avagantavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. Whatever is conjoined with the conditioned characteristics — all of that necessarily co-arises with those conditioned characteristics, namely arising (<s>jāti</s>) and the rest. What is that? He says: whatever arises — form, mind, mental factors, and those dissociated from mind. For the unconditioned has already been excluded. There, 'the unconditioned does not arise at all' — because of this statement. The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) indicates an alternative. Some [things] co-arise with acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>) — those that belong to a sentient being. Some do not — those that do not belong to a sentient being — this is the alternative. Although there is acquisition of analytical and non-analytical cessation, those two do not arise, so they are not included. For this undertaking concerns the rule of co-arising. The question arises: what is the reason that what does not belong to a sentient being has no acquisition? Because it is common to all sentient beings. And one should understand that [a being] co-arises with its co-born acquisition by that very acquisition — not by one from an earlier or later time.

body.text: (II.24cd) gativiṣaya iti. utpattiviṣaya ity arthaḥ. mahābhūmikā iti. mahattvaṃ sarvacittabhavatvāt.
body.translated_text: (II.24cd) 'Destiny-domain' — meaning: birth-domain. 'Great ground' (<s>mahābhūmika</s>) — greatness is because of existing in all minds.

body.text: (II.25) ime kileti. kilaśabdaḥ paramatadyotane. svamataṃ tu chandādayaḥ sarvacetasi na bhavanti. tathā hy anenaivācāryeṇa paṃcaskandhake likhitaṃ. chandaḥ katamaḥ. abhiprete vastuni abhilāṣaḥ. adhimokṣaḥ katamaḥ. niścite vastuni tathaivāvadhāraṇam ityādi. cetanā cittābhisaṃskāra iti. cittapraspandaḥ praspanda [Tib. 116a] iva praspanda ity arthaḥ. viṣayanimittagrāha iti. viṣayaviśeṣarūpagrāha ity arthaḥ. sparśa indriyaviṣayavijñānasaṃnipātajā spṛṣṭir iti. indriyaviṣayavijñānānāṃ saṃnipātāj jātā spṛṣṭiḥ. spṛṣṭir iva spṛsṭiḥ. yadyogād indriyaviṣayaviṣayavijñānāny anyonyaṃ spṛśantīva sa sparśaḥ. dharmapravicaya iti. pravicinotīti pravicayaḥ. pravicīyante vā anena dharmā iti pravicayaḥ. yena saṃkīrṇā iva dharmāḥ puṣpāṇīva pravicīyante uccīyanta ity arthaḥ. ime sāsravā ime 'nāsravāḥ. ime rūpiṇaḥ ime 'rūpiṇa iti. dharmāṇāṃ pravicayaḥ dharmapravicayaḥ. pratītatvāt prajñeti vaktavye ślokabandhānuguṇyena matir iti kārikāyām uktaṃ. smṛtir ālambanasaṃpramoṣa iti. yadyogād ālambanaṃ na mano vismarati. tac cābhilapatīva. sā smṛtiḥ. manaskāraś
body.translated_text: (II.25) 'These indeed' (<s>ime kila</s>) — the particle <s>kila</s> indicates another's position. But his own view is that desire (<s>chanda</s>) and the rest do not exist in every mind. For this same master wrote in the <s>Pañcaskandhaka</s>: 'What is desire? It is longing with respect to a desired object. What is resolve (<s>adhimokṣa</s>)? It is the ascertainment of a determined object as just so' — and so forth. 'Volition (<s>cetanā</s>) is the mental formation of mind' — a stirring (<s>praspanda</s>) of mind, an impulse as it were — this is the meaning. 'The grasper of the sign of the object' — the grasper of the specific form of the object — this is the meaning. 'Contact (<s>sparśa</s>) is the touching born from the conjunction of sense-faculty, object, and consciousness' — the touching born from the conjunction of sense-faculty, object, and consciousness — a touching as it were. That by conjunction with which sense-faculty, object, and consciousness seem to touch one another — that is contact. 'Discrimination of <s>dharmas</s>' (<s>dharmapravicaya</s>) — that which discriminates is discrimination; or, that by which <s>dharmas</s> are discriminated is discrimination — the meaning is: by which <s>dharmas</s>, as if mixed together, are discriminated, sorted out like flowers. 'These are with outflows, these are without outflows; these are material, these are immaterial' — the discrimination of <s>dharmas</s> is <s>dharmapravicaya</s>. Though it should be called <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) because it is understood, <s>mati</s> (intelligence) is said in the verse for metrical reasons. '<s>Smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is the non-forgetting of the object' — that by which the mind does not forget the object, and as it were labels it — that is mindfulness. 'Attention (<s>manaskāra</s>)

body.text: cetasa ābhoga iti. ālambane cetasa āvarjanam. avadhāraṇam ity arthaḥ. manasaḥ kāro manaskāraḥ. mano vā karoti āvarjayatīti manaskāraḥ. adhimuktis tadālambanasya guṇato 'vadhāraṇam. rucir ity anye. yathāniścayaṃ dhāraṇeti yogācāracittāḥ. samādhiś cittasyaikagrateti. agram ālambanam ity [Tib. 116b] eko 'rthaḥ. yadyogāc cittaṃ prabandhena ekatrālambane vartate. sa samādhiḥ. yadi samādhiḥ sarvacetasi bhavati. kim arthaṃ dhyāneṣu yatnaḥ kriyate. balavatsamādhiniṣpādanārthaṃ.
body.translated_text: is the engagement of mind' — the turning of mind toward the object, the fixing — this is the meaning. The action of mind is attention (<s>manaskāra</s>); or, mind acts, turns [toward the object] — that is attention. 'Resolve (<s>adhimukti</s>) is the ascertainment of that object in terms of its qualities.' Others say: inclination (<s>ruci</s>). The <s>Yogācāras</s> say: maintaining according to one's determination. '<s>Samādhi</s> (concentration) is one-pointedness of mind' — [Tib. 116b] 'point' (<s>agra</s>) means object — this is one meaning. That by which mind continues in a stream upon a single object — that is <s>samādhi</s>. If <s>samādhi</s> exists in every mind, why is effort made in the <s>dhyānas</s>? For the purpose of producing powerful <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text: katham ekasmiṃś citte daśānāṃ bhinnalakṣaṇānāṃ caittānām astitvaṃ gamyata iti ata āha. sūkṣmo hi cittacaittānāṃ viśeṣa iti vistaraḥ. sa eṣa viśeṣaḥ cittacaittānāṃ durlakṣyaḥ prabandheṣv api tāvat kiṃ punaḥ kṣaṇeṣu kālaparyantalakṣaṇeṣu. rūpiṇīnām api oṣadhīnāṃ mūrtānām api kāsāṃcit harītakīprabhṛtīnāṃ bahurasānāṃ ṣaḍrasānām indriyagrāhyā jihvendriyagrāhyāḥ duravadhārā duḥparicchedā bhavanti. kiṃ punaḥ ye dharmā amūrtā buddhigrāhyā manovijñānamātragrāhyāḥ. tasmād āptopadiṣṭā iti kṛtvā tathaiva te pratipattavyā ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: How is the existence of ten mental factors with distinct characteristics in a single mind established? Therefore he says: 'For the distinction of mind and mental factors is subtle' — this is the elaboration. This distinction of mind and mental factors is hard to discern even in [mental] streams, how much more so in moments (<s>kṣaṇa</s>) that are the ultimate limit of time. Even among material things — among certain tangible medicinal herbs such as <s>harītakī</s> (chebulic myrobalan) that have many tastes, the six tastes that are graspable by the sense faculties, graspable by the tongue-faculty — they are hard to determine, hard to distinguish. How much more so those <s>dharmas</s> that are immaterial, graspable only by the intellect, graspable only by mind-consciousness. Therefore, because they are taught by authoritative persons, they should be accepted just as taught — this is the intent.

body.text: (II.26) śraddhā cetasaḥ prasāda iti. kleśopakleśakaluṣitaṃ cetaḥ śraddhāyogāt prasīdati. udakaprasādakamaṇiyogād ivodakaṃ. satyaratnakarmaphalābhisaṃpratyaya ity apare iti. ākāreṇa śraddhānirdeśaḥ. satyeṣu caturṣu ratneṣu ca triṣu karmasu ca śubhāśubheṣu tatphaleṣu ca iṣṭāniṣṭeṣu saṃty evaitānīty abhisaṃpratyayo 'bhisaṃpratipattiḥ śraddheti. apramādaḥ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ bhāvaneti. bhāvanā nāma kuśalānāṃ [Tib. 117a] pratilambhaniṣevaṇasvabhāvā.
body.translated_text: (II.26) 'Faith is the serenity of mind' — thus. The mind, polluted by defilements and secondary defilements, becomes serene through the application of faith. Just as a water-purifying [gem] —

body.text: iti vacanāt sā katham apramādo nāma caitasiko bhaviṣyati. yasmin sati sā pratilambhaniṣevaṇabhāvanā bhavati. so 'pramādaḥ tātparyalakṣaṇaḥ. ata āha. yā teṣu avahitateti. tad evaṃ sati bhāvanāhetāv ayaṃ bhāvanopacāraḥ kṛta iti. cetasa ārakṣeti. yaḥ sāṃkleśikebhyaś cittam ārakṣate. so 'pramāda iti. cittakarmaṇyateti. yadyogāc cittaṃ karmaṇyaṃ bhavati. sā cittakarmaṇyatā cittalāghavam ity arthaḥ. nanu ca sūtre kāyapraśrabdhir apy ukteti. kaś ca paryāyo yat praśrabdhisaṃbodhyaṃgadvayaṃ bhavati. asti kāyapraśrabdhir asti cittapraśrabdhiḥ. tatra yāpi kāyapraśrabdhiḥ. tad api praśrabdhisaṃbodhyaṃgam abhijñāyai saṃbhodhaye nirvāṇāya saṃvartate. yāpi cittapraśrabdhiḥ. tad api praśrabdhisaṃbodhyaṃgam abhijñāyai saṃbodhaye nirvāṇāya saṃvartata
body.translated_text: from this statement — how then will <s>apramāda</s> (non-heedlessness) be a separate mental factor? For when it [faith] is present, that attainment, practice, and cultivation —

body.text:
iti. katham iyam ekaivocyate. praśrabdhiś cittakarmaṇyateti. sā tu yathā kāyikī vedaneti. yathā cetasy api vedanā paramāṇusaṃcayātmakendriyāśrayatvāt kāyikīty ucyate tatheyam api praśrabdhir avagantavyā. kathaṃ sā bodhyaṃgeṣu yokṣyata iti asamāhitatvāt paṃcānāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ pṛcchati. tatra tarhīti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 117b] tatra sūtre kāyavaiśāradyam eva kāyakarmaṇyatā bhūtaviśeṣalakṣaṇā prītyadhyākṛtā. prītamanasaḥ kāraḥ praśrabhyata iti vacanāt. kathaṃ sā bodhyaṃgam iti. pṛthakkalāpatvāt sāsravatvāc ca na yujyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. prītiḥ prītisthānīyāś ca dharmāḥ prītisaṃbodhyaṃgam iti vistaraḥ. tīrthikāḥ kila bhagavacchrāvakān evam āhuḥ. śramaṇo bhavanto gautama evam āha. evaṃ yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ paṃca nivaraṇāni prahāya cetasa upakleśakarāṇi prajñādaurbalyakarāṇi sapta bodhyaṃgāni bhāvayateti. vayam apy evaṃ brūmaḥ. tatrāsmākam śramaṇasya ca gautamasya ko viśeṣo dharmadeśanāyāḥ. tebhyo bhagavatā etad upadiṣṭaṃ. paṃca santi daśa bhavanti. daśa santi paṃca vyavasthāpyante. pratighaḥ pratighanimittaṃ ca navāghātavastūni vyāpādanivaraṇam uktaṃ bhagavatā. tadānukūlyāt. tathā sapta santi caturdaśa bhavanti. caturdaśa santi sapta vyavasthāpyante. prītiḥ prītinimittaṃ cety anena bhedena. tadānukūlyād iti. na ca saṃkalpavyāyāmau prajñāsvabhāvāv iti. tayor yathākramaṃ vitarkavīryasvabhāvatvāt. na tau prajñāsvabhāvau. yadā ca triskandho mārgaḥ kriyate śīlaskandhaḥ samādhiskandhaḥ prajñāskandha iti. tatra prajñāskandhanirdeśa uktaṃ. prajñāskandhaḥ katamaḥ. samyagdṛṣṭiḥ samyaksaṃkalpaḥ samyagvyāyāma iti. upekṣā [Tib. 118a] cittasamateti. yadyogāc cittaṃ samam anābhoge vartate. sopekṣā saṃskāropekṣā nāma. trividhā hi upekṣā. vedanopekṣā saṃskāropekṣā apramāṇopekṣā ceti.
nanu coktaṃ durjñāna eṣāṃ viśeṣa iti. sūkṣmo hi cittacaittānāṃ viśeṣaḥ. sa eṣa duḥparicchedaḥ pravāheṣv api tāvad ityādi vacanāt. duḥkhena jñāyate durjñānaḥ. asti hi nāma durjñānam api jñāyate. yad aviruddhaṃ ekasmiṃś cittakṣaṇe dharmāntareṇa sparśādinā. idaṃ tu khalu atidurjñānaṃ yad virodhe 'py avirodha iti. ābhoganābhogayor ekasmiṃś cittakṣaṇe avirodho vyavasthāpyata iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. na hi viruddhayoḥ sukhaduḥkhayor ekasmiṃś cittakṣaṇe bhāvo dṛṣṭa iti. anyatrābhoga iti. anyatrālambane ābhogo 'nyatrānābhoga ity avirodhaḥ. evaṃjātīyakam atrānyad apy āyāsyatīti. virodhajātīyaṃ yathā vitarkavicārau. tayor hi lakṣaṇaṃ cittaudārikatā vitarkaḥ. cittasūkṣmatā vicāra iti.
body.translated_text: thus. How is this said to be one [single mental factor]? '<s>Praśrabdhi</s> (tranquility) is pliancy of mind' — but just as feeling is bodily [as well], so —

children.translated_text: 'Applied thought and sustained thought are [respectively] coarseness and subtlety [of mind]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. tayos tu ekatra citte virodha iti vakṣyate. yas tasya nayaḥ. so 'syapīti. paryāyeṇānayor vṛttir ity abhiprāyaḥ. hrīr apatrāpyaṃ ca paścād vakṣyate iti.
body.translated_text: from this statement. But 'there is mutual opposition of the two in a single mind' — this will be stated [later]. Whatever principle applies to that [case], the same applies to this one as well. In alternation —

children.translated_text: 'Shamelessness is non-regard for transgressions; <s>anapatrāpya</s> (recklessness) is not seeing danger in faults' —

body.text: atra viparyayagrahaṇāt. sa tu prajñātmaka iti. sa tv amohaḥ prajñāsvabhāvaḥ. prajñā ca [Tib. 118b] mahābhūmiketi.
body.translated_text: here, by taking the opposite [of these definitions]: 'But that [<s>amoha</s>] has the nature of wisdom' — that non-delusion has the nature of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). And wisdom is —

body.text: iti vacanāt. nāsau kuśalamahābhūmika evocyate. kiṃ tarhi. akuśalādibhūmiko 'pīti. aviheṭhaneti. yadyogāt paro na viheṭhyate. sāvihiṃsā vihiṃsāpratipakṣaḥ caitasikaḥ. cetaso 'bhyutsāha iti. kuśalakriyāyāṃ yaś cetaso 'bhyutsāhaḥ. tad vīryaṃ. yas tv akuśalādikriyāyāṃ cetaso 'bhyutsāhaḥ. naitad vīryaṃ. kausīdyam eva tat. pravacane paṭhyate. sīdanātmakatvāt. tathā hy uktaṃ bhagavatā. ito bāhyakānāṃ yad vīryaṃ kausīdyam eva tad iti.
body.translated_text: from this statement. It is not called exclusively a wholesome great-ground [mental factor]. Rather, it also belongs to the unwholesome and other grounds. '<s>Aviheṭhana</s>' (non-harmfulness) — if —

body.text: (II.27ab) moho nāmāvidyeti.
body.translated_text: (II.27ab) 'Delusion is namely ignorance' — thus.

children.translated_text: 'A <s>dharma</s> that is the opposite of knowledge — another [entity] — is ignorance.'

body.text: paścād vyākhyāyate. bhāvanāvipakṣo dharma iti. bhāvanāyā abhāvamātrapratipattir mā bhūd iti bhāvanāvipakṣa ity āha. evaṃ kauśīdyādiṣv api vyākhyeyaṃ. kāyagurutācittaguruteti. praśrabdhipratipakṣo dharmaḥ. yathā kāyikī vedaneti. yathā vedanā rūpīndriyāśrayatvāt caitasiky api kāyikīti vyākhyātā. tathā kāyikaṃ styānaṃ. paṃcavijñānakāyasaṃprayuktaṃ styānaṃ kāyikam ity ucyate. auddhatyaṃ cetaso 'vyupaśama iti. nṛtyagītādiśṛṃgāraveṣālaṃkārakādyauddhatyasaṃniśrayadānakarmakaś caitasiko dharmaḥ.
body.translated_text: This is explained later: 'a <s>dharma</s> that is the opposite of cultivation.' The word 'opposite of cultivation' is [used] lest one understand merely the absence of cultivation — [rather, it refers to] the opposite of cultivation —

body.text: na cātra styānaṃ paṭhyate ity abhidharme. prāptijño devānāṃ priyo na tv iṣṭijña [Tib. 119a] iti. pāṭhaprāmāṇyamātreṇa daśa kleśamahābhūmikāḥ prāptā ity etām eva prāptiṃ jānīte devānāṃ priyo na tv ācāryāṇām iṣṭim icchāṃ jānīte. ko 'yaṃ devānāṃ priyo nāma. rjukajātīyo devānāṃ priya ity eke vyācakṣate. aśaṭho hi devānāṃ priyo bhavati. mūrkho devānāṃ priya ity apare.
body.translated_text: 'And torpor (<s>styāna</s>) is not read here' — thus in the <s>Abhidharma</s>. 'One who knows attainments is dear to the gods, but not one who knows what is desired.' In the reading —

children.text: yo hīśvarāṇām iṣṭaḥ sa na tāḍanena śikṣata
children.translated_text: 'He who is desired by the powerful is not trained by beating' —

body.text: iti mūrkho bhavatīti. yathaivāmoha iti. yathaivamohaḥ kuśalamūlaṃ prajñāsvabhāvatvān mahābhūmika iti vyavasthāpito na kuśalamahābhūmika evety avadhāryate. tataś ca kuśalamahābhūmikeṣu na paṭhitaḥ. tathā muṣitasmṛtyādayo
body.translated_text: thus, he becomes a fool. 'Just as non-delusion' — just as non-delusion, being a root of the wholesome, having the nature of wisdom, is [classified as] a great-ground [mental factor] —

body.text: 'pi paṃca mahābhūmikatvāt na kleśamahābhūmikā evety avadhāryante. tataś ca ime na kleśamahābhūmikamadhye paṭhyante. katham ity āha. smṛtir eva hi kliṣṭā muṣitasmṛtitā. samādhir eva kliṣṭo vikṣepa ity evamādīti. ādiśabdena prajñaiva kliṣṭā asaṃprajanyaṃ. manaskāra eva kliṣṭo 'yoniśomanaskāraḥ. adhimuktir eva kliṣṭā mithyādhimokṣa iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: the five too, because they are great-ground [mental factors], are not to be restricted to being exclusively defilement-great-ground. Therefore, these are not defilement-great-ground —

body.text: ata evocyata iti vistaraḥ. yata evaṃ smṛtyādayo muṣitasmṛtitādayo vyavasthāpyante. naitadvyatiriktā. ata evocyate catuṣkoṭika iti. ye mahābhūmikāḥ kleśamahābhūmikā api ta iti kākvāpṛcchati. catuṣkoṭikāḥ. syur mahābhūmikāḥ na kleśamahābhūmikāḥ. [Tib. 119b] syuḥ kleśamahābhūmikā na mahābhūmikāḥ. syur mahābhūmikāś ca kleśamahābhūmikāś ca. syur naiva mahābhūmikā na kleśamahābhūmikāḥ. tṛtīyā smṛtyādaya iti. ye muṣitasmṛtyādayaḥ paṃca yathoktāḥ. ete hi mahābhūmikāḥ kleśamahābhūmikāś ca. caturthī etān ākārāṃ sthāpayitveti. uktanirmuktā dharmāḥ kuśalamahābhūmikādayaś caitasikā rūpādayaś cānya iti. teṣām anyathā catuṣkoṭika iti. dvitīyāyāṃ koṭyāṃ vikṣepaḥ prakṣeptavyaḥ. na tu tṛtīyāyām. ata evaṃ vaktavyaṃ. prathamā koṭiḥ pūrvavat. dvitīyā āśraddhyaṃ kausīdyaṃ avidyā auddhatyaṃ pramādo vikṣepaś ca. tṛtīyā smṛtyādayaś catvāraḥ. muṣitāsmṛtyasaṃprajanyāyoniśomanaskāramithyādhimokṣā ity arthaḥ. caturthī pūrvavat. yat tūktaṃ na cātra styānaṃ paṭhyata iti. tān pratibravīti. styānaṃ punar iṣyata iti vistaraḥ. tasyāpāṭhe kasyāparādha iti. kim asya styānasya apāṭhe mamāparādhaḥ. kim ābhidhārmikasyeti. abhidharmakārasyāyam aparādho na mamety abhiprāyaḥ. styānasya sarvakleśasaṃyogitvenābhimatatvāt. evaṃ tv āhur iti. tatra śāstre styānasyāpāṭhe kāraṇam āhur ābhidhārmikāḥ. kṣiprataraṃ kileti. [Tib. 120a] kilaśabdo 'saṃbhāvanāyāṃ. kathaṃ hi nāma kliṣṭo dharmaḥ śuklasya samādher anuguṇo bhaviṣyati. layauddhatye hi samādhiparipaṃthinī. tat kathaṃ paripaṃthy evānuguṇe. na hy ete jātu sahacariṣṇutāṃ jahīta iti. na hy ete styānauddhatye kadācit sahacaradharmatāṃ tyajata ity arthaḥ. tathāpi yad yasyādhimātram iti. evam api ca styānam auddhatyaṃ vā yasya pudgalasyādhimātraṃ. sa pudgalas taccaritaḥ styānacarita auddhatyacārito vāvagantavyaḥ. kvacid dhi kalāpe kaścid dharma udbhūto bhavatīti. nānyatreti kuśalādiṣu.
body.translated_text: 'Hence it is said' — thus the elaboration. Since in this way, mindfulness and the rest, and confused-mindfulness and the rest, are established [as distinct categories], these [defilement-great-ground factors] are not other than those [previously mentioned ones] —

body.text: (II.27cd)

children.translated_text: 'But in the unwholesome, shamelessness and recklessness' —

body.translated_text: (II.27cd)

body.text: tuśabdo viśeṣaṇe avadhāraṇe vā. akuśala eveti.
body.translated_text: The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) is for specification or for restriction. Meaning: 'only in the unwholesome.'

body.text: iti. parītto 'lpakaḥ. ko 'sau. avidyāmātraṃ. avidyaiva kevalety arthaḥ. tenāvidyāmātreṇeti. nānyena rāgādinā kleśena. bhāvanāheyeneti. na darśanaheyena. manobhūmikenaiveti. na paṃcavijñānakāyikena. yasmād ime krodhādaya upakleśā manobhūmikā eva bhavanti. ato manaḥsaṃprayogāt parīttakleśabhūmikā ucyante. rāgādikalāpe hy avaśyam avidyayā bhavitavyam iti na parītto rāgādikaḥ. tad evaṃ ye sarvatra caitasike. te mahābhūmikā. ye kuśala eva. te kuśalamahābhūmikāḥ. [Tib. 120b] ye kliṣṭe nivṛte cākuśale ca. te kleśamahābhūmikāḥ. yo tv akuśala eva. te 'kuśalamahābhūmikāḥ. ye parīttakleśasaṃprayukte cetasi. te parīttakleśabhūmikāḥ. eṣāṃ tu nirdeśa upakleśeṣu kariṣyata iti. anuśayanirdeśe.
body.translated_text: Thus. 'Limited' means small. What is that? Ignorance alone (<s>avidyāmātra</s>). The meaning is: ignorance only. Therefore, 'by ignorance alone' — not by another affliction such as desire and the rest. 'To be abandoned by cultivation' — not by insight. 'Pertaining to the mind-ground only' — not pertaining to the five sense-consciousness groups. Because these <s>krodha</s> (anger) and other secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>) belong to the mind-ground only. Therefore, because of association with the mind, they are called 'limited-affliction-ground.' For in a group of desire and the rest, ignorance must necessarily be present, so desire and the rest are not limited. Thus, those mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>) that exist in every [mind-moment] are the great ground (<s>mahābhūmika</s>). Those that exist only in the wholesome are the wholesome great ground (<s>kuśalamahābhūmika</s>). [Tib. 120b] Those in the afflicted, covered, and unwholesome are the affliction great ground (<s>kleśamahābhūmika</s>). Those that are only unwholesome are the unwholesome great ground (<s>akuśalamahābhūmika</s>). Those in a mind associated with limited afflictions are the limited-affliction-ground (<s>parīttakleśabhūmika</s>). The exposition of these will be made in the section on secondary afflictions — in the exposition of latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>).

body.text: (II.29-31) anye 'pi cāniyatā iti. ye kadācit kuśale kadācid akuśale kadācid avyākṛte cetasi bhavaṃti. middhādaya iti. ādiśabdenārativijṛṃbhikātandrībhakte 'samatādaya upakleśāḥ kleśāś ca rāgādāyo 'py aniyatatvena gṛhyante. na hy ete rāgādayaḥ paṃcānāṃ prakārāṇām anyatamasmiṃ niyatā bhavanti. na mahābhūmikās sarvatra cetasy abhāvāt. na kuśalamahābhūmikāḥ kuśalatvayogāt. na kleśamahābhūmikāḥ sarvatra kliṣṭe tadabhāvāt. na hi sapratighe cetasi rāgo bhavati sarāge ca cetasi pratighaḥ. iti evam anye 'pi kleśā vaktavyāḥ. atrācāryavasumitraḥ saṃgrahaślokam āha.
body.translated_text: (II.29-31) 'And others that are indeterminate' — those that sometimes exist in a wholesome mind, sometimes in an unwholesome [mind], and sometimes in an indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) mind. '<s>Middha</s> (torpor) and the rest' — by the word 'and the rest,' secondary afflictions such as dissatisfaction (<s>arati</s>), yawning (<s>vijṛmbhikā</s>), drowsiness (<s>tandrī</s>), and lack of equanimity (<s>asamatā</s>), as well as afflictions such as desire (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest, are included as indeterminate. For these — desire and the rest — are not fixed in any one of the five categories. Not great ground, because of their absence in every mind-moment. Not wholesome great ground, because of being connected with wholesomeness [only sometimes]. Not affliction great ground, because of their absence in every afflicted [mind] — for desire does not exist in a mind with aversion, nor aversion in a mind with desire. Thus other afflictions too should be stated. Herein, Master <s>Vasumitra</s> states a summary verse.

body.text:
vitarkacārakaukṛtyamiddhapratighasaktayaḥ
mānaś ca vicikitsā cety aṣṭāv aniyatāḥ smṛtā
body.translated_text:
<s>Vitarka</s> (applied thought), <s>cāra</s> (sustained thought), <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret), <s>middha</s> (torpor), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), <s>sakti</s> (attachment),
<s>māna</s> (pride), and <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt) — these eight are declared indeterminate.

body.text: iti. tad idam aṣṭaniyamavacanaṃ na budhyāmahe. dṛṣṭayo 'pi kasmān nāniyatā iṣyante. na hi sapratighe savicikitse vā citte mithyādṛṣṭiḥ pravartate.
body.translated_text: Thus. 'We do not understand this statement of eight being fixed.' Why are the [wrong] views also not accepted as indeterminate? For wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) does not operate in a mind with aversion or in one with doubt.

children.text:
āveṇikatve 'kuśale dṛṣṭiyukte ca [Tib. 121a] viṃśatiḥ
kleśaiś caturbhiḥ krodhādyaiḥ kaukṛtyenaikaviṃśatir
children.translated_text:
'In the distinctive unwholesome and in that conjoined with views, [Tib. 121a] twenty;
with the four afflictions — <s>krodha</s> (anger) and the rest — and with regret, twenty-one' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. tasmād yadvā tat vedam uktam iti paśyāmaḥ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Therefore, whatever that may be, we regard it as what has been stated.

body.text: kāmāvacaraṃ tāvat paṃcavidham iti. kuśalam ekaṃ. akuśalaṃ dvividham. āveṇikam avidyāmātrasaṃprayuktaṃ rāgādyanyakleśasaṃprayuktaṃ ca. avyākṛtam api dvividhaṃ. nivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ satkāyāntagrāhadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktaṃ. anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ ca vipākajādīni. kukṛtabhāvaḥ kaukṛtyam iti. arthasya kukṛtasya dharmaḥ. sa tu caitasika iti na saṃbadhyate. tasmād āha. iha tu
body.translated_text: The desire-realm [mind] is first fivefold. The wholesome is one. The unwholesome is twofold: the distinctive (<s>āveṇika</s>), associated with ignorance alone, and that associated with other afflictions such as desire and the rest. The indeterminate is also twofold: the covered-indeterminate (<s>nivṛtāvyākṛta</s>), associated with the views of self-existence (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and of extreme views (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>); and the uncovered-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>), which has the nature of maturation-born and the like. The state of having been wrongly done is regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) — it is a property of what was wrongly done. But since that is a mental factor, it does not fit. Therefore he says: 'Rather, here

body.text: punaḥ kaukṛtyālambano dharma iti. kiṃsvabhāva ity āha. cetaso vipratisāra iti. yadi kaukṛtyālambano dharmaḥ kaukṛtyam ucyate. tatsaṃprayuktā apy anye cittacaittāḥ kaukṛtyaṃ prāpnuvanti. na prāpnuvanti. teṣām aprādhānyāt. vipratisārāvasthāyāṃ hi kaukṛtylakṣaṇaṃ caitasikaṃ kaukṛtyākāram udbhūtavṛttikam. anye cittacaittās tadākāreṇānuvartaṃte. kasyacid eva hi dharmasya kasmiṃścic cittakalāpe prādhānyam iti varṇayaṃti. śūnyatālambanavimokṣamukhaṃ śūnyateti. skandhānām antarvyāpārapuruṣarahitālambanaṃ vimokṣamukhaṃ samādhiviśeṣaḥ śūnyatety ucyate. vinīlakavyādhmātakādyaśubhālambanaḥ alobhaḥ aśubhety ucyate. bhāvanāsaṃbaddhatvāt strīliṃganirdeśaḥ. aśubhā bhāvaneti. tathehāpi kaukṛtyālambanaś caitasiko dharmaḥ kaukṛtyam iti. [Tib. 121b] sthānena sthāninām atideśaḥ. sarvo grāma āgata iti. sabhūmikaḥ śālāsamudāyo grāmaḥ. sthāniṣu manuṣyeṣv āgateṣu vaktāro bhavaṃti sarvo grāma āgata iti. evaṃ sarvo deśa āgata iti. sthānabhūtaṃ ca kaukṛtyaṃ vipratisārasyeti. vipratisārālambanatvāt. tasmād yuktas tathānirdeśaḥ. phale vā hetūpacāra iti. hetuḥ kaukṛtyaṃ. phalaṃ vipratisāraḥ. tasmiṃ phale hetur upacaryate. hetuvācakena śabdena phalam ucyata ity arthaḥ. yathā ṣaḍ imāni sparśāyatanāni paurāṇaṃ karmeti. pūrvajanmakṛtasya paurāṇasya karmaṇaś cakṣurādīni ṣaṭ sparśāyatanāni phalāni. teṣu yathā karmopacaryate. tadvat. yat tarhy akṛtālambanaṃ tat kathaṃ kaukṛtyam iti. yad akṛtaṃ. tan na kṛtam iti matvā codayati. akṛte 'pi kṛtākhyā bhavatīti. akṛte 'py arthe kṛtaśabdaprayogo bhavati. katham ity āha. na sādhu mayā kṛtam yat. tan na kṛtam iti. kṛtam iva tad iti kṛtvā. yat kuśalam akṛtvā tapyata iti. yat kuśalaṃ dānādikaṃ akṛtvā tapyate paścāt tāpībhavati. tat kuśalaṃ. akuśalaṃ ca kṛtvā kiṃ. tapyata iti adhikṛtaṃ. yac cākuśalaṃ prāṇātipātādikaṃ kṛtvā tapyate. tad api kuśalaṃ. viparyayād akuśalaṃ. yad akuśalam akṛtvā tapyate kuśalaṃ ca kṛtveti. yat pāpam akṛtvā paścāt tāpībhavati na sādhu mayā kṛtaṃ yat. [Tib. 122a] tan na kṛtam iti. tad akuśalaṃ kaukṛtyaṃ. yac ca kuśalaṃ dānādikaṃ kṛtvā paścāt tāpībhavati na sādhu mayā kṛtaṃ yad dānādikaṃ kṛtam iti. tad apy akuśalaṃ. tad etad ubhayam apy ubhayādhiṣṭhānaṃ bhavatīti. tad etat kaukṛtyam ubhayam api kuśalaṃ cākuśalaṃ ca ubhayādhiṣṭhānaṃ bhavati yathoktena vidhānena.
body.translated_text: regret is a <s>dharma</s> whose object is what was wrongly done.' What is its intrinsic nature? He says: 'Mental remorse (<s>vipratisāra</s>).' If regret is called a <s>dharma</s> whose object is what was wrongly done, then the other mind and mental factors associated with it should also be called regret. They should not, because of their non-predominance. For in the state of remorse, the mental factor characterized as regret, having regret as its aspect, has a prominent function. The other mind and mental factors follow along with that aspect. They explain that some particular <s>dharma</s> has predominance in some particular mind-group. 'The liberation-gate that has emptiness as its object is called emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>)' — the liberation-gate (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>), a special <s>samādhi</s>, that has as its object the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) devoid of an inner agent or person, is called emptiness. 'Non-attachment having the impure — blue-discolored, bloated, and so forth — as its object is called the impure (<s>aśubhā</s>).' The feminine gender is used because of connection with cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — 'impure cultivation.' Likewise here too, a mental-factor <s>dharma</s> whose object is what was wrongly done is [called] regret. [Tib. 121b] The designation of the basis is extended to those based upon it. 'The whole village has arrived' — a village is a collection of houses with their grounds. When the persons who are the basis have arrived, speakers say 'the whole village has arrived.' Similarly, 'the whole country has arrived.' And regret is the basis of remorse — because it is the object of remorse. Therefore such designation is appropriate. Or, it is a figurative expression of cause for effect. The cause is regret; the effect is remorse. The cause is figuratively applied to the effect — the meaning is that the effect is denoted by the word for the cause. Just as 'these six sense-bases are ancient <s>karma</s>' — the six sense-bases such as the eye are the results of <s>karma</s> performed in previous births, and just as <s>karma</s> is figuratively attributed to those [results], so too here. 'Then how is that whose object is what was not done [called] regret?' He raises the objection by thinking that what was not done was not performed. 'Even in what was not done, the designation "done" applies.' Even regarding what was not done, the use of the word 'done' occurs. How? He says: 'What I did not do well — that was not done.' Having conceived 'it is as if done,' [one thinks] 'what wholesome [deed] not having done, one suffers' — not having done some wholesome deed such as giving, one suffers, one feels subsequent burning. That wholesome [regret]. And having done unwholesome — what? 'One suffers' — this is what is under discussion. Having done some unwholesome act such as killing, one suffers. That too is wholesome. In the reverse, it is unwholesome: 'not having done what is unwholesome, one suffers, and having done what is wholesome' — when not having done evil, one subsequently feels burning, [thinking] 'I did not do well — [Tib. 122a] that was not done.' That regret is unwholesome. And having done some wholesome [deed] such as giving, one subsequently feels burning, [thinking] 'I did not do well in doing that giving.' That too is unwholesome. 'Thus both types have both bases' — this regret, both wholesome and unwholesome, has both bases in the manner stated.

body.text: iti. rāgādipṛthagbhūta ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: the meaning is: separate from desire and the rest.

body.text: caśabdaḥ akuśala ity anukarṣaṇārthaḥ. mahābhūmika eva kaścit prajñāviśeṣo dṛṣṭir iti. saṃtīrikā yā prajñā. sā dṛṣṭiḥ. sā cehākuśalā gṛhyate. tasmād āha. mithyādṛṣṭiś cetyādi
body.translated_text: the word 'and' serves to carry forward 'unwholesome.' 'A certain special wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) among the great ground [factors] is a view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>)' — that wisdom which is investigative is a view. And here it is taken as unwholesome. Therefore he says: 'Wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) and so forth' —

body.text: iti kaukṛtyena ceti. luptanidṛṣṭaś cakāro draṣṭavyaḥ. kleśaiś caturbhir ityādiṣu pratyekaṃ vākyaparisamāptir veditavyā. na hi rāgādayaḥ paraspareṇa saṃprayujyanta ity ābhidhārmikāḥ. sa ca kleśa āveṇikoktāś ca viṃśatir iti. daśa mahābhūmikāḥ ṣaṭ kleśamahābhūmikāḥ dvāv akuśalamahābhūmikau vitarko vicāraś ceti viṃśatiḥ. sa ca kleśo rāgaḥ pratigho māno vicikitsā cety ekaviṃśatiḥ. ekaviṃśatir bhavaty eveti kriyāvadhāraṇam avagantavyaṃ. krodhādibhir apīti.
body.translated_text: thus, 'with regret, and' — the dropped 'and' (<s>ca</s>)-particle should be understood. In 'with the four afflictions' and so forth, each statement should be understood as a complete sentence. For the <s>Ābhidhārmika</s>s [hold that] desire and the rest are not mutually associated. That affliction and the stated distinctive twenty — ten great ground [factors], six affliction great ground [factors], two unwholesome great ground [factors], and <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) — [make] twenty. That affliction — desire, aversion, pride, or doubt — [makes] twenty-one. 'There are exactly twenty-one' — the word-emphasis on the verb should be understood as a restriction. 'Also with <s>krodha</s> (anger) and the rest' —

body.text: Tib. 122b
body.translated_text: Tib. 122b

body.text: ebhir api saṃprayukte citte ekaviṃśatir eva caitasikāḥ. te cāveṇikoktāḥ pūrvavat. sa copakleśaḥ krodho vā yāvad vihiṃsā veti. kaukṛtyena ca saṃprayukte te ca pūrvoktāḥ tac ca kaukṛtyaṃ ity ekaviṃśatiḥ. kaukṛtyam api hy upakleśaḥ. svataṃtram iṣyate. samāsata āveṇika ity vistaraḥ. avidyāmātrasaṃprayukte cetasi akuśale dṛṣṭisaṃprayukte cākuśale viṃśatiḥ. anyakleśopakleśasaṃprayukte tv akuśala evaikaviṃśatiḥ.
body.translated_text: In a mind associated with these too, there are exactly twenty-one mental factors. And those are the distinctive [twenty] as stated before. And that secondary affliction — whether <s>krodha</s> or up to <s>vihiṃsā</s>. And in one associated with regret, those previously stated plus that regret [make] twenty-one. For regret too is a secondary affliction. It is considered independent. In brief, 'distinctive' and so forth in detail: in a mind associated with ignorance alone that is unwholesome, and in one associated with views that is also unwholesome — twenty. But in one associated with other afflictions or secondary afflictions that is only unwholesome — twenty-one.

body.text: nivṛtāvyākṛtam iti. kleśācchāditaṃ kuśalākuśalatvena avyākṛtaṃ yat. tan nivṛtāvyākṛtam. anācchāditaṃ tv anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ vipākajairyāpathikaśailpasthānikanairmāṇikasvabhāvaṃ. bahirdeśakā avyākṛtam api kaukṛtyam icchantīti. kaśmīramaṇḍalād ye bahirdeśasthitāḥ. te bahirdeśakāḥ. trayodaśeti kvacid anivṛtāvyākṛte kaukṛtyaṃ trayodaśamam adhikaṃ prakṣipya. middhaṃ pracalāyamānāvasthāyāṃ svapnadarśanāvasthāyāṃ vā kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtatvād iti. śāstre vacanāt. kathaṃ middhaṃ kuśalaṃ vaktavyam akuśalaṃ vaktavyam avyākṛtaṃ vaktavyam iti. āha. kuśalaṃ vaktavyam akuśalaṃ vaktavyam avyākṛtaṃ vaktavyam iti. yatra [Tib. 123a] dvāviṃśatiḥ. tatra trayoviṃśatir iti vistaraḥ. yatra dvāviṃśatiś caitasikā ity uktaṃ. tatra tan middhaṃ trayoviṃśaṃ. trayoviṃśateḥ pūraṇam ity arthaḥ. yatra trayoviṃśatiḥ kaukṛtyam adhikaṃ kvacid iti. tatra tan middhaṃ caturviṃśam. evaṃ yāvad anyatra dvādaśavyākṛte matā middhaṃ
body.translated_text: 'Covered-indeterminate' (<s>nivṛtāvyākṛta</s>) — that which is covered by afflictions and is indeterminate as wholesome or unwholesome is covered-indeterminate. But that which is uncovered is uncovered-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>), having the nature of maturation-born, path-of-conduct, craft-based, supernatural-creation-based, and intrinsic. The outsiders (<s>bahirdeśaka</s>) accept that regret is also indeterminate — those who reside outside the maṇḍala of <s>Kaśmīra</s> are the outsiders. 'Thirteen' — in the uncovered-indeterminate, [they] add regret as a thirteenth extra. <s>Middha</s> (torpor), in the state of drowsiness or in the state of seeing dreams, is wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate — because of the statement in the treatise: 'How should torpor be described as wholesome? As unwholesome? As indeterminate?' He says: 'It should be described as wholesome, as unwholesome, as indeterminate.' Where [Tib. 123a] there are twenty-two, there [become] twenty-three — this is the elaboration. Where twenty-two mental factors have been stated, there that torpor [becomes] the twenty-third, completing the count of twenty-three. Where there are twenty-three with regret added in some cases, there that torpor [becomes] the twenty-fourth. Likewise up to: elsewhere, 'in the twelve [that are] indeterminate, torpor

body.text: trayodaśaṃ vaktavyaṃ. bahirdeśakamatena tu kautṛtyādhike caturdaśaṃ middhaṃ bhavatīti yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: should be stated as the thirteenth.' But according to the outsiders' view, with regret added, torpor becomes the fourteenth — this should be construed.

body.text: (II.32) ato yathoktād iti. ato yathāvarṇitāc caittasahotpādaniyamāt. kaukṛtyaṃ middhaṃ ca sarvathā nāstīti. na kuśalaṃ nāpy avyākṛtaṃ kuta evākuśalam iti. sarvathā middhaṃ kaukṛtyaṃ ca nāsti. śāṭhyamadamāyā varjyā iti.
body.translated_text: (II.32) 'Therefore, from what has been stated' — therefore, from the described rule of co-arising of mental factors. 'Regret and torpor are in no way [present]' — neither wholesome nor indeterminate, how much less unwholesome. In no way do torpor and regret exist. '<s>Śāṭhya</s> (deceit), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), and <s>māyā</s> (fraud) are excluded' —

children.text:
māyā śāṭhyaṃ ca kāmādyadhyānayor brahmavañcanāt.
styānauddhatyamadā dhātutraya
children.translated_text:
'<s>Māyā</s> (fraud) and <s>śāṭhya</s> (deceit), in the desire [realm] and the first <s>dhyāna</s>, because of deceiving <s>Brahmā</s>;
<s>styāna</s> (sloth), <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness), and <s>mada</s> (intoxication) — in three realms' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. etāni varjyante teṣāṃ tatra sadbhāvāt. anyat sarvaṃ tathaiveti. kuśale citte pūrvavat dvāviṃśatiḥ. āveṇike dṛṣṭiyukte ca nivṛtāvyākṛte 'ṣṭādaśa kāmadhātuvat. rāgamānavicikitsānyakleśasaṃprayukte māyāśāṭhyamadopakleśasaṃprayukte ca ekānnaviṃśatiḥ. te ca sa ca kleśa upakleśo vā tatraikānnaviṃśo bhavati. anivṛtāvyākṛte vipākajairyāpathikanairmāṇike pūrvavat dvādaśa.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. These are excluded because of their existence there. 'Everything else is the same' — in the wholesome mind, twenty-two as before. In the distinctive [unwholesome] and view-conjoined [minds], the covered-indeterminate has eighteen, as in the desire realm. In those associated with desire, pride, doubt, or other afflictions, and in those associated with the secondary afflictions of fraud, deceit, or intoxication — nineteen. That affliction or secondary affliction becomes the nineteenth therein. In the uncovered-indeterminate — maturation-born, path-of-conduct, and supernatural-creation — twelve as before.

body.text: kaukṛtyamiddhākuśalāni ceti caśabdaḥ. kiṃ. na santīty [Tib. 123b] adhikṛtaṃ. śeṣaṃ tathaiva vitarkanyūnaṃ. yathāpratisiddhaṃ nāstīti. kaukṛtyamiddhākuśalavitarkā na santīty arthaḥ. vicāraś ca māyāśāṭhyaṃ cety apiśabdād iti. vicāraś ceti etāvati vaktavye vicāraś capīty apiśabdādhikyād arthādhikyam iti. māyāśāṭhyam api tatra nāstīty ayam aparārtho labhyate. madas tu nāpāsyate.
body.translated_text: the word 'and' [connects] 'regret, torpor, and unwholesome.' What? 'Do not exist' — this is what is under discussion. 'The rest is the same, minus applied thought.' 'As each is excluded, it does not exist' — the meaning is that regret, torpor, unwholesome [states], and applied thought do not exist. 'And sustained thought, and fraud and deceit too — from the word "also"' — where 'and sustained thought' alone should have been stated, the addition of the word 'also' indicates an additional meaning — fraud and deceit too do not exist there. This is the other meaning obtained. But intoxication (<s>mada</s>) is not removed.

body.text: iti vacanasāmarthyāt. śeṣaṃ tathaiveti. kuśale vitarkavicāranirmuktā viṃśatiḥ. āveṇike dṛṣṭiyukte ṣoḍaśa. rāgādikleśasaṃprayukte, madopakleśasaṃprayukte ca saptadaśa. daśa mahābhūmikāḥ ṣaṭ kleśamahābhūmikāḥ. sa ca kleśaḥ sa vopakleśaḥ. anivṛtāvyākṛte daśa mahābhūmikā eveti gamanīyaṃ. brahmaṇo hi yāvac chāṭhyam iti vistaraḥ. tatra śāṭhyapūrvakatvān māyāpi gṛhītā bhavati. parṣatsambandhān nordhvam iti. yeṣāṃ parṣad asti. teṣāṃ parṣadgrahaṇārthaṃ māyāśāṭhyaṃ pravartate. aṣṭau parṣadaḥ paṭhyante. kṣatriyaparṣat brāhmaṇaparṣat gṛhapatiparṣat śramaṇaparṣat cāturmahārājikaparṣat trayastriṃśatparṣat māraparṣat brahmaparṣat. tāsām anyatamo 'pi ūrdhvam ato nāstīti māyāśāṭhyabhāvaḥ. brahmaṇas tu parṣad asti. tasmād āha. sa hi svasyāṃ parṣadi niṣaṇṇo 'śvajitā bhikṣuṇā brahmalokagatena praśnaṃ
body.translated_text: by the force of that statement. 'The remainder is likewise' — in the wholesome [mind], twenty [mental factors] free from <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought). In the specific [mental factors], sixteen are associated with [wrong] views. In [minds] associated with <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and other afflictions, and in [minds] associated with <s>mada</s> (pride) and secondary afflictions — seventeen. Ten <s>mahābhūmika</s> (universals) and six <s>kleśamahābhūmika</s> (universal affliction-factors). That affliction or that secondary affliction. In the unobstructed-indeterminate [mind], one should understand [there are] just the ten <s>mahābhūmika</s>s. For as far as <s>śāṭhya</s> (deception) with respect to <s>Brahmā</s> — thus the elaboration. Therein, because <s>māyā</s> (deceit) is preceded by <s>śāṭhya</s>, <s>māyā</s> too is included. 'Not higher, because of the connection with assemblies' — for those who have assemblies, <s>māyā</s> and <s>śāṭhya</s> operate for the purpose of impressing the assembly. Eight assemblies are taught: the <s>Kṣatriya</s> assembly, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> assembly, the householder assembly, the ascetic assembly, the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> assembly, the <s>Trayastriṃśat</s> assembly, the <s>Māra</s> assembly, and the <s>Brahmā</s> assembly. None other than these exists higher — hence the absence of <s>māyā</s> and <s>śāṭhya</s>. But <s>Brahmā</s> has an assembly. Therefore he says: for he, seated in his own assembly, was asked a question by the monk <s>Aśvajit</s> who had gone to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>

body.text: pṛṣṭaḥ. kutremāni catvāri mahābhūtāni apariśeṣaṃ [Tib. 124a] nirudhyanta iti. aprajānann ārūpyadhātau catvāri mahābhūtāni aśeṣaṃ nirudhyanta ity anavabudhyamānaḥ kṣepaṃ kathāprakaraṇam akārṣīt. aham asmi brahmeti vistaraḥ. brahmety uktvā mahābrahmeti vacanaṃ brahmāntarebhya ātmano viśiṣṭatvapradarśanārthaṃ. īśvara īśanaśīlaḥ. kartā nirmātā sraṣṭā sṛja iti paryāyā uttarottaravyākhyāyogo vā. piteva pitṛbhūtaḥ. keṣāṃ. bhāvānāṃ.
body.translated_text: — 'Where do these four great elements cease without remainder?' [Tib. 124a] Not knowing — not comprehending that the four great elements cease without remainder in the formless realm — he made a diversionary conversation of dismissal. 'I am <s>Brahmā</s>' — thus the elaboration. Having said '<s>Brahmā</s>,' the statement 'Great <s>Brahmā</s>' is for the purpose of showing his own superiority over the other <s>Brahmā</s>s. '<s>Īśvara</s>' means one whose nature is to rule. 'Creator' (<s>kartā</s>), 'fashioner' (<s>nirmātā</s>), 'producer' (<s>sraṣṭā</s>) — <s>sṛj</s> and these are synonyms; or [they form] a successive explanatory sequence. 'Like a father' — one who has become like a father. Of what? Of beings.

body.text: (II.33) uktam etad iti vistaraḥ. yā bhūmir yac cittaṃ yāvantaś ca caittāḥ. sā bhūmis tac cittaṃ tāvantaś ca caittā ity uktam etat. tatra vihitam iti śāstre vihitaṃ. tatra vihitam iti kecit paṭhaṃti. sa eva cātrārthaḥ. guṇeṣu guṇavatsu ceti. svaparasāṃtānikeṣu maitrīkaruṇādiṣu guṇeṣu. guṇavatsu ca pudgaleṣu ācāragocaragauravādisaṃpanneṣu. yadyogād gauravaṃ na karoti. asāv agauravatā. nāsti gauravam asyety agauravaḥ. tadbhāvaḥ agauravatā caitasikaviśeṣaḥ. ko 'sāv iti. paryāyāv āhuḥ. apratīśatā abhayavaśavartiteti. śiṣyaṃ prati iṣṭa iti pratīśaḥ. gurusthānīyaḥ. nāsti pratīśo 'syeti apratīśaḥ. tadbhāvaḥ apratīśatā. bhāvābhidhānena caitto gṛhyate. bhayaṃ nāma mānasaś caitto dharmaḥ. bhayena vaśe vartituṃ śīlam asyeti bhayavaśavartī. na bhayavaśavartī [Tib. 124b] abhayavaśavartī tadbhāvo 'bhayavaśavartitā. tad eva cāhrīkyaṃ. nāsti hrīr asyety ahrīkaḥ. tadbhāva āhrīkyaṃ. sa ca gauravapratidvaṃdvo dharmaḥ. na tadabhāvamātraṃ.
body.translated_text: (II.33) 'This has been stated' — thus the elaboration. Whatever ground, whatever mind, and however many mental factors [there are] — that ground, that mind, and that many mental factors have been stated. 'Therein established' means established in the treatise. Some read 'therein established' [differently] — but the meaning is the same. 'With respect to qualities and those possessing qualities' — with respect to qualities such as <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), and so forth in one's own and others' mental continua, and with respect to persons possessing qualities — endowed with proper conduct, domain, reverence, and so forth. Due to connection with which one does not show respect — that is <s>agauravatā</s> (disrespect). 'There is no <s>gaurava</s> (respect) in him' — [he is] <s>agaurava</s> (disrespectful). The state of that is <s>agauravatā</s>, a specific mental factor. What is it? They state two synonyms: <s>apratīśatā</s> (lacking a mentor) and <s>abhayavaśavartitā</s> (not being under the control of fear). '<s>Pratīśa</s>' means 'one who is esteemed by the pupil' — one in the position of a teacher. 'He has no <s>pratīśa</s>' — [he is] <s>apratīśa</s>. The state of that is <s>apratīśatā</s>. By the abstract suffix, a mental factor is indicated. 'Fear' (<s>bhaya</s>) is a mental <s>dharma</s> of the nature of a mental factor. 'One whose nature is to be governed by fear' is <s>bhayavaśavartī</s>. 'Not <s>bhayavaśavartī</s>' [Tib. 124b] is <s>abhayavaśavartī</s>; the state of that is <s>abhayavaśavartitā</s>. And that itself is <s>āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness). 'He has no <s>hrī</s> (shame)' — [he is] <s>ahrīka</s> (shameless). The state of that is <s>āhrīkya</s>. And this <s>dharma</s> is the opposite of <s>gaurava</s> (respect) — not merely its absence.

children.translated_text: '<s>Atrapa</s> (moral recklessness) is seeing no danger in what is blameworthy' —

body.text: avācyam avadyam. ataś cāha. avadyaṃ nāma yad garhitaṃ sadbhir iti. tatrābhayadarśitā anapatrāpyam iti. avadye 'niṣṭaphalādarśitety arthaḥ. bhīyate 'smād ity atra bhayaśabdo 'pādānasādhanaḥ. tasmād bhayaśabdena aniṣṭaṃ phalam ucyate. abhayasya darśanaṃ abhayadarśiteti vistaraḥ. yadi tāvad evaṃ kriyeta na bhayam abhayaṃ. abhayaṃ draṣṭuṃ śīlam asyeti abhadyadarśī. tadbhāvo 'bhayadarśiteti. prajñā vijñāsyate. prajñayā hi abhayaṃ paśyati. atha punar evaṃ kriyate bhayaṃ draṣṭuṃ śīlam asyeti bhayadarśī. na bhayadarśī abhayadarśī. tadbhāvo 'bhayadarśitā. abhayadarśiteti avidyā vijñāsyate. tathā hy avidyāyogād bhayaṃ na paśyati. naiva hi darśanaṃ darśiteti vistaraḥ. na prajñā nāpy avidyā. kiṃ tarhi. tayoḥ prajñāvidyayor yo nimittaṃ upakleśaḥ.
body.translated_text: the unspeakable is the blameworthy (<s>avadya</s>). And therefore he says: '<s>avadya</s> means what is censured by the virtuous.' Therein, seeing no danger is <s>anapatrāpya</s> (lack of moral dread) — the meaning is: not seeing undesirable consequences in what is blameworthy. 'One fears from this' — here the word 'fear' (<s>bhaya</s>) has an ablative sense. Therefore by the word 'fear,' an undesirable result is meant. 'Seeing non-fear' (<s>abhayadarśitā</s>) — thus the elaboration. Now, if it were construed thus: not fear [but] non-fear; 'one whose nature is to see non-fear' is <s>abhayadarśī</s>; the state of that is <s>abhayadarśitā</s> — then <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) would be understood, for it is by <s>prajñā</s> that one sees non-fear. But if it is construed thus: 'one whose nature is to see fear' is <s>bhayadarśī</s>; 'not <s>bhayadarśī</s>' is <s>abhayadarśī</s>; the state of that is <s>abhayadarśitā</s> — then <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) would be understood, for due to the connection with <s>avidyā</s>, one does not see fear. 'It is not seeing that constitutes <s>darśitā</s>' — thus the elaboration. [It is] neither <s>prajñā</s> nor <s>avidyā</s>. What then? Of those two, <s>prajñā</s> and <s>avidyā</s>, whichever is the cause — a secondary affliction

body.text: tad abhayadarśanaṃ. tac cānapatrāpyam [Tib. 125a] iti. apatrapate 'nenety apatrāpyaṃ. kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam iti karaṇe ṇyatpratyayaḥ. na apatrāpyaṃ anapatrāpyam iti. hṛī lajjāyāṃ trapūṣ lajjāyām ity ekārthayor anayor dhātvoḥ katham arthāṃtare vācakatvam iti aparituṣyaṃto 'nye punar āhuḥ. ātmāpekṣayeti vistaraḥ. evam api dve apekṣe yugapat kathaṃ setsyata iti. asminn api pakṣe yugapadapekṣādvayāsaṃbhava iti paśyaṃś codaka aha. evam apīti. apiśabdena ayam api pakṣo duṣyatīty abhiprāyaḥ. āhrīkyam anapatrāpyaṃ caikasmiṃś citte kathaṃ bhavata iti matvā codayati. dve apekṣe yugapat kathaṃ setsyata iti. na khalūcyate yugapad ātmānaṃ paraṃ cāpekṣata iti vistaraḥ. paryāyena vṛttim anayor darśayati. kasyacid dhi doṣair ātmānam apekṣamāṇasyāpi na pravartate lajjā. kasyacit param apekṣamāṇasyeti. viparyayeṇa hrīr apatrāpyaṃ ceti vistaraḥ. prathamena tāvat kalpena
body.translated_text: — that is the seeing of non-fear. And that is <s>anapatrāpya</s> (lack of moral dread) [Tib. 125a]. '<s>Apatrāpya</s>' [means] 'that by which one feels shame' — by the rule '<s>kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam</s>,' the <s>ṇyat</s>-suffix is in the instrumental sense. 'Not <s>apatrāpya</s>' is <s>anapatrāpya</s>. 'Since <s>hrī</s> means shame and <s>trap</s> also means shame — of these two roots having the same meaning, how can they denote different things?' — being dissatisfied [with this], others say: 'with respect to oneself' — thus the elaboration. 'Even so, how can the two references [to self and others] be simultaneous?' — seeing the impossibility of the two references being simultaneous even in this interpretation, the objector says 'even so.' By the word 'even,' the intended meaning is that this interpretation too is flawed. He objects thinking: 'How can <s>āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness) and <s>anapatrāpya</s> (moral recklessness) exist in one mind?' — 'How can the two references be simultaneous?' It is not said that one simultaneously regards oneself and others — thus the elaboration. He shows their occurrence in alternation. For when someone, while regarding himself on account of faults, still has no shame arising — [that is one case]. For another, while regarding others — [likewise]. 'Conversely, <s>hrī</s> and <s>apatrāpya</s>' — thus the elaboration. By the first interpretation,

children.translated_text: 'shamelessness is disrespect and seeing no danger in what is blameworthy is <s>atrapa</s>' —

body.text: anena. sagauravateti vistareṇa bhayadarśitā apatrāpyam iti. bhayadarśitānimittam apatrāpyam ity arthaḥ. dvitīyena kalpena ātmāpekṣayā doṣair alajjanaṃ āhrīkyaṃ parapekṣayānapatrāpyam iti anena. ātmāpekṣayā doṣair lajjanaṃ hrīḥ. parāpekṣayāpatrāpyam iti. evam api dve apekṣe iti vistareṇa codyaparihārau vaktavyau. [Tib. 125b] premagauravayor ekatvaṃ manyaṃte kecit. tasmād anayor nānākaraṇapradarśanārtham āha.
body.translated_text: by this. 'Having respect' — thus with the elaboration: seeing danger is <s>apatrāpya</s> (moral dread). The meaning is: <s>apatrāpya</s> has danger-seeing as its cause. By the second interpretation: 'with respect to oneself, not being ashamed of faults is <s>āhrīkya</s>; with respect to others, <s>anapatrāpya</s>' — by this. With respect to oneself, being ashamed of faults is <s>hrī</s>; with respect to others, <s>apatrāpya</s>. 'Even so, the two references...' — with this elaboration, the objection and its resolution should be stated. [Tib. 125b] Some consider affection (<s>prema</s>) and respect (<s>gaurava</s>) to be the same. Therefore, in order to show the difference between these two, he says:

body.text: premaiva śraddhā na gauravaṃ. na tu śraddhaiva prema. tenāha. dvividhaṃ hi prema kliṣṭaṃ akliṣṭaṃ cetyādi. syāc chraddhā na premeti catuḥkoṭikaḥ. duḥkasamudayasatyayoḥ śraddhaivābhisaṃpratyayarūpā na prema aspṛhaṇīyatvāt. syāt prema na śraddheti. priyatārūpā tṛṣṇā nābhisaṃpratyayarūpeti śraddhā na bhavati. ubhayaṃ śraddhā ca prema ca. abhisaṃpratyayarūpatvāt spṛhaṇīyatvāc ca nirodhamārgasatyayos tadubhayātmakaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ. nobhayam etān ākārān sthāpayitveti. anye caitasikā vedanādayaḥ viprayuktādayaś ca. evaṃ dharmālaṃbanasya premnaḥ śraddhāyāś ca catuḥkoṭikaṃ kṛtvā pudgalālaṃbanasya catuṣkoṭikaṃ karoti. pudgaleṣv iti vistaraḥ. tatra sārdhaṃ viharaṃtīti sārdhavihāriṇaḥ śiṣyāḥ. ye pravrajitāḥ guror aṃte vasaṃtīti aṃtevāsinaḥ. niśrayādhyayanasaṃbaṃdhinaḥ. teṣu putrādiṣu prema na gauravaṃ kliṣṭaṃ akliṣṭaṃ ceti saṃbhavataḥ. gauravaṃ na prema
body.translated_text: thus. Affection itself is faith, not respect. But it is not that faith itself is affection. Therefore he says: 'for affection is twofold — afflicted and unafflicted' and so on. There is a fourfold distinction: 'it may be faith but not affection' — with respect to the truths of suffering and origination, faith itself in the form of conviction [exists], but not affection, because they are not desirable. 'It may be affection but not faith' — craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) in the form of attraction is not in the form of conviction, hence it is not faith. 'Both faith and affection' — because of being in the form of conviction and because of being desirable, with respect to the truths of cessation and the path, [the mental factor] has the nature of both — this is the meaning. 'Neither' — setting aside these aspects, other mental factors such as feeling and so on, and dissociated [factors] and so on. Having thus made a fourfold distinction of affection and faith with respect to <s>dharma</s>s as objects, he makes a fourfold distinction with respect to persons as objects: 'with respect to persons' — thus the elaboration. Therein, 'those who dwell together' — <s>sārdhavihārin</s>s are disciples who have gone forth and live in the presence of the teacher. <s>Antevāsin</s>s are those connected by dependence and study. Toward them, as toward sons and so forth, there is affection but not respect, both afflicted and unafflicted being possible. 'Respect but not affection' —

body.text: iti vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇaṃ gauravaṃ na prema gauravasthānatvāt. ubhayaṃ prema gauravaṃ ca. tadubhayātmakaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ. [Tib. 126a] nobhayam etān ākārān sthāpayitvā yo 'nyo jano 'saṃbaddho nirguṇaḥ. tatra na prema na gauravam iti. tatpūrvikā ca priyatā premeti. guṇasaṃbhāvanāpūrvikā priyatā tac ca prema. tasmān na saiva śraddhā premety ācāryaḥ.
body.translated_text: respect, whose definition will be stated [below], is not affection, because [the teacher] is an object of respect. 'Both affection and respect' — the meaning is: [the mental state] has the nature of both. [Tib. 126a] 'Neither' — setting aside these aspects, whatever other person is unconnected and without qualities, toward them there is neither affection nor respect. 'And the attraction preceded by that is affection' — the attraction preceded by the appreciation of qualities is affection. Therefore, affection is not simply faith — [this is] the teacher's [position].

body.text: iti. yathoktā hrīḥ sagauravatā sapratīśatā sabhayavaśavartitety uktā. yā hrīḥ. tad gauravaṃ. tad evaṃ prema śraddhālakṣaṇaṃ bhavati. hrīlakṣaṇaṃ tu gauravam ity uktaṃ tayor nānākaraṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. <s>Hrī</s> as described [above] — stated as having respect (<s>sagauravatā</s>), having a mentor (<s>sapratīśatā</s>), and being under the control of fear (<s>sabhayavaśavartitā</s>) — that <s>hrī</s> is respect (<s>gaurava</s>). Thus affection has the characteristic of faith, while respect has the characteristic of <s>hrī</s> — this has been stated as the distinction between the two.

body.text: evaṃ sapratīśatāpīti. evaṃ hrīr api dharmeṣu ca pudgaleṣu ca. ye pudgalālaṃbane śraddhāhriyau. te tatra na sta iti pudgalālaṃbane śraddhāhriyāv adhikriyete yayor aikyaṃ manyante. te ārūpyadhātau na staḥ kāmarūpadhātvor eva bhavata ity uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Thus <s>sapratīśatā</s> (having a mentor) also' — thus <s>hrī</s> too [relates] to both <s>dharma</s>s and persons. Those two — faith and <s>hrī</s> — which have persons as their object, they do not exist there. Thus faith and <s>hrī</s> with persons as their object are under discussion — whose identity some assert. Those two do not exist in the formless realm; they exist only in the desire and form realms — this has been stated.

body.text: (II.34) kathaṃ punar anayor ekatra citte yoga iti. na hi tad eva cittaṃ tadyogād audārikaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ ca yujyate vipratiṣedhāt. niṣṭhyūtam iti. niḥpūrvasya ṣṭhīvate niṣṭhāyām etad rūpaṃ niṣṭhyūtaṃ. nirastam ity arthaḥ. nātiśyāyate nātighanībhavati. nātivilīyate nātidravībhavati. nātisūkṣmaṃ bhavati nātyaudārikam iti. madhyamāvastham ity arthaḥ. evaṃ tarhi nimittabhūtāv iti vistaraḥ. yathodakātapau sarpiṣaḥ śyānatvavilīnatvayor nimittabhūtau. na tu punas tatsvabhāvau śyānatvavilīnatvasvabhāvau. evaṃ vitarkavicārau cittasyaudārikatāsūkṣmatayor [Tib. 126b] nimittabhūtau na tu punar audārikasūkṣmatāsvabhāvāv iti. ata evaṃ vaktavyaṃ. cittaudārikatāhetur vitarkaḥ. cittasūkṣmatāhetur vicāra iti. brūyās tvam abhyupagamād adoṣa eṣa iti. tata idaṃ doṣāntaram āhā. āpekṣikī caudārikasūkṣmateti vistaraḥ. bhūmiprakārabhedāt. bhūmibhedāt prakārabhedāc ca. bhūmibhedāt tāvat. prathamadhyānam apekṣya kāmadhātur audāriko mahābhisaṃskārataratvāt. kāmadhātum apekṣya prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ sūkṣmam alpābhisaṃskārataratvāt praśāntam iti. tad eva punar dvitīyaṃ dhyānam apekṣya audārikaṃ. evaṃ yāvad bhavāgraṃ sūkṣmaṃ. prakārabhedād api tasyām eva bhūmau āpekṣikyāv audārikasūkṣmate. tadyathā ya eva te trayaḥ kleśānāṃ mūlaprakārā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā guṇānāṃ ca. kāmadhātau yāvad bhavāgre teṣām adhimātraḥ kleśa audārikaḥ. mṛduḥ sūkṣmaḥ. kleśaviparyayeṇa guṇānām iti. evaṃ bhūmiprakārabhedenāpekṣikyāv
body.translated_text: (II.34) 'But how can these two [vitarka and vicāra] be combined in one mind?' — for it is not proper that the same mind, through connection with them, be both coarse and subtle, because of mutual contradiction. '<s>Niṣṭhyūta</s>' (expelled) — this is the form of <s>ṣṭhīv</s> (to spit) with the prefix <s>niḥ</s> in its completed action; it means 'cast out.' '[The mind] is not overly congealed, nor overly thickened. It is not overly dissolved, nor overly liquefied. It is not overly subtle, nor overly coarse' — the meaning is: it is in a middle state. 'Then they are causes' — thus the elaboration. Just as water and sunlight are causes of butter's congealing and melting respectively, but are not themselves of the nature of congealing and melting, so too <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) are causes of the mind's coarseness and subtlety, [Tib. 126b] but they themselves are not of the nature of coarseness and subtlety. Therefore it should be stated thus: <s>vitarka</s> is the cause of the mind's coarseness; <s>vicāra</s> is the cause of the mind's subtlety. 'You might say there is no fault because of the admission' — thereupon he states this further objection: 'coarseness and subtlety are relative' — thus the elaboration. Due to the distinction of ground and type — due to the distinction of ground and due to the distinction of type. First, due to the distinction of ground: in relation to the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the desire realm is coarse, because of having greater mental elaboration; in relation to the desire realm, the first <s>dhyāna</s> is subtle, because of having less mental elaboration — peaceful. But that same [first dhyāna], in relation to the second <s>dhyāna</s>, is coarse. Thus up to the peak of existence, which is subtle. Due to the distinction of type also, within that very ground, coarseness and subtlety are relative. Just as those three basic types of afflictions — mild, medium, and intense — and likewise of qualities, [apply] from the desire realm up to the peak of existence: among them, the intense affliction is coarse, the mild is subtle.
