Conversely for qualities. Thus, due to the distinction of ground and type, coarseness and subtlety are relative

body.text: audārikasūkṣmate ity ā bhavāgrād audārikasūkṣmate syātāṃ. aniṣṭaṃ caitat. vitarkavicārayoḥ kāmadhātuprathamadhyānabhūmikatvād iti. na caudārikasūkṣmatayā jātibhedo yukta iti. vitarkavicārayor jātibheda iṣyate. anyo vitarko 'nyo vicāra iti. na caudarikatvena sūkṣmatvena ca vitarkavicārayor yathākramaṃ svabhāvabhedo yuktaḥ. kiṃkāraṇaṃ. jātibhinnayor hi vedanāsaṃjñayor audārikasūkṣmatā bhavati. na ca punar audārikasūkṣmatayaiva tayoḥ [Tib. 127a] svabhāvabhedaḥ. kiṃ tarhi. anubhavalakṣaṇatayā nimittodgrahaṇalakṣaṇatayā ca tayoḥ svabhāvabhedaḥ. tasmād apy anayor nāsti lakṣaṇaṃ. anye punar āhur iti sautrāntikāḥ. vāksaṃskārā iti. vāksamutthāpakā ity arthaḥ. vitarkya vicārya vācaṃ bhāṣate nāvitarkya nāvicāryeti. vitarkavicārair evaṃ caivaṃ ca bhāṣiṣya iti. tatra ye audārikāḥ. te vitarkā vāksaṃskārāḥ. karmaṇā svabhāvo dyotito na śakyam anyathā svalakṣaṇaṃ pradarśayitum iti. evaṃ sūkṣmās te vicārāḥ. etasyāṃ kalpanāyāṃ samudāyarūpā vitarkavicārāḥ. paryāyabhāvinaś ca bhavaṃti. cittacaittakalāpasya vāksamutthāpakatvāt. kathaṃ punar anayor ekatra citte yoga ity uktaṃ. ato vaibhāṣika āha. yadi caikatra citte 'nyo dharma audārika iti vistaraḥ. ekatra citte vitarka audārikasvabhāvo 'nyo dharmo vicāras tu sūkṣmasvabhāvo 'paraḥ. tau ca yathākramaṃ cittaudārikatāsūkṣmatāhetutvāc cittaudārikatāsūkṣmatety ucyate. atha vā cittasyaudārikaś cittaudārikaḥ. cittaudārikabhāvaḥ cittaudārikatā. evaṃ cittasūkṣmatāpi vaktavyeti ko 'tra virodhaḥ. na syād virodho yadi vitarkavicārayor jātibhedaḥ syād vedanāsaṃjñāvat. vedanā hy audārikī saṃjñā sūkṣmā. tayos tu jātibhedo 'stīti audārikasūkṣmatāyām apy ekatra citte na virodhaḥ. ekasyāṃ tu jātau anavadhṛtalakṣaṇāyāṃ aikyena ca kaiścid gṛhītāyāṃ mṛdvadhimātratā audārikasūkṣmatālakṣaṇā [Tib. 127b] yugapan na saṃbhavatety arthād ayugapat saṃbhavatīty uktaṃ. tathā hi vedanā anyo vā dharmaḥ paryāyeṇa mṛdutām adhimātratāṃ ca bhajate. naivaṃ vyakto bhavati. kiṃ. jātibhedaḥ. kasmāt. pratyekaṃ jātīnām mṛdvadhimātratvāt. vedanā hy audārikī bhavati. sūkṣmā vāpekṣābhedāt. katham iti. vedanā saṃjñām apekṣya audārikī. rūpam apekṣya sūkṣmā. tathā saṃjñā saṃskārān apekṣyaudārikī. vedanām apekṣya sūkṣmā. vitarkavicāravad eva vā. bhavato 'pi hi kāmāvacarau vitarkavicārāv audārikau prathamadhyānabhūmikau sūkṣmau. dhyānāntare ca vicāraḥ sūkṣmatara iti. tad evaṃ pratyekaṃ jātīnāṃ mṛdvadhimātratvāt. naivaṃ vyakto bhavati. na mṛdvadhimātratayā jātibhedo vyakto bhavatīty arthaḥ. atra
body.translated_text: 'coarseness and subtlety up to the peak of existence' — there would be coarseness and subtlety up to <s>Bhavāgra</s> (the peak of existence). And this is undesirable. Because <s>vitarka</s> (examination) and <s>vicāra</s> (investigation) belong to the desire-realm and first-<s>dhyāna</s> levels. And a distinction of type (<s>jāti</s>) based on coarseness and subtlety is not reasonable. A distinction of type is accepted for <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> — '<s>vitarka</s> is one thing, <s>vicāra</s> is another.' But a difference of intrinsic nature between <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> respectively on the basis of coarseness and subtlety is not reasonable. Why? For coarseness and subtlety pertain to <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), which are different in type. But the difference of intrinsic nature between those two [Tib. 127a] is not due to coarseness and subtlety alone. Rather, their difference of intrinsic nature is due to the characteristic of experiencing and the characteristic of grasping at signs. Therefore, for these two as well, there is no [distinctive] characteristic. 'But others say' — the <s>Sautrāntikas</s>. '<s>Vāksaṃskāras</s>' (verbal formations) — meaning 'that which gives rise to speech.' 'One speaks having examined and investigated, not without examining and not without investigating.' By <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, [one determines:] 'I shall speak thus and thus.' Therein, those that are coarse — those are <s>vitarka</s>, the verbal formations. The intrinsic nature is indicated by its function — because it cannot be shown otherwise by its own characteristic. Similarly, those that are subtle — those are <s>vicāra</s>. On this interpretation, <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> are of the nature of an assemblage. And they function alternately — because the assemblage of mind and mental factors gives rise to speech. 'But how then do these two co-exist in a single mind-moment?' — this has been stated. Therefore the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'If in a single mind-moment, one <s>dharma</s> is coarse' — and so forth in detail. In a single mind-moment, <s>vitarka</s>, being of coarse intrinsic nature, is one <s>dharma</s>, while <s>vicāra</s>, being of subtle intrinsic nature, is another. And those two, respectively, are called 'coarseness of mind' and 'subtlety of mind' because of being the causes of the mind's coarseness and subtlety. Or alternatively, 'coarse with respect to mind' is 'mind-coarse'; the state of being mind-coarse is 'mind-coarseness.' Similarly, 'mind-subtlety' should also be stated — so what contradiction is there? There would be no contradiction if <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> had a difference of type, like <s>vedanā</s> and <s>saṃjñā</s>. For feeling is coarse and perception is subtle. And since there is a difference of type between those two, there is no contradiction even in coarseness and subtlety within a single mind-moment. But when a single type has no determined characteristic, [Tib. 127b] and is grasped as identical by some, mildness and intensity — characterized as coarseness and subtlety — cannot occur simultaneously — meaning they occur alternately; this has been said. For feeling or any other <s>dharma</s> alternately partakes of mildness and intensity. Is this not [similarly] clear? What? A difference of type. Why? Because each type individually has mildness and intensity. For feeling is coarse or subtle depending on the difference of reference. How? Feeling is coarse in reference to perception; subtle in reference to form. Similarly, perception is coarse in reference to formations; subtle in reference to feeling. Or, just like <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> themselves. For even according to you, <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> belonging to the desire-realm are coarse, while those belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> level are subtle. And <s>vicāra</s> in the <s>dhyānāntara</s> (inter-<s>dhyāna</s>) is even more subtle. Thus, since each type individually has mildness and intensity, this is not [made] clear — meaning the difference of type is not made clear by mildness and intensity. Here

body.text:
saṃghabhadrācārya āha. ekatra ca citte audārikasūkṣmate bhavato na ca virodhaḥ. prabhāvakālānyatvāt.
yadā hi cittacaittakalāpe vitarka udbhūtavṛttir bhavati. tadā cittam audārikaṃ bhavati. yadā vicāraḥ. tadā sūkṣmaṃ. rāgamohacaritavyapadeśavat. rāgamohayaugapadye 'pi hi tayor anyatarodbhūtavṛttiyogāt. rāgacarito mohacarita iti vā vyapadiśyate. tadvad ihāpi draṣṭavyam iti. atra vayaṃ brūmaḥ. bhavati kasmiṃścit kalāpe kasyacid dharmasya udbhūtavṛttitvaṃ. kiṃ tv anayor na lakṣaṇaṃ vivecitam iti. na kiṃcid etat. nanu ca cittaudārikatāsūkṣmatālakṣaṇau vitarkavicārāv uktau. [Tib. 128a] satyam uktau. pratyekaṃ tu jātīnām audārikasūkṣmate iti tāv audārikasūkṣmatālakṣaṇau bhavitum arhato yathoktam iti naitad asmān ārādhayati. naiva hi vitarkavicārāv ekatra citte bhavata ity apara ity ācāryamatam. asmin mate yathoktadoṣaprasaṃgo na bhavati. kas tv anayoḥ paryāyavartinor viśeṣaḥ. atra pūrvācāryā āhuḥ. vitarkaḥ katamaḥ. cetanāṃ vā niśritya prajñāṃ vā paryeṣako manojalpo 'nabhyūhābhyūhāvasthayor yathākramaṃ sā ca cittasyaudārikatā. vicāraḥ katamaḥ. cetanāṃ vā niśritya prajñāṃ vā pratyavekṣako manojalpo 'nabhyūhābhyūhāvasthayor yathākramaṃ sā ca cittasūkṣmateti. asmin pakṣe vitarkavicārāv ekasvabhāvau samudāyarūpau paryāyavartinau paryeṣaṇapratyavekṣaṇākāramātreṇa bhinnāv iṣyete. tatrodāharaṇaṃ kecid ācakṣate. tadyathā bahuṣu ghaṭeṣv avasthiteṣu ko 'tra dṛḍhaḥ ko jarjara iti muṣṭinābhighnato ya ūhaḥ. sa vitarkaḥ. iyaṃto jarjarā dṛḍhā veti yad ante grahaṇaṃ. sa vicāra iti. katham idānīṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ paṃcāṅgam iti vistaraḥ. viviktaṃ kāmair viviktaṃ pāpakair akuśalair dharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharatīti sūtre paṃcāṃgam uktaṃ. tat kathaṃ. bhūmitas tat paṃcāṅgam uktaṃ na kṣaṇata iti. prathamadhyānabhūmiḥ [Tib. 128b] kadācid vitarkeṇa vyavakīrṇā kadācid vicāreṇa. tad evaṃ saṃtānam adhikṛtya paṃcāṅgam uktaṃ na kṣaṇam adhikṛtyety adoṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Saṃghabhadra</s> says: And in a single mind-moment, coarseness and subtlety exist without contradiction — because of the difference in the times of predominance. For when, in the assemblage of mind and mental factors, <s>vitarka</s> has a predominant function, then the mind is coarse. When <s>vicāra</s> [has a predominant function], then it is subtle. This is like the designation 'one of lustful disposition' or 'one of deluded disposition.' For even though lust and delusion are simultaneous, because of the predominant function of one or the other, one is designated as 'of lustful disposition' or 'of deluded disposition.' It should be viewed similarly here as well. To this we say: In some assemblage, some <s>dharma</s> does have a predominant function. But the characteristic of these two has not been distinguished — this is [the problem]. This is nothing [i.e., this objection has no force]. Have not <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> been stated as characterized by mind-coarseness and mind-subtlety? [Tib. 128a] True, they have been stated [so]. But since each type individually has coarseness and subtlety, those two should be [able to be] characterized by coarseness and subtlety as stated — this does not satisfy us. For indeed, <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> do not [both] exist in a single mind-moment — [thus says] 'another,' meaning the <s>Ācārya</s>'s [Vasubandhu's] view. On this view, the fault stated [above] does not arise. But what is the distinction between these two that function alternately? Here the earlier <s>Ācāryas</s> say: 'What is <s>vitarka</s>? It is a mental discourse that is investigative, depending on volition (<s>cetanā</s>) or wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), in both the states of non-deliberation and deliberation respectively — and that is the coarseness of mind. What is <s>vicāra</s>? It is a mental discourse that is reflective, depending on volition or wisdom, in both the states of non-deliberation and deliberation respectively — and that is the subtlety of mind.' On this position, <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> are of one intrinsic nature, of the nature of an assemblage, functioning alternately, and are accepted as differing merely by the aspects of searching and reflecting. Therein, some give an illustration: Just as when many pots are standing and one strikes them with the fist [asking] 'which is sturdy, which is fragile?' — the initial assessment is <s>vitarka</s>; and the final determination 'these many are fragile, [these] sturdy' — that is <s>vicāra</s>. 'How then is the first <s>dhyāna</s> said to have five factors?' — and so forth in detail. [The <s>sūtra</s> says:] 'Secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, with <s>vitarka</s>, with <s>vicāra</s>, born of seclusion, with joy and happiness, one enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s>' — thus five factors are stated in the <s>sūtra</s>. How then? Those five factors are stated with respect to the level, not with respect to a single moment. The first <s>dhyāna</s> level [Tib. 128b] is sometimes pervaded by <s>vitarka</s>, sometimes by <s>vicāra</s>. Thus, the five factors are stated with reference to the continuum, not with reference to a single moment — so there is no fault.

body.text: yena kenacit parato viśeṣaparikalpeneti. bhūtenābhūtena vā parata utkarṣaparikalpena śūro 'rthavān asmi śīlavān buddhisaṃpanna iti vā yā cetasa unnatiḥ sa māno nāma caitasiko dharmaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'By any kind of distinction-construction regarding another, whether real or unreal' — by a construction of superiority regarding another, whether real or unreal — 'I am brave, wealthy, virtuous, endowed with intelligence' — whatever elevation of mind [there is] — that mental factor is called <s>māna</s> (pride).

body.text: iti tuśabdo viśeṣaṇārtho bhinnakramaś cāvagantavyaḥ. ata evāha. madas tu svadharmeṣv eva raktasyeti vistaraḥ. cetasaḥ paryādānam iti. yena svadharmeṣv
body.translated_text: the particle 'but' (<s>tu</s>) is for the purpose of distinguishing, and the sequence should be understood as rearranged. Therefore he says: '<s>Mada</s> (intoxication) is [the state] of one who is attached to one's own qualities' — and so forth in detail. 'The intoxication of the mind' — by which, with respect to one's own qualities

body.text: eva rūpaśauryādiṣu raktaṃ cetaḥ paryādīyate saṃnirudhyate. sa rāganiṣyando madaḥ. yaḥ svadharmeṣv eva raktasya darpacetasaḥ paryādānāt kuśaladharmakriyābhyaḥ pratisaṃhāraḥ mada iti ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ. saṃpraharṣaviśeṣo mada iti. kliṣṭasaumanasyam abhipretaṃ. tad etan necchanti vaibhāṣikāḥ. yasmāt saumanasyaṃ ā dvitīyād dhyānāt. madaś ca traidhātukaḥ.
body.translated_text: — such as beauty, valor, and the like — the mind that is attached is overwhelmed, obstructed. That is <s>mada</s> (intoxication), an outflow of attachment (<s>rāga</s>). [According to] <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Saṃghabhadra</s>: <s>Mada</s> is the withdrawal from the practice of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> due to the overwhelming of the proud mind that is attached to one's own qualities alone. '<s>Mada</s> is a special kind of elation' — afflicted mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>) is intended. The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> do not accept this. Because mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>) extends [only] up to the second <s>dhyāna</s>. But <s>mada</s> pertains to all three realms.

children.translated_text: 'Torpor, restlessness, and intoxication — in the three realms' —

body.text: iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of this statement.

body.text: (II.35) uktāḥ saha cittena caittāḥ caittāḥ prakāreṇa iti. cittaṃ tāvat prakāreṇa uktaṃ
body.translated_text: (II.35) 'Mind and mental factors have been described together with their detailed classifications' — thus. Mind has been described in detail [by the verse]:

body.text: ity evamādinā svalakṣaṇaskandhadhātvāyatanakuśalādiprabhedena. caittā api svalakṣaṇaparasparaviśeṣeṇa [Tib. 129a] cittasaṃkhyāvadhāraṇakāmaprathamadhyānādibhūmiprabhedena.
body.translated_text: and so forth, with the classifications of own-characteristic, aggregate, element, sense-base, and wholesome and the rest. Mental factors too [have been described] with the distinctions of own-characteristic, mutual differences, [Tib. 129a] determination of the number [accompanying] mind, and level-distinctions such as the desire-realm, first <s>dhyāna</s>, and so forth.

body.text: iti. yac cittaṃ. tad eva manas tad eva vijñānam ity eko 'rtho 'syety ekārthaṃ. nirvacanabhedas tūcyate. cinotīti cittam iti. kuśalam akuśalaṃ vā cinotīty arthaḥ. nairuktena vidhinaivaṃ siddhaṃ. manuta iti manaḥ. mana jñāna ity asya auṇādikapratyayāt tasyaitad rūpaṃ mana iti. vijānāty ālambanam iti vijñānaṃ kartari lyuṭ. citaṃ śubhāśubhair dhātubhir iti cittaṃ. bhāvanāsaṃniveśayogena sautrāntikamatena yogācāramatena vā. āśrayabhūtaṃ manaḥ āśritabhūtaṃ vijñānam iti āśrayabhāvāpekṣaṃ manaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. That which is mind (<s>citta</s>) — that itself is <s>manas</s>, that itself is consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) — 'it has a single referent' means 'its referent is one' (<s>ekārtham</s>). But a difference in etymology is stated. '<s>Citta</s>' because it accumulates (<s>cinoti</s>) — meaning it accumulates wholesome and unwholesome [dharmas]. This is established by the etymological method itself. '<s>Manas</s>' because it cognizes (<s>manute</s>) — from the root <s>man</s> (to know), by the <s>Auṇādika</s> suffix, it has this form '<s>manas</s>.' '<s>Vijñāna</s>' because it cognizes the object (<s>ālambana</s>) — the suffix <s>lyuṭ</s> is in the agent sense. '<s>Citta</s>' because it is variegated (<s>citam</s>) by wholesome and unwholesome elements — according to the <s>Sautrāntika</s> view, by the imprinting of habitual impressions (<s>bhāvanā</s>), or according to the <s>Yogācāra</s> view. '<s>Manas</s>' insofar as it is a support; '<s>vijñāna</s>' insofar as it is supported — '<s>manas</s>' is [so called] with respect to the capacity of being a support.

children.text: ṣaṇṇām anantarātītaṃ vijñānaṃ yad dhi. tan mana
children.translated_text: 'That which is the immediately-past consciousness of the six — that is <s>manas</s>' —

body.text: ity arthaparigrahāt. āśritabhāvāpekṣaṃ vijñānaṃ. dvayaṃ pratītya vijñānasyotpattir iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of this determination of meaning. '<s>Vijñāna</s>' is [so called] with respect to the capacity of being supported — because of the statement: 'Consciousness arises dependent on the dyad [of sense-faculty and object].'

children.translated_text: 'Mind and mental factors have a support, an object, and an aspect, and are associated' —

body.text: caśabda ekānukarṣaṇārthaḥ. ya eva hi cittacaittā ity anena śabdenābhihitāḥ. ta eva sāśrayā ity anenāpi śabdenābhidhīyante. evaṃ sālambanāḥ sākārāḥ saṃprayuktāś ca. tatra sāśrayā indriyāśritatvāt. ṣaḍāyatanāśritatvād ity arthaḥ. sālambanā viṣayagrahaṇāt. na hi vinālambanena cittacaittā utpadyante. [Tib. 129b] sākārāḥ tasyaivālambanasya prakāreṇa ākāraṇāt. yena te sālambanāḥ
body.translated_text: thus. The particle 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is for drawing together into one. Those very [dharmas] that are designated by the term 'mind and mental factors' — those same ones are designated by the term 'having a support.' Similarly, [they are designated as] 'having an object,' 'having an aspect,' and 'associated.' Therein, 'having a support' — because of being dependent on a sense-faculty; the meaning is: because of being dependent on the six sense-bases. 'Having an object' — because of apprehending objects. For mind and mental factors do not arise without an object. [Tib. 129b] 'Having an aspect' — because of taking on the mode of that very object. That by which they have objects

body.text: tasyaivālaṃbanasya prakāreṇa grahaṇāt. kathaṃ. vijñānaṃ hi nīlaṃ pītaṃ vā vastu vijānāti upalabhata ity arthaḥ. tad eva tathālambanaṃ vastu vedanānubhavati. saṃjñā paricchinatti. cetanābhisaṃskarotīty evamādi. atha vā tasyaivālambanasya vijñānaṃ sāmānyarūpeṇa upalabhyatārūpaṃ gṛhṇāti. viśeṣarūpeṇa tu vedanānubhavanīyatārūpaṃ gṛhṇāti. saṃjñā paricchedyatārūpaṃ gṛhṇātīty evamādi. saṃprayuktāḥ samaṃ prayuktatvād iti. samā aviprayuktāś cānyonyam iti saṃprayuktāḥ. āśrayālambanākārakāladravyasamatābhir iti. yenāśrayeṇa cittam utpadyate. tenaivāśrayeṇa vedanāsaṃjñācetanādaya utpadyante. tathā yenālambanena cittaṃ. tenaiva vedanādayaḥ. yenākāreṇa cittaṃ. tenaiva vedanādayaḥ. yadi hi nīlākāraṃ cittaṃ nīlākārā eva tatsaṃprayuktā vedanādaya utpadyante. yasmiṃś ca kāle cittaṃ tasminn eva vedanādayaḥ. yathā ca cittadravyam ekam evotpadyate na dve trīṇi vā. tathā vedanādravyaṃ ekam evotpadyate na dve trīṇi vā. tathā saṃjñādravyaṃ cetanādravyaṃ ity evamādi. tenedam evāntyaṃ durgamam iti vyācaṣṭe. yathaiva hy ekaṃ cittaṃ evaṃ caittā api ekaikā iti.
body.translated_text: — because of apprehending that very object in a particular mode. How? For consciousness cognizes a blue or yellow thing — meaning 'apprehends.' That very thing which is thus the object, feeling experiences; perception discriminates; volition conditions — and so forth. Or alternatively, consciousness apprehends the general form of that very object — it grasps the aspect of being apprehensible. But feeling, in a specific mode, grasps the aspect of being experienceable. Perception grasps the aspect of being discriminable — and so forth. 'Associated' — because of being engaged together. They are equal and not disjoined from one another — [hence] 'associated.' [They are equal] in support, object, aspect, time, and substance. The support by which mind arises — by that very support do feeling, perception, volition, and the rest arise. Likewise, the object by which mind [arises] — by that same [object do] feeling and the rest. The aspect by which mind [arises] — by that same [aspect do] feeling and the rest. For if the mind has a blue aspect, the feeling and the rest that are associated with it arise with precisely a blue aspect. And at whatever time the mind [arises], at that very time [do] feeling and the rest. And just as the substance of mind arises as one only, not two or three, so too the substance of feeling arises as one only, not two or three. Similarly the substance of perception, the substance of volition — and so forth. Therefore this last [point of equality] is the most difficult [to understand] — he explains. Just as mind is one, so too the mental factors are each one.

body.text: (II.36) viprayuktān vaktukāma ācārya upodghātaṃ karoti nirdiṣṭāś cittacaittāḥ savistaraprabhedā viprayuktās tv [Tib. 130a] avasaraprāptā idānīm ucyanta ity abhiprāyaḥ. savistaraprabhedā iti. vistaraś ca prabhedaś ca vistaraprabhedau. saha vistaraprabhedābhyāṃ savistaraprabhedāḥ. atha vā vistareṇa prabhedaḥ vistaraprabhedaḥ. saha vistaraprabhedena savistaraprabhedāḥ. tatra cittaṃ tāvat savistaraprabhedaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ.
body.translated_text: (II.36) Wishing to discuss the dissociated [formations] (<s>viprayukta</s>), the <s>Ācārya</s> makes a preface: 'Mind and mental factors have been described with their detailed classifications; but the dissociated [formations], whose turn has now come, [Tib. 130a] are now stated' — this is the intent. 'With detailed classifications' means: detail and classification — detailed classification; together with detailed classification — having detailed classifications. Or, classification by way of detail is detailed classification; together with detailed classification — having detailed classifications. Therein, mind has first been described with its detailed classifications:

body.text: evamādinā. caittā api
body.translated_text: and so on. 'Mental factors too' —

body.text: ity ārabhya yāvat
body.translated_text: beginning from this, up to —

body.text: iti vistareṇa.
body.translated_text: thus in detail.

body.text: caśabda evaṃjātīyakānuktaviprayuktapradarśanārthaḥ. saṃghabhedaprabhṛtayo hi dravyataś cittaviprayuktā iṣyante iti ye 'py evaṃjātīyakā iti śāstre 'py uktatvāt. cittaviprayuktā iti cittagrahaṇaṃ cittasamānajātīyapradarśanārthaṃ. cittam iva cittena ca viprayuktā ity arthaḥ. kiṃ ca teṣāṃ cittena samānajātīyatvaṃ.
body.translated_text: The particle 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is for the purpose of showing [other] mind-dissociated [formations] of this type that were not mentioned. For schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s> and the like, in terms of substance, are mind-dissociated —

body.text: yad arūpiṇo 'mī bhavanti. rūpitvād eva hi viprayuktatve 'pi rūpaṃ na viprayuktatve nāma labhate. yad vāmīṣāṃ nāmarūpam iti nāmatvaṃ tat teṣāṃ cittena samānajātīyatvaṃ. caittā api cittena tulyajātīyāḥ. te tu cittena sahālambane saṃprayuktās tadviśeṣaṇārthaṃ viprayuktagrahaṇaṃ asaṃskṛtam api tatsamānajātīyam anālaṃbanatveneti tatparihārārthaṃ saṃskāragrahaṇaṃ [Tib. 130b] ata evāha. ime saṃskārā na cittena saṃprayuktā na ca rūpasvabhāvā iti cittaviprayuktā ucyanta iti.
body.translated_text: that they are formless. For because of being material, even though [they are] dissociated, form does not receive the designation 'dissociated.' That which —

body.text: (II.37) tatreti. vākyopanyāse nidhāraṇe vā. tāvacchabdaḥ krame.
body.translated_text: (II.37) 'Therein' — [is used] for introducing the statement or for specification. The word '<s>tāvat</s>' [indicates] sequence.

body.text: iti. prāptir iti sāmānyasaṃjñā. lābhaḥ samanvaya iti viśeṣasaṃjñā. lābhaḥ pratilambha ity eko 'rthaḥ. samanvayaḥ samanvāgama ity anarthāntaraṃ. pratilambha ity ukte samanvāgamasyāgrahaṇaṃ. samanvāgama ity ukte pratilambhasyāgrahaṇaṃ. prāptir ity ukte tūbhayodgrahaṇaṃ. ata evāha. dvividhā hi prāptiḥ. aprāptavihīnasya ca pratilambhaḥ. pratilabdhena ca samanvāgama iti. aprāptaṃ ca vihīnaṃ cāprāptavihīnaṃ. tasyāprāptavihīnasya pratilambhaḥ. aprāptasya tadyathā duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣānteḥ. vihīnasya tadyathā kāmāvacarasya kāmavairāgyeṇa tyaktasya dhātupratyāgamanāt parihāṇyā vā punaḥpratilambhaḥ. pratilabdhena ca dvitīyādiṣu kṣaṇeṣu samanvāgamaḥ. tasyāḥ samanuvartanāt. yaś ca pratilambhaḥ yaś ca samanvāgamaḥ. sā dvidhā prāptir iti pratilambhe samanvāgame ca prāptiśabdo vartate. abhedavivakṣāyāṃ tu prāptiḥ pratilambhaḥ samanvāgama ity eka evārthaḥ. tathā hi prathame kṣaṇe duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣānteḥ prāptiḥ pratilambha iṣyate. sāpi samanvāgama ity ucyate. prathamakṣaṇastha [Tib. 131a] āryapudgalo duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntyā samanvāgata ity ucyate.
body.translated_text: thus. '<s>Prāpti</s>' is the general designation. 'Attainment' (<s>lābha</s>) and 'conjunction' (<s>samanvaya</s>) are specific designations. '<s>Lābha</s>' and '<s>pratilambha</s>' are one and the same meaning —

children.translated_text: 'One endowed with the <s>ājñāsyāmi</s>-faculty is possessed of thirteen' —

body.text: ityādivacanāt. katham ayaṃ lakṣaṇanirdeśaḥ. na hi bhedavivakṣāyām api paryāyavacanena lakṣaṇanirdeśaḥ kalpate. prāptiḥ katamā. yaḥ pratilambho yaḥ samanvāgama iti. paryāyavacanam api kadācit lakṣaṇāya kalpate. analo jātavedā agnir iti. sūtre 'py uktam avidyā katamā. pūrvānte ajñānam aparānta ajñānam iti vistaraḥ. viparyayād evāprāptir iti siddham iti. viparyayād evāprāptir iti siddhe naitadarthaṃ sūtraṃ kartavyam ity abhiprāyaḥ. aprāptir apratilambho 'samanvāgama iti viparyayād etat trayaṃ gamyate. tathaiva cāpratilambhāsamanvāgamayor aprāptir iti sāmānyasaṃjñā. tasmād evaṃ ca vaktavyaṃ. dvividhā aprāptir aprāptapūrvāṇām apratilambhaḥ. prāptavihīnānām asamanvāgama
body.translated_text: from such statements. How is this a definition? For even when a distinction is intended, a definition is not [properly given] through synonymous terms —

body.text: iti. atha vāpratilabdhasya vihīnaspa cādyāprāptir apratilambhaḥ. apratilabdhena vihīnena ca dvitīyādiṣu kṣaṇeṣv asamanvāgama iti.
body.translated_text: thus. Alternatively, the first non-attainment (<s>aprāpti</s>) is the non-obtaining of what has not been obtained and what has been lost. By the second [type of non-attainment], what has not been obtained and what has been lost —

children.translated_text: '<s>Prāpti</s> and <s>aprāpti</s> [apply] to [<s>dharmas</s>] belonging to one's own continuum' —

body.text: iti. saṃskṛtānāṃ prāptyaprāptī svasaṃtānapatitānām evety avadhāryate. na parasaṃtānapatitānām iti. na parasattvasaṃtatipatitānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ. svasaṃtatau prāptyaprāptī bhavata ity arthaḥ. tenāha. na hi parakīyaiḥ kaścit samanvāgata iti. nāpy asaṃtatipatitānām iti nāsattvasaṃtatipatitānām ity arthaḥ. tasmād āha. na hy asattvasaṃkhyātaiḥ [Tib. 131b] kaścit samanvāgata iti. mālyābharaṇādayaḥ kāṣṭhakuḍyādigatāś ca rūpādayo 'sattvasaṃkhyātāḥ. cakṣurādayaḥ sattvasaṃkhyātāḥ keśādayo rūpīndriyasambaddhāḥ sattvasaṃkhyātā eva veditavyāḥ. tadanugrahopaghātapariṇāmānuvidhānāt. tathā hi rūpīndriyopaghātāt pālityādivikāraḥ keśādīnāṃ dṛśyate. rasāyanopayogena cānugrahāt pālityādipratyāpattir iti sarveṣāṃ sattvasaṃkhyātānāṃ prāptir bhavatīti siddhaṃtaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. It is determined that <s>prāpti</s> and <s>aprāpti</s> of conditioned [<s>dharmas</s>] apply only to those belonging to one's own continuum — not to those belonging to another's continuum.

body.text: iti pratisaṃkhyānirodhāpratisaṃkhyānirodhayor asattvasaṃkhyātayor api prāptyaprāptī bhavataḥ. sarvasattvā apratisaṃkhyānirodhena yathāpratyayavaikalyaṃ samanvāgatāḥ. sakalabandhanādikṣaṇasthavarjyā iti. ādau kṣaṇaḥ duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntikṣaṇaḥ. tatra sthitā ādikṣaṇasthāḥ. sakalāni bandhanāny eṣām iti sakalabandhanā. aprahīṇasarvaprakārakleśāḥ. sakalabandhanāś cādikṣaṇasthāś ca ta iti sakalabandhanādikṣaṇasthāḥ. te varjyā eṣāṃ tair vā varjyāḥ sakalabandhanādikṣaṇasthavarjyāḥ. ke. sarva āryāḥ. te pratisaṃkhyānirodhena samanvāgatāḥ. sakalabandhanādikṣaṇasthās tv āryā na samanvāgataḥ. tasyāṃ hy avasthāyāṃ kṣāṃtivadhyāḥ [Tib. 132a] kleśāś chidyante na chinnāḥ. tannirodho 'pi prāpyate na prāpto
body.translated_text: thus, <s>prāpti</s> and <s>aprāpti</s> apply also to <s>pratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s> (analytical cessation) and <s>apratisaṃkhyā-nirodha</s> (non-analytical cessation), which are designated as non-sentient. For all —

children.translated_text: 'The path that is ceasing abandons the obscuration concerning that [cessation]' —

body.text: iti siddhāntāt. ekaprakāropalikhitādayas tv āryā laukikamārgaprāptena nirodhena tasyām avasthāyāṃ samanvāgatāḥ. ata ūrdhvaṃ dvitīyādiṣu kṣaṇeṣu samanvāgatā eva anāsravamārgaprāptenāpi nirodhena. pṛthagjanāś ca kecit samanvāgatā ity ekaprakāropalikhitādayaḥ. ākāśena tu nāsti kaścit samanvāgata iti asaṃbaṃdhāt. nirodhābhyāṃ tv asti sambandhaḥ. tasmād ākāśasya prāptir nāsti. yasya ca nāsti prāptis tasyāprāptir api nāstīti siddhānta eṣa vaibhāṣikāṇāṃ.
body.translated_text: from this established principle. But the noble ones who are 'inscribed with one type [of practice]' and the like — by the cessation attained through the mundane path, in that stage —

body.text: kuta etad iti. rūpādicakṣurādivatsvarūpakāryānupalambhāt pṛcchati.
body.translated_text: 'Whence is this [known]?' — he asks because the own-nature and function [of <s>prāpti</s>] are not perceived, like form, etc. and the eye, etc.

body.text: sūtrād iti. vyākhyānam eva vaibhāṣikaḥ sādhayati. daśānām aśaikṣāṇāṃ dharmāṇām iti vistaraḥ. daśāśaikṣā dharmāḥ. aṣṭāv aśaikṣāṇy āryamārgāṃgāni samyagvimuktiḥ samyagjñānaṃ ca. teṣām utpādāt saṃmukhībhāvāt. pratilaṃbhād āditaḥ prāpteḥ. samanvāgamāt paścāt prāpteḥ. paṃcāṅgaṃ viprahīṇaḥ. prahīṇapaṃcāṅga ity arthaḥ. paṃcāṃgāni satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ śīlavrataparāmarśo vicikitsā kāmacchando vyāpāda iti. etāny anāgāmiphalaprāptau prahīṇānīti na yujyante. imāni tu prayujyamānāni paṃcāṃgāni paśyāmo yad utordhvabhāgīyāni rūparāga ārūpyarāga auddhatyaṃ māno 'vidyā ceti. pratinidhibhūtāyāḥ prāpter yogāt prakṛtistho 'py arhann ārya ity ucyate. [Tib. 132b] sādhanaṃ cātra. dravyato 'sti samanvāgamaḥ sūtroktatvād āyatanadravyavad iti. ācaryas taṃ pratyāha. tena tarhy asattvākhyair api cakraratnādibhiḥ parasattvair api strīratnādibhiḥ samanvāgamo dravyasan prāpnoti. sūtre vadanāt. katham iti sūtraṃ darśayati. rājā yāvad vistara iti. rājā bhikṣavaś cakravartī saptabhī ratnaiḥ samanvāgataḥ. tasyemāni sapta ratnāni. tadyathā cakraratnaṃ hastiratnaṃ aśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnam eva saptamam iti vistaraḥ. ebhis saptabhī ratnais samanvāgamaḥ sūtra ukto na ca dvavyato 'stīti anaikāntikatāṃ darśayati. pratijñādoṣam cāyam udgrāhayati. anumānavirodhāt. katham ity ucyate. na dravyasan daśāśaikṣadharmasamanvāgamaḥ samanvāgamasvābhāvyāc cakravartisaptaratnasamanvāgamavad iti. anena pratijñāyā dharmasvarūpaṃ viparyāsayati. vaśitvaṃ kāmacāra iti. icchānuvidhāyitvaṃ. tatra vaśitvam iti cakravartisūtre. anyatra punar dravyāntaram iti. aśāśaikṣasamanvāgamasūtre. kaḥ punar evam ayoga iti. pravacane hi dvividham iṣyate dravyasac ca vastu prajñaptisac ceti katham ayuktir iti vaibhāṣikāḥ. ācārya āha. ayam ayoga iti vistaraḥ. iha yad dravyasad vastu tat pratyakṣagrāhyaṃ [Tib. 133a] vā bhaved anumānagrāhyaṃ vā. tatra pratyakṣagrāhyaṃ rūpaśabdādi paṃcendriyagrāhyatvāt. manovijñānagrāhyam api kiṃcit pratyakṣaṃ. rāgadveṣādi svasaṃvedyatvāt. cakṣuḥśrotrādi tv anumānagrāhyaṃ cakṣurvijñānādikṛtyānumeyatvāt. tadbhāvābhāvayos tadbhāvābhāvāt. prāptiḥ punar na pratyakṣagrāhyā na cānumānagrāhyā tatsiddhau niravadyānumānādarśanāt. tasmād dravyadharmāsambhavād ayoga iti sthitam etat. idānīm ācāryas tatpakṣam utthāpyotthāpya dūṣayati. utpattihetur iti vistaraḥ. yasya prāptir asti sa utpadyate hetusadbhāvāt. asaṃskṛtasya na syāt prāptir yasmād asaṃskṛtam anutpādyaṃ. ye ca dharmā aprāptā duḥkhe
body.translated_text: 'From the <s>sūtra</s>' — thus the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> establishes the explanation. 'Of the ten <s>aśaikṣa</s> (no-more-training) <s>dharmas</s>' — thus the elaboration. The ten —

body.text:
dharmajñānakṣāntyādayaḥ. ye ca tyaktāḥ bhūmisaṃcāravairāgyataḥ. tadyathā kāmāvacarā akliṣṭā ūrdhvabhūmyupapattyā kliṣṭāś ca vairāgyeṇa tyaktāḥ. teṣāṃ dhātupratyāgamataḥ parihāṇyā vā katham utpattiḥ syāt. na hi teṣāṃ prāptir asti. anutpannaniruddhatvāt. sahajaprāptihetukā cet. kā. teṣām utpattir adhikṛtā. sahajā yā prāptir idānīm utpadyate. sā teṣāṃ janiketi. āha. jātir idānīṃ kiṃkarī jātijātir veti. kiṃkaraṇaśīlā kiṃkarī. jātir lakṣyaṃ dharmaṃ janayati. [Tib. 133b] jātijātis tu tallakṣaṇaṃ jātiṃ janayati. tena yadi lakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇām utpattiḥ prāptihetukocyeta tatra jātiḥ kiṃkarī. atha lakṣaṇānām. utpattis taddhetukocyeta. tata āha. jātijātir vā kiṃkarīti vikalpaḥ. atha vā yadi bhavataivaṃ kalpyeta. jātir dharmaṃ janayati. prāptiḥ punar jātiṃ janayatīti. tatra ucyate. jātijātir vā kiṃkarīti. sakalabandhanānāṃ khalv apīti vistaraḥ. yeṣām eko 'pi kleśaprakāro na prahīṇaḥ. te sakalabandhanāḥ. teṣāṃ sakalabandhanānāṃ khalv api mṛdumadhyādhimātrakleśotpattiprakārabhedo na syāt. kasmāt. prāptyabhedāt. vikalabandhanānāṃ hi prāptivaikalyān mṛdumadhyādhimātrakleśotpattibhedaḥ parikalpyeta na tu sakalabaṃdhanānāṃ. prāptināṃ tulyatvāt. yato vā sa bheda iti. yato vā kāraṇād abhyāsato 'nyato vā sa bhedaḥ. kasyacit sakalabandhanasyādhimātraḥ. kasyacin madhyaḥ. kasyacin mṛduḥ. tata eva bhedakāraṇāt tadutpattir astu.
teṣāṃ mṛdvādīnāṃ kleśānām utpattiḥ. tasmān notpattihetuḥ prāptir iti. vaibhāṣika āha. kaś caivam āheti vistaraḥ. vyavasthāhetuḥ prāptiḥ. asatyāṃ hi prāptau laukikamānasānām iti. loke bhavo laukikaṃ. mana eva mānasaṃ. laukikaṃ mānasam eṣāṃ te ime laukikamānasāḥ. āryapṛthagjanāḥ. āryāś ca pṛthagjanāś ca. laukikamānasagrahaṇam āryaviśeṣaṇaṃ. [Tib. 134a] pṛthagjanā hi nityam eva laukikamānasāḥ. āsaṃjñikāsaṃjñisamāpattyavasthāyāṃ vā pṛthagjanaviśeṣaṇam api saṃbhavati. teṣāṃ āryapṛthagjanānāṃ. teṣām iti nirdhāraṇe ṣaṣṭhī. sambandhalakṣaṇā vā. teṣāṃ na syād vyavasthānam iti paricchedaḥ. yat kṛtaṃ vyavasthānaṃ. sā prāptiḥ. prahīṇāprahiṇakleśatāviśeṣād iti. prahīṇakleśā āryāḥ. aprahīṇakleśāḥ pṛthagjanāḥ. tadbhāvāḥ. sa eva viśeṣaḥ. iti prahīṇāprahīṇakleśataviśeṣaḥ. tasmād. etad vyavasthānaṃ bhavitum arhati. nanu ca pṛthagjanā api kecit prahīṇakleśā bhavanti. katham avadhāryate. āryā eva prahīṇakleśā iti. atyaṃtasamudghātavacanād evam uktaṃ. etac caiva katham iti. eṣāṃ prahīṇaḥ kleśa eṣām aprahīṇa iti yad etad vyavasthānaṃ. tat kathaṃ bhaviṣyati. prāptau tu satyāṃ kleśaprāptyā etat sidhyati vyavasthānaṃ. tadvigamāvigamāt kleśaprāptivigamāvigamāt chedācchedād
body.translated_text: the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge and the rest. And those that have been abandoned through dispassion from level-transition — for example, the non-afflicted [dharmas] of the desire-realm [that are] abandoned through rebirth in a higher level, and the afflicted [dharmas] abandoned through dispassion — how would their arising occur? For there is no <s>prāpti</s> (acquisition) of those, since they are unarisen and ceased. If [it is said] a co-arisen <s>prāpti</s> is the cause — which is the arising [that was] undertaken [as subject]? The co-arisen <s>prāpti</s> that now arises — that is their generator. He says: 'What then does birth (<s>jāti</s>) do? Or the birth-of-birth (<s>jātijāti</s>)?' '<s>Kiṃkarī</s>' means 'having what function.' Birth generates the target <s>dharma</s>. [Tib. 133b] But the birth-of-birth generates that characteristic — namely, birth. Therefore, if the arising of the target <s>dharmas</s> is said to have <s>prāpti</s> as its cause, then what does birth do? If, on the other hand, it is said to be the cause of the arising of the characteristics — then he says: 'Or what does the birth-of-birth do?' — this is the dilemma. Alternatively, if you conceive it thus — 'birth generates the <s>dharma</s>, and <s>prāpti</s> generates birth' — in that case, he says: 'Or what does the birth-of-birth do?' 'Even for those with complete fetters' — and so on in detail. Those for whom not a single type of affliction has been abandoned — they are those with complete fetters. For those with complete fetters too, the differentiation of mild, medium, and intense affliction-arising should not occur. Why? Because of the non-differentiation of <s>prāpti</s>. For the differentiation of mild, medium, and intense affliction-arising could be conceived for those with incomplete fetters — due to the deficiency of their <s>prāptis</s> — but not for those with complete fetters, since their <s>prāptis</s> are equal. 'Or from whatever [cause] that differentiation [arises]' — from whatever cause — whether habituation or something else — that differentiation [arises]: for some person with complete fetters, [the affliction] is intense; for some, medium; for some, mild. Let the arising of those — the mild and the rest of the afflictions — be from that very differentiating cause. Therefore, <s>prāpti</s> is not the cause of arising. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'But who says this?' — and so on in detail. <s>Prāpti</s> is the cause of determination (<s>vyavasthāhetu</s>). For in the absence of <s>prāpti</s>, for worldly-minded ones (<s>laukikamānasa</s>) — '<s>laukika</s>' means 'belonging to the world'; '<s>mānasa</s>' is the mind itself; those whose [distinguishing feature is] the worldly mind are <s>laukikamānasāḥ</s> — [i.e.,] Noble Ones and ordinary persons. Noble Ones and ordinary persons [together]. The term <s>laukikamānasa</s> qualifies the Noble Ones. [Tib. 134a] For ordinary persons are always worldly-minded. Or, in the state of the <s>asaṃjñika</s> (non-perceptual) and the cessation attainments, it may also qualify ordinary persons. Of those Noble Ones and ordinary persons — 'of those' is a genitive of specification, or one denoting connection — there would be no determination. What determination has been made — that is <s>prāpti</s>. 'Because of the distinction of having abandoned and not having abandoned afflictions' — Noble Ones have abandoned afflictions; ordinary persons have not abandoned afflictions. Their states — that itself is the distinction — thus, 'the distinction of having abandoned and not having abandoned afflictions.' Therefore this determination ought to exist. [Objection:] 'But some ordinary persons too have abandoned afflictions. How is it determined that only Noble Ones have abandoned afflictions?' Because of the statement regarding complete eradication — thus it has been said. 'And how this [is so]' — this determination that 'for some, afflictions have been abandoned; for others, not abandoned' — how will it hold? When <s>prāpti</s> exists, this determination is accomplished through affliction-<s>prāpti</s>. 'Through the presence and absence of that' — through the presence and absence of affliction-<s>prāpti</s> — meaning: through cutting and non-cutting.

body.text: ity arthaḥ. yeṣāṃ tatprāptivigamāḥ. te āryāḥ. yeṣām avigamāḥ. te pṛthagjanā iti. nanu ca pṛthagjanānām api keṣāṃcit kleśaprāptir vigatā. vigatā. na tu lokottareṇa mārgeṇa. sa tarhi lokottaramārgakṛto [Tib. 134b] viśeṣaḥ kathaṃ paricchidyate lokottareṇeyaṃ kleśaprāptir vigatā laukikeneyam iti. sāsravānāsravavisaṃyogaprāptibhedāt. āśryaviśeṣād etat sidhyatīti. ātmabhāvaviśeṣād etad vyavasthānaṃ eṣāṃ prahīṇaḥ kleśa eṣām aprahīṇaḥ kleśa iti sidhyati. tathā parāvṛtta iti. tathānyathābhūtaḥ. tatpraheyāṇāṃ darśanabhāvanāmārgapraheyāṇām. agnidagdhavrīhivad iti. yathāgnidagdho vrīhir abījībhūto bhavati. evaṃ yathoktena nyāyenābījībhūtaḥ āśrayaḥ kleśānāṃ prahīṇakleśa ity ucgate. upahatabījabhāve vā. āśraya ity adhikṛtaṃ. tena laukikena mārgeṇa prahīṇa iti śakyate vaktuṃ. bījasyopaghātamātrabhāvāt. viparyayād aprahīṇa iti. anirdagdhabīja āśraye 'nupahatabījabhāve vā. yaś cāprahīṇa iti vistaraḥ. yaś cāprahīṇo 'nantaroktena vidhinā darśanaprahātavyaḥ kāmāvacaro yāvad bhāvāgrikaḥ bhāvanāprahātavyo vā kāmāvacaro yāvad bhāvāgrikaḥ. tena samanvāgataḥ. yaś ca prahīṇas tathaiva yāvad bhāvāgrikaḥ. tenasamanvāgata iti prajñapyate. prajñaptidharmo 'yam iti darśayati. kuśalā api dviprakārā iti vistaraḥ. yathā kliṣṭā dviprakārā ity apiśabdārthaḥ. samuccaye vā kuśalāś cety arthaḥ. tadbījabhāvānupaghātād iti. teṣām utpattilābhikānāṃ kuśalānāṃ bījaṃ tadbījaṃ. tadbījasya bhāvas tadbījabhāvaḥ [Tib. 135a]. kasya. āśrayasya. tadbījabhāvasyānupaghātas tadbījabhāvānupaghātaḥ. tasmāt. tadbījabhāvānupaghātāt samanvāgataḥ. kaiḥ. ayatnabhāvibhiḥ kuśalaiḥ. upaghātād asamanvāgata ucyate. ko 'sāv ity āha. samucchinnakuśalamūlaḥ. tasya tv iti. tasyāśrayasya tadbījabhāvasya upaghāto mithyādṛṣṭyā veditavyo nānyathā. tenāha. na tu khalu kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ bījabhāvasyātyantaṃ saṃtatau samudghāto yathā kleśānām āryamārgeṇātyantaṃ saṃtatau samudghāta ity abhiprāyaḥ. ye punar iti vistaraḥ. ye prāyogikāḥ. tair utpannaiḥ. teṣām utpattis tadutpattiḥ. tadutpattau vaśitvaṃ sāmarthyaviśeṣaḥ. tasyāvighātāt. kasya. saṃtateḥ. samanvāgama ucyate. kaiḥ. tair yatnabhāvibhiḥ kuśulaiḥ. yasmād evaṃ. tasmād bījam eva śaktiviśeṣa evātra samanvāgamāvasthāyām anapoddhṛtaṃ kliṣṭānāṃ dharmāṇām āryamārgeṇānupahataṃ laukikena mārgeṇa. ayatnabhāvināṃ ca kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyā. paripuṣṭaṃ ca vaśitvakāle yatnabhāvināṃ kuśalānāṃ bījam iti prakṛtaṃ. samanvāgamākhyāṃ labhate. nānyad dravyaṃ. yad vaibhāṣikaiḥ kalpitaṃ. kiṃ punar idaṃ bījaṃ nāmeti.
body.translated_text: Those for whom there is the cessation of that <s>prāpti</s> — they are Noble Ones. Those for whom there is no cessation — they are ordinary persons. [Objection:] 'But for some ordinary persons too, the <s>prāpti</s> of afflictions has ceased.' It has ceased — but not through the supramundane path. 'Then how is the distinction made by the supramundane path [Tib. 134b] — [that] "this affliction-<s>prāpti</s> has ceased through the supramundane [path]" and "this through the mundane [path]"?' Through the distinction of outflow-possessing and outflow-free disconnection-acquisitions (<s>visaṃyogaprāpti</s>). 'Through the distinction of the basis (<s>āśraya</s>), this is accomplished' — through the distinction of the bodily basis, this determination — 'for these, afflictions have been abandoned; for those, afflictions have not been abandoned' — is accomplished. 'One who is thus transformed' — one who has become otherwise [in nature]. 'Of those to be abandoned by that' — of those to be abandoned by the paths of insight and cultivation. 'Like rice burned by fire' — just as rice burned by fire becomes seedless (<s>abījībhūta</s>), so too, the basis [of afflictions] that has become seedless by the method described is called 'one whose afflictions are abandoned.' Or, when the seed-state is merely impaired. 'Basis' is the subject. Therefore, [when abandoned] by the mundane path, it can be said to be 'abandoned' — because the seed has merely been impaired. 'In the opposite case, not abandoned' — when the seed in the basis is unburned, or when the seed-state is unimpaired. 'And that which is not abandoned' — and so on in detail. That which is not abandoned by the method just stated — whether to be abandoned by insight or by cultivation, whether belonging to the desire-realm up to the peak of existence — one is endowed with that. And that which has been abandoned, similarly up to the peak of existence — one is not endowed with that — thus it is designated. He shows that this is a matter of convention (<s>prajñaptidharma</s>). 'Wholesome [dharmas] too are of two kinds' — and so on in detail. Just as afflicted [dharmas] are of two kinds — this is the meaning of the word 'too.' Or, the word 'too' indicates addition: 'wholesome [dharmas] as well.' 'Because of the non-impairment of their seed-state' — the seed of those wholesome [dharmas] that are obtained by birth is 'their seed'; the state of that seed is 'their seed-state.' [Tib. 135a] Of what? Of the basis. The non-impairment of their seed-state is 'the non-impairment of their seed-state.' Therefore — because of the non-impairment of their seed-state, one is endowed. With what? With those wholesome [dharmas] that arise effortlessly. 'Because of impairment, one is said to be not endowed.' Who is that? He says: one whose wholesome roots are cut off (<s>samucchinnakuśalamūla</s>). 'But of that [basis]' — the impairment of that basis's seed-state should be understood as [caused] by wrong view, not otherwise. Therefore he says: 'But the complete eradication of the seed-state of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> in the continuum is not ultimate, as [is] the complete eradication of afflictions by the Noble Path in the continuum' — this is the intent. 'But those which...' — and so on in detail. Those that are produced by effort (<s>prāyogika</s>) — when they have arisen, their arising is 'their arising'; mastery over their arising is a special capacity. Because of the non-obstruction of that — of what? Of the continuum — [one] is said to be endowed. With what? With those wholesome [dharmas] that arise with effort. Because this is so, therefore the seed — the special capacity alone — here, in the state of endowment, is the unextracted [seed] of afflicted <s>dharmas</s> unimpaired by the Noble Path, [or unimpaired] by the mundane path; and [the seed] of effortlessly-arising wholesome <s>dharmas</s> [unimpaired] by wrong view; and the seed of effortfully-arising wholesome [dharmas] that has been nourished at the time of mastery — this is the topic. [This seed] receives the designation 'endowment' (<s>samanvāgama</s>). It is not another substance — which was posited by the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>. 'But what then is this so-called seed?'

body.text:
dravyāśaṃkayā pṛcchati.
yan nāmarūpaṃ phalotpattau samarthaṃ. yat paṃcaskandhātmakaṃ rūpaṃ phalotpattisamarthaṃ sākṣād anantaraṃ [Tib. 135b] pāraṃparyeṇa dūrataḥ. ko 'yaṃ pariṇāmo nāmeti. sāṃkhyānāṃ pariṇāmāśaṃkayā pṛcchati. saṃtater anyathātvam iti. anyathotpādaḥ. kā ceyaṃ saṃtatir iti. kiṃ yathā sāṃkhyānām avasthitadravyasya dharmāntaranivṛttau dharmāṃtaraprādurbhāvaḥ tathāvasthāyinyāḥ saṃtater anyathātvam iti. nety ucyate. kiṃ tarhi. hetuphalabhūtā. hetuś ca phalaṃ ca hetuphalaṃ. hetuphalam iti nairantaryeṇa pravṛttās traiyadhvikāḥ saṃskārāḥ saṃtatir iti vyavasthāpyante. yatra tūktam iti vistaraḥ. yatra tu sūtra uktaṃ. kim ity āha. lobhena samanvāgataḥ abhavyaḥ ayogyaś catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni kāyasmṛtyupasthānādīni utpādayitum iti. yadi bījaṃ prāptiḥ. bījaṃ nityam astīti smṛtyupasthānotpattir na syāt. bhavadīyāyām api prāptau tadutpattir na syād iti tulyam etat. tasmād ubhābhyām api vaktavyaṃ. tatrādhivāsanaṃ lobhasyāvinodanaṃ vā samanvāgama iti. adhivāsanam abhyanujñānam. avinodanam avyupaśamanaṃ. sarvathā prajñaptidharmo na dravyadharma iti. sarvaprakāreṇa yady utpattihetur yadi vyavasthāhetur yady āśrayaviśeṣaḥ yady adhivāsanam avinodanaṃ vā sarvathā prajñaptidharmaḥ prajñaptyā saṃvṛtyā vyavahāreṇa dharmaḥ prajñaptidharmo na dravyadharmaḥ na dravyato dharmaḥ svabhāva ity arthaḥ. atha vā dravyaṃ ca tad dharmaś ca sa dravyadharmo [Tib. 136a] na rūpādivat vidyamānasvalakṣaṇo dharma ity arthaḥ. tasya ca pratiṣedhaḥ tasya ca prajñaptidharmasya pratiṣedho 'samanvāgama iti.
body.translated_text: He asks from the suspicion that it might be a [real] substance. 'That name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) which is capable of producing a result' — that form, having the nature of the five <s>skandhas</s>, which is capable of producing a result, either directly and immediately [Tib. 135b] or indirectly from afar. 'What then is this so-called transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>)?' — he asks from the suspicion of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [concept of] transformation. 'The otherness of the continuum' — arising in a different manner. 'And what is this continuum?' — is it, like the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>' [concept], the arising of a different attribute upon the cessation of another attribute in an enduring substance? [Reply:] It is said: no. What then? '[It] consists of cause and result' — cause and result are <s>hetuphalā</s>; the formations (<s>saṃskārā</s>) of the three time-periods that proceed without interruption as cause-and-result are established as 'continuum.' 'But where it is stated' — and so on in detail. Where it is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s> — what? He says: 'One endowed with greed (<s>lobha</s>) is incapable, unfit to produce the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) — body-mindfulness and the rest.' If the seed is <s>prāpti</s>, [then] since the seed always exists, the arising of the foundations of mindfulness should not occur. [Reply:] 'In your [theory of] <s>prāpti</s> too, their arising should not occur' — this is the same [problem]. Therefore, both [sides] must explain. 'Therein, endowment (<s>samanvāgama</s>) is the tolerance (<s>adhivāsana</s>) or the non-removal of greed.' '<s>Adhivāsana</s>' means acceptance; 'non-removal' means non-pacification. 'In every way, it is a conventionally designated <s>dharma</s>, not a substantially real <s>dharma</s>.' In every manner — whether it is a cause of arising, a cause of determination, a distinction of the basis, or tolerance and non-removal — in every way it is a <s>dharma</s> [existing only] by convention (<s>prajñapti</s>), by conventional reality (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), by usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>) — a conventionally designated <s>dharma</s>, not a substantially real <s>dharma</s>, not a <s>dharma</s> [existing] by intrinsic nature — this is the meaning. Alternatively, 'substance-<s>dharma</s>' means a <s>dharma</s> [that is itself] a substance [Tib. 136a] — not a <s>dharma</s> whose own characteristic is found [to exist] like form and the rest — this is the meaning. And the negation of that — the negation of that conventionally designated <s>dharma</s> — is 'non-endowment' (<s>asamanvāgama</s>).

body.text: idam asyeti jñānacihnaṃ pratilabdhadharmāvipraṇāśakāraṇaṃ ca prāptir ity ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ. idam asyeti jñānacihnaṃ ity asiddham etat. āśrayaviśeṣeṇa tajjñānam iti brūmaḥ. yadi ca pratilabdhadharmavipraṇāśakāraṇaṃ prāptir iṣyate. prāptaparityāgo naiva syāt. bhavati ca. tasmād akāraṇam etat. sa eva ca śaktiviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ bījabhāvam ācāryena vyavasthāpitaṃ dūṣayati. kim ayaṃ śaktiviśeṣaś cittād arthāntaram ato 'narthāntaraṃ. kiṃ cātaḥ. arthāntaraṃ cet. siddhaṃ prāptir astīti. saṃjñāmātre tu vivādaḥ. anarthāntaraṃ cet. nanv akuśalaṃ kuśalasya bījaṃ abhyupagataṃ bhavati. akuśalasya ca kuśalaṃ. ko hi nāma auṣṇyasya tejaso 'narthāntaratve saty auṣṇyam eva dāhakam adhyavasyen na tejaḥ. kuśalabījaṃ hy akuśale cetasy avyākṛte vā vartate. evam akuśalabījaṃ kuśale cetasy avyākṛte vā vartate. tathaiva cāvyākṛtabījam api kuśale
body.translated_text: The master <s>Saṃghabhadra</s> [says]: '<s>Prāpti</s> is the cognitive sign [indicated by] "this belongs to this [person]" and the cause preventing the loss of acquired <s>dharmas</s>.' 'The cognitive sign [indicated by] "this belongs to this [person]"' — this is unestablished. We say: that knowledge [arises] from the distinction of the basis. And if <s>prāpti</s> is accepted as the cause preventing the loss of acquired <s>dharmas</s>, then the relinquishment of what has been acquired should never occur — but it does occur. Therefore, this is not a [valid] cause. And he criticizes the seed-state characterized as a special capacity, which was established by the <s>Ācārya</s> [<s>Vasubandhu</s>]: 'Is this special capacity something different from mind, or not different?' And what follows from this? If it is different, then it is established that <s>prāpti</s> exists — the dispute is merely about the name. But if it is not different, then an unwholesome [mind] would be accepted as the seed of the wholesome, and a wholesome [mind] as [the seed] of the unwholesome. For who indeed, when heat is not different from fire, would conclude that heat alone burns but not fire? For the wholesome seed exists in an unwholesome or indeterminate mind; likewise, the unwholesome seed exists in a wholesome or indeterminate mind; and similarly, the indeterminate seed too [exists] in a wholesome

body.text: cākuśale ca vartate. sāsravabījaṃ cānāsrave 'nāsravabījaṃ ca sāsrave cetasi vartata iti sāṃkaryadoṣaḥ prasajyata iti. atra vayaṃ brūmaḥ. anarthāntarabhāve sāṃkaryadoṣa bhavet. tat tu bījaṃ na cittād arthāntaraṃ vaktavyaṃ. nāpy anarthāntaram. upādāyaprajñaptirūpatvāt. [Tib. 136b] athāpy anarthāntarabhāvas tathāpy adośaḥ. kuśalena hi cittenotpannena svajātīye 'nyajātīye vā svasaṃtānacitte bījam ādhīyeta. tataḥ kāraṇaviśeṣāt kāryaviśeṣa iti viśiṣṭaṃ. tena tac cittam utpadyeta. tad viśiṣṭaṃ cittaṃ kuśalabījakāryakriyāyāṃ samartham utpadyeta. evam akuśalenāpi svajātīye 'nyajātīye vā svasaṃtānacitte bījam ādhīyeta. tac ca tena viśiṣṭaṃ cittam akuśalabījakāryakriyāyāṃ samartham utpadyeta. evam avyākṛtenāpi cittena svajātīye 'nyajātīye vā svasaṃtānacitte bījam ādhīyeta. tac cāpi tena viśiṣṭam avyākṛtabījakāryakriyāyāṃ samartham utpadyeta. sāsraveṇāpy anāsrave citte bījam ādhīyeta. anāsraveṇāpi sāsrava ity evam anyonyabījādhāyakam anyonyajanakaṃ ca cittaṃ cittāntarād utpadyamāmaṃ anyonyavāsyavasakatvena pravartate. na ca kuśalenākuśale citte śaktiviśeṣa āhita iti tad akuśalaṃ kuśalatām āpadyate. kuśalaṃ vā tad akuśalatāṃ. śaktiviśeṣamātratvāt. śaktir bījaṃ vāsanety eko 'yam arthaḥ. evam akuśalādivāsanāpi vaktavyā. yāvat sāsraveṇānāsrave śaktiviśeṣādhāne 'pi. anāsraveṇāpi sāsrave śaktiviśeṣādhāne. na tat sāsravaṃ anāsravaṃ saṃpadyate. anāsravaṃ vā sāsravam iti. bhavatām api vaibhāṣikāṇām idaṃ ciṃtyate. yadā sāsravacittasamanaṃtaraṃ [Tib. 137a] anāsravaṃ anāsravacittasamanantaraṃ vā sāsravacittam utpadyate. tadā kiṃ pūrvakaḥ sāsravakalāpo 'nāsravakalāpo vā śaktimān samanantarapratyayādibhāvenottarakalāpotpattāv utāśaktimān. kiṃ cātaḥ. yady aśaktimān samanantarapratyayādibhāvo 'py asya hīyeta. atha śaktimān. sā śaktiḥ kiṃ sāsrave cetasi sāsravā āhosvid anāsravā. tac cittaṃ sāsravasyānāsravasya ca cittāntarasya samanantarapratyayādibhāvaṃ kuryāt. tat kiṃ yayaiva śaktyā sāsravasya samanantarapratyayādibhāvaṃ kuryāt tayaivānāsravasya. yadi tayaiva kathaṃ śaktikāryasāṃkaryaṃ na bhavet. athānyayā śaktyā sāsravasyānyayānāsravasya samanantarapratyayādibhāvaṃ kuryāt. katham anayor ekatra śaktyos tasmāc cittād ananyayor bhinnarūpatā bhinnakāryatā ca yujyate. yujyate cet. asmākam api cittād ananyāsāṃ śaktīnāṃ tatrāvasthānaṃ kāryabhedaś ca bhaviṣyati. evam anāsravasyāpi cittasya sāsravānāsravacittasamanantarapratyayādibhāvena saṃbhavataḥ tathaiva śaktyor bhinnarūpatā kāryabhedaś ca vaktavyaḥ. tena yad uktaṃ nanv akuśalaṃ kuśalasya bījam
body.translated_text: and it also operates in the unwholesome. And the seed of the defiled [is said to exist] in the undefiled, and the seed of the undefiled in the defiled mind —

body.text: abhyupagataṃ bhavatītyādi tad ayuktaṃ. na hi kuśalāhitena śaktiviśeṣeṇa viśiṣṭaṃ samartham akuśalam akuśalabījakāryaṃ karoti. [Tib. 137b] kiṃ tarhi. kuśalabījakāryam eva karoti. svāhitena tu śaktiviśeṣeṇa tad akuśalaṃ svabījakāryaṃ karoti. tat katham idam ucyate. kuśalasyākuśalaṃ bījam iti. brūyās tvam akuśalacitte tat kuśalabījam āhitaṃ kathaṃ akuśalaṃ na bhavatīti. na bhavanto bījārthaṃ jānate. kuśalena cittena nirudhyamānena. tathā śaktiviśiṣṭam akuśalaṃ cittaṃ janyeta yathā tac cittaṃ svotpattiyogyaṃ bhaviṣyati sākṣāt pāraṃparyeṇa veti śaktiviśeṣa eva bījaṃ. na bījaṃ nāma kiṃcid asti. prajñaptisattvāt. ata eva prāptyaprāptī prajñaptisatyāv ucyete. dravyasatyāv eva tu vaibhāṣikā varṇayanti.
body.translated_text: this is accepted, and so on — that is improper. For [a mind] distinguished by a special capacity deposited by the wholesome [is not properly accounted for] —

body.text: (II.38, 39ab) atītānāṃ dharmāṇām atītāpi prāptir iti vistaraḥ. atītānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tadyathā kliṣṭānām atītā prāptir yā utpannaniruddhā sāgrajāpi saṃbhavati. sahajāpi. paścātkālajāpi. teṣām evānāgatā prāptir anutpannā. pratyutpannā yā paścātkālajā utpannaniruddhā. anāgatānām api prāptir atītā yāgrajotpannaniruddhā. anāgatā yānutpannā. pratyutpannāgrajotpannāniruddhā. tathā pratyutpannānām apy atītā prāptir yāgrajotpannaniruddhā. anāgatā yānutpannā. pratyutpannā yā sahajā. atītādijātisāmānyaṃ ca gṛhītvaivam uktam. na tv ekasyātītasyāvaśyaṃ trividhā prāptir asti. na hi vipākajasyānāgatātītā vā prāptiḥ saṃbhavati.
body.translated_text: (II.38, 39ab) 'The <s>prāpti</s> of past <s>dharmas</s> is also past' — thus the elaboration. Of past <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>prāpti</s> —

children.translated_text: 'The attainment of the morally indeterminate is simultaneous' —

body.text: vacanāt. [Tib. 138a] yadi tu pratidravyaṃ prāptivyavasthā kriyeta saṃbhavaṃ praty etad evaṃ bhavet. kliṣṭānām utpattipratilaṃbhikānāṃ ca kuśalānām atītādīnām atītādayaḥ prāptayo 'vaśyaṃ bhavanti. na hi pṛthagjanasyānutpannasya anāsravasya mārgasyātītā pratyutpannā ca prāptir asti. sāpavādaś cāyam utsargo 'vagantavyaḥ.
body.translated_text: from this statement. But if <s>prāpti</s> were to be established for each individual substance, with reference to possibility —

children.translated_text: 'The attainment of the morally indeterminate is simultaneous' —

body.text: vecanāt. asaṃskṛtānāṃ tu prāpti utpannaniruddhātītā. 'nutpannānāgatā. utpannāniruddhā pratyutpannā. sugamatvāt tu na sūtritam etat. kāmarūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ kāmarūpārūpyāvacarī yathākramam iti. kāmadhātūpapannasya kāmāvacarāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kāmāvacarī prāptiḥ. tasyaiva rūpāvacarāṇāṃ rūpāvacarī. tasyaivārūpyāvacarāṇām ārūpyāvacarī. rūpadhātūpapannasya ca kāmāvacarāṇāṃ. tadyathā nirmāṇacittānāṃ kāmāvacarī. rūpāvacarāṇāṃ rūpāvacarī
body.translated_text: from this statement. But for the unconditioned [<s>dharmas</s>], the <s>prāpti</s> [can be]: arisen-and-ceased, hence past; not-yet-arisen, hence future; arisen-and-not-ceased —

body.text: . ārūpyāvacarāṇām ārūpyāvacarī. ārūpyadhātūpapannasya taddhātukānāṃ taddhātukaiva prāptiḥ.
body.translated_text: of those belonging to the formless realm, [the <s>prāpti</s>] belongs to the formless realm. For one born in the formless realm, [the <s>prāpti</s>] of <s>dharmas</s> belonging to that realm is of that realm —

children.translated_text: 'Of those not attained, [<s>prāpti</s> is] fourfold' — thus.

body.text: adhātvāptānāṃ saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtānām anāsravāṇāṃ caturvidhā prāptiḥ. kāmarūpārūpyāvacarī cānāsravā ca. samāsena sarvān anāptān abhisamasyety arthaḥ. pratyekaṃ tu na caturvidhā. tata āha. tatrāpratisaṃkhyānirodhasyeti vistaraḥ. kāmadhātūpapannasya [Tib. 138b] kāmāvacarādīnāṃ yathāsaṃbhavam apratisaṃkhyānirodhasya prāptiḥ kāmāvacarī. rūpadhātūpapannasya rūpāvacarādīnāṃ apratisaṃkhyānirodhaprāptī rūpāvacarī. ārūpyadhātūpapannasyārūpyāvacarādīnām apratisaṃkhyānirodhaprāptir ārūpyāvacarī. sattvasaṃtānavaśenaiva hi tatprāptir vyavasthāpyate. na tu teṣāṃ vaśena yeṣām apratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. yadi hy evaṃ syāt mārgasatyasyāpratisaṃkhyānirodhaprāptir anāsravā syāt. pratisaṃkhyānirodhasya rūpārūpyāvacarī cānāsravā ceti. na kāmāvacarī. kāmadhātor apratipakṣatvāt. rūpāvacareṇa tu mārgeṇa prāptasya rūpāvacarī prāptiḥ. ārūpyāvacareṇārūpyāvacarī. anāsraveṇa mārgeṇānāsravā. āryasya tu rūpāvacareṇa mārgeṇa prāptasya rūpāvacarī cānāsravā cārūpyāvacareṇārūpyāvacarī cānāsravā ca.
body.translated_text: The <s>prāpti</s> of undefiled conditioned and unconditioned [<s>dharmas</s>] not attained in [any] realm is fourfold: [belonging to] the desire, form, formless [realms], and —

children.translated_text: 'In dispassion through the mundane and noble [paths], the attainments of liberation are twofold' —

body.text: vacanāt. mārgasatyasyānāsravaiveti. laukikīm asya prāptiṃ pratiṣedhayati. seyaṃ samasya caturvidheti. samāsena traidhātukī cānāsravā ceti uktam arthaṃ nigamayati. śaikṣāṇām iti. śaikṣā dharmāḥ śaikṣasyānāsravā dharmā. aśaikṣā aśaikṣasyānāsravā. [Tib. 139a] mārgasatyabhāvā evaite draṣṭavyāḥ. śaikṣāśaikṣebhyas tv anye naiva śaikṣā nāśaikṣāḥ. asaṃskṛtā api yāvan naiva śaikṣā nāśaikṣā iṣyante. teṣāṃ
body.translated_text: from this statement. 'The truth of the path is exclusively undefiled' — he denies a mundane <s>prāpti</s> for it [the path]. This —

body.text: prāptiḥ śaikṣādibhedena. śaikṣī aśaikṣī naiva śaikṣī nāśaikṣī ceti. anāryeṇa prāptasyeti. pṛthagjanena prāptasya. tasyaiva śaikṣeṇeti. tasyaiva pratisaṃkhyānirodhasya śaikṣeṇa mārgeṇa prāptasya śaikṣī. aśaikṣeṇāśaikṣī. kṣayajñānasaṃprayuktena mārgeṇa prāptasya. visaṃyogaprāptisaṃniśrayatvāt kṣayajñānasya. yady api sā vajropamena śaikṣeṇa prāpyate tadāvāhakatvāt. tatprāptatvavacane tu śaikṣyāḥ prāpteḥ aśaikṣī prāptir viśeṣitā syād iti na tena śaikṣeṇa
body.translated_text: <s>prāpti</s>, by the distinction of learner and the rest. [It is] of a learner, of one beyond training, and of neither-learner-nor-beyond-training. When attained by a non-noble [person] —

body.text: aśaikṣīty uktaṃ. tasyaivāryamārgaprāptasyānāsraveti. tasyaiva pratisaṃkhyā nirodhasya āryamārgaprāptasya anāsravā. mārgasatyasya cānāsravā prāptir ity adhikṛtaṃ. āryeṇa laukikamārgaprāptasya pratisaṃkhyānirodhasya prāptiḥ kiṃ sāsravā utāho 'nāsravā. ubhayathety āha. sā kasmān noktā. sāvaśeṣaṃ bhāṣyaṃ. paścād darśayiṣyate
body.translated_text: 'of one beyond training' — thus it is said. Of that very [person] who has attained the noble path, the undefiled — that very analytical cessation —

children.translated_text: 'In dispassion through the mundane and noble [paths], the attainments of liberation are twofold' —

body.text: nocyate. yā tv asaṃkīrṇā prāptiḥ saivehocyate iti veditavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: is not stated [here]. But the unmixed <s>prāpti</s> alone is what is stated here — this should be understood.

body.text: (II.39cd, 40ab) durbalatvād iti. anabhisaṃskāravattvād durbalatvaṃ.
body.translated_text: (II.39cd, 40ab) 'Because of weakness' — weakness is due to being without deliberate effort (<s>anabhisaṃskāravatva</s>).

body.text: dve abhijñe iti. divyacaksurabhijñāṃ [Tib. 139b] divyaśrotrābhijñāṃ. nirmāṇacittaṃ ca varjayitvā. kiṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Two <s>abhijñās</s> (direct knowledges)' — the divine-eye <s>abhijñā</s> and the divine-ear <s>abhijñā</s>. The creation-mind —

children.translated_text: 'The attainment of the morally indeterminate is simultaneous' —

body.text: saṃbandhanīyaṃ. teṣāṃ hi balavattvād iti vistaraḥ. teṣāṃ hi divyacakṣurabhijñādīnāṃ balavattvāt. kiṃ. pūrvaṃpaścātsahajā prāptiḥ. prayogaviśeṣaniṣpatter iti. prayogaviśeṣeṇa niṣpattir divyacakṣurabhijñādīnāṃ. tasyāḥ. prayogaviśeṣaniṣpatter balavattvaṃ. balavattvāt pūrvaṃpaścātsahajā prāptir ity arthasambandhaḥ. śailpasthānikasyāpi kasyacit tadyathā viśvakarmaṇaḥ. airyāpathikasya ca tadyathā sthavirasyāśvajitasya. atyartham abhyastasya bhṛśam ātmasātkṛtasyecchanti vaibhāṣikāḥ. kiṃ. pūrvaṃpaścātsahajā prāptir iti.
body.translated_text: should be connected [here]. 'Because of their strength' — thus the elaboration. For those — the divine-eye <s>abhijñā</s> and the rest —

body.text: caśabdaḥ samuccayārthaḥ. prāptiḥ sahajeti samuccīyate. tac ca kliṣṭaṃ rūpaṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikam eva vijñaptirūpaṃ veditavyaṃ. tato 'nyāsu bhūmiṣu tadutthāpakābhāvāt. adhimātreṇāpīti vistaraḥ. adhimātreṇāpi cittena nivṛtā vijñaptir utthāpitā. tad eva cādhimātraṃ vijñapticittaṃ avijñaptiṃ notthāpayati. ato daurbalyasiddhiḥ. tasyā daurbalyasiddheḥ sahajaiva prāptiḥ.
body.translated_text: The word 'and' is for the purpose of aggregation. '<s>Prāpti</s> (possession) is simultaneous' is what is aggregated. And that afflicted form should be understood as informative form (<s>vijñaptirūpa</s>) belonging to the ground of the first <s>dhyāna</s> only, because in other grounds there is no cause to produce it. 'Even by an intense [mind]' — thus the elaboration. Even by an intense mind, the covered informative [form] is produced. But that same intense informative-mind does not produce non-informative [form] (<s>avijñapti</s>). Therefore its weakness is established. Because its weakness is established, <s>prāpti</s> is simultaneous only.

body.text: prāptibheda iti. vipākajādīnām anivṛtāvyākṛtānāṃ sahajā prāptiḥ. abhijñādvayādīnāṃ tu pūrvaṃpaścātsahajā prāptir iti tadbhedaḥ.
body.translated_text: The distinction of <s>prāpti</s>: for the maturation-born and other uncovered-indeterminate [<s>dharma</s>s], <s>prāpti</s> is simultaneous only. But for the two supernatural knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) and the like, <s>prāpti</s> is prior, subsequent, and simultaneous — that is the distinction.

body.text: Tib. 140a
body.translated_text: Tib. 140a

body.text: kāmāvacarasya kuśalākuśalasya vijñaptyavjñaptirūpasyāgrajāprāptiḥ sarvathā nāsti. yadi kuśalasya yady akuśalasya nāsty eva sarvathety arthaḥ. sahajā cāsti paścātkālajā ceti saṃbhavataḥ. tadyathā prathamasya vijñaptyavijñaptikṣaṇasya ādau sahajā prāptir bhavati. dvitīyādiṣu kṣaṇeṣu tasyaivādyasya kṣaṇasya paścātkālajā bhavati. evam anyeṣām api dvitīyādīnāṃ kṣaṇānāṃ sahajā paścātkālajā prāptir veditavyā. kāmāvacarasyaiva rūpasyāgrajā
body.translated_text: For the informative and non-informative form (<s>vijñaptyavijñaptirūpa</s>) of the desire realm that is wholesome or unwholesome, prior <s>prāpti</s> does not exist in any way. Whether it is wholesome or unwholesome, it does not exist at all — this is the meaning. But simultaneous and subsequent [<s>prāpti</s>] is possible. For example, of the first moment of informative and non-informative [form], simultaneous <s>prāpti</s> occurs at the beginning. In the second and subsequent moments, subsequent <s>prāpti</s> of that very first moment occurs. Likewise, for the second and other moments too, simultaneous and subsequent <s>prāpti</s> should be understood. Since only prior <s>prāpti</s> of desire-realm form is negated

body.text: prāptipratiṣedhād dhyānānāsravasaṃvararūpasyāgrajā prāptir asty evety utsṛṣṭā bhavati.
body.translated_text: , prior <s>prāpti</s> of <s>dhyāna</s> and non-outflow restraint form is left open — it does indeed exist.

body.text: (II.40cd, 41) aprāptir anivṛtāvyākṛtaiva sarvā. kasmād vyavasthāpyate. yady aprāptiḥ kleśānāṃ kliṣṭā bhavet. prahīṇakleśasya kleśavad eva na syāt. yadi kuśalā syāt samucchinnakuśalamūlasya na syāt. anāsravāṇāṃ dharmāṇām aprāptir anāsravā syāt. kiṃ syāt. pṛthagjano na syān nityam āryadharmasamanvāgatatvāt. pāriśeṣyād anivṛtāvyākṛtaivāprāptir iti vyavasthāpyate. pratyutpannasya nāsty aprāptiḥ pratyutpanneti. pratyutpannasya dharmasya prāptir vartate. tasmād asyāprāptir nāsti pratyutpannā. tasya prāptyaprāptyoḥ samavadhānāsaṃbhavāt. atītānāgatayos tu traiyadhvikīti. aprāptānāṃ prāptavihīnānāṃ ca prāyogikānāṃ guṇānām anāgatānāṃ ca cakṣurādīnām api ca yeṣāṃ [Tib. 140b] prāptir nāsti atītāpy asty aprāptir anāgatāpi pratyutpannāpi. srotonyāyena hi teṣām aprāptir utpadyate nirudhyate 'nāgatavasthāneti.
body.translated_text: (II.40cd, 41) All non-possession (<s>aprāpti</s>) is entirely uncovered-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>). Why is it so determined? If non-possession of afflictions were afflicted, then for one who has abandoned afflictions, it would be like the afflictions themselves — it would not exist. If it were wholesome, then for one who has uprooted wholesome roots, it would not exist. Non-possession of non-outflow <s>dharma</s>s would be non-outflow. What would follow? An ordinary person would not exist, because of always being endowed with noble <s>dharma</s>s. By elimination, non-possession is determined as entirely uncovered-indeterminate. 'Of what is presently [arising], there is no non-possession that is present' — of a presently [arising] <s>dharma</s>, <s>prāpti</s> is operating. Therefore its non-possession does not exist as present, because of the impossibility of <s>prāpti</s> and <s>aprāpti</s> coinciding. 'But of past and future [<s>dharma</s>s], it belongs to all three times' — of qualities attained through practice that are not [yet] attained or have been lost, and of future eye-faculties and the like, and also of those [<s>dharma</s>s] whose [Tib. 140b] <s>prāpti</s> does not exist — whether past, future, or present non-possession exists. For their non-possession arises and ceases in the manner of a stream, and abides in the future state.

children.translated_text: 'Of the desire [realm] and the rest, attained, and non-outflow' —

body.text: tridhety anukarṣaṇārthaś cakāraḥ. kāmādiṣu dhātuṣu āptā aviyuktāḥ kāmādyāptāḥ. kāmādyāptānām amalānāṃ cāprāptis trividhā. upapattyāśrayavaśena tadvyavasthāpanāt. dharmasahāvyavasthāpinī hy aprāptiḥ. na prāptivad dharmavaśena vyavasthāpyate. tasmāt kāmadhātūpapannasya kāmarūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ anāsravāṇāṃ ca dharmāṇām aprāptiḥ kāmāvacarī. rūpadhātūpapannasya rūpāvacarī. ārūpyadhātūpapannasya ārūpyāvacarī. tadyathā kāmadhātūpapannasya prāyogikānāṃ guṇānām upapattilābhikānām api kuśalasamucchedāvasthāyām aprāptir avītarāgatvāc ca rūpārūpyāvacarāṇām akliṣṭānām aprāptiḥ pṛthagjanatvāc cānāsravāṇām aprāptiḥ kāmāvacarī. tathā rūpadhātūpapannasya kāmāvacarāṇāṃ bhūmisaṃcāratyaktānāṃ rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ ca prāyogikānāṃ guṇānāṃ pṛthagjanatvāc cānāsravāṇām aprāptī rūpāvacarī. tathaiva cārūpyadhātūpapannasya kāmarūpāvacarāṇāṃ bhūmisaṃcāratyaktānām ārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ ca prāyogikāṇāṃ [Tib. 141a] guṇānāṃ pṛthagjanatvād eva cānāsravāṇām aprāptir ārūpyāvacarīty neyaṃ.
body.translated_text: the word 'and' serves to carry forward 'threefold.' In the desire and other realms, those that are attained — not separated from — are 'attained in the desire [realm] and the rest.' Non-possession of those attained in the desire [realm] and the rest, and of non-outflow [<s>dharma</s>s], is threefold — because it is determined according to the basis of rebirth. For non-possession is determined in accordance with the <s>dharma</s>-possessor, not in accordance with the <s>dharma</s> as in the case of <s>prāpti</s>. Therefore, for one born in the desire realm, non-possession of <s>dharma</s>s belonging to the desire, form, and formless realms, and of non-outflow [<s>dharma</s>s], belongs to the desire realm. For one born in the form realm, it belongs to the form realm. For one born in the formless realm, it belongs to the formless realm. For example, for one born in the desire realm, non-possession of qualities attained through practice and also of those obtained through rebirth — in the state of uprooted wholesome roots — and non-possession of form and formless realm [<s>dharma</s>s] that are unafflicted due to not being free from desire, and non-possession of non-outflow [<s>dharma</s>s] due to being an ordinary person — [all these] belong to the desire realm. Likewise, for one born in the form realm, non-possession of desire-realm [<s>dharma</s>s] abandoned through ground-transition, and of form and formless realm practical qualities, and of non-outflow [<s>dharma</s>s] due to being an ordinary person — belongs to the form realm. Similarly, for one born in the formless realm, non-possession of desire and form realm [<s>dharma</s>s] abandoned through ground-transition, and of formless realm [Tib. 141a] practical qualities, and of non-outflow [<s>dharma</s>s] due to being an ordinary person — belongs to the formless realm. This should be understood.

body.text: pṛthagjanatvaṃ katamat. āryadharmāṇām alābha ity anena śāstrapāṭhenānāsravatvābhāvam aprāpter darśayati. katameṣām āryadharmāṇām alābha iti. āryadharmā duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntim ārabhya sarvo 'nāsravo mārga iti ata evaṃ pṛcchati. sarveṣām aviśeṣavacanād iti. sarveṣāṃ duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntyādīnāṃ śaikṣāśaikṣajñānānām alābhaḥ. kasmāt. aviśeṣtatvāt. yady
body.translated_text: What is the state of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjanatvam</s>)? 'The non-attainment of noble <s>dharma</s>s' — by this statement from the treatise, he shows that non-possession is not of the nature of the non-outflow. 'The non-attainment of which noble <s>dharma</s>s?' Noble <s>dharma</s>s are the entire non-outflow path beginning from the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering — therefore he asks thus. 'Of all, because of the statement without distinction' — non-attainment of all [noble <s>dharma</s>s] beginning from the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering, [including] the knowledges of learners and non-learners. Why? Because of non-distinction. If

body.text: evam utpannāyām api duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntau pariśiṣṭānām āryadharmāṇām alābho 'syāstīti anāryaḥ syāt. tasmād idam āha. sa tu yo vinā lābheneti. yo vinā lābhenālābhaḥ. tat pṛthagjanatvam iti. anyathā hīti vistaraḥ. yady āryadharmāṇāṃ lābhe 'pi sati anyeṣām api dharmāṇām alābhaḥ pṛthagjanatvam iṣyate buddho 'pi śrāvakapratyekabuddhasaṃtānikair āryadharmair asamanvāgamāt anāryaḥ syāt. kevalālābhagrahaṇāt tv aprasaṃgaḥ. evaśabdas tarhi paṭhitavya iti. āryadharmāṇām alābha eveti. ekapadāny api hy avadhāraṇānīti. kevalapadāny apīty arthaḥ. abbhakṣo vāyubhakṣa iti. abbhakṣa eva vāyubhakṣa eveti nocyate. evaśabdasya cārtho gamyate. tadvad ihāpīti. [Tib. 141b] atha vā apa eva yo bhakṣayati so 'bbhakṣaḥ. yo vāyum eva bhakṣayati sa vāyubhakṣa iti. yathātra luptanirdiṣṭasya evakārasyāvadhāraṇārtho gamyate. tadvad ihāpy alābha eveti. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntitatsahabhuvāṃ ity apara iti vistaraḥ. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntes tatsahabhuvāṃ ca vedanādīnāṃ dharmāṇām alābhaḥ pṛthagjanatvam. asmiṃ pakṣe utpannāyām api duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntau pariśiṣṭānām āryadharmāṇām alābho 'stīty anāryaḥ syād iti yo doṣa uktaḥ. sa na saṃbhavati. yadā tarhi phalaprāptiḥ. tadā duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntitatsahabhuvāṃ vihānir iti phalaprāptāv anāryaḥ syād iti doṣaparihārārtham āha. na ca tattyāgāt. na ca teṣāṃ kṣāṃtisahabhuvāṃ tyāgād anāryatvaprasaṃgaḥ. tadalābhasyātyantaṃ hatatvāt. tasyālābhasyātyantavihīnatvāt. katham. asāv atyantaṃ hatas tatsaṃtāne punar anutpatteḥ. te tarhi trigotrā iti. śrāvakapratyekabuddhabuddhagotrā iti. katameṣām alābhaḥ. sarveṣām iti. śrāvakādigotrāṇām. evaṃ tarhi sa eva doṣa iti. buddho 'pi trigotrālābhād anāryaḥ syād ity arthaḥ. punaḥ sa eva parihāra iti. sa tu yo vinālābheneti pūrvavat prapaṃco yāvat tadyathā abbhakṣo vāyubhakṣa iti. yatnas tarhi vyartha [Tib. 142a] iti. kṣāṃtipariśiṣṭāryadharmālābhasadbhāvād anāryaḥ syād ity asya doṣasya parihārāya kṣāntitatsahabhuvām alābhaḥ pṛthagjanatvam iti yo yatnas sa vyarthaḥ syāt. pūrvapakṣadoṣaparihāra evāyam āsthīyate. anutpannāryadharmā saṃtatir iti. anutpannā āryadharmā asyām ity anutpannāryadharmā saṃtatiḥ pṛthagjanatvaṃ. anutpannāryamārgā skandhasaṃtatir ity arthaḥ. arthād utpannāryadharmā saṃtatir āryatvam ity uktaṃ bhavati āśrayaparāvṛtteḥ.
body.translated_text: even when the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering has arisen, one still has non-attainment of the remaining noble <s>dharma</s>s, one would be a non-noble person. Therefore he says: 'But that which is non-attainment apart from attainment' — that non-attainment which exists apart from [any] attainment is the state of being an ordinary person. 'Otherwise' — thus the elaboration. If non-attainment of other <s>dharma</s>s even when attainment [of some noble <s>dharma</s>s] exists were accepted as the state of being an ordinary person, then even the <s>Buddha</s> would be a non-noble person because of not being endowed with the noble <s>dharma</s>s belonging to the continua of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s. But there is no such consequence because of the qualification 'non-attainment only.' 'Then the particle <s>eva</s> should be read' — [reading] 'the non-attainment only of noble <s>dharma</s>s.' For even single words can serve as restrictive particles. Even isolated words — this is the meaning. '<s>Abbhakṣa</s> (water-eater), <s>vāyubhakṣa</s> (wind-eater)' — [one understands] 'one who eats water only, one who eats wind only,' even though it is not explicitly stated. And the meaning of the <s>eva</s>-particle is understood. Likewise here too. [Tib. 141b] Alternatively, one who eats water only is <s>abbhakṣa</s>; one who eats wind only is <s>vāyubhakṣa</s>. Just as here the meaning of restriction of the dropped <s>eva</s>-particle is understood, likewise here too — 'non-attainment only.' 'The other [view is that it is] the non-attainment of the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering and its co-arising [<s>dharma</s>s]' — thus the elaboration. Non-attainment of the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering and its co-arising <s>dharma</s>s such as feeling and the rest is the state of being an ordinary person. In this position, the fault stated — that even when the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering has arisen, having non-attainment of the remaining noble <s>dharma</s>s, one would be a non-noble person — does not occur. 'But when the fruit is attained, at that time the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering and its co-arising [<s>dharma</s>s] are lost, so at fruit-attainment one would be a non-noble person' — to resolve this fault, he says: 'Not from the abandonment of those.' There is no consequence of being a non-noble person from the abandonment of those [<s>dharma</s>s] co-arising with the insight-tolerance, because their non-attainment has been utterly destroyed — because that non-attainment has been utterly eliminated. How? That [non-attainment] is utterly destroyed because of its never arising again in that continuum. 'Then they are of three lineages (<s>gotra</s>)' — the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-lineage, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-lineage, and <s>Buddha</s>-lineage. 'Non-attainment of which?' 'Of all' — of the [noble <s>dharma</s>s] of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and other lineages. 'Then the same fault [applies]' — the meaning is: even the <s>Buddha</s> would be a non-noble person because of non-attainment of three-lineage [<s>dharma</s>s]. 'Again the same resolution' — 'but that which is non-attainment apart from attainment' — the elaboration is as before, up to '<s>abbhakṣa</s>, <s>vāyubhakṣa</s>.' 'Then the effort is useless' — [Tib. 142a] since non-attainment of noble <s>dharma</s>s other than the insight-tolerance exists, one would be a non-noble person — to resolve this fault, the effort of [defining it as] 'non-attainment of the insight-tolerance and its co-arising [<s>dharma</s>s] is the state of being an ordinary person' would be useless. This resolution of the prior objection's fault is adhered to. 'A continuum in which noble <s>dharma</s>s have not arisen' — a continuum in which noble <s>dharma</s>s have not arisen is called 'having unarisen noble <s>dharma</s>s'; [that state of] the continuum is the state of being an ordinary person — a <s>skandha</s>-continuum in which the noble path has not arisen, this is the meaning. It is implied that a continuum in which noble <s>dharma</s>s have arisen constitutes noble status — because of the transformation of the basis.

body.text: atheyam aprāptir iti. sarvadharmāprāptiś codyate. nāryadharmaprāptir eva. yathā tāvad iti. udāharaṇam etat. tasya lābhāt tad vihīyata iti. tasyāryamārgasya lābhāt tat pṛthagjanatvam alābhalakṣaṇaṃ vihīyate.
body.translated_text: 'Now this non-possession' — non-possession of all <s>dharma</s>s is being objected to, not non-possession of noble <s>dharma</s>s only. 'As for example' — this is an illustration. 'From the attainment of that, that is eliminated' — from the attainment of that noble path, that state of being an ordinary person, characterized as non-attainment, is eliminated.
