body.text: kiṃdhātukaṃ tat pṛthagjanatvaṃ. tridhātukam ity eke. nanu copapattyāśrayavaśenālābho vyavasthāpyate. pṛthagjanatvaṃ cālābhasvabhāvaṃ. tasmād asya kāmāvacarasya sattvasya kāmāvacaram eva pṛthagjanatvam asti. na rūpārūpyāvacaram. atas traidhātukaṃ vihīyata iti ayujyamānam etat paśyāmaḥ. atha punar anutpattidharmatāṃ tad āpannam iti kṛtvā traidhātukaṃ tad vihīyata iti upacārakalpanā. bhavatv eṣā. naiṣā vāryate. kāmāvacarasyaiva tv ekasya pṛthagjanatvasya prāptir asti. tal laukikāgrabharmāvasthāyāṃ vihīyata [Tib. 142b] iti vedayāmaḥ. tac ca kāmavairāgye navame vimuktimārge prahīyate. rūpārūpyadhātvor utpadyamānasya tv āryasya pratibhūmyavasthitānāṃ pṛthagjanatvānāṃ āryamārgaprāptisāmarthyān naiva prāptir utpadyate. pratibhūmi tu navame vimuktimārge teṣāṃ prahāṇaṃ bhavatīti avagaṃtavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: To which realm does that state of being an ordinary person belong? 'To all three realms' — say some. But is not non-attainment determined according to the basis of rebirth? And the state of being an ordinary person has the nature of non-attainment. Therefore, for this being belonging to the desire realm, only the desire-realm state of being an ordinary person exists, not that of the form or formless realms. Hence, we see it as improper [to say] that [ordinary-person-hood] belonging to all three realms is eliminated. But again, if one considers that it has attained the nature of never arising again, then [the claim that] threefold [ordinary-person-hood] is eliminated is a figurative expression. Let that be so; it is not prohibited. But we hold that there is possession of only one [kind of] ordinary-person-hood belonging to the desire realm, and that it is eliminated at the stage of the worldly supreme <s>dharma</s>s (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>). [Tib. 142b] And that is abandoned at the ninth liberation-path in [the process of] dispassion from the desire realm. But for a noble one being born in the form or formless realms, because of the power of possession of the noble path, possession of the ordinary-person-hood established at each ground simply does not arise. But at the ninth liberation-path of each ground, the abandonment of those should be understood.

body.text: bhūmisaṃcārāc ceti. yadā ca kāmadhātor vairāgyaṃ kṛtvā prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ saṃcarati. tadā ca tat kāmāvacaraṃ pṛthagjanatvaṃ vihīyate. na cāryo bhavati. prathamadhyānabhūmikapṛthagjanatvaprādurbhāvāt. evam ārūpyadhātusaṃcārād rūpāvacaraṃ pṛthagjanatvaṃ vihīyate. ūrdhvabhūmeś cādharāṃ bhūmiṃ saṃcarate ūrdhvabhūmikaṃ pṛthagjanatvaṃ vihīyata iti vaktavyam. evam anyeṣām api yojyam iti. yathāryamārgasya prāptyā pṛthagjanatvam aprāptir vihīyata iti yojitaṃ. evam anyeṣām api śrutacintāmayādikānāṃ dharmāṇām aprāptir vihīyata iti yojyaṃ. kathaṃ. kāmāvacarāṇāṃ tāvac chrutacintāmayādikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prāptilābhād aprāptir vihīyate. upapattilābhikānāṃ ca kuśalānāṃ prāptyā samucchinnakuśalasyāprāptir vihīyate. bhūmisaṃcārāc ca. yadā cāyaṃ kāmadhātoś cyutvā prathamaṃ dhyānam upapattyā saṃcarati. tadā ca tadbhūmikānāṃ gatisaṃgṛhītānāṃ skaṃdhānām aprāptir vihīyate. akliṣṭāvyākṛtā eva hi gatayo vakṣyante.
body.translated_text: 'And because of ground-transition' — when, having become dispassionate from the desire realm, one transitions to the first <s>dhyāna</s>, at that time that desire-realm ordinary-person-hood is eliminated. But one does not become noble — because of the emergence of ordinary-person-hood belonging to the ground of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Likewise, through transition to the formless realm, form-realm ordinary-person-hood is eliminated. And when one transitions from a higher ground to a lower ground, the higher-ground ordinary-person-hood is eliminated — this should be stated. 'Likewise for others too, this should be applied' — just as it has been construed that through the possession of the noble path, the state of being an ordinary person, [which is] non-possession, is eliminated, likewise for other <s>dharma</s>s too — those produced through learning, reflection, and the like — non-possession is eliminated, this should be applied. How? For desire-realm <s>dharma</s>s produced through learning, reflection, and the like, non-possession is eliminated through the attainment of possession. And for one who has uprooted wholesome roots, non-possession is eliminated through the possession of wholesome [<s>dharma</s>s] obtained through rebirth. And through ground-transition — when this [being], having died from the desire realm, transitions by rebirth to the first <s>dhyāna</s>, at that time non-possession of the <s>skandha</s>s included in the destiny (<s>gati</s>) of that ground is eliminated. For the destinies will be stated as being exclusively unafflicted-indeterminate.

children.translated_text: 'The possession of the indeterminate [Tib. 143a] is simultaneous' —

body.text: coktam. evaṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikānāṃ prāyogikāṇāṃ guṇānāṃ prāpter aprāptir vihīyate. bhūmisaṃcārāc ca. ūrdhvabhūmikānāṃ gatisaṃgṛhītānāṃ skandhānāṃ tadbhūmisaṃcārād vihīyata iti. idam ekeṣāṃ bhūmi saṃcāravyākhyānodāharaṇaṃ tatra aviviktaṃ paśyāmaḥ. ūrdhvabhūmikānāṃ gatisaṃgṛhītānāṃ skandhānām aprāptir na kevalaṃ bhūmisaṃcārād vibīyate. kiṃ tarhi. tatprāptito 'pīti. idaṃ tv asaṃkīrṇam udāharaṇaṃ paśyāmaḥ. tadyathā dvitīyādidhyānabhūmikānāṃ prāyogikāṇāṃ guṇānāṃ tadalābhinaḥ kāmāvacarasya sattvasyāprāptir asti. sa yadi kāmavairāgyaṃ kṛtvā prathamadhyāna upapadyate
body.translated_text: thus it has been stated. Likewise, through the possession of practical qualities belonging to the ground of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, non-possession is eliminated. And through ground-transition — non-possession of <s>skandha</s>s included in the destiny of higher grounds is eliminated through transition to those grounds. We see that this illustration of ground-transition by some is unclear therein. Non-possession of <s>skandha</s>s included in the destiny of higher grounds is not eliminated merely through ground-transition. What then? Through their possession also. But we see this as an unconfused illustration: for example, a being of the desire realm who has not attained [the qualities of] the second and higher <s>dhyāna</s> grounds has non-possession of the practical qualities of those grounds. If that [being], having become dispassionate from the desire [realm], is reborn in the first <s>dhyāna</s>

body.text: . sā teṣām aprāptir bhūmisaṃcārād vihīyate. prathamadhyānabhūmikā tu teṣām aprāptir udbhavatīti. evam anyeṣām api yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: That non-possession (<s>aprāpti</s>) of those [dharmas] ceases due to the change of ground. But the non-possession belonging to the ground of the first <s>dhyāna</s> arises for them. The same should be applied to the others as well.

body.text: nanu caivam anavasthāprasaṃgaḥ prāptīnām iti. prāpter api prāptiḥ. asyā apy anyā. tasyā apy anyā ity anavasthā. parasparasamanvāgamād iti. prāptiprāptiyogāt prāptyā samanvāgataḥ. prāptiyogāt prāptiprāptyā samanvāgata ity arthaḥ. prāptyutpādād iti vistaraḥ. prāptyutpādāt tena dharmeṇa cittena vā samanvāgato bhavati. prāptiprāptyā ca samanvāgata iti vartate. prāptiprāptyutpatteḥ prāptyaiva samanvāgato bhavatīti. evaṃ prāptir ubhayatra vyāpriyate. prāptiprāptis tv ekatreti ato nānavasthā. kuśalasya kliṣṭasya ceti. anayor agrajapaścātkālajaprāptitvād grahaṇaṃ. avyākṛtasya [Tib. 143b] hi sahajaiva prāptir iti. dvitīye kṣaṇa iti vistaraḥ. dvitīye kṣaṇe tasya dharmasya tatprāpteḥ prāptiprāpteś ca prāptaya iti tisraḥ prāptayaḥ. prāptiyogād dhi taiḥ samanvāgato bhavati. tābhis tisṛbhiḥ prāptibhiḥ samanvāgamārthaṃ punas tisro 'nuprāptaya udbhavantīti ṣaḍ bhavanti prāptayaḥ. prathamadvitīyakṣaṇotpannānāṃ dravyāṇām iti. dharmeṇa sārdhaṃ navānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ nava prāptayaḥ sārdham anuprāptibhir aṣṭādaśa bhavanti. evam uttarottaravṛddhiprasaṃgeneti vistaraḥ. uttarottarasya kṣaṇasya vṛddhiḥ prāptibhiḥ. uttarottare vā kṣaṇe vṛddhiḥ prāptīnāṃ. tasyāḥ prasaṃgaḥ uttarottaravṛddhiprasaṃgaḥ. tena. uttarottaravṛddhiprasaṃgena. etāḥ prāptayo visarpantya iti. diṅmātraṃ darśayiṣyāmaḥ. caturthe kṣaṇe prathamakṣaṇotpannais tribhir dharmaiḥ prāptyanuprāptimadbhir bhavitavyaṃ. dvitīyakṣaṇotpannābhir api ṣaḍbhiḥ prāptyanuprāptibhiḥ punaḥ prāptyanuprāptimatībhir bhavitavyam. evaṃ tṛtīyakṣaṇotpannābhir aṣṭādaśabhiḥ prāptyanuprāptibhiḥ punar api prāptyanuprāptimatībhir bhavitavyam iti prathamadvitīyatṛtīyakṣaṇotpannānāṃ saptaviṃśatiḥ prāptayaḥ sārdham anuprāptibhis tāvatībhir iti catuḥpaṃcāśat prāptayaś caturthe kṣaṇe bhavanti. paṃcame tu kṣaṇe prathamadvitīyatṛtīyakṣaṇotpannāḥ prāptyanuprāptayaḥ punaś catuḥpaṃcāśac caturthakṣaṇotpannaprāptyanuprāptayaś ca dviścatuḥpaṃcāśad bhavanti. trīṇi catuḥpaṃcāśatkāni dvāṣaṣtyuttaraśataṃ prāptīnāṃ jāyate. evam uttarottaravṛddhiprasaṃgo vaktavyaḥ. atītānāgatānām ity atra pratyutpannāgrahaṇam anāvaśyakatvāt. [Tib. 144a] utpattilābhikānāṃ ceti. atra prāyogikāgrahaṇam anāvaśyakatvād eva. sasaṃprayogasahabhuvām iti. savedanādisajātyādīnām. anādyantasaṃsāraparyāpannānām anādāv anante ca saṃsāre saṃgṛhītānāṃ. anantā aprameyā ekasya prāṇinaḥ. kiṃ aṅga bahūnāṃ. kṣaṇe kṣaṇe upajāyaṃte prāptaya iti. anantadravyā eva. anantaprāptidravyā ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'But in that case, there would be an infinite regress of <s>prāpti</s>s' — the <s>prāpti</s> of a <s>prāpti</s>, then another of that, then another of that — [leading to] an infinite regress. 'Because of mutual possession' — by the connection with the <s>prāpti</s> of <s>prāpti</s>, one is possessed (<s>samanvāgata</s>) of the <s>prāpti</s>; by the connection with the <s>prāpti</s>, one is possessed of the <s>prāpti</s> of <s>prāpti</s> — this is the meaning. 'Because of the arising of <s>prāpti</s>' — thus the elaboration. Because of the arising of <s>prāpti</s>, one becomes possessed of that <s>dharma</s> or mind. And it follows that one is possessed of the <s>prāpti</s> of <s>prāpti</s>. Because of the arising of the <s>prāpti</s> of <s>prāpti</s>, one becomes possessed of the <s>prāpti</s> itself. Thus the <s>prāpti</s> functions in both [directions], but the <s>prāpti</s> of <s>prāpti</s> functions only in one — therefore there is no infinite regress. 'Of the wholesome and the afflicted' — these two are mentioned because their <s>prāpti</s> belongs to earlier and later times. For the <s>prāpti</s> of the indeterminate [Tib. 143b] is simultaneous. 'At the second moment' — thus the elaboration. At the second moment, there are three <s>prāpti</s>s: [the <s>prāpti</s>] of that <s>dharma</s>, the <s>prāpti</s> of that <s>prāpti</s>, and the <s>prāpti</s> of the <s>prāpti</s> of the <s>prāpti</s>. For by the connection with <s>prāpti</s>, one becomes possessed of them. For the possession of those three <s>prāpti</s>s, three further <s>anuprāpti</s>s (subsequent possessions) arise — making six <s>prāpti</s>s. 'Of the substances arisen in the first and second moments' — of nine substances together with the <s>dharma</s>, nine <s>prāpti</s>s together with the <s>anuprāpti</s>s make eighteen. 'Thus with the progression of successive increase' — thus the elaboration. The increase at each successive moment [comes] through <s>prāpti</s>s; or the increase of <s>prāpti</s>s at each successive moment. That progression is the successive-increase-progression. We shall show just an indication. At the fourth moment, the three <s>dharma</s>s arisen at the first moment must have [their] <s>prāpti</s>s and <s>anuprāpti</s>s. The six <s>prāpti</s>s and <s>anuprāpti</s>s arisen at the second moment must again have [their] <s>prāpti</s>s and <s>anuprāpti</s>s. Likewise, the eighteen <s>prāpti</s>s and <s>anuprāpti</s>s arisen at the third moment must again have [their] <s>prāpti</s>s and <s>anuprāpti</s>s — so the <s>prāpti</s>s of [substances] arisen in the first, second, and third moments are twenty-seven, together with an equal number of <s>anuprāpti</s>s — making fifty-four <s>prāpti</s>s at the fourth moment. At the fifth moment, the <s>prāpti</s>s and <s>anuprāpti</s>s arisen in the first, second, and third moments [number] again fifty-four, and those of the fourth moment's <s>prāpti</s>s and <s>anuprāpti</s>s become twice fifty-four. Three times fifty-four makes one hundred sixty-two <s>prāpti</s>s that are born. Thus the progressive increase should be stated. 'Of past and future' — the non-mention of the present here is because it is unnecessary. [Tib. 144a] 'Of those obtained at birth' — the non-mention of those obtained through practice here is because it too is unnecessary. 'Together with their associated and coexistent [factors]' — together with feeling and the like, [and] with the same-class and the like. 'Encompassed in beginningless and endless <s>saṃsāra</s>' — included in the beginningless and endless cycle of existence. [They are] infinite and immeasurable for a single being — how much more so for many. 'At every moment <s>prāpti</s>s arise' — there are substances of infinite number, meaning substances of infinite <s>prāpti</s>s

body.text: atyutsavo batāyaṃ prāptīnām iti. parihāsavacanam etat. kevalaṃ na pratighātinyaḥ arūpiṇītvāt yato 'vakāśaṃ labhaṃte prāptayaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'What a grand festival of <s>prāpti</s>s this is!' — this is a humorous remark. 'Only they do not collide, because they are formless' — which is why the <s>prāpti</s>s find room.

children.translated_text: '<s>Sabhāgatā</s> (class homogeneity) is the similarity of beings' —

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. samāno bhāgo bhajanam eṣām iti sabhāgāḥ. tadbhāvaḥ sabhāgatā. samāno vā bhāgo bhajanaṃ sabhāgaḥ. sabhāga eva sabhāgatā. yadyogāt sabhāgo bhavati. tad dravyaṃ. sattvānāṃ sāmyaṃ sāmānyaṃ sādṛśyam ity arthaḥ. sattvagrahaṇam asattvanirāsārthaṃ. sattvānāṃ sattvasaṃkhyātānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ sādṛśyaṃ sabhāgatā. asattvasaṃkhyātānāṃ śāliyavādīnāṃ neṣyate. nikāyasabhāga ity asyāḥ śāstre saṃjñeti. jñānaprasthānādike śāstre nikāyasabhāga iti anayā saṃjñayā ayaṃ cittaviprayukto nirdiśyate. iha tu ślokabandhānuguṇyāt sabhāgateti anayā saṃjñayety abhiprāyaḥ. sā punar abhinnā bhinnā ceti. yā sarvasattvavartinī. sā pratisattvam [Tib. 144b] anyānyāpy abhinnety ucyate sādṛśyāt. na hi sā yathā vaiśeṣikāṇām ekā nityā ceti. bhinnā yā kvacid vartate kvacin na vartate. tata āha. bhinnā punar iti vistaraḥ. dhātavas trayaḥ kāmādayaḥ. gatayaḥ paṃca narakādayaḥ. yonayaś catasro 'ṇḍajādayaḥ. jātayo brāhmaṇādayaḥ. ādiśabdena upāsikābhikṣuṇīnaivaśaikṣanāśaikṣādayaḥ saṃgṛhyante. skaṃdhāyatanadhātuta iti. rūpaskandhasabhāgatā yāvad dharmadhātusabhāgatā. aviśiṣṭam iti. sāmānyarūpaṃ. prajñaptiś ceti. abhidhānaṃ cety arthaḥ. evaṃ skandhādibuddhiprajñaptayo 'pi yojyā iti. yadi skandhasabhāgatādravyam aviśiṣṭaṃ na syād anyonyaviśeṣabhinneṣu skandheṣu skandhaḥ skandha ity abhedena buddhir na syāt prajñaptiś ceti. evaṃ dhātvādibuddhiprajñaptayo 'pi yojyā ity eke paṭhanti. teṣām evaṃ vaktavyaṃ. yadi sabhāgateti vistareṇa yāvad anyonyaviśeṣabhinneṣu dhātuṣu kāmāvacaraḥ kāmāvacara iti abhedena buddhir na syāt prajñaptiś ceti.
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration. 'Those whose share (<s>bhāga</s>) — allotment — is the same' are <s>sabhāga</s> (of the same class); the state of that is <s>sabhāgatā</s>. Or: 'the same share — allotment' is <s>sabhāga</s>; <s>sabhāga</s> itself is <s>sabhāgatā</s>. That on account of which [a being] becomes <s>sabhāga</s> — that is the substance. The similarity — commonality — resemblance of beings: this is the meaning. The word 'being' (<s>sattva</s>) is for the purpose of excluding non-beings. <s>Sabhāgatā</s> is the similarity of beings and of <s>dharma</s>s counted as belonging to beings. It is not accepted for non-being entities such as rice, barley, and the like. '<s>Nikāyasabhāga</s>' is the designation of this [entity] in the treatise — in the <s>Jñānaprasthāna</s> and other treatises, this mind-dissociated [factor] is denoted by the designation <s>nikāyasabhāga</s>. But here, for the sake of conformity with the verse meter, the designation <s>sabhāgatā</s> is used — this is the intent. 'And it is both undifferentiated and differentiated' — that which pertains to all beings, that too, though different for each being, [Tib. 144b] is called 'undifferentiated' because of similarity. For it is not the case that it is one and permanent, as the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>s [hold]. 'Differentiated' [means] that which exists in some [cases] and does not exist in others. Therefore he says: 'But the differentiated...' — thus the elaboration. Three realms: desire and the rest. Five destinies: hell-beings and the rest. Four modes of birth: egg-born and the rest. Classes (<s>jāti</s>): <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the rest. By the word 'and so forth,' female lay followers, nuns, those of no-more-training, non-trainees, and the like are included. 'In terms of aggregates, sense-bases, and elements' — the <s>sabhāgatā</s> of the form-aggregate up to the <s>sabhāgatā</s> of the <s>dharma</s>-element. 'Undifferentiated' — a general form. 'And designation' — means 'appellation.' 'Thus the cognitions and designations of aggregates, etc., should also be applied' — if the substance of aggregate-<s>sabhāgatā</s> were not undifferentiated, then regarding aggregates differentiated by mutual distinctions, the uniform cognition 'aggregate, aggregate' and the designation would not [arise]. Thus the cognitions and designations of elements, etc., should also be applied — some read this. For them it should be stated thus: 'If <s>sabhāgatā</s>...' with the elaboration up to 'regarding elements differentiated by mutual distinctions, the uniform cognition "belonging to the desire realm, belonging to the desire realm" and the designation would not [arise].'

body.text: catuḥkoṭika iti. syāt cyavetopapadyeta na ca sattvasabhāgatāṃ vijahyān na ca pratilabheteti. sattvasabhāgatām iti. sattvānāṃ sabhāgatā sattvasabhāgatā manuṣyatvādilakṣaṇā. sattvagrahaṇaṃ [Tib. 145a] hi dharmaviśeṣaṇārthaṃ. sattvasabhāgatā hy atra catuḥkoṭike vivakṣitā na dharmasabhāgateti. na tu sattvas sattva ity ākārasabhāgatehābhipretā. yadi hi sābhipretā syāt. tṛtīyā koṭir na sidhyeta gatisaṃcāre 'pi tasyāḥ sattvasabhāgatāyās tādavasthyāt. tatraivopapadyamāna iti. tadyathā manuṣyagateś cyutvā manuṣyagatāv evopapadyamānaḥ. manuṣyagateś cyavate maraṇād upapadyate ca tasyām eva pratisaṃdhibandhāt. na cāsau manuṣyasabhāgatāṃ vijahāti na ca pratilabhate tasyā manuṣyasabhāgatāyās tādavasthyāt.
body.translated_text: 'A fourfold distinction' — 'one may die and be reborn but neither abandon nor obtain being-<s>sabhāgatā</s>' — '<s>sattvasabhāgatā</s>' means the <s>sabhāgatā</s> of beings, characterized by humanness and the like. The word 'being' [Tib. 145a] is for the purpose of qualifying the <s>dharma</s>. For <s>sattvasabhāgatā</s> (being-homogeneity) is what is intended here in the fourfold distinction, not <s>dharmasabhāgatā</s> (dharma-homogeneity). Nor is the <s>sabhāgatā</s> of the aspect 'being is a being' intended here. For if that were intended, the third alternative would not be established, since even with a change of destiny, that <s>sattvasabhāgatā</s> would remain the same. 'Being reborn in that very [destiny]' — for example, one dying from the human destiny and being reborn in the human destiny itself. One dies from the human destiny through death and is reborn in that same [destiny] through the binding of a new connection (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>). And one neither abandons nor obtains human-<s>sabhāgatā</s>, because that human-<s>sabhāgatā</s> remains the same

body.text: dvitīyā niyāmam avakrāmann iti. sa sattvasabhāgatāṃ pṛthagjanatvasvabhāvāṃ sabhāgatāṃ vijahāti āryatvasvabhāvāṃ sabhāgatām aparāṃ pratilabhate. tṛtīyā gatisaṃcārād iti. tadyathā manuṣyagateś cyutvā devagātāv upapadyamānaḥ. cyavate tathaiva maraṇād upapadyate ca pratisaṃdhibandhāt. sattvasabhāgatāṃ manuṣyasabhāgatālakṣaṇāṃ vijahāti. pratilabhate ca devasabhāgatālakṣaṇām aparām iti. caturthy etān ākārān sthāpayitveti. pūrvoktakoṭisvabhāvaprakārān varjayitvety arthaḥ. tadyathā jīvan pṛthagjana āryo vā kiṃcid alabhamānaḥ.
body.translated_text: The second [alternative]: 'entering the certainty of the noble path (<s>niyāma</s>)' — one abandons the <s>sattvasabhāgatā</s> whose nature is ordinary-personhood (<s>pṛthagjanatvā</s>) and obtains another <s>sabhāgatā</s> whose nature is noble status (<s>āryatva</s>). The third: 'due to change of destiny' — for example, one dying from the human destiny and being reborn in the divine destiny. One dies likewise through death and is reborn through the binding of a new connection. One abandons the <s>sattvasabhāgatā</s> characterized as human-<s>sabhāgatā</s> and obtains another characterized as divine-<s>sabhāgatā</s>. The fourth: 'setting aside these aspects' — meaning: excluding the types described in the previous alternatives. For example, a living being — whether an ordinary person or a noble one — who is not obtaining anything [new].

body.text: yadi pṛthagjanasabhāgatā nāma dravyam asti kiṃ punaḥ pṛthagjanatvena āryadharmalābhasvabhāvena kalpitena prayojanam iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. pṛthagjanasabhāgatayaiva pṛthagjana iti paricchidyeta yathā [Tib. 145b] manuṣyasabhāgatayaiva manuṣya iti. na hi manuṣysabhāgatāyā anyan manuṣyatvaṃ kalpyate vaibhāṣikair alābhavad anyasvabhāvaṃ. tatra ca sādhanaṃ. na svasabhāgatāyā anyat pṛthagjanatvaṃ. svasabhāgatāpratyayābhidheyatvāt. manuṣyatvavat. naiva ca lokaḥ sabhāgatāṃ paśyati arūpiṇītvād iti. na lokaś cakṣuṣā sabhāgatāṃ paśyaty arūpiṇītvād arūpavatītvād arūpasvabhāvatvād vā. yathā na paśyati evaṃ na śṛṇoti yāvan na spṛśatīti. anena pratyakṣāsiddhatāṃ darśayati. na caināṃ prajñayā paricchinattīti. anenānumānenāpi na sidhyatīti darśayati. pratipadyate ca sattvānāṃ jātyabhedam iti. satyā api tasyāḥ kathaṃ tatra vyāpāra iti. jātyabhedapratipattau jātyabhedapratipattir asti. sā tu na sabhāgatayā dravyāntarakalpitayā kṛtā pramāṇenānupalabhyamānatvena tasyā vyāpārasaṃbhavāt. brūyās tvaṃ. na nirnimittā sāmānyabuddhir bhavitum arhati. tena yan nimittaṃ tasyāḥ sāmānyabuddheḥ. tat sabhāgatā nāma dravyam iti. vayam api tāṃ sāmānyabuddhiṃ sanimittāṃm brūmaḥ. sādṛśyakṛtā hi sā buddhiḥ. tac ca sādṛśyaṃ na dravyāntaram iti brūmaḥ. tenocyate. api cāsattvasabhāgatāpi kiṃ neṣyata iti vistaraḥ. na dravyāntarasabhāgatānimittā sattvaḥ sattva iti sāmānyabuddhiḥ. sāmānyākārapravṛttatvāt. śāliyavamudgamāṣādisāmānyabuddhivat. śāliyavasvajātisādṛśyakṛtā [Tib. 146a] hy eṣā sāmānyabuddhiḥ. na ca teṣāṃ svajātisādṛśyaṃ svato 'rthāntaraṃ bhavati. tāsāṃ ca sabhāgatānām iti vistaraḥ. anyā sattvasabhāgatānyā dhātusabhāgatānyā gatisabhāgateti anyonyabhinnāḥ sabhāgatā iṣyante. tāsāṃ sabhāgateti prajñaptir iyaṃ sabhāgatā iyaṃ sabhāgatety abhedena kathaṃ bhavadbhiḥ kriyate. vyavahāraḥ pratyayaś ca kathaṃ jāyate. yady atrāpi sabhāgatāntaraṃ pratijñāyeta yena sabhāgatāsāmānyabuddhir bhavet. bhavet so 'yam apakṣaḥ prākpakṣavirodhāt.
body.translated_text: 'If there is indeed a substance called ordinary-person-<s>sabhāgatā</s>, then what further purpose is served by ordinary-personhood (<s>pṛthagjanatvā</s>), which is conceived as having the nature of non-attainment of noble <s>dharma</s>s?' — this completes the sentence. One would be delimited as an ordinary person by the ordinary-person-<s>sabhāgatā</s> alone, just as [Tib. 145b] one is [delimited as] human by human-<s>sabhāgatā</s> alone. For the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s do not postulate a separate 'humanness' distinct from human-<s>sabhāgatā</s>, since there is no attainment of a different own-nature. And therein the proof: 'ordinary-personhood is not other than one's own <s>sabhāgatā</s>, because it is expressible as having one's own <s>sabhāgatā</s> as its referent — like humanness.' 'Nor does the world perceive <s>sabhāgatā</s>, because it is formless' — the world does not see <s>sabhāgatā</s> with the eye, because it is formless — devoid of form — having a formless own-nature. Just as one does not see it, so one does not hear it, and so on up to: one does not touch it. By this he shows [its] non-establishment by direct perception. 'Nor does one delimit it by wisdom' — by this he shows that it is not established even by inference. 'Yet one does understand the non-difference of class among beings' — even granting its reality, how would it function there? In the understanding of class non-difference, there is [indeed] understanding of class non-difference, but that is not produced by <s>sabhāgatā</s> conceived as a separate substance, because through the impossibility of its functioning due to being unperceivable by any valid means of knowledge. You might say: 'a generic cognition cannot be without a cause; therefore, whatever is the cause of that generic cognition — that is the substance called <s>sabhāgatā</s>.' We too say that generic cognition has a cause. For that cognition is produced by similarity. And we say that similarity is not a separate substance. Therefore it is said: 'moreover, why is a non-being-<s>sabhāgatā</s> also not accepted?' — thus the elaboration. The generic cognition 'being is a being' is not caused by a <s>sabhāgatā</s> that is a separate substance, because [that cognition] operates through a generic aspect — like the generic cognition of rice, barley, mung beans, black beans, and the like. For this generic cognition [Tib. 146a] is produced by the similarity within each respective class of rice, barley, and the like. And for those, the similarity within their own class is not something distinct from themselves. 'And of those <s>sabhāgatā</s>s' — thus the elaboration. Different <s>sabhāgatā</s>s are accepted: being-<s>sabhāgatā</s>, realm-<s>sabhāgatā</s>, destiny-<s>sabhāgatā</s>, and so on — each distinct from the others. The designation 'this is a <s>sabhāgatā</s>, this is a <s>sabhāgatā</s>' applied uniformly to those — how is it made by you? How does the usage and cognition arise? If here too another <s>sabhāgatā</s> were postulated, by which there would be a generic cognition of <s>sabhāgatā</s> — this would be a flawed position, because it contradicts one's own earlier position

body.text: vaiśeṣikāś caivaṃ dyotitā iti. jvalitāḥ samarthitā ity abhiprāyaḥ. te 'pi hi sāmānyapadārthavādino bhavanto 'pīti. ayaṃ tu teṣāṃ vaiśeṣikāṇāṃ viśeṣaḥ. eko 'py anekasmiṃ vartate sraksūtravat. bhūtakaṇṭheguṇavac ceti. yadi dyotitāḥ sāmānyapadārthavāditvāt. yadi na dyotitā ekānekanityānityatvādiviśeṣavāditvāt. na hi paralokāstitvādīni vaiśeṣikaiḥ kalpitānīti na vyavasthāpyante. saced itthaṃtvam āgacchatīti. prāṇātipātenāsevitena bhāvitena bahulīkṛtena narakeṣūpapdyate. saced itthaṃtvaṃ āgacchati manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāṃ prāpnoti prāṇātipātenālpāyur bhavatīti vistaraḥ. idaṃprakāra itthaṃ. tadbhāvaḥ itthaṃtvam iti. [Tib. 146b] śarīrendriyasaṃsthānaceṣṭāhārādisābhāgyakāraṇaṃ anyonyābhir abhisaṃbaṃdhanimittaṃ ca sabhāgateti ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ. tad etad etenaiva pratyuktaṃ. vayam api hy evam icchāmaḥ. na tu sā sabhāgatā dravyāṃtaraṃ. ta eva hi saṃskārās tathākāraṇabhāvaṃ pratipadyaṃte iti.
body.translated_text: and the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> too are thus illuminated — the intent is: they are established, supported. For they too —

body.text: (II.42bcd)

children.translated_text: 'The <s>āsaṃjñika</s> (state of non-perception) — among the non-perceptive [beings] — is the cessation of mind and mental factors' —

body.translated_text: (II.42bcd)

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. asaṃjñinām idam āsaṃjñikaṃ. asaṃjñiṣu vā bhavaṃ āsaṃjñikaṃ. nirudhyaṃte 'nena cittacaittāḥ. cittacaittān vā niruṇaddhīti nirodhaḥ. yenānāgate 'dhvany avasthitāś cittacaittāḥ kālāṃtaraṃ tāvatkālaṃ saṃnirudhyaṃte. notpattuṃ labhaṃte ity arthaḥ. tad āsaṃjñikaṃ nāma dravyaṃ. nadītoyasaṃnirodhavat. setuvad ity arthaḥ. dhyānāṃtarikāvad iti. yathā brahmapurohitā nāma te devā yeṣāṃ kecin mahābrahmāṇaḥ pradeśe bhavaṃti dhyānāṃtarikāyāṃ. tathā bṛhatphalā nāma te devā yeṣām asaṃjñisattvāḥ pradeśe bhavaṃti. na bhūmyaṃtare bhavaṃti. upapattikāle cyutikāle ca saṃjñina iti saṃbaṃdhanīyaṃ. kliṣṭena manasā pratisaṃdhibaṃdhāt.
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration. 'Of the non-perceptive beings, this is the <s>āsaṃjñika</s>.' Or, 'occurring among the non-perceptive — [that is] the <s>āsaṃjñika</s>.' The cessation —

body.text: iti ca niyamāt. pūrvasamāpattisaṃskāraparikṣayād iti. pūrvasamāpattisaṃskāralakṣaṇasya vipākahetoḥ parikṣayāt. tataḥ samāptaphalatvād ity arthaḥ. [Tib. 147a] pūrvasamāpattisaṃskārāvedhaparikṣayād ity apare vyācakṣate. apūrvānupacayāc ceti. cittābhāvāt karmānupacayād ity abhiprāyaḥ. kṣiptā iva kṣīṇavegā iṣavaḥ pṛthivīm iti. upapadyaṃte iti prakṛtaṃ. pūrvam ayaṃ padir janyarthaḥ. idānīm arthavaśād gatyarthaḥ. saṃpadyaṃte gacchaṃtīty arthaḥ. pṛthivīṃ gacchaṃtīti vākyaśeṣa ity spare.
body.translated_text: and from this restriction. 'Because of the exhaustion of the formations of the prior attainment' — [this means] the characteristic of the formations of the prior attainment —

body.text: (II.43) asaṃjñināṃ sattvānāṃ samāpattir asaṃjñā vā samāpattir iti asaṃjñisamāpattiḥ. etāvat tathāśabdenānvākṛṣyata iti. vipāka ity evamāder arthaviśeṣasyānabhiprīteḥ. avyākṛtam eva hi āsaṃjñikaṃ. kuśalaiva ceyaṃ samāpattir
body.translated_text: (II.43) 'The attainment of non-perceptive beings' — or 'the attainment that is non-perception' — [thus] the <s>asaṃjñi-samāpatti</s> —

body.text: iti vakṣyate.
body.translated_text: thus it will be stated.

body.text: paṃcaskaṃdhako vipāka iti. cyutyupapattikāle cittacaittāṇāṃ vipākatvasadbhāvāt.
body.translated_text: 'The retribution is a five-aggregate [collection]' — because at the time of death and rebirth, the retributive nature of mind and mental factors exists.

body.text: tata eva tallābhīti. yata eva parihīṇo 'pi punar utpādyāsaṃjñisattveṣūpapadyate tata eva tallābhī niyāmaṃ nāvakrāmati. niyāmāvakrāṃtyaiva hy āryo 'pāyagatyāsaṃjñikamahābrahmakauravopapattyaṣṭamabhavādīnām apratisaṃkhyānirodhaṃ pratilabhate. vinipātasthānam ivaināṃ paśyaṃtīti. apāyasthānam ivaināṃ paśyaṃtīty arthaḥ. giritaṭādivinipātasthānam ivety apare. niḥsaraṇasaṃjñino hi tāṃ samāpadyaṃte. pṛthagjanā mokṣasaṃjñina ity [Tib. 147b] arthaḥ. na caivam āryā viparītasaṃjñinaḥ pratilabhaṃte. dhyānavad iti. caturthadhyānalābhād atītānāgatam anādimati saṃsāre labdhapūrvaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ pratilabhaṃte yoginaḥ. tasmāt kiṃ tadvad eva atītānāgatāṃ tāṃ pratilabhaṃta iti pṛcchati. anye 'pi tāvan na pratilabhaṃta iti. pṛthagjanā api tāvan nātītānāgatāṃ pratilabhaṃte yeṣāṃ tāvad iyaṃ ātmīyā samāpattiḥ. kiṃ punar āryā yeṣām iyam anātmīyeti. ucitāpi satīti. anādimati saṃsāre labdhapūrvāpi mahābhisaṃskārasādhyatvān mahāyatnābhiniṣpādyatvād ity arthaḥ. acittakatvāc ca.
body.translated_text: 'From that very [attainment], one obtains that [rebirth]' — since even one who has declined, by generating [the attainment] again, is reborn among the non-perceptive beings —

children.translated_text: '[<s>Prāpti</s>] of a single time-period is obtained' —

body.text: samānādhvikā labhyata ity arthaḥ. yathā prātimokṣasaṃvara iti. prātimokṣasaṃvaro 'ṣṭavidho 'pi yadā samādīyate. tadā sa prāpyate. prāptiś ca tasya tasminn eva kṣaṇe utpadyate. labdhayā tu tayā samāpattyā dvitīyādiṣu kṣaṇeṣu prātimokṣasaṃvaravad eva samanvāgato bhavati. yāvan na tyajati tāṃ samāpattiṃ. tattyāgas tu parihāṇyā bhūmisaṃcārād vā. acaittikatvān nānāgatā bhāvyate. kuśalaṃ hi cittam anāgataṃ bhāvyate. na tv iyaṃ acittaketi na tadvad anāgatā bhāvyate.
body.translated_text: the meaning is: [<s>prāpti</s>] of the same time-period is obtained. 'Just as the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint' — the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint —

body.text: samāpattir iti vartate. evaśabdo 'vadhāraṇe. yathāsaṃjñisamāpattinirdeśe athāśabdena nirodhaś cittacaittānām iti atidiśyate. tathaivehāpi [Tib. 148a] nirodhasamāpattinirdeśe sa evaṃprakāro 'tidiśyate iti. śāṃtavihārasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇa manasikāreṇeti. vihāraḥ kṛīdāvihāra iva vihāraḥ. samādhiviśeṣaḥ. śāṃto vihāraḥ śāṃtavihāraḥ. śāṃtavihāre saṃjñā śāṃtavihārasaṃjñā. sā pūrvā asyeti śāṃtavihārasaṃjñāpūrvakaḥ manasikāro manaskāra iti yo 'rthaḥ aluksamāsāt sa manasikāra iti bhavati. saṃjñāveditasamudācārapariśrāṃtā hi tatra śāṃtavihārasaṃjñinas tathāvidhena manasikāreṇa enāṃ nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpadyaṃte. tāṃ tv asaṃjñisamāpattiṃ niḥsaraṇasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇa mokṣasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇety
body.translated_text: 'Attainment' is to be supplied. The word 'likewise' (<s>eva</s>) is for restriction. Just as in the exposition of the non-perception attainment, the word 'now' —

body.text: arthaḥ. aparaparyāyavedanīyā ceti. aparaparyāyas tṛtīyādijanma. tatra vedanīyā. kathaṃ. ya āryaḥ kāmadhātau nirodhasamāpattim utpādya bhavāgra utpadyeta. tasya sā paripūrikopapadyavedanīyā. yas tu tataḥ parihīṇo rūpadhātāv upapadya kālāṃtareṇa ca punar api bhavāgraṃ labdhvā nirodhasamāpattim utpādyānutpādya vā bhavāgra upapadyate. tasya sāparaparyāyavedanīyā bhavati. yas tv iha parinirvāyāt. tasyāniyateti.
body.translated_text: — this is the meaning. 'And [there is <s>karma</s>] ripening in subsequent lives' — 'subsequent lives' means the third and later births. [<s>Karma</s>] ripening in those —

body.text: ucchedabhīrutvād iti. sarvātmabhāvocchedabhīrutvāt. vyathaṃte hy apunarbhavāt prapātād iva bāliśāḥ. asaṃjñisamāpattau kasmād ucchedabhayaṃ na bhavati. [Tib. 148b] tatra rūpasadbhāvāt. rūpe hy ātmasaṃjñām abhiniveśya tāṃ samāpadyaṃte. nirodhasamāpattau tu ārūpyabhūmikatvād rūpam api nāstīti sarvātmabhāvabhāvaṃ paśyaṃto na tāṃ samāpattum utsahaṃte. nanu cārūpyeṣu nikāyasabhāgajīvitendriyādayaś cittaviprayuktā santi. kasmāt tatrātmasaṃjñām abhiniveśya tāṃ na samāpadyaṃte. viprayuktānām adṛśyatvāt. āryamārgabalena cotpādanāt. kathaṃ punar gamyate āryamārgabalena tad utpādanam iti ata āha. dṛṣṭadharmanirvāṇasya tadadhimuktita iti. dṛṣṭe janmani nirvāṇaṃ dṛṣṭadharmanirvāṇaṃ. tasya. tadadhimuktitaḥ. tad iti adhimuktiḥ tadadhimuktiḥ. tena vādhimuktis tadadhimuktiḥ. tadadhimuktes tadadhimuktitaḥ. dṛṣṭe janmani etan nirvāṇam iti āryas tām adhimucyate. kecit punar evaṃ paṭhaṃti. dṛṣṭanirvāṇasya tadadhimuktita iti. evaṃ ca vyācakṣate. dṛṣṭaṃ nirvāṇam aneneti dṛṣṭanirvāṇaḥ. tasyāryasya tasyām adhimuktis tadadhimuktiḥ. tadadhimuktes tadadhimuktitaḥ. etad uktaṃ bhavati. dṛṣṭanirvāṇa āryas tām adhimucyate nānya iti. nanu ca pṛthagjano 'pi laukikena mārgeṇa dṛṣṭanirvāṇaḥ. na pṛthagjano dṛṣṭanirvāṇaḥ. prāptanirvāṇas tu bhavet. taduttarāṃ hi bhūmiṃ pṛthagjanaḥ śāṃtataḥ paśyan vairāgyaṃ labhate na nirvāṇam iti acodyam etat. prayogalabhyaiveyam iti. [Tib. 149a] iyam api samāpattir asaṃjñisamāpattivad eva mahābhisaṃskārasādhyeti. tathaiva
body.translated_text: 'Because of fear of annihilation' — because of fear of the annihilation of all forms of existence. For they are distressed by the [prospect of] non-return to existence —

children.translated_text: '[<s>Prāpti</s>] of a single time-period is obtained' —

body.text: katham ity āha. na cātītā labhyata iti. yadā parihīṇaḥ punas tām utpādayati. tadā prayogeṇāpūrvaiva labhyate. prātimokṣasaṃvaravad iti vistareṇa vyākhyeyā. cittabalena tadbhāvanād iti. cittabalenānāgatabhāvanād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: how? He says: 'And [<s>prāpti</s>] of the past is not obtained.' When one who has declined generates it [the attainment] again, at that time —

children.translated_text: 'Obtained through the enlightenment of the sage' —

body.text: iti. prayogalabhyaiveyam ity utsargasyāyam apavādaḥ. śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ sa vidhir iti kṛtvā.
body.translated_text: thus. 'This is obtained only through effort' — this is an exception to the general rule. For <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, that —

children.translated_text: 'Enlightenment is the knowledge of destruction and the knowledge of non-arising' —

body.text: iti vakṣyati. tenāha. kṣayajñānasamakālam iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: thus it will be stated. Therefore he says: 'simultaneous with the knowledge of destruction' — thus the elaboration.

children.translated_text: 'And the defiled — at the time of the knowledge of destruction' —

body.text: iti buddhā bhagavaṃta etāṃ pratilabhaṃte. nāsti buddhānāṃ kiṃcit prāyogikaṃ nāmeti. yothoktaṃ stotrakāreṇa
body.translated_text: thus, the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, obtain this. There is nothing 'produced by effort' for <s>Buddhas</s>, namely —

children.text:
na te prāyogikaṃ kiṃcit kuśalaṃ kuśalāntaga
icchāmātrāvabaddhā te yatrakāmāvasāyiteti.
children.translated_text: 'They have no preparatory wholesome [<s>dharmas</s>], being those who have reached the end of the wholesome; they are bound only by wish, dwelling wherever they please' —

body.text: kathaṃ punar bhagavān ubhayatobhāgavimukta iti. kleśāvaraṇaṃ samāpattyāvaraṇaṃ cobhayatobhāgaḥ. tato vimuktaḥ. sidhyaty utpāditāyām iveti. sidhyati ubhayatobhāgavimukto bhagavāṃ saṃmukhīkṛtapūrvāyām iva. tasyāṃ vaśitvalābhāt. tatsaṃmukhīkāraṇakāraṇasāmarthyayogataḥ. prāg eva tām iti vistaraḥ. dharmataiṣā yad bodhisattvaś caramabhaviko bhavāgralābhī bhūtvā caturthadhyānasaṃniśrayeṇa darśanamārgam [Tib. 149b] utpādya tataś ca vyutthāya bhavāgraṃ samāpadyate. tato nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpadyate. tato vyutthāya punaś caturthadhyānasaṃniśrayeṇa bhāvāgrikabhāvanāprahātavyakleśaprahāṇaṃ kṛtvā kṣayajñānakālāt prabhṛti anuttarasamyaksaṃbuddho bhavatīty evaṃ śaikṣāvasthāyāṃ sa tām utpādayatīti pāścātyāḥ kaśmīramaṇḍalāt paścād bhavāḥ pāścātyāḥ. netrīpadam iti śāstranāma sthaviropaguptasya. yatredaṃ vākyaṃ. nirodhasamāpattim utpādya kṣayajñānam utpādayatīti vaktavayṃ tathāgata iti. satyābhisamaye ṣoḍaśabhir iti. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāṃtim ārabhya yāvan mārge 'nvayajñanam iti ṣoḍaśabhiś cittakṣaṇaiḥ. bhavāgravairāgye cāṣṭādasabhir iti. navaprakārāṇāṃ kleśānāṃ bhāvāgrikāṇāṃ bhāvanāheyānāṃ prahāṇāya navānaṃtaryamārgā nava ca vimuktimārgā ity aṣṭādaśabhiḥ. ta ete catustriṃśad bhavaṃti ṣoḍaśa caṣṭādaśa ceti. adhobhūmikā na punaḥ praheyā bhavaṃtīti. kāmāvacarādīnāṃ kleśānāṃ laukikena mārgeṇa pṛthagjanatvāvasthāyām eva prahīṇatvāt. yady eṣa niyamaḥ prahīṇakleśapratipakṣotpādanaṃ na kartavyam iti. atha kimarthaṃ prahīṇeṣu kāmāvacareṣu kleśeṣu tatpratipakṣaṃ dharmajñānapakṣam mārgam abhisamayakāla utpādayati. tannāṃtarīyakatvād anvayajñānapakṣasya mārgasya. [Tib. 150a] na hy asatyāṃ dharmajñānapakṣotpattāv anvayajñānapakṣasaṃmukhībhāvaḥ saṃbhavati. etad dhy anvayajñānasyānvayajñānatvaṃ yad ataḥ paścād bhavatīti. pāścātyā āhuḥ. kiṃ punaḥ syād iti vistaraḥ. ko doṣaḥ syād yadi visabhāgaṃ sāsravaṃ cittam aṃtarā saṃmukhīkuryāt
body.translated_text: But how is the Blessed One 'liberated from both sides' (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>)? The obstruction of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and the obstruction of attainments (<s>samāpattyāvaraṇa</s>) — [these] two [constitute] 'both sides' (<s>ubhayatobhāga</s>). [He is] liberated from those. 'It is established as if [the attainment] had been produced' — the Blessed One is established as <s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s> as if [the cessation attainment] had been directly confronted previously — because of having obtained mastery over it, by the power of the cause capable of producing that confrontation. 'Even before that [attainment]' — and so forth in detail. This is the natural order (<s>dharmatā</s>): the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his last existence, having obtained [rebirth at] the peak of existence (<s>Bhavāgra</s>), [Tib. 149b] produces the path of insight (<s>darśanamārga</s>) based on the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, then rising from that, enters the [absorption at] the peak of existence (<s>Bhavāgra</s>), then enters the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>), then rising from that, again based on the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, having accomplished the abandonment of afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation belonging to the peak of existence, from the time of the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) onward, he becomes a perfectly and fully awakened one (<s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbuddha</s>). Thus, he produces that [cessation attainment] at the stage of training (<s>śaikṣa</s>) — [so say] the Westerners (<s>pāścātyāḥ</s>): those who are to the west of the <s>Kaśmīra</s> region are the 'Westerners.' '<s>Netrīpada</s>' is the name of a treatise by the elder <s>Upagupta</s>. Therein is this statement: 'Having produced the cessation attainment, he produces the knowledge of destruction' — this is what should be said of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. 'In the realization of the truths (<s>satyābhisamaya</s>), by sixteen [moments]' — beginning with the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering, up to the subsequent knowledge of the path — by sixteen mind-moments. 'And in the dispassion from the peak of existence, by eighteen [moments]' — for the abandonment of nine types of afflictions belonging to the peak of existence that are to be abandoned by cultivation, nine uninterrupted paths and nine liberation paths — [making] eighteen. Those total thirty-four — sixteen plus eighteen. 'The afflictions of the lower levels need not be further abandoned' — because the afflictions of the desire-realm and the rest have already been abandoned by the mundane path at the stage of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). If this is a fixed rule — that the generation of an antidote to already-abandoned afflictions need not be done — then for what purpose, when the desire-realm afflictions have been abandoned, does [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] at the time of realization generate the path belonging to the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge category, which is the antidote to those? Because the path belonging to the subsequent knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>) category necessarily follows from that. [Tib. 150a] For without the arising of the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge category, the confrontation of the subsequent knowledge category path is not possible. For this is precisely what makes the subsequent knowledge 'subsequent' — that it comes after that [<s>dharma</s>-knowledge]. The Westerners say: 'But what would [happen]?' — and so forth in detail. What fault would there be if [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] were to interpose a dissimilar, outflow-possessing mind-moment in between?

body.text: . vaibhāṣikā āhuḥ. vyutthānāśayaḥ syād iti vistaraḥ. vyutthānabhiprāyaḥ bodhisattvaḥ syāt. vyutthānakuśalaḥ syād ity apare. kuśalamūlārtho hy āśayārthaḥ. tad etad uktaṃ bhavati. īdṛśāni kuśalamūlāni bodhisattvānāṃ yaiḥ saṃmukhībhūtais tāvan na vyuttiṣṭhaṃte yāvad ekāsana evānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ prāpteti. bahirdeśakā āhuh. satyam avyutthānāśayo na tu yathā bhavaṃto varṇayaṃtīti. pūrvam eva tu varṇayaṃti. kṣayajñānasamakālam iti yaḥ pakṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> say: '[The <s>Bodhisattva</s>] would have the intention to rise [from absorption]' — and so forth in detail. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> would have the intention to rise [from absorption]; others say: he would be skilled in rising [from absorption]. For the meaning of '<s>āśaya</s>' (intention) is the meaning of 'wholesome roots' (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). What has been said is this: Such are the wholesome roots of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> that, with those present, they do not rise [from absorption] until, on a single seat, unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) is attained. The outsiders (<s>bahirdeśakāḥ</s>) say: 'True, [the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has] the intention of non-rising, but not in the manner you describe.' But the earlier ones describe [it thus]: that position holds [that the cessation attainment occurs] simultaneously with the knowledge of destruction.

body.text: (II.45cd) yady apy anayor bahuprakāro viśeṣa iti. ekā
body.translated_text: (II.45cd) 'Although there are many kinds of differences between these two' — thus. One [is]

body.text: aparā
body.translated_text: The other [is]

children.translated_text: born at the peak of existence (<s>Bhavāgra</s>).

body.text: ekāṃ niḥsaraṇasaṃjñayā samāpadyate 'parāṃ vihārakāmatayety evamādibahuprakāraviśeṣaḥ. sāmyaṃ tv anayoḥ.
body.translated_text: One enters one [of them] with the perception of escape (<s>niḥsaraṇasaṃjñā</s>), and the other with the desire for [pleasant] abiding — and so forth: such are the many kinds of differences. But their similarity [is as follows]:

children.translated_text: 'Existing in the substrate of the desire and form [realms]' —

body.text: iti. syād rūpabhava iti vistaraḥ. yaḥ kvacid rūpabhavaḥ sarvo 'sau bhavaḥ paṃcavyavacāra iti catuḥkoṭikaḥ. syād rūpabhavo na cāsau bhavaḥ paṃcavyavacāraḥ. [Tib. 150b] rūpāvacarāṇāṃ saṃjñināṃ devānāṃ visabhāge citte sthitānām asaṃjñisamāpattiṃ nirodhasamāpattiṃ ca samāpannānām asaṃjñināṃ ca devānām āsaṃjñike pratilabdhe yo bhavaḥ. syād bhavaḥ paṃcavyavacāro na cāsau rūpabhavaḥ. kāmāvacarāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sabhāge citte sthitānāṃ yo bhavaḥ. syād rūpabhavaḥ sa ca bhavaḥ paṃcavyavacāraḥ. rūpāvacarāṇāṃ saṃjñināṃ devānāṃ sabhāge citte sthitānāṃ asaṃjñināṃ ca devānām āsaṃjñike 'pratilabdhe yo bhavaḥ. syān naiva rūpabhavo na cāsau bhavaḥ paṃcavyavacāraḥ. kāmāvacarāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ visabhāge citte sthitānām asaṃjñisamāpattiṃ nirodhasamāpattiṃ ca samāpannānāṃ yo bhavaḥ. ārūpyabhavaś ca. tatra prathamā koṭir udāharaṇaṃ. rūpabhavo rūpāvacaraṃ skaṃdhapaṃcakaṃ. paṃcavyavacāraḥ paṃcaskaṃdhaka ity arthaḥ. vyavacāra iti kāśyapasya tathāgatasya skaṃdhasaṃjñā. viśeṣeṇāvacāro vyavacāraḥ. anyathībhāvena visaṃvādanam ity arthaḥ. so 'syāstīti vyavacāraḥ. arśaādibhyo 'j ity akāro matvarthīyaḥ. visaṃvādanīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. 'There may be form-realm existence' — and so forth in detail. Whichever form-realm existence there is — the question whether all such [existence] is existence involving five [aggregates] (<s>pañcavyavacāra</s>) is a fourfold <s>koṭi</s> (tetralemma). [1] It may be form-realm existence but not existence involving five [aggregates] — [Tib. 150b] in the case of sentient beings of the form-realm who are abiding in a dissimilar mind-moment, and who have entered the attainment of non-perception (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>) or the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>), and of non-perceptive gods (<s>asaṃjñika</s>) whose existence in the <s>Āsaṃjñika</s> [heaven] has been obtained — that is the existence [in question]. [2] It may be existence involving five [aggregates] but not form-realm existence — in the case of beings of the desire-realm who are abiding in a homogeneous (<s>sabhāga</s>) mind-moment — that is the existence [in question]. [3] It may be both form-realm existence and existence involving five [aggregates] — in the case of sentient beings of the form-realm who are abiding in a homogeneous mind-moment, and of non-perceptive gods whose existence in the <s>Āsaṃjñika</s> [heaven] has not been obtained — that is the existence [in question]. [4] It may be neither form-realm existence nor existence involving five [aggregates] — in the case of beings of the desire-realm who are abiding in a dissimilar mind-moment and who have entered the attainment of non-perception or the cessation attainment — that is the existence [in question]. And also formless-realm existence. Therein, the first alternative is the illustration. 'Form-realm existence' is the aggregate-pentad belonging to the form-realm. '<s>Pañcavyavacāra</s>' means 'involving five aggregates.' '<s>Vyavacāra</s>' is [the term for] 'aggregate' in the vocabulary of <s>Kāśyapa Tathāgata</s>. '<s>Vyavacāra</s>' [etymologically] means 'a particular kind of wandering' — meaning 'deception through becoming otherwise.' 'That which has that [deceptive quality]' is '<s>vyavacāra</s>' — the suffix <s>ac</s> from the '<s>arśa</s>' class has the possessive sense. The meaning is: 'deceptive.'

children.translated_text: 'Form is like a lump of foam; feeling is like a bubble' —

body.text: ādinā visaṃvādanāt. tatra yadi rūpadhātāv asaṃjñisamāpattir neṣyate asaṃjñisamāpattiṃ nirodhasamāpattiṃ [Tib. 151a] samāpannānām iti nocyeta. tena rūpāvacary asaṃjñisamāpattir iti gamyate. tatra api tv ayaṃ viśeṣa iti. tatra sādharmye 'pi viśeṣo bhavati. paścād rūpadhātāv iti. ya āryā nirodhasamāpattim utpādya tataḥ parihīṇā dhyānaṃ ca labdhvā rūpadhātāv upapadyaṃte. taiḥ parihīṇapūrvaiḥ. pūrvābhyāsavaśād rūpadhātau nirodhasamāpattir utpādyeta. asaṃjñisamāpattis tu kāmarūpadhātau prathamato 'pi pṛthagjanair utpādyata ity ayaṃ viśeṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: and so forth — because of [the aggregates'] deceptive nature. Therein, if the attainment of non-perception is not accepted [as existing] in the form-realm, one would not say 'those who have entered the attainment of non-perception and the cessation attainment.' [Tib. 151a] From this, it is understood that the attainment of non-perception belongs to the form-realm. 'But therein there is this distinction' — therein, even though there is similarity, there is a distinction. 'Later, in the form-realm' — those Noble Ones who, having produced the cessation attainment and then having declined from it and having obtained <s>dhyāna</s>, are reborn in the form-realm. By those who have previously declined — through the force of prior practice, the cessation attainment would be produced in the form-realm. But the attainment of non-perception is produced in the desire and form realms even for the first time by ordinary persons — this is the distinction.

body.text: kim apy asti parihāṇir iti. nirvāṇasadṛsīyam samāpattiḥ. katham ataḥ parihāṇir ity asaṃbhāvayan pṛcchati. udāyisūtram iti. āryaśāriputrabhāṣitam etat sūtraṃ. udāyī tu tatra vibaṃdhaka ity udāyisūtram ity ucyate. katham iti. śrāvastyāṃ nidānaṃ. tatrāyuṣmāṃ chāriputro bhikṣūn āmaṃtrayate sma. ihāyuṣmaṃto bhikṣuḥ śīlasaṃpannaś ca bhavati samādhisampannaś ca prajñāsaṃpannaś ca. so 'bhīkṣṇaṃ saṃjñāveditanirodhaṃ samāpadyate ca vyuttiṣṭhate ca. asti caitat sthānam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. sa na haiva dṛṣṭa eva dharme pratipady evājñām ārāgayati. nāpi maraṇakālasamaye. bhedāc ca kāyasyātikramya devān kavaḍīkārabhakṣān anyatamasmin divye manomaye kāya upapadyate. sa tatropapanno 'bhīkṣṇaṃ saṃjñāveditanirodhaṃ [Tib. 151b] samāpadyate ca vyuttiṣṭhate ca. asti caitat sthānam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. tena khalu punaḥ samayenāyuṣmān udāyī tasyām eva parṣadi saṃniṣaṇṇo 'bhut saṃnipatitaḥ. athāyuṣmān udāyī āyuṣmaṃtaṃ śāriputram idam avocat. asthānam etad āyuṣmaṃ chāriputrānavakāśo yad bhikṣur anyatamasmiṃ divye manomaye kāye upapanno 'bhīkṣṇaṃ saṃjñāveditanirodhaṃ samāpadyate ca vyuttiṣtḥate cāsti caitat sthānam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. dvir api trir api āyuṣmāṃ udāyī āyuṣmaṃtaṃ śāriputram idam avocat. asthānam etad āyuṣman. iti pūrvavat. athāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitad abhavat. yāvat trir api me ayaṃ bhikṣur bhāṣitaṃ prativahati pratikrośati. na ca me kaścit sabrahmacārī bhāṣitam abhyanumodate. yan nv ahaṃ yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāmeyaṃ. athāyuṣmāṃ chāriputro yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāṃtaḥ. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vaṃditvaikāṃte niṣaṇṇaḥ. ekāṃte niṣaṇṇaś cāyuśmāṃ chāriputro bhikṣūn āmaṃtrayate sma. ihāyuṣmaṃto bhikṣuḥ śīlasaṃpannaś ca bhavati. pūrvavat. tena khalu samayenāyuṣmān udāyī pūrvavat. evaṃ dvir api trir apy āyuṣmān udāyī āyuṣmaṃtaṃ śāriputram idam avocat. pūrvavat
body.translated_text: 'Is there indeed any decline [from it]?' — This attainment is similar to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Wondering 'How could there be decline from this?' — [the questioner] asks with an attitude of impossibility. 'The <s>Udāyi-sūtra</s>' — this <s>sūtra</s> was spoken by the Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>. But <s>Udāyin</s> is the obstructor therein — hence it is called the '<s>Udāyi-sūtra</s>.' 'How?' — the setting (<s>nidāna</s>) is in <s>Śrāvastī</s>. There the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> addressed the monks: 'Here, Venerables, a monk is accomplished in moral conduct, accomplished in concentration, accomplished in wisdom. He repeatedly enters and rises from the cessation of perception and feeling (<s>saṃjñāvedita-nirodha</s>). There is this possibility — he knows as it truly is. He does not necessarily attain final knowledge (<s>ājñā</s>) in this very life, in the present existence. Nor at the time of death. But after the breakup of the body, having transcended the gods who consume morsels of food, he is reborn in one of the divine, mind-made bodies. Having been reborn there, he repeatedly enters and rises from the cessation of perception and feeling. [Tib. 151b] There is this possibility — he knows as it truly is.' Now at that time, the Venerable <s>Udāyin</s> was seated in that very assembly, having arrived [there]. Then the Venerable <s>Udāyin</s> said this to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'This is impossible, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no occasion for a monk who has been reborn in one of the divine, mind-made bodies to repeatedly enter and rise from the cessation of perception and feeling — [and] there is this possibility — he knows as it truly is.' A second time, and a third time, the Venerable <s>Udāyin</s> said this to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'This is impossible, Venerable' — as before. Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> thought: 'Up to three times this monk contradicts and opposes what I have said. And no fellow practitioner of mine approves of what I have said. I should go to where the Blessed One is.' Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> went to where the Blessed One was. Having approached, having bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Having sat down to one side, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> addressed the monks: 'Here, Venerables, a monk is accomplished in moral conduct' — as before. Now at that time, the Venerable <s>Udāyin</s> — as before. Thus a second time, and a third time, the Venerable <s>Udāyin</s> said this to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> — as before

body.text: . athāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitad abhavat. śāstur api me purastād ayaṃ bhikṣur yāvat trir api bhāṣitaṃ prativahati pratikrośati. na ca me kaścit sabrahmacārī [Tib. 152a] bhāṣitam abhyanumodate. yan nv ahaṃ tūṣnīṃ syāṃ. athāyuṣmāṃ chāriputras tūṣṇīm abhūt. tatra bhagavān āyuṣmaṃtam udāyinam āmaṃtrayate sma. kaṃ punas tvam udāyinn anyatamaṃ divyaṃ manomayaṃ kāyaṃ saṃjānīṣe. nanu yāvad evārūpiṇaṃ saṃjñāmayaṃ. evaṃ bhadanta. tvaṃ tāvan mohapuruṣāndha eva sann acakṣuś cakṣuṣmatā śāriputreṇa bhikṣuṇā sārdham abhidharme 'bhivinaye saṃlapitavyaṃ manyasa iti. tatra bhagavān āyuṣmaṃtam udāyinaṃ saṃmukham avasādya āyuṣmaṃtaṃ ānandam āmaṃtrayate sma. tvam apy ānanda sthaviraṃ bhikṣuṃ viheṭhyamānam adhyupekṣase. kāruṇyam api te mohapuruṣa notpannaṃ sthavire bhikṣau viheṭhyamāna iti. tatra bhagavān āyuṣmaṃtam udāyinam āyuṣmaṃtaṃ cānandaṃ saṃmukham avasādya bhikṣūn āmaṃtrayate sma. iha bhikṣavo bhikṣuḥ śīlasaṃpannaś bhavati. samādhisaṃpannaś ca vistareṇa yāvad asti caitat sthānam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīty uktvā bhagavān utthāyāsanād vihāraṃ prāvikṣat pratisaṃlayanāyeti. atrāyuṣmān udāyī ārūpyāvacaro 'yaṃ manomayaḥ kāya ukta iti manasikṛtvā pratibaṃdham akārṣīt. tatra hi rūpaṃ nāsti. mana eva tu sasaṃprayogam asti. tasmān manomayaḥ kāyaḥ. tatra ceyaṃ samāpattir na samāpadyate iti tasyābhiprāyaḥ. āryaśāriputrasya [Tib. 152b] tu rūpāvacaro divyo manomayakāyo 'bhipretaḥ śuklaśoṇitam anupāyya prādurbhāvāt. ata eva cāsāv āyuṣmān udāyī bhagavatā pṛṣṭaḥ. kaṃ punas tvaṃ udāyinn anyatamaṃ divyaṃ manomayaṃ kāyaṃ saṃjānīṣe. nanu yāvad evārūpiṇaṃ saṃjñāmayam iti. tenāpy evaṃ bhadaṃteti pratipannaṃ. bhagavān api rūpāvacaram eva divyaṃ manomayaṃ kāyam abhipretyāryaśāriputrasya mataṃ samarthayan tam āyuṣmaṃtam udāyinam avasādayati sma. tvaṃ tāvan mohapuruṣāndha eva sann acakṣuś cakṣuṣmatā śāriputreṇa bhikśuṇā sārdham abhidharme 'bhivinaye saṃlapitavyaṃ manyasa iti. asti caitat sthānam iti yad etan nirodhasamāpatteḥ samāpadanaṃ vyutthānam cety etat sthānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. pratipady eveti pūrvam evety arthaḥ. ājñām ārāgayatīty arhattvaṃ prapnotīty arthaḥ. iyaṃ ca samāpattir bhāvāgrikīti vistaraḥ. nirodhasamāpattir bhāvāgrikī. yaś ca tallābhī. tasva bhavāgra evopapattiḥ syān na rūpadhātau. uktaṃ ca sūtre. sa tatra rūpadhātāv upapanno 'bhīkṣṇaṃ saṃjñāveditanirodhaṃ samāpadyate ca vyuttiṣṭhate ceti. tasmād asty ataḥ parihāṇir iti gamyate. yujyata evaitad vaibhāṣikāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Even in the Teacher's presence, this monk contradicts and reproaches my statement up to three times. And not a single fellow practitioner [Tib. 152a] approves my statement. Let me be silent.' Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> became silent. Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Udāyin</s>: 'Which, <s>Udāyin</s>, do you understand as one or another divine mind-made body? Is it not [the one] up to the formless, consisting of perception?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'You, fool, blind one, having no eye — you think you should engage in discussion about <s>Abhidharma</s> and <s>Abhivinaya</s> with the monk <s>Śāriputra</s> who possesses the eye!' Thereupon the Blessed One, having rebuked the Venerable <s>Udāyin</s> to his face, addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'You too, <s>Ānanda</s>, look on with indifference while an elder monk is being harassed. Has not even compassion arisen in you, fool, when an elder monk is being harassed?' Then the Blessed One, having rebuked the Venerable <s>Udāyin</s> and the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> to their faces, addressed the monks: 'Here, monks, a monk is endowed with moral virtue, endowed with concentration' — and so on in detail up to — 'he knows as it really is: "there is this state"' — having said this, the Blessed One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling for solitary meditation. Here, the Venerable <s>Udāyin</s>, thinking 'this mind-made body is said to belong to the formless realm,' raised an objection. For there, form does not exist, but mind alone, together with its associates, does exist. Therefore it is a mind-made body. And this attainment is not entered therein — this was his intent. But for the Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, [Tib. 152b] the divine mind-made body intended was the one belonging to the form-realm, because it manifests without depending on semen and blood. And for this very reason, that Venerable <s>Udāyin</s> was questioned by the Blessed One: 'Which, <s>Udāyin</s>, do you understand as one or another divine mind-made body? Is it not the formless one, consisting of perception?' And by him too it was acknowledged: 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' The Blessed One too, intending the divine mind-made body belonging to the form-realm, validating the Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>'s position, rebuked that Venerable <s>Udāyin</s>: 'You, fool, blind one, having no eye — you think you should engage in discussion about <s>Abhidharma</s> and <s>Abhivinaya</s> with the monk <s>Śāriputra</s> who possesses the eye!' 'There is this state' — this 'state' that he knows as it really is is the entering into and arising from the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>). 'Immediately in practice' means 'already beforehand.' 'He achieves final knowledge' means he attains <s>Arhatship</s>. 'And this attainment belongs to the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>)' — and so on in detail. The cessation attainment belongs to the peak of existence. And one who has obtained it would be reborn only at the peak of existence, not in the form-realm. And it is stated in the <s>Sūtra</s>: 'He, having been reborn there in the form-realm, repeatedly enters into and arises from the cessation of perception and feeling.' Therefore, it is understood that there is decline from this [attainment]. This is consistent for the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>.

body.text:
. sautrāṃtikānāṃ tu katham etat. ārya eva hi nirodhasamāpattilābhī na cāryamārgād asti parihāṇir iti sautrāṃtikasiddhāṃtaḥ. [Tib. 153a] tasyāryasya katham uparibhūmikād āryamārgāt parihāṇir iti iṣyate.
teṣām apy etat sūtraṃ na virudhyate. kathaṃ. yo hi kaścid bhavāgralābhī niyāmam avakrāmati. so 'nāgāmī san nirodhasamāpattim utpādayet. sa bhavāgrān nirodhasamāpatteś ca parihīyeta. na tu mārgāt. ūrdhvabhūmikasyāryamārgasya kadācid anutpāditatvāt. sa parihīṇo bhūtvā dhyānam utpādya rūpadhātāv upapadyet. tasmād asty ataḥ parihāṇir na cāryamārgāt parihāṇir iti na svasiddhāntavirodhaḥ. navānupūrvasamāpattaya iti. catvāri dhyānāni catvāra ārūpyā nirodhasamāpattiś ca. prāthamakalpikaṃ pratīti. āditaḥ samāpattividhāyakaṃ pratīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: But how [is it so] for the <s>Sautrāntikas</s>? For the established doctrine of the <s>Sautrāntikas</s> is that only a Noble One obtains the cessation attainment, and there is no decline from the Noble Path. [Tib. 153a] How then is the decline of that Noble One from the Noble Path of a higher level accepted? For them too, this <s>Sūtra</s> is not contradicted. How? Whoever, having obtained the peak of existence [attainment], enters the fixed course [of certainty] — that [person], being a Non-Returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>), would produce the cessation attainment. He would decline from the peak of existence and from the cessation attainment, but not from the path — because a Noble Path of a higher level has never been produced [by him]. Having declined, he would produce a <s>dhyāna</s> and be reborn in the form-realm. Therefore, there is decline from this [attainment], but no decline from the Noble Path — hence there is no contradiction with their own established doctrine. 'The nine successive attainments' — the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the four formless [attainments], and the cessation attainment. 'With regard to the one [who enters] for the first time' — meaning: with regard to the [instruction] that prescribes the attainment from the beginning.

body.text: niyatobhayathāvedanīyatvād iti. niyatavedanīyāsaṃjñisamāpattir upapadyavedanīyatvāt. ubhayathāvedanīyā nirodhasamāpattir niyatāniyatavedanīyety arthaḥ. niyatavedanīyā anāgāminaḥ. aniyatavedanīyārhata ihaiva parinirvāṇāt. prathamotpādanato 'pīti. asaṃjñisamāpattiṃ kaścit prathamaṃ manuṣyeṣūtpādayati. kaścid rūpadhātau. nirodhasamāpattiṃ tu manuṣyeṣv evotpādayati. parihīṇas tu rūpadhātau. [Tib. 153b] atha kasmān manuṣyeṣv evainām utpādayati. saṃjñāvedanādvāreṇa vitarkavicārādicaittapracāraparikhinno 'nāgāmī tāṃ tena vihāreṇa sukhaṃ vihareyam iti nirodhasamāpattim utpādayati. rūpadhātūpapannas tv anāgāmī rūpadhātoḥ śāṃtatvān na tathā tatratyacaitasikapravṛttyā pīḍyata iti na prathamatas tatrotpādayati. parihīṇas tu pūrvābhyāsatas tām utpādayati. ārūpyadhātūpapanno 'py ata eva śāṃtatvān naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanopapanno notpādayati. nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇaprasaṃgād vā. tatra hi rūpaṃ nāsti cittacaittā yadi nirudhyeran parinirvāṇam evāsya syāt. cittaviprayuktānāṃ kevalānām avasthānāsāmarthyāt. niyatavedanīyasya karmaṇo 'parisamāptaphalasya vighnabhāvenāvasthānān na parinirvāṇasaṃbhavaḥ. asaṃjñisamāpattiṃ tu mokṣasaṃjñayā niḥsaraṇasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇa manasikāreṇa samāpadyata iti rūpadhātāv api prathamataḥ samāpadyate.
body.translated_text: 'Because of being necessarily twofold in its retribution' — the non-perceptual attainment (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>), being of necessarily determined retribution, has retribution at [the time of] rebirth. The cessation attainment has twofold retribution — meaning: determined and undetermined. The determined retribution is for the Non-Returner; the undetermined retribution is for the <s>Arhat</s>, because of attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in this very life. 'Also from the perspective of first production' — some first produce the non-perceptual attainment among humans, some in the form-realm. But the cessation attainment is produced only among humans. One who has declined, however, [produces it again] in the form-realm. [Tib. 153b] But why does one produce it only among humans? A Non-Returner, being oppressed by the operation of mental factors such as applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>) through the door of perception and feeling, produces the cessation attainment [thinking]: 'May I dwell happily by means of that abiding.' But a Non-Returner reborn in the form-realm, because of the peacefulness of the form-realm, is not so afflicted by the operation of mental factors there, and hence does not first produce it there. But one who has declined produces it there due to previous habituation. One reborn in the formless realm too, for this very reason — because of peacefulness — even one reborn in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception does not produce it. Or, because of the consequence of <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder. For there, form does not exist; if mind and mental factors were to cease, it would simply be his <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — because of the impossibility of the mere persistence of [dharmas] dissociated from mind. Because of the obstacle posed by <s>karma</s> of determined retribution whose fruit has not been exhausted, there would be no possibility of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> [in that way]. But the non-perceptual attainment, since one enters it with the perception of liberation and with mental attention preceded by the perception of escape, is entered for the first time even in the form-realm.

body.text: kasmāt punar ete iti vistaraḥ. sarvacittacaittanirodhasvabhāvatvāt ubhe apy ete samāpattī cittacaittanirodhe iti vaktavye ity abhiprāyaḥ. tatprātikūlyena tatsamāpattiprayogād iti. saṃjñāvedanāprātikūlyena tayoḥ samāpattyoḥ prayogāt. saṃjñāprātikūlyenāsaṃjñisamāpattiprayogaḥ [Tib. 154a] saṃjñā rogaḥ saṃjñā śalyaḥ saṃjñā gaṇḍaḥ etac chāṃtaṃ etat praṇītam iti vistaraḥ. saṃjñāveditaprātikūlyena nirodhasamāpattiprayogaḥ. paracittajñānavacanavad
body.translated_text: 'Why then are these [called thus]?' — and so on in detail. Since both these attainments have the nature of the cessation of all mind and mental factors, the intent is: they should be called 'cessation of mind and mental factors.' 'Because of the practice of that attainment through aversion to those' — because of the practice of those two attainments through aversion to perception and feeling. The practice of the non-perceptual attainment is through aversion to perception: [Tib. 154a] 'Perception is a disease, perception is a dart, perception is a sore — this is peaceful, this is excellent' — and so on in detail. The practice of the cessation attainment is through aversion to perception-and-feeling. 'Like the expression "knowledge of others' minds"'

body.text: iti. yathā paracittajñānavacanaṃ na ca paracittajñānena caittā na jñāyaṃte kadācit. atha ca parasya cittaṃ jñāsyāmīty evaṃ prathamataḥ prayogāt paracittajñānam ity ucyate. na paracittacaittajñānam iti. tadvad ihāpy anayoḥ samāpattyos tathā vacanaṃ.
body.translated_text: — just as the expression 'knowledge of others' minds' — yet by the knowledge of others' minds, mental factors are never not known; but because one initially makes effort [thinking] 'I shall know others' minds,' it is called 'knowledge of others' minds,' not 'knowledge of others' mind-and-mental-factors.' Similarly here too, for these two attainments, such is the expression.

body.text: tatrācittakāny eva nirodhasaṃjñisamāpattyāsaṃjñikānīti vaibhāṣikādayaḥ. aparisphuṭamanovijñānasacittakānīti sthaviravasumitrādayaḥ. ālayavijñānasacittakānīti yogācārā iti siddhāṃtabhedaḥ. tasmād idam upanyasyate. katham idānīṃ bahukālaniruddhād iti vistaraḥ. bahukālaniruddhagrahaṇaṃ samanaṃtaraniruddhanirāsārthaṃ. samanaṃtaraniruddhādīdānīṃ kathaṃ bhavati. yadi samanaṃtaraniruddham astīty abhyupagataṃ bahukālaniruddham apy astīti kiṃ nābhyupagamyate iti vaibhāṣikāḥ. na samanaṃtaraniruddhasyāstitvaṃ brūmaḥ api tu vartamānaṃ cittam ātmano 'nyacittahetubhāvaṃ vyavasthāpya nirudhyate 'nyac cotpadyate tulādaṇḍanāmonnāmavat. tac ca niruddham aparaṃ ca cittam [Tib. 154a] utpannaṃ bhavatīty anaṃtaraniruddhāc cittāc cittāntaram utpadyate ity ucyate. vartamānasāmīpye vartamānavad iti kṛtvā. apare punar āhur iti sautrāṃtikāḥ. kathaṃ tāvad ārūpyopapannānām iti vistaraḥ. tāvacchabdaḥ kramārthaḥ. idam eva tāvad dṛṣṭāṃtārthaṃ vaktavyam ity arthaḥ. rūpasya hi samanaṃtarapratyayo neṣyate. tat katham utpadyate. tasmāc cittād eva taj jāyate na rūpād iti brūmaḥ. anyonyabījakaṃ hy etad ubhayam iti. citte 'pi sendriyasya kāyasya bījam asti kāye ca sendriye cittasyeti. paripṛcchāyām iti. paripṛcchānāmaśāstraṃ kṛtiḥ sthaviravasumitrasya. sa tasyām āha. paṃcavastukādīny api hi tasaya saṃti śāstrāṇi. tasmād viśinaṣṭi. tasyaiva doṣa iti. katamaḥ sa doṣaḥ. katham idānīṃ bahukālaniruddhāc cittād iti ya uktaḥ. trayāṇāṃ saṃnipāta iti. iṃdriyaviṣayavijñānānāṃ. saṃjñāvedanayor apy atra nirodho na syād iti. bhadaṃtavasumitrasyaitan mataṃ. sacittakatve 'pi tasyā nirodhasamāpatteḥ saṃjñāvedanayos tatra nirodha iti. tasmād bhadaṃtaghoṣaka evaṃ prasaṃgaṃ karoti. avidyāsaṃsparśajam iti. avidyāsaṃhitaḥ sparśo 'vidyāsaṃsparśaḥ. tasmāj jātam avidyāsaṃsparśajaṃ. na tu vedanotpattāv iti. na tu vedanotpattau sparśo viśeṣita īdṛśaḥ sparśo vedanāpratyaya iti. sa eva bhadaṃtaghoṣaka upasaṃharati. tasmād acittiketi. [Tib. 155a] katham acittikāyāḥ samāpattitvam iti. dhyānādisamāpattitvam arhati. samādhinā hi cittacaittāḥ samā āpādyaṃte ekagrīkriyaṃta ity evaṃ matvā pṛcchati
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> and others [hold that] the cessation attainment, the non-perceptual attainment, and the non-perceptual [realm] are entirely without mind. The Elder <s>Vasumitra</s> and others [hold that they] possess mind, though with indistinct mental consciousness. The <s>Yogācāras</s> [hold that they] possess mind through the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store consciousness) — this is the difference of doctrines. Therefore this [question] is raised: 'How now, from [a mind] that ceased long ago...' — and so on in detail. The expression 'ceased long ago' is for the purpose of excluding what has just ceased (<s>samanantaraniruddha</s>). 'How now does [mind arise] from what has just ceased?' If it is accepted that what has just ceased exists, why is it not accepted that what ceased long ago also exists? — [say] the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>. 'We do not assert the existence of what has just ceased; rather, the present mind, having established the state of being the cause of another mind, ceases, and another arises — like the rising and falling of the beam of a balance.' That [mind] has ceased and another mind [Tib. 154b] has arisen — thus it is said that 'from the mind that ceased immediately, another mind arises.' [This is said] because of its proximity to the present, as if it were present. 'Others, however, say' — the <s>Sautrāntikas</s>. 'How, in the first place, for those reborn in the formless [realm]...' — and so on in detail. The word '<s>tāvat</s>' indicates sequence: meaning, 'just this much should first be stated for the purpose of illustration.' For the immediately-preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) of form is not accepted. Then how does it arise? Therefore we say: it is born from mind alone, not from form. 'For this pair is mutually seeded' — in mind there is also the seed of the body with its sense-faculties, and in the body with its sense-faculties [there is the seed] of mind. 'In the <s>Paripṛcchā</s>' — the <s>Paripṛcchā</s> is a treatise, a composition of the Elder <s>Vasumitra</s>. He states therein. For he also has other treatises such as the <s>Pañcavastuka</s> and so forth. Therefore he specifies. 'That very one's fault' — what is that fault? That which was stated: 'How now, from a mind that ceased long ago...' 'The meeting of three' — of sense-faculty, object, and consciousness. 'There would be no cessation of perception and feeling either, therein' — this is the view of the Venerable <s>Vasumitra</s>: that even when the cessation attainment possesses mind, there is cessation of perception and feeling therein. Therefore the Venerable <s>Ghoṣaka</s> raises this consequence. '<s>Avidyāsaṃsparśaja</s> (born from contact associated with ignorance)' — contact conjoined with ignorance is contact-associated-with-ignorance (<s>avidyāsaṃsparśa</s>); what is born from that is born-from-contact-associated-with-ignorance. 'But not in the arising of feeling' — but contact is not qualified in the arising of feeling as 'such-and-such contact is the condition of feeling.' That same Venerable <s>Ghoṣaka</s> concludes: 'Therefore, it is without mind.' [Tib. 155a] 'How can being without mind qualify as an attainment?' — [this question is raised because] it ought to qualify as an attainment like the <s>dhyāna</s> attainments and so forth. For by <s>samādhi</s>, mind and mental factors are made even, made one-pointed — understanding it thus, he asks.

body.text: . mahābhūtasamatāpādanād iti. mahābhūtāni samāny āpadyaṃte 'nayeti samāpattiḥ. evam asyāṃ niodhasamāpattau dhyānādiṣu ca samāpattitvaṃ. kā punar iha mahābhūtānāṃ samatā. cittotpattiprātikūlyasamavasthānaṃ. samāgacchaṃtīti samāpadyaṃte. samāgacchaṃti tām iti samāpattiḥ karmasādhanaṃ. dhyānādīny api samāgacchaṃti yoginaḥ. tasmād dhyānādīnām api samāpattitvaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: 'Because of bringing the great elements to equilibrium' — the great elements are brought to equilibrium by this — hence it is an attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>). Thus, for this cessation attainment and for the <s>dhyānas</s> and the rest, the status of being an attainment [is established]. What then is the equilibrium of the great elements here? The state of being established in opposition to the arising of mind. '<s>Samāpadyante</s>' means 'they come together'; they come together with it — hence it is a <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) — [the suffix is used] in the objective sense. Yogins also come together with the <s>dhyānas</s> and the rest. Therefore, the <s>dhyānas</s> and the rest too have the status of being attainments.

body.text: dravyata iti svalakṣaṇataḥ. cittotpattipratibaṃdhanāt. yasmāc cittotpattiṃ pratibadhnītaḥ. na. samāpatticittenaiveti. naitad evaṃ. kasmāt. samāpatticittenaiva tatpratibaṃdhanāt. cittotpattipratibaṃdhanād ity arthaḥ. katham iti tat pratipādayati. samāpatticittam eva hīti vistaraḥ. tat samāpatticittam eva nānyad dravyaṃ. cittāṃtaraviruddhaṃ anāgatacittaviruddham utpadyate. yena cittena kālāṃtaraṃ nātyaṃtaṃ apravṛttimātraṃ bhavati. mātraśabdo [Tib. 155b] dravyāṃtaravyāvartanārthaḥ. tadviruddhāśrayāpādanāt. cittaviruddhasyāśrayasya saṃtānasyāpādanāt kāraṇāt. yad etad apravṛttimātraṃ. sāsau samāpattir iti prajñapyate. prajñaptidharmo 'yaṃ na dravyadharma ity arthaḥ. yadi na dravyadharmaḥ katham asau saṃskṛtam iti prajñapyate ity ata āha. tac cāpravṛttimātraṃ. na pūrvam abhūt nottarakālaṃ vyutthitasya yogino bhavatīti. saṃskṛtāsau samāpattir asaṃjñisamāpattir nirodhasamāpattir vā prajñapyate saṃvyavahārato na tu dravyataḥ. atha veti vistaraḥ. āśrayasyaiva tathāsamāpādanaṃ tathāvyavasthānam. avasthāviśeṣaḥ. samāpattijanitāyā asyāḥ samāpattir ity arthaḥ. sa cāvasthāviśeṣaḥ pūrvaṃ nāsīt pāścāc ca na bhavati vyutthitasyeti saṃskṛtatvaṃ na virudhyate. atha vā samāpadanam iti pāṭhaḥ. saṃskṛtāvasthāviśeṣatvād asyāḥ samāpatteḥ saṃskṛtatvaṃ sidhyatīty arthaḥ. evam āsaṃjñikam iti vistaraḥ. cittam evāsau yogī tatrāsaṃjñiṣu cittapravṛttiviruddhaṃ labhate. tac cāpravṛttimātraṃ cittacaittānām iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. āsaṃjnikam iti prajñapyate na tu dravyato 'stīty abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'In terms of substance' means in terms of own-characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). 'Because of obstructing the arising of mind.' Because it obstructs the arising of mind. 'No. By the attainment-mind itself.' This is not so. Why? Because it is obstructed by the attainment-mind itself — the meaning is: because of obstructing the arising of mind. How? He explains that: 'For the attainment-mind itself' — thus the elaboration. That attainment-mind itself, not another substance, arises as opposed to other minds — opposed to future minds. By which mind, for a period of time, there is merely non-occurrence, not permanent [cessation]. The word 'merely' [Tib. 155b] serves to exclude other substances. Because of producing a basis opposed to that — because of producing a continuum of basis opposed to mind. This 'mere non-occurrence' is designated as that attainment. This is a designated <s>dharma</s>, not a substantial <s>dharma</s> — this is the meaning. If it is not a substantial <s>dharma</s>, how is it designated as conditioned? — therefore he says: 'And that mere non-occurrence did not exist before, nor does it exist afterward for the practitioner who has emerged.' That attainment — whether the non-perception attainment (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>) or the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) — is designated as conditioned conventionally, but not substantially. 'Or alternatively' — thus the elaboration. The very establishing of the basis in such a way, the very abiding in such a state — is a special state. The meaning is: this attainment is born from the attainment [process]. And that special state did not exist before and does not exist afterward for one who has emerged — therefore its conditioned nature is not contradicted. Or alternatively, the reading is '<s>samāpadanam</s>' (entering). The meaning is: because this attainment is a conditioned special state, its conditioned nature is established. 'Likewise the <s>āsaṃjñika</s> (non-perceptive state)' — thus the elaboration. That practitioner obtains, among the non-perceptive [beings], the very mind that is opposed to the occurrence of mind. And that is 'mere non-occurrence of mind and mental factors' — this completes the sentence. It is designated as <s>āsaṃjñika</s>, but the intent is that it does not exist substantially.

body.text: (II.46ab) ya ūṣmaṇa iti vistaraḥ. ūṣmaṇo vijñānasya ca jīvitapratibaddhā pravṛttiḥ. tasmāj jīvitam ūṣmaṇo vijñānasya cādhāra ucyate sthitihetus tayor eva. nityānivṛttiprasaṃga [Tib. 156a] iti. nityam eṣāṃ srotaḥ prasajyeta. nikāyasabhāgasya sthitikālāvedha iti. nikāyasabhāgo vyākhyātaḥ. ta eva tathābhūtās saṃskārā rūpādiskaṃdhasvabhāvā iti. teṣāṃ sthitiḥ prabaṃdhaḥ. tasyāḥ kālo yāvat tena sthātavyaṃ. ta eva tāvaṃtaḥ saṃskārakṣaṇāḥ. tasyāvedhaḥ
body.translated_text: (II.46ab) 'That which, of heat' — thus the elaboration. The occurrence of heat (<s>ūṣman</s>) and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is dependent on life (<s>jīvita</s>). Therefore life is said to be the support of heat and consciousness — the cause of their continuance. 'The consequence of permanence and non-cessation' — [Tib. 156a] the stream of these would follow permanently. 'The penetrating determination of the duration of class-homogeneity' — class-homogeneity (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>) has been explained. Those very formations of such a nature, having the own-nature of the form and other aggregates — their continuance is their continuity. The time of that [continuity] — as long as one is to remain — those very moments of formations for that duration. Its penetrating determination

body.text: pratisaṃdhikṣaṇe pūrvajanmakarmaṇo hetubhāvavyavasthānaṃ. kaḥ punar asau hetuḥ. sāmarthyaviśeṣaḥ. sa hi skandhaprabandhalakṣaṇāyāḥ sthiteḥ kṣaṇaparaṃparayā kāraṇaṃ bhavati. ata eva sthitikālāvedha ucyate. tāvatkālaṃ pravāhākṣepalakṣaṇatvāt. tāvat so 'vatiṣṭhata iti. sa nikāyasabhāgaḥ. sasyānāṃ pākakālāvedhavat. yathā sasyānāṃ pākakālāvedhaḥ sāmarthyaviśeṣasvabhāvo bījenāṃkura evādhīyate yaḥ kṣaṇaparaṃparayā ā pākakālāt sasyasaṃtānahetur bhavati. tadvad etat. kṣipteṣusthitikālāvedhavac ca. yathā kṣiptasyeṣoḥ śarasya sthitir ākāśadeśāṃtarotpattiḥ saṃtānānuvṛttiḥ. tasyāḥ kālo maryādā yataḥ pareṇa sā na bhavati. tasyāvedho hetuvyavasthānaṃ. kaḥ punar asau hetuḥ. prayatnabhūtātiśayanirvṛttavāyudhātujanitasāmarthyaviśeṣaḥ. tadyathā kṣipteṣusthitikālāvedho na dravyāṃtaraṃ tadvad ayam āyurlakṣaṇam āvedho draṣṭavyaḥ.
body.translated_text: is the establishing of the causal status of <s>karma</s> from a previous birth at the moment of rebirth-connection (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>). What then is that cause? A special potency (<s>sāmarthyaviśeṣa</s>). For that is the cause, through a succession of moments, of the continuance characterized by the continuum of aggregates. Therefore it is called 'the penetrating determination of the duration' — because of its nature of projecting the stream for that long a time. 'So long does it continue' — that is the class-homogeneity. 'Like the penetrating determination of the ripening-time of crops.' Just as the penetrating determination of the ripening-time of crops — a special potency by nature — is implanted by the seed in the very sprout, and becomes the cause of the crop's continuum through a succession of moments up to the time of ripening. So too is this. 'And like the penetrating determination of the duration of a shot arrow.'
