iti. saṃjñāsamuktayo nāmakāyāḥ. vākyasamuktayaḥ padakāyāḥ. akṣarasamuktayo vyaṃjanakāyāḥ. saṃjñākaraṇam iti lokabhāṣeyaṃ. saṃjñākaraṇaṃ nāmadheyam iti paryāyaḥ. tathā hi loke vaktāro bhavanti. devadatta ity asya saṃjñākaraṇam iti. saṃjñāyāḥ karaṇaṃ saṃjñākaraṇaṃ. yena saṃjñā caitasiko dharmaḥ kriyate janyate. saṃjñaiva vā karaṇaṃ saṃjñākaraṇaṃ. saṃjñāgrahaṇaṃ cānyakaraṇanivṛttyarthaṃ. karaṇagrahaṇaṃ caitasikaviśeṣaṇārthaṃ
body.translated_text: (II.48ab) '<s>Nāmakāya</s> (name-group) and the rest are collections of designations, sentences, and syllables' — collections of designations are <s>nāmakāyas</s>; collections of sentences are <s>padakāyas</s>; collections of syllables are <s>vyañjanakāyas</s>. 'The making of a designation (<s>saṃjñākaraṇa</s>)' — this is a worldly expression. '<s>Saṃjñākaraṇa</s>' is synonymous with 'name' (<s>nāmadheya</s>). For thus speakers in the world say: 'The designation of this [person is] <s>Devadatta</s>.' '<s>Saṃjñākaraṇa</s>' — the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) of designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>); that by which the mental factor of perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) is produced, generated. Or, the designation itself is the instrument — [thus] <s>saṃjñākaraṇa</s>. The mention of '<s>saṃjñā</s>' is for the purpose of excluding other instruments. The mention of '<s>karaṇa</s>' is for the purpose of specifying [that it is not] the mental factor [itself].

body.text: . yadi hi saṃjñā nāmety ucyeta caitasiko 'pi saṃbhāvyeta. tat punaḥ saṃjñākaraṇaṃ [Tib. 169a] nāma rūpaṃ śabdo raso gandho vety evamādi. vākyaṃ padam iti. padyate gamyate 'neneti. padaṃ tu suptiṅantaṃ padaṃ gṛhyate. tenāha. yāvatārthaparisamāptis tadyathā
body.translated_text: For if <s>saṃjñā</s> alone were called 'name,' the mental factor too would be conceivable [as a name]. But that <s>saṃjñākaraṇa</s> [Tib. 169a] — 'name' — is: 'form,' 'sound,' 'taste,' 'smell' — and so forth. 'A sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is a <s>pada</s>' — '<s>pada</s>': that by which one goes (<s>padyate gamyate</s>), that is <s>pada</s>. But a <s>pada</s> ending with a <s>sup</s> or <s>tiṅ</s> suffix is what is meant by <s>pada</s>. Therefore he says: 'That which completes the meaning' — for example:

body.text: iti evamādīti. ādiśabdena
body.translated_text: and so on. By the word 'and so on':—

children.text:
utpādavyayadharmiṇaḥ
utpadya hi nirudhyante. teṣāṃ vyupaśamaḥ sukham

body.text: ity evamādi. asyā gāthāyā evam arthaṃ vyācakṣate.
body.translated_text: and so on. They interpret the meaning of this verse as follows:

body.text: iti pratijñā.
body.translated_text: this is the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>).

children.translated_text: 'Of the nature of arising and passing away' —

body.text: iti hetuḥ. yasmād utpādavyayadharmavantas tasmād anityā iti paricchidyante
body.translated_text: this is the reason (<s>hetu</s>). Because they possess the nature of arising and passing away, therefore they are determined to be impermanent.

body.text: iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ. ya utpadyante nirudhyante ca te anityāḥ. tadyathā ghaṭādayaḥ. tathā ca saṃskārā iti. apare punar vyācakṣate. asiddhahetusādhanārtham etad iti. katham etad gamyate.
body.translated_text: this is the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>). Those that arise and cease are impermanent — such as pots and the like. And so too are conditioned things. Others, however, interpret: this is for the purpose of proving an unestablished reason. How is this understood?

children.translated_text: 'Of the nature of arising and passing away' —

body.text: ta iti yasmād ete utpadya nirudhyamānā dṛṣtā iti. apare varṇayanti.
body.translated_text: that [is known] because 'these, having arisen, are seen to cease.'  Others explain:

children.translated_text: 'Impermanent, alas, are conditioned things — of the nature of arising and passing away' —

body.text: iti paryāyadvayam etad ucyate. kasmād ity āha. yasmād
body.translated_text: this is said as a pair of synonymous expressions. Why? He says: because —

body.text: iti hetuvacanaṃ.
body.translated_text: this is the statement of the reason.

body.text: ye hy anityās te duḥkhā atas
body.translated_text: [since] those that are impermanent are suffering, therefore —

body.text: iti vineyajanaṃ niyojayati. yena kriyāguṇakālasaṃbandhaviśeṣā gamyante. sāvyayakārakaviśeṣaṇaṃ vākyam iti vākyavido vadanti. tadyathā pacati paṭhati gacchatīti kṛṣṇo gauro [Tib. 169b] rakta iti pacati pakṣyati apākṣīd iti kriyāguṇakālānāṃ saṃbandhaviśeṣā gamyante. tat padaṃ. tathā hi sāmānyavartamānānāṃ padānāṃ yad viśeṣe 'vasthānaṃ sa vākyārtha ity āhuḥ. tad evaṃ svalakṣaṇābhidyotakaṃ nāma kriyādisaṃbandhaviśeṣābhidyotakaṃ padam ity uktaṃ bhavati. vyaṃjanam akṣaram iti varṇa ity arthaḥ. na tu hal eva acām api vyaṃjanakatveneṣṭatvāt.
body.translated_text: thus he exhorts the trainable beings. 'A sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is that by which particular connections of action, quality, and time are understood.' Those who know sentences say: 'A sentence is a qualifying expression with particles and case-endings.' For example: 'he cooks,' 'he recites,' 'he goes' — 'black,' 'white,' [Tib. 169b] 'red' — 'he cooks,' 'he will cook,' 'he cooked' — particular connections of action, quality, and time are understood. That is a <s>pada</s>. For thus they say: 'The determination of what is general in words to something specific — that is the meaning of a sentence.' Thus, a name (<s>nāma</s>) illuminates the particular characteristic, and a <s>pada</s> illuminates the particular connection with action and the rest — this is what has been stated. '<s>Vyañjana</s>' is a syllable (<s>akṣara</s>) — meaning: a phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>). But not only consonants (<s>hal</s>) — because vowels (<s>ac</s>) too are accepted as having the function of manifesting.

body.text: nanu cākṣarāṇy api lipyavayavānāṃ nāmānīti. lipayo manuṣyādibhiḥ pattrādiṣu ye likhitāḥ. teṣām akṣarāṇi nāmāni. rūpanāmagrahaṇe rūpapratītivad vyaṃjanagrahaṇe lipipratītiḥ. ato vyaṃjanam api lipyavayavānāṃ nāma bhavatīti lakṣaṇasāṃkaryaṃ. tataś ca yad abhipretaṃ nāmno vyatiriktam anyad eva vyaṃjanam akṣaram iti. tan nopapadyate. na vai lipyavayavānām iti vistaraḥ. viparītam etad iti vyācaṣṭe. yat tu vyaṃjanagrahaṇe lipipratītir iti. tat pratyāyyapratyāyakabhāvena saṃketitatvāt. na tu tannāmabhāvāt.
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'But surely syllables are also names of the parts of written letters.' Written letters are those written by humans and the like on leaves and the like. The syllables are their names. Just as in grasping the name of form, there is the cognition of form — so in grasping a <s>vyañjana</s>, there is the cognition of a written letter. Therefore, <s>vyañjana</s> too is a name of the parts of written letters — [hence] there is a confusion of definitions. And therefore, what was intended — that <s>vyañjana</s>, the syllable, is something different from name — is not tenable. [Reply:] 'Not of the parts of written letters' — and so on in detail. He explains: this is the reverse. That which you say — 'in grasping a <s>vyañjana</s>, there is the cognition of a written letter' — that is because they have been conventionally established in the relationship of signified and signifier, not because [<s>vyañjana</s>] is a name of those [letters].

body.text: samuktir iti uca samavāya ity etasya dhātoḥ ktini samuktir iti etad rūpaṃ bhavati. yo 'rthaḥ samavāya iti. so 'rthaḥ samuktir iti. samavāya ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: '<s>Samukti</s>' (collection) — from the root '<s>uc</s>' with the prefix '<s>sam</s>' (meaning 'coming together'), with the <s>ktin</s> suffix, the form '<s>samukti</s>' is obtained. The meaning that is '<s>samavāya</s>' (assemblage) — that meaning is '<s>samukti</s>.' The meaning is: assemblage.

body.text: nanu ca te iti sautrāntikavacanaṃ. naite vāksvabhāvā iti vistareṇa vaibhāṣikavacanaṃ. na ca ghoṣamātreṇeti. nānakṣarātmakena ghoṣeṇārtho 'vagamyate. kiṃ tarhi. vāṅ nāmni pravartate. tan nāmātmarūpatām iva vāca āpādayad arthatvaṃ dyotayati. tāṃ vācam upādāya padārthaṃ dyotayati. [Tib. 170a] pratyāyayatīty arthaḥ. sautrāntika āha. na vai ghoṣamātraṃ vāg iti vistaraḥ. na vayaṃ ghoṣamātraṃ vāg iti varṇayāmaḥ. kaścid eva tu ghoṣo varṇātmakaḥ. saiva vāk. yo 'rtheṣu kṛtāvadhiḥ kṛtamaryādaḥ. etena saṃketāpekṣaḥ śabdo 'rthaṃ pratyāyayati. na yaḥ kaścic chabda iti darśayati. kṛtasaṃketaḥ śabdo 'rthaṃ pratyāyayatīti. tac caitacchabdamātrāt pratītapadārthakāt sidhyatīti. tac caitadarthadyotanaṃ nāmarahitāc chabdāj jātyādyabhidheyapadārthakāt sidhyatīty ayam asyārtha iti. yady utpādayatīti vistaraḥ. vāci satyāṃ sa cittaviprayukta utpadyata itīṣyate tenāśaṃkyate yady utpādayatīti. evaṃ cet sarvaṃ ghoṣamātraṃ vṛṣabhādigarjitam api nāmotpādayiṣyati. ghoṣasvabhāvā vāg iti kṛtvā. brūyās tvaṃ viśiṣṭa eva ghoṣo yo varṇātmakaḥ saṃbhāvitaḥ. sa eva nāmotpādayatīti. atrocyate. yādṛśo vā ghoṣaviśeṣa iṣyate nāmna utpādakaḥ. sa evārthasya dyotako bhaviṣyati. na tu sa cittaviprayukta ity abhiprāyaḥ. atha prakāśayatīti vistaraḥ. ghoṣeṇotpadyamānena sa cittaviprayukta utpadyate. sa taṃ prakāśayaty arthadyotanāyeti yadīṣyate. atrocyate. sarvaṃ ghoṣamātraṃ nāma prakāśayiṣyatīti pūrvavad vācyaṃ. na khalv api śabdānāṃ sāmagryam astīti. yad anekākṣaraṃ nāma. tadutpattiparikalpo 'nekaśabdāpekṣaḥ. tenaivaṃ vicāryate. ihoccaritapradhvansinaḥ śabdāḥ. tasmād eṣāṃ yugapadavasthānaṃ nāsti. ekasya ca dravyasato [Tib. 170b] dharmasya bhāgaśaḥ khaṇḍaśa utpādo na yukto yathā ghaṭapaṭādeḥ prajñaptisataḥ kalpyata iti katham utpādayantī vāṅ nāmotpādayet. yadā tad utpādayati. tadā
body.translated_text: 'But those' — this is the <s>Sautrāntika</s> statement. 'These are not of the nature of speech' — this is the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> statement in detail. 'Not by mere sound' — meaning is not understood through sound consisting of mere phonemes. What then? Speech operates upon name (<s>nāma</s>). That [speech], bringing name as if to the essential form of speech, illuminates its meaning. Taking up that speech, it illuminates the meaning of the word — i.e., it communicates. The <s>Sautrāntika</s> says: 'Speech is not mere sound,' and so forth in detail. We do not maintain that speech is mere sound. Rather, a certain sound that consists of phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) — that alone is speech, which has established conventions regarding objects. By this he shows that sound communicates meaning dependent on convention (<s>saṃketa</s>), not just any sound. A sound with established convention communicates meaning. And this is established from mere sound whose word-meaning is understood. And this illumination of meaning is established from sound devoid of name, whose word-meanings are categories like <s>jāti</s> (universal) and the rest — this is its meaning. 'If it produces' — and so forth in detail. When speech exists, that <s>cittaviprayukta</s> (mind-dissociated factor) is held to arise; hence the doubt: 'if it produces.' If so, then all mere sound, even the bellowing of bulls and the like, would produce name, since speech has sound as its nature. You might say: only a specific sound that consists of phonemes is recognized, and that alone produces name. To this it is replied: whatever specific sound is held to be the producer of name, that very sound itself will illuminate meaning — but it is not a <s>cittaviprayukta</s> (mind-dissociated factor); this is the intent. 'Or if it manifests' — and so forth in detail. If it is held that when sound is being produced, that <s>cittaviprayukta</s> arises and manifests it for the illumination of meaning — to this it is replied: all mere sound would manifest name, as stated before. Moreover, there is no assemblage (<s>sāmagrī</s>) of sounds. Since name consists of multiple phonemes, the conception of its production depends on multiple sounds. Therefore it is examined thus: sounds uttered here perish [immediately]. Hence there is no simultaneous existence of these. And partial, piece-by-piece production of a single substantially real <s>dharma</s> is not logical — as it is conceived for conventionally real things like pots and cloth — so how could speech, in producing, produce name? When it produces that, then —

body.text: kathaṃ sā tad utpādayatīti vākyārthaḥ. vartamānā hi vāṅ nāmotpādayanty utpādayet. na ca sarve vācchabdakṣanā yugapadvartamānā bhavanti. yadā hi rūpam iti raśabdo vartamāno bhavati. tadā ūkārapakārākārā anāgatā bhavanti. yadā ūkāro vartamāno bhavati. tadā raśabdo 'tītaḥ. pakārākārāv anāgatāu. evaṃ pakārākārāv api kramaśo yadā vartamānau bhavataḥ. tadetare na vartamānā iti. evam sā vāṅ nāma naivotpādayet. brūyās tvaṃ vartamāno raśabdas tasya rūpanāmnaḥ pūrvaṃ bhāgam utpādyati. ūśabdo 'pi vartamāno dvitīyaṃ bhāgam evaṃ yāvad akāraśabdas tasya caturthabhāgam utpādayatīti. tad ayuktam. ekasya dharmasya bhāgaśa utpādasaṃbhavād iti. uktam etat. kathaṃ tāvad atītāpekṣaḥ paścimo vijñaptikṣaṇa utpādayaty avijñaptim iti. prātimokṣasaṃvarasamādāne kāyavāgvijñaptayaḥ pravartante. tāsāṃ nāsti sāmagryaṃ. atha cātītakāyavāgvijñaptikṣaṇāpekṣaḥ paścimo vijñaptikṣaṇaḥ prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītām avijñaptim utpādayati. evam atītaśabdakṣaṇāpekṣaḥ paścimo vācchabdakṣaṇo nāmotpādayatīti. evaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. paścimaśabda eva nāmna utpādāt [Tib. 171a] yo 'pi tam evaikaṃ śṛṇoti yo 'pi paścimam evaikaṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇoti rūpam iti. so 'py arthaṃ pratipadyeta. so 'pi rūpanāmārthaṃ gṛhṇīyāt. tannāmotpatteḥ. na caivaṃ pratipadyate. tasmād ayuktam etat. athāpy evaṃ kalpyetīti vistaraḥ. kṣaṇapratibhāsā varṇavāg vyaṃjanam api tatpratibhāsam iti pakṣāntaram upanyasyate. vāg vyaṃjanaṃ janayati. vyaṃjanaṃ tu nāma janayatīti. atrāpi sa eva prasaṃgo vyaṃjanānāṃ sāmagryābhāvāt. kathaṃ. na khalu vyaṃjanānāṃ sāmagryam asti. na caikasya dharmasya bhāgaśa utpādo yukta iti katham utpādayad vyaṃjanaṃ nāmotpādayet. kathaṃ tāvad atītāpekṣaḥ paścimo vijñaptikṣaṇa utpādayaty avijñaptim. evaṃ tarhi paścima eva vyaṃjane nāmna utpādāt yo 'pi tam evaikaṃ paścimaṃ vyaṃjanotpādakaṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇoti. yo vā tad evaikaṃ paścimaṃ vyaṃjanaṃ śṛṇoti. so 'py arthaṃ pratipadyeta. eṣa eva tu prasaṃgo nāmnaḥ prakāśatve vāca iti. na khalv api śabdānāṃ sāmagryam asti. na caikasya dharmasya bhāgaśaḥ prakāśo yukta iti kathaṃ prakāśayantī vāk nāma prakāsayet. kathaṃ tāvad atītāpekṣaḥ paścimo vijñaptikṣaṇaḥ prakāśayaty avijñaptiṃ. evaṃ tarhi paścima eva śabde nāmnaḥ prakāśād yo 'pi tam evaikaṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇoti. so 'py arthaṃ pratipadyeta. athāpy evaṃ kalpyeta. vāg vyaṃjanaṃ prakāśayati. vyaṃjanaṃ tu nāmeti. atrāpi sa eva prasaṃgo vyaṃjanānāṃ sāmagryabhāvāt. yasya tarhi śabdamātraṃ nāmānekākṣaraṃ ca nāma bhavati na ca śabdānāṃ
body.translated_text: — how does it produce that? This is the meaning of the sentence. For speech, being present, would produce name if it could. But not all phonetic instants of speech exist simultaneously. For when the syllable 'ra' of '<s>rūpam</s>' is present, the sounds ū, pa, and a are future. When ū is present, 'ra' is past and pa and a are future. Similarly, when pa and a are successively present, the others are not present. Thus speech would never produce name. You might say: the present 'ra' sound produces the first part of the name '<s>rūpa</s>'; the present 'ū' sound produces the second part; and so on up to the 'a' sound producing the fourth part. That is illogical, because partial production of a single <s>dharma</s> is impossible — this has been stated. How then does the last moment of intentional action (<s>vijñapti</s>), dependent on past ones, produce the unintentional (<s>avijñapti</s>)? In undertaking the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint, bodily and verbal intentional actions operate. These have no assemblage. Yet the last intentional moment, dependent on past bodily and verbal intentional moments, produces the <s>avijñapti</s> included in the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint. Similarly, the last phonetic moment of speech, dependent on past phonetic moments, produces name. 'If so, then' — and so forth in detail. Since only the last sound produces name, even one who hears only that single [last] sound — who hears only the final sound of '<s>rūpam</s>' — should also understand the meaning and grasp the meaning of the name '<s>rūpa</s>,' because that name has arisen. But one does not understand thus. Therefore this is illogical. 'Or if it were conceived thus' — and so forth in detail. An alternative position is presented: the momentarily-appearing phonetic speech produces <s>vyañjana</s> (syllable), and that syllable-appearance [produces name]. Speech generates <s>vyañjana</s>; <s>vyañjana</s> in turn generates <s>nāma</s>. Here too the same objection applies, because there is no assemblage of syllables. How? There is certainly no assemblage of syllables, and partial production of a single <s>dharma</s> is not logical — so how could <s>vyañjana</s>, in producing, produce name? How then does the last intentional moment, dependent on past ones, produce <s>avijñapti</s>? If so, then since only the last syllable produces name, even one who hears only that single last sound which produces <s>vyañjana</s>, or who hears only that single last <s>vyañjana</s>, should also understand the meaning. This same objection applies if name is manifested by speech: there is no assemblage of sounds, and partial manifestation of a single <s>dharma</s> is not logical — so how could speech, in manifesting, manifest name? How then does the last intentional moment, dependent on past ones, manifest <s>avijñapti</s>? If so, then since only the last sound manifests name, even one who hears only that single sound should also understand the meaning. 'Or if it were conceived thus: speech manifests <s>vyañjana</s>, and <s>vyañjana</s> [manifests] name' — here too the same objection applies, because there is no assemblage of syllables. For one who holds that name is mere sound, and name consists of multiple phonemes, and there is no assemblage of sounds —

body.text:
sāmagryam asti. tasya kathaṃ nāmārthaṃ pratyāyayati. [Tib. 171b] sarvākṣarasmṛtyanantaratvāt arthapratipatteḥ. ata eva ca nāntarīyakanyāyena prathamākṣaraśravaṇakāla eva śeṣākṣarānusmṛtibalena kaścid arthaṃ pratipadyata eveti. vyaṃjanasyāpi vāṅ naivotpādikā na prakāśikā yujyata iti. pūrvaṃ śabdasyotpādyaṃ śabdasya vyaṃgyaṃ vā vyaṃjanam abhyupagamya doṣa udgrāhitaḥ. idānīṃ śabdavyatiriktānupalabdheḥ utpādyavyaṃgyatvam api tasya nāstīti tad eva unmūlayati. na tu śabdānāṃ sāmagryabhāvād iti
dośo vaktavyaḥ. na hy anekaśabdāpekṣā vyaṃjanapratipattiḥ. api ca ghoṣasvabhāvatvād vācaḥ sarvaṃ ghoṣamātraṃ vyaṃjanam utpādayiṣyati prakāśayiṣyati vā. yādṛśo vā ghoṣaviśeṣa iṣyate vyaṃjanasyotpādakaḥ prakāśako vā. sa eva vyaṃjanārthaṃ kariṣyatīti. athāpy arthasahajaṃ nāma jātyādivad iṣyeteti vistaraḥ. atha sahaje nāmni kalpyamāne vācotpādyaṃ prakāśyaṃ vā nāmety evamādighoṣaprasaṃgo na bhaviṣyatīti matvā pakṣāntaram idaṃ vikalpyate. yathā jātyādīni lakṣaṇāni arthasahajāny eveṣyante nātītānāgatasyārthasya vartamānāni bhavanti. evam eva yadi nāmeṣyate. atītānāgatasyārthasya vartamānaṃ nāma na syāt. tataś cātītānāgatārthavyavahāro na śakyeta kartuṃ. na hy atītānāgataṃ nāmārthaṃ dyotayitum arhati. yathātītānāgatā vāṅ nāma notpādayituṃ vyaṃjayituṃ cārhati. nāmabahutve ca na sahajaṃ nāma paricchidyeta. asaṃskṛtānāṃ [Tib. 172a] cānutpattimattvāt sahajanāma na syād iti aniṣṭir eveyaṃ na kartavyaiveyam iṣṭir ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: — there is no assemblage. How then does name communicate meaning? Because understanding of meaning occurs immediately after recollection of all the phonemes. And precisely for this reason, by the principle of invariable connection, even at the time of hearing the first phoneme, someone may understand the meaning through the power of recalling the remaining phonemes. <s>Vyañjana</s> too — speech is neither its producer nor its manifester; this is logical. Previously, the fault was raised by accepting <s>vyañjana</s> as either produced by sound or expressed by sound. Now, since there is no perception of anything apart from sound, its being producible or expressible does not exist — thus that [position] is uprooted. The fault 'because there is no assemblage of sounds' need not be stated, for the understanding of <s>vyañjana</s> does not depend on multiple sounds. Moreover, since speech has sound as its nature, all mere sound would either produce or manifest <s>vyañjana</s>. Or whatever specific sound is held to be the producer or manifester of <s>vyañjana</s>, that very sound itself will serve the purpose of <s>vyañjana</s>. 'Or if name is held to be co-arising with its object, like <s>jāti</s> (birth) and so forth' — and so forth in detail. Thinking that if name is conceived as co-arising, the objections about speech producing or manifesting it would not arise, this alternative is devised. Just as the characteristics like <s>jāti</s> are held to be co-arising with their objects and do not exist as present for past or future objects — if name is similarly held, then present name would not exist for a past or future object. Consequently, conventional usage regarding past and future objects would be impossible, for a past or future name would not be able to illuminate meaning, just as past or future speech would not be able to produce or express name. And with the multiplicity of names, a co-arising name could not be delimited. And since unconditioned things (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) do not arise, there would be no co-arising name for them — thus this position is simply unacceptable; this view should not be adopted — this is the intent.

body.text: gāthā vākyaṃ. sā nānāni saṃniśritā nāmasūtpanneṣu bhāvāt. tasmāt santi nāmāni vākyaṃ ceti vacanāvakāśo 'stīty āha. tatrārtheṣu kṛtāvadhiḥ śabdo nāmeti vistaraḥ. arthakṛtāvadhiśabdasvabhāvānāṃ nāmnāṃ racanāviśeṣo gāthā. vinyāsaviśeṣa ity arthaḥ. paṃktivad iti. yathā paṃktiḥ pipīlīkādīnāṃ racanāviśeṣo na tato dravyāntaram upapadyate. tadvat. ekakālavartināṃ pakṣipipīlikādīnāṃ racanāviśeṣaḥ paṃktir ity ucyate. kramavartināṃ tu śabdānāṃ na racanāviśeṣaḥ tena vaiṣamyam iti vacanāvakāśam abhisamīkṣya dvitīyo dṛṣṭānta upanyasyate. cittānupūrvyavac cetī. yathānukramavartibhyaś cittebhyo nānyad ānupūrvyam asti. tadvat. apārthikā tatprakḷptir iti. nisprayojanā nāmapadayor arthāntaraparikalpanety arthaḥ. na hi sarve dharmās tarkagamyā iti. kecid eva tarkagamyā na sarve. ye hi tathāgatajñānagocarapatitā eva. na te tarkagamyā ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: a <s>gāthā</s> is a sentence (<s>vākya</s>). It is based on names because it exists only where names have arisen. Therefore there is occasion for the statement 'names and sentences exist,' he says. 'A sound with established conventions regarding objects is name' — and so forth in detail. A <s>gāthā</s> is a particular arrangement (<s>racanāviśeṣa</s>) of names whose nature is sounds with established conventions regarding objects. 'Arrangement' means a particular disposition. 'Like a row' — just as a row is a particular arrangement of ants and the like, and no separate substance arises from it, so too [with gāthā]. A row is said to be the particular arrangement of simultaneously existing birds, ants, and the like. But for sounds that occur sequentially, there is no [simultaneous] arrangement; hence, seeing the dissimilarity, a second illustration is presented: 'Like the sequence of minds' — just as there is no separate sequence apart from sequentially occurring minds, so too. 'The conception of them as separate is purposeless' — the meaning is that conceiving name and word as separate entities is without purpose. 'For not all <s>dharmas</s> are accessible to reasoning' — only some are accessible to reasoning, not all. Those that fall within the domain of a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge alone are not accessible to reasoning — this is the intent.

body.text: (II.48cd) cittaviprayuktaprabhedavivakṣayā idam upanyasyate. atha kiṃ pratisaṃyuktā iti vistaraḥ. kasmin dhātau pratisaṃyuktāḥ kiṃ pratisaṃyuktāḥ.
body.translated_text: (II.48cd) This is presented with the intention of discussing the varieties of <s>cittaviprayukta</s> (mind-dissociated factors). 'Now, what are they associated with?' — and so forth in detail. In which realm (<s>dhātu</s>) are they associated? What are they associated with?

body.text: sattvākhyā asattvākhyā iti kiṃ iti.
body.translated_text: 'Designated as sentient (<s>sattvākhya</s>) or non-sentient (<s>asattvākhya</s>)?' — what [is meant]?

children.translated_text: 'Those designated as sentient, obtained in <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Rūpa</s> [realms], outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>), and indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>)' —

body.text: iti. kāmarūpāptā [Tib. 172b] eva sattvākhyā eva niṣyandā evāvyākṛtā eva cety avadhāraṇaṃ. te tv anabhilāpyā iti. te tv ārūpyāptā nāmakāyādayo 'kathyā vācas tatrābhāvāt. kathaṃ te santīti gamyaṃte. yadā te nābhilapyante. tasmāt kāmarūpāptā eva nārūpyāptā iti vaibhāṣikāḥ. sattvākhyā eva ca sattvaprayatnābhinirvṛttavarṇādisvabhāvatvāt. yaś ca dyotayati. sa taiḥ samanvāgata iti. kutaḥ. punar iyam āśaṃkā. anyonyasya taiḥ samanvāgamaḥ syād iti. asyedaṃ nāmeti vyapadeśāt. yathā cakṣurindriyeṇa draṣṭaiva samanvāgato na dṛśyaḥ sattvaḥ. tathā dyotayitaiva taiḥ samanvāgato na dyotyaḥ. naiṣyandikāḥ sabhāgahetujanitatvāt. na vipākajā icchātaḥ pravṛtteḥ. naupacayikā arūpiṇāṃ cayābhāvād iti. anivṛtāvyākṛtāś ca. na kuśalā nākuśalāḥ. kasmāt. samucchinnakuśalamūlakāmavītarāgāṇām api tatsamanvāgamaprasaṃgāt. itarathā hi yadā samucchinnakuśalamūlaḥ kuśalān dharmān dyotayati. tadāsya kuśaladharmasamanvāgamaḥ syāt. evaṃ kāmavītarāgasyāpy akuśaladharmadyotane yojyaṃ. tasmād anivṛtāvyākṛtā eva. anivṛtāvyākṛtānāṃ kuśalākuśalair avirodhāt.
body.translated_text: the emphasis is: obtained only in the <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Rūpa</s> [realms], designated only as sentient, only as outflow, and only as indeterminate. 'But they are inexpressible' — those <s>nāmakāyas</s> (name-groups) and the rest obtained in the Formless Realm (<s>ārūpya</s>) are unspeakable, because speech does not exist there. How then are they known to exist, when they are not expressed? Therefore [they exist] only in the <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Rūpa</s> [realms], not in the Formless — so say the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>. And they are designated as sentient only, because their nature consists of phonemes and the like produced by the effort of sentient beings. And the one who illuminates [meaning] is endowed with them. From where [comes] this further doubt? [The doubt is] that there might be mutual endowment with them. [This is resolved] by the designation 'this is its name.' Just as one endowed with the eye-faculty is the seer, not the visible being, so too the illuminator is endowed with them, not the illuminated. They are of the nature of outflow (<s>naiṣyandika</s>), being produced by homogeneous causes (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>). They are not maturation-born (<s>vipākaja</s>), because they arise from volition. They are not from accumulation (<s>aupacayika</s>), because formless beings have no accumulation. And they are unobstructed-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>) — neither wholesome nor unwholesome. Why? Because otherwise there would be the unwanted consequence that even those who have cut off wholesome roots or who are free from desire in the <s>Kāma</s> realm would be endowed with them. For if it were otherwise, when one who has cut off wholesome roots illuminates wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, he would then be endowed with wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Similarly, this should be applied to one free from <s>Kāma</s> desire illuminating unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore they are only unobstructed-indeterminate, since unobstructed-indeterminate factors do not conflict with either wholesome or unwholesome ones.

body.text: tathāśabdena sattvākhyanaiṣyandikāvyākṛtatvam eva sabhāgatāyā atidiśyate. tridhātvāptāyā apavādarūpeṇa vakṣyamāṇatvāt.
body.translated_text: By the word 'similarly,' the properties of being designated as sentient, being of outflow nature, and being indeterminate are extended to <s>sabhāgatā</s> (homogeneous class). Because the fact that it is obtained in all three realms will be stated [later] by way of exception.

body.text: iti. tuśabdo viśeṣaṇārthaḥ. nāmakāyādibhyo hi sabhāgatā viśiṣyate. katham ity āha.
body.translated_text: the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) serves to indicate a distinguishing quality. For <s>sabhāgatā</s> is distinguished from <s>nāmakāya</s> and the rest. How? He says:

body.text: vipākajāpīty arthaḥ. na kevalam iyaṃ naiṣyandikī. kiṃ tarhi. vipākajāpīti. na tv aupacayikī tathaiva cayābhāvāt.
body.translated_text: The meaning is: it is also maturation-born (<s>vipākaja</s>). Not only is this an outflow-effect (<s>naiṣyandikī</s>); rather, it is also maturation-born. But it is not accumulative (<s>aupacayikī</s>), likewise because of the absence of accumulation.

body.text: dvidhāśabdena naiṣyaṃdikavipākajatvaprabhedāv eva prāptīnām ucyete. prabhedāntarasyoktatvāt.
body.translated_text: by the word 'twofold,' only the distinction of being an outflow-effect and being maturation-born is stated regarding <s>prāpti</s>s, because the other distinction has already been stated.

body.text: jātyādīnāṃ tāv eva prabhedāv evam eva vaktavyau.
body.translated_text: of birth (<s>jāti</s>) and the rest, those very same two distinctions should be stated in the same way.

body.text: 'prāptiḥ. sānivṛtāvyākṛtāpi na vipākajā. na hi vipākasyāpy asamanvāgamo vipāko bhavitum arhati. tathā hy akuśalasya kuśalasāsravasya ca vipāka iṣyate. na cānayor aprāptir vipāko bhavitum arhati. yo hi buddhipūrvakaś cetanātmakas tatsaṃprayuktasamuttho vā dharmaḥ. sa vipākahetuḥ. na cāsamanvāgama
body.translated_text: [is also a] <s>prāpti</s>. Even though it is uncovered-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>), it is not maturation-born. For even the non-possession of maturation cannot qualify as maturation. For maturation is accepted of the unwholesome and of the wholesome-with-outflow. And non-possession of these two cannot qualify as their maturation. For a <s>dharma</s> that is preceded by deliberate intention, that has volition as its nature, or that arises from association with it — that is a maturation-cause (<s>vipākahetu</s>). But non-possession

body.text: evaṃ buddhipūrvakakarṃakṛta iti ato na vipākajaḥ. śeṣam eṣāṃ vaktavyam uktam iti. eṣāṃ prāptilakṣaṇasamāpattyasamanvāgamānāṃ vaktavyaṃ vyākhyātavyam uktaṃ vyākhyātam ity arthaḥ. [Tib. 173b] kiṃ punas tac cheṣam iti. dhātvāptatā sattvāsattvākhyatā kuśalākuśalavyākṛtatā ca. kathaṃ punas tad uktaṃ. prāptes tāvad dhātvāptatoktā
body.translated_text: is not thus produced by deliberate action; therefore it is not maturation-born. 'The remainder concerning these has been stated' — the meaning is: what should be explained regarding these — <s>prāpti</s>, characteristics, attainments, and non-possession — has been explained. [Tib. 173b] What then is that remainder? Their realm-belonging, being-designation or non-being-designation, and wholesome-unwholesome-indeterminate status. How then was that stated? First, the realm-belonging of <s>prāpti</s> was stated —

children.translated_text: 'Of those attained in that [realm], belonging to one's own realm' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. sattvākhyatoktā samanvāgamavacanāt. na hy asattvasaṃkhyātena saṃskṛtena santi samanvāgamāḥ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Its being-designation was stated by the statement regarding possession (<s>samanvāgama</s>). For there are no possessions of conditioned [<s>dharma</s>s] not counted as beings.

children.translated_text: '<s>Prāpti</s> and <s>aprāpti</s> [apply] to those belonging to one's own continuum' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. kathaṃ kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtatoktā.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. How was the wholesome-unwholesome-indeterminate status stated?

children.translated_text: 'Of the wholesome and the rest, [<s>prāpti</s> is] wholesome and the rest' —

body.text: vacanāt. lakṣaṇānām api traidhātukapratisaṃyuktatoktā
body.translated_text: because of this statement. The three-realm-belonging of the characteristics also was stated —

body.text: iti vacanāt. sattvāsattvākhyatāpy ata evoktā. sarvasaṃskṛtasahabhūtvāt. ata eva ca kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtatāpy uktā.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Their being-or-non-being-designation was also stated for this very reason — because of being co-arising with all conditioned [<s>dharma</s>s]. For this very reason, their wholesome-unwholesome-indeterminate status was also stated.

children.text:
caittā dvau saṃvarau teṣāṃ cetaso lakṣaṇāni ca
cittānuvartinaḥ kālaphalādiśubhatādibhir
children.translated_text:
'Mental factors, the two restraints, their characteristics of mind,
following mind — by time, fruit, and so forth, wholesomeness and so forth' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. asaṃjñisamāpatte rūpadhātvāptatoktā
body.translated_text: because of this statement. The realm-belonging of the non-perception attainment (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>) to the form realm was stated —

body.text: iti vacanāt. kuśalatāpi
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Its wholesomeness also [was stated] —

body.text: vacanāt. sattvākhyatāpy ata
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Its being-designation also, for this reason —

body.text: vacanāt. nirodhasamāpatter apy ārūpyadhātvāptatoktā
body.translated_text: because of this statement. The realm-belonging of the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) to the formless realm was also stated —

body.text: vacanāt. kuśalatāpi
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Its wholesomeness also —

body.text: vacanāt. sattvākhyatāpi ata eva. kuśalasaṃskṛtatvāt. asamanvāgamasya tridhātvāptatoktā
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Its being-designation also, for this very reason — because of being wholesome and conditioned. The three-realm-belonging of non-possession (<s>asamanvāgama</s>) was stated —

children.translated_text: 'Of those attained in the desire [realm] and the rest, and of the non-outflow' —

body.text: Tib. 174a
body.translated_text: Tib. 174a

body.text: vacanāt. sattvākhyatā samanvāgamavacanāt. avyākṛtatāpy uktā
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Its being-designation [was stated] by the statement regarding possession. Its indeterminate status was also stated —

body.text: iti vacanāt. śeṣayoś cāsaṃjñikajīvitayoḥ. kiṃ. vaktavyam uktam iti vartate. āsaṃjñikasya rūpāptasattvākhyavipākāvyākṛtatoktā
body.translated_text: because of this statement. And of the remaining two — the <s>āsaṃjñika</s> (non-perceptive state) and life-faculty (<s>jīvita</s>) — what? 'What should be stated has been stated' — this is the continuation. The realm-belonging, being-designation, and maturation-indeterminate status of the <s>āsaṃjñika</s> was stated as belonging to form, being-designation, and maturation-indeterminate —

children.translated_text: 'Those of great fruit are their maturation' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. jīvitasya tridhātvāptatoktā
body.translated_text: because of this statement. The three-realm-belonging of the life-faculty was stated —

body.text: iti vacanāt. āyuṣaś ca traidhātukatvāt. sattvākhyatāpy uktā
body.translated_text: because of this statement — and because lifespan belongs to all three realms. Its being-designation was also stated —

body.text: iti sūtrāt. vipāko hi sattvākhya eva
body.translated_text: from this <s>sūtra</s>. For maturation is exclusively being-designation —

children.translated_text: 'Maturation is an indeterminate <s>dharma</s>, being-designated, born from the determinate' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. ata evāsyānivṛtāvyākṛtatāpy ukteti. ācāryeṇa tu yad darśanaṃ vaktavyam uktaṃ. tad vivṛtaṃ. kathaṃ prāptādīnāṃ sattvākhyatoktā. samanvāgamavacanād ityādi.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Therefore its uncovered-indeterminate status was also stated. But the Master's view — what should be stated has been stated — that has been elucidated: how the being-designation of <s>prāpti</s> and the rest was stated — by the statement regarding possession, and so forth.

body.text: (II.50) ka ime hetavaḥ ke ca pratyayā iti. hetūnāṃ pratyayānāṃ ca kaḥ prativiśeṣaḥ. na kaścid ity āha. tathā hy uktaṃ bhagavatā. dvau hetū dvau pratyayau samyagdṛṣṭer utpādāya. katamau dvau. parataś ca ghoṣo 'dhyātmaṃ ca yoniśomanaskāra iti. hetuḥ pratyayo nidānaṃ kāraṇaṃ nimittaṃ liṃgaṃ upaniṣad iti paryāyāḥ. upaniṣacchabdas tu kadācid upāṃśau kadācit prāmukhya iti. tadyathāpi sūryopaniṣado devā iti. upāṃśuprayoga upaniṣatprayoga [Tib. 174b] iti. yadi prativiśeṣo nāsti kim arthaṃ hetūnāṃ pratyayānāṃ ca pṛthagnirdeśaḥ. anyenārthaviśeṣeṇa hetunirdeśo 'nyena pratyayanirdeśaḥ. hetunirdeśe hi avighnabhāvasahabhūtvasadṛśatvādir arthaviśeṣa uktaḥ. pratyayanirdeśe tu hetusamanantaratvādibhir aparo 'rthaviśeṣa ukta iti. atha katamasmin sūtre ṣaḍ ḍhetava uktāḥ. sarvo hy abhidharmaḥ sūtrārthaḥ sūtranikaṣaḥ sūtravyākhyānam iti. aṃtarhitaṃ tat sūtram iti vaibhāṣikāḥ. tathā hi ekottarikāgama ā śatād dharmanirdeśa āsīt. idānīṃ tv ā daśakād dṛśyaṃta iti kathayanti. api tu saṃti pratiniyatahetuvācakāni sūtrāṇi. tāny udāhariṣyāmaḥ. cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpāṇi cotpadyate cakṣurvijñānam iti kāraṇahetuḥ. jananāvighnabhāvena hy eṣa vyavasthāpyate. imāni trīṇi mārgāṃgāni samyagdṛṣṭim anuparivartante. taiḥ saha jātā vedanā saṃjñā cetanā ceti sahabhūhetuḥ. anyonyānuparivartanaikakṛtyārthena hy eṣa vyavasthāpyate. samanvāgato 'yaṃ pudgalaḥ kuśalair api dharmair akuśalair api yāvad asti cāsyāṇusahagataṃ kuśalamūlam asamucchinnaṃ yato 'sya kuśalamūlād anyat kuśalamūlam utpatsyate
body.translated_text: (II.50) 'What are these causes (<s>hetu</s>) and what are the conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>)?' — what is the distinction between causes and conditions? There is none — he says. For thus it was stated by the Blessed One: 'Two causes, two conditions [lead] to the arising of right view. What two? The voice of another and wise attention (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>).' <s>Hetu</s> (cause), <s>pratyaya</s> (condition), <s>nidāna</s> (source), <s>kāraṇa</s> (reason), <s>nimitta</s> (sign), <s>liṅga</s> (mark), <s>upaniṣad</s> (basis) — these are synonyms. But the word <s>upaniṣad</s> sometimes [means] 'in a whisper' and sometimes 'pre-eminence.' For example, 'the gods have the sun as their <s>upaniṣad</s>' — [Tib. 174b] a whispered usage, an <s>upaniṣad</s> usage. If there is no distinction, for what purpose is there a separate exposition of causes and conditions? The exposition of causes [is made] with one particular meaning, and the exposition of conditions with another. For in the exposition of causes, the specific meanings of non-obstruction, co-existence, similarity, and so forth were stated. But in the exposition of conditions, another specific meaning was stated through immediate succession and the like. 'Now in which <s>sūtra</s> are the six causes stated?' For all <s>Abhidharma</s> is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>s, tested against the <s>sūtra</s>s, and an explanation of the <s>sūtra</s>s. 'That <s>sūtra</s> has been lost' — say the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s. For thus, in the <s>Ekottarikāgama</s>, the exposition of <s>dharma</s>s extended up to a hundred; but now they are seen only up to ten — so they say. However, there are <s>sūtra</s>s that speak of specific causes. We shall cite them. 'Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises' — this is the efficient cause (<s>kāraṇahetu</s>), for it is established through the sense of non-obstruction to production. 'These three path-factors follow right view; feeling, perception, and volition are born together with them' — this is the co-existent cause (<s>sahabhūhetu</s>), for it is established through the sense of mutual accompaniment and single function. 'This person is endowed with both wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s, and there exists in him a minute accompanying wholesome root that has not been cut off, from which wholesome root another wholesome root will arise

body.text: . evam ayaṃ pudgala āyatyāṃ viśuddhidharmā bhaviṣyatīti sabhāgahetuḥ. eṣa hy atītapratyutpannānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ svaphalanirvartanārthena vyavasthāpyate. iyam ucyate darśanamūlikā śraddhāvetyajñānasaṃprayuktā. yad vijānāti. tat [Tib. 175a] prajānātīti saṃprayuktakahetuḥ. ekālaṃbanakṛtyārthena hy eṣa vyavasthāpyate. mithyādṛṣṭeḥ puruṣapudgalasya yac ca kāyakarma taddṛṣṭer yac ca vākkarma yā cetanā yaḥ praṇidhiḥ ye ca saṃskārās tadanvayāḥ. sarve 'py ete dharmā aniṣṭatvāya saṃvartante 'kāntatvāyāpriyatvāyāmanaāpatvāya. tat kasya hetoḥ. dṛṣṭir hy asya pāpikā yad uta mithyādṛṣṭir iti sarvatragahetuḥ. eṣa hi sabhāgavisabhāgakliṣṭadharmaprabaṃdhajanakārthena vyavasthāpyate. iha kṛtasya karmaṇaḥ kuśalasya sāsravasya bhāvanāmayasya tatrotpannā vipākaṃ pratisaṃvedayante. saṃcetanīyasya karmaṇaḥ kṛtasyopacitasya vipāka iti vipākahetuḥ. eṣa hi visadṛśaphalākṣepakatvena vyavasthāpyate. ity ata ete ṣaḍ ḍhetavaḥ sūtrata eva prasiddhā iti
body.translated_text: . Thus this person will in the future become one whose nature tends toward purification' — this is the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>), for it is established for the purpose of producing their own fruits from past and present <s>dharma</s>s. 'This is called faith rooted in insight, associated with understanding-knowledge. What one cognizes, [Tib. 175a] that one discerns' — this is the associated cause (<s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s>), for it is established through the sense of having a single object and single function. 'Whatever bodily action [arises] from the wrong view of a person, whatever verbal action, whatever volition, whatever aspiration, and whatever formations follow from it — all these <s>dharma</s>s conduce to what is undesired, unpleasant, disagreeable, and unwelcome. For what reason? Because his view is evil, namely wrong view' — this is the universally pervasive cause (<s>sarvatragahetu</s>), for it is established for the purpose of generating the continuum of homogeneous, non-homogeneous, and afflicted <s>dharma</s>s. 'Of action performed here, wholesome, with outflows, produced by cultivation, those born there experience the maturation. The maturation of intentional action performed and accumulated' — this is the maturation cause (<s>vipākahetu</s>), for it is established through the sense of projecting a dissimilar fruit. Therefore these six causes are established from the <s>sūtra</s>s themselves —

body.text: vaibhāṣikair ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: the intent is: by the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s.

body.text: iti ātmano 'nya ity arthaḥ. svātmani vṛttivirodhāt svātmā na hetuḥ. sarvadharmāḥ saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtāḥ kāraṇahetur iti. kāraṇam eva hetuḥ kāraṇahetuḥ. yo hetur viśeṣasaṃjñayā nocyate sāmānyaṃ hetubhāvaṃ parigṛhyocyate. sa kāraṇahetuḥ. anyeṣu hi viśeṣasaṃjñānirukteṣu hetuṣu yo na viśeṣitaḥ kāraṇaṃ ca. tasya tad viśeṣaṇaṃ bhavati. yathā rūpāyatanam uktam iti. [Tib. 175b] utpādaṃ praty avighnabhāvāvasthānād iti. yasmād utpādaṃ praty utpattimatāṃ svato 'nye dharmā avighnabhāvenāvatiṣṭhante. tasmāt kāraṇahetur ity ucyate.
body.translated_text: the meaning is: other than oneself. Because of the contradiction of operating upon oneself, one's own self is not a cause. 'All <s>dharma</s>s, conditioned and unconditioned, are the efficient cause (<s>kāraṇahetu</s>).' The cause that is simply a cause is the efficient cause. That cause which is not designated by a specific name but is stated as grasping the general status of being a cause — that is the efficient cause. For among the other causes designated by specific etymologies, that which is not specified [by a special name] and is [simply] a cause — that specification becomes its qualifier. Just as 'the form sense-base' was stated. [Tib. 175b] 'Because of the state of non-obstruction toward arising' — because <s>dharma</s>s other than itself abide in a state of non-obstruction toward the arising of whatever has the capacity to arise, therefore it is called the efficient cause.

body.text: nanu ca ye 'syājānata iti vistaraḥ. jñānaṃ cen nodayanty ete. udapatsyanta āsravās ta iti vistaro lṛṅy arthaḥ. tenāha. asyājānataḥ anutpannadarśanabhāvanāmārgapudgalasya ye darśanabhāvanāmārgavadhyā rāgādaya āsravā udapatsyaṃta. jānata utpannadarśanadarśanabhāvanāmārgasya pudgalasyāsya tadvadhyās te rāgādayo notpadyante. tataḥ kim ity āha. jñānam eṣāṃ vighnam utpattau karoti darśanabhāvanāmārgasaṃgṛhītaṃ. sūryaprabhā ca jyotiṣāṃ darśanasya vighnam utpattau karotīty adhikṛtaṃ. evaṃ sati kathaṃ svabhāvavarjyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ saṃskṛtasya kāraṇahetur bhavaṃti. yasmād āsravotpattau na jñānaṃ kāraṇahetuḥ. jyotirdarśanotpattau ca sūryaprabhā. evaṃ hi vaktavyaṃ syāt. āsravotpattau svabhāvajñānavarjyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ kāraṇahetuḥ.
body.translated_text: 'But those which, when he does not know' — thus the elaboration. 'If knowledge does not impel them, those outflows would arise' — the elaboration has a conditional past tense meaning. Therefore he says: for this person in whom the paths of insight and cultivation have not arisen, those outflows such as desire and the rest, destroyable by the paths of insight and cultivation, would arise. For this person who knows — in whom the paths of insight and cultivation have arisen — those outflows such as desire and the rest, destroyable by them, do not arise. What follows from that? He says: knowledge creates an obstruction to the arising of these [outflows] — [knowledge] included in the paths of insight and cultivation. And sunlight creates an obstruction to the arising of the perception of luminous objects — this is what is under discussion. This being so, how can all <s>dharma</s>s, excluding [their own] nature, be the efficient cause of the conditioned? Since knowledge is not the efficient cause in the arising of outflows, nor sunlight in the arising of the perception of luminous objects. For one would have to say: all <s>dharma</s>s excluding [their own] nature and knowledge are the efficient cause in the arising of outflows

body.text: jyotirdarśanotpattau ca svabhāvasūryaprabhāvarjyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ kāraṇahetur iti. utpadyamānasyāvighnabhāvāvasthānād iti. samagreṣu hetupratyayeṣu anantarabhāvī dharma utpadyamāna ucyate. tasyotpadyamānasyotpādaṃ prati sarvadharmā evāvighnabhāvenāvatiṣṭhaṃte. na sarvasyety avagaṃtavyaṃ. jñāne punaḥ sati ta āsravā notpadyamānā bhavaṃti. prāptyādyabhāvena pratyayasāmagryabhāvāt. jyotirdarśanam api pratyayavaikalyād eva [Tib. 176a] notpadyamānam iti yojyaṃ. atas tadavastham idaṃ svabhāvavarjyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ saṃskṛtasya kāraṇahetur bhavaṃtīti. tadyathānupadrotāraṃ bhojakam iti vistaraḥ. anupadravakaraṃ grāmapatim abhisaṃdhāya manuṣyā brūyuḥ. svāminā smaḥ sukhitā iti. kasmāt ta evaṃ vaktāro bhavanti. yasmād asāv upadravakaraṇe samartha upadravaṃ na karoti. tadyathā nirvāṇasyānutpattidharmāṇāṃ ca. kiṃ. kathaṃ hetubhāvaḥ sarvotpattau. nārakādīnāṃ ca nārakatiryagyonyādikānām ārūpyaskaṃdhotpattau kathaṃ hetubhāvaḥ. nārakādigrahaṇaṃ manuṣyādīnāṃ kadācid bhavet upadeśādinety abhiprāyaḥ. asaṃto 'pi hi eva iti. asaṃto 'pi hy ete nirvāṇādayas tathaiva. yathā saṃto vidyamānā vighnaṃ kartum asamarthāḥ syuḥ. ato 'satāṃ satāṃ caiṣām nirvāṇādīnāṃ vighnakaraṇe nirviśiṣṭatvaṃ. asattulyās ta ity arthaḥ. asamarthe 'pīti vistaraḥ. upadravaṃ kartum asamarthe 'pi bhojake grāmīṇās tathā vaktāro bhavanti. svāminā smaḥ sukhitā iti. sa evātra dṛṣṭānto yaḥ prāktanaḥ. ato 'nenaiva dṛṣṭāṃtena vighnayitum asamarthānām api nirvāṇādīnām avighnabhāvāvasthānāt kāraṇahetubhāvaḥ siddhaḥ. kasmāt punar asattulyānāṃ nirvāṇādīnāṃ kāraṇahetutvam [Tib. 176b] iṣyate. na punar asatāṃ śaśaviṣāṇādīnāṃ. asaddṛṣṭāṃtābhāvāt. na hy asantaṃ bhojakam adhikṛtya grāmīṇā bhavaṃti vaktāraḥ. svāminā smaḥ sukhitā iti. na vā śaśaviṣāṇena smaḥ sukhitā iti. acodyam etat. sāmānyena eva nirdeśaḥ iti. yaś ca pradhānaḥ kāraṇahetur yaś cāpradhānaḥ sarvam adhikṛtyoktaṃ.
body.translated_text: and all <s>dharma</s>s excluding [their own] nature and sunlight are the efficient cause in the arising of the perception of luminous objects. 'Because of the state of non-obstruction toward what is about to arise' — a <s>dharma</s> that will come into being immediately when the causes and conditions are complete is called 'about to arise.' Toward the arising of that which is about to arise, all <s>dharma</s>s simply abide in a state of non-obstruction. But it should be understood: not toward everything. When knowledge is present, those outflows do not become 'about to arise' — because of the absence of the completeness of conditions due to the absence of <s>prāpti</s> and the like. The perception of luminous objects too should be construed as not about to arise precisely because of the deficiency of conditions. [Tib. 176a] Therefore this stands as it is: all <s>dharma</s>s, excluding [their own] nature, are the efficient cause of the conditioned. 'Just as a chieftain who causes no harm' — thus the elaboration. With reference to a village chief who causes no harm, people would say: 'We are happy under our lord.' Why do they say thus? Because he, though capable of causing harm, causes no harm. Just like <s>nirvāṇa</s> and those <s>dharma</s>s whose nature is non-arising — what? How can there be causal status for the arising of everything? And how can there be causal status of hell-beings and the like — of hell-beings, animals, and the like — for the arising of formless-realm aggregates? The intent is that the inclusion of hell-beings and the like might sometimes serve as instruction for humans and the like. 'For even non-existent [<s>dharma</s>s] — just so.' For even these non-existent [<s>dharma</s>s] such as <s>nirvāṇa</s> and the rest are just so — just as existing ones would be incapable of creating obstruction. Therefore, of these non-existent and existent [<s>dharma</s>s] — <s>nirvāṇa</s> and the rest — there is no distinction regarding the creation of obstruction. The meaning is: they are equal to the non-existent. 'Even of one incapable' — thus the elaboration. Even when the chieftain is incapable of causing harm, the villagers still say thus: 'We are happy under our lord.' This is the same illustration as before. Therefore, by this very illustration, even for <s>nirvāṇa</s> and the rest, which are incapable of obstructing, their efficient-cause status is established because of their state of non-obstruction. 'But why is efficient-cause status [Tib. 176b] accepted for <s>nirvāṇa</s> and the rest, which are equal to the non-existent, but not for non-existent things like a hare's horns and the like?' Because there is no illustration of a non-existent [chieftain]. For villagers would not speak with reference to a non-existent chieftain, saying 'We are happy under our lord'; nor 'We are happy with the hare's horn.' This is not a valid objection. The exposition is simply general — whatever efficient cause is primary and whatever is non-primary, the statement was made with reference to all.

body.text: iti. yo hi pradhāno janakaḥ. sa kāraṇahetuḥ. sa sutarām avighnabhāvenāvatiṣṭhate na kevalam itaraḥ. āhāraḥ śarīrasyotpādane 'pi samartha ity adhikṛtaṃ. āhārasamudayāt kāyasamudaya iti vacanāt. rasādipariṇāmayogāt. bījādayo '; ṃkurādīnām iti. bījāṃkuranālagaṇḍaprasavādīnāṃ utpādane samarthā ity evaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. For the principal generator — that is the <s>kāraṇahetu</s>. It remains in a non-obstructive manner all the more so, not just the other [cause]. 'Food is also capable of producing the body' — this has been stated, because of the statement 'from the arising of food, the arising of the body.' Because of the connection with the transformation of taste and so forth. 'Seeds and the like [are causes] of sprouts and the like' — seeds are capable of producing sprouts, stalks, knots, blossoms, and so forth — thus.

body.text: yas tv evaṃ codayatīti vistaraḥ. kāraṇe sati kāryeṇa bhavitavyam iti matvā codayati. kasmān na sarvasyotpādo yugapad bhavati. yathā ca prāṇātipātakārakaḥ prāṇātipātabhāg bhavati. tathā sarve 'pi kasmān na tadbhājo bhavaṃtīti.
body.translated_text: 'But one who objects thus...' — thus the elaboration. Thinking 'when there is a cause, the effect must follow,' he objects: 'why does not everything arise simultaneously? And just as the one who commits killing (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>) is a participant in killing, why are not all others also participants?'

body.text: na kārakabhāveneti. na mukhyavṛttyāsya kāraṇatvam iti darśayati. tena sarvasya tāvad yugapad utpādo na prāpnoti. pratyayasāmagryabhāvenānutpādyamānatvāt. prāṇātipātayogaś ca na bhavaty akārakatvāt. yas tu kārakaḥ. sa prāṇātipātabhāg eva bhavati.
body.translated_text: 'Not in the capacity of an agent' — he shows that its causality is not in the primary sense. Therefore, first, the simultaneous arising of everything does not follow, because [things] are not produced in the absence of a complete assemblage of conditions. And the connection with killing does not apply, because of not being an agent. But whoever is the agent — he alone is a participant in killing.

body.text: manovijñānam utpadyate kuśalākuśalam iti. kuśalaṃ manovijñanam iti nirvāṇālaṃbanatvāt. nirvāṇālaṃbanāt [Tib. 177a] kuśalād akuśalād vā manovijñānam utpadyate. tataś cakṣurvijñānam iti. evaṃ paraṃparayā tasyāpi nirvāṇasya pratyayībhāvād asti sāmarthyaṃ. kva. cakṣurvijñāna ity adhikṛtaṃ. evam anyasyāpi pratipattavyam iti. nārakādīnām apy ārūpyaskaṃdhotpattau sāmarthyaṃ. katham. amī bata nārakapretādayaḥ paramaduḥkhitā iti nārakādyālaṃbanaṃ manovijñānaṃ kuśalam utpadyate. yataḥ krameṇa śīle vyavasthitasya bhāvanāyāṃ prayogāt ārūpyasamāpattir upapattiś copayadyata. iti.
body.translated_text: 'A mental consciousness arises that is wholesome or unwholesome' — a wholesome mental consciousness, because of having <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as its object. From a wholesome or unwholesome [mental consciousness] that has <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as its object, [Tib. 177a] a mental consciousness arises. 'Then a visual consciousness [arises]' — thus, through succession, since even that <s>Nirvāṇa</s> becomes a condition, there is efficacy. Where? With respect to visual consciousness — this has been stated. 'The same should be understood for others as well' — even hell-beings and the like have the capacity for the arising of formless-realm aggregates. How? 'Alas, these hell-beings, <s>preta</s>s, and the like are supremely suffering' — thus a wholesome mental consciousness arises with hell-beings, etc. as its object. From which, gradually, for one established in morality, through the application of cultivation, a formless attainment and rebirth arise.

body.text: (II.51b-d)

children.translated_text: 'The <s>sahabhūhetu</s> (co-existent cause) is [that whose products are] mutually fruits' —

body.translated_text: (II.51b-d)

body.text: iti. hetur iti vartate. sahabhūr hetus te dharmā bhavaṃti. ye dharmā mithaḥphalā ye parasparaphalā ity arthaḥ. sahabhūhetuḥ sahabhuva iti noktaṃ. kasmāt. saṃti hi dharmāḥ kecit sahabhuvo na tu sahabhūhetuḥ. tadyathā nīlādyupādāyarūpaṃ bhūtaiḥ sahabhūr bhavati. na cānyonyaṃ sahabhūhetuḥ. ato
body.translated_text: thus. The word 'cause' (<s>hetu</s>) carries over. Those <s>dharma</s>s that are mutually fruits — whose fruits are reciprocal — they become <s>sahabhūhetu</s>s (co-existent causes). It is not said '<s>sahabhūhetu</s> is a co-existent.' Why? Because there are some <s>dharma</s>s that are co-existent but not <s>sahabhūhetu</s>s. For example, secondary form such as blue and the like is co-existent with the primary elements, but they are not reciprocally <s>sahabhūhetu</s>s. Therefore,

body.text: ity arthaparigrahaḥ. idaṃ ca sāvaśeṣaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ. ato vakṣyati. vināpi cānyonyaphalatvena dharmo 'nulakṣaṇānāṃ sababhūhetuḥ. na tāni tasyety upasaṃkhyātavyam iti. upasaṃkhyānakaraṇaṃ ca mahāśāstratāpradarśanārthaṃ. sopasaṃkhyānaṃ hi vyākaraṇādi mahāśāstram dṛśyate.
body.translated_text: this is the delimitation of meaning. And this definition is incomplete (<s>sāvaśeṣa</s>). Therefore he will say: 'even without mutual fruitfulness, a <s>dharma</s> is a <s>sahabhūhetu</s> of the sub-characteristics; but those are not [<s>sahabhūhetu</s>s] of it — this should be added.' And the making of this addition is for the purpose of demonstrating the greatness of the treatise. For a treatise with additions, like grammar and so forth, is seen to be a great treatise.

body.text: iti. tadyathārthe vatipratyayaḥ. evaṃ ca kṛtvā sarvam eva saṃskṛtaṃ sahabhūhetur yathāyogam iti. [Tib. 177b] yasmāt saṃskṛtalakṣaṇāni lakṣyasya sahabhūhetuḥ. so 'pi teṣām. ato yathāyogaṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ sarvaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ sahabhūhetuḥ saṃskṛtasya lakṣaṇavattvāt. lakṣyalakṣayoś ca sahabhūhetutvāt. na tu sarvaṃ sarvasya. anyalakṣaṇair asahabhūhetutvād iti yathāyogagrahaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. The suffix <s>vati</s> is in the sense of 'just as.' Having done so, all conditioned [things] are <s>sahabhūhetu</s>s as appropriate — [Tib. 177b] because the conditioned characteristics are <s>sahabhūhetu</s>s of the characterized, and that [characterized] is [a <s>sahabhūhetu</s>] of those [characteristics]. Therefore, as appropriate and as possible, all conditioned [things] are <s>sahabhūhetu</s>s of the conditioned, because of possessing characteristics. And because the characterized and characteristics are mutually <s>sahabhūhetu</s>s. But not everything [is a <s>sahabhūhetu</s>] of everything — because of not being a <s>sahabhūhetu</s> with the characteristics of another [dharma]. Hence the qualification 'as appropriate.'

body.text: (II.52a-c)

children.text: teṣāṃ ca ye jātyādayaś cittasya ce
children.translated_text: 'And those birth, etc. of those [dharmas], and of the mind' —

children.text: ti. teṣāṃ ca cittasaṃprayuktānāṃ cetanādīnāṃ dhyānasaṃvarasyānāsravasaṃvarasya ye jātyādayaś catvāro dharmāś cittānuparivartina ucyante.
children.translated_text: thus. And of those mind-associated [factors] such as volition (<s>cetanā</s>) and the like, and of the <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint and the non-outflow restraint — the four <s>dharma</s>s beginning with birth that are said to follow the mind.

body.translated_text: (II.52a-c)

children.translated_text: 'by time, fruit, etc., and wholesomeness, etc.' —

body.text: iti. kālena ca phalādibhiś ca śubhatādibhiś ceti
body.translated_text: thus. 'By time, by fruit and the rest, and by wholesomeness and the rest' —

children.translated_text: 'by time, fruit, etc., and wholesomeness, etc.'

body.text: kālatas tāvad iti vistaraḥ. cittena sahaite ekotpādā ekasthitaya ekanirodhāś ca. tadbhāvaḥ. tayaikotpādasthitinirodhatayeti. ekam adhvānaṃ patitā ekādhvapatitāḥ. tadbhāvaḥ. tenaikādhvapatitatvena caturtheneti. kālataś cittam anuparivartante. ekaphalatayaikavipākatayaikaniṣyaṃdatayā ca cittam anuparivartante. phalam iha puruṣakāraphalaṃ visaṃyogaphalaṃ ca. vipākaphalaniṣyaṃdayoḥ pṛthaggṛhītatvāt. adhipatiphalaṃ tu sarvasādhāraṇatvāt. na gaṇyate. ayaṃ caikaśabdaḥ saṃkhyāne sādhāraṇe vā ekaphalatayetyādi [Tib. 178a]. pūrvakas tv ekaśabdaḥ sahārthe cittena sahotpādasthitinirodhatayety arthaḥ. na hy atra saṃkhyānārthaḥ saṃbhavati. na hi yaś cittasyotpādaḥ. sa eva cittānuparivartināṃ. yo vā teṣāṃ. sa cittasyeti. evaṃ daśabhiḥ kāraṇair iti. kālataś caturbhir ekotpādatayaikasthititayaikanirodhatayaikādhvapatitatvena ceti. nanu caikotpādasthitinirodhatayeti etenaiva ekādhvapatitam uktaṃ. na sarvam uktaṃ. anutpattikadharmiṇi hi citte te cittānuparivartina ekādhvapatitā bhavaṃti. naikotpādanirodhā iti. tasmād ekādhvapatitatvaṃ caturthaṃ kāraṇaṃ ucyate. ekaphalavipākaniṣyaṃdatayeti tribhiḥ. kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtatayā ceti punas tribhir iti daśabhiḥ. paryāyavṛttiṃ jātiṃ vā praty evam uktaṃ daśabhir iti. na hy ekatra citte daśa kāraṇāni bhavaṃti. na hi kuśale cetasi akuśalāvyākṛte kāraṇe bhavataḥ. na cākuśalāvyākṛte citte anutpattidharmiṇi. avyākṛte citte anutpattidharmiṇi ekādhvapatitatvena ekaphalaniṣyaṃdatābhyāṃ avyākṛtatvena ceti caturbhiḥ. utpattidharmiṇi tv ebhir eva caturbhir ekotpādasthitinirodhatābhiś ceti saptabhiḥ. anāsrave 'py evaṃ. avyākṛtatāṃ tu kevalam apanīya kuśalatā [Tib. 178b] prakṣeptavyā. akuśale tu kuśalasāsrave cānutpattikadharmiṇi akuśalatayā kuśalatayā ca yathāvastu ekādhvapatitatvena ekaphalavipākaniṣyandatābhis ceti paṃcabhiḥ. utpattidharmiṇi tu tasminn ebhir eva paṃcabhir ekotpādasthitinirodhatābhiś cety aṣṭābhiḥ.
body.translated_text: 'First, with respect to time' — thus the elaboration. These, together with mind, have the same arising, the same duration, and the same cessation. The state of that — by that identity of arising, duration, and cessation. 'Fallen into the same time-period' means 'fallen into the same temporal path' (<s>ekādhvapatita</s>). The state of that — by that identity of temporal path, as a fourth [criterion]. They follow the mind with respect to time. By identity of fruit, by identity of maturation, and by identity of outflow — they follow the mind. 'Fruit' here means the fruit of personal effort and the fruit of disconnection, since the maturation-fruit and outflow-fruit are mentioned separately. But the dominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>), being common to all, is not counted. This word 'one' (<s>eka</s>) [means] 'of the same [kind]' in counting or in commonality: 'by identity of fruit,' etc. [Tib. 178a] But the earlier [uses of] 'one' are in the sense of 'together' — 'by identity of arising, duration, and cessation with the mind.' For the meaning of counting is not possible here, since the arising of the mind is not identical to that of the mind-followers, nor theirs to the mind's. Thus by ten reasons: with respect to time, by four — identity of arising, identity of duration, identity of cessation, and identity of temporal path. 'But surely identity of arising, duration, and cessation already implies identity of temporal path?' — not everything is implied. For when the mind has the nature of not arising [again], the mind-followers are of the same temporal path but not of the same arising and cessation. Therefore identity of temporal path is stated as the fourth reason. By identity of fruit, maturation, and outflow — three. By wholesomeness, unwholesomeness, and indeterminacy — another three: thus ten. 'With respect to sequential occurrence or birth, it is stated thus: by ten' — for not all ten reasons apply to a single mind. For in a wholesome mind, the reasons of unwholesomeness and indeterminacy do not apply. Nor in an unwholesome or indeterminate mind [do all apply]. In an indeterminate mind that has the nature of not arising [again]: by identity of temporal path, by identity of fruit and outflow, and by indeterminacy — four. But in one that has the nature of arising: by those same four plus identity of arising, duration, and cessation — seven. In the non-outflow also, likewise — [Tib. 178b] only remove indeterminacy and add wholesomeness. But in the unwholesome and the wholesome-with-outflows, for one with the nature of not arising [again]: by unwholesomeness or wholesomeness respectively, by identity of temporal path, and by identity of fruit, maturation, and outflow — five. In one with the nature of arising: by those same five plus identity of arising, duration, and cessation — eight.

body.text: sarvālpaṃ cittam iti. sarvebhyo yad alpaparivāraṃ cittaṃ. tat sarvālpam ity ucyate. tat punaḥ katamat. dvitīyadhyānāt prabhṛti ūrdhvam anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ cittaṃ. tatra vitarkavicārau na staḥ. na cāpi kuśalādimahābhūmikāḥ. kevalamahābhūmikā eva daśa bhavanti. tallakṣaṇānām iti. daśamahābhūmikalakṣaṇānāṃ. na tadanulakṣaṇānāṃ viprakṛṣṭatvāt. svānulakṣaṇānāṃ tu bhavati
body.translated_text: 'The mind with the fewest of all [associates]' — the mind that has the smallest retinue among all [minds] is called 'fewest of all.' What is that? The uncovered-indeterminate mind from the second <s>dhyāna</s> upward. There, <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) do not exist, nor do the <s>mahābhūmika</s>s of the wholesome and other [groups]. Only the ten <s>mahābhūmika</s>s alone exist. 'Of the characteristics of those' — of the characteristics of the ten <s>mahābhūmika</s>s, not of their sub-characteristics, because of being distant. But of their own sub-characteristics, there is [a <s>sahabhūhetu</s> relation]

body.text: saṃnikṛṣṭatvāt. ata āha. aṣṭānāṃ ca svalakṣaṇānulakṣaṇānām iti. svāny anulakṣaṇāni sthāpayitveti. lakṣaṇeṣu anulakṣaṇānāṃ vyāpāraḥ. na viśiṣte ca citte. nyūnāni tāni. rājāyate hi cittaṃ lakṣaṇānulakṣaṇānām. atas cittam anulakṣaṇānāṃ sahabhūhetuḥ. na tu tāni cittasya. lakṣaṇānāṃ tu citte 'sti vyāpāra iti tāni cittasya sahabhūhetur bhavanti.
body.translated_text: because of proximity. Therefore he says: 'and of the eight own sub-characteristics.' 'Setting aside one's own sub-characteristics' — the sub-characteristics operate upon the characteristics, not upon the mind specifically. They are fewer in those [cases]. For the mind is like a king with respect to characteristics and sub-characteristics. Therefore the mind is a <s>sahabhūhetu</s> of the sub-characteristics, but those are not [<s>sahabhūhetu</s>s] of the mind. But the characteristics have an operation upon the mind — therefore they are <s>sahabhūhetu</s>s of the mind.

body.text: caturdaśety apara iti. yathānulakṣaṇānāṃ nāsti dharme vyāpāraḥ. kiṃ tarhi. dharmasya lakṣaṇeṣu. ato na teṣāṃ hetubhāvo dharma iṣyate. tathā saṃprayukteṣv eva tallakṣaṇānāṃ vyāpāraḥ. [Tib. 179a] na citta iti na tāni cittasya sahabhūhetuḥ. cittaṃ tu teṣāṃ rājakalpam iti sahabhūhetur bhavatīty apareṣām abhiprāyaḥ. prakaraṇagrantho hy evaṃ virudhyeta daśānāṃ mahābhūmikānāṃ yāni catvāriṃśal lakṣaṇāni. tāni yadi cittasya sahabhūhetur neṣyeran. yasmāt prakaraṇeṣūktaṃ. catvāry āryasatyāni duḥkhasatyaṃ yāvan mārgasatyaṃ. eṣāṃ kati satkāyadṛṣṭihetukāni na satkāyadṛṣṭer hetuḥ. kati satkāyadṛṣṭer hetur na saktkāyadṛṣṭihetukāni. kati satkāyadṛṣṭihetukāni satkāyadṛṣṭeś ca hetuḥ. kati naiva satkāyadṛṣṭihetukāni na satkāyadṛṣṭer hetuḥ iti praśne kṛte visarjanaṃ karoti. dve naiva satkāyadṛṣṭihetuke na satkāyadṛṣṭer hetuḥ. nirodhasatyaṃ mārgasatyaṃ ca. dvayor bhedaḥ. duḥkhasamudayasatyayor vibhaṃgaḥ. katham iti. duḥkhasatyaṃ syāt satkāyadṛṣṭihetukaṃ na satkāyadṛṣṭer hetuḥ. syāt satkāyadṛṣṭihetukaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭeś ca hetuḥ. syān naiva satkāyadṛṣṭihetukaṃ na satkāyaḍṛṣṭer hetur iti trikoṭikaṃ. dvitīyā koṭir nāsti. tatra satkāyadṛṣṭihetukaṃ na satkāyadṛṣṭer hetuḥ. atītapratyutpannān duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyān anuśayāṃs tatsaṃprayuktaṃ ca duḥkhasatyaṃ sthāpayitvā. [Tib. 179b] atītapratyutpannān samudayadarśanaprahātavyān sarvatragān anuśayān tatsaṃprayuktaṃ ca duḥkhasatyaṃ sthāpayitvā. anāgataṃ ca satkāyadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ sthāpayitvā. satkāyadṛṣṭes tatsaṃprayuktānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ jātiṃ jarāṃ sthitim anityatāṃ ca sthāpayitvā yat tad anyat kliṣṭaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ. satkāyadṛṣṭihetukaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭeś ca hetur yad etat sthāpitam iti. naiva satkāyahetukaṃ na satkāyadṛṣṭer hetur akliṣṭaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ. yathā duḥkhasatyaṃ evaṃ samudayasatyam iti prakaraṇagranthaḥ. tasyārthaṃ vivṛṇmahe. ye 'tītapratyutpannā duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyā daśānuśayāḥ satkāyadṛṣṭyādayaḥ. te sthāpitāḥ. tair daśabhir anuśayaiḥ saṃprayuktaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ vedanādikaṃ sthāpitaṃ. kim atrāsthāpitaṃ. eta evānāgatā daśānuśayās tatsaṃprayuktaṃ ca vedanādikaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ varjayitvānāgatasatkāyadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ. tad dhi
body.translated_text: 'Fourteen, according to others' — just as the sub-characteristics have no operation upon the <s>dharma</s> [itself] — rather, [their operation is upon] the characteristics of the <s>dharma</s> — therefore they are not accepted as having the status of cause with respect to the <s>dharma</s>. Similarly, the characteristics of the associated [factors] operate only upon the associated [factors], [Tib. 179a] not upon the mind — therefore those are not <s>sahabhūhetu</s>s of the mind. But the mind, being like a king, is their <s>sahabhūhetu</s> — this is the intent of the others. The <s>Prakaraṇa</s> treatise would be contradicted thus: if the forty characteristics of the ten <s>mahābhūmika</s>s were not accepted as <s>sahabhūhetu</s>s of the mind. Because in the <s>Prakaraṇa</s> texts it is stated: 'The four noble truths — the truth of suffering up to the truth of the path. Of these, how many are caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (identity-view) but not a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>? How many are a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> but not caused by it? How many are both caused by and a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>? How many are neither caused by nor a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>?' In response to this question: 'Two are neither caused by nor a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>: the truth of cessation and the truth of the path. Of the other two there is a division — of the truths of suffering and origination.' How? 'The truth of suffering may be caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> but not a cause of it; it may be both caused by and a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>; or it may be neither caused by nor a cause of it' — a threefold distinction; the second alternative does not exist. Therein, 'caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> but not a cause of it': setting aside the past and present latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>s) to be abandoned by the insight into suffering and the truth of suffering associated with them; [Tib. 179b] setting aside the past and present universal latent tendencies to be abandoned by the insight into origination and the truth of suffering associated with them; setting aside the future truth of suffering associated with <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>; and setting aside the birth, aging, duration, and impermanence of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and its associated <s>dharma</s>s — whatever other afflicted truth of suffering there is. 'Both caused by and a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>' is what has been set aside. 'Neither caused by <s>satkāya</s>[-<s>dṛṣṭi</s>] nor a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>' is the unafflicted truth of suffering. As with the truth of suffering, so with the truth of origination — [this is] the <s>Prakaraṇa</s> text. We elucidate its meaning: the past and present ten latent tendencies to be abandoned by the insight into suffering — <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and the rest — are set aside. The truth of suffering such as feeling and the like associated with those ten latent tendencies is set aside. What is not set aside here? These same ten latent tendencies as future, and the future truth of suffering such as feeling and the like associated with them — excluding the truth of suffering associated with future <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. For that

body.text: sthāpayiṣyate. anāgataṃ ca satkāyadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ sthāpayitveti vacanāt. tatprāptijātyādayaś cāsthāpitā varjayitvā satkāyadṛṣṭes tatsaṃprayuktānāṃ [Tib. 180a] ca dharmāṇāṃ jātyādīn. te hi sthāpayiṣyante. satkāyadṛṣṭes tatsaṃprayuktānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ jātiṃ jarāṃ sthitim anityatāṃ ca sthāpayitveti vacanāt. tad evaṃ tāvad anāgato 'nuśayas tatsaṃprayuktaṃ ca sthāpitād anyat. tad anyat kliṣṭam ity ucyate satkāyadṛṣṭihetukam. satkāyadṛṣṭihetur asyeti satkāyadṛṣṭihetukaṃ. sabhāgahetunā sarvatragahetunā cātītapratyutpannasatkāyadṛṣṭihetukatvāt. na tu satkāyadṛṣṭer hetuḥ na hy anāgato dharmaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ sarvatragahetur vā vyavasthāpyate. na ca sahabhūhetuḥ saṃprayuktakahetur vātra saṃbhavati. na hi satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ satkāyadṛṣṭyā saha bhavati saṃprayujyate vā. ekasmiṃ kalāpe dvitīyasatkāyadṛṣṭyabhāvāt. na cāpy antagrāhadṛṣṭyādibhiḥ saha bhavati saṃprayujyate vā. pṛthakkalāpatvāt. viprayuktās teṣām atītapratyutpannānāṃ duḥkhadarśanaheyānāṃ prāptayo jātyādayaś cāsthāpitāḥ. te sthāpitakād anye kliṣṭāś ca. te 'pi sarvatragahetunā pūrvotpannasatkāyadṛṣṭihetukā. na tu te satkāyadṛṣṭer hetuḥ. kasmāt. prāptayas tāvad vṛkṣaprapāṭikāvat svasarvatragebhyo bahir avasthitatvān na sarvatragā vyavasthāpyante. sarvatragatvābhāvāc ca [Tib. 180b] na satkāyadṛṣṭeḥ sarvatragahetuḥ. sarvatragajātyādayo 'py yady api sarvatragā iṣṭāḥ.
body.translated_text: will be set aside. Because of the statement: 'And having set aside the future truth of suffering associated with the view of a self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>).' And the <s>prāptis</s>, births, and so forth of those [dharmas] are not set aside — excluding the births and the rest of the <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and [Tib. 180a] the <s>dharmas</s> associated with it. For those will be set aside — because of the statement: 'Having set aside the birth, aging, duration, and impermanence of the <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and the <s>dharmas</s> associated with it.' Thus, so far, the future latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>) and what is associated with it are different from what is set aside. That which is different — that is called 'defiled, having <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> as its cause.' 'Having <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> as its cause' means: <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> is the cause of this — [hence it is] caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. Because of being caused by the past and present <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> through the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>) and the universal cause (<s>sarvatragahetu</s>). But [it is] not a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> — for a future <s>dharma</s> is not established as a homogeneous cause or a universal cause. Nor is a co-existent cause (<s>sahabhūhetu</s>) or an associated cause (<s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s>) possible here. For <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> does not co-exist with [another] <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> or become associated [with one] — because there is no second <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> in a single assemblage (<s>kalāpa</s>). Nor does it co-exist with or become associated with the view of grasping at extremes (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest — because they belong to separate assemblages. The dissociated [dharmas] — the <s>prāptis</s> and births and the rest of those past and present [dharmas] to be abandoned by the insight into suffering — those are not set aside. They are different from what is set aside and are defiled. They too are caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> through the universal cause, [because they are caused by] previously arisen <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. But they are not a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. Why? <s>Prāptis</s>, to begin with, like bark splitting off from a tree, are not established as universal — because they stand outside their own universals. And because of the absence of universality, [Tib. 180b] [they are] not a universal cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. Even though the births and the rest of universals are accepted as universal —

children.text: prāptivarjyāḥ sahabhuvo ye 'py ebhis te 'pi sarvagā
children.translated_text: 'Excluding <s>prāptis</s>, the co-existents of these too are universal' —

body.text: iti siddhāntavacanāt. na tu te cittacaittavat paścimānāṃ cittacaittānāṃ sarvatragahetuḥ. svalakṣyavyāpāraparatvena aprādhānye sati cittacaittāntareṣu sarvatragapuruṣakārābhāvāt. sarvatragavyavasthānaṃ tu teṣāṃ jātyādīnāṃ svasaṃtānasarvatragahetutvāt. tasmān na te satkāyadṛṣṭer hetur iti śāstrārtho lakṣyate. sabhāgahetus tarhi kasmān na bhavati. sabhāgahetuvyavasthā hi puruṣakārāpekṣayāpi. yasya hi dharmasya janane yaḥ puruṣakāravān dharmaḥ. sa tasya sabhāgahetuḥ. idam eva ca jñāpakaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ sabhāgahetuvyavastheti. vibhāṣāyām apy evam uktaṃ. cakṣuś ca cakṣuṣaḥ sabhāgahetur devadattacakṣuṣo devadattacakṣuḥ sabhāgahetuḥ. dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇasya vāmaṃ vāmasya yāvac cakṣurdravyaṃ cakṣurdravyāntarasya. bāhyeṣv api yavo yavasya śāliḥ śāler iti. yadi hi sarvacakṣuḥ sarvasya cakṣuṣaḥ sabhāgahetur iṣyetāvyākṛtatvaṃ tulyam iti kṛtvā naivaṃ viśeṣaṇam ucyeta. tasmān na te satkāyadṛṣṭeḥ sabhāgahetur ity avagantavyaṃ. apare tv āhuḥ. sāvaśeṣam etad bhāṣyaṃ. tasmāt [Tib. 181a] sajātyādikās te 'nuśayās tatsaṃprayuktāś ca dharmāḥ
body.translated_text: because of this doctrinal statement. But they, unlike mind and mental factors, are not a universal cause of subsequent mind and mental factors — because, being devoted to the operation on their own characterized [dharma], in the absence of prominence, there is no universal efficient action (<s>sarvatragapuruṣakāra</s>) upon other minds and mental factors. But the establishment of those births and the rest as universal is because they are the universal cause within their own continuum. Therefore, 'they are not a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>' — this is understood as the meaning of the treatise. 'Why then is it not a homogeneous cause?' The establishment of the homogeneous cause is also with reference to efficient action (<s>puruṣakāra</s>). For whatever <s>dharma</s> has efficient action in generating [another] <s>dharma</s> — that is its homogeneous cause. And this alone is the indicator: the establishment of the homogeneous cause is as desired. In the <s>Vibhāṣā</s> too it is stated thus: 'The eye is the homogeneous cause of [another] eye — <s>Devadatta</s>'s eye is the homogeneous cause of [another] <s>Devadatta</s> eye; the right [eye] of the right, the left of the left, up to: one eye-substance of another eye-substance. Even among external [things], barley of barley, rice of rice.' For if every eye were accepted as the homogeneous cause of every [other] eye, then being morally indeterminate would be the same [for all] — and such qualification would not be stated. Therefore, it should be understood that they are not a homogeneous cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. Others, however, say: this commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>) is incomplete. Therefore, [Tib. 181a] those latent tendencies together with their births and the rest, and the <s>dharmas</s> associated with them

body.text: sthāpitā veditavyā. ye hi dharmasya tatsaṃprayuktānāṃ ca jātyādayaḥ sahabhūhetur bhavanti. taiḥ sārdhaṃ te dharmāḥ pūrvotpannāḥ sarvatragahetuḥ sabhāgahetur vā bhavanto bhavanti.
body.translated_text: should be understood as set aside. For the births and the rest that are the co-existent cause of that <s>dharma</s> and of its associates — together with those, those <s>dharmas</s>, when previously arisen, become the universal cause or the homogeneous cause.

children.text: prāptivarjyāḥ sahabhuvo ye 'py ebhis ta 'pi sarvagā
children.translated_text: 'Excluding <s>prāptis</s>, the co-existents of these too are universal' —

body.text: iti siddhāntāt. ata evoktaṃ. satkāyasaṃprayuktānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ jātiṃ jarāṃ sthitim anityatāṃ ca sthāpayitveti. tasmāj jātyādayo 'pi kecit sthāpitāḥ. ato 'nyad asthāpitam ity avagantavyaṃ. yuktir iha draṣṭavyā. yato yuktiḥ. tato 'vagantavyaṃ. samudayadarśanaprahātavyā api ye sarvatragā atītapratyutpannās tatsaṃprayuktaṃ ca duḥkhasatyaṃ vedanādikaṃ. tat sthāpitaṃ. kim anyat samudayadarśanaprahātavyam asthāpitaṃ. ye sarvatragā anāgatās tatsaṃprayuktaṃ ca duḥkhasatyaṃ vedanādikaṃ. tad asthāpitaṃ. ye 'py asarvatragā rāgādayas traiyadhvikā api. yāś ca teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāptayaḥ. na te sthāpitāḥ. jātyādayas tv ekasmiṃ pakṣe naiva sthāpitāḥ. pakṣāntare tu kecit sthāpitāḥ. kecin na sthāpitāḥ. tad etat sarvam asthāpitaṃ samudayadarśanaprahātavyaṃ [Tib. 181b] sarvatragahetunā satkāyadṛṣṭihetukaṃ bhavati. pūrvotpannasatkāyadṛṣṭihetukatvāt. na tu satkāyadṛṣṭer hetuḥ. sarvatragāṇāṃ tatsahabhuvāṃ cānāgatatvenāsarvatragahetutvāt. asarvatragāṇāṃ ca rāgādīnāṃ tatsahabhuvāṃ ca vedanādīnāṃ jātyādīnāṃ caikasmin pakṣe sarvaprāptīnāṃ cāsarvatragatvāt. nirodhamārgadarśanaprahātavyā bhāvanāprahātavyāś ca kliṣṭā anuśayatatsaṃprayuktatatsamutthajātyādisvabhāvā asthāpitāḥ. te sarvatragahetunā satkāyadṛṣṭihetukāḥ. na tu te satkāyadṛṣṭer hetuḥ. sarvatragahetutvāsaṃbhavād itarahetvayogāc ca. satkāyadṛṣṭihetukaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭeś ca hetur yad etat sthāpitam iti. ye 'tītapratyutpannā duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyā daśānuśayās tatsaṃprayuktaṃ ca duḥkhasatyaṃ yac ca pakṣāntare jātyādikaṃ. tat sabhāgahetunā sarvatragahetunā ca pūrvasatkāyadṛṣṭihetukaṃ. ye ca satkāyadṛṣṭijātyādayas tatsaṃprayuktajātyādayaś ca. te sahabhūhetunā pūrvoktābhyāṃ ca hetubhyāṃ taddhetukāḥ. ye punaḥ satkāyadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktāḥ. te saṃprayuktahetunā ca pūrvoktaiś ca hetubhis taddhetukāḥ. satkāyadṛṣṭeś ca tathaiva hetuḥ. ye 'py atītapratyutpannāḥ samudayadarśanaprahātavyāḥ sarvatragās [Tib. 182a] tatsahabhuvaś ca vedanādayo jātyādayaś ca pakṣāntare. te sarvatragahetunaiva satkāyadṛṣṭihetukāḥ. satkāyadṛṣṭeś ca hetuḥ. pūrvotpannā hi satkāyadṛṣṭis teṣāṃ hetuḥ. te ca pūrvotpannāḥ satkāyadṛṣṭer iti. asaṃkliṣṭaṃ tu duḥkhasatyaṃ kuśalam anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ ca na satkāyadṛṣṭihetukaṃ na ca satkāyadṛṣṭer hetuḥ. paṃcavidhahetutvasambhavāt. janako
body.translated_text: because of this doctrinal [statement].
