For this very reason it is stated: 'Having set aside the birth, aging, duration, and impermanence of the <s>dharmas</s> associated with <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>.' Therefore, some births and the rest too are set aside. What is other than that is to be understood as not set aside. The reasoning should be examined here — from whatever reasoning [follows], that should be understood. Those universals that are to be abandoned by the insight into origination — the past and present [universals] and the truth of suffering associated with them, such as feeling and the rest — that is set aside. What else is not set aside among [dharmas] to be abandoned by the insight into origination? Those universals that are future and the truth of suffering associated with them, such as feeling and the rest — that is not set aside. And the non-universals such as attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest, even though of all three time-periods. And the <s>prāptis</s> of all of them. Those are not set aside. But as for the births and the rest — according to one view, they are not set aside at all; according to another view, some are set aside and some are not. All of that which is not set aside and is to be abandoned by the insight into origination [Tib. 181b] is caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> through the universal cause — because of being caused by previously arisen <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. But [it is] not a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> — because the universals and their co-existents, being future, are not universal causes; and because the non-universals such as attachment and the rest, and their co-existents such as feeling and the rest, and the births and the rest according to one view, and all the <s>prāptis</s>, are not universal. [Dharmas] to be abandoned by the insight into cessation, by the insight into the path, and by cultivation — those that are defiled, having the nature of latent tendencies, their associates, their products, births and the rest — [those] not set aside, they are caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> through the universal cause. But they are not a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> — because of the impossibility of being a universal cause, and because of the inapplicability of the other causes. 'That which is caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and is also a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> — that is what is set aside' — the past and present [dharmas] to be abandoned by the insight into suffering: the ten latent tendencies, the truth of suffering associated with them, and the births and the rest according to the other view. That is caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> through the homogeneous cause and the universal cause, [because they are caused by] prior <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. And the births and the rest of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and the births and the rest of its associates — those are caused [by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>] through the co-existent cause and the two aforementioned causes. And those associated with <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> — they are caused [by it] also through the associated cause, plus the aforementioned causes. And [they are] likewise a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. And the past and present universals to be abandoned by the insight into origination, [Tib. 182a] their co-existents such as feeling and the rest, and the births and the rest according to the other view — they are caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> through the universal cause alone. And [they are] a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> — for the previously arisen <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> is their cause, and they too, previously arisen, are a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. But the undefiled truth of suffering — wholesome and unobstructed-indeterminate — is not caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, nor is it a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> — because of the possibility of [only] five types of cause. For the generative

body.text: hy atra hetur adhikriyate. na kāraṇahetuḥ. sādhāraṇatvāt. vipākahetoś cehāyogaḥ. satkāyadṛṣṭer nivṛtāvyākṛtatvenāvipākatvāt. tatra yad etad uktaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭes tatsaṃprayuktānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ jātiṃ jarāṃ sthitim anityatāṃ ca sthāpayitveti tad virudhyeta. yadi hi satkāyadṛṣtisaṃprayuktadharmajātyādayo na sahabhūhetur bhaveyuḥ. na te sthāpyeran. ye hi sthāpitāḥ. te satkāyadṛṣṭihetukāḥ. satkāyadṛṣṭeś ca hetur iti. ye tarhi tatsaṃprayuktānām ity etan na paṭhanti. teṣāṃ kathaṃ prakaraṇagrantho virudhyetety adhyāhāryaṃ. te hi satkāyadṛṣṭer jātiṃ jarāṃ sthitim anityatāṃ ca sthāpayitvety evaṃ paṭhanti. tatsaṃprayukteṣv eva tallakṣaṇāni vyāpriyante. na satkāyadṛṣṭau. [Tib. 182b] atas tāni tasyā na sahabhūhetur iti teṣām evaṃvādinām abhiprāyaḥ. tair apy etat paṭhitavyam iti. evam apāṭhe doṣa ity atas tair etat paraṃ paṭhitavyaṃ. tatsaṃprayuktānāṃ ceti. tatsaṃprayuktā hi satkāyadṛṣṭer ātmakalpā ekālambanakṛtyādyarthatvāt. tasmād yathā teṣu tatsaṃprayukteṣv etāni lakṣaṇāni sahabhūhetuḥ. tathā satkāyadṛṣṭāv apīti vaibhāṣikābhiprāyaḥ. arthato vaivaṃ boddhavyam iti. satkāyadṛṣṭigrahaṇena satkāyadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktānām api grahaṇam adhikārānuvṛtter vā tair evaṃ boddhavyaṃ. tatsaṃprayuktānāṃ ceti. kāśmīrā na bahirdeśakā iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: cause is the one under discussion here — not the universal cause (<s>kāraṇahetu</s>), because of its generality. And the retributive cause (<s>vipākahetu</s>) is also inapplicable here — because <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, being obstructed-indeterminate (<s>nivṛtāvyākṛta</s>), does not produce retribution. Therein, what was stated — 'having set aside the birth, aging, duration, and impermanence of the <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and the <s>dharmas</s> associated with it' — that would be contradicted. For if the births and the rest of the <s>dharmas</s> associated with <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> were not a co-existent cause, they would not be set aside — for what is set aside is 'caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and also a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>.' Now, those who do not read 'of those associated with it' — for them, how would the <s>Prakaraṇa</s> text be contradicted? — this must be supplied. For they read only: 'Having set aside the birth, aging, duration, and impermanence of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>.' The characteristics [of those dharmas] operate precisely upon the associates of that [<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>], not upon <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> [itself]. [Tib. 182b] Therefore, those are not its co-existent cause — this is the intent of those who hold this view. 'Even by them, this should be read' — thus. This is a fault in the non-reading — therefore they too should further read: 'and of those associated with it.' For [the dharmas] associated with <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> are like the self of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, because of having the same object, function, and the rest. Therefore, just as these characteristics are a co-existent cause of those associates, so too of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> [itself] — this is the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> intent. 'In substance, it should be understood thus' — the mention of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> includes its associates as well, by the continuity of the topic — or, they should understand it thus: 'and of those associated with it.' 'The <s>Kāśmīras</s>, not the outsiders' — he shows [this distinction].

body.text: sahabhv api tad iti. caittādi. cittasya hi caittās tāni ca lakṣaṇāni sahabhūhetuḥ sahabhūni ca tāni bhavanti. dharmasyānulakṣaṇānīti vistaraḥ. dharmasya jātijātyādīni sahabhūni. na sahabhūhetunā hetur viprakṛṣṭatvāt. jātyādiṣu hi teṣāṃ vyāpāro na dharme. tāni cānyonyaṃ tāni cānulakṣaṇāni anyonyaṃ sahabhūni jātyādiṣu vyāpārāt. na sahabhūhetunā hetuḥ. dharmas tu teṣāṃ sahabhūhetur bhavati. prādhānyāt. sa hi rājeva yātrāyāṃ sabhṛtyaḥ tad bhṛtyavargaṃ sarvaṃ svakalāpam ākarṣann iva pravartate. cittānuparivartyanulakṣanāni ceti. cittānuparivartināṃ caittadhyānānāsravasaṃvarāṇām [Tib. 183a] teṣāṃ ca lakṣaṇānām anulakṣaṇāni ca tathaiva cittasya sahabhūni. na tu sahabhūhetunā hetuḥ. evaśabdo 'rthapradarśanārthaḥ. tāni cānyonyam anuparivartyanulakṣaṇāni sahabhūni. na tu sahabhūhetunā hetuḥ. sapratighaṃ copādāyarūpam anyonyam aṣṭadravyakādiṣu paramāṇuṣu rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyātmakaṃ sahabhūḥ. na tu sahabhūhetunā hetuḥ. sapratighagrahaṇam apratighanirāsārthaṃ. apratighaṃ hi dhyānānāsravaṃ saṃvararūpaṃ saptavidhavijñaptisvabhāvaṃ parasparaṃ sahabhūḥ. sahabhūhetunā ca hetur iti. sarvaṃ ca bhūtair iti. sapratighaṃ cāpratighaṃ copādāyarūpaṃ yathāsvabhūtaiḥ sahabhūḥ. na tu sahabhūhetunā hetuḥ. prāptayaś ca sahajāḥ
body.translated_text: 'The co-existent (<s>sahabhū</s>) of that too' — the mental factors and the rest. For mental factors are the co-existent cause of consciousness, as are those characteristics. And they are co-existents [of consciousness]. 'The sub-characteristics of a <s>dharma</s>' — and so on in detail. The birth-of-birth and the rest of a <s>dharma</s> are co-existent [with it], [but] not through the co-existent cause — because of remoteness. For their operation is upon the births and the rest, not upon the <s>dharma</s> [itself]. And those — those sub-characteristics — are mutually co-existent, because of operating upon the births and the rest. [But they are] not a cause through the co-existent cause. But the <s>dharma</s> is their co-existent cause — because of its prominence. For it [the dharma], like a king in a procession, together with its retinue, proceeds as if drawing along its entire retinue — its whole assemblage. 'And the sub-characteristics of those that conform to consciousness' — the sub-characteristics of those [dharmas] that conform to consciousness — mental factors, <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint, non-outflow restraint, [Tib. 183a] and their characteristics — are similarly co-existent with consciousness, [but] not a cause through the co-existent cause. The word 'just' (<s>eva</s>) is for indicating the meaning. And those sub-characteristics that conform [to consciousness] are mutually co-existent, but not a cause through the co-existent cause. 'And resistant derived form (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>) is mutually [co-existent]' — in the eight-substance atoms and the rest, resistant derived form that has the nature of form, sound, smell, taste, and tangible is mutually co-existent, but not a cause through the co-existent cause. The mention of 'resistant' (<s>sapratigha</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the non-resistant. For non-resistant <s>dhyāna</s> and non-outflow restraint-form, having the nature of the sevenfold <s>vijñapti</s>, is mutually co-existent and is also a cause through the co-existent cause. 'And all [derived form] with the elements' — both resistant and non-resistant derived form, each with its own [great] elements, is co-existent, but not a cause through the co-existent cause — because of [the elements'] prominence. 'And co-natal <s>prāptis</s>'

body.text: prāptimato dharmasya sahotpāde 'pi na sahabhūhetuḥ pūrvaṃpaścātkālajāt prāptīnāṃ. asahabhūtvād eva sahabhūhetutvāprasaṃga iti. sahaja iti viśeṣaṇaṃ. kasmād ity āha. anekaphalavipākaniṣyandatvād iti. yasmāt tāsāṃ prāptimatā saha naikaṃ phalaṃ puruṣakāraphalaṃ vṛkṣaprapāṭikāvat pṛthaksrotatvāt. nāpy ekaṃ vipākaphalaṃ.
body.translated_text: even though they co-arise with the <s>dharma</s> possessing <s>prāpti</s>, [they are] not a co-existent cause — because of the <s>prāptis</s> arising [both] before and after [the dharma]. Because of not being co-existent at all, the consequence of not being a co-existent cause [follows]. Hence the qualification 'co-natal' (<s>sahaja</s>). Why? He says: 'Because they do not share a single result — whether retribution or outflow' — because those <s>prāptis</s>, together with the <s>dharma</s> possessing them, do not share a single efficient-action result (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>) — like bark splitting from a tree, because of being separate streams. Nor do they share a single retribution result (<s>vipākaphala</s>) —

children.text: nākṣepike samāpattī acitte prāptayo na ca
children.translated_text: 'In the non-projecting attainments and in mindless [states], <s>prāptis</s> do not [arise]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. [Tib. 183b] na cāpy ekaniṣyandaphalaṃ prāptīnāṃ hi prātaya eva niṣyandaphalaṃ pṛthaksaṃtānatvāt. cittānuparivartinām evaikaṃ phalaṃ vipākaniṣyandaphalaṃ ceṣyate. na prāptīnāṃ. na tāś cittaiḥ sahacariṣṇavaḥ sahacaraṇaśīlāḥ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. [Tib. 183b] Nor do they share a single outflow result (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>) — for the outflow result of <s>prāptis</s> is precisely [other] <s>prāptis</s>, because of being separate continua. Only for those that conform to consciousness is a single result — retribution result and outflow result — accepted, not for <s>prāptis</s>. They [<s>prāptis</s>] do not accompany minds — [they are] not of a nature to accompany [minds].

body.text: sarvam apy etat syād iti. yat tāvat sahabhūhetunā hetur iti vistareṇa yad uktaṃ. bījādīnām iti. ādiśabdenāṃkuranālakāṇḍādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ. eṣa nyāyo na dṛṣṭa iti. sahotpannayor hetuphalabhāvalakṣaṇo nyāyo na dṛṣṭaḥ. pūrvaṃ hi bījaṃ paścād aṃkuraḥ. pūrvam abhighātaḥ paścāc chabda iti. tadyathā pradīpaprabhayor aṃkurachāyayoś ca. kiṃ. hetuphalabhāva iti vartate. pradīpaḥ saprabha evotpadyate. na niṣprabhaḥ. aṃkurasyātape utpadyamānasyaiva chāyā bhavati. atha ca pradīpaḥ prabhāyāḥ sahotpannāyā hetur bhavati chāyāyāś cāṃkuraḥ. tadvat. saṃpradhāryaṃ tāvad iti vistaraḥ. asiddho dṛṣṭānta iti parasyābhiprāyaḥ. yasmāt pūrvotpannaiva vartisnehādikā sāmagrī saprabhasya pradīpasyotpattau hetuḥ. pradīpasya prabhāyāś ca saiva sāmagrī hetuḥ. na tu pradīpaḥ prabhāyā hetur iṣyate. evaṃ sacchāyasyāṃkurasyotpattau pūrvotpannaiva sāmagrī bījātapādikā vācyā. niyamata iti. yasya dharmasya bhāve yasya dharmasya bhāvo niyamena na yadṛcchayā. sa hetuḥ. itaro hetumān kāryadharma [Tib. 184a] ity arthaḥ. sahabhuvāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ. tadyathā bhūtānāṃ caturṇāṃ cittacaittānuparivartināṃ lakṣyalakṣaṇānāṃ caikasya bhāve sarveṣāṃ bhāva ekasya cābhāve sarveṣām abhāva iti yukto hetuphalabhāvaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'All of this would follow.' What was first stated — that [the co-existent cause] is a cause by means of the <s>sahabhūhetu</s> (co-existent cause) — and so forth in detail. 'Of seeds and the rest' — by the word 'and the rest,' sprouts, stalks, joints, and the like are included. 'This principle is not observed' — the principle of a cause-and-effect relationship between simultaneously arisen [entities] is not observed. For the seed is first and the sprout afterwards; the blow is first and the sound afterwards. 'Just as with a lamp and its radiance, and a sprout and its shadow' — what? The cause-and-effect relationship is [in question]. A lamp arises together with its radiance, not without radiance. A shadow exists for a sprout at the very moment it arises in sunlight. And yet the lamp is a cause of the co-arisen radiance, and the sprout of the shadow. Similarly [with the co-existent cause]. 'This should first be examined' — and so forth in detail. The unestablished illustration — this is the opponent's intent. Because the previously arisen aggregate of wick-oil and the rest is the cause of the arising of the lamp together with its radiance; and that very same aggregate is the cause of both the lamp and the radiance. But the lamp is not accepted as the cause of the radiance. Similarly, for the arising of a sprout together with its shadow, the previously arisen aggregate of seed, sunlight, and the rest should be stated [as the cause]. 'By invariable connection' — when one <s>dharma</s> exists, another <s>dharma</s> exists — invariably, not randomly. That [first dharma] is the cause. The other is the effect-<s>dharma</s>, possessing a cause [Tib. 184a] — this is the meaning. And of co-existent <s>dharmas</s> — for example, of the four great elements, of those following mind and mental factors, and of characterized and characteristics — when one exists, all exist, and when one is absent, all are absent — thus the cause-and-effect relationship is reasonable.

body.text: syāt tāvat sahotpannānām iti vistaraḥ. sahotpannānāṃ hetuphalabhāva iṣyate. tadyathā cakṣuḥ sahotpannam api cakṣurvijñānena tadutpattau hetur bhavati. parasparaṃ tu kathaṃ. na hi cakṣurvijñānaṃ tasya cakṣuṣo hetur bhavatīti. āha. ata eva kāraṇād bhāvābhāvayos tadvattvād ity arthaḥ. caittādīnāṃ bhāve cittasya bhāvād abhāve cābhāvāt te 'pi cittasya hetavo bhavantīti. evaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. yady ekasya bhāve sarveṣāṃ bhāvaḥ sarveṣāṃ cābhāva ekasyety ato 'nyonyaṃ hetuphalabhāvaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'There might be [a cause-and-effect relationship] among the co-arisen' — and so forth in detail. A cause-and-effect relationship among co-arisen [entities] is accepted. For example, the eye, though co-arisen with eye-consciousness, is a cause of the arising of that [consciousness]. 'But how [is it] mutually [a cause]?' For eye-consciousness is not a cause of that eye. He says: 'For this very reason — because of possessing that [invariable connection] in existence and non-existence' — this is the meaning. Because when mental factors and the rest exist, mind exists, and when they are absent, mind is absent — therefore they too are causes of mind. 'If so, then' — and so forth in detail. If when one exists, all exist, and when all are absent, one is absent — then there is a mutual cause-and-effect relationship.

body.text: ity avinābhāvino 'pi rūparasagandhaspraṣṭavyasvabhāvasyopādāyarūpasyānyonyam eṣa prasaṃgaḥ. anyonyasahabhūhetuprasaṃga ity arthaḥ. bhūtaiś ca sārdham upādāyarūpasya sahabhūhetutvaprasaṃgaḥ. cittānulakṣaṇādīnāṃ ceti. ādiśabdena cittānuparivartyanulakṣaṇānāṃ ca. cittādibhir iti. atrāpy ādiśabdena cittānuparivartyanulakṣaṇānāṃ ca. cittādibhir iti. atrāpy ādiśabdena cittānuparivartibhiś cānyonyahetuprasaṃgaḥ. tenaiva cādiśabdena prāptibhiḥ sahajābhiḥ [Tib. 184b] prāptimatām eṣa prasaṃga iti vaktavyaṃ. tridaṇḍānyonyabalāvasthānavad iti. anyonyabalenāvasthānam anyonyabalāvasthānaṃ. tridaṇdasyānyonyabalāvasthānaṃ tridaṇḍānyonyabalāvasthānaṃ. tadvat. yathā tridanḍasya daṇḍatrayasyānyonyabalenāvasthānaṃ. evaṃ sahabhuvāṃ cittacaittādīnāṃ hetuphalabhāvaḥ sidhyati. mīmāṃsyaṃ tāvad etad iti vistaraḥ. parīkṣyam etat. na siddho 'yaṃ dṛṣṭānta ity abhiprāyaḥ. sahotpannās trayo daṇḍās teṣāṃ balaṃ. tena sahotpannabalena kim eṣāṃ daṇḍānām avasthānaṃ. āhosvitpūrvasāmagrīvaśāt tathotpādaḥ. āhosvid yathaivaiṣām avasthitaḥ pūrvabhūtabhautikasamudāyalakṣaṇasāmagrīvaśāt sahabhāvaḥ. tathaiva paścād api parasparāśritānām utpāda iti. anyad api ca tatra kiṃcid bhavati nānyonyabalam eveti darśayati. kiṃ tad ity āha. sūtrakaṃ daṇḍatrayaṃ niveśitaṃ. śaṃkuko vā kīlako vety arthaḥ. pṛthivī vā dhārikādhastāt. eṣām api nāmeti. eṣām api sahabhuvām anye 'pi sabhāgasarvatragavipākakāraṇahetavaḥ sūtrakādisthānīyā bhavantīti siddhaḥ sahabhūhetuḥ.
body.translated_text: even for the inseparable derived form (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>) having the nature of color, taste, smell, and tangibility, this consequence [follows] — the consequence of being mutual co-existent causes. And there is the consequence of derived form being a co-existent cause together with the great elements. 'And of those following mind, the characteristics, and the rest' — by the word 'and the rest,' those following mind and the characteristics [are included]. 'And of mind and the rest' — here too, by the word 'and the rest,' those following mind are included — and the consequence of being mutual causes. And by that same word 'and the rest,' it should be stated that for co-arisen <s>prāptis</s> (acquisitions) [Tib. 184b] too, the consequence applies for those possessing <s>prāptis</s>. 'Like a tripod standing by mutual support' — standing by mutual support is 'mutual-support-standing.' The mutual-support-standing of a tripod is 'tripod-mutual-support-standing.' Similarly. Just as a tripod — a set of three sticks — stands by mutual support, so too the cause-and-effect relationship of co-existent [dharmas] such as mind and mental factors is established. 'This should first be examined' — and so forth in detail. This should be investigated. 'This illustration is not established' — this is the intent. The three sticks are co-arisen; their support — by that co-arisen mutual support, is it the standing of those sticks? Or is [their standing] due to the force of a prior aggregate? Or just as their co-existence is due to the force of a prior aggregate characterized by previous great elements and derived matter, so too afterwards the arising of those mutually dependent [sticks] [is due to a prior cause]? And moreover, there is something else present [in the tripod] that is not merely mutual support — he shows this. What is that? He says: 'A thread holding together the three sticks.' Or: 'a peg, a stake' — this is the meaning. Or: 'earth supporting [them] from below.' 'Even for those [co-existent dharmas]' — even for those co-existent [dharmas], other [causes] such as <s>sabhāga</s> (homogeneous), <s>sarvatraga</s> (universal), <s>vipāka</s> (retributive), and <s>kāraṇa</s> (efficient) causes, occupying the position of the thread and the rest, exist. Thus, the co-existent cause is established.

body.text: (II.53, 54ab) kliṣṭāḥ kliṣṭānām iti. kliṣṭā akuśalā nivṛtāvyākṛtāś ca kliṣṭatvasāmānyena sabhāgahetutvam eṣāṃ. tenākuśalā akuśalānāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. nivṛtāvyākṛtā [Tib. 185a] nivṛtāvyākṛtānāṃ. akuśalā nivṛtāvyākṛtānāṃ. nivṛtāvyākṛtāś cākuśalānāṃ sabhāgahetur iti darśitaṃ bhavati, avyākṛtā avyākṛtānām iti. anivṛtāvyākṛtā anivṛtāvyākṛtānām ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: (II.53, 54ab) 'Defiled [dharmas are sabhāgahetu] of defiled [dharmas].' Defiled — unwholesome and obstructed-indeterminate — by the commonality of being defiled, have the sabhāgahetu (homogeneous cause) relationship among them. Thus, unwholesome [dharmas] are the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of unwholesome [dharmas]; obstructed-indeterminate [dharmas] [Tib. 185a] of obstructed-indeterminate [dharmas]; unwholesome of obstructed-indeterminate; and obstructed-indeterminate of unwholesome — it has been shown [that all these are sabhāgahetu]. 'Indeterminate of indeterminate' — unobstructed-indeterminate of unobstructed-indeterminate — this is the meaning.

body.text: rūpam avyākṛtam avyākṛto rūpaskandhaḥ paṃcānāṃ skandhānāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. catvāras tu skandhā vedanādayo na rūpasya sabhāgahetur viśiṣṭatvāt. na hi viśiṣṭo nyūnasya sabhāgahetur iṣyate.
body.translated_text: Indeterminate form — the indeterminate form-aggregate — is the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of the five aggregates. But the four aggregates of feeling and the rest are not the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of form, because of being superior. For a superior [dharma] is not accepted as the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of an inferior [one].

body.text: iti vacanāt. kuśalākuśalaṃ tu rūpam ābhisaṃskārikatvāt samaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ ceti catvāras tasya sabhāgahetur bhavanti.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. But wholesome and unwholesome form, being produced by deliberate effort (<s>ābhisaṃskārika</s>), is both equal and superior — therefore the four [aggregates] are its <s>sabhāgahetu</s>.

body.text: kalalaṃ kalalādīnām iti. paṃcagarbhāvasthāḥ kalalārbudapeśīghanapraśākhāvasthāḥ paṃca jātāvasthāḥ bālakumārayuvamadhyavṛddhāvasthā ity ete daśa daśānām avasthānāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. kalalaṃ kalalāntarasya yāvad
body.translated_text: 'The <s>kalala</s> (embryonic mass) is [sabhāgahetu] of <s>kalala</s> and the rest.' The five embryonic stages are: <s>kalala</s> (embryonic mass), <s>arbuda</s> (blister), <s>peśī</s> (flesh-lump), <s>ghana</s> (solid mass), and <s>praśākhā</s> (limbs). The five postnatal stages are: infant (<s>bāla</s>), youth (<s>kumāra</s>), young adult (<s>yuva</s>), middle-aged (<s>madhya</s>), and elderly (<s>vṛddha</s>). These ten are the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of the ten stages. The <s>kalala</s> [is sabhāgahetu] of the next <s>kalala</s>, up to

body.text: vārddhasya. arbudam arbudasya yāvad vārddhasya. evaṃ yāvad vārddhaṃ vārddhasyaiva. ekaikāpahrāsena ekaikāparihāreṇaikasmin nikāyasabhāge vaktavyaṃ. anyeṣu samānajātīyeṣu nikāyasabhāgeṣu yadā manuṣyajanmano manuṣyajanmaivotpadyate. tadā daśāpy avasthā daśānām apy avasthānāṃ. vṛddhāvasthāpi yāvad avasthāntarāṇāṃ. sā hi vṛddhāvasthā [Tib. 185b] kṣaṇāntare tajjanmavṛddhāvasthāyāḥ. sabhāgahetuḥ. aṃtyā tu janmāntarakalalādīnāṃ daśānām apy avasthānāṃ sabhāgahetur ity avagantavyaṃ. bāhyeṣv api yavo yavasyeti vistaraḥ. yavo yavasya sabhāgahetur na śāleḥ. śāliḥ śāler eva na yavasyety anena tulye 'py avyākṛtatve svasaṃtāna eva sabhāgahetutvaṃ. nānyasaṃtāne jananaśaktyabhāvād iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: the elderly. The <s>arbuda</s> [is sabhāgahetu] of the [next] <s>arbuda</s>, up to the elderly. Similarly, up to: the elderly is [sabhāgahetu] of the elderly alone — by successive subtraction of one [stage], within a single <s>nikāyasabhāga</s> (class-homogeneity), this should be stated. In other homogeneous classes of the same type — when from a human birth a human birth alone arises — then all ten stages are the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of all ten stages. Even the elderly stage [is sabhāgahetu] of the other stages. For that elderly stage, [Tib. 185b] in the next moment, [is sabhāgahetu] of the elderly stage of that [same] birth. The final [elderly stage] is the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of the <s>kalala</s> and the rest — all ten stages — of the next birth; this should be understood. 'Among external [things] too: barley of barley' — and so forth in detail. Barley is the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of barley, not of rice. Rice is [sabhāgahetu] of rice alone, not of barley. By this, he shows that even when the [dharmas] are equally indeterminate, the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> relationship exists within one's own continuum alone — not in another's continuum, because of the absence of the capacity to generate.

body.text: atītāni mahābhūtāni anāgatānāṃ mahābhūtānāṃ hetur adhipatir iti. hetupratyayo 'dhipatipratyayaś cety arthaḥ. ayugapadbhāvān na sahabhūhetuḥ. ata evācittacaittatvāc ca na saṃprayuktakahetuḥ. asarvatragatvān na sarvatragahetuḥ. avyākṛtatvān na vipākahetuḥ. pāriśeṣyāt sabhāgahetur evety avagamyate. yadi sadṛśāḥ sadṛśānāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. evaṃ paścādutpanno 'pi pūrvotpannasya sabhāgahetuḥ prāpnoti. sahotpanno 'pi sahotpannasya. anutpanno 'py anutpannasyety ata āha. te 'pi na sarve. kiṃ tarhi.
body.translated_text: 'Past great elements are the cause and dominant [condition] of future great elements' — meaning: the efficient cause (<s>hetupratyaya</s>) and the dominant condition (<s>adhipatipratyaya</s>). Because of not being simultaneous, [they are] not a co-existent cause. For this very reason, and because of not being mind or mental factors, [they are] not an associated cause (<s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s>). Because of not being universal [afflictions], not a universal cause (<s>sarvatragahetu</s>). Because of being indeterminate, not a retributive cause (<s>vipākahetu</s>). By the process of elimination, it is understood [to be] precisely the <s>sabhāgahetu</s>. 'If similar [dharmas] are the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of similar [dharmas], then even a later-arisen [dharma] should be the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of an earlier-arisen [one]; and a simultaneously-arisen [dharma] of a simultaneously-arisen [one]; and an unarisen [dharma] of an unarisen [one].' Therefore he says: 'Those too, not all [are sabhāgahetu].' Rather:

body.text: agre jātā atītāḥ pratyutpannā vā sabhāgahetuḥ. anāgatā na sabhāgahetur ity arthād uktaṃ bhavati. evam atītāny atītapratyutpannānām iti. pūrvotpannāny [Tib. 186a] atītāni paścādutpannātītānām iti vibhajyavyākhyaṃ. atītapratyutpannāny anāgatānāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. na tu anāgatāny anāgatānām ity uktam. ato gamyate nāsty anāgataḥ sabhāgahetur iti. na kadācid iti. na kadācin na hetur ity adhikṛtaṃ. hetur evety arthaḥ. tasmād asty anāgataḥ sabhāgahetur ity abhiprāyaḥ. sahabhv iti vistaraḥ. sahabhūsaṃprayuktakavipākahetuṣv abhisaṃdhir abhiprāyaḥ. tena vacanaṃ. tasmāt sahabhūsaṃprayuktakavipāka hetvabhisaṃdhivacanād adoṣo na kadācin na hetur iti vacane. bāhuliko hy eṣa nirdeśa iṣyate. caramām avasthām abhisaṃdhāyeti. antyām anāgatāvasthām abhipretyety arthaḥ. adhvatraye 'pi hetur bhavatīti tasyābhiprāyaḥ. tasyāyam aparihāra iti vistaraḥ. tasya vādino 'yam aparihāraḥ. kasmāt. yasmāt sa dharma utpadyamānāvasthāyāḥ pūrvaṃ sabhāgahetur abhūtvā paścād bhavati. na nityaṃ sabhāgahetur ity arthaḥ. bhavīnām anāgatāvasthānām ekā caramāvasthā sabhāgahetutve niyatībhūtā. tadanyā bahvyas tatrāniyatībhūtāḥ santi. tatra ca sāmānyenoktaṃ na hetur iti. evaṃ kṛtvāyam aparihāraḥ. ekāsyām
body.translated_text: [those] born earlier — past or present — are the <s>sabhāgahetu</s>. That the future is not a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> is implicitly stated. Thus, 'past [dharmas are sabhāgahetu] of past and present [dharmas]' — past [dharmas] that arose earlier [Tib. 186a] [are sabhāgahetu] of later-arisen past [dharmas] — this should be analyzed and explained. 'Past and present [dharmas are sabhāgahetu] of future [dharmas].' But 'future [dharmas] are not [sabhāgahetu] of future [dharmas]' — this has been stated. From this it is understood that the future is not a <s>sabhāgahetu</s>. 'Never not a cause' — 'never not a cause' means: [the subject] is always a cause — this is the meaning. Therefore there exists a future <s>sabhāgahetu</s> — this is the intent. 'The co-existent [cause]' — and so forth in detail. The intent is the co-existent, associated, and retributive causes. For those, the statement [is made]. Therefore, from the statement regarding the co-existent, associated, and retributive causes, there is no fault in the statement 'never not a cause.' For this instruction is accepted as pertaining to the majority. 'With reference to the final state' — with the intent of the final future state — this is the meaning. [The idea is:] it is a cause in all three time-periods. 'This is his irrefutable [argument]' — and so forth in detail. This is the irrefutable argument of that proponent. Why? Because that <s>dharma</s>, having not been a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> before the stage of arising, later becomes one — it is not always a <s>sabhāgahetu</s>, is the meaning. Among the many future states, one final state is established as qualified for being a <s>sabhāgahetu</s>; the other many [states] are unqualified for that therein. And the general statement is made 'it is not a cause.' Thus, this is the irrefutable [argument]. In even one

body.text: api hy avasthāyāṃ [Tib. 186b] sa na sabhāgahetur iti śakyam evaṃ vaktuṃ syāt. yo dharmo yasya dharmasya samanantara iti. samanantarapratyaya ity arthaḥ. śakyam anayā kalpanayeti. sa dharma utpadyamānāvasthāyāṃ samanantarapratyayatve niyatībhūto bhavati. ataḥ śakyaṃ tāṃ caramāvasthām abhisaṃdhāyety anayā kalpanayā vaktuṃ syān na kadācin na samanantara iti. kasmād evam āha. yadi sa dharmo notpanno bhavatīti. yadi sa dharmo 'nāgato bhavati nāsau samanantarapratyayo bhavatīty arthaḥ. caramāvasthāvādy āha. dvimukhasaṃdarśanārtham iti vistaraḥ. yathā tatra yo dharmo yasya dharmasya hetuḥ. kadācit sa dharmas tasya dharmasya na hetuḥ. āha. na kadācid iti. tathehāpi kartavyaṃ. yo dharmo yasya dharmasya samanantaraḥ. kadācit sa dharmas tasya dharmasya na samanantara iti. āha. na kadācid iti kartavyaṃ. (yadi sa dharmo notpanno bhavatīti) yathā ceha tathā tatreti. kathaṃ. yo dharmo yasya dharmasya samanantaraḥ. kadācit sa dharmas tasya dharmasya na samanantaraḥ. āha. yadi sa dharmo notpanno bhavatīti. evaṃ tatra kartavyaṃ. kathaṃ. yo dharmo yasya dharmasya hetuḥ. kadācit sa dharmas tasya dharmasya na hetuḥ. āha. yadi sa dharmo notpanno bhavatīti. yadi sa dharmo 'nāgato bhavati nāsau hetupratyayo bhavatīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: state too [Tib. 186b], 'it is not a <s>sabhāgahetu</s>' — it can indeed be stated thus. 'A <s>dharma</s> that is the <s>samanantara</s> (immediately preceding [condition]) of such-and-such a <s>dharma</s>' — meaning: the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>). 'It is possible by this interpretation' — that <s>dharma</s>, in the stage of being about to arise, is established as qualified for being the immediately preceding condition. Therefore it is possible, by this interpretation, to say 'it is never not the immediately preceding [condition].' Why does he say this? 'If that <s>dharma</s> has not [yet] arisen' — if that <s>dharma</s> is future, it is not the immediately preceding condition — this is the meaning. 'The final-state proponent says' — for the purpose of showing two faces. And so forth in detail. Just as there [in the case of the sabhāgahetu], 'a <s>dharma</s> that is the cause of such-and-such a <s>dharma</s> — is there ever a time when that <s>dharma</s> is not the cause of that <s>dharma</s>?' He says: 'Never.' Similarly here too, it should be done. 'A <s>dharma</s> that is the immediately preceding [condition] of such-and-such a <s>dharma</s> — is there ever a time when that <s>dharma</s> is not the immediately preceding [condition] of that <s>dharma</s>?' He says: 'Never.' Thus it should be done. ('If that <s>dharma</s> has not [yet] arisen') — 'Just as here, so too there.' How? 'A <s>dharma</s> that is the immediately preceding [condition] of such-and-such a <s>dharma</s> — is there ever a time when that <s>dharma</s> is not the immediately preceding [condition] of that <s>dharma</s>?' He says: 'If that <s>dharma</s> has not [yet] arisen.' Similarly, it should be done there. How? 'A <s>dharma</s> that is the cause of such-and-such a <s>dharma</s> — is there ever a time when that <s>dharma</s> is not the cause of that <s>dharma</s>?' He says: 'If that <s>dharma</s> has not [yet] arisen.' If that <s>dharma</s> is future, it is not the efficient cause — this is the meaning.

body.text: atrācārya āha. evaṃ sati ko guṇa iti vistaraḥ. iti dvimukhasaṃdarśanena kaścid guṇo labhyate. [Tib. 187a] naiva hy utpadyamānāvasthāyāṃ sa dharmo hetuḥ samanantaro vā mukhyavṛttyā bhavatīty akauśalam evātra śāstrakārasyaivaṃ saṃbhāvyate. kvacit sāvakāśaṃ bruvataḥ. kvacin niravakāśaṃ. sāvakāśaṃ tāvad yad idam uktaṃ. yo dharmo yasya dharmasya hetuḥ. kadācit sa dharmas tasya dharmasya na hetuḥ. āha. na kadācid iti. kathaṃ na kadācin na hetur ity evam uktvā punar varṇayati. caramāvasthāyāṃ sabhāgahetur iti. niravakāśaṃ yadi sa dharmo notpanno bhavati na samanantaraḥ. utpannas tu samanantara iti. ayam atrābhiprāyārtha aikāntikam arthaṃ vyavasthāpya punar anyathākarotīti. tasmāt pūrvaka evaiṣa parihāraḥ sādhur iti. sahabhūsaṃprayuktakavipākahetvabhisaṃdhivacanād adoṣa iti.
body.translated_text: Here the <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'What is the advantage in this case?' — and so forth in detail. Through this two-sided demonstration, some advantage is obtained. For in the state of arising, that <s>dharma</s> is not a cause (<s>hetu</s>) or an immediately preceding [condition] in the primary sense — thus only unskilfulness is attributed to the treatise-author for saying sometimes what has scope and sometimes what has no scope. What has scope is this statement: 'Whatever <s>dharma</s> is the cause of whatever <s>dharma</s> — is there ever a time when that <s>dharma</s> is not the cause of that <s>dharma</s>?' He says: 'Never.' Having said 'how is it never not a cause,' he then explains: 'In the final state, it is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> (homogeneous cause).' What has no scope is: 'If that <s>dharma</s> has not arisen, it is not an immediately preceding [condition]; but if arisen, it is immediately preceding.' The intended meaning here is that having established a definitive meaning, he then makes it otherwise. Therefore the previous resolution alone is sound. There is no fault, because the statement was made with reference to <s>sahabhūhetu</s> (co-existent cause), <s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s> (associated cause), and <s>vipākahetu</s> (maturation cause).

body.text: yat tarhīdam uktam iti vistaraḥ. kuta etad āyātaṃ. anāgato naiva sabhāgahetur ity uktaṃ. tad yadi anāgato naiva sabhāgahetuḥ kasmād anāgatā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ sthāpitā. yad dhi sthāpitaṃ. tat satkāyadṛṣṭihetuṃ satkāyadṛṣṭeś ca hetur iti vyākhyātaṃ. tatra katham anāgatā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ satkāyadṛṣṭer hetuḥ. na tāvat sahabhūhetuḥ saṃprayuktakahetur vā saṃbhavaty asahabhūtvāt. na vipākahetur avyākṛtatvāt. na kāraṇahetuḥ sādhāraṇatvenāgaṇyamānatvāt. [Tib. 187b]
body.translated_text: 'What then was stated' — and so forth in detail. Where does this come from? It was stated that a future [dharma] is never a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> (homogeneous cause). If a future [dharma] is never a <s>sabhāgahetu</s>, why was future <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existing body) set aside? What was set aside was explained as 'the cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and the cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>.' How then can future <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> be a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>? It cannot be a <s>sahabhūhetu</s> or <s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s>, since they do not co-exist. Not a <s>vipākahetu</s> (maturation cause), since it is indeterminate. Not a <s>kāraṇahetu</s> (efficient cause), since it is not counted due to being universal.

body.text: pāriśeṣyāt sabhāgahetuḥ sarvatragahetur vā bhavatīti bhavet. iha ca sabhāgahetur eva sarvatragahetuḥ. ato yady anāgatā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ satkāyadṛṣṭer na sabhāgahetuḥ kasmād asau tṛtīyakoṭyarthaṃ sthāpiteti. vaibhāṣika āha. anāgatasatkāyadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktakaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ sthāpayitvety evam etad kartavyam iti. satkāyadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktakam eva sthāpayitavyaṃ. na tu satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ. tad dhi vedanādikaṃ sahabhūhetunā saṃprayuktakahetuuā vā satkāyadṛṣṭihetukam satkāyadṛṣṭeś ca hetuḥ. na sabhāgahetunā. vinaṣṭako hy ayam anāgatāṃ satkāyadṛṣṭim iti pāṭhaḥ. paścātpadasthena tacchabdena saha na patḥitavyaḥ. saṃprayuktaduḥkhasatyaviśeṣaṇārthaṃ tu samasyaitat padadvayaṃ paṭhitavyaṃ. anāgatasatkāyadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktakam iti. arthato vaivaṃ boddhavyaṃ yady evaṃ na kriyate pāṭhaḥ. bhāṣyākṣepanirvṛttaḥ pāṭho na tantram ity abhiprāyaḥ. prajñaptibhāṣyaṃ kathaṃ nīyate sarvadharmāś catuṣke niyatā iti. hetau niyatā yasya dharmasya yo dharmo hetuḥ. sa dharmas tasya dharmasya na kadācin na hetuḥ. triṣv api kāleṣu hetur ity arthaḥ. evaṃ phale niyatā yasya dharmasya yo dharmaḥ phalaṃ puruṣakārādi yojyaṃ. evam āśraye niyatā yasya dharmasya [Tib. 188a] cakṣurvijñānāder yo dharma āśrayaś cakṣurādir iti yojyaṃ. evam ālambane niyatā yasya dharmasya cakṣurvijñānāder yo dharma ālambanaṃ rūpādir iti yojyaṃ. tena dharmāṇāṃ hetau niyatatvāt triṣv api kāleṣu sabhāgahetur bhavatīti codakābhiprāyaḥ. sarvahetvanabhisaṃdher adoṣa iti darśayan vaibhāṣika āha. hetur atra saṃprayuktakahetuḥ sahabhūhetuś ca na sabhāgahetuḥ sarvatragahetur vā. anāgatāvasthāyām avyavasthāpitatvāt. na vipākahetuḥ. anāniṃjyasya karmaṇah kasyacid gatyantare 'pi vipākādānāt. phalaṃ puruśakāraphalaṃ adhipatiphalaṃ ca. tayoḥ sahabhūsaṃprayuktakahetvoḥ phalatvāt. vaibhāsikāṇām etan matam. anāgataṃ vidyamānam utpadyata iti. tasmād ayaṃ prasaṃjayati. nanu caivaṃ sati sabhāgahetur abhūtvā anāgatāvasthāyāṃ hetur bhavati vartamānāvasthāyām iti prāptaṃ prasaktam ity arthaḥ. iṣyata evāvasthāṃ prati na dravyam iti. iṣyata eva sabhāgahetoḥ sabhāgahetutvāvasthā pūrvaṃ nāsīd idānīṃ bhavatīti. na tu dravyasvalakṣaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ nāsīd idānīṃ bhavatīti. avasthāphalaṃ hi sāmagryaṃ na dravyaphalam iti. hetupratyayasāmagryā vartamānāvasthāphalaṃ na dravyaṃ. yasmād anāgato 'pi sa dharmo [Tib. 188b] dravyato 'sti. na punaḥ pratyutpanna eveti. codaka āha. kiṃ punaḥ syād iti vistaraḥ. vaibhāṣika āha. śāstre tasya grahaṇaṃ syād iti. tasyānāgatasya sabhāgahetoḥ. na cāsti grahaṇaṃ. na hi tatra śāstre uktaṃ. anāgatāni kuśalamūlāni anāgatānāṃ kuśalamūlānāṃ
body.translated_text: By elimination, it would be a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> or a <s>sarvatragahetu</s> (universal cause). And here, the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> itself is the <s>sarvatragahetu</s>. Therefore, if future <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> is not a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, why was it set aside for the purpose of the third alternative? The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: it should be done thus — by setting aside the <s>duḥkhasatya</s> (truth of suffering) associated with future <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. What should be set aside is that which is associated with <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, not <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> itself. For that — the <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and so on — is a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and a cause from <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> through <s>sahabhūhetu</s> or <s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s>, not through <s>sabhāgahetu</s>. The reading is 'this one has corrupted the future <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>'; it should not be read together with the word 'that' in the following position. Rather, this pair of words should be read together as qualifying the associated <s>duḥkhasatya</s>: 'that which is associated with future <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>.' The meaning should be understood thus even if the reading is not made so. The intent is that the reading arises from the critique of the commentary, not from the root text. How is the <s>Prajñapti-bhāṣya</s> interpreted [regarding] 'all <s>dharmas</s> are fixed in the fourfold [classification]'? Fixed with respect to cause: whatever <s>dharma</s> is the cause of whatever <s>dharma</s>, that <s>dharma</s> is never not the cause of that <s>dharma</s> — meaning it is a cause in all three times. Similarly, fixed with respect to fruit: whatever <s>dharma</s> is the fruit of whatever <s>dharma</s>, as personal effort (<s>puruṣakāra</s>) and so on should be applied. Similarly, fixed with respect to basis: the basis of eye-consciousness and the like — the eye and so on — should be applied. Similarly, fixed with respect to object: the object of eye-consciousness and the like — form and so on — should be applied. Therefore, the objector's intent is: since <s>dharmas</s> are fixed with respect to cause, the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> exists in all three times. Showing that there is no fault since the statement does not refer to all causes, the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'cause' here means <s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s> and <s>sahabhūhetu</s>, not <s>sabhāgahetu</s> or <s>sarvatragahetu</s>, since they are not established in the future state. Not <s>vipākahetu</s> either, because the maturation of the immovable (<s>āninjya</s>) action is received even in another destiny. 'Fruit' means <s>puruṣakāraphala</s> (fruit of personal effort) and <s>adhipatiphala</s> (predominant fruit), since those two — <s>sahabhū</s> and <s>saṃprayuktaka</s> causes — have fruithood. This is the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> view. Since the future exists as real and arises, he therefore raises the consequence: is it not the case that, this being so, the <s>sabhāgahetu</s>, having not been [a cause] in the future state, becomes a cause in the present state? — meaning this consequence follows. 'It is accepted with respect to state, not with respect to substance' — it is accepted that the state of being a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> did not exist before and now comes to be, but not that the substantial own-characteristic did not exist before and now comes to be. For the fruit of state is an assemblage, not a fruit of substance. The fruit of the assemblage of causes and conditions is the present state, not a substance, since that <s>dharma</s> exists substantially even when future — but it is not [only] when present. The objector says: 'What then would be?' — and so forth in detail. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'There would be its inclusion in the treatise' — of that future <s>sabhāgahetu</s>. But there is no such inclusion, for it is not stated in that treatise that 'future wholesome roots are the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of future wholesome roots.'

body.text: sabhāgahetur iti. codaka āha. ya eva hīti vistaraḥ. codakasyāyam abhiprāyaḥ. yady apy anāgato 'sti sabhāgahetur na tv asau phaladānagrahaṇakriyāyāṃ samarthaḥ. ya eva hi phaladānagrahaṇakriyāsamarthaḥ phalākṣepakriyāsamarthaś ca. tasyaiva sabhāgahetoḥ atītasya vartamānasya ca grahaṇāt. adoṣo 'nāgatasya sabhāgahetor agrahaṇaṃ. tasya phaladānagrahaṇakriyāyām asāmarthyāt. tasmād asty anāgataḥ sabhāgahetuḥ. atha ca śāstre nokta iti. vaibhāṣika āha. naitad astīti vistaraḥ. naitad yujyate. niṣyandaphalena hi saphalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ.
body.translated_text: 'The <s>sabhāgahetu</s>' — the objector says: 'For the very one who...' — and so forth in detail. The objector's intent is: even if the future <s>sabhāgahetu</s> exists, it is not capable of the function of giving fruit and grasping. For the very one who is capable of the function of giving fruit and grasping, and capable of the function of projecting fruit — only that <s>sabhāgahetu</s>, past or present, is included. There is no fault in not including the future <s>sabhāgahetu</s>, because of its incapacity for the function of giving fruit and grasping. Therefore the future <s>sabhāgahetu</s> exists, yet it is not stated in the treatise. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'This is not so' — and so forth in detail. This is not logical, for the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> is fruitful through the outflow fruit (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>).

children.translated_text:
'The outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>) of <s>sabhāga</s> and <s>sarvatraga</s> [causes];
the outflow is similar to the cause' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. tac cānāgatasyāyuktaṃ. tan niṣyandaphalam ayuktaṃ. kasmāt. pūrvapaścimatābhāvāt. anāgatāvasthāyām idaṃ pūrvam idaṃ paścimam iti na paricchidyate viprakīrṇatvāt. na cāsati pūrvāparabhāve sadṛśaḥ sadṛśasya niṣyando yujyate. atha matam. utpannam atītaṃ vartamānaṃ vā anāgatasya niṣyanda iti. ata āha. na cotpannam anāgatasya niṣyando yujyata iti. yathātītaṃ [Tib. 189a] vartamānasya niṣyando na bhavati. tathānāgatasyāpy utpanno na niṣyando bhavitum arhati. kasmād ity āha. mā bhūd dhetoḥ pūrvaṃ phalam iti doṣāṭ. vipākaphalasya pūrvaṃ saha cāyogād iti. mā bhūd dhetoḥ pūrvaṃ phalam iti pūrvam ayogaḥ. saha cāyogo 'nāgatāvasthāyāṃ. na hi pratyutpannāvasthāyāṃ sahabhūhetor iva vipākahetoḥ sahotpannaṃ phalam upalabhyate. tasmāt. anāgate cādhvani pūrvapaścimatābhāvāt. viprakīrṇatvād anāgatasyādhvano na pūrvaṃ vipākahetuḥ paścād vipākaphalaṃ yujyate. tasmāc ca sabhāgahetuvad vipākahetur apy anāgato na prāpnoti. vaibhāṣika āha. naitad asti yad uktaṃ vipākahetur apy evam iti. na cānyonyaniṣyandatā yuktimatīti. yasya yaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ sadṛśo dharmaḥ. tasya sa eva dharmas tadānīṃ eva kathaṃ niṣyando yokṣyate. na hi putraḥ svasyaiva pitus tadānīm eva pitā bhavatīti. na tv evaṃ vipākahetuḥ. kim. anyonyahetuphalatā na paurvāparyeṇa vinā saṃprasajyate prāpnoti. kasmāt bhinnalakṣaṇatvād dhetuphalayoḥ. hetor anyal lakṣaṇaṃ svabhāva ity arthaḥ. akuśalatā kuśalasāsravatā vā tasya lakṣaṇaṃ. phalasya [Tib. 189b] cānyal lakṣaṇam anivṛtavyākṛtatvaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated. But that is not logical for the future. That outflow fruit is not logical. Why? Because of the absence of before-and-after. In the future state, one cannot determine 'this is before, this is after,' due to [things being] scattered. And without the before-and-after relation, it is not logical that a similar [dharma] is the outflow of a similar one. Or if you think: what has arisen — past or present — is the outflow of the future — therefore he says: 'Nor is it logical that what has arisen is the outflow of the future.' Just as the past is not the outflow of the present, so too what has arisen should not be the outflow of the future. Why? He says: 'Lest the fruit precede the cause — because of that fault.' The impossibility of the maturation fruit being before [the cause] and being simultaneous — 'lest the fruit precede the cause' means the impossibility of preceding; and the impossibility of simultaneity is in the future state. For in the present state, unlike the <s>sahabhūhetu</s>, no fruit is found to have arisen simultaneously with the <s>vipākahetu</s>. Therefore, since there is no before-and-after in the future time-period, and since the future time-period is scattered, it is not logical that the <s>vipākahetu</s> is before and the <s>vipākaphala</s> is after. Therefore, like the <s>sabhāgahetu</s>, the <s>vipākahetu</s> too, when future, does not obtain. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'This is not so, that what was said — the <s>vipākahetu</s> too is likewise.' Nor is mutual outflow-hood logical — for a <s>dharma</s> that is the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of something, being a similar <s>dharma</s>, how could that very <s>dharma</s> at that very time be its outflow? For a son does not become the father of his own father at that very time. But the <s>vipākahetu</s> is not like this. What [is the difference]? Mutual cause-fruit relationship does not arise without sequential order. Why? Because the characteristics of cause and fruit are different. The cause has a different characteristic — i.e., its own-nature — being unwholesome or wholesome-with-outflows. And the fruit has a different characteristic — being unobstructed-indeterminate.

children.text:
vipākahetur aśubhāḥ kuśalāś caiva sāsravāḥ
vipāko 'vyākṛto dharma
children.translated_text:
'The <s>vipākahetu</s> (maturation cause) is unwholesome and wholesome with outflows;
the <s>vipāka</s> (maturation) is an indeterminate <s>dharma</s>' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. tasmād iti vistaraḥ. avasthāvyavasthita eva sabhāgahetuḥ. avasthāyāṃ vyavasthitaḥ. atītāvasthaḥ pratyutpannāvasthaś ca sabhāgahetur nānāgatāvasthaḥ. lakṣaṇavyavasthitas tu vipākahetuḥ. lakṣaṇena vyavasthitas triṣv api kāleṣu yathoktalakṣaṇa ity anāgato 'pi vipākahetur na vāryate na pratiṣidhyate. idam iha vicāryate. kim anāgate 'dhvani sadṛśā dharmā viprakīrṇā iti na śakyate paricchetuṃ ayaṃ hetur idam idam asya niṣyandaphalam iti. ato nānāgataḥ sabhāgahetur vyavasthāpyate. āhosvit yo dharmo yasya dharmasya sabhāgahetur bhavet. sa dharmas tasya hetupratyayavaśān niṣyandaphalaṃ bhaved iti. ato 'nāgatas sabhāgahetur na vyavasthāpyate. naitad vyākhyānakārair vicāritaṃ. mama tu pūrvaka evāyaṃ pakṣaḥ pratibhātīti.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated. 'Therefore' — and so forth in detail. The <s>sabhāgahetu</s> is established only with respect to temporal state — established in a [particular] state: past or present, the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> is [operative], not in the future state. But the <s>vipākahetu</s> is established by characteristic — established by [its] characteristic, in all three times having the stated characteristic, so even the future <s>vipākahetu</s> is not excluded or prohibited. What is examined here is this: is it that in the future time-period, similar <s>dharmas</s> are scattered and it cannot be determined 'this is the cause, this is its outflow fruit,' and therefore the future <s>sabhāgahetu</s> is not established? Or is it that whatever <s>dharma</s> would be the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of whatever <s>dharma</s>, that <s>dharma</s> would be its outflow fruit through the force of causes and conditions, and therefore the future <s>sabhāgahetu</s> is not established? This has not been examined by the commentators. But to me, the former position appears [correct].

body.text: kim eṣa niyama iti. kiṃ svabhūmika evety avadhāryate. nānyathāpy astīty abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Is this a fixed rule?' — is it determined that only within the same ground (<s>bhūmi</s>)? The intent is that it is not otherwise.

children.translated_text: 'But the path, mutually, across nine grounds' —

body.text: iti. tuśabdo viśeṣaṇe. mārga iti mārgasatyaṃ vivakṣitaṃ. sāsravān mārgasatyaṃ viśiṣyate. sāsravo hi dharmaḥ svabhūmika eva sabhāgahetuḥ. nānyabhūmikaḥ mārgas tv anyabhūmiko 'pi sabhāgahetuḥ. iha bhūmigrahaṇe sāravānāsravagrahaṇaṃ. dhātugrahaṇe tu sāsravasyaivety [Tib. 190a] ata āha. yat sāsravāṇāṃ mārgasya ca tulye bhūmibhede mārga eva navabhūmiko 'nyonyaṃ sabhāgahetur na sāsrava iti. kuta ity āha. āgantuko hy asau tāsu bhūmiṣu na taddhātupatitaḥ. tadbhūmikābhis tṛṣṇābhir asvīkṛtatvād iti. na hi kāmarūpārūpya(navabhūmisaṃniśrayādhigamyatvāt navabhūmiko na tadbhūmisaṃgṛhītatvāt) caryas tṛṣṇāḥ sāsravān ivānāsravān dharmān svīkurvanti. yadā tarhi nirvāṇaṃ mārgaṃ vābhilaṣati kuśalo 'sau dharmacchandaḥ. na rāgaḥ. tasya varjyatvād iti vacanāt. samānajātīyasyety anāsravajātīyasya. evaṃ tarhi sarvaḥ sarvasya sabhāgahetuḥ prāpnoti. ata āha.
body.translated_text: the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) marks a distinction. 'Path' (<s>mārga</s>) refers to the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>). The path-truth is distinguished from what has outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>). For a <s>dharma</s> with outflows is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> only within the same ground, not across different grounds. But the path is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> even across different grounds. Here, the term 'ground' (<s>bhūmi</s>) includes both with-outflows and without-outflows, while the term 'realm' (<s>dhātu</s>) refers only to that with outflows. Therefore he says: for equal [and distinguished] division of grounds between what has outflows and the path — only the path, across the nine grounds, is a mutual <s>sabhāgahetu</s>, not what has outflows. Why? He says: because it is a visitor (<s>āgantuka</s>) in those grounds, not one that has fallen into that realm. Because it is not appropriated by the <s>tṛṣṇās</s> (cravings) of those grounds. For the <s>tṛṣṇās</s> of <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Rūpa</s>, and <s>Ārūpya</s> do not appropriate outflow-free <s>dharmas</s> as they do <s>dharmas</s> with outflows — since [the path] is attainable through reliance on [all] nine grounds. When one desires <s>nirvāṇa</s> or the path, that wholesome desire for <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmacchanda</s>) is not craving (<s>rāga</s>), as stated: 'because it is to be excluded.' 'Of the same kind' means of the outflow-free kind. If so, then everything would be the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of everything. Therefore he says:

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: grahaṇaṃ tarhi kim arthaṃ. ūrdhvabhūmikādharabhūmikayor anyonyam ity evam arthaṃ. ūrdhvabhūmiko 'py adharabhūmikayoḥ samaviśiṣṭayoḥ sabhāgahetur bhavati. adharabhūmiko 'py ūrdhvabhūmikayor iti. tadyatheti vistaraḥ. duḥkhe dharmajñānakśāntis tasyā evānāgatāyāḥ sameti kṛtvā sabhāgahetuḥ. viśiṣṭasya ca duḥkhe dharmajñānasya duḥkhe 'nbvayajñānakṣānter yāvad anutpādajñānasya
body.translated_text: then what is the purpose of the word 'mutual'? The meaning is: between what belongs to a higher ground and what belongs to a lower ground, mutually. Even one belonging to a higher ground is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of those belonging to a lower ground — of equal and distinguished [types]. And one belonging to a lower ground [is likewise a <s>sabhāgahetu</s>] of those belonging to higher grounds. 'For example' — and so forth in detail. The <s>duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the knowledge of dharma regarding suffering) is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of that very same [acceptance] when future, being equal; and of the distinguished <s>duḥkhe dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharma regarding suffering), <s>duḥkhe anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (subsequent patient acceptance regarding suffering), up to <s>anutpādajñāna</s> (knowledge of non-arising) —

body.text: . na tu nyūnasya. na hi duḥkhe dharmajñānam anāgatāyāḥ duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣānteḥ sabhāgahetur bhavati. darśanabhāvanāśaikṣamārgās tridvyekeṣām iti. darśanamārgo darśanamārgāntarasya bhāvanāmārgasyāśaikṣamārgasya ca sabhāgahetur iti trayāṇāṃ. bhāvanāmārga bhāvanāmārgāntarasyāśaikṣamārgasya ca sabhāgahetuḥ. na darśanamārgasyeti [Tib. 190b] dvayoḥ. aśaikṣamārgo 'śaikṣamārgāntarasya na darśanamārgabhāvanāmārgayor ity ekasya sabhāgahetuḥ. tatrāpīti. tatra darśanamārgādiṣu mṛdvindriyamārgo darśanamārgasvabhāvo mṛdutīkṣṇendriyamārgasya tatsvabhāvasyaiva. tikṣṇendriyamārgas tīkṣṇdriyamārgasyaiva. na mṛdvindriyamārgasya nyūnatvāt. evaṃ bhāvanāmārgo 'śaikṣamārgaś ca vaktavyaḥ. tad darśayann āha. tadyatheti vistaraḥ. ekasyāpi mṛdvindriyasya pudgalasya ṣaṇmārgāḥ santi. prakṛtitīkṣṇendriyasya trayaḥ. tatra śraddhānusārimārgaḥ śraddhānusārimārgāntarasyātmīyasya sabhāgahetuḥ. dharmānusārimārgasya cātmīyasyānāgatāvasthasya śraddhādhimuktadṛṣṭiprāptasamayavimuktāsamayavimuktamārgāṇāṃ cātmīyāṇāṃ yathāyogam utpattyanutpattidharmāṇāṃ ceti ṣaṇṇāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. śraddhādhimuktamārgaḥ śraddhādhimuktamārgāntarasya dṛṣṭiprāptasamayavimuktāsamayavimuktamārgāṇāṃ cāpareṣām api trayāṇām iti caturṇāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. samayavimuktamārgaḥ samayavimuktamārgāntarasyāsamayavimuktamārgasya ceti dvayoḥ sabhāgahetuḥ. na tu śraddhādhimuktamārgaḥ śraddhānusāridharmānusārimārgayor hetuḥ pūrvakālīnatvāt darśanamārgasya. bhāvanāmārgasya ca viśiṣṭatvāt. evam anyatrāpi yojyaṃ. [Tib. 191a] dharmānusārimārgaḥ dharmānusārimārgāntarasya dṛṣṭiprāptāsamayavimuktamārgayoś ceti trayāṇāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. dṛṣṭiprāptamārgo dṛṣṭiprāptamārgāntarasyāsamayavimuktamārgasya ceti dvayoḥ. asamayavimuktamārgo 'samayavimuktamārgāntarasyaivety ekasya sabhāgahetuḥ. na tu dhamānusārimārgaḥ śraddhānusārimārgasya sabhāgahetuḥ. dharmānusārimārgasyendriyato viśiṣtatvāt. nāpi śraddhādhimuktamārgasyendriyato viśiṣṭatvāt. nāpi samayavimuktamārgasyendriyato viśiṣṭatvāt. samayavimuktamārgas tarhīndriyato viśiṣṭasya dṛṣṭiprāptamārgasya sabhāgahetuḥ prāpnoti. na prāpnoti. aśaikṣamārgasaṃgṛhītatvāt. na hi pūrvakālīnaṃ phalaṃ paścātkālīno hetur iti. dṛṣṭiprāptamārgaḥ punaḥ samayavimuktamārgasya na sabhāgahetur indriyato nyūnatvāt. kathaṃ punar iti vistaraḥ. kathaṃ punar ūrdhvabkūmikasya dvitīyadhyānāt prabhṛti yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmikasya darśanamārgasya bhāvanāmārgasya vā aśaikṣamārgasya vā yathāyogam adhobhūmiko mārgo vijñānānamtyāyatanāt
body.translated_text: But not of what is inferior. For <s>dharmajñāna</s> (dharma-knowledge) of suffering is not a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> (homogeneous cause) of the future insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering. 'The paths of insight, cultivation, and no-more-training [are sabhāgahetus] of three, two, and one respectively' — the insight-path is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of another insight-path, of the cultivation-path, and of the no-more-training path — thus of three. The cultivation-path is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of another cultivation-path and of the no-more-training path, but not of the insight-path — [Tib. 190b] thus of two. The no-more-training path is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of another no-more-training path, not of the insight-path or cultivation-path — thus of one. 'Therein also' — in those insight-paths and so forth, the path with mild faculties that has the nature of the insight-path [is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s>] of the paths with mild and sharp faculties that have that same nature. But the path with sharp faculties [is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s>] only of the sharp-faculty path, not of the mild-faculty path, because of inferiority. The same should be stated for the cultivation-path and the no-more-training path. Showing that, he says: 'for example...' — thus the elaboration. Even for a single person with mild faculties, there are six paths. For one with naturally sharp faculties, three. Therein, the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> (faith-follower) path is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of another <s>śraddhānusārin</s> path belonging to oneself, and of the <s>dharmānusārin</s> (dharma-follower) path belonging to oneself in its future state, and of the <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> (faith-liberated), <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> (view-attainer), <s>samayavimukta</s> (time-liberated), and <s>asamayavimukta</s> (non-time-liberated) paths belonging to oneself, as appropriate, whether having the nature of arising or not-arising — thus of six. The <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> path is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of another <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> path and of the three other paths — <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>, <s>samayavimukta</s>, and <s>asamayavimukta</s> — thus of four. The <s>samayavimukta</s> path is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of another <s>samayavimukta</s> path and of the <s>asamayavimukta</s> path — thus of two. But the <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> path is not a cause of the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> and <s>dharmānusārin</s> paths, because the insight-path is earlier in time, and because the cultivation-path is superior. The same should be applied elsewhere as well. [Tib. 191a] The <s>dharmānusārin</s> path is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of another <s>dharmānusārin</s> path and of the <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> and <s>asamayavimukta</s> paths — thus of three. The <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> path is [a <s>sabhāgahetu</s>] of another <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> path and of the <s>asamayavimukta</s> path — thus of two. The <s>asamayavimukta</s> path is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of another <s>asamayavimukta</s> path alone — thus of one. But the <s>dharmānusārin</s> path is not a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> path, because the <s>dharmānusārin</s> path is superior in terms of faculties. Nor of the <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> path, because of superiority in terms of faculties. Nor of the <s>samayavimukta</s> path, because of superiority in terms of faculties. 'Then should the <s>samayavimukta</s> path be a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of the <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> path, which is superior in terms of faculties?' It does not follow, because [the <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> path] is included in the no-more-training path. For what is earlier in time is not the fruit of what is later — [thus] not a cause. The <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> path is not a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of the <s>samayavimukta</s> path, because of inferiority in terms of faculties. 'But how then...' — thus the elaboration. But how can the path of a lower ground — from the sphere of infinite consciousness

body.text:
prabhṛti yāvad anāgamyabhūmiko yathāyogaṃ darśanamārgo bhāvanāmārgo vā aśaikṣamārgo vā samo vā viśiṣṭo vā bhavati. kathaṃcana bhavitavyaṃ. hīnatvād adharāyā bhūmeḥ. [Tib. 191b] indriyato hetūpacayataś ca. indriyatas tāvat samo bhavati viśiṣṭo vā. darśanamārge śraddhānusārimārgaś caturthadhyānabhūmiko 'dharabhūmikasya tasyaiva śraddhānusārimārgasya samaḥ. ubhayor mṛdvindriyatvāt. tasyaivādharabhūmiko dharmānusārimārgo viśiṣṭaḥ. tīkṣṇendriyatvāt. tathā dharmānusārimārgaś caturthadhyānabhūmiko 'dharabhūmikasya dharmānusārimārgasya samaḥ. evam etāv eva śraddhānusāridharmānusārimārgau caturthadhyānabhūmikāv adharabhūmikayor bhāvanāśaikṣamārgayoḥ pratyekaṃ bhūmīndriyabhedabhinnayoḥ samau vā viśiṣṭau veti saṃbhavato yojyau. tathā bhāvanāmārge ākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmikasya śraddhādhimuktamārgasyādharabhūmikaḥ śraddhādhimuktamārgaḥ samaḥ. ubhayor mṛdvindriyatvāt. tasyaivādharabhūmiko dṛṣṭiprāptamārgo viśiṣṭaḥ. tīkṣṇendriyatvāt. tathā tasyaiva samayavimuktamārgo 'dharabhūmikaḥ samaḥ. ubhayor mṛdvindriyatvāt. tasyaivāsamayavimuktamārgo 'dharabhūmiko viśiṣṭaḥ. tīkṣṇendriyatvāt. evam aśaikṣamārge ākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmikasyāśaikṣamārgasyādharabhūmikaḥ samo viśiṣṭo veti yathāyogaṃ yojyam. anayā diśā sarvabhūmayo yojyāḥ kathaṃ hetūpacayataḥ. ūrdhvabhūmikasyādharabhūmiko mārgaḥ samo viśiṣṭo vā bhavatīty ata idam ucyate. tatra [Tib. 192a] darśanādimārgāṇām iti vistaraḥ. ādigrahaṇena bhāvanāśaikṣamārgopasaṃgrahaḥ. ūrdhvabhūmikāyā duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣānteḥ adhobhūmikaṃ duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ hetūpacayato viśiṣṭaṃ bhavati. duḥkhe dharmajñānād apy ūrdhvabhūmikād adharabhūmikā duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntir yāvad ūrdhvabhūmikān mārge dharmajñānād adharabhūmikā mārge 'nvayajñānakṣāntir hetūpacayato viśiṣṭā bhavati. ekaikādhikasabhāgahetūpacitatvāt. darśanamārgād ūrdhvabhūmikād adhobhūmiko bhāvanāmārgo hetūpacayato viśiṣṭo bhavati. darśanamārgo hi darśanamārgahetūpacito bhāvanāmārgas tu darśanabhāvanāmārgahetūpacitaḥ. ūrdhvabhūmikābhyāṃ darśanabhāvanāmārgābhyām adharabhūmiko 'śaikṣamārgo hetūpacayato viśiṣṭo bhavati.
darśanabhāvanāmārgahetūpacitatvāt. ūrdhvabhūmikasya darśanamārgasyādhobhūmiko darśanamārgo hetūpacayataḥ samānakṣaṇāpekṣayā samo bhavati. evaṃ bhāvanāmārgasya bhāvanāmārgo 'śaikṣamārgasyāśaikṣamārga iti. tad evaṃ kaścid indriyataḥ samo bhavati hetūpacayato viśiṣṭaḥ saty apy adharabhūmikatve. tadyathā prathamadhyānabhūmikāc chraddhānusārimārgād adharabhūmikau śraddhādhimuktasamayavimuktamārgau. kaścid dhetūpacayataḥ samo bhavati indriyato viśiṣṭaḥ. tadyathā
body.translated_text: onward down to the preliminary concentration (<s>anāgamya</s>) ground — be, as appropriate, an insight-path, cultivation-path, or no-more-training path that is equal to or superior to the insight-path, cultivation-path, or no-more-training path of a higher ground from the second <s>dhyāna</s> onward up to the sphere of nothingness? It must somehow be [equal or superior], despite the inferiority of the lower ground. [Tib. 191b] In terms of faculties and in terms of cause-accumulation. First, in terms of faculties, it may be equal or superior. In the insight-path: a <s>śraddhānusārin</s> path belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground is equal to the same <s>śraddhānusārin</s> path of a lower ground, because both have mild faculties. But the <s>dharmānusārin</s> path of that same lower ground is superior, because of having sharp faculties. Likewise, the <s>dharmānusārin</s> path of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground is equal to the <s>dharmānusārin</s> path of a lower ground. In the same way, these two — the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> and <s>dharmānusārin</s> paths of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground — should be applied as equal or superior to the cultivation and no-more-training paths of lower grounds, distinguished by ground and faculty, as possible. Likewise in the cultivation-path: the <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> path of a lower ground is equal to the <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> path of the sphere of nothingness ground, because both have mild faculties. The <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> path of that same lower ground is superior, because of having sharp faculties. Likewise, the <s>samayavimukta</s> path of a lower ground is equal, because both have mild faculties. The <s>asamayavimukta</s> path of that same lower ground is superior, because of having sharp faculties. Similarly in the no-more-training path: for the no-more-training path of the sphere of nothingness ground, the lower ground [path] should be applied as equal or superior as appropriate. In this direction all grounds should be applied. How with respect to cause-accumulation? A path of a lower ground is equal to or superior to that of a higher ground — therefore this is stated. Therein, [Tib. 192a] 'of the insight-path and so forth' — thus the elaboration. By the word 'and so forth,' the cultivation and no-more-training paths are included. The <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering of a lower ground is superior in terms of cause-accumulation to the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering of a higher ground. Even from the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering of a higher ground, the subsequent-knowledge-tolerance regarding suffering of a lower ground, up to: from the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of the path of a higher ground, the subsequent-knowledge-tolerance regarding the path of a lower ground is superior in terms of cause-accumulation — because of being accumulated by one additional <s>sabhāgahetu</s> at each stage. The cultivation-path of a lower ground is superior in terms of cause-accumulation to the insight-path of a higher ground, for the insight-path is accumulated by insight-path causes, but the cultivation-path is accumulated by insight-path and cultivation-path causes. The no-more-training path of a lower ground is superior in terms of cause-accumulation to the insight and cultivation paths of a higher ground, because of being accumulated by insight-path and cultivation-path causes. A lower-ground insight-path is equal in terms of cause-accumulation to the insight-path of a higher ground, considering the same moment. Likewise a cultivation-path to a cultivation-path, a no-more-training path to a no-more-training path. Thus some are equal in terms of faculties but superior in terms of cause-accumulation, despite being of a lower ground — for example, the <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> and <s>samayavimukta</s> paths of a lower ground relative to the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> path of the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. Some are equal in terms of cause-accumulation but superior in terms of faculties — for example

body.text: caturthadhyānabhūmikāc chraddhānusāryādimārgād adhobhūmikadharmānusāryādimārgaḥ samānakṣaṇāpekṣayā. [Tib. 192b] kaścid indriyato hetūpacayataś ca viśiṣṭaḥ. tadyathā caturthadhyānabhūmikāc chraddhānusārimārgād adharabhūmikau dṛṣṭiprāptasamayavimuktamārgau. mṛdumṛdvādīnāṃ cottarottare hetūpacitatarā iti. darśanamārgavarjyāḥ. tasmin mṛdumṛdvādyasaṃbhavāt. tatra mṛdumṛdoḥ prakārād ūrdhvabhūmikād adharabhūmiko 'pi mṛdumadhyo yāvad adhimātramadhyād adhimātrādhimātraḥ samānāsamānakṣaṇāpekṣayā hetūpacayataḥ samo viśiṣṭo vā bhavati. ekaikādhikaprakārahetūpacitatvāt. yad uktaṃ śraddhānusārimārgaḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ sabhāgahetur iti kathaṃ śraddhānusārimārgo dharmānusārimārgasya sabhāgahetur bhavati. na hi tayor ekasaṃtāne saṃmukhībhāvo 'sti. tenāha. yady apy ekasaṃtāne śraddhādharmānusārimārgayor asaṃbhavaḥ. utpannas tv anāgatasya hetur iti. asaṃbhavo hy atrāsaṃmukhībhāvaḥ. na tv abhāvaḥ. santi hi mṛdvindriyāṇāṃ mṛdvindriyamārgavad ātmīyās tīkṣṇendriyamārgā api. dṛṣṭiprāptasamayavimuktamārgās tu tatsaṃtāne saṃmukhībhaveyur api yadīndriyasaṃcāraḥ kriyeta. tasmād utpannaḥ śraddhānusārimārgo 'nutpattidharmiṇo dharmānusārimārgasya śraddhādhimuktadṛṣṭiprāptasamayavimuktāsamayavimuktamārgāṇāṃ ca yathāyogam anāgatānām utpattidharmāṇām anutpattidharmāṇāṃ vā samaviśiṣṭānāṃ sabhāgahetur iti. ācāryavasumitras tv āha. [Tib. 193a] utpannaḥ śraddhānusārimārgo 'nutpannasya dharmānusārimārgasya dṛṣṭiprāptamārgasya vā hetur yadā śraddhānusāryādaya indriyāṇi saṃcaranto dharmānusārimārgādīn saṃmukhīkurvanti. tad ayuktaṃ. na hi śraddhānusārīndriyāṇi saṃcarati. śraddhādhimuktādayas tu saṃcareyuḥ.
body.translated_text: the <s>dharmānusārin</s> path and the like of a lower ground relative to the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> path and the like of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground, considering the same moment. [Tib. 192b] Some are superior in both faculties and cause-accumulation — for example, the <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> and <s>samayavimukta</s> paths of a lower ground relative to the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> path of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground. 'The mild-mild and so forth have successively greater cause-accumulation' — excluding the insight-path, because the mild-mild and other [gradations] are not possible therein. Therein, from the mild-mild type of a higher ground, the mild-medium of a lower ground, up to: from the intense-medium, the intense-intense, is equal to or superior in terms of cause-accumulation considering the same or different moments — because of being accumulated by one additional type-cause at each [stage]. 'It was said that the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> path is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of six — how then is the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> path a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of the <s>dharmānusārin</s> path? For the simultaneous actualization of those two in a single continuum does not occur.' Therefore he says: 'although the co-occurrence of the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> and <s>dharmānusārin</s> paths in a single continuum is impossible, nevertheless, one that has arisen is a cause of a future [one] that has not arisen.' For the impossibility here means non-actualization, not non-existence. For those with mild faculties have, like their own mild-faculty paths, their own sharp-faculty paths as well. The <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> and <s>samayavimukta</s> paths might indeed become actualized in that continuum if a faculty-transfer were to occur. Therefore, the arisen <s>śraddhānusārin</s> path is a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of the future <s>dharmānusārin</s> path that will not arise, and of the <s>śraddhādhimukta</s>, <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>, <s>samayavimukta</s>, and <s>asamayavimukta</s> paths, as appropriate — whether of the nature of arising or not-arising, equal or superior. But teacher <s>Vasumitra</s> says: [Tib. 193a] 'The arisen <s>śraddhānusārin</s> path is a cause of the unarisen <s>dharmānusārin</s> path or the <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> path when the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> and other faculties, undergoing transfer, actualize the <s>dharmānusārin</s> and other paths.' That is incorrect, for the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> does not undergo faculty-transfer. The <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> and others, however, may undergo transfer.

body.text: prāyogikā iti. prayogena nirvṛttāḥ prāyogikāḥ. prāyogikagrahaṇam upapattipratilaṃbhikanirāsārthaṃ. kāmāvacarāḥ śrutamayā iti. ye buddhavacanaśrutena niryātāḥ. te śrutamayāḥ. cintāmayāś cintāmayānām iti. cintāmayānām eva na śrutamayānāṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Obtained through practice' — those produced through practice are <s>prāyogika</s> (practice-born). The term <s>prāyogika</s> is for the purpose of excluding those obtained through birth (<s>upapattipratilaṃbhika</s>). 'Belonging to the desire realm, born of learning (<s>śrutamaya</s>)' — those that have issued from hearing the word of the <s>Buddha</s> are <s>śrutamaya</s>. 'Those born of reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>) [are <s>sabhāgahetu</s>s] of those born of reflection' — of those born of reflection only, not of those born of learning.

body.text: iti vacanāt. bhāvanāmayabhāvād iti. kāmadhātor asamāhitatvāt bhāvanāmayā na santi. cintāmayābhāvād iti. yadā hi cintayitum ārabhante. tadaiṣāṃ samādhir evopatiṣṭhata iti cintāmayābhāvakāraṇaṃ. teṣām apīti. śrutamayādīnāṃ. mṛdumṛdavaḥ sarveṣām iti. mṛdumṛdavo mṛdumṛdvantarāṇāṃ samānāṃ mṛdumadhyādīnāṃ cānyeṣām aṣṭānāṃ viśiṣṭānām iti sarveṣāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. mṛdumadhyā aṣṭānāṃ mṛdumṛduprakāram apāsyate 'sya nyūnatvāt. [Tib. 173b]
body.translated_text: because of that statement. 'Because those born of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>) do not exist' — because the desire realm is not a state of concentration, those born of cultivation do not exist [there]. 'Because those born of reflection do not exist' — for when [beings in the higher realms] begin to reflect, <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) itself presents itself to them — this is the reason for the non-existence of those born of reflection [in higher realms]. 'Of those also' — of those born of learning and the rest. 'The mild-mild [are sabhāgahetus] of all' — the mild-mild [are <s>sabhāgahetu</s>s] of [other] mild-mild [of the same class] that are equal, and of the eight other [types] — mild-medium and so forth — that are superior; thus of all. The mild-medium [are <s>sabhāgahetu</s>s] of eight, the mild-mild type being excluded because of its inferiority. [Tib. 173b]

body.text: eṣā nītir iti. tadyathā mṛdvadhimātrāḥ saptānāṃ madhyamṛdavaḥ saṇṇāṃ yāvad adhimātrādhimātrā adhimātrādhimātrāntarāṇāṃ ekarūpāṇāṃ sabhāgahetur iti. pūrvān pūrvān apāsya teṣāṃ teṣāṃ nyūnatvāt. upapattipratilaṃbhikās tu kuśalā iti. upapattyā pratilaṃbha upapattipratilaṃbhaḥ. sa eśām astīty upapattipratilaṃbhikāḥ. ata iniṭhanāv iti ṭhan. sarve te nava prakārāḥ parasparaṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. mṛdumṛdūnāṃ yāvad adhimātrādhimātrāṇām eva. adhimātrādhimātrā mṛdumṛdūnāṃ yāvad adhimātrādhimātrāṇāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. na samaviśiṣṭānām eva. anābhisaṃskārikatvāt. ābhisaṃskārikasya hi sabhāgahetor nyūnaṃ phalaṃ neṣyate. nānābhisaṃskārikasya. kliṣṭā apy evam iti. sarve navaprakārāḥ parasparaṃ sabhāgahetur aprāyatnikatvāt. pūrvotpannāḥ sarve samānabhūmikānāṃ paścādvartināṃ sarveṣāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. nātra samaviśiṣṭate apekṣyete. te yathākramaṃ catustridvyekeṣāṃ sabhāgahetur iti. vipākajā vipākājādīnāṃ caturṇāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. airyāpathikā airyāpathikādīnāṃ eva trayāṇāṃ. va vipākajānāṃ. teṣām anābhisaṃskārikatvena nyūnatvāt. śailpasthānikā dvayoḥ śailpasthānikanairmāṇikayoḥ. nairmāṇikā nairmāṇikānām eva. [Tib. 194a] na pūrveṣām. uttareṣām uttareṣām ābhisaṃskārikatvāt. nirmāṇacittam api kāmāvacaraṃ caturdhyānaphalam iti. caturṇāṃ dhyānānāṃ phalaṃ prathamadvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānaphalam iti catuṣprakāraṃ kāmāvacaraṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ. tad yathākramaṃ catustridvyekeṣāṃ ca sabhāgahetur iti vartate. prathamadhyānaphalaṃ caturṇāṃ prathamadvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānaphalānāṃ sabhāgahetuḥ. dvitīyadhyānaphalaṃ trayāṇāṃ dvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānaphalānāṃ. tṛtīyadhyānaphalaṃ dvayos tṛtīyacaturthadhyānaphalayoḥ. caturthadhyānaphalaṃ ekasya caturthadhyānaphalāntarasyaiva sabhāgahetuḥ. kā punar atra yuktir yayaivaṃ niyama iti tāṃ yuktiṃ nirdikṣur āha. nottaradhyānaphalaṃ adharadhyānaphalasyeti vistaraḥ. na caturthadhyānaphalaṃ kāmāvacaraṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ prathamadhyānaphalasya kāmāvacarasya nirmāṇacittasya yāvat tṛtīyadhyānadhyānaphalasya kāmāvacarasya nirmāṇacittasya sabhāgahetuḥ. kasmād ity āha. na hy ābhisaṃskārikasya mahāyatnasādhyasya sabhāgahetor hīyamānam amahāyatnasādhyaṃ phalaṃ bhavati. yādṛśena hi yatnaviśeṣeṇa prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ yāvat tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ niṣpādyate. na tādṛśenaiva caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ niṣpādyate. [Tib. 194b] kiṃ tarhi. utkṛṣṭatareṇa yatnaviśeṣeṇa niṣpādyate. tasmāt phalam asyotkṛṣṭatareṇaiva yatnaviśeṣeṇa niṣpādyate ity avagamyate. tena adharadhyānaphalaṃ uttaradhyānaphalasya sabhāgahetuḥ. na tūttaradhyānaphalaṃ adharadhyānaphalasya
body.translated_text: this is the rule. For example, the mild-intense are the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>) of seven [types]; the medium-mild of six; up to the intense-intense being the homogeneous cause of those of the same type as the intense-intense only — having excluded each preceding type because of their inferiority. But the wholesome [<s>dharma</s>s] obtained through rebirth — that obtained through rebirth is 'rebirth-obtained.' Those which possess this are 'rebirth-obtained' — the <s>ṭhan</s>-suffix [is applied] after <s>ini</s>. All nine types are mutually the homogeneous cause — from the mild-mild up to the intense-intense only. The intense-intense is the homogeneous cause of the mild-mild up to the intense-intense — not of the equal and superior only, because of being non-volitional. For the fruit of a volitional homogeneous cause is not accepted as inferior; but [this restriction does] not [apply] to the non-volitional. 'The afflicted also, likewise' — all nine types are mutually the homogeneous cause, because of being non-effortful. All those previously arisen are the homogeneous cause of all subsequent ones belonging to the same ground. Here, [the restriction of] equal and superior is not considered. 'They are the homogeneous cause of four, three, two, or one, respectively' — the maturation-born is the homogeneous cause of four [types] beginning with the maturation-born. The path-of-conduct [type] is [the homogeneous cause] of only three [types] beginning with the path-of-conduct — but not of the maturation-born, because of their inferiority through being non-volitional. The craft-based is [the homogeneous cause] of two: the craft-based and the supernaturally-created. The supernaturally-created is [the homogeneous cause] of the supernaturally-created alone — [Tib. 194a] not of the preceding ones, because each successive one is more volitional. 'The supernaturally-created mind too, belonging to the desire realm, is the fruit of the four <s>dhyāna</s>s' — the fruit of the four <s>dhyāna</s>s means: the fruit of the first, second, third, and fourth <s>dhyāna</s>s — thus the supernaturally-created mind of the desire realm is fourfold. That, respectively, 'is the homogeneous cause of four, three, two, or one' — this continues. The fruit of the first <s>dhyāna</s> is the homogeneous cause of four: the fruits of the first, second, third, and fourth <s>dhyāna</s>s. The fruit of the second <s>dhyāna</s> [is the homogeneous cause] of three: the fruits of the second, third, and fourth <s>dhyāna</s>s. The fruit of the third <s>dhyāna</s> [is the homogeneous cause] of two: the fruits of the third and fourth <s>dhyāna</s>s. The fruit of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is the homogeneous cause of one: another [instance of] the fruit of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> alone. What then is the reasoning by which there is such a restriction? Intending to state that reasoning, he says: 'The fruit of a higher <s>dhyāna</s> is not [the homogeneous cause] of [the fruit of] a lower <s>dhyāna</s>' — thus the elaboration. The desire-realm supernaturally-created mind that is the fruit of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is not the homogeneous cause of the desire-realm supernaturally-created mind that is the fruit of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, up to the fruit of the third <s>dhyāna</s>. Why? He says: for the fruit of a volitional homogeneous cause that is achievable through great effort does not become inferior — achievable through less effort. For the first <s>dhyāna</s> up to the third <s>dhyāna</s> are accomplished by a certain degree of effort, but the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is not accomplished by that same [degree of effort]. [Tib. 194b] Rather, it is accomplished by a more excellent degree of effort. Therefore its fruit too is understood to be accomplished only by a more excellent degree of effort.
