Hence, the fruit of a lower <s>dhyāna</s> is the homogeneous cause of the fruit of a higher <s>dhyāna</s>, but the fruit of a higher <s>dhyāna</s> is not [the homogeneous cause] of the fruit of a lower <s>dhyāna</s>

body.text:
. yathā ca caturthadhyānaphalaṃ yojitaṃ. evaṃ tṛtīyadvitīyadhyānaphalam api yojyaṃ. ata evāhur iti. yasmād ābhisaṃskārikasya sabhāgahetor hīyamānaṃ phalaṃ na bhavati. tasmād āhur ity arthaḥ. kim āhur ity āhuḥ. syād utpanna iti vistaraḥ. duḥkhe dharmajñānam anāsravam utpannam anutpattidharmāṇām anāsravāṇāṃ duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntināṃ na hetuḥ. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntibhyo duḥkhe dharmajñānasyābhisaṃskārikatvena viśiṣṭatvāt. evaṃ hi tad viśiṣṭaṃ. yat kleśavisaṃyogaprāptyā saha utpadyate. viśiṣṭaṃ ca nyūnasya na hetuḥ. tadyathārhattvāt parihīṇasya aśaikṣo mārgaḥ pūrvotpannaḥ sakṛdāgāmyanāgāmimārgayoḥ paścādutpadyamānayor na sabhāgahetuḥ. syād ekasaṃtānaniyataḥ pūrvapratilabdha iti vistaraḥ. anāgatā duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntayaḥ prathama eva kṣaṇe pratilabdhā ekasaṃtānagatāḥ. duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ dvītiyakṣaṇotpannaṃ. tasya tā na hetuḥ. [Tib. 195a] yasmān na pūrvataraṃ phalaṃ. pūrvataraṃ hi duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntibhyaḥ. tasyotpannatvāt. tāsāṃ cānutpannatvāt. anāgato vā dharmaḥ yasmān na sabhāgahetuḥ. anāgatā duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntayaḥ aparimitāḥ pratilabdhā eva na tūtpannāḥ. syāt pūrvotpanna iti vistaraḥ. pūrvaṃ pratilabdhamātro dharmaḥ pṛṣṭo na tūtpannaḥ anutpannaś ca na sabhāgahetur bhavatīti. idānīṃ pūrvotpanno 'pi kim asti na sabhāgahetur iti atiśayarūpeṇa pṛcchyate. adhimātro nyūnasyeti. viśiṣṭo nyūnasyety arthaḥ. tadyathottaraphalaparihīṇasya arhattvaphalaparihīṇasyānāgāmiphalaparihīṇasya
vā adharaphalasaṃmukhībhāve 'nāgāmiphalasaṃmukhībhāve sakṛdāgāmiphalasaṃmukhībhāve vā. yo 'rhattvamārgo 'dhimātraḥ pūrvotpannaḥ. sa paścādutpannasyānāgāmiphalasya sakṛdāgāmiphalasya vā na sabhāgahetuḥ. nyūnatvāt. evam anāgāmiphalaparihīṇasya yo 'nāgāmiphalamārgaḥ. sa pūrvotpannaḥ paścādutpannasya sakṛdāgāmiphalasya na sabhāgahetuḥ. nyūnatvāt. duḥkhe dharmajñānaprāptiś ceti vistaraḥ. duḥkhe dharmajñānaprāptir yā pūrvotpannā. sā uttarakṣaṇasahotpannānāṃ uttaraiḥ kṣaṇair duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntikṣaṇādibhir ā mārge 'nvayajñānakṣānteḥ sahotpannānāṃ duḥkhe [Tib. 195b] dharmajñānakṣāntiprāptīnāṃ na sabhāgahetuḥ. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. tāsāṃ nyūnatvāt. tasyāś ca viśiṣṭatvāt. kathaṃ punas tāsāṃ nyūnatvaṃ tasyāś ca viśiṣṭatvaṃ. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣānter duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ tadvadhyakleśaprāpter vimuktatvāt. hetūpacitataratvāc ca. tasmād dhetūpacitatarābhyo 'pi duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāniprāptibhyo duḥkhe dharmajñānaprāptir viśiṣṭā tāś ca nyūnās tatprāptitvāt. kiṃ ca prathamakṣaṇotpannāyā duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiprāpter duḥkhe dharmajñānaprāptis tasmād eva hetudvayād
body.translated_text: . And just as the fruit of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> has been construed, so too the fruit of the third and second <s>dhyāna</s>s should be construed. 'Therefore they say' — because the fruit of a volitional homogeneous cause does not become inferior, therefore they say — this is the meaning. What do they say? They say: 'It may be the case that an arisen [<s>dharma</s>]' — thus the elaboration. A non-outflow <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering that has arisen is not the cause of non-outflow insight-tolerances regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering that have the nature of non-arising — because the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering is superior to the insight-tolerances regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering through being more volitional. For it is superior in this way: it arises together with the acquisition of disconnection from afflictions. And the superior is not the cause of the inferior. For example, for one who has declined from <s>Arhatship</s>, the previously arisen non-learner's path is not the homogeneous cause of the subsequently arising paths of once-returning or non-returning — because of their inferiority. 'And the possession of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering' — thus the elaboration. The possession of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering that has previously arisen — that is not the homogeneous cause of the possessions of insight-tolerances regarding <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering [Tib. 195a] that co-arise with subsequent moments — the moments of the insight-tolerance regarding subsequent knowledge of suffering and so forth up to the insight-tolerance regarding subsequent knowledge of the path. For what reason? Because those [tolerances] are inferior, and because that [possession] is superior. But how is their inferiority and its superiority [established]? The <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering is superior to the insight-tolerances regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering because of being free from the possession of afflictions destroyable by them, and because of being more cause-enriched. Therefore the possession of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering is superior even to the possessions of insight-tolerances regarding <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering that are more cause-enriched; and those are inferior because of being possessions of that [tolerance]. Moreover, the possession of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering is superior to the possession of insight-tolerance regarding <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering that arose at the first moment for these same two reasons

body.text: viśiṣṭā. nyūnā ca sā duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiprāptiḥ. atas tatpūrvikā apy anyā uttarakṣaṇasahotpannā duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiprāptayo hetūpacitataratve 'pi nyūnā eveti. tasmān na sā tāsāṃ sabhāgahetur iti.
body.translated_text: — and that possession of insight-tolerance regarding <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering is inferior. Therefore the other possessions of insight-tolerances regarding <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering that co-arise with subsequent moments and are preceded by that [first-moment tolerance], even though they are more cause-enriched, are also simply inferior. Therefore that [possession] is not their homogeneous cause.

body.text: (II.54cd)

children.translated_text: 'The associated cause (<s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s>) is [exclusively] mind and mental factors' —

body.translated_text: (II.54cd)

body.text: iti. tuśabdo 'vadhāraṇe bhinnakramaś ca. cittacaittā eva saṃprayuktakahetur iti. evaṃ satīti vistaraḥ. yadi cittacaittā eva saṃprayuktasahetur ity etāvad ucyate bhinnakālajā api bhinnakālajaiḥ saha bhinnasaṃtānajā api ca bhinnasaṃtānajaiḥ saha saṃprayuktakahetuḥ [Tib. 196a] saṃprasajyate. na hi te kālasaṃtānabhinnā na cittacaittā bhavanti. ekākārālambanās tarhīti. yadi cittacaittā ekākārā ekanīlādyākārā ekālambanāś ca ekanīlādyālambanā evaṃ te saṃprayuktakahetur nānyatheti. evaṃ bhinnakālajatvaṃ bhinnasaṃtānajatvaṃ ca vyāvartitaṃ bhavatīty abhiprāyaḥ. evam api sa eva prasaṃgaḥ. bhinnakālasaṃtānajānāṃ anyonyaṃ saṃprayuktakahetutvaprasaṃga iti arthaḥ. saṃbhavati hi bhinnakālasaṃtānajānām api cittacaittānām ekākārālambanatvaṃ. bhinnasaṃtānajānām api prasaṃga iti. bhinnakālajatvam ekaṃ parikṛtaṃ. navacandrādīni hi paśyatāṃ bahūnāṃ ekākārālambanāś cittacaittā vartante.
body.translated_text: thus. The particle 'but' (<s>tu</s>) is for restriction and indicates a change in sequence. 'Only mind and mental factors are the associated cause' — this is the meaning. 'This being so' — thus the elaboration. If it is said merely that mind and mental factors are the associated cause, then even those born at different times would be the associated cause of others born at different times, and even those born in different continua [would be the associated cause] of those born in different continua — [Tib. 196a] [this] would follow. For those that are of different times and different continua are not non-mind-and-mental-factors. 'Then [they must be] of the same aspect and object' — if mind and mental factors that have a single aspect — such as a single blue aspect and the like — and a single object — such as a single blue object and the like — are the associated cause in that way and not otherwise, then the [faults of] being of different times and different continua would be excluded — this is the intent. 'Even so, the same consequence [follows]' — the consequence of mind and mental factors of different times and different continua being mutually associated causes — this is the meaning. For it is possible for mind and mental factors of different times and different continua to have the same aspect and object. 'Even of those born in different continua, the consequence [follows]' — the [fault of] different times has been set aside by one [criterion]. For many who perceive the new moon and the like have mind and mental factors of the same aspect and object.

body.text: iti. samaḥ abhinna āśraya eṣām iti
body.translated_text: thus. Those whose basis is the same — identical — are

body.text: tulyārthe samaśabdagrahaṇe hi jātitulyatvāt sa eva prasaṃgaḥ syāt.
body.translated_text: For if the word 'same' were taken in the sense of 'similar,' then, because of being similar in class, the same consequence would arise.

body.text: anyonyaphalārtheneti vistaraḥ. yathā sahasārthikānāṃ parasparabalena mārgaprayāṇaṃ. evaṃ cittaṃ caittasya phalaṃ. caitto 'pi cittasyety anyonyaphalam iti tenārthena sahabhūhetuḥ. paṃcabhir iti vistaraḥ. paṃcabhis samatābhiḥ. āśrayālambanākārakāladravyasamatābhir ity arthaḥ. [Tib. 196b] samaprayogārthena samapravṛttyarthena saṃprayuktakahetuḥ. yathā teṣām eva sārthikānām anyonyabalena mārgaṃ gacchatāṃ samo 'nnapānasnānaśayanādiparibhogakriyāyāṃ prayogaḥ. tadvat samaprayogatvam eṣām anyonyaṃ bhavati. ata evāha. ekenāpi hi vinā na sarve saṃprayujyanta iti.
body.translated_text: 'For the purpose of mutual fruitfulness' — thus the elaboration. Just as for co-travelers, the journey is accomplished by mutual support, so too mind is the fruit of the mental factor, and the mental factor is the fruit of mind — [they are] mutual fruits. In that sense, [the associated cause] is a co-existent cause (<s>sahabhūhetu</s>). 'By five' — thus the elaboration. By five equalities — equality of basis, object, aspect, time, and substance — this is the meaning. [Tib. 196b] In the sense of equal engagement, equal operation, [it is] the associated cause. Just as those very co-travelers, journeying by mutual support, have equal engagement in the enjoyment of food, drink, bathing, sleeping, and the like — likewise, this equal engagement exists mutually among these [mind and mental factors]. Therefore he says: 'For without even one [of them], they are not all associated.'

body.text: (II.55ab)
body.translated_text: (II.55ab)

body.text: iti. pūrve ca te sarvagāś ca sarvapūrvagāḥ. pūrvotpannāḥ sarvagā ity arthaḥ. svabhūmikāḥ pūrvotpannā atītāḥ pratyutpannā vā sarvatragā anuśayāḥ kliṣṭānāṃ kleśasvabhāvasaṃprayuktasamutthānāṃ paścimānāṃ paścādatītapratyutpannānāṃ anāgatānāṃ ca sarvatragahetuḥ. vyākhyāsyāma iti.
body.translated_text: thus. Those that are previously [arisen] and universally pervasive are the 'previously-and-universally-pervasive.' The meaning is: previously arisen and universally pervasive. The universally pervasive latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) that are previously arisen — past or present — belonging to the same ground, are the universally pervasive cause (<s>sarvatragahetu</s>) of subsequent afflicted [<s>dharma</s>s] — those having the nature of afflictions, associated with [afflictions], or arisen from them — that are subsequent, whether past, present, or future. 'We shall explain' —

children.text:
sarvatragā duḥkhahetudṛggheyā dṛṣṭayas tathā
vimatiḥ saha tābhiś ca yāvidyāveṇikī ca yety
children.translated_text:
'The universally pervasive are those to be abandoned by the insight into suffering and origination: [wrong] views, likewise
doubt, together with them, and the distinctive ignorance' —

body.text: atra paṃcame kośasthāne nirdekṣyāmaḥ. kliṣṭadharmasāmānyakāraṇatveneti vistaraḥ. yasmād ayaṃ sarvatragahetuḥ kliṣṭānām eva sāmānyena paṃcanikāyānām api bhavati. sabhāgahetus tu kliṣṭānāṃ cākliṣṭānāṃ ca. tasmāt pṛthag vyavasthāpyate. kathaṃ kliṣṭadharmasāmānyakāraṇatvam asyeti pratipādayann āha. nikāyāntarīyāṇām api hetutvād iti. eṣāṃ hi prabhāveneti. eṣāṃ hi sarvatragāṇāṃ prabhāvena anyanaikāyikā anyanikāyabhavāḥ kleśā rāgādaya upajāyante. ke punas te. duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyasya sarvatragahetoḥ [Tib. 197a] samudayanirodhamārgadarśanabhāvanāprahātavyā nikāyāntarīyā bhavanti. samudayadarśanaprahātavyasya sarvatragahetor duḥkhanirodhamārgadarśanabhāvanāprahātavyā nikāyāntarīyā bhavanti. sarvān kleśanikāyān gacchanti bhajante ālambane. sarveṣāṃ vā kleśanikāyānāṃ hetubhāvaṃ gacchantīti sarvatragāḥ. ata evoktaṃ. satkāyadṛṣṭimūlakāḥ sarvakleśāḥ satkāyadṛṣṭiprabhavāḥ satkāyadṛṣṭisamudayā iti. ātmagrāhadvāreṇa rāgamānapratighādisamudācārāt. kim āryapudgalasyāpīti. sarvatragā āryapudgalasya sarva eva prahīṇā darśanaprahātavyatvāt. rāgādayaś ca śaikṣānāṃ samudācaranti. te rāgādayas teṣāṃ na sarvatragahetukā iti manyamāna evaṃ pṛcchati. kliṣṭā dharmā iti. aviśeṣitatvāt pṛthagjanāryasaṃtānajā iti gamyate. yaś ca darśanaprahātavyānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ vipāka iti. arthaparisamāptyartham etad uktaṃ. naitad udāharaṇaṃ. avyākṛtāḥ saṃskṛtā dharmā iti. nivṛtāvyākṛtā anivṛtāvyākṛtāś ca gṛhyante. nivṛtāvyākṛtāḥ kāmadhātau satkāyāntagrāhadṛṣṭitatsaṃprayuktasamutthā dharmā rūpārūpyāvacarās [Tib. 197b] ca kliṣṭā dharmāḥ. saṃskṛtagrahaṇaṃ ākāśāpratisaṃkhyānirodhanirāsārthaṃ.
body.translated_text: We shall explain this in the fifth section of the <s>Kośa</s>. 'Because of being the general cause of defiled <s>dharmas</s>' — and so on in detail. Because this universal cause (<s>sarvatragahetu</s>) is generally a cause of the defiled alone — even of the five groups (<s>nikāya</s>). But the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>) is a cause of both defiled and non-defiled. Therefore, [the universal cause] is established separately. Explaining how it is the general cause of defiled <s>dharmas</s>, he says: 'Because of being a cause even of those belonging to other groups.' 'Through the influence of these' — through the influence of these universals, afflictions of other groups — belonging to other groups — such as attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest, arise. Which are those? For a universal cause to be abandoned by the insight into suffering, [Tib. 197a] those to be abandoned by the insights into origination, cessation, the path, and by cultivation belong to other groups. For a universal cause to be abandoned by the insight into origination, those to be abandoned by the insights into suffering, cessation, the path, and by cultivation belong to other groups. 'They go to all affliction-groups, they frequent all objects' — or, 'they assume the state of being causes of all affliction-groups' — hence they are 'universal' (<s>sarvatraga</s>). For this very reason it was stated: 'All afflictions are rooted in <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, arise from <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, have <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> as their origin' — because through the door of self-grasping, attachment, conceit, aversion, and the rest operate. 'Even for a Noble Person?' — all universals of a Noble Person have been completely abandoned, because they are to be abandoned by insight (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>). But attachment and the rest do operate for trainees (<s>śaikṣa</s>). Thinking 'those attachments and the rest of theirs are not caused by universals,' he asks thus. 'Defiled <s>dharmas</s>' — because it is unspecified, it is understood [to mean those] arising in the continua of both ordinary persons and Noble Ones. 'And that which is the retribution of <s>dharmas</s> to be abandoned by insight' — this is stated for the purpose of completing the meaning, not as an illustration. 'Morally indeterminate conditioned <s>dharmas</s>' — both obstructed-indeterminate (<s>nivṛtāvyākṛta</s>) and unobstructed-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>) are included. The obstructed-indeterminate in the desire-realm are <s>dharmas</s> produced by the view of a self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the view of grasping at extremes (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>) and their associates; and the defiled <s>dharmas</s> belonging to the form and formless realms. [Tib. 197b] The mention of 'conditioned' is for the purpose of excluding space and non-analytical cessation.

children.translated_text: '[Space and non-analytical cessation are] supremely indeterminate and permanent' —

body.text: iti tayor avyākṛtatvāt. tatra kāmāvacarāḥ kliṣṭā dharmā yathāyogaṃ sabhāgasarvatragasahabhūsaṃprayuktakahetubhūtais tair eva satkāyadṛṣṭyādibhir avyākṛtahetukāḥ. nānyai rāgādibhiḥ. ūrdhvabhūmikās tv anyair apīti sugamam etat. anivṛtāvyākṛtāḥ sabhāgahetunānivṛtāvyākṛtahetukāḥ. akuśalāḥ kāmāvacarā rāgādayaḥ. te ca sarvatragahetunā satkāyadṛṣṭyādihetukāḥ. idam atrodāharaṇaṃ. akuśalāś ceti hy aviśeṣitatvāt darśanaprahātavyā bhāvanāprahātavyāś ca gṛhyante. idam atra dvitīyajñāpakaṃ. yat tad anyat kliṣṭaṃ duḥkhaṃ satyam iti tṛtīyaṃ jñāpakaṃ. tadanyad dhi kliṣṭaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ darśanaprahātavyaṃ bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ ca aviśeṣitatvāt gṛhyate. sarvatragahetunā
body.translated_text: because of their being indeterminate. Therein, defiled <s>dharmas</s> of the desire-realm are caused by indeterminate [dharmas] — by those very <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and the rest that serve as homogeneous, universal, co-existent, and associated causes, as appropriate — not by other [dharmas] such as attachment and the rest. But those of higher realms are [caused] by others too — this is easily understood. The unobstructed-indeterminate [dharmas] are caused by the unobstructed-indeterminate through the homogeneous cause. The unwholesome [dharmas] are attachment and the rest of the desire-realm. And they are caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and the rest through the universal cause. This is the illustration here. 'And the unwholesome' — because it is unspecified, both those to be abandoned by insight and those to be abandoned by cultivation are included. This is the second indicator here. 'That other defiled truth of suffering' is the third indicator. For that other defiled truth of suffering, being unspecified, includes both [dharmas] to be abandoned by insight and by cultivation. Through the universal cause,

body.text: hi bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ pṛthagjanānām ivāryāṇām api satkāyadṛṣṭihetukaṃ na satkāyadṛṣṭer hetur iti vyākhyātam etat. idaṃ tarhi prajñaptibhāṣyam iti. yady akuśalā avyākṛtahetukā api bhavanti na kevalam akuśalahetukāḥ prajñaptibhāṣyaṃ kathaṃ nīyate. syāt. āryapudgalaḥ kāmavairāgyāt [Tib. 198a] parihīyamāṇo yas tatprathamataḥ kliṣṭāṃ cetanāṃ saṃmukhīkarotīti.kāmavairāgyaparihāṇikāle hi sā āryapudgalasya cetanā sahabhūhetunā ca saṃprayuktakahetunā ca akuśalahetukaiva. nāvyākṛtahetukā satkāyāntagrāhadṛṣṭyoḥ prahīṇatvāt. iti prajñaptibhāṣyārtho lakṣyata iti. anenābhiprāyeṇa codayati. vaibhāṣika āha. aprahīṇaṃ hetum etat saṃdhāyoktam iti. aprahīṇaṃ sahabhūhetuṃ saṃprayuktakahetuṃ ca saṃdhāya abhipretya etat prajñaptibhāṣyam uktaṃ. darśanaprahātavyo hi satkāyadṛṣṭyādikaḥ tasyāś cetanāyā hetuḥ. prahīṇatvāt darśanamārgeṇa noktaḥ prajñaptibhāṣya iti.
body.translated_text: it has been explained that [dharmas] to be abandoned by cultivation, for Noble Ones just as for ordinary persons, are caused by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> [but are] not a cause of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. 'This then is [from] the <s>Prajñapti-bhāṣya</s>' — if the unwholesome can also be caused by the indeterminate, [and] not only by the unwholesome, how is the <s>Prajñapti-bhāṣya</s> led [to its conclusion]? It would be [thus]: A Noble Person, declining from dispassion toward the desire-realm, [Tib. 198a] first faces a defiled volition (<s>cetanā</s>). At the time of decline from desire-realm dispassion, that volition of the Noble Person is caused by the unwholesome alone — through the co-existent cause and the associated cause — not by the indeterminate, because the views of self-existing body and grasping at extremes have been abandoned. Thus, the meaning of the <s>Prajñapti-bhāṣya</s> is understood. With this intent, he raises the objection. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'This was said with reference to the unabandoned cause' — with reference to the unabandoned co-existent cause and associated cause, this <s>Prajñapti-bhāṣya</s> was stated. For the <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and the rest, to be abandoned by insight, are a cause of that volition; but because they have been abandoned by the insight-path, [they are] not mentioned in the <s>Prajñapti-bhāṣya</s>.

body.text: (II.55cd)
body.translated_text: (II.55cd)

body.text: akuśalā avaśyaṃ sāsravā eveti na viśeṣyante. kuśalās tu dviprakārāḥ sāsravā anāsravāś ceti. ato viśeṣyante. ye sāsravāḥ kuśalāḥ. te vipākahetur nānāsravā iti. vipākadharmatvād iti. vipaktiprakṛtitvād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: the unwholesome are necessarily with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) — hence they are not further specified. But the wholesome are of two kinds — with outflows and without outflows. Therefore, they are specified. Those that are wholesome with outflows are the retribution cause (<s>vipākahetu</s>), not the outflow-free [wholesome]. 'Because of having the nature of being retributable (<s>vipākadharmatva</s>)' — meaning: because of having the nature of ripening (<s>vipaktiprakṛti</s>).

body.text: durbalatvāt pūtibījavad iti vistaraḥ. yathā pūtīni bījāni abhiṣyanditāny api durbalatvān nāṃkurotpattihetur bhavati. evam avyākṛtā dharmās tṛṣṇābhiṣyanditā api na vipākotpattihetur bhavanti durbalatvāt. anāsravā balavanto 'pi tṛṣṇānabhiṣyanditatvād vipākaṃ [Tib. 198b] na nirvartayaṃti. yathādbhir anabhiṣyanditavāc chuṣkāṇi balavaṃty api sārabījāni nāṃkuraṃ nirvartayaṃti. tadvat. pūrveṣāṃ svaśaktivaikalyam apareṣāṃ sahakārikāraṇāntaravaikalyaṃ. kiṃpratisaṃyuktam iti. kasmiṃ pratisaṃyuktam. kiṃpratisaṃyuktaṃ vipākam apratisaṃyuktāḥ kāmādiṣv apratisaṃyuktā anāsravā abhinirvartayeṣu. pratisaṃyuktena vipākena bhavitavyaṃ. nāpratisaṃyuktena. kāmadhātvādipratisaṃyuktadharmasvabhāvatvāt. śeṣās tv iti vistarah. akuśalāḥ kuśalasāsravāś ca śeṣā ubhayavidhatvāt ubhayaprakāratvāt balavadabhiṣyaṃditaprakāratvād ity arthaḥ. nirvartayaṃti vipākaṃ yathā sārāṇy abhiṣyaṃditāni bījāny aṃkuraṃ. tadvat.
body.translated_text: 'Because of weakness, like rotten seeds' — and so on in detail. Just as rotten seeds, even though moistened, do not, because of weakness, become causes of the arising of sprouts — so too, indeterminate <s>dharmas</s>, even though irrigated by craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), because of weakness, do not become causes of the arising of retribution. And the outflow-free [dharmas], even though powerful, because of not being irrigated by craving, do not produce retribution. [Tib. 198b] Just as dry seeds, even though strong and of good quality, not being moistened by water, do not produce sprouts — likewise. For the former, there is a deficiency in their own capacity; for the latter, a deficiency in the auxiliary cause. 'In connection with what?' — in what are they connected? 'What retribution is the unconnected [dharma] — the outflow-free, unconnected with the desire-realm and the rest — to produce?' The retribution must be connected [to a realm]. Not unconnected — because of being of the nature of <s>dharmas</s> connected with the desire-realm and the rest. 'But the rest' — and so on in detail. The unwholesome and the wholesome-with-outflows — the rest — because of being of both kinds (<s>ubhayavidha</s>), meaning: because of being both powerful and irrigated — they produce retribution, just as good seeds that are moistened produce sprouts. Likewise.

body.text: vipākasya hetur iti vistaraḥ. yadi vipāka iti bhāvasādhano ghañ. vipaktir vipāka iti tatra ṣaṣṭhīsamāsaḥ. vipākasya hetur iti. atha vipacyate svayam iti karmasādhano ghañ. tatra karmasādhano vipāka eva hetur vipākahetur iti. kiṃ cātaḥ kaś cāto doṣaḥ. yadi vipākasya hetur iti bhāvasādhanaparigrahaḥ. vipākajaṃ cakṣur ity etan na prāpnoti. na hi cakṣur vipakter jātaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. vipaktihetoḥ karmaṇa ity arghaḥ. na hi vipāko hetuh. atha vipāka eva
body.translated_text: 'The cause of retribution (<s>vipāka</s>)' — and so on in detail. If <s>vipāka</s> [is analyzed with] the <s>ghañ</s> suffix in the sense of the action (<s>bhāvasādhana</s>) — '<s>vipakti</s> (ripening) is <s>vipāka</s>' — then [it is] a sixth-case compound: 'the cause of retribution (<s>vipākasya hetu</s>).' But if '<s>vipāka</s>' [means] 'it itself ripens' — with the <s>ghañ</s> suffix in the objective sense (<s>karmasādhana</s>) — then '<s>vipāka</s> (that which ripens) itself is the cause' — '<s>vipākahetu</s>.' And what follows from this? What fault [arises]? If the interpretation is '<s>vipākasya hetu</s>' (cause of ripening) — with the action-noun understanding — then 'an eye born of retribution (<s>vipākaja</s>)' would not be possible. For the eye is not born from ripening [as an action]. Rather, from the cause of ripening — i.e., <s>karma</s> — this is the meaning. For retribution [as ripening] is not a cause. But if the interpretation is '<s>vipāka</s> itself is the cause' — with the objective-noun understanding

body.text: hetur iti karmasādhanaparigrahaḥ. sidhyate tad vipākajaṃ cakṣur iti. karmaiva hi [Tib. 199] vipāko vipacyata iti kṛtvā. kiṃ tu karmaṇo vipāka ity etan na prāpnoti. vipāko hi karmaivocyate na vipaktiḥ. karmaṇo vipāka iti cātra bhāvasādhanārtha iṣṭe na karmasādhanārtha iti. tasmāt karmaṇo vipāka ity etan na prāpnoti. ubhayathāpi yoga ity uktaṃ prāg iti
body.translated_text: — 'an eye born of retribution' is established. For <s>karma</s> itself is <s>vipāka</s> (that which ripens) — in the sense of 'it ripens.' [Tib. 199a] But 'the retribution of <s>karma</s>' would not be possible. For <s>vipāka</s> is said to be <s>karma</s> itself, not the ripening [as a result]. And in 'the retribution of <s>karma</s>,' the action-noun sense is desired, not the objective-noun sense. Therefore, 'the retribution of <s>karma</s>' would not be possible. 'Both interpretations are applicable' — as was stated earlier.

children.translated_text: '<s>Vipākaja</s> (born of retribution) and <s>aupacayika</s> (accumulative). The five internal [sense-faculties]' —

body.text: iti atroktaṃ vipākahetor jātā vipākajāḥ. madhyapadalopād gorathavad iti bhāvasādhanaparigrahaḥ. phalakālaprāptaṃ vā karma vipāka ity ucyate. vipacyata iti kṛtvā. tasmāj jātā vipākajā iti karmasādhanaparigrahaḥ. phalaṃ tu vipaktir eveti vipākaḥ. phalavivakṣyāyāṃ bhāvasādhana evaṃ parigṛhyata ity arthaḥ. tasmād vipākajaṃ cakṣur iti madhyapadalopāt karmasādhanaparigrahād vā sidhyati. karmaṇo vipāka iti ca sidhyati. bhāvasādhanaparigrahāt. vivakṣitapūrvikā hi śabdapratipattir iti. visadṛśaḥ pāko vipāka iti. hetor visadṛśaṃ phalam ity arthaḥ. hetur hi vyākṛta eva. phalaṃ tu avyākṛtam eveti. sahabhūhetvādīnāṃ tu sadṛśa eva pāka iti viśeṣaṇaṃ. [Tib. 199b] abhidharmaśāstra evaṃ vyutpādyate tenedaṃ praty ādiśyate.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated here. Born from the <s>vipākahetu</s> are '<s>vipākaja</s>.' With middle term elision, like '<s>goratha</s>' (bull-cart) — this is the action-noun interpretation. Or, <s>karma</s> that has reached the time of fruition is called '<s>vipāka</s>' — in the sense of 'it ripens.' Those born from that are '<s>vipākaja</s>' — this is the objective-noun interpretation. But the result is precisely the ripening — thus '<s>vipāka</s>.' When the result is intended, the action-noun is thus accepted — this is the meaning. Therefore, 'an eye born of retribution' is established — either through middle-term elision or through the objective-noun interpretation. And 'the retribution of <s>karma</s>' is also established — through the action-noun interpretation. 'For the understanding of words is preceded by [the speaker's] intention.' 'A dissimilar ripening (<s>vipāka</s>)' — meaning: the result is dissimilar from the cause. For the cause is always morally determinate, but the result is always morally indeterminate. But for co-existent causes and the rest, the ripening is similar — this is the distinguishing [feature]. [Tib. 199b] 'In the <s>Abhidharma</s> treatise it is etymologized thus and this is responded to accordingly.'

body.text: ekaskaṃdhako vipākahetur ekaphala iti vistaraḥ. iha prāptayo vṛkṣaprapāṭikāvac cittādibhyaḥ pṛthag avasthitāḥ. tāsāṃ paripūrakanyāyena pṛthak phalaṃ varṇyate. ekaḥ skaṃdho 'syety ekaskaṃdhako vipākahetuḥ. (kāyavākkarma tajjātyādayaś ca. vākkarmaṇo rūpaskaṃdhasaṃgṛhītatvāt.) yatra skaṃdhe prāptayaḥ. tatraiva ca tajjātyādaya ity ekaskaṃdhakaḥ. yad eva ca prāptīnāṃ phalaṃ tad eva tajjātyādīnām iti. sādhāraṇaphalatvāt ekaphalaḥ. dviskaṃdhaka ekaphalo vipākahetuḥ. kāyavākkarma tajjātyādayaś ca. kāyavākkarmaṇo rūpaskaṃdhasaṃgṛhītatvāt tajjātyādīnāṃ ca caṃskāraskaṃdhasaṃgṛhītatvāt dviskaṃdhakaḥ. ekaphalaś ca. teṣām apṛthakphalatvāt. catuḥskaṃdhaka ekaphalaḥ kuśalākuśalāś cittacaittā iti. te saha jātyādibhir iti. teṣāṃ cittacaittānāṃ yathāyogaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānaskaṃdhasaṃgṛhītatvāt. jātyādīnaṃ ca saṃskāraskaṃdhasaṃgṛhītatvāc catuḥskaṃdhako vipākahetur ekaphalaḥ sādhāraṇaphalatvāt. na hi cittasyānyat phalam anyac caittādīnām iti asamāhitatvāt. kāmadhātau paṃcaskaṃdhako vipākahetur nāsti. na hy atra rūpaskaṃdhasaṃgṛhītaṃ kāyavākkarma cittacaittair ekaphalaṃ [Tib. 200a] bhavati. pṛthakkalāpatvāt. triskaṃdhakas tu triṣv api dhātuṣu nāsti cittacaittānām avaśyam ekaphalatvāt. yathāyogaṃ catuḥskaṃdhasvabhāvatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'A one-<s>skandha</s> retribution-cause has one result' — and so on in detail. Here, <s>prāptis</s>, standing separately from mind and the rest like bark splitting from a tree, are described as having separate results according to the method of complement. A retribution-cause consisting of one <s>skandha</s> — bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> and their births and the rest. (Because vocal <s>karma</s> is included in the form-aggregate.) The <s>skandha</s> in which the <s>prāptis</s> exist — in that very [skandha] are the births and the rest — hence one-<s>skandha</s>. And whatever is the result of the <s>prāptis</s>, that very [result] is of the births and the rest — because of having a shared result, [it is] one-result. A two-<s>skandha</s> one-result retribution-cause: bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> and their births and the rest. Because bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> are included in the form-aggregate and the births and the rest in the formation-aggregate — hence two-<s>skandha</s>. And one-result — because their results are not separate. A four-<s>skandha</s> one-result [retribution-cause]: wholesome and unwholesome mind and mental factors. Those together with the births and the rest. Of those mind and mental factors, as appropriate, [they are] included in the feeling-, perception-, formation-, and consciousness-aggregates; and the births and the rest are included in the formation-aggregate — hence a four-<s>skandha</s> retribution-cause [that is] one-result, because of having a shared result. For it is not the case that the result of mind is different and that of mental factors and the rest is another — because of being of one assemblage. In the desire-realm, a five-<s>skandha</s> retribution-cause does not exist. For here, bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> included in the form-aggregate does not have one result [Tib. 200a] with mind and mental factors — because of belonging to separate assemblages. But a three-<s>skandha</s> [retribution-cause] does not exist in any of the three realms — because mind and mental factors necessarily have one result, and as appropriate, have the nature of four <s>skandhas</s>.

body.text: rūpadhātāv ekaskaṃdhaka iti vistaraḥ. prāptiḥ saha jātyādibhiḥ saṃskāraskaṃdhasaṃgṛhītety ekaskaṃdhakaḥ. tathaiva sādhāraṇaphalatvāt ekaphalaḥ. asaṃjñisamāpattir api saha jātyādibhiḥ tathaiva vaktavyā. vijñapte rūpaskaṃdhasaṃgṛhītatvāt. jātyādīnāṃ ca saṃskāraskaṃdhasvabhāvatvāt. dviskaṃdhaka ekaphalaḥ pūrvavat. kuśale cetasy asamāhite 'nuparivartirūpaṃ nāstīti rūpaskaṃdhavarjitavedanādiskaṃdhasaṃgṛhītatvāt catuḥskaṃdhakaḥ. paṃcaskaṃdhakaḥ samāhite cetasi. anuparivartirūpasya cittādibhir ekavartitvāt. ārūpyadhātāv iti vistaraḥ. tatra sarvam eva rūpaṃ nāstīty ekaskaṃdhakaś catuḥskaṃdhakaś ca vipākahetuḥ. prāptir iti. tatra saha svajātyādibhir ekaskaṃdhakaḥ pūrvavat. nirodhasamāpattir api saha svajātyādibhir ekaskaṃdhako vipākahetur ekaphala iti sugamaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'In the form-realm, one-<s>skandha</s>' — and so on in detail. <s>Prāpti</s> together with births and the rest is included in the formation-aggregate — hence one-<s>skandha</s>. Likewise, [it is] one-result because of having a shared result. The non-perceptual attainment (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>) too, together with the births and the rest, should be stated in the same way. Because <s>vijñapti</s> is included in the form-aggregate, and the births and the rest have the nature of the formation-aggregate — [it is] two-<s>skandha</s>, one-result, as before. In a wholesome mind that is not concentrated, there is no form following [the mind] — hence, being included in the feeling- and other aggregates excluding the form-aggregate, [it is] four-<s>skandha</s>. In a concentrated mind, [it is] five-<s>skandha</s> — because the form that follows [the mind] operates together with mind and the rest. 'In the formless realm' — and so on in detail. There, because no form at all exists, [there is] one-<s>skandha</s> and four-<s>skandha</s> retribution-cause. As for <s>prāpti</s> — there, together with its own births and the rest, [it is] one-<s>skandha</s>, as before. The cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) too, together with its own births and the rest, is a one-<s>skandha</s> retribution-cause with one result — this is easily understood.

body.text: asti karmeti vistaraḥ. yasya jīvitendriyaṃ vipākaḥ. tasya karmaṇo 'vaśyaṃ tajjīvitendriyaṃ tajjātyādayaś ca viprayuktā vipākaḥ. [Tib. 200b] tac caitat sarvaṃ dharmāyatanasaṃgṛhītam ity ekam āyatanaṃ vipāko vipacyate. yasya manaāyatanaṃ. tasya dve manodharmāyatane. tasya hi manaāyatanasya kalāpe avaśyaṃ vedanādayaḥ sahabhuvo jātyādayaś ca vipākarūpā bhavaṃti. vedanādijātyādayo dharmāyatanasaṃgṛhītā iti te dve manodharmāyatane vipāko vipacyate. evaṃ yasya spraṣṭavyāyatanam iti. tasya spraṣṭavyasyāvaśyaṃ jātyādayas saṃtīti dharmāyatanam api vipacyate. na kevalaṃ spraṣṭavyāyatanam iti dve āyatane tasya vipacyete. yasya kāyāyatanaṃ tasya tṛīṇi. tad eva kāyāyatanaṃ spraṣṭavyāyatanaṃ ca tadāśrayabhūtacatuṣkaṃ. tasyāvaśyaṃ bhūtacatuṣkāśritatvāt. tasya ca jātyādibhir bhavitavyam iti dharmāyatanam api tatra tṛtīyaṃ vipacyate. evam iti vistaraḥ. evaṃ yasya rūpagaṃdharasāyatanānām anyatamad vipākaḥ. tasya trīṇy āyatanāni vipākaḥ. tad evāyatanaṃ rūpādīnām anyatamat spraṣṭavyāyatanaṃ ca tadāśrayabhūtasvabhāvaṃ dharmāyatanaṃ ca tajjātyādisvabhāvam iti. yasya cakṣurāyatanaṃ. tasya catvāri. tad eva cakṣuḥ kāyāyatanaṃ cāvaśyaṃ cakṣuḥkāyapratibaddhavṛttivāt. spraṣṭavyadharmāyatane ca pūrvavat. evaṃ yasyeti vistaraḥ. evaṃ yasya śrotrādīnām [Tib. 201a] anyatamad vipākaḥ. tasyāpi catvāry āyatanāni vipākaḥ. tad eva śrotrādīnām anyatamad āyatanaṃ kāyaspraṣṭavyadharmāyatanāni ca pūrvavat. asti tat karmeti vistaraḥ. paṃca yāvad ekādaśāyatanānīti saṃbhavataḥ. na tu dvādaśāyatanāni vipākaḥ. śabdāyatanasyāvipākasvabhāvatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'There is a <s>karma</s>' — and so forth in detail. For the <s>karma</s> whose retribution (<s>vipāka</s>) is the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>) — the retribution of that <s>karma</s> is necessarily that life-faculty together with dissociated [formations] such as birth (<s>jāti</s>) and the rest. [Tib. 200b] Since all of that is included in the <s>dharma-āyatana</s> (mental-object sense-base), the retribution ripens as one <s>āyatana</s>. For the [karma] whose retribution is the <s>mana-āyatana</s> (mind sense-base) — for that, two [āyatanas]: the <s>manas</s> and the <s>dharma</s> [āyatanas]. For in the assemblage of that <s>mana-āyatana</s>, necessarily feeling and the rest arise as co-existents, and birth and the rest as retribution-form. Since feeling and the rest, birth and the rest are included in the <s>dharma-āyatana</s>, the retribution ripens as those two <s>āyatanas</s> — the <s>manas</s> and <s>dharma</s>. Similarly, for the [karma] whose [retribution is] the <s>spraṣṭavya-āyatana</s> (tangible-object sense-base) — for that tangible [sense-base], birth and the rest necessarily exist, so the <s>dharma-āyatana</s> too ripens — not the <s>spraṣṭavya-āyatana</s> alone. Thus two <s>āyatanas</s> ripen for it. For the [karma] whose retribution is the <s>kāya-āyatana</s> (body sense-base) — for that, three. That very body sense-base, the tangible-object sense-base — the four-element [group] that is its support, necessarily so because of its dependence on the four-element group — and since birth and the rest must exist for it, the <s>dharma-āyatana</s> also ripens there as the third. 'Similarly' — and so forth in detail. Similarly, for the [karma] whose retribution is any one of the form, smell, or taste sense-bases — for that, three <s>āyatanas</s> are the retribution: that very sense-base — whichever one among form and the rest — the tangible-object sense-base having the nature of the element-group that is its support, and the <s>dharma-āyatana</s> having the nature of birth and the rest of that. For the [karma] whose [retribution is] the eye sense-base — for that, four: that very eye, and the body sense-base necessarily, because the eye operates in dependence on the body; and the tangible-object and <s>dharma</s> sense-bases as before. 'Similarly' — and so forth in detail. Similarly, for the [karma] [Tib. 201a] whose retribution is any one of the ear and the rest — for that too, four <s>āyatanas</s> are the retribution: that very sense-base — whichever one among the ear and the rest — and the body, tangible-object, and <s>dharma</s> sense-bases as before. 'There is that <s>karma</s>' — and so forth in detail. [Thus] from five up to eleven <s>āyatanas</s> are possible. But twelve <s>āyatanas</s> are not the retribution — because the sound sense-base (<s>śabda-āyatana</s>) is not of the nature of retribution.

body.text: atrācāryavasumitro vyākhyāpayati. asti karma yasyaikam eva dharmāyatanaṃ vipāko vipacyata iti nopapadyate. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. ākṣepakakarmaphalatvāj
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Vasumitra</s> explains: 'That there is a <s>karma</s> whose retribution ripens as the <s>dharma-āyatana</s> alone — this is not tenable.' Why? Because the life-faculty is the fruit of a projecting <s>karma</s> (<s>ākṣepaka-karma</s>)

body.text: jīviteṃdriyasya. yadi tāvat kāmadhātau jīvitaṃ vipāko vipacyate. karmaṇas tatrāvaśyaṃ kāyajīviteṃdriye bhavataḥ kalalādyavasthāsu anutpanne ṣaḍāyatane. utpanne tu ṣaḍāyatane saptabhir āyatanair bhavitavyaṃ. cakṣurādibhiḥ ṣaḍbhir manaāyatanena ceti. rūpadhātāv api saptabhir ārūpyadhātāv api manodharmaāyatanābhyām avaśyaṃ bhavitavyaṃ. sakalajanmākṣepakaphalatvāj jīviteṃdriyasya. ko vātra dhātur abhipreta iti brūmaḥ. ārūpyadhātuḥ. nanu ca tatrākṣepakakarmaphalatvāj jīviteṃdriyasya avaśyaṃ manaāyatanenāpi bhavitavyaṃ. na ca jīviteṃdriyam eva vipāko vipacyate. vedanāprabhāvitatvād vipākasyeti. vedanayā 'pi tatra bhavitavyam iti. atrocyate. kṣaṇotpattim etat saṃdhāyoktaṃ. yasmiṃ kṣaṇe ārūpyopapannasya [Tib. 201b] vipākajaṃ cittaṃ na samudācarati. tasmin kṣaṇe jīviteṃdriyam eva vipāko vipacyate. vipākasya jīviteṃdriyasyaivotpādān manaāyatanasya cāsamudācārād iti kim arthaṃ tatsamudācāre manaāyatanam aparaṃ na bhavatīti tasya dve manodharmāyatane iti. tad idaṃ vicāryate. bhavaty evaṃ cāksepakasya karmaṇo jīviteṃdriyaṃ vipāka iti. jīviteṃdriye ca vipacyamāne manaāyatanādīny api vipacyaṃte. nāyatanāṃtaravipākaḥ pratiṣidhyate. vipākahetur iha ciṃtyate. asti tat karma yasyaikam eva dharmāyatanaṃ vipacyate. nānyad āyatanam ity etāvad vivakṣitaṃ. atha mataṃ jīviteṃdriyākṣepakasyaiva karmaṇo manaāyatanādīny api vipacyaṃte. naikam āyatanam iti. atra brūmaḥ. tasyaiva karmaṇo 'nye 'pi manaāyatanādayas tatra vartamānā vipāko na punar anyasya karmaṇa iti. kiṃ kṛto 'yaṃ niyamaḥ. asti hi saṃbhavo yad ekasya karmaṇo nikāyasabhāgo vipākaḥ. 'nyasya jīviteṃdriyaṃ. anyasyaiva ca manaāyatanādīni iti. brūyās tvaṃ yathā yasya cakṣurāyatanaṃ. tasya cakṣuḥkāyaspraṣṭavyadharmāyatanānīti vacane yasya cakṣurāyatanaṃ vipākaḥ. tasya kāyāyatanam āvaśyakatvāt. evaṃ manaāyatanādīny api tasyaiva karmaṇo vipāka iti. [Tib. 202a] tan na. kvacid eva kasyacit pratibaddhavṛttitvāt. na hi vinā kāyeṃdriyeṇa cakṣuriṃdriyaprādurbhāvo 'sti. asaty api tu vipāke manasi jīviteṃdriyaprādurbhāvo 'stīti asamam etat. ācāryasaṃghabhadras tv āha. asti karma yasya dharmāyatanam eva vipāko vipacyate. yasya jīviteṃdriyaṃ. yasya cakṣurāyatanaṃ. tasya paṃca. cakṣuḥkāyarūpaspraṣṭavyadharmāyatanāni. evaṃ yāvaj jihvāyatanaṃ. yasya kāyāyatanaṃ. tasya catvāraḥ. kāyarūpaspraṣṭavyadharmāyanānīti. rūpāvinābhāvitvāt rūpāyatanam api tasyaiva cakṣurnirvartakasya
body.translated_text: Because the life-faculty is the fruit of a projecting <s>karma</s>. If to begin with the retribution of life ripens in the desire-realm — for that <s>karma</s>, necessarily the body and life-faculties exist in the embryonic stages such as <s>kalala</s> (when the six sense-bases have not yet arisen). When the six sense-bases have arisen, there must be seven <s>āyatanas</s> — the six beginning with the eye and the <s>mana-āyatana</s>. In the form-realm too, seven [āyatanas]; and in the formless realm too, necessarily the <s>manas</s> and <s>dharma</s> <s>āyatanas</s> — because the life-faculty is the fruit of a <s>karma</s> that projects an entire birth. 'Which realm is intended here?' — we say: the formless realm. 'But is not the life-faculty necessarily the fruit of a projecting <s>karma</s> there [too]? And must there not necessarily be the <s>mana-āyatana</s> as well? Nor does the life-faculty alone ripen as the retribution — because retribution is produced by feeling (<s>vedanā</s>).' And feeling too must exist there — thus. To this it is said: This is stated with reference to momentary arising. In the moment when, for one reborn in the formless realm, [Tib. 201b] the retribution-born mind does not operate — in that moment, the life-faculty alone ripens as the retribution — because only the life-faculty arises as retribution, and the <s>mana-āyatana</s> does not operate. 'Then why, when [the <s>mana-āyatana</s>] does operate, is the <s>mana-āyatana</s> not also [said to ripen] — [making] the two <s>āyatanas</s>, <s>manas</s> and <s>dharma</s>?' This is examined. It is so that the life-faculty of a projecting <s>karma</s> is the retribution. But when the life-faculty ripens, the <s>mana-āyatana</s> and the rest also ripen. The retribution of another <s>āyatana</s> is not denied. The retributive cause (<s>vipākahetu</s>) is what is being considered here. 'There is that <s>karma</s> whose retribution ripens as the <s>dharma-āyatana</s> alone and no other <s>āyatana</s>' — this much alone is what is intended. Now, if you think that the <s>mana-āyatana</s> and the rest also ripen from the very <s>karma</s> that projects the life-faculty, and not from a single <s>āyatana</s> [alone] — to this we say: the retribution of those other <s>mana-āyatanas</s> and the rest present there is of that very <s>karma</s>, not of another <s>karma</s> — [but] why make this restriction? For it is possible that one <s>karma</s> has the <s>nikāyasabhāga</s> (class-homogeneity) as retribution, another has the life-faculty, and yet another has the <s>mana-āyatana</s> and the rest. You might say: just as when the eye sense-base [is the retribution], the body sense-base necessarily [follows] because of its dependent operation, so too the <s>mana-āyatana</s> and the rest are the retribution of that very [same karma]. [Tib. 202a] Not so — because dependent operation [only applies] in some cases for some [dharmas]. For there is no manifestation of the eye-faculty without the body-faculty. But even without retribution-born mind, there is manifestation of the life-faculty — hence this is not analogous. But <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Saṃghabhadra</s> says: 'There is a <s>karma</s> whose retribution ripens as the <s>dharma-āyatana</s> alone — [namely] the [karma] whose [retribution] is the life-faculty. The [karma] whose [retribution] is the eye sense-base — for that, five: the eye, body, form, tangible-object, and <s>dharma</s> sense-bases. Similarly up to the tongue sense-base. The [karma] whose [retribution] is the body sense-base — for that, four: the body, form, tangible-object, and <s>dharma</s> sense-bases.' [He holds that] because form is inseparable [from the sense-faculties], the form sense-base too is the retribution of that very <s>karma</s> that produces the eye

body.text: karmaṇo vipāka iti samayāntaram icchati. ayaṃ tv ācāryo na rūpāyatanam avaśyaṃ tasyaiva karmaṇo vipāka ity aparaṃ pakṣam avalaṃbate. yasya kāyāyatanaṃ. tasya trīṇi. yasya cakṣurāyatanaṃ. tasya catvārīti. na hy anyonyamavinābhāvino jīvitanikāyasabhāgādīny āvaśyakam ekasyaiva karmaṇo vipāka ity abhiprāyaḥ. tāv etau pakṣau vibhāṣyakārair likhitau. tayor yo yasmai rocate. sa tena parigṛhyate. ity alaṃ prasaṃgena.
body.translated_text: — he accepts another position. But this <s>Ācārya</s> [Vasubandhu] relies on the other position — that the form sense-base is not necessarily the retribution of that very <s>karma</s>. 'The [karma] whose [retribution] is the body sense-base — for that, three. The [karma] whose [retribution] is the eye sense-base — for that, four.' For mutually inseparable [dharmas] such as life-faculty, class-homogeneity (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>), and the like are not necessarily the retribution of a single <s>karma</s> — this is the intent. These two positions are recorded by the <s>Vibhāṣā</s> authors. Whichever [position] appeals to whomever — that is adopted by him. Enough of this digression.

body.text: atha kathaṃ kasyacit karmaṇa ekam āyatanaṃ vipāko vipacyate. kasyacid yāvad ekādaśety ata āha. vicitrāvicitraphalatvāt karmaṇo bāhyabījavad iti vistaraḥ. padmadāḍimanyagrodhādīnāṃ [Tib. 202b] bījāni vicitraphalāni. mūlāṃkuranālapattrakeśarākiṃjalkakarṇikāraiś ca rūpyaṃ hi padmabījādīnāṃ. anekaskaṃdhaśākhāviṭapapattrapallavāṃkurapuṣpaphalasamṛddhāś ca nyagrodhādayaḥ pādapā jaladharāyamāṇā dṛśyaṃte. kānicid avicitraphalāni. tadyathā yavagodhūmādīnāṃ bījāni. ekarūpaphalatvāt. bījadharmataiṣā. ekadhvikasya karmaṇo 'tītasya traiyadhviko vipāko vipacyate atītapratyutpannānāgataḥ. na tu dvaiyadhvikasyāpy atītasya pratyutpannasya caikādhviko 'nāgataḥ. na tu viparyayād iti. bahukṣaṇikasya karmaṇa ekakṣaṇikaḥ. mā bhūd atinyūnaṃ hetoḥ phalam iti vartate. na ca karmaṇā saha vipāko vipacyate. sahotpanne sahabhūsaṃprayuktakahetvor vyāpārāt. vipākahetoś ca visadṛśapākāpekṣatvāt. nāpy anaṃtaraṃ vipāko vipacyate. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. samanaṃtarapratyayaākṛṣṭatvāt samanaṃtarakṣaṇasya. yasmāt samanaṃtarakṣaṇaḥ samanaṃtarapratyayabalenākṛṣṭo na vipākahetubalena. yady apy asau samanaṃtarapratyayo vipākahetuḥ itthaṃ caitad eva. yasmāt samanaṃtarakṣaṇo vipākahetoḥ samanaṃtarapratyayāt kadācit kuṣalaḥ kadācid akuśalaḥ kadācid avyākṛtaḥ. [Tib. 203a] anyathā hi avyākṛta eva syāt. atha vā samanaṃtarakṣaṇasya avipākasvabhāvasya samanaṃtarapratyayākṛṣṭatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. pravāhāpekṣo hi vipākahetuḥ cittacaittādipravāhe sati atikrāṃte vipākahetur vipākaṃ dadyāt. dharmataiṣety abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: Now, how is it that for some <s>karma</s> the retribution ripens as one <s>āyatana</s>, and for some up to eleven? Therefore he says: 'Because <s>karma</s> produces varied and unvaried fruits, like external seeds' — and so forth in detail. The seeds of lotus, pomegranate, banyan, and the rest [Tib. 202b] produce varied fruits — with root, sprout, stalk, leaf, filament, stamen, pericarp, and so forth being the form of the lotus seeds and the rest. And banyan and other trees, flourishing with many trunks, branches, twigs, leaves, shoots, sprouts, flowers, and fruits, are seen towering like rain-clouds. Some [seeds] produce unvaried fruits — such as the seeds of barley, wheat, and the rest, because of producing fruit of a single form. This is the nature of seeds. The retribution of a <s>karma</s> belonging to a single time-period — of a past [karma] — ripens across all three time-periods: past, present, and future. But even for a [karma] of two time-periods — past and present — the retribution is of a single time-period: future, not the reverse. The retribution of a <s>karma</s> of many moments is of a single moment. 'Lest the fruit of the cause be exceedingly diminished' — this is the continuation. And the retribution does not ripen simultaneously with the <s>karma</s> — because for simultaneously arisen [dharmas], the co-existent and associated causes operate. And because the retributive cause requires dissimilar maturation. Nor does the retribution ripen immediately after [the karma]. Why? Because the immediately following moment is drawn by the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>). Since the immediately following moment is drawn by the force of the immediately preceding condition, not by the force of the retributive cause. And even though that immediately preceding condition is also a retributive cause, this is nonetheless [the case]. Because the immediately following moment, due to the retributive cause that is the immediately preceding condition, is sometimes wholesome, sometimes unwholesome, sometimes indeterminate. [Tib. 203a] Otherwise, it would only be indeterminate. Or, because the immediately following moment, being of non-retribution nature, is drawn by the immediately preceding condition — this is the intent. For the retributive cause operates with reference to a continuum — when a continuum of mind and mental factors and so forth exists and [time] has passed, the retributive cause gives its retribution. 'This is the natural order' — this is the intent.

body.text: (II.56ab) uktam eṣām arthato 'dhvaniyama iti. arthata ukto na śabdata ity arthaḥ. dvividhaṃ hi vacanaṃ svaśabdābhitaṃ arthoktaṃ ca. kathaṃ.
body.translated_text: (II.56ab) 'The temporal restriction of these has been stated implicitly' — meaning: stated implicitly, not explicitly. For statement is of two kinds: stated in one's own words, and stated implicitly. How?

children.translated_text: 'The homogeneous cause is similar, born from one's own class, [and] earlier-born' —

body.text: tathā
body.translated_text: also:

children.translated_text: 'The [cause] called universal is of defiled [dharmas], on its own level, the earlier universals' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. sabhāgasarvatragahetū atītapratyutpannāv eva sto nānāgatau. aviśeṣavacanād eva sahabhūsaṃprayuktakavipākahetavas traiyadhvikā ity arthata uktāḥ. sabhāgasarvatragahetū eva hi pūrvotpannau. pūrvotpannāv eva ca tāv ity avadhāraṇāt. parasparaphalatvavacanāt. ciṃtādyakuśalādisvābhāvyāc caiṣām anadhvapatitatvaṃ vyāvartitaṃ. sūtryata iti. sūtraṃ sūtrī vā kriyate sūtryate. uktaṃ cātra kāraṇam iti. katham uktaṃ. [Tib. 203b] niṣyaṃdaphalena hi saphalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ. tac cānāgatasyāyuktaṃ pūrvapaścimatābhāvād iti evamādi. yac caitat kāraṇam uktaṃ sabhāgahetoḥ. sarvatragahetor apy uktarūpaṃ veditavyaṃ. sabhāgahetukalpo hi sarvatragahetuḥ. sabhāgahetur hi kliṣṭaḥ kliṣṭānāṃ. sarvatragahetur api kliṣṭaḥ kliṣṭānām eva. kliṣṭadharmasāmānyakāraṇatvena tv ayaṃ sabhāgahetuḥ pṛthag vyavasthāpyata ity uktam etat. sabhāgahetuvad eva cāyaṃ nānāgataḥ. niṣyaṃdaphalena ca saphala iti. tadvad evāsya vārttā.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. The homogeneous and universal causes are past and present only, not future. From the very statement that makes no distinction — the co-existent, associated, and retributive causes belong to all three time-periods — this is stated implicitly. For only the homogeneous and universal causes are earlier-born. And because it is determined that only those two are earlier-born — and because of the statement of mutual fruitfulness — and because of the intrinsic nature of the others such as deliberate [activity], unwholesome [activity], and the rest — their non-restriction to a time-period is excluded. 'It is sutured' (<s>sūtryate</s>) — a <s>sūtra</s> or stitching together is made. 'And the reason for this has been stated' — how was it stated? [Tib. 203b] Because the homogeneous cause has its fruit as the outflow-fruit (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>). And that is unreasonable for the future — because of the absence of the earlier-later distinction — and so forth. And what has been stated as the reason for the homogeneous cause should be understood as also applying to the universal cause. For the universal cause is of the same type as the homogeneous cause. For the homogeneous cause is a defiled [cause] of defiled [dharmas]; the universal cause too is a defiled [cause] of defiled [dharmas] alone. But because it is the general cause of defiled <s>dharmas</s>, this [universal cause] is established separately from the homogeneous cause — this has been said. And just like the homogeneous cause, this too is not future; and it too has its fruit as the outflow-fruit. Its account is just like that [of the homogeneous cause].

body.text: iti. tryadhvakā eva trayas traya eva tryadhvakā iti avadhāraṇāt. kāraṇahetur anyathā bhavati. kathaṃ cānyathā. sarvādhvagaś cadhvavinirmuktaś ceti. svato 'nye hi svabhāvavarjyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ kāraṇahetur iti. ata evam eva bhavati nānyathā.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Of three time-periods only are the three; and only three are of three time-periods' — this is the determination. The efficient cause (<s>kāraṇahetu</s>) is otherwise. How otherwise? '[It] pervades all time-periods and is also free from time-periods.' For all <s>dharmas</s> other than oneself — excluding one's own intrinsic nature — are the efficient cause. Therefore it is precisely so and not otherwise.

body.text: (II.56cd) hetuḥ phalam iti anyonyāpekṣayaitat dvayam ity ataḥ pṛcchati. kiṃ punas tat phalaṃ yasyaitaddhetavaḥ iti.
body.translated_text: (II.56cd) 'Cause' and 'fruit' are mutually dependent terms — therefore he asks: 'What then is the fruit of which these are the causes?'

children.translated_text: 'The conditioned together with disconnection [from afflictions] is the fruit' —

body.text: iti. ākāśāpratisaṃkhyānirodhavarjyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ phalam ity uktaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: thus. It is said that all <s>dharmas</s> excluding space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and non-analytical cessation (<s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) are the fruit.

body.text: evaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. phalatvād asaṃskṛtasya phalam asaṃskṛtam iti kṛtvā [Tib. 204a] hetunā svato 'nyenāsya bhavitavyaṃ. yasya hetos tad asaṃskṛta phalaṃ. hetutvāc cāsaṃskṛtasya svato 'nyenāsya phalena bhavitavyaṃ. yasya phalasya tad asaṃskṛtaṃ hetuḥ. nsaṃskṛtasya te hetuphale. asaṃskṛtaṃ pratisaṃkhyānirodhalakṣaṇaṃ visaṃyogaphalaṃ bhavati. na ca tasya hetur ajanyatvāt. hetuś ca bhavati saṃskṛtotpādāvighnabhāvāvasthānāt. na ca tasya phalaṃ vyavasthāpyate. phalapratigrahaṇadānāsamarthatvāc ca. ata eva ca ṣaḍvidhahetvasaṃbhavād iti vistaraḥ. na sahabhūhetur asya saṃprayuktakahetur vā saṃbhavati. tena kasyacid dharmasyāsahabhavatvāt. asaṃprayogāc ca. na sabhāgahetur asya kaścid bhavati. asaṃskṛtasyāsadṛśatvāt. samānabhūmitvāyogāc ca. ata eva cāsya na sarvatragahetuḥ. asya cākliṣṭatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'Then thus...' — thus the elaboration. Thinking 'the unconditioned is a fruit, therefore [it must have] a cause other than itself — a cause of which that unconditioned is the fruit,' [Tib. 204a] and 'the unconditioned is a cause, therefore [it must have] a fruit other than itself — a fruit of which that unconditioned is the cause.' These are the cause and fruit of the unconditioned. The unconditioned, characterized as <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (analytical cessation), is a <s>visaṃyogaphala</s> (fruit of disconnection). But it has no cause, because it is not produced. And it is a cause, because it functions as non-obstruction of the arising of the conditioned. But no fruit is established for it, and because it is incapable of receiving or giving fruit. 'Therefore, because of the impossibility of the six types of causes' — thus the elaboration. Neither a <s>sahabhūhetu</s> (co-existent cause) nor a <s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s> (associated cause) is possible for it, because it does not co-exist with any <s>dharma</s>, and because of non-association. No <s>sabhāgahetu</s> (homogeneous cause) exists for it, because the unconditioned has no similar [entity], and because belonging to the same ground is not applicable. For this very reason, no <s>sarvatragahetu</s> (universal cause) [exists] for it either, and because it is unafflicted

body.text: na cāsya vipākahetuḥ. asaṃskṛtasyāvipākasvabhāvatvāt. vipāko hi sattvasaṃkhyāto dhātupatito dharmaḥ. anutpādyatvād eva cāsyaite hetavo na bhavaṃti. anutpādyatvād eva cāsya kāraṇahetur na bhavati. ata evocyate. kasmān mārgo visaṃyogasya kāraṇahetur neṣyate. yasmāt sa utpādāvighnabhāvena vyavasthāpitaḥ. na cāsaṃskṛtam utpattimad iti. anadhvapatitatvāc cāsya hetavo na bhavanti. adhvapatitasya hi dharmasya hetur vyavasthāpyate. [Tib. 204b] evaṃ ṣaḍvidhahetvasaṃbhavān nāsaṃskṛtasya hetuḥ. paṃcavidhaphalāsaṃbhavāc ca nāsaṃskṛtasya phalaṃ. kasmāt. sāmānyatas tāvad adhvavinirmuktasya phalapratigrahaṇadānāsamarthatvāt. tathā hy uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: Nor is there a <s>vipākahetu</s> (maturation cause) for it, because the unconditioned does not have the nature of maturation. For maturation is a <s>dharma</s> counted as sentient and fallen into a realm. And precisely because it cannot be produced, these causes do not exist for it. Precisely because it cannot be produced, the <s>kāraṇahetu</s> (efficient cause) does not exist for it. Therefore it is said: 'why is the path not accepted as a <s>kāraṇahetu</s> of disconnection?' Because that [<s>kāraṇahetu</s>] is established through the non-obstruction of arising, and the unconditioned does not have arising. And because it has not fallen into a time-period, causes do not exist for it — for causes are established for a <s>dharma</s> that has fallen into a time-period. [Tib. 204b] Thus, because of the impossibility of the six types of causes, the unconditioned has no cause. And because of the impossibility of the five types of fruit, the unconditioned has no fruit. Why? In general, because [the unconditioned], being free from temporal periods, is incapable of receiving or giving fruit. As has been stated:

children.text: vartamānāḥ phalaṃ paṃca gṛhṇanti. dvau prayacchataḥ
children.translated_text: 'The five [causes] in the present receive fruit; two give [fruit]' —

children.text: ity evamādi. kiṃ ca na tāvad adhipatiphalaṃ bhavati. tad dhi sahotpannaṃ paścādutpannaṃ ceṣyate.
children.translated_text: and so on. Moreover, first, there is no <s>adhipatiphala</s> (dominant fruit), for that is accepted as co-arisen or subsequently arisen.
'The novel, conditioned dominant fruit belongs to the conditioned alone' —

body.text: iti. tac cānutpattimad iti nāsya sahajaṃ paścājjātaṃ vā phalaṃ bhavati. anutpattimattvād eva. na ca niṣyandaphalam. utpattimato hi sadṛśo dharma utpattimān niṣyandaphalam. ata eva ca na puruṣakāraphalaṃ asaṃskṛtasya puruṣakārābhāvāt. yasya hi balena ya utpadyate prāpyate vā. sa tasya puruṣakāraphalaṃ. ata eva ca na visaṃyogaphalaṃ. mārgasyaiva hi balena visaṃyogaḥ prāpyaḥ. na cāsaṃskṛto mārga iti. na cāpi vipākaphalaṃ. vipākahetuvaidharmyāt. sāsravo hi vipākahetuḥ. na cāsaṃskṛtaṃ sāsravam iti. atha vā paṃcavidhahetuvaidharmyāt paṃcavidhaphalāsaṃbhava iti nāsaṃskṛtasya phalaṃ sambhavati. yad mārgo visaṃyogasya kāraṇahetur neṣyate kasyedānīṃ tat phalaṃ. hetumatā hi phalena bhavitavyaṃ kathaṃ vā kena vā prakāreṇa tat phalaṃ. āha. yat tāvad uktaṃ kasyedānīṃ tat phalam iti [Tib. 205a] mārgasya. yad apy uktaṃ kathaṃ vā tat phalam iti phalaṃ tadbalena mārgabalena prāpter ity arthaḥ. atha vaivaṃ padasaṃbandhaḥ. kasya tat phalam iti. mārgasya tat phalaṃ. katham vā tat phalam iti. tadbalena prāpter iti. prāptir eva tarhi mārgasya phalaṃ prāpnoti. tasyām eva prāptau tasya mārgasya sāmarthyāt na visaṃyogaḥ. kiṃ. mārgasya phalam ity adhikṛtaṃ. tatrāsāmarthyād iti. evaṃ tatra visaṃyoge mārgasyāsāmarthyād ity arthaḥ. tasmān na ca tāvad asya mārgaḥ kathaṃcid api hetuḥ. ṣaṇṇāṃ hetūnām anyatamo 'pi hetur asya mārgo na bhavati. phalaṃ cāsya visaṃyogaḥ. prāpyaṃ phalaṃ na janyam ity abhiprāyaḥ. paṃcavidho hi hetur iti kecid icchaṃti. kārako jñāpako vyaṃjako dhvaṃsakaḥ prāpakaś ceti. kārako hetur bījam aṃkurasya. jñāpako dhūmo
body.translated_text: thus. And since [the unconditioned] does not have arising, it has neither a co-arisen nor subsequently arisen fruit — precisely because it does not have arising. Nor is there an <s>niṣyandaphala</s> (outflow fruit), for a similar <s>dharma</s> that has arising and is the outflow fruit of a <s>dharma</s> that has arising [must itself have arising]. For this very reason, there is no <s>puruṣakāraphala</s> (personal-effort fruit) either, because there is no personal effort in the unconditioned — for whatever arises or is attained through the power of something, that is its personal-effort fruit. For this very reason, there is no <s>visaṃyogaphala</s> (disconnection fruit) either, for disconnection is to be attained only through the power of the path, and the path is not unconditioned. Nor is there a <s>vipākaphala</s> (maturation fruit), because of dissimilarity with the <s>vipākahetu</s> — for the <s>vipākahetu</s> is 'with outflows,' and the unconditioned is not 'with outflows.' Alternatively, because of dissimilarity with the five types of causes, the five types of fruit are impossible — thus there is no fruit of the unconditioned. 'Since the path is not accepted as a <s>kāraṇahetu</s> of disconnection, whose fruit is it now? For a fruit must have a cause — and how, or in what manner, is it a fruit?' He says: 'First, regarding what was said "whose fruit is it now?" — [Tib. 205a] it is the path's. And regarding what was said "how is it a fruit?" — it is a fruit through the attainment by the power of that [path]' — meaning: through the attainment by the power of the path. Alternatively, the word-connection is thus: 'whose fruit is it?' — it is the fruit of the path. 'How is it a fruit?' — through the attainment by its power. 'Then the <s>prāpti</s> (possession) itself would follow as the fruit of the path.' With respect to that <s>prāpti</s> itself, by the power of that path — not the disconnection [but the prāpti is the fruit]. What then? 'It is the fruit of the path' — this has been stated. 'Because of the lack of power therein' — the meaning is: because of the lack of power of the path with respect to that disconnection [itself]. Therefore the path is not in any way whatsoever a cause of this [unconditioned]. None of the six causes — not even one — is the path as its cause. And the disconnection is its fruit — the intent is: an attainable fruit, not a produced one. Some accept five types of causation: productive, indicative, revealing, destructive, and conveyive. The productive cause is the seed for the sprout. The indicative is smoke

body.text: 'gneḥ. vyaṃjako dīpo ghaṭasya. dhvaṃsako mudgaro ghaṭasya. prāpako ratho deśāṃtaraprāpaṇīyasyeti. tad evaṃ mārgaḥ prāpako 'sya. na janako hetuḥ. prāpyaṃ ca visaṃyogaphalaṃ na janyam iti darśitaṃ bhavati. athāsaty adhipatiphala iti vistaraḥ. asaṃskṛtasya yadi phalaṃ syāt adhipatiphalaṃ syāt. tasya kāraṇahetutvena vyavasthāpanāt.
body.translated_text: for fire. The revealing is the lamp for the pot. The destructive is the hammer for the pot. The conveyive is the chariot for what is to be conveyed to another place. Thus the path is a conveyor of this [disconnection], not a productive cause. And the <s>visaṃyogaphala</s> is shown to be attainable, not producible. 'If there is no <s>adhipatiphala</s>...' — thus the elaboration. If the unconditioned had a fruit, it would be an <s>adhipatiphala</s>, because it is established as a <s>kāraṇahetu</s>.

body.text: iti vacanāt tad apy asya [Tib. 205b] nivāritam iti paricchinne codakaḥ pṛcchati. athāsaty adhipatiphale katham asaṃskṛtaṃ kāraṇahetuḥ. utpattyanāvaraṇabhāvena kāraṇahetuḥ. utpattyanāvaraṇabhāvavacanāt. saṃskṛtam eva pratīdam asaṃskṛtam kāraṇahetur vyavasthāpyate. nāsaṃskṛtaṃ pratīti darśitaṃ bhavati. kasmād asya saṃskṛtavat phalaṃ na vyavasthāpyata ity ata āha. na cāsya phalam asti. adhvavinirmuktasya phalapratigrahaṇadānāsamarthatvād iti. adhvasaṃgṛhītasyaiva hi dharmasya phalapratigrahaṇadānasāmarthyam asti nānyasya. vakṣyati hi
body.translated_text: because of this statement, that too [Tib. 205b] has been precluded for it — thus the objector, [seeing the matter] decided, asks: 'If there is no <s>adhipatiphala</s>, how is the unconditioned a <s>kāraṇahetu</s>?' '[It is] a <s>kāraṇahetu</s> by way of non-obstruction of arising.' Because of the statement 'by way of non-obstruction of arising,' it is shown that the unconditioned is established as a <s>kāraṇahetu</s> only with respect to the conditioned, not with respect to the unconditioned. 'Why is no fruit established for it as for the conditioned?' Therefore he says: 'And it has no fruit, because, being free from temporal periods, it is incapable of receiving and giving fruit.' For only a <s>dharma</s> included in a temporal period has the capability of receiving and giving fruit, not another. For it will be said:

body.text: iti. uktaṃ tu paryāyeṇa hetur iti. paryāyeṇoktaṃ na svaśabdenety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. 'But it is said to be a cause figuratively' — the meaning is: it is stated figuratively, not by its own proper term.

body.text: te 'py anityā iti. te 'py anityā evety avadhāraṇād arthān na nityo hetur ity uktaṃ bhavati. ālaṃbanapratyayo 'pīti. yathā hetavo 'trānityā uktāḥ. evaṃ pratyayā apy anityā evoktāḥ ye hetavo ye pratyayā iti vacanāt. tasmād asaṃskṛtam ālaṃbanapratyayo na prāpnoti. utpādāyety avadhāraṇād iti. ye hetavo ye pratyayā rūpasyotpādāya. te 'py anityāḥ. na tu ye 'nutpādāya. dvividhā hi pratyayāḥ. janakāś cājanakāś ca. ālambanapratyayaś cājanakaḥ ālambanamātratvāt. ālambanapratyayo hi nirudhyamāne dharme kāritraṃ karoti. vartamānaiś cittacaittair grahaṇāt.
body.translated_text: 'They too are impermanent' — by the restrictive emphasis in 'they too are indeed impermanent,' it is stated that a permanent [entity] is not a cause. 'The <s>ālambanapratyaya</s> (object-condition) also' — just as causes here are stated to be impermanent, so too conditions are stated to be impermanent, because of the statement 'whatever causes and whatever conditions.' Therefore the unconditioned should not qualify as an <s>ālambanapratyaya</s>. 'Because of the restrictive emphasis on "for the arising of"' — 'whatever causes and whatever conditions for the arising of form — they too are impermanent' — but not those [conditions] for non-arising. For conditions are twofold: productive and non-productive. And the <s>ālambanapratyaya</s> is non-productive, because it is merely an object. For the <s>ālambanapratyaya</s> performs its function when a <s>dharma</s> is ceasing — because it is grasped by present mind and mental factors.

body.translated_text: 'Two causes perform their function when [the dharma] is ceasing' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. nanu ca hetavo 'pīti vistaraḥ. hetur api janakaś cājanakaś ca. tasmād asaṃskṛtasyānāvaraṇabhāvamātreṇājanakasyāpikāraṇahetutvāpratiṣedhaḥ. ukta ālambanapratyayaḥ sūtra iti. catasraḥ pratyayatā ity atra sūtre. na tu pratiṣiddhaḥ. dharmatāyā avirodhān na doṣa ity abhiprāyaḥ. sūtrāṇi ca bahūny antarhitāni. mūlasaṃgītibhraṃśāt. atrācāryo na nirbaṃdhaṃ karoti. dharmatāvirodho nāstīti. kiṃ tu asaṃskṛtam eva vicāryate 'sti vā na veti. sarvam evāsaṃskṛtam iti. na kevalaṃ pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. rūpavedanādivad iti. ādiśabdena saṃjñādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ. yathā rūpād vedanābhāvāntaraṃ vedanāyāś ca saṃjñā yāvat saṃskārebhyo vijñānaṃ. tathā na rūpādibhyaḥ paṃcabhyo
body.translated_text: because of this statement. 'But surely causes also...' — thus the elaboration. A cause too is both productive and non-productive. Therefore, since the unconditioned is merely non-obstructive and non-productive, the status of <s>kāraṇahetu</s> is not denied [to it]. 'The <s>ālambanapratyaya</s> is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>' — in the <s>sūtra</s> [stating] 'there are four types of conditionality.' But it is not denied [there]. The intent is: 'there is no fault, because it does not contradict the nature of things.' And many <s>sūtra</s>s have been lost, due to the deterioration of the original collection. The teacher does not insist on this point — [his position is] that there is no contradiction with the nature of things. Rather, the very unconditioned is examined — whether it exists or not. 'All the unconditioned' — not just <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> alone. 'Like form, feeling, etc.' — by the word 'etc.,' perception and the rest are included. Just as feeling is something different from form, and perception from feeling, up to: consciousness from the formations — similarly, from the five [aggregates] of form and the rest

body.text: 'saṃskṛtaṃ bhāvāntaram asti. ato nāsaṃskṛtaṃ dravyam iti sautrāntikāḥ. spraṣṭavyābhāvamātram iti. sapratighadravyābhāvamātram ity arthaḥ. avindanta ity alabhamānāḥ. utpannānuśayajanmanirodhe utpannānām anuśayānāṃ janmanaś ca nirodhe pratisaṃkhyābalena prajñābalena anyasyānuśayasya janmanaś ca anutpādaḥ pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ [Tib. 206b]. tad evaṃ anuśayanirodhaḥ samudayasatya nirodho janmanirodho duḥkhasatyanirodha ity uktaṃ bhavati. sopadhiśeṣanirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇavyavasthāpanārthaṃ cobhayanirodhavacanaṃ. sautrāntikanayena ke '; nuśayāḥ. kathaṃ ca teṣāṃ janmanaś ca pratisaṃkhyābalena nirodhaḥ. aṣṭānavater anuśayānāṃ vāsanā 'nuśayaḥ. yasya cānuśayasya yaḥ pratipakṣo mārgaḥ pratisaṃkhyā. tena saha prathame kṣaṇe so 'nuśaya utpadyate. tadbalād dvitīyādiṣu kṣaṇeṣu tasya nirodhaḥ. tadbalād eva ca paunarbhavikasya janmanaḥ apratisaṃdhiko nirodhaḥ. tadyathā nikāyasabhāgaśeṣasyeti vistaraḥ. nikāyasabhāgo manuṣyatvādilakṣaṇaḥ. ātmabhāvo vā paṃcaskandhalakṣaṇaḥ. tasya śeṣas tallakṣaṇa evotpadyamānaḥ. tasya nikāyasabhāgaśeṣayāntarāmaraṇe āyuṣyaparisamāpta eva pratyayavaikalyād yo 'nutpādaḥ. so 'pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. pratyayavaikalyaṃ punar aṃtyānāṃ skaṃdhānāṃ maraṇabhavākhyānāṃ nikāyasabhāgasaṃbandhane yad asāmarthyaṃ upakaraṇādipratyayāsāmagryāt. ato 'sau pratisaṃkhyānirodha iti. sopadhiśeṣo nirvāṇadhātuḥ. duḥkhasyānutpāda iti nirvupadhiśeṣaḥ. so 'pi tu duḥkhasyānutpādaḥ. yo 'pratisaṃkhyānirodha ity uktaḥ. nāntareṇa pratisaṃkhyāṃ sidhyati. utpattikāraṇānuśayavaikalyasya [Tib. 207a] pratisaṃkhyānakṛtatvāt. ataḥ pratisaṃkhyānirodha evāsau. svarasaṃ nirodhād iti. svātmanā nirodhān na prajñāsāmarthyenety arthaḥ. avinaṣṭe tadabhāvād iti. avinaṣṭe tasmiṃ anuśaye tasyāpratisaṃkhyānirodhasyābhāvāt. akṛtotpattipratibandhānām iti. akṛte utpattau pratibandha eṣām iti akṛtotpattipratibandhāḥ. teṣāṃ. ya utpattipratibandhabhāvaḥ. etad atra pratisaṃkhyāyāḥ sāmarthyaṃ. yadi tarhy anutpāda eveti vistaraḥ. prahāṇaṃ hi nirvāṇam abhipretaṃ. anāgatasyaiva cānutpāda iti yadi nirvāṇam ucyate. atītapratyutpannasyotpannatvāt nāsty anutpāda iti katham idam uktaṃ sūtre. atītānāgatapratyutpannasya duḥkhasya prahāṇāya saṃvartante iti tat sūtrapadaṃ kathaṃ nīyate. yasya punar dravyāntaraṃ nirvāṇaṃ. tasyātītapratyutpannayor api tadāsevanādibhir nirvāṇaṃ prāpyata iti sunītam idaṃ sūtraṃ bhavatīti. tadālambanakleśaprahāṇād iti. atītapratyutpannaduḥkhālambanakleśaprahāṇād ity arthaḥ. yo rūpe chandarāga iti. chando 'nāgate 'rthe prārthanā. rāgas tu prāpte 'rthe 'dhyavasānaṃ. vistareṇa yāvad vijñānam iti. yo vedanāyāṃ saṃjñāyāṃ saṃskāreṣu vijñāne
body.translated_text: ...there exists another conditioned entity. Therefore, the unconditioned is not a [separate] substance — so say the <s>Sautrāntikas</s>. 'Mere absence of the tangible' means mere absence of resistant substance. 'Not finding' means not obtaining. Regarding the cessation of arisen latent afflictions (<s>anuśaya</s>) and birth: through the power of analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyā</s>), i.e., through the power of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), the non-arising of another <s>anuśaya</s> and of birth is <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (analytical cessation). Thus it has been stated that the cessation of <s>anuśayas</s> is the cessation of the truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>), and the cessation of birth is the cessation of the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>). The mention of both cessations is for the purpose of establishing <s>sopadhiśeṣa</s> (nirvāṇa with remainder) and <s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s> (nirvāṇa without remainder). According to the <s>Sautrāntika</s> system, what are the <s>anuśayas</s>? And how is the cessation of them and of birth accomplished through the power of analytical [knowledge]? The latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the ninety-eight <s>anuśayas</s> is [what is called] <s>anuśaya</s>. Whatever path is the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) of a particular <s>anuśaya</s> — that is the analytical [cessation]. Together with that, in the first instant, that <s>anuśaya</s> arises [for the last time]. By its power, in the second and subsequent instants, there is cessation of that [anuśaya]. And by that very power, there is non-reconnection cessation of rebirth (<s>paunarbhavika janma</s>). For example, regarding the remainder of the <s>nikāyasabhāga</s> (homogeneous class) — and so forth in detail. <s>Nikāyasabhāga</s> has the characteristic of humanness and the like, or the self-existence (<s>ātmabhāva</s>) having the characteristic of the five aggregates. Its remainder — that which arises with that very characteristic. In premature death within the remaining <s>nikāyasabhāga</s>, even when the lifespan is not exhausted, the non-arising due to deficiency of conditions — that is <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (non-analytical cessation). The deficiency of conditions is the incapacity of the final aggregates, called the death-existence, to connect with the <s>nikāyasabhāga</s>, due to the non-assemblage of supporting conditions and the like. Therefore it is <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>. The <s>nirvāṇa</s> element with remainder (<s>sopadhiśeṣa</s>) [is the cessation of afflictions]. The non-arising of suffering — that is [the nirvāṇa element] without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>). But that non-arising of suffering is what was called <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>. It is not accomplished without analytical [knowledge], because the deficiency of the causal <s>anuśaya</s> for arising is not accomplished without analytical [effort]. Therefore it is indeed <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>. 'From spontaneous cessation' — meaning from cessation by its own nature, not by the power of wisdom. 'Because of its absence when [the anuśaya] is not destroyed' — because when that <s>anuśaya</s> is not destroyed, that <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> does not exist. 'Of those whose obstruction to arising has not been accomplished' — those for whom the obstruction to arising has not been accomplished. Their state of having an obstruction to arising — this is the capacity of analytical [cessation] here. 'If then it is merely non-arising' — and so forth in detail. For cessation (<s>prahāṇa</s>) is intended as <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And if non-arising of the future alone is called <s>nirvāṇa</s> — since what is past or present has already arisen, there is no non-arising — then how was this stated in the sūtra: 'They conduce to the abandonment of past, future, and present suffering'? How is that sūtra passage to be interpreted? But for one for whom <s>nirvāṇa</s> is a separate substance, even for the past and present, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is attained through practices such as devotion to it — thus this sūtra is well-explained. 'Through the abandonment of afflictions having those as objects' — meaning through the abandonment of afflictions having past and present suffering as objects. 'Whatever desire-and-attachment toward form' — desire (<s>chanda</s>) is longing for an object not yet obtained; attachment (<s>rāga</s>) is adherence to an object already obtained. 'In detail up to consciousness' — whatever desire-and-attachment toward feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness —

([Tib. 207b] chandarāgaḥ. taṃ prajahīta. chandarāge prahīṇe evaṃ vas tad vijñānaṃ prahīṇaṃ bhaviṣyate. evaṃ triyadhvikasyāpi duḥkhasyeti. chandarāgaprahāṇam eva rūpādiduḥkhaprahāṇaṃ. tasya cānāgatasya chandarāgasyānutpādo bhavati. atas triyadhvikasyāpi duḥkhasya prahāṇaṃ yujyata iti darśayati. eṣa eva naya iti. yady atītānāgatapratyutpannasya kleśasya prahāṇāyeti pāṭhaḥ. tatrāpy eṣa eva naya iti. yaḥ kleśe rāge dveṣe vā chandarāgaḥ. taṃ prajahīteti vistaraḥ. tadālambanakleśaprahāṇād api kleśasya prahāṇaṃ. na svabhāvata eveti traiyadhvikasyāpi kleśasya prahāṇaṃ yujyate ity arthaḥ. atha veti vistaraḥ. pūrvajanmani bhavaḥ paurvajanmikaḥ. ihajanmani bhava aihajanmikaḥ. tad evam aikakṣaṇikaḥ kleśaḥ paryudasto bhavati. katham etat pratyetavyaṃ. paurvajanmikaḥ sarvakleśaḥ sambadhyate aihajanmikaś ca. na punar aikakṣaṇika ity ata āha. yathā tṛṣṇā vicariteṣv iti vistaraḥ.
anyatrāpy evaṃ darśanāt evaṃ pratyetavyaṃ. aṣṭādaśa tṛṣṇāvicaritāni katham atīte 'dhvani ekasmiṃ kṣaṇe yojyaṃta iti ato 'tītaṃ janmādhikṛtyoktaṃ. aṣṭādaśa tṛṣṇāvicaritāni. asmīti bhikṣavaḥ satīttham asmīti [Tib. 208a] bhavati. evam asmīti anyathāsmīti sad asmīti asad asmīti bhavati. bhaviṣyāmīty asya bhavati. na bhaviṣyāmītthaṃ bhaviṣyāmi evaṃ bhaviṣyāmi anyathā bhaviṣyāmīty asya bhavati. syām ity asya bhavati. itthaṃ syām evaṃ syāṃ anyathā syām ity asya bhavati. api syām ity asya bhavati. apītthaṃ syām apy evaṃ syām apy anyathā syām ity asya bhavati. evaṃ yāvat pratyutpannaṃ. tathehāpi paurvajanmikaḥ kṛtsnaḥ kleśapravāhaḥ ajhajanmikaś ca saṃbadhyate naikakṣaṇika iti. tad evaṃ prasādhyatābhiprāyaṃ bravīti. tena ca kleśadvayeneti vistaraḥ. paurvajanmikenaihajanmikena ceti kleśadvayenāsyāṃ saṃtatau pratyutpannāyāṃ bījabhāvo vāsanālakṣaṇaṃ sāmarthyam āhito 'nāgate 'syotpattaye. tasya bījabhāvasya prahāṇāt tad api kleśadvayaṃ prahīṇaṃ bhavati. yathā vipākakṣayād vipākopabhogāt karma kṣīṇaṃ bhavatīty upacaryate. tadvat. [Tib. 208b] anāgatasya tarhi kathaṃ prahāṇaṃ vyavasthāpyate. na hi tena saṃtatau bījabhāva āhito yasya prahāṇāt prahāṇaṃ bhaved ity ata āha. anāgatasya punar duḥkhasya kleśasya vā bījabhāvād atyantam anutpḍaḥ prahāṇam iti. bījabhāvaś ca pratisaṃkhyābalena bhavati. na hi niruddhe 'tīte nirodhābhimukhe ca pratyutpanne yatnaḥ pratipakṣotpādane yatnaḥ sārthakaḥ saprayojanam ity arthaḥ. virāgas teṣām agra iti. rāgakṣayo virāgaḥ pratisaṃkhyānirodha ity arthaḥ. katham asatām asann agro bhavitum arhatīti. katham asatām ākāśādīnām asaṃskṛtānām asann asaṃskṛto virāgo 'gro bhavitum arhatīti. asyottaraṃ bravīti. abhāvo 'pi kaścid iti vistaraḥ. dvitīyasya ceti. dvitīyasya samudayasatyasyānaṃtaraṃ
body.translated_text: — that desire-and-attachment — one should abandon it. When desire-and-attachment is abandoned, that consciousness will be abandoned for you. 'Thus even of suffering in the three time-periods' — the abandonment of desire-and-attachment is itself the abandonment of form-and-other suffering. And the non-arising of that future desire-and-attachment occurs. Therefore, the abandonment of suffering in all three time-periods is logical — this is what he demonstrates. 'This same method' — if the reading is 'for the abandonment of past, future, and present affliction,' here too this same method [applies]: whatever desire-and-attachment toward affliction, toward craving or aversion — one should abandon it, and so forth in detail. Through the abandonment of afflictions having those as objects, the affliction too is abandoned — not through [destroying] its own nature — thus the abandonment of affliction in the three time-periods is also logical; this is the meaning. 'Or' — and so forth in detail. Existence in a previous birth is 'of a previous birth' (<s>paurvajanmika</s>). Existence in this birth is 'of this birth' (<s>aihajanmika</s>). Thus the affliction of a single instant is overcome. How is this to be understood?
