The affliction of a previous birth — all afflictions — is bound, as is that of this birth; but not that of a single instant. Therefore he says: 'Just as craving is active regarding...' — and so forth in detail. Since this is seen elsewhere too, it should be understood thus. How can the eighteen activities of craving (<s>tṛṣṇāvicarita</s>) be applied to a single instant in the past time-period? Therefore it was stated with reference to past lives. The eighteen activities of craving: 'There being <I am>, O monks, there comes to be <I am thus>; <I am so>; <I am otherwise>; <I exist>; <I do not exist>. <I shall be> occurs to him; <I shall not be>; <I shall be thus>; <I shall be so>; <I shall be otherwise>. <May I be> occurs to him; <May I be thus>; <May I be so>; <May I be otherwise>.' And so on up to the present. Similarly here too, the entire affliction-continuum of previous births and that of this birth is bound — not that of a single instant. Thus, expressing the intent to be established, he says: 'By those two afflictions' — and so forth in detail. By the two afflictions — of the previous birth and of this birth — in this present continuum, a seed-state, a potency characterized by latent impression, has been deposited for its future arising. Through the abandonment of that seed-state, that pair of afflictions too becomes abandoned. Just as when maturation is exhausted, through the experience of maturation, action is said to be exhausted — so too. How then is the abandonment of the future established? For no seed-state has been deposited by it in the continuum, through whose abandonment there would be abandonment. Therefore he says: 'But for future suffering or affliction, abandonment is the absolute non-arising from the seed-state.' And the seed-state comes about through the power of analytical [cessation]. For exertion in producing the antidote is meaningful and purposeful regarding what has ceased and is past, and what is present and facing cessation. '<s>Virāga</s> (dispassion) is the foremost of those' — the destruction of attachment (<s>rāga</s>) is dispassion, meaning <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (analytical cessation). 'How can what is non-existent be the foremost of non-existent things?' — how can non-existent dispassion, which is unconditioned, be the foremost of non-existent unconditioned things like space? The answer to this he states: 'Even a certain absence...' — and so forth in detail. 'And of the second' — immediately after the second, the truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>) —

body.text: dṛṣṭaṃ svayaṃ prajñayā uddiṣṭaṃ parebhyo deśanayā trayāṇāṃ pūraṇaṃ tṛtīyaṃ bhavati. kiṃ syād iti. ko dośaḥ syād ity arthaḥ. kiṃ ca punaḥ syād iti. ko guṇaḥ syād ity arthaḥ. kiṃ ca punaḥ syād iti guṇaparipraśna āha. vaibhāṣikapakṣaḥ pālitaḥ syād iti. yat tūktaṃ kiṃ syāt ko doṣaḥ syād iti atrocyate. abhūtaṃ tu parikalpitaṃ syād iti. doṣaḥ syād ity arthaḥ. rūpavedanādivad iti. pratyakṣataḥ. [Tib. 209a] cakṣurādivad iti. karmato numānata ity arthaḥ. asakṛdvyākhyātam etat. vastuna iti. rāgādivastunaḥ. hetuphalādibhāvasaṃbhavād iti. ādiśabdena svasvāmyavayavāvayavisambandhādayo gṛhyante. na hi vastuno nirodhe hetuḥ phalam avayavāvayavītyevamādi. tasyaitarhi prāptiniyama iti vistaraḥ. tasya nirodhasya yo 'yaṃ prāter niyamaḥ. asyaiva nirodhasya prāptir nānyasyeti tasmiṃ prāptiniyame ko hetuḥ. na hi nirodhasya prāptyā sardhaṃ kaścit saṃbandho 'sti hetuphalādibhāvāsaṃbhavāt. dṛṣtadharmanirvāṇaprāpta iti. sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇastha ity arthaḥ. yady abhāvaḥ katham asya prāptiḥ syāt. pratipakṣalābheneti vistaraḥ. āryamārgalābhena kleśasya punarbhavasya cotpāde 'tyantaviruddhasyāśrayasya lābhāt prāptaṃ nirvāṇam ity ucyate. abhāvamātratvam iti. mātraśabdo dravyāntaratvanivṛttyarthaḥ. yat khalv asyeti vistaraḥ. prahāṇaṃ yāvad aprādurbhāva iti paryāyaśabdā ete. aprādurbhāva ity etat sphuṭam ity udāharaṇam uktaṃ. nāsmiṃ prādurbhāva ity ato 'prādurbhāvā ity adhikaraṇasādhanam [Tib. 209b] iti darśayanti. na tu aprādurbhūtir aprādurbhāva iti bhāvasādhanam ity arthaḥ. yata eva tatprāptiḥ parikalpyate yato mārgāt prahāṇaḥ prāptaḥ parikalpyate. tasmiṃ sati mārge prāpte vā duḥkhasyeṣyatām aprādurbhāvaḥ. kim anyena nirvāṇena parikalpitena. vimokṣas tasya cetasa iti. nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇakāle bhagavataḥ. yathāvastu yathālambanaṃ. saṃyogasya vastu yatra kleśena saṃyujyate. sa vastukā dharmā iti sahetukāḥ. parigrahavastu parigṛhyata iti parigrahaḥ. sa eva vastu parigrahavastu.
body.translated_text: — 'seen' by oneself through wisdom, 'taught' to others through instruction — the fulfillment of three [turnings] constitutes the third. 'What would be?' means 'what fault would there be?' 'And what further would be?' means 'what virtue would there be?' In response to this inquiry about the virtue, he says: 'The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> position would be maintained.' As for what was said — 'what would be, what fault would there be?' — to this it is replied: 'But something unreal would be imagined' — meaning there would be a fault. 'Like form, feeling, and so on' — through direct perception. 'Like the eye and so on' — meaning through inference from function. This has been explained many times. 'Of the object' — of the object [such as] attachment and the like. 'Because of the possibility of cause-fruit and other relations' — by the word 'and the like,' relations such as owned-owner, part-whole, and so on are included. For in the cessation of an object, there is no cause, fruit, part-whole, and the like. 'Then there would be a restriction of its <s>prāpti</s> (acquisition)' — and so forth in detail. This restriction of acquisition of that cessation — the acquisition of only this cessation and no other — what is the cause of that restriction of acquisition? For cessation has no relation with <s>prāpti</s>, since the possibility of cause-fruit and other relations does not exist. 'One who has attained <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the visible <s>dharma</s>' — meaning one abiding in <s>nirvāṇa</s> with remainder (<s>sopadhiśeṣa</s>). 'If it is absence, how can there be acquisition of it?' 'Through obtaining the antidote' — and so forth in detail. Through obtaining the noble path (<s>āryamārga</s>), through obtaining a basis that is absolutely opposed to the arising of affliction and renewed existence, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is said to be attained. 'Mere absence' — the word 'mere' is for the purpose of excluding being a separate substance. 'What indeed of this' — and so forth in detail. Abandonment, up to non-manifestation — these are synonymous terms. Non-manifestation — this is stated as a clear example. They show that 'non-manifestation' is a locative compound meaning 'there is no manifestation in this,' not an abstract noun meaning 'the state of non-manifesting.' Since acquisition of it is conceived from that very [path] from which abandonment is attained — when that path exists or is attained, let the non-manifestation of suffering be accepted. What need is there of another imagined <s>nirvāṇa</s>? 'Liberation of that mind' — at the time of <s>nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s> (nirvāṇa without remainder) of the Blessed One. 'According to the real object' (<s>yathāvastu</s>) — according to the object of support (<s>yathālambana</s>). The object of connection (<s>saṃyogavastu</s>) — that with which one is conjoined by affliction; <s>dharmas</s> having that as their object — meaning having causes. The object of possession (<s>parigrahavastu</s>) — what is grasped is possession; that very thing is the object of possession.

body.text: (II.57) ante 'bhihitatvād iti. kārikāyā ante vipākahetuḥ paṭhitaḥ. tasya vipākaphalam eva.
body.translated_text: (II.57) 'Because it is stated at the end' — the <s>vipākahetu</s> (maturation cause) is read at the end of the verse (<s>kārikā</s>). Its [fruit] is the <s>vipākaphala</s> (maturation fruit) alone.

body.text: kāraṇahetuḥ ślokādau paṭhitatvāt. tasy-
body.translated_text: the <s>kāraṇahetu</s> (efficient cause), because it is read at the beginning of the verse. Its —

body.text: adhipatir adhipaḥ. tasmāj jātaṃ adhipajaṃ adhipatiphalam ity arthaḥ. pūrvasyādhipatam iti kecit paṭhanti. adhipater idaṃ phalaṃ ādhipatam iti. ādhipatyam iti tu prāpnoti. dityadityādityapatyuttarapadāṇ ṇya ity apavādāt.
body.translated_text: <s>Adhipati</s> (predominant) means ruler (<s>adhipa</s>). That which is born from it is <s>ādhipaja</s>, meaning <s>adhipatiphala</s> (predominant fruit). Some read '<s>ādhipata</s> of the first.' '<s>Ādhipata</s>' meaning 'this is the fruit of the <s>adhipati</s>.' But grammatically, '<s>ādhipatya</s>' would be obtained, since there is a specific grammatical rule regarding words like <s>aditya</s> and <s>apatya</s> in the final position.

body.text: athāpavādaviṣaye 'py utsargasamāveśa iti bhavet. bhavec ca tadrūpaṃ. etad evādhipatyam iti. yad anāvaraṇabhāvamātrāvasthānaṃ. aṃgībhāvo 'pi vāstīti. pradhānabhāvo 'pi janakabhāvo 'pīty arthaḥ. tad anena dvividhasyāpi kāraṇahetoḥ kārakasya vādhyupekṣakasya vādhipatiphalam [Tib. 210a] astīti darśitaṃ bhavati anyatrāsaṃskṛtāṭ. yasmād vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: Or there might be subsumption of the general rule even in the domain of the exception. And that form would be possible. 'This alone is predominance (<s>ādhipatya</s>)' — which is the mere state of non-obstruction. 'Or there is also the state of being a factor' — meaning also the state of being principal, also the state of being a producer. Thus by this it has been shown that the <s>adhipatiphala</s> (predominant fruit) exists for both types of <s>kāraṇahetu</s> (efficient cause) — whether active or merely permissive — except for the unconditioned. Because it will be stated:

children.translated_text: 'The unprecedented [fruit] of a conditioned <s>adhipati</s> (predominant) is only conditioned.'

body.text:
iti. daśānām āyatanānām iti. cakṣūrūpāyatanayor yāvat kāyaspraṣṭavyāya
tanayoḥ. cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpāṇi cotpadyate cakṣurvijñānaṃ yāvat kāyaṃ pratītya spraṣṭavyāni cotpadyate kāyavijñānam iti vacanāt. kāraṇahetur eva cāyaṃ. na hi cakṣurādīny āyatanāni cakṣurvijñānādīnāṃ sahabhūhetvādayaḥ. paṃca hetavaḥ saṃbhavaṃti. manaāyatanaṃ tu manovijñānasya sabhāgahetvādi saṃbhavati. dharmāyatanam api sahabhūsaṃprayuktakahetvādi saṃbhavatīti na kāraṇahetur evety avadhāryate. tasmād daśānām ity uktaṃ na dvādaśānām iti. bhājanaloke ca karmaṇāṃ. kim. aṃgībhāvo 'sti kāraṇahetor ity adhikṛtaṃ. bhājanaloko hi kuśalākuśalakarmajanito 'py avyākṛto 'pi na vipākaphalam iṣyate. sattvākhyo vipāka iti lakṣaṇāt. tasmāt kāraṇahetor etad adhipatiphalaṃ. śrotrādīnām api na kevalaṃ cakṣuṣo 'sti. kiṃ. cakṣurvijñānasyotpattau pāraṃparyeṇādhipatyaṃ. na sākṣāt yathā cakṣuṣaḥ. kathaṃ jñāyata iti āha. śrutvā draṣṭukāmatotpatteḥ. draṣṭukāmatāyāṃ ca cakṣurvijñānam utpadyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. [Tib. 210b] evamādi yojyam iti. ghrātvā draṣṭukāmatotpatter ity ādi yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: Thus. 'Of the ten sense-bases' — of the eye and form sense-bases, up to the body and tangible sense-bases. Because of the statement: 'Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises; up to: dependent on the body and tangibles, body-consciousness arises.' And this is exclusively the efficient cause (<s>kāraṇahetu</s>). For the sense-bases such as the eye are not the co-existent cause and so forth of eye-consciousness and the rest — five causes are possible. But the mind sense-base can be the homogeneous cause and so forth of mental consciousness. And the <s>dharma</s> sense-base can also be the co-existent and associated cause and the rest — therefore it is not determined to be exclusively the efficient cause. Hence 'of the ten' was stated, not 'of the twelve.' 'And regarding the container-world (<s>bhājanaloka</s>), of actions' — what? Whether there is inclusion [as a fruit] of the efficient cause — this is what is under discussion. For the container-world, though produced by wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>, and though being indeterminate, is not accepted as a maturation-fruit — because of the definition 'maturation is being-designated.' Therefore this is the predominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>) of the efficient cause. 'Even the ear and the rest, not just the eye, have' — what? — 'dominance over the arising of eye-consciousness, indirectly' — not directly as the eye [does]. How is this known? He says: 'Because of the arising of the desire to see upon hearing.' The intent is that eye-consciousness arises from the desire to see. [Tib. 210b] 'And so on should be applied' — 'because of the arising of the desire to see upon smelling' — and so on should be applied.

children.translated_text: 'The outflow-fruit (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>) [belongs to] the homogeneous and universally pervasive [causes]' —

body.text: phalam iti vartate. sabhāgasarvatragahetvor eva niṣyandaphalam ity avadhāryate. puruṣakāraphalam api hi tayor anantaraṃ saṃbhavati.
body.translated_text: 'fruit' is the continuation. It is determined that the outflow-fruit belongs exclusively to the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>) and the universally pervasive cause (<s>sarvatragahetu</s>). For the personal-effort fruit (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>) too is possible for those two immediately [after].

body.text: iti. puruṣakāraphalam eva sahabhūsaṃprayuktakahetvor ity avadhāraṇaṃ. puruṣakārasya phalaṃ paurusaṃ. puruṣakāraphalam ity arthaḥ. puruṣabhāvāvyatirekāt puruṣakāraḥ puruṣabhāvān na vyatiriktaḥ. puruṣakarmaiva hi puruṣakāro na puruṣād anyaḥ. na hi karma karmavadbhyo 'nyad iṣyate bauddhaiḥ. tasmāt puruṣakārasya yat phalaṃ. tat puruṣasyaiveti pauruṣam ity ucyate. yasya dharmasya yat kāritram iti. yasya dharmasya yat karma yā kriyā. sā tasya puruṣakāra ity arthaḥ. nanu cāntarvyāpārapuruṣābhāve dharmamātraṃ puruṣa iti ato dharmakāra iti prāpnoti. na puruṣakāra ity ata āha. puruṣakāra iva hi puruṣakāraḥ. yathā loke kalpitasya puruṣasya puruṣakāraḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. The personal-effort fruit belongs exclusively to the co-existent and associated causes — this is the restriction. The fruit of personal effort (<s>puruṣakāra</s>) is <s>pauruṣa</s> (personal). The meaning is: the personal-effort fruit. 'Because of the non-difference from the person's nature' — personal effort is not different from the person's nature. For personal action itself is personal effort, not something other than the person. For the <s>Bauddha</s>s do not accept that action is different from the agent. Therefore, the fruit of personal effort is the fruit of the person himself — hence it is called <s>pauruṣa</s>. 'Whatever is the activity of whatever <s>dharma</s>' — whatever action, whatever function of whatever <s>dharma</s> — that is its personal effort, this is the meaning. 'But in the absence of an internal agent-person, it would be merely <s>dharma</s> [acting as] person, so it should follow that [it is called] "<s>dharma</s>-effort," not "personal effort"' — therefore he says: 'Personal effort is like personal effort.' Just as in the world, the personal effort of a conventionally designated person [is so called]

body.text: evaṃ dharmasyāpīti puruṣakāra iva puruṣakāraḥ. dṛṣṭāntaṃ kathayati. kākajaṃghā oṣadhir ityādi. kākajaṃghākārā oṣadhiḥ kākajaṃghety ucyate. mattahastīva yo dṛṣṭaḥ śūro vā. sa manuṣyo mattahastīti. kim anyeṣām [Tib. 211a] iti. hetūnāṃ. anyeṣām apy astīti. sabhāgasarvatragakāraṇahetūnāṃ. anyatra vipākahetoḥ. kasmād ity āha. yasmāt sahotpannaṃ samanantarotpannam vā puruṣakāraphalam iti. sahabhūsaṃprayuktakahetvor hi sahotpannaṃ phalam uktaṃ. tac ca puruṣakāraphalam eva. na hy anyat phalaṃ sahotpannam asti. sabhāgasarvatragahetvor anaṃtarotpannam eva puruṣakāraphalaṃ. kāraṇahetos tūbhayathā. kiṃ punar niṣyandaphalād adhipatiphalād vānyat puruṣakāraphalaṃ. nety ucyate. tad eva hi phalaṃ tattan nāma labhate. tathā hi taddhetusadṛśotpatter niṣyandaphalaṃ. tadbalenotpatteḥ puruṣakāraphalaṃ. avighnabhāvāvasthānenotpatteś cādhipatiphalam iti. na caiva vipākaḥ. kiṃ. sahotpanno vā samanantarotpanno vety adhikṛtaṃ.
body.translated_text: so too of a <s>dharma</s> — hence it is personal effort like personal effort. He states an illustration: '<s>Kākajaṅghā</s> (crow's shin) is an herb' and so on. The herb shaped like a crow's shin is called <s>kākajaṅghā</s>. A hero who looks like a mad elephant is [called] 'a mad elephant' — that person. 'Of others' — [Tib. 211a] of [other] causes. 'Others too have [it]' — the homogeneous, universally pervasive, and efficient causes [also have the personal-effort fruit]. Except the maturation cause. Why? He says: 'Because the personal-effort fruit is co-arisen or immediately-after-arisen.' For the fruit of the co-existent and associated causes was stated as co-arisen. And that is exclusively the personal-effort fruit. For no other fruit is co-arisen. The personal-effort fruit of the homogeneous and universally pervasive causes is immediately-after-arisen only. But for the efficient cause, [it can be] either way. 'Is the personal-effort fruit something other than the outflow-fruit and the predominant fruit?' It is said: no. For that very fruit receives those names [respectively]. Thus, because of arising similar to its cause, it is the outflow-fruit. Because of arising by its power, it is the personal-effort fruit. And because of arising through the state of non-obstruction, it is the predominant fruit. And maturation is not — what? — either co-arisen or immediately-after-arisen — this is what is under discussion.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration.

body.text: eva
body.translated_text: exclusively.

body.text: eva
body.translated_text: exclusively.

body.text: evety avadhāraṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: exclusively — this is the restriction.

body.text: iti anivṛtāvyākṛto vivakṣitaḥ. sattva iti ākhyā yasya. sa
body.translated_text: the intended meaning is: uncovered-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>). One whose designation (<s>ākhyā</s>) is 'being' (<s>sattva</s>) —

body.text: sattvasaṃtānaja ity arthaḥ. vyākṛtād udbhavatīti
body.translated_text: The meaning is: born in the continuum of a being. That which arises from the determinate (<s>vyākṛta</s>) —

body.text: aupacayikanaiṣyandikau tu na vyākṛtād udbhavataḥ. [Tib. 211b] nanu ca indriyamahābhūtopacayo dhyānaviśeṣasamāpannasya bhavati. asāv api vyākṛtād udbhavati. sa vipākaḥ prāpnoti. nirmāṇacittaṃ cāpi. tathaiva samādhicittasaṃbhūtatvāt. naiṣa doṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: But the accumulative and the outflow [types] do not arise from the determinate. [Tib. 211b] 'But the accumulation of faculties and great elements occurs for one who has attained a special <s>dhyāna</s>. That too arises from the determinate. So it would qualify as maturation. And the supernaturally-created mind too — likewise, because of being produced from a <s>samādhi</s>-mind.' This is not a fault.

body.text: ity ucchabda uttarakālārthaḥ. vyākṛtāt kuśalād akuśalād vā ya uttarakālam eva bhavati na yugapan nāpy anantaraṃ. sa vipāka iti. samādhijas tūpacayaḥ samādhinā saha cānantaraṃ ca bhavati. nirmāṇacittaṃ tv anaṃtaram eva ca bhavati. vipākaś ca samānabhūmika evābhipreta ity etac cobhayaṃ bhinnabhūmikam
body.translated_text: herein, the prefix <s>ut</s> has the meaning of 'subsequently.' That which arises only subsequently from the determinate — wholesome or unwholesome — not simultaneously and not immediately after, that is maturation. But the accumulation produced by <s>samādhi</s> occurs both simultaneously with and immediately after the <s>samādhi</s>. And the supernaturally-created mind occurs only immediately after. And maturation is intended as belonging to the same ground only — and both of these

body.text: api bhavatīti na vipākasya prasaṃgaḥ.
body.translated_text: can also belong to different grounds — therefore there is no consequence of [their being] maturation.

children.translated_text: 'The outflow is similar to the cause' —

body.text: iti. kuśalakliṣṭānivṛtavyākṛtasādṛśyam adhikṛtya. yady evaṃ kuśalasāsravasya hetor anāsravaṃ niṣyandaphalaṃ prāpnoti kuśalasādṛṣyāt. na. nikāyasādṛśyābhāvāt. samānanikāyo hi sabhāgahetur iṣyate. na sarvaḥ. bhūmitaḥ kliṣṭatayā cāsya sādṛśyam iti. asya sarvatragahetoḥ sādṛśyaṃ bhūmitaḥ kliṣṭatayā ca. kena saha. svaphalena. katham iti. bhūmitas tāvat sarvatragahetuḥ kāmāvacaro yāvad bhāvāgrikaḥ. tatphalam api kāmāvacaraṃ yāvad bhāvāgrikam iti. kliṣṭatayā ca sarvatragahetur api kliṣṭaḥ. tatphalam api kliṣṭaṃ. na tu prakārataḥ sādṛśyaṃ yathā sabhāgahetoḥ. [Tib. 212a] yasya tu prakārato 'pi sādṛśyaṃ. yasya sarvatragahetoḥ svaphalena saha prakārato 'pi sādṛśyaṃ. sa sarvatragahetur abhyupagamyate eva sabhāgahetur iti. bhūmikliṣṭatvasādṛśyād dhi sarvatragahetur bhavati. sabhāgahetuś ca sa bhavati prakārato 'pi sādṛśyāt. ata eva catuṣkoṭikaḥ kriyate. ubhayasvabhāvatayā tṛtīyakoṭisaṃbhavāt. prathamā koṭir asarvatragaḥ sabhāgahetur iti. rāgādikaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ. sa hi sabhāgahetur eva svanaikāyikasya kleśasya. na tu sarvatragahetur asarvatragasvabhāvatvāt. dvitīyānyanaikāyikaḥ sarvatragahetur iti. satkāyadṛṣṭyādikaḥ sarvatragaḥ. sa hi sarvatragahetur eva sarvatragasvabhāvatvāt. anyanaikāyikakliṣṭahetutvāc ca. na sabhāgahetuḥ. anyanaikāyike kliṣṭe sabhāgahetutvābhāvāt. tṛtīyā ekanaikāyikaḥ sarvatragahetur iti. satkāyadṛṣṭyādikaḥ sarvatragaḥ. sa hi ekanaikāyikasya kleśasya sabhāgahetuḥ. ekanaikāyikakliṣṭasādṛśyāt. sarvatragahetuś ca saḥ. tasya sarvatragatvād ekanaikāyikakliṣṭahetutvayogena sarvatragahetutvayogāc ca. caturthī etān ākārān sthāpayitveti. trikoṭyuktāṃ dharmaprakārāṃ varjayitvety arthaḥ. tadyathā kliṣṭā dharmāḥ kuśalānāṃ na sabhāgahetur asādṛśyāt. na sarvatragahetuḥ. ata eva kuśalānāṃ cākliṣṭatvāt. [Tib. 212b] evaṃ kuśalāḥ kliṣṭānāṃ yojyaṃ. kliṣṭā api kliṣṭānāṃ na sabhāgahetuḥ. nāpi sarvatragahetur bhavanti. tadyathā rāgādayo 'nyanaikāyikānāṃ kliṣṭānāṃ na sabhāgahetur anyanaikāyikatvāt. na sarvatragahetur asarvatragatvād rāgādīnām iti. sarvatragā api dharmāḥ kliṣṭānām ekanaikāyikānām api na sabhāgahetur na sarvatragahetuḥ. yady anāgatās te bhavantīti yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. With reference to similarity as wholesome, afflicted, or uncovered-indeterminate. 'If so, then the non-outflow [fruit] of a wholesome-with-outflow cause should follow, because of the similarity of being wholesome.' No — because of the absence of class-similarity (<s>nikāyasādṛśya</s>). For a cause belonging to the same class is accepted as the homogeneous cause, not every [similar cause]. 'Its similarity with its own fruit is through ground and through being afflicted' — the similarity of this universally pervasive cause [with its fruit] is through ground and through being afflicted. With what? With its own fruit. How? First, through ground: the universally pervasive cause belongs to the desire realm up to the peak of existence, and its fruit too belongs to the desire realm up to the peak of existence. And through being afflicted: the universally pervasive cause is also afflicted, and its fruit is also afflicted. But there is no similarity in type, as with the homogeneous cause. [Tib. 212a] 'But for that which has similarity in type also' — that universally pervasive cause which has similarity in type with its own fruit — that universally pervasive cause is accepted as being also a homogeneous cause. For it is a universally pervasive cause through similarity of ground and being afflicted, and it is a homogeneous cause also through similarity of type. Therefore a fourfold classification is made — because of the possibility of the third alternative through having both natures. The first alternative: 'a non-universal homogeneous cause' — desire and the like [serve as] the homogeneous cause. For it is the homogeneous cause only of the affliction of its own class, but not the universally pervasive cause, because of not having a universally pervasive nature. The second: 'a universally pervasive [cause] of another class' — the view of the self-existing body and the like, which is universally pervasive. For it is the universally pervasive cause only, because of having a universally pervasive nature, and because of being the cause of afflicted [<s>dharma</s>s] of another class. But not the homogeneous cause — because of the absence of being a homogeneous cause for afflicted [<s>dharma</s>s] of another class. The third: 'a universally pervasive [cause] of the same class' — the view of the self-existing body and the like, which is universally pervasive. For it is the homogeneous cause of the affliction of the same class, because of similarity to an affliction of the same class. And it is the universally pervasive cause — because of its universality, through the connection of being a universally pervasive cause as well as a cause of afflictions of the same class. The fourth: 'setting aside these aspects' — the meaning is: excluding the types of <s>dharma</s>s mentioned in the three alternatives. For example, afflicted <s>dharma</s>s are not the homogeneous cause of wholesome ones, because of dissimilarity; nor the universally pervasive cause — for this very reason, and because wholesome [<s>dharma</s>s] are unafflicted. [Tib. 212b] Likewise, wholesome of afflicted should be applied. Even afflicted [<s>dharma</s>s] are neither the homogeneous cause nor the universally pervasive cause of [some other] afflicted [<s>dharma</s>s]. For example, desire and the rest are not the homogeneous cause of afflicted [<s>dharma</s>s] of another class, because of being of another class; nor the universally pervasive cause, because desire and the rest are not universally pervasive. Even universally pervasive <s>dharma</s>s are neither the homogeneous cause nor the universally pervasive cause of afflicted [<s>dharma</s>s] of the same class — this should be applied if they are future.

children.translated_text: 'Disconnection (<s>visaṃyoga</s>) is [the fruit of] cessation [attained] through wisdom' —

body.text: dhiyā prāpyamāṇo nirodho visaṃyogaphalam ity arthaḥ. teneti. tena kāraṇena. yasmāt kṣayo nirodho dhīḥ prajñā. tena kāraṇena pratisaṃkhyānirodho visaṃyogaphalam ity uktaṃ bhavatīty ācaṣṭe.
body.translated_text: the meaning is: the cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) attained through wisdom is the disconnection-fruit (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>). 'Therefore' — for that reason. Because cessation is destruction and wisdom is <s>dhī</s> (intellect) — for that reason, analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) is called the disconnection-fruit — this is what he explains.

children.translated_text: 'That which arises through the power of which' —

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. yasya balaṃ yadbalam iti ṣaṣṭhīsamāsaḥ. yasya balāj jāyate
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration. 'Whose power' — the power of which — this is a genitive compound. 'That which arises through whose power' —

body.text: saṃskṛtaṃ.
body.translated_text: conditioned [<s>dharma</s>].

body.text: tasya
body.translated_text: 'of that' —

body.text: puruṣakārāj jātaṃ puruṣakārajaṃ puruṣakāraphalam ity arthaḥ. udāharaṇaṃ kathayati. tadyathā adharabhūmikasya kāmāvacarasya prathamadhyānabhūmikasya vā tatprayogacittasya uparibhūmikaḥ prathamadhyānabhūmiko dvitīyadhyānabūmiko vā samādhiḥ. phalaṃ puruṣakārajam ity adhikṛtaṃ. sāsravasya dharmasya anāsravaḥ. dhyānacittasya nirmāṇacittaṃ tad eva phalaṃ bhavati. [Tib. 213a] ādiśabdenānyad api. tadyathā kāmāvacarān maraṇacittād rūpāvacaraḥ prathamo 'ntarābhavakṣaṇa ity evamādi vijātīyodāharaṇaṃ niṣyandaphalavivecanārthaṃ. adharabhūmikasya hi prayogacittasya uparibhūmikaḥ samādhir na niṣyandaphalaṃ. bhinnabhūmikaṃ hi na hetusadṛśaṃ. nāpi sāsravasya anāsravam iti vaktavyaṃ. na tu sarvaṃ niṣyandaphalaṃ puruṣakāraphalaṃ bhavati yad dhi yasya balāj jāyate sadṛśaṃ samānabhūmikaṃ anaṃtaraṃ ca bhavati. tat tasya puruṣakāraphalaṃ niṣyandaphalaṃ ca bhavati. catuḥkoṭikaṃ cātra bhavati. asti puruṣakāraphalam eva na niṣyandaphalaṃ. yathodāhṛtaṃ. asti niṣyandaphalam eva na puruṣakāraphalaṃ. sabhāgasarvatragahetvor vyavahitaṃ phalaṃ. asty ubhayaṃ. samanantarotpannaṃ sabhāgasarvatragahetvoḥ phalam. asti nobhayaṃ. tadyathā vipākahetor vipākaphalaṃ. pratisaṃkhyānirodho 'pi puruṣakāraphalam iṣyate. na cāsau hetubalāj jāyate nityatvād ity ataḥ kārikāyām anuktaṃ tad upasaṃcaṣṭe. pratisaṃkhyānirodhas tu yadbalāt prāpyata iti vaktavayam iti. pratisaṃkhyābalena hi pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ prāpyate. tasmāt sa pratisaṃkhyāyāḥ puruṣakāraphalaṃ [Tib. 213b] bhavati.
body.translated_text: born from personal effort is 'born of personal effort' — the meaning is: the personal-effort fruit. He states an illustration: for example, the <s>samādhi</s> of a higher ground — of the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground or the second <s>dhyāna</s> ground — [which is the fruit] of the preparatory mind belonging to a lower ground — the desire realm or the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground — is a fruit born of personal effort, this is what is under discussion. A non-outflow [<s>dharma</s>] of an outflow <s>dharma</s>; a supernaturally-created mind of a <s>dhyāna</s>-mind — that very same is the fruit. [Tib. 213a] By the word 'and so forth,' other [examples] too: for example, from the death-mind belonging to the desire realm, the first intermediate-existence moment belonging to the form realm — and so forth. Such cross-type illustrations serve to distinguish [this from] the outflow-fruit. For the <s>samādhi</s> of a higher ground is not the outflow-fruit of the preparatory mind of a lower ground — for what belongs to a different ground is not similar to the cause. Nor should the non-outflow [be said to be the outflow-fruit] of the outflow — this should be stated. But not every outflow-fruit is a personal-effort fruit: for that which arises through the power of which, being similar, belonging to the same ground, and immediately [subsequent] — that is both the personal-effort fruit and the outflow-fruit of that [cause]. And herein there is a fourfold classification: there is [what is] personal-effort fruit alone and not outflow-fruit — as illustrated above. There is outflow-fruit alone and not personal-effort fruit — the non-contiguous fruit of the homogeneous and universally pervasive causes. There is both — the immediately-subsequent fruit of the homogeneous and universally pervasive causes. There is neither — for example, the maturation-fruit of the maturation-cause. Analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) too is accepted as a personal-effort fruit. But since that does not arise through the power of a cause — because of being permanent — what is not stated in the verse, he supplements: 'But it should be said: analytical cessation is attained through the power of that [wisdom].' For analytical cessation is attained through the power of analytical [wisdom]. Therefore it is the personal-effort fruit [Tib. 213b] of analytical [wisdom].

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. apūrvaḥ pūrvotpannād anyaḥ. kaḥ punar asau. sahotpannaḥ paścādutpannaś ca. na hi pūrvaṃ phalaṃ paścād dhetur bhavati. saṃskṛta eva dharmo 'dhipatiphalaṃ nāsaṃskṛtaḥ. saṃskṛtasyaiva nāsaṃskṛtasya. phalapratigrahaṇadānāsamarthatvāt. sarvasyeti. janakasyāvighnabhāvāvasthāyinaś ca. kartuḥ puruṣakāraphalam iti.
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration. 'New' means other than the previously arisen. What then is that? Co-arisen and subsequently arisen. For a fruit does not come first and the cause later. Only a conditioned <s>dharma</s> is a predominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>), not an unconditioned one — [the predominant fruit] of the conditioned only, not of the unconditioned, because of the incapability of receiving and giving fruit. 'Of all' — of both the generator and the one abiding in non-obstruction. 'The personal-effort fruit is of the agent' —

children.text: yadbalāj jāyate yat tat phalaṃ puruṣakārajam
children.translated_text: 'That which arises by the power of which — that is the fruit born of personal effort' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. akartur apy adhipatiphalam iti.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. 'The predominant fruit is even of the non-agent.'

children.translated_text: 'The unprecedented fruit of the sovereign [cause] is conditioned, of the conditioned alone' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. anyeṣām adhipatiphalam eveti. aśilpinām avighnabhāvāvasthāyināṃ tacchilpam adhipatiphalam eva na puruṣakāraphalaṃ. tad evaṃ catuḥkoṭikaṃ bhavati. asti puruṣakāraphalam eva nādhipatiphalaṃ. tadyathā visaṃyogaphalaṃ. asty adhipatiphalam eva na puruṣakāraphalaṃ. udāsīnasya hetor vyavahitaṃ ca phalaṃ. asty ubhayaṃ. sahotpannaṃ anantarotpannaṃ ca kārakasya hetoḥ. asti nobhayaṃ. tadyathā ākāśam apratisaṃkhyānirodhaś ceti.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. 'For others, it is the dominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>) only' — for those without skill, those who remain in a state without obstruction, that skill is the dominant fruit only, not the fruit of personal effort (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>). Thus, there is a fourfold distinction (<s>catuṣkoṭi</s>). [1] There exists the fruit of personal effort only, not the dominant fruit — for example, the fruit of disconnection (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>). [2] There exists the dominant fruit only, not the fruit of personal effort — the [mediated] fruit of an indifferent cause, and also one that is obstructed. [3] There exists both — the co-arisen and immediately subsequent fruit of an active cause. [4] There exists neither — for example, space and non-analytical cessation.

body.text: vartamānā eva phalaṃ
body.translated_text: 'Only when present do they receive fruit' —

body.text: avadhāraṇaṃ. pratigṛhṇantīti. ākṣipanti [Tib. 214a] hetubhāvenāvatiṣṭhanta ity arthaḥ. kāraṇahetur apy evam iti. vartamāna eva phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti natīto nānāgato vā. sa tu nāvaśyaṃ saphala iti nocyate. hy asaṃskṛtaṃ kāraṇahetur iṣyate. na cāsya phalam asti. anāgataś ca kāraṇahetuḥ. na ca pūrvam utpadyamānena dharmeṇa saphalaḥ.
body.translated_text: this is a restriction. 'Receive' means they draw [the fruit]; [Tib. 214a] meaning: they are established in the state of being causes. 'The universal cause (<s>kāraṇahetu</s>) too likewise' — it too receives fruit only when present, not when past or future. But it is not said to be 'necessarily fruitful' — because the unconditioned is accepted as a universal cause, and it has no fruit. And the future is also a universal cause, but it is not fruitful with respect to a <s>dharma</s> arising earlier.

body.text: iti. vartamānāv adhikṛtaṃ. sahabhūsaṃprayuktakahetū vartamānāv eva phalaṃ prayacchataḥ. yuktaṃ tāvad yad atītāv iti. niṣyandaphalena saphalāv etāv uktau.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Present' is the topic. The co-existent cause and the associated cause, only when present, give fruit. 'It is fitting, at least, that when past...' — these two have been stated as fruitful through the outflow result (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>).

children.translated_text: 'The outflow [result] is of the homogeneous and universal [causes]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. atha kathaṃ vartamānau niṣyandaphalaṃ prayacchataḥ. na hi tayor vartamānāvasthāyāṃ niṣyando dṛśyate ity ata āha. samanantaranirvartanāt. kiṃ. phalaṃ prayacchata ity adhikṛtaṃ. tau cāpy atītau bhavata iti. hetuphalayor asamavadhānāt. na punas tad eva datta iti. na punas tad eva phalaṃ prayacchata ity arthaḥ. datta iti hy ākhyātapadaṃ dvivacanāntaṃ. vartamānāvasthāyām eva dattatvāt. na hi vartamānatām ānītaṃ punar ānetuṃ śakyate. yadā ca tāv atītau phalaṃ prayacchataḥ. tadaiva tat svaphalaṃ prayacchataḥ. utpadyamānāvasthāyām eva hi phalaṃ nirvartate nānyadā. kevalaṃ tu vyavahitam tat phalam ity avagantavyaṃ. kuśalamūlāni samucchindan yāḥ prāptīḥ sarvapaścād vijahātīti. iha kuśalamūlāni [Tib. 214b] krameṇa samucchidyante. kathaṃ. mithyādṛṣṭir navaprakārā. mṛdumṛdvī yāvad adhimātrādhimātrā. kuśalamūlāny api nava prakārāṇi tadviparyayeṇa mṛdumṛdvyā mithyādṛṣṭyādhimātrādhimātrāṇi kuśalamūlāni samucchidyante yāvad adhimātrādhimātrayā
body.translated_text: because of this statement. But how do these two, when present, give the outflow result? For no outflow of theirs is seen in their present state. Therefore he says: 'Because of producing [it] immediately after.' What? 'They give fruit' — this is the topic. 'And those two also become past' — because the cause and fruit are not simultaneous. 'But not that same [fruit] given [again]' — meaning: they do not give that same fruit again. For '<s>datta</s>' is a verbal form in the dual number. Because it was given in the present state only. For what has been brought to the present cannot be brought [to the present] again. And when those two, having become past, give fruit — at that very time they give their own fruit. For the fruit is produced only in the state of arising, not at any other time. But that fruit should be understood as obstructed [i.e., mediated]. 'When cutting off wholesome roots, the <s>prāptis</s> that one relinquishes last' — here, wholesome roots [Tib. 214b] are cut off sequentially. How? Wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) is ninefold: mild-mild up to intense-intense. Wholesome roots too are ninefold, in reverse — by the mild-mild wrong view, the intense-intense wholesome roots are cut off, up to: by the intense-intense

body.text: mithyādṛṣṭyā mṛdumṛdūni kuśalamūlāni samucchidyante. bhāvanāheyakleśavat. tatrāṃtyāvasthāyāṃ mṛdumṛdūni kuśalamūlāni na samudācaraṃti. prāptayas tu teṣāṃ mṛdumṛdūnāṃ samudācaranti. tāḥ sarvapaścimakās tadā vijahāti. tāsāṃ prāptīnāṃ prāptīr nirodhayatīty arthaḥ. tāḥ prāptayo 'ntyavasthāḥ kuśalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti. phalaparigrahaṃ karoti. na dadāti svaniṣyandaphalaṃ. kuśalasya kṣaṇāntarasya janyasyābhāvāt. dvitīyā koṭih. dadāti na pratigṛhṇātīti. kuśalamūlāni pratisaṃdadhāno yāḥ sarvaprathamaṃ pratilabhate. yāḥ prāptīḥ sarvapūrvaṃ pratilabhate. tāḥ kuśalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ dadātīti. prāptiṃ svaniṣyandaṃ janayati. na tu pratigṛhṇāti pūrvam eva pratigṛhītatvāt. ayaṃ tu sāvadyo dvitīyakoṭinirdeśaḥ. kuśalamūlapratisaṃdhānakāle hi navaprakārāṇām api kuśalamūlānāṃ prāptayo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannāḥ samaṃ pratilabhyaṃte. tāsāṃ yā atītāḥ prāptayaḥ. sa kuśalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ dadāti na pratigṛhṇāti pratigṛhītatvād [Tib. 215a] iti yuktam etat. yās tu vartamānās tathaiva pratilabdhāḥ prāptayaḥ. sa kuśalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ katham avadhāryate. phalaṃ dadāty eva na pratigṛhṇātīti. sa hi pratigṛhṇāti ca dadāti ceti. evam aviśeṣitatvāt sāvadyo 'yaṃ dvitīyakoṭinirdeśaḥ. tasmād ācarya āha. evaṃ tu vaktavyaṃ syāt. tā eva pratisaṃdadhānasyeti. tā eva prāptayaḥ kuśalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ dadāty eva svaniṣyandaphaladānāt. na pratigṛhṇāti pūrvapratigṛhītatvāt. tṛtīyā koṭiḥ. phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti dadāti ceti. asamucchinnakuśalamūlasya śeṣāsv avasthāsv iti. dve avasthe hitvā. yasyām avasthāyāṃ kuśalamūlāni samucchindan yāḥ prāptīḥ sarvapaścād vijahāti. yasyāṃ cāvasthāyāṃ kuśalamūlāni pratisaṃdadhāno yāḥ sarvaprathamaṃ pratilabhate. yathāsmadādīnāṃ kuśalāḥ prāptayaḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇanti dadati ceti. visabhāgakṣaṇāntarāvyavahita iti vaktavyaṃ. na vaktavyaṃ. visabhāgakṣaṇāntaravyavadhāne 'pi prāptilakṣaṇasya sabhāgahetoḥ phalapratigrahaṇadānasaṃbhavāt. caturthy etān ākārān sthāpayitvā. tadyathā ūrdhvabhūmeḥ parihīṇasya [Tib. 215b] ūrdhvabhūmikānāṃ kuśalānāṃ yāḥ prāptayaḥ. tāḥ kuśalaḥ sabhāgahetur na phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti. pūrvaṃ pratigṛhītatvāt. na dadāti. tadbhūmiparihīṇasya tadbhūmikānāṃ kuśalamūlānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prāptyabhāvāt. evaṃ samucchinnakuśalamūlavasthāyām api vaktavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: wrong view, the mild-mild wholesome roots are cut off — like the afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation. Therein, at the final stage, the mild-mild wholesome roots no longer operate. But the <s>prāptis</s> of those mild-mild [wholesome roots] do operate. Those last ones are then relinquished — meaning: the <s>prāptis</s> of those <s>prāptis</s> are ceased. Those <s>prāptis</s> at the final stage — the wholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> — receive fruit; they take on the fruit. They do not give — they do not give their own outflow result — because of the non-existence of a subsequent wholesome moment to be generated. This is the second alternative (<s>koṭi</s>). 'Gives but does not receive' — when one who is reconnecting wholesome roots first obtains [them], the <s>prāptis</s> that one obtains first of all — those, as the wholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s>, give fruit — they generate a <s>prāpti</s> as their own outflow. But they do not receive — because they were received previously. But this statement of the second alternative has a flaw. For at the time of reconnecting wholesome roots, the <s>prāptis</s> of all nine types of wholesome roots — past, future, and present — are obtained simultaneously. Of those, the past <s>prāptis</s> — the wholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> — give fruit but do not receive, because they were received previously — [Tib. 215a] this is appropriate. But the present <s>prāptis</s> that are likewise obtained — that wholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> — how is it determined that [it] gives fruit only and does not receive? For it both receives and gives. Thus, because of being unspecified, this statement of the second alternative has a flaw. Therefore the <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'It should rather be stated thus: those very [<s>prāptis</s>] of one who is reconnecting...' Those very <s>prāptis</s> — the wholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> — give fruit only, because of giving their own outflow result; they do not receive, because they were received previously. But in the former reading, the second alternative is not tenable, as stated before. The third alternative: '[it] receives fruit and gives' — for one whose wholesome roots are not cut off, in the remaining states. Excluding two states: the state in which, when cutting wholesome roots, one relinquishes the last <s>prāptis</s>; and the state in which, when reconnecting wholesome roots, one first obtains [them]. In [those] remaining states, just as our own wholesome <s>prāptis</s> both receive fruit and give. 'One should say: unobstructed by a dissimilar intervening moment.' One need not say [this]. Because even when obstructed by a dissimilar intervening moment, it is possible for a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> with the character of <s>prāpti</s> to receive and give fruit. The fourth [alternative], excluding these [other three] aspects: for example, for one who has declined from a higher ground, [Tib. 215b] the <s>prāptis</s> of wholesome [dharmas] of that higher ground — that wholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> — does not receive fruit, because it was received previously; and does not give, because of the non-existence of <s>prāptis</s> of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> of that ground for one who has declined from that ground. The same should be stated for the state of having cut off wholesome roots.

body.text: atrācāryasaṃghabhadra āha. naitad yujyate yad uktam. evaṃ tu vaktavyaṃ syāt. tā eva pratisaṃdadhānasyeti. kasmāt. na hi yās tāḥ sarvapaścādvihīnāḥ. tāsām eva tan niṣyandaphalaṃ. yāḥ pratisaṃdadhānaḥ sarvaprathamaṃ
body.translated_text: Here the master <s>Saṃghabhadra</s> says: 'This is not fitting — what was stated: "It should rather be stated thus: those very [<s>prāptis</s>] of one who is reconnecting."' Why? 'For it is not the case that those which were last relinquished — their outflow result is that which one who is reconnecting first obtains.'

body.text: pratilabhata iti. pūrvaniruddhasyāpi hi tatprāptisaṃtānasya sa niṣyanda iti. ataḥ kathaṃ phalagrahaṇāt kṛtsna eva tatsabhāgahetur gṛhītaḥ syād iti tadartham evedam ucyate. tasmād yathānyāsa eva sādhv iti. tad eva ubhayatrāpi pāṭhadoṣa udgrāhite kataraḥ pāṭhaḥ śreyān iti. atrābhidharmapāṭha eva śreyān iti paśyāmaḥ. nanu coktam. aviśeṣitatvāt kuśalapratisaṃdhānakāle pratilabdhā vartamānāḥ prāptayaḥ phalaṃ dadati pratigṛhṇanty api. nanu dadaty eva na pratigṛhṇantīti doṣa iti. naiṣa doṣaḥ. kuśalamūlāni pratisaṃdadhāna iti kuśalamūlaprāptyutpadyamānāvasthāyām etad ucyate na vartamānāvasthāyāṃ tatra ca na kāścid api kuśalamūlaprāptayo vartamānā bhavaṃti. tāḥ kathaṃ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇanti dadati ceti [Tib. 216a] śakyate vaktuṃ. atītās tu svasaṃtāne kuśalamūlaprāptayaḥ sarvā api sabhāgahetubhūtāḥ svaniṣyandaphalaṃ tadānīṃ dadaty eva. samanantaranirvartananyāyena. na pratigṛhṇanti. pūrvaṃ pratigṛhītatvāt. ity anayā yuktyābhidharmapāṭham eva samarthayāmaḥ. nanu caivam aviśeṣite pāṭhe anāgatānāṃ kuśalamūlaprāptīnāṃ dvitīyakoṭitvavacanaprasaṃgaḥ. tā api hi tadānīm atītaprāptivat prāpyante. naiṣa doṣaḥ. anāgatānāṃ sabhāgahetutvābhāvāt sabhāgahetoś cehādhikṛtatvāt. evam api na prāptaya eva vaktavyāḥ. yā eva sarvaprathamaṃ pratilabhata iti. evaṃ tu vaktavyaṃ syāt. yān sarvaprathamaṃ pratilabhata iti. yān kuśalān dharmān ity arthaḥ. cittacaittā api hi kuśalapratisaṃdhāne prathamataḥ pratilabhyante. na kevalaṃ tatprāptayaḥ. asty etat. kiṃ tu prāptīnām eva kuśalapratisaṃdhāne āvaśyakatvād evaṃ vacanaṃ. kuśalaprāptayo hi samyagdṛṣṭyā vicikitsayāpi vā kuśalapratisaṃdhāne 'vaśyam utpadyante. cittacaittās tu vicikitsayā kuśalapratisaṃdhāne na tāvad utpadyanta iti prāptaya evotpadyanta iti varṇayamti.
body.translated_text: 'For even the continuum of <s>prāptis</s> that ceased earlier is that outflow [result].' Therefore, 'how could the entire <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of that [type] be included by the reception of fruit?' — for this purpose alone is this stated. Therefore, 'the reading as originally given is better.' 'That being so, [when] a reading-flaw has been identified in both [versions], which reading is better?' Here, 'we see the <s>Abhidharma</s> reading itself as better.' [Objection:] 'But was it not stated that because of being unspecified, the present <s>prāptis</s> obtained at the time of reconnecting wholesome roots both give fruit and receive — and [stating them under] "gives only, does not receive" is a flaw?' This is not a flaw. 'When one is reconnecting wholesome roots' — this is said with reference to the state when the wholesome-root <s>prāptis</s> are arising, not their present state. And in that [arising state], no wholesome-root <s>prāptis</s> at all are present. How then can it be said [Tib. 216a] that they both receive fruit and give? But all the past wholesome-root <s>prāptis</s> within one's own continuum that have the nature of <s>sabhāgahetu</s> — they give their own outflow result at that time, by the principle of immediately subsequent production. They do not receive, because they were received previously. By this reasoning, we justify the <s>Abhidharma</s> reading itself. [Objection:] 'But if the reading is thus unspecified, there would be the consequence of stating the future wholesome-root <s>prāptis</s> as the second alternative. For those too are obtained at that time, like past <s>prāptis</s>.' This is not a flaw — because future [<s>prāptis</s>] do not have the nature of <s>sabhāgahetu</s>, and the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> is the subject here. 'Even so, it is not only <s>prāptis</s> that should be stated' — [namely,] 'those which one first obtains.' Rather, it should be stated thus: 'those which one first obtains' — meaning: those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> [which one first obtains]. For mind and mental factors too are first obtained at the reconnection of wholesome roots — not only their <s>prāptis</s>. 'This is so. But because only <s>prāptis</s> are necessarily [involved] at the reconnection of wholesome roots, the statement is thus.' For wholesome <s>prāptis</s> necessarily arise at the reconnection of wholesome roots through right view or even through doubt. But mind and mental factors are not yet produced at the reconnection of wholesome roots through doubt — therefore only <s>prāptis</s> are produced — thus they explain.

body.text: akuśalasyeti vistaraḥ. akuśalo 'pi sabhāgahetuś catuṣkoṭikaḥ. asty akuśalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti na dadātīti vistareṇa. [Tib. 216b] prathamā koṭiḥ. kāmavairāgyam anuprāpnuvan yāḥ prāptīḥ sarvapaścād vijahāti. tā akuśalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti na dadāti. kathaṃ kṛtvā. iha kleśo navaprakāraḥ. mārgo 'pi navaprakāraḥ. tatra mṛdumṛdunā mārgeṇādhimātrādhimātraḥ kleśaprakāraḥ prahīyate. yāvad adhimātrādhimātreṇa mṛdumṛduḥ prahīyate. tatprāptayo 'pi tathaiva prahīyante. kāmavairāgyam anuprāpnuvan yā mṛdumṛdūnām akuśalānāṃ prāptīḥ sarvapaścād vijahāti. tā akuśalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti na dadāti. akuśalaprāptikṣaṇāntarābhāvāt. dvitīyā. kāmavairāgyāt parihīyamāṇo yāḥ sarvaprathamaṃ pratilabhate akuśalānāṃ prāptīḥ. tā akuśalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ dadāti na pratigṛhṇāti pūrvavad vaktavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Of the unwholesome' — and so on in detail. The unwholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> too is fourfold (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>). 'There exists an unwholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> that receives fruit but does not give' — and so on in detail. [Tib. 216b] The first alternative: one who is achieving dispassion from the desire-realm relinquishes the last <s>prāptis</s>. Those — the unwholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> — receive fruit but do not give. How so? Here the affliction is ninefold; the path too is ninefold. Therein, by the mild-mild path, the intense-intense type of affliction is abandoned; up to: by the intense-intense [path], the mild-mild [type] is abandoned. Their <s>prāptis</s> too are likewise abandoned. One who is achieving dispassion from the desire-realm relinquishes the <s>prāptis</s> of the mild-mild unwholesome [dharmas] last. Those — the unwholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> — receive fruit but do not give — because of the non-existence of a subsequent moment of unwholesome <s>prāpti</s>. The second [alternative]: one who is declining from dispassion toward the desire-realm first obtains the <s>prāptis</s> of unwholesome [dharmas]. Those — the unwholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> — give fruit but do not receive, because they were received previously — as stated before.

body.text: atrācāryo bravīti. evaṃ tu vaktavyaṃ syāt. ta eva parihīyamāṇasyeti. tā eva yāḥ kāmavairāgyam anuprāpnuvan prāptīḥ sarvapaścād vijahātīti. tā hi pratigṛhītatvāt na pratigṛhṇanti. dadaty eva tu kevalaṃ phalaṃ. pūrvapāṭhe tu dvitīyā koṭir na saṃbhavati yathoktaṃ prāk.
body.translated_text: Here the <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'It should rather be stated thus: those very [<s>prāptis</s>] of one who is declining...' Those very <s>prāptis</s> that one who was achieving dispassion from the desire-realm relinquished last — those, because they were already received, do not receive; they only give fruit. In the former reading, however, the second alternative is not tenable, as was stated before.

body.text: atrācāryasaṃghabhadras tathaiva pratyācaṣṭe. naitad yujyata iti. pūrveṇa samānam etat. sarvaṃ prapaṃcayitavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: Here the master <s>Saṃghabhadra</s> refutes in the same way: 'This is not fitting.' This is the same as before. All [the argumentation] should be elaborated.

body.text: Tib. 217a
body.translated_text: Tib. 217a

body.text: tṛtīyā. kāmavītarāgasya śeṣāsv avasthāsv iti. dve avasthe hitvā. ete eva yathokte prathamadvitīyāvasthe śeṣāsv avasthāsu. yathāsmākaṃ. yā akuśalānāṃ prāptayaḥ. tā akuśalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti dadāti ca. caturthī. etān ākārān yathoktān sthāpayitvā. tadyathā kāmavītarāgasyaparihāṇadharmaṇo yā akuśalānāṃ prāptayaḥ. so 'kuśalaḥ sabhāgahetur na phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti. pūrvaṃ pratigṛhītatvāt. na dadāti. tasya prāptyabhāvāt. evaṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtasyāpīti vistaraḥ. evaṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtasyāpi catuḥkoṭikavidhānam. arhattvaprāptito 'rhattvaparihāṇitaś ca yathāyogaṃ yojyaṃ. asti nivṛtāvyākṛtaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti na dadātīti vistaraḥ. prathamā koṭiḥ. arhattvaṃ prāpnuvan yāḥ prāptīh sarvapaścād vijahāti. sa nivṛtāvyākṛtaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti na dadāti. kliṣṭakṣaṇāntarābhāvāt. dvitīyā. arhattvāt parihīyamāṇo yāḥ sarvaprathamaṃ pratilabhate. evaṃ tu vaktavyaṃ syāt. tā eva parihīyamāṇasyeti. evaṃ hi phaladānam evaikam [Tib. 217b] upapāditaṃ bhavati. pūrvapāṭhasamarthanam api tenaivānukrameṇa vaktavyaṃ. tṛtīyā. bhavāgravītarāgasya śeṣāsv avasthāsu. caturthī. etān ākārān sthāpayitvā. tadyathā arhattvaṃ prāptasya yās tridhātukyo nivṛtāvyākṛtānāṃ prāptayaḥ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ. sa nivṛtāvyākṛtaḥ sabhāgahetur na phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti. pratigṛhītatvāt. na dadāti. prahīṇatvāt. anivṛtāvyākṛtasya paścātpādaka iti. paścātpādakalakṣaṇaṃ vyākhyātam iti na punar ucyate. yo 'nivṛtāvyākṛtaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti dadāty api saḥ. āha. yas tāvad dadāti pratigṛhṇāty api saḥ. anivṛtāvyākṛtasya ā parinirvāṇāt saṃnihitatvāt. syāt pratigṛhṇāti na dadāti. arhataś caramāḥ skandhāḥ sarvopadhiniḥsargeṇānivṛtāvyākṛtaniṣyandābhāvāt. sālambananiyamena tu kṣaṇaśa iti. pūrvam anālambanānāṃ sambhavato niyama uktaḥ sālambananiyamena tu cittacaittānām eva sabhāgahetutvam ucyate kṣaṇaśaḥ kṣaṇāntarāpekṣayā. na tu paryādāya vicchedata ity arthaḥ. kuśalacittānantaram iti vistaraḥ. yadā kuśalcittānantaraṃ kliṣṭam avyākṛtaṃ vā [Tib. 218a] cittaṃ saṃmukhīkaroti. tadā tat kuśalaṃ cittaṃ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti yatas tatsaṃtānapatitaṃ vyavahitam anāgataṃ kuśalaṃ phalaṃ bhaviṣyati. anutpattidharmi vā. na dadāti. yasmād
body.translated_text: The third [alternative]: 'for one free from desire for the desire-realm, in the remaining states' — having excluded the two states, in the remaining states [there are] these same two as described in the first and second states. As in our case: the <s>prāpti</s>s (possessions) of the unwholesome — those unwholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s>s both receive and give fruit. The fourth: 'setting aside these aspects as described' — for example, the <s>prāpti</s>s of unwholesome [dharmas] for one who is free from desire for the desire-realm and has the nature of non-decline — that unwholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> does not receive fruit, because [fruit] has already been received previously; nor does it give [fruit], because of the non-existence of its <s>prāpti</s>. 'Thus for the covered-indeterminate also' — thus the elaboration. For the covered-indeterminate also, a fourfold distinction should be made, to be applied as appropriate from the attainment of <s>Arhatship</s> and from the decline from <s>Arhatship</s>. 'There exists a covered-indeterminate <s>sabhāgahetu</s> that receives fruit but does not give it' — thus the elaboration. The first alternative: when one is attaining <s>Arhatship</s>, the <s>prāpti</s>s that one abandons last of all — that covered-indeterminate <s>sabhāgahetu</s> receives fruit but does not give it, because there is no subsequent afflicted moment. The second: 'when declining from <s>Arhatship</s>, those that one first obtains.' But it should be stated thus: 'those very [prāptis] of the one who is declining.' For thus only the giving of fruit [Tib. 217b] is established. The support for the earlier reading too should be stated in the same sequence. The third: 'for one free from desire for the peak of existence, in the remaining states.' The fourth: 'setting aside these aspects.' For example, one who has attained <s>Arhatship</s> — whatever <s>prāpti</s>s of the covered-indeterminate [dharmas] of the three realms exist as possible — that covered-indeterminate <s>sabhāgahetu</s> does not receive fruit, because [fruit] has been received; nor does it give, because [the dharmas] have been abandoned. 'The subsequent producer of the uncovered-indeterminate' — the definition of 'subsequent producer' has been explained, so it is not stated again. 'Whatever uncovered-indeterminate <s>sabhāgahetu</s> receives fruit also gives it.' He says: 'first, that which gives also receives — because the uncovered-indeterminate is constantly present until <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. There may be [a case where] it receives but does not give — the final aggregates of an <s>Arhat</s>, because there is no uncovered-indeterminate outflow through the complete relinquishment of all substrates.' 'But with the restriction to those having objects, moment by moment' — previously the restriction was stated with respect to those without objects being possible; but with the restriction to those having objects, the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> status is stated only of mind and mental factors, moment by moment — with respect to the next moment. The meaning is: not exhaustively to the point of cessation. 'Immediately after a wholesome mind...' — thus the elaboration. When, immediately after a wholesome mind, an afflicted or indeterminate [Tib. 218a] mind is actualized, then that wholesome mind receives fruit — because the wholesome fruit that has fallen into that continuum, separated [by intervening moments] and future, will come to be; or [the fruit] has the nature of not arising. It does not give — because

body.text:
asyānantaraṃ kuśalam eva nāsti. sadṛśena hi phalena saphalaḥ sabhāgahetur iṣyate. dvitīyā. viparyayād iti. yadā kliṣṭānivṛtāvyākṛtacittānantaraṃ kuśalaṃ cittaṃ saṃmukhīkaroti. tadā yena kuśalena cittena tat kuśalaṃ cittaṃ phalatvena pratigṛhītam āsīt. tad dadāti na tat pratigṛhṇāti. pūrvaṃ pratigṛhītatvāt. tṛtīyā. kuśalacittānantaraṃ kuśalam eveti. saṃmukhīkarotīty adhikṛtaṃ. tat pūrvakaṃ kuśalaṃ cittaṃ dvitīyaṃ cittaṃ phalatvena pratigṛhṇāti dadāti ca. samanantaranirvartanāt. caturthī. etān ākārān sthāpayitveti. yadā kliṣṭāvyākṛtacittānantaraṃ kliṣṭam avyākṛtaṃ vā cittaṃ saṃmukhīkaroti. tadāsau sālambanaḥ kuśalaḥ sabhāgahetur na phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti. pratigṛhītatvāt. na dadāti. kliṣṭāvyākṛtacittasaṃmukhībhāvāt. evam akuśalādayo 'pi yojyā iti. asti sālaṃbano 'kuśalaḥ sabhāgahetuḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhṇāti na dadāti catuḥkoṭikaḥ. prathamā koṭiḥ. akuśalānaṃtaraṃ kuśalam anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ vā cittaṃ saṃmukhīkaroti. [Tib. 218b] dvitīyā. viparyayāt. tṛtīyā. 'kuśalānantaraṃ akuśalam eva. caturthī etān ākārān sthāpayitvā. ādiśabdena nivṛtāvyākṛtaḥ anivṛtāvyākṛtaś ca sabhāgahetur yojyaḥ. nivṛtasya tāvat prathamā koṭiḥ. nivṛtāvyākṛtacittānantaraṃ kuśalaṃ anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ vā cittaṃ sammukhīkaroti. dvitīyā. viparyayāt. tṛtīyā. nivṛtāvyākṛtacittānantaraṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtam eva. caturthī. etān ākārān sthāpayitvā. anivṛtasya prathamā koṭiḥ. anivṛtāvyākṛtānantaraṃ kuśalaṃ kliṣṭaṃ vā cittaṃ saṃmukhīkaroti. dvitīya. viparyayāt. tṛtīyā. anivṛtāvyākṛtānantaraṃ anivṛtāvyākṛtam eva. caturthī.
etān ākārān sthāpayitvā. tasya bījabhāvopagamanād iti. tasya phalasya hetubhāvopagamanād ity upamā sautrāntikaprakriyaiṣā. kvacit pustake nāsty evaṃpāṭhaḥ. yathā jalamaṇḍalam iti vistaraḥ. yatheti dṛṣṭāntapradarśanaṃ. jalamaṇḍalaṃ vāyamaṇḍalasya pratiṣthāphalaṃ. yāvacchabdena jalamaṇḍalasya kāṃcanamayī pṛthivī. kāṃcanamayyāḥ pṛthivyās tathā sasyauṣadhiprabhṛtayaḥ pratiṣṭhāphalam ity adhikāraḥ. aśubhāyāḥ smṛtyupasthānāny ārabhya yāvād anutpādajñānaṃ. [Tib. 219a] evam anyasyāpy ānāpānasmṛtyādeḥ. prayogasya phalaṃ yojyaṃ. sāmagryāḥ phalaṃ sāmagrīphalaṃ. cakṣurādīnām iti. ādiśabdena cakṣūrūpālokamanaskārāṇāṃ grahaṇaṃ. evaṃ bhāvanāyāḥ phalaṃ bhāvanāphalam iti samāsaḥ. etat tu sarvam iti vistaraḥ. etac caturvidhaṃ phalaṃ puruṣakārādhipatiphalayor antarbhūtaṃ. pratiṣṭhāphalaṃ. adhipatiphalāntarbhūtaṃ. prayogaphalādipuruṣakārādhipatiphalayoḥ.
body.translated_text: immediately after it, a wholesome [mind] does not exist. For a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> is accepted as fruitful with a similar fruit. The second [alternative]: 'by the reverse' — when, immediately after an afflicted or uncovered-indeterminate mind, a wholesome mind is actualized, then that wholesome mind by which this wholesome mind had been received as a fruit — it gives [fruit] but does not receive it, because it had been received previously. The third: 'immediately after a wholesome mind, a wholesome [mind] itself' — 'is actualized' is the governing verb. That prior wholesome mind both receives the second mind as a fruit and gives [fruit] — because of immediate production. The fourth: 'setting aside these aspects' — when, immediately after an afflicted or indeterminate mind, an afflicted or indeterminate mind is actualized, then that wholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> having objects does not receive fruit, because it was received previously; nor does it give, because of the actualization of an afflicted or indeterminate mind. 'Thus the unwholesome and the rest should also be applied' — there is a fourfold distinction for the unwholesome <s>sabhāgahetu</s> having objects: 'it receives fruit but does not give it.' The first alternative: immediately after unwholesome [mind], a wholesome or uncovered-indeterminate mind is actualized. [Tib. 218b] The second: by the reverse. The third: immediately after unwholesome, unwholesome itself. The fourth: setting aside these aspects. By the word 'and the rest,' the covered-indeterminate and uncovered-indeterminate <s>sabhāgahetu</s>s should be applied. For the covered [indeterminate], the first alternative: immediately after a covered-indeterminate mind, a wholesome or uncovered-indeterminate mind is actualized. The second: by the reverse. The third: immediately after covered-indeterminate, covered-indeterminate itself. The fourth: setting aside these aspects. For the uncovered [indeterminate], the first: immediately after uncovered-indeterminate, a wholesome or afflicted mind is actualized. The second: by the reverse. The third: immediately after uncovered-indeterminate, uncovered-indeterminate itself. The fourth: setting aside these aspects. 'Because of entering the state of being a seed' — the simile is: because of entering the state of being a cause of that fruit — this procedure follows the <s>Sautrāntika</s> method. In some manuscripts, this reading is not found. 'Just as the water-disc...' — thus the elaboration. 'Just as' introduces an illustration. The water-disc is the support-fruit (<s>pratiṣṭhāphala</s>) of the wind-disc. By the word 'up to': the golden earth is [the support-fruit] of the water-disc; and of the golden earth, crops, herbs, and so forth are the support-fruit — this is the topic. From the mindfulness-establishments regarding the impure, [Tib. 219a] up to the knowledge of non-arising — likewise for other [practices] beginning with the mindfulness of breathing. The fruit of practice should be applied. The fruit of an assemblage of [conditions] is the assemblage-fruit (<s>sāmagrīphala</s>). 'Of the eye and the rest' — by the word 'and the rest,' the eye, form, light, and mental attention are included. Likewise, 'the fruit of cultivation is the cultivation-fruit' — this is the compound. 'But all this...' — thus the elaboration. This fourfold fruit is subsumed under the <s>puruṣakāraphala</s> (personal-effort fruit) and <s>adhipatiphala</s> (dominant fruit). The support-fruit is subsumed under the <s>adhipatiphala</s>. The practice-fruit and the rest [are subsumed] under the <s>puruṣakāraphala</s> and <s>adhipatiphala</s>.

body.text: (II.61, 62ab) kliṣṭā iti vistaraḥ. kleśatatsaṃprayuktatatsamutthāḥ kliṣṭāḥ. vipākahetujātā vipākajāḥ. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntitatsahabhuvaḥ prathamānāsravāḥ.
body.translated_text: (II.61, 62ab) 'Afflicted' — thus the elaboration. The afflictions, those associated with them, and those arisen from them are 'afflicted.' Those born from the maturation cause are 'maturation-born' (<s>vipākaja</s>). The insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering and its co-existents are the 'first non-outflow' (<s>prathamānāsrava</s>)

body.text: tebhyaś ca śeṣāḥ kliṣṭādibhyas tribhyaḥ. vipākavarjyā avyākṛtā airyāpathikaśailpasthānikanairmāṇikāḥ. prathamānāsravakṣaṇavarjyāś ca kuśalā iti. kuśalagrahaṇena sāsravānāsravā gṛhyante. tatra duḥkhe dharmajñānakalāpādayaḥ sarva eva śaikṣāśaikṣamārgā laukikāś ca kuśalāḥ śeṣā ity avagantavyaṃ śeṣāś cātra tṛtīyo rāśiḥ kriyate. tenāha. ta ete caturvidhā dharmāḥ
body.translated_text: 'And the remainder from those three — afflicted, etc.' The indeterminate [dharmas] other than maturation — conduct, craft, magical creation — are excluded from maturation. And the wholesome [dharmas] other than the first non-outflow moment are [the remainder]: by the term 'wholesome,' both with-outflows and non-outflow [wholesome dharmas] are included. Therein, the group beginning with the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering and all the trainee, non-trainee, and mundane wholesome [dharmas] should be understood as the 'remainder.' And the 'remainder' here constitutes the third class. Therefore he says: 'these <s>dharma</s>s are fourfold' —

children.text:
kliṣṭā vipākajāḥ [Tib. 219b] śeṣāḥ prathamāryā yathākramaṃ
vipākaṃ sarvagaṃ hitvā tau sabhāgaṃ ca śeṣajā
children.translated_text:
'The afflicted, the maturation-born, [Tib. 219b] the remainder, and the first noble [dharmas] — in order,
excluding the maturation [cause] and the universal, [and] those two plus the homogeneous — [each] arises from the remaining [causes]' —

body.text: iti. vipākam iti vipākahetuṃ. kliṣtā dharmā vipākahetuṃ hitvā śeṣebhyaḥ paṃcabhyaḥ kāraṇasahabhūsabhāgasaṃprayuktakasarvatragebhyo yathāsaṃbhavaṃ jāyante. svabhāvavarjyāt sarvadharmalakṣaṇāt kāraṇahetoḥ. svakalāpacittādilakṣaṇāt sahabhūhetoḥ. pūrvotpannasvasaṃtānakliṣṭalakṣaṇāt sabhāgahetoḥ. svakalāpacittalakṣaṇāt saṃprayuktakahetoḥ. yasmāt te cittacaittasvabhāvāḥ pūrvotpannasatkāyadṛṣṭyādilakṣaṇāt sarvatragahetor jāyante. na tu vipākahetoḥ. vipākaphalena hi saphalo vipākahetuḥ. na ca kliṣṭā dharmā vipākasvabhāvā iti te na tato jāyante. vipākajāḥ sarvatragahetuṃ hitvā śeṣebhyaḥ paṃcabhya eva hetubhyo jāyante. na tu sarvatragahetoḥ. vipākajānām akliṣṭatvāt. sarvatragākhyaḥ kliṣṭānām iti hi sarvatragahetulakṣaṇaṃ. yady api mithyādṛṣṭyādibhyaḥ sarvatragebhyo vipākajā jāyante. na tu sarvatragahetor iti kṛtvā tato jāyante. kiṃ tarhi. vipākahetor iti. śeṣā iti vistaraḥ. śeṣāṇām [Tib. 220a] avipākasvabhāvatvāt. na vipākahetur asti. akliṣṭasvabhāvatvāc ca na sarvatragahetur asti. atas tau vipākasarvatragahetū varjayitvā śeṣebhyaś caturbhyo jāyante. pūrvavad vyākhyānaṃ. prathamānāsravāḥ tau vipākasarvatragahetū pūrvoktau. caśabdenānukṛṣṭau sabhāgahetuṃ ca hitvā śeṣebhyaḥ kāraṇasahabhūsaṃprayuktakahetubhyo yathāsaṃbhavaṃ jāyante. anāsravāṇām avipākasvabhāvatvāt na vipākahetur asti. akliṣṭatvāt na sarvatragahetuḥ. mārgasya pūrvamanutpāditatvāt na sabhāgahetur asti. na hi sāsravā agradharmā anāsravasya kalāpasya sabhāgahetur yujyate. tasmān na tebhyo jāyante.
body.translated_text: thus. '<s>Vipāka</s>' means the <s>vipākahetu</s> (maturation cause). Afflicted <s>dharma</s>s, excluding the <s>vipākahetu</s>, arise from the remaining five [causes] — <s>kāraṇa</s> (efficient), <s>sahabhū</s> (co-existent), <s>sabhāga</s> (homogeneous), <s>saṃprayuktaka</s> (associated), and <s>sarvatraga</s> (universal) — as appropriate. From the <s>kāraṇahetu</s>, characterized by all <s>dharma</s>s excluding one's own nature. From the <s>sahabhūhetu</s>, characterized by mind and the like of one's own group. From the <s>sabhāgahetu</s>, characterized by the afflicted [dharmas] of one's own continuum that have previously arisen. From the <s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s>, characterized by mind of one's own group. Because those [afflicted dharmas] have the nature of mind and mental factors — from the <s>sarvatragahetu</s>, characterized by previously arisen <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (identity-view) and the like. But they do not arise from the <s>vipākahetu</s>, for the <s>vipākahetu</s> is fruitful through maturation-fruit, and afflicted <s>dharma</s>s do not have the nature of maturation; therefore they do not arise from that. Maturation-born [dharmas], excluding the <s>sarvatragahetu</s>, arise from the remaining five causes only, not from the <s>sarvatragahetu</s>, because maturation-born [dharmas] are unafflicted — for the definition of the <s>sarvatragahetu</s> is that it is 'called universal, of the afflicted.' Although maturation-born [dharmas] arise from universal [causes] such as wrong view and the like, they do not arise from them qua <s>sarvatragahetu</s>; rather, qua <s>vipākahetu</s>. 'The remainder' — thus the elaboration. Because the remainder [Tib. 220a] do not have the nature of maturation, there is no <s>vipākahetu</s>. Because they do not have the nature of being afflicted, there is no <s>sarvatragahetu</s>. Therefore, excluding those two — <s>vipāka</s> and <s>sarvatraga</s> causes — they arise from the remaining four. The explanation is as before. 'The first non-outflow [dharmas]' — those two, the <s>vipāka</s> and <s>sarvatraga</s> causes stated earlier, and — drawn in by the word 'and' — the <s>sabhāgahetu</s> as well — excluding these, they arise from the remaining causes: <s>kāraṇa</s>, <s>sahabhū</s>, and <s>saṃprayuktaka</s>, as appropriate. Because non-outflow [dharmas] do not have the nature of maturation, there is no <s>vipākahetu</s>. Because they are unafflicted, there is no <s>sarvatragahetu</s>. Because the path has not previously arisen, there is no <s>sabhāgahetu</s>. For it is not proper that the with-outflows highest mundane <s>dharma</s>s be a <s>sabhāgahetu</s> of the non-outflow group. Therefore they do not arise from those.

body.text: iti. saṃprayuktakahetusaṃbhavārthaṃ cittacaittagrahaṇaṃ. prāptijātyādayaś ca cittaviprayuktāḥ. anāsravasaṃvaraś ca rūpisvabhāvo 'nāsraveṣu veditavyaḥ. te cittaviprayuktā rūpiṇaś ca cittacaittebhyo 'nye kliṣtādayaḥ kliṣṭavipākajaśeṣaprathamānāsravasaṃgṛhītāḥ tathaivotpadyante yathā cittacaittāḥ. kevalaṃ tu saṃprayuktakahetunaikena varjitāḥ. teṣām asaṃprayuktakasvabhāvatvāt na saṃprayuktakahetor jāyante. katham iti. kliṣṭā cittaviprayuktarūpiṇo [Tib. 220b]
body.translated_text: thus. The mention of mind and mental factors is for the purpose of [showing] the possibility of the <s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s> (associated cause). <s>Prāpti</s>, birth, and the like are mind-dissociated. And the non-outflow restraint, having a material nature, should be understood [as included] among the non-outflow [dharmas]. Those mind-dissociated and material [dharmas] other than mind and mental factors — [those] included among the afflicted, maturation-born, remainder, and first non-outflow [classes] — arise in exactly the same way as mind and mental factors, except that they are excluded from one [cause], namely the <s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s>. Because their nature is not that of associated [dharmas], they do not arise from the <s>saṃprayuktakahetu</s>. How? Afflicted mind-dissociated and material [dharmas], [Tib. 220b]

body.text: vipākasaṃprayuktakahetū hitvā śeṣebhyaś caturbhyo hetubhyo jāyante. vipākajā api saṃprayuktakasarvatragahetū hitvā śeṣebhyaś caturbhya eva. śeṣā vipākasarvatragasaṃprayuktakahetūn hitvā śeṣebhyas tribhyaḥ. prathamānāsravā vipākasarvatragahetū sabhāgahetuṃ ca saṃprayuktakahetuṃ ca hitvā śeṣābhyāṃ hetubhyāṃ jāyaṃta iti. ekahetusaṃbhūto nāstīti. kāraṇasahabhūhetvor avaśyam avinābhāvāt.
body.translated_text: excluding the <s>vipāka</s> and <s>saṃprayuktaka</s> causes, arise from the remaining four causes. Maturation-born [dharmas] too, excluding the <s>saṃprayuktaka</s> and <s>sarvatraga</s> causes, arise from the remaining four only. The remainder, excluding the <s>vipāka</s>, <s>sarvatraga</s>, and <s>saṃprayuktaka</s> causes, arise from the remaining three. The first non-outflow [dharmas], excluding the <s>vipāka</s>, <s>sarvatraga</s>, and <s>sabhāga</s> causes and the <s>saṃprayuktaka</s> cause, arise from the remaining two causes. 'There is none produced from a single cause' — because the <s>kāraṇa</s> and <s>sahabhū</s> causes are invariably always present.

body.text:
(II.62cd, 63) janasya janaikā jātir na hetupratyayair vinety
uktaṃ. ato hetuvistaravacanānantaraṃ pṛcchati pratyayāḥ katama iti. pratyayajātiḥ pratyayateti. pratyayaprakāra ity arthaḥ. gotāvat.
body.translated_text: (II.62cd, 63) 'One birth of a person — [there is] not [any dharma] without causes and conditions' — this has been stated. Therefore, immediately after the detailed statement of causes, he asks: 'what are the conditions?' '<s>Pratyayajāti</s>' means 'type of condition' — the meaning is: the kind of condition. Like lineage (<s>gotra</s>).

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. cittacaittā eva
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration. Mind and mental factors alone

body.text: ity avadhāraṇaṃ
body.translated_text: this is a restrictive qualifier.

body.text: grahaṇaṃ sottarāṇāṃ samanantaratvāt.
body.translated_text: this word is included because [only] those having successors are immediately preceding.

body.text: grahaṇaṃ anāgatanirāsārthaṃ. samaś cāyam anantaraś ca pratyaya iti samanantarapratyaya iti. samānārthe saṃśabdaḥ. kāmāvacarasya rūpasyeti. avijñaptirūpasya kadācit kāmāvacaraṃ avijñaptirūpaṃ rūpāvacaraṃ cāvijñaptirūpam utpadyate sāsravadhyānasaṃmukhībhāve gṛhītasamvarasya. kadācit kāmāvacaraṃ cānāsravaṃ cānāsravadhyānasaṃmukhībhāve. na tu kāmāvacaracittānantaraṃ kadācit [Tib. 221a] kāmāvacaraṃ rūpāvacaraṃ ca yugapac cittam utpadyate. kāmāvacaraṃ ca anāsravaṃ cety ākulo rūpasaṃmukhībhāvaḥ.
body.translated_text: The [word] 'grasping' is for the purpose of excluding the future. And this [condition] is both 'equal' (<s>sama</s>) and 'immediately following' (<s>anantara</s>) — hence '<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>' (immediately preceding condition). The prefix '<s>sam</s>' is in the sense of 'equal' (<s>samāna</s>). 'Of desire-realm form' — of <s>avijñapti</s>-form. Sometimes desire-realm <s>avijñapti</s>-form and form-realm <s>avijñapti</s>-form arise [simultaneously], when one who has taken a restraint confronts an outflow-possessing <s>dhyāna</s>. Sometimes desire-realm and non-outflow [avijñapti-form arise simultaneously], when confronting a non-outflow <s>dhyāna</s>. But it is not the case that, immediately after a desire-realm mind, [Tib. 221a] both desire-realm and form-realm mind arise simultaneously. Nor both desire-realm and non-outflow [mind] — the arising of form [in such cases] is confused (<s>ākula</s>).

body.text: dvitīyotpatter iti. dvitīyaupacayikotpatteḥ. yadā hi bhuktvā svapiti dhyānam vā samāpadyate. tadāhāraja aupacayikaḥ svapnajaś ca samādhijo vā aupacayika utpadyate.
body.translated_text: 'Because of a second arising' — because of a second accumulative arising (<s>aupacayika</s>). For when one eats and then sleeps or enters <s>dhyāna</s>, then food-born accumulative [form] and sleep-born or concentration-born accumulative [form] arise [simultaneously].

body.text: alpabahutarotpatter iti. kiṃ. rūpaṃ na samanantarapratyaya iti prakṛtaṃ. bhadantaḥ sthaviraḥ sautrāntikaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the arising of fewer and more' — what? 'Form is not a <s>samanantarapratyaya</s>' — this is the topic. 'The Venerable Elder' — a <s>Sautrāntika</s>.

body.text: kuśalākuśalāvyākṛteṣu citteṣv iti.
body.translated_text: 'In wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate minds' —

children.text:
savitarkavicāritvāt. kuśale kāmacetasi
dvāviṃśatiś caitaśikāh. kaukṛtyam adhikaṃ kvacit.
āveṇike tv akuśale dṛṣtiyukte ca viṃśatiḥ.
kleśaiś caturbhiḥ krodhādyaiḥ kaukṛtyenaikaviṃśatiḥ.
nivṛte 'ṣṭādaśānyatra dvādaśāvyākṛte matā
children.translated_text: because of having <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought). [The verse states:] 'In a wholesome desire-realm mind, twenty-two mental factors; sometimes with remorse (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) as additional. In a specifically unwholesome [mind] and one conjoined with views, twenty. With four afflictions, anger and the rest, and remorse — twenty-one. In an obstructed [mind], eighteen; otherwise, twelve in an indeterminate [mind] are accepted' —

body.text: ity anena krameṇa kadācid bahubhyaś caittebhyas trayoviṃśater ekaviṃśatir aṣṭādaśa dvādaśa vālpe caittā utpadyante. kadācid alpād bahavo viparyayāt. savitarkavicārādau ca samādhitraye asti savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ samādhiḥ asti avitarko vicāramātraḥ. asty avitarko 'vicāra iti. etasmiṃ samādhitraye caittānām alpabahutarotpattiḥ. ataś ca cittacaittā api na samanantarapratyayāḥ syur iti. asti jātyaṃtaraṃ prati na svajātim [Tib. 221b] iti. asty alpabahutarotpattir jātyantaraṃ prati na svajātiṃ. vitarkavicārādīnāṃ hi kvacic citte jātyantarabhūtānāṃ satāṃ vṛttir avṛttiś ca bhavati. na kadācid bahutarā vedaneti. na hi kadācid vedanaikasmiṃś citte ekā kvacid aparasmiṃ dve tisro veti. rūpasya tu svajātiṃ praty alpabahutarotpattiḥ.
body.translated_text: by this order, sometimes from the many mental factors — twenty-three — [there arise] twenty-one, eighteen, or twelve, or from few, mental factors arise. Sometimes from few, many [arise] — by the reverse. And in the three types of <s>samādhi</s> — with applied and sustained thought, without applied thought but with sustained thought only, and without applied or sustained thought — in these three types of <s>samādhi</s>, there is arising of fewer and more mental factors. And therefore mind and mental factors too would not be <s>samanantarapratyayas</s>. 'There is [arising] with respect to another type, not to its own type' — [Tib. 221b] there is arising of fewer and more with respect to another type, not to its own type. For <s>vitarka</s>, <s>vicāra</s>, and the rest, being of different types, sometimes operate and sometimes do not operate in a given mind. 'Feeling is never more numerous' — for it is never the case that feeling in one mind is one and in another mind two or three. But for form, the arising of fewer and more is with respect to its own type.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ svajāter eveti. kiṃ vedanā vedanāyā eva samanantaraprutyayaḥ. anekavedanotpattāv asāmarthyāt. evaṃ saṃjñādayaḥ. na parajāteḥ. na vedanā saṃjñādīnāṃ. yataś caittānām alpabahutarotpattir na parigṛhītā bhavet.
body.translated_text: 'Is it [the samanantarapratyaya] only of its own type, then?' — Is feeling the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> of feeling alone? Because of the incapacity [to account for] the arising of multiple feelings. Similarly perception and the rest. Not of another type — feeling is not [the samanantarapratyaya] of perception and the rest. Since the arising of fewer and more among mental factors would not be accounted for.

body.text: sāṃtānasabāgikās tv iti vistaraḥ. cittaṃ cittāntarasya samanantarapratyayaḥ. na vedanāyāḥ. vedanā vedanāntarasya. na cittasyeti. saṃtānasabhāgaḥ sabhāgahetur ity arthaḥ. saṃtānasabhāgena dīvyanti vyavaharanti vā sāṃtānasabhāgikāḥ kecid ābhidharmikāḥ. yadi saṃtānaḥ saṃtānāntarasya sabhāgahetuḥ. akliṣṭānantaraṃ yadā kliṣṭam utpadyate. kathaṃ tatra samanantarapratyayavyavastheti. ata āha. yadā tu akliṣṭānantaram iti vistaraḥ. tasya kleśasya paścādutpannasya pūrvaniruddhakleśaḥ kṣaṇāntaravyavahitaḥ samanantarapratyaya iti vyavasthāpayaṃti. tulyajātīyena cittāntareṇāyavadhānāt. akliṣṭena vyavadhānaṃ tv avyavadhānam eva. atulyajātīyatvāt. [Tib. 222a] tadyathā nirodhasamāpatticittaṃ vyutthānacittasya. cittāntareṇāvyavadhānāt. samāpattidravyeṇa vyavahitam api samanantarapratyayo vyavasthāpyate. tadvat.
body.translated_text: 'But the continuum-homogenists (<s>sāṃtānasabhāgikas</s>)' — and so forth in detail. Mind is the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> of another mind — not of feeling. Feeling is [the samanantarapratyaya] of another feeling — not of mind. 'Continuum-homogeneous' (<s>saṃtānasabhāga</s>) means the homogeneous cause within a continuum. Those who maintain or articulate [the doctrine of] continuum-homogeneity are '<s>sāṃtānasabhāgikas</s>' — certain <s>Ābhidharmikas</s>. If the continuum is the homogeneous cause of another continuum — when, immediately after a non-defiled [mind], a defiled [mind] arises — how is the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> established there? Therefore he says: 'But when, immediately after a non-defiled [mind]...' — and so forth in detail. The previously ceased affliction, separated by intervening moments, is the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> of that subsequently arisen affliction — they establish [it thus]. Because of not being intervened by a mind of the same type. But intervention by a non-defiled [mind] is non-intervention, [Tib. 222a] because of being of a different type. Just as the mind [preceding] the cessation attainment [is the samanantarapratyaya] of the emergence-mind — because of not being intervened by another mind [of the same type]. Even though intervened by the substance of the attainment, [it] is established as the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s>. Similarly.

body.text: traidhātukapratisaṃyuktānāṃ yugapatsaṃmukhībhāvād iti. kāmadhātvavītarāgasyāryasya kāmāvacaryāḥ prāpter anantaraṃ traidhātukāpratisaṃyuktānāṃ prāptaya utpadyante. traidhātukaiḥ kleśaiḥ samanvāgatatvāt. evaṃ tajjātyādayo 'py utpadyante. ity evaṃ vyākulasammukhībhāvāt viprayuktā api saṃskārāḥ prāptijātyādayo na samanantarapratyayaḥ.
