body.translated_text: 'Because of the simultaneous arising of [dharmas] connected with the three realms' — for a Noble One who has not attained dispassion from the desire-realm, immediately after the desire-realm <s>prāpti</s>, <s>prāptis</s> unconnected with the three realms arise — because of being endowed with afflictions of the three realms. Similarly, births and the rest of those [prāptis] also arise. Thus, because of confused simultaneous arising, dissociated formations too — <s>prāptis</s>, births, and the rest — are not <s>samanantarapratyayas</s>.

body.text: kasmād anāgata iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Why is the future [not a samanantarapratyaya]?' — and so forth in detail.

body.text: utpannāḥ samanaṃtara
body.translated_text: 'Arisen [dharmas are the] immediately preceding [condition]' —

body.text: iti atītapratyutpannā eva samanantarapratyaya iti pūrvam uktaṃ. ata evaṃ pṛcchati. vyākulatvād iti. vyākulatvād anāgato neṣyate samanantarapratyayaḥ. vyākulatvaṃ punar anāgatasyādhvanaḥ pūrvottarābhāvāt. pūrvottaratāyā abhāvāt.
body.translated_text: thus it was previously stated that only past and present [dharmas] are the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s>. Therefore he asks thus. 'Because of confusion (<s>vyākulatva</s>)' — because of the confusion [of temporal ordering], the future is not accepted as a <s>samanantarapratyaya</s>. The confusion of the future time-period is because of the absence of earlier and later — the absence of the earlier-later relationship.

body.text: vartamāno hi anāgatāt pūrvo vartamānād atīta iti śakyate vaktuṃ. pūrvottarakālayogāt. na tv anāgatasya pūrvapaścimatāsti. ata eva ca vartamāno vartamānasya na samanantarapratyaya iṣyate. pūrvapaścimatāyā abhāvāt tulyavartamānasya na samanantarapratyaya iṣyate. pūrvapaścimatāyā abhāvāt tulyakālatvāt. atītasāṃpratānumānād iti. atītena ca sāṃpratena cānumānāt. atītenānumānam iti darśayann āha. atītaṃ kilādhvānaṃ [Tib. 222b] paśyatīti vistaraḥ. sāṃpratenānumānam iti darśayann āha. idaṃ cāpi saṃpraty evaṃjātīyakam iti vistaraḥ. aparāntaṃ na jānīyād iti. sarvavittvam asya hīyeteti abhiprāyaḥ. phalacihnabhūtaḥ phalaliṃgabhūtaḥ. na sākṣātkārī na sākṣāddarśī.
body.translated_text: For the present is earlier than the future, and the past is earlier than the present — this can be stated, because of the fitness of the earlier-later temporal relationship. But for the future, there is no earlier-later relationship. For this very reason, the present too is not accepted as the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> of the present — because of the absence of the earlier-later relationship, because of being of the same time. 'By inference from the past and the present' — by inference from the past and the present. Showing the inference from the past, he says: 'One sees the past time-period' — [Tib. 222b] and so forth in detail. Showing the inference from the present, he says: 'And this, at present, is of such a kind' — and so forth in detail. 'One would not know the future' — the intent is: his omniscience would be undermined. '[He is] of the nature of a sign of the fruit, of the nature of an indicator of the fruit' — not a direct perceiver, not a direct seer.

body.text: anāgato neṣyate samanaṃtarapratyayo vyākulatvāt pūrvapaścimatāyā 'bhāvād ity ukte 'yam āha. kasmād agradharmānantaram iti vistaraḥ. tasya vaibhāṣikaḥ parihāram āha. yasya yatpratibaddha utpāda iti vistaraḥ. yasya dharmasya duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntyāder yasmiṃ dharme laukikāgradharmādau pratibaddha utpādaḥ. sa tasyānantaram utpadyate. tadyathā bījādīnām aṃkurādayaḥ. aṃkurasya hi bīje pratibaddha utpādaḥ. tasmāt tadanantaram utpadyate. evaṃ kāṇḍādīnāṃ aṃkurādiṣu. vināpi samanantarapratyayenāsaty api samanantarapratyaye. apiśabdāt sati samanantarapratyaye sutarām utpadyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. tasmān nāsti ca kramaniyamāvasthānaṃ tadvat samanantarotpattiniyamaś ca bhavatīti vākyārthaḥ.
body.translated_text: Since it was said that the future is not accepted as a <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> because of confusion, because of the absence of the earlier-later relationship — this one says: 'Why, immediately after the peak of worldly <s>dharmas</s> (<s>agradharmā</s>)...' — and so forth in detail. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> offers a resolution: 'That whose arising is bound to whichever' — and so forth in detail. That <s>dharma</s> — the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering and the rest — whose arising is bound to whichever <s>dharma</s> — the peak of worldly <s>dharmas</s> and the like — that arises immediately after it. Just as sprouts and the rest [arise] from seeds and the like. For the arising of a sprout is bound to a seed; therefore it arises immediately after that. Similarly, of joints and the rest from sprouts and the rest. Even without a <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> — even when a <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> does not exist. The word 'even' (<s>api</s>) [implies]: when a <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> does exist, it arises all the more — this is the intent. Therefore, there is no [fixed] sequential-order abiding — and yet there is a fixed rule of immediately-subsequent arising — this is the meaning of the sentence.

body.text: kasmād arhataś caramā iti.
body.translated_text: 'Why is the last [mind] of the <s>Arhat</s>...' —

body.text: iti vacanād ayaṃ praśna āgataḥ. anyacittasambandhād iti. yasmāt tadanantaraṃ anyacittaṃ na sambadhnanti. āśrayabhāvaprabhāvitaṃ [Tib. 223a] mana iti. yathā cakṣur utpannaṃ cakṣurvijñānāśrayabhāvenāvasthitaṃ yadi kāraṇāntaravaikalyāc cakṣurvijñānaṃ notpadyate na tatra cakṣur aparādhyate. evam arhato 'pi caramaṃ cittaṃ āśrayabhāvenāvasthitaṃ. kāraṇāntaravaikalyāt tu vijñānāntaraṃ notpadyate iti na tad aparādhyate. tad dhi na kāritraprabhāvitaṃ na jananapuruṣakāraprabhāvitam ity arthaḥ. yadi hi taj jananaprabhāvitaṃ syāt jāyamāna eva sati kārye tan manaḥ syāt. na caivam. ato 'saty api janye tan mano bhavaty eva. kāritraprabhāvitas tu samanantarapratyayaḥ saty eva janye samanantarapratyayo bhavati. nāsati. tena yo dharmaḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhītaḥ tena samanaṃtarapratyayena yo dharmaḥ phalaṃ pratigṛhīto jāyatām etad iti. sa sarvair api dharmair abuddhimadbhiḥ sarvaprāṇibhir vā saṃcintyakāribhir na śakyaḥ pratibanddhuṃ yathā notpadyeta motpādīti.
body.translated_text: because of this statement, this question has arisen. 'Because of the connection with another mind' — because they do not connect another mind immediately after that. 'The <s>manas</s> is empowered by the condition of being a support' — [Tib. 223a] just as the eye, having arisen, being established in the condition of being a support for eye-consciousness — if eye-consciousness does not arise due to the deficiency of another condition, the eye is not at fault therein. Similarly, even the last mind of the <s>Arhat</s>, being established in the condition of being a support — another consciousness does not arise due to the deficiency of another condition, so that [last mind] is not at fault. For it is not empowered by [its own] function — it is not empowered by the operative activity of generation — this is the meaning. For if it were empowered by generation, then that <s>manas</s> would exist only when the effect is being produced. But it is not so. Therefore, even without the producible [effect], that <s>manas</s> exists. But the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> is empowered by [its own] function — the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> exists only when the producible [effect] exists, not otherwise. Therefore, the <s>dharma</s> whose fruit has been received by the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> — the <s>dharma</s> whose fruit has been received — 'let it arise!' — even by all <s>dharmas</s> that are non-intelligent, or even by all sentient beings who act deliberately, it cannot be prevented from arising.

body.text: ye dharmāś cittasamanantarā iti vistaraḥ. samanaṃtarapratyayacittajanitāś
body.translated_text: 'Those <s>dharmas</s> that are immediately after mind' — and so forth in detail. Those produced by the mind that is the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s>

body.text: cittasamanantarāḥ. cittasya samāś ca te 'nantarāś ca te iti cittasamanantarāḥ. atha vā cittaṃ samanaṃtaraṃ. samanaṃtarapratyaya eṣām iti cittasamanantarāḥ. kṣaṇāntarāvyavahitāt tu cittaniraṃtarāḥ. te punaś cittasamanantarāḥ cittacaittā [Tib. 223b] dve ca samāpattī asaṃjñinirodhasamāpattī. nāsaṃjñikaṃ cittasamanantaraṃ śāstre paṭhitaṃ karmasāmarthyotpatteḥ. prathamā koṭir iti vistaraḥ. samāpattivyutthānacittaṃ samāpattipraveśacittajanitam. ataś cittasamanantaraṃ na cittaniraṃtaraṃ. samāpattikṣaṇavyavahitatvāt. dvitīyādayaś ca samāpattikṣaṇāḥ. prathamakṣaṇavarjyā ity arthaḥ. cittasamanaṃtarāḥ. tatpratyayajanitatvāt. na cittanirantarāḥ. yathāyogaṃ prathamādikṣaṇavyavahitatvāt. dvitīyā. prathamasya samāpattikṣaṇasya jātyādayaḥ cittanirantarāḥ. kṣaṇāntaravyavahitatvāt. na tu cittasamanantarāḥ. acittasamanantarasvabhāvatvāt. cittacaittā eva hi saha samāpattidvayena cittasamanantarā iṣṭāḥ. sacittikāvasthāyāṃ ca jātyādayaḥ. teṣām aviśeṣitatvāt sarveṣāṃ cittacaittādīnāṃ jātyādayaḥ. ādigrahaṇena ca sarva eva viprayuktā gṛhyante samāpattidvayaṃ varjayitvā. te ca tathaiva cittaniraṃtarā na cittasamanantarāḥ. pūrvavad vyākhyānaṃ. sacittikāvastheti. yadā cittāc cittāṃtaram utpadyate. tadā paścimāś cittacaittāḥ [Tib. 224a] pūrvakeṇa cittena cittasamanaṃtarāś cittaniraṃtarāś ca bhavaṃti. caturthī. dvitīyādīnāṃ samāpattikṣaṇānāṃ vyutthānacittasya ca jātyādayaḥ na cittasamanantarāḥ. acittasamanantarasvabhāvatvāt. na cittaniraṃtarāḥ. prathamādisamāpattikṣaṇavyavahitatvāt. ye tṛtīyacaturthyau te prathamadvitīye iti vistaraḥ. prathamā koṭiḥ. prathamasamāpattikṣaṇaḥ sacittikā cāvasthā. te hi cittasamanaṃtarāḥ samanaṃtarapratyayajanitatvāt. na samāpattiniraṃtarāḥ. prathamasamāpattikṣaṇasya sarvasamāpattikṣaṇabhāvena na tanniraṃtaratvābhāvāt. sacittikāvasthāyāṃ ca samāpattyabhāvāt. dvitīyā. dvitīyādīnāṃ samāpattikṣaṇānāṃ jātyādayo vyutthānacittasya ca. ime dharmāḥ samāpattiniraṃtara na cittasamanantarāḥ. tṛtīyā. accittikāyāḥ samāpatter vyutthānacittaṃ dvitīyādayaś ca samāpattikṣaṇāḥ. ete cittasamanantarāḥ samāpattinirantarāś ca. caturthī. prathamasya samāpattikṣaṇasya sacittikāyāṃ cāvasthāyāṃ jātyādayaḥ. ime dharmā na cittasamanantarā na samāpattinirantarāḥ. acittasamanantarasvabhāvatvāt. [Tib. 224b] pūrvasamāpattikṣaṇabhāvāc ca.
body.translated_text: 'immediately following mind' (<s>cittasamanantara</s>). Equal to mind and immediately following it — they are 'immediately following mind.' Alternatively, mind is the immediately preceding [condition]; those for which it is the immediately preceding condition are 'immediately following mind.' But those that are merely not intervened by another moment [of mind] are 'contiguous with mind' (<s>cittaniraṃtara</s>). Those [dharmas that are] 'immediately following mind' are mind and mental factors [Tib. 223b] and the two attainments — the non-perception attainment and the cessation attainment. The non-perceptive state (<s>āsaṃjñika</s>) is not read as 'immediately following mind' in the treatise, because of arising from the power of <s>karma</s>. The first alternative — thus the elaboration. The emergence-mind of the attainment was produced by the entry-mind of the attainment. Therefore it is 'immediately following mind' but not 'contiguous with mind' — because of being intervened by the attainment-moments. And the second and subsequent moments of the attainment — meaning: excluding the first moment — are 'immediately following mind,' because of being produced by that condition, but not 'contiguous with mind,' because of being intervened by the first and subsequent moments respectively. The second [alternative]: the birth and other [characteristics] of the first attainment-moment are 'contiguous with mind' — because of being intervened by no more than one moment — but not 'immediately following mind,' because of not having the nature of what immediately follows mind. For only mind and mental factors together with the two attainments are accepted as 'immediately following mind.' And in the state with mind, the birth and other [characteristics] — because of their non-differentiation, the birth and other [characteristics] of all mind, mental factors, and the like. By the word 'and the rest,' all dissociated [formations] are included, except the two attainments. And those likewise are 'contiguous with mind' but not 'immediately following mind' — the explanation is as before. 'In the state with mind' — when from one mind another mind arises, then the subsequent mind and mental factors [Tib. 224a] are both 'immediately following mind' and 'contiguous with mind' with respect to the preceding mind. The fourth [alternative]: the birth and other [characteristics] of the second and subsequent attainment-moments and of the emergence-mind are neither 'immediately following mind' — because of not having the nature of what immediately follows mind — nor 'contiguous with mind' — because of being intervened by the first and subsequent attainment-moments. 'Those that are the third and fourth [alternatives] are the first and second' — thus the elaboration. The first alternative: the first attainment-moment and the state with mind. For they are 'immediately following the attainment' (<s>samāpattiniraṃtara</s>) — because of being produced by the immediately preceding condition — but not 'contiguous with the attainment,' because the first attainment-moment, being itself an attainment-moment, is not contiguous to another, and because in the state with mind the attainment is absent. The second: the birth and other [characteristics] of the second and subsequent attainment-moments and of the emergence-mind. These <s>dharma</s>s are 'contiguous with the attainment' but not 'immediately following the attainment.' The third: the emergence-mind from the mindless attainment and the second and subsequent attainment-moments — these are both 'immediately following the attainment' and 'contiguous with the attainment.' The fourth: the birth and other [characteristics] of the first attainment-moment and of the state with mind. These <s>dharma</s>s are neither 'immediately following the attainment' nor 'contiguous with the attainment' — because of not having the nature of what immediately follows mind, [Tib. 224b] and because of the absence of a prior attainment-moment.

body.text: sasaṃprayogasya sacaitasikasya. tathālakṣaṇatvād iti. ālambyalakṣaṇatvāt. āyatanadravyakṣaṇaniyameneti. āyatanaṃ ca dravyaṃ ca kṣaṇaś ca teṣāṃ niyamaḥ. tenaiva. te cittacaittāḥ svasminsvasmin ālambane niyatāḥ. yathā tāvac cakṣurvijñānaṃ sasaṃprayogaṃ rūpāyatane ālambane niyataṃ na śabdāyatanādau.
body.translated_text: 'Of that which has associates, which has mental factors.' 'Because of having such a characteristic' — because of having the characteristic of apprehending objects. 'Through the restriction of sense-base, substance, and moment' — sense-base, substance, and moment — the restriction of these. By that very [restriction], those mind and mental factors are restricted to their own respective objects. For example, first, eye-consciousness together with its associates is restricted to the form sense-base as object, not to the sound sense-base and the rest

body.text: evam āyatananiyamena. tatrāpy āyatane dravyaniyamena nīlarūpe nīlarūpagrāhakam eva cakṣurvijñānaṃ sasaṃprayogaṃ niyataṃ. nānyatra pītādau. evaṃ dravyaniyamena. tatrāpi nīlarūpe ālambane yo nīlarūpakṣaṇo yasyālambanaṃ. sa tasyaiva. nānyasya. ity evaṃ kṣaṇaniyamena. evaṃ śabdāyatanādiṣv api śrotrādivijñānaṃ sasaṃprayogaṃ yojyaṃ. kim āśryaniyamenāpīti. kiṃ cakṣurādyāśrayaniyamenāpy ete cittacaittā niyatāḥ. om ity āha. evam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: . Thus through the restriction of sense-base. Even within that sense-base, through the restriction of substance — eye-consciousness together with its associates is restricted to blue form when apprehending blue form, not to another such as yellow and the rest. Thus through the restriction of substance. Even within that blue form as object, whichever moment of blue form is the object of which [consciousness] — that is [the object] of that alone, not of another. Thus through the restriction of moment. Likewise, for the sound sense-base and the rest, auditory consciousness and the rest together with their associates should be applied. 'Also through the restriction of basis?' — are these mind and mental factors also restricted through the restriction of the eye and other bases? Yes — he says. The meaning is: likewise.

body.text: ālambanapratyayo 'pi sarvadharmā iti manovijñānāpekṣayā. adhiko 'yaṃ pratyaya ity adhipatipratyaya iti. hetupratyayādibhyaḥ. hetupratyayo hi paraṃ paṃca hetavaḥ. ālambanapratyayo hi sahabhuvāṃ na saṃbhavatīti nādhikaḥ. adhikasya vā pratyaya iti. pūrvam adhikaḥ patir adhipatiḥ. sa pratyaya iti [Tib. 225a] samāsaḥ. idānīm adhikasya bhūyasaḥ patir adhipatiḥ. sa pratyaya ity adhipatipratyaya iti samāsaḥ. katham ity āha. sarva iti vistaraḥ. sarvaḥ saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaḥ sarvasya saṃskṛtasya svabhāvavarjyasya sālambanasyānālambanasya ca pratyayo 'dhipatipratyayaḥ. ālambanapratyayas tu sālambanasyaiva nānālambanasya. prathame vigrahe pratyayasyādhikyaṃ darśitaṃ. dvitīye pratyayavataḥ.
body.translated_text: 'The object-condition (<s>ālambanapratyaya</s>) is all <s>dharma</s>s' — with reference to mental consciousness. 'This condition is additional, hence the dominant condition (<s>adhipatipratyaya</s>)' — additional to the cause-condition and the rest. For the cause-condition comprises at most five causes. And the object-condition is not possible for co-existent [<s>dharma</s>s], so it is not additional. Or, it is the condition of what is additional. 'Previously, the additional lord is the dominant [Tib. 225a]' — [in the first analysis] the <s>adhipati</s> ('dominant lord') is what is additional; that is the condition — this is the compound. Now, 'the lord of what is additional — of the greater [number] — is the dominant'; that is the condition — thus the <s>adhipatipratyaya</s> — this is the compound. How? He says: 'all' — thus the elaboration. Every [<s>dharma</s>], conditioned and unconditioned, is the condition of everything conditioned, excluding its own nature, whether having an object or not having an object — [this is] the dominant condition. But the object-condition [applies] only to what has an object, not to what has no object. In the first analysis, the additionality of the condition was shown; in the second, the additionality of what possesses the condition.

body.text: iti. nirudhyamāna evety avadhāraṇaṃ. mithaḥphalatvāt samāśrayatvāc ca sahabhūsaṃprayutakahetvor yathākramaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. The restriction is: 'only when ceasing.' [This applies to] the co-existent and associated causes respectively, because of mutual fruitfulness and because of having the same basis.

body.text: iti. jāyamāna evety avadhāraṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. The restriction is: 'only when arising.'

children.translated_text: 'But the other two conditions, by the reverse' —

body.text: iti. samanantarapratyayaḥ pūrvoktas taṃ paścāduktaṃ kāritrakālaniyamam āśrayate. jāyamāne kāritraṃ karotīty arthaḥ. paścādukta ālambanapratyayaḥ pūrvoktaṃ kāritrakālaniyamam āśrayate. nirudhyamāne kāritraṃ karotīty arthaḥ. evaṃ tau
body.translated_text: thus. The immediately preceding condition, stated first, follows the temporal restriction of function stated afterwards. The meaning is: it performs its function when [the conditioned <s>dharma</s>] is arising. The object-condition, stated afterwards, follows the temporal restriction of function stated first. The meaning is: it performs its function when [the conditioned <s>dharma</s>] is ceasing. Thus those two

body.text: kāritraṃ kurutaḥ. tenāha. samanantarapratyayo jāyamāne kāritraṃ karoty avakāśadānāt. ālambanapratyayo nirudhyamāne. vartamānaiś cittacaittair vartamānagrahaṇād iti. grahaṇārthena hy ālambanapratyayo vyavasthāpyate. na cātītanāgatāś cittacaittā grāhyam arthaṃ gṛhṇantīti.
body.translated_text: perform their function. Therefore he says: the immediately preceding condition performs its function when [the <s>dharma</s>] is arising — through giving way. The object-condition [performs its function] when ceasing — because present mind and mental factors, by the statement 'present,' [are functioning] for apprehension. For the object-condition is established for the purpose of apprehension. And past and future mind and mental factors do not apprehend the object to be grasped.

body.text: etad evāsya kāritram iti. yad anāvaraṇabhāvena sarvasyām avasthāyām avasthānaṃ etad evāsyādhipatipratyayasya kāritram iti sugamatvān nādhipatipratyayasya [Tib. 225b] kāritrakālaniyamaḥ sūcita ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'This alone is its function' — the abiding in a state of non-obstruction in all states — this alone is the function of this dominant condition. Because it is easily understood, the temporal restriction of the function of the dominant condition [Tib. 225b] was not indicated — this is the intent.

body.text: (65) dvividho hetur iti. saṃprayuktakasarvatragavipākahetūnām asaṃbhavāt. samānabhūmikāḥ kuśalā dharmā iti. nirodhasamāpatter bhāvāgrikāḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ sabhāgahetur hetupratyayaḥ. asaṃjñisamāpatter api caturthadhyānabhūmikāḥ. yeṣāṃ balena te samāpattī bhavataḥ. samanantarapratyayaḥ sasaṃprayogaṃ samāpatticittam iti. sarveṣāṃ nirodhasamāpattikṣaṇānām asaṃjñisamāpattikṣaṇānāṃ ca cittāntareṇāvyavadhānāt. pūrvavad iti. svabhāvavarjyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ. cittābhisaṃskārajatvād iti. cittābhogajatvād ity arthaḥ. cittotpattivibandhanāt na samanaṃtarapratyaya iti. samanantarapratyayasya cittotpattihetutvāt.
body.translated_text: (65) 'The cause is twofold' — because of the impossibility of the associated, universally pervasive, and maturation causes. 'Wholesome <s>dharma</s>s belonging to the same ground' — the wholesome <s>dharma</s>s belonging to the peak of existence are the homogeneous cause and the cause-condition of the cessation attainment. And those belonging to the ground of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> [are the same] for the non-perception attainment — by whose power those two attainments come about. 'The immediately preceding condition is the mind together with its associates at the time of entering the attainment' — because all moments of the cessation attainment and the non-perception attainment are not intervened by another mind. 'As before' — all <s>dharma</s>s excluding [their] own nature. 'Because of being produced by mental effort' — the meaning is: because of being produced by mental application. 'Because of obstructing the arising of mind, [the attainment] is not an immediately preceding condition' — because the immediately preceding condition is a cause for the arising of mind.

body.text: iti. tuśabdo 'vadhāraṇe bhinnakramaś ca. dvābhyām eva hetvadhipatipratyayābhyām anye vai cittacaittasamāpattidvayavinirmuktā dharmā jāyante. īśvarapuruṣapradhānādikam iti. ādiśabdena kālasvabhāvaparamāṇvādi gṛhyate. nanu cāta eveti. yadi veśvara ekaṃ kāraṇaṃ puruṣa iti vātra pakṣe ko hetur iti hetur mṛgyate. īśvaravyatiriktaṃ hetuṃ kṛtvā tatsiddher iti abhyupagataṃ bhavati. tadabhyupagamāc caikam īśvaraḥ puruṣa iti vā kāraṇaṃ sarvasya jagata iti asya vādasya vyudāsaḥ parityāgaḥ prāpnotīti piṇḍena vākyarthaḥ. [Tib. 226a]
body.translated_text: thus. The particle 'but' (<s>tu</s>) is for restriction and indicates a change of sequence. Other <s>dharma</s>s — those excluded from mind, mental factors, and the two attainments — arise from only two: the cause-condition and the dominant condition. '<s>Īśvara</s> (God), <s>Puruṣa</s> (primal person), <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), and the like' — by the word 'and the like,' time (<s>kāla</s>), inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>), and the like are included. 'Is it not from this very [argument]' — if <s>Īśvara</s> alone is one cause, or <s>Puruṣa</s> — in this position, what is the [additional] cause? — [when] a cause is sought, it is accepted that [one must] posit a cause other than <s>Īśvara</s> in order to establish that [production]. And from that acceptance, the doctrine that <s>Īśvara</s> or <s>Puruṣa</s> is the single cause of the entire world — the rejection, the abandonment of this doctrine follows. This is the meaning of the passage in summary. [Tib. 226a]

children.translated_text: 'Not from <s>Īśvara</s> and the rest, because of sequence and the like' —

body.text: iti. neśvarāder bhāvā jāyante. kasmāt. kramādibhiḥ. ādigrahaṇena deśakālādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ. atha vānekakāraṇatvānavasthāprasaṃgād anyapuruṣakālanihnavādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ. yadi hy ekam eveti vistaraḥ. yadi hy ekam eva kāraṇam īśvaraḥ syāt mahādevo vā vāsudevo vā anyad vā puruṣādi vety arthaḥ. yugapat sarveṇa jagatā bhavitavyaṃ kāraṇasya sadbhāvāt. na hy etad iṣṭaṃ. sati kāraṇe kāryaṃ na bhavatīti. dṛśyate ca bhāvānāṃ kalalādīnām aṃkurādīnāṃ ca kramasaṃbhavaḥ. tasmāt svakāraṇaparaṃparānirvṛtta iti neśvarādikāraṇam iti gamyate. īśvarādyekakāraṇaṃ jagad iti hi pratijānānasya svakāraṇakramotpāditvādilakṣaṇena dharmaviśeṣeṇa tasya sāpakṣālatvaṃ pakṣasyopalakṣyate. sa tarhi chandavaśād iti. sa kramabheda icchāvaśād īśvarasya syāt. katham ity āha. ayam idānīṃ bhāva utpadyatāṃ yāvad ayaṃ paścād utpadyatām iti. evaṃ kramasaṃbhavaś ca bhāvānāṃ īśvaraś ca kāraṇam iti īśvarakāraṇikābhiprāyaḥ. chandabhedād iti vistaraḥ. īśvaracchandabhedāc caikakāraṇatvābhyupagamāc ca prākpakṣavirodhād dharmasvarūpaviparyayaḥ pakṣasyotpadyate. sa cāpīti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 226b] sa cāpi chandabhedo yugapat syāt. taddhetoś chandabhedahetor īśvarasyābhinnatvād ekatvād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Entities do not arise from <s>Īśvara</s> and the rest. Why? Because of sequence and the like. By the word 'and the like,' place, time, and the like are included. Or alternatively, it includes [the objections from] manifold causation, infinite regress, denial of other agents (<s>puruṣa</s>), time, and so forth. 'If indeed one alone' — thus the elaboration. If <s>Īśvara</s> alone were the single cause — whether <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, or another such as <s>Puruṣa</s> and the rest, this is the meaning — then everything in the world would have to [arise] simultaneously, because of the existence of the cause. For this is not acceptable: that when the cause exists, the effect does not occur. And the sequential arising of entities — of the <s>kalala</s> and the rest, of sprouts and the rest — is observed. Therefore, [entities] are produced by a succession of their own causes — and it is understood that <s>Īśvara</s> and the like are not the cause. For one who asserts that the world has <s>Īśvara</s> and the like as a single cause, the quality of having a counter-example characterized by sequential arising from one's own causes is observed in the thesis. 'He then [might say it is] according to his will' — that difference in sequence would be according to the will of <s>Īśvara</s>. How? He says: 'Let this entity arise now; let that entity arise later.' Thus, sequential arising of entities and <s>Īśvara</s> as cause — this is the intent of the <s>Īśvara</s>-causation theorist. 'Because of difference in will' — thus the elaboration. Because of the difference in <s>Īśvara</s>'s will, and because of the acceptance of single causation — through contradiction with the prior position — a reversal of the nature of the thesis arises. 'And that [difference in will]' — thus the elaboration. [Tib. 226b] That difference in will too would have to be simultaneous — because the cause of that difference in will — <s>Īśvara</s> — is undifferentiated, being one, this is the meaning

body.text: tataś ca eva sa pūrvokto dośo yugapat syād iti. atha manyase. anyad api kāraṇāntaraṃ bhinnaṃ tadutpattau īśvaro 'pekṣata ity ata idam ucyate. kāraṇāntarabhedāpekṣaṇe ce ti vistaraḥ. neśvara eva kāraṇam ity abhyupagame sa eva doṣaḥ. teṣām api ceti vistaraḥ. teṣām api ca kārṇāntarāṇāṃ kramotpattāv iṣyamāṇāyāṃ kāraṇāntarabhedānām api punaḥ kāraṇāntarabhedāpekṣaṇād anavasthāprasaṃgaḥ. teṣām api kāraṇāntarabhedāpekṣaṇaṃ teṣām api kāraṇāntarabhedāpekṣaṇam ity aparyavasānaprasaṃgaḥ syāt. śākyaputrīyam eva nyāyam iti. anādiḥ saṃsāra iti śākyaputrīyaṃ nyāyaṃ nātikrāntaḥ syāt. yaugapadye 'pīti vistaraḥ. athāpi syāt. yaugapadye 'pīśvarachandānāṃ na jagato yaugapadyaṃ. kasmāt. yathāchandaṃ utpādāt. yaś chandaḥ ayam idānīm utpadyatām iti. tasya tasmāc chandād idānīm evotpattiḥ. yaḥ paścād utpadyatām iti. tasya tasmāt paścād utpattiḥ. idaṃ ca paścāt paścāttaram evaṃprakāram iti tasya tasmāt paścāttaraṃ tathaivotpattir iti. tac ca na. teṣāṃ paścād viśeṣābhāvāt. teṣāṃ chandānāṃ paścān na kaścid viśeṣa iti. yathaiva pūrvaṃ nārabhante. tathā paścād api nārabheran. yathā vā paścād ārabhante. tathā pūrvam apīti. atha vā eka evotpādayitā netara iti tesāṃ viśeṣābhāvaḥ. ataḥ prāptam eva bhāvānām īśvaracchandānām [Tib. 227a] iva yaugapadyaṃ. kāraṇāntarāpekṣatve vā chandaviśeṣāṇāṃ pūrvavad dośaḥ. na tasyām īśvaraḥ syād iti. na tasyāṃ prītau īśvaraḥ syād vinopāyena tatkāraṇaśakteḥ. etad īśvarasyeśvaratvaṃ. yad asau kāraṇāntarānapekṣaḥ kuryāt. tathaiva cānyasminn iti. yathā prītāv anīśvaraḥ. evam anyasminn api trailokye neśvara ity anumīyate. yadi ceśvara iti vistaraḥ. narakādiṣu prajāṃ sṛṣṭvā bahubhiś cetibhir upasṛṣṭāṃ. bahubhir anekaiḥ prakārair ītibhir upasargai rogādibhir upasṛṣtām upadrutāṃ prajāṃ sṛṣṭvā yadi prīyeta namo 'stu tasmai ity utprāsavacanam etat. sugītaś ceti vistaraḥ. sūktaś cāyaṃ tam ārabhya tam īśvaram adhikṛtya ślokaḥ śatarudrīye vyāsena
body.translated_text: And then indeed that previously stated fault — [everything arising] simultaneously — would follow. Now you may think: <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) depends on yet another, different subsidiary cause for the production of those [things]. In response to this, it is said: 'If there is dependence on different subsidiary causes' — and so on in detail. [Even] on the assumption that <s>Īśvara</s> alone is not the cause — the same fault [follows]. 'And of those too' — and so on in detail. And if the sequential arising of those subsidiary causes too is desired, then because the differentiation of those subsidiary causes also requires dependence on [further] different subsidiary causes, there is the consequence of infinite regress. '[There would be] dependence on differentiation of subsidiary causes for those, and dependence on differentiation of subsidiary causes for those' — the consequence of non-termination would follow. 'He would not have gone beyond the principle of the <s>Śākyaputrīya</s> [i.e., the Buddhist]' — [namely, the principle that] <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless — this is the Buddhist principle. 'Even if [there is] simultaneity [of desires]' — and so on in detail. Even if there is simultaneity of <s>Īśvara</s>'s desires, there is no simultaneity of the world. Why? Because of production according to [his] desire. The desire 'let this be produced now' — from that desire, production occurs precisely now. The desire 'let this be produced later' — from that, production occurs later. [The desire] 'and this [is to be produced] later, and still later, of such a kind' — from that, production occurs still later in the same way. But this [is refuted]: because there is no differentiation among those [desires] in terms of [being] later. Among those desires, there is no differentiation [that makes one] later — therefore: just as [they do] not begin earlier, so too they would not begin later; or just as they begin later, so too [they would begin] earlier as well. Alternatively, since there is only one producer, not another — there is no differentiation among those [desires]. Therefore, the simultaneity of things is simply entailed, [Tib. 227a] just like [the simultaneity of] <s>Īśvara</s>'s desires. Or, if [<s>Īśvara</s>'s] desire-differentiation depends on subsidiary causes, the same fault as before [follows]. 'He would not be the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) of that [delight]' — He would not be the Lord of that delight without means, because of the power of its cause. This is the sovereignty of <s>Īśvara</s>: that he would act without depending on other causes. 'And likewise with respect to other [things]' — just as [he is] not sovereign over delight, so too it is inferred that [he is] not sovereign over the rest of the three worlds either. 'And if <s>Īśvara</s> [exists]' — and so on in detail. Having created beings in the hells and elsewhere, afflicted by many calamities — having created beings afflicted and tormented by many, various kinds of calamities, misfortunes, diseases, and the like — if he takes delight [in that], 'homage to him!' — this is a mocking exclamation. 'And well-sung [is this verse]' — and so on in detail. And this verse is well-spoken, composed concerning him — that <s>Īśvara</s> — by <s>Vyāsa</s> in the <s>Śatarudrīya</s>:

body.text: yasmān nirdahati tasmād
body.translated_text: 'Because he burns, therefore' —

body.text: ity evaṃ sarvatra. anyeṣām iti. bījādīnāṃ aṃkurādiṣu pratyakṣaḥ puruṣakāro nihnutaḥ syāt. kāraṇebhyo 'nyasya vyāpāradarśanād iti. cakṣūrūpālokamanaskārādibhyaś ca eakṣurvijñānādyutpattau bījakṣetrodakādibhyaś cāṃkurādyutpattau anyasya vyāpārānupalabdheḥ. yathā hi cakṣurādīnāṃ cakṣurvijñānādyutpattau bījādīnāṃ cāṃkurādyutpattau vyāpāro dṛśyate. tadbhāve
body.translated_text: thus everywhere. 'Of others' — the perceptible efficient action of seeds and the rest in [producing] sprouts and the rest would be concealed. 'Because the operation of nothing other than the causes is seen' — because no operation of anything other than the eye, form, light, mental attention, and the rest in the production of visual consciousness and the rest, and [other than] seed, field, water, and the rest in the production of sprouts and the rest, is apprehended. For just as the operation of the eye and the rest in the production of visual consciousness and the rest, and of seeds and the rest in the production of sprouts and the rest, is seen — because of [the effect's] existence when they exist

body.text: bhāvāt tadabhāve cābhāvāt. na tathā cakṣurādibhāve bījādibhāve ca [Tib. 227b] īśvarasyābhāve cakṣurvijñānāṃkurādyabhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ. punaś ca tadbhāve bhāvaḥ. yatas tasyāpi tadutpattau vyāpāro gamyate. atas tadvyāpāradarśanāt saha kāraṇair īśvaraṃ kāraṇaṃ kalpayatāṃ kevalo bhaktivādaḥ syāt. kiṃ ca sahakāriṣu ceti vistaraḥ. yāni sahakārīṇy anyāni tasyeśvarasya. kiṃ teṣv īśvaro neśvaraḥ syāt. tāni hi kāryotpattau svasāmarthyena vyāpriyaṃte. anyeṣu tu sahakāriṣv īśvaraḥ syād iti anyagrahaṇaṃ. ādisarga īśvarahetukaḥ. tathā hi pratyakṣapuruṣakāranihnavo na syāt. kāraṇebhyo 'nyasya vyāpārādarśane cādośo jagataś ceśvaraḥ kāraṇam iti. tasyāpy anyakāraṇānapekṣatvāt. tasyāpy ādisargasyānyakāraṇānapekṣatvāt. īśvara evaikaḥ. kāraṇaṃ nānyad iti. īśvavavad anāditvaprasaṃgaḥ. aniṣṭaṃ caitat tasmān neśvaraḥ kāraṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: and non-existence when they do not exist — the non-existence of visual consciousness, sprouts, and the rest [Tib. 227b] in the absence of <s>Īśvara</s> while the eye and the rest, seeds and the rest [are present] is not seen. And again, [the effect's] existence when he exists [is not seen]. Therefore, since no operation of his in their production is discernible, for those who posit <s>Īśvara</s> as a cause together with the [other] causes, [theirs] would be merely a statement of devotion. 'Moreover, regarding the auxiliaries' — and so on in detail. Those other things that are auxiliaries of that <s>Īśvara</s> — is <s>Īśvara</s> sovereign over them or not? For they operate by their own power in the production of effects. [The word] 'other' means: he would be sovereign over [things] other than the auxiliaries. '[Objection:] The initial creation is caused by <s>Īśvara</s>.' [Reply:] But then the concealment of perceptible efficient action would not [follow]; and since no operation of anything other than the causes is seen, there is no fault — and <s>Īśvara</s> is the cause of the world. [Reply to that:] Because even that [initial creation] does not depend on other causes. Because even that initial creation does not depend on other causes, <s>Īśvara</s> alone is the single cause; there is no other. [Then] the consequence of [the world's] beginninglessness, like <s>Īśvara</s> [himself, follows]. And this is undesired. Therefore, <s>Īśvara</s> is not the cause.

body.text: evaṃ pradhāne 'pi yathāgogaṃ yojyam iti. pradhānam acetanaṃ. tasmāt tatra chandavikalpanāṃ hitvā śeṣapratiṣedhavidhānaṃ yojyaṃ. yady ekam eva kāraṇaṃ pradhānaṃ syāt. yugapat sarveṇa jagatā bhavitavyaṃ syāt. dṛśyate ca bhāvānāṃ kramasaṃbhavaḥ. kāraṇāntarabhedāpekṣaṇe vā na pradhānam eva kāraṇaṃ syāt. teṣām api kramotpattau kāraṇāntarabhedāpekṣanād anavasthāprasaṃgaḥ syād iti vistaraḥ. evaṃ khalv api jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ parigṛhṇatā anyeṣām arthānāṃ pratyakṣaḥ puruṣakāro nihnutaḥ syāt. sahāpi ca kāraṇaiḥ kāraṇaṃ pradhānaṃ kalpayatām [Tib. 228a] kevalo bhaktivādaḥ syāt. kāraṇebhyo 'nyasya vyāpāradarśanāt. sahakāriṣu cānyeṣu kāraṇeṣu tatpradhānam apradhānaṃ syāt. athādisargaḥ pradhānahetukaḥ. tasyāpi mahadādyutpādasvabhāvasyādisargasyādyalakṣaṇatvāt pradhānavat anāditvaprasaṃgaḥ. nityaṃ hi pradhānaṃ pradhānaṃ ca mahataḥ kāraṇam iti pūrvapradhānaṃ pascān mahān iti na sidhyati. prasavadharmi ca pradhānam iti tena nityaṃ pravartitavyaṃ kāraṇāntaranirapekṣatvāt. na hi prakāśaḥ prakāśyam arthaṃ prakāśya punar na prakāśayatīti. svabhāvo hi kṛtārthatāṃ nopekṣate. akṛtabuddhayaḥ paramārthaśāstrair asaṃskṛtabuddhaya ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'The same should be applied, as appropriate, to <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) as well.' <s>Pradhāna</s> is unconscious. Therefore, setting aside the refutation involving desire, the remaining refutations should be applied. If <s>Pradhāna</s> alone were the single cause, the entire world would have to [arise] simultaneously. And the sequential arising of things is observed. Or, if dependence on the differentiation of subsidiary causes [is posited], then <s>Pradhāna</s> alone would not be the cause. If the sequential arising of those too [depends on further] differentiation of subsidiary causes, the consequence of infinite regress would follow — and so on in detail. 'Likewise indeed, for one accepting this as the cause of the world, the perceptible efficient action of other things would be concealed. And for those who posit <s>Pradhāna</s> as a cause together with [other] causes, [Tib. 228a] [theirs] would be merely a statement of devotion' — because no operation of anything other than the causes is seen. 'And with respect to other subsidiary causes, that <s>Pradhāna</s> would not be predominant.' 'But the initial creation is caused by <s>Pradhāna</s>' — for that initial creation too, which has the nature of the arising of <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One) and the rest, because it has the characteristic of being the first, the consequence of beginninglessness, like <s>Pradhāna</s> [itself, follows]. For <s>Pradhāna</s> is eternal, and <s>Pradhāna</s> is the cause of <s>Mahat</s> — so the [claim that] <s>Pradhāna</s> [comes] first and <s>Mahat</s> after is not established. And since <s>Pradhāna</s> has the nature of producing, it should always be active, because of not depending on other causes. For light does not, having illuminated an object, subsequently not illuminate it. For intrinsic nature does not await the completion of its purpose. 'Those of uncultivated intelligence' — meaning: those whose intelligence has not been refined by treatises on the ultimate.

children.translated_text: 'Entities are twofold; of those, the cause' —

body.text: iti. pūrvotpannāni bhūtāni paścādutpannānāṃ svāsaṃtānikānāṃ sabhāgahetur avinirbhāgavartīni sahabhūhetuḥ. bhūtānuvidhāyitvād iti. bhautikaṃ bhūtāny anuvidhatte. tadvikāre vikārāt. ācāryādiniśrayavad iti. yathābhikṣur ācāryam āśrayate. ādiśabdena upādhyāyaṃ ca niśrayate. tadvat. bhūtāni bhautikaṃ niśrayate. evam eṣām iti vistaraḥ. janmahetutvam eṣāṃ bhūtānām ākhyātaṃ tu bhautikasya tebhya utpatteḥ. vikārahetutvaṃ tadanuvidhāyitvāt. ādhārahetutvaṃ
body.translated_text: thus. Previously arisen elements (<s>bhūta</s>) are the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>) of subsequently arisen [elements] within their own continuum, and are the co-existent cause (<s>sahabhūhetu</s>) [of derived form] as inseparably co-existing [with it]. 'Because [derived form] conforms to the elements' — derived form (<s>bhautika</s>) conforms to the elements. In the modification of those [elements], there is modification [of derived form]. 'Like dependence on a teacher and the rest' — just as a monk depends on a teacher — by the word 'and the rest,' and relies on a preceptor. Likewise, derived form depends on the elements. 'Thus, of these' — and so on in detail. The state of being a cause of origination (<s>janmahetu</s>) has been stated for these elements with respect to derived form — because of [derived form's] arising from them. The state of being a cause of modification — because of [derived form's] conformity to them. The state of being a cause of support (<s>ādhārahetu</s>)

body.text: ādhārabhāvāt. sthitihetutvam anucchedahetutvāt. vṛddhihetutvam upabṛmhaṇahetutvād iti. aviśeṣavartitvād iti [Tib. 228b] avighnabhāvavasthānenānyeṣām api hetutvād ity arthaḥ. anyonyaṃ cittānuparivartikāyavākkarneti. kāyakarma cittānuparivarti dhyānānāsravasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ trividhaṃ prāṇātipātādattādānakāmamithyācāraviratibhedena. vākkarmāpi cittānuparivarti dhyānānāsravasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītam eva caturvidhaṃ. mṛṣāvādapaiśunyapāruṣyasaṃbhinnapralāpaviratibhedena. tad evaṃ saptavidhaṃ kāyavākkarmānyonyaṃ sahabhūhetuḥ. prāṇatipātaviratir upādāyarūpaṃ itareṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ sahabhūhetuḥ. tāny api ṣaṭ tasya sahabhūhetur iti sarvaṃ yojyaṃ. nānyad iti. cakṣurādikaṃ sarvam upādāyarūpaṃ prātimokṣasaṃvarādisaṃgṛhītam api yāvan nānyonyaṃ sahabhūhetuḥ pṛthakkalāpatvāt. sabhāgasyeti. kuśalaṃ kuśalasya svāsaṃtānikasya kliṣṭaṃ kliṣṭasyetyādi. yasya kāyavākkarmaṇa iti. vijñaptyavijñaptisvabhāvasya samāhitasyāsamāhitasya vā yathāyogaṃ. ekadhaiva tad iti. vipākahetur evaika ity avadhāraṇaṃ. kāraṇahetos tathaivāgaṇyamānatvāt. pṛthakkalāpatvād iti sahabhūhetvādyayogāt.
body.translated_text: — because of being the substrate. The state of being a cause of sustenance (<s>sthitihetu</s>) — because of being the cause of non-cessation. The state of being a cause of growth (<s>vṛddhihetu</s>) — because of being the cause of augmentation. 'Because of operating without distinction' — [Tib. 228b] meaning: because of being a cause of others too by remaining in an unobstructed state. 'Bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> that conforms to consciousness — mutually [are co-existent causes]' — bodily <s>karma</s> that conforms to consciousness, included in <s>dhyāna</s>- and non-outflow restraint, is threefold: by the distinction of abstaining from killing, abstaining from taking what is not given, and abstaining from sexual misconduct. Vocal <s>karma</s> that conforms to consciousness, included in <s>dhyāna</s>- and non-outflow restraint only, is fourfold: by the distinction of abstaining from false speech, slander, harsh speech, and idle talk. Thus, sevenfold bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> are mutually co-existent causes. The abstention from killing, being derived form, is the co-existent cause of the other six; and those six are its co-existent cause — all should be connected thus. 'Not other [form]' — all derived form such as the eye-faculty and the rest, even though included in <s>Prātimokṣa</s>-restraint and the rest, is nevertheless not mutually a co-existent cause — because of belonging to separate assemblages. 'Of the homogeneous (<s>sabhāga</s>)' — the wholesome [is the homogeneous cause] of one's own wholesome within the same continuum; the defiled of the defiled — and so on. 'Of whichever bodily-vocal <s>karma</s>' — whether having the nature of <s>vijñapti</s> or <s>avijñapti</s>, whether concentrated or unconcentrated, as appropriate. 'That alone' — the restriction is: a retribution cause only. Because the universal cause too is not counted [separately, being included]. 'Because of belonging to separate assemblages' — because of the inapplicability of the co-existent cause and the rest.

body.text: (II.67) rūpadhātāv akuśalaṃ nāstīti. sa viviktaṃ kāmair viviktaṃ pāpakair akuśalair dharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam [Tib. 229a] upasaṃpadya viharatīti vacanāt. tatra rūpadhātāv akuśalaṃ nāsti. akuśalavivekād dhi yaj jātaṃ śubhaṃ. tad vivekam ity ucyate. yathā ca hetuḥ. tathā phalam iti. tatropapattāv api nāsty akuśalam iti gamyate. rūpārūpyadhātau sarva eva kleśopakleśāv avipākatvān nivṛtā eva nākuśalāḥ.
body.translated_text: (II.67) 'In the form-realm there is no unwholesome' — because of the statement: 'He, secluded from sense-desires, secluded from unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, with applied thought and sustained thought, born of seclusion, [experiencing] joy and happiness, enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s>.' [Tib. 229a] There, in the form-realm, there is no unwholesome. For the wholesome that is born from seclusion from the unwholesome is called 'seclusion.' 'And as the cause, so the result' — from this, it is understood that even in rebirth there, there is no unwholesome. In the form and formless realms, all afflictions and secondary afflictions, because of not producing retribution, are obstructed [indeterminate] only, not unwholesome.

body.text: (II.68-71) anantaram iti paścād vakṣyata iti kārikānte. tad iha saṃbandhanīyaṃ. samāpattikāle kuśalam iti. kāmāvacaraprāyogikakuśalacittānantaraṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ sāmantakīyaṃ maulīyaṃ vā cittam utpadyate. pratisaṃdhikāle nivṛtam iti. kāmāvacaropapattipratilambhikamaraṇacittānantaraṃ rūpāvacaraṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ cittam utpadyate pratisaṃdhikāle.
body.translated_text: (II.68-71) 'Immediately after' — [this connects to] what will be stated later at the end of the verse. This should be connected here. 'At the time of attainment, the wholesome' — immediately after a desire-realm practice-born wholesome mind, a mind belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground arises — whether of the preliminary [concentration] or the principal [<s>dhyāna</s>]. 'At the time of rebirth-connection, the obstructed' — immediately after a desire-realm rebirth-obtained death-mind, a form-realm obstructed-indeterminate mind arises at the time of rebirth-connection.

children.translated_text: 'The existence of rebirth is defiled, with all the afflictions of one's own ground' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. upapattir atrāntarābhavopapattir abhipretā. evam antarābhavapratisaṃdhir api kliṣṭo veditavyaḥ. catasṛbhir dūratābhir dūra iti. tatreyam āśrayadūratā. yad ārūpyāvacareṇa āśrayeṇa kāmāvacaraḥ kaścid api dharmo na saṃmukhīkriyate. yathā rūpāvacareṇāśrayeṇa kāmāvacaraṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ saṃmukhīkriyata iti. anayāśrayadūratayā kāmadhātor ārūpyā dūre bhavaṃti. ākāradūratā. yad ārūpyāvacareṇa cittena kāmadhātur nākāryate. yathā rūpāvacareṇa audārika ityādibhir ākāraiḥ. ālambanadūratā. yad ārūpyāvacareṇa
body.translated_text: because of this statement. The 'rebirth' here intended is the rebirth from the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>). Thus, the rebirth-connection from the intermediate existence too should be understood as defiled. 'Far through four [kinds of] distance' — therein, this is the distance of basis (<s>āśrayadūratā</s>): that by a basis belonging to the formless realm, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever of the desire-realm is directly confronted — unlike [the case where] by a form-realm basis, a desire-realm supernaturally-created mind is directly confronted. Through this distance of basis, the formless [realms] are far from the desire-realm. Distance of aspect (<s>ākāradūratā</s>): that by a mind of the formless realm, the desire-realm is not apprehended through aspects — unlike by [a mind of] the form-realm, [which apprehends it] through aspects such as 'coarse' and the like. Distance of object (<s>ālambanadūratā</s>): that by

body.text: cittena na kāmadhātur ālambyate. yathā rūpāvacareṇa. nanu ca rūpadhātur api nārūpyāvacareṇa cittenālaṃbyate.
body.translated_text: a mind of the formless realm, the desire-realm is not taken as object — unlike by [a mind of] the form-realm. [Objection:] But the form-realm too is not taken as object by a mind of the formless realm.

children.translated_text: 'The principal wholesome formless [attainments], having outflows, do not take a lower [realm] as object' —

body.text: Tib. 229b
body.translated_text: Tib. 229b

body.text: iti vacanāt. tat katham idam ucyate kāmadhātor evārūpyā dūrata iti. satyaṃ na maulārūpyāvacareṇa cittena rūpadhātur adhyālaṃbyate. kiṃ tu ākāśānaṃtyāyatanasāmantakacittena audārikādyākāraiś caturthadhyānam ālaṃbyata iti. ato na kāmadhātor iva rūpadhātor ārūpyā dūre vyavasthāpyaṃte. pratipakṣadūratā. yad ārūpyā na kāmadhātoḥ pratipakṣaḥ. yathā rūpadhātuḥ. ity evam āśrayālambanākārapratipakṣadūratābhir api kāmadhātor ārūpyā dūre bhavaṃti. tasmān na kāmāvacarakuśalānantaraṃ ārūpyāvacaraṃ kuśalam utpadyate. śaikṣam aśaikṣaṃ ceti. kāmāvacaraprāyogikakuśalacittānantaraṃ samāpattikāle labdhapūrvaṃ śaikṣam utpadyate. tathaiva cāśaikṣaṃ. kliṣṭasamāpattyutpīḍitasyeti. kliṣṭayā samāpattyā utpīḍitasya yogino 'dharāyāḥ kuśalāyā bhūmeḥ saṃśrayaṇān nivṛtāvyākṛtād api kuśalaṃ cittam utpadyate. varam adharāpi kuśalā bhūmir nordhvā kliṣṭeti. sarvebhyo rūpārūpyacittebhya iti. kuśalāvyākṛtacittasya maraṇasaṃbhavāt.
body.translated_text: because of that statement. 'But then how can it be said that the formless [attainments] are far from the desire realm?' True, the form realm is not taken as an object by a principal formless-realm mind. However, by the mind of the preliminary to the sphere of infinite space, the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is taken as an object through aspects such as 'gross,' etc. Therefore the formless [attainments] are not established as far from the form realm in the way they are from the desire realm. Distance in terms of antidote: the formless [attainments] are not an antidote to the desire realm, as the form realm is. Thus, through the distances of support, object, aspect, and antidote, the formless [attainments] are far from the desire realm. Therefore, immediately after a desire-realm wholesome [mind], a formless-realm wholesome [mind] does not arise. 'And the trainee and non-trainee [minds]' — immediately after a desire-realm practice-born wholesome mind, a previously obtained trainee [mind] arises at the time of attainment. And likewise a non-trainee [mind]. 'For one oppressed by an afflicted attainment' — for a practitioner oppressed by an afflicted attainment, because of resorting to a lower wholesome ground, a wholesome mind arises even from a covered-indeterminate [mind]. [The rationale being:] 'better a lower wholesome ground than a higher afflicted one.' 'From all form- and formless-realm minds' — because death is possible for a wholesome or indeterminate mind.

body.text: tasmād akuśalāc catvāri svabhūmikāny eva. akuśalasyordhvabhūmikuśalaprayogatvāsaṃbhavād aprahāṇāc cordhvabhūmyupapatticittānutpādāt. [Tib. 230a] kuśalaṃ nirmāṇacittād anantaram iti. nirmāṇād vyutthānakāle. tasmād anantaram ekādaśeti. pratisaṃdhisamāpattitadvyutthānanirmāṇapraveśakāleṣv ekādaśacittotpattisaṃbhavaḥ. kathaṃ. svabhūmikāni trīṇi kāmāvacarāṇi ca. vyutthānakāle kuśalaṃ. pratisaṃdhikāle kliṣṭadvayaṃ. anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ ca nirmāṇacittaṃ. ārūpyāvacaraṃ. ca nivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ pratisaṃdhikāle. kuśalaṃ ca samāpattikāle. śaikṣam aśaikṣaṃ ceti. na tv ārūpyāvacaram anivṛtāvyākṛtam. avaśyākliṣṭatvāt. samāpattyādyayogāc ca. na hi tat prayogalabhyaṃ yathā rūpāvacaraṃ kāmāvacaraṃ ca nirmāṇacittaṃ. kāmāvacaraṃ ca kliṣṭadvayaṃ ārūpyāvacaraṃ cānivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ hitveti. na kāmāvacarāt kliṣṭadvayāt rūpāvacaraṃ kuśalam utpadyate. tasya kliṣṭadvayasya tatprayogānarhatvāt. ata eva ca nārūpyāvacarād anivṛtāvyākṛtāt tad utpadyate. kuśalena ca pratisaṃdhibandhābhāvāt. kāmāvacaraṃ kliṣtadvayaṃ śaikṣāśaikṣe ca sthāpayitveti. na kāmāvacarāt kliṣṭadvayād rūpāvacaraṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtam utpadyate. tadaprahāṇe rūpadhātau pratisaṃdhibandhābhāvena nivṛtāvyākṛtacittasaṃbhavāt. na śaikṣāśaikṣābhyāṃ. tatastyena [Tib. 230b] kliṣṭena vyutthānāsaṃbhavāt. kāmāvacarāṇi
body.translated_text: therefore from unwholesome [mind], [only] four [types arise], belonging to one's own ground alone — because the unwholesome is incapable of producing a practice of higher-ground wholesome [mind], and because without abandoning [the unwholesome], a higher-ground rebirth-mind does not arise. [Tib. 230a] 'A wholesome [mind] immediately after a creation-mind' — at the time of emerging from creation. 'Therefore immediately [after that], eleven' — the arising of eleven [types of] mind is possible at the times of rebirth-connection, attainment, emergence from attainment, and entering creation. How? Three belonging to one's own ground and desire-realm [minds]. A wholesome [mind] at the time of emergence. The two afflicted [types] at the time of rebirth-connection. And the uncovered-indeterminate creation-mind. And a formless-realm covered-indeterminate [mind] at the time of rebirth-connection. And a wholesome [mind] at the time of attainment. And the trainee and non-trainee [minds]. But not a formless-realm uncovered-indeterminate [mind], because [the formless realm] is necessarily unafflicted, and because attainment and so forth are not applicable — for that is not obtainable through practice, as are the form-realm and desire-realm creation-minds. 'Excluding the desire-realm two afflicted [types] and the formless-realm uncovered-indeterminate' — from the desire-realm two afflicted [types], a form-realm wholesome [mind] does not arise, because those two afflicted [types] are not fit for that practice. For this very reason, it does not arise from the formless-realm uncovered-indeterminate either. And because there is no rebirth-connection through a wholesome [mind]. 'Excluding the desire-realm two afflicted, the trainee and non-trainee [minds]' — from the desire-realm two afflicted [types], a form-realm covered-indeterminate [mind] does not arise, because without the abandonment of that, the rebirth-connection in the form realm being impossible, [Tib. 230b] a covered-indeterminate mind is impossible. Not from the trainee and non-trainee [minds], because emergence from that afflicted [state] through those is impossible. And from those is not its arising. 'Those same four and the non-trainee' — the three realms' wholesome [minds] at the time of emergence. And the trainee [mind] in the flow. 'The knowledge of destruction immediately after the diamond-like [samādhi]' — and the non-trainee [mind]. 'Five from the five just stated' — from the three realms' wholesome [minds] at the time of attainment, and at the arising immediately after the diamond-like [samādhi] and in the flow. 'Therefore four' — excluding the trainee. For from the non-trainee, a trainee [mind] does not arise. 'How does it not arise at the time of decline?' Because it is separated by the arising of afflictions, and because decline is only for one who has emerged.

body.text: ceti. trīṇīty adhikṛtaṃ. pratisaṃdhikāle kliṣṭadvayaṃ kliṣṭasamādhyutpīḍitasya ca kuśalaṃ. kāmāvacare ca kliṣṭe ārūpyāvacaraṃ ceti. pratisaṃdhikāle. adharadhātukāni ca kliṣṭāni pratisaṃdhikāle. ārūpyāvacarāt kuśalān naveti. svabhūmikāni trīṇi. rūpāvacaraṃ kuśalaṃ tatsamāpattivyutthānakāle pratilomasamāpattau ca. adharabhūmikāni ca kliṣṭāni pratisaṃdhikāle. śaikṣam aśaikṣaṃ ca. kāmāvacaraṃ kuśalaṃ kāmarūpāvacarānivṛtāvyākṛte hitveti. na kāmāvacareṇa kuśalena tatsamāpatter vyutthānaṃ saṃbhavati ativiprakṛṣṭatvāt. ata eva ca nānivṛtāvyākṛtenāpi apaṭutvāt. ata eva ca na rūpāvacareṇānivṛtāvyākṛtena vyutthānaṃ. na caibhiḥ pratisaṃdhibandho 'stīti naiṣām ata utpattiḥ. tatṣaṇṇām anaṃtaram iti vartate. rūpāvacarāt kuśalād iti. samāpattikāle. śaikṣāśaikṣābhyāṃ ceti. vyutthānakāle. rūpāvacaraṃ kuśalam iti. kliṣṭasamādhyutpīḍitasya. nivṛtaṃ cetyādi. pratisaṃdhikāle. kāmarūpāvacarāṇi kliṣtāni śaikṣāśaikṣe ca hitveti. adhobhūmyavītarāgasya tena [Tib. 231a] pratisaṃdher abhāvāt. śaikṣāśaikṣābhyāṃ ca tena vyutthānāsaṃbhavān na tebhyas tadutpattiḥ. tāny eva catvāry aśaikṣaṃ ceti. trīṇi traidhātukāni kuśalāni vyutthānakāle. śaikṣaṃ ca pravāhe. vajropamānantaraṃ kṣayajñānam iti aśaikṣaṃ ceti. paṃca paṃcakād ata evānantaroktād iti. traidhātukebhyaḥ kuśalebhyaḥ samāpattikāle. vajropamānantarotpattau pravāhe ceti. tasmāc catvārīti. śaikṣaṃ hitvā. na hy aśaikṣāt śaikṣam utpadyate. parihāṇikāle kathaṃ notpadyate. kleśotpādavyavahitatvāt. vyutthitasyaiva parihāṇeś ca.
body.translated_text: 'And' [the verse word]. 'Three' is what is governed [by the syntax]. At the time of rebirth-connection, the two afflicted [types]; and for one oppressed by an afflicted attainment, the wholesome [mind]. In the desire-realm afflicted [mind], also the formless-realm [arises]. At the time of rebirth-connection. And the lower-realm [minds] when afflicted, at the time of rebirth-connection. From a formless-realm wholesome [mind], nine [arise]. Three belonging to one's own ground: the form-realm wholesome [mind] at the time of emerging from that attainment and in the reverse-order attainment; and the lower-ground [minds] when afflicted, at the time of rebirth-connection; and the trainee and non-trainee [minds]. 'Excluding the desire-realm wholesome and the desire- and form-realm uncovered-indeterminate' — emergence from that attainment is not possible through a desire-realm wholesome [mind], because of [its] excessive remoteness. And for this very reason it is not [possible] through an uncovered-indeterminate [mind] either, because of [its] dullness. And for this very reason there is no emergence through a form-realm uncovered-indeterminate [mind]. And there is no rebirth-connection through these; hence from these there is no arising of it. 'Immediately after those six' is to be supplied. 'From a form-realm wholesome [mind]' — at the time of attainment. 'And from the trainee and non-trainee [minds]' — at the time of emergence. 'A form-realm wholesome [mind]' — for one oppressed by an afflicted attainment. 'And the covered [indeterminate],' etc. — at the time of rebirth-connection. 'Excluding the desire- and form-realm afflicted [minds] and the trainee and non-trainee [minds]' — because for one not free from passion for the lower ground there is no rebirth-connection through that, and because emergence from that is impossible through the trainee and non-trainee [minds], from these there is no arising of it. 'Those same four and the non-trainee' — the three realms' wholesome [minds] at the time of emergence; and the trainee [mind] in the flow. 'The knowledge of destruction immediately after the diamond-like [samādhi]' — and the non-trainee [mind]. 'Five from the five just stated' — from the three realms' wholesome [minds] at the time of attainment, and at the arising immediately after the diamond-like [samādhi] and in the flow. 'Therefore four' — excluding the trainee. For from the non-trainee a trainee [mind] does not arise. How does it not arise at the time of decline? Because it is separated by the arising of affliction, and because decline is only for one who has emerged.

body.text: (II.72, 73) prāyogikaṃ copapattilābhikaṃ ceti. prāyogikaṃ yat prayogāl labhyate. śrutacintābhāvanāmayaṃ triṣu dhātuṣu yathāsaṃbhavaṃ. upapattilābhikaṃ kāmarūpadhātvor antarābhavapratisaṃdhikṣaṇe prathamato yasya prāptir utpadyate. ārūpyadhātau copapattibhave yasya prāptir utpadyate. vipākajam airyāpathikaṃ śailpasthānikaṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ ceti. hetukarmabhedād ayaṃ bhedaḥ. vipākahetor jātaṃ vipākajaṃ. īryāpatheṣu śayanāsanasthiticaṃkramaṇeṣu bhavaṃ airyāpathikaṃ. śilpasthāneṣu bhavaṃ śailpasthānikaṃ. nirmāṇe cittaṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ. nirmite nirmāṇe vā bhavaṃ nairmitaṃ nairmāṇikam iti vā. tad evocyate. punar viṃśatir bhavantīti. katham ity āha. ṣoḍhā kuśalam anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ ca saptadhā bhittveti. triṣu dhātuṣu prāyogikopapattipratilaṃbhikabhedena [Tib. 231b] kuśalaṃ ṣoḍhā bhittvā. kāmarūpadhātvoś cānivṛtāvyākṛte saptadhā bhittvā. kāmadhātau vipākajairyāpathikaśailpasthānikanairmāṇikabhedena. rūpadhātau ca vipākajairyāpathikanairmāṇikabhedeneti. tāny etāni trayodaśa śeṣāṇi ca saptābhinnāny eva. tadyathā
body.translated_text: (II.72, 73) 'Practice-born and birth-obtained' — practice-born is that obtained through practice: born of learning, reflection, and cultivation in the three realms as appropriate. Birth-obtained [is that] whose <s>prāpti</s> first arises at the moment of rebirth-connection in the intermediate existence in the desire and form realms, and whose <s>prāpti</s> arises in the existence-state in the formless realm. 'Maturation-born, conduct-related, craft-related, and creation-mind' — this distinction is due to the distinction of causal action. That born from a maturation cause is maturation-born (<s>vipākaja</s>). That occurring in the modes of conduct — lying, sitting, standing, walking — is conduct-related (<s>airyāpathika</s>). That occurring in craft-activities is craft-related (<s>śailpasthānika</s>). Mind in creation is creation-mind (<s>nirmāṇacitta</s>) — or that occurring in what has been created or in creation itself is called 'pertaining to what is created' or 'pertaining to creation.' That itself is stated. 'Again, there are twenty' — how? He says: 'dividing the wholesome sixfold and the uncovered-indeterminate sevenfold.' In the three realms, dividing the wholesome sixfold [Tib. 231b] by the distinction of practice-born and birth-obtained. And dividing the uncovered-indeterminate in the desire and form realms sevenfold: in the desire realm by the distinction of maturation-born, conduct-related, craft-related, and creation-related; in the form realm by the distinction of maturation-born, conduct-related, and creation-related. These are thirteen; and the remaining seven are undivided — namely

body.text: kāmāvacaram akuśalaṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ ca. rūpāvacaraṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtam eva ārūpyāvacaraṃ nivṛtāvykṛtam anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ ca. śaikṣam aśaikṣaṃ ceti viṃśati cittāni bhavaṃti. īryāpathādyadhāvād iti. īryāpathaśilpasthānanirmāṇābhāvāt. etāni trīṇy ārūpyadhātau na saṃti. ālambanabhūtasya rūpasyābhāvāt. rūpagandharasaspraṣṭavyāny eṣām ālambanam iti. tatra śayyāsanarūpādayaḥ svaśarīrāvayavarūpādayaś cairyāpathikasyālambanaṃ. śailpasthānikasya śilpasthānarūpādayaḥ nairmāṇikasya nirmāṇarūpādayaḥ. śailpasthānikasya tu śabdo 'pīti. tuśabdo viśeṣaṇe apiśabdena rūpādayaḥ. śabdo 'py asyālambanaṃ. śilpopadeśaśabdam ālambya manovijñānena śilpaṃ śikṣate iti. vipākajasyāvacanāt sarve 'pi rūpādaya ālambanam ity avagantavyaṃ. manovijñānāny eveti. manovijñānasvabhāvāny airyāpathikādīni trīṇi. vikalpābhisaṃskaraṇe [Tib. 232a] pravṛttatvāt. vipākajam avacanāt ṣaḍvijñānasvabhāvam iti jñāpitaṃ bhavati. paṃca tu vijñānakāyam airyāpathikaśailpasthānikayoḥ prāyogikā iti. tatprayogāvasthāyāṃ bhavatvāt prāyogikāḥ. yasmāt te dṛṣṭvā yāvat spṛsṭvotpadyaṃta iti. vipākasya prayogo nāsti. karmasāmarthyena svarasavāhitvāt.
body.translated_text: desire-realm unwholesome and covered-indeterminate; form-realm covered-indeterminate only; formless-realm covered-indeterminate and uncovered-indeterminate; and trainee and non-trainee — [making] twenty minds. 'Because of the absence of conduct and the like' — because of the absence of conduct, craft, and creation. These three do not exist in the formless realm, because of the absence of form which would serve as object. 'Form, odor, taste, and tangibles are their objects' — therein, bed-form and the like, and body-part-form and the like are the object of the conduct-related [mind]. Of the craft-related, craft-related forms and the like. Of the creation-related, creation-forms and the like. 'But for the craft-related, sound also' — the word 'but' is qualifying; the word 'also' [adds to] forms, etc. Sound too is its object — [because] relying on the sound of craft-instruction, one learns the craft through mental consciousness. Because [the text] does not specify for the maturation-born, it should be understood that all forms, etc. are [its] objects. 'They are mental consciousnesses only' — the three [types] beginning with conduct-related are of the nature of mental consciousness, [Tib. 232a] because they operate through conceptual elaboration. Because [the text] does not specify for the maturation-born, it is indicated that [maturation-born mind] has the nature of the six consciousnesses. 'But the five consciousness-groups are preparatory for the conduct-related and craft-related' — they are preparatory because they occur in the preparatory stage of those [activities]. Because those arise after seeing, and so on up to touching. There is no preparation for maturation — because it flows spontaneously by the power of <s>karma</s>.

body.text: airyāpathikābhinirhṛtam iti vistaraḥ. airyāpathikena manovijñānenābhinirhṛtam utpāditaṃ manovijñānam asti dvādaśāyatanālambanaṃ. cakṣurāyatanālambanaṃ yāvad dharmāyatanālaṃbanam anivṛtāvyākṛtasvabhāvam ity apare. tad evaṃ pradarśayaṃti. anyad apy anivṛtāvyākṛtam asti yad airyāpathikādiṣu nāntarbhavatīti. ittham eva ca pratipattavyaṃ. anyathā hi yad vakṣyati
body.translated_text: 'Produced by the conduct-related [mind]' — thus the elaboration. There exists a mind produced — generated — by a conduct-related mental consciousness that has the twelve sense-bases as objects, from the eye sense-base up to the <s>dharma</s> sense-base as object, having the nature of uncovered-indeterminate — according to others. They thus demonstrate: there is another uncovered-indeterminate [mind] that is not included among the conduct-related and the others. And it should be understood precisely thus. For otherwise, what will be stated:

children.text:
kāyākṣiśrotravijñānaṃ vijñaptyutthāpakaṃ ca yat
dvitīyādau tad ādyāptam akliṣṭāvyākṛtaṃ ca tat.
svabhūmikena nirmāṇaṃ bhāṣaṇaṃ tv adhareṇa cety
children.translated_text:
'Body-, eye-, and ear-consciousness, and that which initiates bodily action —
that, obtained in the first [dhyāna], belongs to the second [dhyāna] onward, and it is unafflicted-indeterminate.
Creation is by [a mind] of one's own ground, but speech is also by a lower [ground mind]' —

body.text: tāni vijñānāni eṣāṃ caturṇāṃ katamena saṃgṛhītāni. na tāvad vipākajāni. ūrdhvopapannānām adharabhūmikavipākāsaṃbhavāt. nairyāpathikādīni. īryāpathādyabhāvāt. ajñānādivāsanācittaṃ ca kva praveśayitavyaṃ bhadantānantavarmaṇā 'pi vibhāṣāvyākhyāna uktam. etac catuṣṭayavyatiriktāny avyākṛtāni vijñānāni [Tib. 232b] santīti. sāvaśeṣam etad bhāṣyam ity avagantavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: By which of these four [categories] are those consciousnesses included? They are not maturation-born — because, for those born in higher [realms], lower-ground maturation is impossible. Nor are they conduct-related, etc. — because of the absence of conduct-modes and the like. And the mind of habitual traces of ignorance and the like — where should it be classified? The venerable <s>Anantavarman</s> also stated in the <s>Vibhāṣā</s> commentary: 'there are indeterminate consciousnesses [Tib. 232b] beyond this fourfold [classification].' This commentary should be understood as incomplete.

body.text: anyatrābhijñāphalād iti. kāmāvacaraṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ rūpāvacaraprāyogikānantaram evotpadyate. na kāmāvacaraprāyogikānantaraṃ. rūpāvacaraṃ prāyogikaṃ śaikṣam aśaikṣaṃ ceti. samāpattikāle. svebhyaḥ kuśalakliṣṭebhya iti. svābhyāṃ kuśalābhyāṃ kliṣṭābhyāṃ ca. prayogakāle kliṣṭāsadbhāvāt. kleśaparikhinnasya ca prāyogikotpatteḥ. nānivṛtāvyākṛtebhyaḥ durbalānabhisaṃskāritvāt. rūpāvacarābhyāṃ prāyogikakliṣṭābhyām iti. prāyogikāt kliṣṭāt. śaikṣāśaikṣābhyāṃ
body.translated_text: 'Except the fruit of <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge)' — the desire-realm creation-mind arises only immediately after a form-realm practice-born [mind], not immediately after a desire-realm practice-born [mind]. 'Form-realm practice-born, trainee, and non-trainee [minds]' — at the time of attainment. 'From their own wholesome and afflicted [minds]' — from their own two wholesome and two afflicted [minds]; because at the time of practice, the afflicted [state] does not exist; and because for one wearied by afflictions, a practice-born [mind] arises. 'Not from the uncovered-indeterminate' — because of being weak and lacking intentional construction. 'From the form-realm practice-born and afflicted' — from the practice-born and from the afflicted. 'From the trainee and non-trainee'

body.text:
ca vyutthānakāle. kliṣṭāt kliṣṭasamādhyutpīḍitasya. rūpārūpyāvacare ca kliṣṭe iti. pratisaṃdhikāle. saṃbhavati hy upapattipratilaṃbhikacittasya maraṇaṃ. pūrvavad iti. anyatrābhijñāphalād ity arthaḥ. tad dhi rūpāvacaraprāyogikānantaram evety uktaṃ. rūpāvacarābhyāṃ ceti vistareṇa pūrvavad vyākhyānaṃ. akuśalanivṛtāvyākṛtānantaram iti. akuśalānantaraṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtānantaraṃ ceti vibhaktavyaṃ. tulyatvād dhi tad yugapadvacanaṃ. rūpāvacarebhyaś caturbhyaḥ. anyatra prāyogikābhijñāphalābhyām iti. pratisaṃdhikāle. prāyogike 'bhijñāphale ca sthitasya nāsti maraṇam. atas tābhyāṃ tat kliṣṭadvayaṃ notpadyate. śeṣeṣu tu sthitasyāsti maraṇaṃ. [Tib. 233a] atas tebhyas tat kliṣṭadvayam utpadyate. pratisaṃdhikāle. evam anyatrāpy anyatra prāyogikād iti vyākhyeyaṃ. ṣaḍ anyatra prāyogikābhijñāphalābhyām iti. durbalānabhisaṃskārakatvāt. anayor anantaraṃ prāyogikaṃ notpadyate. rūpāvacaraprāyogikānantarotpatteś ca na tābhyām abhijñāphalotpattiḥ. rūpārūpyāvacare ca kliṣṭe iti. pratisaṃdhikāle. śailpasthānikānantaraṃ ṣaḍ iti. tatrasthasya maraṇāsaṃbhavāt airyāpathikavipākajavad iha rūpārūpyāvacarakliṣṭayor asaṃbhavaḥ. svaṃ cābhijñāphalam eveti. pravāhakāle. rūpāvacaraṃ ca prāyogikam iti. tadvyutthāne. na hy apraviśya dhyānaṃ abhijñāphalād vyutthānam astīti. tadapy asmād eva dvayād iti. tad abhijñāphalaṃ pravāhe tatpraveśakāle ca. kāmāvacarakuśale iti. vyutthānakāle. asti hi saṃbhava upapattipratilaṃbhikenāpi samāpattivyutthānaṃ paṭutvāt. ato dvayor api kuśalayor grahaṇaṃ. abhijñāphalaṃ ceti. kāmāvacaraṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ. ārūpyāvacaraṃ prāyogikaṃ śaikṣāśaikṣaṃ ca samāpattikāle. anyatrairyāpathikavipākajābhyām iti. tayor durbalānabhisaṃskārikatvāt. prāyogikakliṣṭābhyām [Tib. 233b] iti. vyutthānakliṣṭasamāpattyutpīḍitakālayoḥ. kāmāvacare kliṣṭe iti pratisaṃdhikāle. anyatrābhijñāphalād iti. nirmāṇacittasya prāyogikānantarotpatteḥ. ārūpyāvacaraṃ kliṣtam iti. pratisaṃdhikāle. kuśalakliṣṭānīti. kuśale ca kliṣṭe ca kuśalakliṣṭānīti samāsaḥ. kuśalādharabhūmikāśrayaṇāt kuśale. kliṣṭe tu pratisaṃdhikāle.kāmāvacarebhya iti vistaraḥ. pratisaṃdhikāle. prāyogikaśailpasthānikābhijñāphaleṣu mṛtyur nāstīti na tebhyaḥ. kāmāvacare kliṣṭe iti. pratisaṃdhikāle. ārūpyāvacaram api kliṣṭam asminn eva svaṃ prāyogikaṃ ato notpadyate. airyāpathikasya durbalānabhisaṃskāritvena prayogānarhatvāt. evaṃ vipākajam iti. yathairyāpathikam uktaṃ. tathedaṃ vipākajānantaraṃ sapta yāvad anyatrābhijñāphalād iti.
tāv eva granthārthau. abhijñāphalānantaraṃ dve sve iti. vyutthāne pravāhe ca. tad apy ābhyām eveti. praveśe pravāhe ca.
body.translated_text: ...and at the time of emergence. From the afflicted — for one pressed by afflicted concentration. 'And the afflicted of the Form and Formless Realms' — at the time of rebirth-linking (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>). For it is possible for the birth-obtaining mind to die. 'As before' — meaning except for the fruit of superknowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>). For that was said to arise only immediately after the preparatory (<s>prāyogika</s>) [mind] of the Form Realm. 'And from the two of the Form Realm' — the explanation is in detail as before. 'After unwholesome and obstructed-indeterminate' — this should be analyzed as: after unwholesome, and after obstructed-indeterminate. For they are mentioned together due to being equal [in this respect]. 'From the four of the Form Realm, except the preparatory and the fruit of superknowledge' — at the time of rebirth-linking. For one abiding in the preparatory or the fruit of superknowledge, there is no death; therefore from those two, that pair of afflicted [minds] does not arise. But for one abiding in the rest, death exists; therefore from those, that pair of afflicted [minds] arises — at the time of rebirth-linking. Similarly, 'except the preparatory' elsewhere should be explained thus. 'Six, except the preparatory and the fruit of superknowledge' — because of being weak and non-volitional. After these two, the preparatory does not arise. And since the fruit of superknowledge arises immediately after the Form Realm preparatory, it does not arise from those two. 'And the afflicted of the Form and Formless Realms' — at the time of rebirth-linking. 'After the craft-based (<s>śailpasthānika</s>), six' — since death is impossible for one in that state, just as with the path-of-deportment and maturation-born [minds], here too the afflicted of the Form and Formless Realms is impossible. 'And its own fruit of superknowledge only' — during the continuity period. 'And the preparatory of the Form Realm' — at emergence from that. For without entering <s>dhyāna</s>, there is no emergence from the fruit of superknowledge. 'That too from this very pair' — that fruit of superknowledge, during the continuity and at the time of entering it. 'The wholesome of the Desire Realm' — at the time of emergence. For it is possible that emergence from attainment may occur even with the birth-obtaining [mind], due to its acuity. Therefore both types of wholesome are included. 'And the fruit of superknowledge' — the Desire Realm creation-mind (<s>nirmāṇacitta</s>). 'The preparatory of the Formless Realm, and the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>)' — at the time of attainment. 'Except the path-of-deportment and maturation-born' — because of their being weak and non-volitional. 'From the preparatory and afflicted' — at the times of emergence and of being pressed by afflicted concentration. 'The afflicted of the Desire Realm' — at the time of rebirth-linking. 'Except the fruit of superknowledge' — because the creation-mind arises immediately after the preparatory. 'The afflicted of the Formless Realm' — at the time of rebirth-linking. 'Wholesome and afflicted' — wholesome and afflicted together form a compound. In the wholesome, [it occurs] due to resorting to a lower-level basis. In the afflicted, at the time of rebirth-linking. 'From those of the Desire Realm' — and so forth in detail — at the time of rebirth-linking. Death does not occur while in the preparatory, craft-based, or fruit of superknowledge [states], so not from those. 'The afflicted of the Desire Realm' — at the time of rebirth-linking. 'The afflicted of the Formless Realm also — its own preparatory does not arise from this.' Since the path-of-deportment [mind] is too weak and non-volitional to serve as preparation. 'Similarly for the maturation-born' — as stated for the path-of-deportment mind. Similarly, this should be said: after the maturation-born, seven [minds], up to 'except the fruit of superknowledge.' These are the two meanings of the text. 'After the fruit of superknowledge, two — its own' — at emergence and during continuity. 'That too from these two only' — at entry and during continuity.

body.text: rūpāvacaraṃ prāyogikam iti. vyutthānakāle. evaṃ śaikṣam aśaikṣaṃ [Tib. 234a] svāni catvārīti. kuśalaṃ bhavatīti sphuṭaṃ. kliṣṭaṃ āsvādanākāle. 'nivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ tu vyutthānakāle. rūpāvacarāt prāyogikād iti. samāpattikāle. anyatra vipākajād iti. durbalānabhisaṃskāravāhitvād iti kāraṇaṃ vakṣyate. śaikṣāśaikṣābhyāṃ ceti. samāpattikāle. adharadhātukāni ca kliṣṭānīti. rūpāvacarakāmāvacarāṇi pratisaṃdhikāle. prāyogikakliṣṭe iti. prāyogikaṃ kliṣṭasamādhyutpīḍanāt. kliṣtaṃ pratisaṃdhikāle. kāmāvacare 'pi kliṣṭe pratisaṃdhikāla eva. kāmāvacararūpāvacarebhya iti vistaraḥ. taccittasthamaraṇasaṃbhavāt. anyatra prāyogikād iti. vipākajānantaraṃ prāyogikānutpatteḥ. adharāṇi trīṇi kliṣṭānīti. dvidhātukāni pratisaṃdhikāle. kāmāvacaram utpattilābhikam iti. paṭutvād etac chaikṣād vyutthānacittaṃ saṃbhavati. paṭutvād iti kāraṇaṃ vakṣyati. na tu tathā rūpārūpyāvacare upapattilābhike paṭunī iti na te saṃbhavataḥ. śaikṣaṃ pravāhe aśaikṣaṃ ca vajropamānantaraṃ. śaikṣam ekaṃ hitveti. aśaikṣāc chaikṣaṃ notpadyate. tasmād aśaikṣānaṃtaraṃ paṃca. na tu ṣaṭ yathā śaikṣāt. tāni ca paṃca śaikṣavad vaktavyāni [Tib. 234b].
body.translated_text: 'The preparatory of the Form Realm' — at the time of emergence. 'Similarly, the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), the non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), and its own four' — that it is wholesome is clear. Afflicted — at the time of savoring. Obstructed-indeterminate — at the time of emergence. 'From the Form Realm preparatory' — at the time of attainment. 'Except the maturation-born' — the reason will be stated: because of bearing weak non-volitional [activity]. 'From the learner and non-learner' — at the time of attainment. 'And the lower-realm afflicted' — those of the Form and Desire Realms, at the time of rebirth-linking. 'The preparatory and afflicted' — the preparatory, from being pressed by afflicted concentration; the afflicted, at the time of rebirth-linking. The afflicted of the Desire Realm also — only at the time of rebirth-linking. 'From those of the Desire and Form Realms' — and so forth in detail — because death is possible for one in those mental states. 'Except the preparatory' — because the preparatory does not arise immediately after the maturation-born. 'Three lower afflicted' — those of the two realms, at the time of rebirth-linking. 'The birth-obtaining [mind] of the Desire Realm' — due to its acuity, this emergence-mind from the learner [and non-learner states] is possible. 'Due to acuity' — the reason will be stated. But the birth-obtaining [minds] of the Form and Formless Realms are not as acute, so they are not possible. 'The learner — during the continuity; and the non-learner — immediately after the diamond-like [concentration].' 'Except one learner' — from the non-learner, the learner does not arise. Therefore after the non-learner, five [minds]; not six as from the learner. And those five should be stated as for the learner.

body.text: atra viṃśaticittānāṃ samanantarapratyayasya asūtritasya sūtrarūpāḥ saṃgrahaślokāḥ.
body.translated_text: Here, summary verses in sūtra form for the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) of the twenty [types of] mind, which was not stated in sūtra form:

children.text:
prāyogikāc chubhāt kāme daśāṣṭabhyas tad anyathaḥ
śubhān navaikādaśatas tat sapta kliṣṭataḥ pṛthak
caturdaśabhyaś te 'ṣṭāv airyāpathikavipākajāt

nairmitād dve dvayoś caitad rūpe prāyogikāc chubāt
dvādaśaitat tu daśataḥ śubhād aṣṭāv ayatnajāt
tat paṃcabhyo nava kliṣṭāt tad ekādaśataḥ punaḥ
vipākajairyāpathikāt sapta tat paṃcato dvayaṃ
dve abhijñāphalāc cittād dvābhyām eva tathaiva tat
ārūpye yātnikāt sapta kuśalāt ṣaḍbhya eva tat
ayātnikāc chubhāt sapta caturbhyas tat punaḥ smṛtaṃ
kliṣṭād aṣṭau daśabhyas tat ṣaṭ cittāni vipākajāt
caturbhyas tat tu ṣaṭ śaikṣāc caturbhyaḥ punar eva tat.
aśaikṣāt paṃca tad api paṃcabhyaḥ samanaṃtaraṃ.

body.text: īryāpathaśilpābhisaṃskaraṇapravṛttatvāt. na punar ebhyaḥ prāyogikam utpadyata ity adhikṛtaṃ. ato 'saṃbhavād airyāpathikaśailpasthānikānantaraṃ
body.translated_text: Because [those minds] operate for the purpose of activities such as deportment (<s>īryāpatha</s>) and craft (<s>śilpa</s>). The topic under discussion is that the preparatory does not arise from these. Therefore, because of impossibility, after the path-of-deportment and craft-based [minds] —

body.text: prāyogikaṃ notpadyate. tad anyābhisaṃskaraṇapravṛttatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. yasmād airyāpathikam īryāpathābhisaṃskaraṇe pravṛttaṃ. gamanādyākāratvāt. śailpasthānikaṃ ca ślipābhisaṃskaraṇe pravṛttam. idaṃ evaṃ karomīdam evaṃ karomītīty evamākārapravṛttatvāt. durbalānabhisaṃskāravāhitvāc ca vipākajānantaraṃ prāyogikaṃ notpadyate.
