[Tib. 235a] tad dhi vipākajam avyākṛtatvād durbalaṃ. pūrvakarmākṣepāt. ayatnena ca pravṛtter anabhisaṃkāravāhīti. atha vā īryāpathaśilpābhisaṃskaraṇapravṛttatvāt. airyāpathikaśailpasthānikānantaraṃ na prāyogikam utpadyate. durbalānabhisaṃskāravāhitvāc ca airyāpathikaśailpasthānikavipākajānantaraṃ prāyogikaṃ notpadyate. sarveṣām avyākṛtatvena durbalatvāt. anabhisaṃskāravāhitvāc ca vipākajasyaivaikasya airyāpathikaśailpasthānikayor api vā prāyogikābhisaṃskārābhāvāt. anyavyāpāraparatvamātrād dhi tayor abhisaṃskaraṇapravṛttatvam uktaṃ. atha vāyam evāsya vākyasyābhisaṃbandhaḥ. īryāpathaśilpābhisaṃskaraṇapravṛttatvāt. durbalānabhisaṃskāravāhitvāc caitāni vipākajairyāpathikaśailpasthānikāni na prayogikānukūlāni. ato na tadanantaraṃ prāyogikam utpadyata iti saṃbandhanīyaṃ. niṣkramaṇacittaṃ tu anabhisaṃskāravāhīti. prāyogikacittapravāhād yad anyac cittaṃ. tan niṣkramaṇacittaṃ. tena hy asau yogī tataḥ pravāhān niṣkrāmati tadavatāratvāt. niṣkramaṇacittam anbhisaṃskāravāhi anābhogavāhīti yukto 'sya niṣkramaṇacittasya vipākajādīnām anyatamasvabhāvasya [Tib. 235b] prāyogikacittānantaram utpādaḥ. evaṃ tarhīti. yadi na prāyogikānukūlānīti vipākajādibhyo 'nantaraṃ prāyogikaṃ notpadyate. evaṃ tarhi kliṣṭebhyo 'pi prāyogikaṃ notpadyate viguṇatvāt. viguṇo hi kliṣṭo dharmaḥ kuśalasya nānukūla ity arthaḥ tadvirodhitvāt. tathāpīti vistaraḥ. yady api tad viguṇaṃ tathāpi kleśasamudācāraparikhinnasya yoginaḥ tatparijñānāt kleśasamudācāraparijñānād yuktaḥ prāyogikasaṃmukhībhāvaḥ. tatparijñānam eva hi prāyogikaṃ cittam iti. paṭutvād iti. kāmāvacaram utpattipratilaṃbhikaṃ paṭu tac chaikṣādibhyo vyutthānacittaṃ saṃbhavati. ata eva ca kliṣṭasamādhyutpīḍitasya tadāśrayaṇaṃ bhavati. anabhisaṃskāravāhitvāt tu tasya tasmāc chaikṣādīni notpadyante. rūpāvacaraṃ tūpapattipratilaṃbhikaṃ na kāmāvacaravat paṭu. tasmāt kliṣṭasamādhyutpīḍitasya tadāśrayaṇaṃ na bhavati. prāyogikam evāśrīyate. anyonyānantaraṃ cittānām utpādaḥ.
body.translated_text: — the preparatory does not arise, because they operate for a different kind of volitional activity — this is the intent. Since the path-of-deportment [mind] operates in the volitional activity of deportment, having the aspect of walking and the like; and the craft-based [mind] operates in the volitional activity of craft, operating with aspects such as 'I do this thus, I do that thus.' And after the maturation-born, the preparatory does not arise, because of bearing weak non-volitional [activity]. For that maturation-born [mind] is weak due to being indeterminate, and because it is projected by prior action, and because it operates without effort, it bears non-volitional [activity]. Alternatively: because of operating for the purpose of deportment and craft activities, after the path-of-deportment and craft-based [minds], the preparatory does not arise. And because of bearing weak non-volitional [activity], after the path-of-deportment, craft-based, and maturation-born [minds], the preparatory does not arise — because all are weak due to being indeterminate. And due to being non-volitional — this applies to the maturation-born alone, or also to the path-of-deportment and craft-based [minds], because of the absence of preparatory volitional formation. For their operating for different activities was stated merely due to being occupied with other tasks. Or this is the connection of this sentence: because of operating for the purpose of deportment and craft activities, and because of bearing weak non-volitional [activity], these maturation-born, path-of-deportment, and craft-based [minds] are not favorable to the preparatory. Therefore, immediately after them, the preparatory does not arise — this is how it should be connected. 'But the exit-mind is non-volitional' — whatever mind other than the preparatory mind-stream, that is the exit-mind. For by that, the yogin exits from that [preparatory] stream, it being the entry into that. The exit-mind bears non-volitional [activity], bears non-attention — therefore the arising of this exit-mind, whose nature is one of the maturation-born and the like, immediately after the preparatory mind, is fitting. 'If so, then' — if the preparatory does not arise immediately after the maturation-born and the like because they are not favorable to it, then the preparatory should also not arise after the afflicted, since it is deficient. For an afflicted <s>dharma</s> is deficient and not favorable to the wholesome — this is the meaning — being opposed to it. 'Even so' — and so forth in detail. Even though that is deficient, nonetheless, because a yogin wearied by the occurrence of affliction comprehends it — comprehends the occurrence of affliction — the turning toward the preparatory is fitting. For that very comprehension is the preparatory mind. 'Due to acuity' — the birth-obtaining [mind] of the Desire Realm is acute; therefore it is possible as the emergence-mind from the learner and the like. And for this very reason, one pressed by afflicted concentration resorts to it. But because of bearing non-volitional [activity], the learner and the like do not arise from it. However, the birth-obtaining [mind] of the Form Realm is not as acute as that of the Desire Realm; therefore one pressed by afflicted concentration does not resort to it — only the preparatory is resorted to. The arising of minds immediately after one another.

body.text: tāni ca manaskāravaśād utpadyaṃta iti ato manaskāropakṣepaḥ. trayo manaskārā iti vistaraḥ. svalakṣaṇasya manasikaraṇaṃ svalakṣaṇamanaskāraḥ. tadyathā rūpaṇālakṣaṇaṃ rūpam ity evamādi. ādiśabdenānubhavanalaksaṇā vedaneti evamādi.[Tib. 236a] anityatvādimanasikaraṇaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇamanaskāraḥ
body.translated_text: And since those [minds] arise through the force of attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), therefore the topic of attention is introduced. 'Three [types of] attention' — and so forth in detail. Attention to own-characteristics is <s>svalakṣaṇamanaskāra</s> (attention to particular characteristics). For example: 'Form has the characteristic of being molded (<s>rūpaṇa</s>),' and so on. The word 'and so on' includes: 'Feeling has the characteristic of experiencing,' and so on. Attention to impermanence and the like is <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇamanaskāra</s> (attention to general characteristics) —

body.text: ṣoḍaśākārasaṃprayuktaḥ. anityato yāvan nairyāṇikata iti. adhimuktyā na bhūtārthe manasikaraṇaṃ adhimuktimanaskāraḥ. aśubhāyāṃ yāvat kṛtsnāyatanādiṣu. ādiśabdena ṛddhyādīnām abhinirhāre lagutvādyadhimokṣo gṛhyate. tadyathā maharddhiko mahānubhāvaḥ parīttāṃ pṛthivīsaṃjñām apy adhitiṣṭhati. apramāṇām api saṃjñāṃ. sa ākāṃkṣan pṛthivīṃ calayatīti vistaraḥ. aśubhayā sahagataṃ sambaddhaṃ aśubhāsahagataṃ. etad uktaṃ bhavati. aśubhāmanaskārānantaraṃ smṛtisaṃbodhyaṃgaṃ bhāvayati janayati utpādayatīti. samṛtisaṃbodhyaṃgaṃ hy āryamārga iti asty adhimuktimanaskārānantaraṃ āryamārgotpāda iti darśayati. āha. yadi sāmānyamanaskārānāntaram eva nādhimuktimanaskārānaṃtaram āryamārgaṃ saṃmukhīkaroti. idaṃ kathaṃ nīyate. aśubhāsahagataṃ smṛtisaṃbodhyaṃgaṃ bhāvayatīti. ata idam ucyate. aśubhayā tu cittaṃ damayitveti vistaraḥ. prāyogāvasthāyām aśubhayā cittaṃ damayitvā yāvad avasāne sāmānyamanaskārānantaram āryamārgaṃ saṃmukhīkartoi. ato na sūtravirodha iti. āryamārgānantaram apīti vistaraḥ. na kevalaṃ sāmānyamanaskārānantaraṃ āryamārgaṃ saṃmukhīkaroti. [Tib. 236b] āryamārgānantaram api sāmānyamanaskāram eva saṃmukhīkarotīty apare. syāt tāvad iti vistaraḥ. anāyamyādīti. ādiśabdenānāgamyaprathamadhyānadhyānāntaratribhūmisaṃniśrayeṇa niyāmāvakrāntau tanmārgānantaraṃ trimārgānantaraṃ kāmāvacaraṃ sāmānyamanaskāraṃ śrutamayaṃ cintāmayaṃ vā saṃmukhīkuryāt saṃnikṛṣṭatvāt. atha dvitīyādidhyānasaṃniśrayeṇa dvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānasaṃniśrayeṇa niyāmāvakrāntau katham āryamārgānantaraṃ kathaṃ sāmānyamanaskāraṃ saṃmukhīkaroti. na hi kāmāvacaraḥ śakyaḥ saṃmukhīkartum iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. kasmāt. prathamadhyānavyavahitatvenātiviprakṛṣṭatvāt. brūyās tvaṃ dvitīyādidhyānabhūmikam eva saṃmukhīkarotīti. ata āha. na ca tadbhūmikaḥ pratilabdho 'nyatra nirvedhabhāgīyād iti. dvitīyadhyānādibhūmiko 'nāgamyādibhūmiko vānāsravo mārgo 'nyatra nirvedhabhāgīyān na pratilabdha āsīt. anākārapatitas tu laukiko mārgaḥ pratilabdha āsīt. na tu saḥ. tasmād āryasya vyutthānārthaṃ rocate. nirvedhabhāgīyaṃ tarhi sāmānyamanaskāraṃ saṃmukhīkariṣyatīti. ata āha. na cāryo nirvedhabhāgīyam iti vistaraḥ. kim artham iti cet. ata āha. na hi prāptaphalasya tatprayogasaṃmukhībhāvo yukta iti. prayogasya kṛtārthatvān [Tib. 237a] nihīnatvāc ca nirvedhabhāgīyāni cāryamārgasya prayoga iti. anyo 'py asya tajjātīya iti. yaḥ satyālambanatvān nirvedhabhāgīyajātīyaḥ sāmānyamanaskāro bhāvanāṃ gacchati. anāsravamārgotpattikāle prāpyate ity arthaḥ. kathaṃ. śāntaṃ nirvāṇam iti sāmānyamanaskāraḥ sarvanirvāṇālambanatvāt.
body.translated_text: associated with the sixteen aspects — from impermanence up to the aspect of being an escape (<s>nairyāṇika</s>). '<s>Adhimuktimanaskāra</s>' (resolute attention) is mental attention directed not to the real object but through conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>) — in the [meditation on the] impure (<s>aśubhā</s>), up to the <s>kṛtsnāyatana</s> (totality-bases) and so forth. By the word 'and so forth,' the conviction of lightness and the like in the production of supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>) and so forth is included. For example, one of great supernatural power and great might establishes [even] a limited earth-perception, or an unlimited perception. Desiring [to do so], he makes the earth shake — and so forth in detail. 'Accompanied by the impure' means 'connected with the impure' — the [meditation on the] impure accompanied [by mindfulness]. What has been said is this: immediately after the attention on the impure, one cultivates — generates, produces — the mindfulness-<s>saṃbodhyaṅga</s> (awakening-factor of mindfulness). For the mindfulness-<s>saṃbodhyaṅga</s> is the Noble Path — thus [the text] shows that there is arising of the Noble Path immediately after the <s>adhimuktimanaskāra</s>. He says: 'If the Noble Path is brought about only immediately after the <s>sāmānyamanaskāra</s> (general attention), not immediately after the <s>adhimuktimanaskāra</s> — how is this [sūtra passage] interpreted: "one cultivates the mindfulness-<s>saṃbodhyaṅga</s> accompanied by the impure"?' Therefore this is said: 'But having tamed the mind with the impure [meditation]' — and so forth in detail. At the preparatory stage, having tamed the mind with the impure [meditation], ultimately, at the end, one brings about the Noble Path immediately after the <s>sāmānyamanaskāra</s>. Therefore there is no contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s>. 'Even after the Noble Path' — and so forth in detail. Not only does one bring about the Noble Path immediately after the <s>sāmānyamanaskāra</s>; [Tib. 236b] immediately after the Noble Path too, one brings about precisely the <s>sāmānyamanaskāra</s> — [so say] others. 'There may be [the following case]' — and so forth in detail. 'Based on <s>Anāgamya</s> and so forth' — by the word 'and so forth,' [this means:] based on the three levels — <s>Anāgamya</s>, first <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>dhyānāntara</s> — when entering the fixed course [of certainty], immediately after that path — immediately after the three paths — one would bring about a desire-realm <s>sāmānyamanaskāra</s>, whether derived from learning or from reflection, because of proximity. But when entering the fixed course based on the second and further <s>dhyānas</s> — the second, third, or fourth <s>dhyāna</s> — how, immediately after the Noble Path, does one bring about the <s>sāmānyamanaskāra</s>? For a desire-realm [attention] cannot be brought about — this is the sentence-completion. Why? Because of excessive remoteness, being separated by the first <s>dhyāna</s>. You might say: 'One brings about precisely [an attention] belonging to the second and further <s>dhyāna</s> levels.' Therefore he says: 'And no [attention] belonging to that level has been obtained, apart from the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>).' A non-outflow path belonging to the second <s>dhyāna</s> and higher levels, or to the <s>Anāgamya</s> and other levels, had not been obtained apart from the aids to penetration. But a mundane path not having fallen into the [sixteen] aspects had been obtained — but not that [mundane path, as an option here]. Therefore, for a Noble One [who wishes to] emerge [from absorption], [the question of] which [attention] is preferred [arises]. 'Then [the Noble One] will bring about the aids to penetration, the <s>sāmānyamanaskāra</s>.' Therefore he says: 'And a Noble One [does not return to] the aids to penetration' — and so forth in detail. Why? Therefore he says: 'For it is not fitting for one who has attained the fruit to bring about the preparatory [practice] for that [fruit].' Because of the preparatory [practice] having served its purpose, [Tib. 237a] and because of its inferiority — and because the aids to penetration are the preparation for the Noble Path. 'Another [attention] of the same type' — that <s>sāmānyamanaskāra</s> which, because of having truths as its object, belongs to the same type as the aids to penetration — it reaches cultivation [i.e., is developed]. It is obtained at the time of arising of the non-outflow path — this is the meaning. How? 'Peaceful is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>' — the <s>sāmānyamanaskāra</s>, because of having all [forms of] <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as its object.

body.text: tat saṃmukhīkariṣyatīti. sarvasaṃskārā anityā iti vā sarvadharmā anātmāna iti vā śāntaṃ nirvāṇam iti vāryamārgānantaraṃ saṃmukhīkariṣyatīti. tad etan na varṇayanti. kasmāt eṣāṃ tajjātīyānāṃ sāmānyamanaskārāṇāṃ nirvedhabhāgīyapratibaddhabhāvanatvāt. na kilaiṣām anāsravamārgapratibaddhābhāveneti. anāgamyaṃ niśrityeti vistaraḥ. tadbhūmikam iti. anāgamyabhūmikaṃ. tadbhūmikaṃ bhāvāgrikaṃ veti. ākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmikaṃ bhāvāgrikaṃ vā yadi bhavāgropapanno bhavati. śeṣāsu bhūmiṣu svabhūmikam eva vyutthānacittaṃ. nānyabhūmikaṃ. anyabhūmikasya prayogasādhyatvāt. svabhūmikam anabhisaṃskāreṇa bhavatīti. prayogapratibaddhatvād iti. kasya. āryamārgasya. mārgānantaraṃ tūpapattipratilaṃbhikasyāpi kāmāvacarasya saṃmukhībhāva ity adhikṛtaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'That [attention] will be brought about.' Either 'all formations are impermanent,' or 'all <s>dharmas</s> are selfless,' or 'peaceful is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>' — [this sāmānyamanaskāra] will be brought about immediately after the Noble Path. But they do not approve of this. Why? Because these <s>sāmānyamanaskāras</s> of the same type [as the aids to penetration] are cultivated in dependence on the aids to penetration. They are not [cultivated] in dependence on the arising of the non-outflow path. 'Based on <s>Anāgamya</s>' — and so forth in detail. 'Belonging to that level' — belonging to the <s>Anāgamya</s> level. 'Or belonging to that level — the peak of existence' — belonging to the <s>Ākiṃcanyāyatana</s> level, or the peak of existence, if one is reborn at the peak of existence. In the remaining levels, the emergence-mind is only of one's own level — not of another level. Because [attention of] another level must be accomplished through effort. [Attention of] one's own level occurs without deliberate effort. 'Because of being bound to the preparatory [practice]' — of what? Of the Noble Path. But immediately after the path, even the emergence-mind of a desire-realm being obtained through rebirth [can occur] — this is the subject.

children.text: kliṣṭe tridhātuke lābhaḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ dvayor
children.translated_text: 'In the defiled [mind] of the three realms, [there is] acquisition of six, six, [and] two' —

body.text: iti. yathāsaṃkhyena [Tib. 237b] nirdeśaḥ. kāmāvacare kliṣte ṣaṇṇāṃ cittānāṃ lābhaḥ. pratilaṃbha ity arthaḥ. rūpāvacare ṣaṇṇāṃ. ārūpyāvacare dvayor iti. tenāha. kāmāvacare hi kliṣṭa iti vistaraḥ. tair asamanvāgatasyeti. taiḥ ṣaḍbhiś cittair asamanvāgatasya pudgalasya. kathaṃ. iha kuśalapratisaṃdhānaṃ samyagdṛṣṭyā vā vicikitsayā vā. tad yadi vicikitsayā pratisaṃdhatte. tatra vicikitsāsaṃprayukte kliṣṭe citte saṃmukhībhūte yadā rūpadhātor ārūpyadhātor vā kāmadhātuṃ pratyāgacchati. tadāsyāntarābhavapratisaṃdhicitte 'vaśyakliṣṭe tasya kuśalasya lābhas tenāsamanvāgatasyeti. akuśalanivṛtāvyākṛtayor iti vistaraḥ. akuśalaṃ ca nivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ ca kāmāvacaram eva adhikārād rūpāvacarasya ca nivṛtasya pṛthakpāṭhāt. tayor akuśalanivṛtāvyākṛtayo rūpāvacarasya kliṣtasya. kiṃ. lābha iti prakṛtaṃ. kathaṃ lābha ity āha. dhātupratyāgamanāt parihāṇitaś ceti. yadā rūpadhātor ārūpyadhātor vā kāmadhātuṃ pratyāgacchati. tadāsyāṃtarābhavapratisaṃdhicitte 'vaśyaṃ kliṣṭe 'kuśalanivṛtāvyākṛtayor anyatarasmiṃ saṃmukhībhūte tayor akuśalanivṛtāvyākṛtayor lābho bhavati pūrvavihīnatvāt tenāsamanvāgatasya. parihāṇitaś ca. [Tib. 238a] yadā ca kāmavairāgyāt parihīyate. tadāsya kliṣṭe parihāṇicitte saṃmukhībhūte tayoḥ kliṣṭayor lābhas tenāsamanvāgatasya. rūpāvacarasya ca kliṣṭasya dhātupratyāgamanāt. yadārūpyadhātoḥ kāmadhātuṃ pratyāgacchati. tadāsyāntarābhavapratisaṃdhicitte 'vaśyaṃ kliṣṭe rūpāvacarasya kliṣṭasya pūrvavihīnasya lābho bhavati tenāsamanvāgatasya. parihāṇitaś ca. yadā rūpavairāgyāt parihīyate kāmāvacareṇa cittena. tadāsya vairāgyatyaktasya rūpāvacarasya kliṣṭasya lābho bhavati tenāsamanvāgatasya.
body.translated_text: thus. The instruction is in order: [Tib. 237b] in the defiled [mind] of the desire-realm, there is acquisition of six [types of] mind; 'acquisition' means 'obtaining.' In the form-realm, of six; in the formless realm, of two. Therefore he says: 'In the defiled [mind] of the desire-realm' — and so forth in detail. 'Of one not endowed with those' — of a person not endowed with those six [types of] mind. How? Here, the reconnection [at rebirth] is either with right view or with doubt. If one reconnects with doubt — then, when the defiled mind associated with doubt is actualized, when one returns from the form-realm or the formless realm to the desire-realm, at the time of that intermediate-existence and reconnection mind, which is necessarily defiled — there is the acquisition of that wholesome [mind] for one not endowed with it. 'Of the unwholesome and the covered-indeterminate' — and so forth in detail. The unwholesome and the covered-indeterminate belong to the desire-realm alone, because of the governing topic; and because the covered [indeterminate] of the form-realm is mentioned separately. Of those two — the unwholesome and the covered-indeterminate — the defiled [mind] of the form-realm — what? — [leads to] acquisition. This is the subject. How is there acquisition? He says: 'From the return to the realm, and from decline.' When one returns from the form-realm or the formless realm to the desire-realm, at the time of that intermediate-existence and reconnection mind, which is necessarily defiled, when either the unwholesome or the covered-indeterminate is actualized — there is acquisition of those two, the unwholesome and the covered-indeterminate, for one previously bereft [of them], not endowed with them. And from decline: [Tib. 238a] when one declines from desire-realm dispassion, at the time of the defiled decline-mind being actualized — there is acquisition of those two defiled [types] for one not endowed with them. And of the form-realm defiled [mind], from the return to the realm: when one returns from the formless realm to the desire-realm, at the time of that intermediate-existence and reconnection mind, which is necessarily defiled — there is acquisition of the previously bereft form-realm defiled [mind] for one not endowed with it. And from decline: when one declines from form-realm dispassion through a desire-realm mind, there is acquisition of the form-realm defiled [mind], relinquished through dispassion, for one not endowed with it.

body.text: ārūpyāvacarasya kliṣṭasya parihāṇitaḥ. yadā kāmāvacareṇa cittenārūpyavairāgyāt parihīyate. tadāsyārūpyāvacarasya kliṣṭasya lābho bhavati tenāsamanvāgatasya. śaikṣasya ca parihāṇita ity adhikṛtaṃ. yadā kāmāvacareṇa cittenārhattvāt parihīyate. tadāsya śaikṣacittasya lābho bhavati tenāsmanvāgatasya. evaṃ tāvat kāmāvacare kliṣṭe citte saṃmukhībhūte ṣaṇṇāṃ cittānāṃ lābha uktas tair asamanvāgatasya. rūpāvacare kliṣte citte saṃmukhībhūte ṣaṇṇāṃ lābhaḥ tair asamanvāgatasya. rūpāvacarāṇām iti vistaraḥ. yadārūpyadhāto rūpadhātuṃ pratyāgacchati. tadāsya rūpāvacarāntarābhavapratisaṃdhicitte 'vaśyaṃ kliṣṭe rūpāvacarāṇāṃ trayāṇāṃ kuśalasyopapattipratilaṃbhikasya [Tib. 238b] kliṣṭasyānivṛtāvyākṛtasya ca. nirmāṇacittasyāgrajaprāptisadbhāvāt. kāmāvacarasya cānivṛtāvyākṛtasya nirmāṇacittasyaiva. ārūpyāvacarasya kliṣṭasya śaikṣasya ca lābhaḥ. parihāṇito rūpāvacareṇa cittenārhattvāt parihīyamāṇasya tadasamanvāgatasya. evaṃ rūpāvacare 'pi kliṣṭe ṣaṇṇāṃ lābha uktaḥ. ārūpyāvacare tu kliṣṭe dvayor lābhas tābhyām asamanvāgatasya. parihāṇita ārūpyāvacareṇa cittenārhattvāt parihīyamāṇasyaiva kliṣṭasya yasyaikadeśaḥ saṃmukhībhūtaḥ śaikṣasya ceti.
body.translated_text: Of the formless-realm defiled — from decline: when one declines from formless-realm dispassion through a desire-realm mind, there is acquisition of the formless-realm defiled [mind] for one not endowed with it. And of the trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>) — from decline — this is the subject: when one declines from <s>Arhatship</s> through a desire-realm mind, there is acquisition of the trainee mind for one not endowed with it. Thus, when a defiled mind of the desire-realm is actualized, the acquisition of six [types of] mind has been stated for one not endowed with them. When a defiled mind of the form-realm is actualized — the acquisition of six for one not endowed with them. 'Of the form-realm [dharmas]' — and so forth in detail. When one returns from the formless realm to the form-realm, at the time of that form-realm intermediate-existence and reconnection mind, which is necessarily defiled — [there is acquisition of] the three form-realm [types]: wholesome, [Tib. 238b] rebirth-obtained [indeterminate], defiled, and uncovered-indeterminate — because the <s>prāpti</s> of the earlier-born creation-mind (<s>nirmāṇacitta</s>) exists. And of the desire-realm uncovered-indeterminate — the creation-mind alone. And of the formless-realm defiled and the trainee [mind] — the acquisition. From decline, when one declines from <s>Arhatship</s> through a form-realm mind — [there is acquisition of] the trainee [mind] for one not endowed with it. Thus, in the form-realm defiled too, the acquisition of six has been stated. But in the formless-realm defiled, the acquisition of two for one not endowed with those two. From decline, when one declines from <s>Arhatship</s> through a formless-realm mind — [there is acquisition of] the defiled [mind], a portion of which is actualized, and the trainee [mind].

body.text: iti. kuśala iti jātinirdeśaḥ. kuśale kasmiṃścid rūpāvacare trayāṇāṃ lābhaḥ saṃbhavaḥ. katham. ādye tāvad rūpāvacare kuśale citte saṃmukhībhūte tasyaiva kuśalasya rūpāvacarasya lābhas tenāsamanvāgatasya. mauladhyānasaṃgṛhīte tu kuśale citte saṃmukhībhūte kāmāvacararūpāvacarayor anivṛtāvyākṛtayor nirmāṇacittayor lābhaḥ tābhyām asamanvāgatasya. ity evaṃ kuśale rūpāvacare citte saṃmukhībhūte trayāṇāṃ lābha ity ucyate. na tu yugapallābha iti.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Wholesome' is a designation of [moral] class. In some wholesome form-realm [mind], the acquisition of three is possible. How? First, when a form-realm wholesome mind is actualized — [there is] acquisition of that very form-realm wholesome [mind] for one not endowed with it. But when a wholesome mind included in a fundamental <s>dhyāna</s> is actualized — [there is] acquisition of the desire-realm and form-realm uncovered-indeterminate creation-minds for one not endowed with those two. Thus, when a wholesome form-realm mind is actualized, the acquisition of three is stated — but not simultaneous acquisition.

body.text: iti. śaikṣe citte saṃmukhībhūte duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāṃticitte tasyaiva śaikṣasya duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāṃtikalāpasvabhāvasya lābhas tenāsamanvāgatasya. kāmarūpāvacarayoś cānivṛtavyākṛtayor [Tib. 239a] ārūpyāvacarasya ca kuśalasya. kasmiṃ kalāpa ity āha. āryamārgeṇa kāmarūpadhātuvairāgye. katham iti. yadāyam anāgamyabhūmikenāryamārgeṇa kāmavairāgyaṃ karoti. tadā navamavimuktimārgasaṃgṛhīte śaikṣe citte saṃmukhībhūte kāmarūpāvacarayor anivṛtāvyākṛtayor nirmāṇacittayor lābhas tābhyām asamanvāgatasya. yadā tu ṣaḍbhūmikānām āryamārgāṇām anyatamena rūpavairāgyaṃ karoti. tadādyaprakāracitte śaikṣe saṃmukhībhūte 'tītānāgataprāptinyāyenārūpyāvacarasya kuśalasya lābhas tenāsamanvāgatasya. āryamārgagrahaṇaṃ sāsravacittanirāsārthaṃ. śaikṣe citte saṃbhūte 'yaṃ lābho varṇyate.
body.translated_text: thus. When a trainee mind is actualized — in the mind of the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering — [there is] acquisition of that very trainee [mind], having the nature of the assemblage of the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering, for one not endowed with it. And of the desire-realm and form-realm uncovered-indeterminate [Tib. 239a] and the formless-realm wholesome. In which assemblage [does this occur]? He says: through dispassion from the desire and form realms by the Noble Path. How? When this one, by the Noble Path belonging to the <s>Anāgamya</s> level, achieves dispassion from desire — then, when the trainee mind included in the ninth liberation-path is actualized — [there is] acquisition of the desire-realm and form-realm uncovered-indeterminate creation-minds for one not endowed with those two. But when, by any one of the six-level Noble Paths, one achieves dispassion from form — then, when the first-type trainee mind is actualized — [there is] acquisition of the formless-realm wholesome for one not endowed with it, by the principle of past and future <s>prāpti</s>. The mention of 'Noble Path' is for the purpose of excluding outflow-possessing mind. This acquisition occurring in a trainee mind is being described.

body.text: atrācāryaguṇamatir vyācaṣṭe.
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Guṇamati</s> explains.

body.text: tasyaiva śaikṣasya kāmarūpāvacarayoś cānivṛtāvyākṛtayor arūpyāvacarasya ca kuśalasyeti. katham ity ato bravīti. āryamārgeṇa kāmarūpavairāgye yadāyam anāgamyabhūmikenāryamārgeṇa kāmadhātuvairāgyaṃ karoti. tadā yo navamo vimuktimārgaḥ. tasmiṃ mauladhyānabhūmikam apūrvakaṃ śaikṣaṃ labhata iti śaikṣasya lābha ucyate. kāmarūpāvacarayoś cānivṛtāvyākṛtayor nirmāṇacittayor eva tasmiṃ lābhaḥ. ṣaḍbhūmikena tv āryamārgeṇa [Tib. 239b] kāmarūpavairāgye yo navamo vimuktimārgaḥ. tasminn ārūpyāvacaraṃ kuṣalaṃ pratilabhata iti. tacchiṣyo 'py ācāryavasumitras tam evārthaṃ tena vākyena tair eva padavyaṃjanair likhati. tad etad ayuktaṃ vyākhyānaṃ. na hy evaṃ ekavākyena vyākhyātārtho ghaṭate. vākyabhedena ghaṭate. tasyaiva śaikṣasya lābha ity etad ekaṃ vākyaṃ. kāmarūpāvacarayoś ca yāvat kāmarūpadhātuvairāgya ity aparaṃ vākyam. āryamārgeṇa kāmarūpadhātuvairāgya ity etena viśeṣeṇa tasyaiva śaikṣasyety etat pūrvoktaṃ na viśeṣyaṃ vākyāntaratvāt. atadvato hy ayaṃ cittalābho varṇyate.
body.translated_text: 'Of that very learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), and of the uncovered-indeterminate [minds] belonging to the desire and form realms, and of the wholesome [mind] belonging to the formless realm.' How? Therefore he explains: 'through dispassion from the desire and form [realms] by the noble path' — when this [person], through the noble path belonging to the <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary) ground, achieves dispassion from the desire realm, then at the ninth liberation-path, he obtains for the first time a learner [mind] belonging to the principal <s>dhyāna</s> ground — thus the obtainment of the learner [mind] is stated. And the obtainment at that [point] of the uncovered-indeterminate [minds] belonging to the desire and form realms pertains to the supernaturally-created minds alone. But through dispassion from the desire and form [realms] by the noble path of six grounds, [Tib. 239b] at the ninth liberation-path, one obtains the wholesome [mind] belonging to the formless realm. His disciple too, Master <s>Vasumitra</s>, writes that very meaning in that very statement with those very words and syllables. But this explanation is improper. For the meaning explained cannot be construed by a single statement; it is construed through a division of statements. 'Of that very learner, obtainment' — this is one statement. 'And of the uncovered-indeterminate of the desire and form realms... through dispassion from the desire and form realms' — this is another statement. The specification 'through dispassion from the desire and form realms by the noble path' does not qualify the previously stated 'of that very learner,' because it is a different statement. For this mind-obtainment is described of one who does not possess [those minds].

children.translated_text: 'For the mind-obtainment is of one who does not possess [them]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. kathaṃ. navame vimuktimārge śaikṣacittavataḥ pudgalasya śaikṣacittalābho vyavasthāpyate. nanu coktaṃ mauladhyānabhūmikam apūrvaṃ śaikṣaṃ labhyata iti. na atiprasaṃgāt. rūpāvacaram api kuśalaṃ cittaṃ mauladhyānabhūmikam apūrvaṃ pratilabhyata iti tasyāpi lābha iti prasajyeta. ācāryavasumitra āha. śaikṣacittasthitasya kāmadhātuvairāgye kuśalam uṣmagatāvasthāyām eva rūpāvacaraṃ niyāmavākrāntau labdham iti kṛtvā na gaṇyata iti. tad ayuktaṃ śaikṣasyāpy agaṇanāprāpteḥ. śaikṣam api hi darśanamārgāvasthāyāṃ labdham iti na bhavatā tathā sthāpayitavyam iti prāpnoti. ataś cedam apavyākhyānam iti niścīyate. yasmād ācāryeṇaiva [Tib. 240a] miśraślokavyākhyāna evaṃ likhitaṃ. śaikṣasyāśaikṣasya ca niyamāvakrāntyarhattvayor iti.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. How? At the ninth liberation-path, the obtainment of the learner-mind is established for a person who [already] possesses the learner-mind. But was it not said that one obtains for the first time a learner [mind] belonging to the principal <s>dhyāna</s> ground? No — because of over-extension. It would follow that the obtainment of the wholesome mind belonging to the form realm, being a first-time [obtainment] belonging to the principal <s>dhyāna</s> ground, would also be [counted as] an obtainment. Master <s>Vasumitra</s> says: for one established in the learner-mind, when achieving dispassion from the desire realm, the wholesome form-realm [mind] was obtained at the very stage of warmth, and at the entry into the fixed course [of certainty] — therefore it is not counted. But that is improper, because the non-counting of the learner [mind] too would follow. For the learner [mind] too was obtained at the stage of the insight-path — therefore it follows that it should not be so established by you either. Hence this is determined to be a mis-explanation — because the Master himself [Tib. 240a] wrote thus in the explanation of the mixed verse: 'of the learner and the non-learner, at the entry into the fixed course and at <s>Arhatship</s>.'

body.text: iti. prātipadikadhāturūpam etad iti darśayati. yatra citte lābho na vyākhyātaḥ. tatra tasyaiva lābha iti. kathaṃ kṛtvā. kāmāvacare tāvat kuśalacitta iyatāṃ cittānāṃ lābha iti na vyākhyātaḥ. tatra tasyaiva lābho nānyeṣāṃ. tadyathā samyagdṛṣṭyā kuśalamūlapratisaṃdhāne kāmāvacare kuśale citte saṃmukhībhūte tasyaiva kuśalasya cittasya lābhaḥ tenāsamanvāgatasya. nānyeṣāṃ kliṣṭānāṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. He shows that this is a stem-root form. 'Where obtainment of a mind has not been explained, there the obtainment is of that very [type of mind].' How? In the desire-realm wholesome mind, the obtainment of how many minds [is there] — this has not been explained. There the obtainment is of that very [mind] alone, not of others. For example, when wholesome roots are reconnected through right view, and the desire-realm wholesome mind becomes manifest, the obtainment is of that very wholesome mind for one who was not endowed with it — not of others that are afflicted

body.text: traidhātukānām api pūrvapratilabdhatvāt. na kāmāvacarasyānivṛtāvyākṛtasya. vipākajādīnāṃ sahajaprāptitvāt. nirmāṇacittasya prāptyabhāvāt. na rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ kuśalādīnāṃ śaikṣaśaikṣayoś ca prāptyabhāvāt. anivṛtāvyākṛte 'pi kāmāvacare citte lābho na vyākhyātaḥ. tatra tasyaiva lābhaḥ tenāsamanvāgatasya.
body.translated_text: — nor of the [minds] of all three realms, because of their being previously obtained. Not of the desire-realm uncovered-indeterminate [mind], because of the simultaneous possession of the maturation-born and the rest. Nor of the supernaturally-created mind, because of the absence of its possession. Not of the wholesome and the rest of the form and formless realms, and of the learner and non-learner [minds], because of the absence of their possession. In the uncovered-indeterminate mind of the desire realm too, obtainment has not been explained. There the obtainment is of that very [mind] alone, for one not endowed with it.

children.translated_text: 'The possession of the indeterminate is simultaneous' —

body.text: kṛtvā. nanyeṣāṃ kuśalādīnāṃ pūrvapratilabdhatvāt. tathaiva keṣāṃcit prāptyabhāvāc ca. nirmāṇacitte tu saṃmukhībhūte na kasyacil lābha iti na vaktavyaṃ. yatra hi kliṣṭe 'nyatra vā kasyacil lābho nāsti. na tad ucyate. kliṣṭa eva hi traidhātuke ṣaṇṇāṃ yāvad dvayor lābho na tv avaśyam ity avadhāraṇaṃ. rūpāvacare 'py [Tib. 240b] anivṛtāvyākṛte saṃmukhībhūte tasyaiva lābhaḥ. nānyeṣāṃ pūrvavad vaktavyaṃ. tathārūpyāvacare ākāśānantyāyatanasāmantakādyaprakārasaṃgṛhīte kuśalacitte saṃmukhībhūte tasyaiva lābhas tenāsamanvāgatasya. nānyeṣāṃ keṣāṃcit. pūrvapratilabdhatvāt keṣāṃcit prāptyabhāvāt. evaṃ anivṛtāvyākṛte śaikṣe ca.
body.translated_text: by this [principle]. Not of others — the wholesome and the rest — because of being previously obtained, and because of the absence of possession for some likewise. But when the supernaturally-created mind becomes manifest, it should not be said that there is no obtainment of anything. For where in the afflicted or elsewhere there is no obtainment of anything — that is not stated. For only in the afflicted [mind] of the three realms, the obtainment of six, up to two — but necessarily — this is the restriction. In the form-realm [Tib. 240b] uncovered-indeterminate [mind] too, when it becomes manifest, the obtainment is of that very indeterminate [mind] — not of others, as should be stated as before. Likewise, in the formless-realm wholesome mind — that included in [such types as] the preliminary to the sphere of infinite space and the rest — when it becomes manifest, the obtainment is of that very [mind] for one not endowed with it — not of some others, because of being previously obtained for some, and because of the absence of possession for some. Likewise for the uncovered-indeterminate and the learner [minds].

body.text: anye punar abhedenāhur iti. ke. miśrakakārā. abhedeneti traidhātukānāṃ kliṣṭādīnām apṛthakkaraṇāt.
body.translated_text: 'Others, however, state [this] without distinction' — who? The authors of the <s>Miśraka</s> (mixed [verse commentary]). 'Without distinction' — without separating the afflicted and other [types] of the three realms.

body.text: iti. yad uktaṃ. tan nyūnaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ. kuśalaṃ hi traidhātukaṃ sāsravam anāsravaṃ ca. tatra saptānāṃ kaśale citte iti vaktavyṃ na ṣaṇṇām iti tad darśayann āha. kāmāvacarasyeti vistaraḥ. kuśalamūlepratisaṃdhānād iti vyākhyātam etat. anivṛtāvyākṛtayor vairāgyata iti. laukikena lokottareṇa vā mārgeṇa kāmadhātor vairāgye navame vimuktimārge kāmarūpāvacarayor nirmāṇacittayor lābhas tābhyām asamanvāgatasya. rūpārāpyāvacarayoḥ kuśalayos tatastyasamādhilābhata iti. yadā rūpāvacaram anāgamyaṃ prathamato labhate. tadā rūpāvacarasya kuśalasya lābhaḥ. yadākāśānaṃtyāyatanasāmantakaṃ prathamato labhate. tadārūpyāvacarasya kuśalasya lābhaḥ. [Tib. 241a] śaikṣasya cāśaikṣasya ca niyamāvakrāntyarhattvayor iti. yadā niyamam avakrāmati. tadā śaikṣasya duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntikalāpasya lāghaḥ. yadārhattvaṃ prāpnoti. tadāśaikṣasya kṣayajñānakalāpasya lābhaḥ. ity āsv avasthāsv amībhiś cittair yathoktaiḥ saptabhir asamanvāgataḥ samanvāgamanaṃ pratilabhate. śeṣam ata eva vyākhyānād upadhāryam iti. ata eva madīyād vyākhyānāc cheṣam avagantavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. What was stated is an incomplete definition. For the wholesome is threefold-realm, with outflows and without outflows. Therein, 'of seven, in the wholesome mind' should be stated, not 'of six' — showing this, he says: 'of the desire realm' — thus the elaboration. This has been explained as 'through the reconnection of wholesome roots.' 'Of the uncovered-indeterminate, through dispassion' — through dispassion from the desire realm by the mundane or supramundane path, at the ninth liberation-path, the obtainment of the supernaturally-created minds belonging to the desire and form realms for one not endowed with them. 'Of the wholesome of the form and formless realms, through the obtainment of the corresponding <s>samādhi</s>' — when one first obtains the <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary concentration) belonging to the form realm, then the obtainment of the wholesome of the form realm. When one first obtains the preliminary to the sphere of infinite space, then the obtainment of the wholesome of the formless realm. [Tib. 241a] 'And of the learner and the non-learner, at the entry into the fixed course and at <s>Arhatship</s>' — when one enters the fixed course [of certainty], then the obtainment of the learner's assemblage of the insight-tolerance regarding the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering. When one attains <s>Arhatship</s>, then the obtainment of the non-learner's assemblage of the knowledge of destruction. Thus in these stages, one who is not endowed with those seven minds as stated obtains endowment. 'The remainder should be understood from this very explanation' — the remainder should be understood from this very explanation of mine.

children.translated_text: 'In the afflicted mind, the obtainment of nine' —

body.text: ity ekaṃ.
body.translated_text: this is the first.

children.translated_text: 'Of that very [type], in the indeterminate [mind], indeed' —

body.text: iti dvitīyam. ity etac cheṣaṃ. kathaṃ. kliṣṭe tridhātuke citte navānāṃ lābhaḥ. kāmāvacarāṇāṃ caturṇāṃ rūpāvacarāṇāṃ trayāṇām ārūyāvacarasya nivṛtasya śaikṣasya ceti navānāṃ yathāyogaṃ lābhaḥ tair asamanvāgatasya. ko 'yaṃ yathāyogārthaḥ. kāmāvacaro ca kliṣṭe kuśalamūlapratisaṃdhānena vā dhātupratyāgamanena vā kāmāvacarasya kuśalasya lābhaḥ. akuśalanivṛtāvyākṛtayoś ca dhātupratyāgamanena parihāṇyā vā lābhaḥ. rūpāvacara eva klṣṭe rūpāvacarasya kuśalasya kāmāvacararūpāvacarayoś cānivṛtāvyākṛtayor nirmāṇacittayor dhātupratyāgamanāl lābhaḥ. kāmāvacare rūpāvacare vā kliṣṭe rūpāvacarasya vā kliṣṭasya vā dhātupratyāgamanāt parihāṇito vā lābhaḥ. kāmāvacare rūpāvacare ārūpyāvacare vā kliṣṭe [Tib. 241b] ārūpyāvacarakliṣṭaśaikṣayoḥ parihāṇito lābhaḥ. iti yathāyogārthaḥ.
body.translated_text: this is the second. These are the remainder. How? In the afflicted mind of the three realms, the obtainment of nine: of the four belonging to the desire realm, of three belonging to the form realm, of the afflicted belonging to the formless realm, and of the learner — [thus] nine, as appropriate, for one not endowed with them. What is the meaning of 'as appropriate'? In the desire realm, in the afflicted [mind]: through the reconnection of wholesome roots or through return to the [desire] realm, the obtainment of the desire-realm wholesome [mind]. And of the unwholesome and covered-indeterminate, through return to the realm or through decline. In the form realm alone, in the afflicted [mind]: the obtainment of the form-realm wholesome [mind] and of the uncovered-indeterminate supernaturally-created minds belonging to the desire and form realms, through return to the realm. In the afflicted [mind] of the desire or form realm, or of the afflicted [mind] of the form realm: the obtainment of the form-realm afflicted [mind] through return to the realm or through decline. In the afflicted [mind] of the desire, form, or formless realm — [Tib. 241b] of the formless-realm afflicted and learner [minds], through decline. Thus the meaning of 'as appropriate.'

children.translated_text: 'Of that very [type], in the indeterminate [mind], indeed' —

body.text: iti. yac cheṣaṃ. tat tulyam iti pūrvavat. avyākṛtānāṃ hi traidhātukānām anyatamasmiṃ saṃmukhībhūte tasyaivāvyākṛtasya lābhaḥ. tenatenāsamanvāgatasya.
body.translated_text: thus — what is the remainder. That is the same as before. For when any one of the three-realm indeterminate [minds] becomes manifest, the obtainment is of that very indeterminate [mind] alone, for one not endowed with that particular [mind].

children.translated_text: 'The possession of the indeterminate is simultaneous' —

body.text: siddhāntāt. saṃgrahaśloka iti. sarvam
body.translated_text: by this established principle. 'Summary verse' — all [obtainments occur]:

body.text: dhātupratyāgamanād iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of the statement 'through return to the realm.'

body.text: tasyaiva kuśalasyaivamādivacanāt. tatastyasamādhilābhata iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of statements such as 'of that very wholesome [mind]' and the like, and 'through the obtainment of the corresponding <s>samādhi</s>.'

body.text: kāmarūpadhātuvairāgye iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of the statement 'through dispassion from the desire and form realms.'

body.text: parihāṇita iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of the statement 'through decline.'

body.text: vicikitsayā samyagdṛṣṭyā ca kuśalamūlapratisaṃdhānād iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of the statement 'through the reconnection of wholesome roots by doubt and by right view.'

body.text: cittapratilaṃbhaḥ.
body.translated_text: [means] the acquisition of mind.

body.text: pudgalasya tair asamanvāgatasyeti vacanād iti.
body.translated_text: because of the statement 'of a person not endowed with them.'

body.text: ācāryayaśomitrakṛtāyām abhidharmakośavyākhyāyām indriyanirdeśo nāma dvitīyaṃ kośasthānaṃ samāptaṃ.
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmakośavyākhyā</s> composed by Master <s>Yaśomitra</s>, the second <s>kośasthāna</s> called the Exposition of Faculties (<s>Indriyanirdeśa</s>) is completed.

body.text:
III
(lokanirdeśo nāma tṛtīyaṃ kośasthānam)
body.translated_text:
III
(The third <s>kośasthāna</s> called the Exposition of the World — <s>Lokanirdeśa</s>)

body.text: (III.1-3) idam idānīṃ vaktavyam iti. dvitīyasya tṛtīyasya ca kośasthānasya sambandhapradarśanārtham idam uktaṃ. kāmarūpārūpyadhātunaiyamyena cittādīnāṃ kṛto nirdeśa iti. niyamasya bhāvo naiyamyaṃ niyama eva vā naiyamyaṃ. tena cittādīnāṃ kṛto nirdeśaḥ.
body.translated_text: (III.1-3) 'Now this should be stated' — this was said for the purpose of showing the connection between the second and third <s>kośasthāna</s>s. 'The exposition of mind and the rest was made according to the restriction of the desire, form, and formless realms (<s>dhātu</s>)' — the state of restriction is <s>naiyamya</s>, or restriction itself is <s>naiyamya</s>. By that [restriction], the exposition of mind and the rest was made.

children.text:
kuśalākuśalaṃ kāme [Tib. 242a] nivṛtānivṛtaṃ manaḥ.
rūpārūpyeṣv akuśalād anyatreti
children.translated_text:
'In the desire [realm], the wholesome and unwholesome, [Tib. 242a] the covered and uncovered mind;
in the form and formless [realms], except for the unwholesome' —

body.text: vācanāt. ādiśabdena caittādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. By the word 'and the rest,' the mental factors and the rest are included.

children.text:
savitarkavicāratvāt kuśale kāmacetasi.
kaukṛtyamiddhākuśalāny ādye na santy ataḥ
dhyānāntare vitarkaś ca vicāraś cāpy ataḥ param

body.text: iti vacanāt. indriyāṇāṃ kāmādinaiyamyena kṛto nirdeśaḥ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. The exposition of the faculties was made according to the restriction of the desire [realm] and the rest.

children.text:
kāmāptam amalaṃ hitvā rūpāptam strīpum indriye.
duḥkhe ca hitvārūyāptaṃ sukhe cāpohye rūpi ceti
children.translated_text:
'Excluding those attained in the desire [realm], the non-outflow, and those attained in the form [realm] — the female and male faculties;
excluding [that attained in] the formless — pain; and excluding what is [merely] form — pleasure' —

body.text: vacanāt. tena kāmarūpārūpyadhātavo 'nuktalakṣaṇā ity ataḥ pṛcchati. tatra katame te kāmarūpārūpyadhātava iti. ata idam ucyate.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Therefore, the desire, form, and formless realms have unexplained characteristics — hence he asks: 'what then are those desire, form, and formless realms?' Therefore this is stated:

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. catasro gataya iti. narakapretatiryagmanuṣyagatayaś catasraḥ sākalyena kāmadhātāv antargatāḥ. devagatis tu na sākalyena. kiṃ tarhi. ṣaḍ devanikāyā iti darśayati. tatra nīryanta iti nṝ naye. na raṃjayantīti raṃjeḥ. narer iti ri gatireṣaṇayor ity asya pratiṣedhapūrvasya rūpaṃ. nīryante 'smiṃ sattvā apuṇyeneti narakāḥ. na raṃjayanta iti narakā ity apare. narer āsādanārthasyaitad rūpaṃ. na raṃjayati prāvaṃti nāspṛhayaṃti trāṇaṃ iti narakā iti ācāryasaṃghabhabhadraḥ. bhṛśamito 'punarāvṛtter itāḥ pretāḥ. pipāsayā
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration. Four destinies — the hell-being, <s>preta</s>, animal, and human destinies — are included in the desire realm in their entirety. But the divine destiny is not [included] in its entirety. Rather, six classes of gods — this he shows. Therein, [the etymology]: '<s>nṝ</s>' [means] 'they are led' — from the root <s>nī</s> (to lead). '<s>Na raṃjayanti</s>' [means] 'they do not delight' — from the root <s>raṃj</s>. '<s>Nara</s>' is the form of the root <s>ri</s> (to go/seek) preceded by the negative. 'That in which beings are led by demerit' — [these are] <s>naraka</s>s (hells). Others [say]: 'they do not delight' — [hence] <s>naraka</s>s. This is the form of <s>nara</s> in the sense of 'reaching.' 'They do not delight, they do not aspire, there is no refuge' — [these are] <s>naraka</s>s, according to Master <s>Saṃghabhadra</s>. 'Gone far, without return' — [they are] <s>preta</s>s (departed ones). 'Afflicted by thirst'

body.text: parītā ity apare. tiryaggamanāt
body.translated_text: — others [say]. Because of going sideways (<s>tiryak</s>) —

body.text: manasa udbhūtatvān manuṣyāḥ. [Tib. 242b] manor apatyā iti laukikāḥ. dyaur oko yeṣām iti
body.translated_text: Because of having a developed mind (<s>manas</s>) — [they are] <s>manuṣya</s>s (humans). [Tib. 242b] 'The offspring of <s>Manu</s>' — [say] the worldly [etymologists]. Those whose dwelling is the sky (<s>div</s>) —

body.text: kāmaprabhāvito dhātuḥ kāmadhātur iti vakṣyati. catvāro mahārājāno lokapālā virūḍhako virūpākṣo dhṛtarāṣṭro vaiśravaṇaś ca. teṣu bhavāś cāturmahārājikās tanmadhyagatā ity arthaḥ. tadyathā deveṣūpapadyate devamadhye utpadyata ity arthaḥ. caturmahārājasthāne bhavāś cāturmahārājikā madhyapadalopā gorathavad ity apare. sahakṛtasukṛtair atropapadyaṃta iti trayastriṃśāḥ. samānapuṇyair ity arthaḥ. aṣṭau vasavā dvāv aśvinau ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityā iti tāvatpramukhatvāt trayastriṃśā iti laukikāḥ. tadanusāreṇa pravacane 'pi tathā nāmavyavahāra ity apare. duḥkhāt yātāḥ puṇyeneti yāmāḥ. duḥkhāni vā yāmayantīti yāmāḥ. tuṣā tuṣṭyā itāḥ. tuṣo vā vidyante eṣām iti tuṣitāḥ. svayaṃkṛte nirmāṇe ratir eṣām iti nirmāṇaratayaḥ. paranirmitān bhogān vaśe vartayituṃ śīlam eṣām iti paranirmitavaśavartinaḥ. sthānānīti vākyaśeṣa iti. yāni viṃśatisthānāni. sa kāmadhātuḥ. yadi tu viṃśatisthāno viṃśatir iti uttarapadalopaḥ kriyeta. tadyathā pītatoyā aśvāḥ pītā iti [Tib. 243a] sutarāṃ śliṣyati. saṃjīvo yatra sattvān mriyamāṇān vāyavo jīvayaṃti. kālasūtrā yatra kālasūtrāṇi pātayitvā sattvās takṣyaṃte. saṃghāto yatra meṣākṛtayaḥ parvatādaya ubhayata āpatantaḥ sattvān pīḍayanti. rauravo yatra sattvā yātyamānāḥ paramavikṛtaṃ rudaṃti. yatra tu viśeṣeṇa sa mahārauravaḥ. tapano yatrāgnyādibhis tapyante sattvāḥ. yatra tu viśeṣeṇa sa pratāpanaḥ. avīcir yatrātimātrāgnijvālāliṃgitānāṃ sattvānāṃ sukhavīcir antaraṃ nāsti. jambūdvīpo jambūcihno dvīpaḥ. pūrvavidehaḥ sumeroḥ pūrveṇa. avaragodānīyaḥ paścimena. uttarakurur uttareṇa. evaṃ nāmāna ete dvīpā lokapratītāḥ. ṣaṭ cānantaroktā devanikāyāḥ. ity etāni viṃśatiḥ sthānānīti. aṣtau narakāś catvāro dvīpāḥ ṣaṭ cānantaroktāś cāturmahārājikādayaḥ pretās tiryañcaś cābhinnā iti viṃśatisthānaḥ kāmadhātuḥ. yāvad vāyumaṇḍalam iti. adhastād yatrāpmaṇḍalaṃ tiṣṭhati.
body.translated_text: 'The realm influenced by desire (<s>kāma</s>) is the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>)' — this will be stated. The four great kings, the world-guardians, are <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, and <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. Those who exist among them are the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>s — the meaning is: those situated in their midst. Just as 'one is reborn among gods' means 'one is born in the midst of gods.' Others [say]: those who exist in the place of the four great kings are <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> — with elision of the middle word, like <s>goratha</s>. Those who are reborn here through merits performed together are the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s>s (Thirty-Three) — the meaning is: through equal merit. Eight <s>Vasu</s>s, two <s>Aśvin</s>s, eleven <s>Rudra</s>s, and twelve <s>Āditya</s>s — because of having that many leaders, they are called <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> according to the worldly tradition. Following that, in the teaching too the same naming convention [is used] — according to others. 'Gone from suffering by merit' — [hence] <s>Yāma</s>s. Or: 'they restrain sufferings' — [hence] <s>Yāma</s>s. '<s>Tuṣa</s>' — gone by satisfaction. Or: 'satisfaction exists in them' — [hence] <s>Tuṣita</s>s. 'Delight in self-made creations is theirs' — [hence] <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>s (delighting in creation). 'Their nature is to control enjoyments created by others' — [hence] <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>s (controlling others' creations). 'Abodes' completes the sentence. The twenty abodes — that is the desire realm. If, however, a compound-loss of the latter member is made — '<s>viṃśatisthāna</s>' becoming '<s>viṃśati</s>' — like '<s>pītatoyā aśvāḥ</s>' becoming '<s>pītā</s>' — [Tib. 243a] it fits even better. <s>Saṃjīva</s> (Reviving) — where winds revive dying beings. <s>Kālasūtra</s> (Black Thread) — where, having cast black threads upon them, beings are cut. <s>Saṃghāta</s> (Crushing) — where ram-shaped mountains and the like, falling from both sides, crush beings. <s>Raurava</s> (Screaming) — where beings, being tormented, cry out with extreme distortion. Where [the torment is] especially [intense] — that is <s>Mahāraurava</s> (Great Screaming). <s>Tapana</s> (Heating) — where beings are scorched by fire and the like. Where [it is] especially [so] — that is <s>Pratāpana</s> (Great Heating). <s>Avīci</s> (Without Respite) — where, for beings enveloped by excessive fire-flames, there is no interval of pleasant respite. <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — the continent marked by the <s>Jambu</s> [tree]. <s>Pūrvavideha</s> — to the east of <s>Sumeru</s>. <s>Avaragodānīya</s> — to the west. <s>Uttarakuru</s> — to the north. Thus these continents are known by name in the world. And the six classes of gods just mentioned — these are the twenty abodes. Eight hells, four continents, six classes of gods beginning with the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>s, and <s>preta</s>s and animals undivided — thus the desire realm has twenty abodes. 'Down to the wind-disc' — below, where the water-disc rests.

body.text: iti. rūpaprabhāvito dhātuḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. The realm influenced by form.

children.text:
pṛthakpṛthag
dhyānaṃ tribhūmikaṃ tatra. caturthaṃ tu aṣṭabhūmikam
children.translated_text:
'Each separately,
each <s>dhyāna</s> has three grounds therein; but the fourth has eight grounds' —

body.text: iti. tatra rūpadhātau sarveṣām api dhyānānāṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedena pratyekaṃ tribhūmikaṃ. [Tib. 243b] brahmakāyikāḥ brahmapurohitāḥ mahābrahmāṇa
body.translated_text: thus. Therein, in the form realm, each of all the <s>dhyāna</s>s has three grounds by the distinction of mild, medium, and intense. [Tib. 243b] <s>Brahmakāyika</s>s, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>s, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>s

body.text: iti prathamaṃ. parīttābhā āpramāṇābhā ābhāsvarā iti dvitīyaṃ. parīttaśubhā apramāṇaśubhāḥ śubhakṛtsnā iti tṛtīyaṃ. anabhrakāḥ puṇyaprasavā bṛhatphalā iti caturthaṃ. tasya tv adhimātrasyaivānāsravadhyānavyavakiraṇena mṛdumadhyādhimātradhimātratarādhimātratamabhedabhinnena punaḥ paṃca sthānāntarāṇi. abṛhā atapāḥ sudṛṣāḥ sudarśanā ākaniṣṭhāś ceti. ataś caturthaṃ dhyānam aṣṭabhūmikam ity ucyate. tatra bṛhatkuśalamūlaniryātatvād brahmā. kaś cāsau. yo mahābrahmety ucyate. dhyānāṃtaralābhāt paścāt pūrvaṃ cyutyupapattilābhāt pramāṇādiviśeṣādibhiś cāsya mahān. tasya kāyo nivāsa eṣāṃ vidyate iti brahmakāyikāḥ. brahmā purodhīyate eṣām iti brahmapurohitāḥ. āyurvarṇādibhir viśeṣair mahābrahmā eṣām iti mahābrahmāṇaḥ. parīttaiṣām ābhābhāsvarabhūmim apekṣyeti parīttābhāḥ. nābhāpramāṇam eṣām śakyaṃ pramātum ity apramāṇābhāḥ. kṛtsnasthānāntarodbhāsanād ābhāsvarāḥ. manobhūmikaṃ sukhaṃ śubham ity ucyate. tad eṣām anyabhūmim apekṣya parīttam iti parīttaśubhāḥ. apramāṇaṃ śubham eṣām apramāṇaśubhāḥ. śubhaṃ kṛtsnam eṣām iti śubhakṛtsnāḥ. [Tib. 244a] na tadutkṛṣṭataram anyatrāsti sukham ity abhiprāyaḥ. abhravad eṣāṃ bbūmisaṃbaṃdho nāstīty anabhrakāḥ. saha sattvena tadvimānodayavyayād iti vacanān naiṣām upari bhūmyantaram astīti anabhrakāḥ. abhram iva hy upari na bhūmisaṃbandha ity apare. āniṃjyakarmasaṃbhūtatvāt puṇyebhyaḥ prasava eṣām iti puṇyaprasavāḥ. sthānāntarapratibaddhaṃ pārthagjanikaṃ sarvotkṛṣṭaṃ bṛhad eṣāṃ phalam udbhavatīti bṛhatphalāḥ. pṛthagjanāmiśratvāc chuddha āvāsa eṣām iti śuddhāvāsāḥ. śuddhāvāsāṃtarebhyo 'nutkṛṣṭatvād abṛṃhitā ity abṛhāḥ. nālpena vā kālenātmanaḥ sthānaṃ bṛṃhaṃti jahatīty abṛhāḥ. viśiṣṭasamādhilābhān nātra kleśās tapaṃtīty atapāḥ. kalyāṇāśayatvād vā na parāṃs tāpayaṃtīty atapāḥ. pariśuddhadarśanatvāt suṣṭhu paśyantīti sudṛśāḥ. śobhanadarśanatvāt sudarśanāḥ. tadutkṛṣṭatarabhūmyantarābhāvān naite kaniṣṭhā ity akaniṣṭhāḥ jyeṣṭhatvāt. sthānina ete nirdiṣṭāḥ. katham idam ucyate ity etāni saptadaśa sthānānīti. sthāniśabdena sthānanirdeśād adoṣa eva. evaṃ bahirdeśakanayena saptadaśa sthānāni rūpadhātuḥ. ṣoḍaśeti kāśmīrāḥ. ṣoḍaśa sthānāni rūpadhātur iti kāśmīrāḥ. [Tib. 244b] parigaṇa iveti. pariṣaṇḍa iva. āṭavikakoṭṭa ity apare. na tu bhūmyaṃtaram iti. na tu bhūmyaṃtarasaṃbaṃdham iti. atītānāgatāvijñaptyarūpiṇo hi dharmā adeśasthā iti. atītanāgatā rūpiṇo 'py adeśasthāḥ. avijñaptiḥ rūpiṇī vartamānāpy adeśasthā. arūpiṇo vedanādayas tathaiva vartamānā apy adeśasthāḥ. kiṃ aṃgātītānāgatāḥ.
body.translated_text: — this is the first [dhyāna]. <s>Parīttābha</s>s (Limited Radiance), <s>Apramāṇābha</s>s (Immeasurable Radiance), <s>Ābhāsvara</s>s (Streaming Radiance) — the second. <s>Parīttaśubha</s>s (Limited Beauty), <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>s (Immeasurable Beauty), <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>s (Total Beauty) — the third. <s>Anabhraka</s>s (Cloudless), <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>s (Merit-Born), <s>Bṛhatphala</s>s (Great Fruit) — the fourth. But of that [fourth dhyāna], of the intense [grade] alone, through the intermixture of non-outflow <s>dhyāna</s>, distinguished by the division into mild, medium, intense, more intense, and most intense, there are five further stations: <s>Abṛha</s>s (Not Great), <s>Atapa</s>s (Without Torment), <s>Sudṛśa</s>s (Fair-Seeing), <s>Sudarśana</s>s (Beautiful), and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>s (Highest) — therefore the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is said to have eight grounds. Therein, because of being produced from great wholesome roots, [he is called] <s>Brahmā</s>. And who is he? The one called <s>Mahābrahmā</s> — because of obtaining the inter-<s>dhyāna</s>, because of subsequently obtaining [rebirth] after passing away first, and because of distinction in measure and the like, he is great. His body — abode — exists for these [gods], hence <s>Brahmakāyika</s>s. <s>Brahmā</s> is placed before them — hence <s>Brahmapurohita</s>s. Through distinctions of lifespan, complexion, and the like, <s>Mahābrahmā</s> [is the greatest] among them — hence <s>Mahābrahmāṇa</s>s. Their radiance is limited in comparison to the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> ground — hence <s>Parīttābha</s>s (Limited Radiance). The measure of their radiance cannot be measured — hence <s>Apramāṇābha</s>s. Because of illuminating all intermediate stations — <s>Ābhāsvara</s>s. The mental happiness is called '<s>śubha</s>' (beautiful/pure). That, for them, is limited in comparison to other grounds — hence <s>Parīttaśubha</s>s. Their purity is immeasurable — <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>s. Their purity is total — <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>s. [Tib. 244a] The intent is: there is no happiness more excellent than that anywhere else. Their connection with the ground does not exist, like a cloud — hence <s>Anabhraka</s>s. Because of the statement 'their celestial palace arises and perishes together with the being,' there is no ground-level above them — hence <s>Anabhraka</s>s. 'Like a cloud, for above [them] there is no ground-connection' — according to others. Because of being produced by immovable <s>karma</s>, their offspring is from merit — hence <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>s. Because the greatest fruit connected with [this] station, produced by ordinary beings, arises for them as great — hence <s>Bṛhatphala</s>s. Because of being unmixed with ordinary persons, their abode is pure — hence <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>s (Pure Abodes). Because of not being surpassed among the Pure Abodes — not expanded — hence <s>Abṛha</s>s. Or: because they do not expand — abandon — their station in a short time, [they are] <s>Abṛha</s>s. Because of obtaining a distinguished <s>samādhi</s>, afflictions do not torment here — hence <s>Atapa</s>s. Or: because of virtuous disposition, they do not torment others — hence <s>Atapa</s>s. Because of purified vision, they see well — hence <s>Sudṛśa</s>s. Because of beautiful vision — <s>Sudarśana</s>s. Because of the absence of a ground-level more excellent than theirs, they are not the least — hence <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>s, because of being the eldest. These inhabitants have been described. 'How can it be said "these are seventeen stations"?' — since the word 'inhabitant' indicates the station, there is no fault. Thus by the method of external geography, seventeen stations [constitute] the form realm. 'Sixteen' — according to the <s>Kāśmīra</s>s. Sixteen stations [constitute] the form realm — according to the <s>Kāśmīra</s>s. [Tib. 244b] 'Like an enclave' — like a forest-fort according to others. 'But not a ground-level' — but not a ground-level connection. For past, future, non-informative, and formless <s>dharma</s>s have no location. Past and future [dharmas], though material, have no location. Non-informative [dharma], though material and present, has no location. Formless [dharmas] such as feeling, etc., likewise, though present, have no location — how much more so the past and future ones.

body.text: iti karmanirvṛttā janmāntare skandhapravṛttir upapattiḥ. tayā. ārūpyadhātuś caturvidhaś catuḥprakāraḥ. yad utākāśānaṃtyāyatanam iti vistaraḥ. anantam ākāśam iti samāpattiprapogakālākārād ākāśānaṃtyaṃ tasya tad eva cāyatanam. evam anantaṃ vijñānaṃ nāsti kiṃcid iti tadākārād vijñānānaṃtyāyatanam ākiṃcanyāyatanaṃ cocyate. saṃjñā gaṇḍaḥ saṃjñā śalyaḥ āsaṃjñikaṃ sammoha iti saṃjnāmāndyotpatter naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam ity ucyate. na tv eṣāṃ deśakṛtam anuttarādharyam ity adeśasthatvāt.
body.translated_text: thus. Rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>) is the occurrence of aggregates in a new birth, accomplished by <s>karma</s>. By that [rebirth], the formless realm is fourfold — of four types. Namely, the sphere of infinite space — thus the elaboration. 'Space is infinite' — from the aspect [of meditation] at the time of the preparatory practice of the attainment, [there is] infinity of space; and that itself is its base (<s>āyatana</s>). Likewise, 'consciousness is infinite,' 'there is nothing' — from those aspects, [there are] the sphere of infinite consciousness and the sphere of nothingness. 'Perception is a disease, perception is a thorn, the unconscious [attainment] is a delusion' — from the arising of the diminishment of perception, it is called the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. But they have no spatial location — because of having no location.

body.text: yathā rūpiṇām iti vistaraḥ. kiṃkṛteyam āśaṃkā. iha nairātmye sati cittacaittānāṃ kāmarūpadhātvo rūpaniśrayā [Tib. 245a] pravṛttiḥ kalpyeta. ārūpyeṣu tu rūpaṃ nāstīti. tatra cittacaittapravṛttyā na bhavitavyam ity āśaṃkānivṛttyartham idam ucyate.
body.translated_text: 'Just as for material beings...' — thus the elaboration. What prompts this concern? In the absence of a self, the operation of mind and mental factors in the desire and form realms is conceived [Tib. 245a] as dependent on material [support]. But in the formless [realms] there is no form — therefore there should be no operation of mind and mental factors. To remove this concern, this is stated.

children.translated_text: 'Dependent on class-homogeneity (<s>nikāya</s>[-sabhāgatā]) and life-faculty (<s>jīvita</s>[-indriya]) here, the mental continuum' —

body.text: iti. caśabdena pṛthagjanatvasamanvāgamaprāptijātyādayaḥ saṃgṛhyaṃte. durbalatvād iti. kasyacit saṃtateḥ. rūpiṇāṃ sattvānāṃ durbalā cittasaṃtatir avibhūtarūpasaṃjñatvād vinā rūpeṇa na vartate. tato rūpaṃ niśritya vartate. tasyāḥ kena balavattvam iti. tasyā ārūpyāvacaryāḥ kena kāraṇena balavattvam. ata āha. samāpattiviśeṣajatvād iti vistaraḥ. vibhūtarūpasaṃjñeti. vigatarūpasaṃjñety arthaḥ. atas tajjā ārūpyā cittasaṃtatir api rūpanirapekṣā pravartate. tata eva tarhi balavattvāt samāpattiviśeṣajanitatvāt pravartiṣyate. kiṃcid aniśrityety abhiprāyaḥ. yathā rūpiṇām iti vistaraḥ. yathā rūpiṇāṃ rūpaniśrite nikāyasabhāgajīvitendriye. evam arūpiṇāṃ kiṃ niśrite iti vākyārthaḥ. tad etat dvayam anyonyam iti. nikāyasabhāgo jīvitendriyaṃ niśritya pravartate. jīvitendriyaṃ ca nikāyasabhāgam iti. kim arthaṃ na tad eva dvayam anyonyam iti. kiṃ rūpaniśrayeṇeti abhiprāyaḥ. tatredānīm iti. [Tib. 245b] tatrārūpyadhātau kena balavattvaṃ tayor nikāyasabhāgajīvitendriyayoḥ. tad etac cittasaṃtatau samānam iti. asāv api cittasaṃtatiḥ samāpattiviśeṣāj jātā bhavatīti na dvayaṃ niśritya pravartiṣyati. anāśritaiva pravartiṣyata iti. cittacaitteṣu vā samānam iti prakṛtaṃ. kiṃ punaḥ samānaṃ anyonyaniśrayatvaṃ. yathā nikāyasabhāgo jīvitendriyaṃ niśritya pravartate. jīvitendriyaṃ ca nikāyasabhāgaṃ niśritya pravartate. tathā cittaṃ niśritya caittāḥ pratvartiṣyaṃte. caittāṃś ca niśritya cittaṃ pravartiṣyata iti. tadanyāśrayakalpanā niḥprayojaneti. yasyāś cittasaṃtater iti vistaraḥ. cittasaṃtater ākṣepāya hetur ākṣepahetuḥ karmakleśalakṣaṇaḥ. vigatā tṛṣṇāsyeti vītatṛṣṇaḥ. na vītatṛṣṇo 'vītatṛṣṇaḥ. kva. rūpe. tasyāś cittasaṃtateḥ saha rūpeṇa saṃbhavād rūpaṃ niśrītya
body.translated_text: thus. By the word 'and,' ordinary-personhood, possession, <s>prāpti</s>, birth, and the like are included. 'Because of weakness' — of a certain continuum. The mental continuum of material beings is weak — because, not having overcome the perception of form, it does not operate without form. Therefore it operates dependent on form. 'By what is it strong?' — by what reason is that [mental continuum] of the formless realm strong? Therefore he says: 'because of being born from a special attainment' — thus the elaboration. 'Having overcome the perception of form' — meaning: having abandoned the perception of form. Therefore the formless mental continuum born from that also operates independently of form. 'Then, precisely because of that strength — because of being generated by a special attainment — it will operate' — the intent is: without depending on anything [material]. 'Just as for material beings...' — thus the elaboration. Just as for material beings, class-homogeneity and the life-faculty are dependent on form — similarly, for formless beings, on what are they dependent? — this is the meaning of the statement. 'Those two [depend] on each other' — class-homogeneity operates dependent on the life-faculty, and the life-faculty on class-homogeneity. 'Why not those same two on each other?' — the intent is: what need then for a material support? 'Now therein' — [Tib. 245b] therein, in the formless realm, by what are those two — class-homogeneity and the life-faculty — strong? 'That is the same for the mental continuum' — that mental continuum too, being born from a special attainment, will not operate dependent on the two, but will operate without support. 'Or it is the same for mind and mental factors' — this is the topic under discussion. 'What then is the same?' — mutual dependence. Just as class-homogeneity operates dependent on the life-faculty, and the life-faculty dependent on class-homogeneity, so too mental factors will operate dependent on mind, and mind dependent on mental factors. Therefore the postulation of another support is pointless. 'Of whatever mental continuum...' — thus the elaboration. The cause for the projection of the mental continuum is the projecting cause (<s>ākṣepahetu</s>), characterized by <s>karma</s> and afflictions. 'One from whom craving has departed' is one free from craving (<s>vītatṛṣṇa</s>). One not free from craving is <s>avītatṛṣṇa</s>. Where? With respect to form. Of that mental continuum — because of the possibility of [its existing] together with form — operating dependent on form

body.text: pravṛttiḥ. hetos tadvimukhatvād iti. ākṣepaheto rūpavimukhatvād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: is its operation. 'Because the cause is turned away from that' — meaning: because the projecting cause is turned away from form.

body.text: vajravālakavad iti. vajreṇa pratisaṃyukto vālako 'ṅgulīyakaḥ kaṭako vā vajravālakaḥ. maricapānakavac ca. yathā maricaiḥ pratisaṃyuktaṃ pānakaṃ maricapānakaṃ. madhyapadalopāt. tadvat. kāmapratisaṃyukto dhātuḥ kāmadhātur ityādiḥ. [Tib. 246a] rūpaṇīyo veti. bādhanīya ity arthaḥ. rūpayogāc ca sa śakyate bādhituṃ. tadbhāva ārūpyam iti. yadā dhātūttarapadam etad bhavati. tadārūpyadhātur iti yujyate. yadā tu niruttarapada ārūpyaśabdaprayogaḥ. tadyathā atikramya rūpāṇy ārūpyā iti. tadā ārūpā evārūpyā iti svārthe taddhitāt parigrahaḥ kāryaḥ. ārūpye vā sādhava ārūpyā iti paśyāmi. kāmānāṃ vā dhātur iti ṣaṣṭhīsamāsenaiva sādhayati vināpi pratisaṃyuktaśabdalopena. kaś cāsau kāmānāṃ dhātur ity āha. kāmān yo dadhātīti. evaṃ rūpārūpyadhātū veditavyāv iti. rūpāṇāṃ dhātuḥ rūpadhātur iti. rūpāṇi yo dadhātīti. ārūpyasya dhātur ārūpyadhātur ārūpyaṃ yo dadhātīti. kavaḍīkārāhāramaithunopasaṃhita rāga iti. kavaḍīkriyate iti kavaḍīkāraḥ. sa evāhāraḥ. kavaḍīkārāhāraḥ. mithune bhavo maithunaṃ. dvandvāliṃganādi. kavaḍīkārāhāramaithunābhyām upasaṃhitaḥ saṃbaddho janita iti vā kavaḍīkārāhāramaithunopasaṃhitaḥ. rāgaḥ kāmaḥ. kāmyate 'neneti kāma iti kṛtvā. katham evaṃ gamyata iti sthaviraśāriputrabhāṣitayā gāthayā tam arthaṃ darśayati.
body.translated_text: 'Like a diamond ring' — a ring or bracelet connected with a diamond is a <s>vajravālaka</s> (diamond ring). 'And like a pepper drink' — just as a drink mixed with pepper is a pepper drink, through elision of the middle word. Similarly, a realm connected with desires is the Desire Realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), and so on. 'Or that which can be molded (<s>rūpaṇīya</s>)' — meaning that which can be obstructed (<s>bādhanīya</s>). And through connection with form (<s>rūpa</s>), it can be obstructed. 'The state of being without that is formlessness (<s>ārūpya</s>)' — when this is the latter member of a compound with 'realm,' then <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (Formless Realm) is appropriate. But when the word <s>ārūpya</s> is used independently, as in 'having transcended forms, they are formless (<s>ārūpya</s>),' then one should understand it as a secondary suffix in the reflexive sense: 'formless ones are <s>ārūpya</s>.' Or I see it as: 'those who are good in the formless [realm] are <s>ārūpya</s>.' Or 'the realm of desires (<s>kāmānāṃ dhātuḥ</s>)' — this is established simply through a genitive compound, even without elision of the word 'connected.' And what is this realm of desires? He says: 'That which holds (<s>dadhāti</s>) desires.' Similarly, the Form and Formless Realms should be understood: the realm of forms is the Form Realm — that which holds forms; the realm of formlessness is the Formless Realm — that which holds the formless. 'Attachment connected with morsel-food and sexual intercourse' — what is made into morsels (<s>kavaḍīkriyate</s>) is <s>kavaḍīkāra</s>; that itself as food is <s>kavaḍīkārāhāra</s> (morsel-food). What arises in a couple is <s>maithuna</s> (sexual intercourse) — embracing in pairs and the like. That which is connected with, associated with, or born from morsel-food and sexual intercourse is <s>kavaḍīkārāhāramaithunopasaṃhita</s>. This attachment (<s>rāga</s>) is desire (<s>kāma</s>), taking it as 'that by which one desires is <s>kāma</s>.' How is this understood? He demonstrates that meaning with a verse spoken by the Elder <s>Śāriputra</s>:

body.text: Tib. 246b
body.translated_text: Tib. 246b

body.text: na te kāmā yānīti
body.translated_text: 'Those are not desires which...' —

body.text: vistaraḥ. ājīvakena yad uktaṃ gāthāṃtareṇa
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. What was said by the <s>Ājīvaka</s> in another verse:

children.translated_text: 'For a monk who entertains thoughts of desire, there is enjoyment of desires' —

body.text: iti. tad abhyupagataṃ sthavireṇa. trividho hi kāmopabhogaḥ. kāyena vācā manasā ca. tatrāvītarāgo manasā kāmopabhogitve 'pi sati nābhikṣur bhavati. kevalaṃ tv asya śīlam apariśuddhaṃ vartate. yas tu kāyena vācā tāthāgatīṃ śikṣāpadabandhalekhāṃ laṃghayitvā kāmāṃ paribhuṃkte. sa kāmopabhogy abhikṣur bhavatīti. tasmāt sa doṣāntaram āha.
body.translated_text: this was accepted by the Elder. For the enjoyment of desires is threefold: by body, by speech, and by mind. Among these, one not free from attachment who enjoys desires mentally does not become a non-monk; however, his moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) remains impure. But one who, by body or speech, having transgressed the binding rules of training established by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, enjoys desires — that one is an enjoyer of desires and becomes a non-monk. Therefore he states a different fault:

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. yadi tava
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. If according to your

body.text: rūpādayo viṣayāḥ
body.translated_text: objects such as forms and the like

body.text: iti pakṣaḥ śāstā te avītarāga ity abhyupagataḥ. tena
body.translated_text: this position would entail that the Teacher is not free from attachment. Therefore,

body.text: bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: would be —

children.translated_text:
'an enjoyer of desires,
having seen pleasing forms.'

body.text: kāyenāpy upabhuṃjāno 'pi tān viṣayān iti prasaktaṃ. na caivam iṣyate. tasmāt
body.translated_text: It would follow that even one who enjoys those objects with the body [would be an enjoyer of desires]. But this is not accepted. Therefore:

body.text: iti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: this is established.

body.text: kecaneti. kecid ity arthaḥ. nety āheti. pratiṣedhayati. yasmād dhātvantaradharmā dhātvantare samudācaraṃty adhātupatitāś ca. kāmadhātau hi traidhātukānāsravā dharmāḥ samudācaraṃti. evaṃ rūpadhātau kāmāvacaraṃ hi nirmāṇacittaṃ tatra samudācarati. ārūpyadhātāv ārūpyāvacarā [Tib. 247a] anāsravāś ca. tasmāt pratiṣedhayati neti. kiṃ tarhi. yeṣu kāmarūpārūpyarāgā anuśerate. yeṣu kāmarāgo 'nuśete ālaṃbanataḥ saṃprayogato vā yathāsaṃbhavaṃ. te kāmapratisaṃyuktāḥ. yeṣu rūpārūpyarāgāv anuśayāte. te yathākramaṃ rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktā iti. idam idānīṃ tad aśvabandhīyam iti. aśvaś cāśvabandhaś cāśvabandhaṃ. aśvabandham ivāśvabandhīyaṃ. atha vāśvabandhasyedam aśvabandhīyam aśvabandhīyam iti. kasyāyam aśvabandha iti kaścit pṛcchati. tasyetaraḥ kathayati. yasyāyam aśva iti. sa punaḥ pṛcchati. kasyāyam aśva iti. itaraḥ punaḥ kathayati. yasyāyam aśvabandha iti. ubhayam api na jñāyate. aśvabandho 'śva iti ca. yathedam ubhayam asiddhenānyonyena na paricchidyate. tathehāpi na rāgair dhātavaḥ sādhyaṃte. dhātubhiś ca rāgā ity ubhayam apy etan na sidhyati. kṛtanirdeśāni hi sthānāni kāmadhātāv iti.
body.translated_text: 'Some' — meaning certain ones. 'He says no' — he rejects [the view]. Because <s>dharmas</s> of one realm operate in another realm and are not confined to [their own] realm. For in the Desire Realm, <s>dharmas</s> of all three realms and the outflow-free operate. Similarly in the Form Realm — for the Desire Realm creation-mind (<s>nirmāṇacitta</s>) operates there. In the Formless Realm, [only] those belonging to the Formless Realm and outflow-free [dharmas operate]. Therefore he rejects [the view by saying] 'no.' Rather, those in which desire for <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Rūpa</s>, and <s>Ārūpya</s> lie latent (<s>anuśerate</s>) — those in which desire for <s>Kāma</s> lies latent, through the object or through association as the case may be — those are connected with desire (<s>kāmapratisaṃyukta</s>). Those in which attachment to <s>Rūpa</s> and <s>Ārūpya</s> lies latent — those are respectively connected with form and formlessness. Now this is like the 'horse-post' [illustration] — a horse and a horse-post together are 'horse-post.' Something like a horse-post is 'horse-post-like.' Or: this belongs to the horse-post, hence 'pertaining to the horse-post.' Someone asks: whose is this horse-post? Another answers: it belongs to the one whose horse this is. He asks again: whose horse is this? The other answers: it belongs to the one whose horse-post this is. Neither is known — neither the horse-post nor the horse. Just as here both are not delimited by each other which is unestablished, so too here the realms are not established by attachments, nor attachments by realms — both of these are not established. For the places taught [to belong to] the Desire Realm are:

children.text:
narakapretatiryañco manuṣyāḥ ṣaḍ divaukasaḥ
kāmadhātuḥ sa narakadvīpabhedena viṃśatir
children.translated_text:
'Hell-beings, hungry ghosts, animals, humans, and six celestial ones —
the Desire Realm, with divisions of hells and continents, is twenty' —

body.text: iti kāmadhātau kṛtanirdeśāni sthānāni. teṣu sthāneṣv avītarāgasya yo rāgaḥ. sa kāmarāga iti. evaṃrūpārūpyarāgāv iti. kṛtanirdeśāni hi sthānāni. kāmadhātor
body.translated_text: thus the places taught as belonging to the Desire Realm. Whatever attachment one not free from desire has toward those places — that is desire-attachment (<s>kāmarāga</s>). Similarly for attachment to form and formlessness. For the places taught for the Form Realm above the Desire Realm are:

children.translated_text: 'Above, seventeen places constitute the Form Realm' —

body.text: iti. teṣv avītarāgasya yo rāgaḥ. sa rūparāgaḥ. tathā kṛtanirdeśopapattir ārūpyadhātoḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Whatever attachment one not free from desire has toward those — that is form-attachment (<s>rūparāga</s>). Similarly, the taught rebirths of the Formless Realm:

children.translated_text: 'The Formless Realm is without location, fourfold by [mode of] rebirth' —

body.text: iti. teṣv avītarāgasya yo rāgaḥ. sa ārūpyarāga iti. yathāyogam iti. sthānanirdeśāpekṣaṃ. dhyānārūpyeṣu rāga iti. samāpattyupapattidhyāneṣu rāgo rūparāgaḥ. evam ārūpyarāgaḥ. nirmāṇacitte kathaṃ kāmarāga iti. kāmāvacare nirmāṇacitte dhyānaphale kathaṃ kāmavītarāgāṇāṃ kāmarāgaḥ yatas tasya kāmāvacaratvaṃ. yadā hy asāv avītarāgaḥ. tadā nirmāṇacittaṃ na samudācarati. yadā nirmāṇacittaṃ samudācarati. tadā na tasya rāga utpadyate.
body.translated_text: thus. Whatever attachment one not free from desire has toward those — that is formless-attachment (<s>ārūpyarāga</s>). 'As appropriate' — depending on the teaching of places. 'Attachment in <s>dhyānas</s> and formless [attainments]' — attachment to the <s>dhyānas</s> of attainment and of rebirth is form-attachment. Similarly for formless-attachment. 'How can there be desire-attachment in the creation-mind?' — in the creation-mind belonging to the Desire Realm, a fruit of <s>dhyāna</s>, how can those free from desire in the Desire Realm have desire-attachment, given that it belongs to the Desire Realm? For when one is not free from attachment, the creation-mind does not operate; and when the creation-mind operates, attachment does not arise in that person.

body.text: katham asya kāmarāgeṇa vinā kāmāvacaratvaṃ vyavasthāpyate ity arthaḥ. śrutvā parihāya ca tadāsvādanād iti. śrutvā tat parato nirmāṇacitte 'sya rāga utpadyate. parihāya vā ātmīyān nirmāṇacittāt. tasyāsvādanād iti. evaṃdhyāyinaḥ kāmāvacareṇa nirmāṇacittena kāmāvacaraṃ nirmāṇaṃ nirmiṇvantīti śrutvā tadālambano rāga utpadyate. anusmṛtya cātmīyaṃ tatra rāga utpadyate. nirmāṇavaśeneti. manoharaṃ nirmāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā [Tib. 248a] nirmāpake citte nirmāpakasya vā citte rāgaḥ darśayatītthaṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ yasyedṛśaṃ nirmāṇam iti. gandharasanirmāṇād veti. yat kāmāvacaranirmāṇanirmāpakaṃ. kāmāvacaraṃ tac cittaṃ. kāmāvacaradharmahetutvāt. ghaṭahetucittavat. yat tu na kāmāvacaraṃ. na tat kāmāvacaradharmahetuḥ. tadyathā rūpāvacaraṃ cittam. ata evāha. rūpāvacareṇa tayor anirmāṇād iti. kasmāt punaḥ rūpāvacareṇa cittena tayor gandharasayor anirmāṇaṃ. tayor gandharasayoḥ kavaḍīkārāhārasvabhāvatvāt. rūpadhātūpapannaṃ ca tadvītarāgatvād iti.
body.translated_text: The meaning is: how is its belonging to the Desire Realm established without desire-attachment? 'Having heard, or having set aside, through savoring that' — having heard about the creation-mind from others, attachment arises in this person. Or having set aside one's own [creation-mind]. Through savoring that — thus, having heard that meditators create Desire Realm creations with Desire Realm creation-mind, attachment arises having that as its object. And recollecting one's own [experience], attachment arises there. 'Through the power of creation' — seeing a captivating creation, attachment is shown in the creating mind or in the mind of the creator: 'such a creation-mind whose creation is like this.' 'Or from the creation of smell and taste' — whatever creates a Desire Realm creation, that mind belongs to the Desire Realm, because it is a cause of Desire Realm <s>dharmas</s>, like a mind that is the cause of a pot. But what does not belong to the Desire Realm is not a cause of Desire Realm <s>dharmas</s> — for example, a mind of the Form Realm. Therefore he says: 'Because of the non-creation of those two by the Form Realm [mind]' — why is there no creation of those two — smell and taste — by a Form Realm mind? Because smell and taste have the nature of morsel-food, and one reborn in the Form Realm is free from desire for them.

body.text: īṣādhāra iti. īṣāpramāṇavarṣādhāraḥ. nāsti vīcir vā antarikā veti. nairantaryaṃ darśayati. na tūktam ūrdhvam adhaś ceti. ato lokadhātūnāṃ tiryag evāsthānam iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: '<s>Īṣādhāra</s>' — a rain-bearer the size of a pole (<s>īṣā</s>). 'There is no wave or gap' — this shows continuity (<s>nairantarya</s>). 'But it was not said above and below' — thus he shows that the locations of world-systems are only laterally, not above and below.

body.text: (III.4) paṃcamyāś ca pradeśa iti. devagateḥ ṣaṭ kāmāvacarā devā uktāḥ. śeṣā rūpārūpyāvacarāḥ. anyathā hi gatisaṃbhedaḥ syād iti. gatimiśratā. yadi kuśalakliṣṭā api syuḥ gatisaṃbhedaḥ syāt. manuṣyo narakasamvartanīyaṃ karma karoti. yāvad devopapattisamvartanīyam. ity ato manuṣyagatir narakagatir api syāt. yāvad devagatir api. teṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ tadgatiparyāpannatvāt. kāmadhātūpapannaś cordhvabhūmikaiḥ kleśaiḥ samanvāgataḥ kāmāvacareṇa ca [Tib. 248b] sārvagatikena kliṣṭena samanvāgata iti. sa eva manuṣyo nārako yāvad deva iti syāt. sattvākhyā eveti. karmānurūpeṇātmabhāvatas tadgamanāt. ata evoktaṃ.
body.translated_text: (III.4) 'And a portion of the fifth' — of the divine destiny, six Desire Realm gods have been stated; the rest belong to the Form and Formless Realms.
