'Otherwise there would be confusion of destinies' — a mixing of destinies. If [destinies] were also wholesome and afflicted, there would be confusion of destinies. A human performs action conducive to hell-rebirth, up to action conducive to divine rebirth; thus the human destiny would also be the hell destiny, up to the divine destiny — since those actions are included in those destinies. And one born in the Desire Realm is endowed with afflictions of higher grounds and also with afflicted [dharmas] belonging to the Desire Realm that pervade all destinies. Thus that very human would be a hell-being up to a god. 'They are designated as sentient beings only' — because one goes to those [destinies] by self-existence in accordance with action. Therefore it was stated:

children.translated_text: 'According to their actions they will go, experiencing the fruits of merit and demerit' —

body.text: iti. na bhājanasvabhāvā iti. na cāntarābhavasvabhāvā iti. asya pratipādanārthaṃ jñāpakam ānayaṃti prajñaptiṣūktam iti vistaraḥ. sahetukāḥ sagamanā iti. hetuḥ karmabhavaḥ. gamanam antarābhavaḥ. gamyate 'neneti kṛtvā. gatis tu gamyata iti gatiḥ. taddhetoḥ karmabhavasya tābhyo bahiṣkaraṇāt. kuśalākuśalasya karmabhavasya tābhyo gatibhyo bahiṣkaraṇāt. kaśmīre bhavāḥ kāśmīrakāś ca sūtraṃ paṭhantīti. muktakaṃ tat sūtraṃ te eva paṭhanti nānya ity abhiprāyaḥ. nārakāṇām iti vistaraḥ. narakānukūlā nārakāḥ. teṣām iti vistaraḥ. kāyavāṅmanovaṃkānāṃ śāṭhyasamutthitānāṃ karmaṇāṃ doṣakaṣāyāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: thus. 'Not having the nature of the receptacle [world].' 'And not having the nature of the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>)' — to demonstrate this, they bring evidence, [saying] 'it is stated in the <s>Prajñapti</s>' — and so forth in detail. 'Having causes and having movement' — the cause is action-existence (<s>karmabhava</s>); movement is the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>), taking it as 'that by which one goes.' But destiny (<s>gati</s>) means 'that to which one goes.' Because of excluding from those [destinies] their cause, i.e., the action-existence, whether wholesome or unwholesome. 'Those in <s>Kaśmīra</s> are <s>Kāśmīrakas</s>, and they recite the sūtra' — the intent is that they alone recite that independent sūtra, not others. 'Of hell-beings' — and so forth in detail. Those suited to hell are <s>nāraka</s> (hell-beings). Of them — and so forth in detail — of bodily, verbal, and mental crookedness, of actions arisen from deceit, of the defilements of faults —

body.text: dveṣarāgasamutthitānāṃ. ato 'py anivṛtāvyākṛtā eva gataya iti. yasmād uktaṃ nirvṛtte vipāke nārake iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchatīti. gatiṣu sarve 'nuśayā anuśerata iti prakaraṇagranthaḥ parihāryaḥ. vaktavyaḥ parihāra ity arthaḥ. virodhaprasaṃgāt. yadi hi paṃca prakārā dharmā gatisvabhāvā bhaveyuḥ. evaṃ sarve 'nuśayā [Tib. 249a] anuśayīran. yadi tv anivṛtāvyākṛtā eva gatayaḥ syuḥ. evaṃ vaktavyaṃ syāt. bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ sarvatragāś ceti. anivṛtāvyākṛtā hi saṃskṛtā dharmā bhāvanāprahātavyā eva. teṣu ca bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ sarvatragāś cānuśayā anuśerate ālambanataḥ prayogato vā. nānye. tena jñāyate nānivṛtāvyākṛtā eva gataya iti. saṃdhicittāni hi gatīnāṃ paṃca prakārāṇīti. saṃdhicittāni gatīnāṃ praveśāḥ. teṣāṃ paṃcaprakāratvāt. duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaṃ yāvad bhāvanāprahātavyam iti. tatra sarve 'nuśayā anuśerata iti yuktaṃ. grāmopavicāragrahaṇavad iti. grāmaparisāmantakagrahaṇavad ity arthaḥ. paṃcasu kaṣāyeṣv iti. paṃca kaṣāyāḥ. āyuḥkaṣāyaḥ kleśakaṣāyo dṛṣṭikaṣāyaḥ kalpakaṣāyaḥ sattvakaṣāyaś ca. teṣu. kleśadṛṣṭikaṣāyau pṛthag uktau. kleśakaṣāyād dṛṣṭikaṣāyaḥ pṛthag ukta ity arthaḥ. anayoḥ pṛthagvacanaṃ gṛhasthapravrajitapakṣādhikārāt. gatihetujñāpanārtham iti. gatīnāṃ karmodbhavo hetur iti. antarābhave 'py eṣa prasaṃga iti. evam antarābhavo 'pi gatiś ca syāt. pṛthak cāsya vacanaṃ syāt gatigamanajñāpanārtham iti. gacchaṃti tām iti. karmasādhanaparigrahaḥ [Tib. 249b]. na cāntarābhava evaṃ yujyata iti na gatiḥ. ārūpyā apīti vistaraḥ. ārūpyā na gatiḥ syuḥ. cyutideśa evotpādāt. ārūpyagā hi yatra cyavante vihāre vā vṛkṣamūle vā yāvac caturthyāṃ dhyānabhūmau. tatraivotpadyanta iti. antarābhavavan na gatis syāt. evaṃ tarhīti. pūrvapakṣaṃ parityajya pakṣāṃtaram āśriyaṃte. gatyor antarā aṃtarāle bhavatīti aṃtarābhava ity anvārthasaṃjñākaraṇān nāntarābhavo gatir iti. vaibhāṣikā āhuḥ. yat tarhīti vistaraḥ. nirvṛtte vipāka iti vipākaśabdavacanād vipākasvabhāvā gatir iti tadabhiprāyaḥ. itara āha. nirvṛtte vipāke nāraka iti nārako vyavasthāpyate. na tūktaṃ vipāka eveti. na tūktaṃ vipākasvabhāvaiva gatir iti. kiṃ tarhi. vipākavipākasvabhāvā gatiḥ. tasmāt kuśalakliṣṭā api gatayo bhavantīty abhiprāyaḥ. vaibhāṣikaḥ punar āha. yat tarhy uktaṃ tatreti vistaraḥ. anyatra tebhyo dharmebhya iti. vipākajebhya ity abhiprāyaḥ. na tu skandhāntarapratiṣedhaṃ karotīty adhikṛtaṃ. tāś ceti vistaraḥ. avyākṛtatvapakṣe 'pi dvaividhyaṃ. aupacayikasvabhāvā apīti. apiśabdād vipākasvabhāvā apīti. yathoktaṃ
body.translated_text: of those arisen from hatred and passion. Therefore, the <s>gati</s>s (destinies) are exclusively unobstructed-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>). Because it was stated: 'When the retribution in the hells has ceased,' it falls under a [specific] enumeration. The <s>Prakaraṇa</s> treatise [which states] 'In the <s>gati</s>s, all <s>anuśaya</s>s (latent tendencies) lie latent' must be explained away. 'An explanation must be given' — this is the meaning. Because of the consequence of contradiction. For if <s>dharma</s>s of five kinds were the intrinsic nature of <s>gati</s>s, then all <s>anuśaya</s>s would lie latent [in them]. But if the <s>gati</s>s are exclusively unobstructed-indeterminate, then it should be stated thus: 'those to be abandoned by cultivation and the universally pervasive ones.' For unobstructed-indeterminate conditioned <s>dharma</s>s are exclusively to be abandoned by cultivation. And among those, only the <s>anuśaya</s>s to be abandoned by cultivation and the universally pervasive ones lie latent — through objectification or through application — not others. From this it is known that the <s>gati</s>s are not exclusively unobstructed-indeterminate. For the junction-minds (<s>saṃdhicitta</s>) of the <s>gati</s>s are of five kinds. The junction-minds are the entries into the <s>gati</s>s. Because they are of five kinds: from those to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, up to those to be abandoned by cultivation. There, it is fitting that all <s>anuśaya</s>s lie latent. 'Like the designation of a village-environs' — meaning: like the designation of the area surrounding a village. 'In the five <s>kaṣāya</s>s (degenerations)' — the five <s>kaṣāya</s>s are: degeneration of lifespan (<s>āyuḥkaṣāya</s>), degeneration of afflictions (<s>kleśakaṣāya</s>), degeneration of views (<s>dṛṣṭikaṣāya</s>), degeneration of the eon (<s>kalpakaṣāya</s>), and degeneration of beings (<s>sattvakaṣāya</s>). Among those, the degeneration of afflictions and the degeneration of views are stated separately. The degeneration of views is stated separately from the degeneration of afflictions — this is the meaning. The reason for their separate statement is the context of the household and renunciant sides. 'For the purpose of indicating the cause of the <s>gati</s>s' — the cause arising from <s>karma</s> is the cause of the <s>gati</s>s. 'This consequence applies to the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>) as well' — thus the intermediate existence too would be a <s>gati</s>. And a separate statement of it would be made, for the purpose of indicating the going to a <s>gati</s>. 'They go to it' — this involves the instrumental meaning of <s>karma</s>. [Tib. 249b] And the intermediate existence is not fitting in this way — therefore it is not a <s>gati</s>. 'The formless [realms] too' — and so on in detail. The formless [realms] would not be a <s>gati</s>, because arising occurs in the very place of death. For those going to the formless realms — wherever they die, whether in a monastery or at the foot of a tree, up to the ground of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> — they are reborn right there. Like the intermediate existence, [the formless realms] would not be a <s>gati</s>. 'In that case, then' — abandoning the prior position, they resort to an alternative position. Because of making an etymologically transparent designation: 'that which exists in the interval (<s>antarāla</s>) between <s>gati</s>s is the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>)' — the intermediate existence is not a <s>gati</s>. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s say: 'But then' — and so on in detail. 'When the retribution has ceased' — because of the word 'retribution,' the <s>gati</s> has the intrinsic nature of retribution — that is the intent. The other says: 'When the retribution in the hells has ceased' — by this, the hell-being is determined [as belonging to that <s>gati</s>]. But it is not said 'retribution alone.' It is not said that the <s>gati</s> has exclusively the intrinsic nature of retribution. What then? The <s>gati</s> has the nature of both retribution and retribution-nature. Therefore, wholesome and defiled [dharmas] too can be <s>gati</s>s — this is the intent. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> again says: 'But then' — and so on in detail. 'Other than those <s>dharma</s>s' — meaning: other than those of retribution-nature. But he does not make a negation of other <s>skandha</s>s — this is established. 'Those too' — and so on in detail. Even on the position that [<s>gati</s>s] are indeterminate, there is a twofold [classification]. '[They are] of the nature of augmentation (<s>aupacayika</s>) as well.' By the word 'as well,' of the nature of retribution too. As stated:

body.text: naiṣyandikās tu na gṛhyante. vipākasvabhāvā evety ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ pūrvam eva pakṣam icchati.
body.translated_text: but those of outflow-nature (<s>naiṣyandika</s>) are not included. The venerable <s>Saṃghabhadra</s> accepts precisely the former position — that [<s>gati</s>s] have exclusively the nature of retribution.

body.text: (III.5, 6ab) kāmāvacarāḥ ṣaṭ prathamadhyāṇikāś ca. katame te. bahirdeśakanayena brahmakāyikāḥ brahmapurohitā mahābrahmāṇaś ca prathamābhinirvṛttavarjyāḥ. kāśmīranayena punaḥ brahmakāyikā brahmapurohitāś ca prathamābhinirvṛttavarjyāḥ. brahmapurohiteṣy eva hi teṣāṃ nayena mahābrahmāṇo na sthānāntaranayāḥ. anekavarṇaliṃgasaṃsthānatvād iti. varṇo nīlatvādiḥ. liṃgaṃ vastrābharaṇādi. saṃsthānaṃ dairghyādi.
body.translated_text: (III.5, 6ab) The six belonging to the desire-realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>), and [those of] the first <s>dhyāna</s>. What are they? According to the system of the outsiders (<s>bahirdeśaka</s>): <s>Brahmakāyika</s>s, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>s, and <s>Mahābrahmā</s>s, excluding the first-born. According to the <s>Kāśmīra</s> system, however: <s>Brahmakāyika</s>s and <s>Brahmapurohita</s>s, excluding the first-born. For according to their system, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>s are included within the <s>Brahmapurohita</s>s — they are not a separate level. 'Because of having multiple colors, marks, and shapes' — color (<s>varṇa</s>) is blue and so forth. Mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is clothing, ornaments, and so forth. Shape (<s>saṃsthāna</s>) is tallness and so forth.

body.text: āroha unnatatā. pariṇāhas tiryakpramāṇaṃ. ākṛtivigrahaḥ ākṛtilakṣaṇo vigraha ākṛtivigrahaḥ. evaṃ viśeṣite vedānādīnāṃ vigrahaḥ paryudasto bhavati. nāsāv ākṛtilakṣaṇa iti. vigrahaḥ punaḥ śarīraṃ. vāgbhāṣā vāguccāraṇaṃ. katham idānīm iti vistaraḥ. prathamadhyānapratyāgamanena tair dvitīyaṃ tyaktam. tadbhūmikaṃ dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ. pūrvanivāsaṃ katham anvasmārṣuḥ. na tāvat prathamadhyānabhūmikena cittena tadaviṣayatvāt. na dvitīyadhyānabhūmikena tasyālabdhatvāt. punar labdham iti cet. ata āha. labdhāyāṃ ceti vistaraḥ. śīlavrataparāmarśadṛṣṭir mahābrahmālambanā prathamadhyānabhūmikaiva yujyate. sā ca dvitīyadhyānalābhāt prahīṇā na samudācarati. dvtīyadhyānabhūmiketi [Tib. 250b] cet. na. adharālambanatvāyogāt. na hy adharabhūmyālambanaḥ kaścid api kleśa iṣyate. antarābhavasthā adrākṣur iti. antarābhavasthās te taṃ mahābrahmāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvaivam ūcuḥ. imaṃ vayaṃ sattvam adrākṣmeti. ayam api pakṣo na ghaṭate. tathā hi tatrāpy antarābhave dīrgham adhvānam avasthātuṃ na saṃbhavaty upapattipratibandhābhāvāt śuklaśoṇitānapekṣatvāt. teṣāṃ kathaṃ bhavatīyaṃ buddhir imaṃ vayaṃ sattvam adrākṣma dīrghāyuṣaṃ dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhantam iti. dīrghādhvāvasthānāvabodho na prāpnotīty arthaḥ. tasmāt tatrasthā eveti vistaraḥ. prathamadhyānabhūmisthā eva tasya mahābrahmaṇaḥ pūrvavṛttāntaṃ samanusmarantaḥ utpadyamānāvasthāyām eva taṃ mahābrahmāṇaṃ pūrvotpannaṃ dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhantaṃ dṛṣṭavantaḥ. dṛṣṭvā ca paścād uttarakālam adrākṣmety eṣām babhūva. buddhir iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. evaṃ tu satīdam aparihṛtaṃ bhavet. asya ca sattvasyaivaṃ cetasaḥ praṇidhiḥ. vayaṃ copapannā iti. upapattipratilaṃbhikena prathamadhyānabhūmikena tasya mahābrahmaṇa evaṃ cetasaḥ praṇidhim anvasmārṣuḥ. samānabhūmikatvāt. ity adoṣa eṣaḥ. tatsakāśaṃ śravaṇād vā.
body.translated_text: Height (<s>āroha</s>) is tallness. Girth (<s>pariṇāha</s>) is lateral measurement. <s>Ākṛtivigraha</s> — a body characterized by form; thus <s>ākṛtivigraha</s>. When [this term is] thus qualified, the body of <s>Veda</s>-recitation and the like is excluded. It is not characterized by form — this is the meaning. 'Body' (<s>vigraha</s>) here means physical body. Voice (<s>vāgbhāṣā</s>) is vocal utterance. 'How then' — and so on in detail. By returning to the first <s>dhyāna</s>, they abandoned the second. 'Belonging to that ground' — belonging to the ground of the second <s>dhyāna</s>. How did they recollect their former existences? Not by a mind belonging to the ground of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, because that is not its domain. Not by one belonging to the second <s>dhyāna</s>, because that has not been obtained. 'If [you say] it was obtained again' — therefore he says: 'When it has been obtained' — and so on in detail. The view of attachment to mere rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśadṛṣṭi</s>), having <s>Mahābrahmā</s> as its object, is fitting only as belonging to the ground of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. And that is abandoned upon attaining the second <s>dhyāna</s> and does not operate. [Tib. 250b] 'If [it belongs to] the ground of the second <s>dhyāna</s>' — no, because of the impossibility of having a lower [realm] as object. For no affliction whatsoever is accepted as having a lower ground as object. 'Those in the intermediate existence state saw' — those in the intermediate existence state, having seen that <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, spoke thus: 'We have seen this being.' This position too does not work. For even in that intermediate existence, it is not possible to remain for a long time, because there is no obstruction to rebirth, and because [the intermediate being] does not depend on semen and blood. How would they have the cognition 'We have seen this being of long life, abiding for a long time'? The comprehension of abiding for a long time is not attained — this is the meaning. Therefore, 'those abiding right there' — and so on in detail. Those abiding right in the ground of the first <s>dhyāna</s>, recollecting the prior history of that <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, saw that <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, who had arisen previously, abiding for a long time — at the very time of their arising. And having seen [him], subsequently, at a later time, 'we have seen' — this cognition arose in them. 'Cognition' is the completion of the sentence. But if this is so, the following remains unresolved: 'And of this being, [there was] this intention of the mind.' With the mind belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground obtained at rebirth, they recollected the intention of that <s>Mahābrahmā</s>'s mind — because of belonging to the same ground. Therefore, there is no fault here. Or, because of hearing from him.

body.text: nanu ca śubhakṛtsneṣv apy eṣa prasaṃgaḥ. ekatvakāyā nānātvasaṃjñina iti. kathaṃ. yathoktaṃ. te hi maulyāṃ bhūmau sukhendriyaparikhinnāḥ
body.translated_text: But surely this consequence applies to the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>s too: 'having unitary bodies and diverse perceptions.' How? As stated: 'For they, in the principal ground, being wearied by the faculty of pleasure' —

body.text: sāmantakopekṣendriyaṃ saṃmukhīkurvaṃtīti vistareṇa [Tib. 251a] vaktavyaṃ syāt. te caikatvakāyā ekatvasaṃjñina iti paścād vakṣyate. tena sukheneti. tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikena. cetasa utplāvakatvād iti. audbilyakaratvāt. indrasukheneti dvitīyadhyāna. āgamavyapagamasaṃjñitvāt. aciropapannānām āgamasaṃjñitvāt. ciropapannānāṃ vyapagamasaṃjñitvāt. atha vāciropapannānām āgamasaṃjñitvāc ciropapannānām āgamavyapagamasaṃjñitvāt. bhītabhītasaṃjñitvāt. yathākramam aciraciropapannatvāt te nānātvasaṃjñinaḥ. na sukhāduḥkhāsukhasaṃjñitvāt yathoktaṃ vaibhāṣikair iti.
body.translated_text: they turn toward the faculty of equanimity of the preliminary [concentration]' — and so on should be stated in detail [Tib. 251a]. 'And they have unitary bodies and unitary perceptions' — this will be stated later. Therefore, 'by pleasure' — by that belonging to the third <s>dhyāna</s> ground. 'Because of causing the mind to surge' — because of causing elation. 'By the pleasure of <s>Indra</s>' — [refers to] the second <s>dhyāna</s>. 'Because of having perceptions of arrival and departure' — because those recently reborn have perceptions of arrival, and those long reborn have perceptions of departure. Or alternatively, because those recently reborn have perceptions of arrival, and those long reborn have perceptions of both arrival and departure. 'Because of having perceptions of fear' — because of being recently or long reborn respectively, they have diverse perceptions. Not because of having perceptions of pleasant, unpleasant, and neither-pleasant-nor-unpleasant — as stated by the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s.

body.text: prathame dhyāne kliṣṭayā saṃjñayeti. śīlavrataparāmarśasaṃparayuktayā akāraṇe kāraṇābhiniviṣṭatvāt. dvitīye kuśalayā saṃjñayeti. sāmantakamaulasaṃgṛhītatvāt. tṛtīye vipākajayā saṃjñayeti. vipākajasukhasaṃprayogāt.
body.translated_text: 'In the first <s>dhyāna</s>, by a defiled perception' — one conjoined with the attachment to mere rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>), because of being attached to a non-cause as a cause. 'In the second, by a wholesome perception' — because it encompasses both the preliminary and the principal [concentration]. 'In the third, by a maturation-born perception' — because of association with maturation-born pleasure.

body.text: ārūpyās trayo yathāsūtram iti. arūpiṇaḥ santi sattvā ye sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramād anantam ākāśam ity ākāśānaṃtyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharaṃti. tadyathā devā ākāśānaṃtyāyatanopagāḥ. iyaṃ paṃcamī vijñānasthitiḥ. arūpiṇaḥ santi sattvā ye sarvaśa ākāśānaṃtyāyatanaṃ samatikramyānaṃtyaṃ vijñānam iti vijñānānaṃtyāyatanam [Tib. 251b] upasaṃpadya viharaṃti. tadyathā vijñānānaṃtyāyatanopagā devāḥ. iyaṃ ṣaṣṭhī vijñānasthitiḥ. arūpiṇaḥ santi sattvā ye sarvaśo vijñānānaṃtyāyatanaṃ samatikramya nāsti kiṃcid ity ākiṃcanyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharaṃti. tadyathākiṃcanyāyatanopagā devāḥ. iyaṃ saptamī vijñānasthitir iti.
body.translated_text: The three formless [realms] as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are formless beings who, having completely transcended all perceptions of form, [enter] infinite space and, having attained the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), abide thus. Just like the gods who have been reborn in the sphere of infinite space. This is the fifth station of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>). There are formless beings who, having completely transcended the sphere of infinite space, [enter] infinite consciousness and, having attained the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>), [Tib. 251b] abide thus. Just like the gods who have been reborn in the sphere of infinite consciousness. This is the sixth station of consciousness. There are formless beings who, having completely transcended the sphere of infinite consciousness, [enter] nothingness and, having attained the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>), abide thus. Just like the gods who have been reborn in the sphere of nothingness. This is the seventh station of consciousness.'

body.text: paṃca skaṃdhāś catvāraś ca yathāyogam iti. ākāśānaṃtyāyatanāditrayapratisaṃyuktāś catuḥskandhāḥ. anyapratisaṃyuktāḥ paṃcaskaṃdhāḥ.
body.translated_text: The five <s>skandha</s>s and four [<s>skandha</s>s], as appropriate: those associated with the triad beginning with the sphere of infinite space consist of four <s>skandha</s>s. Those associated with others consist of five <s>skandha</s>s.

body.text:
iti. paribhidyate 'neneti paribhedaḥ. tasya vijñānasya paribhedas tatparibhedaḥ. so 'smin vidyata iti tatparibhedavat. śeṣaṃ durgatyādi. apāyeṣu cobhayaṃ nāstīti. nehasathānāṃ gaṃtukāmatā. na tatrasthānāṃ vyuccalitukāmatā. apaṭupracāratvād iti. cittacaittānām atra mandapracāratvāt. abalavad vijñānaṃ na tiṣṭhatīti yuktaṃ vaktuṃ.
(III.6cd, 7ab) bhavāgrāsaṃjñisattvāś ca sattvāvāsā naveti.
body.translated_text:
thus. That by which [consciousness] is subdivided is the subdivision (<s>paribheda</s>). The subdivision of that consciousness is its subdivision (<s>tatparibheda</s>). That which has this [subdivision] is 'having that subdivision' (<s>tatparibhedavat</s>). The remainder — the unfortunate destinies and so forth. 'And in the lower realms, neither [exists]' — those dwelling there have no desire to go [elsewhere], and those dwelling [elsewhere] have no desire to move to there. 'Because of dull functioning' — because of the dull functioning of mind and mental factors there. 'It is fitting to say that consciousness, being weak, does not remain [as a station]' —
(III.6cd, 7ab) '<s>Bhavāgra</s> (the peak of existence) and the <s>asaṃjñisattva</s>s (non-percipient beings) are <s>sattvāvāsa</s>s (abodes of beings) — nine' —

body.text: sūtra uktaṃ. nava sattvāvāsāḥ. katame nava. rūpiṇaḥ santi sattvā nānātvakāyā nānātvasaṃjñinaḥ. tadyathā manuṣyāḥ tadekatyāś ca devāḥ. ayaṃ prathamaḥ sattvāvāsaḥ dvitīyatṛtīyacaturthā api yathā vijñānasthitiṣu. tathā vaktavyāḥ. ayaṃ tu viśeṣaḥ. [Tib. 252a] rūpiṇaḥ saṃti sattvā asaṃjñino 'pratisaṃjñinaḥ. tadyathā devā asaṃjñisattvāḥ. ayaṃ paṃcamaḥ sattvāvāsaḥ.
body.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s> states: 'There are nine abodes of beings (<s>sattvāvāsa</s>). What nine? There are beings with form, having diverse bodies and diverse perceptions — such as humans and certain gods. This is the first abode of beings. The second, third, and fourth should also be stated as in the stations of consciousness.' But here is the distinction: [Tib. 252a] 'There are beings with form, non-percipient and without discrimination — such as the gods called non-percipient beings (<s>asaṃjñisattva</s>). This is the fifth abode of beings.'

body.text: ārūpyāṇāṃ ca sattvāvāsānāṃ trayo vijñānasthitivad vaktavyāḥ. caturthas tv ārūpyaḥ arūpiṇaḥ saṃti sattvāḥ sarvaśa ākiṃcanyāyatanaṃ samatikramya naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharaṃti. tadyathā devā naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanopagāḥ. ayaṃ navamaḥ sattvāvāsa iti. asaṃjñisattvebhyo ye 'nye caturthadhyānopagāḥ kiṃ te sattvāvāsā uta neti. nety āhuḥ. kasmād evam uktam ācāryeṇa ke punar anye. apāyā iti. mukhamātram etad uktaṃ. asaṃjñisattvāsaṃgṛhītāś caturthadhyānopagā ity api vaktavyam. ihāpi tad eva kāraṇaṃ vaktavyaṃ yad vijñānaṣthitiṣūktaṃ. ihasthānāṃ hy apāyagamanaprārthanā nāsti. tatrasthānāṃ ca na vastukāmateti. nāpāyāḥ sattvāvāsāḥ. asaṃjñisattvāsaṃgṛhīteṣu bṛhatphaleṣu yady apīhasthānāṃ gamanaprārthanāsti. tatrasthānāṃ pṛthagjanānām āsaṃjñikapravivikṣā bhavati. āryāṇāṃ tv anabhrakapuṇyaprasaveṣv api śuddhāvāsārūpyapravivikṣā. parinirvātukāmatā ca śuddhāvāsānām api. iti [Tib. 252b] na teṣāṃ tatrāvasthāne buddhiḥ. ato na te sattvāvāsā ity ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ. anye punar vyācakṣate. ke punar anye. apāyā iti apāyānām eva vacanād anabhrakādayaḥ sattvāvāsā iṣṭā ācāryasyeti. tair yuktir anveṣṭavyā. baṃdhanasthānavad iti. yathā baṃdhanasthānāni na sattvāvāsāḥ anicchāvasanāt. evam apāyā iti.
body.translated_text: And of the formless (<s>ārūpya</s>) abodes of beings (<s>sattvāvāsa</s>), three should be stated like the stations of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>). But the fourth formless [abode]: there are formless beings who, having completely transcended the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>), attain and dwell in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). Such as the gods who have reached the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. This is the ninth abode of beings. Are those belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> other than the non-percipient beings (<s>asaṃjñisattva</s>) abodes of beings or not? They say no. Why was it stated thus by the master? Who then are the others? The lower realms (<s>apāya</s>). This was stated only as a preliminary. It should also be stated that those belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> not included among the non-percipient beings [are not abodes of beings]. Here too the same reason should be stated as was stated regarding the stations of consciousness. For those dwelling here have no desire to go to the lower realms. And those dwelling there have no desire for material things. Therefore the lower realms are not abodes of beings. Among the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods not included among the non-percipient beings, even though those dwelling here have a desire to go [there], for ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) dwelling there, there is a desire to enter the state of non-perception. But for noble ones (<s>ārya</s>), even in <s>Anabhraka</s> and <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, there is a desire to enter the Pure Abodes (<s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>) or the formless realms. And even for those in the Pure Abodes, there is the desire for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Thus there is no intention to remain there. Therefore those are not abodes of beings — so says master <s>Saṃghabhadra</s>. Others, however, explain: who then are the others? The lower realms — by the statement referring only to the lower realms, the <s>Anabhraka</s> and the rest are accepted by the master as abodes of beings. They should seek the reasoning [for this]. Like a prison — just as prisons are not abodes of beings because of dwelling there unwillingly, so too the lower realms.

body.text: (III.7cd, 8ab) rūpopagā vijñānasthitir iti. vijñānaṃ tiṣṭhaty asyām iti vijñānasthitiḥ. upagacchatīti upagā. vijñānasya samīpacāriṇīty arthaḥ. rūpaṃ ca tad upagā ca sā rūpopagā. evaṃ yāvat saṃskārāś ca te upagā ca saṃskāropageti. bhagavadviśeṣas tu vyācaṣṭe. rūpopagā vijñānasthitir yāvat saṃskāropageti sautrāntikānāṃ nayenocyate. tatra vijñānasthitir bhavasaṃtatyanucchedaḥ. rūpam upagam asyā vijñānasthiteḥ. seyaṃ rūpopagā. upagam iti upagamyate tadātmīyata iti. evaṃ yāvat saṃskārā upagā asyā vijñānasthiteḥ. seyaṃ saṃskāropagā. atha vā tṛṣṇā sthitiḥ. tiṣṭhaty anayā vijñānaṃ. punarbhavasaṃtatyanucchedāt. iti kṛtvā vijñānasya sthitir vijñānasthitiḥ. sā rūpam upagacchati tadabhiṣvaṅgata iti rūpopagā. evaṃ yāvat saṃskāropagā. vaibhāṣikāṇāṃ punar nayena kārakārtho na śakyate yojayitum [Tib. 253a] iti dūṣayati. atra brūmaḥ. dvividhe 'py asmin vyākhyāne rūpādivyatiriktā vijñānasthitir uktā. tā hi
body.translated_text: (III.7cd, 8ab) 'The station of consciousness accompanied by form (<s>rūpopagā vijñānasthiti</s>)' — consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) abides in it, hence it is a station of consciousness. 'Accompanied' (<s>upagā</s>) means approaching — the meaning is: that which moves near consciousness. Form (<s>rūpa</s>) and that which is accompanied — [hence] accompanied by form. Similarly up to: aggregates (<s>saṃskāra</s>) and those accompanied — [hence] accompanied by aggregates. But master <s>Viśeṣa</s> explains: 'the station of consciousness accompanied by form' and so on up to 'accompanied by aggregates' is stated according to the <s>Sautrāntika</s> method. Therein, the station of consciousness is the non-interruption of the continuity of existence (<s>bhavasaṃtati</s>). Form is the accompaniment of this station of consciousness. This is accompanied by form. 'Accompaniment' means: it is approached, it is made one's own. Similarly up to: aggregates are the accompaniment of this station of consciousness. This is accompanied by aggregates. Alternatively, craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is the station — by it consciousness abides, because of the non-interruption of the continuity of renewed existence. Thus it is the station of consciousness. It approaches form through attachment to it — [hence] accompanied by form. Similarly up to accompanied by aggregates. But according to the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> method, the agent meaning cannot be construed — thus he criticizes. Here we say: in both these interpretations, a station of consciousness distinct from form and the rest has been stated. For those

body.text: iti
body.translated_text: thus

body.text: ity etat sarvaṃ nirastaṃ bhavatīti doṣāṃtaraṃ. tasmāt pūrvakam eva vyākhyānaṃ
body.translated_text: — all this would be refuted, which is an additional fault. Therefore the former interpretation alone

body.text: sādhu. etad vaibhāṣikavyākhyānaṃ varṇayāmo na tair evaṃ vyākhyātaṃ. rūpam upagacchatīti rūpopagā vijñānasthitir ityādi. apare punar vyācakṣate. rūpopagā vijñānasthitir iti. rūpasvabhāvety arthaḥ. yathānyatroktaṃ. khakkhaṭakharagatam iti. svabhāvārtho gatyartha ity abhiprāyaḥ. sthātuḥ parivarjanena. anyo loke sthātā devadattādir anyā sthitiḥ sthānaṃ gṛhādikam ity arthaḥ. vijñānaṃ vāhayati pravartayatīty arthaḥ. naunāvikanyāyena. yathā nāviko nāvaṃ vāhayati. tadvat. na tu vijñānaṃ vijñānam evābhirūhya vāhayatīty arthaḥ. ekasaṃtāne vijñānadvayāsamavadhānaṃ. parasaṃtānavijñānaṃ tu yady api yugapad bhavati. na tu taditarasya samīpe vartata iti na tat tasya sthitir bhavati.
body.translated_text: is correct. We are presenting this <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> interpretation, [saying] they did not explain it thus: 'it approaches form, hence the station of consciousness accompanied by form,' and so on. Others, however, explain: 'the station of consciousness accompanied by form' means having the nature of form. As stated elsewhere: '<s>khakkhaṭakharagatam</s>' — the intent is that the verbal root meaning 'going' conveys the meaning of 'nature.' By excluding one who stands — in the world, the one who stands, <s>Devadatta</s> and the like, is one thing, and the station, i.e. the standing-place such as a house, is another — this is the meaning. It carries, i.e. propels, consciousness — by the analogy of a boatman and a boat. Just as a boatman carries a boat, so too. But consciousness does not carry consciousness itself by mounting upon it — this is the meaning. In one continuum (<s>saṃtāna</s>), two consciousnesses do not co-occur. But consciousness of another's continuum, although it exists simultaneously, does not exist near the other, so it is not a station for it.

body.text: nandī saumanasyaṃ. sapta ca vijñānasthitayaḥ paṃcaskaṃdhasvabhāvāḥ tat katham iti. saptasu vijñānasthitiṣu paṃcaskaṃdhasvabhāvatveneṣṭāsu tat kathaṃ vijñānaṃ na vijñānasthitir [Tib. 253b] iṣṭam iti. evaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. abhedenaikapiṇḍarūpeṇa rūpādīnāṃ skaṃdhānām upapattyāyatanasaṃgṛhīteṣu skaṃdheṣu manuṣyādinikāyasabhāgasaṃgṛhīteṣu. sābhirāmāyāṃ sabhiratyāṃ. vijñānapravṛttau vijñānaṃ vijñānasthitiḥ saptavijñanasthitideśanāyām abhiprīyate. pratyekaṃ tv ekamekaṃ skaṃdhaṃ prati yathā rūpādayo vijñānasya saṃkleśāya bhavaṃti. āśrayasaṃprayogasahabhūbhāvenopagatatvāt. naivaṃ kevalaṃ pṛthag vijñānaṃ. kiṃ. saṃkleśāya bhavatīty adhikṛtaṃ. kasmāt. yugapadāśrayatvādyayogāt. tasmāc caturvijñanasthitideśanāyāṃ kevalaṃ pṛthag vijñānaṃ na sthitiḥ proktam. tathā vineyajanāpekṣayā hy ekatra sūtre 'nyathā vijñānasthitir uktā. anyatra cānyatheti. ata āha. api ca kṣetrabhāveneti vistaraḥ. vijñānasya kṣetrabhāvena catasro vijñānasthitayo rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārasvabhāvā deśitāḥ. vijñānaṃ bījabhāvena vapanīyarūpeṇa sopādānaṃ svabhūmikayā tṛṣṇayā satṛṣṇaṃ. kṛtsnam eva saṃtānagataṃ deśitam iti. na punar bījaṃ bījasya kṣetrabhāvena vyavasthāpayāṃ babhūva bhagavān. na hi loke bījaṃ kṣetrabhāvena vyavasthāpyate. ye ca dharmā iti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 254a] ye ca dharmā vijñānasya sahavartino rūpādayaḥ. ta eva kṣetrabhāvena sādhutarā bhavaṃti. sahavarti hi bījasya kṣetraṃ loke dṛśyate. vijñānaṃ tu vijñānena saha na vartate yugapadabhāvāt. atītānāgatās tarhi rūpādayo na vijñānasthitayaḥ prāpnuvaṃti. te 'py atītānāgatā yathāsvam atītānāgatānāṃ vijñānānāṃ sthitayo bbhavaṃti. tasmāt svabhūmau sarva eva sāsravā rūpādayo vijñānasthitayo bhavantīty avagantavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: <s>Nandī</s> means joy (<s>saumanasya</s>). And the seven stations of consciousness have the nature of the five aggregates — how then [is consciousness excluded]? When the seven stations of consciousness are accepted as having the nature of five aggregates, how then is consciousness not accepted as a station of consciousness? 'In that case' — and so forth in detail. In an undifferentiated, unified form, when the aggregates of form and the rest are included in the aggregates belonging to the sphere of rebirth, in the aggregates included in the class of beings such as humans — in a delightful, pleasurable [abode]. In the operation of consciousness, consciousness is a station of consciousness — in the teaching of seven stations of consciousness, this is intended. But individually, with respect to each single aggregate, just as form and the rest conduce to the defilement of consciousness — because they are approached as support, association, and co-existent [conditions] — consciousness alone, separately, does not [conduce] thus. What then? It is presupposed that [the question concerns] what conduces to defilement. Why? Because of the impossibility of simultaneously being a support and so on. Therefore, in the teaching of four stations of consciousness, consciousness alone, separately, is not stated as a station. Similarly, with regard to the beings to be trained, in one <s>sūtra</s> the station of consciousness is stated in one way, and in another, in another way. Therefore he says: 'Moreover, in the manner of a field' — and so forth in detail. The four stations of consciousness having the nature of form, feeling, perception, and formations are taught as a field for consciousness. Consciousness, in the manner of a seed, as something to be sown, with its basis (<s>sopādāna</s>), with craving (<s>satṛṣṇa</s>) belonging to its own ground — the entire [consciousness] belonging to the continuum is taught. But the Blessed One did not establish a seed as a field for [another] seed. For in the world, a seed is not established as a field. 'And whatever <s>dharma</s>s' — and so forth in detail. Whatever <s>dharma</s>s coexist with consciousness — form and the rest — they alone are more fitting as a field. For in the world, what coexists with a seed is seen as its field. But consciousness does not coexist with consciousness, because of the impossibility of simultaneity. Then past and future forms and the rest would not be stations of consciousness. They too, past and future respectively, are stations of past and future consciousnesses, each according to its own. Therefore, it should be understood that on one's own ground, all defiled forms and the rest are stations of consciousness.

body.text: prathamā koṭir iti vistaraḥ. saptasu yad vijñānam iti. paṃcaskaṃdhasvabhāvatvāt saptānāṃ vijñānasthitīnāṃ. tatra vijñānaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ. na catasṛṣu.
body.translated_text: The first alternative — and so forth in detail. Since the seven stations of consciousness have the nature of five aggregates, consciousness is included therein among the seven. But not among the four.

body.text: vijñānasya tatrāgrahaṇāt. vijñānavarjyāḥ skaṃdhā iti. apāyādiṣv api vijñānaṃ na catasṛṣu saṃgṛhītaṃ. na saptasu apāyādiṣu vijñānaparibhedenāgrahaṇāt. saptasu catvāraḥ skaṃdhā iti. saptasu vijñānasthitiṣu ye vijñānavarjyāś catvāraḥ skamdhā uktāḥ. te catasṛṣv api vijñānasthitiṣu saṃgṛhītāḥ. ubhayātrāpi saṃgṛhītāḥ ity tṛtīyā koṭiḥ. caturthy etān ākārān sthāpayitveti. apāyeṣu caturthe dhyāne bhavāgre ca yad vijñānam anāsravāś ca dharmāḥ.
body.translated_text: Because consciousness is not grasped therein — the aggregates excluding consciousness. Even in the lower realms and so on, consciousness is not included among the four — nor among the seven, because consciousness is not grasped through differentiation in the lower realms and so on. 'Among the seven, four aggregates' — the four aggregates excluding consciousness that are stated among the seven stations of consciousness are also included in the four stations of consciousness — included in both — this is the third alternative. The fourth: setting aside these aspects — consciousness in the lower realms, in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, in the peak of existence, and outflow-free <s>dharma</s>s.

body.text: (III.8cd, 9) yac caitad gatyādibhedabhinnam iti. ādiśabdena [Tib. 254b] bhājanāṃtarābhavabhūmyādir gṛhyate. jarāyur yena mātuḥ kukṣau garbho veṣṭitas tiṣṭhati. tasmāj jātā jarāyujāḥ. bhūtasaṃsvedajā iti. bhūtānāṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ saṃsvedād dravatvalakṣaṇāj jātā bhūtasaṃsvedajāḥ. avikalāś cakṣurindriyādyavaikalyāt. ahīnendriyāḥ kāṇavibhrāntāder abhāvāt. sarvāṅgair upetā hastapādādibhiḥ. sarvaiś ca pratyaṃgair aṃgulyādibhir upetāḥ. sakṛd upajāyaṃte. na kalalādyanupūrvyā aṇḍājādivat. upapādane upapattau sādhukāritvāt. śuklaśoṇitādyanupādānena sakṛd upajātatvāt. upapādukā ity ucyaṃte. krauṃcīnirjātāv iti vistaraḥ. bhinnayānapātrau kila vaṇijau samudratīre krauṃcīṃ samabhigatau. tato nirjātau śailopaśailau sthavirāv iti. paṃcālarājasyeti. tasya mahādevyāḥ paṃcāṇḍaśatāni jātāni. tena rājñā maṃjūṣāyāṃ prakṣipya gaṃgāyām avavāhitāni. licchavirājena sāṃtaḥpureṇa snāyatā sā maṃjūṣohyamānā dṛṣṭā udghāṭitā ca. tasyāṃ paṃcaśatāni dārakāṇāṃ dṛṣṭāni gṛhītāni ceti. māṃdhātṛprabhṛtayaḥ saṃsvedajāḥ. kathaṃ. upoṣadhasya kila rājño mūrdhni piṭako jātaḥ. tasya vṛddher anvayāt paripākānvayāt paribhedānvayād dārako jātah. so 'yaṃ māndhāteti saṃsvedajo bhavati. rājñaḥ khalv api māṃdhātur jānūpari piṭakau jātau [Tib. 255a] tayor vṛddher anvayāt pūrvavad yāvad dārakau jātau. tāv imau cārūpacārau. brahmadattasya kila rājña urasi piṭako jātaḥ. tasya vṛddher anvayāt pūrvavad yāvad dārikā jātā. seyaṃ. kapotamālinīti. āmrapāly api kadalīstaṃbhāj jāteti śrūyate. prāthamakalpikā iti.
body.translated_text: (III.8cd, 9) 'That which, differentiated by the distinctions of destiny and so on' — by the word 'and so on,' the distinction of vessel-world, intermediate existence, ground, and so on is grasped. The membrane (<s>jarāyu</s>) is that by which the embryo remains wrapped in the mother's womb. Born from that, they are womb-born (<s>jarāyuja</s>). Born from the moisture of the elements (<s>bhūta</s>), i.e. earth and the rest — born from moisture characterized by fluidity — they are moisture-born (<s>bhūtasaṃsvedaja</s>). Complete (<s>avikala</s>) means without deficiency of the eye-faculty and the rest. With unimpaired faculties — free from one-eyedness, bewilderment, and the like. Endowed with all limbs — hands, feet, and the rest. And endowed with all minor limbs — fingers and the rest. They arise at once — not through the successive stages of <s>kalala</s> and the rest like egg-born and other [beings]. In spontaneous arising (<s>upapādana</s>), because of being effective in rebirth. Because of arising at once without dependence on semen, blood, and the like, they are called spontaneously born (<s>upapāduka</s>). 'Born from the <s>krauñcī</s> bird' — and so forth in detail. Two merchants whose ship had broken apart reached a <s>krauñcī</s> bird at the seashore. Born from it were the two elders <s>Śailopśaila</s>. 'Of the king of <s>Pañcāla</s>' — his chief queen gave birth to five hundred eggs. The king placed them in a casket and cast them into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. A <s>Licchavi</s> king, bathing with his harem, saw the casket being carried along, opened it, and found five hundred boys inside, and took them. '<s>Māndhātṛ</s> and others are moisture-born.' How? On the head of king <s>Upoṣadha</s>, a boil appeared. Through its growth, through its ripening, through its bursting, a boy was born. He is <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, and thus he is moisture-born. On the knees of king <s>Māndhātṛ</s> himself, two boils appeared. Through their growth, and so on as before, two boys were born. These two are <s>Cāru</s> and <s>Upacāru</s>. On the chest of king <s>Brahmadatta</s>, a boil appeared. Through its growth, and so on as before, a girl was born. She is <s>Kapotamālinī</s>. <s>Āmrapālī</s> too is said to have been born from a plantain trunk. 'Of the first cosmic age' (<s>prāthamakalpika</s>) —

body.text: iti vacanāt. suparṇī garuḍaḥ. pretānāṃ jarāyujatvasiddhyartham ucyate. āyuṣmata iti vistaraḥ. kathaṃ gamyate jarāyujatvasiddhyartham iti.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. <s>Suparṇī</s> means <s>Garuḍa</s>. This is stated to establish that hungry ghosts (<s>preta</s>) can be womb-born. O venerable one — and so forth in detail. How is it understood that this is for establishing the womb-born nature [of hungry ghosts]?

body.text: vacanāt. nanu ca sutarām upapādukatvasiddhyartham iti gamyate. paṃca rātrau
body.translated_text: because of this statement. But would this not rather establish their spontaneous birth (<s>upapāduka</s>) nature? 'Five at night,

children.text: divā paṃca tathāparān. nāsti tṛptis tathāpi me
children.translated_text: five more during the day likewise. Yet there is no satiation for me' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. jarāyujair hi bhakṣitais tṛptir bhavet. jarāyujasiddhyartham eva. nopapādukasiddhyarthaṃ. rātrau paṃcānāṃ sakṛjjanma divā capareṣāṃ
body.translated_text: because of this statement. For if they were consumed as womb-born [beings], there would be satiation. This is indeed for establishing the womb-born nature, not for establishing spontaneous birth. The birth of five at night and of the other five during the day

body.text: paṃcānāṃ na virudhyate. tāvatkālena tadātmabhāvaparipūritaḥ. krameṇāpi ca rātrau paṃcānāṃ divāpareṣāṃ paṃcānāṃ janma na virudhyate. sattvajātiḥ sā tādṛśī karmaṇāṃ cāciṃtyo vipāka iti. abhipravṛddhajighāṃsādoṣatvāt tu nāpi tṛptir astīti.
body.translated_text: is not contradicted. In that much time, that particular bodily form is completed. And even sequentially, the birth of five at night and of the other five during the day is not contradicted. Such is the nature of that class of beings, and the ripening of actions (<s>karma</s>) is inconceivable. But because of the extremely developed desire to kill, there is no satiation.

body.text: prāptopapattivaśitvo 'pīty anena jarāyujopapattau karmabalātkārayogaṃ darśayati. yathānyatīrthyā apabhāṣanta iti. anyatīrthyā maskariprabhṛtayaḥ. yathoktaṃ nirgranthaśāstre ṛddhiṃ bhadanta ko [Tib. 255b] darśayti. māyāvī gautama iti. tathā bhagavantam evoddiśyānyatroktaṃ. kalpaśatasyātyayād evaṃvidho loke māyāvī prādurbhūya māyayā lokaṃ bhakṣayatīti. upajīvatīty arthaḥ. bāhyabījābhāvād iti. bāhyasya śukaśoṇitakardamāder abhāvād ity arthaḥ ādhiṣṭhānikīm iti. yad adhitiṣṭhati idam evaṃ bhavatv iti tad adhiṣṭhānaṃ. tat prayojanam asyās tatra vā bhavā ṛddhir ādhiṣṭhānikī. tām icchatāṃ bauddhānāṃ na yukta eṣa parihāra iti. katamaḥ. ya uktaḥ. śarīradhātūnām avasthāpanārtham iti.
body.translated_text: 'One who has attained mastery over rebirth' — by this, he shows the connection through the force of <s>karma</s> in womb-born (<s>jarāyuja</s>) birth. 'As the non-Buddhist teachers spoke disparagingly' — the non-Buddhist teachers are <s>Maskari</s> and others. As stated in the <s>Nirgrantha</s> scripture: 'Venerable one, who displays supernatural power? The illusionist <s>Gautama</s>.' Similarly, referring to the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself, it is stated elsewhere: 'After the passage of a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, such an illusionist appears in the world and, through illusion, devours the world' — the meaning is 'lives off [the world].' 'Because of the absence of external seed' — the meaning is: because of the absence of external [factors such as] semen, blood, mud, and the rest. 'Pertaining to supernatural determination (<s>ādhiṣṭhānikī</s>)' — that which one determines [thinking] 'let this be thus' is determination (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>). The supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) that has that as its purpose or that arises therein is '<s>ādhiṣṭhānikī</s>.' 'For <s>Buddhists</s> who accept that [type of supernatural power], this refutation is not valid' — which [refutation]? The one that was stated: 'for the purpose of preserving the bodily relics.'

body.text: praśnāt praśnāntaram utpadyata iti. atha kimarthaṃ caramabhaviko bodhisattva iti praśna ukto vistareṇa. tatra coktaṃ. śarīradhātūnām avasthāpanārtham iti vistaraḥ. tasmāt praśnād idaṃ praśnāntaram upajāyate. yady upapādukānām iti vistaraḥ. kāyanidhanaṃ kāyanāśaḥ. upapādukaḥ suparṇī upapādukaṃ nāgam iti viśeṣaṇadvayaṃ kimarthaṃ. kim anupapādukā api suparṇino nāgāś ca santi. santīty āhuḥ. caturvidhā hi garuḍā nāgāś cāṃḍajādibhedāt. teṣām upapādukā uttamāḥ. saṃsvedajā upottamāḥ. jarāyujā madhyāḥ aṇḍajā jaghanyāḥ. tatropapādukaḥ suparṇī sarvān upapādukādīn uddharati bhakṣārthaṃ. saṃsvedajas trīn saṃsvedajādīn. jarāyujo dvau jarāyujāṇḍajau. [Tib. 256a] aṇḍajo 'ṇḍajam eveti varṇayanti. yāvan na mṛta iti. yadā jīvati. tadā tan māṃsādi nāntardhīyata iti nidarśitaṃ bhavati. na punar mṛtasyāsya tṛpyatīti. na punar mṛtenānena tṛpyatīty arthaḥ. tṛpipūrau vibhāṣeti vibhāṣāṣaṣṭhīṣyate. tasya mṛtasyākāśasyeva bhakṣitasya mānsapiṇḍāntardhānān na tṛpyatīty avagantavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'From one question, another question arises' — thus. 'For what purpose does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his last existence...' — this question is stated in detail. And there it was stated: 'for the purpose of preserving the bodily relics' — in detail. From that question, this other question arises: 'If those of spontaneous birth (<s>upapāduka</s>)...' — in detail. '<s>Kāyanidhana</s>' means 'destruction of the body.' 'A spontaneously-born <s>Suparṇī</s> [seizes] a spontaneously-born <s>Nāga</s>' — what is the purpose of the double qualification? Are there also non-spontaneously-born <s>Suparṇīs</s> and <s>Nāgas</s>? They say: yes. For <s>Garuḍas</s> and <s>Nāgas</s> are of four kinds, due to the distinction of egg-born and the rest. Among them, the spontaneously-born are the highest; the moisture-born are next-highest; the womb-born are middling; the egg-born are the lowest. Therein, a spontaneously-born <s>Suparṇī</s> carries off all [Nāgas] — spontaneously-born and the rest — for the purpose of devouring. A moisture-born [Suparṇī carries off] three — moisture-born and the rest. A womb-born [Suparṇī carries off] two — womb-born and egg-born. [Tib. 257a] An egg-born [Suparṇī carries off] an egg-born one alone — thus they describe. 'As long as it has not died' — when it is alive, then its flesh and the rest do not disappear — this is what is demonstrated. 'But it is not satisfied by this dead [Nāga]' — the meaning is: it is not satisfied by this dead one. The sixth case-ending [genitive] is optional, according to the rule '<s>tṛpi</s>-root optionally takes the sixth.' Of that dead [Nāga], whose flesh-lump disappears like [vanishing into] space when devoured — one should understand that [the Suparṇī] is not satisfied.

body.text: sā hi dve gatī iti narakagatir devagatiś ca. tisṛṇāṃ ca pradeśa iti. tiryakpretamanuṣyagatīnāṃ.
body.translated_text: 'For that [spontaneous birth] is [found in] two destinies' — the hell-being destiny and the divine destiny. 'And in a portion of three' — of the animal, <s>preta</s>, and human destinies.

body.text: (III.10) gatyantarālatvāt. gatyor antarālatvāt. nanu cāvyākṛtaiva gatir iṣyate. upapattibhavaś caikāṃtena kliṣṭaḥ. maraṇabhavo 'pi kadācit kuśalaḥ kliṣṭo vā bhavati. na gatiḥ. kathaṃ tayor gatiśabdam adhyāropya gatyantarālatvād ity ucyate. naiṣa doṣaḥ. maraṇopapattibhavayor anivṛtāvyākṛtānāṃ nikāyasabhāgajīvitendriyajātyādīnāṃ
body.translated_text: (III.10) 'Because of being intermediate to the destinies' — because of being the interval between two destinies. Now, it is accepted that destiny itself is indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>). And the birth-existence (<s>upapattibhava</s>) is invariably defiled. The death-existence (<s>maraṇabhava</s>) too is sometimes wholesome, sometimes defiled — [but] not [the same as] destiny. How then can the term 'destiny' be superimposed on those two, and [the statement] 'because of being intermediate to the destinies' be made? There is no fault in this — because at the time of the death-existence and birth-existence, the indeterminate [dharmas] having the nature of destiny — <s>nikāyasabhāga</s> (class-homogeneity), <s>jīvitendriya</s> (life-faculty), <s>jāti</s> (birth-type), and the rest

body.text: gatisvabhāvānāṃ tatkāle vidyamānatvāt. kāmarūpadhātvoś ca kāyendriyasyāpy avaśyaṃ bhāvāt. na copapattivan maraṇabhavo 'vaśyaṃ kliṣṭo nāpy avaśyaṃ kuśalaḥ. tasmāt teṣu gatiśabdam āropya gatyaṃtarālatvād ity uktaṃ. pade gatyarthatvād iti. pada gatāv iti paṭhyate. tenopapannaśabdasyopagatārthaṃ darśayati.
body.translated_text: — which have the nature of destiny, exist at that time. And in the desire and form realms, the body-faculty (<s>kāyendriya</s>) too necessarily exists. Moreover, the death-existence is not necessarily defiled like the birth-existence, nor necessarily wholesome. Therefore, having superimposed the term 'destiny' on those, [the statement] 'because of being intermediate to the destinies' is made. 'Because the root <s>pad</s> has the meaning of going' — [the root] <s>pad</s> is read [in the grammar] as meaning 'going.' By this, he shows that the word '<s>upapanna</s>' (reborn) has the meaning of 'having arrived at.'

body.text: kiṃ tarhi. upapadyamāna iti. abhivyaktiḥ samāptiś ceti. ākṣepakeṇa karmaṇā nikāyasabhāgasyābhivyaktiḥ paripūrakaiḥ parisamāptiḥ. [Tib. 256b] sarvasmiṃ janmani karmadvayasya vyāpārāt.
body.translated_text: What then? 'Being reborn' (<s>upapadyamāna</s>). '<s>Abhivyakti</s>' (manifestation) and '<s>samāpti</s>' (completion) — manifestation of <s>nikāyasabhāga</s> (class-homogeneity) by the projecting <s>karma</s>, and completion by the completing [karmas]. [Tib. 256b] Because in every birth, both types of <s>karma</s> function.

children.translated_text: 'One [karma] projects a single birth; one or many are the completing [karmas]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. atha vā yatra deśe ākṣiptasya karmaṇā nāmarūpasya vipākasya prādurbhāvo 'bhivyaktiḥ. ṣaḍāyatanapūrtiś ca samāptiḥ. sa deśo 'vagantavyaḥ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Alternatively, manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) is the emergence of the maturation (<s>vipāka</s>) — the name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) projected by <s>karma</s> — in whichever place. And completion (<s>samāpti</s>) is the fulfillment of the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>). That place should be understood.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. saṃbadhnaṃs tānaḥ saṃtāno vrīheḥ saṃtāno vrīhisaṃtānaḥ. tena sādharmyād na vicchinnasya bhavasyodbhavo bhavati. yato 'paiti. yatra cotpadyate. tadantarālasaṃtānavartirūpapūrvakam upapattibhavarūpaṃ. svopādānarūpasaṃtānarūpasvabhāvatvāt. vrīhisaṃtānapaścāttararūpavat. saṃtānavartināṃ hi dharmāṇām avicchedena deśāntarotpattyā deśāntareṣu prādurbhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ. tadyathā vrīhisaṃtānasya. vrīhisaṃtānapaścāttararūpaṃ hi yato deśāntarād apaiti. yatra ca deśāṃtara utpadyate. tadantarālasaṃtānavartirūpapūrvakam utpadyate. kṣaṇikavādināṃ hy ayam asmākaṃ siddhāntaḥ. yadā grāmād grāmāṃtaraṃ nīyate vrīhiḥ. na sa viṛhiḥ pūrvatra grāme nirudhya tadgrāmāntarāle 'nutpadyamāno 'nekayojanāntarite 'pi grāmāntara utpadyate. kiṃ tarhi. nirantarākāśadeśotpādanirodhakrameṇotpadyate grāmāntare. tac ca svopādānarūpasaṃtānarūpasvabhāvaṃ. tathopapattibhavarūpam apy utpadyata iti. atrācāryaguṇamatiḥ saha śiṣyeṇācāryavasumitreṇa svanikāyānurāgabhāvitamatir vyākhyānavyāpāram apāsya pratyavasthānapara eva vartate. vayam iha śāstrārthavivaraṇaṃ praty [Tib. 257a] ādriyāmahe. na tad dūṣaṇaṃ. niḥsāratvāt bahuvaktavyabhayāc ca. bhaviṣṇur bhavanaśīlaḥ. vicchinno 'pīti vistaraḥ. ādarśādiṣu bimbāt pratibimbam iti. ādarśodakādiṣu bimbān mukhāt pratibimbaṃ mukhacchāyārūpaṃ vicchinnam utpadyamānaṃ dṛṣṭam ity anenānaikāntikatām udgrāhayati. pratisādhanaṃ vā karoti. yato 'paiti. yatra cotpadyate. na tadantarālasaṃtānavartirūpapūrvakam upapattibhavarūpaṃ. svopādānarūpasaṃtānarūpasvabhāvatvāt.
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration. That which binds the threads (<s>tāna</s>) is a continuity (<s>saṃtāna</s>); the continuity of rice is the 'rice-continuity.' By the analogy with that: the birth of existence does not occur for one whose [continuum] has been cut off. [Rather,] from where it departs and where it arises, the form of birth-existence (<s>upapattibhavarūpa</s>) — preceded by form belonging to the continuity in the interval — has the nature of the form of the continuity of one's own material basis (<s>svopādānarūpa</s>), like the subsequent form of the rice-continuity. For it is observed that <s>dharmas</s> belonging to a continuity, without interruption, manifest in other places through arising in other places — just as with the rice-continuity. For the subsequent form of the rice-continuity — from whichever other place it departs and in whichever other place it arises — arises preceded by the form belonging to the continuity in the interval. For this is our established doctrine, for us who maintain momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikavāda</s>): when rice is carried from one village to another village, that rice does not cease in the first village and then, without arising in the interval, arise in another village even though separated by many <s>yojanas</s>. Rather, it arises in the other village through a sequence of arising and ceasing in uninterrupted spatial locations. And that [process] has the nature of the form of the continuity of one's own material basis. Similarly, the form of birth-existence too arises [in this way]. Here, Master <s>Guṇamati</s>, together with his disciple Master <s>Vasumitra</s>, with a mind cultivated by attachment to his own school, setting aside the activity of commentary, is devoted solely to refutation. We here are concerned with the elucidation of the meaning of the treatise, not with that refutation — because it is without substance and because of the fear of excessive verbosity. '<s>Bhaviṣṇu</s>' means 'having the nature of becoming.' 'Even though cut off' — thus the elaboration. 'From a face [comes] a reflection in mirrors and the rest' — in mirrors, water, and the rest, from the face as original (<s>bimba</s>), a reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) — the image-form of the face — is observed arising as [something] disconnected [from the original]. By this, he raises the objection of inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatā</s>). Or he makes a counter-proof (<s>pratisādhana</s>): from where it departs and where it arises, the form of birth-existence is not preceded by form belonging to the continuity in the interval, [despite] having the nature of the form of the continuity of one's own material basis

body.text: pratibimbarūpavad iti. pratibimbaṃ nāmānyad evotpadyate dharmāntaram ity asiddham etad iti. bimbasāmarthyād eva tatrārśādiṣu pratibimbākāraṃ bhrāntaṃ vijñānam utpadyata ity ācāryasyābhiprāyaḥ. na tatra pratibhiṃbaṃ nāma kiṃcid astīty anena dharmyasiddhiṃ nāma dṛṣṭāntadoṣaṃ darśayati. tasmān nānaikāntatāsti. na caitat pratisādhanaṃ sādhv iti. siddhāv api ca satyām
body.translated_text: — like the form of a reflection. 'A reflection is indeed a different <s>dharma</s> that arises' — this is unestablished. The Master's intent is that, by the power of the original alone, a deluded consciousness having the appearance of a reflection arises there in mirrors and the rest — there is no such thing as a reflection [as a real entity]. By this, he shows the fallacy of the example called 'unestablished subject' (<s>dharmyasiddhi</s>). Therefore there is no inconclusiveness. 'And this counter-proof is not valid' — even if established,

children.translated_text: 'because of dissimilarity, it is not an illustration' —

body.text: iti. pratibimbasya dravyasattvena siddhāv api satyām asāmyād dārṣṭāntikenānidarśanam anudāharaṇaṃ pratibimbakam iti. kathaṃ tāvad asiddham iti. tāvacchabdaḥ krame. asiddhatāyuktiṃ tāvad darśayann āha.
body.translated_text: thus. Even if the reflection is established as a real substance (<s>dravyasattva</s>), because of dissimilarity [with the case at hand], the reflection is not an illustration (<s>anidarśana</s>), not an example, for the subject illustrated. 'How first is it unestablished?' — the word 'first' [indicates] sequence. Showing the reasoning for unestablishment first, he says:

children.translated_text: 'Because of the absence of two [things] together in one [place]' —

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. tatraiva hi ādarśadeśe ādarśarūpaṃ dṛśyate pārśvasthitena na pratibimbakaṃ. pratibiṃbakaṃ ca tatraiva dṛśyate 'bhimukhāvasthitena nādarśarūpaṃ. na caikatradeśe upādāyarūpadvayasyāsti [Tib. 257b] sahabhāvaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. āśrayabhūtabhedāt. āśrayabhūtāni hi taryor bhinnānīti. nāsty ādarśarūpāśrayabhūtair avaṣṭabdhe deśe pratibimbakarūpāśrayabhūtānāṃ tatrāvakāśaḥ. ato nopādāyarūpadvayasyāsti saṃbhavaḥ. tad evaṃ yugapad vijñānadvayasyābhāvāt. upādāyarūpadvayasya caikatra sahabhāvābhāvāt. na tat kiṃcid astīti darśayati. yatraiva hi deśe ādarśarūpaṃ dṛśyate. iti bhimbakaṃ ca tatraiva. na tv anyatra. ko doṣa ity āha. na caikatra rūpadvayasyāsti sahabhāva iti. pūrvavad vādcyaṃ. atha vā
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration. For in that very mirror-location, a person standing to the side sees the mirror-form, not the reflection. And the reflection is seen in that very [location] by a person standing facing it, not the mirror-form. And in one location, there is no coexistence of two derived forms (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>). What is the reason? Because of the difference in the bases of support. For the bases of support of those two are different. There is no room for the base-elements of the reflection-form in the location occupied by the base-elements of the mirror-form. [Tib. 257b] Therefore, there is no possibility of two derived forms [coexisting]. Thus, because of the absence of two cognitions simultaneously, and because of the absence of the coexistence of two derived forms in one place, he shows that that [reflection] does not exist as anything [real]. For in the very location where the mirror-form is seen, so too the reflection is [seen] in that very [location] — but not elsewhere. What is the fault [in this]? He says: there is no coexistence of two forms in one place — the same as stated before should be said. Alternatively,

children.translated_text: 'Because of the absence of two [things] together in one [place]' —

body.text: ity asya sūtrasyāyam arthaḥ. ekatra rūpe puruṣadvayasya paśyata evābhāvāt sahadarśanasya pratibimbam asiddham iti vākyadhyāhāraḥ. katham ity āha. digbhedavyavasthitaiḥ puruṣair ekair uttaradigvyavasthitair itarair dakṣiṇadigvyavasthitaiḥ. ekasmiṃ vāpyambudeśe ekasmiṃs taṭākajaladeśe. svābhimukhadeśasthitānāṃ rūpāṇāṃ dakṣiṇataṭordhvasthitāni rūpāṇy uttaradigvyavasthitapuruṣasvābhimukhasthāni uttarataṭordhvasthitāny api rūpāṇi dakṣiṇadigvyavasthitapuruṣasvābhimukhasthāni. teṣām ubhayeṣāṃ. kiṃ pratibimbakaṃ anyonyam upalabhyate. uttaradigvyavasthitair dakṣiṇataṭādhaḥ pratibimbakam upalabhyate. dakṣiṇadigvyavasthitair apy uttarataṭādhaḥ pratibiṃbakam upalabhyate. evam anyonyam upalabhyate. na tūbhayaṃ [Tib. 258a] yugapad upalabhyate iti vākyārthaḥ. na hi svataṭādhaḥ pratibiṃbakaṃ ekataṭasthaiḥ samantato 'pi vāpījalaṃ paśyadbhir upalabhyate. tataḥ kim iti ced ata āha. na tv ekatra rūpe ghaṭe paṭe vā dvayoḥ paśyatoḥ puruṣayoḥ sahadarśanaṃ
body.translated_text: the meaning of this <s>sūtra</s> is as follows: because of the absence of two persons simultaneously seeing one [and the same] form — [that is,] the absence of simultaneous seeing — the reflection is unestablished. This is the sentence-completion to be supplied. How? He says: by persons stationed in different directions — some stationed in the northern direction, others stationed in the southern direction — in a single pool-water location, in a single pond-water location: the forms situated in one's own facing direction — the forms above the southern bank are facing persons stationed in the northern direction, and the forms above the northern bank too are facing persons stationed in the southern direction — of both those [groups of forms], is the reflection mutually perceived? By those stationed in the northern direction, a reflection is perceived below the southern bank. By those stationed in the southern direction too, a reflection is perceived below the northern bank. Thus it is mutually perceived. But both [reflections] [Tib. 258a] are not perceived simultaneously — this is the meaning of the sentence. For a reflection below one's own bank is not perceived by those standing on one bank, even when looking at the pond-water all around. What follows from this? Therefore he says: but in one form — whether a pot or a cloth — there is no simultaneous seeing by two observing persons

body.text: na bhavati. bhavaty evety arthaḥ. iha tu na bhavati sahadarśanam ity ato na tatra rūpāntarotpattir yukteti. atha vāsyāyam arthaḥ. chāyātapayoś ca dvayos sahaikatrabhāvo na dṛṣṭo loke. yatra chāyā bhavati maṇḍape 'nyatra vā. na tatrātapaḥ. yatra vātapo bhavaty abhyavakāśe. na tatra chāyā. upalabhyate ca chāyāstha ādarśe sūryasya pratibimbakam iti. kathaṃ. taṭāke sūryapratibiṃbakam utpadyate. tattaṭākataṭasthe ca chāyāvati maṇḍape ādarśaḥ sthāpyate. tatrādarśake taṭākasthasya sūryapratibiṃbakasyāparaṃ pratibiṃbakam utpadyate. taṭāke ca yat sūryapratibhimbakaṃ. tat sūryasamuttham ity avaśyam. ātapasvabhāvam ity abhyupagaṃtavyaṃ. yac cāparam ādarśe pratibimbakaṃ. tad ātapasvabhāvapratibiṃbakasamuttham ity etad apy avaśyam ātapasvabhāvam abhyupagaṃtavyam. evaṃ sati chāyātapayoḥ sahasvabhāvaḥ syāt. na cānyatra loke chāyātapayoḥ sahabhāva iti. na yukto 'sya pratibiṃbakasya tatra prādurbhāvaḥ. kūpa ivodakam iti. yathā kūpe dūrāntargatam udakam [Tib. 258b] dṛśyate. tathā candrapratibimbakam apy atraivāntargataṃ dṛśyate. na cādarśas tāvad vastuphalo 'sti. tac ca tatrotpadyamānaṃ. tac ca pratibiṃbakam ādaśa evotpadyamānaṃ. nānyatrādhastād upalabhyeta. upalabhyate ca. ato nāsty eva tat kiṃcit. sāmagryās tu bimbādarśādilakṣaṇāyāḥ. sa tasyāḥ prabhāvo yat tathā darśanaṃ bhavati. acintyo hi dharmāṇāṃ śaktibhedaḥ. ayaso 'yaskāntābhigamanadarśanāt. na kāṣṭhādīnāṃ yathā. candrakāntāc candrodaye 'psaṃbhavaprakṣaraṇadarśanaṃ. nāṃgārādīnām. ity evamādi vaktavyaṃ. ādarśasaṃtānasambaddhatvād iti. na biṃbasaṃtānabhūtaṃ pratibimbam. ādarśasaṃbaddhatvāt. ādarśarūpavat. sahabhāvāc ca. bimbasamānakālarūpāntaravat. tad evaṃ yathā maraṇabhavasyopapattibhavaḥ saṃtānabhūtaḥ. naivaṃ bimbasya pratibimbakam iti. sādhanānanvitaḥ pratibimbakadṛṣṭāntaḥ. vrīhisaṃtānapaścāttararūpadṛṣṭāntas tu svasaṃtānapūrvarūpasaṃtānabhūta iti. tasmād asāmyaṃ dṛṣṭāntasya pratibiṃbasya ceti.
body.translated_text: it does not occur. The meaning is: it does occur. But here simultaneous seeing does not occur — therefore the arising of a different form there is not proper. Alternatively, the meaning is this: the simultaneous coexistence of shade and sunlight — of both together — is not observed in the world. Where there is shade, in a pavilion or elsewhere, there is no sunlight. Where there is sunlight, in an open space, there is no shade. Yet a reflection of the sun is observed in a mirror placed in shade. How? A reflection of the sun arises in a pond. And in a shaded pavilion standing on the bank of that pond, a mirror is placed. In that mirror, another reflection of the sun's reflection that is in the pond arises. And the sun's reflection in the pond — because it has arisen from the sun — must necessarily be admitted as having the nature of sunlight. And the other reflection in the mirror — because it has arisen from a reflection having the nature of sunlight — this too must necessarily be admitted as having the nature of sunlight. This being so, there would be the co-presence of shade and sunlight. But the co-presence of shade and sunlight is not [found] elsewhere in the world — therefore the appearance of this reflection there is not proper. 'Like water in a well' — just as water deep within a well [Tib. 258b] is seen [as if nearby], so too the moon's reflection is seen as if located within [the mirror] itself. Moreover, the mirror is not an object that produces fruit. And yet [the reflection] arises there. And that reflection, arising in the mirror alone, would not be perceived elsewhere or below — yet it is perceived [as below]. Therefore it is nothing at all. Rather, from the assemblage characterized by the image, mirror, and the like — it is the power of that assemblage that such seeing occurs. For the distinction of powers among <s>dharma</s>s is inconceivable — from the observation that iron approaches a lodestone, not like wood, etc. From the observation that water drips from a moonstone at moonrise — not from embers, etc. And so on should be stated. 'Because of being connected with the mirror-continuum' — the reflection is not part of the continuum of the image; because of being connected with the mirror, it is like a form of the mirror. And because of co-existence, it is like a different form contemporary with the image. Thus, just as the birth-existence is part of the continuum of the death-existence — the reflection is not similarly [part of the continuum] of the image. The reflection-example is not accompanied by the proof. But the example of the subsequent form in the rice-continuum — [that form] is part of the continuum of the prior form of its own continuum. Therefore there is a dissimilarity between the example and the reflection.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. dvayenodayo dvayodayaḥ. tasmād bimbāc cādarśāc cety arthaḥ. yat pradhānaṃ kāraṇam ādarśādi. tad āśrityotpadyate pratibimbaṃ. ādarśādi hi pratibhimbasya pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ tadanuvidhānāt. tadyathā yady asis tiryagavasthito bhavati. pratibimbam api tiryag āyataṃ ca dṛśyate. yady [Tib. 259a] ūrdhvam avasthito bhavati. pratibimbam api tathaiva dṛśyate. na caivam upapattibhavasyāpi dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ saṃbhavaḥ maraṇabhavāc cānyataś
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration. 'The arising from the two' is <s>dvayodaya</s>. The meaning is: from both the image and the mirror. The principal cause — the mirror, etc. — dependent on that, the reflection arises. For the mirror, etc. is the principal cause of the reflection, because [the reflection] conforms to it. For example, if a sword is positioned horizontally, [Tib. 259a] the reflection is also seen as horizontally extended. If positioned vertically, the reflection is also seen in the same way. But it is not the case that the birth-existence too arises from two causes — from the death-existence and from another

body.text: ca pradhānabhūtād ādarśasthānīyāt. bāhyaṃ śuklaśoṇitaṃ pradhānakāraṇam iti cet. na. acetanatvāt. upapādukānāṃ ca tadabhāvāt. ato 'py ayam asamāno dṛṣṭāntaḥ. kim anena darśitaṃ bhavati. uktālitaviśeṣaṇe hetāv ayam atulyo dṛṣṭāntaḥ iti. katham iti. yato 'paiti. yatra cotpadyate. tadantarālasaṃtānavartirūpapūrvakam upapattibhavarūpam. advayotpannasvopādānarūpasaṃtānarūpasvabhāvatvāt. vrīhisaṃtānapaścāttararūpavad iti. tad evaṃ sati nāsya sādhanasyānaikāntikatā śakyam udgrāhayituṃ. nāpi pratisādhanaṃ kartum ity uktaṃ bhavati. āgamenāntarābhavasyāstitvaṃ sādhayann āha.
body.translated_text: principal [cause] standing in the place of the mirror. If [one says] 'the external semen and blood are the principal cause' — no, because they are non-sentient. And because they are absent for spontaneously born (<s>upapāduka</s>) beings. Therefore this example too is dissimilar. What has been shown by this? That this is an incomparable example with respect to the stated qualified reason. How? From where one departs and where one is born — the form of the birth-existence, preceded by a form existing in the intermediate continuum between those two, has the nature of a form belonging to the continuum of its own substratum, not arisen from two — like the subsequent form in the rice-continuum. This being so, neither the inconclusiveness of this proof nor a counter-proof can be established — this has been stated. Establishing the existence of the intermediate state (<s>antarābhava</s>) through scripture, he says:

body.text: svaśabdābhidhānād ity arthaḥ. naitat sūtraṃ tair āmnāyata iti. tair nikāyāntarīyaiḥ. kasmān nāmnāyate. tadāgameṣv abhāvāt. nikāyantarāgamaprasiddhaṃ kim iti na pramāṇaṃ kriyate. mūlasaṃgītibhraṃśena samāropitasūtrāśaṃkitatvāt. trayāṇāṃ sthānānām iti. trayāṇāṃ hetūnāṃ. mātā kalyā mātā nīrogā. ṛtumatī rajasvalā. tad etad ubhayaṃ prathamaṃ sthānaṃ bhavati. raktau saṃnipatitāv iti. maithunadharmaṃ kurvantau. idaṃ dvitīyaṃ sthānaṃ. gandharvaś ca pratyupasthita iti tṛtīyaṃ. skaṃdhabhedaś ca pratyupasthita [Tib. 259b] iti maraṇabhavaḥ. paṃcānāgāminaḥ sapta satpuruṣagatayaḥ pudgalanirdeśakośasthāne vakṣyaṃte. upapadyādayo 'pīti. upapadyā nāma te devā ity evamādayaḥ saṃprasajyante. sapta satpuruṣagataya iti. eta eva paṃcāntarāparinirvāyiṇaṃ tridhā bhittvā sapta bhavaṃti. tenāhāntarāparinirvāyiṇas traya uktāḥ kāladeśaprakarṣabhedeneti. kālaprakarṣabhedena deśaprakarṣabhedena ca yathāyogaṃ. sūtraṃ cātra paṭhyate. śrāvastyāṃ nidānaṃ. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma. sapta vo 'haṃ bhikṣavaḥ satpuruṣagatīr deśayiṣyāmy anupādāya ca parinirvāṇaṃ. tac chruṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuruta bhāṣiṣye. sapta satpuruṣagatayaḥ katamāḥ. iha bhikṣur evaṃ pratipanno bhavati. no ca syāṃ no ca me syāt na bhaviṣyāmi na me bhaviṣyati yad asti yad bhūtaṃ tat prajahāmīty upekṣāṃ pratilabhate. sa bhave 'smin na rajyate. sa bhave 'smin na sajyate. athottaraṃ padaṃ śāntaṃ prajñayā pratividhyati. tac cānena padaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtaṃ bhavati. evaṃ pratipannasya bhikṣoḥ kā gatiḥ syāt. kopapattiḥ. ko 'bhisaṃparāya iti syuḥ praṣṭāraḥ. tadyathā bhikṣavaḥ parīttaḥ śakalikāgnir abhinivartamāna eva nirvāyāt. evam eva tasya tāvan mānāvaśeṣam [Tib. 260a] aprahīṇaṃ bhavaty aparijñātaṃ. tasya tāvan mānāvaśeṣasyāprahāṇād aparijñānāt paṃcānām avarabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇād antarāparinirvāyī bhavati. iyaṃ prathamā satpuruṣagatir ākhyātā.
body.translated_text: the meaning is: because of designation by its own proper term. 'This <s>sūtra</s> is not transmitted by them' — by those of other schools. Why is it not transmitted? Because it is absent in their scriptures. 'Why is what is well-known in the scriptures of other schools not taken as authoritative?' — because of the suspicion that <s>sūtra</s>s may have been superimposed through the deterioration of the original collection. 'Of three conditions' — of three causes. 'The mother is healthy, the mother is free from disease' — she is fertile, menstruating. This both is the first condition. 'The two have come together in union' — they are performing the act of intercourse. This is the second condition. 'And a <s>gandharva</s> (intermediate being) is present' — this is the third. 'And a dissolution of aggregates is present' — [Tib. 259b] this is the death-existence. The five types of non-returners and the seven destinations of virtuous persons will be stated in the chapter on the exposition of persons. 'The <s>upapadya</s>s and others too' — statements such as 'those gods called <s>upapadya</s>' become relevant. 'The seven destinations of virtuous persons' — these same five types of intermediate-<s>parinirvāṇa</s> [practitioners], divided threefold, become seven. Therefore it is said: 'three types of intermediate-<s>parinirvāṇa</s> [practitioners] are stated, by the distinction of remoteness in time and place' — by the distinction of remoteness in time and remoteness in place, as appropriate. And a <s>sūtra</s> is recited here: Origin at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'I shall teach you, monks, seven destinations of virtuous persons and <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without substratum. Listen well and carefully attend — I shall speak.' What are the seven destinations of virtuous persons? Here a monk practices thus: 'May I not be, may it not be mine, I shall not be, it shall not be mine — what exists, what has come to be, I abandon' — and he obtains equanimity. He is not attached to this existence, he is not stuck in this existence. And he penetrates with wisdom the higher peaceful state. And that state has been directly realized by him. 'For a monk so practicing, what would be his destiny? What his rebirth? What his future?' — there may be questioners. Just as, monks, a small chip-fire that is turning back would be extinguished — even so, for him, a residue of conceit [Tib. 260a] remains unabandoned, uncomprehended. Because of the non-abandonment and non-comprehension of that residue of conceit, but because of the abandonment of the five lower fetters, he becomes one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate [state]. This is the first destination of a virtuous person declared

body.text: punar aparam bhikṣur evaṃ pratipanno bhavati. no ca syām iti pūrvavat yāvat syuḥ praṣṭāra iti. tadyathāyoguḍānāṃ vāyasphālānāṃ vā pradīptāgnisaṃprataptānām ayoghanena hanyamānānām ayasprapāṭikā utpataṃty eva nirvāyāt. evam eva tasya pūrvavat yāvat paṃcānām avarabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇād antarāparinirvāyī bhavati. iyaṃ dvitīyā satpuruṣagatiḥ. punar aparaṃ bhikṣur evaṃ pratipanno bhavati. pūrvavad yāvad ayasprapāṭikā utplutyāpatitvaiva pṛthivyāṃ nirvāyāt. evam eva tasya pūrvavat yāvad antarāparinirvāyī bhavati. iyaṃ tṛtīyā satpuruṣagatiḥ. punar aparaṃ bhikṣur evaṃ pratipanno bhavatīti pūrvavat yāvad ayasprapāṭikā utplutya patitamātraiva pṛthivyāṃ nirvāyāt. evam eva tasya pūrvavad yāvat paṃcānām avarabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇād upapadyaparinirvāyī bhavati. iyaṃ caturthī satpuruṣagatiḥ. punar aparaṃ bhikṣur evaṃ pratipanna iti pūrvavad yāvad ayasprapāṭikā utplutya parītte tṛṇakāṣṭhe nipatet. sā tatra dhūmam api kuryāt. arcir api saṃjanayet. sā tatra dhūmam api [Tib. 260b] kṛtvārcir api saṃjanayya tad eva parīttaṃ tṛṇakāṣṭhaṃ dagdhvā paryādāya nirupādānā nirvāyāt. evam eva tasya pūrvavad yāvat paṃcānām avarabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇād anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī bhavati. iyaṃ paṃcamī satpuruṣagatiḥ. punar aparaṃ bhikṣur evaṃ pratipanna iti pūrvavad yāvad ayasprapāṭikā utplutya mahati vipule tṛṇakāṣṭhe nipatet. sā tatra dhūmam api kuryāt. arcir api saṃjanayet. sā tatra dhūmam api kṛtvārcir api saṃjanayya tad eva mahad vipulaṃ tṛṇakāṣṭhaṃ dagdhvā paryādāya nirupādānā nirvāyāt. evam eva tasya pūrvavad yāvat paṃcānām avarabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāt sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī bhavati. iyaṃ ṣaṣṭhī satpuruṣagatiḥ. punar aparaṃ bhikṣur evaṃ pratipanna iti pūrvavad yāvad ayasprapāṭikā utplutya mahati vipule tṛṇākāṣṭhe nipatet. sā tatra dhūmam api kuryāt arcir api saṃjanayet. sā tatra dhūmam api kṛtvārcir api saṃjanayya tad eva mahad vipulaṃ tṛṇakāṣṭhaṃ dagdhvā grāmam api dahed grāmapradeśam api nagaram api nagarapradeśam api janapadam api janapadapradeśam api kakṣam api dāvam api dvīpam api ṣaṇḍam api dahet. grāmam api dagdhvā yāvad ṣaṇḍam api dagdhvā mārgāntam āgamya udakāntaṃ vālpaharitakaṃ yā pṛthivīpradeśam āgamya paryādāya [Tib. 261b] nirupādānā nirvāyāt. evam eva tasya pūrvavad yāvat paṃcānām avarabhgīyānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāt ūrdhvaṃsrotā bhavati. iyaṃ saptamī satpuruṣapatir ākhyātā. anupādāya parinirvāṇaṃ katamat. iha bhikṣur evaṃ pratipanna iti pūrvavad yāvat syuḥ praṣṭāra iti. tasyaivaṃ pratipannasya bhikṣor na pūrvasyāṃ diśi gatiṃ vadāmi na dakṣiṇasyāṃ na paścimāyāṃ nottarasyāṃ nordhvaṃ nādho nānuvidikṣu
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, a monk practices thus: "May I not be" — as before, up to "there may be questioners." Just as iron balls or iron filings, blazing and thoroughly heated by fire, when struck with an iron hammer — iron sparks fly up and are extinguished. Even so, for him — as before, up to — because of the abandonment of the five lower fetters, he becomes one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate [state]. This is the second destination of a virtuous person. Furthermore, a monk practices thus — as before, up to — iron sparks, having flown up and fallen, are extinguished upon the ground. Even so, for him — as before, up to — he becomes one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate [state]. This is the third destination of a virtuous person. Furthermore, a monk practices thus — as before, up to — iron sparks, having flown up, just as they have fallen on the ground, are extinguished. Even so, for him — as before, up to — because of the abandonment of the five lower fetters, he becomes one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth. This is the fourth destination of a virtuous person. Furthermore, a monk practices thus — as before, up to — iron sparks, having flown up, fall on a small [pile of] grass and wood. There they would produce smoke and generate flame. There, having produced smoke and generated flame, having burnt that small [pile of] grass and wood, consuming it, [the fire] is extinguished without fuel. Even so, for him — as before, up to — because of the abandonment of the five lower fetters, he becomes one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without exertion. This is the fifth destination of a virtuous person. Furthermore, a monk practices thus — as before, up to — iron sparks, having flown up, fall on a great and vast [pile of] grass and wood. There they would produce smoke and generate flame. There, having produced smoke and generated flame, having burnt that great and vast [pile of] grass and wood, consuming it, [the fire] is extinguished without fuel. Even so, for him — as before, up to — because of the abandonment of the five lower fetters, he becomes one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with exertion. This is the sixth destination of a virtuous person. Furthermore, a monk practices thus — as before, up to — iron sparks, having flown up, fall on a great and vast [pile of] grass and wood. There they would produce smoke and generate flame. There, having produced smoke and generated flame, having burnt that great and vast [pile of] grass and wood, they would also burn a village, a village district, a city, a city district, a country, a country district, a thicket, a forest, an island, a grove. Having burnt a village, up to having burnt a grove, reaching the end of a road, the end of water, a [place of] scanty vegetation, [Tib. 261b] or a tract of earth, [the fire] is extinguished without fuel, consuming [everything]. Even so, for him — as before, up to — because of the abandonment of the five lower fetters, he becomes one who goes upstream (<s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s>). This is the seventh destination of a virtuous person declared. What is <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without substratum? Here a monk practices thus — as before, up to — 'there may be questioners.' For that monk so practicing, I do not declare a destiny in the eastern direction, nor in the southern, nor in the western, nor in the northern, nor above, nor below, nor in the intermediate directions

body.text:
nānyatra. dṛṣṭa eva dharme niśchāyaṃ
