parinirvṛtaṃ śītībhūtaṃ brahmībhūtam iti. idam ucyate 'nupādāya parinirvāṇaṃ. sapta vo 'haṃ bhikṣavaḥ satpuruṣagatīr deśayiṣyāmy anupādāya ca parinirvāṇam iti yad uktam. idam etatprayuktaṃ. anye punar āhur iti vistaraḥ. āyuṣaḥ pramāṇaṃ. tasyāntaraṃ tasminn āyuḥpramāṇāntare 'parisamāpta āyuṣīty arthaḥ. devasamīpāntare vā. devānām antikaṃ devānāṃ samīpam. devasamīpaṃ gatasyāntare yaḥ kleśān prajahāti. so 'ntarāparinirvāyī. sa punar dhātugato vā parinirvāti. yaḥ kleśabījāvasthāyām upapannamātraḥ. asamudācārakleśa ity arthaḥ. saṃjñāgato viṣayasaṃjñāsamudācārāvasthāyāṃ yaḥ parinirvāti. dhātugatāc ciratareṇāyaṃ [Tib. 261b] parinirvāti. vitarkagato vā vitarkasamudācārāvasthāyāṃ yaḥ parinirvāti. ayam api saṃjñāgatāc ciratareṇa parinirvāti. tena trividho bhavaty antarāparinirvāyī yathoktena dṛṣṭāntatrayeṇa. prathamo vā nikāyasabhāgaparigrahaṃ kṛtvā jātamātra ity arthaḥ. yaṃ praty eṣa parīttaḥ śakalikāgnir iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ. dvitīyo devasamṛddhiṃ cānubhūya parinirvātīti. yaṃ praty eṣa dṛṣṭāntaḥ. tadyathāyasprapātiketi. tṛtīyo dharmasaṃgītim anupraviśya dharmasāṃkathyam anupraviśya parinirvāti. yaṃ praty eṣa dṛṣṭāntaḥ. tadyathāyasprapāṭikā utplutya pṛthivyām apatitvaiva nirvāyāt. tad evaṃ vināpy antarābhavena yathāntarāparinirvāyī bhavati. yathā ca tasya dṛṣṭāntatrayeṇa trividho bhedaḥ. tathā sādhitaṃ nikāyāntarīyaiḥ. tasmiṃ sādhite idaṃ codyeta yadi dharmasaṃgītim anupraviśya yaḥ parinirvāti. so 'ntarāparinirvāyīṣyate kīdṛśa upapadyaparinirvāyī bhaviṣyatīty ata āha. upapadyaparinirvāyī punaḥ prakarṣayuktāṃ saṃgītim anupraviśya parinirvātīti. prakarṣayogād utpattyartho bhavatīty abhiprāyaḥ. saṃgītianupraveśasāmānyān [Tib. 262a] naiṣa bhedo yujyata iti vacanāvakāśaṃ matvā punar āha. bhūyasā vāyur upahatyeti. āyuṣo bahu kṣayitvā parinirvātīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: ...and not elsewhere. 'In the visible dharma itself, with certainty, one who has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, become cooled, become one with <s>Brahman</s>' — this is called <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without clinging (<s>anupādāya</s>). What was stated: 'I will teach you, O monks, seven destinations of the good person and <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without clinging' — this is connected to that. 'Others, however, say' — and so forth in detail. 'The measure of lifespan' — its interval, meaning within that lifespan when the lifespan is not exhausted. Or 'within proximity to the gods' — the vicinity of the gods means near the gods. One who, in the interval of going near the gods, abandons the afflictions — that one is an <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa in the interval). Moreover, one attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> either in the element-gone state (<s>dhātugata</s>) — one who has just been reborn in the state of affliction-seeds, meaning without active afflictions. Or in the perception-gone state (<s>saṃjñāgata</s>) — one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the state where object-perception is active; this one attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> after a longer time than the element-gone. Or in the thought-gone state (<s>vitarkagata</s>) — one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the state where thought is active; this one too attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> after a longer time than the perception-gone. Thus the <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> is threefold, as illustrated by the three stated examples. The first, having obtained the <s>nikāyasabhāga</s> (homogeneous class), just born — this is the meaning. For this one, the illustration is 'the small ember-fire.' The second, having also experienced divine prosperity, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — for this one, the illustration is 'like an iron fragment falling.' The third, having entered the <s>dharma</s>-assembly, having entered <s>dharma</s>-discussion, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — for this one, the illustration is 'like an iron fragment that, having leapt up, would be extinguished even before falling to the ground.' Thus, even without an intermediate existence, one becomes an <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>. And the threefold division with the three illustrations has been established by those of other schools. Given that establishment, this objection could be raised: if one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> after entering a <s>dharma</s>-assembly is accepted as an <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>, what kind of <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa upon rebirth) will there be? Therefore he says: an <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> is one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> after entering an assembly of superior quality. The intent is that due to the superior quality, it takes on the meaning of 'after birth.' Thinking there is occasion to say 'this distinction is not logical due to the commonality of entering an assembly,' he further says: 'or having consumed much vital air' — meaning having exhausted much of the lifespan, one attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: ta eta iti vistaraḥ. ta ete sarve 'pi dhātugatādayas trayaḥ śakālikādibhir dṛṣṭāntair na saṃbadhyaṃte. kasmāt. deśagativiśeṣābhāvāt. deśagater viśeṣasyābhāvāt. na hy eṣāṃ deśagativiśeṣo 'sti. tatraiva deśe parinirvāṇāt. sūtroktānāṃ trayāṇāṃ dṛṣṭāntānāṃ daśagativiśeṣo 'stīti. naibhir ete sambadhyaṃte. ārūpyeṣv api ceti vistaraḥ. yadi caivam upapadyaparinirvāyiṇa evāntarāparinirvāyitvena vyavasthāpyeran. ārūpyeṣv api te tathaiva paṭhyeran. tatrāyuḥpramāṇāntare parinirvāṇāt. na caivam. ato naivaṃ sūtrārthaḥ. āyuḥpramāṇāntare vetyādiḥ. kathaṃ punar gamyate. nārūpyeṣv antarāparinirvāyī paṭhyata ity āha
body.translated_text: 'These very ones' — and so forth in detail. These three — the element-gone and the rest — are all not connected with the three illustrations of the ember and so on. Why? Because there is no distinction of spatial movement. Because there is no distinction in their spatial movement — for these have no spatial movement distinction, since they attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in that very place. But the three sūtra illustrations do have a distinction of spatial movement. Therefore these are not connected with those. 'And in the formless [realms] too' — and so forth in detail. If those who attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth were also to be established as <s>antarāparinirvāyins</s>, they would likewise be listed in the Formless Realms too, since they attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> within the lifespan interval there. But this is not so. Therefore the sūtra meaning is not thus — regarding the lifespan interval and so on. How then is it known that the <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> is not listed in the Formless Realms? He says:

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. dhyānaiś caturbhiś catasro daśikā sūtrārthānāṃ. prathamasya dhyānasyaikā daśikā yāvac caturthasyaikā daśikā. tāḥ kṛtvā.
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. Through the four <s>dhyānas</s>, four groups of ten for the sūtra meanings. One group of ten for the first <s>dhyāna</s>, up to one group of ten for the fourth. Having counted those,

children.translated_text: 'Groups of seven through the Formless [attainments], three' —

body.text: iti. ākāśavijñānākiṃcanyāyatanais tisraḥ saptikāḥ. tāsāṃ trayam. antarābhavābhāvād upapattisthānatrayābhāvena ca dvayābhāvāt. tat kṛtvā. naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanena [Tib. 262b]
body.translated_text: thus. Through the bases of Infinite Space, Infinite Consciousness, and Nothingness, three groups of seven — totaling three. Because of the absence of intermediate existence and the absence of two [types] due to the absence of three places of rebirth. Having counted those, with the base of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception —

body.text: teṣām eva trayāṇāṃ ūrdhvaṃ srotasaś cābhāvāt. tāṃ ca kṛtvā vargo bhavati
body.translated_text: Because of the absence of the upward-streamer among those very three [types]. Having counted that, the section becomes

body.text: baddha ity arthaḥ. katham. iha bhikṣur yair ākārair yair liṃgair yair nimittair viviktaṃ kāmair viviktaṃ pāpakair akuśalair dharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharati. sa na haiva tān ākārān tāni liṃgāni tāni nimittāni manasikaroti. api tu yat tatropalabhate rūpagataṃ vā vedanāgataṃ vā saṃjñāgataṃ vā saṃskāragataṃ vā vijñānagataṃ vā. sa tāṃ dharmān rogato manasikaroti. gaṇḍataḥ śalyato 'ghato 'nityato duḥkhataḥ śūnyato 'nātmato manasikaroti. sa tān dharmān rogato manasikṛtya yāvad anātmato manasikṛtya tebhyo dharmebhyaś cittam udvejayati uttāsayati prativārayati. sa tebhyo dharmebhyaś cittam udvejyottrāsya prativārya amṛte dhātāv upasaṃharati. etac chāṃtam etat praṇītaṃ. yad uta sarvopadhipratinisargas tṛṣṇākṣayo virāgo nirodho nirvāṇam iti. 1. etad eva ca sūtram uktvāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ. tasyaivaṃ jānata evaṃ paśyataḥ kāmāsravāc cittaṃ vimucyate bhavāsravād avidyāsravāc cittaṃ vimucyate. vimuktasya vimukto 'smīti jñānadarśanaṃ bhavati kṣīṇā me jātir uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmīti. 2. etad eva ca sūtram uktvā no tu vimucyate. api tu tenaiva dharmacchandena [Tib. 263a] tenaiva dharmasnehena tenaiva dharmapremnā tayaiva dharmābhiratyā antarāparinirvāyī bhavati. 3. na haivāntarāparinirvāyī bhavati. api tūpapadyaparinirvāyī bhavati. 4. na haivopapadyaparinirvāyī bhavati. api tv anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī bhavati. 5. na haivānabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī bhavati. api tu sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī bhavati. 6. na haiva sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī bhavati. api tūrdhvaṃsrotā bhavati. 7. na haivordhvaṃsrotā bhavati. api tu tenaiva dharmacchandena pūrvavat yāvat tayaiva dharmabhiratyā mahābrahmaṇāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. 8. na haiva mahābrahmaṇāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. api tu tenaiva dharmacchandena pūrvavat yāvat tayaiva dharmābhiratyā brahmapurohitānāṃ
body.translated_text: meaning bound together. How? 'Here a monk, by whatever aspects, by whatever marks, by whatever signs, secluded from desires, secluded from unwholesome dharmas, with thought, with examination, born of seclusion, with joy and happiness, having attained the first <s>dhyāna</s>, abides. He does not attend to those aspects, those marks, those signs. Rather, whatever he perceives there — belonging to form, or to feeling, or to perception, or to formations, or to consciousness — he attends to those <s>dharmas</s> as a disease, as a boil, as a dart, as a calamity, as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, as non-self. Having attended to those <s>dharmas</s> as a disease and so on up to non-self, he repels, frightens, and turns back his mind from those <s>dharmas</s>. Having repelled, frightened, and turned back his mind from those <s>dharmas</s>, he directs it toward the deathless element: this is peaceful, this is sublime — namely, the relinquishment of all substrates, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' 1. Having stated this very sūtra, this distinction [follows]: 'For one who thus knows, thus sees, the mind is liberated from the outflow of desire, from the outflow of existence, from the outflow of ignorance. In liberation, the knowledge and vision arises: I am liberated. Destroyed is birth, lived is the holy life, done is what was to be done, I know no further existence beyond this.' 2. Having stated this very sūtra — but he is not liberated. Rather, through that very <s>dharmacchanda</s> (desire for dharma), through that very dharma-affection, through that very dharma-love, through that very dharma-delight, he becomes an <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa in the interval). 3. He does not become an <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>, but rather an <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa upon rebirth). 4. He does not become an <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s>, but rather an <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa without effort). 5. He does not become an <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>, but rather a <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains parinirvāṇa with effort). 6. He does not become a <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>, but rather an <s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s> (upward-streamer). 7. He does not become an <s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s>, but rather, through that very <s>dharmacchanda</s>, as before up to dharma-delight, he is reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods. 8. He is not reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, but rather, through that very <s>dharmacchanda</s>, as before, he is reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> (Ministers of Brahmā) gods.

body.text:
devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. 9. na haiva brahmapurohitānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. api tu tenaiva dharmacchandena pūrvavat yāvat tayaiva dharmābhiratyā brahmakāyikānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. 10. iha bhikṣur yair ākārair yair liṃgair yair nimitair vitarkavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamād adhyātmasaṃprasādāc cetasa ekotībhāvād avitarkam [Tib. 263b] avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharati. sa na haiva tān ākārān tāni liṃgāni tāni nimittāni manasikaroti. api tu tatropalabhate pūrvavad granthaḥ. yāvad virāgo nirodho nirvāṇaṃ. 1. etad eva sūtram uktvā tasyaivaṃ jānata evaṃ paśyataḥ kāmāsravāc cittaṃ vimucyate. bhavāsravād avidyāsravāt pūrvavat yāvat kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmīti. 2. etad eva sūtram uktvā no tu vimucyate. api tu tenaiva dharmacchandena pūrvavat. yāvat tayaiva dharmābhiratyā antarāparinirvāyī bhavati. 3. na haivāntarāparinirvāyī bhavati. api tūpapadyaparinirvāyī bhavati. 4. na haivopapadyaparinirvāyī bhavati api tv anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī bhavati. 5. na haivānabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī bhavati. api tu sābhisaṃkāraparinirvāyī bhavati. 6. na haiva sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī bhavati. api tūrdhvaṃsrotā bhavati. 7. na haivordhvaṃsrotā bhavati. api tu tenaiva dharmacchandena pūrvavat yāvat tayaiva dharmābhiratyā ābhāsvarāṇāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. 8. na haivābhāsvarāṇāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. api tu tenaiva dharmacchandena yāvat tayaiva dharmābhiratyā apramāṇābhānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. 9. na haivāpramāṇābhānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyāṃ upapadyate. api tu tenaiva dharmacchandena pūrvavad yāvat tayaiva dharmābhiratyā parīttābhānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. 10. iha bhikṣur yair ākārair yair liṃgair yair nimittaiḥ prītivirāgād upekṣako viharati. smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisaṃvedayate. yat tad āryā ācakṣate upekṣakaḥ smṛtimāṃ sukhavihārī tṛtīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharati. sa na haiva tān ākārāṃs tāni liṃgāni
tāni nimittāni manasikaroti pūrvavat [Tib. 264a] sarvāṇi sūtrāṇi. kevalaṃ tu nikāyasabhāgatāyāṃ viśeṣaḥ. na haivordhvaṃsrotā bhavati. api tu tenaiva dharmacchandena pūrvavad yāvad chubhakṛtsnānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. 8. na haiva śubhakṛtsnānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. api tenaiva pūrvavat apramāṇaśubhānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. 9. na haivāpramāṇaśubhānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upayadyate. api tu tenaiva pūrvavat parīttaśubhānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. 10. iha bhikṣur yair ākārair yair liṃgair yair nimittaiḥ sukhasya ca prahāṇād duḥkhasya ca prahāṇāt pūrvam eva saumanasyadaurmanasyayor
body.translated_text: 9. He is not reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, but rather, through that very <s>dharmacchanda</s>, as before up to dharma-delight, he is reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> (Brahmā-group) gods. 10. Here a monk, by whatever aspects, marks, and signs — through the subsiding of thought and examination, through internal tranquility, through one-pointedness of mind, without thought, without examination, with joy and happiness born of concentration — having attained the second <s>dhyāna</s>, abides. He does not attend to those aspects, marks, and signs, but rather perceives there, as before — the text [continues]. Up to dispassion, cessation, <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 1. Having stated this very sūtra — for one who thus knows, thus sees, the mind is liberated from the outflow of desire, from the outflow of existence, from the outflow of ignorance — as before up to 'done is what was to be done, I know no further existence beyond this.' 2. Having stated this very sūtra — but he is not liberated. Rather, through that very <s>dharmacchanda</s>, as before, up to dharma-delight, he becomes an <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>. 3. He does not become an <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>, but rather an <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s>. 4-6. [Similarly as before.] 7. He does not become an <s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s>, but rather, through that very <s>dharmacchanda</s>, as before up to dharma-delight, he is reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Radiant) gods. 8. He is not reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, but rather, through that very <s>dharmacchanda</s> up to dharma-delight, he is reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Apramāṇābha</s> (Immeasurable Radiance) gods. 9. He is not reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Apramāṇābha</s> gods, but rather, through that very <s>dharmacchanda</s>, as before up to dharma-delight, he is reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Parīttābha</s> (Limited Radiance) gods. 10. Here a monk, by whatever aspects, marks, and signs — through detachment from joy, abiding in equanimity, mindful and fully aware, experiencing happiness with the body, which the noble ones declare: 'one who is equanimous, mindful, and abides happily' — having attained the third <s>dhyāna</s>, abides. He does not attend to those aspects, marks, and signs — as before, all the sūtras [apply]. Only the distinction is in the homogeneous class: 7. He does not become an <s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s>, but rather, through that very <s>dharmacchanda</s>, as before, he is reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (Complete Beauty) gods. 8. He is not reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods, but rather, as before, he is reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> (Immeasurable Beauty) gods. 9. He is not reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> gods, but rather, as before, he is reborn in the homogeneous class of the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> (Limited Beauty) gods. 10. Here a monk, by whatever aspects, marks, and signs — through the abandonment of happiness and the abandonment of suffering, and even before, [through the disappearance of] mental pleasure and mental pain —

body.text: astaṃgamāt. aduḥkhāsukham upekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharati. sa na haiva tān ākārāṃs tāni liṃgāni vistareṇa sarvāṇi sūtrāṇi pūrvavad vaktavyāni. devanikāyopapattayas tu viśeṣyante. yāvat tayaiva dharmābhiratyā bṛhatphalānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. na haiva pūrvavat puṇyaprasavānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. na haiva pūrvavad anabhrakāṇāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. 10. iha bhikṣur yair ākārair yair liṃgair yair nimittaiḥ sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramāt pratighasaṃjñānāṃ astaṃgamāt [Tib. 264b] nānātvasaṃjñānām amanasikārāt anantam ākāśam ity ākāśānantyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharati. sa na haiva tān ākārān iti pūrvavat. kevalaṃ tu rūpagatam iti na paṭhitavyaṃ. tatra rūpābhāvāt. yāvan nirodho nirvāṇam iti. 1. etad eva sūtram uktvāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ. tasyaivaṃ jānata iti pūrvavat yāvan nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmīti. 2. etad evoktvā no vimucyate. api tu tenaiva dharmacchandena yāvat tayaiva dharmābhiratyā upapadyaparinirvāyī bhavati. 3. na haivopapadyaparinirvāyī bhavati. api tu tenaiva yāvad anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī bhavati. 4. na haivānabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī bhavatīti sarvam uktvā yāvad ūrdhvaṃsrotā na bhavati. api tu tenaiva pūrvavat. yāvat tayaiva dharmābhiratyā ākāśānaṃtyāyatanopagānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyate. 7. iha bhikṣur yair ākārair yair liṃgair yair nimittaiḥ sarvaśa ākāśānaṃtyāyatanaṃ samatikramyānaṃtaṃ vijñānam iti vijñānānaṃtyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharati. sa na haiva tān ākārān ity ākāśānaṃtyāyatanavat sapta sūtrāṇi vaktavyāni. kevalaṃ tu vijñānānaṃtyāyatanopagānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyām upapadyata iti viśeṣaḥ. 7. punar aparam iha bhikṣur yair ākārair [Tib. 265a] yair liṃgair yair nimittaiḥ sarvaśo vijñānānaṃtyāyatanaṃ samatikramya nāsti kiṃcid ity ākiṃcanyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharati. sa na haiva tān ākārān iti pūrvavat sapta sūtrāṇi. 7. punar aparam iha bhikṣur yair iti yāvat sarvaśaḥ ākiṃcanyāyatanaṃ samatikramya naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharati. pūrvavat sarvāṇi sūtrāṇi vaktavyāny ūrdhvaṃsrotasaṃ tv ekam apanīya. 6. tad evaṃ caturbhir dhyānair amṛtadhātucittopasaṃhāracittavimuktyantaropapadyānabhisaṃskārasābhisaṃskāraparinirvāṇordhvagamanatryupapattisthānopapattisvabhāvāś catasraḥ sūtrārthadaśikā uktāḥ. tribhis tv ādyair ārūpyair amṛtadhātucittopasaṃhāracittavimuktyupapadyānabhisaṃskārasābhisaṃskāraparinirvāṇordhvagamanopapattisthānopapattisvabhāvās tisraḥ sūtrārthasaptikāḥ. naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanenordhvagamanaṃ parihāya ṣaṭkikā coktā. ato yo 'sāv
body.translated_text: because of the cessation [of joy]. He enters and abides in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, which is neither painful nor pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness. 'He does not indeed [perceive] those aspects, those marks' — all the <s>sūtra</s>s should be stated in detail as before. But the rebirths among the divine classes are distinguished. Up to: 'through that very delight in the <s>Dharma</s>, he is reborn in the company of the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> (Great Fruit) gods. He is not [reborn] as before in the company of the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> (Merit-Born) gods. He is not [reborn] as before in the company of the <s>Anabhraka</s> (Cloudless) gods.' 10. Here, a monk, by whatever aspects, marks, and signs, having completely transcended all perceptions of form, with the cessation of perceptions of resistance, [Tib. 264b] with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, [thinking] 'space is infinite,' enters and abides in the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>). 'He does not indeed [perceive] those aspects' — as before. Only 'pertaining to form' should not be recited, because of the absence of form there. Up to: 'cessation is <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' 1. Having stated this very <s>sūtra</s>, here is the distinction: 'For one knowing thus' — as before, up to: 'I understand that there is no further existence beyond this.' 2. Having stated this very [sūtra], he is not liberated. But through that very desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, up to through that very delight in the <s>Dharma</s>, he becomes one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth (<s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s>). 3. He does not indeed become one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth. But through that very [desire], up to: he becomes one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without effort (<s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>). 4. He does not indeed become one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without effort — having stated all this, up to: he does not become one who goes upstream (<s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s>). But through that very [desire], as before, up to through that very delight in the <s>Dharma</s>, he is reborn in the company of the gods who have attained the sphere of infinite space. 7. Here, a monk, by whatever aspects, marks, and signs, having completely transcended the sphere of infinite space, [thinking] 'consciousness is infinite,' enters and abides in the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>). 'He does not indeed [perceive] those aspects' — as for the sphere of infinite space, seven <s>sūtra</s>s should be stated. Only the distinction is: 'he is reborn in the company of the gods who have attained the sphere of infinite consciousness.' 7. Furthermore, here a monk, by whatever aspects, [Tib. 265a] marks, and signs, having completely transcended the sphere of infinite consciousness, [thinking] 'there is nothing,' enters and abides in the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>). 'He does not indeed [perceive] those aspects' — as before, seven <s>sūtra</s>s. 7. Furthermore, here a monk, by whatever aspects, and so on up to: having completely transcended the sphere of nothingness, enters and abides in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). As before, all <s>sūtra</s>s should be stated, but removing one [relating to] going upstream. 6. Thus, through the four <s>dhyāna</s>s, four sets of ten <s>sūtra</s>-meanings have been stated, having the natures of: the <s>amṛtadhātu</s> (deathless element), mind-concentration, mind-liberation, being within [the interval], rebirth-<s>parinirvāṇa</s>, effortless-<s>parinirvāṇa</s>, effortful-<s>parinirvāṇa</s>, going upward, rebirth in three places, and rebirth-nature. But through the first three formless [attainments], three sets of seven <s>sūtra</s>-meanings, having the natures of: the <s>amṛtadhātu</s>, mind-concentration, mind-liberation, rebirth-<s>parinirvāṇa</s>, effortless-<s>parinirvāṇa</s>, effortful-<s>parinirvāṇa</s>, going upward, rebirth-place, and rebirth-nature. And through the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, removing going upward, a set of six has been stated. Therefore, the one who

body.text: antarāparinirvāyī. nāsāv āyuṣpramāṇāntarāparinirvāyīti yujyate vaktum. ārūpyeṣv api hy antarāmaraṇasaṃbhavaḥ.
body.translated_text: attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the interval (<s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>) — it is not fitting to say that he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the interval of lifespan. For even in the formless realms, premature death is possible,

body.text: iti vacanāt. tasmāt āgamato 'pi siddho 'ntarābhavo na kevalaṃ yuktita ity apiśabdaḥ [Tib. 265b]. dūṣīmāra iti. krakucchandasya tathāgatasya viduraṃ nāma śrāvakaṃ dūṣī nāma māras tadānīṃ śirasi muṣṭinābhighnan tenāṃgīkṛtaḥ. tatkṣaṇa eva ca svaśarīreṇaivāvīcau mahānarake prapatita iti. svaśarīreṇaiveti vacanān nāsty antarābhava ity abhiprāyaḥ. sa hi jīvann eva nārakībhir jvālābhir iti. jīvann evāsau māro narakotthitābhir agnijvālābhir āliṃgitatvāt svaśarīrāvasthāduḥkhotpatteḥ. svaśarīreṇaiva prapatita ity uktaḥ. na tu kālam akṛtvāntarābhavāvasthānaṃ. narakopapattibhavṝāvasthāṃ ca na gatavān ity abhiprāyaḥ. atyudīrṇaparipūrṇānīti. kṣetrāśayaviśeṣayogād atyudīrṇāni. upacitatvāt paripūrṇāni. samanaṃtaraṃ narakeṣūpapadyata iti. samanantaravacanān nāsty antarābhava ity abhiprāyaḥ. anyāṃ gatim agatveti. upapattyantarapratiṣedhaparam etad vākyaṃ. nāntarābhavapratiṣedhaparam ity abhiprāyaḥ. paṃcaiveti. yadi yathārutaṃ kalpyate. paṃcabhir evānantarryaiḥ kṛtaiḥ na tv ekena dvābhyāṃ vā narakagamanaṃ bhavatīty etat prāpnoti. paṃceti rutāt kriyānantaraṃ cānantaryakriyānantaraṃ ca narakeṣūpapanna iti prāpnoti. yāni kṛtvopacitya samanantaraṃ narakeṣūpapadyata iti rutān na kālāntaraṃ [Tib. 266b] jīvitvā. ko vāntarābhavasyopapadyamānatvaṃ necchatīti. viprakṛtāvasthāvacanāt. upapattyabhimukho hy upapadyamāna ity abhiprāyaḥ. na tu brūma upapanno bhavatīti. na tūpapadyata ity etat padam upapannārtham iti brūmaḥ. tasmād adoṣa eṣsḥ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Therefore, the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>) is established even from scripture, not merely from reasoning — this is [the meaning of] the word 'also.' '<s>Dūṣīmāra</s>' — [the story is:] <s>Dūṣī</s> by name, a <s>Māra</s> at that time, struck on the head with his fist the disciple named <s>Vidura</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Krakucchanda</s>, and was accepted by him. And at that very moment, he fell into the great hell <s>Avīci</s> with his own body. Because of the statement 'with his own body,' the intent is: there is no intermediate existence. [Reply:] For he, while still alive, [was engulfed] by the flames of hell-beings — while that <s>Māra</s> was still alive, being embraced by flames of fire arisen from hell, because of the arising of suffering while still in his own bodily state, it is said 'he fell with his own body.' But it is not that he did not die and [did not pass through] the state of intermediate existence, and did not go through the state of rebirth-existence in hell — this is the intent. 'Extremely intense and complete' — extremely intense because of the special conjunction of field and disposition; complete because of being accumulated. 'He is reborn in the hells immediately' — because of the word 'immediately,' the intent is: there is no intermediate existence. [Reply:] 'Without going to another destiny' — this statement is directed at negating rebirth in another [destiny], not at negating the intermediate existence — this is the intent. 'Only five' — if this is taken literally, the consequence would be that one goes to hell only when all five [acts of] immediate [retribution] have been committed, not by one or two. [Further,] from the literal meaning 'five,' the consequence would follow that immediately after committing the act and immediately after the act of committing, one is reborn in the hells. 'Having committed and accumulated, one is immediately reborn in the hells' — from the literal meaning, not after living for another interval of time. [Tib. 266b] But who does not accept that the intermediate existence is [a state of] being about to be reborn? Because of the statement of a state of being in a changed condition — for one facing rebirth is 'about to be reborn' — this is the intent. But we do not say 'he has been reborn.' Nor do we say that the word 'is reborn' (<s>upapadyate</s>) has the meaning of 'has been reborn.' Therefore, there is no fault here.

children.translated_text: 'One whose age has been brought near [to death]' —

children.text: iti vistaraḥ. mṛtyusamīpam upanītaṃ vayo yena. so 'yam upanītavayāḥ.
children.translated_text: and so on in detail. One whose age has been brought near to death — he is 'one whose age has been brought near' (<s>upanītavayā</s>).

body.text: āmantraṇaṃ. kaścij jīrṇo brāhmaṇa āmantritaḥ.
body.translated_text: is a form of address. A certain old <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is being addressed.

children.translated_text: 'You do not even have a garment for the interval' —

body.text: idam atra jñāpakam. antarābhavābhāva ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: this is the indicator here. The intent is: [this proves] the non-existence of the intermediate existence.

body.text: pathyaudanaṃ
body.translated_text: 'food for the road' —

body.text: pāralaukikaḥ kuśalasaṃbhāras tava nāstīty abhiprāyaḥ. manuṣyeṣv antarāvāso nāstīti. maraṇagatasya te sato manuṣyeṣv antarāvāso nāsti. yatheha kasyacit pratiṣṭhamānasyety abhiprāyaḥ. gamanaviṣṭhānād iti. gamanavirāmāt. ayam atrābhiprāyo yathā tvayā varṇyate. asty antarābhava iti. nāyam abhiprāyo yathā mayā varṇyate. nāsty antarābhava iti. kuta etat. kuto hetor etad bhavati. tulya eṣa bhavato 'py anuyogaḥ. samāna eṣa bhavato 'pi praśna ity arthaḥ. yathoktasūtravirodhād iti. dūṣīmārasūtrādyavirodhāt. na bhavaty etat sūtram antarābhavasyābhāve jñāpakaṃ. jñapakaṃ hi nāmāgatikā gatir [Tib. 266b] iti. yasyā gater anyā gatir nāsti. asāv agatikā gatiḥ. etad uktaṃ bhavati. yadi yaj jñāpakaṃ sūtraṃ. gāthā vā. yesyārthasya dyotanārtham ucyate. yadi tam evārthaṃ dyotayati. nānyad apy arthāntaraṃ tadviruddhaṃ. taj jñāpakam ananyagatikam iti.
body.translated_text: The intent is: you do not have provisions of wholesome [merit] for the next world. 'There is no intermediate dwelling among humans' — for you who have died, there is no intermediate dwelling among humans. The intent is: as if someone were staying here [temporarily]. Because of the cessation of going — because of the stopping of going. The intent here is thus: as you describe it, there is an intermediate existence. This is not the intent: as I describe it, there is no intermediate existence. Whence is this? From what reason does this follow? 'This questioning is equal for you too' — this question is the same for you too — this is the meaning. 'Because of non-contradiction with the stated <s>sūtra</s>s' — because of non-contradiction with the <s>Dūṣīmāra</s> <s>sūtra</s> and the rest. That <s>sūtra</s> does not serve as an indicator of the non-existence of the intermediate existence. [Tib. 266b] For an indicator is defined as 'a course without [another] course' — a course for which there is no other course is a course without [another] course. This has been said: if a <s>sūtra</s> or verse that is an indicator is spoken for the purpose of illustrating a certain meaning, [then only] if it illustrates that very meaning and no other meaning contrary to it — [then] that indicator is one 'without another course.'

children.translated_text: 'Having the form of the existence of the time prior to the [existence] it is going to' —

body.text: iti. ā eṣyad aiṣyat. aiṣyataḥ pūrvakālabhavasyevākṛtir asyeti. aiṣyatpūrvakālabhavākṛtiḥ. kasmāt.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Going to' (<s>aiṣyat</s>) means 'that which will go.' The form of the existence of the time prior to that which it will go to — [the being] has this [form]; thus it is 'having the form of the existence of the time prior to [the existence] it is going to.' Why?

children.translated_text: 'Because of being projected by a single [act]' —

body.text: yasmād aiṣyantī gatis tatprāpakaś cāntarābhavas tenaivaikena karmaṇākṣipyate. śunīprabhṛtīnām iti. śunīsūkarīprabhṛtīnāṃ. paṃcagatika iti. paṃcagatigāmīty arthaḥ. yadi garbhastho 'pi mriyeta tasya nārako 'ntarābhavo mātuḥ kukṣiṃ nirdahet. nārako hi pradīpo bhavati. tadrūpaś cāntarābhava iti. pūrvakālabhave 'pīti vistaraḥ. nārakapūrvakālabhavāvasthā api nārakā na nityaṃ prajvalitā bhavanty utsadeṣu kukūlādiṣu bhramaṃtaḥ. kim aṃgāntarābhavikāḥ. astu vā prajvalita iti. nārako 'ntarābhavaḥ. kukṣāv asaṃśleṣād iti. antarābhavānām acchatvād ātmabhāvasyānyonyaṃ asaṃśleṣān na dāhaḥ. karmapratibandhāc ca. tatkarmapratibandhān na dāha iti kṛtvā. ata eva śunīprabhṛtīnāṃ kukṣer adāhaḥ. koṭīśataṃ cāturdvīpakānām avabhāsitam iti. yataḥ pūrṇayūna iva bodhisattvasyāntarābhavaḥ [Tib. 267a] salakṣaṇānuvyaṃjanaś cāto 'ṃtarābhavasthena tena mātuḥ kukṣiṃ praveṣtum icchatā trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ svakṣetram iti kṛtvāvabhāsitaḥ.
body.translated_text: because the destiny that [the being] will go to and the intermediate existence that leads to it are projected by that one single <s>karma</s>. 'Of female dogs and the rest' — of female dogs, female pigs, and the rest. 'Going to five destinies' — meaning: going to the five <s>gati</s>s. 'If even one in the womb dies, the hell-being intermediate existence would burn through the mother's womb. For a hell-being becomes a flame, and the intermediate existence has that form.' [Reply:] 'Even in the existence of the prior time' — and so on in detail. [Beings in] the state of the existence prior to being hell-beings are also not always blazing as they wander through the intermissions such as <s>kukūla</s> (burning embers) and the like — how much less those in the intermediate existence? Or let it be blazing — the hell-being intermediate existence [still would not burn the womb]: because of non-contact in the womb — because of the transparency of intermediate existences, and because of mutual non-contact of [their] bodies, there is no burning. And because of the obstruction of <s>karma</s> — because of the obstruction of that [mother's] <s>karma</s>, there is no burning. For this very reason, there is no burning of the womb by female dogs and the rest. 'And a hundred <s>koṭi</s>s of four-continent [world-systems] were illuminated' — because the intermediate existence of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [Tib. 267a], like [the moon] full or waning, possessed the [major] marks and minor signs, therefore by him in the intermediate existence state, wishing to enter his mother's womb, the great trichiliocosm was illuminated, considering it his own field.

body.text: pāṃṇḍaraṃ gajapoṭam iti. yady
body.translated_text: 'A white baby elephant' — if

children.translated_text: 'the intermediate existence has the form of the existence of the time prior to [the existence] it is going to,' —

body.text: antarābhavaḥ. kasmād bodhisattvasya mātā gajapotam evaṃrūpam adrākṣīt. nimittamātraṃ tat. tasya bodhisattvasya tiryagyoneś ciravyāvartitatvāt. yataḥ prabhṛti lakṣaṇavipākāni karmāṇy ārabhate kartuṃ kalpaśate śeṣe tataḥ prabhṛti tasya sarvā durgatayo vyāvṛttāḥ. tadyathā kṛkī rājā daśa svapnān adrākṣīt.
body.translated_text: why did the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother see a baby elephant of such a form? That is merely a sign. Because [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] had long since turned away from animal birth. For from the time he begins to perform the <s>karma</s>s that ripen as the [major] marks, with a hundred <s>kalpa</s>s remaining, from that time onward all unfortunate destinies have been turned away for him. Just as King <s>Kṛkin</s> saw ten dreams.

body.text: bhaviṣyato 'rthasya nimittamātram iti. daśa svapnā vinaye paṭhyante. kṛkiṇā kila rājñā daśa svapnā dṛṣtāḥ. hastī vātāyanena nirgatya pucche saktah. kūpas tṛṣitasya pṛṣṭato '; nudhāvati. saktuprasthena muktāprastho labhyate. candanaṃ kāṣṭhārgheṇa vikrīyate. ārāmāḥ puṣpaphalasaṃpannāḥ sarvaṃ ca puṣpaphalam adattādāyibhir hriyate. kalabhair gandhahastinas trāsyante. aśucimrakṣito markaṭaḥ parān upaliṃpati. markaṭābhiṣeko vartate. paṭako 'ṣṭādaśabhir janair ākṛṣyate. mahājanakāya ekatra kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivādenānyonyavighātam āpanna iti. tena ca te bhagavate kāśyapāya tathāgatāya niveditāḥ. [Tib. 267b] bhagavatā ca vyākṛtāḥ. bhaviṣyaty anāgate 'dhvani sākyamunir nāma tathāgataḥ. tasya śrāvakā vistīrṇasvajanabaṃdhuvargaṃ prahāya pravrajitāḥ vihāreṣu gṛhasaṃjñām utpādya saṃgaṃ kariṣyanti hastino vātāyananirgamanapucchalagnavat. kūpasvapnena tacchrāvakā eva brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnām abhyupetya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyaṃti. teṣām śrotukāmatā na saṃsthāsyata ity etad darśayati. saktumuktāprasthasvapnena tacchrāvakā eva saktubhikṣāyā apy arthāyendriyabalabodhyaṃgādīni prakāśayiṣyaṃti. cendanasvapnena tacchrāvakā evābhāvitakāyaśīlaprajñāḥ tīrthyamatāni gṛhītvā buddhavacanena samānīkariṣyantīty etad darśayati. ārāmasvapnena tacchrāvakā evāvāsam āśrayaṃ kṛtvā yat tad bhaviṣyati saṃghasya puṣpaṃ vā phalaṃ vādhikaṃ vā tad vikrīya vikrīya jīvikāṃ kalpayiṣyanti. tena ca gṛhiṇaḥ pratisaṃstariṣyantīty etad darśayati. kalabhasvapnena tacchrāvakā eva duḥśīlaḥ pāpadharmāṇo bhaviṣyanti. ye te bhikṣavaḥ sthavirāḥ śīlavaṃtaḥ kalyāṇadharmāṇaḥ. tān āvāsebhyaḥ pravāsayiṣyaṃtīty etad darśayati. aśucimraksitamarkaṭasvapnena tacchrāvakā eva duḥśīlāḥ pāpadharmāṇaḥ santo ye te bhikṣavaḥ kalyāṇāḥ. tān asadbhir doṣaiś codayiṣyantīty etad darśayati. markaṭābhiṣekasvapnena tacchrāvakā eva sāmantikābhiṣekaṃ vīhāreṣu [Tib. 268a] kariṣyanti. loke 'pi ca paṇḍakā adhirājyaṃ kārayiṣyantīty etad darśayati. paṭasvapnena tacchāsanam evāṣṭādaśadhābhedaṃ gamiṣyati. na ca vimuktipaṭaḥ khaṇḍayiṣyata ity etad darśayati. kalahasvapnena tacchrāvakā eva nikāyaparigrahāt parasparaṃ vivādam āpatsyanta ity etad darśayatīti. saṃgrahaślokaḥ.
body.translated_text: is merely a sign of a future event. Ten dreams are read in the <s>Vinaya</s>. King <s>Kṛkin</s>, it is said, saw ten dreams: an elephant, having exited through a window, was stuck by its tail; a well chased after a thirsty person from behind; a measure of pearls was obtained for a measure of barley-flour; sandalwood was sold at the price of [ordinary] wood; gardens endowed with flowers and fruits — and all the flowers and fruits were taken by thieves; young elephants frightened bull elephants; a monkey smeared with filth besmeared others; an anointing of a monkey took place; a cloth was pulled by eighteen people; a great assembly of people in one place, through quarrel, dispute, conflict, and contention, fell into mutual destruction. And those [dreams] were reported by him to the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>. [Tib. 267b] And the Blessed One explained them: 'In the future, there will be a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>. His disciples, having abandoned their extensive families and kinsmen, will go forth and, generating the perception of household life in their monasteries, will form attachments — like the elephant stuck by its tail while exiting through a window. By the well-dream, those very disciples will approach <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders and teach the <s>Dharma</s> to them, [yet] their desire to listen will not endure — this is what it shows. By the barley-flour-and-pearl-measure dream, those very disciples, even for the sake of a barley-flour alms, will illuminate the faculties, powers, awakening-factors, and the rest. By the sandalwood dream, those very disciples, uncultivated in body, morality, and wisdom, having adopted the doctrines of the heretics, will equate them with the Buddha's word — this is what it shows. By the garden dream, those very disciples, having made a residence their base, whatever will be the <s>Saṅgha</s>'s flowers or fruits or surplus — selling and selling that, they will arrange a livelihood; and thereby householders will be discouraged — this is what it shows. By the young-elephant dream, those very disciples will be of bad morality and evil conduct; and those elder monks who are virtuous and of good conduct — they will banish them from their residences — this is what it shows. By the filth-smeared-monkey dream, those very disciples, being of bad morality and evil conduct, [will falsely accuse] those monks who are virtuous — they will charge them with groundless faults — this is what it shows. By the monkey-anointing dream, those very disciples will perform regional consecrations in their monasteries. [Tib. 268a] And in the world too, eunuchs will exercise sovereignty — this is what it shows. By the cloth dream, that very [Buddha's] teaching will undergo division into eighteen [schools], yet the cloth of liberation will not be torn — this is what it shows. By the quarrel dream, those very disciples, because of sectarian allegiance, will fall into mutual disputes — this is what it shows.' Summary verse:

children.text:
karikūpasaktucandanakalabhārāmās tathā kaper abhiṣekaḥ
aśucikapiḥ paṭakalahāv iti daśa dṛṣṭā nṛpeṇa kṛkiṇā svapnāḥ.
children.translated_text:
'Elephant, well, barley-flour, sandalwood, young elephants, gardens, likewise the monkey's anointing,
the filth-[smeared] monkey, cloth, and quarrels — these ten dreams were seen by King <s>Kṛkin</s>.'

body.text: apatrāpyotsadavāt apatrāpyotkaṭatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the intensification of moral shame (<s>apatrāpya</s>)' — because of the heightening of moral shame.

body.text: upapattibhavaḥ pratisandhikṣaṇa eva. tasmāt pareṇa pratisaṃdhikṣaṇād
body.translated_text: The birth-existence (<s>upapattibhava</s>) is precisely the moment of reconnection (<s>pratisandhikṣaṇa</s>). Therefore, subsequent to that — subsequent to the reconnection-moment

body.text: anyo bhavaḥ pūrvakālabhavaḥ.
body.translated_text: — another existence [arises], [namely] the prior-period existence (<s>pūrvakālabhava</s>).

body.text: rūpiṣu cet sattveṣūpapadyata iti. ārūpyadhātāv antarābhavābhāvād idaṃ viśeṣavacanaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'If it is reborn among material beings' — because of the absence of intermediate existence in the Formless Realm, this qualifying statement is made.

body.text: iti. nārako 'ntarābhavo nārakair evāntarābhavair dṛśyate. evaṃ yāvad devāntarābhavo devāntarābhavair eveti. suviśuddham iti. ekādaśadivyacakṣurapakṣālavarjitaṃ. te punar apakṣālā vicikitsā amanasikāraḥ kāyadauṣṭhulyaṃ styānamiddhaṃ auddhatyaṃ abhyārabhyavīryam audbilyaṃ chaṃbhitatvaṃ nānātvasaṃjñā abhijalpaḥ. abhidhyāyitatvaṃ jñeyeṣu yathāsūtraṃ. abhijñāmayam [Tib. 268b] iti. abhijñāsvabhāvabhāvanāmayam ity arthaḥ. upapattipratilaṃbhikam api devādīnāṃ divyam iṣyate. na tu suviśuddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. An intermediate being of the hells is seen only by intermediate beings of the hells. Similarly, up to: a divine intermediate being is seen only by divine intermediate beings. 'Thoroughly purified' — excluding the eleven impurities of the divine eye. Those impurities, moreover, are: doubt, inattention, physical rigidity, torpor-and-drowsiness, restlessness, excessive exertion, elation, timidity, perception of multiplicity, and verbalization — [and] covetousness toward objects of knowledge, as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>. 'Produced by superknowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>)' — [Tib. 268b] the meaning is: produced through the cultivation of the intrinsic nature of superknowledge. The divine [eye] obtained through rebirth, [possessed by] gods and others, is also accepted [as divine], but it is not thoroughly purified.

body.text: devāntarābhavika iti vistaraḥ. apara āhuḥ. na samānajātīyair evāntarābhavo dṛśyate. kiṃ tarhi. devāntarābhavikaḥ sarvān devāntarābhavikādīn paśyati. manuṣyapretatiryaṅnārakāntarābhavikāḥ pūrvaṃpūrvam apāsya. kathaṃ. manuṣyāntarābhaviko devāntarābhavikaṃ pūrvam apāsya manuṣyapretatiryaṅnārakāntarābhavikān paśyati. pretāntarābhaviko devamanuṣyāntarābhavikau pūrvāv apāsya pretatiryaṅnārakāntarābhavikān paśyati. evaṃ yāvan nārakāntarābhaviko devāntarābhavikādīn pūrvān apāsya nārakāntarābhavikān eva paśyati. gatīnām uttarottaranikṛṣṭatvād iti.
body.translated_text: 'Belonging to a divine intermediate existence' — thus the elaboration. Others say: the intermediate being is not seen only by those of the same birth-type. Rather, one belonging to a divine intermediate existence sees all — those belonging to divine intermediate existence and the rest. Those belonging to human, <s>preta</s>, animal, and hell intermediate existences [see] progressively fewer, excluding [the higher ones]. How? One belonging to a human intermediate existence, excluding one belonging to a divine intermediate existence, sees those belonging to human, <s>preta</s>, animal, and hell intermediate existences. One belonging to a <s>preta</s> intermediate existence, excluding those belonging to divine and human intermediate existences, sees those belonging to <s>preta</s>, animal, and hell intermediate existences. Similarly, up to: one belonging to a hell intermediate existence, excluding those belonging to divine intermediate existence and the rest, sees only those belonging to hell intermediate existence — because each successive destiny is more degraded.

body.text: ata eva gandharva iti. yato gandhagato gandharvaḥ. gandham arvati bhakṣayati gandharva ity arthaḥ. dhātūnām anekārthatvāt. ayam arvati na kevalaṃ gatyarthe vartate. kiṃ tarhi. bhojanarthe 'pīti gatyarthaparigarahe 'py adoṣaḥ. gandham arvati gacchati bhoktum iti gandharva iti. hrasvatvaṃ śakandhukarkandhuvad iti. kṛdanta iti. pararūpanipātanāt. śakandhukarkandhur iti pararūpasiddhir yathā. tathehapi gandharva iti. alpeśākhyo 'nudāro hīnajātīya ity arthaḥ. īṣṭa itīśaḥ. alpa īśo 'lpeśaḥ. alpeśa ity ākhyā yasya so 'lpeśākhyaḥ. viparyayān maheśākhyaḥ.
body.translated_text: For this very reason, [it is called] '<s>gandharva</s>' — because it goes to scent, [it is called] <s>gandharva</s>. '<s>Gandham arvati</s>' means 'it eats scent' — this is the meaning [of <s>gandharva</s>]. Because roots (<s>dhātu</s>) have multiple meanings — this [root] '<s>arv</s>' is not employed only in the sense of 'going,' but also in the sense of 'eating' — therefore even if [it is taken as] comprehending the sense of 'going,' there is no fault: 'it goes to scent in order to eat' — thus [it is called] <s>gandharva</s>. The shortening [of the vowel] is like [in the words] '<s>śakandhu</s>' and '<s>karkandhu</s>.' '[This is] a <s>kṛdanta</s> (primary derivative)' — because of the replacement by the subsequent form. The establishment of the subsequent form is as in '<s>śakandhu</s>' and '<s>karkandhu</s>' — similarly here too, '<s>gandharva</s>.' '<s>Alpeśākhya</s>' means 'of humble designation' — the meaning is: lowly, of inferior birth. '<s>Īṣṭa</s>' is '<s>īśa</s>' (lord). One whose lordship (<s>īśa</s>) is small is '<s>alpeśa</s>' (of little lordship). One whose designation (<s>ākhyā</s>) is '<s>alpeśa</s>' is '<s>alpeśākhya</s>.' Conversely, '<s>maheśākhya</s>' (of great lordship in designation).

body.text: ekanikāyasabhāgatvād iti. yaś ca pūrvakālabhavo yaś cāntarābhavas tatprāpakaḥ. tayor eka eva nikāyasabhāgaḥ ata ekanikāyasabhāgatvāt. [Tib. 269a] yenaiva karmaṇāyuṣyeṇa pūrvakālabhavasyāyur ākṣipyate. tenaivāntarābhavasya. itarathā hi. yadi tasyāntarābhavāyuṣaḥ pṛthagākṣepaḥ syāt. tasyāpy āyuṣah āntarābhavikasya kṣayān maraṇabhavaḥ prasajyet pūrvakālabhavavat. tasmān nāsti niyama iti bhadantaḥ. te taṃ gandhaṃ ghrātvā gandharasābhigṛddhā iti vistaraḥ. te kṣudrajantavas taṃ gandhaṃ ghrātvā tatsahacaraṃ
body.translated_text: 'Because of having a single <s>nikāyasabhāga</s> (class-homogeneity)' — the prior-period existence and the intermediate existence that leads to it — of those two, the <s>nikāyasabhāga</s> is one and the same; therefore, because of having a single <s>nikāyasabhāga</s>. [Tib. 269a] By the very same life-projecting <s>karma</s> that projects the lifespan of the prior-period existence, the [lifespan] of the intermediate existence too is projected. Otherwise — if there were a separate projection of the lifespan of that intermediate existence — then, upon the exhaustion of that lifespan of the intermediate existence, a death-existence would follow, just as with the prior-period existence. Therefore, 'there is no fixed [lifespan]' — [says] the Venerable [<s>Vasubandhu</s>]. 'Having smelled that scent, they become greedy for scent and flavor' — thus the elaboration. Those tiny creatures, having smelled that scent and recollecting the flavor previously experienced together with it, [Tib. 269a] becoming greedy for scent and flavor, [and] dying, awaken the <s>karma</s> that produces the class-homogeneity of worms;

body.text: cānubhūtaṃ rasam anusmṛtya gandharasābhigṛddhāḥ kālaṃ kurvantaḥ kriminikāyasabhāgotpādakaṃ karma vibodhya. tayā gaṃdharasatṛṣṇayā vipākābhimukhaṃ kṛtvāntarābhavasaṃtatyā krimiṣūpajāyanta iti. tatpatyayapracura eva kāla iti. krimipratyayapracure kāle tatsamvartanīyāni karmāṇi krimisamvartanīyāni vipākābhinirvṛttau vṛttiṃ labhaṃte. vipākadānāyābhimukhībhavantīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: and through that craving for scent and flavor, having turned [the karma] toward [its] maturation, they are reborn among worms through the continuity of the intermediate existence. 'At a time when the conditions are abundant' — at a time when the conditions for worms are abundant, the <s>karmas</s> conducive to worm-[rebirth] — those conducive to the arising of worms — obtain their function in the accomplishment of maturation — the meaning is: they become oriented toward the giving of maturation.

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalaṃti khalu dehinām
children.translated_text: 'Having reached the assemblage [of conditions] and the time, the fruits indeed [ripen] for embodied beings' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. nānyatra. nātatpracure kāle. nānyasyām iti. nālpāyuṣi.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. 'Not otherwise' — not at a time when those [conditions] are not abundant. 'Not of another' — not in a [being of] short lifespan.

children.translated_text: 'The arising of a <s>Cakravartin</s> is not below eighty thousand [years of lifespan]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. ata eveti. yasmād vidyamānāny api cakravartisamvartanīyāni karmāṇi vipākābhinirvṛttau kadācid eva vṛttiṃ labhante. bahupratyayāpekṣitvāt. saṃbhavaiṣitvād upapattyabhilāṣitvāt. karmāṇy eva pratyayānāṃ sāmagrīm āvahantīti. karmādhipatyenāśvādīnāṃ prasiddhaṃ kālam atikramya [Tib. 269b] kālāntare 'pi maithunaṃ bhavatīti. ekakarmākṣepād iti. yenaiva karmaṇā gavādinikāyasabhāga ākṣipyate. tenaiva karmaṇā tadantarābhava ākṣipyate. ity ato vaktavyam etat. yad uktaṃ yenānyatra kāle goṣūpapattavyaḥ. sa gavayeṣūpapadyata iti vistareṇa. na nikāyabhedād ekākṣepakatvaṃ hīyate. tatkarmaṇa ekajātīyatvāt. gavyākṛtisaṃsthānāntaraparityāgāc ca. gatiniyatānāṃ hi karmaṇām upapattivaicitryaṃ drṣṭaṃ. kalmāṣapādādivad iti nāsty eṣa doṣa ity ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. 'For this very reason' — because even <s>karmas</s> conducive to a <s>Cakravartin</s>, though existing, obtain their function in the accomplishment of maturation only at certain [times], because of depending on many conditions. 'Because of desiring existence, because of wishing for rebirth' — the <s>karmas</s> themselves bring about the assemblage of conditions. 'Through the predominance of <s>karma</s>' — through the predominance of <s>karma</s>, it is well-known that even for horses and the like, mating occurs at a time beyond the established [season], [Tib. 269b] at another time as well. 'Because of projection by a single <s>karma</s>' — by the very same <s>karma</s> that projects the class-homogeneity of cattle and the like, by that very <s>karma</s> the intermediate existence for those is projected. Therefore this should be said — what was stated: 'one who should be reborn among cattle at another time is [instead] reborn among <s>gavaya</s>s (wild oxen)' — in detail. The oneness of projection is not diminished by the difference of birth-class, because of the single-natured character of that <s>karma</s>, and because of not abandoning the general form and configuration of cattle. For it is observed that <s>karmas</s> determined as to destiny produce variety in rebirth — like [King] <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s> and others. Therefore there is no fault in this — [says] Master <s>Saṅghabhadra</s>.

body.text: iti. anunayasahagatena vā pratighasahagatena vā cittena yathā viparyastamatir bhavati. tad darśayann āha. tatrāsya pitror ity vistaraḥ. mātāpitros tāṃ vipratipattiṃ dvīndriyasamāpattilakṣaṇāṃ. puṃsaḥ sataḥ puruṣasyāntarābhavasya puṃsāyaṃ pauṃsno rāga utpadyate mātari bhāryāyām iva. striyā ayaṃ straiṇo rāga utpadyate pitari bhartarīva. viparyayāt pratigha iti. puṃsaḥ sataḥ pauṃsnaḥ pratigha īrṣyotthānabhūta utpadyate pitari pratisapatnapuruṣa iva. striyās satyāḥ straiṇaḥ pratigha utpadyate mātari pratisapatnyām iva. sa tābhyām eva viparyastābhyāṃ cittābhyāṃ viparyasto raṃtukāmanatayā maithunakarmakāmanatayā taṃ deśaṃ indriyadvayasthānam āśliṣya tām avasthāṃ vipratipattyavasthām ātmany adhimucyate. mayaitat karma kriyata iti. tasmiṃś cāśucau śuklaśoṇite garbhasthānasaṃprāpte āmāśayapakvāśayāntarāsthānasaṃprāpte [Tib. 270a] abhiniviśate pratitiṣṭhatīty arthaḥ. pṛṣṭhābhimukha utkuṭuka iti. maithunakriyātmābhimānakriyāyogāt. āpyāyamāno vardhamānaḥ. etāny
body.translated_text: thus. Whether with a mind accompanied by attraction (<s>anunaya</s>) or accompanied by aversion (<s>pratigha</s>) — how the mind becomes distorted, showing that, he says: 'therein, of the parents' — thus the elaboration. Toward the mother and father, that distorted perception characterized by the encounter of the two organs: if male, being a male [intermediate being], masculine desire arises toward the mother, as toward a wife. If female, feminine desire arises toward the father, as toward a husband. 'Conversely, aversion' — if male, masculine aversion, having the nature of jealous hostility, arises toward the father, as toward a rival man. If female, feminine aversion arises toward the mother, as toward a rival woman. That [intermediate being], with precisely those two distorted minds, being distorted through the desire for sexual intercourse, through the desire for the act of copulation, clings to that place — the location of the two organs — and superimposes that state, the state of intercourse, upon itself [thinking]: 'I am performing this act.' And in that impure semen-and-blood, when it has reached the location of the womb — when it has reached the location between the stomach and the intestines — [Tib. 270a] it adheres, the meaning is: it establishes itself. 'Facing the back, in a crouching position' — because of the application of the self-conceit of performing the act of copulation. '<s>Āpyāyamāna</s>' means 'growing.'  These

body.text: eveti. śuklaśoṇitamahābhūtāni. bhūtāntarāṇy eveti. śuklaśoṇitavyatiriktāni. bījāṃkuranirodhotpādanyāyenaikasminn eva kṣaṇe bījaṃ nirudhyate 'ṃkuraś cotpadyate. tulādaṇḍanāmonnāmavan nāśotpādayoḥ samakālatvāt. yat tat kalalam ity ākhyāyata iti.
body.translated_text: very [elements] — the great elements of semen and blood. 'Other elements indeed' — those distinct from semen and blood. By the principle of the cessation of the seed and the arising of the sprout, at one and the same moment the seed ceases and the sprout arises — because of the simultaneity of destruction and origination, like the rising and falling of the arms of a balance. That which is called '<s>kalala</s>' (embryonic matter) [is thus designated].

body.text: ityādivacanāt. evaṃ ca kṛtvā sūtrapadam iti. valmīka iti bhikṣo asya kāyasyaitad adhivacanaṃ rūpiṇaḥ audārikasya cāturmahābhūtasya odanakulmāṣopacitasya mātāpitraśucikalalasaṃbhūtasyeti vistaraḥ. mātāpitraśucy eva kalalaṃ. tataḥ saṃbhūtasyety arthaḥ. kaṭasir iti. śmaśānaṃ. rudhirabindur upātta iti. idam udāharaṇaṃ. asya kāyendriyabhāvāpattitaḥ. bhūtāntarāṇy va śuklaśoṇitavyatiriktāni. tadyathā parṇakrimer iti. yathā parṇakrimeḥ parṇamahābhūtāny upaniśritya bhūtāntarāṇi karmabhir jāyante. yānīndriyasvabhāvam āpadyaṃte. na parṇamahābhūtāni. bahutvāt tatkrimīṇāṃ. khaṇḍaśaḥ pattrasyādarśanāc ca. sūtrapadaṃ kathaṃ tarhi nīyate mātāpitraśucikalalasaṃbhūtasyety ata āha. aśucisaṃniśrayotpattyabhisaṃdhivacanāt te kalalasya sūtrāvirodha [Tib. 270b] iti. aśucisaṃniśrayeṇotpattir bhūtāntarāṇāṃ. tatrābhisaṃdhir abhiprāyaḥ. tena vacanaṃ kalalasya. tasmān mātāpitraśucikalalasaṃbhūtasyety asya sūtrasyāvirodhaḥ. etad uktaṃ bhavati. śuklaśoṇitasaṃniśrayeṇa kalalākhyāni bhūtāṃtarāṇi śuklaśoṇitasamakālāny utpadyanto sendriyāṇi. yathā parṇasaṃniśrayeṇa parṇasamānakālāni sendriyāṇi krimimahābhūtāny utpadyanta iti.
body.translated_text: Because of such statements. And having done so, the sūtra passage states: "<s>Valmīka</s> (ant-hill) — O monk, this is a designation for this body, which is material, gross, consisting of the four great elements, nourished by rice and barley, born from the impurity of mother and father" — and so forth in detail. The impurity of mother and father itself is the <s>kalala</s> (embryonic matter). The meaning is: born from that. "<s>Kaṭasi</s>" means cremation ground. "A drop of blood taken up" — this is an illustration. From the attainment of the state of body-faculty. The other elements (<s>bhūtāntara</s>) are indeed distinct from semen and blood. "Just as with a leaf-worm" — just as from a leaf-worm, relying upon the great elements of the leaf, other elements arise through <s>karma</s> — those which attain the nature of faculties — not the great elements of the leaf [themselves], because of the multiplicity of those worms and because the leaf is not seen [to be consumed] piece by piece. How then is the sūtra passage "born from the impurity of mother and father" to be construed? To this he says: "Because of the statement with the intent of arising in dependence on impurity, there is no contradiction with the sūtra regarding the <s>kalala</s>." The arising of the other elements is in dependence on impurity. The intent (<s>abhisaṃdhi</s>) therein is the purpose. By that, the statement is about the <s>kalala</s>. Therefore, there is no contradiction with the sūtra "born from the impurity of mother and father." What is being said is this: in dependence on semen and blood, the other elements called <s>kalala</s>, simultaneous with semen and blood, arise endowed with faculties — just as in dependence on a leaf, the great elements of the worm, simultaneous with the leaf and endowed with faculties, arise.

body.text: anyatra tu yathāyogaṃ vaktavyam ity āhur iti. anyatra saṃsvedajaupapādukayor yonyor yathāyogaṃ vyākhyeyam ity āhur abhidharmācāryāḥ. tatra cāyaṃ yogo dṛśyeta iti. ācāryo bhavīti.
body.translated_text: "But for other [birth-types], it should be stated as appropriate" — thus say [the masters]. For the other two birth-types — moisture-born and spontaneous — it should be explained as appropriate, say the <s>Abhidharma</s> masters. "And there, this appropriateness should be seen" — thus says the Master.

body.text: śaityaṃ ca narakeṣv iti śītanarakopapattikāle. yadavastha iti. aurabhrikādyavasthaḥ. yathā bhūtena tadvedyaṃ kṛtaṃ prāk karma tādṛśān sattvān svapna iva prekṣya narake sa dhāvati pārvācāryāḥ yogācārā āryāsaṃgaprabhṛtayaḥ.
body.translated_text: "And cold in the hells" — at the time of rebirth in the cold hells. "In whatever state" — the state of slaughter-house workers and the like. "Having perceived, as it truly is, beings of such kind through previously performed <s>karma</s>, as if in a dream, one rushes to hell" — [this is the view of] the former masters, the <s>Yogācāras</s> beginning with the noble <s>Asaṅga</s>.

body.text: āsanād ivottiṣṭhann iti. ūrdhvopapattisthānagamanāt. manuṣyādivad iti. yathā manuṣyas tiryak pretaś ca gacchati. tadvat.
body.translated_text: "As if rising from a seat" — because of going to a place of upward rebirth. "Like humans and so forth" — just as a human, an animal, or a <s>preta</s> goes, so likewise.

body.text: iti. adhikṣeptāro 'pavaditāra ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: — meaning: those who disparage and censure.

body.text: iti nityagrahaṇāt
body.translated_text: — because of the word "always."

body.text: ity atra nāsti niyamaḥ. bhavati tu saṃprajānann api. pratilomaṃ nirdiṣṭā iti. sūtre hi yaḥ sarvāṇy asaṃprajānan karoti. eṣā prathamā garbhāvakrāntir uktā. tisras tu yathā nirdiṣṭānupūrvikā eveti. yo 'pi janiṣyate. so 'py aṇḍaja [Tib. 271a] iti. aṇḍāj janiṣyate 'ṇḍaja ity abhiprāyaḥ. āvaśyako hy abhūtārtho bhūtavad ucyate. tadyathā vartamānasāmīpye vartamānavad vā. āśaṃsāyāṃ bhūtavac ceti. {yathābhūtena tadvedyaṃ kṛtaṃ prāk karma tādṛśān sattvān svapna iva prekṣya narake sa dhāvati.} kaścit kasmaicid vaktā bhavet. āgacchaṃtam evāgatam māṃ viddhīti. tasmād adośa eṣaḥ. aṇḍāj jāto janiṣyate jāyate cety aṇḍajaḥ. anyebhyo 'pi ḍrśyata iti vacanāt. tasmād aduṣṭam etad ity ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ. atha vā bhāvinyāpi saṃjñayeti. bhaviṣyaṃtyāpi saṃjñayā nirdeśaḥ kriyate. tadyathā saṃskṛtam abhisaṃskarotīti. janitāvasthāyāṃ saṃskṛtaṃ bhavati. na janyamānāvasthāyāṃ. na hi saṃskṛtasya punaḥ saṃskāro yujyate. bhaviṣyantyā tu saṃjñayā tathā nirdeśaḥ kriyate. evam odanaṃ pacatītyādiyojyaṃ. kathaṃ punar asaṃprajānan mātuḥ kukṣiṃ praviśatīti vistaraḥ saṃnikṛṣṭāvasthā upapattideśasya
body.translated_text: — here there is no restriction. But there can also be one who is fully aware (<s>saṃprajānan</s>). "Stated in reverse order" — for the sūtra states: "One who performs all [actions] without full awareness — this is declared the first entry into the womb. But the three are in the order as stated." "One who will be born — that one too is egg-born" — the intent is: one born from an egg, or one who will be born from an egg, is "egg-born." For necessarily a non-actual [referent] is spoken of as if actual. Just as present-proximity is spoken of as present, or just as future-expectation is spoken of as actual. {"Having perceived, as it truly is, through previously performed karma, beings of such kind as if in a dream, one rushes to hell."} Someone might say to another: "Know me as already arrived even as I am coming." Therefore, there is no fault. "Egg-born" — [one who] was born from an egg, will be born, or is being born. "Because of the statement 'it is also seen in others.'" Therefore, this is not faulty — thus says Master <s>Saṃghabhadra</s>. Alternatively, "by a future designation also" — the statement is made using a future designation too. Just as "conditions the conditioned" — it is "conditioned" in the state of having been produced, not in the state of being produced, for re-conditioning of what is already conditioned is not logical. But the statement is made using the future designation. Similarly, "cooks rice" and the like should be construed. "But how does one enter the mother's womb without full awareness?" — and so forth in detail. The proximate state of the place of rebirth —

body.text: viprakṛṣṭāvasthā adhimokṣo 'dhimuktiḥ tathā tiṣṭhāmi niryāmīti. kathaṃ. tathā tiṣṭhato 'py eṣu tiṣṭhāmīti. niṣkrāmato 'py ebhyo niryāmīti. ayam anayor viparyāsayor viśeṣa iti. apare punar āhuḥ. na kevalaṃ rāgadveṣābhyām [Tib. 271b] eva viparyastamatir utpattideśaṃ gacchati. kiṃ tarhi. anyathāpi. katham iti. vāto vāti devo varṣatītyadi. tathārāmaṃ praviśāmy udyānaṃ cetyādi.saṃprajānaṃs tu samyak prajānāti. mātuḥ kukṣiṃ praviśāmīty evamādi. yadi samyak prajānāti kathaṃ kliṣṭenaiva cittena pratisaṃdhibandho vyavasthāpyate. mātṛsnehādiyogāt kliṣṭaṃ cittaṃ bhavati. apara āha. mātuḥ kukṣiṃ praviśala evaṃ viparītau saṃjñādhimokṣāv iti. upapannamātrāvasthāyām etad bhavati vāto vāti yāvad vṛkṣamūlaṃ copasarpāmi kuḍyamūlaṃ ceti. tiṣṭhato 'py eṣu tiṣṭhāmīti. niṣkrāmato 'py ebhyo niryāmīty evamādi. tatra prathameti vistaraḥ. prathamā cakravartinaḥ. yeyaṃ.
body.translated_text: The distant state: conviction (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) is firm belief (<s>adhimukti</s>): "I am staying thus, I am departing thus." How? "Even while staying among these, [one thinks] 'I am staying.' Even while departing from these, [one thinks] 'I am departing.'" This is the distinction between these two perversions. But others say: "Not only through passion and hatred does one go to the place of birth with a perverted mind. But also otherwise." How? "The wind blows, the rain falls" — and so forth. Similarly, "I enter a garden, a park" — and so forth. But one who is fully aware (<s>saṃprajānan</s>) knows correctly: "I am entering the mother's womb" — and so forth. If one knows correctly, how is it established that rebirth-connection (<s>pratisaṃdhibandha</s>) occurs only with a defiled mind? Because of association with attachment to the mother and so forth, the mind becomes defiled. Another says: "At the very moment of entering the mother's womb, thus are the perception and conviction perverted." In the state of just having been reborn, this occurs: "The wind blows" — up to — "I approach the base of a tree, the base of a wall." "Even while staying among these, [one thinks] 'I am staying.' Even while departing from these, [one thinks] 'I am departing'" — and so forth. There, "the first" — and so forth in detail. The first [mode of entry] belongs to a <s>Cakravartin</s>. That which —

body.text: iti. dvitīyā pratyekabuddhasya. yeyaṃ
body.translated_text: — the second belongs to a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. That which —

body.text: iti. tṛtīyā buddhasya. yeyam
body.translated_text: — the third belongs to a <s>Buddha</s>. That which —

body.text: atrāpi bhāvinyeti. te na cakravartyādayas tadānīm iti kṛtvā. ta evaṃ tv ete cakravartyādaya iti paryāyamātram etad uktam. arthas tu sa evety abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: "Here too, by [a future] designation" — because they are not <s>Cakravartin</s>s and the rest at that time. "But these are indeed <s>Cakravartin</s>s and the rest" — this is stated merely as a synonym. The intent is that the meaning is the same.

body.text: (III.18, 19) saṃketā hetuphalasambandhavyavasthāḥ.
body.translated_text: (III.18, 19) Conventions (<s>saṃketa</s>) are the established relationships of cause and effect.

body.text: Tib. 272a
body.translated_text: Tib. 272a

body.text: kleśakarmābhisaṃskṛtam
body.translated_text: "Conditioned by afflictions and <s>karma</s>"

body.text: iti. kleśakarmaparibhāvitam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: — the meaning is: imbued with afflictions and <s>karma</s>.

body.text: iti. saṃtatinyāyasaṃcāri skaṃdhapaṃcakaṃ. kṣaṇikatvāt. pradīpavad iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: — the fivefold aggregate (<s>skandhapañcaka</s>), moving according to the principle of continuity (<s>saṃtatinyāya</s>), because of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) — he shows [it is] "like a lamp."

body.text: iti. ākṣepas tāvatkālaprabandhaḥ. etac ca viśeṣaṇam āyuṣyasyāyuḥsamvartanīyasya karmaṇo bhedāt.
body.translated_text: — the projection (<s>ākṣepa</s>) is a sequence of that duration. And this is a qualifier of the life-determining [karma] (<s>āyuṣya</s>), due to the division of the life-producing <s>karma</s>.

body.text: iti. vyaṃjanāni cakṣurādyadhiṣṭhānāni. tair hi cakṣurādīny abhivyajyante. tasmin varcaḥkūpa iveti. mahākāyanāḍīvraṇa iti. nindāvacanam etat. nāḍī vraṇa iva nāḍīvraṇa iti. ugro durgandha ugradurgandhiḥ. andhakāraś cāsāv ālokarahitatvāt. samalānāṃ ca palvalo 'sau palvala iveti kṛtvā. tasmin satatapratikriye nityakartavyaśauce. śukreṇa pauṃsnena. śoṇitena straiṇena. lasīkayā dravaviśeṣalakṣaṇayā. malena ca saṃklinne samantāt klinne. viklinne viśeṣeṇa klinne. kvathite pūtau picchile ca. tasmiṃ hastau saṃpraveśyāṃgam angaṃ hastapādādikaṃ nikṛtya cchittvā pratyāharanti pratyākarṣayaṃti. taruṇaṃ vraṇaṃ sarujaṃ. taruṇavraṇam ivātmānam ācaraṃs taruṇavraṇāyamānaṃ. taruṇavraṇāyamāna ātmāsyeti taruṇavraṇāyamānātmānam bālakaṃ. śastraṃ ca kṣāraṃ ca śastrakṣāraṃ. tad ivātmānam ācaraṃ śastrakṣārāyamāṇaḥ. śastrakṣārāyamāṇaḥ [Tib. 272b] saṃsparśo 'nayor iti śastrakṣārāyamāṇasaṃsparśau pāṇī. tābhyāṃ parigṛhya snāpayaṃti. tasya vṛddher anvayād anugamāt.
body.translated_text: — the marks are the bases for the eye and other [faculties]. For by them, the eye and other [faculties] are manifested. "In that, like a cesspit" — meaning: a great bodily fistula. This is a term of reproach. A fistula-like wound — thus "fistula-wound." "Foul" (<s>ugra</s>) means "bad-smelling" (<s>durgandhi</s>). And it is darkness, because of being devoid of light. And it is like a pool of impurities — thus "like a pool." In that [womb] requiring constant cleansing, eternally needing purification: with semen — the male [element]; with blood — the female [element]; with serum (<s>lasīkā</s>) — characterized by a particular liquid; and smeared with filth — moistened all around, thoroughly moistened, putrefied, foul, and slimy. In that [womb], having inserted the hands, they pull out limb by limb — hands, feet, and so forth — cutting and extracting them. A fresh wound that is painful — [the infant is] like a tender wound, experiencing itself as a tender wound. [The infant], experiencing itself as if [being touched by] a tender wound — [that is,] the child whose self is experienced as a tender wound. Sharp instruments and caustic (<s>kṣāra</s>) — both sharp instruments and caustic — experiencing oneself as [being touched by] those sharp instruments and caustic. The contact of those two [hands] that cause the experience of sharp instruments and caustic — [they are] hands whose touch is like sharp instruments and caustic. Grasping with those [hands], they bathe [the infant]. Because of the continuity of its growth —

body.text: tasyāhetukatvam iti. āder ahetukatvaṃ. sati cāsyāhetukatve. tadvad eva sarvam ahetukaṃ prāduḥ syāt. dṛṣṭaṃ cāṃkuraādiṣu bījādīnāṃ sāmarthyaṃ.
body.translated_text: "Its being without cause" — the causelessness of the beginning. And if it were without cause, then likewise everything would arise without cause. And the efficacy of seeds and the like is observed in sprouts and so forth.

body.text: aṃkuranālakāṇḍapattrādiṣu bījāṃkuranālakāṇḍādīnāṃ sāmarthyam utpādanāya. kasmāt. deśakālapratiniyamāt. deśakālayos tu pratiniyamāt. tatra deśapratiniyamo bījādisaṃbaddha eva deśa utpatteḥ. kālapratiniyamo bījānantaram utpatteḥ. agnyādīnāṃ vāgniśītoṣṇābhighātacakṣurādīnāṃ pākajādiṣa pākajasukhaduḥkhaśabdacakṣurvijñānādiṣu ḍṛṣṭam sāmarthyaṃ deśakālapratiniyamāt. yadi hi nirhetukaḥ prādurbhāvaḥ syāt. bījādīnām aṃkurādiṣu agnyādīnāṃ ca pākajādiṣu deśakālapratiniyamenotpattiṃ prati sāmarthyaṃ na syāt. sarvaṃ sarvatra sarvadotpadyeta. na caivaṃ dṛṣṭam ity ato nāsti nirhetukaḥ prādurbhāvaḥ. nityakāraṇāstitvavādaḥ prāg eva paryudastaḥ.
body.translated_text: The efficacy of seeds, sprouts, stalks, stems, and the rest for producing sprouts, stalks, stems, leaves, and the rest. Why? Because of the restriction of place and time. That is, because of the restriction of both place and time. There, the restriction of place is that arising occurs only in the place connected with the seed and the rest. The restriction of time is that arising occurs immediately after the seed. The efficacy of fire and the rest — fire, cold, heat, impact, the eye and the rest — in maturation-products and the rest — maturation-born pleasure, suffering, sound, eye-consciousness and the rest — is observed because of the restriction of place and time. For if arising were without cause, there would be no efficacy of seeds and the rest in sprouts and the rest, and of fire and the rest in maturation-products and the rest, through restriction of place and time. Everything would arise everywhere at all times. But this is not observed. Therefore, there is no causeless arising. The doctrine of a permanent cause has already been refuted.

children.translated_text: "Not from <s>Īśvara</s> and the rest, because of sequence and so forth"

body.text: iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: — because of this statement.

body.text: (III.20) śeṣāṇy aṣtau madhya iti. vijñānanāmarūpaṣaḍāyatanasparśavedanātṛṣṇopādānabhavāṃgāni. [Tib. 273a] nāpi rūpārūpyāvacara iti. rūpāvacarasya vijñānāṃgakāla eva nāmarūpaṣaḍāyatanāṃgayoḥ sadbhāvāt. na madhye 'ṣṭāv aṃgāni. ārūpyāvacarasya ca nāmarūpaṣaḍāyatanāṃgayor abhāvāt. mahānidānaparyāyasūtre. vijñānaṃ ced ānanda mātuḥ kukṣiṃ nāvakrāmed api tu tan nāmarūpaṃ kalalatvāyābhisaṃmūrchet. no bhadantetyādi tat sūtraṃ paṭhyate. mātuḥ kukṣyavakramaṇaṃ hi kāmadhātāv eveti. saphalahetukayoḥ pūrvāparāntayor grahaṇād iti. yathākramam etat. pūrvāntasya saphalasya grahaṇād aparāntasya ca sahetukasya grahaṇād iti. tatra pūrvānte hetur avidyā saṃskārāś ca. tasya phalaṃ paṃcāṃgāni. vijñānaṃ yāvad vedaneti. aparānte jātir jarāmaraṇaṃ ceti phalaṃ. tasya trīṇy aṃgāni hetavas tṛṣṇopādānabhavāḥ. tad evaṃ saptāṃgāni paurvāntikaḥ paṃcāṃgāny aparāṃtika iti vyākhyātaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: (III.20) "The remaining eight are the middle" — the limbs of consciousness, name-and-form, six sense-bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, and existence. "Nor in the form and formless realms" — because in the Form Realm, the name-and-form and six-sense-base limbs already exist at the very time of the consciousness-limb, there are not eight limbs in the middle. And because in the Formless Realm, the name-and-form and six-sense-base limbs do not exist. In the <s>Mahānidāna</s> sūtra: "If, <s>Ānanda</s>, consciousness were not to descend into the mother's womb, would name-and-form coalesce into embryonic form (<s>kalala</s>)?" "No, Venerable One" — and so forth, that sūtra is recited. For descending into the mother's womb is only in the Desire Realm. "Because of the inclusion of the fruitful [limbs] in the prior end and the causal [limbs] in the posterior end" — this is in order. Because of the inclusion of the fruitful [limbs] in the prior end and the causal [limbs] in the posterior end. There, in the prior end, the cause is ignorance and formations. Their fruit is the five limbs: consciousness up to feeling. In the posterior end, birth and old-age-and-death are the fruit. Their causes are the three limbs: craving, grasping, and existence. Thus, seven limbs belonging to the prior end and five limbs belonging to the posterior end — this has been explained.

body.text: (III.21-24) atha ka ime 'vidyādaya iti. kim avidyaiva kevalā utāho sarvakleśāḥ āhosvit kleśāvastheti saṃdehe pṛcchati. sāhacaryād iti. yasmād avidyāsahacāriṇaḥ kleśāḥ. tadvaśena teṣāṃ samudācārāc ca. yasmāc cāvidyāvaśena teṣāṃ kleśānāṃ samudācāraḥ. sa punas [Tib. 273b] tadanuvṛttiḥ. mūḍhasya hi kleśasamudācāro nāmūḍhasya. rājāgamanavacana iti vistaraḥ. yathā rājāgacchatīty ukte. tadanuyātṛkāṇāṃ bhṛtyānām āgamanasiddhiḥ. sāhacaryāt tadvaśena teṣāṃ samudācārāt. tadvad etat. tad evam avidyāvaśād. avidyāṃgaḥ kleśadaśety arthaḥ. tasmād uktaṃ
body.translated_text: (III.21-24) "Now, what are these — ignorance and the rest?" — in the doubt whether it is ignorance alone, all afflictions, or the state of affliction — he asks. "Because of association" — because the afflictions are companions of ignorance. "And because of their activity under its power" — because the activity of those afflictions occurs under the power of ignorance. And that [activity] is their occurrence following it. For the activity of afflictions occurs in one who is deluded, not in one who is undeluded. "The analogy of the king's coming" — and so forth in detail. Just as when it is said "the king comes," the coming of the retinue and servants is established — because of association and because of their activity under his power — so too is this case. Thus, under the power of ignorance, the state of affliction is the ignorance-limb — this is the meaning. Therefore it was stated:

children.translated_text: "The prior state of affliction is ignorance."

body.text: na tūktaṃ pūrvāvidyādaśāvidyeti. puṇyādikarmāvastheti. puṇyāpuṇyā karmāvasthety arthaḥ. prāk caturāyatanotpādād iti vaktavya iti. manaḥkāyāyatanayor upapattibhava evotpādāt. tadā tadvyavasthāpanād iti. cakṣurādyāyatanotpattikāle kāyamanaāyatanayor vyavasthāpanād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: "Not stated as 'the prior ignorance-state is ignorance.'" "The state of meritorious and other <s>karma</s>" — the meaning is: the state of meritorious and demeritorious <s>karma</s>. "Before the arising of the four sense-bases, it should be stated" — because the mind and body sense-bases arise only in birth-existence itself, and because at that time their establishment [as separate limbs occurs]. "At the time of the arising of the eye and other sense-bases" — the meaning is: because of the establishment of the body and mind sense-bases [as included in the six-sense-base limb] at the time of the arising of the eye and other sense-bases.

children.translated_text: "That [is] prior to the conjunction of three"

body.text: iti. tat ṣaḍāyatanāṃgaṃ prāk trikasaṃgamāt. prāg indriyaviṣayavijñānatrikasaṃnipātād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: — that six-sense-base limb [exists] before the conjunction of three. The meaning is: before the meeting of the triad of faculty, object, and consciousness.

body.text: iti. ṣaḍindriyaviṣayavijñānasaṃnipātaḥ sparśo jātāvasthāyāṃ vyavasthāpyate. paripūrṇaṣaḍāyatanasamnipātasadbhāvāt. ā kutaḥ. prāk sukhaduḥkhāduḥkhāsukhavedanākāraṇeṣu jñānaśaktitaḥ. sa bālo yāvat sukhāyā vedanāyā etat kāraṇaṃ duḥkhāyā etat kāraṇaṃ aduḥkhāsukhāyāś [Tib. 274b] caitat kāraṇam iti paricchede na śakto bhavati. sāvasthā sparśa ity ucyate. tathā hi bālako 'gnim api spṛśed duḥkhasyaitat kāraṇam ity aparicchindan. paricchede sāmarthye sati
body.translated_text: thus. Contact (<s>sparśa</s>) — the conjunction of the six faculties, objects, and consciousnesses — is established at the stage of being born, because of the actual existence of the complete conjunction of the six sense-bases. From what [point]? From the capacity for knowledge regarding the causes of pleasant, painful, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings. The child, insofar as he is not capable of discriminating 'this is the cause of pleasant feeling, this the cause of painful feeling, [Tib. 274b] this the cause of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling' — that state is called 'contact.' For indeed, a child would even touch fire, not discriminating 'this is the cause of suffering.' When there is the capacity for discrimination,

body.text: vedanety arthaḥ. ā kutaḥ.
body.translated_text: means feeling (<s>vedanā</s>). From what [point]?

body.text: yāvan maithunarāgo na samudācarati. sāvasthā vedanety ucyate. vedanāprakarṣiṇī hi sāvasthā. vedanākāraṇavedanāt.
body.translated_text: as long as desire for sexual intercourse has not manifested. That state is called 'feeling.' For that state is one of predominant feeling, because of feeling the causes of feeling.

children.translated_text: 'Craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) [is the state] of one who desires enjoyments and sexual intercourse' —

body.text: iti. bhogeṣu rūpādikāmaguṇalakṣaṇeṣu. maithune ca lokapratīte rāgiṇaḥ pudgalasya. tadrāgasamudācārāvasthā tṛṣṇety ucyate. paryeṣṭim āpanna iti. eṣa ity etasya dhātor etad rūpaṃ. upādīyate viṣaya ātmabhāvo 'nenety upādānaṃ caturvidhaḥ kleśaḥ. sāvasthopādānam ity ucyate.
body.translated_text: thus. In enjoyments characterized by the sense-pleasures of form and the like, and in sexual intercourse as known in the world — of a person who has desire. The state of the manifestation of that desire is called '<s>tṛṣṇā</s>' (craving). 'Having entered upon searching' — '<s>eṣa</s>' is the form of this root.
