'<s>Upādāna</s>' (grasping) — that by which objects and the self-state are appropriated — is the fourfold affliction. That state is called '<s>upādāna</s>.'

children.translated_text: 'He [performs karma] whose fruit is future existence (<s>bhava</s>)' —

body.text: iti. sa iti paridhāvato nirdeśaḥ. bhaviṣyadbhavaḥ phalam asyeti bhaviṣyadbhavaphalaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. 'He' refers to the one who is running about. 'Whose fruit is future existence' means: future existence is his fruit.

body.text: paunarbhavikam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: meaning: [karma] that leads to renewed existence.

body.text: iti. bhavaty aneneti bhavaḥ karmaparyāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. 'That by which one comes to be' is <s>bhava</s> — a synonym for <s>karma</s>.

body.text: ity ā vidaḥ ā vedanāṃgāt. jarāmaraṇaṃ nāmarūpādicaturaṃgasvabhāvaṃ. vineyajanodvejanārthaṃ bhagavatā jarāmaraṇaśabdena catvāry aṃgāny uktāni.
body.translated_text: thus: 'up to feeling' means up to the link of feeling. Aging-and-death has as its own-nature the four links beginning with <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). For the purpose of alarming the disciples, the <s>Bhagavān</s> expressed four links by the term 'aging-and-death'

body.text: yo bhikṣavo rūpasyotpādaḥ. sa jarāmaraṇasyotpādaḥ. evaṃ yāvad vijñānasyeti.
body.translated_text: 'Monks, the arising of form — that is the arising of aging-and-death. Likewise, up to consciousness.'

body.text: kṣaṇikaḥ kṣaṇe bhavaḥ. kṣaṇo 'syastīti vā [Tib. 274b] kṣaṇikaḥ. prakarṣeṇa dīvyati carati vā prākarṣikaḥ. prabandhayukta ity arthaḥ. evaṃ sāṃbaṃdhikaḥ hetuphalasambandhayukta ity arthaḥ. evam āvasthikaḥ. dvādaśa paṃcaskaṃdhikā avasthā ity arthaḥ. vijñānasahabhuva iti vistaraḥ. rūpam atra sahabhūvijñaptyavijñaptyādi. saṃjñādiskaṃdhatrayaṃ nāma. nāmarūpavyavasthitānīndriyāṇi. tatpratibaddhavṛttitvād indriyāṇām. āśrayatvena vā tāni nāmni vyavasthitānīti. ṣaḍāyatanābhinipātaḥ sparśa iti. cakṣurādīnāṃ svasmiṃ viṣaye pravṛttir abhinipātaḥ. sa tu saṃbhavataḥ. yasya tadānīm abhinipātaḥ saṃbhavati. sa tasya sparśa iti veditavyaḥ. tatsaṃprayuktāni paryavasthānāny upādānaṃ. tayā tṛṣṇayā saṃprayuktāny āhrīkyānapatrāpyādīni paryavasthānāni tad upādānaṃ. tatsamuttham iti. tṛṣṇāsamutthaṃ. cetanāsamuttham ity apare. unmajjanam utpādaḥ paripāko jareti. phalākṣepasāmarthyopaghātaḥ. pūrvakṣaṇāpekṣayā vā. bhaṅgo maraṇam iti. tatkṣaṇavināśaḥ. bhaṃgābhimukhyaṃ bhaṃga ity apare. kṣaṇikaḥ sāṃbandhikaś ca yathā prakaraṇeṣu iti. kathaṃ. prakaraṇeṣu pratītyasamutpādaḥ katamaḥ. sarve saṃskṛtā dharmā [Tib. 275a] iti. tatra saṃskṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ vināśayogāt kṣaṇikaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ. hetuphalabhūtobhayakṣaṇasaṃbandhāt sāṃbandhikaḥ. nirantarajanmatrayasaṃbaddhā iti. dvādaśa paṃcaskaṃdhikā avasthā atītānāgatapratyutpannajanmasaṃbaddhāḥ āvasthikaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ. niraṃtaragrahaṇaṃ trikāṇḍaprasiddhyarthaṃ. sa eva prākarṣika iti. sa evāvasthikaḥ prakarṣayogāt. prākarṣikaḥ. anekakṣaṇikatvād anekajanmikatvād vā.
body.translated_text: 'Momentary' (<s>kṣaṇika</s>) — existence in a moment; or: 'it has a moment,' hence <s>kṣaṇika</s>. [Tib. 274b] 'Extended' (<s>prākarṣika</s>) — it extends or operates over a prolonged [period]; meaning: connected with continuity. Likewise, 'relational' (<s>sāṃbandhika</s>) — meaning: connected with the relation of cause and fruit. Likewise, 'positional' (<s>āvasthika</s>) — meaning: the twelve states, each consisting of five aggregates. 'Co-existent with consciousness' — thus the elaboration. Form here is the co-existent informative and non-informative [forms] and the like. The three aggregates of perception, etc. are 'name' (<s>nāma</s>). The faculties established with name-and-form — because the faculties operate in dependence on them; or those are established as belonging to name. 'The impact of the six sense-bases is contact' — the engagement of eye, etc. in their respective objects is the impact. But that is as possible — whichever [sense] has an impact possible at that time, that should be understood as its contact. 'The mental entanglements associated with that are grasping' — the mental entanglements associated with that craving — shamelessness, moral recklessness, and so forth — those are grasping. 'Arisen from that' — arisen from craving. Or: arisen from volition, according to others. 'Emergence is birth; ripening is aging' — the deterioration of the capacity for projecting fruit; or relative to the preceding moment. 'Breaking is death' — destruction at that [same] moment. Or: the facing toward breaking is breaking, according to others. 'The momentary and relational [types] are as in the <s>Prakaraṇa</s> texts' — how? In the <s>Prakaraṇa</s> texts: 'What is dependent origination?' 'All conditioned <s>dharma</s>s.' [Tib. 275a] Therein, because of the connection with moment-to-moment destruction of conditioned <s>dharma</s>s, the momentary dependent origination [is established]. Because of the connection with both moments as cause and fruit, the relational [type]. 'Connected with three consecutive births' — the twelve states, each consisting of five aggregates, connected with past, future, and present births, is the positional dependent origination. The word 'consecutive' is for establishing the three-section [arrangement]. That itself is the extended — that same positional [type], through the connection with extension, is extended — because of spanning multiple moments or multiple births.

body.text: (III.25ab) ābhiprāyika iti. abhiprāye bhava ābhiprāyikaḥ. vineyābhiprāyavaśāt tathā deśita ity arthaḥ. lākṣaṇiko 'bhidharme lakṣaṇapradhānatvāt. prakaraṇeṣu hi sarvasaṃskṛtagrahaṇāt sattvāsattvākhyaḥ pratītyasamutpāda uktaḥ. sarvasaṃskṛtahetutvayogāt. vineyasammohavinivṛttihetuḥ sattvākhya eva dvādaśāṃgaḥ pratītyasamutpādo deśitaḥ.
body.translated_text: (III.25ab) 'Intentional' (<s>ābhiprāyika</s>) — occurring in accordance with intention. The meaning is: taught thus in accordance with the intention of the disciples. 'Definitional' (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>) — in the <s>Abhidharma</s>, because definition is primary. For in the <s>Prakaraṇa</s> texts, because of including all conditioned [things], the dependent origination is stated as including both sentient and non-sentient, because of the connection with the causality of all conditioned things. [But] the twelve-linked dependent origination, which is the cause of removing the confusion of disciples, was taught as pertaining to sentient beings alone.

body.text: (III.25cd) ata āha.
body.translated_text: (III.25cd) Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'For the removal of confusion regarding the past, future, and middle [periods]' —

body.text: iti. ata eva ca trikāṇḍa iti. kāṇḍa iti bhāgaḥ. ko nv aham abhūvam iti. devo manuṣya iti vā. kathaṃ nv aham abhūvam iti. kena prakāreṇa kayā yuktyety arthaḥ. kiṃ bhaviṣyāmy anāgate 'dhvanīti vistaraḥ. kiṃ nu bhaviṣyāmy
body.translated_text: thus. 'And therefore it is threefold' — '<s>kāṇḍa</s>' means 'section.' 'What indeed was I?' — 'was I a god or a human?' and so on. 'How indeed was I?' — meaning: in what manner, by what logic? 'Will I exist in the future period?' — thus the elaboration. 'Will I indeed exist

body.text: anāgate [Tib. 275b] 'dhvani. āho svin na bhaviṣyāmi. ko nu bhaviṣyāmi. kathaṃ nu bhaviṣyāmīti. kena prakāreṇa kayā yuktyety arthaḥ. kiṃ svid idam iti. ātmabhāvadravyam anveṣate. kathaṃ svid idam iti. kena prakāreṇa kayā yuktyeti. tad evātmabhāvadravyaṃ nāvadhārayati. ke santa iti. ke vayam idānīṃ vidyamānāḥ. ke bhaviṣyāma ity evaṃ nāvadhārayati. sūtre yathākramam iti. avidyā saṃskārāś ca pūrvāntasammohavyāvartanārthaṃ. jātir jarāmaraṇaṃ cāparāntasammohavyāvartanārthaṃ. vijñānaṃ yāvad bhavaś ca madhyasaṃmohavyāvartanārtham iti. tathā hi sūtre evoktam iti vistaraḥ. sūtre 'py evamevaṃ darśitam iti. sūtreṇa svavyākhyānaṃ samarthayati. sa na pūrvāṃtaṃ pratisarati. kiṃ nv aham abhūvam atīte 'dhvanīti vistaraḥ. sa na pūrvāntaṃ pratidhāvati. kiṃ nv aham abhūvam atīte 'dhvanīti. pratītyasamutpādayathābhūtadarśanena naivam atīte 'dhvani saṃmuhyate ity arthaḥ. vistaraśabdena sa nāparāntaṃ pratisarati. kiṃ nu bhaviṣyāmy anāgate 'dhvanīti vistaraḥ tathā na sa madhyāntaṃ pratisarati. kiṃ svid idam iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: in the future [Tib. 275b] period? Or perhaps I shall not exist? What indeed shall I be? How indeed shall I be?' — meaning: in what manner, by what logic? 'What indeed is this?' — one investigates the substance of one's self-state. 'How indeed is this?' — in what manner, by what logic? — one does not ascertain that very substance of the self-state. 'What are we, existing now? What shall we become?' — thus one does not ascertain. 'In the <s>sūtra</s>, in order' — ignorance and formations are for removing confusion about the past. Birth and aging-and-death are for removing confusion about the future. Consciousness up to existence is for removing confusion about the middle. For thus it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s> itself — thus the elaboration. It is thus demonstrated in the <s>sūtra</s> too — he supports his own interpretation by the <s>sūtra</s>. 'He does not run toward the past: "What indeed was I in the past period?"' — thus the elaboration. He does not rush toward the past — through seeing dependent origination as it really is, he is not confused about the past period — this is the meaning. By the word 'elaboration': 'nor does he run toward the future: "What indeed shall I be in the future period?"' — thus the elaboration. Likewise, 'nor does he run toward the middle: "What indeed is this?"' — thus the elaboration.

body.text: tṛṣṇopādānabhavā apīti. sarve tṛṣnopādānabhavā aparāṃtasaṃmohavyāvartanārthaṃ. na madhyasaṃmohavyāvartanārthaṃ. yathā pūrvam upadiṣṭaṃ vijñānaṃ yāvad bhavaś ceti. [Tib. 276a] kā punar atra yuktir ity āha. tasyaiva hy ete hetava iti. yasmād aparāntasyaivaite hetava iti.
body.translated_text: 'Craving, grasping, and existence also' — all of craving, grasping, and existence are for removing confusion about the future, not for removing confusion about the middle — as previously taught: 'consciousness up to existence.' [Tib. 276a] 'What then is the reasoning here?' He says: 'for these are causes of that very [future life]' — because these are indeed causes of the future [life].

body.text: (III.26) kleśakarmāśrayatvād iti. vijñānādīni saptāṃgāni vastūny adhiṣṭhānāni kleśakarmaṇām ity arthaḥ. phalaṃ tatheti. saptaivāṃgāni vijñānanāmarūpaṣaḍāyatanasparśavedanāṃgāni avidyāsaṃskārāṇāṃ phalāni. jātir jarāmaraṇaṃ ca tṛsṇopādānabhavānāṃ phalāni. paṃca hetubhūtānīti. avidyāsaṃskāratṛṣṇopādānabhavāḥ. karmakleśasvabhāvatvād iti. avidyātṛṣnopādānāni kleśasvabhāvāni. saṃskārā bhavaś ca karmasvabhāvāḥ.
body.translated_text: (III.26) 'Because [the seven links] are the basis for afflictions and <s>karma</s>' — meaning: the seven links beginning with consciousness are the substances — the foundations — of afflictions and <s>karma</s>. 'Fruit likewise' — the same seven links — consciousness, name-and-form, six sense-bases, contact, and feeling — are the fruits of ignorance and formations. And birth and aging-and-death are the fruits of craving, grasping, and existence. 'Five are causes' — ignorance, formations, craving, grasping, and existence. 'Because they have the nature of <s>karma</s> and afflictions' — ignorance, craving, and grasping have the nature of afflictions. Formations and existence have the nature of <s>karma</s>.

body.text: vastunaḥ paṃcadhābhedād iti. vijñānanāmarūpaṣaḍāyatanasparśavedanā iti. kleśasya ca dvidheti. tṛṣṇopādānam iti. anāgate 'dhvani phalaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ dvidhābhedād iti. jātir jarāmaraṇam iti. atīte 'dhvani hetuḥ saṃkṣiptaḥ ekamukhakleśopadeśāt. avidyāmukhakleśopadeśād ity arthaḥ. na punar anāgate 'dhvani phalam evaṃ paṃcadhā viśālitaṃ. atīte cādhvani naivaṃ dvidhā hetur viśālita iti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the fivefold division of the basis' — consciousness, name-and-form, six sense-bases, contact, and feeling. 'And the twofold [division] of affliction' — craving and grasping. 'In the future period, the fruit is condensed into a twofold division' — birth and aging-and-death. 'In the past period, the cause is condensed because of the teaching of afflictions under a single heading' — meaning: because of the teaching of afflictions under the heading of ignorance. But in the future period, the fruit is not thus expanded into five. And in the past period, the cause is not thus expanded into two.

body.text: (III.27) yasmād upadarśito 'tra bhagavateti. kaḥ.
body.translated_text: (III.27) 'Because the <s>Bhagavān</s> has shown here' — what?

body.text: ity evamādiko [Tib. 276b]
body.translated_text: and so on — [Tib. 276b]

children.translated_text:
'this is the pattern of the links of existence.
From that, a basis' —

body.text: iti. tataḥ kriyāyāḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. From that, from action [comes a basis].

body.text: iti. tato vastunaḥ vastu.
body.translated_text: thus. From that basis, [comes another] basis.

body.text: iti. vastuna ity adhikṛtaṃ. jāyanta ity atretikaraṇo 'dhyāhāryaḥ. vastunaḥ kleśād veti jñāpitam iti. iti kleśo vastuna utpadyamāno dṛṣṭo vedanāyās tṛṣṇeti. kleśād api tathā kleśo dṛṣṭas tṛṣṇāyā upādānam iti. avidyā ca pūrvāntasarvakleśasvabhāvākhyātā. tad yady upādānaṃ tṛṣṇāyās tad utpadyate iti gamyate. atha tṛṣṇā tadvastuna utpadyata iti gamyate. tasmād avidyā kleśasvabhāvā satī vastunaḥ kleśād veti jñāpitaṃ bhavati. jarāmaraṇaṃ caturaṃgasvabhāvaṃ vastv iti vyākhyātaṃ. vastunaś ceha kleśa utpadyamāno dṛṣṭo vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇeti. tasmāt tataḥ kleśo bhāvī bhaviṣyatīti jñāpitaṃ bhavati. nātra punaḥ kimcid upasaṃkhyeyam evaṃ jñāpitatvāt. kathaṃ punar evaṃ nayo darśita iti gamyata ity āha. evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskaṃdhasya samudayo bhavatīti vacanāt. anyathā hi kim asya sāmarthyam syād iti. yady ayaṃ yathokto nayo na syāt.
body.translated_text: thus. 'From a basis' is the governing word. 'Arise' — here the word 'thus' must be supplied. 'From a basis, or from affliction — this has been indicated.' Thus an affliction arising from a basis has been observed — craving from feeling. Likewise, an affliction from an affliction has been observed — grasping from craving. And ignorance has been declared as having the nature of all afflictions of the past. If grasping arises from craving — that is understood. And if craving arises from its basis [feeling] — that is understood. Therefore ignorance, having the nature of affliction, has been indicated [to arise] from a basis or from an affliction. Aging-and-death, whose own-nature is the four links, has been explained as a basis. And an affliction arising from a basis has been observed here — craving conditioned by feeling. Therefore it is indicated that from that [basis], there will be future afflictions. Nothing further needs to be added here, since it has been thus indicated. 'But how is it understood that such a pattern has been shown?' He says: because of the statement 'thus there is the arising of this entire great mass of suffering.' Otherwise, what would be its import? If this pattern as stated did not exist.

children.text:
kleśāt kleśaḥ kriyā caiva tato vastu tataḥ punaḥ
vastu kleśāś ca jāyanta
children.translated_text:
'From affliction, affliction; and action too; from that, a basis; from that again,
a basis; and afflictions arise' —

body.text: ity etāvad eva brūyāt. avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā yāvaj jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ [Tib. 277a] saṃbhavantīti idaṃ na brūyāt. evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskaṃdhasya samudayo bhavatīti. samudaya utpāda ity anarthāṃtaraṃ. tasmād yathoktaprakārābhidyotakam asya sāmarthyam iti gamyate.
body.translated_text: this alone would be stated. 'Conditioned by ignorance, formations; up to: conditioned by birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and anguish [Tib. 277a] arise' — this would not be stated. 'Thus there is the arising of this entire great mass of suffering' — 'arising' (<s>samudaya</s>) and 'birth' (<s>utpāda</s>) are synonymous. Therefore it is understood that the import [of the formula] illuminates the pattern as stated.

body.text: ayoniśomanaskārahetukāvidyoktā sūtrāṃtara iti. sahetusapratyayasanidānasūtre. katham. avidyā bhikṣavaḥ sahetukā sapratyayā sanidānā. kaś ca bhikṣavo 'viydyāyā hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ kiṃ nidānaṃ. avidyāyā bhikṣavo 'yoniśomanaskāro hetur ayoniśomanaskāraḥ pratyayo 'yoniśomanaskāro nidānam iti sūtre vacanāt. avidyāhetukaś cāyoniśomanaskāra iti. sūtrāntara ukta ity adhikṛtam. cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpāṇi cotpadyate āvilo manaskāro mohaja iti sūtre vacanāt. kim arthaṃ tasyehāvacanaṃ. kathaṃ na bhavāṃgāntaraṃ bhavatīty ata āha. sa cehāpy upādānāntarbhūtatvād ukto bhavatīti. sa ity āvilo manaskāraḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Ignorance caused by improper mental attention is stated in another <s>sūtra</s>' — in the <s>Sahetusapratyayasanidāna-sūtra</s>. How? 'Ignorance, monks, has a cause, has a condition, has an origin. What, monks, is the cause of ignorance? What is its condition? What is its origin? Monks, improper mental attention (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>) is the cause of ignorance, improper mental attention is the condition, improper mental attention is the origin' — because of this statement in the <s>sūtra</s>. 'And improper mental attention is caused by ignorance' — 'stated in another <s>sūtra</s>' is the governing phrase. 'Dependent on the eye and forms, there arises a turbid mental attention born of delusion' — because of this statement in the <s>sūtra</s>. 'Why is it not mentioned here? How does it not become another link of existence?' Therefore he says: 'because here too it is stated as being included within grasping.' 'It' means that turbid mental attention

body.text: iheti pratītyasamutpādasūtre. katham [Tib. 277b] uktaḥ. upādānāntarbhūtatvāt. tathā hy upādānaṃ bhogānāṃ prāptaye kleśasamudācārāvasthā. tatra cāyoniśomanaskāro viparītacetasa ābhogo 'ntarbhūta ity ukto bhavati. ato nāsty ahetukatvam avidyāyāḥ. na cāṃgāntaram upasaṃkhyātavyaṃ dvādaśebhyo 'vidyādibhyaḥ. na cānavasthāprasaṃgo 'vidyāhetukatvād ayoniśomanaskārasya. ity apara iti. sthaviro vasubandhur ācāryamanorathopādhyāya evam āha. ācārya āha. katham iti vistaraḥ. katham ayoniśomanaskārasyopādāne 'ntarbhāvaḥ. na hy ayoniśomanaskāra upādānasvabhāvaḥ. yadi saṃprayogataḥ. yady ayoniśomanaskāra upādānena saṃprayujyate ity ato bhavatāsyopādāne 'ntarbhāva iṣyate. tṛṣṇāvidyayor api pratītyasamutpādāṃgayos tasyāyoniśomanaskārasyāntarbhāvaḥ prāpnoti. ṭṛṣṇāvidyābhyām api hy asau saṃprayujyata iti. tataś caivaṃ vaktavyaṃ syāt. sa cehāpy avidyātṛṣnopādānāntarbhūtatvād ukto bhavatīti. na tv evaṃ vaktavyaṃ. sa cehāpy upādānāntarbhūtatvād ukto bhavatīti. naivam upādānāntarbhāvāvadhāraṇaṃ kartavyam ity abhiprāyaḥ. saty api cāntarbhāva iti. asaṃbhavaṃtam apy antarbhāvam abhyupetya brūmaḥ. katham ayoniśomanaskāro hetur avidyāyā iti vijñāpitaṃ bhavati. [Tib. 278a] na hi tathā sūtre vacanam asti. yadi hy antarbhāveneti vistaraḥ. yadi yasmād upādāne 'ntarbhavaty ayoniśomanaskāraḥ. tasmād ayoniśomanaskāro hetur avidyāyā iti vijñāpitaṃ bhavati. na ca tadaṃgāntaraṃ vaktavyaṃ. upādānavacanād eva tatsiddheḥ. tṛṣṇāvidye api tarhy upādāne 'ntarbhavatah. atas tayor api tatrāntarbhāvād aṃgāntaratvaṃ śakyam akartum. upādānavacanād eva tatsiddheḥ. ukte ca pṛthaktṛṣṇāvidyāṃge. tasmād aparihāra eṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'here' — in the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) <s>sūtra</s>. How [Tib. 277b] is it stated? Because of being subsumed under <s>upādāna</s> (clinging). For <s>upādāna</s> is the state of active affliction for the purpose of obtaining enjoyments. And therein, <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> (improper mental attention), being the mental engagement of one whose mind is inverted, is said to be subsumed. Therefore, there is no causelessness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Nor should another limb be counted in addition to the twelve beginning with <s>avidyā</s>. Nor is there the consequence of infinite regress, because <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> has <s>avidyā</s> as its cause. 'Thus the other [says]' — the Elder <s>Vasubandhu</s>, the student of the teacher <s>Manoratha</s>, spoke thus. The teacher says: 'How' — and so on in detail. How is <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> subsumed under <s>upādāna</s>? For <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> does not have the intrinsic nature of <s>upādāna</s>. 'If through association' — if because <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> is associated with <s>upādāna</s>, you therefore accept its subsumption under <s>upādāna</s>, then the consequence follows that this same <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> is also subsumed under <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) and <s>avidyā</s>, which are [also] limbs of dependent origination. For it is also associated with <s>tṛṣṇā</s> and <s>avidyā</s>. In that case, one would have to say: 'And here too it is said [to be subsumed] because of being subsumed under <s>avidyā</s>, <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, and <s>upādāna</s>.' But one should not say thus: 'And here too it is said because of being subsumed under <s>upādāna</s> [alone].' The intent is: one should not make such a restriction of subsumption under <s>upādāna</s>. 'Even granting the subsumption' — even conceding the subsumption that does not actually hold, we say: how is it made known that <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> is the cause of <s>avidyā</s>? [Tib. 278a] For there is no such statement in the <s>sūtra</s>. 'If through subsumption' — and so on in detail. If because <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> is subsumed under <s>upādāna</s>, it is thereby made known that <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> is the cause of <s>avidyā</s>, and another limb need not be stated — because of the establishment of that simply from the statement of <s>upādāna</s> — then <s>tṛṣṇā</s> and <s>avidyā</s> too are subsumed under <s>upādāna</s>. Therefore, because of their subsumption therein, it should be possible to eliminate them too as separate limbs — because of the establishment of that simply from the statement of <s>upādāna</s>. Yet <s>tṛṣṇā</s> and <s>avidyā</s> are stated as separate limbs. Therefore, this is no resolution.

body.text: anyaḥ punar āheti bhadantaśrīlātaḥ. ayoniśomanaskāro hetur avidyāyā uktaḥ sūtrāntara iti. sahetusapratyayasanidānasūtre. avidyāpi bhikṣavaḥ sahetukā sapratyayā sanidāneti vistareṇa. sa cāpīti vistaraḥ. sa cāpy ayoniśomanaskāraḥ sparśakāle nirdiṣṭaḥ. katham ity āha. cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpāṇi cotpadyate āvilo manaskāro mohaja iti. sparśakālo yo 'yaṃ cakṣurvijñānotpattikālaḥ. āvilo manaskāraḥ ayoniśaḥ pravṛttatvān mohajatvād vā. mohāj jāto mohaja iti. avidyāsaṃsparśajaṃ veditam iti. avidyāsaṃprayuktāt sparśāj jātaṃ avidyāsaṃsparśajaṃ veditaṃ. yatra veditam avidyāsaṃsparśajam. [Tib. 278b] avaśyaṃ tatrāvidyā saṃprayujyate. na hi veditam asaṃprayuktam avidyayā tṛṣṇāhetur bhavatīti. tad evaṃ sparśakāle bhavann ayoniśomanaskāro vedanāsahavartinyā avidyāyāḥ pratyayabhāvena siddha iti. jñāpitam idaṃ bhavaty
body.translated_text: 'Another, however, says' — the venerable <s>Śrīlāta</s>. '<s>Ayoniśomanaskāra</s> is stated as the cause of <s>avidyā</s> in another <s>sūtra</s>' — in the <s>Sahetusapratyayasanidāna</s> <s>sūtra</s> (the <s>Sūtra</s> on Having Causes, Conditions, and Origins): '<s>Avidyā</s> too, O monks, has a cause, has a condition, has an origin' — and so on in detail. 'And that too' — and so on in detail. And that <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> is indicated at the time of contact (<s>sparśa</s>). How? He says: 'Dependent on the eye and forms, there arises a turbid mental attention, born of delusion.' The time of contact is the time of the arising of visual consciousness. Turbid mental attention is [so called] because of operating improperly, or because of being born from delusion. Born from delusion (<s>moha</s>) means <s>mohaja</s>. 'Feeling born from contact associated with <s>avidyā</s>' — feeling born from contact associated with <s>avidyā</s> is 'feeling born from <s>avidyā</s>-contact.' Where feeling is born from <s>avidyā</s>-contact, [Tib. 278b] <s>avidyā</s> is necessarily associated there. For feeling not associated with <s>avidyā</s> does not become a condition for <s>tṛṣṇā</s>. Thus, <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>, occurring at the time of contact, is established as a condition for <s>avidyā</s> that co-occurs with feeling. This makes known

body.text: ayoniśomanaskārahetukāvidyeti. ato nāsty ahetukatvam avidyāyāḥ. ayoniśomanaskārahetukatvāt. na cāṃgāntaram upasaṃkhyeyaṃ dvādaśabhyo 'nyat. yasmāt sparśakāle bhavann ayoniśomanaskāro vedanāsahavartinyā avidyāyāḥ pratyayabhāvena siddha iti. na cāpy anavasthāprasaṃgaḥ. tasyāpy ayoniśomanaskārasya punar mohajavacanāt. āvilo manaskāro mohaja iti. tad etac cakrakam uktaṃ bhavati. ayoniśomanaskārād avidyā. avidyāyāś cāyoniśomanaskāra iti.
body.translated_text: that <s>avidyā</s> has <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> as its cause. Therefore, there is no causelessness of <s>avidyā</s> — because of having <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> as its cause. Nor should another limb be counted in addition to the twelve — because <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>, occurring at the time of contact, is established as a condition for <s>avidyā</s> that co-occurs with feeling. Nor is there the consequence of infinite regress — because of the further statement that this very <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> too is born from delusion: 'a turbid mental attention, born of delusion.' This states a circle: from <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>, <s>avidyā</s>; and from <s>avidyā</s>, <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>.

body.text: evaṃ punaḥ parihāram ācāryaḥ sadoṣaṃ paśyaṃs tasya doṣasyābhivyaktyarthaṃ prasaṃgam ārabhate. tat tarhīti vistaraḥ. tad yathoktam ayoniśomanaskāro hetur avidyāyā iti vistareṇa sūtrato yuktyā vā. tarhīti arthāntaravivakṣāyāṃ. idānīmartha iti bhagavadviśeṣaḥ. etad anyatra sūtra uktam iha punaḥ pratītyasamutpādasūtre vaktavyaṃ. na vaktavyam iti [Tib. 279a] bhadantaśrīlātaḥ. kayā yuktyeti pṛṣṭaḥ. bhadantaśrīlāta āha. na hīti vistaraḥ. arhatām asti vedanā. na ca sā tṛṣṇāyāḥ pratyayībhavatīti. savidyaiva vedanā tṛṣṇāpratyaya iti gamyate. na cāviparītaḥ sparśaḥ kliṣtāyā vedanāyāḥ pratyayībhavatīti prakṛtaṃ. na ca punar niravidyasyārhato viparītaḥ sparśa iti. sparśo 'pi sāvidya eveti gamyate. yo vedanāyāḥ pratyaya uktaḥ pratītyasamutpādasūtre. avidyā cāsya sparśasya hetur iti gamyate. ity anayā yuktyā pṛatītyasamutpādasūtre sāvidyasparśapratyayā vedanā. sāvidyavedanāpratyayā ca tṛṣṇeti gamyate. ato yuktyā yathoktayā. sa cāpi sparśakāle nirdiṣṭa iti vistareṇātra pratītyasamutpāde siddhaṃ bhavaty ayoniśomanaskāro hetur avidyāyā iti. atra codyate. yadi tarhi niravidyā vedanā tṛṣṇāyaḥ pratyayo na bhavatītyādivacanena svagatayaiva yuktyā ayoniśomanaskāro hetur avidyāyā avidyā cāyoniśomanaskārasya hetur iti gamyate. kim sūtrāntarāpāśrayeṇāvidyāyoniśomanaskārayor anyonyahetukatvapradarśanena prayojanam iti. atrocyate. satyam asty etat. kiṃ tu yuktimātram idaṃ pratītyasamutpādasūtre. na kaṇṭhoktiḥ. ataḥ sūtrāntare kaṇṭhoktyeyaṃ [Tib. 279b] yuktir vyavasthāpyata iti tat sūtrāntaropanyāsaprayojanam avagaṃtavyaṃ. atiprasaṃga evaṃ prāpnotīti śāstrakāraḥ. katham atiprasaṃga ity āha. avidyāsparśajaṃ veditaṃ pratītyotpannā tṛṣṇeti sūtrāntare nirdiṣṭaṃ. na ca niravidyaveditasyārhato vedanā tṛṣṇāyāḥ pratyayo bhavati. na cāviparītaḥ sparśaḥ kliṣṭāyā vedanāyāḥ. na ca niravidyasyārhato viparītaḥ sparśa ity anayā yuktyā etad apy aṃgadvayaṃ sparśavedanākhyaṃ iha pratītyasamutpādasūtre 'nucyamānam apy anyatropadiṣṭatvād gamyate ity etasyāpy aṃgadvayasyāvacanaṃ prāptaṃ. tathā sūtrāntara upadiṣṭaṃ. sa puṇyāṃś cet saṃskārān abhisaṃskaroti
body.translated_text: Now the teacher, seeing that this resolution is faulty, introduces a further consequence for the purpose of making that fault evident. 'In that case, then' — and so on in detail. As stated: '<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> is the cause of <s>avidyā</s>' — in detail from the <s>sūtra</s> or by reasoning. 'Then' — with the intention of expressing a different point. 'Now-meaning' — this is the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s distinctive [intention]. 'This, stated in another <s>sūtra</s>, should here in the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> <s>sūtra</s> be stated.' 'It should not be stated' — [says] the venerable <s>Śrīlāta</s>. When asked 'by what reasoning?' — [Tib. 279a] the venerable <s>Śrīlāta</s> says: 'It is not the case' — and so on in detail. <s>Arhat</s>s have feeling, but that [feeling] does not become a condition for <s>tṛṣṇā</s>. Therefore, it is understood that only feeling accompanied by <s>avidyā</s> is a condition for <s>tṛṣṇā</s>. And a non-inverted contact does not become a condition for afflicted feeling — this is established. And for an <s>Arhat</s> free from <s>avidyā</s>, there is no inverted contact. Therefore it is understood that even contact must be accompanied by <s>avidyā</s> — the contact that is stated as a condition for feeling in the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> <s>sūtra</s>. And <s>avidyā</s> is understood to be the cause of this contact. Thus, by this reasoning, in the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> <s>sūtra</s>, feeling has contact accompanied by <s>avidyā</s> as its condition, and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> has feeling accompanied by <s>avidyā</s> as its condition — this is understood. Therefore, by reasoning as stated: 'And that too is indicated at the time of contact' — and so on in detail — it is established here in the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> that <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> is the cause of <s>avidyā</s>. Here it is objected: if, by the reasoning beginning with 'feeling free from <s>avidyā</s> does not become a condition for <s>tṛṣṇā</s>' — by one's own reasoning alone — it is understood that <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> is the cause of <s>avidyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s> is the cause of <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>, what is the purpose of demonstrating the mutual causation of <s>avidyā</s> and <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> through [recourse to] another <s>sūtra</s>? To this it is replied: True, this is so. However, this is merely reasoning in the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> <s>sūtra</s>, not an explicit statement. Therefore, this reasoning is established [Tib. 279b] by an explicit statement in another <s>sūtra</s> — thus the purpose of adducing another <s>sūtra</s> should be understood. 'The consequence of over-extension follows' — [says] the treatise-author. How is there over-extension? He says: 'Feeling born from <s>avidyā</s>-contact — <s>tṛṣṇā</s> arises dependent on that' — this is stated in another <s>sūtra</s>. And feeling of an <s>Arhat</s>, who has feeling free from <s>avidyā</s>, does not become a condition for <s>tṛṣṇā</s>. And a non-inverted contact [does not become a condition] for afflicted feeling. And for an <s>Arhat</s> free from <s>avidyā</s>, there is no inverted contact. By this reasoning, these two limbs called contact and feeling, even though stated here in the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> <s>sūtra</s>, are understood as having been taught elsewhere — therefore the consequence follows that these two limbs too need not be stated. Similarly, it is taught in another <s>sūtra</s>: 'If one performs meritorious <s>saṃskāra</s>s

body.text: puṇyopagam asya vijñānaṃ bhavati. evam apuṇyopagam āniṃjyopagaṃ ca. na ca niravidyasaṃskārasyārhataḥ puṇyopagaṃ vijñānaṃ yāvad āniṃjyopagaṃ vijñānam iti. etad api saṃskārāṃgaṃ yuktyā siddhaṃ. na vaktavyam atreti prāptaṃ. tathā jātim antareṇa jarāmaraṇaṃ na bhavatīti yuktyā gamyata iti. jātyaṃgaṃ na vaktavyaṃ syāt. ityādiprasaṃgaḥ prāpnoti.
body.translated_text: one's consciousness becomes [tending] toward merit. Similarly, [tending] toward demerit, and [tending] toward the imperturbable.' And for an <s>Arhat</s> whose <s>saṃskāra</s>s are free from <s>avidyā</s>, consciousness does not [tend] toward merit, up to: does not [tend] toward the imperturbable. This limb of <s>saṃskāra</s> too is established by reasoning — [therefore] the consequence follows that it need not be stated here. Similarly, because aging and death does not occur without birth — this is understood by reasoning — the limb of birth would not need to be stated. And so on — such consequences follow.

body.text: acodyam eva tv etad iti vistareṇācāryaḥ svamatam āha. kathaṃ paralokād ihaloka iti vistaraḥ. tatrāvidyāsaṃskārābhyām [Tib. 280a] ihalokaḥ sambadhyate. sa cehaloko vijñānanāmarūpaṣaḍāyatanasparśavedanāṃgāni. tṛṣṇopādānabhavaiḥ paralokaḥ saṃbadhyate. sa ca paraloko jātir jarāmaraṇaṃ ca. ity etāvato 'rthasyātra pratītyasamutpādasūtre vineyebhyo vivakṣitatvāt. etasya cārthasya pūrvam evoktatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'But this is not a valid objection' — and so on in detail, the teacher states his own position. 'How from the other world to this world' — and so on in detail. Therein, by <s>avidyā</s> and <s>saṃskāra</s>s, [Tib. 280a] this world is connected. And this world consists of the limbs: <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), and <s>vedanā</s> (feeling). By <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), and <s>bhava</s> (becoming), the other world is connected. And that other world consists of <s>jāti</s> (birth) and <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death). Because this much meaning was intended to be expressed to the trainees here in the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> <s>sūtra</s>. And because this meaning was already stated before —

children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of removing confusion regarding the past, the future, and the middle' —

body.text: ity anena uktatvāt. acodyam eva tv etat vistareṇa yāvan na cāparipūrṇo nirdeśa ity abhisambandhaḥ.
body.translated_text: because it was stated by this [verse]. 'But this is not a valid objection' — and so on in detail, up to: 'nor is the exposition incomplete' — this is the connection.

body.text: ubhayaṃ hi sarve saṃskṛtā dharmā iti. traiyadhvikāḥ sarve saṃskṛtā dharmāḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ. ata eva ca pratītyasamutpannā iti na kaścid viśeṣaḥ. kathaṃ tāvad akṛtā iti. bhāvinyā saṃjñayā yathānāgatāḥ saṃskṛtā ucyante. tathā pratītyasamutpannā ity abhiprāyaḥ. ābhisaṃskārikayā cetanayeti. sarvacetanānāṃ svalakṣaṇam abhidyotayann ābhisaṃskārikayety āha. sā hi vipākābhisaṃskaraṇād ābhisaṃskārikā. tayā cetitatvāt praṇihitatvāt. devo bhaviṣyāmi manuṣyo bhaviṣyāmīty evamādi. ato 'nāgatāḥ saṃskṛtā ucyante. na tu bhāvinyā saṃjñayeti tam abhiprāyaṃ vihanti. anāsravāḥ katham iti. ye sāsravā anāgatā evaṃ cetayituṃ yujyante. [Tib. 280b] ye tv anāsravā anāgatāḥ. te kathaṃ cetayituṃ yujyaṃte. codaka āha. te 'pi cetitāḥ kuśalayā cetanayā. prāptiṃ prati anāsravā dharmāḥ prāpyerann iti. nirvāṇe 'pi prasaṃga iti. nirvāṇam api saṃskṛtatvaṃ prasajyate. prāptiṃ prati cetitatvān nirvāṇaṃ prāpyeteti. tad evam anenārthenānāgatānāṃ saṃskṛtatvavyavasthāpane doṣa iti vidhyaṃtaram upanyasyate. tajjātīyatvād iti vistaraḥ. yathā na ca tāvad rūpyate yad anāgataṃ rūpaṃ rūpyamāṇarūpajātīyatvād rūpam ity atideśaḥ. tathā pratītyasamutpannadharmajātīyatvād anāgatā api dharmāḥ pratītyasamutpannā ity atideśa eṣām anāgatānāṃ bhavatīti.
body.translated_text: 'Both — because all conditioned <s>dharma</s>s [are so]' — all conditioned <s>dharma</s>s across the three times are <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination). And for this very reason, they are also <s>pratītyasamutpanna</s> (dependently originated) — there is no difference. 'How, first, are [future dharmas] unmade (<s>akṛta</s>)?' — By the designation of the future, just as future conditioned [<s>dharma</s>s] are called 'conditioned' (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), so too [they are called] 'dependently originated' — this is the intent. 'By the volition that constructs' — illuminating the specific characteristic of all volitions, he says 'by the one that constructs' (<s>ābhisaṃskārikā</s>). For that [volition] constructs retribution, hence it is 'constructing' (<s>ābhisaṃskārikā</s>). And because of being intended and directed by that — [with thoughts such as] 'I shall become a god, I shall become a human' — and the like. Therefore, future [<s>dharma</s>s] are called 'conditioned' — not merely by the designation of the future — he refutes that intent. 'How [do you account for] the outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>)?' — those that are with-outflows and future can fittingly be intended thus [Tib. 280b]. But those that are outflow-free and future — how can they fittingly be intended? The objector says: 'Those too are intended by wholesome volition — to the effect that outflow-free <s>dharma</s>s would be attained.' 'The consequence applies to <s>nirvāṇa</s> too' — the consequence that <s>nirvāṇa</s> too would be conditioned follows. Because <s>nirvāṇa</s> would also be attained, being intended with respect to attainment. 'Thus, by this meaning there is a fault in establishing the conditioned nature of future [<s>dharma</s>s]' — and an alternative is presented. 'Because of belonging to that class (<s>tajjātīyatva</s>)' — and so on in detail. Just as future form, though not yet being molded (<s>rūpyamāna</s>), is [called] form by extension because it belongs to the class of that which is being molded — similarly, even future <s>dharma</s>s, because of belonging to the class of dependently originated <s>dharma</s>s, are [called] dependently originated by extension.

body.text: (III.28ab) hetuphalabhāvād iti. yasmāt tad evāṃgaṃ hetus tad eva phalaṃ. na caivaṃ saty avyavasthānaṃ bhavatīti. pārāpāravat. hetuphalavad iti. nāvyavasthitaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pratītyasamutpannaś ca bhinnāpekṣatvāt. hetuphalavat
body.translated_text: (III.28ab) 'Because of the relationship of cause and effect' — because that very limb is a cause and that very [limb] is an effect. And this being so, there is no indeterminacy. Like near and far shore. 'Like cause and effect' — dependent origination and the dependently originated are not indeterminate, because of depending on different [reference points]. Like cause and effect

body.text: pitṛputravad vā. tatra hetuphalaṃ. tadyathā bījāṃkurādi. yathā yad apekṣya hetur vyavasthāpyate. na tad apekṣya phalaṃ. yad apekṣya phalaṃ vyavasthāpyate. na tad apekṣya hetuḥ. kiṃ tarhi. phalam [Tib. 281a] apekṣya hetur vyavasthāpyate. hetuṃ cāpekṣya phalam iti. yathā ca yam apekṣya pitā. na tam apekṣya putraḥ. yam apekṣya putraḥ. na tam apekṣya pitā. kiṃ tarhi. tatputram apekṣya piteti. pitaraṃ cāpekṣya putra iti. na ca tad avyavasthitaṃ. tadvad etat.
body.translated_text: or like father and son. Therein, [consider] cause and effect — for example, seed and sprout, etc. Just as that in reference to which something is established as a cause is not the same as that in reference to which [it is established as] an effect; and that in reference to which [something is established as] an effect is not the same as that in reference to which [it is established as] a cause. Rather: in reference to an effect, [something] is established as a cause; and in reference to a cause, [something is established as] an effect. [Tib. 281a] And just as he in reference to whom [one is] a father is not the same as he in reference to whom [one is] a son; and he in reference to whom [one is] a son is not the same as he in reference to whom [one is] a father. Rather: in reference to that son, [one is called] a father; and in reference to [that] father, [one is called] a son. And that is not indeterminate. Likewise is this [case of dependent origination].

body.text: kilety asaṃbhāvanāyāṃ. prathamā koṭir anāgatā dharmā iti. anyadharmahetutvāt pratītyasamutpādaḥ samutpadyate 'smād iti kṛtvā. na pratītyasamutpannāḥ anutpannatvāt. dvitīyārhataś caramā iti. utpannatvāt. tataḥ phalānutpatteś ca. tṛtīyā tadanya iti. arhataś caramebhyo 'nye 'tītapratyutpannā dharmāḥ. caturthy asaṃskṛtā iti. tatphalābhāvād anutpattimattvāc ca.
body.translated_text: '<s>kila</s>' is used in the sense of impossibility. The first extreme [concerns] future <s>dharmas</s>: because of being the cause of other <s>dharmas</s>, it is called <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), taking it as 'it arises from this.' [Future dharmas] are not dependently originated (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>), because they have not arisen. The second [concerns] the final [dharmas] of an <s>Arhat</s>: because they have arisen, and because no fruit arises from them. The third [concerns] those other [than these]: past and present <s>dharmas</s> other than the final [moments] of an <s>Arhat</s>. The fourth [concerns] the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>): because there is no fruit of them, and because they do not arise.

body.text: kiṃ khalv etā iṣṭaya ucyanta iti. āvasthikaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ syāt pratītyasamutpādo na pratītyasamutpannā ity evamādyāḥ. pūrvante 'jñānam iti. yasmād avidyaivoktā nānye skandhāḥ. tasmād avidyaivāṃgam iti. nītārtham etad iti darśayati. nītārtham iti vibhaktārthaṃ. hastipadopamā sūtraṃ. saṃti ca tatrānye 'pi rūpādaya iti. teṣu keśaromādiṣu. na pṛthivīdhātumātram eveti. [Tib. 281b] evam atrāpi yathāpradhānaṃ nirdeśaḥ syād iti. evam atrāpi pratītyasamutpādasūtre. dvādaśasu paṃcaskaṃdhikāsv avasthāsu yatra yasya prādhānyaṃ. tatra tasyatasya nirdeśaḥ syāt. avidyāpradhānāyām avidyeti nirdeśaḥ syāt. saṃskārādipradhānāsu avasthāsu saṃskārādīnāṃ nirdeśaḥ syāt. saṃti ca tatrāṇye 'pi rūpavedanādayo dharmā iti. na hi tatreti vistaraḥ. na hi tatra sūtre keśādayaḥ pṛthivīdhātunā nirdiśyante. keśādayaḥ katame pṛthivīdhātur iti. yata eṣāṃ keśādīnāṃ aparipūrṇo nirdeśaḥ syāt. santi hi tatrānye 'pi rūpādaya iti. rūpādisvabhāvā api keśādayo na kevalaṃ pṛthivīdhātusvabhāvā iti. api tu keśādibhir eva pṛthivīdhātur nirdiśyate. pṛthivīdhātuḥ katamaḥ. keśaromāṇīti. na ca keśādīn abhyatītyāpy atikramyāpy asti pṛthivīdhātur ādhyātmika iti. saṃpūrṇa evāsya pṛthivīdhātor nirdeśaḥ. evam ihāpy avidyādīnāṃ evam ihāpi sūtre 'vidyāsaṃskāravijñānādīnāṃ paripūrṇa eva nirdeśo na sāvaśeṣaḥ. aśrusiṃghāṇakādiṣv iti. aśrusiṃghāṇakādīni na tatra sūtre paṭhyante. tasmān na tadgataḥ pṛthivīdhātur ukta iti sāvaśeṣaḥ evety [Tib. 282a] darśayati. bhavatu vā tathaiveti vistaraḥ. yathā pṛthivīdhātor aśrusiṃghāṇakādiṣv avaśeṣam anuktatvāt. tathaivāvidyāvaśeṣam astu yadi śakyate
body.translated_text: 'Are these said to be the desired [positions]?' — there would be a state-based <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>: '<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> but not <s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>' and so forth. 'Ignorance regarding the prior end' — since only ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is stated and not other aggregates, therefore ignorance alone is the limb (<s>aṅga</s>). He shows that this is of definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>). 'Definitive meaning' means analyzed meaning. [Like in] the <s>Hastipadopamā Sūtra</s> (Sūtra of the Elephant's Footprint Simile): 'And there are also other [elements] such as form.' Among those hairs, body-hairs, and so on — it is not the earth element alone. Similarly here too, the teaching would be according to predominance. Similarly here too in the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> sūtra: in the twelve states each consisting of five aggregates, wherever there is predominance of something, there is the teaching of that. In the state predominated by ignorance, the teaching is 'ignorance.' In states predominated by formations and the rest, the teaching is of formations and the rest. 'And there are also other <s>dharmas</s> such as form and feeling.' 'For in that' — and so forth in detail. For in that sūtra, hairs and the rest are not taught by [the term] earth element — 'what is the earth element? Hairs, body-hairs' and so on. Since the teaching of these hairs and so on would be incomplete — 'for there are also other [elements] such as form' — hairs and so on have the nature of form and the like too, not merely the nature of the earth element. Nevertheless, the earth element is taught precisely through hairs and so on: 'What is the earth element? Hairs, body-hairs.' And there is no internal earth element beyond hairs and so on. The teaching of the earth element is indeed complete. Similarly here too, the teaching of ignorance and the rest — similarly here too in the sūtra, the teaching of ignorance, formations, consciousness, and the rest is indeed complete, not with remainder. 'Regarding tears, mucus, and so on' — tears, mucus, and so on are not listed in that sūtra. Therefore, he shows that the earth element included in those is not stated, and hence is with remainder. 'Or let it be just so' — and so forth in detail. Just as for the earth element, there is a remainder in tears, mucus, and so on that is unstated, similarly let there be a remainder of ignorance, if it can be shown —

body.text: darśayitum. na śakyate darśayitum iti manyamāno yadiśabdaṃ prayuṃkte. pūrvānte 'jñānam aparānte 'jñānaṃ madhyānte 'jñānaṃ buddhe 'jñānaṃ dharme 'jñānaṃ saṃghe 'jñānam ity evamādīnāṃ sarveṣām ajñānasthānānām uktatvāt. jātyaṃtarasya tu vedanāder avidyāyāṃ kiṃ kṛtaḥ prakṣepaḥ paṃcaskaṃdhikāvasthāvidyeti. na hi vedanādīnāṃ avidyātvaṃ yujyata iti. bhāvābhāvaniyama iti. yasya bhāvābhāvayor yasya bhāvābhāvau yathāsaṃkhyena niyatau tad evāṃgaṃ. avidyābhāve saṃskārāṇāṃ bhāvas tadabhāve teṣām abhāva ity avidyaivāṃgaṃ. na vedanādi. na hi vedanādisadbhāve 'rhatāṃ saṃskārā bhavaṃti. ye vijñānāṃgajanakā ity arthaḥ. tasmād āha. saty api ca paṃcaskaṃdhake saṃskārā na bhavaṃtīti vistaraḥ. saty api ca paṃcaskaṃdhake 'rhattvāvasthāyāṃ. puṇyopagaṃ yāvad āniṃjyopagaṃ ca vijñānaṃ na bhavati. pratisaṃdhivijñānaṃ na bhavatīty arthaḥ. tāṃtām upapattiṃ gacchatīty upagaṃ. puṇyopagaṃ vijñānaṃ puṇyopagaṃ. [Tib. 282b] evaṃ yāvad āniṃjyopagaṃ. tathā saty api paṃcaskaṃdhake niravidyāvasthāyāṃ tṛṣṇopādānādayaś ca na bhavantīti. yathānirdeśa eva sūtrārthaḥ. yathāsaṃkīrtitānām evāvidyādīnāṃ grahaṇam ity arthaḥ. ato vidyamānā anye skaṃdhā na pratyayāḥ saṃskārādīnām iti na te 'ṃgaṃ. evaṃ mayā śrutam ityādi. bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati gṛdhrakūṭe parvate bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham ardhatrayodaśabhir bhikṣuśataiḥ. saṃbahulaiś ca bodhisattvair iti. āyuṣamāṃ cchāriputro maitreyaṃ bodhisattvam etad avocat. śālistambham avalokya bhikṣubhyaḥ sūtram idam uktaṃ. yo bhikṣavaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyati. sa dharmaṃ paśyati. yo dharmaṃ paśyati. sa buddhaṃ paśyatīty uktvā bhagavāṃs tūṣṇīṃbabhūva. tad asya bhagavatā bhāṣitasya sūtrasya ko 'rthaḥ. pratītyasamutpādaḥ katamaḥ. dharmaḥ katamaḥ. buddhaḥ katamaḥ. kathaṃ ca pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyan dharmaṃ paśyatītyādi. tatra pratītyasamutpādo nāma idam avidyetyādi. idaṃ cābhisaṃdhāyedam uktaṃ tatra sūtre. utpādād vā tathāgatānām anutpādād vā tathāgatānāṃ sthitaiveyaṃ dharmatā dharmasthititā dharmaniyāmatā [Tib. 283a] tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā bhūtatā satyatā tattvam aviparītatāviparyastatety evamādi bhagavanmaitreyavacanaṃ. yady anāgatā na pratītyasamutpannā iti. yad uktaṃ prathamā koṭir anāgatā dharmā iti. sūtraṃ virudhyata iti. jātijarāmaraṇayoḥ pratītyasamutpannatvaṃ na syāt. uktaṃ ca avidyā yāvaj jātijarāmaraṇam iti. atha veti vistaraḥ. atha jātijarāmaraṇāṃge 'pi pratītyasamutpanne iṣṭe. tayor
body.translated_text: — to be shown. Thinking 'it cannot be shown,' he uses the word 'if.' Since all places of ignorance have been stated — 'ignorance regarding the prior end, ignorance regarding the posterior end, ignorance regarding the middle, ignorance regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, ignorance regarding the <s>Dharma</s>, ignorance regarding the <s>Saṅgha</s>' — and so on. But what basis is there for including feeling and so on of another type within ignorance, given the five-aggregate nature of states? For the identity of feeling and so on with ignorance is not logical. 'The invariability of existence and non-existence' — that whose existence and non-existence are invariably correlated with whose existence and non-existence respectively — that alone is the limb. In the absence of ignorance, formations do not exist; in its absence, they are absent — therefore ignorance alone is the limb, not feeling and the rest. For in the presence of feeling and the rest, the formations of <s>Arhats</s> do not occur — meaning those that generate the consciousness-limb. Therefore he says: 'Even when the five-aggregate [complex] exists, formations do not occur' — and so forth in detail. Even when the five-aggregate complex exists in the state of <s>Arhat</s>-hood, consciousness conducive to merit, up to consciousness conducive to the immovable (<s>āniñjya</s>), does not occur — meaning rebirth-linking consciousness does not occur. '<s>Upaga</s>' means going to such-and-such a rebirth. Consciousness conducive to merit is '<s>puṇyopaga</s>'; similarly up to conducive to the immovable. Similarly, even when the five-aggregate complex exists in the state free from ignorance, craving, clinging, and the rest do not occur. Therefore the sūtra meaning is just as stated — meaning only the listed items such as ignorance are to be accepted. Therefore, the other aggregates that exist are not conditions for formations and the rest, so they are not limbs. 'Thus have I heard' and so on. The Blessed One was dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s> on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain together with a saṅgha of monks, twelve hundred and fifty monks, and numerous bodhisattvas. The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to <s>Maitreya</s> Bodhisattva: having observed a rice-seedling, this sūtra was spoken to the monks. 'Whoever, O monks, sees dependent origination, sees <s>Dharma</s>. Whoever sees <s>Dharma</s>, sees the <s>Buddha</s>' — having said this, the Blessed One fell silent. What then is the meaning of this sūtra spoken by the Blessed One? What is <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>? What is <s>Dharma</s>? What is <s>Buddha</s>? And how does one who sees dependent origination see <s>Dharma</s>? And so on. There, <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> is named thus: 'this is ignorance' and so on. And this was said with this intention in that sūtra: 'Whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not arise, this nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>) stands firm: the fixed order of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasthititā</s>), the certainty of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmaniyāmatā</s>), suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), non-deviation from suchness (<s>avitathatā</s>), non-otherness from suchness (<s>ananyatathatā</s>), reality (<s>bhūtatā</s>), truth (<s>satyatā</s>), actuality (<s>tattva</s>), non-inversion (<s>aviparītatā</s>), non-error (<s>aviparyastatā</s>)' — such is the word of the Blessed <s>Maitreya</s>. 'If future [dharmas] are not dependently originated' — what was stated as 'the first extreme is future dharmas' — the sūtra would be contradicted, since birth and old-age-and-death would not be dependently originated. And it has been stated: 'ignorance, up to birth, old-age-and-death.' 'Or' — and so forth in detail. If the birth-and-old-age-and-death limb too is accepted as dependently originated, their —

body.text: anāgatādhvavyavasthānaṃ naiṣṭavyam iti kṛtvā. trikāṇḍavyavasthā bhidyate.
body.translated_text: — establishment in the future time-period must not be maintained. [Accordingly,] the three-section arrangement is broken.

children.translated_text: 'Two in each of the prior and posterior ends, eight in the middle' —

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: nikāyāntarīyā ity āryamahīśāsakāḥ. utpādasya saṃskṛtalakṣaṇatvād iti. yo 'yam utpādaḥ pratītyasamutpāda iti nikāyāntarīyair nityaḥ parikalpyate. sa saṃskṛtalakṣaṇam uktaṃ. trīṇīmāni saṃskṛtasya saṃskṛtalakṣaṇāni. saṃskṛtasyotpādo 'pi prajñāyate vyayo 'pi sthityanyathātvam apīti. saṃskṛtalakṣaṇatvāc cānityam ity abhiprāyaḥ. brūyās tvaṃ lakṣaṇam api nityaṃ bhavatīti. ata āha. na ca nityaṃ bhāvāṃtaram anityasya lakṣaṇaṃ yujyata iti. na hi nirvāṇam [Tib. 283b] ākāśaṃ vā kasyacid anityasya lakṣaṇaṃ bhavati. prāg utpatter hi lakṣyasya tad astīti kasya laskṣaṇaṃ. vinaṣṭe ca lakṣye kasyeti na yujyate. utpādaś ceti vistaraḥ. utpādaś ca nāmābhūtvābhāvalakṣaṇaḥ. sautrāntikanayenotpattir dharmasya tadānīṃtanaiva bhavatīti. ko'syotpādasyāsaṃskṛtasya tvanmatenāvidyādibhir abhisaṃbandhaḥ. yathaudanena pākasyāsti sambandhaḥ kartṛkriyālakṣaṇa ity odanasya pāka ity ucyate. na hy ākāśarūpayor abhisambandha utpattyutpattṛlakṣaṇo 'sti. yena rūpasyākāśam ity ucyate. evaṃ ko 'syavidyādibhir abhisaṃbandhaḥ. yatas teṣām avidyādīnāṃ pratītyasamutpāda ity ucyate. padārthaś cāsambandho bhavatīti. pratyayaṃ prāpya samudbhavaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ iti padārthaḥ. sa kathaṃ nityaś ca nāma pratītyasamutpādaś ceit.
body.translated_text: 'Those of other schools' — the noble <s>Mahīśāsakas</s>. 'Because arising is a characteristic of the conditioned' — this arising which is conceived by those of other schools as eternal [in the sense that] <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> [is eternal], is said to be a conditioned characteristic: 'These three are the characteristics of the conditioned: arising of the conditioned is perceived, decay is also [perceived], and duration-alteration also.' The intent is that because it is a conditioned characteristic, it is impermanent. You might say that a characteristic too can be eternal; therefore he says: 'Nor is it logical that a permanent separate entity be the characteristic of something impermanent.' For neither <s>nirvāṇa</s> nor space is a characteristic of anything impermanent. Before the arising of the characterized, if it [already] exists, of what is it a characteristic? And when the characterized is destroyed, of what? — this is not logical. 'And arising' — and so forth in detail. And arising by nature has the characteristic of coming-into-being from non-being. According to the <s>Sautrāntika</s> system, the production of a <s>dharma</s> is only its being-at-that-time. What then is the relation of this unconditioned arising, according to your view, with ignorance and the rest? Just as rice has a relation with cooking, having the characteristic of agent-and-action — hence 'the cooking of rice' is said. But space and form have no relation characterized as produced-and-producer, such that one would say 'the space of form.' Similarly, what is its relation with ignorance and the rest, that it is said 'the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> of ignorance and the rest'? And the word-meaning would be unconnected. The word-meaning of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> is: having reached a condition (<s>pratyaya</s>), an arising (<s>samudbhava</s>). How then can it be both eternal and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>?

body.text: pratiḥ prāptyartha iti. prāptidyotaka ity arthaḥ. itir gatāv iti. dhātvarthaḥ. pariṇāmād iti. anekārthā hi dhātavaḥ. pratiś copasargaḥ prāptidyotaka ity ayam itir gatyartham ujjhitvā prāptyartham āpadyate. padiḥ sattārtha iti. padiḥ sattāyām iti. teneti kāraṇena. pūrvakālāyāṃ kriyāyāṃ ktvāvidher iti. samānakartṛkayoḥ pūrvakāla iti vacanāt. na cāsau pūrvam utpādāt [Tib. 284a] kaścid astīti sautrāṃtikamatena. na cāpy akartṛkāsti kriyeti. kartari sati kriyāyā vyavasthāpanāt. āha cātreti. etad vaiyākaraṇacodyaṃ ślokenopanibadhnāty ācāryaḥ.
body.translated_text: '<s>Prati</s>' has the meaning of attainment' — meaning it indicates attainment. '<s>Iti</s> is in the sense of going' — this is the meaning of the verbal root. 'Due to transformation' — for verbal roots have multiple meanings. And <s>prati</s> is a prefix indicating attainment; this root <s>i</s>, abandoning the meaning of going, takes on the meaning of attainment. '<s>Pad</s> is in the sense of existence' — <s>pad</s> is in the sense of being. 'Therefore' — for that reason. 'The <s>ktvā</s>-suffix being in the prior action' — from the rule: 'the prior action [takes ktvā] when the agent is the same.' And according to the <s>Sautrāntika</s> view, nothing exists prior to arising. And there is no action without an agent, since action is established only when there is an agent. 'And he says here' — the <s>Ācārya</s> ties up this grammatical objection in a verse:

body.text: prāpnoty
body.translated_text: attains —

children.translated_text: 'since it does not exist, this is not logical.'

body.text: na hy avidyamānaḥ kartā snānādikriyāṃ kurvan dṛṣṭa iti.
body.translated_text: For a non-existent agent is not seen performing an action such as bathing.

body.text: atha manyase pratītyakriyāṃ samutpādakriyāṃ ca saha karotīty evaṃ.
body.translated_text: if you think it performs the action of reaching and the action of arising simultaneously, then —

body.text: ktvāpratyayaḥ. kasmāt.
body.translated_text: the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix [is not established]. Why?

children.translated_text: 'Because [<s>ktvā</s>] is prescribed for the prior action.'

body.text: pūrvasmiṃ kāle vidhānaṃ ktvāpratyayasya. samānakartṛkayoḥ pūrvakāla iti vacanāt ktvāpratyayo na siddho bhavet. punar utpattāv iti. utpannasya punar utpattau kalpyamānāyām anavasthāprasaṃgaḥ. dvitīye tṛtīye kṣaṇe punaḥpunar utpadyata ity aniṣṭhāprasaṃgaḥ. athānāgata iti vistaraḥ. alabdhātmako 'nāgata iti katham asato 'labdhātmabhāvasya kartṛtvaṃ sidhyati. akartṛkā vā kriyā kathaṃ sidhyati. yata evam ato yadavastha utpadyate śābdikasya śabdavidaḥ. tadavastha eva mama pratyeti. kimavasthaś ceti. kāvasthāsyeti kimavasthaḥ. utpādābhimukho 'nāgata iti. na sarvo 'nāgata utpadyate. kiṃ tarhi. utpādābhimukhaḥ. utpāde 'bhimukhaḥ. utpitsur ity arthaḥ. tadavastha eva [Tib. 284b] utpādābimukhāvastha eva. pratyetīty ucyate. aniṣpannaṃ cedam iti vistaraḥ. śābdikānām idam śābdakīyaṃ kartuḥ kriyāyāś ca vyavasthānaṃ. kasmāt. bhavituḥ kartṛrūpakalpitād arthāt kriyārūpakalpitāyā bhūter anyatvadarśanāt. tasmād acchalaṃ bhavaty utpadyate pratyetīty evamādiṣu.
body.translated_text: The prescription of the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix is for the prior action. From the rule 'the prior action when the agent is the same,' the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix would not be established. 'In re-arising' — if re-arising of what has already arisen is conceived, there would be the consequence of infinite regress: arising again and again in the second, third instants — the consequence of non-termination. 'Or if future' — and so forth in detail. If a future [dharma] that has not obtained its own nature — how can agency be established for what is non-existent, for what has not obtained its own nature? Or how can there be action without an agent? Therefore, whatever state [a dharma] is in when it arises for the grammarian — in that very state it 'reaches' (<s>pratyeti</s>) for me. 'In what state?' — meaning, what is its state? 'Facing arising, [though still] future' — not every future [dharma] arises; rather, [only] one facing arising, oriented toward arising — meaning, one about to arise. 'In that very state' — in the very state of facing arising, it is said to 'reach.' 'And this is unaccomplished' — and so forth in detail. This establishment of agent and action belongs to the grammarians. Why? Because otherness is seen between the meaning conceived as the agent-form of the one-who-will-be and the becoming conceived as the action-form. Therefore there is no [real] deception in [expressions like] 'it comes into being,' 'it arises,' 'it reaches,' and so on.

body.text: āha cātreti. tatsiddhāntena prakriyāṃ darśayati.
body.translated_text: 'And he says here' — he demonstrates the procedure through that established doctrine.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. asann abhāvaḥ alabdhātmakaḥ utpadyate yathā.
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. What is non-existent, i.e., an absence, one that has not obtained its own nature, arises — just as.

body.text: asann ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: Meaning: [it reaches while] non-existent.

children.translated_text: 'If, on the other hand, it is existent' —

body.text: atha labdhātmaka utpadyata iti kalpyate.
body.translated_text: if it is conceived that one who has obtained its own nature arises —

children.translated_text: 'there would be the non-termination [fallacy]: the arisen arises.'

body.text: utpanno 'pi punar utpadyate ity anavasthānād anyadaniṣṭhā prāpnoti. tathā hi sāṃkhyamatānusāreṇa sata evotpādā nāsata iti tad etad adhikṛtya bravīti.
body.translated_text: Since even what has arisen would arise again, due to the non-termination [regress], a further non-termination follows. For according to the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view, only the existent arises, not the non-existent — with reference to that, he says:

body.text: vāśabdo matavikalpārthaḥ. yadi bhavatāṃ sann utpadyata iti pakṣaḥ. asmākam api sann utpadyate. vaibhāṣikanayenānāgatānām astitvāt. sautrāntikanayena ca janakadharmabījasadbhāvāt. tataḥ kim idam ucyate. na cāsau pūrvam utpādāt kaścid asti. yaḥ pratītyottarakālam utpadyata iti. atha vā yadi tarhi sann evotpadyate. pūrvam eva ghaṭo mṛtpiṇḍādīn anapekṣya svataḥ
body.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) is for the purpose of distinguishing positions. If your position is that 'what exists arises,' our [position] too is that what exists arises — according to the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> system, because of the existence of future [dharmas]; and according to the <s>Sautrāntika</s> system, because of the real existence of the seed of the generating <s>dharma</s>. Then why is this said: 'And that [thing] does not exist as anything prior to arising — [yet] depending [on conditions], it arises at a later time'? Alternatively, if indeed what exists alone arises, then it follows that the pot, even prior [to production], is established as existing by itself, without depending on clay-lumps and the rest

body.text: prasiddho 'stīti prāpnoti. apare punar vyācakṣate.
body.translated_text: . Others, however, explain:

body.text: atha mā bhūd aniṣṭheti. asann utpadyate iti pratipadyate. punas tad evopatiṣṭhate.
body.translated_text: thus. Lest it be unaccomplished — [if one says] 'what does not exist arises,' one accepts [that position]. Then the very same [objection] presents itself again:

children.text: asann utpadyate yadvat pratyety api tatheti
children.translated_text: 'Just as what does not exist arises, so too it depends [on conditions]' —

body.text: siddho naḥ pakṣa iti pūrvavad vācyaṃ. yad apy uktam ekasya hi kartur dvayoḥ kriyayoḥ pūrvakālāyāṃ kriyāyāṃ ktvāvidhir bhavatīti tad vyabhicārayann āha.
body.translated_text: thus — 'our position is established' — should be stated as before. As to what was also said: 'For when there is a single agent and two actions, the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix applies to the prior action' — refuting that, he says:

children.translated_text: 'The <s>ktvā</s>-suffix exists even in the case of simultaneity' —

body.text: vistaraḥ. samānakālāyām api kriyāyāṃ ktvāvidhir dṛṣṭaḥ. tadyathā
body.translated_text: thus the elaboration. The <s>ktvā</s>-suffix is observed even in a simultaneous action. For example:

children.translated_text: 'Having reached the lamp, the darkness has gone' —

body.text: iti. atra na pūrvaṃ tamo dīpaṃ prāpnoti paścād gacchati vinaśyati ity arthaḥ. kiṃ tarhi. tasminn eva kāle tamo dīpaṃ prāpnuvad vinaśyati. atha mataṃ. samanaṃtaram eva tan na yugapad iti. ataḥ punar idam ucyate.
body.translated_text: thus. Here, the darkness does not first reach the lamp and afterwards go, i.e., perish — this is the meaning. Rather, at that very time, the darkness, while reaching the lamp, perishes. But if you think: 'that is immediately sequential, not simultaneous' — therefore this further is said:

body.text: na hy asau pūrvaṃ mukhaṃ vyādadāti vidārayati paścāc chete. kiṃ tarhi. yo mukhaṃ vyādadac chete. sa mukhaṃ vyādāya śeta ity ucyate. atha mataṃ. pūrvam asau mukhaṃ vyādadāti. paścāc chete iti. ata āha.
body.translated_text: thus. For he does not first open, i.e., separate, his mouth and afterwards sleep. Rather, he who sleeps while opening his mouth — of him it is said 'he sleeps having opened his mouth.' But if you think: 'he first opens his mouth, and afterwards sleeps' — therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'If afterwards, why not with [the mouth] closed?'

body.text: yaḥ kaścin mukhaṃ vyādāpānaṃtaraṃ ca saṃvṛtya śete. sa mukhaṃ vyādāya śeta ity ucyeta na cocyate. tena jñāyate. yo mukhaṃ vyādadac chete. sa mukhaṃ vyādāya śete ity ucyate iti.
body.translated_text: Anyone who, immediately after opening his mouth, closes it and then sleeps — of him it would be said 'he sleeps having opened his mouth,' but it is not [so] said. From this it is known: he who sleeps while opening his mouth — of him it is said 'he sleeps having opened his mouth.'

body.text: anye punar iti. bhadantaśrīlātaḥ pratir vīpsārtha iti. nānāvācinām adhikaraṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ kriyāguṇābhyāṃ vyāptum icchā vīpsā. tām ayaṃ pratir dyotayati. [Tib. 285b] itau gatau sādhava ityāḥ. tatra sādhur iti yatpratyayaḥ. itau vinaṣṭau sādhavaḥ. anavasthāyina ity arthaḥ. samupasargaḥ samavāyārthaṃ dyotayati. utpūrvaḥ padiḥ prādurbhāvārthaḥ. dhātvarthapariṇāmāt. tāṃ tāṃ sāmagrīṃ pratīti. prater vīpsārthatāṃ darśayati. ityānāṃ vinaśvarāṇāṃ samavāyenotpādaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ. na kaścid dharma eka utpadyate sahotpādaniyamāt. rūpādīnāṃ
body.translated_text: 'Others, however' — the Venerable <s>Śrīlāta</s>. The prefix <s>prati</s> has the meaning of distributiveness (<s>vīpsā</s>). The desire to pervade all objects designated by diverse [terms] with both action and quality is distributiveness (<s>vīpsā</s>). This prefix <s>prati</s> expresses that. [Tib. 285b] '[Those that have] gone (<s>ita</s>) to going (<s>gatau</s>)' — gone to perishing — are <s>sādhavaḥ</s> (good ones, i.e., things). Therein, '<s>sādhu</s>' is [formed with] the <s>yat</s>-suffix. 'Gone to perishing' means 'non-abiding' — this is the meaning. The prefix <s>sam</s> expresses the meaning of conjunction (<s>samavāya</s>). The root <s>pad</s> preceded by <s>ut</s> means 'manifestation' — because of the transformation of the root-meaning. 'Depending on (<s>pratītya</s>) this and that assemblage [of conditions]' — he shows the distributive meaning of <s>prati</s>. The arising, through conjunction, of [things that are] perishable is dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). No <s>dharma</s> whatsoever arises singly, because of the rule of co-arising — of form and the rest:

children.translated_text: 'In the desire [realm], the smallest unit (<s>paramāṇu</s>) consists of eight substances, excluding sound' —

body.text: yāvac
body.translated_text: up to:

body.text: iti niyamāt. eṣā tu kalpaneti vistaraḥ. pratir vīpsārtha ity evamādikā kalpanātraiva
body.translated_text: because of this rule. 'But this is a fabrication' — thus the elaboration. The fabrication that the prefix <s>prati</s> has the meaning of distributiveness and so forth

body.text: pratītyasamutpādasūtre yujyate. iha kathaṃ bhaviṣyati cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpāṇi cotpadyate cakṣurvijñānam iti. na hi pratītyānāṃ cakṣūṃṣi pratītyacakṣūṃṣīti samāsaḥ saṃbhavaty arthāyogāt. cākṣur hi pratītya prāpya rūpāṇi cotpadyate cakṣurvijñānam ity ayam artho gamyate. tena tadavastham eva tac codyaṃ na yukta eṣa padārtha iti vistareṇa yad uktaṃ. katham. ekasya hi kartur dvayoḥ kriyayoḥ pūrvakālāyāṃ kriyāyāṃ ktvāvidhir bhavati. snātvā bhuṃkte iti. na ca pūrvam utpādāc cakṣurvijñānam asti. yac cakṣuḥ pūrvaṃ pratītya rūpāṇi cottarakālam utpadyate. na cāpy akartṛkā kriyeti.
body.translated_text: is fitting only in the <s>Pratītyasamutpāda</s>-<s>sūtra</s>. How would it apply here [in the formula]: 'Depending on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises'? For the compound 'depending-eyes' (<s>pratītyacakṣūṃṣi</s>) — [meaning] 'of the depending-[things], the eyes are the depending-eyes' — is not possible, because of the unsuitability of the meaning. For the meaning understood is: 'having reached, i.e., depending on, the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises.' Therefore that very objection remains as it was — 'this word-meaning is not valid' — as stated in detail. How? 'For when there is a single agent and two actions, the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix applies to the prior action — [as in] having bathed, he eats.' But eye-consciousness does not exist prior to arising — [so] how could it first depend on the eye and forms, and then arise at a later time? 'Nor is there action without an agent.'

body.text: avadhāraṇārthaṃ paryāyadvayam āha. asmin satīty etāvaty [Tib. 286a] ucyamāne. na kevalam avidyāyāṃ satyāṃ saṃskārā bhavaṃti. anyasminn api satīti gamyeta. yathā cakṣuṣi sati cakṣurvijñānaṃ bhavatīti. na cakṣuṣy eva satīty avadhāryate. tena rūpe 'pi satīti gamyate. dvitīyena tu paryāyeṇasyotpādād idam utpadyate ity anena pūrvaparyāyam evāvadhārayati. asyaivotpādād idam utpadyate. nānyasmād iti. aṃgaparaṃparāṃ vā darśayitum iti. asminn aṃge sati. avidyāṃge satīdaṃ saṃskārāṃgaṃ bhavati. asya punar aṃgasya saṃskārāṃgasyotpādād idaṃ vijñānāṃgam utpadyata iti. evam itareṣām apy aṃgānāṃ paraṃparā vaktavyā. janmaparaṃparāṃ vā. kiṃ. darśayituṃ paryāyadvayam āheti vartate. sākṣād iti vistaraḥ. sākṣāt pāraṃparyeṇa saṃtatyāvidyādīnāṃ pratyayabhāvaṃ darśayituṃ paryāyadvayam āha. asmin satīdaṃ bhavatīti sākṣāt pratyayabhāvaṃ darśayati. asyotpādād idam utpadyata iti pāraṃparyeṇa. tatra sākṣād yadāvidyāyāḥ samanaṃtaraṃ kliṣṭāḥ saṃskārā utpadyante. pāraṃparyeṇa tu yadā kuśalā utpadyaṃte. kuśalāvasthāyām avidyāyā abhāvāt. kiṃ ca. avidyā saṃskārāṇāṃ sākṣāt pratyayo vijñānādīnāṃ pāraṃparyeṇa. tad uktaṃ bhavati. avidyāṃge sati saṃskārāṃgaṃ bhavaty asya saṃskārāṃgasyotpādād idam utpadyate vijñānāṃgaṃ sākṣād avidyāpratyayaṃ pāraṃparyeṇeti. [Tib. 286b] etat sarvam ācāryamataṃ. pratiṣedhārtham ity apara iti sthaviravasuvarmā. nāsati hetau bhāvo bhavatīty ahetuvādapratiṣedhārthaṃ prathamena paryāyeṇa. nityahetuvādapratiṣedhārthaṃ na cānutpattimato nityāt prakṛtipuruṣādikāt kiṃcid utpadyata iti dvitīyena. ācārya āha. asyāṃ tu kalpanāyām iti vistaraḥ. pūrvapadasya grahaṇam anarthakam iti. asmin satīdaṃ bhavatīty asya. ubhayavādapratiṣedhasiddher iti. asyotpādād idam utpadyate ity anenaiva paryāyeṇa. hetor astitvam utpattimataś ca hetutvam ity ubhayasyāhetutvanityahetutvalakṣaṇasya vādasya pratiṣedhasiddhitaḥ pūrvaparyāyasyānarthakyaṃ prāpnoti. saṃti tarhi kecid iti vistaraḥ. santi kecid
body.translated_text: He states the two formulae for the purpose of delimitation (<s>avadhāraṇa</s>). When it is said 'this being, that comes to be' — [Tib. 286a] if only this much were stated, it would be understood that not only when ignorance exists do formations come to be, but also when something else exists — just as when the eye exists, eye-consciousness comes to be, but one does not delimit 'only when the eye exists,' since even when form exists [it also comes to be]. But by the second formula — 'from the arising of this, that arises' — he delimits the first formula itself: from the arising of this alone does that arise, not from another. Or, to show the succession of the limbs: when this limb exists — when the limb of ignorance exists — this limb of formations comes to be; and from the arising of this limb — the limb of formations — this limb of consciousness arises. Similarly, the succession of the remaining limbs too should be stated. Or, to show the succession of births: 'he states the two formulae' — this is the sentence-continuation. 'Directly and indirectly' — thus the elaboration. He states the two formulae to show the condition-nature of ignorance and the rest, both directly (<s>sākṣāt</s>) and in succession (<s>pāraṃparya</s>), through the continuum. The [formula] 'this being, that comes to be' shows the condition-nature directly. 'From the arising of this, that arises' [shows it] indirectly. Therein, 'directly' [means] when defiled formations arise immediately after ignorance. 'Indirectly,' however, [means] when wholesome [formations] arise — because of the absence of ignorance in the wholesome state. Moreover, ignorance is the direct condition of formations, and the indirect condition of consciousness and the rest. This has been said: when the limb of ignorance exists, the limb of formations comes to be; from the arising of this limb of formations, the limb of consciousness arises — the consciousness-limb [being] directly [conditioned by] ignorance and indirectly [as well]. [Tib. 286b] All this is the Master's [Vasubandhu's] position. 'For the purpose of negation' — 'another' — [this is] the Elder <s>Vasuvarman</s>. [The formula] 'it is not the case that when the cause does not exist, the effect comes to be' — by the first formula, for the purpose of negating the no-cause doctrine (<s>ahetuvāda</s>). For the purpose of negating the permanent-cause doctrine (<s>nityahetuvāda</s>) — 'nor from a permanent, non-arising [entity] such as <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and the rest does anything arise' — by the second [formula]. The Master responds: 'But in this fabrication' — thus the elaboration. 'The inclusion of the first term is purposeless' — the [formula] 'this being, that comes to be' — this one. 'Because the negation of both doctrines is accomplished' — by the formula 'from the arising of this, that arises' alone, the negation of both doctrines — characterized by no-cause and permanent-cause — is accomplished: the existence of the cause and the cause-nature of what has arising [are both established]. Therefore the purposelessness of the first formula follows. 'There are, however, some' — thus the elaboration. There are some

body.text:
vādinaḥ. ya ātmani saty āśrayabhūte avidyāyā āśrayabhūte saṃskārādīnāṃ saṃskāravijñānanāmarūpādīnāṃ bhāvam utpādaṃ kalpayaṃti. avidyādīnāṃ cāvidyāsaṃskārādīnāṃ utpādāt tadutpattiṃ saṃskārādyutpattiṃ kalpayantīty adhikṛtaṃ. ataḥ kāraṇāt teṣāṃ vādināṃ kalpanāṃ paryudāsayituṃ pratiṣeddhum idaṃ nirdhārayāṃ babhūvāmredayāṃ babhūva. kim ity āha. yasyaivotpādāt yāvat skaṃdhasya samudayo bhavatīti. yasyaivotpādād yad utpadyate. tasminn eva sati tad bhavati. nānyasminn ātmani. yad utāvidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ. [Tib. 287a] avidyāyām eva satyāṃ saṃskārā bhavaṃti. nānyasmin yāvad evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskaṃdhasya samudayo bhavati. kathaṃ. jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavaṃti. evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati. jātyām eva satyāṃ jarāmaraṇādayaḥ saṃbhavaṃti. nānyasminn ātmani. anyathā hy asmin satīdaṃ bhavatīty ucyamāne vaktāras syuḥ. ātmani saty āśrayabhūte avidyādiṣu satsu saṃskārādayo bhavantīti. atha punar dvitīyam eva paryāyaṃ brūyād asyotpādād idam utpadyata iti. evam api tathaiva kalpeyuḥ. satyam avidyādīnām utpādāt saṃskārādaya utpadyante. ātmani tu saty āśrayabhūta iti. ataḥ paryāyadvayena nirdhārayati. yasyotpādād yad utpadyate. tasminn eva sati tad bhavati. nānyasmin ātmani saty āśrayabhūta iti. ācāryā iti pūrvācāryāḥ. aprahīṇajñāpanārtham utpattijñāpanārthaṃ ca. avidyāyāṃ satyām aprahīṇāyāṃ saṃskārā bhavaṃti. na prahīyanta iti prathamena paryāyeṇa darśayati. tasyā evotpādād utpadyanta iti dvitīyena darśayati. evaṃ yāvaj jātyāṃ satyāṃ aprahīṇāyāṃ jarāmaranādayo bhavaṃti. na prahīyaṃte. tasyā evotpādād utpadyanta iti. sthityutpattisaṃdarśanārtham ity apara [Tib. 287b] iti bhadantaśrīlātaḥ. tadarthaṃ paryāyadvayam āheti. yāvat kāraṇasrotas tāvat kāryasroto bhavatīti prathamena paryāyeṇa. kāraṇasyaivotpādāt kāryam utpadyata iti dvitīyena. utpāde tv adhikṛta iti. pratītyasamutpādaṃ vo bhikṣavo deśayiṣyāmīty adhikṛte. kaḥ prasaṃgaḥ kaḥ prastāvaḥ sthitivacanasya. asmin satīdaṃ bhavatīty anena yāvat kāraṇasrotas tiṣṭhati tāvat kāryasrotas tiṣṭhatīti evam asya sthityartho varṇyata iti. bhinnakramaṃ ca bhagavān kim arthaṃ ācakṣīt. utpattir hi prathamaṃ bhavati. paścāt sthitiḥ. utpattipratibaddhā sthitir iti kṛtvā. asyotpādād idam utpadyata iti pūrvaṃ vaktavyaṃ syāt. paścād idam asmin satīdaṃ bhavati. na tv evam. ato nāyam artha iti. punar āheti.
sa eva bhadantaśrīlātaḥ. ācāryaḥ pratyāha. eṣa ced iti vistaraḥ. asmin satīdaṃ na bhavatīty evāvakṣyad iti. nātraivābhāvanirdeśo yuktarūpa iti darśayati. pūrvaṃ ca kāryasyotpādam iti. asyotpādād idam utpadyata iti pūrvam avakṣyat. utpādapūrvakatvād
body.translated_text:
proponents who, when the self exists as a basis, fabricate the coming-to-be, i.e., the arising, of formations, consciousness, name-and-form, and the rest, with ignorance as the basis; and who fabricate from the arising of ignorance, formations, and the rest the arising of formations and the rest — this is the topic at hand. For this reason, in order to exclude, i.e., to negate, the fabrication of those proponents, this was determined and repeated. What [is meant]? He says: 'of whatever [limb] alone, from the arising of which, up to: there comes to be the origination of the [entire] mass of suffering.' From the arising of whatever [limb] alone whatever arises, when that alone exists, that comes to be — not when another, [namely] a self, [exists]. That is to say: formations are conditioned by ignorance — [Tib. 287a] when ignorance alone exists, formations come to be, not when another, [namely] a self, [exists] — up to: thus there comes to be the origination of this entire great mass of suffering. How? Birth-conditioned are aging, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, displeasure, and despair — they come to be. Thus there comes to be the origination of this entire great mass of suffering — when birth alone exists, aging and death and the rest come to be, not when another, [namely] a self, [exists]. Otherwise — if, when it is said 'this being, that comes to be,' the speakers would [mean]: 'when the self exists as basis, when ignorance and the rest exist, formations and the rest come to be.' But if he were to state only the second formula — 'from the arising of this, that arises' — even so, they would fabricate in just the same way: 'truly, from the arising of ignorance and the rest, formations and the rest arise — but when the self exists as basis.' Therefore, by the pair of formulae, he determines: from the arising of whatever [limb] whatever arises, when that alone exists, that comes to be — not when another, [namely] a self, exists as basis. 'The <s>Ācāryas</s>' — the former masters. 'For the purpose of making known the non-abandonment and for the purpose of making known the arising' — when ignorance exists, i.e., is not abandoned, formations come to be, they are not abandoned — this the first formula shows. From the arising of that very [ignorance], they arise — this the second shows. Similarly, up to: when birth exists, i.e., is not abandoned, aging, death, and the rest come to be, they are not abandoned; from the arising of that very [birth], they arise. 'For the purpose of showing persistence and arising' — 'another' [Tib. 287b] — [this is] the Venerable <s>Śrīlāta</s>. For that purpose he states the pair of formulae. 'As long as the stream of cause [flows], so long the stream of effect comes to be' — by the first formula. 'From the arising of the cause alone, the effect arises' — by the second. 'But when arising is the topic' — when it is the topic [introduced by]: 'I shall teach you, monks, dependent origination.' What occasion, what introduction is there for a statement about persistence? [Reply:] By the [formula] 'this being, that comes to be,' 'as long as the stream of cause persists, so long the stream of effect persists' — thus the meaning of persistence is described. 'And why did the Blessed One state [them] in reversed order?' For arising occurs first, then persistence. Since persistence depends on arising — 'from the arising of this, that arises' should be stated first, and then 'this being, that comes to be.' But it is not [stated] thus. Therefore this is not the meaning. 'He says further' —
that very Venerable <s>Śrīlāta</s>. The Master replies: 'If this is [the meaning]' — thus the elaboration. [He says:] '[He] would have said: this being, that does not come to be' — he shows that the indication of non-existence is not fitting here precisely. 'And first, the arising of the effect' — he would have said first 'from the arising of this, that arises,' because destruction is preceded by arising

body.text: vināśasya.
body.translated_text: of destruction.

body.text: sūtra uktaṃ jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavantīti jarāmaraṇasaṃgṛhītā evaṃ te. nāṃgāṃtaram ity avagantavyaṃ.
