[Tib. 288a] tatra sattvāsattvasaṃkhyātasya viṣayasya pariṇāmād ātmabhāvapariṇāmāc caite bhavaṃti. daurmanasyasaṃprayukto vitarkaḥ śokaḥ. śokasamutthitapralāpaḥ paridevaḥ. duḥkhadaurmanasye vyākhyāte. vicchinnavegaṃ daurmanasyam upāyāsaḥ. śokaparidevapūrvakaḥ śrama upāyāsa ity apare. bālo hīti vistaraḥ. bālaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ saṃskāramātram iti. mātragrahaṇam ātmapratiṣedhārtham. aprajānann ity āveṇikīm avidyāṃ darśayati. ātmadṛṣṭy asmimānābhiniviṣṭaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ kāyādibhiḥ kāyavāṅmanobhis trividhaṃ karma puṇyāpuṇyāniṃjyalakṣaṇam ārabhate. āniṃjyam iti. igiḥ prakṛtyantaraṃ tasyaivaitad rūpaṃ. ejater etat rūpam āneṃjyam iti vā pāṭhaḥ. āyatisukhārthaṃ puṇyam iti. anāgatajanmasukhārthaṃ. kiṃ. kāmāvacaraṃ kuśalaṃ karma. sukhaduḥkhāsukhārtham āniṃjyam iti. rūpārūpyāvacaraṃ kuśalaṃ. sukhārtham ā tṛtīyād dhyānāt. tasmād ūrdhvam aduḥkāsukhārthaṃ. aihikasukhārtham apuṇyam iti. ihasukhāpekṣayā tat kṛtaṃ nāyatisukhāpekṣayety arthaḥ. karmākṣepavaśād yathoktaṃ karmāvedhavaśāt. tāṃtāṃ gatiṃ narakādikāṃ gacchati. jvālāgamanayogena. yathā dīrghā tṛṇānusaktā jvālā [Tib. 288b] gacchatīty ucyate. tathā vijñānasaṃtatibhir antarābhavasambandhād antarābhavasaṃbandhenātiviprakṛṭadeśām api tāṃtāṃ gatiṃ gacchati. evaṃ ca kṛtveti. yadi saṃskārapratyayaṃ antarābhavapratisaṃdhicittam upādāya yāvad upapattikṣaṇaḥ sarvāsau vijñānasaṃtatiḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam abhipretaṃ tad upapannaṃ bhavati. vijñānāṃganirdeśe vijñānāṃgasya tṛtīyasya nirdeśe. vijñānaṃ katamat. ṣaḍ vijñānakāyā iti. anyathā hi yadi ṣaṇṇāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ saṃtatir nābhipretā syāt. saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānaṃ pratisaṃdhicittam evābhipretaṃ syāt. atra ṣaḍ vijñānakāyā iti noktaṃ syāt. evaṃ tu vaktavyaṃ syāt. vijñānaṃ katmat. manovijñānam iti. na hi pratisaṃdhikṣaṇe paṃcavijñānakāyasaṃbhavo 'sti. manovijñānenaiva pratisaṃdhibandhāt.
body.translated_text: In the sūtra it is stated: "Conditioned by birth, old-age-and-death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and distress arise." Thus these are included within old-age-and-death — they should be understood as not being separate limbs. There, these arise from the transformation of objects, both those counted as sentient beings and those not, and from the transformation of one's own bodily existence. Grief (<s>śoka</s>) is mental discursive thought (<s>vitarka</s>) conjoined with dejection (<s>daurmanasya</s>). Lamentation (<s>parideva</s>) is wailing that arises from grief. Suffering and dejection have already been explained. Distress (<s>upāyāsa</s>) is dejection whose force has been cut off. Others say: distress is exhaustion preceded by grief and lamentation. "A fool" — and so forth in detail. A fool is an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). "Merely formations" — the word "merely" is for the purpose of negating a self. "Not knowing" — he shows the specific ignorance. One who is attached to and established in the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) and the conceit "I am" (<s>asmimāna</s>) initiates threefold <s>karma</s> — characterized as meritorious, demeritorious, and imperturbable (<s>āniñjya</s>) — through body, speech, and mind. "<s>Āniñjya</s>" — the root <s>iñj</s> is a different root-form; this is its form. Or the reading is: "this is the form of the root <s>ej</s>, <s>ānejya</s>." "Meritorious [karma] is for the sake of future happiness" — for the sake of happiness in a future birth. What [kind]? Wholesome <s>karma</s> belonging to the Desire Realm. "Imperturbable [karma] is for the sake of pleasure, suffering, and neither-pleasure-nor-suffering" — wholesome [karma] belonging to the Form and Formless Realms. For the sake of pleasure, up to the third <s>dhyāna</s>. Above that, for the sake of neither-suffering-nor-pleasure. "Demeritorious [karma] is for the sake of present happiness" — the meaning is: that is performed with regard to present happiness, not with regard to future happiness. "Through the force of karmic projection" — through the force of the stated karmic penetration, one goes to the respective destinies — those of hell-beings and the rest. "By the manner of a flame's going" — just as a long flame, attached to grass, is said to "go," so too, through the consciousness-continuum, by connection with the intermediate existence, one goes to the respective destinies, even in very distant places. "Having done so" — if the rebirth-linking consciousness of the intermediate existence is taken as conditioned by formations, then the entire consciousness-continuum up to the moment of rebirth — of the six consciousness-groups — is intended as consciousness conditioned by formations, and this is established. In the exposition of the consciousness-limb, in the exposition of the third limb — consciousness: "What is consciousness? The six consciousness-groups." For otherwise, if the continuum of the six consciousness-groups were not intended, and consciousness conditioned by formations were intended as only the rebirth-linking mind, then it would not be stated here "the six consciousness-groups." Rather, it should be stated thus: "What is consciousness? Mental consciousness" — for at the moment of rebirth-linking, there is no possibility of the five sense-consciousness groups, since rebirth-linking occurs through mental consciousness alone.

children.translated_text: "Cutting-off, reconnection, dispassion, decline, falling, and rebirth — these are accepted as belonging to mental consciousness alone"

body.text: iti vacanāt. vibhaṃga evaṃ nirdeśād iti. pratītyasmutpādasūtre nāmarūpavibhaṃga evaṃ nirdeśāt. nāma katamat. catvāro 'rūpiṇaḥ skandhā iti. rūpaṃ katamat. yatkimcid rūpam iti vistareṇa. yāvad yac cedaṃ rūpaṃ yac ca nāma.
body.translated_text: — because of this statement. "Because of this exposition in the analysis" — because of this exposition in the analysis of name-and-form in the <s>Pratītyasamutpāda</s> sūtra. "What is name (<s>nāma</s>)? The four formless aggregates." "What is form (<s>rūpa</s>)? Whatever form" — in detail, up to — "whatever is form and whatever is name,

body.text: tad ubhayaṃ nāmarūpam ity ucyata [Tib. 289a] iti. kāmatṛṣṇeti. kāmāvacarī tṛṣṇā. rūpatṛṣṇeti. yā sukhāyāṃ triṣu dhyāneṣu. aduḥkhāsukhāyāṃ caturthe. aduḥkhāsukhāyām ārūpyatṛṣṇeti. ārūpyāvacarī. kāmādīnām upādānam iti. kāmyanta iti kāmāḥ. guṇyanta iti guṇāḥ. kāmā eva guṇāḥ kāmaguṇāḥ. ke punas te. rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāni. dṛṣṭayo dvāṣaṣṭi yathā brahmajāla iti. brahmajālasūtradarśanena tā dṛṣṭayo boddhavyāḥ. kukkuragovratādīnīti. ādiśabdena mṛgavratādīni gṛhyante. nirgranthādīnām iti. ādiśabdena pāṇḍarabhikṣvādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ. brāhṃaṇetyādivistaraḥ. brāhmaṇānāṃ daṇḍājinaṃ pāśupatānāṃ jaṭābhasma. parivrājakānāṃ tridaṇḍamauṇḍyaṃ ādiśabdadvayena kāpālikādīnāṃ kapāladhāraṇādīni gṛhyante. tatsamādānaṃ śīlavratopādānaṃ. ātmeti vādo 'sminn ity ātmavādaḥ. yathoktaṃ. ye kecic chramaṇā brāhmaṇā vā ātmeti samanupaśyantaḥ. [Tib. 289b] samanupśyaṃti sarve ta imān eva paṃcopādānaskandhān iti vistaraḥ. ātmadṛṣṭyasmimānāv ity apara ātmavādam āhuḥ. ātmano hy asattvād ātmavādopādānām iti vādaśabdopanyāse prayojanaṃ darśayati. bālo 'śrutavān pṛthagjana iti. yasya pūrvābhyāsavāsanānirjātopapattilābhikā prajñā nāsti. sa bālaḥ. yasyāgamajā nāsti. so 'śrutavān. yasyādhigamajā satyābhisamayajā nāsti. sa pṛthagjanaḥ. prajñaptim anupatita iti. yathā saṃjñā yathā ca vyavahāraḥ. tathānugata ity arthaḥ. teṣām iti kāmādīnāṃ. chandarāga iti. aprāpteṣu viṣayeṣu prārthanā chandaḥ. prāpteṣu rāgaḥ. teṣu kāmādiṣu yaḥ chandarāgaḥ. tad upādānaṃ. na tu
body.translated_text: both together are called name-and-form." Desire-craving (<s>kāmatṛṣṇā</s>) is craving belonging to the Desire Realm. Form-craving (<s>rūpatṛṣṇā</s>) is [craving] for pleasure in the three <s>dhyāna</s>s and for neither-suffering-nor-pleasure in the fourth. Formless-craving (<s>ārūpyatṛṣṇā</s>) — for neither-suffering-nor-pleasure — is that belonging to the Formless Realm. "Grasping of desires and the rest" — things desired are "desires" (<s>kāma</s>); things valued are "qualities" (<s>guṇa</s>); desires that are qualities are "desire-qualities" (<s>kāmaguṇa</s>). And what are they? Forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles. "The sixty-two views as in the <s>Brahmajāla</s>" — those views should be understood by reference to the <s>Brahmajāla</s> sūtra. "Dog-vow, cow-vow, and the rest" — by the word "and the rest," deer-vow and others are included. "Of the <s>Nirgranthas</s> and the rest" — by the word "and the rest," the white-robed monks and others are included. "Of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>" — and so forth in detail. The staff and deer-skin of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; the matted hair and ashes of the <s>Pāśupatas</s>; the triple staff and tonsure of the wandering ascetics; by the two occurrences of "and the rest," the skull-bearing practices and so forth of the <s>Kāpālikas</s> and others are included. The adoption of these is grasping of rules and rituals (<s>śīlavratopādāna</s>). "A doctrine about self" (<s>ātmavāda</s>) — discourse (<s>vāda</s>) about a self. As stated: "Whatever <s>śramaṇas</s> or <s>brāhmaṇas</s> regard [things] as a self — they all regard precisely these five aggregates of grasping" — and so forth in detail. Others call the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) and the conceit "I am" (<s>asmimāna</s>) "self-doctrine." Since the self does not exist, he shows the purpose of introducing the term "doctrine" (<s>vāda</s>) in "grasping of self-doctrine" (<s>ātmavādopādāna</s>). "A foolish, unlearned ordinary person" — one who does not possess wisdom born from the habitual impressions of previous practice, obtained at birth — that one is a fool. One who does not possess [wisdom] born from scripture — that one is unlearned. One who does not possess [wisdom] born from realization, from the comprehension of the truths — that one is an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). "Having fallen into convention" — the meaning is: having followed in accordance with designation and common usage. "Of those" — of desires and the rest. "Desire-and-passion" (<s>chandarāga</s>) — longing (<s>chanda</s>) is yearning for objects not yet obtained; passion (<s>rāga</s>) is [attachment] to objects already obtained. Whatever desire-and-passion there is toward those desires and the rest — that is grasping. But not —

body.text: abhiprāyaḥ. paunarbhavikam iti punarbhavaphalaṃ. idam atra bhavasyeti. idam atra bhavasya svalakṣaṇaṃ svabhāva ity arthaḥ. vijñānāvakrāntiyogeneti. jvālāgamanayogenāntarābhavasaṃbandhād anāgataṃ janma jātiḥ paṃcaskaṃdhikā nāmarūpasvabhāvatvāt. jarāmaraṇaṃ yathā nirdiṣṭaṃ sūtra iti. jarā katamā. yat tat khālityaṃ [Tib. 290a] pālityaṃ iti vistaraḥ. maraṇaṃ katamat. yā teṣāṃteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasmāttasmāc cyutiś cyavanam iti vistaraḥ. kevalasyātmarahitasyety arthaṃ darśayati. mahata ity anādyantasya. duḥkhaskandhasyeti duḥkhasamūhasya. sa eva tu vaibhāṣikanyāyo yaḥ pūrvam ukta
body.translated_text: — this is the intent. "Productive of renewed existence" (<s>paunarbhavika</s>) means having renewed existence as its fruit. "This is the defining characteristic of existence here" — the meaning is: this is the own-characteristic, the intrinsic nature, of existence here. "By the manner of the descent of consciousness" — by the manner of a flame's going, through connection with the intermediate existence, the future birth is <s>jāti</s> (birth), consisting of five aggregates, because of having the nature of name-and-form. Old-age-and-death are as stated in the sūtra: "What is old age? That which is graying of hair, wrinkling" — and so forth in detail. "What is death? The falling away, the departing of those various beings from those various [states]" — and so forth in detail. He shows the meaning of "merely" (<s>kevala</s>) as "devoid of a self." "Great" means without beginning or end. "Mass of suffering" (<s>duḥkhaskandha</s>) means an accumulation of suffering. "But the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> method is indeed that which was stated before" —

body.text: iti. dvādaśa paṃcaskaṃdhikā avasthā dvādaśaṃgānīti.
body.translated_text: — that is: the twelve states consisting of five aggregates are the twelve limbs.

body.text: (III.28cd) yā na vidyā. cakṣurādiṣv api prasaṃga iti. cakṣuḥśrotrādīny avidyā prasajyante. tāny api hi na vidyeti kṛtvā. na kiṃcid syād iti. yadi vidyāyā abhāvo 'vidyā adravyaṃ syād ity arthaḥ. na caitad yuktam iti. pratyayabhāvenopadeśāt. tadvipakṣa iti. virodhe nañ iti darśayati. na tu yaḥ kaścid anyo mitrād iti. na paryudāsamātra iti darśayati. nāpi mitrabhāva iti. nābhāvārtha iti darśayati. adharmānārthakāryādayaś ceti. ādiśabdenāyuktyavyavahārāmanuṣyādayo gṛhyaṃte. dharmādipratidvandvabhūtā iti. dharmārthakāryayuktivyavahāramanuṣyādipratidvandvabhūtāḥ. na tu ye kecid anye dharmādibhyaś [Tib. 290b] cakṣurādayaḥ. nāpi dharmādyabhāvaḥ. evam avidyāpīti vistaraḥ. kuta etat. pratyayabhāvenopadeśāt. avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā iti. na cāvidyāyā anyeṣāṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ pratyayabhāvenopadeśo yuktaḥ. arhatāṃ saṃskārasaṃbhavāt. na cābhavasya. śaśaviṣāṇādīnāṃ apratyayatvāt.
body.translated_text: (III.28cd) "That which is not knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>)." "The consequence would apply to the eye and the rest as well" — the eye, ear, and the rest would also be ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), since they too are "not knowledge." "Nothing would exist" — if ignorance were the absence of knowledge, it would be a non-entity (<s>adravya</s>) — this is the meaning. "And this is not correct" — because of being taught as having the function of a condition. "Its opposite" (<s>tadvipakṣa</s>) — he shows that the negation [prefix <s>a-</s>] is in the sense of opposition (<s>virodha</s>). "Not just anyone other than a friend" — he shows that it is not merely exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>). "Nor the state of being a friend" — he shows that it does not mean absence (<s>abhāva</s>). "Non-<s>dharma</s>, non-benefit, non-effect, and the rest" — by the word "and the rest," non-propriety, non-convention, non-human, and the rest are included. "Being the opposites of <s>dharma</s> and the rest" — being the opposites of <s>dharma</s>, benefit, effect, propriety, convention, human, and the rest. "Not just anything other than <s>dharma</s> and the rest, such as the eye" — [it does not mean] the eye and the rest which are merely other than <s>dharma</s> and the rest. "Nor the absence of <s>dharma</s> and the rest." "So too ignorance" — and so forth in detail. How is this known? "Because of being taught as having the function of a condition" — "conditioned by ignorance, formations [arise]." And the teaching of the eye and other [faculties] as having the function of a condition for ignorance is not correct — because formations would arise even for <s>Arhats</s>, but they do not arise from what is non-existent, since hare's horns and the like are not conditions.

body.text: (III.29) saṃyojanaṃ yāvad yogaś cāvidyocyata iti. avidyāsaṃyojanaṃ yāvad avidyāyoga iti sūtreṣūcyate. na cābhāvamātraṃ tathā bhavitum arhatīti. na saṃyojanādi bhavitum arhatīty arthaḥ. na cāpi cakṣurādayas tathā bhavitum arhaṃtīty adhikṛtaṃ. sā ca dṛṣṭisvabhāveti nāvidyā yujyata iti. dṛṣṭyavidyayoḥ saṃyojanāditvena pṛthakpāṭhāt. yā tarhi na dṛṣṭir iti. yā kliṣṭā prajñā rāgādisaṃprayuktā.
body.translated_text: (III.29) "Fetter (<s>saṃyojana</s>), up to bond (<s>yoga</s>), is called ignorance" — in the sūtras it is stated: the fetter of ignorance, up to the bond of ignorance. And mere absence cannot qualify as such — it cannot qualify as a fetter and the rest — this is the meaning. "Nor can the eye and the rest qualify as such" — this is presupposed. "And if it has the nature of a view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), then it would not be correct [to call it] ignorance" — because view and ignorance are listed separately as fetters and the rest. "What then is [ignorance] that is not a view?" — it is defiled wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) conjoined with passion and the rest.

children.translated_text: "Because of the association of view with that [ignorance]"

body.text: iti. avidyāsaṃprayuktatvād ity arthaḥ. kathaṃ ca dṛṣṭir avidyayā saṃprayuktā. yasmād avidyālakṣaṇo mohaḥ kleśamahābhūmau paṭhyate. kleśamahābhūmikāś ca sarve 'pi mahābhūmikaiḥ saha saṃprayujyanta iti. dṛṣṭyā satkāyadṛṣṭyādikayā prajñāsvabhāvayā avidyā saṃprayujyata iti gamyate. tasmān nāvidyā prajñā. dvayoḥ prajñādravyayor [Tib. 291a] asaṃprayogāt. avidyopakliṣṭā prajñā na viśudhyatīti. etad udāharaṇaṃ. yenāvidyā prajñāyā arthāntarabhūteti. na ca saiva prajñā tasyāḥ prajñāyā upakleśo yukta iti. prajñopakleśadeśanāyāṃ prajñāyā arthāntarabhūtā avidyā. upakleśatvena nirdiṣṭatvāt. rāgavat. ata āha. yathā cittasyānya iti vistaraḥ. vyavakīryamāṇā na viśudhyatīti. antarāntarotpadyamānayā kliṣṭayā prajñayā vyavakīryamāṇā kṣaṇāntarotpannā kuśalā prajñā na viśudhyatīty arthaḥ. kiṃ tad avaśyaṃ rāgaparyavasthitam iti. rāgasaṃprayuktam ity arthaḥ. upahataṃ tu tat tathā rāgeṇeti. na samudācaratā rāgeṇa. vāsanādhānena tad upahataṃ bhavati. tāṃ vāsanāṃ tad dauṣṭhulyaṃ vyāvartayato yoginaḥ tac cittaṃ vimucyate. evam avidyopahatā kliṣṭā prajñā na śudhyatīti. ataḥ prajñā cāvidyā ca na doṣa iti darśayati. ko hi parikalpayan
body.translated_text: — the meaning is: because of association with ignorance. And how is view associated with ignorance? Because delusion (<s>moha</s>), which has the characteristic of ignorance, is listed in the great affliction-ground (<s>kleśamahābhūmi</s>). And all dharmas of the great affliction-ground are associated with the great-ground [dharmas]. Thus it is understood that ignorance is associated with view — the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest — which has the nature of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). Therefore, ignorance is not wisdom, because two wisdom-substances are not associated. "Wisdom afflicted by ignorance is not purified" — this is an illustration by which [it is shown that] ignorance is something different from wisdom. And it is not correct that that very same wisdom would be the defilement of that wisdom. In the teaching of the defilement of wisdom, ignorance — which is something different from wisdom — is taught as the defilement, because of being stated as a defilement — like passion. Therefore he says: "Just as for the mind, another [thing serves as defilement]" — and so forth in detail. "Being interrupted, it is not purified" — the meaning is: wholesome wisdom arising at another moment is not purified when interrupted by defiled wisdom arising at intermediate moments. "Is that necessarily enveloped by passion?" — the meaning is: conjoined with passion. "But that [mind] is harmed by passion in that way" — not by currently active passion, but it is harmed by the depositing of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). When a yogin eliminates that latent impression — that impairment (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) — then that mind is liberated. Similarly, defiled wisdom harmed by ignorance is not purified. Therefore, he shows that wisdom and ignorance are not a fault [to each other as identical]. "Who would be refuted by [mere] conceptual construction?"

body.text: vāryata iti. parikalpanāmātram etad āgamanirapekṣam iti kathayati.
body.translated_text: — he states that this is mere conceptual construction (<s>parikalpana</s>), without regard for scripture (<s>āgama</s>).

body.text: yo 'pi manyate sarvakleśā avidyeti. bhadantaśrīlātaḥ. evaṃ manyate. avidyeti sarvakleśānām iyaṃ sāmānyasaṃjñā. [Tib. 291b] na rāgādikleśavyatiriktāvidyā nāmāstīti. kasmāt evaṃ manyate. buddhasūtrāt. na ca prajānāti na ca prajānātīty āyuṣman mahākauṣṭhila tasmād avidyocyata iti. satkāyadṛṣṭyādayo 'pi kleśā ajñānasvarūpā viparītagrahaṇata iti. tasyāpy ata eveti vistaraḥ. tasya bhadantasyāta eva pratiṣedhavacanād vyudāsaḥ. pratiṣedhas tanmatasyety adhyāhāryaṃ. katham ity āhā. sarvakleśasvabhāvā hi satī saṃyojanādiṣu pṛthaṅ nocyeta. anunayasaṃyojanādiṣv avidyāsaṃyojanam iti pṛthaṅ nocyeta. śeṣasaṃyojanāvyatirekāt. rāgo baṃdhanaṃ dveṣo bandhanam ity uktvā moho bandhanam iti. kāmarāgānuśaya ityādi uktvā avidyānuśaya iti. ogheṣv avidyaugha iti. yogeṣv avidyāyoga iti pṛthaṅ naivocyeta. kasmāt. parasparāsaṃprayogāt. na hi dṛṣṭir dṛṣṭyā saṃprayujyate. rāgo vā rāgeṇa. dṛṣṭyādisaṃprayuktā cāvidyoktā. kleśamahābhūmikatvena mahābhūmikasaṃprayoganiyamāt. cittam api cāvidyopakliṣṭam evoktaṃ bhavet. [Tib. 292a] rāgopakliṣṭaṃ cittaṃ na vimucyata iti noktaṃ bhavet. avidyopakliṣṭatvavacanenaiva rāgādyupakliṣṭatvasiddheḥ. atha mataṃ viśeṣaṇārthaṃ tathoktam iti. rāgalakṣaṇayāvidyayopakliṣṭacittaṃ na vimucyata iti. prajñāyām api viśeṣaṇaṃ kartavyaṃ syāt. rāgeṇa pratighena mānena veti mā bhūt sarvakleśagrahaṇaprasaṃga iti. iṣṭa iti cet. citte 'pi na viśeṣaṇaṃ kartavyaṃ syāt. avidyopakliṣṭaṃ cittaṃ na vimucyata ity evam eva tu vaktavyaṃ syāt.
body.translated_text: The one who holds that all afflictions are ignorance — the venerable <s>Śrīlāta</s>. He holds thus: '<s>avidyā</s>' (ignorance) is a general designation for all afflictions. [Tib. 291b] There is no entity called 'ignorance' distinct from afflictions such as desire, etc. Why does he hold thus? Because of the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>sūtra</s>: 'He does not know, he does not know — therefore, venerable <s>Mahākauṣṭhila</s>, it is called <s>avidyā</s>.' Even afflictions such as <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (identity-view) and the like have the nature of non-knowledge, because of apprehending in a distorted manner. 'His [view] too, for this very reason' — thus the elaboration. Of that venerable one too, the refutation is for this very reason, by the statement of prohibition — 'the prohibition is of his view' should be supplied. How? He says: if [ignorance] had the nature of all afflictions, it would not be stated separately among the fetters and the like. It would not be stated separately as 'the fetter of ignorance' among the fetter of attachment and the like — because there would be no distinction from the remaining fetters. Having said 'desire is a bond, hatred is a bond,' [there would be no need to say] 'delusion is a bond.' Having said 'the latent tendency of desire for sensuality' and so on, [there would be no need to say] 'the latent tendency of ignorance.' Among the floods, 'the flood of ignorance'; among the yokes, 'the yoke of ignorance' — these would never be stated separately. Why? Because of mutual non-association. For a view is not associated with [another] view, nor desire with desire. And ignorance is stated as associated with views, etc. — because of the rule that, as a universal-affliction-factor (<s>kleśamahābhūmika</s>), it is associated with all [affliction] universals. Moreover, the mind would have been stated as defiled by ignorance alone. [Tib. 292a] 'The mind defiled by desire is not liberated' would not have been stated — since defilement by desire, etc. would be established simply by the statement of defilement by ignorance. Now if one thinks 'it was stated thus for the purpose of qualification — the mind defiled by ignorance having the character of desire is not liberated' — then a qualification regarding wisdom too would have to be made: 'by desire, by aversion, or by conceit' — lest there be the unwanted consequence of including all afflictions. If that is accepted, then no qualification should need to be made regarding the mind either. One should simply say: 'the mind defiled by ignorance is not liberated.'

body.text: saṃprakhyānaṃ prajñā jñānam ity eko 'rthaḥ. tathaiva dośo yathāvidyāyām iti. athāsaṃprakhyānam iti ko 'rthaḥ. yan va saṃprakhyānaṃ. cakṣurādiṣv api prasaṃgaḥ. saṃprakhyānābhāvas tarhi. evaṃ sati na kiṃ cit syāt. na caitad yuktam iti. atha saṃprakhyānavipakṣabhūtaṃ dharmāntaraṃ. tad idaṃ tathaiva na jñāyate. yathaivāvidyā. kiṃ tad iti. evaṃjātīyako 'pīti vistaraḥ. evaṃjātīyakaḥ karmaprabhāvita ity arthaḥ. tasmād avidyāyāḥ karmaṇaḥ kāritreṇa svabhāvo vijñātavyaḥ. asty asau kaścid dharma yo vidyāvipakṣa iti vidyāvipakṣatvaṃ tasyāḥ karmeti. [Tib. 292b] tadyathā cakṣuḥ katamat. yo rūpaprasādaś cakṣurvijñānasyāśraya iti. nanu ca rūpaprasāda iti svabhāvaprabhāvito 'sya nirdeśa iti. na. apratyakṣatvāt. nityaṃ cakṣurvijñānānumeyatvāc ca. asmīti sattvamayateti. avijñātārtham etat. na tena sthavireṇāsyābhidheyam avadhāritaṃ. mayatā punaḥ sautrāṃtikair avidyā prakārabhinnā varṇyate. māno vā. yāsau sūtra ukteti vistaraḥ. mayatānām ity avidyānāṃ prakārabhinnānāṃ
body.translated_text: 'Discernment' (<s>saṃprakhyāna</s>) means wisdom, knowledge — [these are] one meaning. 'The fault is the same as with ignorance' — if then '<s>asaṃprakhyāna</s>' (non-discernment) [is used], what is the meaning? If it means [absence of] discernment — the unwanted consequence would extend to the eye, etc. [which lack discernment]. If then it is the absence of discernment — in that case nothing would exist [as ignorance]. And this is not proper. If then it is a different <s>dharma</s> that is the opposite of discernment — that is not known in itself, [Tib. 292b] just as ignorance [is not]. What is it? 'Of such a kind' — thus the elaboration. 'Of such a kind' means: influenced by <s>karma</s>. Therefore the own-nature of ignorance should be understood through the function of <s>karma</s>. There is indeed some <s>dharma</s> that is the opposite of knowledge — and the fact of being the opposite of knowledge is its function. Just as [the question]: 'what is the eye?' — 'the material clarity that is the support of visual consciousness.' 'But surely the designation [of the eye] through "material clarity" is influenced by [its] own-nature?' No — because it is not directly perceptible, and because it is always inferred through visual consciousness. '<s>Asmīti sattvamayatā</s>' — this has an unknown meaning. The elder did not determine its referent. But <s>mayatā</s> (egoity) is described by the <s>Sautrāntika</s>s as ignorance differentiated by type. Or conceit. 'That which is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>' — thus the elaboration. '<s>Mayatā</s>s' means: of the varieties of ignorance

body.text: nāmeti grahaṇaṃ. tṛṣṇādīnāṃ pṛthagupadeśād iti bhadantadharmatrātasyābhiprāyaḥ. ācārya āha. asty eṣā mayatā. asti sūtre uktā mayatā. tatra jātinirdeśād ekavacanaṃ. sā tv avidyeti. kutaḥ kāraṇād etat paricchidyate. sāvidyeti. bhadantadharmatrātaḥ svābhiprāyaṃ vivṛṇoti. yata eṣā nānyaḥ kleśaḥ śakyate vaktum iti. kasmān na śakyate. tṛṣṇādṛṣṭyasmimānānāṃ pṛthagukteḥ. ācārya āha. nanu cānyo māna eva syād iti. asmimānād anyaḥ ṣaṇṇām anyatamaḥ sa ca mayatā. navidyety abhiprāyaḥ. atra tu punar vicāryamāṇe bahu vaktavyaṃ jāyata iti. atra punar vicāryamāṇe 'vidyāṃge [Tib. 293a] bahur ayaṃ grantho jāyate. yathoktam iti. tasmāt tiṣṭhatv etad etāvad evāstv iti. atha vānyo māṇa eva syāt. na punar avidyeti. kuta etad ity evamādike punar vicāre kriyamāṇe. uttarapratyuttaravacanena bahu vaktavyaṃ jāyate. tasmāt tiṣṭhatv etad alaṃ vicārāntareṇety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: is the inclusion by the word 'name.' 'Because of the separate teaching of craving, etc.' — this is the intent of the venerable <s>Dharmatrāta</s>. The teacher says: 'this <s>mayatā</s> (egoity) exists. <s>Mayatā</s> is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>. There, because of the indication of class, the singular [is used]. But it is ignorance.' From what reason is this determined? 'It is ignorance' — the venerable <s>Dharmatrāta</s> discloses his own intent: 'because this cannot be said to be any other affliction.' Why can it not? Because of the separate statement of craving, view, and the conceit 'I am.' The teacher says: 'but surely it could be just another conceit' — a conceit other than the conceit 'I am,' one of the [other] six; and that would be <s>mayatā</s>, not ignorance — this is the intent. 'But here, when further examined, much would need to be said' — here, when the ignorance-link [Tib. 293a] is further examined, this lengthy discussion arises. 'As stated' — therefore, let this stand; let this much suffice. Alternatively: 'it could indeed be another conceit, not ignorance' — from whence is this [derived]? and so on — when further investigation is undertaken, through statements and counter-statements, much would need to be said. Therefore, let this stand — enough with further investigation — this is the meaning.

body.text: (III.30a) atha nāmarūpam iti. avidyāṃganirdeśānantaraṃ saṃskārāṃgaṃ nirdeṣṭavyaṃ. tadanu vijñānāṃgaṃ. kim ity etad atikramyopanyaste. etad artham atra vakṣyaty ācāryaḥ.
body.translated_text: (III.30a) 'Now, name-and-form' — after the exposition of the ignorance-link, the formations-link should be expounded, and after that the consciousness-link. Why is [name-and-form] presented bypassing those? For this purpose the teacher will state here:

children.translated_text: 'What has been said and what else will be said' —

body.text: iti. rūpaṃ vistareṇoktam iti.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Form has been explained in detail' —

children.text: rūpaṃ paṃcendriyāṇy arthāḥ paṃcavijñaptir eva cety
children.translated_text: 'Form is the five faculties, the five objects, and the informative [form] alone' —

body.text: atra. nāmendriyārthavaśeneti vistaraḥ. nāmavaśena indriyavaśena arthavaśena cārtheṣu rūpādiṣu namatīti nāma. katamasya nāmno vaśeneti. nāmadvaividhyāt pṛcchati. ācāryas tv ācaṣṭe. yad idaṃ loke pratītim iti vistaraḥ. gaur aśva iti. samudāyapratyāyakam. rūpaṃ rasa iti. ekārthapratyāyakaṃ. tad etad vedanādiskaṃdhacatuṣkaṃ nāmaśabdenocyate. yasmāt tannāmavaśena saṃjñākaraṇavaśenārtheṣv apratyakṣeṣv api vā namati pravartate. asya nāmno 'yam artha iti. indriyārthavaśena tu pratyakṣeṣu rupādiṣu namati utpadyate ity arthaḥ. [Tib. 293b] nāmni cāpy arthavaśena namati. asyārthasyedaṃ nāmeti. etasya punaḥ kena nāmatvam iti. etasya saṃjñākaraṇalakṣaṇasya nāmnaḥ kena kāraṇena nāmatvaṃ. teṣu teṣv artheṣu tasya nāmno namanād iti. yasmāt teṣv artheṣu catuḥskandhalakṣaṇaṃ nāma tan nāma namayati pravartayati. tasmād etasya nāmatvaṃ. namayatīti nāmeti kṛtvā. iha nikṣipta iti vistaraḥ. maraṇakāle nikṣipte kāye upapattyantare namanād gamanād arūpiṇo vedanādayaḥ skandhā nāmety ucyante. yathoktaṃ. mṛtasya khalu kālaṃ gatasya jñātaya imaṃ pūtikāyam agninā vā dahaṃti udake vā plāvayanti bhūmau vā nikhananti vātātapābhyāṃ vā pariśoṣaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānāṃ gacchati. yat punar idam ucyate. cittam iti
body.translated_text: here. 'Through name, faculty, and object' — thus the elaboration. Through name, through faculty, and through object. 'That which bends (<s>namati</s>) toward objects such as form, etc. is name (<s>nāma</s>).' 'Through which name?' — he asks because of the twofold [nature of] name. The teacher explains: 'what is known in the world' — thus the elaboration. 'Cow, horse' — conveying a composite. 'Form, taste' — conveying a single thing. These four aggregates beginning with feeling are designated by the word 'name.' Because through the power of that name — through the power of designation — one bends toward (<s>namati</s>), one engages with, even imperceptible objects: 'this is the referent of this name.' But through the power of faculty and object, one bends toward perceptible [things] such as form, etc. — meaning: [consciousness] arises. [Tib. 293b] And with respect to name also, through the power of the object, one bends: 'this is the name of this object.' 'What then makes this a "name"?' — by what reason does this, characterized as designation, have the quality of being a name? 'Because of the bending of that name toward those various objects' — because name, characterized as the four aggregates, bends toward — causes engagement with — those objects. Therefore this has the quality of being a name — because it bends (<s>namayati</s>), it is name (<s>nāma</s>). 'Deposited here' — thus the elaboration. When at the time of death the body is deposited, in the next birth, because of bending toward — going to — [a new existence], the formless aggregates of feeling, etc. are called 'name.' As stated: 'when one has died and passed away, the relatives either burn this putrid body with fire, or submerge it in water, or bury it in the earth, or it undergoes drying, decay, and consumption through wind and heat. But what is called "mind"

body.text: vā mana iti vā vijñānam iti vā śraddhāparibhāvitaṃ śīlatyāgaśrutaprajñāparibhāvitaṃ. tad ūrdhvagāmi bhavati viśeṣagāmy āyatyāṃ svargopagam iti.
body.translated_text: or "mentation" or "consciousness" — cultivated by faith, cultivated by morality, generosity, learning, and wisdom — that goes upward, goes toward distinction, leads to heaven in the future.'

body.text: (III.30b) ṣaḍāyatanam uktam iti.
body.translated_text: (III.30b) 'The six sense-bases have been stated' —

children.text:
tadvijñānāśrayā rūpaprasādāś cakṣurādayaḥ.
vijñānaṃ prativijñaptir manaāyatanaṃ ca tad
children.translated_text:
'The material clarities that are the supports of those consciousnesses — eye, etc.;
consciousness is apprehension-by-apprehension; and that is the mind sense-base' —

body.text: ity atra. manaindriyasya punar niruddhasya anāgatena dharmeṇa rūpādinā utpatsyamānena vartamānena manovijñānena kathaṃ saṃnipātaḥ. yaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ. kāryaṃ manovijñānaṃ. kāraṇaṃ manaindriyaṃ. dharmaś ca rūpādiḥ. [Tib. 294a] ekakāryārtho veti. ekakāryam evārtha ekakāryārthaḥ. ekakāryatvam ity arthaḥ. katham ekakāryārtha ity āha. sarve ca te trayo 'pi manaindriyādayaḥ sparśotpattau praguṇā anukūlā bhavantīti.
body.translated_text: here. But the mind-faculty, having ceased, and a future <s>dharma</s> such as form, etc. that will arise, and the present mental consciousness — how is their conjunction [possible]? [Tib. 294a] That which is the relation of effect and cause — the effect is mental consciousness, the cause is the mind-faculty, and the <s>dharma</s> is form, etc. 'Or [they] have a single effect as their purpose' — a single effect itself is the purpose; the meaning is: having a single effect. 'How do they have a single effect as their purpose?' He says: all three — mind-faculty and the rest — are favorable, conducive to the arising of contact.

body.text: ṣaṭṣaṭko dharmaparyāya iti. ṣaṭṣaṭkāny asminn iti ṣaṭṣatkaḥ. ādhyātmikabāhyavijñānasparśavedanātṛṣṇāṣaṭkasaṃbhavāt. ṣaṭ sparśakāyā iti jñāpakaṃ. ananyatve hi satīndriyārthavijñāneṣūkteṣu sparśakāyavacanaṃ punar uktaṃ syāt. tataś ca ṣaṭṣaṭkatvaṃ hīyate. mā bhūd dharmāyatanād vedanātṛṣṇayoḥ. pṛthagbhāva iti. yadi pṛthaṅnirdeśāt pṛthagbhāvo bhavet. vedanātṛṣṇe api dharmāyatanāt pṛthaṅ nirdiṣṭe. tayor api vedanātṛṣṇayor dharmāyatanāt pṛthagbhāvaḥ syāt. na ca tayoḥ pṛthagbhāva iṣyate. dharmāyatanāntarbhāvāt. naiṣa doṣa iti vistaraḥ. naiṣa doṣa iti yathoktas tadvyatiriktasyāpi vedanātṛṣṇāvyatiriktasyāpi dharmāyatanasya saṃjñādisvabhāvasya bhāvād astitvāt. na caivam iti vistaraḥ. na caivaṃ bhavatas trayānāṃ saṃnipātaḥ sparśa ity evaṃ bruvāṇasya [Tib. 294b] sparśabhūtād indriyārthavijñānatrayād anyad asparśabhūtaṃ trayam indriyārthavijñānatrayam asti. yasya śeṣasyātra sūtre grahaṇaṃ syāt. ṣaṭ sparśakāyā iti prayojanavaśād apṛthagbhāve 'pi sparśabhūtāt trayāt. tasmād apṛthagbhāve 'pi vedanātṛṣṇayoḥ pṛthaṅnirdeśo yukto vineyakāryavaśāt. na tu bhavataḥ saṃnipātamātrasparśavādinaḥ kenacid api prayojanena ṣaṭ sparśakāyā iti pṛthaṅnirdeśo yuktaḥ. yasmāt ṣaṭ sparśakāyā iti vacanenendriyārthavijñānatrayam uktam iti tadavacanaṃ prāptam ity ataḥ ṣaṭṣaṭko dharmaparyāyā iti na sidhyet. mama tu sidhyati. sparśavedanātṛṣṇāṣaṭkavacane 'pi tadvyatiriktadharmāyatanādyarthendriyavijñānaṣaṭkasaṃbhavāt. tasmāt ṣaṭ sparśakāyā iti pṛthaṅnirdeśād asti cittasaṃprayuktaṃ sparśākhyaṃ dharmāntaram iti siddhaṃ. atha brūyād asau. indriyārthāv avijñānakau nirdiṣṭāv asmin sūtre. ṣaḍ ādhyātmikāni ṣaṭ bāhyānīti vacanāt. ata indriyaviṣayavijñanatrayaṃ sparśabhūtam ity asya śeṣasya jñāpanārtham atra grahaṇaṃ syāt. ṣaṭ
body.translated_text: 'The <s>dharma</s>-discourse of the six sixes' — 'it contains six sixes,' hence 'of the six sixes.' Because of the occurrence of six [groups]: internal, external, consciousness, contact, feeling, and craving. 'The six bodies of contact' serves as an indicator. For if [contact] were not different [from the triad of faculty, object, and consciousness], then after stating the faculties, objects, and consciousnesses, the statement 'bodies of contact' would be redundant. And thus the six-six character would be diminished. 'Lest feeling and craving be [considered] different from the <s>dharma</s> sense-base' — if separate statement implied separate existence, then feeling and craving, also stated separately from the <s>dharma</s> sense-base, would be separate from the <s>dharma</s> sense-base. But their separateness is not accepted, because of their inclusion within the <s>dharma</s> sense-base. 'This is not a fault' — thus the elaboration. This is not a fault, because of the existence — the reality — of the <s>dharma</s> sense-base that is distinct from those [feeling and craving], having the nature of perception, etc. 'And it is not so [for you]' — thus the elaboration. And it is not so for you, who say 'the conjunction of the three is contact' — [Tib. 294b] [for you,] apart from the triad of faculty, object, and consciousness that constitutes contact, there is no other triad of faculty, object, and consciousness that is not contact, the inclusion of which remainder in this <s>sūtra</s> would [justify the separate statement]. 'The six bodies of contact' — due to a [specific] purpose, even though not separate from the triad that constitutes contact. Therefore, even though feeling and craving are not separate [from the <s>dharma</s> sense-base], their separate statement is proper due to the needs of the disciples. But for you, who hold that contact is merely conjunction, no purpose whatever justifies the separate statement 'six bodies of contact.' Because the statement 'six bodies of contact' would [on your view simply] state the triad of faculty, object, and consciousness — so the omission of that [separate statement] would follow — and therefore the <s>dharma</s>-discourse of the six sixes would not be established. But for me it is established — because even when the six [groups] of contact, feeling, and craving are stated, the six [groups] of <s>dharma</s> sense-base, etc. and faculties and consciousnesses distinct from those still exist. Therefore, from the separate statement 'six bodies of contact,' it is established that there exists a different <s>dharma</s> associated with mind called 'contact.' Now he might say: 'faculties and objects without consciousness are mentioned in this <s>sūtra</s> — because of the statement "six internal, six external." Therefore the inclusion [of the separate mention] would be for the purpose of indicating the remainder — that the triad of faculty, object, and consciousness constitutes contact.' The six

body.text: sparśakāyā iti. asya samādheḥ pratiṣedhārtham idam ārabhyate. yady apīndriyārthau syātām avijñānakau. tatsabhāgāv ity arthaḥ. na tu punar vijñānam anindriyārthakaṃ. avaśyaṃ hi vijñānaṃ sendriyārthakaṃ bhavati. tac ca vijñānam apadiṣṭam atra ṣaḍ vijñānakāyā iti. [Tib. 295a] tasmāt triṣu nirdiṣṭeṣu indriyārthavijñāneṣu ṣaḍvijñānakāyavacanena punaḥ sparśagrahaṇam anarthakaṃ prāpnoti. ṣaṭ sparśakāyā iti. ataḥ saṃnipātād anyaḥ sparśa iti siddhaṃ. atra bhadantaśrīlāta āha. na khalv iti vistaraḥ. pūrvotpanne cakṣūrūpe kāraṇaṃ. na tu vijñānasahotpanne. nāpi sarvacakṣurvijñānam iti. paścād utpannaṃ pūrvayoś cakṣūrūpayoḥ. na sahotpannayoḥ. ato yeṣāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ. te vijñānendriyaviṣayāḥ sparśabhāvena vyavasthitāḥ. ṣaṭ sparśakāyā ity asmin sūtre. tad idam anyathā na jñāpitaṃ syāt.
body.translated_text: bodies of contact — this is begun for the purpose of refuting that understanding. 'Even if the faculty and object were without consciousness' — meaning: of the same class [as conscious ones]. 'But consciousness is never without faculty and object' — for consciousness necessarily has faculty and object. And that consciousness has been indicated here: 'six bodies of consciousness.' [Tib. 295a] Therefore, when the three — faculties, objects, and consciousnesses — have been indicated, the further inclusion of contact through the statement 'six bodies of consciousness' becomes purposeless — 'six bodies of contact.' Therefore it is established that contact is something other than the conjunction. Therein the venerable <s>Śrīlāta</s> says: 'not indeed...' — thus the elaboration. The previously arisen eye and form are the cause, but not [the eye and form] co-arisen with consciousness. Nor is it all visual consciousness. The subsequently arisen [consciousness depends] on the prior eye and form, not on co-arisen ones. Therefore those [members] that stand in a cause-effect relation — those consciousnesses, faculties, and objects are established as having the nature of contact — in this <s>sūtra</s> 'six bodies of contact.' This would not have been indicated otherwise.

body.text: na vā evaṃ pathanti. vai iti nipātaḥ. na vai evaṃ paṭhantīty arthaḥ. kathaṃ punaḥ paṭhanti. ya eṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṃgateḥ saṃnipātāt samavāyād utpannaḥ. sa sparśa iti paṭhanti. kāraṇe vā kāryopacāro 'yam iti. saṃgatau saṃnipāte samavāye kāraṇe kāryopacāraḥ sparśa iti. yathā
body.translated_text: Or they do not recite thus. '<s>vai</s>' is a particle. The meaning is: they do not indeed recite thus. How then do they recite? 'That which is born from the meeting, coming together, and conjunction of these <s>dharma</s>s — that is contact (<s>sparśa</s>)' — thus they recite. Or this is a figurative attribution of the effect to the cause — contact is figuratively attributed to meeting, coming together, and conjunction, which are causes. Just as [in the expression]:

body.text: iti. atibahuvistaeṇa prakāreṇa visartuṃ śīlam asyā iti atibahuvistaraprakāravisāriṇī.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Whose habit is to spread in an exceedingly extensive manner' — that whose nature (<s>śīla</s>) is to spread (<s>visartu</s>) in exceedingly extensive and numerous ways is 'exceedingly extensive in manner of spreading' (<s>atibahuvistaraprakāravisāriṇī</s>).

body.text: (III.30cd) adhivacanam ucyate nāmeti. adhyucyate 'nenety adhivacanaṃ. vāṅ nāmni pravartate. nāmārthaṃ [Tib. 295b] dyotayatīty adhivacanaṃ nāma. tad kila nāmasya manovijñanasaṃprayuktasyādhikaṃ bāhulyenālambanam. ato 'dhivacanasaṃsparśa iti. sparśaḥ saṃsparśa ity eko 'rthaḥ. manovijñānena nīlaṃ vijānātīti. abhidheyaṃ vijānātīty arthaḥ. nīlam iti ca vijānātīti. asyārthasyedaṃ nāmeti vijānāti. eka āśrayaprabhāvita iti. prathama āśrayeṇa prabhāvitaḥ pratighāśrayaḥ saṃsparśaḥ pratighasya vā saṃsparśaḥ pratighasaṃsparśaḥ. ālaṃbanaprabhāvita iti. adhivacanād ālambanasaṃsparśaḥ adhivacane vā saṃsparśaḥ adhivacanasaṃsparśa iti.
body.translated_text: (III.30cd) 'Designation (<s>adhivacana</s>) is said to be name (<s>nāma</s>)' — that by which [something] is designated is <s>adhivacana</s>. Speech operates with respect to name. Name illuminates meaning — [Tib. 295b] thus it is <s>adhivacana</s>. Indeed, the object of name, which is associated with mental consciousness, is predominantly and extensively [its] object-support. Therefore [it is called] <s>adhivacanasaṃsparśa</s> (designation-contact). '<s>Sparśa</s>' and '<s>saṃsparśa</s>' have one and the same meaning. 'By mental consciousness one cognizes blue' — meaning: one cognizes the referent. 'And one cognizes [it] as blue' — one cognizes: 'this is the name of this object.' 'The first is influenced by the support (<s>āśraya</s>)' — the first, influenced by the [sense-]support, is <s>pratigha</s>-support contact; or the contact of <s>pratigha</s> (resistance) is <s>pratighasaṃsparśa</s> (resistance-contact). 'Influenced by the object (<s>ālambana</s>)' — from designation, it is <s>ālambanasaṃsparśa</s> (object-contact); or the contact in designation is <s>adhivacanasaṃsparśa</s>.

body.text: vacanam adhikṛtya vacanam avadhāryārtheṣu rūpādiṣu manovijñānasya pravṛttiḥ. na paṃcānāṃ cakṣurvijñānādīnāṃ vacanam adhikṛtyārtheṣu pravṛttiḥ. atas tad evādhivacanaṃ manovijñānaṃ vacane pravartate 'dhivacanam iti. tena saṃprayuktas tasya vā saṃsparśasyādhivacanasaṃsparśaḥ. tena cāyaṃ dvitīyaḥ saṃsparśaḥ saṃprayogaprabhāvita ity ucyate.
body.translated_text: Taking speech as the basis — having determined speech, mental consciousness operates with respect to objects such as form and the rest. But the five [consciousnesses] — visual consciousness and the rest — do not operate with respect to objects taking speech as their basis. Therefore, that very designation is mental consciousness, which operates in speech — [hence] <s>adhivacana</s> (designation). The contact associated with that, or the contact of that, is <s>adhivacanasaṃsparśa</s>. And this second type of contact is said to be 'influenced by association' (<s>saṃprayogaprabhāvita</s>).

children.translated_text: 'Contacts [associated with] knowledge, ignorance, and the other' —

body.text: iti. vidyāvidyetaraś ca vidyāvidyetare. te eva sparśā
body.translated_text: thus. Those of knowledge, ignorance, and the other — they are 'of knowledge, ignorance, and the other.' Those very contacts are

children.translated_text: 'the contacts of knowledge, ignorance, and the other.'

body.text: vidyāhvaḥ avidyāhvaḥ tābhyām itaraś cety arthaḥ. vidyety anāsravā prajñā. avidyā kliṣṭam ajñānam. naivavidyānāvidyā yā kuśalasāsravā yā cānivṛtāvyākṛtā prajñā. [Tib. 296a] tatsaṃprayuktā ete yathākramaṃ saṃsparśā veditavyāḥ. punar avidyāsaṃsparśasyeti. vistaraḥ. avidyāsaṃsparśasya sarvakleśasaṃprayuktasyābhīkṣṇasamudācārī nityasamudācārī ekadeśaḥ. tasya grahaṇād dvau sparśau bhavato
body.translated_text: 'Of knowledge' means outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) wisdom. '<s>Avidyā</s>' (ignorance) means afflicted nescience. 'Neither knowledge nor ignorance' means wisdom that is wholesome-with-outflows and unobstructed-indeterminate. [Tib. 296a] These contacts should be understood as associated with those respectively, in order. 'Moreover, of <s>avidyā</s>-contact' — and so on in detail. Of <s>avidyā</s>-contact, which is associated with all afflictions: 'frequently occurring' means constantly occurring — this is a portion [of it]. Because of its inclusion, there are two types of contact:

children.translated_text: 'The contacts of ill-will and affection — three beginning with that to be experienced as pleasure' —

body.text: iti. sukhasya vedaḥ sukhavedaḥ. sukhavede sādhuḥ sukhavedyaḥ. sukhaṃ yā vedyam asminn iti sukhavedyaḥ. sa ādir eṣām iti sukhavedyādayaḥ. sukhavedanādihitatvād iti. sukhavedanāyai hitaḥ sukhavedanīyaḥ. prāk krītāc chaḥ. vedyate tad vedayituṃ vā śakyam iti. vedyata iti karmamātre kṛtya iti darśayati. vedayituṃ śakyam ity arhe kṛtyatṛcaś cety asminn arthe kṛtya iti darśayati. ta ete ṣoḍaśeti. cakṣuḥsaṃsparśo yāvan manaḥsaṃsparśa iti ṣaṭ. punaḥ pratighasaṃsparśo 'dhivacanasaṃsparśo vidyāsaṃsparśo 'vidyāsaṃsparśo naivavidyānāvidyāsaṃsparśo vyāpādasaṃsparśo 'nunayasaṃsparśaḥ sukhavedanīyo duḥkhavedanīyo 'duḥkhāsukhavedanīyaś ca sparśa iti ṣoḍaśa.
body.translated_text: thus. The experience (<s>veda</s>) of pleasure is <s>sukhaveda</s>. That which is suitable for the experience of pleasure is <s>sukhavedya</s>. Or: that in which pleasure is the object of experience is <s>sukhavedya</s>. That which begins with this is 'beginning with <s>sukhavedya</s>.' 'Because of being conducive to pleasant feeling and so forth' — that which is conducive to pleasant feeling is '<s>sukhavedanīya</s>' (to be experienced as pleasant). The suffix <s>cha</s> is [applied] to [a word] prior to the purchased [item]. '<s>Vedya</s>' means 'it is experienced' or 'it is capable of being experienced.' '<s>Vedyate</s>' — he shows [the suffix] <s>kṛtya</s> in the sense of mere action. 'Capable of being experienced' — he shows [the suffix] <s>kṛtya</s> in the sense of capability, from [the rule about] <s>kṛtyatṛc</s> and so on. These are sixteen: eye-contact up to mind-contact — six. Further: resistance-contact (<s>pratighasaṃsparśa</s>), designation-contact (<s>adhivacanasaṃsparśa</s>), knowledge-contact (<s>vidyāsaṃsparśa</s>), ignorance-contact (<s>avidyāsaṃsparśa</s>), neither-knowledge-nor-ignorance-contact (<s>naivavidyānāvidyāsaṃsparśa</s>), ill-will-contact (<s>vyāpādasaṃsparśa</s>), affection-contact (<s>anunayasaṃsparśa</s>), contact to be experienced as pleasant (<s>sukhavedanīya</s>), contact to be experienced as painful (<s>duḥkhavedanīya</s>), and contact to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant (<s>aduḥkhāsukhavedanīya</s>) — sixteen.

body.text: (III.32ab)

children.translated_text: 'Contact has been stated; feeling is to be stated' —

body.translated_text: (III.32ab)

body.text: nanu ca vedanāpy uktā
body.translated_text: 'But surely feeling too has already been stated' —

body.text: iti. athoktam apy ucyate. na tarhīdaṃ vaktavyaṃ. yac coktaṃ yac ca vakṣyamāṇaṃ. tan na vakṣyāmīti.
body.translated_text: thus. Well then, what has been stated is being stated [again]. 'In that case, this should not be stated: what has been stated and what will be stated — I shall not state that' —

children.translated_text: 'What has been stated will also be stated again in another way' —

body.text: Tib. 296b
body.translated_text: Tib. 296b

body.text: iti vācanāt. prakāranirdeśād adoṣaḥ. pūrvaṃ laksaṇam uktam idānīṃ prakāra iti.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. There is no fault, because of the exposition of types. Previously the characteristic was stated; now the types [are stated].

body.text: jāte hīti vistaraḥ. jāte hi janye dharme dharmasya janakasya nāsti sāmarthyam sahotpannatvāt. pratijñāviśiṣṭam iti. pratijñāyā aviśiṣṭam etat sādhanam ity arthaḥ. yadi pratijñāviśiṣṭaṃ sādhanaṃ neṣyate. anyonyajanakaprasaṃgāt
body.translated_text: 'For when [it] has arisen' — and so on in detail. For when the produced <s>dharma</s> has arisen, the producer <s>dharma</s> has no capacity [to produce it], because of being co-arisen. '[The proof is] no different from the thesis' — meaning: this proof is no different from the thesis. If [you say] the proof is not different from the thesis — because of the consequence of mutual production

body.text: tarhi. kiṃ. kathaṃ sahotpannayor janyajanakabhāvaḥ sidhyatīty adhikṛtam. anena pratijñādoṣa udgrāhyate. asti sahotpannayor janyajanakabhāva iti pratijñā pūrvābhyupagamavirodhinīti. iṣṭatvād adoṣa iti. purvābhyupagamaṃ darśayati. iṣtam idaṃ. sūtre tv aniṣṭam iti. iṣṭam idam abhidharme
body.translated_text: then what? How is the producer-produced relationship of co-arisen [<s>dharma</s>s] established? — this is the topic under discussion. By this, the fault of the thesis is to be extracted. The thesis 'there is a producer-produced relationship between co-arisen [dharmas]' contradicts prior agreement. 'There is no fault because it is accepted' — he shows the prior agreement. This is accepted — in the <s>Abhidharma</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Co-existent [causes] are those which are mutually fruits' —

body.text: iti. sūtre tv aniṣṭaṃ. tat pratipādayann āha. cakṣuḥsaṃsparśaṃ pratītyotpadyate cakṣuḥsaṃsparśajā vedaneti. sūtraprāmāṇyenānyonyaphalatvaṃ bhaṃktvā sahotpannakāryakāraṇabhāvabibhaṃkṣayā āha. janakadharmātikramāc cāyuktam iti. janakasyāyaṃ dharmaḥ prasiddho yā bhinnakālatā. tadyathā pūrvaṃ bījaṃ paścād aṃkura ityādi. tatrāpi [Tib. 297a] pūrvam indriyārthau paścād vijñānam iti. prathamakṣaṇotpannāv indriyārthau vijñānaṃ tu dvitīye kṣaṇa iti. yathā tarhi chāyāṃkurayor iti. kiṃ. sahotpannayor janyajanakabhāvaḥ. utpanna eva hy aṃkuraś chāyāṃ janayati. na prathame kṣaṇe 'ṃkuro niśchāyo bhavati dvitīye sacchāya iti. evaṃ sparśavedanayor apīti. anayor api chāyāṃukurayoḥ pūrvasāmagrī hetur iti śakyaṃ vaktuṃ. sahabhūhetunirdeśe tv ayam artha ukta iti na punar ucyate.
body.translated_text: thus. But in the <s>sūtra</s>, it is not accepted. Demonstrating that, he says: 'Dependent on eye-contact, there arises feeling born of eye-contact.' On the authority of the <s>sūtra</s>, having broken the mutual fruit-relationship, wishing to break the cause-effect relationship of co-arisen [dharmas], he says: 'And it is not logical, because it transgresses the characteristic of the producer.' The well-known characteristic of a producer is temporal difference [between cause and effect] — for example, first the seed, then the sprout, and so forth. Even there too, [Tib. 297a] first the faculty and object, then consciousness. The faculty and object arise in the first moment; consciousness in the second moment. 'Then, as in the case of shadow and sprout' — what? — there is a producer-produced relationship between co-arisen [things]. For only once the sprout has arisen does it produce a shadow. It is not the case that in the first moment the sprout is without shadow and in the second with shadow. Similarly for contact and feeling. Even for these — shadow and sprout — it is possible to say that the prior assemblage [of conditions] is the cause. But this meaning has been stated in the exposition of the co-existent cause (<s>sahabhūhetu</s>), so it is not stated again.

body.text: sparśād uttarakālaṃ vedanety apara iti bhadantaśrīlātaḥ. so 'sau trayāṇāṃ saṃnipātaḥ sparśa iti. yo 'yaṃ janakajanitabhāvaḥ. vedanā tṛtīye kṣaṇe iti. indriyārthakṣaṇaḥ prathamaḥ vijñānotpattikṣaṇo dvitīyo vedanotpattikṣaṇas tṛtīya iti. na sarvatra vijñāne vedanā prāpnotīti. vijñānakṣaṇe dvitīye vedanāyā abhāvāt. na ca sarvavijñānaṃ sparśaḥ. vedanākṣaṇe tṛtīye vijñānaṃ na sparśaḥ. pūrvadvitīyakṣaṇayoḥ sparśa eva vidhīyate. pūrvasparśahetukā hy uttarasparśe vedanā. yo 'yam idānīṃ dvitīyaḥ kṣaṇaḥ sparśabhāvenoktaḥ. tatra pūrvasparśahetukā prathamakṣaṇavijñānahetukā [Tib. 297b] vedanotpadyate. tatsparśapūrvikāpy anyasminn ity evaṃ sarvatra vijñāne vedanā prāpnoti. sarvaṃ ca vijñānaṃ sparśa iti. te ca sparśāḥ savedanakā iti bhinnālambanayor iti vistaraḥ. bhinnam ālambanam anayoḥ. tau bhinnālambanau. pūrvasya rūpam ālambanam uttarasya śabdaḥ tayor bhinnālambanayoḥ pūrvasparśahetukā rūpālambanasparśahetukā uttaratra sparśe śabdālambane yad vedanotpadyate. ity etad ayuktaṃ. kathaṃ hi nāmeti doṣam āviṣkaroti. anyajātīyālambanasparśasaṃbhūtā rūpaprakārālambanāt sparśāt saṃbhūtā vedanā anyālambanā bhaviṣyati. śabdālaṃbanā bhaviṣyati. vidhurakāraṇatvāt kāryasyāsaṃbhāvanā. yadā hi rūpālambanāt sparśāt saṃbhūtā vedanā rūpālambanaiva vedanā bhaviṣyati. tadā pūrvasparśahetukottaratra sparśe vedaneti yuktaṃ. yadā tu rūpālambanāt
body.translated_text: 'Contact precedes feeling in time' — the other [says] — the venerable <s>Śrīlāta</s>. 'That coming together of the three is contact' — this state of producer and produced [he explains]: feeling [arises] in the third moment. The first moment is that of the sense-faculty and object; the second is the moment of the arising of consciousness; the third is the moment of the arising of feeling. 'Not in every consciousness is feeling obtained' — because feeling is absent in the second moment of consciousness. And not every consciousness is contact — in the third moment, the moment of feeling, consciousness is not contact. Contact is established only in the first and second moments. For feeling in a subsequent contact is caused by a prior contact. That which is now stated as the second moment in the nature of contact — therein, feeling arises caused by a prior contact, i.e., caused by consciousness of the first moment. [Tib. 297b] 'Preceded by that contact, in another [moment] too' — thus feeling is obtained in every consciousness. And every consciousness is contact. And those contacts have feeling. 'Of different objects' — and so on in detail. Different is the object of these two. Those two [are] of different objects. The former has form as its object, the latter has sound [as its object]. Of those two having different objects, the feeling that arises in the latter contact — which has sound as its object — caused by the prior contact which has form as its object, i.e., caused by the contact having form as its object — this is not logical. How indeed — he makes the fault evident — feeling arising from contact having an object of a different type — arising from a contact having form as its aspect of object — will have a different object, namely will have sound as its object. Because of the remoteness of the cause, the effect is inconceivable. For when feeling arising from a contact having form as its object will itself be a feeling having form as its object — then 'feeling caused by a prior contact in a subsequent contact' is logical. But when from a contact having form as its object

body.text: sparśāc chabdālambanā vedanotpadyate. tadā katham etad yokṣyate. kāraṇānurūpaṃ hi loke kāryaṃ dṛśyate. atha mataṃ rūpālambanāt sparśāt saṃbhūtā vedanā śabdālambanasparśasaṃprayuktāpi rūpālambanā bhavatīti. ata idam āha. yena vā cittena saṃprayuktā. tato bhinnālambaneti. tataḥ śabdālambanāc cittād bhinnālambanā. [Tib. 298a] yata utpannā rūpālambanā. tena samālambanety arthaḥ. kathaṃ cāsau tena saṃprayuktety ucyate. samaṃ prayuktā hi saṃprayuktā. yady abhinnāśrayatvāt kathaṃ śrotrāśrayotpannā satī rūpālambanā bhaviṣyati. kathaṃ na bhaviṣyati. cittacaittānām āśrayeṇaikaviṣayapravṛttatvāt. tasmād anyatarālambanatve 'pi vedanāyā doṣaḥ. sa doṣaḥ pradarśyate. yadi tāvad rūpālambanāt sparśād utpannā vedanā śabdādyālambanāntaram ālambate. sa rūpālambanaḥ sparśaḥ sukhavedanīyo yāvad aduḥkhāsukhavedanīya iti na prāpnoti. ekālambanayā tu vedanayā tathā nirdeśo yukta iti. astu tarhīti vistaraḥ. yady evaṃ doṣo 'stu tarhi. tasmiṃ kāle. kasmiṃ kāle. śabdālaṃbanakāle. sparśabhūtaṃ vijñānam avedanakaṃ. tasmāc ca śabdālambanād yat pūrvaṃ vijñānaṃ savedanakaṃ tan na sparśaḥ. evaṃ hi nirdoṣaṃ bhavatīti. anyathā hi yadi pūrvotpannaṃ savedanakaṃ vijñānaṃ sparśaḥ syāt. tadaivaṃ sparśapratyayā vedaneti yathokto doṣaḥ syāt. punaḥ kāraṇaṃ. kiṃcid vijñānam avedanakaṃ. kiṃcic ca na sparśaḥ pratyayavaidhuryāt. vidhurā hi pratyatā vipratibhandhenāvasthitāḥ. na hi sarvaḥ samanantarapratyayo vedanāpratyayaṃ sparśabhūtaṃ vijñānaṃ [Tib. 298b] janayituṃ samartha iti. tad evaṃ tasya bhinnālambanaṃ vijñānam ekāntenāvedanakaṃ. tadutpādakaṃ cāsparśabhūtaṃ. yadi tu rūpālambanāc cakṣurvijñānād anantaraṃ rūpālambanam eva cakṣurvijñānam utpadyate. manovijñānaṃ vā. tat savedanakaṃ pūrvotpannaṃ sparśa iti. evaṃ satīti. mahābhūmikaniyamo bhidyata iti. sparśavedanayoḥ paryāyeṇa niyamāt. tisrā bhūmaya iti. savitarkā savicārā kāmadhātuḥ prathamaṃ ca dhyānam. avitarkā vicāramātrā dhyānāntaram. avitarkā avicārā dvitīyād dhyānāt prabhṛti yāvad bhavāgraṃ. kuśalā bhūmiḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ. evam akuśalā avyākṛtāḥ. śaikṣī bhūmiḥ śaikṣasyānāsravā dharmāḥ. aśaikṣī aśaikṣasyānāsravā dharmāḥ. naiva śaikṣīnāśaikṣī bhūmiḥ sāsravā dharmāḥ. asaṃskṛtā iha nocyante. caittasambandhāt. tad ya etasyām iti vistaraḥ. tad iti vākyopanyāse. ya iti ye caitasikāḥ. etasyāṃ sarvasyāṃ bhūmāv iti. savitarkasavicārāyāṃ bhūmau. yāvan naivaśaikṣīnāśaikṣyāṃ bhūmau. te mahābhūmikāḥ vedanācetanādayo yathoktāḥ.
body.translated_text: there arises feeling having sound as its object — then how will this be coherent? For in the world, the effect is seen to conform to the cause. Or if it is thought that feeling arising from a contact having form as its object, even when associated with a contact having sound as its object, has form as its object — to this he says: 'Or from the consciousness with which [the feeling] is associated — [the feeling] has a different object from that.' From that consciousness having sound as its object, [the feeling] has a different object. [Tib. 298a] Since [it arose] from [a contact with] form as object, it has the same object — this is the meaning. And how can it be said to be 'associated' with that [consciousness]? For 'associated' (<s>saṃprayukta</s>) means 'operating together.' If because of having the same support — how will [a feeling] arisen in dependence on the ear-support have form as its object? How will it not? Because mind and mental factors operate on one object through [the same] support. Therefore, even if feeling has either [possible] object, there is a fault. That fault is demonstrated: if feeling arisen from contact having form as its object takes a different object such as sound and the rest — then the statement that that contact having form as object is 'to be experienced as pleasant,' up to 'to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant' — this is not obtained. But with feeling having the same object, such a statement is logical. 'Then let it be so' — and so on in detail. If there is such a fault, then let it be. At that time — at what time? — at the time of having sound as object — the consciousness that has the nature of contact is without feeling. And from that [consciousness having] sound as object, the prior consciousness that had feeling is not contact. For thus it becomes faultless. Otherwise, if the prior consciousness that had feeling were contact, then the fault as stated — 'feeling conditioned by contact' — would follow. Again, the reason: some consciousness is without feeling, and some is not contact — because of the remoteness of conditions. 'Remote' means conditions standing in an obstructed [state]. For not every immediately preceding condition is capable of producing [Tib. 298b] a consciousness that has the nature of contact and has feeling as its condition. Thus, the consciousness of [that person] having a different object is entirely without feeling, and what produces it is not of the nature of contact. But if from a visual consciousness having form as its object, there arises next a visual consciousness again having form as its object — or a mental consciousness — that, having feeling, and being produced previously, is contact. This being so, the restriction of the <s>mahābhūmika</s>s (great ground-[dharmas]) is broken — because of the alternation of contact and feeling. 'Three grounds' — with applied thought and sustained thought: the Desire Realm and the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Without applied thought, with sustained thought alone: the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>. Without applied thought and without sustained thought: from the second <s>dhyāna</s> onward up to the peak of existence. The wholesome ground consists of wholesome <s>dharma</s>s. Similarly, the unwholesome and indeterminate [grounds]. The trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>) ground consists of the outflow-free <s>dharma</s>s of a trainee. The non-trainee (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) ground consists of the outflow-free <s>dharma</s>s of a non-trainee. The neither-trainee-nor-non-trainee ground consists of <s>dharma</s>s with outflows. The unconditioned are not stated here — because of their connection with mental factors. 'Now, whatever [mental factors] in this [ground]' — and so on in detail. '<s>Tad</s>' introduces the sentence. '<s>Ya</s>' — whatever mental factors. 'In this entire ground' — in the ground with applied thought and sustained thought, up to the neither-trainee-nor-non-trainee ground — those <s>mahābhūmika</s>s: feeling, volition, and the rest, as stated.

ye kuśalāyām eva bhūmau. [Tib. 299a] te kuśalamahābhūmikāḥ śraddhādayaḥ. ye kliṣtāyām eva. te kleśamahābhūmikāḥ. avidyādayo yathoktā eva. te punar yathāsaṃbhavam iti vistaraḥ. te punar mahābhūmikādayaḥ. ye yasyāṃ saṃbhavanti. te tasyāṃ paryāyeṇa. na tu sarve yugapat. ity apare. tadyathā vedanā sarvāsu bhūmiṣu bhavaty api na yugapat saṃjñācetanāsparśamanaskārādibhir bhavati. tathā sparśo vedanādibhiḥ.
tathā kuśalāyāṃ vitarkādaya ityevamādikaṃ. apare punar evaṃ vyācakṣate. yathā paṃcaskaṃdhake likhitaṃ. tathedaṃ grahītavyam iti. tadyathā chandaḥ katamaḥ. abhipretavastuny abhilāṣaḥ. anabhiprete nāsti chanda ity abhiprāyaḥ. adhimokṣaḥ katamaḥ. niścite vastuni tathaivāvadhāraṇaṃ. smṛtiḥ katamā. saṃstute vastuny asaṃpramoṣaḥ. cetaso 'bhilapanatā. samādhiḥ katamaḥ. upaparīkṣye vastuni cittasyaikāgratā. prajñā katamā. tatraiva pravicayo yogāyogavihito 'nyathā cety evamādiḥ paṃcaskaṃdhakagrantho draṣṭavyaḥ. tatra hy uktaṃ paṃca sarvatragāḥ. vedanāsaṃjñāsparśamanaskāracetanāḥ. paṃca pratiniyataviṣayāḥ. chandādhimokṣasmṛtisamādhiprajñā [Tib. 299b] ity evamādi. akuśalamahābhūmikās tu pāṭhaprasaṃgenāsaṃhitā iti. sūtrādiṣu pāṭhāt. kuśalam akuśalam avyākṛtam ity evaṃ pāṭhaprasaṃgenāsaṃhitāḥ. adhyāropitāḥ paścād ity arthaḥ. pūrvaṃ na paṭhyaṃte sma. prakaraṇapāde mahābhūmikāḥ kuśalamahābhūmikāḥ kleśamahābhūmikāḥ parīttakleśamahābhūmikāś ceti caturvidhā paṭhyante. sahajātā ity ucyante. na sparśasahajātā iti. aviśeṣitatvād ete vedanādayaḥ parasparasahajātāḥ. na tu sparśenety arthaparigraheṇa parihartavyaṃ sūtram ity arthaḥ. maitrīsahagatam iti. ayaṃ sahaśabdo nāvaśyaṃ yugapadbhāve samanaṃtare 'pi dṛṣṭaḥ. na hi maitryāḥ smṛtisaṃbodhyaṃgasya ca samavadhānam asti. naitryā ekāntasāsravatvāt. smṛtisaṃbodhyaṃgasya caikāntānāsravatvāt. tasmād ajñāpakam etat. saṃdṛṣṭā iti. sahotpannā ity abhiprāyaḥ. tatra hi sūtra iti. yatraivoktaṃ. yā vedanā yā cetanā yā ca saṃjñeti vistareṇa. tatra sūtra ity arthaḥ. tan na vijñāyata iti vistaraḥ. kiṃ tāvad ayam eṣāṃ vedanādīnāṃ ālambananiyamaḥ ālambane niyamaḥ. yad evālambanaṃ vedayate. tad eva cetayate yāvad vijñānaṃ vijānātīti. [Tib. 300a] utāho kṣaṇaniyamaḥ yasminn eva kṣaṇe vedayate. tasminn eva yāvad vijānātīti. vayaṃ brūmaḥ. ālambananiyamo 'yam iti. tasmān na sūtravirodha ity abhiprāyaḥ. ācārya āha. tatraiva sūtre āyuruṣmaṇoḥ sāhabhāvye saṃsṛṣṭavacanāt siddhaḥ kṣaṇaniyama iti. āyur uṣmā ca saṃsṛṣṭau. imau dharmau na visaṃsṛṣṭāv iti. āyuruṣmaṇoḥ
body.translated_text: Those that exist only in the wholesome ground — those are the <s>kuśalamahābhūmikas</s> (great-ground-factors of the wholesome): faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the rest. Those that exist only in the afflicted [ground] — those are the <s>kleśamahābhūmikas</s> (great-ground-factors of affliction): ignorance and the rest, just as stated. 'And those, as possible' — and so forth in detail. Those <s>mahābhūmikas</s> and the rest — those that occur in whichever [ground], they occur in that [ground] in succession, but not all simultaneously — so say others. For example, feeling exists in all grounds, yet does not occur simultaneously with perception, volition, contact, attention, and the rest. Similarly, contact [does not occur simultaneously] with feeling and the rest. Similarly, in the wholesome [ground], thought (<s>vitarka</s>) and the rest, and so on. Others, however, explain thus: as written in the <s>Pañcaskandhaka</s> (Treatise on the Five Aggregates), so this should be understood. For example: what is desire (<s>chanda</s>)? Aspiration toward a desired object; with respect to what is not desired, there is no desire — this is the intent. What is resolve (<s>adhimokṣa</s>)? Determination regarding a certain object just as it is. What is mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>)? Non-forgetfulness regarding a familiar object; the naming activity of the mind. What is concentration (<s>samādhi</s>)? One-pointedness of mind regarding an object to be examined. What is wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>)? Investigation therein, arranged as appropriate and inappropriate, and otherwise — thus the <s>Pañcaskandhaka</s> text should be consulted. For there it is stated: five are universal — feeling, perception, contact, attention, and volition; five have determinate objects — desire, resolve, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom — and so on. 'The unwholesome great-ground-factors, however, were included through textual association' — from their listing in sūtras and the like: 'wholesome, unwholesome, indeterminate' — thus included through textual association; meaning they were superimposed later and were not previously listed. In the <s>Prakaraṇapāda</s>, four types are listed: <s>mahābhūmikas</s>, <s>kuśalamahābhūmikas</s>, <s>kleśamahābhūmikas</s>, and <s>parīttakleśamahābhūmikas</s>. 'They are called co-born' — 'not co-born with contact' — since they are undifferentiated, these feeling and the rest are mutually co-born, but not [specifically] with contact — the sūtra should be interpreted by grasping the meaning thus. 'Accompanied by loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>)' — this word 'accompanied' (<s>saha</s>) is not necessarily [used] for simultaneity; it is also seen for immediate succession. For there is no co-occurrence of <s>maitrī</s> and the mindfulness factor of awakening (<s>smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅga</s>) — since <s>maitrī</s> is exclusively with outflows, and the mindfulness factor of awakening is exclusively without outflows. Therefore this is not indicative [of simultaneity]. 'Seen together' — the intent is co-arisen. 'For in that sūtra' — where indeed it was stated: 'whatever feeling, whatever volition, and whatever perception' — and so forth in detail — in that sūtra, this is the meaning. 'That is not understood' — and so forth in detail. Is this a restriction of their object (<s>ālambana</s>) — that the very object that is felt is also intended, up to consciousness cognizing? Or is it a restriction of moment — that in the very moment one feels, in that very moment one cognizes, and so on? We say: this is a restriction of object. Therefore there is no contradiction with the sūtra — this is the intent. The <s>Ācārya</s> says: in that very sūtra, from the statement of co-existence regarding lifespan and warmth (<s>āyuṣ</s> and <s>uṣman</s>), the restriction of moment is established — 'lifespan and warmth are conjoined; these two dharmas are not disjoined' — of lifespan and warmth,

body.text: sahotpannatoktā bhavati. tayor anālambanatvāt. tad evaṃ sādhitaṃ bhavati. avaśyaṃ sahotpannāni vedanāsaṃjñācetanāvijñānāni. tatra sūtre saṃsṛṣṭavacanenoktatvāt. āyuruṣmavad iti. tad katham iti vistaraḥ. tat kathaṃ vijñānaṃ cāsti. na ca trayāṇām indriyaviṣayavijñānānāṃ saṃnipātaḥ. tasmād avaśyaṃ vijñānāstitve saṃnipāto 'bhyupagantavyaḥ. saṃnipātaś ca te sparśa iti. tenedaṃ te virudhyate. na sarvavijñānaṃ sparśa iti. saṃnipāto vā na sparśa iti. punaḥsaṃdhikaraṇaṃ cātra draṣṭavyam iti. pūrvatrāsiddham iti sakāralopasyāsiddhatvād guṇo na prāpnoti. parihāras tu. īṣadarthe 'yaṃ nañ draṣṭavyaḥ. īṣatsiddham asiddham ity ataḥ siddhatvāt sakāralopasya guṇo bhavati. saiṣa dāśarathī rāma iti yathā.
body.translated_text: co-arising is stated, since those two have no object (<s>anālambana</s>). Thus it has been established: feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness are necessarily co-arisen, because in that sūtra it is stated through the word 'conjoined,' just like lifespan and warmth. 'How then?' — and so forth in detail. How then does consciousness exist, and yet the conjunction (<s>saṃnipāta</s>) of the three — faculty, object, and consciousness — [not occur]? Therefore, when consciousness exists, conjunction must necessarily be accepted. And 'conjunction is contact (<s>sparśa</s>).' Therefore this [position] contradicts yours: either 'not all consciousness is contact' or 'conjunction is not contact.' And here a re-joining [of the compound] should be seen. 'Previously not established' — since the elision of the letter 'sa' is not established, the euphonic change (<s>guṇa</s>) should not obtain. But the resolution is: this negative particle should be seen as meaning 'slightly' — 'slightly established is not-established' — therefore, since the sa-elision is established, the euphonic change occurs. Like '<s>sa eṣa Dāśarathī Rāma</s>' (That very Rāma, son of Daśaratha).

body.text: (III.32cd) ṣaṭ saumanasyopavicārā iti vistaraḥ. cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā saunanasyasthānīyāni rūpāṇi upavicarati. śrotreṇa śabdān śrutvā saumnanasyasthānīyāṃ śabdān upavicarati. evaṃ yāvan manasā dharmān vijñāya saumanasyasthānīyān [Tib. 300b] dharmān upavicarati. evaṃ cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā daurmanasyasthānīyāny upekṣāsthānīyāni ceti vistareṇa yojyaṃ. trayo bhaviṣyantīti. saumanasyadaurmanasyopekṣāsvabhāvatraividhyāt. eka iti. manovijñānamātrasaṃprayogāt. ṣaḍ iti. rūpādiviśayaṣaṭkabhedāt. tribhir api sthāpaneti. yad vedanādravyaṃ manovijñānamātrasaṃprayuktam ekaṃ. tat saumanasyādisvabhāvatrayabhedāt tridhā bhidyate. tat punaḥ pratyekaṃ viṣayaṣaṭkabhedāt ṣoḍhā bhidyate. ity aṣṭādaśa bhavaṃti. svabhāvavyavasthāpanāyām asatyāṃ saumanasyadaurmanasyopekṣopavicārā na syāt. saṃprayogavyavasthāpanāyām asatyāṃ manopavicārā ity eva na syāt. aṣṭādaśavyatiriktāś ca syuḥ. rūpādiviṣayaṣaṭkālambanavyavasthāpanāyām asatyāṃ pratyekaṃ saumanasyādiṣodhābhedenāṣṭādaśa manopavicārā iti na syāt. tasmāt tribhir api vyavasthāpaneti siddhaṃ. asaṃbhinnālambanā iti. asaṃmiśrālambanāḥ. trayo dharmopavicārā ubhayatheti. ye rūpādiviṣayapaṃcakavyatiriktadharmālambanāḥ. te dharmopavicārā asaṃbhinnālambanāḥ. ye tu rūpādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ viṣayāṇāṃ dvau tṛīn [Tib. 301a] yāvat ṣaḍ api viṣayān ālambante. te saṃbhinnālambanāḥ.
body.translated_text: (III.32cd) 'Six <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure) mental explorations (<s>upavicāra</s>)' — and so forth in detail. Having seen forms with the eye, one mentally explores forms that are grounds for mental pleasure. Having heard sounds with the ear, one mentally explores sounds that are grounds for mental pleasure. Similarly up to: having cognized <s>dharmas</s> with the mind, one mentally explores <s>dharmas</s> that are grounds for mental pleasure. Similarly with 'having seen forms with the eye, [one mentally explores] those that are grounds for mental displeasure and those that are grounds for equanimity' — this should be applied in detail. 'There will be three' — because of the threefold nature: mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>), mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). 'One' — because of being associated with mind-consciousness alone. 'Six' — because of the sixfold division of objects: form and the rest. 'Established through all three' — the single feeling-substance associated with mind-consciousness alone is divided into three through the threefold nature of mental pleasure, displeasure, and equanimity. Each of those is then divided into six through the sixfold division of objects. Thus there are eighteen. Without the establishment by nature, there would be no mental pleasure, displeasure, and equanimity explorations. Without the establishment by association, there would be no designation as 'mental explorations.' And there would be [types] other than eighteen. Without the establishment by the sixfold object, there would be no eighteen mental explorations with the sixfold division of mental pleasure and the rest for each. Therefore, establishment through all three is proven. 'Of unmixed objects' — of unmixed objects [of perception]. 'The three <s>dharma</s>-explorations in both ways' — those that have as their object <s>dharmas</s> other than the five objects of form and the rest — those are <s>dharma</s>-explorations with unmixed objects. But those that take as their object two, three, up to all six objects among the six objects of form and the rest — those have mixed objects.

body.text: manaḥ kileti. kilaśabdaḥ paramatadyotakaḥ. manaḥ kila pratītyāśritya viṣayān upavicaranty ālambanta ity arthaḥ. upavicārayantīti pravartayanti. katham ity āha. vedanāvaśena manaso viṣayeṣu punaḥpunar vicāraṇād iti punaḥpunar ity upaśabdasyārthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'The mind, indeed (<s>kila</s>)' — the word <s>kila</s> indicates another's position. 'Depending on the mind, they explore objects' — meaning they take as objects. 'They cause to explore' means they cause to operate. How? He says: through the force of feeling, because of the mind's repeated exploration of objects — 'repeated' is the meaning of the prefix <s>upa</s>.

body.text: nāpy upavicāriketi. asantīrikety arthaḥ. ayoga ity asaṃbhavaḥ. yadi mana evāśritā vedanā manopavicāraḥ. tṛīye dhyāne yat sukhaṃ. tan mana evāśritaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Nor are there explorations' — meaning they do not exist. '<s>Ayoga</s>' means impossibility. If feeling based on the mind alone were a mental exploration, then the happiness (<s>sukha</s>) in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, which is based on the mind alone —

body.text: na cakṣurindriyādyāśritam iti. tasya kasmān manopavicāreṣv agrahaṇaṃ. āditaḥ kileti viṣtaraḥ. ādāv āditaḥ. kileti paramate. kāmadhātau manobhūmikaṃ sukḥaṃ nāsti. tasmān na tan manopavicāraḥ. ataḥ paścād api tṛtīye dhyāne sukhendriyasya manaāśritatve 'pi manopavicāreṣv agrahaṇaṃ. yathā saumanasyopavicārasya pratidvaṃdvena daurmanasyopavicāraḥ. naivaṃ. sukhopavicārasya pratidvaṃdvena duḥkhopavicāro 'sti. manovijñānanāśritatvād duḥkhasya. ataḥ sarvatra tat sukhaṃ na manopavicāra iti.
body.translated_text: — and not based on the eye-faculty and the rest — why is it not included among the mental explorations? 'From the beginning, indeed (<s>kila</s>)' — and so forth in detail. At the beginning, from the start — '<s>kila</s>' in another's view — in the Desire Realm, there is no happiness (<s>sukha</s>) belonging to the mental ground. Therefore it is not a mental exploration. Hence, later too, even though the happiness-faculty in the third <s>dhyāna</s> is mind-based, it is not included among the mental explorations. Just as the mental displeasure exploration is the counterpart of the mental pleasure exploration — it is not so [that] there is a pain exploration as the counterpart of a happiness exploration, because pain (<s>duḥkha</s>) is not based on mind-consciousness. Therefore, that happiness is not a mental exploration in any case.

body.text: saumanasyasthānīyānīti. saumanasyajanakāni. paṃceti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 301b] paṃcabhir vijñānakāyair abhinirhṛtatvam utpāditatvam abhisaṃdhāya cetasikṛtvā etad uktaṃ cakṣuṣā rūpāṇīti vistareṇa. manobhūmikās tv ete. tadyathā aśubhā. cakṣurvijñānābhinirhṛtā ca pūrvaṃ vinīlakādidarśanāt. manobhūmikā ca samāhitatvāt. api tv iti. cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā yāvat kāyena spraṣṭavyāni spṛṣṭveti vacanād acodyam etat. yadi cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi paśyan saumanasyasthānīyāni rūpāṇy upavicaratīty uktaṃ syāt. yāvat kāyena spraṣṭavyāni spṛśann iti. syāc codyaṃ. na tv evam uktam ity acodyam evaitat. yo 'py adṛṣṭveti vistaraḥ. yo 'pi śrutvā parato manasopavicaraty ālambate. te 'pi tasya manopavicārāḥ. itarathā hīti vistaraḥ. rūpadhātvālambanā rūpādyupavicārā na syuḥ. kāmadhātūpapannena rūpāvacarāṇāṃ rūpādīnām apratyakṣīkṛtatvāt. kāmadhātvālambanāś ca gandharasaspraṣṭavyopavicārā rūpadhātūpannasya na syuḥ. tasya gaṃdhādīnām aviṣayatvāt. yathā tu vyaktataraṃ. tathoktam iti. pratyakṣīkṛtarūpādyālambanānāṃ manopavicārāṇāṃ vyaktataratvāt. yo 'pi rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā tatsahacarāṃ chandān upavicarati. so 'pi tasya manopavicāraḥ. yathā tv anākulaṃ. tathoktaṃ. kathaṃ cānākulam ity āha. indriyārthavyavacchedata [Tib. 302a] iti. cakṣurādīndriyavyavacchedena. rūpādyarthavyavacchedena coktam iti. anyathā hy ākulaṃ syāt. eakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā saumanasyasthānīyāṃ chandān upavicaratīty evamādi.
body.translated_text: 'Grounds for mental pleasure' — means producing mental pleasure. 'Five' — and so forth in detail. Intending that [they are] produced, brought about by the five consciousness-groups, this was said: 'having seen forms with the eye' — and so forth in detail. But these belong to the mental ground. For example, the meditation on the foul (<s>aśubhā</s>): it is produced by eye-consciousness (from previously seeing blue-discolored corpses and the like), and belongs to the mental ground (because it occurs in concentration). 'However' — since it is said 'having seen forms with the eye, up to having touched tangibles with the body,' this is not an objection. If it had been said 'one who is seeing forms with the eye explores forms that are grounds for mental pleasure,' up to 'one who is touching with the body' — then there would be an objection. But since it was not said thus, this is indeed not an objection. 'One who, even without having seen' — and so forth in detail. Even one who, having heard from others, mentally explores and takes as object — those too are his mental explorations. 'Otherwise' — and so forth in detail — mental explorations with Form Realm objects, such as form and the rest, would not exist [for a Desire Realm being], since one born in the Desire Realm has not directly perceived the forms and the like of the Form Realm. And mental explorations of smell, taste, and tangible objects with Desire Realm objects would not exist for one born in the Form Realm, since smell and the rest are not his domain. 'But as it is more evident, so it was stated' — because mental explorations with directly perceived objects of form and the like are more evident.
