Even one who, having seen forms, explores the desires accompanying them — that too is his mental exploration. 'But as it is unconfused, so it was stated.' How is it unconfused? He says: 'Through the distinction of faculties and objects' — stated through the distinction of faculties like the eye and through the distinction of objects like form. Otherwise it would be confused — like saying 'having seen forms with the eye, one explores grounds-for-mental-pleasure desires' and so on.

body.text: asti saṃtānaṃ niyamyeti. kasyacit sattvasya saṃtānam avekṣya. yad asya kiṃcitsaumanasyasthānīyam eva. yāvad upekṣāsthānīyam eva. na tv ālambanaṃ. kiṃ. niyamya. kiṃkāraṇaṃ. tad eva hy ālambanaṃ kasyacit saumanasyasthānīyaṃ. kasyacin neti.
body.translated_text: 'There is [variation when] a continuum is fixed' — having observed a particular being's continuum, whatever for him is exclusively a ground for mental pleasure, up to exclusively a ground for equanimity — but not the object [itself]. What [does it depend on]? It is fixed [by the individual]. For what reason? Because that very same object is a ground for mental pleasure for one person and not for another.

body.text: (III.33-35ab) evaṃ yāvad ārūpapratisaṃyuktā iti kati rūpapratisaṃyuktāḥ. teṣāṃ ca kati kimālambanāḥ. katy ārūpyapratisaṃyuktāḥ. teṣāṃ ca kati kimālambanā iti.
body.translated_text: (III.33-35ab) 'Thus, up to those associated with the formless' — how many are associated with the Form [Realm]? And how many of them have what objects? How many are associated with the Formless [Realm]? And how many of them have what objects?

children.translated_text: 'In <s>Kāma</s>, all have their own realm as object' —

body.text: iti. kāme kāmāvacarāṇāṃ manopavicārāḥ sarve 'ṣṭādaśa santi. sa eva ca kāmadhātuḥ teṣāṃ sarveṣām ālambanaṃ. svo dhātur ālambanam eṣām iti svālambanā iti kārikāpadavigrahaḥ
body.translated_text: thus. In <s>Kāma</s> [Realm], all eighteen mental explorations of the Desire Realm exist. And that very Desire Realm is the object of all of them. 'Their own realm is their object, hence they have their own realm as object' — this is the analysis of the verse-word.

children.translated_text: 'The Form [Realm] is the domain of twelve' —

children.text: iti. rūpī dhātuḥ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ dvādaśānāṃ manopavicārāṇāṃ gocaraḥ. ṣaḍ gandharasopavicārān apāsyeti. dvau gandharasāv ālambanau saumanasyopavicārau hitvā dvau gandharasālambanau daurmanasyopavicārau hitvā dvau tadālambanāv eva copekṣopavicārau hitveti. [Tib. 302b] kasmāt. tatra rūpadhātau tayor gandharasayor abhāvāt.
children.translated_text: thus. The Form Realm is the domain of twelve mental explorations belonging to the Desire Realm, setting aside the six smell-and-taste explorations. Setting aside the two smell-and-taste-object mental pleasure explorations, setting aside the two smell-and-taste-object mental displeasure explorations, and setting aside the two equanimity explorations with those same objects. Why? Because in the Form Realm, those two — smell and taste — do not exist.
'Without the smell, taste, olfactory-consciousness, and gustatory-consciousness elements' —

body.text: iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated.

children.translated_text: 'The higher [realm is the domain] of three' —

body.text: iti. trayāṇāṃ saumanasyadaurmanasyopekṣādharmopavicārāṇāṃ kāmāvacarāṇām uttaro dhātur ārūpyadhātur ālambanaṃ. tatra rūpādyabhāvāt.
body.translated_text: thus. The higher realm, the Formless Realm, is the object of three: the Desire Realm mental explorations of <s>dharma</s> — of mental pleasure, mental displeasure, and equanimity. Because form and the rest do not exist there.

body.text: daurmanasyopavicārāṇāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ abhāvāt.
body.translated_text: Because of the absence of the six mental displeasure explorations.

body.text: iti. aṣṭānām ālambanam aṣṭālambanaṃ. gandharasopavicārāṃś caturo hitveti. saumanasyopekṣopavicārau gandhālambanau dvau rasālambanau ca dvau hitvety arthaḥ. tatra tayor abhāvāt.
body.translated_text: thus. The object of eight is 'eight-object' (<s>aṣṭālambana</s>). 'Excluding the four — the mental examinations (<s>upavicāra</s>) having scent and taste [as objects]' — excluding the two <s>saumanasya</s>-examinations (those associated with joy) and the two <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations (those associated with equanimity) having scent and taste as objects — this is the meaning. Because of the absence of those two [i.e., scent and taste] there [in the form realm].

children.translated_text: 'The formless [realms are] the object of two' —

body.text: iti. saumanasyopekṣādharmopavicārayoḥ prathamadvitīyadhyānabhūmikayor ārūpyadhātur ālambanaṃ. rūpādyabhāvāt. ṣaḍ upekṣopavicārā eva santi nānya iti. rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmālambanā upekṣopavicārā eva santi. saumanasyopavicārāṇām api tṛtīye caturthe cābhāvāt. gandharasālambanau tu tatra kāmāvacaragandharasālambanāv ity avagantavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. Of the two <s>saumanasya</s>- and <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations of <s>dharmas</s>, belonging to the levels of the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>, the Formless Realm is the object — because of the absence of form and the rest [there]. 'Only six <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations exist, not others' — only <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations having form, sound, scent, taste, touch, and <s>dharmas</s> as objects exist [in the third and fourth dhyānas]; the <s>saumanasya</s>-examinations too do not exist in the third and fourth [dhyānas]. But the scent-and-taste object ones there should be understood as having desire-realm scent and taste as their objects.

body.text: tatra catvārā iti. ākāśānaṃtyāyatanasāmantakānantaryamārgasya caturthadhyānālambanatvāt. tatra ca rūpaśabdaspraṣṭavyadharmasadbhāvāt. yeṣāṃ tad vyavacchinnālambanam astīti. yeṣām ācāryāṇāṃ matena tad ākāśānaṃtyāyatanasāmaṃtakaṃ [Tib. 303a] vyavacchinnālambanaṃ pṛthakpṛthag rūpādyālambanam asamastālambanam ity arthaḥ. audārikādibhir ākārais tac caturthadhyānam ālambata iti ekeṣām ācāryāṇāṃ matam. yeṣām ācāryāṇāṃ matena paripiṇḍitālambanam eva tad ākāśānaṃtyāyatanasāmantakaṃ caturthadhyānabhūmikaskandhapaṃcakālambanam iti mataṃ. teṣām ācāryāṇāṃ. tatraika eva
body.translated_text: 'Therein, four' — because the preliminary path (<s>sāmantaka</s>), the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) of the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), has the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> as its object; and because form, sound, touch, and <s>dharmas</s> exist there [in the fourth dhyāna]. 'Of those who [hold] that its object is discrete' — of those masters whose view is that the preliminary [to the ākāśānantyāyatana] [Tib. 303a] has a discrete object — meaning a separate, individual object of form and the rest, not a collective object. [They hold that] it apprehends the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> through the aspects of grossness and the rest — this is the view of certain masters. Of those masters whose view is that the preliminary [to the ākāśānantyāyatana] has a collective object — i.e., has the five aggregates belonging to the level of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> as its object — of those masters,

body.text: saṃmiśrālambano dharmopavicāra iti.
body.translated_text: 'therein there is only one <s>dharma</s>-examination of mixed object.'

body.text: iti. keṣāṃ pakṣe. yeṣāṃ
body.translated_text: thus. According to whose position? Of those whose position is:

body.text: iti pakṣaḥ. na hi maulānām iti vistaraḥ. maulānām ārūpyāṇām adharo dhātur nālambanam adharabhūmikaṃ sāsravaṃ vastu nālambanam ity arthaḥ. paścāt pravedayiṣyāmīti.
body.translated_text: this position. 'For the principal [formless attainments] do not...' — thus the elaboration. The lower realm is not the object of the principal formless [attainments] — meaning: a thing with outflows belonging to a lower level is not their object. 'It will be explained later' —

children.translated_text: 'The principal wholesome formless [attainments] do not have a lower [realm] with outflows as their object' —

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: (III.35c) prathameti vistaraḥ. prathamadvitīyadhyānabhūmikair aṣṭābhiḥ samanvāgataḥ tṛtīyacaturthadhyānabhūmikaiś caturbhiḥ. katamair ity āha. kliṣṭaiḥ. gandharasālaṃbanān paryudasya. tatra gandharasābhāvāt. kathaṃ. prathamadvitīyayor dhyānayor dvādaśopavicārāḥ santīty uktaṃ. saumanasyopekṣopavicārāṇāṃ ṣaḍviṣayālambanavyavasthāpanāt. tatra svabhūmyālambanā rūpaśabdaspraṣṭavyadharmālambanāḥ saumanasyopavicārāś catvāraḥ kliṣṭāḥ. ye copekṣopavicārāḥ kliṣṭā eva catvāraḥ. taiḥ kāmadhātūpapanno rūpāvacarakuśalalābhī [Tib. 303]b samanvāgataḥ. adharabhūmyupapanno hy ūrdhvabhūmikaiḥ kliṣṭaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati. na tu viśiṣṭaiś caturbhir gandharasālambanaiḥ. teṣām akliṣṭatvāt. rūpāvacarakuśalālābhitvāt. ca. nāsty akliṣṭarūpāvacaradharmalābha iti. na taiḥ samanvāgataḥ. tṛtīyacaturthadhyānabhūmikā api ṣaḍ evopekṣopavicārā uktāḥ. teṣāṃ ye svabhūmyālambanāḥ kliṣṭāḥ. taiḥ samanvāgatas tathā. yau tu gaṃdharasālambanau. na tau kliṣṭau. ataḥ pūrvoktenaiva nyāyena na tābhyāṃ samanvāgataḥ. kliṣṭenaiveti. nākliṣṭena kuśalasyābhāvāt. lābhī rūpāvacarasyeti vistaraḥ. kāmadhātūpapanna eva lābhī rūpāvacarasya kuśalasya cittasyānāgamyasaṃgṛhītasyāvītarāgaḥ kāmadhātoḥ sarvaiḥ kāmāvacarair aṣṭādaśabhir api samanvāgataḥ. prathamadhyānabhūmikair daśabhir iti. kathaṃ daśabhir ity āha. saumanasyopavicāraiḥ kliṣṭair gaṃdharasālambanāv apāsyeti. saumanasyopavicārāḥ sāmaṃtakeṣu na bhavaṃti. sāmantakānām upekṣendriyasaṃprayogitvāt. ato maulasaṃgṛhītair eva saumanasyopavicāraiḥ kliṣṭaiḥ svabhūmyālambanaiś caturbhiḥ. samanvāgataḥ. na tu gandharasālambanābhyāṃ. maulakuśalālābhenākliṣṭalābhābhāvāt. na hi kliṣṭaṃ dhyānam adharālambanam asti. ṣaḍbhir upekṣopavicārair anāgamyabhūmikair iti. atrāviśeṣābhidhānād upekṣopavicāraiḥ [Tib. 304a] kliṣṭair api caturbhiḥ samanvāgataḥ sāmantakasaṃgṛhītaiḥ. ṣaḍbhiś copekṣopavicāraiḥ kuśalaiḥ
body.translated_text: (III.35c) 'The first...' — thus the elaboration. [A being] endowed with eight belonging to the levels of the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>, and four belonging to the levels of the third and fourth <s>dhyānas</s>. Which [four]? He says: 'defiled ones.' Excluding those having scent and taste as objects — because of the absence of scent and taste there. How [is this]? It was stated that there are twelve examinations in the first and second <s>dhyānas</s> — because of establishing the six-object classification for both <s>saumanasya</s>- and <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations. Therein, four <s>saumanasya</s>-examinations having one's own level as object — those having form, sound, touch, and <s>dharmas</s> as objects — are defiled; and four <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations that are defiled alone. With those, [Tib. 303b] one born in the desire realm who has obtained wholesome [states] of the form realm is endowed. For one born in a lower level is endowed with defiled [states] of a higher level — but not with the distinguished four having scent and taste as objects, because of their being non-defiled, and because of not having obtained wholesome [states] of the form realm. 'There is no obtaining of non-defiled form-realm <s>dharmas</s>' — therefore one is not endowed with those. In the third and fourth <s>dhyānas</s> too, only six <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations were stated. Of those, the ones that have one's own level as object and are defiled — with those one is endowed, in the same manner. But the two having scent and taste as objects — those two are not defiled; therefore, by the very principle stated before, one is not endowed with those two. 'Only with defiled ones' — not with non-defiled ones, because of the absence of wholesome [states]. 'One who has obtained the form realm...' — thus the elaboration. One born in the desire realm who has obtained wholesome mind of the form realm, included in <s>Anāgamya</s> (the preliminary concentration), [and who is] not free from desire for the desire realm, is endowed with all eighteen desire-realm [examinations]; and with ten belonging to the level of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. How [is it] ten? He says: 'excluding the <s>saumanasya</s>-examinations that are defiled and have scent and taste as objects.' <s>Saumanasya</s>-examinations do not exist in the preliminary [concentrations], because the preliminaries are associated with the faculty of equanimity. Therefore, with four <s>saumanasya</s>-examinations that are defiled, having one's own level as object, and included in the principal [dhyāna]: one is endowed. But not with the two having scent and taste as objects — because of not having obtained non-defiled [states] through not having obtained the principal wholesome [dhyāna]; for there is no defiled <s>dhyāna</s> having a lower [realm] as object. 'With six <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations belonging to the <s>Anāgamya</s> level' — here, because of the non-specific statement, one is endowed with four <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations [Tib. 304a] that are defiled too, included in the preliminary; and with six wholesome <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations

body.text:
kāmadhātvālambanaiḥ svabhūmyālambanair api. dvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānārūpyajaiḥ pūrvavad iti. kathaṃ. sa eva kāmadhātāv upapanno lābhī rūpāvacarasya kuśalasya cittasyāvītarāgo dvitīyadhyānabhūmikair aṣṭābhiḥ. yair eva. alābhī gandharasālambanān apāsya. trtīyacaturthadhyānabhūmikaiś caturbhiḥ kliṣṭair eva. gandharasālambanau paryudasya. ārūpyāvacareṇaikena kliṣṭenaiva. anayā vartanyā mārgeṇa śeṣam anugantavyaṃ. kathaṃ. prathamadhyānopapanno dvitīyadhyānabhūmikasya kuśalasya cittasyālābhī prathamadhyānabhūmikaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvāgataḥ. dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaiḥ kliṣṭair aṣṭābhiḥ. tṛtīyacaturthadhyānārūpyajaiḥ pūrvavat. lābhī dvitīyadhyānabhūmikasya kuśalacittasya tadbhūmyavītarāgaḥ sarvaiḥ prathamadhyānabhūmikaiḥ. dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaiṛ aṣṭābhiḥ. caturbhiḥ saumanasyopavicāraiḥ kliṣṭaiḥ. gandharasālambnāv apāsya. caturbhiś copekṣopavicārair dvitīyadhyānasāmantakasaṃgṛhītaiḥ. tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikais caturbhiḥ kliṣṭaiḥ. gandharasālambanau paryudasya. evaṃ caturthadhyānabhūmikaiḥ. ārūpyāvacareṇaikena kliṣṭenaiva. dvitīyadhyānopapannas tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikasya kuśalasya cittasyālābhī [Tib. 304a] dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvāgataḥ. tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikaiś caturbhiḥ kliṣṭaiḥ. caturthadhyānārūpyajaiḥ pūrvavat. lābhī tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikasya kuśalacittasya tadbhūmyavītarāgaḥ sarvair dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaiḥ. tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikaiś caturbhir upekṣopavicāraiḥ kliṣṭair gandharasālambanāv apāsya. caturbhiś copekṣopavicārais tṛtīyadhyānasāmantakasaṃgṛhītaiḥ. caturthadhyānārūpyajaiḥ pūrvavat. eṣā dik. anayā diśā tṛtīyādiṣv api
dhyāneṣūpapannasya svabhūmyūrdhvabhūmikair upekṣopavicārair eva kliṣṭaiḥ kuśalaiś ca samanvāgamo yathāsaṃbhavaṃ yojyaḥ. upekṣādharmopavicāreneti. kāmāvacarasya nirmāṇacittasyopekṣāsaṃprayogitvāt.
body.translated_text: having the desire realm as object and also having one's own level as object. 'With those produced by the second, third, fourth <s>dhyānas</s>, and the formless [attainments] — as before' — how? That very [being] born in the desire realm who has obtained wholesome mind of the form realm, not free from desire [for the desire realm], is endowed with eight belonging to the level of the second <s>dhyāna</s> — the very same [as before]. Not having obtained [the wholesome of that level] — excluding those having scent and taste as objects. And with four belonging to the levels of the third and fourth <s>dhyānas</s>, defiled alone — excluding those having scent and taste as objects. And with one formless-realm [examination], defiled alone. By this method, the remainder should be understood. How? One born in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, not having obtained wholesome mind belonging to the level of the second <s>dhyāna</s>, is endowed with all those belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> level; with eight defiled ones belonging to the second <s>dhyāna</s> level; with those produced by the third, fourth <s>dhyānas</s>, and formless [attainments] — as before. One who has obtained wholesome mind of the second <s>dhyāna</s>, not free from desire for that level: with all those belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> level; with eight belonging to the second <s>dhyāna</s> level — four <s>saumanasya</s>-examinations that are defiled, excluding those having scent and taste as objects; and four <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations included in the preliminary of the second <s>dhyāna</s>. With four belonging to the third <s>dhyāna</s> level — defiled, excluding those having scent and taste as objects. Similarly with those belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> level. With one formless-realm [examination], defiled alone. One born in the second <s>dhyāna</s>, not having obtained [Tib. 304a] wholesome mind belonging to the level of the third <s>dhyāna</s>, is endowed with all those belonging to the second <s>dhyāna</s> level; with four belonging to the third <s>dhyāna</s> level — defiled; with those produced by the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and formless [attainments] — as before. One who has obtained wholesome mind of the third <s>dhyāna</s>, not free from desire for that level: with all those belonging to the second <s>dhyāna</s> level; with four <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations, defiled, belonging to the third <s>dhyāna</s> level — excluding those having scent and taste as objects; and with four <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations included in the preliminary of the third <s>dhyāna</s>. With those produced by the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and formless [attainments] — as before. This is the direction [of analysis]. By this direction, for one born in the third and further <s>dhyānas</s> too, the possession of <s>upekṣā</s>-examinations alone — defiled and wholesome — belonging to one's own and higher levels, should be applied as appropriate. 'With the <s>upekṣā</s>-<s>dharma</s>-examination' — because the creation-mind (<s>nirmāṇacitta</s>) of the desire realm is associated with equanimity.

body.text: apara āheti. ayam eva śāstrakāraḥ. na hi yo yasmād iti vistaraḥ. yaḥ pudgalaḥ yasmād rūpāder vītarāgaḥ. na sa tad rūpādy ālambanam upavicarati. katham upavicarati. tatrānunīyate vā. pratihanyate vā. apratisaṃkhyāya vopekṣata ity evaṃ. yadāpratisaṃkhyāyopekṣate nābhujati. tadā 'kuśalatvam. ato 'pratisaṃkhyāyeti viśeṣaṇam. ataḥ sāsravā api na sarve. kiṃ tarhi. sāṃkleśikāḥ. saṃkleśe bhavāḥ sāṃkleśikāḥ. saṃkleśānukūlāḥ. yaiḥ saumanasyādibhir mano viṣayān upavicarati. yeṣāṃ pratipakṣeṇa ṣaṭ sātatā vihārā iti. yeṣāṃ sāṃkleśikānāṃ prativyūhena. satataṃbhavāḥ sātatāḥ. vihārā yogaviśeṣā bhavaṃti. te ca ṣaṭ. katham ity āha. cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā naiva sumanā [Tib. 305a] bhavati. nānunīyate. na durmanā na pratihanyate. upekṣako bhavati
body.translated_text: 'Another says' — this is the treatise-author himself. 'For one who is free from desire for a given [level] does not examine that' — thus the elaboration. The person who is free from desire for form and the rest does not examine that form and the rest as an object. How does one examine? One is either attracted to it, or repelled by it, or regards it with equanimity without discernment (<s>apratisaṃkhyāya</s>). When one regards with equanimity without discernment, not partaking [of the object] — then it is unwholesome. Therefore the qualifier 'without discernment.' Therefore not all [examinations] with outflows [are upavicāras], but rather [only] those that pertain to defilement (<s>sāṃkleśika</s>). Those that exist in defilement are '<s>sāṃkleśika</s>' — favorable to defilement. Those <s>saumanasya</s>-examinations and the rest by which the mind examines objects — as the antidote to which the six constant abodes (<s>sātatā vihāra</s>) [are taught]. Of those defilement-related [examinations], as the counter-measure: those that exist constantly are 'constant' (<s>sātatā</s>); the abodes, i.e., the special modes of practice, are [thus six]. And they are six. How? He says: 'Having seen forms with the eye, one is neither joyful [Tib. 305a] — not attracted — nor displeased — not repelled — one remains equanimous

body.text: nābhujati. kathaṃ nābhujati. kim apratisaṃkhyāyāho svit pratisaṃkhyāyeti. viśeṣayann āha. smṛtimān saṃprajānann iti. smṛtisaṃprayuktayā prajñayā pratisamīkṣamāṇa ity arthaḥ. evaṃ yāvan manasā dharmān vijñāyeti. viṣayaṣaṭkabhedāt ṣaṭ sātatā iti. na hy arhata iti vistaraḥ. arhato laukikaṃ kuśalaṃ sāsravaṃ dharmālambanaṃ dharmāyatanālambanam adhigamadharmālaṃbanaṃ vā saumanasyam asti. tasya hi buddhasāṃtānikāṃ guṇān saṃmukhīkurvataḥ kuśalam saumanasyam utpadyate. na tasyaiṣa pratiṣedho yujyate. kasya tarhi. yat tu tatsāṃkleśikaṃ manasa upavicārabhūtaṃ. tasyaiṣa pratiṣedho lakṣyate. tasmāt sāsravā api na sarve saumanasyādaya upavicārā iti. atra bhadantānaṃtavarmā āha. ayuktam etat. kasmāt. sūtre 'nyathānirdeśāt. sūtre hi bhagavatā na sāṃkleśikā evopavicārā uktāḥ. evaṃ hy āha. tatra bhikṣavo ya ime ṣaṭ saumanasyopavicārāḥ. tān āśritya tān pratiṣṭhāya. ya ime ṣaṭ saumanasyopavicārāḥ. tān prajahīta. tatra bhikṣavo ya ime ṣaḍ upekṣopavicārāḥ. tān āśritya tān pratiṣṭhāya. ya ime ṣaḍ upekṣopavicārāḥ. tān prajahīta. dve bhikṣavo upekṣe. nānātvasaṃniśritā ekatvasaṃniśritā ca. tatra bhikṣavo yeyam ekatvasaṃniśritā upekṣā. tām āśritya tām adhiṣṭhāya. yeyaṃ nānātvasaṃniśritā upekṣā. tāṃ [Tib. 305b] prajahīteti. etasmāt sūtrāj jñāyate. na sāṃkleśikā eva saumanasyādaya upavicārā iti. tad etad ajñāpakaṃ. prahāṇavacane 'pi sāṃkleśikatvavinivṛtteḥ. na hītareṇetarasya saṃniśrayaprahāṇavacane 'pi saty eṣāṃ manopavicārāṇāṃ sāṃkleśikatvaṃ vinivartate. anyathāsaṃbhavāt. evaṃ āha. mānaṃ niśritya māna eva prahātavya iti. na tu jātu kvacin māno vyavadānikaḥ saṃbhavati. tasmāt kleśānāṃ parasparavirodhena vṛtter vṛttyantarasya cāpekṣayā guṇavattvāt. gurulāghavaṃ abhisaṃdhāya sūtre vacanād adoṣaḥ. nandādayo 'tra nidarśanaṃ. ataś caitad evaṃ. yad upekṣopavicārāṇām upekṣopavicārān eva prahāṇāya saṃniśrayatvena dideśa bhagavān. dve bhikṣava upekṣe ityādivacanāt. nanu ca gardhāśritanaiṣkramyāśritabhedena ṣaṭtriṃśac chāstṛpadānīti vacanāt siddham eṣāṃ sāṃkleśikavyavadānikatvaṃ vaibhāṣikamatānusārāt. adoṣaḥ. ācāryasyāpi manopavicāravyatiriktās tatra saumanasyādayas saṃti. punas ta eveti vistaraḥ. ta evāṣṭādaśopavicārāḥ kecid bhavāśritā adhiṣvaṃgāśritāḥ. kecin naiṣkramyāśritāḥ. naiṣkramyaṃ niṣkramabhāvaḥ saṃkleśāt saṃsāraduḥkhād vā. gardhanaiṣkramyāśritabhedena. dvāv aṣṭādaśakau ṣaṭtriṃṣac chāstṛpadāni. tadbhedasya teṣāṃ manopavicārānāṃ dvidhābhedasya
body.translated_text: he does not consume. How does he not consume? Is it without deliberation or with deliberation? Making a distinction, he says: 'Mindful and clearly comprehending' — meaning: examining with wisdom associated with mindfulness. Similarly up to: 'Having cognized <s>dharma</s>s with the mind.' 'Six types of continuity (<s>sātatā</s>), because of the sixfold division of objects.' 'For an <s>Arhat</s>' — and so on in detail. An <s>Arhat</s> has worldly wholesome mental pleasure with outflows that has <s>dharma</s>s as its object, or the <s>dharma</s>-base as its object, or the <s>dharma</s>s of attainment as its object. For when he turns his attention to the virtues belonging to the <s>Buddha</s>'s continuum, wholesome mental pleasure arises. The negation [in the <s>sūtra</s>] is not fitting with respect to him. With respect to whom then? That which is afflictive (<s>sāṃkleśika</s>) and has the nature of a mental exploration (<s>upavicāra</s>) of the mind — the negation is seen [to apply] to that. Therefore, not all mental pleasures and the rest that are with-outflows are explorations. Here the venerable <s>Anantavarman</s> says: this is not correct. Why? Because of a different exposition in the <s>sūtra</s>. For in the <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> did not speak of explorations as exclusively afflictive. For he said thus: 'Therein, O monks, whatever these six mental pleasure explorations are — relying on those, having established oneself in those, whatever these six mental pleasure explorations are — one should abandon them. Therein, O monks, whatever these six equanimity explorations are — relying on those, having established oneself in those, whatever these six equanimity explorations are — one should abandon them. Two equanimities, O monks: that relying on diversity and that relying on unity. Therein, O monks, whatever this equanimity relying on unity is — relying on that, having established oneself in that, whatever this equanimity relying on diversity is — [Tib. 305b] one should abandon it.' From this <s>sūtra</s>, it is known that not only the afflictive mental pleasures and the rest are explorations. But this is not indicative [of what you claim]. Even in a statement of abandonment, the afflictive nature is not removed. For even when there is a statement of relying on one to abandon the other, the afflictive nature of these mental explorations is not removed — because otherwise it would be impossible. Thus it is said: 'Relying on conceit, conceit itself is to be abandoned.' But conceit never, anywhere, becomes purificatory. Therefore, because afflictions function through mutual opposition, and because of the superiority relative to another functioning — considering [their relative] heaviness and lightness, the statement in the <s>sūtra</s> is without fault. <s>Nanda</s> and others are the illustration here. And therefore it is thus: that the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught equanimity explorations as the basis for abandoning equanimity explorations themselves: 'Two equanimities, O monks' — and so on. Surely, because of the statement 'thirty-six master-positions by the division of those relying on attachment and those relying on renunciation,' the afflictive and purificatory nature of these is established — following the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> position. There is no fault. Even for the <s>Ācārya</s>, there exist mental pleasures and the rest distinct from the mental explorations. 'Again, those very ones' — and so on in detail. Those very eighteen explorations — some are relying on existence (<s>bhavāśrita</s>), relying on attachment (<s>adhiṣvaṃgāśrita</s>); some are relying on renunciation (<s>naiṣkramyāśrita</s>). Renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>) is the state of going forth — from defilement or from the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. By the division into those relying on attachment and those relying on renunciation, the two [groups of] eighteen make thirty-six master-positions. Of those divisions — of those mental explorations' twofold division

body.text: śāstrā buddhena gamitatvād deśitatvād yathāsūtraṃ.
body.translated_text: having been guided, i.e., taught by the Master, the <s>Buddha</s>, according to the <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: Tib. 306a
body.translated_text: Tib. 306a

body.text: (36, 37) kleśakarmavastūnīti prajñāpitam iti.
body.translated_text: (36, 37) 'Afflictions, actions, and bases' — this is designated thus.

children.text: kleśās trīṇi dvayaṃ karma sapta vastv
children.translated_text: 'Afflictions are three, actions are two, bases are seven' —

body.text: iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of this statement.

body.text: evaṃ karmāṇi vipākotpattāv iti. āsannaṃ kāraṇam ity adhikṛtaṃ. kleśo 'pi hi kāraṇaṃ vipākasya. tat tu viprakṛṣṭaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Thus, actions [function] at the arising of retribution' — the proximate cause is the topic under discussion. For affliction too is a cause of retribution, but that is remote.

body.text: (III.38) te ca vyākhyātā iti.
body.translated_text: (III.38) 'And those have been explained' —

children.text:
mṛtyūpapattibhavayor antarābhavatīha yaḥ.
sa punarmaraṇāt pūrvam upapattikṣaṇāt para
children.translated_text:
'He who exists in the interval between the death-existence and the rebirth-existence —
that one [is] after death but before the moment of rebirth' —

body.text: iti. vacanāt vyākhyātāḥ. na paryavasthānaiḥ svataṃtrair iti. īrṣyāmātsaryakrodhamrakṣaiḥ. svātantryam eṣām. avidyānirmuktair anyakleśair asaṃprayogāt. avidyā hi sarvatraiva vidyata iti. na tatsaṃprayogenāsvātantryaṃ. āhrīkyādibhis tv anyakleśasaṃprayuktaiḥ pratisaṃdhibaṃdho na pratiṣidhyate. yady api sāvasthā mandiketi vistaraḥ. yady api sā maraṇāvasthā cittacaittasamudācārasyāpaṭutvāt.
body.translated_text: because of this statement, they have been explained. 'Not by the secondary afflictions (<s>paryavasthāna</s>) independently' — by jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), and concealment (<s>mrakṣa</s>). Their independence [is impossible] — because of the impossibility of association with other afflictions released from ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). For <s>avidyā</s> exists everywhere [with afflictions]. Therefore, through association with it, there is no independence [of secondary afflictions]. But by shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and the rest, which are associated with other afflictions, rebirth-connection is not negated. 'Even if that state becomes enfeebled' — and so on in detail. Even if that state of dying becomes enfeebled, because of the dullness of the operation of mind and mental factors —

body.text: iti vedanāmāndyāt. yas tu pudgalo yatra kleśe 'bhīkṣṇaṃ satataṃ caritaḥ pravṛttaḥ āsannaś ca maraṇakālasya pudgalasya. tadānīṃ maraṇakāle sa eva kleśaḥ samudācarati samutthāya mithyāḍrṣṭyādir api. pūrvāvedhāt pūrvākṣepāt. pūrvābhyāsād ity arthaḥ. atha vā yo 'sau tadānīṃ kleśa upatiṣṭhate. tasya pūrvaṃ phalabhāvena parigrahāvedhāt ākṣepāt. sa tadānīm upatiṣṭhata iti. kāmarūpadhātvor [Tib. 306b] aparisaṃkhyānāt. sarva eva catvāro bhavāḥ santīti. traya evārūpyeṣu
body.translated_text: because of the feebleness of feeling. But whatever person has been frequently and constantly engaged in whatever affliction, and is near the time of death — at that time, at the time of death, that very affliction becomes active, having arisen — even wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest — because of prior impression, because of prior impetus. The meaning is: because of prior habitual practice. Alternatively, whatever affliction comes into being at that time — because of the prior acceptance as fruit [of that affliction], through impetus — it comes into being at that time. 'Because [all four types] are not excluded in the Desire and Form Realms' — [Tib. 306b] because all four types of existence (<s>bhava</s>) indeed exist [there]. 'Only three in the Formless [Realm]' —

body.text: iti avadhāraṇāt. anayor itarayor dhātvor bhavacatuṣṭayaṃ tu jñātaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: because of this restriction. Of these other two realms, the fourfold existence is understood.

body.text: (III.39-41) niṣyandābhāvād iti. mūtrapurīṣābhāvād ity arthaḥ. sūkṣmāṇāṃ vā sūkṣmā iti. sūkṣmāṇāṃ sa sūkṣma āhāraḥ. bālakā jātamātrāḥ. svedajantukādayo yūkādayaḥ. ādiśabdena garbhasthāḥ. kavaḍīkārāhārāḥ
body.translated_text: (III.39-41) 'Because of the absence of outflow' — meaning: because of the absence of urine and feces. 'Or for minute [beings], minute [food]' — for minute beings, that food is minute. 'Infants' means newly born. 'Sweat-born creatures and the rest' — lice and the like. By the word 'and the rest,' those in the womb [are included]. '<s>Kavaḍīkāra</s> food (<s>kavaḍīkārāhāra</s>)' —

body.text: iti. kāmadhātāv eva kavaḍīkārāhāra ity avadhāraṇaṃ. kasmād ity āha. tadvītarāgāṇāṃ kavaḍīkārāhāravītarāgāṇāṃ tatra rūpārūpyadhātvor upapatteḥ. kavaḍīkṛṭyābhyavaharaṇāt piṇḍīkṛtya gilanāt kavaḍīkāraḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. The restriction is that <s>kavaḍīkāra</s> food exists only in the Desire Realm. Why? He says: because of the rebirth there — in the Form and Formless Realms — of those free from desire for <s>kavaḍīkāra</s> food. <s>Kavaḍīkāra</s> means making into morsels and consuming — [i.e.,] making into lumps and swallowing.

body.text: kavaḍīkṛtyābhyavaharaṇaṃ punar mukhena nāsikayā grāsavyavacchedād iti gandharasaspraṣṭavyāyatanāni sarvāṇy eva kavaḍīkāra ity ukte pṛcchati chāyātapajvālāprabhāsu
body.translated_text: Making into morsels and consuming, moreover, [is done] through the mouth and nose — because of the division of mouthfuls. Thus, all odor-, taste-, and tangible-sense-bases are <s>kavaḍīkāra</s>. When this is stated, he asks [about] shadow, sunlight, flame, and radiance

body.text: teṣāṃ gandhādīnāṃ katham āhāratvaṃ. na hi tatratyānāṃ gaṃdhādīnāṃ kavaḍīkṛtyābhyavaharaṇam astīti. bāhulyena kila eṣa nirdeśa iti. na tatratyānāṃ gandhādīnāṃ kavaḍīkāratvam iti pratipadyate. bāhulikas tu nirdeśaḥ
body.translated_text: how is there food-nature in those odors and the like? For there is no making-into-morsels-and-consuming of odors and the like belonging to those [shadow, etc.]. 'This exposition is indeed by preponderance' — he concedes that those odors and the like [in shadow, etc.] are not <s>kavaḍīkāra</s>. But the exposition is by preponderance:

children.translated_text: 'In <s>Kāma</s>, having the nature of three sense-bases' —

body.text: iti. kilaśabdaḥ paramatena svābhiprāyo 'dhikriyate. yāny api tv iti vistaraḥ. yāny api tu nābhyavahriyaṃte chāyādiṣu sthitiṃ cāharaṃti yāpanāṃ cāharaṃtī. tāny api sūkṣma āhāraḥ. snānābhyaṃgavat. yathā snānaṃ cābhyaṃgaś ca na kavaḍīkṛtyābhyavahriyate. āhāraś ca. tadvad iti.
body.translated_text: thus. The word '<s>kila</s>' indicates that another's position is being adopted while [stating] one's own view. 'But those that too' — and so on in detail. But those that are not consumed [in the ordinary way], yet in shadow and the rest bring about stability and bring about sustenance — those too are subtle food. 'Like bathing and anointing' — just as bathing and anointing are not consumed by making into morsels, yet are food — similarly.

children.translated_text: 'Because of not supporting one's own sense-faculty and the released' —

body.text: iti. svākṣasya svendriyasya tenānanugrahāt. muktānāṃ ca. kāmadhātor anāgāmyarhatām ananugrahāt. na rūpāyatanam āhāraḥ. rūpāyatanaṃ cābhyavahārakāla iti. yasmin kāle antarmukhapraviṣṭa āhāro bhujyate cakṣurviṣayātītaḥ. tasmiṃ kāle svam indriyaṃ cakṣurindriyaṃ tanmahābhūtāni ca tasyendriyasya. yāni mahābhūtāni āśrayaḥ. tāni nānugṛhṇāti tad rūpāyatanaṃ. kuta evānyānīndriyāṇi śrotrādīny anugrahīṣyati. aviṣayatvāt. aviṣayo hi śrotrādīnāṃ rūpāyatanaṃ. dṛśyamānaṃ tarhi bhojanakāle 'nugrahīṣyatīty ata āha. yadāpi ca dṛśyamāna iti vistaraḥ. atha katham idaṃ gamyate. tadāpi tadālambanaḥ sukhavedanīyaḥ sparśa āhāro na rūpam iti. ata āha. muktānām iti vistaraḥ. yadi tad dṛṣyamānam āhārakṛtyaṃ kuryāt. muktānām anāgāmyarhatāṃ kavaḍīkārāhāravītarāgāṇāṃ sumanojñam apy āhāraṃ paśyatāṃ anugrahaṃ kuryāt. yathā gandharasaspraṣṭavyāyatanāni indriyamahābhūtānām anugrahaṃ kurvanty abhyavahārakāle. tasmāt tadālambanaḥ sukhavedanīyaḥ sparśa āhāro bhavatīti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Of one's own sense-faculty' — one's own faculty — because of not supporting it. 'And of the released' — because of not supporting the non-returners and <s>Arhat</s>s of the Desire Realm who are free from desire for <s>kavaḍīkāra</s> food. The visible-form sense-base is not food. 'And the visible-form sense-base at the time of consumption' — at the time when food entered inside the mouth is consumed, having passed beyond the domain of the eye — at that time, it does not support its own faculty, the eye-faculty, nor the great elements of that faculty — those great elements that are the support [of the faculty]. It does not support those. How then would it support other faculties — the ear and the rest? Because [the visible-form base] is not their domain. For the visible-form sense-base is not the domain of the ear and the rest. 'But when seen, at the time of eating, it would support [them]' — therefore he says: 'even when being seen' — and so on in detail. But how is this understood? 'Even then, the contact that has it as object and is to be experienced as pleasant is food, not the visible form' — therefore he says: 'of the released' — and so on in detail. If that visible form, when seen, were to perform the function of food, then even for the released — the non-returners and <s>Arhat</s>s who are free from desire for <s>kavaḍīkāra</s> food — seeing even the most delightful food, it would support them, just as the odor-, taste-, and tangible-sense-bases support the faculties and great elements at the time of consumption. Therefore, the contact that has it as object and is to be experienced as pleasant is food — this is established.

body.text: iti vijñety ādantam etat. prajñeti yathā. vijñānam ity arthaḥ. kavaḍīkārāhāras tryāyatanātmakatvāt sāsrava iti siddhaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus — this ends with '<s>vijñā</s>.' Like '<s>prajñā</s>' [is short for <s>prajñāna</s>]. The meaning is: consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). <s>Kavaḍīkāra</s> food, because of having the nature of three sense-bases, is established as with-outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>).

body.text: sparśādayaḥ sāsravā anāsravāś ca saṃbhavantīti atas ta eva viśeṣitāḥ
body.translated_text: contact and the rest — since they can be both with-outflows and without-outflows, they are therefore specifically qualified:

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: na caivam anāsravā dharmā iti. na caivaṃ te bhūtānāṃ sthitaye yāpanāyai [Tib. 307b] sambhavaiṣiṇāṃ cānugrahāyeti. manonirjātatvād iti. nirvṛtter iti na tūpapatteḥ. mana ity avadhāraṇaṃ. ata eva bravīti. śuklaśoṇitādikaṃ kiṃcid bāhyam anupādāya bhāvād iti. ādiśabdena kardamapuṣpādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'And outflow-free <s>dharma</s>s are not thus' — and outflow-free [<s>dharma</s>s] are not thus [i.e., not food] — for the purpose of sustaining and supporting beings, [Tib. 307b] and for the benefit of those seeking [re]birth. 'Because of being produced from mind' — from cessation (<s>nirvṛtti</s>), not from rebirth. 'Mind' is restrictive. Therefore he says: 'Because of existing without depending on anything external such as semen and blood.' By the word 'and the rest,' the inclusion of mud, flowers, and the like [is indicated].

body.text: upapattyabhimukhatvāt abhinirvṛttir iti. upapattyabhimukhī nirvṛttir janmāsyeti abhinirvṛttiḥ. savyābādham iti saduḥkhaṃ. savyābādham abhinirvartyeti. idam atra jñāpakaṃ. antarābhavo 'bhinirvṛttir iti. tathāsti pudgala iti vistaraḥ. asmāt sūtrāc catuṣkoṭikād abhinirvṛttir antarābhava iti. asti pudgalo yasyābhinirvṛttisaṃyojanaṃ prahīṇaṃ nopapattisaṃyojanaṃ prahīṇaṃ nopapattisaṃyojanaṃ. asti yasyopapattisaṃyojanaṃ prahīṇaṃ nābhinirvṛttisaṃyojanaṃ. asti yasyābhinirvṛttisaṃyojanaṃ ca prahīṇaṃ upapattisaṃyojanaṃ ca. asti yasya naivābhinirvṛttisaṃyojanaṃ prahīṇaṃ nopapattisaṃyojanaṃ. dvidhātuvītarāgasyeti. kāmarūpadhātuvītarāgasyeti. anāgāmina iti viśeṣaṇaṃ. pṛthagjanānāṃ antarābhavasaṃyojanasyātyantāprahāṇāt. tad dhi bhikṣavaḥ prahīṇaṃ yad āryayā prajñayā prahīṇam iti vacanāt. tasya ca punarbhāvitvāt. tatra prathamā koṭir dvidhātuvītarāgasyānāgāminaḥ. dvitīyāntarāparinirvāyiṇaḥ. tṛtīyārhataḥ. caturthī tadanyeṣām asmadādeḥ. [Tib. 308a] pṛthagjanasya āryasya cāvītarāgasya kāmadhātuvītarāgasya rūpadhātāv upapadyamānasya ceti. bhūtā vārhanta iti. pūrvam evoktaḥ paryāyaḥ. bhūtā utpannāḥ saṃbhavaiṣiṇo 'ntarābhavikā iti. idānīm ayam aparaḥ paryāyaḥ. bhūtā arhantas traidhātukavītarāgatvāt. saṃbhavaiṣiṇaḥ satṛṣṇāḥ. traidhātuke saṃbhavaiṣitvāt.
body.translated_text: 'Because of being directed toward rebirth, it is <s>abhinirvṛtti</s>' — the birth that is the cessation directed toward rebirth is <s>abhinirvṛtti</s>. 'With affliction' (<s>savyābādha</s>) means with suffering. 'Bringing about [a birth] with affliction' — this is the indicator here: the intermediate existence is <s>abhinirvṛtti</s>. 'Thus there is a person' — and so on in detail. From this <s>sūtra</s> of four alternatives (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>), <s>abhinirvṛtti</s> is the intermediate existence. There is a person whose <s>abhinirvṛtti</s>-fetter has been abandoned but not the <s>upapatti</s> (rebirth)-fetter. There is one whose rebirth-fetter has been abandoned but not the <s>abhinirvṛtti</s>-fetter. There is one for whom both the <s>abhinirvṛtti</s>-fetter and the rebirth-fetter have been abandoned. There is one for whom neither the <s>abhinirvṛtti</s>-fetter has been abandoned nor the rebirth-fetter. 'Of one free from desire in two realms' — of one free from desire in the Desire and Form Realms. 'Of a non-returner' — this is a qualifier, because for ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), the intermediate existence fetter is never ultimately abandoned. For 'that, O monks, is abandoned which is abandoned by noble wisdom' — because of this statement. And because of its recurrence [for ordinary persons]. Therein, the first alternative is of a non-returner free from desire in two realms. The second is of an <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state). The third is of an <s>Arhat</s>. The fourth is of others such as ourselves — [Tib. 308a] of ordinary persons, of noble ones not yet free from desire, of those free from desire in the Desire Realm, and of those being reborn in the Form Realm. 'Or <s>bhūta</s>s mean <s>Arhat</s>s' — the synonym has been stated before. '<s>Bhūta</s>s' means 'arisen'; those seeking [re]birth (<s>saṃbhavaiṣin</s>) are those in the intermediate existence. Now another synonym: <s>bhūta</s>s are <s>Arhat</s>s, because of being free from desire in all three realms. Those seeking birth are those with craving — because of seeking birth in the triple realm.

body.text: sthitaya iti. avasthāpanāya. anugrahāyeti. punarbhavāya saṃbhavāyety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'For stability' — meaning: for sustaining. 'For support' — meaning: for renewed existence, for [re]birth.

body.text: sarve 'py ubhayatheti. sarve 'pi catvāra āhārāḥ. bhūtānāṃ sattvānāṃ sthitaye 'nugrahāya ca. tathā saṃbhavaiṣiṇām iti. yuktaṃ tāvan manaḥsaṃcetanā karmasvabhāvatvāt. tatprabhāvitaṃ ca vijñānaṃ bījaṃ. sparśo 'pi tatsaṃprayukto bhavaty anugrahāyeti. kavaḍīkāras tu kathaṃ saṃbhavaiṣinām anugrahāyeti. ata ucyate. kavaḍīkāro 'pi hīti vistaraḥ. tadrāgiṇām iti. kavaḍīkārarāgiṇāṃ. punarbhavāya saṃvartata iti asya jñāpanārtham idaṃ sūtrapadam upanyasyate. uktaṃ hi bhagavateti vistaraḥ. tatra rogādibhiḥ paṃca upādānaskaṃdhā uktāḥ. tasya rogasya catvāra āhārā mūlaṃ. mūlaṃ ca hetur iti anena kavaḍīkāro 'pi tadrāgiṇāṃ punarbhavāya saṃvartata iti siddhaṃ. anye punar jarāmaraṇasya pratyaya ity etad evodāharaṇaṃ bruvate. asmāj janmanaḥ pareṇa jarāmaraṇaṃ vyavasthāpitam ity abhiprāyaḥ. kavaḍīkāro 'pi bhūtānāṃ sattvānām ihasthitaya iti yuktaṃ pratyakṣatvāt. [Tib. 308b] tathā sukhavedanīyaḥ sparśo vijñānaṃ cānugrāhakam ity uktaṃ. atha manaḥsaṃcetanā katham iti. ata idam ucyate. manaḥsaṃcetanāpi ceti vistaraḥ. ata eva manaḥsaṃcetanāgrahaṇena sparśavijñāne api gṛhīte bhavataḥ. tatsaṃprayogitvāt. pradrutā iti prasṛtāḥ. saṃgītiparyāya ity abhidharmaśāstre.
body.translated_text: 'All in both ways' — all four nutriments (<s>āhāra</s>) [serve] for the maintenance and benefit of existing beings, and likewise for those seeking rebirth. Mental volition (<s>manaḥsaṃcetanā</s>) is fitting, since it has the nature of action (<s>karma</s>). And consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), empowered by that, is the seed. Contact (<s>sparśa</s>) too, being associated with that, [serves] for benefit. But how does morsel-food (<s>kavaḍīkāra</s>) serve for the benefit of those seeking rebirth? Therefore it is said: 'For morsel-food too indeed' — and so forth in detail. 'Of those attached to it' — of those attached to morsel-food. 'It conduces to renewed existence' — to indicate this, this sūtra passage is cited. 'For the Blessed One has said' — and so forth in detail. There, by [the terms] disease and the like, the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>) are described. The four nutriments are the root of that disease. And root means cause — by this it is established that morsel-food too conduces to renewed existence for those attached to it. Others, however, cite this very passage as an example of a condition for old-age-and-death, with the intent that old-age-and-death is established as subsequent to this birth. That morsel-food [serves] for the maintenance of existing beings here — this is fitting, being directly perceived. Similarly, it is stated that contact productive of pleasant feeling, and consciousness, are beneficial. But how does mental volition [serve thus]? Therefore this is stated: 'Mental volition too' — and so forth in detail. Therefore, by the inclusion of mental volition, contact and consciousness too are included, since they are associated with it. 'Engaged' (<s>pradrutā</s>) means active. '<s>Saṃgītiparyāya</s>' — in the <s>Abhidharma</s> treatise.

body.text: teṣāṃ puṣṭaye sparśa iti. sukhavedanīyenānugrahāt. yaḥ kaścid vedanāskaṃdhaḥ saṃjñāskaṃdhaḥ. sarvaḥ sa sparśaṃ pratītyeti vacanāt. manaḥsaṃcetanāyāḥ punarbhavasyākṣepa iti. tasyāḥ karmasvabhāvatvāt. kathaṃ ca punas tayā punarbhava ākṣipyate. tadutpattipratyayaparasparānukūlyāvasthānāt. karmaparibhāvitād vijñānabījād abhinirvṛttir iti. bījād ivāṃkurasya punarbhavasyotpāda ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Contact for their nourishment' — through the benefit of what is productive of pleasant feeling. Because of the statement: 'Whatever feeling-aggregate, whatever perception-aggregate — all that is dependent on contact.' Mental volition projects renewed existence — because it has the nature of action. And how does it project renewed existence? Through the state of mutual accord of the conditions for its production. From the consciousness-seed perfumed by action comes actualization — meaning the arising of renewed existence is like a sprout from a seed.

body.text: yaḥ kavaḍīkāraḥ sa āhāra iti praśne āha. syāt kavaḍīkāro nāhāraḥ. syād āhāro na kavaḍīkāraḥ. syād ubhayaṃ. syān nobhayam iti catuṣkoṭikaṃ. dvitīyā koṭis traya āhārā iti. manaḥsaṃcetanāsparśavijñānāni. caturthī etān ākārān sthāpayitveti. śabdo duḥkhavedanāsaṃprayuktāś ca sarve cittacaittāḥ. evaṃ sparśādibhir api yathāyogaṃ catuṣkoṭikāni kartavyānīti. yaḥ kaścit sparśaḥ. sarvaḥ sa āhāraḥ. syāt sparśo nāhāra iti catuṣkoṭikaṃ. evaṃ yā kācin manaḥsaṃcetanā. sarvā sā āhāraḥ. syāt manaḥsaṃcetanā nāhāra iti catuṣkoṭikaṃ. tathā [Tib. 309a] yat kiṃcid vijñānaṃ. sarvaṃ tad āhāraḥ. syād vijñānaṃ nāhāra iti catuṣkoṭikam. sparśasya tāvat prathamā koṭiḥ. yaṃ sparśaṃ pratītyendriyāṇām apacayo bhavati. mahābhūtānāṃ ca paribhedaḥ. dvitīyā traya āhārāḥ. tṛtīyā yaṃ sparśaṃ pratītya indriyāṇām upacayo bhavati. mahābhūtānāṃ ca vṛddhiḥ. caturthī etān ākārān sthāpayitveti. evaṃ yāvad vijñānaṃ catuṣkoṭikaṃ. prathamā koṭiḥ yad vijñānaṃ pratītyendriyāṇām apacayo bhavati mahābhūtānāṃ paribhedaḥ. dvitīyā koṭis traya āhārāḥ vijñānavarjyāḥ. tṛtīyā yad vijñānaṃ pratītya indriyāṇām upacayo bhavati. mahābhūtānāṃ ca vṛddhiḥ. caturthy etān akārān sthāpayitvā.
body.translated_text: To the question 'Is whatever is morsel-food a nutriment?', he says: there might be morsel-food that is not a nutriment; there might be a nutriment that is not morsel-food; there might be both; there might be neither — a fourfold schema (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>). The second alternative is the three nutriments — mental volition, contact, and consciousness. The fourth is 'setting aside these aspects' — [all] mind and mental factors associated with painful feeling, and sounds. Similarly, for contact and the rest, fourfold schemas should be made as appropriate. 'Whatever contact — is all of it a nutriment? Might there be contact that is not a nutriment?' — a fourfold schema. Similarly, 'whatever mental volition — is all of it a nutriment? Might there be mental volition that is not a nutriment?' — a fourfold schema. Likewise, 'whatever consciousness — is all of it a nutriment? Might there be consciousness that is not a nutriment?' — a fourfold schema. For contact, the first alternative: contact dependent on which there is decrease of the faculties and breaking up of the great elements. The second: the three [other] nutriments. The third: contact dependent on which there is increase of the faculties and growth of the great elements. The fourth: setting aside these aspects. Similarly up to the fourfold schema for consciousness: the first alternative — consciousness dependent on which there is decrease of the faculties and breaking up of the great elements; the second — the three nutriments excluding consciousness; the third — consciousness dependent on which there is increase of the faculties and growth of the great elements; the fourth — setting aside these aspects.

body.text: syāt sparśādīn pratītyeti vistareṇa aparaḥ praśnaḥ. sparśādīn iti sparśacetanāvijñānadharmān iti evaṃ netavyaṃ. evaṃ ca granthaḥ kartavyaḥ. syāt sparśādīn pratītyendrīyāṇām upacayo bhavati. mahābhūtānāṃ ca vṛddhiḥ. na ca te āhārāḥ. syāt. anyabhūmikān anāsravāṃś ca. pratītyety abhisaṃbaṃdhāt dvitīyāprayogaḥ. yo 'pi paribhukta iti vistaraḥ. kena saṃbandhenedam uktaṃ. anyabhūmikān anāsravāṃś ca pratītyānāhāra ity ukte 'rthād etad uktaṃ bhavati. svabhūmikān sāsravāṃ pratītya āhāra iti. yaṃ ceha paribhukta iti. kavaḍīkāro bhoktur bādhām ādadhāti. sa kim āhāraḥ. so 'py āhāraḥ. āpāte bhojanavelāyām anugrahāt.
body.translated_text: 'Might there be, dependent on contact and the rest' — and so forth in detail, another question. 'Contact and the rest' should be understood as the <s>dharmas</s> of contact, volition, and consciousness. And the text should be constructed thus: might there be, dependent on contact and the rest, increase of the faculties and growth of the great elements, yet they are not nutriments? There might — those of other grounds and outflow-free ones. Due to the connection with 'dependent,' the second formulation [is understood]. 'What has been consumed' — and so forth in detail. By what connection is this stated? When it is said that dependent on those of other grounds and outflow-free ones, [they are] not nutriments, it is implicitly stated that dependent on those of one's own ground and with outflows, [they are] nutriments. 'And what has been consumed here' — morsel-food inflicts harm on the eater. Is that a nutriment? It too is a nutriment — because of benefit at the outset, at the time of eating.

body.text: sarvāsu sarvaḥ. evaṃ yoniṣv iti. kāmadhātau [Tib. 309b] paṃcānāṃ gatīnāṃ catasṛṇāṃ ca yonīnāṃ sadbhāvāt. catuḥkoṭikaṃ bādhyate. prakaraṇagranthaś ceti. prathame catuṣkoṭike yeyaṃ tṛtīyā koṭiḥ. yaṃ kavaḍīkāraṃ pratītyendriyāṇām upacayo bhavati. mahābhūtānāṃ ca vṛddhir iti asyā bādhāc catuṣkoṭikaṃ bādhyate. na kevalam upacayakaraḥ. kiṃ tarhi. apacayakaro 'pi kavaḍīkārāhāra
body.translated_text: 'All in all destinies and births' — because in the Desire Realm, the five destinies and the four modes of birth all exist. The fourfold schema is challenged. 'And the <s>Prakaraṇa</s> text' — in the first fourfold schema, the third alternative — morsel-food dependent on which there is increase of the faculties and growth of the great elements — by challenging this, the fourfold schema is challenged. Not only does morsel-food promote growth; rather, morsel-food that causes decrease is also a nutriment.

body.text: iti. prakaraṇagranthaś ca kiṃ bādhyate. kīdṛśaḥ prakaraṇagrantha iti. tad darśayann āha. kavaḍīikārāhāraḥ katamaḥ yam kavaḍīkāraṃ pratītyendriyāṇām upacayo bhavati vistareṇa yāvad vijñānam iti. upacayāhārābhisaṃdhivacanād avirodha iti. upacayāhārābhiprāyeṇa catuṣkoṭikavacanaṃ prakaraṇagranthavacanaṃ ca. tasmāt. tayor avirodhaḥ. yo hy upacayāya. sa mukhyaḥ. āhāralakṣaṇaprāptatvād iti. kavaḍīkārāhāralakṣaṇaprāptatvāt. katham ity āha. so 'pi hi jighatsāṃ pipāsāṃ ca pratihantuṃ samartha iti. pradīptāyasaguḍalakṣaṇa āhāro jighatsāpratighāte samarthaḥ. kvathitatāmralakṣaṇaḥ pipāsāpratighāte iti yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: Thus. And what in the <s>Prakaraṇa</s> text is challenged? What kind of <s>Prakaraṇa</s> text? Showing that, he says: 'What is morsel-food nutriment? Morsel-food dependent on which there is increase of faculties' — and so forth in detail up to consciousness. 'There is no contradiction, because the statement refers to the growth-nutriment' — the statements of the fourfold schema and the <s>Prakaraṇa</s> text are made with the intention of the growth-nutriment. Therefore there is no contradiction between the two. For that which is for growth is primary, since it has attained the characteristic of the morsel-food nutriment. How? He says: 'For it too is capable of counteracting hunger and thirst.' A nutriment having the nature of burning-hot iron balls is capable of counteracting hunger; one having the nature of boiling copper [is capable of counteracting] thirst — this is to be understood.

body.text: kavaḍīkārāhāraprasaṃgenedam ucyate. uktaṃ bhagavatā yaś ca bāhyakānām iti vistaraḥ. jaṃbudvīpo jambuṣaṇḍaḥ. tathā hy uktaṃ bhagavatā. yāḥ kāścij jambuṣaṇḍāt sravaṃtyaḥ. sarvāḥ samudranimnāḥ samudrapravaṇāḥ samudraprāgbhārā iti. tannivāsino jambuṣaṇḍagatāḥ. kukṣimanto bhojanaśaktyupetā akalalādyavasthā ity abhiprāyaḥ. tad etad ayuktam. ekam iti vacanād iti. yadi jaṃbūdvīpanivāsinaḥ kukṣimanto jaṃbuṣaṇḍagatā [Tib. 310a] iśyeran. yaś ca jambuṣaṇḍagatān pṛthagjanān iti vaktavyaṃ syāt. uktaṃ ca yaś caikaṃ jaṃbuṣaṇḍagatam iti. tasmād ayam artho na ghaṭate. kaś cātra viśeṣa iti. kim atrāścaryaṃ yad bahūṃ bhojayitvā bahu puṇyaṃ syāt. na tv alpīyasaḥ śatamātrān vītarāgān ity arthaḥ. saṃnikṛṣto bodhisattva iti. āsannābhisambodhiḥ.
body.translated_text: In connection with morsel-food nutriment, this is said. 'The Blessed One stated: and among the outsiders' — and so forth in detail. <s>Jambudvīpa</s> is <s>Jambuṣaṇḍa</s> (the Rose-Apple Grove). For thus the Blessed One stated: 'Whatever [rivers] flow from the Rose-Apple Grove — all flow toward the ocean, tend toward the ocean, incline toward the ocean.' Those dwelling there, situated in the Rose-Apple Grove — the intent is those with bellies, endowed with the capacity for eating, in the <s>kalala</s> (embryonic) and subsequent stages. But this is not correct — because of the statement 'one.' If those dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, having bellies, situated in the Rose-Apple Grove, were accepted, it should be said 'one who [feeds] ordinary persons situated in the Rose-Apple Grove.' And it is stated 'one who [feeds] one person situated in the Rose-Apple Grove.' Therefore this meaning does not hold. 'And what distinction is there here?' — what is remarkable about acquiring much merit by feeding many? But not by [feeding] fewer — merely a hundred who are free from attachment, is the meaning. 'A <s>bodhisattva</s> near [enlightenment]' — near to full awakening.

children.translated_text: 'From when is there a <s>bodhisattva</s>? From when one performs the actions [that create the] marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>)' —

body.text: ity abhiprāyaḥ. na tv iyam anvarthā saṃjñeti. nārthānugatā. nārthavācakaṃ padam ity arthaḥ. nāpi paribhāṣitā artham anapekṣya. bodhisattva eva tv eṣa jaṃbuṣaṇḍagata iti. kṛṣigrāmakaṃ vyavalokanāya nirgataḥ sarvārthasiddho bodhisattvo jaṃbūvṛkṣamūle niṣaṇṇaḥ prathamaṃ dhyānam utpāditavān. ata āha. sa hi pṛthagjanaḥ kāmavairāgyasambandheneti. sa cāpi hi bodhisattvaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ kāmavītarāgaś ca. bāhyakāś ca tathaiva kāmavītarāgāḥ pṛthagjanāś ca. anena sambandhena tebhyo bāhyakebhyo bahutareṇa dānaphalena viśiṣyamāṇa ity evam uktaḥ. sa tebhyo bāhyakebhyo 'nantebhyo viśiṣyamāṇo
body.translated_text: this is the intent. 'But this is not a meaningful designation' — not following the meaning; meaning the word does not convey the meaning. 'Nor is it a conventional designation regardless of meaning.' 'But this very one is the <s>bodhisattva</s> situated in the Rose-Apple Grove' — <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having gone out to observe the farming village, sat at the base of a <s>jambu</s> tree and generated the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Therefore he says: 'For he, an ordinary person, through the connection of freedom from desire in the Desire Realm.' That <s>bodhisattva</s> too is an ordinary person and free from desire in <s>Kāma</s>. And the outsiders are likewise free from desire in <s>Kāma</s> and ordinary persons. Through this connection, he is said to be distinguished from those outsiders by greater fruit of giving. He, being distinguished from those innumerable outsiders —

children.translated_text: 'And the gift to a <s>bodhisattva</s> is immeasurable, even [compared to gifts] to non-noble ones' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. śatagrahaṇaṃ tu pūrvādhikārād iti. tatraiva sūtre śatādhikāro 'dhikṛtaḥ. yaś ca tiryagyonigatānāṃ śatāya dānaṃ dadyāt. yaś caikasmai duḥśīlāya manuṣyabhūtāya [Tib. 310b] dānaṃ dadyāt. tataḥ śataguṇo vipākaḥ
body.translated_text: because of this statement. 'But the mention of a hundred is from the previous context' — in that very sūtra, the context of a hundred was the topic. 'One who would give a gift to a hundred beings born in the animal realm; and one who would give a gift to a single immoral human being — from that, a hundredfold maturation is to be expected.'

body.text: pratikāṃkṣitavyaḥ. yāvad yaś ca bāhyakānām iti vistaraḥ. itthaṃ caitad evam iti. itthaṃ caitad evaṃ bodhisattva eva tv eṣa jambuṣaṇḍe niṣaṇṇo yujyata iti. yad enaṃ bodhisattvam apāsya. bāhyakebhya eva srotaāpattiphalapratipannakaṃ viśeṣayāṃ babhūveti. bāhyakebhyo vītarāgebhyaḥ srotaāpattiphalapratipannakāya dānam aprameyataraṃ. srotaāpannāya tato 'prameyataraṃ. sakṛdāgāmiphalapratipannakāyeti vistaraḥ. yadi nirvedhabhāgī jaṃbuṣaṇḍagato 'bhaviṣyat. jaṃbuṣaṇḍagatād eva vyaśeṣayiṣyat. kathaṃ. yaś ca jaṃbuṣaṇḍagatānāṃ śataṃ bhojayet. yaś caikaṃ srotaāpattiphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratipannakaṃ. ato dānād idaṃ mahāphalataram iti. na tv evaṃ. srotaāpattiphalapratipannakādibhyo viśiṣṭataratvād ato bodhisattva eva tv eṣa jaṃbuṣaṇḍagato yujyate.
body.translated_text: 'Up to: and among the outsiders' — and so forth in detail. 'This is thus, this is so' — this is thus, this is so: this very one, the <s>bodhisattva</s> sitting in the Rose-Apple Grove, is fitting. That, having set aside this <s>bodhisattva</s>, [the sūtra] made the one practicing for the fruit of stream-entry superior to the outsiders. A gift to one practicing for the fruit of stream-entry is more immeasurable than to outsiders free from attachment. To a stream-enterer, even more immeasurable than that. To one practicing for the fruit of once-returning — and so forth in detail. If one in the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (penetration) stage had been the one in the Rose-Apple Grove, he would have been distinguished from the one in the Rose-Apple Grove itself: 'one who feeds a hundred of those in the Rose-Apple Grove; and one who [feeds] a single person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry — this latter gift bears greater fruit.' But this is not so. Since [the bodhisattva] is more distinguished than those practicing for stream-entry and so on, therefore this very <s>bodhisattva</s> alone is fitting as the one in the Rose-Apple Grove.

body.text: (III.42-44ab) āyuḥkṣayādibhir iti. asty āyuḥkṣayān maraṇaṃ na puṇyakṣayāt. asti puṇyakṣayān nāyuḥkṣayād ityādi.
body.translated_text: (III.42-44ab) 'Through exhaustion of lifespan and so on' — there is death through exhaustion of lifespan but not through exhaustion of merit; there is [death] through exhaustion of merit but not through exhaustion of lifespan — and so on.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. kuśalamūlasamucchedo mithyādṛṣṭyā. sā ca mānasy eva. saṃtīrakatvāt. kuśalamūlapratisaṃdhānaṃ samyagdṛṣṭyā vicikitsayā vā. te ca mānasyau. dhātubhūmivairāgyaṃ dhātuto bhūmito vā [Tib. 311a] vairāgyaṃ manovijñāna eva. samāhita eva citte labhyatvāt. parihāṇir ayoniśomanasikārapravartitā. manovijñānena cāyoniśomanasikāro vikalpa iti. cyutiḥ saṃkṣiptapaṃcendriyapracārasya pravāhacchedānukūle vijñāne bhavati. upapattir api viparyastamater bhavatīti manovijñāna eva yujyate. antarābhavapratisaṃdhir apy uktarūpa iti. pratisaṃdhisāmānyād anukto 'py uktakalpa iti nocyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. cyutir eva
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. The cutting off of wholesome roots is through wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), which is only mental (<s>mānasa</s>), since it involves deliberation. The reconnection of wholesome roots is through right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) or through doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), both of which are mental. Dispassion from realms and grounds — dispassion from a realm or a ground — occurs only in mind-consciousness, since it is obtained only in a concentrated mind. Loss (<s>parihāṇi</s>) is set in motion by improper attention (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>), and improper attention is conceptualization through mind-consciousness. Death (<s>cyuti</s>) occurs in the consciousness favorable to cutting off the stream of the contracted five-sense activity. Rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>) too occurs for one of inverted mind, so it is fitting only for mind-consciousness. 'The rebirth-linking in the intermediate existence is also of the stated type' — since it is of the general class of rebirth-linking, even though not separately stated, it is considered as if stated — this is the intent. Death (<s>cyuti</s>) itself is —

body.text: ekārthatāṃ darśayati. bhāve ktotpannatvāt. itare hi vadane paṭvyāv iti sukhaduḥkhe.
body.translated_text: He shows the identity of meaning. Because the <s>kta</s> [suffix] arises in the sense of state (<s>bhāva</s>). For the other [terms] — 'happiness and suffering are to be spoken' — [they take different forms] in expression.

body.text: visabhāgabhūmikatvād iti. samāhitaṃ cittaṃ samāhitabhūmikatvāt visabhāgaṃ kāmadhātoḥ. ataś cyuticittam upapatticittam vā na yujyate. yadā tarhi rūpadhātāv eva mriyate upapadyate vā. tadā samāhitabhūmikaṃ cittaṃ tad bhaviṣyatīty ata āha. ābhisaṃskārikatvād iti. abhisaṃskāro yatnaḥ. abhisaṃskāreṇa nirvṛttam ābhisaṃskārikaṃ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. na tad ābhisaṃskārikaṃ cyuticittam upapatticittaṃ vā yujyate. maraṇāvasthāyā apaṭutvāt. anugrāhakatvāc ca. yasmāc ca samāhitaṃ cittam auugrāhakaṃ. na cchedānukūlaṃ. ato 'pi samāhitacittasya cyutir nāsti. nāpy acittakasyeti vistaraḥ. nāpy acittakasya. [Tib. 311b] kiṃ. cyutiḥ. upapattir veti prakṛtaṃ. acittako nirodhasamāpattisamāpanno
body.translated_text: Because of belonging to a dissimilar ground — concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>) mind, because of belonging to the ground of concentration, is dissimilar to the Desire Realm. Therefore it is not fitting as a death-consciousness (<s>cyuticitta</s>) or a rebirth-consciousness (<s>upapatticittam</s>). But when one dies or is reborn in the Form Realm itself, then that mind would belong to the ground of concentration — therefore he says: because of being volitionally produced (<s>ābhisaṃskārikatva</s>). <s>Abhisaṃskāra</s> means effort. That which is produced by effort is volitionally produced. Its nature [is such]. Therefore, that volitionally produced [mind] is not fitting as a death-consciousness or rebirth-consciousness — because of the incapacity at the time of dying. And because of being supportive — since concentrated mind is supportive, it is not conducive to cutting off [the life-stream]. For this reason too, there is no death for one with concentrated mind. 'Nor for one without mind' — and so forth in detail. Nor for one without mind. What? Death or rebirth — this is the topic. One without mind is one who has attained the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>)

body.text: 'saṃjñisamāpattisamāpannaḥ tadvipāke vāvasthitaḥ. so 'cittaka upakrantuṃ mārayituṃ na śakyate śastrādibhiḥ. ato nācittakasyāsti cyutiḥ. yadā cāsyāśrayo vipariṇantum ārabheteti. śastreṇāgninā vopakramān nirodhasamāpattiṃ asaṃjñisamāpattiṃ vā samāpannasya asaṃjñisamāpatter vipāke sthitasya vipākāvedhaparisamāpter avaśyam asya tadānīm āśrayapratibaddhaṃ cittaṃ āśraye bījabhāvenāsti. tat sammukhībhūya paścāt pracyaveta. kaḥ pracyaveta. pudgalaḥ. yadi pudgalo 'dhikriyet. asamānakartṛkatvāt ktvāvidhir na prāpnoti. cittaṃ tarhi pracyaveta. atha vaivam abhisaṃbandhaḥ. yadā cāśrayo vipariṇaṃtum anyathātvam āpattum ārabheta. avaśyam asya pudgalasya tadāśrayapratibaddhaṃ bījabhāvenāvasthitaṃ cittaṃ sammukhībhūya samudācarya pariṇantum ārabheta. paścāt pracyaveta pudgala iti. atha vā saṃmukhībhūyeti saṃmukhībhāvyety arthe ṇilopāt.
body.translated_text: or one who has attained the non-perception attainment (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>), or one who is established in the fruition thereof. Such a mindless one cannot be assaulted or killed by weapons and the like. Therefore there is no death for one without mind. 'And when his physical basis begins to deteriorate' — whether from assault by weapons or fire, for one who has attained the cessation attainment or the non-perception attainment, or for one established in the fruition of non-perception attainment, upon the completion of the fruition's duration, there must necessarily at that time be mind bound to the physical basis, existing in the basis in seed form. That [mind], having become manifest, would then pass away. Who would pass away? The person (<s>pudgala</s>). If the person is the subject, the <s>ktvā</s>-construction does not apply because the agents are not identical. Then the mind would pass away. Or alternatively, the connection is thus: when the physical basis begins to deteriorate, to undergo change, necessarily this person's mind, which is bound to that basis and exists in seed form, having become manifest and having arisen, would begin to change. Afterward the person would pass away. Or alternatively, 'having become manifest' (<s>saṃmukhībhūya</s>) is [used] in the sense of 'being made manifest' (<s>saṃmukhībhāvya</s>), by the elision of the causative suffix.

children.translated_text: There is a wind that makes leaves grow, there is another that dries leaves —

body.text: iti yathā. upapattau cāyuktaṃ acittakatvaṃ. kasmāt. cittacchedahetvabhāvāt. avaśyaṃ kliṣṭatayā pratisaṃdhicittasya nirodhasamāpattyādyasaṃbhavāt. vinā ca kleśenānupapatteḥ. sarvakleśair hi tadbhūmikair upapattipratisaṃdhibandho bhavati. na ca cittam antareṇa kleśāḥ kadācid api bhavantīti. ato 'pi nāsti acittakasyopattih.
body.translated_text: just so. And it is not fitting to be mindless at the time of rebirth. Why? Because of the absence of a cause for the cutting off of mind. Since the rebirth-linking consciousness is necessarily afflicted (<s>kliṣṭa</s>), the cessation attainment and the like are impossible [at that moment]. And because without an affliction there is no rebirth. For the rebirth-linking bond of existence occurs through all afflictions belonging to that ground. And afflictions never exist without mind. Therefore, for this reason too, there is no rebirth for one without mind.

body.text: maraṇabhavas triprakāra ity uktam iti.
body.translated_text: It has been stated that death-existence is of three kinds.

children.translated_text: 'Rebirth-existence is afflicted, through all afflictions belonging to one's own ground' —

body.text: iti. upapattibhava eva [Tib. 312a] kliṣṭa ity avadhāraṇāt. maraṇapūrvāṃtakālāntarābhavās triprakārāḥ kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtā uktāḥ. atha vā
body.translated_text: thus. Because of the restriction that rebirth-existence alone is afflicted. Death, the period preceding it, and the intermediate existence have been stated as of three kinds — wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. Or alternatively,

children.text:
nirodhayaty uparamann ārūpye jīvitaṃ manaḥ
upekṣāṃ ceti
children.translated_text: 'In the Formless [Realm], mind, delighting in cessation, terminates the lifespan and equanimity' —

body.text: vistareṇa yāvac
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail, up to

body.text: uktaṃ. ato maraṇabhavas triprakāra ity utsargaḥ. arhaṃs tu
body.translated_text: this has been stated. Therefore, the general rule is that death-existence is of three kinds. But for an <s>Arhat</s>,

children.translated_text: '[He] attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the pair of indeterminate [states]' —

body.text: ity evam apavādaḥ. asti cet kāmadhātau vipāka upekṣeti.
body.translated_text: thus is the exception. If there exists in the Desire Realm a resultant equanimity [feeling] —

children.translated_text: 'Some [hold that] below too there is the intermediate [feeling]' —

body.text: iti ekīyamatena. nāsti ced iti.
body.translated_text: thus, according to the view of some. If it does not exist —

children.translated_text: 'Beyond that, what is to be experienced is neither-suffering-nor-pleasure' —

body.text: ity aparamatena. airyāpathika eveti. airyāpathikajātīyaṃ tad yatra nirvāti.
body.translated_text: thus, according to another view. It is only of the deportment type (<s>airyāpathika</s>) — that in which [the <s>Arhat</s>] attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> belongs to the class of deportment [consciousness].

children.translated_text: 'Resultant, deportment, craft-based, and magically created — the indeterminate in <s>Kāma</s> is fourfold' —

body.text: iti. na etāvad evāvyākṛtam iṣyata iti vyākhyātam etat. tad dhi cittacchedānukūlam iti. apratisaṃdhikacittacchedānukūlaṃ. durbalatvāt. paramāpaṭutvād ity arthaḥ. sapratisaṃdhikacittacchede kuśalākuśalam api cittaṃ saṃbhavati.
body.translated_text: thus. Not only this much is accepted as indeterminate — this has been explained. For that is conducive to the cutting off of mind — [meaning] conducive to the cutting off of mind without rebirth-linking. Because of weakness — the meaning is: because of extreme incapacity. But in the cutting off of mind with rebirth-linking, even wholesome or unwholesome mind is possible.

body.text: teṣāṃ yathāsaṃkhyam iti. pādayor apāyagāmināṃ vijñānaṃ saṃnirudhyate. nābhyāṃ manuṣyagāmināṃ. hṛdaye devagāmināṃ. arūpitvād adeśasthaṃ vijñānaṃ kathaṃ teṣu nirudhyata iti. ata āha. kāyendriyasya teṣu nirodhād iti. teṣu pādādiṣu kāyendriyapratibaddhavṛtti hi kāmadhātau rūpadhātau ca vijñānam iti. [Tib. 312b] teṣām api hṛdaye vijñānaṃ nirudhyata iti. yathāsaṃkhyanirdeśād evāyam artho labhyate. kathaṃ. hṛdayaṃ ca hṛdayaṃ ca hṛdaye. pādaś ca nābhiś ca hṛdaye ceti
body.translated_text: 'Of those, respectively' — consciousness ceases in the feet of those going to the lower realms; at the navel of those going to the human realm; at the heart of those going to the divine realm. Since [formless beings] are without form, how does consciousness, being not located in any place, cease in them? Therefore he says: because of the cessation of the body-faculty in those [locations]. In those [locations] — feet and the rest — consciousness operates bound to the body-faculty in the Desire and Form Realms. For them too, consciousness ceases at the heart — this meaning is obtained from the statement of respective correlation. How? Heart and heart — [means] at the heart. Feet and navel and heart — thus

body.text: catvāro 'rthāḥ. adhogaś ca nṛgaś ca suragaś ca ajagaś cety eto 'pi catvāro 'rthāḥ. tena yathāsaṃkhyasiddhiḥ.
body.translated_text: four meanings. Going below, going to humans, going to gods, and going to the formless — these too are four meanings. Thus the respective correlation is established.

body.text: prāyeṇeti grahaṇam devādīnāṃ sukhamṛtyutvāt. na tu punas tāni kāṣṭhānīva cchidyante. kiṃ tarhīti. tīvrābhir vedanābhiś chidyanta iveti. chinnavad vā na punaś ceṣṭanta iti chinnānīty ucyaṃte iti. chinnāṃgapratyaṃgavat na punaś ceṣṭaṃta iti chinnānīty ucyante. saiṣā kālpanikī chedavṛttiḥ. marmaṇāṃ dvidhābhāvakaraṇāt. aptejovāyunāṃ anyatamenety ukte pṛcchati. kasmāt na pṛthivīdhātuneti. aptejovāyudhātupradhānā yathāyogam iti. yathāsaṃbhavaṃ abdhātupradhānaḥ śleṣmā. tejodhātupradhānaṃ pittaṃ. vāyudhātupradhāno vāyuśeṣa iti. bhājanalokasaṃvratanīsādharmyeṇety apara iti. tisro bhājanasaṃvartanyaḥ tejaḥsaṃvartanī apsaṃvartanī vāyusaṃvartanī ca. tāsāṃ ca sādharmyeṇa aptejovāyudhātūnām anyatameneti vistareṇoktam iti.
body.translated_text: 'Generally' — this qualification is because gods and the rest have a pleasant death. But those [vital points] are not cut like pieces of wood. What then? They are as if cut by intense feelings. Or they are called 'cut' because, like those with severed limbs and minor limbs, they no longer move. This cutting is figurative — because it involves making the vital points twofold. When it is said 'by one of water, fire, or wind element,' he asks: why not the earth element? 'Predominated by water, fire, and wind elements respectively' — as appropriate: phlegm is predominated by the water element; bile is predominated by the fire element; the remaining wind is predominated by the wind element. 'By analogy with the dissolution of the vessel-world, according to others' — there are three dissolutions of the vessel-world: dissolution by fire, dissolution by water, and dissolution by wind. And by analogy with those, by one of water, fire, or wind elements — this has been stated in detail.

body.text: (III.44cd) katham ārād yātā. ātyantikavisaṃyogaprāptilābhāt. pṛthagjanānāṃ tv asti visaṃyogaprāptilābhaḥ. na tv ātyaṃtika iti te na ārād yātā eveti. te hi mithyātve 'pi niyatā bhaveyur iti. yady ānantaryāṇi kuryur ity arthaḥ. na ca ta iti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 313a] na ca te mokṣabhāgīyalābhinaḥ kālaniyamena samyaktve niyatāḥ. yathā saptakṛtvaḥparamādayaḥ. ādiśabdena kulaṃkulaikavīcikādayo gṛhyante. kālaniyamaś caiṣāṃ pudgalanirdeśe vakṣyate. niyatebhyo dvayebhya ebhyo 'nye 'niyatāḥ. pratyayāpekṣaṃ hīti vistaraḥ. yadi samyaktve pratyayaṃ labhante. samyaktve niyatāḥ. atha mithyātve. mithyātve niyatāḥ. athobhayasmiṃ na pratyayaṃ labhante. anubhayabhāktve 'pi.
body.translated_text: (III.44cd) How have they gone far? Through obtaining the attainment of ultimate separation (<s>ātyantikavissaṃyoga</s>). But ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) do obtain the attainment of separation, yet it is not ultimate — therefore they have not truly gone far. For they could become fixed in wrongness — the meaning is: if they were to commit the heinous acts (<s>ānantarya</s>). 'But not those' — and so forth in detail. But those who have obtained the aids to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>) are not fixed in rightness with a time-limit — like those who are at most seven-times-reborn (<s>saptakṛtvaḥparama</s>) and the rest. By the word 'and the rest,' clan-to-clan (<s>kulaṃkula</s>), one-seeder (<s>ekavīcika</s>), and the rest are grasped. And the time-limit for these will be stated in the exposition of persons (<s>pudgalanirdeśa</s>). Those other than these two fixed groups are undetermined. 'For it depends on conditions' — and so forth in detail. If they obtain conditions for rightness, they become fixed in rightness. If for wrongness, fixed in wrongness. If they obtain conditions for neither, then [they remain] in neither category.

body.text: (III.45-47) uktaḥ sattvalokaḥ avidyādikramanirdeśena.
body.translated_text: (III.45-47) The world of beings has been explained through the exposition of the sequence beginning with ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>).

body.text: icchantīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: means 'they desire.'

children.translated_text: 'The wind-circle (<s>vāyumaṇḍala</s>), sixteen hundred thousand [<s>yojana</s>s] in depth, immeasurable [in circumference]' —

body.text: lakṣaṣoḍaśakaṃ vedhanabhāvana. pariṇāhenāsaṃkhyam iti. samantaparikṣepeṇāsaṃkhyam ity arthaḥ. karmādhipatyena karmasāmarthyena. tatra nidarśanaṃ. yathā bhuktaṃ pītaṃ cānnaṃ ca yathāsaṃkhyena nāpakvaṃ pakvāśayaṃ patati. pakvam eva pakvasthānaṃ gacchatīty arthaḥ. kusūlanyāyena koṣṭhanyāyena. samantāt prākāravad āsthitam ity arthaḥ. pakvakṣīraśarībhāvayogena pakvakṣīraśarībhāvanyāyena. yathā pakvasya kṣīrasya śarī. strīliṃganirdeśaḥ śara ity arthaḥ. atha vā śarasya bhāvaḥ śarībhāvaḥ strīprayogaḥ. yathāsau śaro ghanībhāvena bhavati. evaṃ jalasyopariṣṭhāt kāṃcanamayī bhūmir iti. śeṣaṃ trayo lakṣāḥ sahasrāṇi ca viṃśatir iti. viṃśatisahasrottarāṇām ekādaśānāṃ lakṣāṇām aṣṭāv apanīya etāvac cheṣaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: sixteen hundred thousand in depth. Immeasurable in circumference — meaning immeasurable in the surrounding perimeter. Through the dominion of <s>karma</s>, through the power of <s>karma</s>. An illustration therein: just as food that has been eaten and drunk does not fall undigested into the stomach (<s>pakvāśaya</s>) — only the digested goes to the place of digestion, this is the meaning. By the method of a granary, by the method of a storehouse — meaning: standing like a surrounding wall. By the method of the solidification of boiled milk — by the method of the skin-formation (<s>śarī</s>) of boiled milk. The word is in feminine gender — meaning <s>śara</s> (skin/crust). Or alternatively, the state of <s>śara</s> is <s>śarībhāva</s>, a feminine usage. Just as that crust forms through solidification — similarly, above the water, there is a golden earth. As for the remainder — three hundred thousand and twenty — subtracting eight from eleven hundred thousand plus twenty thousand, this much remains.

body.text: vistaraḥ. caturdvīpakasya etat parimāṇam ucyate. na trisāhasramahāsāhasrasya. samānaṃ hy etad ubhayam. etad iti. jalakāṃcanamaṇḍalaṃ.
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. This measurement is stated for the four-continent [world-system], not for the three-thousandfold great-thousandfold [world-system]. For both are the same — this [refers to] the water and gold circles.

body.text: Tib. 313b
body.translated_text: Tib. 313b

body.text: samantatas tu triguṇam
body.translated_text: 'But threefold all around' —

body.text: iti. samantaparikṣepeṇa triguṇam etad ubhayaṃ. sarvasya parimaṇḍalasyeyaṃ sthitiḥ. yad asya tiryakpramāṇasya triguṇam eva samantaparikṣiptasya pramāṇam iti.
body.translated_text: thus. This, both [the water and gold circles], is threefold in surrounding perimeter. This is the measure of every circular [formation]: its circumference is exactly three times its lateral dimension.

body.text: (48-51) tena caturdvīpakaś cakrīkṛta iti. cakraṃ kṛtaś cakrīkṛtaḥ. cakrākāratāṃ gamitaḥ. ata eva cakravāḍa ity ucyate.
body.translated_text: (48-51) By that, the four-continent [world] is made into a wheel (<s>cakrīkṛta</s>) — made into a wheel means given the form of a wheel. For this very reason it is called <s>Cakravāḍa</s>.

body.text: iti ayomayoḥ. yathāsaṃkhyaṃ caturṣu pārśveṣv iti. uttarakurupārśvasuvarṇamayaṃ pūrvavidehapārśvaṃ rūpyamayaṃ. jaṃbūdvipapārśvaṃ vaiḍūrya mayaṃ. avaragodānīpārśvaṃ sphaṭikamayaṃ.
body.translated_text: means made of iron. 'Respectively on the four sides' — the side facing <s>Uttarakuru</s> is made of gold; the side facing <s>Pūrvavideha</s> is made of silver; the side facing <s>Jambudvīpa</s> is made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli); the side facing <s>Avaragodānīya</s> is made of crystal.

body.text: nānāvidhabījagarbhāḥ. nānāprakārasāmarthyayuktāḥ. bahuvidhaprabhāvabhinnair vāyubhir iti. tadutpādane 'nekaprakārasāmarthyabhinnair vāyubhir ity arthaḥ. asamādhāneneti. ayugapadbhāvenety arthaḥ. na hi yadā kāryaṃ. tadā kāraṇaṃ tiṣṭhati. na hi avasthitasya dravyasyeti. rūparasādyātmakasya. dharmāntaranivṛttāv iti. kṣīranivṛttau. dharmāntaraprādurbhāva iti. dadhijanma. sa eva dharmī. neti. rūpādyātmakakṣīrādidharmebhyo 'nyo dharma utpādavyaye 'py anutpanno 'vinaṣṭaḥ. pariṇāma iti. kṣīranivṛttau dadhibhāvaḥ. tad eva cedam iti. kṣīram eva dadhi. na cedaṃ tatheti. na
body.translated_text: 'Containing seeds of various kinds' — endowed with powers of various kinds. 'By winds differentiated by manifold potencies' — by winds differentiated by manifold potencies for the production of that — this is the meaning. 'Not simultaneously' (<s>asamādhānena</s>) — meaning: not at the same time. For when the effect [exists], the cause does not persist at that time. 'For of an entity that persists' — of one having the nature of visible form, taste, and the rest. 'Upon the cessation of one entity' (<s>dharmāntaranivṛttau</s>) — upon the cessation of milk. 'The arising of another entity' (<s>dharmāntaraprādurbhāva</s>) — the birth of yogurt. That very same substance — no. A <s>dharma</s> other than the <s>dharma</s>s having the nature of form, taste, and the rest of milk — [a <s>dharma</s> that is] unarisen and unperished even in arising and perishing — this is transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>). Upon the cessation of milk, there is the state of yogurt. 'And this is indeed that' — milk is indeed yogurt. 'And this is not so' —
