body.text: cedaṃ dadhi kṣīram. tad evedam iti. yat pariṇāmenety uktaṃ. na cedaṃ tatheti. tasyaiva dravyasyānyathībhāvamātraṃ pariṇāma iti vacanāt. apūrvaiṣā vāco yuktir iti. svavacanaviruddhety abhiprāyaḥ. pūrvottarayor hi kṣaṇayor anyathātvam iṣyate. yayoś cānyathātvaṃ tayor anyatvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ. tadyathā devadattayajñadattayoḥ. tasmāt kāryakāraṇayor anyatvena bhavitavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: and this yogurt is not milk. 'This is indeed that' — as was stated 'by transformation.' 'And this is not so' — because of the statement: transformation is merely the becoming-otherwise of that very substance. 'This is an unprecedented logical construction' — the intent is: it contradicts itself. For between the earlier and later moments, difference is accepted. And where there is difference, there is seen to be distinctness — just as between <s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Yajñadatta</s>. Therefore, between cause and effect there must be distinctness.

body.text: suvarṇādaya iti. suvarṇarūpyamaṇimṛdādayaḥ. ṣaṣṭiyojanaśatasahasrasamucchrāya iti. ṣaṣṭyadhiko yojanalakṣa ucchrāya ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Gold and the rest' — gold, silver, gems, clay, and the rest. 'A height of sixty hundred thousand <s>yojana</s>s' — the meaning is: a height of one hundred thousand <s>yojana</s>s plus sixty.

body.text: (52, 53) aṣṭāṃgopetasyeti.
body.translated_text: (52, 53) 'Endowed with eight qualities' —

children.text:
śītalācchalaghusvādumṛduniḥpūtigaṃdhikaṃ [Tib. 314a]
pītaṃ na bādhate kukṣiṃ na kaṇṭhaṃ kṣiṇoti taj jalam
children.translated_text: 'Cool, clear, light, sweet, soft, pure in odor — when drunk, it does not harm the stomach nor irritate the throat — such is that water' —

body.text: iti aṣṭāṃgasaṃgrahaślokaḥ. pārśvatas tu triguṇo bhavati yugaṃdharatīreṇa gaṇyamāna iti. sa ābhyaṃtaraḥ samudro yugaṃdharapārśvenāyāṃataḥ saṃkhyāyamānas triguṇa iti kṛtvā. catvāriṃśadyojanasahasrādhikalakṣadvayam āyāmo bhavati yugaṃdharapārśve. aśītir ekā tadubhayataś cetarayor diśos tatsīmānadīvaipulyayogena apare dve aśītīti tisro 'śītayaḥ. catvāriṃśadadhikaṃ lakṣadvayaṃ bhavatīti.
body.translated_text: this is the verse summarizing the eight qualities. 'But on its side, it is threefold, measured by the shore of <s>Yugaṃdhara</s>' — that inner ocean, measured by the side of <s>Yugaṃdhara</s>, being threefold — therefore: the length on the side of <s>Yugaṃdhara</s> is two hundred thousand plus forty thousand <s>yojana</s>s. Eighty-one [times] on both sides in the other two directions, with the addition of the width of its boundary rivers, the other two [give] eighty-one — [thus] three eighty-ones. It becomes two hundred thousand plus forty [thousand].

children.translated_text: Three hundred thousand and twenty-two thousand.

body.text: nimindharagiricakravāḍayor aṃtare ekasyāṃ diśi bāhyasya samudrasya tatparimāṇam uktaṃ. atra sahasram ekaṃ dve śate cānye ardhāṣṭāśītir eveti vaktavyaṃ. nyūnatvāt. evam aparasyām diśi vaktavyam. evaṃ dvayoḥ sahasrayoḥ paṃcasu śateṣu paṃcasaptatau ca yojanānāṃ prakṣipteṣu sa ādhāraḥ pūrito bhavati. ya uktaḥ
body.translated_text: Between Nimindhara mountain and Cakravāḍa, the measurement of the outer ocean in one direction has been stated. Here it should be said: one thousand, two hundred, and half of eighty-eight — because of the deficit. The same should be stated for the other direction. Thus, when two thousand five hundred and seventy-five yojanas are added in, that support is filled up. Which was stated:

children.text:
tiryak trīṇi sahasrāṇi sārdhaṃ śatacatuṣṭayaṃ
lakṣadvādaśakaṃ caiva jalakāṃcanamaṇḍalam
children.translated_text:
'Horizontally, three thousand four hundred,
and twelve lakṣas — the water-and-gold disc' —

body.text: iti. anayā caturdvīpasaṃkhyayā yathāvinyāsam atiricyamānatvāt. tad idaṃ parihriyate. naiṣa doṣaḥ. cakravāḍabahirjalakāṃcanamaṇḍalasya etāvatātiricyamānatvāt. na tarhi caturdvīpakaḥ tena cakravāḍena cakrīkṛtaḥ. uparibhūmir anena cakrīkṛtā. na jalamaṇḍalam ity avagantavyaṃ. apara āha. na sumervādayaḥ parvatā atyantacchinnataṭīsamucchrāyaghanā bhavaṃti. kiṃ tarhi. parvatākāranyāyena kiṃcidatiricyamānādharabhāgā durlakṣaviśeṣatvāt.
body.translated_text: thus. Because with the count of four continents, arranged in order, there is an excess. This is resolved: there is no fault — because of the excess being that much of the water-and-gold disc outside <s>Cakravāḍa</s>. Then the four continents are not encircled by that <s>Cakravāḍa</s>. It should be understood that the upper surface is encircled by it, not the water disc. Another says: <s>Sumeru</s> and the other mountains are not solid columns with absolutely sheer cliffs. Rather, according to the mountain-shape principle, their lower portions extend somewhat outward, the difference being imperceptible.

body.text: samocchrāyaghanāś ca ta
body.translated_text: 'And they are solid in their full height' —

body.text: ity uktvā. atas [Tib. 314b] taistaiḥ kiṃcidatiricyamānair adhobhāgais tad ādheyaṃ
body.translated_text: having said this, therefore [Tib. 314b] with those somewhat extending lower portions, what is contained

body.text: sumervādikaṃ ādhāraṃ jalakāṃcanamaṇḍalātmakam vyāpnotīty avirodha eṣa iti.
body.translated_text: — namely <s>Sumeru</s> and the rest — pervades the support consisting of the water-and-gold disc. Thus there is no contradiction.

body.text: (III.54-57) anya iti vistaraḥ. na bodhisattvāśrayād anya āśrayo vajrāsanapradeśād vānyaḥ pradeśas taṃ vajropamaṃ samādhiṃ soḍhuṃ samartha iti. yaś ca dvīpo yadākṛtir iti. pratyakṣam etat. bhūmivaśāt sattvānāṃ vaicitryaṃ. himavadvindhyavāsināṃ kirātaśabarāṇāṃ gauraśyāmate dṛśyate.
body.translated_text: (III.54-57) 'Another' — this is the elaboration. No other physical support than the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s body, and no other location than the <s>vajrāsana</s> (diamond seat), is capable of enduring that diamond-like <s>samādhi</s>. 'And whatever continent has whatever shape' — this is directly perceived. The diversity of beings is due to the land. Among the <s>Kirātas</s> and <s>Śabaras</s> dwelling in the <s>Himālaya</s> and <s>Vindhya</s> [mountains], fair and dark complexions are seen.

body.text: iti. sthānināṃ bahutvāt sthānasyāpi bahuvacananirdeśaḥ. eko rākṣasair iti. cāmarāvaracāmarayor anyataraḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Because of the plurality of inhabitants, the place too is indicated in the plural. 'One [is inhabited] by <s>rākṣasas</s>' — one of <s>Cāmara</s> or <s>Avaracāmara</s>.

body.text: iti. kīṭākṛtīnāṃ parvatānāṃ navakāt. tadadhikāreṇāyaṃ jaṃbūdvīpa iti. jaṃbūvṛkṣādhikāreṇa. jambuvṛkṣacihno dvīpo jambudvīpaḥ. phalādhikāreṇa veti. jaṃbvā vā. lup ceti phalam api jambūḥ. tatphalacihno jambūdvīpa ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. From the group of nine mountains shaped like insects. 'This is <s>Jambudvīpa</s> by virtue of that' — by virtue of the <s>jambu</s> tree. The continent marked by the <s>jambu</s> tree is <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. 'Or by virtue of the fruit' — <s>jambū</s> with elision [of the final vowel] can also refer to the fruit. The meaning is: the continent marked by that fruit is <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.

body.text: iti. catuḥprākārā ity arthaḥ. catuḥsaṃniveśā ity apare.
body.translated_text: thus. Meaning: having four ramparts. Others say: having four enclosures.

body.text: iti. ayaḥprākāraparikṣiptā ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Meaning: surrounded by iron ramparts.

body.text: iti. ayasopariṣṭhāc chāditāḥ. ayasāpithitadvārā ity apare.
body.translated_text: thus. Covered over with iron from above. Others say: having doors blocked with iron.

body.text: iti vyāptāḥ. pūrvavad iti. utkṣipte pāde punar api saṃjāyate tvaṅmānsaśoṇitam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: means pervaded. 'As before' — meaning: when the foot is lifted, skin, flesh, and blood are generated again.

body.text: Tib. 315a
body.translated_text: Tib. 315a

body.text: kṣuramārgādikaṃ trayam
body.translated_text: 'The triad beginning with the razor-path' —

body.text: iti. kṣuramārgāsipattravanaśālmalīvanaṃ ceti trayaḥ. śyāmalaśabalāś ca śvāno bhakṣayantīti. asipattravanāntarbhūtāḥ. ayastuṇḍāś ca vāyasā iti. śālmalīvanāntarbhūtāḥ. prāsā bhindipālādayaḥ. adhikayātanāsthānatvād utsadā iti. ucchabdo 'dhikārthaḥ. adhikaṃ sīdyante 'treti utsadāḥ. kathaṃ punar yātanādhikyam ity āha. narakeṣv iti vistaraḥ. apara iti. sthaviramanorathaḥ. sa ūrdhvārthaṃ ucchabdam iti. tenāhā narakāvarodhād avīcyādinarakāvarodhāt ūrdhvam eṣu kukūlādiṣu sīdanti. atas tadutsadā iti.
body.translated_text: thus. The triad is: the razor-path (<s>kṣuramārga</s>), the sword-leaf forest (<s>asipattra-vana</s>), and the silk-cotton tree forest (<s>śālmalī-vana</s>). 'Dark and mottled dogs devour [them]' — these are included within the sword-leaf forest. 'And iron-beaked crows' — these are included within the silk-cotton tree forest. Spears, javelins, and the like (<s>prāsa</s>, <s>bhindipāla</s>, etc.). They are called 'additional' (<s>utsada</s>) because they are places of additional torment. The prefix <s>ut-</s> means 'additional.' They suffer additionally there — hence <s>utsada</s>s. How is the torment additional? He says: 'In the hells' — this is the elaboration. 'Another' — the elder <s>Manoratha</s>. He [takes] the prefix <s>ut-</s> in the sense of 'above.' Therefore he says: above the confinement of hell — above the confinement of <s>Avīci</s> and other hells — they suffer in these burning pits (<s>kukūla</s>) and the rest. Therefore they are 'additional' (<s>utsada</s>) to those [hells].

body.text: praśnāt praśnāntaram iti. ṣoḍaśotsadāḥ katama ity uktvā. caturtha utsado
body.translated_text: 'From one question to another question' — having stated 'what are the sixteen additional [hells]?', the fourth additional [hell]

body.text: vaitaraṇī. yasyāṃ te sattvāḥ asiśaktiprāsahastaiḥ puruṣair ubhābhyāṃ tīrābhyāṃ prativāryamāṇād ūrdhvam api gacchantaḥ svidyante pacyanta iti. tasmād idaṃ praśnāntaraṃ upajāyate. kiṃ te narakapālā iti vistaraḥ. vivartanīvāyuvad iti yathā vivartanyāṃ vāyavo bhājanalokābhinirvṛttaye ceṣṭante. tadlat te bhūtabhautikamātrā narakapālā iti.
body.translated_text: is <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> — in which those beings, being turned back from both banks by men holding swords, spears, and lances in their hands, even as they go upward, are boiled and cooked. Therefore this further question arises: 'Are those hell-guardians [sentient beings]?' — this is the elaboration. 'Like the winds of the cosmic evolution period' — just as during the period of cosmic evolution, winds exert themselves for the production of the vessel world, similarly those hell-guardians are mere elemental and derived matter.

body.text: iti. pāpakarmāṇaḥ sattvā narakapālā jāyaṃta ity arthaḥ. ye te yameneti. ye te yamena devadūtīyasūtroktenānuśāsanenānuśiṣṭāḥ. tāṃ sattvān narakasthāneṣu prakṣipanti yamarājadhānīnivāsinaḥ. ta ete yamarākṣasā uktāḥ. na tu ye kāraṇā yātanāḥ kārayaṃti asiśaktiprāsahastādayaḥ [Tib. 315b]. tasyedānīṃ karmaṇaḥ kva vipāka iti. narakapālānāṃ narakakṛtasya karmaṇaḥ kva vipākaḥ. teṣv eveti vistaraḥ. yeṣv ānaṃtaryakāriṇāṃ vipākāvakāśaḥ. teṣu narakeṣu teṣāṃ narakapālānāṃ ko vipratibandhaḥ. etad uktaṃ bhavati. teṣām api tāvad ānantaryakāriṇāṃ mahadānantaryakarmaṇo vipākasyātimahato narakeṣv avakāśo 'sti. kim aṃga punar narakapālānāṃ yat karma tatkāraṇāḥ kārayatām iti. kṛtāvadhitvāt kṛtamaryādatvāt narakapālān prati. ete na dagdhavyā iti. bhūtaviśeṣanirvṛtter vā. bhūtaviśeṣās tādṛśās teṣāṃ karmabhir abhinirvṛttāḥ. yat tenāgninā na dahyante.
body.translated_text: thus. Beings of evil <s>karma</s> are born as hell-guardians — this is the meaning. 'Those who by <s>Yama</s>' — those who are instructed by the instruction spoken by <s>Yama</s> in the <s>Devadūtīya-sūtra</s> — those who cast beings into hell-locations, dwellers of the capital of King <s>Yama</s> — these are called <s>Yamarākṣasas</s>. But not those who inflict punishments — those holding swords, spears, and lances [Tib. 315b]. Then where is the retribution of that <s>karma</s>? Where is the retribution of the <s>karma</s> done in hell by the hell-guardians? 'In those very [hells]' — this is the elaboration. In those hells where there is room for the retribution of those who have committed the immediate-retribution crimes (<s>ānantarya</s>) — in those hells, what obstacle is there for the retribution of those hell-guardians? This is what is meant: even for those who have committed the immediate-retribution crimes, there is room in the hells for the retribution of their great <s>ānantarya-karma</s>, which is exceedingly great. How much more so for the hell-guardians' <s>karma</s> committed while serving as agents of punishment? 'Because of having a set limit' — because of having a fixed boundary with respect to the hell-guardians: 'these are not to be burned.' Or, because of the production of special material elements — special material elements of such a nature are produced by their <s>karma</s>s, such that they are not burned by that fire.

body.text: kāyaśabdavikārānurūpāṇīti. kāyavikārānurūpāṇi arbudo nirbuda utpalaḥ padmo mahāpadmaś ceti nāmāni. arbudādyākārakāyatvāt tatratyānāṃ sattvānāṃ. śabdavikārānurūpāṇi aṭhaṭhaḥ hahavaḥ huhuva ity etāni nāmāni.
body.translated_text: 'Corresponding to bodily and vocal transformations' — the names corresponding to bodily transformation are: <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — because of the beings there having bodies in the shape of <s>arbuda</s> and so forth. The names corresponding to vocal transformation are: <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, and <s>Huhuva</s>.

body.text: ata eveti. dhānyarāśivad adhoviśālatvāt. bahir iti nāntargataḥ.
body.translated_text: 'For this very reason' — because they are wider at the bottom, like a heap of grain. 'Outside' — meaning not inside.

body.text: (III.61-63) taijasaṃ sūryakāntātmakaṃ āpyaṃ candrakāntātmakaṃ. yathāsaṃbhavam iti. tadubhayamaṇḍalaṃ dṛṣṭyādīnāṃ deśakālāvasthāntarānurūpyeṇa anugrahārtham upaghātārthaṃ ca. evam anyeṣv api yojyam iti. kathaṃ. yadā pūrvavidehe rātraḥ. tadā jaṃbūdvīpe [Tib. 316a] sūryāstaṃgamanam avaragodānīye madhyāhnaḥ uttarakurāv udaya ity evam anyatrāpi yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: (III.61-63) The fiery [disc] is made of sun-gems (<s>sūryakānta</s>); the watery [disc] is made of moon-gems (<s>candrakānta</s>). 'As appropriate' — the two discs [of sun and moon], for the purposes of benefiting and harming beings through sight and the rest, [function] in accordance with different places, times, and conditions. 'Similarly, it should be applied to the others as well.' How? When it is night in <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, [Tib. 316a] then in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> the sun is setting, in <s>Avaragodānīya</s> it is midday, and in <s>Uttarakuru</s> it is sunrise — thus it should be applied to the other [continents] as well.

children.translated_text: 'On the last ninth [day] of the second month of the rainy season' —

body.text: iti. prāvṛṇmāsāś catvāraḥ śrāvaṇo yāvat kārttikaḥ. sarve ca māsāḥ kṛṣṇapakṣādyāḥ. tatra bhādrapadaśuklapakṣanavamyāṃ rātrir vardhate.
body.translated_text: thus. The rainy-season months are four, from <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> through <s>Kārttika</s>. And all months begin with the dark fortnight. There, on the ninth day of the bright fortnight of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, the night increases.

children.translated_text: 'It decreases in the fourth [month] of the winter [months].'

body.text: hemantīmāsāś catvāro mārgaśīrṣādyāḥ phālgunāntāḥ. tatra phālgunaśuklapakṣanavamyāṃ hīyate nilavaṃlavaṃla. kāladhvanor atyantasaṃyoge dvitīyā.
body.translated_text: The winter months are four, from <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> through <s>Phālguna</s>. There, on the ninth day of the bright fortnight of <s>Phālguna</s>, it decreases. The doubling of '<s>lavala</s>' is due to the extreme conjunction of time and sound.

body.text: aparapārśve chāyā patantī vikalaṃ maṇḍalaṃ darśayatīti. tadyathā staṃbhe pradīpacchāyā patantī. yathāyathā staṃbha āsanno bhavati. tathātathā staṃbhaḥ svachāyayā chādyate. dūre hi vartamāne pradīpe paripūrṇastaṃbho dṛśyate. kiṃcid āsanne kiṃcit kṣīyate yāvad āsanne staṃbho naṣṭarūpo vartate. tadvad etat. vāhayogaḥ sa tādṛśa iti. punas tiryag avanāmonnāmayogenādhobhāgaś candramaṇḍalasya kṣīyate. ūrdhvaṃ vardhate ceti yogācārāḥ. cāturmahārājakāyikā iti caturmahārājānāṃ kāyaḥ. tatra bhavāś cāturmahārājakāyikāḥ. sumerupariṣaṇḍādīnīti. ādiśabdena yugaṃdharādīni.
body.translated_text: The shadow falling on the other side shows an incomplete disc. Just as the shadow of a lamp falling on a pillar — the closer the pillar is, the more the pillar is covered by its own shadow. For when the lamp is far away, the full pillar is visible; when somewhat closer, it is somewhat diminished; when very close, the pillar appears to have lost its form. It is like that. 'That is the arrangement of the vehicle' — and by the mechanism of oblique tilting downward and upward, the lower part of the moon's disc diminishes and the upper part increases — so say the <s>Yogācāras</s>. '<s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s>' — the retinue (<s>kāya</s>) of the four great kings. Those who belong to it are the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> [gods]. '<s>Sumerupariṣaṇḍa</s> and so forth' — by the word 'and so forth,' <s>Yugaṃdhara</s> and the rest [are included].

body.text: iti. yojanadaśasahasrapramāṇāntarā ity arthaḥ. ardham ākṣiptam iti. ardham avaṣṭabdhaṃ.
body.translated_text: meaning: with an interval measuring ten thousand <s>yojanas</s>. 'Half is projected' — half is suspended.

body.text: iti. sadāmattā iti vaktavye ślokabandhānuguṇyena sadāmadā ity uktam arthaikatvāt. caturthyāṃ catvāro mahārājānaḥ svayaṃ prativasantīti. dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ pūrvadigbhāge. [Tib. 316b] virūḍhako dakṣiṇe. virūpakṣaḥ paścime. vaiśramaṇa uttarasminn ity anukramo 'vagantavyaḥ. cāturmahārājikā devā ity uktam iti. yasmāc caturthyāṃ pariṣaṇḍāyāṃ catvāro mahārājānaḥ svayaṃ prativasaṃti. ata evam uktaṃ mahārājikā devā iti. mahārājeṣu bhavā iti kṛtvā mahiṣṭho mahattamaḥ.
body.translated_text: though '<s>Sadāmattā</s>' should be said, '<s>Sadāmadā</s>' is said for metrical conformity, the meaning being the same. 'On the fourth [terrace], the four great kings themselves reside.' [Tib. 316b] <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> on the eastern side, <s>Virūḍhaka</s> on the southern, <s>Virūpākṣa</s> on the western, <s>Vaiśramaṇa</s> on the northern — this is the order to be understood. 'The <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods' — this was so stated because on the fourth terrace the four great kings themselves reside. Therefore it is said '<s>Mahārājika</s> gods' — because they belong to the great kings. The superlative of 'great' is the greatest.

body.text: (III.66-69) sa viṃśatisahasradig
body.translated_text: (III.66-69) 'That one [has] twenty-thousand [yojanas] in each direction' —

body.text: iti. yady evaṃ katham idam uktaṃ
body.translated_text: thus. If so, how was this stated:

children.translated_text: 'And they are solid in their full height' —

body.text: iti. madhyabhāgam evābhisamīkṣyaivam uktam iti teṣām abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Their intent is that this was stated with reference to only the middle portion.

body.text: iti. adhikam ardham asminn iti adhyardhaṃ. adhyardhaṃ yojanam asyety
body.translated_text: thus. That in which the half is exceeded is <s>adhyardha</s>. One whose [measure is] one-and-a-half <s>yojanas</s> —

body.text: samucchrāyeṇeti adhyāhāryaṃ. dhātuśatena raṃgaśatena. nānāratnasthānavidhānasaṃpadeti. nānāratnavidhānasampadā nānāsthānavidhānasampadā ca. sarvānyabhavanānāṃ śriyas tāsāṃ mahimāno mahattvāni. hrepaṇo lajjano lajjājanaka ity arthaḥ. dairghyeṇārdhatṛtīyaṃ yojanaśataṃ pārśvam iti. ekaṃ pārśvam etatpramāṇaṃ. yāvac caturtham apy etatpramāṇam iti.
body.translated_text: 'In height' — this is to be supplied. 'With a hundred mineral pigments' — with a hundred dyes. 'Endowed with the arrangement of various gem-seats' — endowed with the arrangement of various gems and the arrangement of various seats. The splendors of all other palaces — their grandeurs, their greatnesses — are put to shame (<s>hrepaṇa</s>), meaning causing embarrassment, causing a sense of inferiority. 'In length, two-and-a-half hundred <s>yojanas</s> is one side' — one side is of that measure; up to the fourth [side] is also of that measure.

body.text: śobhanā bhūmaya eṣām iti
body.translated_text: 'those whose grounds are beautiful' —

body.text: iti. catasro diśo 'syeti
body.translated_text: 'that which has four directions' —

body.text: kriyāviśeṣaṇaṃ. bhāgurimatena dikchabdo 'kāranto bhavati. viṃśatiyojanāny atikramya kṛīḍāsthānāni bhavantīti. viṃśatiyojanāny antaritānīty ucyate. trāyastriṃśānām iti. trayastriṃśās teṣu bhavās trāyastriṃśāḥ. teṣāṃ. kāmaratiprakarṣālayaḥ kāmarativiśeṣasthānaṃ. vṛkṣānatikramaṃ [Tib. 317a] saṃdhāyoktam iti. taṃ kovidāravṛkṣam anatikramya sa gandho vartate. tasya paṃcāśadyojanāni śākhāpattrapalāśam iti evaṃ vṛkṣānatikramaṃ saṃdhāyoktaṃ paṃcāśadyojanāni prativātaṃ gandho vātīti. atrottaram āhuḥ. na hi nāma prativātaṃ vāto bhavati. yatraivotpadyate. tatraiva dhvansyate. na deśāntare saṃtānaṃ saṃtanoti. uktaṃ ca paṃcāśadyojanāni prativātam iti. tasmād asamādhir eṣaḥ. tasmāt samādhyantaram idam āha. tasyaiva tv iti vistaraḥ. kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ yojanaśatam atra vātaṃ gaṃdho vāti prativātaṃ tu paṃcāśat. na tataḥ pareṇeti ata āha. mandataratamasamāraṃbhāt tv iti vistaraḥ. mṛdumārutapratibadhyamānatayā mandataratamasamāraṃbhaḥ. tataś ca sa gandhasaṃtāna āśv eva samucchidyate. ataḥ kāraṇāt na tathā viprakṛṣṭam adhvānaṃ yojanaśatapramāṇaṃ prasarpatīti.
body.translated_text: this is an adverbial modifier. According to <s>Bhāguri</s>'s view, the direction-word ends in <s>a</s>. 'Having traversed twenty <s>yojanas</s>, there are pleasure grounds' — they are said to be separated by twenty <s>yojanas</s>. 'Of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> [gods]' — the thirty-three; those belonging to them are <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>. Of those [gods]. 'The abode of the excellence of desire-pleasure' — the place of special desire-pleasure. [Tib. 317a] 'This is said with reference to not exceeding the tree' — that fragrance extends without exceeding that <s>kovidāra</s> tree. Its branches, leaves, and foliage [extend] fifty <s>yojanas</s> — thus, said with reference to not exceeding the tree, 'the fragrance wafts fifty <s>yojanas</s> against the wind.' To this they raise the following objection: for wind does not blow against the wind — where it arises, there it perishes; it does not extend a continuum to another place. And it is stated 'fifty <s>yojanas</s> against the wind.' Therefore this is inconsistent. Therefore he states another resolution: 'But of that very [tree]' — this is the elaboration. What is the reason that the fragrance wafts a hundred <s>yojanas</s> with the wind but only fifty against the wind, and not beyond that? Therefore he says: 'But because of progressively weaker and weakest onset' — this is the elaboration. Because of being impeded by gentle breezes, the onset is progressively weaker and weakest. Therefore that fragrance-continuum is very quickly cut off. For this reason, it does not travel as far a distance as a hundred <s>yojanas</s>.

body.text: utāho vāyur adhivāsito jāyata iti. yathā tileṣu puṣpagaṃdhād gandhāntaram utpadyate 'nyad eva na sa pauṣpo gandha ity āha. yadi paṃcāśadyojanaṃ prativātagandho vāti. yat tarhi bhagavatoktaṃ
body.translated_text: Or, a perfumed wind arises — just as in sesame seeds, a different fragrance is produced from the scent of flowers, and that is not the flower's fragrance — [so he says]. If the fragrance against the wind wafts fifty <s>yojanas</s>, then what the Blessed One said —

children.translated_text: 'The fragrance of flowers does not travel against the wind' —

body.text: vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: this is the elaboration.

body.text: mustādiḥ.
body.translated_text: such as <s>mustā</s> (cyperus) and the like.

body.text: kṛtyākṛtyaṃ samarthayanta iti. kāryākāryaṃ saṃpratīcchanti saṃpradhārayantīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'They deliberate what should and should not be done' — meaning: they accept and consider what is proper and improper to do.

body.text: (III.70ab) samāsena yeṣāṃ bhājanaṃ prajñāyata iti. bhājanaṃ sthānaṃ. vistareṇānye 'pi devāḥ krīḍāpramoṣakaprahāsakādayaḥ santīti. ataḥ samāsenoktaṃ.
body.translated_text: (III.70ab) In brief, that which is known as their vessel — vessel means abode. In detail, there are also other gods such as Krīḍāpramoṣaka, Prahāsaka, and others. Therefore it is stated in brief.

body.text: (III.70cd) dvaṃdvena [Tib. 317b] yāvad īkṣitena maithunam eṣām iti
body.translated_text: (III.70cd) By coupling, up to by gazing — their sexual union is [as follows]:

children.translated_text: Those whose sexual union is through coupling, embracing, holding hands, laughing, and gazing.

body.text: saṛveṣāṃ samāpattyeti. ṣaṇṇām api kāmabhujāṃ dvaṃdvasamāpattyā paridāhavigamaḥ. kālaparimāṇaṃ tu prajñaptāv uktam iti. yāvatā kālena dvaṃdvāliṃganapāṇyāptihasitekṣitāni bhavaṃti. tāvatā kālena eṣāṃ bhūmisambandhavāsināṃ yāmatuṣitanirmāṇaratiparanirmitavaśavartināṃ yathākramaṃ dvaṃdvasamāpattir
body.translated_text: The consummation of all — for all six classes of desire-realm beings (<s>kāmabhuj</s>), the burning passion subsides through the consummation of coupling. The measure of time is stated in the <s>Prajñapti</s>. By whatever duration coupling, embracing, holding hands, laughing, and gazing occur, by that duration, for those dwelling in connection with these grounds — the <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, and <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods — respectively the consummation of coupling [occurs]

body.text: iti vaibhāṣikāḥ. yāvadyāvad iti vistaraḥ. yāvadyāvat pareṇa paratareṇa viṣayāṇāṃ tīvrataratvāt rāgo 'pi tīvrataraḥ. tāvattāvan maithunakāra ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: — thus say the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>. 'More and more' — and so forth in detail. The more and more intense the objects become, the more intense the passion (<s>rāga</s>) also becomes. Accordingly, the manner of sexual union [becomes more refined] — this is the intent.

body.text: (III.71cd) te punaś catvāro devanikāyā iti. cāturmahārājakāyikā yāvat tuṣitāḥ. yathotpannaparibhogaḥ sa eṣām astīti yathotpannaparibhoginaḥ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. yathecchayātmanirmitaṃ. tasya paribhogaḥ. pūrvavat. yathecchātmaparanirmitaparibhogitvād iti. ātmanā pareṇa ca nirmite. yathecchayātmaparanirmite. tayoḥ paribhogaḥ pūrvavat. yathecchaparanirmitaparibhogitvād iti kecit paṭhanti. tatra pāṭhe evaṃ vigrahaḥ. paranirmitaṃ yathecchaṃ paranirmitaṃ. tasya paribhoga iti. pūrvavat. nirmāṇaratīnāṃ paranirmitāṃ kāmān paribhoktuṃ na samṛdhyati. tad evaṃ paranirmitavaśavartināṃ nirmāṇaratibhyo [Tib. 318a] viśeṣaḥ pradarśito bhavati. bāhyarūpādiviṣayanirmāṇaṃ cātra veditavyaṃ. vivekajena prathamadhyānabhūmikena. akuśalaviviktatvāt. samādhijena ca dvitīyadhyānabhūmikena. vitarkavicāravigamāt. prītisukheneti. prītilakṣaṇena sukhena. niḥprītikena ca sukhena. saumanasyavigamāt. sukhaṃ viharanta iti. sukham iti kriyāviśeṣaṇaṃ. sukhopapattitvaṃ vicāryam iti. sukhābhāvān na dhyānāntaraṃ sukhopapattir iti śakyaṃ vaktuṃ. kuśalavipākatvena sukhakalpatvāt sukhopapattir iti na śakyaṃ vyavasthāpayituṃ. caturthe 'pi dhyāne sukhopapattiprasaṃga iti cet. na. tasyāṃ bhūmau sukhābhāvāt. tasmād vicāryaṃ saṃpradhāryam etad iti bhāvaḥ.
body.translated_text: (III.71cd) Those again, four classes of gods — from <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> up to <s>Tuṣita</s>. One who enjoys things as they arise — they have this [characteristic], hence they are 'enjoyers of things as arisen' (<s>yathotpannaparibhogin</s>). The state of that. Therefore. [Enjoying] what is self-created according to wish — the enjoyment of that. As before. Because of enjoying what is created by oneself and others according to wish — created by oneself and by another. What is self-and-other-created according to wish — the enjoyment of both, as before. Some read 'because of enjoying what is other-created according to wish.' In that reading, the analysis is thus: other-created means created by another according to wish. The enjoyment of that — as before. For the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, it does not succeed to enjoy pleasures created by others. Thus is shown the distinction of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods from the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods. And here, the creation of external objects such as visible form should be understood. Born of seclusion — belonging to the ground of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Because of being secluded from unwholesome [states]. And born of concentration — belonging to the ground of the second <s>dhyāna</s>. Because of the disappearance of applied and sustained thought (<s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>). With joy and happiness — with happiness characterized by joy (<s>prīti</s>). And with happiness devoid of joy — because of the disappearance of elation (<s>saumanasya</s>). 'Dwelling in happiness' — 'happiness' is a qualifier of the action. The matter of being a 'happy birth' (<s>sukhopapatti</s>) should be examined — because of the absence of happiness, it cannot be said that the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> [state] is a happy birth. Because of being a wholesome fruition and thus resembling happiness, it cannot be definitively established as a happy birth either. If one objects that in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> too there would be the absurd consequence of a happy birth — no, because of the absence of happiness in that ground. Therefore 'should be examined' means 'should be deliberated' — this is the meaning.

body.text: (III.72cd) evaṃ śeṣā iti. ṛddhyā vā yāmās tuṣitāṃ gaccheyuḥ. yadi ṛddhimatā nīyeran. devena vā tatratyena. samānabhūmikās tu cāturmahārājakāyikāḥ trayastriṃśāṃ gacchanti. āgataṃ tūrdhvopapannaṃ paśyed iti. samānabhūmikaṃ nordhvabhūmikam iti. prathamadhyānopapanno na dvitīyadhyānopapannam ityādi. tadicchayeti. ūrdhvopapanecchayā. ihatyam iveti. ihabhava ihatyaḥ. adhobhūmika ity arthaḥ. ihatyam iva paśyed iti nikāyāntarīyāḥ. yathā spraṣṭavyam ity udāharaṇamātram etat. [Tib. 318b] yathā śabda ity etad api gamyeta.
body.translated_text: (III.72cd) Thus the remainder — by supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), the <s>Yāma</s> gods could go to <s>Tuṣita</s>. If they are taken by one possessing supernatural power. Or by a god from that [higher realm]. But those of the same ground — the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods go to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven. But one could see one who has been reborn above — one of the same ground, not one of a higher ground. One born in the first <s>dhyāna</s> [cannot see] one born in the second <s>dhyāna</s>, and so forth. By the wish of that one — by the wish of the one reborn above. As if belonging to this [lower realm] — 'of this existence' means 'belonging to this [realm],' meaning 'of a lower ground.' One would see [them] as if belonging to this [lower realm] — thus say the followers of other schools (<s>nikāyāntarīya</s>). Just as touch — this is merely an illustration. Just as sound — this too can be inferred.

body.text: caturṇāṃ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ yāmādisthānānāṃ. dviguṇottaram iti. yāmasthānād dviguṇaṃ tuṣitasthānam ityādi. caturthaṃ tv aparimāṇam iti. tārakāvat atalavāṭakapratibaddhavimānatvāt aparimāṇatvasaṃbhava ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: Of the four desire-realm abodes beginning with <s>Yāma</s>. Doubling progressively — the <s>Tuṣita</s> abode is double that of the <s>Yāma</s> abode, and so forth. But the fourth is immeasurable — because their mansions are attached to star-like canopy-platforms, immeasurability is possible — this is the intent.

body.text:
(III.73, 74) sahasraṃ brahmalokānām
iti. brahmakāyikabrahmapurohitamahābrahmaṇām ity arthaḥ. loke tathā pratītatvāt.
body.translated_text: (III.73, 74) 'A thousand <s>Brahmā</s>-worlds' — the meaning is: of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, and <s>Mahābrahmā</s> [gods]. Because it is so understood in the world.

body.text: iti. mahato lokadhātoś cūḍābhūtatvāt cūlika ity ucyate. saṃbhavo hi vivarta iti. vividhavartanaṃ vivartaḥ. vividhā vā vartante 'sminn iti vivartaḥ. saṃvartanaṃ saṃvartaḥ. samvartante vāsminn iti saṃvartaḥ. tasmiṃ hi kāle sattvā ekasmin dhyāne dvitīye tṛtīye caturthe vā saṃvartante saṃgacchanta iti.
body.translated_text: because it is the crest (<s>cūḍā</s>) of the great world-system, it is called <s>cūlikā</s>. For origination is evolution (<s>vivarta</s>) — manifold turning is evolution; or that in which [things] variously turn is evolution. Dissolution is <s>saṃvarta</s>; or that in which [beings] converge is <s>saṃvarta</s>. For at that time, beings converge — come together — in one <s>dhyāna</s>, or the second, third, or fourth.

children.text: vivartate ca saṃvṛtta āste saṃvartate samam
children.translated_text: It evolves, having dissolved it remains, and dissolves simultaneously —

body.text: iti uttaratra vyākhyāsyāmaḥ.
body.translated_text: this we shall explain further on.

children.translated_text: The inhabitants of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in measurement, are four [cubits] or three and a half cubits —

body.text: iti. sārdhatrihastapramāṇaśarīrāḥ. kecit tu caturhastapramāṇaśarīrāḥ.
body.translated_text: meaning their bodies measure three and a half cubits. But some [say] their bodies measure four cubits.

body.text: iti. pūrvo goda uttara iti cāhvaya eṣāṃ. te
body.translated_text: meaning: <s>Pūrva</s>, <s>Goda</s>, and <s>Uttara</s> are their names. They are

body.text: teṣāṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ aṣṭahastapramāṇāḥ pūrvavidehakāḥ ṣoḍaśahastapramāṇāḥ godānīyāḥ dvātriṃśaddhastapramāṇakā auttarakauravā iti.
body.translated_text: Of those, respectively: the inhabitants of <s>Pūrvavideha</s> measure eight cubits; the inhabitants of <s>Godānīya</s> measure sixteen cubits; and the inhabitants of <s>Uttarakuru</s> measure thirty-two cubits.

body.text: vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail.

body.text: iti vakṣyamāṇatvāt pāda iti krośasyeti gamyate. krośacaturthabhāgamātraṃ ca śarīraṃ [Tib. 319a] cāturmahārājakāyikānāṃ. dvipādamātraṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ yāvad adhyardhakrośamātraṃ paranirmitavaśavartināṃ. yojanatrayeṇa hīnaṃ dviguṇam iti. dviguṇaṃ kṛtvā tṛīṇi yojanāny apaneyāni. paṃcaviṃśayojanaśatam anabhrakāṇāṃ śarīrapraṃāṇam iti. puṇyaprasavānām iti. puṇyaprasavānām ardhatṛtīyaṃ yojanaśataṃ śarīrapramāṇaṃ. bṛhatphalānāṃ paṃcayojanaśatānīti gaṇayitavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: because this will be stated [later], it is understood that 'quarter' refers to a quarter of a <s>krośa</s>. The body of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods measures only a quarter of a <s>krośa</s>. That of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods measures two quarters. Up to the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, [the body measures] one and a half <s>krośa</s>s. 'Doubling minus three <s>yojana</s>s' — doubling and then subtracting three <s>yojana</s>s. The body measurement of the <s>Anabhraka</s> gods is five hundred <s>yojana</s>s. Of the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> gods — the body measurement of the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> gods is two hundred and fifty <s>yojana</s>s. That of the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods should be calculated as five hundred <s>yojana</s>s.

body.text: (III.77cd-80) kumudapadmavad iti. yatheha kumudāni ahani saṃkucanti rātrau vikasanti. padmāni tu viparyayeṇa. tathā tatra keṣāṃcid eva puṣpāṇāṃ saṃkocād ahani ca vikāsād ahorātravyavasthānaṃ. śakunīnāṃ ca kūjanākūjanāt. akūjanād rātriḥ kūjanāt prabhātaṃ. viparyayeṇa vā yathāśakunijāti. middhāpagamopagamāc ca. middhopagamād rātriḥ prajñāyate. middhāpagamāt prabhātam iti.
body.translated_text: (III.77cd-80) Like <s>kumuda</s> and <s>padma</s> — just as here <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotuses) close during the day and bloom at night, while <s>padma</s> (day-lotuses) do the opposite, similarly there, through the closing of certain flowers during the day and their blooming, and through the singing and non-singing of birds, the distinction of day and night is established. From the non-singing [of birds] it is night; from the singing, it is dawn. Or conversely, depending on the species of bird. And from the onset and departure of drowsiness (<s>middha</s>) — from the onset of drowsiness, night is recognized; from the departure of drowsiness, it is dawn.

body.text: iti. viṃśatir adhikaṃ. adhikaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ. tenāha. evam teṣāṃ yathākramaṃ catvāriṃśat ṣaṣṭir aśītiḥ kalpasahasrāṇy āyuḥpramāṇam iti. vijñānānaṃtyāyatane
body.translated_text: meaning twenty more. The meaning is: [twenty] more than that. Therefore he says: thus, for them respectively, the lifespan measure is twenty, forty, sixty, and eighty thousand <s>kalpa</s>s. In the realm of Infinite Consciousness (<s>Vijñānānantyāyatana</s>)

body.text: catvāriṃśat. ākiṃcanyāyatane ṣaṣṭiḥ. bhavagre 'śītir iti. tasmād adho mahākalpasyārdham iti vistaraḥ. aśītir antarakalpā mahākalpaḥ. tasyārdhaṃ catvāriṃśad antarakalpāḥ. tasya mahākalpārdhasya kalpīkṛtasya yad ardhaṃ viṃśatir antarakalpāḥ. tad brahmakāyikānāṃ āyuḥpramāṇaṃ. [Tib. 319b] yat tadardhakalpīkṛtaṃ catvāriṃśad antarakalpāḥ. tad brahmapurohitānām āyuḥpramāṇaṃ. tad evam ātmīyārdhaṃ mahābrahmaṇa āyuḥpramāṇaṃ. sa hy adhyardhaḥ kalpa ity ucyate ṣaṣṭyantarakalpasaṃkhyā. mahābrahmādīnām iti. ādiśabdena brahmapurohitānāṃ brahmakāyikānāṃ ca prātilomyena grahaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: forty [thousand]. In the realm of Nothingness (<s>Ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>), sixty [thousand]. At the summit of existence (<s>Bhavāgra</s>), eighty [thousand]. Therefore, below that is half a great <s>kalpa</s> — and so forth in detail. Eighty intermediate <s>kalpa</s>s make a great <s>kalpa</s>. Half of that is forty intermediate <s>kalpa</s>s. Half of that half great <s>kalpa</s>, treated as a <s>kalpa</s>, is twenty intermediate <s>kalpa</s>s — that is the lifespan of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods. That half-<s>kalpa</s> treated as a <s>kalpa</s>, [halved again, equals] forty intermediate <s>kalpa</s>s — that is the lifespan of the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods. Thus the own-half is the lifespan of <s>Mahābrahmā</s>. For that is called one and a half <s>kalpa</s>s, being sixty intermediate <s>kalpa</s>s in number. 'Beginning with <s>Mahābrahmā</s>' — by the word 'beginning,' the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> and <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods are grasped in reverse order.

body.text: iti parīttābhād devanikāyād iti nirdeśāpekṣaṇāt.
body.translated_text: this is because the specification depends on [starting from] the <s>Parīttābha</s> class of gods.

body.text: (III.81-83) teṣām āyuḥpramāṇam uktam iti. teṣāṃ mahābrahmaṇāṃ brahmapurohitānāṃ brahmakāyikānāṃ.
body.translated_text: (III.81-83) Their lifespan has been stated — of those <s>Mahābrahmā</s>s, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>s, and <s>Brahmakāyika</s>s.

children.translated_text: 'Equal to the lifespan of the desire-realm gods' —

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. cāturmahārājakāyikānāṃ yad āyuḥpramāṇam uktaṃ. sa saṃjīve ahorātraḥ. evaṃ yāvad yat paranirmitavaśavartinām āyuḥpramāṇam uktaṃ. sa tapane ahorātraḥ.
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. The lifespan stated for the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods — that constitutes one day-and-night in <s>Saṃjīva</s> [hell]. Similarly, up to: the lifespan stated for the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods — that constitutes one day-and-night in <s>Tapana</s> [hell].

body.text: iti. kāmadevānām iva
body.translated_text: meaning: like the desire-realm gods.

body.text: tatra tasyeveti vatiḥ. tena yāvat dvādaśamāsakeneti tena tatratyenāhorātreṇa teṣāṃ triṃśadrātrakeṇa māsena dvādśamāsakena samvatsareṇa tatratyāni divyāni paṃca varṣaśatāny āyur ityādi. evam anyeṣv api yathāyogaṃ yojyam iti. yad yāmānām āyuḥpramāṇaṃ. tat saṃghāte mahānarake ekaṃ rātriṃdivam. tena rātridivena tasmin varṣasahasradvayam āyuḥpramāṇaṃ. evam anyeṣv api yathāyogaṃ yojyaṃ. aṣṭāv ime bhikṣava iti. aṣṭāv ime bhikṣavaḥ nāgā mahānāgāḥ kalpasthā dharaṇiṃdharāḥ apratyuddhāryāḥ suparṇinaḥ pakṣirājasya devāsuram api [Tib. 320a] saṃgrāmam anubhavanty api pratyanubhavanty api. te punaḥ katame. tadyathā nando nāgarājaḥ upanando nāgarājaḥ aśvatarī nāgarājaḥ mucilindo nāgarājaḥ manasvī nāgarājaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭro nāgarājo mahākālo nāgarāja elapattro nāgarāja iti. cūlikābaddha iti śikhābaddhaḥ.
body.translated_text: There, 'as if of that' — this is the [meaning of the suffix] '-vat.' Therefore, 'up to twelve months' means: by that day-and-night of that [hell], by a month of thirty nights, by a year of twelve months — [reckoning by] the divine [time units] there — five hundred years is the lifespan, and so on. Similarly, in the others too, it should be applied as appropriate. The lifespan of the <s>Yāma</s> gods constitutes one day-and-night in the <s>Saṃghāta</s> great hell. By that day-and-night, the lifespan there is two thousand years. Similarly, in the others too, it should be applied as appropriate. 'These eight, O monks' — 'these eight, O monks, are <s>nāga</s>s, great <s>nāga</s>s, abiding for a <s>kalpa</s>, supporting the earth, irresistible, who experience and endure the battle between <s>Suparṇin</s>, the king of birds, and the gods and <s>asura</s>s.' And who are they? Namely: <s>Nanda</s> the <s>Nāga</s> king, <s>Upananda</s> the <s>Nāga</s> king, <s>Aśvatarī</s> the <s>Nāga</s> king, <s>Mucilinda</s> the <s>Nāga</s> king, <s>Manasvī</s> the <s>Nāga</s> king, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> the <s>Nāga</s> king, <s>Mahākāla</s> the <s>Nāga</s> king, and <s>Elapatra</s> the <s>Nāga</s> king. '<s>Cūlikābaddha</s>' means 'bound at the topknot.'

body.text: (III.84ab) ekajātipratibaddhasyeti. ekajanmapratibadhabuddhatvasya. caramabhavikasyeti antyajanmanaḥ, yena tasminn eva janmani arhattvaṃ sākṣāt
body.translated_text: (III.84ab) Of one bound to a single birth — of one whose <s>Buddha</s>-hood is bound to a single birth. Of one in their final existence (<s>caramabhavika</s>) — of one in their last birth, by which in that very birth <s>Arhat</s>-ship is to be directly realized

body.text: kartavyam. tasya nāsty antareṇa kālakriyā yāvad arhattvaṃ na prāpnoti. śraddhānusāridharmānusāriṇoḥ nāsty antareṇa kālakriyā yāvac chraddhādhimuktadṛṣṭiprāptau na bhavataḥ. tadgarbhayor iti. bodhisattvacakravartigarbhayoḥ. tanmātror nāsty antareṇa kālakriyā yāvan na tau jāyete. evamādīnām iti. ādiśabdena nirodhāsaṃjñisamāpattisamāpannānāṃ maitryādisamāpannānāṃ ca nāsty antareṇa kālakriyā yāvat tasmāt samādher na vyuttiṣṭhante.
body.translated_text: . For that one, there is no death in the interim until <s>Arhat</s>-ship is attained. For a <s>Śraddhānusārin</s> (faith-follower) and a <s>Dharmānusārin</s> (dharma-follower), there is no death in the interim until they become a <s>Śraddhādhimukta</s> (one resolved through faith) and a <s>Dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> (one who has attained through view). 'Of those who bear them' — of those bearing a <s>Bodhisattva</s> or a <s>Cakravartin</s> [in their womb]. For the mothers of those, there is no death in the interim until those two are born. 'And the like of such ones' — by the word 'and the like,' for those who have attained the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) or the non-perception attainment (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>), and for those who have attained the <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) meditation and the like, there is no death in the interim until they emerge from that <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text: iti. abhidharmavacanakāle yaḥ puruṣahastaḥ. sa grahītavyaḥ. yena cāturdvīpakādiparimāṇavyavasthānaṃ.
body.translated_text: meaning: the human cubit at the time the <s>Abhidharma</s> was spoken — that is to be taken. By which the measurement of the four-continent [world] and the rest is established.

body.text: (III.87, 88) hemantānām iti. yathā varṣā ity ekasminn apy arthe bahuvacanaṃ prasiddhaṃ. evaṃ hemantā grīṣmā iti draṣṭavyaṃ. pravacane traya eva rtavo na yathā loke ṣaḍ iti. śiśiro hi śītasāmānyād dhemanta ity uktaḥ. vasanto 'py uṣṇasāmānyād grīṣma ity uktaḥ. śarad api vṛṣṭisāmānyād [Tib. 320b] varṣā ity ukteti.
body.translated_text: (III.87, 88) 'Of the winters' — just as '<s>varṣā</s>' (rains) is well-known in the plural even for a single season, similarly '<s>hemantā</s>' (winters) and '<s>grīṣmā</s>' (summers) should be understood. In the teaching, there are only three seasons, not six as in the world. For '<s>śiśira</s>' (cool season) is called '<s>hemanta</s>' (winter) due to the similarity of cold. '<s>Vasanta</s>' (spring) is also called '<s>grīṣma</s>' (summer) due to the similarity of heat. And '<s>śarad</s>' (autumn) is called '<s>varṣā</s>' (rains) due to the similarity of rainfall.

body.text: iti. sarvabauddhānāṃ hemantāḥ prathama ṛtuḥ. grīṣmā dvitīyaḥ. varṣās tṛtīyaḥ. tatrādhikam ardham asyeti adhyardho māsaḥ. tasminn
body.translated_text: for all Buddhists, winter is the first season, summer the second, and rains the third. Therein, 'one and a half' — a month and a half that is in excess. In that

children.translated_text: 'when a month and a half has passed' —

body.text: mārgaśīrṣe sapauṣardhe 'tikrānte.
body.translated_text: when <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> and half of <s>Pauṣa</s> have elapsed.

body.text: pauṣasyardhe 'vaśiṣṭe kṛṣṇacaturdaśyām.
body.translated_text: in the remaining half of <s>Pauṣa</s>, on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight.

body.text: bauddhair
body.translated_text: Buddhists

body.text: tyajyate ity arthaḥ. cāturdaśiko 'tra bhikṣubhiḥ poṣadhaḥ kriyate. evaṃ māghe phālgunārdhe 'tikrānte śeṣe 'rdhamāse phālgunāvaśiṣṭe punar apara ūnarātro nipātyate. tathā grīṣmeṣu vaiśākhakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ āṣāḍhacaturdaśyāṃ cāparāv ūnarātrau nipātyete. varṣeṣv api bhādrapadakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ kārttikakṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ cāparāv ūnarātrau nipātyete.
body.translated_text: meaning: is abandoned. On that [day], the <s>Upoṣadha</s> (observance) is performed by the monks on the fourteenth. Similarly, when <s>Māgha</s> and half of <s>Phālguna</s> have elapsed, in the remaining half-month of <s>Phālguna</s>, another shortened night is dropped. Likewise in summer, on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight of <s>Vaiśākha</s> and on the fourteenth of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, two more shortened nights are dropped. And in the rains too, on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight of <s>Bhādrapada</s> and on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight of <s>Kārttika</s>, two more shortened nights are dropped.

body.text: (III.89-92) gatisaṃvartanīti. narakādyāḥ paṃca gatayo gatyekadeśe devagatau saṃvartante. ekasthībhavantīty arthaḥ. dhātusaṃvartanī ceti. kāmadhātuḥ rūpadhātau saṃvartata iti. sattvasaṃvartanīti. yadā sattvā eva samvartante dhyāneṣv ekasthībhavanti. na tu tāvad bhājanāni saṃvartante. vinaśyantīty arthaḥ. bhājanasamvartanīti. yadā bhājanāny eva samvartante na tu sattvāḥ. ekasyāpi sattvasya tatrābhāvāt. yad ayaṃ loka iti vistaraḥ. yad ayaṃ
body.translated_text: (III.89-92) 'Destiny-dissolution' (<s>gatisaṃvartanī</s>) — the five destinies beginning with the hells dissolve into one part of the destinies, namely the divine destiny. They become unified — this is the meaning. 'And realm-dissolution' (<s>dhātusaṃvartanī</s>) — the Desire Realm (<s>Kāmadhātu</s>) dissolves into the Form Realm (<s>Rūpadhātu</s>). 'Being-dissolution' (<s>sattvasaṃvartanī</s>) — when beings alone dissolve, becoming unified in the <s>dhyāna</s>s, but the vessel-worlds do not yet dissolve — meaning: do not yet perish. 'Vessel-dissolution' (<s>bhājanasaṃvartanī</s>) — when the vessel-worlds alone dissolve, but not the beings, because not even a single being remains there. 'That which is this world' — and so forth in detail.

body.text: loko viṃśatim antarakalpān vivṛtto jātaḥ. yāvan narakotpattiprabhṛti niryātaṃ. [Tib. 321a] tan niṣṭhitaṃ vaktavyam ity arthaḥ. tat pratipannaṃ vaktavyam iti tat saṃvartanam ārabdhaṃ vaktavyam ity arthaḥ. evaṃ tiryaksaṃvartanī pretasaṃvartanī ca vaktavyeti. yadā tiryakṣv ekasattvo 'pi nāvaśiṣṭo bhavati. iyatā 'yaṃ lokaḥ samvṛtto bhavati tiryaksamvartanyā. yasya tadānīṃ niyataṃ tiryagvedanīyaṃ karma dhriyate. sa lokadhātvantaratiryakṣu kṣipyate. evaṃ pretasaṃvartanī yojyā yadā preteṣv iti vistareṇa. manuṣyasahacariṣṇava iti. manuṣyasahacaraṇaśīlāḥ. gomahiṣādayaḥ. dharmatāpratilaṃbhikam iti. dharmatā nāma kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tadānīṃ pariṇāmaviśeṣaḥ. tayā pratilaṃbho 'syāstīti dharmatāpratilaṃbhikaṃ. yan manuṣyeṣv iti. jambūdvīpamanuṣyeṣv ity abhiprāyaḥ. evaṃ pūrvavidehagodānīyasamvartanyau yojyau. uttarakurusaṃvartanī tv evaṃ vaktavyā bhaveti. sa kālo yad uttarakurau manuṣyāś cyavanta eva nopapadyante. yadā tatraikasattvo pi nāvaśiṣṭo bhavati. iyatāyaṃ lokaḥ saṃvṛtto bhavati uttarakurusamvartanyeti. kasmād evaṃ vaktavyā. na tu jaṃbudvīpasamvartanyādivad ity āha. tatra vairāgyābhāvāt. tatrottarakurau vairāgyābhāvāt. ita eva sāmantakād iti. cāturdvīpakasāmantakād ity arthaḥ. tadākṣepake karmaṇi parikṣīṇa iti. bhājanākṣepake bhājanotpādake parikṣīṇa ity arthaḥ. brāhmaṃ vimānaṃ nirdahad arciḥ paraiti [Tib. 321b] gacchatīty arthaḥ. tac ca tadbhūmikam evārcir iti. prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ. kasmād ity āha. na hi visabhāgā visadṛśāḥ apakṣālā upadravāḥ agnyādayaḥ kramante tāpayanta ity arthaḥ. āha. yady evaṃ kim idam ucyate. tasmād eva ceti vistareṇety ata ucyate. tadsambaddhasaṃbhūtatvād iti vistaraḥ. tena kāmāvacareṇārciṣā sambaddhaṃ saṃbhūtaṃ rūpāvacaram arciḥ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmād iti. evam anyasyām iti. yathā tejaḥsamvartanyām uktam evam anyasyām apy apsaṃvartanyāṃ vāyuṣaṃvartanyāṃ ca yathāsaṃbhavaṃ veditavyaṃ. kathaṃ kṛtvā. narakādisaṃvartanīṃ pūrvavad uktvā yāvad iyatāyaṃ lokaḥ samvṛtto bhavati sattvasamvartanyā. tataḥ śūnye bhājane sahajo 'bdhātuḥ saṃbhavati. yas taṃ bhājanalokaṃ lavaṇam iva vilopayati. sa kāmāvacaro 'bdhātuḥ prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ abdhātuṃ saṃbadhnāti. sa ca dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ sambadhnāti. sa cābdhātus tribhūmiko 'pi svenasvena bhājanena sahāntardhīyate. evaṃ vāyusaṃvartanyāṃ sahajo vāyuḥ saṃbhavatīti vaktavyaṃ. katham iti. pūrvavad uktvā yāvat sahajo vāyudhātuḥ saṃbhavatīti. yas taṃ bhājanalokaṃ kāmāvacaraṃ yāvat tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ krameṇa pāṃsurāśim iva
body.translated_text: 'This world, having evolved over twenty intermediate <s>kalpa</s>s, has come into being' — up to the point beginning with the arising of hell-beings, it has been completed — this is the meaning of 'it is to be stated as concluded.' 'It is to be stated as commenced' means: that dissolution has begun and is to be stated — this is the meaning. 'Similarly, the animal-dissolution and the <s>preta</s>-dissolution are to be stated' — when not even a single being remains among the animals, to that extent this world has dissolved through animal-dissolution. One who at that time has karma definitely to be experienced as an animal is cast into the animals of another world-system. Similarly, the <s>preta</s>-dissolution is to be understood: 'when among the <s>preta</s>s' — and so forth in detail. 'Companions of humans' (<s>manuṣyasahacariṣṇavaḥ</s>) — those habitually accompanying humans, such as cows, buffaloes, and the like. 'Obtained through natural law' (<s>dharmatāpratilaṃbhikam</s>) — <s>dharmatā</s> here means the special maturation of wholesome <s>dharma</s>s at that time; that which has its obtainment through this <s>dharmatā</s> is called <s>dharmatāpratilaṃbhika</s>. 'That which is among humans' — the intent is: among the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Similarly, the dissolutions of <s>Pūrvavideha</s> and <s>Godānīya</s> are to be understood. But the dissolution of <s>Uttarakuru</s> is to be stated thus: that is the time when humans in <s>Uttarakuru</s> only pass away and are not reborn. When not even a single being remains there, to that extent this world has dissolved through the <s>Uttarakuru</s>-dissolution. Why is it to be stated thus, and not like the <s>Jambudvīpa</s>-dissolution and the rest? He says: because of the absence of dispassion there. Because there is no dispassion in <s>Uttarakuru</s>. 'From the neighboring [concentration] itself' — meaning: from the neighboring concentration of the four-continent [world-system]. 'When the karma projecting that is exhausted' — meaning: when the karma projecting the vessel-world, the karma producing the vessel-world, is exhausted. 'The flame, burning the <s>Brahma</s> palace, passes beyond' — meaning: it goes. 'And that flame is of that very ground' — meaning: of the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. Why? He says: for dissimilar, meaning unlike, calamities (<s>apakṣāla</s>), meaning disasters such as fire and the rest, do not advance — meaning: do not heat [what is dissimilar]. He asks: if so, what is meant by this statement? 'Therefore from that very' — and so forth in detail — therefore it is said: 'because of being produced in connection with that' — and so forth in detail. The flame connected with and produced from that Desire-Realm flame is the Form-Realm flame. Its nature [is such]. 'Therefore' — thus. 'Similarly in another' — just as stated regarding the fire-dissolution, similarly in another dissolution too — the water-dissolution and the wind-dissolution — it is to be understood as appropriate. How so? Having stated the destiny-dissolution and the rest as before, up to 'to that extent this world has dissolved through being-dissolution,' then in the empty vessel-world, a natural water-element arises that dissolves that vessel-world like salt. That Desire-Realm water-element connects with the first-<s>dhyāna</s>-ground water-element, and that connects with the second-<s>dhyāna</s>-ground [water-element]. And that water-element, though belonging to three grounds, disappears together with its respective vessel-world. Similarly, regarding the wind-dissolution, a natural wind arises — this is to be stated. How? Having stated as before, up to 'a natural wind-element arises' — that [wind] gradually

body.text: vikarati vidhvaṃsayati. yāvat tenaiva sārdham antardhīyate.
body.translated_text: scatters and destroys that vessel-world of the Desire Realm up to the third-<s>dhyāna</s>-ground, like a heap of dust, until it disappears together with that very [wind].

body.text: vivartakalpaṃ vistareṇa vaktukāma āha. tathā hi samvṛtto loka iti vistaraḥ. tatheti yathā varṇitaṃ. tadeti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 322a] yadākāśe mandamandā vāyavaḥ spandante. tadā prabhṛti yad ayaṃ loko viṃśatim antarakalpān saṃvṛtto 'sthāt. tan niryātaṃ parisamāptaṃ vaktavyaṃ. tad upayātaṃ vaktavyam iti. tad ārabdhaṃ vaktavyam ity arthaḥ. yathoktakramavidhānam iti. yathoktena krameṇa vidhānena ca sarvaṃ jāyate. yathoktaḥ kramo vāyumaṇḍalaṃ apmaṇḍalam tataḥ kāṃcanamayī pṛthivī tataḥ sumervādayaś ceti. yathoktaṃ vidhānaṃ yasya yad vidhānam uktaṃ āyāmodvedhapariṇāhasaṃsthānalakṣaṇaṃ. tat tathā sarvaṃ jāyate. prathamaṃ tu brāhmam iti vistaraḥ. yat paścāt saṃvartate. tat pūrvaṃ vivartata iti sthitiḥ. tenāha. prathamaṃ tu brāhmaṃ vimānam utpadyate. tato yāvad yāmīyam iti. yāvacchabdena brahmavimānānantaraṃ paranirmitavaśavartivimānaṃ tadanaṃtaraṃ nirmāṇarativimānaṃ tato 'nantaraṃ yāvad yāmīyaṃ vimānam utpadyate. tato yāmīyavimānotpattyanantaraṃ vāyumaṇḍalādīnīti. yad uta bhājanavivartanyeti na sattvavivartanyeti darśayati. śūnye brāhme vimāne utpadyata iti mahābrahmā. anye 'pi ca sattvā iti tadparivārāḥ. tataś cyutvā brahmapurohiteṣv iti. tata ābhāsvarebhyaḥ. tan niryātaṃ bhavatīti. tad vivartanaṃ lokasya parisamāptaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: Wishing to explain the evolution-<s>kalpa</s> (<s>vivartakalpa</s>) in detail, he says: 'For thus the world having dissolved' — and so forth in detail. 'Thus' means: as described. 'That' — and so forth in detail. When in space, gentle breezes begin to stir, from that point onward, this world stood evolved over twenty intermediate <s>kalpa</s>s — that is to be stated as concluded, as completed. 'That is to be stated as commenced' means: that [evolution] has begun and is to be stated — this is the meaning. 'Arrangement in the stated order' (<s>yathoktakramavidhāna</s>) — everything arises according to the stated order and arrangement. The stated order is: wind-circle, water-circle, then golden earth, then <s>Sumeru</s> and the rest. The stated arrangement is: whatever arrangement has been stated for each — in terms of length, height, circumference, shape, and characteristics — everything arises exactly so. 'But first the <s>Brahma</s> [palace]' — and so forth in detail. What dissolves last evolves first — this is the principle. Therefore he says: first the <s>Brahma</s> palace arises, then [others] up to the <s>Yāma</s> palace. By the word 'up to,' after the <s>Brahma</s> palace, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> palace, then the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> palace, then successively up to the <s>Yāma</s> palace arises. Then after the arising of the <s>Yāma</s> palace, the wind-circle and the rest — this shows that it pertains to vessel-evolution, not being-evolution. In the empty <s>Brahma</s> palace, <s>Mahābrahmā</s> arises. 'And other beings also' — his retinue. 'Then, having passed away from there, among the <s>Brahmapurohita</s>s' — meaning: from the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> [heaven]. 'That is concluded' — meaning: that evolution of the world is completed.

body.text: tad upayātaṃ bhavatīti. ārabdhaṃ vivṛttāvasthānam ity arthaḥ. ekānnaviṃśatir antarakalpā aparimitāyuṣām [Tib. 322b] iti. eko 'ntarakalpo brahmalokavimānādibhājananirvṛttyātikrānta iti ekonaviṃśatir avaśiṣṭā antarakalpā aparimitāyuṣāṃ mānuṣyāṇāṃ atikrāmanti ā narakasattvaprādurbhāvāt. sā ca vivartamānāvasthātikrāntā evāvagantavyā. prādurbhūte nārake sattve vivṛttāvasthā prārabdhā. seyam ucyate. aparimitāyuṣām eva hrasatāṃ yāvad daśavarṣāyuṣām eko vivṛttavasthāntarakalpaḥ. tenāha. so 'sau vivṛttānāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ prahamāntarakalpa iti. tato 'ṣṭādaśa
body.translated_text: 'That is commenced' — meaning: the period of the evolved state (<s>vivṛttāvasthāna</s>) has begun. 'Nineteen intermediate <s>kalpa</s>s of those with immeasurable lifespans' — one intermediate <s>kalpa</s> has passed with the completion of the vessel-world beginning with the <s>Brahma</s>-realm palace, and the remaining nineteen intermediate <s>kalpa</s>s of humans with immeasurable lifespans pass until the appearance of hell-beings. And this should be understood as having passed during the evolving state (<s>vivartamānāvasthā</s>). When a hell-being appears, the evolved state (<s>vivṛttāvasthā</s>) has begun. This is stated as follows: one intermediate <s>kalpa</s> of the evolved state consists of those with immeasurable lifespans decreasing until those with ten-year lifespans. Therefore he says: 'That is the first intermediate <s>kalpa</s> of those who are evolved and abiding.' Then eighteen

body.text: tatas tu
body.translated_text: Then

body.text: iti. viṃśatyantarakalpaparimāṇā vivṛttavasthāvagantavyā.
body.translated_text: Thus the evolved state is to be understood as having a measure of twenty intermediate <s>kalpa</s>s.

body.text: paṃcaskaṃdhasvabhāvaḥ kalpaḥ
body.translated_text: 'A <s>kalpa</s> has the nature of the five aggregates' (<s>pañcaskandhasvabhāva</s>) —

children.translated_text: 'They are indeed time (<s>adhvan</s>) and topics of discourse (<s>kathāvastu</s>)' —

body.text: iti. muktakam iti. na caturāgamāntargatam ity arthaḥ. aṣṭkaṃ madhyād
body.translated_text: thus. '<s>Muktaka</s>' means: not included within the four <s>āgama</s>s — this is the meaning. 'Eight [positions] from the middle

body.text: vismṛtam iti. aṣṭau sthānāni kvāpi pradeśe pramuṣitatvāt na paṭhitāni. tenātra dvāpaṃcāśāt sthānāni bhavaṃti. ṣaṣṭyā ca saṃkhyāsthānair bhavitavyaṃ. tāny aṣṭakāni svayaṃ kānicin nāmāni kṛtvā paṭhitavyāni. yena ṣaṣṭisaṃkhyāsthānāni paripūrṇāni bhaveyuḥ. asaṃkhyā iti. asaṃkhyeyāḥ. saṃkhyānenāsaṃkhyeyāḥ asaṃkhyā iti. bahuvacananirdeśād anuktā api taddhitā bhavaṃti. yady evaṃ
body.translated_text: have been forgotten' — eight positions have not been recited because they were forgotten in some passage. Therefore here there are fifty-two positions. And there should be sixty numerical positions. Those eight should be recited by making up some names oneself, so that the sixty numerical positions would be complete. '<s>Asaṃkhya</s>' means: innumerable (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>). By enumeration, the innumerable ones are <s>asaṃkhya</s> — thus. Because of the plural usage, even the unstated secondary derivatives (<s>taddhita</s>) apply.

body.text: iti katham uktaṃ. naiṣa doṣaḥ. nāsti saṃkhyāpareṇaiṣv iti asaṃkhyāḥ asaṃkhyeyāḥ kalpāḥ. asaṃkhyāś cāsaṃkhyāś ca asaṃkhyāś ceti asaṃkhyāḥ. teṣāṃ trayaṃ. teṣāṃ kalpānāṃ asaṃkhyatrayodbhavatīti
body.translated_text: if so, how is this stated? There is no defect. Those in which there is no further counting are <s>asaṃkhya</s>s, incalculable <s>kalpa</s>s. Incalculable and incalculable and incalculable — [these are] the incalculables. The triad of those — of those <s>kalpa</s>s, 'arising from three incalculables' —

body.text: buddhatvam
body.translated_text: <s>Buddhahood</s> (<s>buddhatva</s>) —

body.text: iti evaṃ tad vyākhyātavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus it is to be explained.

body.text: tasyābhimatatvād iti. tasya parārthasyābhimatatvāt. yo hy abhimataḥ. sa svārtho dṛṣṭa iti. [Tib. 323a] taddhetor iti. ātmasnehahetoḥ. ātmasnehaṃ tebhya iti vistaraḥ. ātmasnehaṃ tebhyaḥ svāsāṃtānikebhyaḥ saṃskārebhyo nivartya apekṣāṃ karuṇālakṣaṇāṃ vardhayitvā taddhetor apekṣāhetor duḥkhāny udvahantīti saṃbhāvyaṃ pratipattavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Because of its being desired by him' — because of the desirability of benefit for others (<s>parārtha</s>). For what is desired is seen as one's own purpose. 'Because of that cause' — because of the cause of self-love. 'Self-love from those' — and so forth in detail. Having turned self-love away from those formations belonging to one's own continuum, and having increased concern characterized by compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), 'because of that cause' — because of the cause of concern — 'they bear sufferings' — this is to be considered and understood.

children.translated_text: 'The middle one [seeks] only the cessation of suffering' —

body.text: pratyekabuddhaḥ śrāvako duḥkhanivṛttim eva mokṣam eva prārthayate.
body.translated_text: The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> and the <s>Śrāvaka</s> seek only the cessation of suffering, only liberation.

body.text: sāṃsārikaṃ. kutaḥ.
body.translated_text: worldly [happiness]. Why?

children.translated_text: Because that is the abode of suffering —

body.text: yasmāt tat sāṃsārikaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhasthānaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: because that worldly happiness becomes the ground of suffering.

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ
body.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> —

children.translated_text: through sufferings in his own continuum, [seeks] the happiness of others —

body.text: ābhyudayikaṃ.
body.translated_text: the worldly prosperity (<s>ābhyudayika</s>) [of others].

children.translated_text: And the complete cessation of suffering alone —

body.text: niḥśreyasasvabhāvāṃ pareṣāṃ prārthayate. atha vā
body.translated_text: having the nature of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), he seeks [this] for others. Or alternatively,

body.text: ābhyudayikanaiḥśreyasikaṃ prārthayate.
body.translated_text: both worldly prosperity and the highest good — he seeks [for others].

children.translated_text: And the complete cessation of suffering alone —

body.text: buddhalakṣaṇām ātmīyāṃ parahitakriyopāyabhūtāṃ prārthayate. kasmād ity āha.
body.translated_text: characterized by <s>Buddhahood</s>, his own [cessation], which is the means for accomplishing the welfare of others — he seeks. Why? He says:

children.translated_text: 'Because he himself suffers from their suffering' —

body.text: iti. yasmāt paraduḥkhaiḥ. sa bodhisattvo duḥkhī bhavati. ata eva sukhaṃ dviprakāraṃ prārthayata iti.
body.translated_text: thus. Because by the sufferings of others, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes one who suffers. For this very reason he seeks happiness of two kinds.

body.text: (III.93) apakarṣasyādhastād iti vistaraḥ. varṣaśatasyādhastāt paṃca kaṣāyā abhyutsadā bhavanti. abhyadhiko bhavantīty arthaḥ. varṣaśate 'py utsadā na tv abhyutsadā yathādhastāt. āyuḥkaṣāya iti. kiṭṭabhūtaṃ pratyavaraṃ kaṣāyaḥ. āyur eva kaṣāya āyuḥkaṣāyaḥ. evaṃ kalpakaṣāyādayaḥ. yathākramam iti. jīvitavipattir āyuḥkaṣāyeṇa. upakaraṇavipattiḥ kalpakaṣāyeṇa. dhānyapuṣpaphalauṣadhādīny upakaraṇāni alparasavīryavipākaprabhāvāni. hi tāni bhavaṃti. naiva vā bhavaṃti. dvābhyāṃ kuśalapakṣavipattir [Tib. 323b] iti. kleśakaṣāyeṇa dṛṣṭikaṣāyeṇa ca kuśalapakṣasya vipattiḥ. katham ity āha. kāmasukhallikātmaklamathānuyogādhikārād iti. kāmasukham eva kāmasukhallikā. kāmasukhalīnateti vā kāmatṛṣṇā vā kāmasukhallikā yayā kāmasukhe sajyate. ātmaklamatha ātmopatāpaḥ ātmapīḍety arthaḥ. kāmasukhallikātmaklamathayor anuyogo 'nusevanaṃ. tasyādhikāraḥ. tasmāt. tad uktaṃ. kāmasukhallikānuyogam ātmaklamathānuyogaṃ vādhikṛtyārabhya kleśadṛṣṭikaṣāyābhyāṃ kuśalapakṣavipattir bhavatīti. evaṃ tāvad aviśeṣeṇa. gṛhipravrajitapakṣayor vā. gṛhipakṣasya kleśakaṣāyeṇa kuśalapakṣavipattiḥ. pravrajitapakṣasya dṛṣṭikaṣāyeṇa. yathākramaṃ kāmapradhānā gṛhiṇaḥ dṛṣṭipradhānāḥ pravrajitā iti. ekeneti sattvakaṣāyeṇa.
body.translated_text: (III.93) 'Below the decrease' — and so forth in detail. Below one hundred years, the five corruptions (<s>kaṣāya</s>) become greatly prevalent. They become excessive — this is the meaning. Even at one hundred years they are prevalent, but not as greatly as below [that lifespan]. 'Lifespan-corruption' (<s>āyuḥkaṣāya</s>) — <s>kaṣāya</s> means dregs, inferior. Lifespan itself as corruption is lifespan-corruption. Similarly for <s>kalpa</s>-corruption and the rest. 'Respectively' — the calamity of life [corresponds to] lifespan-corruption; the calamity of resources [corresponds to] <s>kalpa</s>-corruption — grains, flowers, fruits, herbs, and the rest, the resources, become of little flavor, potency, and effect; indeed they become [so], or they do not exist at all. 'Through two, the calamity of the wholesome class' — through affliction-corruption (<s>kleśakaṣāya</s>) and view-corruption (<s>dṛṣṭikaṣāya</s>) there is the calamity of the wholesome class. How? He says: 'because of the predominance of the pursuit of sensual pleasure and self-mortification.' Sensual pleasure itself is <s>kāmasukhallikā</s>; or being attached to sensual pleasure [is <s>kāmasukhallikā</s>]; or craving for sensual pleasure is <s>kāmasukhallikā</s>, by which one is attached to sensual happiness. Self-mortification (<s>ātmaklamatha</s>) means self-affliction, self-torment — this is the meaning. The pursuit (<s>anuyoga</s>) means the repeated practice of sensual pleasure and self-mortification. Its predominance — therefore. That is stated: because of undertaking the pursuit of sensual pleasure or the pursuit of self-mortification, through affliction-corruption and view-corruption there is the calamity of the wholesome class. Thus far in general. Or in the classes of householders and renunciants: for the householder class, the calamity of the wholesome class is through affliction-corruption; for the renunciant class, through view-corruption — respectively, because householders are predominantly [subject to] desire and renunciants are predominantly [subject to] views. 'Through one' — through being-corruption (<s>sattvakaṣāya</s>).

body.text: dvividhā hi pratyekabuddhā iti. yasmād vargacāriṇo 'pi pratyekabuddhāḥ śrāvakapūrviṇo bhavaṃti. na kevalaṃ khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpāḥ. tasmād utkarṣe 'pi teṣām utpattir na virudhyate. ye hi utpāditasrotaāpattiphalasakṛdāgāmiphalāḥ aṃtarhite buddhaśāsane svayam arhattvam adhigacchaṃti. te vargacāriṇaḥ. te ca pūrvabuddhotpādakāla eva prākṛtasamvegatvān na punaḥ samvejanīyā iti. tadīryāpathasaṃdarśanād iti. pratyekabuddheryāpathasaṃdarśanāt paryaṃkabandhasamādhirūpasaṃdarśanāt. na cāryās santaḥ kaṣṭāni tapāṃsi tapyerann [Tib. 324a] iti. satyadarśanakāla eva śīlavrataparāmarśadṛṣṭeḥ prahīṇatvāt. śīlavrataparāmarśapūrvakatvāc ca kaṣṭatapaḥkriyāyāḥ. khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpā iti. yathā khaḍgaviṣāṇā advitīyā bhavaṃti. evaṃ te gṛhasthapravrajitaiḥ anyaiś ca pratyekabuddhair asaṃsṛṣṭavihāriṇa iti. khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpā ity ucyante.
body.translated_text: For <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s are of two kinds. Since even the group-dwelling (<s>vargacārin</s>) <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s have prior training as <s>Śrāvaka</s>s, not only the rhinoceros-horn-like ones (<s>khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpa</s>). Therefore, even at the height [of the teaching], their arising is not contradicted. Those who, having produced the fruits of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>) and once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), attain <s>Arhatship</s> by themselves when the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching has disappeared — they are the group-dwellers (<s>vargacārin</s>). And they, already in the time of a previous <s>Buddha</s>'s arising, being of ordinary spiritual urgency (<s>prākṛtasaṃvega</s>), need not be further stirred to urgency. 'From seeing the deportment of those' — from seeing the deportment of <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s, from seeing the form of cross-legged meditation (<s>paryaṅkabandhasamādhi</s>). 'And being noble, they would not practice harsh austerities' — because at the very time of seeing the truths, the view of clinging to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśadṛṣṭi</s>) has been abandoned, and because the practice of harsh austerities is preceded by clinging to rules and rituals. 'Rhinoceros-horn-like' (<s>khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpa</s>) — just as rhinoceros horns are singular, so too they dwell without association with householders, renunciants, and other <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s — thus they are called 'rhinoceros-horn-like.'

body.text: iti. kalpaśatakṛtabodhihetur ity arthaḥ. ata eva vyācaṣṭe. mahākalpānāṃ
body.translated_text: thus. The meaning is: one whose cause of awakening has been cultivated over a hundred <s>kalpa</s>s. For this very reason he explains: of great <s>kalpa</s>s

body.text: śataṃ bodhisaṃbhāreṣu śīlasamādhiprajñālakṣaṇeṣu caritaḥ kṛtaprayoga iti. śakyaṃ ca tair iti vistaraḥ. athāpi te pratisaṃvitprāptā na bhaveyuḥ. tathāpi taiḥ praṇidhijñānena pūrvabuddhānām anuśāsanam anusmṛtya dharmo deśayituṃ śakyate. ṛddher āviḥkaraṇād iti. ākāśagamanādikāyāḥ sattvānugrahārthaṃ prakāśanāt. nāpi sattvānām abhavyatvāt. dharmaṃ na deśayantīti vākyaśeṣaḥ. kasmād ity āha. tathā hīti vistaraḥ. yasmād dhi laukikavītarāgās tadānīṃ saṃvidyaṃte. tasmāl lokottaravītarāgā api saṃbhaveyur ity abhiprāyaḥ. yady ete na hetavo dharmadeśanāyā akaraṇe. kas tarhi hetur ity āha. kiṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. pūrvābhyāsavaśena asaṃsargābhyāsavaśenālpotsukhatādhimuktatvāt. tatkṛtarucitvād ity arthaḥ. gaṇaparikarṣaṇaprasaṃgaparihārārthaṃ ca notsahante gaṃbhīradharmagrahaṇāya pareṣāṃ vyāpartuṃ. tathā vyāpāre hi sati gaṇaḥ parikraṣṭavyaḥ syāt. gaṇaparikarṣaṇaprasaṃgaṃ punaḥ [Tib. 324b] kasmāt pariharanti. vyākṣepasaṃsargabhīrutvāt. vyākṣepasaṃsargābhyāṃ bhīrutvāt. vyākṣepo 'bhipretasamādhyādikarmaṇy apravṛttiḥ. saṃsargo 'nyasaṃparkaḥ. vyākṣepasaṃsargabhīrutvaṃ punaḥ pūrvābhyāsavaśāt.
body.translated_text: a hundred — one who has practiced, who has made effort in the requisites of awakening (<s>bodhisaṃbhāra</s>) characterized by morality (<s>śīla</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). 'And it is possible for them' — and so forth in detail. Even if they have not attained the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), still, through their resolution-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>), recollecting the instructions of former <s>Buddha</s>s, they are able to teach the <s>Dharma</s>. 'From the manifestation of supernatural power' — from making manifest the bodily [powers] such as traveling through the sky, for the benefit of beings. 'Nor because of the incapacity of beings' — the remainder of the sentence is: they do not teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Why? He says: 'For thus' — and so forth in detail. Since those with mundane dispassion (<s>laukikavītarāga</s>) exist at that time, therefore those with supramundane dispassion (<s>lokottaravītarāga</s>) too should be possible — this is the intent. If these are not the reasons for not teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, then what is the reason? He says: 'What then' — and so forth in detail. Through the force of previous habituation — through the force of habituation to non-association, because of being inclined toward little zeal (<s>alpotsukhatā</s>). The meaning is: because of having a taste formed by that. And in order to avoid the occasion of leading a group, they do not exert themselves to engage others in grasping the profound <s>Dharma</s>. For if they were to so engage, a group would have to be led. Why then do they avoid the occasion of leading a group? Because of fear of distraction and association — fear of both distraction and association. Distraction is non-engagement in the intended activities of meditation (<s>samādhi</s>) and the like. Association is contact with others. And the fear of distraction and association is due to the force of previous habituation.

body.text: (III.94, 95) eṣa prājñaptika iti prajñaptiśāstranirdeśaḥ. caturvidhās cakravartina iti. sūtre tu suvarṇacakravarty evoktaḥ prādhānyāt. asthānaṃ vartamānakālāpekṣayā. anavakāśaḥ anāgatāpekṣayā. anāgate 'py adhvani saṃbhavāt yugapad dvayor iti. apūrvācaramāv iti.naikaḥ pūrvo nāparaḥ paścāt. kiṃ tarhi. sahety arthaḥ. samasama iti vīpsā. atha vā samaiḥ sarvasattveṣu buddhair bhagavadbhiḥ sama iti samasamaḥ. tāvato 'nabhisaṃskāreṇeti. tāvato lokadhātor anābhogena darśanāt. nikāyāntarīyā iti mahāsāṃghikaprabhṛtayaḥ. na caikatreti lokadhātau. puruṣāyuṣam iti. puruṣasyāyuḥ puruṣāyuṣaṃ. tad bibhrateti vartate. idam indriyam iti śraddhādi. asyāṃgasyeti. asya pratyayasya. kim idam ekaṃ lokadhātum adhikṛtyeti. ekacāturdvīpakaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ vā lokadhātum adhikṛtyaitad uktam ity abhiprāyaḥ. cakravartino 'pi ceti vistaraḥ. asthānam anavakāśo yad apūrvacaramau dvau tathāgatau loka utpadyeyātām iti nānena vacanena lokadhātvantarotpādapratiṣedhaḥ. tathāgatānāṃ tathoktatvāt. [Tib. 325a] tadyathā cakravartināṃ. cakravartino 'pi hi tathoktāḥ. asthānam anavakāśo yad apūrvacaramau dvau cakravartinau loka utpadyeyātām iti. janāḥ prākṛtamanuṣyāḥ. manuṣyāś tu matimantaḥ. śastrāṇy āvahanti utkṣipanti. gṛhapatiratnaṃ kośādhyakṣajātīyaḥ. pariṇāyakaratnaṃ balādhyakṣajātīyaḥ. tadsambandhajātīyam iti. tena
body.translated_text: (III.94, 95) 'This is designational' — this is the exposition according to the <s>Prajñaptiśāstra</s>. 'Wheel-turning monarchs (<s>cakravartin</s>) are of four kinds' — but in the <s>sūtra</s>, only the gold-wheel-turning monarch is mentioned, because of preeminence. 'Impossible' — with reference to the present time. 'No occasion' — with reference to the future. 'Even in the future period, two simultaneously' — thus. 'Neither first nor last' — not one first and not another afterward. What then? The meaning is: simultaneously. '<s>Samasama</s>' — this is a repetitive [compound]. Or alternatively, <s>samasama</s> means equal to <s>Buddha</s>s who are equal toward all beings. 'Without volitional effort for that extent' — from seeing that extent of the world-system (<s>lokadhātu</s>) without deliberate effort. 'Those of other schools' (<s>nikāyāntarīya</s>) — the <s>Mahāsāṃghika</s>s and others. 'Not in one' — world-system. 'A human lifespan' (<s>puruṣāyuṣam</s>) — the life of a person. 'It bears that' — is the verb. 'This faculty' — faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the rest. 'Of this factor' — of this condition. 'Is this said with reference to one world-system?' — the intent is: is this said with reference to a single four-continent [system] or a three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system? 'Of a <s>cakravartin</s> also' — and so forth in detail. 'It is impossible, there is no occasion that two <s>Tathāgata</s>s, neither first nor last, should arise in the world' — by this statement there is no negation of arising in another world-system, because <s>Tathāgata</s>s are spoken of thus. Just as with <s>cakravartin</s>s — for <s>cakravartin</s>s too are spoken of thus: 'It is impossible, there is no occasion that two <s>cakravartin</s>s, neither first nor last, should arise in the world.' 'People' — ordinary humans. 'But humans of intelligence.' 'They take up weapons' — they raise [weapons]. The householder-jewel is of the class of a treasury superintendent. The general-jewel (<s>pariṇāyakaratna</s>) is of the class of a military superintendent. 'Of the class related to that' — by that

body.text: cakravartinā sambaddhaḥ. tatsaṃbaddhasya tatsaṃbandhena vā samvartanaṃ tasmai hitaṃ tadanukūlaṃ tatsambaddhasamvartanīyam iti. yena sattvena karmopacitaṃ. tasminn utpanne cakravartini. svāny evainaṃ sattvaṃ karmāṇy utpādayanti. na tu sattvaś cakravartikuśalavipākotpattipratyayabhāvam āpadyate. sa ca kuśalavipākaś cakravartina evety avagantavyaṃ. deśasthatarāṇīti abhraṣṭasthānāni. uttaptatarāṇi prabhāsvarāṇi. saṃpūrṇatarāṇi akhaṇḍarūpāṇi. cakravartirājaprastāvenedaṃ vicāryate.
body.translated_text: <s>cakravartin</s>, connected. That which is conducive to the benefit of one connected with that, conducive through connection with that — this is 'conducive to one connected with that.' By whichever being <s>karma</s> has been accumulated, when that <s>cakravartin</s> has arisen, it is that being's own <s>karma</s>s that produce [the results]. But the being does not become a condition for the arising of the wholesome fruition of the <s>cakravartin</s>. And that wholesome fruition should be understood as belonging to the <s>cakravartin</s> alone. 'More locally situated' — meaning: not fallen from their positions. 'More radiant' — luminous. 'More complete' — unbroken in form. This is examined in the context of the discussion of the <s>cakravartin</s> king.

body.text: (III.96) kiṃ khalu yāvat sarājakā iti. rūpāvacarā ivāsann ity asyārthasya pratipādanāya sūtram ānayati. sūtra uktam iti vistaraḥ. dṛśyarūpatvād rūpiṇaḥ. upapādukatvān manomayāḥ. hastapādatadaṃgulyādyupetatvāt sarvaṃgapratyaṃyopetaḥ. samagrendriyatvāt avikalāḥ. kāṇavibrāntādyabhāvād ahīnendriyāḥ. darśanīyasaṃsthānatvāt śubhāḥ. ramaṇīyavarṇatvāt varṇasthāyinaḥ. ādityādiprabhānapekṣatvāt svayaṃprabhāḥ. karmarddhisaṃyogenākāśacaratvāt vihāyasaṃgamāḥ. kavaḍīkārāhārānapekṣatvāt [Tib. 325b] prītibhakṣāḥ. prītyāhārā iti paryāyau. tathā dīghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhantīti. madhusvādurasa iti. madhuna iva svāduraso 'sya rasa iti. ayoniśomanaskārasya grāhabhūtasya grāsatāṃ gatānāṃ sattvānāṃ kāma eva grahaḥ. tenāveśas tasyāraṃbha iti. sāyamāśārtham iti. aparahṇabhojanārthaṃ. prātarāśārtham iti. prātarbhojanārtham. saṃnidhikāraḥ saṃgrahaḥ. kṣetrāṇi vibhajya akṛṣṭoptena śālinā tadvṛttikalpanāt. kṣatriyādisaṃjñānāṃ nairuktena vidhinā siddhiḥ.
body.translated_text: (III.96) 'Is it indeed the case that as long as [they are] with a king?' — in order to demonstrate this meaning, that they were as if of the Form Realm (<s>rūpāvacara</s>), he adduces a <s>sūtra</s>. 'It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>' — and so forth in detail. 'Having visible form' (<s>rūpin</s>) — because of being of visible material form. 'Mind-made' (<s>manomaya</s>) — because of being spontaneously born (<s>upapāduka</s>). 'Endowed with all limbs and minor limbs' — because of being furnished with hands, feet, fingers, and the rest. 'Complete in faculties' (<s>avikala</s>) — because of having all faculties complete. 'With undiminished faculties' — because of the absence of being one-eyed, mad, and the like. 'Beautiful' (<s>śubha</s>) — because of having an attractive bodily form. 'Of lasting complexion' (<s>varṇasthāyin</s>) — because of having a pleasing color. 'Self-luminous' (<s>svayaṃprabha</s>) — because of not depending on the light of the sun and the like. 'Moving through the sky' (<s>vihāyasaṃgama</s>) — because of traveling through the sky through the connection with <s>karma</s>-based supernatural power. 'Feeding on joy' (<s>prītibhakṣa</s>) — because of not depending on solid food (<s>kavaḍīkārāhāra</s>). 'Nourished by joy' (<s>prītyāhāra</s>) — these are synonyms. 'Long-lived, they endure for a long period of time.' '<s>Madhusvādurasa</s>' — one whose taste is sweet like honey (<s>madhu</s>). Through improper attention (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>), which has become a seizing force, of beings who have come to be seized — desire itself is the seizing. By that comes possession; its onset.
