This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the first material basis of meritorious action, of great fruit, up to great extent, possessing which, for a son of good family — in detail — up to: merit constantly arises. Furthermore, <s>Cunda</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family establishes a dwelling in that very monastery. This is the second material basis of meritorious action, of great fruit, up to: merit constantly arises. Furthermore, <s>Cunda</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family provides bedding and seats in that very dwelling — namely, gives a bed, a chair, a cushion, a bolster, a round pillow, and a square [cushion]. This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the third material basis of meritorious action, as before. Furthermore, <s>Cunda</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family establishes a permanent alms-offering in that very dwelling, a favorable sacrifice. This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the fourth material basis of meritorious action, of great fruit, as before. Furthermore, <s>Cunda</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family gives gifts to newcomers and to those departing. This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the fifth material basis of meritorious action, as before. Furthermore, <s>Cunda</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family gives gifts to the sick or to those attending the sick. This is the sixth material basis of meritorious action, as before. Furthermore, <s>Cunda</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family — when there are cold spells, heat waves, wind storms, or rain storms — during such cold spells up to rain storms, provides food, refreshments, or rice-gruel drinks and offers them to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, [saying]: 'May the Noble Ones, with bodies not wet, with robes not rained upon, partake of this and dwell in comfort and ease.' This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the seventh material basis of meritorious action, of great fruit, up to: merit constantly arises. For a faithful son or daughter of good family endowed with these seven material bases of meritorious action, it is not possible to take the measure of the merit — 'this much merit, or this much fruit of merit, or this much ripening of merit.' Rather, because of the abundance of merit, it goes into the reckoning of a great mass of merit

gacchatīty evamādi. dvir apy āyuṣmān mahācundo bhagavantam etad avocat. labhyaṃ bhadanta niraupadhikaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu prajñapayituṃ mahāphalaṃ yāvan mahāvaistārikaṃ. labhyaṃ cundeti bhagavāṃs tasyāvocat. saptemāni cunda [Tib. 12a] niraupadhikāni puṇyakriyāvastūni. yaiḥ samanvāgatasya śrāddhasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhitur vā carato vā tiṣṭhato vā vistareṇa yāvad upajāyata eva puṇyaṃ. katamāni sapta. iha cunda śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā śṛṇoti tathāgataṃ vā tathāgataśrāvakaṃ vā amukaṃ grāmakṣetram upaniśritya viharatīti. śrutvā ca punar adhigacchati prītiprāmodyam udāraṃ kuśalaṃ naiṣkramopasaṃhitaṃ. idaṃ cunda prathamaṃ niraupadhikaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu pūrvavat. yāvad upajāyata eva puṇyaṃ. punar aparaṃ cunda śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā śṛṇoti tathāgataṃ vā tathāgataśrāvakaṃ vā udyuktam āgamanāya. śrutvā ca punar adhigacchatīti pūrvavat. idaṃ cunda dvitīyaṃ niraupadhikaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu. punar aparaṃ cunda śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā
vā śṛṇoti tam eva tathāgataṃ vā tathāgataśrāvakaṃ vā adhvānamārgapratipannaṃ tad eva grāmakṣetram anuprāptaṃ. śrutvā ca punar adhigacchatīti pūrvavat. idaṃ cunda tṛtīyaṃ niraupadhikaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu. yāvad upajāyata eva puṇyaṃ. [Tib. 12b] punar aparaṃ cunda śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā śṛṇoti tathāgataṃ vā tathāgataśrāvakaṃ vā tad eva grāmakṣetram anuprāptaṃ. śrutvā ca punar adhigacchatīti pūrvavat. idaṃ cunda caturthaṃ niraupadhikaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu pūrvavat. yavad upajāyata eva puṇyaṃ. punar aparaṃ śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tam eva tathāgataṃ vā tathāgataśrāvakaṃ vā darśanāyopasaṃkrāmati. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ adhigacchatīti pūrvavat. idaṃ cunda pañcamaṃ niraupadhikaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu. punar aparaṃ cunda śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tasyaiva tathāgatasya vā tathāgataśrāvakasya vā antikād dharmaṃ śṛṇoti. śrutvā ca punar adhigacchatīti. pūrvavat. idaṃ cunda ṣaṣṭhaṃ niraupadhikaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu. punar aparaṃ śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tasyaiva tathāgatasya vā tathāgataśrāvakasya vā antikād dharmaṃ śṛṇoti. śrutvā ca buddhaśaraṇaṃ gacchati dharmaśaraṇaṃ gacchati saṃghaśaraṇaṃ gacchati. śikṣāpadāni ca pratigṛhṇāti. idaṃ cunda saptamaṃ niraupadhikaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu mahāphalam iti pūrvavat. bahugranthabhayān na sarvaṃ likhitaṃ. na hy ājñāpanavijñapteḥ karmapatha upayujyate. tasya prāṇātipātādikarmaṇo 'kṛtatvāt. syān mataṃ. kṛte tasmin karmaṇi tadājñāpanavijñapteḥ [Tib. 13a] karmapatho bhaviṣyatīti. atra idam ucyate. kṛte 'pi ca tasyāḥ svabhāvāviśeṣād iti. pareṇa kṛte 'pi tasmin
body.translated_text: — and so forth. A second time too, the venerable <s>Mahācunda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Is it possible, Venerable Sir, to designate a non-material (<s>niraupadhika</s>) basis of meritorious action, of great fruit, up to great extent?' 'It is possible, <s>Cunda</s>' — thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke to him. 'There are, <s>Cunda</s>, seven non-material bases of meritorious action, possessing which, for a faithful son or daughter of good family, whether walking or standing — in detail — up to: merit constantly arises. What are the seven? Here, <s>Cunda</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family hears that the <s>Tathāgata</s> or a disciple of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is dwelling near a certain village or district. Having heard, one experiences an exalted, wholesome joy and gladness connected with renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>). This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the first non-material basis of meritorious action, as before, up to: merit constantly arises. Furthermore, <s>Cunda</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family hears that the <s>Tathāgata</s> or a disciple of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is engaged in coming. Having heard, one experiences [joy] — as before. This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the second non-material basis of meritorious action. Furthermore, <s>Cunda</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family hears that the very same <s>Tathāgata</s> or disciple of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having set out on the road, has reached that very village or district. Having heard, one experiences [joy] — as before. This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the third non-material basis of meritorious action, up to: merit constantly arises. Furthermore, <s>Cunda</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family hears that the <s>Tathāgata</s> or a disciple of the <s>Tathāgata</s> has reached that very village or district. Having heard, one experiences [joy] — as before. This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the fourth non-material basis of meritorious action, as before, up to: merit constantly arises. Furthermore, a faithful son or daughter of good family approaches that very <s>Tathāgata</s> or disciple of the <s>Tathāgata</s> for an audience. Having seen, one experiences [joy] — as before. This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the fifth non-material basis of meritorious action. Furthermore, <s>Cunda</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family hears the <s>Dharma</s> from that very <s>Tathāgata</s> or disciple of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having heard, one experiences [joy] — as before. This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the sixth non-material basis of meritorious action. Furthermore, a faithful son or daughter of good family hears the <s>Dharma</s> from that very <s>Tathāgata</s> or disciple of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having heard, one goes to the <s>Buddha</s> for refuge, goes to the <s>Dharma</s> for refuge, goes to the <s>Saṃgha</s> for refuge, and accepts the training rules. This, <s>Cunda</s>, is the seventh non-material basis of meritorious action, of great fruit — as before. Not everything has been written, for fear of excessive length. For the action-path (<s>karmapatha</s>) does not apply to the informative expression (<s>vijñapti</s>) of a command. Because that action of killing and the rest has not been performed [by the commander]. One might think: when that action has been performed [by the agent], the action-path will apply to the informative expression of the command. To this it is said: even when performed, because of no difference in its intrinsic nature — even when that

body.text: karmaṇi tasyā ājñāpanavijñapter na kaścit svabhāvaviśeṣo 'sti. yena tadānīṃ karmapathaḥ syāt. tasmāt pūrvavat. tasyāḥ svabhāvāviśeṣāt. yathaiva pūrvavat karmapatho na vyavasthāpyate. tathaiva paścād ity ato 'stīty abhyupagantavyā yāsau tadānīm utpadyate karmapathasaṃgṛhīteti. ekādaśabhir āyatanair asaṃgṛhītam iti. dharmāyatanavarjyaiḥ. vākkarmāntājīvānām ayogād iti. vijñaptisvabhāvānām evāsaṃbhavād ity arthaḥ. yat tarhīdam uktam iti vistaraḥ. ko 'syabhisaṃbandhaḥ. yadi vā mataṃ. yady avijñaptir na syād aṣṭaṃgo 'yaṃ mārgo na syāt. tatra vijñaptyayogāt. tasmād asty avijñaptir iti. yat tarhīdam uktam iti vistareṇoktvā yāvat samyaksamādhir iti kim artham evam ucyate. pūrvam eva cāsyeti sarvaṃ. mārgasya samāpattikālāt pūrvam ity arthaḥ. vijñaptirūpās ta uktā ity abhiprāyaḥ. vaibhāṣikāḥ pariharanti. laukihamārgavairāgyam iti vistaraḥ. laukikamārgavairāgyāvasthāyāṃ vāgādisvabhāvaṃ [Tib. 13b] vijñāptirūpam. etad abhisaṃdhāyaitad uktaṃ. na tu mārgakāle tatsaṃgṛhītaṃ vāgādyavijñaptirūpaṃ nāstīti.
body.translated_text: action has been performed by another, there is no intrinsic difference in that informative expression of the command by which it could then be an action-path. Therefore, as before — because of no difference in its intrinsic nature. Just as before, an action-path is not established [for it], so too afterward — therefore the <s>avijñapti</s> (non-informative form) must be accepted, which arises at that time and is included in the action-path. 'Not included in the eleven sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>)' — excluding the <s>dharmāyatana</s>. 'Because of the non-application of vocal action, bodily action, and livelihood' — meaning: because of the impossibility of those having the nature of <s>vijñapti</s> (informative form). 'But then what has been stated' — and so forth in detail. What is the connection of this? If it is the view that: if <s>avijñapti</s> did not exist, this eightfold path would not exist, because of the non-application of <s>vijñapti</s> therein, therefore <s>avijñapti</s> exists — then having stated 'but then what has been stated' in detail, up to 'right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>)' — why is this said? 'And previously, all of this' — meaning: prior to the time of entering the path. The intent is: they have been stated as having the form of <s>vijñapti</s>. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s defend [this]. 'Dispassion through the mundane path' — and so forth in detail. In the state of dispassion through the mundane path, there is <s>vijñapti</s>-form having the nature of speech and the like. With reference to this, that statement was made — but it is not the case that at the time of the path, there is no <s>avijñapti</s>-form included in that [path] having the nature of speech and the like.

body.text: samādhiviṣayarūpam iti. samādher ālambanam asthisaṃkalādi. deśanāvaraṇād apratigham iti. yad rūpaṃ deśam āvṛṇoti. tat pratighaṃ. viparyayād apratigham iti siddhaṃ. katham idānīṃ tad rūpam iti. yadi na rūpayituṃ śakyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. etad avijñaptau samānaṃ. avijñaptir api vā deśaṃ nāvṛṇotīti tulyaṃ. anāsrave samādhau anāsravam iti. mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkurvāṇo yogācāras tadrūpam āśayaṃ cāśrayaṃ ca pratilabhate. yat samyagdṛṣṭivad anāsravaṃ śīlaṃ pratilabhate. yasmin sati prakṛtiśīlatāyāṃ saṃtiṣṭhate. atha vā. anāsrave 'pi samādhau tad evaṃvidhaṃ rūpaṃ ta ācāryā icchanti. arhato yad rūpaṃ bāhyaṃ cety apara iti. apara ācāryā varṇayanti. arhato yad rūpaṃ cakṣurāyatanādi. bāhyaṃ ca kāṣṭhakuḍyādi. tad anāsravaṃ rūpaṃ. kutaḥ. āsravāṇām aniśrayatvāt. na hy arhatsāṃtānikaṃ rūpaṃ bāhyaṃ cāsravāṇāṃ kleśānāṃ niśraya iti. yady evaṃ yat tarhy aviśeṣeṇa sūtra uktaṃ sāsravā dharmāḥ katame. yāvad eva ckaṣur yāvad eva rūpāṇīti [Tib. 14a] vistaraḥ. tat punar āsravāṇām apratipakṣatvāt sāsravam uktaṃ. cittacaittaviśeṣā hi āsravapratipakṣa iti. paryāyeṇa tarhīti vistaraḥ. tad evārhato rūpaṃ bāhyaṃ cāsravāṇām apratipakṣatvāt sāsravam āsravāṇām aniśrayatvād anāsravam iti. tathā ca laksaṇasaṃkaraḥ syād iti doṣaḥ. yāni rūpāṇīti. yāni rūpāṇy āyatanānīty arthaḥ. vistareṇa yāvad ye dharmāḥ sāsravāḥ sopādānīyāś cetaḥkhilamrakṣavastv iti vacanāt. santy anāsravāṇi rūpāyatanānīti. tāni punaḥ katamāni sāsravāṇi sopādānīyāni.
body.translated_text: 'Form that is the object of concentration' (<s>samādhiviṣayarūpa</s>) — the object of concentration is [things like] skeletal visualizations (<s>asthisaṃkalā</s>) and the like. 'Non-resistant because of obstructing location' (<s>deśanāvaraṇāt apratigha</s>) — that form which obstructs a location is resistant (<s>pratigha</s>); the opposite is non-resistant — this is established. 'How then is it form?' — the intent is: if it cannot be shaped. 'This is the same for <s>avijñapti</s>' — <s>avijñapti</s> too does not obstruct a location, so the objection is equal. 'In the uncontaminated concentration, it is uncontaminated' — a practitioner (<s>yogācāra</s>) who brings the path face to face obtains form of that [uncontaminated] nature, as well as a disposition and a basis. The uncontaminated morality (<s>śīla</s>) he obtains, like right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), [is uncontaminated]. When that exists, he becomes established in natural morality (<s>prakṛtiśīlatā</s>). Or alternatively, even in uncontaminated concentration, those teachers accept such form. 'The form of an <s>Arhat</s> that is external too — according to others' — other teachers explain. The form of an <s>Arhat</s> — eye-base (<s>cakṣurāyatana</s>) and the rest — and external [form] — wood, walls, and the like — that is uncontaminated form. Why? Because it is not a support for the contaminants (<s>āsrava</s>). For neither the form belonging to an <s>Arhat</s>'s continuum nor external [form] is a support for the contaminants, the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). If so, then what about the statement made without distinction in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'What are the contaminated <s>dharma</s>s? All the way up to the eye, all the way up to forms' — and so forth in detail? That is said to be contaminated because of not being the antidote to the contaminants. For it is specific mental states and mental factors that are the antidote to the contaminants. 'Then by implication' — and so forth in detail. That very form of an <s>Arhat</s> and external [form], because of not being the antidote to the contaminants, is contaminated; because of not being a support for the contaminants, is uncontaminated — thus. And then there would be the defect of confusion of characteristics. 'Which forms' — meaning: which form-bases (<s>rūpāyatana</s>). In detail, up to: 'which <s>dharma</s>s are contaminated, with clinging, are objects of mental obstruction and attachment' — from this statement, there exist uncontaminated form-bases. And which then are those contaminated, with clinging?

body.text:
pṛthagjanarūpāṇi. āsravāṇāṃ niśrayatvāt tadapratipakṣatvāc ca. katamāny anāsravāṇi. yāny arhato rūpāṇi bāhyāni ca. āsravāṇām aniśrayatvāt. dharmatā hy eṣeti. dharmāṇām anādikālikā śaktiḥ. guṇaviśeṣād iti. dhyānāpramāṇādiguṇaviśeṣāt. anugrahaviśeṣāc ceti. śarīrasya varṇabalādiviśeṣāt. tadālambaneti vistaraḥ. sapratigrāhakam ālambanam asyāḥ. seyaṃ tadālambanā dānacetanā. [Tib. 14b] tayā paribhāvitāḥ saṃtatayaḥ sūkṣmaṃ pariṇāmaviśeṣaṃ phalotpattinimitaṃ prāpnuvanti. kathaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. bahutaraphalābhiniṣpattaye kathaṃ bhaviṣyatīty abhiprāyaḥ. na hy atra dātṝṇāṃ dāyāḥ paribhujyante. yatparibhogāt bhoktṝṇāṃ guṇaviśeṣād anugrahaviśeṣāc cānyamanasām api dātṝṇām iti vistareṇa yāvat samarthā bhavaṃti. yāvad upajāyata eva puṇyam iti vā. tadālambanecetanābhyāsād iti. tathāgatatacchrāvakālambanacetanābhyāsāt. saṃtatayaḥ sūkṣmaṃ pariṇāmaviśeṣaṃ prāpnuvanti. yenāyatyāṃ bahutaraphalābhiniṣpattaye samarthā bhavanti. caratas tiṣṭhato jāgrato yuktam evaṃ svapatas tu katham ity ata āha. svapneṣv api tāś cetanā anuṣaṅgiṇyo bhavantīti. avijñaptivādinas tu vaibhāṣikasya niraupadhike puṇyakriyāvastuni yatra vijñaptir nāsti. kevalaṃ taṃ śrutvādhigacchati prītiprāmodyam udāraṃ kuśalaṃ. tatra katham avijñaptiḥ syāt. tasya śrotur vijñaptisamādhyor asaṃbhavāt. avijñaptir hi vijñapteḥ samādher vā saṃbhavet. aupadhikeṣv apīti vistaraḥ. ārāmadānādiṣv [Tib. 15a] api. tadālambanacetanābhyāsāt. pratigrāhaka ālambanam asyāś cetanāyā iti pūrvavat. āha. yady aupadhikeṣv api evam abhīkṣṇaṃ tadālambanacetanābhyāsāt. yat tarhi sūtram iti vistaraḥ. apramāṇaṃ cetaḥsamādhiṃ iti. maitryādisaṃprayuktaṃ. cetanāviśeṣa iti. etadālambanacetanasyāpi dāyakasyāpramāṇaḥ puṇyabhiṣyando 'stīti darśayati. kriyāphalaparisamāptāv iti. maulakarmapathaprayogaḥ kriyā. maulakarmapathaḥ phalaṃ tasya parisamāptau. eṣa eva nyāya iti. svayaṃprayogeṇa pareṣām upaghātaviśeṣāt kartuḥ sūkṣmaḥ saṃtatipariṇāmaviśeṣo jāyata iti sarvaṃ. kārye kāraṇopacārād iti. saṃtatipariṇāmaviśeṣaḥ karmapatho bhavatīti saṃtatipariṇāmaviśeṣaḥ kāryaṃ. karmapathaḥ kāraṇaṃ. yo 'sau kāyavācoḥ prayogaḥ. sa hi cetanālakṣaṇasya karmaṇaḥ panthā iti. tasmin kārye karmapatha iti kāraṇopacāraḥ. kāyikavācikatvaṃ
tu tasya saṃtatipariṇāmaviśeṣasya. tatkriyāphalatvāt. kāyavākkriyāyāḥ phalatvād ity arthaḥ. yathā avijñaptivādinām avijñaptir [Tib. 15b] iti. yathā vaibhāṣikāṇām avijñaptivādinām avijñaptiḥ karmapatha ity ākhyāyate. kārye kāraṇopacārāt. kāyikavācikatvaṃ tu tatkriyāphalatvād iti. avijñaptir
body.translated_text: the forms of ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) — because of being a support for the contaminants, and because of not being their antidote. Which are uncontaminated? The forms of an <s>Arhat</s> and external [forms] — because of not being a support for the contaminants. 'For this is the nature of things' (<s>dharmatā</s>) — the beginningless potency of <s>dharma</s>s. 'Because of a special quality' — because of a special quality such as <s>dhyāna</s>, the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), and the rest. 'And because of a special benefit' — because of a special quality of the body such as complexion, strength, and the rest. 'Having that as its object' — this is the elaboration. That which has a recipient as its object. This giving-volition (<s>dānacetanā</s>) has that as its object. [Tib. 14b] By it, the mental continuums that have been cultivated attain a subtle special transformation that is the cause of the production of fruit. 'How will it come about?' — the intent is: how will the production of greater fruit come about? For here, the gifts are not enjoyed by the donors. From the enjoyment of which, because of the special qualities and special benefits of those who enjoy [the gifts], even for donors whose minds are otherwise occupied — in detail — up to: they become capable. Or up to: merit indeed arises. 'From the repeated practice of volition having that as its object' — from the repeated practice of volition having the <s>Tathāgata</s> and his disciples as its object, the continuums attain a subtle special transformation, by which they become capable of producing greater fruit in the future. For one walking, standing, or waking, this is appropriate — but how about one sleeping? Therefore he says: 'Even in dreams, those volitions are consequent.' But for the proponent of <s>avijñapti</s>, [the objection is raised] against the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>: in the non-material basis of meritorious action (<s>niraupadhika puṇyakriyāvastu</s>), where there is no <s>vijñapti</s> (informative form) — one merely hears and attains an exalted, wholesome joy and gladness — how could there be <s>avijñapti</s>? Because of the impossibility of both <s>vijñapti</s> and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) for that hearer. For <s>avijñapti</s> could arise from <s>vijñapti</s> or from <s>samādhi</s>. 'Even in the material [bases of merit]' — this is the elaboration — even in the giving of gardens [Tib. 15a] and the rest. From the repeated practice of volition having that as its object. A recipient is the object of this volition — as before. He says: 'If even in the material [bases], thus, through frequent repeated practice of volition having that as its object' — 'but then what about the <s>sūtra</s>' — this is the elaboration. 'Immeasurable mental concentration' — associated with loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and the rest. 'A special volition' — this shows that even for the donor whose volition has that as its object, there is an immeasurable overflow of merit. 'At the completion of the action and its result' — the preliminary of the principal action-path is the action; the principal action-path is the result; at the completion of that. 'This is the same principle' — all [the following]: through one's own effort, because of a special harm to others, a subtle special transformation of the continuum arises for the agent. 'Through figurative transfer from cause to effect' — the special transformation of the continuum is the action-path, [expressed] figuratively. The special transformation of the continuum is the effect; the action-path is the cause — that is, the exertion of body and speech. For that is the path of action characterized by volition (<s>cetanā</s>). Through figurative transfer to that effect of the [term] 'action-path' as cause. The bodily and vocal nature of that special transformation of the continuum is because of being the result of that action — the result of bodily and vocal action, is the meaning. 'Just as for the proponent of <s>avijñapti</s>, the <s>avijñapti</s>' — [Tib. 15b] just as for the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s who are proponents of <s>avijñapti</s>, the <s>avijñapti</s> is called an action-path — through figurative transfer from cause to effect; and its bodily and vocal nature is because of being the result of that action — the <s>avijñapti</s>

body.text: adravyam iti prakārāntareṇa darśayan bhadanta āha. upātteṣu skandheṣv iti vistaraḥ. sattvasaṃkhyāteṣu vartamāneṣu skandheṣu trikālayā cetanayā prāṇātipātāvadyena spṛśyate ghātaka iti. kathaṃ trikālayety āha. haniṣyāmi hanmi hatam iti cāsya yadā bhavatīti. tad evam atra cetanaiva karmety uktaṃ bhavati. ācāryo bhadantamataṃ kenacid bhāgenābhipretaṃ kenacid bhāgenānabhipretaṃ darśayann āha. na tv iyateti vistaraḥ. yadi kaścid evaṃ prayojayet. manmātaraṃ mārayeti. uccalite ca mārake tasyaivaṃ bhavet. hatā tena manmāteti. tasya hatābhimānina ānantaryakarma syāt. na ceṣyate. tasmāt svayaṃ ghnann iti bhadantena viśeṣyaṃ vaktavyam. tat evāha. svayaṃ tu ghnata iti vistaraḥ. etāvāṃś cetanāsamudācāra iti. haniṣyāmi hanmi hatam iti. yuktarūpa iti. yukta eva yuktarūpa iti. svārthe rūpapratyayaḥ. nāmadheyavat. [Tib. 16a] yathā nāmaiva nāmadheyam ity eke vyācakṣate. praśastarūpo yuktarūpaḥ. yuktaṃ vā rūpaṃ svabhāvo 'syeti yuktarūpaḥ. tathaivasaṃjñāyamāna iti. yathaivāvijñaptir duravabodhā. tathaiva saṃtatipariṇāmaviśeṣo 'pīti. cittānvayakāyaprayogeṇeti. cittapūrvakeṇa kāyaprayogeṇety arthaḥ. tābhyāṃ pṛthagbhūtam iti. cittakāyābhyāṃ pṛthagbhūtaṃ. yatkṛtaprayogasaṃbhūteti. yena kṛto yatkṛtaḥ. yatkṛtāt prayogāt saṃbhūtā. kriyāparisamāptiḥ karmapathaparisamāptiḥ. tasyaiva cittacaittasya prayoktus tannimittas tatprayoganimittaḥ saṃtatipariṇāmo bhavatīti. bhavati paritoṣo 'smākam iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. cittacaittasaṃtānāc cāyatyāṃ phalotpatteḥ. nāvijñaptiḥ. kiṃ. bhavati paritoṣa iti vartate. vijñaptyabhāvād ity evamādīni. samutthāpakasya dharmasyābhāvāt samutthāpyasya dharmasyābhāva ity arthaḥ. avijñaptir dravyato nāstīti sādhitam etat. ādiśabdenābhyupetyākaraṇamātratvāt. atītāni mahābhūtāny [Tib. 16b] upādāya prajñapteḥ. teṣām avidyamānatvādi. tad evāstu. dharmāyatanaparyāpannam iti. yad dhyāyināṃ samādhiviṣayarūpaṃ samādhiprabhāvād utpadyata ity uktaṃ tad dhy anidarśanaṃ cāpratighaṃ ca. aṃga tāvad ācakṣeti. aṃgāprātilomya iti paṭhyate. hanta tāvad ācakṣeti. ehi tāvad ācakṣety artha ity apare. ato nimitta iti vistaraḥ. yata evam. ato nimitte 'vijñaptau naimittikopacārāt. samyagādyupacārāt. avijñaptau tadā vyākriyate. samyagvākkarmantājīvākhyā kriyata ity arthaḥ. āśayaṃ cāśrayaṃ ceti. āśayaḥ prāṇātipātādyakaraṇāśayaḥ. śraddhādyāśayo vā. āśraya āśrayaparāvṛttiḥ.
body.translated_text: is not a real substance — showing this through another mode, the venerable teacher says: 'In the appropriated aggregates' — this is the elaboration. In the aggregates belonging to a sentient being, in the presently existing aggregates, one is touched by the sin of taking life through volition of the three times — as a killer. How is it through volition of the three times? He says: 'When one has [the thought] "I will kill, I am killing, and I have killed."' Thus here, volition alone is action — this is what is stated. The master, showing that the venerable teacher's view is accepted in some part and not accepted in some part, says: 'But not only this much' — this is the elaboration. If someone were to instigate thus: 'Kill my mother.' And when the killer has set out, that one would think: 'He has killed my mother.' For that one who has the conceit of having killed, there would be an immediate-retribution <s>karma</s> (<s>ānantaryakarma</s>) — and this is not accepted. Therefore the venerable teacher should add the qualification 'killing by oneself.' He says just that: 'But when killing oneself' — this is the elaboration. 'This much is the operation of volition' — namely: 'I will kill, I am killing, I have killed.' 'Fitting' (<s>yuktarūpa</s>) — 'fitting' means simply 'fitting.' The suffix <s>rūpa</s> is used in its own sense, like in the word '<s>nāmadheya</s>' [Tib. 16a] — just as some explain that '<s>nāmadheya</s>' means simply 'name.' A praiseworthy form is <s>yuktarūpa</s>. Or: that whose form, whose nature, is fitting — that is <s>yuktarūpa</s>. 'Being equally hard to understand' — just as <s>avijñapti</s> is hard to understand, so too is the special transformation of the continuum. 'Through bodily exertion that follows upon mind' — through bodily exertion that is preceded by mind, is the meaning. 'Separate from those two' — separate from mind and body. 'Born from the effort made by that one' — by whom the effort was made — of that one; born from the effort made by that one — the completion of the action, the completion of the action-path. Of that very mind-and-mental-factor, the agent's, caused by that, caused by that effort — a transformation of the continuum arises. 'We are satisfied' — this is the rest of the sentence. And because of the production of fruit in the future from the continuum of mind and mental factors — not <s>avijñapti</s>. What? 'We are satisfied' — this is continued. 'Because of the absence of <s>vijñapti</s>' and so forth — because of the absence of the <s>dharma</s> that gives rise [to it], the absence of the <s>dharma</s> that is given rise to, is the meaning. <s>Avijñapti</s> does not exist as a real substance — this has been established. By the word 'and so forth,' [the following arguments are included]: merely because of non-performance; because of being designated in dependence on past great elements [Tib. 16b]; because of their non-existence — and the rest. 'Let that be so' — 'included in the <s>dharmāyatana</s>' — the form that is the object of concentration for meditators (<s>dhyāyin</s>), which arises through the power of concentration — that is indeed non-visible and non-resistant. 'Please explain' — this is read as '<s>aṃgāprātilomya</s>' [i.e., 'not contrary']. 'Please explain' means: come now, explain. Others say: come, explain — this is the meaning. 'Therefore from the cause' — this is the elaboration. Since this is so, therefore, with respect to the indicator (<s>nimitta</s>), namely <s>avijñapti</s>, through figurative transfer from the indicated to the indicator — through figurative transfer of right [speech] and so forth — <s>avijñapti</s> is then designated. The designation of right speech, right action, right livelihood is made — this is the meaning. 'Both the disposition and the basis' — the disposition (<s>āśaya</s>) is the intention of non-killing and the rest, or the disposition of faith and the rest. The basis (<s>āśraya</s>) is the transformation of the basis.

body.text:
ato nimitte āśaye āśraye ca naimittikopacāraṃ. samyagvāgādyupacāraṃ kṛtvāṣṭau mārgāṃgāni vyavasthāpyanta iti. tad akriyāmātram iti. mithyāvāgādyakriyāmātraṃ. katamat tad ity āha. yad asāv iti vistaraḥ. yady akriyāmātram aṃgaṃ kathaṃ tad anāsravam ity āha. tac cānāsravamārgasaṃniśrayalābhād anāsravam iti. yady akriyāmātram aṃgaṃ. tathādravyasat. katham aṣṭāv aṃgāni bhavantīty āha. na hi sarvatreti [Tib. 17a] vistaraḥ. vidhipūrvam iti. śīlagrahaṇavidhipūrvaṃ. anyacitto na saṃvṛtaḥ syād iti cet. yadi sā cetanā saṃvaraḥ. tasmāc cetanācittād anyacitto na saṃvṛtaḥ syāt. yathā cetanā yā kāyavācau saṃvṛṇoti nāsau tadānīm astīti. na tadbhāvanayeti vistaraḥ. naitad evaṃ. tadbhāvanayā cittasaṃtānabhāvanayā kriyākāle prāṇātipātādicitte pratyupasthite smarataḥ ahaṃprāṇātipātādibhyaḥ prativirata iti pratyupasthitasmṛteḥ. tatpratyupasthānād yayā cetanayā kāyavācau saṃvṛṇoti. tasyāḥ sammukhībhāvāt. ityartham eva tasyāḥ samādānam iti. katham.
ayam akriyāpratijñām anusmṛtya dauḥśīlyaṃ na kuryād iti. na kaścin muṣitasmṛtiḥ śikṣāṃ bhidyād iti. yāsāv avijñaptiḥ setubhūtā dauḥśīlyaṃ pratibadhnāti. sā tadānīṃ vidyata iti.
body.translated_text: Therefore, with respect to the indicator, the disposition, and the basis, having made figurative transfer from the indicated — having made figurative transfer of right speech and the rest — the eight path-factors are established. 'That is mere non-performance' — mere non-performance of wrong speech and the rest. What is that? He says: 'That which that one' — this is the elaboration. If mere non-performance is a path-factor, how is it uncontaminated? He says: 'And that is uncontaminated because of obtaining the support of the uncontaminated path.' If mere non-performance is a path-factor, and thus not a real substance, how are there eight factors? He says: 'For not everywhere' — [Tib. 17a] this is the elaboration. 'Preceded by the procedure' — preceded by the procedure of undertaking the precepts. 'If someone of a different mind were not restrained' — if that volition is the restraint, then someone whose mind is different from the volition-mind would not be restrained. 'Just as the volition that restrains body and speech does not exist at that time' — 'not by the cultivation of that' — this is the elaboration. This is not so. By the cultivation of that — by the cultivation of the mental continuum — at the time of action, when a mind [inclined toward] killing and the rest has arisen, for one who remembers: 'I am restrained from killing and the rest' — for one whose mindfulness has arisen — because of the arising of that [mindfulness], the volition by which one restrains body and speech becomes present. Therefore the undertaking of that [restraint] is for this very purpose: that this one, recollecting the vow of non-performance, would not commit misconduct. No one of confused mindfulness would break the training. That <s>avijñapti</s> which serves as a dike obstructs misconduct — at that time it exists.

body.text: (IV.5cd) na hi saiva sāmagrīti vistaraḥ. na saiva pṛthivīdhātvādīnāṃ mahābhūtānāṃ vijñaptyāśrayāṇāṃ sāmagrī sūkṣmaphalā cānidarśanāpratighavijñaptiphalatvāt audārikaphalā ca sanidarśanasapratighavijñaptiphalatvād yujyate. tasmād [Tib. 17b] anyāny eva mahābhūtāni upādāyāvijñaptir utpadyate.
body.translated_text: (IV.5cd) 'For not the same assemblage' — this is the elaboration. The same assemblage of great elements — earth-element and the rest — that are the support of <s>vijñapti</s> (informative form), is not reasonable as both producing a subtle result, because of being the result of non-visible, non-resistant <s>vijñapti</s>, and producing a gross result, because of being the result of visible, resistant <s>vijñapti</s>. Therefore [Tib. 17b] different great elements are the support from which <s>avijñapti</s> arises.

body.text: (IV.6ab) yadātanī vijñaptir iti vistaraḥ. yadābhavā vijñaptir yadātanī vijñaptiḥ. evaṃ tadātanāni mahābhūtāni. yatkālasaṃbhūtā vijñaptiḥ kiṃ tatkālasaṃbhūtāny eva mahābhūtāny upādāyāvijñaptir utpadyate. sarvam iti. sarvam upādāyarūpaṃ vijñaptir avijñaptir dhyānānāsravasaṃgṛhītā cakṣuḥśrotrarūpaśabdādi caivaṃ samānakālāny eva mahābhūtāny upādāya vartate. prāyeṇeti grahaṇaṃ kiṃcit kāmāvacaryavijñaptinirāsārthaṃ. ata evāha. kiṃcid vartamānam anāgataṃ atītāni mahābhūtāny upādāyeti. kiṃcid upādāyarūpaṃ vartamānam atītāni mahābhūtāny upādāya vartate. kiṃcid anāgatam upādāyarūpam atītāni mahābhūtāny upādāya vartate. kiṃ punas tad upādāyarūpaṃ yad evaṃ bhūtam iti darśayann āha.
body.translated_text: (IV.6ab) 'The <s>vijñapti</s> belonging to that time' — this is the elaboration. The <s>vijñapti</s> that does not exist, the <s>vijñapti</s> belonging to that time — thus the great elements belong to that time. The <s>vijñapti</s> that is produced at what time — is it only the great elements produced at that same time, in dependence on which, that <s>avijñapti</s> arises? 'All' — all derived form — <s>vijñapti</s>, <s>avijñapti</s>, that included in <s>dhyāna</s> and the uncontaminated [paths], and eye, ear, visible form, sound, and the rest — all of these exist in dependence on great elements of the same time. The word 'generally' is for the purpose of excluding certain <s>vijñaptis</s> belonging to the Desire Realm. Therefore he says: 'Something present [depends on] past great elements; something future [depends on] past great elements.' Some derived form that is present exists in dependence on past great elements. Some future derived form exists in dependence on past great elements. What derived form is of this nature? Showing this, he says:

children.translated_text: 'After the moment, <s>avijñapti</s> arises from past great elements belonging to the Desire Realm.'

body.text: kāmāvacarasamvarādigrahaṇakāle avijñaptiḥ sahajāni mahābhūtāny upādāyotpadyate. evam anyāpy avijñaptis tāny evopādāyotpadyate. yasmāt tāny asyā āśrayārthena saṃbhavanti. yathānyeṣām upādāyarūpāṇāṃ pratyutpannāni
body.translated_text: At the time of undertaking the Desire Realm restraint and the rest, <s>avijñapti</s> arises in dependence on the co-arisen great elements. Similarly, other <s>avijñapti</s> too arises in dependence on those very [great elements] — since those [great elements] serve as its support. Just as the present great elements are the support of other derived forms,

body.text: mahābhūtāny āśrayaḥ [Tib. 18a] evaṃ tasyā atītāny āśrayaḥ. pravṛttyanuvṛttikāraṇatvād yathākramam iti. atītāni mahābhūtāni pravṛttikāraṇatvāt ākṣepakāraṇatvāt āśrayārthena bhavanti. pratyutpannāni śarīramahābhūtāny anuvṛttikāraṇatvād adhiṣṭhānakāraṇatvāt saṃniśrayārthena bhavanti. cakrasyeveti vistaraḥ. yathā cakrasya pāṇyāvedhaḥ. evam asyāḥ pravṛttikāraṇaṃ. yathā bhūmipradeśaḥ. evam anupravṛttikāraṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: so too past [great elements] are the support of that [<s>avijñapti</s>] [Tib. 18a]. Because of being the cause of initiation and continuation, respectively. Past great elements serve as the support in the sense of being the cause of initiation, the cause of projection. Present great elements of the body serve as the support in the sense of being the cause of continuation, the cause of sustaining. 'Like a wheel' — this is the elaboration. Just as the thrust of the hand [is the cause of initiation] of a wheel, so too is the cause of initiation of this [<s>avijñapti</s>]. Just as the ground-surface [is the cause of continuation], so too is the cause of continuation.

body.text: (IV.6cd) kālaniyamam uktvā bhūminiyamaṃ pṛcchati. atha kutastyānīti vistaraḥ. yāvac caturthadhyānabhūmikam iti. ārūpyeṣu bhūtabhautikānām abhāvāt. dhātvapatitatvād iti. anāsravasya kāyavākkarmaṇo dhātvapratisaṃyuktatvāt. nāsti niyamata ity abhiprāyaḥ. anāsravāṇi tarhi mahābhūtāny upādāya kasmān na bhavatīty ata āha. anāsravāṇāṃ ca mahābhūtānām abhāvād iti. kiṃ punar asyā mahābhūtaiḥ kāryam ity ata āha. tadbalena cotpatter iti. mahābhūtabalena cotpatter ity arthaḥ. atha cittabalenaiva tadutpattiḥ kasmān na bhavati. anupādāyarūpatvaprasaṃgāt.
body.translated_text: (IV.6cd) Having stated the temporal restriction, he asks about the ground restriction. 'Now, from what [ground] do they belong?' — and so forth in detail. Up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground — because of the non-existence of primary and secondary elements in the formless realms (<s>ārūpya</s>). 'Because of not falling within a realm' (<s>dhātvapatitatva</s>) — because uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>) bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> is not connected with any particular realm. The intent is: there is no restriction. If so, why does it not arise dependent on uncontaminated great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>)? Therefore he says: 'because of the non-existence of uncontaminated great elements.' What function then do the great elements serve for it? Therefore he says: 'and because it arises through the power of those' — meaning: because it arises through the power of the great elements. Then why does it not arise through the power of mind alone? Because there would be the undesirable consequence of it being non-derived form (<s>anupādāyarūpa</s>).

body.text:
(IV.7, 8) avijñaptir anaupāttiketi.
amūrtatvāc cittacaittādhiṣṭhānabhāvāyogāt.
body.translated_text: (IV.7, 8) '<s>Avijñapti</s> is non-appropriated (<s>anaupāttika</s>)' — because of being immaterial (<s>amūrta</s>), and because it is not fitting to be governed by mind and mental factors.

children.translated_text: 'And it is of the outflow type (<s>naiṣyandikī</s>)' —

body.text: Tib. 18b
body.translated_text: because of being wholesome or unwholesome, it is not maturation-born (<s>vipākajā</s>) —

body.text: kuśalākuśalatvāt na vipākajā
iti vacanāt. vipākajasya cāvyākṛtatvād
body.translated_text: from this statement. And because what is maturation-born is indeterminate —

body.text: iti vacanāt. naupacayikī upacayābhāvāt. pāriśeṣyān naiṣyandikī.
body.translated_text: from this statement. It is not of the accumulation type (<s>aupacayikī</s>), because of the absence of accumulation. By elimination, it is of the outflow type.

body.text: sattvasaṃtānapatitatvāt.
body.translated_text: because it falls within the continuum of a being.

body.text: naiṣyandikopāttamahābhūtajā. samutthāpakacittāpekṣatvāt asamāhitacittavijñaptyadhikārāc ca. na svapnasamādhyādyaupacayikamahābhūtajā. ata eva ca na vipākajamahābhūtajā.
body.translated_text: born from outflow-type appropriated great elements. Because of depending on the originating mind, and because of belonging to the domain of informative action of non-concentrated mind — it is not born from the accumulation-type great elements of dreams, concentration, and the like. And for this very reason, it is also not born from maturation-born great elements.

body.text: vistaraḥ. sāsravānāsravasamādhijatvāt. dhyānānāsravajasamvarāvijñaptiḥ samādhijety ucyate. anupāttāni ca mahābhūtāny upādāyeti. samāhitacittavaśena tatra śarīre cittānuvṛttitvāt. upāttāni hi mahābhūtāni nirodhasamāpattyādyavasthāsu
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. Because it is born from contaminated and uncontaminated concentration. The <s>avijñapti</s> of restraint born from <s>dhyāna</s> and the uncontaminated [path] is called 'born from concentration.' 'And dependent on non-appropriated great elements' — because, through the power of concentrated mind, mind conforms to that body. For appropriated great elements, in states such as the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) and the like

body.text: cittam antareṇāpi vartante. yāvat saṃbhinnapralāpād iti. yāvacchabdenādattādānāt kāmamithyācārān [Tib. 19a] mṛṣāvādāt paiśunyāt pāruṣyāt saṃbhinnapralāpād iti. cittavat bhūtābhedāt. yathā tadutpādakaṃ cittam abhinnam. evaṃ bhūtāny api tadutpādakāny abhinnāny eva. na cādhārārthenāvijñapter mahābhūtāny āśrayaḥ. kiṃ tarhi. tatpravartanārthena. tasmād
body.translated_text: continue even without mind. Up to 'frivolous speech' (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>) — by the word 'up to': from taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, slander, harsh speech, and frivolous speech. 'Because of the non-division of elements, like mind' — just as the mind that produces them is undivided, so too the elements that produce them are undivided. And the great elements are not the support of <s>avijñapti</s> for the purpose of being a base. What then? For the purpose of its operation. Therefore —

body.text: vacanaṃ na virudhyati. prātimokṣasamvare tv anyānyānīti. acittānuparivartanīyatvāt. vijñaptis tu naiṣyandikīti. ākṣepavaśenānuvṛtteḥ. upāttā tu kāyikīti. na vācikīty arthaḥ. kāyikī hi kāyamahābhūtāvinirbhāgavartitvāt tadāśrayabhūtānām upāttā. na tu vācikī. tadvinirbhāgavartitvāt.
body.translated_text: this statement is not contradicted. 'But in the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint, they are different' — because of not conforming to mind. 'But <s>vijñapti</s> is of the outflow type' — because it continues through the force of impetus. 'But the appropriated [<s>vijñapti</s>] is bodily' — meaning: not vocal. For the bodily [<s>vijñapti</s>], because of operating inseparably from the great elements of the body, is appropriated by those that serve as its support. But not the vocal [<s>vijñapti</s>], because of operating separately from them.

body.text: atra codayanti. śāstraviruddham etad. evaṃ hy āha. yānīmāny upāsakasya pañca śikṣāpadāni. eṣāṃ katy upāttāni. katy anupāttāni. āha. sarvāṇy anupāttānīti. avijñaptilakṣaṇaśikṣāpadābhisaṃdhivacanād bāhulikatvād vā tathānirdeśasyety adoṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: Here they raise an objection: this contradicts the treatise (<s>śāstra</s>). For it says thus: 'Of the five training rules of a lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>), how many are appropriated and how many non-appropriated?' It answers: 'All are non-appropriated.' Because the statement refers to the training rules characterized as <s>avijñapti</s>, or because of that statement being general — there is no fault.

body.text: punaḥprabandhād avaibhāṣikīyam [Tib. 19b] iti. ekasaṃsthānotpattāv itarasaṃsthānānivṛtteḥ. kathaṃ vistareṇa yāvat saṃsthānadvayaṃ sidhyatīti. anyonyāvakāśadānāt. tanmahābhūtair abhivyāpanād iti. vijñaptyāśrayair mahābhūtair aṅgasyābhivyāpanāt. anabhivyāpane ca punar vijñaptimahābhūtaiḥ kathaṃ kṛtsnenāṃgena vijñāpayet. na hi śakyate vaktuṃ. kāyaikadeśenāsau vijñāpayati. na sarvakāyeneti. vijñaptyāśrayāṇi mahābhūtāni tadaṃgaṃ na vyāpyāvatiṣṭhanta iti. suṣiratvāt kāyasyāsti teṣām avakāśa iti. abhivyāpane 'pi na mahīyasāṅgena bhavitavyaṃ. suṣiratvena kāyānupraveśāt. pīnena tarhi guruṇā vā tenāṃgena na bhavitavyaṃ. sūkṣmatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'From renewed continuity, it is non-<s>Vaibhāṣika</s>' — because when one configuration arises, another configuration does not cease. How then — in detail — up to: is the duality of configuration established? Through mutual accommodation. 'Through pervading by those great elements' — through the pervading of a limb by the great elements that are the support of <s>vijñapti</s>. And if there is no pervading, how could one inform with the entire limb through the great elements of <s>vijñapti</s>? For one cannot say: one informs with only a part of the body, not with the entire body. [One might say:] the great elements that are the support of <s>vijñapti</s> do not pervade that limb and remain — because the body has cavities, there is space for them. Even with pervading, the limb need not become larger — because they enter the body through its cavities. Then it should not become thicker or heavier — because of [their] subtlety.

children.translated_text: 'It has been stated as twofold, threefold, and fivefold' —
'Volition (<s>cetanā</s>) and what is done by it — that [is <s>karma</s>]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. dvividham uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: from this statement, it has been stated as twofold.

children.translated_text: 'Volition is mental <s>karma</s>; vocal and bodily <s>karma</s> are born from it' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. trividham uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: from this statement, it has been stated as threefold.

children.translated_text: 'Those two are informative and non-informative action (<s>vijñapti</s> and <s>avijñapti</s>)' —

body.text: iti. kāyavākkarmaṇo vijñaptyavijñaptitve bhedāt. cetanātmanaḥ karmaṇaś ca pañcasattvāt pañcavidham uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. Because of the division of bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> into informative and non-informative, and the five-ness of <s>karma</s> whose nature is volition — it has been stated as fivefold.

body.text: iti. [Tib. 20a] kuśalākuśalaivāvijñaptir ity arthād uktaṃ bhavati. balavat karmeti. avijñaptilakṣaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. It is implicitly stated that <s>avijñapti</s> is only wholesome or unwholesome. 'Powerful <s>karma</s>' — characterized by <s>avijñapti</s>.

body.text: apiśabdād iticaśabdārthenāpiśabdena kāma ity ākṛṣyate.
body.translated_text: by the word 'even' (<s>api</s>), with the meaning of the words 'and so forth,' the word 'even' draws in '<s>Kāma</s>.'

body.text: anāsravāvijñaptivad iti. yathā na ca tāvad anāsravāyā avijñapter anāsravāṇi mahābhūtāni. atha ca punar yasyāṃ bhūmau jātas tām utpādayati. tadbhūmikāni mahābhūtāny upādāyotpadyate. evaṃ na ca tāvad ārūpyāṇi mahābhūtāni syuḥ. atha ca punar yasyāṃ bhūmau jāta ārūpyām utpādayati. tadbhūmikāni mahābhūtāny upādāyārūpyāvacary avijñaptir bhaviṣyatīti. na. tasyā dhātvapatitatvād iti. nehāsāmyāt. yasmād avijñaptir anāsravā dhātvapatitā kāmarūpārūpyāvacarīti. tṛṣṇābhir asvīkṛtatvāt tasyā dhātuto bhūmito vā naiva sabhāgāni nāpi visabhāgāni mahābhūtāni bhavantīty ato yatrajātas tatrajāni mahābhūtāny upādāyotpadyate. ārūpyāvacarī tv avijñaptir nārhati kāmarūpāvacarāṇi visabhāgāni mahābhūtāny upādāya bhavituṃ. dhātupatitavād ity abhiprāyaḥ. kiṃ ca. sarvarūpavaimukhyāc cārūpyasamāpattir nālaṃ rūpotpattaye. rūpabhūmikā tv anāsravā samāpaṭtir alaṃ [Tib. 20b] rūpotpattaye 'vijñaptyutpattaye ity arthaḥ. kasmāt. sarvarūpavaimukhyād ity abhiprāyaḥ. kathaṃ cārūpyasamāpatteḥ sarvarūpaṃ vaimukhyam ity ato bravīti. vibhūtarūpasaṃjñatvād iti. vigatarūpasaṃjñatvād ity arthaḥ. dauḥśīlyapratipakṣeṇa śīlam iti vistaraḥ. dauḥśīlyaṃ kāmāvacaram akuśalasamutthānatvāt. tasya rūpabhūmikaṃ śīlam avijñaptilakṣaṇaṃ pratipakṣa iti yujyate. ārūpyāvacaram apy evaṃ bhaviṣyatīti ced ata āha. ārūpyāś ca kāmadhātor iti vistaraḥ. ārūpyāḥ kāmadhātoś catasṛbhir dūratābhir dūre. dūratvāc cārūpyasaṃgṛhītaṃ śīlaṃ kāmadhātupratipakṣe na kalpate. catasraś ca dūratā vyākhyātāḥ purastād iti na punar vyākhyāyante. pratipakṣadūratā cātrodāharaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Like uncontaminated <s>avijñapti</s>' — just as uncontaminated <s>avijñapti</s> does not have uncontaminated great elements, yet it produces [<s>avijñapti</s>] in whichever ground one is born and arises dependent on the great elements of that ground — similarly, just as there would not be formless-realm great elements, yet one born in whichever formless ground would produce [<s>avijñapti</s>] in that ground, and formless-realm <s>avijñapti</s> would exist dependent on the great elements of that ground. No — 'because of its falling within a realm' (<s>dhātvapatitatva</s>). The analogy does not hold here. Because uncontaminated <s>avijñapti</s> does not fall within any realm — it does not belong to the Desire, Form, or Formless Realm. Because it is not claimed by the cravings (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), it has neither similar nor dissimilar great elements with respect to any realm or ground — therefore it arises dependent on the great elements of whichever [ground] one is born in. But formless-realm <s>avijñapti</s> is not fitting to exist dependent on dissimilar great elements belonging to the Desire or Form Realm — because of falling within a [specific] realm, is the intent. Moreover, because of aversion to all form, the formless attainment is not capable of producing form — meaning: of producing <s>avijñapti</s>. But the uncontaminated attainment belonging to the Form Realm ground is capable of producing form — meaning: of producing <s>avijñapti</s>. Why? Because of aversion to all form — this is the intent. And how does the formless attainment have aversion to all form? Therefore he says: 'because of having transcended the perception of form' (<s>vibhūtarūpasaṃjñatva</s>) — meaning: because of having abandoned the perception of form. 'Morality (<s>śīla</s>) as the antidote to immorality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>)' — and so forth in detail. Immorality belongs to the Desire Realm, because of originating from the unwholesome. Morality characterized as <s>avijñapti</s> belonging to the Form Realm ground is its antidote — this is fitting. If one says: the formless-realm [morality] too would be so — therefore he says: 'and the formless [states] are far from the Desire Realm' — and so forth in detail. The formless [states] are far from the Desire Realm through four distances. And because of being far, morality included in the formless is not fit as an antidote to the Desire Realm. And the four distances have been explained previously, so they are not explained again. The distance of antidote is the example here.

body.text: iti. savicārayor eva bhūmyor ity avadhāraṇārtha āraṃbhaḥ. vitarkya vicārya vācaṃ bhāṣata iti vitarkavicārapūrvakatvāt kāyavākkarmaṇoḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. The emphasis is: in the two grounds with <s>vicāra</s> only. Because bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> are preceded by <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), since one deliberates and examines before speaking.

children.translated_text: 'Even in <s>Kāma</s> [Realm], the obstructed (<s>nivṛtā</s>) does not exist' —

body.text: na kevalam avicārāsu bhūmiṣv iti darśayati. brahmaloka evāstīty uktaṃ bhavati. tata ūrdhvam iti. brahmalokād ūrdhvaṃ. bāhyamahādhūtahetukam iti. vāyuprabhṛtīnāṃ [Tib. 21a] śabdāyatanaṃ. vijñaptiśabdapratiṣedhaparam etad vacanaṃ
body.translated_text: he shows: not only in the grounds without <s>vicāra</s>. It is stated that it exists only in <s>Brahmaloka</s>. 'Above that' — above <s>Brahmaloka</s>. 'Caused by external great elements' — the sound-base (<s>śabdāyatana</s>) of wind and the like. This statement is intended to negate <s>vijñapti</s>-sound

body.text: . na tu bāhyamahābhūtahetukam eva. pāṇyādyaṅgaśabdo 'pi hi dvitīyādiṣu dhyāneṣu saṃbhavati. anyathā hi śāstravirodhaḥ syāt. tathā hi śāstra uktaṃ. śabdadhātunā kaḥ samanvāgataḥ. āha. kāmarūpāvacaraḥ. ko 'samanvāgatah. āha. ārūpyāvacara iti. na hi bāhyenāsattvasaṃkhyātena samanvāgato yujyate.
body.translated_text: — but not [to say] that it is caused only by external great elements. For sound produced by limbs such as hands and the like is also possible in the second and other <s>dhyāna</s>s. Otherwise there would be a contradiction with the treatise. For in the treatise it is stated: 'Who possesses the sound-element (<s>śabdadhātu</s>)?' It answers: 'One belonging to the Desire and Form Realms.' 'Who does not possess it?' It answers: 'One belonging to the Formless Realm.' For it is not fitting to say one is 'possessed of' something external, not counted as a being.

children.translated_text: 'Possession and non-possession [apply to what] falls within one's own continuum' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. asyaiva ca doṣaparihārārtham anye punar āhur iti. dvitīyādiṣv api dhyāneṣu vijñaptir astīti. kiṃbhūmikā. prathamadhyānabhūmikā. vaibhāṣikapakṣa evāyaṃ. na pakṣāntaraṃ.
body.translated_text: from this statement. And for the purpose of avoiding this very fault, others say: <s>vijñapti</s> exists even in the second and other <s>dhyāna</s>s. Of what ground? Of the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. This is the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> position itself, not an alternative position.

children.text:
kāyākṣiśrotravijñānaṃ vijñaptyutthāpakaṃ ca yat
dvitīyādau tadā vyāptam akliṣṭavyākṛtaṃ ca tad
children.translated_text: 'Body-, eye-, and ear-consciousness, and that which produces <s>vijñapti</s> — in the second [<s>dhyāna</s>] and above, these are then pervading, and they are unobstructed-indeterminate' —

body.text: iti siddhāntāt. evaṃ tarhi dvitīyādidhyānabhūmikā bhavati pakṣāntaraṃ. sā tu kiṃ vyākṛtā utāvyākṛtety āha. anivṛtāvyākṛtā. na tu kuśalā na kliṣṭeti. parasparasaṃbhāṣaṇādikurvatāṃ tatastyānām avyākṛtā vijñaptir bhavati. [Tib. 21b kiṃkāraṇaṃ na kuśalā na kliṣṭāstīty āha. na hi teṣūpapanna iti vistaraḥ. na hi dvitīyādiṣu dhyāneṣūpapannaḥ tathājātīyaṃ kuśalakliṣṭajātīyam adhobhūmikaṃ cittaṃ saṃmukhīkaroti. yena cittena kuśalāṃ kliṣṭāṃ vā vijñaptiṃ samutthāpayet. kiṃkāraṇam iti āha. nyūnatvāt prahīṇatvāc ceti. kuśalam adhobhūmikaṃ nyūnatvān na saṃmukhīkaroti. prahīṇatvāc ceti na kliṣṭam. arthād etad uktaṃ bhavati. avyākṛtam adhobhūmikaṃ cittaṃ saṃmukhīkaroti. tena tāṃ samutthāpayatīti. etad uktaṃ bhavati. adhobhūmikena cittenordhvabhūmikā vijñaptir utthāpyata iti. tad evaṃ necchanti vaibhāṣikāḥ. prathamadhyānikaiva hi sā vijñaptiḥ prathamadhyānabhūmikacittasamutthāpitatvāt. tasmād āha. pūrvam eva tu varṇayantīti.
body.translated_text: from this established doctrine. If so, then it belongs to the second and other <s>dhyāna</s> grounds — [this would be] an alternative position. But is it determinate or indeterminate? He says: unobstructed-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛtā</s>) — not wholesome and not afflicted. For those born there who engage in mutual conversation and the like, the <s>vijñapti</s> is indeterminate. Why is there no wholesome or afflicted [<s>vijñapti</s>]? He says: 'For one born in those [grounds]' — and so forth in detail. For one born in the second and other <s>dhyāna</s>s does not bring face to face a mind of the type of wholesome or afflicted [mind] belonging to a lower ground, by which mind one would produce wholesome or afflicted <s>vijñapti</s>. What is the reason? He says: 'because of being inferior and because of being abandoned.' One does not bring face to face the wholesome [mind] of a lower ground because of its inferiority; nor the afflicted — because of its being abandoned. Implicitly this is stated: one brings face to face the indeterminate mind of a lower ground, and by that produces it [<s>vijñapti</s>]. This is what is stated: <s>vijñapti</s> belonging to a higher ground is produced by mind belonging to a lower ground. But the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s do not accept this. For that <s>vijñapti</s> belongs to the first <s>dhyāna</s> alone, because it is produced by mind belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. Therefore he says: 'But they explain it as before.'

body.text: tac ca kāmadhātāv iti. tac ca bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ nivṛtavyākṛtaṃ cittaṃ kāmadhātau nāsti. satkāyāntagrāhadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktam eva hi kāmadhātau nivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ cittam iṣyate. tena ca na vijñaptiḥ samutthāpyate. antarmukhapravṛttatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'And that [mind] does not exist in the Desire Realm' — that obstructed-indeterminate (<s>nivṛtavyākṛta</s>) mind, which is to be abandoned through meditation, does not exist in the Desire Realm. For in the Desire Realm, only the mind associated with the views of the self-existence (<s>satkāya</s>) and extreme (<s>antagrāha</s>) views is accepted as obstructed-indeterminate. And <s>vijñapti</s> is not produced by that [mind] — because of its inward-directed operation.

body.text: (IV.10cd, 11) svabhāvata ity ātmataḥ. paramakṣematvād iti. akṣemaleśānubandhabhāvāt. [Tib. 22a] yad dhi svabhāvasaṃprayogasamutthānataḥ kuśalaṃ na tat paramakṣemam ity uktaṃ bhavati. asaṃprayuktānāṃ kuśalatvābhāvād iti. kuśalamūlādibhir asaṃprayuktānāṃ caittādīnāṃ kuśalatvābhāvāt. tatsaṃprayogakuśalatvasiddhiḥ. tair eva kuśalamūlādisaṃprayuktair ity ādiśabdena hryapatrāpyayor grahaṇaṃ. auṣadhipānīyasaṃbhūtakṣīravad iti. pītauṣadhapānīyāyā
body.translated_text: (IV.10cd, 11) 'By own nature' means: by itself. 'Because of being supremely secure' (<s>paramakṣematva</s>) — because of not being followed by the slightest insecurity. For what is wholesome through own nature, association, or origination is not supremely secure — this is what is stated. 'Because of the absence of wholesomeness in those not associated [with wholesome roots]' — because of the absence of wholesomeness in mental factors and the like not associated with wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) and the rest. Thus the establishment of wholesomeness through association with those is proven. 'By those very [factors] associated with wholesome roots and the rest' — by the word 'and the rest,' modesty (<s>hrī</s>) and shame (<s>apatrāpya</s>) are included. 'Like milk produced from a medicinal drink' — [just as] for a [cow] that has drunk a medicinal drink

body.text: gor yat kṣīraṃ. tad auṣadhapānīyasaṃbhūtaṃ. prāptīnāṃ tv iti vistaraḥ. prāptīnāṃ kuśalānāṃ visabhāgacittasamutthāpitānāṃ. visabhāgaṃ cittaṃ kuśalād anyat. vicikitsayā kuśalamūlapratisaṃdhāne yāḥ kuśalānāṃ prāptayaḥ. tāsāṃ kuśalatvaṃ. na tāvat parinirvāṇavat paramārthakṣematvāt. nāpy alobhādivat svabhāvataḥ kuśalam atatsvabhāvatvāt. nāpi vedanādivat saṃprayogato viprayuktatvāt. nāpi samutthānatas tatsamutthānacittasya [Tib. 22b] kliṣṭatvāt. evaṃ punarbhavapratisaṃdhāv api upapattipratilaṃbhikakuśalaprāptayo vaktavyāḥ. kathaṃ tāsāṃ kuśalatvam iti vaktavyam etat. kartavyo 'tra yatna ity abhiprāyaḥ. atra pariharanti. kuśalamūlasamutthāpanīyatvād anāgatāvasthāyām eva tāḥ kuśalamūlā bhavanti. kliṣṭena cittena tatprāptivibandho 'panīyate. na tatkuśalatvam āpadyata iti.
body.translated_text: the milk of a cow — that is produced from medicinal water. 'But of the acquisitions (<s>prāpti</s>)' — and so forth in detail. Of the acquisitions of wholesome [dharmas] that are originated by dissimilar mind. Dissimilar mind is mind other than wholesome. When wholesome roots are reconnected through doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), the acquisitions of wholesome [dharmas] — their wholesomeness: it is not [wholesome] in the ultimate sense like <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, because of being ultimately secure. Nor is it wholesome by own-nature like non-attachment (<s>alobha</s>) and the rest, because of not having that nature. Nor is it wholesome through association like feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) and the rest, because of being dissociated [from mind]. Nor is it [wholesome] through origination, because the mind that originates it is afflicted. Similarly, regarding the rebirth-linking of renewed existence, the acquisitions of wholesome [dharmas] obtained through rebirth should be stated — how their wholesomeness [is established] should be explained. The intent is: effort should be made here. Here they resolve [the difficulty]: because those [acquisitions] are to be originated by wholesome roots, in their future state they are wholesome roots. By the afflicted mind, the obstruction to their acquisition is removed — [the afflicted mind] does not bring about their wholesomeness.

body.text: sarvaduḥkhapravṛttyātmakatveneti. sarvasya duḥkhasya pravṛttir ātmā svabhāvo 'syeti sarvaduḥkhapravṛttyātmakaḥ. tadbhāvena. paramārthenākṣemaḥ saṃsāraḥ. kāyavākkarmajātyādiprāptaya iti. kāyavākkarmāṇi vijñaptyavijñaptisvabhāvāny asamvaranaivasamvaranāsamvarasaṃgṛhītāni. jātyādayo jātijarāsthityanityatālakṣaṇālakṣaṇasvabhāvaḥ. prāptayo 'kuśalānāṃ. vyādhyapathyauṣadhādibhir upameyā iti. saṃsāro vyādhinopameyaḥ. vyādhisaṃsāra ity arthaḥ. lobhādīny apathyauṣadhenopameyāni. anyasaṃprayogasamutthānāpekṣatvāt. tatsaṃprayuktā apathyauṣadhimiśrapānīyena. kāyavākkarmajātyādiprāptayo [Tib. 23a] 'pathyauṣadhapānīyasaṃbhūtakṣīreṇopameyāḥ. evaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. yadi paramārthenākuśalaḥ saṃsāraḥ. na kiṃcit sāsravam avyākṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati kuśalaṃ vā. saṃsārābhyantaratvāt sāsravasya. paramārthata evam uktam iti abhyupagatam etat sarvaṃ saṃsāraparyāpannam akuśalam iti. vipākaṃ tu pratīti vistaraḥ. yad vipākaṃ prati na vyākriyate. savipākam etad iti. tad avyākṛtam ity ucyate. tad uktaṃ bhavati. yat sāsravaṃ. tad akuśalaṃ paramākṣematvāt. vipākaṃ praty avyākaraṇārthāvyākṛtam iti. kuśalam api. tathaivākuśalam. iṣṭavipākatvāt kuśalam ity avagantavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Because of having the nature of the operation of all suffering' — that whose nature (<s>ātman</s>), whose own-nature, is the operation of all suffering — that is one whose nature is the operation of all suffering. Through that state. In the ultimate sense, <s>saṃsāra</s> is insecure. 'Acquisitions of bodily action, verbal action, birth, and the rest' — bodily and verbal actions having the nature of informative and non-informative [action], included in non-restraint, neither-restraint-nor-non-restraint, and non-restraint. Birth and the rest — having the nature of birth, aging, persistence, impermanence, characteristic, and non-characteristic. Acquisitions of unwholesome [dharmas]. 'To be compared with disease, unwholesome medicine, and the like' — <s>saṃsāra</s> is to be compared with disease — meaning: disease-<s>saṃsāra</s>. Attachment (<s>lobha</s>) and the rest are to be compared with unwholesome medicine — because of dependence on the association and origination of others. Those associated with them [are compared] with water mixed with unwholesome medicine. Acquisitions of bodily action, verbal action, birth, and the rest are to be compared with milk produced from water [mixed with] wholesome medicine. 'If so then' — and so forth in detail. If <s>saṃsāra</s> is ultimately unwholesome, then nothing with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) would be indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) or wholesome — because the with-outflows is within <s>saṃsāra</s>. It is conceded that in the ultimate sense this is so — everything encompassed by <s>saṃsāra</s> is unwholesome. 'But with respect to retribution' — and so forth in detail. That which is not determined with respect to retribution — 'this has retribution' — that is called indeterminate. This amounts to saying: whatever has outflows is unwholesome because of ultimate insecurity; it is indeterminate in the sense of not being determined regarding retribution. And wholesome too — likewise unwholesome [in the ultimate sense]. Because of producing desirable retribution, it should be understood as wholesome.

body.text: yadi samuttānavaśād iti vistaraḥ. cetanāyā eva kuśalākuśalatvam ity anenābhiprāyeṇa. kāyavākkarmaṇaḥ kuśalākuśalatvaṃ vicārayati. kiṃ na mahābhūtānām iti. kuśalākuśalatvaṃ. kuśalākuśalena hi cittena kāyavākkarma tanmahābhūtāni samutthāpyate. vaibhāṣika āha. karmaṇi hi kartur abhiprāyo na mahābhūteṣu na mahābhūtāni kuryām iti. kiṃ tarhi. idaṃ karma kuryām iti. na karmavan mahābhūtānāṃ kuśalākuśalatvam iti. [Tib. 23b] ācārya āha.
body.translated_text: 'If through origination' — and so forth in detail. With the intent that only volition (<s>cetanā</s>) is wholesome or unwholesome, he investigates the wholesomeness or unwholesomeness of bodily and verbal action. 'Why not of the great elements?' — their wholesomeness or unwholesomeness [is questioned]. For bodily and verbal action, together with their great elements, is originated by wholesome or unwholesome mind. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: for the doer's intent is directed toward the action, not toward the great elements — [the doer thinks] 'I shall not make the great elements,' but rather 'I shall make this action.' Therefore the great elements do not have wholesomeness or unwholesomeness like the action. The <s>Ācārya</s> (master) says:

body.text: samāhitasya kartur avijñaptau nāsty abhiprāyaḥ. avijñaptiṃ kuryāṃ iti. na cāsamāhitaṃ cittaṃ tasyāḥ samutthāpakam asti. yad evam abhiprāyaṃ kuryāt. visabhāgatvāt visadṛśatvāt bhūmito 'samādhānād vā. kathaṃ tasyāḥ samāhitāyā avijñapteḥ kuśalatvaṃ. mahābhūtavat tasyāḥ kuśalatvaṃ na syād ity abhiprāyaḥ. divyayor api vā cakṣuḥśrotrayoḥ kuśalatvaprasaṃga iti. yady antareṇāpi tadabhiprāyam avijñapteḥ kuśalam iti. atha vā ayam asyābhisambandhaḥ. yadi visabhāgāsamāhitacittavaśena tasyāḥ kuśalatvaṃ. divyayor api cakṣuḥśrotrayoḥ kuśalatvaprasaṃgaḥ. prayogakāle tadabhiprāyasaṃbhavāt. na ca tayoḥ kuśalam asty
body.translated_text: for one in concentration (<s>samāhita</s>), the doer has no intent toward non-informative action (<s>avijñapti</s>) — [one does not think] 'I shall make non-informative action.' Nor is non-concentrated mind the originator of that [non-informative action], which would have such an intent — because of being dissimilar in ground, because of being unlike [the concentrated state], or because of non-concentration. How then is that concentrated non-informative action wholesome? The intent is: like the great elements, its wholesomeness should not [be established]. 'Or there would be the consequence of the wholesomeness of the divine eye and ear too' — if non-informative action is wholesome even without that intent [being directed toward it], or alternatively, the connection is thus: if its wholesomeness is through the force of dissimilar non-concentrated mind, then there would be the consequence that the divine eye and ear too are wholesome — because of the possibility of such intent at the time of the preparatory practice. Yet they are not wholesome —

body.text: (IV.12-14) yad uktaṃ darśanaprahātavyaṃ cittaṃ vijñapter asamutthāpakam iti. darśanaprahātavyasyāṃtarmukhapravṛttatvād ity evaṃ bruvatāṃ kiṃ tarhi bhagavatoktam iti virudhyate. tad bhagavatoktam iti vākyārthaḥ. kiṃ tad ity ucyate. tato mithyādṛṣṭer iti vistaraḥ. kathaṃ mithyādṛṣṭer darśanaprahātavyāyāḥ [Tib. 24a] mithyāvāk vijñaptisvabhāvā mithyākarmāntaś ca tatsvabhāva evety uktam iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.12-14) What was stated — that mind to be abandoned by seeing [the truths] (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>) is not the originator of informative action (<s>vijñapti</s>) — those who say 'because [mind] to be abandoned by seeing operates inwardly' — what then about what the Blessed One said? — this is contradicted. The meaning of the sentence is: that which the Blessed One said [is contradicted]. What is that? It is said: 'From wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>)' — and so forth in detail. How is it stated that from wrong view, which is to be abandoned by seeing, wrong speech has the nature of informative action, and wrong bodily conduct too has that very nature?

children.translated_text: 'Designated as arising from the cause and from that moment' —

body.text: iti. hetutthānaṃ ca tatkṣaṇotthānaṃ ca hetutatkṣaṇotthānaṃ. hetutatkṣaṇotthānam iti saṃjñitaṃ
body.translated_text: thus. Arising from the cause and arising from that moment — [hence] arising from the cause and from that moment. Designated as arising from the cause and from that moment —

children.translated_text: designated as arising from the cause and from that moment. 'Designated' —

body.text: iti saṃjñīkṛtaṃ. atha vā hetutatkṣaṇotthānaṃ saṃjñāsyeti hetutatkṣaṇotthānasaṃjñaṃ. hetutatkṣaṇotthānasaṃjñīkṛtaṃ
body.translated_text: means made into a designation. Or alternatively, that which will be designated as arising from the cause and from that moment — [hence] bearing the designation of arising from the cause and from that moment. Made into a designation of arising from the cause and from that moment —

children.translated_text: designated as arising from the cause and from that moment.

body.text: hetusamutthānam iti. samuttiṣṭhate 'neneti samutthānaṃ. hetuś ca sa samutthānaṃ ca tat hetusamutthānaṃ. tatkṣaṇasamutthānam iti. sa kṣaṇaḥ kriyākṣaṇaḥ. tatkṣaṇe samutthānaṃ tatkṣaṇasamutthānaṃ. tatraiva kṣaṇe samutthānasadbhāvāt. tatraiva kriyākṣaṇe tatkṣaṇasamutthānasya bhāvād ity arthaḥ. ākṣepakatvād ity utpādakatvāt. kim idānīm iti vistaraḥ. tasya tatkṣaṇasamutthānasya tasyāṃ vijñapanakriyāyāṃ sāmarthyaṃ. yena tadānīṃ tadanuvartakam ity ucyate. tena hīti vistaraḥ. tena hi tatkṣaṇasamutthānena vinā asau vijñaptir mṛtasyeva na syād ākṣiptā satī hetusamutthānena janitāpi satī. tadyathā. kaścid grāmaṃ gamiṣyāmīty ākṣiptakriyāntarā mriyet. tasyānuvartakacittābhāvād
body.translated_text: 'Arising from the cause' (<s>hetusamutthāna</s>) — that by which it arises is the origination (<s>samutthāna</s>). The cause and that origination — [hence] cause-origination. 'Arising from that moment' (<s>tatkṣaṇasamutthāna</s>) — that moment is the moment of action. Origination in that moment — [hence] arising in that moment — because of the existence of the origination in that very moment. In that very moment of action, because of the existence of the arising in that moment — this is the meaning. 'Because of impelling' — meaning: because of producing. 'What now' — and so forth in detail. The power of that arising-in-that-moment in that informative activity — by which it is said to be its follower at that time. 'For by that' — and so forth in detail. For without that arising-in-that-moment, that informative action would not exist, like [the action] of a dead person, even though impelled by the cause-origination, even though generated. For example: someone, having been impelled to the action of 'I shall go to the village,' dies in the midst of another action. Because of the absence of the following mind

body.text: gamanaṃ na bhavati. tadvat. acittakasya tarhīti [Tib. 24b] vistaraḥ. yadi tatkṣaṇasamutthānena vināsau mṛtasyeva na syāt. nirodhasamāpattilābhinaḥ kasyacid upasaṃpādyamānasya kāyavijñaptim ābadhnataḥ tatkālopasthitanirodhasamāpattitvād acittakasya saṃvarotpattau karmavācanāvasānakālīnāyāṃ tatsaṃvarāntargatā kāyavijñaptiḥ kathaṃ bhavati. katham utpadyate tatkṣaṇasamutthānaṃ vinety arthaḥ. evaṃ virodhite samādhyaṃtaraḥ śrīyate. sphuṭatarā tarhīti. tatkṣaṇasamutthānena sacittakasya vyaktatarā vijñaptir bhavatīty etat tasya sāmarthyaṃ.
body.translated_text: the going does not occur — so too. 'Then for one without mind' — and so forth in detail. If without the arising-in-that-moment, that [informative action] would not exist, like [the action] of a dead person — then for someone who has obtained the cessation attainment, who is being ordained and is binding bodily informative action, since the cessation attainment comes upon him at that time and he is without mind — in the arising of restraint at the end of the ordination formula, how does the bodily informative action included within that restraint exist? How does it arise without the arising-in-that-moment? — this is the meaning. When this contradiction is raised, a middle ground is found: 'More distinct then' — [meaning] the informative action of one with mind, through the arising-in-that-moment, becomes more manifest — this is its power.

children.translated_text: 'That to be abandoned by seeing [the truths] is the initiator (<s>pravartaka</s>)' —

body.text: iti. pravartakam eva dṛṣṭiheyam ity avadhāryate. kathaṃ punas tat pravartakam ity āha. tatsamutthāpakayor vitarkavicārayor nidānabhūtatvāt hetubhūtatvāt. vijñapteḥ pravartakam iti. na tv anuvartakam iti vistaraḥ. yat tad bahirmukhaṃ cittam anuvartakaṃ. tasya yo vijñaptikriyākālaḥ. tasmiṃ tadabhāvāt. tasya darśanaprahātavyasya pravartakasyābhāvād ity arthaḥ. atas tan nānuvartakaṃ. ayaṃ cānyo doṣaḥ. tatsamutthāpitaṃ ca rūpam iti vistaraḥ. yadi tad anuvartakaṃ syād darśanaprahātavyaṃ. tena darśanaprahātavyena samutthāpitaṃ kāyavāgvijñaptirūpaṃ darśanaprahātavyaṃ syāt. yathā bhāvanāprahātavyena cittena samutthāpitaṃ [Tib. 25a] kāyavākkarma bhāvanāprahātavyam iti. kiṃ syād iti codakaḥ. abhidharmo bādhitaḥ syād iti vaibhāṣikaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. It is restricted that what is to be abandoned by seeing is only the initiator. How then is it the initiator? He says: because of being the basis, the cause, of the deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>) and examination (<s>vicāra</s>) that originate it. It is the initiator of informative action, but not its sustainer (<s>anuvartaka</s>) — and so forth in detail. That outward-directed mind which is the sustainer — at the time of the action of informative expression — at that time, because of its absence — because of the absence of the initiator to be abandoned by seeing — this is the meaning. Therefore it is not the sustainer. And this is another fault: 'And the form originated by it' — and so forth in detail. If that which is to be abandoned by seeing were the sustainer, then the bodily and verbal informative form originated by that which is to be abandoned by seeing would be to be abandoned by seeing — just as bodily and verbal action originated by mind to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>) is to be abandoned by cultivation. 'What would it be?' — thus the objector. 'The <s>Abhidharma</s> would be contradicted' — says the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>.

children.translated_text: 'That which is to be abandoned by seeing is not unafflicted, nor is it form' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. kiṃ ca vidyāvidyābhyāṃ cāvirodhāt. vidyayā darśanamārgeṇa satkāyadṛṣṭyādivat tasya rūpasyāvirodhāt. aprahāṇād ity arthaḥ. dṛṣṭasatyānām api tatsamanvāgatatvān nāsti rūpaṃ darśanaprahātavyaṃ. avidyayā cāvirodhāt. kiṃ cāvidyayāpi rūpaṃ na virudhyate. na hi kliṣṭākliṣṭarūpasamudācārāvasthāyāṃ tatprāptipravāhe vā saty avidyā na bhavati avidyāyāṃ ca satyāṃ tan na bhavati. yathā anāsravo mārgo 'vidyayā virudhyate. pṛthagjanāvasthāyāṃ tadanutpādāt. tadutpāde vāryavasthāyāṃ kasyāścid avidyāyāḥ prahāṇāt. tad evam anāsravavad aprahātavyam api na bhavati. na ced aprahātavyaṃ. nāpi darśanaprahātavyaṃ. pāriśeṣyād bhāvanāprahātavyam iti siddhaṃ. itara āha. [Tib. 25b] sādhya eṣa pakṣo vidyayā rūpaṃ na virudhyata iti. yo hi darśanaprahātavyaṃ rūpam icchati. sa kathaṃ vidyayā rūpasyāvirodhaṃ grahīṣyati. vaibhāṣika āha. bhūtāny apīti vistaraḥ. yadi tad rūpaṃ darśanaprahātavyacittasamutthāpitaṃ
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Moreover, because of non-contradiction with knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). Because of non-contradiction of that form with knowledge, i.e. the path of seeing — like the view of the self-collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest — meaning: because of non-abandonment. Even for those who have seen the truths, because of being endowed with that [form], there is no form to be abandoned by seeing. And because of non-contradiction with ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) too — moreover, form is not contradicted even by ignorance. For it is not the case that in the state of the operation of afflicted and unafflicted form, or in the continuity of its acquisition, when ignorance exists, that [form] does not exist, or when that exists, ignorance does not exist — as the uncontaminated path is contradicted by ignorance: because of its non-arising in the state of an ordinary person; or because at its arising, in the noble state, certain ignorances are abandoned. Thus, like what is uncontaminated, it is also not to be abandoned. If not to be abandoned, then also not to be abandoned by seeing. By elimination, it is established as to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>). The other [teacher] says: this thesis is what needs to be proved — that form is not contradicted by knowledge. For one who accepts that form is to be abandoned by seeing — how would he accept the non-contradiction of form by knowledge? The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'The great elements too' — and so forth in detail. If that form originated by mind to be abandoned by seeing

body.text: darśanaprahātavyaṃ syāt. tadāśrayabhūtāny api tarhi darśanaprahātavyāni syuḥ. kasmāt. samānacittotthāpitatvāt. yena hi darśanaprahātavyena cittena tad rūpaṃ samutthāpitaṃ. tenaiva tadāśrayabhūtāny apīti. na ca tāni tathā bhavitum arhanti. akliṣṭāvyākṛtatvāt. darśanaprahātavyānāṃ ca kliṣṭatvāt. itara āha. naivaṃ bhaviṣyati. darśanaprahātavyāni syur iti. katham ity āha. yathā na kuśalākuśalāni bhavanti. yathā yena cittena kuśalākuśalena kuśalākuśalaṃ rūpaṃ samutthāpitaṃ. tenaiva tadāśrayabhūtāni samutthāpitāni. tac ca kāyavākkarmasvabhāvaṃ rūpaṃ kuśalākuśalaṃ. na tadāśrayabhūtānīti. tadvat. sa eva punaḥ parāvṛtyāha. atha vā punar bhavaṃtu darśanaprahātavyānīti. vaibhāṣika āha. naivaṃ śakyaṃ bhavitum. darśanaprahātavyānīti vākyaśeṣaḥ. kasmāt. akliṣṭasya [Tib. 26a] dharmasya vidyāvidyābhyām avirodhāt. na hy akliṣṭo dharmaḥ anivṛtāvyākṛtaḥ kuśalasāsravaś ca vidyayānāsraveṇa mārgeṇa virudhyate. yathā kliṣṭā dharmāḥ prāpticchedād virudhyaṃte. tadālambanakleśaprāpticchedāt tu virodho na pratiṣidhyate. nāpy avidyayā virudhyate. prāpticchedena tadālambanakleśaprahātavyena ca. bhūtāni cākliṣṭāni. tatra yad uktam atha vā punar bhavaṃtv iti. tad ayuktaṃ. tad evam atra sādhanam uttiṣṭhate. na darśanaprahātavyāni kliṣṭarūpāśrayamahābhūtāni. akliṣṭatvāt. akliṣṭacittacaittadharmavad iti. tad evaṃ vaibhāṣikaḥ
body.translated_text: were to be abandoned by seeing, then the great elements that are its support should also be to be abandoned by seeing. Why? Because of being originated by the same mind. For by the very mind to be abandoned by seeing that originated that form, those supporting great elements too [were originated]. Yet those [great elements] cannot be so — because of being unafflicted and indeterminate. And what is to be abandoned by seeing is afflicted. The other says: it will not be so — they will not be to be abandoned by seeing. How? He says: just as they are not wholesome or unwholesome. Just as when bodily and verbal action — wholesome or unwholesome form — is originated by wholesome or unwholesome mind, the great elements supporting it are originated by that very [mind], yet the form having the nature of bodily and verbal action is wholesome or unwholesome, but not the supporting great elements — so too. Then he reverses himself and says: or alternatively, let them be to be abandoned by seeing. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: it is not possible for them to be so — to be abandoned by seeing — this is the completion of the sentence. Why? Because an unafflicted <s>dharma</s> is not contradicted by knowledge or ignorance. For an unafflicted <s>dharma</s> — unobscured-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>) and wholesome-with-outflows — is not contradicted by knowledge, i.e. the uncontaminated path — just as afflicted <s>dharma</s>s are contradicted through the cutting off of acquisition. But contradiction through the cutting off of acquisition of the affliction that has it as object is not denied. Nor is it contradicted by ignorance — through the cutting off of acquisition or through the affliction to be abandoned that has it as object. And the great elements are unafflicted. Therefore, what was said — 'or alternatively, let them be to be abandoned by seeing' — that is not fitting. Thus here, this proof arises: the great elements that support afflicted form are not to be abandoned by seeing — because of being unafflicted — like unafflicted mind and mental factors. Thus the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>

children.translated_text: 'The consciousness to be abandoned by seeing is the initiator' —

body.text:
iti sacodyaparihāraṃ pratiṣṭhāpya nigamayati. ato hetusamutthānam iti vistaraḥ. yad uktaṃ mithyādṛṣṭer mithyāsaṃkalpo yāvat mithyākarmānta iti. tasya sūtrasya na virodho bhavatīti.
pravartakaṃ cānuvartakaṃ ceti. antarbahirmukhapravṛttatvāt.
body.translated_text:
Thus, having established [the point] with the resolution of objections, he concludes. 'Therefore, originating from a cause' — and so forth in detail. What was stated — 'from wrong view, wrong intention, up to wrong bodily action' — there is no contradiction with that <s>sūtra</s>.
'Both initiating and sustaining' — because of functioning in both inward-directed and outward-directed modes.

body.text: ity avadhāraṇam avikalpakatvāt.
body.translated_text: this is a restriction, because of being non-conceptual.

body.text: Tib. 26b
body.translated_text: 'Neither [initiating nor sustaining]

body.text: nobhayam anāsravam iti. na pravartakaṃ. nāpy anuvartakaṃ. samāhitāntarmukhapravṛttatvāt.
body.translated_text: is uncontaminated' — not initiating, nor sustaining, because of functioning in a concentrated, inward-directed mode.

body.text: amlāyamāneti. ahīyamānā. cānaṭpratyayantaś cāyaṃ śabdaḥ. kuśalaikatānā iti. kuśalaikaprabandhā ity arthaḥ. buddho bhagavān nāga ity uktaḥ sūtre. kathaṃ. tathāgata udāyin sadevake loke samāraka iti vistareṇoktvāha āgo na karoti kāyena vācā manasā. tasmān nāga ity ucyate iti. āgo na karotīty aparādhaṃ na karotīty arthaḥ. anicchayāsyeti. anicchayāsya buddhasya cittasyāvisaraṇād viṣayeṣv agamanād evam uktaṃ.
