body.translated_text: 'Fading' (<s>amlāyamāna</s>) — meaning: diminishing. And this word ends with the <s>cānaṭ</s> suffix. 'Single-mindedly wholesome' (<s>kuśalaikatānā</s>) — the meaning is: of a single continuous flow of wholesomeness. The <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s> is called '<s>Nāga</s>' in the <s>sūtra</s>. How? Having said in detail: '<s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Udāyin</s>, in the world with its gods, with <s>Māra</s>' — he says: 'He commits no offense (<s>āga</s>) by body, speech, or mind. Therefore he is called <s>Nāga</s>.' 'He commits no offense' means he commits no wrongdoing — this is the meaning. 'Of one without desire' — because of the <s>Buddha</s>'s mind not wandering, not going toward objects, thus it is said.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. caturṣv īryāpatheṣu caraṃ carāmīti. yāvan niṣīdam niṣīdāmīty upasthitasmṛtitvān nityasamāhitaḥ sa ucyate.
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. Walking in the four postures, [thinking] 'I am walking,' up to sitting, [thinking] 'I am sitting' — because of having established mindfulness, he is called always concentrated.

body.text: nirabhisaṃskāravāhitvād iti. abhāvo hi saṃskārasya prayatnasya nirabhisaṃskāraṃ. nirabhisaṃskāraṃ vahatīti nirabhisaṃskāravāhī. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmād iti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of carrying without volitional effort' (<s>nirabhisaṃskāravāhitva</s>) — for the absence of <s>saṃskāra</s>, of effort, is 'without volitional effort.' One who carries [the mind-stream] without volitional effort is <s>nirabhisaṃskāravāhin</s>. Its state [is the abstract noun]. 'Therefore' — thus.

body.text: na vā sarvaṃ darśanaprahātavyaṃ pravartakam iti. syād etad evaṃ. yadi sarvaṃ darśanaprahātavyaṃ pravartakam iṣyeta. na tu sarvaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. mithyādṛṣṭyādikam eva pravartakaṃ vijñapter na satkāyadṛṣṭyādikam [Tib. 27a] ity ata āha. na vā sarvam iti viśeṣaṇaṃ vaktavyam īdṛśaṃ pravartakam īdṛśaṃ neti. akuśalāvyākṛtacittasyeti. upasaṃpādyamānasya kenacid yogenākuśalāvyākṛtacittasya. prātimokṣasamvaravijñaptir aṃjalyādikā kuśalā na prāpnoti. tadanuvartakacittam akuśalāvyākṛtam iti kṛtvā. yathā pravartakam iti vistaraḥ. yathā pravartakaṃ cittaṃ bhāvanāprahātavyam. tathā vijñaptir vyavasthāpyate. na tu yathā darśanaprahātavyaṃ pravartakaṃ tathā vyavasthāpyate. kasmāt. bhāvanāheyenāntaritatvāt. yasmāt tatpravartakaṃ darśanaprahātavyaṃ bhāvanāheyena pravartakenāntaritaṃ. kathaṃ kṛtvā. tadyathāsty ātmeti mayā pareṣāṃ gamayitavyam iti pūrvam evāvadhārya tato vāksamutpādakena cittena bahirmukhapravṛttena bhāvanāprahātavyena savitarkeṇa savicāreṇa vācaṃ bhāṣate. asty ātmety evamādi. ato yathā pravartakam iti vistaraḥ. tad evam avaśyaṃ darśanaprahātavyasya pravartakasyānantaraṃ pravartakam eva bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ kuśalam [Tib. 27b] akuśalam avyākṛtaṃ cotpadyate. tadvaśāc ca vijñapteḥ kuśalāditvam iti. evaṃ tu vaktavyam iti vistaraḥ. evaṃ tu vaktavyam anyavyavahitaṃ bhāvanāheyavyavahitaṃ hetusamutthānaṃ saṃdhāyoktam iti. paraṃparāhetusamutthānaṃ saṃdhāyety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Or, not all that is to be abandoned by seeing is initiating' — one might think thus, if all that is to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>) were accepted as initiating. But not all is. What then? Only wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) and the like are initiating of informative action (<s>vijñapti</s>), not the view of the self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the like. Therefore he says: 'Or, not all' — a qualification must be stated: such-and-such is initiating, such-and-such is not. 'Of one with unwholesome or indeterminate mind' — of one who, through some practice, has unwholesome or indeterminate mind when undertaking [the vow]. The <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint informative action such as bowing and the like, being wholesome, would not be obtained — because the sustaining mind is unwholesome or indeterminate. 'As the initiating [mind]' — and so forth in detail. Just as the initiating mind is to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>), so the informative action is classified — but not as the initiating [mind] that is to be abandoned by seeing. Why? Because of being intervened by what is to be abandoned by cultivation. Since that initiating [mind] to be abandoned by seeing is intervened by an initiating [mind] to be abandoned by cultivation. How so? For example, having first determined 'I must make others believe that a self exists,' then, with an outward-directed mind that is to be abandoned by cultivation, having conceptual thought (<s>savitarka</s>) and examination (<s>savicāra</s>), one utters speech producing that thought — 'A self exists' and so on. Therefore 'as the initiating [mind]' — and so forth in detail. Thus necessarily, immediately after the initiating [mind] to be abandoned by seeing, an initiating [mind] to be abandoned by cultivation arises — whether wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate. And by the force of that, the informative action has its wholesomeness and the like. 'But it should be stated thus' — and so forth in detail. But it should be stated thus: 'intervened by another, intervened by what is to be abandoned by cultivation, the statement was made with reference to indirect causal origination' — the meaning is: with reference to indirect causal origination.

body.text: (IV.15ab)
body.translated_text: (IV.15ab)

body.text: vistaraḥ. trividhety uddiśya.
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. Having indicated 'threefold,'

body.text: vivṛṇoti. saṃvaraś ca saḥ. asaṃvaraś ca saḥ. saṃvarāsaṃvaraḥ. saṃvarāsaṃvaraś ca saḥ. itarā ca sā.
body.translated_text: he elaborates. It is restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>), it is non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>) — [thus] restraint-and-non-restraint. And it is restraint-and-non-restraint, and it is the other.

body.text: samāsaḥ.
body.translated_text: [this is] the compound.

body.text: (IV.16) pratiniyatalakṣaṇatvād iti. bhikṣusaṃvarasyānyal lakṣaṇam evaṃ yāvad upavāsasaṃvarasyānyal lakṣaṇaṃ. tathā hi vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: (IV.16) 'Because of having specifically defined characteristics' — the characteristics of the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint are different, and so on up to the characteristics of the fasting restraint (<s>upavāsasaṃvara</s>) being different. For thus it will be stated:

body.text: paṃcāṣṭadaśasarvebhyo varjyebhyo viratigrahāt
body.translated_text: 'Through the undertaking of abstention from five, eight, all, and what is to be avoided' —

body.text: upāsakopavāsasthaśramaṇoddeśabhikṣuteti.
body.translated_text: 'layperson (<s>upāsaka</s>), one observing the fast (<s>upavāsastha</s>), novice (<s>śramaṇoddeśa</s>), and <s>bhikṣu</s>.'

body.text: aṣṭavidhatve tu sāṃkaryasaṃbhavaḥ. ya eva hi bhikṣusamvaraḥ. sa eva bhikṣuṇīsamvara ity evamādi. śrāmaṇerī ca punaḥ śikṣamāṇā ceti. śrāmaṇerī parivṛttavyaṃjanā śramaṇero bhavati. śikṣamāṇā cāpi parivṛttavyaṃjanā śrāmaṇera eva bhavati. kim evaṃ neṣyate. parivṛttavyaṃjano bhikṣur bhikṣusaṃvaraṃ ca tyajati. bhikṣuṇīsaṃvaraṃ ca pratilabhata ity ata āha. na ca vyaṃjanaparivṛttāv iti vistaraḥ. na bhikṣubhikṣuṇīvyaṃjanaprādurbhāve pārvasaṃvaratyāgakāraṇam asti.
body.translated_text: But if there were eightfold [classification], there would be the possibility of confusion — for the very same <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint would be the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> restraint, and so on. 'And a <s>śrāmaṇerī</s> (female novice), and a <s>śikṣamāṇā</s> (probationer)' — a <s>śrāmaṇerī</s> whose sexual characteristics have changed becomes a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (male novice). And a <s>śikṣamāṇā</s> whose sexual characteristics have changed also becomes a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>. Why is it not accepted thus: one whose characteristics have changed, being a <s>bhikṣu</s>, abandons the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint and obtains the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> restraint? Therefore he says: 'And upon the change of sexual characteristics' — and so forth in detail. There is no reason for the abandonment of the former restraint upon the appearance of the <s>bhikṣu</s> or <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> sexual characteristics.

body.text: Tib. 28a
body.translated_text: Tib. 28a

body.text:
prātimokṣadamatyāgaḥ śikṣānikṣepaṇāc cyuteḥ
ubhayavyaṃjanotpatter mūlacchedān niśātyayād
body.translated_text:
'The abandonment of <s>prātimokṣa</s> discipline [occurs] through renouncing the training, through death,
through the arising of both sexual characteristics, through cutting off the root, and through the passing of the night' —

body.text: ity atra yat kāraṇam uktaṃ. nāpy apūrvasaṃvarapratilaṃbhe kāraṇam astīti vartate. yad uktaṃ
body.translated_text: here, the reason stated [for abandonment] — it continues: nor is there a reason for the obtaining of a new restraint. As stated:

body.text: prātimokṣākhyaḥ paravijñāpanādibhir
body.translated_text: 'Called <s>prātimokṣa</s>, through informing others and the like' —

body.text: iti. ato vijñāyate na bhikṣusaṃvarād anyo bhikṣuṇīsaṃvara iti. evaṃ śrāmaṇerādīnām api vaktavyaṃ. tasmād abhinno 'nanyaś caturṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīśikṣamāṇāśrāmaṇeryupāsikāsaṃvarāṇāṃ tribhyo bhikṣuśrāmaṇeropāsakasaṃvarebhyaḥ svabhāvaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. From this it is understood that the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> restraint is not different from the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint. Similarly, it should be stated for <s>śrāmaṇerī</s>s and the rest. Therefore, the intrinsic nature of the four restraints — of <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, <s>śikṣamāṇā</s>, <s>śrāmaṇerī</s>, and <s>upāsikā</s> — is not different, not other, from the three restraints of <s>bhikṣu</s>, <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, and <s>upāsaka</s>.

body.text: kiṃ te saṃvarā iti vistaraḥ. yathā paṃcasaṃkhyāyām anyāni paṃca prakṣipya paṃcavṛddhiyogād daśa bhavanti. paṃcadaśasaṃkhyāyāṃ cānyāni paṃca prakṣipya viṃśatir bhavaṃti. dīnārasateravac ca. yathā pūrvako dīnāro dvitīyena saha satero bhavati. tathā hi loke ekadīnāramūlyena dvitīyaṃ dīnāraṃ dīnāramūlyaṃ vā tena pūrvakeṇa dīnāramūlyena sahādhikam apekṣya kaścid vaktā bhavet. dīnārasatero mayā labdha iti. dīnāradvayaṃ mayā labdham ity arthaḥ. kim evam eta upāsakaśrāmaṇerabhikṣusaṃvarāḥ virativṛddhiyogāt prāṇātipātādiviratiṣu tathaivāvasthitāsu punar nṛtyagītaviratyādīnām apūrvāṇāṃ viratīnāṃ [Tib. 28b] vṛddhiyogād anyonya ucyaṃte. anya upāsakasaṃvarāc chrāmaṇerasaṃvaraḥ śrāmaṇerasaṃvarāc cānyo bhikṣusaṃvara iti ekadeśaviśeṣayogād anyonyavyavasthety arthaḥ. āho svit pṛthag eva te sakalā upajāyante. anyāḥ prāṇātipātādivirataya upāsakasya. tato 'nyāḥ śrāmaṇerasya. tato 'nyāś ca bhikṣoḥ. ity ekasmiṃ bhikṣusaṃtāne tisraḥ prāṇātipātādiviratayaḥ. evam adattādānaviratayaḥ. ity evamādi. evaṃ śeṣā iti. nṛtyagītaviratyādayaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'What are those restraints?' — and so forth in detail. Just as when five additional [items] are added to the number five, through the addition they become ten; and when another five are added to the number fifteen, they become twenty. And like a <s>dīnāra</s> with a half. Just as a former <s>dīnāra</s>, together with a second, becomes one-and-a-half. For in the world, someone who has obtained something worth one <s>dīnāra</s> plus a second <s>dīnāra</s> or the value of a <s>dīnāra</s>, with reference to the excess over the former <s>dīnāra</s>-value, would say: 'I have obtained one-and-a-half <s>dīnāra</s>s' — the meaning is: I have obtained two <s>dīnāra</s>s. Is it thus — that the <s>upāsaka</s>, <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, and <s>bhikṣu</s> restraints, through the addition of abstentions, while the abstentions from killing and the like remain in the same state, through the addition of new abstentions such as from dancing, singing, and the rest, are called different from one another? The <s>śrāmaṇera</s> restraint is different from the <s>upāsaka</s> restraint, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint is different from the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> restraint — the meaning is: they are classified differently through the addition of partial distinctions. Or do they arise separately and completely? Are the abstentions from killing and the like of the <s>upāsaka</s> different, those of the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> different from those, and those of the <s>bhikṣu</s> yet different? Thus, in a single <s>bhikṣu</s>'s continuum there would be three sets of abstentions from killing and the like, similarly three sets of abstentions from taking what is not given — and so on. 'Similarly for the rest' — abstentions from dancing, singing, and the like.

body.text: madapramādebhya iti. uccaśayanādimadyapānādibhyaḥ. bahutarebhyaḥ
body.translated_text: 'From intoxication and heedlessness' — from high beds and seats, drinking intoxicants, and the like. 'From more

body.text: prāṇātipātādīnāṃ nidānebhya iti. upāsakāc chrāmaṇero bahutarebhyaḥ prāṇātipātādinidānebhyo nivartate. tadyathā vikālabhojanaṃ prāṇātipātanidānaṃ bhavet. tasmāc chrāmaṇero nivartate. nopāsaka ity evamādi yojyaṃ. evaṃ cāsati. evaṃ ca yadi na syād ity arthaḥ. bhikṣusaṃvaraṃ pratyācakṣāṇas tyajaṃs trīn api upāsakasaṃvarādīn vijahyāt. dvayor upāsakaśrāmaṇerasaṃvarayos tatra bhikṣusaṃvare 'ntarbhāvāt.
body.translated_text: causes of killing and the like' — the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> refrains from more causes of killing and the like than the <s>upāsaka</s>. For example, eating at improper times could be a cause of killing — the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> refrains from that, but not the <s>upāsaka</s> — and so on should be connected. 'And if this were not so' — and if it were not thus, is the meaning. One who renounces the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint would also abandon all three — the <s>upāsaka</s> restraint and the rest — because the two, the <s>upāsaka</s> and <s>śrāmaṇera</s> restraints, would be included within that <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint.

body.text: (IV.17) viratisamādānād iti. vijñaptyavijñaptiviratir [Tib. 29a] iti vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: (IV.17) 'Through the undertaking of abstention' — it will be stated: informative and non-informative abstention (<s>vijñaptyavijñaptivirati</s>).

body.text: (IV.18) samāpādanād iti. pratisaṃsthāpanād ity arthaḥ. pāpakarmaṇo hi sattveṣu viṣamaṃ saṃpravartate. sāpi tu vijñapticittābhyāṃ kriyata iti. vijñaptyā ca kriyate prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītā avijñaptiś cittena ca kriyate dhyānānāsravasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītā avijñaptiḥ. samādhinā kriyata ity arthaḥ. tad evaṃ kriyata iti kriyeti karmasādhanaṃ.
body.translated_text: (IV.18) 'Through producing' (<s>samāpādana</s>) — the meaning is: through establishing (<s>pratisaṃsthāpana</s>). For evil <s>karma</s> operates unevenly among beings. 'But that too is produced by informative action and mind' — non-informative action included in the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint is produced by informative action (<s>vijñapti</s>), and non-informative action included in the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) restraints is produced by mind — the meaning is: produced by concentration (<s>samādhi</s>). 'Thus it is produced, hence it is an action (<s>kriyā</s>)' — [the word] <s>kriyā</s> is a derivative based on the sense of action.

body.text: kriyāhetutvād iti. kriyāyā hetutvāt. saṃvarastho hy saṃvaraparirakṣaṇārthaṃ kriyāṃ vijñaptilakṣaṇām ārabhate. kriyāphalatvāc ceti. vijñaptilakṣaṇāyāḥ kriyāyāḥ phalatvād ity arthaḥ. samādhisaṃbhūtā kathaṃ kriyā bhavati. samādhijāyāś cetanāyāḥ phalatvāt sāpi kriyā. prātimokṣasaṃvarādhikārād vā. na tatra cittāḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Because of being a cause of action' — because of being the cause of action (<s>kriyā</s>). For one established in restraint undertakes action characterized by informative expression for the purpose of protecting the restraint. 'And because of being the fruit of action' — the meaning is: because of being the fruit of action characterized by informative expression. 'How is that which arises from concentration an action?' — because of being the fruit of volition (<s>cetanā</s>) born of concentration, that too is action. Or alternatively, [this is said] in the context of the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint. 'Not those in mind' — [the minds therein are not action-paths].

body.text: evaṃ tāvad aviśeṣeṇa prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ saṃśabdyata iti. ādyo 'pi kṣaṇo dvitīyādayo 'pi ca kṣaṇāḥ prātimokṣasaṃvara ity ucyate. prātimokṣasvabhāvas tv ādyakṣaṇa eva. tadartham āha. punaḥ ādye vijñaptyavjñaptī prātimokṣa ity ucyate. pāpasya tena pratimokṣaṇād iti. prathamenaiva kṣaṇena pāpaṃ pratimokṣate. [Tib. 29b] utsṛjyate tyajata ity arthaḥ. pratimokṣa iti prāpte prātimokṣa iti vacanaṃ svārthe vṛddhividhānāt. svārthe pratyaye kṛte vṛddhikaraṇād ity arthaḥ. vaikṛtavaiśasavat. yathā vikṛtam eva vaikṛtam. viśasam eva māraṇaṃ vaiśasaṃ. evaṃ pratimokṣa eva prātimokṣa iti. prātimokṣasaṃvara ity apīti. prātimokṣaś cāsau saṃvaraś ca. kāyavācoḥ saṃvaraṇārtha ity arthaḥ. karmapatha ity apy ucyata iti. maulaḥ karmapatha ity arthaḥ. dvitīyādiṣu kṣaṇeṣu prātimokṣasaṃvara eva. prātimokṣajātīyaḥ prātimokṣād vā jātaḥ saṃvaraḥ prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ. na prātimokṣaḥ. yasmāt na tena pāpaṃ pratimokṣate. prathamakṣaṇa eva pratimokṣitatvāt.
body.translated_text: Thus, without distinction, the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint is referred to — both the first moment and the second and subsequent moments are called '<s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint.' But the intrinsic nature of <s>prātimokṣa</s> belongs to the first moment alone. For this purpose he says: 'Again, the informative and non-informative actions of the first [moment] are called <s>prātimokṣa</s>.' 'Because of the releasing (<s>pratimokṣaṇa</s>) of evil by that' — by the very first moment, evil is released, cast off, abandoned — this is the meaning. When '<s>pratimokṣa</s>' is expected, the word '<s>prātimokṣa</s>' is used because of the application of <s>vṛddhi</s> in the reflexive sense — meaning: when the suffix is applied in the reflexive sense, <s>vṛddhi</s> is performed. Like <s>vaikṛta</s> and <s>vaiśasa</s> — just as <s>vikṛta</s> (distortion) itself is <s>vaikṛta</s>, and <s>viśasa</s> (slaughter) itself is <s>vaiśasa</s> — so too <s>pratimokṣa</s> itself is <s>prātimokṣa</s>. 'Also called <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint' — it is both <s>prātimokṣa</s> and restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) — the meaning is: for the purpose of restraining body and speech. 'Also called action-path (<s>karmapatha</s>)' — meaning: the root action-path. In the second and subsequent moments, it is <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint [only] — of the <s>prātimokṣa</s> class, or a restraint born from <s>prātimokṣa</s> — [hence] <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint. Not <s>prātimokṣa</s> [itself]. Because evil is not released by that, since it was already released in the first moment.

body.text: (IV.19) aṣṭāv eva nikāyā ity avadhāraṇe pṛcchati. kiṃ khalu bāhyakānām iti vistaraḥ. samādānaśīlam iti viśeṣaṇaṃ. śīladvaividhyāt. dvividhaṃ hi śīlaṃ. samādānaśīlaṃ dharmatāpratilaṃbhikaṃ ca. tatra samādānśīlaṃ yad gṛhyate.
body.translated_text: (IV.19) Regarding the restriction 'only eight orders' (<s>nikāya</s>), he asks: 'Is it the case that for outsiders' — and so forth in detail. 'Morality of undertaking' — this is a qualification, because of the twofold nature of morality. For morality is twofold: morality of undertaking (<s>samādānaśīla</s>) and morality obtained through the nature of things (<s>dharmatāpratilaṃbhika</s>). Of these, morality of undertaking is that which is taken up

body.text: idaṃ cedaṃ ca na kariṣyāmīti. dharmatāpratilaṃbhikaṃ dhyānasaṃvaro 'nāsravasaṃvaraś ca. bhavasaṃniśritatvād iti. mokṣārthinām api teṣāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādyupahatatvāt. bhavaviśeṣa eva ca teṣāṃ keṣāṃcin mokṣa iti. bhavasaṃniśritam eva śīlaṃ. tato 'sti teṣāṃ samādānaśīlaṃ. na prātimokṣasaṃvara iti. sāmantakam apy atra dhyānaṃ kṛtvocyata iti. yasmāt sāṃantake 'pi dhyānasaṃvaro 'nāsravasaṃvaraś [Tib. 30a] ceṣyate. tasmād dhyānasāmantakam apy atra dhyānaśabdenocyata itīṣyate. apiśabdān maulam api gṛhyata eva. sahabhūhetāv ucyamāna iti.
body.translated_text: [with the resolve] 'I shall not do this or that.' Morality obtained through the nature of things is the <s>dhyāna</s> restraint and the outflow-free restraint. 'Because of being dependent on [mundane] existence' (<s>bhavasaṃniśritatva</s>) — because even those who seek liberation, being afflicted by wrong views and the like — and because for some of them, liberation is merely a special form of existence. Their morality is dependent on existence alone. Therefore they have morality of undertaking, but not <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint. 'The preliminary [concentration] too is spoken of here as <s>dhyāna</s>' — since the <s>dhyāna</s> restraint and outflow-free restraint are also accepted in the preliminary [concentration] (<s>sāmantaka</s>), therefore the preliminary of <s>dhyāna</s> too is spoken of here by the word '<s>dhyāna</s>' — this is accepted. By the word 'also,' the root [concentration] too is included. 'When the co-existent cause is being discussed' —

children.translated_text: 'The mental associates — the two restraints belong to those' —

body.text: ity atra. trayāṇām iti. prātimokṣasaṃvaradhyānasaṃvarānāsravasaṃvarāṇāṃ.
body.translated_text: here. 'Of the three' — of the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint, <s>dhyāna</s> restraint, and outflow-free restraint.

body.text: anyacittācittakasyāpy anuvṛtter iti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of continuing even for one with a different mind or without mind' —

children.translated_text: 'Even for one who is distracted or without mind' —

body.text: vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of this statement.

body.text: (IV.20ab)
body.translated_text: (IV.20ab)

body.text: iti grahaṇaṃ kāmāvacarasyaiva dauḥśīlyasya pratipakṣatvāt. ānaṃtaryamārgeṣv iti. teṣāṃ prahāṇamārgatvāt. tatsamutthāpakānām iti. dauḥśīlyasamutthāpakānām. ata eveti. yasmād anāgamyānantaryamārgeṣv eva tadvyavasthānaṃ. tasmāc catuḥkoṭikaṃ kriyate. prathamā koṭir anāgamyānantaryamārgavarjyo dhyānasaṃvaraḥ. anāgamyabhūmikeṣu vimuktiprayogaviśeṣamārgeṣu maulaprathamadhyānādiṣu vā caturthād dhyānād ānantaryavimuktiprayogaviśeṣamārgeṣu yo dhyānasaṃvaraḥ. ayaṃ dhyānasaṃvaro na prahāṇasaṃvaraḥ. [Tib. 30b] tena dauḥśīlyasya tatsamutthāpakānāṃ ca kleśānām aprahāṇāt. dvitīyānāgamyānantaryamārgeṣv anāsravasaṃvaraḥ. ayaṃ prahāṇasaṃvaraḥ tenaiva dauḥśīlyādiprahāṇāt. na dhyānasaṃvaro 'nāsravatvāt. tṛtīyānāgamyānantaryamārgeṣu sāsravasaṃvaraḥ ayaṃ prahāṇasaṃvaraś ca tena dauḥśīlyādiprahāṇāt. dhyānasaṃvaraś ca sāsravasamādhijatvāt. caturthī anāgamyānantaryamārgavarjyo 'nāsravasaṃvaraḥ. ayaṃ na dhyānasaṃvaro 'nāsravatvāt. nāpi prahāṇasaṃvaras tena dauḥśīlyādyaprahāṇāt. sa punas tathaivānāgamyabhūmikeṣu vimuktiprayogaviśeṣamārgeṣu vistareṇa yo 'nāsravasaṃvaraḥ. saṃvaraniyamenaivam uktam. anyathāpy anye dharmā vaktavyāḥ syuḥ. evaṃ syād anāsravasaṃvaro na prahāṇasaṃvara iti catuṣkoṭikaṃ. prathamā koṭir anāgamyānantaryamārgavarjyo 'nāsravasaṃvaraḥ.
body.translated_text: The word 'iti' is used because it is the antidote only to the immorality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>) of the Desire Realm. 'In the uninterrupted paths (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>)' — because those are the paths of abandonment. 'Of those that give rise to it' — of those that give rise to immorality. 'For this very reason' — since its establishment is only in the preliminary concentration (<s>anāgamya</s>) and the uninterrupted paths, therefore a fourfold classification (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>) is made. The first alternative: <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint (<s>dhyānasaṃvara</s>) excluding the uninterrupted paths of the preliminary concentration — the <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint in the liberation, preparatory, and special paths of the preliminary-concentration ground, or in the uninterrupted, liberation, preparatory, and special paths from the first fundamental <s>dhyāna</s> onward up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. This <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint is not abandonment-restraint (<s>prahāṇasaṃvara</s>), because immorality and the afflictions that give rise to it are not abandoned thereby. The second: the outflow-free restraint (<s>anāsravasaṃvara</s>) in the uninterrupted paths of the preliminary concentration. This is abandonment-restraint, because immorality and the rest are abandoned thereby. It is not <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint, because of being outflow-free. The third: the contaminated restraint (<s>sāsravasaṃvara</s>) in the uninterrupted paths of the preliminary concentration — this is both abandonment-restraint, because immorality and the rest are abandoned thereby, and <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint, because of being born from contaminated concentration. The fourth: the outflow-free restraint excluding the uninterrupted paths of the preliminary concentration. This is not <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint, because of being outflow-free. Nor is it abandonment-restraint, because immorality and the rest are not abandoned thereby. And that, similarly, is the outflow-free restraint in the liberation, preparatory, and special paths of the preliminary-concentration ground — in detail. This is stated with restriction to restraint alone. Otherwise, other <s>dharma</s>s too would have to be mentioned. Thus there would be the fourfold classification: outflow-free restraint that is not abandonment-restraint. The first alternative: outflow-free restraint excluding the uninterrupted paths of the preliminary concentration.

body.text: (IV.20cd) manaḥsaṃvaro 'pi smṛtisaṃprajñānasvabhāvaḥ indriyasaṃvaro 'pi smṛtisaṃprajñānasvabhāva iti dvisvabhāvajñāpanārthaṃ [Tib. 31] dvigrahaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: (IV.20cd) The mind-restraint (<s>manaḥsaṃvara</s>) too has the nature of mindfulness and clear comprehension (<s>smṛtisaṃprajñāna</s>), and the sense-faculty restraint (<s>indriyasaṃvara</s>) too has the nature of mindfulness and clear comprehension — the dual mention is for the purpose of indicating two natures.

body.text: dvivacananirdeśād eva hi dvitvasiddhiḥ. kathaṃ punar gamyate. etāv evaṃsvabhāvād iti. āgamāt. anyatarā kila devatā bhikṣuṃ viṣayeṣv indriyāṇi vicārayantam avocat. bhikṣo bhikṣo vraṇaṃ mā kārṣīd iti. bhikṣur āha. pidhāsyāmi devate. devatāha. kuṃbhamātraṃ bhikṣo vraṇaṃ kṛtvā kena pidhāsyasi. bhikṣur āha. smṛtyā devate pidhāsyāmi. saṃprajanyena ceti.
body.translated_text: For the establishment of duality is from the very instruction in dual expression. But how is it understood that these two have this very nature? From scripture (<s>āgama</s>). A certain deity, it is said, addressed a monk who was letting his senses wander among objects: 'Monk, monk, do not make a wound!' The monk replied: 'I shall cover it, deity.' The deity said: 'Having made a wound the size of a pot, monk, with what will you cover it?' The monk replied: 'With mindfulness, deity, I shall cover it. And with clear comprehension.'

body.text: (IV.21, 22) sa yāvat tām avijñaptiṃ na tyajatīti. śikṣānikṣepādi.
body.translated_text: (IV.21, 22) As long as he does not abandon that non-informative action (<s>avijñapti</s>) — meaning: the abandonment of the training rules and the like.

children.translated_text: 'From the moment onward, with the past [avijñapti]' —

body.text: prathame kṣaṇe vartamānasyaiva samanvāgato bhavatīty uktaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: it is stated that in the first moment, one is endowed only with the present [<s>avijñapti</s>].

children.translated_text: 'One possessing <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint is always [endowed] with the past and unarisen [avijñapti]' —

body.text: dhyānasaṃvaravān kiṃ pṛthagjano 'thāryaḥ. ubhaya ity āha. aviśeṣitatvāt. so 'tītānāgatayā avijñaptyā samanvāgataḥ. kiṃlakṣaṇayā. dhyānasaṃvarādhikārād dhyānasaṃvaralakṣaṇayeti gamyate. sa janmāntaratyaktam iti. udāharaṇapradarśanaparam etat. idaṃ janma tyaktam api hi gṛhyate.
body.translated_text: one possessing <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint — is this an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) or a Noble One (<s>ārya</s>)? He says: both. Because no distinction is made. That one is endowed with past and future <s>avijñapti</s>. Of what characteristic? Since this is in the context of <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint, it is understood to be of <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint characteristic. 'That one, abandoned in a previous life' — this serves to show an example. For [<s>avijñapti</s>] abandoned in this very life is also grasped.

children.translated_text: 'But a Noble One, in the first [moment], not with the past [avijñapti]' —

body.text: āryaḥ sadātītājātayā avijñaptyā [Tib. 31b] samanvāgataḥ. kiṃlakṣaṇayā. anāsravayā. āryādhikārāt. ata evāha. āryapudgalo 'py evam anāsravayeti. ayaṃ tu viśeṣa iti. tuśabdārthaṃ darśayati. sa ca bhinnakramaḥ. prathame tu kṣaṇe duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāntikṣaṇe nābhyatītayā avijñaptyā samanvāgata ity arthaḥ. kasmāt. anādimati saṃsāre mārgasya pūrvam anutpāditatvāt. nanu ca phalaprāptikāla indriyasaṃcārakāle 'pi vā pūrvamārgatyāge naivātītayā avijñaptyā samanvāgama iṣyate. evaṃ tarhi sa cāpi phalamārgasya prathamakṣaṇo bhavati. tatra nātītayāvijñaptyā samanvāgato bhavati. phalamārgasya pūrvam anutpāditatvād iti vyākhyātavyaṃ. ācāryavasumitras tv asya codyasya parihāram āha. anāsravasaṃvaro 'tra prakṛtaḥ. sa ca duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāntikāla eva labdhaḥ. atas tena prathame kṣaṇe nātītena samanvāgato dvitīyādiṣv atītānāgateneti. ūrdhvaṃ tu yo mārgāntaralābhaḥ. tatrānāsravasaṃvarasādṛśyam astīti na tad ucyata iti. tad iha sādṛśyam astīti na budhyāmahe. kiṃ sāsravasaṃvaro 'stīty apekṣyedam ucyate. āho svid anāsravo 'stīti. yadi sāsravo 'stīty abhiprīyate. [Tib. 32a] duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāntikāle 'pi so 'stīti nātītayā samanvāgata iti pratiṣedhānupapattiḥ. atha phalaprāptikāle 'tītānāsravasaṃvaro 'stīty abhiprīyate. vihīnaḥ sa katham astīti śakyaṃ vaktum iti cintyo 'syābhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: a Noble One is always endowed with past and unarisen <s>avijñapti</s>. Of what characteristic? Of outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) [characteristic]. Because this is in the context of Noble Ones. Therefore he says: 'A Noble person too, likewise, with outflow-free [<s>avijñapti</s>].' 'But there is this distinction' — he shows the meaning of the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>). And that has a broken sequence. But in the first moment — the moment of the <s>duḥkhadharma­jñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the knowledge of suffering as a <s>dharma</s>) — one is not endowed with past <s>avijñapti</s>, is the meaning. Why? Because in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, the path has never before been produced. But is it not accepted that even at the time of obtaining the fruit, or at the time of sense-faculty activity, through the abandonment of a prior path, one is not endowed with past <s>avijñapti</s>? In that case, that too is the first moment of the fruit-path. There, one is not endowed with past <s>avijñapti</s>, because the fruit-path has never before been produced — thus it should be explained. But <s>Ācārya Vasumitra</s> states the resolution of this objection: outflow-free restraint is the subject here. And that is obtained only at the time of <s>duḥkhadharma­jñānakṣānti</s>. Therefore, in the first moment one is not endowed with the past [outflow-free restraint], and from the second moment onward with the past and future. But as for the subsequent attainment of another path, there is similarity to outflow-free restraint therein, so it is not mentioned. Here, we do not understand what the similarity consists in. Is it said with reference to [the question] 'does contaminated restraint exist?' or 'does outflow-free [restraint] exist?' If the intent is 'contaminated exists,' then even at the time of <s>duḥkhadharma­jñānakṣānti</s> that exists, so the negation 'not endowed with the past' would be unjustified. If the intent is 'past outflow-free restraint exists at the time of obtaining the fruit,' then since it has been lost, how can it be said to exist? — his intention should be considered thus.

children.translated_text: 'One established in concentrated or Noble path' —

body.text: iti. samāhitamārgasthaś ca laukikasamāhitamārgasthaḥ āryamārgasthaś ca
body.translated_text: meaning: one established in the concentrated [mundane] path, and one established in the Noble path —

children.translated_text: the two established in concentrated and Noble paths.

body.text: dhyānānāsravasaṃvarānvitāv ity arthaḥ. atra cāryamārgābhirūḍha āryamārgastho veditavyo nausthanāyena. tadyathā yo nāvam abhirūḍhaḥ. sa nausthaḥ. evaṃ ya āryamārgam abhirūḍhaḥ samāpannaḥ. sa āryamārgasthaḥ. anyathā hy āryamārgasamanvito 'py āryamārgastha iti kṛtvā. prakṛtistho 'py āryo vartamānayā anāsravayā avijñaptyā samanvāgata iti prāpnoti. anyaḥ punar evaṃprasaṃgaṃ pariharan vyācaṣṭe. ekaśeṣo 'tra kriyate. samāhitaś ca samāhitāryamārgaś ca mārgau samāhitāryamārgau. tayoḥ sthitau
body.translated_text: The meaning is: endowed with <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint and outflow-free restraint respectively. And here, 'one established in the Noble path' should be understood as one who has mounted the Noble path, by the analogy of a ship — just as one who has boarded a ship is 'one established on the ship,' so one who has mounted, entered upon, the Noble path is 'one established in the Noble path.' Otherwise, even one who possesses the Noble path [but is not in meditation], treating such as 'one established in the Noble path,' would entail that even a Noble One in the natural state would be endowed with present outflow-free <s>avijñapti</s>. Another [commentator], avoiding this consequence, explains: a residual compound (<s>ekaśeṣa</s>) is made here — 'concentrated' and 'concentrated Noble path' are the two paths, 'concentrated-and-Noble-paths.' Established in those two —

body.text: tau yathākramaṃ vartamānayā dhyānasaṃvarāvijñaptyānāsrava[Tib. 32b] saṃvarāvijñaptyā ca samanvāgatau. na tu vyutthitau. na tu tanmārgavyutthitau tayā vartamānayā samanvāgatau. tasyāś cittānuparivartanīyatvāt. evaṃ vyākhyāyate. yac coditam ācāryasaṃghabhadreṇa. katham avijñapteḥ pratyutpannatā āryamārgasthavacanād eva gamyate. tatsamāpanna evāyaṃ. na punas tatsamanvāgamavacanaprasaṃga iti cet. na. dhyānādhikārāt. tatravijñaptyabhāvāc ca.
body.translated_text: Those two are respectively endowed with present <s>avijñapti</s> of <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint and outflow-free restraint. But not when emerged — not when emerged from those respective paths are they endowed with that present [<s>avijñapti</s>], because it follows the mind. Thus it is explained. And what was objected by <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> — 'How is the present-ness of <s>avijñapti</s> understood merely from the statement of being established in the Noble path? This one has entered that [path]; there should then be no need for the statement of endowment' — this is not [a valid objection]. Because this is in the context of <s>dhyāna</s>. And because <s>avijñapti</s> does not exist therein [in the formless realm].

body.text: (IV.23ab) yo naivasaṃvaraṇāsaṃvare sthitas sa madhyastha iti. yo na bhikṣvādiḥ. na ca kaivartādiḥ. sa madhyasthaḥ. dauḥśīlyaśīlāṃgādisaṃgṛhīteti. dauḥśīlyaṃ prāṇātipātādi. śīlāṃgaṃ prāṇātipātaviratyādi. yan nasaṃvaraṇāsaṃvarasaṃgṛhītam. ādiśabdena stūpavandanākhaṭacapeṭādikriyāvijñaptir gṛhyate.
body.translated_text: (IV.23ab) One who is established in neither-restraint-nor-non-restraint is one who is neutral (<s>madhyastha</s>) — one who is not a monk and the like, nor a fisherman and the like. That one is neutral. 'Included in immorality and moral components and the like' — immorality is killing living beings and the like. Moral component (<s>śīlāṃga</s>) is refraining from killing and the like. That which is included in neither restraint nor non-restraint. By the word 'and the like,' the <s>avijñapti</s> of actions such as <s>stūpa</s>-worship, slapping, and the like is grasped.

body.text: (IV.23cd,24ab) asaṃvarasaṃvarasthau pudgalāv akuśalakuśaladharmapratiṣṭhitāv ity anayor viparyayam asaṃbhāvayan pṛcchati. kim asaṃvarastha iti vistaraḥ. tau yāvad anuvartete iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.23cd, 24ab) Not considering the reversal possible for the two persons established in non-restraint and restraint — persons established in unwholesome and wholesome <s>dharma</s>s — he asks: 'Is one established in non-restraint —' and so forth in detail. 'As long as they continue' —

children.translated_text: the impulse of faith and the impulse of affliction.

body.text: anyeṣv atītayāpīti. dvitīyakṣaṇādiṣu atītayā.
body.translated_text: 'In the others too, with the past [<s>avijñapti</s>]' — in the second moment and onward, with the past [<s>avijñapti</s>].

body.text: (IV.24cd, 25ab) kṣaṇād ūrdhvam ā tyāgād [Tib. 33a] iti. yo yasyās tyāgas tasmād ā tyāgāt tayātītayā vijñaptyā samanvāgataḥ. kathaṃ. saṃvaralakṣaṇāyās tāvad vijñaptes tyāgaḥ śikṣānikṣepādibhiḥ. tasmād ā tyāgād anayātītayā vijñaptyā samanvāgataḥ. asaṃvaralakṣaṇāyāḥ saṃvarasamādānādibhis tyāgaḥ. tesmād ā tyāgād anayā samanvāgataḥ. naivasaṃvaranāsaṃvaralakṣaṇāyāḥ prasādakleśavegacchedādibhis tyāgaḥ. tasmād ā tyāgād anayā samanvāgata iti. yo hi saṃvarādyavijñaptisamanvāgataḥ. so 'vaśyaṃ maulakarmapathasvabhāvayā kṣaṇād ūrdhvam atītayāvijñaptyā samanvāgataḥ. anāgatayā tu vijñaptyā na kaścit
body.translated_text: (IV.24cd, 25ab) 'From the moment onward until abandonment' — whoever's abandonment of whichever [<s>avijñapti</s>], from that [moment] until that abandonment, one is endowed with that past <s>vijñapti</s> (informative action). How? First, the abandonment of <s>vijñapti</s> characterized as restraint is through abandoning the training rules and the like. Therefore, from that [moment] until that abandonment, one is endowed with that past <s>vijñapti</s>. The abandonment of [<s>vijñapti</s>] characterized as non-restraint is through undertaking restraint and the like. Therefore, from that [moment] until that abandonment, one is endowed with that [past <s>vijñapti</s>]. The abandonment of [<s>vijñapti</s>] characterized as neither-restraint-nor-non-restraint is through the cessation of the impulse of faith or affliction and the like. Therefore, from that [moment] until that abandonment, one is endowed with it. For one who is endowed with <s>avijñapti</s> of restraint and the rest, that one is necessarily endowed, from the moment onward, with past <s>avijñapti</s> having the nature of the fundamental action-paths. But with future <s>vijñapti</s>, no one

body.text: samanvāgata iti. cittānanuparivartanīyatvāt. cittasyāpīti. cittasyāpi tarhi nivṛtāvyākṛtasya mā bhūt prāptiḥ. anubandhinī mā bhūd ity arthaḥ. kasmād ity āha. jaḍā hi vijñaptir anālambanatvāt. parataṃtra ca cittaparatantratvāt. na caivaṃ cittam iti. na jaḍaṃ. na parataṃtraṃ cety arthaḥ. kasmāt. tadviparyayāt sā durbalena nivṛtāvyākṛtena cittenotthāpitā durbalatarā bhavatīti.
body.translated_text: is endowed — because it does not follow the mind. 'Of the mind too' — then let there be no acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>) of the mind too, of the obstructed-indeterminate [mind]. The meaning is: let it not be a following [acquisition]. Why? — he says: for <s>vijñapti</s> is inert (<s>jaḍā</s>), because of having no object (<s>anālambanatvāt</s>). And it is dependent on another (<s>paratantra</s>), because of being dependent on the mind. 'But the mind is not so' — not inert, and not dependent on another — this is the meaning. Why? Because of the opposite of that. That [<s>vijñapti</s>], being produced by the weak obstructed-indeterminate mind, becomes even weaker.

body.text: (IV.25cd) maulasaṃgṛhītatvād [Tib. 33b] iti. cetanāyāḥ tadarthatvāt.
body.translated_text: (IV.25cd) 'Because of being included in the fundamental [action-paths]' — because volition (<s>cetanā</s>) has that as its purpose.

children.translated_text: 'One who is neutral, acting with mild volition, is endowed only with <s>vijñapti</s>' —

body.text: iti. madhyasthagrahaṇaṃ saṃvarāsaṃvarasthanirāsārthaṃ. saṃvarāsaṃvarasthā hi vijñaptyavijñaptibhyām avaśyaṃ samanvāgatāḥ. mṛducetanagrahaṇaṃ tīvracetananirāsārthaṃ. tīvracetanā hi vijñaptiṃ kurvann avijñaptiṃ samutthāpayet. prāg evāvyākṛtam iti. mṛdvyā cetanayā prāg evāvyākṛtaṃ kurvan. yatra hi mṛdvyā cetanayā kuśalam akuśalaṃ vā kurvan naivasaṃvaranāsaṃvare sthito vijñaptyaiva samanvāgato bhavati avijñapter anutpādāt. prāg evāvyākṛtaṃ kurvan sutarāṃ vijñaptyaivāsau samanvāgato nāvijñaptyā. avijñaptyutpādāśaṃkāyā abhāvāt. anyatreti vistaraḥ. anyatra saptabhya aupadhikebhyaḥ puṇyakriyāvastubhyaḥ. karmapathebhyaś ca prāṇātipātādibhyaḥ. tatra hy avyākṛtam api kurvann avijñaptyā samanvāgato bhavati. satatasamitaṃ carato vā tiṣṭhato vā vistareṇa yāvad upajāyata eva puṇyam iti sūtre vacanāt. prāṇātipātādīṃś ca karmapathāṃ mṛducetanayāpi kurvan avijñaptyā samanvāgato bhavati. [Tib. 34a] yenāryapudgaleneti vistaraḥ. parivṛttajanmanāryapudgalena yadā na tāvad vijñaptaṃ bhavati. kalalādyavasthāyām ārūpyopapattau ca. vijñaptaṃ vā punar vihīnam avyākṛtacittotthāpitavijñaptivihīnāc ca. na hi tasyāḥ prāptir anubandhinī bhavati. kṛtastūpādikasya vā. tadvastucchedāt. sa hi tadānīm avijñaptim api parityajati prāg eva vijñaptim iti. āsv avasthāsu janmāntaraparivṛttāv āryapudgalo 'nāsravayaivāvijñaptyā janmāntaralabdhayā samanvāgato na vijñaptyā. nanu ca pṛthagjanasyāpy ayaṃ vidhiḥ saṃbhavati. saṃbhavati. anāvaśyakatvāt tu pṛthagjano noktaḥ. yo hi dhyānalābhī parivṛttajanmāntaraḥ rūpadhātāv akṛtavijñaptiḥ kṛtavijñaptivihīno vā. sa eva tathā saṃbhavati nānya iti. kāmāvacarasattvābhisaṃdhivacanād vā. atha vā udāharaṇarūpa āryapudgala uktas tena pṛthagjano 'pi tathā grahītavyaḥ. ata eva
body.translated_text: the mention of 'neutral' (<s>madhyastha</s>) is for the purpose of excluding those established in restraint and non-restraint. For those established in restraint and non-restraint are necessarily endowed with both <s>vijñapti</s> and <s>avijñapti</s>. The mention of 'mild volition' (<s>mṛducetanā</s>) is for the purpose of excluding intense volition. For one acting with intense volition would generate <s>avijñapti</s> along with <s>vijñapti</s>. 'All the more so with indeterminate [action]' — all the more so when acting with mild volition in indeterminate [matters]. For when one established in neither-restraint-nor-non-restraint acts with mild volition in wholesome or unwholesome [matters], one is endowed only with <s>vijñapti</s>, because <s>avijñapti</s> does not arise. All the more so when acting in indeterminate [matters], that one is endowed only with <s>vijñapti</s>, not with <s>avijñapti</s>, because there is no possibility of <s>avijñapti</s> arising. 'Except' — and so forth in detail. Except for the seven material bases of meritorious action (<s>aupadhika puṇyakriyāvastu</s>). And except for the action-paths of killing and the rest. For therein, even when performing indeterminate [action], one is endowed with <s>avijñapti</s> — because of the <s>sūtra</s> statement: 'For one who constantly and continuously walks, stands — in detail — up to: merit indeed arises.' And even when performing the action-paths of killing and the rest with mild volition, one is endowed with <s>avijñapti</s>. 'By a Noble person who has changed births' — and so forth in detail. By a Noble person who has been reborn in a different life — when there is no <s>vijñapti</s>, as in the embryonic stage (<s>kalalā</s>) and the like, or at rebirth in the Formless Realm. Or when <s>vijñapti</s> has been abandoned — being devoid of <s>vijñapti</s> produced by indeterminate mind. For acquisition of that [<s>vijñapti</s>] is not a following [acquisition]. Or for one who has built a <s>stūpa</s> and the like — because of the destruction of that object. For at that time, one abandons even <s>avijñapti</s>, let alone <s>vijñapti</s>. In these states, a Noble person reborn in a different life is endowed only with outflow-free <s>avijñapti</s> obtained in a previous life, not with <s>vijñapti</s>. But is not this same situation possible for an ordinary person too? It is possible. But because it is not necessary, the ordinary person is not mentioned. For only one who has attained <s>dhyāna</s>, has been reborn in a different life, in the Form Realm, has not performed <s>vijñapti</s>, or is devoid of performed <s>vijñapti</s> — only such a one is possible [in this situation], not another. Or because the statement refers to beings of the Desire Realm. Or alternatively, the Noble person is mentioned as an example, and by that the ordinary person too should be understood likewise. Therefore

children.translated_text: 'One who is neutral, acting with mild volition, is endowed only with <s>vijñapti</s>' —

body.text: ity atrokto 'nyatraupadhikapuṇyakriyāvastukarmapathebhya iti. sāvaśeṣam etad vacanam iti kṛtvā. evaṃ dve koṭī sūtrite prathamadvitīye [Tib. 34b] tṛtīyacaturthyau tu yojye. tṛtīyā saṃvarāsaṃvaramadhyasthās tīvrayā cetanayā kuśalam akuśalaṃ vā kurvantaḥ. caturthī yena janmāntaraparivṛttau pṛthagjanena na tāvad vijñaptaṃ bhavati. vijñaptaṃ vā vihīnam iti.
body.translated_text: thus 'apart from the action-paths that are material bases of meritorious action' is stated here. Taking this statement as having a remainder. Thus two alternatives are formulated in the <s>sūtra</s>, the first and second; [Tib. 34b] but the third and fourth are to be supplied. The third: those who are intermediate between restraint and non-restraint, performing wholesome or unwholesome [acts] with intense volition. The fourth: an ordinary person whose turn of births has not yet reached [the point of] informative [action], or whose informative [action] has been lost.

body.text: (IV.27) sahabhūtatvād iti. yasmād dhyānacittena saha bhavati dhyānasaṃvaraḥ. paro vijñāpayatīti pratyāpayati. pudgalād anya iti. śrāmaṇeraśrāmaṇeryupāsakopāsikopavāsasaṃvarāḥ. niyāmāvakrāntyā āryamārgāvatāraṇena. paṃcakānām ājñātakauṇḍinyādīnāṃ. ehibhikṣukayeti ehi bhikṣo cara brahmacaryam iti bhagavato vacane. ehīti coktaḥ sugatena tāyinā muṇḍaś ca kāṣāyadharo babhūveti. śāstur abhyupagamān mahākāśyapasyeti. mahākāśyapaḥ kila yāṃyāṃ devatāpratimāṃ vandate. sāsā sphuṭati. tasya mahānubhāvāt. sa bhagavantam upasaṃkramya na vandate. māsya rūpavināśo bhūd iti. tam abhiprāyaṃ viditvā bhagavāṃś codayati sma. vandasva kāśyapa tathāgatam iti. tena bhagavān vanditaḥ. tataḥ sa bhagavato rūpam avikopitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ayaṃ me śāsteti sa bhagavantam abhyupagatād [Tib. 35]a asyopasaṃpad iti. praśnārādhanena sodāyina iti. sodāyinā praśnavisarjanena bhagavān ārādhitas tenārādhanena tasyopasaṃpat. gurudharmābhyupagameneti. aṣṭau gurudharmāḥ. bhikṣor antikād bhikṣuṇīnām upasaṃpat bhikṣuṇībhāvaḥ. anvardhamāsam avavādo grāhyo bhikṣor antikāt. abhikṣuke āvāse varṣā nopagantavyā. pravāraṇāyām ubhayasaṃghas tribhiḥ sthānaiḥ pravārayitavyaḥ. na codayitavyo bhikṣur āpattim āpannaḥ nākroṣṭavyaḥ. gurudharmāpattau mānāpyam ardhamāsaṃ caritavyaṃ. varṣaśatopasaṃpannayāpy bhikṣuṇyā tatkṣaṇopasaṃpanno bhikṣur vandyaḥ. na ca bhikṣuṇyā kvacid bhikṣuś codayitavyaḥ. ity evamādayaḥ. eṣām abhyupagamena tasyā upasaṃpat. dūtena dharmadinnāyā iti. tayā kilāntaḥpuragatayaiva pravrajyārthaṃ buddhāya dūtaḥ preṣita iti. vinayadharapañcameneti. catvāro bhikṣavaḥ saṃghaḥ. tatra jñaptivācakena paṃcamenopasaṃpādyate pratyantikeṣu janapadeṣu. madhyameṣu tu janapadeṣu daśamena jñaptivācakenopasaṃpādyate. ṣaṣṭibhadravargapūgopasaṃpāditānām [Tib. 35b] iti. bhadro varga eṣām iti. bhadravargāṇāṃ ṣaṣṭiḥ kulaputrāḥ. teṣāṃ pūgena samūhenopasaṃpāditānāṃ. śaraṇagamanatraivācikena buddhaśaraṇaṃ gacchāma iti trirvacanenopasaṃpat. teṣāṃ nāvaśyaṃ vijñaptyadhīna iti. teṣāṃ vinayadharāṇām idam mataṃ. nāvaśyaṃ vijñaptyadhīnaḥ prātimokṣasaṃvara
body.translated_text: (IV.27) 'Because of being co-existent' — because the <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint (<s>dhyānasaṃvara</s>) exists together with the <s>dhyāna</s>-mind. 'Another causes one to understand' — meaning: causes one to accept. 'Different from the person' — the restraints of novices (<s>śrāmaṇera</s>), female novices (<s>śrāmaṇerī</s>), male lay followers (<s>upāsaka</s>), female lay followers (<s>upāsikā</s>), and the fasting vow (<s>upavāsa</s>). 'Through entering the definite course' (<s>niyāmāvakrānti</s>) — through entering the Noble Path. 'Of the group of five' — <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s> and the others. 'By the "Come, monk" formula' (<s>ehibhikṣuka</s>) — by the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words: 'Come, monk, practice the holy life.' 'And when the <s>Sugata</s>, the Protector, said "Come," he became tonsured and wearing ochre robes.' 'Through the master's acceptance, [in the case] of <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>' — <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, it is said, used to bow to whatever image of a deity [he encountered], and that image would split apart because of his great power. Having approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he did not bow — [thinking] 'may there not be destruction of his form.' Knowing that intention, the <s>Bhagavān</s> urged him: 'Bow, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, to the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' He bowed to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then, seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s form undamaged, [he thought] 'this is my teacher,' and he accepted the <s>Bhagavān</s> — [Tib. 35a] from his acceptance came his ordination. 'Through satisfying with questions, [in the case] of <s>Sodāyin</s>' — <s>Sodāyin</s> satisfied the <s>Bhagavān</s> by answering his questions; through that satisfaction came his ordination. 'Through acceptance of the weighty <s>dharma</s>s' — the eight weighty <s>dharma</s>s: nuns' ordination, their becoming <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>s, is from a <s>bhikṣu</s>. Instruction is to be received from a <s>bhikṣu</s> every half-month. The rains retreat is not to be observed in a place without <s>bhikṣu</s>s. At the invitation (<s>pravāraṇā</s>), both <s>saṃgha</s>s are to be invited to comment on three grounds. A <s>bhikṣu</s> who has committed an offense is not to be admonished or rebuked [by a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>]. For a grave offense, a <s>mānāpya</s> penance of a half-month is to be observed. Even a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> ordained a hundred years must bow to a <s>bhikṣu</s> ordained at that very moment. And a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> must never admonish a <s>bhikṣu</s>. These and similar [rules]. Through acceptance of these, her ordination [was conferred]. 'By messenger, [in the case] of <s>Dharmadinnā</s>' — she, while still within the inner quarters, sent a messenger to the <s>Buddha</s> for the purpose of going forth. 'With a <s>Vinaya</s>-holder as fifth' — four <s>bhikṣu</s>s constitute a <s>saṃgha</s>. Therein, in border regions, one is ordained with a fifth who is the announcer of the formal act (<s>jñaptivācaka</s>). But in the central regions, one is ordained with a tenth as announcer. 'Of the sixty of the <s>Bhadravargīya</s>s ordained in a group' — [Tib. 35b] those whose group is auspicious are the <s>Bhadravargīyas</s>. Sixty sons of good family. By their group, by their assembly, they were ordained. 'By the three-fold recitation of taking refuge' — ordination through the threefold recitation 'I go to the <s>Buddha</s> for refuge.' 'For those [<s>Vinaya</s>-holders], the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint is not necessarily dependent on informative action' — this is the view of those <s>Vinaya</s>-holders: the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint is not necessarily dependent on <s>vijñapti</s>

body.text: iti. buddhaprabhṛtīnām avijñaptidhīnatvāt. atha vā teṣām iti yeṣāṃ vijñaptir nāsty upasaṃpatkriyāyāṃ.
body.translated_text: because for the <s>Buddha</s> and others, it depends on <s>avijñapti</s>. Or alternatively, 'for those' means: for those who have no <s>vijñapti</s> in the ordination procedure.

body.text: (IV.28ab)
body.translated_text: (IV.28ab)

body.text: iti saṃvarasya. kālo nityaḥ padārtho 'stīty eke. tadāśaṃkayā pṛcchati. kālo nāma ka eṣa dharma iti. kāla ity asyābhidhānasya kim abhidheyam ity arthaḥ. saṃskāraparidīpanādhivacanam etad iti. saṃskārāṇām atītānāgatapratyutpannānām abhidyotakaṃ nāmeti. tadyathātītaḥ kālo yāvat pratyutpanna iti traiyadhvikāḥ saṃskārā eva gamyaṃte. tena ca tatrāprayogād iti. tena visabhāgenāśrayeṇa tatra samādāne aprayogāt. asmaraṇāc ca tenāśrayeṇa tatsamādānaṃ na samarati. vaibhāṣika āha. kutas tv etad evaṃ tarkyate. yathānantaram uktaṃ. ācārya āha. pareṇāpi saṃvarotpattau yuktyavirodhād iti. nātra yuktir virudhyate. yathā jīvitād ūrdhvaṃ saty api samādāne [Tib. 36a] saṃvarotpattau yuktivirodho visabhāgāśrayatvād ity evamādi. na kālāntaravipannam eti ahorātrādiyāvatkriyāśayena.
body.translated_text: meaning: of the <s>saṃvara</s>. 'Some hold that time (<s>kāla</s>) is an eternal category.' Out of suspicion of that, one asks: 'What <s>dharma</s> is this called time?' The meaning is: what is the referent of the designation 'time'? 'This is an illuminating term for conditioned things' — a name that illuminates past, future, and present conditioned things. For example: past time, up to present — conditioned things of the three time-periods are understood. 'And because of non-exertion with that [dissimilar] support for that [undertaking]' — because of the non-exertion for that undertaking with a dissimilar support. 'And because of not remembering' — with that [dissimilar] support, one does not remember that undertaking. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'From what is this thus inferred?' — just as what was stated next. The master says: 'Even by the arising of restraint through another [person], there is no contradiction with reason.' The reason is not contradicted here: just as, after death, even though the undertaking exists, [Tib. 36a] there is a contradiction with reason for the arising of restraint because of the dissimilar support — and so forth. 'Not lost due to a different time-period' — by the intention of a day-and-night-period and so forth.

body.text: (IV.28cd) avijñaptivad asaṃvaro 'pi nāsti dravyata iti. yathā nāsty avijñaptir dravyata iti pratipāditaṃ. tathā asaṃvaro 'pi na dravyato 'sti. cetanāvyatirikta ity abhiprāyaḥ. pāpakriyābhisaṃdhir iti. pāpakriyābhiprāya ity arthaḥ. sānubandha iti savāsana ity arthaḥ. savāsanaś cetanāviśeṣo 'saṃvara ity arthaḥ. yato 'nubandhāt tadvān asaṃvaravān ity ucyate. asaṃvarika ity arthaḥ. tasyānirākṛtatvāt. tasyābhisaṃdheḥ sānubandhasyānirākṛtatvāt. tadviruddhayā cetanayānupahatatvād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.28cd) 'Non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>) too does not exist as a substance, like <s>avijñapti</s>' — just as it has been demonstrated that <s>avijñapti</s> does not exist as a substance, so too non-restraint does not exist as a substance. The intent is: [it is] not different from volition (<s>cetanā</s>). 'The intention of evil action' — meaning: the intention of evil action. 'With residual impression' (<s>sānubandha</s>) means with latent tendency (<s>savāsana</s>), is the meaning. A special volition with latent tendency is non-restraint, is the meaning. Because of the residual impression, one possessing it is called 'one possessing non-restraint' — meaning: one characterized by non-restraint. 'Because of its non-repudiation' — because of the non-repudiation of that intention with its residual impression. The meaning is: because of not being damaged by a contrary volition.

body.text: (IV.29) sa bhuktvāpi gṛhṇīyād iti. sūryodaya eva saṃvara uttiṣṭhate. samādānaniyamacittasyotthāpakatvāt. bhuktvāgrahaṇaṃ tv abhivyaktyarthaṃ. kapotakam iti. aṃguṣṭharahitasyāṃgulicatuṣkasyeturahastāṃguṣṭhapradeśinyor antarālavinyasanāt kapotakaḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.29) 'Even after eating, one may take [the vow]' — the restraint arises at sunrise itself, because of the power of the mind that is determined to undertake [the vow]. But the mention of 'after eating' is for the purpose of making it manifest. '<s>Kapotaka</s>' — because of placing the thumb-free four fingers between the thumb and index finger, [the gesture is called] <s>kapotaka</s> (pigeon-like).

body.text: pārājikābhāvaḥ saṃghavaśeṣādyabhāvaḥ.
body.translated_text: the absence of <s>pārājika</s> [offenses], the absence of <s>saṃghavaśeṣa</s> and other [offenses].

body.text: iti niyamaḥ. tadabhāvād ity akālabhojanāt. ubhayaṃ na syād iti. smṛtiḥ saṃvegaś ca.
body.translated_text: means a rule. 'Because of its absence' — meaning: because of eating at an improper time. 'Both would not exist' — meaning: mindfulness and spiritual urgency.

body.text: na tu teṣām iti vistareṇācāryo vaibhāṣikamataṃ yuktyā [Tib. 36b] virodhayati. na tu teṣām eva samyagdṛṣṭyādīnāṃ samyagdṛṣṭidharmapravicayasaṃbodhyaṃgasamādhīnāṃ. ta eva samyagdṛṣṭyādayo 'ṅgatvāga kalpaṃte. yujyanta ity arthaḥ. kasmāt. yuktivirodhāt. pūrvakāḥ samyagdṛṣṭyādaya
body.translated_text: 'But not of those' — in detail, the master refutes the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> view with reasoning. [Tib. 36b] 'But not those very right views and the rest — the right view that is discrimination of <s>dharma</s>s, the awakening-factor of investigation, the concentrations' — those very right views and the rest are deemed to be factors. They are deemed fitting, is the meaning. Why? Because of contradiction with reasoning. The earlier right views and the rest

body.text: uttareṣāṃ samyagdṛṣṭyādīnām aṅgaṃ yadi syur iti vyavasthāpyate. evam asyāṃ kalpanāyāṃ prathamakṣaṇotpanna āryamārgo nāṣṭāṃgaḥ syāt. na hi tatra pūrvotpannā samyagdṛṣṭir aṅgam astīti. saptāṅgaḥ syāt. bodhyaṃgeṣv api paścimaḥ kṣaṇo na bodhyaṃgaṃ syāt. na hy anyā pareṇa bodhir asti yasyās tad aṅgaṃ syāt. atha matam anāgatāyā bodhes tad aṃgam iti. anāgatabodhir na syāt. evaṃ samādhir yojyaḥ.
body.translated_text: if they were factors of the later right views and the rest — thus it is established. In this imagination, the Noble Path arisen at the first moment would not be eightfold. For there is no previously arisen right view that is a factor therein. It would be sevenfold. Among the awakening factors (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) too, the last moment would not be an awakening factor, for there is no other subsequent awakening of which it would be a factor. If one thinks it is a factor of future awakening — there would be no future awakening. The same should be applied to concentration (<s>samādhi</s>).

body.text: (IV.31ab) anyatrājñānād iti. dātur grahītur vā vismaraṇād avyutpatteś ca. saṃdigdhasya vipannāśayasya vānādarapūrvakaṃ śaraṇam avagacchataḥ saṃvaro notpadyata iti. gṛhīti. uddeśapadam. avadātavasana iti. nirdeśapadaṃ. puruṣa iti. uddeśapadaṃ. puruṣendriyeṇa samanvāgata iti. tannirdeśapadaṃ. yadi na vinā saṃvareṇopāsako bhavati. yat tarhi sūtra uktaṃ. tad uktam iyatopāsako bhavatīti. tat katham iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. āha. nāsty atra sūtravirodha iti. [Tib. 37a mahānāmasūtrasya.
body.translated_text: (IV.31ab) 'Except through ignorance' — because of the forgetting or lack of understanding of either the donor or the recipient. For one who is doubtful, or whose intention is corrupted, or who takes refuge carelessly — restraint does not arise. 'Householder' — this is the general term. 'Wearing white clothes' — this is the specific term. 'Male person' — this is the general term. 'Endowed with the male faculty' — this is the specific term. If one cannot become a lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>) without the restraint, then what about the <s>sūtra</s> statement — 'to that extent one becomes a lay follower' — the rest of the sentence is: how then? He says: 'There is no contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s> here.' [Tib. 37a] Of the <s>Mahānāma-sūtra</s>.

body.text: (IV.31cd)

children.translated_text: 'The instruction is like that of a <s>bhikṣu</s>' —

body.translated_text: (IV.31cd)

body.text: iti. upāsakaśikṣāpadoktiḥ bhikṣur iva. yathaiva hi bhikṣur labdhasaṃvaro 'pi jñapticaturthena karmaṇā śikṣāpadāni yathāsthūlaṃ grāhyate pratyāyyate itaś cāmutaś ca pārājikādibhyas tava saṃvaraḥ. anyāni ca te sabrahmacāriṇaḥ kathayiṣyantīti. śrāmaṇeraś ca. kiṃ. śikṣāpadāni grāhyate labdhasaṃvaro 'pi pūrvaṃ. yadaiva hi tenābhyupagatam aham evaṃnāmā taṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddha śākyamuniṃ śākyādhirājaṃ pravrajitam anupravrajāmi. gṛhasthaliṃgaṃ parityajāmi. pravrajyāliṃgaṃ samādadāmi. śramaṇoddeśaṃ māṃ dhāraya. evaṃ yāvat trir apīti. tathopāsako 'pi buddhaśaraṇaṃ gacchāmi. yāvat saṃghaśaraṇaṃ gacchāmi. dvir api trir api. ity anena labdhasaṃvaro 'pi punaḥ śikṣāpadāni grāhyate. prāṇātipātaṃ prahāya prāṇātipātāt prativiramāmīti vistareṇa.
body.translated_text: thus. The instruction in the training rules for a lay follower is like [that of] a <s>bhikṣu</s>. For just as a <s>bhikṣu</s>, even after obtaining the restraint, is made to accept training rules through a formal act with an announcement and three-part motion (<s>jñapticaturtha karma</s>) — 'Your restraint is from these and those <s>pārājika</s> offenses and the rest; and your fellow practitioners will tell you the rest' — and a novice too — what? — is made to accept training rules even after previously obtaining the restraint. For at the very moment when he has accepted: 'I, named such-and-such, following that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the supreme <s>Śākya</s>, go forth following him who has gone forth. I abandon the marks of a householder. I undertake the marks of one gone forth. Consider me a student of the <s>śramaṇa</s>.' Thus up to three times. Similarly, a lay follower too — 'I go to the <s>Buddha</s> for refuge, up to: I go to the <s>Saṃgha</s> for refuge, twice and thrice' — even after obtaining the restraint through this, is again made to accept training rules: 'Abandoning the taking of life, I refrain from taking life' — and so on in detail.

body.text: (IV.32abc) ekadeśakārī. ya ekaṃ śikṣāpadaṃ rakṣati. pradeśakārī. yo dve rakṣati. yadbhūyaskārī. yas trīṇi catvāri vā rakṣati. paripūrṇakārī. yaḥ paṃcāpi rakṣati. sa tatkārīty ukta iti. ekadeśakārī yāvat paripūrṇakārīty [Tib. 37b] arthaḥ. na hy evaṃ sūtrapāṭha iti. na hy evaṃ mahānāmasūtrapāṭho yāvajjīvaprāṇāpetam ity uktaḥ. yathā mahānāmasūtrapāṭha iti. kiyatā bhadanta upāsako bhavati. yataś ca mahānāman gṛhī vistareṇa yāvad upāsakaṃ māṃ dhārayeti. iyatopāsako bhavatīti. yatra tv eṣa pāṭha iti. yatra sūtrāntare eṣa pāṭhaḥ. yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇāpetaṃ śaraṇagatam abhiprasannam iti. tatas te dṛṣṭasatyāḥ pudgalāḥ avetyaprasādānvayam avetyaprasādahetukaṃ prāṇair api
body.translated_text: (IV.32abc) 'One who practices a portion' (<s>ekadeśakārī</s>) — one who keeps one training rule. 'One who practices a section' (<s>pradeśakārī</s>) — one who keeps two. 'One who practices mostly' (<s>yadbhūyaskārī</s>) — one who keeps three or four. 'One who practices completely' (<s>paripūrṇakārī</s>) — one who keeps all five. 'He is called the doer of that' — [Tib. 37b] meaning: an <s>ekadeśakārī</s> up to a <s>paripūrṇakārī</s>. 'For the <s>sūtra</s> reading is not thus' — for the reading of the <s>Mahānāma-sūtra</s> is not as saying 'lifelong, abstaining from taking life.' What is the reading of the <s>Mahānāma-sūtra</s>? 'To what extent, Venerable Sir, is one a lay follower?' — and in detail — up to: 'consider me a lay follower; to that extent one is a lay follower.' 'But where this reading [is found]' — where in another <s>sūtra</s> this reading occurs: 'lifelong, abstaining from taking life, one who has gone for refuge, one of confirmed faith.' From that, those persons who have seen the truths, following their confirmed faith, faith arising from that cause — even at the cost of their lives

body.text: jīvitahetor api saddharmopagamanaṃ darśayati. abhavyā vayam enaṃ dharmaṃ parityaktum iti. na tv eṣa lakṣaṇāpadeśaḥ saṃvarasya. na tv anena sūtreṇa lakṣaṇam apadiśyata ity arthaḥ. prāṇāpetaṃ tu na kvacit paṭhyata iti. nāpi mahānāmasūtre. nāpi dṛṣṭasatyasūtre. kaś caitad aparisphuṭārthaṃ paṭhed iti. madhyapadalopavikalpān na jñāyate. kiṃ prāṇebhyo 'petaṃ prāṇair vā 'petaṃ prāṇapetaṃ. utāho prāṇātipātādibhyo 'petaṃ prāṇāpetam iti. praśna eva na yujyata iti. yo 'yaṃ praśnaḥ kiyatā bhadantopāsaka ekadeśakārī bhavati. yāvat paripūrṇakārīti. eṣa praśno na yujyate. kuto visarjanam iti. iha mahānāmann upāsakaḥ [Tib. 38a] prāṇātipātaṃ prahāya prāṇātipātāt prativirato bhavati. iyatā mahānāmann upāsakaḥ śikṣāyām ekadeśakārī bhavati. viśtareṇa dvābhyāṃ śikṣāpadābhyāṃ prativirataḥ pradeśakārī bhavati. tribhyaḥ prativirataḥ caturbhyo vā yadbhūyaskārī bhavati. paṃcabhyaḥ prativirataḥ paripūrṇakārī bhavatīty etad visarjanaṃ suṣṭhu na yujyate. tanmātraśikṣāksamāṃ praty eṣa praśno yujyate iti. ekasya śikṣāpadasya dvayos tataḥ pareṇa vā kṣamām iti. vināpi saṃvareṇopāsakaḥ prajñapita iti. mahānāmasūtre. yataḥ khalu mahānāmaṃ gṛhī avadātavasana ity evamādinā.
body.translated_text: even for the sake of life itself — demonstrate the approach to the true <s>Dharma</s>: 'We are incapable of abandoning this <s>Dharma</s>.' But this is not an indication of the characteristic of restraint. The meaning is: by this <s>sūtra</s>, a characteristic is not indicated. 'But "abstaining from taking life" is not read anywhere' — neither in the <s>Mahānāma-sūtra</s> nor in the <s>sūtra</s> of those who have seen the truths. Who would read this with unclear meaning? Because of alternatives in the elision of the middle word, it is not known whether it means 'separated from life-breath' (<s>prāṇebhyo 'petam</s>) or 'equipped with life-breath' (<s>prāṇair apetam</s>) or 'separated from [acts like] taking life' (<s>prāṇātipātādibhyo 'petam</s>). 'The question itself is not fitting' — this question: 'To what extent, Venerable Sir, is a lay follower one who practices a portion, up to one who practices completely?' — this question is not fitting. From where [would come] the answer? 'Here, <s>Mahānāma</s>, a lay follower [Tib. 38a] having abandoned the taking of life, refrains from the taking of life; to that extent, <s>Mahānāma</s>, a lay follower is one who practices a portion of the training.' In detail: 'refrained from two training rules, one is a <s>pradeśakārī</s>; refrained from three or four, one is a <s>yadbhūyaskārī</s>; refrained from five, one is a <s>paripūrṇakārī</s>' — this answer does not properly fit. 'This question fits with respect to one's capacity for just that much training' — capacity for one training rule, for two, and for more — [fits] with respect to that. 'A lay follower is designated even without the restraint' — in the <s>Mahānāma-sūtra</s>: 'From which, <s>Mahānāma</s>, a householder, wearing white clothes' — and so forth.

body.text: (IV.32d) arhato 'pi mṛduḥ prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ syād iti. yadi samutthāpakam asya cittaṃ mṛdu syāt. pṛthagjanasyādhimātra iti. yady asyādhimātraṃ cittam iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.32d) Even an <s>Arhat</s>'s <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint would be weak — if the mind that originates it were weak. And an ordinary person's (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) would be intense — if his mind were intense.

body.text: anyatrājñānād iti. dātur grahītuś ca. tadanādaratas tu śaraṇagamanair vinā na syād upāsaka iti.
body.translated_text: 'Except through ignorance' — of both the giver and the receiver. 'But because of disrespect for that' — without the going for refuge, one would not be a lay practitioner (<s>upāsaka</s>).

body.text: (IV.33) buddhakarakān iti. buddhaprajñaptihetūn. ata evāha. yeṣāṃ prādhānyena sa ātmabhāvo buddha ity ucyate. anye 'pi hi guṇā aprādhānyenāśritā bhavati. yeṣāṃ vā lābheneti. kṣayajñānādayaḥ saparivārā iti. ādiśabdenānutpādajñānam aśaikṣī ca samyagdṛṣṭir gṛhyate. saparivāragrahaṇenānāsravāḥ paṃca skaṃdhā gṛhyante. rūpakāyasya pūrvaṃ paścāc cāviśeṣād iti. kiṃ. na rūpakāyaṃ [Tib. 38b] śaraṇaṃ gacchatīti saṃbandhaḥ. yādṛśo bodhisattvāvasthāyāṃ rūpakāyas tādṛśaḥ paścād apīti.
body.translated_text: (IV.33) '<s>Buddhakarakā</s>' means the causes of the designation '<s>Buddha</s>.' For this very reason he says: by the predominance of which [qualities], that person (<s>ātmabhāva</s>) is called <s>Buddha</s>. For other qualities too are depended upon, but not predominantly. 'Or by the obtaining of which' — the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and the rest, together with their retinue. By the word 'and the rest,' the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>) and the non-learner's right view (<s>aśaikṣī samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) are grasped. By the expression 'together with retinue,' the five outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) aggregates are grasped. 'Because the material body (<s>rūpakāya</s>) is the same before and after' — what? One does not go for refuge in the material body — this is the connection. For the material body is the same in the <s>bodhisattva</s> stage and afterward.

body.text: lakṣaṇataḥ sarvabuddhān iti. na kaṇṭhoktita ity abhiprāyaḥ. mārgasyāvilakṣaṇatvād iti. laukikasya mārgasya puṇyajñānasaṃbhāralakṣaṇasya lokottarasya ca kṣayajñānādilakṣaṇasyāvilakṣaṇatvāt tulyatvāt. nāyurjātyādilakṣaṇānām. atas tulyalakṣaṇāḥ sarve buddhā iti.
body.translated_text: 'All <s>Buddha</s>s by their characteristics' — the intent is: not explicitly stated. 'Because the path has the same characteristics' — because the worldly path, characterized by the accumulation of merit and knowledge, and the supramundane [path], characterized by the knowledge of destruction and the rest, have the same characteristics, are identical — but not with respect to the characteristics of lifespan, birth, and the like. Therefore all <s>Buddha</s>s have identical characteristics.

body.text: saṃghībhavanty abhedyatvād iti. sadevakenāpi lokena mārgaṃ praty abhedyatvāt saṃghībhavaṃti. samagrarūpā bhavantīti. lakṣaṇata iti. pūrvavad
body.translated_text: 'They form a <s>Saṃgha</s> because of being indivisible' — because of being indivisible with respect to the path, even by the world together with its gods, they form a <s>Saṃgha</s> — they become of complete form. 'By their characteristics' — as before

body.text: vyākhyātavyaṃ. yo 'sau bhaviṣyatīti vistaraḥ. tatra bhagavāṃs trapusabhallikau vaṇijāv āmaṃtrayate sma. etaṃ yuvāṃ buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchataṃ. dharmaṃ ca. yo 'sau bhaviṣyaty anāgate 'dhvani saṃgho nāma tam api śaraṇaṃ gacchatam iti. yadā saṃgho nāsti tadaivam uktam anāgatam eva saṃgham adhikṛtya. tat kathaṃ sarvasaṃghān asau śaraṇaṃ gacchatīty anena virudhyate. tatpratyakṣabhāvina iti. yat saṃgharatnaṃ tayos bhallikayor dharmacakrapravartanānantaraṃ pratyakṣībhaviṣyatti. tasyodbhāvanārthaguṇataḥ [Tib. 39a] prakāśanārthaṃ sa evādhikṛto bhaviṣyatīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: should be explained. 'That which will come into being' — and so forth in detail. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the two merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s>: 'You two, go to this <s>Buddha</s> for refuge, and to the <s>Dharma</s>. And that which in the future time will be called <s>Saṃgha</s> — go to that too for refuge.' When the <s>Saṃgha</s> did not yet exist, this was said with reference to the future <s>Saṃgha</s> alone. How then is this contradicted by [the statement] that he goes for refuge to all <s>Saṃgha</s>s? 'That which would become manifest to them' — that <s>Saṃgha</s>-jewel which would become manifest to those two, <s>Bhallika</s> and the other, immediately after the turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel — for the purpose of revealing its qualities, for the purpose of illuminating it, that very one was made the subject — this is the meaning.

body.text: śāṃtyekalakṣaṇatvād iti. svaparasāṃtānikānāṃ kleśānāṃ duḥkhasya ca yā śāntiḥ. tal lakṣaṇam asyeti śāntyekalakṣaṇaṃ nirvāṇaṃ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. asau sarvaṃ nirvāṇaṃ gacchati.
body.translated_text: 'Because of having the single characteristic of peace' — the peace of afflictions and suffering belonging to one's own and others' continuums — that is its characteristic — [hence] having the single characteristic of peace: <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Its state [is the abstract noun]. Therefore, he goes for refuge to all <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: āśrayavipādanād iti. teṣām aśaikṣāṇāṃ ya āśrayo rūpaskandhaḥ. tasya vipādanād vikopanāt tadāśrayiṇo 'pi te buddhakarakā dharmā vipāditā bhavaṃti. śāstraṃ tu naivam iti vistaraḥ. abhidharmaśāstraṃ naivaṃ vācakaṃ. naivaṃ darśakaṃ. aśaikṣā dharmā eva buddha iti. kiṃ tarhi. buddhakarakā iti. ke te buddhakarakāḥ ye buddhatvasya buddhaprajñapteś ca hetavo laukikalokottarā dharmāḥ. te buddha iti. ata āśrayasya laukikapaṃcaskandhalakṣaṇasya buddhatvāpratiṣedhād acodyam evaitat. yad uktaṃ yady aśaikṣā dharmā eva buddhaḥ kathaṃ tathāgatasyāntike duṣṭacittarudhirotpādanād ānantaryaṃ bhavatīti. anyathā hīti vistaraḥ. yady aśaikṣā dharmā buddhaḥ. [Tib. 39b] śaikṣāśaikṣā eva dharmāḥ saṃghaḥ. laukikacittastho na buddhaḥ syān na saṃghaḥ. kasmāt. na hi laukikaṃ aśaikṣā dharmāḥ śaikṣāśaikṣāś ceti. yadi vā śaikṣā dharmā eva buddhakarakā budddhaḥ syāt nāśrayo 'pi. śīlam eva sa bhikṣusaṃvarākhyaṃ bhikṣukarakaṃ bhikṣuḥ syāt. nāśrayaḥ. āha. yady āśrayasyāpi buddhatvaṃ kasmād evam āha śāstre. yo buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchati. aśaikṣān asau buddhakarakān dharmān śaraṇaṃ gacchatīty aśaikṣadharmān evāvadhārayati. evaṃ vaibhāṣikeṇokte ācāryo dṛṣṭāntena samādhim āha. yathā tu yo bhikṣuṃ pūjayatīti vistaraḥ. yathā tu yo bhikṣuṃ pūjayati śīlamukhena. bhikṣukarakam asau śīlaṃ pūjayati. na ca punaḥ śīlam eva bhikṣuḥ. evaṃ yo buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchaty aśaikṣamukhena. aśaikṣān asau buddhakarakān dharmāṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchati. na punaḥ svasaṃtānikā aśaikṣā eva dharmā buddhaḥ. tasmād adoṣa eṣaḥ. yo buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchati. aśaikṣān asau buddhakarakān dharmāṃś charaṇaṃ gacchatīti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the deterioration of the basis' — the basis, the form-aggregate, of those non-learners (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) — because of its deterioration, its destruction, the <s>Buddha</s>-making qualities that depend on it are also deteriorated. 'But the treatise does not [say] thus' — and so forth in detail. The <s>Abhidharma</s> treatise does not say thus, does not show thus — that the non-learner <s>dharma</s>s alone are the <s>Buddha</s>. What then? They are <s>Buddha</s>-making (<s>buddhakaraka</s>). Who are those <s>Buddha</s>-makers? The mundane and supramundane <s>dharma</s>s that are the causes of <s>Buddhahood</s> and the designation '<s>Buddha</s>' — those are the <s>Buddha</s>. Therefore, since the <s>Buddhahood</s> of the basis, characterized by the five mundane aggregates, is not denied, this is not even objectionable — namely, what was said: 'if the non-learner <s>dharma</s>s alone are the <s>Buddha</s>, how can a heinous act arise from producing blood with evil intent toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' 'For otherwise' — and so forth in detail. If the non-learner <s>dharma</s>s were the <s>Buddha</s>, and the learner and non-learner <s>dharma</s>s alone were the <s>Saṃgha</s> — then one with mundane mind would not be a <s>Buddha</s>, nor a <s>Saṃgha</s>. Why? Because mundane [mind] is not non-learner <s>dharma</s>s, nor learner or non-learner [<s>dharma</s>s]. Or if only the learner <s>dharma</s>s were the <s>Buddha</s>-making, the <s>Buddha</s> — the basis too would not [be the <s>Buddha</s>]. The restraint called <s>bhikṣu</s>-restraint alone, the <s>bhikṣu</s>-making morality — that alone would be the <s>bhikṣu</s>, not the basis. He says: if the basis too has <s>Buddhahood</s>, then why is it stated thus in the treatise: 'One who goes for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s> goes for refuge to the non-learner <s>Buddha</s>-making <s>dharma</s>s' — restricting to non-learner <s>dharma</s>s alone? When the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> has stated this, the <s>Ācārya</s> resolves [it] with an analogy: 'But just as one who honors a <s>bhikṣu</s>' — and so forth in detail. Just as one who honors a <s>bhikṣu</s> through the avenue of morality — he honors the <s>bhikṣu</s>-making morality. Yet morality alone is not the <s>bhikṣu</s>. Similarly, one who goes for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s> through the avenue of the non-learner [<s>dharma</s>s] — he goes for refuge to the non-learner <s>Buddha</s>-making <s>dharma</s>s. Yet the non-learner <s>dharma</s>s belonging to one's own continuum alone are not the <s>Buddha</s>. Therefore this is no fault — one who goes for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s> goes for refuge to the non-learner <s>Buddha</s>-making <s>dharma</s>s.

body.text: so 'ṣṭādaśāveṇikān iti. teṣām asādhāraṇatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'He [goes for refuge to] the eighteen exclusive [qualities]' — the intent is: because of their uncommon nature.

body.text: vāgvijñaptisvabhāvānīti. grahaṇakālam adhikṛtya.
body.translated_text: 'Having the nature of vocal informative action' — with reference to the time of taking [the vows].

body.text: caityakalpitā vṛkṣāś caityavṛkṣāḥ. tān iti. ata eveti. yasmād
body.translated_text: Trees designated as <s>caitya</s>s are <s>caitya</s>-trees. Those [are referred to]. For this very reason —

children.translated_text: 'By going to this refuge, one is freed from all suffering.'

body.text: ataḥ sarvasaṃvarasamādāneṣu upāsakādisaṃvarasamādāneṣu dvārabhūtānīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: Therefore, in all undertakings of restraint — in the undertakings of the <s>upāsaka</s> restraint and the rest — [the refuges] serve as the gateway — this is the meaning.

body.text: (IV.34ab) āpāyikatvāc ca. yasmāc ca kāmamithyācāra ekāṃtenāpāyikaḥ apāyasaṃvartanīyaḥ. na tathābrahmacaryaṃ. akriyāniyamo hy akaraṇasaṃvara iti. akriyāyām akaraṇe niyama ekāṃtatā akriyāniyamaḥ. so 'karaṇasaṃvaraḥ. akaraṇalakṣaṇaḥ saṃvaraḥ. na samādānikasaṃvara ity arthaḥ. sa ca sautrāṃtikanayenāvasthāviśeṣa eva. vaibhāṣikanayena tu śīlāṃgam avijñaptir iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.34ab) And because of leading to the lower realms (<s>āpāyikatva</s>) — because sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>) definitely leads to the lower realms, is conducive to the lower realms. Non-celibacy (<s>abrahmacaryam</s>) is not so [defined]. 'The restraint of non-performance is a definite restriction on non-performance' — non-performance means not doing; a definite restriction, a one-sidedness, on non-performance is the restraint of non-performance. A restraint characterized by non-performance — meaning: not the restraint of undertaking (<s>samādānikasaṃvara</s>). And that, according to the <s>Sautrāntika</s> method, is merely a particular state. But according to the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> method, it is non-informative action (<s>avijñapti</s>) as a component of morality (<s>śīlāṅga</s>).

body.text: (IV.34cd) ya upāsakāḥ saṃta iti vistaraḥ. ye gṛhītapaṃcaśikṣāpadāḥ saṃto bhāryāḥ pariṇayanti vivāhayaṃti. kiṃ tair upāsakais tābhyo 'pi strībhyaḥ saṃvaraḥ pratilabdhaḥ. pratilabdhapūrvaka ity arthaḥ. atha na pratilabdha ity adhikṛtaṃ. vaibhāṣika āha. pratilabdha iti. mā bhūt prādeśika iti sarvāgamyāt prativirateḥ. kāmamithyācārāt prativiramāmīti agamyācārāt prativiramāmi. na tv asmāt saṃtānāgamyācarāt prativiramāmīty abhiprāyaḥ. ata evāha.
body.translated_text: (IV.34cd) 'Those lay practitioners (<s>upāsaka</s>) who exist' — and so forth in detail. Those who have taken the five training rules and who marry wives — do those lay practitioners obtain restraint for those women too? The meaning is: have [the women] previously obtained [restraint]? Now if they have not obtained it — this is presupposed. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: they have obtained it. 'Lest it be partial' — because of abstention from all that is not to be approached (<s>agamya</s>). 'I abstain from sexual misconduct' — the intent is: 'I abstain from improper sexual conduct, but I do not abstain from proper sexual conduct with my own wife.' For this very reason he says:

body.text: iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail.

body.text: Tib. 40b
body.translated_text: meaning: wrongful through prohibition. For one who performs an action prohibited by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, there is sin — because of disrespect for the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. 'That is not afflicted — it is merely known to be non-intoxicating and is drunk' — when the <s>Abhidharma</s> scholar has stated this, the Vinaya-holders establish [that]

body.text: iti. pratiṣedhasāvadyaṃ. bhagavatpratiṣiddhaṃ karmācarataḥ pāpaṃ bhavati. bhagavacchāsanānādarāt. na tat kliṣṭaṃ yad amadanīyamātrāṃ viditvā pibatīty ābhidhārmikeṇokte. prakṛtisāvadyaṃ madyam iti vinayadharāḥ sādhayaṃti. prakṛtisavadyam upāle sthāpayitveti. prakṛtisāvadyena karmaṇā na cikitsyaḥ. prajñaptisavadyena tu cikitsanīya ity abhiprāyaḥ. śākyeṣu glāneṣu madyapānaṃ nābhyanujñātam. ato gamyate prakṛtisāvadyaṃ tad iti. yadi hi hat prajñaptisāvadyaṃ syāt glānaśākyopasthānāya tad anujñāyate. na cānujñāyate. tena tat prakṛtisāvadyam iti. idaṃ coktaṃ māṃ śāstāram uddiśadbhiḥ śākyamunir naḥ śāstety upadiśadbhiḥ kuśāgreṇāpi madyaṃ na pātavyam iti. prakṛtisāvadyaṃ tad iti bhagavatā tat pratiṣiddhaṃ. na tu madanīyam ity avetya. kuśāgramātrasya madyasyāmadanīyatvāt. āryaiś ceti vistaraḥ. prakṛtisāvadyaṃ
body.translated_text: intoxicants are wrongful by nature (<s>prakṛtisāvadya</s>).
