'Wrongful by nature, O <s>Upāli</s>, setting aside' — [this means:] one should not be treated with an action wrongful by nature; but one should be treated with an action wrongful by prohibition — this is the intent. When <s>Śākya</s>s are ill, the drinking of intoxicants is not permitted. From this it is understood that it is wrongful by nature. For if it were wrongful only by prohibition, it would be permitted for attending to sick <s>Śākya</s>s. But it is not permitted. Therefore it is wrongful by nature. And this was said: 'By those who designate me as teacher, who declare "<s>Śākyamuni</s> is our teacher" — intoxicants should not be drunk even in the amount [that fits] on the tip of a blade of grass.' It is wrongful by nature — therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> prohibited it, not because it is intoxicating — since an amount on the tip of a blade of grass is not intoxicating. And by the noble ones (<s>ārya</s>) — and so forth in detail. Intoxicants are wrongful by nature

body.text: madyaṃ. janmāṃtaragatair apy āryair anadhyācārāt. prāṇivadhādivad iti sādhanaṃ. kāyaduścaritavacanāc cety [Tib. 41a] aparaṃ sādhanaṃ. prakṛtisāvadyaṃ madyaṃ. kāyaduścaritavacanāt. prāṇivadhādivat. caturvidhaṃ hi nandikasūtrādiṣu kāyaduścaritam uktam. prāṇātipātaḥ adattādānaṃ kāmamithyācāraḥ surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānam iti. utsargavihitasyāpīti vistaraḥ. anena bhagavadvacanasya pūrvāparavirodhaṃ pariharaṃti. kathaṃ. bhadaṃteti vistareṇa madyapānasya sāmānyavacanam utsargaḥ. śākyeṣu glāneṣu madyapānaṃ nābhyanujñātam ity apavāda iti. madyapānaṃ glānāvasthāyām api nānujñātam iti gamyate. apavādaḥ punaḥ prasaṃgaparihārārthaṃ. sakṛtpītaṃ hi madyaṃ vyasanībhavet. uktaṃ hi bhagavatā. trīṇi sthānāni pratiṣedhamāṇasya nāsti tṛptir vā. alaṃtā vā. paryāptir vā. madyam abrahmacaryaṃ styānamiddhaṃ ceti. prasaṃgaparihāraḥ kasmād ity āha. madanīyamātrāniyamāt. saiva hi mātrā dravyakālaprakṛtiśarīrāvasthā apekṣya madanīyā cāmadanīyā ca bhavati. ata eva ca kuśāgrapānapratiṣedha ity atiśayavacanaṃ. tad evaṃ na prakṛtisāvadyam iti manasikṛtvā bhagavatā tatpariharaṇīyam uktaṃ. [Tib. 41b] kiṃ tarhi. prasaṃgadoṣād iti darśitaṃ. āryair anadhyācaraṇaṃ hrīmattvād iti. paṃca śaikṣāṇi balāni sūtre paṭhyaṃte. katamāni paṃca. śraddhābalaṃ vīryabalaṃ hrībalam apatrāpyabalaṃ prajñābalaṃ ceti. ato hrīmattvān na pibaṃti. na tu prakṛtisāvadyatvāt. yadi hrīmattvāt tad anadhyācaraṇam ajñātam udakādivat kasmān na pibaṃtīty ata āha. tena ca smṛtināśād iti. madyaṃ hi pibataḥ kāryākāryasmṛtir naśyatīti. yady evam alpakaṃ tu pibaṃtu. yāvatyā mātrayā smṛtir naśyatīty ata āha. alpakasyāpy apānam. aniyamāt. viṣavad iti. yathā kālaprakṛtiśaktiyogād alpam api viṣaṃ kadācin mārayati. evaṃ madyam api madayatīti. duścaritavacanaṃ pramādasthānatvād iti. madenākuśalaparihārāt. kuśalakaraṇāc ca. atra pramādasthānagrahaṇaṃ nānyeṣv iti. atraiva śikṣāpade pramādasthānagrahaṇaṃ surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānaṃ prahāya surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānāt prativiramāmīti vacanāt. nānyeṣu śikṣāpadeṣu prāṇātipātaviratyādiṣu pramādasthānagrahaṇaṃ. prāṇātipātapramādasthānaṃ prahāya prāṇātipātapramādasthānāt prativiramāmīti [Tib. 42a] pramādasthānaṃ na paṭhyate. kiṃ tarhi. prāṇātipātaṃ prahāya prāṇātipātāt prativiramāmīti. evam adattādānādi yojyaṃ. kasmād ity āha. teṣāṃ prakṛtisāvadyatvāt. teṣāṃ prāṇātipātaviratyādīnāṃ śikṣāpadānāṃ prakṛtisāvadyatvāt. tad uktaṃ bhavati. pramādasthānam etad iti madyapānāt prativirantavyaṃ. na tu prakṛtisāvadyam etad iti. atyāseviteneti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: because even noble ones who have gone to other births do not transgress [this precept] — like killing living beings and the like — this is the proof. And from the statement of bodily misconduct (<s>kāyaduścarita</s>) — this is another proof. Intoxicants are wrongful by nature, because of the statement of bodily misconduct, like killing living beings and the like. For in the <s>Nandika Sūtra</s> and others, fourfold bodily misconduct is stated: killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, and [consuming] intoxicating liquors and spirits that are a basis for heedlessness. 'Even of what is prescribed as a general rule' — and so forth in detail. By this they resolve the apparent contradiction within the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words. How? O venerable one — and so forth in detail: the general statement about drinking intoxicants is the general rule (<s>utsarga</s>). 'When <s>Śākya</s>s are ill, the drinking of intoxicants is not permitted' — this is the exception (<s>apavāda</s>). It is understood that the drinking of intoxicants is not permitted even in the state of illness. The exception is for the purpose of preventing habitual indulgence — for intoxicants, once drunk, could become an addiction. For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'For three things, when one does not restrain oneself, there is no satisfaction, no sufficiency, no limit: intoxicants, unchastity, and sloth-and-torpor.' The prevention of habitual indulgence — why? He says: because the measure of intoxication is not fixed. For that very measure, depending on the substance, time, constitution, and bodily condition, can be intoxicating or non-intoxicating. And for this very reason, the prohibition of drinking even [the amount on] the tip of a blade of grass is a statement of emphasis. Thus, the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated that it should be avoided, not with the thought 'this is wrongful by nature,' but rather — as shown — because of the fault of habitual indulgence. 'The noble ones' non-transgression is because of their sense of shame (<s>hrī</s>)' — five powers of a learner are read in the <s>sūtra</s>: which five? The power of faith, the power of energy, the power of shame, the power of moral dread, and the power of wisdom. Therefore, because of their sense of shame they do not drink — not because [intoxicants are] wrongful by nature. 'If their non-transgression is because of shame, like water and the like, why do they not drink unknowingly?' — therefore he says: 'And because of the destruction of mindfulness by that' — for drinking intoxicants destroys the mindfulness of what should and should not be done. 'If so, let them drink a small amount — up to the measure at which mindfulness is not destroyed' — therefore he says: 'Even of a small amount, the non-drinking [is prescribed].' Because of indeterminacy — like poison. Just as a small amount of poison can sometimes kill, depending on time, constitution, and potency — so too intoxicants can intoxicate. 'The statement of misconduct is because of being a basis for heedlessness' — because of failing to avoid the unwholesome due to intoxication, and because of failing to perform the wholesome. 'Here, the inclusion of "basis for heedlessness" is not in the others' — the inclusion of 'basis for heedlessness' is only in this training rule — 'I abstain from intoxicating liquors and spirits that are a basis for heedlessness, setting aside [their use as] a basis for heedlessness' — because of this statement. Not in the other training rules — abstention from killing and the rest. 'Setting aside the basis for heedlessness of killing' is not read — 'I abstain from the basis for heedlessness of killing.' Rather: 'Setting aside killing, I abstain from killing.' Similarly, taking what is not given and the rest should be connected. Why? He says: because of their being wrongful by nature. Because those — the training rules of abstention from killing and the rest — are wrongful by nature. This amounts to saying: 'this is a basis for heedlessness' — one should abstain from drinking intoxicants — but not [with the thought] 'this is wrongful by nature.' 'When excessively indulged in' — and so forth in detail.

body.text:
surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānenāsevitena bhāvitena bahulīkṛtena kāyasya bhedān narakeṣūpapadyata iti nandikasūtre vacanāt. atyāsevitena madyapānena durgatigamanābhidhānaṃ tatprasaṃgena madyapānaprasaṃgena abhīkṣṇam ajasram akuśalasaṃtatipravṛtteḥ. akuśalānāṃ yā saṃtatiḥ. tasyāḥ pravṛtteḥ. āpāyikasyāpāyaprayojanasyāpūrvasya karmaṇa ākṣepād āvedhaḥ. yataḥ. vṛttilābhād vā phaladānāya vā pūrvopacitasya karmaṇo maraṇāvasthāyāṃ vṛttilābhaḥ. yataḥ. tasmād ākṣepāt vṛttilābhād vā durgatigamanābhidhānam
iti saṃbandhanīyaṃ. annāsava iti. taṇḍulakṛtaḥ. dravāsava iti. ikṣurasādikṛtaḥ. te veti vistaraḥ. surāmaireye kadācid aprāptamadyabhāve [Tib. 42b] . yadā nave bhavataḥ. kadācit pracyutamadyabhāve. yadā atipurāṇe bhavataḥ. ity ato madyagrahaṇaṃ. yadi madanīyaṃ. tato doṣa ity abhiprāyaḥ. pūgaphalakodravādayo 'pīti. ādiśabdena niṣpāvādayo gṛhyaṃte. madyapāne nāmadyatve 'py adoṣaḥ. surāmaireye na bhavata iti. surāmaireyasvabhāvasya madyasya pāne doṣa ity arthaḥ. sarvapramādāspadatvād iti. sarvapramādānāṃ sarvasmṛtipramoṣāṇāṃ prāṇātipātādyakuśalānāṃ hetubhūtānāṃ sthānam āspadaṃ pratiṣṭheti pramādasthānaṃ madyapānam.
body.translated_text: from the statement in the <s>Nandika Sūtra</s>: 'Through the basis of heedlessness that is intoxicating liquor (<s>surā</s>), spirits (<s>maireya</s>), and strong drink (<s>madya</s>), when practiced, cultivated, and multiplied, upon the breakup of the body one is reborn in the hells.' The declaration of going to a bad destiny through excessive indulgence in drinking intoxicants — through the occasion of drinking intoxicants, because of the constant and continuous operation of an unwholesome continuum, the continuum of unwholesome [states], its operation — there is an impetus (<s>āvedha</s>) from the projection of a new <s>karma</s> leading to a bad destiny (<s>āpāyika</s>). Or from the obtaining of function, or for the purpose of giving fruit, the <s>karma</s> previously accumulated obtains function at the time of death. Therefore, from that projection or obtaining of function, the declaration of going to a bad destiny — this is how it should be connected. 'Grain-distillate' (<s>annāsava</s>) — made from rice. 'Liquid-distillate' (<s>dravāsava</s>) — made from sugarcane juice and the like. 'Those indeed' — and so forth in detail. <s>Surā</s> and <s>maireya</s> sometimes have the state of not yet having attained intoxicating power — when they are new; sometimes have the state of having lost intoxicating power — when they are very old. Therefore the inclusion of '<s>madya</s>' (strong drink) [in the term]. The intent is: if it is intoxicating, then there is fault. 'Betel-nut, millet, and the like' — by the word 'and the like,' <s>niṣpāva</s> (beans) and the rest are included. In drinking intoxicants, if there is no intoxication, there is no fault. 'It does not belong to <s>surā</s> or <s>maireya</s>' — the meaning is: in the drinking of <s>madya</s> whose intrinsic nature is <s>surā</s> or <s>maireya</s>, there is fault. 'Because of being the ground of all heedlessness' — the drinking of intoxicants is the basis of heedlessness, meaning the ground, the foundation, the abode of all forms of heedlessness, all losses of mindfulness, all unwholesome [acts] beginning with killing of living beings that serve as causes.

body.text: (IV.36) yata eko labhyate iti. yato maulādibhyaḥ sattvāsattvākhyebhyaś ca. prātimokṣasaṃvaro labhyate. tataḥ śeṣau dhyānānāsravasaṃvarau. maulaprayogapṛṣṭhebhya iti. maulaprayogapṛṣṭhebhyo 'kuśalebhyaḥ karmabhyaḥ. maulaprayogapṛṣṭhasvabhāvās trayāṇāṃ yathākramaṃ pratipakṣabhūtāḥ prātimokṣasaṃvarākhyā vijñaptyavijñaptayo labhyaṃte. sattvāsattvākhyebhyo vastubhyaḥ prāṇivanaspatyādyadhiṣṭhānalakṣaṇebhyaḥ. prakṛtipratikṣepaṇasāvadyebhyaś ca karmabhyaḥ prāṇātipātavanaspatibhaṃgādilakṣaṇebhyaḥ. tad etad ubhayam apy ubhayādhiṣṭhānaṃ bhavati. prakṛtisāvadyam api sattvādhiṣṭhānam asattvādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca. prajñaptisāvadyam api sattvādhiṣṭhānam asattvādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca. [Tib. 43a] na punar evaṃ grahītavyaṃ. prakṛtisāvadyaṃ sattvādhiṣṭhānaṃ pratikṣepaṇasāvadyam asattvādhiṣṭhānam iti. tatra tāvat prakṛtisāvadyaṃ sattvādhiṣṭhānaṃ prāṇivadhādi. prajñaptisāvadyam api sattvādhiṣṭhānaṃ bhikṣoḥ strīhastādigrahaṇaṃ. sahāgāraśayyādi ca. prakṛtisāvadyam asattvādhiṣṭhānaṃ jātarūpādyapaharaṇaṃ. prajñaptisāvadyam asattvādhiṣṭhānaṃ vṛkṣapattrādicchedo bhikṣoḥ. āhārādiṣu ca vinayokta upadeśaḥ. sattvādhiṣṭhānapravṛttatvād iti. sattvaprajñaptyadhiṣṭhānapravṛttatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. vartamānā eva hi dharmāḥ sattvaprajñaptyadhiṣṭhānā nātītā nānāgatāḥ. teṣāṃ
body.translated_text: (IV.36) 'From which one is obtained' — from root [actions] and the like, and from things called beings and non-beings — the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint is obtained. From those, the remaining two — the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) restraints. 'From root, preparatory, and subsequent [actions]' — from unwholesome <s>karma</s>s that are root, preparatory, and subsequent. Informative and non-informative actions called <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint, which serve as antidotes to the respective root, preparatory, and subsequent natures of the three, are obtained. 'From things called beings and non-beings' — from objects characterized by living beings, plants, and the like as bases. 'And from <s>karma</s>s that are naturally blameworthy and blameworthy by designation' — from <s>karma</s>s characterized by killing living beings, breaking plants, and the like. Both of these have both [types of] basis. What is naturally blameworthy (<s>prakṛtisāvadya</s>) can have a being-basis or a non-being-basis. What is blameworthy by designation (<s>prajñaptisāvadya</s>) can also have a being-basis or a non-being-basis. But one should not understand it thus: what is naturally blameworthy has a being-basis [only] and what is blameworthy by designation has a non-being-basis [only]. Therein, what is naturally blameworthy with a being-basis is killing living beings and the like. What is blameworthy by designation with a being-basis is a <s>bhikṣu</s>'s grasping a woman's hand and the like, and sharing a bed with a householder and the like. What is naturally blameworthy with a non-being-basis is stealing gold and the like. What is blameworthy by designation with a non-being-basis is a <s>bhikṣu</s>'s cutting trees, leaves, and the like, and instructions stated in the <s>Vinaya</s> regarding food and the like. 'Because of operating with a being-basis' — the intent is: because of operating with a being-designation-basis. For only present <s>dharma</s>s have being-designation-bases, not past or future ones

body.text: nirupākhyakalpatvāt. ata evāha. nātītānāgatehyaḥ. teṣām asattvasaṃkhyātatvād iti. nanu cāsattvaprajñaptiadhiṣṭhhānapravṛtto 'pi prātimokṣasaṃvaro bhavati. sattvāsattvākhyebhyaḥ prāpyata iti vacanāt. sa cāpy evaṃ na pratiṣidhyate. yathaiva hi sattvākhyebhyo vartamānebhye eva labhyata ity ucyate. tathā vartamānebhya evāsattvākhyebhyo 'pi labhyata iti vaktavyaṃ. vartamānādhiṣṭhanatām eva hy anena vacanenātidiṣati. na prayogapṛṣṭhebhya iti. samāhitāvasthāyām ekāṃtamaulatvāt. asamāhitāvasthāyāṃ ca na saṃvarābhāvāt. kuta eva prajñaptisāvadebhya iti. abhyupagamābhāvāt. sarvakālebhyaś ceti. atītānāgatayor api saṃvarayor lābhāt tatsahabhūcittavat.
body.translated_text: — because of their being quasi-non-existent. For this very reason he says: 'Not from past or future ones.' 'Because they are not counted as beings' — but does not the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint also operate with a non-being-designation-basis? — because of the statement 'it is obtained from [things] called beings and non-beings.' That too is not denied thus. For just as it is said that it is obtained from present [things] called beings only, so too it should be stated that it is obtained from present [things] called non-beings only. For by this statement he teaches only the present-basis-ness [of it]. 'Not from preparatory and subsequent [actions]' — because in the concentrated state, it is exclusively of the root type; and in the non-concentrated state, because there is no absence of restraint [to be antidoted]. 'How then from [things] blameworthy by designation?' — because of the absence of acceptance [of this as a source for dhyāna/anāsrava restraints]. 'And from all times' — because even past and future restraints are obtained, like the mind co-existent with them.

body.text: ata eveti. yasmād [Tib. 43b] ete saṃvarā evaṃ labhyaṃte. yathā vistareṇoktam. ataś catuṣkoṭikaṃ kriyate. vistara iti. saṃti tāni skandhadhātvāyatanāni. yebhyo dhyānānāsravasaṃvarau labhyete. na prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ. saṃti tāni. yebhyaḥ prātimokṣasaṃvaro na dhyānānāsravasaṃvarau. saṃti tāni. yebhya ubhayaṃ labhyate. saṃti tāni. yebhyo nobhayaṃ labhyata iti. vistarārthaḥ. prathamā koṭiḥ. vartamānebhyaḥ prāṇātipātādikarmapathaprayogapṛṣthebhyaḥ pratikṣepaṇasāvadyāc ca vṛkṣabhaṃgādikād yaḥ saṃvaraḥ. sa prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ.
body.translated_text: 'For this very reason' — because these restraints are obtained in the manner elaborated in detail — therefore the four-fold analysis (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>) is made. 'In detail' — there are those aggregates, elements, and sense-bases from which the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraints are obtained, but not the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint. There are those from which the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint [is obtained] but not the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraints. There are those from which both are obtained. And there are those from which neither is obtained. This is the meaning of the elaboration. The first alternative: the restraint from present action-path preparatory and subsequent [actions] of killing and the like, and from what is blameworthy by designation such as breaking trees and the like — that is the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint.

body.text: iti vacanāt. prayogapṛṣṭhatvāt tu na dhyānānāsravasaṃvarau. dvitīya. atītānāgatebhyo maulebhyaḥ karmapathebhyaḥ prāṇātipātādibhyaḥ kāyavācikebhyaḥ saptabhyaḥ saṃvaro yaḥ. tau dhyānānāsravasaṃvarau.
body.translated_text: from this statement. But because of being preparatory and subsequent, not the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraints. The second [alternative]: the restraint from past and future root action-paths — the seven bodily and vocal [paths] beginning with killing — that constitutes the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraints.

body.text: ity vacanāt. na prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ. atītānāgatatvāt. tṛtīyā. pratyutpannebhyaḥ maulebhyaḥ karmapathebhya iti. pratyutpannakarmapathatvāt prātimokṣasaṃvaro bhavati. maulakarmapathatvāc ca dhyānānāsravasaṃvarau. caturthī atītanāgatebhyaḥ sāmaṃtakapṛṣṭhebhya iti. atītānāgatatvān na prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ. sāmaṃtakapṛṣṭhatvān na dhyānānāsravasaṃvarau [Tib. 44b] svasaṃtāne vartamānebhyaḥ karmapathebhyaḥ saṃvaro na yujyata iti paśyann āha. na tu saṃvaralābhakāle vartamānāḥ karmapathāḥ saṃtīti. vartamānādhiṣṭhānebhyas tebhyaḥ karmapathebhya iti vaktavyam iti śikṣayaty ācāryaḥ. yato vastunaḥ prativiramati. tasya vartamānatvāsaṃbhavāt. nātītavartamānānām iti. utpannatvād eṣāṃ saṃvaraṇaṃ na yujyate. na hy utpannānām anutpattiḥ śakyate kartuṃ. anāgatānāṃ tu śakyata iti. teṣām eva saṃvaraṇaṃ yujyata ity ācāryābhiprāyaḥ
body.translated_text: from this statement. Not the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint — because of being past and future. The third [alternative]: from present root action-paths — because of being present action-paths, the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint applies; and because of being root action-paths, the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraints [apply]. The fourth [alternative]: from past and future neighboring-preliminary and subsequent [actions] — not the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint because of being past and future; not the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraints because of being neighboring-preliminary and subsequent. Seeing that restraint from action-paths present in one's own continuum is not fitting, he says: 'But at the time of obtaining restraint, present action-paths do not exist.' The <s>Ācārya</s> teaches that one should say 'from those action-paths having a present basis.' Because of the impossibility of the thing from which one refrains being present — since it is not being performed [at that time]. 'Not of past and present ones' — because these have already arisen, restraining them is not fitting. For the non-arising of what has already arisen cannot be brought about. But it can be brought about for future ones. Therefore, restraining those alone is fitting — this is the <s>Ācārya</s>'s intent

body.text: . vaibhāṣikāṇāṃ tu tathāvacane 'yam abhiprāyo lakṣyate. prāṇātipātādiprayogamaulapṛṣṭhānāṃ yathākramaṃ saṃvaraṇāya prātimokṣasaṃvaraprayogamaulapṛṣṭhāni pravartaṃte. naitāni pravartiṣyaṃta iti. arthata evaitāni pratipakṣabhūtāni tāni rundhantīvotpadyaṃte. prayogaḥ prayogam evaṃ bhavītīva tvām ahaṃ saṃvṛṇomi. mā tvam utthā iti. evaṃ yāvat. pṛṣṭhaḥ pṛṣṭham evaṃ bravītīveti yojyaṃ. tathā skandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ karmapathaprayogamaulapṛṣṭhasvabhāvānāṃ vartamānānāṃ rundhāno vartamānebhyas tebhyo labhyate. prātimokṣasaṃvara ity ucyata iti. tasmān naivaṃ vaktavyam iti.
body.translated_text: . But for the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s, the intent discerned in such a statement is this: the preparatory, root, and subsequent [actions] of the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint operate respectively as antidotes to the preparatory, root, and subsequent [actions] of killing and the like. 'These will not operate' — meaning: these antidotes effectively block those, arising as if to prevent them. The preparatory [antidote] is as if saying to the preparatory [offense]: 'You shall be thus' — 'I restrain you, do not arise.' Similarly up to: the subsequent [antidote] is as if saying to the subsequent [offense] — this should be connected. Thus, restraining the present aggregates, elements, and sense-bases — which have the nature of action-path preparatory, root, and subsequent — from those present ones it is obtained. It is called the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint. Therefore it should not be stated thus [i.e., the Ācārya's formulation is unnecessary].

body.text: (IV.37) kaścit sarvebhya iti vistaraḥ. bhikṣusaṃvaraḥ sarvebhyaḥ karmapathebhyo labhyate. sarvakarmapathā varjanīyā ity arthaḥ. kaścic caturbhyaḥ. tato 'nyaḥ. [Tib. 44b] tato bhikṣusaṃvarād anyaḥ. saṃvaraḥ śrāmaṇerādisaṃvaraś caturbhya evāṃgebhyo labhyate. kāyikebhyaḥ prāṇātipātādibhyas tribhyo vācikāc ca mṛṣāvādāt. yady alobhādveṣāmohāḥ kāraṇānīti. saṃvarakāraṇāni dvihdā iṣyaṃte. alobhādveṣāmohā vā kāraṇāni. mṛdumadhyādhimātrāṇi vā cittānīti. yadi pūrvaḥ paryāyo 'bhiprīyate. sarvaiḥ kāraṇair alobhādisvabhāvair labhyate saṃvaraḥ. kuśale samutthāpake cetasi teṣāṃ yugapat bhāvāt. yadi mṛdvādīni cittāni kāraṇānīṣyaṃte. ekena kāraṇena labhyate. teṣām ayugapat bhāvāt. paścimaṃ paryāyam iti. mṛdvādikāraṇapakṣaṃ. asti saṃvarasthāyīti vistaraḥ. sarvasattveṣu saṃvṛtaḥ sarvasattvānugate kalyāṇāśaye sati saṃvarotpatteḥ. na sarvāṃgair upāsakādisaṃvarasya sarvāṃgāprativiratatvāt. na sarvakāraṇair mṛdvādīnāṃ kāraṇatvena yugapad asaṃbhavāt. bhikṣusaṃvaras tu sarvāṃgair api. sarvāṃgaprativiratatvāt. yas trividhena cittena trīn saṃvarān samādatta iti. tadyathā mṛdunā cittena upāsakasaṃvaraṃ samādatte. madhyena śrāmaṇerasaṃvaram. [Tib. 45a] adhimātreṇa bhikṣusaṃvaram iti. sarvakāraṇaiś ca na tu sarvāṃgair iti. upāsakādisaṃvarāṇām ekaikasya mṛdvādyekaikakāraṇatvāt. tathā gṛhṇata iti. paṃcaniyamakriyayā gṛhṇataḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.37) 'A certain one from all' — and so forth in detail. The <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint is obtained from all action-paths — meaning: all action-paths are to be avoided. 'A certain one from four' — another, other than the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint, meaning other than that — the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> and other restraints are obtained from four components only: from the three bodily ones — killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct — and from the vocal one of false speech. 'If non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion are the causes' — the causes of restraint are accepted as twofold: non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion are the causes; or mild, moderate, and intense minds are [the causes]. If the former alternative is preferred, the restraint is obtained through all the causes having the nature of non-greed and the rest — because of their simultaneous existence in a wholesome originating mind. If mild and other minds are accepted as the causes, it is obtained through a single cause — because of their non-simultaneous existence. 'The latter alternative' — the position of mild and other causes. 'There is one who abides in restraint' — and so forth in detail. One who is restrained with respect to all beings — because the restraint arises when there is a wholesome intention directed toward all beings. Not with all components — because the <s>upāsaka</s> and other restraints do not involve abstention from all components. Not with all causes — because of the impossibility of mild and other [minds] being causes simultaneously. But the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint is with all components too — because of abstaining from all components. 'One who undertakes three restraints with threefold mind' — namely: with mild mind, one undertakes the <s>upāsaka</s> restraint; with moderate [mind], the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> restraint; with intense [mind], the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint. 'With all causes but not with all components' — because each individual one of the <s>upāsaka</s> and other restraints has one each of mild and other [minds] as its cause. 'Taking thus' — taking with the act of the fivefold determination.

body.text: katham aśakyebhya iti. ye haṃtum eva na śakyāḥ. tebhyo 'śakyebhyaḥ sattvebhyaḥ kathaṃ saṃvaralābhaḥ. atrācāryaḥ samādhim āha. sarvasattvajīvitānupaghātādhyāśayenābhyupagamād iti. sarvasattvānāṃ jīvitasyānupaghātenādhyāśayena saṃvarābhyupagamāt. vaibhāṣikā apy asyaiva praśnasya parihārāṃtaram āhuḥ. yadi punaḥ śakyebhya eveti vistaraḥ. cayāpacayayuktaḥ syāt. śakyatām āgateṣu satteṣu saṃvaraś cīyeta. asakyatām āgateṣv apacīyeta.
body.translated_text: 'How from those that are impossible?' — those beings that simply cannot be killed — from those impossible-to-[harm] beings, how is the obtaining of restraint [possible]? Here the <s>Ācārya</s> states a resolution: 'through the acceptance with the intention of non-destruction of the life of all beings' — through the acceptance of the restraint with the intention of non-destruction, of non-harming, of the life of all beings. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s too state another resolution to this very question: 'But if only from those that are possible' — and so forth in detail. It would be subject to increase and decrease — when beings come into the range of possibility, the restraint would increase; when they go beyond the range of possibility, it would decrease.

body.text: śakyāśakyānāṃ manuṣyādidevādīnām itaretarasaṃcārāt. devādayo manuṣyādīn saṃcaraṃti. manuṣyādayaś devādīn iti. imaṃ vaibhāṣikaparihāraṃ sāvakāśaṃ paśyann ācārya āha. naivaṃ bhaviṣyatīti vistaraḥ. naivaṃ cayāpacayayuktaḥ saṃvaro bhaviṣyati. kathaṃ kṛtvā. yathā hy apūrvatṛṇādyutpattau. śoṣe vā tṛṇādīnāṃ. yady api tṛṇādibhyo 'pi saṃvaro labhyate. tathāpi saṃvarasya vṛddhihrāsau na bhavataḥ. [Tib. 45b] evaṃ śakyāśakyasaṃcāre 'pi na syātāṃ vṛddhihrāsau cayāpacayāv ity arthaḥ. tasmāc chakyebhya eva saṃvaro labhyate. na cāyaṃ doṣaḥ syād iti. vaibhāṣikā āhuḥ. na sattvānām iti vistaraḥ. na tad evaṃ. yathā hy apūrvatṛṇādyutpattāv iti vistareṇa yad uktaṃ. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. sattvānāṃ pūrvaṃ saṃcārāt paścāc ca bhāvāt. tṛṇagulmalatādīnāṃ pūrvaṃ paścāc cābhāvāt. ato na tṛṇādidṛṣṭāṃtena cayāpacayadoṣo nivāryate. evaṃ vaidharmyamātram uktaṃ. na sādhyasādhanārtha iti. ācāryaḥ punar āha. yadā parinirvṛtā na saṃty eveti vistaraḥ. tasmāt pūrvaka eva hetuḥ sādhur iti. sarvasattvajīvitānupaghātādhyāśayenābhyupagamād iti. ata śakyāśakyebhyaḥ saṃvaro labhyata iti siddhaṃ. evaṃ tarhi yadi sarvasattvebhyo labhyate prātimokṣasaṃvaraḥ. pūrvabuddhaparinirvṛtebhyas tasyālābhāc chīlanyūnatā syāt. sattvānāṃ pūrvebhyo nyūnatvāt. ācārya āha. sarveṣāṃ buddhānāṃ pūrvaṃ paścāc cotpannānām aviśeṣeṇa sarvasattvebhyo lābhāt. yadi hi te py aparinirvṛtā abhaviṣyan. saṃprati tebhyo 'pi te 'lapsyaṃta iti.
body.translated_text: because of the mutual movement of those who can and cannot [be harmed] — humans and the like, gods and the like. Gods and the like approach humans and the like, and humans and the like approach gods and the like. Seeing this <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> resolution as having an opening, the <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'It will not be so' — and so forth in detail. The restraint will not have increase and decrease in this way. How so? Just as when new grass and the like grow, or when grass and the like wither — even though restraint is obtained with respect to grass and the like too, still the restraint does not increase or decrease. Similarly, even with the movement of those who can and cannot [be harmed], there would be no increase or decrease — this is the meaning. Therefore, restraint is obtained only from those who can [be harmed], and there would be no fault in this. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s say: 'Not of beings' — and so forth in detail. It is not so as stated in detail — 'just as when new grass and the like grow.' Why? Because beings previously move about and afterward continue to exist, whereas grass, shrubs, creepers, and the like previously and afterward do not exist. Therefore, the fault of increase and decrease cannot be prevented by the example of grass and the like. Thus, only a point of dissimilarity has been stated, not for the purpose of establishing what is to be proven. The <s>Ācārya</s> again says: 'When those who have attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> no longer exist' — and so forth in detail. Therefore, the previous reason alone is sound. 'Because of accepting the intention of non-harm to the lives of all beings' — therefore it is established that restraint is obtained from those who can and those who cannot [be harmed]. Well then, if <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint is obtained from all beings, then since it is not obtained from those <s>Buddha</s>s who attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> previously, there would be a deficiency in morality, because beings are fewer than the earlier ones. The <s>Ācārya</s> says: because all <s>Buddha</s>s — those arisen earlier and later — without distinction obtain [restraint] from all beings. For if those too had not attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, even now they would obtain [restraint] from those.

body.text: sarvakarmapathebhya iti. kāyikavācikebhyaḥ. nāsti hi vikalenāsaṃvareṇeti. prāṇātipātenaiva [tib 46a] nādattādānenety evamādi. mṛdunaivāsaṃvareṇa samanvāgata iti. pūrvapratilabdhatvāt. adhimātrayā tu prāṇātipātavijñaptyā. kiṃ. samanvāgata iti vartate. na vipākaphalaviśeṣa iti. evaṃ madhyādhimātreṇa yojyam iti. yo madhyena cittenāsaṃvaraṃ pratilabhate. so 'dhimātreṇāpi cittena prāṇino jīvitād vyavaropayan madhyenaivāsaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bhavati. adhimātrayā tu prāṇātipātavijñaptyā. evaṃ yo 'dhimātreṇa yāvad adhimātreṇaivāsaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bhavati. adhimātrayā ca prāṇātipātavijñaptyā. ittham api ca yojyaṃ. yo 'dhimātracittenāsaṃvaraṃ pratilabhate. sa mṛdunāpi cittena prāṇino jīvitād vyavaropayan adhimātrenaivāsaṃvareṇa samanvāgato bhavati. mṛdvyā tu prāṇātipātavijñaptyety evamādi.
body.translated_text: 'From all action-paths' — from bodily and vocal ones. 'For there is no incomplete non-restraint' — meaning: not by killing alone and not by stealing alone, and so on. 'Endowed with only mild non-restraint' — because of having been previously obtained. 'But with intense informative action of killing' — what? — 'endowed' is continued. Not a special fruition-result. 'Thus it should be connected with moderate and intense' — one who obtains non-restraint with moderate mind, even when depriving living beings of life with intense mind, is endowed with only moderate non-restraint, but with intense informative action of killing. Similarly, one who [obtains non-restraint] with intense [mind] — up to: is endowed with intense non-restraint alone, and with intense informative action of killing. And it should also be connected thus: one who obtains non-restraint with intense mind, even when depriving living beings of life with mild mind, is endowed with intense non-restraint alone, but with mild informative action of killing — and so on.

body.text: nāgabaṃdhā hastipakāḥ. vāgurikā iti. paṃpā nāma prāṇijātir vāgurākhyā. tāṃ ghnantīti vāgurikāḥ. arthata āsaṃvarikā iti. rājānaś cādhikaraṇasthāś ca
body.translated_text: '<s>Nāgabandha</s>s' — elephant keepers. '<s>Vāgurikā</s>s' — there is a creature called <s>pampā</s>, known as <s>vāgurā</s>; those who kill them are <s>vāgurikā</s>s. 'In substance, they are non-restrainers (<s>āsaṃvarika</s>)' — kings and judges

body.text: daṇḍanetṛtvād ihāpaṭhitā api āsaṃvarikā eva draṣṭavyāḥ. evam anye 'pi yojyā iti. kurkuṭāṃ ghnaṃtīti. kaurkuṭikā ity evamādīni. yuktas tāvad iti vistareṇoktvā yāvat katham asaṃvaraḥ sarvasattvedhyo yujyata iti praśnite. vaibhāṣikaḥ parihāram āha. mātrādīn api hīti vistaraḥ. ācārya āha. na hi tāvat [Tib. 46b] ta eva ta iti. te mātrādaya iti jānānā hanyur ity aghātyebhyas tebhyo 'saṃvaraḥ kathaṃ yujyate. kiṃ cāryībhūtānāṃ punaḥ paśūbhavituṃ nāsty avakāśaḥ. teṣām urabhrādyupapattyasaṃbhavāt. tebhyaḥ katham asaṃvaraḥ syāt. yadi vānāgatātmabhāvāpekṣayā urabhrādayo bhaviṣyaṃtīti vartamānān mātrāder asaṃvaraḥ syāt. urabhrān api te aurabhrikāḥ putrībhūtān anāgate janmani sarvathā na hanyur iti. na syāt tebhya urabhrebhyo 'saṃvaraḥ. vaibhāṣika āha. kathaṃ hi nāma jighāṃsatām iti vistaraḥ. ācārya āha. etan mātrādiṣu samānam iti vistaraḥ. kathaṃ hi nāmājighāṃsatāṃ putrādibhūtānām aurabhrikādīnāṃ tebhyo mātrādibhyaḥ syād asaṃvara iti.
body.translated_text: though not listed here, should be regarded as non-restrainers because of being directors of punishment. 'Similarly, others too should be connected' — 'those who kill roosters' are <s>kaurkuṭika</s>s, and so on. Having stated 'this is fitting' in detail, up to the question 'how is non-restraint from all beings fitting?' — the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> gives a resolution: 'For they [would kill] even mothers and the like' — and so forth in detail. The <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'For indeed they are not the same ones' — those who, knowing them to be mothers and the like, would kill — how then is non-restraint from those who would not be killed fitting? Moreover, 'for those who have become Noble Ones, there is no possibility of again becoming animals' — because of the impossibility of their taking birth as sheep and the like, how could there be non-restraint from them? Or if, with reference to future births, [one says] that they will become sheep and the like, and therefore there is non-restraint from their present [existence as] mothers and the like — then those sheep-slaughterers (<s>aurabhrika</s>s) too, [whose sheep] having become their sons in a future birth, will certainly never kill them — so there should be no non-restraint from those sheep. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'How indeed could those intent on killing' — and so forth in detail. The <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'This applies equally to mothers and the like' — and so forth in detail. How indeed could there be non-restraint from those mothers and the like on the part of sheep-slaughterers and the rest who do not intend to kill and who have become sons and the like?

body.text: vikalaḥ karmapathāṃgataḥ. prādeśiko 'pi syāt. ekasyāpy aṃgasya aviramāt. sattvadeśakālasamayaniyamayogena pradeśaviratatvāt. saṃvaraś ca tathaiva. vikalo 'pi prādeśiko 'pi syāt. anyatrāṣṭavidhāt pūrvoktāt prātimokṣasaṃvarāt. kasmād ity āha. tanmātraśīladauḥśīlyapratibandhād iti. asaṃvaras tanmātraṃ śīlaṃ pratibadhnāti. saṃvaraś ca tanmātraṃ dauḥśīlyaṃ pratibadhnātīti.
body.translated_text: 'Incomplete in action-path constituents' (<s>vikala</s>) — could also be partial (<s>prādeśika</s>), because of not abstaining from even one constituent. Partial in abstaining because of the restriction of beings, places, times, and occasions. And restraint likewise — could be both incomplete and partial. Except for the previously stated eightfold <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint. Why? He says: 'Because of the obstruction of that-extent morality and that-extent immorality' — non-restraint obstructs that-extent morality, and restraint obstructs that-extent immorality.

body.text: (IV.38) tatkulīnair iti. āsaṃvarikakulīnaiḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.38) 'By those of such family' — by those of non-restrainer families (<s>āsaṃvarikakulīna</s>).

body.text: iti. ādareṇa īhanaṃ kriyāraṃbhaḥ. kṣetraṃ cādānaṃ cādarehanaṃ ceti samāsaḥ. tasmād avijñaptir utpadyate. tithīti vistaraḥ. tithibhaktaṃ. yāvad ardhamāsabhaktam ity arthagatiḥ. ādiśabdena maṇḍalakaraṇādi gṛhyate. ādareṇa vā tadrūpeṇeti.tīvrakleśatayā. tīvraprasādatayā cety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Earnest endeavor (<s>ādarehaṇa</s>) means the undertaking of an activity with earnestness. Field and reception and earnest endeavor — this is the compound. From that, non-informative action (<s>avijñapti</s>) arises. 'On a lunar day (<s>tithi</s>)' — and so forth in detail. A lunar-day offering — up to: a half-month offering, is the contextual meaning. By the word 'and the like,' making <s>maṇḍala</s>s and the like are included. 'Or with earnestness of that nature' — meaning: with intense affliction (<s>kleśa</s>), or with intense faith (<s>prasāda</s>).

body.text: (IV.39, 40) samādānaviruddhavijñaptyutpādād iti. yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇātipātādibhyaḥ prativiramāmīti yat samādānaṃ. tena viruddhāyā vijñapter utpādāt. iti prathamena kāraṇena prātimokṣasaṃvaratyāgaḥ. āśrayatyāgād iti. yenāśrayeṇa saṃvaro gṛhītaḥ. tasya tyāgān maraṇād iti. dvitīyena kāraṇena tattyāgaḥ. āśrayavikopanād iti. yādṛśenāśrayeṇa saṃvara upāttaḥ. tādṛśo na bhavati. vikopanāt. iti tṛtīyena kāraṇena tattyāgaḥ. nidānacchedād iti. nidānaṃ kuśalamūlāni. tasya cchedāt. caturthena kāraṇena tattyāgaḥ. tāvad evākṣepāc ceti. upavāsasaṃvarasyāhorātram ākṣepaḥ. iti paṃcamena kāraṇena tasyopavāsasaṃvarasya tyāgaḥ. pūrvoktaiś ca caturbhiḥ kāraṇair iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.39, 40) 'Through the arising of informative action contrary to the undertaking' — the undertaking that 'I shall refrain from killing living beings and the like for life' — from the arising of informative action contrary to that, by this first reason there is abandonment of <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint. 'Through the abandonment of the basis' — through the abandonment, through the death, of the basis by which the restraint was taken — by this second reason there is its abandonment. 'Through the corruption of the basis' — the basis by which the restraint was assumed no longer remains as it was, through corruption — by this third reason there is its abandonment. 'Through the cutting off of the root' — the root (<s>nidāna</s>) means the wholesome roots; through their cutting off — by this fourth reason there is its abandonment. 'And through the expiry of that duration' — the duration of the fasting restraint (<s>upavāsasaṃvara</s>) is one day and night — by this fifth reason there is the abandonment of that fasting restraint. And by the four previously stated reasons as well.

body.text: patanīyena ceti. ebhiś ca yathoktaiḥ paṃcabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ patanīyena ceti.
body.translated_text: 'And through a <s>pārājika</s> offense' — through these five reasons as stated, and through a <s>pārājika</s> offense

body.text: pataṃty aneneti patanīyaṃ. tac caturvidhaṃ. abrahmacaryaṃ. yathoktapramāṇam adattādānaṃ. [Tib. 47b] manuṣyavadhaḥ. uttarimanuṣyadharmamṛṣāvādaś ceti.
body.translated_text: — that by which one falls (<s>patanti</s>) is <s>patanīya</s> (a defeating offense). And it is fourfold: unchastity (<s>abrahmacaryam</s>), taking what is not given in the stated measure, killing a human being (<s>manuṣyavadha</s>), and falsely claiming superhuman qualities (<s>uttarimanuṣyadharmamṛṣāvāda</s>).

children.translated_text: 'But the <s>Kāśmīrī</s>s hold that one who has committed [a <s>pārājika</s>] is like a debtor' —

body.text: āgamād yuktitaś ca. tatrāyam āgamaḥ. vinaya uktaṃ. duḥśīlaś cet bhikṣur bhikṣuṇīm anuśāsti. saṃghāvaśeṣam āpadyata iti. āpannapārājiko hi bhikṣur duḥśīlo 'bhipretaḥ. nānāpannapārājikaḥ. prakṛtisthaḥ śīlavān iti viparyayeṇa vacanād ato 'vagamyate. asty asya duḥśīlasyāpi sato bhikṣubhāvaḥ. yasmāt saṃghāvaśeṣam āpadyata ity uktam iti. yuktir api na hy ekadeśakṣobhāt sakalasaṃvaratyāgo yukta iti. na maulīm apy āpattim āpannasyeti. patanīyām apy āpattim āpannasyety arthaḥ. naiva cānyāpattim iti. saṃghāvaśeṣādikaṃ. āviṣkṛtāyām iti. deśitāyāṃ.
body.translated_text: from scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and reasoning (<s>yukti</s>). The scriptural [basis] here is: it is stated in the <s>Vinaya</s>: 'If an immoral <s>bhikṣu</s> instructs a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, he incurs a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> [offense].' For the 'immoral <s>bhikṣu</s>' intended here is one who has committed a <s>pārājika</s>, not one who has not committed a <s>pārājika</s> — because of the contrary statement 'one established in [his] natural state is virtuous.' From this it is understood: even for this immoral one, the state of being a <s>bhikṣu</s> exists, since it is said that he incurs a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s>. The reasoning too: for it is not fitting that through the violation of one part, the entire restraint is abandoned. 'Not even for one who has committed a fundamental offense' — meaning: not even for one who has committed a <s>pārājika</s> offense. 'Nor indeed another offense' — a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> and the like. 'When it has been disclosed' — meaning: when it has been confessed.

body.text: yat tarhi bhagavatoktam iti vistareṇa yāvat parājitam iti. tat katham iti vākyādhyāhāraḥ. paramārthabhikṣutvaṃ saṃdhāyaitad uktam iti. satyadarśanabhavyatvena tasyāpannasya paramārthabhikṣutvāprāpteḥ. bahukleśebhyo nandaprabhṛtibhyaḥ. maulyāpy āpattyā na bhikṣutvaṃ naśyatīti viditvā tāṃ kuryur iti vākyārthaḥ [Tib. 48a] saṃjñābhikṣur iti. yasyānupasaṃpannasya bhikṣur iti nāma. pratijñābhikṣur iti. abrahmacaryādipravṛttau duḥśīlaḥ. bhikṣata iti bhikṣur iti. yācanakaḥ. bhinnakleśatvād bhikṣur iti. arhan. asmiṃs tv artha iti. yat yat bhagavatoktam abhikṣur bhavaty aśramaṇa iti vistareṇa. etasminn arthe. yathoktebhyaś caturbhyo bhikṣubhyo 'nya evāyaṃ paṃcamo jñapticaturthopasaṃpanno bhikṣur iti. yad apy uktaṃ paramārthabhikṣutvaṃ saṃdhāyaitad uktaṃ. tat pratyāha. na cāsau pūrvaṃ paramārthabhikṣur āsīt. yataḥ paścād abhikṣur bhavet. abhikṣur bhavaty aśramaṇa iti vacanāt. ity upamāṃ kurvateti. mastakacchinnatālopamāṃ kurvatā śāstraiva datto 'nuyoga iti saṃbaṃdhanīyaṃ. parihṛtaḥ praśna ity arthaḥ. ekagrāsaparibhoga āhārasya. ekapārṣṇipradeśaparibhogo vihārasyeti sambhdhaḥ. sarvabhikṣusaṃbhogabahiṣkṛtaś ca śāstreti. sarvasmāt bhikṣubhis saha saṃbhogād ekapaṃktibhojanādikād bahiṣkṛto buddhena. nāśayata kāraṇḍavakam iti. kāraṇḍavako yavākṛtitvād yavas tṛṇaviśeṣaḥ. yo yavadūṣīty ucyate. evam asāv abhikṣur bhikṣvākṛtir [Tib. 48b] iti. kaśaṃbakam nāma pūtikāṣṭham. evam asau pūtibhūto bhikṣuḥ. taṃ śīlavatsaṃghād yūyam apakarṣateti bhagavāṃ
body.translated_text: 'But what the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated' — in detail, up to 'defeated' — 'how [is this to be understood]?' — this is the implied completion of the sentence. 'This is said with reference to ultimate <s>bhikṣu</s>-hood' — because that offender has not attained ultimate <s>bhikṣu</s>-hood through being fit for seeing the truths. 'Because of the many who have strong afflictions, like <s>Nanda</s> and others' — knowing that <s>bhikṣu</s>-hood is not lost even through a fundamental offense, they might commit it — this is the sentence meaning. 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> by designation' (<s>saṃjñābhikṣu</s>) — one who, being unordained, has the name '<s>bhikṣu</s>.' 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> by declaration' (<s>pratijñābhikṣu</s>) — one who, engaging in unchastity and the like, is immoral. 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> because he begs' (<s>bhikṣate</s>) — a mendicant. 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> because of having broken the afflictions' (<s>bhinnakleśatvāt</s>) — an <s>Arhat</s>. 'But in this sense' — whatever the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated — 'he is not a <s>bhikṣu</s>, not a <s>śramaṇa</s>' — in detail — in this sense: this fifth one, ordained through a motion followed by three announcements (<s>jñapticaturthopasampadna</s>), is a <s>bhikṣu</s> other than those four <s>bhikṣu</s>s as stated. As for what was said — 'this was said with reference to ultimate <s>bhikṣu</s>-hood' — he replies to that: 'And that one was not previously an ultimate <s>bhikṣu</s>, such that afterward he would become a non-<s>bhikṣu</s>' — from the statement 'he is not a <s>bhikṣu</s>, not a <s>śramaṇa</s>.' 'Making the simile' — by making the simile of a palm tree with its crown cut off, the <s>Śāstra</s> (the <s>Kośa</s>) itself gives the reply — this is to be connected. The meaning is: the question is resolved. 'The consumption of food in one mouthful, the use of a dwelling in one heel-spot' — this is the connection. 'And excluded from all communal enjoyments of <s>bhikṣu</s>s by the Teacher' — excluded by the <s>Buddha</s> from all communal enjoyments with <s>bhikṣu</s>s, such as eating in one row and the like. 'Destroy the <s>kāraṇḍava</s>' — <s>kāraṇḍava</s> is a type of grass having the shape of barley, which is called 'barley-spoiler.' Thus that one is a non-<s>bhikṣu</s> having the appearance of a <s>bhikṣu</s>. '<s>Kaśaṃbaka</s>' is rotten wood. Thus that one is a <s>bhikṣu</s> who has become rotten. 'You should remove him from the virtuous <s>saṃgha</s>' — thus the <s>Bhagavān</s>

body.text: bhikṣūn ājñāpayāmāsa. athotplāvinaṃ vāhayateti. utplāvī nāma vrīhimadhye 'bhyaṃtarataṇḍulahīno vṛīhir eva. tathāsau śīlasārahīno bhikṣvākṛtiḥ. taṃ pravāhayata. niṣkrāmayatety arthaḥ. mārgajinaḥ śaikṣo 'śaikṣaḥ. mārgadaiśiko buddhaḥ. mārge jīvati śīlavāṃ bhikṣur mārganimittaṃ jīvanāt. mārgadūṣī duḥśīlaḥ. idam atrodāharaṇaṃ. dagdhakāṣṭheti vistaraḥ. yathā yad dagdhaṃ. na tat kāṣṭhaṃ. pūrvakāṣṭhākṛtimātrāvaśeṣasādharmyāt. tad dagdhaṃ kāṣṭham ity ucyate. hradaś ca śuṣko 'pi hrada ity ucyate. śukanāsā gṛhādiṣu rūpakārakṛtā. śukanāsākṛtitvāc chukanāsety ucyate. evam asau bhikṣvākṛtisāmānyamātrāvaśeṣāc chramaṇa uktaḥ. pūtibījam aṃkurājanakatvād abījam api bījam ity ucyate. tadākāramātrāvaśeṣatvād alātacakraṃ cakram iti. cakrākṛtitvāt. mṛtasattvaś cāsattvo 'pi sattva ity ucyate. sattvākṛtimātrāvaśeṣatvāt. tadvad eṣa draṣṭavyaḥ. śikṣādattako nāma bhikṣur adhimātrarāgatayā [Tib. 49a] striyā abhrahmacaryaṃ kṛtvā. tadanaṃtaram eva jātasaṃvegaḥ kaṣṭaṃ mayā kṛtam ity ekasminn api praticchādanacitte 'nutpanne bhikṣusaṃgham upagamyāviṣkarotīdaṃ mayā pāpaṃ kṛtam iti. sa āryasaṃghopadeśāt sarvabhikṣunavakāṃtikatvādi daṇḍakarma kurvāṇaḥ śikṣādattaka ity ucyate. tad yadi dauḥśīlyād abhikṣur eva syāt. sa na syāt. na hi tasya punar upasaṃpādanaṃ kriyate. bhikṣuś ca sa vyavasthāpyate. tasmān na dauḥśīlyād abhikṣutvam iti. na brūma iti vistaraḥ. na vayaṃ brūmaḥ. sahādhyāpattyā abrahmacaryād eva sarvaḥ pārājiko bhavati. kiṃ tarhi. praticchādanacittena. kiṃ na punaḥ pravrājyate. anikṣiptaśikṣa ity adhyāhāryaṃ. tīvrānapatrāpyavipāditatvāt. tīvreṇānapatrāpyeṇa vipāditāsya saṃtatiḥ. tasyāḥ saṃtater evaṃ vipāditatvāt saṃvarasyābhavyatvaṃ. tasmān na punaḥ pravrājyata ity adhikāraḥ. na tu khalu bhikṣubhāvāpekṣayā. na tu khalu tasya bhikṣubhāvo 'stīty apekṣayā na pravrājyate. tathā hy asau parājayiko nikṣiptaśikṣo pi na pravrājyate. tīvrānapatrāpyavipāditatvāt saṃtateḥ.
body.translated_text: he commanded the monks. 'Now expel the floater' — a 'floater' (<s>utplāvī</s>) is a grain of rice that is empty of inner grain. Similarly, that one who lacks the essence of morality has merely the appearance of a monk. 'Expel him' — the meaning is: cast him out. A 'conqueror of the path' (<s>mārgajina</s>) is a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) or a non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). A 'guide of the path' (<s>mārgadaiśika</s>) is the <s>Buddha</s>. One who 'lives by the path' is a virtuous monk, because he lives by means of the path. A 'corrupter of the path' (<s>mārgadūṣin</s>) is one of bad morality. This is the illustration here. 'Burnt wood' — and so forth in detail. Just as what is burnt is not [really] wood; because of the similarity of retaining merely the form of former wood, that burnt [thing] is called 'wood.' A dried-up lake too is [still] called a 'lake.' A 'parrot-nose' (<s>śukanāsā</s>) is an ornamental feature made on houses and the like. Because of having the shape of a parrot's beak, it is called a 'parrot-nose.' Similarly, that one is called an ascetic (<s>śramaṇa</s>) because of retaining merely the general appearance of a monk. A rotten seed, because of being unable to produce a sprout, though not [really] a seed, is [still] called a 'seed' — because of retaining merely that appearance. A fire-brand circle (<s>alātacakra</s>) [is called] a 'circle' — because of having the shape of a circle. And a dead being, though not [really] a being, is [still] called a 'being' — because of retaining merely the appearance of a being. Similarly should this [case] be seen. The one called <s>Śikṣādattaka</s> is a monk who, due to excessive passion, committed sexual misconduct with a woman. Immediately afterward, having become remorseful, [thinking] 'What a terrible thing I have done!' — without even a single thought of concealment having arisen — he approached the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks and disclosed: 'This evil has been committed by me.' He, performing the disciplinary procedure of being treated as the most junior of all monks and the like, on the instruction of the Noble <s>Saṃgha</s>, is called <s>Śikṣādattaka</s>. If, then, through immorality alone one would cease to be a monk, he would not exist [as a monk]. For no re-ordination (<s>upasaṃpādana</s>) is performed for him. Yet he is established as a monk. Therefore, one does not lose monkhood through immorality. 'We do not say' — and so forth in detail. We do not say that every <s>pārājika</s> [offender] becomes [defeated] simply by committing sexual misconduct together with the offense. Rather, [it is] through the thought of concealment. Why is he not re-ordained then? '[Because he is] one who has not abandoned the training' should be supplied. Because his mental continuum has been corrupted by intense shamelessness (<s>anapatrāpya</s>). Because that mental continuum has been so corrupted, the incapacity for restraint [follows]. Therefore, the topic is: he is not re-ordained. But not because of the consideration that he lacks monk-status. It is not because of the consideration that monk-status does not exist for him that he is not re-ordained. For that very <s>pārājika</s> offender, even if he has abandoned the training, is not re-ordained — because his mental continuum has been corrupted by intense shamelessness.

body.text: iti. rūpasvabhāvaṃ kuśalam arūpasvabhāvaṃ cābhipretaṃ. ata eva ca sarvam eveti vyācaṣṭe. dvābhyām iti. upapattito vā. parihāṇito vā. [Tib. 49b] tenāha upapattito veti vistaraḥ. ūrdhvam upapadyamāno 'dharaṃ parityajati. adhaś copapadyamāna uparibhūmikam iti. parihāṇito vā samāpatteḥ tatsamāpattisaṃgṛhītaṃ kuśalaṃ tyajyate. nikāyasabhāgatyāgāc ca kiṃcid iti. nirvedhabhāgīyaṃ yat pṛthagjanāvasthāyām utpāditaṃ yāvat kṣāṃtir iti. tad asaty api bhūmisaṃcāre nikāyasabhāgatyāgena tyajyate. yadā kāmadhātau mṛtvā tatraivopapadyate
body.translated_text: the intent is both the wholesome having the nature of form and that having the nature of the formless. For this very reason he explains 'all indeed.' 'Through two [means]' — either through rebirth, or through decline. Therefore he says 'through rebirth or' — and so forth in detail. When being reborn above, one abandons the lower; and when being reborn below, [one abandons] that belonging to the higher ground. Or through decline — from an attainment, the wholesome included in that attainment is abandoned. 'And some through abandonment of the class of beings' (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>) — the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) that were produced during the stage of an ordinary person, up to patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>) — those are abandoned through the abandonment of the class of beings, even without a change of ground. When one dies in the Desire Realm and is reborn right there

body.text: . vakṣyati hi
body.translated_text: . For it will be stated:

children.text: bhūmityāgāt tyajaty āryas tāny anāryas tu mṛtyuta
children.translated_text: 'A Noble One abandons those through abandoning the ground; but a non-Noble One, through death' —

body.text: iti. pūrvako mārga iti. prayogānaṃtaryavimuktimārgasvabhāvaḥ pratipannakamārgaḥ. phalaṃ phalaviśiṣṭo veti. uttaro mārgo 'dhikṛtaḥ. tadyathā 'nāgāmī yady anāgāmiphalāt parihīyate. tenānāgāmiphalam uttaro mārgas tyajyate. yadi tv anāgāmī dvitīyaṃ dhyānaṃ labhate. tasmāc ca parihīyate. sa tasya phalaviśiṣṭo mārgo dvitīyadhyānabhūmikas tyajyate.
body.translated_text: thus. The 'prior path' — the path that has been practiced, having the nature of preparatory, uninterrupted, and liberation paths. 'Or the fruit or what is distinguished by the fruit' — the higher path is the subject. For example, if a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) declines from the fruit of non-returning, by that, the higher path [leading to] the fruit of non-returning is abandoned. But if a non-returner attains the second <s>dhyāna</s> and then declines from it, the path distinguished by the fruit belonging to the ground of the second <s>dhyāna</s> is abandoned.

body.text: (IV.42ab) hetupratyayabaleneti. sabhāgahetubalena. parato ghoṣabalena cety arthaḥ. dhyānasaṃvaraṃ vā labhata iti. anāsravasaṃvaraṃ vā labhata iti nocyate. dhyānasaṃvarapūrvotpādenaiva tattyāgāt. akaraṇāśnyata iti. etat karma na kariṣyāmīty āśayato 'pi śastrajālatyāge vinā saṃvaragrahaṇenāsaṃvaracchedo na bhavati. tadyathā roganidānaparihāre 'pi tasya pravṛddhasya rogasyauṣadhena vinā [Tib. 50a] vinivṛttir na bhavati. tadvat. tad uktaṃ bhavati. asaṃvaratyāgecchāyāṃ saṃvaro grahītavyo nānyatheti. tallābhasyeti. asaṃvaralābhasya.
body.translated_text: (IV.42ab) 'Through the power of the causal condition' — through the power of the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>). 'And through the power of hearing from another' — this is the meaning. 'Or one obtains <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint' — but it is not said 'or one obtains outflow-free restraint.' Because the latter is abandoned only through the prior arising of <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint. 'Through the intention of non-performance' — even with the intention 'I shall not perform this <s>karma</s>,' without formally undertaking restraint through abandoning the net of weapons, the cutting off of non-restraint does not occur. Just as even when the cause of a disease is removed, without medicine, the cure of a disease that has grown strong does not occur — so too. Thus it has been stated: when there is the wish to abandon non-restraint, restraint must be undertaken — not otherwise. 'Of the obtaining of that' — of the obtaining of non-restraint.

body.text: (IV.42cd) katham avijñaptir iti. vijñaptir apīti vaktavyaṃ. svasamutthāpitāyā atītāyā vijñaptes tatkāla eva prāpticchedāt.
body.translated_text: (IV.42cd) 'How is <s>avijñapti</s> [abandoned]?' — <s>vijñapti</s> too should be mentioned. Because at that very time, the acquisition of past <s>vijñapti</s>, which was produced by oneself, is cut off.

children.translated_text: 'Through impulse, gift, action, purpose, life-root severance — but the intermediate [form]' —

body.text: iti ca paṭhitavyaṃ. naivasaṃvaranāsaṃvara ity arthaḥ. athāpy avijñaptir api kevalocyate. tatra vijñapter avacane kāraṇaṃ vaktavyam ity ucyate. vijñapter anāvaśyakatvāt. tathā hi vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: should also be read thus. The meaning is: the neither-restraint-nor-non-restraint [form]. Even if only <s>avijñapti</s> alone is mentioned, in that case, a reason must be given for not mentioning <s>vijñapti</s> — it is said: because of the non-necessity of [mentioning] <s>vijñapti</s>. For it will be stated:

children.translated_text: 'Six unwholesome ones, <s>avijñapti</s>, and one that is twofold' —

body.text: iti. avijñaptivacanena ca vijñaptivacanasiddhes tadavacanaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. And since by stating <s>avijñapti</s>, the statement of <s>vijñapti</s> is accomplished, therefore it is not [separately] stated.

body.text: anye tv āhuḥ. na niruddhāyā naivasaṃvaranāsaṃvarasaṃgṛhītāyā vijñapter anubaṃdhinī prāptir ity ata etadavijñapter eva tyāgakāraṇam ucyata iti.
body.translated_text: Others, however, say: since there is no following acquisition for <s>vijñapti</s> that has ceased and is included in neither-restraint-nor-non-restraint, therefore only the cause of the abandonment of <s>avijñapti</s> is stated.

body.text: kuṃbhakāracakreṣugativad iti. yathā kuṃbhakāracakrasya iṣoś ca gatiḥ. yena kāraṇena saṃskāraviśeṣeṇa ākṣipto bhavati. tasya cchedāt sāpi cchidyate. tadvat. alaṃ samādāneneti pratyākhyānavacanena. yathāsamāttam akurvata iti. tadyathā buddham avanditvā. maṇḍalakam akṛtvā vā [Tib. 50b] na bhokṣya iti. tad akṛtvā bhuṃjānasya sā madhyamā avijñaptiś chidyate. yaṃtrajālādīti ādiśabdena śastraviṣādi gṛhyate. kuśalamūlāni samucchettum
body.translated_text: Like the motion of a potter's wheel and an arrow — just as the motion of a potter's wheel and an arrow [continues due to an impetus]: that by which causal factor, a specific impetus, it was set in motion — through the cessation of that, that [motion] too ceases. So too. 'Enough with the undertaking' — through the statement of renunciation. 'Not doing as undertaken' — for example, 'I shall not eat without first worshipping the <s>Buddha</s> or without making a <s>maṇḍala</s>.' When, not having done that, one eats, that intermediate <s>avijñapti</s> is cut off. 'Traps and nets and the like' — by the word 'and the like,' weapons, poison, and the rest are grasped. 'Begins to cut off the wholesome roots'

body.text: ārabhata iti. kuśalamūlasamucchedaprāraṃbhāvasthāyām eva cchidyate. na samucchedāvasthayām iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: — he shows that [the <s>avijñapti</s>] is cut off at the very stage of beginning the cutting off of wholesome roots, not at the stage of [actual] cutting off.

body.text: iti. arūpagrahaṇaṃ rūpacchedasyoktatvāt.
body.translated_text: the mention of 'formless' (<s>arūpa</s>) is because the cutting off of form has already been stated.

body.text: iti. atra vairāgyataś ca kiṃcid iti vaktavyaṃ. yathā kuśalaṃ daurmanasyendriyam iti. sarvam eveti. kāmarūpārūpyāvacaraṃ. yaḥ prahāṇamārga iti. darśanamārgo bhāvanāmārgaś ca. laukiko vā lokottaro vā yathāsaṃbhavaṃ. asau saparivāra iti. asāv upakleśaprakāraḥ satatsahabhūprāptyanucaraḥ upakleśaprakārasyeti grahaṇaṃ kleśasyāpy upakleśatvena sarvasaṃgrahārthaṃ. tathā hi śāstra uktaṃ. ye yāvat kleśā upakleśā api te syur upakleśā na kleśa iti.
body.translated_text: here, 'and through dispassion, some [are abandoned]' should also be stated. Just as the wholesome mental displeasure faculty (<s>daurmanasyendriya</s>). 'All indeed' — belonging to the Desire, Form, and Formless Realms. 'That which is the path of abandonment' — the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) and the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>). Whether mundane or supramundane, as appropriate. 'That with its retinue' — that type of secondary affliction (<s>upakleśa</s>), together with the acquisitions of its co-existent [dharmas], is an accompanier. The mention of 'type of secondary affliction' is for the purpose of including all [afflictions], since primary afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) too are secondary afflictions [in a broader sense]. For thus it is stated in the treatise: 'All afflictions would also be secondary afflictions, but secondary afflictions are not [necessarily primary] afflictions.'

body.text: (IV.44, 45) ubhayāśraya iti vistaraḥ. strīpuruṣāśayasya kleśasyādhimātratayā. pratisaṃkhyānasya tatpratipakṣabhāvanālakṣaṇasyākṣamatvāt. tīvrasya ca hrīvyapatrāpyasyābhāvād eṣāṃ saṃvaro nāstīti. pratidvaṃdvabhāvād iti. yasmāt saṃvarasyāsaṃvaraḥ [Tib. 51a] pratidvaṃdvabhūtaḥ. tasmāt yatraiva saṃvaraḥ. tatraivasaṃvara iti. teṣāṃ ṣaṇḍhādīnām asaṃvarābhāvo dvitīyaṃ kāraṇaṃ. samādānasamādhyabhāvād iti. samādānabhāvāt prātimokṣasaṃvaro nāsti. samādhyabhāvāc ca dhyānānāsravaṣaṃvarau na staḥ. tadabhāvas tu māṃdyena kuśaleṣv avyutpatteḥ. pāpakriyāśayābhāvāc cāsaṃvaro nāsti. yadyogād yadvipādanāc ceti. yena hrīvyapatrāpyeṇa yogād yasya hrīvyapatrāpyasya vipādanāc ca. yathākramaṃ saṃvarasaṃvarau syātāṃ. tat tīvraṃ hrīvyapatrāpyam āpāyikānāṃ nāstīti. yady āpāyikānāṃ saṃvarāsaṃvarau na staḥ. yat tarhi sūtra uktam iti yistaraḥ. tat kathaṃ. prātimokṣasaṃvaro manuṣyāṇām eva. na devānām. asaṃvegāt. dhyānānāsravasaṃvarau tu hetukarmadharmabhāvanād yathāsaṃbhavaṃ.
body.translated_text: (IV.44, 45) 'Dependent on both' — and so forth in detail. Because of the intensity of the affliction that is the disposition of women and men. Because of the incapacity for analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyāna</s>), characterized by the cultivation of the antidote to that. And because of the absence of intense shame (<s>hrī</s>) and moral dread (<s>vyapatrāpya</s>), these [eunuchs and the like] do not have restraint. 'Because of being the opposite' — since non-restraint is the opposite of restraint, therefore wherever there is restraint, there alone is non-restraint. The absence of non-restraint for those eunuchs and the like is the second reason. 'Because of the absence of undertaking and concentration' — because of the absence of undertaking, there is no <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint. Because of the absence of concentration, the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraints do not exist. The absence of those, however, is due to dullness, [resulting in] lack of proficiency in wholesome [dharmas]. And because of the absence of the intention to commit evil, non-restraint does not exist. 'Through the application of which, and through the corruption of which' — through the application of that shame and moral dread, and through the corruption of that shame and moral dread — restraint and non-restraint respectively would exist. That intense shame and moral dread does not exist for those in the lower realms (<s>āpāyika</s>). If those in the lower realms have neither restraint nor non-restraint, then what about what is stated in the <s>sūtra</s> — and so forth in detail — how is that? <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint belongs to humans alone, not to gods — because of the absence of urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>). But <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraints [occur] through causal <s>karma</s> and the cultivation of the <s>dharma</s>, as appropriate.

body.text: (IV.46ab) tatkālam atyaṃtaṃ ceti. yad iṣṭavipākaṃ. tat tatkālaṃ. duḥkhaparitrāṇāt kṣemaṃ. yan nirvāṇaprāpakaṃ. tad atyaṃtaṃ duḥkhaparitrāṇāt kṣemaṃ. parinirvṛtasya yan nityakālaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāsti.
body.translated_text: (IV.46ab) 'At that time and ultimately' — that which has a desirable fruition — that is [meritorious] for that time, providing relief from suffering, [hence] beneficial. That which leads to <s>nirvāṇa</s> — that is ultimately beneficial, providing relief from suffering. For one who has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, suffering does not exist for all time.

body.text: (IV.46cd, 47) nanu ca trīṇi dhyānāni seṃjitāny uktāni bhagavatā. yad atra vitarkitam vicāritam ity evam ādi. idam atrāryā iṃjitam ity āhur iti. ādiśabdena dvitīya uktaṃ. yad atra prītir avigatā. idam atrāryā iṃjitam āhuḥ. tṛtīye 'pi yad atra sukhaṃ [Tib. 51b] sukham iti cetasa ābhogaḥ. idam atrāryā iṃjitam ity āhur iti. atha kasmāt sarvam eva rūpārūpyāvacaraṃ kuśalaṃ karmāniṃjyam
body.translated_text: (IV.46cd, 47) But the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated that the three <s>dhyāna</s>s are 'with movement' (<s>señjita</s>). What is here thought and deliberated — and so forth. This, the Noble Ones call 'movement' (<s>iñjita</s>). By the word 'and so forth,' what is stated regarding the second: the joy therein that has not departed — this, the Noble Ones call 'movement.' And in the third too: the mental engagement with 'happiness, happiness' therein — this, the Noble Ones call 'movement.' Then why is all wholesome <s>karma</s> belonging to the Form and Formless Realms called 'imperturbable' (<s>āniñjya</s>)

body.text: uktam ity āha. āniṃjyapratyayagāminam iti. āniṃjyānukūlabhāginaṃ. akaṃpyānukūlabhāginaṃ mārgam ārabhyety arthaḥ. kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ samādhisapakṣālatayā seṃjitam evānyatrāniṃjyam uktam ity āha.
body.translated_text: ? — he says: 'tending toward the condition of imperturbability' — meaning: sharing in that which is favorable to imperturbability, meaning: the path that is favorable to that which is unshakeable — this is the meaning. What then is the reason that what is allied with concentration is called 'with movement' everywhere except [the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and above where it is] 'imperturbable'? — he says:

children.text: tadbhūmiṣu yataḥ karma vipākaṃ prati neṃjatīti.
children.translated_text: 'Because in those grounds, <s>karma</s> does not waver with respect to its fruition.'

body.text: bhogādi saṃvartanīyam iti. bhogo dravyasaṃpat. ādiśabdena saurūpyasausvaryādi gṛhyate. tad eveti vistaraḥ. yat tad deveṣu vipacyeta. tat bahulīkṛtam evaṃ śīlamayaṃ bhāvanāmayaṃ. tasya caivaṃ bhavati. aho batāhaṃ devasubhagānāṃ manuṣyasubhagānāṃ vā sabhāgatāyām upapadyeyeti. yāvat sa tatra upapadyata iti.
body.translated_text: 'Leading to enjoyment and the like' — enjoyment means material prosperity. By the word 'and the like,' beauty, sovereignty, and the rest are grasped. 'That very [<s>karma</s>]' — and so forth in detail. That which would ripen among gods — that, when greatly cultivated, whether consisting of moral conduct or of meditation — and of that one [there is the aspiration]: 'Oh, may I be reborn in the company of gods who are fortunate or of humans who are fortunate!' — until one is reborn there.

body.text: (IV.48-50) kāmadhātus trīṇi ca dhyānānīti. kṃadhātuprathamadhyānayoḥ [Tib. 52a] kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ caitasikaṃ ca saumanasyaṃ sukhā vedanā. dvitīye dhyāne saumanasyaṃ sukhā vedanā. tṛtīye dhyāne caitasikaṃ sukham iti. tadbhāvajñāpanārtham iti. tacchabdena duḥkham abhisaṃbadhyate. tasya duḥkhasya kāmadhātāv evāstitvajñāpanārtham ihagrahaṇaṃ. sasaṃbhārair iti. saṃbhriyate utpādyate 'neneti saṃbhāraḥ. indriyaviṣayāśrayalakṣaṇaḥ. tena sasaṃbhārā vedanā phalaṃ.
body.translated_text: (IV.48-50) 'The Desire Realm and the three <s>dhyāna</s>s' — in the Desire Realm and the first <s>dhyāna</s>, bodily happiness and mental elation (<s>saumanasya</s>) constitute pleasant feeling. In the second <s>dhyāna</s>, elation is the pleasant feeling. In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, mental happiness [is the pleasant feeling]. 'For the purpose of indicating its existence' — by the word 'that,' suffering is connected. The mention of 'here' is for the purpose of indicating that suffering exists only in the Desire Realm. 'With its requisites' — that by which [feeling] is assembled, produced, is a requisite (<s>saṃbhāra</s>), characterized by sense-faculty, object, and basis. Thus, feeling together with its requisites is the fruit.

body.text: iti. dhyānāṃtarakarmaṇo dhyānāṃtarotpattau vipākena veditena bhavitavyaṃ. tatra sukhā duḥkhā vā vedanā nāsti. nāsti. tasmād asyāduḥkhāsukhā vedanā vipāka iti. caturthād dhyānād adho 'py aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyaṃ karmāstīti. dhyānāṃtare vā kasyacit karmaṇo 'nyasya vipāko vedanā na syān na saṃbhavati. na hi sukhavedanīyasya maulaprathamadhyānabhūmikasya karmaṇo dhyānāṃtare sa vipāka iti yujyate vaktuṃ. savitarkatvena dhyānāṃtarato maulasya nihīnatvāt. nāpi kāmāvacarasya duḥkhavedanīyasya karmaṇo bhūmyaṃtaratvāt. ata eva caturthadhyānādibhūmikasya. tato vītarāgatvāc ca.
body.translated_text: thus. For <s>karma</s> of the <s>dhyānāntara</s> (inter-mediary concentration), when there is rebirth in the <s>dhyānāntara</s>, the maturation must be experienced as feeling. There, neither pleasant nor painful feeling exists. It does not exist. Therefore, the feeling that is its maturation is neither-painful-nor-pleasant (<s>aduḥkhāsukhā</s>). [One might ask:] there is <s>karma</s> to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant even below the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. Or in the <s>dhyānāntara</s>, the maturation-feeling of some other <s>karma</s> would not exist, is not possible. For it is not fitting to say that the maturation of <s>karma</s> belonging to the root first <s>dhyāna</s> ground that is to be experienced as pleasant [occurs] in the <s>dhyānāntara</s> — because the root [first <s>dhyāna</s>] is inferior to the <s>dhyānāntara</s> by virtue of having <s>vitarka</s>. Nor of Desire Realm <s>karma</s> to be experienced as painful — because of belonging to a different ground. For this very reason, [the same applies] for [<s>karma</s>] belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground and above. And because of dispassion from that [lower ground].

body.text: etaddoṣaparijihīrṣayā dhyānāṃtarakarmaṇo dhyāna eva sukhendriyaṃ vipāka ity eke bruvate.
body.translated_text: Wishing to avoid this fault, some say: the maturation of <s>dhyānāntara</s> <s>karma</s> is the pleasure-faculty (<s>sukhendriya</s>) in the [root first] <s>dhyāna</s> itself.

body.text: Tib. 52b
body.translated_text: Others [say]

body.text: naiva tasya dhyānāṃtarakarmaṇo vedanā vipākaḥ. kiṃ tarhi rūpādīty apare. kiṃ teṣāṃ dhyānāṃtaropapattau vedanā nāsti. asti. na tu sā vipākasvabhāvā. kiṃ tarhi. naiṣyandikīti.
body.translated_text: : the feeling of that <s>dhyānāntara</s> <s>karma</s> is not at all the maturation. What then? Form and the rest [are the maturation]. Do they then have no feeling when reborn in the <s>dhyānāntara</s>? They do. But that [feeling] is not of the nature of maturation. What then? It is of the outflow type (<s>naiṣyandikī</s>).

body.text: atrācārya āha. tadetad ucchāstraṃ. yad etad uktaṃ. dhyānāṃtarakarmaṇo dhyāna eva sukhendriyaṃ vipāka iti. yac coktaṃ. naiva tasya vedanā vipāka iti. tad etad ubhayam apy ucchāstraṃ. tat pratipādayann āha. śāstre hi paṭhitam iti vistaraḥ. avitarkasya karmaṇa iti. dhyānāṃtarakarmaṇa ity arthah. ataḥ kuśalasyāvitarkasya karmaṇaś caitasiky eva vedanā vipāko vipacyata ity avadhāraṇān na tasya karmaṇo dhyāna eva sukhendriyaṃ vipāko nāpi vedanāto 'nya iti gamyate. avitarkaṃ hi karma dhyānāṃtarāt prabhṛty ūrdhvam iti.
body.translated_text: Here the <s>Ācārya</s> says: both of these are contrary to the treatise (<s>ucchāstra</s>). What was said — 'the maturation of <s>dhyānāntara</s> <s>karma</s> is the pleasure-faculty in the <s>dhyāna</s> itself' — and what was said — 'the feeling of that is not at all the maturation' — both of these are contrary to the treatise. Demonstrating this, he says: 'For it is read in the treatise (<s>śāstra</s>)' — and so forth in detail. 'Of <s>karma</s> without <s>vitarka</s>' — meaning: of <s>dhyānāntara</s> <s>karma</s>. Therefore, from the restriction that 'for wholesome <s>karma</s> without <s>vitarka</s>, feeling that is mental (<s>caitasikī</s>) alone matures as maturation,' it is understood that neither is the pleasure-faculty in the <s>dhyāna</s> the maturation of that <s>karma</s>, nor is something other than feeling [its maturation]. For <s>karma</s> without <s>vitarka</s> means from the <s>dhyānāntara</s> upward.

body.text: iti. na pūrvaṃ na paścāt. yugapad ity arthaḥ. sukhavedanīyasya rūpam iti cakṣurādikaṃ. duḥkhavedanīyasya cittacaittā iti. paṃcavijñānakāyikāḥ. daurmanasyasyāvipākatvāt. aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyasya cittaviprayuktā iti. jīvitendriyādayaḥ [Tib. 53a] na hi kāmadhātor anyatreti. duḥkhavedanīyasya karmaṇo 'nyatrabhāvāt.
body.translated_text: meaning: not before and not after — simultaneously, is the meaning. 'Of [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced as pleasant, the form' — eye-faculty and the rest. 'Of [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced as painful, mind and mental factors' — those belonging to the five sense-consciousness groups. Because displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) is not maturation. 'Of [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant, [the maturation is] what is dissociated from mind' — the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>) and the rest. 'For not anywhere other than the Desire Realm' — because <s>karma</s> to be experienced as painful does not exist elsewhere.

body.text: kim idānīṃ tad iti. aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyaṃ. evaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. yady adho 'pi caturthād dhyānād aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyaṃ karmāsti kuśalaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'What then is that?' — [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant. 'If so, then' — and so forth in detail. If there is wholesome <s>karma</s> to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant even below the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>,

children.translated_text: 'Wholesome [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced as pleasant, from <s>dhyāna</s> up to the third' —

body.text: ity asya virodhaḥ. na hi kevalaṃ sukhavedanīyaṃ kuśalam ā tṛtīyād dhyānāt. kiṃ tarhi. aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyam apy astīti. iṣṭavipākaṃ ca kuśalam ity asya virodhaḥ. na hi kevalam iṣṭavipākaṃ kuśalam iṣṭāniṣṭaviparītavipākam api kuśalam astīti. bāhulika eṣa nirdeśa iti. bāhulyenaivaṃ nirdiṣṭam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: this is contradicted. For it is not the case that only [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced as pleasant is wholesome up to the third <s>dhyāna</s>; rather, [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant also exists. And 'wholesome [<s>karma</s>] has a desirable maturation' — this too is contradicted. For it is not the case that wholesome [<s>karma</s>] has only a desirable maturation; there is also wholesome [<s>karma</s>] with maturation that is neither desirable nor undesirable. 'This statement is a general one' (<s>bāhulika</s>) — meaning: it was stated thus in a general way.

children.translated_text: 'Wholesome [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced as pleasant, from <s>dhyāna</s> up to the third' —

body.text: iti. iṣṭavipākaṃ ca kuśalam iti.
body.translated_text: thus. 'And wholesome [<s>karma</s>] has a desirable maturation' — thus.

body.text: katham punar avedanāsvabhāvam iti. sukham anubhūyate. na karmety evam abhisamīkṣya pṛcchati. sukhavedanāhitaṃ sukhavedanīyam iti. sukhavedanotpattyanukūlam ity arthaḥ. sukho 'sya vedanīya iti veti. sukho 'sya vipāko 'nubhavanīya ity arthaḥ. snānīyakaṣāyavad [Tib. 53b] iti. yathā yena snāti. sa snānīyaḥ kaṣāyaḥ. evaṃ yena sukhaṃ vipākaṃ vedayate. tat karma
body.translated_text: 'But how can what does not have feeling as its intrinsic nature [be called to-be-experienced]?' — considering that 'pleasure is experienced, not <s>karma</s>' — thus he asks. 'To be experienced as pleasant means producing pleasant feeling' (<s>sukhavedanāhita</s>) — meaning: favorable to the arising of pleasant feeling. 'Or: its pleasant [result] is to be experienced' — meaning: its pleasant maturation is to be experienced. 'Like bathing-alkali' (<s>snānīyakaṣāya</s>) — just as that with which one bathes is the bathing-alkali, so too that <s>karma</s> by which one experiences a pleasant maturation

body.text: vedanīyaṃ. sukhasya vipākasya vedanīyaṃ karma sukhavedanīyaṃ. karaṇe 'pi kṛtyavidhānāt. etad evaṃ duḥkhavedanīyam iti. duḥkhavedanāhitaṃ duḥkhavedanīyam iti vistarṇa pūrvavad yojyaṃ. evam aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyam api.
body.translated_text: is 'to be experienced.' The <s>karma</s> 'to be experienced' of pleasant maturation is '<s>karma</s> to be experienced as pleasant' — because the <s>kṛtya</s> suffix also applies to the instrument. 'Thus it is for to-be-experienced-as-painful' — to-be-experienced-as-painful means producing painful feeling — and so on should be connected in detail as before. Similarly for to-be-experienced-as-neither-painful-nor-pleasant.

body.text: svabhāvavedanīyateti. svabhāvavedanānubhavalakṣaṇena vedanīyasvabhāvaḥ. evaṃ yāvat saṃmukhībhāvena vedanīyateti yojyaṃ. sukhavedanīyaḥ sparśa iti. sukhavedanāhitaṃ sukhaṃ vedanīyam asminn iti sukhavedanīyaḥ sparśaḥ. ālambanavedanīyateti. vedanīyā viṣayāḥ. ālambanīyā ity arthaḥ. rūpapratisaṃvedī no tu rūparāgapratisaṃvadīti. rūpaṃ pratyanubhavati. no tu rūparāgaṃ pratyanubhavatīty arthaḥ. atha vā no tu sa rūpaṃ rāgeṇa pratyanubhavaty ālaṃbata iti. dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyam iti. dṛṣṭe janmani vedanīyaṃ vipākalakṣaṇam asyeti dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ karmeti vistaraḥ. yasmin samaya iti vistaraḥ. yasmin samaye sukhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayate anubhavati. dve asya vedanā duḥkhā aduḥkhāsukhā ca tasmin samaye [Tib. 54a] niruddhe bhavata iti.
body.translated_text: 'To-be-experienced by own nature' (<s>svabhāvavedanīyatā</s>) — to-be-experienced having the nature of own-nature-feeling, of experience. Similarly up to 'to-be-experienced by coming face to face' (<s>saṃmukhībhāva</s>) should be connected. 'Touch to be experienced as pleasant' — the touch that is the cause of pleasant feeling, in which there is pleasant to-be-experienced — this is touch to be experienced as pleasant. 'To-be-experienced as object' (<s>ālambanavedanīyatā</s>) — the objects are to be experienced, meaning: to be taken as objects. 'One who experiences form, not one who experiences passion for form' — one experiences form, but does not experience passion for form — this is the meaning. Or alternatively, one does not experience form with passion, does not take it as object [with passion]. 'To be experienced in the present life' (<s>dṛṣṭadharmavedanīya</s>) — <s>karma</s> whose maturation is to be experienced in the present birth — <s>karma</s> to be experienced in the present life, and so forth in detail. 'At which time' — and so forth in detail. At which time one experiences, one undergoes, pleasant feeling — at that time his two other feelings, painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant, have ceased.

body.text: (IV.51) āraṃbhavaśād iti. dṛṣṭa eva janmani vipākāraṃbhād ity arthaḥ. tannāmavyavasthānam iti. dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyam ity evaṃnāmavyavasthānam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.51) 'Because of the commencement of maturation' (<s>āraṃbhavaśāt</s>) — meaning: because of the commencement of maturation in this very present birth. 'The establishment of that name' — meaning: the establishment of the name 'to be experienced in the present life.'

body.text: asti hīti vistaraḥ. saṃnikṛṣṭaphalasya karmaṇaḥ suvarcalādṛṣṭāṃtaḥ. viprakṛṣṭaphalasya yavagodhūmādayaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'For there is' — and so forth in detail. For <s>karma</s> with proximate fruit, the <s>suvarcalā</s> plant is the example; for [<s>karma</s>] with remote fruit, barley, wheat, and the like.

body.text: dārṣṭāṃtikāḥ sautrāṃtikāḥ. teṣām evaṃ prathamadvitīye koṭyau varṇayatāṃ karmāṣṭavidhaṃ. dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ niyatam aniyataṃ ca vipākaṃ prati. evaṃ yāvad aniyatavedanīyam iti. upapadyavedanīyaṃ niyatam aniyataṃ ca vipākaṃ prati. aparaparyāyavedanīyam api niyatam aniyataṃ ca. aniyatavedanīyam api yo dṛṣṭadharmādyaniyatavedanīyaṃ. tan niyatam aniyataṃ ca. ity aṣṭavidhaṃ.
body.translated_text: The <s>Dārṣṭāntikas</s> are the <s>Sautrāntikas</s>. For them, in formulating the first and second alternatives thus, <s>karma</s> is eightfold: to be experienced in the present life — determined and undetermined with respect to maturation. Similarly up to: to be experienced at an indefinite time. To be experienced at rebirth — determined and undetermined with respect to maturation. To be experienced in a later life — also determined and undetermined. And to be experienced at an indefinite time — that which is indefinite as to present-life and the rest — also determined and undetermined. Thus eightfold.

body.text: (IV.52, 53) caturvidhaṃ karmākṣiped iti. dṛṣṭadharmādivedanīyaṃ caturvidhaṃ karmākṣiped ity arthaḥ. katham ity āha. syāt triṣu prāṇātipātādattādānamṛṣāvādeṣu paraṃ prayojya kāmamithyācāre svayam ātmanā prayuktaḥ. teṣāṃ karmanāṃ yugapatparisamāptau. ekaṃ dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyam aparam upapadyavedanīyam aparaṃ cāparaparyāyavedanīyam anyac cāniyatavedanīyam iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.52, 53) 'A fourfold <s>karma</s> would project' — meaning: the fourfold <s>karma</s> to be experienced in the present life and the rest would project. How? He says: one may, with respect to three — killing, taking what is not given, and false speech — employ another, and with respect to sexual misconduct engage personally. Upon the simultaneous completion of those <s>karma</s>s, one is to be experienced in the present life, another at rebirth, another in a later life, and yet another at an indefinite time.

body.text: kuśalānām akuśalānāṃ ca yathāsaṃbhavam iti. yatrākuśalasya saṃbhavaḥ kāmadhātāv eva nānyatra.
