body.translated_text: 'Of wholesome and unwholesome as applicable' — the unwholesome is possible only in the Desire Realm, not elsewhere.

body.text: ity [Tib. 54b] asyotsargasyāyam apavādaḥ. śubhasya narake trividheti. tridhaivety avadhāraṇaṃ. narakeṣu kuśalasya karmaṇas trividhasyaivākṣepaḥ. na caturvidhasya. dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ sthāpayitvā. atra narakeṣv iṣṭavipākābhāvāt. śubhagrahaṇam aśubhanirāsārthaṃ. akuśalasya hi caturvidhasyāpi narakeṣv ākṣepaḥ saṃbhavati.
body.translated_text: this is the exception to that general rule. 'Of the wholesome, threefold in the hells' — 'threefold only' is a restriction. In the hells, the projection of wholesome <s>karma</s> is of three types only, not four — setting aside that to be experienced in the present life, because of the absence of desirable maturation there. The mention of 'wholesome' is for the purpose of excluding the unwholesome. For the projection of even fourfold unwholesome [<s>karma</s>] is possible in the hells.

children.translated_text: 'One who is dispassionate toward that, stable, [and] an ordinary person' —

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: yato virakto yadvirakta iti samāsaḥ. sthiragrahaṇaṃ parihāṇadharmaṇo nirāsārthaṃ. tasya hi tasyāṃ bhūmāv upapadyavedanīyaṃ karma saṃbhavati. bālagrahaṇam āryanivṛttyarthaṃ. āryasya hi tatropapadyavedanīyaṃ aparaparyāyavedanīyaṃ ca na saṃbhavati. anāgāmitvāt.
body.translated_text: The compound is: 'dispassionate toward that from which one is dispassionate.' The mention of 'stable' (<s>sthira</s>) is for the purpose of excluding one of the nature of retrogression (<s>parihāṇadharman</s>). For one of the nature of retrogression, <s>karma</s> to be experienced at rebirth in that ground is possible. The mention of 'ordinary person' (<s>bāla</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the Noble person (<s>ārya</s>). For a Noble person, <s>karma</s> to be experienced at rebirth and in a later life there is not possible — because of being a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>).

children.translated_text: 'Nor does a Noble person produce [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced in another [life]' —

body.text: nāparaparyāyavedanīyakṛd api. nopapadyavedanīyakṛd apīty arthaḥ. tatra yuktiṃ darśayann āha. na hy asau bhavyaḥ punar ādhastīṃ bhūmim āyātum iti. na hy asāv āryo 'parihāṇadharmā yato vītarāgaḥ. tata ādhastīm adhastātbhavāṃ bhūmim āyātuṃ bhavyaḥ. parihāṇadharmā tu bhavyaḥ. tadyathā. āryo bhavāgralābhī parihāṇadharmā yaḥ parihāya rūpadhātāv upapadyeta. tasyopapadyavedanīyam aparaparyāyavedanīyaṃ cāpi saṃbhavati yathoktam udāyisūtre. aniyataṃ kuryād iti. aniyatavedanīyam aparihāṇadharmāpy āryo dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ ca yatropapannaḥ. [Tib. 55a] tatra kuryāt. kāmadhātor bhavāgrād vā vītarāga iti. kāmavītarāgo 'nāgāmī. bhavāgravītarāgo 'rhan. tayor iti kāmadhātubhavāgrayoḥ. paścāt pravedayiṣyāma iti.
body.translated_text: nor does one produce [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced in a later life. Nor to be experienced at rebirth — this is the meaning. Showing the reasoning therein, he says: 'For that one is not capable of coming again to a lower ground.' For that Noble person, not of the nature of retrogression, who is dispassionate from that — is not capable of coming to a ground below that, a ground of lower existence. But one of the nature of retrogression is capable. For example: a Noble person who has attained the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>), of the nature of retrogression, who having retrogressed would be reborn in the Form Realm — for that one, <s>karma</s> to be experienced at rebirth and even in a later life is possible, as stated in the <s>Udāyi Sūtra</s>. 'One may produce indeterminate [<s>karma</s>]' — even a Noble person not of the nature of retrogression may produce <s>karma</s> to be experienced at an indefinite time, and to be experienced in the present life, where one is born — there one may produce it. 'One dispassionate from the Desire Realm or from the peak of existence' — one dispassionate from <s>Kāma</s> is a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>); one dispassionate from the peak of existence is an <s>Arhat</s>. 'Of those two' — of the Desire Realm and the peak of existence. 'We shall explain later.'

children.translated_text: 'One who dies does not lose the fruit' —

body.text: ityādi.
body.translated_text: and so forth.

body.text: (IV.54) aṃtarābhavavedanīyaṃ ca. kiṃ. niyatam aniyataṃ ceti. yan niyatam ekādaśavidham uktaṃ. dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ yat tad iti. kalalavedanīyaṃ niyataṃ yāvad aṃtarābhavavedanīyaṃ niyatam iti. yāś ca tadanvayā daśāvasthā iti. aṃtarābhavapūrvikā ity arthaḥ. ata evānyad aṃtarābhavavedanīyaṃ karma noktam iti. caturvidhaṃ karma. dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyam upapadyavedanīyam aparaparyāyavedanīyaṃ aniyatavedanīyaṃ cety atra noktam. upapadyavedanīyenaiva tasyāntarābhavasyākṣepāt.
body.translated_text: (IV.54) 'And [<s>karma</s>] to be experienced in the intermediate existence.' What? — determined and undetermined. That which has been stated as elevenfold determined: to be experienced in the present life — that which — to be experienced as <s>kalala</s> (embryo), determined, up to: to be experienced in the intermediate existence, determined. 'And the ten states that follow from that' — meaning: preceded by the intermediate existence. For this very reason, another [category of] <s>karma</s> to be experienced in the intermediate existence was not stated — in the fourfold <s>karma</s> of to be experienced in the present life, at rebirth, in a later life, and at an indefinite time — it was not stated therein, because the intermediate existence is projected by <s>karma</s> to be experienced at rebirth itself.

body.text: (IV.55) niyatāniyataṃ karmety uktam ato bravīti. kīdṛśaṃ punaḥ karma niyatam
body.translated_text: (IV.55) Since it has been stated that <s>karma</s> is determined and undetermined, therefore he says: 'What kind of <s>karma</s> is determined?'

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. phalasamāpattiviśeṣaprāpta iti. darśanamārgaphalaprāpto 'rhattvaphalaprāptaś ca phalaviśeṣaprāpta iṣyate. viśeṣagrahaṇam anāsravamārgaprāpyaphalagrahaṇārthaṃ. samāpattiviśeṣaprāpto nirodhāraṇāmaitrīsamāpattilābhī. atrāpi viśeṣagrahaṇaṃ [Tib. 55b] tadanyalaukikasamāpattiviśeṣaṇārthaṃ. yathā tathā ceti. yadi puṇyabuddhyā yadi dveṣādinā. yo 'pi hi pārasikaḥ puṇyabuddhyā mātaraṃ mārayati. pitaraṃ vā. tad akuśalam ānaṃtaryaṃ karma niyataṃ saṃpadyate. nānyad iti. yad ato viparītaṃ mandakleśaprasādakṛtam ityādi.
body.translated_text: — and so forth in detail. 'Having attained special fruition and attainment' — one who has attained the fruit of the path of seeing, and one who has attained the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s>, are accepted as having attained special fruition. The mention of 'special' is for the purpose of including fruit obtainable through the uncontaminated path. 'Having attained special attainment' — one who has obtained the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>), the <s>araṇā</s> [attainment], and the <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) attainment. Here too, the mention of 'special' is for the purpose of distinguishing from other mundane attainments. 'In whatever way' — whether with the thought of merit or through hatred and the like. For even a Persian (<s>pārasika</s>) who kills his mother with the thought of merit — or his father — that unwholesome <s>ānantarya</s> (immediate-retribution) <s>karma</s> becomes determined. 'Not other' — that which is the opposite of this, performed with mild affliction and devotion, and so forth.

body.text: (IV.56) saṃghastrīvādasamudācārād iti. bhikṣuṇā kila kenacid vyavahāraparājitena saṃghaḥ striyo yūyam iti samudācaritaḥ. tasya dṛṣṭa eva dharme puruṣavyaṃjanam aṃtarhitaṃ. strīvyaṃjanaṃ ca prādurbhūtam iti. tad idaṃ kṣetraviśeṣād dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ bhavati. āśayaviśeṣād iti. śaṃṭhena gavām apuṃstvaṃ kariṣyamāṇam abhivīkṣya mamedṛśam apuṃstve duḥkham iti tīvreṇāśayena teṣāṃ gavām apuṃstvaṃ pratimokṣitaṃ. tasya dṛṣṭa eva dharme puruṣendriyaṃ prādurbhūtam. idam āśayaviśeṣād dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ karma saṃvṛttaṃ.
body.translated_text: (IV.56) 'From addressing the <s>Saṃgha</s> as women' — a certain <s>bhikṣu</s>, it is said, having been defeated in a legal dispute, addressed the <s>Saṃgha</s> saying: 'You are women!' In that very present life, his male characteristics disappeared and female characteristics appeared. This is <s>karma</s> to be experienced in the present life because of the special nature of the field (<s>kṣetra</s>). 'Because of the special nature of intention' — a eunuch (<s>śaṃṭha</s>), seeing that castration was about to be performed on cows, [thought] with intense intention: 'May beings like me [be spared] the suffering of castration!' and liberated those cows from castration. In that very present life, the male faculty appeared for him. This is <s>karma</s> that became to-be-experienced-in-the-present-life because of the special nature of intention.

body.text: iti. tato bhūmer atyaṃtavairāgyāt tad adṛṣṭadharmavedanīyam api karma dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ saṃpadyate. yathānāgāmyarhatām avītarāgāvasthākṛtaṃ. punar adharabhūmyanāgamanād anupādāya ca parinirvāṇāt. na tv avasthāyām iti. yad aniyataṃ dṛṣṭadharmādyavasthāsu. na cāniyataṃ vipāke. niyatatvāt. tad eva dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyaṃ bhavati. ata evāha. yat punar avasthāṃtare dṛṣṭadharmādike niyatam. tasya tatraivavasthāṃtare vipākaḥ. [Tib. 56a] tadvato 'tyaṃtavairāgyāsaṃbhavād iti. evam avasthāṃtaraniyatavipākena karmaṇā tadvatpudgalasyātyaṃtaṃ tasyā bhūmer vairāgyāsaṃbhavād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Therefore, because of complete dispassion from that ground, even that karma which is to be experienced as not-visible-dharma-experienced becomes visible-dharma-experienced. Just as [karma done] by non-returners and Arhats in the state of not-yet-dispassionate. Furthermore, because of not returning to a lower ground, and because of parinirvāṇa without clinging. 'But not in the life-state' — that which is indeterminate with respect to the life-states of visible-dharma and the rest, yet not indeterminate with respect to retribution — because of being determinate [in retribution] — that itself becomes visible-dharma-experienced. Therefore he says: but that which is determinate in another life-state such as visible-dharma and the rest — its retribution is in that very other life-state. [Tib. 56a] Because of the impossibility of complete dispassion from the ground for the person possessing it — this is the meaning. Thus, with karma whose retribution is determinate in another life-state, because of the impossibility of complete dispassion from that ground for the person possessing it — this is the meaning.

body.text: (IV.57) kṣetraviśeṣād ity uktam ataḥ pṛcchati. kīdṛśaṃ punaḥ kṣetram iti. araṇāvyutthitasyeti vistaraḥ. apramāṇeṣu sattveṣu araṇayā hito 'dhyāśayo 'bhiprāyaḥ. tenānugatā. atyudagreṇa tīkṣṇena. apramāṇena puṇyena paribhāvitānugatā ca saṃtatir vartate. araṇām uttaratra vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: (IV.57) 'Because of a special field' was stated; therefore he asks: 'What kind of field is it?' 'Of one who has emerged from <s>araṇā</s>' — this is the elaboration. The beneficial intention toward immeasurable beings through <s>araṇā</s> (non-contention) — this is the intention. Accompanied by that; with extremely prominent, keen, immeasurable merit — the continuum operates as cultivated and accompanied [by it]. He will discuss <s>araṇā</s> later on:

body.text: ity atra. maitrīvyutthitasyeti vistaraḥ. apramāṇeṣu sattveṣu sukham utpadyatām
body.translated_text: in that [passage]. 'Of one who has emerged from loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>)' — this is the elaboration. The intention 'May happiness arise for immeasurable beings'

body.text: ity adhyāśayaḥ. tenānugatā. atyudagreti sarvaṃ pūrvavat. pratyagrāśrayaparivṛttinirmaleti. pratyagrābhinavā. aciravyutthitatvāt. pratyagrāśrayasya śarīrasya parivṛttyā nirmalā saṃtatiḥ. eteṣu pudgaleṣu kṛtānāṃ karāpakārāṇām upakārāpakārāṇāṃ kuśalākuśalānāṃ. phalaṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharma ihaiva janmani prāpyata iti. sadyo'rthaṃ darśayati. sadya iveti kṛtvā. śeṣasya tv iti vistaraḥ. śeṣo bhāvanāmārgaḥ sakṛdāgāmyanāgāmiphalaprāpakaḥ. aparipūrṇaḥ svabhāvaḥ phalaṃ vāsyety aparipūrṇasvabhāvaphalaḥ. tasya bhāvaḥ. [Tib. 56b] tasmāt. aparipūrṇasvabhāvaphalatvāt. kā punas tasya paripūrṇasvabhāvatā paripūrṇaphalatā ca. aśaikṣatvaṃ paripūrṇasvabhāvatā. sa hi mārgo 'śaikṣasvabhāvaḥ. yenārhattvaṃ prāpyate. paripūrṇaphalatāpy arthattvaprāptiḥ. sa hi phalamārgas tribhiḥ phalaiḥ phalavān iti. atha vā kṣayajñānasaṃgṛhīto mārgaḥ paripūrṇasvabhāvaphalaḥ. paripūrṇasvabhāvo yasmād aśaikṣamārgaḥ. paripūrṇaphalo niravaśeṣaphalatvāt. tadvyutthitānām iti. śeṣabhāvanāmārgavyutthitānāṃ. na te tadvyutthitās tathā puṇyakṣetraṃ bhavaṃti. yathārhattvavyutthitāḥ. prāg eva laukikamārgavyutthitāḥ. bhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ hi kleśānāṃ sāvaśeṣaniravaśeṣaprahāṇād ayaṃ viśeṣa ukta ity avagaṃtavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: — this is the intention. Accompanied by that; with extremely prominent — all as before. 'With a freshly transformed and pure basis' — fresh means new, because of having emerged recently. The continuum is pure through the transformation of the fresh basis, the body. For those who have performed acts of benefit and harm — acts of benefit and harm, wholesome and unwholesome — toward these persons, the fruit is obtained in this very visible dharma, in this very birth. He shows the immediate effect: 'immediately,' as it were. 'But of the remaining' — this is the elaboration. The remaining is the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), which leads to the fruits of once-returning and non-returning. Its nature or fruit is incomplete — hence 'having incomplete nature and fruit.' The abstract noun of that. [Tib. 56b] Therefore — because of having incomplete nature and fruit. What then is its complete nature and complete fruit? The non-learner state (<s>aśaikṣatva</s>) is the complete nature, for that path has the nature of the non-learner. By which <s>Arhatship</s> is attained. Complete fruit too is the attainment of <s>Arhatship</s>. For that fruit-path is endowed with three fruits. Or alternatively, the path included in the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) has complete nature and fruit. Complete nature because it is the non-learner path. Complete fruit because of having fruit without remainder. 'Of those who have emerged from that' — of those who have emerged from the remaining cultivation-path. They, having emerged from that, are not as much a field of merit as those who have emerged from <s>Arhatship</s>. How much less those who have emerged from the mundane path. For this distinction is stated because of the partial and complete abandonment of afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation — this should be understood.

body.text: (IV.58) tasyā avaśyaṃ savitarkasavicāratvād iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.58) 'Because it necessarily has deliberation and examination' (<s>savitarkasavicāra</s>) —

children.translated_text: 'For the five consciousness-elements have deliberation and examination' —

body.text: iti niyamāt. vitarkavicārayoś cādhyānāṃtarādisvabhāvāt. na cāvitarkasya karmaṇaḥ savitarka vicāro 'dharabhūmiko vipāko yujyata iti. tasya hi duḥkhā vedanā vipāka iti vistaraḥ. tasyākuśalasya duḥkhā vedanā vipāka iṣyate. tasyāniṣṭaphalatvāt. [Tib. 57a] caitasikī ca duḥkhā vedanā daurmanasyaṃ nānyad asti. na ca daurmanasyaṃ vipāka iti vyākhyātam etad iti. indriyanirdeśe
body.translated_text: because of this rule. And because deliberation and examination have the nature of [being limited to] below the first <s>dhyāna</s> and the rest. And because it is not fitting that karma without deliberation should have retribution in a lower ground with deliberation and examination. 'For its retribution is painful feeling' — this is the elaboration. The retribution of that unwholesome [karma] is accepted as painful feeling, because of producing an undesirable result. [Tib. 57a] And the mental painful feeling is displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) — there is no other. And it has been explained that displeasure is not retribution — in the chapter on faculties:

children.text:
vipāko jīvitaṃ dvedhā dvādaśāṃtyāṣṭakād ṛte
daurmanasyāc ceti.
children.translated_text: 'Retribution is the life-faculty, twofold [feeling], and the twelve ending in the eighth, except for displeasure' —

body.text: (IV.59) daurmanasyaṃ na vipāka ity etad amṛṣyann āha. yat tarhīti vistaraḥ. yadi daurmanasyaṃ na vipākaḥ. yat tarhi sattvānāṃ cittakṣepo bhavati. katamasminn asau citte bhavati kena vā kāraṇeneti. tasyāyam abhiprāyaḥ. cittakṣepo na paṃcasu vijñānakāyeṣu. teṣām avikalpakatvāt. sa cākuśalaketuko 'niṣṭatvāt. ity ato vipākena daurmanasyena bhavitavyam iti. avikalpakatvād iti. abhinirūpaṇānusmaraṇavikalpābhyām avikalpakatvāt paṃcānāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ
body.translated_text: (IV.59) Not accepting that displeasure is not retribution, he says: 'But then' — this is the elaboration. If displeasure is not retribution, then the mental disturbance that occurs in beings — in what kind of mind does it occur, and by what cause? His intent is this: mental disturbance does not occur in the five consciousness-groups, because of their being non-conceptual. And it has an unwholesome root, because of being undesirable. Therefore it must be retributive displeasure. 'Because of being non-conceptual' — because of the absence of deliberative and recollective conceptualization in the five consciousness-groups

body.text: . cittakṣepasya cāsadvikalpalakṣaṇatvāt. agniṃ vā dāveṣūtsṛjaṃtīti. dāvas tṛṇādigahanāṃvito deśaviśeṣaḥ. anyena vā kenacid iti. aniṣṭavedanādinā. vāsiṣṭhīprabhṛtīnām iti. bhagavān mithilikāyāṃ viharati sma. mithilāmravaṇe. tena khalu punaḥ samayena vasiṣṭhasagotrāyā brāhmaṇyāḥ ṣaṭ putrāḥ kālagatāḥ. sā teṣāṃ kālakriyayā nagnonmattā kṣiptacittā tenatenānuhiṇḍaṃtī yena mithilāmravaṇaṃ tenopasaṃkrāṃtā. tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān anekaśatāyā bhikṣuparṣadaḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaṃ deśayati sma. adrākṣīd vasiṣṭhasagotrā [Tib. 57b] brāhmaṇī bhagavaṃtaṃ dūrād eva. dṛṣṭvā ca punar jehrīyamāṇarūpā utkuṭakāsthāt. smṛtiṃ ca labdhavatī. adrākṣīt bhagavān vasiṣṭhasagotrāṃ brāhmaṇīṃ dūrād eva. dṛṣṭvā ca punar āyuṣmaṃtam ānandam āmaṃtrayate sma. anuprayacchānanda vasiṣṭhasagotrāyai brāhmaṇyai uttarāsaṃgaṃ. dharmam asyai deśayiṣyāmi. āyuṣmān ānando vasiṣṭhasagotrāyai brāhmaṇyai uttarāsaṃgam adāt. atha vasiṣṭhasagotrā brāhmaṇī uttarāsaṃgaṃ prāvṛtya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāṃtā. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikaṃte niṣaṇṇā. ekāṃtaniṣaṇṇāṃ vasiṣṭhasagotrāṃ brāhmaṇīṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati. samādāpayati. samuttejayati. saṃpraharṣayatīty evamādi. vistaragraṃthabhayāt sarvasūtraṃ na likhitaṃ. ayaṃ tatrārthaḥ bhagavāṃs tasyai dānakathādi kṛtvā. catvāry āryasatyāni deśitavān. yāvat tayā srotaāpattiphalam adhigatam. adhigamya ca bhagavato 'ṃtikāt prakrāntā. tasyā apareṇa samayena saptamaḥ putraḥ kālagataḥ. sā tatkālakriyayā na śocati. tām aśocaṃtīṃ svabhartābravīt. tvaṃ pūrvaṃ putramaraṇena paritaptāsi. idānīṃ nāsi paritaptā. nūnaṃ te putrās tvayā bhakṣitāḥ. yato na paritapyasa iti. sā taṃ pratyuvāca.
body.translated_text: . And because mental disturbance has the characteristic of false conceptualization. 'Or they release fire in forests' — a forest is a specific area overgrown with thickets of grass and the like. 'Or by some other [cause]' — by unpleasant feeling and the like. 'Of <s>Vāsiṣṭhī</s> and the rest' — the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Mithilā</s>, in the <s>Mithilā</s> Mango Grove. At that time, six sons of a <s>brāhmaṇī</s> of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s lineage had died. She, due to their deaths, became naked, mad, her mind disturbed, wandering here and there, and came to the <s>Mithilā</s> Mango Grove. At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, seated before an assembly of several hundred <s>bhikṣu</s>s, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>brāhmaṇī</s> of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s lineage [Tib. 57b] saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar. Having seen him, she felt embarrassed and squatted down. And she recovered her mindfulness. The <s>Bhagavān</s> saw the <s>brāhmaṇī</s> of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s lineage from afar. Having seen her, he addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Give the <s>brāhmaṇī</s> of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s lineage an upper robe, <s>Ānanda</s>. I will teach her the <s>Dharma</s>.' The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> gave the <s>brāhmaṇī</s> of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s lineage an upper robe. Then the <s>brāhmaṇī</s> of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s lineage, having wrapped herself in the upper robe, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, she bowed her head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat to one side. To the <s>brāhmaṇī</s> of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s lineage sitting to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructs, encourages, inspires, and delights her with a talk on the <s>Dharma</s> — and so forth. The entire <s>sūtra</s> has not been written for fear of excessive length. The point here is: the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave her a talk on giving and the rest, taught her the four noble truths, and she attained the fruit of stream-entry. Having attained it, she departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. At a later time, her seventh son died. She did not grieve at his death. Seeing her not grieving, her husband said to her: 'Before, you were tormented by the death of your sons. Now you are not tormented. Surely your sons were eaten by you — since you are not tormented.' She replied to him:

children.text:
putrapautrasahasrāṇi jñātisaṃghaśatāni ca
dīrghe 'dhvani mayā brahmaṃ khāditāni tathā tvayā.
putrapautrasahsrāṇāṃ parimāṇaṃ na vidyate
anyonyaṃ khādyamānānāṃ [Tib. 58a] tāsutāsūpapattiṣu.
kaḥ śocet paritapyeta parideveta vā punaḥ
jñātvā niḥsaraṇaṃ loke jāteś ca maraṇasya ca.
sāhaṃ niḥsaraṇaṃ jñātvā jāteś ca maraṇasya ca
na śocāmi na tapyāmi kṛte buddhasya śāsana
children.translated_text:
'Thousands of sons and grandsons, and hundreds of kinship groups,
In the long course, O <s>Brahmin</s>, have been eaten by me and by you.
Of thousands of sons and grandsons, no measure is found,
Of those who devoured one another [Tib. 58a] in those births and rebirths.
Who would grieve, be tormented, or lament,
Having known the escape in the world from birth and death?
I, having known the escape from birth and death,
Do not grieve, am not tormented — for the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> has been fulfilled.'

body.text: ity evamādi. kathaṃ na caitasikī vedanā vipākaḥ prāpnoti. tasyākuśalasya karmaṇa iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. mahābhūtānāṃ prakopo vipāka iti. vipaktir vipākaḥ. tasmāj jātam ato vipākajaṃ cittam. ata eva sa ca karmavipākaja ity uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: And so forth. How is it that mental feeling is not established as retribution? — of that unwholesome karma, is the rest of the sentence. 'The derangement of the great elements is the retribution' — maturation (<s>vipakti</s>) is retribution (<s>vipāka</s>). The mind born from that — therefore born from retribution (<s>vipākaja</s>). For this very reason it was said: 'And that is born from the retribution of karma' —

body.text: na tūktaṃ. sa ca karmaja iti. evaṃ cedaṃ iti vistaraḥ. yasmāt karmajena yāvat bhraṣṭasmṛtikaṃ cittaṃ vartate. tasmād idaṃ catuṣkoṭikaṃ yujyata iti. ubhayaṃ kṣiptacittasya kliṣṭaṃ cittam ity eva tatrodāharaṇaṃ. na hi kliṣṭaṃ cittaṃ vipāko yujyate.
body.translated_text: but it was not said: 'And that is born from karma.' 'If it is thus' — this is the elaboration. Since through retribution-born [mind] — up to: the mind operates with lost mindfulness — therefore this fourfold analysis is fitting. The example for 'both' is the afflicted mind of one whose mind is disturbed. For afflicted mind is not reasonably retribution —

body.text: iti vacanāt. abhinunnā abhipīḍitāḥ. hācittaparidevakaś cātra nāraka ihodāhāryaḥ. kṣiptacittā nārakā bhavaṃtīti. anyatra buddhād iti. mahāpuṇyasaṃbhāratvān na buddhasya. tadvat bhūtavaiṣamyenāpi cittaṃ kṣipyate. na karmaṇeti. kiṃ. āryāṇāṃ kṣipyate cittaṃ anyatra bhūtavaiṣamyād eva. kiṃ kāraṇam ity āha. niyatasya karmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ pṛthagjanāvasthāyām [Tib. 58b] eva vipākāt. aniyatasyāvipākād āryāvasthāyāṃ. ata eva caitad aniyatam ity ucyate. paṃcabhayasamatikramād iti. paṃca bhayāni. ājīvikābhayam aślokabhayaṃ pariṣacchāradyabhayaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ durgatibhayaṃ ca. tatrāślokabhayam akīrtibhayaṃ. parṣacchāradyabhayaṃ sabhāyāṃ sāṃkucityaṃ. aprasādikasyeti. aprasadanīyasya karmaṇaḥ. dharmatābhijñatvād iti. sarvaṃ sāsravaṃ duḥkhaṃ. sarve saṃskārā anityāḥ. sarvā dharmā anātmāna iti. dharmasvabhāvābhijñatvāt.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. '<s>Abhinnunā</s>' means oppressed, afflicted. The example of the lamenting hell-being should be cited here: hell-beings have disturbed minds. 'Except for the <s>Buddha</s>' — because of the <s>Buddha</s>'s great accumulation of merit, [his mind] is not [disturbed]. Similarly, the mind is also disturbed by the imbalance of material elements — not by karma. What? The minds of noble ones are disturbed — only through the imbalance of elements. For what reason? He says: because the retribution of determinate karma [occurred] already before, in the state of an ordinary person. [Tib. 58b] And because indeterminate [karma] does not have retribution in the state of a noble one. For this very reason it is called indeterminate. 'Because of the transcendence of five fears' — the five fears are: fear regarding livelihood, fear of disrepute, fear of timidity in assemblies, fear of death, and fear of bad destinations. Therein, fear of disrepute is fear of loss of fame. Fear of timidity in assemblies is shrinking in public gatherings. 'Of one who is disagreeable' — of disagreeable karma. 'Because of knowing the nature of <s>dharma</s>s' — 'All that has outflows is suffering; all formations are impermanent; all <s>dharma</s>s are without self' — because of knowing the intrinsic nature of <s>dharma</s>s.

body.text: (IV.60ab) kuṭilānvayatvād iti. kuṭilahetukatvāt. sādhyam hi kauṭilyaṃ. raṃjanānvayatvād iti yathā kaṣāyo raṃjanahetuḥ. tathāpīty atas tatsādharmyād evam uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: (IV.60ab) 'Because of following a crooked [cause]' — because of having a crooked cause. For crookedness is what is to be proved. 'Because of following a dyeing [cause]' — just as a dye (<s>kaṣāya</s>) is a cause of coloring, so too — 'even so' — therefore, because of similarity to that, it is thus stated.

body.text: anena śubhaṃ viśeṣyate. nāśubhaṃ. tasyāvaśyaṃ kāmāptatvāt. ārūpyāptaṃ kasmān nocyata iti. tad api hy akuśalena na vyatibhidyate. na vyatimiśryata ity arthaḥ. yatra kileti vistaraḥ. kilaśabdaḥ paramate. yatra kilāṃtarābhaviko aṃtarābhave bhavo vipākaḥ. evam aupapattibhaviko 'pi. trividhasya ca kāyavāṅmanaskarmaṇo vipāko dhyānasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītayoḥ kāyavākkarmaṇoḥ dvitīyādiṣv api dhyāneṣu sadbhāvād asti. tatraivoktaṃ śuklaṃ śuklavipākam [Tib. 59a] iti. tad api tūktaṃ sātrāṃtara iti. tad apy ārūpyāptaṃ. asti karma śuklaṃ śuklavipākaṃ. tadyathā prathame dhyāne. evaṃ yāvat bhavāgra iti. anena svābhiprāyaṃ darśayati. yena kilaśabdaṃ prayuktavān. saṃtānata etad vyavasthāpitam iti. ekasmin saṃtāne kuśalaṃ cākuśalaṃ ca samudācaratīti kṛtvā kuśalam akuśalena vyavakīryate. anyonyavirodhād iti. kuśalam akuśalena virudhyate. akuśalaṃ ca kuśaleneti. dvirūpatā na
body.translated_text: by this, the wholesome is qualified, not the unwholesome — because of the latter necessarily being obtained in the Desire Realm. 'Why is that obtained in the Formless Realm not mentioned?' — because that too is not different from the unwholesome. Not different means not mixed — this is the meaning. 'Where indeed' — this is the elaboration. The particle <s>kila</s> indicates another's view. Where indeed the intermediate-existence [karma] is the retribution in the intermediate existence — so too the birth-existence [karma]. And the retribution of the threefold karma — bodily, vocal, and mental — exists because of the existence of bodily and vocal karma included in the <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint in the second and subsequent <s>dhyānas</s> too. Therein it was stated: 'white with white retribution' — [Tib. 59a]. 'That too was stated in another <s>sūtra</s>' — that too, [karma] obtained in the Formless Realm — 'There is karma that is white with white retribution, such as in the first <s>dhyāna</s>; so too up to the peak of existence' — by this he shows his own view, for which reason he used the particle <s>kila</s>. 'This is established in terms of the [mental] continuum' — in a single continuum, both wholesome and unwholesome operate; therefore the wholesome is interspersed with the unwholesome. 'Because of mutual opposition' — the wholesome is opposed by the unwholesome, and the unwholesome by the wholesome. 'The two natures' are not

body.text: yujyate.
body.translated_text: fitting.

body.text: nāvaśyam akuśalaṃ kuśalena vyavakīryata iti vistaraḥ. vyavakīryate na tv avaśyaṃ. yasmāt kāmadhātau pratipakṣabhūtasya samādher abhāvād akuśalasya balavattvaṃ. ata eva ca kuśalasya durbalatvaṃ. tathā hi kāmadhātau mithyādṛṣṭyā kuśalamūlasamucchedo bhavati. na tu samyagdṛṣṭyā mithyādṛṣṭisamucchedo bhavati.
body.translated_text: 'The unwholesome is not necessarily interspersed with the wholesome' — this is the elaboration. It is interspersed, but not necessarily. Because in the Desire Realm, due to the absence of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) that serves as an antidote, the unwholesome is powerful. And for this very reason, the wholesome is weak. For indeed, in the Desire Realm, through wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) there is the cutting off of wholesome roots. But through right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), there is no cutting off of wrong view.

body.text: ābhiprāyiko hy eṣo 'śuklaśabda iti. vipākaśuklatābhāvād aśuklaṃ. na tu naiva śuklam ity arthaḥ. api ca yac chuklam uktaṃ. tan na bhavatīty aśuklaṃ. mahatyāṃ śūnyatāyām iti. mahāśūnyatārthasūtre. anivṛtāvyākṛtāś ca śuklāḥ. akliṣṭatvāt. avipākaṃ dhātvapatitatvād [Tib. 59b] iti. anāsravā dharmāḥ na dhātupatitāḥ. dhātupatitaś ca vijpāka ity ato 'nāsravaṃ karmavipākaṃ. kasmād ity āha. pravṛttivirodhata iti. anāsravaṃ hi karma dhātupatitānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pravṛttiṃ viruṇaddhi. na tu janayatīty avipākaṃ.
body.translated_text: For this word 'non-white' (<s>aśukla</s>) is used with a special intention. It is non-white because of the absence of whiteness as retribution — but the meaning is not that it is not white at all. Moreover, what was called 'white' — that does not come into being — [hence] non-white. 'In the great emptiness' — in the <s>sūtra</s> on the meaning of great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>). And the unobstructed-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>) [dharmas] are white — because of being unafflicted. '[It is] without retribution because of not falling within a realm' — outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) <s>dharma</s>s do not fall within a realm. And retribution does fall within a realm. Therefore outflow-free <s>karma</s> is without retribution. Why? He says: because of contradicting the operation [of realm-bound dharmas]. For outflow-free <s>karma</s> obstructs the operation of <s>dharma</s>s that fall within a realm — it does not generate them. Therefore it is without retribution.

body.text: (IV.62, 63) karmakarmakṣayāyeti. dviḥ karmagrahaṇaṃ yat tat karmāstīty apadiṣṭaṃ. tat karma sat saṃvidyamānam apracyutasvabhāvaṃ karmakṣayāya saṃvartata ity asya caturthasya karmaṇo dyotanārthaṃ. atha vā. vīpsāprayoga eṣaḥ. karmaṇaḥ karmaṇaḥ kṣayāya saṃvartata ity arthaḥ. eatasṛṣv iti vistaraḥ. dharmakṣāṃtigrahaṇaṃ kāmavairāgye cānaṃtaryamārgagrahaṇaṃ kāmāvacarasya kṛṣṇasya karmaṇaḥ prahāṇamārgatvāt. anāsravamārgasyaivehādhikṛtatvāl laukikā ānaṃtaryamārgās tatprahāṇabhūtā api na gṛhyaṃte.
body.translated_text: (IV.62, 63) '<s>Karma</s>-<s>karma</s>-cessation' — the double use of the word '<s>karma</s>' indicates that '<s>karma</s> exists.' That <s>karma</s>, being existent, being present, not having fallen from its own-nature, conduces to the cessation of <s>karma</s> — this is for the illumination of this fourth [type of] <s>karma</s>. Or alternatively, this is a distributive usage — it conduces to the cessation of each and every <s>karma</s> — this is the meaning. 'In these four' — and so forth in detail. The inclusion of <s>dharma</s>-patience (<s>dharmakṣānti</s>) and the mention of the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) for dispassion from <s>Kāma</s> [are given] because [these are] the paths of abandonment of dark <s>karma</s> belonging to the Desire Realm. Because only the outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) path is the topic here, the mundane uninterrupted paths, even though they function as paths of abandonment, are not included.

children.translated_text: 'Of the white, in the dispassions from <s>dhyāna</s>' —

body.text: iti. kuśalasyaivety avadhāryate. tatra kṛṣṇābhāvāt. kliṣṭasaṃskāraprahāṇam aṣṭābhiḥ. navamena tu kuśalasyāpi.
body.translated_text: thus. It is restricted to the wholesome alone — because of the absence of the dark therein. The afflicted formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are abandoned through eight [uninterrupted paths]; but through the ninth, even the wholesome too.

body.text: na hi tasya svabhāvaprahāṇam iti. prāpticchedaprahāṇaṃ. prahīṇasyāpi kuśalasya saṃmukhībhāvāt. tadālambanakleśaprahāṇād iti. tadālaṃbanasya kleśasya prahāṇāt tasya kuśalasya prahāṇaṃ bhavati. tadālaṃbanakleśaprahānaṃ ca navamasya tadālaṃbanakleśaprakārasya prahāṇe sati bhavatīti. navamānaṃtaryamārgacetanaiva kṛṣṇaśuklasya [Tib. 60a] karmaṇaḥ kṣayāya bhavati. tadā hi navamasya kleśaprakārasya prāpticchede visaṃyogaprāptir utpadyate. tasya ca kṛṣṇaśuklasya karmaṇo 'nyasyāpi cānivṛtavyākṛtasya sāsravasya dharmasya visaṃyogaprāptir utpadyata iti varṇayaṃti. evaṃ caturdhyānavairāgyeṣv api vaktavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'For there is no abandonment of its own-nature' — the abandonment is through the cutting off of acquisition (<s>prāpticcheda</s>). Because even what has been abandoned as wholesome can become manifest again. 'Through the abandonment of the affliction that has it as object' — through the abandonment of the affliction that has that [wholesome dharma] as its object, the abandonment of that wholesome [dharma] occurs. And the abandonment of the affliction that has it as object occurs when the ninth type of affliction having it as object is abandoned. The volition (<s>cetanā</s>) of the ninth uninterrupted path alone conduces to the cessation of dark-and-white <s>karma</s>. For at that time, when the acquisition of the ninth type of affliction is cut off, the acquisition of separation (<s>visaṃyogaprāpti</s>) arises. And for that dark-and-white <s>karma</s>, as well as for other unobstructed-indeterminate with-outflows <s>dharma</s>s, the acquisition of separation arises — so they explain. Similarly, this should be stated for the dispassions from the four <s>dhyāna</s>s.

body.text: tena tadvedanīyam iti. tena narakagatinaiyamyakāraṇena. tadvedanīyaṃ
body.translated_text: 'By that, to be experienced as that' — by that cause of being fixed in the destiny of the hells. To be experienced as that

body.text: narakavedanīyam arthaḥ. ato 'nyatreti vistaraḥ. tato narakagater anyatra kāmadhātau manuṣyādigatau akuśalasya kuśalasya ca karmaṇo vipākas tena gatinaiyamyakāraṇena. tadanyakāmadhātuvedanīyam ubhayam apy aviśeṣya miśrīkṛtya kṛṣṇaśuklam ity uktaṃ. na punar evaṃ grahītavyaṃ. kuśalam api kṛṣṇaśuklam. evam akuśalam apīti.
body.translated_text: — meaning: to be experienced in the hells. 'But elsewhere' — and so forth in detail. Elsewhere than the hell destiny, in the Desire Realm, in the destinies of humans and the like, the retribution of both unwholesome and wholesome <s>karma</s>, through that cause of fixity in a destiny — to be experienced in the remainder of the Desire Realm — both [wholesome and unwholesome] are combined without distinction and called 'dark-and-white.' But it should not be understood thus: the wholesome too is dark-and-white, and likewise the unwholesome.

body.text: kuśalenāmiśratvād iti. na hi kuśalaṃ darśanaprahātavyam asti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of being unmixed with the wholesome' — for there is no wholesome [dharma] that is to be abandoned by seeing [the truths] (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>).

children.translated_text: 'That which is to be abandoned by seeing is not unafflicted' —

body.text: iti niyamāt. atra codyate. kāmāvacaraṃ
body.translated_text: because of this restriction. Here it is objected: the Desire Realm

body.text: iti viśeṣyaṃ vaktavyam. itarathā hi rūpārūpyāvacarasyāpi darśanaheyasya kṛṣṇavipākatvavacanaprasaṃga iti. na vaktavyam.
body.translated_text: should be stated as the qualified [subject]. For otherwise, there would be the consequence of saying that what is to be abandoned by seeing in the Form and Formless Realms also has dark retribution. [But] it need not be stated [separately] —

body.text: iti. kāmajam ity asyobhayaviśeṣaṇatvāt. kāmajaṃ dṛggheyaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ. kāmajam anyat kṛṣṇaśuklam [Tib. 60b] iti. tad dhīti vistaraḥ. tad dhi kāmāvacaraṃ bhavanāprahātavyaṃ. kuśalaṃ cākuśalaṃ ca saṃbhavati. tan miśrīkṛtyobhayam api kṛṣṇaśuklam ity uktaṃ. na punaḥ pratyekaṃ.
body.translated_text: because of this [statement]. Because 'born from <s>Kāma</s>' qualifies both. What is to be abandoned by seeing and born from <s>Kāma</s> is dark. The other, born from <s>Kāma</s>, is dark-and-white. 'For that' — and so forth in detail. For that belonging to the Desire Realm, to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>), can be both wholesome and unwholesome. Both are combined and called 'dark-and-white.' But not individually.

body.text: (IV.65) trīṇi mauneyānīti. munitā vā munikarma vā mauneyaṃ kāpeyavat.
body.translated_text: (IV.65) 'Three <s>mauneya</s>s' — <s>mauneya</s> is the state of a sage (<s>munitā</s>) or the action of a sage, like <s>kāpeya</s> [from <s>kapi</s>].

body.text: iti. muner idam maunaṃ. aśaikṣa iti vistaraḥ. aśaikṣaṃ kāyakarmāvijñaptisvabhāvaṃ kāyamaunam. evaṃ vāṅmaunaṃ. atha kasmād avijñaptir eva gṛhyate. na punar vijñaptir api. vijñapteḥ sāsravatvenāśaikṣatvāsaṃbhavāt. mana eva manomaunam iti. svārthe vṛddhividhānāt. cittaṃ hi paramārthamunir iti. sarvakleśajalpoparater iti kāraṇaṃ vakṣyate. tat kilakāyavākkarmabhyām aśaikṣābhyām anumīyate aśaikṣām iti. kathaṃ tathāgato 'numātavyaḥ. praśāṃtena kāyakarmaṇā praśāṃtena vākkarmaṇeti sūtre vacanāt. kilaśabdena vaibhāṣikamataṃ dyotayitvācāryaḥ svamataṃ āha. api khalv iti vistaraḥ. cittāvijñaptyabhāvād iti. yasmāc cittasyavijñaptir nāsty ato na manaskarma viratisvabhāvaṃ. viramārthena ca maunam iti. viramo viratiḥ. sarvākuśalaviramārthena [Tib. 61a] maunam ity abhiprāyaḥ. ato mano eva sarvākuśalebhyo virataṃ maunam ity ucyate. sarvakleśajalpoparater iti. vitathālaṃbanajalpanāt kleśā jalpā ity ucyaṃte. te cārhata uparatā ity arhan paramārthamuniḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Belonging to a sage (<s>muni</s>) — this is <s>mauna</s>. 'Non-learner' (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) — and so forth in detail. The non-learner bodily <s>karma</s> having the nature of non-informative action (<s>avijñapti</s>) is bodily sage-silence (<s>kāyamauna</s>). Similarly, vocal sage-silence. But why is only non-informative action grasped and not also informative action? Because informative action, being with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>), cannot be non-learner. 'Mind itself is mental sage-silence' — because of the application of <s>vṛddhi</s> in the reflexive sense. 'For mind is the ultimate sage' — the reason will be stated: 'because of cessation from the prattle of all afflictions.' That [sage-nature] is indeed inferred from the non-learner bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> — that it is non-learner. How is the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be inferred? Because of the statement in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'through peaceful bodily action, through peaceful verbal action.' Having indicated the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> view with the word '<s>kila</s>' (indeed), the <s>Ācārya</s> states his own view: 'moreover, indeed' — and so forth in detail. 'Because of the non-existence of non-informative action of mind' — since mind does not have non-informative action, therefore mental <s>karma</s> does not have the nature of abstention (<s>virati</s>). And sage-silence is in the sense of cessation — cessation is abstention. In the sense of cessation from all unwholesome [dharmas], sage-silence — this is the intent. Therefore, mind itself, having ceased from all unwholesome [dharmas], is called sage-silence. 'Because of cessation from the prattle of all afflictions' — because afflictions are called 'prattle' (<s>jalpa</s>), since they prattle about false objects. And those have ceased for the <s>Arhat</s> — therefore the <s>Arhat</s> is the ultimate sage.

body.text: śucibhāvaḥ śauceyaṃ. śaucam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: the state of being pure — <s>śauceya</s>. The meaning is: purity (<s>śauca</s>).

body.text: grahaṇaṃ sāsravānāsravasucaritaparigrahārthaṃ. tāvatkālam atyaṃtaṃ ceti. tāvatkāladuścaritamalāpakarṣakaṃ sāsraveṇa sucaritatrayeṇa. atyaṃtam anāsraveṇa. tad dhi bhikṣavaḥ prahīṇaṃ yad āryayā prajñayeti sūtrāt. mithyāmaunaśaucādhimuktānāṃ vivecanārtham iti. tūṣṇīṃbhāvamātreṇa śuddhidarśino mithyāmaunādhimuktāḥ. kāyamalāpakarṣaṇamātreṇa śuddhidarśino mithyāśaucādhimuktāḥ. teṣāṃ vivecanaṃ tato darśanāt pracyāvanaṃ. tadartham etānīti
body.translated_text: the inclusion [is given] for the purpose of encompassing both with-outflows and outflow-free good conduct. 'For that much time and ultimately' — through the with-outflows triad of good conduct, [purification occurs] for that much time, removing the stain of misconduct. Through the outflow-free [triad], ultimately — because of the statement in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'That, O monks, is abandoned which is abandoned by noble wisdom.' 'For the purpose of distinguishing those committed to false sage-silence and false purity' — those who see purity in mere silence are committed to false sage-silence. Those who see purity merely in the removal of bodily impurities are committed to false purity. Their distinguishing means turning them away from that view. These [true sage-silence and purity] are for that purpose.

body.text: (IV.66) saṃcetanīyasūtre vacanād iti. saṃcetanīyaṃ karma kṛtvopacitya narakeṣūpapadyate. kathaṃ ca bhikṣavaḥ saṃcetanīyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ bhavaty upacitaṃ. iha bhikṣava ekatyaḥ saṃciṃtya trividhaṃ karma kāyena karma karoty upacinoti caturvidhaṃ vācā trividhaṃ manaseti vistareṇoktvāha [Tib. 61b]. kathaṃ bhikṣavas trividhaṃ manasā saṃcetanīyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ bhavaty upacitaṃ. yathāpīhaikatyo 'bhidhyālur bhavati. vyāpannacittaḥ. yāvan mithyādṛṣṭiḥ. khalu bhikṣava ihaikatyo bhavati viparītadarśīti vistaraḥ. na cānyad abhidhyādivyatiriktaṃ tatra manaskarmoktam ity abhidyādaya eva manaskarmeti dārṣṭāṃtikāḥ sautrāṃtikaviśeṣā ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.66) 'Because of the statement in the <s>Saṃcetanīya Sūtra</s>' — having performed and accumulated intentional (<s>saṃcetanīya</s>) <s>karma</s>, one is reborn in the hells. And how, O monks, is intentional <s>karma</s> performed and accumulated? Here, O monks, a certain one intentionally performs and accumulates threefold <s>karma</s> by body, fourfold by speech, threefold by mind — having stated this in detail, he says: how, O monks, is threefold intentional <s>karma</s> performed and accumulated by mind? Just as here a certain one is covetous (<s>abhidhyālu</s>), of malicious mind, up to: one of wrong view. Indeed, O monks, a certain one here has perverted views — and so forth in detail. And no other mental <s>karma</s> apart from covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) and the rest is stated therein — therefore covetousness and the rest alone are mental <s>karma</s> — [so say] the <s>Dārṣṭāntika</s>s, a sub-type of the <s>Sautrāntika</s>s — this is the meaning.

body.text: evaṃ tu sati karmakleśayor aikyaṃ syād iti. abhidhyāvyāpādamithyādṛṣṭayaḥ kleśāḥ. ta eva karmeti. tad aikyaṃ syāt. naitad asti. kaścit kleśo 'pi karma syād iti. cetanā karma cetayitvā ceti vacanāt. yady evaṃ saṃcetanīyasūtraṃ kathaṃ nīyata ity āha. sūtre tv iti vistaraḥ. sūtre tu cetanāyās tanmukhenābhidhyādimukhena pravṛttes tair abhidhyādibhis tāṃ cetanāṃ darśayati. abhidhyāluḥ khalu bhikṣavo bhavatīti vistareṇa. anyathā cetanāmataṃ bhikṣavaḥ karma vadāmi cetayitvā cety etad virudhyate. karmakleśayoś caikye abhidharmavirodhaḥ syāt. parānugrahopaghābhisaṃdhyabhāva iti vistaraḥ. pareṣām anugrahopaghātayor abhisaṃdhyabhāve kathaṃ samyagdṛṣṭimithyādṛṣṭyor yathākramaṃ [Tib. 62a] kuśalākuśalatvam iti. ato bravīti. tanmūlatvād iti. yasmāt parānugrahābhisaṃdheḥ paropaghātābhisaṃdheś ca samyagdṛṣṭimithyādṛṣṭī mūlaṃ kāraṇam ity arthaḥ. atas tayoḥ kuśalākuśalatvaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'If so, there would be identity of <s>karma</s> and affliction' — covetousness, malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>), and wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) are afflictions. If they themselves are <s>karma</s>, there would be identity [of the two]. This is not the case — [for] some affliction too would be <s>karma</s>. Because of the statement: 'Volition (<s>cetanā</s>) is <s>karma</s>, O monks — having willed, one performs.' 'If so, how is the <s>Saṃcetanīya Sūtra</s> to be interpreted?' — he says: 'But in the <s>sūtra</s>' — and so forth in detail. In the <s>sūtra</s>, because volition operates through their avenue — through the avenue of covetousness and the rest — he shows that volition through covetousness and the rest: 'A certain one is indeed covetous, O monks' — and so forth in detail. Otherwise, [the statement] 'Volition is <s>karma</s>, O monks — having willed' would be contradicted. And if <s>karma</s> and affliction were identical, there would be a contradiction with the <s>Abhidharma</s>. 'Because of the absence of the intention to benefit or harm others' — and so forth in detail. In the absence of the intention to benefit or harm others, how would right view and wrong view respectively be wholesome and unwholesome? Therefore he says: 'because of being the root of that' — because right view and wrong view are the root, the cause, of the intention to benefit others and the intention to harm others, respectively — this is the meaning. Therefore the wholesomeness and unwholesomeness of those two [is established].

body.text: (IV.67) yathāyogam iti yathāsaṃbhavaṃ. katham ity āha. kuśalāḥ sucaritedhyaḥ akuśalā duścaritebhyaś ceti. kliṣṭaś cānyo 'pīti. vadhabaṃdhanādi. tasya nātyaudārikatvād iti. tasya prayogapṛṣṭhabhūtasya klṣṭasyānyasyāpi
body.translated_text: (IV.67) 'As appropriate' means as applicable. How? He says: wholesome [dharmas are obtained] from good conduct, unwholesome from misconduct. 'And also other afflicted [dharmas]' — striking, binding, and the like. 'Because of its not being very gross' — because the other afflicted [dharma] that belongs to the preparatory and subsequent [stages]

body.text: anatyaudārikatvāt. manoduścaritasya ca pradeśaś cetanā. na saṃgṛhīteti vartate. madyādiviratidānejyādika iti. prathamenādiśabdena tāḍanabaṃdhanādiviratir gṛhyate. dvitīyenāpi snapanodvartanaviṣamahastapradānādir gṛhyate. priyavacanādika ity. ādiśabdena dharmadeśanāmārgakathanādir gṛhyate. manaḥsucaritasya cetanā na saṃgṛhīteti vartate.
body.translated_text: is not very gross. And volition (<s>cetanā</s>) is a part of mental misconduct — it is not included [in the action-paths] — this is the continuation. 'Abstention from intoxicants and the rest, giving, worship, and the like' — by the first 'and the rest,' abstention from striking, binding, and the like is grasped. By the second 'and the like,' bathing, anointing, giving the hand of poison, and the like are grasped. 'Kind words and the like' — by the word 'and the like,' teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, indicating the path, and the like are grasped. And volition is a part of mental good conduct — it is not included — this is the continuation.

body.text: iti. ṣaḍ avijñaptir avaśyaṃ. na tv avijñaptir eva ṣaḍ ity avadhāraṇaṃ. maulavijñaptyabhāvād iti. yasmān maulī karmapathasaṃgṛhītā vijñaptir nāsti. ājñāpanavijñaptis tv asti prayogasamgṛhīteti vaibhāṣikasiddhāṃtaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Six are necessarily non-informative action — but the restriction is not that non-informative action is only six. 'Because of the absence of root informative action' (<s>maulavijñapti</s>) — because root informative action included in the action-path does not exist [for those six]. But the informative action of command does exist, being included in the preparatory [stage] — this is the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> doctrine.

body.text: Tib. 62b
body.translated_text: Tib. 62b

body.text: dvidhaika
body.translated_text: 'One is twofold' —

body.text: iti. dvidhaivaika ity avadhāraṇārtha āraṃbhaḥ. tatkālamaraṇa iti. vijñaptikālamaraṇe. kālāṃtaramaraṇe tv avijñaptir eva bhavati.
body.translated_text: thus. The word 'only' (<s>eva</s>) indicates a restriction that one is twofold. 'Death at that time' — when death occurs at the time of the informative action. But when death occurs at another time, it is non-informative action alone.

body.text: iti. dvividhā evety avadhāraṇaṃ. vijñaptyadhīnatvāt samādānaśīlasyeti. śīlaṃ hi dvividhaṃ. samādānaśīlaṃ prātimokṣasaṃvaro dharmatāśīlaṃ ca dhyānānāsravasaṃvarau. samādānaśīlaṃ vijñaptyadhīnaṃ. tad dhi parasmād ādīyate. dharmatāśīlaṃ tu na vijñaptyadhīnaṃ. cittamātradhīnatvāt. ata evāha.
body.translated_text: thus. The restriction is 'twofold only.' 'Because informative action is dependent on the morality of undertaking' — for morality is twofold: morality of undertaking (<s>samādānaśīla</s>), which is the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint; and morality by nature of things (<s>dharmatāśīla</s>), which is the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraints. Morality of undertaking depends on informative action — for it is received from another. But morality by nature of things does not depend on informative action — because it depends on mind alone. For this very reason he says:

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: (IV.69abc)
body.translated_text: (IV.69abc)

body.text: iti. kāmāvacarakarmapathaprayogā avaśyaṃ vijñaptiḥ. na tv avaśyam avijñaptir ity ata evāha.
body.translated_text: thus. The preparatory [actions] of Desire Realm action-paths are necessarily informative action. But not necessarily non-informative action — for this very reason he says:

body.text: paryavasthāneneti. āhrīkyādinā. ghanaraseneti. ghanavegena. tasyānudharmaṃ ceṣṭeteti. tasya karmapathasyānudharmam anu sadṛśaṃ karma. tadyathā mṛte 'pi prāṇini punaḥ prahāradānaṃ koṣaṇaṃ mānsacchedanam ity evamādi. dvau kṣiṇātīti śabdau. parasya carmāpanayanam arthaḥ. pūrvasyārthāṃtaraṃ draṣṭavyaṃ. phalaparipūritaś ceti. prayogasya maulaḥ karmapathaḥ phalaparipūriḥ. yo hy prayujyate maulaṃ karmapathaṃ [Tib. 63a] na janayati. tasya prayogaphalam asti na tu phalaparipūriḥ. evam anyeṣv apīti. yathā tāvad iha kaścit parasvaṃ hartukāmo maṃcād utthiṣṭhati śastraṃ gṛhṇāti. paragṛhaṃ gacchati. supto na vety ākarṇayati. parasvaṃ spṛśati. yāvan
body.translated_text: 'Through mental engulfment' (<s>paryavasthāna</s>) — by shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and the rest. 'With thick relish' — with intense momentum. 'One acts in conformity with it' — one performs action conforming to, similar to, that action-path. Such as: even after a living being has died, [one continues with] further striking, tormenting, flesh-cutting, and the like. 'Two cut off' (<s>kṣiṇāti</s>) — these are two words. The flaying of another's skin is the meaning [of the second]. A different meaning should be seen for the former [usage]. 'And the fruit is fulfilled' — the root action-path is the fruit-fulfillment of the preparatory [stage]. For one who engages in the preparatory [stage] but does not generate the root action-path — that one has the fruit of the preparatory but not the fruit-fulfillment. 'Similarly in the others too' — for example, a certain one wishing to steal another's property rises from his bed, takes a weapon, goes to the other's house, listens [to check] whether [the owner] is sleeping or not, touches the other's property, until

body.text: na sthānāt pracyāvayati. tāvat prayogaḥ. yasmiṃs tu kṣaṇe sthānāt pracyāvayati. tatra yā vijñaptis tatkṣaṇikā cāvijñaptir ayaṃ maulaḥ karmapathaḥ. dvābhyām hi kāraṇābhyām adattādānāvadyena spṛśyate prayogataḥ phalaparipūritaś ca. tataḥ param avijñaptikṣaṇāḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavaṃti. yāvat tatparasvaṃ vibhajate. vikrīṇīte. gopāyati. anukīrtayati vā tāvad asya vijñaptikṣaṇā api pṛṣṭhaṃ bhavaṃtīti. evam anyeṣv api paṃcasu yathāsaṃbhavaṃ yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: does not displace from the position — this far is the preparatory [stage]. But at the moment when it displaces from the position, the informative action (<s>vijñapti</s>) at that moment and the non-informative action (<s>avijñapti</s>) of that moment constitute the root action-path (<s>maulakarmapatha</s>). For through two reasons one is touched by the fault of taking what is not given: through the preparatory [stage] and through the completion of the result. After that, the moments of <s>avijñapti</s> constitute the subsequent [stage]. As long as one divides that stolen property, sells it, conceals it, or announces it, the moments of <s>vijñapti</s> also constitute the subsequent [stage]. Similarly, in the other five [action-paths], it should be applied as appropriate.

body.text: maraṇabhavastha iti. amṛta eva. na caiṣa siddhāṃta iti.
body.translated_text: 'One established in the existence of dying' — [meaning:] one who has not yet died. And this is not the established doctrine.

children.text: samaṃ prāk ca mṛtasyāsti na maulo 'nyāśrayodayād
children.translated_text: 'Simultaneously, and for one who has already died, the root [action-path] does not exist, because of the arising of another basis' —

body.text: iti siddhāṃtāt. tan na vaktavyam iti. vyaparopayatīti. viprakṛtāvasthāyām ayogāt. evaṃ tu vaktavyaṃ syāt. mṛte prāṇini yā vijñaptis tatkṣaṇikā cāvijñaptiḥ. syaṃ maulaḥ karmapatha iti. yac cāpīdam iti vistaraḥ. vaibhāṣikair asya śāstravākyasyaivam artho vyākhyātaḥ. atra śāstre prayogaśabdena pṛṣṭham uktam iti. prayoga iva prayogaḥ. prayogasadṛśī kriyety arthaḥ. asyārthasya virodhaḥ. [Tib. 63b] kasmāt. maulasyaiva tadānīm aniruddhāt. mṛte prāṇini maulakarmapathavyavasthāpanād ity atrābhiprāyaḥ. vaibhāṣika āha. yathā na doṣas tathāstv iti. kathaṃ ca na doṣa ity ācāryaḥ. vaibhāṣikaḥ punar āha. maula evātra prayogaśabdenokta iti. kutra. yo 'yaṃ praśnaḥ syāt prāṇī hataḥ prānātipātaś cāniruddha ity atra. pṛṣṭhaṃ prayogaśabdenoktam iti kim ayaṃ pakṣaḥ parityakta eva. sa ca na parityakta eva. ubhayam api hi saṃbhavati. yadi maraṇabhavānaṃtarakṣaṇavartī prāṇī bhavaty atra prayogaśabdena maula ukta itīṣyate. tataḥ pareṇa tu pṛṣṭha iti. ācārya āha. vijñaptis tarhi tadā kathaṃ maulaḥ karmapatho bhavatīti. mṛte hi prāṇini vijñaptir akiṃcitkarī. na hi tena vijñaptiprahāreṇa mṛtasya māraṇaṃ punar astīti manyāmāno 'yaṃ pṛcchati. kasmād avjñaptiṃ na pṛcchati. yasmād asāv anidarśanatvād apratighatvāc ca prahārākhyā na bhavati. kathaṃ ca na bhavitavyam iti vaibhāṣikeṇokte. svābhiprāyam ācāryo vivṛṇoti. asāmarthyād iti. prāṇini mṛte tasyāḥ sāmarthyaṃ na dṛśyata iti vaibhāṣika āha. avijñaptir idānīṃ kathaṃ bhavaty asati sāmarthye maulaḥ karmapatha iti. yasmād evam avijñaptir asāmarthye 'pi maulaḥ karmapatho bhavati. tasmāt prayogaphalaparipūrikāle maulakarmapathaparisamāptikāle prāṇino mṛtatvāvasthāyāṃ. tad ubhayaṃ vijñaptyavijñaptyākhyaṃ [Tib. 64a] karmapathaḥ syād yujyetety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: this is the established doctrine. Therefore, it should not be stated thus. 'Dispossesses' — because of the inapplicability in the state of being altered. Rather, it should be stated thus: when the living being has died, the <s>vijñapti</s> at that moment and the <s>avijñapti</s> of that moment would be the root action-path. 'And also this' — and so forth in detail. The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> have explained the meaning of this treatise-statement thus: in this treatise, the subsequent [stage] is referred to by the word 'preparatory' — a 'preparatory' that is like the preparatory, meaning: an action resembling the preparatory — this is the meaning. The contradiction of this meaning — why? Because the root [action-path] itself has not yet ceased at that time. The intent here is: because the root action-path is established [as occurring] when the living being dies. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: let it be such that there is no fault. The <s>Ācārya</s> asks: and how is there no fault? The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> again says: the root [action-path] itself is referred to here by the word 'preparatory.' Where? In the question 'suppose a living being has been killed but the act of killing has not yet ceased' — here. 'The subsequent [stage] is referred to by the word "preparatory"' — has this position been abandoned then? It has not been abandoned. For both are possible. If a living being exists in the moment immediately following the existence of dying, here the root is accepted as being referred to by the word 'preparatory.' But after that, the subsequent [stage]. The <s>Ācārya</s> says: how then does <s>vijñapti</s> at that time constitute a root action-path? For when a living being has died, <s>vijñapti</s> accomplishes nothing. For there is no killing of the dead one by that <s>vijñapti</s>-blow — thinking thus, he asks this. Why does he not ask about <s>avijñapti</s>? Because that, being invisible and non-resistant, is not called a 'blow.' And how should it not be [a root action-path]? — when the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says this, the <s>Ācārya</s> discloses his own view: because of incapacity. When a living being has died, its capacity is not seen — says the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>. How then is <s>avijñapti</s> a root action-path when there is no capacity? Since <s>avijñapti</s>, even without capacity, is a root action-path, therefore at the time of the completion of the preparatory result, at the time of the completion of the root action-path, when the living being is in the state of having died — both <s>vijñapti</s> and <s>avijñapti</s> would be action-paths — the meaning is: this would be fitting.

body.text: evam anyeṣv api yathāyogaṃ yojyam iti. yathā parasvaṃ hartukāmaḥ kāryasiddhaye parakīyaṃ hṛtvā tena paśunā baliṃ kuryāt. dāreṣu cāsya vipratipadyeta
body.translated_text: 'Similarly, in the others too, it should be applied as appropriate' — for example, one who wishes to steal another's property, for the accomplishment of the purpose, having stolen another's animal, might perform a sacrifice with that animal. And he might transgress against that one's wives

body.text: tair eva tadapahārārthaṃ. anṛtapiśunaparuṣasāṃtvabhedaiś cāsya mitrabhedaṃ kuryāt. yāny asya paritrāṇāya kalperan. abhidhyāṃ ca tatsve kuryāt. taddravyasvāmini ca vyāpādaṃ mithyādṛṣṭiṃ bṛṃhayet. evaṃ kāmamithyācārādiṣu yathāsaṃbhavaṃ yojyaṃ. eṣā dik.
body.translated_text: — by those very [means], for the purpose of stealing that [property]. And through false, divisive, harsh, or conciliatory speech, he might cause the breaking of that one's friendships — those that would serve for protecting [his property]. He might have covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) toward that one's property. And toward the owner of that property, he might have malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>), and he might foster wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>). Similarly, in sexual misconduct and the rest, it should be applied as appropriate. This is the direction [of explanation].

body.text: (IV.69d, 70ab) nātra sarveṣāṃ karmapathānām lobhādibhir niṣṭeti. na ca sarveṣāṃ lobhena. kiṃ tarhi. keṣāṃcid eva kāmamithyācārādīnāṃ. nāpi sarveṣāṃ vyāpādena. kiṃ tarhi. keṣāṃcid eva prāṇātipātādīnāṃ. evaṃ na sarveṣāṃ mohena. kiṃ tarhi. keṣāṃcid eva mithyādṛṣṭyādīnām eveti. tryaṃbukāḥ varatāḥ. ādiśabdena vyāghrādayaḥ. yaś ca mithyādṛṣṭipravartita iti. nāsti paraloka iti kṛtvā nirapekṣo haṃti. ayam api mohajaḥ. anyalābhasatkārayaśo'rtham iti. anyalābhasyārthe parasvaṃ harati. yathāśvahārikaḥ. satkārasya yaśavo vārthaṃ harati. idam api lobhajam adattādānaṃ. [Tib. 64b] yac ca mithyādṛṣṭipravartitaṃ. tad api mohajam adattādānaṃ. tatra mohaprādhānyāt. upaiti mātaram abrahmacaryārthe. upasvasāram upaitīti vartate. upasvasāraṃ bhaginīm ity arthaḥ. upasagotrām upaiti. samānagotrām ity arthaḥ. upahāyajamānaḥ. ye cāhur iti vistaraḥ. udūkhalāditulyo mātṛgrāmaḥ. yathodūkhalādayaḥ sādhāraṇā upabhogyāḥ. evaṃ strījanaḥ. tasmān na doṣo 'sty abhigacchatām iti. mṛṣāvādādayo lobhajāḥ dveṣajāś ca pūrvavad iti. mṛṣāvādapaiśunyapāruṣyasaṃbhinnapralāpāḥ lobhajāḥ anyalābhasatkārayaśo'rthaṃ vā. ātmasuhṛtparitrāṇārthaṃ vā. dveṣajāḥ vairaniryātanārthaṃ.
body.translated_text: (IV.69d, 70ab) Here, not all action-paths are completed by greed and the rest — and not all are [completed] by greed. Rather, only certain ones — sexual misconduct and the rest. Nor are all [completed] by malice. Rather, only certain ones — killing and the rest. Similarly, not all by delusion. Rather, only certain ones — wrong view and the rest. '<s>Tryaṃbuka</s>s' are snakes. By the word 'and the like,' tigers and the rest [are included]. 'And one who is driven by wrong view' — thinking 'there is no other world,' one kills without concern. This too is born of delusion. 'For the purpose of obtaining another's gain, honor, or fame' — for the purpose of another's gain, one steals another's property. Like a horse-thief. For the purpose of honor or fame, one steals. This too is taking what is not given born of greed. And that which is driven by wrong view — that too is taking what is not given born of delusion, because of the predominance of delusion therein. 'One approaches one's mother for the purpose of unchastity. One approaches one's own sister' — this is to be construed. 'One's own sister' means one's sister. 'One approaches one of the same clan' (<s>upagotra</s>) — meaning one of the same lineage. 'One who follows [the view of] the sacrificer.' And those who say — and so forth in detail: 'Womankind is like a mortar and the rest — just as mortars and the rest are common [objects] to be used, so is womankind. Therefore there is no fault for those who approach them.' False speech and the rest born of greed and hatred are as before — false speech, slander, harsh speech, and idle talk are born of greed: for the purpose of obtaining another's gain, honor, or fame, or for the purpose of protecting oneself and one's friends. Born of hatred: for the purpose of wreaking vengeance.

body.text: na parihāsayuktaṃ. mithyādṛṣṭipravartita iti. nāsti paraloka iti nirmaryādaya yo mṛṣāvādo 'yaṃ mohajaḥ. paiśunyādayas tu. paiśunyapāruṣyābaddhapralāpāḥ mṛṣāvādavan modhajāḥ. yaś ceti vistaraḥ. yaś ca vedasāṃkhyavaiśeṣikādyasatpralāpaḥ. sa cāpi mohajaḥ saṃbhinnapralāpaḥ.
body.translated_text: not [if] connected with jest. 'Driven by wrong view' — making those who are without limits [in morality think] 'there is no other world' — such false speech is born of delusion. And slander and the rest — slander, harsh speech, and meaningless talk — are born of delusion like false speech. 'And that which' — and so forth in detail. That idle talk which consists of the false doctrines of <s>Veda</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>, and the rest — that too is idle talk born of delusion.

body.text: (IV.70cd) tasya ceti. kuśalacittasya. nānāvāsaṃ praviśatīti. [Tib. 65a] maṇḍalaṃ praviśatīty arthaḥ. nānāvāsā hi tasmin mahāsīmāmaṇḍale bhavaṃti. tṛtīye karmavācana iti. jñapticaturthena karmaṇā śrāmaṇera upasaṃpādyate. tatra jñaptyā idaṃnāmānam upasaṃpādayet saṃgha iti. liṅṅartha ucyate. karmavācanena laḍartha ucyate. imaṃ saṃgha upasaṃpādayatīti. tatra karmavācanaṃ trir ucyate. tṛtīyasya karmavācanasyāparisamāpteḥ prayogaḥ karmapathasyāvagaṃtavyaḥ. tasyāvasāne tu yā vijñaptis tatkṣaṇikā vāvijñaptir
body.translated_text: (IV.70cd) 'Of that' — of the wholesome mind. 'Enters the various dwelling' — meaning: enters the <s>maṇḍala</s> (assembly). For there are various dwellings in that great boundary-<s>maṇḍala</s>. 'At the third act of the motion' (<s>karmavācana</s>) — a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> is ordained through a motion with three acts (<s>jñapticaturthakarman</s>). Therein, by the motion (<s>jñapti</s>) it is expressed: 'May the <s>Saṃgha</s> ordain this one named so-and-so' — the optative mood is used. By the act of the motion, the indicative mood is used: 'The <s>Saṃgha</s> is ordaining this one.' Therein, the act of the motion is recited three times. Before the completion of the third act of the motion, the preparatory [stage] of the action-path should be understood. At its conclusion, the <s>vijñapti</s> at that moment, or the <s>avijñapti</s> of that moment

body.text: ayaṃ maulaḥ karmapathaḥ. tata ūrdhvaṃ yāvan niśrayā ārocyaṃta iti. catvāro niśrayāś cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayyāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyalakṣaṇā yathoktena vidhinā tasyopasaṃpāditasyārocyaṃte. tadadhiṣṭhānaṃ ca vijñapayati. niśrayādhiṣṭhānaṃ ca vijñaptiṃ karotīty arthaḥ. avijñaptiś ca yāvad anuvartate. yāvat saṃvaro na tyajyata ity arthaḥ. idaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ.
body.translated_text: — this is the root action-path. From that point onward, until the supports (<s>niśraya</s>) are announced — the four supports, characterized by robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicine for the sick, are announced to that ordained one according to the prescribed procedure. And [the preceptor] makes known its undertaking — makes the informative expression of the undertaking of the supports — this is the meaning. And the <s>avijñapti</s> continues as long as the restraint is not abandoned — this is the meaning. This is the subsequent [stage].

body.text: (IV.71, 72ab) vadhavyāpādapāruṣyaniṣṭhā dveṣeṇeti.
body.translated_text: (IV.71, 72ab) 'Killing, malice, and harsh speech are completed by hatred' —

body.text: dveṣeṇaivety avadhāraṇaṃ. parityāgaparuṣacittasaṃmukhībhāvād iti. parityāgacittasaṃmukhībhāvāt prāṇātipātasya niṣṭhā dveṣeṇa. paruṣacittasaṃmukhībhāvāt tu vyāpādapāruṣyayoḥ.
body.translated_text: the emphasis is: 'by hatred alone.' Because of the coming face-to-face with the mind of abandonment and harshness — because of the coming face-to-face with the mind of abandonment, killing is completed by hatred. Because of the coming face-to-face with the harsh mind, malice and harsh speech [are completed by hatred].

body.text: Tib. 65b
body.translated_text: (72cd) 'Stated in four sections' (<s>kāṇḍa</s>) — stated in four divisions. How?

body.text: (72cd) caturbhiḥ kāṇḍair uktā iti. caturbhir bhāgair uktāḥ. kathaṃ.

children.translated_text: 'Killing, malice, and harsh speech are completed by hatred' —

body.text: ekaḥ kāṇḍaḥ.
body.translated_text: this is the first section.

children.translated_text: 'From greed: approaching another's wife, covetousness, and the completion of taking what is not given' —

body.text: iti dvitīyaḥ.
body.translated_text: this is the second.

body.text: tṛtīyah.
body.translated_text: this is the third.

children.translated_text: 'For the rest, [completion] through three is accepted' —

body.text:
iti caturthaḥ kāṇḍaḥ. bhogādhiṣṭhānā iti. viṣayādhiṣṭhānāḥ. nāmarūpādhiṣṭhāneti. paṃcaskandhādhiṣṭhānety arthaḥ. nāma hi vedanādayaḥ skaṃdhāḥ rūpaṃ rūpaskaṃdhaḥ. adhiṣṭhānam adhikaraṇaṃ viṣaya ity anarthāṃtaraṃ. nāmakāyādhiṣṭhānā mṛṣāvādādayo vāgnāmni pravartata iti kṛtvā.
(IV.73ab)
body.translated_text:
this is the fourth section. 'Based on enjoyment' — meaning: based on sense-objects. 'Based on name-and-form' — meaning: based on the five aggregates. For 'name' is the aggregates of feeling and the rest; 'form' is the form aggregate. 'Basis' (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), 'ground' (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), and 'object' (<s>viṣaya</s>) are synonymous. 'False speech and the rest are based on the name-body' — because speech operates in the domain of names.
(IV.73ab)

body.text: iti pratiṣedhāt pṛṣṭham api na bhavatīti gamyate. maulapūrvatvāt pṛṣṭhasya. na ca prāṇātipātāvadyena spṛśyata iti. na maulenety abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: from this negation, it is understood that the subsequent [stage] also does not exist. Because the subsequent [stage] is preceded by the root [action-path]. And one is not touched by the fault of killing — the intent is: not by the root [action-path].

children.translated_text: 'Because of the arising of another basis' —

body.text: iti. visabhāgāśrayodayād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: meaning: because of the arising of a dissimilar basis.

body.text: (IV.73cd) arthato hi te 'nyonyaṃ prayoktāra iti. na vācā te 'nyonyaṃ prayoktāraḥ. kiṃ tarhi. prāṇātipātakaraṇābhyupagamād [Tib. 66a] arthata iti ekakāryatvāt.
body.translated_text: (IV.73cd) 'For in meaning they are each other's instigators' — they are not each other's instigators by speech. Rather, through the agreement to perform killing, in meaning — because of having one purpose.

body.text: (IV.74ab) saṃjñāya paricchidyety arthaḥ. nānyaṃ bhramitveti. na bhrāṃtyānyaṃ mārayatīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.74ab) 'By the cognition being delimited' — this is the meaning. 'Not having erred and [killing] another' — meaning: one does not kill another through error.

body.text: kṣaṇikeṣu skaṃdheṣv iti. svarasenaiva vinaśvarāṇāṃ skaṃdhānāṃ katham
body.translated_text: 'In momentary aggregates' — the intent is: how can the cessation of aggregates that are by their very nature perishable

body.text: anyenaiṣāṃ nirodhaḥ kriyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. prāṇo nāma vāyuḥ. kāyacittasaṃniśrito vartata iti. kathaṃ cittasaṃniśrito vāyuḥ pravartate. cittapratibaddhavṛttitvāt. tathā hi nirodhāsaṃjñisamāpattisamāpannasya mṛtasya ca na pravartate. śāstre 'py uktaṃ. ya ime āśvāsapraśvāsāḥ. kiṃ te kāyasaṃniśritā vartaṃta iti vaktavyaṃ. cittasaṃniśritā vartaṃta iti vaktavyaṃ. naiva kāyacittasaṃniśritā vartaṃta iti vaktavyaṃ. kāyacittasaṃniśritā vartanta iti vaktavyam. āha. kāyacittasaṃniśritā vartaṃta iti vaktavyam iti vistaraḥ. tam api pātayatīti. taṃ prāṇaṃ vināśayatīty arthaḥ. utpannasya svarasanirodhād anāgatasyotpattiṃ pratibadhnan nirodhayatīty ucyate. yathā pradīpaṃ nirodhayati. ghaṇṭāsvanaṃ vā. kṣaṇikam api saṃtaṃ. kathaṃ ca sa nirodhayati. anāgatasyotpattipratibaṃdhāt. jīvitendriyaṃ vā prāṇa iti. cittaviprayuktasvabhāvam enaṃ darśayati.
body.translated_text: be brought about by another? <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath/life) is wind (<s>vāyu</s>). It operates dependent on body and mind — how does wind dependent on mind operate? Because its functioning is bound to the mind. For thus, for one who has attained the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) or the non-perception attainment (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>), and for a dead one, it does not operate. In the treatise too it is stated: 'These inhalations and exhalations — is it to be said that they operate dependent on the body? Is it to be said that they operate dependent on the mind? It is not to be said that they operate dependent only on the body and mind [separately]. It is to be said that they operate dependent on body and mind.' He says: 'It is to be said that they operate dependent on body and mind' — and so forth in detail. 'Brings down that too' — meaning: destroys that <s>prāṇa</s> (breath). Since the future [moment's breath], because of the natural cessation of the arisen, [would have ceased anyway,] by obstructing the arising of the future [moment], one is said to 'cease' [the breath] — just as one 'ceases' a lamp, or the sound of a bell, even though they are momentary. And how does one cease [them]? By obstructing the arising of the future [moment]. Or alternatively, '<s>prāṇa</s>' is the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>) — he shows this as having the nature of what is dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayukta</s>).

body.text: kasya taj jīvitaṃ. yas tadabhāvān mṛta iti. yaḥ prāṇī jīvitasyābhāvān mṛto bhavati. sa bauddhānāṃ nāsti nairātmyavāditvāt. [Tib. 66b] ata evaṃ pṛcchati. kasyeti ṣaṣṭhīṃ. pudgalavāde pudgalapratiṣedhaprakaraṇe. asaty ātmani kasyeyaṃ smṛtiḥ. kim athaiṣā ṣaṣṭhīty atra pradeśe ciṃtayiṣyāmi. āstāṃ tāvad etat sāmānyāsikam ity abhiprāyaḥ. tasmāt sendriyaḥ kāyo jīvatīti. sendriyasyaiva kāyasya taj jīvitaṃ. nātmana iti darśayati. sa eva cānindriyo mṛta iti.
body.translated_text: Whose is that life? [It belongs to] the one who, in its absence, is dead. That living being who, in the absence of life, becomes dead — that one does not exist for Buddhists, because they hold the doctrine of non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>). For this very reason he asks: 'whose?' — using the genitive. In the exposition of the person (<s>pudgalavāda</s>), in the section on the refutation of the person: 'In the absence of a self, whose is this mindfulness?' — 'Is this then the [meaning of] the genitive?' — at that point I shall consider [this]. Let this general topic be set aside for now — this is the intent. Therefore, the body endowed with faculties lives — the life [belongs] to the body endowed with faculties alone, not to a self — he shows. And that very [body], devoid of faculties, is dead.

body.text: abuddhipūrvād iti vistaraḥ. asaṃcintyakṛtād api prāṇipātāt kartur adharmo yathāgnisaṃsparśād abuddhipūrvād asaṃciṃtyakṛtād dāha iti. nirgraṃthā nagnāṭakāḥ. teṣāṃ nirgraṃthānām evaṃ vādināṃ abuddhipūrve 'pi parastrīdarśanasaṃsparśana eṣa prasaṃgaḥ. pāpaprasaṃga ity arthaḥ. agnidṛṣṭāṃtāt. nirgraṃthaśiroluṃcane ca nirgraṃthaśiraḥkeśotpāṭane ca. duḥkhotpādanabuddhyabhāve 'py adharmaprasaṃgaḥ. agnidāhavat. kaṣṭatapodeśane ca. nirgraṃthaśāstur adharmaprasaṃgo buddhyanapekṣāyāṃ. parasya duḥkhotpādanam adharmāya bhavatīti kṛtvā. tadviṣūcikāmaraṇe ca. nirgraṃthānāṃ viṣūcikayā ajīrṇena maraṇe. dātur annadātur adharmaprasaṃgaḥ. annadānena maraṇakāraṇāt. abuddhipūrvo 'pi hi prāṇivadhaḥ kāraṇam adharmasyeti. mātṛgarbhasthayoś ca. mātur garbhasthasya cānyonyaduḥkhanimittatvād adharmapraṣaṃgaḥ. tata evāgnidṛṣṭāṃtāt. vadhyasyāpi ca tatkriyāsaṃbaṃdhāt. prāṇātipātakriyāsaṃbaṃdhāt [Tib. 67a]. adharmaprasaṃgaḥ. vadhye hi sati prāṇātipātakriyā vadhakasya bhavati. agnisvāśrayadāhavat. agnir hi na kevalam anyajanaṃ dahati. kiṃ tarhi. svāśrayam api indhanaṃ dahatīti. tadvat. na hi teṣāṃ cetanāviśeṣo 'pekṣyate. kārayataś ca pareṇa vadhādi
body.translated_text: "Without prior cognition" — and so forth in detail. Even from the killing of a living being done without deliberation, unintentionally, there is demerit (<s>adharma</s>) for the doer — just as from contact with fire, burning occurs without prior cognition and without deliberation. The <s>Nirgrantha</s>s are naked ascetics. For those <s>Nirgrantha</s>s who hold this view, even in the seeing and touching of another's wife without prior cognition, this consequence follows — the consequence of sin, that is. From the fire analogy. And in the plucking of a <s>Nirgrantha</s>'s head-hair — in the pulling out of the hair from a <s>Nirgrantha</s>'s head — even without the cognition of producing suffering, there would be the consequence of demerit, like fire-burning. And in the teaching of harsh austerities — there would be the consequence of demerit for the <s>Nirgrantha</s> teacher, if cognition is not taken into account, because producing suffering in another constitutes demerit. And in their death from cholera — when <s>Nirgrantha</s>s die from cholera, from indigestion, there would be the consequence of demerit for the giver, the food-giver, because the giving of food is the cause of death, since even killing of a living being without prior cognition is a cause of demerit. And for a mother and the one in her womb — because the mother and the one in the womb are mutual causes of suffering for each other, there would be the consequence of demerit, from that very fire analogy. And even for the one being killed, because of the connection with the act of killing — because of the connection with the act of taking life, there would be the consequence of demerit. For when a victim exists, the act of taking life belongs to the killer — like fire burning its own support. For fire does not burn only another person; rather, it burns its own support, fuel, as well. Likewise. For no special volition is required by them. And for one who has another perform killing and the like

body.text: adharmasyāprasaṃgaḥ. pareṇāgniṃ saparśayataḥ sparśayitus tenādāhavat. āgneyadharmābhyupagamāt. acetanānāṃ ca kāṣṭhādīnāṃ kāṣṭhaloṣṭavaṃśādīnāṃ. gṛhapāte tatrāṃtaḥsthitānāṃ prāṇināṃ vadhāt. pāpaprasaṃgaḥ. na hi buddhiviśeṣaḥ pramāṇīkriyate. na vā dṛṣṭāṃtamātrād ahetukāt. siddhir asyārthasyeti.
body.translated_text: there would be no consequence of demerit — like when another makes fire touch [something], there is no burning for the one who makes it touch, because of accepting the inherent nature of fire [as the cause]. And for inanimate things such as wood and the like — wood, clods, bamboo, and the like — upon the collapse of a house, because of the killing of living beings situated within, there would be the consequence of sin. For no special cognition is made authoritative. Nor is establishment of this matter [achieved] merely from an analogy without a [valid] reason.

body.text: (IV.74cd) anyatra saṃjñāvibhramād iti. yadi devadattadravyaṃ harāmīty abhiprāyamāṇo yajñadattadravyaṃ harati. nādattādānam ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.74cd) "Except through confusion of perception" — if, intending "I will take <s>Devadatta</s>'s property," one takes <s>Yajñadatta</s>'s property, it is not taking what is not given — this is the intent.

body.text: parinirvāṇakāle parigṛhītam iti. dātṛjanapuṇyānugrahārthaṃ. aparigrahe hi stūpe dānam aphalaṃ syāt. pratigrāhakābhāvāt. parivartakaṃ mṛtasya bhikṣoś cīvarādidravyaṃ. kṛte karmaṇi jñaptikarmaṇi.
body.translated_text: "Appropriated at the time of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>" — for the purpose of favoring the merit of donors. For if a <s>stūpa</s> were unowned, a gift [to it] would be fruitless, because of the absence of a recipient. <s>Parivartaka</s> — the robe and other property of a deceased <s>bhikṣu</s>. "When the formal act has been performed" — when the <s>jñaptikarma</s> (motion-act) has been performed.

body.text: (IV.75ab) garbhiṇīgamane garbhoparodhaḥ. pāyayaṃtī stanyopabhogāvasthāputrikā strī. abrahmacaryakaraṇe hi tasyāḥ stanyaṃ kṣīyate. bālakasya vā puṣṭaye tat stanyaṃ na bhavatīti.
body.translated_text: (IV.75ab) In approaching a pregnant woman, there is obstruction of the fetus. A nursing woman (<s>pāyayantī</s>) — a woman with a child at the stage of breast-feeding. For in committing unchastity with her, her milk diminishes, or that milk does not serve for the nourishment of the child.

body.text: Tib. 67b
body.translated_text: "Like the taking of life" — just as when one intends to kill <s>Devadatta</s> but kills <s>Yajñadatta</s>, it is not taking of life — likewise here: the application is intended for one object but another object is enjoyed — therefore it would not be sexual misconduct, according to others.

body.text: prāṇātipātavad iti. yathā devadattaṃ mārayāmīty abhiprāyeṇa yajñadattaṃ mārayato na prāṇātipāto bhavati. tadvad. ihānyasmiṃ vastuni prayogo 'bhipreto 'nyac ca vastu paribhuktam iti. na syāt kāmamithyācāra ity apare.
aṃtato rājña iti. yady anyaḥ kaścid rakṣitā nāsti. aṃtataḥ sarvapaścād rājño 'ṃtikāt sa kāmamithyācāraḥ. tasya hi tan na marṣaṇīyam iti.
body.translated_text: "At the very least, of the king" — if there is no other protector. At the very least, after all others, from the king's [authority], that constitutes sexual misconduct. For that is not tolerable to him.

body.text: (IV.75cd) āhosvid abhijñātuṃ samartha iti. yo 'pi hy artham abhijñātuṃ samarthaḥ. so 'py arthābhijña iti śakyate vaktum. artham abhijānīta iti viprakṛtāvasthāyām abhipretatvāt. manovijñānaviṣayatvād vākyārthasyeti. nāsty atra devadatto 'sti vety ucyamāne śabdaḥ śrotrā vijñāyate. tadanaṃtaraṃ tu cakṣurādisamūho devadatto vākyārtho vikalpena manovijñānena vijñāyate. tenāvijñaptir eva maulaḥ karmapathaḥ syāt. vāgvijñapteḥ śrotravijñānena saha nirodhāt. iṣyate ca vijñaptyavijñaptisvabhāvo maulaḥ karmapatha iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.75cd) "Or one who is capable of understanding the meaning" — for even one who is capable of understanding the meaning can be called "one who understands the meaning" (<s>arthābhijña</s>). Because the intent is the state of being in a normal condition when he understands the meaning.
