"Because the meaning of a sentence is the object of mental consciousness" — when it is said "here <s>Devadatta</s> exists or does not exist," the sound is cognized by the ear. But immediately after, the collection of eye-faculty and the rest — <s>Devadatta</s>, the meaning of the sentence — is cognized through conceptualization by mental consciousness. Therefore, only non-informative action (<s>avijñapti</s>) would be the fundamental action-path, because vocal informative action ceases together with auditory consciousness. But it is accepted that the fundamental action-path has the nature of both informative and non-informative action.

body.text: (IV.76) mṛtakalpāni. ata eteṣu matākhyeti. nairuktaṃ vidhim ālaṃbhya vaibhāṣikā vyācakṣate. svendriyaiḥ prāptā matā ity ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ. vistareṇa yāvan manasā dharmā iti. ye tvayā ghrāṇena gandhā na ghrātāḥ. jihvayā rasā nāsvāditāḥ. kāyena spraṣṭavyāni [Tib. 68b] na spṛṣṭāni. yāvad ye tvayā manasā dharmā na vijñātā iti. triṣu viṣayeṣu rūpaśabdadharmeṣu dṛṣṭaśrutavijñātāpadeśād yathākramaṃ. gandhādiṣu gaṃdharasaspraṣṭavyeṣu matākhyā gamyate. te mataśabdenocyaṃte. evaṃ cāniṣyamāṇe gaṃdhādiṣu matākhyety aniṣyamāṇe. dṛṣṭādibhāvabāhyatvāt. gandhādīnām arūpalakṣaṇatvena
body.translated_text: (IV.76) "Dead-like" (<s>mṛtakalpa</s>). Therefore "in those, called <s>mata</s>" — the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s explain through the etymological method. <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> [says]: <s>mata</s> means apprehended by one's own sense-faculties. In detail, up to "by mind, <s>dharma</s>s." "Those smells which you have not smelled with your nose, those tastes which you have not tasted with your tongue, those tangibles which you have not touched with your body, up to those <s>dharma</s>s which you have not cognized with your mind." In the three objects — form, sound, and <s>dharma</s>s — the designations "seen," "heard," and "cognized" are applied respectively. In smell and the rest — smell, taste, and tangible — the designation <s>mata</s> is understood. They are expressed by the word <s>mata</s>. And if <s>mata</s> is not accepted for smell and the like — because of being outside the scope of "seen" and the rest — because smell and the like, having the character of non-form

body.text: dṛṣṭabhāvabāhyatvād aśabdadharmāyatanalakṣaṇatvena ca śrutavijñātabhāvabāhyatvāt. gaṃdhādiṣu vyavahāro na syāt. dṛṣṭa iti vā yāvad vijñāta iti vety eṣā yuktiḥ. teṣu matākhyeti. ācārya āha. sūtraṃ tāvad iti vistaraḥ. anyārthatvād iti. yasmāt sūtrasyānya evārthaḥ. sūtrārthaṃ bravīti. atra ca te tava ṣaḍvidhe viṣaye rūpādau. caturṣu dṛṣṭādivyavahāreṣu. dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātavyavahāreṣu. dṛṣṭādivyavahāramātraṃ bhaviṣyatīti. rūpe dṛṣṭam iti vyavahāro bhaviṣyati. yāvad vijñātam iti. evaṃ śabdāḍiṣu. atra ca te mālakīmātar dṛṣṭe viṣayaṣaṭke dṛṣṭamātraṃ bhaviṣyati. śrute viṣayaṣaṭke. mate vijñāte viṣayaṣaṭke eva vijñātamātram ity evaṃ tat sūtrapadaṃ vyākhyāyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. na hi priyāpriyanimittādhyāropas tava bhaviṣyatīti sūtrārthaḥ. [Tib. 68b] nanu ca yāni tvayā cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi na dṛṣṭānīty evoktāni. na tu na śrutāni yāvan na vijñātānīty evoktāni. evaṃ śabdā na śrutā ity evoktāḥ. na tu na dṛṣṭā yāvan na vijñātā ity uktāḥ. evaṃ yāvad dharmā na vijñātā ity evoktāḥ. na tu na dṛṣṭā yāvan na spṛṣṭā iti. naiṣa doṣaḥ. udāharaṇarūpam etad uktaṃ bhagavatā. yathā hi rūpāṇi na dṛṣṭānīty uktāni. tathā na śrutāni. yāvan na vijñātānīti vaktavyāni. evaṃ śabdādiṣu vaktavyaṃ. tenaiva lakṣaṇam ucyate. yat paṃcabhir indriyair iti vistaraḥ. yat paṃcabhir indriyaiḥ pratyakṣaṃ rūpādi tad dṛṣṭaṃ. yat parata āgamitaṃ viṣayaṣaṭkaṃ tac chrutaṃ. yad yuktyanumānato rucitam abhipretaṃ tan mataṃ yuktyanumānam iti. avyabhicāryanumānaṃ. tac ca ṣaḍviṣayagocaraṃ. ṣaṣṭho 'nyatra dṛṣṭād iti. ṣaṣṭho viṣayo dharmāḥ. sa dṛṣṭavyavahāraṃ varjayitvā tribhiḥ śrutādibhir vyavahārair vyavahriyate. ato nāsti gandhādiṣu vyavahārābhāvaprasaṃgaḥ. tasmād yuktir apy eṣā na yuktir bhavati. yā vaibhāṣikair [Tib. 69a] uktāḥ evaṃ cāniṣyamāṇa ity evamādikā. yasmād anyathāpi gaṃdhādiṣu vyavahāro bhavatīti.
body.translated_text: are outside the scope of "seen," and because they have the character of non-sound and non-<s>dharma</s>-<s>āyatana</s>, they are outside the scope of "heard" and "cognized" — there would be no usage for smell and the like, whether as "seen" or up to "cognized" — this is the reasoning. "In those, [the designation] <s>mata</s>" — the <s>Ācārya</s> says: "First, the <s>sūtra</s>" — and so forth in detail. "Because it has a different meaning" — because the <s>sūtra</s> has a different meaning altogether. He states the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>: "And here, for you, in the sixfold object beginning with form — in the four usages beginning with 'seen' — the usages of seen, heard, <s>mata</s>, and cognized — there will be merely the usage." In form, there will be the usage "seen"; up to "cognized" — similarly for sounds and the rest. "And here, for you, O daughter of <s>Mālakī</s>, in the sixfold object that is seen — there will be merely the seen; in the sixfold object that is heard — in the sixfold object that is <s>mata</s>; in the sixfold object that is cognized — there will be merely the cognized" — thus that <s>sūtra</s> passage is explained, is the intent. "There will be no superimposition of signs of pleasant and unpleasant upon you" — this is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. But is it not the case that "forms not seen by you with the eye" is indeed what was said, not "not heard" up to "not cognized"? Similarly, sounds were said to be "not heard," not "not seen" up to "not cognized." Similarly, up to <s>dharma</s>s were said to be "not cognized," not "not seen" up to "not touched." This is no fault. This was stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as illustrative. Just as forms were said to be "not seen," similarly "not heard" up to "not cognized" should be stated. Similarly for sounds and the rest. Therefore, the characteristic is stated: "whatever by the five sense-faculties" — and so forth in detail. Whatever is directly perceived by the five sense-faculties — form and the rest — is "seen." Whatever is learned from another regarding the sixfold object is "heard." Whatever is approved through reasoned inference is <s>mata</s> — reasoned inference means non-deviating inference, and that pertains to the sixfold object. "The sixth, other than seen" — the sixth object, <s>dharma</s>s, excluding the usage "seen," is expressed through the three usages of "heard" and the rest. Therefore, there is no consequence of the absence of usage for smell and the like. Therefore, this reasoning is not valid — which was stated by the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s: "And if not accepted" — and so on — because usage for smell and the like is possible in other ways.

body.text: yat pratyakṣīkṛtaṃ cakṣuṣeti. na paṃcabhir indriyaiḥ. yac chrotreṇa śrutaṃ parataś cāgamitam iti ubhayam apy abhīṣṭaṃ. pratyātmaṃ pratisaṃveditaṃ sukhādy asamāhitena cittena. adhigataṃ tu samāhitena. laukikenaiva. na lokottareṇa. laukikaṃ vyavahārādhikārāt. tad evaṃ yogācāranayenāpi ṣaḍ apy ete viṣayāḥ pratyekaṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ dṛṣṭā iti vā vyavahriyaṃte. śrutāḥ. matāḥ. vijñātā ity evety ato nāsti gaṃdhādiṣu vyavahārābhāvaprasaṃga iti.
body.translated_text: "What has been made directly perceptible by the eye" — not by the five sense-faculties. "What has been heard by the ear, and what has been learned from another" — both are accepted. "What has been experienced personally" — happiness and the like — by a non-concentrated mind. "But what has been realized" — by a concentrated mind, and only a mundane one, not a supramundane one — mundane, because [the discussion is] in the context of conventional usage. Thus, even by the <s>Yogācāra</s> method, these six objects are each expressed, according to possibility, as "seen," "heard," "<s>mata</s>," or "cognized" — therefore, there is no consequence of absence of usage for smell and the like.

body.text: yaḥ kāyenānyatheti. kāyasaṃjñayā yo 'rthaṃ gamayati. tasyāpi mṛṣāvādaḥ. parākrameta vyāyaccheta. vācā parākrameteti. vācā paraṃ mārayed ity arthaḥ. iha tu prāṇātipātasya kāyikatvāt kāyiky evāvijñaptir maulasaṃgṛhītā. na vācikī. nāpy atra kāyikī vijñaptiḥ syāt. kāyena parākrameteti. atra mṛṣāvādasya vācikatvād vāciky evāvijñaptir maulasaṃgṛhītety avagaṃtavyaṃ. ubhayāvadyena veti. [Tib. 69b] kāyavāgavadyena. ṛṣīṇāṃ manaḥpradoṣeṇa kāyāvadyena yogo bhavati. poṣadhanidarśanaṃ cātreti. vāgavadyena yogo bhavati. bhikṣupoṣadhe hi kacci 'ttha pariśuddhā iti vinayadhareṇānuśrāvite. yadi kaścit bhikṣuḥ satīm āpattiṃ nāviṣkuryāt. tūṣṇīṃbhāvenaivādhivāsayet sa mṛṣāvādī bhaved iti. kathaṃ tayoḥ karmapathaḥ sidhyatīti. kathaṃ tayo ṛṣibhikṣvoḥ kāyavāgbhyām aparākramamāṇayoḥ prāṇātipāto mṛṣāvādaś ca yathākramaṃ karmapathaḥ sidhyatīti. kartavyo 'tra yatnaḥ. vaibhāṣikaiḥ kartavyaḥ samādhir ity arthaḥ. atrācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ samādhim āha. ṛṣayo 'rthata ājñāpayitāro bhavaṃti. teṣāṃ hi sattvaparityāgapravṛttaṃ pāpāśayam avetyāmanuṣyās tadabhiprasannāḥ kāyena parākramaṃte. yena teṣāṃ ṛṣīṇāṃ karmaptha utpadyate. kathaṃ. paravijñaptyeti. avaśyaṃ tathāvidhasya kāyavāgvikārā bhavaṃti. api ca śapaṃti te tathā. tatra cāvaśyaṃ kāyavākceṣṭayā bhavitavyaṃ anye tv āhuḥ. na kāmadhātāv avaśyam avijñaptiḥ sarvaiva vijñaptyadhīnā bhavati. phalaprāptyaiva saha paṃcakādīnāṃ prātimokṣasaṃvarotpattisaṃbhāvāt. ity akuśalāpy evaṃjātīyā kācid vijñaptim aṃtareṇāpi syāt. pūrvavijñaptaṃ tair iti [Tib. 70a] avaśyam itaratrāpi bhaviṣyati. ṛṣīṇāṃ tāvad uktaṃ poṣadhamṛṣāvāde 'pi. yad apariśuddhaḥ saṃghamadhyaṃ praviśait. niṣīdati. svam īryāpathaṃkalpayati. tatsaṃbaddhaṃ vā yatkiṃcid bhāṣate. sāsya pūrvavijñaptir iti.
body.translated_text: "One who, by means of the body, otherwise" — one who conveys meaning through a bodily gesture, for that one too there is false speech. "One would exert oneself, would strive" — "one would exert by speech" — meaning: one would kill another by speech. But here, because the taking of life is bodily, only bodily non-informative action (<s>avijñapti</s>) is included in the fundamental [action-path], not vocal. Nor would there be bodily informative action here — [in the case of] "exerting by body." Here, because false speech is vocal, only vocal non-informative action is included in the fundamental [action-path] — this should be understood. "Or by the offense of both" — by the offense of body and speech. The connection of <s>ṛṣi</s>s with bodily offense occurs through mental malice. "And the illustration of <s>poṣadha</s> is here" — the connection with vocal offense occurs. For in the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>poṣadha</s> (confession ceremony), when the <s>Vinaya</s>-holder announces "Are you pure?", if a certain <s>bhikṣu</s>, having an actual offense, does not disclose it, approving by silence alone — he would be one who speaks falsely. "How is the action-path accomplished for those two?" — how, for those two — <s>ṛṣi</s>s and <s>bhikṣu</s>s — who do not exert themselves through body and speech respectively, are the taking of life and false speech accomplished as action-paths? "Effort should be made here" — the meaning is: the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s should give a resolution. Here <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> gives a resolution: the <s>ṛṣi</s>s in effect become commanders. For non-human beings, recognizing the evil intention of those [<s>ṛṣi</s>s] directed toward abandoning beings, being devoted to them, exert themselves bodily — whereby the action-path arises for those <s>ṛṣi</s>s. How? "Through the informative action of another." Necessarily, bodily and vocal gestures occur for one of such a nature. Moreover, they curse thus, and there necessarily must be bodily and vocal gestures [involved]. Others, however, say: not necessarily in the Desire Realm is all non-informative action (<s>avijñapti</s>) dependent on informative action, because of the possibility of the arising of <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint for the five [sense-beings] and the like simultaneously with the attainment of the fruit. Therefore, some unwholesome [<s>avijñapti</s>] of this kind too could exist without informative action. "Previously informed by them" — necessarily this will apply elsewhere too. For the <s>ṛṣi</s>s it has been stated; in the case of false speech at <s>poṣadha</s> too — the impure one who enters the midst of the <s>saṃgha</s>, sits down, arranges his posture, or says anything connected with that — that is his prior informative action.

body.text: (IV.77, 78ab) sarvaṃ kliṣṭaṃ vacanaṃ saṃbhinnapralāpa iti. mṛṣāvādāditrayam api. na kevalam anyaṃ kliṣṭaṃ. saiva ca saṃbhinnapralāpiteti. yasya guṇasya hi bhāvād dravye śabdaniveśaḥ. tasya. tadabhidhāne tvatalāv iti. tatpratyayena kliṣṭavacanalakṣaṇaḥ saṃbhinnapralāpa ucyate. tadyogena hi. saṃbhinnapralāpayogena hi. sa pudgalaḥ saṃbhinnapralāpī bhavati.
body.translated_text: (IV.77, 78ab) "All afflicted speech is frivolous talk (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>)" — the three beginning with false speech too, not only other afflicted [speech]. "And that very one is [called] frivolous talk" — the quality by whose presence a designation is applied to a substance — in its designation, the <s>tvatal</s> [suffixes apply]. By the suffix derived from that, afflicted speech having the characteristic [of frivolous talk] is called <s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>. Through connection with that — through connection with frivolous talk — that person becomes a frivolous talker.

body.text: mṛṣāvādāditrayād yad anyakliṣṭaṃ vacanaṃ. sa saṃbhinnapralāpa ity uktvodāharaṇaṃ darśayann āha.
body.translated_text: Having stated that afflicted speech other than the three beginning with false speech is frivolous talk, he shows an example.

children.translated_text: "Like flattering speech, singing, drama, and false scriptures" —

body.text: lapanāṃ karotīti. lābhayaśaskāmatayā sevābhidyotikāṃ vācaṃ niścārayatīty
body.translated_text: "One who makes flattering speech" — one who, through desire for gain, fame, or pleasure, utters speech that displays servility

body.text: arthaḥ. paridevasaṃgaṇikādikam iti. ādiśabdena paridevasaṃgaṇikābhyāṃ yo 'nyaḥ kliṣṭacittānāṃ kaścid ālāpaḥ.
body.translated_text: is the meaning. 'Lamentation, gossip, and the rest' — by the word 'and the rest,' any other conversation of those with afflicted minds, other than lamentation and gossip.

body.text: āvāhavivāhādyabhilāpasadbhāvād iti. āvāho dārikāyā dārakagṛhāgamanaṃ. vivāho dārakasya dārikāgṛhāgamanaṃ. āvāhaḥ praveśanakaḥ. vivāhaḥ pariṇayanam ity apare. ādiśabdena raktacittānām ālāpaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the existence of utterances such as marriage ceremonies and the like' — <s>āvāha</s> is the bride going to the groom's house. <s>Vivāha</s> is the groom going to the bride's house. <s>Āvāha</s> is the bringing in; <s>vivāha</s> is the leading away — according to others. By the word 'and the like,' the conversation of those with passionate minds.

body.text: (IV.78cd, 79ab) viṣameṇānyāyeneti. [Tib. 70b] uddeśanirdeśarūpau paryāyau.
body.translated_text: (IV.78cd, 79ab) 'Crookedly, unjustly' — [Tib. 70b] these are synonyms in the form of summary and elaboration.

body.text: tathā hīti vistaraḥ. yasmāt paṃcānāṃ nivaraṇānām adhikāreṇa. kāmacchandaṃ kāmatṛṣṇāsvabhāvam adhikṛtyoktaṃ. so 'bhidhyāṃ loke prahāya vigatābhidhyena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. vyāpādaṃ styānamiddham auddhatyakaukṛtyaṃ vicikitsāṃ loke prahāya tīrṇakāṃkṣo bhavati. tīrṇavicikitsaḥ. akathaṃkathī kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu. sa paṃca nivaraṇāni prahāyety evamādi. ato jñāyate sarvaiva kāmāvacarī tṛṣṇābhidhyeti.
body.translated_text: Thus indeed — this is the elaboration. Because, in the context of the five hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>), sensual desire having the nature of craving for sensory pleasures is addressed: 'Having abandoned covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) in the world, one dwells for the most part with a mind free from covetousness. Having abandoned ill-will, sloth-and-torpor, restlessness-and-worry, and doubt in the world, one becomes one who has crossed beyond uncertainty, one who has crossed beyond doubt, without perplexity regarding wholesome <s>dharma</s>s. Having abandoned the five hindrances' — and so forth. From this it is known that all Desire Realm craving is covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>).

body.text: audārikaduścaritasaṃgrahād iti. daśasv akuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu yad audārikam duścaritaṃ. tat saṃgṛhītaṃ. na sarvam. evaṃ kuśaleṣu. ato na sarvābhidhyā karmapathaḥ. kiṃ tarhi. yā parasve viṣamaspṛhā. sā karmapatha ity apareṣām abhiprāyaḥ. mā bhūc cakravartināṃ uttarakauravāṇāṃ cābhidhyā karmapatha iti. na hi tatra kāmāvacarī tṛṣṇā nāsti. na ca tatrākuśalāḥ karmapathā iṣyaṃte.
body.translated_text: 'Because of including gross misconduct' — among the ten unwholesome action-paths, what is gross misconduct is included, not everything. Similarly for the wholesome. Therefore not all covetousness is an action-path. What then? The unjust craving for what belongs to another — that is an action-path, according to the view of others. Lest the covetousness of <s>cakravartins</s> and the inhabitants of <s>Uttarakuru</s> be an action-path — for Desire Realm craving does exist there, yet unwholesome action-paths are not accepted there.

body.text: saiṣā sākalyena karmaphalāryāpavādiketi. tathā hy eṣā paṭhyate. nāsti dattam. nāstīṣṭaṃ. nāsti hutaṃ. nāsti sucaritaṃ. nāsti duścaritaṃ. nāsti sucaritaduścaritānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipākaḥ. nāsty ayaṃ lokaḥ. nāsti paralokaḥ. nāsti mātā. [Tib. 71a] nāsti pitā. nāsti sattva
body.translated_text: 'That [wrong view] completely denies <s>karma</s>, its fruit, and the Noble Ones' — for it is read thus: 'There is no gift given. There is no sacrifice. There is no oblation. There is no good conduct. There is no bad conduct. There is no fruit and retribution of good and bad <s>karma</s>s. There is no this world. There is no other world. There is no mother. [Tib. 71a] There is no father. There is no being

body.text: upapādukaḥ. na saṃti loke 'rhaṃta iti. tatra nāsti dattaṃ. yāvan nāsti duṣcaritam iti karmāpavādikā. tathā nāsti mātā. nāsti piteti karmāpavādikaiva. nāsti sucaritaduścaritānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipākaḥ. nāsty ayaṃ lokaḥ. nāsti paralokaḥ. tathā nāsti sattva upapāduka iti phalāpavādikā. na saṃti loke 'rhaṃta ity āryāpavādikā. ādimātraṃ tu śloke darśitam iti.
body.translated_text: spontaneously born. There are no <s>Arhats</s> in the world.' There, 'there is no gift given,' up to 'there is no bad conduct' — this denies <s>karma</s>. Similarly, 'there is no mother, there is no father' — this too denies <s>karma</s>. 'There is no fruit and retribution of good and bad <s>karma</s>s,' 'there is no this world,' 'there is no other world,' and similarly 'there is no being spontaneously born' — this denies the fruit [of karma]. 'There are no <s>Arhats</s> in the world' — this denies the Noble Ones. But only the beginning was shown in the verse.

children.translated_text: 'The nihilistic view [denies] the wholesome and unwholesome' —

body.text: iti udāharaṇamātratvāt.
body.translated_text: because it is merely an example.

body.text: (IV.79cd) karmaṇaḥ paṃthāna iti. cetanākhyasya karmaṇaḥ paṃthānaḥ. katham ity āha. tatsaṃprayogiṇī hi cetanā. abhidhyādisaṃprayogiṇī teṣām abhidhyādīnāṃ vāhena gatyā vahati. gacchatīty arthaḥ. tadvaśena tathābhisaṃskaraṇāt. yasmād abhidhyādīnāṃ yathākramaṃ saktipratikūlamithyānitīraṇākārāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: (IV.79cd) 'The path of action (<s>karma</s>)' — the path of action characterized by volition (<s>cetanā</s>). How? He says: the volition associated with those — the volition associated with covetousness and the rest — carries, moves, by the conveyance, the movement, of those covetousness and the rest. The meaning is: it goes [along that path]. Because of being fashioned in accordance with that: because, in accordance with covetousness and the rest, which respectively have the aspects of attachment, hostility, and false determination

body.text: vaśena. tadanurūpā cetanābhisaṃskaroti. cetayata ity arthaḥ. atas teṣāṃ vāhena vahati. karma ca. kāyavākkarmasvabhāvatvāt. karmaṇaś ca cetanākhyasya paṃthāna iti karmapathāḥ. tatsamutthānacetanāyāḥ [Tib. 71b] kāyavākkarmasamutthānacetanāyāḥ. tān adhiṣṭhāya tān prāṇātipātādīn adhiṣṭhāya pravṛtteḥ. asarūpāṇām apy ekaśeṣasiddher iti. śabdasarūpāṇām arthasarūpāṇāṃ vā ekaśeṣa iṣyate. yathā vṛkṣaś ca vṛkṣaś ca vṛkṣau. vakraṣ ca kuṭilaś ca vakrāv iti. iha tu karma ca karmapathāś ceti na karmaśabdasya karmapathaśabdasya ca sārūpyaṃ śabdataḥ nāpy arthataḥ. karmārthasya karmapathārthasya ca bhinnatvād ekaśeṣo na prāpnoti. yasmāt tv asarūpāṇāṃ sākalyenaikadeśena tu sarūpāṇām ekaśeṣaḥ sidhyati. iṣyata ity arthaḥ. tadyathā guṇo yaṅlukor iti. yaṅ ca yaṅluk yaṅlukau. tayor iti. na śakyate vaktuṃ. yaṅ ca luk ca yaṅlukāv iti ayaṃ luko 'niṣṭatvāt. ekadeśasārūpyāt tu. yaṅo yaṅlugekadeśasya ca yaṅ iti sārūpyāt sidhyaty ekaśeṣo yaṅlukor iti. ato jñāpakād ayam api sidhyati. karma ca karmapathāś ca karmapathā iti. paścāt punaḥ sarūpaikaśeṣaḥ. karmapathāś cābhidhyaḥ karmapathāś ca prāṇātipātādaya iti karmapathāḥ. atha vaivaṃ yojanā. karmaṇaḥ paṃthānaḥ karmapathāḥ. karma ca te karmapathāś ca karmakarmapathāḥ. karmapathāś cābhidhyādayaḥ. karmakarmapathāś ca prāṇātipātādayaḥ. [Tib. 72a] karmapathā iti. evam anabhidhyādaya iti vistaraḥ. kuśalā api karmapathā evam eva yojyāḥ. anabhidhyādayo hi karmaṇaḥ paṃthāna eva. prāṇātipātaviratyādayaś ca karma ca karmaṇaś ca paṃthāna iti.
body.translated_text: — in accordance with them, the corresponding volition fashions, that is, wills — this is the meaning. Therefore, it carries by the conveyance of those. And they are <s>karma</s> — because of having the nature of bodily and vocal action. And they are the path of action characterized by volition — hence 'action-paths.' Of the volition that originates them — [Tib. 71b] the volition that originates bodily and vocal action — because of proceeding by relying on those, by relying on those [acts of] taking life and the rest. 'Even of dissimilar [terms], the singular-remainder (<s>ekaśeṣa</s>) construction is established' — the singular-remainder is accepted for words that are similar in sound or similar in meaning. Just as 'tree and tree = two trees' (<s>vṛkṣau</s>); 'crooked and curved = two crooked ones' (<s>vakrau</s>). But here, 'karma and karma-paths' — neither the word 'karma' nor the word 'karma-path' has similarity either in sound or in meaning. Because the meaning of 'karma' and the meaning of 'karma-path' are different, the singular-remainder should not apply. But since the singular-remainder of dissimilar [terms] is established — is accepted, is the meaning — when they are similar in whole or in part. For example: '<s>yaṅ</s> and <s>yaṅluk</s>' — <s>yaṅ</s> and <s>yaṅluk</s> are <s>yaṅluks</s>. 'Of those two' — it cannot be said: '<s>yaṅ</s> and <s>luk</s> are <s>yaṅluks</s>' — because this <s>luk</s> [form] is undesired. But through partial similarity — because of the similarity of <s>yaṅ</s> and the <s>yaṅ</s>-portion of <s>yaṅluk</s> — the singular-remainder 'of <s>yaṅluks</s>' is established. Therefore, by this indicative rule, this too is established: 'karma and karma-paths = karma-paths.' Afterward, there is a singular-remainder of similar terms: 'karma-paths that are covetousness and karma-paths that are killing and the rest = karma-paths.' Or alternatively, the construction is thus: the paths of action are karma-paths. And those that are both karma and karma-paths are karma-karma-paths. Karma-paths are covetousness and the rest. Karma-karma-paths are killing and the rest. [Tib. 72a] 'Karma-paths' — thus. Similarly, 'non-covetousness and the rest' — this is the elaboration. The wholesome action-paths too should be construed in exactly the same way. For non-covetousness and the rest are merely paths of action. And abstention from killing and the rest are both action and paths of action.

body.text: yasmāt tadartha iti vistaraḥ yasmān maulakarmapathārthaṃ teṣaṃ tatprayogāṇāṃ pravṛttiḥ. yasmāc ca maulakarmapathamūlikā teṣāṃ tatpṛṣṭhānāṃ pravṛttiḥ. ato na tāni karmapathāḥ. yady api karmapatho 'pi karmapathasya prayoga uktaḥ. sa tu maulatvāt karmapathaḥ. na tu prayogapṛṣṭhabhūtatvād iti. yathaudārikasaṃgrahād ity uktaṃ prāg iti.
body.translated_text: 'Because for their sake' — this is the elaboration. Because the operation of those preparations is for the sake of the principal action-path. And because the operation of those aftermaths is rooted in the principal action-path. Therefore those are not action-paths. Even though an action-path is also stated as a preparation for an action-path, that is an action-path because of being principal, not because of being a preparation or aftermath. 'As stated before, "because of including gross [misconduct]"' —

children.translated_text: 'Because of including gross [misconduct], the ten action-paths are stated' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. yāni prayogapṛṣṭhāni. tāni na saṃgṛhītāni. yeṣāṃ ceti vistaraḥ. yeṣāṃ maulānām utkarṣāpakarṣeṇādhyātmikabāhyānāṃ bhāvānām utkarṣāpkarṣau loke bhavataḥ. na tu prayogapṛṣṭhānāṃ. atas ta eva karmapathāḥ. teṣāṃ cotkarṣāpakarṣeṇa tadutkarṣāpakarṣaṃ vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. The preparations and aftermaths are not included. 'And of which' — this is the elaboration — of which principal [action-paths], through their increase and decrease, the increase and decrease of internal and external entities in the world occurs — but not of preparations and aftermaths. Therefore those alone are action-paths. And through their increase and decrease, [the text] will state the increase and decrease of those [worldly entities]:

children.translated_text: 'All give fruits of predominant influence, outflow, and retribution' —

body.text: ity atra. ato na tāni prayogapṛṣṭhāni karmapathāḥ.
body.translated_text: in that passage. Therefore those preparations and aftermaths are not action-paths.

body.text: teṣāṃ te kathaṃ karmapathā iti. na hi teṣām abhidhyādibhyo 'nyan manaskarmāsti cetanā. yasya karmaṇas te 'bhidhyādayaḥ paṃthāna iti karmapathāḥ syuḥ. [Tib. 72b] ta eva praṣṭavyā iti. tair eva parihāro vaktavyaḥ. ya evaṃ manyaṃte. api tu śakyam iti vistaraḥ. svamatena tatpakṣaṃ samarthayati. itaretarāvāhanād veti. kiṃ. te 'bhidhyādayaḥ karmapathā iti prakṛtaṃ. abhidhyā vyāpādamithyādṛṣṭī āvāhayati. te ca tām iti. karma ca te. karmaṇaś caiṣām ekatarasya panthāna iti karmapathāḥ.
body.translated_text: 'How are those their action-paths?' — for there is no mental action other than covetousness and the rest that is volition, of which action those covetousness and the rest would be paths, so as to be called action-paths. [Tib. 72b] 'Those very ones should be asked' — the resolution should be stated by those very ones who think thus. 'But it is possible' — this is the elaboration. He supports that position with his own view. 'Because of mutual conveyance' — what? Those covetousness and the rest are action-paths — this is the topic. Covetousness conveys ill-will and wrong view, and those [convey] it. And they are both <s>karma</s> and the path of one or another of the actions — hence action-paths.

body.text: (IV.80, 81) mithyādṛṣṭyā kuśalamūlasamuccheda ity etam arthaṃ vaktukāma upodghātaṃ bravīti. sarva ete 'kuśalānām iti vistaraḥ. adhimātraparipūrṇayeti. adhimātrādhimātrayety arthaḥ. kiṃ tarhi śāstra uktam iti. yadi mithyādṛṣṭyā kuśalamūlasamucchedo nākuśalamūlaiḥ. yat tac chāstra uktaṃ. yair akuśalamūlaiḥ kuśalamūlāni samucchinattītyādi. tāni hi lobhādisvabhāvāni. na mithyādṛṣṭisvabhāvānīty arthaḥ. akuśalamūlādhyāhṛtatvād iti vistaraḥ. akuśalamūlair lobhādibhir adhimātrair mithyādṛṣṭir adhyāhṛtāpanītā. tasmāt. akuśalamūlādhyāhṛtatvān mithyādṛṣṭeḥ. teṣv eva tatkarmopadeśaḥ. teṣv evākuśalamūleṣu. mithyādṛṣṭeḥ kuśalamūlasamucchedakaṃ yat karma. tasyopadeśaḥ [Tib. 73a].
body.translated_text: (IV.80, 81) Wishing to state that through wrong view there is the cutting off of wholesome roots, he makes a preliminary statement: 'All these are of unwholesome [roots]' — this is the elaboration. 'Intense and complete' — meaning: intense-intense. 'But what then is stated in the treatise?' — if the cutting off of wholesome roots is through wrong view and not through the unwholesome roots — then that which is stated in the treatise: 'By which unwholesome roots one cuts off the wholesome roots' — and so on — those have the nature of greed and the rest, not the nature of wrong view — this is the meaning. 'Because of being impelled by the unwholesome roots' — this is the elaboration. Wrong view is impelled, driven, by the unwholesome roots of greed and the rest when intense. Therefore — because of wrong view being impelled by the unwholesome roots — the instruction of that action is in those very [unwholesome roots]. In those very unwholesome roots, the instruction of the action of wrong view that cuts off wholesome roots [is given] [Tib. 73a].

body.text: prajñaptibhāṣyaṃ tarhi kathaṃ nīyate. yadi kāmāvacarāṇi kuśalamūlāni samucchidyaṃte. rūpārūpyāvacarair asamanvāgatatvād iti varṇyaṃte. tatprāptidūrīkaraṃam iti. rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ prāpter dūrīkaraṇam abhipretya tasya pudgalasya. etad uktaṃ traidhātukāni kuśalamūlāni samucchinnānīti. kathaṃ ca punas tatprāptidūrīkaraṇaṃ. saṃtates tadabhājanatvāpādanāt. yasmād asau tatsaṃtatiḥ pūrvaṃ bhājanabhūtā tatprāptīnāṃ. kuśalamūlasamucchedād idānīṃ tatprāptīnām abhājanam āpāditeti. atas tatprāptir dūrīkṛtā bhavati.
body.translated_text: How then is the <s>Prajñaptibhāṣya</s> to be understood? If [only] the Desire Realm wholesome roots are cut off — because of not being endowed with the Form and Formless Realm [roots] — [the statement] is explained [thus]. 'The removal of the acquisition of those' — the removal of the acquisition of Form and Formless Realm [roots] is intended with reference to that person. This is what is stated: the wholesome roots of the three realms are cut off. And how is the removal of their acquisition [effected]? Through rendering the continuum unfit for them. Because that continuum, which was formerly a vessel for those acquisitions, is now rendered a non-vessel for those acquisitions through the cutting off of wholesome roots. Thus their acquisition is removed.

body.text: prāyogikebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ parihīṇatvād iti. śrutaciṃtābhāvanāmayebhyaḥ prāyogikebhyaḥ pūrvam evāsau mṛdumṛdvyavasthāyāṃ tebhyaḥ parihīṇaḥ. tadaiva tasya prāpticcheda ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Because of having already declined from the practice-born [roots]' — from those born of hearing, thinking, and meditation, from the practice-born [roots], one has already earlier declined, in the stage of mild-mild. At that very time, the cutting of their acquisition [occurs] — this is the meaning.

body.text: ānaṃtaryavimuktimārgasthānīye iti. hetvapavādinī ānaṃtaryamārgasthānīyā. phalāpavādinī vimuktimārgasthānīyā. tad uktaṃ bhavati. ubhe apy ete hetuphalāpavādinyau mithyādṛṣṭī kuśalasamucchede vyāpriyete. naikaiveti.
body.translated_text: 'Occupying the position of the uninterrupted and liberation paths' — the [view] that denies the cause occupies the position of the uninterrupted path. The [view] that denies the fruit occupies the position of the liberation path. This is what is stated: both these wrong views — denying cause and denying fruit — are active in the cutting off of wholesome roots. Not one alone.

body.text: aparaḥ pakṣaḥ sāsravālaṃbanayaiveti. duḥkhasamudayālaṃbanayā. nānāsravālaṃbanayā 'nirodhamārgālaṃbanayety [Tib. 73b] arthaḥ. sabhāgadhātvālaṃbanayaiva
body.translated_text: Another position: 'Only with an object that has outflows' — with suffering and origination as objects. Not with an outflow-free object — not with cessation and path as objects [Tib. 73b] — this is the meaning. 'And only with an object of the same realm'

body.text: ceti. kāmadhātvālaṃbanayaivety arthaḥ. na visabhāgadhātvālaṃbanayā na rūpārūpyadhātvālaṃbanayā. kuśalamūlāni samucchidyaṃta ity adhikṛtaṃ kasmād ity āha. saṃprayogamātrānuśāyitvena durbalatvād iti. anāsravālaṃbanā visabhāgadhātvālaṃbanā ca yā mithyādṛṣṭiḥ. sā saṃprayogamātreṇa saṃprayukteṣu dharmeṣv anuśete nālaṃbanataḥ. tasmād asau durbalā bhavati. ato na tayā samucchidyaṃte.
body.translated_text: — meaning: only with a Desire Realm object. Not with a dissimilar realm as object — not with the Form or Formless Realm as object. The wholesome roots are cut off — this is the subject under discussion. Why? He says: 'Because of being weak due to being latent only through association' — the wrong view that has an outflow-free object or a dissimilar-realm object is latent in the associated <s>dharma</s>s only through association, not through its object. Therefore it is weak. Hence the wholesome roots are not cut off by it.

body.text: evaṃ tu varṇayaṃti vaibhāṣikāḥ. sarvayeti. yā ca hetum apavadate yā ca phalaṃ. yā ca sabhāgaṃ dhātum ālaṃbate yā ca visabhāgaṃ. yā ca sāsravaṃ yā cānāsravam ālaṃbate. sarvayaiva tayā samucchidyaṃte.
body.translated_text: But the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> explain thus: 'By every [wrong view]' — both that which denies the cause and that which denies the fruit; both that which takes a same-realm object and that which takes a dissimilar-realm object; both that which takes an object with outflows and that which takes an outflow-free object — by every such [wrong view], they are cut off.

body.text: darśanaprahātavyā iveti. yathā duḥkhādidarśanaheyāḥ kleśā nava prakārā api duḥkhādisatyadarśanāt sakṛt prahīyaṃte. tadvan nava prakārāṇy api kuśalamūlāni sakṛt samucchidyaṃta ity ete.
body.translated_text: 'Like those to be abandoned by seeing' — just as the afflictions to be abandoned by seeing — suffering and the rest — nine types, are abandoned at once through the seeing of the truth of suffering and the rest, so too the nine types of wholesome roots are all cut off at once — this [is their view].

body.text: bhāvanāheyakleśavad iti. yathā navaprakāreṇa mārgeṇa navaprakāraḥ kleśaḥ prahīyate. mṛdumṛdunā mārgeṇa adhimātrādhimātrakleśaprakāraḥ prahīyate. yāvad [Tib. 74a] adhimātrādhimātreṇa mṛdumṛduḥ. evaṃ navaprakārayāpi mithyādṛṣṭyā navaprakārāṇi kuśalamūlāni samucchidyaṃte. ṛdumṛdvyā mithyādṛṣṭyā adhimātrādhimātraḥ kuśalamūlaprakāraḥ samucchidyate. yāvad adhimātrādhimātrayā mṛdumṛduḥ kuśalamūlaprakāra iti. evam ayaṃ graṃthaḥ paripālito bhavati. yadi bhāvanāheyakleśavad yathoktaṃ tāni samucchidyaṃte. aṇusahagatāni mṛdumṛdūni. yair akuśalamūlaiḥ kuśalamūlāni samucchinattīti. adhimātrādhimātrair akuśalamūlaiḥ kuśalamūlasamuccheda uktaḥ. na mṛdumṛdvādibhir ity abhiprāyaḥ. yadi kramaśaḥ samucchidyaṃte 'sya tarhītyādi. kathaṃ. samāptim etat saṃdhāyoktam iti. kuśalamūlasamucchedasamāptiṃ saṃdhāya katamāny adhimātrāṇīti vistareṇa etad uktaṃ. mṛdumṛdvādisamucchedas tv anukto 'pi grahītavyaḥ. tasmāt samāptim eva saṃdhāyaitad uktaṃ. tair niravaśeṣacchedāt. yasmāt tair navabhir mithyādṛṣṭiprakāraiḥ kuśalamūlānāṃ niravaśeṣacchedo bhavati. eko 'pi hi prakāras teṣām asamucchinna iti. mṛdumṛdunavamaḥ prakāraḥ sarveṣāṃ navānām api prakārāṇāṃ punarutpattau hetuḥ syād iti. ataḥ samāptim etat saṃdhāyoktaṃ.
body.translated_text: Like the afflictions abandoned through cultivation (<s>bhāvanāheya</s>) — just as the afflictions are abandoned by the path in nine modes, the most gross by the mildest path, up to the mildest by the most intense — so too by wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) in nine modes, the nine types of wholesome roots are cut off. By the mildest wrong view, the most intense type of wholesome root is cut off, up to by the most intense wrong view, the mildest type of wholesome root. Thus this text is maintained. If, like the afflictions abandoned through cultivation, those [wholesome roots] are cut off as stated: [then] those accompanied by the subtle are the mildest. 'By which unwholesome roots one cuts off the wholesome roots' — the cutting off of wholesome roots is stated as being by the most intense unwholesome roots, not by the mildest and the rest — this is the intent. If they are cut off sequentially, then this and the rest [follow]. How? 'This is stated with reference to the completion' — stated with reference to the completion of the cutting off of wholesome roots: 'which are the most intense?' and so forth — this is stated in detail. The cutting off of the mildest and the rest, though not stated, should also be understood. Therefore, this is stated with reference to completion alone. Because of the complete cutting off by those — since by those nine types of wrong view, the complete, without-remainder cutting off of wholesome roots occurs. For even if one type of them remains uncut — the ninth type, the mildest of the mild — it would be a cause for the re-arising of all nine types. Therefore this is stated with reference to completion.

body.text: ubhayeneti. vyutthānena cāvyutthānena ca.
body.translated_text: 'By both' — by the concentrated state and by the non-concentrated state.

body.text: tattyāgāt [Tib. 74b] tasya tyāga iti. yo mṛdumṛdunā cittena saṃvaraḥ samātta āsīt. tasya mṛdumṛdoś cittasya mṛdumṛdukuśalamūlasaṃprayuktasya
body.translated_text: 'Through the abandonment of that, the abandonment of that [restraint]' — the restraint that had been undertaken with the mildest mind — through the abandonment, the cutting off, of that mildest mind associated with the mildest wholesome root

body.text: tyāge samucchede tasya saṃvarasya tyāgo bhavati. evaṃ yāvad yo 'dhimātrādhimātreṇa cittena samāttaḥ saṃvaraḥ. tattyāgāt tasya tyāga iti.
body.translated_text: — the abandonment of that restraint occurs. Similarly, up to: the restraint undertaken with the most intense mind — through the abandonment of that, the abandonment of that [restraint].

body.text: karmaphale pratyakṣatvād iti. aciropapannasya devaputrasya trīṇi cittāni samudācaraṃti. kuto 'haṃ cyutaḥ. kutropapannaḥ. kena karmaṇety evaṃ karmaphalapratyakṣatvān na deveṣu kuśalamūlāni samucchidyaṃte. jaṃbūdvīpa eveti. tatra viśeṣeṇa tārkikatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. sarvālpair aṣṭābhir indriyaiḥ samanvāgataḥ paṃcabhir vedanendriyaiḥ kāyajīvitamanaindriyaiś ca. samucchinnakuśalamūla eva. tasya hi śraddhādīni samucchinnāni. pṛthagjanatvāc ca nājñāsyāmīndriyādīni saṃti. cakṣurādīny api na saṃti. vaikalyayoge. kramamaraṇāvasthāyāṃ vā. evaṃ paurvavidehako gaudānīyaka iti. atideśād asty anayor api kuśalamūlasamuccheda iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the directness of the fruit of <s>karma</s>' — for a <s>devaputta</s> (son of the gods) who has just been reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where have I passed away? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' — thus, because of the directness of the fruit of <s>karma</s>, wholesome roots are not cut off among the gods. 'In <s>Jambudvīpa</s> alone' — because there, in particular, [beings] are inclined to speculation — this is the intent. 'Endowed with only eight faculties, the fewest' — endowed with five feeling-faculties, the body-faculty, life-faculty, and mind-faculty. One whose wholesome roots are cut off. For his faith and other [spiritual] faculties are cut off. And because of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), the faculties of 'I-shall-come-to-know' (<s>ajñāsyāmīndriya</s>) and the rest do not exist. The eye-faculty and the rest also do not exist — in the case of being crippled. Or in the state of gradual dying. 'Similarly, one of <s>Pūrvavideha</s> and of <s>Godānīya</s>' — by the extension [of the rule], he shows that there is also cutting off of wholesome roots for these two.

children.translated_text: 'A woman or a man cuts off' —

body.text: iti. strī pumāṃś ceti caśabdo luptanirdiṣṭaḥ. yaḥ strīndriyeṇa samanvāgato niyatam asāv aṣṭābhir indriyaiḥ samanvāgataḥ. caturbhir vedanendriyais tribhiś ca kāyajīvitamanaindriyaiḥ [Tib. 75a] strīndriyeṇāṣṭamena. śraddhādīni samucchinnakuśalamūlāvasthāyāṃ vyabhicāryaṃta ity abhiprāyaḥ. ayam eva cātrārtho virudhyate. cakṣurādīny api vyabhicāryaṃte pūrvavat.
body.translated_text: the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is elided. One who is endowed with the female faculty — that one is necessarily endowed with eight faculties: with four feeling-faculties, and with three — body, life, and mind faculties — and with the female faculty as the eighth. The intent is that faith and the other [spiritual faculties] are variable [i.e., may be absent] in the state of cut-off wholesome roots. This same meaning here is contradicted [by the objection that] the eye and other [faculties] are also variable, as before.

body.text: teṣām apīti. teṣām api samucchettṝṇām uktānāṃ. tṛṣṇācarito na samucchinatti. dṛḍhagūḍhapāpāśayatvād iti. dṛḍho gūḍhaḥ pāpaś cāśayo 'bhiprāyo 'syeti samāsaḥ. dṛḍhaḥ sthiraḥ. gūḍhaḥ pracchannaḥ. pāpo 'kalyāṇaḥ. tṛṣṇācaritapakṣatvād iti. tṛṣṇācaritajātīyatvād ity arthaḥ. yathā tṛṣṇācaritaś calāśayaḥ. tadvat te ṣaṇḍhādaya iti. āpāyikavac ca. yathāpāyikāḥ kliṣṭākliṣṭayoḥ prajñayor adṛḍhatvān na kuśalamūlāni samucchindaṃti. evaṃ ṣaṇdhādayaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Of those too' — of those stated as cutting off [wholesome roots]. 'One of craving-conduct does not cut off — because of having firm, hidden, and evil intentions' — the compound: one whose intention is firm, hidden, and evil. 'Firm' means stable. 'Hidden' means concealed. 'Evil' means unwholesome. 'Because of belonging to the class of craving-conduct' — meaning: because of being of the type of craving-conduct. Just as one of craving-conduct has an unstable intention, so too those eunuchs and the rest. And like those in the lower realms — just as those in the lower realms, because of the weakness of both afflicted and unafflicted wisdom, do not cut off wholesome roots, so too eunuchs and the rest.

body.text: pratisaṃdhitānīti. pratisaṃdhikṛtāni pratisaṃdhitāni. prātipadikadhātuḥ. pratisaṃhitānīty apare paṭhaṃti. ārogyabalalābhavad iti. yathārogyaṃ pūrvaṃ bhavati. krameṇa tu balalābho bhavati. tadvat.
body.translated_text: 'Reconnected' (<s>pratisaṃdhita</s>) — meaning: made to reconnect, reconnected. The nominal stem is [formed thus]. Others read 'pratisaṃhita' (reunited). 'Like recovery and the gaining of strength' — just as recovery comes first, and the gaining of strength occurs gradually — so too.

children.translated_text: 'Here, one who has committed a heinous act (<s>ānantarya</s>) [does not reconnect]' —

body.text: iti. ānaṃtaryakāriṇa eva neha pratisaṃdhir bhavatīti. arthata etad uktaṃ bhavaty anānaṃtaryakāriṇa iha pratisaṃdhir bhavatīti. aṃtarābhavastha iti. narakagamanāyāṃtarābhavasthaḥ. cyutyabhimukha iti. [Tib. 75b] narakāc cyutyabhimukhaḥ. hetubaleneti. sabhāgahetubalena. yasmād yeṣāṃ mithyādṛṣṭiḥ svayaṃ rocate. pratyayabaleneti. parato ghoṣabalena. yasmād yeṣāṃ mithyādṛṣṭī rocate. hetubalasya sāratvāt. evaṃ yaḥ svabaleneti. yaḥ svatarkabalena. sa cyavamānaḥ. yaḥ parabalena. parataḥ śrutabalena. sa upapadyamānaḥ.
body.translated_text: meaning: one who has committed a heinous act does not reconnect here. In effect, what has been stated is: one who has not committed a heinous act reconnects here. 'One established in the intermediate existence' — one in the intermediate existence heading toward the hells. 'Facing death' — facing death from the hells. 'By the power of the cause' — by the power of the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>). Because for some, wrong view appeals to them by itself. 'By the power of the condition' — by the power of hearing from another. Because for some, wrong view [appeals] from hearing. Because of the strength of the power of the cause — thus: one who [cuts off] by one's own power — by one's own power of reasoning — that one is in the process of dying [from the hells]. One who [cuts off] by another's power — by the power of hearing from another — that one is in the process of being reborn [in a new life].

body.text: ya āśayavipanna iti. mithyādṛṣṭisaṃmukhībhāvena vipanno vinaṣṭaḥ. sa dṛṣṭe dharme janmani pratisaṃdadhāti. ya āśayaprayogavipannaḥ. yo mithyādṛṣṭisaṃmukhībhāvenānaṃtaryakṛiyayā ca vipannaḥ. sa bhedāt kāyasya pratisaṃdadhāti. atra ca yaḥ svabalena parabaleneti pūrvoktasyaivāyaṃ paryāyaḥ. evaṃ yo dṛṣṭivipanno yo dṛṣṭiśīlavipanna iti. anaṃtarapūrvoktasyaivāyaṃ paryāya ity avagaṃtavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'One whose disposition is corrupted' — corrupted, destroyed, by the coming face-to-face with wrong view. That one reconnects [wholesome roots] in the visible <s>dharma</s>, in this very life. 'One whose disposition and conduct are corrupted' — one who is corrupted by the coming face-to-face with wrong view and by the performance of heinous acts. That one reconnects upon the breakup of the body [i.e., after death]. And here, 'one by one's own power and by another's power' is a synonym for what was stated just before. Similarly, 'one corrupted in view and one corrupted in view and conduct' should be understood as a synonym for what was stated immediately before.

body.text: pūraṇādaya iti. ādiśabdena ṣaṭ śāstāro gṛhyaṃte. tadyathā pūraṇakāśyapaḥ. maskarī gośālīputraḥ. saṃjayī vairaṭīputraḥ. ajitaḥ keśakaṃbalaḥ. kakudaḥ kātyāyanaḥ. nirgrantho jñātiputra iti. te samucchinnakuśalamūlāḥ. nāstikatvāt. na mithyātvaniyatāḥ. anānaṃtaryakāritvāt. [Tib. 76a] ānaṃtaryakāriṇo hi mithyātvaniyatāḥ ajātaśatrur mithyātvaniyataḥ. ānaṃtaryakāritvāt. na samucchinnakuśalamūlaḥ. samyagdṛṣṭikatvāt. devadattaḥ samucchinnakuśalamūlaś ca mithyātvaniyataś ca. saṃghabhedakatvāt tathāgataduṣṭacittarudhirotpādakatvāc ca. caturthy etān ākārān sthāpayitvety asmadādayaḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Pūraṇa</s> and the rest — by the word 'and the rest,' the six teachers are grasped. Namely: <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Maskarī Gośālīputra</s>, <s>Saṃjayī Vairaṭīputra</s>, <s>Ajita Keśakambala</s>, <s>Kakuda Kātyāyana</s>, and <s>Nirgrantha Jñātiputra</s>. They have cut off their wholesome roots — because of being nihilists. [But] they are not fixed in wrongness (<s>mithyātvaniyata</s>) — because they have not committed heinous acts. For those who have committed heinous acts are fixed in wrongness. <s>Ajātaśatru</s> is fixed in wrongness — because he committed heinous acts. [But he] has not cut off his wholesome roots — because of having right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>). <s>Devadatta</s> has both cut off his wholesome roots and is fixed in wrongness — because of splitting the <s>Saṃgha</s> and because of drawing blood from the <s>Tathāgata</s> with malicious intent. The fourth [category], setting aside these [three] types — such as ourselves and others.

body.text: (IV.82) vinānyenābhidhyādīsaṃmukhībhāva iti. vinānyena karmapathena prāṇātipātādinābhidhyādīnām anyatamasaṃmukhībhāve. sā cetanā ekena karmapathena saha vartate. abhidhyayā vā vyāpādena vā mithyādṛṣṭyā vā. akliṣṭacetaso veti. kuśalāvyākṛtacittasya. tasya prayoktuḥ prayogeṇa. rūpiṇāṃ prāṇātipātādīnāṃ kāmamithyācāravarjyānaṃ anyatamasya niṣṭhāpane. tenaikena saha cetanā vartate. abhidhyādivyatiriktakliṣṭacittasya veti vaktavyaṃ. tasyāpi hy ayaṃ ayaṃ vidhiḥ saṃbhavati. vyāpannacittasya prāṇivadha iti vistaraḥ. vyāpādena prāṇātipātena ceti dvābhyāṃ saha vartate. kāmamithyācāre. saṃbhinnapralāpe ca. dvābhyāṃ saha vartate. abhidhyayā kāmamithyācāreṇa ceti dvābhyāṃ. saṃbhinnapralāpenābhidhyādīnāṃ cānyatamena ceti. [Tib. 76b] dvābhyām eva. idaṃ codyate. vyāpannacittasya prāṇivadha ity abhidhyāviṣṭasya cādattādāna iti. kim idaṃ svayaṃ kurvata ucyate. utāho pareṇa kāṛayataḥ. yadi svayaṃ kurvataḥ. vyāpannacittasyābhidhyāviṣṭasya ceti viśeṣaṇaṃ na yujyate. prāṇivadhe vyāpādasyāvaśyakatvāt. adattādāne cābhidhyāyāḥ. vyabhicāre hi viśeṣaṇam iṣyate. atha pareṇa kārayataḥ. abhidhyāvyāpādamithyādṛṣṭyanyatamacittasya. prāṇivadhe. adattādānakāmamithyācārasaṃbhinnapralāpeṣu veti vaktavyaṃ. ucyate svayaṃ kurvata iti. nanu coktaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ na yujyata iti. naiṣa doṣaḥ. na hīdaṃ viśeṣaṇam ucyate. kiṃ tarhi. svarūpākhyānam etat. vyāpādābhidhyayor dvitīyabhūtayos tatrāstitvaṃ kathyata iti. evam apy abhidhyādyanyataracittasya tān prāṇātipātādīn kārayato
body.translated_text: (IV.82) 'Without another, the coming face-to-face with covetousness and the rest' — without another action-path such as killing and the rest, when the coming face-to-face with any one of covetousness and the rest occurs, that volition (<s>cetanā</s>) operates together with one action-path — with either covetousness, malice, or wrong view. 'Or of one with an unafflicted mind' — of one with a wholesome or indeterminate mind. By that instigator's instigation — in the completion of any one of the form-realm [action-paths] of killing and the rest, excluding sexual misconduct — the volition operates together with that one. 'Or of one with an afflicted mind other than covetousness and the rest' should also be stated — for that situation too is possible. 'Of one with a corrupt mind, the killing of a living being' — and so forth in detail. [The volition] operates together with two: with malice and with killing. In sexual misconduct and idle talk, [it] operates together with two. Together with covetousness and sexual misconduct — these two. Together with idle talk and any one of covetousness and the rest — only two. This is questioned: 'of one with a corrupt mind, killing' and 'of one engulfed by covetousness, taking what is not given' — is this said of one who acts oneself, or of one who has another act? If of one who acts oneself, the qualifications 'of one with a corrupt mind' and 'of one engulfed by covetousness' are not fitting — because malice is necessary in killing, and covetousness in taking what is not given. For qualifications are desired where there is variation. If of one who has another act — of one whose mind contains any one of covetousness, malice, or wrong view — in killing, in taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, and idle talk — this should be stated. It is replied: it is said of one who acts oneself. But was it not said that the qualification is not fitting? This is not a fault. For this is not stated as a qualification. Rather, it is a statement of the nature [of the mental state] — it is said that malice and covetousness, being secondary [to the primary motivation], exist therein. Even so, of one whose mind contains any one of covetousness and the rest, for one who has another perform those killing and the rest

body.text: dvābhyāṃ saha cetanā vartata iti saṃbhavet. tasmāt tad api vaktavyaṃ. satyaṃ vaktavyam etat. udāharaṇamātraṃ tv etad uktam ity adoṣaḥ. vyāpannacittasya prāṇimāraṇāpaharaṇe yugapad iti. yatra māraṇenaivāpaharaṇaṃ sidhyati. tatra hi vyāpādaprāṇivadhādattādānakarmapathā yugapat bhavaṃtīti. na tarhīti vistaraḥ. yadi [Tib. 77a] parakīyadravyāpaharaṇakāle vyāpādo bvhavati. na tarhīdānīm adattādānasya lobhenaiva niṣṭhā sidhyatīti. lobhadveṣayor yugapadabhāvāt. ananyacittasyeti vistaraḥ. apaharaṇacittasyaiva tatparisamāptāv adattādānaparisamāptau sa niyamo jñeyaḥ.
body.translated_text: — the volition would operate together with two. Therefore that too should be stated. True, it should be stated. But this is stated merely as an illustration, so there is no fault. 'Of one with a corrupt mind, simultaneously killing and stealing' — where through the very act of killing, stealing is accomplished. For there, the action-paths of malice, killing, and taking what is not given occur simultaneously. 'Then is it not the case' — and so forth in detail. If at the time of stealing another's property there is malice, then taking what is not given is no longer completed by greed alone — because greed and hatred do not exist simultaneously. 'Of one with no other mind' — that restriction should be understood when the mind of stealing alone completes the taking of what is not given.

children.translated_text: 'From greed: approaching another's wife, covetousness, and the completion of taking what is not given' —

body.text: iti. anyacittasya tu māraṇacittasya nāyaṃ niyamaḥ. bhedābhiprāyasyānṛtavacana iti. bhedābhiprāyatvāt tad evānṛtaṃ paiśunyaṃ bhavati. tad eva saṃbhinnapralāpaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. But of one with a different mind — with a mind of killing — this restriction does not apply. 'False speech with the intention of division' — because of the intention of division, that very falsehood becomes slander. That very [speech] is idle talk.

body.text: siddhāṃtāt. evaṃ bhedābhiprāyatvāt tad eva paruṣavacanaṃ paiśunyaṃ. tathaiva ca saṃbhinnapralāpa iti. caturbhiḥ saha vartate. katham ity āha. tatr hi mānasa eko bhavati. vācikās traya iti. anṛtavacane 'bhidhyā vyāpādo vā bhavet. vācikās trayaḥ. mṛṣāvādapaiśunyasaṃbhinnapralāpāḥ. paruṣavacane 'pi mānasa eko vyāpādaḥ. vācikās trayaḥ. pāruṣyapaiśunyasaṃbhinnapralāpāḥ. nāmata evaṃ trayo bhavati. na tu svabhāvataḥ. tad eva hy anṛtavacanaṃ paiśunyaṃ saṃbhinnapralāpa iti cocyate. na tu trayaḥ svabhāvā bhavaṃti. evaṃ paruṣavacanam api trināmakaṃ bhavatīti yojyaṃ. apare punar vyācakṣate. svabhāvabhedo 'py astīti. mṛṣāvādapaiśunyasaṃbhinnapralāpāvijñaptayo hi bhidyaṃte. tathā pāruṣyapaiśunyasaṃbhinnapralāpāvijñaptayo bhidyaṃta iti. [Tib. 77b] abhidhyādigatasyeti vistaraḥ. abhidhyādigatasya vā caturbhiḥ saha vartate. tatra mānasa eko 'bhidhyādīnām anyatamaḥ. tatprayogeṇābhidhyādigataprayogeṇānyakarmapathatrayasya prāṇivadhādikasya niṣṭhāgamane samāptikāle. evaṃ paṃcaṣaṭsaptabhir yojayitavyā. kā. cetanā. kathaṃ. paṃcabhis tāvat vartate. abhidhyādigatasya tatprayogeṇānyacatuṣṭayaniṣṭhāgamane. evam abhidhyādigatasyānyapaṃcaṣaṭniṣṭhāgamane ṣaḍbhiḥ saptabhiś ca saha vartate. aṣṭābhiḥ saha vartate. ṣaṭsu prāṇātipātādiṣu prayogaṃ kṛtvābhidhyāgatasya svayaṃ kāmamithyācāraṃ kurvataḥ samaṃ niṣṭhāgamane. navabhiḥ saha vartata iti nāsty etat. mānasānāṃ karmapathānāṃ
body.translated_text: from the doctrinal position. Thus, because of having the intention of differentiation, that very harsh speech is slander, and likewise idle talk. It co-exists with four [action-paths]. How? He says: therein, one mental [action-path] exists and three vocal ones. In false speech, covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) or malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>) may be present — the three vocal ones are: false speech, slander, and idle talk. In harsh speech too, one mental one — malice — and three vocal ones: harsh speech, slander, and idle talk. These are three in name only, not in own-nature. For that very false speech is called slander and idle talk — but there are not three own-natures. Similarly, harsh speech too should be connected as having three names. Others, however, explain that there is a difference of own-nature too — for the non-informative actions (<s>avijñapti</s>) of false speech, slander, and idle talk are distinct. Likewise, the non-informative actions of harsh speech, slander, and idle talk are distinct. 'Of one engaged in covetousness and the rest' — and so forth in detail. Or [the volition] of one engaged in covetousness and the rest co-exists with four. Therein, one mental one — whichever of covetousness and the rest [is present]. Through the engagement of that — through the engagement in covetousness and the rest — at the completion, at the time of fulfillment, of another three action-paths such as killing of living beings and the like. Similarly, it should be connected with five, six, and seven. Which? Volition (<s>cetanā</s>). How? First, it co-exists with five — at the completion of another four [action-paths] during the engagement of one engaged in covetousness and the rest. Similarly, at the completion of another five, six, and so on for one engaged in covetousness and the rest, it co-exists with six and seven respectively. It co-exists with eight — when one has engaged in the preparatory [stage] of six [action-paths] beginning with killing, and, being engaged in covetousness and the rest, is simultaneously performing sexual misconduct, at the joint completion. It does not co-exist with nine — because of the impossibility of mental action-paths

body.text: yugapadasaṃbhavāt.
body.translated_text: occurring simultaneously.

body.text: iti. naikenaiva mānasena. kuśale cetasya anabhidhyāvyāpādayor avaśyaṃ bhāvāt. nāpi rūpīnaikena saṃvarasaṃgṛhītena karmapathena saha cetanā vartate. kliṣṭāvyākṛtacittāvasthāyām api upāsakasaṃvarādiṣu prāṇātipātādattādānakāmamithyācāramṛṣāvādānām avaśyaṃ sahabhāvāt. na paṃcabhir eva. kuśale cetasy anbhidhyāvyāpādayor dvayor avaśyaṃ sahabhāvāt. saṃvarasaṃgṛhītānāṃ ca prāṇātipātādīnām [Tib. 78a] eṣāṃ caturṇāṃ avaśyaṃ sahabhāvāt. nāṣṭābhir eva. bhikṣusaṃvarasaṃgṛhītānāṃ kāyikavācikānāṃ kliṣṭāvyākṛtāvasthāyāṃ saptānām eva saṃbhavāt. kuśalacittāvasthāyāṃ ca navānāṃ daśānāṃ vā saṃbhavāt. pāriśeṣyāt dvyādibhiḥ saha vartata ity uktaṃ bhavati. tatra dvābhyām iti vistaraḥ. tatra dvābhyāṃ saha vartate. kuśaleṣu paṃcasu vijñāneṣv anabhidhyā cāvyāpādaś ca staḥ na samyagdṛṣṭiḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Not with a single mental [action-path] alone — because in a wholesome mind, non-covetousness (<s>anabhidhyā</s>) and non-malice (<s>avyāpāda</s>) necessarily exist. Nor does a volition co-exist with a single form-based action-path included in restraint — because in the state of afflicted or indeterminate mind too, in the <s>upāsaka</s> restraint and the like, abstentions from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and false speech necessarily co-exist. Not with five alone — because in a wholesome mind, the two — non-covetousness and non-malice — necessarily co-exist; and the four restraint-included [action-paths] of abstention from killing and the rest necessarily co-exist. Not with eight alone — because in the state of afflicted or indeterminate mind, with the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint, only seven [form-based action-paths] are possible; and in the state of wholesome mind, nine or ten are possible. By elimination, it is stated that [volition] co-exists with two and so forth. Therein, with two — and so forth in detail. It co-exists with two — in the five wholesome consciousnesses (sense-consciousnesses), non-covetousness and non-malice exist but not right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) —

children.translated_text: 'The cognition co-arising with the five consciousnesses is not a view, because of non-deliberation' —

body.text: iti siddhāṃtāt. ato 'nabhidhyāvyāpdābhyāṃ dvābhyām evātra saha vartate. ārūpyasamāpattau ca kṣayānutpādajñānayor iti. ārūpyasamāpattisaṃgṛhītayoś ca kṣayānutpādajñānayor ābhyām eva dvābhyāṃ saha vartate.
body.translated_text: because of this doctrinal position. Therefore, here it co-exists with only two — non-covetousness and non-malice. 'And in the formless attainment, of the knowledge of destruction and non-arising' — with the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>) included in the formless attainment, it co-exists with those two alone —

children.translated_text: 'The knowledge of destruction and non-arising is not a view' —

body.text: iti tatra samyagdṛṣṭyabhāvāt. ārūpyasamāpattigrahaṇaṃ dhyānasamāpattisaṃgṛhītayoḥ kṣayānutpādajñānayoḥ saptavidhakāyikavācikānāsravasaṃvarasvabhāvakarmapathanivṛttyarthaṃ. kṣayānutpādajñānagrahaṇaṃ samyagdṛṣṭinirāsārthaṃ. kṣayānutpādajñānayor asamyagdṛṣṭisvabhāvatvāt. tribhiḥ saha vartate. samyagdṛṣṭisaṃprayukte [Tib. 78b] manovijñāne. rūpikarmapathābhāva iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. tatra hy anabhidhyāvyāpādasamyagdṛṣṭaya eva trayaḥ karmapathā bhavaṃtīti. caturbhir iti vistaraḥ. akuśalāvyākṛtacittasyeti viśeṣaṇān mānasā na saṃtīti daśitaṃ bhavati. upāsakaśrāmaṇerasaṃvarasamādāne ca. prāṇātipātādattādānakāmamithyācāramṛṣāvādaviratilakṣaṇāś catvāra eva karmapathāḥ saṃti. madyapānādiviratīnāṃ daśakarmapathānaṃtarbhāvāt. paiśunyaviratyādīnāṃ copāsakaśrāmaṇerasaṃvarasaṃgrahāt. śrāmaṇerasaṃvarasamādānavacanāc copavāsasaṃvarasamādānam uktarūpam avagaṃtavyaṃ. śrāmaṇerasaṃvarasamādāne tv abrahmacaryād viratis tṛtīyaḥ karmapathaḥ. tatra ca kāmamithyācāro 'ṃtarbhūta eva. ṣaḍbhiḥ kuśaleṣu paṃcasu vijñāneṣu tatsamādāne. upāsakaśrāmaṇerasaṃvarasamādāne taiś caturbhir yathoktair
body.translated_text: because of the absence of right view therein. The mention of formless attainment is for the purpose of excluding the seven bodily and vocal outflow-free restraint action-paths that are included in <s>dhyāna</s> attainment when the knowledge of destruction and non-arising [occurs therein]. The mention of knowledge of destruction and non-arising is for the purpose of excluding right view — because the knowledge of destruction and non-arising does not have the nature of right view. It co-exists with three — in the mental consciousness associated with right view, in the absence of form-based action-paths — this is the completion of the sentence. For therein, only the three action-paths of non-covetousness, non-malice, and right view exist. 'With four' — and so forth in detail. The qualification 'of one with unwholesome or indeterminate mind' shows that mental [action-paths] are absent. And in the undertaking of the <s>upāsaka</s> and <s>śrāmaṇera</s> restraint, only four action-paths exist — abstentions from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and false speech — because abstention from intoxicants and the like is not included within the ten action-paths; and because abstentions from slander and the rest are not included in the <s>upāsaka</s> and <s>śrāmaṇera</s> restraint. And from the statement of <s>śrāmaṇera</s> restraint undertaking, the fasting restraint (<s>upavāsasaṃvara</s>) undertaking should also be understood as being of the same type. But in the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> restraint undertaking, abstention from unchastity (<s>abrahmacaryā</s>) is the third action-path — and sexual misconduct is included within that. With six — in the five wholesome consciousnesses, at the time of that [restraint] undertaking: in the <s>upāsaka</s> and <s>śrāmaṇera</s> restraint undertaking, with those four as stated

body.text: anabhidhyāvyāpādābhyāṃ ceti ṣaḍbhiḥ. paṃcasu vijñāneṣu samyagdṛṣṭyabhāvāt. saptabhiḥ kuśale manovijñāne tadsamādāna eva. upāsakaśrāmaṇerasaṃvarasamādāna eva tair eva yathoktaiḥ samyagdṛṣṭyā ca saptamena karmapathena. manovijñāne hi kuśale samyagdṛṣṭir [Tib. 79a] astīti. akuśalāvyākṛtacittasya ca bhikṣusaṃvarasamādāne saptabhir eva rūpibhiḥ. na mānasaiḥ. akuśalāvyākṛtacittatvāt. navabhiḥ kuśaleṣu paṃcasu vijñāneṣu tatsamādāne. bhikṣusaṃvarasamādāne. samyagdṛṣṭer evābhāvāt. kṣayānutpādajnānasaṃprayukte ca manovijñāne tair eva navabhiḥ saha vartate. tatrāpi samyagdṛṣṭyabhāvāt. tasminn eva ceti. kṣayānutpādajñānasaṃprayukta eva dhyānasaṃgṛhīte manovijñāne. navabhir eva. dhyānasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītai rūpibhiḥ saptabhir anabhidhyāvyāpādābhyāṃ ca. daśabhis tato 'nyatreti. kṣayānutpādajñānavarjite kuśale manovijñāne bhikṣusaṃvarasamādāna eva. sarvā ceti vistaraḥ. sarvā ca dhyānānāsravasaṃvarasahavartinī kṣayānutpādajñānasaṃprayuktā cetanā saptabhiḥ kāyikavācikair dhyānānāsravasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaiḥ. tribhiś ca mānasair iti. daśabhiḥ saha vartate. saṃvarasaṃgṛhītaiḥ karmapathaiḥ sahaiva cetanā [Tib. 79b] vartata iti darśitaṃ.
body.translated_text: and with non-covetousness and non-malice — [making] six. Because right view does not exist in the five consciousnesses. With seven — in the wholesome mental consciousness, at the time of that very [restraint] undertaking: in the <s>upāsaka</s> and <s>śrāmaṇera</s> restraint undertaking alone, with those very [four] as stated and with right view as the seventh action-path — because right view exists in the wholesome mental consciousness. And for one with afflicted or indeterminate mind, in the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint undertaking, with seven form-based [action-paths] alone — not mental ones, because of having afflicted or indeterminate mind. With nine — in the five wholesome consciousnesses, at the time of that [<s>bhikṣu</s> restraint] undertaking: in the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint undertaking — because of the absence of right view alone. And in the mental consciousness associated with the knowledge of destruction and non-arising, it co-exists with those very nine — because of the absence of right view therein too. 'And in that very' — in the mental consciousness included in <s>dhyāna</s>, associated with the knowledge of destruction and non-arising alone — with nine only: seven form-based [action-paths] included in the <s>dhyāna</s> restraint, and non-covetousness and non-malice. With ten — 'elsewhere than that' — in the wholesome mental consciousness excluding that associated with the knowledge of destruction and non-arising, in the <s>bhikṣu</s> restraint undertaking alone. 'And all' — and so forth in detail. All volition co-existing with the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraint, associated with the knowledge of destruction and non-arising, [co-exists] with seven bodily and vocal [action-paths] included in the <s>dhyāna</s> and outflow-free restraint, and three mental ones — [making] ten. It has been shown that volition co-exists only with action-paths included in restraint.

body.text: saṃvaranirmuktena tv aṣṭavidhasaṃvaranirmuktena tv ekenāpi saha syāt. katham ity āha. anyacittasyeti. tatsaṃvaranirmuktanirmuktakuśalakarmapathasamutthāpakāc cittād anyacittasya. kliṣṭāvyākṛtacittasyety arthaḥ. ekāṃgaviratisamādāne. prāṇātipātāṃgavirateḥ. adattādānavirater vā samādāne. tenaikena karmapathena saha vartate. paṃcāṣṭabhir apīti. kuśalamanovijñānasya pudgalasya dvyaṃgasamādāne yugapan mānasais tribhiḥ. rūpibhyāṃ dvābhyām iti paṃcabhiḥ. paṃcāṃgasamādāne yugapat taiś ca rūpibhiḥ paṃcabhiḥ. mānasaiś ca tribhir ity aṣṭābhiḥ. udāharaṇarūpaṃ caitad uktam. ato 'nyathāpi śakyate vaktum. kliṣṭāvyākṛtacittasya saṃvarāsaṃgṛhītapaṃcāṃgasamādāne paṃcabhiḥ saha vartata iti.
body.translated_text: But with [action-paths] free from restraint — free from the eightfold restraint — it may co-exist even with a single one. How? He says: 'Of one with a different mind' — of one whose mind is different from the mind that originates that wholesome action-path free from [the eightfold] restraint — meaning: of one with afflicted or indeterminate mind. In the undertaking of a single component of abstention — abstention from killing alone, or the undertaking of abstention from stealing alone — it co-exists with that single action-path. 'Even with five or eight' — for a person with wholesome mental consciousness, in the undertaking of two components: simultaneously with three mental [action-paths] and two form-based ones — [making] five. In the undertaking of five components: simultaneously with those and five form-based ones, and three mental ones — [making] eight. And this is stated by way of example — it can also be stated otherwise: for one with afflicted or indeterminate mind, in the undertaking of five components not included in restraint, it co-exists with five.

body.text: (IV.83, 85) raṃjanīyavastvabhāvād iti. narake raṃjanīyavastvabhāvāt na saṃmukhībhāvato 'bhidhyāsti. karmaphalapratyakṣatvāc ca na mithyādṛṣṭiḥ. ata eveti. prayojanābhāvān na paiśunyaṃ. nityabhinnatvāc cānyonyasauhārdyādyabhāvataḥ. amamaparigrahatvān na kurau [Tib. 80a] saṃmukhībhāvato 'sty abhidhyākarmapathaḥ. snigdhasaṃtānatvād āghātavastvabhāvāc ca na vyāpādaḥ. apāpāśayatvāc ca na mithyādṛṣṭiḥ. trayo 'py ete 'bhidhyādayo na saṃti.
body.translated_text: (IV.83, 85) 'Because of the absence of desirable objects' — because of the absence of desirable objects in the hells, covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) does not exist as a face-to-face [action-path]. And because the fruits of <s>karma</s> are directly perceived [there], wrong view does not exist. For this very reason — because of the absence of purpose, slander does not exist; and because of being always divided, because of the absence of mutual affection and the like [among hell-beings]. 'In <s>Uttarakuru</s>' — because of being without a sense of 'mine' and possessiveness, covetousness as a face-to-face action-path does not exist there. Because of having a kindly continuum and because of the absence of objects of resentment, malice does not exist. And because of having a sinless disposition, wrong view does not exist. These three — covetousness and the rest — do not exist [there].

body.text: asya saṃmukhībhāvata iti vyākhyānaṃ. apāpāśayatvān na prāṇātipātādayaḥ ṣaḍ api saṃmukhībhāvataḥ saṃti. niyatāyuṣkatvān na prāṇātipātaḥ dravyastṛiparigrahābhāvād yathākramaṃ nādattādānaṃ kāmamithyācāraś ca. prayojanabhāvāc ca na mṛṣāvādapaiśunyapāruṣyāṇi.
body.translated_text: this is the explanation of its face-to-face [operation]. Because of their sinless disposition, the six [action-paths] beginning with killing do not exist as face-to-face [operations]. 'Because of having a fixed lifespan' — killing does not exist. 'Because of the absence of personal possession of material goods' — taking what is not given and sexual misconduct respectively do not exist. And because of the absence of purpose — false speech, slander, and harsh speech do not exist.

body.text: yadi parigraho nāsti katham eṣām abrahmacaryam iti pṛcchati.
body.translated_text: 'If there is no possession, how is their unchastity [explained]?' — this is his question.

body.text: saṃvaranirmuktā iti. naivasaṃvaranāsaṃvarasaṃgṛhītā ity arthaḥ. anyagatisthaṃ tu mārayatīti. pretādigatisthaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Free from restraint' — meaning: included in neither-restraint-nor-non-restraint. 'But one kills one established in another destiny' — one established in the destiny of hungry ghosts (<s>preta</s>) and the like.

body.text: devā api śiromadhyacchedān mriyaṃta iti. śiraśchedān madhyacchedāc ca devā api mriyaṃte. devo devaṃ na mārayatīty ukte avadhyā devā ity abhipretaṃ. devānāṃ hy aṃgapratyaṃgāni chinnāni chinnāni punar jāyaṃte. yady apy evaṃ tathāpi śiromadhyacchedāc chiraśchedān madhyacchedāc ca na punaḥ pratisaṃdhānam ity asti devānām vadha ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Gods too die from the severing of head or middle' — gods too die from the severing of the head or the severing of the middle. When it is said 'a god does not kill a god,' the intent is that gods are [normally] unkillable. For the limbs and minor limbs of gods, when severed, grow back again. Even though this is so, still, from the severing of the head or middle, there is no regrowth — therefore the killing of gods is possible — this is the intent.

body.text: yadbhūmyāśrayam iti vistaraḥ. paṃca bhūmayaḥ. yāvāc caturthadhyānabhūmiṃ. yadbhūmir āśrayo 'syeti yadbhūmyāśrayam. anāsravaṃ śīlam āryeṇotpāditaṃ [Tib. 80b] nirodhitam. utpāditaṃ vartamānam adhvānaṃ gamitaṃ. nirodhitam atītam adhvānaṃ gamitam. ekabhūmyāśrayaṃ yāvac caturbhūmyāśrayaṃ vā. tenārūpyeṣv atītena samanvāgato bhavati. paṃcabhūmyāśrayeṇa tv anāgatena. kāmāvacarāśrayeṇa yāvac caturthadhyānāśrayeṇa ca. yatropapanno yatra vā nopapannaḥ. tadāśrayeṇa. anyatra narakottarakurubhya iti. tatra samādānaśīlābhāvāt. anyatrobhayatheti. anyatra kāmadhātau deveṣūttarakuruvarjyeṣu ca manuṣyeṣūbhayathā. saṃvaranirmuktāḥ saṃvarasaṃgṛhītaś ca. trividhaḥ saṃvaraḥ prātimokṣasaṃvaro dhyānasaṃvaro 'nāsravasaṃvaraś ca yathāsaṃbhavaṃ grahītavyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'That whose basis belongs to which ground' — and so forth in detail. There are five grounds — up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground. That whose basis belongs to which ground — [hence] 'having a basis of that ground.' Outflow-free morality, produced and ceased by a noble one (<s>ārya</s>) — 'produced' means brought into the present time-period; 'ceased' means brought into the past time-period — having a basis of one ground up to four grounds. Therefore in the formless [realms], one is endowed with [morality] that is past. Having a basis of five grounds, however, [is the case] for the future — having a basis of the Desire Realm up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. Whether reborn there or not reborn there — having that basis. 'Except for the hells and <s>Uttarakuru</s>' — because of the absence of morality of undertaking (<s>samādānaśīla</s>) there. 'Elsewhere, in both ways' — elsewhere in the Desire Realm, among gods and among humans excluding <s>Uttarakuru</s>, in both ways: free from restraint and included in restraint. The threefold restraint — <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint, <s>dhyāna</s> restraint, and outflow-free restraint — should be understood as applicable.

body.text: (IV.86) āsevitabhāvitabahulīkṛtair iti. prayogamaulapṛṣṭhāvasthāsu. kiṃ tarhi. tenālpāyur bhavatīti. āyuṣo 'lpatvān niṣyandaphalam iti darśayati. bāhyā bhāvāḥ. oṣadhibhūmyādayaḥ. alpaujaso 'lpavīryaḥ. aśanirajobahulā iti. aśaniḥ śilāvarṣaṃ. rajo dhūlivṛṣṭiḥ kṣāravṛṣṭir vā. yataḥ sasyādivināśaḥ. rajo'vakīrṇā iti dhūlir utthitā. utkūlanikālāḥ unnatanimnāḥ. ūṣarajaṃgalāḥ. ūṣarāś ca jaṃgalāś ca te. bāhyā bhāvā ity adhikṛtāḥ. tā bhūmaya ihābhipretāḥ. pratikruṣṭā vigarhitāḥ. viṣamartupariṇāmā iti viṣama ṛtupariṇāma eṣām iti viṣamartupariṇāmāḥ [tib 81a] sasyādaya oṣadhayaḥ. yasmin ṛtau varṣitavyaṃ. tatra na varṣati. yasmiṃ śītena bhavitavyaṃ. tasmin na śītaṃ. yasminn uṣṇena bhavitavyaṃ. tatra tan na bhavatīti yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: (IV.86) 'When practiced, cultivated, and multiplied' — in the stages of preparatory, root, and subsequent [actions]. What then? 'By that one becomes short-lived' — he shows that the shortness of lifespan is an outflow result (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>). 'External things' — herbs, lands, and the like. 'Of little vitality, of little potency.' 'Abounding in thunderbolts and dust' — thunderbolts mean showers of stones; dust means dust-storms or alkali-rain, by which crops and the like are destroyed. 'Covered with dust' — dust has risen. 'Hilly and uneven' — elevated and low-lying. 'Saline and arid' (<s>ūṣarajaṃgala</s>) — both saline and arid. These are 'external things' as the topic. Those lands are what is intended here. 'Despised' means reviled. 'Of irregular seasonal change' — those whose seasonal changes are irregular — crops, herbs, and the like. In the season when it should rain, it does not rain; when it should be cold, it is not cold; when it should be hot, it is not hot — this should be connected.

body.text: tad vipākaphalam iti sattvasaṃtāne. idaṃ niṣyandaphalam iti bāhyaṃ
body.translated_text: 'That is maturation result' — in the continuum of a being. 'This is outflow result' — external

body.text: tad vastv iti. na tad vipākaphalaṃ.
body.translated_text: that thing — it is not maturation result.

body.text: tatra prayogeṇeti vistaraḥ. narake prāṇātipātaprayogeṇa tīvraṃ duḥkham anubhavati. prāṇātipātaprayogeṇa hi vadhyasya prāṇino 'tīvatīvraṃ duḥkhaṃ bhavati. iha maulenālpāyur bhavati. yathā tasya vadhyasya prāṇina āyur upadrūyata iti. tādṛśam evaitat. kṣaṇiko hi maulaḥ karmapathaḥ. tatra ca na duḥkhā vedanāstīti yuktam iha mauleneti vaktuṃ. āha. yadi tatra prayogeṇeha maulena. kasmād evam uktaṃ. prāṇātipātenāsevitena bhāvitena bahulīkṛtena narakeṣūpapadyate. prāṇātipātena mauleneti sūtrārthaṃ paśyann evaṃ pṛcchati. saparivāragrahaṇād iti. maula eva prāṇātipātaḥ. tasya prayogaḥ parivāraḥ. tasmiṃ prayoge prāṇātipātopacāraṃ kṛtvaivam uktaṃ prāṇātipāteneti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: 'By the preparatory [stage] therein' — and so forth in detail. In the hells, through the preparatory stage of killing, one experiences intense suffering — for through the preparatory stage of killing, extremely intense suffering occurs for the living being to be slain. 'Here, through the root [action-path], one becomes short-lived' — just as the lifespan of the living being to be slain is damaged, exactly so is this. For the root action-path is momentary, and therein there is no painful feeling — therefore it is fitting to say 'here, through the root [action-path].' He asks: if through the preparatory [stage] there, and through the root [action-path] here, then why is this said: 'Through killing, when practiced, cultivated, and multiplied, one is reborn in the hells'? He asks this seeing the <s>sūtra</s> meaning as 'through killing' meaning 'through the root [action-path].' 'Because of the inclusive mention' (<s>saparivāragrahaṇa</s>) — the root itself is killing; its preparatory [stage] is its retinue (<s>parivāra</s>). Having figuratively applied [the term] 'killing' to that preparatory [stage], it was stated thus: 'through killing' — and so forth in detail.

body.text: naitad dvayam ativartate. vipākaphalam adhipatiphalaṃ ceti. svasaṃtāne vipākaphalam anyatrādhipatiphalam iti kṛtvā. sādṛśyaviśeṣat tu tathoktam iti. iṣṭajīvitopacchedabhogavyasanādilakṣaṇāt [Tib. 81b] sādṛśyaviśeṣāt tu tathoktaṃ. saced itthaṃtvam āgacchati manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāṃ prāṇātipātenālpāyur bhavaty adattādānena bhogavyasanī bhavatīti vistareṇa. bhavati hy atra hetuvipākaphalayoḥ sādṛśam iti. evaṃ kuśaleṣv api vaktavyaṃ. niṣyandaphalaṃ phaladvayaṃ nātivartate. sādṛśyaviśeṣāt tu tathoktaṃ. saced itthaṃtvam āgacchati manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāṃ prāṇātipātaviratyā dīrghāyur bhavatīti vistareṇa.
body.translated_text: 'It does not go beyond these two — maturation result and dominant result (<s>adhipatiphala</s>)' — considering that in one's own continuum it is maturation result and elsewhere it is dominant result. 'But it is so called because of a special resemblance' — because of a special resemblance characterized by the cutting off of desired life, loss of possessions, and the like. 'If one attains the state of becoming a human' — meaning: attaining the common existence (<s>sabhāgatā</s>) of humans — 'through killing, one becomes short-lived; through taking what is not given, one suffers loss of possessions' — and so forth in detail. For there is indeed a resemblance between cause and maturation result. Similarly, it should be stated for the wholesome too. The outflow result does not go beyond the two results — but it is so called because of a special resemblance. 'If one attains the state of becoming a human' — 'through refraining from killing, one becomes long-lived' — and so forth in detail.

body.text: iti. ojo hṛdayapradeśe bhavati. evam anyeṣām api yojyam iti. adattādānaṃ hi kurvatā dravyasvāmino duḥkham utpāditaṃ. bhogavyasanaṃ kṛtaṃ. ojo nāśitam. ato 'sya duḥkhanād bhogatyājanād ojonāśanāc ca trividhaṃ phalaṃ. katham ojo nāśitaṃ. taddhetunāśanāt. bhogavyasanena ca tasyopaghātāt. ata evoktaṃ. adattādānenāśanirajobahulā iti. tena tadojasaḥ sopaghātatā bhavatīti. evaṃ paradāram abhigacchatā parasya duḥkham utpāditaṃ. sa sapatnadāratā kṛtā. ojo nāśitaṃ. yenaujasā tejasvīti loke nirucyate. ata evoktaṃ. kāmamithyācāreṇa rajo'vakīrṇā iti. evam anyeṣām api yojyam. eṣā dik.
body.translated_text: thus. Vitality (<s>ojas</s>) exists in the region of the heart. 'Similarly for the others too, it should be connected' — for one who takes what is not given has caused suffering to the owner of the property, has brought about loss of possessions, and has destroyed vitality. Therefore, from that causing of suffering, that depriving of possessions, and that destruction of vitality, there is a threefold fruit. How is vitality destroyed? Through the destruction of its cause, and through the damage to it by loss of possessions. For this very reason it was stated: 'through taking what is not given, [the lands become] abounding in thunderbolts and dust' — because thereby, the vitality of those [lands] becomes damaged. Similarly, by one who approaches another's spouse, suffering is caused to the other, he is made to have a rival's wife, and vitality is destroyed — the vitality by which one is called 'brilliant' in the world. For this very reason it was stated: 'through sexual misconduct, [the lands become] covered with dust.' Similarly for the others too, it should be connected. This is the direction [of explanation].

body.text: akuśalaviparyayeṇa sarvaṃ yojayitavyam iti. kathaṃ. adattādānaviratyāsevitayā [Tib. 82a] bhāvitayā bahulīkṛtayā deveṣūpapadyate. saced itthaṃtvam āgacchati manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāṃ sa na bhogavyasanī bhavatīti. evaṃ kāmamithyācāraviratyāsevitayā bhāvitayeti vistareṇoktvā. yāvan manuṣyāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: 'Everything should be connected by the reverse of the unwholesome' — how? 'Through refraining from taking what is not given, when practiced, cultivated, and multiplied, one is reborn among the gods. If one attains the state of becoming a human, one does not suffer loss of possessions.' Thus, having stated in detail 'through refraining from sexual misconduct, when practiced and cultivated,' up to: 'attaining the common existence of humans, one does not become one prone to false accusation.' Everything should be connected in this direction.
