By one who refrains from killing, suffering is not caused to the other, [the other] is not killed, and vitality is not destroyed — therefore there is a threefold fruit. Similarly, by one who refrains from taking what is not given, suffering is not caused to the owner of the property, loss of possessions is not brought about, and vitality is not destroyed — therefore there is a threefold fruit. By one who refrains from sexual misconduct, suffering is not caused to the other, he is not made to have a rival's wife, and vitality is not destroyed — therefore there is a threefold fruit. Similarly in other cases too, it should be connected.

body.text: sabhāgatāṃ nābhyākhyānabahulo bhavatīti. anayā diśā sarvaṃ yojayitavyaṃ. prāṇātipātād viramatā parasya duḥkhaṃ notpāditaṃ. na māritaḥ. naujo nāśitam. ity atas trividhaṃ phalaṃ. evam adattādānāt prativiramatā nārthasvāmino duḥkham utpāditaṃ. na bhogavyasanaṃ kṛtaṃ. naujo nāśitam. ato 'sya trividhaṃ phalaṃ. kāmamithyācārād viramatā parasya duḥkhaṃ notpāditaṃ. na sa sapatnadāraḥ kṛtaḥ. nāpy ojo nāśitam. ato 'sya trividhaṃ phalaṃ. evam anyatrāpi yojayitavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: '[does not destroy] the share [of others]' — he does not become one abounding in false accusation. Everything should be connected in this direction. By one who refrains from killing, suffering is not caused to the other, [the other] is not killed, and vitality (<s>ojas</s>) is not destroyed. Therefore there is a threefold fruit. Similarly, by one who refrains from taking what is not given, suffering is not caused to the owner of the property, loss of possessions is not brought about, and vitality is not destroyed. Therefore there is a threefold fruit for that. By one who refrains from sexual misconduct, suffering is not caused to the other, he is not made to have a rival's wife, and vitality is not destroyed. Therefore there is a threefold fruit for that. Similarly in other cases too, it should be connected.

body.text: kautukamaṃgalatithimuhūrtanakṣatrādidṛṣṭinā.
body.translated_text: One who holds views regarding auspicious signs, festive occasions, auspicious times, moments, asterisms, and the like.

body.text: kāyasthitihetavaś cīvarapiṇḍapātāśayanāsanādayo bhikṣoḥ parapratibhaddhāḥ. piṇḍapātaṃ niśrityeti vacanāt. tasya paradhīnavṛtter
body.translated_text: the causes for sustaining the body — robes, almsfood, lodging, and the like — are dependent on others for a <s>bhikṣu</s>. Because of the statement: 'dependent on almsfood.' For one whose livelihood depends on others,

body.text: mithyājīvā bhaveyuḥ kuhanā. lapanā. naimittikatā. naiṣpeṣitā. lābhena lābhaniścikīrṣā ca. te
body.translated_text: wrong livelihoods may arise: <s>kuhanā</s> (hypocrisy), <s>lapanā</s> (flattery), <s>naimittikatā</s> (hinting), <s>naiṣpeṣitā</s> (belittling), and the desire to obtain gain through gain (<s>lābhena lābhaniścikīrṣā</s>). These

body.text: bhavaṃti ājīvayogā iti.
body.translated_text: the practices of livelihood.

body.text: śīlaskaṃdhikāyām iti. śīlaskaṃdhikā nāma nipātaḥ. tatroktaṃ. yathā tridaṇḍinn eke śramaṇabrāhmaṇāḥ śraddhādeyaṃ paribhujya vividhadarśanasamāraṃbhānuyogam anuyuktā viharaṃti. tadyathā. hastiyuddhe. 'śvayuddhe. rathayuddhe. pattiyuddhe. yaṣṭiyuddhe. muṣṭiyuddhe. sārasayuddhe. vṛṣabhayuddhe. mahiṣayuddhe. ajayuddhe. meṣayuddhe. kukkuṭayuddhe. vartakayuddhe. lābakayuddhe. strīyuddhe. puruṣayuddhe. kumārayuddhe. kumārikāyuddhe. iṭgālavaśe. utsatikāyāṃ. dhvajāgre. balāgre. [Tib. 82b] senāvyūhe. anīkasaṃkarśaṇe. mahāsamājaṃ vā pratyanubhavanty eke. ity apy evaṃrūpāc chramaṇo vividhadarśanasamāraṃbhānuyogāt prativirato bhavati. yathāpi tatra tridaṇḍinn eke śramaṇabrāhmaṇāḥ śraddhādeyaṃ paribhujya vividhaśabdaśravaṇasamāraṃbhānuyogayuktā viharaṃti. tadyathā. hastiśabde. aśvaśabde. rathaśabde. pattiśabde. śaṃkhaśabde. bherīśabde. āḍaṃbaraśabde. nṛttaśabde. gītaśabde. śayyāśabde. acchaṭāśabde. pāṇisvare
body.translated_text: 'In the <s>Śīlaskandha</s> section' — the <s>Śīlaskandhikā</s> is the name of a chapter. Therein it is stated: 'Just as some <s>śramaṇa</s>s and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s who carry the triple staff, having consumed what was given in faith, live engaged in the pursuit of various spectacles — namely: elephant fights, horse fights, chariot fights, infantry fights, staff fights, fist fights, wrestling matches, bull fights, buffalo fights, goat fights, ram fights, rooster fights, quail fights, partridge fights, women's contests, men's contests, boys' contests, girls' contests, in <s>iṭgāla</s> [ball games], in <s>utsatikā</s> [acrobatics], at the tops of banners, at the head of armies, in military arrays, in troop inspections — or some experience great assemblies — the <s>śramaṇa</s> abstains from such pursuit of various spectacles. Just as therein some <s>śramaṇa</s>s and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s who carry the triple staff, having consumed what was given in faith, live engaged in the pursuit of hearing various sounds — namely: the sound of elephants, the sound of horses, the sound of chariots, the sound of infantry, the sound of conches, the sound of drums, the sound of kettledrums, the sound of dancing, the sound of singing, the sound of cymbals, the sound of hand-clapping, the sound of hand-drums

body.text: . kuṃbhatūṇīre kacite. citrākṣare. citrapadavyaṃjane. lokāyatapratisaṃyukte. ākhyāyikā vā śrotum icchanty eke. ity apy evaṃrūpāc chramaṇo vividhaśabdaśravaṇasamāraṃbhānuyogāt prativirato bhavatīty evamādi. mithyāviṣayaparibhogād asamyagviṣayaparibhogāt.
body.translated_text: , the sound of tumbling drums, in embroidered [compositions], in ornate syllables, in ornate sentences, in what is connected with the <s>Lokāyata</s> [materialist philosophy] — or some wish to hear stories — the <s>śramaṇa</s> abstains from such pursuit of hearing various sounds' — and so forth. 'From the enjoyment of wrong objects' — from the enjoyment of improper objects.

body.text: (IV.88, 89) yāni pūrvaṃ paṃca phalāny uktānīti. adhipatiphalaṃ. puruṣakāraphalaṃ. niṣyandaphalaṃ. vipākaphalaṃ. visaṃyogaphalaṃ ca. prahāṇārthaṃ mārga iti. bhāvasādhanaṃ. prahāṇāya mārgaḥ
body.translated_text: (IV.88, 89) 'The five fruits that were previously stated' — the dominant result (<s>adhipatiphala</s>), the human-effort result (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>), the outflow result (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>), the maturation result (<s>vipākaphala</s>), and the separation result (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>). 'The path is for abandonment' (<s>prahāṇārtham</s>) — this is a <s>bhāva</s> derivation. The path for abandonment —

body.text: iti. prahīyate 'neneti karaṇasādhanaṃ. prahāṇo mārga iti ca vigrahaḥ. samādhijā uttare sadṛśā dharmā iti. samādhijagrahaṇam asamādhijanirāsārtham. sadṛśagrahaṇam [Tib. 83a] anāsravāvyākṛtanirāsārthaṃ. sahabhuva iti. saṃprayuktāś ca tatra vedanādayaḥ. viprayuktāś ca jātyādayaḥ. yac cānāgataṃ bhāvyata iti. anāgato dharmas tadbalena prāpyata iti. tasya tat puruṣakāraphalam ata eva tac ca prahāṇaṃ puruṣakāraphalaṃ vyavasthāpyate. na kevalaṃ visaṃyogaphalam iti. pūrvotpannavarjyā iti pūrvotpannaṃ phalaṃ na yujyata iti kṛtvā. tathā hy uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus: 'that by which one abandons' — this is an instrument derivation. 'The path that is abandonment' — is also the grammatical analysis. '<s>Dharma</s>s born of concentration, subsequent, and similar' — the mention of 'born of concentration' is for the purpose of excluding those not born of concentration. The mention of 'similar' is for the purpose of excluding uncontaminated indeterminate [<s>dharma</s>s]. 'Co-existent' (<s>sahabhu</s>) — associated [<s>dharma</s>s] such as feeling and the rest therein, and dissociated [<s>dharma</s>s] such as birth (<s>jāti</s>) and the rest. 'And what future [<s>dharma</s>] is cultivated' — the future <s>dharma</s> that is obtained through the power of that. That is its human-effort result. For this very reason, that abandonment too is established as human-effort result — not merely separation result. 'Excluding the previously arisen' — considering that a previously arisen [result] is not fitting as a fruit. For thus it was stated:

children.translated_text: 'The fruit of a dominant [cause] is only unpreceded, conditioned, and of a conditioned [cause]' —

body.text: iti. vipākaphalaṃ hitveti. anāsravasyāvipākatvāt. tasya hi niṣyandaphalaṃ samādhijā uttare sadṛśā dharmāḥ. visaṃyogaphalaṃ visaṃyoga eva yat tat prahāṇaṃ. puruṣakāraphalaṃ tadākṛṣṭā dharmāḥ. tadyathā vimuktimārgaḥ. sahabhuvaḥ. yac cānāgataṃ bhāvyate. tac ca prahāṇaṃ. adhipatiphalaṃ svabhāvād anye sarve saṃskrtāḥ pūrvotpannavarjyāḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Excluding the maturation result' — because the uncontaminated does not produce maturation. For its outflow result is: <s>dharma</s>s born of concentration, subsequent, and similar. Its separation result is separation itself — that which is abandonment. Its human-effort result is: <s>dharma</s>s drawn forth by it — such as the liberation path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>), the co-existent [<s>dharma</s>s], and the future [<s>dharma</s>] that is cultivated, and also that abandonment. Its dominant result is all other conditioned [<s>dharma</s>s] excluding the previously arisen, other than its own nature.

body.text: iti. prahāṇamārgād yad anyasāsravaṃ karma samāhitam asamāhitaṃ ca. tad api caturbhiḥ phalaiḥ saphalaṃ visaṃyogaphalaṃ hitvā. aprahāṇamārgatvād asya visaṃyogaphalaṃ nāsti. tasya hi vipākaphalaṃ svabhūmāv iṣṭo 'niṣṭo vā vipākaḥ. [Tib. 83b] niṣyandaphalaṃ uttare sadṛśā dharmāḥ. puruṣakāraphalaṃ tadākṛṣṭā dharmāḥ sahabhuvo 'naṃtarabhuvo vā. adhipatiphalaṃ śeṣaṃ pūrvavat.
body.translated_text: thus. Contaminated <s>karma</s>, whether concentrated or non-concentrated, that is other than the path of abandonment — that too is fruitful with four results, excluding the separation result. Because of not being a path of abandonment, it has no separation result. For its maturation result is: the desirable or undesirable maturation in its own ground. Its outflow result is: subsequent similar <s>dharma</s>s. Its human-effort result is: <s>dharma</s>s drawn forth by it, whether co-existent or immediately subsequent. Its dominant result is the remainder, as before.

body.text: iti. śeṣagrahaṇaṃ prahāṇamārganirāsārthaṃ. tat punaḥ kathaṃ. śeṣaṃ prayogavimuktiviśeṣamārgeṣu. tasyāprahāṇamārgatvād visaṃyogaphalaṃ nāsti.
body.translated_text: thus. The mention of 'remaining' is for the purpose of excluding the path of abandonment. What then is the remaining? In the stages of the preparatory path (<s>prayoga</s>), liberation path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>), and special path (<s>viśeṣamārga</s>). Because of not being a path of abandonment, it has no separation result.

body.text: anāsravatvāc ca na vipākaphalaṃ. śeṣaṃ pūrvavat. avyākṛtaṃ ca yan nivṛtāvyākṛtam anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ ca. tad api tribhiḥ saphalaṃ. saprahāṇamārgatvān na tasya visaṃyogaphalam. avyākṛtatvāc ca na vipākaphalaṃ. śeṣaṃ pūrvavad evāsti.
body.translated_text: And because of being uncontaminated, it has no maturation result. The remainder is as before. And the indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) — both obstructed-indeterminate and unobstructed-indeterminate — that too is fruitful with three [results]. Because of not being a path of abandonment, it has no separation result. And because of being indeterminate, it has no maturation result. The remainder exists as before.

children.translated_text: 'Four, two, and likewise three for the wholesome' —

body.text: yathākramam etat. kathaṃ. kuśalasya kuśalā dharmāś catvāri phalāni. tasyaivākuśalā dve phale. tasyaivāvyākṛtās trīṇi phalānīti. vipākaphalaṃ hitveti. vipākasyāvyākṛtvāt. akuśalā dve iti. purūṣakārādhipatiphale. na niṣyandaphalaṃ. yasmāt kuśalā dharmā akuśalānāṃ na sabhāgahetur iti. na vipākaphalaṃ. avyākṛtatvād vipākasya. yasmāc cākuśalā vipākaṃ prati vyākriyaṃte. na visaṃyogaphalaṃ. akuśalatvāt. [Tib. 84a] pāriśeṣyāt puruṣakārādhipatiphale eva. te ca pūrvavad vyākhyātavye. avyākṛtāś catvārīti. katham akuśalasyāvyākṛtā dharmā niṣyandaphalaṃ. kathaṃ ca na bhavitavyaṃ. visadṛśatvāt. visadṛśā hy akuśālayākṛtā dharmāḥ. savipākāvipākatvāt. naiṣa doṣaḥ. akūśalanivṛtāvyākṛtānāṃ hi dharmāṇāṃ kliṣṭasāmānyenāsti sādṛśyaṃ. tasmād akuśalānāṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtāḥ nivṛtāvyākṛtānāṃ cākuśalāḥ niṣyandaphalaṃ yujyaṃte. tenāha. avyākṛte hīti vistaraḥ. akuśalānāṃ sarvatragāṇāṃ duḥkhasamudayadarśanaprahātavyānāṃ. duḥkhadarśanaheyānāṃ ca rāgādīnāṃ. satkāyāntagrāhadṛṣṭī niṣyandaphalaṃ. sabhāgasarvatragayor niṣyandaphalam iti. akuśalā hīti vistaraḥ. akuśalā duḥkhādidarśanaheyāḥ paṃcanaikāyikāḥ. avyākṛtayoḥ satkāyāṃtagrāhadṛṣṭyoḥ niṣyandaphalaṃ. etāny eva trīṇi vipākavisaṃyogaphale hitvā.
body.translated_text: This is in sequence. How? For wholesome [<s>dharma</s>s], wholesome <s>dharma</s>s [constitute] four fruits. For that very [wholesome], unwholesome [<s>dharma</s>s constitute] two fruits. For that very [wholesome], indeterminate [<s>dharma</s>s constitute] three fruits. Excluding the ripening-fruit (<s>vipākaphala</s>) — because the ripening is indeterminate. Unwholesome [as fruit of wholesome constitute] two — the person-effort fruit (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>) and the dominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>). Not the outflow-fruit (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>) — because wholesome <s>dharma</s>s are not the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>) of unwholesome ones. Not the ripening-fruit — because the ripening is indeterminate. Since unwholesome [<s>dharma</s>s] are determined with respect to ripening — not the separation-fruit (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>) — because of being unwholesome. By elimination, [they are] the person-effort and dominant fruits alone. And those should be explained as before. Indeterminate [constitute] four — how are indeterminate <s>dharma</s>s the outflow-fruit of unwholesome? And how should it not be so? Because of dissimilarity. For unwholesome and indeterminate <s>dharma</s>s are indeed dissimilar — because of being respectively with-ripening and without-ripening. This is not a fault. For between unwholesome and obstructed-indeterminate <s>dharma</s>s, there is a similarity in the general characteristic of being afflicted. Therefore, obstructed-indeterminate [<s>dharma</s>s] are fittingly the outflow-fruit of unwholesome ones, and unwholesome ones the outflow-fruit of obstructed-indeterminate ones. Therefore he says: 'For among the indeterminate' — and so forth in detail. Of the unwholesome universal [afflictions] (<s>sarvatraga</s>) to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and origination, and of passion and the rest to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering — the identity-view (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the extreme-view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>) are the outflow-fruit. The outflow-fruit is [through] the homogeneous and universal [causes]. 'For unwholesome' — and so forth in detail. The unwholesome [<s>dharma</s>s] to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and the rest, belonging to five categories — [are] the outflow-fruit of the two indeterminate identity-view and extreme-view. These very three, excluding the ripening-fruit and separation-fruit.

body.text: (IV.91) atītasya karmaṇas triyadhvikā atītānāgatapratyutpannā dharmāḥ. pratyekaṃ catvāri phalāni. visaṃyogaphalaṃ hitvā. tasyānadhvapatitavāt. kathaṃ kṛtvā. atītasya karmaṇaḥ paścād atītas tadvipāko vipākaphalaṃ. [Tib. 84b] tadākṛṣṭāḥ. sahajātītāḥ paścādanaṃtarātītā vā puruṣakāraphalaṃ. svabhāvavarjyāḥ tena sahotpannāḥ paścādutpannāś cātītāḥ adhipatiphalaṃ. paścādutpannātītāḥ sadṛśā dharmā niṣyandaphalaṃ. atītasyānāgatas tadvipāko vipākaphalaṃ. yadbalena prāpyate 'nāgato dharmaḥ. tat puruṣakāraphalaṃ. adhipatiphalaṃ yad anāgataṃ. tasya phalaṃ. niṣyandaphalaṃ tatsadṛśam anāgataṃ. evaṃ pratyutpannā api tasyātītasya catvāri phalāni yojyāni.
body.translated_text: (IV.91) For past <s>karma</s>, <s>dharma</s>s of the three time-periods — past, future, and present — [constitute] four fruits each, excluding the separation-fruit, because that [separation] does not fall within a time-period. How is this? For past <s>karma</s>: its ripening that has subsequently become past is the ripening-fruit. Those drawn by it — [<s>dharma</s>s] that have arisen simultaneously and become past, or those past through being immediately subsequent — are the person-effort fruit. Excluding its own nature, those co-arisen with it and those arisen subsequently that are past — are the dominant fruit. Those past <s>dharma</s>s that are similar and arisen subsequently — are the outflow-fruit. For the past [<s>karma</s>], future [<s>dharma</s>s]: its ripening that is future is the ripening-fruit. That future <s>dharma</s> which is obtained through its power — that is the person-effort fruit. The dominant fruit is whatever is future — its fruit. The outflow-fruit is whatever is future and similar to it. Thus, present [<s>dharma</s>s] too should be connected as four fruits of that past [<s>karma</s>].

body.text: iti. pratyutpannasyāpy anāgatā dharmāś catvāri phalāni. etāny eva visaṃyogaphalaṃ hitvety arthaḥ. tāny apy evam eva yojyāni. pratyutpannā dharmāḥ pratyutpannasya dve puruṣakārādhipatiphale iti. tasya hi sahotpannaṃ tadbalāj
body.translated_text: meaning: of the present [<s>karma</s>] too, future <s>dharma</s>s [constitute] four fruits. These very [four], excluding the separation-fruit — this is the meaning. And those too should be connected in the same way. Present <s>dharma</s>s [constitute] two for the present [<s>karma</s>]: the person-effort fruit and the dominant fruit. For what has co-arisen with it, born through its power

body.text: jātam iti puruṣakāraphalam adhipatiphalaṃ ca bhavaty eva. avisaṃyogasvabhāvān na visaṃyogaphalaṃ. pūrvottaratābhāvān na niṣyandaphalaṃ. pravāhāpekṣatvād vipākasya na vartamānaṃ vartamānasya vipākaphalaṃ. niṣyandavisaṃyogaphale hitveti. anāgato 'nāgatasya na niṣyandaphalaṃ. yasmāt sabhāgasarvatragahetū nānāgatau bhavataḥ. tasya viprakīrṇatvāt. sādṛśyena cāsyedaṃ phalam iti paricchettum aśakyatvāt. na visaṃyogaphalaṃ. yasmād anāgato visaṃyogo na bhavati. vipākaphalaṃ tu bhaved anāgatasya hy akuśalasya kuśalasāsravasya vānāgataṃ paścādutpatsyamānaṃ ca vipākaphalaṃ. puruṣakāraphalaṃ [Tib. 85a]. sahajam anāgatam anaṃtarabhāvi cānāgataṃ. adhipatiphalaṃ tu sugamam iti na punar ucyate.
body.translated_text: — is indeed the person-effort fruit and the dominant fruit. Not the separation-fruit, because it does not have the nature of separation. Not the outflow-fruit, because of the absence of a prior-later [relationship]. Because the ripening requires a continuum-process, a present [<s>dharma</s>] is not the ripening-fruit of a present [<s>karma</s>]. Excluding the outflow-fruit and separation-fruit — a future [<s>dharma</s>] is not the outflow-fruit of a future [<s>dharma</s>], because the homogeneous and universal causes are not future. Because of its [future <s>dharma</s>s'] being scattered — and because it is impossible to determine 'this is its fruit through similarity.' Not the separation-fruit, because future separation does not exist. But the ripening-fruit could be [of a future <s>dharma</s>] — for the ripening-fruit of a future unwholesome or wholesome contaminated [<s>dharma</s>] is future and will arise subsequently. The person-effort fruit — a co-arisen future [<s>dharma</s>] and one immediately subsequent to a future [<s>dharma</s>]. The dominant fruit is easily understood and therefore is not stated again.

body.text: (IV.92ab)
body.translated_text: (IV.92ab)

body.text: na visaṃyogaphalaṃ. visaṃyogasyābhūmisvabhāvatvāt. anāsravāś cet trīṇi phalānīti. niṣyandaphalasya tṛtīyasya saṃbhavāt.
body.translated_text: not the separation-fruit — because separation does not have the nature of a ground. If they are outflow-free, three fruits — because of the possibility of the outflow-fruit as the third.

children.translated_text: 'The path of nine grounds is mutual' —

body.text: iti hi siddhāṃtaḥ.
body.translated_text: for this is the established doctrine.

body.text: (IV.92cd, 93ab) śaikṣasya karmaṇaḥ śaikṣā dharmās trīṇīti. yasmād vipākaphalaṃ na śaikṣaṃ. visaṃyogaś cāpi na śaikṣaḥ. naivaśaikṣanāśaikṣā api trīṇi. na vipākaphalam asyāsti. śaikṣasyāvipākatvāt. na niṣyandaphalaṃ. naivaśaikṣanāśaikṣasya śaikṣeṇāsadṛśatvāt. visaṃyogaphalaṃ tu bhavati. visaṃyogasya naivaśaikṣanāśaikṣasvabhāvatvāt. puruṣakāraphalam api bhavati. śaikṣeṇa naivaśaikṣanāśaikṣākṛṣṭisaṃbhavāt. adhipatiphalaṃ cāsty eva. iti trīṇi saṃbhavaṃti. aśaikṣasya tv iti vistaraḥ. aśaikṣasya śaikṣā dharmā ekam adhipatiphalaṃ. na niṣyandaphalaṃ. nyūnatvāt.
body.translated_text: (IV.92cd, 93ab) Of a learner's (<s>śaikṣa</s>) <s>karma</s>, learner <s>dharma</s>s [constitute] three — because the ripening-fruit is not a learner [<s>dharma</s>], and separation too is not a learner [<s>dharma</s>]. Neither-learner-nor-non-learner (<s>naivaśaikṣanāśaikṣa</s>) [<s>dharma</s>s] too [constitute] three — there is no ripening-fruit for it, because a learner [<s>dharma</s>] has no ripening. Not the outflow-fruit — because a neither-learner-nor-non-learner [<s>dharma</s>] is dissimilar to a learner [<s>dharma</s>]. But the separation-fruit exists — because separation has the nature of neither-learner-nor-non-learner. The person-effort fruit also exists — because of the possibility of a learner [<s>dharma</s>] drawing a neither-learner-nor-non-learner [<s>dharma</s>]. The dominant fruit certainly exists. Thus three are possible. But for a non-learner's (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) [<s>karma</s>] — and so forth in detail. Of a non-learner, learner <s>dharma</s>s [constitute] one — the dominant fruit alone. Not the outflow-fruit — because of being lesser.

body.text: iti vacanāt. na puruṣakāraphalaṃ. sahānaṃtarotpādābhāvāt. na hy aśaikṣānaṃtaraṃ śaikṣam utpadyate. ca naivaśaikṣanāśaikṣasvabhāvam iti. [Tib. 85b] na cāśaikṣasya vipāko bhavatīty ato na vipākaphalaṃ. aśaikṣās trīṇīti. puruṣakārādhipatiniṣyandaphalāni. na vipākavisaṃyogaphale. tayor naiva śaikṣanāśaikṣasvabhāvatvāt. yac cāśaikṣasvabhāvaṃ. tad iha ciṃtyate. naivaśaikṣanāśaikṣā dve puruṣakārādhipatiphale iti. puruṣakāraphalaṃ. tadyathā. tadākṛṣṭā aṇaṃtarabhāvino dharmāḥ. adhipatiphalaṃ. pūrvavat. yathoktakāraṇatvān na phalatrayaṃ. aśaikṣā apy evam ity. dve puruṣakārādhipatiphale
body.translated_text: because of this statement. Not the person-effort fruit — because of the impossibility of co-arising or immediately-subsequent arising. For a learner [<s>dharma</s>] does not arise immediately after a non-learner [<s>dharma</s>]. Nor [is it] a neither-learner-nor-non-learner [<s>dharma</s>] by nature. And there is no ripening of a non-learner [<s>dharma</s>], hence not the ripening-fruit. Non-learner [<s>dharma</s>s constitute] three — the person-effort, dominant, and outflow-fruits. Not the ripening-fruit and separation-fruit — because both have the nature of neither-learner-nor-non-learner. And whatever has the nature of non-learner — that is considered here. Neither-learner-nor-non-learner [<s>dharma</s>s constitute] two — the person-effort and dominant fruits. Person-effort fruit — for example: <s>dharma</s>s immediately following those drawn by it. Dominant fruit — as before. For the three stated reasons, not the other three fruits. Non-learner [<s>dharma</s>s of neither-learner-nor-non-learner] also similarly — two: person-effort and dominant fruits

body.text: ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: — this is the meaning.

body.text: iti. darśanaheyādayaḥ.
body.translated_text: meaning: to-be-abandoned-by-seeing and the following.

body.text: iti. darśanaheyādayaḥ. bhāvanāheyā dve iti. anāsravamārgavyutthāne bhāvanāheyāḥ kuśalāḥ puruṣakāraphalaṃ. ādyaṃtavad iti vistaraḥ. ādyaṃtayor ivādyaṃtavat. madhye 'pi jñāpanārthaṃ punar yathākramagrahaṇaṃ. katham. ādau yathākramārtho 'nukramaśabdaḥ prayuktaḥ.
body.translated_text: meaning: to-be-abandoned-by-seeing and the following. To-be-abandoned-by-cultivation [<s>dharma</s>s constitute] two — at the emergence from the outflow-free path, the wholesome [<s>dharma</s>s] to be abandoned by cultivation are the person-effort fruit. 'Like the beginning and end' — and so forth in detail. Like the beginning and end — just as in the beginning and end. The re-mention of 'in sequence' even in the middle is for the purpose of indicating [the pattern]. How? In the beginning, the word 'in sequence' is used in the sense of following the order.

children.text: aśubhasya śubhādyā dve trīṇi catvāry anukramam
children.translated_text: 'Of the unwholesome, two from the wholesome and the like, three, four — in sequence' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. aṃte 'pi prayuktaḥ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. At the end too, it is used:

children.text: apraheyasya te tv ekaṃ dve catvāri yathākramam
children.translated_text: 'Of what is not to be abandoned, those [constitute] one, two, four — in sequence' —

body.text: iti. yathaivam ādyaṃtayor yathākramārtha uktaḥ. [Tib. 86a] tathā madhye 'pi avagaṃtavyaḥ. eṣa hi peyāladharma iti. eṣo 'bhisaṃkṣepanyāyaḥ. anyathā hy
body.translated_text: thus. Just as at the beginning and end the meaning of 'in sequence' is stated, so too in the middle it should be understood. For this is the convention of abbreviation. Otherwise,

children.translated_text: 'Of the indeterminate, two, three — these from the wholesome and the like' —

body.text: ity evamādiṣu yathākramam iti sarvatra vaktavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: in such passages, 'in sequence' would have to be stated everywhere.

body.text: (IV.95) ayoniśomanaskārasaṃbhūtatvād iti. ayonyā anyāyena kleśayogena. yaḥ pravṛtto manaskāraḥ. tatra saṃbhūtaḥ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmād iti. yena yathā gaṃtavyaṃ. yena pudgalena yathā gaṃtavyaṃ. tathā na gacchatīty asyāyogavihitaṃ karma.
body.translated_text: (IV.95) 'Because of being born from improper attention (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>)' — improper, that is, wrongful, through the application of affliction — attention that has operated thus; born therein — its state; therefore. 'By whom as it should be gone' — by which person, as one should go — not going thus is <s>karma</s> prescribed against the proper way.

children.translated_text: 'Even that which has deviated from the rule' —

body.text: apiśabdena kliṣṭaṃ cāpīti gṛhyate.
body.translated_text: by the word 'even' (<s>api</s>), 'and also afflicted' is grasped.

body.text: tadubhābhyām anyan nobhayatheti. na yogavihitaḥ. nāyogavihitaḥ. kiṃ ca tadanyad avyākṛtaṃ karma vidhibhraṣṭavidhibhraṣṭābhyām anyad avyākṛtam iti.
body.translated_text: 'Other than both of those, not in either way' — not prescribed according to the proper way, not prescribed against the proper way. What then? Other than those two — indeterminate <s>karma</s>, other than both prescribed-according-to-rule and prescribed-against-rule, is indeterminate.

body.text: (IV.96ab) janmeti nikāyasabhāgasyākhyeti. cittaviprayuktasya saṃskārasya. na tu jāter ity abhiprāyaḥ. yat tarhīti. yady ekam eva karmaikam eva janmākṣipati. yat sthaviraniruddhenoktaṃ so 'haṃ tasyeti vistareṇa. tat kathaṃ na virudhyata iti vākyārthaḥ. tena janmāntare tagaraśikhine pratyekabuddhāya [Tib. 86b] piṇḍapāto dattaḥ. tenaivam uktaṃ. so 'haṃ tasyeti vistareṇa. nirvartyeti. viṭhapitvety arthaḥ. tulye 'pi mānuṣye kaścit sakalendriyo bhavati kaścid vikalendriyaḥ. paripūrakasya karmaṇo bhedāt tad anupapanmam.
body.translated_text: (IV.96ab) 'Birth' means the designation of class-of-beings (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>) — of a conditioned force dissociated from mind. The intent is: not of the birth [itself]. 'If then' — if a single <s>karma</s> projects a single birth, then what the Elder <s>Niruddha</s> said — 'I myself, for that one' — in detail — how is that not contradicted? — this is the meaning of the statement. For in a previous life, by him, alms-food was given to the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> <s>Tagaraśikhin</s>. Because of that, it was said thus: 'I myself, for that one' — in detail. 'Having completed' — meaning: having arranged. Even though human birth is the same, some are endowed with all faculties and some are defective in faculties — because of the difference of completing <s>karma</s>. This is not inconsistent

body.text: ākṣepakarmaphalatvāc cakṣurādīnāṃ. ṣaḍāyatanaṃ hy ākṣipyata iti. varṇādayas tu paripūrakasya karmaṇaḥ phalam iti. yuktaṃ vaktuṃ. tulye 'pi mānuṣye kaścid varṇavān kaścin neti. tadutpattivirodhipratyayaparihāre paripūrakakarmasāmarthyān na virodhaḥ. anyathā hi na kaścid vikalendriyaḥ syāt sati janmākṣepa iti.
body.translated_text: — because the eye and the rest are the fruits of projecting <s>karma</s>. For the six sense-bases are projected. But complexion and the rest are the fruit of completing <s>karma</s>. It is fitting to say: even though human birth is the same, some are handsome and some are not. Through the removal of conditions that oppose their arising, through the power of completing <s>karma</s>, there is no contradiction. Otherwise, no one would be defective in faculties when there is the projection of birth.

body.text: (IV.96cd) anyad api savipākam iti. vedanādikaṃ. karmasahabhūtvād iti. yasmāt karmaṇā cetanākhyena saha te samāpattī na bhavataḥ. nāpi kāyavākkarmabhyām acittikatvāt. prāptibhiś ca nākṣipyate savipākābhir api. karmaṇānekaphalatvāt. tadākṣepakeṇa karmaṇā saha bhavaṃtyo 'pi prāptayo na tena sahaikaphalā iti. vṛkṣaprapāṭikā iva hi prāptayo bahiravasthāyino bhavaṃti.
body.translated_text: (IV.96cd) 'Other things too that have ripening' — feeling and the rest. 'Because of not being co-existent with <s>karma</s>' — because those two attainments do not exist together with <s>karma</s> called volition (<s>cetanā</s>). Nor with bodily and vocal <s>karma</s>, because [those attainments] are without mind. 'And through acquisitions (<s>prāpti</s>), it is not projected, even those with ripening' — because of <s>karma</s> having multiple fruits. Even though acquisitions exist together with the projecting <s>karma</s>, the acquisitions do not share a single fruit with it. For acquisitions, like leaves from a tree-branch, are external appendages.

body.text: (IV.97) karmāvaraṇam iti. karmaivāvaraṇaṃ. kleśa evāvaraṇaṃ. vipāka evāvaraṇam iti. āryāmārgaprāyogikāṇāṃ ca kuśalamūlānām iti. uṣmagatādīnāṃ. apāyādiniyatānīti [Tib. 87a]. narakatiryakpretaniyatāni. ādiśabdenāsaṃjñisamāpattimahābrahmasaṃvartanīyaṃ ca niyataṃ karma gṛhyate. ṣaṇḍhapaṇḍakobhayavyaṃjanasaṃvartanīyaṃ ca vaktavyaṃ. tathāṇḍajasaṃsvedajastrītvāṣṭamabhavaniyatāni karmāṇi vaktavyāni. āryā hi narakādiṣu nopapadyaṃte. aṇḍajāṃ saṃsvedajāṃ ca yoniṃ na pratipadyaṃte. strītvam aṣṭamaṃ ca bhavaṃ na nirvartayiṣyaṃti. saptakṛtvo bhavaparamatvāt. sudarśakānīti. sukhena dṛśyaṃte parebhyā iti sudarśāni. sudarśāny eva sudarśakāni. evaṃ sukhena prajñapyaṃte ātmaneti suprajñeyāni. suprajñeyāny eva suprajñapakāni. svārthe kaḥ. paryāye dvayaṃ caitat. sudarśakāni suprajñapakānīti. adhiṣṭhānata iti. karmapatho 'dhiṣṭhānaṃ. trayāṇām ānaṃtaryāṇāṃ prāṇātipātaḥ karmapatho 'dhiṣṭhānaṃ. ekasya mṛṣāvādaḥ karmapatho 'dhiṣṭhānaṃ. paṃcamasya prāṇātipātaprayogo 'dhiṣṭhānaṃ. evam adhiṣṭhānataḥ sudarśakāni. suprajñapakāni. phalataḥ. sarveṣām aniṣṭaphalatvāt. gatitaḥ. narakagatiprāpakatvāt. upapattitaḥ. upapadyavedanīyatvāt. pudgalataḥ. gariṣṭhakleśasamudācārāt suprajñātaḥ pudgalaḥ. ayaṃ pitṛghātakaḥ. yāvad ayaṃ tathāgataśarīre duṣṭacittarudhirotpādaka [Tib. 87b] iti. apare punar vyācakṣate. adhiṣṭhānataḥ. pūrvavat. phalataḥ. narakaphalatvāt. gatitaḥ. manuṣyagatikaraṇāt.
body.translated_text: (IV.97) '<s>Karmic</s> obstruction' (<s>karmāvaraṇa</s>) — <s>karma</s> itself is obstruction. Affliction itself is obstruction. Ripening itself is obstruction. 'And of wholesome roots that are preparatory for the Noble Path' — of the warmth (<s>uṣmagata</s>) and the rest. 'Fixed for the lower realms and the rest' — fixed for the hells, animals, and hungry ghosts. By the word 'and the rest,' <s>karma</s> leading to the attainment of non-perception (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>) and leading to the dissolution of <s>Mahābrahmā</s> world is also grasped as fixed [obstructing] <s>karma</s>. <s>Karma</s> leading to being a eunuch, neuter, or hermaphrodite should also be stated. Likewise, <s>karma</s> fixed for egg-born, moisture-born, female, and the eighth existence should be stated. For Noble Ones are not reborn in the hells and the rest. They do not take egg-born or moisture-born birth. They will not bring about femaleness or an eighth existence — because of being at most seven-times-reborn (<s>saptakṛtvo bhavaparama</s>). '<s>Sudarśaka</s>' — meaning: easily seen by others. <s>Sudarśaka</s> means exactly <s>sudarśana</s>. Similarly, 'easily known by oneself' — <s>suprajñeya</s> is exactly <s>suprajñapaka</s>. The [suffix] <s>ka</s> is in the reflexive sense. And this pair is a synonym. '<s>Sudarśaka</s> and <s>suprajñapaka</s>' — [meaning] easily seen and easily known. From the basis — the action-path is the basis. For three heinous acts (<s>ānantarya</s>), killing is the action-path basis. For one, false speech is the action-path basis. For the fifth, the preparatory of killing is the basis. Thus they are easily seen from the basis. Easily known — from the fruit, because all have undesirable fruits. From the destiny — because they lead to the hell destiny. From the mode of rebirth — because they ripen as immediately-experienced [<s>karma</s>]. From the person — a person well-known because of the operation of the heaviest afflictions: 'this one is a patricide,' up to 'this one drew blood from the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body with evil intent.' Others, however, explain: from the basis — as before. From the fruit — because they have hell as their fruit. From the destiny — because they are done by one in the human destiny.

children.translated_text: 'In three continents, a heinous act [can occur]' —

body.text: iti. vacanāt. upapattitaḥ. tathaivopapadyavedanīyatvāt. pudgalataḥ. strīpuṃsau. na ṣaṇḍhaḥ paṇḍako vā. ity evaṃ paṃcabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sudarśakāni suprajñapakāni. na tu punas tāny apāyādiniyatāni karmāṇi paṃcabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sudarśakāni suprajñapakānīti. na tāny uktāni. uttarottarāvāhanād iti.
body.translated_text: — from this statement. From the mode of rebirth — because it is experienced in the [same] birth in which [the action was done]. From the person — it is a woman or man, not a eunuch (<s>ṣaṇḍha</s>) or impotent person (<s>paṇḍaka</s>). Thus, through these five causes, [the actions of definite retribution] are easily discerned and easily identified. But those actions determined for the lower realms and the like — those are not said to be easily discerned and easily identified through five causes. Not those are spoken of. 'Because of each successive [obstruction] bringing about [the next]'

body.text: yasmāt kleśāvaraṇaṃ karmāvaraṇaṃ āvahati. karmāvaraṇaṃ cāpāye 'niṣṭaṃ vipākam āvahatīti. kleśāvaraṇaṃ sarvapāpiṣṭhaṃ. tataḥ karmāvaraṇaṃ laghu. tato vipākāvaraṇaṃ. vipākāvaraṇasya hi dṛṣṭa eva dharme vyāpāraḥ. na dvitīya iti. yasya dharmasya yogāt pitṛvadhādeḥ so 'naṃtaro bhavati. tasyābhidhāne bhāvapratyayaḥ. ānaṃtaryam iti. śrāmaṇyavat. yathā yenānāsraveṇa mārgeṇa yogāc chramaṇo bhavati. tadabhidhāne bhāvapratyayaḥ.
body.translated_text: — since the obstruction of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) brings about the obstruction of action (<s>karmāvaraṇa</s>), and the obstruction of action brings about an undesirable retribution in the lower realms — therefore the obstruction of afflictions is the worst of all. After that, the obstruction of action is lighter. After that, the obstruction of retribution (<s>vipākāvaraṇa</s>). For the obstruction of retribution has its activity in this very life alone, not in a second [life]. 'That, because of whose conjunction, patricide and the like becomes an immediate [act]' — the abstract suffix indicates the state of being. <s>Ānantarya</s> (immediate consequence) — like <s>śrāmaṇya</s>. Just as that uncontaminated path through whose conjunction one becomes a <s>śramaṇa</s> — the abstract suffix indicates the state of being.

children.translated_text: '<s>Śrāmaṇya</s> (being a renunciant) is the stainless path' —

body.text: iti. tadvat.
body.translated_text: thus. Similarly.

body.text: (IV.98) nottarakurāv iti. niyatāyuṣkatvāt. prakṛtiśīlatvāt. tatra śāsanabhāvāc ca. yad evāsaṃvarabhāve kāraṇam iti. pāpe 'py asthirāśayatvāt. yatraiva ca saṃvaraḥ. tatrāsaṃvaro 'pi. pratidvaṃdvabhāvāt. ity asaṃvaraḥ
body.translated_text: (IV.98) 'Not in <s>Uttarakuru</s>' — because of having a fixed lifespan; because of having natural morality; and because of the non-existence of the teaching there. 'That very thing which is the cause of the state of non-restraint' — because of having an unstable disposition even toward evil. And wherever there is restraint, there is also non-restraint — because of being counterparts. Thus non-restraint

body.text: na bhavatīti. [Tib. 88a] yadvipādanād iti. yasya hrīvyapatrāpyasya vipādanād vikopanād ānaṃtaryeṇa spṛśyeran ṣaṇḍhādayaḥ. tat teṣāṃ mātāpitror aṃtike na tīvraṃ bhavati. ity atas teṣām ānaṃtaryaṃ
body.translated_text: does not exist. 'Because of the corruption of which' — because of the corruption, the ruination of their sense of shame (<s>hrī</s>) and fear of wrongdoing (<s>vyapatrāpya</s>), eunuchs and the like would be affected by immediate [acts]. But for them, [the sense of shame] toward mother and father is not intense. Therefore, for them, the immediate [act]

body.text: yadi vikalātmabhāvahetutvād alpopakāratvam iti. atas teṣām ānaṃtaryaṃ neṣyate. jātyandhādīnām api strīpuṃsānāṃ mātrādivadhād ānaṃtaryaṃ na syāt. na. adhigamadharmaviruddhasyātmabhāvavaikalyasya vivakṣitatvāt. yad vaikalyam adhigamadharmavirodhi. tad adhikṛtaṃ tenaiva ca mātrālpasnehatvaṃ. na jātyandhādivaikalyena. ata eva tiryakpretānām api neṣyete.
body.translated_text: 'If because of causing a defective state of being, there is little benefit' — therefore the immediate [act] is not accepted for them. [But then] for those born blind and the like too — women and men — there would be no immediate [act] from killing a mother and the like. No. Because the intended [deficiency] is one that is contrary to the <s>dharma</s> of attainment (<s>adhigamadharma</s>). The deficiency that is contrary to the <s>dharma</s> of attainment — that is what is intended. And because of that very [deficiency], there is little affection toward the mother — not because of the deficiency of being born blind and the like. For this very reason, for animals and hungry ghosts too, [the immediate act] is not accepted.

children.translated_text: 'Because of little benefit and absence of shame' —

body.text: eva. aśvājāneyavad iti. paṭubuddhīnāṃ syād ānaṃtaryaṃ tiryakpretānām apīty adhikṛtaṃ. aśvājāneyavad iti. śrūyate yathā kaścid eva viśiṣṭāśva ājāneyo mātaraṃ na gacchatīti. vāsasā mukhaṃ pracchādya mātaraṃ gamitas tena paścāt jñātvā svam aṃgajātam utpāṭitam iti. evam ājāneyo 'śvaḥ paṭubuddhiḥ. asyānaṃtaryaṃ syād ity abhiprāyaḥ. manuṣyasyāpy amānuṣaṃ mātāpitaraṃ mārayato na syād ānaṃtaryaṃ. naiva bhaved ānaṃtaryam ity arthaḥ. katham.
body.translated_text: indeed. 'Like a thoroughbred horse' — the intended [meaning] is: for those with keen intelligence, there could be an immediate [act] even among animals and hungry ghosts. 'Like a thoroughbred horse' — it is heard that a certain distinguished horse, a thoroughbred, did not approach its mother. When its face was covered with cloth and it was made to approach the mother, afterwards, having realized [what happened], it tore off its own genitals. Thus a thoroughbred horse has keen intelligence — the intent is: for such a one there could be an immediate [act]. 'Even when a human kills a non-human mother or father, there would be no immediate [act].' There would indeed be no immediate [act] — this is the meaning. How?

children.translated_text: 'Because of little benefit and absence of shame' —

body.text: eva. na hi manuṣyānurūpam upakāram amanuṣyaḥ kartuṃ samarthaḥ [Tib. 88b] na ca manuṣyasyāmanuṣyayor mātāpitror aṃtike tīvraṃ hrīvyapatrāpyaṃ saṃtiṣṭhate. gativailakṣaṇyenālpasnehatvāt.
body.translated_text: indeed. For a non-human is not capable of providing benefit appropriate for a human, and for a human, intense shame and fear of wrongdoing does not persist in relation to non-human parents — because of little affection due to the difference of destinies.

body.text: (IV.99) catvāri kāyakarmeti. mātṛvadhādīni. ekaṃ vākkarmeti. saṃghabhedaḥ. trīṇi prāṇātipāta iti. mātṛvadhādīni. ekaṃ mṛṣāvādaḥ. saṃghabhedaḥ
body.translated_text: (IV.99) 'Four bodily actions' — matricide and the like. 'One vocal action' — schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. 'Three [are] killing' — matricide and the like. 'One [is] false speech' — schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>

body.text: . ekaṃ prāṇātipātaprayogaḥ. tathāgataśarīre duṣṭacittarudhirotpādanaṃ kasmān na prāṇātipāta ity āha. anupakramadharmāṇo hi tathāgatā iti. aparopakramamaraṇadharmāṇa ity arthaḥ. hetau phalopacārād iti. mṛṣāvādo hetuḥ saṃghabhedasya cittaviprayuktalakṣaṇasya. tasmin hetau phalopacāraḥ. cittaviprayukto dharmaḥ phalam upacaryate. saṃghabheda iti. bhidyate. vāneneti. karaṇasādhanaparigrahād vā mṛṣāvādaḥ saṃghabheda ity ucyate. mṛṣāvādena hi saṃgho bhidyate. na tu saṃghabheda iti bhāvasādhanaparigrahaḥ.
body.translated_text: . 'One [is] the preparation for killing' — maliciously drawing blood from the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Why is it not killing? — he says: 'For <s>Tathāgata</s>s are of a nature not subject to being harmed.' The meaning is: they have the nature of not dying through being harmed by another. 'Because of metaphorical designation of the effect in terms of the cause' — false speech is the cause of the schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, which has the characteristic of a <s>dharma</s> dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayukta</s>). In that cause, there is metaphorical designation of the effect: the <s>dharma</s> dissociated from mind, which is the effect, is metaphorically designated [as the cause]. 'Schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>' — [the <s>Saṃgha</s>] is split. Because of the acceptance of the instrumental meaning, false speech is called 'schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>' — for by false speech the <s>Saṃgha</s> is split. But the schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s> is not accepted as having the abstract meaning.

body.text: mukhyavṛttyā vaibhāṣikāṇāṃ dravyasattā. tenāha.
body.translated_text: In the primary sense, for the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s, it has real existence (<s>dravyasattā</s>). Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'Its own-nature is a [<s>dharma</s>] dissociated [from mind]. It is an unafflicted, indeterminate <s>dharma</s>' —

body.text: iti. sa kim ānaṃtaryaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. naivāsāv evaṃlakṣaṇam ānaṃtaryaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ. naiva ca tena viprayuktena dharmeṇa bhettā samanvāgataḥ. tena nāsāv ānaṃtaryam ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Would that be an immediate [act]?' — the meaning is: that very thing of such characteristics is indeed not an immediate [act]. And moreover, the one who splits [the <s>Saṃgha</s>] is not endowed with that <s>dharma</s> dissociated [from mind] — therefore it is not an immediate [act] — this is the intent.

body.text: (IV.101) [Tib. 89a] sa punar mṛṣāvādaḥ saṃghabhedasahajo viprayuktadharmasahajo vāgvijñaptyavijñaptisvabhāva ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.101) That false speech, moreover, co-arisen with the schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, co-arisen with the <s>dharma</s> dissociated [from mind] — the meaning is: it has the own-nature of vocal and non-manifest (<s>avijñapti</s>) [action].

body.text: (IV.102) bhikṣur bhinattīti. buddhasya bhikṣutvāt. tatpratispardhivṛttitvāc ca bhettuḥ. na gṛhī bhikṣuṇyādaya iti. teṣām anādeyāśrayatvāt. sa ca dṛṣṭicarita eva. dṛḍhagūḍhāśayatvāt. satkāyadṛṣṭyādiṣu paṃcasu caritaḥ pravṛtto dṛṣṭicaritaḥ. dṛṣṭir vā caritam asyeti dṛṣṭicaritaḥ. sa hy ūhāpohasāmarthyād anyaṃ śāstāraṃ mārgāṃtaraṃ ca grāhayituṃ samarthaḥ. na tṛṣṇācarita iti. saṃkleśavyavadānapakṣayor asthirāśayatvāt. duṣprasahatvād iti. durabhibhavatvāt. pratyakṣadharmatvād iti. āgamādhigamadharmayoḥ sākṣātkāritvād ity arthaḥ. na kṣāṃtilābhina iti. na nirvedhabhāgīyakṣāṃtilābhina ity arthaḥ. dṛṣṭasatyakalpatvāt.
body.translated_text: (IV.102) 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> splits [the <s>Saṃgha</s>]' — because the <s>Buddha</s> is a <s>bhikṣu</s>; and because the one who splits acts in rivalry with him. 'Not a householder, a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, and the like' — because their basis is not authoritative. And that [one who splits] is exclusively one of view-conduct (<s>dṛṣṭicarita</s>) — because of having a firm and deep disposition. One who practices the five [wrong] views beginning with the view of the self-aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) is 'one of view-conduct.' Or: 'view' is his 'conduct' — hence 'one of view-conduct.' For that one, through the capacity of reasoning and argumentation, is capable of making [others] accept another teacher and another path. Not one of craving-conduct (<s>tṛṣṇācarita</s>) — because of having an unstable disposition toward both the side of defilement and the side of purification. 'Because of being difficult to overcome' — because of being difficult to defeat. 'Because of being one who directly realizes the <s>dharma</s>' — the meaning is: because of directly realizing both the <s>dharma</s> of scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and the <s>dharma</s> of attainment (<s>adhigama</s>). 'Not one who has attained patience' — the meaning is: not one who has attained the patience of the penetration-conducive wholesome roots (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) — because of being like one who has seen the truths.

children.translated_text: 'He does not stay overnight' (<s>na vivasaty asau</s>) —

body.text: na tāṃ rātriṃ parivasatīty arthaḥ. bhinnam bhavatīti kathaṃ bhinnam ity āha. mārgapravṛttiviṣṭhāpanād iti. mārgapravṛttivibandhanād ity arthaḥ. yāvad dhi saṃgho na pratisaṃdhīyate. tāvan mārgapravṛttir viṣṭhitā bhavati. na kasyacit saṃtāne mārgaḥ. saṃmukhībhavatīty arthaḥ. cakrabhedanimittatvāt. saṃghabhedaś cakrabheda ity ucyate.
body.translated_text: the meaning is: he does not stay that night. 'How is [the <s>Saṃgha</s>] split?' — he says: 'Because of the obstruction of the progress of the path' — the meaning is: because of the hindrance to the progress of the path. For as long as the <s>Saṃgha</s> is not reunited, the progress of the path is obstructed — in no one's continuum does the path come face-to-face — this is the meaning. 'Because of being the cause of breaking the wheel' — the schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s> is called 'breaking of the wheel' (<s>cakrabheda</s>).

body.text: (IV.103) avaśyaṃ hi saṃghena dvayoḥ pakṣayoḥ sthātavyam iti. buddhapakṣe [Tib. 89b] bhettṛpakṣe ca sthātavyam ity arthaḥ. saṃgho hi catvāro bhikṣavaḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.103) 'For the <s>Saṃgha</s> must necessarily stand in two factions' — the meaning is: it must stand in the <s>Buddha</s>'s faction and in the faction of the one who splits. For the <s>Saṃgha</s> consists of four <s>bhikṣu</s>s.

body.text: saṃghadvayena ca bhavitavyam ity aṣṭābhir bhikṣubhir bhedyair bhavitavyaṃ. navamena ca bhettrā. anyas tu saṃghabheda iti. cakrabhedād anyaḥ. nātrānaṃtaryam ity abhiprāyaḥ. yasmād asau karmabhedād bhavati. vyagrā iti. nānāmatayaḥ karmāṇi poṣadhādīni saṃghakarmāṇi.
body.translated_text: And since there must be two <s>Saṃgha</s>s, there must be eight <s>bhikṣu</s>s who can be split, and a ninth who is the one who splits. 'But another schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>' — different from breaking the wheel — the intent is: therein there is no immediate [act]. Because that arises from the division of actions (<s>karmabheda</s>). 'Discordant' (<s>vyagrā</s>) means: holding different views. 'Actions' means the <s>Saṃgha</s>-actions of <s>poṣadha</s> and the like.

body.text: iti. saṃghadvayenātrāpi bhavitavyaṃ. na bhettā śāstṛmānī bhavatīty aṣṭābhir eva bhikṣubhir bhavitavyaṃ. na navādibhir iti.
body.translated_text: thus. Here too there must be two <s>Saṃgha</s>s. The one who splits does not claim to be the teacher — therefore there must be exactly eight <s>bhikṣu</s>s, not nine or more.

body.text: (IV.104) ekaraso bhavatīti. avyagra ekamatir bhavatīty arthaḥ. pūrvasyām avasthāyāṃ prītiprāmodyajātaḥ. paścimāyām atīva manasi udvignasaṃjātasaṃvegaḥ. arbudāt pūrvam iti. doṣo 'rbudaṃ. dṛṣṭyarbudaṃ śīlārbudaṃ vā. atra dṛṣṭyarbudaṃ. yathoktaṃ. yathāhaṃ bhagavato bhāṣitasyārtham ājānāmi. ya ime bhagavatāṃtarāyikā dharmā ākhyātāḥ. te pratiṣevyamāṇā nālam aṃtarāyeti. tathā tad eva cittaṃ saṃdhāvati saṃsaratītyādi. śīlārbudaṃ dauḥśīlyaṃ. tena ca pratisaṃdhānīyatvād iti. tena ca śrāvakayugena yasmāt pratisaṃdhānīya ity arthaḥ. [Tib. 90a] avaśyaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ buddhānāṃ śrāvakayugaṃ bhavati. ekaḥ prajñāvatām agraḥ. dvitīyaḥ ṛddhimatāṃ. iha śākyamuner āryaḥ śāradvatīputraḥ prajñāvatām agraḥ. āryo mahāmaudgalyāyana ṛddhimatāṃ. pratidvaṃdvābhāvād iti. yasmāt parinirvṛte bhagavati tasya bhettuḥ pratidvaṃdvabhūto nāsti. sīmāyām abaddhāyām iti. maṇḍalasīmāyām. ekasyāṃ hi sīmāyāṃ pṛthakkarmakaraṇāt saṃghadvaidhaṃ bhavati. nanu ca prakṛtisīmāsti. grāmanagarādi. satyam asti. jñaptisīmāyāṃ tu satyāṃ sā prakṛtisīmā vyavasthāpyata iti. tasyā api bandho vyavasthāpyata eveti veditavyaṃ. karmādhīnatvād iti. yena śiṣyasaṃghabhedasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma kṛtaṃ bhavati. tasyaiva tadbhedo bhavati. nānyasya. śākyamuninā ca kila bodhisattvāvasthāyāṃ paṃcābhijñasya ṛṣeḥ parṣadbhedaḥ kṛta āsīt. yenāsya devadattena saṃgho bhinna iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.104) 'Becomes of one flavor' — the meaning is: becomes harmonious, of one view. In the former state, [the <s>Saṃgha</s>] is filled with joy and delight. In the latter state, [the one who split is] exceedingly distressed in mind, with remorse arisen. 'Before the abscess' (<s>arbudāt pūrvam</s>) — the abscess is the fault. An abscess of views or an abscess of morality. Here, an abscess of views. As stated: 'As I understand the meaning of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching, these <s>dharma</s>s declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as obstructive — when practiced, they are not sufficient to obstruct.' Similarly, 'that very mind runs and wanders' and so forth. An abscess of morality is immorality. 'And because of the need for reunification by that [pair]' — the meaning is: because of the need for reunification by that pair of <s>śrāvaka</s>s. And necessarily, all <s>Buddha</s>s have a pair of <s>śrāvaka</s>s — one foremost among the wise, the second foremost among those with supernatural powers. In this case, of <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Noble <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (Śāriputra) is foremost among the wise, and the Noble <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> is foremost among those with supernatural powers. 'Because of the absence of a counterpart' — because, after the <s>Bhagavān</s> has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, there is no counterpart to that one who splits. 'When the boundary (<s>sīmā</s>) has not been established' — the boundary of the circle (<s>maṇḍala</s>). For schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s> occurs through performing separate actions within one boundary. 'But is there not a natural boundary? — villages, cities, and the like.' True, there is. But when a formal boundary (<s>jñaptisīmā</s>) exists, that natural boundary is established [by it] — its establishment too should be understood as being established. 'Because of being dependent on action (<s>karma</s>)' — the schism belongs only to the one who has performed the action conducive to the schism of the disciple-<s>Saṃgha</s>, not to another. And reportedly, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, had caused the schism of the assembly of a <s>ṛṣi</s> who possessed the five <s>abhijñā</s>s — because of which his <s>Saṃgha</s> was split by <s>Devadatta</s>.

body.text: (IV.105, 106ab) guṇakṣetratvād iti. guṇānām āśrayatvād ity arthaḥ. atha vā guṇaiḥ kṣetraṃ guṇakṣetraṃ. guṇayogād dhi tat puṇyasya kṣetraṃ bhavati. yathā kṣetre bījam uptaṃ mahāphalaṃ bhavati. evaṃ puṇyabījam atroptaṃ mahāphalam bhavati. nānyatreti. na sāmānyastrīvadhādiṣu.
body.translated_text: (IV.105, 106ab) 'Because of being a field of merit (<s>guṇakṣetra</s>)' — the meaning is: because of being the basis of virtues. Alternatively, a field by virtues is a field of merit — because by the conjunction of virtues, it becomes a field for merit. Just as a seed sown in a field yields great fruit, so the seed of merit sown here yields great fruit. 'Not elsewhere' — not in the killing of ordinary women and the like.

children.translated_text: 'Because of the rejection and corruption of a field of benefit and a field of merit' —

body.text: iti. upakārikṣetrasya guṇakṣetrasya vā nirākṛteḥ parityāgān mātṛpitṛvadhādiṣv
body.translated_text: thus. Because of the rejection — the abandonment — of either a field of benefit or a field of merit, in matricide, patricide, and the like

body.text: [Tib. 90b] ānaṃtaryaṃ. tasya vipādanāc ca vikopād ānaṃtaryaṃ. tathāgataśarīre duṣṭacittarudhirotpādanāt. saṃghasyāpi yad bhedanaṃ. tad api tadvipādanaṃ. tad etad uktaṃ bhavati. upakārikṣetratvāt. guṇakṣetratvāc ca. tannirākaraṇavipādanān mātṛvadhādiṣv evānaṃtaryaṃ nānyatreti.
body.translated_text: there is an immediate [act]. And because of the corruption of that — the ruination — there is an immediate [act]: from maliciously drawing blood from the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and from the splitting of the <s>Saṃgha</s> — that too is corruption of that. What has been said is this: because of being a field of benefit, and because of being a field of merit, and because of the rejection and corruption of those, in matricide and the like alone there is an immediate [act], not elsewhere.

body.text: yadi punar mātur vyaṃjanaparivṛttaṃ syāt pitur veti. vyaṃjanaparāvṛttyā tan mātṛtvaṃ tat pitṛtvaṃ vā vinaṣṭam iti. mātur māraṇābhāvāt pitur māraṇābhāvād vā na syād ānaṃtaryam iti. tadabhāvāśaṃkayā pṛcchati.
body.translated_text: 'If, however, the mother's sex-characteristics were to change, or the father's' — through the change of sex-characteristics, that motherhood or fatherhood would be destroyed. Because of the non-existence of killing of a mother or killing of a father, there would be no immediate [act] — suspecting this non-existence, he asks.

body.text: iti. yasyāḥ śoṇitād udbhavo 'syeti
body.translated_text: thus. She from whose blood this one has arisen —

body.text: sarvakṛtyeṣv avalokyeti. sarvamātṛyogyeṣu kāryeṣu draṣṭavyety abhiprāyaḥ. mātṛkalpatvāt. āpyāyikā katāhārikā. poṣikā stanyadāyikā. saṃvardhikā audārikāhārādikalpikā. apare vyācakṣate. āpyāyikā stanyadhātṛketi yo 'rthaḥ. poṣikā audārikāhārābhyāsataḥ. [Tib. 91a] saṃvardhikā snānodvartanaviṣamaparihārata iti. maṃcatalāvalīneti. maṃcopari prāvaraṇakalpanena puruṣo 'tra supta iti manyamānena putreṇa tatraśastraprahāraḥ kṛtaḥ. tena śastraprahāreṇa maṃcatalāvalīnā mātā māritety udāhāryaṃ. dhāvakasya ca rajakasya putreṇa maśakaṃ mārāyāmīti maśakaprayogeṇa pitur māranam iti. dve avijñaptī ānaṃtaryavijñaptiḥ. kevalaprāṇātipātavijñaptiś ca. vijñaptis tv ānaṃtaryam eva tatsaṃgṛhītaiva sā nānyety arthaḥ. tasyāpy ekam eveti. arhadvadhākhyaṃ. gaccha śikhaṇḍinaṃ brūhīti rauruke nagare udrāyaṇo nāma rājā śikhaṇḍinaṃ nāma putram abhiṣicya pravrajitaḥ. pravrajyārhattvaṃ adhigatavān. sa raurukābhyāśam āgatavān. punā rājyam ākāṃkṣatīti. amātyaprakrāmitena tena śikhaṇḍinā rājñā svapitā māritaḥ. tena tu māryamāṇāvasthāyāṃ sa mārako manuṣya ukto gaccha śikhaṇḍinaṃ brūhīty evamādi. dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyām iti vaktavyam iti. gaccha śikhaṇḍinaṃ brūhi. dvābhyām ānaṃtaryakāraṇābhyāṃ bhavatā kṛtam ānaṃtaryam iti. tena vaktavyaṃ. dvābhyāṃ vā [Tib. 91b] mukhābhyāṃ paribhāṣita iti. mukhadvitvād ānaṃtaryadvitvopacāra ity abhiprāyaḥ. kāraṇadvitvād dhi gurutaraṃ tad ānaṃtaryaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'To be looked upon in all duties' — the meaning is: she should be regarded in all tasks suitable for a mother, because of being like a mother. <s>Āpyāyikā</s> (the nourisher) is <s>katāhārikā</s> (the food-preparer). <s>Poṣikā</s> (the sustainer) is the one who gives breast-milk. <s>Saṃvardhikā</s> (the raiser) is the one who prepares coarse food and the like. Others explain: <s>āpyāyikā</s> means the wet-nurse — that is the meaning. <s>Poṣikā</s> is through the practice of coarse food. <s>Saṃvardhikā</s> is through bathing, anointing, and avoiding dangers. 'Hidden beneath a bed' — a covering was arranged on top of the bed, and the son, thinking 'a man sleeps here,' struck with a weapon there. By that weapon-strike, the mother who was hidden beneath the bed was killed — this is the example to be cited. And the son of a washerman struck a mosquito [on his father], intending 'I will kill the mosquito,' and by the mosquito-expedient caused the death of his father. Two <s>avijñaptī</s>s [arise]: the <s>ānantarya</s> notification and the mere killing notification. But the notification is only <s>ānantarya</s> — it is included in that very [<s>ānantarya</s>], not another — this is the meaning. 'For that too, only one' — namely, that called arhat-slaying. 'Go, tell <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>' — in the city of <s>Rauruka</s>, a king named <s>Udrāyaṇa</s>, having consecrated his son named <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, went forth [as a renunciant]. Having gone forth, he attained <s>arhatship</s>. He came near <s>Rauruka</s>. 'He desires the kingdom again' — instigated by ministers, King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> killed his own father. But while being killed, he [<s>Udrāyaṇa</s>] told the killer: 'Go, tell <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>' and so forth. 'It should be said: on two grounds' — Go, tell <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>: 'On two <s>ānantarya</s> grounds, you have committed <s>ānantarya</s> [crime].' That should be stated. Or, 'he was reproached with two mouths.' The intent is: because of the duality of mouths, the duality of <s>ānantarya</s> is figuratively applied. For because of the duality of grounds, that <s>ānantarya</s> is more grievous.

body.text: (IV.106cd) āśrayasyātyaṃtaṃ tadviruddhatvād iti. utpannāryamārgasyāśrayasya taiḥ karmapathaiḥ viruddhatvāt. ekāvadānaṃ cātrodāharaṇaṃ. chekaḥ kila śākyamanuṣyo virūḍhakabhayād viṣamaṃ vanapradeśam āśritya lubdhakavṛttim aśiśriyat. bhagavatā ca trāyastriṃśeṣu traimāsyāṃ kurvatā tato 'vatīrya
body.translated_text: (IV.106cd) 'Because of the absolute opposition of the basis to those' — because of the opposition of the basis in which the noble path (<s>āryamārga</s>) has arisen to those action-paths. And here one tale (<s>avadāna</s>) is cited as an example. A <s>Śākya</s> man named <s>Cheka</s>, out of fear of <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, took refuge in a dangerous forest region and adopted the livelihood of a hunter. And the Blessed One, having spent the three-month [retreat] among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> [gods], descended from there

body.text: chekāya saparijanāya dharmo deśitaḥ. tena srotaāpattiphalam adhigataṃ. tatputraiś ca phalaprāptaiḥ pūrvaṃ pratānitāni kūṭajālādīni mṛgebhyaḥ. tatprayogeṇa ca māryamāṇeṣv api mṛgeṣu phalaprāptyā na te punar akuśalaiḥ karmapathaiḥ spṛṣṭā iti.
body.translated_text: and taught the <s>Dharma</s> to <s>Cheka</s> together with his retinue. By him the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>) was attained. And by his sons who had attained the fruit, the nets and snares that had previously been set for deer [were left]. And even though deer were being killed by those contrivances, through attaining the fruit, they were no longer touched by unwholesome action-paths.

body.text: (IV.107) paṃcamatṛtīyaprathamāni gurutarāṇīti. iyam ānaṃtaryakarmapāṭhānupūrvī. mātṛvadhaḥ pitṛvadho 'rhadvadhaḥ saṃghabhedas tathāgate duṣṭacittarudhirotpādanam iti. paṃcamaṃ duṣṭacittarudhirotpādanaṃ. tat saṃgha bhedavarjyebhyo 'vaśiṣṭebhyaś caturbho gurutaraṃ. tṛtīyam arhadvadhaḥ. tan mātāpitṛvadhābhyāṃ gurutaraṃ. prathamaṃ mātṛvadhaḥ. tat pitṛvadhāt gurutaraṃ. tenāha. sarvalaghuḥ pitṛvadha iti. niyamasyeti. tad evāvadhāryety arthaḥ. vipākavistaram adhikṛtya saṃghabhedo mahāsāvadya [Tib. 92a] uktaḥ. aṃtarakalpavipākadānat. mahājanavyāpādanam adhikṛtya manodaṇḍaḥ. daṇḍakāraṇyādiśūnyakaraṇāt. na hy anyena kāyakarmaṇā vākkarmaṇā vā tāvato mahājanasya vyāpādaḥ saṃbhavatīti. kuśalamūlasamucchedam adhikṛtya mithyādṛṣṭir mahāsāvadyā. na hy anyad akuśalamūlaṃ kuśalamūlāni samucchinatti. samudācāramātravirodhitvād iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.107) 'The fifth, third, and first are more grievous' — this is the order of listing the <s>ānantarya</s> <s>karma</s>s. Matricide, patricide, arhat-slaying, schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and maliciously drawing blood from the <s>Tathāgata</s>. The fifth — maliciously drawing blood — is more grievous than the remaining four excluding schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. The third — arhat-slaying — is more grievous than matricide and patricide. The first — matricide — is more grievous than patricide. Therefore he says: 'Patricide is the lightest of all.' 'Of the fixed [determination]' — the meaning is: that alone is to be ascertained. Regarding the extent of maturation, schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s> is declared greatly blameworthy — because of producing maturation for an intermediate <s>kalpa</s>. Regarding harm to a great multitude, the mental punishment (<s>manodaṇḍa</s>) [is most blameworthy] — because of emptying <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s> and the like. For by no other bodily <s>karma</s> or vocal <s>karma</s> is the harm of so great a multitude possible. Regarding the cutting off of wholesome roots, wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) is greatly blameworthy — for no other unwholesome root cuts off the wholesome roots, because [other defilements] merely oppose [them] in their occurrence.

body.text: (IV.108, 109ab) na tv anaṃtaram evti. narake 'vaśyam utpattyā tāni tatsādṛśyāt tatsabhāgāny ucyaṃte. na tu tatrānaṃtarotpattyā. anyathā hy ānaṃtaryāṇy eva syur ity apareṣāṃ abhiprāyaḥ. anaṃtarabhāvitve 'pi na tāny ānaṃtaryāṇy eva saṃbhavaṃty atulyakālavipākatvād iti. prathamapākṣikāṇāṃ parihāraḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.108, 109ab) 'But not immediately after' — because of necessarily taking rebirth in hell, those [offenses] are called 'similar to those [<s>ānantarya</s>s]' due to their resemblance to them, but not because of taking rebirth immediately there. For otherwise they would simply be <s>ānantarya</s>s — this is the view of others. Even though there is the nature of immediate [rebirth], those do not become <s>ānantarya</s>s themselves because of not having maturation of equal duration — this is the response of the first party.

children.translated_text: Violation of a mother who is an <s>arhatī</s>

body.text: mātṛvadhānaṃtaryasabhāgaṃ. niyatipatitabodhisattvamāraṇaṃ pitṛvadhānaṃtaryasabhāgaṃ. śaikṣamāraṇaṃ arhadvadhānaṃtaryasabhāgaṃ. saṃghāyadvārahārikā saṃghabhedānaṃtaryasabhāgaṃ. stūpabhedanaṃ tathāgataduṣṭacittarudhirotpādānaṃtaryasabhāgaṃ. saṃghāyadvārahārikā punar akṣayanīvyapahāra ity ācāryavasumitraḥ. [Tib. 92b] evaṃ tu vyācakṣate sukhāyadvārahāriketi. yat sukhopayogikaṃ yena saṃgho jīvikāṃ kalpayati tasyāpahāra iti.
body.translated_text: is similar to the <s>ānantarya</s> of matricide. Killing a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is destined [for awakening] is similar to the <s>ānantarya</s> of patricide. Killing a <s>śaikṣa</s> (learner) is similar to the <s>ānantarya</s> of arhat-slaying. Obstructing the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s donations is similar to the <s>ānantarya</s> of schism. Destroying a <s>stūpa</s> is similar to the <s>ānantarya</s> of maliciously drawing blood from the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Now, 'obstructing the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s donations' — teacher <s>Vasumitra</s> [says]: [it means] the seizure of an inexhaustible fund (<s>akṣayanīvī</s>). But they explain it thus: 'obstructing the [<s>Saṃgha</s>'s path to] comfort' — that which is conducive to comfort, by which the <s>Saṃgha</s> arranges its livelihood, the seizure of that.

body.text: (IV.109cd) tadvipākabhūmyatikramād iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.109cd) 'Because of transcending the ground of that maturation' —

children.translated_text: 'One who has obtained <s>kṣānti</s> does not go to the evil destinies'

body.text: ity apāyabhūmyatikramāt. tathaiveti. tadvipākabhūmyatikramāt. yathā puruṣasya deśatyāgaṃ kurvato dhanikā uttiṣṭhaṃte tathaivety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: — because of transcending the ground of the evil destinies. 'Similarly' — because of transcending the ground of that maturation. Just as when a person leaves a region, creditors rise up — similarly is the meaning.

body.text: (IV.110) mahāsālakulaja iti. mahāprākārakulaja ity arthaḥ. kṣatriyamahāśālakulajo yāvat gṛhapatimahāśālakulaja iti. mahāgṛhapatikulaja ity arthaḥ. kadarthanā mahāparibhavapūrvikā viheṭhanā. yayoḥ kāyavācoḥ pravṛttyā parasya duḥkhadaurmanasye bhavatas tadapekṣayā tannigraho yaṃtraṇety ucyate.
body.translated_text: (IV.110) 'Born in a great family' — meaning: born in a family with great enclosures. Born in a <s>kṣatriya</s> great-household family, up to born in a householder great-household family. 'Born in a great householder family' — this is the meaning. <s>Kadarthanā</s> (contempt) is vexation preceded by great disrespect. The restraint (<s>nigraha</s>) with regard to those two — bodily and vocal — through whose activity suffering and displeasure arise for another, is called 'restraint' (<s>yaṃtraṇā</s>).

body.text: (IV.111) ekanavataṃ kalpam upādāyeti. ekanavateḥ pūraṇaḥ kalpa ekanavataḥ. tam upādāya. aśibaddhakena grāmaṇyā nirgranthaśrāvakena bhagavān uktaḥ. kim anarthāyāsi bho gautama kulānāṃ pratipanno yas tvam īdṛśe durbhikṣa iyatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham aśanivad utsādayaṃ bhikṣām aṭasīti. sa bhagavatābhihitaḥ. ito 'haṃ grāmaṇi ekanavataṃ kalpam upādāyeti [Tib. 93b] vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.111) 'Taking ninety-one <s>kalpa</s>s as basis' — that which completes ninety-one is the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s>. Taking that as basis. A village headman named <s>Aśibaddhaka</s>, a disciple of the <s>Nirgrantha</s>s, said to the Blessed One: 'Are you, sir <s>Gautama</s>, devoted to the detriment of families, you who in such a famine, together with this great assembly of monks, like a thunderbolt devastating [everything], go wandering for alms?' He was addressed by the Blessed One: 'From here, headman, taking ninety-one <s>kalpa</s>s as basis' — and so forth in detail.

body.text: etāṃ caturo doṣān vyāvartayatīti. durgatidoṣam akulīnatādoṣaṃ vikalendriyatādoṣaṃ strībhāvadoṣaṃ ceti. dvau ca guṇau pratilabhate. jātismaratāguṇam anivartakatāguṇaṃ ceti.
body.translated_text: 'This removes four defects' — the defect of evil destiny, the defect of low birth, the defect of deficient faculties, and the defect of being female. 'And one obtains two virtues' — the virtue of remembering past lives and the virtue of non-retrogression.

body.text: saṃnikṛṣṭaṃ bodhisattvaṃ sthāpayitveti. yo lakṣaṇavipākakarmakārī.
body.translated_text: 'Except for the proximate <s>bodhisattva</s>' — that is, the one who performs the <s>karma</s> that matures as the [thirty-two] marks.

body.text: s trisāhasrako nirvartata iti. yena sarvasattvakarmādhipatyena trisāhasra
body.translated_text: The three-thousandfold [world-system] comes into being — by the sovereignty of the <s>karma</s> of all beings, the three-thousandfold

body.text: mahāsāhasraprādurbhāvaḥ. tasya tat parimāṇam iti. uktaṃ puṇyasya parimāṇaṃ. teṣām evaṃkṛtaparimāṇānāṃ śatenaikaṃ mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaṃ nirvartate. evaṃ yāvad dvātriṃśattamam apīti. kecit te vyācakṣate. buddhālaṃbhanamanaskārasaṃmukhībhāvāt paṃcāśac cetanā bhavaṃti. aham apītthaṃ syām ity aparāḥ paṃcāśad ity evaṃ puṇyaśataṃ bhavatīti. apare varṇayaṃti. kāmadhātur viṃśatisthānāni. rūpadhātuḥ ṣoḍaśa. ārūpyāś catvāraḥ. aṣṭau ca śītanarakā ity aṣṭacatvāriṃśad vikalpaṃ traidhātukaṃ bhavati. tadālaṃbanam asya bodhisattvasya karuṇācittam utpadyate. tatas tatsaṃprayuktāś cetanā aṣṭacatvāriṃśad bhavaṃti. ato 'naṃtaraṃ buddhālaṃbanā cetanotpadyate. yathānenāsmāt traidhātukāt sattvā mocitā ity ekā cetanā. ato 'naṃtaraṃ dvitīyā cetanotpadyate. aham apy evaṃ mocayeyam ity ātmālaṃbaneti. paṃcāśac cetanā bhavaṃti [Tib. 93b] tāsāṃ punar dviḥsaṃmukhībhāvāc cetanāśataṃ bhavatīti. anye āhuḥ. prāṇātipātaviratir buddhasya bhagavataḥ paṃcabhiḥ kāraṇair upetā bhavati. paṃca kāraṇāni. maulakarmapathapariśuddhiḥ. sāmaṃtakapariśuddhiḥ. vitarkānupaghātaḥ. smṛtyanuparigṛhītatvaṃ. nirvāṇapariṇāmitatvaṃ
body.translated_text: great-thousandfold [world-system] manifests. That is its measure. The measure of merit has been stated. With a hundred of those merits thus measured, one mark of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) comes into being. Thus up to the thirty-second also. Some explain it thus: Because of the mental engagement and encounter with the <s>Buddha</s> as object, fifty <s>cetanā</s>s (volitions) arise — 'May I too become like this' — another fifty — thus a hundred merits arise. Others explain: The Desire Realm has twenty stations, the Form Realm sixteen, the Formless [Realm] four, and the eight cold hells — thus the triple realm amounts to forty-eight divisions. The compassionate mind of this <s>bodhisattva</s> arises taking those as its object. Then the <s>cetanā</s>s associated with that are forty-eight. After that, a <s>cetanā</s> arises with the <s>Buddha</s> as its object: 'Just as by him beings have been liberated from this triple realm' — one <s>cetanā</s>. After that, a second <s>cetanā</s> arises: 'May I too liberate [them] thus' — with oneself as object. Thus fifty <s>cetanā</s>s arise; through their twofold encounter, a hundred <s>cetanā</s>s arise. Others say: The refraining from killing of the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> is endowed with five factors. The five factors are: purity of the root action-path, purity of the preparatory [stage], non-harm by deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>), being sustained by mindfulness, and being dedicated to <s>nirvāṇa</s>

body.text: ceti. tadālaṃbanā api cetanāḥ paṃca bhavaṃti. evaṃ daśakarmapathālaṃbanā daśa paṃcakāś cetanānāṃ paṃcāśac cetanā bhavaṃti. tāsāṃ dviḥsaṃmukhībhāvāc cetanāśataṃ bhavatīty etat puṇyaśataṃ. yathā ayam asādhāraṇadaśakuśalakarmapathanirjāto bhagavān evam aham api syām iti kṛtvā. tad evaṃ saty ekaikaṃ puṇyaśatajam ity etat sidhyati.
body.translated_text: . The <s>cetanā</s>s taking those as objects are also five. Thus, fifty <s>cetanā</s>s arise as groups of five taking the ten action-paths as objects. Through their twofold encounter, a hundred <s>cetanā</s>s arise — this is the 'hundred merits.' 'Just as this Blessed One has arisen through the uncommon ten wholesome action-paths, may I too become thus' — having thought so. Thus, when this is so, the statement 'each arises from a hundred merits' is established.

body.text: (IV.112) paryupāsayāmāseti. liṭy āṃpratyayāṃtasyāser etad rūpaṃ. paryupāsitavān ity arthaḥ. yatra bhagavateti vistaraḥ. prabhāsanāmnā kuṃbhakārakumārabhūtenāsukhodakābhyaṃgaparicaryābhir upasthānaṃ kṛtvādyaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ.
body.translated_text: (IV.112) '<s>Paryupāsayāmāsa</s>' (he attended upon) — this is the form of <s>ās</s> with the suffix <s>liṭ</s> ending in <s>āṃ</s>-pratyaya. The meaning is: he attended upon. 'Where the Blessed One' — and so forth in detail. By <s>Prabhāsa</s>, who was a potter-youth named <s>Kumbhakāra</s>, having performed service with water and ointment and the like, the first aspiration was made.

body.text: (IV.114, 115) tadāsya kṣāṃtiśīlapāramite paripūrṇe iti. cetasā tāvad akopataḥ kṣāṃtipāramitāparipūriḥ. kāyavāgbhyāṃ duśaritākaraṇāc chīlapāramitāparipūrir iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.114, 115) 'Then his perfections of patience and morality are complete' — the completion of the perfection of patience is through non-anger by the mind. The completion of the perfection of morality is through non-commission of misconduct by body and speech.

children.translated_text: 'Not in heaven, nor on earth' — and so forth in detail.

body.text: uddeśapadanyāyenoktaṃ.
body.translated_text: — stated according to the method of summary verses (<s>uddeśapada</s>).

children.text:
nāsmin loke na vaiśravaṇālaye
na marubhavane. divye sthāna
children.translated_text: 'Not in this world, nor in the abode of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, nor in the celestial dwelling of the <s>Marut</s>s, in the divine realm'

body.text: iti. tadvyaktyarthaṃ nirdeśapadāni.
body.translated_text: — these are the explanatory verses (<s>nirdeśapada</s>) for clarifying that.

body.text: iti. manuṣyaloke.
body.translated_text: — in the human world.

body.text: Tib. 94a
body.translated_text: 'The abode of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>' — in the realm of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> [gods]

body.text: vaiśravaṇālaya iti. cāturmahārājikasthāne.

children.translated_text: — in the dwelling of the <s>Marut</s>s, meaning the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven. This is the meaning.

body.text: yāmādisthāne. lokadhātvaṃtareṣv api tatsadṛśasyābhāvajñāpanārtham āha.
body.translated_text: — in the realms of <s>Yāma</s> and above. In order to convey the absence of anything similar even in other world-systems, he says:

children.translated_text: 'Not in the directions nor in the intermediate directions.'

body.text: atha na śraddhīyate.
body.translated_text: Now, if one does not believe,

body.text: naraḥ kaścid
body.translated_text: '[let] some person'

body.text: imāṃ
body.translated_text: 'this'

body.text: bahusattvādhyāsitāṃ. saha parvataiḥ kānanaiś ca.
body.translated_text: — inhabited by many beings, together with mountains and forests.

body.text: svayaṃ prastyavekṣatām ity abhiprāyaḥ. nava ca kalpāḥ pratyudāvartitā iti. tena vīryāraṃbheṇaikanavatyā kalpaiḥ paripūrṇā vīryapāramiteti kṛtvā. ata evoktam ekanavatyāṃ kalpeṣv ākṣiptam iti. bodheḥ pūrvasamanaṃtaram iti. kṣayānutpādajñānalakṣaṇāyā bodheḥ pūrvasamanaṃtaraṃ. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. paripūrṇapāramito hi bodhim adhigacchati. nāparipūrṇapāramita iti.
body.translated_text: — the intent is: let him examine it himself. 'And nine <s>kalpa</s>s were turned back' — by that exertion of energy, since in ninety-one <s>kalpa</s>s the perfection of energy was completed. Therefore it was stated: 'cast over ninety-one <s>kalpa</s>s.' 'Immediately preceding enlightenment' — immediately preceding the enlightenment characterized by the knowledge of destruction and non-arising (<s>kṣayānutpādajñāna</s>). For what reason? Because one who has completed the perfections attains enlightenment — not one whose perfections are incomplete.

body.text: (IV.116) yathāyogam iti. kiṃcit puṇyaṃ ca kriyā ca. kiṃcit puṇyaṃ ca kriyā ca. kiṃcit puṇyam eva. kriyā ca. kiṃcit puṇyaṃ ca vastu ca. kiṃcid vastv eveti. katham ity āha. tadyatheti vistaraḥ. karma ca te paṃthānaś ca. prāṇātipātādayaḥ sapta karmapathāḥ. karmasvābhāvyāc cetanāpathatvāc ca. trayas tv abhidhyādayaḥ paṃthāna eva karmaṇaś cetanākhyasyeti [Tib. 94b] karmapathāḥ. kāyavākkarma trividheti. puṇyaṃ tāvad iṣṭavipākatvāt. kriyā karmasvabhāvatvāt. vastu tatsamutthānacetanāyās tad adhiṣṭhāya pravṛtteḥ. tatsamutthāpikā cetanā kāyavākkarmasamutthāpikā. puṇyam iṣṭavipākatvāt. kriyā manaskarmatvāt. na vastu kriyānadhiṣṭhānatvāt. tatsahabhuvo vedanādayaḥ. iṣṭavipākatvāt puṇyam eva. na tu kriyādhiṣṭhānaṃ vā. tallakṣaṇābhāvāt. śīlamayam iti. pūrvavat traidhaṃ yojyaṃ. maitrī puṇyam iti. pūrvavad yojyaṃ. puṇyakriyāyāś ca vastu. tatsaṃprayuktāyā maitrīsaṃprayuktāyāś cetanāyāḥ maitrīmukhena maitrīvaśenābhisaṃskaraṇād abhisaṃcetanāt. tatsahabhūr maitrīsahabhūś cetanā śīlaṃ ca dhyānasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ puṇyaṃ ca kriyā ca pūrvavat. na hi dhyānasaṃvaraṃ pravartayeyam ity adhiṣṭhāya cetanā pravartate. tena na kriyādhiṣṭhānaṃ. anye tatsahabhuvo vedanādayaḥ puṇyam eva pūrvavat. tad evaṃ. dānamaye puṇyaṃ ca kriyā ca vastu ca. puṇyaṃ kriyā ca. punyaṃ ca. puṇyakriyāvastu. śīlamaye puṇyaṃ ca [Tib. 95a] kriyā ca kriyāvastu ca. puṇyakriyāvastu. bhāvanāmaye puṇyakriyāvastu ca. puṇyaṃ kriyā ca. puṇyaṃ ceti. puṇyakriyāvastu. avayavasarūpāṇām apy ekaśeṣa iṣyate. guṇo yaṅlukor iti yathā.
body.translated_text: (IV.116) 'As applicable' — some are merit and action; some are merit and action; some are merit only; and action; some are merit and substance; some are substance only. How? He says: 'that is to say' — and so forth in detail. They are both <s>karma</s> and paths. The seven action-paths beginning with killing are action-paths because of having the intrinsic nature of <s>karma</s> and because of being paths of volition (<s>cetanā</s>). But the three beginning with covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) are paths alone — paths of <s>karma</s>, which is called volition — hence action-paths. 'Bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> is threefold' — first, it is merit (<s>puṇya</s>) because of having a desirable maturation; action (<s>kriyā</s>) because of having the intrinsic nature of <s>karma</s>; and substance (<s>vastu</s>) because the volition originating it operates governing that. The volition that originates it — the volition that originates bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> — is merit because of having a desirable maturation; action because of being mental <s>karma</s>; but not substance, because it is not the ground of action. Its co-existent [<s>dharma</s>s] — feeling and the rest — are merit only, because of having a desirable maturation; but neither action-ground nor [having] that characteristic. 'Consisting of morality (<s>śīlamaya</s>)' — should be connected in three ways as before. '<s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) is merit' — should be connected as before. And it is substance of the basis of meritorious action — because of the volition associated with <s>maitrī</s> forming [its activity] by way of, under the influence of, <s>maitrī</s>. The volition co-existent with <s>maitrī</s>, and the morality included in the <s>dhyāna</s> restraint, are both merit and action as before. For the volition does not operate governing [it with the thought] 'I should produce the <s>dhyāna</s> restraint.' Therefore it is not the ground of action. Other co-existent [<s>dharma</s>s] — feeling and the rest — are merit only, as before. Thus, in the basis of meritorious action consisting of giving (<s>dānamaya</s>): merit, action, and substance; merit and action; and merit — [these are] the basis of meritorious action. In that consisting of morality: merit, action, and action-substance — [this is] the basis of meritorious action. In that consisting of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>): the basis of meritorious action, and merit and action, and merit — [this is] the basis of meritorious action. Even for words having the form of components, the singular remainder (<s>ekaśeṣa</s>) is accepted — as in the rule '<s>guṇo yaṅlukoḥ</s>.'

body.text: (IV.117) yad api dīyate tad dānam iti deyaṃ vastu karmaṇi lyuḍ iti kṛtvā.
body.translated_text: (IV.117) 'What is given, that is a gift (<s>dāna</s>)' — the thing to be given, taking the <s>lyuḍ</s> suffix in the sense of the object of action.

children.translated_text: 'That by which one gives is a gift' —

body.text: iti. iha tu kuśalam iṣṭaṃ dānam iti. deyasya hi vastrāder avyākṛtatvaṃ. rāgādibhir apīty ādiśabdena krodherṣyādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. But here, a wholesome, desirable [act] is the gift. For the thing to be given — cloth and the rest — is indeterminate. 'Through passion and the rest too' — by the word 'and the rest,' anger, envy, and the like are included.

children.translated_text: 'With the desire for worship and kindness' —

body.text: caityāparinirvṛtebhyaḥ pūjā. indriyamahābhūtānugrahakāmā tayā. yena kalāpeneti
body.translated_text: worship is to <s>caitya</s>s (shrines) and those who have not yet attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Desiring kindness toward the faculties and great elements — with that [desire]. 'By whichever collection'

body.text: cittacaittakalāpena.
body.translated_text: — by the collection of mind and mental factors.

body.text: iti. paṃca skaṃdhāḥ. kāyavāgvijñaptis tad avijñaptir api vā rūpaskaṃdho draṣṭavyaḥ. svabhāve caiṣa mayad iti. na vikārādiṣu. tadyathā tṛṇamayaṃ gṛham iti. na tṛṇānāṃ vikāro 'sti. tais tu nirvikārair eva tat kṛtam ity atas tṛṇamayaṃ tṛṇasvabhāvaṃ tad iti gamyate. tatsvābhāvye 'pi sati. tadvikāratāṃ parikalpya mayat kriyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. tatprakṛtivacane mayad ity anena vā lakṣaṇena mayad vidhīyate. evaṃ parṇamayaṃ bhājanam ity etad api vaktavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. The five aggregates. The bodily and vocal <s>vijñapti</s>, and the <s>avijñapti</s> thereof — should be seen as the form aggregate.
