'And the <s>maya</s> [suffix] is in the sense of own-nature' — not in the senses of modification and the like. Just as 'a house made of straw' (<s>tṛṇamaya</s>) — there is no modification of straw; rather, with straw unchanged, that is made — therefore 'made of straw' is understood as 'having straw as its nature.' Even when there is something of that nature, the intent is: having imagined it to be a modification of that, the <s>maya</s> suffix is applied. Or alternatively, the <s>maya</s> suffix is ordained by the rule '<s>tatprakṛtivacane mayaṭ</s>' — 'in the statement of having that as its nature.' Similarly, 'a vessel made of leaves' (<s>parṇamaya</s>) — this too should be stated.

body.text: (IV.118ab) sthāpayitvā dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyam iti. tad ubhayārtham iti kṛtvā sthāpyate. tad vipākabhūmer [Tib. 95b] atyaṃtasamatikrāṃtatvāt. kāmadhātor atyaṃtasamatikrāṃtatvād ity arthaḥ. kāmadhātur hi dānasya vipākabhūmir iti.
body.translated_text: (IV.118ab) 'Setting aside [that] to be experienced in the present life' — that is set aside for both purposes — because of having completely transcended the maturation-ground — meaning: because of having completely transcended the Desire Realm. For the Desire Realm is the maturation-ground of giving.

body.text: (IV.119) śrutādiguṇayukta iti. ādiśabdena tyāgaprajñālpecchatādiguṇayuktaḥ. satkṛtyādi dadātīti. satkṛtyety ādir asyeti satkṛtyādi. kriyāviśeṣaṇam etat. yathākramaṃ catvāro viśeṣā iti. sātkṛtyadātā satkāralābhī bhavati. svahastadātā udārebhyo bhogebhyo ruciṃ labhate. kāladātā kāle bhogāl labhate. nātikrāṃtakālāt. yān na bhoktum evāsamarthaḥ. parān anupahatyadātā 'nācchedyāṃ bhogāṃ labhate.
body.translated_text: (IV.119) 'Endowed with learning and other qualities' — by the word 'and the rest,' endowed with the qualities of generosity, wisdom, few desires, and the like. 'Gives with respect and the like' — '<s>satkṛtya</s> and the like' is the beginning thereof. This qualifies the action. 'Respectively, four distinctions' — one who gives with respect obtains respect in return. One who gives with one's own hand obtains relish for excellent enjoyments. One who gives at the right time obtains enjoyments at the right time — not past the proper time — which one is not even unable to consume. One who gives without harming others obtains possessions that cannot be taken away.

body.text: (IV.120) ṛtusukhasparśāni cāsyāṃgānīti. śīte uṣṇāni. uṣṇe śītāni. sādhāraṇe sādhāraṇāni.
body.translated_text: (IV.120) 'And its limbs are [things] pleasant to touch according to the season' — in cold [weather], warm things; in hot [weather], cool things; in moderate [weather], moderate things.

body.text: (IV.121ab) śītalikādiṣu ceti. ādiśabdena vardalikāvarṣalikādiṣu. yathāsūtram uktam etat. yathā mātāpitror iti. upakāritvaviśeṣāt kārāpakārau mahāphalau tayor bhavata ity artho 'vagaṃtavyaḥ. ṛkṣamṛgajātakādyudāharaṇāt vipāka iti. evaṃ ṛkṣamṛgayor guhāṃ praveśya gātroṣmaśītopanayenohyamānanadyuttāraṇena vopakāriṇor apakārakaraṇena sadyo 'ṃgapātāt. [Tib. 96a] ādiśabdena kapijātakādy udāhāryaṃ. śīlavate dattvā śatasahasraguṇo vipāka ity evamādīti. ādiśabdena srotaāpattiphalapratipannakāya dattvā aprameyo bhavati vipākas tato 'prameyataraḥ srotaāpannāyetyādi.
body.translated_text: (IV.121ab) 'In cold spells and the like too' — by the word 'and the like,' in heat waves, rain storms, and the like. This is stated according to the <s>sūtra</s>. 'As toward mother and father' — from the special nature of their being benefactors, both benevolent and harmful [acts] toward them are of great fruit — this meaning should be understood. 'From the examples such as the bear-and-deer <s>jātaka</s>, maturation' — thus, when a bear and deer entered [another's] cave, the one to whom they were benefactors — through warming with body-heat and carrying across a swollen river — when he harmed them, his limbs fell off immediately. By the word 'and the like,' the monkey <s>jātaka</s> and others should be cited. 'Having given to one of morality (<s>śīlavat</s>), the maturation is a hundred-thousandfold' — and so forth. By the word 'and the rest': having given to one established on the path to stream-entry, the maturation is immeasurable; from that, even more immeasurable to a stream-enterer — and so forth.

body.text: (IV.121cd) tat sthāpayitveti. anaṃtaroktaṃ bodhisattvadānaṃ. tad dhi samyaksaṃbodhyarthaṃ sarvasattvārthaṃ ca. śeṣaṃ sugamatvān na vibhaktam iti. yad etad adān me dānam ity evamādikaṃ. adān me dānam iti. dattam anena me
body.translated_text: (IV.121cd) 'Setting that aside' — the giving of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> just mentioned. For that is for the sake of perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) and for the sake of all beings. 'The rest is not elaborated because of being easy to understand' — that which begins with 'he has not given me a gift.' 'He has not given me a gift' — meaning: formerly a gift was given by him to me

body.text: pūrvam iti dānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ. dāsyati me dānam iti caturthaṃ. dattapūrvaṃ me pitṛbhiś ca pitāmahaiś ceti dānam iti paṃcamaṃ. svargārthaṃ dānam ṣaṣṭhaṃ. kīrtyarthaṃ saptamaṃ. cittālaṃkārārthaṃ yāvad uttamārthasya prāptaye dānam ity aṣṭamaṃ. cittālaṃkārārthaṃ ṛddhyarthaṃ. cittapariṣkārārthaṃ aṣṭau cittapariṣkārāḥ mārgāṃgāni. tadarthaṃ. yogasaṃbhārārthaṃ yoganidānārthaṃ. uttamārthasya prāptir arhattvaṃ nirvāṇasya vā prāptiḥ. tasmai prāptaye dānaṃ. caturbhedam apy ekam aṣṭamaṃ bhavati. nirvāṇaprāpakam evaitad iti kṛtvā. sugamam uktam ācāryeṇa.
body.translated_text: — this is the third [type of giving]. 'He will give me a gift' — this is the fourth. 'It was formerly given by my fathers and grandfathers — this is a gift' — this is the fifth. 'Giving for the sake of heaven' is the sixth. 'For the sake of fame' is the seventh. 'For the sake of adorning the mind, up to for the attainment of the supreme goal' is the eighth. 'For the sake of adorning the mind' — for the sake of psychic powers. 'For the sake of equipping the mind' — the eight equipments of the mind are the factors of the path; for the sake of those. 'For the sake of the provisions for practice' — for the sake of the basis of practice. 'The attainment of the supreme goal' is <s>Arhatship</s> or the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Giving for the sake of that attainment. Though it has four divisions, it is a single eighth [type] — considering that this alone leads to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. This was stated by the <s>Ācārya</s> as easy to understand.

body.text: (IV.122) [Tib. 96b] caturvidhe kṣetraviśeṣa iti. gatiduḥkhopakāriguṇakṣetre katamasmin pakṣa iti. yasmād asya gatikṣetratā guṇakṣetratā ca na saṃbhavati tasmāt pṛcchati. samaviṣamasya prakāśayiteti dharmadharmasya.
body.translated_text: (IV.122) 'In the fourfold field-distinction' — the field of destiny, of suffering, of benefaction, and of qualities — in which category [does this fall]? He asks because neither the destiny-field nor the quality-field is applicable to him. 'Of one who is equal and unequal' — of one who has both <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.

body.text: (IV.123) vipākanaiyamyāvasthānād iti. niyatavipākadānāvasthānād ity arthaḥ. kasyacit kṣetravaśenaiveti. tadyathā. sāmānyapuruṣavadhāt pitṛvadhaḥ. tatraiva kṣetre punar adhiṣṭhānavaśād iti. karmapathavaśāt. katham ity āha. mātāpitroḥ prāṇātipātanāt guru karma na tv evam adattādikāt guru. na hi mātāpitror dravyāpaharaṇakarma tadvadhavat guru bhavati. tadvadhasyānaṃtaryasvabhāvatvād ādiśabdena mṛṣāvādapaiśunyādigrahaṇaṃ. evam anyad api yojyam iti. kasyacit prayogaviśeṣeṇa guru sampadyate vipākanaiyamyāvasthānāt. kasyacic cetanāviśeṣeṇa. kasyacid āśayaviśeṣeṇa.
body.translated_text: (IV.123) 'Because of the state of certainty of maturation' — meaning: because of the state of giving with certain maturation. 'For some, by the power of the field alone' — for example, killing of a father from killing an ordinary person — [it is heavier] in that very field. And 'by the power of the basis in that very [field]' — by the power of the action-path. How? He says: 'from the killing of mother and father, the <s>karma</s> is heavy, but not similarly from taking what is not given and the like.' For the <s>karma</s> of stealing the property of mother and father is not as heavy as killing them — because killing them has the nature of <s>ānantarya</s> (immediate-retribution). By the word 'and the like,' false speech, slander, and the rest are included. Similarly, other [cases] should be connected. 'For some, it becomes heavy through the distinction of effort' — from the state of certainty of maturation. 'For some, through the distinction of volition. For some, through the distinction of intention.'

body.text: (IV.124) nābuddhipūrvaṃ na sahasā kṛtam iti. atha vā nābuddhipūrvaṃ kṛtam idaṃ kuryām ity asaṃciṃtya kṛtaṃ. tan nopacitam. avyākṛtaṃ hi tat karma. na sahasā kṛtam iti. buddhipūrvam api na sahasā kṛtaṃ. yad abhyāsena bhāṣyākṣepān mṛṣāvādādyanuṣṭhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tad akuśalaṃ [Tib. 97a] na punar upacitaṃ. yāvat tribhir iti. kāyavāṅmanoduścaritaiḥ. niṣpratipakṣaṃ ceti. pratideśanādipratipakṣābhāvataḥ. akuśalaṃ cākuśalaparicāraṃ ceti. yaḥ kṛtvāpy anumodata iti. vipākadāne niyatam iti. puṣṭākuśalalakṣaṇasamutpādāt. evaṃ kuśalam api yojyam iti. kathaṃ. saṃcetanataḥ saṃciṃtya kṛtaṃ bhavati. nābuddhipūrvakṛtaṃ bhavati. tadyathā. avyākṛtena cittena pāṣāṇaṃ dadāmīti suvarṇapiṇḍaṃ dadyāt. kṛtaṃ tan na punar upacitaṃ. avyākṛtaṃ hi tat karma. na sahasā kṛtaṃ. yathā bhāṣyākṣepāt satyavacanaṃ kṛtaṃ tat kuśalaṃ na punar upacitaṃ. kaścid ekena sucaritena sugatiṃ yāti. kaścid yāvat tribhiḥ. kaścid ekena karmapathena. kaścid yāvad daśabhiḥ. tatra yo yāvatā gacchati. tasminn asamāpte kṛtaṃ karma nopacitaṃ. samāpte tūpacitaṃ. evaṃ yāvad vipākadāne niyatam iti. saṃbhavato yojyam.
body.translated_text: (IV.124) 'Not done without deliberation' — or alternatively, 'not done without deliberation' means: done without having thought 'I should do this' — that is not accumulated. For that <s>karma</s> is indeterminate. 'Not done hastily' — even though done with deliberation, not done hastily — that which is done through habitual utterance as false speech and the like, that is unwholesome but not accumulated. 'Up to through three' — through bodily, vocal, and mental misconduct. 'And without antidote' — from the absence of an antidote such as confession and the like. 'And unwholesome, accompanied by unwholesome service' — one who even after doing [an unwholesome act] rejoices in it. 'Is determined in the giving of maturation' — because of the arising of the characteristics of a reinforced unwholesome [action]. 'Similarly, the wholesome too should be connected' — how? It is done deliberately — done with deliberation. Not done without deliberation — for example, with indeterminate mind, intending 'I give a stone,' one might give a lump of gold. That is done but not accumulated — for that <s>karma</s> is indeterminate. Not done hastily — as when truthful speech is spoken through habitual utterance, that is wholesome but not accumulated. Some go to a good destiny through a single good conduct; some through up to three. Some through a single action-path; some through up to ten. Therein, for one who goes through however many [action-paths], the <s>karma</s> done before those are complete is not accumulated; but when they are complete, it is accumulated — and so on, up to: it is determined in the giving of maturation — this should be connected as applicable.

body.text: (IV.125ab) caitye sarāgasyeti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: (IV.125ab) 'To a <s>caitya</s>, of one with passion' — and so forth in detail.

children.translated_text: 'For the benefit of self, others, or both' —

body.text: atra. puṇyam eva tyāgānvayam apaśyann āha. kasyacid apy anugrahābhāvād. iti. sati hi pratigrahītari yuktaṃ tyāgānvayaṃ puṇyaṃ. tatra hi prītyanugraheṇa [Tib. 97b] grahītā yujyata iti.
body.translated_text: here. Not seeing merit as a consequence of relinquishment alone, he says: 'because of the absence of benefit to anyone.' For when there is a recipient, it is fitting that merit follows from relinquishment. For in that case, the recipient is gratified by the joy and benefit [of receiving].

children.translated_text: 'Like <s>maitrī</s> and the like, [merit arises] even without a recipient' —

body.text: maitryādiṣv iva maitryādivat. agṛhṇati asati pratigrāhake puṇyaṃ bhavati. asaty api parānugrahe. kuśalamūlādibalādhānāt. tathā hy atīte pi puṇavati tathāgatādau. tad bhaktikṛtaṃ caityadānaṃ puṇyaṃ bhavati. dānamānakriyā tarhi vyarthā prāpnotīti. yadi svacittād eva puṇyaṃ bhavec cittenaiva dānamānāv anuṣṭheyau. tata eva puṇyaprāpteḥ. na. tatkarmasamutthāpikāyā bhakteḥ prakṛṣṭataratvāt. naitad evaṃ. kasmāt. yasmād dānamānau bhagavataś cittamātreṇa ciṃtayato yā bhaktiḥ. tata iyaṃ dānamānau kurvato bhaktiḥ prakṛṣṭatarā. kāyavākkarmaṇor api pravartanāt. cittamātreṇa hi cintayato bhaktiḥ kāyavākkarmaṇī na pravartayataḥ. yathā hīti vistaraḥ. yathā hi śatruṃ hanmīti kṛtābhiprāyasya kasyacit tatsamutthitaṃ tadabhiprāyasamutthitaṃ kāyavākkarma śatrusaṃjñayā śatrur ayaṃ na tāvan mriyata ity anayā saṃjñayā tasmin mṛte 'pi kurvato bahutaram apuṇyaṃ jāyate cetanānubaṃdhāt. nābhiprāyamātreṇa kriyāśūnyena. tathā hy atīte 'pi parinirvṛte 'pi bhagavati tadbhaktisamutthāṃ śāstṛbhaktisamutthāṃ dānamānakriyāṃ pṛṣṭhabhūtām iva kurvato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ jāyate. na bhaktimātreṇa kriyāśūnyeneti.
body.translated_text: as in <s>maitrī</s> and the like — like <s>maitrī</s> and the like. Even without a recipient, merit arises — even without benefit to another — because of the strengthening of wholesome roots and the like. For thus, even when the <s>Tathāgata</s> and the like are of the past [i.e., have passed away], that <s>caitya</s>-offering made with devotion is merit. 'Then the actions of gift-giving and worship would be pointless' — if merit arose from one's own mind alone, gift-giving and worship could be practiced by mind alone, since merit would come from that alone. No — because the devotion originating from those actions is even more excellent. This is not so. Why? Because the devotion of one who merely thinks with mind about the <s>Bhagavān</s>, compared to the devotion of one who performs gift-giving and worship, is less excellent — because bodily and vocal actions also operate [in the latter]. For when one merely thinks with mind, the devotion does not set in motion bodily and vocal actions. 'Just as' — and so forth in detail. Just as one who has formed the intention 'I shall kill my enemy,' performing bodily and vocal action originating from that, from that intention — with the perception 'this is my enemy,' even when that [enemy] has died, performing [actions] with the perception 'this enemy has not yet died' — much more demerit arises because of the continuity of volition. Not from mere intention devoid of action. Similarly, even when the <s>Bhagavān</s> has passed away, even when he has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, for one who performs the acts of gift-giving and worship originating from devotion to the Teacher — which are, as it were, subsequent [to his presence] — much more merit arises. Not from mere devotion devoid of action.

body.text: (IV.125cd) kukṣetre tarhy [Tib. 98a] aniṣṭaphalaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. taskarādibhyo dānam āniṣṭaphalam iti nirgraṃthāḥ. sukṣetre hīṣṭaphalaṃ. kukṣetre tu viparītam ity ato bravīti.
body.translated_text: (IV.125cd) 'In a bad field, then, the fruit would be undesirable' — the <s>Nirgrantha</s>s [say]: giving to thieves and the like has an undesirable fruit. For in a good field, the fruit is desirable; but in a bad field, the opposite — therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'Even in a bad field, the fruit is desirable, because of the non-reversal of fruit and seed' —

body.text: iti. na kṣetraviśeṣād iṣṭaṃ phalam iti brūmaḥ. kiṃ tarhi. viśiṣṭam iti. na hi sukṣetre prāṇatipātādibījasyeṣṭaṃ phalaṃ bhavatīti. kukṣetre 'pi hi phalasya mṛdvīkāphalasya bījāt mṛdvīkābījād. aviparyayo dṛṣṭaḥ. mṛdvīkāphalam eva madhuraṃ dṛṣṭam ity arthaḥ. na tu niṃbaphalam evaṃ. niṃbabījān niṃbaphalam eveti. tiktam iti. mṛdvīkābījaṃ kuśalasyodāharaṇaṃ. niṃbabījam akuśalasya.
body.translated_text: thus. We do not say that a special field produces a desired fruit. What then? A superior one. For in a good field, the seed of killing and the like does not produce a desired fruit. Even in a poor field, from the seed of a grape — from a grape seed — no reversal is seen. The meaning is: a grape fruit is seen to be sweet alone. But not so a <s>nīmba</s> (neem) fruit. From a neem seed, only a neem fruit — [which is] bitter. The grape seed is an illustration of the wholesome. The neem seed is [an illustration] of the unwholesome.

body.text: iti. prāṇatipātādilakṣaṇaṃ prakṛtisāvadyaṃ rūpaṃ dauḥśīlyaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. Form characterized by killing of living beings and the like, blameworthy by nature (<s>prakṛtisāvadya</s>), is immorality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>).

body.text: prajñaptisāvadyatvāt. samāttaśikṣasya tu tadadhyācārād dauḥśīlyam iti. gṛhītatadviramaṇasya bhagavadvacanānādarād dauḥśīlyaṃ jāyate. arthād uktaṃ bhavati. asamāttaśikṣasya na duḥśīlyam iti.
body.translated_text: because of being blameworthy by designation (<s>prajñaptisāvadya</s>). But for one who has undertaken the training, immorality arises from transgressing that. Immorality arises from disrespecting the word of the Blessed One by one who has accepted that abstention. The meaning is implicitly stated: for one who has not undertaken the training, there is no immorality [of this type].

body.text: iti. catvāro guṇā asyeti caturguṇaṃ. dauḥśīlyena yathokteneti.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Having four qualities' means fourfold. 'By immorality as described' —

body.text: ity anena. [Tib. 98b] lobhādibhir iti. na tair dauḥśīlyahetubhiḥ samudācaradbhir upahataṃ bhavati. dauḥśīlyavipakṣāśritam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: by this [verse]. [Tib. 98b] 'By desire and the rest' — it is not damaged by those causes of immorality when they are active. The meaning is: it relies on the opposite of immorality.

body.text: maulaiḥ karmapathair viśuddham iti. prāṇatipātādibhir maulair akhaṇḍitam ity arthaḥ. sāmaṃtakair viśuddham iti. prāṇātipātādiprayogair adūṣitam ity arthaḥ. vitarkair iti. kāmavitarkādibhiḥ. smṛtyānuparigṛhītam iti. kāyādismṛtyupasthānair dṛḍhīkṛtaṃ. śīlasmṛtyā vānuparigṛhītaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Purified by root action-paths' — the meaning is: unbroken by the root [action-paths] of killing and the like. 'Purified by adjacent [actions]' — the meaning is: not corrupted by the preparatory [actions] of killing and the like. 'By discursive thoughts' — by thoughts of sensual desire and the like. 'Guarded by mindfulness' — strengthened by the foundations of mindfulness such as mindfulness of body and the rest. Or: guarded by mindfulness of morality.

body.text: āśāstiśīlam iti. āśāstiḥ prārthanā. yad bhavabhogasatkāratṛṣṇākṛtam iti. bhave bhoge ca satkāre ca yā tṛṣṇā. tayā yat samāttam ity arthaḥ. samyagdṛṣṭikānām iti. buddhaśāsanapratipannānāṃ. anyatīrthikānāṃ hi na bodhyaṃgānukūlam asaddṛṣṭikatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'Aspirational morality' (<s>āśāstiśīla</s>) — <s>āśāsti</s> means aspiration or prayer. 'That which is made by craving for existence, enjoyment, and honor' — the craving that is for existence, enjoyment, and honor — that by which [morality] is undertaken — this is the meaning. 'Of those with right view' — of those who have entered the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching. For those of other traditions, [their morality] is not conducive to the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), because of having wrong views.

body.text: (IV.127ab)
body.translated_text: (IV.127ab)

body.text: iti. samāhitagrahaṇam asamāhitanivṛttyarthaṃ. kuśalagrahaṇaṃ samāhitāsvādanāsaṃprayuktakliṣṭadhyānanivṛttyarthaṃ. tat samāhitakuśalasadṛśam utpadyate. samādhisvabhāvasahabhū yad iti. samādhisvabhāvaṃ tena ca saha bhavati yad ity arthaḥ. tad dhi samāhitam [Tib. 99a] iti vistaraḥ. tat samāhitaṃ kuśalam atyarthaṃ cittaṃ saṃvāsayati. bhāvayati. asamāhitam api vāsayati. na tv evam atyartham iti darśayati. katham ity āha. guṇais tanmayīkaraṇāt saṃtateḥ. yasmāt samādhiguṇais tanmayī kriyate cittasaṃtatiḥ. atra dṛṣṭāṃtam āha. puṣpais tilavāsanāvad iti. yathā puṣpais tilā bhāvyaṃte. puṣpagaṃdhamayīkaraṇāt. tadvat. tad idam uktaṃ bhavati. bhāvanā vāsanā. tatsvabhāvaṃ puṇyaṃ bhāvanāmayam iti.
body.translated_text: thus. The mention of 'concentrated' is for the purpose of excluding the non-concentrated. The mention of 'wholesome' is for the purpose of excluding concentrated [states that are] associated with tasting [absorption] or afflicted concentration (<s>kliṣṭadhyāna</s>). That arises similar to concentrated wholesome [karma]. 'That which exists together with the nature of concentration' — the meaning is: that which has the nature of concentration and exists together with it. 'For that indeed is concentrated' — and so forth in detail. That concentrated wholesome [karma] perfumes the mind exceedingly. It cultivates [the mind]. Non-concentrated [karma] also perfumes [it], but not to such an extent — this is shown. How? He says: 'Because of making the continuum saturated with qualities.' Because the mental continuum is made saturated with the qualities of concentration. Here he gives an illustration: 'Like the perfuming of sesame seeds with flowers.' Just as sesame seeds are perfumed by flowers — by making them saturated with the fragrance of flowers — in the same way. This is what has been said: cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) is perfuming (<s>vāsanā</s>). That which has its nature as merit is merit born of cultivation.

body.text: (IV.127cd) atha śīlaṃ bhāvanā ca kasmai saṃvartata iti vākyaśeṣato 'rthaṃ pṛcchati.
body.translated_text: (IV.127cd) Now, asking 'For whose benefit does morality and cultivation conduce?' — this is the remainder of the sentence.

body.text: iti. śīlaṃ prādhānyena svargāya bhavati. anyat tu na prādhānyena svargāya bhavati. kim anyat. dānaṃ. dānam api hi svargāya saṃbhavati. śīlam api
body.translated_text: thus. Morality primarily conduces to heaven. But another thing does not primarily conduce to heaven. What other thing? Giving. For giving too is possible for [attaining] heaven. Morality too

body.text: visaṃyogāya saṃbhavati. śamathavipaśyanayoḥ śīlapratiṣṭhānatvāt. bhāvanā prādhānyena visaṃyogāya. sākṣādvisaṃyogaprāpakatvāt. prahāṇamārgasaṃgṛhītatvād vā. puṇyakriyāvastuprasaṃgenedam upanyasyate.
body.translated_text: is possible for [attaining] separation (<s>visaṃyoga</s>). Because tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>) and insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>) are grounded in morality. Cultivation primarily [conduces] to separation — because of directly bringing about the attainment of separation. Or because of being included in the path of abandonment. This is presented in connection with the bases of meritorious activity (<s>puṇyakriyāvastu</s>).

body.text: (IV.128ab) sūtra uktaṃ. catvāraḥ pudgalāḥ brāhmaṃ puṇyaṃ prasavaṃti. apratiṣṭhite pṛthivīpradeśe tathāgatasya śārīraṃ stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati. ayaṃ prathamaḥ pudgalo brāhmaṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati. cāturdeśe bhikṣusaṃghe ārāmaṃ niryātayati tatraiva cārāme vihāraṃ [Tib. 99b] pratiṣṭhāpayati. ayaṃ dvitīyaḥ pudgalo brāhmaṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati. bhinnaṃ tathāgataśrāvakasaṃghaṃ pratisaṃdadhāti. ayaṃ tṛtīyaḥ pudgalo brāhmaṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati. maitrīsahagatena cittenāvaireṇāsaṃspardhenāvyābādhena vipulena mahadgatenāpramāṇena subhāvitenaikāṃ diśam adhimucya spharitvopasaṃpadya viharati. tathā dvitīyāṃ. tathā tṛtīyāṃ. tathā caturthīm. ity ūrdhvam adhas tiryak sarvataḥ sarvam imaṃ lokaṃ spharitvopasaṃpadya viharati. ayaṃ caturthaḥ pudgalo brāhmaṃ puṇyaṃ prasavatīti. yal lakṣaṇavipākasya karmaṇaḥ parimāṇajñāpanāyoktam iti. yad uktaṃ saṃnikṛṣṭaṃ bodhisattvaṃ sthāpayitvā. yāvatsarvasattvānāṃ bhogaphalam ity evamādi.
body.translated_text: (IV.128ab) It is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Four persons generate <s>brāhma</s> merit. One who, in a region of the earth where [a <s>stūpa</s>] has not been established, erects a <s>stūpa</s> for the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — this first person generates <s>brāhma</s> merit. One who, to the community of monks of the four directions, bestows a monastery and therein in that very monastery establishes a dwelling [Tib. 99b] — this second person generates <s>brāhma</s> merit. One who reunites the divided community of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s disciples — this third person generates <s>brāhma</s> merit. One who, with a mind accompanied by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), without enmity, without rivalry, without harming, vast and great, immeasurable and well-cultivated, pervading one direction with resolve, having pervaded it, dwells having reached [it]. Likewise the second. Likewise the third. Likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, this entire world, having pervaded it, dwells having reached [it] — this fourth person generates <s>brāhma</s> merit.' That which was stated for making known the measure of <s>karma</s> that produces the major marks. What was stated, 'Setting aside a <s>bodhisattva</s> in his final birth,' up to: 'the enjoyment-fruit of all beings' — and so forth.

body.text: idaṃ brāhmaṃ puṇyam iti. brahmaṇām idaṃ brāhmaṃ. brahmapurohitāś cātra brahmaśabdenocyate. kasmāt. brahmapurohitānāṃ kalpāyuṣkatvāt. brahmapurohitānāṃ hi kalpam āyur uktaṃ. anena ca karmaṇā kalpaṃ svargeṣu modate.
body.translated_text: 'This is <s>brāhma</s> merit' — belonging to <s>Brahmā</s>, this is <s>brāhma</s>. And here, by the word '<s>Brahmā</s>' the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> [gods] are meant. Why? Because the <s>Brahmapurohita</s>s have a lifespan of one <s>kalpa</s>. For the lifespan of the <s>Brahmapurohita</s>s is stated to be one <s>kalpa</s>. And through this <s>karma</s>, one rejoices in the heavens for a <s>kalpa</s>.

children.text: brāhmaṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati. kalpaṃ svargeṣu modata
children.translated_text: 'One generates <s>brāhma</s> merit. One rejoices in the heavens for a <s>kalpa</s>' —

body.text: iti. nikāyāṃtarapāṭhavacanāt. tatsādharmyād etad brāhmaṃ puṇyam ucyate. nanu ca kāmadhātau nāsti kuśalasya karṃaṇaḥ kalpaṃ vipāka iti. satyam ekasya nāsti. [Tib. 100a] ekādhiṣṭhānās tu bahvyaś cātanā bhavaṃti. yāsāṃ krameṇa kalpapramāṇaṃ svārgikaṃ phalam abhinirvartate. cyutasya punas tatraiva janmasaṃdhānāt.
body.translated_text: because of the statement from another school's recension. Because of similarity to that, this is called '<s>brāhma</s> merit.' But is there not, in the Desire Realm, no maturation of a <s>kalpa</s> for a single wholesome <s>karma</s>? True — for a single one there is not. [Tib. 100a] But many volitions (<s>cetanā</s>) having a single basis exist, whose heavenly fruit, in sequence, produces a measure of a <s>kalpa</s> — because of reconnecting to birth in that very [place] after death.

body.text: bṛhatpuṇyaṃ brāhmam ity apare.
body.translated_text: Others [say]: great merit is <s>brāhma</s>.

body.text: ity. ādiśabdena dvādaśānām aṃgānāṃ grahaṇaṃ. sūtrageyavyākaraṇagāthodānanidānāvadānetivṛttakajātakavaipulyādbhutadharmopadeśā iti dvādaśānām aṃgānāṃ. akliṣṭadeśaneti. akliṣṭacittasamutthāpitety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. By the word 'and so forth,' the twelve divisions [of scripture] are grasped: <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s>, <s>gāthā</s>, <s>udāna</s>, <s>nidāna</s>, <s>avadāna</s>, <s>itivṛttaka</s>, <s>jātaka</s>, <s>vaipulya</s>, <s>adbhutadharma</s>, and <s>upadeśa</s> — of these twelve divisions. 'Unafflicted teaching' — meaning: produced by an unafflicted mind.

body.text: (IV.129) puṇyabhāgīyam iti. puṇyasya bhāgaḥ prāptir iti puṇyabhāgaḥ. iṣṭaphalaprāptir
body.translated_text: (IV.129) 'Merit-conducive' (<s>puṇyabhāgīya</s>) — a portion (<s>bhāga</s>) of merit means the attainment of merit — the portion of merit. The meaning is

body.text: ity arthaḥ. tasmai hitaṃ puṇyabhāgīyaṃ. ata evoktaṃ yad iṣṭavipākam iti. tatprāptyanukūlam iti. atha vā trayo bhāgāḥ. puṇyo bhāgaḥ apuṇyo bhāgaḥ aniṃjyo bhāgaḥ. tasmai hitaṃ puṇyabhāgīyaṃ. atha vā puṇyaṃ bhajata iti puṇyabhāk. puṇyabhāg eva puṇyabhāgīyaṃ. svārthe kapratyayaḥ. evaṃ mokṣabhāgīyaṃ. atha vā saṃsārabhāgo mokṣabhāgaś ceti dvau bhāgau. [Tib. 100b] tatra yan mokṣabhāgāya hitaṃ. tan mokṣabhāgīyaṃ. mokṣaprāptir vā mokṣabhāgaḥ. tasmai hitaṃ. tatprāptyanukūlam iti mokṣabhāgīyaṃ. tasya lakṣaṇaṃ paścād vakṣyate. evaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyam api yojyaṃ. paścād vyākhyāsyāma iti.
body.translated_text: : the attainment of a desired fruit. Conducive to that is 'merit-conducive.' Therefore it was said: 'that which has desired maturation.' 'Favorable to the attainment of that.' Or alternatively, there are three portions: the merit portion, the demerit portion, and the imperturbable (<s>āniñjya</s>) portion. Conducive to the [merit] portion is 'merit-conducive.' Or alternatively, one who partakes of merit is 'merit-partaking' (<s>puṇyabhāk</s>). 'Merit-partaking' itself is 'merit-conducive' — the <s>ka</s> suffix is used in the reflexive sense. Similarly for 'liberation-conducive' (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>). Or alternatively, there are two portions: the <s>saṃsāra</s> portion and the liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) portion. [Tib. 100b] Therein, that which is conducive to the liberation portion — that is 'liberation-conducive.' Or: the attainment of liberation is the liberation portion. Conducive to that — favorable to the attainment of that — is 'liberation-conducive.' Its characteristic will be stated later. Similarly, 'penetration-conducive' (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) should also be construed. 'We shall explain later' —

body.text: ity atra. karmādhikāreṇaiṣāṃ karmasvabhāvānāṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate.
body.translated_text: here. Their characteristic as having the nature of <s>karma</s> is stated in connection with the topic of <s>karma</s>.

body.text: (IV.130) yad idaṃ loka ityādi.
body.translated_text: (IV.130) 'What is [known] in the world' — and so forth.

body.text: iti. sacittacaitasikakalāpaṃ. yena tat kāyakarmotthāpyate. tat kāyakarma sasamutthānaṃ yogapravartitaṃ. lipir mudrā ca. kāraṇe kāryopacārāt. yena hi kāyakarmaṇā lipir likhyate mudrā vā khanyate. sā lipir mudrā sa śāstre 'bhiprete. na yathā loke. hy akṣaracihnaṃ pustakādau lipir iṣyate. akṣarānakṣaracihnaṃ ca mudreti. gaṇanā kāvyaṃ ca vākkarma. yogapravartitaṃ sasamutthānam iti vartate. paṃcaskaṃdhasvabhāvānīti. lipimudrayoḥ kāyakarma rūpaskaṃdhaḥ. gaṇanākāvyayor vākkarma rūpaskaṃdhaḥ. vedanādayas tūbhayatrāpi samutthānabhūtāś catvāraḥ skaṃdhā iti. paṃcaskaṃdhasvabhāvāny etāni bhavaṃti. yan manasā saṃkalanaṃ dharmāṇām iti. ekaṃ dve trīṇīty evamādi sā saṃkhyā. [Tib. 101a] yat tu vācā na manasā sā gaṇanety ābhidhārmikāḥ. iyaṃ ca saṃkhyā saparivāragrahaṇāc catuskaṃdhasvabhāvā.
body.translated_text: meaning: together with its aggregate of mind and mental factors (<s>cittacaittasikakalāpa</s>). By which that bodily <s>karma</s> is produced — that bodily <s>karma</s> together with its origination is 'set in motion by application' (<s>yogapravartita</s>). Writing (<s>lipi</s>) and seal-stamping (<s>mudrā</s>) — [these are designated thus] by figurative application of the effect to the cause. For by whatever bodily <s>karma</s> writing is written or a seal is stamped — that writing and seal are what is intended in the treatise — not as [the terms are used] in the world. For in the world, letter-marks in books and the like are considered 'writing,' and marks of letters and non-letters are [considered] 'seals.' Counting (<s>gaṇanā</s>) and poetry (<s>kāvya</s>) are vocal <s>karma</s> — 'set in motion by application, together with its origination' continues. 'Having the nature of the five aggregates' — for writing and seal-stamping, the bodily <s>karma</s> is the form aggregate; for counting and poetry, the vocal <s>karma</s> is the form aggregate. But in both cases, the four aggregates beginning with feeling, being the origination, [complete the five]. Thus these have the nature of the five aggregates. 'That which is the mental calculation of <s>dharma</s>s' — 'one, two, three' and so forth — that is number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>). [Tib. 101a] But that which is by speech and not by mind is counting — so say the <s>Ābhidhārmika</s>s. And this number, because of the inclusion of its retinue, has the nature of the four aggregates.

body.text: (IV.131) lipyādilakṣaṇanirdeśānuṣaṃgeṇa sāvadyādīnām api dharmāṇāṃ lakṣaṇanirdeśopanyāsaḥ. dharmaskaṃdhakavibhāṣāyām ete paryāyā nidiṣṭāḥ. tatpratyāsanneyam iti. ime paryāyā upanyasyaṃta ity aparaḥ saṃbaṃdhaḥ. sahāvadyena kleśalakṣaṇena vartaṃta iti
body.translated_text: (IV.131) In connection with the exposition of the characteristics of writing and the like, the characteristics of blameworthy and other <s>dharma</s>s are also presented. In the <s>Dharmaskandhaka Vibhāṣā</s>, these synonyms are set forth. 'It is closely connected to that' — these synonyms are presented — this is another connection. 'Operating together with the blameworthy, with the characteristic of affliction' — thus

body.text: kleśacchāditatvān
body.translated_text: 'Because of being covered by afflictions' —

body.text: kleśā api hi saṃprayogiṇā kleśāṃtareṇa nivṛtāḥ. niṣkṛṣṭatvād āryais tyaktatvād vā
body.translated_text: For afflictions too are obstructed by other afflictions that are associated [with them]. 'Because of being extracted' — or because of being abandoned by the noble ones (<s>ārya</s>s) —

body.text: tu kleśayogato 'vagaṃtavyāḥ.
body.translated_text: should be understood through connection with afflictions.

body.text: kuśalānāsravāḥ. te
body.translated_text: wholesome and outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>). These are

body.text: śuddhiprakarṣagatatvāt. hīnapraṇītebhyo 'nye madhyā iti siddham iti. kliṣṭā eva hīnāḥ. śubhāmalā eva ca praṇītā ity avadhāraṇād ato 'nye na hīnāḥ. na praṇītā iti madhyāḥ siddhāḥ.
body.translated_text: Because of having reached the excellence of purity. 'Other than the inferior and excellent are the middling' — this is established. Because of the restriction that only the afflicted are inferior and only the auspicious and stainless are excellent, therefore others — being neither inferior nor excellent — are established as middling.

children.translated_text:
'Conditioned and auspicious [dharmas]
are to be practiced' (<s>sevya</s>) —

body.text: iti. aviśeṣeṇa sāsravā anāsravā vā sevitavyāḥ. paryupāsitavyāḥ. saṃtānādhyā ropaṇataḥ. śeṣā asevitavyā iti. ke śeṣā. asaṃskṛtāś ca. ye ca na kuśalāḥ. kliṣṭā [Tib. 101b] nivṛtāvyākṛtā ity arthaḥ. anabhyasanīyatvād iti. paunaḥpunyena kartum aśakyatvād ity arthaḥ. anutpādyatvād ity apare. aphalatvāc ceti. saṃskṛtasya hi hetuphale. nāsaṃskṛtasya te iti. sottarā iti sātiśayāḥ. akuśalāḥ nivṛtāvyākṛtaiḥ sottarāḥ. nivṛtāvyākṛtānām aniṣṭavipākābhāvāt. nivṛtāvyākṛtā anivṛtāvyākṛtaiḥ saṃskṛtaiḥ sottarāḥ. teṣām akliṣṭatvāt. te 'pi kuśalasāsravaiḥ sottarāḥ kuśalasāsravāṇām iṣṭaphalatvāt. te 'py anāsravais sottarāḥ. nihkleśatvāt. anāsravā api saṃskṛtā asaṃskṛtaiḥ sottarāḥ. asaṃskṛtānāṃ nityatvāt. asaṃskṛtāv apy ākāśapratisaṃkhyānirodhau pratisaṃkhyānirodhena sottarau. pratisaṃkhyānirodhasya kuśalanityatvāt.
body.translated_text: thus. Without distinction, whether with outflows or outflow-free, they should be practiced — should be attended to — through implanting [them] in one's continuum. The remainder should not be practiced. What is the remainder? The unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), and that which is not wholesome — meaning: afflicted and obstructed-indeterminate. [Tib. 101b] Because of being incapable of repeated practice — meaning: because of being impossible to do repeatedly. Others [say]: because of being incapable of being produced. 'And because of being fruitless' — for conditioned [dharmas] have causal fruit, but not the unconditioned. 'Having a superior' (<s>sottara</s>) means having something surpassing [them]. The unwholesome has a superior in the obstructed-indeterminate — because the obstructed-indeterminate does not have undesirable maturation. The obstructed-indeterminate has a superior in the unobstructed-indeterminate conditioned [dharmas] — because those are unafflicted. Those too have a superior in the wholesome-with-outflows — because wholesome-with-outflows [dharmas] have desired fruit. Those too have a superior in the outflow-free — because of being free from afflictions. Even the conditioned outflow-free has a superior in the unconditioned — because of the permanence of the unconditioned. Even among the unconditioned, space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and non-analytical cessation (<s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) have a superior in analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) — because analytical cessation is wholesome and permanent.

body.text: na hi nirvāṇād viśiṣṭatamam asti. tathā hy uktaṃ ye kecid bhikṣavo dharmāḥ saṃskṛtā vā asaṃskṛtā vā virāgas teṣāṃ agra ākhyāyata iti. pratisaṃkhyānirodho hi nityatvāt sarvasaṃskṛtebhya utkṛṣṭaḥ. kuśalatvāc cāsaṃskṛtābhyām ākāśapratisaṃkhyānirodhābhyām [Tib. 102a] utkṛṣṭatara iti.
body.translated_text: for there is nothing more excellent than <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For thus it was stated: 'Whatever <s>dharma</s>s, O monks, whether conditioned or unconditioned — dispassion (<s>virāga</s>) is declared the foremost among them.' For analytical cessation, being permanent, is superior to all conditioned [dharmas]. And being wholesome, it is more superior than the two unconditioned — space and non-analytical cessation — [Tib. 102a] which are most excellent.

body.text: ācāryayaśomitrakṛtāyāṃ sphuṭārthāyām abhidharmakośavyākhyāyāṃ caturthakośasthānaṃ samāptaṃ. 4.
body.translated_text: The fourth <s>kośasthāna</s> (chapter) is completed in the <s>Sphuṭārthā Abhidharmakośavyākhyā</s> composed by <s>Ācārya Yaśomitra</s>. 4.

body.text: V (anuśayanirdeśo nāma pañcamaṃ kośasthānam)
body.translated_text: V (<s>Anuśayanirdeśa</s>: the fifth <s>kośasthāna</s>, 'Exposition of Latent Dispositions')

body.text: ity uktam iti. caturthasyādāv uktaṃ. ato 'nena saṃbaṃdhenānuśayopanyāsa iti saṃbandhaṃ darśayati. tāni ca karmāṇi yathoktalakṣaṇaprabhedāni anuśayavaśād upacayaṃ gacchaṃti. vipākanaiyamyenātra uttiṣṭhaṃte. vipākadānāya niyatībhavaṃtīty arthaḥ. aṃtareṇa cānuśayān vinānuśayair bhavasya janmano 'bhinirvartane utpādane na samarthāni bhavaṃti kuśalāny akuśalāni vā karmāṇi. na hy arhataḥ paunarbhavikāni karmāṇy aniyatāni na saṃti. anuśayābhāvāt tu punarbhavābhinirvartane na samarthāni bhavaṃti. ata evaiṣām aniyatatvaṃ sidhyati. hy arthe cāyaṃ caḥ paṭhitavyaḥ. yasmād aṃtareṇānuśayān bhavābhinirvartane na samarthāni bhavaṃti. tasmād anuśayavaśād upacayaṃ gacchaṃtīty abhiprāyaḥ. apare punar etad vākyadvayam evaṃ vyācakṣate. tāni ca karmāṇy anuśayavaśād upacayaṃ gacchaṃti. yāny akṛtāni karmāṇi. tāny anuśayavaśāt punarbhavābhinirvartana upacīyaṃta ity arthaḥ. na hy arhatāṃ karmāṇi punarbhavābhinirvartana upacīyaṃte. aṃtareṇa cānuśayāṃ bhavābhinirvartane na samarthāni bhavaṃtīti. yāni ca kṛtāni. tāny apy aṃtareṇānuśayāṃ bhavābhinirvartane na śaktāni bhavaṃti. na hy arhatāṃ pṛthagjanāvasthāyāṃ kṛtāni [Tib. 102b] kuśalākuśalāni paunarbhavikāny aniyatāni karmāṇi na saṃti. anuśayavaikalyāt tu tāni bhavābhinirvartane na samarthāni. ity evaṃ pṛthagarthābhidhānāt. samuccaye 'yaṃ cakāra iti.
body.translated_text: thus it was stated. It was stated at the beginning of the fourth [chapter]. Therefore he shows the connection: the presentation of latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>) is through this connection. And those karmas, with the previously stated characteristics and divisions, accumulate through the power of latent dispositions. 'They arise here with the certainty of retribution' — the meaning is: they become determined for giving retribution. And without latent dispositions, without the latent dispositions, neither wholesome nor unwholesome karmas are capable of producing, of generating existence, birth. For it is not that <s>Arhat</s>s do not have indeterminate karmas that lead to further rebirth. But because of the absence of latent dispositions, they are not capable of producing further rebirth. For this very reason, the indeterminacy of those [karmas] is established. And the word 'ca' should be read in the sense of 'hi' (for). Since without latent dispositions they are not capable of producing existence, therefore they accumulate through the power of latent dispositions — this is the intent. Others, however, explain this pair of statements thus: 'And those karmas accumulate through the power of latent dispositions' — those karmas which have not been performed, those accumulate through the power of latent dispositions for the production of further rebirth — this is the meaning. For the karmas of <s>Arhat</s>s do not accumulate for the production of further rebirth. 'And without latent dispositions, they are not capable of producing existence' — and those which have been performed, even those, without latent dispositions, are not capable of producing existence. For it is not that <s>Arhat</s>s do not have wholesome and unwholesome karmas that lead to further rebirth, that are indeterminate, which were performed in the state of ordinary persons. But through the deficiency of latent dispositions, those are not capable of producing existence. Thus, because of expressing two separate meanings, this word 'ca' is in the sense of aggregation.

children.translated_text: 'The root of existence is the latent dispositions' —

body.text: iti. punarbhavasya karmabhavasya vā mūlam anuśayāḥ. tadupacayasamutthānahetutvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. mūlaṃ dṛḍhīkarotīti. prāptir hi mūlaṃ. tām anucchedārthena dṛḍhīkarotīty arthaḥ. saṃtatim avasthāpayatīti. paraṃparayā kleśaprabaṃdhaṃ sthāpayatīty arthaḥ. kṣetraṃ āpādayatīti. āśrayam ātmotpattyanukūlaṃ
body.translated_text: thus. The latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>) are the root of further existence or of karma-existence. The intent is: because of being the cause of the accumulation and origination of that. 'It makes the root firm' — for acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>) is the root; it makes that firm for the purpose of not cutting it off — this is the meaning. 'It establishes the continuum' — it establishes the succession of afflictions through a chain — this is the meaning. 'It produces the field' — it produces a basis favorable to self-arising

body.text: karotīty arthaḥ. niṣyandaṃ nirvartayatīti. svaniṣyandam upakleśaṃ janayati. tadyathā rāga āhrīkyauddhatyamatsarān janayati. dveṣaḥ krodherṣye ityādi. karmabhavam abhinirharatīti. karmaiva bhavaḥ karmabhavaḥ. taṃ punarbhavābhinirvṛttaye janayatīty arthaḥ. idam asya
body.translated_text: — this is the meaning. 'It brings forth the outflow' — it generates its own outflow, the secondary affliction (<s>upakleśa</s>). For example, desire (<s>rāga</s>) generates shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), and envy (<s>mātsarya</s>). Hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) [generates] anger (<s>krodha</s>) and jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) — and so on. 'It brings forth karma-existence' — karma itself is existence — karma-existence; it generates that for the production of further rebirth — this is the meaning. This is the illustration of the meaning of

children.translated_text: 'The root of existence is the latent dispositions' —

body.text: ity arthasaṃdarśanaṃ. svasaṃbhāraṃ parigṛhṇātīti. svasaṃbhāraḥ kleśasyāyoniśomanaskāraḥ. taṃ parigṛhṇāti. tasyānāgatasya hetubhāvenāvatiṣṭhata ity arthaḥ. ālaṃbane saṃmohayatīti. yathābhūtagrahaṇāt. buddhyupaghātād vā saṃmohayatīti. vijñānasroto namayatīti. vijñānasaṃtatim [Tib. 103a] ālaṃbane punarbhave vā namayati. yadi
body.translated_text: thus. 'It grasps its own requisites' — the own requisite of an affliction is improper attention (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>); it grasps that, meaning: it serves as a cause for that future [affliction] in the form of a condition — this is the meaning. 'It deludes regarding the object' — because of not grasping [the object] as it really is, or because of impairing cognition, it deludes. 'It bends the stream of consciousness' — it bends the continuum of consciousness toward the object, or toward further rebirth. If

body.text: punarbhavagrahaṇam idam asyodāharaṇaṃ. kuśalapakṣād vyutkramayatīti. kuśalapakṣāt parihāpayati. bandhanārthaṃ ca spharati. bandhanakāryaṃ vyāpnoti tanotīty arthaḥ. katham ity āha. dhātvanatikramaṇayogena dhātvanatikamaṇaprakāreṇety arthaḥ. tad idam uktaṃ bhavati. yaḥ kleśo yaddhātukaḥ sa taṃ dhātuṃ nātikrāmayatīti. ṣoḍaśety anyaḥ. eṣu ṣaṭ prakṣipya. āśrayadauṣṭhulyaṃ janayaty akarmaṇyatāpādanāt. guṇān dveṭti tadvirodhitvāt. apavādānām āspadīkaroti vidvadvigarhitakāyakarmotthāpanāt. satpathād udvartayati viparītadaiśikasaṃsevābhimukhīkaraṇāt. vividhānarthabījaṃ ropayati sarvasaṃsāravyasanānāṃ tatprabhavatvāt. ādhipatyaphalena ca lokasyāniṣṭam upasaṃharati tadvegena bāhyabhāvavikārāpatteḥ. rāgavaśenānyeṣām apīti. yatra rāgaḥ. tatrālaṃbane 'nye pratighādayo 'py anuśerate. premād dveṣo jāyate mānādayo 'pīti sūtraṃ. ata eva ca rāgānuśayanābhāvād anāsravavisabhāgadhātvoḥ kleśā nānuśerata iti. etac ca paścāt pravedayiṣyāma iti. yad dhi vastv ātmadṛṣṭitṛṣṇābhyāṃ svīkṛtaṃ. tatrānye 'py anuśayā anuśayitum utahaṃte. ārdra iva paṭe rajāṃsi saṃsthātum ity etat jñāpayiṣyāmaḥ.
body.translated_text: the mention of 'further rebirth' — this is an illustration thereof. 'It causes one to deviate from the wholesome class' — it causes one to fall from the wholesome class. 'And it pervades for the purpose of bondage' — it pervades, extends, spreads the function of bondage — this is the meaning. How? He says: through the method of not transcending the element (<s>dhātu</s>) — through the method of not transcending the element, is the meaning. This amounts to saying: whichever affliction belongs to whichever element, that one does not make [beings] transcend that element. 'Sixteen' — according to another [classification]. Adding six to these. 'It generates unsuitability of the basis (<s>āśrayadauṣṭhulya</s>)' — because of producing unworkability. 'It hates good qualities' — because of being opposed to them. 'It makes [beings] a ground for reproaches' — because of causing the undertaking of bodily actions censured by the wise. 'It makes [beings] deviate from the right path' — because of causing one to face toward perverted guides. 'It plants the seeds of manifold misfortune' — because all the calamities of <s>saṃsāra</s> originate from it. 'And through its dominant result, it brings what is undesirable upon the world' — because through its force, the external world undergoes deterioration. 'Through desire, others too' — wherever there is desire (<s>rāga</s>), in that object, other [afflictions] too such as aversion (<s>pratigha</s>) and the rest lie latent. From the <s>sūtra</s>: 'From love, hatred arises; pride and the rest too.' For this very reason, because of the absence of the latency of desire, afflictions do not lie latent in uncontaminated [dharmas] and in a dissimilar element. 'And this we shall explain later.' For whatever object has been appropriated through the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) and craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), in that object the other latent dispositions too are able to become latent — just as dust is able to adhere to a damp cloth — this we shall make known.

body.text: (V.2) āhosvit kāmarāga evānuśaya iti. vaibhāṣikanayena paryavasthānam evānuśayaḥ. vātsīputrīyanayena prāptir anuśayaḥ. sautrāṃtikanayena bījam. uttaraniḥsaraṇam iti. paścānniḥsaraṇam ity arthaḥ. sthāmaśaḥ susamavahataṃ.
body.translated_text: (V.2) 'Or is it only sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>) that is a latent disposition?' — according to the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> method, the manifest affliction (<s>paryavasthāna</s>) itself is the latent disposition. According to the <s>Vātsīputrīya</s> method, acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>) is the latent disposition. According to the <s>Sautrāntika</s> method, the seed (<s>bīja</s>). 'The subsequent escape' — meaning: the later escape. 'Firmly, well-sustained'

body.text: balaśaḥ suṣṭhu samyag avahatam ity arthaḥ. sānuśayaṃ prahīyata iti. idam atrodāharaṇaṃ. [Tib. 103b] idam atra virudhyate. sahayogasamāse hy anyatvam dṛṣṭaṃ. tadyathā saputro devadatta iti. tathā ca sati sūtravirodhaḥ. abhidharmavirodha iti. kāmarāgānuśayas tribhir indriyaiḥ saṃprayuktaḥ. katamais tribhiḥ. sukhasaumanasyopekṣendriyaiḥ saṃprayukta iti. na hi viprayuktasya prāptilakṣaṇasya ebhir indriyaiḥ saṃprayogo yujyata iti śāstravirodhaḥ.
body.translated_text: — the meaning is: by force, properly and completely sustained. 'It is abandoned together with the latent disposition' (<s>sānuśayaṃ prahīyate</s>) — this is the illustration here. This contradicts here. For in a co-occurring compound (<s>sahayogasamāsa</s>), otherness is seen — for example: '<s>Devadatta</s> together with his son' (<s>saputro devadattaḥ</s>). And this being so, there is contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s>. Contradiction with the <s>Abhidharma</s>: 'The latent disposition of sensual desire (<s>kāmarāgānuśaya</s>) is associated with three faculties. Which three? The faculties of pleasure, mental pleasure, and equanimity.' For it is not fitting that what is dissociated, having the character of acquisition, should be associated with these faculties — this is the contradiction with the treatise.

body.text: sānuśyaṃ sānubandham ity arthād iti. kāmarāgasyānubandho 'nuśayaśabdenoktaḥ. anubaṃdhaḥ punaḥ kleśāṃtarasyotpādānukūlyenavāsthānaṃ. anuvṛttir vā anuśayaḥ. sānuśayaṃ prahīyate. na punar anuvartate saṃkleśa ity arthaḥ. aupacāriko vā sūtre 'nuśayaśabdaḥ upacāre bhava aupacārikaḥ. kutr'; aupacārika ity āha. prāptau. mukhyavṛttyā paryavasthāne 'nuśayaśabdo vartate. upācāreṇa tu prāptau. tasyānuśayahetubhāvāt. tadyathā duḥkhavedanāhetutvāt agnir duḥkha ity ucyate. tadvat. lākṣaṇikas tv abhidharme 'nuśayaśabdaḥ. lakṣaṇe bhavo lakṣaṇena vā dīpyati [Tib. 104a] lākṣaṇikaḥ. lākṣaṇika ity āha. kleśa eveti. ālaṃbnasaṃprayogataś cānuśerata ity anuśayā iti. tasmāt saṃprayuktā evānuśayāḥ. atra cārthe ślokam udāharaṃti.
body.translated_text: 'Together with the latent disposition means together with the consequence' (<s>sānubandham</s>) — [this is said] from the meaning. The consequence of sensual desire is expressed by the word 'latent disposition.' The consequence, moreover, is the persistence favorable to the arising of another affliction, or the continuity. 'Together with the latent disposition, it is abandoned' — the meaning is: the defilement does not recur. Or alternatively, the word 'latent disposition' in the <s>sūtra</s> is figurative (<s>aupacārika</s>) — that which exists in a figurative usage is figurative. Where is it figurative? He says: in acquisition. The word 'latent disposition' applies in its primary sense to the manifest affliction (<s>paryavasthāna</s>), but figuratively to acquisition — because of being a cause of the latent disposition. Just as fire is called 'suffering' because of being a cause of painful feeling — likewise. But in the <s>Abhidharma</s>, the word 'latent disposition' is used characteristically (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>) — that which exists in the characteristic, or is illuminated by the characteristic, is characteristically [used]. 'Characteristically' means: the affliction itself [is the latent disposition]. Because they lie latent through object and association, they are latent dispositions. Therefore, the latent dispositions are associated only. And on this matter they cite a verse:

children.text:
cittakleśakaratvād āvaraṇatvāc chubhair viruddhatvāt
kuśalasya copalaṃbhād aviprayuktā ihānuśayā
children.translated_text:
'Because of making the mind afflicted, because of being an obstruction, because of being opposed to wholesome [dharmas],
and because of the finding of wholesomeness — herein, the latent dispositions are not dissociated' —

body.text: iti. cittakleśakaratvād iti. asya vivaraṇaṃ. yasmād anuśayaiḥ kliṣṭaṃ cittaṃ bhavati. na viprayuktaiḥ kliṣṭaṃ cittaṃ bhavati. āvaraṇatvād iti. asya padasya vivaraṇaṃ. apūrvaṃ kuśalaṃ notpadyata iti. sānuśaye citte kuśalam apūrvaṃ notpadyate. śubhair viruddhatvād iti. asya padasya vivaraṇaṃ. utpannāc ca parihīyata iti. anuśayāḥ śubhair viruddhāḥ. yasmād utpannāt kuśalāt parihīyate. tasmāt kuśalair viruddhā anuśayāḥ. tasmān na viprayuktā iti. yasmāc cetasy avidyamānais tair yathoktakliṣṭādi na saṃbhavati. saṃprayuktaiḥ punaḥ sarvam etad yujyata iti. atha viprayuktair apy evaṃ syād iti. viprayuktaiḥ kliṣṭaṃ cittaṃ bhavati. apūrvaṃ kuśalaṃ notpadyate. utpannāc ca parihīyata iti. yady evaṃ kuśalaṃ na kadācid apy upalabhyeta. teṣāṃ viprayuktānāṃ nityasaṃnihitatvāt. [Tib. 104b] yasmāt kliṣṭāvasthāyāṃ kuśalāvasthāyāṃ anyasyāṃ vā te viprayuktā vartaṃta iti upalabhyeta ca kuśalam. ataḥ
body.translated_text: thus. 'Because of making the mind afflicted' — the explanation of this: since by the latent dispositions the mind becomes afflicted, and the mind does not become afflicted by what is dissociated. 'Because of being an obstruction' — the explanation of this expression: 'A new wholesome [dharma] does not arise' — in a mind with latent dispositions, a new wholesome [dharma] does not arise. 'Because of being opposed to wholesome [dharmas]' — the explanation of this expression: 'One falls from what has already arisen' — the latent dispositions are opposed to wholesome [dharmas], since one falls from wholesomeness that has already arisen; therefore the latent dispositions are opposed to the wholesome. 'Therefore they are not dissociated' — since, when those [latent dispositions] are not present in the mind, the above-mentioned affliction and the rest are not possible, but when associated, all of this is fitting. But if even by those that are dissociated it were thus — the mind would become afflicted by what is dissociated, a new wholesome [dharma] would not arise, and one would fall from what has already arisen — if so, then wholesomeness would never be found at all, because of the constant proximity of those dissociated [latent dispositions]. Since in the afflicted state, in the wholesome state, or in any other state, those dissociated [latent dispositions] would persist. But wholesomeness is indeed found. Therefore,

children.translated_text: 'because of the finding of wholesomeness, herein, the latent dispositions are not dissociated' —

body.text:
iti sthitam etat.
ācārya āha: tad idam ajñāpakaṃ. yad idaṃ vaibhāṣikair uktaṃ. cittakleśakaratvād ityādi. yo hi viprayuktam anuśayam icchatīti vātsīputrīyaḥ. sarvam etad iti. cittakleśādi. kleśakṛtam evecchatīti. paryavasthānakṛtam evety arthaḥ. paryavasthānaṃ ca na nityasaṃnihitaṃ bhavatīti kuśalopalaṃbhasiddhiḥ. kāmarāgasyānuśaya iti pakṣaparigrahe sānuśayaṃ prahīyata iti nāsti sūtravirodhaḥ. kiṃ tu viprayukto 'nuśaya iti prāpnoti. ata āha. na cānuśayaḥ saṃprayukto na viprayukta iti. katham ity āha. tasyādravyāntaratvād iti. śaktirūpasya bījasya rāgādibhyo 'narthāṃtaratvāt. ātmabhāvasyāśrayasya. kleśajā pūrvotpannakleśajanitā. kleśotpādanaśaktiḥ kleśotpādanāya [Tib. 105a] śaktiḥ. yathānubhavajñānajā sṃṛtyutpādanaśaktir na dravyāṃtarabhūtā. tadvat. smṛtyutpādanahetur dravyāṃtarabhūtaḥ kaścid viprayukta ity āśaṃkya dṛṣṭāntāṃtaram upanyasyati. yathā cāṃkurādīnām iti vistaraḥ. yathā cāṃkurādīnāṃ pūrvotpannā śāliphalajā śāliphalāṃtarotpādanāya śaktir na dravyāṃtarabhūtā. tadvat. yas tv iti. vātsīputrīyaḥ. yadi kleśasyānuśaya itīsyate. yat tarhi sūtra eva kleśo 'nuśaya uktaḥ ṣaṭṣaṭke sūtre. 'sya pudgalasya bhavati sukhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ rāgānuśaya iti. rāga evānuśayaḥ. sukhavedanāvasthāyāṃ hi rāgaḥ samudācaraṃn evam uktaḥ. na tu tasya bījam ity abhiprāyaḥ. bhavatīti vacanān nāsau tadaivānuśaya iti. anuśaya eva rāgasyāyam uktaḥ. na rāgaḥ. bhavatīti vacanāt. tasyām avasthāyām utpadyamānasya rāgasyānuśayo bhavatīti. bījam utpadyate. na tūtpannam iti. bījaprakṛtāvasthātra kathyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. kadā tarhi bhavatīti. kadānuśayo 'stīty arthaḥ. yadā prasupto bhavati. yadoparato bhavatīty arthaḥ. hetau vā tadupacāra iti. hetau rāge anuśayopacāraḥ. rāgo hi rāgānuśayasya hetuḥ. tathā hi [Tib. 105b] rāgajā rāgotpādanaśaktī rāgānuśaya ity uktam iti. tad idam uktaṃ bhavati. kvacid anuśayaśabdena bījam ucyate. kvacit paryavasthānam iti.
body.translated_text:
this is established.
The <s>Ācārya</s> says: this is non-demonstrative. What was stated by the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s — 'because of making the mind afflicted' and so on — for one who accepts a dissociated latent disposition, that is, the <s>Vātsīputrīya</s>, all of this — the affliction of the mind and the rest — he accepts as done by the affliction itself, meaning: done by the manifest affliction (<s>paryavasthāna</s>) alone. And the manifest affliction is not constantly present — therefore the finding of wholesomeness is established. In accepting the <s>kāmarāga</s> as a latent disposition, [when one reads] 'it is abandoned together with the latent disposition' — there is no contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s>. But [on this view], the latent disposition should be dissociated — therefore he says: 'And the latent disposition is neither associated nor dissociated.' How? He says: 'Because of not being a separate substance' — because the seed, having the form of a potency, is not a separate entity from desire and the rest. [It is a potency] of the basis, of the support. 'Born from afflictions' — generated by previously arisen afflictions — the potency for producing afflictions, the potency for producing [future] afflictions. Just as the potency for producing memory, born from experiential cognition, is not a separate substance — likewise. The cause of producing memory, being a separate substance, some dissociated [entity] — lest one suspect this, he adduces another example: 'Just as for sprouts and the like' — and so forth in detail. Just as the potency for producing another rice-fruit, born from previously arisen rice-fruit, for sprouts and the like, is not a separate substance — likewise. 'But one who' — the <s>Vātsīputrīya</s>. 'If the affliction is accepted as a latent disposition' — then what about the <s>sūtra</s> in the <s>Ṣaṭṣaṭka Sūtra</s>, where the affliction is called a latent disposition: 'This person has the latent disposition of desire (<s>rāgānuśaya</s>) with respect to pleasant feeling' — desire itself is the latent disposition. In the state of pleasant feeling, desire, when manifestly operating, is spoken of thus — not its seed, is the intent. 'From the word "exists" (<s>bhavati</s>), it is not the latent disposition itself at that time' — this very latent disposition of desire is spoken of, not desire itself, because of the word 'exists.' The meaning is: the latent disposition of desire that is arising in that state exists. 'The seed arises, but has not yet arisen' — what is spoken of here is the seed-state, the natural state — this is the intent. 'When then does it exist?' — the meaning is: when does the latent disposition exist? 'When it is dormant' (<s>prasupta</s>) — when it is inactive, is the meaning. 'Or it is a figurative usage in the cause' — the figurative usage of 'latent disposition' is applied to desire, the cause. For desire is the cause of the latent disposition of desire. For thus: the potency for producing desire, born from desire, is the latent disposition of desire — it was said. This amounts to saying: sometimes by the word 'latent disposition,' the seed is meant; sometimes the manifest affliction.

body.text: samāpattirāgo hi teṣāṃ prāyeṇeti. āsvādanāsaṃprayukte dhyāne prāyeṇa teṣāṃ rāgaḥ. vimānādiṣv api teṣāṃ rāgo 'stīty ataḥ prāyeṇeti grahaṇaṃ. sa cāṃtarmukhapravṛttaḥ samāhitarūpatvāt. tathā ca sati mokṣasaṃjñopatiṣṭhate. tadvicchandanārthaṃ bhagavān deśayāmāsa kāmarāgo bhavarāga ity evamādi.
body.translated_text: 'For their desire is mostly for attainment' (<s>samāpattirāga</s>) — mostly their desire is for concentration (<s>dhyāna</s>) associated with relishing (<s>āsvādana</s>). Because they also have desire for celestial palaces and the like, the word 'mostly' is used. And that [desire] operates inwardly, because of being in a concentrated form. And this being so, the perception of liberation arises [for them]. In order to dispel this, the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught: 'sensual desire, desire for existence' — and so on.

body.text: bhave rāga eṣaḥ. naiṣa mokṣe. mokṣe kuśalo dharmacchanda iti. ātmabhāva eva tu bhava ity ācāryamataṃ. samāpattiṃ sāśrayām iti. samāpāttiṃ sātmabhāvām. āsvādayanta ātmabhāvam evāsvādayaṃti. na kāmaguṇān. kāmavītarāgatvāt. ataḥ sa rāgo bhavarāga ity ukto na kāmarāga iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: this is passion for existence. Not for liberation. [Desire] for liberation is the wholesome desire for the <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmacchanda</s>). But it is the personal existence itself that is [called] 'existence' — this is the <s>Ācārya</s>'s view. 'The attainment together with its support' — the attainment together with its personal existence. Those who relish [it] relish the personal existence itself, not the sense-pleasures — because of being free from passion for sense-pleasures. Therefore, that passion is called 'passion for existence' (<s>bhavarāga</s>), not 'passion for sense-pleasures' (<s>kāmarāga</s>) — he shows.

body.text: (V.3) abhidharma iti. na sūtra ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: (V.3) '<s>Abhidharma</s>' — the intent is: not <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: (V.4, 5) sapta samudayadarśanaheyā iti. satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ phalabhūtān paṃcopādānaskandhān ālaṃbata iti duḥkhadarśanaheyaiva. evam aṃtagrāhadṛṣṭiḥ [Tib. 106a] teṣām eva skandhānāṃ śāśvatocchedāṃtagrahaṇāt. śīlavrataparāmarśo 'pi tān eva skandhāṃ śuddhito muktito nairyāṇikataś cālaṃbata iti na samudayadarśanaheyaḥ. evaṃ nirodhadarśanaheyā api yojyāḥ. aṣṭau mārgadarśanaheyā iti. śīlavrataparāmarśam adhikaṃ prakṣipya. mārgeṇa śudhyati. tam apāsyānyena śīlavratena śuddhiṃ pratyetīti vipratipannatvāt. mārgadarśanaprahātavyo bhavati. yo hi kleśo yasya satyasyāpavādāya pravṛttaḥ. sa tasmin dṛṣṭe prahīyate. sarpabhrāṃtir iva rajjudarśanāt. satyānāṃ darśanamātreṇa prahāṇād iti. nābhyāsena prahāṇād ity abhiprāyaḥ. dṛṣṭasatyasya paścān mārgābhyāsena prahāṇāt. kim ete bhāvanāheyā ity adhikāraḥ. tad evam abhyāso bhāvanā punaḥpunarutpādanam ity arthaḥ. satkāyadṛṣṭir ekaprakāreti. ātmātmīyākāreṇa duḥkhe vipratipannatvāt duḥkhadarśanaheyaiva. evam aṃtagrāhadṛṣṭir iti. asāv apy ātmābhimatasya vastunaḥ śāśvatocchedāṃtāropād duḥkha eva vipratipanneti duḥkhadarśanaheyaiva. mithyādṛṣṭiś catuṣprakāreti. duḥkhādisatyalakṣaṇāpavādapravṛttatvāt satyacatuṣṭaye 'pi vipratipanneti. catuḥsatyadarśanaheyā. evaṃ dṛṣṭiparāmarśo 'pi catuṣprakāra eva. sa hi hīne 'gradarśanaṃ. tatra samudayanirodhamārgapraheyālaṃbanaḥ samudayanirodhamārgadarśanaheyaḥ. śeṣo duḥkhadarśanaheyaḥ. evaṃ vicikitsā sarvatrasaṃśayākāreti sarvatravipratipannatvāc catuḥsatyadarśanaheyā. śīlavrataparāmarśo dviṣprakāra iti. īśvarādiṣv ahetuṣu hetugraho nityātmaviparyāsāt pravartata iti duḥkhadarśanaheyaḥ. amārge mārgadarśanaṃ mārgadarśanaheyaḥ.
body.translated_text: (V.4, 5) Seven are to be abandoned by the seeing of origination (<s>samudayadarśanaheya</s>) — identity-view (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) takes as its object the five clinging-aggregates that are the fruit, hence it is to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering alone. Similarly, the extreme-view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>) — because it grasps those very aggregates as eternal or annihilated. The attachment to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>) too takes those very aggregates as objects from the perspectives of purity, liberation, and leading to liberation — hence it is not to be abandoned by the seeing of origination. Similarly, those to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation (<s>nirodhadarśanaheya</s>) should be connected. Eight are to be abandoned by the seeing of the path (<s>mārgadarśanaheya</s>) — adding the attachment to rules and rituals. [One thinks] 'one is purified by the path,' but rejecting that, one expects purification through other rules and rituals — because of being deluded. Hence it is to be abandoned by the seeing of the path. For whatever affliction operates as the denial of a given truth — that is abandoned when that [truth] is seen. Like the mistaking of a rope for a snake [which is eliminated] by seeing the rope. 'Because of being abandoned by the mere seeing of the truths' — the intent is: not abandoned by repeated practice. 'Because of being abandoned by subsequent practice of the path, after having seen the truths.' 'Are these then to be abandoned by cultivation?' — this is the topic. Thus: repeated practice is cultivation, meaning repeated production — this is the meaning. Identity-view is of one kind — because of being deluded in [the truth of] suffering through the mode of self and what-belongs-to-self, it is to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering alone. Similarly, the extreme-view — because it too superimposes the extremes of eternity and annihilation on the entity believed to be the self, it is deluded in suffering alone, hence to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering alone. Wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) is of four kinds — because of operating as the denial of the characteristics of the four truths beginning with suffering, it is deluded in all four truths, hence to be abandoned by the seeing of all four truths. Similarly, the view-attachment (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>) too is of exactly four kinds. For it is the seeing of the inferior as supreme. Therein, that which takes as its object what is to be abandoned by the seeing of origination, cessation, and the path — is to be abandoned by the seeing of origination, cessation, and the path [respectively]. The remainder is to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering. Similarly, doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), having the mode of uncertainty regarding everything, being deluded regarding everything, is to be abandoned by the seeing of all four truths. Attachment to rules and rituals is of two kinds — the grasping of non-causes as causes operates from the delusion of permanence and self, hence is to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering. Seeing the path in what is not the path — is to be abandoned by the seeing of the path.

body.text: kīdṛśā eta iti. rāgādayaś catvāraḥ kleśāḥ. paryanuyujyaṃte hi rāgapratighamānāvidyā ity anaṃtarādhikṛtāḥ. te ceme darśanaheyāḥ. ime bhāvanāheyā iti duḥparicchedāḥ. na tu satkāyadṛṣṭyādayaś cityaṃte. ye hi duḥkhasatyavipratipannāḥ. te duḥkhadarśanaheyā iti. evaṃ yāvad ye mārgasatyavipratipannāḥ te mārgadarśanaheyā iti [Tib. 106b] suparicchedam etat. tatra
body.translated_text: 'Of what kind are these?' — the four afflictions of passion and the rest. For the immediately preceding subject is passion, aversion, pride, and ignorance. And these — [the question is:] which of these are to be abandoned by seeing and which by cultivation — are hard to determine. But identity-view and the rest are not in question. For those deluded in the truth of suffering are to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering — similarly up to those deluded in the truth of the path are to be abandoned by the seeing of the path — this is easy to determine. Therein

body.text: ya iti rāgādayaḥ. yasya satyasya darśanaṃ yaddarśanam. yaddarśanena heyāḥ. ta ālaṃbanam eṣāṃ. ta ime yaddarśanaheyālaṃbanāḥ. te taddarśanaheyāḥ. te rāgādayaḥ. tasya satyasya darśanaṃ taddarśanaṃ. taddarśanena heyās taddarśanaheyāḥ. etad uktaṃ bhavati. ye rāgādayo duḥkhadarśanaheyaṃ yāvan mārgadarśanaheyaṃ kleśam ālaṃbaṃte. te taddarśanaheyā iti. yadālaṃbanā yaddarśanaheyālaṃbanāś ceti vaktavyaṃ. caturāryasatyālaṃbano 'py avidyānuśayo bhavatīti. na vaktavyaṃ. ekaśeṣavidhānasiddheḥ. yac ca satyaṃ yaddaraśanaheyāś ca kleśā ālaṃbanam eṣāṃ. ta ime yaddarśaheyālaṃbanāḥ. te taddarśanaheyā iti. nanu ca samudayadarśanaprahātavyaḥ sarvatrago 'vidyānuśayo duḥkhanirodhādisatyadarśanaheyādyālaṃbano 'pi bhavati. paṃcanikāyālaṃbanatvāt. tataś cāsya duḥkhanirodhādisatyadarśanaheyatvaprasaṃgaḥ syād iti. na doṣaḥ. yady api hi sa paṃcanikāyālaṃbanaḥ samudayarūpākāratas [Tib. 107a] tu tān nikāyān ālaṃbate. tena tathālaṃbanataḥ samudayadarśanaprahātavya eva sa iti. evaṃ duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyo 'pi saṃyojyaḥ. evaṃ ca sati ye 'pi vyācakṣate. ye yaddarśanaheyālaṃbanā iti sarva eva darśanaheyā adhikriyaṃte na kevalā rāgādaya iti. teṣām api vyākhyāne imāv eva codyaparihārau vaktavyau.
body.translated_text: 'those which' — meaning: passion and the rest. Which take as their object [afflictions] to be abandoned by the seeing of a given truth — those whose object is to be abandoned by that seeing. Those are to be abandoned by that seeing. Those — passion and the rest — whose seeing of a given truth [abandons them] — that seeing by which they are to be abandoned — they are to be abandoned by that seeing. What has been stated is: those passions and the rest that take as their object afflictions to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, up to those to be abandoned by the seeing of the path — they are to be abandoned by that [respective] seeing. 'Taking as their object what has such objects, and to be abandoned by that seeing too' should be stated. [Objection:] the latent tendency of ignorance (<s>avidyānuśaya</s>) can take the four noble truths themselves as its object — [this is problematic]. [Reply:] this need not be stated — because it is established through the single-remainder procedure (<s>ekaśeṣa</s>). Both the truth and the afflictions to be abandoned by a given seeing are the objects of these — those whose objects are to be abandoned by that seeing — they are to be abandoned by that seeing. But does not the universal (<s>sarvatraga</s>) latent tendency of ignorance to be abandoned by the seeing of origination also take as its object [afflictions] to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, cessation, and the rest — because of having objects belonging to five categories? Would there then not be the absurd consequence that it should be to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, cessation, and the rest? There is no fault. For although it has objects belonging to five categories, it takes those categories as objects in the mode of origination. Therefore, from taking [them] as objects in that mode, it is to be abandoned by the seeing of origination alone. Similarly, that to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering should be connected. And this being so, even those who explain that in 'those that take as their object what is to be abandoned by a given seeing,' all those to be abandoned by seeing are the subject — not only passion and the rest — for their explanation too, these very objection and resolution must be stated.

body.text: rūpārūpyadhātvor duḥkhābhāvāt pratighābhāvaḥ. duḥkhāyāṃ hi vedanāyāṃ pratigho 'nuśete. sā copari nāstīti. dveṣaś ca rūkṣo vātavyādhivat. te ca sattvāḥ śamathasnigdhasaṃtataya iti. vipākābhāvāc ca. aniṣṭo hy asya vipākaḥ. tau dhātau vigatāniṣṭavipākau. āghātavastvabhāvāc ca. na hi tatra bāhyāḥ kuśakṣārakaṇṭakādayo nādhyātmikā tāpāpasmārādayaḥ saṃti. maitryādikuśalamūlasaṃbhūtatvāt parigrahābhāvāc ca. ākāraprakāradhātubhedair iti. ākārabhedo daśānām anuśayānāṃ
body.translated_text: In the Form and Formless Realms, because of the absence of suffering [feeling], aversion is absent. For aversion lies latent in painful feeling, and that [painful feeling] does not exist above. And hatred is rough, like a wind-disease. And those beings have continuums moistened by calm (<s>śamatha</s>). And because of the absence of ripening [of hatred] — for its ripening is undesirable, and those two realms are free from undesirable ripening. And because of the absence of objects of resentment — for there are no external [irritants] like thorny grass, alkali, and thorns, nor internal ones like burning fevers, seizures, and the like. And because of being born from wholesome roots of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the rest, and because of the absence of possessiveness. 'Through the distinctions of mode, category, and realm' — the mode-distinction: of the ten latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) —

children.translated_text: 'The views of self, what-belongs-to-self, permanent, annihilated, nihilistic, inferior, and supreme' —

body.text: ity evamādikaḥ. prakārabhedo duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyo nikāyo yāvad bhāvanāprahātavya iti. dhātubhedaḥ kāmāvacaraḥ. rūpāvacaraḥ. ārūpyāvacara iti. tatra rāgānuśayaḥ prakāradhātubhedābhyāṃ paṃcadaśavidha iti. tasya parasparam ākārabhedo nāsti. sarvo hi rāgaḥ saktyākāraḥ. tasmān nākārabhedena vyavasthāpyate. pratighānuśayaḥ prakārabhedāt paṃcavidhaḥ. na
body.translated_text: and so forth. The category-distinction: the category to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, up to the category to be abandoned by cultivation. The realm-distinction: belonging to the Desire Realm, the Form Realm, and the Formless Realm. Therein, the latent tendency of passion, through the category and realm distinctions, is fifteenfold — it has no mode-distinction from the others, for all passion has the mode of attachment. Therefore it is not established through mode-distinction. The latent tendency of aversion, through category-distinction [alone], is fivefold. It has no

body.text: parasparam ākārabhedo 'sti. sarvasya pratighākāratvāt. dhātubhedo 'pi nāsti. rūpārūpyadhātvos tadabhāvāt. mānānuśayaḥ prakāradhātubhedābhyāṃ paṃcadaśavidhaḥ. nākārabhedo 'sti. sarvasyonnatyākāratvāt. tathā avidyā paṃcadaśavidhā. tābhyām [Tib. 107b] eva. nākārabhedo 'sti. sarvasyā asaṃprakhyānākāratvāt. vicikitsā dvādaśavidhā. tābhyām eva. nākārabhedaḥ. sarvasyāḥ saṃśayākāratvāt. dṛṣṭyanuśaya ākāraprakāradhātubhedaiḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadvidhaḥ. [evam ete ṣaḍ anuśayā iti vistaraḥ.]
body.translated_text: mode-distinction from the others, because all aversion has the mode of aversion. Nor is there realm-distinction — because of its absence in the Form and Formless Realms. The latent tendency of pride, through category and realm distinctions, is fifteenfold. There is no mode-distinction, because all [pride] has the mode of self-exaltation. Similarly, ignorance is fifteenfold — through those very two [distinctions]. There is no mode-distinction, because all [ignorance] has the mode of non-discernment. Doubt is twelvefold — through those very two. There is no mode-distinction, because all doubt has the mode of uncertainty. The view-latent tendency (<s>dṛṣṭyanuśaya</s>), through mode, category, and realm distinctions, is thirty-sixfold. [Thus these six latent tendencies — and so forth in detail.]

children.translated_text: 'Those born at the summit of existence are to be destroyed by patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>)' —

body.text: iti. kṣāṃtivadhyagrahaṇaṃ bhāvanāheyanivṛttyarthaṃ. bhavāgrajagrahaṇaṃ tadanyabhūmikaviśeṣaṇārthaṃ. na hi laukiko 'sti bhavāgrapratipakṣabhūto bhāvanāmārga iti. śeṣāsu bhūmiṣv iti. kāmadhātau yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmau. yathāyogam iti. kāmadhātau dharmajñānakṣāṃtiheyāḥ. tata ūrdhvam avaśiṣṭāsu bhūmiṣv anvayajñānakṣāṃtiheyāḥ. ta ete āryāṇāṃ darśanaheyās ta eva ca pṛthagjanānāṃ bhāvanāheyāḥ. dvividho hi bhāvanāmārgaḥ. laukiko lokottaraś ca. tathā hi śāstra uktaṃ. bhagavataḥ śrāvako darśanena jahāti. pṛthagjano bhāvanayā jahātīti.
body.translated_text: the mention of 'to be destroyed by patient acceptance' is for the purpose of excluding [those] to be abandoned by cultivation. The mention of 'born at the summit of existence' is for qualifying those of other grounds. For there is no mundane cultivation-path that serves as the antidote to the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). 'In the remaining grounds' — from the Desire Realm up to the ground of Nothingness (<s>Ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>). 'As applicable' — in the Desire Realm, they are to be abandoned by the patient acceptances of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge (<s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s>). In the grounds above that, in the remaining grounds, they are to be abandoned by the patient acceptances of subsequent-knowledge (<s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s>). These are to be abandoned by seeing for Noble Ones — and those same ones are to be abandoned by cultivation for ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). For the cultivation-path is twofold: mundane and supramundane. For thus it is stated in the treatise: 'The disciple of the <s>Bhagavān</s> abandons by seeing; the ordinary person abandons by cultivation.'

children.translated_text: 'Those not to be destroyed by patient acceptance [are to be abandoned] by cultivation alone' —

body.text: iti. akṣāṃtivadhyagrahaṇaṃ bhāvanāheyopasaṃgrahārthaṃ. sarvāsu bhūmiṣu. kāmadhātau yāvad bhavāgre. ye rāgapratighamānāvidyānuśayā yathāyogaṃ bhavaṃti akṣāṃtivadhyā jñānavadhyāḥ. [Tib. 108a] te ubhayeṣām āryāṇāṃ pṛthagjanānām ca nityaṃ bhāvanāheyā eva. laukikena lokottareṇa vā bhāvanāmārgeṇa. bhavāgre tu lokottareṇaiva. ūrdhvabhūmikasya laukikasya mārgasyābhāvāt.
body.translated_text: the mention of 'not to be destroyed by patient acceptance' is for the purpose of including [them under] those to be abandoned by cultivation. In all grounds — from the Desire Realm up to the summit of existence. The latent tendencies of passion, aversion, pride, and ignorance that exist as applicable and are not to be destroyed by patient acceptance but to be destroyed by knowledge — those are always to be abandoned by cultivation alone for both — Noble Ones and ordinary persons — by the mundane or supramundane cultivation-path. But at the summit of existence, by the supramundane alone — because of the absence of a mundane path belonging to a higher ground.

body.text: naiva hi bāhyakānāṃ darśanaprahātavyāḥ prahīyaṃta iti. bhāvanāprahātavyā eva teṣāṃ viṣkabhyaṃte. darśanaheyās tu sarvāsv api bhūmiṣu lokottaramārgavadhyā eva. tathā hi mahākarmavibhāgasūtre. vītarāgāṇāṃ kāmadhātvālaṃbanānāṃ dṛṣṭīnāṃ samudācāra uktaḥ. ihānanda ekatyaḥ prāṇātipātāt prativirato bhavati. yāvan mithyādṛṣṭeḥ. ihācārataḥ prativirataḥ. kāyasya bhedāt paraṃ maraṇād apāyadurgativinipātanarakeṣūpapadyate. tam evaṃ yaḥ paśyati śramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bāhyatīrthika ṛddhimān divyacakṣuḥ paracittavit. tasyaivaṃ bhavati. nāsti kāyasucaritaṃ nāsti kāyasucaritasya vipākaḥ. nāsti vāṅmanaḥsucaritaṃ. nāsti vāṅmanaḥsucaritasya vipāka
body.translated_text: For the outsiders' [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing are not abandoned — they are merely suppressed through those to be abandoned by cultivation. But those to be abandoned by seeing are to be destroyed by the supramundane path alone, in all grounds. For thus it is stated in the <s>Mahākarmavibhaṅga Sūtra</s>: the occurrence of the views belonging to the Desire Realm of passion-free [persons] is stated. 'Here, <s>Ānanda</s>, a certain person refrains from killing living beings, up to from wrong view. Here he refrains from [bad] conduct. Upon the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the hells, in a bad destiny, in perdition.' 'Whoever — an ascetic or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, an outside sectarian, endowed with supernatural power, possessing the divine eye, knowing the minds of others — sees that one thus, to him this thought occurs: there is no good bodily conduct; there is no result of good bodily conduct; there is no good vocal or mental conduct; there is no result of good vocal or mental conduct'

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. iyaṃ mithyādṛṣṭiḥ kāmadhātvālaṃbanā. tasya karmaṇaḥ kāmāvacaratvāt. tatraiva ca narakasaṃbhavād iti. pūrvāṃtakalpakānāṃ ca śāśvatavādināṃ. [Tib. 108b] brahmajālasūtre vītarāgāṇāṃ kāmadhātvālaṃbanānāṃ dṛṣṭīnāṃ samudācāra uktaḥ. pūrvajanmadarśanānusāreṇa ya evam utpannadṛṣṭikāḥ. te pūrvāṃtakalpakāḥ. śāśvatavādino bahavas tatroktāḥ. teṣām udāhraṇam ekaṃ darśayiṣyāmaḥ. ihaikatyaḥ śramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vāraṇyagato vā vṛkṣamūla gato vā śūnyāgāragato vā ātaptānvayāt. prahāṇānvayāt. bhāvanānvayāt. bahulīkārānvayāt samyanmanasikārānvayāt. tadrūpaṃ śāṃtaṃ cetaḥsamādhiṃ spṛśati. yathā samāhite citte viṃśatiṃ saṃvartavivartakalpān samanusmarati. tasyaivaṃ bhavati. śāśvato 'yam ātmā lokaś ceti. tad evaṃ sarva eva ete pūrvāṃtakalpakāḥ śāśvatavādinaḥ. anayā śāśvatadṛṣṭyātmānaṃ lokaṃ cālaṃbamānāḥ kāmadhātum apy ālaṃbaṃte. ity evaṃ kāmadhātvālaṃbanānāṃ dṛṣṭīnāṃ samudācāra uktaḥ. tathā tasminn eva brahmajālasūtre pūrvāṃtakalpakānāṃ ekatyaśāśvatikānāṃ vītarāgāṇāṃ kāmadhātvālaṃbanānāṃ dṛṣṭīnāṃ samudācāra uktaḥ. kathaṃ. bhavati bhikṣavaḥ sa samayo yad ayaṃ lokaḥ saṃvartate. saṃvartamāne loke yadbhūyasā sattvā ābhāsvare devanikāya
