upapadyaṃte. te tatra bhavaṃti rūpiṇo manomayā avikalā ahīnendriyāḥ sarvāṃgapratyaṃgopetāḥ śubhā varṇasthāyinaḥ [Tib. 109a] svayaṃprabhā vihāyasaṃgamāḥ prītibhakṣāḥb prītyāhārā dīrghāyuṣā dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhaṃti. bhavati bhikṣavaḥ sa samayo yad ayaṃ loko vivartate. vivartamāne loke ākāśe śūnyaṃ brāhmaṃ vimānam abhinirvartate. athānyataraḥ sattva āyuḥkṣayāt puṇyakṣayāt karmakṣayāt ābhāsvarād devanikāyāc cyutvā śūnye brāhme vimāna upapadyate. sa tatraikāky advitīyo 'nupasthāyako dīrghāyur dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhati. atha tasya sattvasya dīrghasyādhvano 'tyayāt tṛṣṇotpannā aratiḥ saṃjātā. aho batānye 'pi sattvā ihopapadyeran mama sabhāgatāyāṃ. evaṃ ca tasya sattvasya cetaḥpraṇidhiḥ. anye ca sattvā āyuḥkṣayāt puṇyakṣayāt karmakṣayāt ābhāsvarād devanikāyāc cyutvā tasya sattvasya sabhāgatāyām upapannaḥ. atha tasya sattvasyaitad abhavat. aham asmy ekāky advitīyo 'nupasthāyako dīrghāyur yāvad anye 'pi sattvā ihopapadyeran mama sabhāgatāyām. evaṃ cetaḥpraṇidhiḥ. ime ca sattvā ihopapannā mama sabhāgatāyāṃ. mayaite sattvā nirmitāḥ. aham eṣāṃ sattvānām īśvaraḥ kartā nirmātā sraṣṭā sṛjaḥ pitṛbhūto bhāvānām iti. teṣām api sattvānām evaṃ bhavati. imaṃ vayaṃ
body.translated_text: — and so forth in detail. This wrong view has the Desire Realm as its object — because that <s>karma</s> belongs to the Desire Realm, and because rebirth in hell occurs there. And of those who speculate about the prior end (<s>pūrvāntakalpaka</s>), the eternalists (<s>śāśvatavādin</s>): in the <s>Brahmajālasūtra</s>, the occurrence of views that are free from passion [toward the Desire Realm] yet have the Desire Realm as their object is stated. Following the vision of previous births, those who have thus arisen views are speculators about the prior end. Many eternalists are mentioned therein. We shall show one example of them. Here, a certain <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having gone to the forest, or gone to the root of a tree, or gone to an empty dwelling, through the course of ardor, through the course of striving, through the course of cultivation, through the course of intensification, through the course of right mental engagement, touches a mental concentration (<s>cetaḥsamādhi</s>) that is of such a form, peaceful, such that with concentrated mind he recollects twenty world-cycles of evolution and dissolution. To him it occurs thus: 'This self and the world are eternal.' Thus indeed, all these are speculators about the prior end, eternalists. Taking the self and the world as object through this eternalist view, they also take the Desire Realm as object. Thus the occurrence of views that have the Desire Realm as their object is stated. Similarly, in that very <s>Brahmajālasūtra</s>, the occurrence of views of those who speculate about the prior end, the partial-eternalists, who are free from passion [toward the Desire Realm] yet have the Desire Realm as their object, is stated. How? There comes a time, monks, when this world contracts. When the world is contracting, for the most part beings are reborn in the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> class of gods. They exist there as form-beings, mind-made, with all limbs intact, with unimpaired faculties, endowed with all major and minor limbs, of beautiful appearance, self-luminous, traversing the sky, feeding on joy, nourished by joy, long-lived, abiding for a long period. There comes a time, monks, when this world evolves. When the world is evolving, an empty <s>Brahmā</s> palace manifests in space. Then a certain being, through the exhaustion of lifespan, through the exhaustion of merit, through the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, falling from the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> class of gods, is reborn in the empty <s>Brahmā</s> palace. He abides there alone, without a companion, without an attendant, long-lived, for a long period. Then, after the passage of a long time, craving-born dissatisfaction arises in that being: 'Oh, would that other beings too would be reborn here in my class of existence!' And such is the mental aspiration of that being. And other beings, through the exhaustion of lifespan, through the exhaustion of merit, through the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, falling from the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> class of gods, are reborn in the class of existence of that being. Then it occurs to that being: 'I am the one who is alone, without a companion, without an attendant, long-lived, up to: would that other beings too would be reborn here in my class of existence. Such was my mental aspiration. And these beings have been reborn here in my class of existence. These beings were created by me. I am the lord, creator, fashioner, producer, generative father of these beings.' And to those beings too it occurs thus: 'This

body.text:
sattvam adrākṣma ekākinam advitīyam [Tib. 109b] anupasthāyakaṃ dīrghāyuṣaṃ dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhaṃtaṃ. tasyāsya sattvasya dīrghasyādhvano 'tyayāt tṛṣṇotpannā aratiḥ saṃjātā. aho batānye 'pi sattvā ihopapadyeran mama sabhāgatāyām. evaṃ cāsya sattvasya cetasaḥpraṇidhiḥ. vayaṃ cehopapannā asya sattvasya sabhāgatāyām. anena vayaṃ sattvena nirmitāḥ. eṣo 'smākaṃ sattva īśvaro yāvat pitṛbhūto bhāvānāṃ. athānyataraḥ sattva āyuḥkṣayāt puṇyakṣayāt. karmakṣayāt tasmāt sthānāc cyutvā teṣām itthaṃtvam āgacchati manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāyāṃ. sa vṛddher anvayād indriyāṇāṃ paripākāt keśaśmaśrūṇy avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya samyaga eva śraddhayā agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajyāṃ pravrajati. so 'raṇyagato vā vṛkṣamūlagato vā vistareṇa yāvat tadrūpaṃ śāṃtaṃ cetaḥsamādhiṃ spṛśati. yathā samāhite citte pūrvakam ātmabhāvaṃ samanusmarati. tasyaivaṃ bhavati. yo 'sau brahmā yena vayaṃ nirmitāḥ. sa nityo dhruvaḥ śāśvataḥ avipariṇāmadharmā. ye tu vayaṃ tena brahmaṇā nirmitāḥ. te vayaṃ anityā adhruvā āśāśvatā vipariṇāmadharmāṇa iti. tad evaṃ kāmadhātur api tayāṃtagrāhadṛṣṭyālaṃbito bhavati. ataḥ kāmadhātvālaṃbanānāṃ dṛṣṭīnāṃ samudācāra uktaḥ. [Tib. 110a] tathā tatraiva brahmajālasūtre ahetusamutpattikānāṃ pūrvāntakalpānām iti prakṛtaṃ. vītarāgāṇāṃ kāmadhātvālaṃbanānāṃ dṛṣṭīnāṃ samudācāra uktaḥ. kathaṃ. saṃti rūpadhātāv asaṃjñisattvā nāma devāḥ. saṃjñotpādāt teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasmāt sthānāt cyutir bhavati. ato 'nyatamaḥ sattvas tasmāt sthānāc cyutvā itthaṃtvam āgacchati manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāyāṃ. pūrvavad yāvat pūrvakam ātmabhāvaṃ samanusmarati. tasyaivaṃ bhavati. ahetusamutpanna ātmā lokaś ca. tad anenaivam eva bhavati. ahetusamutpanna ātmā lokaś ca. aham asmi pūrvaṃ nābhūvan so 'smy etarhi saṃbhūta ity ahetusamutpanna ātmā lokaś ca. ity evam ātmānaṃ lokaṃ cālaṃbamānās tayā mithyādṛṣṭyā kāmadhātum apy ālambanta ity eteṣāṃ kāmadhātvālaṃbānāṃ dṛṣṭīnāṃ samudācāra uktaḥ. kathaṃ ca punar eṣām ātmā lokaś cāhetusamutpanna ity evaṃ mithyādṛṣṭir bhavati. pūrvakṛtaṃ kuśalasāsravam akuśalaṃ vā na hetur ātmano lokasyety evam apavadati. iti kāmadhātuvītarāgāṇāṃ teṣāṃ rūpāvacaryas tā dṛṣṭayo bhaviṣyaṃtīti vacanāvakāśaṃ matvāha. na ca rūpāvacarāṇāṃ kleśānāṃ kāmadhātur ālaṃbanaṃ
vītarāgatvād [Tib. 110b] iti. naitāḥ kāmāvacaryo dṛṣṭayaḥ. mithyājñānāni punar etāni. iti kecit pariharaṃti tad eṣāṃ ayuktaṃ. taddṛṣṭirūpatvāt.
body.translated_text: being we saw alone, without a companion, without an attendant, long-lived, abiding for a long period. After the passage of a long time, craving-born dissatisfaction arose in this being: would that other beings too would be reborn here in my class of existence. Such was the mental aspiration of this being. And we have been reborn here in the class of existence of this being. We were created by this being. This being is our lord, up to generative father of beings.' Then a certain being, through the exhaustion of lifespan, through the exhaustion of merit, through the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, falling from that station, comes to be in the class of existence of humans. He, through the course of growth, through the maturation of faculties, having shaved off hair and beard, having put on saffron robes, with right faith, goes forth from home to homelessness. Having gone to the forest, or gone to the root of a tree, in detail, up to: he touches a mental concentration that is of such a form, peaceful, such that with concentrated mind he recollects his previous existence. To him it occurs thus: 'That <s>Brahmā</s> by whom we were created — he is permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change. But we who were created by that <s>Brahmā</s> — we are impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, subject to change.' Thus indeed, even the Desire Realm is taken as object by that extreme-grasping view. Therefore the occurrence of views having the Desire Realm as their object is stated. Similarly, in that very <s>Brahmajālasūtra</s>, the topic is: of the speculators about the prior end who hold the view of non-causal origination — the occurrence of views that are free from passion [toward the Desire Realm] yet have the Desire Realm as their object is stated. How? There are gods in the Form Realm called 'non-percipient beings' (<s>asaṃjñisattva</s>). When perception arises for those beings, they fall from that station. Then one of those beings, having fallen from that station, comes to be in the class of existence of humans. As before, up to: he recollects his previous existence. To him it occurs thus: 'The self and the world have arisen without cause.' Indeed, to him it is thus: 'The self and the world have arisen without cause. I did not exist before; having not existed, I have now come into being' — thus: 'the self and the world have arisen without cause.' Thus, taking the self and the world as object, through that wrong view they take even the Desire Realm as object — thus the occurrence of views having the Desire Realm as their object is stated. And how indeed does the wrong view arise for them that the self and the world have arisen without cause? It rejects [the view that] previously performed wholesome-with-outflows or unwholesome [<s>karma</s>] is the cause of the self and the world. Thus, those who are free from passion toward the Desire Realm — their views will be of the Form Realm — thinking there is room for such a statement, he says: 'And the defilements of the Form Realm do not have the Desire Realm as their object, because of freedom from passion [toward it].' 'These views do not belong to the Desire Realm. Rather, these are wrong cognitions (<s>mithyājñāna</s>)' — thus some respond. That is incorrect for them — because those have the nature of views.

body.text: parihīṇāḥ [kathaṃ tarhi vītarāgāṇāṃ kāmālaṃbanadṛṣṭisamudācāra ity āha. dṛṣṭyutpādetyādi.] devadatta iveti vaibhāṣikāḥ. yathā devadatto bhagavato 'lpotsukavihāritāśayasya bhikṣusaṃghaparikarṣaṇāya pāpakecchāsamutpādād ṛddheḥ parihīṇaḥ. sūtre vacanāt. evaṃ hi sūtre paṭhyate. atha devadattasya lābhasatkāreṇābhibhūtasya idam evaṃrūpaṃ pāpakam icchāgataṃ utpannam aho bata me bhagavān bhikṣusaṃghaṃ pratiniḥsṛjet. ahaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ parikarṣayaṃ bhagavān alpotsuko viharet dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārayogam anuyuktaḥ. sahacittotpādād devadattas tasyā ṛddheḥ parihīṇa iti vistaraḥ. evaṃ te 'pi dṛṣṭyutpādasamakālaṃ parihīṇā iti.
body.translated_text: 'Fallen [from attainment]' — [how then is the occurrence of desire-realm-object views for those free from passion explained? He says: 'Through the arising of views' and so forth.] 'Like <s>Devadatta</s>' — the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s [say]. Just as <s>Devadatta</s>, through the arising of evil desire to attract the Blessed One's <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>saṃgha</s> — whose disposition was to dwell with few concerns — fell from his supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>). Because of the statement in the <s>sūtra</s>. For thus it is read in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Then to <s>Devadatta</s>, overcome by gain and honor, this evil wish-born [thought] arose: "Oh, would that the Blessed One would hand over the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>saṃgha</s> to me. I would guide the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>saṃgha</s>, and the Blessed One, with few concerns, would dwell devoted to the practice of comfort in the present life." Simultaneously with the arising of that thought, <s>Devadatta</s> fell from that supernatural power' — and so forth in detail. Similarly, those too fall [from their attainment of freedom from desire] at the very time of the arising of views.

body.text: (V.7) etatpūrvako hi teṣv ātmagrāha iti. nityapiṇḍasaṃjñāpūrvakaḥ.
body.translated_text: (V.7) 'For the grasping of self in those is preceded by this' — preceded by the perception of a permanent mass (<s>nityapiṇḍasaṃjñā</s>).

body.text: sarvaiveti. paṃcaprakārāpi. satkāya iti. paṃcasūpādānaskandheṣu. sarvaiva hi viparītadṛṣṭisvabhāvapravṛttā dṛṣṭiḥ mithyādṛṣṭiḥ satkāyadṛṣṭyādikā mithyopanidhyānāt. anyās tu samāropikā iti. katham ucchedadṛṣṭiḥ samāropikā. bāhulika eṣa nirdeṣaḥ. āryaḥ prahīṇatvād iti. tyaktatvāt. ohāk tyāga ity etasya dhātor grahaṇāt. ādiśabdalopaḥ kṛta iti. dṛṣṭyādīnām upādānaskaṃdhānāṃ paratvena pradhānatvenāmarśo dṛṣṭiparāmarśa iti. paraśabdaprayogeṇa cāyam atiśayārtho [Tib. 111a] labhyata ity ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ. ahetau hetudṛṣṭir iti. duḥkhadarśanaprahātavya ucyate. amārge ca mārgadṛṣṭir iti. mārgadarśanaprahātavyaḥ. śīlavratamātrakam iti. śīlavratam api bauddhānāṃ mokṣaprāptaye bhavati. na tu tanmātrakam ity atas tadanyeṣāṃ dṛṣṭiḥ. atrāpi kila ādiśabda iti. śīlavratādiparāmarśaḥ. śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. śīlavrataṃ hi rūpaskaṃdhasaṃgṛhītam. ato 'nyaskandhagrahaṇārtham ādiśabda iti.
body.translated_text: 'All' — of all five types. '<s>Satkāya</s>' — regarding the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>). Indeed, every view that operates with the intrinsic nature of a perverted view is wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) — <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (identity-view) and the rest are [wrong view] because of wrong attention (<s>mithyopanidhyāna</s>). But the others are superimpositions (<s>samāropikā</s>). 'How is the annihilationist view (<s>ucchedadṛṣṭi</s>) a superimposition?' This statement is made according to the majority [of cases]. 'The Noble One, because of having abandoned' — because of having relinquished. From the use of the root <s>ohāk</s> meaning 'relinquishment.' 'Elision of the word <s>ādi</s> is made' — thus. The apprehension of the aggregates of clinging that are views and the rest as supreme, as preeminent — that is view-clinging (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>). And by the use of the word <s>para</s> (supreme), the sense of excellence is obtained — [says] teacher <s>Saṃghabhadra</s>. 'A view of cause in what is not a cause' — is said to be abandoned by seeing suffering (<s>duḥkhadarśanaprahātavya</s>). 'And a view of path in what is not a path' — is to be abandoned by seeing the path (<s>mārgadarśanaprahātavya</s>). 'Mere morality and vows' — morality and vows are practiced by Buddhists too for the attainment of liberation, but not those alone — therefore the view belongs to those other [non-Buddhists]. 'Here too, the word <s>ādi</s>' — thus: clinging to morality-and-vows and the rest (<s>śīlavratādiparāmarśa</s>). The clinging to morality and vows (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>). For what reason? Morality and vows are included in the form aggregate. Therefore the word <s>ādi</s> is for the purpose of including the other aggregates.

body.text: (V.8) kasmād ayaṃ na samudayadarśanaprahātavya iti. hetau vipratipannatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. tatkṛto 'pi kāraṇābhiniveśa iti. nityaikātmakartṛgrāhakṛto 'pīty arthaḥ. tata eva prahīyata iti. duḥkhadarśanād eva prahīyate. yas tarhi jalāgnipraveśādibhiḥ svargopapattiṃ paśyati. śīlavratena vā śuddhim iti. nāyaṃ tatkṛtaḥ kāraṇābhiniveśaḥ. kathaṃ duḥkhadarśanāt prahīyate. tasmāt samudayadarśanaprahātavyaḥ evāyaṃ bhaviṣyatīty abhiprāyāḥ. vaibhāṣika āha. so 'pi duḥkhadarśanaprahātavya iti vistaraḥ duḥkhe vipratipannatvād iti vaibhāṣikāḥ. kathaṃ ca punar duḥkhe vipratipannaḥ. [Tib. 111b] tena svargagamanāc chuddhidarśanād vā. atiprasaṃga iti vistareṇācāryaḥ. sarveṣāṃ sāsravālaṃbanānāṃ adṛṣṭisvabhāvānāṃ ca duḥkhādidarśanaprahātavyānāṃ
body.translated_text: (V.8) 'Why is this not to be abandoned by seeing origination (<s>samudayadarśana</s>)?' — the intent is: because of being wrongly directed regarding the cause. 'The attachment to a cause produced by that' — the meaning is: produced by the grasping of a permanent, unitary self as agent. 'Is abandoned from that very [seeing]' — is abandoned from seeing suffering alone. 'But when one who enters fire, water, and the like sees rebirth in heaven, or [sees] purification through morality and vows' — this attachment to a cause is not produced by that [self-grasping]. How is it abandoned by seeing suffering? Therefore this will be to be abandoned by seeing origination — this is the intent. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'That too is to be abandoned by seeing suffering' — and so forth in detail. 'Because of being wrongly directed regarding suffering' — the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s [say]. And how is one wrongly directed regarding suffering? Through seeing that [one attains] heaven or purification from that [practice]. 'Overextension' — and so forth in detail, the <s>Ācārya</s> [responds]. Of all [views] that have contaminated [<s>dharma</s>s] as their object, that do not have the intrinsic nature of views, and that are to be abandoned by seeing suffering and the rest

body.text: duḥkhe vipratipannatvāt. sarvaṃ hi sāsravaṃ vastu duḥkham iti duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaprasaṃgaḥ. tathā ca sati na kaścit samudayādidarśanaprahātavyaḥ syāt. idaṃ cāparaṃ vaktavyaṃ. kīdṛśo vānyaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśo mārgadarśanaprahātavyaḥ sa vaktavyaḥ. yo 'pi hi gośīlādinā śudhyati yāvat sukhaduḥkhavyatikramaṃ cānuprāpnotīti paśyati. tasyāpy ayam akāraṇaṃ kāraṇataḥ pratyetīti duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśa iti paṭhyeta. vaibhāṣika āha. yo mārgadarśanaprahātavyālaṃbana iti. yo mārgadarśanaheyān aṣṭau mithyādṛṣṭyādīn ālaṃbate. sa mārgadarśanaprahātavyaḥ śīlavataparāmarśa iti. so 'pi hi nāma duḥkhe vipratipanna ity ācāryaḥ. mithyādṛṣṭyādayo hi mārgadarśanaprahātavyā aṣṭāv anuśayaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśasyālambanaṃ. te ca sāsravatvād duḥkhasatyasaṃgṛhītāḥ. tatra ca sa vipratipanna iti. duḥkhadarśanaprahātavya eva syād [Tib. 112a] ity abhiprāyaḥ. yasya ceti vistaraḥ. yasya ca pudgalasya nāsti mārga iti mārgālaṃbanā mithyādṛṣṭirasti vicikitsā vā. sa pudgalo nāsti mokṣamārga iti paśyan. vicikitsan vā. kim asti mārgaḥ. nāstīti saṃdihyan. kathaṃ tayā mithyādṛṣṭyā śuddhiṃ pratyeṣyati pratipatsyate etayā mithyādṛṣṭyā etayā vā vicikitsayeti. mithyādṛṣṭivicikitsāyogād eva hi tasya śuddhipratipattir nāsti. athānyam iti vistaraḥ. athānyaṃ sāṃkhyādiparikalpitaṃ mokṣamārgaṃ parāmṛśya gṛhītvā. eṣa mokṣamārgo bauddhīyo nāstīty āha. so 'pīti. tīrthikaḥ. tenaivānyena sāṃkhyādiparikalpitena śuddhiṃ pratyeti. na tayā mithyādṛṣṭyeti kṛtvā. tasyāpy asau śīlavrataparāmarśo mārgadarśanaprahātavyālaṃbano na sidhyati. kiṃ tarhi. sāṃkhyādiparikalpitamārgālaṃbana eveti ayaṃ cānyo doṣaḥ. yaś cāpīti vistaraḥ. yaś cāpi mithyādṛṣṭikaḥ samudayanirodhadarśanaprahātavyayā mithyādṛṣṭyā śuddhiṃ pratyeti. sa kasmān na taddarśanaheyaḥ. sa śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ kasmān na samudayanirodhadarśanaheya ity arthaḥ. tasmāt parīkṣya eṣo 'rtha iti. yasmād ayaṃ duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśo na saṃbhavati. mārgadarśanaprahātavyaś ca. atiprasaṃgādidoṣāt [Tib. 112b] tasmāt parīkṣya eṣo 'rthaḥ. śīlavrataparāmarśo duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaḥ mārgadarśanaprahātavyaś ceti. tad idam ācāryeṇa saṃśayāvadyaṃ kṛtaṃ. na svamataṃ darśitaṃ.
body.translated_text: because of being mistaken about suffering. For all contaminated things (<s>sāsrava vastu</s>) are suffering — hence there would be the undesirable consequence that [all afflictions having contaminated objects] are to be abandoned by seeing suffering. And if so, nothing would be to be abandoned by seeing the origin and the rest. And this further point must be stated: what other clinging to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>), to be abandoned by seeing the path, should be described? For even one who sees that one is purified by the practice of cow-observances and the like, up to one who sees that one attains the transcendence of pleasure and pain — for that one too, this [clinging] apprehends what is not a cause as a cause — so it would be read as clinging to rules and rituals to be abandoned by seeing suffering. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'That which has as its object what is to be abandoned by seeing the path' — that which takes as object the eight [afflictions] beginning with wrong view that are to be abandoned by seeing the path — that is the clinging to rules and rituals to be abandoned by seeing the path. 'Even that one is mistaken about suffering' — says the <s>Ācārya</s>. For the eight latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>) to be abandoned by seeing the path, beginning with wrong view, which are the object of that clinging to rules and rituals — those, being contaminated, are included in the truth of suffering. And with respect to those, that [person] is mistaken — the intent is: therefore it would be to be abandoned by seeing suffering alone. 'And for one who' — and so forth in detail. And for that person who has no path — for whom there exists wrong view regarding the path or doubt — that person, seeing 'there is no path to liberation,' or doubting — 'does the path exist or not?' — how will he pursue purification through that wrong view or through that doubt? For because of his engagement with wrong view and doubt, he has no pursuit of purification. 'But if another' — and so forth in detail. But if, having grasped another path to liberation devised by <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s and the like, he says: 'The Buddhist path to liberation does not exist' — that one too, that non-Buddhist, pursues purification by that very other [path] devised by <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s and the like, not by that wrong view. And thus, his clinging to rules and rituals having as its object what is to be abandoned by seeing the path is not established. Rather, it has as its object only the path devised by <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s and the like. And this is another fault: 'And one who' — and so forth in detail. And one who, being of wrong views, pursues purification through the wrong view to be abandoned by seeing the origin or cessation — why is that [clinging] not to be abandoned by seeing those? Why is that clinging to rules and rituals not to be abandoned by seeing the origin or cessation? — this is the meaning. 'Therefore, this matter should be examined' — since this clinging to rules and rituals to be abandoned by seeing suffering is not tenable, nor that to be abandoned by seeing the path — because of the fault of over-extension and the like — therefore this matter should be examined: that clinging to rules and rituals is to be abandoned by seeing suffering and to be abandoned by seeing the path. This was made by the <s>Ācārya</s> as an occasion for doubt; his own position was not shown.

body.text: anya āhur yogācāramatim apekṣyaivaṃ kṛtaṃ. yogācārā hy aṣṭāviṃśatyuttaraṃ kleśaśataṃ varṇayaṃti. yathaiva hi duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyā ime daśānuśayā bhavaṃti. satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ. aṃtagrāhadṛṣṭiḥ. mithyādṛṣṭiḥ. dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ.
body.translated_text: Others say: this was done with reference to the <s>Yogācāra</s> view. For the <s>Yogācāra</s>s describe one hundred and twenty-eight afflictions. Just as these ten latent dispositions are to be abandoned by seeing suffering — the view of the self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the extreme view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>),

body.text: śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ. vicikitsā. rāgaḥ. pratighaḥ. mānaḥ. avidyā ceti. tathaiveme daśa samudayadarśanaprahātavyāḥ. tathaiva ca daśa nirodhadarśanaprahātavyāḥ. daśa mārgadarśanaprahātavyā iti. catvāriṃśat kāmāvacarā darśanaheyā bhavaṃti. bhāvanāheyās tu ṣaṭ. akalpikā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ. ucchedadṛṣṭiḥ. sahajo rāgaḥ. pratighaḥ. mānaḥ. avidyā ceti. ṣaṭcatvāriṃśat kāmavācarā anuśayā bhavaṃti. rūpāvacarās tv ekacatvāriṃśad eta eva pratighavarjyāḥ. yathā rūpāvacarāḥ. evam ārūpyāvacarā iti.
body.translated_text: clinging to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), passion (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), pride (<s>māna</s>), and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) — similarly, these same ten are to be abandoned by seeing the origin; similarly, ten by seeing cessation; and ten by seeing the path. Thus, forty Desire-Realm [afflictions] are to be abandoned by seeing. Those to be abandoned by cultivation are six: non-conceptual view of the self-existing body (<s>akalpikā satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the annihilationist view (<s>ucchedadṛṣṭi</s>), innate passion (<s>sahaja rāga</s>), aversion, pride, and ignorance. Thus, forty-six Desire-Realm latent dispositions exist. The Form-Realm ones are forty-one — these same, minus aversion. As are the Form-Realm ones, so are the Formless-Realm ones.

body.text: atra kaścit samādhim āha. yad uktam atiprasaṃgaḥ sarveṣāṃ sāsravālaṃbanānāṃ duḥkhe vipratipannatvād iti. atra brūmaḥ nātiprasaṃgaḥ. duḥkhādimukhena vipratipatteḥ. yady api sāsravālaṃbanā [Tib. 113a] duḥkhasatyavipratipannāḥ. tathāpi tu kecid duḥkhamukhena vipratipannāḥ. kecit samudayamukhena. kecin nirodhavipratipannavipratipannāḥ. kecin mārgavipratipannavipratipannāḥ. tatra ye duḥkhamukhena duḥkhe vipratipannāḥ. te duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyāḥ. śīlavrataparāmarśaś ca duḥkhamukhena duḥkhe vipratipanno nityātmagrahaṇāt. tasmād duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaḥ. yas tu mārgavipratipannavipratipannaḥ. tadyathā sāṃkhyanirgraṃthādayaḥ svaparikalpitaṃ mārgaṃ gṛhītvā nāsti bauddhānāṃ mokṣamārga iti mithyādṛṣṭim utpādayaṃti. tāṃ ca mithyādṛṣṭiṃ śīlavrataparāmarśo 'grataḥ paśyati. ayam eṣāṃ śīlavrataparāmarśo mārgadarśanaprahātavyaḥ. mārgavipratipannavipratipannatvāt. nāsti tu sa śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ yaḥ samudayamukhena vipratipadyeta. nāpi yo nirodhamukhena vipratipannavipratipannaḥ syāt. tasmād duḥkhamārgadarśanaprahātavya eva śīlavrataparāmarśa iti. kathaṃ punaḥ samudayanirodhamukhena na vipratipadyate. atrācāryasaṃghabhadra āha. [Tib. 113b] śūlavrataparāmarśaḥ samudayanirodhadarśanaprahātavyaḥ. taccharīrānupapatteḥ. akāraṇe hi kāraṇabhiniveśaḥ. amārge ca mārgābhiniveśeḥ. śīlavrataparāmarśaśarīraṃ. samudayāpavādikāyāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyāṃ śuddhyabhiniveśe nanv ākasmikāj janmadarśanam asya syāt. kvacid api kāraṇabuddhyabhāvāt. duḥkhasamudayayor hi dravyato 'vyatirekāt. īśvarādiskandhā api tenāpoditāḥ syuḥ. nirodhāpavādikāyāṃ tu mithyādṛṣṭau śuddhipratyāgamanān nirodhopāyakalpanaiva na saṃbhavati. kathaṃ nāsti nirodha iti taddarśanapṛṣṭhena tadupāyakalpanā vyarthā bhavet. evaṃ ca śīlavrataparāmarśaśarīrānupapattiḥ. mārgadarśanaprahātavyo 'pi śīlavrataparāmarśa evaṃ na saṃbhavet. nāsti
body.translated_text: Here, someone offers a resolution: what was stated — 'there is over-extension, because of all [afflictions] having contaminated objects being mistaken about suffering' — to this we say: there is no over-extension, because the mistake is through the door of suffering and the rest. Even though [afflictions] having contaminated objects are mistaken about the truth of suffering, nevertheless some are mistaken through the door of suffering, some through the door of the origin, some are mistaken through the mistake about cessation, and some are mistaken through the mistake about the path. Therein, those that are mistaken about suffering through the door of suffering are to be abandoned by seeing suffering. And clinging to rules and rituals that is mistaken about suffering through the door of suffering — because of grasping [things] as permanent and as self — is therefore to be abandoned by seeing suffering. But that which is mistaken through the mistake about the path — for example, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>s, <s>Nirgrantha</s>s, and the like, having grasped a path of their own devising, generate the wrong view 'there is no path to liberation for the Buddhists.' And that clinging to rules and rituals regards that wrong view as foremost — this clinging to rules and rituals of theirs is to be abandoned by seeing the path, because of being mistaken through the mistake about the path. But there is no clinging to rules and rituals that would be mistaken through the door of the origin, nor any that would be mistaken through the mistake about cessation. Therefore, clinging to rules and rituals is to be abandoned by seeing suffering and by seeing the path only. But how is it that it is not mistaken through the door of the origin and cessation? Here the <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> says: clinging to rules and rituals to be abandoned by seeing the origin and cessation [does not exist] because of the inapplicability of its essential character (<s>śarīra</s>). For grasping what is not a cause as a cause, and grasping what is not the path as the path — this is the essential character of clinging to rules and rituals. When, in connection with wrong view that denies the origin, there is a grasping of purification — would this not amount to seeing birth as causeless? — because of the absence of any understanding of a cause anywhere. For since suffering and the origin are not different in substance, the aggregates and the like posited by <s>Īśvara</s> and the rest would also be accounted for thereby. But when, in connection with wrong view that denies cessation, the pursuit of purification would be impossible — for how could one devise a means to cessation while holding 'there is no cessation'? Behind such a view, devising a means to cessation would be pointless. And thus, the essential character of clinging to rules and rituals is inapplicable. The clinging to rules and rituals to be abandoned by seeing the path, too, would not be possible in this way — because of the inapplicability of devising a path behind [the view] 'there is no path.' For one who has wrong view regarding the path, or doubt — that one, seeing 'there is no path to liberation,' or doubting — how will he pursue purification through that? It is indeed tenable that there is grasping of purification in connection with wrong view that denies the Noble Path. By the rational grasping thereof. For another path to liberation has been established in his mind, from which, in connection with wrong view denying the true path, a rational understanding arises: this is rational — that another path to liberation does not exist. Or he doubts another path to liberation. Thus, from the rational grasping of the means to purification, it is tenable. And that other path to liberation established in his mind — that indeed is not the object of his clinging to rules and rituals to be abandoned by seeing the path — because it takes as object only what belongs to his own school. If one thinks that [clinging] to be abandoned by seeing cessation is also applicable, because of the power of devising [means thereto] — for another locus of liberation has been established in his mind, from which, in connection with wrong view denying true liberation, there is a rational grasping — therefore this is the same. No — because of the inapplicability of grasping of purification when cessation is denied, through the commonality of grasping [things] as permanent and peaceful. For when there is a difference in understanding entities as real or not-real, someone seeks a means to liberation — surely he has the certainty 'liberation exists.' And one who has the certainty that liberation exists surely has the grasping of permanence and peace with respect to it — otherwise, aspiration thereto would be inapplicable. Therefore, just as for followers of this teaching, even the difference in understanding <s>nirvāṇa</s> as real or not-real [does not affect] the commonality of grasping permanence and peace — seeing the denial thereof as a fault. Even for one in whose mind some locus of liberation has been established, because of the commonality of grasping permanence and peace, in the denial of liberation, the rational grasping is tenable. For rules and rituals and the like are different from the Noble Path — both in intrinsic nature and in aspect. But there is no difference in the grasping of permanence and peace. Therefore there is no commonality of devising [means]. Thus, clinging to rules and rituals to be abandoned by seeing the path alone is possible, not that to be abandoned by seeing cessation. Here, clinging to rules and rituals is accepted as twofold by the <s>Ābhidharmikas</s>. Therein, what kind of clinging to rules and rituals is established as to be abandoned by seeing suffering, and what kind as to be abandoned by seeing the path? Even one who pursues purification through cow-observances and the like — that one too sees the path in what is not the path. That whose object is rules and rituals and the like — that suffering — that clinging to rules and rituals is to be abandoned by seeing suffering. That whose object is the mistake about the path — that is to be abandoned by seeing the path. That whose object is rules and rituals and the like is not a mistake about the path. Thus it does not cause harm as [much as] that whose object is the mistake about the path. Because that whose object is rules and rituals and the like is coarse, not far-gone, not of firm intention, and destructible with little effort — and the opposite for that whose object is the mistake about the path.

body.text:
mārga iti darśanapṛṣṭhena mārgaparikalpanānupapatteḥ. yasya hi mārgālaṃbanā mithyādṛṣṭir vicikitsā vāsti. sa nāsti mokṣamārga iti paśyan vicikitsan vā kathaṃ tayā śuddhiṃ pratyeṣyatīti. upapadyata evasyāryamārgāpavādikāyāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyāṃ śuddhyabhiniveśaḥ. nyāyatas tatgrahaṇāt. anyā hi tena mokṣamārgo hṛdi niveśito bhavati. yato 'sya sadbhūtamārgāpavādikāyāṃ mithyādṛṣṭau nyāyabuddhir utpadyate. eṣa nyāyo yad anyo mokṣamārgo nāsti. yac ca syān na vety anyaṃ mokṣamārgaṃ vicikitsatīti. nyāyato hi śuddhyupāyagrahaṇam upapadyate. yaś cāsāv anyo mokṣamārgas tena hṛdi niveśitaḥ. [Tib. 114a] sa naiva tasya mārgadarśanaheyasya śīlavrataparāmarśasya viṣayaḥ. svanaikāyikamātrālaṃbanatavāt. atha mataṃ nirodhadarśanaheyo 'pi prayujyate. tatkalpanāsāmarthyāt. anyad dhi tena mokṣasthānaṃ hṛdi niveśitaṃ bhavati. yato 'sya sadbhūtamokṣāpavādikāyāṃ mithyādṛṣṭau nyāyato grahaṇaṃ. ataḥ samānam etad iti. tan na. nityaśāṃtagrahaṇasāmānyena tadapavāde śuddhyabhiniveśānupapatteḥ. dravyādravyasaṃpratipattibhede hi kaścin mokṣopāyam anveṣate. dhruvaṃ tasyāsti mokṣa iti niścayaḥ. yasya cāsti mokṣaniścayo dhruvaṃ. tasya tatra nityaśāṃtagrahaṇam. anyathā tatra prārthanānupapatteḥ. tatra yathehadhārmikāṇāṃ nivāṇe dravyādravyasaṃpratipattibhedo 'pi nityaśāṃtagrahaṇasāmānyāt tadapavāde doṣo darśanam eva. yenapi kiṃcin mokṣasthānaṃ hṛdi niveśitaṃ syāt. tasyāpi nityaśāṃtagrahaṇasāmānyān mokṣāpavāde nyāyagrahaṇam upapadyate. bhinnā hi śīlavratādayaḥ svabhāvataś cākārataś cāryamārgāt. nāsti tu nityaśāṃtagrahaṇabheda iti. nāsti kalpanāsāmānyaṃ. ato mārgadarśanaprahātavya eva śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ saṃbhavati. na nirodhadarśanaprahātavya iti. iha [Tib. 114b] sīlavrataparāmarśo dviprakāra iṣyate ābhidharmikaiḥ. tatra kīdṛśaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśo duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyo vyavasthāpyate. kīdṛo mārgadarśanaprahātavyaḥ. yo 'pihi gośīlādinā śudbhiṃ pratyeti. so 'py amārge mārgaṃ paśatīti. yaḥ śīlavratādiduḥkhālaṃbanaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ. sa duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaḥ. yo mārgavipratipattyālaṃbanaḥ. sa mārgadarśanaprahātavyaḥ. yaḥ śīlavratādyālaṃbanaḥ. sa na mārgavipratipattiḥ. tathā na bādhate. yathā mārgavipratipattyālaṃbanaḥ. yasmāc chīlavratādyālaṃbana audārikaḥ. na dūragataḥ na dṛḍhāśayaḥ alpayatnaghātyaḥ. tadviparyayān mārgavipratipattyālaṃbana
iti.
body.translated_text: 'the path' — because the devising of a path through the door of seeing is untenable. For one who has the wrong view that takes the path as its object, or doubt: that one, seeing 'there is no path to liberation,' or doubting, how will he pursue purification through that? It is indeed tenable that there is grasping of purification in connection with wrong view that denies the Noble Path, by the rational grasping thereof. For another path to liberation has been established in his mind, from which, in connection with wrong view denying the true path, a rational understanding arises in him. This is rational: that another path to liberation does not exist; and he doubts whether another path to liberation might exist or not. For from the rational [grasping] there is a tenable grasping of the means to purification. And that other path to liberation established by him in his mind — [Tib. 114a] that indeed is not the object of his clinging to rules and rituals to be abandoned by seeing the path, because it takes as object only what belongs to his own school. Now if it is held that [clinging] to be abandoned by seeing cessation is also applicable, because of the power of devising [means] thereto — for another locus of liberation has been established by him in his mind, from which, in connection with wrong view denying true liberation, there is a rational grasping; therefore this is the same — that is not so. Because of the inapplicability of grasping of purification when [cessation] is denied, through the commonality of grasping [things] as permanent and peaceful. For when there is a difference in understanding entities as real or not-real, someone seeks a means to liberation; surely he has the certainty 'liberation exists.' And one who has the certainty that liberation exists surely has, with respect to it, the grasping of permanence and peace — otherwise aspiration thereto would be inapplicable. Therefore, just as for followers of this teaching, even the difference in understanding <s>nirvāṇa</s> as real or not-real [does not affect] the commonality of grasping permanence and peace — seeing the denial thereof as the fault [to be abandoned by seeing]; even for one in whose mind some locus of liberation has been established, because of the commonality of grasping permanence and peace, in the denial of liberation, the rational grasping is tenable. For rules and rituals and the like are different from the Noble Path both in intrinsic nature and in aspect. But there is no difference in the grasping of permanence and peace. Therefore there is no commonality of devising [means]. Thus, clinging to rules and rituals to be abandoned by seeing the path alone is possible, not that to be abandoned by seeing cessation. Here, clinging to rules and rituals is accepted as twofold by the <s>Ābhidharmikas</s>. Therein, what kind of clinging to rules and rituals is established as to be abandoned by seeing suffering, and what kind as to be abandoned by seeing the path? Even one who pursues purification through cow-observances and the like — that one too sees the path in what is not the path. That clinging to rules and rituals whose object is rules and rituals and the like — that suffering — is to be abandoned by seeing suffering. That whose object is the mistake about the path is to be abandoned by seeing the path. That whose object is rules and rituals and the like is not [a grasping of] the mistake about the path. Thus it does not cause harm as [much as] that whose object is the mistake about the path. Because that whose object is rules and rituals and the like is coarse, not far-gone, not of firm intention, and destructible with little effort, [Tib. 114b] and the opposite for that whose object is the mistake about the path.

children.translated_text: 'A set of four inversions (<s>viparyāsa</s>) from each of three views' —

body.text: iti. dṛṣṭitrayasvabhāvā viparyāsā iti darśayati. satkāyadṛṣṭer ātmadṛṣṭir ātmaviparyāsa
body.translated_text: thus he shows that the inversions have the intrinsic nature of three views. 'The self-view (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) from the view of the self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) is the inversion of self'

body.text: iti. nātmīyadṛṣṭir ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: — the intent is: not the view of 'mine' (<s>ātmīyadṛṣṭi</s>).

body.text: sakalety apara iti. sakalā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ ātmadṛṣṭir ātmīyadṛṣṭiś cātmaviparyāsa ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'The complete [view]' — according to another. The complete view of the self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) — both the self-view and the view of 'mine' — is the inversion of self, is the meaning.

body.text: vaibhāṣika āha. katham ātmīyadṛṣṭir viparyāsa iti. na hy ātmīyaviparyāsa ity ucyate. kathaṃ ca na bhavitavyam iti paraḥ. viparyāsasūtrād iti vaibhāṣikaḥ. [Tib. 115a] anātmani ātmeti viparyāsa iti sūtravacanāt. na punar ātmīya iti. asty evaṃ sūtranirdeśaḥ. na punar asāv ātmadṛṣṭer arthāṃtarabhūtā. kathaṃ kṛtvā. ātmānam eva tatra paṃcopādānaskaṃdheṣu vāśinaṃ paśyann ātmīyaṃ paśyatīti. na kevalam ātmānaṃ paśyaty ātmīyam api paśyatīty arthaḥ. ātmadṛṣṭir evāsau dvimukhīti. ātmātmīyamukhī ekā dravyato 'stīti ahaṃkāramamakāramukhadvayavatīty arthaḥ. athāham ity etasmāt prathamanirdiṣṭān mameti ṣāṣṭhīnirdiṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭyaṃtaraṃ syāt. mayā mahyam ity etad api syāt. dṛṣṭyaṃtaram iti prakṛtaṃ. mayeti tṛtīyānirdeśān mahyam ity ca caturthīnirdeśāt. aniṣṭaṃ caitat. tasmāt sakaleti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: 'How is the view of "mine" an inversion?' — for it is not called 'the inversion of mine' (<s>ātmīyaviparyāsa</s>). 'And how should it not be so?' — says the other. 'From the inversion <s>sūtra</s>' — says the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>. From the <s>sūtra</s> statement: 'the inversion [of perceiving] self in what is non-self.' And not [the inversion of perceiving] 'mine.' There is indeed such a <s>sūtra</s> statement. But that is not something different from the self-view. How so? In seeing the self as exercising mastery over those five clinging-aggregates, one sees [them as] 'mine.' The meaning is: not only does one see a self, one also sees 'mine.' The self-view itself is two-faced — facing both self and mine, being one in substance — meaning: having two faces, namely the 'I'-making (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) and the 'mine'-making (<s>mamaṃkāra</s>). But if from this first-person 'I' (<s>aham</s>), the genitive 'mine' (<s>mama</s>) were a different view — then 'by me' (<s>mayā</s>) and 'to me' (<s>mahyam</s>) would also be different views. The continuation is: this too would be a different view — 'by me' from the instrumental and 'to me' from the dative. And this is undesired. Therefore, 'the complete [view]' is established.

body.text: kasmād anye kleśā na viparyāsā iti. satkāyadṛṣṭyaṃtagrāhadṛṣṭiparāmarśebhyo 'nye ucchedamithyādṛṣṭiśīlavrataparāmarśarāgādayaḥ. tribhiḥ kāraṇair iti.
body.translated_text: Why are other afflictions not perversions? Other than the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the extreme view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), and the [two types of] clinging (<s>parāmarśa</s>) — annihilationist wrong view, clinging to morality and rituals, desire, and the rest. Because of three reasons —

body.text: viparyāsānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ. yatraitāni samastāni kāraṇāni saṃti. te viparyāsāḥ sthāpitāḥ. yatra tu na samastāni. te na viparyāsā ity uktaṃ bhavati. tanmātraśuddhyālaṃbanād [Tib. 115b] iti. yasmāc chīlavratamātreṇa śuddhir ity ālaṃbate nitīrayati. tasmān naikāntaviparyastaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ. na hi śīlavrataṃ śuddhikāraṇaṃ na bhavati. kevalaṃ tu na bhavatīti. katham asya samāropakatvaṃ. tanmātreṇa śuddhikāraṇabhāvasamāropāt. yady asaṃtīrako na viparyāsaḥ yat tarhi sūtra uktaṃ. tat kathaṃ. na hi saṃjñā saṃtīrikā nāpi cittaṃ.
body.translated_text: this is the establishment of the perversions. Where all these reasons exist together — those are established as perversions. But where they do not all exist together — those are not perversions — this is what has been said. 'Because of grasping purification by that alone as the object' — [Tib. 115b] because it assesses, determines, that purification is by morality and rituals alone. Therefore the clinging to morality and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>) is not entirely perverted. For morality and rituals are indeed a cause of purification — they are simply not the sole [cause]. How then is there superimposition in this case? Because of superimposing that purification is caused by those alone. If [it is objected that] what is without assessment is not a perversion — then what is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>, how [is it to be understood]? For neither perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) makes assessments, nor does mind (<s>citta</s>).

body.text: dvādaśa viparyāsā iti. caturṣu viparyāseṣu pratyekaṃ saṃjñācittadṛṣṭiviparyāsā iti. katham ity ucyate. anitye nityam iti vistaraḥ evaṃ yāvad anātmany ātmeti. duḥkhe sukham iti saṃjñādṛṣṭacittaviparyāsās trayaḥ. aśucau śucīty eta eva trayaḥ. yāvad anātmany ātmeti eta eva traya iti. tatrāṣṭau darśanaprahātavyā iti. anitye nityam iti saṃjñācittadṛṣṭiviparyāsās trayaḥ. anātmany ātmeti punas trayaḥ. duḥkhe sukham iti dṛṣṭiviparyāsaḥ. aśucau śucīti dṛṣṭiviparyāsa iti. catvāro bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ. katama ity āha. daḥkhe ca
body.translated_text: 'Twelve perversions' — in the four perversions, there are individually perception-perversion, mind-perversion, and view-perversion. How? It is stated: 'In what is impermanent, [grasping] permanence' — and so forth in detail, thus up to 'in what is non-self, [grasping] self.' 'In what is suffering, [grasping] happiness' — these three are perception, view, and mind perversions. 'In what is impure, [grasping] purity' — these same three. Up to 'in what is non-self, [grasping] self' — these same three. Among these, eight are to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>): 'in what is impermanent, [grasping] permanence' — these three are perception, mind, and view perversions; 'in what is non-self, [grasping] self' — again three; 'in what is suffering, [grasping] happiness' — the view-perversion; 'in what is impure, [grasping] purity' — the view-perversion. Four are to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>). Which? He says: 'In suffering

body.text: saṃjñācittaviparyāsāv aśucau ceti. duḥkhe sukham iti saṃjñācittaviparyāsau dvau. aśucau śucīti saṃjñācittaviparyāsāv aparau dvāv iti catvāraḥ. avītarāgasyāryasyeti. [Tib. 116a] srotaāpannasya sakṛdāgāminaś ca.
body.translated_text: the perception and mind perversions, and in the impure' — 'in what is suffering, [grasping] happiness' — these are two perception and mind perversions; 'in what is impure, [grasping] purity' — another two perception and mind perversions — making four. 'Of the noble one who has not yet become dispassionate' — [Tib. 116a] of the stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) and the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>).

body.text: tadviparyāsāv apīti. sattvasaṃjñāsamudācārāt sattvacittasamudācārāc ca. tadviparyāsāv api kiṃ neṣyete. sattvālaṃbanasaṃjñācittaviparyāsāv api kiṃ neṣyete. ātmaviparyāsāv api kiṃ neṣyete ity abhiprāyaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇam ity āhuḥ. na hi striyām ātmani ca vinā sattvasāṃjñayā kāmarāgo yukta iti. tasmād etāv apy anātmany ātmeti saṃjñācittaviparyāsau bhāvanāprahātavyāv iti prāptaṃ. vistara iti vacanād evaṃ neyaṃ. duḥkhe sukham iti aśucau śucīti yāvad anātmany ātmeti saṃjñāviparyāsaś cittaviparyāso dṛṣṭiviparyāsaḥ prahīyata iti. tāsmād dṛṣṭisamutthe eva dṛṣṭisaṃprayukte eva saṃjñācitte viparyāsau nānye. nādṛṣṭisaṃprayukte ity arthaḥ. etad uktaṃ bhavati. asty asau saṃjñācittavibhramaḥ. na tu viparyāsaḥ. yasmād asau dṛṣṭisamuttho na bhavati. kasmād ity āha. tatkālabhrāṃtimātratvād iti. strīdarśanakāle bhrāṃtimātratvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. yasmāt tatkālam eva darśanakālam evāryāṇāṃ bhrāṃtiḥ. tathā mithyājñānaṃ bhavati. alātacakracitrayakṣabhrāṃtivat. [Tib. 116b] yathā alāta āśu bhramyamāṇe tatkālamātraṃ cakram iti bhrāṃtir utpadyate. na paścāt. citralikhitaṃ ca yakṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatkālaṃ bhrāṃtir utpadyate yakṣa iti. tadvat. āryasyātra paridhyānān muhūrtaṃ sukhaśucibhrāṃtiḥ sattvabhrāṃtir vā. na tv asau viparyāsaḥ. uktaṃ hi bhagavatā dhandhāḥ khalu bhikṣavaḥ śrutavata āryaśrāvakasya smṛtisaṃpramoṣā utpadyaṃte. atha ca punaḥ kṣipram evāstaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchaṃtīti.
body.translated_text: 'Those two perversions as well' — because of the occurrence of the perception of beings (<s>sattvasaṃjñā</s>) and the occurrence of the mind of beings (<s>sattvacittā</s>). Why are those two perversions not accepted as well? — why are the perception and mind perversions regarding a being as object not accepted? — [that is,] why are the self-perversions not accepted? — this is the intent. What is the reason? — they say. For without the perception of a being, desire for a woman or for oneself is not reasonable. Therefore these two — perception and mind perversions of 'self' in what is non-self — are to be abandoned by cultivation — this is what follows. 'In detail' — because of the word 'in detail,' it should be led thus: 'In what is suffering, [grasping] happiness' — 'in what is impure, [grasping] purity' — up to 'in what is non-self, [grasping] self' — the perception-perversion, mind-perversion, and view-perversion are abandoned. Therefore, only perception and mind perversions that are originated from a view (<s>dṛṣṭisamuttha</s>) — that are associated with a view — are perversions, not others. Not those unassociated with a view — this is the meaning. This is what has been said: there is indeed that confusion of perception and mind, but it is not a perversion — because it is not originated from a view. Why? He says: 'Because it is mere momentary confusion.' The intent is: because of being mere confusion at the time of seeing a woman. Because the confusion of noble ones exists only at that time — at the time of seeing. So too wrong cognition arises — like the confusion of a fire-brand circle or a painted <s>yakṣa</s>. [Tib. 116b] Just as when a fire-brand is rapidly whirled, at that very moment alone a confusion arises as 'a circle,' but not afterwards. And seeing a painted <s>yakṣa</s>, at that time a confusion arises as '<s>yakṣa</s>' — in the same way. For a noble one, through inattention, there is momentary confusion of pleasure and purity, or confusion of a being — but that is not a perversion. For the Blessed One stated: 'Indeed, O monks, the losses of mindfulness that arise for the learned noble disciple are sluggish, and yet they quickly go to their setting, destruction, and exhaustion.'

body.text: yady asau saṃjñācittabhramo na viparyāso yat tarhi sthavirānandeneti vistaraḥ. āryeṇa vāgīśena sthavirānanda uktaḥ.
body.translated_text: If that confusion of perception and mind is not a perversion, then what about [the exchange between] the elder <s>Ānanda</s> — and so forth in detail. The elder <s>Ānanda</s> was addressed by the noble <s>Vāgīśa</s>:

children.text:
kāmarāgābhibhūtatvāc cittaṃ me paridahyate.
aṃga me gautama brūhi śāṃtitvam anukampayeti.
children.translated_text:
'Overwhelmed by sensual desire,
my mind is burning.
Please tell me, O <s>Gautama</s>,
the calming [of this], out of compassion.'

children.text:
viparyāsena saṃjñānāṃ cittaṃ te paridahyate
nimittaṃ varjyatāṃ tasmāc chubhaṃ rāgopasaṃhitam
children.translated_text:
'Through the perversion of perceptions,
your mind is burning.
Therefore, avoid the sign
of the beautiful that is connected with desire.'

body.text: iti. sa hi srotaāpannaḥ. tasya cānayā gāthayā viparyāsāstitvaṃ paridīpitam iti. tasmād iti vistaraḥ. yasmān nikāyāṃtarīyamataṃ vaibhāṣikair āgamena virudhyate. vaibhāṣikamataṃ ca nikāyāṃtarīyaiḥ. tasmāt sarva evāṣṭau saṃjñācittaviparyāsāḥ
body.translated_text: For he [<s>Vāgīśa</s>] was a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>). And by this verse, the existence of perversions in him is indicated. 'Therefore' — and so forth in detail. Because the view of the other schools is contradicted by scripture according to the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s, and the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> view [is contradicted] by the other schools — therefore, all eight perception and mind perversions

body.text: śaikṣasyāprahīṇā ity apare. kecit tṛtīyapākṣikāḥ. sūtravirodhaṃ ca pariharaṃti. katarasya sūtrasya. yad idaṃ vaibhāṣikaiḥ sūtram [Tib. 117a] ānītaṃ. yaś ca śrutavān āryaśrāvaka iti vistareṇa yāvat prahīyata iti. te 'pi cāryasatyānām iti vistaraḥ. te 'pi cāṣṭau saṃjñācittaviparyāsā āryasatyānāṃ duḥkhādīnāṃ yathābhūtajñānāt prahīyaṃte. na vinā tena yathābhūtajñānena. ity upāyasamākhyānād upāyapravartanān nāsti tasya sūtrasya virodhaḥ. yad idam uktam idaṃ duḥkham āryasatyam ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayo 'yaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam iti. tan na darśanamārgam evādhikṛtya. kiṃ tarhi. bhāvanāmārgam apīti. bhāvanāmārgo 'pi hy anāsravaś caturāryasatyālaṃbana eveti.
body.translated_text: are unabandoned for a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) — so say others. Some are a third party. And they avoid the contradiction with scripture. With which scripture? This scripture that was cited by the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s — [Tib. 117a] 'the learned noble disciple' and so forth in detail up to 'are abandoned.' They too — and the four noble truths — and so forth in detail. Those eight perception and mind perversions too are abandoned through the knowledge as it really is (<s>yathābhūtajñāna</s>) of the noble truths — suffering and the rest. Not without that knowledge as it really is. Because of the declaration of the means and the operation of the means, there is no contradiction with that <s>sūtra</s>. What was stated — 'This is the noble truth of suffering, this is the origin of suffering, this is the cessation of suffering, this is the path leading to the cessation of suffering as a noble truth' — that is not stated with reference to the path of seeing alone. What then? To the path of cultivation as well. For the path of cultivation too is outflow-free and has the four noble truths as its object.

body.text: (V.10) pravṛttibhedād iti. ākārabhedād ity arthaḥ. aprāpte viśeṣādhigama iti. samādhisaṃniśritāḥ sāsravāś cānāsravāś ca dharmā viśeṣās tasyādhigamaḥ sākṣātkaraṇaṃ viśeṣādhigamaḥ. tasminn aprāpte asaṃmukhīkṛte. sa viśeṣādhigamaḥ prāpto mayety abhimānaḥ. aguṇavato guṇavān aham iti. aguṇānvitasya guṇavān aham asmīti viparītaviṣayo māno mithyāmānaḥ. mithyāmānābhimānayoḥ kaḥ prativiśeṣaḥ. [Tib. 117b] pratilabdhaviśeṣādhigamapratirūpakaguṇasyābhiprāya iti savastuko 'bhimānaḥ. mithyāmānas tu nirguṇasya sato guṇavān aham asmīti nirvastukaḥ. mānavidhā iti. mānaprakārāḥ. sadṛśo hīno 'stīti mānavidhā saḍṛśo 'smīti mānavidhā hīno 'smīti mānavidheti vaktavyaṃ. dṛṣṭisaṃniśritās traya iti. pṛthagjanam adhikṛtya dṛṣṭisaṃniśritā ity ucyaṃte. ātmadṛṣṭiḥ pūrvam aham iti. paścād anaṃtaram ime mānāḥ. atimānamānonamānā yathākramaṃ ete bhavaṃti. kathaṃ śreyān aham asmīti mānavidhā dṛṣṭisaṃniśrito 'timānaḥ. 'sadṛśo 'smīti mānavidhā dṛṣṭisaṃniśrito mānaḥ hīno 'smīti mānavidhā dṛṣṭisaṃniśrita ūnamānaḥ. dvitīyaṃ trayam etatprātilaumyena yathākramaṃ neyaṃ. asti me śreyān asti me sadṛśaḥ asti me hīna iti dṛṣṭisaṃniśritā ūnamānamānātimānāḥ. tṛtīyaṃ nāsti me śreyān nāsti me sadṛśo nāsti me hīna iti. yathākramaṃ dṛṣṭisaṃniśritā mānātimānonamānāḥ. prākaraṇaṃ tu nirdeśaṃ parigṛhyeti. prakaraṇapādanirdeśaḥ. ko 'sau. yo 'sau pūrvam uktaḥ. hīnād viśiṣṭo 'smi [Tib. 118a] samena vetyādinirdeśaḥ. śreyān asmīti māno 'pi syāt hīnāpekṣayā. hīnād viśiṣṭo 'smi samena veti mānalakṣaṇanirdeśāt. atimāno 'py ayaṃ syāt samāpekṣayā. samād viśiṣṭo 'smīty atimānalakṣaṇanirdeśāt. mānātimāno 'py ayaṃ syāt visiṣṭāpekṣayā. viśiṣṭād
body.translated_text: (V.10) 'Because of the difference of operation' — meaning: because of the difference of aspect (<s>ākāra</s>). 'When the special attainment has not been reached' — the special [dharmas] — contaminated and uncontaminated <s>dharma</s>s supported by concentration — their attainment, their direct realization, is 'special attainment.' When that has not been reached, not been brought face to face — 'that special attainment has been reached by me' — this is conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>). 'For one without qualities, [thinking] I have qualities' — for one not endowed with qualities, [thinking] 'I have qualities' — conceit having a perverted object is wrong conceit (<s>mithyāmāna</s>). What is the distinction between wrong conceit and overestimating conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>)? [Tib. 117b] For one who has the semblance of a quality resembling a special attainment that has been obtained, the intent [constitutes] overestimating conceit, which has a basis. But wrong conceit, for one who has no quality at all, [thinking] 'I have qualities,' has no basis. 'Types of conceit' (<s>mānavidhā</s>) — varieties of conceit. '[Thinking] there exists one equal, one inferior' — these types of conceit should be stated as: 'I am equal,' 'I am inferior.' 'Three are based on views' (<s>dṛṣṭisaṃniśrita</s>) — they are called 'based on views' with reference to an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). First the self-view (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) [arises as] 'I' — then immediately after, these conceits. Superiority-conceit (<s>atimāna</s>), conceit (<s>māna</s>), and inferiority-conceit (<s>ūnamāna</s>) — these arise respectively. How? 'I am superior' — this type of conceit based on views is superiority-conceit. 'I am equal' — this type of conceit based on views is conceit. 'I am inferior' — this type of conceit based on views is inferiority-conceit. The second triad should be led in reverse order respectively: 'there exists one superior to me,' 'there exists one equal to me,' 'there exists one inferior to me' — these are inferiority-conceit, conceit, and superiority-conceit based on views. The third [triad]: 'there is none superior to me,' 'there is none equal to me,' 'there is none inferior to me' — these are respectively conceit, superiority-conceit, and inferiority-conceit based on views. 'But taking the doctrinal exposition' — the exposition of the <s>Prakaraṇapāda</s>. Which is that? That which was stated previously: 'I am superior to one inferior, [Tib. 118a] I am equal to one equal' — and so forth as the exposition. '[Thinking] I am superior' — this could also be [mere] conceit, with reference to an inferior [person]. Because of the definition of conceit as 'I am superior to one inferior, I am equal to one equal.' This could also be superiority-conceit, with reference to an equal [person]. Because of the definition of superiority-conceit as 'I am superior to one equal.' This could also be conceit-about-conceit (<s>mānātimāna</s>), with reference to a superior [person]. Because of the definition of conceit-about-conceit

body.text: viśiṣṭo 'smīti mānātimānalakṣaṇanirdeśāt.
body.translated_text: as 'I am superior to one superior.'

body.text: sarva iti grahaṇam asmimāno 'pi bhāvanāprahātavyaḥ. na kevalaṃ śeṣāḥ. śeṣā api darśanaprahātavyāḥ. na kevalam asmimāna iti pradarśānārthaṃ. nāvaśyam iti. prahīṇaṃ na samudācaratīti niyamaḥ. tathā hi śraddhādimiddhaduḥkhendriyacakṣur ādayaḥ prahīṇā api saṃudācaraṃti. darśanaheyānām antarmukhatvāt. bhāvanāheyālaṃbanaiva rāgadveṣamohair vijñaptir utthāpyata iti. bhāvanāheyam eva vadhādiparyavasthānaṃ.
body.translated_text: The word 'all' [indicates that] the 'I am' conceit (<s>asmimāna</s>) too is to be abandoned by cultivation — not only the remainder. The remainder too are to be abandoned by seeing — not only the 'I am' conceit — this is for the purpose of showing [both]. 'Not necessarily' — the rule is: what has been abandoned does not [necessarily] become active. For indeed, faith and the rest, drowsiness, and the suffering faculty, the eye [consciousness] and the rest — even though abandoned, they become active. 'Because of the inward-directedness of what is to be abandoned by seeing.' The informative action is generated only by desire, hatred, and delusion that have as their object what is to be abandoned by cultivation. Only the mental engulfment (<s>paryavasthāna</s>) of violence and the like is to be abandoned by cultivation.

children.translated_text: 'The mental engulfment of violence and the like' —

body.text: iti. ādiśabdenādattādānakāmamithyācāramṛṣāvādagrahaṇaṃ. tad bhāvanāheyaṃ bhāvanāheyadharmālaṃbanatvād iti. bhāvanāheyā vadhādikasattvādayaḥ eva dharmā asyālaṃbanam iti kṛtvā. satkāyadṛṣṭyādayo 'pi hi yady api bhāvanāheyān dharmān ālaṃbaṃte na tu kevalaṃ bhāvanāheyā ity ato na te bhāvanāheyāḥ. tatra prārthaneti. tatra traidhātukyām anityatāyāṃ prārthanā. kiṃ tatrāpi prārthanā bhavati. [Tib. 118a] bhavatīty āha. yathoktaṃ sūtre. yāvad ayam ātmā jīvati tiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati. tāvat sarogaḥ sagaṇḍaḥ saśalyaḥ sajvaraḥ saparidāhakaḥ. yataś cāyam ātmā ucchidyate vinaśyati na bhavati. iyatāyam ātmā samyak samucchinno bhavatīti. bhavatṛṣṇāyāḥ pradeśo gṛhyata iti. aho batāham airāvaṇo nāgarājaḥ syām ity evamādikā bhavatṛṣṇā na samudācarati. ādiśabdena kuveraḥ syāṃ strī syām ity evamādikā gṛhyate. prādeśagrahaṇād indraḥ syām ity evamādikā samudācaratīti darśitaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: by the word 'and the like,' taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, and false speech are grasped. That is to be abandoned by cultivation because it has as its object <s>dharma</s>s to be abandoned by cultivation. Because beings and other <s>dharma</s>s that are [objects of] violence and the like are themselves to be abandoned by cultivation. For the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest, even though they have as their object <s>dharma</s>s to be abandoned by cultivation, are not exclusively [objects] to be abandoned by cultivation — therefore they are not [only] to be abandoned by cultivation. 'Therein, aspiration' — therein, in the impermanence of the three realms, [there is] aspiration. Does aspiration arise even therein? [Tib. 118a] It does — he says. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'As long as this self lives, remains, endures, continues — so long is it with disease, with boils, with thorns, with fever, with burning. But when this self is cut off, destroyed, and ceases to be — then this self is properly and completely cut off.' A portion of craving for existence (<s>bhavatṛṣṇā</s>) is grasped [here]. [But] craving for existence such as 'Oh, may I become <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, the king of elephants!' — such craving for existence does not become active. By the word 'and the like,' [cravings] such as 'may I become <s>Kubera</s>,' 'may I become a woman' are grasped. Through the mention of 'a portion,' it is shown that [craving] such as 'may I become <s>Indra</s>' does become active.

body.text: (V.11) mānavidhā api bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ santīty uktam iti.
body.translated_text: (V.11) Types of conceit (<s>mānavidhā</s>) too are to be abandoned by cultivation — this has been stated.

children.translated_text: '[Abandoned] by the exhaustion of seeing and cultivation' —

body.text: iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of this statement.

children.translated_text:
'And types [of conceit] and the I-am [conceit] do not arise
for a noble one' —

body.text: pūrvaṃ bhāvanāheyaparigrahaṇaṃ kṛtaṃ.
body.translated_text: the inclusion of what is to be abandoned by cultivation was made earlier —

children.translated_text: '[Abandoned] by the exhaustion of seeing and cultivation' —

'The mental engulfment of violence and the like
is to be abandoned by cultivation, likewise' —

body.text: ity anena granthena. saṃprati teṣāṃ vidhādīnāṃ āryasyāsamudācāra ucyate.
body.translated_text: by this passage. Now the non-occurrence of types [of conceit] and the rest for a noble one is stated.

children.translated_text:
'And types [of conceit] and the I-am [conceit] do not arise
for a noble one' —

body.text: ādigrahaṇena yāvad bhavatṛṣṇāyā grahaṇam iti. vadhādiparyavasthānasya vibhavatṛṣṇāyāḥ pradeśasya bhavatṛṣṇāyāś ca grahaṇam ity arthaḥ. na saṃbhavaṃti na samudācaraṃti.
body.translated_text: By the word 'and the rest,' up to the craving for existence is grasped. The meaning is: the mental engulfment of violence and the like, a portion of craving for annihilation (<s>vibhavatṛṣṇā</s>), and craving for existence are grasped. They do not arise — they do not become active.

body.text: iti. tatpūrvakatvena tadupabṛṃhitatvāt. vadhādiparyavasthānaṃ mithyādṛṣṭipuṣṭaṃ tadabhyāsena karmaphalāpavāditvāt. bhagnapṛṣṭhatvāt tatpoṣakābhāvena bhaganpṛṣṭhatvād [Tib. 119a] ity arthaḥ. kaukṛtyaṃ bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ. bhāvanāheyadharmālaṃbanatvāt.
body.translated_text: because of being nourished and supported by those [views] as their predecessor. The mental engulfment of violence and the like is nourished by wrong view — because through habitual practice of that [wrong view], one denies the fruits of <s>karma</s>. 'Because of having a broken back' — the meaning is: because of having a broken back through the absence of its nourisher. Regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) is to be abandoned by cultivation — because it has as its object <s>dharma</s>s to be abandoned by cultivation.

body.text: iti. sarvatra gacchaṃtīti sarvatragāḥ. paṃcāpi nikāyān ālaṃbaṃta ity arthaḥ. paṃcānām api nikāyānāṃ hetubhāvenāvatiṣṭhanta ity apare. vakṣyati hi eṣāṃ prabhāvenānyanaikāyikā api kleśā upajāyaṃta iti. ekādaśānuśayā iti vistaraḥ. sapta dṛṣṭayo duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyāḥ satkāyadṛṣṭyādayaḥ paṃca. samudayadarśanaprahātavye dve dṛṣṭī mithyādṛṣṭiparāmarśadṛṣṭī iti sapta. dve vicikitse duḥkhasamudayadarśanaprahātavye. dve avidye duḥkhasamudayadarśanaprahātavye eva. ekadeśato na sākalyataḥ. ye hy avidye etatsarvatragasaṃprayukte. āveṇikyau ca. te eva sarvatrage bhavato na rāgādisaṃprayukte. ity evam ekādaśānuśayāḥ sarvatragāḥ. navānuśayāḥ sākalyataḥ. dvāv ekadeśata iti kṛtvā. dhātubhedena tu trayastriṃśat. āveṇikīti ko 'rthaḥ. evam āhuḥ. saṃparko veṇir ity ucyate na veṇir aveṇiḥ. pṛthagbhāva ity arthaḥ. evaṃ hy uktam aveṇir bhagavān aveṇir bhikṣusaṃgha [Tib. 119b] iti. pṛthag bhagavān pṛthag bhikṣusaṃgha ity abhiprāyaḥ. aveṇyā caraty āveṇikī. nānyānuśayasahacāriṇīty arthaḥ. sakalasvadhātvālaṃbanatvād iti. yasmād ete sakalaṃ svadhātum ālaṃbaṃte. tasmāt sarvatragā ity ucyaṃte. kaḥ sakaleneti vistaraḥ. kaḥ sakalena kāmadhātunā śuddhiṃ pratyeti. akāraṇaṃ vā kāraṇataḥ sakalaṃ kāmadhātuṃ pratyetīty adhikṛtaṃ. tasmāc chīlavrataparāmarśo na sarvatraga ity abhiprāyaḥ. nocyate sakalaṃ niravaśeṣam anekaṃ bhedabhinnaṃ svadhātuṃ yugapad ālaṃbaṃte. api tu paṃcaprakāram api sarvayugapad ālaṃbaṃte. duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaṃ yāvad bhāvanāprahātavyam iti. prakārasarvatāyāṃ sarvaśabdo 'yaṃ draṣṭavya ity eṣa vaibhāṣikāṇāṃ parihāraḥ. yātrātmadṛṣṭir iti. paṃcasūpādānaskandheṣu. tatrātmatṛṣṇā teṣām ātmābhiniveśavastutvāt. yatrāgraśuddhidṛṣṭī. yatra vastuni paṃcopādānaskaṃdhalakaṣaṇe 'gradṛṣṭir dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ. śuddhidṛṣṭiś ca śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ. tatra prārthanā tṛṣṇālakṣaṇā. tatra tatprārthaneti kecit paṭhaṃti. tatra vastuni tasya
body.translated_text: thus. 'Going everywhere' (<s>sarvatraga</s>) — they go everywhere, meaning: they take the five classes (<s>nikāya</s>) as their object. Others [say]: they serve as causes for all five classes. For it will be stated: through the power of these, afflictions belonging to other classes too arise. 'Eleven latent dispositions' — and so forth in detail. Seven views to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering — the five beginning with the view of the self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). To be abandoned by the seeing of origination — two views, wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) and the clinging view (<s>parāmarśadṛṣṭi</s>) — [thus] seven. Two doubts (<s>vicikitsā</s>) to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and origination. Two ignorances (<s>avidyā</s>) to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering and origination precisely. Partially, not entirely. For those two ignorances that are associated with these universal [dispositions] and are distinctive (<s>āveṇikī</s>) — those alone are universal, not those associated with desire and the rest. Thus, eleven latent dispositions are universal — nine latent dispositions entirely, and two partially. But by element-distinction, thirty-three. What is the meaning of 'distinctive' (<s>āveṇikī</s>)? They say thus: contact (<s>saṃparka</s>) is called <s>veṇi</s>; what is not <s>veṇi</s> is <s>aveṇi</s> — meaning: separateness. For thus it was said: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> is distinct (<s>aveṇi</s>), the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>saṃgha</s> is distinct.' The intent is: the <s>Bhagavān</s> is separate, the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>saṃgha</s> is separate. That which operates in a distinctive manner is <s>āveṇikī</s> — meaning: not accompanying other latent dispositions. 'Because of taking the entire own element as object' — since these take the entire own element as their object, therefore they are called 'universal.' 'Who attains purity through the entire [Desire Realm]?' — and so forth in detail. Who attains purity through the entire Desire Realm? Whether groundlessly or reasonably, [the topic] is set as apprehending the entire Desire Realm. Therefore, clinging to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>) is not universal — this is the intent. It is not said that they simultaneously take as object the entire, without remainder, manifold, differentiated own element. Rather, they take as object all five types simultaneously — what is to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, up to what is to be abandoned by cultivation. The word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) here should be seen in the sense of totality of types — this is the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s' resolution. 'Where the view of self exists' — in the five aggregates of clinging. Therein, self-craving (<s>ātmatṛṣṇā</s>) — because they are the ground for clinging to self. 'Where the foremost and purity views' — in whichever object having the character of the five aggregates of clinging, the foremost view is the clinging view (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>), and the purity view is clinging to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>). Therein the craving (<s>prārthanā</s>) having the nature of desire (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). Some read 'therein, that craving' — in that object, of that

body.text: pudgalasya prārthanā tatprārthanety arthaḥ. tena ca māna iti. tena ca vastunā mānaḥ. taddvāreṇonnatir ity arthaḥ. evaṃ satīti. evaṃ tṛṣṇāmānayoḥ sarvatragatve sati. [Tib. 120a] satkāyadṛṣṭyādivad darśanabhāvanāheyālaṃbanatvāt etad ubhayaṃ tṛṣṇāmānalakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ prahātavyaṃ kena prahātavyaṃ. kiṃ darśanaprahātavyam utāho bhāvanayeti. ye yaddarśanaheyālaṃbanāḥ. te taddarśanaheyā iti niyamaṃ manasikṛtvā pṛcchati. anyathā hi satkāyadṛṣṭyādivad evaitad ubhayaṃ darśanaprahātavyam eva syād iti kim atra praṣṭavyaṃ syāt. na hi satkāyadṛṣṭyādayo na darśanabhāvanāheyālaṃbanāḥ. na ca te na darśanaheyā bhavaṃtīti. atrācāryaḥ samādhim āha. bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ vyāmiśrālaṃbanatvād iti. yadi tṛṣṇāmānau darśanaprahātavyālaṃbanāv eva syātāṃ darśanaprahātavyau. na tu evam. ato vyāmiśrālaṃbanatvād bhāvanāprahātavyau. avaśiṣṭā bhāvanaheyā iti lakṣaṇaniyamāt. atha veti. sa evācāryaḥ parāvṛtya punar bravīti. punar astu darśanaprahātavyam iti. kim. etad ubhayam iti vartate. kasmād ity āha. dṛṣṭibalādhānavartitvād iti. dṛṣṭer balādhānam sāmarthyaṃ. dṛṣṭibalādhānena vartituṃ śīlam asyeti dṛṣṭibalādhānavarti tadubhayaṃ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. tadubhayaṃ [Tib. 120b] darśanaprahātavyam astv iti. vaibhāṣika idānīṃ svapakṣaṃ sthāpayati. svalakṣaṇakleśāv etau na sāmānyakleśau bhavataḥ. tasmān na sarvatragāv iti. yatrātmadṛṣṭiḥ. tatra tṛṣṇāmānau. na tu yugapat sarvasmin. svalakṣaṇakleśatvāt. ekadeśālaṃbanau hi tau. tasmān na sarvatragau. na cet sarvatragau. tena yau yaddarśanaheyālaṃbanau. tau taddarśanaheyau. pariśiṣṭau bhāvanāheyāv iti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: person, the craving, that craving — this is the meaning. 'And thereby, pride' (<s>māna</s>) — pride through that object; elevation through that means — this is the meaning. 'This being so' — given this universality of craving and pride, the question arises — like the view of the self-existing body and the rest, because they take as object what is to be abandoned by seeing and by cultivation — is this pair, having the character of craving and pride, to be abandoned by seeing or by cultivation? With the rule 'those that take as object what is to be abandoned by a particular seeing are to be abandoned by that seeing' in mind, he asks. For otherwise, since this pair, like the view of the self-existing body and the rest, would be to be abandoned by seeing alone, what would there be to ask? For neither is it the case that the view of the self-existing body and the rest do not take as object what is to be abandoned by seeing and cultivation, nor is it the case that they are not to be abandoned by seeing. Here the <s>Ācārya</s> gives a resolution: 'To be abandoned by cultivation, because of having a mixed object' — if craving and pride took only what is to be abandoned by seeing as their object, they would be to be abandoned by seeing. But it is not so. Therefore, because of having a mixed object, they are to be abandoned by cultivation — from the rule 'the remainder are to be abandoned by cultivation.' 'Or alternatively' — that same <s>Ācārya</s>, turning around, speaks again: 'Or let it be to be abandoned by seeing.' What? The continued sense is: this pair. Why? He says: 'Because of operating in dependence on the power of views' — the power of views is their capacity; that which has the character of operating in dependence on the power of views — the abstract noun thereof; therefore — let this pair be to be abandoned by seeing. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> now establishes his own position: 'These two are afflictions of particular characteristic, not afflictions of general characteristic. Therefore they are not universal.' Where the view of self exists, there craving and pride [exist]. But not simultaneously with all [objects] — because of being afflictions of particular characteristic. Since they take only a partial object. Therefore they are not universal. And if they are not universal, then the rule 'those that take as object what is to be abandoned by a particular seeing are to be abandoned by that seeing' does not apply; the remaining ones are to be abandoned by cultivation — this is established.

body.text: kadācit visabhāgam edaṃ dhātum ālaṃbate. kadācid dvāv iti. kadācit trīṃ dhātūn iti noktam etat. kāmadhātusthās tu kadācid visabhāgam ekarūpadhātum ārūpyadhātuṇ vālaṃbaṃte. kadācid rūpārūpyau dvāv iti.
body.translated_text: 'Sometimes it takes a dissimilar element as object — sometimes two' — it is not said 'sometimes three elements.' But those residing in the Desire Realm sometimes take one dissimilar element as object — one Form Realm element or the Formless Realm element. Sometimes both — both Form and Formless [elements].

body.text: ātmātmīyatvenāgrahaṇād iti. yasmāt taṃ brahmāṇaṃ ātmatvenātmīyatvena na gṛhṇāti. ataḥ satkāyadṛṣṭir na bhavati brahmaṇi sattvadṛṣṭiḥ. yasmāc cāntagrāhadṛṣṭiḥ satkāyadṛṣṭisamutthitā. ato nityadṛṣṭir api tasmin brahmaṇi nāṃtagrāhadṛṣṭir iti. kā tarhīyaṃ dṛṣṭir iti. yeyaṃ brahmaṇi sattvadṛṣṭiḥ. nityadṛṣṭiś ca. neyaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ mithyājñānaṃ punar etad iti. viparītālaṃbanatvān mithyājñānam etat. na hi sarvā viparītālaṃbanā prajñā dṛṣṭir iṣyate. anātmany evātmeti viparītā [Tib. 121a] prajñā satkāyadṛṣṭir iṣyate. tatsamutthāpitā
body.translated_text: 'Because of not grasping as self or belonging to self' — since one does not grasp that <s>Brahmā</s> as self or as belonging to self, therefore the view of the self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) does not exist — [rather,] the belief in <s>Brahmā</s> as a being. And since the eternalist view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>) arises from the view of the self-existing body, therefore the view of permanence regarding that <s>Brahmā</s> is also not an eternalist view. What then is this view? This belief in <s>Brahmā</s> as a being and the view of permanence — this is not a [wrong] view; rather, it is erroneous cognition (<s>mithyājñāna</s>) — because of having an inverted object, it is erroneous cognition. For not all inverted wisdom is accepted as a view. The inverted wisdom 'self' with regard to what is not self is accepted as the view of the self-existing body. And the view of permanence originated from that

body.text: ca nityadṛṣṭir aṃtagrāhadṛṣṭiḥ. nānyā. yaiva hy ahaṃkārasya saṃniśrayībhavati. saiva satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ. mahābrahmaṇi ca sattvadṛṣṭir aham ity ahaṃkārasya na saṃniśrayībhavati. tenoktam ātmātmīyatvenāgrahaṇād iti.
body.translated_text: is the eternalist view — not otherwise. For that alone which serves as the ground of the sense of 'I' is the view of the self-existing body. And the belief in a being regarding <s>Mahābrahmā</s> does not serve as the ground of the sense 'I.' Therefore it is said: 'because of not grasping as self or belonging to self.'

body.text: iti. vedanādayaḥ. prāptayas tu naivam anekaphalatvād iti. anekaphalavipākaniṣyandā hi prāptayaḥ prāptimatety uktaṃ. ato na sarvatragadharmaprāptayaḥ sarvatragā vyavasthāpyaṃte. ata eveti. yasmāt sahabhuvo 'pi sarvatragā avasthāpyaṃte. tasmāc catuṣkoṭikaṃ kriyate. prathamā koṭir anāgatāḥ sarvatragā anuśayā iti. ete sarvatragasya svābhāvyāt. na sarvatvagahetur anāgatāvasthāyāṃ sarvatragahetor anavasthāpanāt. dvitīyā atītapratyutpannās tatsahabhuvaḥ. sarvatragasahabhuvo 'tītapratyutpannatvāt sarvatragahetur bhavaṃti. na sarvatragā anuśayāḥ ananuśayasvabhāvatvāt. tṛtīyacatuṣṭhyau yojye. tṛtīyātītapratyutpannāḥ sarvatragā anuśayāḥ. caturthī tān ākārān sthāpayitvā. tadyathā anāgatās tatsahabhuvaḥ [Tib. 121b] prāptyādayaś ca.
body.translated_text: thus — feeling and the rest. But the acquisitions are not like this, because of having multiple fruits. For the acquisitions have multiple maturation and outflow results — [it is said] 'the possessor of the acquisition.' Therefore the acquisitions of universal dharmas are not classified as universal. 'For this very reason' — since even co-existent [dharmas] are classified as universal. Therefore the fourfold classification (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>) is made. The first alternative: future universal latent dispositions — these are universal by their own nature. [They are] not universal causes — because in the future state, the universal cause is not established. The second alternative: past and present co-existent [dharmas] of those [universal latent dispositions] — the co-existent dharmas of universal [latent dispositions], being past or present, are universal causes. [They are] not universal latent dispositions — because of not having the nature of latent dispositions. The third and fourth [alternatives] should be connected. The third: past and present universal latent dispositions. The fourth: setting aside those aspects — for example, future co-existent [dharmas] of those, and acquisitions and the like.

body.text: iti. ṣaḍ evety avadhāraṇaṃ. tasmān na rāgādayo 'nāsravālaṃbanā yujyante.
body.translated_text: thus. Only six — this is a restriction. Therefore it is not fitting that desire and the rest take uncontaminated [dharmas] as their object.

children.text: na rāgas tasya varjyatvān na dveṣo 'napakārata
children.translated_text: 'No desire, because of avoidance of that; no aversion, because of non-harm' —

body.text: ityādivacanāt. avidyā ca tābhyām iti. mithyādṛṣṭivicikitsābhyāṃ yā saṃprayuktā. yā cāveṇiky avidyā. sa eko 'vidyānuśaya iti. trayo nirodhadarśanapraghātavyā anāsravālaṃbanāḥ. evaṃ mārgadarśanaprahātavyā apy eta eva traya iti ṣaḍ bhūmaubhūmau bhavaṃti. tadgocarāṇāṃ viṣaya iti. tau nirodhamārgau. gocara eṣām iti tadgocarāḥ. teṣāṃ. yathākramaṃ trayāṇāṃ.
body.translated_text: and so forth from this statement. 'And the ignorance associated with those two' — the ignorance that is associated with wrong view and doubt, and the distinctive (<s>āveṇikī</s>) ignorance — that is one latent disposition of ignorance. Three are to be abandoned by the seeing of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), taking uncontaminated [dharmas] as object. Similarly, those to be abandoned by the seeing of the path — these same three — thus six [exist] on each ground. 'The object of those having that as their domain' — those two, cessation and path, are the domain of these; therefore they are 'those having that as their domain.' Of those [anuśayas], of the three respectively.

body.text: svabhūminirodhaḥ
body.translated_text: 'the cessation of the own ground' —

body.text: ālaṃbanaṃ.
body.translated_text: the object.

body.text: tu dharmajñānapakṣyaḥ ṣaḍbhūmiko 'nvayajñānapakṣyo navabhūmiko mārgagocarāṇām apareṣāṃ trayāṇām anuśayānām ālaṃbanaṃ. kathaṃ kṛtvā. nirodhālaṃbanā ete trayānuśayā navabhūmikā bhavaṃti. kāmāvacarā yāvad bhāvāgrikāḥ. teṣāṃ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ kāmāvacaradharmanirodha evālaṃbanaṃ. prathamadhyānabhūmikānāṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikadharmanirodha evālaṃbanaṃ. teṣāṃ yāvad bhavāgrabhūmikānāṃ bhavāgrabhūmikadharmanirodha
