body.translated_text: but the path belonging to the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class is of six grounds; that belonging to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class is of nine grounds — [this path is] the object of the other three latent dispositions that take the path as their domain. How? These three latent dispositions taking cessation as their object are of nine grounds — from the Desire Realm up to the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). Of those belonging to the Desire Realm, only the cessation of Desire Realm dharmas is the object. Of those belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, only the cessation of first <s>dhyāna</s> ground dharmas is the object. Up to those belonging to the peak-of-existence ground, only the cessation of peak-of-existence ground dharmas

body.text: evālaṃbanaṃ. mārgas tu dharmajñānapakṣyaḥ [Tib. 122a] ṣaḍbhūmikaḥ. anāgamyadhyānāṃtarabhūmikaś caturdhyānabhūmikaś ca. sa sarva eva kāmāvacarāṇāṃ eṣāṃ trayāṇām anuśayānām ālaṃbanaṃ. anvayajñānapakṣyaḥ punar navabhūmikaḥ. anāgamyadhyānāṃtaracaturdhyānākāśavijñānākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmikaḥ. sa sarva eva prathamadhyānabhūmikānām eṣāṃ trayāṇām anuśayānām ālaṃbanam. evaṃ yāvad bhavāgrabhūmikānām iti. kasmāt punaḥ svabhūminirodha eva tadgocarālambanaṃ. mārgas tu ṣaḍbhūmiko 'pi navabhūmiko 'pi vā teṣām ālaṃbanam ity atra hetuṃ darśayati. mārgo hy anyonyahetuka iti. katham anyonyahetukaḥ. ṣaḍbhūmiko dharmajñānapakṣyo mārgo 'dharabhūmikasyordhvabhūmikasya vā samasya viśiṣṭasya vā dharmajñānapakṣyāṃtarasyānvayajñānapakṣyasyāpi ca mārgasya hetur bhavati. so 'pi tasyānvayajñānapakṣo navabhūmiko yojyaḥ vistareṇaitad vyākhyātaṃ
body.translated_text: is the object. But the path belonging to the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class is of six grounds — the preliminary concentration (<s>anāgamya</s>), the inter-<s>dhyāna</s> ground, and the four <s>dhyāna</s> grounds. That entire [path] is the object of these three latent dispositions belonging to the Desire Realm that take the path as their domain. The path belonging to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class, moreover, is of nine grounds — <s>anāgamya</s>, inter-<s>dhyāna</s>, the four <s>dhyāna</s>s, the space-infinity base, consciousness-infinity base, and nothingness base grounds. That entire [path] is the object of these three latent dispositions belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. Similarly, up to those belonging to the peak-of-existence ground. Why then is only the cessation of the own ground the object of those having cessation as their domain, while the path of six grounds or nine grounds is the object of those? To show the reason for this, he says: 'For the path is mutually causal.' How is it mutually causal? The path belonging to the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class, of six grounds, is a cause of the path belonging to the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class of a lower, higher, equal, or superior ground, and also of the path belonging to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class. And that path belonging to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class, of nine grounds, should also be connected in detail. This has been explained in detail:

children.translated_text: 'But the nine-ground path is mutually [causal] for equal and superior [paths]' —

body.text: ity atra. tad evaṃ kāmāvacarānāṃ mārgālaṃbanānām anāgamyabhūmiko dharmajñānapakṣyo yāvac caturthadhyānabhūmika ālaṃbanaṃ. anvayajñānapakṣyo 'pi mārgo 'nāgamyabhūmiko yāvad ākikṃcanyāyatanabhūmikaḥ prathamadhyānabhūmikānām eṣāṃ mārgālaṃbanānām ālaṃbanam. evaṃ yāvad bhavāgrabhūmikānām iti. yadi [Tib. 122b] kāmāvacarā mārgālaṃbanā mithyādṛṣṭyādayo rūpārūpyapratipakṣam api nirodhamārgākhyaṃ dharmajñānam ālambaṃte. sakalo 'pi hi dharmajñānapakṣyo 'nyonyahetuka iti. kasmāt ta eva mithyādṛṣṭyādayo 'nvayajñānapakṣyam api mārgaṃ nālaṃbaṃte dharmajñānānvayajñānayor anyonyahetukatvād ity āha. yady api dharmajñānānvayajñāna iti vistaraḥ. anvayajñānaṃ na kāmadhātupratipakṣa iti. na te tad ālaṃbaṃte. dharmajñānaṃ tu kāmadhātupratipakṣa iti rūpārūpyapratipakṣam apy ālambate. dharmajñānaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: here. Thus, for those belonging to the Desire Realm that take the path as their object, the path belonging to the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class from the <s>anāgamya</s> ground up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground is the object. The path belonging to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class too — from the <s>anāgamya</s> ground up to the nothingness-base ground — is the object of these path-taking [latent dispositions] belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. Similarly, up to those belonging to the peak-of-existence ground. If the Desire Realm latent dispositions taking the path as object — wrong view and the rest — take as object even the <s>dharmajñāna</s> that is the antidote to the Form and Formless [Realms] in the form of cessation and path — for the entire <s>dharmajñāna</s> class is mutually causal — why do those same wrong view and the rest not also take the path belonging to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class as their object, since <s>dharmajñāna</s> and <s>anvayajñāna</s> are mutually causal? He says: 'Even though <s>dharmajñāna</s> and <s>anvayajñāna</s>' — and so forth in detail. <s>Anvayajñāna</s> is not the antidote to the Desire Realm — therefore they do not take it as their object. But <s>dharmajñāna</s> is the antidote to the Desire Realm — therefore, even though it is the antidote to the Form and Formless [Realms], it takes [it] as object. 'Then <s>dharmajñāna</s>' — and so forth in detail.

children.text: dharmajñānaṃ nirodhe yan mārge vā bhāvanāpathe
children.translated_text: 'That <s>dharmajñāna</s> which pertains to cessation or path on the cultivation path' —
'is the antidote to the three realms' —

body.text: iti siddhāntād dharmajñānaṃ rūpārūpyapratipakṣaḥ tadbhāvāt tadbhūmikānāṃ rūpārūpyabhūmikānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādīnām ālaṃbanaṃ bhaviṣyati. na tat sakalam iti vistaraḥ. na tad dharmajñānaṃ sakalaṃ pratipakṣo rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ. kiṃ tarhi kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. duḥkhasamudayadharmajñānayor bhāvanāmārgasaṃgṛhītayor etadapratipakṣatvāt. rūpārūpyadhātvor apratipakṣatvād ity arthaḥ. ato na rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādīnāṃ taddharmajñānam
body.translated_text: From this established doctrine, <s>dharmajñāna</s> (dharma-knowledge) is the antidote to the Form and Formless [Realms]; because of its being such, it will be the object of wrong views and the rest belonging to the Form and Formless Realm grounds. 'Not that entirely' — and so forth in detail. That <s>dharmajñāna</s> is not entirely the antidote to the Form and Formless Realms. What then, and for what reason? Because <s>dharmajñāna</s> of suffering and origination, when included in the cultivation-path (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), is not the antidote to them — meaning: not the antidote to the Form and Formless Realms. Therefore, the <s>dharmajñāna</s> belonging to the Form and Formless Realms is not the object of wrong views and the rest belonging to those [realms]

body.text: ālaṃbanaṃ. [Tib. 123a] kiṃ ca nāpi sakalayor iti vistaraḥ. nāpi sakalayo rūpārūpyadhātvos taddharmajñānaṃ pratipakṣaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. darśanaprahātavyānām apratipakṣatvāt.
body.translated_text: . Moreover, 'not even of both entirely' — and so forth in detail. Not even of both Form and Formless Realms is that <s>dharmajñāna</s> the antidote. For what reason? Because it is not the antidote to those to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>).

children.text: dharmajñānaṃ nirodhe yan mārge vā bhāvanāpatha
children.translated_text: '<s>Dharmajñāna</s> regarding cessation or the path is the cultivation-path'

body.text: iti vacanāt. atra nigamanaṃ karoti ity ādyābhāvān na bhavaty ālaṃbanam iti. duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgāṇām ādyayor duḥkhasamudayadharmajñānayor yathoktarūpārūpyapratipakṣatvaṃ praty abhāvāt. rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ darśanabhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ cādyeṣu darśanaprahātavyeṣu pratipakṣatvaṃ prati tasya dharmajñānasyābhāvāt. na tadbhūmikānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādīnāṃ mārgālaṃbanānāṃ rūpārūpyabhūmikānāṃ dharmajñānam ālaṃbanaṃ bhavati. tad eva traidhātukān aṣṭādaśānāsravālaṃbanān apāsya śeṣā aśītir anuśayāḥ sāsravālaṃbanā iti sthāpitaṃ.
body.translated_text: — because of this statement. Here he draws the conclusion: 'because of the absence of the first, it is not an object.' Because of the absence of the first two — <s>dharmajñāna</s> of suffering and origination — as antidotes to the Form and Formless Realms as stated. And because of the absence of that <s>dharmajñāna</s> as antidote to the first [category], those to be abandoned by seeing, among those belonging to the Form and Formless Realms that are to be abandoned by seeing and by cultivation. The <s>dharmajñāna</s> is not the object of wrong views and the rest belonging to the Form and Formless Realm grounds that have the path as their object. Thus, having excluded the eighteen uncontaminated-object [latent tendencies] from the triple realm, the remaining eighty latent dispositions are established as having contaminated objects.

body.text: na varjyanīyaḥ syād iti. na prāpticchedena praheyaḥ syād ity arthaḥ. yathā kuśalo dharmacchando 'bhilāṣarūpaḥ samyagdṛṣṭir iti na prāpticchedena praheyaḥ. tadvad ayaṃ syāt. ato nānāsravālaṃbanaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Would not be one to be excluded' — the meaning is: would not be one to be abandoned by the cutting of acquisition (<s>prāpticcheda</s>). Just as wholesome desire for the <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmacchanda</s>), having the form of aspiration, right view — is not to be abandoned by the cutting of acquisition — similarly, this would be so. Therefore it is not one having an uncontaminated object.

children.translated_text: 'Aversion does not [lie latent] because of the absence of harm'

body.text: iti. navāghātavastulakṣaṇavyatītatvān nirodhamārgayor nātra dveṣaḥ. bhūtārthaśuddhitvād [Tib. 123b] iti. bhūtārthena śuddhir nirodhaḥ. kleśamalaprahīṇatvāt. mārgo 'pi paramārthaśuddhiḥ paramārthena śudhyaty anayeti kṛtvā. yas tayoḥ śuddhir iti grāho na śīlavrataparāmarśa iti yujyate vyavasthāpayituṃ. agrau ca tāv iti. bhūtārthaśuddhitvāt tau nirodhamārgau agrau. api ca parāmarśau yady anāsravālaṃbanau syātāṃ samyagdṛṣṭilakṣaṇaṃ bhajetāṃ. śuddhatvād agratvāc cānāsravāṇām. ataś ca na darśanaheyau syātāṃ agrau hīne ca vastuny agra iti grāho dṛṣṭiparāmarśo yujyate. na caivaṃ nirodhamārgāv iti. na tayor agragrāho dṛṣṭiparāmarśo bhavati.
body.translated_text: — because of having transcended the nature of the nine bases of resentment (<s>āghātavastu</s>), aversion does not [lie latent] here in cessation and the path. 'Because of being purified by reality' — cessation is purification by reality, because of the abandonment of the stain of defilements. The path too is purification by the ultimate — because one is purified by the ultimate through it. The grasping that these two are pure is not fitting to be established as attachment to morality and vows (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>). 'And those two are supreme' — because of being purified by reality, those two — cessation and the path — are supreme. Moreover, if the two attachments were to have an uncontaminated object, they would partake of the nature of right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) — because of the purity and supremacy of uncontaminated [dharmas]. And in that case, they would not be to be abandoned by seeing. For the grasping of the inferior as supreme in a superior object — this is view-attachment (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>), which is fitting. But cessation and the path are not thus — the grasping of them as supreme is not view-attachment.

body.text: (V.17, 18) katy ālaṃbanato 'nuśerate. kati saṃprayogata eveti. katy ālaṃbanata eveti nāvadhāraṇena pṛcchati. yasmād ya ālaṃbanato 'nuśerate. te 'vaśyaṃ saṃprayogato 'nuśerate iti. ye tu saṃprayogata evānuśerate. te nālaṃbanato 'nāsravavisabhāgabhūmyālaṃbanā anuśayā iti.
body.translated_text: (V.17, 18) 'How many lie latent by way of object? How many by way of association alone?' — 'How many by way of object alone?' — he does not ask with a restrictive [particle]. Because those that lie latent by way of object necessarily lie latent by way of association too. But those that lie latent by way of association alone do not [lie latent] by way of object — the latent dispositions having an uncontaminated or dissimilar-ground object.

body.text: ānuguṇyartho 'trānuśayārthaḥ. na tadbhūmikāḥ pratyayās tadupapattaye ānuguṇyena vartanta iti. na ca te tadanuguṇā iti. na ca te nirodhādayaḥ teṣāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādīnāṃ anuguṇāḥ. vātikasya rūkṣānanuśayanavat. yathā vātikasya rūkṣaṃ nānuśeta ity ukte na kāyasyānuguṇyena vartata iti gamyate.
body.translated_text: The meaning of 'latent disposition' (<s>anuśaya</s>) here is in the sense of conformity (<s>ānuguṇya</s>). The conditions belonging to that ground do not operate in conformity for the arising of those [latent dispositions]. And those — cessation and the rest — are not in conformity with those wrong views and the rest. Like the non-agreement of dry [food] with one having a wind-disease (<s>vātika</s>). Just as when it is said 'dry [food] does not agree with one having a wind-disease,' it is understood that [the food] does not operate in conformity with the body.

body.text: pūrvasmiṃs tu pakṣe pratiṣṭhālābhārtho na teṣu pratiṣṭhāṃ labhata iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: But in the former position, [the meaning is] in the sense of obtaining a foundation — because of the statement: 'it does not obtain a foundation in them.'

body.text: Tib. 124a
yena dharmeṇeti. vedanādinā.
body.translated_text: 'By which <s>dharma</s>' — by feeling and the rest.

body.text: (V.19) tac ca tayor nāstīti. tac ca duḥkhaṃ tayoḥ rūpārūpyadhātvor nāsti. kasmāt. paravyābādhahetvabhāvāt. paravyābādhasya hetur vyāpādādiḥ. tasyābhāvāt. etad agraṃ dṛṣṭigatānām iti. etad viśiṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭiprakārebhyaḥ. nātisāvadyam ity arthaḥ. mokṣo mārgopaniṣat ucchedas tu nirhetuko 'bhipreta iti bhrāṃteḥ sāvadyam ucchedadarśanam iti viśeṣaḥ. svadravyasaṃmūḍhatvād iti. svasaṃtatipatitānām upādānaskaṃdhānām ātmātmīyatvena grahaṇāt svadravyasaṃmūḍhā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ. teṣām eva śāśvatocchedāntagrāhadṛṣṭir api tathaiva. yathā ca te dṛṣṭī. tathā tatsaṃprayoginy apy avidyeti. aparapīḍāpravṛttatvāc ca. kim. avyākṭe satkāyāṃtagrāhadṛṣṭī iti prakṛtaṃ. te hi na kācid api parapīḍāṃ kurutaḥ. svargatṛṣṇāsmimānayor apy eṣa prasaṃga iti. svargatṛṣṇāyā asmimānasya ca dānādibhir avirodhāt svadravyasaṃmūḍhātvād aparapīḍāpravṛttatvāc cāvyākṛtatvaprasaṃgaḥ. na ceṣyate. tasmān naibhiḥ kāraṇair anayor avyākṛtatvam ity anenābhiprāyeṇa pūrvācāryamatam [Tib. 124b] upanyasyati. sahajā satkāyadṛṣṭir ityādi. vikalpitā tv akuśaleti. yātmavādibhiḥ kapilolūkādibhir vikalpitā. sā nāvyākṛtā. kiṃ tarhi. akuśaleti. antagrāhadṛṣṭir api. yā tair vikalpitā. sāpy akuśalā. tatpūrvakatvāt tu sā tulyavārttety anuktāpi gamyata eva.
body.translated_text: (V.19) 'And that does not exist in those two' — and that suffering does not exist in those two — the Form and Formless Realms. Why? Because of the absence of the cause of harm to others. The cause of harm to others is malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>) and the like; because of its absence. 'This is the foremost of the views' (<s>dṛṣṭigata</s>) — this is distinguished from the [other] types of views. The meaning is: not very blameworthy. 'Liberation has the path as its proximate cause; but annihilation is intended as without cause' — because of error, the annihilationist view is blameworthy — this is the distinction. 'Because of being deluded about one's own substance' — because of grasping the aggregates of clinging that have fallen into one's own continuum as self and what-belongs-to-self, identity-view (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) is deluded about one's own substance. Similarly, the extreme-grasping view of those very [aggregates] as eternal or annihilated is likewise. And just as those views [are], so too is the ignorance associated with them. 'And because of not operating to harm others' — what [follows]? That identity-view and extreme-grasping view are indeterminate — this is the topic. For those two do not cause any harm to others. 'This absurd consequence applies to craving for heaven and the conceit "I am" too' — because craving for heaven and the conceit 'I am' are not opposed to giving and the rest, and because of being deluded about one's own substance, and because of not operating to harm others, there would be the absurd consequence of their being indeterminate. And this is not accepted. Therefore, identity-view and the rest are not indeterminate for these reasons — presenting the view of earlier teachers with this intent. 'Innate identity-view' and so on. 'But the conceptually constructed is unwholesome' — that which is conceptually constructed by those who hold the doctrine of self, such as <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Ulūka</s> (i.e., <s>Kaṇāda</s>), and the rest — that is not indeterminate. What then? It is unwholesome. The extreme-grasping view too — that which is conceptually constructed by them — that too is unwholesome. And because of being preceded by that [identity-view], it is of equal status — even though not stated, it is understood.

body.text: iti. iheti. kāmāvacaraśeṣābhisaṃgrahārthaṃ. kāmadhātau satkāyadṛṣṭyādiśeṣāḥ kleśā akuśalā evety avadhāryate.
body.translated_text: — 'here' is for the purpose of including the remainder belonging to the Desire Realm. It is ascertained that in the Desire Realm, the remaining defilements other than identity-view and the rest are exclusively unwholesome.

body.text: (V.20) katy akuśalamūlāni kati neti. eṣām aṣṭānavater anuśayānām ity anuvṛttatvenaivaṃ vivarjanaṃ kriyate.
body.translated_text: (V.20) 'How many are unwholesome roots and how many are not?' — of these ninety-eight latent dispositions — thus this exclusion is made by way of continuation.

children.translated_text: 'In the Desire [Realm], unwholesome roots are passion, aversion, and delusion'

body.text: iti. kāmadhātau ye rāgapratighamohāḥ. te sarva eva paṃca prakārā apy akuśalamūlāni. kuśalamūlavipakṣeṇa vyavasthānāt. nānye 'nuśayā iti. mūḍhir iti mohaparyāyaḥ. sarvo mohaḥ anyatra satkāyāṃtagrāhadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktān mohād iti. katham iha na sūtritaṃ labhyate.
body.translated_text: — in the Desire Realm, whatever passion, aversion, and delusion — all these, of all five types, are unwholesome roots, because of being established as the opposite of wholesome roots. 'Not the other latent dispositions.' '<s>Mūḍhi</s>' is a synonym for <s>moha</s> (delusion). 'All delusion except that associated with identity-view and extreme-grasping view' — how is it that this is not stated in the <s>sūtra</s>?

body.text: ity adhikārād ekadeśanirdeśāt. ata evocyate. yady akuśalaṃ cākuśalasyaiva ca mūlam iṣṭam iti. eta evety avadhāraṇāc cheṣā anuśayā mithyādṛṣṭyādayo
body.translated_text: — because of this topic, and because of the partial statement. Therefore it is said: 'If the unwholesome is intended, and if only the root of the unwholesome is intended' — because of the restriction 'these alone,' the remaining latent dispositions — wrong view and the rest

body.text: nākuśalamūlānīti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: — are not unwholesome roots. This is established.

body.text: eṣām evāṣṭānavater anuśayānāṃ.
body.translated_text: Of these very ninety-eight latent dispositions.

body.text: Tib. 125a
body.translated_text: The use of 'three' is for the purpose of distinguishing from the view of outsiders. It is shown that there are exactly three, not four. Which three? He says:

body.text: trigrahaṇaṃ bahirdeśakamatād viśeṣaṇārthaḥ. trīṇy eva na catvārīti darśitaṃ bhavati. katamāni trīṇīty āha.

seti avyākṛtatāṃ darśayatīti. avyākṛtamūlānīti. anenāvyākṛtaśabdena kevalena tṛṣṇāvidyāmatayo viśeṣitā iti darśayati. atra ca matir akleśasvabhāvāpy avyākṛtamūlam itīṣyate vaibhāṣikaiḥ. yā kācid avyākṛtā tṛṣṇeti. āsvādanāsaṃprayukteṣu dhyānārūpyeṣūpapattikāle vā vimānādiṣu saṃbhavataḥ. yā kācid avidyā rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ kāmadhātau ca satkāyāṃtagrāhadṛṣṭisaṃprayogiṇīti. evaṃ prajñā ca yā kācid avyākṛtā. aṃtato vipākajāpi. kāmadhātau vipākajairyāpathikaśailpasthānikanirmāṇacittasaṃprayuktā satkāyāṃtagrāhadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktā ca rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ sarvakleśasaṃprayuktā prajñā. vipākajādisaṃprayuktā ca yathāsaṃbhavam avyākṛtā prajñā. dvaidhavṛtter iti. dvidhābhāvo dvaidhaṃ. dvaidhe vṛttiḥ. tasyāḥ. na vicikitsā mūlaṃ bhavitum arhati. dvaidhavṛttitaś calatvāt. unnatilakṣaṇeneti [Tib. 125b]. unnater lakṣaṇaṃ. tena. ūrdhvavṛttir bhavati. tasmān na māno mūlaṃ bhavitum arhati. mūlāni sthirāṇy adhovṛttīni ceti. mūlavaidharmyān na vicikitsā mūlam asthiratvāt. na māno 'nadhovṛttitvād iti vaktavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'That' (<s>sā</s>) indicates the indeterminate [quality] — thus: indeterminate roots. By this he shows that craving, ignorance, and cognition are qualified by the single word 'indeterminate.' And here, cognition (<s>mati</s>), even though not having the intrinsic nature of a defilement, is accepted by the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s as an indeterminate root. 'Whatever indeterminate craving' — that which occurs in <s>dhyāna</s>s and formless [attainments] not associated with relishing (<s>āsvādana</s>), or at the time of rebirth in celestial palaces and the like. 'Whatever ignorance in the Form and Formless Realms, and in the Desire Realm that associated with identity-view and extreme-grasping view.' Similarly, 'whatever indeterminate cognition — even that born of maturation (<s>vipākaja</s>).' In the Desire Realm: cognition associated with maturation-born, deportment (<s>airyāpathika</s>), craft (<s>śailpasthānika</s>), and creation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) consciousness, and that associated with identity-view and extreme-grasping view; in the Form and Formless Realms: cognition associated with all defilements, and that associated with maturation-born [consciousness] and the rest as applicable — this is indeterminate cognition. 'Because of having a dual operation' — duality is the state of being twofold; operation in duality — of that [doubt]. Doubt cannot be a root — because of instability, due to its dual operation. 'Through the characteristic of elevation' — the characteristic of elevation: by that. [Pride] operates upwardly. Therefore pride cannot be a root. Roots are stable and operate downwardly. Because of dissimilarity with roots, doubt is not a root due to instability; pride is not [a root] due to not operating downwardly — this should be stated.

body.text: te ity avyākṛtāḥ. avyākṛtā tṛṣṇeti. rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ. dṛṣṭir api tayoś ca kāmadhātau ca satkāyāṃtagrāhadṛṣṭisvabhāvā. avidyāpi kāmadhātau tatsaṃprayogiṇy eva. rūpārūpyadhātvoś ca sarvā. tṛṣṇādṛṣṭimānottaradhyāyina iti. ya āsvādanāsaṃprayuktadhyānadhyāyī. sa tṛṣṇottaradhyāyī. yo dhyānaniśrayeṇa śāśvatādidṛṣṭim utpādayati. sa dṛṣṭyuttaradhyāyī. mānottaradhyāyī ca. yas tena manyate lābhy aham asya dhyānasya nānye tatheti. sa mānottaradhyāyī. tatra tṛṣṇottaraṃ tṛṣṇoparikaṃ. dhyātuṃ śīlam asyeti tṛṣṇottaradhyāyī. atha vā. tṛṣṇottaraś ca tṛṣṇādhika ity arthaḥ. dhyāyī ca tṛṣṇottaradhyāyī. evaṃ dṛṣṭyuttaradhyāyī ca. mānottaradhyāyī ca. te cāvidyāvaśād bhavaṃtīti. te ca trayo dhyāyino 'vidyāvaśād avidyāyogāt tathā bhavaṃti. ato 'vidyāpy avyākṛtamūlam [Tib. 126a] iti. samāpattisamāpannānāṃ ca etāḥ kleśasamudācārāvasthāḥ avyākṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ mūlaṃ kāraṇam iti.
body.translated_text: 'Those' — meaning: indeterminate. 'Indeterminate craving' — in the Form and Formless Realms. 'View too' — in those two [realms] and in the Desire Realm, having the intrinsic nature of identity-view and extreme-grasping view. 'Ignorance too' — in the Desire Realm, only that associated with those [views]; and in the Form and Formless Realms, all [ignorance]. '<s>Tṛṣṇā</s>-superior meditators, <s>dṛṣṭi</s>-superior meditators, and <s>māna</s>-superior meditators' — one who meditates on <s>dhyāna</s> associated with relishing (<s>āsvādana</s>) is a craving-superior meditator. One who, on the basis of <s>dhyāna</s>, produces eternalist and similar views is a view-superior meditator. And a pride-superior meditator: one who thinks with regard to that [<s>dhyāna</s>] 'I am an attainer of this <s>dhyāna</s>, others are not so.' In this context, 'craving-superior' means craving-predominant. One whose habit is to meditate [thus] is a craving-superior meditator. Or alternatively, 'craving-superior' means craving-dominated, meaning craving-excessive — and a meditator — thus a craving-superior meditator. Similarly, a view-superior meditator. And a pride-superior meditator. 'And those [meditators] exist through the power of ignorance' — and those three meditators exist through the power of ignorance, through the connection with ignorance, they become so. Therefore ignorance too is an indeterminate root. And these states of occurrence of defilements for those who have attained concentrations are the root, the cause, of indeterminate <s>dharma</s>s.

body.text: (V.22) avyākṛtasaṃbandhena paryanuyuṃkte. yāni sūtre caturdaśāvyākṛtavastūnīti vistaraḥ. śāśvato lokaḥ. aśāśvato lokaḥ. ity evamādi. kiṃ tāny avyākṛtatvād iti. kiṃ tāni naiva kuśalāni nākuśalānīty avyākṛtatvāt. nāvyākṛtavastūny apadiśyaṃte. sthāpanīyapraśno 'vyākṛta iti. yaḥ sthāpanīyatvena na vyākṛto na kathitaḥ. so 'vyākṛtaḥ praśnaḥ. tasya vastv adhiṣṭhānam ity avyākṛtavastu. tatprasaṃgenedam upanyasyate. caturvidho hi praśna iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: (V.22) He interrogates in connection with the indeterminate. 'The fourteen undeclared matters (<s>avyākṛtavastu</s>) that are in the <s>sūtra</s>' — and so forth in detail. 'The world is eternal. The world is non-eternal.' And so on. 'Are those [called undeclared] because of being indeterminate?' — are those neither wholesome nor unwholesome, [and hence called undeclared] because of being indeterminate? No — they are not designated as undeclared matters [in that sense]. 'A question to be set aside is undeclared' — a question that is undeclared, not answered, because it should be set aside — that is an undeclared question. Its subject matter (<s>vastu</s>) is the undeclared matter. In this connection, this is presented: 'For a question is fourfold' — and so forth in detail.

children.translated_text: 'Like [the question about] the otherness of self with respect to the distinctions of death and rebirth'

body.text: iti. maraṇavad utpattivad viśiṣṭavad ātmānyatādivad iti. yathāsaṃkhyam ekāṃśavyākaraṇādiṣūdāharaṇāni. mariṣyaṃtīti maraṇodāharaṇam ekāṃśavyākaraṇe. sakleśā janiṣyaṃte na niḥkleśā ity utpattyudāharaṇaṃ vibhajyavyākaraṇe. kān adhikṛtya praśnayasīti viśiṣṭatodāharaṇaṃ paripṛcchāvyākaraṇe. kim anyaḥ skandhebhyaḥ sattva iti [Tib. 126b] ātmānyatodāharaṇaṃ sthāpanīyavyākaraṇa iti. kiṃ sarvasattvā mariṣyaṃtīty ekāṃśena vyākartavyam iti. yathoktaṃ bhagavatā alpakaṃ bhikṣavo manuṣyāṇāṃ jīvitaṃ. gamanīyaḥ samparāyaḥ. caritavyaṃ kuśalaṃ. nāsti jātasyāmaraṇam iti. kim anyaḥ skandhebhyo sattvo 'nanya iti sthāpanīya iti. yathoktaṃ bhagavatā. kiṃ tu bho gautama sa karoti sa pratisaṃvedayate. avyākṛtam etat brāhmaṇa. anyaḥ karoty anyaḥ pratisaṃvedayate. avyākṛtam etad brāhmaṇa. sa karoti sa pratisaṃvedayata iti pṛṣṭo 'vyākṛtam etad iti vadasi. anyaḥ karoti anyaḥ pratisaṃvedayata iti pṛṣṭo 'vyākṛtam etad iti vadasi. tat ko 'tra khalv asya bhavato gautamasya bhāṣitasyārthaḥ. sa karoti sa pratisaṃvedayata iti brāhmaṇa śāśvatāya paraiti. anyaḥ karoti anyaḥ pratisaṃvedayata iti ucchedāya paraiti. etāvaṃtāv anugamya tathāgato madhyayā pratipadā dharmaṃ deśayatīti.
body.translated_text: thus: 'like death, like arising, like distinction, like self-and-other, and the like' — these are illustrations, in order, for the categorical declaration and the rest. 'They will die' — the illustration of death for the categorical declaration. 'Those with afflictions will be reborn, not those without afflictions' — the illustration of arising for the analytical declaration. 'With regard to whom do you ask?' — the illustration of distinction for the counter-question declaration. 'Is a being other than the aggregates?' — the illustration of self-and-other for the declaration to be set aside. 'Will all beings die?' — this should be categorically declared. As stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Short, O monks, is the life of human beings. The future world must be gone to. Wholesome [deeds] must be practiced. For one who is born, there is no non-dying.' 'Is a being other than or not other than the aggregates?' — this should be set aside. As stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'But, Master <s>Gautama</s>, does the same one who acts experience [the result]? This is undeclared, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. Does a different one act and a different one experience [the result]? This is undeclared, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. Asked whether the same one who acts experiences [the result], you say "this is undeclared." Asked whether a different one acts and a different one experiences [the result], you say "this is undeclared." What then, indeed, is the meaning of this venerable <s>Gautama</s>'s statement? O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, "the same one who acts experiences [the result]" leads to eternalism. "A different one acts and a different one experiences [the result]" leads to annihilationism. Having pursued both of these, the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> by the middle way.'

body.text: apara āheti bhadaṃtarāmaḥ. idam apy ekāṃśena vyākartavyaṃ. na sarve janiṣyaṃta iti. na kevalam idam ekāṃśena vyākartavyaṃ. sarve sattvā mariṣyaṃtīti yas tu pṛcched iti vistareṇācāryaḥ. yas tu pṛcched anena prakāreṇa ye mariṣyaṃti. kiṃ te janiṣyaṃta iti. tasya vibhajyavyākaraṇaṃ syāt. na sarva janiṣyaṃte. kiṃ tarhi. sakleśā janiṣyaṃte. na niḥkleśā [Tib. 127a] iti. tasmād yad uktam idam ekāṃśena vyākartavyaṃ na sarve janiṣyaṃta iti. tan nopapadyate. tena yujyata eva vaibhāṣikodāharaṇam ity abhiprāyaḥ. sa eva bhadantarāma āha. manuṣyeṣu cobhayam asti. hīnatvaṃ viśiṣṭatvaṃ ca. etad ubhayam āpekṣikam astīty ubhayam ekāṃśena vyākartavyaṃ tatyathā kiṃ
body.translated_text: 'Another says' — this is Venerable <s>Rāma</s>. 'This too should be categorically declared: not all will be reborn.' Not merely this should be categorically declared — 'All beings will die.' But whoever would ask — says the <s>Ācārya</s> in detail — whoever would ask in this manner: 'Will those who die be reborn?' — for that one, the analytical declaration would be [appropriate]: 'Not all will be reborn. Rather, those with afflictions will be reborn, not those without afflictions.' Therefore, what was said — 'this should be categorically declared: not all will be reborn' — that is not tenable. Hence the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> illustration is indeed fitting — this is the intent. That same Venerable <s>Rāma</s> says: 'Among humans there is both — inferiority and distinction. This twofold [quality] exists relatively. Therefore both should be categorically declared. For example:

body.text: vijñānaṃ kāryaṃ kāraṇam iti praśna ekāṃśena vyākriyate. hetuphalāpekṣayā kāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ ceti. tatra yad uktaṃ kiṃ manuṣyo hīno viśiṣṭa iti. paripṛcchya vyākartavyaṃ kān adhikṛtya praśnayasīti. tad ayuktaṃ. yasmād ayam ekāṃśena vyākaraṇīyaḥ praśna iti. ekāṃtena tu pṛcchata ity ācāryo vaibhāṣikapakṣaṃ samarthayati. ekāṃtena tu pṛcchataḥ kiṃ manuṣyo hīna eva viśiṣṭa eveti. naikāṃtavyākaraṇād dhīna iti vā viśiṣṭa iti vā. vibhajyavyākaraṇaṃ yujyate kān adhikṛtya praśnayasīti. tatra tad uktaṃ manuṣyeṣv evobhayam astīti vistareṇa. tad ayuktaṃ. sa evāha. skaṃdhebhyo 'nyaḥ sattva iti sarvaṃ. yas tu sthāpanīya ity ācāryaḥ vaibhāṣikanayenoktam [Tib. 127b] etac caturvidhasyodāharanaṃ.
body.translated_text: "Is consciousness an effect or a cause?" — this question is to be categorically declared. It is both a cause and an effect, from the perspective of cause and fruit. Therein, what was said — 'Is a human being inferior or distinguished?' — [one should respond with] the counter-question: 'With regard to whom do you ask?' — that is not fitting. Because this question should be categorically declared. 'But when asked with an absolute intent' — the <s>Ācārya</s> supports the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> position. When asked with an absolute intent: 'Is a human being exclusively inferior or exclusively distinguished?' — since neither absolute declaration — 'inferior' or 'distinguished' — [is correct], the analytical declaration is fitting: 'With regard to whom do you ask?' Therein, what was said — 'Among humans there is both' — and so forth in detail — that is not fitting. That same one [Venerable <s>Rāma</s>] says: '[The question whether] a being [is other than] the aggregates' — the whole of it. 'But it should be set aside' — says the <s>Ācārya</s>. According to the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> method, this was stated as the illustration for the fourfold [classification].

body.text:
ābhidhārmikā āhūr iti. ṣaṭpādabhidharmamātrapāṭhinaḥ. duḥkhaprajñaptir yāvan mārgaprajñaptir iti. caturṇām āryasatyānāṃ prajñaptiḥ yathāsūtraṃ. arthopasaṃhitatvād iti. arthapratisaṃyuktatvād ity arthaḥ. etad eva śaṭhasyeti. etad eva vibhajyavyākaraṇīyapraśnavacanaṃ. śaṭhasya viheṭhanābhiprāyasya praṣṭuḥ paripṛcchāvyākaraṇaṃ veditavyaṃ. bhadantarāma āha. yadā tāv iti vistaraḥ. yadā tau śaṭhāśaṭhau na kiṃcit pṛcchataḥ. kevalam adhyeṣayato dharmān vadeti. tayoś ca śaṭhāśaṭhayor na kiṃcid vyākriyate ime dharmā rūpādayaḥ savistaraprabhedā iti. kevalaṃ paripṛchyete katamān vadāmīti. tad katham anayoḥ śathāśaṭhayoḥ praśno bhavati. kathaṃ ca vyākaraṇam ābhidhārmikasya. yo hīti vistareṇācāraḥ. yo hi panthānaṃ brūhīti tadanabhijña āha. kiṃ tena paṃthā na pṛṣṭo bhavati. adhyeṣaṇamukhenaivāsya ity abhiprāyaḥ. yathā hi panthānaṃ brūhīti bruvatoktaṃ bhavati katamaḥ panthā iti. evaṃ dharmān vadeti bruvatoktaṃ bhavati katame dharmā iti. paripṛcchyaiva ca vyākaraṇāt bahavo dharmāḥ katamān vadāmīti paripṛcchyaiva tasya praśnasya teṣāṃ vā dharmāṇāṃ vyākaraṇāt. dharmabahutvaṃ vyākṛtam iti kṛtvā. kathaṃ na paripṛcchāvyākaraṇam iti. paripṛcchyavyākaraṇam [Tib 128a] ity arthaḥ. tatra yad uktaṃ tayoś ca na kiṃcit vyākriyate kevalaṃ paripṛchyete yāvat kathaṃ ca vyākaraṇam iti. tad ayuktaṃ.
ācārya āha. sūtrāntād eveti vistaraḥ. evaṃ tu sūtre vyākṛtaṃ. saṃskṛtena vyavasthāpya paṭhyate. saṃcetanīyaṃ karma kṛtvā kiṃ pratisaṃvedayate. kiṃ sukhaṃ duḥkham aduḥkhāsukham ity evaṃ pṛṣṭena vibhajyavyākaraṇīyaḥ
body.translated_text:
The <s>Ābhidhārmikas</s> say — those who recite only the six <s>Pāda-Abhidharma</s>s. The designation of suffering, up to the designation of the path — the designation of the four Noble Truths, according to the <s>sūtra</s>. 'Because of being connected with meaning' — meaning: because of being associated with meaning. 'This very [question] of the deceitful one' — this very question that calls for analytical declaration: for the deceitful one, whose intent is to harass, the questioner — the counter-question declaration should be understood. Venerable <s>Rāma</s> says: 'When those two' — and so forth in detail. When those two — the deceitful and the non-deceitful — ask nothing at all but merely request 'teach the <s>dharma</s>s' — for those two, the deceitful and non-deceitful, nothing is declared: 'these <s>dharma</s>s are form and the rest, with detailed divisions.' Rather, they are merely counter-questioned: 'Which [<s>dharma</s>s] shall I teach?' Then how is there a question for these two — the deceitful and non-deceitful? And how is there a declaration for the <s>Ābhidhārmika</s>? 'For whoever' — says the <s>Ācārya</s> in detail. For whoever says 'tell [me] the way,' being unfamiliar with it — is not the way asked about by that? Through the mode of request itself — this is the intent. Just as when one says 'tell [me] the way,' what has been said is 'which is the way?' Similarly, when one says 'teach the <s>dharma</s>s,' what has been said is 'which are the <s>dharma</s>s?' And it is through counter-questioning itself that the declaration is made — because of the multiplicity of <s>dharma</s>s, [asking] 'which shall I teach?' — through counter-questioning that very question, or those very <s>dharma</s>s, and declaring them — since the multiplicity of <s>dharma</s>s has been declared, how is it not a counter-question declaration? The meaning is: it is a declaration-through-counter-question. Therein, what was said — 'for those two nothing is declared; rather they are merely counter-questioned' and so forth up to 'how is there a declaration?' — that is not fitting.
The <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'From the <s>sūtra</s> itself' — and so forth in detail. Thus it has been declared in the <s>sūtra</s>. When put in constructed [language], it is read: 'Having performed intentional <s>karma</s>, what does one experience? Pleasure, suffering, or neither-suffering-nor-pleasure?' — when asked thus, the analytical declaration is [appropriate]

body.text: praśnaḥ. saṃcetanīyasya kuśalādibhedāt. kuśalasāsravaṃ saṃcetanīyaṃ karma kṛtvā sukham aduḥkhāsukhaṃ vā pratisaṃvedayate. akuśalasaṃcetanīyaṃ karma kṛtvā duḥkhaṃ pratisaṃvedayata iti. saced evaṃ vaded audārikam iti rūpi. vistaraḥ prabhedo na bhavati yāvad anyo jīva iti. yāvacchabdena sarvaṃ vaktavyaṃ. na bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇād. bhavati ca na bhavati ca tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāt. naiva bhavati na na bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāt. sa jīvas tac charīram. anyo jīvo 'nyac charīram iti.
body.translated_text: — because of the distinction of intentional [<s>karma</s>] as wholesome and the rest. Having performed wholesome contaminated intentional <s>karma</s>, one experiences pleasure or neither-suffering-nor-pleasure. Having performed unwholesome intentional <s>karma</s>, one experiences suffering. 'If one were to say: "Coarse" — then it is form' — and so forth in detail. There is no division, up to: '[is] a being other than [the body]?' — by the word 'up to,' everything should be stated: the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not exist after death; the <s>Tathāgata</s> both exists and does not exist after death; the <s>Tathāgata</s> neither exists nor does not exist after death; the life-principle is the same as the body; the life-principle is other than the body.

body.text: (V.23, 24) sa tena tasmiṃ saṃyukta iti. pudgalas tenānuśayena baddha iti jñāyata evety arthaḥ. svalakṣanākleśāś [Tib. 128b] ceti. svalakṣaṇaṃ sukhavedanīyādi vastu. tatra rāgaḥ sukhavedanīyam eva vastu ālaṃbyotpadyata iti. svalakṣaṇakleśa ity ucyate. tena sukhavedanīyena vastunālaṃbyamānenonnatir bhavatīti māno 'pi svalakṣaṇakleśaḥ. tathā duḥkhavedanīyaṃ vastv ālaṃbya pratigha utpadyata iti pratigho 'pi svalakṣaṇakleśa ity ucyate. sāmānyakleśāś ca. dṛṣṭivicikitsādayaḥ sāmānyāḥ sāmānyena vā kleśāḥ sāmānyakleśāḥ. ete hy aviśeṣeṇa sukhavedanīyādike vastuny utpadyaṃta iti. atas tad ālaṃbya utpannāḥ sāmānyakleśā ity ucyaṃte.
body.translated_text: (V.23, 24) 'He is bound by that in that' — the meaning is: it is known that the person is bound by that latent disposition. 'And afflictions of specific characteristics' — the specific characteristic is an object such as what is pleasant to experience. There, passion arises taking as its object only what is pleasant to experience — hence it is called an 'affliction of specific characteristic.' Through what is pleasant to experience as an object, self-exaltation occurs — hence pride too is an affliction of specific characteristic. Similarly, aversion arises taking as its object what is painful to experience — hence aversion too is called an affliction of specific characteristic. 'And afflictions of general characteristics' — views, doubt, and the rest are general, or general afflictions — afflictions of general characteristics. For these arise indiscriminately in objects that are pleasant to experience and the rest. Therefore, having arisen taking those as objects, they are called afflictions of general characteristics.

body.text: iti. atītavartamānaiḥ. rāgapratighamānā yasmiṃ vastuny utpannā iti vistaraḥ. ete rāgādayaḥ ṣaḍvijñānakāyikā apy aviśeṣābhidhyānād yathāyogaṃ yasmiṃ vastuny utpannās traiyadhvike duḥkhadarśanaprahātavye yāvad bhāvanāprahātavye. na ca prahīṇāḥ. tasmin vastuni tai rāgādibhiḥ saṃyuktaḥ. dāmneva balīvardaḥ kīlake. ete hi svalakṣaṇakleśatvān na sarvasya pudgalasyāvaśyaṃ sarvatrotpadyanta iti. kasyacit kasmiṃścid utpadyaṃta ity arthaḥ. ato
body.translated_text: meaning: through past and present [ones]. The passion, aversion, and pride that have arisen in a given object — and so forth in detail. These passion and the rest, though also belonging to the six classes of consciousness, without distinction — as applicable, in whatever object they have arisen, [whether that object belongs to] the three time-periods, to be abandoned by seeing suffering, up to to be abandoned by cultivation — if they have not been abandoned, one is bound by those passion and the rest in that object. Like an ox [bound] by a rope to a stake. For these, because of being afflictions of specific characteristics, do not necessarily arise for every person in every [object]. Rather, for some [persons] in some [objects] they arise — this is the meaning. Therefore:

children.translated_text: 'In which [objects] they have arisen and not been abandoned' —

body.text: iti tadviśeṣaṇaṃ. aprahīṇā iti viśeṣaṇaṃ. yasmād yai rāgādibhir yasmin vastuni [Tib. 129a] saṃyukta āsīt. yadi te prahīṇā bhaveyur na taiḥ sarvatra saṃyuktaḥ. prahīṇena niranuśayaviṣayatvāt.
body.translated_text: this is their qualification. 'Not been abandoned' is a qualification. Because if one had been bound by those passion and the rest in a given object, and if those were abandoned, one would not be bound by those everywhere — because what has been abandoned no longer has an object with latent [tendencies].

body.text: iti mānasagrahaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: the mention of 'mental' [is significant].

body.text: iti paṃcavijñānakāyikānām anyathā vyavasthāpyamānatvāt. rāgapratighaviśeṣaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: because those belonging to the five classes of consciousness are established differently. And this is a qualification of passion and aversion

body.text: caitat. mānasyāvaśyaṃ mānasatvāt. ebhir anāgataiḥ sarvatra traiyadhvike paṃcanaikāyike 'pi yathāsvaṃ saṃyuktaḥ. na hi tat sāsrasvaṃ vastu. yat svalakṣaṇakleśenāpi rāgeṇa na sarāgaṃ. dveṣena ca na sadveṣaṃ. mānena ca na samānaṃ. sarvasāsravavastvālaṃbanā hi yathāsvaṃ aparimitā anāgatā rāgādayo bhavaṃti. anyai rāgapratighair anāgatair anāgata eva vastuni saṃyukta iti. sarve cittacaittā ālaṃbane niyatā iti. tair utpattidharmibhir anāgata eva vastuni saṃyuktaḥ. vartamānaviṣayatvāt paṃcānāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ. rāgapratighair iti mānavacanaṃ mānānāṃ mānasatvāt.
body.translated_text: . Not of pride — because pride is necessarily mental. By these future [passion and aversion of the mental consciousness], one is bound everywhere — in [objects belonging to] the three time-periods and the five categories — each as applicable. For there is no contaminated object that is not an object of passion through the specific-characteristic affliction of passion, or not an object of aversion through aversion, or not an object of pride through pride. For all contaminated objects are, as applicable, the unlimited objects of future passion and the rest. 'By other future [afflictions] of passion and aversion, in future objects only' — all minds and mental factors are fixed in their objects. Those [five-sense-consciousness afflictions], being of the nature of those that will not arise, are bound in future objects only. Because the five classes of consciousness [operate only] with present objects. The mention of 'passion and aversion' without mention of pride [is] because pride is [always] mental.

children.translated_text: 'Equal, capable of functioning, to be abandoned by seeing — [these] belong to the ground of mental consciousness' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. paṃcavijñānakāyikair api na kevalaṃ mānasair ity apiśabdo dyotayati. tair anutpattidharmibhiḥ sarvatra vastuni traiyadhvike saṃyuktaḥ. ete hy anutpattidharmiṇo 'nāgata evādhvani vyavatiṣṭhaṃte. [Tib. 129b] eṣāṃ cālaṃbanāni saṃcaraṃti. sasaṃprayogā hi kleśāḥ suvarcalāvad anutpattidharmiṇo viṣayābhimukhā evāvatiṣṭhaṃte. tathā hy anutpattidharmiṇo naivālaṃbanam ālaṃbyotpadyaṃta iti. ataḥ keṣāṃcid ālaṃbanam atītaṃ. keṣāṃcid vartamānaṃ. keṣāṃcid anāgataṃ bhavati. na hy ālaṃbanānutpattita eva teṣām anutpattiḥ. kiṃ tari. pratyayavaikalyāt. avasthāphalaṃ hi sāmagryaṃ na dravyaphalam iti siddhāṃtaḥ.
body.translated_text: because of this statement. 'Even by those of the five classes of consciousness, not merely by mental [ones]' — the word 'even' indicates [an additional case]. By those [five-consciousness afflictions] that will not arise, one is bound in every object across the three time-periods. For these, being of the nature of those that will not arise, remain established in the future time-period alone. And their objects range [freely]. For afflictions, together with their associates, being of the nature of those that will not arise, remain facing their objects like <s>suvarcalā</s> [sunflower]. For thus, those that will not arise never arise by taking an object. Therefore, for some the object is past; for some, present; for some, future. For it is not because of the non-arising of the object that they do not arise. Rather, because of the deficiency of conditions. For the established doctrine is: the state-fruit belongs to the aggregate [of conditions], not the substance-fruit.

children.translated_text: 'By all the remaining [afflictions], one is bound everywhere' —

body.text: iti. traiyadhvikair api dṛṣṭyādibhir anekanaikāyikair api traiyadhvike paṃcaprakāre 'pi vastuni saṃyutaḥ saṃyukta ity arthaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇam ity āha. sāmānyakleśatvād iti. ete hi sarvasya sarvasmin saṃbhavaṃti. paṃcopādānaskaṃdhālaṃbanatvāt.
body.translated_text: meaning: by [afflictions] belonging to the three time-periods, such as views and the rest, even those belonging to five categories, one is bound in objects belonging to the three time-periods and the five categories. For what reason? — he says: 'Because of being afflictions of general characteristics.' For these are possible for everyone in everything — because of taking the five clinging-aggregates as their object.

body.text: (V.25) kathaṃ tatra tena ca saṃyukta iti. katham atītānāgate vastuni. tena cātītānāgatenānuśayena saṃyukta iti. visaṃyukto vā. kathaṃ vā aprahīṇaprahīṇāvasthāyāṃ vyavasthāpyaṃte. saṃskṛtalakṣaṇayogād iti. yasmāt saṃskṛtalakṣaṇāni jātyādīni saṃskārāṇām arthasaṃcārāya pravartante. atas teṣāṃ aśāśvatatvaṃ pratijñāyate. rūpaṃ ced bhikṣava ity asya sūtrasyāyam āditaḥ pāṭhaḥ. rūpam anityam atītānāgataṃ. kaḥ punar vādaḥ pratyutpannasya. evaṃdarśī śrutavān āryaśrāvakaḥ atīte rūpe 'napekṣo bhavati. anāgataṃ rūpaṃ nābhinandati. pratyutpannasya rūpasya nirvide [Tib. 130a] virāgāya nirodhāya pratipanno bhavati. atītaṃ ced bhikṣavo rūpaṃ nābhaviṣyan na śrutavān āryaśrāvako atīte rūpe 'napekṣo 'bhaviṣyat. yasmāt tarhy asty atītaṃ rūpaṃ. tasmāc
body.translated_text: (V.25) 'How is it connected with that therein?' — how is a past or future thing connected with, or disconnected from, that past or future latent disposition? Or how are [things] established in the states of being abandoned and not-abandoned? 'Because of the applicability of conditioned characteristics' — because the conditioned characteristics — birth (<s>jāti</s>) and the rest — operate for the purpose of transitioning the conditioned things through their functions. Therefore, their impermanence is affirmed. 'O monks, if form' — this is the reading from the beginning of this <s>sūtra</s>: 'Form is impermanent, both past and future. What need be said of the present? Seeing thus, the learned Noble disciple is without concern for past form, does not delight in future form, and is on the path toward revulsion, dispassion, and cessation with regard to present form. O monks, if past form did not exist, the learned Noble disciple would not be without concern for past form. But since past form does exist, therefore

body.text: chrutavān āryaśrāvako atītarūpe 'napekṣo bhavati. anāgataṃ ced rūpaṃ nābhaviṣyan na śrutavān āryaśrāvako 'nāgataṃ rūpaṃ nābhyanandiṣyat. yasmāt tarhy asty anāgataṃ rūpaṃ. tasmāc chrutavān āryaśrāvako 'nāgataṃ rūpaṃ nābhinandati. pratyutpannaṃ ced bhikṣavo rūpaṃ nābhaviṣyad iti vistaraḥ. na śrutavān āryaśrāvako 'tīte rūpe 'napekṣo 'bhaviṣyad iti. nirviṣayatvād vairāgyakāle 'tītaviṣayāpekṣāryaśrāvakasyānapekṣā matir na syād ity arthaḥ. yadātītaṃ rūpam apekṣyate. tadā tatrāsaktir iti. abhyanandiṣyad ity abhyalaṣiṣyat. pratyutpannaṃ ced bhikṣavo rūpaṃ nābhaviṣyan na śrutavān āryaśrāvakaḥ pratyutpannasya rūpasya nirvide virāgāya nirodhāya pratipanno 'bhaviṣyad ity etan noktam ubhayapakṣaprasiddhatvāt.
body.translated_text: the learned Noble disciple is without concern for past form. If future form did not exist, the learned Noble disciple would not not-delight in future form. But since future form does exist, therefore the learned Noble disciple does not delight in future form. If present form did not exist' — and so forth in detail. 'The learned Noble disciple would not be without concern for past form' — the meaning is: because of the absence of an object, at the time of dispassion, the non-concern of the Noble disciple who has regard for the past object would not be possible as a cognition. When past form is regarded, there is at that time non-attachment to it. 'Would have delighted' means 'would have desired.' 'If present form did not exist, the learned Noble disciple would not be on the path toward revulsion, dispassion, and cessation with regard to present form' — this was not stated because it is well-known to both sides.

body.text: iti pūrvaṃ kaṇṭhata uktam iti pradarśitam. idānīm arthato na kaṇṭhata iti viśeṣaḥ. [Tib. 130b] na dvayaṃ pratītya manovijñānaṃ syāt. yad atītānāgatālaṃbanam iti viśeṣaḥ. tato vijñānam eva na syāt ālaṃbanābhāvād iti. vijñeye sati vijñānam iti kṛtvā. sādhanaṃ cātra. sadālaṃbanam eva manovijñānam. upalabdhisvabhāvatvāt. cakṣurvijñānavad iti.
body.translated_text: what was stated before was shown explicitly. Now [it is shown] from the meaning, not explicitly — this is the distinction. 'Mental consciousness, which has past and future [objects], would not exist from the dyad' — this is the distinction. 'Then consciousness itself would not exist, because of the absence of an object.' Because where there is something to be cognized, there is consciousness. And the proof here is: mental consciousness always has an object — because of having the nature of apprehension — like visual consciousness.

body.text: iti. vidyamānasvalakṣaṇaṃ śubhāśubham atītaṃ karma. vipaktikāla utpadyamānaphalatvāt. vartamānadharmavad iti.
body.translated_text: thus. Past wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>, having existing specific characteristics, [continues to produce its fruit] — because at the time of maturation, its fruit arises. Like a present <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: (V.26) bhāvānyathātvaṃ bhavatīti. atītānāgatapratyutpannasya bhāvasyānyathātvaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ. na dravyānyathātvaṃ. na rūpādisvalakṣaṇasyānyathātvam ity arthaḥ. anāgato hi vartamānam adhvānaṃ pratipadyamāno 'nāgatabhāvaṃ jahāti. vartamānabhāvaṃ pratilabhate. vartamāno 'py atītaṃ. suvarṇaṃ kṣīraṃ ceti dṛṣṭāṃtadvayaṃ yathākramaṃ ākṛtiguṇānyathātvajñāpanārthaṃ. lakṣaṇānyathikasya lakṣaṇavṛttilābhāpekṣo vyavahāraḥ. ata evāha. dharmo 'dhvasu pravartamāno 'tīto 'tītalakṣaṇayuktaḥ. anāgatapratyutpannābhyāṃ lakṣaṇābhyām aviyukta iti vistaraḥ. yady anāgatam atītapratyutpannābhyāṃ viyuktaṃ syāt. evaṃ sati nānāgatam evotpannam atītam veti syāt. athātītam anāgatapratyutpannābhyāṃ viyuktaṃ syāt. nānāgataṃ vartamānaṃ cātītaṃ syāt. vartamānam atītānāgatābhyāṃ viyuktaṃ syāt. anāgatam eva vartamānaṃ vartamānam evātītaṃ syāt labdhavṛttinā hi lakṣaṇena yukto vyavasthāpyate. tadanyenāviyukto na virahita ity arthaḥ. ata evodāharati.
body.translated_text: (V.26) 'There is change of state (<s>bhāva</s>), not [change] of substance' — the meaning is: there is change of state of the past, future, and present entity — not change of substance, not change of the specific characteristics of form and the rest. For what is future, upon entering the present time-period, abandons the state of being future and obtains the state of being present. The present [entering] the past [is] also [so]. The two examples of gold and milk are, respectively, for the purpose of showing change of shape and change of quality. 'For the one [who holds] change of characteristics, the usage depends on the obtaining of the function of the characteristic.' For this very reason he says: 'A <s>dharma</s> occurring in the time-periods, when past, is conjoined with the past characteristic and not disconnected from the future and present characteristics' — and so forth in detail. If the future were disconnected from the past and present [characteristics], then it would not be the case that the unarisen would be what has become past or arisen. And if the past were disconnected from the future and present [characteristics], what is future and present could not be past. If the present were disconnected from the past and future, the future alone would be what is present, and what is present alone would be past. For that which is established by the characteristic whose function has been obtained — that which is not disconnected from the others means not separated — this is the meaning. For this very reason he gives the illustration

body.text: tadyathā. puruṣa ekasyāṃ striyāṃ raktaḥ [Tib. 131a] śeṣāsv avirakta iti. ekasyāṃ striyām asya rāgādhyavasānaṃ vartate. śeṣāsu strīṣu rāgaprāptir evāsti. na samudācāra iti. avasthānyathikasyāvasthāpekṣo vyavahāraḥ. yasyām avasthāyāṃ so dharmaḥ kāritraṃ na karoti. tasyām anāgata ucyate. yasyāṃ karoti. tasyāṃ vartamānaḥ. yasyāṃ kṛtvā niruddhaḥ. tasyām atīta ity avasthāṃ avasthāṃ prāpya anyo 'nyo nirdiśyate. anāgatāvasthāṃ prāpyānāgato yāvad atītāvasthāṃ prāpyātīta iti. avasthāntarataḥ. na dravyāṃtarata iti abhinnalakṣaṇo 'nāgatādyavasthāprāpto 'nāgatādiśabdanirdeśaḥ kevalaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ. ata evodāharati. yathaikā vartiketi vistaraḥ. yathaikā gulikā ekāṃke nikṣiptā ekasthāne sthāpitā ekam ity ucyate. evaṃ śatāṃke śataṃ. sahasrāṃke sahasram ity ucyate. avasthāṃtarāpekṣayā. na punas tasyāḥ svabhāvānyathātvaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. sthānāṃtaraviśeṣāt saṃkhyābhidyotakaṃ saṃjñāṃtaram utpadyata iti. pūrvāparam apekṣyānyonya ucyata iti. pūrvam aparaṃ cāpekṣyatītānāgatavartamānā ucyaṃta ity arthaḥ. pūrvam evātītaṃ vartamānaṃ vāpekṣyānāgata [Tib. 131b] iti. pūrvaṃ vātītaṃ aparaṃ vānāgatam apekṣya vartamāna iti. aparam eva vartamānam anāgataṃ vāpekṣyātīta iti. pūrvāparāpekṣo 'nyathānyathikasya vyavahāraḥ. ata evodāharati. yathaikā strī mātā vocyate duhitā ceti. yathaikā strī duhitaram apekṣa mātety ucyate. mātaram apekṣya duhitā ceti. pūrvāparāpekṣayā na dravyāṃtarataḥ. sāṃkhyapakṣe nikṣeptavya iti. yaḥ sāṃkhyapakṣe pratiṣedhaḥ. sa eva tatpakṣasya pratiṣedhaḥ. sāṃkhyapakṣaḥ pratiṣiddha ity abhiprāyaḥ. dvitīyasyāpi bhadantaghoṣakasyāpi adhvasaṃkaraḥ prāpnoti. yo 'tītādhvābhipretaḥ. sa vartamānaḥ anāgato 'pi prāpnoti. kathaṃ kṛtvā. 'tīte atītalakṣaṇayukto bhavann anāgatavartamānalakṣaṇābhyām aviyuktaḥ. yukta evety arthaḥ. anāgato 'py anāgatalakṣaṇayuktaḥ atītavartamānalakṣaṇābhyām aviyuktaḥ. vartamāno 'pi vartamānalakṣaṇayukto 'tītānāgatalakṣaṇābhyām aviyukta iti kṛtvā. ekaikasya trilakṣaṇayogāt atīto 'nāgato vartamānaś ca prāpnoti. ity evam anāgatavartamānāv api yojyau. kim atra sāmyam iti. puruṣasya kasyāṃcit kevalaṃ samanvāgamaḥ. kim evaṃ dharmasyaikaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vidyate. ita eva lakṣaṇe [Tib. 132a] na vidyete. yata evam udāhriyata iti asāmyaṃ. caturthasyāpi bhadaṃtabuddhadevasyāpi ekasminn evādhvani trayo 'dhvānaḥ prāpnuvantīti. ekasminn evatīte
body.translated_text: 'just as a man, passionate toward one woman, is not dispassionate toward the rest.' His passionate fixation operates toward one woman; toward the rest of the women, there is only the acquisition of passion, not its manifest operation. 'For the one [who holds] change of state, the usage depends on the state.' In whichever state that <s>dharma</s> does not perform its function, in that it is called future. In whichever it performs it, in that it is present. In whichever, having performed it, it has ceased — in that it is past. Thus, upon reaching state after state, it is designated differently — upon reaching the future state, it is [called] future, up to: upon reaching the past state, it is [called] past. Through change of state, not through change of substance — the meaning is: it is only upon reaching the states of future and the rest that there is the designation by the words 'future' and the rest, with undifferentiated characteristics. For this very reason he gives the illustration: 'just as a single counter' — and so forth in detail. Just as a single counter, placed on the one-position, established on one place, is called 'one'; similarly, on the hundred-position, 'hundred'; on the thousand-position, 'thousand' — with reference to the change of position. But there is no change of its own-nature. Rather, from the distinction of a different position, a different designation that illuminates the number arises. 'With reference to prior and posterior, they are called mutually [other]' — with reference to what is prior and posterior, they are called past, future, and present — this is the meaning. With reference to what is prior alone — the past or the present — it is called future. With reference to what is prior — the past — and what is posterior — the future — it is called present. With reference to what is posterior alone — the present or the future — it is called past. 'For the one [who holds] change of relativity, the usage depends on prior and posterior.' For this very reason he gives the illustration: 'just as one woman is called both mother and daughter.' Just as one woman, with reference to her daughter, is called 'mother,' and with reference to her mother, 'daughter' — with reference to prior and posterior, not through change of substance. 'It should be placed in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position' — the refutation that is [applied] to the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position is the very refutation of that position too — the intent is: the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> position is refuted. Even for the second [theorist], the venerable <s>Ghoṣaka</s>, confusion of the time-periods (<s>adhvasaṃkara</s>) follows. What is intended as the past time-period — that comes to be present and future too. How so? Being past, while conjoined with the past characteristic, being not disconnected from the future and present characteristics — meaning: being conjoined. The future too, while conjoined with the future characteristic, being not disconnected from the past and present characteristics. And the present, while conjoined with the present characteristic, being not disconnected from the past and future characteristics. Since each one has the conjunction of three characteristics, the past comes to be future and present too — similarly the future and present should be connected. 'What similarity is there here?' — the man has mere possession with respect to some [women]. Is it the case that the <s>dharma</s> similarly has one characteristic [active] and others [inactive]? From this very [consideration] — 'this characteristic does not exist here' — therefore the illustration is given — showing the dissimilarity. Even for the fourth [theorist], the venerable <s>Buddhadeva</s>, three time-periods come to be present in a single time-period — in a single past

body.text: 'dhvani pūrvāparakṣaṇavyavasthāsti. tatra pūrvapaścimau kṣaṇāv atītānāgatau. pūrvaḥ kṣaṇo 'tītaḥ paścimo 'nāgataḥ. madhyamaḥ pratyutpannaḥ. ity atīte 'dhvani trayo 'dhvānaḥ prāpnuvaṃti. ata eṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ
body.translated_text: time-period, there is the distinction of prior and posterior moments. Therein, the prior and posterior moments are past and future — the prior moment is past, the posterior is future, and the middle is present. Thus, in the past time-period, three time-periods come about. For this very reason, for all of these,

body.text: iti vaibhāṣikaḥ. kathaṃ kṛtvā śobhana ity āha. yasmāt tasya
body.translated_text: says the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>. How is it excellent? He says: because for that one —

body.text: kāritraṃ punaḥ cakṣurādīnāṃ darśanādīnīti. rūpādīnām api svendriyagocaratvaṃ kāritraṃ. gady evam iti vistaaraḥ. yadi kāritreṇa vyavasthāpitāḥ. tatsabhāgasya cakṣuṣaḥ kiṃ kāritraṃ. yad dhi kāritralakṣaṇaṃ svakarma na karoti tat tatsabhāgaḥ. tasya ca nāsti kāritraṃ darśanalakṣaṇaṃ. kathaṃ tat pratyutpannam ity abhiprāyaḥ. phaladānapratigraha iti. tac cakṣuḥ svaniṣyandaphalaṃ parigṛhṇāti ākṣipati. phalaṃ ca dadāti niṣyandaphalam anaṃtaraṃ dadāti. puruṣakāraphalaṃ ca. yady api darśanakāritraṃ na karoti. anyat tu phalaṃ karotīti. tasya phaladānaparigrahasadbhāvāt tat pratyutpannam iti vyavasthāpyate. [Tib. 132b] atītānām api tarhi sabhāgahetvādīnām iti. ādiśabdena vipākahetvādīnāṃ parigrahaṇaṃ. teṣāṃ phaladānāt.
body.translated_text: 'Function' is seeing and the like for the eye and the rest. For form and the rest too, being within the range of their respective sense-faculties is their function. 'If [established] by function' — and so forth in detail. If [the time-periods] are established by function, what is the function of a homologous eye (<s>tatsabhāga cakṣus</s>)? For the characteristic of function — its own operation — it does not perform; that is what is homologous. And it has no function of seeing. The intent is: how then is it present? 'Giving and receiving of fruit' — that eye receives, draws forth, its outflow-fruit. And it gives fruit — it gives an outflow-fruit immediately following, and also a human-effort result. Even though it does not perform the function of seeing, it performs another fruit [function]. Because the giving and receiving of fruit exists for it, it is established as present. 'But then even for past [<s>dharma</s>s], such as homologous causes and the like' — by the word 'and the like,' maturation causes and the rest are included. Because of their giving of fruit —

children.translated_text: 'Two present and past [causes] give [fruit]; one past [cause] gives' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. kāritraprasaṃgaḥ. kāritram astīti. tataś caiṣāṃ sabhāgahetvādīnāṃ atītānāṃ vartamānatvaprasaṃgaḥ. vartamānavat kāritrasadbhāvād iti lakṣaṇasaṃkaraḥ. brūyās tvaṃ yeṣāṃ phalaparigrahaḥ phaladānaṃ cobhayam asti. te vartamānāḥ. yeṣāṃ tv ekataraṃ. na te vartamānā iti. tata idam ucyate. ardhakāritrasya veti. prasaṃga ity adhikṛtaṃ. ardhakāritrasya vā prasaṃgaḥ. ardhavartamānā iti vā te 'tītāḥ prasajyaṃte. uparataphalaparigrahakāritratvād dhi te 'tītalakṣaṇayuktāḥ. vartamānaphaladānakāritratvāc ca vartamānalakṣaṇayuktā iti. sa eva lakṣaṇasaṃkaradoṣaḥ. etad dhy atītādīnām adhvanāṃ lakṣaṇam iṣṭaṃ. uparatakāritram atītam aprāptakāritram anāgataṃ prāptānuparatakāritraṃ vartamānam iti.
body.translated_text: from this statement, there would be the consequence of [their having] function. That they have function [implies] the consequence that these past homologous causes and the like would be present — like present [<s>dharma</s>s], because of the existence of function. This is confusion of characteristics. You might say: those for which both receiving and giving of fruit exist — those are present; but those for which only one [exists] — they are not present. To this it is said: 'Or the consequence of half-function' — 'consequence' is the topic. There is the consequence of half-function, or they follow as being half-present. Because of having ceased the function of receiving fruit, they are conjoined with the past characteristic. But because of having the function of giving present fruit, they are also conjoined with the present characteristic. This is the very defect of confusion of characteristics. For this is the accepted characteristic of the past and the rest of the time-periods: what has ceased functioning is past; what has not yet attained function is future; what has attained but not ceased functioning is present.

body.text: iti. napuṃsakaliṃgam etacchabdarūpaṃ. ko vibandha ity arthaḥ. ko vighno 'syeti kiṃ vighnaṃ kāritram ity apare. pratyayānām asāmagryam iti cet. tatraitat syāt. pratyayānāṃ hetusamanaṃtarādīnām asāmagryam. ato na sarvadā kāritraṃ karotīti. na. nityam astitvābhyupagamāt. [Tib. 133a] na pratyayānām asāmagryaṃ kalpayituṃ yujyate. yasmād iha bhavadbhir nityaṃ pratyayānām
body.translated_text: this word-form is neuter gender. The meaning is: what is the impediment? 'What is the obstacle to function?' — according to others. 'If [the answer is] the non-aggregation of conditions' — here this could be [the response]: the non-aggregation of conditions — causes, immediately-preceding [conditions], and the rest — therefore it does not always perform its function. No — because of the acceptance that [<s>dharma</s>s] always exist. It is not fitting to imagine a non-aggregation of conditions — because according to you, conditions always exist

body.text: astitvam abhyupagamyate. satām avināśāt. yac ca tat kāritram atītam iti vistaraḥ. yac ca kāritram atītam ucyate anāgataṃ pratyutpannam iti cocyate siddhāṃte uparatakāritram atītam ity evamādivacanāt. kiṃ kāritrasyāpy anyat kāritram asti. yatas tasyātītāditvaṃ kathyate. yady asty anavasthāprasaṃgaḥ. na ced asti athānāgatāditvaṃ kāritrasya svarūpasattāpekṣayā evaṃ bhāvānām apy anāgatāditvaṃ bhaviṣyati. kiṃ kāritrakalpanayā. kathaṃ tad atītam ityādi. atha tan naivātītam iti vistaraḥ. yan naivātītaṃ nāpy anāgataṃ na pratyutpannaṃ tad asaṃskṛtam ity asaṃskṛtatvān nityam astīti prāptaṃ. kāritram ity adhikṛtaṃ. tataḥ kim ity āha. ato na vaktavyaṃ. yadā kāritraṃ na karoti dharmas tadānāgata iti. kāritrasya kartum aśakyatvaprāpteḥ. syād eṣa doṣa iti vistaraḥ. syād eṣa doṣaḥ kāritrasyānyat kāritram ity atiprasaṃgo 'saṃskṛtatvaprasaṃgo vā yadi dharmāt kāritram anyat syāt. tat tu khalu nānyad iti. naiṣa doṣaḥ. tenaivātmaneti. yaḥ pratyutpannasya svabhāvaḥ. tenety arthaḥ. kim asya pūrvaṃ nāsīd ity anāgatāvasthāyāṃ. yadi kāritram ananyatvād dharma eva nāsīd ity uktaṃ bhavat. kiṃ ca paścān nāstīty atītāvasthāyāṃ. yadi kāritraṃ [Tib. 133b] dharma eva nāstīty uktaṃ bhavet. dharmakāritrayor ananyatvāt. yady abhūtvā bhavatīti neṣyate pratyutpanno na sidhyati. bhūtvā ca punar na bhavatīti yadi neṣyate atīto 'dhvā na sidhyati. anāgatas tu yo na tāvad abhūtvā bhavatīty arthād gamyate evam adhvatrayaṃ sidhyaty ato 'nyathā na sidhyatīty vākyārthaḥ. utpādavināśayor ayogād iti. sarvakālāstitvād utpādavināśayor ayogaḥ. tasmād vāṅmātram etat saṃskṛtalakṣaṇayogān na śāśvatatvaprasaṃga iti. apūrvaiṣā vāco yuktir iti. pūrvāparaviruddhaiṣā vāco yuktir ity arthaḥ. sarvadā cāsty utpādavināśābhyāṃ ca yujyata iti.
body.translated_text: existence is accepted — because of the non-destruction of existing things. And that activity (<s>kāritra</s>) [being] past — and so forth in detail. And that which is called 'past activity,' and that which is called 'future' or 'present' — in the [Sarvāstivāda] system, because of statements such as 'the past is that whose activity has ceased.' Does activity itself also have another activity? — for which its pastness and so forth would be spoken of. If so, there is the consequence of infinite regress. If not, then the pastness and so forth of activity would be through the existence of its own-nature — and [accordingly] the pastness and so forth of entities too would be the same. What is the need for postulating activity? How then is that past? — and so forth. But if that is neither past — and so forth in detail. That which is neither past, nor future, nor present — that is unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) — and being unconditioned, it follows that it is permanent and existent. 'Activity' is the topic. What follows from that? He says: therefore it should not be said — 'When a <s>dharma</s> does not perform its activity, then it is future.' Because it follows that activity is incapable of being performed. 'This fault would arise' — and so forth in detail. This fault would arise — over-extension [i.e., that activity requires another activity], or the consequence of being unconditioned — if activity were something different from the <s>dharma</s>. But that is indeed not different. Therefore there is no fault. 'By that very self' — by whatever is the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of the present. By that — this is the meaning. Did this not exist previously? — in the future state. If activity, being non-different [from the <s>dharma</s>], is the <s>dharma</s> itself that did not exist — this is what would be said. Furthermore, does it not exist afterwards? — in the past state. If activity, [Tib. 133b] being the <s>dharma</s> itself, does not exist — this would be said. Because activity and <s>dharma</s> are non-different. If it is not accepted that [a <s>dharma</s>] comes into being after not having been — the present is not established. And if it is not accepted that after having been, it again ceases to be — the past time-period is not established. But the future is that which has not yet come into being — this is understood from the meaning. Thus the three time-periods are established, and otherwise they are not established — this is the sentence-meaning. 'Because of the impossibility of arising and destruction' — because of existing at all times, arising and destruction are impossible. Therefore this is mere speech — 'because of being endowed with conditioned characteristics, the consequence of eternalism does not arise.' 'This is an unprecedented verbal trick' — the meaning is: this is a verbal trick contradicting what precedes and what follows — 'it always exists, and yet it is endowed with arising and destruction.'

body.text: yad rūpādeḥ svalakṣaṇaṃ. tat sarvasmin kāle vidyata itīṣyate. yadi rūpādeḥ svabhāvaḥ sarvadāsti tena rūpādibhāvo nityaḥ prāpnoti. ata āha.
body.translated_text: that which is the specific characteristic of form and the rest — that is accepted as existing at all times. If the intrinsic nature of form and the rest always exists, then that entity (<s>bhāva</s>) of form and the rest follows as being permanent. Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'And the entity is not accepted as permanent' —

body.text: evaṃ sati tasmāt svabhāvād bhāvo nūnam anya iti. ata āha.
body.translated_text: this being the case, therefore the entity must be something other than the intrinsic nature. Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'And the entity is not other than the intrinsic nature' —

body.text: iti. tad idamicchāmātratvāt
body.translated_text: thus. 'This, being merely a matter of wish,

children.translated_text: is clearly the play of [a capricious] Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>).'

body.text: nātra yuktir asti. atītaṃ tu yad bhūtapūrvam iti. na svalakṣaṇenāstīti darśayati.
body.translated_text: There is no reasoning here. 'But the past is that which previously existed' — he shows that [the past] does not exist by its specific characteristic.

body.text: anāgataṃ yat sati hetau bhaviṣyatīti. avidyamānam [Tib. 134a] api hetusadbhāvād vyavasthāpyata iti darśayati. evaṃ hi kṛtvāstīty ucyata iti. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhaviṣyati ceti kṛtvā. na tu punar dravyata evaṃ bhavati. hetuphalāpavādadṛṣṭipratiṣedhārtham iti. hetvapavādadṛṣṭipratiṣedhārtham asty atītam ity uktaṃ. phalāpavādadṛṣṭipratiṣedhārtham asty anāgatam iti. āsīd atītaṃ bhaviṣyaty anāgatam iti vaktavye 'stīti vacanam astiśabdasya nipātatvāt. trikālaviṣayo hi nipātaḥ. āsīdarthe bhaviṣyadarthe 'pi vartate. yathāsti dīpasyeti vistaraḥ. yathāsti dīpasya prāg abhāvo 'sti paścād abhāva iti vaktāro bhavaṃti. na ca dravyato 'sti. yathā cāsti niruddhaḥ. sa pradīpo na tu mayā nirodhita iti vaktāro bhavaṃti. na cāstiprayogān niruddho 'py asāv astīti. nanu ca vaidhāṣikasya niruddho 'py asāv astīti. satyam asti. na tu pradīparūpatām eva bhibhrāṇaḥ so 'sti. evam atītānāgatam astīty uktaṃ asaty api dravyasattve. anyathā hy atītānāgata eva na sidhyet. yadi tenaiva lakṣaṇena vidyetātītānāgata eva na sidhyed ity arthaḥ. yady atītaṃ bhūtapūrvaṃ yat tarhi laguḍaśikhīyakān iti vistaraḥ. laguḍaśikhīyakaiḥ parivrājakair nāryo nidānaṃ. nālaṃdāyā [Tib. 134b] buddhabhāṣitaṃ ca sūtraṃ. saṃyuktakāgame ca. āryamahāmaudgalyāyanaś ca mārita ity āhur abhiyuktāḥ. yato no mārita ity atra sūtra evaṃ paṭhyate. laguḍaśikhīyakāḥ parivrājakā ānaṃtaryakāriṇo yat karmābhyatītaṃ. tan nāstīty evaṃvādina iti vistavaḥ. kiṃ te laguḍaśikhīyakāḥ parivrājakās tasya karmaṇa ānaṃtaryasya bhūtapūrvatvaṃ necchaṃti. etad uktaṃ bhavati. icchaṃti sma te tasya karmaṇo bhūtapūrvatvaṃ. kiṃ tu na dravyam iti tasmiṃ karmaṇi te vipratipannāḥ. nāsti tat karmābhyatītam iti. yato bhagavatā yatra te vipratipannāḥ svabhāve. tat karmābhyatītam astīti vistareṇa. tasmād asti svabhāvenātītam iti vistaraḥ. tatra punaḥ sūtre yad bhūtapurvaṃ karma. na tad evātītam ity abhisaṃdhāyoktaṃ tat karmāstīti. kiṃ tarhi. tadāhitaṃ tena bhūtapūrveṇa karmaṇā āhitam arpitaṃ. tasyāṃ saṃtatau phaladānasāmarthyaṃ saṃdhāyoktam ity anenābhiprāyeṇoktam iti. kathaṃ gamyata ity āha. anyathā hi svena bhāvena vidyamānam atītaṃ na sidhyed iti. svalakṣaṇena vidyamānaṃ tat karma pratyutpannalakṣaṇena vidyamānam atītam iti na sidhyet. pratyutpannam eva sidhyed ity abhiprāyaḥ. tadāhitam iti vistareṇaivam
body.translated_text: 'The future is that which will exist when the cause is present' — [Tib. 134a] he shows that even though not existing [presently], it is established because of the existence of its cause. 'For having done thus, it is said to exist' — having done thus — i.e., having previously existed and being about to exist. But it does not exist as a substance (<s>dravya</s>) in this way. 'For the purpose of refuting the view that denies cause and effect' — for the purpose of refuting the view that denies cause, it is said 'the past exists.' For the purpose of refuting the view that denies effect, it is said 'the future exists.' Where one should say 'it was' for the past and 'it will be' for the future, [instead] the word 'exists' (<s>asti</s>) is used because the word <s>asti</s> is an indeclinable particle (<s>nipāta</s>). For an indeclinable particle ranges over the three times — it functions in the sense of 'was' and in the sense of 'will be.' 'Just as there exists the prior non-existence of a lamp' — and so forth in detail. Just as people say 'there exists the prior non-existence of a lamp' and 'there exists the subsequent non-existence [of a lamp]' — but [the non-existence] does not exist as a substance. And just as people say 'the extinguished [lamp] exists — that lamp was not extinguished by me' — but it is not the case that because of the use of 'exists,' the extinguished [lamp] actually exists. But does the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> not [hold that] even the extinguished exists? True, it exists — but that lamp does not exist while maintaining the very form of a lamp. Thus, the past and future are said to 'exist' even though they do not exist as substances. For otherwise, the past and future would simply not be established. If it were cognized by that very characteristic — by the present characteristic — the past and future would not be established — the meaning is: it would be established as present alone. 'That which was deposited by it' — and so forth in detail, when stated thus

body.text: ucyamāne 'bhyatītaṃ tat karmāstīti sidhyati. itthaṃ caitad evam iti. yathānāgataṃ [Tib. 135a] dravyato nāsty atītaṃ ceti. vartamāne 'dhvanīti vistaraḥ. vartamānabhāvenābhūtvā bhavatīty arthaḥ. na. adhvano bhāvād anarthāṃtaratvāt. naiva tad evam. adhvanaḥ pratyutpannasya bhāvāc cakṣuḥsaṃjñakād anarthāṃtaratvāt. adravyāṃtaratvād ity arthaḥ. ya eva vartamāno 'dhvā. sa eva bhāvaḥ. tat kathaṃ sa eva vartamānaḥ svātmany adhvay abhūtvā bhaviṣyati. tathā hy uktaṃ
body.translated_text: 'that past <s>karma</s> exists' is established. 'And thus this is so' — just as the future does not exist as a substance, [Tib. 135a] so too the past. 'In the present time-period' — and so forth in detail. The meaning is: by not having existed in its present form, [it] comes into being. No — because of the existence of the time-period, because of being no different thing. This is not so — because of the existence of the present time-period, because of being no different thing from that designated as 'the eye' (<s>cakṣus</s>). The meaning is: because of being no different substance. The very thing that is the present time-period — that itself is the entity (<s>bhāva</s>). Then how will that very present thing, in its own time-period, come into being after not having been? For thus it was stated:

children.translated_text: 'Those very time-periods are the subject of discourse' —

body.text: iti. atha svātmani cakṣuṣi cakṣur abhūtvā bhavati siddham idam anāgataṃ cakṣur nāstīti. ālaṃbanamātram iti. mātraśabdo janakatvavyāvartanārthaḥ. tadrūpotpatter ālaṃbanaṃ dharmā ity abhiprāyaḥ. yad anāgataṃ sahasrair iti. saṃnikṛṣṭam apy anāgataṃ janakaṃ na yujyate. kim aṃgāticireṇa kālena yad bhaviṣyati. na hi pūrvakālīnasya phalasya paścātkālīno hetur yujyata iti. nirvānaṃ ceti. nirvāṇaṃ hi vijñānaṃ niruddhān na janayet. saṃsārapravṛttinirodhād ity abhiprāyaḥ. abhūd bhaviṣyati ceti. yad vartamānāvasthāyāṃ rūpam abhūt bhaviṣyati ca. tad ālaṃbanam ity arthaḥ. kathaṃ jñāyate evaṃ tad ālaṃbyate na punar astīty [Tib. 135b] ata āha. na hi kaścid atītaṃ rūpaṃ vedanāṃ vā smarann astīti paśyati. kiṃ tarhi. abhūd iti smarati tad rūpaṃ yathādṛṣṭaṃ yathānubhūtāṃ ca vedanāṃ cakṣurvijñānānubhavabalena. yathā khalv apīti vistareṇācārya evopacayahetum āha. vartamānarūpam iva bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac ca gṛhyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. yadi ca tathaivāstīti yathā vartamānaṃ. vartamānaṃ tat prāpnoti. atha nāsti tat tathaiva asad apy ālaṃbanaṃ bhavatīti siddhaṃ. vartamānavadrūpasyābhāvāt. tasya ca smaryamāṇatvāt. tad eva tadvikīrṇam iti. yad eva tad vartamānaṃ. tad eva vikīrṇam atītānāgataṃ. na. vikīrṇasyāgrahaṇād iti. na yuktam etat. vikīrṇasyāgrahaṇāt. pūrvaṃ na vikīrṇam idānīṃ vikīrṇam etad rūpam ity evam asyāgrahaṇāt. yadi ca tat tad eveti vistaraḥ. yadi ca vartamānāvasthāyāṃ piṇḍībhūtaṃ rūpaṃ. tad atītāvasthāyām anāgatāvasthāyāṃ ca paramāṇuśo vibhaktam ato na vartamānavat gṛhyate. evaṃ sati tādavasthyān nityāḥ paramāṇavaḥ syuḥ. anāgatāḥ pratyutpannā atītāś ca ta eva ta iti. evaṃ ca sati paramāṇusaṃcayavibhāgamātram eva prāpnoti. na tu kaścid utpādo nāpi nirodha ity ājīvikānāṃ pāṣaṇḍināṃ vādaḥ parigṛhīto bhavati. tathā ceṣyamāṇe sūtram apāstaṃ bhavati. cakṣur bhikṣava utpadyamānam
body.translated_text: thus. But if the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) comes into being in itself after not having been — then it is established that the future eye does not exist. 'Merely as an object' (<s>ālaṃbanamātra</s>) — the word 'merely' is for the purpose of excluding causative capacity. The intent is: <s>dharma</s>s are objects of the arising of that kind of cognition. 'That which is future, by thousands' — even a near future [<s>dharma</s>] is not a reasonable cause. How much less so one that will exist after an exceedingly long time. For a later cause of an earlier result is not reasonable. 'And <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — for <s>nirvāṇa</s>, being [the cessation of] consciousness, would not generate [anything] from what has ceased — the intent being: because of the cessation of the continuation of <s>saṃsāra</s>. 'Existed and will exist' — that form which existed and will exist in the present state — that is the object — this is the meaning. How is it known that it is cognized thus but does not exist? [Tib. 135b] Therefore he says: for no one remembering past form or feeling sees [it] as 'existing.' What then? One remembers 'it existed' — that form as it was seen and that feeling as it was experienced, through the power of visual consciousness experience. 'Just as indeed' — and so forth in detail, the <s>Ācārya</s> himself states the reason for accumulation. The intent is: past and future form is grasped as though it were present form. And if it exists just so — just as the present [exists] — it follows that it is present. But if it does not exist — it is established that even what is non-existent can be an object. Because of the absence of form like that of the present — and because of its being remembered. 'That very thing scattered' — whatever is that present [form] — that very thing, scattered, is the past and future. No — because the scattered is not grasped.
