This is not correct — because the scattered is not grasped. [One does not grasp] 'this form was previously not scattered, [and] now is scattered' — because of not grasping it thus. And if that is that very thing — and so forth in detail. And if form that is consolidated in the present state — that very thing, in the past and future states, is divided atom by atom, and therefore is not grasped like the present — then being so, the atoms would be permanent, being in the same state [across times] — future, present, and past being the same. And this being so, it would follow that there is merely the aggregation and separation of atoms — but there would be no arising and no cessation — thus the doctrine of the <s>Ājīvika</s> heretics would be adopted. And if accepted thus, the <s>sūtra</s> would be set aside: 'The eye, O monks, being produced

body.text:
na kutaśicd āgacchati. nirudhyamānaṃ na kvacit saṃnicayaṃ gacchati. iti hi bhikṣavaś cakṣur [Tib. 136a] abhūtvā bhavati bhūtvā ca prativigacchatīti. kathakṃ punar idaṃ sūtram apaviddhaṃ virodhitaṃ bhavati. yasmāc cakṣur utpadyamānaṃ svena rūpeṇa na kutaścid āgacchatīty etat padaṃ bādhitaṃ bhavati. nirudhyamānaṃ na kvacit saṃnicayaṃ gacchatīty etad api padaṃ bādhitaṃ bhavati. atīte 'dhvani tatparamāṇūnāṃ viprakīrṇasaṃcitatvābhyupagamāt. aparamāṇusaṃcitānām iti. vedanādīnām aparamāṇvātmanāṃ kathaṃ viprakīrṇatvaṃ. mūrtānāṃ hi saṃcitatvaṃ viprakīrṇatvaṃ vābhavad bhaven nāmūrtānāṃ. te 'pi ca yathotpannānubhūtāḥ smaryanta iti. vartamānarūpā eva smaryante. yadi ca te tathaiva saṃti. yathā vartamānā nityāḥ prāpnuvaṃti. atha na saṃti tadrūpāḥ asad apy ālaṃbanam iti siddhaṃ. trayodaśam apy āyatanam ālaṃbanaṃ syād iti. trayodaśānām āyatanānāṃ pūraṇaṃ trayadaśam āyatanaṃ. tad vijñānasyālaṃbanaṃ syāt. asadālaṃbanatva iṣyamāṇe tadālaṃbanaṃ vā vijñānaṃ syāt. evaṃ vaibhāṣikeṇokte ācārya āha. atha trayodaśam iti vistaraḥ. etad eva nāmeti vaibhaṣikāḥ. yad etan nāma tryodaśam āyatanam iti. tad ālaṃbanaṃ. evaṃ tarhi nāmaiva nāstīti [Tib. 136b] pratīyeta. nābhidheyaṃ trayodaśāyatanābhāvalakṣaṇaṃ. kiṃ ca yaś ca śabdasya prāgabhāvam ālaṃbate. kiṃ tasyālaṃbanaṃ. bhavatīti vākyaśeṣaḥ. evaṃ prakṛte vaibhāṣika āha. śabda evālaṃbanam iti prakṛtaṃ. evaṃ tarhīti vistareṇācāryaḥ. yaḥ śabdasya prāgabhāvam ālaṃbate. śabda eva tenālaṃbito bhavati. na prāgabhāvaḥ. prāptam idaṃ bhavati. yaḥ śabdābhāvaṃ prārthayate. tasya śabda eva kartavyaḥ syād iti. anāgatāvastha iti cet syān mataṃ. yasyāsau prāgabhāvaḥ. so 'nāgatāvasthas tenālaṃbyate. tasmād yaḥ śabdābhāvaṃ prārthayate. na tasya śabda eva kartavyaḥ syād iti. tad ucyate. sati kathaṃ nāstīti buddhir iti. vidyamāne tasmiṃ śabde yasyāsau prāgabhāvaḥ katham asya nāstibuddhir yā prāgabhāvam ālaṃbate. vartamāno nāstīti cet. tatraitat syāt vartamāno nāstīty evaṃ tadālaṃbanān nāstibuddhis tasyotpadyata iti. na. ekatvāt. yad eva tad anāgataṃ. tad eva vartamānaṃ bhavati. na tasmād anyad iti. kathaṃ tasminn eva vartamāne nāstibuddhir utpadyate. yo vā tasya viśeṣaḥ. yo vā tasyānāgatasya paścād viśeṣo vartamānāvasthāyāṃ bhavati. tatra viśeṣe vartamāno nāstīti tadbuddhir
utpadyate. 'tasyābhūtvābhāvasiddhiḥ. tasya viśeṣasyābhūtvā pūrvaṃ paścād bhāvaḥ. tasya siddhir iti. [Tib. 137a] bhāvaś cābhāvaś ceti. bhāvo vartamānāvasthyāyām abhāvo 'tītānāgatāvasthayoḥ. iti vijñānasyobhayam ālaṃbanaṃ bhavati. yady abhāvo vijñānasyālaṃbanaṃ yat tarhīti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: it does not come from anywhere when arising; when ceasing, it does not go to any repository. Thus, O monks, the eye, not having been, comes to be; and having been, it passes away.' How then is this sūtra refuted and contradicted? Because the eye 'when arising, does not come from anywhere by its own form' — this statement is contradicted. 'When ceasing, it does not go to any repository' — this statement too is contradicted, because of accepting that the atoms of those [past dharmas] are in a scattered or aggregated state in the past time-period. 'Of those not composed of atoms' — for feeling and the rest, which do not have the nature of atoms, how can there be a state of being scattered? For only material things could have a state of being aggregated or scattered, not immaterial things. 'And they too are remembered as experienced when they arose' — they are remembered precisely in the form they had when present. And if they exist thus just as when present, they would turn out to be permanent. But if they do not exist in that form, then it is established that even non-existent [things] can be objects. A thirteenth sense-base would be the object — a thirteenth sense-base, the completion of thirteen sense-bases. That would be the object of consciousness. If non-existent objects are accepted, consciousness having that as object would be [possible]. Or [consciousness taking] it as object. When the Vaibhāṣika has said this, the Ācārya says: 'But if a thirteenth' — and so forth in detail. 'This very name' — the Vaibhāṣikas say: what has this very name 'thirteenth sense-base' — that is the object. If so, then it would be understood that the name itself does not exist — not the referent having the characteristic of the non-existence of thirteen sense-bases. Moreover, one who takes the prior non-existence of sound as object — what is the object of that? 'It exists' is the remainder of the sentence. When the Vaibhāṣika has said thus in this context: 'Sound itself is the object,' the Ācārya says in detail thus: one who takes the prior non-existence of sound as object — sound itself is taken as object by that one, not the prior non-existence. This consequence follows: one who desires the non-existence of sound would have to produce sound itself. If one thinks [the answer is:] 'in the future state' — the one of which that is the prior non-existence, that one in the future state is taken as object by that one; therefore, one who desires the non-existence of sound would not have to produce sound itself. To this it is said: 'How can there be the cognition "it does not exist" regarding what exists?' — when that sound of which that is the prior non-existence exists, how can the cognition of non-existence arise — the cognition that takes the prior non-existence as its object? 'If [one says] "it does not exist as present"' — one might think thus: the cognition of non-existence arises for that one from [the thought] 'it does not exist as present.' No — because of identity. That which is future — that very thing becomes present; it is not different from it. How then does the cognition of non-existence arise with respect to that very thing that is present? Or whatever distinction of that thing — whatever distinction of that future thing later occurs in the present state — with regard to that distinction, 'it does not exist as present' — this cognition of non-existence arises. 'The establishment of the having-not-been-ness of that' — of that distinction, having not been before and afterward coming to be — the establishment thereof. Both existence and non-existence — existence in the present state, non-existence in the past and future states. Thus both become the object of consciousness. If non-existence is the object of consciousness, 'then what' — and so forth in detail.

body.text: bodhisattvena caramabhavikenaivam uktaṃ. yal lokenāsti. taj jñāsyāmīty eṣa saṃbhavo nāstīti vacanād abhāvālaṃbanaṃ na bhavatīti darśitaṃ bhavati. ācāryo 'nyābhiprāyatām asya sūtrasya darśayann āh. apare ābhimānikā iti vistaraḥ. apariśuddhasamādhayo 'pare ābhimānikā bhavaṃti. asaṃtam apy avabhāsaṃ divyacakṣuravabhāsaṃ prayogāvasthāyāṃ saṃtam ity eva paśyaṃti. ahaṃ tu santam evāvabhāsaṃ pūrvarūpaṃ divyacakṣuṣo 'stīti paśyāmīty ayaṃ tatra sūtre 'bhiprāyaḥ. kuto 'sya vimarśa iti. sarvabuddhīnāṃ sadviṣayatve vyavasthāpyamāne kuto 'sya vimarśavicāraḥ saṃdeho vā syāt. yad uta loke nāstīti vistareṇa ya uktaḥ. sadasadālaṃbane tu buddhīnām ayaṃ vimarśaḥ saṃbhavati. nānyathā. ko vā viśeṣa iti. ko vā bodhisattvasyānyebhyo viśeṣaḥ yadi te 'pi santam evāvabhāsaṃ paśyaṃti nāsaṃtaṃ. sadasadālaṃbanatve hi buddhīnām ayaṃ viśeṣo bhavati. itthaṃ caitad evaṃ [Tib. 137b] sat. asadālaṃbanā buddhaya iti. sac ca sato jñāsyaty asac cāsata itīdam atrodāharaṇaṃ. sac ca vastu sattvataḥ paraiṣyati jñāsyati asac cāsattvata ity asadālaṃbanā buddhaya iti siddhaṃ. tasmād ayam apy ahetur iti. yad etad bodhisattvenoktam iti. tatpūrvakād iti. karmapūrvakāt cittasaṃtānaviśeṣāt. ātmavādapratiṣedha iti. śāstrāvasāne vātsīputrīyamatapratiṣedhe. utpādas tarhi abhūtvā bhavatīti. utpādaḥ pūrvaṃ nāstīdānīṃ bhavatīti siddho 'pūrvaprādurbhāvaḥ. utpādasyotpādavatā saha tulyavārttatvāt. atha sarva evastīti. utpādo 'pi yady asti na kevalaṃ hetur anāgataṃ ca phalam ity abhiprāyaḥ. kasyedānīṃ kva sāmarthyam iti. kasya hetoḥ kva phale sāmarthyaṃ. hetuś ca yathoktaḥ utpādaḥ phalaṃ cānāgatam astīti. vartamānīkaraṇa iti vaibhāṣikaḥ. kim idānīṃ vartamānīkaraṇam iti vistareṇācāryaḥ. notpādo vartamānīkaraṇaṃ. tasya vidyamānatvāt. ata evaṃ pṛcchati. deśāṃtarākarṣaṇaṃ cet. yadi manyase hetunā phalasya deśāṃtarākarṣaṇaṃ vartamānīkaraṇam iti. atra brūmaḥ. nityaṃ prasaktaṃ phalam iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. kevalaṃ deśāṃtarād deśāṃtarākarṣaṇaṃ. na kiṃcid apūrvam utpadyata iti. nityaṃ prasaktaṃ. arūpiṇāṃ ca [Tib. 138a] vedanādīnāṃ. kathaṃ taddeśāṃtarākarṣaṇā. amūrtatvenādeśasthatvān na tad yujyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. yac ca tadākarṣaṇaṃ kriyāsaṃjñakaṃ. tad abhūtvā bhūtam ity abhūtvābhāvasiddhir ity abhiprāyaḥ. svabhāvaviśeṣaṇaṃ cet. yadi manyase hetunā svabhāvo 'sya phalasya viśeṣyate. tena phalaviśeṣaṇaṃ. bhavatīti. atra brūmaḥ. siddham abhūtvābhavanam iti. siddham abhūtvā viśeṣaṇasya
body.translated_text: By the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence, it was said thus: 'Whatever exists in the world — that I shall know.' By the word 'this is not possible,' the absence of non-existent objects is demonstrated through the statement of non-existence. The <s>Ācārya</s>, showing the different intent of this <s>sūtra</s>, says: 'Others are presumptuous' — and so forth in detail. Others with impure concentration are presumptuous. Even though the radiance, the radiance of the divine eye, does not actually exist in the preparatory stage, they see it as existing. But I see the radiance that actually exists — the precursor of the divine eye — as existing — this is the intent in that <s>sūtra</s>. 'Whence would his investigation come?' — if all cognitions were established as having existent objects, whence would his investigation, deliberation, or doubt come — namely, what was stated in detail 'it does not exist in the world'? But if cognitions have both existent and non-existent objects, this investigation is possible, not otherwise. 'Or what would be his distinction?' — or what would be the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s distinction from others, if they too see only what exists, not what does not exist? If cognitions have both existent and non-existent objects, this distinction exists. 'This being so' — given that cognitions have non-existent objects — 'it is established that cognitions have non-existent objects.' And the existing, he will know by its existence; the non-existing, by its non-existence — this is the illustration here. The existing thing he will ascertain by its existence; and the non-existing by its non-existence — thus it is established that cognitions have non-existent objects. 'Therefore this too is not a reason' — what was stated by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. 'From that as prior cause' — from a special [transformation of] the mental continuum having <s>karma</s> as prior cause. 'Refutation of the doctrine of self' — in the refutation of the <s>Vātsīputrīya</s> view at the conclusion of the treatise. 'Then arising means "coming-to-be after not-having-been"' — arising is established as not-having-existed-before and now existing — a novel appearance. Because arising operates simultaneously with what possesses arising. 'But if everything exists' — even arising, if it exists — not only the cause and the future effect — this is the intent. 'Whose power now over what?' — whose cause's power over which effect? Since the cause as stated and the arising, and the effect in the future, both exist. 'Making present' — says the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>. 'What now is making present?' — the <s>Ācārya</s> says in detail. Arising is not making present, because it already exists. For this very reason he asks: 'If dragging to another location' — if you think that making present means the cause dragging the effect to another location — to this we say: the remainder of the sentence is: the effect would be eternally consequent. It would be merely dragging from one location to another; nothing new would arise — [hence] eternally consequent. 'And for immaterial things' — feeling and the rest — how would there be dragging to another location? Since, being immaterial and thus not located in a place, that is not fitting — this is the intent. And whatever that dragging is, designated as 'action' — that, having not-been and [then] been, establishes the having-not-been — this is the intent. 'If qualification of own-nature' — if you think that the cause qualifies the own-nature of its effect, that constitutes the effect's qualification — coming to be — to this we say: 'the having-not-been-and-then-being is established' — the having-not-been of the qualification

body.text: bhavanaṃ prādurbhāva iti. adhvatrayaṃ vā. kiṃ. sarvam astīty adhikṛtaṃ. yathātra tad asti tathoktam iti. yad bhūtapūrvaṃ tad atītaṃ. yat sati hetau bhaviṣyati. tad anāgataṃ. yad bhūtvāvinaṣṭaṃ. tat pratyutpannam. ity evaṃ sarvāstivādaḥ śāsane sādhur bhavati. kathaṃ tena tasmiṃ vā saṃyuktā iti. kathaṃ tenātītānāgatena kleśena tasmin vā atītānāgate vastuni kathaṃ saṃyukta iti. tajjataddhetvanuśayabhāvāt kleśeneti. tasmād atītāj jātas tajjaḥ. tasyānāgatasya hetus taddhetuḥ. tajjaś cāsau taddhetuś ca tajjataddhetuḥ. tajjataddhetur anuśayo bījaṃ tajjataddhetvanuśayaḥ. tasya bhāvāt. atītenānāgatena ca kleśena yathākramaṃ saṃyuktaḥ. tad atītānāgataṃ vastv ālaṃbanam asyeti tadālaṃbanaḥ kleśas tasyānuśayaḥ. tasya bhāvād atīte 'nāgate ca vastuni yathākramaṃ saṃyukta iti
body.translated_text: and [then] being — appearance — is established. 'Or the three time-periods' — what? 'Everything exists' — is the topic. 'As it exists here, so it is stated.' That which existed before is past. That which, given the cause, will be — that is future. That which, having been, has not perished — that is present. Thus the <s>Sarvāstivāda</s> doctrine is sound within the teaching. 'How by that or in that are they connected' — how are they connected by that past or future affliction, or in that past or future object? 'Because of the existence of the [potency] born-of-that, caused-by-that, and having the character of latent disposition, with regard to the affliction' — therefore born from that past [affliction] is 'born-of-that'; being the cause of that future [affliction] is 'caused-by-that.' Born-of-that and caused-by-that — born-of-that-and-caused-by-that. The born-of-that-and-caused-by-that latent disposition is the seed — born-of-that-and-caused-by-that-latent-disposition. Because of the existence of that, one is connected by the past and future affliction respectively. 'That' — the past or future object is the object of this, hence 'having-that-as-object'; the affliction that is a latent disposition of that — because of the existence of that, one is connected in the past and future object respectively.

body.text: dharmateti. [Tib. 138b] dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvaḥ. atītādikādhvavyavasthāne sati tatsaṃvyavahāravyutpādanārtham āha. asti paryāya ityādi. asti vacanakramaḥ. yad utpadyate. tan nirudhyata ity uktvā. dṛṣṭāṃtam āha. rūpam utpadyate rūpaṃ nirudhyate dravyānanyatvāt. anyad utpadyate 'nyan nirudhyate. anāgatam utpadyate 'nyad utpādābhimukhatvāt. vartamānaṃ nirudhyate 'nyan nirodhābhimukhatvāt. adhvāpy utpadyate utpadyamānasya dharmasyādhvasaṃgṛhītatvād adhvasvabhāvatvād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'The nature of dharmas' — the own-nature of dharmas. Given that the classification of time-periods as past and the like exists, in order to explain the conventional usage of that, he says: 'There is a sequential expression' — and so on. There is a sequence of words: 'What arises, that ceases' — having said this, he gives an example: 'Form arises, form ceases' — because of the non-otherness of the substance. 'Something else arises, something else ceases' — what is future arises, being something other because of facing arising. What is present ceases, being something other because of facing cessation. 'A time-period too arises' — because the arising dharma is included in a time-period, because of having the nature of a time-period — this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: 'Those very time-periods are the subject of discussion' (<s>kathāvastu</s>) —

body.text: iti lakṣaṇāt. adhvano 'py upādānarūpād utpadyate dharmaḥ. kasmād ity āha. anekakṣaṇikatvād anāgatasyādhvana iti. yasmād anekeṣāṃ kṣaṇānām anāgatānāṃ rāśirūpāṇāṃ kaścid eva kṣaṇa utpadyate. ato 'dhvano 'py utpadyata ity ucyate.
body.translated_text: from this definition. A dharma arises even from the time-period that is of the nature of clinging-form. Why? He says: 'Because the future time-period is of many moments' — since from the mass of many future moments, having the nature of a collection, only a certain moment arises. Therefore it is said to arise even from the time-period.

children.translated_text: 'But by all the remaining [latent dispositions], everywhere' —

body.text: prasaṃgenāgatam atītānāgatavicāraṇaṃ. yad yastu prahīṇam ityādi. iha prahāṇaṃ prāptivigamāt. visaṃyogas tadālaṃbanakleśaprahāṇāt. darśanabhāvanāmārgāv adhikṛtya
body.translated_text: arrived at by digression is the examination of the past and future. 'Whatever has been abandoned' — and so forth. Here, abandonment is through the removal of acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>). Separation (<s>visaṃyoga</s>) is through the abandonment of the affliction taking that as its object. With reference to the paths of seeing and cultivation,

children.translated_text: 'When what is to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering has been abandoned' —

body.text: ityādi. prāk prahīṇe ityādi.
body.translated_text: and so forth. 'Previously, when it has been abandoned' — and so forth.

body.text: iti. samudayadarśanaprahātavyaiḥ sarvatragaiḥ.
body.translated_text: thus — by the universal [latent dispositions] to be abandoned by the seeing of origination.

children.translated_text: 'By the remaining impurities having that as their object' —

body.text: iti. prahīṇaprakāraviṣayānuśayair ity arthaḥ. tadyathādhimātrādhimātre prakāre prahīṇe 'dhimātramadhyādibhiḥ śeṣair aprahīṇair anuśayaiḥ saṃyuktaḥ. tathā hy asāv adhimātrādhimātreṇa prahīṇena kleśaprakāreṇa visaṃyukto 'pi sa saṃyukta eva taiḥ śeṣair iti.
body.translated_text: the meaning is: by the latent dispositions whose object is the abandoned type. For example, when the most-intense-of-the-most-intense type has been abandoned, one is still connected by the remaining unabandon latent dispositions — moderate-of-the-most-intense and the rest. For even though one is disconnected from that most-intense-of-the-most-intense affliction-type that has been abandoned, one is still indeed connected by those remaining [unabandon latent dispositions].

body.text: (V.29-31) piṇḍavibhāṣāṃ kurvaṃti. saṃkṣepavyākhyāṃ kurvaṃtīty arthaḥ. ke. vaibhāṣikāḥ. ṣoḍaśeti. kāmāvacarāḥ paṃca prakārāḥ. [Tib. 139a] duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgadarśanaprahātavyāś catvāro bhāvanāprahātavyaś ca paṃcamaḥ. evaṃ yāvad ārūpyāvacarāḥ paṃca prakārā iti paṃcadaśa. anāsravaś ca ṣoḍaśa iti ṣoḍaśa dharmāḥ. ime ca dharmāḥ ye darśanaprahātavyāḥ. te catuḥskandhasvabhāvāḥ. ye bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ. te paṃcaskandhasvabhāvāḥ. kathaṃ. yā vedanā yair darśanaprahātavyair anuśayaiḥ saṃprayuktāḥ. sa vedanāskandhaḥ. yāḥ saṃjñāḥ. sa saṃjñāskandhaḥ. ye 'nuśayāḥ ye ca tatsaṃprayuktāś cetanādayo yāś caiṣāṃ vedanādīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ caitasikānāṃ prāptayo jātijarāsthityanityatāś ca viprayuktāḥ. sa saṃskāraskandhaḥ. yac caibhiḥ saṃprayuktaṃ manovijñānaṃ. sa vijñānaskandhaḥ. iti catuḥskandhasvabhāvā darśanaprahātavyāḥ. bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ punar ato 'nye sāsravā dharmāḥ. kathaṃ. bāhyādhyātmikaṃ sarvaṃ sāsravaṃ rūpaṃ rūpaskandhaḥ. anāsravadarśanaprahātavyavarjyāś ca vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānaskandhā iti paṃcaskandhasvabhāvā bhāvanāprahātavyā veditavyāḥ. cittāny api ṣoḍaśaitāny eveti. kāmāvacaraṃ duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaṃ yāvad bhāvanāprahātavyam [Tib. 139b] iti paṃca cittāni. evaṃ rūpāvacarāṇy ārūpyāvacarāṇi ca paṃcapaṃca anāsravaṃ ca cittam iti ṣoḍaśa cittāni. tāni tatṣoḍaśadharmālaṃbanāni varṇyaṃte. amuṣminn iyaṃto 'nuśayā iti. amuṣmiṃ dharme iyaṃto 'nuśayā ye tena cittena saṃprayuktā ālaṃbanataḥ saṃprayogato vānuśerata ity etad abhyūhitavyaṃ.

children.translated_text: 'Those born in the Desire Realm, to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origination, and by cultivation'

body.translated_text: (V.29-31) They make a summary exposition (<s>piṇḍavibhāṣā</s>) — the meaning is: they make a condensed explanation. Who? The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s. 'Sixteen' — those belonging to the Desire Realm are of five types: those to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path — four, and those to be abandoned by cultivation as the fifth. Similarly, up to those belonging to the Formless Realm are of five types — thus fifteen. And the uncontaminated as the sixteenth — thus sixteen <s>dharma</s>s. And these <s>dharma</s>s: those to be abandoned by seeing have the intrinsic nature of four aggregates. Those to be abandoned by cultivation have the intrinsic nature of five aggregates. How? Whatever feelings are associated with the latent dispositions to be abandoned by seeing — that is the feeling aggregate. Whatever perceptions — that is the perception aggregate. Whatever latent dispositions, and the volitions and other [mental factors] associated with them, and the acquisitions, birth, aging, persistence, and impermanence of all these mental factors beginning with feeling — the dissociated [formations] — that is the formations aggregate. And whatever mental consciousness is associated with these — that is the consciousness aggregate. Thus those to be abandoned by seeing have the intrinsic nature of four aggregates. Those to be abandoned by cultivation, moreover, are other contaminated <s>dharma</s>s beyond these. How? All contaminated form, external and internal, is the form aggregate. And the feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness aggregates excluding those [to be abandoned by seeing] and the uncontaminated — thus those to be abandoned by cultivation should be known as having the intrinsic nature of five aggregates. 'The consciousnesses too are these very sixteen' — the Desire Realm consciousness to be abandoned by the seeing of suffering, up to that to be abandoned by cultivation — thus five consciousnesses. Similarly, five each belonging to the Form and Formless Realms, and the uncontaminated consciousness — thus sixteen consciousnesses. Those are described as having those sixteen <s>dharma</s>s as their objects. 'In such-and-such [dharma], this many latent dispositions' — it should be inferred that in such-and-such a <s>dharma</s>, this many latent dispositions — those that are associated with that consciousness — lie latent by way of object or by way of association.

body.text: iti. duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāpraheyāḥ kāmāvacarā ity arthaḥ. eṣā vigraha jātir iti. svakatrayaṃ caikarūpāptaṃ cāmalaṃ ca. svakatrayaikarūpāptāmalāni vijñānāni.
body.translated_text: — the meaning is: those belonging to the Desire Realm, to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, and by cultivation. 'This is the expanded form' — [the compound means:] one's own three, those attained with the Form Realm, and the uncontaminated. Consciousnesses of one's own three, those attained with the Form Realm, and the uncontaminated.

children.translated_text: 'Consciousnesses of one's own three, those attained with the Form Realm, and the uncontaminated.'

body.text: teṣāṃ
body.translated_text: 'Their'

body.text: kāmāvacarās tāvad iti vistaraḥ. kāmāvacarā duḥkhasamudayadarśanaprahātavyā
body.translated_text: 'First, the Desire Realm' — and so forth in detail. Those belonging to the Desire Realm, to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination

body.text: yathākramaṃ daśasaptānuśayāḥ. tatsahabhuvas tatprāptayaś ca sānucarāḥ. bhāvanāheyāś caturanuśayās tatsahabhuvas tatprāptayaś ca sānucarāḥ. sarvaṃ sāsravaṃ rūpaṃ. anye cākliṣṭā dharmāḥ. ete dharmāḥ paṃcānāṃ cittānām ālaṃbanaṃ. keṣām ity āha. svadhātukānāṃ trayāṇāṃ teṣām eveti. kāmāvacarāṇāṃ duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāheyānāṃ. [Tib. 140a] kathaṃ kṛtvā. duḥkhadarśanaheyās tāvad duḥkhadarśanaheyasya sarvatragāsarvatragasaṃprayuktasya. samudayadarśanaprahātavyasya ca sarvatragasaṃprayuktasya. bhāvanāheyasya ca kuśalasya. rūpāvacarasyaikasya bhāvanāheyasyaiva. laukikena mārgeṇa kāmadhātūpapannasya kāmāvacaradharmālaṃbanāvasthāyāṃ. rūpadhātūpapannasya ca kāmadhātudarśanāvasthāyāṃ. anāsravasya ca dharmajñānapakṣasya ceti paṃcānāṃ cittānām ālaṃbanaṃ bhavaṃti. na kāmāvacarayor nirodhamārgadarśanaheyayoś cittayor ālaṃbanam. anāsravālaṃbanayoś cittayor nirodhamārgālaṃbanatvāt. sāsravālaṃbanayorś ca nirodhamārgadarśanaheyamātrālaṃbanatvāt. nordhvabhūmikānāṃ kliṣṭānāṃ. adharabhūmikānālaṃbanatvāt. nārūpyāvacarasya kuśalasya. catasṛbhir dūratābhir dūratvāt. evaṃ samudayadarśanaheyā dviprakārasya samudayadarśanaheyasya. duḥkhadarśane heyasya ca sarvatragasaṃprayuktasya. bhāvanāheyasya kuśalasya. rūpāvacarasyaikasya bhāvanāheyasyaiva. anāsravasya ceti. paṃcānām evālaṃbanaṃ bhavaṃti. vyākhyānaṃ ca pūrvavad eva kartavyaṃ. bhāvanāheyā api paṃcānām evālaṃbanaṃ bhavaṃti. duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyayoḥ [Tib. 140b] sarvatragasaṃprayuktayoś cittayor bhāvanāheyasya ca kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtasya yathāsaṃbhavaṃ. rūpāvacarasyaikasya bhāvanāheyasyaiva. anāsravasya ceti. pūrvavad eva vācyaṃ.
body.translated_text: — in order, ten and seven latent dispositions respectively, along with their co-existents and their acquisitions, together with their retinue. Those to be abandoned by cultivation — four latent dispositions, along with their co-existents and their acquisitions, together with their retinue. All contaminated form. And other non-afflicted <s>dharma</s>s. These <s>dharma</s>s are the objects of five consciousnesses. Of which? He says: 'Of the three belonging to one's own realm — those very ones' — of those belonging to the Desire Realm, to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, and by cultivation. How so? Those to be abandoned by seeing suffering are first [the objects] of the consciousness to be abandoned by seeing suffering, associated with both universal and non-universal [latent dispositions]. And of the consciousness to be abandoned by seeing origination, associated with the universal [latent dispositions]. And of the consciousness to be abandoned by cultivation that is wholesome. Of the single Form Realm [consciousness] to be abandoned by cultivation alone — through the mundane path, for one born in the Desire Realm, in the state of having Desire Realm <s>dharma</s>s as object; and for one born in the Form Realm, in the state of viewing the Desire Realm. And of the uncontaminated [consciousness] belonging to the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class — thus they are objects of five consciousnesses. They are not the object of the two Desire Realm consciousnesses to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path — because those two consciousnesses have cessation and the path as their objects, being consciousnesses with uncontaminated objects; and because those two, being consciousnesses with contaminated objects, have only those to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path as their objects. Nor of the afflicted [consciousnesses] of upper grounds — because they do not have lower-ground [dharmas] as objects. Nor of the wholesome Formless Realm [consciousness] — because of distance through four types of remoteness. Similarly, those to be abandoned by seeing origination are objects of five [consciousnesses]: of the twofold [consciousness] to be abandoned by seeing origination; of the [consciousness] to be abandoned by seeing suffering, associated with the universal [latent dispositions]; of the wholesome [consciousness] to be abandoned by cultivation; of the single Form Realm [consciousness] to be abandoned by cultivation alone; and of the uncontaminated. The explanation should be made as before. Those to be abandoned by cultivation too are objects of exactly five: of the two consciousnesses to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, associated with the universal [latent dispositions]; and of the consciousness to be abandoned by cultivation — wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate as applicable; of the single Form Realm [consciousness] to be abandoned by cultivation alone; and of the uncontaminated. This should be stated as before.

children.translated_text: 'Of one's own, lower three, upper single, and uncontaminated'

body.text: iti. svakānām adharāṇāṃ ca trayaṃ svakādharatrayaṃ ca ūrdhvaikaṃ cāmalaṃ ceti vigrahaḥ. rūpāvacarās ta eva triprakārā dharmā iti. duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāheyās teṣām adhikṛtatvāt. te 'ṣṭānāṃ cittānām ālaṃbanaṃ. svadhātukānāṃ trayāṇāṃ teṣām eva duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāheyānāṃ pūrvavad vyākhyeyaṃ. adharadhātukānāṃ trayāṇāṃ teṣām eva. teṣāṃ duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyayor visabhāgadhātusarvatragasaṃprayuktayoś cittayor bhāvanāheyasya ca śrutamayasya ca cintāmayasya vā. ūrdhvadhātukasyaikasya bhāvanāheyayaivākāśānāṃtyāyatanasāmantakasaṃgṛhītasya anāsravasya cānvayajñānapakṣasyeti.
body.translated_text: — the analysis is: one's own and lower [making] three, that is 'one's own-and-lower three'; and one upper; and the uncontaminated. 'Those very threefold <s>dharma</s>s belonging to the Form Realm' — those to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, and by cultivation, since those are the topic. They are the objects of eight consciousnesses. 'Of the three belonging to one's own realm — those very ones' — of those belonging to the Form Realm, to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, and by cultivation — should be explained as before. 'Of the three belonging to the lower realm — those very ones.' Of those [Desire Realm] consciousnesses to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, associated with the universal [latent dispositions] of a dissimilar realm; and of the consciousness to be abandoned by cultivation that is [born of] learning (<s>śrutamaya</s>) or reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>). Of the single upper-realm [consciousness] to be abandoned by cultivation alone — that included in the preliminary to the space-infinity base (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>). And of the uncontaminated belonging to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) class.

children.translated_text: 'Objects of those attained with the triple realm and the uncontaminated'

children.text: iti. tridhātvāptānāṃ trayāṇām anāsravasya ca gocarāḥ. ta eveti ta eva duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāheyā [Tib. 141a] adhikṛtāḥ. triprakarāṇāṃ teṣām eveti. kāmarūpāvacarāṇāṃ duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyānāṃ visabhāgadhātusarvatragasaṃprayuktānāṃ caturṇāṃ bhāvanāprahātavyayor dvayor yathāyogaṃ. svadhātukānāṃ ca trayāṇāṃ. katameṣāṃ. sarvatragāsarvatragasaṃprayuktayor yathāyogaṃ dvayor bhāvanāprahātavyasya cānāsravasya ceti. daśānāṃ cittānām ālaṃbanaṃ bhavaṃti.
children.translated_text: — objects of those attained with the triple realm, [specifically] the three, and of the uncontaminated. 'Those very ones' — those very [dharmas] to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, and by cultivation are the topic. 'Of three types of those very ones' — of the Desire and Form Realm [consciousnesses] to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, associated with the universal [latent dispositions] of a dissimilar realm — four [consciousnesses]; of the two to be abandoned by cultivation, as applicable. And of the three belonging to one's own realm. Of which? Of the two associated with the universal and non-universal [latent dispositions] respectively, to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, as applicable; and of the one to be abandoned by cultivation; and of the uncontaminated. They are objects of ten consciousnesses.
'Those to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path — objects of all, one's own, and superior'

body.text: iti. sarvagrahaṇaṃ traidhātukopasaṃgrahārthaṃ.
body.translated_text: — the word 'all' is for the purpose of including the triple realm.

body.text: iti vacanāt pūvoktānāṃ ca gocarā ity arthād uktaṃ bhavati. atha vā svenādhikāni svādhikāni. svādhikānāṃ gocarāḥ svādhikagocarā iti. tasyādhikasyeti. rāgādisaṃprayuktasya. na mithyādṛṣṭyādisaṃprayuktasya. tasya nityaṃ nirodhamārgālaṃbanatvāt. pūrvoktānāṃ paṃcānām iti. kāmāvacarāṇāṃ trayāṇāṃ. dvinikāyasarvatragasaṃprayuktabhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ. rūpāvacarasya bhāvanāprahātavyasyaiva. anāsravasya ceti. mārgadarśanaprahātavyā apy evam iti. kim evaṃ. [Tib. 141b] ṣaṇṇāṃ cittānām ālaṃbanam iti. navānām ekādaśānāṃ ca cittānām ālaṃbanaṃ bhavatīti. rūpāvacarā nirodhamārgadarśanaprahātavyā navānāṃ cittānām ālaṃbanaṃ bhavaṃti. ārūpyāvacarā ekādaśānām iti. kathaṃ. rūpāvacarā nirodhamārgadarśanaprahātavyā dharmāḥ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ visabhāgadhātusarvatragasaṃprayuktabhāvanāheyānāṃ trayāṇāṃ. svadhātukānāṃ ca trayāṇāṃ dvinikāyasarvatragasaṃprayuktabhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ. ārūpyāvacarasya bhāvanāprahātavyasyākāśānaṃtyāyatanasaṃgṛhītasya. anāsravasya cānvayajñānapakṣasya. tasyaiva cādhikasya nirodhadarśanaprahātavyasya mārgadarśanaprahātavyasya vā cittasya. iti navānāṃ pratyekam ālaṃbanaṃ bhavaṃti. ārūpyāvacarā api nirodhamārgadarśanaprahātavyā dharmāḥ pratyekam ekādaśānāṃ cittānām ālambanaṃ bhavaṃti. kāmarūpāvacarāṇāṃ visabhāgadhātusarvatragasaṃprayuktabhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ. svadhātukānāṃ ca trayāṇāṃ dvinikāyasarvatragasaṃprayuktakabhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ. nirodhamārgadarśanaprahātavyasya ca pratyekam adhikasya. anāsravasya cānvayajñānapakṣasya. ity ekādaśānām ālaṃbanaṃ bhavaṃti.
body.translated_text: — from this statement, 'and objects of the previously stated [consciousnesses]' is also implicitly stated. Or alternatively, 'one's own and superior' (<s>svādhika</s>) — [the compound means:] one's own superior; objects of one's own superior — 'objects of one's own-and-superior.' 'Of that superior' — of that associated with desire (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest, not of that associated with wrong view and the rest — because the latter always have cessation and the path as their object. 'Of the five previously stated' — of the three belonging to the Desire Realm, associated with the universal [latent dispositions] of two classes and to be abandoned by cultivation; of that belonging to the Form Realm to be abandoned by cultivation alone; and of the uncontaminated. 'Those to be abandoned by seeing the path likewise' — likewise what? They are objects of six consciousnesses. They are objects of nine and eleven consciousnesses. Those belonging to the Form Realm, to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path, are objects of nine consciousnesses [each]. Those belonging to the Formless Realm, of eleven. How? The Form Realm <s>dharma</s>s to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path are [objects] of the three Desire Realm [consciousnesses] associated with the universal [latent dispositions] of a dissimilar realm and to be abandoned by cultivation; and of the three belonging to one's own realm, associated with the universal [latent dispositions] of two classes and to be abandoned by cultivation; of the Formless Realm [consciousness] to be abandoned by cultivation, included in the space-infinity base; and of the uncontaminated belonging to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class; and of that very superior consciousness to be abandoned by seeing cessation or seeing the path. Thus they are objects of nine [consciousnesses] each. The Formless Realm <s>dharma</s>s to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path too are objects of eleven consciousnesses each: of the six Desire and Form Realm [consciousnesses] associated with the universal [latent dispositions] of a dissimilar realm and to be abandoned by cultivation; and of the three belonging to one's own realm, associated with the universal [latent dispositions] of two classes and to be abandoned by cultivation; and of the [consciousness] to be abandoned by seeing cessation or the path, the superior one, respectively; and of the uncontaminated belonging to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class. Thus they are objects of eleven.

children.translated_text: 'The uncontaminated — objects of those at the end of the triple realm, the three, and the uncontaminated'

body.text: iti. anāsravā nirodhādayaḥ. triṣu dhātuṣu [Tib. 142a] yāny antyāni trayāṇi
body.translated_text: — the uncontaminated [dharmas] are cessation and the rest. In the three realms, those that are final — the three

body.text: nirodhamārgadarśanabhāvanāprahātavyalakṣaṇāni. teṣāṃ yathāyogam anāsravasya ca gocarāḥ. kathaṃ. pratisaṃkhyānirodhāryamārgau tāvat tadālaṃbanānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭivicikitsāvidyāsaṃprayuktānāṃ bhāvanāprahātavyānām anāsravasya ca dharmajñānānvayajñānapakṣasya yathāyogam ālaṃbanaṃ. ākāśāpratisaṃkhyānirodhau tu bhāvanāprahātavyasyaivākliṣṭasya cittasyālaṃbanam iti veditavyaṃ. ācāryaguṇamativasumitrau tu vyācakṣāte ākāśāpratisaṃkhyānirodhau bhāvanāprahātavyasya kliṣṭākliṣṭasyālaṃbanam iti. tad ayuktaṃ.
body.translated_text: — characterized as to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path, and by cultivation. Their objects, as applicable, and of the uncontaminated. How? Analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) and the noble path (<s>āryamārga</s>) are the objects of the consciousnesses associated with wrong view, doubt, and ignorance that have them as their domain, [those consciousnesses being] to be abandoned by cultivation; and of the uncontaminated [consciousness] belonging to the <s>dharmajñāna</s> or <s>anvayajñāna</s> class as applicable. But space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and non-analytical cessation (<s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) should be known as the objects of only the non-afflicted consciousness to be abandoned by cultivation. But teachers <s>Guṇamati</s> and <s>Vasumitra</s> explain: space and non-analytical cessation are the objects of both afflicted and non-afflicted consciousnesses to be abandoned by cultivation. That is incorrect —

children.text:
mithyādṛg vimatī tābhyāṃ yuktāvidyātha kevalā
nirodhamārgadṛggheyāḥ ṣaḍ anāsravagocarā
children.translated_text:
'Wrong view, doubt, ignorance associated with those two, and also distinctive [ignorance] —
those to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path — six have uncontaminated objects'

body.text: iti niyamāt. ato na kliṣṭacittasya bhāvanālaṃbanam iti siddhāṃtaḥ.
body.translated_text: — because of this restriction. Therefore the established doctrine is that [space and non-analytical cessation] are not objects of the afflicted consciousness to be abandoned by cultivation.

children.translated_text: 'Objects of five, eighteen, ten, and ten consciousnesses'

body.text: iti. kāmāvacarāḥ duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāheyāḥ paṃcānāṃ gocarāḥ. rūpāvacarā aṣṭānām. ārūpyāvacarā daśānām. amalā api daśānām eveti. pūrvavyākhyānānusāreṇa yojyaṃ. etāny eva ṣoḍaśa cittāni ṣaṭtriṃśad bhavaṃti. kāmadhātau duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyam asarvatragasaṃprayuktaṃ sabhāgavisabhāgasarvatragasaṃprayuktaṃ ca. evaṃ rūpadhātau duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyaṃ pratyekaṃ triprakāraṃ. ārūpyadhātāv anyatra visabhāgadhātubhūmisarvatragasaṃprayuktāt. nirodhamārgadarśanaheyaṃ dhātutraye 'pi pratyekaṃ dvidhā sāsravānāsravālaṃbanatvāt. bhāvanāheyam api kliṣṭākliṣṭabhedāt dviprakāraṃ. anāsravam api dharmajñānapakṣam anvayajñānapakṣaṃ ceti dvidhā.
body.translated_text: — those belonging to the Desire Realm, to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, and by cultivation, are objects of five [consciousnesses]. Those belonging to the Form Realm, of eight. Those belonging to the Formless Realm, of ten. The uncontaminated too, of exactly ten. This should be connected following the earlier explanation. These very sixteen consciousnesses become thirty-six: in the Desire Realm, [the consciousness] to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination — [each subdivided into] non-universal-associated, own-class-universal-associated, and dissimilar-class-universal-associated. Similarly in the Form Realm, each of those to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination is of three types. In the Formless Realm, excluding [the subdivision of] the dissimilar-realm-ground-universal-associated. Those to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path, in each of the three realms, are each twofold — because of having contaminated and uncontaminated objects. Those to be abandoned by cultivation too are twofold — because of the division into afflicted and non-afflicted. The uncontaminated too is twofold — belonging to the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class and the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class.

body.text: kāmāvacaraṃ bhāvanāprahātavyam iti. paṃcavijñānakāyikaṃ sukhendriyaṃ. rūpāvacaraṃ paṃcaprakāram [Tib. 142a] iti. prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ trivijñānakāyikaṃ. tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ mānasam ity abhisamasya yathāyogaṃ paṃcaprakāraṃ duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaṃ yāvad bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ. anāsravaṃ ca tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikam eva.
body.translated_text: 'The Desire Realm, to be abandoned by cultivation' — the pleasure faculty belonging to the five sense-consciousness bodies. 'The Form Realm, of five types' — that belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, of the three consciousness-bodies; and that belonging to the third <s>dhyāna</s> ground, which is mental — synthesizing accordingly, it is of five types: to be abandoned by seeing suffering, up to to be abandoned by cultivation. And the uncontaminated belongs to the third <s>dhyāna</s> ground alone.

body.text: kāmāvacarasya catuḥprakārasyeti. duḥkhasamudayamārgadarśanabhāvanāpraheyasya. duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyayoḥ sukhendriyam ālaṃbanaṃ bhavati. yasmād duḥkhasamudayasatyasaṃgṛhītaṃ svabhūmikam ūrdhvabhūmikaṃ vā sukhendriyaṃ satkāyamithyādṛṣṭyādīnām ālaṃbanaṃ bhavati. mārgadarśanaheyasya ca mithyādṛṣṭyādisaṃprayuktasya mārgasatyasaṃgṛhītaṃ sukhendriyam ālaṃbanaṃ. bhāvanāheyarāgādisaṃprayuktasya ca cittasya
body.translated_text: Regarding the four types of the Desire Realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>): that which is to be abandoned by seeing suffering, by seeing origination, by seeing the path, and by cultivation. For the [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, the pleasure faculty (<s>sukhendriya</s>) becomes an object. Because the pleasure faculty included in the truth of suffering and origination, belonging to one's own ground or a higher ground, becomes the object of identity-view (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), and the rest. And for the [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing the path, the pleasure faculty included in the truth of the path becomes the object of the [consciousness] associated with wrong view and the rest. And for the consciousness associated with passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest that are to be abandoned by cultivation

body.text: tatpaṃcavijñānakāyikaṃ sukhendriyam ālaṃbanam. iti catuṣprakārasyāsya tad ālaṃbanaṃ. na tu nirodhadarśanaheyasya cittasya. tatra mithyādṛṣṭyādīnāṃ nirodhālaṃbanatvāt. dṛṣṭiparāmarśādīnāṃ ca svanikāyālaṃbanatvāt. tatra ca sukhendriyābhāvāt. tenocyate 'nyatra nirodhadarśanaheyād iti. rūpāvacarasya paṃcaprakārasyeti. yasmāt tṛtīyadhyānasaṃgṛhītaṃ paṃcaprakāraṃ sukhendriyaṃ bhavati. mārgadarśanabhāvanāheyasyeti. ārūpyāvacarasya mārgadarśanaheyasya mithyādṛṣṭyādisaṃprayuktasya cittasya mārgasaṃgṛhītaṃ sukhendriyam ālaṃbanaṃ. tad eva ca bhāvanāheyasya kuśalasya cittasyālaṃbanam. anāsravasya ca sarvam apy ālaṃbaṇaṃ [Tib. 143a] bhavati. tatra yathāsaṃbhavam iti. yasmād anāsrave anuśayā nānuśerate. yasmāt kvacid eva kecid anuśerate. tasmād yathāsaṃbhavam ity ucyate. tatra vijñāne kāmāvacarāś catvāro nikāyāḥ. tadyathā nithyādṛṣṭisaṃprayukte sukhendriyālaṃbane daśāpi duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyā anuśayā ālaṃbanato 'nuśerate saṃprayogato vā yathāsaṃbhavaṃ. evaṃ samudayadarśanaprahātavyāḥ. mārgadarśanaprahātavyā api tatra sukhendriyālaṃbane vijñāne 'nuśerate. mārgasukhendriyālaṃbane hi mithyādṛṣṭyādisaṃprayukte vijñāne mithyādṛṣṭyādayaḥ saṃprayogato 'nuśerate. dṛṣṭiparāmarśādayo 'py ālaṃbanato 'nuśerate. tasmāt so 'pi nikāyas tatrānuśete. bhāvanāheyo 'pi nikāyo 'trānuśete. tatra rāgādīnāṃ sukhendriyālaṃbanavijñānālaṃbanayogāt. nirodhadarśanaprahātavyanikāyas tu tatra nānuśete. sukhendriyālaṃbanavijñānābhāvāt. rūpāvacarāḥ saṃskṛtālaṃbanā iti. rūpāvacaraṃ sukhendriyālaṃbanaṃ paṃcaprakāram asti. tatra catvāro nikāyā anuśerata iti sugamam etat. nirodhadarśanaprahātavyās [Tib. 143b] tu saṃskṛtālaṃbanāḥ katham anuśerate. tṛtīye dhyāne dṛṣṭiparāmarśādayaḥ sukhendriyeṇa saṃprayujyaṃte. te cānyonyālaṃbanāḥ. te tatra sukhendriyālaṃbanavijñāne saṃprayogata ālaṃbanato vānuśerate. ārūpyāvacarau dvau nikāyāv iti. mārgadarśanabhāvanāheyanikāyau. mārgasukhendriyālaṃbane mithyādṛṣṭyādisaṃprayukte mithyādṛṣṭyādayaḥ saṃprayogato 'nuśerate. dṛṣṭiparāmarśādayas tu tatrālaṃbanato 'nuśerate. bhāvanāheyo 'pi nikāyo 'nuśete. bhāvanāheyaṃ hi kuśalaṃ cittaṃ mārgam ālaṃbate. tatra sa rāgādinikāyo 'nuśete. sarvatragāś cārūpyāvacarā anuśayās tatraiva vijñāne mārgālaṃbanamithyādṛṣṭyādisaṃprayukte vā vijñāne 'nuśerata iti vijñātavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: the pleasure faculty belonging to the five classes of consciousness (<s>pañcavijñānakāya</s>) becomes the object. Thus, for these four types, that [pleasure faculty] is the object. But not for the consciousness to be abandoned by seeing cessation (<s>nirodhadarśanaheya</s>). There, because wrong view and the rest have cessation as their object. And because clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>) and the rest have their own group as their object. And because the pleasure faculty is absent there. Therefore it is said 'except for that to be abandoned by seeing cessation.' Regarding the five types of the Form Realm (<s>rūpāvacara</s>): because the pleasure faculty included in the third <s>dhyāna</s> is of five types. Regarding that to be abandoned by seeing the path and by cultivation: for the consciousness of the Formless Realm (<s>ārūpyāvacara</s>) that is to be abandoned by seeing the path, being associated with wrong view and the rest, the pleasure faculty included in the path becomes the object. And that very same [pleasure faculty] becomes the object of the wholesome consciousness to be abandoned by cultivation. And for the uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>), everything becomes the object. Therein, 'as applicable' — because latent afflictions (<s>anuśaya</s>) do not lie latent in the uncontaminated. Because only some lie latent in some [objects]. Therefore it is said 'as applicable.' Therein, in [that] consciousness, there are four groups (<s>nikāya</s>) of the Desire Realm. Namely: in [a consciousness] associated with wrong view that has the pleasure faculty as its object, all ten [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing suffering lie latent by way of object or by way of association, as applicable. Similarly, those to be abandoned by seeing origination. Those to be abandoned by seeing the path also lie latent therein, in the consciousness having the pleasure faculty as its object. For in a consciousness associated with wrong view and the rest that has the path-[included] pleasure faculty as its object, wrong view and the rest lie latent by way of association. Clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>) and the rest also lie latent by way of object. Therefore that group too lies latent therein. The group to be abandoned by cultivation also lies latent here — because of the connection of passion and the rest with having the consciousness that has the pleasure faculty as its object as their object. But the group to be abandoned by seeing cessation does not lie latent therein — because of the absence of a consciousness having the pleasure faculty as its object [in that category]. The Form Realm [afflictions] that have conditioned [phenomena] as objects: the pleasure faculty belonging to the Form Realm, being an object, is of five types. Therein, four groups lie latent — this is easily understood. But how do those to be abandoned by seeing cessation, which have conditioned [phenomena] as objects, lie latent? In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, clinging to views and the rest are associated with the pleasure faculty. And these have each other as objects. They lie latent in the consciousness having the pleasure faculty as its object, by way of association or by way of object. Two groups of the Formless Realm: the groups to be abandoned by seeing the path and by cultivation. In [a consciousness] associated with wrong view and the rest that has the path-[included] pleasure faculty as its object, wrong view and the rest lie latent by way of association. But clinging to views and the rest lie latent therein by way of object. The group to be abandoned by cultivation also lies latent — for the wholesome consciousness to be abandoned by cultivation takes the path as its object; therein that group of passion and the rest lies latent. And the universal (<s>sarvatraga</s>) Formless Realm latent afflictions lie latent in that very consciousness associated with wrong view and the rest that has the path as its object — this should be understood.

body.text: tasyaiva dvādaśavidhasyeti. kāmāvacarasya catuṣprakārasyānyatra nirodhadarśanaheyāt.
body.translated_text: Regarding that very twelvefold [consciousness]: [consisting of] the four types of the Desire Realm except for that to be abandoned by seeing cessation

body.text: rūpāvacarasya paṃcaprakārasyārūpyāvacarasya ca dviprakārasya mārgadarśanabhāvanāheyasyānāsravasya cety anyonyālaṃbanayogatas tasya sukhendriyālaṃbanaṃ vijñānam ālaṃbanaṃ bhavati. ārūpyāvacarasya ca bhūyo dviprakārasya tat sukhendriyālaṃbanaṃ vijñānam ālaṃbanaṃ bhavati. katamasyety āha. duḥkhasamudayadarśanaprahātavyasyeti. [Tib. 144a] ārūpyāvacarasya sarvatragasaṃprayuktasya hi duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyabhedāt dviprakārasya cittasyārūpyāvacaramārgadarśanaheyamithyādṛṣṭyādisaṃprayuktaṃ vijñānaṃ mārgālaṃbanaṃ cārūpyāvacaraṃ bhāvanāheyaṃ kuśalam ālaṃbanaṃ bhavati. evam idaṃ caturdaśavidhaṃ sukhendriyālaṃbanavijñānālaṃbanaṃ tatrārūpyāvacarau duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyau vardhayitveti. pūrvaṃ sarvatragā evārūpyāvacarāḥ sukhendriyālaṃbane vijñāne 'nuśerate. sukhendriyālaṃbanālaṃbane tu sakalāv apy ārūpyāvacarau duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyau nikāyāv anuśayāte. tasmāt tatra sarvatragasaṃprayukte citte duḥkhasaṃudayadarśanaheyā anuśayāḥ saṃprayogata ālaṃbanato vā yathāyogam anuśerate. śeṣās tu pūrvavad yojyāḥ.
body.translated_text: the five types of the Form Realm, the two types of the Formless Realm that are to be abandoned by seeing the path and by cultivation, and the uncontaminated — through the connection of mutual objectification, the consciousness having the pleasure faculty as its object becomes their object. And additionally, two types of the Formless Realm [take] that consciousness having the pleasure faculty as its object as their object. Of which [types]? — he says: those to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination. For the consciousness of the Formless Realm, which is of two types — to be abandoned by seeing suffering and to be abandoned by seeing origination — being associated with the universals (<s>sarvatraga</s>), [takes as its object] the consciousness associated with wrong view and the rest of the Formless Realm that has the path as its object, and the wholesome Formless Realm [consciousness] to be abandoned by cultivation. Thus this fourteenfold consciousness having the pleasure-faculty-object-consciousness as its object, having added two Formless Realm [groups] to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination. Previously, only the universal Formless Realm [afflictions] lay latent in the consciousness having the pleasure faculty as its object. But in the consciousness whose object is the pleasure-faculty-object [consciousness], both complete Formless Realm groups — to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination — lie latent. Therefore, therein, in the consciousness associated with the universals, the latent afflictions to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination lie latent by way of association or by way of object, as applicable. The rest should be connected as before.

body.text: anayā vartanyānyad api gaṃtavyam iti. anena vartmanānyad api boddhavyaṃ. kathaṃ. duḥkhendriyālaṃbane katy anuśayā anuśerata iti praśna āgate vicārayitavyaṃ. duḥkhendriyam ekavidhaṃ kāmāvacaraṃ bhāvanāprahātavyaṃ paṃcavijñānakāyikatvāt. tat samāsataḥ paṃcavidhasya vijñānasyālaṃbanaṃ bhavati. kāmāvacarasya [Tib. 144b] triprakārasya. duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyayoḥ sarvatragasaṃprayuktayor vijñānayor bhāvanāprahātavyasya ca. rūpāvacarasya ca bhāvanāprahātavyasya. anāsravasya ca. idaṃ paṃcavidhaṃ duḥkhendriyālaṃbanaṃ vijñānaṃ. tatra yathāsaṃbhavaṃ kāmāvacarās trayo nikāyā duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāheyāḥ. tatra hi sarvatragasaṃprayukte citte bhāvanāheye ca duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyau nikāyau saṃprayogata ālaṃbanato vā yathāsaṃbhavam anuśayāte. bhāvanāheye ca bhāvanāheyo nikāyo 'nuśete. rūpāvacara eko bhāvanāheyaḥ. tatra bhāvanāheye citte 'nuśete. sarvatragāś ca rūpāvacarās tatraivety avagaṃtavyaṃ. duḥkhendriyālaṃbanālaṃbane vijñāne katy anuśayā anuśerate. tat punar duḥkhendriyālaṃbanaṃ pañcavijñānaṃ katamasya vijñānasya ālaṃbanaṃ. tasyaiva paṃcavidhasyānyonyālaṃbanayogena. kāmāvacarasya ca bhūyo mārgadarśanaheyasya anāsravālaṃbanasya. rūpāvacarasya ca sarvatragasaṃprayuktasyālaṃbanaṃ bhavati. tena hi rūpāvacaraṃ duḥkhendriyālaṃbanaṃ kuśalaṃ bhāvanāprahātavyam
body.translated_text: 'By this method, other [cases] too should be understood' — by this procedure, other [cases] too should be comprehended. How? When the question arises: 'In the consciousness having the pain faculty (<s>duḥkhendriya</s>) as its object, how many latent afflictions lie latent?' — one should investigate. The pain faculty is of one kind — belonging to the Desire Realm, to be abandoned by cultivation, because of belonging to the five classes of consciousness (<s>pañcavijñānakāya</s>). That, in summary, becomes the object of fivefold consciousness. Of the Desire Realm, three types: the two [consciousnesses] associated with the universals, to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, and that to be abandoned by cultivation. And of the Form Realm, that to be abandoned by cultivation. And of the uncontaminated. This is the fivefold consciousness having the pain faculty as its object. Therein, as applicable, three groups of the Desire Realm — to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origination, and cultivation. For therein, in the consciousness associated with the universals and in that to be abandoned by cultivation, the two groups to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination lie latent by way of association or by way of object, as applicable. And in that to be abandoned by cultivation, the group to be abandoned by cultivation lies latent. One [group] of the Form Realm — to be abandoned by cultivation — lies latent therein, in the [Form Realm] consciousness to be abandoned by cultivation. And the universal Form Realm [afflictions] lie latent in that very [consciousness] — this should be understood. In the consciousness whose object is the pain-faculty-object [consciousness], how many latent afflictions lie latent? Now, that fivefold consciousness having the pain faculty as its object — of which consciousness is it the object? Of that very fivefold [consciousness], through the connection of mutual objectification. And additionally, of the Desire Realm [consciousness] to be abandoned by seeing the path, which has the uncontaminated as its object. And of the Form Realm [consciousness] associated with the universals, it becomes the object. For that [consciousness] takes as its object the Form Realm wholesome [consciousness] to be abandoned by cultivation, which has the pain faculty as its object

body.text: ālaṃbyate. ārūpyāvacaram apy ākāśānaṃtyāyatanasāmantakasaṃgṛhītaudārikādyākāraṃ [Tib. 145a] duḥkhendriyālaṃbanam ālaṃbate. tad idam aṣṭavidhaṃ duḥkhendriyālaṃbanālaṃbanaṃ vijñānaṃ. tatra kāmāvacarāś catvāro nikāyāḥ. duḥkhasamudayamārgadarśanabhāvanāheyāḥ. rūpāvacarās trayo nikāyāḥ. duḥkhasamudayadarśanabhāvanāprahātavyāḥ. ārūpyāvacara eko bhāvanāprahātavyaḥ. sarvatragāś cānuśayā anuśerata iti vijñātavyaṃ. saumanasyendriyālaṃbane vijñāne katy anuśayā anuśerata iti praśne vicārayitavyaṃ. tat punaḥ saumanasyendriyālaṃbanaṃ vijñānam ekādaśavidhaṃ. kāmarūpāvacaraṃ paṃca prakāram anāsravaṃ ceti. tad etat samāsatas trayodaśavidhasya vijñānasyālaṃbanaṃ bhavati. kāmāvacarasya paṃcaprakārasya saṃskṛtālaṃbanasya tasya saṃskṛtatvāt. evaṃ rūpāvacarasya. ārūpyāvacarasya tu dviprakārasya mārgadarśanabhāvanāheyasya. anāsravasya ca. idaṃ trayodaśavidhaṃ saumanasyendriyālaṃbanavijñānaṃ. tatra yathāsaṃbhavaṃ kāmāvacararūpāvacarāḥ paṃcanikāyāḥ saṃskṛtālaṃbanāḥ. ārūpyāvacarau dvau nikāyau. sarvatragāś cānuśayāḥ anuśerata iti vijñātavyaṃ. saumanasyendriyālaṃbanālaṃbane vijñāne katy anuśayā anuśerate. tat punaḥ saumanasyendriyālaṃbanaṃ [Tib. 145a] trayodaśavijñānaṃ katamasya vijñānasyālaṃbanaṃ. tasyaiva trayodaśavidhasya. ārūpyāvacarasya ca bhūyo dviprakārasya duḥkhasamudayadarśanaprahātavyasya. idaṃ paṃcadaśavidhaṃ saumanasyendriyālaṃbanaṃ vijñānaṃ. tatrārūpyāvacarau dvau duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyau vardhayitvā. kāmāvacararūpāvacarāḥ saṃskṛtālaṃbanāḥ. ārūpyāvacarāś catvāro nikāyāḥ anyatra nirodhadarśanaheyāt. anuśayā anuśerata iti vijñātavyaṃ. anayā diśā anyad api gaṃtavyam iti.
body.translated_text: And the Formless Realm [consciousness], included in the preliminary stage of the Infinity of Space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), having the aspects of coarseness and the rest, also takes the pain faculty as its object. This is the eightfold consciousness whose object is the pain-faculty-object [consciousness]. Therein, four groups of the Desire Realm — to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origination, the path, and cultivation. Three groups of the Form Realm — to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origination, and cultivation. One of the Formless Realm — to be abandoned by cultivation. And the universal latent afflictions lie latent — this should be understood. When the question [arises]: 'In the consciousness having the mental pleasure faculty (<s>saumanasyendriya</s>) as its object, how many latent afflictions lie latent?' — one should investigate. Now, the consciousness having the mental pleasure faculty as its object is of eleven kinds — belonging to the Desire Realm, the Form Realm, five types each, and the uncontaminated. That, in summary, becomes the object of thirteenfold consciousness. Of the Desire Realm, five types, because they have conditioned [phenomena] as objects, since that [mental pleasure faculty] is conditioned. Similarly of the Form Realm. But of the Formless Realm, two types — to be abandoned by seeing the path and by cultivation. And of the uncontaminated. This is the thirteenfold consciousness having the mental pleasure faculty as its object. Therein, as applicable, five groups each of the Desire Realm and Form Realm, because they have conditioned [phenomena] as objects. Two groups of the Formless Realm. And the universal latent afflictions lie latent — this should be understood. In the consciousness whose object is the mental-pleasure-faculty-object [consciousness], how many latent afflictions lie latent? Now, that thirteenfold consciousness having the mental pleasure faculty as its object — of which consciousness is it the object? Of that very thirteenfold [consciousness]. And additionally, of two more types of the Formless Realm — to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination. This is the fifteenfold consciousness having the mental pleasure faculty as its object. Therein, having added the two Formless Realm [groups] to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination: the Desire Realm and Form Realm [groups] have conditioned [phenomena] as objects. Four groups of the Formless Realm — except for that to be abandoned by seeing cessation. The latent afflictions lie latent — this should be understood. 'By this direction, other [cases] too should be understood.'

children.translated_text: 'In two ways, that which has latent [afflictions] is defiled' —

body.text: iti. anuśayānair ananuśayānaiś cānuśayaiḥ sānuśayaṃ kliṣṭam ity arthaḥ. tatsahitatvāt sadāvasthitatvāt. akliṣṭaṃ cittam anuśayānair eva sānuśayaṃ vivecayituṃ śakyatvāt. tathā hi vakṣyati
body.translated_text: the meaning is: that which has latent afflictions, [meaning] with latent and with non-latent afflictions, is defiled — because of being accompanied by them, because of [their] being always established. Undefiled consciousness is accompanied by latent [afflictions] alone — because it can be distinguished. For thus it will be stated:

children.translated_text: 'The affliction to be abandoned [relates to] the object and to its own nature' —

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: (V.33) sarvasya sarvānaṃtaram utpattisaṃbhavān nāsty eṣām utpattau sārvajanyaḥ kramaniyamaḥ. duḥkhataḥ skandhān apohyeti. nedaṃ duḥkham ity ātmato 'bhiniveśāt. rūpam ātmety evaṃdṛṣṭikasya vedanādyātmagrāhadṛṣṭiḥ
body.translated_text: (V.33) Because the arising of each [affliction] is possible immediately after any [other], there is no universal fixed order in their arising. '[One] removes the aggregates as suffering' — [meaning:] 'this is not suffering,' because of the attachment to self. For one who has the view 'form is the self,' the view grasping feeling and the rest as the self

body.text: pratyanīkā.
body.translated_text: is opposed [to it].

body.text: (V.34) aprahīṇo bhavaty aparijñāta iti. aprahīṇas tatprāptyanucchedāt. aparijñātas tatpratipakṣasya cānutpatteḥ. kāmarāgaparyavasthānīyā iti. paryavatiṣṭhate ebhir iti paryavasthānīyāḥ snānīyavat. kāmarāgasya paryavasthānīyā anukūlā iti. kāmarāga eva vā paryavasthānaṃ [Tib. 146a] kāmarāgaparyavasthānaṃ. tasmai hitāḥ kāmarāgaparyavasthānīyāḥ. te punā rūpādayo viṣayāḥ ābhāsagatā bhavaṃtīti. viṣayarūpatām āpannā bhavaṃtīty arthaḥ. tatra cāyoniśomanaskāra iti. tatra cābhāsagateṣu viṣayeṣu viparītaḥ samanaṃtarapratyaya ity arthaḥ. hetuviṣayaprayogabalānīti. hetubalaṃ kāmarāgotpattaye kāmarāgānuśayo 'prahīṇo bhavaty aparijñātaḥ. kāmarāgaparyavasthānīyā viṣayabalaṃ. tatra cāyoniśomanaskāraḥ prayogabalaṃ. evam anyo 'pi kleśa utpadyata iti. pratighānuśayo 'prahīṇo bhavaty aparijñātaḥ. pratighaparyavasthānīyā dharmā ābhāsagatā bhavaṃti. tatra cāyoniśomanaskāra ity eṣa nayaḥ.
body.translated_text: (V.34) 'It is unabandoned and uncomprehended.' Unabandoned because the acquisition of it has not been cut off. Uncomprehended because the counteragent to it has not yet arisen. '<s>Kāmarāgaparyavasthānīya</s>' — '<s>paryavasthānīya</s>' [means] 'that by which one is overwhelmed,' like <s>snānīya</s> ('that which is for bathing'). '<s>Kāmarāgaparyavasthānīya</s>' means 'favorable to sensual passion.' Or, sensual passion itself is the overwhelming (<s>paryavasthāna</s>), hence <s>kāmarāgaparyavasthāna</s>; that which is beneficial to it is <s>kāmarāgaparyavasthānīya</s>. 'Those objects of form and the rest come into appearance' — the meaning is: they come to assume the nature of objects. 'And therein, improper mental attention (<s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>)' — the meaning is: therein, in those objects that have come into appearance, a distorted immediately-preceding condition. 'The powers of cause, object, and application' — the power of cause for the arising of sensual passion is the unabandoned and uncomprehended latent disposition of sensual passion. The <s>kāmarāgaparyavasthānīya</s> [dharmas] are the power of object. And therein, improper mental attention is the power of application. 'Thus another affliction also arises' — the latent disposition of aversion is unabandoned and uncomprehended; the <s>dharma</s>s favorable to the overwhelming of aversion come into appearance; and therein, improper mental attention — this is the method.

body.text: (V.35-38) catvāro yogā eta eveti. kāmayogo bhavayogo dṛṣṭiyogo 'vidyāyogaś ceti.
body.translated_text: (V.35-38) 'The four bonds (<s>yoga</s>) are these very same' — the bond of sensual desire (<s>kāmayoga</s>), the bond of existence (<s>bhavayoga</s>), the bond of views (<s>dṛṣṭiyoga</s>), and the bond of ignorance (<s>avidyāyoga</s>).

body.text: avidyāsravasya pṛthaguktatvāt. saha paryavasthānair āhrīkyādibhir vakṣyamāṇaiḥ ekacatvāriṃśad dravyāṇi. ekatriṃśad anuśayā iti. dvādaśa dṛṣṭayaḥ. duḥkhadarśanaprahātvyā paṃca. samudayadarśanaprahātavye dve. nirodhadarśanaprahātavye dve eva. [Tib. 146b] tisro mārgadarśanaprahātavyāḥ. catasro vicikitsāḥ. paṃca rāgāḥ. evaṃ pratighā mānāś ca. daśa paryavasthānānīty evam ekacatvāriṃśat.
body.translated_text: because the outflow of ignorance (<s>avidyāsrava</s>) has been stated separately. Together with the wrappings (<s>paryavasthāna</s>) — shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and the rest, which will be described — there are forty-one substances. 'Thirty-one latent dispositions' — twelve views: five to be abandoned by seeing suffering, two to be abandoned by seeing the origin, two to be abandoned by seeing cessation, three to be abandoned by seeing the path. Four doubts. Five passions. Likewise aversions and prides. Ten wrappings — thus forty-one.

body.text: evakāraḥ paryavasthānanirāsārthaḥ. ṣaḍviṃśatir anuśayā iti. dvādaśa dṛṣṭayaś catasro vicikitsāḥ paṃca rāgāḥ paṃca mānā iti. nanu ca tatrāpy asti paryavasthānadvayam iti. tatra rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ.
body.translated_text: the word 'alone' is for the purpose of excluding the wrappings. 'Twenty-six latent dispositions' — twelve views, four doubts, five passions, five prides. 'But is there not also a pair of wrappings therein?' — therein, in the Form and Formless Realms.

children.translated_text: 'Torpor, restlessness, and intoxication — in the three realms' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. kasmād iha tasyāgrahaṇam iti. tasya paryavasthānadvayasya. asvātaṃtryād iti. katham asvātaṃtryaṃ. rāgādisaṃprayogitvād īrṣyādivad avidyāmātrāsaṃprayogitvāc ca. etad dhi dvayaṃ rāgādibhiḥ saṃprayujyate. na tathā īrṣyāmātsaryakaukṛtyakrodhamrakṣāḥ. svataṃtrāḥ. avidyāmātreṇa saṃprayogād iti. te hy ubhaye 'pīti. rūpārūpyāvacarā apīty arthaḥ. aṃtarmukhapravṛttā iti. na viṣayapradhānā ity arthaḥ. yenaiva ca kāraṇena bhavarāga ukta iti.
body.translated_text: from this statement. 'Why are they not included here?' — that pair of wrappings. 'Because of non-independence.' How is there non-independence? Because they are associated with passion and the rest, like envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) and the rest, and because they are not associated with ignorance alone. For this pair is associated with passion and the rest. But envy, miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>), regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), and concealment (<s>mrakṣa</s>) are not so — they are independent, because of being associated with ignorance alone. 'For both of these' — meaning: even those belonging to the Form and Formless Realms. 'Of inward-directed operation' — meaning: they are not predominantly oriented toward objects. 'And for the very reason that the passion for existence (<s>bhavarāga</s>) was stated' —

children.translated_text: 'Because of being inward-directed, it is done for the purpose of distinguishing from the notion of liberation in that [existence]' —

body.text: iti. anena ca bhavāsrava iti. avidyāsrava iti siddham iti. avidyā pūrvoktābhyām āsravābhyāṃ bahiṣkṛtā. tasmāt sā traidhātuky api avidyāsrava iti siddham etat. paṃcadaśadravyāṇīti. triṣv api dhātuṣv avidyāyāḥ pratyekaṃ paṃcaprakāratvāt. sarveṣāṃ teṣām iti. kāmāsravādīnāṃ saṃsārasya ca. ukto hy avidyā hetusaṃrāgāyetyādi.
body.translated_text: thus. 'And by this, the outflow of existence (<s>bhavāsrava</s>)' — 'the outflow of ignorance (<s>avidyāsrava</s>) is established' — thus. Ignorance is excluded from the two previously stated outflows. Therefore, even that [ignorance] belonging to the three realms is established as the outflow of ignorance. 'Fifteen substances' — because ignorance in each of the three realms is of five kinds each. 'Of all of them' — of sensual desire outflow and the rest, and of <s>saṃsāra</s>. For it was stated: 'ignorance is for the sake of generating attachment' and so forth.

children.text:
yāḥ kāścana durgatayaḥ asmin loke parata ca
avidyāmūlikāḥ sarvā icchālobhasamutthitā
children.translated_text:
'Whatever misfortunes there are in this world and the next,
all have ignorance as their root, arising from desire and greed' —

body.text: iti ca.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: iti. āsravā [Tib. 147a] evaughā yogāś ca bhavaṃti. kevalaṃ
body.translated_text: thus. The outflows themselves are floods (<s>ogha</s>) and bonds (<s>yoga</s>). Only —

body.text: katham iti vivriyate. kāmāsrava eva kāmaughaḥ kāmayogaś ca. evaṃ bhavāsrava eva bhavaugho bhavayogaś ca. avidyaughayogas tu pūrvavad evāvagaṃtavyaḥ. dṛṣṭiyoga iha caturtha uktaḥ. tenāha anyatra dṛṣṭibhya iti. tāḥ kileti. kilaśabdaḥ paramatadyotakaḥ. vineyajanavaśāt tu dṛṣṭiyogaḥ pṛthag ukta ity abhiprāyo yujyate. āsraveṣu dṛṣṭayaḥ kimarthaṃ na pṛthag sthāpitā ity āha.
body.translated_text: How — this is explained. The sensual-desire outflow itself is the sensual-desire flood and the sensual-desire bond. Similarly, the existence outflow itself is the existence flood and the existence bond. The flood and bond of ignorance should be understood as before. The view-bond is stated here as the fourth. Therefore he says 'except for views.' The word <s>kila</s> indicates the other's position. 'But the view-bond is stated separately because of [the needs of] those to be disciplined' — this intention is fitting. 'Why are views not separately established among the outflows?' — he says:

children.translated_text: 'For those without companions, not among the outflows' —

body.text: ityādi. asahāyānāṃ dṛṣṭīnām āsyānukūlatā avasthānānukūlatā calatvāt paṭutvāc ca na bhavati. nāsanānukūlatety arthaḥ. āseti rūpe prāpte āpiśaleṣṭyā āsyeti rūpaṃ bhavati. tad idam uktaṃ bhavati. yasmād etā dṛṣṭayo 'sahāyā nāsanānukūlāḥ sasahāyās tv āsanānukūlā bhavaṃti. tasmāt sasahāyā evaitā āsraveṣūktāḥ. miśrīkṛtyoktā ity arthaḥ. kimartham ity āha. āsayaṃtīty āsravāṇāṃ nirvacanaṃ paścād vakṣyatīty ata āsanārtham āsraveṣu bhavitavyam ity abhiprāyaḥ. tad evaṃ kāmaugha ekānnatriṃśad dravyāṇīti. dvādaśadṛṣṭyapanayanān nāsravavad ekacatvāriṃśad dravyāṇi bhavaṃti. kiṃ tarhy ekānnatriṃśad dravyāṇi bhavaṃti. katham ity āha. rāgapratighamānā iti sarvaṃ. bhavaugho [Tib. 147b] 'ṣṭāviṃśatir dravyāṇīti. bhavāsravo dvāpaṃcāśad dravyāṇy uktāni. tataś caturviṃśatir dṛṣṭīr apanīyāṣṭāviṃśatir dravyāṇi. rāgamānā viṃśatir iti dvidhātukā rāgā daśa bhavaṃti. mānā api daśeti viṃśatiḥ. dṛṣṭyoghaḥ
body.translated_text: and so forth. For views without companions, the suitability for sitting (<s>āsya</s>) — the suitability for remaining — does not exist, because of instability and sharpness. The meaning is: they are not suitable for sitting. The form <s>āsya</s> is derived — when the form <s>āse</s> is expected, by the <s>Āpiśali</s> rule, the form <s>āsya</s> comes about. This is what is stated: since these views, being without companions, are not suitable for sitting, but with companions are suitable for sitting — therefore they are stated among the outflows only with companions — meaning: stated in mixed form. Why? — he says. 'They flow out (<s>āsravanti</s>)' — the etymological analysis of 'outflows' (<s>āsrava</s>) will be stated later, therefore there must be sitting among the outflows — this is the intent. Thus, the sensual-desire flood is twenty-nine substances — by removing the twelve views, it does not become forty-one substances like the outflow. Rather, it becomes twenty-nine substances. How? — he says: 'passions, aversions, and prides' — and so forth. The existence flood is twenty-eight substances — the existence outflow was stated as fifty-two substances; removing the twenty-four views from that, there are twenty-eight substances. 'Passions and prides are twenty' — passions belonging to two realms are ten; prides also are ten — thus twenty. The view-flood

body.text: ṣaṭtriṃśad dravyāṇīti. triṣu dhātuṣu tridvādaśa dṛṣṭaya iti. avidyaughaḥ paṃcadaśa dravyāṇi. pūrvavat. oghavad yogā iti. kāmayoga ekānnatriṃśad dravyāṇi. rāgapratighamānāḥ paṃcadaśa vicikitsāś catasraḥ daśa paryavasthānānīti. bhavayogo 'ṣṭāviṃśatir dravyāṇi. rāgamānā viṃśatiḥ vicikitsā aṣṭau dṛṣṭiyogaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśad dravyāṇi. avidyāyogaḥ paṃcadaśa dravyāṇi.
body.translated_text: is thirty-six substances — in the three realms, three times twelve views. The ignorance-flood is fifteen substances — as before. 'The bonds are like the floods' — the sensual-desire bond is twenty-nine substances: passions, aversions, and prides are fifteen; doubts are four; wrappings are ten. The existence-bond is twenty-eight substances: passions and prides are twenty; doubts are eight. The view-bond is thirty-six substances. The ignorance-bond is fifteen substances.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. ke yathoktāḥ. yogā ity adhikṛtaṃ tasmād vivriyate. kāmayoga eva sahāvidyayā kāmopādānam iti. avidyā kāmopādānātmavādopādānayor yathāsvam aṃtarbhāvyate.
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. Which 'very same'? — 'bonds' is the governing [word], therefore it is explained: the sensual-desire bond itself, together with ignorance, is the clinging of sensual desire (<s>kāmopādāna</s>). Ignorance is included in the clingings of sensual desire and of self-doctrine (<s>ātmavādopādāna</s>), each respectively.

body.text: pṛthakkaraṇāc catuṣṭvaṃ. kāmopādānaṃ dṛṣṭyupādānaṃ śīlavratopādānam ātmavādopādānam iti. dṛṣṭiyogāc chīlavrataṃ niṣkṛṣyeti. ṣaṭtriṃśaddravyakād dṛṣṭiyogāt dhātubhedena ṣacchīlavrataparāmarśān niṣkṛṣya. dṛṣṭyupādānaṃ triṃśad dravyāṇi. śīlavratopādānaṃ ṣaḍ dravyāṇi kāmadhātau dve evaṃ rūpadhātāv [Tib. 148a] ārūpyadhātau ceti. mārgapratidvaṃdvād iti. sāṃkhyayogajñānādibhir mokṣaprāptidarśanān mārgapratidvaṃdvabhūtaṃ śīlavratopādānaṃ. ubhagapakṣavipralaṃbhanāc ceti vistaraḥ. gṛhipravrajitapakṣavipralaṃbhanāc cety arthaḥ. anaśanādibhir iti. ādiśabdena jalāgniprapatanamaunavīrādānādir gṛhyate. anaśanādīni śīlavratasaṃgṛhītānīṣṭaviṣayaparivarjanaṃ ca. iṣṭaviṣayaparivarjaneneti. rasaparityāgabhūmiśayyāmalapaṃkadhāraṇanagnacaryākeśolluṃcanādinā śuddhipratyāgamanāt.
body.translated_text: by separating, the fourfold [classification arises]: the clinging of sensual desire (<s>kāmopādāna</s>), the clinging of views (<s>dṛṣṭyupādāna</s>), the clinging of rules and rituals (<s>śīlavratopādāna</s>), and the clinging of self-doctrine (<s>ātmavādopādāna</s>). 'From the thirty-six-substance view-bond, extracting the clinging to rules and rituals by division of realms' — extracting the six clingings to rules and rituals from the view-bond of thirty-six substances [divided] by realm. The clinging of views is thirty substances. The clinging of rules and rituals is six substances — two in the Desire Realm, similarly in the Form Realm and Formless Realm. 'Because of being an adversary of the path' — because of seeing the attainment of liberation through <s>Sāṃkhya</s>-yoga knowledge and the like, the clinging to rules and rituals is an adversary of the path. 'And because of deceiving both sides' — and so forth in detail. Because of deceiving the sides of householders and renunciants — this is the meaning. 'Through fasting and the rest' — by the word 'and the rest,' entering into water, fire, leaping [from heights], silence, heroic postures, and so forth are included. Fasting and the rest are included in rules and rituals, as well as abstention from desired objects. 'Through the abstention from desired objects' — through the relinquishing of flavors, lying on the ground, wearing mud and dirt, going naked, pulling out hair, and the like — because of the coming-back of purification [through such practices].

children.translated_text: 'But ignorance is not a grasper, [so] it is mixed' —

body.text: na kevalāvidyā bhavam upādadāti. kasmād ity āha. asaṃprakhyānalakṣaṇatayā apaṭutvād iti. miśritā tv anyakleśasaṃparkavaśād upādadātīty abhiprāyaḥ. etaḥ kileti. kilaśabdaḥ paramatadyotakaḥ. tena svamatam ucyate. sūtre tu bhagavatoktam iti vistareṇa. evaṃ yāvad dṛṣṭiyoga iti. kathaṃ. dṛṣṭiyogaḥ katamaḥ. vistareṇa yāvad yo 'sya bhavati dṛṣṭiṣu dṛṣṭirāgo dṛṣṭicchando dṛṣṭisneha iti pūrvavat. chandarāgaś copādānam uktaṃ sūtrāṃtareṣu. katham. upādānaṃ katamat. yo 'tra chandarāga iti. etad ācāryamataṃ. tad uktaṃ bhavati rāga evātra yogaḥ. [Tib. 148b] upādānaṃ vā. nānye kleśā iti. tenocyate kāmādiṣu yaś chandarāga iti.
body.translated_text: ignorance alone does not cling to existence. Why? — he says: because of being dull, having the characteristic of non-comprehension (<s>asaṃprakhyāna</s>). But mixed — the intent is: through contact with other afflictions, it clings. 'These, <s>kila</s>' — the word <s>kila</s> indicates the other's position; thereby his own position is stated. 'But in the <s>sūtra</s>, the Blessed One said' — and so forth in detail. 'Thus up to the view-bond' — how? 'What is the view-bond? In detail, up to: whatever passion for views, desire for views, affection for views that he has' — as before. And desire-attachment (<s>chandarāga</s>) is stated as clinging in other <s>sūtra</s>s. How? 'What is clinging? Whatever desire-attachment (<s>chandarāga</s>) therein.' This is the <s>Ācārya</s>'s position. This is what is stated: it is passion alone that is the bond here, or clinging — not other afflictions. Therefore it is said: 'whatever desire-attachment in sensual desires and the rest.'

body.text: iti vistareṇa. aṇavaḥ śerate ity anuśayāḥ. nairuktena vidhināsya siddhiḥ.
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. They are subtle and they lie dormant (<s>śerate</s>) — therefore [they are called] latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>). This is established by the etymological method (<s>nairuktena vidhinā</s>).

body.text: sūkṣmapracāratvād iti. sūkṣmapravṛttitvād ity arthaḥ. kathaṃ punaḥ sūkṣmā pravṛttiḥ. arūpiṇāṃ durvijñānatayā. ālaṃbanataś chidrānveṣiśatruvat dṛṣṭiviṣavac ca. saṃprayogato 'yoguḍodakasaṃtāpavat sparśaviṣavac ca. ubhayato dhātryaḥ kumārakam anuśerate. evam ete 'py ālaṃbanāt saṃprayuktebhyo vā svām saṃtatiṃ vardhayaṃtaḥ prāptibhir upaciṃvaṃti. anubadhnaṃtīti. anukrānteś cāturthakajvaravan mūṣikāviṣavac cety anye. aprayogeṇa anābhogena. pratinivārayato 'pi niṣedhayato 'pi pudgalasya punaḥpunaḥ saṃmukhībhāvād anubadhnaṃty ato 'nuśayā iti. āsayaṃti saṃsāra ity āsravā iti. nairukto vidhiḥ. āsanārtho vā. āsravaṃti bhavāgrād yāvad avīcim iti. ṣaḍbhir āyatanavraṇaiś cakṣurādibhir āyatanair vraṇabhūtair āsravaṃti kṣaraṃti. bhavāgrād yāvad avīciṃ gacchaṃti. bhavāgrāvītarāgasyāpy āvīcikakleśasamudācārāt tadutpannasya vā tatrotpattisaṃbhavāt. ka āsravaṃti. anuśayāḥ. āsravaṃtīty āsravā ity acpratyayaḥ. haraṃtīty oghāḥ. śleśayantīti yogāḥ. upagṛhṇaṃtīty upādānānīty arthapradarśanam. etad uktaṃ vaibhāṣikaiḥ. vahana etad rūpam oghā iti. vahaṃti haraṃti gatyaṃtaraṃ viṣayāṃtaraṃ veti oghāḥ. yojayaṃti śleṣayaṃti gatyantare viṣayāṃtare veti yogāḥ. upādadaty upagṛhṇaṃti punarbhave kāmādiṣu vā vijñānasaṃtatiṃ ity upādānānīti. evaṃ tu sādhīyaḥ syād iti. evaṃ tu sādhutaraṃ syād ity ācāryaḥ.
