[Tib. 149a] katham ity āha. āsravati gacchaty ebhir anuśayaiḥ saṃtatir vijñānasaṃtatir viṣayeṣv ity āsravāḥ. karaṇasādhanaṃ. mahatābhisaṃskāreṇa kuśalair dharmaiś cittasaṃtānaḥ pratisroto nīyate viṣayebhyo nivāryate. teṣām eva saṃskārāṇāṃ pratipraśrabdhyeti. teṣām eva prayatnānāṃ vyuparameṇety arthaḥ. adhimātravegatvād oghā iti. oghasādharmyaṃ darśayati. ogha ivaughā iti kṛtvā. tadanuvidhānād iti. rāgādyanuvidhānāt. nādhimātrasamudācāriṇo hi yogā iti. oghayogānāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ darśayati. ye hi nādhimātrasamudācāriṇaḥ. te yogāḥ. ye tv adhimātrasamudācāriṇa eva. ta oghā iti. kathaṃ ca te yogā ity āha. vividhaduḥkhayojanāj jātyādibhir vividhair duḥkhair yojanād ity arthaḥ. abhīkṣṇānuṣaṃgato vā. yasmād vā saṃtatāv abhīkṣṇaṃ yujyaṃte. tasmād yogā iti. kāmādyupādānād iti. yaiḥ kāmādayaḥ upādīyaṃte. tāni kāmādyupādānāni chandarāgātmakāni.
body.translated_text: 'Because of subtle operation' — meaning: because of subtle functioning. How then is the operation subtle? Because the formless [afflictions] are difficult to discern. From the side of their object — like an enemy seeking an opening, and like eye-poison. From the side of their association — like the heat of water mixed with [raw] sugar, and like contact-poison. From both sides — just as nurses tend to a child while it sleeps, so too these [latent dispositions], through their object or through their associates, nourish their own continuum and augment [it] through acquisitions (<s>prāpti</s>). 'They pursue' (<s>anubadhnanti</s>) — others [say]: like a quartan fever and like rat-poison, because of persisting. Without effort, without deliberate attention — even when the person tries to ward off and restrain [them], because of repeatedly coming face to face, they pursue — therefore they are 'latent dispositions' (<s>anuśaya</s>). 'They flow into <s>saṃsāra</s>, therefore <s>āsrava</s>s (outflows)' — this is the etymological method. Or in the sense of 'seat' (<s>āsana</s>). 'They flow out from the peak of existence down to <s>Avīci</s>' — through the six sense-base wounds — through the sense-bases such as the eye and the rest, being like wounds, they flow out, they leak. They go from the peak of existence down to <s>Avīci</s> — because even for one not dispassionate from the peak of existence, afflictions of the <s>Avīci</s> [hell] become active, or because one born there can be born in <s>Avīci</s>. What flows? The latent dispositions. 'They flow' — therefore '<s>āsrava</s>s' — with the <s>ac</s> suffix. 'They carry away' — therefore 'floods' (<s>ogha</s>). 'They bind' — therefore 'bonds' (<s>yoga</s>). 'They seize' — therefore 'clingings' (<s>upādāna</s>) — this is a demonstration of meaning. This is stated by the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s: their nature is carrying — therefore 'floods.' They carry and sweep away to another destiny or another object — therefore floods. They yoke and bind to another destiny or another object — therefore bonds. They seize and grasp the consciousness-continuum in renewed existence or in sense-objects such as the objects of desire — therefore clingings. 'But thus it would be more fitting' — 'but thus it would be more proper' — says the <s>Ācārya</s>. [Tib. 149a] How? He says: the continuum — the consciousness-continuum — flows, goes, through these latent dispositions into objects — therefore '<s>āsrava</s>s' — an instrumental derivation. Through great effort, through wholesome <s>dharma</s>s, the mental continuum is led against the current, is diverted from objects. 'Through the subsiding of those very formations' — meaning: through the cessation of those very efforts. 'Because of having intense velocity, [they are called] floods' — he shows the similarity to a flood. Considering: like a flood, therefore floods. 'Because of conformity to those' — because of conformity to passion and the rest. 'For bonds are not [those] operating with intense [force]' — he shows the difference between floods and bonds. Those that do not operate with intense [force] — they are bonds. But those that operate with intense [force] only — they are floods. And how are they bonds? He says: 'Because of yoking to various sufferings' — meaning: because of yoking to various sufferings such as birth and the rest. 'Or because of frequent attachment' — or because they are frequently yoked to one's continuum — therefore bonds. 'Because of clinging to desire and the rest' — those by which desire and the rest are clung to — those are clingings to desire and the rest, having the nature of attachment-desire (<s>chandarāga</s>).

body.text: (V.40ab) ta evānuśayāḥ punar yāvat paryavasthānabhedena paṃcadhā bhittvoktā iti. ta evānuśayā āsravādibhedena caturdhoktāḥ. saṃyojanabaṃdhanānuśayopakleśaparyavasthānabhedena [Tib. 149b] punaḥ paṃcadhā bhittvoktāḥ sūtre 'bhidharme ca. nanu cānuśayavyatiriktāny āhrīkyādīni paryavasthānāni nirdiśyaṃte. katham idam ucyate. anuśayā eva paryavasthānānīti. satyaṃ bhavaṃti tadvyatiriktāni. avyatiriktāny api tv iṣyante. tathā hi vakṣyati. kleśo 'pi hi haryavasthānaṃ. kāmarāgaparyavasthānapratyayaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratisaṃvedayata iti sūtre vacanād iti.
body.translated_text: (V.40ab) 'Those very latent dispositions, again, divided fivefold through the division of fetters, bonds, latent dispositions, secondary afflictions, and engulfments' — those very latent dispositions, stated fourfold as outflows and the rest, are stated again divided fivefold through the divisions of fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), bonds (<s>bandhana</s>), latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>), secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>), and engulfments (<s>paryavasthāna</s>) [Tib. 149b] in the <s>sūtra</s>s and <s>Abhidharma</s>. But are not shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and the rest taught as engulfments distinct from the latent dispositions? How then is it said that the latent dispositions themselves are the engulfments? True, there are those distinct from them. But those not distinct are also accepted. For thus it will be stated: 'An affliction too is an engulfment.' Because of the statement in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'One experiences suffering caused by the engulfment of sensual passion.'

body.text: (V.40cd-42) evam anyāny api yathāsaṃbhavaṃ yojyānīti. pratigherṣyāmātsaryasaṃyojanāni kāmāvacarāṇi. mānāvidyādṛṣṭiparāmarśavicikitsāsaṃyojanāni traidhātukāni. dṛṣṭisaṃyojanaṃ tisro dṛṣṭaya iti. satkāyāṃtagrāhamithyādṛṣṭayaḥ. parāmarśasaṃyojanaṃ dve dṛṣṭī iti. dṛṣṭiśīlavrataśīlavrataparāmarśau. ata evocyata iti. yata eva tisro dṛṣṭayo dṛṣṭisaṃyojanaṃ dve dṛṣṭī parāmarśasaṃyojanam. ata evocyate. syād dṛṣṭisaṃprayukteṣv iti vistareṇa praśnaḥ. dṛṣṭisaṃprayukteṣv iti. parāmarśadṛṣṭisaṃprayukteṣu vedanādiṣu. anunayasaṃyojanena saṃyukto rāgeṇa. na dṛṣṭisaṃyojanena satkāyadṛṣṭyādilakṣaṇena. na ca tatra dṛṣṭyanuśayo nānuśayīteti. na ca tatra dṛṣṭisaṃprayukteṣu dharmeṣu dṛṣṭyanuśayo nānuśayīta. [Tib. 150a] kiṃ tarhi. anuśayīta. dviḥ pratiṣedhaḥ prakṛtiṃ gamayati. āha syād iti vistareṇa praśnavisarjanaṃ. samudayajñāna utpanna iti viśeṣaṇaṃ sarvatragadṛṣṭisaṃyojanaprahāṇasaṃdarśānarthaṃ. nirodhajñāne 'nutpanna iti. parāmarśadṛṣṭidvayāprahāṇena tatsaṃprayogasattāpradarśanārthaṃ. nirodhamārgadarśanaprahātavyeṣu yāvaddharmeṣv iti. vedanādiṣu. teṣu hy anunayasaṃyojanena nirodhadarśanaheyena mārgadarśanaheyena vā saṃyuktaḥ. kīdṛśena. tadālaṃbanena. yasmād asāv etān nirodhadarśanamārgaprahātavyān dṛṣṭiparāmarśaśīlavrataparāmarśasaṃprayuktān vedanādidharmān ālaṃbya rāga utpadyate. tasmād ālaṃbanatas tena saṃyuktaḥ. dṛṣṭisaṃyojanenāsaṃyuktaḥ. kasmād ity āha. sarvatragasya duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyasvabhāvasya samudayajñānotpatteḥ prahīṇatvāt. asarvatragasya ca tadālaṃbanasaṃprayogiṇo dṛṣṭisaṃyojanasyābhāvād iti. yady api hy asarvatragaṃ mithyādṛṣṭisvabhāvaṃ nirodhamārgadarśanaprahātavyaṃ dṛṣṭisaṃyojanam asti. na tu tat parāmarśadṛṣṭisaṃprayuktavedanādidharmālaṃbanam. anāsravālaṃbanatvāt. tasmān nālambanato [Tib. 150b] dṛṣṭisaṃyojanena saṃyuktaḥ. na cāpi tat tair vedanādibhiḥ saṃprayogi. tatpṛthakkalāpatvāt.
body.translated_text: (V.40cd-42) 'Similarly, the others too should be connected as applicable.' The fetters of aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), and miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>) belong to the Desire Realm. The fetters of pride (<s>māna</s>), ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), clinging (<s>parāmarśa</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>) belong to all three realms. 'The view-fetter is three views' — the views of the self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), extreme view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), and wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>). 'The clinging-fetter is two views' — the clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>) and the clinging to morality and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>). 'For this very reason it is stated' — since three views are the view-fetter and two views are the clinging-fetter, for this very reason it is stated: 'There might be, in those associated with view' — and so forth in detail, the question. 'In those associated with view' — in feelings and the rest that are associated with the clinging-views (<s>parāmarśadṛṣṭi</s>). Bound by the attraction-fetter (<s>anunayasaṃyojana</s>) — by passion. Not by the view-fetter characterized by the view of the self-existing body and the rest. 'And the view-latent disposition does not lie latent therein' — and the view-latent disposition does not lie latent in those <s>dharma</s>s associated with view. [Tib. 150a] What then? It does lie latent. The double negation conveys the affirmative. He says 'there might be' — and so forth in detail, the question and answer. 'When the knowledge of origination has arisen' — this qualification is for the purpose of showing the abandonment of the universal view-fetter. 'When the knowledge of cessation has not arisen' — for the purpose of showing the existence of the association of the two clinging-views, [because of] the non-abandonment of the two clinging-views. 'In <s>dharma</s>s to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path' — in feelings and the rest. For in those one is bound by the attraction-fetter to be abandoned by seeing cessation or by seeing the path. Of what kind? Having those as its object. Because that passion arises taking as its object those <s>dharma</s>s — feelings and the rest — to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path, which are associated with the clinging to views and the clinging to morality and rituals. Therefore, from the side of the object, one is bound by that [attraction-fetter]. Not bound by the view-fetter. Why? He says: because the universal [view-fetter], having the intrinsic nature of [what is] to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, has been abandoned through the arising of the knowledge of origination. And because there is no non-universal view-fetter having those as object and being associated with them. For even though a non-universal wrong view having the intrinsic nature of [what is] to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path — a view-fetter — exists, it does not take as its object the feelings and other <s>dharma</s>s associated with clinging-views — because it takes outflow-free [dharmas] as its object. Therefore, [Tib. 150b] one is not bound by the view-fetter from the side of the object either. Nor is it associated with those feelings and the rest — because of belonging to a different aggregate (<s>kalāpa</s>).

body.text: tasmāt saṃprayogato 'pi na tena saṃyuktaḥ. dṛṣṭyanuśayaś ca teṣv anuśete. kīdṛśas sa ity āha. te eva parāmarśadṛṣṭī saṃprayogata iti. dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśo vā teṣu vedanādiṣu dharmeṣu saṃprayogato 'nuśete. svakalāpasaṃbhūtatvāt. na ca tatra dṛṣṭisaṃyojanam anuśete. tayor dṛṣṭisaṃyojanam ity asaṃjñitavān na dṛṣṭyanuśayagrahaṇe paṃcadṛṣṭigrahaṇam bhavati. dṛṣṭisaṃyojanagrahaṇe tu satkāyāṃtagrāhamithyādṛṣṭīnām eva grahaṇaṃ. na parāmarśadṛṣṭyor ity avagaṃtavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: Therefore, one is not bound by it from the side of association either. 'And the view-latent disposition lies latent therein' — of what kind is that? He says: 'Those very two clinging-views, from the side of association.' The clinging to views or the clinging to morality and rituals lies latent in those <s>dharma</s>s — feelings and the rest — from the side of association — because of belonging to the same aggregate. But the view-fetter does not lie latent therein. 'Not having designated those two [clinging-views] as the view-fetter' — in the grasping of 'view-latent disposition,' the grasping of all five views occurs. But in the grasping of 'view-fetter,' only the grasping of the views of the self-existing body, extreme view, and wrong view occurs — not of the two clinging-views — this should be understood.

body.text: iti. parāmarśadṛṣṭī. aṣṭādaśa dravyāṇi tisro dṛṣṭayo bhavaṃtīti vākyaśeṣaḥ. aṣṭādaśasaṃkhyeyadravyāḥ satkāyāṃtagrāhamithyādṛṣṭaya iti vākyārthaḥ. aṣṭādaśaiva dravyāṇīti prakṛtaṃ. dve parāmarśadṛṣṭī bhavaṃti. kathaṃ. kāmadhātau satkāyāṃtagrāhadṛṣṭī dve. te ca duḥkhadarśanaprahātavye eveṣṭe. mithyādṛṣṭiś catuḥprakārāḥ. duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyā yāvan mārgadarśanaprahātavyā. ity evaṃ kāmadhātau ṣaḍ bhavaṃti. yathā kāmadhātau ṣaḍ evaṃ rūpadhātāv ārūpyadhātau [Tib. 151a] cety aṣṭādaśa bhavaṃti. aṣṭādaśaiva dve parāmarśadṛṣṭī. kathaṃ. kāmadhātau dṛṣṭiparāmarśo duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyo yāvan mārgadarśanaprahātavya iti catuḥprakārāḥ. śīavrataparāmarśo 'pi duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyaḥ. mārgadarśanaprahātavyaś ceti dviprakāraḥ. ity evaṃ kāmadhātau ṣaḍ bhavaṃti. yathā kāmadhātāv evaṃ rūpadhātāv ārūpyadhātau ca. ity evam aṣṭādaśaiva dravyāṇi bhavaṃti. na śeṣā iti dṛṣṭayaḥ. grāhyagrāhakabhedād iti. dṛṣṭisaṃyojanaṃ grāhyaṃ. parāmarśasaṃyojanaṃ grāhakam iti. yata iti. yataḥ kāraṇāt. ekāṃtākuśalatvasvātaṃtryalakṣaṇāt.
body.translated_text: meaning: the two clinging-views. 'Eighteen substances (<s>dravya</s>) are the three views' — this is the remainder of the sentence. The sentence-meaning is: the views of the self-existing body, extreme view, and wrong view have eighteen countable substances. 'Eighteen substances only' — this is the topic. 'Are the two clinging-views.' How? In the Desire Realm, the views of the self-existing body and extreme view are two — and they are accepted as to be abandoned by seeing suffering only. Wrong view is fourfold — to be abandoned by seeing suffering up to to be abandoned by seeing the path. Thus in the Desire Realm, six exist. As in the Desire Realm, six, so too in the Form Realm and in the Formless Realm [Tib. 151a] — thus eighteen exist. 'Eighteen only are the two clinging-views.' How? In the Desire Realm, the clinging to views is fourfold — to be abandoned by seeing suffering up to to be abandoned by seeing the path. The clinging to morality and rituals is twofold — to be abandoned by seeing suffering and to be abandoned by seeing the path. Thus in the Desire Realm, six exist. As in the Desire Realm, so in the Form and Formless Realms — thus eighteen substances exist. 'The remaining are not views.' 'Because of the distinction of what is grasped and what grasps' — the view-fetter is what is grasped; the clinging-fetter is what grasps. 'Because' — because of the reason — characterized by being invariably unwholesome and autonomous.

body.text: iti. eṣv āhrīkyādiṣu paryavasthāneṣu niṣkṛṣyobhayam
body.translated_text: among these engulfments beginning with shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>). 'Having extracted both' —

body.text: uktaṃ. na hy anyat paryavasthānam evaṃjātīyakam iti. anāhrīkyānapatrāpyam apy ekāṃtākuśalaṃ. na tu svataṃtraṃ rāgādikleśasaṃprayogāt. kaukṛtyam api svataṃtram avidyāmātrasaṃprayogāt. na tv ekāṃtākuśalaṃ. tad dhi kuśalam api. styānauddhatyamiddhāny apy asvataṃtrāṇi rāgādisaṃprayogāt. [Tib. 151b] na tv ekāṃtākuśalāni. kuśalavyākṛtāny api hi tāni bhavaṃti. yatraitad ubhayam iti. yatraikāṃtākuśalatvaṃ ca svātaṃtryaṃ cety etad ubhayaṃ syāt. tad evaṃjātīyakam anyat paryavasthānaṃ nāstīty abhisaṃbandhaḥ.
body.translated_text: are stated [as fetters]. For there is no other engulfment of this kind. Shamelessness (<s>anāhrīkya</s>) and lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>) are also invariably unwholesome — but not autonomous, because of being associated with the afflictions of passion and the rest. Regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) too is autonomous, because of being associated with ignorance alone — but not invariably unwholesome, for it can also be wholesome. Torpor (<s>styāna</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), and drowsiness (<s>middha</s>) too are not autonomous, because of being associated with passion and the rest. [Tib. 151b] Nor are they invariably unwholesome, for they can also be wholesome and indeterminate. 'Where this twofold [quality exists]' — where both invariable unwholesomeness and autonomy exist — there is no other engulfment of such a kind — this is the connection.

body.text: yasya punar daśeti. yasya vaibhāṣikasya daśa paryavasthānāni. tasya krodhamrakṣāv apy ubhayaprakārāv ekāṃtākuśalau svataṃtrau ceti. tasmān na bhavaty ayaṃ parihāra iti. kas tarhi parihāras tasya iti. atrācāryasaṃghabhadra āha. abhīkṣṇasamudācāritvād īrṣyāmātsaryayoḥ pṛthaksaṃyojanam iti. ata eva ca ṣaṭtriṃśatsaṃyojanatve 'pi kāmadhātūpapannānāṃ īrṣyāmātsaryasaṃyojanāḥ kauśika devamanuṣyā ity uktam. ādhikyena hi sugatāv etat kleśadvayaṃ bandhanam iti. atha vā.
body.translated_text: 'But for one who [holds] ten' — for the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> who [holds] ten engulfments — for him, anger (<s>krodha</s>) and resentment (<s>mrakṣa</s>) are also of both kinds — invariably unwholesome and autonomous. 'Therefore this defense does not hold.' What then is his defense? Here <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> says: 'Because of frequently becoming active, envy and miserliness are [stated as] separate fetters.' And for this very reason, even in the thirty-six classification of fetters, it was stated: 'The fetters of envy and miserliness, O <s>Kauśika</s>, [bind] gods and humans.' For this pair of afflictions is a bond predominantly in a good destiny. Alternatively:

children.text:
alpeśākhyālpabhogakāraṇatvāt sarvasūcanāt
dvipakṣasaṃkleśatvāc ca. mātsaryerṣye pṛthak kṛte.
children.translated_text:
'Because of causing little authority and few enjoyments, because of indicating all [secondary afflictions],
and because of afflicting both sides — envy and miserliness are made separate.'

body.text: yad ayaṃ sugatāv apy upapannaḥ pragāḍhaṃ paribhavam udvahati. tatrerṣyāmātsarye kāraṇaṃ. tathā hy
body.translated_text: That one born even in a good destiny bears deep humiliation — therein envy and miserliness are the cause. For thus:

children.text: alpeśākhyo 'lpabhogaś ca bandhanāv apy ubhayān mata
children.translated_text: 'One of little authority and few enjoyments — both bonds are considered [the cause]' —

body.text: iti. dvividhāś copakleśāḥ saṃtāpasahagatāḥ. āmodasahagatāś ca. ta ābhyāṃ sarve sūcitā bhavaṃti. gṛhipakṣaś cābhyāṃ bhogādhiṣṭhānābhyām atīva kliśyate. pravrajitapakṣo 'pi dharmādhiṣṭhānābhyāṃ. devāsurapakṣau vā bhinnodarahetor atyarthaṃ kliśyataḥ. ata evoktaṃ bhagavatā. īrṣyāmātsaryasaṃyojanāḥ kauśika devamanuṣyā iti. [Tib. 152a] tasmād daśabhyaḥ paryavasthānebhya etad eva dvayaṃ saṃyojanam iti.
body.translated_text: thus. And secondary afflictions are of two kinds: accompanied by distress, and accompanied by delight. All of those are indicated by these two [envy and miserliness]. The householder's side is exceedingly afflicted by these two, which are based on possessions. The renunciant's side too [is afflicted] by those based on <s>Dharma</s>. Or the sides of gods and <s>asura</s>s are exceedingly afflicted because of the cause of divided bellies. For this very reason the Blessed One stated: 'The fetters of envy and miserliness, O <s>Kauśika</s>, [bind] gods and humans.' [Tib. 152a] Therefore, from among the ten engulfments, this pair alone is a fetter.

body.text: (V.43-44) avaro hi bhāgaḥ kāmadhātur iti. traidhātukasamudāyāpekṣayā kāmadhātur avaro nihīno dhātur ekāṃtasamāhitatvāt. akuśaladharmāpāyagatiduḥkhadaurmanasyasadbhāvāt. ghanakleśatvāc ca.
body.translated_text: (V.43-44) 'For the lower portion is the Desire Realm' — with respect to the aggregate of the three realms, the Desire Realm is the lower, inferior realm — because of not being invariably concentrated. Because of the existence of unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s, lower destinies (<s>apāyagati</s>), suffering, and mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>). And because of having dense afflictions.

body.text: iti. tadaprahāṇe kāmadhātvanatikramāt. dauvārikānucarasādharmyād iti. dauvārikasadharmaṇau kāmachandavyāpādau. tau hi kāmadhātubandhanāgārān niḥkramaṇaṃ na dattaḥ. dauvārikavat. anucarasadharmāṇaḥ satkāyadṛṣṭyādayaḥ. yathā hi dauvārikapramāde bandhanāgārāt puruṣo niṣkrāṃto 'pi dauvārikānucarair nivartyate. tathehāpy amībhir iti. tribhiḥ. sattvāvaratām iti. pṛthagjanatvalakṣaṇāṃ sattvāvaratāṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśīlavrataparāmarśavicikitsāsaṃyojanair nātikrāmati. dvābhyāṃ kāmachandavyāpādābhyāṃ. dhātvavaratāṃ kāmadhātusvabhāvāṃ nātikrāmati. nātivartate. āryebhyo hy avarāḥ pṛthagjanāḥ. dhātuṣu ca kāmadhātur avaraḥ. tasmād eva tāny avarabhāgīyāni
body.translated_text: — because when those are not abandoned, one does not transcend the Desire Realm. 'By analogy with a gatekeeper and his attendants' — sensual desire (<s>kāmachanda</s>) and malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>) are similar to a gatekeeper. For those two do not permit exit from the prison-house of the Desire Realm — like a gatekeeper. Identity-view (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest are similar to the gatekeeper's attendants. For just as when the gatekeeper is negligent, a person who has escaped from the prison is turned back by the gatekeeper's attendants — so too here, by these — by the three. 'The inferior state of beings' — the inferior state of beings characterized by the state of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), one does not transcend through the three fetters of identity-view, attachment to morality and vows, and doubt. Through the two — sensual desire and malice — one does not transcend the inferior state of the realm, the state of being in the Desire Realm. One does not pass beyond it. For ordinary persons are inferior compared to Noble Ones. And among the realms, the Desire Realm is inferior. Therefore those are called 'pertaining to the lower part' (<s>avarabhāgīya</s>)

body.text: apare yogācārāḥ.
body.translated_text: — other <s>Yogācāra</s>s [also hold this].

body.text: paryādāya trisaṃyojanaprahāṇād iti. niravaśeṣataḥ satkāyadṛṣṭiśīlavrataparāmarśavicikitsāsamyojanaprahāṇād ity arthaḥ. ṣaṭ kleśāḥ [Tib. 152b] prahīṇā iti. paṃca dṛṣṭayo vicikitsā ca. na tu rāgādaya uktāḥ savaśeṣatvāt. tisro dṛṣṭīr apahāyeti. aṃtagrāhamithyādṛṣṭidṛṣṭiparāmarśadṛṣṭīḥ. trayam evāheti. satkāyadṛṣṭiśīlavrataparāmarśavicikitsātrayam evāha. ka āha. bhagavān. tathā hi sūtre paṭhyate. kiyatā bhadaṃta srotaāpanno bhavati. yataś ca mahānāmann āryaśrāvakaḥ idaṃ duḥkham āryasatyam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ. ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ. iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam iti yathabhūtaṃ prajānāti. trīṇi cāsya saṃyojanāni prahīṇāni bhavaṃti parijñātāni. tadyathā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ śīlavrataparāmarśo vivcikitsā ca. sa eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāt srotaāpanno bhavaty avinipātadharmā saṃbodhiparāyaṇaḥ saptakṛdbhavaparamaḥ saptakṛtvo devāṃś ca manuṣyāṃś ca saṃsṛtya saṃdhāvya duḥkhasyāṃtaṃ kariṣyatīti. sarvam etad vaktavyaṃ syāt. bhaved ity arthaḥ. triprakārāḥ kila kleśā iti. darśanaheyā ihādhikṛtāḥ. ekaprakārāḥ satkāyāṃtagrāhadṛṣṭayaḥ duḥkhadarśanamātrapraheyatvāt. dviprakārāḥ śīlavrataparāmarśāḥ. catuṣprakārāḥ vicikitsāmithyādṛṣṭiparāmarśāḥ. tatra satkāyadṛṣṭir mukham ekaprakārāṇāṃ. ataḥ satkāyadṛṣṭigrahaṇād antagrāhadṛṣṭir [Tib. 153a] api gṛhītā bhavati. vicikitsā mukhaṃ catuḥprakārāṇāṃ. atas tadgrahaṇān mithyādṛṣṭiparāmarśānāṃ grahaṇaṃ bhavati. śīlavrataparāmarśas tu sākṣād eva gṛhītaḥ. ye tu rāgādayo darśanaheyāḥ. te 'pi tadālaṃbanatvāt gṛhītā eveti śakyate vaktum iti. aṃtagrāhadṛṣṭiḥ satkāyadṛṣṭipravartiteti. ātmanaḥ śāśvatocchedānugrahaṇāt. dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ śīlavrataparāmarśapravartita iti. yena śuddhiṃ pratyeti. tasyāgrato grahaṇāt. mithyādṛṣṭir vicikitsāpravartiteti. saṃśayitasya mithyāśravaṇacintanān mithyāniścayotpatteḥ. ato mūlagrahaṇān mūlasaṃbhūtagrahaṇasiddhir ity aṃtagrāhadṛṣṭyādayo 'py uktarūpā veditavyāḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Through the complete abandonment of the three fetters' — the meaning is: through the complete, without-remainder abandonment of the fetters of identity-view, attachment to morality and vows, and doubt. 'Six afflictions are abandoned' — the five views and doubt. But desire and the rest are not mentioned, because they remain with a residue. 'Without abandoning three views' — the views of extreme-grasping (<s>antagrāha</s>), wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), and view-attachment (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>). 'He mentions only three' — he mentions only the three: identity-view, attachment to morality and vows, and doubt. Who mentions? The Blessed One. For thus it is read in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'By how much, venerable sir, does one become a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>)? Inasmuch, <s>Mahānāman</s>, as a noble disciple truly knows: "This is the noble truth of suffering," and truly knows: "This is the origination of suffering, this is the cessation of suffering, this is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering — the noble truth" — and three fetters of his are abandoned, fully understood — namely: identity-view, attachment to morality and vows, and doubt. Through the abandonment of these three fetters, he becomes a stream-enterer, one not subject to falling into evil destinies, destined for complete awakening, having at most seven existences — having transmigrated and wandered through [the realms of] gods and humans seven times, he will make an end of suffering.' All this should have been stated. The meaning is: it could have been stated [that all six are abandoned]. 'Afflictions are of three types' — those to be abandoned by seeing are the topic here. Of one type are identity-view and extreme-grasping view — because of being to be abandoned solely by seeing suffering. Of two types are the attachments to morality and vows. Of four types are doubt, wrong view, and view-attachment. Therein, identity-view is the representative of those of one type; therefore, from the mention of identity-view, extreme-grasping view too is included. Doubt is the representative of those of four types; therefore, from its mention, the inclusion of wrong view and view-attachment follows. Attachment to morality and vows is directly mentioned. And those desires and the rest that are to be abandoned by seeing — they too, because of having those [views] as their objects, can be said to be included. 'Extreme-grasping view is set in motion by identity-view' — because of grasping the self as eternal or annihilated. 'View-attachment is set in motion by attachment to morality and vows' — because of grasping as supreme that through which one expects purification. 'Wrong view is set in motion by doubt' — because for one who is uncertain, through wrong hearing and wrong reflection, a wrong conviction arises. Therefore, from the mention of the root, the inclusion of that which arises from the root is established — thus extreme-grasping view and the rest should be understood as stated.

body.text: apare punar āhur ity ayam evācāryaḥ. mārgavibhramaḥ katham ity āha. anyamārgasaṃśrayaṇād iti.
body.translated_text: 'But others say' — this is the <s>Ācārya</s> himself. 'How is the deviation regarding the path?' He says: 'because of resorting to another path.'

body.text: (V.45) avarabhāgīyasaṃyojanavacanād anyabhāgīyam apy astīty arthād uktaṃ bhavati. ata idam ucyate.
body.translated_text: (V.45) From the mention of 'lower-part fetters,' it is implicitly stated that there are also [fetters] pertaining to another part. Therefore this is stated:

body.text: iti. saṃyojanaprasaṃgaḥ.
body.translated_text: — in the context of fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>).

body.text: (V.46) saṃyojanādibhedena punas te paṃcadhoditā
body.translated_text: (V.46) 'And those, in their divisions as fetters and the rest, are stated as fivefold'

body.text: ity anena saṃbaṃdhena saṃyojananirdeśānaṃtaraṃ baṃdhananirdeśāvasaro 'paraparyāyaḥ. rāgo bandhanaṃ sarva iti. sarva iti prakārato dhātutaś ca. sarvadveṣaḥ. kiṃ sarvaḥ. prakārata eva [Tib. 153b] mohaḥ sarvaḥ prakārato dhātutaś ca. ālaṃbanasaṃprayogābhyām iti. svaparasāṃtānikyāṃ sukhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ yathāyogaṃ rāgo 'nuśete. duḥkhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ dveṣaḥ ālaṃbanasaṃprayogābhyām ity eva. aduḥkhāsukhāyāṃ mohaḥ tābhyām ity eva. nanu ca rāgadveṣāv apy aduḥkhāsukhāyāṃ yathāyogaṃ tathaivānuśayāte. kasmān moha evocyata iti āha. na tathā rāgadveṣāv iti. rāgadveṣāv apy anuśayāte. na tu tathā yathā mohaḥ. moho hy apaṭutvād apaṭvyām aduḥkhāsukhāyāṃ vedanāyām anukūlatvāt sutarām anuśeta iti. svāsāṃtānikālaṃbanato vā niyama iti. svāsāṃtānikasukhādyanubhūtisāmarthyāt tathā niyamaḥ. svasaṃtānavedanāyāṃ hi sukhāyāṃ rāgo duḥkhāyāṃ dveṣo 'duḥkhāsukhāyāṃ mohaḥ saṃprayogata iti.
body.translated_text: — by this connection, after the exposition of fetters, there is occasion for the exposition of bonds (<s>bandhana</s>) — another synonym. 'Desire is a bond, in all [respects]' — 'all' means in type and in realm. 'All hatred.' 'What, all?' In type only. 'Delusion — all, in type and in realm.' 'By way of object and association' — in pleasant feeling, whether belonging to one's own or another's continuum, as applicable, desire lies latent. In painful feeling, aversion [lies latent] — by way of object and association, exactly so. In neither-painful-nor-pleasant [feeling], delusion [lies latent] — by those two, exactly so. But do not desire and aversion also lie latent, as applicable, in neither-painful-nor-pleasant [feeling]? Why is only delusion mentioned? He says: 'Desire and aversion do not [lie latent] in the same way' — desire and aversion do lie latent, but not in the same way as delusion. For delusion, because of dullness, lies latent all the more readily in the dull neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, because of compatibility. 'Or the restriction is from one's own continuum as object' — because of the capacity of experience of pleasure and the rest in one's own continuum, such is the restriction. For in pleasant feeling of one's own continuum, desire [lies latent] by association; in painful [feeling], aversion; in neither-painful-nor-pleasant, delusion — by association.

body.text: apare tu vyācakṣate. na tathā rāgadveṣāv iti. sukhāyāṃ yathā rāgo 'nuśete na tathā dveṣaḥ. kiṃ punaḥ sukhāyām api dveṣo 'nuśete. anuśete śatrusukhe ālaṃbanataḥ. yathā ca duḥkhāyāṃ dveśo 'nuśete [Tib. 154a] na tathā rāgaḥ. kiṃ punar duḥkhāyām api rāgo 'nuśete. anuśete śatruduḥkhe ālaṃbanataḥ. svāsāṃtānikālaṃbanato vā niyama iti. atha vā svāsāṃtānike sukhe ālaṃbanataḥ saṃprayogato vā rāgo 'nuśete. na parasāṃtānike śatrusukhe. evaṃ duḥkhe svāsāṃtānike dveśo 'nuśete ālaṃbanataḥ saṃprayogato vā. na pārasāṃtānike śatruduḥkhe. ity evaṃ svāsāṃtānikālaṃbanato niyamaḥ. sukhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ rāgo 'nuśeto. ālaṃbanasaṃprayogābhyāṃ duḥkhāyāṃ dveṣa iti.
body.translated_text: Others, however, explain: 'Desire and aversion do not [lie latent] in the same way' — in pleasant [feeling], as desire lies latent, aversion does not in the same way. But does aversion also lie latent in pleasant [feeling]? It does — in the pleasant [feeling] of an enemy, by way of object. And just as aversion lies latent in painful [feeling], desire does not in the same way. But does desire also lie latent in painful [feeling]? It does — in the painful [feeling] of an enemy, by way of object. 'Or the restriction is from one's own continuum as object' — or alternatively, in one's own continuum's pleasant [feeling], desire lies latent by way of object and association. Not in another's continuum's — an enemy's pleasant [feeling]. Similarly, in one's own continuum's painful [feeling], aversion lies latent by way of object and association. Not in another's continuum's — an enemy's painful [feeling]. Thus the restriction is from one's own continuum as object. 'In pleasant feeling, desire lies latent, by way of object and association; in painful, aversion' — thus.

body.text: (V.46) cittopakleśanād iti. cittakliṣṭakaraṇāt.
body.translated_text: (V.46) 'Because of afflicting the mind' — because of making the mind defiled.

body.text: iti. kleśebhyo 'nya ity arthaḥ. ta upakleśā eveti. kleśasamīparūpāḥ. kleśo vā samīpavarty eṣām iti. kleśapravṛttyanuvṛtter aparipūrṇakleśalakṣaṇatvāc copakleśāḥ. upakleśāś caitasā eva te na cittaviprayuktāḥ. ye kṣudravastuke paṭhitā iti. kṣudravastuke pravacanabhāge ye paṭhitāḥ. na tu cetanādaya evety abhiprāyaḥ. tadyathā aratir [Tib. 154b] vijṛṃbhikā cetaso līnatvaṃ tandrī bhakṣe 'samatā nānātvasaṃjñā amanasikāraḥ kāyadauṣṭhulyaṃ śṛṃgī bhittirīkā anārdavatā anārdavatā asvabhāvānuvartitā kāmavitarko vyāpādavitarko vihiṃsāvitarko jñātivitarko janapadavitarko 'maravitarko 'vamanyanāpratisaṃyukto vitarkaḥ kulodayatāpratisaṃyukto vitarkaḥ śokaḥ duḥkhaṃ daurmanasyam
body.translated_text: — meaning: other than the afflictions. 'Those are secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>) only' — having a form proximate to the afflictions. Or: those near which an affliction exists. And because of following the operation of afflictions, and because of having incomplete affliction-characteristics, they are secondary afflictions. Secondary afflictions are mental factors only — not [dharmas] dissociated from mind. 'Those that are read in the <s>Kṣudravastu</s>' — those that are read in the section of the canon called <s>Kṣudravastu</s>. The intent is: but not volition and the rest. Namely: discontent (<s>arati</s>), yawning (<s>vijṛṃbhikā</s>), mental sluggishness (<s>cetaso līnatva</s>), drowsiness (<s>tandrī</s>), dissatisfaction with food (<s>bhakṣe asamatā</s>), perception of diversity (<s>nānātvasaṃjñā</s>), inattention (<s>amanasikāra</s>), bodily unsuitability (<s>kāyadauṣṭhulya</s>), lustful display (<s>śṛṅgī</s>), wall-clinging (<s>bhittirīkā</s>), lack of gentleness (<s>anārdavatā</s>), lack of gentleness (<s>anārdavatā</s>), following what is not one's own nature (<s>asvabhāvānuvartitā</s>), sensual thought (<s>kāmavitarka</s>), malicious thought (<s>vyāpādavitarka</s>), harmful thought (<s>vihiṃsāvitarka</s>), thought about relatives (<s>jñātivitarka</s>), thought about one's country (<s>janapadavitarka</s>), thought about immortality (<s>amaravitarka</s>), thought connected with looking down on others (<s>avamanyanāpratisaṃyukta vitarka</s>), thought connected with family prestige (<s>kulodayatāpratisaṃyukta vitarka</s>), grief (<s>śoka</s>), suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>)

body.text: upāyāsa iti. [tandrīti jaḍatā.]
body.translated_text: , and despair (<s>upāyāsa</s>). [Drowsiness (<s>tandrī</s>) means dullness (<s>jaḍatā</s>).]

children.translated_text: 'Therein, shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>) have been explained' —
'Shamelessness (<s>ahrī</s>) is non-reverence; not seeing danger in what is blameworthy is lack of moral dread (<s>atrapa</s>).'

body.text: dharmāmiṣeti vistaraḥ. dharmasyāmiṣasya kauśalasya ca pradāne virodhī cittasyāgraho mātsaryaṃ. mā mattaḥ saratv ity ākāro matsaraḥ. matsara eva mātsaryaṃ. matsariṇo vā bhāvo mātsaryaṃ. kaukṛtyaṃ styānaṃ ca vyākhyāte iti. kukṛtabhāvaḥ kaukṛtyaṃ. iha tu tadālaṃbano dharmaḥ kaukṛtyaṃ. kāyacittākarmaṇyatā styānam iti. cittābhisaṃkṣepo middham ity etāvaty ucyamāne samāpattāv api prasaṃga ity ato viśeṣyate. kāyasaṃdhāraṇāsamartha iti. tat tu kliṣṭam eva paryavasthānaṃ. kaukṛtyaṃ ceti. yat kliṣṭaṃ middhaṃ. tat paryavasthānaṃ. yat tu kuśalam avyākṛtaṃ vā na tat [Tib. 155a] paryavasthānaṃ. trividhaṃ hi middham iṣyate. kaukṛtyaṃ ca. yat kliṣṭaṃ. tat paryavasthānaṃ. na kuśalaṃ. kuśalākusalaṃ hi tad iṣyate. vyāpādavihiṃsāvarjitaḥ sattvāsattvayor āghātaḥ krodha iti. sattvaviṣaye āghātaviśeṣo vyāpādaḥ. amī bhavaṃtaḥ sattvā hanyaṃtāṃ vā badhyaṃtāṃ vā śīryaṃtāṃ vā anayena vyasanam āpadyaṃtām ity ākārapravṛtto vyāpādaḥ. sattvākarṣaṇasaṃtrāsanatarjanādikarmapravṛttā vihiṃsā. tābhyām anyaḥ sattvāsattvayor āghātaḥ krodhaḥ. tadyathā śikṣākāmasya bhikṣoś cittaprakopaḥ. kaṃṭakādiṣu ca prakopa iti. yathākramaṃ jñātājñātānām iti. rājādibhir jñātānāṃ mrakṣavatāṃ pudgalānāṃ mrakṣas tṛṣṇāniṣyandaḥ. mā me lābhasatkāro na bhavaiṣyatīti. ajñātānām avidyāniṣyandaḥ karmasvakatām aśraddadhānaḥ tad avadyaṃ pracchādayati. na parasyāṃtike viśuddhyarthaṃ deśayatīty evam ubhayaniṣyando mrakṣa ity eke. katham anapatrāpyam avidyāniṣyandaḥ. yasmād
body.translated_text: '<s>Dharma</s>, material gain' — and so forth in detail. Opposition to giving of <s>Dharma</s>, material gain, and skill — the mind's non-release — is miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>). 'May [the good] not flow from me' — this is the mode of stinginess (<s>matsara</s>). Stinginess itself is miserliness. Or: the state of being stingy is miserliness. 'Regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) and torpor (<s>styāna</s>) have been explained' — the state of having done wrongly is regret. But here, the <s>dharma</s> that has [wrong action] as its object is regret. 'Unsuitability of body and mind for action is torpor.' 'Mental contraction is sloth (<s>middha</s>)' — if only this much were stated, it would apply even to meditative attainment — therefore it is specified: 'incapable of maintaining the body.' But that [sloth] is exclusively an afflicted wrapping (<s>paryavasthāna</s>). 'And regret' — that sloth which is afflicted is a wrapping. But that which is wholesome or indeterminate is not a wrapping. For sloth is accepted as threefold. And regret — that which is afflicted is a wrapping, not the wholesome [kind]. For that is accepted as [either] wholesome or unwholesome. 'Anger (<s>krodha</s>) is hostility toward beings and non-beings, excluding malice and harmfulness' — hostility specifically directed toward beings is malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>): 'May these beings be killed, bound, destroyed, or come to misfortune and ruin' — malice operates in such a mode. Harmfulness (<s>vihiṃsā</s>) operates in the activity of dragging beings away, frightening, threatening, and the like. Other than those two, hostility toward beings and non-beings is anger. For example: the agitation of mind of a monk who wishes to train. And agitation toward thorns and the like. 'Of those known and unknown, respectively' — concealment (<s>mrakṣa</s>) of persons known to kings and the like is an outflow of craving — 'may my gain and honor not be lost.' Of those unknown [to authorities], it is an outflow of ignorance — one who does not believe in the ownership of karma conceals that fault, not confessing it before another for the purpose of purification — thus some [say] it is an outflow of both. How is lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>) an outflow of ignorance? Because

children.translated_text: 'not seeing danger in what is blameworthy is lack of moral dread.'

body.text: iti. yat kliṣṭaṃ. tad eva paryavasthānādhikārāt.
body.translated_text: — that which is afflicted — that alone, because of the topic being wrappings (<s>paryavasthāna</s>).

body.text: iti. yathā śarīrān malā jāyaṃte evam ime māyādayo malā iva kleśebhya utpadyaṃte. kṣipati prerati. madaḥ pūrvoktaḥ
body.translated_text: — just as stains arise from the body, so these — deceit (<s>māyā</s>) and the rest — arise from the afflictions like stains. 'It throws, impels.' Intoxication (<s>mada</s>) was previously stated:

children.text: madaḥ svadharme raktasya paryādānaṃ tu cetasa
children.translated_text: 'Intoxication (<s>mada</s>) is the mind's preoccupation with one's own qualities, of one attached'

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: — thus.

body.text: (V.51) yaś ca yaddarśanaheyasaṃprayukta iti. yasya satyasya darśanaṃ yaddarśanaṃ. yaddarśanena heyo yaddarśanaheyaḥ. tena saṃprayukto yaddarśanaheyasaṃprayuktaḥ. sa taddarśanaheyaḥ. sa tasya satyasya darśanena heyaḥ. kaḥ. āhrīkyādiḥ. tadanye bhāvanāheyā eva.
body.translated_text: (V.51) 'That which is associated with what is to be abandoned by a given seeing' — the seeing of a given truth is that seeing; that which is to be abandoned by that seeing is to-be-abandoned-by-that-seeing; that which is associated with what is to-be-abandoned-by-that-seeing is associated-with-what-is-to-be-abandoned-by-that-seeing. That is to be abandoned by that seeing — it is to be abandoned by the seeing of that truth. What? Shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and the rest. Those other than those are to be abandoned by cultivation alone.

body.text: iti. āhrīkyādibhyo 'nye īrṣyādayo bhāvanāheyā eva. na darśanaheyāḥ.
body.translated_text: — other than shamelessness and the rest — jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) and the rest — are to be abandoned by cultivation alone, not by seeing.

body.text: na rāgādiparataṃtrā ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: — the meaning is: not dependent on desire and the rest.

body.text: (V.52) styānauddhatyamiddhāny akuśalāvyākṛtānīti. paryavasthānādhikārān middhaṃ kuśalam apīti nocyate.
body.translated_text: (V.52) 'Torpor, restlessness, and sloth are unwholesome and indeterminate' — sloth, even though wholesome too, is not mentioned because of the topic being wrappings.

body.text: iti. yathāsaṃbhavam iti. kāmadhātoḥ pareṇa yāvaṃtaḥ saṃbhavaṃti. te punar māyāśāṭhyādayaḥ.
body.translated_text: — 'as applicable' — however many arise beyond the Desire Realm — those, moreover, are deceit, flattery, and the rest.

body.text: (V.52) vitathātmasaṃdarśanatayeti. vitathasyātmanaḥ saṃdarśanatayā mahābrahmā āyuṣmaṃtam aśvajitaṃ vaṃcayituṃ pravṛttaḥ. kutremāni brahman mahābhūtāny apariśeṣaṃ nirudhyaṃta iti pṛṣṭo [Tib. 156a] 'prajānan kṣepam akārṣīt. aham asmi brahmā mahābrahmā īśvaraḥ kartā nirmātā sraṣṭā sṛjaḥ pitṛbhūto bhāvānām iti māyayā vaṃcayitum ārabdhaḥ. atha sa mahābrahmā āyuṣmaṃtam aśvajitaṃ kare gṛhītvā ekāṃte asthād ekāṃtasthitaś cedam uktavān. vidyamāne tathāgate māṃ praṣṭavyaṃ manyasaitīdam asya śāṭhyaṃ dṛśyate. svapariṣallajjayā hy ātmīyajñānatāṃ nigūhamānaḥ sa tathā kṛtavān iti. uktam api śāṭhyam iti tathā hi
body.translated_text: (V.52) 'By showing a false self' — by showing a false self, <s>Mahābrahmā</s> set about to deceive the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>. When asked, 'Where, O <s>Brahman</s>, do these great elements cease without remainder?' — though knowing, he made a deflection. 'I am <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, the Lord, the creator, the fashioner, the maker, the progenitor, the father of beings' — he began to deceive by this illusion. Then <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, taking the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s> by the hand, stood apart, and standing apart said this: 'While the <s>Tathāgata</s> is present, you think I should be questioned' — this duplicity (<s>śāṭhya</s>) of his is seen. For, concealing his own lack of knowledge out of embarrassment before his own retinue, he acted thus. It is also said that [this is] duplicity, for thus:

children.text: kaukṛtyamiddhākuśalāny ādye dhyāne na saṃty ata
children.translated_text: 'Regret, torpor, and unwholesome [dharmas] do not exist in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, therefore'

body.text: iti. atroktam api prasaṃgeneti
body.translated_text: — thus. Here too it is said 'by digression' —

body.text: iti prasaṃgeneti. paṃcāpanīyeti māyāśāṭhyastyānauddhatyamadān.
body.translated_text: — by digression. 'The five to be removed' — deceit (<s>māyā</s>), duplicity (<s>śāṭhya</s>), torpor (<s>styāna</s>), restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>), and intoxication (<s>mada</s>).

body.text: (V.53) tehi sakale manobhūmike iti. mānamiddhe.
body.translated_text: (V.53) 'By these two, belonging to the entire mental ground' — pride (<s>māna</s>) and torpor (<s>middha</s>).

body.text: īrṣyāmātsaryādayaḥ. ye ca kleśamahābhūmikeṣūktā ity āśraddhyakausīdyapramādā eva. nānye styānauddhatyayor ihaiva pūrvaṃ gṛhītatvāt. mohasya kleśagrahaṇena grahaṇāt.
body.translated_text: envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>), and the rest. And those stated among the affliction-great-ground [dharmas] — these are just lack of faith (<s>āśraddhya</s>), laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), and heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>). Not others, because torpor and restlessness have already been included here previously. Because delusion (<s>moha</s>) is included through the inclusion of afflictions.

body.text: iti. sukhavedanāsvabhāvābhyām indriyābhyām ity arthaḥ. harṣadainyākāravartitvād iti. harṣākāravartī rāgo dainyākāravartī dveṣa iti yathāsaṃkhyena. [Tib. 156b] ṣaḍvijñānabhūmikatvāc ceti. paṃcavijñānabhūmikatvād rāgaḥ sukhendriyeṇa saṃprayuktaḥ. dveṣaś ca duḥkhendriyeṇa. manovijñānabhūmikatvāt tu rāgaḥ saumanasyendriyeṇa. dveṣaś ca daurmanasyendriyeṇa saṃprayuktaḥ. puṇyakarmaṇāṃ pāpakarmaṇāṃ ca yathākramaṃ iti. puṇyakarmaṇāṃ mithyādṛṣṭir daurmanasyena saṃprayuktā. puṇyakriyāyā nairarthakyadarśanāt. pāpakarmanāṃ mithyādṛṣṭiḥ saumanasyena sasṃprayuktā. svakṛtapāpavaiphalyadarśanāt. catasro dṛṣṭaya iti. satkāyadṛṣṭir aṃtagrāhadṛṣṭir dṛṣṭiparāmarśaḥ śīlavrataparāmarsaś ca. katham ucchedadṛṣṭiḥ saumanasyena saṃprayuktā. tasyābhinatatvāt. upekṣā saṃtiṣṭhata iti vināśāvasthāyāṃ mandatvāt. yasyāṃ bhūmau yāvantīndriyāṇīti.
body.translated_text: the meaning is: by the two faculties having the nature of pleasant feeling. Because passion operates with the aspect of delight, and aversion operates with the aspect of dejection — in respective order. And because they belong to the six consciousness grounds: passion is associated with the pleasure faculty because it belongs to the five consciousness grounds. And aversion with the pain faculty. But because it belongs to the mental consciousness ground, passion is associated with the mental pleasure faculty (<s>saumanasyendriya</s>). And aversion is associated with the mental displeasure faculty (<s>daurmanasyendriya</s>). 'Of meritorious and demeritorious actions respectively' — wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) of meritorious actions is associated with mental displeasure, because of seeing the futility of meritorious activity. Wrong view of demeritorious actions is associated with mental pleasure, because of seeing the fruitlessness of one's own committed sins. 'The four views' — identity-view (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), extreme-grasping view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>), clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>), and clinging to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>). How is the annihilationist view (<s>ucchedadṛṣṭi</s>) associated with mental pleasure? Because of inclination toward it. 'Equanimity remains' — because in the state of destruction, [feeling] is mild. 'In whichever ground, however many faculties' —

children.text:
saumanasyasukhopekṣāḥ upekṣāsumanaskaje.
sukhopekṣe upekṣā ca vido dhyānopapattiṣu
children.translated_text:
'Mental pleasure, pleasure, and equanimity in [those born] from equanimity and mental pleasure;
pleasure and equanimity, and equanimity — the feelings in the <s>dhyāna</s>s and births' —

body.text: iti avagaṃtavyaṃ. tatrapy ūrdhvabhūmiṣu. caturvijñānakāyikāḥ prathama eva dhyāne. cakṣuḥśrotrakāyamanovijñānabhūmikāḥ. prathame hi dhyāne trivijñānakāyikaṃ sukhendriyam asti. [Tib. 157a] manovijñānakāyikaṃ saumanasyendriyaṃ. cāturvijñānakāyikaṃ upekṣendriyaṃ. tata ūrdhvaṃ manobhūmikam eva. dvitīye dhyāne saumanasyopekṣendriye. tṛtīye sukhopekṣendriye. caturthe dhyāne ārūpyeṣu copekṣendriyam eva. tatra sarve 'py anuśayā yathāyathaṃ vedanendriyeṇa saṃprayuktāḥ. tatra śamathasnigdhasaṃtānatvāt harṣadainyākāravyavasthā nāsti. dainyākāravartitvād eṣāṃ kaukṛtyādīnāṃ na saumanasyena saṃprayogaḥ. manobhūmikatvā na duḥkhendriyeṇa.
body.translated_text: thus it should be understood. There too, in the higher grounds: the four consciousness-bodies belong to the first <s>dhyāna</s> alone — the eye, ear, body, and mental consciousness grounds. For in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the pleasure faculty belongs to three consciousness-bodies. The mental pleasure faculty belongs to the mental consciousness-body. The equanimity faculty belongs to four consciousness-bodies. Above that, it belongs to the mental ground alone. In the second <s>dhyāna</s>, the mental pleasure and equanimity faculties. In the third, the pleasure and equanimity faculties. In the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and the formless realms, the equanimity faculty alone. Therein, all the latent dispositions are associated with the feeling-faculties as applicable. Therein, because the mental continuum is smooth through tranquility, there is no establishment of the aspects of delight and dejection. Because they operate with the aspect of dejection, regret and the rest are not associated with mental pleasure. Because they belong to the mental ground, [they are] not [associated] with the pain faculty.

body.text: (V.56-57) lobhānvayatveneti. lobhahetudatvena. lobhasamutthenety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: (V.56-57) 'Because of being a consequence of passion' — because of being caused by passion. The meaning is: because of being produced by passion.

body.text: iti. sukhasaumanasyābhyāṃ. tṛtīye dhyāne sukheneti. madasya mānasattvāt. yathā avidyāyā iti. yathā avidyāyāḥ na kvacit kleśe upakleśe vā saṃprayogapratiṣedho 'sti. evam upekṣāyā apīti. akuśalamahābhūmikatvāt āhrīkyānapatrāpyayoḥ.
body.translated_text: with pleasure and mental pleasure. 'In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, with pleasure' — because intoxication is mental in nature. 'Just as ignorance' — just as there is no prohibition of association of ignorance with any affliction or secondary affliction, so too for equanimity. Because of belonging to the unwholesome-great-ground, regarding shamelessness (<s>āhrīkya</s>) and lack of moral dread (<s>anapatrāpya</s>):

children.translated_text: 'But in the unwholesome, shamelessness and lack of moral dread' —

body.text: vacanāt. kleśamahābhūmikatvāc ca styānauddhatyayoḥ. ṣaḍ vijñānakāyā akuśalāḥ kliṣṭāḥ saṃbhavaṃtīty ataḥ paṃcabhir apīndriyaiḥ saṃprayoga eṣāṃ [Tib.157b] saṃbhavatīti.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated. And because torpor and restlessness belong to the affliction-great-ground. Since the six consciousness-bodies can be unwholesome and afflicted, association of these [dharmas] with all five faculties is possible.

body.text: (V.58) kiṃ traidhātukyastyānauddhatyavicikitsā gṛhyaṃta iti. āsāṃ traidhātukatvāt tā eva niṣkṛṣya pṛcchyaṃte. kevalo 'yam iti vistaraḥ akuśalā rāśir iti bhikṣavo yad uta paṃca nivaraṇānīti te samyag vadamānā vadyuḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ. kevalo 'yaṃ bhikṣavaḥ paripūrṇākuśalarāśir yad uta paṃca nivaraṇānīti vistareṇaikāṃtākuśalatvavacanāt. kāme nivaraṇāni nānyatreti. vṛttisūtrapadayor ekavākyatā. nivaraṇānīti dhyānasamāpattyādīnām āvaraṇānīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: (V.58) 'Are torpor, restlessness, and doubt that belong to all three realms included?' — because these belong to all three realms, they alone are singled out and asked about. 'Merely this' — and so forth in detail. 'The entirety of the unwholesome' — thus: 'O monks, that which is the entirety of the unwholesome mass, namely the five hindrances' — they would speak correctly when saying this. For what reason? 'O monks, this is indeed the complete unwholesome mass, namely the five hindrances' — because of the statement of being exclusively unwholesome in detail. 'Hindrances are in desire [realm], not elsewhere' — the sentence on activity and the <s>sūtra</s>-word form a single statement. 'Hindrances' means 'obstructions' — obstructions to <s>dhyāna</s>, attainments, and the like.

children.translated_text: 'Because of having a single counteragent and nutriment' —

body.text: iti. ekavipakṣāhārakṛtyatvād ity arthaḥ. aṃtareṇāpi hi bhāvapratyayaṃ bhāvapradhāne nirdeśo bhavet. atha vā ekaṃ vipakṣāhārakṛtyaṃ ekavipakṣāhārakṛtyaṃ. tata iti. vipakṣaḥ pratipakṣa iti. ślokabandhānuguṇyena pratipakṣa iha vipakṣo 'bhipretaḥ. kleśaviruddhaḥ pakṣo vipakṣa iti kṛtvā. abhidharme tu kṛṣṇaḥ pakṣo vipakṣaḥ śuklaviruddhaḥ pakṣo vipakṣaḥ. śuklapakṣaḥ pratipakṣa iti pratītaṃ.
body.translated_text: the meaning is: because of having a single counteragent and nutriment. For even without a causal compound, a statement may be predominantly about the thing. Or alternatively: a single counteragent-and-nutriment is 'single-counteragent-and-nutriment'; from that. 'Counteragent' (<s>vipakṣa</s>) means 'antidote' (<s>pratipakṣa</s>). In accordance with the verse-construction, 'antidote' is here intended as 'counteragent.' [Meaning:] a faction opposed to afflictions is a counteragent. But in <s>Abhidharma</s>, the dark faction is the counteragent — the faction opposed to the white is the counteragent; the white faction is the antidote — this is established.

body.text: bhakte asamateti. atibahubhuktvāhārasya yaḥ kāyoparodhaḥ. anāhāra iti pratipakṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Immoderation in food' — the physical obstruction from eating excessively. 'Abstention from food' is the antidote.

body.text: styānamiddhena prajñāskandhasya. kiṃ. vighāta iti prakṛtaṃ. [Tib. 158a]
body.translated_text: 'By torpor-and-drowsiness, of the wisdom-aggregate' — what? 'Obstruction' — this is the topic under discussion.

body.text: etasyāṃ tu kalpanāyām iti vistaraḥ. śīlaskaṃdhaḥ samādhiskaṃdhaḥ prajñāskandha iti. yayānupūrvyā skandhā vyavasthitāḥ. tayaivānupūrvyā tadvipakṣabhūtāni nivaraṇāni paṭhyeran. kāmacchando vyāpādaḥ auddhatyakaukṛtyaṃ styānamiddhaṃ vicikitsā ceti. auddhatyakaukṛtyanivaraṇasya pūrvaṃ grahaṇaṃ prāpnoti. samādhiskaṃdhasya prajñāskaṃdhāt pūrvam uktatvāt. na caivam ato naitat kāraṇam ity abhiprāyaḥ. kiṃ punar atra kāraṇam ity āha. ato yathāsaṃkhyam etābhyāṃ styānamiddhena auddhatyakaukṛtyena ca nivaraṇābhyāṃ samādhiprajñāskaṃdhayor upaghāta iti. katham ity āha. samādhiprayuktasya hi styānamiddhād bhayaṃ samānarūpakalpatvāt. evaṃ dharmapravicayaprayuktasyauddhatyakaukṛtyād bhayam iti.
body.translated_text: 'But in this interpretation' — and so forth in detail. 'The morality aggregate, the concentration aggregate, the wisdom aggregate' — in whatever order the aggregates are established, in that very order, the hindrances that are their counteragents should be read: sensual desire, ill-will, restlessness-and-regret, torpor-and-drowsiness, and doubt. [But then] the hindrance of restlessness-and-regret should be taken first, since the concentration aggregate was stated before the wisdom aggregate. But it is not so — therefore this is not the reason. This is the intent. Then what is the reason here? — he says: therefore, respectively by these two — torpor-and-drowsiness and restlessness-and-regret — hindrances, there is impairment of the concentration and wisdom aggregates. How? — he says: for one engaged in concentration, there is danger from torpor-and-drowsiness because of having a similar character. Similarly, for one engaged in investigation of <s>dharma</s>s, there is danger from restlessness-and-regret.

body.text: anye tv anyathā varṇayaṃtīti pūrvācāryaḥ. [Tib. 158] cāragatasyeti piṇḍapātārthaṃ paribhramataḥ. nimittagrāhāt. strīrūpam iti strīśabda iti vā grahaṇāt. vihāragatasya pratisaṃlīnasya sthitasya vā niṣaṇṇasya vā caṃkramyamāṇasya vā. tatpūrvakau priyāpriyaviṣayanimittagrāhapūrvakau priyāpriyaviṣayapūrvakau vā. yathākramaṃ śamathavipaśyanayor aṃtarāyaṃ kuruta iti. śamathasya styānamiddham aṃtarāyaṃ karoti. pratyāsannarūpatayā styānamiddhopasthānāt. vipaśyanāyā auddhatyakaukṛtyavicikitse aṃtarāyaṃ
body.translated_text: 'But others explain differently' — the former teachers. 'Of one who has gone on alms-round' — of one wandering for the purpose of collecting alms-food. 'Because of grasping at signs' — because of grasping at the sign of female form or the sound 'woman.' 'Of one who has gone to the dwelling, in seclusion' — of one seated in seclusion, or seated, or walking back and forth. 'Having those as antecedents' — having as antecedents the grasping of signs of pleasant and unpleasant objects, or having pleasant and unpleasant objects as antecedents. 'They respectively create obstacles for <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>' — torpor-and-drowsiness creates an obstacle for <s>śamatha</s>, because of the proximity of torpor-and-drowsiness [to its nature]. Restlessness-and-regret and doubt create obstacles for <s>vipaśyanā</s>

body.text: kurutaḥ. auddhatyakaukṛtyasya kṛtadvaṃdvaikavadbhāvasya vicikitsayā saha punar dvaṃdvaḥ. auddhatyakaukṛtyaṃ ca vicikitsā ca auddhatyakaukṛtyavicikitse iti. vicikitsā tu punar vyutthitasyāpi tasya dharmanidhyānakāle 'ṃtarāyaṃ karoti.
body.translated_text: — restlessness-and-regret, having the character of a compound-pair, forms another pair with doubt. Restlessness-and-regret and doubt — [these are] 'restlessness-regret-and-doubt.' But doubt creates an obstacle even for one who has emerged [from meditation], during the time of contemplation of <s>dharma</s>s.

body.text: apare punar evaṃ pāṭhaṃ paṭhaṃti. styānamiddham auddhatyakaukṛtyaṃ vicikitsā ceti. evaṃ ca vyācakṣate. styānamiddhaṃ śamathasyāṃtarāyaṃ karoti. auddhatyakaukṛtyaṃ vipaśyanāyāḥ. vicikitsā ca vyutthitasya dharmanidhyānakāle 'ṃtarāyaṃ karotīti.
body.translated_text: Others read the text thus: 'torpor-and-drowsiness, restlessness-and-regret, and doubt.' And they explain thus: torpor-and-drowsiness creates an obstacle for <s>śamatha</s>. Restlessness-and-regret, for <s>vipaśyanā</s>. And doubt creates an obstacle during the time of contemplation of <s>dharma</s>s for one who has emerged [from meditation].

body.text: (V.59) visabhāgadhātusarvatragāṇām iti. vistaraḥ. visabhāgadhātusarvatragāṇāṃ duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyatvena dvibhedānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādīnāṃ. yad ālaṃbanaṃ parijñāyate duḥkhasamudayānvayajñānapakṣeṇa mārgeṇa rūpārūpyadhātvālaṃbanāvasthāyāṃ. na te tadā prahīyaṃte. duḥkhadharmajñānena samudayadharmajñānena ca yathāyogaṃ pūrvam eva prahīṇatvāt. dharmajñānavadhyā hi te kāmāvacaratvāt. nirodhamārgadarśanaprahātavyānāṃ ca sāsravālaṃbanānāṃ [Tib. 159a] dṛṣṭiparāmarśādīnāṃ yadālaṃbanaṃ nirodhamārgadṛgdṛggheyaṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādikaṃ duḥkhasamudayasatyasvabhāvaṃ duḥkhasamudayadharmajñānapakṣeṇānvayajñānapakṣeṇa vā yathādhātu parijñāyate. na te tadā prahīyaṃte. nirodhamārgadarśanapraheyatvād iti. na ca tathā teṣām ālaṃbanaṃ parijñāyate pūrvam eva jñātatvāt. katham eṣāṃ prahāṇam ālaṃbanaparijñānāt tatprahāṇaṃ na yujyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. tatrālaṃbanaparijñānāt kāmāvacarāḥ svadhātvalaṃbanā rūpārūpyāvacarāś ca duḥkhasamudayadṛggheyāḥ prahīyaṃte. tatra visabhāgadhātvālaṃbanānām ālaṃbanaṃ parijñayā paśyataḥ prahāṇāṃ duḥkhasamudayānvayajñānakṣāṃtyor yugapad dvidhātvālaṃbanatvāt. svabhūmyālaṃbanānām iti viśeṣaṇaṃ. visabhāgadhātusarvatraganirāsārthaṃ. tadālaṃbanasaṃkṣayād iti. visabhāgadhātusarvatragā ālaṃbanam eṣāṃ satkāyadṛṣṭyādīnām iti. tadālaṃbanāḥ sabhāgadhātusarvatragāḥ. teṣāṃ kṣayāt prahāṇāt. te visabhāgadhātusarvatragāḥ prahīyaṃte. [taddhetutvenopastaṃbhaprahāṇād visabhāgadhātusarvatragānāṃ prahāṇam ālaṃbanaprahāṇā]. ālaṃbanaprahāṇād iti. dṛṣṭiparāmarśādyālaṃbanānāṃ nirodhamārgadarśanaheyānāṃ mithyādṛṣṭyādīnāṃ prahāṇāt. te 'pi dṛṣṭiparāmarśādayaḥ sāsravālaṃbanāḥ prahīyaṃte.
body.translated_text: (V.59) 'Of the dissimilar-realm universals' — in detail: of the dissimilar-realm universals that are twofold as being to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination — wrong view and the rest. When the object [of these] is fully comprehended by the path belonging to the suffering and origination <s>anvayajñāna</s> class, in the state of having Form and Formless Realm objects — they are not then abandoned. Because they have already been abandoned previously by <s>dharmajñāna</s> of suffering and <s>dharmajñāna</s> of origination, as applicable. For they are to be destroyed by <s>dharmajñāna</s>, because they belong to the Desire Realm. And of those to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path — the contaminated-object [afflictions like] clinging to views and the rest — when their object, namely the wrong view and the rest that are to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path, having the nature of the truth of suffering and origination, is fully comprehended by the suffering and origination <s>dharmajñāna</s> class or <s>anvayajñāna</s> class as per the realm — they are not then abandoned, because they are to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path. Nor is their object thus fully comprehended, because it has already been known previously. How then is their abandonment? The abandonment from full comprehension of the object — the intent is: the abandonment from full comprehension of the object is not fitting. Therein, from the full comprehension of the object, the Desire Realm [afflictions] that have their own realm as object, and the Form and Formless Realm [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination, are abandoned. Therein, for those having dissimilar-realm objects, the abandonment from comprehension of the object occurs for one who sees through the suffering and origination <s>anvayajñāna</s> tolerances, simultaneously, because they have objects in two realms. 'Of those having their own ground as object' — this qualifier is for the purpose of excluding the dissimilar-realm universals. 'From the destruction of those having that as object' — the dissimilar-realm universals are the objects of identity-view and the rest. Those having that as object are the same-realm universals. From the destruction — from the abandonment — of those, the dissimilar-realm universals are abandoned. [From the abandonment through the support of those being their causes, the abandonment of the dissimilar-realm universals occurs — abandonment from object-abandonment.] 'From the abandonment of the object' — from the abandonment of the wrong view and the rest that are the objects of clinging to views and the rest, which are to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path and have contaminated objects. Those [clinging to views and the rest] that have contaminated objects are also abandoned.

children.translated_text: 'From the arising of the antidote, destruction' —

body.text: iti. bhāvanāheyānāṃ pratipakṣodayād eva kṣayaḥ nālaṃbanaparijñānādibhya
body.translated_text: of those to be abandoned by cultivation, destruction occurs from the arising of the antidote alone, not from full comprehension of the object and the like —

body.text: iti darśayati. paścāt pravedayiṣyāma iti.
body.translated_text: he shows thus. 'Later we shall explain' —

children.text: navaprakārā doṣā hi bhūmaubhūmau tathā guṇā
children.translated_text: 'Nine kinds of faults in each ground, and likewise qualities' —

body.text: ity atra vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: he will explain there.

body.text: (V.60ab) prahāṇapratipakṣa ānaṃtaryamārga iti. [Tib. 159b] vipakṣapratidvaṃdvī pakṣaḥ pratipakṣaḥ. prahāṇāya pratipakṣaḥ prahāṇapratipakṣaḥ. vimuktimārgo 'pi hi pratipakṣo na tu prahāṇāyety ata itthaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ. prahīyate vāneneti prahāṇaṃ. prahāṇaś cāsau pratipakṣaś ca prahāṇapratipakṣaḥ. tadyathā duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāṃtiḥ. ādhārapratipakṣas tasmāt pareṇeti. tasmād ānaṃtaryamārgāt pareṇa. yo mārgo vimuktimārgaḥ. sa hy ādhāraḥ prahāṇasya tatprāptyādhāraṇāt. ādhāryate 'nenety ādhāraḥ. sa eva pratipakṣaḥ ādhārapratipakṣaḥ. tadyathā duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāṃteḥ paraṃ duḥkhadharmajñānam iti tenocyate. yena tatprāpitam iti vistaraḥ. yena mārgeṇa tatprāpitam ānaṃtaryamārgaprāpitaṃ prahāṇam ādhāryate. tatprāptyanucchedātma ādhārapratipakṣa iti. dūrībhāvapratipakṣa iti vistaraḥ. kleśaprāptir dūrībhavati yena sa dūrībhāvaḥ. sa eva pratipakṣo dūrībhāvapratipakṣaḥ. dūrībhavanaṃ vā dūrībhāvaḥ. tasmai pratipakṣo dūrībhāvapratipakṣaḥ. vimuktimārgāt pareṇa yo mārga iti. yo 'sau vimuktimārgo duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ. tasmāt pareṇa yo mārgo duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāṃtyādi. sa dūrībhāvapratipakṣa iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: (V.60ab) 'The antidote of abandonment (<s>prahāṇapratipakṣa</s>) is the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>).' The opponent of the adverse side is the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>). The antidote for the purpose of abandonment is the antidote of abandonment. For the path of liberation (<s>vimuktimārga</s>) too is an antidote, but not for the purpose of abandonment — hence this qualification. 'That by which [afflictions] are abandoned is abandonment' — abandonment, and it is an antidote — hence the antidote of abandonment. For example, the <s>duḥkhadharmajñānakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the knowledge of the truth of suffering). 'The antidote of support (<s>ādhārapratipakṣa</s>) is the one after that' — after that uninterrupted path. The path that is the path of liberation (<s>vimuktimārga</s>) — for it is the support of abandonment, because it supports the acquisition of that [abandonment]. 'That by which [something] is supported is the support' — it itself is the antidote, hence the antidote of support. For example, after the <s>duḥkhadharmajñānakṣānti</s>, the <s>duḥkhadharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of the truth of suffering) — therefore it is said. 'By which that was brought about' — in detail. By which path that was brought about — the abandonment brought about by the uninterrupted path — is supported. The antidote of support has the nature of non-interruption of that acquisition. 'The antidote of distancing (<s>dūrībhāvapratipakṣa</s>)' — in detail. That by which the acquisition of the affliction becomes distant is the distancing. That itself is the antidote, hence the antidote of distancing. Or, the act of making distant is the distancing; the antidote for that is the antidote of distancing. 'The path after the path of liberation' — that which is the path of liberation, namely the <s>duḥkhadharmajñāna</s>; the path after that, namely the <s>duḥkhānvayajñānakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the inferential knowledge of suffering) and so forth — he shows that to be the antidote of distancing.

body.text: vimuktimārgo 'pīty apara iti. [Tib. 160a] sa cāpy ādyo vimuktimārgo dūrībhāvapratipakṣa ity ucyate. so 'pi hi tāṃ kleśaprāptiṃ dūrīkaroti. evaṃ ca sati vimuktimārga ādhārapratipakṣo dūrībhāvapratipakṣa iti vaca nāmadvayaṃ labhata ity uktaṃ bhavati. taṃ dhātuṃ doṣato darśanād vidūṣayatīti. anityādibhir ākārair yena taṃ dhātuṃ vidūṣayatīty arthaḥ. tad evaṃ sati yo 'pi duḥkhasamudayālaṃbanaḥ prahāṇapratipakṣādiḥ. sa cāpi vidūṣaṇāpratipakṣa iti darśitaṃ bhavatīti. api tv iyam ānupūrvī sādhvī bhaved ity ācāryaḥ. sopānanyāyasamāśrayāt lakṣaṇāsāṃkaryāc ceyam ānupūrvī sādhvīti darśayati. duḥkhasamudayālaṃbanaḥ prayogamārga iti. prayogamārga evoṣmagatādi gṛhyate. nānaṃtaryamārgādi. prahāṇapratipakṣāditvena tadvyavasthāpanāt. sarvānaṃtaryamārga iti. paścātkālīno 'pi yo 'nyaḥ. vimuktimārgaḥ sarva ity eva cādhikriyate. viśeṣamārgas tu ya etattrayavyatiriktaḥ. sa iha gṛhyate.
body.translated_text: 'The path of liberation too' — says another. That first path of liberation too is called the antidote of distancing. For it too makes that acquisition of the affliction distant. And this being so, the path of liberation receives two names — the antidote of support and the antidote of distancing — this has been stated. 'Because of seeing that realm (<s>dhātu</s>) as a fault, it debases it' — the meaning is: by which, through the aspects of impermanence and the rest, it debases that realm. This being so, it is shown that the antidote of abandonment and the rest that have suffering and origination as their objects — they too are antidotes of debasement (<s>vidūṣaṇāpratipakṣa</s>). 'But this sequence would be proper' — says the <s>Ācārya</s>. He shows that this sequence is proper, based on the analogy of a staircase and because of non-confusion of characteristics. 'The preparatory path (<s>prayogamārga</s>) that has suffering and origination as its object' — only the preparatory path, such as the heat stage (<s>uṣmagata</s>) and so forth, is taken [as the antidote of debasement], not the uninterrupted path and so forth — because those are established as antidotes of abandonment and the rest. 'All uninterrupted paths' — even those that come later. 'All' applies precisely to the path of liberation. But the special path (<s>viśeṣamārga</s>), which is distinct from these three — that is taken here [as the antidote of distancing].

body.text: (V.60cd) na hi saṃprayogāt kleśo vivecayituṃ śakyata iti. svakalāpāt vivecanāśakyatvāt. [Tib. 160b] anāgatas tāvac chakyetālaṃbanād vivecayituṃ. vivecitasya
body.translated_text: (V.60cd) For an affliction cannot be separated from its association — because of the impossibility of separating it from its own aggregate. A future [affliction] can indeed be separated from its object — of the separated one,

body.text: tasya na punas tad vastv ālaṃbyotpattir ity ataḥ kāraṇāt. atītas tu kathaṃ yad vastvālaṃbyotpannaḥ. na hy ālaṃbitaṃ vastv anālaṃbinīkartuṃ śakyate. eṣo 'pi naikāṃta iti. caturbhiḥ prakāraiḥ kleśānāṃ kṣaya iṣyate.
body.translated_text: that one does not arise again taking that object — for this reason. But how [can] a past [affliction be separated], which has already arisen taking that object? For an object that has been taken cannot be made un-taken. 'This too is not absolute' — the destruction of afflictions is accepted in four ways:

children.text:
ālaṃbanaparijñānāt tadālaṃbanasaṃkṣayāt
ālaṃbanaprahāṇāc ca pratipakṣodayāt kṣaya
children.translated_text:
'Through the full knowledge of the object, through the destruction of that object,
through the abandonment of the object, and through the arising of the antidote — destruction' —

body.text: iti. tasmād ālaṃbanaparijñānād iti nāyam ekāṃtaḥ. tasmād vaktavyam etad iti parihartavyam etad ity arthaḥ. atrācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ pariharati. ālaṃbanāt kleśāḥ prahātavyāḥ. ālaṃbanaparijñānabalena hi kleśāḥ prahīyaṃte. dvividhaṃ cānuśayālaṃbanaṃ. saṃyogavastu asaṃyogavastu ca. tatra saṃyogavastuviṣayāṇām anuśayānāṃ tadanuśayabalotpāditānām atadviṣayāṇām api pudgalasya saṃtāne prāptir akliṣṭacittasyāpy avicchedena pravartate. anāgatātītakleśahetuphalabhūtā. evam asaṃyogavastuviṣayāṇām atadviṣayāṇām api ca tadviṣayakleśapṛṣṭhasamudācariṇāṃ kleśānāṃ prāptir veditavyā. sā hy anāgatānām utpattau pratyayagamanād dhetubhūtā bhavati. atītānāṃ ca niṣyandabhāvāt [Tib. 161a] phalabhūtā. sā ca tatprahāṇapratipakṣaniṣyandaprāptisamavadhānaviruddhā. tadādhāritatvāt kleśānām. ato yenālaṃbanenotpannāḥ kleśā anyālaṃbanān api kleśān pravartayaṃti. tadālaṃbanaprahāṇapratipakṣaniṣyandotpattau tatprāptivigame te kleśās tadālaṃbanā api saṃto hetuphalāpakrāṃtāḥ prahīṇā ity ucyaṃte. tad yasmād aparijñāte kasmiṃścit kleśaviṣaye atadviṣayāṇām api kleśānāṃ tadviṣayakleśabalenaprāptir anāgatātītakleśahetuphalabhūtā saṃtatau pravartate yathā vastu. tasmād ālaṃbanāt kleśāḥ prahātavyā ity abhimataṃ iti.
body.translated_text: thus. Therefore, 'through the full knowledge of the object' — this is not absolute. Therefore this must be explained — meaning: this must be resolved. Here, <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Saṃghabhadra</s> resolves [it]. Afflictions are to be abandoned through the object. For it is by the power of full knowledge of the object that afflictions are abandoned. And the object of latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>) is twofold: the connected object (<s>saṃyogavastu</s>) and the unconnected object (<s>asaṃyogavastu</s>). Therein, for latent dispositions whose domain is the connected object — those produced by the power of that latent disposition, even those whose domain is other [than the connected object] — in the person's continuum, the acquisition continues uninterruptedly even for one with undefiled consciousness. [This acquisition is] the cause and fruit of past and future afflictions. Similarly, for latent dispositions whose domain is the unconnected object, and also for those whose domain is other [than that], the acquisition of afflictions that manifest subsequently to afflictions of that domain should be understood. For that [acquisition] becomes a cause, since upon the arising of future [afflictions], it serves as the approach to conditions. And it is a fruit, since it is of the nature of the outflow of past [afflictions]. And that [acquisition] is opposed by the concurrence of the outflow-acquisition of the antidote of abandonment of that [object]. Because afflictions are based on that [acquisition]. Therefore, afflictions that have arisen in a certain object activate afflictions having other objects too. Upon the arising of the outflow of the antidote of abandonment of that object, upon the disappearance of that acquisition, those afflictions — even while being objects of that — having departed from the status of cause and fruit, are said to be 'abandoned.' Since, when a certain domain of affliction is not fully known, the acquisition of afflictions having other domains too — produced by the power of afflictions having that domain — continues in the continuum as cause and fruit of past and future afflictions, as applicable — therefore the accepted position is: afflictions are to be abandoned through the object.

body.text: nanu ca tadālaṃbanaprahāṇādibhir api kleśāḥ prahīyaṃta ity abhipretaṃ. kim idam uktam ālaṃbanaparijñānabalena kleśāḥ prahīyaṃta iti. te 'pi duḥkhasatyādiparijñānabalenaiva prahīyaṃte. tadbhāvābhāvayoge tadbhāvābhāvayogāt. yeṣām api hi pratipakṣodayāt prahāṇam ucyate. te 'pi bhāvanāheyāḥ. kleśā ālaṃbanaduḥkhasatyādiparijñānabalenaiva prahīyaṃta ity avagaṃtavyaṃ. vyavasthāmātraṃ tu tad yad uktaṃ. tadālaṃbanaprahāṇādibhir [Tib. 161b] api kleśāḥ prahīyanta ity abhiprāyo lakṣyate.
body.translated_text: But is it not accepted that afflictions are also abandoned through the destruction of that object and the rest? Why then is it said that afflictions are abandoned by the power of full knowledge of the object? Those too are abandoned by the power of the full knowledge of the truth of suffering and the rest as objects. Because of the correlation: when that [full knowledge] exists, those exist; when that [full knowledge] is absent, those are absent. For even those whose abandonment is said to be through the arising of the antidote — those too, being to be abandoned by cultivation, are afflictions that should be understood as abandoned by the power of full knowledge of the object, namely the truth of suffering and the rest. It is merely a classificatory [distinction] that was stated — 'afflictions are also abandoned through the destruction of that object and the rest' — this is the discerned intention.

body.text: svāsāṃtānikaḥ prāpticchedād iti vistaraḥ. svasaṃtānakleśaḥ prāptivigamāt prahīṇo vaktavyaḥ. parasaṃtānakleśas tu na prāpticchedāt. svasaṃtāne tatprāptyabhāvāt. kiṃ tarhi tadālaṃbanasvāsāṃtānikakleśaprahāṇāt. pārasāṃtānikakleśālaṃbanasvāsāṃtānikakleśaprāpticchedād ity arthaḥ. sarvaṃ
body.translated_text: 'One's own continuum — through the cutting of acquisition' — in detail. An affliction of one's own continuum should be said to be abandoned through the disappearance of acquisition. But an affliction of another's continuum is not [abandoned] through the cutting of acquisition — because of the absence of its acquisition in one's own continuum. Then through what? Through the abandonment of an affliction of one's own continuum that has that [other's affliction] as its object. The meaning is: through the cutting of the acquisition of an affliction of one's own continuum that has the affliction of another's continuum as its object. All

body.text: rūpaṃ kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtaṃ. akliṣṭaś ca dharma ity arūpī kuśalasāsravaṃ anivṛtavyākṛtaś ca. tathaiva tadālaṃbanasvāsāṃtānikakleśaprahāṇāt prahīṇo vaktavya iti.
body.translated_text: form — wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. And the undefiled <s>dharma</s> that is formless — wholesome with outflows, and the unobstructed indeterminate. In the same way, it should be said to be abandoned through the abandonment of an affliction of one's own continuum that has that [form or undefiled dharma] as its object.

children.translated_text: 'Like [the distance] of elements, virtue, regions, and the pair of time-periods' —

body.text: ivaśabdo 'trodāhāraṇaṃ. tadyathārthe draṣṭavyaḥ. vailakṣaṇyāl lakṣaṇadūratā. tadyathā bhūtānāṃ. bhinnalakṣaṇo hi pṛthivīdhātor abdhātus tasmāt pṛthivīdhātor abdhātur dūre bhavati. vipakṣatvād vipakṣadūratā. tadyathā śīlasya dauḥśīlyaṃ. deśavicchedāt deśadūratā. tadyathā pradeśasya paścimasamudrasya pūrvasamudrāt. kālataḥ kāladūratā. tadyathādhvadvayasyātītānāgatalakṣaṇasya. [Tib. 162a] tad dhy atītānāgataṃ dūram ucyate. kvocyate. abhidharme. evaṃ hy āha. dūre dharmāḥ katame. atītānāgatā dharmāḥ. aṃtike dharmāḥ katame. pratyutpannā dharmāḥ. asaṃskṛtaṃ ceti. tad dūram iti. tad atītānāgatam.
body.translated_text: the word 'like' (<s>iva</s>) here is for illustration — it should be seen as meaning 'such as.' Distance of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇadūratā</s>) — because of difference of characteristics. Such as [the distance] of elements: for the water element (<s>abdhātu</s>), having a different characteristic from the earth element (<s>pṛthivīdhātu</s>), is distant from that earth element. Distance of opposition (<s>vipakṣadūratā</s>) — because of being opposites. Such as bad conduct (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>) [is distant] from virtue (<s>śīla</s>). Distance of place (<s>deśadūratā</s>) — because of spatial separation. Such as [the distance] of a region: the western ocean from the eastern ocean. Distance of time (<s>kāladūratā</s>) — in terms of time. Such as the pair of time-periods (<s>adhvadvaya</s>) characterized as past and future. For the past and future are called distant. Where is this stated? In the <s>Abhidharma</s>. For thus it says: 'What <s>dharma</s>s are distant? Past and future <s>dharma</s>s. What <s>dharma</s>s are near? Present <s>dharma</s>s. And the unconditioned' — that is distant — that which is past and future.

body.text: utpadyamānaṃ ceti. utpādābhimukham anāgataṃ cety arthaḥ. na cirabhūtabhāvitveneti. na cirabhūtatvenātītaṃ nāpi cirabhāvitvenānāgataṃ dūram ity arthaḥ. vartamānam apy evaṃ dūraṃ prāpnotīti. adhvanānātvena pratyutpanno 'dhvatayā vartamānam api dūraṃ prāpnoti. yathātītānāgatam atītānāgatādhvatayā. akāritrāt tarhi tad dūram iti. uparatakāritram atītam aprāptakāritram anāgatam iti. tad atītānāgataṃ dūram ucyate. asaṃskṛtasya katham aṃtikatvam iti. tasya kāritrābhāvād aṃtikatvaṃ na syāt. tac ceṣyate aṃtike dharmāḥ katame. pratyutpannā dharmāḥ. asaṃskṛtaṃ ceti śāstrapāṭhāt. sarvatra tatprāpter iti. sarvatra deśe tasyāsaṃskṛtasya pratisaṃkhyāpratisaṃkhyānirodhasya prāptyutpādāt. atītānāgate 'pi [Tib. 162b] prasaṃga iti kuśalāder atītānāgatasya sarvatra deśe prāptiḥ saṃbhavatīty atītānāgate 'py aṃtikatvaprasaṃgaḥ. ākāśaṃ ca katham iti. ākāśaṃ ca katham aṃtikaṃ. na hi tasya prāptir astīti. atītānāgatam anyonyam iti. atītād anāgataṃ dūram anāgatāc cātītam ity arthaḥ. asaṃskṛtaṃ cāvyavahitatvād iti. na kenacid vyavahitaṃ. yathā vartamānenātītānāgatam iti. evaṃ tasyāṃtikatvaṃ. evam apīti. asyām api kalpanāyāṃ. yad anaṃtaram atītānāgataṃ. tad vartamānasyāṃtikatvād ubhayaṃ prāpnoti. dūram āsannaṃ ceti. tad dhy atītaṃ vartamānāṃtaritatvād anāgatād dūraṃ. vartamānāc cāvyavahitatvād aṃtikam iti prāpnoti. ity evam anāgatam api neyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'And that which is arising' — that which is facing arising, meaning the future — this is the meaning. 'Not because of having existed long ago' — not because of having existed long ago is the past distant, nor because of being to exist far in the future is the future distant — this is the meaning. 'Even the present would then attain distance' — since it is different from the [other] time-periods, even what is present would attain distance by being a different time-period from the past and future — just as the past and future [are distant] by being past and future time-periods. 'Then that would be distant because of non-functioning (<s>akāritra</s>)' — the past has ceased functioning; the future has not yet attained functioning — thus, the past and future are called distant. 'How is the unconditioned near?' — because of the absence of functioning in it, [the unconditioned] should not be near. Yet this is accepted: 'What <s>dharma</s>s are near? Present <s>dharma</s>s. And the unconditioned' — from the reading of the treatise.
