'Because of the acquisition of it everywhere' — because in every place, the acquisition of that unconditioned — [namely] analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) and non-analytical cessation (<s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) — arises. 'The consequence [would apply] to the past and future too' — because the acquisition of wholesome and the rest that are past and future is possible in every place, there would be the consequence of nearness for the past and future too. 'And what about space (<s>ākāśa</s>)?' — and how is space near? For there is no acquisition of it. 'The past and the future [are distant] from each other' — the future is distant from the past, and the past from the future — this is the meaning. 'And the unconditioned, because of not being obstructed' — not obstructed by anything — as the past and future are by the present — thus its nearness. 'Even so' — even in this supposition: 'that which is immediately past and future' — that, because of the nearness of the present, attains both — distance and nearness. For that which is past, being separated by the present from the future, is distant from the future; and being not obstructed from the present, it attains nearness. Thus the future too should be understood.

body.text: evaṃ tu yuktaṃ syād iti. svamatam ācāryasya. dharmasvalakṣaṇād anāgataṃ dūraṃ. kasmāt. asaṃprāptatvāt. yasmād anāgatena svalakṣaṇaṃ na saṃprāptam
body.translated_text: 'But this would be proper' — this is the <s>Ācārya</s>'s own view. The future is distant from the own-characteristic of a <s>dharma</s>. Why? Because of not having attained [it]. Because by the future, its own-characteristic has not been attained

body.text: iti. atha vā yasmāt tatsvalakṣaṇam asaṃprāptam anupasthitam iti. atītaṃ ca. kiṃ dharmasvalakṣaṇād dūraṃ. tatpracyutatvāt. yasmāt tad dharmasvalakṣaṇaṃ. tasmād atītāt pracyutaṃ. tad dhy atītaṃ yad dharmasvalakṣaṇāt pracyutam iti.
body.translated_text: . Or alternatively, because that own-characteristic has not been attained, has not been established. And the past — is it too distant from the own-characteristic of a <s>dharma</s>? Because of having fallen away from it. Because that <s>dharma</s>'s own-characteristic has fallen away from the past. For that which is past is what has fallen away from the <s>dharma</s>'s own-characteristic.

children.translated_text: 'Through the arising of the antidote, destruction' —

body.text: ity uktam. ataḥ pṛcchati. kiṃ mārgaviśeṣagamanād iti vistaraḥ. prahāṇaviśeṣa [Tib. 163a] iti. viśiṣyate prahāṇam ity arthaḥ. pratipakṣo vimuktimārga etasminn abhipreta iti. tasya visaṃyogaprāptisahotpādād ānaṃtaryamārge hi na tāvad visaṃyogaprāptir asti. utpādābhimukhatvāt. vimuktimārgo 'pi hi pratipakṣa iti śakyate vyavasthāpayituṃ. mukhyapratipakṣeṇānaṃtaryamārgeṇa sahaikakāryatvāt. tathā hy uktam ubhābhyāṃ hi tasya prāptiḥ visaṃyogaprāpter āvāhakasaṃniśrayatvād iti. phalāni catvārīti. caturgrahaṇam ekānnanavatiphalapratipattinirāsārthaṃ. puruṣakārādipaṃcaphalapratipattinirāsārthaṃ vā. phalaprāptir api vimuktimārgāvasthāyām eva gṛhyate. visaṃyogalābhāstitvayogād indriyavivṛddhiḥ indriyasaṃcāra iti. indriyādhikyapratipattinirāsārtham etad arthapradarśanaṃ indriyavivṛddhir ity ucyate. phalaprāptivacanenaiva siddher ity ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ. atra brūmaḥ. satyaṃ phalaprāptir evendriyavivṛddhiḥ. phalaprāptiviśeṣas tu pradarśayitavyo yatra punar visaṃyogaphalalābho bhavati. anyathā hi phalaprāptivacanam api na kartavyaṃ syāt. pratipakṣodayavacanenaiva tatsiddheḥ. [Tib. 163b] ity alam anayātikhalinikayā. keṣāṃcid yāvad dvayor iti. keṣāṃcit kleśānāṃ ṣaṭsu kāleṣu viaṃyogalābhaḥ. yāvacchabdena keṣāṃcit paṃcasu. keṣāṃcic caturṣu. keṣāṃcit triṣu. keṣāṃcid dvayor iti. keṣāṃcid dvayor iti. keṣāṃcid ekāsmin kāla iti noktaṃ. punaḥprāptasya visaṃyogasyādhikṛtatvāt. saṃbhavati hi bhāvāgrikasya navamasya prakārasyaikasminn eva kāle tīkṣṇendriyasya visaṃyogalābhaḥ. sa tu na punarlābha iti nocyate. tatra tāvan mṛdvindriyasya ṣaṭsu kāleṣu visaṃyogalābhaḥ. duḥkhasamudayanirodhadarśanaheyānāṃ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ mārgadarśanaheyānāṃ pratipakṣodayakāle. srotaāpattiphalakāle sakṛdāgāmiphalakāle 'nāgāmiphalakāle 'rhattvaphalakāle indriyasaṃcārakāle ceti ṣaṭsu kāleṣu visaṃyogalābhaḥ. saṃbhavaṃ ca praty evam ucyate. na hi mṛdvindriyo 'vaśyam indriyāṇi saṃcarati. tasyaiva mṛdvindriyasya rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ mārgadarśanaheyānāṃ mārgānvayajñānakāle pratipakṣodayakāla iti vā phalaprāptikāla iti vā gṛhīte prathamato visaṃyogalābhaḥ. punaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalaprāptikāle
body.translated_text: — thus it was stated. Therefore he asks. 'Is it from the attainment of a distinction of path?' — and so forth in detail. 'Distinction of abandonment' — the meaning is: the abandonment is distinguished. 'The counteragent intended here is the liberation-path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>)' — because its acquisition of disconnection (<s>visaṃyogaprāpti</s>) arises simultaneously with it. For in the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), there is not yet an acquisition of disconnection, because it faces toward arising. The liberation-path too can be established as a counteragent, because of its having a single function together with the primary counteragent, the uninterrupted path. For thus it was stated: 'The acquisition [of disconnection] is from both, because [they] serve as the vehicle and support for the acquisition of disconnection.' 'The fruits are four' — the mention of 'four' is for the purpose of rejecting the view that there are eighty-nine fruits, or for the purpose of rejecting the view of five fruits beginning with the fruit of human effort (<s>puruṣakāra</s>). The attainment of fruit is also understood as [occurring] in the state of the liberation-path alone, because of the connection with obtaining disconnection. '<s>Indriyavivṛddhi</s> (faculty-growth), <s>indriyasaṃcāra</s> (faculty-transfer)' — this illustration of meaning is called 'faculty-growth' for the purpose of rejecting the view that there is an excess of faculties. 'Because it is established by the very statement of fruit-attainment' — says <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s>. To this we say: it is true that faculty-growth is indeed fruit-attainment; however, the specific kind of fruit-attainment where there is again the obtaining of the fruit of disconnection must be shown. Otherwise, even the statement of fruit-attainment would not need to be made, because that would be established by the very statement of the arising of the counteragent. Thus, enough of this overly restive [horse]. 'For some, up to two [occasions]' — for some afflictions, the obtaining of disconnection [occurs] in six occasions. By the word 'up to,' for some in five, for some in four, for some in three, for some in two. 'In one occasion' is not stated, because the topic is the re-obtaining of disconnection. For it is possible that the obtaining of disconnection for the ninth type of the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) [occurs] in just one occasion for one of sharp faculties; but that is not a re-obtaining, so it is not mentioned. Therein, first, for one of dull faculties (<s>mṛdvindriya</s>), the obtaining of disconnection [occurs] in six occasions: at the time of the arising of the counteragent for those to be abandoned by seeing suffering, origination, and cessation belonging to the Desire Realm and those to be abandoned by seeing the path; at the time of the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpatti</s>); at the time of the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmi</s>); at the time of the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmi</s>); at the time of the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship; and at the time of faculty-transfer — thus the obtaining of disconnection in six occasions. And this is stated with reference to possibility, for one of dull faculties does not necessarily transfer faculties.

body.text:
yāvad indriyasaṃcārakāla iti paṃcasu kāleṣu. bhāvanāheyānām api tasyaive kāmāvacarāṇāṃ paṃcaprakārāṇāṃ adhimātrādhimātrasya yāvan madhyamadhyasya. [Tib. 164a] teṣv eva srotaāpattiphalakālavarjyeṣu paṃcasu kāleṣu visaṃyogalābhaḥ. madhyamṛdos tu ṣaṣṭhasya prakārasya tasyaiva caturṣu kāleṣu. pratipakṣodayaphalaprāptikālayor ekatvāt. tasminn anyatarasmin. anāgāmiphalakāle. arhattvaphalaprāptikāle. indriyasaṃcārakāle ceti. tasyaiva mṛdvadhimātrasya mṛdumadhyasya ca saptamāṣṭamayoḥ prakārayoḥ pratipakṣodayakāle 'nāgāmiphalakāle yāvad indriyasaṃcārakāle veti caturṣv eva kāleṣu visaṃyogalābhaḥ. tasyaiva mṛdumṛdor aṃtyasya prakārasya pratipakṣodayakāla iti vā phalaprāptikāla iti vaikatarasmin. arhattvaphalakāle. indriyasaṃcārakāle ceti triṣu kāleṣu visaṃyogalābhaḥ. tasyaivārhattvaphalaṃ prāpnuvato ye navaprakārā rūpārūpyāvacarāḥ kleśā bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ prahīṇāḥ adhimātradhimātro yāvan mṛdumṛdur iti. teṣāṃ bhāvāgrikaṃ mṛdumṛduprakāram aṃtyaṃ hitvā sarveṣāṃ triṣv eva kāleṣu visaṃyogalābhaḥ. pratipakṣodayakāle 'rhattvaphalakāle indriyasaṃcārakāle
ceti. yas tv asyaivārūpyāvacaro mṛdumṛdur aṃtyaḥ kleśaprakāraḥ. tasya pratipakṣodayārhattvaphalaprāptikālaikatvāt. pratipakṣodayakāla iti vārhattvaphalakāla iti vā anyatarasminn indriyasaṃcārakāle ceti. [Tib. 164b] dvayoḥ kālayor visaṃyogalābha iti. evaṃ tāvan mṛdvindriyasyoktaṃ. tīkṣṇendriyasya punaḥ keṣāṃcit kleśānāṃ paṃcasu kāleṣu. keṣāṃcid yāvad dvayor iti vaktavyaṃ. indriyasaṃcārakālam ekam apāsya. tasya hi sarvatrendriyasaṃcāro nāsti. tasyaikasminn eva kāle kleśānāṃ visaṃyogalābho 'sti. bhāvāgrikasya bhāvanāheyasya mṛdumṛdoḥ prakārasya. sa tu punarlābho na bhavatīti na vaktavya iti paśyāmaḥ.
body.translated_text: For that very one of dull faculties, at the time of <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge of the path) for those to be abandoned by seeing the path belonging to the Form and Formless Realms — whether this is taken as the time of the arising of the counteragent or the time of fruit-attainment — the first obtaining of disconnection [occurs]. Then, at the time of attaining the fruit of once-returning, up to the time of faculty-transfer — in five occasions. Even for those to be abandoned by cultivation, for that same [dull-faculty person], regarding the five types of Desire-Realm [afflictions] from the most intense of the most intense (<s>adhimātrādhimātra</s>) up to the middling of the middling (<s>madhyamadhya</s>) — in those same five occasions, excluding the time of the fruit of stream-entry, the obtaining of disconnection [occurs]. But for the sixth type, the mild-middling (<s>madhyamṛdu</s>), for that same [person], in four occasions — because the times of the arising of the counteragent and fruit-attainment are one. In one or the other of those; at the time of the fruit of non-returning; at the time of attaining the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship; and at the time of faculty-transfer. For the seventh and eighth types — the mild-intense (<s>mṛdvadhimātra</s>) and mild-middling (<s>mṛdumadhya</s>) — of that same [person], the obtaining of disconnection in exactly four occasions: at the time of the arising of the counteragent, at the time of the fruit of non-returning, up to the time of faculty-transfer. For the final type — the mild of the mild (<s>mṛdumṛdu</s>) — of that same [person], at one or the other of the time of the arising of the counteragent or the time of fruit-attainment; at the time of the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship; and at the time of faculty-transfer — the obtaining of disconnection in three occasions. For that same one attaining the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship, whichever nine types of afflictions belonging to the Form and Formless Realms that are to be abandoned by cultivation have been abandoned — from the most intense of the most intense up to the mild of the mild — for all of them, excluding the final mild-of-the-mild type belonging to the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>), the obtaining of disconnection in exactly three occasions: at the time of the arising of the counteragent, at the time of the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship, and at the time of faculty-transfer. But for the final type — the mild of the mild belonging to the Formless Realm — since the times of the arising of the counteragent and the attainment of the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship are one: at one or the other of the time of the arising of the counteragent or the time of the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship, and at the time of faculty-transfer — the obtaining of disconnection in two occasions. Thus, this has been stated for one of dull faculties. For one of sharp faculties (<s>tīkṣṇendriya</s>), however, for some afflictions in five occasions, for some up to two — this should be stated, removing the single [occasion] of the time of faculty-transfer. For that one does not have faculty-transfer at all. That one has the obtaining of disconnection from afflictions in just one occasion — for the mild-of-the-mild type of what is to be abandoned by cultivation belonging to the Peak of Existence. But that is not a re-obtaining — so we consider it should not be stated.

body.text: (V.63, 64) phale hetūpacārād iti. prahāṇaṃ phalaṃ parijñā jñānasvabhāvo hetuḥ tasmin prahāṇe. phale hetūpacāraḥ. prahāṇaṃ parijñeti. tadyathā ṣaḍ imāni sparśāyatanāni pūrvam abhisaṃskṛtāny abhisaṃcetitāni paurāṇaṃ karma veditavyaṃ iti. kaḥ punaḥ prahāṇaṃ parijñāśabdenāpadiśate. sūtre evaṃ hi paṭhyate. parijñeyāṃś ca vo bhikṣavo dharmān deśayiṣyāmi. parijñāṃ ca parijñāvantaṃ ca pudgalaṃ. parijñeyā dharmāḥ katame. paṃcopādānaskandhāḥ. parijñā katamā. yad atra cchandarāgaprahāṇaṃ. chandarāgasamatikramaḥ. iyam ucyate parijñeti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: (V.63, 64) 'Through figurative designation of the cause upon the fruit' — abandonment is the fruit; comprehension (<s>parijñā</s>), having the nature of knowledge, is the cause, in relation to that abandonment. [This is] the figurative designation of the cause upon the fruit — 'abandonment is comprehension.' Just as: 'These six sense-spheres (<s>sparśāyatana</s>), previously conditioned and intended — this should be understood as ancient <s>karma</s>.' Who then designates abandonment by the word 'comprehension'? In the <s>sūtra</s>, for thus it is read: 'I shall teach you, O monks, the <s>dharma</s>s to be comprehended, comprehension, and the person who has comprehended. What are the <s>dharma</s>s to be comprehended? The five clinging-aggregates (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>). What is comprehension? Whatever abandonment of desire-attachment (<s>chandarāga</s>) therein, the transcendence of desire-attachment — this is called comprehension' — and so forth in detail.

children.translated_text: 'The exhaustion of the two non-types of sensual desire and the rest' —

body.text: eketi.
body.translated_text: 'is one.'

children.translated_text:
'From the obtaining of uncontaminated disconnection, from the impairment of the Peak of Existence,
from the destruction of two causes, comprehension is from the transcendence of a realm' —

body.text: ity atra parijñāvyavasthāpane kāraṇaṃ vakṣyate. avarabhāgīyaprahāṇam iti. kāmadhātvāsravaprahāṇam ity arthaḥ. iyam eva cāsyāḥ saṃjñā. rūpāsravaprahāṇam iti. rūpadhātvāsravaprahāṇam ity arthaḥ. rūparāgakṣayaparijñety asyā nāma. yady apy anyeṣāṃ kleśopakleśānāṃ mānādīnāṃ rūpāvacarāṇāṃ prahāṇam iyaṃ parijñā vyavasthāpyate. rāgasya tu tatra prādhānyād ūrdhvabhāgīyasya saṃyojanasya prahāṇaṃ rūparāgakṣayaparijñety uktaṃ. sarvasaṃyojanaparyādāna [kun tu sbyor ba thams cad yoṅs su grugs paḥi] yoṅs su śes paḥo. ṣes bya ba ḥdi ni zag pa thams cad spaṅs paḥi miṅ yin no. yoṅs su śes pa ni tha dad par bstan la. ṣes bya ba ni bsgroms pas spaṅ bar bya ba gzugs na spyod pa rnams spaṅs pa ni gzugs kyi ḥdod chags zad paḥi yoṅs su śes pa yin no. gzugs med par nams kyi ni kun tu sbyor ba thams cad yoṅs su grugs paḥi yoṅs su śes pa yin no. ṣes ḥbyuṅ baḥi phyir ro. mthoṅ baḥi spaṅ bar bya bar nams kyi ni ma yin te. ṣes bya ba ni ciḥi phyir gzugs daṅ gzugs med pa na spyod paḥi mthoṅ bas spaṅ bar bya bar nams kyi yoṇs su śes pa so sor mi bstan te. de bṣin du gzugs daṅ gzugs med pa na spyod pa mthoṅ bas spaṅ bar bya bar nams spaṅs pa yaṅ yoṅs su śes pa gsum yin te. ṣe ḥbyuṅ baḥi phyir ro. bsgom pa spaṅ bar bya bar nams kyi gñen po mi ḥdra baḥi phyir ro ṣes bya ba ni ḥdi ltar sa daṅ sa na gzugs na spyod [Tib. 165b] paḥi bsgom pas spaṅ bar bya ba rnam pa dguḥi gñen po bar chad med pa daṅ rnam par grol baḥi lam zag pa med pa mi lcogs pa med pa la sogs paḥi sa daṅ zag pa daṅ bcas pa bsam gtan gñis paḥi ñer ba stogs kyis bsdus pa nas nam mkhaḥ mthaḥ yas skye mched kyi ñer bsdogs kyis bsdus paḥi bar rnam pa dgu yod la gzugs med pa na spyod pa rnams kyi gñen po bar chad med paḥi lam daṅ. rnam par grol baḥi lam in ci rigs par zug pa med paḥi sa ḥog ma pa ḥam. ci rigs par zag pa daṅ bcas pa goṅ maḥi ñer bsdogs kyis bsdus pa dag yod de. gṣan kho na yin pas gñen po mi ḥdra baḥi phyir ḥdi dag gis yoṅs su 'śes pa tha dad par stan to. mthoṅ bas spaṅ bar bya ba rnams kyi gñen po ni ḥdra ste. rjes su śes paḥi bzod pa la sogs pa gzugs na spyod par nams kyi gñen po de dag ñid gzugs med par nams kyi yaṅ yin pas yoṅs su śes pa tha tad du rnam par mi bṣag go.
body.translated_text: herein, the reason for the establishment of comprehension will be stated. 'The abandonment of the lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīya</s>)' — the meaning is: the abandonment of the outflows of the Desire Realm. And this very name belongs to it. 'The abandonment of the outflow of form' — the meaning is: the abandonment of the outflows of the Form Realm. Its name is 'the comprehension of the exhaustion of passion for form' (<s>rūparāgakṣayaparijñā</s>). Although this comprehension is established as the abandonment of other afflictions and secondary afflictions such as pride and the rest belonging to the Form Realm, nevertheless, because of the predominance of passion therein, the abandonment of the upper fetters (<s>ūrdhvabhāgīya</s>) is called 'the comprehension of the exhaustion of passion for form.' [The Tibetan passage continues:] The comprehension of the complete exhaustion of all fetters — this is the name for the abandonment of all outflows. Comprehension is shown as distinct. That is to say: the abandonment of those to be abandoned by cultivation belonging to the Form Realm is the comprehension of the exhaustion of passion for form. Those of the Formless Realm constitute the comprehension of the complete exhaustion of all fetters. Because it so arises. Those to be abandoned by seeing are not [separately named] — because the counteragents of those to be abandoned by seeing belonging to the Form and Formless Realms are not separately established as comprehensions, since the very counteragents of those belonging to the Form Realm are also [counteragents] of those belonging to the Formless Realm. Similarly, the abandonment of those to be abandoned by seeing belonging to the Form and Formless Realms is also threefold comprehension, because it so arises. Because the counteragents of those to be abandoned by cultivation are dissimilar — for thus: the counteragents — uninterrupted paths and liberation paths — of the nine types to be abandoned by cultivation belonging to the Form Realm ground by ground are uncontaminated [paths] of the faculties of no-more-learning and the like, or contaminated [paths] included in the immediately higher preliminary stage, up to those included in the preliminary stage of the Infinity of Space sphere; and for those belonging to the Formless Realm, the counteragent uninterrupted paths and liberation paths, as applicable, belonging to a lower stage or, as applicable, contaminated [paths] included in a higher preliminary stage — these are exclusively different; because the counteragents are dissimilar, these comprehensions are separately established. But the counteragents of those to be abandoned by seeing are similar — the subsequent-knowledge tolerances and the rest that are the counteragents of those belonging to the Form Realm are also [counteragents] of those belonging to the Formless Realm, so comprehension is not separately established.

body.text: (V.64-66) tha maḥi cha daṅ mthun pa spaṅs pa la sogs pa yoṅs su śes pa ste ṣes bya ba ni tha maḥi cha daṅ ṃthun pa spaṅs paḥi yoṅs su śes pa daṅ. gzugs kyi ḥdod chags zad paḥi yoṅs su śes pa daṅ. kuntu sbyor ba thams cad yoṅs su gtugs paḥi yoṅs su śes paḥo. ḥdi dag ni bsgom paḥi lam gyi ḥbras bu yin paḥi phyir śes paḥi ḥbras bu yin te. bsgom paḥi lam la bzod pa dag ni med do.
body.translated_text: [The Tibetan continues:] The comprehension of the abandonment of the lower parts and the rest — namely: the comprehension of the abandonment of the lower parts, the comprehension of the exhaustion of passion for form, and the comprehension of the complete exhaustion of all fetters — these are the fruit of the path of cultivation, and therefore are the fruit of knowledge. For in the path of cultivation there are no tolerances.

body.text: ji ltar yoṅs su śes pa bzod paḥi ḥbras bu yin ṣes bya ba ni yoṅs su śes pa daṅ śes pa ṣes bya ba don gcig ste. śes pa daṅ yoṅs su śes pa ni zag pa med paḥi ye śes yin no ṣes ḥbyuṅ baḥi phyir ro. bam po bṣi bcu rtsa bṣi pa.
body.translated_text: As for 'How is comprehension the fruit of tolerance?' — comprehension and knowledge are synonymous. For knowledge and comprehension are uncontaminated wisdom — because it so arises. End of the forty-fourth chapter.

children.text: dri med bzod rnams śes pa med.

body.text: ṣas ḥbyuṅ bas bzod pa ni śes paḥi ṅo bo [Tib. 166a] ñid yin par yaṅ mi ruṅ na. de ji ltar yoṅs su śes pa bzod paḥi ḥbras bu yin te. ḥbras bu la rgyu btags byas na yaṅ mi ruṅ ṅo sñam du bsam pa yin no. ḥdir bzod pa rnams ni śes paḥi ḥkhor can yin paḥi phyir ṣes bya ba smos te. ḥdi dag la ḥkhor śes pa yod pas na śes paḥi ḥkhor can te. bzod par nams so. deḥi phyir śes paḥi ḥbras bu yaṅ bzod par nams kyi ḥbras bu ṣes byaḥo. rgyal baḥi ḥkhor la rgyal po ñe bar btags pa bṣin te dper na rgyal poḥi ḥkhor la rgyal po ñe bar btags paḥi phyir ḥkhor gyis byas pa la yaṅ rgyal pos byas pa ṣes byaa daṅ ḥdra ḥo. śes pa daṅ ḥbras bu gcig phyir ro ṣes bya ba ni bzod pa dag ni śes pa daṅ lhan cig ḥbras bu gcig pa yin te. bzod pa dag gi ḥbras bu gaṅ yin pa de ñid śes rnams kyi yin pas bzod paḥi ḥbras bu yaṅ yoṅs su śes par ruṅ ṅo.
body.translated_text: If patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) is not even of the nature of knowledge [Tib. 166a], then how is full comprehension (<s>parijñā</s>) the fruit of patience? Even figuratively applying [the name of] the cause to the fruit is not reasonable — this is the thought. Here he says: 'Because the patiences have knowledge as their retinue.' Because these [patiences] have knowledge as their retinue — they are 'having knowledge as retinue' — this is a concession to patience. Therefore, the fruit of knowledge too is conceded to be the fruit of patience. Just as [things] done by the retinue of a king are figuratively attributed to the king — because the king's [name] is figuratively applied to the king's retinue, what is done by the retinue is also said to be done by the king — in the same way. 'Because knowledge and [patience] share the same fruit' — the patiences share the same fruit as knowledge — whatever is the fruit of the patiences, that itself is [also the fruit] of knowledge. Therefore the fruit of patience too can be [called] full comprehension.

children.text: mi lcogs med ḥbras thams cad do
children.translated_text: 'All are the fruit of the irresistible [path]' (<s>ānantarya</s>) —

body.text: ṣes bya ba ni ḥdi ltar mi lcogs paḥi sa paḥi lam gyis khams gsum paḥi mthoṅ ba daṅ bsgom pas spaṅ bar bya baḥi zag pa rnams spaṅ ba srid de.
body.translated_text: this means: through the path of the irresistible level, it is possible to abandon the outflows to be abandoned by seeing and cultivation belonging to the three realms.

children.text: zag med mi lcogs med pa yis. thams cad las ni ḥdod chags bral.
children.translated_text:
'Through the outflow-free irresistible [path],
dispassion from all [is achieved]' —

body.text: ṣes ḥbyuṅ baḥi phyir ro. gzugs daṅ gzugs med pa na ñon moṅs pa spaṅs paḥi raṅ bṣin gaṅ dag yin paḥo. ṣes bya ba ni bye brag tu smra ba rnams na re gzugs daṅ gzugs med pa na spyod paḥi mthoṅ bas spaṅ bar bya ba rnams spaṅs pa ji skad bśad paḥi yoṅs su śes pa gsum daṅ. bsgom pas spaṅ bar bya ba gzugs na spyod pa rnams spaṅs pa gzugs kyi ḥdod chags zad paḥi yoṅs su śes pa daṅ gzugs med pa na spyod pa rnams spaṅs pa kun tu sbyor ba thams cad yoṅs su gtugs paḥi [Tib. 166b] yoṅs su śes pa ṣes bya ba lṅa ste. bsam gtan gyi dṅos gṣi la brten nas gzugs daṅ gzugs med pa na spyod paḥi ñon moṅs pa spoṅ ba srid paḥi phyir ro. ḥdod pa na spyod paḥi ñon moṅs pa spaṅs pa ni bsam gtan gi dṅos gṣiḥi ḥbras bu ma yin te. bsam gtan gyi dṅos gṣi rnams ni ḥdod paḥi
body.translated_text: because of this statement. 'Those that have the intrinsic nature of abandoning afflictions in the Form and Formless [Realms]' — the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s say: in the Form and Formless Realms, the three comprehensions as described — [resulting from] the abandonment of what is to be abandoned by seeing — and the comprehension of the exhaustion of form-realm desire from abandoning what is to be abandoned by cultivation in the Form Realm, and the comprehension of the exhaustion of all fetters from abandoning those operating in the Formless Realm — [Tib. 166b] making five, are the fruit of the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>s — because it is possible to abandon the afflictions operating in the Form and Formless Realms based on the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>s. But the abandonment of afflictions operating in the Desire Realm is not the fruit of the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>s — because the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>s

body.text: khams kyi gñen po ma yin paḥi phyir ro. de lta bas na ḥdod chags daṅ bral ba rnams la bral baḥi thob pa zag pa med pa yod du zin kyaṅ tha maḥi cha daṅ mthun pa spaṅs paḥi yoṅs su śes pa bṣin du ḥdod pa na spyod pa mthoṅ bas spaṅ bar bya ba spaṅs pa ni bsam gtan gyi dṅos gṣiḥi ḥbras bu ma yin no ṣes zer ro. btsun pa dbyaṅs sgrogs kyi lugs kyis ni brgyad de. ṣes bya ba ni btsun pa dbyaṅs sgrogs de ni ḥdod paḥi ḥdod chags daṅ bral baḥi gaṅ zag gi yaṅ ḥdod pa na spyod pa mthoṅ bas spaṅ bar bya ba rnams spaṅ spa yoṅs su śes pa gsum gyi ṅo bo ñid ḥphag paḥi lam gyi ḥbras bu yin par ḥdod do. ciḥi phyir ṣe na. bral baḥi thob pa zag pa med pa rñed paḥi phyir te. bsam gtan gyi dṅos gṣi la rten nas ṅes pa ḥjug pa na yaṅ ma thoṅ bas spaṅ bas spaṅ bar bya baḥi zag pa sṅon ḥjig rten paḥi lam gyis spaṅs pa rnams kyis bral baḥi thob pa zag pa med pa yaṅ ḥthob la de la na mthoṅ baḥi lam gyis nus pa yod pas gzugs daṅ gzugs med pa ba spyod paḥi mthoṅ bas spaṅ bar bya ba spaṅs pa bṣin du. ḥdod pa na spyod paḥi mthoṅ bas spaṅ bar bya ba sṅon spaṅs paḥi yoṅs su śes pa yaṅ dṅos gṣi bsam gtan gyi ḥbras buḥo ṣes bya bar rnam pa bṣag go. de lta ba sna ḥdod pa na spyod paḥi mthoṅ bas spaṅ bar bya ba spaṅs paḥi yoṅs su śes pa gsum po ḥdi dga daṅ sṅar bśad pa gzugs daṅ gzugs med paḥi yoṅs su śes pa daṅ bcas pa yoṅs su śes pa brgyad bsam gtan gyi ḥbras bu yin [Tib. 167a] no. śes bya ba ni btsun pa dbyaṅs sgrogs kyi gṣuṅ lugs yin no. tha maḥi cha daṅ mthun pa spaṅs paḥi yoṅs su śes pa ni mi lcogs pa med paḥi ḥbras bu kho na yin no. ṣes bya ba ni ḥdod pa las ḥdod chags ma bral ba ni mi lcogs pa med pa kho nas tha maḥi cha daṅ mthun pa spoṅ bar byed kyi dṅos gṣis ni ma yin te. de na ma thob paḥi phyir ro. ḥdod chags daṅ bral ba ston du ḥgro ba yaṅ gaṅ gi tshe bsam gtan la brten nas ñes pa la des kyaṅ so soḥi skye boḥi snas skabs na ḥjig rten paḥi lam gyis ḥdod pa na spyad paḥi ñon moṅs pa thams cad spaṅs pas de bsam gtan gyi dṅos gṣiḥi ḥbras bu ma yin no. sems kyi skad cig ma bcu drug la deḥi tha maḥi cha daṅ mthun pa spaṅs pa yoṅs su śes pa bsam gtan gyi dṅos gṣi la brten par yaṅ rnam par bṣag mod kyi deḥi ḥbras bu ṣes bya bar rnam par bṣag pa ni ma yin no. ḥo na ci ṣe na. gnas skabs de na tha maḥi cha daṅ mthun pa spaṅs pa ḥjig rten paḥi lam gyis thob paḥi bral baḥi thob pa zag pa med pa yaṅ ḥthob pas de spaṅ spaḥi yoṅs su śes par rnam par bṣag ste. deḥi tshe ni mthoṅ bas spaṅ bar bya ba sṅa ma spaṅs pas sṅar mthoṅ baḥi lam gyis spaṅ bar bya ba spaṅs pa gaṅ yin pa daṅ. sṅar spaṅs pa tha maḥi cha daṅ mthun pa spaṅs pa bsdoms nas tha maḥi cha daṅ mthun pa spaṅs paḥi yoṅs su śes pa gcig tu rnam par bṣag ste.
body.translated_text: are not the antidote of the Desire Realm. Therefore, even though outflow-free separation-acquisitions exist among the dispassions, the comprehension of abandoning what is concordant with the final portion — like the comprehension of abandoning what operates in the Desire Realm to be abandoned by seeing — is not the fruit of the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>. According to the venerable <s>Ghoṣaka</s>'s system, there are eight. The venerable <s>Ghoṣaka</s> accepts that even for a person who has become dispassionate from the Desire Realm, the abandoning of what operates in the Desire Realm to be abandoned by seeing — having the intrinsic nature of three comprehensions — is the fruit of the noble path. Why? Because of obtaining an outflow-free separation-acquisition. For even when entering the definite [path] based on the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>, the outflows to be abandoned by seeing that were previously abandoned by the mundane path also obtain an outflow-free separation-acquisition, and since the path of seeing has the power therein — just as the comprehension of abandoning what operates in the Form and Formless Realms to be abandoned by seeing — so too the comprehension of what was previously abandoned operating in the Desire Realm to be abandoned by seeing is established as the fruit of the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>. If so, these three comprehensions of abandoning what operates in the Desire Realm to be abandoned by seeing, together with the previously described Form and Formless comprehensions, [Tib. 167a] make eight comprehensions that are the fruit of the <s>dhyāna</s> — this is the venerable <s>Ghoṣaka</s>'s system. The comprehension of abandoning what is concordant with the final portion is exclusively the fruit of the irresistible [path]. For one who has not become dispassionate from desire, it is exclusively the irresistible [path] that abandons what is concordant with the final portion, not the fundamental [<s>dhyāna</s>] — because it has not been obtained therein. Even for one who has become dispassionate and is going to [enter] the stream — when, based on the <s>dhyāna</s>, entering the definite [path], even that one, at the time of the ordinary person, has all the afflictions operating in the Desire Realm abandoned by the mundane path — therefore that is not the fruit of the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>. In sixteen moments of mind, the comprehension of abandoning what is concordant with the final portion is also established as based on the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>, but it is not established as its fruit. What then? At that time, the comprehension of abandoning what is concordant with the final portion — the outflow-free separation-acquisitions previously obtained through abandonment by the mundane path — is also obtained. And what is established as the comprehension of that abandonment is the combination of what was previously abandoned by the path of seeing that is to be abandoned by seeing, and what was previously abandoned as concordant with the final portion, into a single comprehension of abandoning what is concordant with the final portion.

body.text: khams las ḥdod chags bral ba daṅ ḥbras bu thob phyir de dag bsdoms ṣes thams cad bsdoms paḥi gtan tshigs yod paḥi phyir ro. de lta bas na tha maḥi cha daṅ mthun pa spaṅs paḥi yoṅs su śes pa de ni mi lcogs pa med paḥi ḥbras bu kho nar rnam pa bṣag gi. dṅos gṣiḥi ḥbras bu ni ma [Tib. 167b] yin te. ḥdi la ni bye brag tu smra ba daṅ. btsun pa dbyaṅs sgrogs kyi gṣuṅ lugs mthun no.
body.translated_text: 'Because of dispassion from the realm and the obtaining of fruit, these are combined' — because there is reason for combining all. Therefore, the comprehension of abandoning what is concordant with the final portion is established exclusively as the fruit of the irresistible [path] — not [Tib. 167b] the fruit of the fundamental [<s>dhyāna</s>]. In this, the systems of the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> and the venerable <s>Ghoṣaka</s> agree.

body.text: bsam gtan khyad par can yaṅ bsams bṣin du blta bar byaḥo ṣes bya ba ni bsam gtan khyad par can gyi zag pa med pas kyaṅ ñon moṅs pa spoṅ bar ḥgyur te. de lta bas na mi lcogs pa med pa daṅ. dṅos gṣiḥi bsam gtan rnams kho naḥi ḥbras bu kho na bśad kyi. bsam gtan khyad par can gyi ni ma yin no. deḥi phyir bsam gtan khyad par can yaṅ bsam gtan bṣin du blta bar byaḥo ṣes bya ba smos te. bsam gtan khyad par can ni bsam gtan daṅ po kho na rtog pa daṅ bral bas khyad par du ḥphags paḥi phyir ro. [nam mkhaḥ mthaḥ yas skye mched kyi ñer bsdogs kyi ṣes ba ba ni.] dhyānāṃtaraṃ bhavatīti. ākāśānaṃtyāyatanasāmaṃtakasyeti. laukikasyāpi tasya parijñā phalaṃ vyavasthāpyate. āryasyaivānāsravavisaṃyogaprāptisaṃbhavāt.
body.translated_text: 'The special <s>dhyāna</s> should also be considered accordingly' — through the outflow-free [path] of the special <s>dhyāna</s> too, afflictions are abandoned. Therefore, only the fruits of the irresistible [path] and the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>s alone are described, not [those] of the special <s>dhyāna</s>. Therefore it is said: the special <s>dhyāna</s> should also be considered like the <s>dhyāna</s>. The special <s>dhyāna</s> is only the first <s>dhyāna</s>, distinguished by being free from discursive thought (<s>vitarka</s>). [The preparatory stage of the ākāśānantyāyatana — ] the <s>dhyānāntara</s> (intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>) exists. Even for its mundane [counterpart], the comprehension-fruit is established — because the attainment of outflow-free separation-acquisition is possible for a noble one alone.

body.text: anāsravasya.
body.translated_text: the outflow-free [ones].

body.text: iti. āryasya laukikena mārgeṇa kāmarūpadhātuvairāgye.
body.translated_text: for the dispassion from the Desire Realm and the Form Realm through the mundane path of a noble one.

body.text: iti. bhāvanāmārgasaṃgṛhītasya. paścime rūparāgakṣayasarvasaṃyojanaparyādānaaparijñe.
body.translated_text: that which is included in the path of cultivation. In the last [comprehensions]: the exhaustion of form-realm desire and the exhaustion of all fetters.

children.translated_text: that which is included in the path of cultivation.

children.text:
dharmajñānaṃ nirodhe yan mārge vā bhāvanāpathe
tridhātupratipakṣas tad
children.translated_text:
'<s>Dharma</s>-knowledge regarding cessation or the path,
on the path of cultivation,
is the antidote of the three realms' —

body.text: iti. tasya paścimās tisraḥ phalam avarabhāgīyaprahāṇarūparāgakṣayasarvasaṃyojanaparyādānaparijñāḥ. kasmād ity āha. [Tib. 168a] traidhātukabhāvanāheyapratipakṣatvād iti.
body.translated_text: its last three [comprehensions] as fruit are: the comprehension of lower-portion abandonment, the exhaustion of form-realm desire, and the exhaustion of all fetters. Why? He says: [Tib. 168a] because of being the antidote of what is to be abandoned by cultivation in all three realms.

body.text: tayor dharmajñānānvayajñānayoḥ pakṣasya. ṣaṭ paṃca ca yathāyogaṃ pakṣagrahaṇena kṣāṃtijñānayor grahaṇaṃ. yā eva dharmajñānakṣāṃtijñānānām
body.translated_text: of the class of those two — <s>dharma</s>-knowledge and subsequent knowledge. Six and five respectively. By the word 'class,' patience and knowledge are grasped. Whatever [comprehensions belong to] <s>dharma</s>-knowledge, patience, and knowledge

body.text: iti. dharmajñānakṣāṃtīnāṃ dharmajñānānāṃ ceti samāsaḥ. dharmajñānakṣāṃtīnāṃ kāmāvacaradarśanaheyaprahāṇasvabhāvā yathoktas tisraḥ parijñāḥ phalaṃ. dharmajñānānām iti bhāvanāmārge. duḥkhasamudayajñānasaṃgṛhītānām ekāvarabhāgīyaprahāṇaparijñā. nirodhamārgasaṃgṛhītānāṃ tu tisro 'py avarabhāgīyaprahāṇarūparāgakṣayasarvasaṃyojanaparyādānaparijñāḥ. yā evānvayakṣāṃtijñānānām iti. anvayajñānakṣāṃtīnāṃ anvayajñānānāṃ ca. tāś ca rūpārūpyāvacaradarśanaheyaprahāṇasvabhāvā yathoktās tisraḥ parijñāḥ dve ca paścime iti.
body.translated_text: — this is a compound of '<s>dharma</s>-knowledge-patiences' and '<s>dharma</s>-knowledges.' The three comprehensions as described — having the intrinsic nature of abandoning what is to be abandoned by seeing in the Desire Realm — are the fruit of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge-patiences. 'Of <s>dharma</s>-knowledges' — on the path of cultivation. Of those included in the suffering and origination [knowledges], one comprehension: the abandonment of the lower portion. But of those included in cessation and path [knowledges], all three: the comprehensions of lower-portion abandonment, exhaustion of form-realm desire, and exhaustion of all fetters. 'Whatever [belongs to] subsequent-knowledge patiences and knowledges' — of subsequent-knowledge patiences and subsequent-knowledges. And those three comprehensions, having the intrinsic nature of abandoning what is to be abandoned by seeing in the Form and Formless Realms — and the last two.

body.text: (V.67) kasmān naikaikaṃ prahāṇam iti. duḥkhadarśanaheyaprahāṇasamudayadarśanaheyaprahāṇaṃ vistareṇa yāvad bhāvāgrikasya mṛdumṛdoḥ prakārasya prahāṇam iti kasmān na gṛhyate.
body.translated_text: (V.67) 'Why is not each individual abandonment [called a comprehension]?' — the abandonment of what is to be abandoned by seeing suffering, the abandonment of what is to be abandoned by seeing origination, in detail up to the abandonment of the mild-mild type belonging to the peak of existence — why is it not grasped [as a separate comprehension]?

children.translated_text: 'Because of the attainment of outflow-free separation' —

body.text: iti. anāsravavisaṃyogaprāpter ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: meaning: because of the attainment of outflow-free separation-acquisition (<s>visaṃyogaprāpti</s>).

children.translated_text: 'Because of partial destruction of the peak of existence' —

body.text: iti. bhavāgrapradeśaprahāṇād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: meaning: because of abandoning a portion of the peak of existence.

children.translated_text: 'Because of the destruction of both types of cause' —

body.text: iti. duḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyasarvatragahetudvayaprahāṇād ity arthaḥ. tatprahāṇaṃ
body.translated_text: meaning: because of abandoning both types of universal cause to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination.

body.text: ebhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ prakṛṣṭaṃ tatprahāṇam ity atra parijñeti vyavasthāpyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. anyeṣu dharmānvayajñāneṣv iti. samudayadharmajñānam ārabhya yāvat kṣayajñānam ity eteṣu dharmajñānānvayajñāneṣu. jñānaphalaṃ tu prahāṇam iti. bhāvanāmārge. tad dhi na kṣāṃtiphalam iti.
body.translated_text: the intent is: for these reasons, that abandonment is pre-eminent, and therefore it is established as 'comprehension' here. 'In the other <s>dharma</s>-knowledges and subsequent-knowledges' — starting from the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of origination up to the knowledge of destruction — in these <s>dharma</s>-knowledges and subsequent-knowledges. 'But the abandonment is the fruit of knowledge' — on the path of cultivation. For that is not the fruit of patience.

body.text: iti. caśabdo luptanirdiṣṭaḥ. dhātvatikramāc ceti. ata eva vivriyate caturthāc ceti. yadā dhātuṃ samatikrāmatīti. kāmadhātuṃ rūpadhātum ārūpyadhātuṃ vā samatikrāmati. tadā parijñākhyāṃ labhata iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. kasmāt. kṛtsnadhātuvairāgyāt. kṛtsnasya dhātor vairāgyāt. na vikalīkaraṇamātratvāt. tadā hi suṣṭhu prahāṇam ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is stated with elision. Meaning: 'and because of transcending a realm.' Therefore it is explained: 'and from the fourth' — when one transcends a realm — transcends the Desire Realm, the Form Realm, or the Formless Realm — then one obtains the designation 'comprehension' — this is the remainder of the sentence. Why? Because of dispassion from the entire realm — because of dispassion from the realm in its entirety — not merely from partial destruction. For at that time, there is thorough abandonment — this is the intent.

body.text: ubhayasaṃyogavisaṃyogam iti. ālaṃbyālaṃbakakleśalakṣaṇaḥ saṃyoga ubhayasaṃyogaḥ. tasmād visaṃyoga ubhayasaṃyogavisaṃyogaḥ. tat paṃcamaṃ kāraṇam āhur ābhidhārmikāḥ. [Tib. 169a] anena ca kāraṇena prahāṇaṃ parijñety ucyata iti. yaḥ prakāraḥ prahīṇa iti duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyo yāvaṃ mārgadarśanaprahātavyo bhāvanāprahātavyaś ca. yadi tatra prahīṇe
body.translated_text: 'Disjunction from dual conjunction' — the conjunction characterized by the object-and-objective affliction is dual conjunction. The disjunction from that is 'disjunction from dual conjunction.' This the <s>Ābhidhārmika</s>s state as the fifth reason. And because of this reason, abandonment is called comprehension (<s>parijñā</s>). Whatever type has been abandoned — to be abandoned by seeing suffering, up to to be abandoned by seeing the path, and to be abandoned by cultivation — if, when that type has been abandoned

body.text: prakāre anyena tadālaṃbanena kleśena darśanaprahātavyena bhāvanāprahātavyena visaṃyukto bhavati. evam idam api paṃcamaṃ kāraṇaṃ prahāṇasya parijñāvidhāne āhur apare. sa tu nānyad iti vistaraḥ. sa tūbhayasaṃyoga ubhayahetusamudghātāt duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyasya samudayadarśanaprahātavyasya ca sarvatragahetoḥ samudghātād dhātusamatikramāc ca nānyaḥ. tathā hi duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyeṣu prahīṇeṣv api na tāvad asti hetudvayasamudghāto yāvat tadālaṃbanaḥ samudayadarśanaprahātavyaḥ sarvatragahetur aprahīṇo bhavati. bhāvanāprahātavyeṣu ca prahīṇeṣv api yāvad aṣṭāsu prakāreṣu na tāvad dhātvatikramo 'sti yāvan na navamasyāpi prakārasya prahāṇam ity ato na punar brūmaḥ.
body.translated_text: , one becomes disjoined from another affliction that has that as its object, whether to be abandoned by seeing or by cultivation — thus this fifth reason too, in the establishment of abandonment as comprehension, others state. But that is not different — and so forth in detail. But that dual conjunction is not different from the uprooting of the two [universal] causes — from the uprooting of the universal cause to be abandoned by seeing suffering and the universal cause to be abandoned by seeing origination — and from the transcendence of a realm. For indeed, even when those to be abandoned by seeing suffering have been abandoned, there is not yet the uprooting of the two causes as long as the universal cause to be abandoned by seeing origination that has those as its object has not been abandoned. And even when those to be abandoned by cultivation have been abandoned, in eight types there is not yet the transcendence of a realm until the ninth type too has been abandoned — therefore we do not state this again.

body.text: vistaraḥ. pṛthagjanas tāvan naiva samanvāgataḥ. anāsravavisaṃyogaprāptyabhāvāt. āryo 'pi darśanamārgastho yāvat samudayadharmajñānakṣāṃtau. yāvacchabdena duḥkhadharmānvayajñānakṣāṃtijñāneṣu samudayadharmajñānakṣāṃtau ca naiva samanvāgataḥ. hetudvayasyāprahīṇatvāt. samudayadharmajñāna ekayā samanvāgataḥ samudayānvayajñānakṣāṃtāv apy ekayaiva samanvāgata ity avagaṃtavyaṃ. samudayānvayajñāne dvābhāṃ pūrvoktayā ekayā kāmāvacaraduḥkhasamudayadarśanaheyaprahāṇaparijñayā rūpārūpyāvacaraduḥkhasamudayadarśanaprahāṇaparijñayā ca. nirodhadharmajñānakṣāṃtāv api dvābhyām eva. nirodhadharmajñāne tisṛbhir iti neyaṃ. yāvat paṃcabhir darśanāsthaḥ samanvāgato na ṣaḍbhiḥ ṣoḍaśasya kṣaṇasya bhāvanāmārgasaṃgṛhītatvāt. mārgānvayajñāne ṣaḍbhir iti. pūrvoktābhiś ca rūpārūpyāvacaramārgadarśanaprahāṇaparijñayā ca. nanu ca paścād vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: — and so forth in detail. An ordinary person, first, is never endowed [with comprehension] — because of the absence of acquisition of uncontaminated disconnection. A Noble One too, while standing on the seeing-path, up to the patient acceptance of subsequent knowledge of origination (<s>samudayadharmajñānakṣānti</s>) — by the word 'up to,' in the patient acceptances and knowledges of dharma-knowledge and subsequent knowledge of suffering, and in the patient acceptance of dharma-knowledge of origination — is never endowed [with comprehension], because of the two causes not having been abandoned. At the dharma-knowledge of origination, one is endowed with a single [comprehension]. At the patient acceptance of subsequent knowledge of origination too, one should be understood as endowed with exactly one. At the subsequent knowledge of origination, with two — the one previously stated, and the comprehension of the abandonment of those to be abandoned by seeing suffering and origination belonging to the Desire Realm, and the comprehension of the abandonment of those belonging to the Form and Formless Realms. At the patient acceptance of dharma-knowledge of cessation too, with exactly two. At the dharma-knowledge of cessation, with three — and so on. Up to: one standing on the seeing-path is endowed with five, not six — because the sixteenth moment is included in the cultivation-path. At the subsequent knowledge of the path (<s>mārgānvayajñāna</s>), with six. 'But does he not state later:' —

children.text:
catuḥphalavyavasthā tu paṃca kāraṇasaṃbhavāt
pūrvatyāgo 'nyamārgāptiḥ kṣayasaṃkalaṇaṃ phale
jñānāṣṭakasya lābho 'tha ṣoḍaśākārabhāvaneti.
children.translated_text:
'The establishment of the four fruits is due to the possibility of five causes:
previous relinquishment, attainment of another path, exhaustion-aggregation in the fruit,
obtaining the eight knowledges, and cultivation of the sixteen modes.'

body.text: bhavati prahāṇasaṃkalanaṃ. na tu parijñāsaṃkalanam ity avirodhaḥ. yāvat kāmavairāgyaṃ na prāpta iti. yāvacchabdena bhāvanāheyakleśaprathamaprakāraprahāṇe [Tib. 170a] yāvad aṣṭamaprakāraprahāṇe 'pi ṣaḍbhir eva samanvāgataḥ. parihīṇo 'pi tata iti. kāmavairāgyaparihāṇyā hi tatsaṃkalanavigataḥ. kāmavairāgyaṃ prāptaḥ pūrvaṃ paścād veti. abhisamayāt pūrvaṃ paścād vā. kathaṃ. laukikena mārgeṇa kāmavītarāgo bhūtvā niyāmam avakrāṃto mārge 'nvayajñāne ekayāvarabhāgīyaprahāṇaparijñayā samanvāgataḥ. yasmād asāv āryaḥ ṣoḍaśakṣaṇaṃ prāpto 'nāgāmy eva bhavati. na srotaāpannaḥ. sakṛdāgāmī
body.translated_text: There is aggregation of abandonment, but not aggregation of comprehension — so there is no contradiction. 'Up to one who has not attained freedom from desire for the Desire Realm' — by the word 'up to,' even at the abandonment of the first type of afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation, up to the abandonment of the eighth type, one is endowed with exactly six. 'Even one who has fallen from that' — for through the loss of freedom from desire for the Desire Realm, one is divested of that aggregation. 'One who has attained freedom from desire for the Desire Realm, whether previously or later' — whether before or after the decisive penetration (<s>abhisamaya</s>). How? Having become free from desire for the Desire Realm through the mundane path, having entered the determined course (<s>niyāma</s>), at the subsequent knowledge of the path, one is endowed with a single comprehension — the comprehension of the abandonment of the lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīya</s>). Since that Noble One, having reached the sixteenth moment, becomes a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) — not a stream-enterer or once-returner

body.text: vā. paṃcāvarabhāgīyaprahāṇāc cānāgāmī iti paṭhyate. tasmād darśanaheyaprahāṇānāṃ paṃcāvarabhāgīyaprahāṇasya ca saṃkalanād ekayaivāvarabhagīyaprahāṇaparijñayā samanvāgataḥ. paścād vābhisamayād ānupūrvikaḥ kāmavairāgyaprāpta ekayaivāvarabhāgīyaprahāṇaparijñayā samanvāgataḥ. arhattvaprāpta ekayaiveti. tadā parijñāsaṃkalanāt. parihīṇo 'pi rūpāvacareṇeti. viśeṣaṇaṃ kāmāvacareṇa parihāṇau ṣaṭparijñāsamanvāgamaparihārārtham ārūpyāvacareṇa ca parihāṇau dviparijñāsamanvāgamaparihārārtham iti. rūpavairāgyaṃ [Tib. 170b] prāpto dvābhyām iti. anāgāmī rūpavītarāga ity arthaḥ. dhātuvairāgyeṇa kasmān na saṃkalanaṃ bhavati. phalaprāptyabhāvāt. dhātuvairāgyaphalaprāptibhyāṃ samastābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ parijñāsaṃkalanam iṣyate. na kevalena parihīṇo 'pi. ārūpyāvacareṇety arhattvaprāptisaṃkalitayor avarabhāgīyaprahāṇarūparāgakṣayaparijñayor ārūpyāvacareṇa kleśenārhattvāt parihāṇau punarlābhāt. rūpāvacareṇa tu parihāṇāv ekayā samanvāgataḥ syāt. kāmāvacareṇa ca ṣaḍhiḥ samanvāgataḥ syād ity ārūpyāvacaraparyavasthānagrahaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: . And it is read that one is a non-returner through the abandonment of the five lower fetters. Therefore, through the aggregation of the abandonment of those to be abandoned by seeing and the abandonment of the five lower fetters, one is endowed with exactly a single comprehension — the comprehension of the abandonment of the lower fetters. Or, having attained freedom from desire for the Desire Realm subsequently, after the decisive penetration, in gradual sequence, one is endowed with exactly a single comprehension — the comprehension of the abandonment of the lower fetters. Having attained <s>arhat</s>ship too, with exactly one — because of the aggregation of comprehensions at that time. 'Even one who has fallen — through the Form Realm' — the qualification 'through the Form Realm' is for the purpose of avoiding [the conclusion of] endowment with six comprehensions in the case of falling through the Desire Realm, and for the purpose of avoiding [the conclusion of] endowment with two comprehensions in the case of falling through the Formless Realm. 'Having attained freedom from desire for the Form Realm, with two' — meaning: a non-returner free from desire for the Form Realm. 'Why is there no aggregation through freedom from desire for a realm?' Because of the absence of fruit-attainment. The aggregation of comprehensions is accepted from the combination of both causes — freedom from desire for a realm and fruit-attainment — not from one alone. 'Even one who has fallen — through the Formless Realm' — of the two comprehensions aggregated at the time of attaining <s>arhat</s>ship — the comprehension of the abandonment of the lower fetters and the comprehension of the exhaustion of passion for form — through falling from <s>arhat</s>ship by a Formless Realm affliction, and through re-attaining [them]. But in the case of falling through the Form Realm, one would be endowed with a single [comprehension]. And in the case of falling through the Desire Realm, one would be endowed with six — hence the mention of 'through the Formless Realm.'

body.text: (V.69ab) anāgāmyarhator iti. kāmavītarāgānāgāmīha vivakṣitaḥ. rūpavītarāgānāgāminaḥ parijñādvayasamanvāgamavacanāt. na bhūyasya iti. na bahutarāḥ. ānupūrvikasrotaāpannavad ity abhiprāyaḥ. dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyām iti vyākhyātaṃ. saṃkalanam iti ko 'rthaḥ ekatvena vyavasthāpanam iti yo 'rthaḥ. tayoś cāvasthayor iti. kāmavītarāgānāgāmyarhattvāvasthayor etad ubhayaṃ. dhātuvairāgyaṃ phalaprāptiś ceti. ekaparijñocyata iti. rūpavītarāgasyānāgāmina [Tib. 171a] ekāvarabhāgīyaprahāṇaparijñā arhato 'py ekā sarvasaṃyojanaparyādānaparijñeti.
body.translated_text: (V.69ab) 'Of the non-returner and the <s>arhat</s>' — the non-returner free from desire for the Desire Realm is intended here, because of the statement that the non-returner free from desire for the Form Realm is endowed with two comprehensions. 'Not more' — not a greater number; the intent is: like the gradual stream-enterer. 'Through two causes' — this has been explained. 'What is the meaning of aggregation (<s>saṃkalana</s>)?' — the meaning is: establishment as one. 'And in those two states' — in the two states of non-returner free from desire for the Desire Realm and <s>arhat</s>ship — both of these [apply]: freedom from desire for a realm and fruit-attainment. 'One comprehension is stated' — for the non-returner free from desire for the Form Realm, one comprehension of the abandonment of the lower fetters; for the <s>arhat</s> too, one comprehension of the complete exhaustion of all fetters.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: — and so forth in detail.

body.text: tyajatīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: the meaning is: gives up.

body.text: kaścid ekāṃ kaścid dve kaścit ṣaṭ. kaścit paṃcāpnotīty etan nāsti. ata āha.
body.translated_text: someone one, someone two, someone six. 'Someone attains five' — this does not [occur]. Therefore he says:

body.text: paṃca naiva kaścid āpnoti. iti sūtrārthanayaḥ. vṛttis tu vivriyate arhattvāt parihīyamāṇo yena kenacit cittena sarvasaṃyojanaparyādānaparijñām ekāṃ tyajati. saṃkalane tasyā ekaikasyā arhattvāvasthāyām astitvāt. evaṃ kāmavairāgyāt parihīyamāṇo rūpavītarāgo 'nāgāmī ekām evāvarabhāgīyaprahāṇaparijñāṃ. dve parijñe tyajatīti. avarabhāgīyaprahāṇaparijñāṃ. rūparāgakṣayaparijñāṃ ca. ko 'sāv ity āha. anāgāmī rūpavītarāgaḥ kāmavairāgyāt parihīyamāṇa iti. paṃca tyajati vītarāgapūrvī mārgānvayajñāna [tib 171b] iti. abhisamayacitte ṣoḍaśe. sa hy avarabhāgīyaprahāṇaparijñālābhe. laukikamārgaprāptasya tasyānāsravavisaṃyogaprāptyā pūrvikāḥ paṃca parijñāḥ paṃcadaśakṣaṇalabdhās tyajati. ṣaṣṭhīṃ tu rūpārūpyāvacaramārgadarśanaheyaprahāṇaparijñāṃ na tyajati. kiṃ tu dhātuvairāgyaphalalābhato 'trāvarabhāgīyaprahāṇaparijñāyāṃ saṃkaliteti naṣṭarūpeva sā nopanyasyate. ānupūrviko yo na vītarāgapūrvī kāmavairāgyāt kāraṇāt ṣaṭ tyajati. yās traidhātukānāṃ darśanaprahātavyānāṃ prahāṇaparijñāḥ.
body.translated_text: No one at all attains five. This is the approach to the <s>sūtra</s> meaning. But the method (<s>vṛtti</s>) is explained: One falling from <s>arhat</s>ship relinquishes, by whichever mind, the single comprehension of the complete exhaustion of all fetters — because of the existence of each one singly at the time of <s>arhat</s>ship, through aggregation. Similarly, one falling from freedom from desire for the Desire Realm — a non-returner free from desire for the Form Realm — [relinquishes] the single comprehension of the abandonment of the lower fetters. 'Relinquishes two comprehensions' — the comprehension of the abandonment of the lower fetters and the comprehension of the exhaustion of passion for form. Who is this? He says: a non-returner free from desire for the Form Realm, falling from freedom from desire for the Desire Realm. 'Relinquishes five — one who was previously free from desire, at the subsequent knowledge of the path' — at the sixteenth moment of the decisive penetration. For he, having obtained the comprehension of the abandonment of the lower fetters, relinquishes — through the uncontaminated disconnection-acquisition of one who has previously attained through the mundane path — the five comprehensions previously obtained at the fifteenth moment. But he does not relinquish the sixth — the comprehension of the abandonment of those to be abandoned by seeing the path belonging to the Form and Formless Realms. Rather, because of the obtaining of freedom from desire for a realm and fruit-attainment, that is aggregated into the comprehension of the abandonment of the lower fetters — and so, being as though destroyed in form, it is not mentioned. One who is gradual, not one who was previously free from desire, relinquishes six through [the cause of] freedom from desire for the Desire Realm — the comprehensions of the abandonment of those to be abandoned by seeing belonging to the triple realm.

body.text: lābho 'py evam iti. kaścid ekāṃ labhate. paṃceti muktvā. yāvat ṣaṭ labhate. yaḥ kaścid apūrvaṃ labhata iti. darśanamārgastho bhāvanāmārgastho vā navānāṃ parijñānāṃ yo pratilabdhapūrvāṃ pratilabhate prathamataḥ. sa tām ekāṃ labhate. bhāvanāmārge 'pi hi vītarāgapūrvī darśanamārgāṃte avarabhāgīyaprahāṇaparijñām ekāṃ labhate. ānupārviko 'pi kāmavairāgye navame vimuktimārge tām eva labhate. arhann apy anyām labhata iti. kevalād ārūpyavairāgyāt parihīyata iti. nānyavairāgyād iti darśayati. sa hy avarabhāgīyaprahāṇaparijñāṃ [Tib. 172a] rūparāgakṣayaparijñāṃ ca labhate. kaścit ṣaḍ yo 'nāgāmiphalāt parihīyata iti. ānupūrviko 'nāgāmī. na hi vītarāgapūrviṇaḥ parihāṇir asti. tadvairāgyasya dvimārgaprāpaṇāt. ata eva ca naiva kaścit paṃca labhate. vītarāgapūrviṇo hi yadi parihāṇir abhaviṣyat. sa eva yugapat paṃca parijñā alapsyateti.
body.translated_text: 'Attainment is also likewise' — someone attains one, excluding five, up to someone attains six. 'Whoever newly attains' — whether standing on the seeing-path or the cultivation-path, whoever attains for the first time any of the nine comprehensions that was not previously obtained — that one attains that single one. Even on the cultivation-path, one who was previously free from desire, at the end of the seeing-path, attains the single comprehension of the abandonment of the lower fetters. The gradual one too, at the ninth liberation-path of freedom from desire for the Desire Realm, attains that very one. An <s>arhat</s> too attains another [single comprehension]. 'One who falls only from freedom from desire for the Formless Realm' — he shows: not from freedom from desire for another [realm]. For that one attains the comprehension of the abandonment of the lower fetters and the comprehension of the exhaustion of passion for form. 'Someone [attains] six — one who falls from the fruit of non-returning' — a gradual non-returner. For one who was previously free from desire does not have a fall — because the freedom from desire for that [Desire Realm] was achieved through two paths. For this very reason, no one at all attains five. For if the one who was previously free from desire had a fall, that very one would have simultaneously attained five comprehensions.

body.text: ācāryayaśomitrakṛtāyām abhidharmakośavyākyāyām anuśayanirdeśo nāma paṃcamaṃ kośasthānaṃ samāptaṃ.
body.translated_text: The fifth chapter called the Exposition of Latent Dispositions (<s>Anuśayanirdeśa</s>) is completed in the <s>Abhidharmakośavyākhyā</s> composed by <s>Ācārya Yaśomitra</s>.

body.text: VI (pudgalamārganirdeśo nāma ṣaṣṭhaṃ kośasthānam)
body.translated_text: VI (The sixth chapter called the Exposition of Persons and Paths — <s>Pudgalamārganirdeśa</s>)

body.text: (VI.1) paṃcamasya ṣaṣṭhasya ca kośasthānayoḥ saṃbaṃdham upadarśayann idam upanyasyati. uktaṃ yathāprahāṇam ityadi. yathāprahāṇaṃ parijñā labhata iti. phale hetūpacārād iti vacanāt. tad api ca
body.translated_text: (VI.1) Showing the connection between the fifth and sixth chapters, he presents this: 'It has been stated that comprehension is obtained according to abandonment' and so on. Comprehension is obtained according to abandonment — because of the statement 'through figurative designation of the cause upon the fruit.' And that too —

children.translated_text: 'The abandonment of afflictions has been stated'

body.text: uktaṃ. katham ity āha.
body.translated_text: — it has been stated. How? He says:

children.translated_text: 'Through seeing and cultivation of the truths'

body.text: iti. dvaṃdvaikavadbhāvanirdeśaḥ. satyānāṃ darśanād bhāvanāc ca bhāvanāyā iti vā. satyadarśanabhāvanāt kāraṇād darśanaheyā bhāvanāheyāś ca kleśā iti vistareṇoktaṃ
body.translated_text: — the statement is like a <s>dvandva</s> [compound] in the singular. Through the seeing and through the cultivation of the truths; or through the cultivation of the seeing of truths. Through the seeing and cultivation of the truths, the afflictions to be abandoned by seeing and those to be abandoned by cultivation have been stated in detail —

children.text:
daśaita sapta saptaṣṭau tridvidṛṣṭivivarjitāḥ
yathākramaṃ prahīyaṃte kāme duḥkhādidarśanaiḥ.
catvāro bhāvanāheyā
children.translated_text:
'Ten, these seven, seven-eight, excluding two and one view,
are abandoned in order in the Desire [Realm] by seeing suffering and the rest.
Four are to be abandoned by cultivation'

body.text: ity ādinā. [Tib. 172b] satyadarśanaṃ ca darśanamārgeṇa satyabhāvanaṃ ca bhāvanāmārgeṇety ata idam ucyate. tāv idānīṃ darśanabhāvanāmārgau kim anāsravau sāsravāv iti. mārganirdeśopanyāsa iti saṃbandhaḥ. traidhātukapratipakṣatvād iti darśanamārgasya. laukikatve sati bhavāgrapratipakṣo na syād iti. kiṃ ca navaprakārāṇāṃ darśanaheyānāṃ sakṛtprahāṇāc ca. na bhāvanāmārgavat. na hi laukikasyaiṣā śaktir asti. traidhātukaprahāṇe ca prakāraprahāṇe ca. yadi lokottarasya navaprakārasakṛtprahāṇe śaktiḥ. bhāvanāheyānām api lokottareṇa sakṛtprahāṇaprasaṃgaḥ. lokottareṇaiva sakṛtprahāṇam ity avadhāryate. na tu sakṛtprahāṇam eva lokottareṇeti ato na tatprasaṃgaḥ. bhāvanāheyā hi kleśā dṛḍhāḥ savastukatvāt. ato lokottareṇāpy eṣāṃ na sakṛtprahāṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: — and so forth. The seeing of truths is by means of the seeing-path (<s>darśanamārga</s>), and the cultivation of truths is by means of the cultivation-path (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) — therefore this is stated. 'Now then, are those seeing and cultivation paths uncontaminated or contaminated?' The connection is: the presentation of the path. 'Because of being the antidote to the triple realm' — of the seeing-path. If it were mundane, then the antidote to the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) would not exist. Moreover, because of the simultaneous abandonment of nine types of those to be abandoned by seeing — not like the cultivation-path. For the mundane [path] does not have this power — for the abandonment of the triple realm and for the abandonment of [all nine] types. If the supramundane has the power for the simultaneous abandonment of nine types, there would be the consequence that those to be abandoned by cultivation too should be simultaneously abandoned by the supramundane [path]. It is ascertained that the simultaneous abandonment is by the supramundane alone — but not that simultaneous abandonment is exclusively supramundane. Therefore there is no such consequence. For afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation are firm, because of being with a basis. Therefore even by the supramundane, there is no simultaneous abandonment of them.

body.text: (VI.2) itarathā hīti. yadi yathābhisamayaṃ nirdeśo nābhiprīyeta. pūrvaṃ hetunirdeśaḥ samudayasatyanirdeśaḥ. hetūnāṃ loke pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭatvāt. yathā smṛtyupasthānadhyānādīnām iti. tadyathā smṛtyupasthānādīnām upapattyanukūlā deśanā. kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ hi pūrvam utpadyate. yathaudārikālaṃbanataḥ [Tib. 173a] sūkṣmaudārikapracārato vā pūrvottarahetuphalabhāvato vā. tato vedanāsmṛtyupasthānaṃ. tataś cittasmṛtyupasthānam ity eṣām upapattyanukūlā deśanā evaṃ dhyānānām. ādiśabdena vimokṣābhibhvāyatanakṛtsnāyatanādīnām apy upapattyanukūlā deśanā. keṣāṃcit prarūpaṇānukūleti. pradarśanānukūlā avabodhānukūlety arthaḥ. yathā samyakprahāṇānām iti. kṛṣṇaśuklapakṣayoḥ pratyekam utpannānutpannabhedataḥ. utpannaṃ hi sukhāvabadhaṃ nānutpannaṃ. kṛṣṇapakṣo vā vineyajanena sukham avabudhyate. katham utpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya chandaṃ janayati vyāyacchate. vīryam ārabhate cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti praṇidadhāti. anutpannānām anutpādāya chandaṃ janayatīti pūrvavat. anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām utpādāya chandaṃ janayatīti pūrvavat. utpannānāṃ sthitaye asaṃmoṣatāyai chandaṃ janayatīti pūrvavat. na hy eṣa niyamo yat pūrvam utpannānāṃ prahāṇāya chandaṃ janayati. paścād anutpannānām anutpādāyeti. kiṃ tarhi. pūrvaṃ cānutpannānām anutpādāya chandaṃ janayati. [Tib. 173b] paścāc cotpannānāṃ prahāṇāyety etad udāharaṇaṃ. evaṃ śuklapakṣo 'pi yojyaḥ. satyānāṃ tv abhisamayānukūleti hetuphalayoḥ pūrvapaścādbhāvena duḥkhasamudayasatyayoḥ paścātpūrvanirdeśaprasaṃga iti darśayati. yatra hi sakta iti. duḥkhasatye. yena bādhyata iti tenaivaṃ. yataś ca mokṣam iti. tata eva duḥkhasatyāt. tad evādau payogāvasthāyāṃ. kasmād ity āha. vyavacāraṇāvasthāyāṃ parīkṣāvasthāyāṃ nirvedhabhāgīyāvasthāyām ity arthaḥ. vyādhiṃ dṛṣṭveti. vyādhir duḥkhasatyasyopamānaṃ. tannidānaṃ samudayasatyasya. tatkṣayo nirodhasatyasya. tadbheṣajaṃ mārgasatyasyopamānaṃ. sūtre 'py eṣa satyānāṃ dṛṣṭāṃta iti. vyādhyādisūtre. kathaṃ. caturbhir aṃgaiḥ samanvāgato bhiṣak śalyāpahartā rājārhaś ca bhavati rājayogyaś ca rājāṃgatve ca saṃkhyāṃ gacchati. katamaiś caturbhiḥ. ābādhakuśalo bhavati. ābādhasamutthānakuśalaḥ. ābādhaprahāṇakuśalaḥ. prahīṇasya cābādhasyāyatyām anutpādakuśalaḥ. evam eva caturbhir aṃgaiḥ samanvāgatas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'nuttaro bhiṣak śalyāpahartety ucyate. katamaiś caturbhiḥ. iha bhikṣavas [Tib. 174a] tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha idaṃ duḥkham āryasatyam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ. ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ.
body.translated_text: (VI.2) 'For otherwise' — if the teaching in the order of realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) were not preferred. The teaching of causes first is the teaching of the truth of origination. Because causes are seen first in the world. 'Just as for the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), <s>dhyāna</s>s, and the rest' — just as for the foundations of mindfulness and the rest, the teaching is in accordance with arising (<s>upapatti</s>). For the body-foundation of mindfulness arises first — because of having a coarse object, or because of proceeding from coarse to subtle, or because of the relation of cause and fruit in the preceding and subsequent. Then the feeling-foundation of mindfulness. Then the mind-foundation of mindfulness — thus the teaching of these is in accordance with arising. Similarly for the <s>dhyāna</s>s. By the word 'and the rest,' the teaching of the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), stations of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>), totality-stations (<s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>), and the rest is also in accordance with arising. 'For some, in accordance with exposition' — the meaning is: in accordance with demonstration, in accordance with comprehension. 'Just as for the right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>)' — because of the division into arisen and unarisen in each of the dark and bright sides. For what has arisen is easily comprehended, not what has not arisen. Or the dark side is easily comprehended by those to be disciplined. How? 'He generates desire for the abandonment of arisen evil unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s, exerts himself, arouses vigor, takes hold of the mind, and applies it. He generates desire for the non-arising of unarisen [evil <s>dharma</s>s]' — as before. 'He generates desire for the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharma</s>s' — as before. 'He generates desire for the maintenance and non-loss of arisen [wholesome <s>dharma</s>s]' — as before. For there is no fixed rule that first he generates desire for the abandonment of arisen [evils] and afterwards for the non-arising of unarisen [evils]. Rather, first he generates desire for the non-arising of unarisen [evils], and afterwards for the abandonment of arisen [evils] — this is an example. The bright side too should be connected in the same way. 'But for the truths, in accordance with realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>)' — he shows that [this would entail] the teaching of the truth of origination before the truth of suffering, because of the prior-and-posterior relation of cause and fruit. 'Wherein one is attached' — in the truth of suffering. 'By which one is afflicted' — likewise. 'And from which liberation [comes]' — from that very truth of suffering. 'That itself first, in the stage of application (<s>prayogāvasthā</s>).' Why? — he says. The meaning is: in the stage of investigation (<s>vyavacāraṇāvasthā</s>), the stage of examination (<s>parīkṣāvasthā</s>), the stage of the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). 'Having seen the disease' — the disease is the analogy for the truth of suffering. Its cause is [the analogy] for the truth of origination. Its destruction is [the analogy] for the truth of cessation. Its medicine is the analogy for the truth of the path. 'In the <s>sūtra</s> too, this is the example for the truths' — in the <s>sūtra</s> on disease and the rest. How? 'Endowed with four qualities, a physician, a surgeon, becomes worthy of a king, fit for a king, and is counted among the king's retinue. With which four? He is skilled in disease, skilled in the cause of disease, skilled in the cessation of disease, and skilled in the non-arising in the future of a disease that has ceased. Even so, endowed with four qualities, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, is called the supreme physician, the surgeon. With which four? Here, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, truly knows: "This is the noble truth of suffering. This is the origin of suffering. This is the cessation of suffering.

body.text: iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti. pūrvāvedhād iti. pūrvākṣepāt. dṛṣṭabhūminiḥsaṃgāśvaprasaraṇavad iti. yathā bhūmau dṛṣṭāyāṃ niḥsaṃgam aśvasya prasaraṇaṃ. tadvat. aśvadhāvanavad iti kecit paṭhaṃti. dhāvi prakṛtyaṃtaraṃ vyācakṣate. iṇo bodhanārthatvād iti. sarvo gatyartho bodhanārtho 'pi bhavatīti. dravyato 'pīty apiśabdān nāmato 'pīti darśitaṃ. aviparītatvād iti. yasmāt tad āryāṇām anyeṣāṃ cāviparītaṃ. duḥkham eva nānyathā. āryais tu yathaitāni satyāni. tathā dṛṣṭāni. duḥkhasatyaṃ duḥkhata anityataḥ śūnyato 'nātmataś ca. evaṃ yāvan mārgo mārgataḥ nyāyataḥ pratipattito nairyāṇikataś ca. nānyair anāryaiḥ evaṃ dṛṣṭāni. ata āryāṇām etāni satyāny ucyaṃte. na tv anāryāṇāṃ satyāny ucyaṃte. kasmāt. viparītadarśanāt. te hi duḥkham aduḥkhata [Tib. 174b] ity evamādibhir ākārair duḥkhasatyaṃ paśyaṃti. samdayam asamudayata ity evamādibhiḥ. nirodham anirodhata ity evamādibhiḥ. mārgam amārgata ity evamādibhir iti.
body.translated_text: This is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering — the noble truth" — thus he truly knows.' 'Because of prior penetration' — because of prior initiation. 'Like the unobstructed running of a horse on seen ground' — just as a horse runs unobstructedly on ground that has been seen; likewise. Some read '<s>aśvadhāvanavat</s>' (like the galloping of a horse). They explain '<s>dhāvi</s>' as another verbal root. 'Because the verbal root <s>iṇ</s> has the meaning of knowing' — 'every root meaning motion also has the meaning of knowing.' 'Even in substance' — from the word 'even,' 'also by name' is shown. 'Because of being non-inverted' — because that is non-inverted for nobles and for others. Suffering is nothing but [suffering], not otherwise. But the truths are as the nobles see them — thus seen: the truth of suffering [is seen] as suffering, as impermanent, as empty, and as non-self. Similarly, up to: the path [is seen] as path, as method, as practice, as leading to deliverance. Not so by others, the non-nobles. Therefore these are called the truths of the nobles, not the truths of non-nobles. Why? Because of their inverted seeing. For they see the truth of suffering through the aspects of non-suffering and the like. The truth of origination through [the aspects of] non-origination and the like. The truth of cessation through [the aspects of] non-cessation and the like. The truth of the path through [the aspects of] non-path and the like.

body.text: iti. tadyathā nirodhasatyaṃ vyathaṃte 'punarbhavāt prapātād iva bāliśā iti.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Just as [they] tremble at the truth of cessation, [fearing] non-re-becoming, like fools [fearing] a precipice.'

children.translated_text: 'But the nobles know it as suffering' —

body.text: ity upādānaskaṃdhapaṃcakaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus, the group of five clinging-aggregates.

body.text: dve āryāṇāṃ satye iti. duḥkhasamdayasatye aviparītadarśanāt. dve ārye. kuśalatayānāsravatayā ca. āryāṇāṃ ca satye. aviparītadarśanāt. evam ekaśeṣanirdeśāc cāryasatye iti bhavati.
body.translated_text: 'Two are truths of the nobles' — because of non-inverted seeing of the truths of suffering and origination. [These] two are noble — because of being wholesome and uncontaminated. And [they are] truths of the nobles — because of non-inverted seeing. Thus, from the teaching by way of singular residue, it becomes 'noble truths' (<s>āryasatya</s>).

body.text: (VI.3) yadā vedanaikadeśo duḥkhasvabhāva iti. vedanāskandhaikadeśo duḥkhadaurmanasyasvabhāvaḥ.
body.translated_text: (VI.3) 'When a portion of feeling has the nature of suffering' — a portion of the aggregate of feeling has the nature of suffering and mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>).

body.text: iti. manaāpā api vipariṇāmaduḥkhatayā saṃskāraduḥkhatayā ca duḥkhā. amanaāpā duḥkhaduḥkhatayā saṃskāraduḥkhatayā ca. tadanye duḥkhāḥ saṃskāraduḥkhatayaiveti yathāyogārthaḥ. mana āpnuvaṃtīti manaāpāḥ. punaḥ saṃdhikaraṇaṃ cātreti vyākhyātaṃ. tebhyo 'nya iti manaāpāmanaāpebhyo 'nya iti.
body.translated_text: thus. The agreeable ones (<s>manāpa</s>) too are suffering through the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>) and through the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>). The disagreeable ones are [suffering] through the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>) and through the suffering of conditioned existence. Those other than these are suffering through the suffering of conditioned existence alone — this is the meaning of 'as applicable.' '<s>Manāpa</s>' — those that satisfy the mind (<s>mana āpnuvanti</s>). 'And here the <s>sandhi</s>-joining is again' — thus it is explained. 'Those other than these' — other than the agreeable and disagreeable.

body.text: tisro vedanā yathākramam iti. sukhā vedanā [Tib. 175a] manaāpā duḥkhā amanaāpā aduḥkhasukhā naiva manaāpā nāmanaāpety arthaḥ. tadvaśeneti. vedanāvaśena. avedanāsvabhāvā api rūpaśabdādayas tadanukūlatvān manaāpādisaṃjñāṃ labhaṃte. vipariṇāmena duḥkhateti. anityatāvipariṇāmenety
body.translated_text: 'The three feelings respectively' — the meaning is: pleasant feeling is agreeable, painful feeling is disagreeable, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is neither agreeable nor disagreeable. 'Because of that' — because of feeling. Even form, sound, and the rest, which do not have the nature of feeling, acquire the designations of agreeable and the rest because of being favorable to that [feeling]. 'Suffering through change' — the meaning is: through the change of impermanence

body.text: arthaḥ yathoktaṃ.
body.translated_text: — as stated:

children.text:
hā caitraratha hā vāpi hā maṃdākini hā priye
ity ārttā vilapaṃto 'pi gāṃ pataṃti divokasa
children.translated_text:
'Alas, <s>Caitraratha</s>! Alas! And alas, <s>Mandākinī</s>! Alas, beloved!
Thus lamenting in anguish, the celestial beings fall to the earth.'

body.text: iti. duḥkhasvabhāvenaiveti. upaghātasvabhāvenety arthaḥ. duḥkhā vedanā utpādaduḥkhā sthitiduḥkheti. nanv eṣā arthāpattito vipariṇāmasukhā prāpnoti. tathā ca sati lakṣaṇasaṃkaraḥ syāt. nedam asyā lakṣaṇaṃ. kiṃ tarhi vidūṣaṇārtham ayam upadeśa iti. atha vā bhavatv eva sāttra. yena rūpeṇa vidūṣyate. tad evāpekṣate iti. duḥkhaiva bhavati. yathā sukhā vedanā utpādasthitisukhatvāt sukhāpi satī vipariṇāmaduḥkhatayā duḥkhety eva vidūṣyate vidūṣaṇīyatvenābhiprīyamāṇatvād iti. saṃskāreṇaiva duḥkhateti. saṃskaraṇenaiva jananenaivety arthaḥ. yad anityaṃ. tad duḥkhaṃ. yan na niyatasthitaṃ. tad duḥkhaṃ. yaj yāyate vinaśyati ca. tad duḥkham [Tib. 175b] ity arthaḥ. tenoktaṃ. pratyayābhisaṃskaraṇād iti. pratyayair abhisaṃskriyate yasmāt. tasmāt tad duḥkham iti. vedanāvat tadvedanīyā api saṃskārā veditavyā iti. sukhavedanīyānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ vipariṇāmena duḥkhatā. sukhavedanīyāḥ saṃskārā utpādasukhāḥ sthitisukhā vipariṇāmaduḥkhā iti. duḥkhavedanīyānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ duḥkhavedanīyasvabhāvenaiva duḥkhatā. duḥkhavedanīyāḥ saṃskārā utpādaduḥkhā sthitiduḥkhā iti. aduḥkhāsukhavedanīyānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ saṃskāreṇaiva duḥkhatā. pratyayābhisaṃskaraṇāt. yad anityam. tad duḥkham iti.
body.translated_text: 'By its very nature of suffering' — the meaning is: by its nature of affliction. 'Painful feeling is suffering at arising, suffering while persisting.' But does this not, by implication, arrive at [the conclusion that it is] pleasant through change? And if so, there would be confusion of characteristics. This is not its characteristic. What then? This teaching is for the purpose of debasement (<s>vidūṣaṇa</s>). Or alternatively: let there be that [pleasantness]; whatever form it is debased by — that it depends on. Thus it is suffering alone. Just as pleasant feeling, being pleasant because of being pleasant at arising and persisting, even while being pleasant, is spoken of as suffering through the suffering of change — spoken of as needing-to-be-debased, because it is preferred as needing-to-be-debased. 'Suffering by conditioned existence alone' — the meaning is: by conditioning alone, by production alone. What is impermanent is suffering. What is not of fixed abiding is suffering. What passes away and perishes is suffering — this is the meaning. Therefore it is stated: 'because of being conditioned by conditions' — because it is conditioned by conditions, therefore it is suffering. 'Even the objects of feeling (<s>vedanīya</s>), which are conditioned things, should be understood like feelings' — of conditioned things that are objects of pleasant feeling, suffering through change; pleasant-feeling-objects are conditioned things that are pleasant at arising, pleasant while persisting, and suffering through change. Of conditioned things that are objects of painful feeling, suffering by the very nature of painful-feeling-objects; painful-feeling-objects are conditioned things that are suffering at arising, suffering while persisting. Of conditioned things that are objects of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, suffering by conditioned existence alone — because of being conditioned by conditions. What is impermanent is suffering.

body.text: duḥkham eva duḥkhatā duḥkhaduḥkhatā. yāvad iti vacanāt vipariṇāma eva duḥkhatā vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā saṃskāra eva duḥkhatā saṃskāraduḥkhateti vācyam. ayaṃ paryāyo vigraheṇaiva viśiṣṭo nārthena. sa eva hy atrārtho grahītavyaḥ. asādhāraṇatvād iti vistaraḥ. manaāpāḥ saṃskārāḥ asādhāraṇā duḥkhaduḥkhatāyāḥ. atas teṣām asādhāraṇatvād vipariṇāmaduḥkhatoktā. amanaāpāś cāsādhāraṇā vipariṇāmaduḥkhatāyāḥ. atas teṣām asādhāraṇatvād duḥkhaduḥkhatokteti. [Tib. 176a] sarve tu manaāpādayaḥ saṃskāraduḥkhatayā duḥkhāḥ tasyā vyāpinītvāt. yadi sarve 'pi tathā duḥkhāḥ kasmāt sarve (vipariṇāmaduḥkhatayā) na paśyaṃtīti ata āha. tāṃ tv āryā eva paśyaṃti nānye. katham itīdam upanyasyate āha cātreti sarvam.
body.translated_text: 'Suffering itself is suffering-ness: the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>). Similarly, change itself is suffering-ness: the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>). Conditioned existence itself is suffering-ness: the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>)' — from the word 'similarly,' this should be stated. This alternative formulation is distinguished only in expression, not in meaning — the very same meaning should be grasped here. 'Because of non-commonality' — and so forth in detail. Agreeable conditioned things are not common to the suffering of suffering. Therefore, because of their non-commonality [with the suffering of suffering], they are stated as [suffering through] the suffering of change. And disagreeable [conditioned things] are not common to the suffering of change. Therefore, because of their non-commonality, they are stated as [suffering through] the suffering of suffering. But all — agreeable and the rest — are suffering through the suffering of conditioned existence, because it pervades [everything]. If all are thus suffering, why do not all see [them as suffering through] the suffering of change? Therefore he says: 'But only nobles see that, not others.' How? — this is raised. He says 'and here' — and so forth.

body.text: evaṃ tarhīti yadi saṃskāraduḥkhatayā sarve 'pi saṃskārā duḥkhāḥ mārge 'pi saṃskāraduḥkhatāprasaṃgaḥ. saṃskṛtatvtā pratyayajanitatvād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'If so' — if all conditioned things are suffering through the suffering of conditioned existence, the consequence of the suffering of conditioned existence [extending] even to the path [follows] — because of being conditioned, because of being produced by conditions — this is the meaning.
