Others read: '<s>tadālaṃbanā ālaṃbanasmṛtyupasthānam</s>' — 'those that are apprehended are the objects (<s>ālaṃbana</s>).' Who [are they]? Body, feeling, mind, and <s>dharma</s>s. This being so, the object-foundation of mindfulness has the nature of all <s>dharma</s>s. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'O monks, "all <s>dharma</s>s" — this is a designation for the four foundations of mindfulness.'

body.text: tayā hi prajñayā tadvān prajñāvān. anupaśyaḥ kriyata iti. anupaśyatīty
body.translated_text: 'For by that wisdom, one who has it is wise; one is made a contemplator (<s>anupaśya</s>)' — meaning: he contemplates

body.text: anupaśyaḥ. pāghrādhmādheṭdṛśaḥ śa iti śapratyayaḥ. anupaśyaṃ pudgalaṃ karotīty anupaśyayati. prajñāsvabhāve tv evaṃ vigrahaḥ. anupaśyasya karaṇam anupaśyaneti. tayā hi prajñayā tadvān prajñāvān anupaśyaḥ kriyate. yathā prajñāyogāt prājñaḥ pudgala ucyate. evam anupaśyanāyogād anupaśya ity ato 'nupaśyanā prajñeti siddhaṃ. yataś coktaṃ bhagavatā. adhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ kāye kāyānupaśyī kāyānudarśī viharatīti. tenāpi jñāyate 'nupaśyanā prajñeti. katham iti sādhayaty anupaśyam asyāsti. kiṃ tad darśanaṃ. darśanalakṣaṇaṃ hy anupaśyam. ato 'nupaśyī pudgalo daṇḍivat. tataḥ saptamītatpuruṣaḥ. kāye 'nupaśyī kāyānupaśyīti. kāyam anupaśayituṃ śīlam asyeti kāyānupaśyīti ṇinir api yadi vidhīyeta tathāpy etadrūpaṃ sidhyatīti paśyāmaḥ.
body.translated_text: — hence <s>anupaśya</s>. The suffix <s>śa</s> is formed by the rule '<s>pāghrādhmādheṭdṛśaḥ śa</s>.' It makes a person a contemplator — hence <s>anupaśyanā</s> (contemplation). But if [the foundation of mindfulness] has the nature of wisdom, then the grammatical analysis is thus: the making of a contemplator is contemplation (<s>anupaśyanā</s>). For by that wisdom, one who has it is wise and is made a contemplator. Just as by connection with wisdom one is called a 'wise person,' so by connection with contemplation one [is called] a 'contemplator' — therefore contemplation is wisdom — this is established. And because the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Internally, individually, he dwells contemplating the body in the body — a body-contemplator.' From that too it is known that contemplation is wisdom. How? — he establishes: 'He has a contemplation.' What is that? 'Seeing.' For 'contemplation' has the characteristic of 'seeing.' Therefore the contemplating person [is designated] like 'one with a stick' (<s>daṇḍin</s>). Therefore the locative compound (<s>saptamītatpuruṣa</s>): 'a contemplator in the body' is 'a body-contemplator' (<s>kāyānupaśyī</s>). 'If the suffix <s>ṇin</s> were also applied — [meaning] one whose habit is to contemplate the body — [then the form] <s>kāyānupaśyī</s> — even then we consider that this same form would be established.'

body.text: smṛtyudrekatvād iti. smṛtyadhikatvād ity arthaḥ. [Tib. 190b] smṛtibalādhānavṛttitvād iti. balasyādhānaṃ. smṛter balādhānaṃ smṛtibalādhānaṃ. smṛtibalādhānena vṛttir asyā iti smṛtibalādhānavṛttiḥ prajñā. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. dārupāṭakīlasaṃdhāraṇavad yathā dārupāṭena tīkṣṇakīlena dārupāṭasya saṃdhāraṇam. evam asyāḥ prajñāyāḥ smṛtibalādhānenālaṃbane vṛttir iti. yadi hi smṛtir ālaṃbanaṃ dharayaty evaṃ prajñā prajānātīti. tad evaṃ smṛtyopatiṣṭhata iti smṛtyupasthānaṃ prajñeti vaibhāṣikīyo 'rthaḥ kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam iti kartary api lyuḍ bhavatīti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the predominance of mindfulness' — the meaning is: because of the abundance of mindfulness. 'Because of functioning through the placing of the power of mindfulness' — the placing of power; the placing of the power of mindfulness is the 'placing of the power of mindfulness.' The functioning of this [wisdom] through the placing of the power of mindfulness makes it 'functioning through the placing of the power of mindfulness' — wisdom. Its state [of being that]. Therefore. 'Like the holding of a split piece of wood by a sharp nail' — just as there is the holding of a split piece of wood by a sharp nail; so too, the functioning of this wisdom upon its object through the placing of the power of mindfulness. For if mindfulness holds the object, thus wisdom discerns — this is the meaning. 'Thus, that which is established [in mindfulness] through mindfulness is the foundation of mindfulness — [which is] wisdom' — this is the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> meaning. 'The frequentative suffix <s>lyuṭ</s> [applies] also in the agent sense.'

body.text: evaṃ tu yujyata ity ācāryaḥ. karaṇasādhanam etat. smṛtir anayopatiṣṭhata iti. arthapradarśanamātram etat. vigrahas tv evaṃ kartavyaḥ. upatiṣṭhate 'nenety upasthānaṃ. smṛte upasthānaṃ smṛtyupasthānam iti. kathaṃ smṛtir anayopatiṣṭhata ity āha. yathādṛṣṭasyābhilapanād iti. yasmād yathādṛṣṭo 'rthaḥ prajñayā. tathaivābhilapyate. smṛtyodgṛhyata ity arthaḥ. kva punar upatiṣṭhate. kāye yāvad dharmeṣu. kāye smṛtyupasthānaṃ kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ. evaṃ yāvad dharmeṣu smṛtyupasthānaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānam iti. yathā ca svabhāvasmṛtyupasthānasya. evaṃ saṃsargasmṛtyupasthānasyāpi. yathaiva hi prajñayā smṛtir upatiṣṭhate kāyādiṣu. evaṃ tatsaṃprayuktair apīti.
body.translated_text: 'But this is appropriate thus' — says the <s>Ācārya</s>. This is an instrumental-meaning derivation (<s>karaṇasādhana</s>): 'Mindfulness is established by means of this' — this is merely an illustration of the meaning. But the grammatical analysis should be done thus: that by which it is established is the <s>upasthāna</s> (establishment); the establishment of mindfulness is the <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundation of mindfulness). How is mindfulness established by means of it? — he says: 'Because of articulating what has been seen as it was seen' — because whatever meaning was seen by wisdom, that very thing is articulated — the meaning is: it is grasped by mindfulness. Where then is it established? In the body, up to in the <s>dharma</s>s. The establishment of mindfulness in the body is the body-foundation of mindfulness. Similarly, up to: the establishment of mindfulness in the <s>dharma</s>s is the <s>dharma</s>-foundation of mindfulness. And just as for the essential-nature foundation of mindfulness, so too for the association-foundation of mindfulness. For just as mindfulness is established in the body and the rest by wisdom, so too by those associated with it [wisdom].

body.text: idānīṃ sūtroktāṃ smṛtyupashānānāṃ karṇasādhanatvam asaṃbadhyamānaṃ dṛṣṭvā kārakāṃtareṇārthaṃ vivakṣur [Tib. 191a] āha. yatra tūktam iti vistaraḥ. yathā kāyasya samudayāstaṃgatāv uktau. evaṃ vedanādīnām api vaktavyau. kathaṃ. sparśasamudayāt vedanāyāḥ samudayo bhavati. sparśanirodhād
body.translated_text: Now, having seen that the <s>sūtra</s>-stated [understanding of] the foundations of mindfulness as instrumental meaning (<s>karaṇasādhana</s>) does not connect, wishing to express the meaning through another grammatical case, he says: 'But where it is stated' — and so forth in detail. Just as the arising and passing away of the body are stated, so too [those] of feeling and the rest should be stated. How? 'From the arising of contact (<s>sparśa</s>), there is the arising of feeling. From the cessation of contact

body.text: vedanāyā astaṃgamaḥ. nāmarūpasamudayāc cittasya samudayo bhavati. nānarūpanirodhāc cittasyāstaṃgamāḥ. manasikārasamudayād dharmāṇāṃ samudayo bhavati. manasikāranirodhād dharmāṇām astaṃgama iti. atra sūtre ālaṃbanam eva kāyavedanācittadharmāḥ smṛtyupasthānaṃ. smṛtir atra kāyādiṣūpatiṣṭhata iti kṛtvā. tad evam adhikaraṇasādhanaṃ darśitaṃ bhavati. upatiṣṭhate smṛtir asminn ity upasthānam. smṛter upasthānaṃ smṛtyupasthānaṃ. evaṃ yāvad dharmā eva smṛtyupasthānaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānam iti vigrahaḥ. yadi cātra sūtre ālaṃbanaṃ smṛtyupasthānaṃ nābhipretam abhaviṣyat. na bhagavān evam avakṣyat. kathaṃ ca bhikṣavaś caturṇāṃ smṛtyupasthānānāṃ samudayaś ca bhavaty astaṃgamaś ca. āhārasamudayāt kāyasya samudayo bhavati. āhāranirodhāt kāyasyāstaṃgama iti vistaraḥ. kāyādīnāṃ hi smṛtyupasthānatve sati tathā vacanaṃ yujyeta. tasmāt kāyādaya ālaṃbanasmṛtyupasthānam iti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: there is the passing away of feeling. From the arising of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>), there is the arising of mind. From the cessation of name-and-form, there is the passing away of mind. From the arising of mental attention (<s>manasikāra</s>), there is the arising of <s>dharma</s>s. From the cessation of mental attention, there is the passing away of <s>dharma</s>s.' In this <s>sūtra</s>, body, feeling, mind, and <s>dharma</s>s as objects alone are the foundation of mindfulness — because mindfulness is established here in the body and the rest. Thus, the locative meaning (<s>adhikaraṇasādhana</s>) has been shown: <s>upasthāna</s> is that in which mindfulness is established; the foundation of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) is the establishment of mindfulness [in them]. Similarly, up to: <s>dharma</s>s themselves are the foundation of mindfulness — the <s>dharma</s>-foundation of mindfulness — this is the grammatical analysis. And if in this <s>sūtra</s> the object were not intended as the foundation of mindfulness, the <s>Bhagavān</s> would not have spoken thus: 'And how, O monks, is there the arising and passing away of the four foundations of mindfulness? From the arising of food (<s>āhāra</s>), there is the arising of the body. From the cessation of food, there is the passing away of the body' — and so forth in detail. For only when body and the rest are [understood as] foundations of mindfulness would such a statement be fitting. Therefore, it is established that the body and the rest are the object-foundation of mindfulness.

body.text: yathālaṃbanaṃ caiṣāṃ nāmeti. eṣāṃ kāyasṃṛtyupasthānādīnāṃ [Tib. 191b] ālaṃbanāpekṣayā kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ yāvad dharmasmṛtyupasthānam iti nāma vyavasthāpate. svaparobhayasaṃtatyālaṃbanatvāt. parasaṃtatyālaṃbanatvāt. ubhayasaṃtatyālaṃbanatvāc ca pratyekam ekaikaśaḥ eṣāṃ kāyasmṛtyupasthānādīnāṃ traividhyaṃ bhavati. sūtre vacanāt. katham. adhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānupaśyī viharati. ātāpī saṃprajānan smṛtimān vinīya loke 'bhidhyādaurmanasye. bahirdhā ye kāyanupaśyī viharati ātāpīti pūrvavat. adhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānupaśyī viharatīti pūrvavat. evaṃ tāvat kāyasmṛtyupasthānasya traividhyaṃ. vedanāsmṛtyupasthānādīnām apy adhyātmaṃ vedanānāṃ vedanānupaśyī viharatīti vistareṇa traividhyaṃ yojyaṃ. audārikasya pūrvaṃ darśanād iti. kāyas tribhya audārikaḥ. ṣaḍvijñānavijñeyatvād iti. tasya pūrvaṃ darśanaṃ. dvābhyāṃ vedanā prakāraudārikatayeti tadanaṃtaraṃ tasyā darśanaṃ. sūkṣmapracāratvād durvijñatayā dharmāḥ sūkṣmā ity atas tebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ cittasya darśanam. aṃte dharmāṇām iti. sa ceti kāmarāgaḥ. sa ca cittasyeti sa vedanābhilāṣaḥ. tatkleśāprahāṇāt. tadadāṃtatvaṃ. yathākramam iti. [Tib. 192a] śuciviparyāsasya pratipakṣeṇa kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ. sukhaviparyāsasya pratipakṣeṇa vedanāsmṛtyupasthānaṃ. yatkiṃcid veditam idam atra duḥkhasyeti. nityaviparyāsasya pratipakṣeṇa cittasmṛtyupasthānānāṃ. cittasya laghuparivartitvāt. ātmaviparyāsasya pratipakṣeṇa dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ. piṇḍavibhāgato dharmāṇām anātmakāritvād dharmamātraṃ rahitam ātmaneti
body.translated_text: 'And their name is according to the object.' The name — mindfulness of the body (<s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) up to mindfulness of <s>dharma</s>s (<s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) — [Tib. 191b] is established with reference to the object of these [foundations]. Because of taking one's own continuum, another's continuum, and both continua as objects — because of taking another's continuum as object, and because of taking both continua as object — each one of these foundations of mindfulness individually has a threefold [division]. Because of the statement in the <s>sūtra</s>. How? 'One dwells contemplating the body in the body internally — ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and mental displeasure with respect to the world. One dwells contemplating the body in the body externally — ardent' — and so forth as before. 'One dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally' — and so forth as before. Thus far is the threefold [division] of mindfulness of the body. For mindfulness of feeling and the rest too — 'one dwells contemplating feelings in feelings internally' — the threefold [division] should be connected in detail. 'Because of first seeing what is coarse' — the body is coarser than the other three — because of being cognizable by the six consciousnesses. Its seeing comes first. Feeling is coarse in two respects by its variety — therefore its seeing [comes] immediately after. Because of subtle operation, being difficult to discern, <s>dharma</s>s are subtle — therefore the seeing of mind comes before them. '<s>Dharma</s>s come at the end.' 'That' means sensual passion. 'That of the mind' means the desire for feeling. 'Because of non-abandonment of those afflictions' — 'that untamedness.' 'In order' — [Tib. 192a] mindfulness of the body is the antidote of the perversion of purity (<s>śuciviparyāsa</s>). Mindfulness of feeling is the antidote of the perversion of pleasure (<s>sukhaviparyāsa</s>) — 'whatever is felt, that is within suffering here.' Mindfulness of mind is the antidote of the perversion of permanence (<s>nityaviparyāsa</s>) — because of the mind's rapid turning. Mindfulness of <s>dharma</s>s is the antidote of the perversion of self (<s>ātmaviparyāsa</s>) — because of the selfless operation of <s>dharma</s>s when analyzed into aggregates — '<s>dharma</s>s alone, devoid of self'

body.text: dharmanirvacanataḥ. dharmā ime pṛthagpṛthag avasthitāḥ. na ca kaścit svataṃtra ātmeti. taddarśanād vā. caturtham ubhayatheti. dharmasmṛtyupasthānam asaṃbhinnālaṃbanam amiśrālaṃbanaṃ bhavati. kāyavedanācittavyatiriktadharmālaṃbanatvasaṃbhavāt. saṃbhinnālaṃbanam api bhavati. kāyādīnāṃ dve trīṇi catvāri vā samastāni paśyatīti. yadi kāyaṃ vedanāṃ ca dve paśyati dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ. tat saṃbhinnālaṃbanaṃ. yadi kāyam yāvad dharmāṃś ca paśyati. tad api tathaiva. yad api kāyaṃ vedanāṃ cittaṃ dharmāṃś ca samastān paśyati. tad api saṃbhinnālaṃbanaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthāmam iti.
body.translated_text: — from the etymology of '<s>dharma</s>.' 'These <s>dharma</s>s exist separately and individually — and there is no independent self' — or because of seeing that. 'The fourth in both ways' — mindfulness of <s>dharma</s>s has an unmixed object — an object that is not mixed — because of the possibility of taking as object <s>dharma</s>s other than body, feeling, and mind. It also has a mixed object — because one sees two, three, or all four of body, feeling, and the rest together. If one sees body and feeling — that is mindfulness of <s>dharma</s>s with a mixed object. If one sees body up to <s>dharma</s>s — that too is likewise. And if one sees all together — body, feeling, mind, and <s>dharma</s>s — that too is mindfulness of <s>dharma</s>s with a mixed object.

body.text: iti. kāyavedanācittādharmān abhisamasya.
body.translated_text: having comprehended body, feeling, mind, and <s>dharma</s>s together.

body.text: ity uṣmaprakāraṃ kuśalamūlaṃ. pūrvarūpatvād iti. prathamanimittatvāt. pūrvasvabhāvatvād vā. prākarṣakatvād iti. [Tib. 192b] prābaṃdhikatvād ity arthaḥ. eṣāṃ tu viśeṣaṇaṃ paścād vakṣyāma iti saptame kośasthāne
body.translated_text: a wholesome root of the nature of heat. 'Because of being a precursory form' — because of being the first sign. Or because of being the first intrinsic nature. 'Because of being the drawer-forth' — [Tib. 192b] meaning: because of being the sustainer.

body.text: iti atra. yadi te 'pi tādṛśāḥ. atha kim artham upadiśyaṃta ity ata āha. utkṛṣṭataratvāt tu nāmāṃtaram iti. atha kasmān mūrdhāna ity ucyaṃta ity āha. calakuśalamūlamūrdhatvād iti. mūrdhaśabdo 'yaṃ prakarṣaparyaṃtavācī. tathā hi loke vaktāro bhavaṃti. mūrdhagatā khalv asya śrīr iti. dve hi kuśalamūle cale. uṣmagatamūrdhalakṣaṇe parihāṇisaṃbhavāt. dve acale kṣāṃtilaukikāgradharmalakṣaṇe viparyayāt. tatra tayor yan mṛdu. tad uṣmagataṃ. yad adhimātraṃ. te mūrdhānaḥ. acalayor api yan mṛdu. sā kṣāṃtiḥ. yad adhimātraṃ. te laukikāgradharmāḥ. ebhyo hi pāto 'tikramo veti. mūrdhabhyaḥ pātaḥ parihāṇiḥ. atikramo vā kṣāṃtisaṃmukhībhāvo vā. mūrdhnāṃ calatvāt. vṛkṣādimūrdhebhyo hi loke pāto vā bhaved atipāto vā. upariṣṭhānuprāptir iti mūrdhasādharmyaṃ. satyeṣv ākārāṇāṃ prathamato vinyasanam iti. satyeṣv anityādyākārāṇām ādita upanipātanaṃ. tadālaṃbanānāṃ pravartanam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: here. If those too are of such a nature, then for what purpose are they taught? — therefore he says: 'But because of being more excellent, [they have] a different name.' But why are they called 'summits' (<s>mūrdhan</s>)? He says: 'Because of being the summit of the unstable wholesome roots.' This word 'summit' (<s>mūrdha</s>) denotes the extreme of excellence. For thus in the world, people say: 'Indeed, his prosperity has reached the summit.' For there are two unstable wholesome roots — characterized by heat and summits — because of the possibility of falling away. And two stable ones — characterized by patience and supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>s — because of the opposite. Among those, what is mild — that is heat. What is intense — those are the summits. And among the stable ones too, what is mild — that is patience. What is intense — those are the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>s. 'For from these there is either falling or transcending' — from the summits there is falling — regression. Or transcending — facing patience. Because of the instability of the summits. For in the world, from the summit of a tree and the like, there is either falling or climbing higher. 'The attainment of the position above' — this is the similarity to summits. 'The first placement of aspects upon the truths' — the initial application of the aspects such as impermanence and the rest upon the truths. The meaning is: the commencement of [their operation] taking those as objects.

body.text: dharmasmṛtyupasthānād [Tib. 193a] anyair apīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: meaning: [Tib. 193a] by others too apart from mindfulness of <s>dharma</s>s.

body.text: abhyāsenottoptīkaraṇaṃ. vivardhayata iti vistaraḥ. vivardhayato yogino vardhanena
body.translated_text: making more intense through repeated practice. 'One increases' — and so forth in detail. Through the increase of the practitioner who increases,

body.text: viśiṣṭānāṃ kuśalamūlānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvaḥ. pūrvapratilabdhānām iti. aviśiṣṭānām asaṃmukhībhāvaḥ. kasmāt. abahumānāt. nyūnatvenāvahumānād ity arthaḥ. adhimātrasatyakṣamaṇād iti. uṣmagatāvasthāyāṃ mṛdu satyaṃ kṣamate rocate. mūrdhāvasthāyāṃ madhyaṃ. tadanaṃtaram idānīm adhimātrasatyakṣamaṇāt kṣāṃtir utpadyate. katham ity ata āha. aparihāṇita iti. yasmāt kṣāṃtir na parihīyate. mūrdhabhyas tu parihīyata ity asti saṃbhavaḥ.
body.translated_text: the arising face-to-face of distinguished wholesome roots [occurs]. 'Of those previously obtained' — of the undistinguished ones, there is no facing. Why? Because of lack of esteem — meaning: because of disregarding them as inferior. 'Because of intense patience regarding the truths' — in the stage of heat, one mildly assents to the truths. In the stage of summits, moderately. Then immediately after, because of intense assent to the truths, patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) arises. How? — therefore he says: 'Because of non-falling-away.' Because patience does not fall away — but from the summits one can fall away — there is a possibility.

body.text: iti. mṛdumadhye kṣāṃtī tathaiva. yathā mūrdhāna uktāḥ. tathaivākaraṇāt dharmasmṛtyupasthānena. satyeṣv ākārāṇām ākaraṇād ity arthaḥ. sarvasyā iti. mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedabhinnāyāḥ sarvasyāḥ kṣāṃteḥ. dharmasmṛtyupasthānenaiva vacanaṃ. nānyena kāyasmṛtyupasthānādinā. kasmāt. agradharmaśleṣāt. agradharmā hi darśanamārgaśleṣāt. dharmasmṛtyupasthānātmaka eveti. agradharmaśleṣād iti [Tib. 193b] agradharmāṇāṃ kāmāvacaraduḥkhasatyālaṃbanānām anaṃtarotpādāt kṣāṃteḥ kāmāvacaratvaduḥkhasatyālaṃbanam. agradharmaśleṣād dhi tatsādṛśyam iti. niyamāvacanād iti. adhimātrakṣāṃtivad uṣmagatādīnām ālaṃbanaṃ pratiniyamāvacanāt. adhimātrakṣāṃtyavadhāraṇenaiva hi traidhātukaduḥkhādyālaṃbanatvam eṣām uṣmagatādīnāṃ sidhyati. kathaṃ. kāmāptam eva duḥkhaṃ viṣayo 'syām. seyaṃ kāmāptaduḥkhaviṣayā adhimātrā kṣāṃtiḥ. kṣāṃter evety avadhāraṇāt anyāny uṣmagatādīni traidhātukaduḥkhādyālaṃbanānīti siddhaṃ. yadā kileti vistaraḥ. yadā kila rūpārūpyapratipakṣādīnām. adiśabdena rūpārūpyanirodhasamudayaduḥkhānāṃ kāmāvacarapratipakṣādīnāṃ ca grahaṇaṃ. ekaikasatyākārālaṃbanāpahrāsenaikaikasya satyākārasya ekaikasya satyālaṃbanasya cāpahrāsena yāvat kāmāvacaram eva duḥkhaṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣaṇābhyāṃ manasikaroti. eṣā sarvaiva rūpārāpyapratipakṣākārahrāsāt prabhṛti madhyā kṣāṃtiḥ. katham. anvayajñānapakṣaṃ tāvan mārgaṃ mārgato nyāyataḥ pratipattito nairyāṇikataś ceti [Tib. 194a] taiś caturbhir ākārair ākārayati. tatas tribhir ekaṃ hitvā. tato dvābhyāṃ dvau hitvā. tata ekena. tato mārgasatyaṃ hitvā. rūpārūpyanirodhaṃ caturbhiḥ svair ākārair ākārayati. tatas tribhiḥ dvābhyām ekenaiva cākārya nirodhasatyaṃ cāpāsya. samudayasatyaṃ caturbhiḥ svair ākāraiḥ. tribhiḥ dvābhyām ekena cākārya. tathaiva tad apāsya. duḥkhasatyaṃ svair ākārair yāvad ekenākārya. tad api satyam apāsya. kāmāvacarapratipakṣaṃ svaiś caturbhir ākāraiḥ tribhiḥ dvābhyām ekena cākārayati. tad apāsya.
body.translated_text: the mild and middling patiences are just like that — just as the summits were described. Likewise, because of operating with mindfulness of <s>dharma</s>s — meaning: because of operating with aspects upon the truths. 'Of all' — of all patience divided into mild, middling, and intense. 'By mindfulness of <s>dharma</s>s alone' — not by another, such as mindfulness of the body and the rest. Why? 'Because of contiguity with the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>s.' For the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>s are contiguous with the path of seeing — [Tib. 193b] and are of the nature of mindfulness of <s>dharma</s>s alone. Because of contiguity with the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>s, the patience is similar to them — from the contiguity of the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>s, it has that similarity. 'Because of the absence of a statement of restriction' — because of the absence of a statement restricting the object of heat and the rest, as in the case of intense patience. For through the restriction to intense patience alone, the object of these — heat and the rest — as being the suffering truth and the rest belonging to the three realms — is established. How? '[Intense patience has] the suffering of the Desire Realm alone as its object.' This intense patience has the suffering of the Desire Realm as its object. Because of the restriction 'of patience alone,' the others — heat and the rest — are established as having the suffering truth and the rest of the three realms as their objects. 'When indeed' — and so forth in detail. When indeed, of the antidotes of the Form and Formless [Realms] and the rest — by the word 'and the rest,' the cessation, origination, and suffering [truths] of the Form and Formless [Realms], and the antidotes and the rest of the Desire Realm are grasped. Through the reduction of the aspects and objects one by one — through the reduction of each individual truth-aspect and each individual truth-object — one mentally attends to the suffering of the Desire Realm alone in two moments. All of this, from the beginning of the reduction of Form and Formless antidote aspects, is middling patience. How? One first takes the path from the subsequent-knowledge class (<s>anvayajñānapakṣa</s>) [and contemplates it] as path, as reasonable, as practice, as leading to liberation — [Tib. 194a] with those four aspects. Then with three — removing one. Then with two — removing two. Then with one. Then, having removed the truth of the path [of the upper realms], one takes the cessation of the Form and Formless [Realms] with its four proper aspects. Then with three, with two, with one alone — and having set aside the truth of cessation, the truth of origination with its four proper aspects. With three, with two, with one — and having similarly set that aside, the truth of suffering with its proper aspects, up to with one — and having set aside that truth too, the Desire Realm antidote with its four proper aspects, with three, with two, with one. Having set that aside,

body.text: kāmāvacaranirodhasamudayasatye tathaiva svākārahrāsakrameṇākāryāpāsya ca. kāmāvacaraṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ caturbhir ākārair ākārayati. tatas tribhiḥ tato dvābhyām ākārayatīti. evaṃ hi hrāsāraṃbhāt prabhṛti sarva ete kṣaṇā madhyā kṣāṃtir ity uktaṃ bhavati. tṛtīye kṣaṇe tadālaṃbanaivādhimātrā kṣāṃtiḥ. caturthe agradharmās tadālaṃbanā eva. mrdvī tu kṣāṃtir yā purastād adhimātrebhyo mūrdhabhyo 'naṃtaraṃ kāmāvacaraṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ yāvan mārgasatyaṃ. rūpārūpyāvacaraṃ ca. svaiḥsvaiḥ sarvair ākārair anapahrāsaṃ manasikurvata ity avagaṃtavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: the truths of cessation and origination of the Desire Realm — similarly, through the sequential reduction of their own aspects and having set [them] aside — the truth of suffering of the Desire Realm [is contemplated] with four aspects, then with three, then with two. Thus, from the beginning of the reduction, all these moments are stated as middling patience. In the third moment, the intense patience takes that very [suffering of the Desire Realm] as object. In the fourth, the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>s take that very thing as object. But the mild patience — which precedes [and comes] immediately after the intense summits — should be understood as one mentally attending to the suffering of the Desire Realm up to the truth of the path, and of the Form and Formless Realms, with all their respective aspects without reduction.

body.text: Tib. 194b
body.translated_text: Tib. 194b

body.text: evaṃ tāvad eke vyācakṣate. ākārāpahrāsapūrvaka ālaṃbanāpahrāsa iti.
body.translated_text: Thus far, some explain: the reduction of objects follows the reduction of aspects.

body.text: apare punar vyācakṣate. ekaikasatyākārālaṃbanāpahrāseneti. naivaṃ grahītavyaṃ ekaikasatyākārālaṃbanāpahrāsene ceti. kiṃ tarhi. rūpārūpyapratipakṣādīnām ekaikeṣāṃ satyānāṃ ye ākārāḥ. teṣām ālaṃbanahrāseneti vyākhyātavyam iti.
body.translated_text: Others, however, explain: 'through the reduction of the aspects and objects of each individual truth' — this should not be taken as 'through the reduction of the aspects and objects of each individual truth.' Rather, it should be explained: the aspects of each individual truth of the Form and Formless antidotes and the rest — [what is meant is] through the reduction of [the truths that serve as] objects [of those aspects].

body.text: ekānnaviṃśatikṣaṇaśataṃ madhyā kṣāṃtir iti varṇayaṃti. ākārāpahrāsa. pūrvake hy ālaṃbanāpahrāse sati atibahavaś cittakṣaṇā visarpaṃti. na caitan nyāyyaṃ. na hi satyeṣu vidyamāneṣu ākāratyāgo yujyate. yadā tu satyāni tyaktāni bhavaṃti. tadākāratyāga iti yuktaṃ. evaṃ ca sati pūrvaṃ satyālaṃbanahrāsaṃ karoti paścād ākārahrāsaṃ. na hi maule viṣaye 'napākṛte tadālaṃbanāpākaraṇaṃ nyāyyaṃ. samāhitāsamāhitaduḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgā aṣṭau vyavasthāpyaṃte. eṣām ākārā dvātriṃśad bhavaṃtīty etad adhunā nyāyāṃtaram upadiśyate. kathaṃ kṛtvā. yadā kāmāvacaraṃ duḥkhaṃ caturbhir ākārair manasikaroti. evaṃ yāvad rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ pratipakṣaṃ caturbhir ākārair manasikarotīyaṃ mṛdvī kṣāṃtiḥ. yadā punaḥ kāmāvacaraduḥkhaṃ caturbhir ākārair manasikarotīty evaṃ yāvat kāmāvacarāṇāṃ [Tib. 195a] saṃskārāṇāṃ pratipakṣaṃ manasikaroti caturbhir ākāraiḥ. rūpārūkyāvacarāṇāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ pratipakṣaṃ parityajataḥ prabhṛti madhyā kṣāṃtir ārabdhā. tatra ca rūpārūpyāvacarapratipakṣaparityāge 'ṣṭāviṃśatiś cittakṣaṇā bhavaṃti. kāmāvacarasaṃskārapratipakṣaparityāge caturviṃśatiḥ. rūpārūpyāvacarasaṃskāranirodhaparityāge viṃśatiḥ. kāmāvacaranirodhaparityāge ṣoḍaśa rūpārūpyāvacarasamudayaparityāge dvādaśa. kāmāvacarasamudayaparityāge 'ṣṭau. rūpārūpyāvacaraduḥkhaparityāge catvāraḥ. kāmāvacaraṃ duḥkhaṃ caturbhir ākārair manasikaroti. tasya bhavaṃty ākārāś catvāraḥ. sa ca yogācāro dvividhaḥ.
body.translated_text: They describe one hundred and nineteen moments as middling patience — [those who hold] reduction of aspects. For in the prior [system of] reduction of objects, extremely many mental moments would elapse. And this is not reasonable — for when the truths are [still] present [as objects], the removal of aspects is not reasonable. But when the truths have been removed, then the removal of aspects is reasonable. And this being so, one first makes the reduction of truth-objects and afterwards the reduction of aspects. For it is not reasonable to remove the object of a root [truth] when it has not been set aside. 'Concentrated and non-concentrated suffering, origination, cessation, and path — eight are established.' Their aspects are thirty-two — this is now another method being taught. How? When one mentally attends to the suffering of the Desire Realm with four aspects — thus, up to when one mentally attends to the antidote of the Form and Formless Realms with four aspects — this is mild patience. But when one mentally attends to the suffering of the Desire Realm with four aspects — thus, up to when one mentally attends to the antidote of the Desire Realm [Tib. 195a] with four aspects — [and] from the point when one abandons the antidote of the Form and Formless Realms — middling patience has begun. Therein, in the abandoning of the Form and Formless antidote, there are twenty-eight mental moments. In the abandoning of the Desire Realm-formations antidote, twenty-four. In the abandoning of the cessation of the Form and Formless Realms, twenty. In the abandoning of the Desire Realm cessation, sixteen. In the abandoning of the origination of the Form and Formless Realms, twelve. In the abandoning of the Desire Realm origination, eight. In the abandoning of the suffering of the Form and Formless Realms, four. One mentally attends to the suffering of the Desire Realm with four aspects — its aspects are four. And that practitioner is twofold.

body.text: dṛṣṭicaritaḥ. tṛṣṇācaritaś ca. dṛṣṭicarito 'pi dvividhaḥ. ātmadṛṣṭi caritaḥ. ātmīyadṛṣṭicaritaś ca. yo hy ātmadṛṣṭicarito bhavati. so 'nātmākāreṇa niyāmam avakrāmati. yas tv ātmīyadṛṣṭicaritaḥ. sa śūnyākāreṇa. tṛṣṇāśarito 'pi dvividhaḥ. asmimanopahataḥ. kausīdyādhikaś ca. tatra yo 'smimānophataḥ. so 'nityākāreṇa niyāmam avakrāmati. yaḥ kausīdyādhikaḥ. sa duḥkhākāreṇa. tatrātmadṛṣṭicarito yogācāraḥ punas tat kāmāvacaraṃ duḥkhaṃ tribhir ākārair manasikaroti. ekam ākāraṃ hitvā. tato dvābhyām anātmaśūnyatākārābhyāṃ. tata ekam anātmākāraṃ dviḥ saṃmukhīkaroti. duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāṃtiduḥkhadharmajñānasadṛśam [Tib. 195b] iti. eṣā madhyā kṣāṃtir ity evam ekānnaviṃśaṃ cittaśataṃ bhavati. evam ātmīyādhimuktasya tu śūnyānātmākārābhyām ākārayataḥ śūnyākāraṃ dviḥ saṃmukhīkaroti. eṣāsya madhyā kṣāṃtiḥ evam ekānnaviṃśakṣaṇaśatam. evaṃ tṛṣṇācarito dviprakāraḥ. asmimānopahataḥ. kausīdyādhikaś ca vaktavyā iti. adhimātrā tu kṣāṃtir ekam eva kṣaṇaṃ. sā yathāpudgalacaritam anityākāreṇa vā duḥkhākāreṇa vā śūnyākāreṇa vā anātmākāreṇa vā saṃprayukteti. atha kim artham ekaikasatyākārālaṃbanahrāsaḥ kriyate. pūrvaṃ hi tena traidhātukaṃ vidūṣayatā samastaḥ pratipakṣa ālaṃbitaḥ. paścāt kāmadhātoḥ pūrvaṃ praheyaparijñeyatvāt kāmāvacara eva duḥkhe 'vatiṣṭhata iti. tatpuruṣakāreṇa mārgākarṣaṇād iti. vinā sabhāgahetunā. pūrvasyānāsravasyābhāvāt. laukikāgradharmapuruṣakāreṇa mārgasatyasyākarṣaṇāt. sarvalaukikaśreṣṭhatvam agradharmāṇāṃ gamyate.
body.translated_text: one of view-conduct (<s>dṛṣṭicarita</s>) and one of craving-conduct (<s>tṛṣṇācarita</s>). The one of view-conduct is also twofold: one of self-view conduct (<s>ātmadṛṣṭicarita</s>) and one of mine-view conduct (<s>ātmīyadṛṣṭicarita</s>). One who is of self-view conduct enters the certainty (<s>niyāma</s>) through the aspect of non-self (<s>anātma</s>). But one who is of mine-view conduct, through the aspect of emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>). The one of craving-conduct is also twofold: one afflicted by the pride 'I am' (<s>asmimāna</s>) and one dominated by laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>). Therein, one who is afflicted by the pride 'I am' enters the certainty through the aspect of impermanence (<s>anitya</s>). One who is dominated by laziness, through the aspect of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>). Therein, the practitioner (<s>yogācāra</s>) of self-view conduct then contemplates that Desire Realm suffering through three aspects, setting aside one aspect. Then through two — the aspects of non-self and emptiness. Then he brings the one aspect of non-self to the fore twice — resembling the <s>duḥkhadharmajñānakṣānti</s> and <s>duḥkhadharmajñāna</s>. This is the middling tolerance — thus there are nineteen hundred mind-moments. Similarly, for one inclined toward what is 'mine,' contemplating through the aspects of emptiness and non-self, he brings the aspect of emptiness to the fore twice. This is his middling tolerance — thus nineteen hundred moments. Similarly, the one of craving-conduct is twofold — afflicted by the pride 'I am' and dominated by laziness — should be stated. But the supreme tolerance (<s>adhimātra kṣānti</s>) is just a single moment. It is associated with the aspect of impermanence, or suffering, or emptiness, or non-self, according to the person's conduct. Then, for what purpose is the reduction of aspects and objects of each truth made? For previously, when debasing all three realms, he took the entire counteragent as object. Afterward, because the Desire Realm is to be abandoned and comprehended first, he rests in Desire Realm suffering alone. 'By the effort of that person, the path is attracted' — without a homogeneous cause, because of the absence of a prior uncontaminated [path]. By the effort of the mundane supreme <s>dharma</s>s, the truth of the path is attracted. The supremacy of the supreme <s>dharma</s>s among all mundane [dharmas] is understood.

body.text: sarve tu paṃca skaṃdhāḥ saparivāragrahaṇād iti. samāhitabhūmidatvād uṣmagatādīnām avijñaptilakṣaṇo rūpaskaṃdho 'stīti [Tib. 196a] paṃca skaṃdhā uṣmagatādayaḥ saparivāragrahaṇāt saparivārā gṛhyaṃte iti. mā bhūd āryasyeti. prāptisaṃmukhībhāvāt āryapudgalasyoṣmagatādīnāṃ phalaprāptiprayogabhūtānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvo mā bhūd iti prāptayo noṣmagatādiṣu gṛhyaṃte. na hi prāptaprayogaphalasyāryasya prayogasaṃmukhīkaraṇaṃ nyāyyam iti.
body.translated_text: 'But all five aggregates, because of inclusion with retinue' — because they belong to the ground of concentrated [attention], the heat stage (<s>uṣmagata</s>) and the rest have an imperceptible form (<s>avijñapti</s>) characterized as the form aggregate — thus the heat stage and the rest are five aggregates. Because of inclusion with retinue, they are included with retinue. 'Lest there be for the Noble' — because of the proximity of attainment, lest there be the proximity of the heat stage and the rest — which serve as the preliminary practice for fruit-attainment — for the Noble person, acquisitions (<s>prāpti</s>) are not included in the heat stage and the rest. For it is not proper for a Noble one who has attained the fruit of the preliminary practice to bring the preliminary practice to the fore again.

body.text: trisatyālaṃbanoṣmagatākaraṇa iti. duḥkhasamudayamārgālaṃbanoṣmagatākaraṇe. dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ pratyutpannaṃ. yatnajanyasya kāryasyākaraṇe samastālaṃbanatvena dharmasmṛtyupasthānasyaiva samarthatvāt. pratiniyatālaṃbanatvena hi kāyasmṛtyupasthānādīny asamarthānīti anāgatāni catvāri
body.translated_text: 'In the production of heat having three truths as object' — in the production of the heat stage having suffering, origination, and the path as objects, the <s>dharma</s> foundation of mindfulness (<s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) is present. Because in the production of an effect brought about by effort, only the <s>dharma</s> foundation of mindfulness is capable, since it takes all [truths] as its object. Because the body foundation of mindfulness and the rest, having restricted objects, are incapable — the four that are future

body.text: bhāvyaṃta iti. yasmāt smṛtyupasthānena kāyavedanādayo 'pi duḥkhasatyādisaṃgṛhītā gṛhyaṃte. kāyasmṛtyupasthānādīni ca pūrvapratilabdhāni bhavaṃtīty ataś catvāry api bhāvyaṃte prāptyutpādād iti. nirodhasatyālaṃbane tad evobhayatheti. nirodhasatyālaṃbane uṣmagatākaraṇe. dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ pratyutpannaṃ. tad eva cānāgataṃ bhāvyate. na kāyasmṛtyupasthānādīni. nirodhasatye kāyādyabhāvāt. [Tib. 196b] sarvatrākārāḥ sabhāgā iti. trisatyālaṃbanasya nirodhasatyālaṃbanasya coṣmagatasyākaraṇe sadṛśā evākārā bhāvyaṃte. duḥkhasatyālaṃbane duḥkhasatyākārā eva catvāro bhāvyaṃte. na samudayasatyādyākārāḥ. samudayasatyādyākārālaṃbane samudayasatyādyādyākārā eva catvāro bhāvyaṃte. nānya ityādi. vivardhana iti. trisatyālaṃbane. kāyasmṛtyupasthānādīnām anyatamat pratyutpannaṃ saṃbhavati. mirodhasatyālaṃbane 'ntyaṃ pratyutpannaṃ. ubhayatrānāgatāni catvāri. ākāraḥ sarve 'pi ṣoḍaśāpi bhāvyaṃte. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. labdhatvāt gotrāṇāṃ saṃbhavastaś catuḥsatyālaṃbanakāyasmṛtyupasthānādijātīnāṃ labdhatvād ity arthaḥ. mūrdhākaraṇa iti vistaraḥ. mūrdhākaraṇe sarvatrāpi dharmasmṛtyupasthānam eva pratyutpannaṃ. kāyādismṛtyupasthānānām ākaraṇe 'sāmarthyāt. nirodhālaṃbanavivardhane 'pi aṃtyaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ pratyupannam. itareṣām ayogāt. trisatyālaṃbanavivardhane tu caturṇām anyatamat pratyutpannam. anāgatāni sarvatra catvāri. ākārā api sarve. labdhatvāt gotrāṇām ity avagaṃtavyaṃ. [Tib. 197a] kṣāṃtīnāṃ sarvatrāṃtyam iti. ākaraṇe vivardhane cāṃtyaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ pratyutpannaṃ. tathā hy uktaṃ. sarvasyāḥ kṣāṃtyā dharmeṇa vardhanam iti. agradharmeṣv aṃtyam iti. agradharmeṣu saṃmukhīkriyamāṇeṣv aṃtyaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ pratyutpannam. anāgatāni catvāri anutpattidharmāny eva prāpyaṃte. ākāraś catvāri eveti. anityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmākārāḥ. anyābhāvād iti. yasmād anyasamudayādyākārā agradharmā na saṃti duḥkhamātrālaṃbanatvāt. yathā tarhy agradharmāsvabhāvakāyasmṛtyupasthānādyasaṃmukhībhāve 'py agradharmasamudācārāvasthāyām anāgatāni kāyasmṛtyupasthānādīni bhāvyaṃte. evam agradharmāsvabhāvasamudayādyādyākārā ānagatā bhāvyaṃta iti kiṃ neṣyata ity ataḥ punar āha. darśanamārgasādṛśyāc ceti. duḥkhākārā eva catvāro bhāvyaṃte. kasmāt. darśanamārgasādṛśyāt. darśanamārge hi yasya satyasya darśanaṃ bhavati. tadākārā eva bhāvyaṃte. darśanamārgasadṛśyā hy agradharmāḥ. kiṃ punar
body.translated_text: are cultivated. Since through the <s>dharma</s> foundation of mindfulness, the body, feeling, and the rest that are included in the truth of suffering and the rest are also apprehended. And the body foundation of mindfulness and the rest have been previously obtained — therefore, all four too are cultivated, because of the arising of acquisition. In the production of the heat stage having the truth of cessation as object, that same [dharma foundation of mindfulness] in both ways — in the production of the heat stage having the truth of cessation as object, the <s>dharma</s> foundation of mindfulness is present. That same [dharma foundation of mindfulness] is cultivated as future as well. Not the body foundation of mindfulness and the rest, because of the absence of the body and the rest in the truth of cessation. The aspects are always homogeneous — in the production of the heat stage having three truths as object or the truth of cessation as object, only homogeneous aspects are cultivated. In the case of the truth of suffering as object, only the four aspects of the truth of suffering are cultivated — not the aspects of the truth of origination and the rest. In the case of the truth of origination and the rest as objects, only the four aspects of the truth of origination and the rest are cultivated — not others, and so forth. 'In growth' — having three truths as object, any one of the body foundation of mindfulness and the rest is present. Having the truth of cessation as object, the last [dharma foundation] is present. In both cases, the four that are future [are cultivated]. All aspects — all sixteen too — are cultivated. For what reason? Because the lineages have been obtained — the meaning is: because lineages of the types of body foundation of mindfulness and the rest having the four truths as object have been obtained as possibilities. 'In the production of the summit' — and so forth in detail. In the production of the summit, everywhere the <s>dharma</s> foundation of mindfulness alone is present — because of the incapacity of the body and other foundations of mindfulness in the [summit's] production. In the growth of the cessation-object [summit] too, the last — the <s>dharma</s> foundation of mindfulness — is present, because the others are unfitting. But in the growth of the three-truth-object [summit], any one of the four is present. The four that are future everywhere. The aspects too are all — because the lineages have been obtained — this should be understood. 'Of the tolerances, everywhere the last' — in both the production and growth, the last — the <s>dharma</s> foundation of mindfulness — is present. For thus it was stated: 'The growth of all tolerance is through the <s>dharma</s> [foundation].' 'In the supreme <s>dharma</s>s, the last' — in the supreme <s>dharma</s>s being brought to the fore, the last — the <s>dharma</s> foundation of mindfulness — is present. The four that are future are obtained as having the nature of non-arising alone. The aspects are four only — the aspects of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self. Because there are no others — since supreme <s>dharma</s>s with aspects of origination and the rest do not exist, because they have only suffering as their object. 'But just as, even when the body foundation of mindfulness and the rest that are of the nature of supreme <s>dharma</s>s are not brought to the fore, in the state of the arising of supreme <s>dharma</s>s, the future body foundations of mindfulness and the rest are cultivated — similarly, why are not the future aspects of origination and the rest cultivated?' — to this he further says: 'And because of similarity to the path of seeing.' Only the four aspects of suffering are cultivated. Why? Because of similarity to the path of seeing. For in the path of seeing, only the aspects of that truth which is being seen are cultivated. And the supreme <s>dharma</s>s are similar to the path of seeing. What moreover

body.text: eṣāṃ darśanamārgeṇa sādṛśyaṃ anuśleṣāt. tathaiva prathamataḥ kāmāvacaraduḥkhālaṃbanatvaṃ [Tib. 197b] tulyabhūmikatvaṃ vā. tathā hi darśanamārgam adhikṛtya vakṣyati.
body.translated_text: is their similarity to the path of seeing? Because of proximity — in the same way, having the Desire Realm suffering as object first, or being of the same ground. For thus, regarding the path of seeing, he will say:

children.translated_text: 'It is of one ground with the supreme <s>dharma</s>s' —

body.text: iti . yad vā pṛthagjanatvaghātāya duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāṃter ānaṃtaryamārgabhūtā agradharmā bhavaṃti. tad eṣāṃ darśanamārgeṇa sādṛśyaṃ. sadṛśā hy ānaṃtaryamārgā vimuktimārgair iti.
body.translated_text: thus. Or, the supreme <s>dharma</s>s function as the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) for the destruction of the state of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) through the <s>duḥkhadharmajñānakṣānti</s>. That is their similarity to the path of seeing. For the uninterrupted paths are similar to the liberation paths.

body.text: (VI.21-23) vidha vibhāga iti vistaraḥ. tasya dhātor etad yañirūpaṃ. niścita iti. niḥśabdasyārthaṃ darśayati. kathaṃ punar niścito vedha ity āha. tena vicikitsāprahāṇāt niścitaḥ. satyānāṃ ca vibhajanāt. idaṃ duḥkham ayaṃ yāvan mārga iti. nirvedha āryamārgaḥ. tasya bhāgo darśanamārgaikadeśaḥ. tasyāvāhakatvenākarṣakatvena hitatvāt tasmai hitam iti chaḥ. tena nirvedhabhāgīyam iti bhavati.
body.translated_text: (VI.21-23) '<s>Vedha</s>' means division (<s>vibhāga</s>) — and so forth in detail. This is the nominal form of that root. '<s>Niścita</s>' (certain) — he shows the meaning of the prefix <s>niḥ</s>. How then is it a certain penetration? — he says: because by that, doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>) is abandoned — [it is] certain. And because of the division of the truths: 'this is suffering, this is — up to — the path.' <s>Nirvedha</s> is the noble path. Its portion (<s>bhāga</s>) is a part of the path of seeing. Because of being beneficial (<s>hita</s>) to it, by being its vehicle and attractor — hence [the suffix] <s>cha</s>. Thus it becomes <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (aids to penetration).

children.translated_text: 'Belonging to the ground of the access [concentration], the intermediate [dhyānas], and the [main] dhyānas' —

body.text: iti. anāgamyaṃ cāṃtaraṃ ca dhyānāni ca bhūmayo 'syety
body.translated_text: thus. The access (<s>anāgamya</s>), the intermediate (<s>antara</s>), and the <s>dhyāna</s>s are the grounds of this —

children.translated_text: [hence] 'belonging to the ground of the access, the intermediate, and the <s>dhyāna</s>s.'

body.text: nordhvam iti. nārūpyeṣu nirvedhabhāgīyam asti. darśanaparivāratvāt. darśanamārgaprayogatvād ity arthaḥ. tadabhāvaḥ. dāmadhātvālaṃbanatvād iti. tasya darśanamārgasyābhāvas tadabhāvaḥ. kva. ūrdhvam iti vartate. ārūpyeṣv ity arthaḥ. kasmāt. kāma dhātvanālaṃbanāt. yasmād ārūpyāḥ kāmadhātuṃ [Tib. 198a] nālaṃbaṃte. āha. kiṃ kāmadhātvālaṇbanena darśanamārgeṇa prayojanam iti. ata ucyate. tasya pūrvaṃ parijñeyapraheyatvād iti. tasya kāmadhātor duḥkharūpasya pūrvaṃ parijñeyatvāt. samudayarūpasya ca praheyatvāt. atra ca hetur yasmāt sa yogī kāmāvacareṇa duḥkhena vihanyate. tena sa pūrvaṃ tato mokṣam anveṣata iti. teṣāṃ rūpadhātau paṃcaskaṃdhako vipāka iti. teṣāṃ nirvedhabhāgīyānāṃ rūpāvacaratvāt yadi ca yogī rūpadhātāv upapadyeta. tatas tasya tatra paṃca skaṃdhako vipāko 'bhinirvartate. paripūrikāṇy eva ca tānīṣṭavedanīyajananāt. nākṣepakāṇi nikāyasabhāgasya. bhavadveṣitvāt. anityādibhir ākārair bhavaṃ dviṣaṃtīti.
body.translated_text: 'Not above' — the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) do not exist in the formless realms. Because of being attendants of seeing (<s>darśana</s>). The meaning is: because of being the preliminary practice of the path of seeing. [Why?] Because of the absence of that [path of seeing]. 'Because of not having the Desire Realm as object' — the absence of that — of the path of seeing — [is] 'the absence of that.' Where? 'Above' is implied — meaning: in the formless realms. Why? Because they do not take the Desire Realm as object. Since the formless [attainments] do not take the Desire Realm as object. He says: 'What is the purpose of [requiring] the path of seeing to have the Desire Realm as object?' Therefore it is said: 'because that [Desire Realm] is to be comprehended and abandoned first.' Because the Desire Realm in its suffering form is to be comprehended first, and in its origination form is to be abandoned first. And the reason here is: because that practitioner is afflicted by Desire Realm suffering, therefore he first seeks liberation from it. 'Of those [nirvedhabhāgīyas], the fruition in the Form Realm is a fivefold aggregate' — because the aids to penetration belong to the Form Realm, if a practitioner were to be reborn in the Form Realm, then a fivefold aggregate fruition would manifest for him there. And those are exclusively fulfilling — because of generating pleasant fruition. Not projecting — not projecting a class-homogeneity (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>). Because of aversion toward existence — because they debase existence through the aspects of impermanence and the rest.

children.translated_text: 'The first two' — having the nature of the heat stage (<s>uṣmagata</s>) and the summit (<s>mūrdhan</s>).
'Have the Desire Realm as their basis' —

body.text: yasmād ihaiva satyābhisamayao nānyadhātau. nordhvaṃ hi dṛkpathaḥ asaṃvegāt. iha vidhā tatra niṣṭheti cāgamād iti. triṣu dvīpeṣūttarakuruvarjyeṣv iti vyākhyāyate. uttarakauravāṇāṃ mṛdvindriyatvāt. deveṣu saṃmukhībhāva iti. kāmāvacareṣu. caturthaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyaṃ [Tib. 198b] deveṣv api. teṣv eva ca nānyatra.
body.translated_text: because the realization of the truths (<s>satyābhisamaya</s>) occurs here [in the Desire Realm] alone and not in another realm. 'For above, the path of seeing does not [exist], because of the absence of urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>).' 'Here the practice, there the accomplishment — and from scripture' — it is explained as in the three continents excluding <s>Uttarakuru</s>. Because the <s>Uttarakuravans</s> have dull faculties. 'The proximity among the gods' — among the Desire Realm [gods]. The fourth aid to penetration — the supreme <s>dharma</s>s — also [arises] among the gods. And among them alone, not elsewhere.

body.text: tṛīṇi nirvedhabhāgīyāny anyatra agradharmebhyaḥ. ihaiva janmani strīpuruṣendriyaparāvṛttau ubhayāśrayāṇi strīpuruṣendriyāśrayāṇi striyaḥ puruṣāś ca labhaṃte. striyo hy etāny utpādya janmāṃtarastrībhāvaprādurbhāve stryāśrayāṇi saṃmukhīkurvaṃti. janmāṃtarapuruṣabhāvaprādurbhāve tu puruṣāśrayāṇi saṃmukhīkurvaṃti. na hi tallābhinīnāṃ strīṇāṃ janmāṃtare strībhāvo na saṃbhavati. puruṣā api tathaiva strībhāve janmāṃtare sati stryāśrayāṇi saṃmukhīkurvaṃti. puruṣabhāve puruṣāśrayāṇīti. agradharmān praty āha.
body.translated_text: Three aids to penetration other than the supreme <s>dharma</s>s — here in this very birth, when there is a transformation of the sex-faculty (<s>strīpuruṣendriya</s>), they have both bases — having the female and male faculty as basis. Both women and men obtain them. For women, having produced these, when female existence manifests in the next birth, they bring to the fore those with female basis. But when male existence manifests in the next birth, they bring to the fore those with male basis. For it is not the case that women who have obtained those cannot have female existence in the next birth. Men too, similarly, when there is female existence in the next birth, bring to the fore those with female basis. When there is male existence, those with male basis. Regarding the supreme <s>dharma</s>s, he says:

children.translated_text: 'A woman obtains the supreme <s>dharma</s>s with both bases' —

body.text: stry evobhayāśrayān agradharmān labhate. na puruṣaḥ. tathā hi strī tān labdhvā stryāśrayais tais tadānīṃtanaiḥ samanvāgatā bhavati. janmāṃtaraparāvṛttau ca kāmadhātau puruṣāśrayaprādurbhāve puruṣāśrayaiḥ sa puruṣaḥ samanvāgata iti. puruṣas tu puruṣāśrayān eva labhate. kasmād ity āha. strītvasyāpratisaṃkhyānirodhalābhād iti. tasmiṃ janmani strītvaṃ janmāṃtare 'pi punar nāstīty asyāpratisaṃkhyānirodhalābhaḥ. yo hy agradharmān utpādayati. so 'vaśyam anaṃtaraṃ darśanamārgam utapādayen [Tib. 199a] na ca dṛṣṭasatyasya punaḥ strītvaprādurbhāva iti siddhāṃtaḥ.
body.translated_text: a woman alone obtains the supreme <s>dharma</s>s with both bases, not a man. For thus, a woman, having obtained them, is at that time endowed with those having female basis. And in the next birth, upon the transformation to male existence in the Desire Realm, that man is endowed with those having male basis. But a man obtains only those with male basis. Why? — he says: 'Because of obtaining the non-analytical cessation (<s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) of femininity.' In that birth, femininity — and even in the next birth — does not exist; this is the obtaining of its non-analytical cessation. For one who produces the supreme <s>dharma</s>s must necessarily produce the path of seeing immediately afterward. And the established doctrine is that for one who has seen the truths, femininity does not manifest again.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. yadbhūmikāni nirvedhabhāgīyāni pratilabdhāni prathamadhyānabhūmikāni yāvac caturthadhyānabhūmikāni. tāṃ bhūmiṃ tyajan prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ yavac caturthaṃ tyajann āryas tāny api yathāsvaṃ prathamadhyānadhūmikāni yāvac caturthadhyānabhūmikāni tyajati. nānyathā na mṛtyunā parihāṇyā vā. yathā pṛthagjana ity arthaḥ. bhūmityāgaḥ punar bhūmisaṃcārād iti. na vairāgyata iti darśayati. pṛthagjanas tv iti vistaraḥ. pṛthagjanas tu nikāyasabhāgatyāgenaiva tyajati nirvedhabhāgīyāni saty asati vā bhūmisaṃcāre. tathā hi pṛthagjano yadbhūmikanirvedhabhāgīyalābhī bhavati. tata ūrdhvam upapadyamānas tāni bhūmisaṃcāre 'pi mṛtyunaiva tyajati. avītarāgas tv asati bhūmi saṃcāre mṛtyunā tyajati. kāmadhātāv evopadyate. na tv evam
body.translated_text: — and so forth in detail. Whatever ground the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> [wholesome roots] obtained belong to — those belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, up to those belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground — when a Noble One relinquishes that ground — relinquishing the first <s>dhyāna</s>, up to the fourth — he also relinquishes those [<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s] accordingly — those belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, up to those belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground. Not otherwise — not through death or through decline — as an ordinary person does, is the meaning. 'The relinquishment of a ground, moreover, is through ground-transfer' — he shows: not through freedom from desire. 'But an ordinary person' — and so forth in detail. But an ordinary person relinquishes the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s through the relinquishment of the class of existence (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>) alone, whether or not there is ground-transfer. For indeed, an ordinary person who has obtained the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s belonging to a given ground — when being reborn above that, even with ground-transfer, he relinquishes them only through death. But one not free from desire, without ground-transfer, relinquishes through death — he is reborn in the Desire Realm itself. But not so

body.text: āryapudgalas tat kuśalamūlasaṃtater darśanamārgopabṛṃhitatvāt. pṛthagjana eva tathā tyajatīti kathaṃ gamyate. aṇḍakalalādigataḥ pṛthagjanaḥ kāyena samanvāgataḥ. na kāyakarmaṇeti śāstre vacanāt.
body.translated_text: a Noble person — because of the continuum of wholesome roots having been strengthened by the seeing-path. How is it understood that only an ordinary person relinquishes them thus? From the statement in the treatise: 'An ordinary person who has entered the egg, embryo, and the like is endowed with the body, not with bodily <s>karma</s>.'

body.text: ācaryavasumitras tu vyācaṣṭe. pṛthagjanas tu nikāyasabhāgatyāgenaiva tyajati. saty asati vā bhūmisaṃcāra iti. sakalaṃ dhyānam atra bhūmigrahaṇena [Tib. 199b] gṛhyate. tatra pṛthagjano yadā brāhmakāyikebhyaś cyutvā brahmapurohiteṣūpapadyate. tadā nikāyasabhāgatyāgena tyajati. yadā tu prathamāt dhyānāc cyutvā dvitīya upapadyate. tadā bhūmityāganikāyasabhāgatyāgābhyām iti. tad ayuktaṃ. brahmalokopapannānāṃ nirvedhabhāgīyābhāvāt. kāmadhātau hi nirvedhabhāgīyāny utpadyaṃte. kāmadhātucyavanād eva ca teṣāṃ nirvedhabhāgīyatyāga iti. ācāryasaṃghabhadreṇāpi darśitam etat. nanu ca pṛthagjano 'pi yadbhūmikanirvedhabhāgīyalābhī bhavati. tata ūrdhvam upapadyamāno nirvedhabhāgīyāni vijahyād iti. nāsty etat. nikāyasabhāgatyāgād eva tyaktatvāt. maraṇabhavāsthito hi tāni tyajati. aṃtarābhavasthitena tu tyaktāni. ata ūrdhvam upapadyamānasya tan masti yad vijahyād iti. mṛtyunaivety ucyata iti. prātimokṣasaṃvaravad iti. yathā prātimokṣasaṃvaras tyaktaḥ punar ādīyamāno 'pūrva eva labhyate. kasmāt. anucitayatnasādhyatvāt. anucitatvāt yatnasādhyatvāc ca. yasmād anādim atisaṃsāre nocitāni bhavaṃti. āryamārgaparivāratvāt. tasmān na vairāgyalabhyāni. yasmād yatnasādhyāni. tasmān na pūrvatyaktāni labhyaṃta iti. sati pratisīmādaiśika iti. sīmā nāma [Tib. 200a] maryādā. tasyā daiśiko deśayitā praṇidhijñānalābhī. tasmin sati labdhavihīnāt pareṇotpādayati. yad anutpāditaṃ. tad utpādayatīty arthaḥ. asati pratisīmadaiśike mūlād evoṣmagatāt prabhṛtīty arthaḥ. ete punar vihāniparihāṇī iti.
body.translated_text: But teacher <s>Vasumitra</s> explains: 'An ordinary person relinquishes through the relinquishment of the class of existence alone, whether or not there is ground-transfer.' The word 'ground' here includes the entire <s>dhyāna</s>. Therein, when an ordinary person, having fallen from the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> [gods], is reborn among the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> [gods], he relinquishes through relinquishment of the class of existence. But when, having fallen from the first <s>dhyāna</s>, he is reborn in the second, then through both ground-relinquishment and class-of-existence-relinquishment. That is incorrect — because of the absence of <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s for those reborn in the <s>Brahmaloka</s>. For the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s arise in the Desire Realm, and their relinquishment is only through falling from the Desire Realm. This was also shown by <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s>. 'But does not an ordinary person too, having obtained the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s belonging to a given ground, when being reborn above, relinquish the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s?' This is not so — because they are relinquished through relinquishment of the class of existence alone. For one situated in the dying existence relinquishes them; but one situated in the intermediate existence has already relinquished them. Therefore, for one being reborn above, there is nothing [left] that he would relinquish — thus it is said 'through death alone.' 'Like <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint' — just as <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint, having been relinquished and then taken up again, is obtained as something entirely new. Why? Because of being accomplishable through effort with what is unpracticed. Because they are unpracticed and because they are accomplishable through effort. Since in the beginningless, exceedingly long <s>saṃsāra</s>, they have not been practiced. Because of being an accompaniment of the noble path — therefore they are not obtainable through freedom from desire. And because of being accomplishable through effort — therefore those previously relinquished are not obtained again. 'When there is a boundary-teacher' — a boundary (<s>sīmā</s>) is a demarcation; the teacher of that is the one who instructs [where one left off], one who has obtained the knowledge of aspiration (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>). When such a one exists, he produces from another [person] what was lost from the obtained — meaning: he produces what was not yet produced [up to that point]. 'When there is no boundary-teacher, from the root, from the heat [stage] onward' — this is the meaning. These, moreover, are diminishment and decline.

body.text: ityādivacanād vihānir uktā.
body.translated_text: — from this and similar statements, diminishment (<s>vihāni</s>) is stated.

children.translated_text: 'And the first two [stages are lost] through decline'

body.text: vacanāt praihāṇir apy uktā. tenaite iti nirdiśati.
body.translated_text: — from this statement, decline (<s>parihāṇi</s>) too is stated. Therefore he indicates 'those.'

body.text: iti vihāniparihāṇyoḥ sāmānyarūpaparigrahād ubhayor grahaṇaṃ. parihāṇis tu doṣakṛtā. kleśakṛtety arthaḥ. nāvaśyaṃ vihānir iti. sā hi guṇakṛtāpi bhavati na kevalaṃ doṣakṛtā. guṇakṛtā tadyathā darśanamārgotpattau pṛthagjanatvasya
body.translated_text: — because of the inclusive form that is common to both diminishment and decline, both are included. But decline is caused by a defect — meaning: caused by an affliction. Diminishment is not necessarily [caused by a defect] — for that can also be caused by a quality, not only by a defect. Caused by a quality: for example, the diminishment of the state of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) at the arising of the seeing-path

body.text: vihāniḥ. doṣakṛtā tu tadyathā mithyādṛṣṭyā kuśalamūlavihāniḥ. pratisaṃdhicittena vā keṣāṃcid dharmāṇāṃ vihānir iti. tad evaṃ yā parihāṇiḥ. vihānir api sā. yā tu vihāniḥ. nāvaśyam asau parihāṇiḥ. guṇaviśeṣebhya eva hi parihāṇir iti.
body.translated_text: . Caused by a defect: for example, the diminishment of wholesome roots through wrong view. Or the diminishment of certain <s>dharma</s>s through the relinking consciousness (<s>pratisaṃdhicitta</s>). Thus, whatever is decline is also diminishment; but whatever is diminishment is not necessarily decline — for decline is only from special qualities.

body.text: (VI.24) anutpattidharmatāṃ pratilabhata iti. apratisaṃkhyānirodhaṃ teṣāṃ gatyādīnāṃ pratilabhata [Tib. 200b] ity arthaḥ. tāṃ tu yathāyogam iti. tāṃ tv anutpattidharmatāṃ. yathāsaṃbhavaṃ mṛdvyām adhimātrāyāṃ ca kṣāṃtau pratilabhata iti vartate. kathaṃ kṛtvā. mṛdvyāṃ kṣāṃtyām apāyagatīnām anutpattidharmatāṃ pratilabhate. adhimātrāyam aṇḍajasaṃsvedajayonyoḥ. mṛdvyām asaṃjñitvottarakurumahābrahmopapattīnāṃ. adhimātrāyāṃ ṣaṇḍhapaṇḍakobhayavyaṃjanāśrayāṇām. adhimātrāyām aṣṭamādibhavānāṃ. aṣṭamādinavamādibhavānāṃ. darśanaheyakleśānāṃ cānutpattidharmatām eveti.
body.translated_text: (VI.24) 'One obtains the state of non-arising (<s>anutpattidharmatā</s>)' — the meaning is: one obtains the non-analytical cessation (<s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) of those destinies and the rest. 'That, as applicable' — that state of non-arising; the text continues: one obtains it at the mild and intense patient acceptances (<s>kṣānti</s>), as applicable. How so? At the mild patient acceptance, one obtains the state of non-arising of the evil destinies (<s>apāyagati</s>). At the intense, of egg-born and moisture-born modes of birth. At the mild, of the states of non-perception (<s>asaṃjñitva</s>), <s>Uttarakuru</s> and <s>Mahābrahmā</s> rebirths. At the intense, of the supports characterized as eunuch, hermaphrodite, and androgyne. At the intense, of the eighth and subsequent existences — of the ninth and subsequent existences [respectively]. And of the afflictions to be abandoned by seeing — the state of non-arising exactly.

body.text: (VI.25) tasyaiva tu gotrasyeti. kṣāṃtiparibhāvitasya śrāvakagotrasyety ācāryamataṃ. tasya kṣāṃtiparibhāvitatvenāvivartyatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: (VI.25) 'Of that very lineage (<s>gotra</s>)' — the meaning is: of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> lineage that has been cultivated through patient acceptance — this is the <s>Ācārya</s>'s view. The intent is: because of its irreversibility through having been cultivated through patient acceptance.

body.text: iti. pratyekabuddhaḥ kṣāṃtim api śrāvakagotrād vivartya syāt. na hi te parārtham apāyān avagāhanta ity abhiprāyaḥ. āniṃjyapaṭusamādhitvād iti. aṣṭapakṣālmuktatvād āniṃjyaḥ samādhiḥ. ata eva paṭur uttaptatīkṣṇendriyatvād vā.
body.translated_text: — a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> might turn away even from the patient acceptance [stage], from the <s>Śrāvaka</s> lineage. For the intent is: they do not plunge into evil destinies for the sake of others. 'Because of having an immovable and acute concentration' — the concentration is immovable because of being free from the eight faults. Therefore it is acute — because of having blazing, sharp faculties.

body.text: yeṣāṃ tu khaḍgād anyo 'pīti. yeṣām ābhidhārmikāṇāṃ matena khaḍgād anyo 'pi pratyekabuddho 'sti. utpāditanirvedhabhāgīyamātro 'pi vargacārī pratyekabuddha ity abhiprāyaḥ. teṣām uṣmagatamūrdhabhyāṃ tadgotrāṇāṃ vyāvartanasyāpratiṣedhaḥ khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpasyaivāvadhāraṇāt. [Tib. 201a]
body.translated_text: But for those for whom there exists a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> other than the rhinoceros-horn [type] — for those <s>Ābhidhārmika</s>s in whose view there exists a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> other than the rhinoceros-horn type — the intent is: even one who has merely produced the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s, who practices in a group, is a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. For them, the non-prohibition of turning away from the heat and summit [stages] for those of that lineage — because the restriction applies only to one who is like a rhinoceros-horn.

body.text: iti. yaḥ kṣipraṃ mokṣaṃ prāpnoti. sa ekasmiṃ janmani mokṣabhāgīyam utpādayet. dvitīye nirvedhabhāgīyāni. tṛtīye āryamārga iti. yas tu pūrvasmin janmani saṃbhṛtamokṣabhāgīyo bhavati. sa ekasminn api janmani nirvedhabhāgīyāny āryamārgaṃ cotpādayatīty avagaṃtavyaṃ bījāvaropaṇetyādi bījāvaropaṇaṃ mokṣabhāgīyotpādanaṃ. sasyābhivṛddhir nirvedhabhāgīyotpattiḥ. phalotpattir āryamārgaḥ. asyāṃ dharmatāyām iti. pravacanadharmatāyām. avatāraparipākavimuktayo bhavaṃtīti. avatāro mokṣabhāgīyena. paripāko nirvedhabhāgīyaiḥ. vimuktir āryamārgeṇeti. tatpraṇidhānaparigrahaṇād iti.
body.translated_text: — one who attains liberation quickly: in one birth, one would produce the <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s> [wholesome roots]; in a second, the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s; in a third, the noble path. But one who has accumulated the <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s> in a previous birth — that one should be understood as producing both the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s and the noble path in a single birth. 'The planting of the seed' and so forth — the planting of the seed is the production of the <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>; the growth of the crop is the arising of the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s; the production of fruit is the noble path. 'In this nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>)' — in the nature of the teaching. 'There are entry, maturation, and liberation' — entry is through the <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>; maturation is through the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s; liberation is through the noble path. 'Because of the embrace of aspiration for that' —

body.text: manaḥpraṇidhānaparigrahāt. praṇidhānaṃ punaś cetanāviśeśaḥ. ekabhikṣām api dattveti kāyakarma. ekaśikṣām api cādāyeti vākkarma. tac ca manaskarmotthānam iti. trikarmasvabhāvam alpakam apy etat mokṣābhilāṣabalādhānān mokṣabhāgīyam ākṣipati. mokṣasya bhāgaḥ prāptir mokṣabhāgaḥ. [Tib. 201b] tasmai hitaṃ mokṣabhāgīyam iti. nānyatra prajñānirvedayor abhāvād yathāyogam iti. kuruṣu tāvad ubhayaṃ nāsti. apāyeṣu nirvedo 'sti prajñā nāsti. deveṣu prajñāsti nirvedo nāstīti. ato manuṣyeṣv eva triṣu dvīpeṣv ākṣipyate. nānyatra.
body.translated_text: because of the embrace of mental aspiration. Moreover, aspiration is a special form of volition (<s>cetanā</s>). 'Even by giving a single alms-meal' — this is bodily <s>karma</s>. 'And by undertaking a single precept' — this is vocal <s>karma</s>. And that is originated by mental <s>karma</s>. Even this small [act], of the nature of the three <s>karma</s>s, because of the power of aspiration for liberation, casts [one toward] the <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>. A portion (<s>bhāga</s>) of liberation is the attainment of liberation — hence <s>mokṣabhāga</s>. That which is conducive (<s>hita</s>) to that is <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>. 'Not elsewhere, because of the absence of wisdom and disenchantment as applicable' — in <s>Uttarakuru</s>, first, neither exists. In the evil destinies, disenchantment exists but not wisdom. Among the gods, wisdom exists but not disenchantment. Therefore, [the <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>] is cast only among humans in the three continents — not elsewhere.

children.translated_text: 'But the order of the decisive penetration (<s>abhisamaya</s>) has been begun to be stated' —
'One established in conduct, possessing learning and reflection, engages in cultivation'

body.text: ity ārabhya nirvedhabhāgīyānukramaḥ. tatprasaṃgena mokṣabhāgīyopanyāsa iti.
body.translated_text: — beginning from this, the sequence of the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s [is stated]. The presentation of the <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s> is in connection with that.

body.text: nirvedhabhāgīyair api dharmakṣamaṇam. ato niṣyandena viśeṣaṇaṃ. yasyā dharmajñānaṃ niṣyaṃdaḥ. sā dharmajñānakṣāṃtiḥ. dharmajñānārthaṃ kṣāṃtir dharmajñānakṣāṃtiḥ. puṣpaphalavṛkṣavad yathā puṣpārthaṃ vṛkṣaḥ puṣpavṛkṣaḥ. phalārthaṃ vṛkṣaḥ phalavṛkṣaḥ. kārikāyāṃ tu dharmakṣāṃtir iti vacanam ekadeśagrahaṇato devadatto datta iti yathā. samyaktvaṃ nirvāṇam ity uktam iti. samyaktavaṃ katamat. yat tat paryādāya rāgaprahāṇam iti vistaraḥ. tatra niyamo niyāma iti. tatra samyaktve niyama ekāṃtībhāvo niyāma iti ghañi rūpaṃ. api tu niyama iti yamaḥ samupaniviṣu cety appratyayasya vibhāṣitatvāt. tasyāhigamanam avakramaṇam iti. [Tib. 202a] tasyaikāṃtībhāvasyābhigamanaṃ prāptiḥ. tad eva viparyāsasyāpakramān niyāmāvakrāṃtir ity ucyate. tasyāṃ ceti dharmajñānakṣāṃtau. pradīpajātivad iti. pradīpasyeva jāter iva cety arthaḥ. yathā pradīpasyānāgatasya tamovināśane sāmarthyaṃ. jāteś cānāgatāyā janyajanane. tathā pṛthagjanatvavyāvartane sāmarthyam anāgatāyā dharmajñānakṣāṃter abhyupagamyate. nānyad iti. kleśaprahāṇāṃ kāritraṃ. laukikair agradharmair iti apara iti. pṛthagjanatvaṃ vyāvartata iti prakṛtaṃ. na. taddharmatvād iti. na yuktam etal laukikair agradharmais tadvyāvartana iti. kasmāt. te 'pi hi pṛthagjanadharmāḥ. kathaṃ pṛthagjanadharmasya pṛthagjanadharmaṃ vyāvartiṣyaṃta iti. tadvirodhitvād adoṣaḥ. agradharmāṇāṃ pṛthagjanantvavirodhitvāt adoṣa eṣaḥ. kiṃ.
body.translated_text: Even by the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>s there is patient acceptance of dharmas. Therefore, the qualification is by way of outflow: that whose outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>) is <s>dharmajñāna</s> — that is <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of dharma-knowledge). Or: the patient acceptance for the purpose of dharma-knowledge is <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s>. Like a flower-tree and fruit-tree: just as the tree for the purpose of flowers is the flower-tree; the tree for the purpose of fruit is the fruit-tree. But in the verse, the expression '<s>dharmakṣānti</s>' is from partial mention — like '<s>Datta</s>' for '<s>Devadatta</s>.' 'The right course (<s>samyaktva</s>) is <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — it was stated. What is the right course? 'That which is the complete abandonment of desire' — and so forth in detail. 'Therein, the determination (<s>niyama</s>) is the determined course (<s>niyāma</s>)' — therein, in the right course, the determination — the state of being definitive — is the determined course. This is the <s>ghañ</s>-suffix form. Moreover, '<s>niyama</s>' — '<s>yama</s>' with '<s>sam</s> and <s>upani</s> and <s>vi</s>,' the <s>ap</s>-suffix being optional. The approach to that — the attainment — is its entrance (<s>avakramaṇa</s>). That itself, from the departure of distortion (<s>viparyāsa</s>), is called 'entrance into the determined course' (<s>niyāmāvakrānti</s>). 'And in that' — in that <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s>. 'Like the arising of a lamp' — the meaning is: like a lamp, like an arising. Just as the future lamp has the capacity to destroy darkness, and just as future arising [has the capacity] for the production of what is to be produced — so the capacity for the removal of the state of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjanatvavyāvartana</s>) is acknowledged for the future <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s>. 'Not anything else' — [has] the function of abandoning afflictions. 'By the mundane supreme dharmas (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>)' — says another. The topic is: [whether] the state of being an ordinary person is removed [by them]. No — 'because of being of the nature of that' — it is not fitting that the state of being an ordinary person is removed by mundane supreme dharmas. Why? Because those too are dharmas of an ordinary person. How would a dharma of an ordinary person remove a dharma of an ordinary person? 'No fault, because of being opposed to it' — because of the mundane supreme dharmas being opposed to the state of being an ordinary person, this is no fault. What [further objection is there]?

body.text: yathety āha. śatruskandhārūḍhatadghātanavad iti. yathā śatruskandhārūḍha eva kaścic chatruṃ ghātayet. evaṃ kilāgradharmāḥ pṛthagjanatvaśatruskandhārūḍhās tad eva pṛthagjanatvaṃ ghātayeyur iti.
body.translated_text: He says: 'like killing an enemy while mounted on the enemy's shoulders.' Just as someone, while mounted on the very shoulders of an enemy, might kill that enemy — so indeed the supreme dharmas, while mounted on the shoulders of the enemy that is the state of being an ordinary person, might destroy that very state of being an ordinary person.

body.text: ubhayair iti. laukikair agradharmaiḥ [Tib. 202b] kṣāṃtyā ca pṛthagjanatvaṃ vyāvartyate. katham ity āha. ānaṃtaryavimuktimārgasādharmyād iti. laukikānām agradharmāṇām ānaṃtaryamārgeṇa sādharmyaṃ. kṣāṃter vimuktimārgeṇa. yathā hy ānaṃtaryamārgeṇa kleśaḥ prahīyate. vimuktimārgeṇa prahīṇaḥ evaṃ laukikair agradharmaiḥ pṛthagjanatvaṃ vihīyate. kṣāṃtyā vihīnam iti.
body.translated_text: 'By both' — the state of being an ordinary person is removed by the mundane supreme dharmas and by the patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>). How? He says: 'by analogy with the uninterrupted path and the liberation path.' The mundane supreme dharmas have an analogy with the uninterrupted path; the patient acceptance with the liberation path. Just as by the uninterrupted path an affliction is abandoned, and by the liberation path it is [confirmed as] abandoned — so by the mundane supreme dharmas the state of being an ordinary person is diminished, and by the patient acceptance it is [confirmed as] diminished.

body.text: anāsravādhikāraḥ sarvatreti. tena tato 'traiva dharmajñānam anāsravam iti gamyate. tad duḥkhe dharmajñānam ity ucyate iti. śāstre tena nāmnā vyavahāra it darśayati. samastālaṃbanā rūpārūpyāvacaraduḥkhālaṃbanatvāt. prathamato dharmatattvajñānād iti. ādito duḥkhādidharmatattvajñānād ity arthaḥ. tadanvayatvād iti. taddhetukatvād ity arthaḥ. tathaivānugamād iti. yathaiva dharmajñānenānugataṃ parijñātaṃ duḥkhādisatyaṃ duḥkhādibhir ākāraiḥ. tathaiva rūpārūpyāvacaraduḥkhādyanugamād anvayajñānam etad iti vistaraḥ. evaṃ samanaṃtarotpattikrameṇa śeṣe samudaye rūpārūpyāvacare 'nvayajñānakṣāṃtir [Tib. 203a] iti vistareṇa yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'The topic of the uncontaminated [applies] everywhere' — from this, it is understood that here indeed the <s>dharmajñāna</s> is uncontaminated. That is called 'the <s>dharmajñāna</s> of suffering.' He shows that in the treatise, the usage is by that name. 'Having a complete object' — because of having the suffering of the Form and Formless Realms as object. 'From the first knowledge of the true nature of <s>dharma</s>s' — the meaning is: from the first knowledge of the true nature of <s>dharma</s>s such as suffering and the rest. 'Because of being its continuation (<s>anvaya</s>)' — the meaning is: because of being caused by it. 'Because of following in exactly that way' — just as the truth of suffering and the rest was followed — comprehended — by the <s>dharmajñāna</s> through the aspects of suffering and the rest, in exactly that way, because of following the suffering and the rest of the Form and Formless Realms, this is the subsequent knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>) — and so forth in detail. 'Thus, in the order of immediately-successive arising, for the remaining origination belonging to the Form and Formless Realms, the subsequent-knowledge tolerance (<s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s>)' — and so forth — should be connected in detail.

body.text: nikāyāṃtarīyā āryadharmaguptaprabhṛtayaḥ. abhedena hy abhisamaya ucyata iti. ṣoḍaśa citto 'yaṃ satyābhisamaya iti. darśanābhisamaya ālaṃbanābhisamayaḥ kāryābhisamayaś caivaṃ ṣoḍaśacittaka ity abhedaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Those of other schools (<s>nikāyāntarīya</s>)' — such as the noble <s>Dharmaguptaka</s>s and others. 'For the realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) is said to be without distinction' — 'This realization of the truths consists of sixteen mind-moments' — the realization of seeing (<s>darśanābhisamaya</s>), the realization of the object (<s>ālaṃbanābhisamaya</s>), and the realization of function (<s>kāryābhisamaya</s>) — thus consisting of sixteen mind-moments without distinction.

body.text: darśanābhisamaya iti. darśanam evābhisamayaḥ. evam ālaṃbanābhisamayaḥ kāryābhisamayaś ca. darśanābhisamayo 'nāsravayā prajñayā. tad dhi bhikṣavo dṛṣṭaṃ. yad anāsravayā prajñayā dṛṣṭam iti vacanāt. prajñaiva darśanam iti vyavasthāpyate. ālaṃbanaṃ grahaṇaṃ tatsaṃprayuktair api vedanādibhir bhavati. apiśabdāt prajñayāpi. yasmāc cittacaittaiḥ satyāny ālaṃbyaṃte. kāryaṃ yasya satyasya yat kartavyaṃ. tadyathā duḥkhasya parijñānaṃ. samudayasya prahāṇaṃ. nirodhasya sākṣātkaraṇaṃ. mārgasya bhāvanaṃ. tad viprayuktair api śīlajātyādibhir bhavati. apiśabdāt prajñātatsaṃprayuktair api. prajñāsaṃprayuktaviprayuktair hi tatkāryacatuṣṭayaṃ [Tib. 203b] kriyate. jātyādibhir ity ādiśabdāl lakṣaṇāṃtarāṇi prāptayaś ca gṛhyaṃte. duḥkhe hīti vistaraḥ. duḥkhe hi dṛśyamāne prajñayā. tasyābhisamayitur duḥkhasya vā trividho
body.translated_text: 'The realization of seeing' — seeing itself is the realization. Similarly, the realization of the object and the realization of function. The realization of seeing [occurs] through uncontaminated wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). Because of the statement: 'That, O monks, is [truly] seen which is seen through uncontaminated wisdom' — it is established that seeing is wisdom itself. Object-apprehension (<s>ālaṃbana</s>) — grasping — also occurs through [mental factors] such as feeling and the rest that are associated with it [wisdom]. From the word 'also,' by wisdom too. Because the truths are apprehended by mind and mental factors. Function (<s>kārya</s>) — whatever function is to be performed for each truth: namely, the full comprehension (<s>parijñāna</s>) of suffering, the abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>) of origination, the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkaraṇa</s>) of cessation, and the cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of the path. That [function] also occurs through [factors] dissociated [from thought] such as morality, birth, and the rest. From the word 'also,' by wisdom and those associated with it too. For the fourfold function is performed by [factors both] associated with and dissociated from wisdom. 'By birth and the rest' — from the word 'and the rest,' other conditioned characteristics and acquisitions are included. 'For when suffering [is being seen]' — and so forth in detail. For when suffering is being seen by wisdom, of that realization-subject or of suffering, the threefold

nirodhasya tatprāptyutpādāt. bhāvanaṃ mārgasya saṃmukhībhāvāt. ākārabhedād iti. pratyekam eṣāṃ duḥkhādīnām ākārabhedāt. na ca duḥkhākāreṇa samudayādīnāṃ darśanaṃ yujyate. tadākārārthabhedataḥ. athāpy anātmākāreṇa sarveṣāṃ satyānāṃ darśanam iti brūyāt nikāyāṃtarīyaḥ. śūnyatānātmate sarvasatyānāṃ sāmānyaṃ lakṣaṇam iti kṛtvā. na tarhi satyānāṃ duḥkhādito darśanaṃ syāt. duḥkhataḥ samudayato nirodhato prayogāvasthāyām [Tib. 204a] āryaśrāvakasya duḥkhaṃ vā duḥkhato manasikurvata ity evamādi. ato 'nātmākāreṇa sarveṣāṃ darśanād ekābhisamaya eveti. tac cāyuktam. anāsraveṇa manasikāreṇa saṃprayukto samudayādidarśanasaṃmukhībhāvaśaktilābho vaśitvalābhaḥ. tasmād iti. aṃtarā tu vyutthānām asti nāstīti vicāryaṃ syād iti. śeṣeṣu vaśitvalābhād aṃtarā vyutthānaṃ prāpnotīti doṣaḥ syād ity abhiprāyaḥ. ubhayathāpi ca vicāryamāṇe bahūnāṃ sūtrāṇāṃ virodhaḥ. yathā ca teṣāṃ virodhaḥ. tathāgameṣu śrotavyaḥ. ekasya darśane śeṣāṇāṃ kāryābhisamayavacanād iti. yasmād asty etat vacanaṃ. duḥkhe hi dṛśyamāne
