sūtre satyānāṃ krameṇābhisamayo virudhyate. ata ucyate. darśanābhiśamayaṃ tu pratīti vistaraḥ. sadṛṣṭāṃtāni trīṇi sūtrāṇīti. saṃyuktāgame paṭhyaṃte. kathaṃ. anāthapiṇḍada āha. kiṃ nu bhadaṃta caturṇām āryasatyānām anupūrvābhisamayaḥ. āhosvid ekābhisamaya iti. caturṇāṃ gṛhapate āryasatyānām anupūrvābhisamayo na tv ekābhisamayaḥ. yo gṛhapate evaṃ vaded ahaṃ
body.translated_text: realization is as stated. How? — he says. 'The realization of origination and the rest' — of origination, cessation, and the path — 'through abandonment, direct realization, and cultivation respectively.' Abandonment of origination — through the cutting of the acquisition of afflictions. Direct realization of cessation — through the arising of the acquisition of that [cessation]. Cultivation of the path — through its coming face-to-face. 'Because of the difference of aspects' — because of the difference of aspects of each of these — suffering and the rest. And seeing origination and the rest through the aspect of suffering is not fitting — because of the difference of the meanings of those aspects. Even if someone of another school were to say: 'Through the aspect of non-self, there is the seeing of all truths' — thinking: emptiness and non-self are the common characteristic of all truths — then, the seeing of the truths would not be [in the order] from suffering onwards — [i.e.,] from suffering, from origination, from cessation, from the path. And this being the case, in saying 'through the aspect of non-self, there is the seeing of all,' there would be contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s>. For in the <s>sūtra</s> it is stated thus: 'Of the noble disciple' — and so forth in detail. Now, if you think: 'There is no contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s>, because prior to the stage of realization, in the stage of preliminary practice, the noble disciple mentally attends to suffering as suffering' and so forth — therefore 'through the aspect of non-self, there is the seeing of all, hence a single realization.' That too is not proper. Because of the statement: 'The investigation of <s>dharma</s>s associated with uncontaminated mental attention.' For in the stage of preliminary practice, uncontaminated mental attention is not possible. 'If [you say it is] in the path of cultivation' — 'of the noble disciple who mentally attends to suffering as suffering' — and so forth in detail. No — just as [there is] seeing, [there is also] cultivation. This is not so. For just as the seeing of the truths [occurred] previously, so too their cultivation afterward — the meaning is: it becomes the path of cultivation. 'Because of obtaining mastery over the rest' — 'obtaining mastery' means the obtaining of the ability to come face-to-face with the seeing of origination and the rest without [further] preliminary practice. 'Therefore' — the intent is: because of obtaining mastery over the rest, one would achieve emergence in between [truths] — that would be a fault. 'And when examined in both ways, there is contradiction with many <s>sūtra</s>s.' And the way in which they contradict — this should be heard in the <s>Āgama</s>s. 'Because of the statement of the functional realization of the rest when one is being seen' — because there exists this statement: 'For when suffering is being seen, there is a threefold realization of it; and of origination and the rest, a functional realization through abandonment, direct realization, and cultivation' — therefore, since we too accept this, there is no fault. He says: 'Even though the realization is accepted' — even though the [threefold] realization is accepted. 'In the <s>sūtra</s>, the sequential realization of the truths is contradicted.' Therefore it is said: 'But regarding the realization of seeing' — and so forth in detail. '[There are] three <s>sūtra</s>s with illustrations.' These are read in the <s>Saṃyuktāgama</s>. How? '<s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said: "Is there, Venerable Sir, a sequential realization of the four noble truths, or a single realization?" "Of the four noble truths, O householder, there is a sequential realization, not a single realization. O householder, whoever were to say: 'I

[Tib. 205a] talakam apratiṣṭhāpya cchadanaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmīti. maivaṃ voca iti syād vacanīyaḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ. asthānam anavakāśo yat kūṭāgārasyeti pūrvavat. yāvat sthānam etad vidyate. yan mūlapādaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya bhittiṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmīti pūrvavat. yāvad evam eva gṛhapate nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate. yad duḥkhasatyam adṛṣṭvā samudayasatyaṃ drakṣyatīti vistaraḥ. athānyataro bhikṣur āha. kiṃ nu bhadaṃta caturṇām āryasatyānām anupūrvābhisamayaḥ. āhosvid ekābhisamaya iti. bhagavān āha. caturṇāṃ bhikṣo satyānām iti. pūrvavad yāvat tadyathā bhikṣo ya evaṃ vaded ahaṃ catuṣkaḍevarasya sopānasya prathamasopānakaḍevaram anabhiruhya dvitīyam abhirokṣyāmīti. dvitīyam anabhiruhya tṛtīyaṃ. tṛtīyam anabhiruhya caturtham abhirokṣyāmīti. maivaṃ voca iti
syād vacanīyaḥ. tat kasya hetoḥ. asthānam anavakāśo yac catuṣkaḍevarasya sopānasya prathamasopānakaḍevaram anabhiruhya dvitīyakaḍevaram abhirokṣyati. evaṃ yāvat tṛtīyam anabhiruhya caturtham abhirokṣyati. evam ihāpi nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate. yad duḥkhasatyam adṛṣṭvā samudayasatyaṃ drakṣyatītyādi. [Tib. 205b] tathāryānanda āha. kiṃ nu bhadaṃta caturṇām āryasatyānām anupūrvābhisamayaḥ. utāho ekābhisamaya iti. pūrvasūtravat. yāvat. tadyathānanda ya evaṃ vaded ahaṃ catuṣpadikāyā niḥśreṇyāḥ prathamaṃ niḥśreṇīpadam anabhiruhya prāsādam abhirokṣyāmīti. maivaṃ voca iti syād vacanīyaḥ. vistareṇa yāvad evam evānanda ya evaṃ vaded ahaṃ duḥkham āryasatyam anabhisametya samudayasatyam abhisameṣyāmīti vistareṇa yāvan nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyata iti. etāni trīṇi sūtrāṇi. yo duḥkha iti vistaraḥ. atha mataṃ syād yo duḥke niṣkāṃkṣo nirvicikitso buddhe 'pi sa iti sūtrād ekābhisamaya iti. katham. aśaikṣā hi dharmā buddhaḥ. ta evāśaikṣā dharmā mārgaḥ. tasmād duḥkhābhisamayān mārgo 'pi tenābhisamito yasmād duḥkhavad buddhe 'pi niṣkāṃkṣo nirvicikitsa iti. kāṃkṣā vicikitsety anarthāṃtaraḥ. atha vāniścayābhilāṣaḥ kāṃkṣā vimatir vicikitsā
body.translated_text: shall realize the noble truth of origination without having realized the noble truth of suffering' — and so forth in detail, up to: 'I shall realize the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering' — one should say to him: 'Do not speak thus.' For what reason? It is impossible and inconceivable that one would realize the noble truth of origination without having realized the noble truth of suffering — as before, up to: 'this situation does not exist.' 'This situation exists' — as before. Just as, O householder, whoever were to say: 'I shall erect the walls of a tower or a tower-hall without having established the foundation. I shall erect the platform without having erected the walls. I shall erect the roof without having erected the platform' — one should say to him: 'Do not speak thus.' For what reason? It is impossible and inconceivable that one would [erect a] tower — as before, up to: 'this situation exists — that having established the foundation, one will erect the walls' — as before, up to: 'in exactly the same way, O householder, this situation does not exist — that without having seen the truth of suffering, one will see the truth of origination' — and so forth in detail. Then another monk said: 'Is there, Venerable Sir, a sequential realization of the four noble truths, or a single realization?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Of the four truths, O monk' — as before, up to: 'Just as, O monk, whoever were to say: "I shall ascend to the second landing of a four-landing staircase without having ascended the first landing. Without having ascended the second, the third. Without having ascended the third, I shall ascend the fourth" — one should say to him: "Do not speak thus." For what reason? It is impossible and inconceivable that one would ascend the second landing of a four-landing staircase without having ascended the first landing. Similarly, up to: without having ascended the third, one will ascend the fourth. Even so here, this situation does not exist — that without having seen the truth of suffering, one will see the truth of origination' — and so forth. Then the noble <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'Is there, Venerable Sir, a sequential realization of the four noble truths, or a single realization?' As in the previous <s>sūtra</s>, up to: 'Just as, O <s>Ānanda</s>, whoever were to say: "I shall ascend to the upper story without having ascended the first rung of a four-rung ladder" — one should say to him: "Do not speak thus." In detail, up to: "Even so, O <s>Ānanda</s>, whoever were to say: 'I shall realize the truth of origination without having realized the noble truth of suffering' — in detail, up to: 'this situation does not exist.'" These are the three <s>sūtra</s>s. 'Whoever [is free from] doubt regarding suffering' — and so forth in detail. Now, if one were to think: 'From the <s>sūtra</s> — "whoever is free from doubt and free from uncertainty regarding suffering is also [free from doubt] regarding the <s>Buddha</s>" — [there is] a single realization.' How? For the <s>aśaikṣa</s> (learnerless) <s>dharma</s>s are the <s>Buddha</s>. And those very <s>aśaikṣa</s> <s>dharma</s>s are the path. Therefore, from the realization of suffering, the path too is realized by him — because, just as with suffering, he is also free from doubt and free from uncertainty regarding the <s>Buddha</s>. 'Doubt' and 'uncertainty' (<s>kāṃkṣā</s>, <s>vicikitsā</s>) are synonymous. Or, 'doubt' (<s>kāṃkṣā</s>) is indecisiveness, desire [for certainty]; 'uncertainty' (<s>vicikitsā</s>) is perplexity

body.text: yathoktalakṣaṇā. nāsamudācārāvaśyaṃprahāṇābhisaṃdhivacanād iti. naitad evaṃ sūtrād ekābhisamaya iti. asamudācārasya [Tib. 206a] vaśyaṃprahāṇasya cābhisaṃdhivacanāt. duḥkhe 'bhisamite buddhaviṣaye vicikitsāyā asamudācāro 'vaśyaṃprahāṇaṃ ca bhavati. ato yo duḥkhe niṣkāṃkṣo nirvicikitso buddhe 'pi. sa ity uktam abhisaṃdhiḥ.
body.translated_text: — as defined. 'Because of the statement with the intention of non-occurrence and necessary abandonment' — this is not so — that from the <s>sūtra</s> there is a single realization. Because of the statement with the intention of non-occurrence and necessary abandonment. When suffering has been realized, in the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>, there is non-occurrence and necessary abandonment of doubt. Therefore it was said with this intention: 'Whoever is free from doubt regarding suffering is also [free from doubt] regarding the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: (VI.30cd) anaṃtaryaśakyatvād iti. kṛtyāś ca śaki liṅ ceti śakyārthe kṛtyapratyayaḥ aṃtarayituṃ śakyā aṃtaryāḥ. nāṃtaryāḥ anaṃtaryāḥ. kleśaprāptiṃ te vicchindaṃti. viprakṛtāvasthā sā teṣām iṣyate. ānaṃtaryamārgeṇeti bhāve svarthe vṛddhividhānaṃ. anantarabhāvo anaṃtaramārgo vā ānaṃtaryaṃ. tasya mārgā ānaṃtaryamārgāḥ. vimuktimārgāḥ. vimuktimārgā iti. vimuktau mārgā vimuktimārgāḥ. kleśavimuktyavasthāmārgā ity arthaḥ. dvābhyāṃ cauraniṣkāsanakapāṭapidhānavad iti. yathā dvābhyām ekena cauro niṣkāsyate. dvitīyena tadapraveśāya kapāṭaḥ pidhīyate. evam ānaṃtaryamārgeṇa kleśacauro niṣkāsyate. tatprāpticchedataḥ. vimukitmārgeṇa ca visaṃyogaprāptikapāṭaṃ pidhīyate. vartamānīkaraṇataḥ. yadi punar iti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 206b] yadi punar dvitīyenānaṃtaryamārgeṇaiva duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāṃtyā saha visaṃyogaprāptir utpadyeta. naiva duḥkhe dharmajñānam utpadyate. yad anena kartavyaṃ. tad duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāṃtyaiva kriyetety abhiprāyaḥ. prahīṇavicikitsaṃ jñānaṃ tatraivālaṃbane kāmāvacaraduḥkhe prahīṇavicikitsaṃ jñānaṃ notpannaṃ syāt. tatra hi duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāṃtiḥ savicikitsaiva vartate vicikitsāyā aprahīṇatvāt. na ca tatra duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāṃtiḥ prahīṇavicikitseti śakyate vyavasthāpayituṃ. atadviṣayatvāt.
body.translated_text: (VI.30cd) 'Because of being impossible to obstruct (<s>anantarya</s>)' — the <s>kṛtya</s> suffix in the sense of 'capable' [is formed by the rule] '<s>kṛtyāś ca śaki liṅ ca</s>' — capable of being obstructed is <s>antarya</s>; not <s>antarya</s> is <s>anantarya</s> (uninterruptible). They cut off the acquisition of afflictions. That state is their accepted condition. 'By the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>)' — the <s>vṛddhi</s>-augment in the locative sense of own-nature. The state of being uninterrupted (<s>anantara</s>), or the uninterrupted path, is <s>ānantarya</s>; the paths of that are the <s>ānantaryamārga</s>s. 'Liberation paths (<s>vimuktimārga</s>)' — paths in liberation are liberation paths. The meaning is: paths in the state of liberation from afflictions. 'By both, like the expelling of a thief and the closing of a door' — just as by two [agents], one expels the thief and the second closes the door to prevent his re-entry; so too, by the uninterrupted path, the thief of affliction is expelled — through the cutting of its acquisition; and by the liberation path, the door of the acquisition of disconnection (<s>visaṃyogaprāpti</s>) is closed — through its being made present. 'But if' — and so forth in detail. But if, by the second uninterrupted path — the <s>duḥkhānvayajñānakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the subsequent knowledge of suffering) — together with it, the acquisition of disconnection were to arise, then the <s>duḥkhadharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of the truth of suffering) would not arise at all. The intent is: what was to be done by it would be done by the <s>duḥkhānvayajñānakṣānti</s> alone. 'A knowledge free from doubt would [not arise] regarding that very object' — a knowledge free from doubt regarding that very Desire-Realm suffering object would not have arisen. For therein, in suffering, the <s>duḥkhadharmajñānakṣānti</s> operates still with doubt — because doubt has not been abandoned. And the <s>duḥkhānvayajñānakṣānti</s> cannot be established as free from doubt regarding that suffering — because of not having that as its domain.

body.text: kṣāṃtibhir iti vistaraḥ. kṣāṃtibhiḥ kleśaprahāṇād yo 'yaṃ sāstrapāṭhaḥ. navasaṃyojananikāyāḥ. duḥkhadharmajñānaprahātavyaḥ saṃyojananikāyaḥ. samudayadharmajñānaprahatavyo nirodhadharmajñānaprahātavyo mārgadharmajñānaprahātavyaḥ duḥkhānvayajñānaprahātavyaḥ samudayānvayajñānaprahātavyo nirodhānvayajñānaprahātavyo mārgānvayajñānaprahātavyo bhāvanāprahātavyaś ca saṃyojananikāya iti. sūtre 'py uktam. iti hi bhikṣavo jñānavadhyāḥ kleśāḥ. vidyudupamaṃ cittam iti. tasya virodhaḥ. na hi tatra
body.translated_text: 'By the patiences' — and so forth in detail. 'By patiences, through the abandonment of afflictions' — this is the reading of the treatise. Nine classes of fetters: the class of fetters to be abandoned by <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering, the class to be abandoned by <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of origination, the class to be abandoned by <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of cessation, the class to be abandoned by <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of the path, the class to be abandoned by subsequent knowledge of suffering, the class to be abandoned by subsequent knowledge of origination, the class to be abandoned by subsequent knowledge of cessation, the class to be abandoned by subsequent knowledge of the path, and the class of fetters to be abandoned by cultivation. In the <s>sūtra</s> too it is stated: 'Thus indeed, O monks, afflictions are to be killed by knowledge. Mind is like lightning.' The contradiction with that [arises]: for therein

body.text: kṣāṃtiprahātavyaḥ saṃyojananikāya ity uktaṃ. na kṣāṃtīnām iti [Tib. 207a] vistaraḥ. naitad evaṃ. kasmāt. kṣāṃtīnāṃ jñānaparivāratvāt. kṣāṃtayo jñānasya parivārā ity ataḥ kṣāṃtiprahātavyaḥ saṃyojananikāyo jñānaprahātavya ucyate. rājaparivārakṛtasya rājakṛtavyapadeśavat. yathā rājaparivārakṛtasya kasyacid arthasya rājakṛta iti vyapadeśo bhavati. tadvad bhāvanāprahātavyas tu saṃyojananikāyo jñānaprahātavya eva. tatra ānaṃtaryamārgo 'pi jñānasvabhāva iti. kleśaprahāṇe hy ānaṃtaryamārga eva viśeṣeṇādhikriyate.
body.translated_text: it is not stated that there is a class of fetters to be abandoned by patience. 'Not of the patiences' — [Tib. 207a] and so forth in detail. This is not so. Why? Because the patiences have knowledge as their retinue. Since the patiences are the retinue of knowledge — therefore the class of fetters to be abandoned by patience is called 'to be abandoned by knowledge.' Just as what is done by the king's retinue is designated as done by the king — just as a designation 'done by the king' is given to something done by the king's retinue — in the same way. But the class of fetters to be abandoned by cultivation is indeed 'to be abandoned by knowledge.' For therein, the uninterrupted path too has the nature of knowledge. For in the abandonment of afflictions, it is the uninterrupted path alone that is principally employed.

body.text: (VI.31ab) adṛṣṭasatyadarśanād iti jñānena katham adṛṣṭasatyadarśanaṃ bhavati. tad apy adṛṣṭe satyāṃtare sati bhavatīti darśanamārgāṃtarālavartijñānaṃ darśanamārgaḥ pāraṃparyam abhisaṃdhāya. tenāpy adṛṣṭam iva paśyatīti. atha vā adṛṣṭadṛṣṭer aḍṛṣṭadarśanāt. paṃcadaśakṣaṇā darśanamārgo yāvad asya pudgalasyādṛṣṭadarśanaṃ pravartate. tāvad asya kṣaṇā darśanamārgaḥ. tasya dṛṣṭe 'pi duḥkhe adṛṣṭadarśanam asya samudaye pravartata evety āha. bhāvanāmārga eva ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇa iti vākyādhyāhāraḥ.
body.translated_text: (VI.31ab) 'Because of seeing an unseen truth' — how is the seeing of an unseen truth possible through knowledge? That too occurs when there is another unseen truth remaining — the knowledge occurring in the interval of the path of seeing is [called] the path of seeing with reference to the series (<s>pāraṃparya</s>). Because by that [knowledge] too, one sees as if unseen. Or alternatively: 'because of the seeing of the unseen by the unseen seer' (<s>adṛṣṭadṛṣṭi</s>). The fifteen moments are the path of seeing, as long as the seeing of the unseen continues for this person — those moments of his are the path of seeing. Even though suffering has been seen by him, the unseen seeing of origination continues for him — this is stated. 'The sixteenth moment is the path of cultivation alone' — this is the supplement to the sentence.

body.text: nanu ca tenāpy adṛṣṭaṃ paśyati kiṃ tad adṛṣṭam ity āha. mārgānvayajñānakṣāṃtim iti. mārgānvayajñānakṣāṃtir ātmānaṃ virahayya śeṣam anvayajñānapakṣyaṃ mārgam ālaṃbate. svātmani [Tib.207b] vṛttivirodhāt. tenocyate. mārgānvayajñānakṣāṃtim adṛṣṭāṃ paśyatīti. satyaṃ prati ciṃteti vistaraḥ. satyaṃ prati cintā dṛṣṭaṃ na dṛṣṭam iti. na tu kṣaṇaṃ prati dṛṣṭaḥ kṣaṇo na veti. kasmāt. paṃcadaśena kṣaṇena yad anvayajñānapakṣalakṣaṇaṃ satyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ. tad eva ṣoḍaśenāpīti. nāsty apūrvadṛṣṭasatyadarśanam iti. na ṣoḍaśakṣaṇo darśanamārga iti vyavasthāpyate. na hy ekakṣaṇenādṛṣṭena mārgānvayajñānakṣāṃtilakṣaṇena satyaṃ tanmārgasatyam aḍṛṣṭaṃ bhavati. laukikaṃ dṛṣṭāṃtam āha. yathā naikaluṅgena ekasasyaśalākayā dātreṇālūnenācchinnena kedāram alūnaṃ bhavati. kiṃ tarhi. lūnam evety arthaḥ. tathā hi kecit pramādād alūne 'pi ekaluṃge vaktāro bhavaṃti lūnam asmābhiḥ kedāram iti. phalatvād iti vistaraḥ. phalatvād ityadihetubhir bhāvanāmārgam eva ṣoḍaśakṣaṇaṃ sādhayati. bhāvanāmārgaḥ ṣoḍaśaḥ kṣaṇaḥ. saṃskṛtaśrāmaṇyaphalatvāt. sakṛdāgāmiphalavat yāvad arhattvaphalavad vā. tathā bhāvitāṣṭajñānaṣoḍasākāratvād vihīnapratipannakamārgatvāt prābaṃdhikatvāc ca. [Tib. 208a] phalāṃtaravad eva bhāvanāmārgaḥ. ṣoḍaśe hi kṣaṇe 'ṣṭau jñānāni bhāvyaṃte. duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ duḥkhe 'nvayajñānaṃ yāvan
body.translated_text: But if by that [sixteenth moment] too one sees the unseen, what is that unseen? He says: 'The <s>mārgānvayajñānakṣānti</s>' — the <s>mārgānvayajñānakṣānti</s> (patience of subsequent knowledge of the path), excluding itself, takes as object the remaining path belonging to the subsequent knowledge class. [Tib. 207b] Because of the impossibility of operation upon itself. Therefore it is said: 'one sees the <s>mārgānvayajñānakṣānti</s> which was unseen.' 'Thinking with respect to the truth' — and so forth in detail. The deliberation 'seen or not seen' is with respect to the truth — not with respect to a moment, as to whether a moment is seen or not. Why? Because whatever truth characterized by the subsequent-knowledge class was seen by the fifteenth moment — that very same [truth] is [seen] also by the sixteenth. 'There is no fresh seeing of an unseen truth' — therefore the sixteenth moment is not established as the path of seeing. For by one moment being unseen — that characterized by <s>mārgānvayajñānakṣānti</s> — the truth — that truth of the path — does not become unseen. He gives a worldly illustration: 'Just as by one stalk — by one grain-stalk — of a crop, being uncut by the sickle — the field does not become uncut.' Rather — the meaning is: it is [considered] cut. For indeed, some through carelessness, even when one stalk is uncut, say 'the field has been cut by us.' 'Because of being a fruit' — and so forth in detail. He establishes the sixteenth moment as the path of cultivation by reasons such as 'because of being a fruit.' The path of cultivation is the sixteenth moment — because of being the fruit of the conditioned <s>śrāmaṇya</s>. Like the fruit of once-returning, up to like the fruit of <s>Arhat</s>ship. Also because of cultivating the eight knowledges and sixteen aspects that have been cultivated — because of being a deficient-path of the trainee — and because of being continuous. [Tib. 208a] Just like the other fruits, it is the path of cultivation. For in the sixteenth moment, eight knowledges are cultivated: the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering, the subsequent knowledge of suffering, up to

body.text: mārge 'nvayajñānam iti. ākārā api ṣoḍaśānityādyā bhāvyaṃte. tadvad eva ca darśanamārge 'ṣṭajñānaṣoḍaśākārabhāvanā nāsti. tatra hi sabhāgajñānākārabhāvanaiva
body.translated_text: the subsequent knowledge of the path. The sixteen aspects too — impermanence and the rest — are cultivated. And in the path of seeing itself, the cultivation of the eight knowledges and sixteen aspects does not exist. For therein, only the cultivation of homogeneous knowledge and aspects [occurs] —

children.translated_text:
'As they arise, the patiences and knowledges
are cultivated in the seeing [path]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. mārgānvayajñāne ca pūrvamārgasya pratipannakamārgasya vihāniḥ. na ca darśanamārge pūrvamārgavihānir iti. prābaṃdhikaṃ cedaṃ mārgānvayajñānaṃ. na ca darśanamārge kṣāṃtir jñānaṃ vā kiṃcit prābaṃdhikam astīty ato 'pi mārgānvayajñānaṃ bhāvanāmārga iti. itaraḥ pratyavasthānaṃ karoti. darśanamārgaḥ ṣoḍaśaḥ kṣaṇaḥ. avaśyakāparihāṇitvāt. duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāṃtyādivad iti. pūrvapakṣaṃ vā dūṣayati. anumānapatitadharmasvarūpaviparyayāpakṣālo 'yaṃ pakṣa iti. bhāvanāmārgatve 'pi sādhyamāne tad aparihāṇitvam anenānumānenāpatatīti. tad idam aṃtarnītam abhisamīkṣya punar āha. aparihāṇis tv iti vistaraḥ. yasmād darśanaheyānāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇaṃ mārgānvayajñānenādhārapratipakṣeṇa [Tib. 208b] saṃdhāryate. yadi ca tasmāt phalamārgāt ṣoḍaśāt kṣaṇāt parihāṇiḥ syāt srotaāpattiphalāt parihāṇiḥ syāt. na ca srotaāpattiphalāt parihāṇir ity ato na tasmāt parihīyate. itara āha. ata eveti. kim ayam. aparihāṇihetur evocyate. vayam apy etam artham abhidadhmahe. kim ayam upalabdhisamam iti cottaram udgrāhyate. ācārya āha. ata eva darśanamārga iti cet. yadi manyase yata eva darśanaheyaprahāṇasaṃdhāraṇaṃ mārgānvayajñānena. ata eva darśanamārga iti. tan na. atiprasaṃgāt. yadi mārgānvayajñānena darśanaheyaprahāṇasaṃdhāraṇam ity ato darśanamārgaḥ syāt. evaṃ saty atiprasaṃgaḥ syāt. tasmān mārgānvayajñānāt pareṇa sarveṇa bhāvanāmārgeṇa darśanaheyaprahāṇasaṃdhāraṇam iti sarva eva darśanamārgaḥ syāt. aniṣṭaṃ caitat. ṣoḍaśa eva hi kṣaṇo darśanamārgo bhavadhir iṣyate. na saptadaśāṣṭadaśa ityādikaḥ kṣaṇaḥ pravāhanyāyenotpadyate. dvitīye tṛtīye vā divase ya utpadyate tajjātīyo viśeṣamārgasaṃgṛhītaḥ. tan nāsti. tato 'pi hi nāsti parihāṇiḥ. tad evaṃ saty āvaśyakāparihāṇitvaṃ yo hetur uktaḥ. so 'naikāṃtika iti darśitaṃ bhavati. [Tib. 209a] tadanaikāṃtikatvāc cāpratisādhanaṃ tat. na pūrvapakṣadūṣaṇaṃ ceti. āha. sapta jñānāni duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ yāvan mārge dharmajñānaṃ kasmād durśanamārgo na punar aṣṭamaṃ mārge 'nvayajñānam
body.translated_text: from this statement. And in the <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge of the path), there is deficiency of the prior path — the path of the trainee. And in the path of seeing, there is no deficiency of the prior path. And this <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s> is continuous (<s>prābandhi</s>). And in the path of seeing, no patience or knowledge is continuous — therefore, for this reason too, the <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s> is the path of cultivation. The opponent makes his objection: 'The path of seeing is sixteen moments — because of necessary non-regression.' Just like the <s>duḥkhadharmajñānakṣānti</s> and the rest. Or he criticizes the prior position: 'This position is one whose arguments, being those of the inference, cannot withstand the reversal of the own-form of the <s>dharma</s>.' Even when establishing it as the path of cultivation, that non-regression falls within this very inference. Having recognized this as imported [into the argument], he says again: 'But non-regression' — and so forth in detail. Because the abandonment of afflictions to be abandoned by seeing is sustained by <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s> as the ground-antidote. [Tib. 208b] If there were regression from that fruit-path — the sixteenth moment — there would be regression from the fruit of stream-entry. But there is no regression from the fruit of stream-entry — therefore there is no regression from that. The opponent says: 'For that very reason' — what is this? 'This very thing is stated as a reason for non-regression.' We too express this same meaning. 'Is it the same as the direct observation?' — this answer too is to be understood. The <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'If you think: for the very reason that the abandonment of what is to be abandoned by seeing is sustained by <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s> — for that very reason it is the path of seeing — that is not so. Because of over-extension.' If, because <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s> sustains the abandonment of what is to be abandoned by seeing, it would be the path of seeing — then, this being the case, there would be over-extension. For all the subsequent path of cultivation sustains the abandonment of what is to be abandoned by seeing — so all of it would be the path of seeing. And this is undesired — for only sixteen moments are accepted as the extent of the path of seeing, not the seventeenth, eighteenth, and so forth. The [sixteenth moment] arises by the stream method — even that produced on the second or third day, being of the same type, is included in the special path. That does not exist [for the opponent either] — for from that too there is no regression. Then, this being so, the reason that was stated — necessary non-regression — [Tib. 209a] is shown to be inconclusive. And because of its inconclusiveness, that is not a proof — not a refutation of the prior position. He says: '[If] seven knowledges — the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering up to the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of the path — why is [only this much] the path of seeing, and not also the eighth — the subsequent knowledge of the path?'

body.text: ity abhiprāyaḥ. darśanasyāsamāptatvād iti. mārgānvayajñānakṣāṃtau darśanaṃ samāptaṃ. sarveṣāṃ satyānāṃ tadānīṃ dṛṣṭatvāt. duḥkhe dharmajñāna utpanne yady api kāmāvacaraṃ duḥkhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ. rūpārūpyāvacaraduḥkhādi tu na tāvad dṛṣṭam. evaṃ yāvat. mārge dharmajñāna utpanne rūpārūpyapratipakṣo na tāvad dṛṣṭa iti. sāvaśeṣaṃ darśanaṃ na samāptam iti. tadaṃtarālatvād iti. darśanamārgāṃtarālatvāt. tayor vā dvayoḥ kṣāṃtyor aṃtarālatvāt. tāny api sapta jñānāni darśanamārgaḥ. śeṣadraṣṭavyasākāṃkṣatvāt tasya yogina ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: — this is the intent. 'Because the seeing is not completed' — at the time of <s>mārgānvayajñānakṣānti</s>, the seeing is completed — because all truths have been seen at that time. When the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of suffering has arisen, even though the suffering of the Desire Realm is seen, the suffering and the rest of the Form and Formless Realms are not yet seen. Thus, up to: when the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of the path has arisen, the antidote of the Form and Formless Realms is not yet seen. The seeing being incomplete — not completed. 'Because of being in the interval' — because of being in the interval of the path of seeing. Or because of being in the interval of those two patiences. Those seven knowledges too are the path of seeing — the intent being: because that practitioner still longs to see the remainder to be seen.

body.text: (VI.31cd, 32) pūrvaṃ parapratyayena paroditena arthānusaraṇād duḥkhādisatyapratipatter ity arthaḥ. pūrvam iti viśeṣaṇena bhāvanākāle paropadeśanirapekṣam arthānusaraṇam iti kathitaṃ bhavati. evaṃ dharmānusārīti. dharmair anusāro dharmānusāraḥ. so 'syāstīti dharmānusārī. dharmair anusartuṃ śīlam asyeti vā. [Tib. 209b] pūrvaṃ svayam eva sūtrādibhir dharmair dvādaśāṃgaiḥ pravacanair arthānusaraṇāt. pūrvavad vyākhyānaṃ. yāvat paṃca prakārāḥ prahīṇā bhavaṃtīti. yāvacchabdena yady eko dvau trayaś catvāraḥ paṃca prahīṇāḥ prakārā bhavaṃti. tathaiva prathamaphalapratipannakāv ucyete. yathā sakalabandhanau.
body.translated_text: (VI.31cd, 32) 'Previously, through the advice of another' — through the instruction delivered by another, because of pursuing the meaning — the meaning is: because of realizing the truths of suffering and the rest. Through the qualification 'previously,' it is implicitly stated that at the time of cultivation, one pursues the meaning independently of another's instruction. 'Similarly, the <s>dharma</s>-follower' (<s>dharmānusārī</s>). Following by means of <s>dharma</s>s is <s>dharmānusāra</s> — one who has that is a <s>dharmānusārī</s>. Or: one whose habit is to follow by means of <s>dharma</s>s. [Tib. 209b] Previously, by oneself, through <s>sūtra</s>s and other <s>dharma</s>s — the twelve divisions of the teaching — because of pursuing the meaning. The explanation is as before. 'Up to five types being abandoned' — by the word 'up to,' whether one, two, three, four, or five types are abandoned — just so, the two candidates for the first fruit are described. Just as having the full bond.

children.translated_text: 'For the second, below the destruction of nine' —

body.text: iti. dvitīye iti dvitīyanimittam ity arthaḥ. carmaṇi dvīpinaṃ haṃtīti yathā. arvāṅ navakṣayāt. navaprakāraprahāṇād adharataḥ navaprakāraprahāṇaparihāreṇārthād uktaṃ bhavati. yadi tayoḥ pudgalayos tasmāt paṃcaprakāraprahāṇāt pareṇa ṣaṭ saptaṣṭau vā prakārāḥ pūrvaṃ laukikena mārgeṇa prahīṇā bhavaṃti. tau dvitīyaphalapratipannakāv iti. dvitīya iti vacanāt. pratipannakāv iti cādhikārād evaṃ padārthavyavasthā labhyate. ūrdhvaṃ ceti prathamadhyānavītarāgau. yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanād vītarāgau.
body.translated_text: thus. 'For the second' means: for the purpose of the second. Like 'one kills a leopard for its skin.' 'Below the destruction of nine' — below the abandonment of nine types; by excluding the abandonment of nine types, the meaning is implicitly stated. If, for those two persons, beyond that abandonment of five types, six, seven, or eight types have been previously abandoned by the mundane path — they are candidates for the second fruit. Because of the word 'second' and the governing term 'candidates,' this determination of word-meanings is obtained. 'And above' — [they are] dispassionate from the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Up to dispassionate from the [realm of] Nothingness (<s>Ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>).

body.text: (VI.33) arhattvaṃ tu na śakyam āditaḥ prāptum iti. anāgāmiphalam aprāpyādita evārhattvaṃ prāptuṃ na śakyate. kasmād ity āha. bhāvanāheyaprahāṇāt. na hi darśanamārgeṇa bhāvāgrikāṇāṃ bhāvanāheyānāṃ prahāṇam astīti. yathā darśanamārgasvabhāveṣu paṃcadaśasu kṣaṇeṣu vartamānaḥ aditas tṛtīyaphalapratipannakād [Tib. 210a] arhattvaphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratipannakaḥ syāt. ṣoḍaśe tu citta utpanne ādito 'nāgāmino 'rhan syāt. bhāvāgrikabhāvanāheyaprahāṇād dhy arhattvaṃ pratisthāpyate. āha. yadi darśanamārgeṇa bhāvāgrikāṇāṃ bhāvanāheyānāṃ prahāṇaṃ nāstīti ato 'rhattvaṃ aśakyaṃ
body.translated_text: (VI.33) 'But <s>Arhat</s>ship cannot be attained from the very beginning' — it is not possible to attain <s>Arhat</s>ship from the very beginning without first attaining the fruit of non-returning. Why? He says: 'Because of the abandonment of what is to be abandoned by cultivation.' For there is no abandonment by the path of seeing of what is to be abandoned by cultivation belonging to the peak of existence. Just as, while being in the fifteen moments that have the nature of the path of seeing, one could be a candidate for the third fruit from the very beginning — [Tib. 210a] at the production of the sixteenth mind, one could be an <s>Arhat</s> from the very beginning as a non-returner. For <s>Arhat</s>ship is established through the abandonment of what is to be abandoned by cultivation belonging to the peak of existence. He says: 'If there is no abandonment by the path of seeing of what is to be abandoned by cultivation belonging to the peak of existence, and therefore <s>Arhat</s>ship is impossible'

body.text: pūrvam eva. tarhi pṛthagjanāvasthāyām eva bhāvanāmārgeṇa bhavāgravairāgyāt tatphalapratipannakaḥ. teṣu vartamāno 'rhattvaphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratipannako bhaviṣyati. ṣoḍaśe tu cittakṣaṇa ādito 'rhann iti. ata ucyate. pūrvaṃ ca bhavāgravairāgyasaṃbhavād iti. na hi pūrvaṃ pṛthagjanāvasthāyāṃ laukikena mārgeṇa bhavāgravairāgyasaṃbhavaḥ. uparibhūmyabhāvāt. tasmād āditaḥ pratipannako 'rhaṃś ca na syād iti. śraddhāprajñādhikatvenādhimokṣadṛṣṭiprabhāvitatvād iti. śraddhādhikatvenādhimokṣaprabhāvitatvāc chraddhādhimuktaḥ. śraddhādhiko muktaḥ śraddhādhimukta iti kṛtvā. na tu tasya prajñā naivāsti. tayā na tu prabhāvita iti. na tan nāma labhate. prajñādhikatvena dṛṣṭiprabhāvitatvāt dṛṣṭiprāptaḥ. na tu tasya śraddhā nāsīti pūrvavad vācyaṃ. apare tu punaḥ. [Tib. 210b] nairuktavidhim ālaṃbya vyācakṣate. śraddhādhipatyena darśanaheyebhyo muktaḥ śraddhādhimuktaḥ. dṛṣṭyādhipatyena prāptaphalo prāptaphalāḥ dṛṣṭiprāpta iti.
body.translated_text: previously indeed. Then, in the very state of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), through dispassion from the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) by means of the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), one would be a practitioner directed toward that fruit. While engaged in those [practices], one would be a practitioner directed toward the direct realization of the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship. But at the sixteenth mind-moment, one would be an <s>arhat</s> from the very beginning. Therefore it is said: 'And because of the impossibility of dispassion from the Peak of Existence previously.' For previously, in the state of being an ordinary person, dispassion from the Peak of Existence through the mundane path is not possible — because of the absence of a higher ground. Therefore, one cannot be simultaneously a practitioner [directed toward stream-entry] from the beginning and an <s>arhat</s>. 'Because of predominance of faith and wisdom, [and] because of being dominated by conviction and view' — one who is liberated through faith (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>) [is so called] because of predominance of faith, [hence] being dominated by conviction. One liberated through faith is one who is predominant in faith — thus [the name]. But it is not the case that wisdom is entirely absent in him; rather, he is not dominated by it — hence he does not receive that name. One who has attained [through] views (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>) [is so called] because of predominance of wisdom, [hence] being dominated by view. But it is not the case that faith is absent in him — this should be stated as before. Others, however, explain by relying on the etymological method: one who is liberated (<s>mukta</s>) from what is to be abandoned by seeing, through the predominance of faith, is liberated through faith (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>). One who has attained the fruit through the predominance of view is one who has attained views (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>).

children.translated_text: 'Up to the destroyer of five types' —

body.text: iti uktam. ataḥ pṛcchati kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇam iti vistaraḥ. phalaviśiṣṭo mārgo na labhyata iti. phalād viśiṣṭo mārgaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalapratipannakādiḥ. prathamādiprakārabhāvanāheyapratipakṣamārgo na bhāvyata ity arthaḥ. yāvan na viśeṣāya prayujyata iti. yāvan nāprahīṇakleśaprahāṇāya phalāṃtaraprāptinimittaṃ prayogaṃ karoti. tāvat pratipannako nocyate. yadā prayujyate. tadā pratipannaka ity arthād uktaṃ bhavati. tadā hi pūrvaprahīṇakleśapratipakṣasyāpratilabdhapūrvasya tatprahāṇasya cānāsravā prāptir utpadyata iti siddhāṃtaḥ. evam anyatrāpi phale veditavyam iti. ṣoḍaśe citte srotaāpanna evocyata iti vacanāt. srotaāpanna ukta ity ato 'nyatrāpi. sakṛdāgāmiphale anāgāmiphale ca veditavyaṃ. laukikena mārgeṇa prahīṇāṣṭaprakāro 'pi ṣoḍaśe citte sakṛdāgāmy evocyate. nānāgāmiphalapratipannakaḥ. yasmāt phale phalaviśiṣṭasya mārgasya lābho nāstīti. evaṃ kāmavītarāga ūrdhvaṃ vā ṣoḍaśe citte nārhattvaphalapratipannaka ucyate. yasmāt phale phalaviśiṣṭasyeti [Tib. 211a] pūrvavat. yas tu tṛtīyadhyānavītarāga iti vistaraḥ. tṛtīyadhyānavītarāgaḥ adharāṃ bhūmiṃ niśrityānāgamyaṃ dhyānāṃtaraṃ prathamaṃ dvitīyaṃ vā dhyānaṃ niśritya niyāmam avakrāmatīty asti saṃbhavaḥ. so 'vaśyaṃ phalaviśiṣṭaṃ mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkaroti tṛtīyadhyānasaṃgṛhītaṃ vā. yatas tṛtīyadhyānasaṃgṛhītam anāsravaṃ sukhendriyaṃ labhyate. asti hi sambhāvanā yad asau phalaviśiṣṭamārgaṃ saṃmukhīkuryāt. yasmād asya tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikaḥ kleśaḥ prahīṇa iti. tena so 'vaśyaṃ phalaviśiṣṭaṃ mārgaṃ
body.translated_text: this was stated. Therefore he asks: 'What is the reason?' — in detail. 'A path distinguished from the fruit is not obtained' — a path distinguished from the fruit — such as the practitioner directed toward the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmi</s>) and the rest — meaning: the path that is the antidote of the first and other types of afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation is not cultivated. 'As long as one does not exert oneself for distinction' — as long as one does not make the effort for the purpose of attaining another fruit, [meaning] for the abandonment of unabandoned afflictions — so long one is not called a practitioner [directed toward a higher fruit]. When one exerts oneself — then one is implicitly called a practitioner. For then, the uncontaminated acquisition of the abandonment — not previously obtained — of the antidote of previously-abandoned afflictions arises — this is the established doctrine. 'In the case of other fruits too, it should be understood in the same way' — because of the statement: 'at the sixteenth mind-moment, one is called a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) alone.' From this statement — 'a stream-enterer is stated' — in the case of other fruits too: in the case of the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmi</s>) and the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmi</s>), it should be understood. Even one who has previously abandoned eight types [of afflictions] through the mundane path — at the sixteenth mind-moment, that one is called a once-returner only, not a practitioner directed toward the fruit of non-returning. Because 'at the [time of the] fruit, a path distinguished from the fruit is not obtained.' Similarly, one who is dispassionate from the Desire Realm or higher — at the sixteenth mind-moment, one is not called a practitioner directed toward the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship — because 'at the [time of the] fruit, a path distinguished [from the fruit is not obtained]' — as before. 'But one who is dispassionate from the third <s>dhyāna</s>' — in detail. One dispassionate from the third <s>dhyāna</s>, relying on a lower ground — the access concentration (<s>anāgamya</s>), the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, or the first or second <s>dhyāna</s> — enters the certainty (<s>niyāma</s>) — there is this possibility. That one necessarily brings face-to-face the path distinguished from the fruit — [which is] included in the third <s>dhyāna</s>. Because the uncontaminated pleasure faculty (<s>sukhendriya</s>) included in the third <s>dhyāna</s> is obtained. For there is the possibility that this one would bring face-to-face the path distinguished from the fruit — because this one's afflictions belonging to the ground of the third <s>dhyāna</s> have been abandoned. Therefore, that one is necessarily determined to bring face-to-face the path distinguished from the fruit

body.text: saṃmukhīkarotīti niyamyate. anyathā hi yadi na saṃmukhīkarotīty arthaḥ. sa tasmād ūrdhvopapannaḥ. sa āryaḥ. tasmāt tṛtīyadhyānād ūrdhvaṃ caturthe dhyāne ārūpyeṣu vā sukhendriyeṇāsamanvāgataḥ syāt. yad dhi sāsravaṃ sukhendriyaṃ. tad bhūmisaṃcārāt tyaktaṃ. yad api cānāsravaṃ. tad api. yadi na saṃmukhīkṛtaṃ syād ubhayenāpi sukhendriyenāsamanvāgataḥ syād āryāṇāṃ cordhvopapannānām avaśyaṃ sukhendriyeṇāsamanvāgama uktaḥ. sukhendriyeṇa caturthadhyānārūpyopannaḥ pṛthagjano na samanvāgataḥ. āryas tu samanvāgata iti vacanāt. yaś cāpi saumanasyendriyeṇa samanvāgataḥ. so 'vaśyaṃ paṃcabhir upekṣājīvitamanaḥsukhasaumanasyendriyair ity evamādivacanāc ca. [Tib. 211b] atra brūmaḥ. asty eṣa vibhāṣāyāṃ likhitapakṣaḥ. sa tu na sthāpanāpakṣo lakṣyate. apara āhur iti vacanāt. yo hi caturthadhyānalābhī ṣaṇṇāṃ bhūmīnām anyatamāṃ bhūmiṃ niśritya niyāmam avakrāmati. sa ṣaḍbhūmikenānāgāmiphalenānāgamyabhūmikena yāvac caturthadhyānabhūmikena ṣoḍaśe citte samanvāgato bhavati. tathā vītarāgatvāt. yas tṛtīyadhyānalābhī. sa paṃcabhūmikena. caturthadhyānabhūmikaṃ hitvā. evaṃ yo dvitīyadhyānalābhī. sa caturbhūmikena. tṛtīyacaturthabhūmike hitvā. yas tu vītarāgaḥ prathamadhyānalābhī vā dvitīyālābhī. sa yady anāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnoti. tribhūmikenāsāv anāgāmiphalena samanvāgataḥ. anāgamyadhyānāṃtaraprathamadhyānabhūmikena. sarvajaghanyo 'pi hy anāgāmy avaśyam eva tribhūmikenānāgāmiphalena samanvāgata iti varṇayaṃti. tasmād aparapakṣāpekṣayaivam uktam ācāryeṇeti yuktaṃ syāt.
body.translated_text: . Otherwise — meaning: if one does not bring it face-to-face — that one, reborn above that [third dhyāna], would be a Noble one. That Noble one, above the third <s>dhyāna</s> — in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> or in the formless [realms] — would be unendowed with the pleasure faculty (<s>sukhendriya</s>). For whatever contaminated pleasure faculty [one had] — that has been abandoned through the transfer of ground. And whatever uncontaminated [pleasure faculty] — that too, if not brought face-to-face, one would be unendowed with both types of pleasure faculty. But for Noble ones reborn above, necessary endowment with the pleasure faculty has been stated. Because of the statement: 'An ordinary person born in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> or the formless [realms] is not endowed with the pleasure faculty; but a Noble one is endowed.' And because of the statement: 'Whoever is endowed with the mental-pleasure faculty (<s>saumanasyendriya</s>), that one is necessarily [endowed] with five — equanimity, life, mind, pleasure, and mental-pleasure faculties' — and similar statements. To this we say: this is a position recorded in the <s>Vibhāṣā</s>, but it does not appear to be the established position — because of the statement 'others say.' For one who has attained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, entering the certainty relying on any one of the six grounds — the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmi</s>) belonging to six grounds, from the access concentration up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground, at the sixteenth moment one is endowed [with it]. Because of [their] dispassion. Similarly, for one who has attained the third <s>dhyāna</s> — with fivefold [fruit], excluding the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground. For one who has attained the second <s>dhyāna</s> — with fourfold, excluding the third and fourth ground. But for one dispassionate who has attained the first <s>dhyāna</s> or has not attained [any] — if that one obtains the fruit of non-returning, that one is endowed with the fruit of non-returning belonging to three grounds — the access concentration, the intermediate [dhyāna], and the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. For even the least [accomplished] non-returner is necessarily endowed with the fruit of non-returning belonging to three grounds — thus they explain. Therefore, it would be proper that the <s>Ācārya</s> stated this with reference to the other position.

body.text: (VI.35ab) evaṃ tāvad bhūyaḥkāmavītarāgāṇām iti. bhūyovītarāgāṇāṃ. kāmavītarāgāṇāṃ ca. tatra bhūyovītarāgo yasya saptāṣṭau vā prakārāḥ pūrvaṃ laukikena mārgeṇa prahīṇā bhavaṃti. yasya [Tib. 212a] nava prakārāḥ prahīṇāḥ. sa kāmavītarāgaḥ. bhūyovītarāgāṇāṃ pudgalavyavasthā
body.translated_text: (VI.35ab) 'Thus indeed, for those who are further-dispassionate and those dispassionate from the Desire Realm' — for those who are further-dispassionate and for those who are dispassionate from the Desire Realm. Therein, one who is further-dispassionate is one for whom seven or eight types [of afflictions] have been previously abandoned through the mundane path. One for whom nine types have been abandoned — that one is dispassionate from the Desire Realm. The classification of persons for those who are further-dispassionate [is established by the verse]:

children.translated_text: 'In [the attainment of] the second [fruit], before the destruction of nine [types]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. kāmavītarāgāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: from this statement. For those dispassionate from the Desire Realm [the verse]:

body.text: vacanāt. yathaite kāmadhātāv iti.
body.translated_text: from this statement. 'Just as these [afflictions] in the Desire Realm'

children.translated_text: 'Up to the destroyer of five types. In [the attainment of] the second [fruit], before the destruction of nine [types].

body.text: iti vacanāt. kāmadhātau nava prakārāḥ kleśā upadiṣṭāḥ. celād iti vastrāt. eṣa dṛṣṭāṃtayoga iti. drstāṃtayuktir dṛṣṭāṃtayogo dṛṣṭāṃtaprakāra ity apare.
body.translated_text: from this statement. In the Desire Realm, nine types of afflictions have been taught. 'From the cloth (<s>celā</s>)' means from the garment. 'This is the application of the illustration' — the suitability of the illustration is the application of the illustration, the mode of the illustration — [say] others.

body.text: tad evam anayā yuktyānena vā prakāreṇānyo 'pi dṛṣṭāṃto vaktavya iti sūcayati. anyathā hy eṣa dṛṣṭāṃta ity eva brūyāt. anādisaṃsāra iti. anādau saṃsāre. svahetuparaṃparayā dhyāpitā abhivardhitās tataś cādhimātrapramāṇam eteṣām ity abhiprāyaḥ. teṣāṃ kleśānām unmūlanāt prāpticchedataḥ. mūlasadharmiṇyo hi prāptayas tatprabaṃdhatvāt kleśānāṃ tṛvṛtkarṣaniṣkarṣaṇavad iti. yathā trivṛtkarṣeṇa dharaṇena subahukāle saṃvardhitānāṃ vātapittādīnāṃ doṣāṇāṃ niṣkarṣaṇaṃ. evaṃ kṣāṇikamṛdukenāpy āryamārgeṇa kleśānāṃ. yathā ca kṣaṇikenālpena pradīpena [Tib. 212b] mahatas tamaso ghātaḥ. tadvat kleśānām iti.
body.translated_text: Therefore, by this reasoning, by this mode, another illustration too should be stated — he indicates. Otherwise, he would have simply said 'this is the illustration.' 'Beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>' — in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>. Through the succession of their own causes, [the afflictions] have been nourished and increased, and from that they have reached an intense magnitude — this is the intent. From the uprooting of those afflictions — from the cutting of acquisition. For acquisitions are similar to roots, because they are the continuum of the afflictions — like the illustration of a strong purgative medicine. Just as through a strong purgative medicine, over a very long time, the faults of wind, bile, and the rest that have been nourished are purged — similarly, by even a momentary, mild Noble path, the afflictions [are purged]. And just as by a momentary, small lamp, a great darkness is destroyed — so too the afflictions.

body.text: (VI.35cd) saptakṛtvaḥ paramaṃ janmāsyeti. saptakṛtvo janmaprakarṣaṇāsya. nātaḥ param ity arthaḥ. tena mārgeṇa nirvāṇagamanād ity arthaḥ. srotasā hi loke gamyate.
body.translated_text: (VI.35cd) 'Seven times at most is the birth for this one' (<s>saptakṛtvaḥ paramaṃ janmāsya</s>) — this one has birth seven times at most; not beyond that — this is the meaning. 'Because of going to <s>nirvāṇa</s> by that path' — this is the meaning. For in the world, one goes by a stream (<s>srotas</s>).

body.text: ādyamārgalābhāc cet. ādyo 'nāsravo mārgo darśanamārgas tasya lābhāc cet srotaāpannaḥ. aṣṭamako 'pi syāt. srotaāpattiphalapratipannako 'pi syād ity arthaḥ. tathā hi pratilomakrameṇārhata ārabhyāṣṭānāṃ puruṣapudgalānām arhatpratipannakādīnāṃ srotaāpattiphalapratipanno 'ṣṭamako bhavati śraddhānusārī dharmānusārī vā tasyāpy ādyamārgalābhāt so 'pi srotaāpannaḥ syāt. ādyaphalalābhāc cet. atha mataṃ apūrvaphalasya lābhāt srotaāpanna iti. bhūyovītarāgo 'pi syāt. yaḥ prahīṇaṣaṭkleśaprakāraḥ ṣoḍaśe kṣaṇe sakṛdāgāmī. so 'pi srotaāpannaḥ syāt. tasyāpy apūrvaphalalābhāt. evaṃ kāmavītarāgo 'pi syāt. tasyāpi tad ādyaṃ phalam iti. idānīṃ parihāra [Tib. 213a] ucyate. sarvaphalaprāpiṇam adhikṛtyādyaphalalābhād iti. sarvaphalam iti. srotaāpattiphalādīni catvāri. tatprāptuṃ śīlam asyeti sarvaphalaprāpī. sarvaphalaprāpti asyāsīti vā sarvaphalaprāpī. tam adhikṛtya tam abhisaṃdhāyādyaphalalābhād apūrvaphalalābhāt srotaāpanna ucyate. kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇam iti vistaraḥ. kasmāt sa eva srotaāpanna ucyate. nāṣṭamakaḥ sa cāpi hy āryamārgasrotaāpanna iti. pratipannakaphalamārgalābhād iti vistaraḥ. yasmāt tena sarvaphalaprāpiṇā pratipannakamārgaḥ paṃcadaśakṣaṇasvabhāvaḥ. bhāvanāmārgaś ca ṣoḍaśakṣaṇo labdhaḥ. aṣṭamakena tu pratipannakaḥ mārga eva labdha iti. itaś ca darśanabhāvanāmārgalābhāt. yasmāc ca tena darśanamārgaś ca sa eva bhāvanāmārgaś ca sa eva labdhaḥ. aṣṭamakena tu darśanamārga eveti. sakalasroto'bhisamayāc ca mārgānvayajñāne. yasmāc cānena sakalaṃ sroto'bhisamitaṃ mārgānvayajñānakṣāṃtikṣaṇasyāpi darśanān na tv aṣṭamakena. tasmād
body.translated_text: 'If because of the attainment of the first path' — the first uncontaminated path is the path of seeing; if because of the attainment of that, one is a stream-enterer — then even the eighth person (<s>aṣṭamaka</s>) would be [a stream-enterer] — meaning: even the practitioner directed toward the fruit of stream-entry would be so. For thus, in reverse order beginning from the <s>arhat</s>, of the eight persons — the <s>arhat</s> practitioner and the rest — the practitioner directed toward the fruit of stream-entry is the eighth person, who is either a faith-follower (<s>śraddhānusārin</s>) or a <s>dharma</s>-follower (<s>dharmānusārin</s>). That one too has the attainment of the first path; therefore that one too would be a stream-enterer. 'If because of the attainment of the first fruit' — if it is held that one is a stream-enterer because of the attainment of a previously-unobtained fruit — then even the further-dispassionate one would be [a stream-enterer]. One who has abandoned six types of afflictions, [becoming] a once-returner at the sixteenth moment — that one too would be a stream-enterer, because that one too has the attainment of a previously-unobtained fruit. Similarly, one dispassionate from the Desire Realm too would be [a stream-enterer] — because for that one too, that is the first fruit. Now the resolution is stated: 'With reference to one who is a potential attainer of all fruits, because of the attainment of the first fruit.' 'All fruits' — the four, namely stream-entry and the rest. One whose character (<s>śīla</s>) it is to attain them — or one who has the potential for attaining all [fruits] — is a potential attainer of all fruits. With reference to that one, with that one intended, because of the attainment of the first fruit — the previously-unobtained fruit — one is called a stream-enterer. 'But what is the reason?' — in detail. Why is it that only that one is called a stream-enterer, and not the eighth person? For that one too has entered the stream of the Noble path. 'Because of the attainment of the practitioner-path and the fruit-path' — in detail. Because by that potential attainer of all fruits, the practitioner-path — whose own-nature is fifteen moments — and the path of cultivation, which is the sixteenth moment, have been attained. But by the eighth person, only the practitioner-path has been attained. 'And because of the attainment of the paths of seeing and cultivation' — and because by that one, both the path of seeing and that which is the path of cultivation have been attained; but by the eighth person, the path of seeing alone. 'And because of the complete realization of the entire stream (<s>sakalasroto'bhisamaya</s>) at the [moment of] <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s>' — and because by this one, the entire stream has been realized at the moment of <s>mārgānvayajñānakṣānti</s> too — [the entire stream] having been seen; but not by the eighth person. Therefore

body.text: ebhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sarvaphalaprāpy eva srotaāpanna ity ucyate nāṣṭamakaḥ. prakarṣagater hi tathā vacanaṃ. tadyathā loke yaḥ prakarṣeṇa bhāsaṃ karoti. sa bhāskara ucyate. na khadyotakaḥ. [Tib. 213b] tadvat. tasmād anyān iti. tasmāt sāṃpratikād bhavād anyān. saptasthānakauśalasaptaparṇavad iti. yathā saptakasāmānyāt saptasthānakuśalo bhikṣur uktaḥ sūtre. kathaṃ. vistaram uktvāha. kathaṃ ca bhikṣavo bhikṣuḥ saptasthānakuśalo bhavati. rūpaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. rūpasamudayaṃ rūpanirodhaṃ rūpanirodhagāminīṃ pratipadaṃ rūpasyāsvādam ādīnavaṃ niḥsaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. evaṃ vedanāṃ saṃjñāṃ saṃskārān vijñānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. vijñānasamudayaṃ vistareṇa yāvan niḥsaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti. evam anena nyāyena paṃcasaptakāni paṃcatriṃśad iti. paṃcatriṃśat kuśalaḥ prāpnoti. saptaparṇavac ca. yathā ca pattrikāyāṃ pattrikāyāṃ saptaparṇasādṛśyād anekaśatapattro 'pi san sa vṛkṣaḥ saptaparṇa ity ucyate. tadvat. prathamo dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ pravacane siddhaḥ. dvitīyo loka iti dṛṣṭāṃtadvayopanyāse prayojanam. yadi saptakasāmānyāt saptakṛtvaḥ parama iti vyākhyāyate.
body.translated_text: for these reasons, only the potential attainer of all fruits is called a stream-enterer, not the eighth person. 'For the designation is made from the superlative.' Just as in the world, one who illuminates to the highest degree is called the 'light-maker' (<s>bhāskara</s>), not the firefly. Similarly. Therefore 'other than' — other than the present existence — seven [more births]. 'Like skill in seven stations (<s>saptasthānakauśalya</s>) and the seven-leaf tree (<s>saptaparṇa</s>)' — just as, from the commonality of seven, a monk is called skilled in seven stations in the <s>sūtra</s>. How? Having stated in detail, he says: 'And how, O monks, is a monk skilled in seven stations? He knows form as it truly is. He knows the origination of form, the cessation of form, the practice leading to the cessation of form, the gratification of form, the danger, and the escape as they truly are. Similarly, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness — he knows as they truly are. The origination of consciousness, in detail up to the escape — he knows as they truly are.' Thus, by this method, five times seven makes thirty-five. He attains [proficiency in] thirty-five. 'And like the seven-leaf tree' — just as a tree, despite having many hundreds of leaves, because of the similarity to seven leaves on each leaf, is called a seven-leaf tree (<s>saptaparṇa</s>). Similarly. The first illustration is established in the teaching. The second is in the world — this is the purpose of presenting two illustrations. If the explanation of 'seven times at most' is given from the commonality of seven.

body.text: yat tarhi sūtra uktaṃ. tad virudhyata ity ato 'pavyākhyānam etad ity abhiprāyaḥ. ekasyāṃ gatāv aṣṭamaṃ bhavaṃ nābhinirvartayatīty avirodhaḥ. yathārutaṃ vā kalpyamāna iti. saptakṛtvo devāṃś ca manuṣyāṃś ca saṃsṛtya saṃdhāvya [Tib. 214a] duḥkhasyāṃtaṃ karotīti devamanuṣyavacanād aṃtarābhavo 'pi na syāt. iṣyate ca devamanuṣyagatyoḥ saptabhavābhinirvartanam. aṃtarābhavās tu na gaṇyāṃta iti. yadi aṃtarābhavaiḥ saha saptabhavā gaṇyeran janmacatuṣṭayam evāsya syāt. tad evānenāniṣṭāpattivacanena tadātmīyaṃ vyākhyānam ekasyāṃ gatāv iti samarthayati. itara āha. evam apy ūrdhvaṃsrotasa iti vistaraḥ. yady ekasyāṃ gatāv aṣṭamaṃ bhavaṃ nābhinirvartayatīti vyākhyāpayasi. kathaṃ tarhi ūrdhvasrotaso 'ṣṭamabhavābhinirvṛttir ekasyāṃ gatau bhavati. bhavāgraparamasyeti viśeṣaṇaṃ kim artham. akaniṣṭhaparamasyāpi aṣṭamabhavābhinirvṛttiḥ saṃbhavati.
body.translated_text: What was stated in the <s>sūtra</s> — that is contradicted — therefore this is an alternative explanation — this is the intent. 'He does not produce an eighth existence in a single destiny' — there is no contradiction. Or, if construed literally: 'Having transmigrated and wandered among gods and humans seven times, he makes an end of suffering' — from the statement of gods and humans, the intermediate existence too would not exist. But it is accepted that there is the production of seven existences in the destinies of gods and humans. The intermediate existences, however, are not counted. If the seven existences were counted together with intermediate existences, he would have only four births. By this very statement of undesired consequence, he supports his own explanation — 'in a single destiny.' The other says: 'Even so, for the one going upward (<s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s>)' — and so forth in detail. If you explain that 'he does not produce an eighth existence in a single destiny,' how then does the one going upward produce an eighth existence in a single destiny? 'Whose maximum is the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>)' — what is the purpose of this qualifier? For even one whose maximum is <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, the production of an eighth existence is possible.

children.text: sa pluto 'rdhaplutaḥ sarvaś cyutaś cānyo bhavāgraga
children.translated_text: 'He leaps, half-leaps, passes through all, and departs — another goes to the Peak of Existence' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. sa cāpi vaktavyaḥ. bhavaprakarṣavivakṣāyāṃ tu bhavāgraparamagrahaṇam ity abhiprāyaṃ lakṣayāmaḥ. kāmadhātvabhisaṃdhivacanād iti. kāmadhātau caikā gatir manuṣyagatiḥ. devagatir vā. tasyām aṣṭamabhavaṃ nābhinirvartayati. na tu rūpārūpyadhātvor iti. kim atra jñāpakaṃ. sūtraṃ yuktir vā. kāmadhātum adhikṛtyedam uktam iti. [Tib. 214b] sūtram āgamaḥ.
body.translated_text: from this statement. And he too should be discussed. But when one intends the excellence of existences, the inclusion of 'whose maximum is the Peak of Existence' — we perceive this intent. 'Because of the statement with reference to the Desire Realm' — in the Desire Realm, there is one destiny — the human destiny, or the divine destiny. In that [single destiny], he does not produce an eighth existence — but not in the Form and Formless Realms. What is the indication here? — a <s>sūtra</s> or reasoning? That this was stated with reference to the Desire Realm — the <s>sūtra</s> is the scripture.

body.text: yuktir atrānumānaṃ. yena codakenaivaṃ coditaṃ kim atra jñāpakaṃ sūtraṃ yuktir veti. sa eva punar āha. iha caiva kiṃ jñāpakaṃ pratyekaṃ devamanuṣyeṣu iti vistaraḥ. pratyekaṃ devamanyuṣyeṣu saptakṛtvaḥ saṃsṛtyeti. na punar ubhayeṣv eva devamanuṣyeṣu saptakṛtva iti. tad uktaṃ bhavati. yo manuṣyeṣu dṛṣṭasatyaḥ. sa deveṣu triṣkṛtvaḥ saṃsṛtya manuṣyeṣu ca triṣkṛtva eva tato devān āgamya parinirvātīti. yo vā deveṣu dṛṣṭasatyaḥ. sa tathaiva. sa manuṣyeṣu triṣkṛtvo deveṣu ca triṣkṛtva eva saṃsṛtya tato manuṣyān āgamya parinirvātīti. evaṃ hi paṭhyate saptakṛtvo devāṃś ca manuṣyāṃś ceti. sāmānyarūpeṇa hi paṭhyate. na pratyekam iti viśiṣya paṭhyata ity arthaḥ. evaṃ vaibhāṣikapakṣe saṃśayāvasthe kṛte ācāryaḥ samarthayann āha. pratyekam api tu kāśyapīyā iti vistaraḥ. kāśyapīyā nikāyāṃtarīyāḥ. ta evaṃ paṭhanti. saptakṛtvo devān saptakṛtvo manuṣyān iti. evaṃ pratyekamartho labhyate. tad anenobhayam api parihṛtaṃ bhavati. yad uktaṃ kim atra jñāpakaṃ sūtraṃ yuktir vā kāmadhātum adhikṛtyedam uktam iti. yac coktam iha caiva kiṃ jñāpakaṃ. pratyekaṃ devamanuṣyeṣu saptakṛtva iti. [Tib. 215a] pratyekamarthaparigraheṇaiva hi kāmadhātvabhisaṃdhir api sūcito bhavati. na hi rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ saptakṛtvo devamanuṣyeṣu saṃsaraṇaṃ yujyate. tatropapannānām anāgāmināṃ manuṣyānāgamanāt. yuktir apy ata eva gamyate. yatraiva saptakṛtvobhavaparama uktaḥ. tatraiva bhūmāv aṣṭamabhavapratiṣedha upapadyate nānyatreti. nātrābhiniveṣṭavyam iti. iha caiva kiṃ jñāpakam iti. tajjātīya iti. tatprakāraḥ. yena tāvatā kālenāvaśyaṃ saṃtatiparipākān nāṣṭamaṃ bhavam abhinirvartayati. saptapadāśīrviṣadaṣṭavat. saptapadāśīrviṣeṇa tena daṣṭo yathā saptapadāni gatvā mriyate. na pareṇa nārvāk. viṣajātiḥ sā tādṛśī. cāturthakajvaravac ca. yathā cāturthako jvaraś caturtha evāhani bhavati. na pareṇa nārvāk. rogajātiḥ sā tādṛśī. tadvat. dve avarabhāgīye iti. kāmacchandavyāpādau. kāmāvītarāgatvād etau bhavataḥ. paṃcordhvabhāgīyānīti.
body.translated_text: Reasoning here is inference. By the very objector who raised the challenge — 'what is the indication here, a <s>sūtra</s> or reasoning?' — that same one further says: 'And here too, what is the indication that it is specifically among gods and humans separately?' — and so forth in detail. Is it specifically among gods and humans separately that he transmigrates seven times? Or is it not among both gods and humans together seven times? This has been stated: one who has seen the truths among humans — he transmigrates among gods three times and among humans three times, then coming to the gods, attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Or one who has seen the truths among gods — he likewise, transmigrating among humans three times and among gods three times, then coming to humans, attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For thus it is read: 'seven times among gods and humans' — in a general form. It is not read specifying 'separately' — this is the meaning. When the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> position has been thus placed in a state of doubt, the <s>Ācārya</s>, supporting [his view], says: 'But the <s>Kāśyapīyas</s> indeed separately' — and so forth in detail. The <s>Kāśyapīyas</s> are members of another school. They read thus: 'seven times among gods, seven times among humans.' Thus the meaning of 'separately' is obtained. By this, both [objections] are resolved. What was said — 'what is the indication here, a <s>sūtra</s> or reasoning, that this was stated with reference to the Desire Realm?' And what was said — 'and here too, what is the indication, separately among gods and humans, seven times?' For by the acceptance of the meaning of 'separately,' the reference to the Desire Realm too is indicated. For it is not tenable that in the Form and Formless Realms one transmigrates seven times among gods and humans. Because <s>Anāgāmins</s> reborn there do not come back to humans. The reasoning too is understood from this very [fact]. Wherever the maximum of seven existences is stated, there alone the prohibition of an eighth existence is fitting, not elsewhere. 'One should not insist on this' — 'and here too, what is the indication?' 'Of that type' — of that kind. One who, within such a period of time, necessarily [makes an end] because of the maturation of the continuum, does not produce an eighth existence. 'Like one bitten by a seven-step viper' — just as one bitten by a seven-step viper — by that [viper] — dies after walking seven steps, not more and not less. That species of poison is of such a nature. 'And like a quartan fever' — just as a quartan fever occurs on the fourth day alone, not more and not less. That species of disease is of such a nature. Likewise. 'The two lower fetters' — sensual desire (<s>kāmacchanda</s>) and ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>). These exist because of not being free from passion for the Desire Realm. 'The five upper fetters' —

children.translated_text: 'The two passions — for form and for the formless — restlessness, pride, and delusion' —

body.text: yato 'rvāṇ nirvāṇaṃ ca na prāpnoti. na cāṣṭamaṃ bhavam abhinirvartayatīti. [Tib. 215b] saptasaṃyojanāvaśeṣatvād ity ahetur eṣa ity ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ. na hy ūrdhvabhāgīyāni kāmadhātau janmābhinirvartayituṃ samarthāny ūrdhvabhūmikatvād iti. etad dhetuvādinaḥ punar āhuḥ. yady api tāny ūrdhvabhūmikāni. tatprāptisāmarthyāt tu tāvatāṃ bhavānām abhinirvṛttir bhavati.
body.translated_text: because one attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> neither below [in lower realms] nor does one reach <s>nirvāṇa</s> and does not produce an eighth existence. Because of the remainder of seven fetters — says <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> — this is not a [valid] reason. For the upper fetters, belonging to the upper grounds, are not capable of producing birth in the Desire Realm. The proponents of this [seven-fetter] reason further say: even though those [upper fetters] belong to the upper grounds, by the power of their acquisition, the production of so many existences occurs.

body.text: na hi tāni ūrdhvam api vipākahetutvena vyavasthāpyaṃte. avyākṛtatvād iti. aṃtareṇety aṃtarārvāg ity arthaḥ. dharmatāpratilaṃbhikam iti. aśaikṣamārgasāmarthyapratilaṃbhikam ity arthaḥ. sa hi tasya svabhāvo yad bhikṣuliṃgena yojayatīti.
body.translated_text: For those [upper fetters] are not established as fruition-causes even above, because they are indeterminate. 'Within' means 'short of' — meaning: before. '<s>Dharmatāpratilambhika</s>' (obtained by the nature of things) — meaning: obtained by the power of the path of no-more-learning (<s>aśaikṣamārga</s>). For it is its nature that [the practitioner] is conjoined with the mark of a monk.

body.text: avinipātadharmeti. sūtre paṭhyate. srotaāpanno bhavann avinipātakadharmā niyataṃ saṃbodhiparāyaṇaḥ saptakṛtvaḥparamaḥ saptakṛtvo devāṃś ca manuṣyāṃś ca saṃdhāvya saṃsṛtya duḥkhasyāṃtaṃ karotīti. kasmād evaṃ bhavatīty āha. tadgāmikakarmānupacayād iti. vinipāto 'pāyo narakādiḥ. taṃ gacchatīti tadgāmi. tadgāmy eva tadgāmikaṃ. kiṃ. karma. tasyānāgatasyānupacayād āryāvasthāyāṃ. upacitavipākadānavaiguṇyāc ca saṃtateḥ. pṛthagjanāvasthāyām upacitasyāniyatavedanīyasya tadgāmikasya karmaṇo vipākadānavaiguṇyāt saṃtateḥ. avinipātadharmā bhavatīty ucyate. [Tib. 216a] īdṛśī tasya skaṃdhasaṃtatiḥ parāvṛttā. yad asau tadgāmikasya karmaṇa upacitasya vipākadānavaiguṇyenāvasthiteti. kasmāt punaḥ sā skaṃdhasaṃtatir upacitatadgāmikakarmavipākadānavaiguṇyenāvasthiteti. tata ucyate. balavatkuśalamūlādhivāsanād iti. yasmād asau skaṃdhasaṃtatir babavadbhiḥ. kuśalamūlair adhivāsitā paribhāvitā. kathaṃ ca punar balavatkuśalamūlādhivāsitā. prayogāśayaśuddhitaḥ. prayogaśuddhita āśayaśuddhitaś ca. tatra prayogaśuddhir āryakāṃtāni śīlāni. āśayaśuddhir buddhādiṣv avetyaprasāda iti. kṣāṃtim api notpādayed iti. kṣamaṇam api notpādayet. cittam api notpādayet. prāg eva prayogam ity abhiprāyaḥ. atha vā. apāyaniyate tu karmaṇi saty asau pudgalaḥ kṣāṃtim api nirvedhabhāgīyalakṣaṇāṃ notpādayati. kim aṃgānāsravaṃ mārgam iti. yathā balavatkuśalamūlādhivāsitā upacitākuśalavipākadānaviguṇā bhavati. tac chlokenopadarśayati.
body.translated_text: 'Of the nature of not falling into lower realms (<s>avinipātadharma</s>)' — it is read in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'A stream-enterer is of the nature of not falling [into lower realms], is fixed (<s>niyata</s>), is destined for awakening (<s>saṃbodhiparāyaṇa</s>), is one of at most seven [births], and having transmigrated and wandered among gods and humans seven times, makes an end of suffering.' Why does this happen? — he says: 'Because of the non-accumulation of <s>karma</s> leading to that' — a lower realm (<s>vinipāta</s>) is a bad destiny (<s>apāya</s>) — the hells and the like. One who goes there is '<s>tadgāmi</s>.' '<s>Tadgāmi</s>' itself is '<s>tadgāmika</s>.' What? — <s>Karma</s>. Because of the non-accumulation of that [karma] which is future, in the state of being a Noble (<s>ārya</s>). And because of the impairment of the fruition-giving capacity of the continuum with regard to [karma] already accumulated — of the <s>karma</s> leading to that [lower realm] which was accumulated in the state of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), which bears uncertain fruition (<s>aniyatavedanīya</s>), because of the impairment of the continuum's capacity for giving fruition. He is said to be of the nature of not falling into lower realms. Such is the transformation of his aggregate-continuum, that it remains with the impairment of the fruition-giving capacity of the accumulated <s>karma</s> leading to that [lower realm]. And why does the aggregate-continuum remain with the impairment of the fruition-giving capacity of the accumulated <s>karma</s> leading to lower realms? Therefore it is said: 'because of the pervasion by powerful wholesome roots.' Since that aggregate-continuum is pervaded — permeated — by powerful wholesome roots. And how is it pervaded by powerful wholesome roots? 'Because of the purity of practice and intention.' Because of the purity of practice and because of the purity of intention. Therein, purity of practice is the morality dear to the Nobles (<s>āryakāntaśīla</s>). Purity of intention is the confirmed confidence (<s>avetyaprasāda</s>) in the <s>Buddha</s> and the rest. 'Would not produce even tolerance' — would not produce even patient acceptance. Would not produce even a thought — let alone a practice — this is the intent. Or alternatively: when <s>karma</s> determining [rebirth in] a lower realm exists, that person does not produce even tolerance characterized by the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>), let alone the uncontaminated path. Just as the [continuum] pervaded by powerful wholesome roots becomes impaired in the fruition-giving capacity of the accumulated unwholesome — this he illustrates with a verse:

body.text: sarvam.
body.translated_text: all [of the verse follows].

body.translated_text: 'having done' —

body.text: apāyaṃ.
body.translated_text: to a lower realm.

body.text: punar
body.translated_text: 'however' —

body.text: pāpaṃ kṛtvā
body.translated_text: 'sin having done' —

body.text: apāyaṃ. tad arthadvayaṃ yathākramaṃ [Tib. 216b] dṛṣṭāṃtadvayena sādhayati.
body.translated_text: the lower realm. The two propositions are established in sequence by two illustrations.

children.translated_text: 'remaining in the form of a lump' —

body.text: asaṃskṛtatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'because of not being fashioned.'

body.text: punar lohaṃ
body.translated_text: 'however, that iron' —

body.text: san
body.translated_text: 'being' —

body.text: jātam udake
body.translated_text: 'born in water' —

body.text: tarati. tadabhisaṃskāraguṇāt. evam abudho guṇair apātrīkṛtatvān majjati. na tu budho guṇaiḥ pātrīkṛtatvād iti.
body.translated_text: crosses over. Because of the quality of fashioning. Thus, the fool, not being fashioned into a vessel by [spiritual] qualities, sinks. But not the wise one, because of being fashioned into a vessel by [spiritual] qualities.

body.text: yasmāt pareṇa duḥkhaṃ nāstīti. yasmād duḥkhāt pareṇa duḥkhaṃ nāsti bhavāṃtarasaṃgṛhītaṃ. sa duḥkhasyāṃto duḥkhāvasānam ity arthaḥ. anyathā hi maraṇakāle duḥkhasyāṃto bhavati. sapratisaṃdhikaṃ tu tad duḥkham. ata āha. apratisaṃdhikaṃ duḥkhaṃ karotīty artha iti. kathaṃ nirvāṇaṃ karotīti. nityatvāt karaṇaṃ na yujyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. tatprāptivibaṃdhāpanayanād iti. nirvāṇaprāptivibaṃdhāpanayanāt. tatprāpter vibaṃdhaḥ kleśaprāptir upadhir vā tadapanayanān nirvāṇaṃ karoti. tadyathākāśaṃ maṇḍapāvasthāne na lakṣyate. sati tasya vibaṃdhe. tadapanayanān nityam apy ākāśaṃ karotīty ucyate. tenāha. yathākāśaṃ kuru maṇḍapaṃ pātayeti bhavaṃti vaktāra iti. anyo 'pi veti pṛthagjanaḥ paripakvasaṃtānaḥ na tu niyata iti. kadācid ihaiva parinirvāyāt aṃtarābhaveṣu cety ato nocyate.
body.translated_text: Because after that there is no more suffering — because after that suffering, there is no suffering included in another existence — that end of suffering is the cessation of suffering — this is the meaning. For otherwise, at the time of death too, there is an end of suffering. But that suffering has a reconnection [to a new existence]. Therefore he says: 'He makes suffering without reconnection — this is the meaning.' 'How does one make <s>nirvāṇa</s>?' — because of its permanence, making is not tenable — this is the intent. 'Because of the removal of the obstruction to the attainment of that' — the removal of the obstruction to the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The obstruction to the attainment of that — the acquisition of afflictions or the substrates (<s>upadhi</s>) — because of the removal of that, one makes <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Just as space in the place of a pavilion is not perceived when the obstruction exists. Because of the removal of that [obstruction], even though space is permanent, one is said to 'make' it. Therefore he says: 'Just as people say: "Make space — bring down the pavilion."' 'Or another too' — an ordinary person whose continuum has matured, but who is not fixed. He might attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s> here in this very [life], or in intermediate existences — therefore he is not mentioned.

body.text: dve vā trīṇi vā janmāny asyeti [Tib. 217a] dvitrijanmā. kecid evaṃ paṭhaṃti. dvitrajanmeti. dve vā trīṇi vā dvitrāṇi. saṃkhyayāvyayāsannādūrādhikasaṃkhyāḥ
body.translated_text: one who has two or three births is 'of two or three births' (<s>dvitrijanman</s>). Some read thus: '<s>dvitrajanman</s>' — two or three are '<s>dvitra</s>.' 'Numbers, indeclinables, near-and-far, and additional numbers

body.text: saṃkhyeya iti samāsaḥ. bahuvrīhau saṃkhyeye ḍaj iti samāsāṃtaḥ. dvitrānyajanmāny asyeti dvitrajanmeti. śloke tu dvayor grahaṇam iti. kleśaprahāṇajanmanoḥ. kasmād ity āha. srotaāpannasyānupūrvikasya darśanaprahātavyeṣu prahīṇeṣu bhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ kleśānām ekasya prakārasya yāvac caturṇāṃ paścāt prahāṇe sati. tatpratipakṣasyaikadvitryādikleśaprakārapratipakṣasyānāsravasyendrigasya lābhas tasyānuktasiddhatvāt ślokena tasyāgrahaṇaṃ. na hi vinā pratipakṣeṇa kleśaprakāraprahāṇam asti. laukikenāpi hi mārgeṇa tasyāryasya kleśaprakāraprahāṇe 'nāsravasya tatpratipakṣasyendriyasya lābho bhavati. janma tu kadācid alpīyaḥ syāt. yadīhaiva parinirvāyāt aṃtarābhave upapadya vā. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. pareṇa bhavyatvāt. srotaāpattiphalāt pareṇa sakṛdāgāmitvasya yāvad arhattvasya bhavyatvāt. ato 'sya janmano grahaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: [form] a numeral compound' — thus the compound. In the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, the suffix <s>ḍaj</s> is added after a numeral compound — thus the compound-ending. 'One whose births are two or three' — thus '<s>dvitrajanman</s>.' But in the verse, the inclusion of 'two' — of both affliction-abandonment and births. Why? — he says: for the stream-enterer who [attains <s>nirvāṇa</s>] in sequence, when the [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing have been abandoned and when one type, up to four types, of the afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation are subsequently abandoned, there is the obtaining of the uncontaminated faculty that is the antidote of one, two, three, or more types of affliction — because that [obtaining] is established without being stated, the verse does not include it. For without the antidote, there is no abandonment of an affliction-type. And even when that Noble one abandons affliction-types through the mundane path, there is the obtaining of the uncontaminated faculty that is the antidote of those [types]. But the births might sometimes be fewer — if he attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s> here in this very [life], or having been reborn in the intermediate existence. For what reason? Because of the possibility afterward — because of the possibility of [attaining] the state of once-returner up to <s>arhat</s>ship after the fruit of stream-entry. Therefore, his births are included [in the verse].

children.translated_text: 'Of two or three births, a clan-to-clan (<s>kulaṃkula</s>)' —

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: niyamārtham idam iha vicāryate. ya ekadvividhamuktaḥ. sa kiṃ bhavati. kulaṃkula ity eke.
body.translated_text: This is discussed here for the purpose of determination. One who is freed from one or two [types of affliction] — what does he become? A clan-to-clan — say some.

body.text: grahaṇaṃ tu udāharaṇārthaḥ. parimāṇārthaṃ vā nātaḥ pareṇeti. ekadvividhamuktaḥ paṃcaṣaṭjanmety apare. [Tib. 217b] tricaturvidhamukta iti viśeṣaparigrahāt. naitad vyākhyānakārair vicāritam iti vicāryam etat.
body.translated_text: the inclusion is for the purpose of illustration. Or for the purpose of determining the limit — not more than this. 'One freed from one or two types has five or six births' — say others. Because of the specific inclusion of 'freed from three or four types.' 'This has not been discussed by the commentators' — this is [a matter] to be investigated — this [remains to be] investigated.

body.text: kasmān na paṃcaprakāraprahāṇāt. kiṃ. kulaṃkulo bhavatīty adhikāraḥ. tatprahāṇa iti vistaraḥ. paṃcaprakāraprahāṇe ṣaṣṭhayāpi prakārasyāvaśyaṃ prahāṇāt. kasmād ity āha. na hi tasyaikaḥ prakāraḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ phalaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ vighnayituṃ samartha iti. ekavīcikasyeveti. viparītadṛṣṭāṃta eṣaḥ. yathaikavīcikasyaikaḥ prakāro navamo 'nāgāmiphalaṃ vighnayituṃ samarthaḥ. naivam asya srotaāpannasya ṣaṣṭhaḥ prakāraḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ vighnayituṃ samartha iti. kasmād ity āha. dhātvanatikramād iti. ekavīciko hi kāmadhātum atikrāmati. ato 'syaiko 'pi prakāro navamaḥ phalaṃ vighnayituṃ samartho dhātvatikramasya duṣkaratvāt. sakṛdāgāmī tu dhātuṃ nātikrāmatīti. na tasyaikaḥ kleśaḥ prakāraḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ phalaṃ vighnayituṃ samartha iti.
body.translated_text: 'Why not through the abandonment of five types?' The topic is: one becomes a <s>kulaṃkula</s> (clan-to-clan practitioner). 'The abandonment of that' — and so forth in detail. At the abandonment of five types, the sixth type too is necessarily abandoned. Why? He says: 'For one single type, the sixth, is not capable of obstructing the fruit — the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>).' 'Like an <s>ekavīcika</s> (one-interval practitioner)' — this is a contrasting example. Just as for an <s>ekavīcika</s>, a single type — the ninth — is capable of obstructing the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>). Not so for this stream-enterer — the sixth type is not capable of obstructing the once-returner fruit. Why? He says: 'because of not transcending the realm.' For an <s>ekavīcika</s> transcends the Desire Realm. Therefore even a single type — the ninth — is capable of obstructing the fruit, because of the difficulty of transcending a realm. But a once-returner does not transcend the realm. Therefore one single affliction-type — the sixth — is not capable of obstructing the fruit.

body.text: tatra vānyatra vā devanikāya iti. tadyathā trāyastriṃśeṣu satyāni dṛṣṭvā dve trīṇi vā kulāni saṃsṛtya. tatraiva trāyastriṃśeṣu parinirvāti. anyatra vā.
body.translated_text: 'In that or in another class of gods' — for example, having seen the truths among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> [gods], having transmigrated through two or three families, he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in those very <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> [gods]. Or in another [class]

body.text: cāturmahārājakāyikeṣu yāmeṣu vā parinirvāti. evam anyatrāpi yojyaṃ. rāgadveṣamohānāṃ tanutvād ity ucyata iti sūtre. kathaṃ. trayāṇāṃ samyojanānāṃ [Tib. 218a] prahāṇāt rāgadveṣamohānāṃ ca tanutvāt sakṛdāgāmībhavatīti. mṛduprakārāvaśeṣatvād iti. mṛdvadhimātro mṛdumadhyo mṛdumṛdur ity etanmātrāvaśeṣatvāt.
body.translated_text: — he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> among the <s>Cāturmahārājikāyika</s> [gods] or among the <s>Yāma</s> [gods]. Other cases too should be connected similarly. 'In the <s>sūtra</s> it is stated: because of the thinning of desire, aversion, and delusion.' How? 'Through the abandonment of three fetters and the thinning of desire, aversion, and delusion, one becomes a once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>).' 'Because of only the mild types remaining' — because only the mild-intense (<s>mṛdvadhimātra</s>), mild-middling (<s>mṛdumadhya</s>), and mild-mild (<s>mṛdumṛdu</s>) types remain.

children.translated_text: 'One whose seven or eight portions of defect are exhausted'
