body.text: iti. doṣāṃśo doṣāvayavaḥ saptāṣṭaprakāralakṣaṇaḥ. indriyata iti cātra tṛtīyaṃ kāraṇaṃ na sūtritaṃ tathaiva vyākhyeyaṃ. katham asyeti vistaraḥ. katham asyaikavīcikasyaikaprakāro navamaḥ phalaṃ vighnayituṃ samartho na hi kulaṃkulasyaikaḥ prakāraḥ phalaṃ vighnayituṃ samartha iti. ucyate. dhātvatikramāt. yasmād asau navame prakāre prahīṇe kāmadhātusamatikrāṃto bhavati. na punas tatropapadyate. sa ca navamaḥ prakāraḥ karmaṇā saha tatropapadyavedanīya ity atas tadvipākaniṣyandaphalabhūmyatikramāt phalaṃ vighnayituṃ samartho bhavati. avasthātraye hi karmāṇi vighnāyopatiṣṭhaṃta ity uktaṃ prāk.
body.translated_text: — a portion of defect is a component of defect characterized by seven or eight types. 'By way of faculties' — this third reason is not stated in the <s>sūtra</s>; it should be explained in the same way. 'How is it for this one?' — and so forth in detail. How is it that for this <s>ekavīcika</s> a single type — the ninth — is capable of obstructing the fruit, while for a <s>kulaṃkula</s> a single type is not capable of obstructing the fruit? He says: 'because of transcendence of a realm.' Since, when the ninth type has been abandoned, he has transcended the Desire Realm and does not take rebirth there again. And that ninth type, together with its <s>karma</s>, is experienced-upon-rebirth there — therefore, because of the transcendence of the ground of its maturation and outflow-fruit, it is capable of obstructing the fruit. For it was said earlier: 'in the three states of existence, <s>karma</s>s stand as obstructions.'

children.translated_text: 'At the attainment of patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>), non-returning, and <s>arhat</s>ship, <s>karma</s> becomes an extreme obstacle'

body.text: iti. iha tu kleśeṣu yojayitavyaṃ. ata evāha. yathā karmāṇi. evaṃ kleśā ityādi. tasyavaikajanmavyavahitatvād iti. tasya kṣīṇasaptāṣṭaprakārasya sakṛdāgāminaḥ. ekena janmanā vāvahitatvān nirvāṇasya. ekena vā kleśaprakāreṇa vyavahitam asyānāgāmiphalam ity [Tib. 218b] ekavīcikaḥ. na tāvat kulaṃkulo bhavaty ekavīciko veti. laukikena mārgeṇa pūrvaṃ tricaturvidhamukto 'pi na tāvat kulaṃkulo bhavati. kṣīṇasaptāṣṭaprakāro 'pi na tāvad ekavīciko bhavati. tatpratipakṣānāsravendriyalābhasyābhāvāt. ata evāha. yāvat phalaviśiṣṭo mārgo na saṃmukhīkṛta iti. phalaviśiṣṭe tu tatpratipakṣe tadūrdhvaprakārapratipakṣe vā saṃmukhīkṛte tadānāsravendriyalābhāt. kulaṃkulo bhavaty ekavīciko vety arthād uktaṃ bhavati. paṃcānām iti vistaraḥ. paṃcānām avarabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇāt anāgāmīty ucyate sūtre. prahāṇasaṃkalanāt. satkāyadṛṣṭyādīnāṃ prahāṇaikatvavyavasthāpanāt dve trīṇi vā pūrvaṃ prahīṇānīti. yadi tāvat kāmavītarāgo niyāmam avakrāmati. dve pūrvaṃ prahīṇe laukikena mārgeṇa. kāmacchando vyāpādaś ca. satkāyadṛṣṭyādīnām aparyādāya prahāṇāt. athānupūrvikaḥ. trīṇi pūrvaṃ prahīṇāni. kena. darśanamārgeṇa satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ śīlavrataparāmarśo vicikitsā ca. tasmāt sākalyena paṃcānāṃ prahāṇād ity ucyate.
body.translated_text: — but here it should be applied to afflictions. Therefore he says: 'just as <s>karma</s>s, so too afflictions' and so on. 'Because of being separated by only one birth' — for that once-returner whose seven or eight types are exhausted. Because <s>nirvāṇa</s> is separated from him by only one birth. Or: his non-returner fruit is separated by one affliction-type — [hence] he is an <s>ekavīcika</s>. 'He does not initially become a <s>kulaṃkula</s> or an <s>ekavīcika</s>' — even though one has been freed of three or four types by the mundane path beforehand, one does not initially become a <s>kulaṃkula</s>; even though one whose seven or eight types are exhausted, one does not initially become an <s>ekavīcika</s> — because of the absence of obtaining an uncontaminated faculty as the antidote to those. Therefore he says: 'as long as the path distinguished by the fruit has not been brought face-to-face.' But when the antidote distinguished by the fruit — or the antidote to the upper types — has been brought face-to-face, then, because of obtaining an uncontaminated faculty — one becomes a <s>kulaṃkula</s> or an <s>ekavīcika</s>; this is implicitly stated. 'Of five' — and so forth in detail. One is called a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) in the <s>sūtra</s> through the abandonment of five lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīya saṃyojana</s>). Because of the aggregation of abandonment. Because the abandonment of identity-view and the rest is established as one — two or three have been previously abandoned. If one enters the determined course having already attained freedom from desire for the Desire Realm, two were previously abandoned by the mundane path — sensual desire and malice — because of the incomplete abandonment of identity-view and the rest. But if one is gradual, three were previously abandoned — by the seeing-path: identity-view, attachment to morality and vows, and doubt. Therefore, through the abandonment of five in total, it is stated [thus].

children.translated_text: 'He is one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate [state], upon rebirth, with effort, or without effort'

body.text: iti. so 'nāgāmī. aṃtarā utpanne saṃskāreṇāsaṃskāreṇa [Tib. 219a] parinirvṛtir asyeti aṃtarotpannasaṃskārāsaṃskāraparinirvṛtiḥ. yat tūktam evam utpannasyeti. tan na budhyāmahe. katham utpannasyānāgāminaḥ parinirvṛtir asyeti bahuvrīhiḥ samāso bhavati. anyapadārthe hi bahuvrīhir ucyate. na svapadārthe. tenaivam iha pāṭhaṃ paśyāmaḥ evam utpanne 'syeti. lekhakenaikāro 'tra vināśita iti. tathāpāṭhe hy ayam arthaḥ saṃbhavati. utpanne janmani parinirvṛtir asyeti utpannaparinirvṛtiḥ. athaivam eva pāṭhaḥ syāt. evaṃ vyākhyāyeta. anādare ṣaṣṭhī. tayaivaṃ samāsaḥ kriyeta. utpannasya janmanaḥ parinirvṛtir asyānāgāmina ity utpannaparinirvṛtir anāgāmīti. atha vā utpannasyety utpannajātir ucyate. utpannānām iti yo 'rthaḥ. so 'rtha utpannasyeti. tenotpannānāṃ yā parinirvrṭiḥ. sā asyety utpannaparinirvṛtiḥ. atha parinirvṛtyarthād eva kevalād anāgāmyarthasyānyatvāt. pūrvapadārthānanyatve 'py anāgāmisamānādhikaraṇasyotpannaśabdasya parinirvṛtiśabdena saha bahuvrīhiḥ samāsa itīccheyuḥ. subhaṇitam etat syāt. sa evānāgāmī punaḥ paṃcadhā bhavatīti. aṃtarāparinirvāyī upapadyaparinirvāyī sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī ūrdhvaṃsrotāś ceti nigamayati.
body.translated_text: — he is a non-returner. One for whom there is <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate [state], upon rebirth, with conditioning, or without conditioning — he is 'one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state, upon rebirth, with or without conditioning.' Now, what was stated as 'of one thus arisen' — that we do not understand. How can 'of one arisen, the non-returner, his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>' be a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound? For a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> is stated in the sense of another word, not in the sense of its own word. Therefore we see the reading thus: 'upon arising.' A vowel was corrupted here by a scribe. For in that reading, this meaning is possible: 'one whose <s>parinirvāṇa</s> is upon arising in a birth' — hence 'one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon arising.' Or if the reading is exactly thus, it would be explained as: a sixth case used in the sense of disregard. By that, the compound would be made thus: 'one whose <s>parinirvāṇa</s> is regardless of having arisen in a birth, a non-returner' — hence 'one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon arising, a non-returner.' Or alternatively, '<s>utpannasya</s>' — birth is called '<s>utpannajāti</s>.' The meaning of '<s>utpannānām</s>' (of the arisen ones) — that is the meaning of '<s>utpannasya</s>.' Therefore: the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> that belongs to the arisen ones — that is his; hence 'one whose <s>parinirvāṇa</s> is that of the arisen.' Or, since from the very meaning of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the meaning of non-returner is different — if they wish [to hold] that even though there is no otherness from the prior-word meaning, a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound [is formed] of the word '<s>utpanna</s>' coordinated with '<s>anāgāmin</s>' together with the word '<s>parinirvṛti</s>' — that would be well-stated. He concludes: that very non-returner is again fivefold: <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state), <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains it upon rebirth), <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains it with effort), <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> (one who attains it without effort), and <s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s> (one who goes upstream).

body.text: abhiyuktavāhimārgatvād iti. abhiyukto vīryavān ārabdhavīrya ity arthaḥ. vāhī mārgo asyeti vāhimārgaḥ. kathaṃ mārgo vāhī. vinābhisaṃskāreṇa saṃmukhībhāvāt. abhiyuktaś cāsau vāhimārgaś cābhiyuktavāhimārgaḥ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. utpannamātro nacirāt parinirvāti. sopadhiśeṣeṇa nirvāṇeneti. nirvāṇadvaividhyād viśinaṣṭi sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇena parinirvāti. sarvāsravakṣayaṃ karatīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Because of having a path that is earnest and flowing (<s>abhiyuktavāhimārga</s>)' — <s>abhiyukta</s> means energetic, one whose energy is aroused — this is the meaning. One whose path is flowing — hence '<s>vāhimārga</s>.' How is the path flowing? Because of coming face-to-face without effort. And he is earnest and he has a flowing path — hence '<s>abhiyuktavāhimārga</s>.' Having that nature — therefore. Having just arisen, he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> before long. 'With the <s>nirvāṇa</s> with a remainder of clinging (<s>sopadhiśeṣa</s>)' — because of the twofold nature of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, he distinguishes: he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with the <s>nirvāṇa</s> with a remainder of clinging. The meaning is: he accomplishes the complete destruction of all outflows.

body.text: so 'pi nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇeneti. na kevalam aṃtarāparinirvāyī nirupadhiśeṣaparinirvāṇena parinirvāty arhattvaṃ prāpyāyur aparisamāpya. upapadyaparinirvāyy [Tib. 219b] api tatsadṛśa ity apare. na. āyurutsargāvaśitvāt. naitad evaṃ so 'pi nirupadhiśeṣaparinirvāṇeneti. kasmāt. āyurutsargāvaśitvāt. āyuṣa utsarge tasyāvaśitvāt. kasmāt punar asyātrāvaśitvaṃ. yat prāṃtakoṭikacaturthadhyānalābhina āyurutsargavaśitvaṃ. tac ca prāṃtakoṭikaṃ dhyānaṃ manuṣyeṣv eva triṣu dvīpeṣūtpādyate. sa ca rūpadhātūpapanna iti. kim aṃtarāparinirvāyiṇo 'sty āyurutsargavaśitvaṃ. yata evam asau nirupadhiśeṣaparinirvāṇena parinirvāti. tasyāpi vaśitvaṃ nāsti. aṃtarābhavāvasthānāya
body.translated_text: 'He too, with the <s>nirvāṇa</s> without a remainder of clinging (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>)' — not only the <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with the <s>nirvāṇa</s> without a remainder of clinging, having attained <s>arhat</s>ship and without completing [his] lifespan — the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> too is similar to that — [say] others. No — because of the mastery of relinquishing the life-span. This is not so: 'he too [attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>] with the <s>nirvāṇa</s> without a remainder of clinging.' Why? Because of the mastery of relinquishing the life-span. Because of his mastery in the relinquishment of the life-span. Why does he have mastery here? Because the mastery of relinquishing the life-span belongs to one who has obtained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> of the border-peak (<s>prāntakoṭika</s>). And that border-peak <s>dhyāna</s> is produced only among humans in the three continents. And he is reborn in the Form Realm. Does the <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> have mastery in relinquishing the life-span — so that he thus attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with the <s>nirvāṇa</s> without a remainder of clinging? He too does not have mastery. But

body.text: tu tādṛśaṃ karma nāsti. yādṛśam upapadyaparinirvāyiṇa iti. ato 'ṃtarāparinirvāyī śīghraṃ parinirvāti. upapadyaparinirvāyī tu yāvadāyuḥ sthitvā parinirvātīty upapadyaparinirvāyy eva sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇena parinirvātīty ucyate. sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī kileti. kileti kilaśabdo vaibhāṣikamatadyotakaḥ. svamataṃ hi sūtrānusāreṇa paścād vakṣyate. apratiprasrabdhaprayoga iti. pūrvaprayogāvedhenānirākṛtaprayoga ity arthaḥ. sābhisaṃskāraṃ saprayatnaṃ. abhiyuktāvāhimārgatvād iti. abhiyuktatvāt avāhimārgatvāc ca tasya yoginaḥ. [Tib. 220a] ata evāsau sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī sidhyati. anabhisaṃskāreṇeti. pūrvaviparyayeṇa. prayogasya pratiprasrabdhatvāt. abhiyogavāhimārgābhāvād iti. abhiyogasya vīryasyābhāvāt. vāhimārgasya cābhāvād ity arthaḥ. tad evam abhiyogādinānātvāt parinirvāṇaviśeṣa ukto bhavati. upapadyaparinirvāyiṇo hy ubhayam asti. abhigogaś ca vāhī ca mārga iti. sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyiṇo 'bhjyogo 'sti. na tv asya vāhī mārgaḥ. anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyiṇas tūbhayam api nāsti. nābhiyogo na ca vāhī mārga iti.
body.translated_text: he does not have <s>karma</s> of such a kind as would sustain his intermediate existence — the kind that the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> has. Therefore the <s>antarāparinirvāyin</s> attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> quickly. But the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s>, having remained for the duration of his lifespan, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — thus only the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> is said to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with the <s>nirvāṇa</s> with a remainder of clinging. 'The <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>, it is said (<s>kila</s>)' — the word <s>kila</s> indicates the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> view. For his own view, following the <s>sūtra</s>, he will state later. 'With unrelaxed effort (<s>apratiprasrabdhaprayoga</s>)' — meaning: with effort not interrupted, not withdrawn, through the unbroken continuity of previous effort. '<s>Sābhisaṃskāra</s>' means with exertion. 'Because of having an earnest but non-flowing path (<s>abhiyuktāvāhimārga</s>)' — because of the earnestness and the non-flowing nature of the path of that practitioner. For that very reason he is established as a <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>. 'Without conditioning (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>)' — the reverse of the previous. Because of the relaxation of effort. 'Because of the absence of earnest effort and a flowing path' — because of the absence of earnest effort — of energy — and because of the absence of a flowing path — this is the meaning. Thus, because of the variety of earnest effort and the rest, the distinction of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> has been stated. For the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s>, both exist — both earnest effort and a flowing path. For the <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>, there is earnest effort, but his path is not flowing. For the <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>, however, neither exists — neither earnest effort nor a flowing path.

body.text: saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtālaṃbanamārgaparinirvāṇād iti. saṃskṛtaṃ saṃskāra ity eko 'rthaḥ. evam asaṃskṛtaṃ asaṃskāra iti. saṃskārālaṃbanena mārgeṇa duḥkhasamudayamārgālaṃbanena mārgeṇa yaḥ kleśān prajahāti. sa sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī. yo 'saṃskārālaṃbanena nirodhālaṃbanena. so 'nabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyīti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> through a path having conditioned or unconditioned [dharmas] as its object' — '<s>saṃskṛta</s>' (conditioned) and '<s>saṃskāra</s>' (conditioning) are synonymous. Likewise '<s>asaṃskṛta</s>' (unconditioned) and '<s>asaṃskāra</s>' (non-conditioning). One who abandons afflictions through a path having conditioned [dharmas] as its object — a path having suffering, origination, and the path as its object — is a <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>. One [who does so] through a path having unconditioned [dharmas] — cessation — as its object is an <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>.

body.text: tat tu na. atiprasaṃgād [Tib. 220b] iti. tat tu naivaṃ. kasmāt. atiprasaṃgāt. aṃtaropapadyaparinirvāyiṇor api saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtālaṃbanamārgaparinirvāṇāt pratyekaṃ sābhisaṃskārānabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyitvaprasaṃgaḥ. tatrasthau dvāv eva pudgalau syātāṃ. na paṃceti. anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī pūrvaṃ paṭhyata iti. sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyiṇaḥ pūrvam ayaṃ paṭhyate. anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyīti. tathaiva yujyata iti vistaraḥ. anabhisaṃskārasābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyiṇor yathākramaṃ. vāhyavāhimārgayoḥ pudgalayoḥ parinirvāṇasyānabhisaṃskārasādhyatvāt pūrvasyābhisaṃskārasādhyatvāc cetarasya. kathaṃ tathā sādhyatvam ity āha. ayatnayatnaprāptitas tatparinirvāṇasya yathākramam ity eva.
body.translated_text: 'But that is not so — because of overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).' But it is not so. Why? Because of overextension. Since even for the <s>antarā</s>- and <s>upapadya</s>-parinirvāyins, <s>parinirvāṇa</s> occurs through a path having conditioned or unconditioned [dharmas] as its object — there would be the consequence that each of them is both a <s>sābhisaṃskāra</s>- and <s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>-parinirvāyin. [In that case,] there would be only two persons located there, not five. 'The <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> is listed first' — this one is listed before the <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>: <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>, [then] <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>. 'This is fitting exactly so' — and so forth in detail. For the <s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>- and <s>sābhisaṃskāra</s>-parinirvāyins in order: the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the persons with non-flowing and flowing paths is accomplishable without conditioning for the former and accomplishable with conditioning for the latter. How is it accomplishable thus? He says: 'because of their <s>parinirvāṇa</s> being attained without effort and with effort respectively.'

body.text: atha vāhyavāhimārgayor iti. mārgayor eva grahaṇaṃ na pudgalayor abhisaṃbaṃdhaḥ. vāhino mārgasyānabhisaṃskārasādhyatvād avāhinaś cābhisaṃskārasādhyatvāt. ayatnayatnaprāptitaḥ. ayatnasaṃmukhībhāvataḥ pūrvamārgasya. yatnaprāptita itarasyeti. [Tib. 221a] tad evam anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī pūrvaṃ yujyate. āha. yady anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyiṇo vāhī
body.translated_text: Or alternatively, 'of the non-flowing and flowing paths' — the word refers to the paths themselves, not the connection to persons. Because of the non-flowing path being accomplishable without conditioning, and the non-flowing being accomplishable with conditioning. 'Through attainment without effort and with effort' — through the coming face-to-face without effort of the former path, and through the attainment with effort of the latter. Thus the <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> is first — this is fitting. He says: 'If the path of the <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s> is flowing because of being accomplishable without conditioning

body.text: mārgo 'nabhisaṃskāraśādhyatvāt upapadyaparinirvāyiṇo 'pi vāhī mārga iti. kas tayor viśeṣa iti. ata ucyate. upapadyaparinirvāyiṇas tu mārgo vāhitaro jitataraḥ. nānabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyiṇa evam adhimātrataro hetūpacayataḥ. mṛdutarāś cānuśayāḥ mārgādhimātrataratvena kṣapitatvāt.
body.translated_text: — then the path of the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> too is flowing. What is the distinction between them?' Therefore it is said: 'But the path of the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s> is more flowing, more powerful — not so that of the <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>, being more intense, because of the greater accumulation of causes.' And the latent dispositions are milder — because they have been worn away by the more intense path.

body.text: ūrdhvasrotā iti. ūrdhvasroto gatir asyeti ūrdhvasrotāḥ. yatra ūrdhvam iti paṭhyate.
body.translated_text: 'One whose stream goes upward (<s>ūrdhvasrotās</s>)' — one whose course goes upward is an <s>ūrdhvasrotās</s>. Where the reading '<s>ūrdhvam</s>' is found —

children.translated_text: 'Upward, from taming and from the body' —

body.text: ūrdhvaṃdamikaḥ ūrdhvaṃdehika iti. tatpratyayasaṃniyogenordhvaśabdasya māṃtato 'pi nipātyata iti veditavyaṃ. yathā ciraśabdasya ciraṃtanam ity ūrdhvam iti nipāto 'stīty apare. akārāṃto 'pi tūrdhvaśabdo 'sty eveti na vāryate. vyavakīrṇāvyavakīrṇadhyānatvād iti. miśritāmiśritadhyānatvād ity arthaḥ. anāsraveṇa sāsravasya dhyānasya miśritatvāt. iha dhyānāni vyavakīrya dhyānatrayāt parihīyata iti. dhyānavyavakiraṇaṃ caturthadhyānavyavakiraṇapūrvakam.
body.translated_text: thus: <s>ūrdhvaṃdamika</s> (one who tames upward) and <s>ūrdhvaṃdehika</s> (one who goes upward in body). It should be understood that by the obligatory connection with the affix, the word <s>ūrdhva</s> is declined even with the <s>m</s>-ending. Just as the word <s>cira</s> [has the form] <s>ciraṃtana</s>. Others [say]: the indeclinable '<s>ūrdhvam</s>' exists. But the word <s>ūrdhva</s> ending in <s>a</s> also exists — this is not to be denied. 'Because of having mixed and unmixed <s>dhyāna</s>s' — the meaning is: because of having mixed and unmixed meditations — because of mixing the contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>) <s>dhyāna</s> with the uncontaminated. 'Here, having interspersed the <s>dhyāna</s>s, he falls away from the three <s>dhyāna</s>s' — the interspersion of <s>dhyāna</s>s is preceded by the interspersion of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: iti vacanāt. caturtham eva hi dhyānam ādito vyavakiraṇe samarthaṃ. nānyat. caturthāc ca dhyānād aparihīṇasya prathamādiṣu dhyāneṣūpapattir nāstīty ata ucyate. dhyānatrayāt [Tib. 221b] parihīṇa iti. kathaṃ ca parihīṇa ity āha. prathamaṃ dhyānam āsvādyeti. madhyānimajjanāt madhye 'nimajjanāt. ardhapluto nāmeti vistaraḥ. ya ekam api sthānāṃtaraṃ vilaṃghya śuddhāvāseṣūpapadyākaniṣṭhān praviśatīty evaṃ vākyābhisaṃbaṃdhaḥ. dṛṣṭisthānatvād iti. mahābrahmaṇāṃ prathamopapannānāṃ ca mahābahmaṇi nirmāyakābhimānataḥ. ekamāyakatvāc ceti. kiṃ. mahābrahmasv āryo nopapadyate. āryasya hi prabhāvavatas tatrotpāde saty ubhayanāyakatvaṃ syāt. niḥsapatnena ca karmaṇā tatrādhipatim. ataḥ sasapatnaṃ na bhavatīti. sarvāṇi sthānāṃtarāṇīti. brahmakāyikebhyaś cyutvā brahmapurohitādīni sudarśanāntāni caturdaśasthānāṃtarāṇi saṃcaryākaniṣṭhān praviśati. yatropapannas tatas tatra cātyaṃtam anāgamanād iti. yatropapannas tadyathā. prathamadhyāne. tato 'tyaṃtam anāgamanāt kāmadhātau. tathā yatropapannas tatra cātyaṃtam anāgamanāt. tatra ca punaḥ prathame dhyāne 'tyaṃtam anāgamanāt. paripūrṇam anāgāmitvaṃ punas tatra dvitīyajanmākaraṇāt. śamathacarito hy eṣa iti. ya eṣa bhavāgraparamaḥ sa samādhipriyaḥ. ārūpyeṣu ca samādhir atipraśāṃtaḥ. tasmād ayam ārūpyān praviśati. pūrvakas tu vipaśyanācarita iti. yo 'sāv akaniṣṭhaparama
body.translated_text: from this statement. For only the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is capable of interspersion from the beginning, not another. And because one who has not fallen away from the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> does not take rebirth in the first and other <s>dhyāna</s>s — therefore it is said: 'fallen away from the three <s>dhyāna</s>s.' And how has he fallen away? — he says: 'savoring the first <s>dhyāna</s>.' 'Because of not sinking in the middle' — because of not sinking in the middle [stages]. He is called 'half-leaper' — and so forth in detail. 'Whoever, skipping even one intermediate station, takes rebirth in the Pure Abodes (<s>śuddhāvāsa</s>) and enters [the realm of] <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>' — this is the sentence-connection. 'Because of being a basis for [wrong] views' — because the <s>Mahābrahmā</s>s and those first-born [there] have the conceit of being the creator with respect to <s>Mahābrahmā</s>. 'And because of being sole creator.' What — does a Noble one not take rebirth in [the realm of] <s>Mahābrahmā</s>? For if a Noble one of great power were born there, there would be dual leadership. And through <s>karma</s> without a rival, [he would be] the chief there. Therefore it would not be without a rival. 'All intermediate stations' — having departed from the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> [realm], he traverses fourteen intermediate stations from the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> and the rest up to <s>Sudarśana</s>, and enters <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>. 'Because of never returning from where he is reborn, and from there [too]' — where he is reborn — for example, in the first <s>dhyāna</s> — from there, never returning to the Desire Realm. Likewise, because of never returning from where he is reborn, to there [again] — never again returning to the first <s>dhyāna</s>. His non-returning is complete, because of not having a second birth there. 'For this one is of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) conduct' — this one whose highest [attainment] is the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) is fond of concentration. And in the formless [realms], concentration is exceedingly peaceful. Therefore this one enters the formless [realms]. 'But the previous one is of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) conduct' — the one who was stated as

body.text: uktaḥ. [Tib. 222a] sa prajñāpriyaḥ śuddhāvāsān praviśati. aṃtarāparinirvāṇam iti vistaraḥ. naitat prati śāstrakārair niścitaṃ. na ca pratiṣiddham ato 'pratiṣedhād ūrdhvasrotaso 'kaniṣṭhaparamasya bhavāgraparamasya cāṃtarā akaniṣṭhāṃ bhavāgraṃ ca praviśya parinirvāṇaṃ yujyamānaṃ paśyāmaḥ. saṃbhavaṃ tu paśyāma ity arthaḥ. nanu cākaniṣṭhaparamo bhavāgraparama iti coktam ata āha. akaniṣṭhabhavāgraparamatvaṃ tu pareṇa gatyabhāvād akaniṣṭhebhyo bhavāgrāc cordhvaṃ gatyabhāvāt. tadyathā srotaāpannasya saptakṛtvaḥ paramatvaṃ. na hi tasya dvau trīn vā bhavān abhinirvartya parinirvāṇaṃ na saṃbhavatīti. tataḥ pareṇa tv aṣṭamaṃ bhavaṃ nābhinirvartayatīti. saptakṛtvaḥ parama ukta iti.
body.translated_text: having <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> as highest — that one, being fond of wisdom, enters the Pure Abodes. 'Intermediate <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (<s>antarāparinirvāṇa</s>)' — and so forth in detail. This has not been determined by the treatise-authors, nor has it been refuted. Therefore, because of non-refutation, we see it as reasonable that an <s>ūrdhvasrotās</s> whose highest [attainment] is <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> or the Peak of Existence, having entered <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> or the Peak of Existence, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in between. The meaning is: we see it as possible. 'But was it not stated that his highest is <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> or the Peak of Existence?' — therefore he says: 'The maximality of <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> and the Peak of Existence is because of the absence of a further destination' — because there is no destination above <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> or above the Peak of Existence. Just as the stream-enterer's maximality of seven births. For it is not the case that <s>parinirvāṇa</s> is impossible for him after accomplishing two or three existences; rather, he does not produce an eighth existence. Therefore he is stated as 'seven births at most.'

body.text: sa punaś caturvidha ity aṃtarāparinirvāyyabhāvān na paṃcavidhaḥ. ete ṣaḍ anāgāmino bhavaṃtīti. aṃtarāparinirvāyī upapadyaparinirvāyī sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī ūrdhvasrotāḥ ārūpyagaś ca. ṣaṣṭhaś caturdhābhedam avigaṇayyeti. dṛṣṭadharmaparinirvāyī. dṛṣṭajanmaparinirvāyīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'That one is again fourfold' — because of the absence of the class of intermediate <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, it is not fivefold. 'These are six [types of] non-returners' — the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in between (<s>antarāparinirvāyī</s>), the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth (<s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>), the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with exertion (<s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī</s>), the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without exertion (<s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī</s>), the one whose stream goes upward (<s>ūrdhvasrotās</s>), and the one gone to the formless [realms] (<s>ārūpyaga</s>). The sixth, disregarding the fourfold division. 'One who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmaparinirvāyī</s>)' — the meaning is: one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the visible birth.

body.text: (VI.40) katham eṣāṃ trayāṇām iti [Tib. 222b] vistaraḥ. trayo 'nāgāmina iti nirbhidya noktā ity anavabudhyamāna itaraḥ pṛcchati. ācāryo 'py arthāpattyoktā eta iti paśyan vivṛṇoti. aṃtaropapadyaparinirvāyiṇor aṃtarāparinirvāyiṇaḥ upapadyaparinirvāyiṇaś cety arthaḥ. ūrdhvasrotasaś ca tṛtīyasyeti. āśvanāśuciraparinirvāṇāt dṛṣṭāṃtatrayeṇeti. āśuparinirvāyī anāśuparinirvāyī ciraparinirvāyī ca dṛṣṭāṃtatrayeṇa yojayyitavyāḥ. tadyathā parīttaḥ śakalikāgnir abhinirvartamāna eva nirvāyāt. evaṃ prathamo ya āśuparinirvāyī. tadyathāyoguḍānāṃ vāyasphālānāṃ vādīptāgnisaṃprataptānāṃ ayoghanena hanyamānānāṃ ayaḥprapāṭikotpataty eva nirvāyāt. evaṃ dvitīyo yo 'nāśuparinirvāyī. tadyathāyoguḍānām iti pūrvavad yāvad ayaḥprapāṭikotplutya pṛthivyām apatitaiva nirvāyāt. evaṃ tṛtīyo yaś ciraparinirvāyī. etac ca sūtraṃ vistareṇa purastāl likhitam iti na punar likhyate. upapadyābhisaṃskārānabhisaṃskāraparinirvāṇād iti. upapadya parinirvāṇād abhisaṃskāreṇānabhisaṃskāreṇa parinirvāṇāt [Tib. 223a] tridhābhedān navānāgāmino bhavaṃtīti saṃbaṃdhaḥ. upapadyaparinirvāyī ya upapannamātraḥ parinirvāti. na tv abhisaṃskāreṇānabhisaṃskāreṇa vā parinirvāti. sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī tu nopapadyaiva parinirvāti. kiṃ tarhi. abhisaṃskāreṇāpratiprasrabdhasya pūrvābhisaṃskārasya sāmarthyataḥ parinirvāti. asya hi yady api vāhī mārgo 'sti abhiyogena tu parinirvāti. upapadyaparinirvāyī tu nābhiyogeneti viśeṣaḥ. anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī
body.translated_text: (VI.40) 'How are these three' — and so forth in detail. 'Three non-returners are not stated explicitly' — the other, not understanding, asks. The <s>Ācārya</s> too, seeing that these are stated by implication, explains. 'Of the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in between and the one who attains upon rebirth' — the meaning is: of the <s>antarāparinirvāyī</s> and the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>. 'And of the <s>ūrdhvasrotās</s>, the third.' 'By means of three illustrations — the swift, the not-swift, and the slow <s>parinirvāṇa</s>' — the swift attainer of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the not-swift attainer, and the slow attainer should be connected with the three illustrations. Just as a small splinter-fire would be extinguished while being produced — thus the first, who is the swift attainer of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Just as iron balls or wind-blown [sparks] — lit, heated by fire — when struck with an iron hammer, an iron splinter flies up and would be extinguished — thus the second, who is the not-swift attainer. Just as iron balls — as before, up to — an iron splinter, having leapt up and fallen to the ground, would be extinguished — thus the third, who is the slow attainer. And this <s>sūtra</s> has been previously written in full and is therefore not written again. 'Through <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth, with exertion, and without exertion' — through <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth, through <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with and without exertion — the connection is: from the threefold division, there are nine non-returners. The one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> as soon as he is reborn — but not with or without exertion. The one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with exertion does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth alone. Rather, he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> through exertion — through the power of prior effort that has not been relaxed. For this one, even though there is a continuing path, he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> through effort. The one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth [does so] without effort — this is the distinction. The one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without exertion

body.text:
punaḥ pratiprasrabdhapūrvābhisaṃskāro 'bhisaṃskāram anaṃtareṇa parinirvātīty ayam eva eṣāṃ viśeṣo 'vagaṃtavyaḥ. yathā tu sābhisaṃskārānabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyiṇāv apy upapadyaparinirvāyyākhyāṃ labhete. tathā darśayann āha. sarve hy eta upapadyaparinirvāṇād upapadyaparinirvāyiṇa iti. plutādibhedād iti. plutārdhaplutasarvacyutabhedād ity arthaḥ. sarveṣāṃ vā trayāṇām iti. aṃtaropapadyaparinirvāyyūrdhvasrotasām āśvanāśuciraparinirvāṇāt [Tib. 223b] tridhābhedaḥ. kaścid aṃtarāparinirvāyī āśuparinirvāyī bhavati. kaścid anāśuciraparinirvāyī. evam upapadyaparinirvāyī. ūrdhvasrotāś ceti. asmāc ca tridhābhedān navānāgāmino bhavaṃtīti sa eva saṃbaṃdho vācyaḥ. tadviśeṣaḥ punar iti vistaraḥ. teṣāṃ punas trayāṇām aṃtaropapadyaparinirvāyiṇoḥ ūrdhvasrotasaś ca. navānāṃ caiṣām eva pratyekaṃ tridhābhedād yathā varṇitād viśeṣaḥ. karmakleśendriyaviśeṣāt. karmaṇaḥ kleśasyendriyasya ca viśeṣād bhavati. katham ity āha. trayāṇām iti vistaraḥ. abhinirvṛttir aṃtarābhāvaḥ abhinirvṛttivedanīyasya karmaṇa upacitatvād aṃtarāparinirvāyī. upapadyavedanīyasya karmaṇa upacitatvād upapadyaparinirvāyī. aparaparyāyavedanīyasya karmaṇa upacitatvād ūrdhvaṃsrotā ity evaṃ tāvat teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ karmaviśeṣād viśeṣaḥ. mṛdumadhyādhimātrakleśasamudācāratvād yathākramam eṣām eva kleśaviśeṣād viśeṣaḥ. adhimātramadhyamṛdvindriyatvāc ca yathākramam eṣām evendriyaviśeṣād viśeṣa iti. teṣām api pratyekam ata eva yathāyogaṃ viśeṣa iti. teṣām api pratyekaṃ bhinnānāṃ navānām ity arthaḥ. ata eva karmādiviśeṣāt [Tib. 224a] yathāyogaṃ na yathākramaṃ. viśeṣo 'vagaṃtavyaḥ. katham ity āha. prathamayos trikayor iti vistaraḥ. yac cāṃtarāparinirvāyiṇāṃ trikaṃ. yac copapadyaparinirvāyiṇāṃ. tayos trikayoḥ kleśendriyaviśeṣāt. mṛdumadhyādhimātrakleśasamudācāratvāt adhimātramadhyamṛdvindriyatvāc ca. yathākramaṃ viśeṣaḥ. na tu karmaviśeṣāt. yasmāt prathamasya trikasyābhinirvṛttivedanīyaṃ karma tulyaṃ. dvitīyasya copapadyavedanīyaṃ karma tulyam iti. paścimasya trikasyāparaparyāyavedanīyakarmaviśeṣāc ca viśeṣaḥ. plutādīnāṃ hy aparaparyāyavedanīyaṃ karma bhinnam
iti. ato 'paraparyāyavedanīyakarmaviśeṣāt. kleśendriyaviśeṣāc ca. cakārānukṛṣṭatvāt viśeṣo mṛdumadhyādhimātrakleśasamudācāratvāt. adhimātramadhyamṛdvindriyatvāc ca. yathākramam ity arthaḥ. ta ete navaprakārakleśendrigatvād iti. ta ete navānāgāmino navaprakārakleśatvāt. navaprakārendriyatvāc ca. navānāgāmino bhavaṃti. karmaṇo 'grahaṇam avyapitvāt. na hi prathamayos
body.translated_text: — whose prior exertion has been relaxed — attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without [further] exertion. This very distinction among them should be understood. But as for how the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with exertion and the one without exertion also obtain the designation of 'one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth' — showing this, he says: 'For all of these [attain parinirvāṇa] upon rebirth — therefore they are all ones who attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth.' 'From the division into leaper, half-leaper, and all-station-departing' — the meaning is: from the division into leaper (<s>pluta</s>), half-leaper (<s>ardhapluta</s>), and all-station-departing (<s>sarvasthānacyuta</s>). 'Or of all three' — of the <s>antarāparinirvāyī</s>, <s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>, and <s>ūrdhvasrotās</s> — from the threefold division into swift, not-swift, and slow <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Some <s>antarāparinirvāyī</s>s are swift attainers of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; some are not-swift-and-slow attainers. Similarly, the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s> and the <s>ūrdhvasrotās</s>. And from this threefold division, there are nine non-returners — this same connection should be stated. 'The distinction among them is further' — and so forth in detail. Of those three — the <s>antarāparinirvāyī</s>, the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>, and the <s>ūrdhvasrotās</s> — and of these same nine individually, from the threefold division as described, the distinction [arises] from the distinction of <s>karma</s>, affliction, and faculty. From the distinction of <s>karma</s>, affliction, and faculty. How? — he says: 'Of the three' — and so forth in detail. Fruition — the intermediate state (<s>antarābhava</s>) — because of having accumulated <s>karma</s> to be experienced in the fruition-[birth], one is an <s>antarāparinirvāyī</s>. Because of having accumulated <s>karma</s> to be experienced upon rebirth, one is an <s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>. Because of having accumulated <s>karma</s> to be experienced in a subsequent life, one is an <s>ūrdhvasrotās</s>. Thus, first, the distinction of these three is from the distinction of <s>karma</s>. Because of operating with mild, middling, and intense afflictions respectively — the distinction of these same [three] is from the distinction of affliction. And because of having intense, middling, and mild faculties respectively — the distinction of these same [three] is from the distinction of faculty. 'Of those [nine] individually too, from the same, as applicable, the distinction [arises]' — of those same [nine] individually divided — the meaning is: of the nine. 'From the same' — from the very same distinction of <s>karma</s> and the rest. 'As applicable, not in sequence' — the distinction should be understood. How? — he says: 'Of the first two triads' — and so forth in detail. The triad of <s>antarāparinirvāyī</s>s and the triad of <s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>s — of these two triads, the distinction is from the distinction of affliction and faculty: because of operating with mild, middling, and intense afflictions, and because of having intense, middling, and mild faculties, respectively. But not from the distinction of <s>karma</s> — because the <s>karma</s> of the first triad — fruition-experienceable — is the same, and of the second — rebirth-experienceable — is the same. 'And of the last triad, the distinction is from the distinction of subsequent-life-experienceable <s>karma</s>' — for the <s>karma</s> of the leaper, half-leaper, and all-station-departing that is experienceable in subsequent lives is different. Therefore, from the distinction of subsequent-life-experienceable <s>karma</s>, and from the distinction of affliction and faculty — from the word 'and,' indicating what is drawn in — the distinction is from mild, middling, and intense affliction operating, and from intense, middling, and mild faculties, respectively — this is the meaning. 'These nine, because of the nine types of affliction and faculty' — these nine non-returners, because of nine types of affliction and because of nine types of faculty, are nine non-returners. '<s>Karma</s> is not mentioned because of non-pervasiveness' — for there is no distinction from the distinction of <s>karma</s> in the first two

body.text: trikayoḥ karmaviśeṣād [Tib. 224b] viśeṣo 'stīti. kathaṃ punar ete navaprakārakleśā bhavaṃti. iha kleśas triprakāro mṛdumadhyādhimātra iti. mṛdur aṃtarāparinirvāyiṇāṃ. madhya upapadyaparinirvāyiṇāṃ. adhimātra ūrdhvasrotasāṃ. tatra prathamo 'ntarāparinirvāyī mṛdumṛdukleśaḥ. dvitīyo mṛdumadhyakleśaḥ tṛtīyo mṛdvadhimātrakleśaḥ. upapadyaparinirvāyiṇāṃ prathama upapadyaparinirvāyī madhyamṛdukleśaḥ. dvitīyaḥ sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī madhyamadhyakleśaḥ. tṛtīyo 'nabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī madhyādhimātrakleśaḥ. ūrdhvasrotasām api pluto 'dhimātramṛdukleśaḥ ardhapluto 'dhimātramadhyakleśaḥ. sarvasthānacyuto 'dhimātrādhimātrakleśa iti. kathaṃ navaprakārendriyā bhavaṃti. tathaivendriyam api triprakāram adhimātraṃ mṛdu ceti. adhimātram aṃtārāparinirvāyiṇāṃ. madhyam upapadyaparinirvāyiṇāṃ. mṛdūrdhvasrotasāṃ. tatra prathamo 'ṃtarāparinirvāyī adhimātrādhimātrendriyaḥ. dvitīyo 'dhimātramadhyendriyaḥ. tṛtīyo 'dhimātramṛdvindriyaḥ. upapadyaparinirvāyiṇāṃ [Tib. 225a] prathamaṃ upapadyaparinirvāyī madhyādhimātrendriyaḥ. sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī madyamadhyendriyaḥ. anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyi madhyamṛdvindriyaḥ. ūrdhvasrotasām api pluto mṛdvadhimātrendriyaḥ. ardhapluto mṛdumadhyendriyaḥ. sarvasthānacyuto mṛdumṛdvindriya iti.
body.translated_text: triads. How then do these become nine types of affliction? Here, affliction is of three types: mild, middling, and intense. The mild [belongs to] the <s>antarāparinirvāyī</s>s, the middling to the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>s, and the intense to the <s>ūrdhvasrotās</s>es. Therein, the first <s>antarāparinirvāyī</s> has mild-of-the-mild affliction, the second has mild-of-the-middling affliction, the third has mild-of-the-intense affliction. Of the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>s: the first — the one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth — has middling-of-the-mild affliction; the second — the one who attains with exertion — has middling-of-the-middling affliction; the third — the one who attains without exertion — has middling-of-the-intense affliction. Of the <s>ūrdhvasrotās</s>es too: the leaper has intense-of-the-mild affliction, the half-leaper has intense-of-the-middling affliction, and the all-station-departing one has intense-of-the-intense affliction. How do they become nine types of faculty? In exactly the same way, faculty too is of three types: intense, middling, and mild. The intense [belongs to] the <s>antarāparinirvāyī</s>s, the middling to the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>s, and the mild to the <s>ūrdhvasrotās</s>es. Therein, the first <s>antarāparinirvāyī</s> has intense-of-the-intense faculty; the second has intense-of-the-middling faculty; the third has intense-of-the-mild faculty. Of the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyī</s>s: the first — the one who attains upon rebirth — has middling-of-the-intense faculty; the one who attains with exertion has middling-of-the-middling faculty; the one who attains without exertion has middling-of-the-mild faculty. Of the <s>ūrdhvasrotās</s>es too: the leaper has mild-of-the-intense faculty, the half-leaper has mild-of-the-middling faculty, and the all-station-departing one has mild-of-the-mild faculty.

body.text: (VI.41) kathaṃ tarhi sūtre sapta satpuruṣagatayo deśitā iti. sapta vo 'haṃ bhikṣavaḥ satpuruṣagatīr deśayiṣyāmi. anupādāya ca parinirvāṇam. ity etat sarvaṃ sūtraṃ gatisūtrata ity atra pradeśe likhitam iti na punar likhyate. atra ca sūtre sapta satpuruṣagatayo deśitāḥ. trayo 'ṃtarāparinirvāyiṇāḥ. traya upapadyaparinirvāyiṇa iti ṣaṭ gatayaḥ. ūrdhvaṃsroto gatiś ca saptamīti. ūrdhvasravaṇadharmeti. kṛdaṃtam etac chabdarūpam iti. vidhārtham etac chabdarūpam iti darśayati. ūrdhvam iti ca kriyāviśeṣaṇam iti. tasyābhedanirdeśād iti. tasyordhvaṃsrotasaḥ plutādibhedānirdeśād ity arthaḥ. vineyāśayāpekṣo hi sūtranirdeśaḥ. nānyāḥ śaikṣā gataya iti. na srotaāpannasakṛdāgāmigataya ity arthaḥ. gatir utpattiḥ saṃparāya ity ete sūtre paryāyā ucyaṃte. teṣām ity anāgāmināṃ. sati ca karmaṇi vṛttiḥ prāṇātipātādyakaraṇāt. asati cāvṛttir abrahmacaryādyakaraṇāt. [Tib. 225b] akuśalena hi cittenābrahmacaryādikaraṇam iti. teṣāṃ tu vītarāgāṇāṃ saty eva karmaṇi vṛttir nāsati prahīṇakuśalatvāt. na punaḥ pratyāgatir iti. yāsu gatiṣūpapannāḥ. tatratatra caiṣām atyaṃtam anāgamanam ity arthaḥ. na tv etad yathoktam anyatrāstīty. yad etat saty eva vṛttir asati cāvṛttir evāpunaḥpratyāgamanaṃ ca. tad etat
body.translated_text: (VI.41) 'How then are seven destinations of good persons taught in the <s>sūtra</s>?' — 'I shall teach you, O monks, seven destinations of good persons and <s>nirvāṇa</s> without clinging.' This entire <s>sūtra</s> has been written at the section of the destination <s>sūtra</s> — therefore it is not written again. And in this <s>sūtra</s>, seven destinations of good persons are taught — three who attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate [existence], three who attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s> upon being reborn — [making] six destinations. And the one going upward (<s>ūrdhvaṃsrotas</s>) is the seventh destination. '<s>Ūrdhvasravaṇadharma</s>' — this is a verbal form with a <s>kṛt</s> suffix. He shows that this form is for the purpose of indication. 'And "upward" qualifies the action.' 'Because of non-differentiation in the teaching of that one' — the meaning is: because of the non-differentiation of the one going upward into types such as 'leaping' and the rest. For the <s>sūtra</s> teaching is with reference to the dispositions of those to be trained. 'There are no other learner destinations' — the meaning is: there are no destinations of stream-enterers and once-returners. 'Destination, birth, future life — these are stated as synonyms in the <s>sūtra</s>.' 'Of those' — of the non-returners. 'And there is the performance of existing <s>karma</s>' — because of not performing killing and the rest. 'And non-performance of non-existing [karma]' — because of not performing unchastity and the rest. [Tib. 225b] For unchastity and the like are done with an unwholesome mind. But for those who are dispassionate, there is only the performance of existing <s>karma</s>, not the non-existing — because unwholesomeness has been abandoned. 'And they do not come back again' — to whatever destinations they are born — in each of those, their not coming back at all — this is the meaning. 'But this, as stated, does not exist elsewhere' — that which was stated — 'the performance of existing [karma] only, non-performance of non-existing, and non-return' — that

body.text: srotaāpanne sakṛdāgāmini ca nāstīti.
body.translated_text: does not exist for the stream-enterer and once-returner.

body.text: anyeṣām apīti. srotaāpannasakṛdāgaminām apīty arthaḥ. pāryāyikam iti. paryāye bhavaṃ pāryāyikaṃ. kenacit prakāreṇa bhavatīty arthaḥ. katham ity āha. paṃcavidhasya pāpasyātyaṃtamakaraṇasaṃvarapratilaṃbhād iti. paṃcavidhasya pāpasya prāṇātipātādattādānakāmamithyācāramṛṣāvādamadyapānalakṣaṇasyākaraṇenākriyayā saṃvaraḥ saṃvaraṇam. tasya pratilaṃbhāt. na hy āryā janmāṃtare 'py etat paṃcavidhaṃ pāpam adhyācaraṃti. akaraṇasaṃvaravacanaṃ. samādānasaṃvarasyānāvaśyakatvāt. prāyeṇeti. darśanagrahātavyānām akuśalānāṃ sarveṣām atyaṃtaprahāṇāt. bhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ ca kāmāvacarāṇāṃ keśāṃcit saṃbhavataḥ. yeṣām iti vistaraḥ. yeṣāṃ tu niḥparyāyeṇa na prakārāṃtareṇa srotaāpannasakṛdāgāmivat satpuruṣatvaṃ. [Tib. 226a] kiṃ tarhi. sarvasya pāpasyātyaṃtamakaraṇasaṃvarapratilaṃbhāt. sarveṣāṃ cākuśalānāṃ darśanaprahātavyānāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇāt. bhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ ca kāmāvacarāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ navaprakārāṇām api prahāṇāt. teṣāṃ satpuruṣāṇām anāgāminām iha sūtre 'dhikāraḥ. sapta satpuruṣagataya ity ato 'nyeṣāṃ pāryāyikaṃ satpuruṣatvaṃ na pratiṣidhyate.
body.translated_text: 'Of others too' — meaning: of stream-enterers and once-returners too. 'Figuratively' (<s>pāryāyika</s>) — existing by way of a figure of speech. The meaning is: it exists in a certain manner. How? He says: 'Because of the attainment of the restraint of absolute non-performance of fivefold evil.' The restraint — the restraining — through the non-performance, the non-doing, of fivefold evil characterized by killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and intoxicants — because of the attainment of that. For noble ones do not engage in this fivefold evil even in other births. The mention of 'non-performance restraint' is because the undertaking-restraint (<s>samādānasaṃvara</s>) is not obligatory [for them]. 'For the most part' — because of the absolute abandonment of all the unwholesome [dharmas] to be abandoned by seeing. And because some of the Desire-Realm [afflictions] to be abandoned by cultivation still exist. 'Of those' — and so forth in detail. Of those for whom the good-personhood is not figurative — not by another manner, like for stream-enterers and once-returners. [Tib. 226a] What then? Because of the attainment of the restraint of absolute non-performance of all evil. Because of the abandonment of all unwholesome afflictions to be abandoned by seeing. And because of the abandonment of all nine types of Desire-Realm [afflictions] to be abandoned by cultivation. For those good persons — the non-returners — this <s>sūtra</s> is the topic. Since 'seven destinations of good persons' — therefore the figurative good-personhood of the others [i.e., stream-enterers and once-returners] is not denied.

body.text: (VI.42) kiṃ punaḥ parivṛttajanmano 'py anāgāmina eśa bhedo 'sti. aṃtarāparinirvāyīty evamādikaḥ. parivṛttajanmānāgāmīyaḥ prathame janmani srotaāpattiphalaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ vā prāpya dvitīye janmany anāgāmī bhavati. kāma iti viśeṣaṇaṃ. yasmāt rūpadhātau parivṛttajanmā kadācid ārūpyān praviśatīti. tatraiva janmani parinirvāṇād iti. kāmadhātau duḥkhabahulatvenāsya tīvrasaṃvegatvāt. yat tarhīti vistaraḥ. śakreṇoktam itaś cyuto 'haṃ manuṣyeṣūpapanno yady arhattvaṃ prāpya na parinirvāmi. ye te devā akaniṣṭhā iti viśrutāḥ. aṃte me hīyamānasya tatropapattir bhaviṣyatīti. sa hi deveṣv eva srotaāpanno manuṣyāṃś cāgatya parinirvāsyāmīti vacanāt parivṛttajanmā bhavet. aṃte nikāyasabhāgāvasāne mama hīyamānasyārhattvād [Tib. 226b] aprāptiparihāṇyā parihīyamāṇasya. tatrākaniṣṭheṣūpapattir bhaviṣyatīti prārthanāvacanād dhātvaṃtaragamanam astīti darśitaṃ bhavatīti gamyate. tat kathaṃ kāmadhātau parivṛttajanmāṃtara āryo dhātvāṃtaraṃ na gacchatīty ucyata iti. sūtrārtho dṛśyate. brūyās tvaṃ. dharmalakṣaṇānabhijñatvāc chakreṇaivam uktaṃ. tasmād adoṣa iti. bhagavatā tarhy evaṃ śṛṇvatā kasmād asau na nivārito mā tvam eva voca ity ata ucyate. bhagavatāpy anivāraṇaṃ. saṃharṣaṇīyatvād iti. kāmaduḥkhaparityāgābhilāṣeṇa saṃharṣaṇīyam ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: (VI.42) 'But does this differentiation exist even for a non-returner with intervening birth (<s>parivṛttajanman</s>)?' — [the differentiation] such as 'one who attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate [existence]' and the like. A non-returner with intervening birth is one who, having obtained the fruit of stream-entry or once-returning in the first birth, becomes a non-returner in the second birth. The qualification 'Desire [Realm]' [is added] because sometimes a non-returner with intervening birth in the Form Realm enters the Formless [Realm]. 'Because of final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in that very birth' — because of his intense urgency due to the prevalence of suffering in the Desire Realm. 'But then what about' — and so forth in detail. <s>Śakra</s> stated: 'When I die from here and am reborn among humans, if I do not attain <s>Arhat</s>ship and attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s> — those gods who are known as <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> — at the end, as I decline, my rebirth will be there.' For he, having become a stream-enterer among the gods, by saying 'I shall come to humans and attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — would be one with intervening birth. 'At the end' — at the conclusion of the class-homogeneity — 'as I decline' — [Tib. 226b] as I undergo the decline of non-attainment of <s>Arhat</s>ship — 'rebirth will be there in <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>' — from this expression of aspiration, it is shown that going to another realm exists — this is understood. How then is it said that a noble one with intervening birth in the Desire Realm does not go to another realm? The <s>sūtra</s> meaning is seen. You should say: because of not comprehending the characteristics of <s>dharma</s>s, <s>Śakra</s> spoke thus — therefore there is no fault. But why was he not restrained by the Blessed One, who heard this, [saying] 'Do not speak thus'? — therefore it is said: because of not being restrained by the Blessed One either — because of deserving encouragement. The intent is: [it is] deserving of encouragement, through the desire for abandoning the suffering of desire.

body.text: cyutinimittopapattiduḥkhodvignasya saṃharṣaṇīyatvād ity ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ.
body.translated_text: Because of deserving encouragement [due to] distress at the suffering of the signs of death and rebirth — says <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s>.

body.text: indriyāṇāṃ paripakvataratvād iti. prajñādīnām indriyāṇāṃ niṣyandaphalapuṣṭiviśeṣād ity arthaḥ. āśrayaviśeṣalābhāc ca. yasmāc cāśrayaviśeṣam anupahataṃ mārgasaṃmukhībhāvānukūlaṃ pratilabhate. dṛṣyaṃte hi tīkṣṇendriyā api saṃta āśrayavaiguṇyāt guṇebhyaḥ parihīyamāṇā ity ato janmāṇtaraparivāsenendriyāṇāṃ paripakvataratvād indriyasaṃcāro nāsti. āśrayaviśeṣalābhāc ca parihāṇir nāsty anenaiva janmāṃtaraparivāsena dhātvaṃtaragamanaṃ na bhavatīti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the greater maturation of the faculties' — meaning: because of the special nourishment as outflow-fruit of the faculties such as wisdom and the rest. 'And because of obtaining a special basis' — and because one obtains a special basis — undamaged and favorable to the approach of the path. For indeed, even those with sharp faculties are seen to decline from [their] qualities because of defects of the basis. Therefore, through the sojourn in another birth, because of the greater maturation of the faculties, there is no change of faculties. And because of obtaining a special basis, there is no regression — and by this very sojourn in another birth, there is no going to another realm.

body.text: mārgasyājitatvād asaṃmukhībhāvata iti. [Tib. 227a] yasmān mārgasyājitatvād asaṃmukhībhāvaḥ. tasmāt kāraṇād avītarāgaḥ śaikṣaḥ srotaāpannaḥ sakṛdāgāmī ca nāṃtarāparinirvāyī bhavati. anuśayānāṃ ca nātimandatvāt. yasmāc cānuśayās tasya nātimandāḥ. ato nāṃtarāparinirvāyī bhavatīty ayam ācāryasya parihāraḥ. vaibhāṣikāṇāṃ kaḥ parihāra ity āha. dussamatikramatvāt kāmadhātor iti vaibhāṣikā iti. katham ity ucyate. bahu hy anena kartavyaṃ bhavati. akuśalāvyākṛtakleśaprahāṇam akuśalānāṃ kāmāvacarāṇāṃ avyākṛtānāṃ ca rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇam anena kartavyaṃ. vītarāgeṇa punaḥ śaikṣeṇāvyākṛtānām eva prahāṇam iti. dvitriśrāmaṇyaphalaprāptir iti. dve vā trīṇi vā śrāmaṇyāni phalāni prāptavyāni. sakṛdāgāminā dve śrāmaṇyaphale prāptavye. anāgāmiphalam arhattvaphalaṃ ca. srotaāpannena trīṇi sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ anāgāmiphalam arhattvaphalaṃ ca. vītarāgeṇa punar ekam evārhattvaphalaṃ prāptavyam iti. tridhātusamatikramaś cāvītarāgeṇa kartavyaḥ. vītarāgeṇa tu rūpāvītarāgeṇāṃtarāparinirvāyinā bhavatā dvidhātusamatikramaḥ [Tib. 227b] kartavya iti.
body.translated_text: 'Because the path has not been mastered — because of non-approach' — [Tib. 227a] because the path has not been mastered, there is non-approach [to <s>nirvāṇa</s>]. For this reason, a learner who has not become dispassionate — a stream-enterer and once-returner — does not attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate [existence]. 'And because the latent dispositions are not exceedingly mild' — and because his latent dispositions are not exceedingly mild — therefore he does not attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate [existence] — this is the <s>Ācārya</s>'s resolution. What is the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s' resolution? He says: 'Because the Desire Realm is difficult to transcend — [say] the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s.' How? It is said: for much must be done by him — the abandonment of unwholesome and indeterminate afflictions: the abandonment of unwholesome Desire-Realm [afflictions] and indeterminate Form and Formless Realm afflictions must be done by him. But by one who has become dispassionate, only the abandonment of the indeterminate [afflictions is needed]. 'The attainment of two or three <s>śrāmaṇya</s>-fruits' — two or three <s>śrāmaṇya</s>-fruits are to be attained. By the once-returner, two <s>śrāmaṇya</s>-fruits are to be attained — the non-returner fruit and <s>Arhat</s>ship fruit. By the stream-enterer, three — once-returner fruit, non-returner fruit, and <s>Arhat</s>ship fruit. But by one who has become dispassionate, only the one <s>Arhat</s>ship fruit is to be attained. 'And the one who has not become dispassionate must transcend the three realms. But the one who has become dispassionate — [Tib. 227b] the one going upward in the intermediate [existence] who has not become free from passion for the Form [Realm] — must transcend two realms.'

body.text: (VI.43) ākīryata iti. vyavakīryate vyatibhidyate. anāsravābhyāṃ sāsravaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ miśrīkriyata ity arthaḥ. sukhapratipadām agratvād iti. sukhāḥ pratipadaś catvāri maulāni dhyānāni.
body.translated_text: (VI.43) 'Is interspersed' (<s>ākīryate</s>) — meaning: is scattered, is interposed. The fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is mixed — the meaning is: contaminated [meditation] is mixed with uncontaminated. 'Because of being the best of the pleasant practices' — the four fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>s are pleasant practices.

children.translated_text: 'The path in the <s>dhyāna</s>s is a pleasant practice' —

body.text: vacanāt. tāsāṃ caturthaṃ dhyānam agram aṣṭāpakṣālamuktatvāt. yadā kileti. kilaśabdo vaibhāṣikamatadyotakaḥ. svamataṃ tu paścād darśayiṣyati. aśakyaṃ tu kṣaṇavyavakiraṇam iti vistareṇa dvau hi kṣaṇāv ānaṃtaryamārgasadṛśāv iti. anāsravasāsravau. tṛtīyo vimuktimārgasadṛśa ity anāsravaḥ. mṛdvindriyāḥ kleśabhīrutayā ca vyavakiraṃti. caśabdāc chuddhāvāsopapattyarthaṃ dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārārthaṃ ca vyavakiraṃti. tīkṣṇendriyās tu śuddhāvāsopattyarthaṃ
body.translated_text: from this statement. Among those, the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is the best, because of being free from the eight faults. 'When indeed' — the word <s>kila</s> indicates the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> position. His own position he will show later. 'But moment-by-moment interspersing is impossible' — and so forth in detail: 'for there are two moments similar to the uninterrupted path' — uncontaminated and contaminated. 'The third is similar to the liberation path' — uncontaminated. 'Those with mild faculties intersperse because of fear of afflictions' — and by the word 'and,' for the purpose of rebirth in the Pure Abodes (<s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>) and for the purpose of dwelling in pleasant abiding in the present life, they intersperse. 'But those with sharp faculties intersperse only for the purpose of rebirth in the Pure Abodes

body.text: dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārārtham eva ca vyavakiraṃti. na kleśabhīrutayā. teṣāṃ parihāṇyasaṃbhavāt. kathaṃ punaḥ kleśabhīrutayā aparihāṇyarthaṃ vyavakiraṃtīty āha. āsvādanāsaṃprayuktasamādhidūrīkaraṇāt aparihāṇyartham iti. phalān na parihīyeyam iti.
body.translated_text: and for the purpose of dwelling in pleasant abiding in the present life — not because of fear of afflictions.' Because regression is not possible for them. 'How then do they intersperse for the purpose of non-regression, because of fear of afflictions?' He says: 'Because of distancing from the concentration associated with tasting (<s>āsvādanāsaṃprayukta</s>) — for the purpose of non-regression.' Meaning: 'May I not regress from the fruits.'

body.text: (VI.44ab) paṃcaprakāreti vistaraḥ. mṛdvī madhyādhimātrādhimātratarā adhimātratameti. [Tib. 228a] prathamāyāṃ trīṇi cittānīti. tasya pudgalasya tāvatī śaktir ity evam upariṣṭhād api vaktavyaṃ. dvitīyāyāṃ ṣaḍ iti. anāsravaṃ sāsravam anāsravam iti trīṇi. punar anāsravaṃ sāsravam anāsravam ity aparāṇi trīṇīti ṣaḍ bhavaṃti. evam eva ca tṛtīyāyāṃ nava caturthyāṃ dvādaśa paṃcamyāṃ paṃcadaśeti yojyaṃ. tāsāṃ yathāsaṃkhyam iti. tāsāṃ vyavakīrṇabhāvanānāṃ yathākramaṃ paṃca śuddhāvāsāḥ phalaṃ. mṛdvyā bhāvanāyā avṛhāḥ phalam evaṃ yāvad adhimātratamāyā bhāvanāyā akaniṣṭhāḥ phalam iti. śraddhādīndriyādhikyād iti bhadaṃtaśrīlātamatam. śraddhādhikāyā bhāvanāyā avṛhāḥ phalaṃ. evaṃ yāvat prajñādhikāyā bhāvanāyā akaniṣṭhāḥ phalam iti.
body.translated_text: (VI.44ab) 'Fivefold' — and so forth in detail. Mild, middling, intense, more intense, and most intense. [Tib. 228a] 'In the first, three minds' — that person has that much capacity — similarly, it should be stated for the above as well. 'In the second, six' — uncontaminated, contaminated, uncontaminated — three. Again uncontaminated, contaminated, uncontaminated — another three — making six. And just so, in the third nine, in the fourth twelve, in the fifth fifteen — should be connected. 'Of those respectively' — of those interspersed cultivations, in order, the five Pure Abodes are the fruit. Of mild cultivation, <s>Avṛha</s> is the fruit; thus up to of the most intense cultivation, <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> is the fruit. 'Because of the predominance of the faculties of faith and the rest' — this is the venerable <s>Śrīlāta</s>'s view. Of cultivation predominated by faith, <s>Avṛha</s> is the fruit; thus up to of cultivation predominated by wisdom, <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> is the fruit.

body.text: (VI.44cd) yo hi kaścid anāgāmīti. śraddhādhimukto vā dṛṣṭiprāpto vā. kāyena sākṣātkaraṇam iti. cittābhāvāt kāyenaiva sākṣātkaroti. kathaṃ kāyenaivety āha. kāyāśrayotpatteḥ. evaṃ tu bhavitavyam iti svamatam ācāryasya. prāpti jñānasākṣātkriyābhyām iti. samādhikāle tadanukūlāśrayaprāptisākṣātkaraṇāt. vyutthānakāle ca tatpratisaṃvedanājñānasākṣātkaraṇāt. pratyakṣīkāro [Tib. 228b] hi sākṣātkriyeti. savijñānakāyaśāṃtipratilaṃbhāvasthāyāṃ sākṣātkriyā yujyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. savijñānakakāyaśāṃtipratilaṃbhena vā avijñānakakāyaśāṃtyavasthāyāṃ tatprāptir gamyata iti.
body.translated_text: (VI.44cd) 'Whoever is a non-returner' — whether faith-liberated (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>) or one who has attained right view (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>). 'Realization by body' (<s>kāyena sākṣātkaraṇa</s>) — because of the absence of [a separate] mind, one realizes with the body alone. How 'with the body alone'? He says: because of the arising of the body-basis. 'But it should be thus' — this is the <s>Ācārya</s>'s own view. 'Through acquisition and through the direct realization of knowledge' — at the time of concentration, because of the direct realization of attaining a basis favorable to that [concentration]. And at the time of emergence, because of the direct realization of the knowledge of experiencing that. For direct perception [Tib. 228b] is direct realization. The intent is: at the stage of attaining the pacification of the body-with-consciousness, direct realization is possible. Or: through the attainment of the pacification of the body-with-consciousness, the state of pacification of the unconscious body is understood.

body.text: aṣṭādaśa śaikṣā ity atra sūtra iti. anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir bhagavaṃtam apṛcchat. kati bhadaṃta dakṣiṇīyā iti. bhagavān āha. aṣṭādaśa gṛhapate śaikṣā navāśaikṣā dakṣiṇīyā iti. aṣṭādaśa śaikṣāḥ katame. srotaāpattiphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratipannakaḥ. srotaāpannaḥ. sakṛdāgāmiphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratipannakaḥ. sakṛdāgāmī. anāgāmiphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratipannakaḥ. anāgāmī. arhattvaphalasākṣātkrivāyai pratipannakaḥ. śraddhānusārī. dharmānusārī. śraddhādhimuktaḥ. dṛṣṭiprāptaḥ. kulaṃkulaḥ. ekavīcikaḥ. aṃtarāparinirvāyī. upapadyaparinirvāyī. sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī. anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī. ūrdhvasrotāḥ. itīme gṛhapate 'ṣṭādasa śaikṣāḥ. navāśaikṣāḥ katame. parihāṇadharmā. cetanādharmā. anurakṣaṇādharmā. sthitākaṃpyaḥ. prativedhanābhavyaḥ. akopyadharmā. [Tib. 229a] cetovimuktaḥ. prājñāvimuktaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Eighteen are learners' — here in the <s>sūtra</s>: the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'How many, Venerable One, are worthy of offerings (<s>dakṣiṇīya</s>)?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Eighteen learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and nine non-learners (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), O householder, are worthy of offerings.' What are the eighteen learners? The practitioner directed toward the direct realization of the fruit of stream-entry; the stream-enterer; the practitioner directed toward the direct realization of the fruit of once-returning; the once-returner; the practitioner directed toward the direct realization of the fruit of non-returning; the non-returner; the practitioner directed toward the direct realization of the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship; the faith-follower (<s>śraddhānusārin</s>); the <s>dharma</s>-follower (<s>dharmānusārin</s>); one liberated through faith (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>); one who has attained views (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>); a clan-to-clan (<s>kulaṃkula</s>); a one-seeder (<s>ekavīcika</s>); one who attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate [state] (<s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>); one who attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s> upon birth (<s>upapadyaparinirvāyin</s>); one who attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s> with effort (<s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>); one who attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s> without effort (<s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin</s>); one going upward (<s>ūrdhvasrotas</s>). These, O householder, are the eighteen learners. What are the nine non-learners? One of the nature of falling away (<s>parihāṇadharman</s>); one of the nature of deliberation (<s>cetanādharman</s>); one of the nature of guarding (<s>anurakṣaṇadharman</s>); one who is stable and unshakable (<s>sthitākampya</s>); one incapable of penetration (<s>prativedhanābhavya</s>); one of unshakable nature (<s>akopyadharman</s>); one liberated through mind (<s>cetovimuktaḥ</s>); one liberated through wisdom (<s>prājñāvimukta</s>);

body.text: ubhayatobhāgavimuktaḥ. itīme gṛhapate navāśaikṣā iti. tisraḥ śikṣās tatphalaṃ ceti. adhiśīlam adhicittam adhiprajñam iti tisraḥ śikṣā āryamārgalakṣaṇāḥ. tāsāṃ phalaṃ visaṃyogaḥ. tadviśeṣeṇa hi śaikṣāṇāṃ vyavasthānam iti. śikṣāviśeṣeṇa tatphalaviśeṣeṇa cety arthaḥ. kathaṃ punas tadviśeṣaḥ. anyādṛsyo 'nyādṛśyo 'ṣṭādaśānāṃ śaikṣāṇāṃ śikṣāḥ visaṃyogaphalaṃ ceti. nirodhasamāpattiś ca na śaikṣā aprahāṇamārgasvābhāvyāt. na śikṣā phalam avisaṃyogaphalasvābhāvyāt. ato na tadyogān nirodhasamāpattiyogāt śaikṣaviśeṣa uktaḥ. yathaite 'ṣṭādaśa śaikṣāḥ. na punar asau na śaikṣaḥ. tatra yad idam ucyate. aṣṭādaśa śaikṣā ity atra sūtre kiṃ kāraṇaṃ kāyasākṣī noktaḥ śaikṣa ity evaṃ noktaḥ.
body.translated_text: one liberated in both ways (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>). These, O householder, are the nine non-learners.' 'The three trainings and their fruit' — the higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>), the higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>), and the higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>) — these three trainings have the characteristic of the Noble path. Their fruit is disconnection (<s>visaṃyoga</s>). For the classification of the learners is through the distinction of those [trainings]. The meaning is: through the distinction of training and the distinction of its fruit. 'But how is there a distinction in those?' — the trainings and disconnection-fruit of the eighteen learners are each of different kinds. 'And the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) is not a training' — because of its own-nature being a non-abandonment path. 'Nor is it a fruit of training' — because of its own-nature being a non-disconnection fruit. Therefore, a distinction of learners is not stated from the connection with cessation-attainment. Just as these are eighteen learners [without counting the body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣin</s>)], it is not the case that that one is not a learner. Therein, what is said — 'in the <s>sūtra</s> stating eighteen learners, for what reason is the body-witness not stated as a learner' — thus it is not stated.

children.translated_text: 'The distinction according to gross [categories]' — five who are reborn in the Form Realm.
'Another, going to the Formless Realm, is fourfold. The other attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> here' —

body.text: ity evamādi. sūkṣmaṃ tu bhidyamānā iti vistaraḥ. atrācāryo gaṇanopāyapradarśanārthaṃ [Tib. 229b] prathamam aṃtarāparinirvāyiṇa indriyabhūmigotrādibhedaṃ vyutpādayati. kiṃ kāraṇam. tadbhede hi gaṇite yathāṃtarāparinirvāyiṇa indriyādibhedād bhedaḥ. evaṃ yāvad ūrdhvasrotasa iti sukham atideśaṃ kariṣyāmīti. bhūmibhedāś catvāra iti. te evāṃtarāparinirvāyiṇaḥ. bhūmayaś catvāri dhyānāni. rūpopagānām anāgāmināṃ vivakṣitatvāt. tatra prathame dhyāne 'ṃtarāparinirvāyī yāvac caturtha iti catvāraḥ. parihāṇadharmādigotrabhedāt ṣaḍ iti. ta eva parihāṇadharmā cetanādharmā anurakṣaṇādharmā sthitākaṃpyaḥ prativedhanābhavyaḥ akopyadharmā ceti. sthānāṃtarabhedāt ṣoḍaśeti. brahmakāyikādīny akaniṣṭhāṃtāni. mahābrahmaṇo vaibhāṣikanītyāsthānāṃtaraḥ. bahirdeśakanayenāpi sthānāṃtaratve tatrāryo notpadyata ity agaṇanaṃ. tad evaṃ sthānāṃtarabhedāt ṣoḍaśāṃtarāparinirvāyiṇaḥ. bhūmivairāgyabhedāt ṣaṭtriṃśad iti. bhūmibhedāt tadvairāgyabhedāc ca ṣaṭtriṃśad aṃtarāparinirvāyiṇaḥ. katham iti pratipādayati. rūpadhātan [Tib. 230a] sakalabandhana iti vistaraḥ. rūpadhātau prathame dhyāne sakalabandhana ekaprakāravītarāgo yāvad aṣṭaprakāravītarāga iti nava. dvitīye 'pi nava sakalabandhano yāvad aṣṭaprakāravītarāga iti. tathā tṛtīye nava. tathā caturthe naveti. catvāro navakāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśad bhavaṃti. yāvac caturthadhyānāṣṭaprakāravītarāga iti. yāvacchabdenāyam arthavistaro labhyate. caturthadhyānanavamaprakāravītarāgo nocyate. yasmād asāv ārūpye sakalabandhano bhavati. na cehārūpyago 'dhikriyate. rūpopagānām iha vivakṣitatvāt. aṃtarābhavasaṃbandhād
body.translated_text: and so forth. 'But when divided finely' — in detail. Here, the <s>Ācārya</s>, for the purpose of showing the method of enumeration, first explains the divisions of intermediate <s>nirvāṇa</s>-attainers (<s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>) by faculties, grounds, lineages, and the rest. For what reason? Because when their divisions are enumerated — just as intermediate <s>nirvāṇa</s>-attainers are divided by the distinctions of faculties and the rest — 'similarly, up to those going upward (<s>ūrdhvasrotas</s>),' he will easily make the extension. 'The divisions of ground are four' — those same intermediate <s>nirvāṇa</s>-attainers — the grounds are the four <s>dhyāna</s>s, because non-returners reborn in the Form Realm are intended. Therein, one who is an intermediate <s>nirvāṇa</s>-attainer in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, up to the fourth — thus four. 'From the division of lineage such as the nature of falling away and the rest, six' — those same [intermediate nirvāṇa-attainers divided as:] nature of falling away (<s>parihāṇadharman</s>), nature of deliberation (<s>cetanādharman</s>), nature of guarding (<s>anurakṣaṇadharman</s>), stable and unshakable (<s>sthitākampya</s>), incapable of penetration (<s>prativedhanābhavya</s>), and of unshakable nature (<s>akopyadharman</s>). 'From the division of location, sixteen' — from <s>Brahmakāyika</s> and the rest, up to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>. <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, according to the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> method, is not a [separate] location. Even according to the method of the outsiders, though it is [considered] a [separate] location, a Noble one is not born there — hence it is not counted. Thus, from the division of location, there are sixteen intermediate <s>nirvāṇa</s>-attainers. 'From the division of ground-dispassion, thirty-six' — from the division of ground and the division of dispassion from that [ground], thirty-six intermediate <s>nirvāṇa</s>-attainers. How? — he demonstrates. 'In the Form Realm, one with complete bondage' — in detail. In the Form Realm, in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, one with complete bondage, one dispassionate from one type, up to one dispassionate from eight types — thus nine. In the second too, nine — one with complete bondage, up to one dispassionate from eight types. Similarly in the third, nine. Similarly in the fourth, nine. Four times nine makes thirty-six. 'Up to one dispassionate from eight types of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>' — by the word 'up to,' this full meaning is obtained. One dispassionate from nine types of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is not stated — because that one has complete bondage in the Formless [Realm]. And here, one going to the Formless Realm is not under discussion — because those reborn in the Form Realm are intended here. 'Because of the connection with the intermediate existence'

body.text:
iti. tathā ca sati sthānāṃtaragotravairāgyendriyabhedād iti vistaraḥ. sthānāṃtarāṇāṃ gotrāṇāṃ vairāgyāṇām indriyāṇāṃ ca bhedāt. dvānavatīni dvānavatyadhikāni paṃcaviṃśatiśatāni bhavaṃti teṣām aṃtarāparinirvāyiṇāṃ. kathaṃ kṛtvā tatha bhavaṃtīty āha. ekasmiṃ sthāne. tadyathā brahmapurohite ṣaṭ gotrāṇi parihāṇadharmādibhedāt. gotragotra iti vīpsā nava pudgalāḥ. sakalabandhano yāvad aṣṭaprakāravītarāgaḥ svasmāt sthānāt. tadyathā brahmapurohitāt. [Tib. 230b] ṣaṇṇavakāni gotraṣaṭ pudgalanavakagrahaṇāc catuḥpaṃcāśat. ṣoḍaśa catuḥpaṃcāśatkāni. ṣoḍaśasthānāṃtaragrahaṇāt. catuḥṣaṣṭyādi. catuḥṣaṣṭyadhikāni aṣṭau śatāni. indriyabhedāt tu triguṇū mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedāt. ity evaṃ kṛtvā. kiṃ dvānavatīni paṃcaviṃśatiśatāni bhavaṃti. yena nyāyena sakalabandhano yāvad aṣṭaprakāravītarāga iti nava pudgalā vyavasthāpitāḥ. taṃ nyāyaṃ darśayann āhayo hy adhare dhyāna iti vistaraḥ. yo hy adhare dhyāne prathame yāvat tṛtīye navaprakāravītarāgaḥ. sa uttare dhyāne dvitīye yāvac caturthe sakalabandhana ity uktaḥ. kasmād ity āha. samagaṇanārtham iti. caturṣu dhyāneṣu navanava yathā syur iti. anyathā hi viṣamā gaṇanā syāt. prathame dhyāne daśa syuḥ sakalabandhano yāvan navaprakāravītarāga iti. dvitīye nava ekaprakāravītarāgo yāvan navaprakāravītarāga iti. evaṃ tṛtīye nava caturthe tv aṣṭau syuḥ. ekaprakāravītarāgo yāvad aṣṭaprakāravītarāga iti. navaprakāravītarāgasyārūpyasakalabandhanatvād ity uktaṃ evaṃ yāvad ūrdhvasrotasa iti. evam upapadyasābhisaṃskārānabhisaṃskārordhvasrotasām api. sthānāṃtaragotravairāgyendriyabhedāt [Tib. 231a] pratyekaṃ dvānavatīni paṃcaviṃśatiśatāni bhavaṃtīty abhisamasya punaḥ paṃcābhedāṃś catvāriṃśadūnāni trayodaśasahasrāṇy anāgāmināṃ bhavaṃti. ārūpyagais tu sahopapadyādicaturbhedabhinnair atitarāṃ bahavo bhavaṃti. anayā tu vartanyā gamyata eveti na likhyate.
(VI.45, 46)
body.translated_text:
— this being so, 'from the division of location, lineage, dispassion, and faculties' — in detail. From the divisions of locations, lineages, dispassions, and faculties — twenty-five hundred and ninety-two. Of those intermediate <s>nirvāṇa</s>-attainers. How is it that they become so? — he says. 'In one location' — for example, in <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, six lineages from the division of nature of falling away and the rest. 'Lineage by lineage' — the repetition [indicates:] nine persons — one with complete bondage, up to one dispassionate from eight types from one's own location — for example, from <s>Brahmapurohita</s>. Six times nine — from the six lineages and the nine-person grouping — makes fifty-four. Sixteen times fifty-four — from the sixteen locations — four hundred sixty-four and more. Four hundred sixty-four — and more. From the division of faculties, tripled — from the division into mild, middling, and intense. Thus having calculated: there are twenty-five hundred and ninety-two. 'By the method through which one with complete bondage up to one dispassionate from eight types — thus nine persons — are established' — he shows this method, saying: 'For one who is dispassionate from nine types in a lower <s>dhyāna</s>' — in detail. One who is dispassionate from nine types in a lower <s>dhyāna</s> — the first, up to the third — is said to have complete bondage in the upper <s>dhyāna</s> — the second, up to the fourth. Why? — he says: 'For the purpose of equal enumeration' — so that there may be nine each in the four <s>dhyāna</s>s. Otherwise, there would be an uneven count: in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, there would be ten — one with complete bondage, up to one dispassionate from nine types. In the second, nine — one dispassionate from one type, up to one dispassionate from nine types. Similarly in the third, nine. But in the fourth, there would be eight — one dispassionate from one type, up to one dispassionate from eight types — because one dispassionate from nine types has complete bondage in the Formless [Realm] — as stated. 'Similarly, up to those going upward (<s>ūrdhvasrotas</s>)' — similarly, for those who attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> upon birth, with effort, without effort, and those going upward too — from the division of location, lineage, dispassion, and faculties, each individually has twenty-five hundred and ninety-two. Then, combining the five divisions [of non-returners], there are twelve thousand nine hundred sixty minus forty — [that is,] twelve thousand nine hundred and twenty non-returners. But together with those going to the Formless Realm, divided into four divisions — those who attain [<s>nirvāṇa</s>] upon birth and the rest — [the total] becomes exceedingly many. But this method can be understood [from what has been said] — so it is not written.
(VI.45, 46)

body.text: ābhavāgrāṣṭabhāgakṣid
body.translated_text: 'The destroyer of eight types up to the Peak of Existence' (<s>ābhavāgrāṣṭabhāgakṣit</s>) —

body.text: iti. ābhavāgrād āṣṭau prakārān kṣiṇotīty ābhavāgrāṣṭabhāgakṣid ābhavāgrāṣṭaprakārakṣayakṛd ity arthaḥ. ayam anāgāmī prathamadhyānaikaprakāravairāgyāt prabhṛtīti. yasmāt kāmavairāgyād anāgāmī vyavasthāpyate. tasmāttataḥ pareṇārhattvaphalapratipannako bhavati. yathā vajraḥ sarvaṃ bhinatti. evam ayaṃ samādhiḥ sarvam anuśayaṃ bhinattīti sāmarthyāt vajra upamā asyeti vajropamaḥ. bhinnatvād asau na sarvāṃ bhinattīti. traidhātukān
body.translated_text: the meaning is: one who destroys eight types from [each ground] up to the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) — one who brings about the destruction of eight types up to the Peak of Existence. This non-returner, beginning from dispassion from one type of the first <s>dhyāna</s> — because a non-returner is established from dispassion from the Desire Realm — therefore, after that, one becomes a practitioner directed toward the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship. Just as a diamond (<s>vajra</s>) splits everything, so this concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) splits all latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>) — because of this capacity, a diamond is the simile for it — hence 'diamond-like' (<s>vajropama</s>). 'Because of being split, it does not split all [of them]' — the [afflictions] of the three realms

body.text: darśanaprahātavyān bhāvanāprahatavyāṃś ca kāmāvacarān yāvad bhāvāgrikān aṣṭau prakārān. yadi sarvān na bhinatti kasmāt sarvānuśayabhedīty ucyata ity āha. sarvāṃs tu bhettuṃ samartha iti. saṃbhavam adhikṛtyoktam ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: that are to be abandoned by seeing, and those to be abandoned by cultivation belonging to the Desire Realm, up to eight types belonging to the Peak of Existence. If it does not split all, why is it called 'the splitter of all latent dispositions'? — he says: 'But it is capable of splitting all' — the intent is: this was stated with reference to capacity.

body.text: anāgamyasaṃgṛhītā iti vistaraḥ. nava bhūmīḥ anāgamyaṃ dhyānāṃtaraṃ [Tib. 231b] catvāri dhyānāni trīṃś cārūpyān bhavāgravarjyān niśrityārhattvaprāptir ity ata evaṃ pratanyate. duḥkhasamudayānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktā aṣṭāv iti. bhāvāgrikaduḥkhālaṃbanānvayajñānākāraiś caturbhiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāro bhāvāgrikasamudayālaṃbanānvayajñānākaraiḥ caturbhir aparaiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāra ity aṣṭau. evam eva nirodhamārgadharmajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktā aṣṭāv iti vaktavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Included in the access concentration (<s>anāgamya</s>)' — in detail. Relying on nine grounds — the access concentration, the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, the four <s>dhyāna</s>s, and the three formless [attainments] excluding the Peak of Existence — the attainment of <s>arhat</s>ship [is possible] — therefore it is detailed thus. 'Associated with the aspects of the subsequent knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>) of suffering and origination, eight' — four associated with four aspects of the subsequent knowledge of suffering having the Peak of Existence as its object, and four associated with four other aspects of the subsequent knowledge of origination having the Peak of Existence as its object — thus eight. 'Similarly, associated with the aspects of the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge (<s>dharmajñāna</s>) of cessation and the path, eight should be stated' —

children.text:
dharmajñānaṃ nirodhe yan mārge vā bhāvanāpathe
tridhātupratipakṣas tad
children.translated_text:
'The <s>dharma</s>-knowledge that is of cessation or of the path, in the path of cultivation,
is the antidote of the three realms' —

body.text: iti siddhāṃtāt tayor evehopanyāso na duḥkhasamudayadharmajñānayor grahaṇaṃ. evaṃ yāvad iti. yāvacchabdena yathā prathamadhyānanirodhālaṃbanākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāraḥ. evaṃ dvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānākāśavijñānākiṃcanyāyatanabhavāgranirodhālaṃbanāḥ pratyekaṃ catvāraś catvāro vaktavyāḥ. mārgānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāra ity atra pratibhūmimārgālaṃbanānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāraḥ catvāra iti nocyate. kasmād ity āha. kṛtsnasyānvayajñānapakṣasyālaṃbanād iti. aviśiṣṭo hy anvayajñānapakṣo mārgaḥ pratipakṣabhāvenānyonyahetukaś ca mārga iti samastam evālaṃbyate. [Tib. 232a] na nirodhavad ity ataś catvāra eva mārgānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktā iti. ta ime jñānākārālaṃbanabhedabhinnā iti. jñānākārabhedenālaṃbanabhedena ca bhinnāḥ. atha vā jñānānām ākārāṇām ālaṃbanānāṃ ca tribhedena bhinnāḥ. jñānākārabhedabhinnās tāvat. duḥkhasamudayānvayajñānākārair ityevamādivacanāt. ālaṃbanabhedabhinnā api. bhāvāgrikaduḥkhasamudayālaṃbanair ityevamādivacanāt. dvāpaṃcāśad iti. ādito dvyaṣṭāv iti ṣoḍaśa. prathamadhyānanirodhālaṃbanāś catvāro yāvan mārgānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāra iti navacatuṣkāṇi ṣaṭtriṃśat. ṣoḍaśa ca ṣaṭtriṃśac ca dvāpaṃcāśad bhavaṃti. yathānāgamyasaṃgṛhīta iti vistaraḥ. maulaṃ dhyānam anāgamyapraviśyotpadyata ity anāgamyaṃ. yena prakāreṇānaṃtaroktenānāgamyasaṃgṛhītā dvāpaṃcāśad vajropamā bhavaṃti. tenaiva prakāreṇa dhyānāṃtarasaṃgṛhītā dvāpaṃcāśad bhavaṃti. kathaṃ kṛtvā. dhyānāṃtarasaṃgṛhītā bhāvāgrikaduḥkhasamudayānvayajñānākāraiḥ
body.translated_text: from this established doctrine, only those two [dharmajñānas] are presented here, not the <s>dharma</s>-knowledges of suffering and origination.
