'Similarly up to' — by the word 'up to': just as four are associated with aspects having the cessation of the first <s>dhyāna</s> as object, so four each associated with aspects having the cessation of the second, third, fourth <s>dhyāna</s>s, the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the Peak of Existence as object should be stated separately. 'Associated with the aspects of the subsequent knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>) of the path, four' — here it is not said 'four each associated with aspects of the subsequent knowledge of the path having [each] ground as its object.' Why? — he says: 'Because of taking the entire subsequent-knowledge class as object' — for the path of the subsequent-knowledge class is undifferentiated, and the path is a mutual cause of the path — therefore it takes [the path] in its entirety as object, not separately like cessation. Therefore, only four are associated with aspects of the subsequent knowledge of the path. 'These, divided by the distinction of knowledges, aspects, and objects' — divided by the distinction of knowledges, by the distinction of aspects, and by the distinction of objects. Or alternatively, divided by the threefold distinction of knowledges, aspects, and objects. First, divided by the distinction of knowledges and aspects — because of the statement 'associated with the aspects of the subsequent knowledge of suffering and origination' and so forth. Also divided by the distinction of objects — because of the statement 'having the suffering and origination of the Peak of Existence as object' and so forth. 'Are fifty-two' — initially, two groups of eight make sixteen. Four associated with aspects having the cessation of the first <s>dhyāna</s> as object, up to four associated with aspects of the subsequent knowledge of the path — nine groups of four make thirty-six. Sixteen plus thirty-six makes fifty-two. 'Just as those included in the access concentration (<s>anāgamya</s>)' — in detail. The main <s>dhyāna</s> is entered through the access concentration — hence 'access.' By the same method that has just been stated, the fifty-two diamond-like [concentrations] included in the access concentration exist — by that very method, those included in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> are also fifty-two. How? Those included in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, associated with the aspects of the subsequent knowledge of suffering and origination having the Peak of Existence as object

body.text: saṃprayuktā aṣṭau. nirodhamārgadharmajñānākāraiḥ [Tib. 232b] saṃprayuktā aṣṭau. nirodhānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāḥ prathamadhyānanirodhālaṃbanāś catvāraḥ. evaṃ yāvad bhavāgranirodhālaṃbanāś catvāraḥ. mārgānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāraḥ. kṛtsnasyānvayajñānapakṣasyālaṃbanāt. ta ime jñānākārālaṃbanabhedabhinnā dvāpaṃcāśad bhavaṃti. yathā dhyānāṃtarasaṃgṛhītā evaṃ prathamadhyānasaṃgṛhītā dvāpaṃcāśāt. yāvac caturthadhyānasaṃgṛhītā dvāpaṃcāśad iti. yathāsaṃkhyam iti vistaraḥ. ākāśānaṃtyāyatanasaṃgṛhītā aṣṭāviṃśatiḥ. vijñānānaṃtyāyatanasaṃgṛhītāś caturviṃśatiḥ. ākiṃcanyāyatanasaṃgṛhītā viṃśatiḥ. bhavāgra āryamārgo nāstīti tatsaṃgṛhītā na saṃtīti na ciṃtyaṃte. teṣu dharmajñānasyābhāvād iti. teṣv ākāśānaṃtyāyatanādiṣu dharmajñānasyābhāvāt. dharmajñānasya ṣaḍbhūmikatvāt. tasmān nirodhamārgadharmajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktā aṣṭau na bhavaṃti. adhobhūminirodhālaṃbanasya cānvayajñānasyābhāvāt. nirodhānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś caturdhyānanirodhālaṃbanāḥ ṣoḍaśa punar na bhavaṃtīty aṣṭāviṃśatir bhavaṃti. dvāpaṃcāśato 'ṣṭau ṣoḍaśa caivāpanīyeti kṛtvā. katham. ākāśānaṃtyāyatanasaṃgṛhītā bhāvāgrikaduḥkhasamudayānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktā aṣṭau. nirodhānvayajñānākāraiḥ [Tib. 233a] saṃprayuktā ākāśānaṃtyāyatanādinirodhālaṃbanāḥ ṣoḍaśa. mārgānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāra iti. ta ime jñānākārālaṃbanabhedabhinnā aṣṭāviṃśatir bhavaṃti. evaṃ vijñānānaṃtyāyatananirodhālaṃbanāś caturo 'panīya caturviṃśatir yojyāḥ. ākiṃcanyāyatanasaṃgṛhītā vijñānānaṃtyāyatananirodhālaṃbanān apy aparān apanīya viṃśatir iti. kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ svabhūmyūrdhvabhūmikanirodham evālaṃbaṃta ārūpyā nādhobhūmikaṃ dhyānavat. na hy adhobhūmikaṃ duḥkham anālaṃbya tannirodhaḥ śakyam ālaṃbituṃ. duḥkhaṃ ca sarvaṃ sāsravam eva. eṣa ca niyamaḥ.
body.translated_text: associated with the aspects of the <s>dharmajñāna</s> of [suffering and origination] — eight. Associated with the aspects of the <s>dharmajñāna</s> of cessation and path — eight. Associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of cessation — those having the cessation of the first <s>dhyāna</s> as object — four. Similarly, up to those having the cessation of the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) as object — four. Associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path — four, because of taking the entire <s>anvayajñāna</s> class as object. These, differentiated by distinctions of knowledge, aspect, and object, become fifty-two. Just as those included in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, so those included in the first <s>dhyāna</s> are fifty-two, up to those included in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> are fifty-two. 'Respectively' — and so forth in detail. Those included in the Infinity of Space sphere (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>) are twenty-eight. Those included in the Infinity of Consciousness sphere (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>) are twenty-four. Those included in the Nothingness sphere (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>) are twenty. Since there is no noble path in the Peak of Existence, those included therein do not exist and are not considered. 'Because of the absence of <s>dharmajñāna</s> in those' — because of the absence of <s>dharmajñāna</s> in those [spheres] such as the Infinity of Space and the rest, since <s>dharmajñāna</s> belongs to [only] six grounds. Therefore, those associated with the aspects of the <s>dharmajñāna</s> of cessation and path — eight — do not exist. And because of the absence of <s>anvayajñāna</s> having the cessation of a lower ground as object — those associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of cessation having the cessation of the four <s>dhyāna</s>s as object — sixteen — again do not exist. Thus there are twenty-eight — having removed eight and sixteen from fifty-two. How? Those included in the Infinity of Space sphere — associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of suffering and origination of the Peak of Existence — eight. Associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of cessation — those having the cessation of the Infinity of Space sphere and the rest as object — sixteen. Associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path — four. These, differentiated by distinctions of knowledge, aspect, and object, become twenty-eight. Similarly, for the Infinity of Consciousness sphere — having removed four [for] the cessation of the Infinity of Space as object — twenty-four should be formulated. Those included in the Nothingness sphere — having removed another four [for] the cessation of the Infinity of Consciousness as object as well — twenty. But what is the reason that the formless [attainments] take only the cessation of their own ground and higher grounds as object, not of lower grounds — unlike the <s>dhyāna</s>s? For one cannot take the cessation of a lower ground as object without taking as object the suffering of that lower ground. And all suffering is exclusively contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>). And this is the restriction:

children.translated_text: 'The main wholesome formless [attainments] do not have a contaminated lower [ground] as their domain' —

body.text: ity etat kāraṇaṃ. dhyānānāṃ tu samastālocanatvān na pratiṣedhaḥ. vakṣyati hi
body.translated_text: this is the reason. But for the <s>dhyāna</s>s, because of their capacity for complete survey, there is no prohibition. For he will say:

body.text: iti. atha kasmān nirodham evālaṃbaṃte na punar duḥkhaṃ samudayaṃ vā. bhavāgrād adhobhūmer vītarāgatvāt. tasya hi bhāvāgrika eva navamaḥ prakāro vajropamavadhyo 'vaśiṣṭa iti. adhobhūmipratipakṣālaṃbanaṃ tu bhavatīti anvayajñānam adhikṛtaṃ. tac ca vajropamasamādhisaṃprayuktaṃ veditavyaṃ. tasya pratipakṣasya anyonyahetutvād iti
body.translated_text: thus. But why do they take only cessation as object and not suffering or origination? Because of freedom from passion toward the grounds below the Peak of Existence. For that [practitioner at the Peak of Existence] has only the ninth type belonging to the Peak of Existence remaining, to be destroyed by the diamond-like [samādhi]. But taking the antidote of a lower ground as object does occur — the <s>anvayajñāna</s> is the topic here. And that should be understood as associated with the diamond-like concentration (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>). Because of the mutual causality of that antidote —

body.text: Tib. 233b
anyonyaṃ navabhūmis tu mārgaḥ samaviśiṣṭayor
body.translated_text: 'But the path of nine grounds is mutual for those of equal and superior [faculties]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. sarvaṃ hi mārgānvayajñānaṃ navabhūmikānvayajñānapakṣālaṃbanam iti.
body.translated_text: from this statement. For all <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path takes the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class of nine grounds as its object.

body.text: yeṣāṃ tv iti vistaraḥ. yeṣām ābhidhārmikānāṃ mārgānvayajñānam api na kevalanirodhānvayajñānam ekaikabhūmipratipakṣālaṃbanam iṣṭaṃ. teṣām aṣṭāviṃśatim adhikān prakṣipya anāgamyasaṃgṛhītā aśītir vajropamā bhavaṃti. kathaṃ kṛtvā. pūrvakāḥ kṛtsnasyānvayajñānapakṣyasyālaṃbanā mārgānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāraḥ. idānīm ekīyamatenaikaikabhūmipratipakṣālaṃbanā api vyavasthāpyaṃte. anāgamyasaṃgṛhītāḥ prathamadhyānapratipakṣālaṃbanā mārgānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāraḥ. evaṃ yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanapratipakṣālaṃbanā mārgānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāra ity evam aṣṭāviṃśatir adhikā bhavaṃti. evam aṣṭāviṃśatim adhikān prakṣipya dvāpaṃcāśad aśītir bhavaṃti. kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ bhavāgrapratipakṣālaṃbanā mārgānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāro na gaṇyaṃte. āha. na bhavāgrasaṃgṛhīto 'nāsravo mārgo bhavāgrapratipakṣo 'sti. prathamadhyānabhūmikas tv asti. yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmika iti. tasmāt tadbhūmipratipakṣālaṃbanā evoktāḥ. na bhavāgrapratipakṣālaṃbanā iti. apare punar vyācakṣate. yeṣāṃ tu mārgānvayajñānam apy ekaikabhūmipratipakṣālaṃbanam [Tib. 234a] iṣṭaṃ. yathā nirodhānvayajñānam iṣṭam ity abhiprāyaḥ. teṣāṃ bhāvāgrikaduḥkhasamudayānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktā aṣṭau. nirodhamārgadharmajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktā aṣṭau. nirodhānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāḥ prathaṃadhyānanirodhālaṃbanāś catvāraḥ. evaṃ yāvad bhavāgranirodhālaṃbanāś catvāra iti dvātriṃśad bhavaṃti. evaṃ mārgānvayajñānākārair api saṃprayuktās tathaiva dvātriṃśad iti kṛtvā. aṣṭāviṃśatim adhikān prakṣipyānāmyasaṃgṛhītā aśītir vajropamā bhavaṃtīti. teṣāṃ hi ye hi kṛtsnasyānvayajñānapakṣasyālaṃbanān mārgānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāś catvāras te na saṃti. bhavāgrapratipakṣālaṃbanās tu tatsthāne bhavaṃtīty ato aśītir vajropamā bhavaṃtīti. evaṃ yāvac caturthadhyānasaṃgṛhītāḥ katham. aṣṭāviṃśatim adhikān prakṣipya dhyānāṃtarasaṃgṛhītā aśītir vajropamā bhavaṃti. yathā dhyānāṃtarasaṃgṛhītāḥ. evaṃ prathamadvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānasaṃgṛhītā pratidhyānam aśītir vajropamā bhavaṃti. ākāśānaṃtyāyatanādiṣv iti. bhavāgravarjyeṣu triṣv ārūpyeṣu yathākramaṃ catvāriṃśat dvātriṃśac caturviṃśatiś ca bhavaṃti. kathaṃ kṛtvā. [Tib. 234b] ākāśānaṃtyāyatane tāvad aṣṭāviṃśatyāṃ vajropameṣv ākāśānaṃtyāyatanapratipakṣālaṃbanān
body.translated_text: 'But for those' — and so forth in detail. For those <s>Ābhidharmikas</s> for whom the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path too — not merely the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of cessation — is accepted as having the antidote of each individual ground as its object, for them, adding twenty-eight additional [types], those included in the access concentration (<s>anāgamya</s>) become eighty diamond-like [samādhis]. How so? Previously, those associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path, taking the entire <s>anvayajñāna</s> class as object, were four. Now, according to the view of some, those having the antidote of each individual ground as object are also established. Those included in the access concentration, associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path having the antidote of the first <s>dhyāna</s> as object — four. Similarly, up to those having the antidote of the Nothingness sphere as object, associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path — four. Thus there are twenty-eight additional. Adding these twenty-eight additional to fifty-two, there are eighty diamond-like [samādhis]. But what is the reason that those associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path having the antidote of the Peak of Existence as object — four — are not counted? He says: there is no uncontaminated path included in the Peak of Existence that is the antidote of the Peak of Existence. But there is one belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, up to one belonging to the Nothingness sphere ground. Therefore, only those having the antidote of those grounds as object are stated, not those having the antidote of the Peak of Existence as object. But others explain: for those for whom the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path too is accepted as having the antidote of each individual ground as object — just as the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of cessation is accepted — this is the intent. For them: associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of suffering and origination of the Peak of Existence — eight. Associated with the aspects of the <s>dharmajñāna</s> of cessation and path — eight. Associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of cessation, having the cessation of the first <s>dhyāna</s> as object — four, up to those having the cessation of the Peak of Existence as object — four — thus thirty-two. Similarly, associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path — also thirty-two. Adding twenty-eight additional, those included in the access concentration become eighty diamond-like [samādhis]. For those, the four associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path taking the entire <s>anvayajñāna</s> class as object do not exist. But those having the antidote of the Peak of Existence as object come in their place — therefore there are eighty diamond-like [samādhis]. Similarly, up to those included in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> — how? Adding twenty-eight additional, those included in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> become eighty diamond-like [samādhis]. Just as those included in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, so those included in the first, second, third, and fourth <s>dhyāna</s>s — per <s>dhyāna</s>, there are eighty diamond-like [samādhis]. 'In the Infinity of Space and the rest' — in the three formless [spheres] excluding the Peak of Existence, respectively there are forty, thirty-two, and twenty-four. How so? In the Infinity of Space sphere first — in the twenty-eight diamond-like [samādhis], adding four associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path having the antidote of the Infinity of Space sphere as object, up to four having the antidote of the Nothingness sphere as object —

body.text: mārgānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktāṃś caturaḥ prakṣipya yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanapratipakṣālaṃbanāṃś catura iti. dvādaśa prakṣipya catvāriṃśad bhavaṃti. evaṃ caturviṃśatyāṃ vijñānāyatanapratipakṣālaṃbanāṃś caturaḥ prakṣipyākiṃcanyāyatanapratipakṣālaṃbanāṃś caturaḥ prakṣipya dvātriṃśad bhavaṃti. evaṃ viṃśatyām ākiṃcanyāyatanapratipakṣālaṃbanāṃś caturaḥ prakṣipya caturviṃśatir bhavaṃti. āha. nanv apadiṣṭam adhobhūmipratipakṣālaṃbanaṃ tu bhavati. tasyānyonyahetutvād iti. atha kasmāt svabhūmyūrdhvabhūmipratipakṣālambanā evoktā ākāśānaṃtyāyatanādisaṃgṛhītāḥ. nādhobhūmipratipakṣālaṃbanā iti. atrocyate. aviśeṣya navabhūmikam anvayajñānapakṣaṃ mārgam adhobhūmipratipakṣālaṃbanaṃ bhavatīty uktaṃ. na punar ākāśānantyāyatanādisaṃgṛhītasyādhobhūmipratipakṣālaṃbanaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. svabhūmyūrdhvabhūmikapratipakṣālaṃbanaṃ eva. tatrāviśeṣarūpeṇādharālaṃbanam anvayajñānaṃ bhavati. na viśeṣasvarūpeṇa. svabhūmyūrdhvabhūmyālaṃbanaṃ tu viśeṣarūpeṇāpi bhavatīti. eṣa tu pūrvako vaibhāṣikāṇāṃ sthāpanāpakṣaḥ. sāmānyarūpeṇaiva sarvam anvayajñānapakṣam ālaṃbate 'nvayajñānam iti. [Tib. 235a] tathā hy ācāryasaṃghabhadreṇoktaṃ. sarvaṃ hi mārgānvayajñānaṃ navabhūmikānvayajñānapakṣālaṃbanam iti. apare tv evaṃ vyācakṣate. bhāvāgrikaduḥkhasamudayānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktā aṣṭāu. nirodhānvayajñānākāraiḥ saṃprayuktā ākāśānaṃtyāyatananirodhālaṃbanāś catvāraḥ. evaṃ yāvad bhāvāgrikanirodhālaṃbanāś catvāra iti ṣoḍaśa. mārgānvayajñanākārair api saṃprayuktā ākāśānaṃtyāyatanapratipakṣālaṃbanāś catvāraḥ. evaṃ yāvad bhavāgrapratipakṣālaṃbanāś catvāra iti ṣoḍaśa. ta ete dviṣoḍaśa pūrvoktāś cāṣṭāv iti. catvāriṃśad ākāśānaṃtyāyatanasaṃgṛhītā vajropamā bhavaṃti. vijñānānaṃtyāyatahasaṃgṛhītā dvātriṃśat. ākāśānaṃtyāyatananirodhapratipakṣālaṃbanān aṣṭāvapanīyeti. ākiṃcanyātanasaṃgṛhītāś caturviṃśatiḥ. vijñānānaṃtyāyatananirodhapratipakṣālaṃbanān apy aparān aṣṭāv apanīyeti. bhavāgrasyāpi hi te 'dhobhūmikaṃ pratipakṣamārgam ācakṣata iti.
body.translated_text: adding twelve, there are forty. Similarly, in the twenty-four [of the Infinity of Consciousness sphere], adding four having the antidote of the Infinity of Consciousness sphere as object and four having the antidote of the Nothingness sphere as object — adding eight — there are thirty-two. Similarly, in the twenty [of the Nothingness sphere], adding four having the antidote of the Nothingness sphere as object, there are twenty-four. He says: but was it not stated that 'taking the antidote of a lower ground as object does occur, because of mutual causality'? Then why are only those having the antidote of their own ground and higher grounds as object stated for those included in the Infinity of Space sphere and the rest, not those having the antidote of a lower ground as object? To this it is said: without distinguishing, it was stated that <s>anvayajñāna</s> taking the path of nine grounds as the antidote of a lower ground as object occurs. But it is not [stated] that what is included in the Infinity of Space sphere and the rest takes the antidote of a lower ground as object. Rather, only the antidote of its own ground and higher grounds as object. Therein, the <s>anvayajñāna</s> having a lower [ground] as object occurs in an undifferentiated form, not in a specific form. But having its own ground and higher ground as object occurs in a specific form as well. But this is the former <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> position of establishment — that <s>anvayajñāna</s> takes the entire <s>anvayajñāna</s> class as object only in a general form. For thus <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> said: 'For all <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path takes the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class of nine grounds as its object.' But others explain thus: associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of suffering and origination of the Peak of Existence — eight. Associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of cessation, having the cessation of the Infinity of Space sphere as object — four, up to those having the cessation of the Peak of Existence as object — four — thus sixteen. Associated with the aspects of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> of the path, having the antidote of the Infinity of Space sphere as object — four, up to those having the antidote of the Peak of Existence as object — four — thus sixteen. These two sixteens and the previously stated eight — forty diamond-like [samādhis] included in the Infinity of Space sphere. Those included in the Infinity of Consciousness sphere are thirty-two — having removed eight for the cessation and antidote of the Infinity of Space sphere as object. Those included in the Nothingness sphere are twenty-four — having removed another eight for the cessation and antidote of the Infinity of Consciousness sphere as object as well. For they hold that the Peak of Existence too has a path of a lower ground as its antidote.

body.text: punar gotrendriyabhedād bhūyāṃso bhavaṃtīti. kathaṃ. ye tāvad aṣṭau sarvaprathamā uktāḥ. teṣāṃ. yo bhāvāgrikaduḥkhālaṃbano 'nityākārasaṃprayukto [Tib. 235b] vajropamaḥ. tasya ṣaḍgotrabhedāt ṣoḍhābhedaḥ. evaṃ duḥkhādyākārasaṃprayuktānāṃ trayāṇāṃ pratyekaṃ ṣoḍhābhedaḥ. teṣām
body.translated_text: Furthermore, from the distinction of lineage (<s>gotra</s>) and faculty (<s>indriya</s>), they become more numerous. How? First, of the eight that were stated first, whichever diamond-like [samādhi] has the suffering of the Peak of Existence as object and is associated with the aspect of impermanence — that one has a sixfold division from the distinction of six lineages. Similarly, those associated with the aspects of suffering and the rest — of [each of] the three, there is a sixfold division individually. Of those

body.text: api pratyekaṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātrendriyabhedād bhedaḥ. yathā caiṣāṃ pratyekaṃ gotrendriyabhedāḥ. evaṃ bhāvāgrikasamudayālaṃbanānāṃ caturṇāṃ pratyekaṃ ṣaḍgotrabhedāt ṣoḍhābhedaḥ. indriyabhedāc ca tridhābhedaḥ. yathā caiṣām aṣṭānāṃ gotrendriyabhedāt pratyekaṃ ṣoḍhā tridhā ca bhedaḥ. evaṃ sarveṣām anāgāmyasaṃgṛhītānāṃ jñānākārālaṃbanabhedabhinnānāṃ yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanasaṃgṛhītānāṃ gotrendriyabhedād bhedaḥ. anayā vartanyā yojyaḥ. evaṃ vā yojyaḥ. prathame pakṣe dvāpaṃcāśad anāgāmyasaṃgṛhītāḥ. yāvad viṃśatir ākiṃcanyāyatanasaṃgṛhītā ity abhisamasya caturaśītir uttarāṇi trīṇi śatāni vajropamānāṃ bhavaṃti. tāni ṣaḍguṇīkṛtya triguṇīkṛtya ca ṣaṭsahasrāṇi navaśatāni dvādaśottarāṇi bhavaṃti. dvitīyapakṣe yatrādito 'śītiḥ. yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatane caturviṃśatir iti. ekapiṇḍataḥ ṣaṭsaptatyuttarāṇi paṃcaśatāni bhavaṃti. gotrendriyabhedāt ṣaṭguṇīkṛtya triguṇīkṛtya ca. daśasahasrāṇi aṣṭaṣaṣṭyuttarāṇi ca trīṇi śatāni vajropamānāṃ [Tib. 236a] bhavaṃtīti.
body.translated_text: too, individually, there is a division from the distinction of dull, middling, and sharp faculties. Just as for each of these there are distinctions of lineage and faculty, so too for the four having the origination of the Peak of Existence as object — individually, there is a sixfold division from the distinction of six lineages, and a threefold division from the distinction of faculties. Just as for these eight there is a sixfold and threefold division individually from the distinction of lineage and faculty, so too for all [diamond-like samādhis] included in the access concentration, differentiated by distinctions of knowledge, aspect, and object, up to those included in the Nothingness sphere — from the distinction of lineage and faculty, there is a division. This should be formulated according to this method. Or it should be formulated thus: in the first position, those included in the access concentration are fifty-two, up to those included in the Nothingness sphere are twenty — combining [all of] these, there are three hundred and eighty-four diamond-like [samādhis]. Multiplying those by six and by three — there become six thousand nine hundred and twelve. In the second position, where initially there are eighty, up to in the Nothingness sphere twenty-four — in a single total, there are five hundred and seventy-six. From the distinction of lineage and faculty, multiplying by six and by three, there become ten thousand three hundred and sixty-eight diamond-like [samādhis].

body.text: ata eva tat kṣayajñānam iti. kuta ity āha. sarvāsravakṣayaprāptisahajatvāt prathamata iti. yasmāt sarvāsravakṣayaprāptyā saha jātaṃ tatprathamato jñānaṃ. tasmāt kṣayajñānam ity ucyate. madhyapadalopāt. nairuktividhānato vā. sarvagrahaṇaṃ srotaāpannādijñānaviśeṣaṇārthaṃ. prathamatograhaṇam anutpādajñānādiviśeṣaṇārthaṃ. saṃketāpekṣayā hiśabdapravṛttiḥ. ata eva sa iti. svarthaparisamāpteḥ. sa parārthakaraṇārhattvād arhan. parārthakaraṇayogyatvād ity arthaḥ. sarvasarāgapūjārhattvāc ceti. sarāgāḥ pṛthagjanaśaikṣāḥ teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pūjām arhatīty arhan. siddhaṃ bhavatīti. kiṃ siddhaṃ bhavatīty āha. anye sapta pūrvoktāḥ pudgalāḥ śaikṣā iti. trayaḥ phalasthāś catvāraś ca pratipannakā uktāḥ. asāv evāśaikṣa ity avadhāraṇād etadanye āryāḥ śaikṣā iti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: For this very reason, that is the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>). Whence? — he says: 'because of being born simultaneously with the attainment of the destruction of all outflows, it is the first [such knowledge].' Since that knowledge born simultaneously with the attainment of the destruction of all outflows is the first — therefore it is called the knowledge of destruction. By the elision of the middle word. Or by the etymological method. The word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) is for the purpose of distinguishing from the knowledge of the stream-enterer and the rest. The word 'first' is for the purpose of distinguishing from the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>) and the rest. For the operation of words depends on convention. 'For this very reason, he' — because of the completion of his own purpose. He, being worthy (<s>arhat</s>) of benefiting others, is an <s>arhat</s>. The meaning is: because of being fit for benefiting others. 'And because of being worthy of the worship of all those with passion' — those with passion (<s>sarāga</s>) are ordinary persons and learners; he is worthy of the worship of all of them — therefore [he is called] an <s>arhat</s>. 'It is established' — what is established? — he says: the other seven previously stated persons are learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>). Three who abide in fruit and four who are practitioners have been stated. Because of the determination 'that one alone is a non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>),' it is established that the other Noble ones are learners.

body.text: kena te śaikṣā iti. kena kāraṇena te sapta pudgalāḥ śaikṣā ity ucyaṃta ity āha. āsravakṣayāya nityaṃ śikṣaṇaśīlatvād iti. śikṣā śīlam eṣām iti śaikṣāḥ. śīlaṃ. chattrādibhyo ṇa iti lakṣaṇāt. kva śikṣaṇaśīlāḥ. śikṣātraye. [Tib. 236b] kiṃ śikṣātrayam. adhiśīlam adhicittam adhiprajñaṃ ca. kiṃsvabhāvās tā ity āha. tāḥ punaḥ śīlasamādhiprajñāsvabhāvā iti. śīle śīkṣā adhiśīlam evaṃ yāvat prajñāyāṃ śikṣety adhiprajñam iti. avyayaṃ vibhaktāv ity avyayībhāvasamāsaḥ. śikṣākriyāṇāṃ tv avyatirekāc chīlādisvabhāvāḥ śikṣā iti vyācaṣṭe. pṛthagjano 'pi śaikṣaḥ prāpnotīti. pṛthagjano 'pi vinayoktāsu śikṣāsu śikṣata iti. na. yathābhūtaṃsatyāprajñānāt. naitad evaṃ. kasmāt. yathābhūtaṃ satyānāṃ duḥkhādīnāṃ aprajñānād anavabodhāt. tad dhi bhikṣavo
body.translated_text: 'Why are they learners?' — by what reason are those seven persons called learners? — he says: 'because of having the disposition of always training for the destruction of outflows.' Training (<s>śikṣā</s>) is their disposition (<s>śīla</s>) — hence 'learners.' '<s>Śīla</s>' — from the rule 'after <s>chattra</s> and the rest, the suffix <s>ṇa</s>.' Where do they have the disposition of training? In the threefold training. What is the threefold training? The higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>), the higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>), and the higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>). What is their own-nature? — he says: 'those are of the nature of morality, concentration, and wisdom.' Training in morality is the higher morality; similarly, up to training in wisdom is the higher wisdom. 'An indeclinable in a case-form' — an <s>avyayībhāva</s> compound. But because the training-activities are not different from [morality and the rest], he explains that morality and the rest are the own-nature of the trainings. 'Does not even an ordinary person attain [the status of] learner?' — for an ordinary person too trains in the trainings stated in the <s>Vinaya</s>. No — because of not knowing the truths as they truly are. This is not so. Why? Because of not knowing — not understanding — the truths such as suffering and the rest as they truly are. For thus, O monks

body.text: dṛṣṭaṃ yad āryayā prajñayeti vacanāt. tathā hi sūtre adhiśīlam adhicittaṃ vā śikṣāṃ vistareṇoktvāha. adhiprajñaṃ śikṣā katamā. idaṃ duḥkham āryasatyam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ. ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ. iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam iti. yathābhūtasatyaprajñānāt. yatra ca śikṣitāḥ śīlādiṣu. tatra punar aparaśikṣaṇāt. prātimokṣasaṃvaraparityāgataḥ uṣmagatādiparihāṇitaś cāryaḥ punar yady api kiṃcit parityajati. na tu sarvaṃ. [Tib. 237a] na hy āryasya kadācid api śikṣātrayaṃ nāstīti. prakṛtistha ārya iti. asamāhitāvasthā sattvānāṃ prakṛtiḥ. tatrastha āryaḥ piṇḍapātacārādigataḥ. na śikṣaṇaśīla iti. na śaikṣaḥ syād ity abhiprāyaḥ. āśayata iti chandataḥ. sthitādhvagavat. adhvaga ucyate yo 'dhvānaṃ gacchati. saṃsthito 'py adhvaga ity ucyate. gamanāśasyāparityāgāt. tadvat. prāptyanuṣaṃgataś ca. śīlasamādhiprajñānāṃ ca prāptayaḥ prakṛtisthasyāpy anuṣajyaṃte. tasmāt prakṛtistho 'pi nāśikṣaṇaśīla eveti.
body.translated_text: 'it is seen that by Noble wisdom' — from this statement. For thus in the <s>sūtra</s>, having stated in detail the higher morality and the higher mind as training, he says: 'What is the training in higher wisdom? He knows as it truly is: "this is the noble truth of suffering, this is the noble truth of the origin of suffering, this is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, this is the noble truth of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering."' Because of knowing the truths as they truly are. And where they have trained — in morality and the rest — they train again further. Because a Noble one, even if he relinquishes the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint or falls away from the heat stage and the rest, still relinquishes something — but not everything. For a Noble one never lacks the threefold training. 'A Noble one in the natural state' — the natural state of beings is the non-concentrated state. A Noble one in that state — one who has gone on alms-round and the like — [one might say] does not have the disposition of training — hence would not be a learner. This is the intent. 'Because of intention' — because of desire. 'Like a traveler who has stopped.' One who travels a road is called a traveler. Even one who has stopped is called a traveler — because of not having abandoned the desire to travel. Likewise. 'And because of the connection with acquisition' — for the acquisitions of morality, concentration, and wisdom are connected even with one in the natural state. Therefore, even one in the natural state does not lack the disposition of training.

body.text: śaikṣāśaikṣanirdeśapraśaṃgenedam ucyate. atha śaikṣā dharmāḥ katamā ityādi. śaikṣasyānāsravā dharmāḥ saṃskṛtasvabhāvāḥ. evam aśaikṣasyāśaikṣā dharmāḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Learner and non-learner designation' — this is said by way of a digression on that topic. Now, what are learner <s>dharma</s>s? — and so forth. The uncontaminated <s>dharma</s>s of a learner — of conditioned nature — are [learner dharmas]. Similarly, the non-learner <s>dharma</s>s of a non-learner.

body.text: nirvāṇaṃ kasmān na śaikṣaṃ. yac chaikṣeṇa prāptam ity abhiprāyaḥ. aśaikṣapṛthagjanayor api tadyogād iti. pṛthagjano 'pi laukikamārgaprāptena nirvāṇena yujyate.
body.translated_text: 'Why is <s>nirvāṇa</s> not a learner [dharma]?' — the intent is: that which has been attained by a learner. Because of the connection of the non-learner and the ordinary person too with it — an ordinary person too is connected with <s>nirvāṇa</s> attained through the mundane path.

body.text: prathamaḥ pratipannaka iti. darśanamārgasthaḥ. śeṣāṇām iti vistaraḥ. śeṣāṇāṃ pratipannakānāṃ sakṛdāgāmyanāgāmyarhattvaphalapratipannakānāṃ triphalasthāvyatirekāt. [Tib. 237b] srotaāpattisakṛdāgāmyanāgāmiphalasthebhyo 'vyatirekāt. sakṛdāgāmipratipannakādayaḥ srotaāpannādibhyo nānya ity arthaḥ. anupūrvādhigamaṃ praty evam ucyata iti. anupūrveṇa catuḥphalaprāptiṃ praty ucyate. dravyata paṃceti. bhūgaḥkāmavītarāgau tu syātāṃ. bhūyovītarāgaḥ kṣīṇaṣaṭprakāraḥ. kāmavītarāgaḥ kṣīṇanavaprakāraḥ. darśanamārge darśanamārgāvasthāyāṃ yathākramaṃ sakṛdāgāmyanāgāmiphalapratipannakau syātāṃ. na ca srotaāpannasakṛdāgāminau. kiṃ tarhi. tadvyatiriktau. tathā ca sati dravyataḥ sapta bhavaṃti. srotaāpattisakṛdāgāmyanāgāmiphalapratipannakās trayaś catvāraś ca phalasthā ity arhattvaphalapratipannaka eko 'nāgāmiphalasthān na vyatirikta ity avagaṃtavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'The first practitioner' — one on the path of seeing. 'Of the remaining' — and so forth in detail. Of the remaining practitioners — those directed toward the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and <s>arhat</s>ship — because of non-difference from the three fruit-abiders, because of non-difference from the stream-enterer, once-returner, and non-returner fruit-abiders. The meaning is: the practitioners directed toward once-returning and the rest are not different from the stream-enterer and the rest. 'This is said with respect to sequential attainment' — it is said with respect to the sequential attainment of the four fruits. 'In substance, five' — the greatly dispassionate one and the one dispassionate from the Desire Realm — these two would be [additional]. The greatly dispassionate one has destroyed six types; the one dispassionate from the Desire Realm has destroyed nine types. In the path of seeing — in the state of the path of seeing — they would respectively be practitioners directed toward the fruits of once-returning and non-returning. And they are not stream-enterers or once-returners. What then? They are different from those. This being so, in substance there are seven. The stream-enterer, the once-returner, and non-returner fruit-abiders are three; the four practitioners are: the practitioner directed toward stream-entry, and these [two], and the practitioner directed toward <s>arhat</s>ship makes one — the practitioner directed toward <s>arhat</s>ship is not different from the non-returner fruit-abider — this should be understood.

body.text: (VI.47ab) dvividho hi bhāvanāmārga ukta iti.
body.translated_text: (VI.47ab) 'For the path of cultivation is said to be twofold' —

children.translated_text: 'The path of cultivation is twofold; but that called seeing is uncontaminated' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. tatkleśānuśayitatvād iti yasmāt tadbhūmikaḥ kleśas tatra laukike
body.translated_text: from this statement. 'Because of latent afflictions being deposited in it through the object' — because the affliction belonging to that ground is deposited in that mundane

body.text: mārge ālaṃbanato 'nuśayitaḥ. yo hi kleśa iti vistareṇa sādharmyavaidharmyadṛṣṭāṃtaṃ darśayati. yo yadbhūmiko mārgaḥ. na sa tadbhūmikakleśapratipakṣaḥ. [Tib. 238a] tatkleśānuśayitatvāt. asamāhitatadbhūmikadharmāṃtaravat. vaidharmyeṇa tūparisāmaṃtakamārgavad anāsravavat pratipakṣamārgavad vā. laukikenāpi vairāgyam iti. uparibhūmisāmaṃtakena. lokottareṇāpīti. tatpratipakṣeṇa svādharabhūmikenānāsraveṇa mārgeṇa.
body.translated_text: path through [its] object. For whatever affliction — he shows this through a comparison of similarity and dissimilarity in detail. Whatever path belongs to whatever ground — that is not the antidote of the affliction belonging to that ground, because of latent afflictions being deposited in it through the affliction of that [ground]. Like [other] non-concentrated <s>dharma</s>s belonging to that ground. By way of dissimilarity, however: like the preparatory path of a higher [ground], or like the uncontaminated [path], or like the antidote path. 'Dispassion through the mundane [path] too' — through the preparatory [concentration] of a higher ground. 'And through the supramundane' — through the antidote of one's own or lower ground, through the uncontaminated path.

body.text: (VI.47cd)

children.translated_text: 'Through the mundane [path], the dispassion of a Noble one' —

body.translated_text: (VI.47cd)

body.text: iti. tadyathā srotaāpannaḥ śamathacaritaḥ. laukikena mārgeṇa vairāgyaṃ gacchataḥ pratiprakāraṃ viśaṃyogaprāptayaḥ sāsravo 'nāsravaś cotpadyaṃte.
body.translated_text: for example, a stream-enterer of <s>śamatha</s>-conduct. When he attains dispassion through the mundane path, for each type [abandoned], both contaminated and uncontaminated disconnection-acquisitions (<s>visaṃyogaprāpti</s>) arise.

body.text: dhyānaṃ niśrityeti. yasmāc chaikṣaḥ ṣaḍ bhūmīr niśrityendriyāṇi saṃcarati. nārūpyam iti.
body.translated_text: 'Relying on a <s>dhyāna</s>' — because a learner transfers faculties relying on six grounds, not on a formless [attainment].

children.text: aśaikṣo nava niśritya bhūmīḥ śaikṣas tu ṣaḍ
children.translated_text: 'A non-learner, relying on nine grounds; a learner, on six' —

body.text: iti vacanāt tenāha. yo dhyānaṃ niśrityendriyāṇi saṃcarati. sa kṛtsnapūrvamārgatyāgād ārūpyamārgāṇāṃ mṛdvindriyasaṃgṛhītānāṃ pūrvalabdhānāṃ tyāgāt. kevaphalamārgalābhāc ca kevalasyānāgāmiphalasya tīkṣṇendriyasvabhāvasya lābhāt.
body.translated_text: from this statement. Therefore he says: one who transfers faculties relying on a <s>dhyāna</s> — that one, because of abandoning the entire former path — because of the abandoning of the formless-realm paths that were previously obtained, [which are] included among dull faculties — and because of obtaining the fruit-path alone — because of obtaining only the fruit of non-returning, having the nature of sharp faculties —

children.text: sa viśeṣaṃ phalaṃ tyaktvā phalm āproti vardhayann
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned the distinctive fruit, he obtains the fruit by increasing [his faculties]' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. ūrdhvabhūmikakleśavisaṃyogena ārūpyāvacarakleśavisaṃyogenāsamanvāgataḥ syāt. ayaṃ cāparo doṣaḥ. tyakte ca tasminn ūrdhvabhūmikleśavisaṃyoge [Tib. 238b] taiḥ kleśair ūrdhvabhūmikaiḥ samanvāgataḥ syād iti.
body.translated_text: from this statement — would become unendowed with the disconnection from the afflictions of the upper grounds — unendowed with the disconnection from the formless-realm afflictions. And this is another fault: having abandoned that disconnection from the afflictions of the upper grounds, he would become endowed with those afflictions — with the upper-ground afflictions.

children.translated_text: 'But like one half-liberated from the Peak of Existence and born above, there is non-endowment' —

body.text: ity ardhena vimukto 'rdhavimuktaḥ. bhavāgrād ardhavimukto bhavāgrārdhavimuktaḥ. ūrdhvaṃ jāta ūrdhvajātaḥ. bhavāgrārdhavimuktaś cordhvajātaś ca bhavāgrārdhavimuktordhvajātau. tayor iveti. bhavāgrārdhavimuktordhvajātavat. samanvayas taiś tasyeti vākyaśeṣaḥ. tuśabdaḥ pūrvadoṣavyāvartanārthaḥ. tam arthaṃ vivṛṇvann āha. asatyām iti vistaraḥ. asatyām api tasya pudgalasya laukikyāṃ visaṃyogaprāptau. na taiḥ kleśaiḥ samanvāgamaḥ syāt tadyathā bhavāgrārdhaprakāravimuktasyeti vistaraḥ. tasya hi laukikī bhavāgrārdhaprakāravisaṃyogaprāptir nāsti. tatpratipakṣalaukikamārgābhāvāt. lokottarā ca tadvisaṃyogaprāptir dhyānaṃ niśrityendriyasaṃcāreṇa tyaktā syāt. na ca punas tair bhāvāgrikakleśaprakāraiḥ samanvāgamo bhavatīty abhyupagamyate bhavadbhiḥ. tadvad asya syāt. yathā ca pṛthagjanasya prathamadhyānabhūmer ūrdhvaṃ jātasya dvitīyadhyānādyupapannasya. kāmāvacarakleśavisaṃyogaprāptityāgāt. prathamadhyānabhūmikāyā visaṃyogaprāpter
body.translated_text: one liberated from half is 'half-liberated.' One half-liberated from the Peak of Existence is '<s>bhavāgrārdha-vimukta</s>.' One born above is 'born-above.' Both the one half-liberated from the Peak of Existence and the one born above — these are '<s>bhavāgrārdha-vimukta-ūrdhva-jāta</s>.' Like those two — '<s>bhavāgrārdha-vimukta-ūrdhva-jāta-vat</s>.' 'His endowment with those' — this is the completion of the sentence. The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) is for the purpose of removing the prior fault. Explaining this meaning, he says: 'Even in the absence of' — and so forth in detail. Even in the absence of the mundane disconnection-acquisition of that person — he would not be endowed with those afflictions. Just as one half-liberated from types of the Peak of Existence — and so forth in detail. For that one does not have the mundane disconnection-acquisition of the half-types of the Peak of Existence — because of the absence of a mundane path that is the antidote of those. And the supramundane disconnection-acquisition of that [Peak of Existence] would have been abandoned through faculty-transfer relying on a <s>dhyāna</s>. Yet there is no endowment with those Peak-of-Existence affliction-types — this is accepted by you. Likewise for this one. And just as for an ordinary person born above the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground — one who has been reborn in the second <s>dhyāna</s> and the rest — because of the abandonment of the Desire Realm affliction disconnection-acquisition — of the disconnection-acquisition of the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground —

children.translated_text: 'Wholesome [attainments] obtained through <s>dhyāna</s> are abandoned through ground-transfer and falling away' —

body.text: iti niyamāt tyāgo bhavati. tasmān na punas taiḥ kāmāvacaraiḥ [Tib. 239a] kleśaiḥ samanvāgamo bhavatīty abhyupagamyate. tadvad asyāpi pudgalasya syāt. pṛthagjanasyetigrahaṇaṃ. yasmād āryasya laukikena mārgeṇa kāmadhātor ūrdhvaṃ vā vairagyaṃ gacchataḥ kleśavisaṃyogaprāptir laukikī lokottarā ca bhavati. tatra yā laukikī kāmāvacarakleśavisaṃyogaprāptiḥ. tasyāḥ prathamadhyānabhūmer ūrdhvajātasya bhūmisaṃcāreṇa tyāgo bhavati na lokottarāyāḥ.
body.translated_text: because of the restriction — abandonment occurs. Therefore, there is no endowment with those Desire Realm afflictions again — this is accepted. Likewise for this person too. The inclusion of 'ordinary person' [is significant] — because for a Noble one who attains dispassion from the Desire Realm and above through the mundane path, the disconnection-acquisition is both mundane and supramundane. Therein, the mundane disconnection-acquisition of the Desire Realm afflictions — of one born above the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground — through ground-transfer, abandonment occurs — but not of the supramundane.

children.translated_text: 'But for a Noble one, through fruit-attainment, emergence, and falling away' —

body.text: iti tyāganiyamāt. tasyāṃ ca satyāṃ lokottarāyāṃ prathamadhyānād ūrdhvaṃ jātasyāpy āryasya na punas taiḥ samanvāgamaḥ saṃbhavati. na tv evaṃ pṛthagjanasyeti pṛthagjanagrahaṇaṃ. tasmād ajñāpakam etat. tyakte kleśāsamanvayād iti yad uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: because of this restriction of abandonment. And when the supramundane [disconnection-acquisition] exists — even for a Noble one born above the first <s>dhyāna</s> — there is no endowment with those [Desire Realm afflictions] again. But for an ordinary person, it is not so — hence the inclusion of 'ordinary person.' Therefore this [argument] is not probative. 'When the afflictions are abandoned, there is no endowment' — this is what was stated.

body.text: iti. svordhvādhobhūmitaḥ. tasya sāsravānāsravatvāt.
body.translated_text: meaning: from one's own ground, from higher grounds, and from lower grounds. Because of it being both contaminated and uncontaminated.

body.text: (VI.49) upekṣendriyasāmānyād iti. caturthadhyānādisamāpattitatsāmaṃtakayor upekṣendriyaṃ tulyam iti. kaścin na śaknotīti mṛdvindriyaḥ. indriyasaṃcārasya duṣkaratvād iti. upekṣendriyānaṃtaraṃ sukhendriyasya saumanasyendriyasya vā duṣkaratvāt. maulasāmaṃtakayor upekṣendriyasāmānye sati kim arthaṃ maulād evāṃtyaṃ vimuktimārgaṃ saṃmukhīkaroti. na sāmaṃtakāt. vītarāgabhūmibāhumānyāt. [Tib. 239b] nādharāyā vītarāgatvād iti. tatsāmaṃtakena vādhovairāgyasya kṛtatvāt. satyākārapravṛttā iti. anityādyākārapravṛttāḥ.
body.translated_text: (VI.49) 'Because of the commonality of the equanimity faculty' — the equanimity faculty in the main attainment of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and the rest and in its preparatory [concentration] is the same. 'Some are unable' — those with dull faculties. 'Because of the difficulty of faculty-transfer' — because of the difficulty of [transitioning from] the equanimity faculty immediately to the pleasure faculty or the mental pleasure faculty. 'When the equanimity faculty is the same in the main [attainment] and preparatory [concentration], for what purpose does he bring the final liberation-path to the fore from the main [attainment] alone, not from the preparatory?' Because of esteeming the ground [from which one is] dispassionate. 'Not from the lower, because of being dispassionate from it' — or because the dispassion from that [ground] has already been accomplished through that preparatory [concentration]. 'Operating with aspects of the truths' — operating with aspects of impermanence and the rest.

body.text: (VI.50) saṃbhavata iti. yady adharāṃ bhūmim audārikataḥ paśyaṃty ūrdhvaṃ tadviparyayeṇa śāṃtata ity eke. apare vyācakṣate. śāṃtādyākārāṇāṃ kadācid ekenāpy ākāreṇākārayaṃti. nāvaśyaṃ samastair iti. audārikata iti. audārikam ity audārikataḥ. aśāṃtatvād audārikataḥ. katham aśāṃtādharā bhūmiḥ. mahābhisaṃskārataratvāt. idaṃ mahābhisaṃskāraṃ yatnasādhyaṃ mārgeṇa sahādharaṃ sthānaṃ. idam api mahābhisaṃskāraṃ saha mārgeṇordhvaṃ sthānam. idam anayor atiśayeneti mahābhisaṃskārataraṃ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. khilaṃ durbhedaṃ. kutsitaṃ khilaṃ duḥkhilam iti duḥkhilataḥ. katham apraṇītādharā bhūmir ity āha. bahudauṣṭhulyataratvena pratikūlabhāvād iti. dauṣṭhulyaṃ kāyacittayor akarmaṇyatā kleśānukūlatety arthaḥ. bahudauṣṭhulyam
body.translated_text: (VI.50) 'It is possible' — some [say]: if they see the lower ground as coarse, the upper is the reverse of that — [seen as] peaceful. Others explain: of the aspects such as peaceful and the rest, sometimes they operate with even a single aspect — not necessarily with all of them. 'As coarse (<s>audārikata</s>)' — 'coarse' means coarseness (<s>audārikataḥ</s>). Because of non-peacefulness, [it is seen as] coarse. How is the lower ground non-peaceful? Because of requiring greater conditioning (<s>mahābhisaṃskāra</s>). This lower station, together with the path, requires great conditioning — is achievable through effort. This upper station too, together with the path, requires great conditioning. But this [lower one] requires even greater conditioning than those two — hence <s>mahābhisaṃskāratara</s>. Its state — because of that. Therefore. 'Hard' (<s>khila</s>) means 'difficult to penetrate.' That which is contemptible and hard is 'painfully-hard' (<s>duḥkhila</s>) — hence 'as painfully-hard' (<s>duḥkhilataḥ</s>). How is the lower ground not excellent (<s>apraṇīta</s>)? — he says: 'Because of being adverse through having even more gross impurity (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>).' <s>Dauṣṭhulya</s> is the unwieldiness of body and mind, the favorableness to afflictions — this is the meaning. 'Having much gross impurity'

body.text: asyeti. bahudauṣṭhulyam. idam api bahudauṣṭhulyaṃ samārgam adharaṃ sthānaṃ. idam api bahudauṣṭhulyaṃ samārgam ūrdhvaṃ sthānam. idam anayor atiśayeneti bahudauṣṭhulyataraṃ. tadbhāvāt. [Tib. 240a] sthūlabhittikata iti. sthūlabhittikabhāvena. tayaivatadbhūmyaniḥsaraṇāt. tayaiva bhūmyā tasyā eva bhūmer aniḥsaraṇāt. bhittyaniḥśaraṇavat. yathā tayaiva bhittyā tasyā eva bhitter aniḥsaraṇaṃ. tadavaṣṭabdhākāśadeśāt. teṣāṃ viparyayeṇeti. alpābhisaṃskāratvāt alpadauṣṭhulyataratvenāpratikūlabhāvāt tayā bhūmyā tadbhūminiḥsaraṇād yathākramaṃ śāṃtapraṇītaniḥsaraṇākārāḥ.
body.translated_text: — of this. This lower station, together with the path, has much gross impurity. This upper station too, together with the path, has much gross impurity. But this [lower one] has even more gross impurity than those two — hence <s>bahudauṣṭhulyatara</s>. Because of its state. 'As having thick walls (<s>sthūlabhittikata</s>)' — in the manner of having thick walls. 'Because of not escaping from that very ground by that very [ground]' — because of not escaping from that very ground through that very ground — like not escaping from a wall. Just as there is no escaping from that very wall through that very wall — because of the space-region being blocked by it. 'By the reverse of those' — because of requiring little conditioning, because of being non-adverse through having less gross impurity, and because of escaping from that ground through that ground — respectively, the aspects of peaceful, excellent, and escape [arise].

body.text: (VI.51) gatam ānuṣaṃgikaṃ. idaṃ vaktavyam iti. kṣayajñānāṃtarābhāvi vaktavyam. anuṣaṃgeṇa tu laukikānāṃtaryavimuktimārgalakṣaṇanirdeśa iti.
body.translated_text: (VI.51) 'The incidental [discussion] has concluded. This must now be stated' — what comes immediately after the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) must be stated. But incidentally, the teaching of the characteristics of the mundane uninterrupted and liberation paths [was given].

children.translated_text: 'If unshakable, from the knowledge of destruction, the cognition of non-arising' —

body.text: iti. apunaḥkartavyatājñānaṃ. tad asya tadānīm utpadyate. parihāṇisaṃbhavād iti. kleśotpādāvakāśo 'stīti nāsyānutpādajñānam utpadyate. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. parihāṇisaṃbhavāt. yasmād asya parihāṇiḥ saṃbhavati. yasya punar anutpādajñānaṃ. na tasya parihāṇir iti.
body.translated_text: thus. The knowledge of 'it-need-not-be-done-again' (<s>apunaḥkartavyatājñāna</s>) — that arises for this one at that time. 'Because of the possibility of regression' — because there is an opening for the arising of afflictions, the knowledge of non-arising does not arise for this one. For what reason? Because of the possibility of regression — since regression is possible for this one. But for one who has the knowledge of non-arising, there is no regression.

body.text: (VI.52) tena hi śramaṇo bhavatīti. śrāmaṇyayogāc chramaṇo bhavati. yathā śauklyayogāc chuklaḥ paṭa iti. śamayati kleśān iti śramaṇaḥ. tanniṣyandapuruṣakāraphalatvād iti. tasya śrāmaṇyasyānaṃtaryamārgalakṣaṇasya yathāyogaṃ vimuktimārgā asaṃskṛtāni ca [Tib. 240b] niṣyandaphalatvāt puruṣakāraphalatvāc ca. vimuktimārgās tasya niṣyandaphalaṃ puruṣakāraphalaṃ ca. asaṃskṛtāni puruṣakāraphalam eva.
body.translated_text: (VI.52) 'Therefore he is a <s>śramaṇa</s>' — he is a <s>śramaṇa</s> because of connection with <s>śrāmaṇya</s> (the ascetic state). Just as a cloth is white because of connection with whiteness. 'He pacifies afflictions — hence <s>śramaṇa</s>.' 'Because of being the outflow-fruit and human-effort-fruit of that' — of that <s>śrāmaṇya</s> characterized as the uninterrupted path, the liberation paths and unconditioned [cessations] are, as applicable, outflow-fruits and human-effort-fruits. The liberation paths are its outflow-fruit and human-effort-fruit. The unconditioned [cessations] are human-effort-fruit only.

children.text: yadbalāj jāyate yat tat phalaṃ puruṣakārajaṃ.
children.translated_text: 'Whatever is produced through the power of that — that is the fruit of human effort (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>).'

body.text: yadbalāt prāpyate ca yat tac ca puruṣakāraphalam iti kṛtvā.
body.translated_text: 'And whatever is attained through the power of that — that too is the fruit of human effort' — because of this.

body.text: (VI.53) evaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. yathā pṛthagjanasya pāṇineḥ pravacane upasaṃkhyānaṃ kriyate. evaṃ sarvajñasyāpi buddhasyopasaṃkhyānaṃ kartavyam upajāyata iti vākyārthaḥ. pūrvamārgatyāga iti vistaraḥ. pūrvamārgatyāgaḥ pratipannakamārgatyāgāt. apūrvamārgaprāptiś ca phalamārgalābhād iti. sarvasyaikaprāptilābhād iti. sarvasya darśanaheyaprahāṇasyaikā bhāvanāmārgasaṃgṛhītā prāptiḥ srotaāpattiphalaprāptikāle labhyate. tathā sakṛdāgāmiphalaprāptikāle darśanaheyaprahāṇasya ṣaḍvidhabhāvanāmārgaheyaprahāṇasya ca sarvasyaikā sakṛdāgāmiphalasaṃgṛhītā prāptir labhyate. evam anāgāmyarhattvaphalayor api yojyaṃ. caturvidhānāṃ dharmānvayajñānānāṃ iti. satyabhedāc caturvidhānāṃ dharmajñānānām anvayajñānānāṃ ca tathaiva caturvidhānām
body.translated_text: (VI.53) 'If so' — and so forth in detail. Just as for the ordinary person <s>Pāṇini</s>, an additional enumeration is made in the teaching — so too an additional enumeration of even the omniscient <s>Buddha</s> should be made — this is the sentence-meaning. 'Abandonment of the prior path' — and so forth in detail. The abandonment of the prior path is through the abandonment of the practitioner-path. And the attainment of a new path is through the obtaining of the fruit-path. 'Because of the obtaining of a single acquisition of the whole' — a single acquisition, included in the path of cultivation, of the entire abandonment of what is to be abandoned by seeing, is obtained at the time of attaining the fruit of stream-entry. Similarly, at the time of attaining the fruit of once-returning, a single acquisition included in the fruit of once-returning is obtained — of the entire abandonment of what is to be abandoned by seeing and the sixfold abandonment of what is to be abandoned by cultivation. For the fruits of non-returning and <s>arhat</s>ship too, this should be connected similarly. 'Of the fourfold <s>dharma</s>- and subsequent-knowledges' — of the <s>dharma</s>-knowledges that are fourfold by the division of truths, and of the subsequent knowledges that are likewise fourfold

body.text: iti. yugapadaṣṭajñānalābhaḥ.
body.translated_text: — the simultaneous obtaining of eight knowledges.

body.text: (VI.54) laukikamārgaprāptaṃ phaladvapam iti. sakṛdāgāmiphalam [Tib. 241a] anāgāmiphalaṃ ca. tad dhi laukikenāpi mārgeṇa prāptaṃ saṃbhavati. tat kathaṃ śrāmaṇyasyānāsravamārgalakṣaṇasya phalaṃ yujyate. darśanamārgaphalam api prahāṇam iti. apiśabdād bhāvanāmārgaphalam api prahāṇaṃ gṛhyate. tasya dviprakārasyāpi prahāṇasya sakṛdāgāmiphalasaṃgṛhītānāgāmiphalasaṃgṛhītā vā ekā prāptir labhyate. tasmād darśanamārgaphalaprahāṇayogād asaṃskṛtaṃ sakṛdāgaṃiphalam anāgāmiphalaṃ vā śrāmaṇyaphalaṃ bhavati. yat trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇam iti. trisaṃyojanaprahāṇaṃ darśanamārgeṇa. paṃcāvarabhāgīyaikadeśānāṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśīlav\rataparāmarśavicikitsānāṃ darśanamārgeṇaiva prahāṇaṃ. tasya prahāṇasya sakṛdāgāmyanāgāmiphalatve. kiṃ. kṛtaḥ prakṣepaḥ. tena jñāyate. prahāṇamiśrīkaraṇād evam uktaṃ bhagavateti. tadbalena parihīṇād iti.
body.translated_text: (VI.54) 'The twofold fruit obtained through the mundane path' — the fruit of once-returning and the fruit of non-returning. For those can be obtained even through the mundane path. How then is it fitting that they are fruits of <s>śrāmaṇya</s>, which has the characteristic of the uncontaminated path? 'Even the abandonment that is the fruit of the path of seeing' — from the word 'even,' the abandonment that is the fruit of the path of cultivation is also included. Of that twofold abandonment, a single acquisition included in the fruit of once-returning or included in the fruit of non-returning is obtained. Therefore, because of connection with the abandonment that is the fruit of the path of seeing, the unconditioned fruit of once-returning or non-returning is a fruit of <s>śrāmaṇya</s>. 'That which is the abandonment of the three fetters' — the abandonment of the three fetters is through the path of seeing. The abandonment of a portion of the five lower fetters — the view of the self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), clinging to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>) — is through the path of seeing alone. When that abandonment is [counted toward] the fruit of once-returning or non-returning — what? 'An inclusion is made.' From this it is known that the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke thus by mixing the abandonments. 'Through the power of that, from the regressed one' —

children.translated_text: 'In the case of dispassion through the noble and mundane [paths], the acquisitions of disconnection are twofold' —

body.text: iti tatranāsravayā visaṃyogaprāptyā tat prahāṇaṃ yal laukikamārgasaṃprāptaṃ saṃdhāryate. prāptiyogenāvaśyam upatiṣṭhata ity arthaḥ. mriyate na phalabhraṣṭa iti. tadabhāve hi laukikasyeva parihīṇasya maraṇaṃ syāt. tadbalenety anāsravavisaṃyogaprāptibalenety [Tib. 241b] arthaḥ. saiva ca vartamānalaukikamārgopajanitānāsravā prātir anāgataś cāṣṭāṃga āryamārgo laukikabalena prāpyamāṇaḥ saṃskṛtaṃ śrāmaṇyaphalaṃ vyavasthāpyamānaṃ na virudhyate. sūtre tv asaṃskṛtaṃ śrāmaṇyaphalam udgrāhyate. prādhānyāt. saṃskṛtam apy atraiṣṭavyam iti.
body.translated_text: thus. Through the uncontaminated acquisition of disconnection, that abandonment which was obtained through the mundane path is sustained. The meaning is: it necessarily persists through the connection of [uncontaminated] acquisition. 'He does not die having fallen from the fruit' — for in the absence of that [uncontaminated acquisition], as if one who had regressed from the mundane [path], death would occur. 'Through the power of that' — the meaning is: through the power of the uncontaminated acquisition of disconnection. And that very uncontaminated acquisition generated by the present mundane path, and the future eightfold noble path being obtained through the power of the mundane [path] — the conditioned fruit of <s>śrāmaṇya</s> being so established is not contradicted. But in the <s>sūtra</s>, the unconditioned fruit of <s>śrāmaṇya</s> is to be accepted — because of predominance. The conditioned too should be accepted here.

body.text: (VI.55, 56) kleśānāṃ vāhanād brāhmaṇyam iti. vāhitā anenānekavidhāḥ pāpakā akuśalā dharmā iti brāhmaṇaḥ. tadbhāvo brāhmaṇyam anāsravo mārgaḥ. kathaṃ brahmacakram ity āha. brahmacakraṃ tu brahmavartanād iti. yasmād brahmaṇā pravartitaṃ. tasmāt brahmacakram iti. anuttarabrāhmaṇyayogād iti. anuttarānāsravamārgayogād ity arthaḥ. eṣa hi bhagavān brāhmety etad udāharaṇaṃ jīvakenoktam etat.
body.translated_text: (VI.55, 56) '<s>Brāhmaṇya</s> (brahmanhood) is from the carrying away of afflictions' — 'By this one, many kinds of evil unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s have been carried away' — hence <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. Its state is <s>brāhmaṇya</s> — the uncontaminated path. How is it the Brahma-wheel (<s>brahmacakra</s>)? — he says: 'But the Brahma-wheel is from the setting in motion by <s>Brahma</s>' — because it was set in motion by <s>Brahma</s> — therefore it is the Brahma-wheel. 'Because of connection with supreme <s>brāhmaṇya</s>' — the meaning is: because of connection with the supreme uncontaminated path. For this <s>Bhagavān</s> is a Brahman — this illustration was given by <s>Jīvaka</s>.

children.translated_text: 'Because of swiftness and the rest, and because of spokes and the rest' —

body.text: iti. āśugatvādibhir arādibhiś cety arthaḥ. āśugatvād iti vistaraḥ. idaṃ mārgasya cakraratnena sādharmyam ucyate. yathā cakraratnam āśugam. evaṃ
body.translated_text: thus. The meaning is: because of swiftness and the rest, and because of spokes and the rest. 'Because of swiftness' — and so forth in detail. This describes the similarity of the path with the jewel-wheel (<s>cakraratna</s>). Just as the jewel-wheel is swift — so too

body.text: darśanamārgaḥ. paṃcadaśabhiś cittakṣaṇaiḥ satyābhisamayād āśuga iti. tyajanakramaṇāt. yathā tad anyaṃ deśaṃ tyajaty anyaṃ deśaṃ krāmati. [Tib. 242a] evam ayam ānaṃtaryamārgaṃ tyajati vimuktimārgaṃ krāmati saṃmukhībhāvataḥ. satyāṃtaratyajanakramaṇād vā. ajitajayajitādhyāvasanāt. yathā tad ajitāni grāmanigamādīni jayati. jitāni cādhyāvasati. evam ayam ānaṃtaryamārgeṇājitān satkāyadṛṣṭyādīn kleśāṃ jayati tatprāticchedāt. jitāṃś cādhyāvasati vimuktimārgeṇa. kleśavisaṃyogaprāptisahotpādāt. utpatananipatanāc ca. yathā ca tat kvacid utpatati kvacin nipatati. evam ayam ānaṃtaryavimuktimārgāṇāṃ punaḥpunaḥ saṃmukhībhāvāt. kāmādiduḥkhādisatyālaṃbanato vā yathāyogam utpatati ca. rūpārūpyadhātvālaṃbanād utpatati. kāmadhātvālaṃbanān nipatatīti.
body.translated_text: the path of seeing — it is swift because of the realization of the truths in fifteen mind-moments. 'Because of abandoning and advancing.' Just as that [jewel-wheel] abandons one region and advances to another — so too this [path] abandons the uninterrupted path and advances to the liberation path, through its coming face-to-face. Or, because of abandoning and advancing with respect to different truths. 'Because of conquering the unconquered and establishing the conquered.' Just as that [jewel-wheel] conquers unconquered towns and villages and establishes the conquered — so too this [path], through the uninterrupted path, conquers the unconquered afflictions such as the view of the self-existing body and the rest, through the cutting of their acquisition; and establishes the conquered through the liberation path — because of the co-arising with the acquisition of disconnection from afflictions. 'And because of rising and descending.' Just as that [wheel] rises somewhere and descends somewhere — so too this [path], because of the repeated coming face-to-face of the uninterrupted and liberation paths; or, as applicable, it rises because of having the suffering and other truths of the Desire Realm and the rest as objects — it rises because of having the Form and Formless Realm as objects, and descends because of having the Desire Realm as object.

body.text: samyagdṛṣṭir iti vistaraḥ. iha śīlaṃ pratiṣṭhāya samādhilābhaḥ samādhilābhāt prajñā yathābhūtaṃ bhāvyata ity ataḥ samyagvākkarmāṃtājivā nābhisthānīyāḥ. samyagdṛṣṭyādīnāṃ tatpratibaddhavṛttitvāt śīlam ādhārabhūtam iti kṛtvā. samādhir nemisthāṇīyas tenetareṣām upagrahāt. samyagdṛṣṭyādayo 'rasthānīyaḥ. [Tib. 242b] aravad itaś cāmutaś ca pravṛttatvāt. kuta etad iti. kiṃ svamatam etad vaibhāṣikāṇāṃ darśanamārgo dharmacakram ity āhodvid āgamata iti. tadutpattau pravartitam iti. darśanamārgotpattau pravartitaṃ dharmacakram iti sūtre vacanāt. kathaṃ. bhagavān bārāṇāsyāṃ viharati sma ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve. tatra bhagavān paṃcakāṃ bhikṣūn āmaṃtrayate sma. idaṃ duḥkham āryasatyam iti bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam ananuśruteṣu dharmeṣu yoniśomanasikurvataś cakṣur udapādi jñānaṃ vidyā buddhir udapādi. ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ. ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ. iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam iti. pūrvam ananuśruteṣu dharmeṣu yoniśomanasikurvataś cakṣur udapādi jñānaṃ vidyā buddhir udapādi. tat khalu duḥkham āryasatyam abhijñayā parijñātavyaṃ mayeti pūrvam ananuśruteṣu dharmeṣu yoniśomanasikurvataś cakṣur udapādīti pūrvavat. tat khalu duḥkhasamudaya āryasatyam abhijñayā prahātavyaṃ mayeti pūrvam ananuśruteṣu dharmeṣu pūrvavat. tat khalu duḥkhanirodha āryasatyam abhijñayā sākṣātkartavyaṃ mayeti pūrvam ananuśruteṣu dharmeṣu pūrvavat. tat khalu duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam abhijñayā bhāvayitavyaṃ mayeti pūrvam ananuśruteṣu dharmeṣu pūrvavat. [Tib. 243a] tat khalu duḥkham āryasatyam abhijñayā parijñātaṃ mayeti pūrvam ananuśruteṣu dharmeṣu pūrvavat. tat khalu duḥkhasamudaya āryasatyam abhijñayā prahīṇaṃ mayeti pūrvam ananuśruteṣu dharmeṣu pūrvavat. tat khalu
body.translated_text: 'Right view' — and so forth in detail. Here, having established morality, concentration is obtained; from the obtaining of concentration, wisdom is cultivated as it truly is — therefore right speech, right action, and right livelihood are the hub (<s>abhiṣṭhāna</s>). Because morality serves as the foundation for right view and the rest, since their functioning depends on it. Concentration is the rim (<s>nemi</s>) — because it encompasses the others. Right view and the rest are the spokes (<s>ara</s>) — because of operating here and there, like spokes. 'From where is this [known]?' — is this the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s' own view — that the path of seeing is the <s>dharmacakra</s> — or from scripture? 'At its arising, it was set in motion' — because of the statement in the <s>sūtra</s> 'the <s>dharmacakra</s> was set in motion at the arising of the path of seeing.' How? 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Bārāṇasī</s>, in the Deer Park at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the group of five monks: "This is the noble truth of suffering, O monks. Regarding <s>dharma</s>s previously unheard, when properly attending, the eye arose, knowledge arose, understanding arose, wisdom arose. This is the origin of suffering. This is the cessation of suffering. This is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering — the noble truth. Regarding <s>dharma</s>s previously unheard, when properly attending, the eye arose, knowledge arose, understanding arose, wisdom arose. That noble truth of suffering is to be fully known through direct knowledge by me — regarding <s>dharma</s>s previously unheard, when properly attending, the eye arose" — as before. "That noble truth of the origin of suffering is to be abandoned through direct knowledge by me — regarding <s>dharma</s>s previously unheard" — as before. "That noble truth of the cessation of suffering is to be directly realized through direct knowledge by me — regarding <s>dharma</s>s previously unheard" — as before. "That noble truth of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering is to be cultivated through direct knowledge by me — regarding <s>dharma</s>s previously unheard" — as before. "That noble truth of suffering has been fully known through direct knowledge by me — regarding <s>dharma</s>s previously unheard" — as before. "That noble truth of the origin of suffering has been abandoned through direct knowledge by me — regarding <s>dharma</s>s previously unheard" — as before. "That

body.text: duḥkhanirodha āryasatyam abhijñayā sākṣātkṛtaṃ mayeti pūrvam ananuśruteṣu dharmeṣu pūrvavat. tat khalu punar duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam abhijñayā bhāvitaṃ mayeti pūrvam ananuśruteṣu dharmeṣu pūrvavat. yāvac ca mama bhikṣava eṣu caturṣv āryasatyeṣv evaṃ triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ na cakṣur udapādi. na jñānaṃ na vidyā na buddhir udapādi. na tāvad aham asmāt sadevakāl lokāt samārakāt sabrahmakāt saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ sadevamānuṣāsurāyā mukto niḥsṛto visaṃyukto viprayukto viparyāsāpagatena cetasā bahulaṃ vyahārṣaṃ. na tāvad aham anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddho 'smīty adhyajñāsiṣaṃ. yataś ca mama bhikṣava eṣu caturṣv āryasatyeṣv evaṃ triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ cakṣur udapādi yāvad buddhir udapādi. tato 'ham asmāt sadevakād yāvat viprayukto viparyāsāpagatena cetasā [Tib. 243b] bahulaṃ vyahārṣaṃ. tato 'ham anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddho 'smīti adhyajñāsiṣaṃ. asmin khalu punar dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe āyuṣmataḥ kauṇḍinyasya virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur utpannam aśīteś ca devatāsahasrāṇāṃ. tatra bhagavān āyuṣmaṃtaṃ kauṇḍinyam āmaṃtrayate sma. ājñātas te kauṇḍinya dharmaḥ. ājñāto me bhagavan. ājñātas te kauṇḍinya dharmaḥ. ājñāto me sugata. ājñāta āyuṣmatā kauṇḍinyena dharma iti bhaumā yakṣāḥ śabdam udīrayaṃti ghoṣam anuśrāvayaṃti. etan mārṣā bhagavatā bārāṇasyām ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve triparivartadvādaśākāraṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartitaṃ. apravartitapūrvaṃ śramaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā māreṇa vā brahmaṇā vā. kenacit punar loke sahadharmeṇa bahujanahitāyeti vistaraḥ. tad evam āryasya kauṇḍinyasya darśanamārga utpanne devatābhir uktaṃ bhagavatā pravartitaṃ dharmacakram iti sūtravacanāt. darśanamārgo dharmacakram iti gamyate.
body.translated_text: 'The noble truth of the cessation of suffering has been directly realized by me through <s>abhijñā</s> (direct knowledge)' — regarding <s>dharma</s>s not previously heard, as before. 'That noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering has been cultivated by me through <s>abhijñā</s>' — regarding <s>dharma</s>s not previously heard, as before. 'As long as, O <s>bhikṣu</s>s, regarding these four Noble Truths, the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) of three turnings and twelve aspects had not arisen in me — neither knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), nor insight (<s>vidyā</s>), nor wisdom (<s>buddhi</s>) had arisen — so long I did not, from this world with its <s>deva</s>s, with its <s>Māra</s>, with its <s>Brahmā</s>, from among the generations including <s>śramaṇa</s>s and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, including <s>deva</s>s, humans, and <s>asura</s>s — freed, released, disconnected, disjoined, with a mind free from distortion — extensively rejoice. So long I did not realize: "I have awakened to the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)." But when, O <s>bhikṣu</s>s, regarding these four Noble Truths, the eye of three turnings and twelve aspects arose in me, and wisdom arose — then I, from this world with its <s>deva</s>s and the rest, disjoined, with a mind free from distortion, extensively rejoiced. Then I realized: "I have awakened to the unsurpassed perfect awakening." When indeed this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) was being spoken, in the venerable <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> the dustless, stainless <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (dharma-eye) arose regarding <s>dharma</s>s, and in eighty thousand <s>devatā</s>s [as well]. Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>: "You have understood the <s>dharma</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>." "I have understood, <s>Bhagavān</s>." "You have understood the <s>dharma</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>." "I have understood, <s>Sugata</s>." 'The <s>dharma</s> has been understood by the venerable <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>' — the earthly <s>yakṣa</s>s raise a cry and proclaim the message: 'This, venerable sirs, is the <s>dharmacakra</s> of three turnings and twelve aspects set in motion by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in <s>Bārāṇasī</s>, at the <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park (<s>Mṛgadāva</s>) — never before set in motion by any <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>deva</s>, <s>Māra</s>, or <s>Brahmā</s>, or by anyone in the world — [set in motion] together with the <s>dharma</s>, for the benefit of many beings,' and so forth in detail. Thus, when the <s>darśanamārga</s> (seeing path) arose in the Noble <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, the <s>devatā</s>s said: 'The <s>dharmacakra</s> has been set in motion by the <s>Bhagavān</s>' — from this <s>sūtra</s> statement, it is understood that the <s>darśanamārga</s> is the <s>dharmacakra</s>.

body.text: kathaṃ triparivartam iti vistaraḥ. idaṃ duḥkham ārgasatyam ity ekaḥ parivartaḥ. tat khalu parijñātavyam iti dvitīyaḥ. tat khalu parijñātam iti tṛtīyaḥ. ity ete trayaḥ parivartāḥ. ekaikasmin parivarte idaṃ duḥkham ity asmiṃś cakṣur udapādi jñānaṃ [Tib. 244a] vidyā buddhir udapādīti catvāra ākārāḥ. parijñātavyam ity asmin punaś catvāraḥ. parijñātam ity asmin punar api catvāraḥ. ity ete dvādaśākārāḥ. tatra pratyakṣārthatvād anāsravā prajñā cakṣuḥ. niḥsaṃśayatvāj jñānaṃ. bhūtārthatvāt vidyā. viśuddhatvād buddhiḥ. viśuddhā dhīr buddhir iti nirukteḥ. punar bāhyakānāṃ satyeṣu darśanaṃ kudṛṣṭivicikitsāvidyānām apratipakṣaḥ sāsravaṃ ceti tato viśeṣaṇārthaṃ cakṣurādigrahaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: How is it of three turnings? And so forth in detail. 'This is the noble truth of suffering' — this is the first turning. 'That indeed is to be fully comprehended (<s>parijñātavya</s>)' — this is the second. 'That indeed has been fully comprehended' — this is the third. Thus there are these three turnings. In each turning — 'regarding this, that this is suffering, the eye arose, knowledge, insight, and wisdom arose' — these are four aspects. 'Regarding "it is to be fully comprehended," again four.' 'Regarding "it has been fully comprehended," again four.' Thus there are twelve aspects. Therein, because of directly perceiving the object, uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>) <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>). Because of being free from doubt, it is knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). Because of being true in meaning, it is insight (<s>vidyā</s>). Because of being pure, it is wisdom (<s>buddhi</s>) — from the etymology: 'purified discernment is <s>buddhi</s>.' Furthermore, the grasping of eye and so forth is for the purpose of distinguishing from the outsiders' (<s>bāhyaka</s>) seeing of the truths, [which is] not an antidote to wrong views, doubt, and ignorance, and is contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>)

body.text: punas triṣu parivarteṣu prathamaṃ darśanaṃ cakṣuḥ. yathādṛṣṭavyavacāraṇaṃ jñānaṃ. yāvadbhāvikatām upādāya vidyā. yāvadvidyamānagrahaṇāt. yathāvadbhāvikatām upādāya buddhiḥ. yathābhūtārthāvabodhāt. punar ananuśruteṣu dharmeṣv ānumānikajñānapratiṣedhārthaṃ cakṣur ity āha. ādhimokṣikajñānapratiṣedhārthaṃ jñānam iti. ābhimānikajñānapratiṣedhārthaṃ vidyeti. sāsravapratiṣedhārthaṃ buddhir iti. prati satyam evaṃ bhavaṃtīti. ayaṃ duḥkhasamudaya āryasatyaṃ. tat khalu prahātavyaṃ. tat khalu prahīṇam ity ete trayaḥ parivartāḥ. ekaikasmiṃ parivarte cakṣur udapādi jñānaṃ vidyā buddhir ity ete dvādaśākārāḥ. evaṃ nirodhamārgasatye api yojye. āha. yadi prati satyam evaṃ bhavaṃti. trayaḥ parivartā dvādaśa cākārāḥ [Tib. 244b] dvādaśa parivartāḥ aṣṭacatvāriṃśac cākārāḥ prāpnuvaṃti. kasmāt triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāram ity uktam. ata ucyate. trikadvādaśakasādharmyāt tu triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāram uktam iti. dvayasaptasthānakauśaladeśanāvad iti. dvayadeśanāvat. saptasthānakauśaladeśanāvac ca. tadyathā vistaram uktvā tena hi bhikṣo dvayaṃ te deśayiṣyāmi tac chṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru bhāṣiṣye. dvayaṃ katamat. cakṣūrūpāṇi yāvan manodharmāś ceti. yatheha dvayasādharmyād dvayam ity uktam. evaṃ trikadvādaśakasādharmyāt triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāram uktaṃ. yathā ca saptasthānakuśalo bhikṣuḥ rūpaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. rūpasamudayaṃ. rūpanirodhaṃ. rūpanirodhagāminīṃ pratipadaṃ. rūpasyāsvādaṃ cādīnavaṃ ca. niḥsaraṇaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti. saptasthānakuśalo bhikṣuḥ trividhārthopaparīkṣī kṣipram evāsmin dharmavinaye duḥkhasyāṃtaṃ prajānātīti. pratyekaṃ skaṃdheṣu saptasthānakauśalasādharmyāt. evam ihāpi trikadvādaśakasādharmyāt triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāram uktam iti. ebhiś ceti vistaraḥ. ebhiś ca parivartair yathāsūtranirdiṣṭair darśanabhāvanāśaikṣamārgā [Tib. 245a] yathāsaṃkhyaṃ darśitāḥ. idaṃ duḥkham āryasatyam ity ārabhya yāvad iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam iti darśanamārgo darśitaḥ. tat khalu duḥkham āryasatyam abhijñayā parijñātavyam ity ārabhya yāvat tat khalu duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam abhijñayā bhāvayitavyam iti bhāvanāmārgo darśitaḥ. tat khalu duḥkham āryasatyam abhijñayā parijñātam ity ārabhya yāvat tat khalu duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam abhijñayā bhāvitam ity aśaikṣamārgo darśita iti. atrācārya āha. yady evam iti vistaraḥ. yady evam ebhiḥ parivartair darśanādimārgā yathāsaṃkhyaṃ darśitāḥ. na tarhi darśanamārga eva triparivarto dvādaśākāraḥ. kiṃ tarhi. ekaparivartaś caturākāra iti. katham asau darśanamārgo dharmacakraṃ vyavasthāpyate. triparivartābhāve
body.translated_text: Furthermore, in the three turnings, the first seeing is the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>). Investigation in accordance with what has been seen is knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). With reference to its enduring nature, it is insight (<s>vidyā</s>) — because of apprehending what is constantly present. With reference to its accurate nature, it is wisdom (<s>buddhi</s>) — because of comprehending objects as they truly are. Furthermore, 'regarding <s>dharma</s>s not previously heard,' to negate inferential knowledge, he says 'eye' (<s>cakṣus</s>). To negate knowledge based on conviction (<s>ādhimokṣikajñāna</s>), he says 'knowledge' (<s>jñāna</s>). To negate knowledge based on conceit (<s>ābhimānikajñāna</s>), he says 'insight' (<s>vidyā</s>). To negate the contaminated, he says 'wisdom' (<s>buddhi</s>). 'For each truth it is thus' — 'This is the noble truth of the origin of suffering (<s>samudaya</s>). That indeed is to be abandoned (<s>prahātavya</s>). That indeed has been abandoned (<s>prahīṇa</s>)' — these are three turnings. In each turning, 'the eye arose, knowledge, insight, wisdom' — these are twelve aspects. Likewise for the truths of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) and the path (<s>mārga</s>), it should be applied. He says: 'If it is thus for each truth — three turnings and twelve aspects — then twelve turnings and forty-eight aspects follow. Why is it said "of three turnings and twelve aspects"?' Therefore it is said: 'Because of the homogeneity of threes and twelves, it is said to be of three turnings and twelve aspects.' Just like the teaching of dyads and the teaching of seven bases of skill. Like the teaching of dyads — and like the teaching of the seven bases of skill. Just as, having spoken in detail: 'I shall teach you a dyad, O <s>bhikṣu</s>; listen well and carefully, I shall speak. What is the dyad? The eye and forms, up to the mind and <s>dharma</s>s.' Just as here, because of the homogeneity of dyads, it is said 'a dyad' — so too, because of the homogeneity of threes and twelves, 'of three turnings and twelve aspects' is said. And just as 'a <s>bhikṣu</s> skilled in seven bases truly knows form; the arising of form; the cessation of form; the path leading to the cessation of form; the gratification of form, the danger, and the escape — truly knows them.' 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> skilled in seven bases, who investigates the meaning in three ways, quickly in this <s>dharma</s> and <s>vinaya</s> knows the end of suffering.' Because of the homogeneity of seven bases of skill for each aggregate individually — so here too, because of the homogeneity of threes and twelves, 'of three turnings and twelve aspects' is said. 'By these [turnings]' — and so forth in detail. By these turnings as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>darśanamārga</s> (seeing path), <s>bhāvanāmārga</s> (cultivation path), and <s>aśaikṣamārga</s> (non-learner's path) are shown respectively. 'This is the noble truth of suffering' — beginning from this, up to 'this is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering' — the seeing path is shown. 'That noble truth of suffering is to be fully comprehended through <s>abhijñā</s>' — beginning from this, up to 'that noble truth of the path is to be cultivated through <s>abhijñā</s>' — the cultivation path is shown. 'That noble truth of suffering has been fully comprehended through <s>abhijñā</s>' — beginning from this, up to 'that noble truth of the path has been cultivated through <s>abhijñā</s>' — the non-learner's path is shown. Here the <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'If so' — and so forth in detail. 'If so, these turnings show the seeing and other paths respectively. Then the seeing path alone is not of three turnings and twelve aspects. Rather, it is of one turning and four aspects.' How then is it established as the <s>dharmacakra</s>? The intent is: 'In the absence of three turnings

body.text:
cakrasādharmyābhāvān na cakraṃ yujyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. tasmāt sa eva dharmaparyāyo dharmacakraṃ. tad eva sūtraṃ dharmacakraṃ. dharmacakraprakāśanāt. triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ ca yujyate. tadarthaprakāśanāt. triḥparivartanād iti. duḥkhaṃ yāvan mārga ity ekaṃ parivartanaṃ. [Tib. 245b] parijñātavyaṃ yāvad bhāvayitavyam iti dvitīyaṃ. parijñātaṃ yāvad bhāvitam iti tṛtīyaṃ. caturṇāṃ satyānāṃ tridhākaraṇād iti. duḥkhaṃ samudayo nirodho mārga iti satyasvarūpaṃ praty eka ākaraṇaprakāraś caturākāraḥ. parijñātavyaṃ prahātavyaṃ sākṣātkartavyaṃ bhāvayitavyaṃ iti kartavyarūpāṃ parijñānakriyāṃ prati dvitīya ākaraṇaprakāraś caturākāraḥ. parijñātaṃ prahīṇaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ bhāvitam iti pariniṣṭhitāṃ parijñānādikriyāṃ
prati tṛtīya ākaraṇaprakāraś caturākāra iti. dvādaśākāraṃ bhavati. tasya punar iti. dharmaparyāyasya. pravartanaṃ parasaṃtānme gamanaṃ vineyajanasaṃtāne preraṇaṃ. kathaṃ gamanam. arthajñāpanāt. atha vā sarva evāryamārgo darśanabhāvanāśaikṣamārgo dharmacakraṃ. vineyajanasaṃtāne kramaṇāt. kramaṇāc cakram iti kṛtvā. yadi sarva evāryamārgo dharmacakraṃ. katham āryājñātakauṇḍinyasya darśanamārgamātrotpāde tat pravartitam ity uktaṃ. ata ucyate. tat tu parasaṃtāne āryakauṇḍinyasaṃtāne. darśanamārgotpādanād vartayitum ārabdham ādau vartitam ity etat pravartitam ity ucyate. ādikarmaṇi praśabdo vartate. prabhukta odana iti yathā.
body.translated_text: — because of the absence of the homology with a wheel — it cannot be a wheel.' Therefore, that very <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) is the <s>dharmacakra</s>. That very <s>sūtra</s> is the <s>dharmacakra</s> — because it illuminates the <s>dharmacakra</s>. And 'of three turnings and twelve aspects' is fitting — because it illuminates the meaning of that. 'Because of being turned three times' — suffering up to the path is one turning. 'To be fully comprehended' up to 'to be cultivated' is the second. 'Fully comprehended' up to 'cultivated' is the third. 'Because of presenting the four truths in three ways' — the intrinsic nature of the truths — suffering, origination, cessation, path — this is one mode of presentation with four aspects. The form of what is to be done — to be fully comprehended, to be abandoned, to be directly realized, to be cultivated — regarding the activity of comprehension, this is a second mode of presentation with four aspects.
