The completed activity of comprehension and the rest — fully comprehended, abandoned, directly realized, cultivated — this is a third mode of presentation with four aspects. Thus there are twelve aspects. 'The setting in motion of that [dharmaparyāya]' — of the <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. Setting in motion is its going to another's mental continuum, its impelling into the mental continuum of the trainable person. How is it a going? Through making the meaning known. Alternatively, all the Noble path — the seeing, cultivation, and non-learner's paths — is the <s>dharmacakra</s>. Because of its progression in the mental continuum of the trainable person. Because of its progression, it is a wheel — this being so. If all the Noble path is the <s>dharmacakra</s>, how is it said that it was set in motion upon the mere arising of the <s>darśanamārga</s> in the Noble <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>? Therefore it is said: 'That [dharmacakra], upon generating the <s>darśanamārga</s> in another's continuum — in the continuum of Noble <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> — having begun to turn, was initially set in motion.' The prefix 'pra-' applies to the initial action. Just as [one says] 'the food has been eaten (<s>prabhukta</s>)' [at the first mouthful].

body.text: (VI.57) tṛtīyasya tu kasmād aprāptir iti. rūpadhātūpapanno [Tib. 246a] yadi niyāmam avakrāmet. ṣoḍaśe cittakṣaṇe kasmād anāgāmiphalaprāptir na syād ity abhiprāyaḥ. parihāra ucyate.
body.translated_text: (VI.57) 'But why is the third [fruit] not attained?' — the meaning is: if one who has been reborn in the Form Realm were to enter the determined course (<s>niyāma</s>), why would the attainment of the fruit of <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner) not be [possible] at the sixteenth mind-moment? The answer is stated:

children.translated_text: 'For there is no seeing path above' —

body.text: iti. śravaṇābhāvād iti. ārūpyeṣu śrāvakabodhir eva bhavaṃtī bhavet. svayaṃbhubodher asaṃbhavāt. śrāvakābhisamayaś ca parato ghoṣam aṃtareṇa na bhavati. kiṃ ca adhodhātvanālaṃbanāc ca.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Because of the absence of hearing' — in the Formless [Realms], there could be <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple) awakening alone, since self-arisen (<s>svayaṃbhu</s>) awakening is impossible. And the realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) of a <s>śrāvaka</s> does not occur without hearing the voice of another. Moreover, 'because of not having lower realms as their object-domain' —

children.translated_text: 'The fundamental wholesome formless [attainments], being contaminated, do not have a lower [realm] as their domain' —

body.text: iti. traidhātukālaṃbanena ca darśanamārgeṇa bhavitavyam ity ataḥ. sa tatra na bhavatīti. vidhānaṃ vidhā upāya ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. And because the seeing path must have all three realms as its object-domain — therefore it does not occur there. 'Method' (<s>vidhāna</s>) means 'method' (<s>vidhā</s>), 'means' (<s>upāya</s>) — this is the meaning.

body.text: (VI.58, 59ab) parihāṇaṃ dharmaḥ svabhāvo 'syeti parihāṇadharmā. cetanādharmā ātmamāraṇadharmā. anurakṣaṇādharmā yas tāṃ vimuktim anurakṣituṃ śaknoti. sthitākaṃpyaḥ yasyāṃ viomuktau sthitaḥ. tasyāṃ akaṃpyaḥ. prativedhanābhavyaḥ. indriyasaṃcārabhavyaḥ. akopyadharmākopyo 'nivāryo dharmo 'syety akopyadharmā. sa ca dvividhaḥ. svabhāvatas tīkṣṇendriyaḥ.
body.translated_text: (VI.58, 59ab) 'One of the nature of falling away' (<s>parihāṇadharman</s>) — falling away is the <s>dharma</s> (nature), the inherent character, of this one — hence one of the nature of falling away. 'One of the nature of deliberation' (<s>cetanādharman</s>) — one whose nature is self-destruction. 'One of the nature of guarding' (<s>anurakṣaṇadharman</s>) — one who is able to guard that liberation. 'One who is stable and unshakable' (<s>sthitākampya</s>) — one who, being established in that liberation, is unshakable from it. 'One incapable of penetration' (<s>prativedhanābhavya</s>). 'One capable of faculty-transformation' (<s>indriyasaṃcārabhavya</s>). 'One of unshakable nature' (<s>akopyadharman</s>) — one whose <s>dharma</s> (nature) is unshakable, irremovable — hence one of unshakable nature. And that one is of two kinds: one with sharp faculties by nature

body.text: ndriyasaṃcāratas tīkṣṇendriyaś ca.
body.translated_text: and one with sharp faculties through faculty-transformation.

body.text: evety avadhāraṇaṃ. śraddhādhimuktā bhūtvā ete jātā ity arthaḥ. śraddhādhimuktapūrvakā iti yāvad uktaṃ bhavati. ṣaṣṭhas [Tib. 246b] tv anyathāpi bhavatīti vyākhyātaṃ sāmayikīti. samaye upakaraṇārogyadeśaviśeṣādilakṣaṇe bhavā sāmayikī. kāṃtā ca. kāṃtā cetovimuktiḥ. kasmāt kāṃteti. nityānurakṣyatvāt. kāṃtaṃ hi nityam anurakṣyam iti loke dṛśyate. sūtre 'py uktaṃ. tadyathā nāmaikākṣasya puruṣasya jñātaya ekam akṣi sādhu ca suṣṭhu cānurakṣitavyaṃ manyeran. māsya śītaṃ māsyoṣṇaṃ māsya rajo'ṃśavaś cakṣuṣi nipateyur māsya yad apy ekaṃ cakṣur avinaṣṭaṃ tad api vinaśyed iti. evam eva samayavimuktasyārhato 'nurakṣya eṣa dharmo 'nukaṃpyo 'nugrāhyaḥ. tata evaṃ samayavimukto 'rhan sādhu ca suṣṭhu cānurakṣitavyaṃ manyate. kaccid aham etasmād dharmān na parihīyeyeti. sa tasmān na parihīyata iti. ghṛtaghaṭavad iti. yathā ghṛtasya pūrṇo ghaṭo ghṛtaghaṭa iti bhavati. madhyagatasya pūrṇaśabdasya lopāt. yathā vā ghṛtāpekṣo ghaṭo ghṛtaghaṭo yatra ghṛtaṃ prakṣepsyate. apekṣaśabdalopāt ghṛtaghaṭa iti bhavati. evam ihāpi madhyagatasyāpekṣaśabdasya lopāt samayāapekṣāś caite vimuktāś ceti samayavimuktāḥ. samayaḥ punar upakaraṇādir ity [Tib. 247a] uktaṃ. kathaṃ kopayitum aśakyatvād ity āha. aparihāṇita iti. kālāṃtarātyaṃtavimuktito veti. kālāṃtaravimuktitaḥ samayavimuktatvam. atyaṃtavimuktito 'samayavimuktitvam ity arthaḥ. katham evam ity āha. parihāṇisaṃbhavāsaṃbhavataḥ. parihāṇisaṃbhavāt kālāṃtaravimuktyā samayavimukta ity ucyate. parihāṇyasaṃbhavād atyaṃtavimuktyāsamayavimukta ity ucyate.
body.translated_text: 'Only' is a restriction. The meaning is: having been faith-liberated (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>), these have arisen. What has been said is: they have the faith-liberated [state] as their predecessor. 'The sixth, however, is explained as arising otherwise too' — as 'occasional' (<s>sāmayikī</s>). That which exists at a particular occasion (<s>samaya</s>) characterized by favorable conditions, health, special location, and the like is occasional. 'And beloved (<s>kāntā</s>)' — the beloved liberation of mind (<s>cetovimukti</s>). Why 'beloved'? Because of needing to be constantly guarded. For in the world, it is seen that what is beloved must always be guarded. In the <s>sūtra</s> too it is stated: 'Just as the relatives of a one-eyed man would think that his one eye should be carefully and properly guarded — "May neither cold, nor heat, nor particles of dust fall upon his eye; may even his one undestroyed eye not be destroyed." In just this way, for the <s>arhat</s> liberated by occasion (<s>samayavimukta</s>), this <s>dharma</s> is to be guarded, to be protected, to be supported. Therefore, the <s>arhat</s> liberated by occasion thinks "it should be carefully and properly guarded" — "May I not fall away from these <s>dharma</s>s." And he does not fall away from them.' 'Like a ghee-pot' — just as a pot full of ghee becomes a ghee-pot — through the elision of the middle word 'full.' Or just as a pot in relation to ghee is a ghee-pot — [a pot] into which ghee will be poured — through the elision of the word 'in relation to,' it becomes 'ghee-pot.' Similarly here too, through the elision of the middle word 'in relation to': these are in relation to occasions and are liberated — hence 'liberated by occasion' (<s>samayavimukta</s>). An occasion, moreover, is favorable conditions and the rest — as stated. 'Because of being impossible to shake' — he says: 'from the perspective of non-falling-away.' 'Or from the perspective of temporary and ultimate liberation' — temporary liberation is liberation by occasion (<s>samayavimukta</s>); ultimate liberation is liberation not by occasion (<s>asamayavimukta</s>) — this is the meaning. How so? — he says: 'Because of the possibility and impossibility of falling away.' Because of the possibility of falling away, one is called liberated by occasion through temporary liberation. Because of the impossibility of falling away, one is called liberated not by occasion through ultimate liberation.

children.translated_text: 'And that one is a successor of the view-attained (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>)' —

body.text: iti. yadā śaikṣo bhūtvendriyāṇi saṃcarati. sa dṛṣṭiprāptatām āpadyate. atha svabhāvatas tīkṣṇendriyaḥ sa ṣoḍaśe cittakṣaṇe dṛṣṭiprāpta eva. tasmād asāv akopyadharmā dṛṣṭiprāptapūrvaka ity ucyate. yas tv arhattvāvasthāyām indriyāṇi saṃcarati. nāsāv akopyadharmā dṛṣṭiprāptapūrvaka ity avagaṃtavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. When, as a learner, one transfers one's faculties, one attains the state of being view-attained. Or, if one is of sharp faculties by nature, at the sixteenth mind-moment one is view-attained from the very beginning. Therefore, that one of unshakable nature (<s>akopyadharman</s>) is said to have the view-attained [state] as predecessor. But one who transfers faculties in the state of <s>arhat</s>ship — that one should be understood as not being an <s>akopyadharman</s> having the view-attained as predecessor.

body.text: (VI.59cd)

children.translated_text: 'Some are of the nature of deliberation (<s>cetanādharman</s>) from the very beginning as their lineage' —

body.translated_text: (VI.59cd)

body.text: iti. parihāṇadharmā nocyate. yasmād uttāpanāgato na bhavatīti. tadgotrā āditaḥ kecid ity apadiṣṭaṃ. tat kim idaṃ parihāṇadharmagotraṃ nāma yāvad akopyadharmagotram [Tib. 247b] iti na taiḥ parihāṇadharmādigotram apadiṣṭaṃ. tatra kecid evaṃ varṇayaṃti kuśalamūlāni gotram iti. kasyacid dhi tādṛśāni kuśalāni bhavaṃti. yaḥ parihāṇadharmā yāvad akopyadharmā. anye
body.translated_text: thus. 'The nature of falling away' (<s>parihāṇadharman</s>) is not stated — because one who has not reached the state of being heated (<s>uttāpanāgata</s>) cannot be [of that nature]. 'It has been stated that some [belong to] that lineage from the beginning.' But what then is this lineage of the nature of falling away, up to the lineage of unshakable nature? — the lineage of the nature of falling away and the rest has not been indicated by them. Therein, some explain thus: the wholesome roots are the lineage. For some person has wholesome roots of such a kind that he is of the nature of falling away, up to of unshakable nature. Others

body.text: punar āhuḥ pṛthagjanāvasthām ārabhyendriyabhedo gotram iti. sautrāṃtikāḥ punar varṇayaṃti bījaṃ sāmarthyaṃ cetaso gotram iti. pṛthagjanāvasthāyāṃ śaikṣāvasthāyāṃ ca parihāṇadharmabīje sati hetau parihāṇadharmagotraka ity ucyate. evam aśaikṣāvasthāyāṃ tadbījavṛttilābhāt parihāṇadharmety ucyate. evaṃ yāvad akopyadharmeti. tatra parihāṇadharmeti vistaraḥ. parihāṇadharmā yaḥ parihātuṃ bhavya iti. yady etāvad brūyāt. na ca cetanādidharmety etan na brūyāt. sarva evaite cetanādharmādayaś catvāraḥ parihātuṃ bhavyā ity eṣām evānyataraḥ parihāṇadharmā syāt. na tebhyo 'nyaḥ paṃcamaḥ. atas tebhyo 'nya evāyaṃ paṃcama iti viśeṣayan na ca cetanādidharmety āha. cetanādharmādīnāṃ punaś caturṇāṃ parihāṇadharmakatve 'sati [Tib. 248a] ekaikasya viśeṣalakṣaṇāpadeśād eva punar idaṃ vaktavyaṃ jāyate. cetanādharmā cetayituṃ bhavyo na cānurakṣaṇādharmā yāvat prativedhanābhavya iti. evam anurakṣaṇādharmā parihāṇipratyayaṃ balavaṃtam aṃtareṇeti. yadi parihāṇipratyayo balavān syāt parihīyeta sa ity abhiprāyaḥ. anena balavatpratyayavacanena parihāṇadharmaṇaḥ pūrvoktād viśinaṣṭi. parihāṇadharmā hy abalavatāpi parihāṇipratyayena parihīyate. parihāṇipratyayāḥ punar yathā sūtraṃ. paṃca hetavaḥ paṃcapratyayāḥ samayavimuktasyārhataḥ parihāṇāya saṃvartaṃte. katame paṃca. karmāṃtaprasṛto bhavati. bhāṣyaprasṛto bhavati. adhikaraṇaprasṛto bhavati. dīrghacārikāyogam anuyukto bhavati. dīrgheṇa ca rogajātena spṛṣṭo bhavatīti. ananurakṣann apīty anenānurakṣaṇādharmaṇo viśinaṣṭi. sa hy anurakṣann eva na parihīyeta. ayaṃ tv ananurakṣann apīti. ananurakṣayann api tatphalaṃ sthātuṃ bhavyas tatphale. na hātuṃ tatphalāt. nāpi vardhayituṃ prativedhanābhavyatāprāptyā. vinābhiyogena vinā vīryeṇa. anenārthād uktaṃ bhavati. yady abhiyogaṃ kuryād bhavyaḥ syād iti prativedhanābhavyāc cāyam evaṃ viśeṣito bhavati. [Tib. 248b] sa hi vinā apy abhiyogena prativeddhuṃ bhavya iti.
body.translated_text: say: the distinction of faculties beginning from the state of being an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) is the lineage. The <s>Sautrāntika</s>s, however, explain: a seed (<s>bīja</s>), a capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) of the mind, is the lineage. When, in the state of being an ordinary person or in the state of being a learner, there is the seed — the cause — of the nature of falling away, one is called 'of the lineage of the nature of falling away.' Similarly, in the state of being a non-learner, because of obtaining the activity of that seed, one is called 'of the nature of falling away.' Similarly, up to 'of unshakable nature.' Therein, 'of the nature of falling away' — in detail. One of the nature of falling away is one who is capable of falling away. If one were to say only this much — 'and not of the nature of deliberation and the rest' — without saying that, all these four — of the nature of deliberation and the rest — would be capable of falling away, and any one of these could be of the nature of falling away — not a fifth different from them. Therefore, distinguishing this one as a fifth different from them, he says: 'and not of the nature of deliberation and the rest.' As for the four — of the nature of deliberation and the rest — when they are not of the nature of falling away, one should state the specific characteristic of each individual one. 'Of the nature of deliberation — one who is capable of deliberating, not of the nature of guarding and the rest, up to not incapable of penetration' — thus. 'Similarly, of the nature of guarding — without a powerful cause of falling away' — the meaning is: if a powerful cause of falling away were present, he would fall away — this is the intent. By this mention of a powerful cause, he distinguishes [the nature of guarding] from the nature of falling away stated earlier. For the nature of falling away falls away even through a weak cause of falling away. 'Even without guarding' — by this he distinguishes from the nature of guarding. For that one does not fall away only when guarding. But this one, even without guarding [the fruit], is capable of remaining in that fruit — not of losing it, not of growing through obtaining the state of incapable-of-penetration (<s>prativedhanābhavya</s>). 'Without effort (<s>abhiyoga</s>), without energy (<s>vīrya</s>)' — by this, what has been implicitly stated is: if he were to make an effort, he would be capable [of penetration] — and thus he is distinguished from the incapable-of-penetration. For that one, even without effort, is capable of penetrating.

body.text: prathamau dvāv iti vistaraḥ. parihāṇadharmā sātatyasatkṛtyaprayogavikalaḥ. cetanādharmāpi sātatyaprayogeṇa vikalaḥ. viśeṣeṇa tu satkṛtyaprayogeṇa vikala ity anayor viśeṣaḥ. mṛdvindriyas tv iti ṣaṣṭhād viśinaṣṭi. ṣaṣṭho hi tīkṣṇendriyaḥ. indriyakṛto hy anayor viśeṣo na prayogakṛta iti. evaṃ ca kṛtveti vistaraḥ. yasmān nāvaśyam evaṃ bhavati. tasmād rūpārūpyadhātvor api ṣaḍ arhaṃto na kevalaṃ kāmadhātāv eva ṣaḍ ity abhiprāyaḥ. rūpārūpyadhātvor dvau sthitākaṃpya ekaḥ. akopyadharmā ca dvitīyaḥ. sthitākaṃpyas
body.translated_text: 'The first two' — in detail. One of the nature of falling away (<s>parihāṇadharman</s>) is deficient in continuous (<s>sātatya</s>) and reverential (<s>satkṛtya</s>) application. One of the nature of deliberation (<s>cetanādharman</s>) too is deficient in continuous application, but specifically deficient in reverential application — this is the distinction between them. 'But of dull faculties' — by this he distinguishes from the sixth. For the sixth is of sharp faculties. The distinction between these two is made by faculties, not by application. 'And having done so' — in detail. Because it is not necessarily always so — therefore the intent is: even in the Form and Formless Realms, there are six <s>arhat</s>s, not only in the Desire Realm. In the Form and Formless Realms, two [exist] — the stable-and-unshakable (<s>sthitākampya</s>) is one; and the unshakable (<s>akopyadharman</s>) is the second. The stable-and-unshakable

body.text: tāvad baddhābhiruciḥ syān na prativedhanābhavyatākriyādaravān iti. na kāmadhātau sthitākaṃpyaḥ prativedhanābhavyatām āpadyate. rūpārūpyadhātvaś ca parihāṇipratyayo balavān nāstīti. nāsau parihīyate. na cendriyāṇi saṃcaraṃtīti sthitākaṃpyagotraka eva saṃ tatra bhavati. akopyavimuktiyogāc cākopyadharmāpi bhavati. eveti dvāv eva tau bhavataḥ. nāto 'nye. tayo rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ parihāṇicetanendriyasaṃcārābhāvāt. parihāṇadharmā tāvat tatra nāsti. parihāṇyabhāvāt. anurakṣaṇādharmāpi nāsti. parihāṇyabhāvenānurakṣitavyāyogāt. [Tib. 249a] ata eva cendriyasaṃcārābhāvāt prativedhanābhavyo 'pi na bhavati. tathā coktaṃ.
body.translated_text: — that one would be attached to delight, but not earnest about attaining the state of incapable-of-penetration. The stable-and-unshakable does not attain the state of incapable-of-penetration in the Desire Realm. And in the Form and Formless Realms, there is no powerful cause of falling away — therefore that one does not fall away. Nor do faculties transfer [there] — therefore one of the lineage of stable-and-unshakable alone exists there. And one of unshakable nature also exists because of the connection with unshakable liberation (<s>akopyavimukti</s>). 'Only' — only those two exist, no others. Because of the absence of falling away, deliberation, and faculty-transfer in the Form and Formless Realms. First, the nature of falling away does not exist there — because of the absence of falling away. The nature of guarding also does not exist — because of the absence of anything to be guarded, due to the absence of falling away.

children.translated_text: 'That one born above is not subject to faculty-transfer or falling away' —

body.text: iti. tatra ca nātmasaṃcetanā na parasaṃcetanāstīti cetanādharmāpi na bhavatīti.
body.translated_text: from this statement. And there is neither self-deliberation nor other-deliberation — therefore the nature of deliberation also does not exist.

body.text: (VI.60ab) cetanādharmādīnāṃ caturṇām iti. cetanānurakṣaṇādharmasthitākaṃpyaprativedhanābhavyānāṃ. na hi parihāṇadharmā punaḥ svagotrāt parihīyata iti. tasya gotrasyākṛtrimatvāt. parihāṇadharmādīnāṃ paṃcānām iti. yasmāt parihāṇadharmaṇo 'pi phalāt parihāṇiḥ saṃbhavati. phalasyāgaṃtukatvāt.
body.translated_text: (VI.60ab) 'Of the four, [namely those] of the nature of deliberation and the rest' — of those of the nature of deliberation, guarding, stable-and-unshakable, and incapable-of-penetration. For one of the nature of falling away does not fall away from his own lineage — because that lineage is innate (<s>akṛtrima</s>). 'Of the five, [namely those] of the nature of falling away and the rest' — because for one of the nature of falling away too, falling away from the fruit is possible — because the fruit is adventitious (<s>āgantuka</s>).

body.text: iti. gotrāt phalāc ca. sa tasmān na parihīyata ity arhan. kasmād ity āha. śaikṣāśaikṣamārgābhyāṃ dṛḍhīkṛtatvād iti. yac chaikṣāvasthāyāṃ gotram asti. tac chaikṣeṇa mārgeṇa bhāvitaṃ. aśaikṣāvasthāyāṃ ca punar bhāvitam iti. tābhyāṃ dṛḍhīkṛtatvān na tasmāt so 'rhan parihīyate. śaikṣas tu katham ity āha. śikṣas tu laukikalokottarābhyāṃ dṛḍhīkṛtatvāt prathamāt gotrān na parihīyate. yat tad ātmīyaṃ prathamaṃ gotraṃ tal laukikena mārgeṇa pūrvaṃ bhāvitaṃ. śaikṣeṇa ca mārgeṇa punar bhāvitam iti. tato [Tib. 249b] na parihīyate.
body.translated_text: from lineage and from fruit. 'He does not fall away from that' — thus the <s>arhat</s>. Why? — he says: 'Because of being made firm by the learner's and non-learner's paths.' The lineage that exists in the learner's state — that was cultivated by the learner's path. And in the non-learner's state it was again cultivated. Because of being made firm by those two [paths], that <s>arhat</s> does not fall away from it. 'But the learner — how?' — he says: 'The learner, because of being made firm by the mundane and supramundane [paths], does not fall away from the first lineage.' That which is his own first lineage — that was previously cultivated by the mundane path. And by the learner's path it was again cultivated. Therefore he does not fall away from it.

body.text: atra kaścid āha. yad ucyate. yasya yat prathamaṃ gotraṃ. sa tasmān na parihīyate śaikṣāśaikṣamārgābhyāṃ dṛḍhīkṛtatvād iti. tad etad akāraṇaṃ. yasmād yo 'pi cetanādharmā uttāpanāgatas tasmāt gotrāt parihīyate. tad gotraṃ śaikṣāśaikṣābhyāṃ mārgābhyāṃ dṛḍhīkṛtam iti. parihāṇir na prāpnoti. tasmāt gotram eva tat tādṛśaṃ yasmād ādyān na parihīyate. uttāpanāgatāt tu parihīyata iti. yad apy uktaṃ śaikṣas tu laukikalokottarābhyāṃ dṛḍhīkṛtatvān na parihīyata ity etad apy akāraṇaṃ. srotaāpannasya parihāṇiprasaṃgāt. na hi srotaāpattiphalaṃ laukikena mārgeṇa dṛḍhīkṛtam iti. kartavyo 'tra yatna iti.
body.translated_text: Here someone says: 'What is stated — "he whose lineage is the first, he does not fall away from it, because of being made firm by the learner's and non-learner's paths" — that is not a [valid] reason. Because even one of the nature of deliberation (<s>cetanādharman</s>), when heated (<s>uttāpanāgata</s>), falls away from that lineage — and that lineage has been made firm by the learner's and non-learner's paths.' Therefore falling away is not precluded. Therefore, it is only such a lineage from which one does not fall away from the first [lineage], but one does fall away from what is attained through heating. 'And what was stated — "the learner, because of being made firm by the mundane and supramundane [paths], does not fall away" — that too is not a [valid] reason. Because of the consequence of falling away for the stream-enterer.' For the fruit of stream-entry has not been made firm by the mundane path. An effort should be made here.

body.text: atra vayam ācāryasyābhiprāyaṃ darśayāmo yenaivam uktaṃ. katham iti. yat tāvad uktaṃ cetanādharmā uttāpanāgatas tasmāt gotrāt parihīyata iti. tad ayuktaṃ. yad dhi cetanādharmagotraṃ śaikṣāvasthāyāṃ bhāvitaṃ punaś cāśaikṣāvasthāyām api bhāvitam iti dṛḍhīkṛtaṃ. naiva sa tasmād arhattvāt parihīyamāṇaḥ parihīyate. śaikṣāvasthāyāṃ prathamībhūtatvāt. uktaṃ cācāryasaṃghabhadreṇa yaḥ śaikṣāvasthāyāṃ gotrāṃtaram adhigamyārhattvaṃ prāpnoti. asāv [Tib. 250a] api taṃ mārgaṃ parityajati. na cottāpanāgata eva gotre nāvatiṣṭhata iti. yat tu cetanādharmagotram aśaikṣāvasthāyām idānīm evādhigataṃ na śaikṣāvasthāyām adhigataṃ. sa tasmāt parihīyamāṇaḥ parihīyate. tadavasthādvayādṛḍhīkṛtatvāt. iti na kāraṇam evaitad bhavati. yad apy uktaṃ śaikṣas tu laukikalokottarābhyāṃ mārgābhyāṃ dṛḍhīkṛtatvān na parihīyeta ity etad apy akāraṇaṃ. srotaāpannasya parihāṇiprasaṃgāt. na hi srotaāpattiphalaṃ laukikena lokottareṇa dṛḍhīkṛtam iti. tad apy anavabuddhyābhihitaṃ. tad gotraṃ prati kāraṇam ucyate. na phalaṃ prati. tatra hi kāraṇāṃtaraṃ vakṣyate. yena prathamāt phalān na parihīyate. na hi kiṃcid apy asti phalaṃ yad yugapad ubhābhyāṃ laukikalokottarābhyāṃ prāpyate. gotraṃ tu laukikalokottarābhyāṃ mārgābhyāṃ dṛḍhīkṛtaṃ bhavati. aihajanmikenoṣmagatādinā pārajanmikena vā prahāṇamārgeṇānyena vā laukikena mārgeṇa lokottareṇa śaikṣāvasthāyāṃ bhāvitatvāt. yat tu paścātpratilabdham uttāpanayeti. yad āgaṃtukaṃ gotraṃ paścād eva na dvayor avasthayor adhigataṃ tasmāt [Tib. 250b] parihīyate.
body.translated_text: Here we show the <s>Ācārya</s>'s intent by which he has spoken thus. How? First, as to what was stated — 'one of the nature of deliberation (<s>cetanādharman</s>), having been heated up, regresses from that lineage (<s>gotra</s>)' — that is improper. For the <s>cetanādharma</s>-lineage that was cultivated in the learner stage and then again cultivated in the non-learner stage as well has been strengthened. One who is regressing from that <s>arhat</s>ship does not regress [from that lineage]. Because it became primary in the learner stage. And <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> has stated: 'Even one who, in the learner stage, having attained another lineage, reaches <s>arhat</s>ship — [Tib. 250a] he too abandons that path. But it is not the case that one who was heated up does not remain in the lineage.' But the <s>cetanādharma</s>-lineage that was attained only now in the non-learner stage, not attained in the learner stage — one who is regressing from that does regress. Because it was not strengthened through the two stages. Thus this is not a reason at all. As to what was also stated — 'but a learner, because of being strengthened through both mundane and supramundane paths, does not regress' — that too is not a reason. Because it would absurdly follow that a stream-enterer would regress. For the fruit of stream-entry is not strengthened by both mundane and supramundane [paths]. That too was stated without understanding. That is stated as a reason with respect to the lineage, not with respect to the fruit. For therein another reason will be stated by which there is no regression from the first fruit. For indeed there is no fruit at all that is attained simultaneously by both mundane and supramundane [paths]. But the lineage is strengthened by both mundane and supramundane paths — because of having been cultivated in the learner stage by the mundane [path] beginning with heat (<s>uṣmagata</s>) in this very life or by the abandonment path in another life, or by another mundane path, or by the supramundane [path]. But what was obtained later by heating up — [Tib. 250b] what is an adventitious lineage obtained only later, not attained in the two stages — from that one regresses.

body.text: gotraṃ nirdiśya phalaṃ nirdiśyate. yasya ca yat prathamaṃ phalam iti vistaraḥ. ata eva ca srotaāpattiphalān nāsti parihāṇir iti. yasmāt srotaāpattiphalaṃ yadi prāpyate 'vaśyaṃ prathamaṃ bhavati. sakṛdāgāmyanāgāmiphale tu kadācit tu prathame bhavato yadi bhūyovītarāgakāmavītarāgayoḥ. kadācid aprathame yady ānupūrvikasya. tatra yadyat phalaṃ prathamaṃ bhavati srotaāpattiphalaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ anāgāmiphalaṃ vā. na tasmāt parihīyate. yat tu paścāt sakṛdāgāmiphalam anāgāmiphalaṃ arhattvaphalaṃ vā. tataḥ parihīyate. evaṃ ca kṛtveti. yasya ca yat prathamaṃ gotraṃ phalaṃ ca. sa tasmān na parihīyata iti kṛtvā. yathākramaṃ paṃca ṣaṭ sapta prakārā iti. anurakṣaṇādharmaṇaḥ paṃca prakārā bhavaṃti. tadavasthasya parinirvāṇam indriyasaṃcāraḥ parihāya vā śaikṣatvaṃ cetanādharmagotrapratyāgamanaṃ parihāṇadharmagotrapratyāgamanaṃ ca. sthitākaṃpyasya ṣaṭ prakārā bhavaṃti.
body.translated_text: Having indicated the lineage, the fruit is indicated. 'And whoever's first fruit' — and so forth in detail. For this very reason there is no regression from the fruit of stream-entry — because the fruit of stream-entry, if it is attained, necessarily becomes the first. But the fruits of once-returning and non-returning sometimes become the first — when there is one who has become more dispassionate (<s>bhūyovītarāga</s>) or one who is dispassionate from the Desire Realm (<s>kāmavītarāga</s>). And sometimes they are not the first — when there is one of sequential [practice] (<s>ānupūrvika</s>). Therein, whatever fruit becomes the first for a person — whether the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning — from that one does not regress. But what comes afterwards — the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or the fruit of <s>arhat</s>ship — from that one regresses. And thus, having considered this: whoever's first lineage and first fruit — that person does not regress from that — therefore, in order: five, six, and seven types should be formulated. One of the nature of guarding (<s>anurakṣaṇadharman</s>) has five types: <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in that very stage, change of faculties, learnership through regression, return to the <s>cetanādharma</s>-lineage, and return to the <s>parihāṇadharma</s>-lineage. One who is stable and unshakable (<s>sthitākampya</s>) has six types

body.text: ta eva ca paṃca anurakṣaṇādharmagotrapratyāgamanaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ. prativedhanābhavyasya sapta prakārā bhavaṃti. eta eva ca ṣaṭ sthitākaṃpyagotrapratyāgamanaṃ ca saptamam iti. yasya ca yat [Tib. 251a] prathamaṃ gotraṃ śaikṣāvasthāyām āsīt. sa śaikṣībhūtaḥ. punar iti vākyādhyāhāraḥ. tatraivāvatiṣṭhate nānyasmin. anyathā hi gotraviśeṣalābhāc chaikṣāvasthād gotrād viśiṣṭaṃ tad gotraṃ bhavatīti. ato viśiṣṭagotralābhāt vṛddhir evāsya pudgalasya syāt. na parihāṇir iti. kathaṃ kṛtvā. yathā tāvat parihāṇadharmā arhattvāvasthāyām indriyottāpanayā prativedhābhavyatāprāptaḥ. so 'rhattvāt parihīyate. śaikṣībhūtas tadgotrād api parihīyamāṇo na sthitākaṃpyagotre tiṣṭhati. pratilomato yāvan na cetanādharmagotre. kiṃ tarhi. parihāṇadharmagotra eva tiṣṭhatīti. anyathā hīti yady anyagotre 'vatiṣṭheta. gotraviśeṣalābhād iti parihāṇadharmagotraviśiṣṭagotralābhāt. tasmād avaśyam arhattvāt parihīyamāṇa indriyottāpanād api gotrāt parihīyata iti.
body.translated_text: — those same five plus return to the <s>anurakṣaṇadharma</s>-lineage as the sixth. One incapable of penetration (<s>prativedhanābhavya</s>) has seven types — those same six plus return to the <s>sthitākampya</s>-lineage as the seventh. And whoever's [Tib. 251a] first lineage was in the learner stage — that one, having become a learner, again — the word 'again' is a supplement to the sentence — remains in that very [lineage], not in another. For otherwise, because of obtaining a superior lineage, that lineage from the learner stage would become superior — and so, because of obtaining a superior lineage, there would only be advancement for this person, not regression. How is this so? Just as, for instance, one of the nature of falling away (<s>parihāṇadharman</s>), in the <s>arhat</s>ship stage, through the heating up of faculties, obtains incapability of penetration (<s>prativedhanābhavya</s>). That one, regressing from <s>arhat</s>ship, having become a learner, even when regressing from that lineage, does not remain in the <s>sthitākampya</s>-lineage. In reverse order, [one does not remain] even in the <s>cetanādharma</s>-lineage. Rather, one remains only in the <s>parihāṇadharma</s>-lineage. For otherwise — 'otherwise' means: if one were to remain in another lineage — because of obtaining a superior lineage — a lineage superior to the <s>parihāṇadharma</s>-lineage — because of that. Therefore, necessarily, one who is regressing from <s>arhat</s>ship, even when regressing from the lineage obtained by heating up of faculties, returns to the <s>parihāṇadharma</s>-lineage alone.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ prathamāt phalān nāsti parihāṇir iti. yasya yat prathamaṃ phalaṃ srotaāpattiphalaṃ vā sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ vā anāgāmiphalaṃ vā. darśanaheyānām avastukatvād anadhiṣṭhānatvād ity arthaḥ. ātmādhiṣṭhānapravṛttā hy eta iti vistaraḥ. ātmano 'dhiṣṭhānena pravṛttā ete darśanaheyāḥ. kasmād ity āha. satkāyadṛṣṭimūlatvāt. yasmād [Tib. 251b] ātmadarśanavaśena darśanaheyānāṃ samudācāraḥ. uktaṃ ca yāni vā punaḥ pṛthag loke dṛṣṭigatāni. tāni satkāyadṛṣṭimūlakāni satkāyadṛṣṭisamudayāni satkāyadṛṣṭijātīyāni satkāyadṛṣṭiprabhavānīti. sa cātmā nāstīty avastukatvān nāsti parihāṇir iti. satyālaṃbanatvād iti. satyānāṃ nityādito grahanāt. katamaś ca kleśo naivaṃ. bhāvanāprahātavyo 'pi hi rāgādir vitathālaṃbanaḥ. śucisukhanityātmākāraiḥ satyāditattvālaṃbanāt. ātmatvam abhūtam adhyāropayaṃtīti. yathoktaṃ. ye kecid bhikṣava ātmeti ātmīya iti samanupaśyaṃtaḥ samanupaśyaṃti. imān eva te paṃcopādānaskandhān ātmata ātmīyataś ca samanupaśyaṃtīti. tadadhiṣṭhānānupravṛttāś cāṃtagrāhādaya iti. ātmādhiṣṭhānānupravṛttāḥ. śāśvata ātmā. ucchedīti vā. nāsty ātmā. ayam evāgraḥ. iyam eva śuddhiḥ. kim asāv asti nāstītyevamādyākārapravṛttās tadanyaddarśanaheyā avastukā ucyaṃte. niradhiṣṭhānā ucyaṃta ity arthaḥ. na tv ātmādileśo 'stīti. ādigrahaṇenātmīyagrahaṇaṃ īśvarādigrahaṇaṃ vā. [Tib. 252a] pratiniyataṃ manaāpāmanaāpādilakṣaṇam iti. rāgasya bhāvanāheyasya manaāpaṃ keśadaṃtaśubhādilakṣaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: What then is the reason that there is no regression from the first fruit? Whoever's first fruit — whether the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning — because the [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing are insubstantial (<s>avastuka</s>) and without basis (<s>anadhiṣṭhāna</s>) — this is the meaning. For these operate based on self (<s>ātman</s>) as their basis — and so forth in detail. These [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing operate due to the basis of self. Why? — he says: because they are rooted in the view of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). Because [Tib. 251b] the manifestation of [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing is under the influence of the view of self (<s>ātmadarśana</s>). And it is stated: 'Whatever views (<s>dṛṣṭigata</s>) exist separately in the world — they are rooted in the view of the personal aggregate, arisen from the view of the personal aggregate, of the same kind as the view of the personal aggregate, originating from the view of the personal aggregate.' And since that self does not exist — because of insubstantiality, there is no regression. 'Because of having truth as object' — because of apprehending the truths as permanent and so forth. And which affliction is not so? Even [afflictions] to be abandoned by cultivation, such as desire and the rest, have an unreal object. Because of apprehending the truths [through the aspects of] pure, pleasant, permanent, and self — from the true reality of truth and the rest as object. They superimpose the unreal nature of self — as stated: 'Whatever monks view as self or as belonging to self — they view just these five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>) as self or as belonging to self.' And the extreme views (<s>antagrāha</s>) and the rest follow the basis of self — they follow the basis of the self. [Thinking:] 'The self is eternal,' or 'The self will be annihilated,' or 'There is no self,' or 'This alone is the highest,' or 'This alone is purity.' Those operating in such aspects — the other [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing are called insubstantial and without basis. The meaning is: they are called without foundation. But it is not that there is not even a trace of self and the rest. By the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), [it includes] the apprehension of 'belonging to self' (<s>ātmīya</s>) or the apprehension of 'a Lord' (<s>īśvara</s>) and the rest. [Tib. 252a] 'Having a distinct object characterized by what is agreeable and disagreeable and the like' — the object of desire (<s>rāga</s>), which is to be abandoned by cultivation, is what is agreeable — characterized by the beauty of hair, teeth, and the like

body.text: vastu. pratighasyāmanaāpaṃ tadaśubhatādilakṣaṇaṃ. mānasyāpi manaāpaṃ avidyāyā api tad eva dvayaṃ saṃmohanīyaṃ kiṃcid iti. na tu darśanaheyānām ātmādilakṣaṇam iti. na tu darśanaheyānām ātmātmīyalakṣaṇaṃ pratiniyataṃ vastu kiṃcid asti. anyatra tadālaṃbanebhyo rāgādibhyaḥ. tasmād avastukā ucyaṃte. tasmān na pratiniyatavastukā ucyaṃta ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: — that is its object. The object of aversion (<s>pratigha</s>) is what is disagreeable — characterized by the unattractiveness of that and the like. The object of pride (<s>māna</s>) too is what is agreeable. The object of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) too is that very twofold — something that causes delusion. But the [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing do not have self and the rest as their object — but the [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing do not have a distinct object characterized by self and belonging to self. No such object exists for them, apart from desire and the other [afflictions] that take those as their objects. Therefore they are called insubstantial — therefore they are called without a distinct object — this is the meaning.

body.text: api khalv iti vistareṇācāryaḥ. āryasya śaikṣasyānupanidhyāyato 'saṃtīrayataḥ smṛtisaṃpramoṣāt kliṣṭasmṛtiyogāt kleśa utpadyate. rāgādikaḥ. nopanidhyāyataḥ. rajjvām iva sarpasaṃjñā kasyacid anupanidhyāyataḥ smṛtisaṃpramoṣāj jāyate. nopanidhyāyataḥ. tadvat. ātmadṛṣṭyādīnām iti. aṃtagrāhadṛṣṭyādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ. kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ. na cānupanidhyāyata ātmadṛṣṭyādīnām utpattir yujyate. saṃtīrakatvāt. keṣām. ātmadṛṣṭyādīnāṃ kleśānāṃ. ato 'nupanidhyānād āryasyātmadṛṣṭyādīnām utpattir na yujyata iti. parihāṇikāraṇābhāvān nāsti darśanaheyaprahāṇāt [Tib. 252b] parihāṇir iti.
body.translated_text: 'Moreover' — and so forth, the <s>Ācārya</s> [explains] in detail. For a noble learner (<s>āryaśaikṣa</s>) who is not reflecting, not examining, because of the loss of mindfulness (<s>smṛtisaṃpramoṣa</s>), because of the application of defiled mindfulness (<s>kliṣṭasmṛti</s>), an affliction arises — desire and the rest. But not for one who is reflecting. Just as the perception of a snake in a rope arises for someone who is not reflecting, because of the loss of mindfulness — not for one who is reflecting — so it is in this case too. 'Of the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest' — the word 'and the rest' includes the apprehension of extreme views (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>) and the like. And what is the reason? The arising of the view of self and the rest is not possible for one who is not reflecting. Because they are examining (<s>saṃtīraka</s>). Of which? — of the afflictions such as the view of self and the rest. Therefore, because of non-reflection, the arising of the view of self and the rest is not possible for a noble one. Because of the absence of a cause for regression, there is no regression from the abandonment of what is to be abandoned by seeing.

body.text: arhattvād api nāstīti. na kevalaṃ darśanaheyaprahāṇān nāsti parihāṇir arhattvād api nāsti parihāṇir ity apiśabdena darśayati. aprathamābhyāṃ tu sakṛdāgāmyanāgāmiphalābhyāṃ parihāṇiḥ saṃbhavati. laukikena mārgeṇa tatprāptisaṃbhavād ity abhiprāyaḥ. eṣa eva ca nyāya ity ācāryaḥ samarthayati. tad dhi bhikṣavaḥ prahīṇam iti. tad eva prahīṇaṃ. yad āryaprajñayā prahīṇaṃ. tad dhi na punar utpadyate. laukikyā tu yat prahīṇaṃ. tat punar utpadyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. śaikṣasya cāpramāda iti vistareṇa dvitīyaṃ sūtrapadaṃ jñāpakam arhattvān nāsti parihāṇir iti. ayaṃ cāsyārthaḥ śaikṣasyāpramādanimittam apramādakarma pravedayāmy apramādaḥ śaikṣeṇa kartavya iti.
body.translated_text: 'From <s>arhat</s>ship too there is none' — not only is there no regression from the abandonment of what is to be abandoned by seeing, but from <s>arhat</s>ship too there is no regression — he shows this with the word 'too' (<s>api</s>). But from the non-first fruits of once-returning and non-returning, regression is possible — because it is possible to attain those through the mundane path — this is the intent. 'And this very reasoning' — the <s>Ācārya</s> supports [this]. 'For that, O monks, is abandoned' — that alone is abandoned which is abandoned by noble wisdom (<s>āryaprajñā</s>). That indeed does not arise again. But what is abandoned by the mundane [path] — that does arise again — this is the intent. 'And for a learner, non-negligence' — and so forth in detail, the second <s>sūtra</s>-passage is an indication that there is no regression from <s>arhat</s>ship. And this is its meaning: 'For a learner, I teach the deed of non-negligence as having non-negligence as its cause; non-negligence is to be practiced by a learner.'

body.text: nanu ca śaikṣasyāpy āryayā prajñayā prahāṇam asti. kathaṃ tasyāpramādakaraṇīyaṃ śāstīti. yasmād anadhigatam anena phalāṃtaram adhigaṃtavyaṃ. laukikamārgagataṃ ca tasya prahāṇam astīti. atra vaibhāṣiko brūyād arhato 'py aham ānanda lābhasatkāram aṃtarāyakaraṃ vadāmīti sūtre vacanād asty arhato 'pi parihāṇir ity ata idam ucyate. arhato 'pi vistareṇa yāvad atra sūtre dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāramātrād eva parihāṇir ukteti. [Tib. 253a] kathaṃ. yatra bhagavān āyuṣmaṃtam ānandam āmaṃtrayate sma. arhato 'py aham ānanda lābhasatkāram aṃtarāyakaraṃ vadāmīti. āyuṣmān ānanda āha. tat kasmād bhagavān evam āha. arhato 'py aham ānanda lābhasatkāram aṃtarāyakaraṃ vadāmīti. bhagavān āha. na haivānandāprāptasya prāptaye. anadhigatasyādhigamāya. asākṣātkṛtasya sākṣātkriyāyai. api tu ye 'nena catvāra
body.translated_text: But does a learner not also have abandonment by noble wisdom? How then is he instructed to practice non-negligence? Because he has another fruit yet unattained that must be attained. And because he has abandonment that was accomplished through the mundane path. To this a <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> would say: since in the <s>sūtra</s> it is stated 'For an <s>Arhat</s> too, O <s>Ānanda</s>, I declare gain and honor to be an obstruction,' therefore there is regression even from <s>arhat</s>ship — and so this is stated. 'For an <s>Arhat</s> too' — and so forth in detail, up to: in this <s>sūtra</s>, only regression from dwelling in happiness in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra</s>) is stated. [Tib. 253a] How? Where the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'For an <s>Arhat</s> too, O <s>Ānanda</s>, I declare gain and honor to be an obstruction.' The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'Why then does the <s>Bhagavān</s> speak thus — "For an <s>Arhat</s> too, O <s>Ānanda</s>, I declare gain and honor to be an obstruction"?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Not indeed, O <s>Ānanda</s>, for the attainment of what is unattained, for the realization of what is unrealized, for the direct experience of what is not directly experienced. But rather, the four

body.text: ādhicaitasikā dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārā adhigatāḥ. tato 'ham asyānyatamasmāt parihāṇiṃ vadāmi. tac cākīrṇasya viharataḥ. yā tv anenaikākināvyapakṛṣṭenāpramattenātāpinā prahitātmanā viharatā akopyā cetovimuktiḥ kāyena sākṣātkṛtā. tato 'syāhaṃ na kenacit paryāyeṇa parihāṇiṃ vadāmi. tasmāt tarhy ānandaivaṃ te śikṣitavyaṃ. yal lābbasatkāram abhibhaviṣyāṇo na cātyantair lābhasatkārakaiś cittaṃ paryādāya sthāsyati. evaṃ te ānanda śikṣitavyam iti. yadi vaibhāṣika evaṃ brūyāt. akopyā iti viśeṣaṇāt sāmayikyā asti parihāṇir iti. tata āha. sāmayikyā astīti ced iti. vayam apy evaṃ brūmaḥ. sāmayikyā asti parihāṇir iti. sā tu vicāryā sā tu sāmayikī vimuktir vicāryā. katham ity āha. kim arhattvaṃ sāmayikī vimuktir asti. [Tib. 253b] āhosvid dhyānāny eva laukikāni sāmayikī vimuktir iti. kasmād evam āśaṃkyata ity āha. maulo hi dhyānasamādhir iti. dhyānam eva samādhir dhyānasamādhiḥ. mauladhyānagrahaṇaṃ sukhapratipadām agratvāt. samaye saṃmukhībhāvāt. kasmiṃścit kāle niḥśabdādike saṃmukhībhāvāt. samaye bhavā samāyikī vimuktir ity ucyate. punaḥpunar eṣaṇīyatvāt kāṃteti. parihāṇau parihāṇau kamanīyatvāt prārthanīyatvād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: the mental <s>dharma</s>s that constitute the pleasant abiding in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra</s>) have been attained. From any one of those, I declare his falling away. And that [falling away occurs] when he dwells surrounded [by distractions]. But when he, dwelling alone, withdrawn, heedful, ardent, with a resolute mind, has directly realized with the body the unshakable liberation of mind (<s>akopyā cetovimukti</s>) — from that, I declare no falling away of his by any means whatsoever. Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, you should train thus: "I will overcome gain and honor, and my mind will not be overwhelmed by extreme gains and honors." Thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, you should train.' If the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> were to say: 'Because of the qualifier "unshakable," there is falling away from the occasional [liberation]' — to that he says: 'If [there is falling away] from the occasional.' We too say thus: there is falling away from the occasional [liberation]. But that [occasional liberation] should be examined — that occasional liberation should be examined. How? — he says: is <s>arhat</s>ship an occasional liberation? Or are merely the mundane <s>dhyāna</s>s the occasional liberation? Why is this doubted? — he says: 'For the main <s>dhyāna</s> concentration' — the <s>dhyāna</s> itself is the concentration — hence '<s>dhyāna</s>-concentration.' The main <s>dhyāna</s> is taken because of its being the foremost of the pleasant practices. 'Because of coming to the fore on an occasion (<s>samaya</s>)' — because of coming to the fore at some time, characterized by quiet conditions and the like. Because of existing on an occasion, it is called occasional liberation. 'Because of needing to be constantly sought, it is beloved (<s>kāntā</s>)' — upon each falling away, because of being desirable, because of needing to be sought — this is the meaning.

body.text: āsvādanīyatvād ity apara iti bhadaṃtarāmaḥ. sāsravatvād āsvādanāsaṃprayuktadhyānayogāt kāṃtety abhiprāyaḥ. arhattvavimuktis tv iti vistaraḥ. arhattvam eva vimuktir arhattvavimuktiḥ. nityānugatatvāt prāptiyogena. na yujyate sāmayikīty anena sāmayikyā vimukter viparyayeṇārhattvavimuktiṃ darśayati. apunaḥprārthanīyatvān na kāṃtety anena kāṃtaviparyaye 'rhattvavimuktir na kāṃteti. nityānugatatvenāstitvād aprārthanīyatvān na kāṃtety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Because of being savored' — says another — namely, the Venerable <s>Rāma</s>. Because of being contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>), because of its connection with <s>dhyāna</s> not dissociated from savoring — it is beloved — this is the intent. 'But the liberation of <s>arhat</s>ship' — and so forth in detail. <s>Arhat</s>ship itself is the liberation — hence 'liberation of <s>arhat</s>ship.' Because of being constantly accompanying — through the connection of acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>). 'It is not fitting [to call it] occasional' — by this, he shows the liberation of <s>arhat</s>ship by contrast with occasional liberation. 'Because of not needing to be sought again, it is not beloved' — by this, showing the reverse of the beloved, the liberation of <s>arhat</s>ship is not beloved. Because of existing as constantly accompanying, because of not needing to be sought — it is not beloved — this is the meaning.

body.text: ādhicaitasikebhya eveti. adhicetasi bhavā [Tib. 254a] ādhicaitasikā dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāḥ. tebhya eva. kim arthaṃ parihāṇim avakṣyad iti. ye te caitasikā drṣṭadharmasukhavihārā adhigatāḥ. tato 'ham asyānyatamasmāt parihāṇiṃ vadāmīti vacanāt. yady arhattvāt sāmayikī vimuktilakṣaṇāt parihāṇisaṃbhavo 'bhaviṣyat. kim arthaṃ tebhya eva parihāṇim avakṣyat. na tebhya eva parihāṇim avakṣyad ity arthaḥ. vaśitvabhraṃśād iti. samādhisaṃmukhībhāvavaśitvabhraṃśād ity arthaḥ. so 'parihāṇadharmeti. aparihāṇadharmā akopyadharmaṇo 'nyaḥ sūtre paṭhitaḥ. aṣṭādaśaśaikṣān vistareṇoktvāha. navāśaikṣāḥ katame. parihāṇadharmā. aparihāṇadharmā. cetanādharmā. anurakṣaṇādharmā. sthitākaṃpyaḥ. prativedhanābhavyaḥ. akopyadharmā.
body.translated_text: 'From the mental [attainments] alone' — those that exist in the higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>) are 'of the higher mind' (<s>ādhicaitasika</s>) — the pleasant abidings in the present life. From those alone. For what purpose would he speak of falling away? — because of the statement: 'Whatever mental [attainments] that are pleasant abidings in the present life have been attained by him — from any one of those, I declare his falling away.' If there were the possibility of falling away from <s>arhat</s>ship, characterized by occasional liberation — for what purpose would he speak of falling away from those alone? The meaning is: he would not speak of falling away from those alone. 'Because of the loss of mastery' — the meaning is: because of the loss of mastery over bringing concentration to the fore. 'That one is of the nature of non-falling-away' — one of the nature of non-falling-away, different from the <s>akopyadharman</s>, is read in the <s>sūtra</s>. Having stated the eighteen learners in detail, he says: 'What are the nine non-learners? One of the nature of falling away. One of the nature of non-falling-away. One of the nature of deliberation. One of the nature of guarding. One who is stable and unshakable. One incapable of penetration. One of unshakable nature.

body.text: prajñāvimuktaḥ. ubhayatobhāgavimuktaḥ. ima ucyaṃte navaśaikṣā iti. yaḥ parihīyate dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyaḥ. sa parihāṇadharmā. yo na parihīyate tata eva. so 'parihāṇadharmā. evaṃ [Tib. 254b] cetanādharmādayo 'pi yojyāḥ. kathaṃ. yaḥ samādhibhraṃśabhayād ātmānaṃ cetayate. sa cetanādharmā. yo 'nurakṣati kathaṃcid guṇaviśeṣaṃ. so 'nurakṣaṇādharmā. yo yasminn eva guṇe sthitaḥ. tasmād ananurakṣann api na kaṃpyate. sa sthitākaṃpyaḥ. yaḥ pareṇa pratividhyati. guṇaviśeṣam utpādayatīty arthaḥ. sa prativedhanābhavyaḥ. yo na kupyati utpannebhyo na parihīyate. so 'kopyadharmā.
body.translated_text: One liberated through wisdom. One liberated in both ways. These are called the nine non-learners.' One who falls away from the pleasant abidings in the present life — that one is of the nature of falling away. One who does not fall away from those very [abidings] — that one is of the nature of non-falling-away. Similarly, those of the nature of deliberation and the rest should be connected. How? One who, out of fear of losing concentration, deliberates regarding himself — that one is of the nature of deliberation. One who somehow guards the distinguished quality — that one is of the nature of guarding. One who, established in that very quality, is unshakable from it even without guarding — that one is stable and unshakable. One who penetrates further — the meaning is: produces a distinguished quality — that one is incapable of penetration. One who is not disturbed — who does not fall away from what has arisen — that one is of unshakable nature.

body.text: ko viśeṣa iti. aparihāṇadharmādīnāṃ trayāṇām aparihāṇiyogād viśeṣam apaśyan praśnayati. anuttāpanāgata iti. svabhāvatas tīkṣṇendriyaḥ. neṃdriyottāpanāṃ prāpta ity arthaḥ. tasmān na kaṃpyata iti. tasmāt guṇaviśeṣād ity arthaḥ. eṣa viśeṣo lakṣyata iti. ācāryaḥ svamataṃ darśayati. nanu cāyuṣmān gautiko 'rhattvāt parihīṇa ity evaṃ yadi vaibhāṣiko brūyād ity asya pratividhānam ārabhyate. āyuṣmān gautika iti vistaraḥ. śaikṣībhūta iti na tāvad arhan. śastram ādhārayann iti. śastraṃ vāhayan. kāyajīvitanirapekṣatvāt kāraṇān maraṇakāla evārhattvaṃ prāptaḥ. śastrādhārād uttarakāla ity arthaḥ. [Tib. 255a] parinirvṛttaś ca tenaiva śastraprahāreṇa.
body.translated_text: 'What is the distinction?' — not seeing a distinction among the three beginning with the nature of non-falling-away, because of their common characteristic of non-falling-away, he asks. 'One who has not reached the state of being heated (<s>uttāpanāgata</s>)' — one who is of sharp faculties by nature. The meaning is: one who has not attained the heating of faculties. 'Therefore he is not shaken' — the meaning is: from that quality. 'This distinction is to be noted' — the <s>Ācārya</s> shows his own view. 'But the venerable <s>Gautika</s> fell from <s>arhat</s>ship' — if the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> were to say this — the refutation of this is begun. 'The venerable <s>Gautika</s>' — and so forth in detail. 'He became a learner' — so he was not an <s>arhat</s> at that time. 'Wielding a weapon' — bearing a weapon. Because of indifference to body and life, from that cause, at the very time of death, he attained <s>arhat</s>ship. The meaning is: at the time after wielding the weapon. And he attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> by that very weapon-blow.

body.text: daśottare ceti. daśottaranāmasūtre. kim uktam ity āha. eko dharma utpādayitavyaḥ. katama ity āha. sāmayikī kāṃtā cetovimuktir iti. dṛṣṭadhārmasukhavihāra ity abhiprāyaḥ. eko dharmaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ. katama ity āha. akopyā cetovimuktir iti. arhattvam ity abhiprāyaḥ. pṛthagvacanād dhy akopyavimuktilakṣaṇād arhattvād arhattvasvabhāvā na kāṃtā cetovimuktir uktety abhiprāyaḥ. dviprakāratvād arhattvasya pṛthagvacanam iti vaibhāṣikavacanāvakāśaṃ paśyan punar āha. yadi cārhattvam iti vistaraḥ. yady arhattvam eva sāmayikī kāṃtā cetovimuktir abhaviṣyat. kim arthaṃ tatraiva daśake na sūtrāṃtare arhattvasya dvigrahaṇam akariṣyat. eko dharmaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ. akopyā cetovimuktir iti. naivākariṣyad ity arthaḥ. evaṃ hy avakṣyat. eko dharmaḥ sākṣātkartavyaś cetovimuktir iti. brūyās tv arhattvaṃ dviprakāram. ato vacanavibhāgenocyate. ekam utpādayitavyaṃ dvitīyaṃ sākṣātkartavyam iti. atra brūmaḥ. na ca kvacid arhattvam utpādayitavyam uktaṃ. [Tib. 255b] kiṃ tarhi. sākṣātkartavyam iti. tatratatra sūtre. abhyupetyāpi brūmaḥ. mṛdvindriyasaṃgṛhītaṃ cotpādayitavyam iti. kim anena jñāpanena jñāpitaṃ kathitaṃ bhavati. yadi tāvad utpādayituṃ śakyam ity etaj jñāpitaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: 'And in the <s>Daśottara</s>' — in the <s>sūtra</s> called <s>Daśottara</s>. What is said? — he says: 'One <s>dharma</s> is to be produced. What is it?' — he says: 'The occasional, beloved liberation of mind.' The intent is: the pleasant abiding in the present life. 'One <s>dharma</s> is to be directly realized. What is it?' — he says: 'The unshakable liberation of mind.' The intent is: <s>arhat</s>ship. Because of the separate statement, the intent is: the occasional, beloved liberation of mind, characterized by <s>arhat</s>ship, is not the unshakable liberation — hence the separate statement. He says: 'If there is a twofold nature of <s>arhat</s>ship, [that would justify] the separate statement' — seeing an opening for the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> statement, he further says: 'If indeed <s>arhat</s>ship were the occasional, beloved liberation of mind' — and so forth in detail. If <s>arhat</s>ship were the occasional, beloved liberation of mind, for what purpose in that very group of ten [in the <s>Daśottara</s>] would the twofold statement of <s>arhat</s>ship not have been made [as a single item]? 'One <s>dharma</s> is to be directly realized: the unshakable liberation of mind.' He would not have done so — this is the meaning. For thus he would have said: 'One <s>dharma</s> is to be directly realized: the liberation of mind.' 'You might say that <s>arhat</s>ship is twofold, therefore it is stated separately.' To this we say: nowhere is <s>arhat</s>ship [said to be] something to be produced. Rather, [it is said to be] something to be directly realized — in various <s>sūtra</s>s. 'Even accepting this, we say' — [accepting that] the one included in dull faculties is to be produced. What is indicated by this indication, what is conveyed? If this indicates that 'it is able to be produced' —

body.text: śaki liṅ ceti kṛtyapratyayalakṣaṇāt. anyad api śakyaṃ yat tīkṣṇendriyasaṃgṛhītam arhattvaṃ. tathā ca saty evaṃ sūtre vaktavyaṃ syāt. eko dharma utpādayitavyaḥ. cetovimuktir iti. athotpādanam arhatīty etaj jñāpitaṃ bhavati. arhe kṛtyatṛcaś ceti lakṣaṇaparigrahāt. anyat sutarām arhati yat tīkṣṇendriyasaṃgṛhītam arhattvaṃ. tad dhy akopyatvāt suṣṭhūtpādayitum arhatīty abhiprāyaḥ. kathaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. yadi sāmayikī vimuktir arhattvaṃ bhavati. evaṃ tadyogāt samaya vimukto 'rhann iti yujyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. samayāpekṣaḥ samādhisaṃmukhībhāva iti. yasmād asya samādhiḥ sāsravo 'nāsravo 'pi vā samayam ārogyadeśaviśeṣādilakṣaṇam apekṣate. abhidharme 'pi coktam iti vistaraḥ. kāmarāgānuśayo 'prahīṇo bhavatīty etad udāharaṇam. idaṃ cāpy udāharaṇaṃ. tatra cāyoniśomanaskāra iti. paripūrṇotpattir evam iti cet. syān matā paripūrṇakāraṇasya kleśasyaivam utpattiḥ. aparipūrṇakāraṇasya tu kleśasya viṣayabalād eveti. [Tib. 256a] tad ayuktaṃ. kasmād ity āha. kasya vāparipūrṇakāraṇasyotpattir iti. kasyotpattiḥ. yataḥ aparipūrṇakāraṇasyotpattir asti. yāvatī hi hetupratyayasāmagrī kāryasyotpattaye prasiddhā. sā tadekadeśavikalā satī tasyotpattaye na bhavati. tadyathā cakṣū rūpālokamanaskārasāmagrī cakṣurvijñānasyotpattaye prasiddhā. sa tadanyetaravikalā satī tadutpattaye na bhavatīti. tasmān na kiṃcid etat.
body.translated_text: from the rule 'the affixes of obligation (<s>kṛtya</s>) [indicate] ability' — the other too, which is included in sharp faculties — the <s>arhat</s>ship [of that type] — is also able [to be produced]. This being so, in the <s>sūtra</s> it should have been said: 'One <s>dharma</s> is to be produced — the liberation of mind.' Or if it indicates that 'it deserves to be produced' — from the acceptance of the rule 'the affixes of obligation [indicate] deservingness' — the other one, included in sharp faculties, all the more deserves [to be produced]. For that, being unshakable, properly deserves to be produced — this is the intent. 'How then?' — and so forth in detail. If occasional liberation is <s>arhat</s>ship, then by its connection, one would be an <s>arhat</s> liberated by occasion (<s>samayavimukta</s>) — this is the intent. 'The coming to the fore of concentration depends on an occasion (<s>samaya</s>)' — since his concentration, whether contaminated or uncontaminated, depends on an occasion characterized by favorable conditions, health, special location, and the like. 'And it is stated in the <s>Abhidharma</s> too' — and so forth in detail. 'The latent disposition of sensual passion is unabandon' — this is an example. And this too is an example: 'And therein, improper mental attention' — [referring to] the arising of afflictions. 'If [you say] that is [only] full production' — one might think: the arising of an affliction with a fully complete cause is thus [i.e., actual production]. But for an affliction with an incomplete cause, [it arises merely] by the force of the object. That is not right. Why? — he says: 'Whose arising is there with an incomplete cause?' Whose arising is there? Since whatever totality of cause-and-condition assemblage is established for the production of an effect — that, being deficient in one or another part, does not serve for the production of that [effect]. Just as the assemblage of the eye, form, light, and mental attention is established for the production of eye-consciousness — that, being deficient in one or another [factor], does not serve for the production of that [eye-consciousness]. Therefore this [argument about incomplete causes] amounts to nothing.

body.text: tadrūpa iti tatprakāraḥ. tatsvabhāva iti vā. atha notpanna iti pratipakṣaḥ tadbījadharmatāyām iti. kleśabījasvabhāva ity arthaḥ. tasyām anapoddhṛtāyām anunmūlitāyāṃ kathaṃ kṣīṇāsravo bhavatīti. brūyās tvaṃ na bhavatīti. ata āha. akṣīṇāsravo vā katham arhan bhavatīti.
body.translated_text: 'Of that nature' — of that kind, or of that own-nature. 'But if it has not arisen' — the antidote is [the topic]. 'In the nature of that affliction-seed' — the meaning is: in the own-nature of the affliction-seed. When that [nature] has not been extracted, not been uprooted — how can one be one whose outflows are destroyed (<s>kṣīṇāsrava</s>)? 'You might say: he does not become [one whose outflows are destroyed]' — therefore he says: 'Or, if his outflows are not destroyed, how can he be an <s>arhat</s>?'

body.text: evaṃcarata iti. smṛtimataś carata ity arthaḥ anaṃtaraṃ smṛtivacanāt. śaikṣas sa ity asya vacanasya parihārārthaṃ sa eva parihāṇivādy āha. sa hi tatrārhann eva jñāpita iti. kathaṃ kṛtvā jñāpita ity āha. dīrgharātram iti vistaraḥ. aparihāṇivādinaḥ syād evaṃ vacanāvakāśaḥ. śaikṣasyedaṃ vivekanimnacittam ucyate yāvan nirvāṇaprāgbhāram iti. asya parihārārthaṃ parihāṇivādī punar āha. arhato hy etad balam anyatroktam iti sūtre. kathaṃ. kati bhadaṃtārhato bhikṣoḥ kṣīṇāsravasya balāni. [Tib. 256b] aṣṭau śāriputrārhato bhikṣor dīrgharātraṃ vivekanimnaṃ cittaṃ yāvan nirvāṇaprāgbhāraṃ. aṃgārakarṣūpamāś cānena kāmā dṛṣṭā bhavaṃti. yathāsya kāmān jānataḥ kāmān paśyato yaḥ kāmeṣu kāmacchandaḥ kāmasnehaḥ vistareṇa yāvat kāmādhyavasānaṃ. tatrāsya cittaṃ na paryādāya tiṣṭhatīti vistaraḥ. kiṃ ca śītībhūtaṃ
body.translated_text: 'Thus conducting himself' — the meaning is: conducting himself with mindfulness, from the subsequent mention of mindfulness. 'He is a learner' — for the purpose of resolving this statement, the proponent of falling away says: 'For that one is indicated as an <s>arhat</s> in that very [sūtra].' How is he indicated? — he says: 'For a long time' — and so forth in detail. The proponent of non-falling-away would have this opening to say: 'This mind inclined toward seclusion, up to tending toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, is stated of a learner.' For the purpose of resolving this, the proponent of falling away says again: 'For this is stated elsewhere as a power of the <s>arhat</s>' — in the <s>sūtra</s>. How? 'How many, Venerable One, are the powers of an <s>arhat bhikṣu</s> whose outflows are destroyed?' 'Eight, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, are the powers of an <s>arhat bhikṣu</s>. For a long time, his mind is inclined toward seclusion, up to tending toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And sensual pleasures are seen by him as like a pit of burning coals. Such that for him, knowing sensual pleasures, seeing sensual pleasures — whatever desire for sensual pleasures, affection for sensual pleasures, in detail up to whatever adherence to sensual pleasures — his mind is not overwhelmed by them' — and so forth in detail. 'And what is more — [sensual pleasures are] cooled

body.text: vāṃtībhūtam iti cābhidhānāt. tatraivāṃgārakarṣūpame sūtre 'rhann eva jñāpita iti.
body.translated_text: and vomited' — from this designation. In that very burning-coal-pit <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>arhat</s> alone is indicated.

body.text: asty etad evam iti. aṃgārakarṣūpame yad uktam arhann eva jñāpita iti. yāvat tu cāro na supratividdha iti. piṇḍapātādicāraḥ. śaikṣāvasthām adhikṛtyaivaṃvacanād adoṣa iti. yad etad uktaṃ. kadācit smṛtisaṃpramoṣād utpadyaṃte pāpakā akuśalā vitarkā iti. tac chaikṣām adhikṛtyoktaṃ nārhattvāvasthāṃ. yat tūktaṃ dīrgharātraṃ vivekanimnaṃ iti. tac chaikṣasyāpi saṃbhavati. arhatas tu prakarṣeṇa bhavatīti viśeṣāḥ. yac cāpy uktaṃ sāsravasthānīyair dharmaiḥ śītībhūtaṃ vāṃtībhūtam iti. tad api śaikṣāvasthām adhikṛtya saṃbhavati. kāmāvacarāsravasthānīyadharmaśītībhāvābhidhānāt. [Tib. 257a] arhattvāvasthāṃ cādhikṛtya tathābhidhānād adoṣa iti ācāryasyābhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'This is so' — that in the burning-coal-pit [sūtra], what is said is indeed an indication of the <s>arhat</s>. 'But as long as conduct has not been well-penetrated' — the conduct of alms-rounds and the like. Because of this statement with reference to the state of being a learner — there is no fault. What was stated — 'sometimes, from loss of mindfulness, evil, unwholesome thoughts arise' — that was stated with reference to the state of being a learner, not the state of <s>arhat</s>ship. But what was stated — 'for a long time, [his mind is] inclined toward seclusion' — that too is possible for a learner. But for an <s>arhat</s>, it exists to an eminent degree — this is the distinction. And what was also stated — '[sensual pleasures are] cooled and vomited by <s>dharma</s>s that stand in the place of contaminated [dharmas]' — that too is possible with reference to the state of being a learner, from the designation of coolness toward <s>dharma</s>s that stand in the place of Desire Realm outflows. And with reference to the state of <s>arhat</s>ship too, such a designation [is possible] — there is no fault — this is the <s>Ācārya</s>'s intent.

body.text: (VI.60cd) prayogāsaṃbhavān na darśanamārga iti. paṃcadaśakṣaṇo darśanamārgaḥ. tatrendriyasaṃcāre prayogāvakāśo nāsti. kaścit pṛthagjanāvasthāyām indriyāṇi saṃcaratīti. [kim anityādyākārapatitena mārgeṇendriyāṇi saṃcarati.] kim audārikādyākāreṇa mārgeṇendriyāṇi saṃcarati. utāho śāṃtādyākāreṇeti. aviśeṣitatvād ubhayathāpi saṃbhavatīti paśyāmaḥ. tathā hy enam artham ācāryaḥ sūcayiṣyati. na hi sāsraveṇa mārgeṇāryāṇām indriyasaṃcāra ity āryāṇām iti viśeṣaṇāt. api nāma mamendriyāṇi tīkṣṇāni syur iti prayogam abhisaṃdhāya. mārgaṃ laukikaṃ lokottaraṃ cānyasyānaṃtaryavimuktimārgakrameṇendriyāṇi saṃcaratīti veditavyaṃ. kaścic chraddhādhimuktāvasthāyām ity atrāśaikṣavacanaṃ. śaikṣapṛthagjanādhikārāt. aśaikṣo 'pi tv iṃdriyāṇi saṃcaratīti boddhavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: (VI.60cd) 'Because of the impossibility of application, not the seeing path' — the seeing path has fifteen moments. Therein, there is no opportunity for application to faculty-transfer (<s>indriyasaṃcāra</s>). Someone transfers faculties in the state of being an ordinary person. [Does one transfer faculties through a path that falls under aspects of impermanence and so forth?] Does one transfer faculties through a path of coarse and other aspects, or through a path of peaceful and other aspects? Since no distinction has been specified, we consider that it is possible in both ways. For the <s>Ācārya</s> will indicate this meaning thus: 'Not through a contaminated path do Noble ones transfer faculties' — the qualifier 'of Noble ones' [implies the distinction]. With the intention of applying effort: 'May my faculties become sharp!' — one should understand that faculties are transferred through mundane and supramundane paths in the sequence of uninterrupted and liberation paths, in another way. Someone [says] 'in the state of faith-liberation (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>)' — here the word 'non-learner' [is used] because the context concerns learners and ordinary persons. But it should be understood that a non-learner too transfers faculties.

body.text: (VI.61) katham akopyadharmaṇo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyaḥ parihāṇir iti. tīkṣnendriyatvād asya dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyaḥ parihāṇir na saṃbhavet. kim utākopyāyā vimukter ity asaṃbhāvayan pṛcchati. buddhasyopabhogaparihāṇir eveti. vineyakāryavyāpṛtatvād [Tib. 257b] dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārān nopabhuṃkte. na saṃmukhīkarotīty arthaḥ. sā cāprāptaparihāṇiś ceti. akopyadharmaṇaḥ sā copabhogaparihāṇiḥ kutaścid vyāsaṃgāt. aprāptiparihāṇiś ca pudgalaviśeṣadharmaprāpaṇāt. yasmād akopyadharmāpi kaścin mahāśrāvakāṇām āryaśāriputramaudgalyāyanādīnāṃ prāṃtakoṭikādīn dharmān. svayaṃbhuvāṃ ca kāṃścid dharmān na prāpnoti. mahāśrāvakā api svayaṃbhuvāṃ kāṃścid viśeṣadharmān na prāpnuvaṃtītyādi. anyasyārhata iti parihāṇadharmāder mṛdvindriyasya prāptaparihāṇir apy asti. apiśabdāt pūrvokta api
body.translated_text: (VI.61) 'How can there be falling away from pleasant abidings (<s>dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra</s>) for one of unshakable nature (<s>akopyadharman</s>)?' — since this one has sharp faculties, falling away from pleasant abidings should not be possible — how much less from unshakable liberation — he asks, expressing impossibility. 'For the <s>Buddha</s>, it is only enjoyment-falling-away' — because of being occupied with the task of training disciples, he does not enjoy the pleasant abidings, does not bring them to the fore — this is the meaning. 'And that is also non-attainment-falling-away' — for one of unshakable nature, that enjoyment-falling-away is due to some preoccupation; and the non-attainment-falling-away is because of not attaining certain <s>dharma</s>s specific to particular persons. For even one of unshakable nature among the great <s>śrāvaka</s>s — the Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, and others — does not attain certain <s>dharma</s>s such as <s>prāntakoṭika</s> and the like belonging to the self-arisen ones (<s>svayaṃbhu</s>). The great <s>śrāvaka</s>s too do not attain certain special <s>dharma</s>s of the self-arisen ones, and so forth. For another <s>arhat</s> — one of the nature of falling away (<s>parihāṇadharman</s>) and others with dull faculties — there is also attainment-falling-away. By the word 'also' (<s>api</s>), the previously stated [types of falling away]

body.text: parihāṇī sta iti. akopyadharmaṇa upabhogaparihāṇivacanāt sūtravirodha iti. yad etad uktaṃ. ye 'nena catvāra iti vistareṇa. yāvat tato 'ham asyānyatamasmāt parihāṇiṃ vadāmīti. tasya sutrasyāvirodhaḥ. ṣaṇṇām apy arhatām akopyā vimuktir ity ukte vaibhāṣiko brūyāt. yadi sarvasyaivārhato 'nāsravā vimuktir akopyā. kasmād asamayavimukta evākopyadharmā vyavasthāpito nānya iti. ata idam ucyate. sarvasyānāsravā vimuktir [Tib. 258a] akopyeti. satyam asty etat. akopyadharmavyavasthānaṃ tu yathā tathoktam iti. dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyas tu kaścil lābhasatkāravyākṣepadoṣāt parihīyate vaśitvabhraṃśāt. yo mṛdvindriyaḥ. kaścin na parihīyate. yas tīkṣṇendriyaḥ. sa evākopyadharmā vyavasthāpitaḥ. yata eva ca dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyo lābhasatkāravyākṣepadoṣāt parihīyate. mṛdvindriyo na tīkṣṇendriyaḥ. ata etad acodyaṃ. katham. akopyadharmaṇo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāt parihāṇir ity aparihāṇivādī. atha vā ayam anyaḥ saṃbaṃdhaḥ. pūrvam akopyadharmaṇo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyaḥ parihāṇir nāstīty uktaṃ. sūtre ca. yasyākopyā vimuktiḥ. tasya dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāt parihāṇir uktā. aviśeṣyābhidhānād ata idam ucyate. sarvasyānāsravā vimuktir akopyeti. na tayaivākopyadharmā vyavasthāpyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. ata evocyate akopyadharmavyavasthānaṃ tu yathā tathoktam iti. ata etad acodyam iti. yad uktaṃ sūtram āśritya katham akopyadharmaṇo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyaḥ parihāṇi iti.
body.translated_text: also exist — this is the meaning. 'Because of the statement of enjoyment-falling-away for one of unshakable nature, there is contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s>' — referring to what was stated: 'Those four' and so forth in detail, up to 'Therefore I declare his falling away from one of these.' The non-contradiction with that <s>sūtra</s> [is explained]. 'When it is said that the unshakable liberation of all six types of <s>arhat</s>s [is unshakable]' — the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> would say: 'If indeed the uncontaminated liberation of every <s>arhat</s> is unshakable, why is only the non-occasionally-liberated (<s>asamayavimukta</s>) established as one of unshakable nature and not the others?' Therefore this is stated: 'The uncontaminated liberation of all is unshakable' — truly this is so. 'But the establishment of the unshakable nature is as has been stated' — [meaning] someone falls away from pleasant abidings due to the fault of distraction by gain, honor, and fame — through loss of mastery — one who has dull faculties; someone does not fall away — one who has sharp faculties. That very one is established as of unshakable nature. And precisely because one falls away from pleasant abidings due to the fault of distraction by gain, honor, and fame, one with dull faculties [falls away], not one with sharp faculties — therefore this is not a valid objection: 'How can there be falling away from pleasant abidings for one of unshakable nature?' — [says] the proponent of non-falling-away. Alternatively, this is another connection: previously it was stated that there is no falling away from pleasant abidings for one of unshakable nature. And in the <s>sūtra</s>, for one whose liberation is unshakable, falling away from pleasant abidings is stated. Since no distinction is made, therefore this is stated: 'The uncontaminated liberation of all is unshakable' — not by that alone is one established as of unshakable nature — this is the intent. Therefore it is said: 'But the establishment of the unshakable nature is as has been stated.' Therefore this is not a valid objection — referring to what was stated relying on the <s>sūtra</s>: 'How can there be falling away from pleasant abidings for one of unshakable nature?'

body.text: (VI.62) dhandhā iti mandāḥ. anyathā hy [Tib. 258b] anāśvāsikam iti. yady arhattvāt parihīṇaḥ punar jāyeta sucīrṇabrahmacarye 'smin mārge cāpi subhāvite tuṣṭa āyuḥkṣayād bhavati rogasyāpagame yathety āśvāsaḥ. evaṃvidho na syād iti. tad akāryam abrahmacaryādilakṣaṇaṃ śūrapraskhalanāpatanavad iti. yathā śūrasya praskhalane apatanaṃ bhavati śaktita ātmadhāraṇāt. tadvad āryaḥ phalāt parihīṇo 'pi tatphalam alabdhvā na mriyate. śūragrahaṇam avihvalatvāt. balavāṃ chūra ity apare.
body.translated_text: (VI.62) 'Slow' (<s>dhandhā</s>) means 'sluggish.' 'Otherwise, for there would be no reassurance' — if one who has fallen from <s>arhat</s>ship were to be reborn again, then with the holy life well-practiced and this path well-cultivated, one is satisfied, and by the exhaustion of life one dies — just as upon the disappearance of a disease — this is the reassurance. Such [reassurance] would not exist. 'That wrongdoing, characterized by unchaste conduct and the like, is like the stumbling and falling of a hero' — just as when a hero stumbles, there is a fall but [recovery] is possible through self-support by his own strength, similarly a Noble one, even when fallen from a fruit, does not die without having regained that fruit. The term 'hero' (<s>śūra</s>) is used because of not being confounded. 'A strong hero' — say others.

body.text: (VI.63, 64) katham abhyastam ity āha. śaikṣāśaikṣamārgābhyāṃ dṛḍhīkṛtatvād iti prayogamārgas tu sarvatraika eveti. akopyaprativedhe dṛṣṭiprāptatāyāṃ ca.
body.translated_text: (VI.63, 64) 'How is it practiced?' — he says: 'Because of being made firm by the learner's and non-learner's paths.' But the path of application is the same everywhere. [This refers to] the penetration of unshakable nature and the attainment of view-attained status.

body.text: na hi sāsraveṇeti. āryendriyasaṃcārasya vivakṣitatvāt. anyathā hi kaścit pṛthagjanāvasthāyāṃ indriyāṇi saṃcaratīty etad virudhyate.
body.translated_text: 'Not through a contaminated [path]' — because the faculty-transfer of Noble ones is what is intended. Otherwise, the statement 'Someone transfers faculties in the state of being an ordinary person' would be contradicted.

body.text: nānyatra parihāṇyasaṃbhavād iti. parihāṇibhayād dhīndriyasaṃcāra iṣyate. anyatra ṣaṭsu kāmāvacareṣu devanikāyeṣu rūpārūpyadhātvoś ca parihāṇir nāstīty āha. ūrdhavdhātūpapanna āryo naivendriyāṇi saṃcarati. nāpi kathaṃcit
body.translated_text: 'Not elsewhere, because of the impossibility of falling away' — faculty-transfer is desired because of the fear of falling away. Elsewhere — in the six divine classes of the Desire Realm and in the Form and Formless Realms — there is no falling away, he says. 'A Noble one born above does not transfer faculties at all, nor does he in any way

body.text: parihīyate [Tib. 259a] iti. uktam atra kāraṇaṃ. kālāntaraparivāsenendriyāṇāṃ paripakvataratvāt. āśrayaviśeṣalābhāc ceti. atha kasmāt kāmāvacareṣu deveṣu parihāṇir nāsti. ye pūrvam abhyudārebhyo 'pi viṣayebhyaḥ saṃvijaṃto niyataṃ satyāni paśyaṃti. te kathaṃ tān evālaṃbya parihāsyaṃte. avaśyaṃ hi te tīkṣṇendriyā bhavantīty abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: fall away' — thus. The reason has been stated here: because of the faculties becoming more mature through the passage of time, and because of obtaining a special basis (<s>āśraya</s>). 'But why is there no falling away among the Desire Realm <s>deva</s>s?' — Those who previously, having been revulsed even from excellent sense objects, determinately see the truths — how would they fall away by depending on those very [sense objects]? The intent is: they must necessarily have sharp faculties.

body.text: tatphalasya navabhūmisaṃgṛhītatvasaṃbhavāt. phalaṃ phalaviśiṣṭaṃ ceti. phalaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ. phalaviśiṣṭaṃ prathamadhyānādi prahāṇāya prayogānantaryavimuktiviśeṣamārgalakṣaṇaṃ. phalamārgam eva pratilabhata iti. kāmadhātuvairāgyamātrasaṃgṛhītaṃ. na cānāgāmiphalam ārūpyasaṃgṛhītam iti. paṃcānām avarabhāgīyānāṃ prahāṇād anāgāmīti sūtre vacanāt. darśanamārgasya ca tatrābhāvāt. tadabhāvaḥ kāmadhātvanālaṃbanād iti vyākhyātam etat.
body.translated_text: because of the possibility that the fruit of that [non-learner] is included in nine grounds. 'The fruit and the fruit-distinguished' — the fruit is the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>). The fruit-distinguished refers to the distinctive path characterized by the application, uninterrupted, and liberation paths for the purpose of abandoning the first <s>dhyāna</s> and so forth. 'He obtains the fruit-path alone' — [meaning] that which is included merely in the dispassion from the Desire Realm, and the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>) is not included in the Formless [Realm]. Because the <s>sūtra</s> states: 'One is a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) because of the abandonment of the five lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīya</s>).' And because the seeing path does not exist there. 'The absence of that is because it does not have the Desire Realm as its object-domain' — this has been explained.

body.text: (VI.65ab) akopyadharmā ca dvividha iti. sūtre paṭhitatvāt akopyabheda eva
body.translated_text: (VI.65ab) 'And one of unshakable nature is twofold' — because it is read in the <s>sūtra</s>. The division of the unshakable is indeed

body.text: iti. akopyadharmā mṛdumadhyādhimātrendriyabhedāt tridhā bhidyate. śrāvako hy akopyadharmādhimātramṛdvindriyaḥ. [Tib. 259b] pratyekabuddho 'dhimātramadhyendriyaḥ. samyaksaṃbuddho 'dhimātrādhimātrendriya iti. mṛdumṛdvādinavaprakārendriyabhedād iti. parihāṇidharmā mṛdumṛdvindriyo yāvad bhagavān adhimātrādhimātrendriya iti.
body.translated_text: thus. One of unshakable nature is divided threefold by the distinction of dull, medium, and sharp faculties. For the <s>śrāvaka</s> of unshakable nature has the supremely dull faculties; the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> has the supremely medium faculties; the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> has the supremely sharp faculties. 'By the ninefold distinction of faculties — dull-dull and so forth' — one of the nature of falling away has the dullest-dull faculties, up to the <s>Bhagavān</s> who has the supremely sharp faculties.

body.text: (VI.65cd, 66ab) sapta bhavaṃtīti. pratyekabuddhasamyaksaṃbuddhāv ubhayatobhāgavimuktasaṃgṛhītāv eveti kṛtvā. pūrvam eveti vistaraḥ. pūrvam eva pṛthagjanāvasthāyāṃ parapratyayena parataḥ śrutvā smṛtyupasthānādīn dharmān. paścād artheṣu prayogāt. cintābhāvanāsevanād ity arthaḥ. tathā pūrvam eva pṛthagjanāvasthāyāṃ prajñayā dvādaśāṃgapravacanadharmānusāreṇa svayam evaṃ bodhipakṣādīn dharmān anusarann artheṣu prayogāt. cintābhāvanāsevanāt. ity evaṃ prayogataḥ śraddhādharmānusāriṇau bhavataḥ. śraddhādhimokṣaprajñādhikyata iti. śraddhādhimokṣādhikyataḥ prajñādhikyataś ca. śraddhayādhimokṣaḥ śraddhādhimokṣaḥ. tasyādhikyān mṛdvindriyatvaṃ. prajñādhikyāt tīkṣṇendriyatvaṃ. vimuktita iti. kleśavimuktitaḥ prajñayā kleśād vimuktaḥ prajñāvimukta iti kṛtvā. samāpattivimuktita iti. samāpattito vimuktitaś ca.
body.translated_text: (VI.65cd, 66ab) 'There are seven [persons]' — considering that the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> and <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> are both included in the category of those liberated on both sides (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>). 'From the very beginning' — in detail. From the very beginning, in the state of being an ordinary person, having heard from others through reliance on others, [learning] <s>dharma</s>s such as the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) and the rest; afterwards, through application to the meanings, through reflection, cultivation, and practice — this is the meaning. Similarly, from the very beginning, in the state of being an ordinary person, through one's own wisdom, following the <s>dharma</s>s such as the aids to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) and the rest in accordance with the twelve-fold word of the teaching, independently following the meanings through application — through reflection, cultivation, and practice. Thus, from application, the faith-follower (<s>śraddhānusārin</s>) and the <s>dharma</s>-follower (<s>dharmānusārin</s>) arise. 'Because of the preponderance of faith-conviction and wisdom' — because of the preponderance of faith-conviction (<s>śraddhādhimokṣa</s>) and because of the preponderance of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). Faith-conviction (<s>śraddhādhimokṣa</s>) is conviction through faith; because of its preponderance, there are dull faculties; because of the preponderance of wisdom, there are sharp faculties. 'From liberation' — from liberation from afflictions. One who is liberated from afflictions through wisdom is 'wisdom-liberated' (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>) — considering this. 'From attainment-liberation' — and from liberation through attainment.

body.text: tatrendriyata [Tib. 260a] iti vistaraḥ. yathaite śraddhānusāriṇo gaṇyaṃte. tathā yathāgranthaṃ pradarśayiṣyāma. indriyatas trayaḥ. mṛdumadhyādhimātrendriyatvāt.
