body.translated_text: 'Therein, from faculties' — in detail. Just as these faith-followers are counted, so we shall show according to the text. From faculties, there are three — because of having dull, medium, and sharp faculties.

body.text: atra punar evam avagantavyaṃ. yady api śraddhānusāriṇaḥ sarva eva mṛdvindriyāḥ. tathāpi tāratamyenāvasthānād eṣāṃ punas tridhābhedaḥ mṛdumadhyādhimātrendriyā iti. gotrataḥ paṃca. kathaṃ. parihāṇadharmagotrako yāvat prativedhanābhavyagotraka iti paṃca bhavaṃti. punar eṣāṃ gotrendriyabhedāt paṃcadaśānām ekaiko mārgataḥ paṃcadaśa bhavaṃti. katham ity ucyate. aṣṭakṣāntisaptajñānasthā iti. darśanamārgo hi paṃcadaśakṣaṇāḥ. aṣṭau kṣāntayaḥ. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāṃtir yāvan mārge anvayajñānakṣāntiḥ. sapta jñānāni. duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ yāvan mārge dharmajñānaṃ. mārge 'nvayajñānasya bhāvanāmārgasaṃgṛhītatvāt. aṣṭau ca sapta ca paṃcadaśa bhavanti. ta evaṃ tatrasthāḥ paṃcadaśa bhavaṃti. evam eṣāṃ mārgataḥ paṃcadaśadhābhinnānāṃ punar ekaiko vairāgyatas trisaptatiḥ. kathaṃ. sakalabandhanas tāvat kāmadhātāv ekaḥ. kāmavairāgyān nava. ekaprakāravītarāgo yāvan navaprakāravītarāgaḥ. evaṃ yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanavairāgyān naveti. bhavāgravairāgyān naveti na saṃbhavati. laukikasya mārgasya bhavāgrapratipakṣasyābhāvāt. ta ete 'ṣṭau navakā dvisaptatiḥ. [Tib. 260b] sakalabandhanena pūrvoktena saha trisaptatir bhavaṃti. punar ete vairāgyataḥ pratyekaṃ trisaptatibhinnāḥ. pratyekam āśrayato nava. katham ity āha. tridvīpaṣaḍdevanikāyajā iti. trayo dvīpā uttarakuruvarjyāḥ. uttarakurau mārgābhāvāt. ṣaḍ devanikāyāḥ kāmāvacarāḥ. tata ūrdhvaṃ darśanamārgābhāvāt. teṣu jātā iti. pratyekam ete navaguṇā bhavaṃti. indriyagotramārgavairāgyāśrayataḥ piṇḍitā iti. nigamana ucyate. iyanta iti vṛttau likhitāḥ. evam anye 'pi pudgalāḥ saṃbhavataḥ saṃkhyeyā iti. dharmānusāriprabhṛtayaḥ. yathendriyagotramārgavairāgyāśrayataḥ śraddhānusāriṇaḥ saṃkhyātāḥ. tathaiva saṃkhyeyāḥ saṃbhavata iti. dharmānusāridṛṣṭiprāptasamayavimuktānāṃ gotrabhedo nāsti. śraddhādhimuktasamayavimuktayos tu gotrabhedo 'py astīti. saṃbhavata ity ucyate. tatrendriyatas trayo dharmānusāriṇaḥ. gotrata eka eveti bhedo nāsti. mārgataḥ paṃcadaśa aṣṭakṣāntisaptajñānasthāḥ. vairāgyatas trisaptatiḥ. sakalabandhanaḥ. kāmavairāgyān nava. evaṃ yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanavairāgyāt. [Tib. 261a] āśrayato nava. tridvīpaṣaḍdevanikāyajā iti. evam indriyamārgavairāgyāśrayataḥ piṇḍitāḥ. sahasrāṇy ekānnatriṃśat saṃpadyaṃte. śatāni ca paṃca paṃcaṣaṣṭiś ca. evam indriyatas trayaḥ śraddhādhimuktāḥ. gotrataḥ paṃca pratyekaṃ. vairāgyatas trisaptatiḥ pratyekameva pūrvavat. āśrayato nava. tridvīpaṣaḍdevanikāyajā iti. evam indriyagotravairāgyāśrayataḥ piṇḍitāḥ. nava sahasrāṇi saṃpadyante.
body.translated_text: Here, moreover, it should be understood thus: although all faith-followers (<s>śraddhānusārin</s>) have dull faculties, nevertheless, because of their standing in degrees of gradation, they are further divided threefold — those of mild, middling, and intense faculties. By lineage (<s>gotra</s>), five — how? Those of the lineage of falling away (<s>parihāṇadharmagotra</s>), up to those of the lineage of incapable-of-penetration (<s>prativedhanābhavyagotra</s>) — thus there are five. Furthermore, of those fifteen [resulting from] the division by lineage and faculty, each one by path-[moment] becomes fifteen — how is this stated? 'Standing in the eight <s>kṣānti</s>s and seven <s>jñāna</s>s.' For the seeing path (<s>darśanamārga</s>) consists of fifteen moments. Eight <s>kṣānti</s>s (patient acceptances): <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> regarding suffering, up to <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> regarding the path. Seven <s>jñāna</s>s: <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding suffering, up to <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding the path — because the <s>anvayajñāna</s> regarding the path is included in the cultivation path (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>). Eight and seven make fifteen. Thus those standing therein become fifteen. Of these, each one of the fifteen differentiated by path further becomes seventy-three by dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) — how? First, one with complete bondage (<s>sakalabandhana</s>) in the Desire Realm is one. From Desire Realm dispassion, nine — one dispassionate from one type, up to one dispassionate from nine types. Likewise, up to dispassion from the Nothingness sphere (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), nine. 'From dispassion from the Peak of Existence, nine' — this is not possible, because of the absence of a mundane path that is the antidote of the Peak of Existence. These are eight nines, which make seventy-two. Together with the previously mentioned one with complete bondage, they become seventy-three. Furthermore, these seventy-three differentiated by dispassion each individually [become] nine by basis (<s>āśraya</s>) — how? He says: 'Born in the three continents and six <s>deva</s>-classes.' The three continents exclude <s>Uttarakuru</s> — because of the absence of the path in <s>Uttarakuru</s>. The six <s>deva</s>-classes are those of the Desire Realm. Above that, because of the absence of the seeing path. Those born in them — individually, these become nine-fold. 'Aggregated by faculty, lineage, path, dispassion, and basis' — the conclusion is stated. 'So many' — are written in the <s>vṛtti</s> (auto-commentary). 'Similarly, other persons too are to be enumerated as they arise' — the <s>dharma</s>-followers (<s>dharmānusārin</s>) and the rest. Just as the faith-followers have been enumerated by faculty, lineage, path, dispassion, and basis — in the same way they are to be enumerated as they arise. For the <s>dharmānusārin</s>, the view-attained (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>), and the occasionally-liberated (<s>samayavimukta</s>), there is no distinction by lineage. But for the faith-liberated (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>) and the occasionally-liberated, there is also distinction by lineage — therefore 'as they arise' is said. Therein, by faculty there are three <s>dharma</s>-followers. By lineage, only one — hence there is no distinction. By path, fifteen — standing in the eight <s>kṣānti</s>s and seven <s>jñāna</s>s. By dispassion, seventy-three. By basis, nine — born in the three continents and six <s>deva</s>-classes. Thus, aggregated by faculty, path, dispassion, and basis, twenty-nine thousand five hundred and sixty-five are obtained. Similarly, by faculty there are three faith-liberated (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>). By lineage, five each. By dispassion, seventy-three each, just as before. By basis, nine — born in the three continents and six <s>deva</s>-classes. Thus, aggregated by faculty, lineage, dispassion, and basis, nine thousand

body.text: śatāni cāṣṭau paṃca paṃcāśac ca. kevalaphalastho ṣoḍaśacittaprāpto 'dhikṛtaḥ.
body.translated_text: eight hundred and fifty-five are obtained. 'Only the fruit-attainer at the sixteenth mind-moment is under discussion.'

children.translated_text: 'The faith-liberated (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>) and the view-attained (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>) are [respectively] of dull and sharp faculties — that' —

body.text: anayo iha vivakṣitatvāt.
body.translated_text: — is what is intended here.

body.text: bhagavadviśeṣas tv āha. mārgato nava bhavaṃti. bhāvanāmārgasthatvād iti. tan na budhyāmahe kenābhiprāyeṇaivam uktam iti. yady ayam abhiprāyo bhavet. mārgato bhūmaubhūmau nava bhavantīti. vairāgyatas trisaptatir iti sa evārtho darśito bhavet. tatavyatirekād iti. yuktaṃ syāt. tad eva hi parimāṇaṃ syāt. atha navabhūmikānāsravabhāvanāmārgasthatvān navatvam eṣāṃ vyavasthāpyeta. tathā sati. tatparimāṇaṃ punar navaguṇīkriyeta. etāvantaś ca bhaveyur aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi. śatāni ca ṣaṭ. paṃcanavatiś cety evam uttaratrāpi vaktavyaṃ. yadi tu śraddhādhimukta ā vajropamāt samādher gṛhyeta. tato 'nyathā gaṇayitavyaṃ. indriyatas trayaḥ śraddhādhimuktāḥ. [Tib. 261b] gotrataḥ paṃca pratyekaṃ. vairāgyata ekāśītiḥ trisaptattau bhavāgrāṣṭaprakāravītarāgān aṣṭāv adhikān prakṣipya. āśrayata ekānnatriṃśat. kathaṃ kāmadhātau navopapattisthānāni. rūpadhātau ṣoḍaśa sthānāni. catvāraś cārūpyā iti. evam indriyagotravairāgyāśrayataḥ piṇḍitāḥ sahasrāṇi paṃcatriṃśat. śate ca dve. paṃcatriṃśac ceti. dṛṣṭiprāptasya gotrabhedo nāsti. indriyavairāgyāśrayataḥ piṇḍitāḥ sahasraṃ saṃpadyante. śatāni ca nava. ekā saptatiś ca. yadi tv ā vajropamāt samādher dṛṣṭiprāpto gṛhyate. tata evaṃ saṃkhyātavyāḥ. indriyavairāgyāśrayataḥ piṇḍitāḥ. saptacatvāriṃśad adhikāni sapta sahasrāṇi saṃpadyante. kāyasākṣī śraddhādhimuktadṛṣṭiprāptayor antarbhūta iti na gaṇyate. yadi punar gaṇyate indriyatas trayaḥ. yadi śraddhādhimuktaḥ sa kāyasākṣī gotrataḥ paṃca. yadi dṛṣṭiprāpto nāsti gotrabhedaḥ. mārgata ubhayor api nāsti bhedaḥ. ākiṃcanyāyatanavītarāgatvāt vairāgyato 'pi nāsti bhedaḥ. yady api bhavāgre sakalabandanaḥ ekaprakāravītarāgo yāvad aṣṭaprakāravītarāga iti. mārgato vairāgyato vāsti bhedaḥ. na tu mārgavairāgyakṛtaṃ kāyasākṣitvam iti. nāsya tatkṛtas tadbhedo vyavasthāpyate. [Tib. 262a] āśrayato vā bahudhābhedaḥ. kāmāvacarāśrayatvāt yāvad bhavāgrāśrayatvād iti bhagavadviśeṣaḥ. katham ākāśānaṃtyāyatanādyāśrayaḥ kāyasākṣī bhavati. evaṃ tu yuktaṃ paśyāmaḥ. āśrayataḥ paṃcaviṃśatiḥ. kāmadhātau navopapattisthānāni. rūpadhātau ca ṣoḍaśa sthānāniti. tatra hy āryo nirodhasamāpattim utpādayet. yadi tu kāmarūpāśrayotpāditanirodhasamāpattiyogāt kāyasākṣībhūtasyānāgāminaḥ. tatsamanvāgamamātraprayogāt.
body.translated_text: But <s>Bhagavadviśeṣa</s> says: 'By path, they become nine — because of standing in the cultivation path (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>).' We do not understand with what intent this was said. If this were the intent — 'by path, on each ground they become nine' — then the meaning 'by dispassion, seventy-three' would already be shown thereby. Because of the distinction from that [interpretation], it would be fitting. For the measure itself would be that same. But if the nine-ness of these is established because of standing in the uncontaminated cultivation path of nine grounds — in that case, their measure would again be multiplied by nine. And they would become so many: eighty-eight thousand, six hundred and ninety-five — this should be stated for the subsequent [calculations] as well. If, however, the faith-liberated (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>) is taken up to the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s>, then the calculation should be done differently. By faculty, three faith-liberated ones. By lineage, five each. By dispassion, eighty-one — adding eight additional [persons] dispassionate from eight types of the Peak of Existence to the seventy-three. By basis, twenty-nine — how? In the Desire Realm, nine birth-locations. In the Form Realm, sixteen locations. And four formless [realms]. Thus, aggregated by faculty, lineage, dispassion, and basis, thirty-five thousand two hundred and thirty-five are obtained. For the view-attained (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>), there is no distinction by lineage. Aggregated by faculty, dispassion, and basis, one thousand nine hundred and seventy-one are obtained. But if the view-attained is taken up to the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s>, then they should be enumerated thus: aggregated by faculty, dispassion, and basis — seven thousand and forty-seven are obtained. The body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣin</s>), being included in the faith-liberated and the view-attained, is not counted [separately]. But if he is counted: by faculty, three. If the body-witness is faith-liberated, by lineage, five. If view-attained, there is no distinction by lineage. By path, for both there is no distinction — because of being one dispassionate from the Nothingness sphere. By dispassion too, there is no distinction. Even though at the Peak of Existence one with complete bondage, one dispassionate from one type, up to one dispassionate from eight types — there is distinction by path or dispassion. Yet the body-witness status (<s>kāyasākṣitva</s>) is not produced through the path or dispassion — therefore no distinction of body-witness produced thereby is established. By basis, there could be manifold distinction — because of being based in the Desire Realm, up to based in the Peak of Existence. But <s>Bhagavadviśeṣa</s> [says]: how can a body-witness have the Infinity of Space sphere and the rest as basis? But we see it thus as fitting: by basis, twenty-five — nine birth-locations in the Desire Realm and sixteen locations in the Form Realm. For there a Noble one would produce the cessation-attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>). But if the body-witness status of a non-returner who produced the cessation-attainment with a Desire or Form Realm basis is accepted — merely through the connection of possessing that [attainment]

body.text: paścād api bhavāgrāśrayaṃ kāyasākṣitvam iṣyeta. bhavāgraṃ ṣaḍviṃśatitama āśrayaḥ syād ity avagantavyaṃ. evam indriyagotrāśrayataḥ parigaṇya gaṇayitavyaḥ. prajñāvimuktasyāpi bhedaḥ. indriyatas trayaḥ prajñāvimuktaḥ. gotrataḥ paṃca. yadi samayavimuktāḥ. athāsamayavimuktā nāsti bhedaḥ. evam ubhayatobhāgavimukto 'pi yojayitavyaḥ.
body.translated_text: — subsequently, even a body-witness status with the Peak of Existence as basis may be accepted. The Peak of Existence would be the twenty-sixth basis — this should be understood. Thus, having enumerated by faculty, lineage, and basis, the body-witness should be calculated. The distinction of the wisdom-liberated (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>) too [is as follows]: by faculty, three are wisdom-liberated. By lineage, five — if they are occasionally-liberated (<s>samayavimukta</s>). But if non-occasionally-liberated (<s>asamayavimukta</s>), there is no distinction. Similarly, the one liberated in both ways (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>) too should be applied.

body.text: (VI.66cd) prajñāsamādhibalābhyāṃ kleśavimokṣāvaraṇavimuktatvād iti. prajñābalena kleśāvaraṇavimuktatvāt. samādhibalena ca vimokṣāvaraṇavimuktatvāt. vimokṣāḥ punar aṣṭau vakṣyante rūpī rūpāṇi paśyatīti vistaraḥ. tatra kleśāvaraṇam [Tib. 262b] iti. kleśā evāvaraṇaṃ. vimokṣāvaraṇaṃ iti. vimokṣāṇām āvaraṇaṃ. tat punaḥ kāyacittayor akarmaṇyatā. yayā vimokṣān utpādayituṃ na śaknotīti.
body.translated_text: (VI.66cd) 'Because of being liberated from the obstruction of afflictions and from the obstruction of liberation through the power of wisdom and concentration respectively' — because of being liberated from the obstruction of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) through the power of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), and because of being liberated from the obstruction of liberation (<s>vimokṣāvaraṇa</s>) through the power of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>). The liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), moreover, are the eight that will be stated: 'One possessing form sees forms,' and so forth in detail. Therein, 'obstruction of afflictions' — the afflictions themselves are the obstruction. 'Obstruction of liberation' — the obstruction of the liberations. And that is the unfitness-for-work (<s>akarmaṇyatā</s>) of body and mind, because of which one is unable to produce the liberations.

body.text: (VI.67) kleśān prahāyeha hi yas tu paṃceti. paṃcāvarabhāgīyāni saṃyojanāni satkāyadṛṣṭyādīny uktāni. ahāryadharmety aparihāṇidharmety arthaḥ. phalata eveti vistaraḥ. śraddhādhimuktatvān nendriyataḥ paripūrṇatvam. akāyasākṣitvān na samāpattitaḥ. anāgāmitvāt tu phalataḥ paripūrṇatvam asti. indriyata eveti. dṛṣṭiprāptatvād indriyataḥ paripūrṇatvam. avītarāgatvāt tu na phalato nāpi samāpattitaḥ. anāgāmiphalasamāpattyor abhāvāt evam anyeṣām api saṃbhavato yojyaṃ. samāpattita eveti. samāpattita eva paripūrṇatvaṃ nendriyaphalābhyām iti nāsty etat. kasmāt. na hy asatyām anāgāmiphalaprāptau nirodhasamāpattir asti. samāpattīndriyataś ca vinā phaleneti. samāpattīndriyata eva ca paripūrṇatvaṃ na phalata ity etad api nāsti. yasmād anāgāmiphalam aprāptasya nirodhasamāpattir nāstīti. indriyataḥ samāpattitaś ceti. [Tib. 263a] tīkṣṇendriyatayā nirodhasamāpattilābhatayā cety arthaḥ. indriyata eveti vistaraḥ. asamayavimuktasyeti vacanāt. asyendriyataḥ paripūrṇatvaṃ. prajñāvimuktasyeti vacanāt. na samāpattito 'sya paripūrṇatvaṃ. anirodhasamāpattilābhī hi prajñāvimukta ity uktaṃ. samāpattita eveti. samayavimuktasyeti vacanāt. nendriyataḥ paripūrṇatvam asya bhavati. ubhayatobhāgavimuktasyeti vacanāt. samāpattito 'sya paripūrṇatvaṃ. nirodhasamāpattilābhīty ubhayatobhāgavimukta ity uktaṃ. indriyasamāpattibhyāṃ. kiṃ. paripūrṇatvaṃ. asamayavimuktatvād indriyataḥ ubhayatobhāgavimuktatvāt samāpattita iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: (VI.67) 'One who has abandoned five afflictions here' — the five lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīya saṃyojana</s>), namely <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and the rest, which have been stated. 'Of irremovable nature' (<s>ahāryadharma</s>) — meaning one of the nature of non-falling-away (<s>aparihāṇidharman</s>). 'From the perspective of the fruit alone' — and so forth in detail. Because of being faith-liberated (<s>śraddhādhimukta</s>), there is no completeness from the perspective of faculties. Because of not being a body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣin</s>), not from the perspective of attainment. But because of being a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>), there is completeness from the perspective of the fruit. 'From the perspective of faculties alone' — because of being view-attained (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>), there is completeness from the perspective of faculties. But because of not being dispassionate [from the Desire Realm], not from the perspective of the fruit, nor from the perspective of attainment — because of the absence of the non-returner fruit and the [cessation-]attainment. Similarly, for the others, it should be applied as they arise. 'From the perspective of attainment alone' — there is no such case. Why? Because there is no attainment of the cessation-attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) without the attainment of the non-returner fruit. 'From the perspectives of attainment and faculties, and without the fruit' — this too does not exist. Because, as stated, without the non-returner fruit attainment, the cessation-attainment does not exist. 'From the perspectives of faculties and attainment together' — the meaning is: from the perspective of sharp faculties and from the perspective of the cessation-attainment. 'From the perspective of faculties alone' — and so forth in detail. Because of the statement 'non-occasionally-liberated' (<s>asamayavimukta</s>), there is completeness from the perspective of faculties. Because of the statement 'wisdom-liberated' (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>), there is no completeness from the perspective of attainment — for it has been stated that one who has not attained the cessation-attainment is wisdom-liberated. 'From the perspective of attainment alone' — because of the statement 'occasionally-liberated' (<s>samayavimukta</s>), there is no completeness from the perspective of faculties. Because of the statement 'liberated in both ways' (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>), there is completeness from the perspective of attainment — for it has been stated that one who has attained the cessation-attainment is liberated in both ways. 'From the perspectives of both faculties and attainment' — what? — completeness. Because of being non-occasionally-liberated, completeness from the perspective of faculties; because of being liberated in both ways, completeness from the perspective of attainment — he shows this.

body.text: (VI.68) ānantaryamārgo yenāvaraṇaṃ prajahātīti. aprahāṇamārgasaṃbhavāt. asti sa ānantaryamārgo yenāvaraṇaṃ na prajahāti. indriyasaṃcārādiṣu.
body.translated_text: (VI.68) 'The <s>ānantaryamārga</s> (uninterrupted path) is that by which one abandons obstructions' — because of the possibility of a non-abandonment path, there exists an <s>ānantaryamārga</s> by which one does not abandon obstructions — in the cases of faculty-transfer (<s>indriyasaṃcāra</s>) and the like.

body.text: yas tatpraheyāvaraṇanirmuktaḥ prathamata iti. ya ānantaryamārgapraheyeṇāvaraṇena nirmuktaḥ. prathamata iti viśeṣaṇaṃ. yasmāt tṛtīyādiṣu kṣaṇeṣu tajjātīyo [Tib. 263b] mārgo viśeṣamārga itīṣyate. tena eva cāha. viśeṣamārgo ya ebhyo 'nyo mārga iti. prayogamārgādibhyo 'nya ity arthaḥ. kiṃ ca yadi prathamata iti na brūyāt. vimuktimārgo yas tatpraheyāvaraṇanirmukta ity etāvad brūyāt. evaṃ sati duḥkhadharmajñānāt pareṇa sarve ānantaryamārgādayas tatpraheyāvaraṇanirmuktā utpadyanta iti. sarve vimuktimārgāḥ syuḥ. aniṣṭaṃ caitat. ānantaryamārgādiṣv api vimuktimārgaprasaṃgāt. tasmād ānantaryamārgasya duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāntyāder yatpraheyam āvaraṇaṃ. duḥkhadarśanaprahātavyo nikāyo yāvad bhāvanāprahātavyaḥ. tena praheyāvaraṇena nirmukto yaḥ prathamata utpadyate. sa vimuktimārgaḥ. nānyas tat praheyāvaraṇanirmuktatve 'pīti. ya ebhyaḥ prayogamārgādibhyas tribhyo 'nyaḥ. sa viśeṣamārgaḥ. ṣoḍaśān mārgānvayajñānakṣaṇāt pareṇa saptadaśādayas tajjātīyā ye 'nāsravāḥ kṣaṇāḥ. te viśeṣamārgasvabhāvā ity avagantavyaṃ. evam anyad api vimuktijñānaṃ. yat prākarṣikaṃ kṣayajñānādi. tad api vaktavyaṃ. yaś ca dṛṣṭadharmasakhavihārāya vaiśeṣikaguṇābhinirhārāya vā mārgaḥ. so 'pi viśeṣamārga [Tib. 264a] eva prayogamārgo yasmād ānantaryamārgotpattir ity uktaṃ. ato laukikā agradharmāḥ prayogamārga iti gamyate. yas tu pratilomataḥ kṣāntyādimārgaḥ. sa kasminn antarbhavatīti vaktavyam. āha. prayogamārga evāntarbhavati. viprakṛṣṭas tv asau prayogamārga ity ayaṃ tasyāgradharmebhyo viśeṣaḥ. udāharaṇārthatvāc cācāryeṇa saṃnikṛṣṭa eva prayogamārga ukta iti.
body.translated_text: 'That which is freed from the obstruction to be abandoned by that' — 'first' means: that which is freed from the obstruction to be abandoned by the uninterrupted path. 'First' is a qualifier. Because in the third and subsequent moments, a path of that same type is considered to be the special path (<s>viśeṣamārga</s>). And for this very reason he says: 'The special path is whatever other path than these' — other than the preparatory path (<s>prayogamārga</s>) and the rest — this is the meaning. Moreover, if he were not to say 'first' — if he were to say only this much: 'The liberation path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>) is that which is freed from the obstruction to be abandoned by that' — then, since all the uninterrupted paths and the rest that arise after the <s>duḥkhadharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of the dharma of suffering) are freed from the obstruction to be abandoned by that, all would be liberation paths. And this is undesirable — because of the unwanted consequence that even uninterrupted paths would be liberation paths. Therefore, the obstruction to be abandoned by the uninterrupted path — beginning with <s>duḥkhadharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patience regarding the knowledge of the dharma of suffering) — whatever is the obstruction to be abandoned: the group to be abandoned by seeing suffering, up to that to be abandoned by cultivation. That which is first produced freed from the obstruction to be abandoned by that — that is the liberation path, not another, even though freed from the obstruction to be abandoned by that. Whatever is other than these three — the preparatory path and the rest — that is the special path. The uncontaminated moments from the seventeenth onward, after the sixteen paths following the moment of <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge), which are of that same type — those should be understood as having the nature of the special path. Likewise, any other liberation-knowledge (<s>vimuktijñāna</s>) — the ultimate knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and the like — that too should be stated. And whatever path is for dwelling in happiness in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra</s>) or for the accomplishment of special qualities (<s>vaiśeṣikaguṇa</s>) — that too is the special path alone. 'The preparatory path is that from which the uninterrupted path arises' — this was stated. From this it is understood that the mundane supreme dharmas (<s>agradharmāḥ</s>) are the preparatory path. But the path of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) and the rest in reverse order — in which [category] is that included? — this must be stated. He says: it is included in the preparatory path alone. But that is a remote preparatory path — this is its distinction from the supreme dharmas. And because the <s>Ācārya</s> spoke of the proximate preparatory path alone for the purpose of illustration.

body.text: eṣa hi nirvāṇasya panthāḥ. tena tadgamanād iti. loke yena gamyate. sa mārga iti pratītaḥ. anena ca nirvāṇaṃ gamyate prāpyate. tasmān mārga iti darśayati. mārgayaṃty anena veti. mārgo 'nveṣaṇa iti dhātuḥ paṭhyate. tasyaitad ghañi rūpaṃ mārga iti. yena nirvāṇam anviṣyate. sa mārga iti. vimuktiviśeṣamārgayoḥ kathaṃ mārgatvam iti. na hi tābhyāṃ nirvāṇaṃ prāpyate. prayogānantaryamārgayor eva tatprāptau sāmarthyān na tayor iti abhiprāyaḥ. tajjātīyādhimātrataratvād iti. prahāṇamārgajātīyau cālaṃbanākārānāsravatvasādṛsyāt. adhimātratarau ca hetūpacayataḥ. yathā hy ānantaryamārgaś catuḥsatyālaṃbanaṣoḍaśākāro 'nāsravaś ca. evaṃ vimuktiviśeṣamārgāv api. adhimātrataratvenaiva tu tasmād viśeṣa iti. [Tib. 264b] uttarottaraprāpaṇāt. nirupadhiśeṣapraveśād veti. yasmād vimuktimārgeṇa viśeṣamārgeṇa ca uttarottaro
body.translated_text: For this is the road to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Because of going to that by it. In the world, that by which one goes is understood as a path (<s>mārga</s>). And by this, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is reached, attained — therefore he shows it is a path. 'They search by means of it' — the root <s>mārg</s> meaning 'to search' is read. Its form with the suffix <s>ghañ</s> is <s>mārga</s>. That by which <s>nirvāṇa</s> is searched for — that is the path. How do the liberation and special paths have the nature of a path? For <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not attained by those two. The intent is: only the preparatory and uninterrupted paths have the capacity for that attainment, not those two. 'Because of being of a superior degree of that same type' — and both [liberation and special paths] are of the same type as the path of abandonment, because of the similarity of object-domain, aspect, and uncontaminated nature. And they are of a superior degree because of the accumulation of causes. For just as the uninterrupted path has the four truths as its object-domain, has sixteen aspects, and is uncontaminated — so too the liberation and special paths. But they are distinguished from it precisely by being of a superior degree. Because of leading to successively higher [attainments]. Because of entry into <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>). Because by the liberation path and the special path, successively higher

body.text: mārgaḥ prāpyate. tasmāt anayor mārgatvam ity arthaḥ. yasmād vā tābhyāṃ nirupadhiśeṣaṃ nirvāṇaṃ praviśati. yadutpattau nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇapraveśa iti.
body.translated_text: paths are attained — therefore these two have the nature of a path — this is the meaning. Or because by those two one enters <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder. At whose arising there is entry into <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder.

body.text: apare punar evaṃ vyācakṣate. uttarottaraprāpaṇān nirupadhiśeṣapraveśaḥ. tasmād anayor mārgatvam iti.
body.translated_text: Others, however, explain thus: entry into <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder is through leading to successively higher [attainments]. Therefore these two have the nature of a path.

body.text: (VI.69) nirvāṇapratipādanād iti. yasmād anena nirvāṇaṃ pratipadyata ity arthaḥ. evaṃ sukhāpi dvividheti. asti pratipat sukhā dhandhābhijñā. asti sukhā kṣiprābhijñeti. aṃgaparigrahaṇaśamathavipaśyanāsamatābhyām ayatnavāhitvād ity aṃgaiḥ parigrahaḥ. śamathavipaśyanayoḥ samatvaṃ. aṃgaparigrahaś ca śamathavipaśyanāsamatvaṃ ca. tābhyām ayatnavāhitvaṃ. tasmāt sukhā pratipat. yasmād aṃgaparigṛhītāni dhyānāni śamathavipaśyanābhyāṃ samāni ca. tasmād ayatnavāhīni. ataś ca sukhāsau pratipad iti. aṃgāparigrahād iti vistaraḥ. aṃgāparigrahād anāgamyadhyānāṃtarārūpyā yatnavāhinaḥ. śamathavipaśyanānyūnatvāc ca saṃbhavatas te [Tib. 265a] yatnavāhinaḥ. śamathanyūnatvād anāgamyadhyānāṃtare yathavāhinī. vipaśyanānyūnatvāc cārūpyā yatnavāhinaḥ. tadbhāvāt. te 'nāgamyādayo duḥkhā pratipad iti. dhandhābhijñeti. dhandhābhijñāsyām iti. dhandhābhijñā mandaprajñety arthaḥ. kṣiprābhijñeti tīkṣṇaprajñā. dhandhasya mandasya pudgalasyeyam abhijñā dhandhābhijñeti. ṣaṣṭhītatpuruṣeṇāpy etat sidhyatīti darśayati. evaṃ kṣiprasya tīkṣṇasya pudgalasyābhijñā kṣiprābhijñeti yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: (VI.69) 'Because of the establishment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — the meaning is: because by this, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is reached. 'Thus the pleasant [practice] too is twofold' — there is a pleasant practice with slow penetration, and a pleasant practice with swift penetration. 'Because of non-effortful progress through the grasping of the limbs and the equilibrium of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight)' — the grasping of the limbs means the grasping by the limbs [of meditation]. The equality of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> is their equilibrium. Through the grasping of limbs and through the equilibrium of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> — because of non-effortful progress through these two. Therefore the practice is pleasant. Because the <s>dhyāna</s>s grasped by the limbs are equal in <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> — therefore they progress without effort. And because of this, that practice is pleasant. 'Because of non-grasping of limbs' — and so forth in detail. Because of non-grasping of limbs, the preliminary stage (<s>anāgamya</s>), the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, and the formless [attainments] progress with effort. And because of the deficiency of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> — where possible, they progress with effort. Because of the deficiency of <s>śamatha</s>, the preliminary stage and intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> progress with effort. Because of the deficiency of <s>vipaśyanā</s>, the formless [attainments] progress with effort. Because of that state — therefore those — the preliminary stage and the rest — are painful practices. 'Slow penetration' — one who has slow penetration. Slow penetration means dull wisdom — this is the meaning. 'Swift penetration' means sharp wisdom. '<s>Dhandha</s>' (slow) — of a slow, dull person, this is the penetration — hence slow penetration. He shows that this is also established through a genitive <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound. Similarly, the penetration of a swift, sharp person is swift penetration — this should be connected.

body.text: (VI.70) catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni. kāyavedanācittadharmāsmṛtyupasthānāni yathoktāni. catvāri samyakprahāṇāni. utpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya chandaṃ janayati. vyāyacchate. vīryam ārabhate. cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti. pradadhāti. anutpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpādāya chandaṃ janayatīti pūrvavat. anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām utpādāya chandaṃ janayatīti pūrvavat. utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye asaṃmoṣāya bhāvanāparipūraye bhūyobhāvāya vṛddhivipulatājñānasākṣātkriyāyai chandaṃ janayatīti pūrvavat. catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ. chandasamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgata ṛddhipādaḥ. evaṃ vīryacittamīmāṃsāsamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgata ṛddhipādaḥ. ṛddhipādā ṛddhihetava ity arthaḥ. [Tib. 265b] paṃcendriyāṇi. śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñendriyāṇi. paṃca balāni. śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñābalāni. saptabodhyaṃgāni. smṛtidharmapravicayavīryaprītipraśrabdhisamādhyupekṣābodhyaṃgāni. smṛtir eva saṃbodhyaṃgaṃ smṛtisaṃbodhyaṃgam. evaṃ yāvad upekṣaiva saṃbodhyaṃgaṃ
body.translated_text: (VI.70) The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>): the foundations of mindfulness of body, feeling, mind, and <s>dharma</s>s — as stated. The four right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>): for the abandonment of arisen evil unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s, one generates desire, makes effort, arouses energy, takes hold of the mind, and applies it. For the non-arising of unarisen evil unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s, one generates desire — as before. For the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharma</s>s, one generates desire — as before. For the stability, non-confusion, development, completion, abundance, growth, and extensiveness of arisen wholesome <s>dharma</s>s, and for their realization through direct knowledge, one generates desire — as before. The four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>): the basis of supernatural power endowed with the conditioning factors of concentration of desire and abandonment. Likewise, the basis of supernatural power endowed with the conditioning factors of concentration of energy, mind, and investigation. The bases of supernatural power are the causes of supernatural power — this is the meaning. The five faculties (<s>indriya</s>): the faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. The five powers (<s>bala</s>): the powers of faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. The seven limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>): the limbs of awakening of mindfulness, dharma-investigation, energy, joy, tranquility, concentration, and equanimity. Mindfulness itself as a limb of awakening is the mindfulness-limb-of-awakening. Similarly, up to equanimity itself as a limb of awakening

body.text: upekṣāsaṃbodhyaṃgam iti. āryāṣṭaṃgo mārgaḥ. samyagdṛṣṭiḥ. samyaksaṃkalpaḥ. samyagvāk. samyakkarmāntaḥ. samyagājīvaḥ. samyagvyāyāmaḥ. samyaksmṛtiḥ. samyaksamādhir iti. aśeṣavidyāprahanād iti. yasmād aśeṣatraidhātukyavidyāprahāṇaṃ. tasmād ubhayaṃ bodhiḥ. anena śaikṣapṛthagjanānāṃ prajñā na bodhir vyavasthāpyata iti darśayati. kiṃ ca yathākramaṃ. tābhyāṃ svārthasya yathābhūtaṃ kṛtāpunaḥkartavyatāvabodhāc ca. kṣayajñānena yathābhūtaṃ kṛtāvabodhāt tat kṣayajñānaṃ bodhiḥ. duḥkhaṃ me parijñātam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. samudayo me prahīṇa iti. nirodho me sākṣātkṛta iti. mārgo me bhāvita iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti. anutpādajñānena yathābhūtam apunaḥkartavyam iti. [mārgo me bhāvito na punar bhāvayitavya] tad anutpādajñānam api bodhiḥ. duḥkhaṃ me parijñātaṃ na punaḥ parijñātavyam. [Tib. 266a] iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. samudayo me prahīṇo na punaḥ prahātavya iti. nirodho me sākṣātkṛto na punaḥ sākṣātkartavya iti. mārgo me bhāvito na punar bhāvayitavya iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti. duḥkhaṃ me parijñātam ity anena kṣayajñānaṃ. na punaḥ parijñātavyam ity anenānutpādajñānam. ity ubhayam api tīkṣṇendriyasya pudgalasya darśayatīti sarvaṃ neyaṃ. tad evaṃ kṣayajñānam anutpādajñānaṃ ca bodhir ity avayavārthaṃ prasādhya samudayārthaṃ prasādhayann āha.
body.translated_text: is the equanimity-limb-of-awakening. The Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>): right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration. 'Because of the abandonment of all ignorance without remainder' — because there is the abandonment of ignorance throughout all three realms without remainder — therefore both [knowledge of destruction and knowledge of non-arising] are <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). By this he shows that the wisdom of learners and ordinary persons is not established as <s>bodhi</s>. Moreover, in due order: 'And because of the awakening to the fact that one's own goal has been truly accomplished and need not be done again, through those two.' Through the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>), because of awakening to what has been truly accomplished — that knowledge of destruction is <s>bodhi</s>. 'Suffering has been fully comprehended by me' — thus one truly knows. 'The origin has been abandoned by me.' 'Cessation has been directly realized by me.' 'The path has been cultivated by me' — thus one truly knows. Through the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>), because of [awakening to] what truly need not be done again — 'the path has been cultivated by me and need not be cultivated again' — that knowledge of non-arising too is <s>bodhi</s>. 'Suffering has been fully comprehended by me and need not be fully comprehended again' — thus one truly knows. 'The origin has been abandoned by me and need not be abandoned again.' 'Cessation has been directly realized by me and need not be directly realized again.' 'The path has been cultivated by me and need not be cultivated again' — thus one truly knows. 'Suffering has been fully comprehended by me' — by this, the knowledge of destruction. 'Need not be fully comprehended again' — by this, the knowledge of non-arising. Thus both are shown for a person of sharp faculties — all this should be understood. Having thus established the component meaning — that the knowledge of destruction and the knowledge of non-arising are <s>bodhi</s> — establishing the composite meaning, he says:

body.text: iti. tasyā bodher anulomas tadanulomaḥ. tadbhāvas tādanulomyaṃ. tasmāt. tādanulomyato bodhipakṣā. bodhipakṣe sādhavo 'nulomā iti bodhipakṣāḥ. smṛtyupasthānādayaḥ saptatriṃśad ucyaṃte pravācane.
body.translated_text: thus. That which conforms to that <s>bodhi</s> is conforming to it (<s>tadanuloma</s>). Its state is conformity (<s>tādanulomya</s>). Therefore — because of conformity — they are aids to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>). Those that are wholesome and conforming on the side of awakening are the aids to awakening. The foundations of mindfulness and the rest — thirty-seven — are spoken of in the teaching.

body.text: (VI.71) daśa dravyāṇīti. keṣāṃcin matena. vakṣyati hi vaibhāṣikāṇām ekādaśa kāyavākkarmaṇor asaṃbhinnatvād iti.
body.translated_text: (VI.71) 'Ten substances' — according to the view of some. For he will state: 'According to the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s, eleven — because of the non-separation of bodily and vocal action.'

body.text: iti. prajñā smṛtyupasthānam ity arthaḥ. smṛtir upatiṣṭhate 'nayeti kṛtvā. tathā hi sūtra uktaṃ. kāye [Tib. 266b] kāyanupaśyī vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is the foundation of mindfulness — this is the meaning. Because mindfulness stands near (<s>upatiṣṭhate</s>) by means of it. For thus it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Contemplating the body in the body' — in detail.

body.text: iti. yasmād uktam utpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya chandaṃ janayati. vyāyacchate. vīryam ārabhata iti sarvaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. Because it is stated: 'For the abandonment of arisen evil unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s, one generates desire, makes effort, arouses energy' — all of this.

children.translated_text: 'The bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) are concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>)' —

body.text: iti. yasmād uktaṃ chandasamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgatam ṛddhipādaṃ
body.translated_text: thus. Because it is stated: 'One cultivates the basis of supernatural power endowed with the conditioning factors of concentration of desire and abandonment'

body.text: bhāvayatīti sarvaṃ prahāṇasaṃskārāḥ punar atrāṣṭau sūtre paṭhyante. kathaṃ. tathābhūtasya yaś chandaḥ. yo vyāyāmaḥ. yā śraddhā. yā praśrabdhiḥ. yā smṛtiḥ. yat saṃprajanyaṃ. yā cetanā. yopekṣā. ima ucyante prahāṇasaṃskārā iti. indriyāṇi tāvad iti vistaraḥ. svanāmagrahaṇena yānīndriyabalasvabhāvāni śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñā dravyāṇi paṃca. teṣāṃ prajñaiva sā yāni catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni. yac ca bodhyaṃgeṣu dharmapravicayasaṃbodhyaṃgaṃ. yā ca mārgāṃgeṣu samyagdṛṣṭiḥ. na dravyāntaraṃ. vīryam eva tad yāni catvāri samyakprahāṇāni. yac ca bodhyaṃgeṣu vīryasaṃbodhyaṃgaṃ. yaś ca mārgāṃgeṣu samyagvyāyāmaḥ. samādhir eva ca sa ye catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ. yac ca bodhyaṃgeṣu samādhisaṃbodhyaṃgaṃ. [Tib. 267a] yac ca mārgāṃgeṣu samyaksamādhiḥ. kim avaśiṣyate yan na prajñendriyādisvabhāvaṃ. bodhyaṃgeṣu prītipraśrabdhyupekṣāsaṃbodhyaṃgāny avaśiṣyante. mārgāṃgeṣu samyaksaṃkalpāḥ. śīlāṃgāni ca trīṇi. samyagvāk samyakkarmāntaḥ samyagājīva iti. daśa dravyāṇīti. śraddhādīni paṃca. prītisaṃbodyaṃgādīni ca paṃceti. śīlāṃgāni trīṇy avijñaptisvabhāvānīti kṛtvaikaṃ dravyaṃ vyavasthāpyate.
body.translated_text: — all of this. The conditioning factors of abandonment (<s>prahāṇasaṃskāra</s>), moreover, are read as eight in the <s>sūtra</s>. How? 'Of one who is in such a state — whatever desire, whatever effort, whatever faith, whatever tranquility, whatever mindfulness, whatever clear comprehension, whatever volition, whatever equanimity — these are called the conditioning factors of abandonment.' As for the faculties — and so forth in detail. By their own name-designation, the five substances that have the nature of the faculties and powers — faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom — are the five substances. Of those, wisdom itself is that which constitutes the four foundations of mindfulness, and which in the limbs of awakening is the dharma-investigation-limb-of-awakening, and which in the path-limbs is right view — not a different substance. Energy itself is that which constitutes the four right exertions, and which in the limbs of awakening is the energy-limb-of-awakening, and which in the path-limbs is right effort. And concentration itself is that which constitutes the four bases of supernatural power, and which in the limbs of awakening is the concentration-limb-of-awakening, and which in the path-limbs is right concentration. What remains that is not of the nature of the wisdom-faculty and the rest? In the limbs of awakening, the joy, tranquility, and equanimity limbs of awakening remain. In the path-limbs, right intention. And the three morality-limbs — right speech, right action, and right livelihood. 'Ten substances' — the five beginning with faith, and the five beginning with the joy-limb-of-awakening. The three morality-limbs, being of the nature of <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest [action]), are established as one substance.

body.text: vaibhāṣikāṇām ekādaśa dravyāṇi. kāyavākkarmaṇor asaṃbhinnatvāt dve dravyaṃ iti kṛtvā. abhiprāyavaśāt pakṣadvaye 'py adoṣaḥ. yadi tu mukhyavṛttyā tasmin kalāpe yāvaṃti dravyāṇi saṃti. tāvaṃti gaṇyeran. naiva tāni daśa dravyāṇi samāhitavijñaptirūpāṇāṃ saptadravyatvāt. ṣoḍaśa dravyāṇīti vaktavyaṃ syāt.
body.translated_text: For the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s, eleven substances (<s>dravya</s>). Because of the non-separation of body-action and speech-action, taking the two as one substance. Because of the intent, there is no fault in either position. But if, in the primary sense, however many substances exist in that aggregate (<s>kalāpa</s>), that many should be counted. Those are not just ten substances — because the forms of concentrated awareness (<s>samāhitavijñaptirūpa</s>) have seven substances. One would have to say sixteen substances.

body.text:
(VI.72) pradhānagrahaṇenaivam uklaṃ. prajñādisvabhāvāḥ smṛtyupasthānādaya iti. sarve tu prāyogikaguṇāḥ sāsravānāsravāḥ śrutacintābhāvanāmayā yathāyogaṃ smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādāḥ. prādhānyaṃ punas tadbalenānyeṣāṃ [Tib. 267b] vṛtteḥ. na punas te na santi. prajñāpradhānāni hi smṛtyupasthānānīty ataḥ prajñāgrahaṇaṃ. na tu prajñaiva smṛtyupasthānaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. prajñāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprītipraśrabdhyupekṣāsamyaksaṃkalpādayo 'pīti. prāyogikagrahaṇam upapattilabhyaśraddhādinirāsārthaṃ. evaṃ vīryapradhānāni samyakpradhānāni. samādhipradhānā ṛddhipādā iti vistareṇa vaktavyaṃ.
ṛddhipādāḥ samādhaya iti kuta etat. sūtrāt. uktaṃ hi chandaṃ cāpi bhikṣavo bhikṣur adhipatiṃ kṛtvā labhate samādhiṃ. so 'sya bhavati chandasamādhiḥ.
body.translated_text:
(VI.72) It was stated thus by taking the principal. The <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>s (foundations of mindfulness) and the rest have <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and the rest as their own-nature. But all qualities produced by practice (<s>prāyogikaguṇa</s>), whether contaminated or uncontaminated, born of hearing, reflection, or cultivation, are, as appropriate, <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>s (foundations of mindfulness), <s>samyakpradhāna</s>s (right exertions), and <s>ṛddhipāda</s>s (bases of supernatural power). The predominance, however, is because the others function through the power of that [principal one]. [Tib. 267b] It is not that they do not exist [in the group]. For since the <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>s have <s>prajñā</s> as predominant, therefore <s>prajñā</s> is mentioned. But it is not that <s>prajñā</s> alone is a <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>. Rather, <s>prajñā</s>, <s>vīrya</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, <s>prīti</s>, <s>praśrabdhi</s>, <s>upekṣā</s>, <s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s>, and the rest too are [included]. The mention of 'produced by practice' (<s>prāyogika</s>) is for the purpose of excluding those obtained by birth (<s>upapatilabhya</s>), such as faith and the rest. Similarly, the <s>samyakpradhāna</s>s have <s>vīrya</s> as predominant; the <s>ṛddhipāda</s>s have <s>samādhi</s> as predominant — this should be stated in detail.
How is it known that the <s>ṛddhipāda</s>s are <s>samādhi</s>s? From the <s>sūtra</s>. For it is stated: 'A monk, O monks, making desire (<s>chanda</s>) predominant, obtains <s>samādhi</s>. That becomes his <s>chandasamādhi</s> (desire-concentration).

body.text: cittaṃ vīryaṃ mīmāṃsāṃ cāpi bhikṣavo bhikṣur adhipatiṃ kṛtvā labhate samādhiṃ. so 'sya bhavati mīmāṃsāsamādhir iti.
body.translated_text: Making mind (<s>citta</s>), energy (<s>vīrya</s>), and investigation (<s>mīmāṃsā</s>) predominant, a monk, O monks, obtains <s>samādhi</s>. That becomes his <s>mīmāṃsāsamādhi</s> (investigation-concentration).'

body.text: tena hi samyak kāyavāṅmanāṃsi pradhīyaṃta iti. pradhīyaṃte dhāryaṃte niyamyante pravartyante vā kadācid aneneti pradhānaṃ. tatpratiṣṭhitatvād iti. yasmāt sarvaguṇasaṃpattilakṣaṇā ṛddhis tasmin samādhau pratiṣṭhitā. ṛddheḥ pādaḥ pratiṣṭheti ṛddhipāda iti.
body.translated_text: 'For by that, body, speech, and mind are properly mastered' — they are mastered, held, restrained, or sometimes directed by this — hence it is a <s>pradhāna</s> (exertion). 'Because of being established therein' — because <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power), characterized by the accomplishment of all qualities, is established in that <s>samādhi</s>. The base (<s>pāda</s>) of <s>ṛddhi</s> is its foundation — hence <s>ṛddhipāda</s> (base of supernatural power).

body.text: ye tv āhuḥ samādhir eva ṛddhiḥ. pādāś chaṃdādayaḥ. chandacittavīryamīmānsā iti. teṣām evaṃvādināṃ vaibhāṣikāṇāṃ trayodaśa bodhipakṣāḥ prāpnuvanti. chandacittayor ādhikyād ekādaśasu [Tib. 268a] prakṣepe. vīryaprajñe tv atra nādhike. samyakpradhānasmṛtyupasthāneṣv antarbhāvāt. bahudhā bhavatīti vistara iti. bahudhābhūtvaiko bhavati. āvirbhavaṃ. tirobhāvaṃ jñānadarśanena pratyanubhavati. tiraḥ kuḍyaṃ tiraḥ prākāram asajjamānaḥ kāyena gacchati. tadyathākāśe. pṛthivyām unmajjananimajjanaṃ karoti. tadyathodake. udake 'bhidyamānena srotasā gacchati. tadyathā pṛthivyām. ākāśe paryaṃkeṇa krāmati. tadyathā śakuniḥ pakṣī. imau vā punaḥ bhūyo candramasāv evaṃ mahardhikāv evaṃ mahānubhāvau pāṇinā āmārṣṭi parimārṣṭi. yāvad brahmalokaṃ kāyena vaśe vartayata iti. iyam ucyate ṛddhiḥ. ṛddhipādāḥ katame. chandasamādhiḥ. vīryasamādhiḥ. cittasamādhiḥ. mīmānsāsamādhiḥ. ima ucyante ṛddhipādā iti. evaṃlakṣaṇaḥ samādhiḥ. tasmān na samādhir eva rudhir iti. atrācāryasaṃghabhadra āha. na bhavaty eṣa teṣāṃ doṣaḥ. samādhiṃ hi te ṛddhipādam icchanti. ṛddhir apīti. chandādayas tūcyante samādheś catustvajñāpanārthaṃ. kaścid dhi samādhiḥ kuśalamūlaprayogāvasthāyāṃ pradhānī bhavati. kaścit kuśalamūlaniṣpannāvasthāyāṃ. pūrvo 'tra rddhipādaḥ. uttara rddhir iti. sūtravirodho 'pi caiṣāṃ na bhavati. ṛddhipādaphalam ṛddhiśabdenoktaṃ. [Tib. 268b] parijñāphalasya tacchabdābhidhānavad ityādi.
body.translated_text: But those who say '<s>samādhi</s> itself is <s>ṛddhi</s>, and the bases (<s>pāda</s>) are desire (<s>chanda</s>) and the rest — desire, mind, energy, and investigation' — for those <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s who hold this view, thirteen <s>bodhipakṣa</s>s (aids to awakening) would follow. Because of the addition of desire and mind [Tib. 268a] to the eleven — since <s>vīrya</s> and <s>prajñā</s> are not additional here, being already included in the <s>samyakpradhāna</s>s and <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>s. 'It becomes manifold' — and so forth in detail. Having become manifold, it becomes one. It appears and disappears. It experiences through knowledge and vision. It goes through walls, through ramparts, unobstructed, with the body — just like through space. It dives in and out of the earth — just as in water. It goes upon water without breaking [the surface] — just as on earth. It travels through space cross-legged — just like a bird with wings. 'These two — the sun and moon — so mighty, so powerful — it touches and strokes them with its hand. Up to the Brahma-world, it exercises mastery with the body.' This is called <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power). What are the <s>ṛddhipāda</s>s? <s>Chandasamādhi</s>, <s>vīryasamādhi</s>, <s>cittasamādhi</s>, and <s>mīmāṃsāsamādhi</s>. These are called <s>ṛddhipāda</s>s. <s>Samādhi</s> of such characteristics — therefore <s>samādhi</s> alone is not <s>ṛddhi</s>. Therein, <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> says: this is not a fault for them. For they hold <s>samādhi</s> to be the <s>ṛddhipāda</s> and also <s>ṛddhi</s>. Desire and the rest are stated for the purpose of indicating the fourfold [nature] of <s>samādhi</s>. For indeed, some <s>samādhi</s> becomes predominant in the stage of the practice of wholesome roots, and some in the stage of the accomplishment of wholesome roots. The former is here the <s>ṛddhipāda</s>; the latter is <s>ṛddhi</s>. And the contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s> also does not arise for them. The fruit of the <s>ṛddhipāda</s> is designated by the word '<s>ṛddhi</s>' — [Tib. 268b] just as the fruit of full understanding is designated by that [same] word, and so forth.

body.text: mṛdvadhimātrabhedād iti. mṛdūnīndriyāṇi adhimātrāṇi balāni. katham eṣāṃ mṛdvadhimātrabheda iti hetum āha. avamardanīyānavamardanīyatvād iti. tadvipakṣabhūtair āśraddhyakausīdyamuṣitasmṛtitāvikṣepāsaṃprajanyair antarāsamudācārād indriyāṇy avamṛdyante na tv cvaṃ balānīti. punas tāny uktani.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the distinction of mild and intense' — the faculties (<s>indriya</s>) are mild; the powers (<s>bala</s>) are intense. How is there this distinction of mild and intense? — he states the reason: 'Because of being defeatable and undefeatable.' By their opposites — lack of faith (<s>āśraddhya</s>), laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), lost mindfulness (<s>muṣitasmṛtitā</s>), distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>), and non-discernment (<s>asaṃprajanya</s>) — because of their occasional non-manifestation, the faculties are defeated. But the powers are not [defeated] in this way. They have been stated again [for this reason].

body.text: iti. paṃcāvasthā ime uktāḥ.
body.translated_text: — thus. These five stages have been stated.

body.text: dve avasthe iti. saptasv avasthāsu
body.translated_text: two stages — thus. In seven stages,

body.text: prabhāvyaṃte vyavasthāpyante pradhānīkriyante vā. ādikarmikāvasthāyāṃ smṛtyupasthānāni. uṣmagatāvasthāyāṃ samyakpradhānāni. mūrdhāvasthāyām ṛddhipādāḥ. kṣāntyavasthāyām indriyāṇi. laukikāgradharmāvasthāyāṃ balāni. bhāvanāmārgāvasthāyāṃ bodhyaṃgāni. darśanamārgāvasthāyām āryāṣṭāṃgo mārga iti. viśeṣādhigamahetur vīryasaṃvardhanaṃ. tasmād uṣmagateṣu samyakpradhānāni. [Tib. 269a] aparihāṇīyakuśalamūlapraveśatvāt. mūrdheṣv iti. aparihāṇyanukūlānāṃ kuśalamūlānāṃ praveśo mūrdhataḥ.
body.translated_text: they are manifested, established, or made predominant. In the beginner's stage (<s>ādikarmika</s>), the <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>s (foundations of mindfulness). In the heat stage (<s>uṣmagata</s>), the <s>samyakpradhāna</s>s (right exertions). In the summit stage (<s>mūrdhan</s>), the <s>ṛddhipāda</s>s (bases of supernatural power). In the patience stage (<s>kṣānti</s>), the faculties (<s>indriya</s>). In the stage of supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>s (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>), the powers (<s>bala</s>). In the cultivation path stage (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), the awakening factors (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>). In the seeing path stage (<s>darśanamārga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>). 'The cause of attaining a special [realization] is the nurturing of energy' — therefore, in the heat stage, the <s>samyakpradhāna</s>s. [Tib. 269a] 'Because of entering the wholesome roots that are not subject to falling away' — 'in the summits' — the entry into wholesome roots not subject to falling away [occurs] from the summits.

children.translated_text: 'One who has attained summits does not cut the roots' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. praviśaty ebhir iti kṛtvā praveśaḥ. aparihāṇir hi kṣāntiṣu bhavati. tadavasthāḥ. samādhayaḥ samṛddher āśrayībhavaṃtīti. mūrdhasv ṛddhipādā vyavasthāpyaṃte. apunaḥparihāṇita iti vistaraḥ. yasmāt kṣāntiṣu punaḥparihāṇir nāsti. ādyayor eva hi parihāṇisaṃbhavaḥ. tasmād ādhipatyaprāptāni śraddhādīni bhavaṃti. tadbhāvāt kṣāntiṣv indriyāṇi vyavasthāpyaṃte. kleśānavamardanīyatvād iti. yasmāt kleśair nāvamṛdyante. tasyām avasthāyāṃ kleśāsamudācārāt. laukikānyadharmānavamardanīyatvād vā. atha vā laukikair anyair dharmair anavamardanīyatvād agradharmāvasthāyāṃ śraddhādīni balānīti prabhāvyante. bodhyāsannatvād iti. kṣayānutpādajñānāsannatvād ity arthaḥ. bhāvanāmārgo hi kṣayānutpādajñānāsannaḥ. darśanamārgas tu dūro tadantarālabhāvanāmārgavyavahitatvāt. gamanaprabhāvitatvād iti. mārgo hi loke gamanaprabhāvitaḥ. gacchaṃty aneneti mārgaḥ. gacchatīti vā mārgaḥ. pāṭaliputram ayaṃ panthā gacchatīti loke vacanāt. darśanamārgaś cātiśayena gamanaprabhāvito na bhāvanāmārgaḥ. katham ity āha. tasyāśugāmitvād [Tib. 269b] iti. tadvān api tenāśu gacchati. bhāvanāmārgeṇa tu bhūmibhedena prākarṣakatvāt bahunā kālena gacchati.
body.translated_text: from this statement. Because one enters through these — hence 'entry.' For non-falling-away occurs in the patiences. In that stage, the <s>samādhi</s>s serve as the basis for <s>ṛddhi</s> (accomplishment) — therefore, in the summits, the <s>ṛddhipāda</s>s are established. 'Because of non-regression' — and so forth in detail. Because in the patiences there is no further regression — for the possibility of regression exists only in the first two [stages]. Therefore, [the faculties of] faith and the rest, having attained predominance, exist [there]. Because of their being so, in the patiences, the faculties are established. 'Because of being undefeatable by afflictions' — because they are not defeated by afflictions — because of the non-manifestation of afflictions in that stage. Or because of being undefeatable by other mundane <s>dharma</s>s — alternatively, because of being undefeatable by other mundane <s>dharma</s>s, in the stage of supreme <s>dharma</s>s, faith and the rest are manifested as powers. 'Because of proximity to awakening' — the meaning is: because of proximity to the knowledge of destruction and non-arising (<s>kṣayānutpādajñāna</s>). For the cultivation path is close to the knowledge of destruction and non-arising. But the seeing path is far [from it], because it is separated by the intervening cultivation path. 'Because of being characterized by going' — for a path in the world is characterized by going. A path is that by which one goes. Or the path itself goes — as in the worldly saying 'this road goes to <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.' And the seeing path is especially characterized by going, not the cultivation path. How? — he says: 'Because of its swift-going nature' — [Tib. 269b] one who possesses that goes swiftly by that. But through the cultivation path, because of its extensive nature due to the differentiation of grounds, one goes over a long time.

body.text: apare punar āhur ity ācāryaḥ. asmadādaya ity abhiprāyāt. yathā vaibhāṣikair bhinnaḥ kramaḥ. tathā tam abhittvā bodhipakṣāṇām ānupūrvīṃ varṇayaṃti. darśanamārge bodhyaṃgānīti kṛtvā. bahuvidheti vistaraḥ. bahuprakāro viṣayo rūpādibhedāt. nīlādibhedāc ca. tasmin vyāseko vikṣepaḥ. bahuvidhaviṣayavyāsekena visartuṃ śīlam āsām iti. bahuvidhaviṣayavyāsekavisāriṇyo
body.translated_text: 'Others, however, say' — the <s>Ācārya</s> [speaks] with the intent 'we and the like.' Just as the order differs from the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s — having stated that, they describe the sequence of the <s>bodhipakṣa</s>s. Because [they hold that] the <s>bodhyaṅga</s>s [are assigned] to the seeing path. 'Manifold' — and so forth in detail. The object is of many kinds, because of the differentiation into form and the rest, and because of the differentiation into blue and the rest. Therein, scattering (<s>vyāseka</s>) is distraction. Because of their habit of wandering due to distraction in manifold objects — [Tib. 269b] because of the wandering [cognitions] that are scattered in manifold objects

body.text: buddhayaḥ. tāsāṃ nigrahārthaṃ smṛtyupasthānāni. gardhāśritānāṃ tṛṣṇāśritānām ity arthaḥ. smarasaṃkalpānām ity anubhūtaviṣayasmṛtisaṃkalpānām ity arthaḥ. kāmasaṃkalpānām iti vā. tadbaleneti. catuḥsmṛtyupasthānabalenety arthaḥ. caturvidhakāryasaṃpādanāyeti. caturvidhaṃ kāryam utpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇam. anutpannānām anutpādaḥ. tathānutpannānāṃ kuśalānām utpādaḥ. utpannānāṃ sthityādīni. tataḥ samādhiviśodhanād iti. tataḥ samyakpradhānebhyo 'nataraṃ samādher viśodhanād ṛddhipādāḥ [Tib. 270a] prabhāvyaṃte. lokottaradharmādhipatibhūtānīti. tadāvāhakatvād adhipatibhūtāni veditavyāni. tāny evendriyāṇi. yadā nirjitavipakṣasamudācārāṇi. nirjitaśraddhyādisamudācārāṇi bhavaṃti. tadā balāni. indriyāvasthāyāṃ hi kleśasamudācāraḥ saṃbhavati. kṣāntyavasthāyāḥ prākarṣakatvāt. darśanamārge bodhyaṃgānīti. anāsravā prajñā bodhir iti kṛtvā. ubhayor mārgāṃgānīti. darśanabhāvanāmārgayoḥ. katham ity āha. tathā hy uktam iti vistaraḥ. bhāvanayā paripūrir bhāvanāparipūriḥ tāṃ gacchaty āryāṣṭāṃgo mārgaḥ. tasmin gacchati catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni bhāvanāparipūriṃ yacchaṃti. yācat sapta bodhyaṃgānīti. bhāvanāparipūriṃ gacchaṃtīti vacanāt bhāvanāmārge 'pi āryāṣṭāṃgo mārgo bhavatīti gamyate. na hi darśanamārge bhāvanā paripūriṃ gacchati. kiṃ tarhi bhāvanāmārga iti. punaś coktam ubhayor mārgāṃgāni vyavasthāpyaṃta iti. caturṇām āryasatyānām etad adhivacanam iti darśanamārgaṃ darśayati. yathāgatena mārgeṇa prakramaṇam iti vistareṇa yāvan mārgasyaitad [Tib. 270b] adhivacanam iti bhāvanāmārgaṃ darśayati. yathāgatena yathāprāptena mārgeṇa prakramaṇaṃ yāvad bodhir iti. tad evaṃ darśanamārge bhāvanāmārge ca mārgāṃgāni vyavasthāpyanta iti. ata ubhayor āryāṣṭāṃgo mārga eṣṭavya iti.
body.translated_text: — for the purpose of restraining those, the <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>s [are taught]. 'Of those attached' — the meaning is: of those based on craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). 'Of those with amorous thoughts' — the meaning is: of those with recollections and intentions regarding experienced objects. Or: 'of those with sensual thoughts.' 'Through the power of that' — the meaning is: through the power of the four <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>s. 'For the accomplishment of the fourfold task' — the fourfold task is: the abandonment of arisen evil unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s; the non-arising of unarisen ones; similarly, the arising of unarisen wholesome [<s>dharma</s>s]; and the stability and the rest of arisen ones. 'Then, because of the purification of <s>samādhi</s>' — then, after the <s>samyakpradhāna</s>s, because of the purification of <s>samādhi</s>, the <s>ṛddhipāda</s>s [Tib. 270a] are manifested. 'Having become the rulers of supramundane <s>dharma</s>s' — they should be understood as having become rulers because of bringing [those <s>dharma</s>s] about. Those very things are the faculties (<s>indriya</s>). When they have conquered the manifestation of their opposites — when they have conquered the manifestation of lack of faith and the rest — then they are powers (<s>bala</s>). For in the stage of faculties, the manifestation of afflictions is possible — because of the extensive nature of the patience stage. 'In the seeing path, the <s>bodhyaṅga</s>s' — because uncontaminated <s>prajñā</s> is <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). 'The path-limbs of both' — of both the seeing path and the cultivation path. How? — he says: 'For thus it is stated' — and so forth in detail. 'The noble eightfold path goes to the fulfillment of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāparipūri</s>).' When it goes there, the four <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>s reach the fulfillment of cultivation, up to the seven <s>bodhyaṅga</s>s. Because of the statement 'they go to the fulfillment of cultivation,' it is understood that the noble eightfold path exists in the cultivation path too. For the seeing path does not go to the fulfillment of cultivation. Rather, it is the cultivation path. And again it is stated: 'the path-limbs of both are established.' He shows the seeing path: 'This is the designation of the four noble truths.' He shows the cultivation path in detail up to: 'the path's designation' — [Tib. 270b] proceeding by the path as attained, up to awakening. Thus, path-limbs are established in both the seeing path and the cultivation path — therefore, the noble eightfold path should be accepted in both.

body.text: (VI.74) siddho 'nukramaḥ. pūrvaṃ bodhyaṃgāni paścād āryāṣṭāṃgo mārga iti.
body.translated_text: (VI.74) The sequence is established — first the <s>bodhyaṅga</s>s, then the noble eightfold path.

body.text: anāsravāṇy evety avadhāraṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: the restriction 'uncontaminated alone' [applies].

body.text: iti. smṛtyupasthānādayo balaparyantāḥ.
body.translated_text: that is, the <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>s and the rest up to the powers.

body.text: (VI.75) balavāhanīyatvād iti. balena vīryeṇa saṃmukhīkaraṇīyatvāt. anāgamye prītyabhāvaḥ. sukhādhigamyaṃ cittaṃ prīṇāti. netarad iti. kiṃ cādharabhūmisāśaṃkatvāc ca. parihāṇiṃ prati sāśaṃka iti. ataś ca tatra prītyabhāvaḥ. sāśaṃkatāyāṃ hi cittaṃ na prīyate. saṃkalpavarjyā iti. saṃkalpo
body.translated_text: (VI.75) 'Because of requiring effort to bring [it] face-to-face' — because of needing to be brought face-to-face with strength, with energy. 'In the access concentration (<s>anāgamya</s>), there is no joy (<s>prīti</s>).' The mind delights in what is easily attained — not in the other. And moreover, because of apprehension regarding the lower ground — apprehension regarding regression. And for this reason too there is no joy there. For when there is apprehension, the mind does not delight. 'Excluding intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>)' — <s>saṃkalpa</s>

body.text: vitarkaḥ.
body.translated_text: is <s>vitarka</s> (initial application of thought).

children.translated_text: 'In the Desire Realm and at the Peak of Existence, devoid of awakening-factors and path-limbs' —

body.text: iti. kathaṃ bhavāgre kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ bhavati. na hi tatra kāyo vidyate. kāyālambanā hi prajñā kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ. na ca bhavāgraṃ kāmadhātuṃ rūpadhātuṃ cālāmbate. [Tib. 271a]
body.translated_text: thus. How can the <s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundation of mindfulness of the body) exist at the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>)? For there is no body there. For the <s>prajñā</s> having the body as its object is the <s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s>. And the Peak of Existence does not take the Desire Realm or the Form Realm as its object. [Tib. 271a]

children.translated_text: 'The fundamental wholesome formless [attainments] — contaminated — do not have a lower [realm] as their domain' —

body.text: iti siddhāntāt. naitat kenacid vyākhyākāreṇa likhitaṃ. tad idam atra vyavasthāpayāmaḥ. kāyasya kaḥ svabhāvaḥ. bhautikatvam ity uktaṃ. bhūtaṃ bhautikaṃ ca kāya ity arthaḥ. tatra yadi kevalabhūtālaṃbanā kevalabhautikālaṃbanā tadubhayālaṃbanā vā prajñā bhavet. kāyasmṛtyupasthānam eva tad bhavet. bhavāgre ca kuśalasāsravā prajñā mārgata iti nyāyata iti vānāsravasaṃvaramārgālaṃbanata iti. sāsravadharālaṃbanā hi maulāḥ kuśalārūpyā neṣyaṃte. na tv anāsravadharālaṃbanā iti. atas tad atra kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ veditavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: — from this established doctrine. This has not been written by any commentator. Therefore we establish this here. What is the own-nature of the body (<s>kāya</s>)? It has been stated that it is materiality (<s>bhautikatva</s>) — the meaning is: the body is the great elements (<s>bhūta</s>) and derivative matter (<s>bhautika</s>). Therein, if there were wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) having as its object only the great elements, only derivative matter, or both — that would be the foundation of mindfulness of the body (<s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s>) alone. And at the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>), wholesome contaminated wisdom — from the perspective of the path, or from the perspective of reasoning, or from the perspective of having an uncontaminated restraint-path (<s>anāsravasaṃvaramārga</s>) as object. For the main wholesome formless [attainments] are not accepted as having contaminated <s>dharma</s>s as object — but they are not [rejected as] having uncontaminated <s>dharma</s>s as object. Therefore, that should be understood here as the foundation of mindfulness of the body (<s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s>).

body.text: (VI.77, 78) catvāro 'vetyaprasādāḥ buddhe 'vetyaprasādo dharme saṃghe cāryakāntāni ca śīlānīti. tatra duḥkhasatyādīnāṃ dharmatvād abuddhasaṃghasvabhāvatvāc ca. yathākramaṃ satyatrayam abhisamayan paśyan dharme cāvetyaprasādam āryakāntāni cāśīlāni anāsravāṇi pratilabhate. na buddhe na saṃghe vā avetyaprasādaṃ. [duḥkhasatyādīnāṃ dharmatvād. abuddhasaṃghasvabhāvatvāc ca. yathā] mārgasatyam abhisamayato buddhe tasya ca srāvakasaṃghe 'vetyaprasādaṃ pratilabhate. mārgasatyasya buddhasaṃghasvabhāvatvāt. ko 'yam iha dharmo 'bhipreta [Tib. 271b] iti. bahavo dharmāḥ kuśalā dharmā ity evamādayaḥ. tat ko 'yam iha dharmo 'bhipretaḥ. yad uktaṃ dharme cāvetyaprasādaṃ pratilabhata iti. atha vā buddharatnaṃ saṃgharatnaṃ cedam ucyate. tasmād idam api dharmarātnam ihābhipretaṃ bhavet. ratnatrayasya hy ayaṃ svabhāva uktaḥ.
body.translated_text: (VI.77, 78) The four confirmed confidences (<s>avetyaprasāda</s>) are: confirmed confidence in the <s>Buddha</s>, in the <s>Dharma</s>, in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and the moralities beloved of the Noble Ones (<s>āryakāntaśīla</s>). Therein, because the [first three] truths — suffering and the rest — have the nature of <s>dharma</s> and do not have the nature of <s>Buddha</s> or <s>Saṃgha</s>, one who realizes, who sees, the three truths in sequence obtains confirmed confidence in the <s>Dharma</s> and the uncontaminated moralities beloved of the Noble Ones — not confirmed confidence in the <s>Buddha</s> or the <s>Saṃgha</s>. [Because the first three truths have the nature of dharma and do not have the nature of Buddha or Saṃgha — just as] from the realization of the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>), one obtains confirmed confidence in the <s>Buddha</s> and in his <s>śrāvaka</s>-<s>Saṃgha</s> — because the truth of the path has the nature of <s>Buddha</s> and <s>Saṃgha</s>. 'What is the <s>dharma</s> intended here?' — many <s>dharma</s>s [exist]: 'wholesome <s>dharma</s>s,' and so forth. So what is the <s>dharma</s> intended here — that with regard to which it is said 'one obtains confirmed confidence in the <s>Dharma</s>'? Alternatively, this is called the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel and the <s>Saṃgha</s>-jewel. Therefore this <s>Dharma</s>-jewel too would be intended here — for the own-nature of the Three Jewels (<s>ratnatraya</s>) has been stated:

children.text:
buddhasaṃghakarāṃ dharmān aśaikṣān ubhayāṃś ca saḥ
nirvāṇaṃ ceti śaraṇaṃ yo yāti śaraṇatrayam
children.translated_text: 'One who takes refuge in the threefold refuge — [namely] the non-learner <s>dharma</s>s that make up the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s>, both [learner and non-learner dharmas], and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>' —

body.text: iti. tat kim ayaṃ nirvāṇadharmo 'bhipreta ity ataḥ pṛcchati. ko 'yam iha dharmo 'bhipreta iti.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Is it then the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-<s>dharma</s> that is intended?' — therefore he asks: 'What is the <s>dharma</s> intended here?'

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. duḥkhasamudayanirodhasatyāni. bodhisattvasya ca śaikṣāvasthāyāṃ
body.translated_text: and so forth in detail. [Namely,] the truths of suffering, origination, and cessation. And in the learner stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>

body.text: anāsravo mārgaḥ. pratyekabuddhasya ca śaikṣāśaikṣalakṣaṇo mārgo dharma ihābhipreta iti. ataś catvāry apīti vistaraḥ. mārgasatyam apy abhisamayan dharmam api bodhisattvapratyekabuddhamārgalakṣaṇam abhisamayati. tasmāc catvāry api satyāny abhisamayato dharme 'vetyaprasādalābha ity uktam iti. buddhasaṃghayor mārgo dharma iti nocyate. yasmāt tadabhisamayato buddhe saṃghe cāvetyaprasādalābha iti. kathaṃ punar mārgasatyābhisamayataḥ śraddhālakṣaṇānāṃ trayāṇāṃ buddhadharmasaṃghāvetyaprasādānāṃ yugapat saṃmukhībhāvaḥ. saiva śraddhādhiṣṭhānabhedāpekṣayā [Tib. 272a] nāmatrayaṃ labhata ity adoṣaḥ. atha vā dharme 'vetyaprasādo vartamānaḥ. anāgatās tu trayo bhāvyaṃte. tenocyate
body.translated_text: the uncontaminated path. And for the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, the path characterized as both learner and non-learner — the <s>dharma</s> intended here. Therefore 'four also' — and so forth in detail. Even when realizing the truth of the path, one also realizes the <s>dharma</s> characterized as the path of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. Therefore, from the realization of all four truths, there is the obtaining of confirmed confidence in the <s>Dharma</s> — this is what has been said. Of the <s>Buddha</s> and <s>Saṃgha</s>, the path is the <s>dharma</s> — this is not said. Because from its realization, there is the obtaining of confirmed confidence in the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s>. But how can there be the simultaneous arising of the three confirmed confidences — in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s> — which have the character of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), from the realization of the truth of the path? That very faith, with respect to the division of its bases (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), obtains three names — this is not a fault. Alternatively, the confirmed confidence in the <s>Dharma</s> is present; but the three regarding the future are being cultivated. Therefore it is said:

children.translated_text: 'The obtaining [of confirmed confidence], at the realization of the path, is in the <s>Buddha</s> and his <s>Saṃgha</s> as well' —

body.text: yady adhiṣṭhānāpekṣayāvetyaprasādavyavasthānaṃ dharmāvetyaprasādaḥ pūrvaṃ paṭhitavyaḥ syād ity ata āha. yathā tu vyutthitaḥ saṃmukhīkaroti. tathaiṣām ānupūrvam iti. vaidyabhaiṣajyopasthāyakabhūtatvād iti. vaidyabhūto bhagavān anuttaro viṣak śalyaharteti sūtrāt. dharmabhaiṣajyadaiśikatvāc ca. bhaiṣajyabhūto dharmaḥ kleśavyādhibhaiṣajyatvāt. nirvāṇārogyasaṃprāpakatvāc copasthāyakabhūtaḥ saṃgho nirvāṇārogyaprāptaye parasparopasthānāt. cittaprasādakṛtaḥ śīlaprasāda iti. trividhaś cittaprasādaḥ. samyaksaṃbuddho bata bhagavān. svākhyāto 'sya dharmavinayaḥ. supratipanno 'sya śrāvakasaṃgha iti. tena kṛtaḥ śīlaprasādaḥ. śīlam eva prasādaḥ. śīlasya vā prasādo 'nāsravatvaṃ śīlaprasādaḥ. ante trayāṇāṃ prasādānāṃ caturtha uktaḥ śīlaprasādaḥ. kasmād ity āha. evaṃ prasannasya samyaksaṃbuddho bata bhagavān iti vistareṇaiṣā pratipattiḥ. [Tib. 272b] āryakāntaśīlapratipattir ity arthaḥ. ārogyabhūtatvād vā. kim ante śīlaprasāda uktaḥ. vaiyabhaiṣajyopasthāyakārogyānukramataḥ. daiśikamārgasārthikayānavad vā. kim. ante caturtha ukta ity adhikṛtaṃ. daiśikabhūto bhagavān. mārgabhūto dharmaḥ. sārthikabhūtaḥ saṃghaḥ. yānabhūtāny āryakāntāni śīlānīti. āryāṇaṃ kāntāni prayāṇīty āryakāntānīti.
body.translated_text: If the establishment of confirmed confidences is with respect to the bases, then the confirmed confidence in the <s>Dharma</s> should be recited first — therefore he says: 'But according to how, upon emerging [from the path], one brings them face to face — thus is their order.' 'Because of being analogous to a physician, medicine, and attendant' — the <s>Bhagavān</s> is analogous to a physician — from the <s>sūtra</s>: 'the unsurpassed remover of the arrow of poison.' And because he indicates the medicine of <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Dharma</s> is analogous to medicine — because of being the medicine for the disease of afflictions. And because of leading to the attainment of the health of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s> is analogous to attendants — because of mutually attending to one another for the attainment of the health of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. 'The confidence in morality is produced by the confidence of mind (<s>cittaprasāda</s>)' — the threefold confidence of mind is: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> is indeed a perfectly awakened one. His <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> are well-proclaimed. His <s>śrāvaka</s>-<s>Saṃgha</s> is well-practicing.' The confidence in morality (<s>śīlaprasāda</s>) is produced by that. Morality itself is the confidence. Or the confidence of morality — its uncontaminated nature — is the confidence in morality. The confidence in morality is stated as the fourth, after the three confidences. Why? He says: 'For one thus confident — "The <s>Bhagavān</s> is indeed a perfectly awakened one," and so forth in detail — this is the practice.' The practice of morality beloved of the Noble Ones — this is the meaning. 'Or because of being analogous to health' — why is the confidence in morality stated at the end? 'In the sequence of physician, medicine, attendant, and health.' Or like the analogy of guide, path, caravan, and vehicle — what? — is stated as the fourth at the end — this is what is under discussion. The <s>Bhagavān</s> is analogous to a guide. The <s>Dharma</s> is analogous to the path. The <s>Saṃgha</s> is analogous to the caravan. The moralities beloved of the Noble Ones are analogous to vehicles. 'Beloved of the Noble Ones' (<s>āryakānta</s>) — the practices (<s>prayāṇa</s>) beloved of the Noble Ones are 'beloved of the Noble Ones.'

body.text: (VI.79, 80) aṣṭābhir iti. aṣṭābhir aṃgaiḥ samanvāgataḥ śaikṣaḥ. katamair aṣṭabhiḥ. śaikṣyā samyagdṛṣṭyā yāvac chaikṣeṇa samyaksamādhineti. daśabhir aṃgaiḥ samanvāgato 'śaikṣaḥ. katamair daśabhiḥ. aśaikṣyā samyagdṛṣṭyā yāvad aśaikṣeṇa samyaksamādhinā aśaikṣyā samyagvimuktyā aśaikṣeṇa ca samyagjñāneneti. vimuktitatpratyātmajñānābhyāṃ prabhāvita iti. tasyāṃ
body.translated_text: (VI.79, 80) 'With eight [factors]' — a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) is endowed with eight factors. Which eight? With learner's right view, up to learner's right concentration. A non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) is endowed with ten factors. Which ten? With non-learner's right view, up to non-learner's right concentration, non-learner's right liberation, and non-learner's right knowledge. 'Empowered by liberation and its self-knowledge (<s>pratyātmajñāna</s>)' — in that

body.text: vimuktau pratyātmajñānaṃ tatpratyātmajñānaṃ vimuktiś ca tatpratyātmajñānaṃ ca. vimuktitatpratyātmajñānaṃ. tābhyāṃ prabhāvitaḥ. kleśavimuktyā kleśavimuktipratyātmajñānena ca. kleśebhyo vimukto 'smīti prabhāvitaḥ. prakarṣita ity arthaḥ. tasyaivāśaikṣasya tadvacanaṃ vimuktivacanaṃ vimuktijñānavacanaṃ ca. nyāyyaṃ na śaikṣasyeti. adhimokṣaḥ saṃskṛtā vimuktir [Tib. 273a] iti. dhātvarthaikatvāt aṃgānāṃ saṃskṛtatvād iti. yathā samyagdṛṣṭyādīni saṃskṛtāni. tathā vimuktir api saṃskṛtaiva gṛhyate nāsaṃskṛtā. visabhāgatvād visadṛśatvāt. dve vimuktī sūtra ukte iti. rāgavirāgāc cetovimuktiḥ. avidyāvirāgāt prajñāvimuktir iti. cetovimuktiḥ prajñāvimuktiś cety arthaḥ. vimuktiskaṃdho 'pi sa eveti. śīlaskandhaḥ. samādhiskandhaḥ prajñāskandhaḥ. vimuktiskandhaḥ. vimuktijñānadarśanaś cety atra draṣṭavyaḥ.
body.translated_text: liberation, the self-knowledge is the self-knowledge of that [liberation] — liberation and the self-knowledge of that. The self-knowledge of liberation — empowered by those two. Empowered by the liberation from afflictions and by the self-knowledge of liberation from afflictions — 'I am liberated from the afflictions' — empowered [means] enhanced. This is the meaning. That statement of liberation and liberation-knowledge belongs properly to the non-learner alone, not to the learner. 'Conviction (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) liberation' — because of the identity of meaning of the verbal roots, and because the factors are conditioned. Just as right view and the rest are conditioned, so liberation too is grasped as conditioned alone, not as unconditioned — because of dissimilarity [in nature]. 'Two liberations are stated in the <s>sūtra</s>' — 'From the dispassion toward desire, there is mental liberation (<s>cetovimukti</s>). From the dispassion toward ignorance, there is wisdom-liberation (<s>prajñāvimukti</s>).' The meaning is: mental liberation and wisdom-liberation. 'The liberation-aggregate (<s>vimuktiskandha</s>) too is that very same' — the morality-aggregate (<s>śīlaskandha</s>), the concentration-aggregate (<s>samādhiskandha</s>), the wisdom-aggregate (<s>prajñāskandha</s>), the liberation-aggregate (<s>vimuktiskandha</s>), and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation (<s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s>) — this should be seen here.

body.text: yat tarhi sūtra uktam iti. catvārīmāni vyāghrabodhyāyanāḥ pariśuddhipradhānāni. katamāni catvāri. śīlapariśuddhipradhānaṃ. samādhipariśuddhipradhānaṃ. dṛṣṭipariśuddhipradhānaṃ. vimuktipariśuddhipradhānaṃ ceti vistareṇoktvāha. katamac ca vyāghrabodhyāyanā vimuktipariśuddhipradhānaṃ. yāvad yaś chando vīryam iti vistaraḥ. vyāghrabodhyāyanā iti bahuvacanaṃ. teṣāṃ bahutvāt. vimuktipariśuddhipradhānam iti. vimukteḥ pariśuddhiḥ vimuktipariśuddhiḥ. tasyai pradhānaṃ vīryavimuktipariśuddhipradhānaṃ. [Tib. 273b] tad evam atra vimuktipariśuddhipradhāna iti praśnatrayaṃ. tatra iha bhikṣo rāgāc cittaṃ viraktaṃ bhavati vimuktaṃ. dveṣāt. mohād viraktaṃ bhavati vimuktaṃ. vimuktir uktā. ity aparipūrṇasya vā vimuktiskandhasya paripūraye. paripūrṇasya vānugrahāyāyeti. vimuktipariśuddhiḥ paripūryanugrahalakṣaṇoktā. yaś chando vīryam iti vistareṇa pradhānam uktaṃ. yata evaṃ rāgādibhyo vimuktiḥ prahāṇam ity evaṃlakṣaṇā vimuktir uktā sūtre nādhimuktiḥ. tasmān nādhimokṣa eva vimuktiḥ. kiṃ tarhi. tattvajñānāpanīteṣu rāgādiṣu cetaso vaimalyam anāsravatvam anarthāntarabhūtaṃ ghṛtamaṇḍasvacchatāvad iti apara ity ācāryaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'What then is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>' — 'These, O <s>Vyāghrabodhyāyana</s>, are four [factors] having purification as their chief [aim]. Which four? The [factor] having purification of morality as chief. The [factor] having purification of concentration as chief. The [factor] having purification of view as chief. And the [factor] having purification of liberation as chief' — having spoken in detail, he says: 'And what, O <s>Vyāghrabodhyāyana</s>, is the [factor] having purification of liberation as chief?' Up to 'whatever desire, energy,' and so forth in detail. '<s>Vyāghrabodhyāyana</s>' is in the plural because of their being many. 'The [factor] having purification of liberation as chief' — the purification of liberation is the purification of liberation; its chief is the energy — the [factor] having purification of liberation as chief. Thus here there are three questions regarding the [factor] having purification of liberation as chief. Therein: 'Here, O <s>bhikṣu</s>, the mind becomes dispassionate from desire, liberated; from aversion, from delusion, it becomes dispassionate, liberated' — liberation is stated. 'Either for the fulfillment of the unfulfilled liberation-aggregate, or for the support of the fulfilled one' — the purification of liberation — characterized by fulfillment and support — is stated. 'Whatever desire, energy,' and so forth in detail — the chief is stated. Since liberation characterized as release from desire and the rest is thus stated in the <s>sūtra</s> — not conviction (<s>adhimukṣa</s>) — therefore conviction alone is not liberation. Rather, what then? The purity of mind, the uncontaminated state, that is not a separate entity [from the mind], [arising] when desire and the rest have been removed by the knowledge of reality — like the clarity of clarified butter — thus [says] another <s>Ācārya</s>.

body.text: (VI.81ab) tadutpattivibandhatvād iti. tasyāśaikṣasya cittasyotpattau vibandhatvāt. kleśaprāptir hi vibandhaḥ. yat tarhi notpadyamānam iti. yad anāgataṃ vajropamāt samādher anantaraṃ na bhavaty aśaikṣam eva. laukikaṃ vety aśaikṣasaṃtāna eva yal laukikaṃ. yat tu niyatam utpattau. tad evoktam iti. yad utpādābhimukham anāgataṃ. tad evoktaṃ śāstre vimucyata iti. tadvimucyamānatayā [Tib. 274a] sūpalakṣyatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: (VI.81ab) 'Because of being an obstruction to the arising of that' — because of being an obstruction to the arising of the mind of that non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). For the acquisition of afflictions (<s>kleśaprāpti</s>) is the obstruction.
