'What then is not arising' — what is future and does not come into existence immediately after the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s> — that is exclusively non-learner. Or if mundane [mind arises] — [it arises] only in the continuum of the non-learner. But what is determined to arise — that alone is stated. What is facing arising, that is future — that alone is stated in the treatise as 'being liberated' — the intent is: because of being well-observed through its being liberated.

body.text: tata evotpattyāvaraṇād iti. tata eva kleśaprāptitaḥ. tadutpattivibaṃdhād
body.translated_text: 'From that very obstruction to arising' — from that very acquisition of afflictions. 'Because of being an obstruction to the arising of that'

body.text: iti tad evātra kāraṇaṃ vaktavyaṃ. yady aśaikṣasaṃtānalaukikam api vimucyata ity abhyupagamyate. śaikṣasyāpi laukikam utpadyate. kasmān na vimucyata ity abhyupagamyate. ata āha. na tat tādṛśam ityādi. kleśaprāptisahitaṃ tacchaikṣasya laukikaṃ. na tv aśaikṣasya laukikam evaṃ bhavatīty asāmyaṃ.
body.translated_text: — that very reason is to be stated here. If the mundane [mind] in the continuum of the non-learner too is accepted as being liberated — then the mundane [mind] of the learner too arises; why is it not accepted as being liberated? Therefore he says: 'That is not of such a kind' and so forth. The mundane [mind] of the learner is accompanied by the acquisition of afflictions. But the mundane [mind] of the non-learner is not thus — this is the dissimilarity.

body.text: (VI.81cd)
body.translated_text: (VI.81cd)

body.text: iti. nirodhābhimukhaḥ.
body.translated_text: meaning facing cessation.

body.text: ity aśaikṣacittāvaraṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: meaning the obstruction of the non-learner's mind.

body.text: (VI.82) yā cāsaṃskṛtā vimuktir uktā śāstre ihaiva vā
body.translated_text: (VI.82) 'And the unconditioned liberation stated in the treatise — or right here' —

children.translated_text: 'The unconditioned [liberation] is the abandonment of afflictions' —

body.text: iti. ye ca trayo dhātava ucyaṃte. kvocyaṃte. sūtre śāstre 'pi vā.
body.translated_text: thus. 'And the three elements (<s>dhātu</s>) that are stated' — where are they stated? In the <s>sūtra</s>, or in the treatise as well.

body.text: iti. bhedavivakṣāyām evam ucyate. abhedavivakṣāyāṃ tu yo virāgaḥ. tat prahāṇam apy ucyate. nirodho 'pītyādi.
body.translated_text: thus. When distinction is intended, it is stated thus. But when non-distinction is intended: whatever is dispassion, that is also called abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>), also called cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), and so forth.

body.text: (VI.83) vastuna iti. sāsravasya rūpādeḥ. catuṣkoṭika iti. syān nirvidyate na virajyate. syād virajyate na nirvidyate. syād ubhayaṃ. syān nobhayam [Tib. 274b] iti.
body.translated_text: (VI.83) 'Of the entity (<s>vastu</s>)' — of contaminated form and the rest. 'A four-cornered [analysis] (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>)' — [1] there may be disenchantment (<s>nirvedha</s>) without dispassion; [2] there may be dispassion without disenchantment; [3] there may be both; [4] there may be neither.

children.translated_text: 'Disenchantment occurs through the patient acceptances and knowledges of suffering and origination' —

body.text: iti. anena vastuhetukaṃ nirvedaṃ darśayati.
body.translated_text: by this he shows disenchantment with respect to the entity and its cause (<s>vastuhetu</s>).

children.translated_text: 'Dispassion occurs through all [knowledges] by which one abandons' —

body.text: iti prahāṇakriyāhetukaṃ virāgaṃ darśayati. evaṃ catuṣkoṭikaṃ sidhyatīti. evaṃ nirvedavirāgakāraṇaṃ paricchidya yojyam. anena catuṣkoṭikaṃ sidhyatīty abhiprāyaḥ. katham ity āha. nirvidyata eveti vistaraḥ. nirvidyata eva duḥkhasamudayakṣāṃtibhir duḥkhasamudayajñānaiś ca nirvedavastvālaṃbanatvāt. duḥkhasamudayau hi nirvedasya vastunī ālaṃbanam iti. na virajyate. kleśān aprajahad iti vacanena prahāṇakriyāyā asaṃbhavāt. virajyata eva nirodhamārgakṣāntibhir darśanamārge. nirodhamārgajñānair bhāvanāmārge. kleśān prajahad iti prahāṇakriyāsaṃbhavāt. na nirvidyate. prāmodyavastvālaṃbanatvāt. nirvāṇamārgau hi prāmodyavastunī ālaṃbanam iti. ubhayapūrvaiḥ kleśān prajahad iti nirvidyate ca virājyate ca pūrvair duḥkhasamudayakṣāntijñānaiḥ. kathaṃ. nirvidyate. nirvedavastvālaṃbanatvāt. virajyate. kleśān prajahad [Tib. 275a] iti vacanena prahāṇakriyāsadbhāvāt. nobhayam
body.translated_text: thus he shows dispassion (<s>virāga</s>) caused by the activity of abandonment (<s>prahāṇakriyā</s>). Thus the tetralemma (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>) is established. Having thus delimited the cause of disenchantment (<s>nirveda</s>) and dispassion, it should be connected. The intent is: by this the tetralemma is established. How? — he says: 'One is disenchanted only' — in detail. One is disenchanted only — through the patient acceptances (<s>kṣānti</s>) regarding suffering and origination, and through the knowledges (<s>jñāna</s>) of suffering and origination — because of having as object-domain the bases of disenchantment. For suffering and origination are the bases, the object-domain, of disenchantment. One is not dispassionate — because of the statement 'not abandoning afflictions,' since the activity of abandonment is impossible. One is dispassionate only — through the patient acceptances regarding cessation and the path on the seeing path, and through the knowledges of cessation and the path on the cultivation path — because of the possibility of the activity of abandonment, since the statement is 'abandoning afflictions.' One is not disenchanted — because of having as object-domain the bases of joy (<s>prāmodya</s>). For <s>nirvāṇa</s> and the path are the bases, the object-domain, of joy. Both — one is both disenchanted and dispassionate — through the prior patient acceptances and knowledges of suffering and origination, together with abandoning afflictions. How? One is disenchanted — because of having as object-domain the bases of disenchantment. One is dispassionate — because of the statement 'abandoning afflictions,' since the activity of abandonment exists. Neither

body.text: uttaraiḥ kleśān aprajahad iti. na ca nirvidyate. na ca virajyate. uttarair nirodhamārgakṣāntijñānaiḥ prāmodyavastvālaṃbanatvāt na nirvidyate. kleśān aprajahad iti vacanena prahāṇakriyāyā abhāvāt na virajyate.
body.translated_text: — through the subsequent [patient acceptances and knowledges], since one is not abandoning afflictions. One is neither disenchanted nor dispassionate. Through the subsequent patient acceptances and knowledges of cessation and the path — because of having as object-domain the bases of joy, one is not disenchanted. Because of the statement 'not abandoning afflictions,' since the activity of abandonment does not exist, one is not dispassionate.

body.text: āha. apadiṣṭaṃ prathamāyāṃ koṭyaṃ caturthyāṃ ca kleśāṃ aprajahad iti. kaḥ kān kleśān na prajahāti. tatra vītarāga iti vistaraḥ. tatrārthopakṣepārthaṃ. vītarāgaḥ kāmadhātor yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanād api. satyāni paśyann abhisamayan. dharmajñānakṣāṃtibhir dharmajñānair dharmajñānakṣāntibhiś ca kleśān na prajahāti. laukikena bhāvanāmārgeṇa pūrvaṃ prahīṇatvāt. anāsravā tu kevalaṃ visaṃyogaprāptir utpadyate. anvayajñānakṣāntibhis tv avaśyaṃ kleśān prajahāti. na hi laukikena mārgeṇa bhavāgravairāgyam asti. jñānais tu bhāvanāmārga. prayogavimuktiviśeṣamārgair ānantaryamārgair ap iva kaiścid indriyasaṃcārādyāvasthāsu na kleśān prajahāti. [Tib. 275b] ke 'vaśiṣyaṃte. tadanya ānantaryamārgās taiḥ kleśān prajahātīti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: He says: 'It has been stated in the first and fourth alternatives that one is not abandoning afflictions. Who does not abandon which afflictions?' Therein — in detail, for the purpose of introducing the topic. One dispassionate from the Desire Realm, up to even from the Sphere of Nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), seeing the truths, realizing them — through <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s>s, <s>dharmajñāna</s>s, and <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s>s — does not abandon afflictions, because they were previously abandoned by the mundane cultivation path. But only the uncontaminated acquisition of disconnection (<s>visaṃyogaprāpti</s>) arises. Through <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s>s, however, one necessarily abandons afflictions — for there is no mundane path for dispassion from the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). But through the <s>jñāna</s>s — the cultivation path — through the preparatory, liberation, and special paths, and through some uninterrupted paths too, in certain circumstances such as faculty-transfer — one does not abandon afflictions. What remains? — the other uninterrupted paths: by those one abandons afflictions — this is established.

body.text: ācāryayaśomitrakṛtāyāṃ sphuṭārthāyām abhidharmakośavyākhyāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ kośasthānaṃ samāptaṃ.
body.translated_text: The sixth chapter (<s>kośasthāna</s>) is completed in the <s>Sphuṭārthā Abhidharmakośavyākhyā</s> composed by <s>Ācārya Yaśomitra</s>.

body.text: blank
body.translated_text: [blank]

body.text: VII jñānanirdeśo nāma saptamaṃ kośasthānam
body.translated_text: VII. The seventh chapter (<s>kośasthāna</s>) called the Exposition of Knowledge (<s>jñānanirdeśa</s>)

body.text: (VII.1) ṣaṣṭhāt kośasthānād anantaraṃ saptamasyopanyāse saṃbaṃdhaṃ darśayann āha. kṣāntayaś cocyante. jñānāni ceti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: (VII.1) Showing the connection in the presentation of the seventh [chapter] immediately after the sixth chapter, he says: 'Patient acceptances (<s>kṣānti</s>) are spoken of, and knowledges (<s>jñāna</s>) too' — in detail.

children.translated_text: 'From the mundane supreme dharmas (<s>agradharmāḥ</s>), the <s>dharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of dharma) is uncontaminated' —

body.text: atrāṣṭau kṣāntaya uktāḥ.
body.translated_text: herein, eight patient acceptances are stated.

children.translated_text: 'Regarding suffering in the Desire Realm, then in that very [realm], the <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharma); and again likewise' —

body.text: ity atra jñānāni.
body.translated_text: herein, the knowledges [are stated].

children.translated_text: 'If the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>), or the non-learner's right view' —

body.text: ity atra samyagdṛṣṭiḥ.
body.translated_text: herein, right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) [is stated].

children.text: saiva vimuktī dve jñānaṃ bodhir yathoditety
children.translated_text: 'That itself is the two liberations, knowledge, and awakening as stated' —

body.text: atra samyagjñānaṃ. ihaiva vā ṣaṣṭhakośasthānāvasāna etat sarvam uktam.
body.translated_text: herein, right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) [is stated]. Or, all this was stated right here, at the end of the sixth chapter.

children.translated_text: 'One becomes disenchanted through the patient acceptances and knowledges of suffering and origination; one becomes dispassionate' —
'through all those by which one abandons' —

body.text: iti. śāstrasaṃbandhena vāyam upanyasyate. śāstre hi kṣāntayaś cocyante. jñānāni ca samyagdṛṣṭiḥ samyagjñānaṃ ca. tatpratyāyanāya cāyam ārabhyata ity ataḥ pṛcchati. kiṃ punaḥ kṣāntayo na jñānam iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Or, this is presented by connection with the treatise (<s>śāstra</s>). For in the treatise, patient acceptances are spoken of, and knowledges, and right view, and right knowledge. And this [chapter] is begun for the purpose of explaining those — therefore he asks: 'But are patient acceptances not knowledge?' — in detail.

children.translated_text: 'The stainless patient acceptances are not knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>)' —

body.text: iti. amalā eva kṣāntayo na jñānam ity [Tib. 276a] avadhāraṇāt sāsravāḥ kṣāntayo jñānam ity uktaṃ bhavati. saṃvṛtijñānaṃ hi tad iṣyate. tatpraheyasyety. kṣāntipraheyasya vicikitsānuśayasyāprahīṇatvāt. prahīyate hi tāsv avasthāsv anuśayaḥ. na prahīṇo viprakṛtāvasthatvāt. niścitaṃ ca jñānam iṣyate. nāniścitam. iti na kṣāntayo jñānaṃ. kṣamaṇarūpeṇa ca kṣāntaya utpadyante. na niścayarūpeṇeti na jñānam iti varṇayanti. vicikitsānuśayasyāprahīṇatvād
body.translated_text: thus. Because the stainless patient acceptances alone are not knowledge — from this restriction — it is stated that contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>) patient acceptances are knowledge. For those are accepted as conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>). 'Because of that which is to be abandoned by it' — because the latent disposition of doubt (<s>vicikitsānuśaya</s>) to be abandoned by patient acceptance has not been abandoned. For in those stages, the latent disposition is being abandoned — it has not [yet] been abandoned, because of being in a remote state. And knowledge is accepted as being certain (<s>niścita</s>), not uncertain. Therefore, patient acceptances are not knowledge. And they explain: patient acceptances arise in the form of acceptance (<s>kṣamaṇa</s>), not in the form of certainty (<s>niścaya</s>) — therefore they are not knowledge. 'Because of the non-abandonment of the latent disposition of doubt to be abandoned by it'

body.text: ity etāvati vaktavye tatpraheyasyeti viśeṣaṇaṃ kim arthaṃ. dvitīye hi kṣaṇe prathamakṣāntipraheyo vicikitsānuśayaḥ prahīṇo bhavatīti prathamaiva kṣāntir na jñānam iti gamyeta. na tv anyāḥ kṣāntayaḥ. ity atas tatpraheyasyeti viśeṣaṇaṃ. [yad vā duḥkhadharmajñānādīnāṃ jñānatvapratipādanārthaṃ. yadi vicikitsānuśayāprahīṇatvād ity etāvad ucyate. evaṃ] saṃtīraṇātmakatvād iti. upanidhyānasvabhāvatvād ity arthaḥ. asaṃtīraṇāparimārgaṇāśayatvād iti. nāsti saṃtīraṇam asyety asaṃtīraṇaṃ. parimārgaṇe āśayo 'bhiprāyaḥ parimārgaṇāśayaḥ. nāsya parimārgaṇāśaya ity aparimārgaṇāśayaṃ. asaṃtīraṇaṃ ca tad aparimārgaṇāśayaṃ ca asaṃtīraṇāparimārgaṇāśayaṃ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. kṣayajñānam anutpādajñānaṃ ca na dṛṣṭir ity [Tib. 276b] arthaḥ. yāvad ayam akṛtakṛtyaḥ. tāvad duḥkhādīni satyāny upanidhyāyati parimārgayati cāśayato yathoktair anityādibhir ākāraiḥ. kṛtakṛtyasya punar yathā dṛṣṭiṣv eva duḥkhādiṣv āryasatyeṣu pratyavekṣaṇamātraṃ tābhyāṃ bhavatīti duḥkhaṃ mayā parijñātaṃ na punaḥ parijñeyam ityādi. tasmān na te dṛṣṭisvabhāve.
body.translated_text: — this much being sufficient to say, what is the purpose of the qualifier 'to be abandoned by it'? In the second moment, the latent disposition of doubt to be abandoned by the first patient acceptance has already been abandoned — so one would understand that only the first patient acceptance is not knowledge, not the others. Therefore, [the qualifier] 'to be abandoned by it' [is used]. [Alternatively, for the purpose of establishing that the <s>duḥkhadharmajñāna</s> and the rest are knowledge: if only 'because of the non-abandonment of the latent disposition of doubt' were said, then] 'Because of having the nature of examination (<s>saṃtīraṇa</s>)' — the meaning is: because of having the nature of careful consideration (<s>upanidhyāna</s>). 'Because of not having the nature of non-examination and non-searching' — that which has no examination is non-examination. That whose inclination (<s>āśaya</s>) is toward searching is of-searching-inclination. That which does not have searching-inclination is of-non-searching-inclination. Non-examination and of-non-searching-inclination — its state. Therefore — the meaning is: the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>) are not view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>). As long as this one has not accomplished his task — so long he carefully considers and searches, with the relevant aspects of impermanence and the rest, the truths of suffering and the rest. But for one who has accomplished his task — just as with the views, regarding the noble truths of suffering and the rest — through those two [knowledges], there is merely a reviewing (<s>pratyavekṣaṇa</s>): 'Suffering has been fully comprehended by me, need not be fully comprehended again,' and so forth. Therefore those two are not of the nature of view.

children.translated_text: 'The other noble wisdom, in both ways' —

body.text: iti. duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ yāvan mārge 'nvayajñānaṃ. sā prajñopanidhyānapravṛttā prahīṇatadviṣayavicikitsā ca.
body.translated_text: thus. The <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding suffering, up to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> regarding the path — that wisdom, operating through careful consideration, and having the doubt regarding its object-domain abandoned —

body.text: laukikī. sā sarvaiva jñānam ity avadhāraṇaṃ. na sā prajñāsti. yan na jñānam ity arthaḥ. kā punar asau prajñā. paṃcavijñānakāyikā kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtā mānasī yā dṛṣṭisvabhāvakleśasaṃprayuktā anivṛtāvyākṛtā ca. yā punar dṛṣṭisvabhāvā yā ca mānasī kuśalā. sā kiṃ bhavatīty āha.
body.translated_text: means worldly (<s>laukikī</s>). That is entirely knowledge — from the restriction. There is no wisdom that is not knowledge — this is the meaning. But what is that wisdom? That which accompanies the five sense-consciousnesses — whether wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate — and the mental [consciousness] that is associated with afflictions of the nature of view, and the unobstructed-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>). But that which is of the nature of view, and that which is mental and wholesome — what is that? — he says:

body.text: iti. eṣā ṣaḍvidhā laukikī prajñā dṛṣṭiḥ. anyā na dṛṣṭiḥ. ṣaḍ evety avadhāraṇāt. kā punar anyā. yā pūrvam uktā laukikī. jñānaṃ tv eṣā cānyā ceti. eṣā ca ṣaḍvidhā dṛṣṭisvabhāvā prajñā. tato 'nyā ca pūrvoktā jñānam ity ucyate. ata eva ca
body.translated_text: thus. This sixfold worldly wisdom is view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>). The other is not view — from the restriction 'six only.' But what is the other? That which was previously stated as worldly. 'But this and the other are knowledge' — this sixfold wisdom of the nature of view, and the other previously stated — are called knowledge.

body.text: iti cakāraḥ paṭhyate. yasmād etāḥ ṣaṭ jñānāni cocyante dṛṣṭayaś ceti.
body.translated_text: thus, the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is read. Because these six are called both knowledges and views.

body.text: (VII.2, 3) daśabhir jñānaiḥ. katamaiḥ. [Tib. 277a] dharmānvayasaṃvṛtiparacittaduḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgakṣayānutpādajñānair avadhāraṇārtho 'yam ārambho daśaiva jñānāni. cyutyupapādapudgalajñānādīnām eṣām evāntarbhāvāt.
body.translated_text: (VII.2, 3) 'Through ten knowledges.' Which? <s>Dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharma), <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge), <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> (conventional knowledge), <s>paracittajñāna</s> (knowledge of others' minds), <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> (knowledge of suffering), <s>samudayajñāna</s> (knowledge of origination), <s>nirodhajñāna</s> (knowledge of cessation), <s>mārgajñāna</s> (knowledge of the path), <s>kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of destruction), and <s>anutpādajñāna</s> (knowledge of non-arising). This beginning is for the purpose of restriction: there are ten knowledges only — because the knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapādajñāna</s>), the knowledge of persons (<s>pudgalajñāna</s>), and the like are included within these very [ten].

body.text: samāsena tu dve eva sāsravam anāsravaṃ ceti. prāyeṇeti viśeṣaṇaṃ. ghaṭapaṭādikaṃ saṃvṛtisadvastu saṃvṛtijñānam ālaṃbate. svasāmānyalakṣaṇam api tu kadācid gṛhṇāti. sāṃvṛtam iti. saṃvṛtau bhavaṃ sāṃvṛtaṃ.
body.translated_text: In brief, however, there are only two — contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>) and uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>). 'For the most part' — is a qualifier. Conventional knowledge takes as its object-domain the conventional real entities such as pots, cloths, and the like. But sometimes it also grasps the specific and general characteristics [of dharmas]. 'Conventional' (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>) — that which exists in the conventional [realm] is conventional.

body.text: api saṃkṣipyamāṇaṃ
body.translated_text: 'when condensed too' —

body.text: duḥkhajñānādīnām anayor evāntarbhāvāt. ālaṃbanaṃ saṃbhavata iti. yasya yad ālaṃbanaṃ. tasya tad bhavati. na hi cakṣurvijñānasya śabdālaṃbanaṃ. tadālaṃbanatvād iti. duḥkhādyālaṃbanatvād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: Because the knowledge of suffering and the rest are included within these two alone. 'Object-domain is possible' — whatever has whatever as its object-domain, that becomes that. For eye-consciousness does not have sound as its object-domain. 'Because of having that as its object-domain' — the meaning is: because of having suffering and the rest as its object-domain.

body.text: (VII.4)
body.translated_text: (VII.4)

body.text: iti. ete eva dharmānvayajñāne dve duḥkhādyālaṃbanabhedāc caturvidhe. adṛṣṭisvabhāve satī kṣayajñānam anutpādajñānaṃ cocyate.
body.translated_text: thus. These very <s>dharmajñāna</s> and <s>anvayajñāna</s> — the two — are fourfold because of the division by object-domain of suffering and the rest. Not being of the nature of view, the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>) are [also] spoken of.

body.text: te punaḥ kṣayānutpādajñāne prathamotpanne satī
body.translated_text: 'those' — the knowledge of destruction and the knowledge of non-arising — 'when first arisen' —

body.text: duḥkhasamudayālaṃbane avaśyaṃ bhavata ity arthaḥ. kasmād ity āha. duḥkhasamudayākārair bhāvāgrikaskaṃdhālaṃbanatvād iti. [tasya hi sarvapaścād bhavāgram eva prahīyate. tasmād yena ca pīḍyate yena ca baddhaṃ tata eva mokṣaṃ bahu manyamāno 'nantaraṃ kṣīṇaṃ bhavāgram ālaṃbate. tac ca duḥkhaṃ yā samudayā cityato duḥkhasamudayākārair bhavāgram ālaṃbate.] yasmād avaśyaṃ te prathamotpannakṣayānutpādajñāne [Tib. 277b] duḥkhākārair anityādibhiḥ samudayākārair vā hetvādibhir bhāvāgrikān skaṃdhān ālaṃbate. aprathamotpanne tv anyasatyālaṃbane api te bhavata ity arthād uktaṃ bhavati. vajropamānantaraṃ kṣayajñānaṃ bhavati. tadanantaraṃ cānutpādajñānam ity ataḥ pṛcchati. kiṃ vajropamo 'pi tābhyām ekālaṃbano bhavatīti. tābhyām iti prathamotpannābhyām ity arthaḥ. yathā kṣayānutpādajñāne ekālaṃbane kiṃ vajropamo 'pi tābhyām ekālaṃbana ity apiśabdasyārthaḥ. yadi duḥkhasamudayālaṃbano bhavati. kiṃ. tābhyām ekālaṃbano bbhavatīti saṃbhavaḥ. atha nirodhamārgālaṃbano bhavati naikālaṃbanaḥ. tayor niyamena bhāvāgrikaskaṃdhālaṃbanatvāt. yathā hi viṣakāṇḍaviddhasya mṛtasya viṣaṃ sarvam aṃgam abhivyāpya vraṇadeśa eva maraṇakāle 'vatiṣṭhate nānyatra. tadvad asya yoginaḥ praheya eva bhāvāgrikaskaṃdhalakṣaṇe jñānam avatiṣṭhate.
body.translated_text: The meaning is: they necessarily have suffering and origination as their object-domain. Why? — he says: because of having as their object-domain the aggregates of the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) through the aspects of suffering and origination. [For that which is last of all is the Peak of Existence alone that is abandoned. Therefore, greatly valuing the liberation from that very thing by which one is afflicted and by which one is bound, one immediately afterward takes as object-domain the Peak of Existence that has been destroyed. And that is suffering and origination — therefore one takes as object-domain the Peak of Existence through the aspects of suffering and origination.] Because necessarily those first-arisen knowledge of destruction and knowledge of non-arising take as their object-domain the aggregates of the Peak of Existence through the aspects of suffering — impermanence and the rest — or through the aspects of origination — cause and the rest. But when not first arisen, they can also have another truth as their object-domain — this is stated implicitly. The knowledge of destruction arises immediately after the diamond-like [concentration] (<s>vajropama</s>). And the knowledge of non-arising arises immediately after that. Therefore he asks: 'Is the diamond-like [concentration] too of the same object-domain as those two?' 'Those two' means: as those two that are first arisen — this is the meaning. Just as the knowledge of destruction and knowledge of non-arising are of the same object-domain — is the diamond-like [concentration] too of the same object-domain as those two? — this is the meaning of the word 'too.' If it has suffering and origination as its object-domain — what? — then it would be of the same object-domain as those two — this is possible. But if it has cessation and the path as its object-domain, it would not be of the same object-domain — because those two necessarily have the aggregates of the Peak of Existence as their object-domain. Just as the poison in one pierced by a poisoned arrow — when the person dies, the poison, having pervaded all the limbs, settles at the wound-site alone at the time of death, not elsewhere — similarly, for this yogin, the knowledge settles precisely at the characteristics of the Peak-of-Existence aggregates that are to be abandoned.

children.translated_text: 'One who knows others' minds through four [knowledges]' —

body.text: iti. caturbhya eva dharmajñānādibhyas tatsaṃgṛhītatvāt. na duḥkhajñānādibhyaḥ. anyākāratvāt. anāsravaṃ hi paracittajñānaṃ mārgākāram eva mārgajñānatvāt. yat tu sāsravaṃ. tal laukikākāraṃ sarāgam [Tib. 278a] vigatarāgam ityādi. śraddhādhimuktasamayavimuktamārgeṇeti. yathāsaṃkhyaṃ śraddhādhimuktamārgena dṛṣṭiprāptamārgaṃ na jānāti. samayavimuktamārgeṇāsamayavimuktamārgaṃ na jānāti. adhareṇottaram iti. anāgāmimārgeṇārhanmārgaṃ na jānāti. arhanmārgeṇa pratyekabuddhamārgam ityādi. kāmadhātūrdhvadhātupratipakṣālaṃbanatvāt tayor iti. tayor dharmajñānapakṣānvayajñānapakṣayoḥ. dharmajñānapakṣasya kāmadhātupratipakṣa ālaṃbanam. anvayajñānapakṣasya ūrdhvadhātupratipakṣa ālaṃbanam iti niyamaḥ. darśanamārge paracittajñānaṃ nāstīty avyāpāratvāt darśanamārgasya. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiṃ dharmajñānaṃ ceti saṃbhavaṃ praty evam ucyate. kadācid dhi prayogavaśād duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntiṃ duḥkhe 'nvayajñānaṃ ca jñātuṃ saṃbhavati. aṣṭamaṃ ca samudayānvayajñānam iti. dharmajñānapakṣau dvau kṣaṇau jñātvānvayajñānapakṣaṃ pareṇa cittaṃ jñāsyāmīti prayogaṃ kṛtvā samudayānvayajñānam aṣṭamaṃ saṃbhāvayati. mṛduprayogatvād iti alpaprayogatvād ity arthaḥ. śrāvakasya hi mahāprayogasādhyaṃ tad anvayajñānapakṣālaṃbanaṃ [Tib. 278b] paracittam. ato yāvat sa tatra prayogam ārabhate. tāvad ayaṃ ṣoḍaśaṃ cittam anuprāpto bhavatīti. aṃtarā na jānāti. prathamadvitīyapaṃcadaśān iti etān eva trīn jānāti. kathaṃ. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiṃ dharmajñānaṃ ca jñātvā prayogāntaraṃ ca kṛtvā paṃcadaśakṣaṇaṃ mārgānvayajñānakṣāntiṃ jānātīti.
body.translated_text: Thus. From only the four — <s>dharmajñāna</s> and the rest — because of being included in those. Not from <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> (knowledge of suffering) and the rest. Because of having different aspects. For uncontaminated knowledge of others'' minds has only the aspect of the path, since it is a <s>mārgajñāna</s> (knowledge of the path). But that which is contaminated has mundane aspects — with attachment, [Tib. 278a] without attachment, and so forth. "By the path of <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> (faith-liberated) and <s>samayavimukta</s> (occasionally-liberated)" — in due order: by the path of the <s>śraddhādhimukta</s>, one does not know the path of the <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> (attainment-through-view); by the path of the <s>samayavimukta</s>, one does not know the path of the <s>asamayavimukta</s> (non-occasionally-liberated). "A lower [does not know] a higher" — by the path of the <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner), one does not know the path of the <s>arhat</s>; by the path of the <s>arhat</s>, [one does not know] the path of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, and so forth. "Because of the two having as their domain the antidotes to the Desire Realm and the upper realms" — of those two, the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class and the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class. The domain of the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class is the antidote to the Desire Realm. The domain of the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class is the antidote to the upper realms — this is the restriction. Knowledge of others' minds does not exist in the path of seeing — because of the non-engagement of the path of seeing. "It is said thus regarding the possibility of [knowing] the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patience of knowledge of dharmas) and <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharmas) regarding suffering" — sometimes, by the force of practice, it is possible to know the <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> regarding suffering and the <s>anvayajñāna</s> regarding suffering. "And the eighth, the <s>samudayānvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge of the origin)" — having known the two moments of the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class, and having made the effort thinking "I will know the mind of another through the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class," one admits the possibility of the <s>samudayānvayajñāna</s> as the eighth [moment]. "Because of mild practice" — the meaning is: because of little practice. For the <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple), [knowing] the mind of another with the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class as its domain is attainable through great practice. [Tib. 278b] Therefore, for as long as he engages in that practice, by that time this one has reached the sixteenth mind-moment. Thus he does not know [the minds of those] in between. "The first, second, and fifteenth" — he knows only these three. How? Having known the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> regarding suffering and <s>dharmajñāna</s>, and having made another effort, he knows the fifteenth moment — the <s>mārgānvayajñānakṣānti</s> (patience of inferential knowledge of the path).

body.text: (VII.7) katham anāsraveṇa jñānenaivaṃ janātīti. anāsravaṇāṃ duḥkhādyākāratvat. idaṃ ca saṃvṛtyākāraṃ duḥkhaṃ me parijñātam ity evamādyākāratvād ataḥ pṛcchati. tadviśeṣeṇa tayor viśeṣa iti. tasya saṃvṛtijñānadvayasya tatpṛṣṭhalabdhasya viśeṣeṇa duḥkhaṃ me parijñātaṃ yāvan me mārgo bhāvita iti jānāti. duḥkhaṃ me parijñātaṃ na punaḥ parijñeyaṃ. yāvan mārgo me bhāvito na punar bhāvayitavyaḥ iti ca jānātīty evaṃrūpeṇa tayor anāsravayoḥ kṣayānutpādajñānayor viśeṣaḥ śāstre jñāpito darśitaḥ. ata eva tad upādāyety uktaṃ. tad upādāyeti pūrvīkṛtya tat puraskṛtyety arthaḥ. niṣyaṃdane tayor nirvikalpayor viśeṣo 'numīyata ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: (VII.7) "How does one know thus through uncontaminated knowledge?" Because uncontaminated [knowledges] have aspects of suffering and the rest. And this [knowledge of destruction and non-arising] has conventional aspects — because of having aspects such as "Suffering has been fully comprehended by me" — therefore he asks. "By the distinguishing feature of that, the distinction of those two" — by the distinguishing feature of that twofold conventional knowledge, which is obtained subsequently to it, one knows "Suffering has been fully comprehended by me," up to "The path has been cultivated by me." [One also knows] "Suffering has been fully comprehended by me and need not be fully comprehended again," up to "The path has been cultivated by me and need not be cultivated again" — and thus by such a distinguishing feature, the distinction of those two uncontaminated knowledges — the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>) — is indicated and shown in the treatise. Therefore it is said "taking that as basis" — "taking that as basis" means having made that primary, having placed that foremost — this is the meaning. From the outflow of those two non-conceptual [knowledges], the distinction is inferred — this is the intent.

body.text: anāsraveṇāpy evaṃ jānātīti. ṣoḍaśākāravyatirikto 'sty anāsrava ākāraḥ.
body.translated_text: "One knows thus also through an uncontaminated [aspect]" — there is an uncontaminated aspect distinct from the sixteen aspects.

body.text: tenaivaṃ jānātīty apare. yadi tad upādāya yaj jñānaṃ darśanam iti śāstravacanena duḥkhaparijñānādisaṃvṛtijñānaphalam [Tib. 279a] amāsravaṃ kṣayānutpādajñānam ucyate. yad idam ucyate.
body.translated_text: Others [say] one knows thus through that. If, taking that as basis, the knowledge which is called "seeing" — by this statement of the treatise, the uncontaminated <s>kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of destruction) and <s>anutpādajñāna</s> (knowledge of non-arising) are called the fruit of conventional knowledge of full comprehension of suffering and the rest. [Tib. 279a] Then what is stated:

children.translated_text: "The knowledge of destruction and non-arising is not view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>)" —

body.text: iti na dṛṣṭir iti. tad virudhyate. tenāha. darśanavacanaṃ tu bhāṣyākṣepād iti. yad etac chāstre vacanaṃ yaj jñānaṃ darśanam iti. bhāṣyākṣepād bhavati. duḥkhajñānādiṣu hi jñānaṃ darśanaṃ vidyā buddhir bodhir iti paṭhyate. tatpāṭhākṣepeṇāyam upatiṣṭhate tatpāṭhināṃ pāṭhaḥ. na tu te kṣayānutpādajñāne darśanasvabhāve. na dṛṣṭisvabhāve ity arthaḥ. pratyakṣavṛttitvād veti. pratyakṣā vṛttir asya jñānadvayasya. tad iyaṃ pratyakṣavṛttiḥ. tadbhāvat. anayor darśanavacanaṃ. na hy etajjñānadvaye ānumānikavad āgāmikavad vā parokṣavṛttiḥ. pratyakṣavṛttiś ca darśanam iṣyate. tadyathā cakṣurvijñānaṃ. tadsādharmyād etad api jñānadvayaṃ darśanam ity uktam. ata evoktam iti. ata eva pratyakṣavṛttitvād uktaṃ śāstre yat tāvaj jñānaṃ. darśanam api tat. syāt tu darśanaṃ na jñānam aṣṭāv ābhisamayāntikāḥ kṣāntayaḥ. tad idam uktaṃ bhavati darśanatvam anayor iṣyate. na dṛṣṭitvam iti.
body.translated_text: that is, it is not <s>dṛṣṭi</s> — that would be contradicted. Therefore he says: "But the statement "seeing" is due to the implication of the treatise (<s>bhāṣya</s>)." This statement in the treatise — "which knowledge is seeing" — arises from the implication of the <s>bhāṣya</s>. For in [the section on] <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> and the rest, "knowledge, seeing, <s>vidyā</s>, <s>buddhi</s>, <s>bodhi</s>" is read. By the implication of that reading, this stands for those who follow that reading. But those two [knowledges of destruction and non-arising] are not of the nature of <s>darśana</s> (seeing) — they are not of the nature of <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (view) — this is the meaning. "Because of functioning through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>)" — the functioning of this pair of knowledges is direct perception; this is its directly perceptible functioning; because of being such. The statement "seeing" applies to these two. For in this pair of knowledges, there is no indirect functioning as in inferential or scriptural [knowledge]. And directly perceptible functioning is accepted as "seeing" — just as eye-consciousness [is seeing]. By similarity with that, this pair of knowledges too is called "seeing." "Therefore it is said" — therefore, precisely because of functioning through direct perception, it is said in the treatise: "that which is knowledge is also seeing." But it may be seeing and not knowledge — the eight <s>kṣānti</s>s (patiences) that are at the culmination of full understanding. This amounts to saying: the status of seeing is accepted for these two, not the status of <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (view).

body.text: tatreti teṣu daśasu jñāneṣu saṃvṛtijñānaṃ saṃvṛtijñānam eva svabhāvasaṃgrahataḥ. ekasya ca paracittajñānasya bhāga ekadeśaḥ. tasya hi sāsravānāsravasya [Tib. 279b] sāsrava eva bhāgaḥ saṃvṛtijñānaṃ. nānāsravo bhāga iti. dharmajñānaṃ daśasu jñāneṣv ekaṃ jñānaṃ dharmajñānam eva. saptānāṃ ca bhāgo duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgaparacittakṣayānutpādajñānānām. kathaṃ. duḥkhajñānaṃ hi dharmānvayajñānasvabhāvaṃ. tasya yo dharmajñānabhāgaḥ. tad dharmajñānam. evaṃ samudayajñāsya yāvad anutpādajñānasya dharmānvayajñānasvabhāvasya yo dharmajñānabhāgaḥ. tad dharmajñānaṃ. na tv anvayajñānabhāga iti. paracittajñānasya tu dharmānvayamārgasaṃvṛtijñānasvabhāvasya dharmajñānabhāgo dharmajñānam iti. evam anvayajñānam ekam anvayajñānam eva. saptānāṃ ca bhāgaḥ. teṣām eva duḥkhajñānādīnām yo 'nvayajñānabhāgaḥ. tad anvayajñānam iti yojyaṃ. duḥkhajñānaṃ daśasu jñāneṣv ekaṃ jñānaṃ. tad eva duḥkhajñānaṃ. caturṇāṃ ca bhāgo dharmānvayakṣayānutpādajñānānām. etāni hi dharmajñānādīni catvāri catuḥsatyālaṃbanāni bhavanti. ya eṣāṃ duḥkhasatyālambano bhāgaḥ. tad duḥkhajñānaṃ. nānyo bhāgaḥ. ity evaṃ samudayanirodhajñāne
body.translated_text: "Therein" — among those ten knowledges, conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>) is conventional knowledge itself in terms of intrinsic nature. And a portion — a part — of one, the knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>). For of that [paracittajñāna], which has both contaminated and uncontaminated [aspects], [Tib. 279b] only the contaminated portion is conventional knowledge — not the uncontaminated portion. <s>Dharmajñāna</s> — among the ten knowledges, one knowledge is <s>dharmajñāna</s> itself. And it is a portion of seven: <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> (knowledge of suffering), <s>samudayajñāna</s> (knowledge of origin), <s>nirodhajñāna</s> (knowledge of cessation), <s>mārgajñāna</s> (knowledge of path), <s>paracittajñāna</s>, <s>kṣayajñāna</s>, and <s>anutpādajñāna</s>. How? For <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> has the intrinsic nature of both <s>dharma</s>-[jñāna] and <s>anvaya</s>-[jñāna]. That portion of it which is the <s>dharmajñāna</s> portion — that is <s>dharmajñāna</s>. Similarly, the <s>dharmajñāna</s> portion of <s>samudayajñāna</s>, up to <s>anutpādajñāna</s> — which has the intrinsic nature of both <s>dharma</s> and <s>anvaya</s> [jñāna] — that is <s>dharmajñāna</s>. Not the <s>anvayajñāna</s> portion. And the <s>dharmajñāna</s> portion of <s>paracittajñāna</s>, which has the intrinsic nature of <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>mārga</s>-, and <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> — that is <s>dharmajñāna</s>. Similarly, <s>anvayajñāna</s> — one [knowledge] is <s>anvayajñāna</s> itself among the ten. And it is a portion of seven. Of those same — <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> and the rest — that which is the <s>anvayajñāna</s> portion is <s>anvayajñāna</s> — this should be connected. <s>Duḥkhajñāna</s> — among the ten knowledges, one knowledge is <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> itself. And it is a portion of four: <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>kṣaya</s>-, and <s>anutpādajñāna</s>. For these four — <s>dharmajñāna</s> and the rest — take the four truths as their objects. That portion of them which has the truth of suffering as its object is <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> — not another portion. Thus <s>samudayajñāna</s> and <s>nirodhajñāna</s>

body.text: yojye pratyekam. ekaṃ jñānaṃ samudayajñānaṃ nirodhajñānaṃ vā. caturṇāṃ ca bhāgo dharmānvayakṣayānutpādajñānānāṃ yaḥ samudayālaṃbanabhāgo nirodhālaṃbanabhāgo vā. tat samudayajñānaṃ nirodhājñānaṃ ca. mārgajñānaṃ daśasu jñāneṣv [Tib. 280a] ekaṃ jñānaṃ tad eva mārgajñānaṃ. paṃcānāṃ ca bhāgaḥ. dharmānvayakṣayānutpādaparacittajñānānaṃ. etāni paṃca mārgajñānāni mārgajñānasvabhāvāni bhavanti. ya eṣāṃ mārgajñānabhāgaḥ. tan mārgajñānaṃ netara iti. paravittajñānaṃ daśasu jñāneṣv ekaṃ jñānaṃ. caturṇāṃ ca bhāgo dharmānvayamārgasaṃvṛtijñānānāṃ. etāni hi catvāri jñānāni paracittāparacittajñānaṃ svabhāvāni bhāvaṃti. ya eṣāṃ paracittajñānabhāgaḥ. tat paracittajñānaṃ. netara iti. kṣayajñānaṃ daśasu jñāneṣv ekaṃ jñānaṃ tad eva kṣayajñānaṃ svabhāvasaṃgrahataḥ. ṣaṇṇāṃ ca bhāgo dharmānvayaduḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgajñānānāṃ. kṣayajñānaṃ duḥkhaṃ me parijñātam ity evamādyākārajñānaniṣyandaṃ. tatra yat kāmāvacaraduḥkhādyālaṃbanaṃ. tad dharmajñane 'ntarbhavati. yad rūpārūpyāvacaraduḥkhādyālaṃbanaṃ. tad anvayajñāne 'ntarbhavati. yat pratyekaṃ duḥkhādyālaṃbanaṃ. tad duḥkhajñānaṃ yāvan mārgajñānaṃ vā bhavati. tatra ya eṣām evaṃlakṣaṇo bhāgaḥ. tat kṣayajñānaṃ netara iti. ṣaṇṇāṃ bhāga ity ucyate. [Tib. 280b] evam anutpādajñānaṃ daśasu jñāneṣv ekaṃ jñānaṃ tad evānutpādajñānaṃ. ṣaṇṇāṃ ca bhago dharmānvayaduḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgajñānānāṃ yo bhāgaḥ. duḥkhaṃ me parijñātaṃ na punaḥ parijñeyam ity evamādyākāraniṣyandaṃ. tad anutpādajñānaṃ. rūpārūpyāvacraduḥkhādyālaṃbanam. tad anvayajñānaṃ. netaro bhāga iti. ṣaṇṇāṃ bhāga ity ucyate.
body.translated_text: should be connected individually. One knowledge is <s>samudayajñāna</s> or <s>nirodhajñāna</s>. And it is a portion of four — <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>kṣaya</s>-, and <s>anutpādajñāna</s> — whatever portion has the origin as its object or cessation as its object — that is <s>samudayajñāna</s> or <s>nirodhajñāna</s>. <s>Mārgajñāna</s> — among the ten knowledges, one knowledge is <s>mārgajñāna</s> itself. And it is a portion of five: <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>kṣaya</s>-, <s>anutpāda</s>-, and <s>paracittajñāna</s>. [Tib. 280a] These five are <s>mārgajñāna</s>s — they have the intrinsic nature of <s>mārgajñāna</s>. That portion of them which is the <s>mārgajñāna</s> portion — that is <s>mārgajñāna</s>, not the other. <s>Paracittajñāna</s> — among the ten knowledges, one knowledge [is paracittajñāna itself]. And it is a portion of four: <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>mārga</s>-, and <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>. For these four knowledges have the intrinsic nature of both knowledge-of-others''-minds and non-knowledge-of-others''-minds. That portion of them which is the <s>paracittajñāna</s> portion — that is <s>paracittajñāna</s>, not the other. <s>Kṣayajñāna</s> — among the ten knowledges, one knowledge is <s>kṣayajñāna</s> itself in terms of intrinsic nature. And it is a portion of six: <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>duḥkha</s>-, <s>samudaya</s>-, <s>nirodha</s>-, and <s>mārgajñāna</s>. <s>Kṣayajñāna</s> is the outflow of knowledge with aspects such as "Suffering has been fully comprehended by me." Therein, that which has as its object the suffering and the rest pertaining to the Desire Realm — that is included in <s>dharmajñāna</s>. That which has as its object the suffering and the rest pertaining to the Form and Formless Realms — that is included in <s>anvayajñāna</s>. That which has as its object each [truth] individually — suffering and the rest — that is <s>duḥkhajñāna</s>, up to <s>mārgajñāna</s>. Therein, that portion of them having such characteristics — that is <s>kṣayajñāna</s>, not the other. Thus it is said to be a portion of six. [Tib. 280b] Similarly, <s>anutpādajñāna</s> — among the ten knowledges, one knowledge is <s>anutpādajñāna</s> itself. And it is a portion of six: <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>duḥkha</s>-, <s>samudaya</s>-, <s>nirodha</s>-, and <s>mārgajñāna</s> — the portion which is the outflow of [aspects such as] "Suffering has been fully comprehended by me and need not be fully comprehended again" — that is <s>anutpādajñāna</s>. [That which has as its object] the suffering and the rest pertaining to the Form and Formless Realms — that is <s>anvayajñāna</s>. Not the other portion — thus it is said to be a portion of six.

body.text: (VII.8)
body.translated_text: (VII.8)

body.text: iti. ākāraś ca gocaraś cākāragocaraṃ. ākāraś cākāragocaraṃ. ākārākāragocaram. tasmāt. svabhāvataḥ saṃvṛtijñānam iti. svabhāvena svabhāvataḥ. saṃvṛtijñānaṃ. kasmād ity āha. apramārthajñānatvād iti. kāmadhātupratipakṣo dharmajñānaṃ. ūrdhvadhātupratipakṣo 'nvayajñānaṃ. tathā hi śāstra uktaṃ. dharmajñānaṃ katamat. kāmapratisaṃyukteṣu saṃskāreṣu yad anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ. kāmapratisaṃyuktānāṃ
body.translated_text: thus. Aspect and domain is aspect-domain. Aspect and aspect-domain is aspect-aspect-domain. From that. "By intrinsic nature, it is conventional knowledge" — by its own nature, intrinsically, it is conventional knowledge. Why? He says: "Because it is not knowledge of ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>)." The antidote to the Desire Realm is <s>dharmajñāna</s>. The antidote to the upper realms is <s>anvayajñāna</s>. For thus it is stated in the treatise: "What is <s>dharmajñāna</s>? Whatever uncontaminated knowledge regarding formations connected with the Desire Realm. Whatever

body.text: saṃskārāṇāṃ hetau yad anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ. kāmapratisaṃyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ nirodhe yad anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ kāmapratisaṃyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ prahāṇāya mārge yad anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ. idam ucyate dharmajñānam. api khalu dharmajñāne dharmajñānabhūmau ca yad anāsravaṃ. idam ucyate dharmajñānam. anvayajñānaṃ katamat. rūpārūpyapratisaṃyukteṣu saṃskāreṣu yad anāsravaṃ jñānam. rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ [Tib. 281a] hetau yad anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ. rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ nirodhe yad anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ. rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ prahāṇāya mārge yad anāsravaṃ jñānam. idam ucyate anvayajñānaṃ. api khalv anvayajñāne anvayajñānabhūmau ca yad anāsravaṃ jñānam. idam ucyate 'nvayajñānam iti. ākārato duḥkhasamudayajñāne iti. ākārata eva nālaṃbanataḥ paṃcopādānaskaṃdhalakṣaṇatvena tayor abhedāt. tathā hi śāstra uktaṃ. duḥkhajñānaṃ katamat. paṃcopādānaskaṃdhān anityato duḥkhataḥ śunyato 'nātmataś ca manasikurvato yad anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ. idam ucyate duḥkhajñānaṃ. samudayajñānaṃ katamat. sāsravaṃ hetukaṃ hetutaḥ samudayataḥ prabhavataḥ pratyayataś ca manasikurvato yad anāsravaṃ jñānam. idam ucyate samudayajñānaṃ. ākārālaṃbanato nirodhamārgajñāne iti. ākārataś cālaṃbanataś ca nirodhamārgajñāne vyavasthāpyete. tathā hi śāstra uktaṃ. nirodhajñānaṃ katamat. nirodhaṃ nirodhataḥ śāntataḥ. praṇītato niḥsaraṇataś ca manasikurvato yad anāsravaṃ jñānam. idam ucyate nirodhajñānam iti. mārgajñānaṃ katamat. mārgaṃ mārgato nyāyataḥ pratipattito nairyāṇikataś ca manasikurvato yad anāsravaṃ jñānam. idam ucyate mārgajñānam iti. prathamata [Tib. 281b] iti grahaṇam anutpādajñānaviśeṣaṇārthaṃ. tad api hi kṛtakṛtyasaṃtāna utpadyate. sarvānāsravahetukatvād iti. prathamotpannāni daśa jñānāny adhikṛtya sabhāgahetunā sarvānāsravahetukam anutpādajñānaṃ. kṣayajñānaṃ tu na sarvānāsravahetukaṃ. na hy anutpādajñānam asya hetur bhavati viśiṣṭatvāt.
body.translated_text: — whatever uncontaminated knowledge there is regarding the cause of conditioned things (<s>saṃskāra</s>). Whatever uncontaminated knowledge there is regarding the cessation of conditioned things connected with the Desire Realm. Whatever uncontaminated knowledge there is regarding the path for the abandonment of conditioned things connected with the Desire Realm. This is called <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharmas). Moreover, whatever is uncontaminated in <s>dharmajñāna</s> and in the ground of <s>dharmajñāna</s> — this is called <s>dharmajñāna</s>. What is <s>anvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge)? Whatever uncontaminated knowledge there is regarding conditioned things connected with the Form and Formless Realms. Whatever uncontaminated knowledge there is regarding the cause of conditioned things connected with the Form and Formless Realms. Whatever uncontaminated knowledge there is regarding the cessation of conditioned things connected with the Form and Formless Realms. Whatever uncontaminated knowledge there is regarding the path for the abandonment of conditioned things connected with the Form and Formless Realms. This is called <s>anvayajñāna</s>. Moreover, whatever is uncontaminated in <s>anvayajñāna</s> and in the ground of <s>anvayajñāna</s> — this is called <s>anvayajñāna</s>. 'The knowledge of suffering and origination [is distinguished] by aspects' — by aspects alone, not by object-domain, because of the non-difference between those two, since both have the characteristic of the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>). For thus it is stated in the <s>śāstra</s>: What is <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> (knowledge of suffering)? Whatever uncontaminated knowledge there is when one attends to the five aggregates of clinging as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, and as non-self — this is called <s>duḥkhajñāna</s>. What is <s>samudayajñāna</s> (knowledge of origination)? Whatever uncontaminated knowledge there is when one attends to what is contaminated and has a cause, as cause, as origination, as arising, and as condition — this is called <s>samudayajñāna</s>. 'The knowledge of cessation and the path [is distinguished] by both aspects and object-domain' — the knowledge of cessation and the knowledge of the path are established by both aspects and object-domain. For thus it is stated in the <s>śāstra</s>: What is <s>nirodhajñāna</s> (knowledge of cessation)? Whatever uncontaminated knowledge there is when one attends to cessation as cessation, as peace, as excellence, and as escape — this is called <s>nirodhajñāna</s>. What is <s>mārgajñāna</s> (knowledge of the path)? Whatever uncontaminated knowledge there is when one attends to the path as path, as method, as practice, and as leading out — this is called <s>mārgajñāna</s>. The word 'first' qualifies the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>). For that too arises in the continuum of one who has done what was to be done (<s>kṛtakṛtya</s>). 'Because of being caused by all uncontaminated [dharmas]' — with reference to the ten knowledges that have arisen first, the knowledge of non-arising is caused by all uncontaminated [dharmas] through the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>). But the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) is not caused by all uncontaminated [dharmas], for the knowledge of non-arising is not its cause, since [the knowledge of non-arising] is superior.

body.text: (VII.9) sakalasya sakalapratipakṣatvād iti. sakalasya kāmadhātor darśanabhāvanāprahātavyasaṃgṛhītasya paṃcaprakārasya sakalaṃ dhārmajñānaṃ darśanabhāvanāmārgasaṃgṛhītaṃ caturāryasatyālaṃbanaṃ pratipakṣa iti kṛtvā kāmadhātor eva pratipakṣo dharmajñānam ity uktam. api tv asti saṃbhavo yad rūpārūpyadhātor api dharmajñānaṃ pratipakṣaḥ. katamat tad dharmajñānaṃ. yan nirodhe mārge ca dharmajñānaṃ. nirodhamārgau hy adhātupatitau. tāv adharāv api na hinau vyavasthāpyete. duḥkhasamudayasatve tv
body.translated_text: (VII.9) 'Because of being the antidote of the whole in its entirety' — because the entire <s>dharmajñāna</s>, included in both the seeing and cultivation paths and having the four Noble Truths as its object-domain, is the antidote of the entire Desire Realm included in what is to be abandoned by seeing and cultivation — in its five kinds — therefore it is said that <s>dharmajñāna</s> is the antidote of the Desire Realm alone. However, there is the possibility that <s>dharmajñāna</s> is also the antidote of the Form and Formless Realms. Which <s>dharmajñāna</s> is that? That which is <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding cessation and the path. For cessation and the path do not fall within any realm. Those two, even though lower, are not established as inferior. But regarding the truths of suffering and origination

body.text: adharabhūmike nihīne. na tad ālambanaṃ dharmajñānaṃ rūpārūpyadhātupratipakṣa ity avagaṃtavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: — what pertains to a lower ground is inferior. One should not understand that <s>dharmajñāna</s> having that as its object-domain is the antidote of the Form and Formless Realms.

body.text: grahaṇaṃ tu rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ darśanaheyānām anvayajñānakṣāntivadhyatvāt. anvayajñānaṃ tarhi nirodhamārgālaṃbanabhāvanāmārgasaṃgṛhītaṃ kasmāt tridhātupratipakṣo na bhavati. kāmadhātor jitatvāt. dharmajñānenaiva kāmadhātuḥ [Tib. 282a] pūrvatarajito bhavati. tataḥ paścād anvayam utpadyate. tataḥ kāmadhātor jitatvān na tat kāmadhātupratipakṣa iti. dharmajñānaṃ tu rūpārūpyadhātor ajitatvāt pratipakṣo yujyate. [karmān nirodhamārgadharmajñānābhyām eva traidhātukabhāvanāprahātavyakleśaprahāṇaṃ na pūrvābhyāṃ. śāntanairyāṇikatāsābhāgāt. na hi kāmāvacarasaṃskārāṇāṃ. nirodhāt pratipakṣād vā rūpārūpyāvacarasaṃskārāṇāṃ nirodhasya pratipakṣasya vāsti kaścid viśeṣaḥ. sarvo hi nirodhaḥ kuśalo 'saṃskṛto mārgaś ca nairyāṇikaḥ.] anvayam ity anvetīty anvayaṃ jñānaṃ.
body.translated_text: is because those to be abandoned by seeing in the Form and Formless Realms are destroyed by the <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (inferential knowledge-patience). 'Then why is <s>anvayajñāna</s> — included in the cultivation path and having cessation and the path as its object-domain — not the antidote of all three realms?' Because the Desire Realm has already been conquered. The Desire Realm was already conquered earlier by <s>dharmajñāna</s> alone. After that, the inferential [knowledge] arises. Therefore, because the Desire Realm has been conquered, it is not the antidote of the Desire Realm. But <s>dharmajñāna</s>, because the Form and Formless Realms have not [yet] been conquered, is fittingly an antidote. [Because cessation and the path of the Desire Realm are not different from the cessation and path of the Form and Formless Realms with respect to peacefulness and the character of leading out. For all cessation is wholesome, unconditioned; and the path leads out.] '<s>Anvaya</s>' (inferential) — that which follows after (<s>anveti</s>) is <s>anvaya</s>; [so] knowledge [that follows] is <s>anvayajñāna</s>.

body.text: (VII.10-12ab) sarvatheti. bhāvanāmārgasaṃgṛhītam api. tān purastād iti. tān anityādīn ākārān ūrdhvaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ. ṣoḍaśākāram uṣmagatādiṣu. svasāmānyalakṣaṇādigrahaṇād iti. svalakṣaṇagrahaṇāt sāmānyalakṣaṇagrahaṇāc ca. ādiśabdena bhuṃkṣva tiṣṭha gacchety evam ākāraṃ ca. na hy ete svalakṣaṇākārāḥ. kiṃ tarhi. evamākārā eveti.
body.translated_text: (VII.10-12ab) 'In every way' — included in the cultivation path as well. 'Those, later' — those aspects of impermanence and the rest we shall explain later. The sixteen aspects in the heat stage (<s>uṣmagata</s>) and the rest. 'Because of the grasping of specific and general characteristics, and so forth' — because of the grasping of specific characteristics and the grasping of general characteristics. By the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), [it means] also of the form 'eat, stand, go.' For these are not aspects of specific characteristics. Rather, they are simply of such a form.

body.text: ubhayam api tv iti. sāsravānāsravaṃ. yat tarhīti vistaraḥ. rāgasya ca cittasya ca yugapadgrahaṇam ity abhiprāyaḥ. sūtraṃ punar evaṃ paṭhyate. sarāgaṃ cittaṃ sarāgaṃ cittam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. vigatarāgaṃ cittaṃ vigatarāgaṃ cittam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. yathā sarāgaṃ vigatarāgam. evaṃ sadveṣaṃ vigatadveṣaṃ samohaṃ vigatamohaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ vikṣiptaṃ līnaṃ pragṛhītam uddhatam [Tib. 282b] anuddhatam avyupaśāntaṃ bhāvitam avimuktaṃ vimuktam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti. vastramalāyugapadgrahaṇavad iti. yathā vastramalayor na yugapadgrahaṇaṃ. tadvat. kathaṃ. yathā yadā vastram iti paricchinnākāraṃ vijñānam utpadyate na tadā malaṃ gṛhṇāti. yadā ca malam iti paricchinnākāraṃ vijñānam utpadyate. na tadā vastraṃ gṛhṇāti.
body.translated_text: 'But both' — contaminated and uncontaminated. 'If so, then' — in detail. The intent is: the simultaneous grasping of desire (<s>rāga</s>) and mind (<s>citta</s>). Moreover, the <s>sūtra</s> is read thus: 'One truly knows a mind with desire (<s>sarāga</s>) as a mind with desire. One truly knows a mind free from desire (<s>vigatarāga</s>) as a mind free from desire.' Just as [the sūtra distinguishes] with-desire and free-from-desire, so too: with-hatred (<s>sadveṣa</s>), free-from-hatred (<s>vigatadveṣa</s>); with-delusion (<s>samoha</s>), free-from-delusion (<s>vigatamoha</s>); contracted (<s>saṃkṣipta</s>), distracted (<s>vikṣipta</s>); sunken (<s>līna</s>), uplifted (<s>pragṛhīta</s>); agitated (<s>uddhata</s>), non-agitated (<s>anuddhata</s>); not calmed (<s>avyupaśānta</s>); cultivated (<s>bhāvita</s>); unreleased (<s>avimukta</s>), released (<s>vimukta</s>) — one truly knows as they really are. 'Like the simultaneous grasping of cloth and stain' — just as there is no simultaneous grasping of cloth and stain, similarly. How? Just as when a cognition arises with the determined aspect 'cloth,' at that time it does not grasp the stain; and when a cognition arises with the determined aspect 'stain,' at that time it does not grasp the cloth.

body.text: saṃsṛṣṭasarāgatā saṃyuktasarāgatā ceti. saṃsṛṣṭasarāgatā saṃprayogāt. saṃyuktasarāgatā rāgaprāptyanubaṃdhād ity eke. anuśayānarāgālaṃbanatvād ity apare. dvābhyām iti. saṃsṛṣṭasarāgatayā saṃyuktasarāgatayā ceti. tato
body.translated_text: 'Mixed-with-desire state and conjoined-with-desire state' — the mixed-with-desire state is through association (<s>saṃprayoga</s>). The conjoined-with-desire state is through the connection of the acquisition of desire (<s>rāgaprāptyanubandha</s>) — according to some. Because of having dormant-desire (<s>anuśaya</s>) as its object-domain — according to others. 'Through both' — through the mixed-with-desire state and the conjoined-with-desire state. 'Other than that is contaminated'

body.text: 'nyat sāsravam iti. yat kliṣṭam avyākṛtaṃ kuśalaṃ ca laukikaṃ. tat saṃyogasarāgatayā sarāgaṃ.
body.translated_text: — that is: what is afflicted, indeterminate, and mundanely wholesome — that is with-desire through the conjoined-with-desire state.

body.text: tad evam ubhayam apy etat sarāgam evoktaṃ. āha. kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇam ekīyamatena rāgapratipakṣo vigatarāgam ity ucyate. yatas ta āhuḥ. yadi hi rāgeṇāsaṃprayuktaṃ vigatarāgaṃ syād anyakleśasaṃprayuktam api. dveṣādisaṃprayuktam api. syāt vigatarāgaṃ. [Tib. 283a] tad api hi rāgeṇāsaṃprayuktaṃ saṃprayuktam api. na ca sūtre dveṣādisaṃprayuktaṃ vigatarāgam ity uktaṃ. sadveṣaṃ samoham ityādivacanāt. yeṣāṃ punā rāgapratipakṣo vigatarāgam iti. teṣām ayam adoṣaḥ. na hi rāgapratipakṣo dveṣādibhiḥ saṃprayujyata iti.
body.translated_text: Thus both of these are stated as 'with desire.' He says: 'But what is the reason that, according to the view of some, the antidote of desire is called "free from desire"?' Because those [proponents] say: 'If what is not associated with desire were "free from desire," then even what is associated with other afflictions — associated with hatred and the rest — would be "free from desire." For that too is not associated with desire — yet even what is associated [with other afflictions, would be free from desire]. But in the <s>sūtra</s>, what is associated with hatred and the rest is not called "free from desire" — because of the statements "with hatred," "with delusion," and so forth. For those who hold that the antidote of desire is "free from desire" — for them this is not a fault. For the antidote of desire is not associated with hatred and the rest.'

body.text: evaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. yadi rāgasaṃprayuktaṃ cittaṃ sarāgaṃ rāgapratipakṣo vigatarāgaṃ. tadapratipakṣaḥ sarāgacittasyāpratipakṣaḥ. cittam akliṣṭam anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ. naiva sarāgaṃ rāgeṇāsaṃprayogāt. na viyatarāgaṃ rāgasyāpratipakeṣatvāt. evamādīti. ādiśabdena sadveṣaṃ samoham iti tulyaprasaṃgo yojyaḥ. katham. atra tu sūtre dveṣasaṃprayuktaṃ cittaṃ sadveṣaṃ dveṣapratipakṣo vigatadveṣam iti. yadi hi dveṣeṇāsaṃprayuktaṃ vigatadveṣaṃ syāt. anyakleśasaṃprayuktam iti syād ity eke. evaṃ tarhi tad [Tib. 283b] apratipakṣaś cittam akliṣṭaṃ naiva sadveṣaṃ syāt na vigatadveṣam. ity evaṃ samohaṃ cittaṃ vigatamoham iti vaktavyaṃ. tasmād rāgasaṃyuktatayāpi sarāgaṃ cittam atreṣṭavyaṃ. apiśabdād rāgasaṃprayuktatayāpīty apare. ābhidhārmikāḥ. evaṃ yāvat samohaṃ vigatamohaṃ ceti. tasmād dveṣasaṃyuktatayāpi sadveṣaṃ mohasaṃyuktatayāpi samoham atra sūtre eṣṭavyam iti.
body.translated_text: 'If so, then' — in detail. If a mind associated with desire is 'with desire' and the antidote of desire is 'free from desire,' then the non-antidote — the non-antidote of a mind with desire — a mind that is unafflicted and indeterminate-unobscured — is neither with desire, because of non-association with desire, nor free from desire, because of not being the antidote of desire. 'And so forth' (<s>evamādi</s>) — by the word 'and so forth,' the same consequence should be applied to 'with hatred' and 'with delusion.' How? Here in the <s>sūtra</s>, a mind associated with hatred is 'with hatred,' and the antidote of hatred is 'free from hatred.' If what is not associated with hatred were 'free from hatred,' then what is associated with other afflictions would also be [free from hatred] — say some. 'If so, then the non-antidote — an unafflicted mind — would be neither with hatred nor free from hatred.' Similarly, it should be stated for 'with delusion' and 'free from delusion.' Therefore, a mind 'with desire' should be accepted here [in this sūtra] as also being so through the conjoined-with-desire state. By the word 'also' (<s>api</s>), [it should be accepted] as also through the mixed-with-desire state — say others, the <s>Ābhidhārmika</s>s. Likewise up to 'with delusion' and 'free from delusion.' Therefore, 'with hatred' should also be accepted here in this <s>sūtra</s> through the conjoined-with-hatred state, and 'with delusion' through the conjoined-with-delusion state.

body.text: ālaṃbanābhisaṃkṣepād iti. kuśalaṃ cittaṃ vikṣepeṇa na saṃprayujyate. tasmāt tadālaṃbane tasyābhisaṃkṣepa iti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the contraction of the object-domain' — a wholesome mind is not associated with distraction. Therefore, in its object-domain, there is contraction.

body.text: saṃkṣiptaṃ vikṣiptaṃ ca syāt. kliṣṭamiddhasaṃprayogād iti. dvividhaṃ middhaṃ. kliṣṭam akliṣṭaṃ ca. tad eva hi cittaṃ kliṣṭaṃ middhasaṃprayuktam iti saṃkṣiptaṃ syād iti. kliṣṭam iti ca vikṣiptaṃ syād iti sāṃkaryadoṣaḥ. sāstravirodhaś ceti. kathaṃ. saṃkṣiptaṃ cittaṃ yathābhūtaṃ saṃprajānāti vistareṇa yathā vṛttau. teṣām anvayajñānaṃ tāvat saṃkṣiptacittālaṃbanaṃ na saṃbhavati. kāmadhātor ūrdhvaṃ middhabhāvād anvayajñānasya [Tib. 284a]
body.translated_text: 'It could be both contracted and distracted — because of association with afflicted torpor (<s>middha</s>)' — torpor is of two kinds: afflicted and unafflicted. That very mind that is afflicted and associated with torpor — would be contracted; and because afflicted, it would be distracted — this is the fault of confusion. And there is contradiction with the <s>śāstra</s>. How? 'One truly knows a contracted mind' — in the same way as [explained] in detail in the commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>). Of those, <s>anvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge) cannot have a contracted mind as its object-domain — because above the Desire Realm there is no torpor (<s>middha</s>), and because <s>anvayajñāna</s>

body.text: ca kāmadhātvanālaṃbanatvāt. mārgajñānam api saṃkṣiptacittālaṃbanaṃ na saṃbhavati. mārgajñānaṃ hi mārgālaṃbanaṃ. na ca mārgasaṃgṛhītaṃ cittaṃ middhasaṃprayogīti. tenaivaṃ vaktavyaṃ abhaviṣyat tajjñānaṃ dve [jñāne]. dharmajñānaṃ saṃvṛtijñānaṃ ceti. ye tu varṇayanti saṃkṣiptaṃ cittaṃ kuśam ālaṃbanābhisaṃkṣepād iti. teṣām etad doṣadvayaṃ na bhavati. tad akliṣṭena middhena na saṃprayujyata iti saṃkṣiptaṃ vikṣiptaṃ ca na prāpnoti. nāpi śāstravirodhaḥ. kuśalaṃ traidhātukasaṃgṛhītam asaṃgṛhītaṃ ca saṃkṣiptaṃ cittaṃ tajjñānaṃ catvāri jñānānīti siddhaṃ. rūpārūpyakuśalacittālaṃbanam anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ anvayajñānaṃ bhavati. mārgasaṃgṛhītakuśalālaṃbanaṃ mārgajñānam apīti.
body.translated_text: does not have the Desire Realm as its object-domain. <s>Mārgajñāna</s> (knowledge of the path) also cannot have a contracted mind as its object-domain. For <s>mārgajñāna</s> has the path as its object-domain, and a mind included in the path is not associated with torpor. Therefore, one would have to say that the knowledge [of a contracted mind] consists of two [knowledges]: <s>dharmajñāna</s> and <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> (conventional knowledge). But those who explain 'a contracted mind is wholesome — because of the contraction of the object-domain' — for them this twofold fault does not arise. Because it [a wholesome contracted mind] is not associated with unafflicted torpor — it does not follow that it is both contracted and distracted. Nor is there contradiction with the <s>śāstra</s>. A wholesome mind included in all three realms and not included [in any realm] can be a contracted mind — the knowledge of it is four knowledges — this is established. The uncontaminated knowledge having as its object-domain a wholesome mind of the Form and Formless Realms is <s>anvayajñāna</s>. That having as its object-domain what is wholesome and included in the path is also <s>mārgajñāna</s>.

body.text: vyavadānaparīttair niṣevitatvād iti. alpakuśalamūlair niṣevitatvād ity arthaḥ. tadviparyayād iti. vyavadānamahadbhir niṣevitatvād ity arthaḥ. mūlādīnaṃ balāntānāṃ alpabahutvam ekaikasya mūlasyālpabahutvād yathākramaṃ parīttaṃ ca veditavyaṃ. katham ity āha. kliṣṭaṃ hi [Tib. 284b] dvābhyām akuśalamūlābhyāṃ samūlaṃ mohena lobhadveṣayoś cānyatareṇa. ekasmin kalāpe 'nayor asamavadhānāt. kuśalaṃ tribhir alobhādveṣāmohair eṣām avinābhāvāt. tajjātīyānāgatabhāvanābhāvād iti. kliṣṭajātīyasyānāgatasya bhāvanāyāḥ pratilaṃbhasyābhāvāt kuśalasaṃskṛtā dharmā bhāvayitavyā iti nyāyāt. tribhiś ca skaṃdhaiḥ sānuparivartaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāraskaṃdhaiḥ. na vijñānaskandhena. ekasmin kalāpe dvitīyavijñānābhāvāt. na ca svātmanā svātmani vṛttivirodhāt. kuśalaṃ tu mahāparivāraṃ tajjātīyānāgatabhāvanāsadbhāvāt. caturbhiś ca skaṃdhaiḥ sānuparivartaṃ. taiś ca vedanādibhis tribhiḥ. rūpaskaṃdhena ca dhyānānāsravasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītena cittānuparivartanāsaṃbhavayogataḥ. alpabalaṃ khalv api kliṣṭam iti. nanu ca kuśalam api durbalam ekena mithyādṛṣṭikṣaṇena kuśalapaṃcaskaṃdhasamudghātāt. na tad atyaṃtam ucchidyate punaḥ pratisaṃdhānāt. duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāṃtya tu daśānām anuśayānām atyaṃtasamuccheda iti tasād apīty apiśabdena pūrvoktād apīti. tatpratipakṣatvād iti. auddhatyapratipakṣatvād ity arthaḥ. evam avyupaśāntaṃ vyupaśāntaṃ ceti. avyupaśāṃtaṃ [Tib. 285a] kliṣṭam auddhatyasaṃprayogāt. vyupaśāntaṃ kuśalaṃ tatpratipakṣatvād iti kleśasaṃprayogāsaṃprayogato vā tad avyupaśāntaṃ vyupaśāntaṃ ca bhavati. samāhitaṃ kuśalaṃ tatpratipakṣatvād iti. vikṣepapratipakṣatvāt. pṛatilaṃbhaniṣevaṇabhāvanābhyām iti. alabdhapūrvasya prāptiḥ pratilambhaḥ. saṃmukhībhāvo
body.translated_text: 'Because of being frequented by those whose purification is small' — the meaning is: because of being frequented by those with few wholesome roots. 'Because of the reverse' — the meaning is: because of being frequented by those whose purification is great. The fewness and abundance of roots and the rest up to powers — because of the fewness and abundance of each individual root — should be understood in order as small. How? — he says. For the defiled [Tib. 284b] is rooted in two unwholesome roots — in delusion (<s>moha</s>) together with one of greed (<s>lobha</s>) or aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>). Because these two do not co-occur in one aggregate (<s>kalāpa</s>). The wholesome is rooted in three — non-greed (<s>alobha</s>), non-aversion (<s>adveṣa</s>), and non-delusion (<s>amoha</s>) — because these are inseparable from each other. 'Because of the absence of cultivation of the future of that kind' — because of the absence of the attainment of cultivation of the future of the defiled kind — because of the principle that wholesome conditioned <s>dharma</s>s are to be cultivated. And [the defiled is] with a retinue of three aggregates — the feeling, perception, and formation aggregates. Not with the consciousness aggregate — because of the absence of a second consciousness in one aggregate. Nor with itself — because of the contradiction of functioning upon itself. But the wholesome has a great retinue — because of the actual existence of cultivation of the future of that kind. And with a retinue of four aggregates — those three beginning with feeling, and also the form aggregate included in the <s>dhyāna</s> and uncontaminated restraints (<s>saṃvara</s>) — because of the connection of the impossibility of following consciousness. 'Even though the defiled has little power' — but is not the wholesome also weak — because by one moment of wrong view, the five wholesome aggregates are demolished? It is not ultimately destroyed — because of being reconnected again. But by the <s>duḥkhadharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patience of dharma-knowledge of suffering), there is the ultimate elimination of ten latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>) — therefore, 'even' — by the word 'even,' [it is shown that it is] even beyond what was previously stated. 'Because of being the antidote of that' — the meaning is: because of being the antidote of restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>). 'Thus, unquieted and quieted' — unquieted [Tib. 285a] is the defiled, because of association with restlessness; quieted is the wholesome, because of being the antidote of that — or because of association and non-association with afflictions, it is unquieted and quieted. 'Concentrated is the wholesome, because of being the antidote of that' — because of being the antidote of distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>). 'Through attainment, practice, and cultivation' — attainment (<s>pratilaṃbha</s>) is the obtaining of what was not previously obtained. Coming face-to-face

body.text: niṣevaṇaṃ. te eva bhāvane. tābhyām abhāvitatvāt abhāvitaṃ. na hi kliṣṭaṃ kuśalavad anāgataṃ bhāvyate. na ca niṣevaṇārhaṃ bhavati nihīnatvāt.
body.translated_text: is practice (<s>niṣevaṇa</s>). Those two themselves are the cultivations (<s>bhāvanā</s>). Through those two — uncultivated because of not having been cultivated by those two. For the defiled is not cultivated like the wholesome with respect to the future. Nor is it worthy of practice, because of its inferiority.

children.translated_text: 'The cultivations called attainment and practice, of the wholesome and conditioned' —

body.text: iti. tābhyām iti pratilambhaniṣevaṇābhyām ity arthaḥ. svabhāvasaṃtānavimuktibhyām avimuktatvād iti. kleśaiḥ saṃprayogān na svabhāvavimuktyā vimuktaṃ. kṣīṇakleśasaṃtānānutpatteś ca na saṃtānavimuktyā ca vimuktaṃ. kuśalaṃ tu kleśāsaṃprayogāt. kṣīṇakleśasaṃtānotpatteś ca vimuktaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Through those two' means: through attainment and practice. 'Because of non-liberation through own-nature liberation and series-liberation' — because of association with afflictions, it is not liberated through own-nature liberation. And because of the non-arising of a series in which afflictions are destroyed, it is not liberated through series-liberation either. But the wholesome, because of non-association with afflictions and because of the arising of a series in which afflictions are destroyed, is liberated.

body.text: styānamiddhasahagatam iti. styānamiddhasaṃprayuktaṃ adhyātmaṃ saṃnirodhasahagatam iti. etad eva nigamayati na tu vipaśyanayā samanvāgatam iti. anuvikṣiptam ity asya nirdeśaṃ karoty anuvisṛtam iti.
body.translated_text: 'Accompanied by sloth-torpor (<s>styānamiddha</s>)' — associated with sloth-torpor. 'Accompanied by internal cessation' — this very [point] he concludes: 'but not endowed with insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>).' He glosses 'scattered' (<s>anuvikṣipta</s>): 'dissipated' (<s>anuvisṛta</s>).

body.text: middhasahagatasya kliṣṭasya vikṣiptatvāpratijñānād [Tib. 285b] iti. kim iti kṛtvā vikṣiptatvam atra na pratijñāyate. kiṃ middhasahagate kliṣṭe citte vikṣiptatvaṃ nāstīti na pratijñāyate. āhosvid vidyamānam apy atra vikṣiptatvam. saṃkṣiptatvenaiva sthāpitatvān na pratijñāyate. ubhayathāpi vyācakṣate. kecid vyācakṣate. middhasahagatād dhi kliṣṭād yad anyat kliṣṭaṃ. tad vikṣiptaṃ pratijñāyate. middhasahagataṃ tu kliṣṭam akliṣṭaṃ cāviśeṣeṇa saṃkṣiptam eveti. apare punar vyācakṣate. yan middhasaṃprayuktaṃ. tat saṃkṣiptam eva na vikṣiptaṃ. yat tu viṣayeṣu visṛtaṃ. tad eva vikṣiptam ity ato 'tra middhasaṃprayukte citte. na pratijñāyata iti. varaṃ śāstravirodha iti. abuddhoktam abhidharmaśāstram ity abhiprāyaḥ. abhinnalakṣaṇavacanād iti. sarvāṇi tāni kliṣṭāny uktānīti. kliṣṭatvalakṣaṇam eṣāṃ vikṣiptādīnām avimuktāntānām. kliṣṭatvaṃ punaḥ kleśamahābhūmikaiḥ saṃprayogaḥ. saṃkṣiptapragṛhītādīnāṃ cābhinnalakṣaṇavacanān nārthaviśeṣa ukto bhavatīti saṃbandhaḥ. ādiśabdena mahadgatānuddhatavyupaśāntasamāhitabhāvitavimuktānāṃ [Tib. 286a] grahaṇaṃ. kuśalam eṣām abhinnaṃ. kiṃ punaḥ kuśalatvaṃ. kuśalaṃ mahābhūmikaiḥ saṃprayogaḥ. na vai nokta iti vistaraḥ. vai iti nipātaḥ. na nokta iti dvau pratiṣedhau ukta evety arthaḥ. ka uktaḥ. padānām arthaviśeṣaḥ. ity āha. kliṣṭasāmānye 'pi vikṣiptādīnāṃ tulye kliṣṭatve teṣāṃ doṣāviśeṣasaṃdarśanād ity apy etat kliṣṭaṃ cittaṃ vikṣepayogād vikṣiptaṃ kliṣṭaṃ. kausīdyayogāl līnam auddhatyayogād uddhatam ity evamādidoṣe viśeṣasaṃdarśanād ukta evārthaviśeṣo bhavati. evaṃ kuśalasyāpi saṃkṣiptāder
body.translated_text: 'Because the defiled accompanied by torpor (<s>middha</s>) is not declared to be distracted' — [Tib. 285b] — for what reason is distraction not declared here? Is there no distraction in defiled mind accompanied by torpor, and therefore it is not declared? Or does distraction actually exist there, but because it is subsumed under 'contracted' (<s>saṃkṣipta</s>), it is not declared? Both interpretations are given. Some explain: whatever defiled [mind] is other than that accompanied by torpor — that is declared to be distracted. But defiled mind accompanied by torpor, and non-defiled [mind accompanied by torpor], are without distinction both just 'contracted.' Others, however, explain: whatever is associated with torpor — that is just contracted, not distracted. But whatever is dissipated toward objects — that alone is distracted — therefore, here regarding mind associated with torpor, it is not declared [as distracted]. 'Better [to accept] the contradiction with the treatise' — the intent is: the <s>Abhidharma</s> treatise was not spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>. 'Because of the statement of undifferentiated characteristics' — all those are stated as defiled. The characteristic of these — distracted and the rest up to unliberated — is defiledness. And defiledness is association with the affliction-<s>mahābhūmika</s>s. And because of the statement of undifferentiated characteristics of contracted, held-up, and the rest — no distinction of meaning is stated — this is the connection. By the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), [Tib. 286a] the apprehension of great, unarisen, quieted, concentrated, cultivated, and liberated [is included]. Wholesome is their undifferentiated [characteristic]. And what is wholesomeness? Association with the wholesome <s>mahābhūmika</s>s. 'It has indeed been stated' — and so forth in detail. The particle <s>vai</s> — 'not not-stated' — the two negations mean 'stated indeed.' What was stated? The distinction of meaning of the terms. Thus he says: 'Even though there is commonality in defiledness among distracted and the rest — since their defiledness is equal — because of showing the distinction of faults' — and this too: 'the defiled mind is distracted because of the connection with distraction; defiled because of the connection with laziness, it is sluggish; because of the connection with restlessness, it is agitated' — thus, because of showing the distinction of faults, a distinction of meaning is indeed stated. Similarly, for the wholesome too — contracted, held-up, and the rest

body.text:
guṇaviśeṣasaṃdarśanād ity apy etat kuśalaṃ cittaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ pragṛhītam iti vistareṇokta evārthaviśeṣo bhavati. sūtravirodhasyāparihārād iti. sūtre hi styānamiddhasahagataṃ saṃkṣiptam uktaṃ. styānayogena yat kliṣṭaṃ middhasaṃprayuktaṃ. tat saṃkṣiptaṃ na kuśalaṃ. styānasya kleśamahābhūmikatvāt. yadi ca sūtre iti vistaraḥ. yadi [Tib. 286b] yuṣmannītyā sūtre līnam evoddhataṃ bhagavatābhipretaṃ syāt. līnoddhatayoḥ pṛthagvacanaṃ noktaṃ syāt. katham ity āha. yasmin samaye cittaṃ līnaṃ kausīdyasaṃprayuktaṃ. līnābhiśaṃki līnam etad bhaviṣyatīty abhiśaṃkato līnābhiāśaṃki. akālas tasmin samaye praśrabdhisamādhyupekṣāsaṃbodhyaṃgānāṃ bhāvanāyā ity eṣa niyamo na syāt. evaṃ ca vaktavyaṃ syāt. akālas tasmin samaye dharmavicayavīryaprītisaṃbodhyaṃgānāṃ bhāvanāyā apīti. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. tad eva līnaṃ cittam uddhatam iti kṛtvā. tathā yasmin samaye uddhataṃ cittaṃ bhavaty auddhatyābhiśaṃki. akālas tasmin samaye dharmavicayavīryaprītisaṃbodhyaṃgānāṃ bhāvanāyā ity eṣa niyamo na syāt. evaṃ ca vaktavyaṃ syāt. akālas tasmin samaye praśrabdhisamādhyupekṣāsaṃbodhyaṃgānāṃ bhāvanāyā apīti. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. tad evoddhataṃ cittaṃ līnam iti kṛtvā. avibhāgena vā vaktavyaṃ syāt. yasmin samaye cittaṃ līnaṃ bhavati līnābhiśaṃki uddhataṃ vā bhavaty auddhatyābhiśaṃki. akālas tasmin samaye praśrabdhisamādhyupekṣādharmavicayavīryaprītisaṃbodhyaṃgānāṃ bhāvanāyā iti. smṛtisaṃbodhyaṃgasyāgrahaṇaṃ sarvatragatvāt smṛteḥ. ubhaye 'pi citte 'nukta siddhitaḥ. [Tib. 287a] smṛtiṃ khalv ahaṃ sarvatragatāṃ vadāmīti sūtre vacanāt. kathaṃ punar vaibhāṣikeṇa yad eva līnaṃ. tad evoddhatam ity abhīṣṭaṃ gamyate. līnaṃ cittaṃ kliṣṭaṃ kausīdyasaṃprayogāt. uddhataṃ cittaṃ kliṣṭam auddhatyasaṃprayogād iti vacanāt. kiṃ punar atra bodhyaṃgānāṃ vyagrā bhāvaneti. kiṃ kadācit praśrabdhyādibhāvanaiva na dharmapravicayādibhāvanā. kadācid dharmavicayādibhāvanaiva
na praśrabdhyādibhāvaneti vyagrā bhāvanā. manasikaraṇaṃ teṣāṃ bhāvaneṣṭā. na saṃmukhībhāva iti. manasikaraṇam ālaṃbanīkaraṇaṃ. līne citte akālaḥ praśrabdhyādīnām ālaṃbanīkaraṇasyābhogakaraṇasyety arthaḥ. uddhate ca citte akālo dharmavicayādīnām iti. na tu saṃmukhībhāvo bhāvaneṣṭā. tasmin kāle na praśrabhdyādayaḥ saṃmukhīkartavyāḥ. dharmavicayādayas tu saṃmukhīkartavyāḥ. dharmavicayādayo vā na saṃmukhīkartavāḥ. praśrabdhyādayas tu kartavyā
body.translated_text: — because of showing the distinction of qualities — and this too: 'the wholesome mind is contracted, held-up' — and so forth in detail — a distinction of meaning is indeed stated. 'Because of the non-resolution of the contradiction with the <s>sūtra</s>' — for in the <s>sūtra</s>, what is accompanied by sloth-torpor (<s>styānamiddha</s>) is stated as contracted. What is defiled through the connection with sloth (<s>styāna</s>) and associated with torpor (<s>middha</s>) — that is contracted, not wholesome. Because sloth is a <s>kleśamahābhūmika</s> (affliction-<s>mahābhūmika</s>). 'If, moreover, according to your view' — and so forth in detail. If, [Tib. 286b] according to your view, in the <s>sūtra</s>, what is sluggish (<s>līna</s>) alone were intended by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as restless (<s>uddhata</s>), then the separate statement of sluggish and restless would not have been made. How? — he says. 'At whatever time the mind is sluggish, associated with laziness' — one who suspects sluggishness, suspecting 'this will become sluggish' — that is not the time for the cultivation of the awakening factors of tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) — this restriction would not hold. And it would have to be stated thus: 'it is not the time for the cultivation of the awakening factors of dharma-investigation, energy, and joy either.' For what reason? Because that very sluggish mind is restless — thus considering. Similarly, 'at whatever time the mind is restless, one who suspects restlessness — it is not the time for the cultivation of the awakening factors of dharma-investigation, energy, and joy' — this restriction would not hold. And it would have to be stated thus: 'it is not the time for the cultivation of the awakening factors of tranquility, concentration, and equanimity either.' For what reason? Because that very restless mind is sluggish — thus considering. Or it would have to be stated without distinction: 'at whatever time the mind is sluggish, one who suspects sluggishness, or the mind is restless, one who suspects restlessness — it is not the time for the cultivation of the awakening factors of tranquility, concentration, equanimity, dharma-investigation, energy, and joy.' The mindfulness awakening factor is not mentioned because mindfulness pervades all [states]. And in both minds, because it is established without being stated. [Tib. 287a] Because of the <s>sūtra</s> statement: 'Mindfulness, I say, is one that pervades all.' 'But how is it understood by the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> that what is sluggish is also restless?' Because of the statement: 'sluggish mind is defiled because of the connection with laziness; restless mind is defiled because of the connection with restlessness.' 'What, then, is the proper cultivation of the awakening factors?' — whether sometimes the cultivation is only of tranquility and the rest, not of dharma-investigation and the rest; or sometimes the cultivation is only of dharma-investigation and the rest, not of tranquility and the rest — that is the proper cultivation. 'Attending to them is what is intended as cultivation — not bringing face-to-face.' Attending (<s>manasikāra</s>) is making into an object. When the mind is sluggish, it is not the time for making tranquility and the rest into objects, for directing attention [to them] — this is the meaning. And when the mind is restless, it is not the time for dharma-investigation and the rest. But it is not bringing face-to-face that is intended as cultivation. At that time, tranquility and the rest should not be brought face-to-face, but dharma-investigation and the rest should be brought face-to-face.
