Or dharma-investigation and the rest should not be brought face-to-face, but tranquility and the rest should be brought face-to-face

body.text: iti. kausīdyādhikam atreti vistaraḥ. yatra kausīdyam [Tib. 287b] adhikam auddhatyaṃ tu nyagbhāvena vartate. tal līnaṃ. yatra cauddhatyam adhikaṃ kausīdyaṃ tu nyagbhāvena. tad uddhatam. ity anayor viśeṣād avirodhaḥ sūtrasya pṛthagvacane. tayos tu sahabhāvād ekasmin kalāpe yugapad bhāvāt tad eva līnaṃ tad evoddhatam iti brūma iti. līnaṃ kliṣṭaṃ kausīdyasaṃyogāt. uddhataṃ kliṣṭam auddhatyasaṃyogād iti. ācārya āha. ābhiprāyikaṃ yāvat sūtre tu nāyam abhiprāya iti. kausīdyādhikaṃ līnam auddhatyādhikam uddhatam iti. yasmād āha. yasmin samaye līnaṃ cittaṃ bhavati vistareṇa na tv evaṃ viśinaṣṭi kausīdyādhikam anddhatyādhikam iti vā.
body.translated_text: — thus. 'Where laziness predominates' — and so forth in detail. Where laziness [Tib. 287b] predominates and restlessness exists in a subordinate manner — that is sluggish. And where restlessness predominates and laziness exists in a subordinate manner — that is restless. Thus, because of their distinction, there is no contradiction with the separate statement in the <s>sūtra</s>. But because of their co-existence — because of their simultaneous existence in one aggregate — we say: 'that very one which is sluggish is also restless.' 'Sluggish is defiled because of the connection with laziness; restless is defiled because of the connection with restlessness.' The <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'This is [stated] with a [particular] intent' — up to: 'but in the <s>sūtra</s>, this is not the intent.' That what has predominant laziness is sluggish, and what has predominant restlessness is restless — [the Buddha does not say this]. Because he says: 'at whatever time the mind is sluggish' — and so forth in detail — but he does not make the distinction 'having predominant laziness' or 'having predominant restlessness.'

body.text: yat tūktaṃ sarvam eva rāgasaṃyuktaṃ cittaṃ sarāgam iti. katham uktaṃ. tatra rāgasaṃprayuktaṃ cittaṃ dvābhyāṃ sarāgaṃ. tato 'nyat sāsravaṃ saṃyogasarāgam iti vacanāt. tatra rāgasaṃyuktatayāpi sarāgaṃ cittam atreṣṭavyam iti vacanāt. anāsravam api sarāgaṃ prāpnoti śaikṣam iti. śaikṣasaṃtāne rāgasya sāvaśeṣatvāt. [Tib. 288a] rāgālaṃbanaṃ cet. atha mataṃ rāgasya yad ālaṃbanaṃ. tad rāgasaṃyuktaṃ sarāgaṃ ca bhavati. arhato 'pi sāsravaṃ cittaṃ parakīyasya rāgasyālaṃbanatvāt rāgasaṃyuktam iti kṛtvā sarāgam iti gṛhṇīyāt paracittavit paracittajñānaṃ vā. atha mataṃ na tad rāgeṇālaṃbyata iti. tata ucyate. kathaṃ vā tat sāsravam iti. sāmānyakleśālaṃbanatvād iti cet. atha mataṃ sāmānyakleśānāṃ dṛṣṭivicikitsāvidyānām ālaṃbaṇaṃ tad ataḥ sāsravam iti. evam api samohaṃ grḥṇīyāt. arhataḥ sāsravaṃ cittaṃ mohālaṃbanatvāt. moho 'pi sāmānyakleśaḥ. parakīyasya ca mohasyārhaccittam ālaṃbanībhavatīti. na ca paracittajñānaṃ prāptyālaṃbanam iti. yasmāt paracittajñānaṃ cittacaittālaṃbanam iṣyate. tasmān na rāgapraptisahitatvena rāgasaṃyuktatvāt sarāgam iti. nāpi taccitālaṃbanarāgālaṃbanam iti. tad iti yat tat parakīyaṃ cittaṃ paracittajñānena [Tib. 288b] gṛhyate. tat tacchabdenocyate. [tasyālaṃbanaḥ]. taccittālaṃbanas taccittālaṃbano rāgaḥ. ālaṃabanam asya paracittajñānasyeti tad bhavati taccittālaṃbanarāgālaṃbanaṃ. yasmād evaṃvidhaṃ rāgaṃ nālaṃbate paracittajñānaṃ viprakṛṣṭatvāt. ekaikadravyagocaraṃ hi paracittajñānaṃ. na ca parakīyacittajñānaṃ tasya cittasyālaṃbanaṃ gṛhṇāti. ākārālaṃbananirapekṣaṃ hi tad iti vacanāt. raktam idaṃ eittaṃ jānātīti vacanāc ca. tasmād api na rāgasaṃyogāt sarāgaṃ cittam iti. asaṃprayuktaṃ vigatarāgam iti. satyām api rāgaprāptāv ity abhiprāyaḥ. tatra tat saṃdhāyoktam iti rāgādiprāptivigamaṃ. saṃdhāyoktaṃ
body.translated_text: But what was stated — 'all mind conjoined with desire is "with-desire" (<s>sarāga</s>)' — how is this stated? Therein, 'a mind associated (<s>saṃprayukta</s>) with desire is "with-desire" in two ways. Other than that, contaminated [mind] is "with-desire" through conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>)' — from this statement. And from the statement: 'therein, mind should be accepted as "with-desire" also through being conjoined with desire.' But then even uncontaminated [mind] would be "with-desire" — the learner's [mind] — because desire has a remainder in the learner's continuum. If [you say it is because] it has desire as its object — if you hold that whatever is the object of desire, that is conjoined with desire and is "with-desire" — then even the contaminated mind of an <s>arhat</s>, being an object of another's desire, would be grasped as conjoined with desire and therefore as "with-desire" — by the knower of others' minds or by the knowledge of others' minds. If you hold that it is not taken as object by desire — then it is said: how is it contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>)? If [you say] because of being an object of universal afflictions (<s>sāmānyakleśa</s>) — if you hold that it is an object of the universal afflictions — views, doubt, and ignorance — and therefore is contaminated — then one should also grasp it as 'with delusion' (<s>samoha</s>). Because the contaminated mind of an <s>arhat</s> is an object of delusion. Delusion too is a universal affliction. And the mind of an <s>arhat</s> becomes an object of another's delusion. And the knowledge of others' minds does not take acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>) as its object — because the knowledge of others' minds is accepted as having mind and mental factors as its object. Therefore, it is not 'with-desire' because of being conjoined with desire through being accompanied by the acquisition of desire. Nor is it the object of desire that takes that mind as its object — the word 'that' refers to the other's mind that is apprehended by the knowledge of others' minds. The desire that takes that mind as its object — the object of that desire-taking-that-mind-as-object becomes the object of this knowledge of others' minds — this too is not the case. Because the knowledge of others' minds does not take as its object such desire, due to remoteness. For the knowledge of others' minds has a single substance as its scope. And the knowledge of another's mind does not apprehend the object of that mind — because of the statement that it is independent of aspect and object. And because of the statement: 'It knows this mind as desirous (<s>rakta</s>).' Therefore, from that too, mind is not 'with-desire' through conjunction with desire. '[Mind] not associated [with desire] is "free from desire" (<s>vigatarāga</s>)' — the intent is: even though the acquisition of desire exists. 'That was said with this intention' — he shows that it was said with reference to the departure of the acquisition of desire and the rest

body.text: na saṃprayogam iti darśayaty anāvartikadharmi kāmabhave rūpabhave ārūpyabhave iti. traidhātukavairāgyasaṃdarśanād ity abhiprāyaḥ. nanu coktam iti vistaraḥ. kvoktam. atra tu sūtra iti vistareṇa yāvad yadi hi rāgeṇāsaṃprayuktaṃ cittaṃ vigatarāgaṃ syād anyakleśasaṃprayuktam [Tib. 289a] api vigatarāgaṃ syād ity atra. etenābhisaṃdhinā rāyaviprayuktatvād vigatarāgam anyakleśasaṃprayuktam apīty anena. yady evaṃ sadveṣaṃ samoham ity evamādi. na vaktavyaṃ syād ity ata āha. na tu tad vigatarāgam ityādi. na tu tad dveṣādisaṃprayuktaṃ cittaṃ vigatarāgam api sad vigatarāgam iti kṛtvā gṛhyate. kiṃ tarhi. sadveṣaṃ samoham ity evamādi dveṣādisaṃprayogitayā viśiṣṭatvāt. ādiśabdena cātra saṃkṣiptaṃ vikṣiptam ity evamādisūtroktāni padāni gṛhyante.
body.translated_text: — not with reference to association — [by citing]: 'of irreversible nature (<s>anāvartikadharman</s>), in the Desire Realm, in the Form Realm, in the Formless Realm.' The intent is: because it shows dispassion from all three realms. 'But was it not stated' — and so forth in detail. Where was it stated? 'In this <s>sūtra</s>' — and so forth in detail, up to: 'if mind not associated with desire were "free from desire," then [mind] associated with another affliction would also be "free from desire"' — at this point. With this intention — 'because of being dissociated from desire, it is "free from desire" even though associated with another affliction' — by this. If so, then 'with aversion' (<s>sadveṣa</s>), 'with delusion' (<s>samoha</s>), and so forth — one should not have to say [these separately]. Therefore he says: 'But that [mind] associated with aversion and the rest, even though free from desire, is not grasped as "free from desire." Rather, [it is grasped as] "with aversion," "with delusion," and so forth — because of being specifically qualified by association with aversion and the rest.' By the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), the terms stated in the <s>sūtra</s> such as 'contracted' (<s>saṃkṣipta</s>), 'distracted' (<s>vikṣipta</s>), and so forth are grasped.

body.text: anyathā hīti vistaraḥ. yady asmin vastuni rūpādike raktam iti vijānīyāt tad rūpālaṃbanam api syāt. tathā ca sati na tat paracittajñānaṃ syād rūpālaṃbanatvāt. tadālaṃbanaṃ ca paracittaṃ gṛhṇataḥ svabhāvagrahaṇaṃ prāpnuyād iti. sālaṃbanaparacittagrahaṇe hīṣyamāṇe svātmā paracittajñānena gṛhyeta. asti hi saṃbhavo yat paracittavid yasya cittaṃ gṛhṇāti. asāv api tasya paracittavidaś cittam ālaṃbeta. tataś ca paracittajñānasya svālaṃbanaparijñānāt [Tib. 289b] svam evāsau paracittavic cittam ālambeta. na caitat prāpyaṃ. yat tenaiva cittena tad eva gṛhyate. sarvaṃ ceti vistaraḥ. dravyasya svalakṣaṇaṃ ca cittacaittāś ca pratyutpannāś ca parasaṃtatiś ca kāmarūpapratisaṃyuktāś cāpratisaṃyuktāś ca viṣayo 'syeti samāsavigrahaḥ. dravyagrahaṇaṃ saṃvṛtisannirāsārthaṃ. svalakṣaṇagrahaṇaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇanivṛttyarthaṃ. cittacaittagrahaṇaṃ rūpādiviśeṣaṇārthaṃ. pratyutpannagrahaṇam atītānāgatavivecanārthaṃ. parasaṃtatigrahaṇaṃ svasaṃtativyudāsārthaṃ. kāmarūpapratisaṃyuktāpratisaṃyuktagrahaṇaṃ ārūpyapratisaṃyuktapratiṣedhārthaṃ. darśanamārgapratiṣiddham iti. darśanamārge vartamānaḥ paracittajñānaṃ na saṃmukhīkarotīty ato darśananārgasaṃgṛhītaṃ nāsti. na hi darśanamārgo vyavacchinnacittacaittālaṃbano bhavati. bhāvanāmārga upalabhyate. bhāvanāmārgasaṃgṛhītaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ. śūnyatānimittaviprayuktam iit. śūnyatāsamādhinā ānimittasamādhinā ca viprayuktaṃ. śūnyatāsamādhir duḥkhajñānasaṃyuktaḥ. ānimittasamādhir nirodhajñānasaṃprayuktaḥ. na ca paracittajñānaṃ. [Tib. 290a] duḥkhajñānaṃ duḥkhanirodhajñānaṃ vā bhavaty ākārālambanabhedāt. atas tābhyāṃ viprayuktam ucyate. arthād uktaṃ bhavaty apraṇihitasamādhisaṃprayuktaṃ
body.translated_text: 'Otherwise' — and so forth in detail. If it knew 'desirous regarding this entity — form and the rest' — then that [knowledge] would also have form as its object. And that being so, it would not be the knowledge of others' minds, because of having form as its object. And apprehension of the own-nature of the object should follow when grasping another's mind together with its object. For if the apprehension of another's mind together with its object is accepted, one would apprehend one's own self through the knowledge of others' minds. For it is possible that the one who knows others' minds apprehends the mind of someone [else], and that person too takes as object the mind of the knower of others' minds. Then, because of the knowledge of others' minds comprehending its own object, that very knower of others' minds would take his own mind as object. And this should not follow — that by that very mind, that very [mind] is apprehended. 'All' — and so forth in detail. [The knowledge of others' minds has as its scope:] substance and particular characteristics; mind and mental factors; present [only]; another's continuum; [that which is] connected and unconnected with the Desire and Form [Realms]. The mention of 'substance' is for the purpose of excluding conventional [reality]. The mention of 'particular characteristics' is for the purpose of excluding general characteristics. The mention of 'mind and mental factors' is for the purpose of specifying [them] as distinct from form and the rest. The mention of 'present' is for the purpose of distinguishing from past and future. The mention of 'another's continuum' is for the purpose of excluding one's own continuum. The mention of 'connected and unconnected with the Desire and Form [Realms]' is for the purpose of excluding what is connected with the Formless [Realm]. 'Excluded from the seeing path' — one who is in the seeing path does not bring the knowledge of others' minds face to face — therefore [knowledge] included in the seeing path does not exist. For the seeing path does not have mind and mental factors as its uninterrupted object. [But] it is found in the cultivation path — the meaning is: [knowledge] included in the cultivation path exists. 'Dissociated from emptiness and signlessness' — dissociated from the emptiness <s>samādhi</s> and the signless <s>samādhi</s>. The emptiness <s>samādhi</s> is associated with the knowledge of suffering (<s>duḥkhajñāna</s>). The signless <s>samādhi</s> is associated with the knowledge of cessation (<s>nirodhajñāna</s>). And the knowledge of others' minds is neither the knowledge of suffering nor the knowledge of cessation of suffering — because of the difference in aspect and object. Therefore it is said to be dissociated from those two. It is implicitly stated that it can be associated with the wishless <s>samādhi</s> (<s>apraṇihitasamādhi</s>)

body.text: saṃbhavatīti. kṣayānutpādajñānasaṃgṛhītam iti. kṣayajñānenānutpādajñānena na saṃgṛhītaṃ. na kṣayānutpādajñānasvabhāvam ity arthaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. dravyasvalakṣaṇasaṃtīraṇaparimārgaṇāśayaṃ paracittajñānaṃ. na caiva kṣayajñānam anutpādajñānaṃ ceti tābhyām asaṃgṛhītaṃ. ānantaryamārgaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ ceti. sa hi prahāṇamārgo bhavati. paracittajñānaṃ ca vimuktiviśeṣamārga iti. pāramārthikayor api saṃvṛtibhajanād iti. paramārthanimitte paramārthena vā dīvyataḥ pāramārthike. tayoḥ saṃvṛtibhajanāt. yasmād ete saṃvṛtiṃ bhajete. ataḥ śūnyānātmākārau na staḥ. kathaṃ punar ete saṃvṛtiṃ bhajete. kṣīṇā me jātiḥ. nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānātīti yathākramaṃ. katham ete anāsrave satī evamākāre. tadbalenānvvyavahārataḥ. anyena jñāneneti vākyaśeṣaḥ. yasmāt tatpṛṣṭhanirjāte saṃvṛtijñāne evamākāre pravartete. atas tanniṣyandena tayoḥ saṃvṛtibhajanam ity ucyate. na tu mukhyavṛttyā tayoḥ saṃvṛtibhajanam [Tib. 290b] ity abhiprāyaḥ. yataś caiva niṣyandenātmadṛṣṭiṃ bhajamāne iva te pravartete. atra tasmāc chūnyānātmākāravivarjitaiś caturdaśabhir evākāraiḥ saṃprayukte iti.
body.translated_text: — being possible. 'Included in the knowledge of destruction and non-arising (<s>kṣayānutpādajñāna</s>)' — not included in the knowledge of destruction or the knowledge of non-arising. The meaning is: it does not have the own-nature of the knowledge of destruction or non-arising. For what reason? The knowledge of others' minds has the disposition of investigating the substance and particular characteristics — the meaning is: of seeking [them]. And neither the knowledge of destruction nor the knowledge of non-arising is so — therefore it is not included in those two. 'And the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) is excluded' — for that is the path of abandonment. And the knowledge of others' minds is the path of liberation or the distinctive path (<s>viśeṣamārga</s>). 'Even of the two ultimate ones, because of partaking of convention' — the ultimately signless (<s>paramārthanimitta</s>) — or one that shines (<s>dīvyati</s>) ultimately — is the ultimately [real]. Of those two, because of partaking of convention — since they partake of convention — therefore the aspects of emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>) and non-self (<s>anātman</s>) do not exist [for them]. But how do they partake of convention? 'My births are exhausted' and 'I know there is no further existence' — respectively. How are they of such aspects while being uncontaminated? Through the force of that — through subsequent conventional knowledge (<s>anvavyavahāra</s>). 'By another knowledge' — this is the completion of the sentence. Because in the conventional knowledge arisen subsequent to that (<s>tatpṛṣṭhanirjāta</s>), such aspects operate. Therefore, through the outflow of that, the partaking of convention of those two is spoken of. The intent is: it is not through the primary usage that those two partake of convention. And since through that outflow they operate as if partaking of the view of self — therefore, here, 'they are associated with only fourteen aspects, excluding the aspects of emptiness and non-self.'

body.text: (VII.12) apratisaṃyuktenety anāsraveṇa. anityam ity anityataḥ. ayaṃ hi tasipratyayaḥ svārthe prayuktaḥ. evaṃ sarvatrāyaṃ pratyayo jñātavyaḥ. atha vāntareṇāpi bhāvapratyayaṃ bhāvapradhāno nirdeśo bhavati. anityena rūpeṇa bhāvo 'nityata iti. evam anyatrāpi yojyaṃ. asty etat sthānam asty etad vastv iti. etāv api dvāv ākārāv anāsravau. asty etat sthānam ity asty etal lakṣaṇam ity arthaḥ. asty etad vastv ity ayaṃ hetur ity arthaḥ. yogavihitato vijānīyād iti. aviparītato vijānīyād ity arthaḥ. nāsyāyam artha iti vistaraḥ. asyeti vākyasya padadvayasya vā. asty etat sthānam asty etad vastv ity asty ayaṃ saṃbhavo 'sty ayaṃ yogo yad anityādito vijānīyād iti mataṃ cet. na. naitad asti. anyatrāvacanāt. anyatra vākye padadvayasyāvacanāt. darśanaprahātavyeneti. darśanaprakāreṇa. ātmata ātmīyataś ceti. satkāyadṛṣṭyā saṃprayuktena cittena. ucchedataḥ śāśvata iti. antagrāhadṛṣṭyā. ahetuto 'kriyāto 'pavādata iti mithyādṛṣṭyā. agrataḥ śreṣṭhato viśiṣṭataḥ paramata iti dṛṣṭiparāmarśena. śuddhito muktito nairyāṇikata iti śīlavrataparāmarśena. [Tib. 291a] kāṃkṣāto vimatito vicikitsāta iti vicikitsāta. rajyeteti rāgeṇa. dviṣyād iti dveṣeṇa. manyeteti mānena. muhyed iti mohena. ayogavihitatā vijānīyād iti. evam ātmādibhir viparītatā vijānīyād iti nigamayati. atrāpi vākye eṣa
body.translated_text: (VII.12) 'With the unconnected' — meaning with the uncontaminated. 'Impermanent' means 'as impermanent.' For this suffix <s>-tas</s> is used in the sense of the word itself. This suffix should be known thus everywhere. Alternatively, even without the suffix expressing state (<s>bhāvapratyaya</s>), a statement predominated by state [is possible]: 'the state of being impermanent — impermanence.' Similarly, it should be applied elsewhere. 'There is this occasion, there is this entity' — these two aspects too are uncontaminated. 'There is this occasion' — the meaning is: there is this characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). 'There is this entity' — the meaning is: this is the cause (<s>hetu</s>). 'One should know through yogic investigation (<s>yogavihita</s>)' — the meaning is: one should know correctly, without error. 'This is not the meaning of that' — and so forth in detail. Of this sentence, or of these two words. 'There is this occasion, there is this entity' — [meaning:] there is this possibility, there is this connection, that one should know as impermanent and the rest — if this is the view — no, this is not so. Because of its not being stated elsewhere — because of the non-statement of those two words in other sentences. 'By what is to be abandoned by seeing' — in the manner of seeing. 'As self, as belonging to self' — by the mind associated with the view of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). 'As annihilation, as permanence' — by the extreme view (<s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s>). 'As without a cause, as without action, as denigratory' — by wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>). 'As foremost, as best, as distinguished, as supreme' — by the clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>). 'As purifying, as liberating, as leading out' — by the clinging to moralities and observances (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>). 'With doubt, with uncertainty, with hesitation' — by doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>). 'One would be attracted' — by desire (<s>rāga</s>). 'One would hate' — by aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>). 'One would be conceited' — by pride (<s>māna</s>). 'One would be deluded' — by delusion (<s>moha</s>). 'One should know through non-yogic [investigation]' — he concludes thus: 'one should know erroneously through self and the rest.' 'In that sentence too, this

body.text: pāṭho 'bhaviṣyad iti. na caivam. ato gamyate nāyam asyārtha iti.
body.translated_text: reading would have been [expected]' — but it is not so. Therefore it is understood that 'this is not the meaning of that.'

body.text: (VII.13) sapta dravata iti. duḥkhākārāś catvāro dravyato bhavanti. samudayādyākārās tv ekaika iti sapta. ya eva hetvākāraḥ. sa eva samudayaḥ prabhavaḥ pratyayaś ca paryāyamātraṃ nārthabhedaḥ. śakra indraḥ puraṃdara iti yathā. evaṃ nirodha eva śāntaḥ praṇīto niḥsaraṇam ity eka ākāraḥ. mārga eva ca nyāyaḥ pratipan nairyāṇika ity eka ākāra iti. tad idam uktaṃ bhavati. duḥkhākārāṃś caturaḥ pṛthag yoginaḥ sammukhīkuryuḥ. hetvādyākārāṇāṃ tv ekaikam ity ekīyamataṃ.
body.translated_text: (VII.13) 'Seven are real substances (<s>dravya</s>)' — the four aspects of suffering exist as [separate] substances. But the aspects of origination and the rest are each one [substance] — thus seven. Whatever is the aspect of cause (<s>hetu</s>), that itself is origination (<s>samudaya</s>), arising (<s>prabhava</s>), and condition (<s>pratyaya</s>) — it is merely a synonym, not a difference in meaning. Just as <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Purandara</s> [are synonyms]. Likewise, cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) itself is peace (<s>śānta</s>), excellence (<s>praṇīta</s>), and escape (<s>niḥsaraṇa</s>) — one aspect. And the path (<s>mārga</s>) itself is method (<s>nyāya</s>), practice (<s>pratipat</s>), and leading out (<s>nairyāṇika</s>) — one aspect. This is what is said: the four aspects of suffering — yogins would bring them face to face separately. But of the aspects of cause and the rest — each is one — this is the view of some.

body.text: vaibhāṣikā varṇayanti duḥkhākāravat samudayādyākārāṇāṃ sarveṣām api pṛthakpṛthak saṃmukhīkartavyatvāt. prajñāsvabhāvā hy ākārā iti bruvate. pratyayādhīnatvād iti vistaraḥ. na niyatabhavam anityaṃ pratyayādhīnatvāt pratyayapratibaddhajanmatvād ity arthaḥ. pīḍanātmakatvād [Tib. 291b] iti. bādhanātmakatvād ity arthaḥ. vipakṣeṇeti. pratipakṣeṇety arthaḥ. viruddhaḥ pakṣo vipakṣa iti kṛtvā. hetur bījadharmayogeneti. prakṛṣṭāvasthatāṃ hetor darśayaty ādibījavat. yogaśabdo 'tra nyāyarthaḥ. samudayaḥ prādurbhāvayogeneti. saṃnikṛṣṭāvasthatāṃ hetor darśayati. yataḥ kṣaṇād anantaram utpadyate samudety asmād iti kṛtvā. prabhavaḥ prabaṃdhayogeneti. saṃtatiyogenānucchedaṃ darśayati. bījāṃkurakāṇḍanālādivat. abhiniṣpādanārthena pratyaya iti. hetvādibhyo bahubhya utpadyata iti darśayati. tadyathā mṛtpiṇḍadaṇḍādibhyo bahubhyo niṣpadyate ghaṭaḥ. tadvat. agninirvāpaṇād iti. rāgadveṣamohāgninirvāpaṇād ity arthaḥ. nirupadravatvād iti. nirduḥkhatvād ity arthaḥ. sarvāpakṣālaviyuktatvād iti. sarvaduḥkhakāraṇavimuktatvāt. gamanārthena nirvāṇasya. yogayuktatvād upapattiyuktatvād upāyayuktatvād vā. samyakpratipādanārthena pratipad iti. pratipadyate nirvāṇam anayeti pratipat. nairyāṇika iti. atyaṃtaṃ niryāṇāya prabhavatīti nairyāṇikaḥ.
body.translated_text: The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s explain: just as with the aspect of suffering, all aspects — those of origination and the rest — must each be individually brought face-to-face. For they say: 'Aspects are of the nature of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>).' 'Because of being dependent on conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>)' — in detail. 'Impermanent because of not having fixed existence — because of being dependent on conditions' — the meaning is: because birth is bound to conditions. 'Because of having the nature of affliction (<s>pīḍana</s>)' — the meaning is: because of having the nature of oppression (<s>bādhana</s>). 'By the opponent (<s>vipakṣa</s>)' — the meaning is: by the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>). An opposing side is a <s>vipakṣa</s> — thus considering. 'Cause (<s>hetu</s>) in the manner of a seed-dharma' — he shows the remote state of the cause, like a primordial seed. The word <s>yoga</s> here means 'manner' (<s>nyāya</s>). 'Origination (<s>samudaya</s>) in the manner of manifestation' — he shows the proximate state of the cause. Because from the immediately preceding moment it arises — it originates from this — thus considering. 'Source (<s>prabhava</s>) in the manner of continuity' — he shows non-interruption through the manner of continuity, like seed, sprout, stalk, stem, and so forth. 'Condition (<s>pratyaya</s>) in the sense of bringing about the effect' — he shows that it is produced from many [factors] such as causes and the rest. Just as a pot is produced from many [things] such as a lump of clay, a stick, and the rest — so too. 'Because of the extinguishing of the fire' — the meaning is: because of the extinguishing of the fires of desire (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>). 'Because of being without calamity (<s>nirupadrava</s>)' — the meaning is: because of being free from suffering. 'Because of being free from all defilement (<s>sarvāpakṣāla</s>)' — because of being free from all causes of suffering. 'In the sense of going' — of going to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Because of being connected with method (<s>yoga</s>), because of being connected with fitness (<s>upapatti</s>), or because of being connected with means (<s>upāya</s>). 'Practice (<s>pratipad</s>) in the sense of correct establishment' — one reaches <s>nirvāṇa</s> by this — hence practice. 'Leading out (<s>nairyāṇika</s>)' — because it is fully capable of ultimate leading out.

body.text: anātyantikatvād [Tib. 292a] anityam iti. pūrvaṃ prāgutpattyabhāvenānityam uktam. idānīṃ pradhvaṃsābhāveneti darśayati. abhinyāsabhūtatvād iti. bhārabhūtatvād ity arthaḥ. duḥkhena bhārabhūtena hi sa pudgalo bhidyate. ākramyata ity arthaḥ. akāmakāritvād iti. kāmataḥ kartuṃ śīlam asyeti kāmakārī. na kāmakāry akāmakārī. tadbhāvāt anātmā. sūtre 'py ayam artha uktaḥ. rūpaṃ ced bhikṣava ātmābhaviṣyat. na rūpam ātmavyābādhāya saṃvarteta. labhyeta ca rūpe evaṃ bhavatv evaṃ mā bhūd iti kāmakāry ātmeti
body.translated_text: 'Impermanent because of non-ultimateness (<s>anātyantikatva</s>)' — previously, impermanence was stated because of the absence prior to arising. Now he shows [impermanence] because of the absence through destruction (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>). 'Because of having the nature of a burden (<s>abhinyāsa</s>)' — the meaning is: because of being a burden. For the person is crushed by suffering, which is a burden — the meaning is: is oppressed. 'Because of non-freedom-of-will (<s>akāmakāritva</s>)' — one whose habit is to act at will is a <s>kāmakārī</s>. One who is not a <s>kāmakārī</s> is an <s>akāmakārī</s>. Because of that state — non-self (<s>anātman</s>). This meaning is also stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'If, O <s>bhikṣu</s>s, form were the self, form would not conduce to affliction of the self. And it would be possible with regard to form [to say]: "Let my form be thus; let my form not be thus" — the self being one who acts at will'

body.text: niruktiparigrahāt. hetur āgamanayogeneti. hi gatau hinoty asmād iti hetuḥ. asmād utpadyata ity arthaḥ. unmajjanayogeneti. anāgatādhvana unmajjatīvety arthaḥ. prasaraṇayogeneti. prabandhayogena. pratisaraṇārthena pratyaya iti. janikriyāpratipradhānabhūta ity abhiprāyaḥ. asaṃbandhaḥ saṃbaṃdhoparamād iti. pūrvasya duḥkhasyoparamāt. uttarasya saṃbaṃdhoparamo nirodha ity arthaḥ. trisaṃskṛtalakṣaṇavimuktatvāt. utpādavyayasthīty [Tib. 292b] anyathātvavimuktatvāt. paramāśvāsatvād iti sarvaduḥkhocchittyā paramakṣematvāt. nirvāṇapurāvirodhanārthena pratipad iti. yasmād anena nirvāṇapuraṃ na virodhyate na visaṃvādyate. kiṃ tarhi pratipadyata evety ataḥ pratipat. pratipadyate anayeti kṛtvā.
body.translated_text: — because of the acceptance of the etymology. 'Cause (<s>hetu</s>) in the manner of arising (<s>āgamana</s>)' — for <s>hetu</s> is [from the root] <s>hi</s> meaning 'to go': it propels from this — this is a <s>hetu</s>. The meaning is: from this it arises. 'In the manner of emerging (<s>unmajjana</s>)' — the meaning is: it emerges, as it were, from the future time-period. 'In the manner of spreading forth (<s>prasaraṇa</s>)' — in the manner of continuation. 'Condition (<s>pratyaya</s>) in the sense of support (<s>pratisaraṇa</s>)' — the intent is: that which is the chief foundation for the activity of birth. 'Non-connection (<s>asaṃbandha</s>) — because of the cessation of connection' — because of the cessation of the prior suffering. The meaning is: the cessation of connection with the subsequent is cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). 'Because of being free from the three conditioned characteristics' — because of being free from arising, passing away, and duration- and-change (<s>sthityanyathātva</s>). 'Because of supreme consolation (<s>paramāśvāsa</s>)' — because of being the supreme security through the complete elimination of all suffering. 'Practice (<s>pratipad</s>) in the sense of not conflicting with the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — because by this the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not obstructed, not contradicted. Rather, it is precisely reached — therefore it is a practice. Because one reaches by it — thus considering.

body.text: chandamūlakā iti. chandahetukā ity arthaḥ. tṛṣṇāparyāya iha chaṃdaḥ. chandasamudayā iti. chandasamudgamā ity arthaḥ. chandajātīyā iti. chandapratyayā ity arthaḥ. prabhavaśabdaḥ kevalaṃ paścāt paṭhitavyaḥ. ābhidhārmikair iti vākyādhyāhāraḥ. sūtrānusaraṇaṃ hi kartavyam ity abhiprāyaḥ. hetutaḥ samudayataḥ. pratyayataḥ prabhavataś ceti.
body.translated_text: 'Rooted in desire (<s>chandamūlaka</s>)' — the meaning is: having desire as its cause. The word desire (<s>chanda</s>) here is a synonym for craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). 'Of the origination of desire (<s>chandasamudaya</s>)' — the meaning is: of the arising of desire. 'Of the kind of desire (<s>chandajātīya</s>)' — the meaning is: having desire as condition. The word 'source' (<s>prabhava</s>) alone should be read afterward. 'By the <s>Ābhidhārmika</s>s' — this is a sentence-supplement. The intent is: one should follow the <s>sūtra</s>. From the cause (<s>hetu</s>), from the origination (<s>samudaya</s>), from the condition (<s>pratyaya</s>), and from the source (<s>prabhava</s>) —

body.text: kaḥ punar eṣāṃ [padānāṃ] chandānām [iva vā] viśeṣaḥ. asmīty abhedenātmabhāvacchanda iti. anavadhāryaikaṃ dravyaṃ samasteṣu paṃcasūpādānaskaṃdheṣu asmīty abhedena prakārāntaraviśiṣṭasya pratyutpannasyātmabhāvavastuno 'nālaṃbanataḥ traiyadhvikātmabhāvanālambanato vā ātmabhāvaprārthanā ātmabhāvacchanda iti prathamaḥ. syām ity abhedeneti punarbhavamātraprārthanā na viśeṣarūpāprārthaneti dvitīyaḥ. itthaṃ syām iti. idaṃprakāraḥ [Tib. 293a] syām iti bhedena punarbhavaccandas tṛtīyaḥ. pratisaṃdhibandhacchandaś caturtha iti. pratisaṃdhir eva baṃdhaḥ. pratisaṃdher vā baṃdhaḥ pratisaṃdhibaṃdhaḥ. tatra chandaḥ prārthaneti caturthaḥ. karmābhisaṃskāracchando vā caturtha ity adhikṛtaṃ. karmaṇo vābhisaṃskāraḥ. tatra chandaḥ. evaṃ caivaṃ ca dānaṃ dāsyāmīti. kathaṃ punas te chandā mūlādiśabdavācyā iti pratipādayann āha. tatra prathama iti vistaraḥ. ādiḥ kāraṇam ādau vā kāraṇam ādikāraṇaṃ. tadbhāvāt chandamūlakāḥ. hetvartho hi mūlaśabdaḥ. phalasyeva bījam iti. yathā phalasya bījam ādikāraṇaṃ viprakṛṣṭakāraṇaṃ. tadvad ayam ādicchando duḥkhasya. tena tatsamudāgamād iti. tena dvitīyena chadena punarbhavasya samudāgamāt kṣaṇaparaṃparayā phalasyevāṃkurādiprasavaḥ. yathā paraṃparayāṃkurādiprasavaḥ phalasya samudayaḥ. tadvat. tṛtīyacchanda itthaṃ syām iti. tajjātīyaduḥkhapratyaya iti. yatprakāraḥ punarbhavacchandaḥ. tatprakārasya duḥkhasya
body.translated_text: 'What then is the distinction among these terms — of these desires?' 'In the manner of undifferentiatedness: "I am" — the desire for self-existence (<s>ātmabhāvacchanda</s>)' — without determining a single substance among all five aggregates of clinging, [thinking] 'I am' without differentiation — not taking as object-domain the present self-existence qualified by particular modes, or taking as object-domain self-existence across the three time-periods — the longing for self-existence is the desire for self-existence — this is the first [desire]. 'In the manner of undifferentiatedness: "May I be" — the desire for mere re-existence, not a desire for a particular form' — this is the second. '"May I be thus" — "May I be of this particular kind"' — in the manner of differentiation, the desire for re-existence is the third. 'The desire for the connection of rebirth-linking is the fourth' — rebirth-linking itself is the connection, or the connection of rebirth-linking. The desire therein — the longing — is the fourth. 'Or the desire for the conditioning of <s>karma</s> is the fourth' — this is an alternative. The conditioning of <s>karma</s>, or the conditioning by <s>karma</s> — the desire therein. 'Thus and thus I shall give gifts,' and so forth. How then are these desires denoted by the terms 'root' and the rest? — establishing this, he says: 'Therein, the first' — in detail. A cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>) is a beginning, or a cause at the beginning is a beginning-cause (<s>ādikāraṇa</s>). Because of that state — rooted in desire. For the word 'root' (<s>mūla</s>) has the meaning of 'cause.' 'Like the seed of a fruit' — just as the seed is the beginning-cause, the remote cause, of the fruit — so too this initial desire is [the remote cause] of suffering. 'Through the attainment of that' — through the attainment of the second desire — because of the attainment of re-existence through a succession of moments, like the production of sprout and the rest from the fruit through a series. Just as through a series there is the production of sprout and the rest — that is the origination of the fruit. So too. The third desire — 'May I be thus' — 'is the condition (<s>pratyaya</s>) for the suffering of that type' — because the desire for re-existence of that particular type

body.text: pratyayaḥ saṃbhavati tasya viśeṣarūpatvād viśeṣaphalarūpam eva phalam utpadyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. phalasyeva kṣetrodakapāṣyādikam iti. pāṣiḥ śuṣko gomayaḥ. ādiśabdena [Tib. 293b] vātātapādir gṛhyate. tato 'pi hi phalasaṃpad iti. vīryaṃ śītavīryatā uṣṇavīryateti. vipākaḥ uṣṇapariṇāmatā madhurapariṇāmateti. prabhāvaḥ sāmarthyaviśeṣaḥ. tadyathāmlatve tulye bījapūrakarasaḥ pittaṃ janayaty āmalakarasaṃ tu śamayatīti. tata eva tatsaṃbhavād iti. tata eva pratisaṃdhibaṃdhacchandāt tasya punarbhavalakṣaṇasya saṃbhavād utpādāt. phalasyeva puṣpāvasānaṃ. yathā puṣpāvasānaṃ phalasya prabhavaḥ. tadvat. atra caturthaccandaḥ sākṣāddhetuḥ punarbhavasya. pūrvakās trayaḥ pāraṃparyeṇa hetavaḥ. atha ceti vistaraḥ. tṛṣṇāvicaritānāṃ dvav paṃcakau gaṇau dvav catuṣkau catvāraś chandā yathākramaṃ bhavanti. prathamacchandaḥ paṃcākāraḥ. dvitīyo 'pi paṃcākāraḥ. tṛtīyaś catuḥprakāraḥ. caturtho 'pi catuḥprakāraḥ. katham. asmīti bhikṣavaḥ satyātmadṛṣṭau satyām ittham asmīti bhavatīdaṃ prakāro 'smīti bhavati. tadyogāt tṛṣṇām utpādayatīty arthaḥ. evam asmīti yathā pūrvam eva nānyathety arthaḥ. anyathāsmīty anyena prakāreṇa varṇapratibhānādidarśanāt. sad asmīti bhavati. viparyayād asad asmīty ayam abhedena paṃcadhātmabhāvaccandaḥ prathamaḥ. bhaviṣyāmīty asya bhavatīti śāśvatarūpeṇa. na bhaviṣyāmīty ucchedarūpeṇa. itthaṃ bhaviṣyāmīti vistareṇa pūrvavad vyākhyānam. [Tib. 294a] ity ayam abhedena paṃcadhāpunarbhavacchando dvitīyaḥ. syām ity asya bhavati. itthaṃ syām evaṃ syām anyathā syām ity asya bhavatīty ayaṃ bhedena caturdhāpunarbhavacchaṃdas tṛtīyaḥ. api tu syām ity asya bhavaty apītthaṃ syām apy evaṃ syām apy anyathā syām ity asya caturdhāpratisaṃdhibaṃdhacchandas caturthaḥ. tatra prathamo duḥkhasyādikāraṇatvān mūlahetur iti vistareṇa pūrvavad yojyaṃ. pratiniyatatvāt pratipad iti. niyatapratipādanaṃ pratipat. kathaṃ punaḥ pratiniyatā. anayaiva tadgamanāt.
body.translated_text: becomes the condition — because of its specific form, a fruit of specific form alone is produced — this is the intent. 'Like the field, water, dried cow-dung, and the rest for the fruit' — <s>pāṣi</s> means 'dried cow-dung.' By the word 'and the rest,' wind, heat, and the like are included. For from those too there is the prosperity of the fruit. 'Potency (<s>vīrya</s>)' — cold potency, hot potency. 'Ripening (<s>vipāka</s>)' — hot ripening, sweet ripening. 'Power (<s>prabhāva</s>)' — a distinction of capacity. For example: although equal in sourness, the juice of the <s>bījapūra</s> (citron) generates bile, while the juice of the <s>āmalaka</s> (emblic myrobalan) pacifies it. 'Because of the arising of that from that very [desire]' — because of the arising, the production, of that which has the characteristic of re-existence, from that very desire for rebirth-linking-connection. 'Like the culmination in the blossom of the fruit' — just as the culmination in the blossom is the source (<s>prabhava</s>) of the fruit — so too. Here the fourth desire is the direct cause of re-existence; the prior three are causes through succession. 'And moreover' — in detail. The groups of desires, as traversed by craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), are: two sets of five, two sets of four — the four desires are in sequence. The first desire has five modes; the second too has five modes; the third has four modes; the fourth too has four modes. How? 'O <s>bhikṣu</s>s, when the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) exists, there arises "I am thus" — "I am of this kind" — by its connection, one produces craving' — this is the meaning. Similarly, '"I am" is as before — not otherwise' — this is the meaning. '"I am otherwise" — because of the sight of a different kind by color, appearance, and the like.' '"I am existent"' — this is so. 'Conversely, "I am non-existent"' — this fivefold desire for self-existence, in the manner of undifferentiatedness, is the first. '"I shall be" arises for this one' — in the manner of eternalism. '"I shall not be"' — in the manner of annihilationism. '"I shall be thus"' — in detail, the explanation is as before. This fivefold desire for re-existence, in the manner of undifferentiatedness, is the second. '"May I be" arises for this one; "May I be thus; may I be so; may I be otherwise"' — this fourfold desire for re-existence, in the manner of differentiation, is the third. '"But may I be" arises for this one; "but may I be thus; but may I be so; but may I be otherwise"' — this fourfold desire for rebirth-linking-connection is the fourth. 'Therein, the first is the root-cause because of being the beginning-cause of suffering' — in detail, the connection should be made as before. 'Because of being determinate, the practice (<s>pratipad</s>)' — a determinate establishment is a practice. How then is it determinate? Because of going to that [nirvāṇa] by this very [practice] alone.

body.text: yathoktam iti vistaraḥ. nityasukhātmīyātmadṛṣṭicaritānām iti. nityaṃ sukham ātmīyaṃ ātmeti ca dṛṣṭicaritam eṣāṃ. ta ime nityasukhātmīyātmadṛṣṭicaritāḥ pudgalāḥ. teṣāṃ pratipakṣeṇa yathākramam anityādyākārāḥ. nāsti hetur ity ahetudṛṣṭicaritānāṃ pratipakṣeṇa hetvākāraḥ. eko hetur īśvaraḥ pradhānaṃ cety ekahetudṛṣṭicaritānāṃ samudayākāraḥ. samudayo hetur naikahetur iti. pariṇamate bhāva iti pariṇāmadṛṣṭicaritānāṃ prabhavākāraḥ.
body.translated_text: 'As stated' — in detail. 'Of those whose conduct is the view of permanent, pleasant, mine, and self' — whose view-conduct is [the view that things are] permanent, pleasant, mine, and self. Those persons are those whose conduct is the view of permanent, pleasant, mine, and self. As antidotes for them, in due order, are the aspects of impermanence and the rest. 'For those whose conduct is the view of no cause' — as the antidote for those whose conduct is the view of no cause (<s>ahetudṛṣṭi</s>), there is the aspect of cause (<s>hetu</s>). 'One cause, such as a Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) or Primal Nature (<s>Pradhāna</s>)' — for those whose conduct is the view of a single cause, the aspect of origination (<s>samudaya</s>): origination is a cause, not a single cause. 'For those whose conduct is the view of transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>)' — the aspect of source (<s>prabhava</s>).

body.text: ādibhavo 'yaṃ. na tu pūrvam avasthitaḥ pariṇamata iti. buddhipūrvakṛto 'yaṃ loka iti buddhipūrvakṛtadṛṣṭicaritānāṃ [Tib. 294b] pratyayākāraḥ. nedam īśvarabuddhikṛtaṃ jagat. kiṃ tarhi. taṃtaṃ pratītya tattad bhavatīti. vīpsārtho hi pratiśabdaḥ. tasmād anekapratyayajanitaṃ jagad iti jñāpitaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: This is a beginning-existence — but it does not first stand and then transform. 'For those whose conduct is the view that this world was made by an intelligence (<s>buddhipūrvakṛta</s>)' — for those whose conduct is the view that this world was made by an intelligence — the aspect of condition (<s>pratyaya</s>). This world was not made by an intelligent Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). Rather, in dependence on this-and-that, this-and-that comes to be. For the prefix <s>prati</s> has the meaning of distributiveness (<s>vīpsā</s>). Therefore it is indicated that the world was produced from multiple conditions.

body.text: evaṃ tu yuktaṃ syād iti. sautrāntikamatam. ālambanagrahaṇaprakāra ākārā iti. nairuktā vidhir iti darśayaty ālambanaśabdād ākāraṃ gṛhītvā prakāraśabdāc ca kāraśabdaṃ. śeṣavarṇalope ca kṛte ākāra iti rupaṃ bhavati. tad evaṃ sati prajñāpi sākārā bhavatīti siddhaṃ. sālambā iti. ālambety ākārāntam etac chabdarūpaṃ. ghañantaṃ vā ālamba iti. sahālambena sahālambayā vā vartante sālambaḥ. sālambanā ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'But this would be fitting thus' — this is the <s>Sautrāntika</s> view. 'Aspects are the manner of grasping the object-domain (<s>ālambana</s>)' — he shows the etymological derivation: taking the word <s>ākāra</s> (aspect) from the word <s>ālambana</s> (object-domain) and the word <s>kāra</s> (manner) from the word <s>prakāra</s> (mode), and with the elision of the remaining letters, the form <s>ākāra</s> results. This being so, it is established that wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) too has aspects. 'With support (<s>sālambanā</s>)' — <s>ālamba</s> is a word-form ending in <s>ākāra</s>, or ending in <s>ghañ</s> — <s>ālamba</s>. Together with support, or together with the supported — <s>sālambaḥ</s>. The meaning is: having support (<s>sālambanā</s>).

body.text: (VII.14, 15) kuśalādibhedam iti. ādiśabdenākuśalāvyākṛtabhūmyāśrayagrahaṇaṃ. ślokādau bhavatvād ādyam iti ihādyaṃ. na śāstram iti vyācaṣṭe. śāstre hi dharmajñānam ādyaṃ paṭhitam iti.
body.translated_text: (VII.14, 15) 'The distinction of wholesome and the rest' — by the word 'and the rest,' the inclusion of unwholesome, indeterminate, ground, and basis [is indicated]. 'The first in the verse, because of being at the beginning' — here, 'first' [means first in the verse, not in the treatise]. He explains: 'not the treatise.' For in the treatise, <s>dharmajñāna</s> is read first.

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: kāmāvacaraduḥkhādyālambanatvāt. ārūpyatraye cāsti bhāvanāmārgasaṃgṛhītam evānvayajñānaṃ.
body.translated_text: Because of having as its object-domain suffering and the rest of the Desire Realm. And in the three formless [realms], there exists <s>anvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge) included in the cultivation path alone.

body.text: iti. duḥkhajñānādīnām anvayajñānasvabhāvatvasambhavāt. na rūpārūpyadhātvoḥ saṃmukhīkriyata iti. yuktaṃ tāvad ārūpyadhātau dharmajñānaṃ na saṃmukhīkriyata iti. ārūpyāṇāṃ kāmāvacaraduḥkhādyanālaṃbanatvāt. rūpadhātau tu kasmān na saṃmukhīkriyate. kecid āhuḥ. kāmadhātuvidūṣaṇaparaṃ dharmajñānaṃ. rūpadhātūpapannasya ca dharmajñānaṃ na kāmadhātuṃ vidūṣayitum [Tib. 295a] upajāyate. tasya vairāgyabhūmisaṃcāraparityaktatvāt. kāmadhātūpapannas tu tad vītarāgo 'pi tat saṃmukhīkaroti. kāmadhātūpapatteḥ sāvaśeṣatvād ity ato na rūpadhātau dharmajñānaṃ saṃmukhīkriyate. ācāryasaṃghabhadras tv āha. dharmajñānaṃ kāmedhātāv eva saṃmukhīkriyate. na rūpārūpya dhātvoḥ. tatsamāpattivyutthānacittānāṃ kāmadhātāv eva sadbhāvāt. anuparivartakāśrayābhāvād vā. dharmajñānānuparivartakasya hi śīlasya kāmāvacarāṇy eva bhūtāny āśrayaḥ. dauḥśīlyasamutthāpakakleśaprāptivibaṃdhakatvāt. prātipakṣikatvāt. tāni ca tatra na saṃtīti dharmajñānam kāmadhātv āśrayaṃ eveti.
body.translated_text: Thus. Because <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> (knowledge of suffering) and the rest can have the nature of <s>anvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge). "It is not brought face-to-face in the Form and Formless Realms" — it is indeed reasonable that <s>dharmajñāna</s> is not brought face-to-face in the Formless Realm, because the formless [attainments] do not take as their object-domain the suffering and the rest pertaining to the Desire Realm. But why is it not brought face-to-face in the Form Realm? Some say: <s>dharmajñāna</s> is devoted to the corruption of the Desire Realm. And for one reborn in the Form Realm, <s>dharmajñāna</s> does not arise for the purpose of corrupting the Desire Realm, [Tib. 295a] because that [Desire Realm] has been relinquished through transfer to the ground of dispassion. But one reborn in the Desire Realm brings it face-to-face even if free from desire — because of the residual [connection with] rebirth in the Desire Realm. Therefore <s>dharmajñāna</s> is not brought face-to-face in the Form Realm. But <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> says: <s>dharmajñāna</s> is brought face-to-face only in the Desire Realm, not in the Form and Formless Realms — because the post-attainment and post-emergence minds of that attainment exist only in the Desire Realm. Or because of the absence of a supporting basis for what follows along with <s>dharmajñāna</s>. For the supporting basis of the morality (<s>śīla</s>) that follows along with <s>dharmajñāna</s> is only the material elements (<s>bhūta</s>) pertaining to the Desire Realm — because of obstructing the acquisition of afflictions that give rise to immorality, because of being an antidote. And those [material elements] do not exist there — therefore <s>dharmajñāna</s> has only the Desire Realm as its support.

body.text: (VII.16) nirodhajñānam ekaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānanirdeśa
body.translated_text: (VII.16) <s>Nirodhajñāna</s> (knowledge of cessation) is one <s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundation of mindfulness of dharmas). In the exposition of the <s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s>

body.text: uktaṃ. dharmāḥ kāyavedanācittebhyo 'nya iti. anyāni jñānāni catvāri smṛtyupasthānānīti. dharmānvayasaṃvṛtiduḥkhasamudayamārgakṣayānutpādajñānāni catuḥsmṛtyupasthānasvabhāvāni santi. duḥkhajñānam api hi kadācit kāyālaṃbanaṃ. kadācid yāvad dharmālambanaṃ. evaṃ samudayajñānaṃ. mārgajñānam api yad anāsravasaṃvarālambanaṃ kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ tad bhavati. śeṣaṃ sugamaṃ.
body.translated_text: it was stated: "<s>dharma</s>s are those other than body, feeling, and mind." The other knowledges have the nature of four foundations of mindfulness. <s>Dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>saṃvṛti</s>-, <s>duḥkha</s>-, <s>samudaya</s>-, <s>mārga</s>-, <s>kṣaya</s>-, and <s>anutpādajñāna</s> have the nature of all four foundations of mindfulness. For <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> (knowledge of suffering) sometimes has body as its object-domain, sometimes up to <s>dharma</s>s as its object-domain. Similarly <s>samudayajñāna</s>. <s>Mārgajñāna</s> too — that which has the uncontaminated restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) as its object-domain is the <s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundation of mindfulness of the body). The rest is easy to understand.

body.text: (VII.17) anyatrānvayajñānād iti. dharmajñānaṃ yady anāsravaṃ jñānam ālaṃbeta [Tib. 295b] dharmajñānapakṣam evālambeta. evam anvayajñānam anvayajñānapakṣam evālambeteti niyamaḥ. tatra dharmajñānasya mārgajñānabhūtasya dharmajñānāntaraṃ duḥkhajñānādīni cānutpādajñānāntāny ālambanaṃ saṃbhavanti. duḥkhasamudayajñānabhūtasya tu saṃvṛtijñānam ālaṃbanaṃ saṃbhavati. paracittajñānabhūtasya ca paracittajñānam ālaṃbanaṃ saṃbhavatīti. nava jñānāni tasyālaṃbanam iti. evam anvayajñānam api yojyaṃ. mārgajñānasyāpi navaivānyatra saṃvṛtijñānāt. na hi mārgajñānaṃ saṃvṛtijñānam ālambate. anāsravamārgālambananiyamāt. dve saṃvṛtiparacittajñāne iti. duḥkhasamudayasatyāṃtarbhūte. paracittajñānaṃ yad anāsravaṃ. tasya navānāsravāṇi jñānāny ālaṃbanaṃ. yat sāsravaṃ tasya saṃvṛtijñānaṃ prarcittajñānaṃ cālambanaṃ saṃbhavati. kṣayānutpādajñāne duḥkhajñānādisvabhāva iti daśāpi jñānāni tayor ālambanāni bhuvanti.
body.translated_text: (VII.17) "Except for <s>anvayajñāna</s>" — if <s>dharmajñāna</s> were to take uncontaminated knowledge as its object-domain, [Tib. 295b] it would take only the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class as its object-domain. Similarly, <s>anvayajñāna</s> would take only the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class as its object-domain — this is the restriction. Therein, for <s>dharmajñāna</s> functioning as <s>mārgajñāna</s>, other <s>dharmajñāna</s>s and <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> and the rest up to <s>anutpādajñāna</s> are possible object-domains. For one functioning as <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> or <s>samudayajñāna</s>, <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> (conventional knowledge) is a possible object-domain. And for one functioning as <s>paracittajñāna</s>, <s>paracittajñāna</s> is a possible object-domain. Thus nine knowledges are the object-domain of that [<s>dharmajñāna</s>]. Similarly <s>anvayajñāna</s> should be connected. For <s>mārgajñāna</s> too, nine only — except for <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>. For <s>mārgajñāna</s> does not take <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> as its object-domain — because of the restriction that it takes the uncontaminated path as its object-domain. The two — <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> and <s>paracittajñāna</s> — are included in the truths of suffering and origination. As for <s>paracittajñāna</s> that is uncontaminated — nine uncontaminated knowledges are its object-domain. That which is contaminated — <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> and <s>paracittajñāna</s> are its possible object-domains. <s>Kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of destruction) and <s>anutpādajñāna</s> (knowledge of non-arising), having the nature of <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> and the rest, take all ten knowledges as their object-domains.

body.text: (VII.18, 19) saṃprayuktaviprayuktabhedād iti.
body.translated_text: (VII.18, 19) "Because of the distinction of associated and disassociated" —

body.text: iti. viprayuktāḥ prāptyādayaḥ. kuśalāvyākṛtabhedād iti. kuśalaṃ pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ paramakṣematvāt. avyākṛtāv [Tib. 296a] ākāśapratisaṃkhyānirodhāv iti. kāmāvacarānāsravāś catvāra iti. saṃprayuktaviprayuktabhedāt. rūpārūpyāvacarānāsravāḥ ṣaḍ iti. pratyekaṃ saṃprayuktaviprayuktabhedāt. kāmarūpārūpyāvacarā api tata eva bhedāt ṣaṭ. dvāv anāsravāv iti. tata eva kāmarūpāvacarānāsravaḥ saṃprayuktā iti. ārūpyāvacarāṃāṃ cittacaittānāṃ viprayuktāsaṃskṛtānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ paracittajñānāviṣayatvāt. avyākṛtam asaṃskṛtaṃ muktveti. kṣayānutpādajñānayoś catuḥsatyālambanatvād avyākṛtasya cāsaṃskṛtasya tadvyatiriktatvāt.
body.translated_text: thus. The disassociated are acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>) and the rest. "Because of the distinction of wholesome and indeterminate" — the wholesome is <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (cessation through deliberation), because of being supremely secure. The indeterminate [Tib. 296a] are <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (cessation not through deliberation). "Four pertaining to the Desire Realm and uncontaminated" — because of the distinction of associated and disassociated. "Six pertaining to the Form and Formless Realms and uncontaminated" — because of the distinction of associated and disassociated for each individually. "Those pertaining to the Desire, Form, and Formless Realms are also six, for the same reason of distinction." "Two uncontaminated" — for the same reason: the associated pertaining to the Desire and Form Realms are uncontaminated. Because all <s>citta</s>s and <s>caitta</s>s of the Formless Realm, as well as all disassociated [dharmas] and unconditioned [dharmas], are not the object-domain of <s>paracittajñāna</s> (knowledge of others' minds). "Excluding indeterminate unconditioned" — because <s>kṣayajñāna</s> and <s>anutpādajñāna</s> take the four Noble Truths as their object-domain, and because the indeterminate unconditioned is distinct from those.

body.text: (VII.20) syād ekena jñānena sarvadharmān jānīyāt. na syād iti. kathaṃ gamyate. sūtrāt. ihāsmākaṃ bho gautama upasthānaśālāyāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ saṃnipatitānām evaṃrūpāntarākathāsamudāhāro 'bhūt. śramaṇo gautamaḥ
body.translated_text: (VII.20) "Could one know all <s>dharma</s>s with a single knowledge? No." How is this understood? From the <s>sūtra</s>. "Here, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, when we were seated and assembled in our assembly hall, a conversation of the following sort arose: The ascetic <s>Gautama</s>

body.text: kilaivam āha. nāsti sa kaścic chramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā. yaḥ sakṛt sarvaṃ jānīyāt sarvaṃ paśyed iti. tathyam idaṃ bho gautama smarāmi bhavato 'ham evaṃ vaktum. api tu nāsti sa kaścic chramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā. yaḥ sakṛt sarvaṃ jñāsyati vā drakṣyati veti.
body.translated_text: reportedly says thus: There is no ascetic or <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who could know everything at once and see everything at once. This is true, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>: I recall you to have said thus. However, there is no ascetic or <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who will know everything at once or see everything at once."

body.text: viṣayiviṣayabhedād iti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 296b] viṣayiṇo viṣayasya ca bhedāt. yasmād yo viṣayī. na sa eva tasya viṣayo bhavati. svātamani vṛttivirodhāt. na hi saivāsidhārā tayaiva chidyate. tasmāt tena saṃvṛtijñānena svabhāvo na gṛhyate. nāpi tena caittāḥ sahabhuvo gṛhyante. ekālambanatvāt. yad eva hi tasya saṃvṛtijñānasyālambanaṃ. tad eva saṃprayuktānāṃ. yadi ca te saṃprayuktā gṛhyeran svabhāvālambanāḥ syuḥ. saṃvṛtijñānenaikālaṃbanāt. na caitad yuktaṃ. tasmān na te tena gṛhyante. atisaṃnikṛṣṭatvāc ca. na tena viprayuktāḥ sahabhuvo 'pi gṛhyante. cakṣuṣo 'ñjanāñjanaśalākādarśanavat. tac ceti saṃvṛtijñānaṃ. tasya vyavacchinnabhūmyālambanatvād iti. yasmād bhāvanāmayaṃ rūpāvacaraṃ saṃvṛtijñānaṃ vyavacchinnam eva bhūmim ālambate. kāmadhātuṃ vā prathamaṃ vā dhyānaṃ yāvad bhavāgraṃ vā. kiṃ kāraṇam. ānantaryavimuktimārgāṇām adharottarabhūmyālambanatvāt yathākramaṃ.
body.translated_text: "Because of the distinction of the subject and the object" — in detail. [Tib. 296b] Because of the distinction of the subject (<s>viṣayin</s>) and the object (<s>viṣaya</s>). Since that which is the subject is not its own object — because of the contradiction of functioning upon itself. For the very edge of a sword is not itself cut by itself. Therefore, by that conventional knowledge, its own nature is not grasped. Nor are the co-arising <s>caitta</s>s (mental factors) grasped by it — because of having the same object-domain. For whatever is the object-domain of that conventional knowledge, that very thing is [the object-domain] of the associated [dharmas]. And if those associated [dharmas] were grasped, they would have their own nature as object-domain — because of having the same object-domain as conventional knowledge. And this is not reasonable. Therefore they are not grasped by it. Also because of extreme proximity. Nor are the co-arising disassociated [dharmas] grasped by it — like the eye not seeing the collyrium, the applicator-stick, or the mirror. "And that" — conventional knowledge. "Because of its object-domain being of a delimited ground" — since <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> (conventional knowledge) born of cultivation and pertaining to the Form Realm takes only a delimited ground as its object-domain — either the Desire Realm, or the first <s>dhyāna</s>, up to the Peak of Existence. For what reason? Because the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantarya</s>) and liberation path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>) have respectively a lower and upper ground as their object-domain, in sequence.

children.translated_text: "The peaceful and so forth, the coarse and so forth — having a higher and lower domain" —

body.text: iti vacanāt. yadi ca tat sarvabhuṃyālambanaṃ syāt. sarvato yugapad vairāgyaṃ syāt. prayogaviśeṣamārgayor api yathāsaṃbhavaṃ kācid eva bhūmir ālambanaṃ. kathaṃ. nirvedhabhāgīyaprayogamārgasaṃgṛhītasya hi yasya kāmadhātur ālambanaṃ. [Tib. 297a] na tasyetarau dhātū. yasyetarau dhātū. na tasya kāmadhātur ālambanaṃ. aśubhāpramāṇābhibhvāyatanādividūṣaṇe viśeṣamārgasaṃgṛhītasya kāmadhātur evālambanaṃ. netarau dhātū.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated. And if it took all grounds as its object-domain, there would be simultaneous dispassion from everything. For the preparatory and special paths too, only some particular ground is the object-domain, as applicable. How? For that which is included in the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (aids to penetration) preparatory path and has the Desire Realm as its object-domain — [Tib. 297a] that does not have the other two realms [as its object-domain]. And that which has the other two realms [as its object-domain] does not have the Desire Realm as its object-domain. That included in the special path — such as the <s>aśubhā</s> (impurity meditation), <s>apramāṇa</s> (immeasurables), <s>abhibhvāyatana</s> (bases of mastery), and corruption [meditations] — has only the Desire Realm as its object-domain, not the other two realms.

children.translated_text: "One with desire, at the first uncontaminated moment, is endowed with one knowledge" —

body.text: iti. yasmāt kṣāntijñānaṃ na bhavati anyenāpi anāsraveṇa jñānena samanvāgato na bhavati rāgīti grahaṇaṃ. yasmād vītarāgaḥ paracittajñānenāpi samanvāgato bhavati.
body.translated_text: thus. Since a <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) is not a <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) — one is not endowed with any other uncontaminated knowledge either. "One with desire" is stated because one who is free from desire (<s>vītarāga</s>) is endowed also with <s>paracittajñāna</s> (knowledge of others' minds).

body.text: iti. tad eva duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ cocyate duḥkhajñānaṃ ceti. nāmabhedāt dvitvopacāre. dharmajñānena duḥkhajñānena saṃvṛtijñānena ceti tribhiḥ samanvāgataḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. That very <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding suffering is also called <s>duḥkhajñāna</s> (knowledge of suffering) — because of the difference in name, there is a figurative attribution of duality. One is endowed with three: <s>dharmajñāna</s>, <s>duḥkhajñāna</s>, and <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> (conventional knowledge).

body.text: iti duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣaṇe samudayamārganirodhadharmajñānakṣaṇeṣu ca. kṣāntiṣu pūrvavad evāsamanvāgamāt duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣaṇe hy anvayam eva vardhate. na dharmajñānaṃ. tena samanvāgatapūrvatvāt. samudayadharmajñānakṣaṇe samudayajñānam eva vardhate. [Tib. 297b] na dharmānvayajñāne. pūrvam eva tābhyāṃ samanvāgatatvāt. evaṃ nirodhamārgadharmajñānakṣaṇayor nirodhamārgajñāne eva vardhete iti vaktavyaṃ. vītarāgas tu sarvatrādhikena paracittajñāneneti. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntau yāvan mārge dharmajñānakṣaṇe paracittajñānenāpi samanvāgataḥ. taiś ca yathoktair jñānair iti veditavyaṃ. mārge 'nvayajñāne tu tair eva saptabhir avītarāgaḥ samanvāgataḥ. vītarāgas tv aṣṭābhiḥ. taiś ca paracittajñānena ceti. kṣayānutpādajñānābhyāṃ tv arhann eva samanvāgata iti subodhān na tadarthaṃ sūtritam ity avagantavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: that is, at the moment of <s>anvayajñāna</s> regarding suffering, and at the moments of <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding origination, path, and cessation. At the <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) moments, as before, there is no endowment [with additional knowledges]. At the moment of <s>anvayajñāna</s> regarding suffering, only <s>anvayajñāna</s> increases — not <s>dharmajñāna</s>, because one was already endowed with that before. At the moment of <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding origination, only <s>samudayajñāna</s> (knowledge of origination) increases — [Tib. 297b] not <s>dharma</s>- or <s>anvayajñāna</s>, because one was already endowed with those two before. Similarly, at the moments of <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding cessation and path, only <s>nirodha</s>- and <s>mārgajñāna</s> increase — this should be stated. But one who is free from desire is additionally endowed with <s>paracittajñāna</s> everywhere — at the moment of <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> regarding suffering up to the moment of <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding the path, one is also endowed with <s>paracittajñāna</s> along with those knowledges as stated — this should be understood. But at the moment of <s>anvayajñāna</s> regarding the path, one who is not free from desire is endowed with those very seven. But one who is free from desire is endowed with eight — those [seven] plus <s>paracittajñāna</s>. One is endowed with <s>kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of destruction) and <s>anutpādajñāna</s> (knowledge of non-arising) only as an <s>arhat</s> — since this is easy to understand, it was not formulated as a verse — this should be understood.

body.text: iti. iha dvividhā bhāvanādhikṛtā. pratilaṃbhabhāvanā niṣevaṇabhāvanā. pratilaṃbhabhāvanā prāptitaḥ niṣevaṇabhāvanā saṃmukhḥibhāvataḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Here two kinds of cultivation are intended: cultivation as attainment (<s>pratilaṃbhabhāvanā</s>) and cultivation as practice (<s>niṣevaṇabhāvanā</s>). Cultivation as attainment is from [initial] acquisition; cultivation as practice is from bringing face-to-face.

body.text: iti yāniyāny utpannāni tānitāni bhāvyaṃta iti. tadyathā duḥkhadharmajñānakṣāntāv utpannāyāṃ tajjātīyā kṣāntir evānāgatā bhāvyate. tadākārāś catvāra iti. kṣāṃtyākārā anityādyāś catvāraḥ sabhāgatvāt. nānye. evaṃ duḥkhe dharmajñāna utpanne tad evānāgataṃ bhāvyate. tadākārāś catvāra eva bhāvanāṃ gacchanti. evaṃ duḥkhānvayajñānakṣāṃtyādiṣu yojyaṃ. sabhāgajñānākārabhāvanaiveti. kasmāt [Tib. 298a] sabhāgajñānabhāvanā sabhāgākārabhāvanā ca darśanamārga eva bhavati. na bhāvanāmārga iti. kṣāṃtīnām aparipraśnaḥ. bhāvanāmārge tāsām abhāvāt. tāsām api vā praśnaḥ kartavyaḥ. tāsām api sabhāgabhāvanāt. na hi duḥkhakṣāntāv utpannāyāṃ samudayādiduḥkhakṣāntyākarā bhāvyante. udāharaṇamātrārthatvāt tu jñānaparipraśno na kṣāntiparipraśna iti. gotrāṇām apratilabdhatvād iti. sabhāgahetunām apratilabdhatvād ity arthaḥ. kathaṃ kṛtvā. duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntāv utpannāyāṃ tadgotraṃ tadākārāṇāṃ ca caturṇāṃ gotrāṇi labdhāni bhavanti. na duḥkhadharmajñānādīnāṃ. kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇam anityādīnāṃ ākārāṇām ekaikasminn ākāre saṃmukhībhūte pariśiṣṭānām ākārāṇāṃ gotrāṇi pratilabhyaṃte. yatas te bhāvanāṃ gacchanti. tulyālambanatayā sabhāgatvāt. sarveṣāṃ gotrāṇi pratilabdhāni bhavanti. evaṃ duḥkhe dharmajñāna utpanne yāvan mārge 'nvayajñānakṣāntāv utpannāyāṃ tadgotrāṇi tadākarāṇi ca caturṇāṃ
body.translated_text: that is, whichever [knowledges] have arisen — those are cultivated. For example, when the <s>duḥkhadharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patience of dharma-knowledge of suffering) has arisen, only the future patience of the same type is cultivated. Its aspects are four — the aspects of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) — impermanence and the rest, four in number — because of being homogeneous. Not others. Similarly, when the <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding suffering has arisen, only that very future [<s>dharmajñāna</s>] is cultivated. Its aspects — four only — undergo cultivation. Similarly, this should be connected for the <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> regarding suffering and the rest. "Only the cultivation of homogeneous knowledge and aspects" — why does the cultivation of homogeneous knowledge and homogeneous aspects occur only in the path of seeing, [Tib. 298a] not in the path of cultivation? The question about <s>kṣānti</s>s (patiences) need not be raised — because of their non-existence in the path of cultivation. Or the question about <s>kṣānti</s>s should also be raised — because they too undergo homogeneous cultivation. For when the <s>duḥkhakṣānti</s> (patience regarding suffering) has arisen, aspects of <s>samudaya</s> (origination) and the rest are not cultivated for the suffering-patience. This is because [the verse] is merely illustrative, so the question is about <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), not about <s>kṣānti</s>. "Because of the non-attainment of the lineages (<s>gotra</s>)" — the meaning is: because of the non-attainment of the homogeneous causes (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>). How so? When the <s>duḥkhadharmajñānakṣānti</s> has arisen, the lineage of that and the lineages of its four aspects are obtained — but not [the lineages] of <s>duḥkhadharmajñāna</s> and the rest. What, then, is the reason that, among the aspects of impermanence and the rest, when any one aspect has been brought face-to-face, the lineages of the remaining aspects are obtained, so that they undergo cultivation? Because of being homogeneous through having the same object-domain. The lineages of all are obtained. Similarly, when the <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding suffering has arisen, up to when the <s>mārgānvayajñānakṣānti</s> has arisen, the lineages of that and the four aspects

body.text: gotrāṇi labdhāni bhavantīti tad eva bhāvanāṃ gacchati nānyat. bhāvanāmārge tu punaḥ sarveṣāṃ jñānānāṃ sabhāgavisabhāgānāṃ tadākarāṇāṃ ca saṃmukhībhāvāt sarveṣāṃ hetavo labdhā bhavantīti. tadviśiṣṭā jñānākārā bhāvanāṃ gacchaṃty anāgatāḥ.
body.translated_text: are obtained — that alone undergoes cultivation, not another. But in the path of cultivation, because all knowledges — homogeneous and heterogeneous — and their aspects come face-to-face, the causes of all are obtained. Therefore, knowledges and aspects distinguished thereby undergo cultivation as future [dharmas].

body.text: ity alabdhapūrvaṃ. na dharmajñāneṣv akṛtsnasatyābhisamayād iti. [Tib. 298b] na hi tadānīṃ rūpārūpyāvacaraṃ duḥkaṃ parijñātaṃ samudayaḥ prahīṇas tannirodhaḥ sākṣātkṛta iti. mārgasya pūrvaṃ laukikena mārgeṇānabhisamitatvād iti. laukikamārgeṇa pūrvam anādigatisaṃsāre duḥkhasamudayanirodhā abhisamitāḥ. na tu saṃvṛtijñānena kadācin mārgo mārgādibhir ākārair abhisamitaḥ. tasmāt trayāṇām ekaikasya satyasyābhisamayānte bhāvanāṃ. gacchati. na mārgānvayajñāne. na tu mārgaḥ śakyate kṛtsno bhāvayitum iti. saṃmukhīkartum ity arthaḥ. samudayo 'pi tadā na sarvaḥ prahīṇa iti. nirodhamārgadarśanabhāvanāprahātavyaḥ. duḥkhaṃ punaḥ sarvaṃ traidhātukaṃ parijñātaṃ tasya parijñeyatvād ity ataḥ samudayam eva praticodyate. tatsatyadarśanaheya iti. samudayasatyadarśanaheya ity arthaḥ. bahugotratvād iti. ātmabhāvasaṃtatisāmānyaviśeṣo gotraṃ. tāni bahūni gotrāṇy asyeti bahugotro mārgaḥ. śrāvakagotrāt pratyekabuddhagotram anyat. tathā buddhagotraṃ. śrāvakagotram apy anyonyaṃ bhinnaṃ. mṛdvadhimātrādibhedāt. teṣāṃ kaścid eva darśanaheyapratipakṣo bhāvyate saṃmukhīkriyata ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: — that is, not previously obtained. 'Not at the <s>dharmajñāna</s>s, because of the incomplete realization of the truths' — for at that time, the suffering of the Form and Formless Realms has not been fully comprehended, the origination has not been abandoned, and the cessation of that has not been directly realized. 'Because the path was not previously realized through the mundane path' — through the mundane path, in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, suffering, origination, and cessation were realized. But by conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>), the path was never realized through aspects of path and the rest. Therefore, at the end of the realization of each of the three truths, it enters cultivation — not at the <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge of the path). 'But the path cannot be cultivated in its entirety' — the meaning is: it cannot be brought face-to-face. 'At that time, the origination too has not been entirely abandoned' — [the origination] to be abandoned by seeing and cultivation of cessation and the path. 'But all the suffering of the three realms has been fully comprehended, because it is to be fully comprehended' — therefore the objection is raised only against origination. 'To be abandoned by seeing of that truth' — the meaning is: to be abandoned by seeing of the truth of origination. 'Because of having many lineages (<s>gotra</s>)' — the lineage is the general and specific [character] of the continuity of the state of self (<s>ātmabhāva</s>). That which has many lineages is called the path of many lineages. The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> lineage is different from the <s>śrāvaka</s> lineage. Similarly the <s>Buddha</s> lineage. The <s>śrāvaka</s> lineage too is mutually different — because of the distinctions of dull, sharp, and the rest. Of those, only some antidote to what is abandoned by seeing is cultivated — the meaning is: brought face-to-face.

body.text: na mārgaḥ. śakyate kṛtsno bhāvayituṃ. darśanamārgaparivāratvād iti. darśanamārgasya [Tib. 299a] parivāraḥ saṃvṛtijñānam. ataḥ satyatrayāṃte eva darśanamārgo bhāvyate. na mārgasatyaṃte tasya bhāvanāmārgatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'The path cannot be cultivated in its entirety — because of being the retinue of the seeing path' — the retinue of the seeing path is conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>). Therefore, at the end of only three truths the seeing path is cultivated, not at the end of the truth of the path, because that [cultivation] belongs to the cultivation path.

body.text: sādhyatvād ajñāpakam iti. sādhyam idaṃ darśanamārgaparivāra eva. na bhāvanāmārgaparivāro 'pīti. vayaṃ hi bhāvanāmārgaparivāro 'pi tad iti brūmaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Because it is to be established, it is not indicative' — this [point] that it is only the retinue of the seeing path, not also the retinue of the cultivation path, is what is to be established. For we say that it is also the retinue of the cultivation path.

body.text: satyālaṃbanaṃ viśiṣṭataram iti. darśanāvasthāyāṃ yal laukikaṃ pūrvam āsīta. tato viśiṣṭam eva ca laukikam ity abhiprāyaḥ. yas tatsaṃmukhībhāvasamarthāśrayalābha iti. tasya saṃvṛtijñānasya saṃmukhībhāve samarthāśrayasya yo lābhaḥ. eṣa eva tasya lābhaḥ. nārthāntarabhūta iti. gotre 'bhilabdhe labdhaṃ gautrikam iti. gotraṃ tadutpādanasamartho hetuḥ. tatra bhavaṃ gautrikaṃ saṃvṛtijñānam. etad uktaṃ bhavati tatsaṃmukhībhāvasamarthāśrayalābhe tad api tenāśrayeṇotpadyamānaṃ labdhaṃ bhavatīti. atha kasmād
body.translated_text: 'Having the truths as its object-domain is more distinguished' — the intent is: what existed previously as mundane [knowledge] at the time of seeing — the mundane [knowledge] is indeed more distinguished than that. 'The one who obtains a basis capable of bringing that face-to-face' — the obtaining of a basis capable of bringing that conventional knowledge face-to-face — that very thing is its obtaining, not something different. 'When the lineage is obtained, what belongs to the lineage is obtained' — the lineage is a cause capable of producing that. What exists in that [lineage] — the conventional knowledge belonging to the lineage — is [also obtained]. What is said is this: when a basis capable of bringing that face-to-face is obtained, that too, being produced by that basis, is obtained. But why

body.text: evaṃ necchaṃti vaibhāṣikāḥ. darśanamārgalabhyaṃ tat. tasya kathaṃ bhāvanāmārge saṃmukhībhāvo bhaviṣyatīti. darśanamārge cotpattyanavakāśo 'syāsti tad anutpattidharmakam iti varṇayaṃte.
body.translated_text: do the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s not accept this? 'That is obtained through the seeing path. How will it come face-to-face in the cultivation path?' — thus [they argue]. And they explain that there is no opportunity for its arising in the seeing path — therefore it has the nature of never arising.

body.text: evaṃ yāvac caturthadhyānabhūmika iti vistaraḥ. prathamadhyānabhūmikaś ced bhavati tribhūmikaṃ bhāvyate. prathamadhyānabhūmikam anāgamyabhūmikaṃ [Tib. 299b] kāmāvacaraṃ ca. dhyanāṃtarabhūmikaś cec caturbhūmikaṃ bhāvyate. dhyānāntarabhūmikaṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikādīni ca pūrvoktāni evaṃ dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaś cet paṃcabhūmikaṃ. dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ yāvat kāmāvacaraṃ. tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikaś cet ṣaṭbhūmikaṃ. tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ yāvat kāmāvacaraṃ. caturthadhyānabhūmikaś ced bhavati saptabhūmikaṃ bhāvyate. caturthadhyānabhūmikaṃ. yāvat kāmāvacaraṃ ceti. ekasya parisaṃkhyānāt siddhaṃ bhavati śeṣaṃ catvārīti. nirodhe 'ntyam evāntyam eva ca nirodha ity ubhayāvadhāraṇāc cheṣaṃ catuḥsmṛtyupasthānam iti siddhaṃ bhavati. duḥkhe 'bhisamite yat saṃvṛtijñānaṃ bhāvyate. tac catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni duḥkhasya kāyādisvabhāvatvāt. evaṃ samudaye 'pi vaktavyaṃ. tat satyākāram eveti. duḥkhe 'bhisamite yat saṃvṛtijñānaṃ bhāvyate. tat pratyekam anityaduḥkhaśūyānātmākāraṃ. evaṃ samudaye nirodhe ca vaktavyaṃ. ālambanam asya tad eveti. tasyākārasya tadālambanatvāt. prāyogikam iti. nopapattilabhyaḥ. catuḥpaṃcaskaṃdhasvabhāvānīti. kāmāvacaram [Tib. 300a] anuparivartakarūpābhāvāc catuḥskaṃdhasvabhāvaṃ. vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānaskaṃdhasvabhāvam ity arthaḥ. ūrdhvabhūmikāni tu paṃcasvabhāvāni dhyānasaṃvaralakṣaṇarūpaskandhasvabhāvāt.
body.translated_text: Thus up to 'belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground' — in detail. If it belongs to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, what is cultivated pertains to three grounds: the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, the <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary) ground, and the Desire Realm. If it belongs to the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> ground, what is cultivated pertains to four grounds: the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> ground and the previously stated first <s>dhyāna</s> ground and the rest. Similarly, if it belongs to the second <s>dhyāna</s> ground, five grounds [are cultivated]. The second <s>dhyāna</s> ground up to the Desire Realm. If to the third <s>dhyāna</s> ground, six grounds — the third <s>dhyāna</s> ground up to the Desire Realm. If it belongs to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground, what is cultivated pertains to seven grounds — the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground up to the Desire Realm. 'Because of the reckoning of one, the remaining four are established' — and because of the delimitation 'the last alone' and 'cessation alone' — through both delimitations, the remaining [cultivation pertaining to] the four foundations of mindfulness is established. When suffering has been realized, whatever conventional knowledge is cultivated — that consists of four foundations of mindfulness, because suffering has the nature of body and the rest. Similarly, it should be stated regarding origination as well. 'It has the aspect of just that truth' — when suffering has been realized, whatever conventional knowledge is cultivated, it has the aspects of impermanent, suffering, empty, and non-self individually. Similarly, it should be stated regarding origination and cessation. 'The object-domain of this is that very thing' — because the aspect has that as its object-domain. 'Produced by practice' (<s>prāyogika</s>) — not obtained by birth (<s>upapatilabhya</s>). 'Having the nature of four or five aggregates' — in the Desire Realm, because of the absence of accompanying form (<s>anuparivartaka-rūpa</s>), it has the nature of four aggregates — the meaning is: having the nature of the feeling, perception, formation, and consciousness aggregates. But those belonging to higher grounds have the nature of five [aggregates], because of form-aggregate nature characterized by the <s>dhyāna</s> restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>).

body.text: (VII.25, 26) dve jñāne pratyutpanne iti. anvayajñānaṃ mārgajñānaṃ ca. mārgānvayajñānasya tadubhayasvabhāvatvāt. anāgatāni ṣaḍ iti. dharmajñānādīni. na saṃvṛtijñānaṃ bhāvyate. labdhapūrvatvāt vakṣyati hi
body.translated_text: (VII.25, 26) 'Two knowledges are present' — <s>anvayajñāna</s> and <s>mārgajñāna</s>, because the <s>mārgānvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge of the path) has the nature of both. 'Six are future' — <s>dharmajñāna</s> and the rest. Conventional knowledge is not cultivated — because it was previously obtained. For he will state:

children.translated_text: 'What was previously obtained is not cultivated' —

body.text: iti. na paracittajñānam avītarāgatvāt.
body.translated_text: thus. Not the knowledge of others' minds — because of not being dispassionate.

body.text: ekaprakāraprahāṇe yāvad aṣṭaprakāraprahāṇe. yāvan na vītarāgo bhavatīti. yāvan na prahīṇanavaprakāko bhavati. atrāntare prayogānantaryavimuktiviśeṣamārgeṣu bhāvyamāneṣu sapta jñānāni bhāvyante. dharmajñānādīni paracittajñānavarjitāni bhāvyante. laukikaś cet. yadi śāṃtādyudārādyākāro bhāvanāmārgaḥ saṃvṛtijñānaṃ pratyutpannaṃ. caturṇāṃ dharnajñānānām
body.translated_text: at the abandonment of one type, up to the abandonment of eight types — up to when one has not become dispassionate — up to when one has not abandoned the nine types. In this interval, when application, uninterrupted, liberation, and distinctive paths are being cultivated, seven knowledges are cultivated — <s>dharmajñāna</s> and the rest, excluding the knowledge of others' minds. 'If mundane' — if the cultivation path has aspects of peaceful and the rest, or coarse and the rest, conventional knowledge is present. 'Of the four <s>dharmajñāna</s>s'

body.text: iti. duḥkhasasmudayanirodhamārgadharmajñānānām anyatamat. anvayajñānānāṃ kāmadhātvapratipakṣatvān nānvayajñānānām anyatamat. paṃcasu cābhijñāsv iti. āsravakṣayābhijñanam apāsya. [Tib. 300b] caturṇām anvayajñānānām iti. duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgānvayajñānāṃ. dvayoś ca dharmajñānayor iti. nirodhamārgālaṃbanayos tridhātupratipakṣatvayogāt. saṃvṛtijñānaṃ na bhāvyate bhavāgrāpratipakṣatvād iti. saptabhūmivairāgye lokottare 'pi bhāvyamāne saṃvṛtijñānaṃ bhāvyate. saṃvṛtijñānam api hi tasya kleśaprakārasya pratipakṣo bhavati. na kevalaṃ lokottaram iti. saṃvṛtijñānam api tatra bhāvyate tajjātīyam. akopyaprativedhe tu na tathā pratipakṣarūpaṃ bhūtaṃ saṃvṛtijñānam asti. ato 'tra na bhāvyate. tatra kṣayajñānaṃ saptamam iti. ānantaryamārgasthitatvāt kṣayajñānaṃ tatra bhāvyate. nānutpādajñānaṃ na hy ānantaryamārgasthito 'kopyadharmā bhavati. akopyadharmaṇaś cānutpādajñānaṃ bhāvyata iti. bhavāgravairāgye vimuktimārgeṣv aṣṭāsu saptaiva jñānāni bhāvyanta iti. paracittajñānaṃ kathaṃ bhāvyate. ānantaryamārge pratiṣiddhaṃ paracittajñānaṃ na vimuktimārge. ataḥ ekaprakāre prahīṇe yāvad aṣṭaprakāre prahīṇe pūrvaparacittajñānaviśiṣṭaṃ paracittajñānaṃ bhāvyate. yat sa evaṃvidha āryapudgalas tato mārgād vyutthitaḥ saṃmukhīkuryāt. saṃtānaviśeṣād dhi paracittajñānaviśeṣa iṣyate.
body.translated_text: — that is, of the <s>dharmajñāna</s>s of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path, one or another [is cultivated]. Not one or another of the <s>anvayajñāna</s>s — because they are not antidotes of the Desire Realm. 'And in the five <s>abhijñā</s>s' — excluding the <s>abhijñā</s> of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>). 'Of four <s>anvayajñāna</s>s' — the <s>anvayajñāna</s>s of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path. 'And of two <s>dharmajñāna</s>s' — those having cessation and the path as their object-domain, because of having the fitness of being antidotes of all three realms. 'Conventional knowledge is not cultivated, because of not being the antidote of the Peak of Existence' — even when the dispassion from the seven grounds is being cultivated through the supramundane [path], conventional knowledge is [also] cultivated. For conventional knowledge too is an antidote of that type of affliction — not only the supramundane. Therefore conventional knowledge is also cultivated there, being of the same class. But at the penetration of the unshakable [nature], conventional knowledge of such an antidotal form does not exist — therefore it is not cultivated there. 'Therein, the knowledge of destruction is the seventh' — because of being in the state of the uninterrupted path, the knowledge of destruction is cultivated there. Not the knowledge of non-arising — for one in the state of the uninterrupted path is not [yet] of unshakable nature. And the knowledge of non-arising is cultivated for one of unshakable nature. 'At the dispassion from the Peak of Existence, in the eight liberation paths, just seven knowledges are cultivated.' How is the knowledge of others' minds cultivated? The knowledge of others' minds is prohibited in the uninterrupted path but not in the liberation path. Therefore, when one type has been abandoned up to when eight types have been abandoned, a knowledge of others' minds more distinguished than the previous one is cultivated — which such a Noble person, having emerged from that path, would bring face-to-face. For the distinction of the knowledge of others' minds is accepted because of the distinction of the [mental] continuum.
