body.text: ubhayor api sarāgavītarāgayor [Tib. 301a] vimuktimārge bhāvaneti. prayogamārge tu tayor iti. tayor eva sarāgavītarāgayoḥ saṃvṛtijñānasyāpi bhāvanā. vimuktimārge kim arthaṃ vivādaḥ. darśanamārgasādṛśyāt tatra tad ābhisamayāntikavad bhāvyeta ity eke. na cābhisamayo 'sti darśanamārgasādṛśyaṃ cety apara ity evaṃ vivādaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'For both — with desire and dispassionate — cultivation in the liberation path' — but in the application path, of those two. Of those very two — with desire and dispassionate — there is also cultivation of conventional knowledge. 'Why is there dispute regarding the liberation path?' Because of similarity with the seeing path, it would be cultivated there as at the end of realization — [say] some. But there is no realization, though there is similarity with the seeing path — [say] others. Such is the dispute.

body.text: (VII.28-30) ṣaṇṇāṃ bhāvanā pūrvavad iti. dharmānvayaduḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgajñānānāṃ. na saṃvṛtijñānasya darśanamārgasādṛśyād iti. kim atra darśanamārgeṇa sādṛśyaṃ. phalaprāptiḥ. yathā darśanamārgeṇa srotaāpattiphalaṃ vā sakṛdāgāmyanāgāmiphalaṃ vā prāpyate. evam anenāpy ānantaryamārgeṇa śaikṣasya śaikṣendriyottāpanāyāṃ tīkṣṇendriyasaṃgṛhītāni saṃskṛtāni srotaāpattiphalādīni prāpyaṃte. darśanamārge cānantaryamārgāvasthāyāṃ na saṃvṛtijñānabhāvanāsti evam ihāpi. ity evaṃ darśanamārgasādṛśyād ānantaryamārge na saṃvṛtijñānasya bhāvanā. tathaiveti. dharmānvayaduḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgajñānānām. atrāpi saṃvṛtijñānaṃ na bhāvyate bhavāgrāpratipakṣatvāt. na paracittajñānaṃ sarvānantaryamārge pratiṣedhatvāt.
body.translated_text: (VII.28-30) 'Cultivation of six as before' — of <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>duḥkha</s>-, <s>samudaya</s>-, <s>nirodha</s>-, and <s>mārgajñāna</s>. 'Not of conventional knowledge, because of similarity with the seeing path' — what is the similarity with the seeing path here? The attainment of a fruit. Just as through the seeing path, the fruit of stream-entry or the fruits of once-returning and non-returning are attained, so too through this uninterrupted path, in the heating of faculties of a learner, the fruits of stream-entry and the rest included in sharp faculties and conditioned are attained. And in the seeing path, at the stage of the uninterrupted path, there is no cultivation of conventional knowledge — similarly here too. Thus, because of similarity with the seeing path, in the uninterrupted path there is no cultivation of conventional knowledge. 'Likewise' — of the <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>duḥkha</s>-, <s>samudaya</s>-, <s>nirodha</s>-, and <s>mārgajñāna</s>s. Here too conventional knowledge is not cultivated, because of not being the antidote of the Peak of Existence. Not the knowledge of others' minds — because it is prohibited in all uninterrupted paths.

body.text: [Tib. 301b] kiṃ punaḥ śeṣam iti vistaraḥ. kathaṃ kāmavairāgye navamo vimuktimārgaḥ śeṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'What, then, remains?' — in detail. How is the ninth liberation path in the dispassion from the Desire Realm a remainder?

children.translated_text: 'In the cultivation path with desire, above that seven cultivations' —

body.text: vacanāt. saptabhūmivairāgyābhijñāvyavakīrṇabhāviteṣu vimuktimārgāḥ śeṣāḥ.
body.translated_text: from this statement. The liberation paths in the dispassion from the seven grounds, the <s>abhijñā</s>s, and the intermixed cultivations — these are the remainders.

children.translated_text: 'In the victory over seven grounds, <s>abhijñā</s>s, attainment of unshakable [nature], and non-intermixed cultivation —'

body.text: iti vacanāt. tathā yo 'kopyatāṃ saṃcarati. tasyāpy ante vimuktimārge daśānāṃ bhāvaneti vacanāt. aṣṭau vimuktimārgāḥ śeṣā bhavanti. sarve ca vītarāgasyānāgāminaḥ prayogaviśeṣamārgāḥ śeṣās teṣāṃ bhāvanāyām avacanāt. śaikṣasyaivam iti yad apadiṣṭaṃ
body.translated_text: from this statement. Similarly, for one who transfers to the unshakable state — for that one too, at the end, in the liberation path, there is the cultivation of ten [knowledges] — from this statement. Eight liberation paths are the remainders. And all the application and distinctive paths of a dispassionate non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) are remainders — because of no statement about their cultivation. 'For the learner thus' — what has been indicated as:

body.text: kathaṃ punaḥ evam aviśeṣite viśeṣapratipattir labhyate. aśaikṣasyāvaśyaṃ navadaśajñānabhāvanāyogāt. ata evāhāśaikṣasya punar abhijñādīti. ādiśabdena vyavakīrṇabhāvanādhyānādigrahaṇam. abhijñābhinirhāre vyavakīrṇabhāvanāyāṃ ca ye prayogavimuktiviśeṣamārgāḥ. teṣu yadi samayavimukto navajñānāni bhāvyante. anutpādajñānaṃ hitvā. yady akopyadharmā [Tib. 302a] daśa tad eva prakṣipya. aṣṭau nava ceti. samayavimuktasyāṣṭau akopyadharmaṇo nava paracittajñānaṃ hitvā. tasyānantaryamārgeṣu pratiṣedhāt. dvayos tv abhijñāvimuktimārgayor iti. divyaśrotracakṣurabhijñāvimuktimārgayoḥ.
body.translated_text: but how, when no distinction has been made, is the specific understanding obtained? Because for a non-learner there is necessarily the fitness for the cultivation of nine or ten knowledges. Therefore he says: 'For a non-learner, <s>abhijñā</s>s and the rest.' By the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), the inclusion of intermixed cultivation of <s>dhyāna</s>s and the rest [is indicated]. In the accomplishment of <s>abhijñā</s>s and in intermixed cultivation, whatever application, liberation, and distinctive paths [exist] — in those, if one is occasionally liberated (<s>samayavimukta</s>), nine knowledges are cultivated, excluding the knowledge of non-arising. If one is of unshakable nature (<s>akopyadharman</s>), ten [knowledges are cultivated], including that very [knowledge of non-arising]. Eight and nine — for the occasionally liberated, eight; for one of unshakable nature, nine — excluding the knowledge of others' minds, because it is prohibited in the uninterrupted paths. 'But for both, in the <s>abhijñā</s> liberation paths' — in the liberation paths of the divine ear and divine eye <s>abhijñā</s>s.

body.text: iti vacanāt tadvimuktimārgāv avyākṛtau. na cāvyākṛtasya dharmasyānāgatabhāvanāsti. pṛthagjanasya tu kāmatridhyānavairāgya iti. caturthadhyānāgrahaṇam. yasmāc caturthadhyānavairāgye yo 'ntyo vimuktimārgaḥ. tatra maulākāśānantyāyatanapratilambhaḥ. na cārūpyadhātusaṃgṛhītaṃ paracittajñānam asti. rūpātītārthābhiniṣpādyatvāt. prayogābhijñātrayo vimuktimārgapramāṇādiguṇābhinirhāreṣv iti. prayogamārgāś cābhijñātrayavimuktimārgāś cāpramāṇādiguṇābhinirhārāś ceti vigrahaḥ. ādiśabdena vimokṣābhibhvāyatanādiguṇagrahaṇam. apramāṇādīnāṃ guṇānām abhinirhāra iti. dhyānabhūmikagrahaṇaṃ sāmantakanirāsārthaṃ. [Tib. 302b] tatra hi paracittajñānaṃ nāsti. abhijñātrayam ṛddhiviṣayābhijñā pūrvenivāsānusmṛtyabhijñā cetaḥparyāyābhijñā ca. teṣu ca kāmatridhyānavairāgyāntyavimuktimārgeṣu
body.translated_text: — from this statement, those two liberation paths are indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>). And there is no cultivation of the future of an indeterminate <s>dharma</s>. 'But for an ordinary person, dispassion from the Desire Realm and the three <s>dhyāna</s>s' — the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is not included. Because the final liberation path in dispassion from the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> — therein there is the attainment of the fundamental Infinity of Space sphere (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>). And there is no knowledge of others' minds included in the Formless Realm — because it accomplishes a purpose that transcends form. 'In the preparatory [paths], the three <s>abhijñā</s> liberation paths, the accomplishment of the <s>apramāṇa</s>s and other qualities' — the analysis is: the preparatory paths, and the three <s>abhijñā</s> liberation paths, and the accomplishments of the <s>apramāṇa</s>s and other qualities. By the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), the qualities of liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), overmastering bases (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>), and the rest are included. The accomplishment of the qualities such as the <s>apramāṇa</s>s and the rest. The mention of '<s>dhyāna</s>-ground' is for the purpose of excluding the access concentration (<s>sāmantaka</s>). [Tib. 302b] For there, knowledge of others' minds does not exist. The three <s>abhijñā</s>s are: the <s>abhijñā</s> of the domain of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiviṣaya</s>), the <s>abhijñā</s> of recollection of former lives (<s>pūrvenivāsānusmṛti</s>), and the <s>abhijñā</s> of knowledge of others' mental dispositions (<s>cetaḥparyāya</s>). And in those final liberation paths of dispassion from the Desire Realm and the three <s>dhyāna</s>s

body.text: dhyānabhūmikeṣu cābhijñātrayavimuktimārgeṣu. apramāṇavimokṣābhibhvāyatanakṛtsnāyatanādiguṇābhinirhāreṣu ca. dhyānabhūmikeṣv eva prayogavimuktiviśeṣamārgeṣu saṃvṛtijñānam anāgataṃ bhāvyate. yat tatsaṃgṛhītaṃ paracittajñānaṃ ca viśiṣṭam eva bhāvyate. yat tadguṇaviśeṣalābhī saṃmukhīkuryāt. anyatra nirvedhabhāgiyebhya ūṣmagatādibhyaḥ. teṣu hi nirvebhabhāgīyeṣu paracittajñānaṃ na bhāvyate. kiṃ kāraṇam ity āha. darśanamārgaparivāratvād iti. yathā darśanamārge paracittajnānaṃ na bhāvyate. tathā tatparivāre 'pi na bhāvyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. anyatreti vistaraḥ. pṛthagjanasyaivānyatrāpūrvamārgalābhe kāmatridhyānavairāgye 'ntyavimuktimārgān hitvā yaḥ prayogānantaryavimuktimārgalābhaḥ. tasminn anyatrāpūrvamārgalabhe saṃvṛtijñānam evānāgataṃ bhāvyate. na paracittajñānaṃ [Tib. 303a] tathābhijñātrayapramāṇādiguṇābhinirhāreṣu ya ānantaryamārgalābhaḥ. tasmiṃś cānyatrāpūrvamārgalābhe saṃvṛtijñānam evānāgataṃ bhāvyate. prayogamārgeṣu na paracittajñānaṃ tadapratipakṣatvāt.
body.translated_text: — and in the three <s>abhijñā</s> liberation paths belonging to the <s>dhyāna</s>-ground, and in the accomplishments of the qualities of <s>apramāṇa</s>s, liberations, overmastering bases, <s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>s, and the rest — in the preparatory, liberation, and special paths belonging to the <s>dhyāna</s>-ground alone, conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>) is cultivated as future. And the knowledge of others' minds included in that [conventional knowledge] is cultivated only when it is special — when one who has obtained that special quality would bring it face-to-face. Except for the penetration-conducive [roots] (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) — the heat stage (<s>uṣmagata</s>) and the rest. For in those penetration-conducive [roots], knowledge of others' minds is not cultivated. For what reason? — he says: 'Because of being the retinue of the seeing path' — just as in the seeing path, knowledge of others' minds is not cultivated, so too in its retinue it is not cultivated — this is the intent. 'Except' — and so forth in detail. For an ordinary person alone, except for the attainment of a previously unattained path — setting aside dispassion from the Desire Realm and the three <s>dhyāna</s>s, the final liberation paths — whatever attainment of preparatory, uninterrupted, and liberation paths there is — in that, except for the attainment of a previously unattained path, only conventional knowledge is cultivated as future — not knowledge of others' minds. [Tib. 303a] Similarly, in the three <s>abhijñā</s>s and the accomplishments of the qualities of <s>apramāṇa</s>s and the rest, whatever attainment of uninterrupted paths there is — in that too, except for the attainment of a previously unattained path, only conventional knowledge is cultivated as future. In the preparatory paths, not knowledge of others' minds — because of not being its antidote.

body.text: (VII.31, 32) atha kasmin mārga iti laukike lokottare vā. yadbhūmiko mārga iti. anāgamyādikaḥ sāsravo 'nāsravo vā. yāṃ ca bhūmiṃ prathamato labhata iti. vairāgyataḥ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ yāvad bhavāgraṃ tadbhūmikam ity arthaḥ. kathaṃ kṛtvā. yady anāgamyabhūmisaṃniśrayeṇa hi laukikena mārgeṇa kāmadhātuvairāgyāt prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ labhate anāgmyabhūmikaṃ sāmantakasvabhāvaṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ ca maulasvabhāvaṃ. navame vimuktimārge saṃvṛtijñānaṃ bhāvyate. evaṃ dvitīyadhyānasāmantakasaṃniśrayeṇa prathamadhyānavairāgyāt dvitīyaṃ dhyānaṃ labhate. tathaiva dvitīyadhyānasāmantakasaṃgṛhītaṃ mauladvitīyadhyānasaṃgṛhītaṃ ca bhāvyate. evaṃ yāvad yadi naivasaṃjñāsaṃjñāyatanasāmantakasaṃniśrayeṇākiṃcanyāyatanavairāgyād bhavāgraṃ labhata iti vistareṇa yojyaṃ. yadāpy anāsravānāgamyabhūmisaṃniśrayeṇa kāmadhātuvairāgyāt [Tib. 303b] prathamadhyānaṃ labhate. tadāpi tathaiva tatsaṃvṛtijñānaṃ bhāvyate. yadāpi maulaprathamadhyānabhūmikasaṃniśrayeṇa prathamadhyānavairāyānāsravsaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ labhate. tadāpi prathamadhyānaprathamaprakārapratipakṣabhūtaṃ yāvan navamapratipakṣabhūtaṃ dvitīyadhyānasāmantakasaṃgṛhītaṃ saṃvṛtijñānaṃ labhate. sā hi prathamato bhūmis tadā labhyate. navame tu vimuktimārge mauladvitīyasaṃgṛhītam api saṃvṛtijñānam anāgataṃ bhāvyate. evam anāsravadhyānāntarabhūmisaṃniśrayeṇa yāvad anāsravākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmisaṃniśrayeṇa saṃvṛtijñānabhāvanā yojya.
body.translated_text: (VII.31, 32) Now, on what path? — on the mundane or supramundane. 'Whatever ground the path belongs to' — the access concentration (<s>anāgamya</s>) and the rest, whether contaminated or uncontaminated. 'And whatever ground one first attains' — the meaning is: belonging to that ground which one first attains through dispassion — the first <s>dhyāna</s>, up to the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). How is this? If one, relying on the access concentration ground, through the mundane path, from dispassion with the Desire Realm, attains the first <s>dhyāna</s> — [both] that belonging to the access concentration ground, having the nature of the preliminary, and that belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, having the nature of the fundamental — in the ninth liberation path, conventional knowledge is cultivated. Similarly, relying on the preliminary of the second <s>dhyāna</s>, from dispassion with the first <s>dhyāna</s>, one attains the second <s>dhyāna</s>. Just so, what is included in the preliminary of the second <s>dhyāna</s> and what is included in the fundamental second <s>dhyāna</s> is cultivated. Thus, up to: if, relying on the preliminary of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, from dispassion with the Nothingness sphere, one attains the Peak of Existence — this should be connected in detail. And even when, [Tib. 303b] relying on the uncontaminated access concentration ground, from dispassion with the Desire Realm, one attains the first <s>dhyāna</s> — then too, just so, that conventional knowledge is cultivated. And even when, relying on the fundamental first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, from dispassion with the first <s>dhyāna</s>, one attains the uncontaminated first <s>dhyāna</s> — then too, one obtains the conventional knowledge included in the preliminary of the second <s>dhyāna</s>, being the antidote of the first type up to the ninth type of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. For that ground is first attained at that time. And in the ninth liberation path, the conventional knowledge included in the fundamental second [<s>dhyāna</s>] too is cultivated as future. Thus, the cultivation of conventional knowledge relying on the uncontaminated intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> ground, up to relying on the uncontaminated Nothingness sphere ground, should be connected.

body.text: yasyā bhūmer vairāgrāya.
body.translated_text: for the dispassion from which ground.

body.text: yasyā bhūmer lābho yallābhaḥ.
body.translated_text: the attainment of which ground is the attainment of which.

body.text: bhayatrā-
body.translated_text: 'in both' —

body.text: ca tato
body.translated_text: 'and from that' —

body.text: 'nāsravajñānaṃ. katham iti vṛttyā vyācaṣṭe. yadbhūmivairāgyāyāpi hi na kevalaṃ yadbhūmika ity apiśabdaḥ. dvividho 'pi mārgo bhavatīti. laukiko lokottaraś ca. prayogamārgādi ādiśabdenānantaryavimuktiviśeṣamārgagrahaṇaṃ. yāṃ ca bhūmiṃ labhate vairāgyata iti. uparibhūmikaṃ. tadbhūmikāny adhobhūmikāni vānāsravāṇi bhāvanāṃ gacchanti. tadyathā dvitīyam anāsravaṃ dhyānaṃ niśritya tṛtīyadhyānavairāgyaṃ [Tib. 304a] karoti. yadbhūmiko mārgo dvitīyadhyānabhūmikas tadbhūmikam anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvanāṃ gacchati. yasyāś ca bhūmervairāgyaṃ karoti tṛtīyāyā bhūmes tadbhūmikaṃ tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ navame vimuktimārge 'nāsravaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvanāṃ gacchati. adhobhūmikaṃ ca prathamadhyānabhūmikam anāgamyabhūmikaṃ vānāsravaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvanāṃ gacchati. adhobhūmikam api hi tatprayogamārgādikaṃ saṃbhavāmi tajjātīyam iti bhāvanāṃ gacchati. atha tu tṛtīyadhyānasāmantakaṃ niśritya dvitīyadhyānavairāgyaṃ karoti. tatrāṣṭāsv ānantaryamārgeṣu vimuktimārge ca tasya sāmantakasya sāsravatvāt tadbhūmikam anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ na bhāvanāṃ gacchati. abhāvāt. adhobhūmikaṃ tu tajjātīyaṃ dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ dhyānāntarabhūmikaṃ prathamadhyānabhūmikam anāgamyabhūmikaṃ ca tajjātīyam anāsravaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvanāṃ gacchati. evam anyatrāpi yojyam eṣā dig iti. sāsravāś ca kṣayajñāna iti. anāsravāś ceti caśabdaḥ. yān guṇān arhadbhūtvā saṃmukhīkuryāt te sāsravās tasyām avasthāyāṃ. bhāvanāṃ gacchaṃti. apramāṇavimokṣādaya iti. ādiśabdenābhibhvāyatanakṛtsnāyatanādayo gṛhyante. ucchvasaṃtīva peḍāsādharmyeṇeti. [Tib. 304b] yā peḍā rajjvā nipīḍya baddhā. sā rajjūcchedād ucchvasatīva peḍocyate. ucchvastīva pratirūpakaśabdābhidhānāt. tasya rajjūcchedād ucchvasantīva peḍāyāḥ sādharmyeṇa. yathāsau rajjvā nipīḍya baddhā
body.translated_text: — uncontaminated knowledge. How? — he explains by the method of application (<s>vṛtti</s>). 'For the dispassion from which ground too' — not only that belonging to that ground — [this is indicated by] the word 'too' (<s>api</s>). 'The path is also twofold' — mundane and supramundane. By the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>) after 'preparatory path,' the uninterrupted, liberation, and special paths are included. 'And whatever ground one attains through dispassion' — the upper ground. 'The uncontaminated [knowledges] belonging to that ground, belonging to lower grounds, or [both], go to cultivation.' For example, relying on the uncontaminated second <s>dhyāna</s>, one performs dispassion from the third <s>dhyāna</s>. [Tib. 304a] The path belonging to that ground — the second <s>dhyāna</s> ground — the uncontaminated knowledge belonging to that ground goes to cultivation. And the uncontaminated knowledge belonging to the ground from which one becomes dispassionate — the third ground — that belonging to the third <s>dhyāna</s> ground goes to cultivation in the ninth liberation path. And the uncontaminated knowledge belonging to a lower ground — the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground or the access concentration ground — also goes to cultivation. For indeed, the lower-ground preparatory paths and the rest, being of the same kind as that, also go to cultivation. But when one relies on the preliminary of the third <s>dhyāna</s> and performs dispassion from the second <s>dhyāna</s> — therein, in the eight uninterrupted paths and the liberation path, because that preliminary is contaminated, the uncontaminated knowledge belonging to that ground does not go to cultivation — because of its non-existence. But the lower-ground [uncontaminated knowledge] of the same kind — belonging to the second <s>dhyāna</s> ground, the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> ground, the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, and the access concentration ground — the uncontaminated knowledge of the same kind does go to cultivation. Similarly, this should be connected elsewhere too — this is the indication. 'And contaminated [knowledges] — the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>)' — the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) means: and uncontaminated [ones too]. Whatever qualities one would bring face-to-face having become an <s>arhat</s> — those contaminated ones, in that stage, go to cultivation — the <s>apramāṇa</s>s, liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), and the rest. By the word 'and the rest,' the overmastering bases (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>), <s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>s, and the rest are included. 'They breathe freely, as it were, like a basket' — [Tib. 304b] a basket (<s>peḍā</s>) that was pressed and bound with a rope — when the rope is cut, it breathes freely, as it were — is said to breathe freely. It breathes freely, as it were — because of the expression by a metaphorical word. Because of the similarity with the basket that breathes freely when the rope is cut — just as that basket, pressed and bound by a rope

body.text: peḍā rajjūcchedād ucchvasatīva. evaṃ yathoktā aśubhādayo guṇā vajropamena samādhinā kleśaprāptirajjūcchedād aśailṣasaṃtāne vartsyanta ucchvasantīva. ucchvāsasya prāṇidharmatvād aupamikaṃ. kasmād ity āha. svacittādhirājyaprāptasyeti sarvaṃ. sarveṣām rājñām adhiko rājādhirājaḥ. tadbhāva ādhirājyaṃ. svacitte 'dhirājyaṃ kleśaparādhīnatāvigamāt. svacittaiśvaryam ity arthaḥ. tatprāptasyārhataḥ prāptibhiḥ prābhṛtasthānīyābhiḥ sarveṣāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratyudgamanānte guṇā bhāvanāṃ gacchanti. ādhirājye prāptau kasyacid rājādhirājasya prābhṛtena vastrādinā viṣayāṇāṃ janapadānāṃ. yathā pratyudgamanaṃ. tadvat tad eva kleśaprāptirajjūcchede sati svaprāptilābhāt ucchvasantīva guṇā uttaptatarāṇāṃ teṣāṃ prāptir utpadyata ity arthaḥ. kāmadhātāv arhattvaprāptāv evāśubhādayo yathāsaṃbhavaṃ śrutacintābhāvanāmayās traidhātukā bhāvanāṃ gacchanti. rūpārūpyadhātvos tv arhattvaprāptau yathākramaṃ dvidhātukaikadhātukāḥ. [Tib. 305a] evaṃ bhūmito 'pi boddhavyaṃ naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanopapannasyārhattvaprāptau tadbhūmikā eva ity avagaṃtavyaṃ. yat kiṃcil labhyata iti vistaraḥ. yad vihīnaṃ punar labhyate saṃmukhīkriyate saṃsārocitaṃ. na tad anāgataṃ bhāvyate. bhāvitotsṛṣṭatvāt saṃsāre. yad evātra dhyānāpramāṇādyanucitaṃ saṃsāre viśiṣṭām anāsravāṇuguṇaṃ. tat saṃmukhībhāve tajjātīyam evānāgataṃ viśiṣṭaṃ bhāvyata iyt ācāryo darśayati. ācāryasaṃghabhadro 'py etam evārthaṃ vyācaṣṭe. labdhapūrvaṃ na bhāvyate. yat pratilabdhavihīnaṃ punar labhyate na tad bhāvyaṃ. arthād gamyate yad alabdhapūrvaṃ labhyate tad bhāvyate. yatnābhimukhīkaraṇāt. apratiprasrabdho hi mārgo yatnenābhimukhīkriyata iti. tadāvedhasya balavattvād anāgato bhāvanāṃ gacchati. pratiprasrabdhapūrvas tv ayatnena saṃmukhībhavati. bhāvitapratiprasrabdhatvāt kṛtakṛtyadattaphalatvāc ca vegahīna iti tatsaṃmukhībhāvad anāgato na bhāvyata iti. yo 'nāgato yatnena janyate. sa bhāvyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. tad evaṃ sati yad uktaṃ saṃvṛtijñānaṃ tāvad iti vistareṇa. tad āryasaṃtānapatitam eva gṛhyate saṃsārānucitatvād iti ācāryavasumitreṇātra likhitam. atra kila vaibhāṣikā āhuḥ. naitad evaṃ. [Tib. 305b] kutaḥ. yasmād alabdham eva tad bhavati tyaktatvāt. tasmād bhāvitotsṛṣṭasyāpi punarlābhe bhavaty eva bhāvaneti. kathaṃ tad apūrvaṃ bhavati yāvatā labdhapūrvam iti. na hy evaṃvidhaṃ loke pūrvaṃ prasiddham iti. apare punar vyācakṣate. ekaṃ janmedam adhikṛyoktam na janmāntaraṃ. yad vihīnam asminn eva janmani punar labhyate. na tad bhāvyate. bhāvitotsṛṣṭatvāt. janmāntare tu yal labhyate. tad bhāvyate. na labhyate
body.translated_text: breathes freely, as it were, when the rope is cut — so the qualities such as the <s>aśubha</s> (impurity meditation) and the rest as described will exist in the non-learner's (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) continuum, breathing freely, as it were, through the cutting of the rope of the acquisition of afflictions by the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s>. Because breathing is a property of living beings, [the expression is] figurative. Why? — he says: 'Because of having attained sovereignty over one's own mind' — all of this. A king over (<s>adhi</s>) all kings (<s>rāja</s>) is a great king (<s>rājādhirāja</s>). His state is sovereignty (<s>ādhirājya</s>). Sovereignty over one's own mind — because of the departure from subjugation to afflictions — means mastery over one's own mind — this is the meaning. For that <s>arhat</s> who has attained that, through acquisitions (<s>prāpti</s>) that serve as offerings, at the conclusion of the reception of all wholesome <s>dharma</s>s, the qualities go to cultivation. Just as when sovereignty is attained, for a certain great king, through offerings of cloth and the like from the provinces and districts — just as there is a reception — so too, when the rope of the acquisition of afflictions is cut, because of obtaining one's own acquisitions, the qualities breathe freely, as it were — the meaning is: the acquisitions of those qualities, which have been further heated, arise. When <s>arhat</s>ship is attained in the Desire Realm alone, the [qualities of] <s>aśubha</s> and the rest, as applicable, born of hearing, reflection, and cultivation, belonging to the three realms, go to cultivation. But when <s>arhat</s>ship is attained in the Form and Formless Realms, [Tib. 305a] respectively belonging to two realms or one realm. Thus one should understand with respect to the grounds too — when one is born in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception and attains <s>arhat</s>ship, only those belonging to that ground — this should be understood. 'Whatever is obtained' — and so forth in detail. Whatever was lost and is obtained again — whatever is brought face-to-face that was practiced in <s>saṃsāra</s> — that is not cultivated as future. Because it was cultivated and discarded in <s>saṃsāra</s>. But whatever here — such as <s>dhyāna</s>s, <s>apramāṇa</s>s, and the rest — was not practiced in <s>saṃsāra</s>, being special, following uncontaminated [qualities] — that, when brought face-to-face, the future of the same kind alone — [that which is] special — is cultivated — the <s>Ācārya</s> shows. <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> too explains this very meaning: 'What was previously obtained is not cultivated.' What was obtained and lost and is obtained again — that is not to be cultivated. By implication it is understood that what is obtained for the first time is cultivated. Because of being brought face-to-face through effort. For indeed, a path that has not lapsed is brought face-to-face through effort. Because of the strength of its thrust, the future goes to cultivation. But what had previously lapsed comes face-to-face without effort — because of having been cultivated, lapsed, given fruit, and lost momentum — therefore, from its coming face-to-face, the future is not cultivated. That which, as future, is produced through effort — that is cultivated — this is the intent. This being so, what was stated — 'conventional knowledge, then' — and so forth in detail — that is taken as pertaining to a noble one's continuum alone, because of not being practiced in <s>saṃsāra</s> — thus <s>Ācārya Vasumitra</s> has written here. Herein, reportedly, the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s say: this is not so. [Tib. 305b] Why? Because that itself is not previously obtained — because of having been discarded. Therefore, even when what was cultivated and discarded is obtained again, there is indeed cultivation. 'How then is it not previously obtained, since it was previously obtained?' It is not well-known in the world that [something obtained and lost] is 'previously obtained.' Others, however, explain: this is stated with reference to one birth, not to another birth. What is lost in this very birth and obtained again — that is not cultivated — because of having been cultivated and discarded. But what is obtained in another birth — that is cultivated. It is not obtained

body.translated_text: — because of having forgotten the cultivation.

body.text: (VII.33) caturvidhā hi bhāvaneti. pratilambha eva bhāvanā pratilambhabhāvana. anāgataprāptir eva bhāvanety arthaḥ. evaṃ niṣevaṇam eva pratipakṣa eva vinirdhāvanam eva bhāvāneti vaktavyaṃ. kiṃ niṣevaṇaṃ. kiṃ ca yāvad vinirdhāvanam iti. niṣevaṇaṃ punaḥpunaḥsaṃmukhīkaraṇaṃ pratipakṣo mārgo yathoktaṃ sūtre. bhāvitakāyo bhāvitacitta iti. bhāvitapratipakṣakāyacitta ity arthaḥ. kāyapratipakṣaḥ punaś caturdhyānavirāgyāya yo mārgaḥ. tathā hy uktaṃ bhāvitakāyo bhikṣur ity ucyate bhāvitacitto bhāvitaśīlaḥ. katḥaṃ bhāvitakāyo bhavati. kāyād vigatarāgo vigataspṛho vigatapipāso vigatapremā vigataniyaṃtiḥ. atha vā yo 'sau rūparāgakṣayānantaryamārgaḥ. so 'nena vigatarāgo bhavatīty [Tib. 306a] āgamaḥ. vinirdhāvanaṃ kleśaprāptichedaḥ. anāgatānām eketi. pratilambhabhāvanā. pratyutpannānām ubhe iti. pratilambhaniṣevaṇabhāvane. tad evam iti vistaraḥ. yasmāt pratilambhaniṣevaṇabhāvane kuśalasaṃskṛtānām ity aviśeṣeṇoktaṃ sāsravāṇām anāsravaṇāṃ ca. pratipakṣavinirdhāvanabhāvane ca sāsravāṇāṃ dharmāṇām ity aviśeṣeṇoktaṃ kliṣṭānām akliṣṭānāṃ ca. tasmād evam itthaṃ kuśalasāsravāṇāṃ catasro bhāvanā bhavanti. yeṣāṃ bhāvanā kuśalatvāt pratilambhaniṣevaṇabhāvane bhavataḥ. sāsravatvāc ca pratipakṣavinirdhāvanabhāvane bhavata iti. ye tarhi na kuśalasāsravāḥ ye saṃskṛtā ye 'nāsravā ye ca kliṣṭāvyākṛtāḥ. teṣāṃ kati bhāvanā ity āhānāsravāṇāṃ dve iti. pratilambhaniṣevaṇabhāvane. kliṣṭāvyākṛtānāṃ ca. kiṃ dve bhāvane bhavataḥ. pratipakṣavinirdhāvanabhāvane iti.
body.translated_text: (VII.33) 'For cultivation is fourfold' — obtaining itself is cultivation — cultivation by obtaining (<s>pratilambhabhāvanā</s>). The meaning is: the acquisition of what is future is cultivation. Likewise, familiarization (<s>niṣevaṇa</s>) itself, antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) itself, and removal (<s>vinirdhāvana</s>) itself are cultivations — this should be stated. What is familiarization? And what, up to, is removal? Familiarization is bringing face to face again and again. The antidote is the path — as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'one whose body is cultivated, whose mind is cultivated' — meaning one whose body and mind are cultivated through the antidote. The antidote of the body, moreover, is the path for dispassion from the four <s>dhyāna</s>s. For thus it is stated: 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> is called "one whose body is cultivated, whose mind is cultivated, whose morality is cultivated." How does the body become cultivated? One becomes dispassionate from the body, free from longing, free from thirst, free from attachment, free from fixation.' Or alternatively, the <s>ānantaryamārga</s> (uninterrupted path) for the destruction of desire for form — through this one becomes dispassionate — this is the scriptural authority. Removal is the cutting off of the acquisition of afflictions. 'Of future [dharmas], one' — the cultivation by obtaining. 'Of present ones, both' — the cultivations by obtaining and familiarization. 'Thus it is so' — and so forth in detail. Since the cultivations by obtaining and familiarization are stated as 'of wholesome conditioned [dharmas]' without distinction — both contaminated and uncontaminated. And the cultivations by antidote and removal are stated as 'of contaminated <s>dharma</s>s' without distinction — both afflicted and non-afflicted. Therefore, thus it is that wholesome contaminated [dharmas] have four cultivations — those that have cultivation. Because of being wholesome, they have the cultivations by obtaining and familiarization. And because of being contaminated, they have the cultivations by antidote and removal. 'Then for those that are not wholesome-contaminated — those that are conditioned, those that are uncontaminated, and those that are afflicted-indeterminate — how many cultivations do they have?' He says: 'Of the uncontaminated, two' — the cultivations by obtaining and familiarization. 'And of the afflicted-indeterminate' — what? — two cultivations. The cultivations by antidote and removal.

body.text: indriyāṇāṃ pūrveti. cakṣurādīnāṃ saṃvarabhāvanety arthaḥ. kāyasyottareti. vibhāvanabhāvanā. tat punar bhāvanādvayam āgamena yathākramaṃ darśayati. ṣaḍ imānīndriyāṇīti vistaraḥ. sa punar indriyasaṃvaraḥ smṛti [Tib. 306b] saṃprajñānasvabhāva uktaḥ. vibhāvanāpi kāyālambanasya kleśasya nirdhāvanaṃ. te tv iti vistaraḥ. te tu saṃvaravibhāvanabhāvane pratipakṣanirdhāvanabhāvanāntarbhūte yathākramam ubhayam ubhayatrāntarbhūtam ity api na virudhyate.
body.translated_text: 'Of the faculties, the former' — the meaning is: the cultivation of restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) of the eye and the rest. 'Of the body, the latter' — the cultivation by purification (<s>vibhāvana</s>). Moreover, he shows that pair of cultivations sequentially through scriptural authority. 'These six faculties' — and so forth in detail. That restraint of the faculties has been stated as having the own-nature of mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) and clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajñāna</s>). Purification too is the removal (<s>nirdhāvana</s>) of the affliction that has the body as its object. 'But those two' — and so forth in detail. But those two — the cultivations of restraint and purification — are included in the cultivations by antidote and removal respectively — both are included in both — this too is not contradictory.

body.text: (VII.34ab) sāmānyena sarveṣām iti. śrāvakapratyekabuddhasamyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ kṣayajñānakṣaṇe guṇabhāvanoktā
body.translated_text: (VII.34ab) 'In general, of all' — of the <s>śrāvaka</s>s, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s, and perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>s, the cultivation of qualities is stated at the moment of the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) —

children.translated_text: 'And the contaminated ones [are cultivated] at the moment of the knowledge of destruction' —

body.text: buddhadharmān varṇayanti. tadyathā. nāsti tathāgatasya skhalitaṃ. nāsti ravitaṃ. nāsti dravatā. nāsti nānātvasaṃjñā. nāsty avyākṛtaṃ manaḥ. nāsty apratisaṃkhyāyopekṣā. nāsty atīteṣu pratihataṃ jñānadarśanaṃ. nāsty anāgateṣu pratihataṃ jñānadarśanaṃ. nāsti pratyutpanneṣu pratihataṃ jñānadarśanaṃ. sarvaṃ kāyakarma jñānānuparivarti. sarvaṃ vākkarma jñānānuparivarti. sarvaṃ manaskarma jñānānuparivarti. nāsti chaṃdahāniḥ. nāsti vīryahāniḥ. nāsti smṛtihāniḥ. nāsti samādhihāniḥ. [Tib. 307a] nāsti prajñāhāniḥ. nāsti vimuktijñanadarśanahānir iti. tatra ravitaṃ nāma sahasā kriyā. dravatā krīḍābhiprāyatā. nānātvasaṃjñā sukhaduḥkhāduḥkhāsukheṣu viṣayeṣu rāgadveṣamohato nānātvasaṃjñā. śeṣaṃ sugamaṃ. daśa balāni. sthānāsthānajñānabalaṃ. karmavipākajñānabalaṃ. dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalaṃ. indriyaparāparajñānabalaṃ. nānādhimuktijñānabalaṃ. nānādhātujñānabalaṃ. sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabalaṃ. pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñānabalaṃ. cyutyupapattijñānabalaṃ. āsravakṣayajñānabalaṃ ca. sūtraṃ tu daśāyuṣmantas tathāgatabalāni. katamāni daśa. ihāyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ sthānaṃ ca sthānato yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. asthānaṃ cāsthānataḥ. idaṃ prathamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ. yena balena samanvāgatas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha udāram ārṣabhasthānaṃ pratijānāti brāhmaṃ cakraṃ pravartayati. parṣadi samyaksiṃhanādaṃ nadati. punar aparam āyuṣmantas tathāgato 'tītānāgatapratyutpannāni karmadharmasamādānāni [Tib. 307b] sthānato hetuto vastuto vipākataś ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. yad āyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ pūrvavat. yāvad vipākataś ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. idaṃ dvitīyaṃ tathāgatabalam. yena baleneti pūrvavat. punar aparam āyuṣmantas tathāgato dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattīnāṃ saṃkleśavyavadānavyavasthānaviśuddhiṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. yad āyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ pūrvavat. punar aparam āyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ indriyaparāparatāṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. yad āyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ pūrvavat. idaṃ caturthaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ. yena baleneti pūrvavat. punar aparam āyuṣmantas tathāgato nānāvimuktikaṃ lokam anekavimuktikam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. yad āyuṣmaṃtas tathāgataḥ pūrvavat. idaṃ paṃcamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ. yena baleneti pūrvavat. punar aparam āyuṣmaṃtas tathāgto nānādhātukaṃ anekadhātukam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. yad āyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ [Tib. 308a] pūrvavat. idaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ. yena baleneti pūrvavat. punar aparam āyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ sarvatragāminīṃ pratipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. yad āyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s that are distinct from the powers and the rest. Namely: (1) The <s>Tathāgata</s> has no stumbling. (2) No idle chatter. (3) No running about. (4) No perception of diversity. (5) No indeterminate mind. (6) No equanimity without reflective examination. (7) No obstructed knowledge and vision regarding the past. (8) No obstructed knowledge and vision regarding the future. (9) No obstructed knowledge and vision regarding the present. (10) All bodily action follows knowledge. (11) All verbal action follows knowledge. (12) All mental action follows knowledge. (13) No decline of aspiration. (14) No decline of energy. (15) No decline of mindfulness. (16) No decline of concentration. (17) No decline of wisdom. (18) No decline of the knowledge and vision of liberation. Therein, 'idle chatter' (<s>ravita</s>) means hasty action. 'Running about' (<s>dravatā</s>) means playful intention. 'Perception of diversity' (<s>nānātvasaṃjñā</s>) means the perception of diversity arising from desire, aversion, and delusion toward pleasant, painful, and neither-pleasant-nor-painful objects. The rest is easy to understand. The ten powers are: (1) the power of knowledge of what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānajñānabala</s>); (2) the power of knowledge of the fruition of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmavipākajñānabala</s>); (3) the power of knowledge of <s>dhyāna</s>s, liberations, concentrations, and attainments; (4) the power of knowledge of the superiority and inferiority of faculties; (5) the power of knowledge of various dispositions; (6) the power of knowledge of various elements; (7) the power of knowledge of the paths leading everywhere; (8) the power of knowledge of recollection of former abodes; (9) the power of knowledge of death and rebirth; (10) the power of knowledge of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñānabala</s>). The <s>sūtra</s>, however, [reads]: 'There are, O venerable ones, ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. What are the ten? Here, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows what is possible as possible and what is impossible as impossible. This is the first power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. By which power endowed, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one, claims the supreme bull-like position, turns the <s>Brahmā</s>-wheel, and roars the lion's roar properly in the assembly. Furthermore, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows past, future, and present actions and their undertaking of <s>dharma</s>s — as to their ground, cause, entity, and fruition. Because, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> [knows them] — as before, up to — truly knows them as to their fruition. This is the second power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. By which power — as before. Furthermore, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows the defilement, purification, establishment, and distinction of <s>dhyāna</s>s, liberations, concentrations, and attainments. Because, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> — as before. Furthermore, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows the superiority and inferiority of faculties of other beings, other persons. Because, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> — as before. This is the fourth power. By which power — as before. Furthermore, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows the world as having various dispositions, of many dispositions. Because, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> — as before. This is the fifth power. By which power — as before. Furthermore, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows the world as having various elements, of many elements. Because, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> — as before. This is the sixth power. By which power — as before. Furthermore, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows the paths leading everywhere. Because, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s>

body.text: pūrvavat. idaṃ saptamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ. yena baleneti pūrvavat. punar aparam āyuṣmantas tathāgato 'nekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsam anusmarati. tadyathaikām api jātiṃ dve tisraś catasraḥ paṃca ṣaṭ saptāṣṭau nava daśa viṃśatiṃ yāvad anekān api saṃvartavivartakalpān anusmarati. amī nāma te bhavantaḥ sattvāḥ. yatrāham āsa evaṃnāmā evaṃjātya evaṃgotra evamāhāra evaṃsukhaduḥkhapratisaṃvedī evaṃ dīrghāyur evaṃcirasthitikaḥ evamāyuṣparyantaḥ so 'haṃ tasmāt sthānāc cyuto 'mutropapannaḥ tasmād api cyuta ihopapannaḥ. iti sākāraṃ sanidānaṃ soddeśam anekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsam anusmarati. yad āyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ pūrvavat. idam aṣṭamāṃ tathāgatabalaṃ. yena baleneti pūrvavat. punar aparam āyuṣmantas tathāgato divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāṃtamānuṣyakeṇa sattvān paśyati cyavanān apy upapadyamānān api suvarṇān durvarṇān durbalān hīnān praṇītān sugatim api gacchato durgatim api yathākarmopagān sattvān [Tib. 308b] yathābhūtaṃ prajānāty amī bhavantaḥ kāyaduścaritena smanvāgatā vāṅmanoduścaritena samanvagatāḥ. āryāṇām apavādakāḥ mithyādṛṣṭayo mithyādṛṣṭikarmadharmasamādānahetos taddhetuṃ tatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhedāt paraṃ maraṇād apāyadurgativinipāte narakeṣūpapadyaṃte. amī punar bhavantaḥ sattvāḥ kāyasucaritena samanvāgatāḥ vāṅmanaḥsucaritena samanvāgatāḥ āryāṇām anapavādakāḥ samyagdṛṣṭayaḥ samyagdṛṣṭikarmadharmasamādānahetos taddhetuṃ tatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhedāt sugatan svargaloke deveṣūpapadyante. yad āyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ pūrvavat. idaṃ navamaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ . yena baleneti pūrvavat. punar aparam āyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ āsravāṇāṃ kṣayād anāsravāṃ cetovimuktiṃ prajñāvimuktiṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayam abhijñāya sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya prativedayate kṣīṇā me jātir uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmīti. yad āyuṣmantas tathāgataḥ pūrvavat. idaṃ daśamaṃ tathagatabalaṃ. yena baleneti pūrvavat.
body.translated_text: — as before. This is the seventh power. By which power — as before. Furthermore, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> recollects various kinds of former abodes — namely, one birth, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, twenty, and up to many eons of dissolution and evolution. He recollects: 'Those beings had such names; where I was, I had such a name, such a birth, such a clan, such food, such an experience of pleasure and pain, such a lifespan, such a duration of life, such a limit of lifespan. Having departed from that place, I was reborn elsewhere; having departed from there too, I was reborn here.' Thus, with its characteristics, with its causes, with its specifications, he recollects various kinds of former abodes. Because, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> — as before. This is the eighth power. By which power — as before. Furthermore, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, sees beings departing and being reborn — beautiful and ugly, weak, inferior, and excellent, going to good destinies and bad destinies — and truly knows beings as they go according to their <s>karma</s>: 'These beings, endowed with bodily misconduct, endowed with verbal and mental misconduct, who disparage the Noble Ones, who hold wrong views, who undertake actions in accordance with wrong-view <s>dharma</s>s — because of that cause, that condition, upon the breaking up of the body, after death, they are reborn in the lower realms, in bad destinies, in perdition, in the hells. But these beings, endowed with bodily good conduct, endowed with verbal and mental good conduct, who do not disparage the Noble Ones, who hold right views, who undertake actions in accordance with right-view <s>dharma</s>s — because of that cause, that condition, upon the breaking up of the body, they are reborn in good destinies, in the heavenly world, among the <s>deva</s>s.' Because, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> — as before. This is the ninth power. By which power — as before. Furthermore, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsrava</s>), having directly known and realized the outflow-free mental liberation (<s>cetovimukti</s>) and wisdom-liberation (<s>prajñāvimukti</s>) in this very life, having accomplished and abiding therein, declares: 'Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done — I know there is no further existence.' Because, O venerable ones, the <s>Tathāgata</s> — as before. This is the tenth power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. By which power — as before.

body.text: (VII.34cd-36) sthānāsthāne daśa jñānānīti. sthānaṃ cāsthānaṃ sthānāsthānaṃ. tatra jñānam eva balaṃ jñānabalaṃ. tad daśajñānāni. [Tib. 309a] daśajñānasvabhāvam ity arthaḥ. kathaṃ kṛtvā. sthānāsthānaṃ samāsena saṃskṛtaṃ cāsaṃskṛtaṃ ca tad api saṃskṛtam aṣṭadhā bhettavyaṃ. kāmarūpārūpyāvacarānāsravāṇāṃ saṃprayuktaviprayuktabhedāt. tathā saṃskṛtaṃ dvidhā bhettavyaṃ. kuśalāvyākṛtabhedāt. tatra saṃvṛtijñānabalasya daśāpi dharmā viṣayaḥ.
body.translated_text: (VII.34cd-36) 'In [the power of knowledge of] what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthāna</s>), ten knowledges' — possible and impossible together constitute <s>sthānāsthāna</s>. Therein, knowledge itself that is a power is knowledge-power (<s>jñānabala</s>). That consists of ten knowledges — meaning it has the own-nature of ten knowledges. How is this so? What is possible and impossible is, in summary, both conditioned and unconditioned. And that conditioned [aspect] should be divided eightfold — from the distinction of what is connected and unconnected with the Desire, Form, Formless [Realms], and the uncontaminated. Likewise, the conditioned should be divided twofold — from the distinction of wholesome and indeterminate. Therein, the object-domain of the conventional knowledge-power (<s>saṃvṛtijñānabala</s>) is all ten <s>dharma</s>s

body.text: daśasv api dharmeṣu tasya vṛttir ity arthaḥ. dharmajñānasya paṃca. kāmāvacarānāsravāś catvāraḥ kuśalaṃ cāsaṃkṛtaṃ. anvayajñānasya sapta. rūpārūpyāvacarānāsravāḥ ṣaṭ kuśalaṃ cāsaṃskṛtaṃ. duḥkhasamudayajñānayoḥ ṣaṭ kāmarūpārūpyāvacarāḥ. nirodhajñānasyaikaḥ kuśalam evāsaṃskṛtaṃ. mārgajñānasya dvāv anāsravau. paracittajñānasya trayaḥ. kāmarūpāvacarānāsravāḥ saṃprayuktāḥ. kṣayānutpādajñānayor nava dharmā viṣayaḥ. avyākṛtam asaṃskṛtaṃ muktvā. evaṃ kṛtvā sthānāsthānajñānabalaṃ daśa jñānāni. kathaṃ punar daśā dharmāḥ sthānāsthānam ity uccyaṃte. saṃbhavaḥ sthānaṃ asaṃbhavo 'sthānam iti. atha vā asthānam anavakāśo yaḥ strī buddhatvaṃ kārayiṣyati. sthānam etad yat puruṣa iti. asthānam anavakāśo yaḥ strī brahmatvaṃ [Tib. 309b] kārayiṣyati. sthānam etat purusa iti. tathā sthānam etad yad duḥkhasya nirodha iti. evamādyākārapravṛttaṃ sthānāsthānajñānabalam avagaṃtavyaṃ. aṣṭau karmaphala iti. karmaṇaḥ sāsravasya tadvipākasya ca duḥkhasamudayasatyasaṃgṛhītatvāt. nirodhamārgajnāne na bhavata iti. ato 'nyāni tadālaṃbanāni aṣṭau jñānāni saṃbhavanti.
body.translated_text: — meaning it functions in all ten <s>dharma</s>s. Of <s>dharmajñāna</s>, five [are the object-domain]: four connected with the Desire Realm and the uncontaminated, plus the unconditioned wholesome. Of <s>anvayajñāna</s>, seven: six connected with the Form and Formless Realms and the uncontaminated, plus the unconditioned wholesome. Of the knowledges of suffering and origination, six: those connected with the Desire, Form, and Formless Realms. Of the knowledge of cessation, one: the unconditioned wholesome alone. Of the knowledge of the path, two: the two uncontaminated ones. Of the knowledge of others' minds, three: the connected ones of the Desire and Form Realms and the uncontaminated — the associated ones. Of the knowledges of destruction and non-arising, nine <s>dharma</s>s are the object-domain — excluding the indeterminate unconditioned. Thus, the knowledge-power of what is possible and impossible consists of ten knowledges. But how are the ten <s>dharma</s>s called 'what is possible and impossible'? What is possible (<s>sthāna</s>) is what can occur (<s>saṃbhava</s>); what is impossible (<s>asthāna</s>) is what cannot occur. Alternatively, it is impossible (<s>asthāna</s>) — there is no occasion — that a woman would become a <s>Buddha</s>. It is possible that a man [would]. It is impossible that a woman would become a <s>Brahmā</s>. It is possible that a man [would]. Likewise, 'it is possible that there is cessation of suffering' — the knowledge-power of what is possible and impossible that operates in such aspects should be understood. 'Eight [knowledges pertain to] <s>karma</s>-fruition' — because contaminated <s>karma</s> and its fruition are included in the truths of suffering and origination, the knowledges of cessation and the path are not applicable. Therefore, the other eight knowledges that take those as their object are possible.

children.translated_text: 'In <s>dhyāna</s>s and the rest, accomplishments, and dispositions' —

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. dhyānam ādir āsām iti dhyānādayo dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattayaḥ. dhyānāni catvāri. vimokṣā aṣṭau. samādhayas trayaḥ śūnyatādyāḥ. samāpattī dve. asaṃjñinirodhasamāpattī. navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ. akṣāṇīndriyāṇi. adhimokṣāś caitasikāḥ. dhyānādayaś cākṣāṇi cādhimokṣāś ceti dvandvaḥ. teṣu nava jñānāni nirodhajñānaṃ hitvā. kathaṃ kṛtvā. dhyānādīnāṃ sāsravānāsravasaṃprayuktaviprayuktabhedāt tadālaṃbanāni nava jñānāni saṃbhavanti. nirodhajñānaṃ tu na bhavati. [teṣāṃ san nirodhajñānaṃ tu na bhavati.] teṣāṃ saṃskṛtatvāt. indriyeṣv api śraddhādiṣu. [Tib. 310a] yat pradhānāpradhānajñānaṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātrendriyabhedena. tat parāparajñānabalaṃ. teṣv api sāsravānāsravabhedabhinneṣu nava jñānāni saṃbhavanti nirodhajñānaṃ hitvā. pradhānādiṣu rucayo nānādhimuktayaḥ. tāḥ punaḥ sāsravānāsravās traidhātukāś ca tadālambanatvāt nirodhajñānaṃ hitvā. evaṃ nānādhātujñānabalaṃ. tatra hi dhātuḥ pūrvābhyāsavāsanāsamudāgata āśayo dhātur ity ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ. sa punas tu eva te cittacaittā viśiṣṭāḥ. teṣāṃ tathaiva sāsravānāsravabhedabhinnānāṃ nirodhajñanaṃ hitvā nava jñānāni bhavantīti pūrvavad yojyaṃ. pratipatsv iti vistaraḥ. bahvyo 'tra pratipado narakādigāminyaḥ. narakagāminī pratipat
body.translated_text: — in detail. '<s>Dhyāna</s> and the rest' — '<s>dhyāna</s> is the first of these' — hence <s>dhyāna</s> and the rest: <s>dhyāna</s>s, liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), and attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>). The <s>dhyāna</s>s are four. The liberations are eight. The concentrations are three — emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and the rest. The attainments are two — the attainment of non-perception (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>) and the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>). And the nine sequential-abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihāra</s>). The sense-fields (<s>akṣa</s>) are the faculties (<s>indriya</s>). The dispositions (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) are mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>). '<s>Dhyāna</s>s and the rest, sense-fields, and dispositions' — this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. Among those, nine knowledges [operate], excluding the knowledge of cessation (<s>nirodhajñāna</s>). How so? Because of the division of the <s>dhyāna</s>s and the rest into contaminated and uncontaminated, associated and dissociated [aspects], nine knowledges are possible as having those as their object-domain. But the knowledge of cessation does not occur — because those are conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). Regarding the faculties too — beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the rest — whatever knowledge of predominance and non-predominance [among faculties], by the division of faculties into mild, middling, and intense — that is the power of knowledge of superior and inferior [faculties] (<s>parāparajñānabala</s>). Among those too, differentiated by the division of contaminated and uncontaminated, nine knowledges are possible, excluding the knowledge of cessation. The predilections toward predominant [qualities] and the rest are the diverse dispositions (<s>nānādhimukti</s>). Those again, being contaminated and uncontaminated and belonging to the three realms, and because of having those as object-domain — excluding the knowledge of cessation. Thus [is explained] the power of knowledge of diverse elements (<s>nānādhātujñānabala</s>). Therein, the element (<s>dhātu</s>) is — <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> [says]: the disposition (<s>āśaya</s>) produced through the impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) of prior practice is the element. But those are precisely the distinguished mental and mental-factor [dharmas]. Of those, differentiated by the division of contaminated and uncontaminated in the same way — excluding the knowledge of cessation, nine knowledges exist — this should be connected as before. 'Regarding the practices (<s>pratipad</s>)' — in detail. The practices here are many — those leading to the hells and the rest. The practice leading to the hells

body.text: yāvad devagāminī. nirodhagāmini ca. tatra yā narakādigāminyaḥ pratipadaḥ. tā hetuḥ. pratipadyante tābhir iti kṛtvā. mārgo hi pratipady ucate. tena hi visaṃyogaḥ pratipadyate. nirodhas tu kathaṃ. sa cāpi pratipat. pratipadyate tam iti kṛtvā. pratipatphalaṃ vā pratipad ity ucyate. ata evāha. yadi saphalā pratipad gṛhyata iti. hetur hi sarvatragāmini pratipad iheṣyate. [Tib. 310b] tathā hi vyācakṣate. sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabalam iti. satkāyasamudayagāminīty artha iti. tatra satkāyaḥ paṃcopādānaskaṃdhāḥ. samudaya utpāda ihābhipretaḥ. evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskaṃdhasya samudayo bhavatīti vacanāt. satkāyanirodho visaṃyogaḥ. tatra sarvatra gaṃtuṃ śīlam asyā iti sarvatragāminī cāsau pratipac ca sarvatragāminīpratipat. tat jñānaṃ tad eva ca balam iti. sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabalaṃ. tad daśa jñānāni yojyāni. yadi nirodhajñānam evāsravakṣayajñānam iti. āsravāṇāṃ kṣaye nirodhe jñānam. āsravanirodhālambanaṃ jñānam ity arthaḥ. evaṃ sati ṣaḍ jñānāni bhavanti. nirodhajñānajātir eva dharmajñānādibhedabhedinīkṛtvā. atha kṣīṇāsravasaṃtāna iti. āsravakṣaye sati yaj jñānaṃ. tad āsavakṣayajñānam ity arthaḥ. kṣīṇāsravasaṃtāne sarvāṇi jñānāni samudācarantīti daśa jñānāni bhavaṃti.
body.translated_text: — up to that leading to the <s>deva</s> realms. And that leading to cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). Therein, the practices leading to the hells and the rest — those are the cause (<s>hetu</s>). Because one reaches by them — thus considering. For the path is called 'practice.' By that, disconnection (<s>visaṃyoga</s>) is reached. But cessation — how [is it a practice]? That too is a practice. Because one reaches it — thus considering. Or, the fruit of practice is called 'practice.' For this very reason he says: 'If practice together with its fruit is intended.' For the cause — the all-destination-going practice (<s>sarvatragāminī pratipad</s>) — is what is intended here. For thus they explain: 'the power of knowledge of the all-destination-going practice' — means: of that leading to the origin of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāya</s>) — this is the meaning. Therein, the personal aggregate is the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>). The origination (<s>samudaya</s>) here means arising. From the statement: 'Thus there comes to be the origination of this entire great mass of suffering.' The cessation of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyanirodha</s>) is disconnection (<s>visaṃyoga</s>). Therein, 'all-destination-going' — one whose habit is to go to all [destinations] — and that is a practice — hence the all-destination-going practice. The knowledge of that is the power — that itself is the power. [This is] the power of knowledge of the all-destination-going practice. Those ten knowledges should be connected. If the knowledge of cessation alone is the knowledge of the destruction of outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñāna</s>) — [that is:] knowledge of cessation, of the destruction of outflows. The meaning is: knowledge having the cessation of outflows as its object-domain. In that case, six knowledges operate — considering only the divisions of <s>nirodhajñāna</s> [into <s>dharmajñāna</s> and the rest]. But if [it means] 'in the continuum of one whose outflows are destroyed' (<s>kṣīṇāsrava</s>) — knowledge that arises when outflows are destroyed — the meaning is: the knowledge of the destruction of outflows. In the continuum of one whose outflows are destroyed, all knowledges operate — hence ten knowledges exist.

body.text: anyatra buddhānutpādād iti. jaṃbūdvīpād anyatra buddhānutpādad iti jaṃbūdvīpapuruṣāśrayāṇi daśa balāni buddhāśrayotpatter ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Except for the non-arising of a <s>Buddha</s> elsewhere' — [the meaning is:] except for the non-arising of a <s>Buddha</s> elsewhere than in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. The intent is: the ten powers have their basis in a <s>Jambudvīpa</s> human being, because of the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>-basis [only there].

body.text: tad eva daśavidhajñānam anyasya balaṃ nocyata iti. anyasyāpy etad asti na tu balaṃ vyāhatatvāt. [Tib. 311a] yat tv avyāhataṃ. tad balam āveṇika ity abhiprāyaḥ. pravrajanaprekṣapuruṣapratyākhyānam iti vistaraḥ. pravrajanaṃ pravrajyā prekṣyate pravrajanaprekṣaḥ. tasya pravrajanaprekṣasya puruṣasya pratyākhyānaṃ pravrajanaprekṣapuruṣapratyākhyānaṃ. tad udāharaṇaṃ yathā anyasya vyāhanyate jñānam iti. āryaśāriputreṇa kila kasyacit pravrajyāprekṣasya puruṣasya mokṣabhāgīyaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ vyavalokayatā na dṛṣṭam iti pratyākhyāto na pravrājita ity arthaḥ. bhagavatā tu dṛṣṭaṃ pravrājitaś ca. taṃ cādhikṛtya bhikṣubhiḥ prṣṭena bhagavatoktaṃ. anenaivedaṃ karma kṛtaṃ. yad arhattvaṃ prāptā. na hi karmāṇi pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante. nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau. api tūpātteṣv eva skaṃdhadhātvāyataneṣv iti vistaraḥ. idaṃ coktaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'That very tenfold knowledge is not called a power for another' — another too has this, but it is not a power, because of being impeded (<s>vyāhata</s>). But what is unimpeded — that is a power, which is exclusive (<s>āveṇika</s>) — this is the intent. 'The rejection of the person contemplating ordination' — in detail. Contemplating ordination is a person who contemplates ordination (<s>pravrajana</s>). The rejection of that person contemplating ordination. This is the illustration of how another's knowledge is impeded. Reportedly, the Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, examining a certain person who was contemplating ordination, did not see the wholesome root conducive to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya kuśalamūla</s>) — and therefore rejected him, did not ordain him — this is the meaning. But the <s>Bhagavān</s> saw it and ordained him. And regarding him, when asked by the monks, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By this very one was this <s>karma</s> done, by which <s>arhat</s>ship was attained. For <s>karma</s>s do not ripen in the earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element. Rather, they ripen only in the appropriated aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>)' — in detail. And this was said:

children.text:
mokṣabījam ahaṃ hy asya svasūkṣmam upalakṣaye.
dhātupāṣāṇavivare nilīnam iva kāñcanam
children.translated_text:
'For I perceive in this one the liberation-seed,
subtle, of one's own [making] —
concealed in a crevice of the element-rock,
like gold [hidden therein].'

body.text: iti. upapattyādiparyantājñānaṃ ceti. ādiśabdena cyutiparyantājñānaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'And the ignorance regarding the limit of rebirth and the rest' — by the word 'and the rest,' the ignorance regarding the limit of death [is included].

body.text: iti. balasyeyaṃ saṃjñā nārāyaṇam iti. yasya ca tad balam. asāv api nārāyaṇa ity ucyate. cāṇūramahānagnavat.
body.translated_text: thus. This is the designation of the power: '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.' And the one who has that power is also called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. Like <s>Cāṇūra</s> and the great naked one (<s>mahānagna</s>).

body.text: bhadanta iti [Tib. 311b] dārṣṭāṃtikaḥ sthaviraḥ. anyathā hīti. yadi mānasavat kāyikabalaṃ neṣyate. anaṃtasya jñānabalasya sahiṣṇur na syāt. sahanaśīlo bhagavān na bhaved ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'The Venerable' (<s>Bhadanta</s>) — this is the elder (<s>sthavira</s>), the <s>Dārṣṭāntika</s>. 'For otherwise' — if bodily strength were not accepted like mental [strength], the <s>Bhagavān</s> would not be able to endure the infinite strength of knowledge (<s>jñānabala</s>). The meaning is: the <s>Bhagavān</s> would not have the capacity for endurance.

body.text: saṃdhiṣv anya ity uktam asthisaṃdhiviśeṣopanyāsaḥ. nāgagraṃthir iti vistaraḥ. nāgagranthisaṃdhayo buddhāḥ. nāgapāśo nāgagraṃthiḥ. śaṃkalāsaṃdhayaḥ pratyekabuddhāḥ. śaṃkusaṃdhayaś cakravartinaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'In the joints, another is stated' — the presentation of a distinction of bone-joints. 'Elephant-knot joints' — in detail. <s>Buddha</s>s have elephant-knot joints. An elephant-knot is an elephant-noose. <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s have chain-joints. <s>Cakravartin</s>s have pin-joints.

children.translated_text: 'the sevenfold strength of elephants and the rest' —

body.text: iti. hastyādīnāṃ hastigandhahastimahānagnapraskaṃdivarāṃgacāṇūranārāyaṇānāṃ saptakaṃ tasya balaṃ daśabhir adhikaṃ daśabhyo vādhikaṃ. katham ity āha. yad daśānāṃ prākṛtahastināṃ sānānyahastināṃ balaṃ. tad ekasya gandhahastino balaṃ. evaṃ yad daśānāṃ gandhahastināṃ balaṃ. tad ekasya mahānagnasya balaṃ. yāvad yad daśānāṃ cāṇūrāṇāṃ balaṃ. tad ekasya nārāyaṇasya balam iti.
body.translated_text: thus. The group of seven — elephants and the rest: elephant, scent-elephant (<s>gandhahastin</s>), great naked one (<s>mahānagna</s>), <s>Praskandin</s>, <s>Varāṅga</s>, <s>Cāṇūra</s>, and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — the strength of that [group] is greater by ten, or greater than ten. How? — he says: the strength of ten ordinary elephants is the strength of one scent-elephant. Similarly, the strength of ten scent-elephants is the strength of one great naked one. Up to: the strength of ten <s>Cāṇūra</s>s is the strength of one <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

body.text: daśottaravṛddhinagaḥ. daśottaravṛddhyārdhanārāyaṇabalam iti. āditas tathaiva prakramya yad daśānāṃ praskandināṃ balaṃ. tad ardhanārāyaṇaṃ. taddviguṇaṃ nārāyaṇam iti.
body.translated_text: 'Increasing by tens' — half-<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> strength with increase by tens. Starting from the beginning in the same way: the strength of ten <s>Praskandin</s>s is half-<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. Double that is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

body.text: yathā tu bahutaraṃ. tathā yujyata ity ācāryaḥ. pūrvakam eva pakṣaṃ samarthayati. anyathā hy anantajñānabalasahiṣṇur na syād iti tad eva kāraṇaṃ. devadattahatahastipādāṃguṣṭhasaptaprākāraparikhākṣepaś [Tib. 312a] cānyathā na syād iti.
body.translated_text: 'But as much greater as possible — that is fitting' — the <s>Ācārya</s> supports the former position. For otherwise, he would not be able to endure the infinite strength of knowledge — that very reason [applies]. And the casting of the foot-toe of the elephant killed by <s>Devadatta</s> over seven walls and moats would otherwise not be possible.

body.text: mahābhūtaviśeṣa eveti. mahābhūtaviśeṣasvabhāvam evedaṃ balaṃ na bhautikam iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: 'It is a distinction of the great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>) alone' — he shows that this strength has the nature of a distinction of the great elements, not derivative matter (<s>bhautika</s>).

body.text: upādāyarūpasaptabhyo 'rthāntaram iti. ślakṣnatvādibhyaḥ pūrvoktebhyo 'nyad eva balaṃ nāmopādāyarūpam ity apare.
body.translated_text: 'Something different from the seven kinds of derivative matter' — others [say]: the strength called derivative matter (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>) is something other than the seven — smoothness and the rest — previously stated.

body.text: (VII.38ab) yathāsūtram eveti. catvārīmāni śāriputra tathāgatasya vaiśāradyni. yair vaiśaradyaiḥ samanvāgatas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha udāram ārṣabhaṃ sthānaṃ pratijānāti brāhmyaṃ cakraṃ pravartayati parṣadi samyak siṃhanādaṃ nadati. katamāni catvāri. samyaksaṃbuddhasya bata me sato ime dharmā
body.translated_text: (VII.38ab) 'As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>' — 'There are, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, four kinds of fearlessness (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Endowed with these fearlessnesses, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one, claims the eminent, bull-like station, turns the Brahma-wheel, and correctly roars the lion's roar in the assembly. What are the four? "These <s>dharma</s>s have not been fully awakened to by me who am a perfectly awakened one" — here, any <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s> might rightfully challenge me, might remind me.

body.text: anabhisaṃbuddhā ity atra māṃ kaścic chramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā saha dharmeṇa codayet. smārayet. tatrāhaṃ nimittam api na samanupaśyāmi. evaṃ cāhaṃ nimittam asamanupaṣyan kṣemaprāptaś ca viharāmy abhayaprāptaś ca vaiśāradyaprāptaś ca udāram ārṣabhaṃ sthānaṃ pratijānāmi brāhmyaṃ cakraṃ pravartayāmi. parṣadi samyak siṃhanādaṃ nadāmi. idaṃ prathamaṃ vaiśāradyaṃ. kṣīṇāsravasya bata me sata ime āsravā aprahīṇā ity atra māṃ kaścid iti pūrvavat. yāvat parṣadi samyak siṃhanādaṃ [Tib. 312b] nadāmi. idaṃ dvitīyaṃ vaiśāradyaṃ. ye vā punar mayā śrāvakāṇām āntarāyikā dharmā ākhyātāḥ. tān pratiṣevamāṇasya nālam antarāyāyety atra māṃ kaścid iti pūrvavat. idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vaiśāradyaṃ. yo vā punar mayā śrāvakāṇāṃ mārga ākhyātaḥ āryo nairyāṇiko nairvedhiko niryāti. tatkarasya samyagduḥkhakṣayāya duḥkhasyāntakriyāyai sa na niryāsyatīty atra māṃ kaścid iti pūrvavat. idaṃ caturthaṃ vaiśāradyam iti. yathā sthānāsthānajñānabalam iti vistaraḥ. yathā sthānāsthānajñānabalaṃ daśa jñānāni sarvabhūmisaṃgṛhītaṃ ca. evaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhasya bata me sata ity etad vaiśāradyaṃ. tathaiva daśadhā dharmāṇāṃ bhedaṃ kṛtvā yojyaṃ. yathāsravakṣayajñānabalaṃ ṣaṭ daśa vā jñānāni daśabhūmisaṃgṛhītaṃ ca. evaṃ kṣīṇāsravasyeti dvitīyaṃ vaiśāradyam atrāpi tathaiva dharmāṇāṃ bhedaṃ kṛtvā ṣaṭ daśa vā jñānānīti yojyaṃ. yathā karmasvakajñānabalam aṣṭau jñānāni nirodhamārgajñāne hitvā sarvabhūmisaṃgṛhītaṃ ca. evaṃ ya vā punar mayā śrāvakāṇām āntarāyikā iti vistareṇa tṛtīyaṃ vaiśāradyam. atrāpi tathaiva dharmāṇāṃ bhedaṃ kṛtvā duḥkhasamudayasatyasaṃgṛhītā evāntarāyikāḥ. na nirodhamārgasatyasaṃgṛhītā [Tib. 313a] ity aṣṭau jñānānīti yojyaṃ. yathā sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabalaṃ daśa jñānāni nava vā sarvabhūmisaṃgṛhītaṃ ca. evaṃ yo vā mayā śrāvakāṇāṃ niryāṇāya mārga ākhyāta ity etad vaiśāradyaṃ. atrāpi saphalasāsravānāsravamārgagrahaṇato daśa jñānāni. aphalatadgrahaṇato vā naveti yojyaṃ. nirbhayatā hi vaiśāradyam. ebhiś ca jñānair nirbhayo bhavatīti jñānāni vaiśāradyānīti vaibhāṣikāḥ.
body.translated_text: Therein I do not perceive even a sign [of such a challenge]. And thus, not perceiving a sign, I dwell having attained security, having attained fearlessness, having attained confidence, I claim the eminent, bull-like station, I turn the Brahma-wheel, I correctly roar the lion's roar in the assembly. This is the first fearlessness. "These outflows have not been abandoned by me who am one whose outflows are destroyed" — here any one might — as before, up to — I correctly roar the lion's roar in the assembly. This is the second fearlessness. "The <s>dharma</s>s that I have declared to be obstructive for disciples — practicing those, they do not suffice for obstruction" — here any one might — as before. This is the third fearlessness. "The path that I have declared for disciples — the noble, leading-out, penetrating path — practicing it, for the correct destruction of suffering, for the ending of suffering, it will not lead out" — here any one might — as before. This is the fourth fearlessness.' 'Just as the power of knowledge of what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānajñānabala</s>)' — in detail. Just as the power of knowledge of what is possible and impossible comprises ten knowledges and is included in all grounds — so too, the fearlessness '[these dharmas] have not been fully awakened to by me who am a perfectly awakened one' — likewise, having made the tenfold division of <s>dharma</s>s, it should be connected. Just as the power of knowledge of the destruction of outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñānabala</s>) comprises six or ten knowledges and is included in ten grounds — so too, the second fearlessness, 'whose outflows are destroyed' — here too, likewise, having made the division of <s>dharma</s>s, six or ten knowledges should be connected. Just as the power of knowledge of one's own <s>karma</s> (<s>karmasvakajñānabala</s>) comprises eight knowledges, excluding the knowledge of cessation and the knowledge of the path, and is included in all grounds — so too, the third fearlessness 'the <s>dharma</s>s declared by me as obstructive for disciples' — in detail. Here too, likewise, having made the division of <s>dharma</s>s — the obstructive [dharmas] are included in the truths of suffering and origination alone, not in the truths of cessation and the path — eight knowledges should be connected. Just as the power of knowledge of the all-destination-going practice (<s>sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabala</s>) comprises ten or nine knowledges and is included in all grounds — so too, the fearlessness 'the path declared by me for disciples for leading out.' Here too, from the inclusion of the path together with its fruit — whether contaminated or uncontaminated — ten knowledges. Or, from the non-inclusion of the fruit and from the non-inclusion of the contaminated path, nine should be connected. 'For fearlessness (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) is freedom from fear (<s>nirbhayatā</s>). And through these knowledges one becomes fearless — hence the knowledges are fearlessnesses' — thus [say] the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s.

body.text: ācārya āha. jñānakṛtaṃ tu vaiśāradyaṃ. na jñānam eveti. atha va ācāryavacanam evaitat sarvaṃ. nirbhayatā hi vaiśāradyaṃ. tathā hi tadbhayapratipakṣo dharmaś caitasikaḥ. bhayam api caitasiko dharma iti. ebhiś ca jñānair hetubhūtair nirbhayo bhavatīti. tat kathaṃ jñānam eva vaiśāradyaṃ. jñānakṛtaṃ tu vaiśāradyaṃ yujyate na jñānam eveti.
body.translated_text: The <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'But fearlessness is produced by knowledge (<s>jñānakṛta</s>), not knowledge itself.' Or rather, all of this is the <s>Ācārya</s>'s statement: 'For fearlessness is freedom from fear. For that — the antidote to that fear — is a mental <s>dharma</s>. Fear too is a mental <s>dharma</s>.' And through these knowledges, which serve as causes, one becomes fearless. Therefore, how can knowledge itself be fearlessness? Rather, fearlessness is produced by knowledge — not knowledge itself — this is fitting.

body.text: (VII.38cd) yathāsūtram iti trīṇīmāni bhikṣavaḥ smṛtyupasthānāni. yāny āryaḥ.
body.translated_text: (VII.38cd) 'As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>' — 'There are, O <s>bhikṣu</s>s, three mindful establishments (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) that the Noble one

body.text: sevate. yāny āryaḥ sevamāno 'rhati gaṇam anuśāsayituṃ. katamāni trīni. iha bhikṣavaḥ śāstā śravakāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati anukaṃpakaḥ kāruṇiko 'rthakāmo hitaiṣī karuṇāyamānaḥ. idaṃ vo hitāya idaṃ vo sukhāya idaṃ vo hitasukhāya. [Tib. 313b] tasya me śrāvakāḥ śuśrūṣante. śrotram avadadhati. ājñācittam upasthāpayanti. pratipadyante dharmasyānudharman prati. na vyatikramya vartante śāstuḥ śāsane. tena tathāgatasya na nandī bhavati na saumanasyaṃ na cetasa utplāvitatvam. upekṣakas tatra tathāgato viharati smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan. idaṃ prathamaṃ smṛtyupasthānaṃ. yad āryaḥ sevate. yad āryaḥ sevamāno 'rhati gaṇam anuśāsayitum. punar aparaṃ śāstā dharmaṃ deśayati pūrvavat. tasya te śrāvakā na śuśrūṣante. na śrotram avadadhati. nājñācittam upasthāpayanti. na pratipadyante dharmasyānudharmaṃ. vyatikramya vartante śāstuḥ śāsane. tena tathāgatasya nāghāto bhavati nākṣāntir nāpratyayo na cetaso 'nabhirāddhiḥ. upekṣakas tatra tathāgato viharati smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan. idaṃ dvitīyaṃ smṛtyupasthānaṃ. yad āryaḥ sevate. yad āryaḥ sevamāno 'rhati gaṇam anuśāsayituṃ. punar aparaṃ bhikṣavaḥ yāvac chāsane tatra tathāgatasya na nandī bhavati na saumanasyaṃ na cetasa utplāvitatvaṃ. nāghāto nākṣāntir nāpratyayo [Tib. 314a] na cetaso 'nabhirāddhiḥ. upekṣakas tatra tathāgato viharati smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan. idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ smṛtyupasthānaṃ. yad āryaḥ sevate. yad āryaḥ sevamāno 'rhati gaṇam anuśāsayitum iti.
body.translated_text: frequents. Which, when the Noble One frequents, he is worthy of instructing the assembly. What are those three? Here, O monks, the Teacher teaches the <s>dharma</s> to the disciples, compassionate, merciful, desiring their welfare, seeking their benefit, feeling compassion: "This is for your benefit, this is for your happiness, this is for your benefit and happiness." [Tib. 313b] My disciples listen attentively, lend their ears, apply their minds to understanding, and practice in conformity with the <s>dharma</s>. They do not transgress the Teacher's instruction. Thereby the <s>Tathāgata</s> has no delight, no gladness, no elation of mind. The <s>Tathāgata</s> dwells therein with equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending. This is the first foundation of mindfulness which the Noble One frequents, which, when the Noble One frequents, he is worthy of instructing the assembly. Furthermore, the Teacher teaches the <s>dharma</s> as before. Those disciples do not listen attentively, do not lend their ears, do not apply their minds to understanding, do not practice in conformity with the <s>dharma</s>, and transgress the Teacher's instruction. Thereby the <s>Tathāgata</s> has no anger, no impatience, no displeasure, no dissatisfaction of mind. The <s>Tathāgata</s> dwells therein with equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending. This is the second foundation of mindfulness which the Noble One frequents, which, when the Noble One frequents, he is worthy of instructing the assembly. Furthermore, O monks, [Tib. 314a] up to: regarding the instruction, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has no delight, no gladness, no elation of mind, no anger, no impatience, no displeasure, no dissatisfaction of mind. The <s>Tathāgata</s> dwells therein with equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending. This is the third foundation of mindfulness which the Noble One frequents, which, when the Noble One frequents, he is worthy of instructing the assembly.

body.text: iti. ubhayasvabhāvam iti darśayati. smṛtaḥ saṃprajānann iti vacanāt. yadā śrāvakasyāpīti vistaraḥ. yadā śrāvakasyāpi hīnakleśasya śuśrūṣamāṇeṣu ca śiṣyeṣv aśuśrūṣamāṇeṣu ca ubhayeṣu ca śuśrūṣamāṇāśuśrūṣamāṇeṣu ca. nandī anunayo ma bhavati. āghāto vā dveṣo vā.
body.translated_text: thus. He shows that it has the nature of both — from the statement "mindful and clearly comprehending." "When a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple) also" — in detail. When even a <s>śrāvaka</s> of diminished afflictions, whether the students are obedient or disobedient or both obedient and disobedient — [Tib. 314b] delight or approval does not arise; nor does anger or hatred.

body.text: kasmād ete āveṇikā asādhāraṇā buddhadharmā ucyaṃte. savāsanaprahāṇaḍ iti. savāsanānām ānamdyādīnāṃ prahāṇāt. kā punar iyaṃ vāsanā nāma śrāvakāṇāṃ. yo hi yatkleśacaritaḥ pūrvaṃ. tasya tatkṛtaḥ kāyavāgaceṣṭāvikārahetusāmarthyaviśeṣaś citte vāsanety ucyate. avyākṛtaś cittaviśeṣo vāsaneti bhadantānantavarmā. atha veti vistareṇācāryaḥ. yasya śrāvakā buddhasya bhagavataḥ śrāvakā bhavanti nānyasya. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. śuśrūṣamāṇe cāśuśrūṣamāṇe cobhayasmiṃś ca śuśrūṣamāṇāśuśruṣamāṇeṣu [Tib. 314b] ubhayeṣu tasyaiva śravakavatas tatanutpādaḥ. ānandyāghātānutpādaḥ. āścaryam adbhutaṃ
body.translated_text: Why are these called exclusive (<s>āveṇika</s>), uncommon <s>buddhadharma</s>s? "Because of the abandonment together with their residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>)" — because of the abandonment of delight and the rest together with their <s>vāsanā</s>s (residual impressions). What, then, is this so-called <s>vāsanā</s> of the <s>śrāvaka</s>s? Whatever affliction-conduct one formerly had — the distinctive capacity of the cause of the modification of bodily and vocal behavior produced by that — that is called <s>vāsanā</s> in the mind. "<s>Vāsanā</s> is an indeterminate mental distinction" — says <s>Bhadanta Anantavarman</s>. "Or" — the <s>Ācārya</s> [explains] in detail. "Whose <s>śrāvaka</s>s" — they are <s>śrāvaka</s>s of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, not of another. For what reason? In both [cases] — whether [disciples] are obedient or disobedient, or both obedient and disobedient — [Tib. 314b] for that very possessor of disciples, there is the non-arising of those. The non-arising of delight and anger. "A wonder, a marvel

body.text: vyavasthāpyate. nānyasya śrāvakasyety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: is established" — the meaning is: not of another <s>śrāvaka</s>.

body.text: (VII.39) anyathā hīti vistaraḥ. yadi saṃvṛtijñānasvabhāvā na syād adveṣasvabhāvā syāt karuṇāvat. na sarvasattvālaṃbanā sidhyet. na traidhātukasattvālaṃbanā sidhyed ity arthaḥ. yathā karuṇā na traidhātukasattvālambanā. kiṃ tarhi. kāmāvacarasattvālaṃbanā. duḥkhitasattvālambanatvād evaṃ siddhaṃ syād ity abhiprāyaḥ. na ca triduḥkhatākārā sidhyed iti vartate karuṇāvat. yathā karuṇā duḥkhatākāraiva na triduḥkhatākārā duḥkhaduḥkhatāsaṃskāraduḥkhatāvipariṇāmaduḥkhatākarā. tathā na syāt. iṣyate ca triduḥkhatākāreti. ataḥ saṃvṛtijñānasvabhāveti. mahacchabdavācyatākāraṇaṃ darśāyann āha.
body.translated_text: (VII.39) "Otherwise indeed" — in detail. If it were not of the nature of <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s> (conventional knowledge) but of the nature of <s>adveṣa</s> (non-hatred), like <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), then it would not be established as having all beings of the three realms as its object-domain. The meaning is: it would not be established as having beings of all three realms as its object-domain. Just as <s>karuṇā</s> does not have beings of the three realms as its object-domain — rather, it has only beings of the Desire Realm as its object-domain — because of having suffering beings as its object-domain — so too it would be established — this is the intent. "Nor would it be established as having the aspect of the three kinds of suffering (<s>triduḥkhatā</s>)" — this continues — like <s>karuṇā</s>. Just as <s>karuṇā</s> has only the aspect of suffering (<s>duḥkhatā</s>), not the aspect of the three kinds of suffering — the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>), the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>), and the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>) — so too [<s>mahākaruṇā</s>] would not be [so established]. And the aspect of the three kinds of suffering is accepted [for <s>mahākaruṇā</s>]. Therefore it is of the nature of <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>. Showing the reason for being designated by the word "great" (<s>mahā</s>), he says:

body.text: kasmād iyam ityādi. saṃbhāreṇa mahāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhārasamudāgamād iti. mahāpuṇyasaṃbhārasamudāgamāt. mahājñānasaṃbhārasamudāgamāc cety arthaḥ. tatra mahāpuṇyasaṃbhāras tisraḥ pāramitāḥ. [Tib. 315a] dānaśīlakṣāntipāramitāḥ. mahājñānasaṃbhāraḥ prajñāpāramitā. vīryadhyānapāramite tu dvidhā ubhayatravyāpārāt. na hi vinā vīryeṇa dānaṃ dīyate śīlaṃ samādīyate kṣāntir bhāvyata iti mahāpuṇyasaṃbhārabhāgīyaṃ vīryaṃ bhavati. tathā nāntareṇa vīryaṃ prajñā bhavatīti mahājñānasaṃbhārabhāgīyaṃ bhavati. tathā maitryādicaturvidhāpramāṇabhāvanāpakṣaṃ dhyānaṃ mahāpuṇyasaṃbhārabhāgīyaṃ. smṛtyupasthānādisaptatriṃśadbodhipakṣadharmabhāvanāpakṣaṃ dhyānaṃ mahājñānasaṃbhārabhāgīyaṃ. tad evaṃ mahāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhārābhyāṃ samudāgamān nirvṛtter mahatīyaṃ karuṇeti mahākaruṇā. ākāreṇa triduḥkatākaraṇāt. yasmāt tisṛbhir api duḥkhatābhir ākārayati na duḥkhaduḥkatayaiva karuṇāvat. ālambanena traidhātukasattvālaṃbanatvāt. yasmāt traidhātukopapannan sattvān ālambate na ca kāmadhātūpapannān eva karuṇāvat.

children.translated_text: "Beings of the Desire Realm are the domain [of karuṇā]" —

body.translated_text: "Why is this" and so forth. "Because of the full accomplishment of the accumulations of great merit and knowledge" — because of the full accomplishment of the great accumulation of merit and the full accomplishment of the great accumulation of knowledge — this is the meaning. Therein, the great accumulation of merit is three <s>pāramitā</s>s: [Tib. 315a] <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (morality), and <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) <s>pāramitā</s>s. The great accumulation of knowledge is the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). But the <s>vīrya</s> (energy) and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) <s>pāramitā</s>s are twofold, because of their engagement in both. For without energy, generosity is not given, morality is not undertaken, patience is not cultivated — therefore energy pertains to the accumulation of great merit. Similarly, without energy, wisdom does not arise — therefore it pertains to the accumulation of great knowledge.
