Likewise, <s>dhyāna</s> pertaining to the cultivation of the fourfold <s>apramāṇa</s> (immeasurables) — loving-kindness and the rest — pertains to the accumulation of great merit. <s>Dhyāna</s> pertaining to the cultivation of the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣadharma</s>s (aids to awakening) beginning with the foundations of mindfulness pertains to the accumulation of great knowledge. Thus, because of the full accomplishment of the accumulations of great merit and knowledge, this <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) is great — hence <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion). "By aspect" — because of having the aspect of the three kinds of suffering. Since it operates through all three kinds of suffering — not only through the suffering of suffering like <s>karuṇā</s>. "By object-domain" — because of having beings of the three realms as its object-domain. Since it takes as its object-domain beings born in all three realms — not only those born in the Desire Realm, like <s>karuṇā</s>.

body.text: Tib. 315b
body.translated_text: Tib. 315b

body.text: iti vacanāt. samatvena sarvasattveṣu samavṛttitvāt. yasmāt sarvasattveṣu traidhātukaparyāpanneṣu samaṃ vartate saṃskāraduḥkhatākāreṇa. ato 'pi mahākaruṇety ucyate. tato 'dhimātratarābhāvād iti. prajñāsvabhāvatayā tīkṣṇataratvāt. yathā hi tayā karuṇāyate. na tathā karuṇayeti. nānākaraṇaṃ viśeṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated. "Because of equal engagement toward all beings" — since it engages equally toward all beings included in the three realms, through the aspect of the suffering of conditioned existence (<s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s>). For this reason too it is called <s>mahākaruṇā</s>. "Because of the absence of anything more intense" — because of being sharper due to its nature as <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). For just as it compassionates (<s>karuṇāyate</s>) — so <s>karuṇā</s> does not [compassionate in the same way] — the difference is the distinction of different functioning.

body.text: adveṣāmohasvabhāvatvād iti. yathākramaṃ karuṇāyā adveṣasvabhāvatvāt. mahākaruṇāyāś cāmohasvabhāvatvād ity arthaḥ. ekatriduḥkhatākāratvād iti. ekaduḥkhatākāratvāt karuṇāyāḥ. triduḥkhākāratvāc ca mahākaruṇāyaḥ. ity
body.translated_text: "Because of having the nature of <s>adveṣa</s> (non-hatred) and <s>amoha</s> (non-delusion)" — in due order: because <s>karuṇā</s> has the nature of <s>adveṣa</s>, and because <s>mahākaruṇā</s> has the nature of <s>amoha</s> — this is the meaning. "Because of having the aspect of one and three kinds of suffering" — because <s>karuṇā</s> has the aspect of one kind of suffering, and because <s>mahākaruṇā</s> has the aspect of three kinds of suffering.

body.text: ubhayatrāpi sarvatra yāthāsaṃkhyena yojayitavgyaṃ. caturdhyānacaturthadhyānabhūmikatvād iti. karuṇā caturdhyānabhūmika. anāgamyadhyānāntarayoḥ prathamadhyānagrahaṇena grahaṇān na ṣaḍbhūmikety uktaṃ. mahākaruṇā tu caturthadhyānabhūmikaiva sarvasamādhikarmaṇyatvena tasyaiva tadutpādanasamarthatvāt. śrāvakādibuddhasaṃtānajatvād iti. ādiśabdena pratyekabuddhapṛthagjanāṃ grahaṇaṃ. kāmabhavāgravairāgyalabhyatvād iti. kāmavairāgyalabhyā karuṇā. [Tib. 316a] bhavāgravairāgyalabhyā mahākaruṇā. aparitrāṇaparitrāṇata iti. karuṇayā śrāvakādayaḥ karuṇāyanta eva kevalaṃ anuglāyaṃty evety arthaḥ. na saṃsārabhayāt paritrāyante. mahākaruṇayā tu karuṇāyamāno bhagavān mahataḥ saṃsārabhayāt paritrāyte. atulyatulyakaruṇāyanāt. karuṇayātulyaṃ karuṇāyate. duḥkhitānām eva karunāyanāt. mahākaruṇayā tu tulyaṃ sarvasattvasamakruṇāyanāt.
body.translated_text: In both cases, everywhere, the connection should be made in due order (<s>yāthāsaṃkhya</s>). "Because of belonging to the four <s>dhyāna</s>s and the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground" — <s>karuṇā</s> belongs to the four <s>dhyāna</s> grounds. Because the <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary) and <s>dhyānāntara</s> (intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>) are included under the first <s>dhyāna</s>, it is not said to belong to six grounds. But <s>mahākaruṇā</s> belongs only to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground — because that [ground] alone is capable of producing it, through its fitness for all <s>samādhi</s> activities. "Because of arising in the continuums of <s>śrāvaka</s>s and the rest, and of the <s>Buddha</s>" — by the word "and the rest" (<s>ādi</s>), <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s and ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) are included. "Because of being obtained through dispassion from the Desire Realm and the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>)" — <s>karuṇā</s> is obtained through dispassion from the Desire Realm. [Tib. 316a] <s>Mahākaruṇā</s> is obtained through dispassion from the Peak of Existence. "Because of non-rescue and rescue" — by <s>karuṇā</s>, <s>śrāvaka</s>s and the rest merely compassionate — they only sympathize — this is the meaning. They do not rescue from the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>. But the <s>Bhagavān</s>, compassionating with <s>mahākaruṇā</s>, rescues from the great fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>. "Because of unequal and equal compassionating" — with <s>karuṇā</s>, one compassionates unequally — because of compassionating only toward the suffering. With <s>mahākaruṇā</s>, however, equally — because of equal compassionating toward all beings.

body.text: (VII.40) pūrvapuṇyajñānasaṃbhārasaṃudāgamata iti. pūrveṣu janmasu puṇyasaṃbhāreṇa pūrvoktena jñānasaṃbhāreṇa ca samudāgamataḥ. dharmakāyapariniṣpattita iti. anāsravadharmasaṃbhārasaṃtāno dharmakāyaḥ. āśrayaparivṛttir vā. arthacaryayā ceti. svargāpavargakāraṇam artho lokasya. tasya saṃpādanam arthacaryā. tulyā hi sarveṣāṃ buddhānāṃ mahākaruṇā parārthahetuḥ. yathākālam iti. sarvatrābhisaṃbadhyate. kathaṃ. cirālpajīvanād yathākālaṃ dīrghāyuṣi prajāyāṃ dīrgāyuṣo buddhā bhavanti. alpāyuṣy alpāyuṣaḥ. yathāsaṃbhavaṃ kṣatriyaguruke loke kṣatriyā bhavanti. brāhmaṇaguruke brāhmaṇāḥ. yathākālam eva ca kāśyapādigotrāḥ. [Tib. 316b] gautamādigotrāś ca. tathālpapramāṇe loke 'lpapramāṇāḥ. analpapramāṇe 'nalpapramāṇā iti. hetusaṃpadaṃ puṇyajñanasaṃbhāralakṣaṇāṃ. phalasaṃpadaṃ dharmakāyalakṣaṇāṃ. upakārasaṃpadaṃ jagadarthacaryālakṣaṇāṃ. sarvaguṇajñānasaṃbhārābhyāsa iti. guṇāḥ paṃcapāramitāsvabhāvāḥ. jñānānāni ca prajñāpāramitāsvabhāvāni. teṣāṃ guṇajñānānāṃ saṃbhāraḥ. tasyābhyāsaḥ punaḥpumahprayogaḥ. dīrghakālābhyāsas tribhir asaṃkhyeyair mahākalpaiḥ. nirantarābhyāso 'sāntaratayā. satkṛtyabhyāsas tīvrādaratayā. caturvidhā phalasaṃpad iti. dharmakāyapariniṣpattyā jñānādisaṃpadaś catasro bhavantīti tā api phalasaṃpada iti vyavasthāpyante. jñānasaṃpac caturvidheti vakṣyati. tathā prahāṇasaṃpat prabhāvasaṃpat rūpakāyasaṃpac ca caturvidheti vakṣyati. tad evāsāṃ vyākhyānaṃ bhaviṣyati. caturvidhopakārasaṃpat. ktham ity āha. apāyatrayasaṃsāraduḥkhatyantanirmokṣasaṃpad iti. apāyatrayaṃ ca narakādi saṃsāraś ca. tayor duḥkhaṃ.
body.translated_text: (VII.40) "Because of the full accomplishment of the previous accumulations of merit and knowledge" — because of the full accomplishment through the accumulation of merit in former lives, and through the accumulation of knowledge as previously stated. "Because of the perfection of the <s>dharmakāya</s>" — the continuum of the accumulation of uncontaminated <s>dharma</s>s is the <s>dharmakāya</s>. Or the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>). "And because of beneficent activity" — the cause of heavenly and liberating [attainments] is the goal (<s>artha</s>) of the world. Its accomplishment is beneficent activity. For the <s>mahākaruṇā</s> of all <s>Buddha</s>s is equally the cause of others' welfare. "At the appropriate time" — this qualifies everything. How? Because of living for a long or short time — at the appropriate time, in a long-lived generation, <s>Buddha</s>s are long-lived; in a short-lived [generation], short-lived. As appropriate: in a world where the <s>kṣatriya</s>s are prominent, [the <s>Buddha</s>s] are <s>kṣatriya</s>s; where <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s are prominent, they are <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s. And at the appropriate time, they are of the <s>Kāśyapa</s> lineage and the rest, [Tib. 316b] or of the <s>Gautama</s> lineage and the rest. Similarly, in a world of small stature, they are of small stature; in a world of large stature, of large stature. The perfection of the cause is characterized by the accumulations of merit and knowledge. The perfection of the result is characterized by the <s>dharmakāya</s>. The perfection of beneficence is characterized by activity for the welfare of beings. "Through the practice of the accumulation of all qualities and knowledge" — qualities are of the nature of the five <s>pāramitā</s>s; knowledges are of the nature of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. The accumulation of those qualities and knowledges — the practice of that is repeated, sustained effort. Long-term practice is through three incalculable great <s>kalpa</s>s (aeons). Uninterrupted practice is without gaps. Earnest practice is with intense devotion. The fourfold perfection of the result — through the perfection of the <s>dharmakāya</s>, four perfections of knowledge and the rest arise — those too are established as perfections of the result. The perfection of knowledge is fourfold — as he will state. Similarly, the perfection of abandonment, the perfection of power, and the perfection of the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>) are each fourfold — as he will state. That itself will be the explanation of these. The fourfold perfection of beneficence — how? He says: "The perfection of liberation from the suffering of the three lower realms and <s>saṃsāra</s> entirely" — the three lower realms are the hells and the rest, and <s>saṃsāra</s>. The suffering of those two.

body.text: tato 'tyantanirmokṣaḥ. saiva saṃpad iti. yānatrayasugatipratiṣṭhāpanasaṃpad [Tib. 317a] veti. yānatraye ca śrāvakayānādau. sugatau ca pratiṣṭhāpanaṃ. saiva saṃpad iti. iyaṃ vā caturvidhopakārasaṃpat. anupadiṣṭajñānam iti svayam abhisaṃbodhanārthena. sarvatrajñānamn iti niravaśeṣasvalakṣaṇāvabodhanārthena. sarvathājñānam iti. sarvaprakārāvabodhanārthena. ayatnajñānam itīcchāmātrāvabodhanārthena sarvakleśaprahāṇam iti traidhātukadarśanabhāvanāheyakleśocchitteḥ atyantaprahāṇam ity aparihāṇitaḥ. savāsanaprahāṇam iti. anubaṃdhābhāvataḥ. sarvasamāpattyāvaraṇaprahāṇam ity ubhayatobhāgavimukteḥ. bāhyaviṣayanirmāṇapariṇāmādhiṣṭhānavaśitvasaṃpad iti. tatrāpūrvabāhyaviṣayotpādanaṃ nirmāṇam. aśmādīnāṃ suvarṇādibhāvāpādanaṃ pariṇāmaḥ. dīrghakālāvasthānam adhiṣṭhānam iti. āyuṣa utsarge 'dhiṣṭhāne ca vaśitvasaṃpad āyurutsargādhiṣṭhānavaśitvasaṃpad iti. āvṛteti vistaraḥ. āvṛtagamanaṃ cākāśagamanaṃ ca sudūrakṣipragamanaṃ ca. brāhmaṇād ity anavad ekaśeṣaḥ. alpe bahūnāṃ praveśaḥ. paramāṇau bahūnāṃ hastyādīnāṃ [Tib. 317b] praveśaḥ. sa cety āvṛtākāśāsudūrakṣipragamanālpabahupahupraveśaḥ. tayor vaśitvasaṃpad iti yojyaṃ. vividhā nānāprakārā nijāḥ svābhāvikāḥ. ke. āścaryadharmāḥ. teṣāṃ saṃpad iti yojyaṃ. dharmataiṣā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ yat teṣāṃ gacchatāṃ nimnasthalaṃ ca samībhavati. yad uccaṃ. tan nicībhavati. yan nīcaṃ. tad uccībhavati. aṃdhāś cakṣūṃṣi pratilabhaṃte. badhirāḥ śrotram. unmattāḥ smṛtim iti yathāsūtraṃ sarvam anusartavyaṃ. lakṣaṇasaṃpad iti. dvātriṃśatāṃ mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇānām ūrṇoṣṇīṣādīnāṃ saṃpat. anuvyaṃjanasaṃpad iti. vṛttāṃgulitāmratuṃganakhatvādīnāṃ aśīter anuvyaṃjanānāṃ saṃpat. balasaṃpan nārāyaṇaṃ balaṃ. vajrasārāṇy asthīny asyeti vājrasārāsthi. vajrasārāsthiśarīram asyeti vajrasārāsthiśarīraḥ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasya saṃpad iti. vajrasārāsthiśarīratāsaṃpad iti.
body.translated_text: — from that, ultimate liberation. That itself is the accomplishment. Or, the accomplishment of establishing [beings] in the three vehicles and in the good destinies. [Tib. 317a] In the three vehicles — the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle and the rest — and in good destinies — establishing [beings]. That itself is the accomplishment. Or this is the fourfold accomplishment of benefit. 'Uninstructed knowledge' — for the purpose of self-awakening. 'Omniscient knowledge' — for the purpose of apprehending all specific characteristics without remainder. 'Knowledge in all ways' — for the purpose of apprehending in all modes. 'Effortless knowledge' — for the purpose of apprehending by mere wish. 'Abandonment of all afflictions' — because of the cutting off of afflictions to be abandoned by seeing and cultivation in the three realms. 'Ultimate abandonment' — because of non-regression. 'Abandonment together with the dispositions (<s>vāsanā</s>)' — because of the absence of traces (<s>anubandha</s>). 'Abandonment of all obstructions to attainments' — because of being liberated in both ways (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>). 'Accomplishment of mastery over the creation, transformation, and sustaining of external objects' — therein, creation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) is the production of previously non-existent external objects. Transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) is the bringing of stones and the like to the state of gold and the like. Sustaining (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) is maintaining for a long time. Accomplishment of mastery over relinquishing and sustaining the life-span — the accomplishment of mastery over relinquishing the life-span and sustaining it. 'Concealed' — and so forth in detail. Concealed going, sky-going, and going very far in an instant. 'From a Brahmin' — and so forth — this is a singular remainder (<s>ekaśeṣa</s>). The entry of many into a small [space] — the entry of many elephants and the like [Tib. 317b] into an atom. 'And that' — the concealed, sky, very-far, and instantaneous goings, and the entry of many into a small space and of a small space into many — the accomplishment of mastery over both of those should be connected. 'Various' — of many kinds; 'natural' — inherent. Which? — wondrous <s>dharma</s>s. Their accomplishment — this should be connected. It is the nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) of <s>Buddha</s>s, the <s>Bhagavān</s>s, that as they walk, uneven ground becomes level; what is high becomes low, what is low becomes high; the blind obtain eyes, the deaf obtain hearing, the mad obtain mindfulness — all of this should be followed as in the <s>sūtra</s>. 'Accomplishment of marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>)' — the accomplishment of the thirty-two marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) — <s>ūrṇā</s>, <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>, and the rest. 'Accomplishment of secondary marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>)' — the accomplishment of eighty secondary marks — rounded fingers, copper-colored prominent nails, and the rest. 'Accomplishment of strength' — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> strength. 'Diamond-essence bones' — one whose bones are of diamond-essence. 'A body with diamond-essence bones' — one who has a body with diamond-essence bones. Its state — its accomplishment — the accomplishment of having a body with diamond-essence bones.

body.text: etat sāmāsikaṃ sāṃkṣepikaṃ. ye kecit prasādajātāḥ satpuruṣā buddhaṃ bhagavantam astāviṣuḥ stuvanti stoṣyaṃti vā. sarve te etayaiva trividhayā saṃpadeti. yady anekā asaṃkhyeyāḥ kalpā asyety anekāsaṃkhyeyakalpaṃ jīvitaṃ. tad yady adhitiṣṭheyur buddhā bhagavantaḥ. [Tib. 318a] evaṃ te sakalaṃ tanmāhātmyaṃ jñātuṃ vaktuṃ vaktuṃ ca samarthāḥ. tasyānantaprabhedatvenātibahutvād ity abjiprāyaḥ. evaṃ ca tāvad iti vistaraḥ. guṇāś ca jñānāni ca prabhāvaś
body.translated_text: This is summarized, in brief. Whatever faithful, virtuous persons have praised, are praising, or will praise the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> — all of them [praise him] through just this threefold accomplishment. If <s>Buddha</s>s, the <s>Bhagavān</s>s, were to sustain a lifespan of innumerable many <s>kalpa</s>s — [Tib. 318a] even so, they would be capable of knowing and expressing that entire greatness. Because of the infinite varieties [of his qualities] — this is the intent. 'And thus' — and so forth in detail. The qualities, the knowledges, the power

body.text: copakāraś ceti dvaṃdvaḥ. anantāś ca te 'dbhutāś ceti punaḥ karmadhārayaḥ. eta eva mahāratnāni. teṣām ākarās tathāgatāḥ. atha ca punar bālāḥ pṛthagjanāḥ svaguṇadāridryeṇānumānabhūtena hatādhimokṣā hatarucayaḥ yāvad buddhaṃ nādriyaṃte buddhe nādaraṃ kurvantīty arthaḥ. śraddhāmātrakeṇāpīti. niradhigamenety arthaḥ. aniyatavipākānām iti. niyatavipākānām alaṃghanīyatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. deveṣu bhasvā daivī. avaṃdhyeṣṭaprakṛṣṭāśusvaṃtaphalatvād iti. avaṃdhyaphalaṃ phaladānanaiyamyenāvasthānāt. iṣṭaphalaṃ divyaviṣayaphalatvāt. prakṛṣṭaphalaṃ prabhūtaphalatvāt. āśuphalaṃ dṛṣṭadharmādivedanīyaphalatvāt. svantaphalaṃ nirvāṇāphalatvāt. tadbhāvāt. anuttaraṃ puṇyakṣetram ucyaṃte tathāgatā iti. kārān ity upakārān pūjādikān.
body.translated_text: and the benefit — this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. And they are infinite, and they are wondrous — this again is a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound. These very things are the great jewels. Their mines are the <s>Tathāgata</s>s. And yet, foolish ordinary persons, with their confidence diminished and their interest destroyed by the poverty of their own qualities — which serves as a measure [of their blindness] — [Tib. 317b] do not honor the <s>Buddha</s> — the meaning is: they do not show respect to the <s>Buddha</s>. 'Even through faith alone' — the meaning is: without any realization. 'Of those whose fruition is indeterminate' — the intent is: because the fruition of those with determinate fruition cannot be transgressed. 'Among gods, a divine splendor.' 'Because of having unfailing, desired, excellent, swift, and self-ending fruit' — unfailing fruit, because of standing firm in the certainty of giving fruit; desired fruit, because of having divine objects as its fruit; excellent fruit, because of abundant fruit; swift fruit, because of having fruit experienceable in this very life and the like; self-ending fruit, because of having <s>nirvāṇa</s> as its fruit. Because of being such [a field]. 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>s are called unsurpassed fields of merit.' 'Benefits' — services, such as worship and the like.

body.text: (VII.41) yathāyogam iti. yathāsaṃbhavaṃ. [Tib. 318b] kecid guṇāḥ śrāvakasādhāraṇā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ araṇāpraṇidhijñānādayaḥ. kecit pṛthagjanasādhāraṇāḥ abhijñādhyānārāpyādayaḥ. ādiśabdena śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitādayo gṛhyante.
body.translated_text: (VII.41) 'As applicable' — as possible. [Tib. 318b] Some qualities of <s>Buddha</s>s, the <s>Bhagavān</s>s, are shared with <s>śrāvaka</s>s — <s>araṇā</s>, <s>praṇidhijñāna</s>, and the rest. Some are shared with ordinary persons — <s>abhijñā</s>s, <s>dhyāna</s>s, formless [attainments], and the rest. By the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>), wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), and the rest are included.

body.text: (VII.42) na kasyacit tadālaṃbano rāga utpadyate dveṣo māno veti. tenātmano darśanādiparihārāt. yathāyathā ca tenābhisamitaṃ bhavaty araṇāsamādher abhyutthitenāsya māṃ dṛṣṭvā rāga utpatsyate asya dveṣaḥ asya māna asyāprasāda utpatsyate iti. tathātathā vyutthito 'pi tasmāt samādher anuveṣṭate. paracittarakṣaṇopāyaviśeṣe tu tasyāraṇāsamādher utpattimātrasāmarthyād eva pareṣāṃ kleśo notpadyata ity artho gṛhyate. raṇayatīti kleśayatīty arthaḥ. sukhapratipadām agratvāc caturthadhyānasya tadbhūmikaivāraṇā. nānyadhyānabhūmikā. parihartuṃ na śaknotīti parihāṇi saṃbhavāt.
body.translated_text: (VII.42) 'No desire arises in anyone taking that as object, nor hatred, nor pride' — thereby, avoidance of seeing oneself and so forth [is ensured]. And whatever the one who has emerged from the <s>araṇā</s>-<s>samādhi</s> has realized: 'desire will arise in this person upon seeing me, hatred in this one, pride in this one, lack of faith will arise in this one' — accordingly, even after emerging from that <s>samādhi</s>, one arranges oneself [accordingly]. But with respect to the special means of protecting others' minds — by the mere power of the arising of that <s>araṇā</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, afflictions do not arise in others — this meaning is understood. '<s>Raṇayati</s>' means 'afflicts' — this is the meaning. Because the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is the best of the pleasant practices, the <s>araṇā</s> belongs to that ground alone — not to another <s>dhyāna</s>-ground. 'Cannot avoid' — because regression is possible.

body.text: ke. rāgādayo bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ. avastukāḥ kleśā darśanaprahātavyāḥ. sarvatragāḥ sakalasvabhūmyālaṃbanatvāt parasaṃtatyālaṃbanā api bhavantīti. parihartum aśakyāḥ sarvatragāḥ. [Tib. 319a]
body.translated_text: which ones? — desire and the rest, to be abandoned by cultivation. 'Afflictions without [a real] object (<s>avastuka</s>)' — those to be abandoned by seeing. 'Universal (<s>sarvatraga</s>)' — because of having one's own entire ground as object-domain, and because they can also have another's continuum as object-domain. The universal ones cannot be avoided. [Tib. 319a]

children.translated_text: 'But that has all [dharmas] as its object' —

body.text: iti. sarvam ālaṃbata iti sarvālaṃbanaṃ. sarvo vāsyālaṃbana iti sarvālambanaṃ. nāraṇāvat kleśamātrālambanaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. rūpādyālaṃbanam apīty arthaḥ. ārūpyas tu na sākṣāt praṇidhijñānena jñāyante. kim kāraṇaṃ. yasmāt praṇidhijñānaṃ caturthadhyānabhūmikaṃ. vakṣyati ca
body.translated_text: thus. It takes all as its object — hence 'having all as its object.' Or all is its object — hence 'having all as its object.' Unlike <s>araṇā</s>, it does not have only afflictions as its object. Rather, it also has form and the rest as its object — this is the meaning. But the formless [beings] are not known directly by <s>praṇidhijñāna</s>. For what reason? Because <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> belongs to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground. And he will state:

children.translated_text: 'The <s>abhijñā</s> has its own and lower grounds as its domain' —

body.text: iti. praṇidhijñānaṃ cābhijñāvat bhavatīti. niṣyandacaritaviśeṣād iti. tatra niṣyaṃdo mandamandatā. caritam ārūpyasamāpattivihāraḥ. tad evaṃ kāryeṇāsyānumānaṃ. kāraṇena ca kāryāsyeti paridīpitam. tataḥ pracyutānāṃ tatsamāpattilābhiṇāṃ ca tad ubhayaṃ pratyakṣaṃ. kārṣakanidarśanaṃ cātreti. yathā kārṣakaḥ phalena bījaṃ pratipadyate. bījena vā phalam iti. yathā vā kārṣako jānīte īdṛśe kṣetre īdṛśāphalaṃ dhānyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. dhānyaṃ vā dṛṣṭvā kṣetram anuminoti. īdṛśam asya kṣetram iti. evaṃ śāntamūrtiṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā anuminoti ārūpyāc cyuto 'yam. ārūpyeṣu copapatsyata iti. vaibhāṣikā iti vacanaṃ. pareṣām asty anenārūpyajñānam iti sūcayati. na hi buddānām asty aviṣaya ity abhiprāyaḥ. [Tib. 319b] praṇidhipūrvakam ity ābhogapūrvakaṃ. praṇidhāyābhujyety arthaḥ. yāvāṃs tatsamādhiviṣaya iti. yāvāṃ cchrāvakasya viṣayaḥ. tāvaj jānāti. pratyekabuddhasya ca yāvatsvaviṣaya ityādi.
body.translated_text: thus. And <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> is like an <s>abhijñā</s>. 'Because of the special character of the outflow-conduct' — therein, the outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>) is gentle slowness. The conduct (<s>carita</s>) is abiding in the formless attainment. Thus, the inference of this [formless being] is through its effect. And through the cause, [inference of] its effect — this has been illuminated. For those who have fallen from that [formless realm], and for those who have obtained that attainment — both of those are direct perception. 'And there is the illustration of the farmer' — just as a farmer infers the seed from the fruit, or the fruit from the seed. Or just as a farmer knows: 'in such a field, grain of such a fruit will grow.' Or seeing the grain, he infers the field: 'such is its field.' Similarly, seeing a being of peaceful appearance, one infers: 'this one has fallen from the Formless [Realm]' and 'this one will be reborn in the Formless [Realms].' The mention of '<s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s' indicates that for others, there is knowledge of the Formless [beings] by this [<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>]. The intent is: for <s>Buddha</s>s, there is no [domain that is] outside [their knowledge]. [Tib. 319b] 'Preceded by aspiration' — preceded by intent (<s>ābhoga</s>). Having aspired, one applies — this is the meaning. 'To the extent of the domain of that <s>samādhi</s>' — to the extent that is the domain of a <s>śrāvaka</s>, that much one knows. And to the extent of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>'s own domain — and so forth.

body.text: (VII.43-45) dharmapratisaṃvid iti. iha deśanādharmaḥ. anekārtho hi dharmaśabdaḥ. tadyathā dharmaṃ vo bhikṣavo deśayiṣyāmi. ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayiṣyāmiti, atra deśanādharmaḥ. dharmaḥ katamaḥ. āryāṣṭāṃgamārga ity atra pratipattidharmaḥ. tathā dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchetety atra phaladharmo nirvāṇam ityādi. avivartyam iti. aśakyaṃ vivartayituṃ. akopyadharmamanuṣyāśrayatvam iti tathāśabdenedam evārthadvayaṃ saṃbadhyate. ālambanādīnāṃ pṛthagvacanāt. yuktamuktābhilāpitāyām iti. yuktam arthasaṃbaṃdhaṃ. muktam asaktaṃ. yuktamuktam abhilapatīti yuktamuktābhilāpī. tadbhāvaḥ. tasyāṃ. yuktamuktābhilāpitāyāṃ. samādhau vaśī samādhivaśī. samādhivaśinaḥ saṃprakhyānam asaṃmoṣaḥ. samādhivaśisaṃprakhyānaṃ. [Tib. 320a] tatra cāvivartyaṃ jñānaṃ pratibhānapratisaṃvid iti viśeṣaḥ. kathaṃ. navajñānasvabhāvā pratibhānapratisaṃvit. yā vāgālambanā. sā duḥkhasamudayadharmānvayakṣayānutpādasaṃvṛtijñānasvabhāvā. yā mārgālambanā. sā mārgadharmānvayakṣayānutpādaparacittasaṃvṛtijñānasvabhāvety abhisamasya navajñānasvabhāvā anyatra nirodhajñānāt. sarvadharmāś ced artho daśa jñānānīti. na hi so 'sti dharmaḥ. yo daśānāṃ jñānānāṃ yathāsaṃbhavaṃ nālambanībhavati. nirvāṇāṃ ced arthaḥ ṣaṭ jñānānīti. nirodhajñānasya dharmajñānādipaṃcasvabhāvatvāt.
body.translated_text: (VII.43-45) '<s>Dharmapratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of <s>dharma</s>s)' — here, the <s>dharma</s> of teaching is meant. For the word '<s>dharma</s>' has many meanings. For instance: 'I shall teach you the <s>dharma</s>, O monks — good in the beginning, good in the middle, good at the end, with good meaning, with good words — I shall reveal the holy life that is complete, perfect, pure, and spotless' — here, it is the <s>dharma</s> of teaching. 'What is the <s>dharma</s>? The Noble Eightfold Path' — here, it is the <s>dharma</s> of practice. Similarly, 'one should go for refuge to the <s>dharma</s>' — here, the fruit-<s>dharma</s> is <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and so forth. 'Irreversible' — impossible to reverse. 'Unshakable nature and human basis' — by the word 'thus,' these two very meanings are connected. 'Because of the separate statement of object-domain and the rest.' 'In correctly-and-freely-spoken speech' — what is correct (<s>yukta</s>) is connected with meaning; what is free (<s>mukta</s>) is unattached. One who speaks in a correctly-and-freely manner is a correctly-and-freely speaker. Its state — in that correctly-and-freely-spoken speech. 'One who has mastery in <s>samādhi</s>' — a master of <s>samādhi</s>. The clear comprehension of the master of <s>samādhi</s> — the non-confusion — is the clear comprehension of the master of <s>samādhi</s>. [Tib. 320a] Therein, the irreversible knowledge within that is the <s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of ready speech) — this is the distinction. How? The <s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s> has nine knowledges as its own-nature. That which has speech as its object — that has the own-nature of the <s>duḥkha</s>-, <s>samudaya</s>-, <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>kṣaya</s>-, <s>anutpāda</s>-, and <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>s. That which has the path as its object — that has the own-nature of <s>mārga</s>-, <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>kṣaya</s>-, <s>anutpāda</s>-, <s>paracitta</s>-, and <s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>s — thus, taking them together, it has nine knowledges as its own-nature, excluding the <s>nirodhajñāna</s>. 'If all <s>dharma</s>s are the object, ten knowledges' — for there is no <s>dharma</s> that does not become the object of the ten knowledges as applicable. 'If <s>nirvāṇa</s> is the object, six knowledges' — because <s>nirodhajñāna</s> has five own-natures: <s>dharmajñāna</s> and so forth.

body.text: nāmakāyādivāgālambanatvād iti. na hi duḥkhādijñānam anāsravaṃ duḥkhaikadeśaṃ samudayaikadeśaṃ vā svalakṣaṇākāreṇālambate. kiṃ tarhi. paṃcopādānaskaṃdhān sāmānyalakṣaṇākāraiḥ. atas te saṃvṛtijñānasvabhāve iti. ūrdhvaṃ nāmakāyabhāvād iti. ārūpyadhātau dharmapratisaṃvin nāstīti. yatra ca nāmakāyāḥ. tatraiva padavyañjanakāyā iti [Tib. 320b] tulyavārttā. nāmakāyabhāvavacanena padavyañjanakāyābhāvasiddhiḥ. ūrdhvaṃ vitarkābhāvād iti. dvitīyadhyānādiṣu. vitarkya vicārya vācaṃ bhāṣata iti sūtraṃ nāmādyālambanatvaṃ punar āsāṃ pratisaṃvidāṃ samāpannasyāpi. vyutthitasyāpi tatpṛṣṭhalabdhair avivartyair jñānair nāmādyālambanatvaṃ. bhāṣaṇaṃ punas tatpṛṣṭhenaiva. strīpuruṣādyadhivacana iti. ādiśabdena kālakārakādisaṃgrahaḥ. adhivacanaṃ punaḥ paryāyaḥ. tad adhikṛtya vā vacanaṃ tadadhivacanaṃ. tasyāsaktatāyām iti. tasyādhivacanasya tasya padavyañjanasya vā. ata evāsāṃ kramasiddhir iti. yataḥ padavyañjanānusāreṇārthapratipattiḥ. tasyaikadvibahustrīpuruṣādyadhivacanaṃ tasyāsaktatety ataḥ kramasiddhir iti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of having name-groups (<s>nāmakāya</s>) and the like — speech — as its object' — for uncontaminated knowledge of suffering and the like does not take a part of suffering or a part of origination as its object through the aspect of specific characteristics. Rather, [it takes] the five aggregates of clinging through aspects of general characteristics. Therefore, those [analytical knowledges pertaining to names, words, and syllables] have the own-nature of conventional knowledge. 'Because of the absence of name-groups above' — in the Formless Realm, there is no <s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s>. And wherever name-groups exist, [Tib. 320b] there alone do word-groups and syllable-groups exist — this is a matter of equal application. By the statement of the absence of name-groups, the absence of word-groups and syllable-groups is established. 'Because of the absence of initial thought (<s>vitarka</s>) above' — in the second <s>dhyāna</s> and above. 'Having investigated and deliberated, one speaks speech' — this is the <s>sūtra</s>. The object-domain of name-groups and the rest by these analytical knowledges — for one who has attained [<s>samādhi</s>] too, and for one who has emerged too — through the irreversible knowledges obtained in the aftermath of that, the object-domain of name-groups and the rest. But speaking is only through the aftermath [knowledge]. 'The designation of woman, man, and the rest' — by the word 'and the rest,' time, agent, and the like are included. The designation (<s>adhivacana</s>) is a synonym. Or: speech regarding that — the designation thereof (<s>tadadhivacana</s>). 'In the non-attachment to that' — of that designation, or of that word and syllable. From this very fact, the order of these [four analytical knowledges] is established — since apprehension of meaning follows words and syllables. The designation of that as 'one, two, many, woman, man, and the rest' — in the non-attachment to that — from this, the order is established.

body.text: tasmād rūpam ity evaṃādīti. ādiśabdena vijānātīti vijñānaṃ. cinotīti cittam ity evamādi saṃgrahataḥ. uttarottarapratibhā pratibhānam iti vādanyāyena. yathākramam iti. dharmapratisaṃvido gaṇitaṃ pūrvaprayogaḥ. arthapratisaṃvido buddhavacanaṃ. niruktipratisaṃvidaḥ śabdavidyā. pratibhānapratisaṃvido hetuvidyeti. buddhavacanam eveti vaibhāṣikāḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, form' — and examples of this kind. By the word 'and the rest,' 'one cognizes, hence <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); one accumulates, hence <s>citta</s> (mind)' — and examples of this kind should be included. 'Progressively higher eloquence (<s>pratibhā</s>) is ready speech (<s>pratibhāna</s>)' — according to the method of debaters. 'In order' — the enumeration (<s>gaṇita</s>) of <s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s> corresponds to a preliminary practice. The <s>arthapratisaṃvid</s> corresponds to the word of the <s>Buddha</s>. The <s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s> corresponds to the science of grammar (<s>śabdavidyā</s>). The <s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s> corresponds to the science of reasoning (<s>hetuvidyā</s>). 'The word of the <s>Buddha</s> alone' — [say] the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s.

body.text: iti. [Tib. 321a] kiṃcic caturthaṃ dhyānam araṇātmakaṃ. kiṃcit praṇidhijñānātmakaṃ. kiṃcit tripratisaṃvidātmakaṃ. kiṃcit tadvyatiriktaṃ kevalaṃ prāntakoṭikam iti. tisraḥ pratisaṃvida iti. niruktipratisaṃvidaṃ muktvā tatra vitarkābhāvāt. savitarkavicāreṇa tadutthāpanaṃ. kathaṃ tarhy aviśeṣeṇaitad uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. Some [portions of] the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> have the nature of <s>araṇā</s> (non-conflict). Some have the nature of <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> (resolution-knowledge). Some have the nature of the three <s>pratisaṃvid</s>s (analytical knowledges). And some, being distinct from those, are merely <s>prāntakoṭika</s> (culminating). 'Three <s>pratisaṃvid</s>s' — excluding the <s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of etymology), because of the absence of <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) there. 'Its production through [meditation] accompanied by initial and sustained application' — but how then is it stated without distinction:

body.text: iti. ete ucyante. niruktipratisaṃvidaḥ tadbalena lābho na tu sā caurthadhyānabhūmikā. kiṃ tarhi. kāmadhātuprathamadhyānabhūmikety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. These are said [to be so]. The <s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s> is obtained through the power of that [fourth <s>dhyāna</s>], but it itself does not belong to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground. Rather, it belongs to the Desire Realm and the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground — this is the meaning.

body.text: iti. sarvabhūmyanukūlitam ity arthaḥ. pragatā antā koṭir asyeti. pragatā antaṃ prāntā. prāntā koṭir asyeti prāntakoṭikā. catuṣkoṭikavad iti. yathā catuṣkoṭikaś catuḥprakārapraśnaḥ. tadvat.
body.translated_text: meaning adapted to all grounds. 'Having reached the extreme limit' (<s>prāntakoṭika</s>) — the extreme (<s>prānta</s>) is that which has gone to the end (<s>anta</s>). The extreme limit (<s>prāntakoṭi</s>) is the end-point of that which has reached the extreme. Just like a four-cornered [analysis] (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>) — just as the four-cornered [analysis] is a question of four types — so too [is this].

body.text: (VII.47-50) ṛddhiviṣayeti vistaraḥ. ṣaḍ abhijñāḥ. ṛddhiviṣayajñānasākṣātkriyādivyaśrotracetaḥparyāgapūrvenivāsacyutyupapādāsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā iti. sūtraṃ cātra. iha bhikṣur anekavidham ṛddhiviṣayaṃ pratyanubhavati. eko bhūtvā bahudhā bhavati bahudhābhūtvā eko bhavatīti vistaragraṃtha ṛddhipādā ity atra likhito draṣṭavyaḥ. yāvad iyam ucyate ṛddhiviṣayajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñeti. iha bhikṣur divyena śrotreṇa viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakeṇa ubhayāṃ cchabdān śṛṇoti mānuṣān amānuṣān api ye vā dūre [Tib. 321b] ye vāntika iti. iyaṃ ucyate divyaśrotrajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā. ikha bhikṣur divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāṃtamānuṣyakeṇa sattvān paśyatīti bahuḥ sūtravad granthaḥ. yāvad iyam ucyate divyacakṣurjñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā. iha bhikṣur anekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsam anusmaratīti bahuḥ sūtravad granthaḥ. yāvad iyam ucyate pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā. iha bhikṣuḥ parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ vitarkitaṃ vicaritaṃ manasā mānasaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. sarāgacittaṃ sarāgaṃ cittam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. vigatarāgaṃ vigatarāgam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. sadveṣaṃ vigatadveṣaṃ samohaṃ vigatamohaṃ vikṣiptaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ līnaṃ pragṛhītam uddhatam anuddhatam avyupaśāntaṃ vyupaśāntaṃ samāhitam asamāhitam abhāvitaṃ bhāvitam avimuktaṃ cittam avimuktaṃ cittam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. vimuktaṃ cittaṃ vimuktaṃ cittam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. iyam ucyate cetaḥparyāyajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā. iha bhikṣur idaṃ duḥkham āryasatyam iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ. ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ. iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam [Tib. 322a] iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti. tasyaivaṃ jānata evaṃ paśyataḥ kāmāsravāc cittaṃ vimucyate. bhavāsravād avidāsravāc cittaṃ vimucyate. vimuktasya vimukto 'smīti jñānadarśanaṃ bhavati. kṣīṇā me jātir yāvan nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajanāmīti. iyam ucyate āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā. ṛddhiḥ samādhiḥ. ṛddhiviṣayo nirmāṇaṃ gamanaṃ ca. ṛddhiviṣaye jñānaṃ. tasya sākṣātkriyā saṃmukhībhāvaḥ. ṛddhiviṣayajñānasakṣātkriyābhijñā. divyaṃ śrotraṃ. tatra jñānaṃ. tasya sākṣātkriyā divyaśrotrajñānasākṣatkriyā. cetaḥparyāyo viśeṣaḥ. raktaṃ dviṣṭaṃ mūḍham iti vā kramo vā paryāyaḥ. kadācid raktaṃ kadācid dviṣṭaṃ mūḍhaṃ ceti. tatra jñānaṃ. tasya sākṣātkriyā. pūrvenivāsaḥ skaṃdhega ivāluk. tasyānusmṛtiḥ tatra jñānaṃ. tasya sākṣātkriyeti.
body.translated_text: (VII.47-50) 'The domain of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiviṣaya</s>)' — and so forth in detail. The six <s>abhijñā</s>s (direct knowledges) are: the <s>abhijñā</s> of direct realization of knowledge of the domain of supernatural power, the <s>abhijñā</s> of the divine ear, the <s>abhijñā</s> of knowledge of others' mental dispositions, the <s>abhijñā</s> of recollection of former abodes, the <s>abhijñā</s> of death and rebirth, and the <s>abhijñā</s> of direct realization of knowledge of the destruction of the outflows. And the <s>sūtra</s> here [reads]: 'Here a <s>bhikṣu</s> experiences various kinds of supernatural power. Having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one' — the detailed text should be seen as written [earlier] under '<s>ṛddhipāda</s>s.' Up to: 'This is called the <s>abhijñā</s> of direct realization of knowledge of the domain of supernatural power.' 'Here a <s>bhikṣu</s>, with the divine ear, purified and surpassing the human, hears both kinds of sounds — human and non-human, whether distant or near.' This is called the <s>abhijñā</s> of direct realization of knowledge of the divine ear. 'Here a <s>bhikṣu</s>, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, sees beings' — the extensive text is like the <s>sūtra</s>. Up to: 'This is called the <s>abhijñā</s> of direct realization of knowledge of the divine eye.' 'Here a <s>bhikṣu</s> recollects various kinds of former abodes' — the extensive text is like the <s>sūtra</s>. Up to: 'This is called the <s>abhijñā</s> of direct realization of knowledge of recollection of former abodes.' 'Here a <s>bhikṣu</s> truly knows the thoughts, reflections, and mental [activities] of other beings, other persons. He truly knows a mind with desire as a mind with desire. He truly knows a mind free from desire as free from desire. With aversion, free from aversion; with delusion, free from delusion; distracted, contracted; sluggish, uplifted; agitated, non-agitated; not calmed; cultivated; unreleased, released — he truly knows as they really are.' This is called the <s>abhijñā</s> of direct realization of knowledge of others' mental dispositions. 'Here a <s>bhikṣu</s> truly knows: "This is the noble truth of suffering. This is the noble truth of the origin of suffering. This is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering. This is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering." For one thus knowing, thus seeing, the mind is liberated from the outflow of sensual desire, from the outflow of existence, from the outflow of ignorance. In the liberated one, the knowledge and vision arises: "I am liberated." "Birth is exhausted," up to, "I know there is no further existence."' This is called the <s>abhijñā</s> of direct realization of knowledge of the destruction of the outflows. Supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) is concentration (<s>samādhi</s>). The domain of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiviṣaya</s>) is transformation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) and locomotion (<s>gamana</s>). Knowledge of the domain of supernatural power — its direct realization (<s>sākṣātkriyā</s>) is its being brought face to face — [this is] the <s>abhijñā</s> of direct realization of knowledge of the domain of supernatural power. The divine ear — therein, knowledge — its direct realization — [this is] the direct realization of knowledge of the divine ear. Others' mental dispositions (<s>cetaḥparyāya</s>) — a distinctive state. 'Desirous, hateful, deluded' — or alternatively, <s>paryāya</s> means a succession: 'sometimes desirous, sometimes hateful, deluded.' Therein, knowledge — its direct realization. Former abodes (<s>pūrvenivāsa</s>) — like '<s>skandhega</s>,' [an irregular compound] without elision. Their recollection (<s>anusmṛti</s>) — therein, knowledge — its direct realization.

body.text: cyutiś copapādaś ca cyutyupapādau. tayor jñānaṃ. tasya sākṣātkriyā. āsravāṇāṃ kṣayaḥ. tatra jñānaṃ. tasya sākṣātkriyābhijñeti pratyekam abhisaṃbaṃdhaḥ. śrāmaṇyaphalavad iti. yathā saṃskṛtaṃ śrāmaṇyaphalaṃ vimuktimārgasvabhāvaṃ. tadvat.
body.translated_text: Departure and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapāda</s>) — departure and rebirth together. Their knowledge — its direct realization. The destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>) — therein, knowledge — its direct realization — [this is] the <s>abhijñā</s> — thus the individual connection should be made. 'Like the fruit of the ascetic life (<s>śrāmaṇyaphala</s>)' — just as the conditioned fruit of the ascetic life has the own-nature of the liberation path — so too [does this abhijñā].

children.translated_text: 'The [abhijñā] of others' minds consists of five knowledges' —

body.text: iti. cetasi cetaḥparyāyair yābhijñā. [Tib. 322b] sā jñānapaṃcakasvabhāvety arthaḥ. anāsravasya paracittajñānasya dharmānvayamārgaparacittajñānatvasaṃbhavāt. sāsravasya ca saṃvṛtiparacittajñānasaṃbhavāt.
body.translated_text: the <s>abhijñā</s> that is [the knowledge of] others' mental dispositions — that has the own-nature of five knowledges — this is the meaning. Because of the possibility of uncontaminated knowledge of others' minds being <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>mārga</s>-, and <s>paracittajñāna</s>. And because of the possibility of contaminated [knowledge of others' minds being] conventional and <s>paracittajñāna</s>.

body.text: iti. yathāsravakṣayajñānabalam. āsravakṣayajñānam āsravakṣayālambanam iti cet. ṣaṭ jñānāni. nirodhajñānasya dharmānvayakṣayānutpādajñānasaṃjñitatvāt. saṃvṛtijñānasya ca nirodhālambanatvasaṃbhavāt. āsravakṣaye sati yaj jñānaṃ. kṣīṇāsravasaṃtāne taj jñānam iti cet. daśa jñānāni. kṣīṇāsravasaṃtāne daśajñānasadbhāvāt. evam āsravakṣaya ālambanabhūte yābhijñā. sā ced āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyābhijñā. ṣaṭ jñānāni. tadvat. āsravakṣaye sati yābhijñā. sā ced daśa jñānāni. tadvad iti. sarvabhūmikāpy eṣeti.
body.translated_text: meaning like the knowledge-power of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣayajñānabala</s>). If the knowledge of the destruction of the outflows means 'knowledge having the destruction of outflows as its object' — then [it consists of] six knowledges. Because the knowledge of cessation (<s>nirodhajñāna</s>) can be designated as <s>dharma</s>-, <s>anvaya</s>-, <s>kṣaya</s>-, and <s>anutpādajñāna</s>. And because conventional knowledge can have cessation as its object. [But] if the knowledge of the destruction of the outflows means 'knowledge arising when the outflows are destroyed' — knowledge in the continuum of one whose outflows are destroyed — then [it consists of] ten knowledges, because all ten knowledges exist in the continuum of one whose outflows are destroyed. Thus, the <s>abhijñā</s> regarding the destruction of outflows as its object-domain — if that is the <s>abhijñā</s> of direct realization of knowledge of the destruction of the outflows — [it consists of] six knowledges. Like that [power]. [But] the <s>abhijñā</s> arising when the outflows are destroyed — if that [is it] — [it consists of] ten knowledges. Like that [power]. 'This one also belongs to all grounds' —

body.text: ity anenaiva vacanenāyam artho labhyate. yasmāc ca
body.translated_text: by this very statement, this meaning is obtained. And because —

body.text: ity avadhāryate. tasmād apīyam ṣaṣṭhy abhijñā sarvabhūmiketi gamyate.
body.translated_text: this is determined. Therefore, from this too, it is understood that this sixth <s>abhijñā</s> belongs to all grounds.

body.text: tisras tāvan na santīti. ṛddhidivyaśrotradivyacakṣurabhijñā. kasmāt. rūpālaṃbanatvāt. na hy ārūpyāṇāṃ rūpam ālaṃbanam. vibhūtarūpasaṃjñātvāt. rūpatīrthābhiniṣpādyatvād [Tib. 323a] iti. rūpatvadvāraniṣpādyatvāt rūpālaṃbanamārganiṣpādyatvād ity arthaḥ. īdṛśe rūpe īdṛśaṃ cittaṃ bhavatīti na cārūpyāṇāṃ rūpam ālaṃbanaṃ. pūrvenivāsānusmṛtir api nāsty anupūrvāvasthāntarasmaraṇābhiniṣpatteḥ. yasmād anupūrvam ātmano 'vasthāntarāṇi smaranto niṣpādayanti. na cārūpyāṇāṃ kāmāvacarā dharmā ālaṃbanaṃ. vakṣyati hi
body.translated_text: 'The first three [abhijñās] do not exist [in the Formless Realm]' — the <s>abhijñā</s>s of supernatural power, divine ear, and divine eye. Why? Because of having form as their object. For the formless [attainments] do not have form as their object — because of having transcended the perception of form. 'Because of being accomplished through the gateway of form' — meaning because of being accomplished through the gateway of form, because of being accomplished through the path that has form as its object. 'In such a form, such a mind arises' — and the formless [attainments] do not have form as their object. The <s>abhijñā</s> of recollection of former abodes also does not exist [there] — because of being accomplished through the sequential recollection of successive states. Since they accomplish it by sequentially remembering one's own successive states — and the formless [attainments] do not have Desire Realm <s>dharma</s>s as their object. For he will state:

children.translated_text: 'The fundamental wholesome formless [attainments], being contaminated, do not have a lower [realm] as their domain' —

body.text: iti. tāni cāvasthāntarāṇy ātmanaḥ kāmāvacarāṇy abhiniṣpādanakāle tasyālambanam ity etasmāt tadbhūmikā nāstīti. sthānagotrādyālambanatvāc ca. tasmād api cyuto 'mutropapannaḥ. tathā hi sūtra uktaṃ. amī nāma
body.translated_text: thus. And those successive states of oneself that belong to the Desire Realm are at the time of accomplishment the object of that [recollection] — therefore it does not belong to that ground. And because of having location, clan, and the rest as object. From this too: 'having departed from that place, he was reborn elsewhere.' For thus the <s>sūtra</s> states: 'Those

body.text: te sattvāḥ. yatrāham abhūvam evaṃnāmā evaṃgotra evaṃjātir evamāhāra evaṃsukhaduḥkhapratisaṃvedī evaṃdīrghāyur evaṃcirasthitika evamāyuṣparyantaḥ. yo 'haṃ tasmāc cyuto 'mutropapannaḥ. tasmād api cyuto ['mutropapannaḥ tasmāc cyuta] ihopapanna iti sākāraṃ soddeśam anekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsam anusmaratīti. na cārūpyāḥ sthānagotrādyālambanāḥ [Tib. 323b] adhobhūmyālambanāś cety etasmād api kāraṇān nārūpyabhūmikāḥ. kathaṃ paracittajñānaṃ rūpatīrthābhiniṣpādyam ity ata āha. paracittaṃ hi jñātukāma iti vistaraḥ. ābhujata iti. ābhogaṃ kurvataḥ. nimittaṃ udgṛhyeti. cittaprakāraṃ paricchidyety arthaḥ. tatprātilomyeneti. tasyaiva cittasya pratīpaṃ samanantaraniruddhāny avasthāntarāṇi manasikaroti. vilaṃghyāpi smaraṇam iti. ekaṃ janma dve vā vilaṃghyāpi vyatikramyāpi smaraṇaṃ. śuddhāvāsānāṃ kathaṃ smaraṇam iti. yady anubhūtapūrvasyaiva smaraṇaṃ. na hi śuddhāvāsānām ihāgamanam asty anāgāmitvāt. tena naiṣām ihānubhūtiḥ. nāpi tatra. pṛthagjanānāṃ tatrānupapatteḥ. śravaṇevānubhūtatvād iti. śrutaṃ hi tena bhavati. śuddhāvāsā nāma devā evaṃbhūtā iti. dvividho hy anubhavo darśanānubhavaḥ śravaṇānubhavaś ca. parasaṃtatyadhiṣṭhānenotpādanam iti. dhyānasaṃgṛhītaṃ pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānaṃ. tena cārūpyāvacaraṃ cittaṃ na gṛhṇāti. kathaṃ ca punaḥ parasaṃtatyadhiṣṭhānenotpādanaṃ. samanaṃtaraniruddhān manovijñānāt parakīyān nimittam udgṛhyeti vistaraḥ. anyeṣām iti. ya ārūpyebhyo na pracyutāḥ. teṣāṃ svasaṃtatyadhiṣṭhānenaivotpādanaṃ pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānasya sukaratvāt.
body.translated_text: beings had such names. Where I was, I had such a name, such a clan, such a birth, such food, such an experience of pleasure and pain, such a lifespan, such a duration of life, such a limit of lifespan. Having departed from that place, I was reborn elsewhere. Having departed from there too, [I was reborn elsewhere. Having departed from there,] I was reborn here' — thus, with its characteristics, with its specifications, he recollects various kinds of former abodes. And the formless [attainments] do not have location, clan, and the rest as their object, nor do they have a lower ground as their object — from this reason too they do not belong to the formless ground. How is the knowledge of others' minds accomplished through the gateway of form? Therefore he says: 'For one who desires to know others' minds' — and so forth in detail. 'Of one who applies himself' (<s>ābhujata</s>) — meaning: of one who makes an effort. 'Having grasped the sign' (<s>nimittam udgṛhya</s>) — meaning: having discerned the mode of mind. 'In reverse order of that' (<s>tatprātilomyena</s>) — he attends to the successive states that have just ceased, in reverse order of that very mind. 'Recollection even by skipping' — recollection even by skipping one or two births — even by passing over them. 'How is recollection [possible] for those in the Pure Abodes (<s>śuddhāvāsa</s>)?' — if recollection is only of what was previously experienced — for there is no coming here from the Pure Abodes, because of being non-returners (<s>anāgāmin</s>). Therefore, they have no experience here. Nor [do they have experience] there — because ordinary persons are not reborn there. 'Because of being experienced through hearing' — for he has heard: 'There are <s>deva</s>s called those of the Pure Abodes who are of such a nature.' For experience is of two kinds: experience through seeing and experience through hearing. 'Production through the empowerment of another's continuum' — the knowledge of recollection of former abodes included in <s>dhyāna</s> — by that, the mind belonging to the Formless Realm is not apprehended. And how does production through the empowerment of another's continuum [work]? 'Having grasped the sign from the mental consciousness of another that has just ceased' — and so forth in detail. 'Of others' — of those who have not departed from the formless [realms]. For them, the production of the knowledge of recollection of former abodes through the empowerment of one's own continuum alone [is easy] — because of the ease [of accomplishing it].

body.text: ṛddhyādīnām iti. ṛddhidivyaśrotradivyacakṣurabhijñānāṃ [Tib. 324a] tisṛṇāṃ yathākramaṃ laghutvamanasikaraṇam ṛddheḥ prayogaḥ. śabdamanasikaraṇaṃ divyaśrotrasya. ālokamanasikaraṇaṃ divyacakṣuṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Of supernatural power and the rest' — of the three <s>abhijñā</s>s of supernatural power, divine ear, and divine eye, respectively in order: the preliminary practice of supernatural power is the attention to lightness (<s>laghutvamanasikaraṇa</s>); of the divine ear, the attention to sound (<s>śabdamanasikaraṇa</s>); of the divine eye, the attention to light (<s>ālokamanasikaraṇa</s>).

body.text: katham etā labhyaṃta iti prāptim adhikṛtya praśnaḥ. saṃmukhībhāvas tu citānām anucitānāṃ ca prayogata eva. anucitāḥ prayogata iti. vaiśeṣikyo yā anutpāditapūrvāḥ. sarvāsāṃ tu prayogenotpādanam iti. yāś ca vairāgyāl labhyante. yāś ca prayogataḥ. tāsāṃ sarvāsāṃ.
body.translated_text: 'How are these obtained?' — the question is with respect to acquisition. But the bringing face-to-face of both practiced and unpracticed [<s>abhijñā</s>s occurs] through effort alone. 'Unpracticed ones through effort' — the special ones that have not been previously produced. But the production of all [<s>abhijñā</s>s] is through effort. And whatever are obtained through dispassion, and whatever through effort — of all of those.

body.text: anyatra śabdād iti uccheditvāc chabdo na nirmīyate. vakṣyati hi.
body.translated_text: 'Except for sound' — because sound is perishable, it is not magically created. For he will state:

children.translated_text: 'What is magically created, belonging to the Desire Realm and external, consists of four sense-spheres (<s>āyatana</s>)' —

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: kathaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. yadi cakṣurabhijñā rūpāyatanālambanā kathaṃ tarhi cyutyupapādajñānenāmī bata bhavantaḥ sattvāḥ kāyaduścaritena samanvāgatā ity evamādi. na vāṅmanaskarmasamanvāgamāś cakṣurvijñānena gṛhyante. ādiśabdena mithyādṛṣṭigrahaṇam. na tad iti. tad vāṅmanaskarmasamanvāgamādi tena cakṣurjñānena na jānāti. kena tarhīty āha. abhijñāparivārajñānaṃ tu tad iti. mānasaṃ tad ity arthaḥ. śeṣe iti. pūrvenivāsānusmṛtyāsravakṣayābhijñe te catuḥsmṛtyupasthānasvabhāve. [Tib. 324b] katham. āsravakṣayābhijñā catuḥsmṛtyupasthānasvabhāvā daśajñānasvabhāvatvat. ṣaṭjñānasvabhāvatve 'pi kāyavedanācittasmṛtyupasthānāny apy anāgatāni bhāvyante.
body.translated_text: 'How then' — and so forth in detail. If the <s>abhijñā</s> of the divine eye has form-sense-sphere (<s>rūpāyatana</s>) as its object, how then does one know through the knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapādajñāna</s>) that 'those beings are endowed with bodily misconduct' and so forth? For endowment with verbal and mental <s>karma</s> is not apprehended by eye-consciousness. By the word 'and so forth,' the apprehension of wrong view [is included]. 'Not that' — that endowment with verbal and mental <s>karma</s> and the rest is not known by that eye-knowledge. By what, then? He says: 'But that is the knowledge that accompanies the <s>abhijñā</s>' — meaning it is mental. 'In the remaining [two]' — the <s>abhijñā</s>s of recollection of former abodes and destruction of the outflows — those two have the own-nature of the four foundations of mindfulness. How? The <s>abhijñā</s> of the destruction of the outflows has the own-nature of the four foundations of mindfulness because of having the own-nature of ten knowledges. Even when [it has] the own-nature of six knowledges, the foundations of mindfulness of the body, feeling, and mind — even the future ones — are cultivated.

body.text: kathaṃ tarhi te caturdhyānabhūmike sidhyataḥ. na hi dvitīyādidhyānabhūmikaṃ cakṣurjñānaṃ śrotrajñānaṃ vāsti. cakṣuhśrotravijñānasaṃprayuktatvāt. tayoś ca dvitīyādiṣu dhyāneṣv abhāvāt. vakṣyati hi
body.translated_text: How then are those two [<s>abhijñā</s>s] established as belonging to the four <s>dhyāna</s> grounds? For there is no eye-knowledge or ear-knowledge belonging to the ground of the second <s>dhyāna</s> and above — because of their association with eye-consciousness and ear-consciousness, and because of the absence of those two in the second <s>dhyāna</s> and above. For he will state:

children.text:
kāyākṣiśrotravijñānaṃ vijñaptyutthāpakaṃ ca yat
dvitīyādau tad ādyāptam
children.translated_text: 'The body-consciousness, eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, and that which generates bodily and verbal intimation — in the second [<s>dhyāna</s>] and above, those belong to the first [<s>dhyāna</s>]' —

body.text: iti. āśrayavaśeneti vistaraḥ. cakṣuḥśrotrāśrayavaśena tajjñānayor api caturdhyānabhūmikatvaṃ. cakṣuhśrotre caturdhyānabhūmike vyavasthāpyete. prādhānika eṣa nirdeśo bāhuliko veti. pradhāne bhavaḥ prādhānikaḥ. evaṃ bāhulikaḥ. kuśalā abhijñāḥ pradhānabhūtāḥ. atas tadapekṣayā nirdeśaḥ kriyate. kuśalā prajñābhijñeti. atha vā bāhulyenābhijñāḥ kuśalāḥ. ata evaṃ nirdeśa iti. mudgādibhāve 'pi māṣarāśivyapadeśavat.
body.translated_text: — thus. 'Because of the basis' — in detail. Because of the basis of the eye and ear, those two knowledges too belong to the four <s>dhyāna</s> grounds. The eye and ear are established as belonging to the four <s>dhyāna</s> grounds. 'Is this exposition principal or predominant?' — what exists in the principal is 'principal' (<s>prādhānika</s>); similarly, what exists in the majority is 'predominant' (<s>bāhulika</s>). The wholesome <s>abhijñā</s>s are the principal ones — therefore the exposition is made with reference to those. 'Wholesome <s>prajñā</s> is <s>abhijñā</s>' — alternatively, <s>abhijñā</s>s are predominantly wholesome — therefore the exposition is thus. Just as even when beans (<s>mudga</s>) and the like are present, the designation 'heap of black beans (<s>māṣa</s>)' [applies].

children.translated_text: 'Because of removing [confusion about] the former end and so forth' —

body.text: yāvad yathākramam iit. bhagavadviśeṣādayas tāvad āhuḥ. pūrvāntasaṃmohaṃ pūrvenivāsānusmṛtyā nivartayati. cyutyupapādābhijñaya [Tib. 325a] madhyasaṃmoham. āsravakṣayābhijñayāparāntasaṃmohaṃ. nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmīti. teṣāṃ vyākhyānakārāṇām abhiprāyaḥ. atītaḥ pratyutpanno 'nāgato 'dhvety adhvānukramaḥ. tasmād evam arthagatir iti.
body.translated_text: up to 'in order' — thus. <s>Bhagavadviśeṣa</s> and the other [commentators] first say: one removes confusion about the former end through the recollection of former abodes (<s>pūrvenivāsānusmṛti</s>); confusion about the middle through the <s>abhijñā</s> of death-and-rebirth (<s>cyutyupapāda</s>); confusion about the later end through the <s>abhijñā</s> of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>) — 'I know there is no further existence from this.' That is the intent of those commentators. Past, present, future — this is the order of the time periods. Therefore, thus is the understanding of the meaning.

body.text: ācāryasaṃghabhadras tu vyācaṣṭe. pūrvāntādau nivartanāt. pūrvenivāsābhijñā hi pūrvāntasaṃmohaṃ vyāvartayati. aparāntasaṃmohaṃ cyutyupapādābhijñā. madhyasaṃmoham āsravakṣayābhijñā. ity ataś ca tisṛṇām eva vidyātvaṃ pūrvayātmaparavipaddarśanāt saṃvegotpatteḥ. parayā pareṣām eva. tathā saṃvignasya bhūtārthāvagamāt tṛtīyayeti. kim atra pratipattavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s>, however, explains: 'Because of removing [confusion about] the former end and so forth' — for the <s>abhijñā</s> of recollection of former abodes removes confusion about the former end; the <s>abhijñā</s> of death-and-rebirth removes confusion about the later end; the <s>abhijñā</s> of the destruction of the outflows removes confusion about the middle. And for this reason, only three are <s>vidyā</s>s (knowledges) — because of the arising of revulsion (<s>saṃvega</s>) through seeing one's own and others' misfortune by the first; by the second, of others alone; similarly, because of the comprehension of true reality by the third for one who is revulsed. What should be accepted here?

body.text: ācāryasaṃghabhadravyākhyānam eva yuktarūpaṃ paśyāmaḥ. ācāryasyāpi tathaivābhiprāyo lakṣyate. tathā hi pūrvenivāsacyutyupapādāsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyās tisra ity uktvāha. etā hi pūrvāntāparāntamadhyasaṃmohaṃ vyāvartayanti yathākramam iti. kathaṃ punar gamyateti tisra evābhijñās tisro vidyā iti. yasmād evam āha. aśaikṣī [Tib. 325b] pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānasākṣātkriyā vidyā. aśaikṣī cyutyupapādajñānasākṣātkriyā vidyā. aśaikṣy āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkriyā vidyeti vidyātrayavyavasthāpanānusūtrād eva. evaṃ hy āha. tripiṭo bhavati trividya iti. aśaikṣī vidyeti. anāsravatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. naiva rttate pūrvenivāsacyutyupapadābhijñe na śaikṣyau nāśaikṣyau sāsravatvāt.
body.translated_text: We consider the explanation of <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s> to be fitting. The <s>Ācārya</s> [Vasubandhu]'s intent too appears to be the same. For thus, having stated 'the three direct realizations of the knowledge of former abodes, death-and-rebirth, and destruction of the outflows,' he says: 'For these remove confusion about the former end, the later end, and the middle respectively.' 'But how is it understood that only three <s>abhijñā</s>s are three <s>vidyā</s>s?' Because he says thus: 'The non-learner's direct realization of the knowledge of recollection of former abodes is a <s>vidyā</s>; the non-learner's direct realization of the knowledge of death-and-rebirth is a <s>vidyā</s>; the non-learner's direct realization of the knowledge of the destruction of the outflows is a <s>vidyā</s>' — from the <s>sūtra</s> establishing the triad of <s>vidyā</s>s. For thus he says: 'One who has the three baskets (<s>piṭaka</s>s) possesses the three <s>vidyā</s>s.' 'Non-learner's <s>vidyā</s>' — the intent is: because of being uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>). The <s>abhijñā</s>s of recollection of former abodes and death-and-rebirth are not at all [to be taken as] — neither learner's nor non-learner's — because of being contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>).

body.text: (VII.52) trīṇi prātihāryāṇi yathākramam iti. ṛddhiviṣayābhijñā ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ. cetaḥparyāyābhijñā ādeśanāprātihāryaṃ. īdṛśaṃ te cittam iti. āsravakṣayābhijñā anuśāsanaprātihāryaṃ. yathābhūtopadeśa ity arthaḥ. prātiśabdayor ādikarmabhṛśārthatvād iti. praśabda ādikarmārthaḥ. idam anena karma prārabdham iti. atiśabdaś ca bhṛśārthaḥ atigata iti. tad idam uktaṃ bhavati. vineyamanasām ādita ādau atibhṛśaṃ haraṃty ebhir iti prātihāryāṇi. pratihatamadhyasthānām iti. nairuktaṃ vidhim āśrityoktaṃ. varṇāgamo varṇaviparyayaś ceti yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: (VII.52) 'Three miraculous displays (<s>prātihārya</s>) in order' — the <s>abhijñā</s> of the domain of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiviṣaya</s>) is the miraculous display of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>). The <s>abhijñā</s> of reading others' minds (<s>cetaḥparyāya</s>) is the miraculous display of mind-reading (<s>ādeśanāprātihārya</s>) — 'Your mind is thus.' The <s>abhijñā</s> of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>) is the miraculous display of instruction (<s>anuśāsanaprātihārya</s>) — the meaning is: instruction in accordance with reality. 'Because the syllables <s>prāti</s> have the meanings of initial action and intensity' — the syllable <s>pra</s> has the meaning of initial action — 'this action has been initiated.' The syllable <s>ati</s> has the meaning of intensity — 'surpassed.' What is said is this: they carry away (<s>haranti</s>) the minds of the trainable from the very beginning (<s>āditas</s>), exceedingly (<s>atibhṛśam</s>) — therefore [they are called] <s>prātihārya</s>s (miraculous displays). 'Of those whose [wrong views have been] counteracted' — this is stated based on the etymological method. The addition of letters and transposition of letters should be applied.

body.text: iti. kleśakṣayanāntarīyatvād iti.
body.translated_text: thus. Because of necessarily leading to the destruction of afflictions.

body.text: (VII.53, 54) ṛdhyatīti. saṃpadyata ity arthaḥ. dūrasyāsannādhimokṣeṇeti. adhimokṣeṇa nirvṛttā ādhimokṣikī. yad dūraṃ. tad āsannam adhimucya tenāśv āgamanād ādhimokṣikīty ucyate.
body.translated_text: (VII.53, 54) '<s>Ṛdhyati</s>' — the meaning is: succeeds, accomplishes. 'Through resolving what is distant as near' — accomplished through resolve is 'resolutive' (<s>ādhimokṣikī</s>). What is distant — resolving it as near, and by arriving quickly through that — it is called 'resolutive.'

body.text: iti. nādhyātmikaṃ nirmīyate. tannirmāṇe saty apūrvasattvaprādurbhāvaprasaṃgāt. svaparaśarīrasaṃbaddham iti. yat svātmā siṃhāyate nāgāyate vā. tat svaśarīrasambaddhaṃ. [Tib. 326a] yast svātmano bahir nirmīyate siṃho nāgo vā. tat paraśarīrasaṃbaddhaṃ. dvividhaṃ tathaiveti. svaparaśarīrasaṃbadhaṃ. evaṃ rūpadhātāv iti. yathā kāmadhātūpapanno dvividhaṃ nirmāṇaṃ nirmiṇoti. kāmāvacaraṃ rūpāvacaraṃ ca. tad api dvividhāṃ svaparaśarīrasaṃbaddham iti caturvidhaṃ. evaṃ rūpadhātūpapanno 'pi caturvidhaṃ nirmiṇotīti. aṣṭavidhaṃ samāsato nirmāṇaṃ. vastrābharaṇavan na
body.translated_text: thus. Internal [forms] are not created — because if they were created, it would follow that unprecedented beings would come into existence. 'Connected with one's own and others' bodies' — when one's own self takes the form of a lion or elephant, that is connected with one's own body. When one creates a lion or elephant externally from oneself, that is connected with another's body. 'Both are likewise twofold' — connected with one's own and others' bodies. 'Similarly in the Form Realm' — just as one born in the Desire Realm creates twofold creations — Desire Realm and Form Realm — that too is twofold — connected with one's own and others' bodies — thus fourfold. Similarly, one born in the Form Realm also creates fourfold — thus, in summary, creation is eightfold. 'There is no being-endowed-with' like clothing and ornaments —

body.text: samanvāgama iti. yathā ca vastrābharaṇaiḥ svaśarīrasaṃbaddhair apy asattvasaṃkhyātatvāt indriyādhiṣṭhānāsaṃbandhatvād vā na samanvāgamaḥ. tadvat.
body.translated_text: — just as one is not endowed with (<s>samanvāgama</s>) clothing and ornaments, even though they are connected with one's own body — because they are not counted as sentient beings, or because of the absence of connection with the basis of the sense faculties — similarly [with created forms].

body.text: dvyāyatanam iti. rūpaspraṣṭavyāyatanaṃ. na gandharasāyatanaṃ. samanvāgamābhavād ity abhiprāyaḥ. na śabdāyatanam uccheditvāt. abhighātajatvād ity apare. āgantukatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Two sense-spheres' — the form and tangible sense-spheres. Not the smell and taste sense-spheres — the intent is: because of the absence of being-endowed-with. Not the sound sense-sphere — because of being discontinuous. 'Because of arising from impact' — say others. The intent is: because of being adventitious.

body.text: (VII.55-58) dvitīyadhyānaphalaṃ trīṇīti. adharabhūmike ca dve svabhūmikaṃ ceti. catvāri paṃca ca yojyānīti. tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikāni catvāri. adharabhūmikāni trīṇi svabhūmikaṃ ceti. caturthadhyānabhūmikāni paṃcādarabhūmikāni catvāri svabhūmikaṃ ceti. dvitīyādidhyānaphalam iti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 326b] dvitīyadhyānaphalaṃ nirmāṇam yan nirmātrā nirmitaṃ. prathamadhyānabhūmikān nirmāṇaphalāt prathamadhyānaphalād gatito viśiṣyate. tad dvitīyadhyānaphalaṃ nirmāṇaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānabhūmiṃ gacchati. prathamadhyānaphalaṃ tu tāṃ na gacchati. kiṃ tarhi. prathamadhyānabhūmim eveti gamanaviśeṣād viśiṣyate. evaṃ tṛtīyādidhyānaphalam yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: (VII.55-58) 'The fruit of the second <s>dhyāna</s> is three' — two belonging to lower grounds and one belonging to its own ground. 'Four and five should be applied' — those belonging to the third <s>dhyāna</s> ground are four — three belonging to lower grounds and one belonging to its own ground. Those belonging to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground are five — four belonging to lower grounds and one belonging to its own ground. 'The fruit of the second and higher <s>dhyāna</s>s' — in detail. The creation that is the fruit of the second <s>dhyāna</s> — created by the creator — is distinguished from the creation-fruit of the first <s>dhyāna</s> — the fruit of the first <s>dhyāna</s> — by destination. That creation which is the fruit of the second <s>dhyāna</s> goes to the second <s>dhyāna</s> ground. But the fruit of the first <s>dhyāna</s> does not go there — rather, it goes only to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground — thus it is distinguished by the distinction of destination. Similarly, the fruit of the third and higher <s>dhyāna</s>s should be applied.

body.text: iti mauladhyānānām iva vairāgyato nirmāṇacittānāṃ lābhaḥ. śuddhakād dhyānād anaṃtaraṃ nirmāṇacittam iti. nirmāṇacittasaṃmukhībhāve yad ādiṃ. tac chuddhakād utpadyate. nirmāṇacittād veti dvitīyādipravāhe. nirmāṇacittād api śuddhakam iti. nirmāṇacittād vyutthāne nirmāṇacittaṃ ca pravāhe. samādhiphalasthitasyeti. samādhinirmāṇacittasthitasya, ūrdhvabhūmikas tv iti. dvitīyādidhyānabhūmikaḥ. prathamadhyānabhūmikena bhāṣyate. ūrdhvaṃ dvitīyādiṣu vijñaptisamutthāpakasya savitarkasya savicārasya cittasyābhāvāt. tathā hy uktaṃ. vitarkya vicārya vācaṃ bhāṣata iti.
body.translated_text: thus. Just as the attainment of fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>s is through dispassion, so is the attainment of creation-minds. 'The creation-mind [arises] immediately after a pure <s>dhyāna</s>' — at the initial bringing face-to-face of the creation-mind, it arises from a pure [<s>dhyāna</s>]. 'Or from a creation-mind' — in the continuation of the second and subsequent [moments]. 'From a creation-mind also a pure [<s>dhyāna</s> arises]' — upon emerging from the creation-mind, a pure [<s>dhyāna</s> arises]; and a creation-mind [arises] in the continuation. 'For one established in the fruit of <s>samādhi</s>' — for one established in the creation-mind produced by <s>samādhi</s>. 'But one belonging to a higher ground' — belonging to the second and higher <s>dhyāna</s> grounds — speaks by means of the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. Because above [the first <s>dhyāna</s>], in the second and higher, there is no mind with <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application) that gives rise to vocal expression. For thus it is stated: 'Having applied initial and sustained thought, one speaks a word.'

body.text: nirmāṇacittābhāvān nirmitābhāva iti. nimittābhāve naimittikasyāpy abhāva ity asantaṃ [Tib. 327a] katham enaṃ nirmitaṃ bhāṣayantīti abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the absence of a creation-mind, there is absence of the created one' — in the absence of the basis, there is also the absence of what is based — 'the nonexistent [creation-mind] — how do they make the created one speak?' — this is the intent.

body.text: iti. nirmāṇacittena nirmitaṃ nirmāya tataś cādhiṣṭhāyāvasthānakāmatayā tiṣṭhatv etad iti. tata uttarakālam anyena vijñaptisamutthāpakena savitarkasavicārakeṇa cittena vācaṃ pravartayanti nirmātāraḥ. pūrvābhiprāyaṃ hi saṃtatir anuvartate. pūrvaṃ hi tena cetasi vyavasthāpitaṃ nirmāṇaṃ nirmāsyāmi tad adhiṣṭhāsyāmi tad vācayiṣyāmīti. avasthādvaye 'dhiṣṭhānasaṃbhavāt pṛcchati.
body.translated_text: thus. Having created a creation by means of the creation-mind, and then having empowered it — with the wish for it to remain, [thinking] 'let this stand' — then, at a later time, by another mind that has <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> and gives rise to vocal expression, the creators cause speech. For the continuum follows the prior intention. For previously, he had established in his mind: 'I will create a creation, I will empower it, I will make it speak.' 'Because of the possibility of empowerment in two states' — he asks.

body.text: kiṃ jīvita evādhiṣṭhānam ityādi. āryamahākāśyapādhiṣṭhāneneti. āryamahākāśyapādhimokṣeṇety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Is the empowerment only of life?' and so forth. 'By the empowerment of the Noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>' — the meaning is: by the resolve (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) of the Noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>.

children.translated_text: 'But the threefold [supernatural power] born of rebirth' —

body.text: iti. kadācid dhi devādayaḥ parānugrahārthaṃ parān nirmiṇvanti. kadācid viheṭhanārtham ityādi. tatkṛtaṃ ceti vistaraḥ. devādikṛtaṃ ca svaparasambaddhaṃ nirmāṇaṃ navāyatanikaṃ. kutaḥ. aśabdarūpyāyatanatvāt. yasmād aśabdāni cakṣurāyatanarūpāyatanādīni tatra santīti. śabdaḥ saṃtānābhāvān na nirmāyate. acittakatvāc ca na manodharmāyatane. acittako nirmita iti kathaṃ gamyate. śāstrāt. evaṃ hy āha. tannirmitaś cāturmahābhautiko vaktavyo [Tib. 327b] na cāturmahābhautiko vaktavyaḥ. āha. caturmahābhautiko vaktavyaḥ. upādāyarūpiko nopādāyarūpiko vaktavyaḥ. āha. upādāyarūpiko vaktavyaḥ. acittiko vaktavyaḥ. kasya cittavaśena vartata iti vaktavyaṃ. āha. nirmātus cittavaśena vartata iti. yadi tarhi navāyatanikaṃ nirmīyate. indriyanirmāṇāt kathaṃ nāpūrvasattvaprādurbhāvo bhavati. sattvasaṃkhyātāni hīndriyāṇīti. ata āha. indriyāvinirbhūtatvād iti. yasmāc cakṣurādibhir indriyaiḥ paṃcabhiḥ svaparaśarīrasambaddhaṃ nirmāṇaṃ rūparasaspraṣṭavyasvabhāvam avinirbhāgenāvasthitaṃ bhavan navāyatanikam ity ucyate. na tv indriyaṃ nirmīyata iti eṣa siddhāntaḥ. yat punas tad eva svaparaśarīrasambaddhaṃ nirmiṇoti tac caturāyatanikam eva bhavati.
body.translated_text: thus. For sometimes <s>deva</s>s and the like create for the benefit of others; sometimes for the purpose of harassing — and so forth. 'And that which is created by them' — in detail. The creation connected with one's own and others' bodies, created by <s>deva</s>s and the like, consists of nine sense-spheres. Why? Because it has the nature of sense-spheres other than sound and form [i.e., not the smell-taste sphere]. Since in that [creation] there exist the eye sense-sphere, the form sense-sphere, and the rest, which are soundless. Sound is not created — because of the absence of a continuum. And because of being mindless, not the mind and <s>dharma</s> sense-spheres. How is it known that the created one is mindless? From the <s>śāstra</s>. For thus it says: 'That created one — should it be said to consist of the four great elements or not?' He says: 'It should be said to consist of the four great elements.' 'Should it be said to consist of derived form (<s>upādāyarūpa</s>) or not?' He says: 'It should be said to consist of derived form.' 'It should be said to be mindless. By whose mind does it operate?' He says: 'It operates by the mind of the creator.' If, then, what is created consists of nine sense-spheres — because of the creation of sense faculties (<s>indriya</s>), how is there no coming-into-existence of unprecedented beings? For sense faculties are counted as sentient beings. Therefore he says: 'Because of not being differentiated as sense faculties' — since the creation connected with one's own and others' bodies, having the own-nature of form, taste, and tangibles, exists undifferentiated by the five sense faculties of eye and the rest — therefore it is called 'consisting of nine sense-spheres.' But a sense faculty is not created — this is the established doctrine. Moreover, that which creates that very [creation] connected with one's own and others' bodies — that consists of just four sense-spheres.

body.text: (VII.60ab) yathā māṃdhātur āntarābhavikānāṃ ceti. karmajāyā ṛddher etad udāharaṇam ucyate.
body.translated_text: (VII.60ab) 'Just as for <s>Māndhātṛ</s> and intermediate-state beings' — this is stated as an example of <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power) born of <s>karma</s>.

body.text: (VII.59) kim ete divye eveti. kim ayaṃ divyaśabdo mukhyavṛttiḥ. āhosvid aupacārika ity abhiprāyaḥ. yadi hy ete divi bhave divye ity artho gṛhyate. mukhyavṛttir ayaṃ śabdo bhavati. atha tu divye iveti divye ity aupacārikaḥ. yathā bodhisattvacakravartigṛhapatiratnānām iti. aupacārikatve dṛṣṭāntaṃ darśayati. vijñānasahitatvād iti. [Tib. 328a] rūpadarśanamukhenābhinirhṛtatvān nityaṃ vijñānasahitam iti. sabhāgam eva. kāṇavibhrāntābhāvād iti. kāṇam abhyantaravikalaṃ. vibhrāntaṃ kekaraṃ sarvataś ca na paśyatīti. arthād uktaṃ bhavati. divyaṃ cakṣuḥ pṛṣṭhato 'pi paśyati. pārśvato 'pi paśyati na tv evam adivyaṃ cakṣur iti.
body.translated_text: (VII.59) 'Are these exclusively divine?' — the intent is: is this word 'divine' (<s>divya</s>) used in the primary sense or figuratively? For if the meaning is taken as 'divine' — 'belonging to the divine existence (<s>divi bhave</s>)' — then the word is used in the primary sense. But if [it means] 'like the divine' — then 'divine' is figurative. 'Like [the possessions] of <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, <s>Cakravartin</s>s, and householder-jewels' — he shows an example for the figurative usage. 'Because of being accompanied by consciousness' — because of being produced through the means of seeing form, it is always accompanied by consciousness. It is only of the same class (<s>sabhāga</s>). 'Because of the absence of one-eyed and confused [vision]' — one-eyed (<s>kāṇa</s>) means internally defective; confused (<s>vibhrānta</s>) means cross-eyed. And [the divine eye] does not see only [in one direction] — what is implicitly stated is: the divine eye sees from behind too, and from the side too. But the non-divine eye does not [see] in this way.

body.text: (VII.60, 61) divyaśrotrādikam api catuṣṭayam iti. ādiśabdena divyaṃ cakṣuḥ pūrvenivāsānusmṛtiḥ paracittajñānaṃ ca. etad api divyaśrotrādikaṃ catuṣṭayam.
body.translated_text: (VII.60, 61) 'The divine ear and the other group of four' — by the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), the divine eye, the recollection of former abodes, and the knowledge of others' minds [are included]. This group of four including the divine ear and the rest [is also discussed].

body.text: upapattipratilabdham asti. divyaṃ cakṣuḥ keṣām upapattipratilaṃbhikaṃ. kāmāvacarāṇāṃ devānām anāgāmināṃ ca rūpāvacarāṇāṃ. nārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ. tatra rūpābhāvat dṛṣṭir gamanaṃ nirmāṇaṃ ca nāsti. nāpi divyaṃ śrotraṃ cakṣuś cāsti. paracittajñānam api nāsti. svaparasaṃtānaparicchedābhāvāt. pūrvenivāsānusmṛtir api nāsti. kāmarūpāvacarasattvavat tādṛśasyātmabhāvasyāsamudāgamāt. atha vā sarvā apy abhijñā na santi. kāmarūpāvacarasattvavat tādṛśasyātmabhāvasyāsamudāgamāt. na yathā bhāvanāphalaṃ kuśalam eveti. viparītadṛṣṭāntaḥ. anyagatisthā nityaṃ jānata iti. tābhyāṃ paracittapūrvenivāsānusmṛtibhyāṃ devādigatisthā nityaṃ jānate. [Tib. 328b] duḥkhavedanānabhyāhatatvāt.
body.translated_text: there is that obtained through birth. Whose divine eye is obtained through birth? Of <s>deva</s>s of the Desire Realm and of <s>anāgāmin</s>s (non-returners) in the Form Realm. Not of those in the Formless Realm. Because of the absence of form there, [divine] sight, going, and emanation do not exist. Nor do the divine ear and eye exist. Knowledge of others' minds also does not exist — because of the absence of discrimination of one's own and others' mental continuums. Recollection of former lives also does not exist — because of the non-accomplishment of such a personal existence as that of beings in the Desire and Form Realms. Alternatively, none of the <s>abhijñā</s>s exist [there] — because of the non-accomplishment of such a personal existence as that of beings in the Desire and Form Realms. Not as the fruit of cultivation is exclusively wholesome — this is the counter-example. "Those in other destinies always know" — by those two, <s>paracittajñāna</s> (knowledge of others' minds) and <s>pūrvenivāsānusmṛti</s> (recollection of former lives), those in the <s>deva</s> and other destinies always know. [Tib. 328b] Because of not being afflicted by painful feeling.

children.translated_text: "For humans, there is none obtained through birth" —

body.text: iti. manuṣyāṇām etad yathoktam ṛddhyādikaṃ vairāgyalābhikaṃ tarkavidyauiadhakarmakṛtaṃ cāsti. na tūpapattikalābhikam asti. yat tarhi prakṛtijātismarā iti. prakṛtijātismaratvaṃ pūrvenivāsānusmṛtyā sā copapattau bhavatīti. katham. asāv utpattilābhikā na bhavatīty abhiprāyaḥ. āha. karmaviśeṣajāsau teṣām iti. teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ karmaviśeṣanirvṛttā. upapattilābhikaṃ hi nāma yad upapattikāla eva sarveṣāṃ nisargato labhyate. na tu yat kasyacid evopapattikālād ūrdhvaṃ. yathā pakṣiṇām ākāśagamanaṃ. tasmāt karmaviśeṣajāsau teṣāṃ. katham ity āha. trividhā hīti vistaraḥ. bhāvanāphalaṃ yathoktam. upapattipratilabdhā devādīnāṃ. karmajā yathā teṣāṃ bodhisattvānām iti.
body.translated_text: thus. For humans, the supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>) and the rest as described are obtained through dispassion, and also produced through reasoning, knowledge, herbs, and <s>karma</s>. But they are not obtained through birth. What then about those who are "natural birth-rememberers" (<s>prakṛtijātismara</s>)? Natural birth-remembering is through recollection of former lives, and that occurs at birth — how [then]? The intent is: that is not obtained through birth [in the technical sense]. He says: "That is born of special <s>karma</s> for them" — for those <s>bodhisattva</s>s, it is produced by special <s>karma</s>. For what is called "obtained through birth" is that which is naturally obtained by all at the very time of birth — not that which is obtained only by someone after the time of birth, like the flying of birds through space. Therefore, that is born of special <s>karma</s> for them. How? He says: "For it is threefold" — in detail. The fruit of cultivation is as stated. That obtained through birth belongs to <s>deva</s>s and the rest. That born of <s>karma</s> belongs to those <s>bodhisattva</s>s.

body.text: ācāryayaśomitrakṛtāyām abhidharmakośavyākhyāyāṃ saptamaṃ kośasthānaṃ.
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmakośavyākhyā</s> composed by <s>Ācārya Yaśomitra</s>, the seventh <s>kośasthāna</s> (chapter).

body.text: blank
body.translated_text: [blank]

body.text: VIII (samāpattinirdeśo nāmāṣṭamaṃ kośasthānam)
body.translated_text: VIII (<s>Samāpattinirdeśa</s> — Exposition of Attainments, the eighth <s>kośasthāna</s>)
