body.text: (VIII.1, 2) saptamād anantaram aṣṭamasya kośasthānasyopanyāse saṃbaṃdhaṃ darśayann āha. jñānādhikāreṇeti vistaraḥ. jñānādhikāreṇa daśānām jñānānām adhikāreṇa jñānamayānāṃ jñānasvabhāvānāṃ praṇidhijñānābhijñānādīnāṃ kṛto nirdeśaḥ anyasvabhāvānāṃ tu [Tib. 329a] samādhyādīnāṃ kartavyaḥ. sarvaguṇāśrayatvād iti kāmam ārūpyā api guṇāśrayā bhavanti. na sarvaguṇāśrayāḥ. dhyānāni tu sarvaguṇāśrayā iti.
body.translated_text: (VIII.1, 2) Showing the connection in the introduction of the eighth chapter immediately after the seventh, he says: "By the topic of knowledge" — in detail. By the topic of knowledge — by the topic of the ten knowledges — the exposition has been made of those having the nature of knowledge, such as the <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> (resolutional knowledge), <s>abhijñā</s>s (superknowledges), and the rest. But for those having a different nature — [Tib. 329a] <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and the rest — [the exposition] is to be made. "Because of being the support of all qualities" — although indeed the formless [attainments] too are supports of qualities, they are not supports of all qualities. But the <s>dhyāna</s>s are supports of all qualities.

body.text: kāryadhyānāni kāraṇadhyānāni cety arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: the meaning is: effect-<s>dhyāna</s>s and cause-<s>dhyāna</s>s.

body.text: iti. śubhānāṃ cittānām aikāgryaṃ. abhedeneti. sarveṣām api lakṣaṇānām. etal lakṣaṇam ata āha. samādhisvabhāvatvād iti. dhyānānām iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. atha vā abhedeneti samādhimātragrahaṇaṃ. bhedena
body.translated_text: thus. The one-pointedness (<s>aikāgrya</s>) of wholesome minds. "Without distinction" — of all [their] characteristics. This is the characteristic, therefore he says: "Because of having the nature of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration)." The remainder of the sentence is: "of the <s>dhyāna</s>s." Alternatively, "without distinction" means grasping <s>samādhi</s> alone. "With distinction" —

body.text: iti. avijñaptirūpaskaṃdhaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. The <s>avijñaptirūpa</s> (non-manifest form) aggregate.

body.text: ekālambanatā ekālambanatvaṃ cittānāṃ. kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ caittānām apy ekālaṃbanatve ekālambanatvaṃ cittānām ity ucyate. na punar ekālambanatā cittacaittānām ity ucyate. prādhānyāt cittāny evaikālambanāni samādhir iti. avasthāviśeṣatvāc citragurvāvat. vaibhāṣika āha. na cittāny eva samādhiḥ. yena tu tāny ekāgrāni vartante samāhitāni. sa dharmaḥ samādhiḥ. yathā vaiśeṣikanaye śuklaguṇayogāc chuklaḥ paṭaḥ. sa eva guṇo 'sya [Tib. 329b] śauklam ity ucyate. tadvat. nanu ca kṣaṇikatvāt sarvaṃ cittam ekāgraṃ. kim idam ucyate yena tu tāny ekāgrāṇi vartante. sa dharmaḥ samādhir iti. dvitīyasya tasmād avikṣepa iti cet. yady etat syād dvitīyasya cittasya tasmāt samādheḥ
body.translated_text: "One-objectness" (<s>ekālambanatā</s>) is the state of minds having one object. What, then, is the reason that, even though <s>caitta</s>s (mental factors) also have one-objectness, it is said "the one-objectness of minds" — and not "the one-objectness of <s>citta</s> and <s>caitta</s>s"? Because of predominance — minds alone having one object constitute <s>samādhi</s>. Because of being a special state — like a painting-master. The <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> says: it is not minds alone that are <s>samādhi</s>. Rather, that <s>dharma</s> by which they function with one-pointedness, in a collected manner — that <s>dharma</s> is <s>samādhi</s>. Just as in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system, cloth is white through connection with the white quality — [Tib. 329b] that very quality is called its whiteness — so too. But since all <s>citta</s> is one-pointed due to momentariness, what is meant by saying "that <s>dharma</s> by which they function with one-pointedness — that is <s>samādhi</s>"? If [one says:] "non-distraction of the second [moment] from that [<s>samādhi</s>]" — if this were the case, that the non-distraction of the second mind-moment is from that <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: [avikṣepaḥ. kasminn ālambane] na vikṣepo 'sminn ālambana iti. saṃprayukte samādhivaiyarthyaṃ. yat prathamaṃ cittaṃ samādhisaṃprayuktaṃ. tasmin saṃprayukte samādhivaiyarthyaṃ. tatra kāritraṃ samādhir na karoti dvitīye karotīti kṛtvā. kiṃ ca yata eva ca kāraṇāt samādhir ekāgratālakṣaṇo 'bhipretaḥ. tata eva ca kāraṇāt cittānām ekālaṃbanatvaṃ kiṃ neṣyate. kiṃ samādhinā arthāntarabhūtenety abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: — [non-distraction meaning] not being distracted regarding this object — then when associated [with <s>samādhi</s>], <s>samādhi</s> would be purposeless. The first mind that is associated with <s>samādhi</s> — regarding that associated [mind], <s>samādhi</s> would be purposeless — because <s>samādhi</s> does not perform its function regarding it but performs [its function] regarding the second. Moreover, for whatever reason <s>samādhi</s> is intended as having the characteristic of one-pointedness — for that very reason, why is the one-objectness of minds not accepted? What need is there for <s>samādhi</s> as something different? — this is the intent.

body.text: na. durbalatvāt samādheḥ. na mahābhūmikatvāt samādheḥ sadbhāvāt sarvasya cittasyaikāgryatāprasaṃgaḥ. yac cittaṃ durbalena samādhinā saṃprayujyate. na tad ekāgraṃ bhavati. yat punar balavatā. tac cittam ekāgram iti. saty api mahābhūmikatve samādher na sarvacittānām ekāgratāprasaṃgaḥ.
body.translated_text: No. Because of the weakness of <s>samādhi</s>. Since <s>samādhi</s> is a <s>mahābhūmika</s> (universally present mental factor), from its existence [in all minds], it would follow that all <s>citta</s> is one-pointed. But the mind that is associated with weak <s>samādhi</s> is not one-pointed. But that which [is associated] with strong [<s>samādhi</s>] — that mind is one-pointed. Thus, even though <s>samādhi</s> is a <s>mahābhūmika</s>, the consequence that all minds are one-pointed does not follow.

body.text: cittāny eveti vistaraḥ. cittāny evaikāgrāṇi samādhir nārthāṃtarabhūta iti. tathā hy adhicittaṃ śikṣeti. adhicittaṃ śikṣā katamā. catvāri dhyānānīti sarvaṃ. tathā cittapariśuddhipradhānaṃ catvāry eva dhyānāni. ity uktāni. [Tib. 330a] likhitam idaṃ sūtram
body.translated_text: "Minds alone" — in detail. Minds alone having one-pointedness constitute <s>samādhi</s>, not something different in nature. For thus: "the training in higher mind" (<s>adhicittaṃ śikṣā</s>). What is the training in higher mind? The four <s>dhyāna</s>s — all of this. Similarly, "the four <s>dhyāna</s>s have been stated as having the purification of mind as predominant." [Tib. 330a] This <s>sūtra</s> has been cited

children.translated_text: "The bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) are concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>)" —

body.text: ity atra. yathā hy adhiśīlam śikṣā śīlam eva. na tasmād anyā. adhiprajñāṃ ca śikṣā prajñaiva. na tasyā anyā. evam adhicittaṃ śikṣā cittam eva. na tasmād anyā. na cittavyatiriktasamādhir astīty arthaḥ. adhicittaṃ hi śikṣā samādhir iṣyate. yathā cāsminn eva sūtre śīlaparīśuddhipradhānaṃ vimuktipariśuddhipradhānaṃ ity ukte. na śīlapariśuddhiḥ śīlād anyā. evaṃ dṛṣṭipariśuddhiḥ vimuktipariśuddhiś ca. tathaiva cittapariśuddhir api na cittād anyā. cittapariśuddhir hi caturdhyānalakṣaṇasamadhir iti.
body.translated_text: in this context. For just as the training in higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>) is morality itself, not something other than that, and the training in higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>) is wisdom itself, not something other than that — so too the training in higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>) is mind itself, not something other than that. There is no <s>samādhi</s> distinct from mind — this is the meaning. For the training in higher mind is accepted as <s>samādhi</s>. And just as in this very <s>sūtra</s>, when "having the purification of morality as predominant" and "having the purification of liberation as predominant" are stated — the purification of morality is not other than morality; similarly, the purification of view and the purification of liberation [are not other than view and liberation] — so too the purification of mind is not other than mind. For the purification of mind is <s>samādhi</s> characterized by the four <s>dhyāna</s>s.

body.text: evaṃ tarhīti. yadi samādhisvabhāvāni dhyānāni sarvasamādhidhyānaprasaṃgaḥ. kuśalakliṣṭāvyākṛtanām api samādhīnāṃ dhyānaprasaṃgaḥ. samādher mahābhūmikatvāt. na. prakarṣayukta iti vistaraḥ. naitad evaṃ prakarṣayukte samādhau dhyānanāmavidhānat. bhāskaravat. tadyathā ya eva prakarṣeṇa bhāsaṃ karoti. sa eva bhāskaraḥ. [Tib. 330b] na khadyotakādiḥ. tadvat. sa hīti vistaraḥ. sa hy aṃgasamāyuktaḥ samādhiḥ śamathavipaśyanābhyāṃ yuganaddhābhyām ivāśvābhyāṃ ratho vahatīti yuganaddhavāhī. tadbhāvāt dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra uktaḥ sūtre. sukhā ca pratipad iti. aṃgasamāyukta eva samādhiḥ. sukhā ca pratipad ity ukta iti vartate. sutarāṃ tena dhyāyanti sukhatvāt. kliṣṭaya kathaṃ dhyānatvam iti. yadi kuśalāṃgasamāyuktaḥ samādhir dhyānaṃ. kliṣṭasyāsvādanāsaṃprayuktasya kathaṃ dhyānatvayuktam
body.translated_text: "In that case" — if the <s>dhyāna</s>s have the nature of <s>samādhi</s>, it would follow that all <s>samādhi</s> is <s>dhyāna</s>. Even wholesome, afflicted, and indeterminate <s>samādhi</s>s would [all] be <s>dhyāna</s>s — because <s>samādhi</s> is a <s>mahābhūmika</s>. No. "Because endowed with excellence" — in detail. This is not so — the designation "<s>dhyāna</s>" is given when <s>samādhi</s> is endowed with excellence. Like the sun (<s>bhāskara</s>). Just as only that which eminently produces light is called "the light-maker" (<s>bhāskara</s>) — [Tib. 330b] not a firefly and the like — so too. "For that" — in detail. For that <s>samādhi</s> endowed with [its] limbs (<s>aṅga</s>) — [being] a vehicle drawn by the paired [horses of] <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) yoked together — is called "yoked-pair-drawn" (<s>yuganaddhavāhī</s>). Because of being such, it is called "pleasant abiding in the present life" (<s>dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra</s>) in the <s>sūtra</s>. "And the practice is pleasant" — only <s>samādhi</s> endowed with limbs is said to be "pleasant practice" — this continues. All the more so, through that one meditates (<s>dhyāyanti</s>) because of its pleasantness. "How can the afflicted be a <s>dhyāna</s>?" — if <s>samādhi</s> endowed with wholesome limbs is <s>dhyāna</s>, how is it fitting that the afflicted — that associated with relishing (<s>āsvādana</s>) — be a <s>dhyāna</s>

body.text: iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. trividhaṃ dhyānam
body.translated_text: — this is the remainder of the sentence. "The <s>dhyāna</s> is threefold:" —

children.translated_text: "that associated with relishing, the pure, and the uncontaminated" —

body.text: iti vacanāt. mithyopanidhyānād iti. mithyānitīraṇād ity arthaḥ. atiprasaṃga iti. kāmarāgaparyavasthitenāpi cetasā mithyopanidhyānāt tatprasaṃgaḥ. na. tatpratirūpa eveti vistaraḥ. naitad evaṃ atiprasaṃga iti. tat pratirūpa eva hi nātibahuvilakṣaṇe kliṣṭe dhyānam iti saṃjñāsaṃniveśaḥ. pūtibījavat. yathā kiṃcid abījaṃ pāṣāṇādy atyantatajjātivilakṣaṇam na pūtibījam ity ucyate. kiṃ tarhi. bījajātīyam evopahataṃ yad bhavati. tasminn eva saṃjñāsaṃniveśaḥ pūtibījam iti. uktāni cākuśalāny api dhyānānīti. sa kāmarāgaparyavasthitaḥ [Tib. 331a] kāmarāgaparyavasthānam antarīkṛtvā dhyāyati pradhyāyatīti vistaraḥ. anena kāmarāgādiparyavasthānasyāpi dhyānatve sati na doṣa iti darśayati. dhūmāgnivad iti. yathā dhūmo 'treti dhūmavacanenāgnir apy ukto bhavati sāhacaryāt. na vināgninā dhūmo bhavatīti. anenaiva cāvinābhāvitvena dhūmasyābhyarhitatvaṃ. yatra hi dhūmaḥ. tatrāgniḥ. na tu yatrāgniḥ. tatra dhūmaḥ. tathā hy ayoguḍāṃgārādiṣv agnir eva gṛhyate. na dhūmaḥ. asmāc cābhyarhitatvād dhūmasya pūrvanipāto vāsudevārjunavat. anyathā hi dvaṃdve 'pīty agniśabdasya pūrvanipātaḥ syāt. kathaṃ punaḥ sāhacaryeṇa hi prītisukhavān vicāro vinā vitarkeṇa nāsti. yathā dhyānāntaravicāraḥ. na prītisukhavān ity avitarkaḥ. naivam ayaṃ vicāraḥ. viśeṣito hy ayaṃ vicāraḥ. prītisukhasahapaṭhitaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated. "Because of wrong meditation (<s>mithyopanidhyāna</s>)" — the meaning is: because of wrong examination. "Overextension" — even with a mind overcome by <s>kāmarāga</s> (desire for sensual pleasures), because of wrong meditation, that [designation of <s>dhyāna</s>] would follow. No. "It is the counterfeit alone" — in detail. This is not so — there is no overextension. The designation "<s>dhyāna</s>" is applied only to that which is the counterfeit [of true <s>dhyāna</s>] — to the afflicted which is not excessively dissimilar [from true <s>dhyāna</s>]. Like a rotten seed. Just as something that is not a seed at all — a stone and so forth — being utterly dissimilar from that class [of seeds], is not called "a rotten seed." Rather, the designation "rotten seed" is applied only to what belongs to the seed-class but is spoiled. "And unwholesome <s>dhyāna</s>s too have been stated" — [Tib. 331a] He [who is] overcome by the obsession of <s>kāmarāga</s>, having made the obsession of <s>kāmarāga</s> his object, meditates, ruminates — in detail. By this he shows that even if the obsession with <s>kāmarāga</s> and the rest were [considered] <s>dhyāna</s>, there is no fault. "Like smoke and fire" — just as by the word "smoke," fire too is mentioned, because of their constant association. For there is no smoke without fire. And it is by this very inseparability that smoke is honored [with priority in mention]. For where there is smoke, there is fire — but not where there is fire, there is smoke. For in iron balls, embers, and the like, only fire is apprehended, not smoke. And because of this honored status of smoke, smoke is placed first [in the compound <s>dhūmāgni</s>] — like <s>Vāsudeva</s>-<s>Arjuna</s>. Otherwise, in a <s>dvandva</s> compound, the word "fire" would be placed first. But how, through constant association, is <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) accompanied by joy and happiness never without <s>vitarka</s> (initial thought) — like the <s>vicāra</s> of the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> — not accompanied by joy and happiness — so it is without <s>vitarka</s>. This is not so — this <s>vicāra</s> is qualified — it is read together with joy and happiness.

children.translated_text: "Endowed with sustained thought, joy, and happiness" —

body.text: iti. prītisukhavatā vicāreṇa prītisukhena ca saṃprayuktaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam ity arthaḥ. yadi punar vitarkaprītisukhavad iti sūtraṃ kriyeta ko doṣaḥ syāt. na śakyam evaṃ kartuṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. The first <s>dhyāna</s> is associated with <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) that is accompanied by joy and happiness, and with joy and happiness — this is the meaning. If, however, the <s>sūtra</s> were formulated as "endowed with initial thought, joy, and happiness" — what fault would there be? It cannot be formulated thus.

body.text: iti vakṣyati. vitarkavarjitaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānam [Tib. 331b] iti dhyānāntaram api dvitīyaṃ dhyānaṃ prāpnoti. kiṃ ca catvāry aṃgāni prathamadhyānanirdeśāvasāne 'nenānukrameṇoktāni. savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharatīti. tatra vicāraprītisukhasamādhayaḥ prathame dhyāne bhavaṃti. ebhiś caturbhir aṃgair vitarkeṇa ca sarvaprathamoktena paṃcāṃgam ucyate. dvitīyaṃ punar ucyate. avitarkam avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharatīti.
body.translated_text: he will state. The second <s>dhyāna</s> is devoid of <s>vitarka</s> (initial thought) — [Tib. 331b] thus the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> (<s>dhyānāntara</s>) too would be the second <s>dhyāna</s>. Moreover, four limbs have been stated at the conclusion of the exposition of the first <s>dhyāna</s> in this order: "Endowed with initial thought, endowed with sustained thought, born of seclusion, with joy and happiness — one enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s>." Therein, sustained thought, joy, happiness, and concentration exist in the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Together with initial thought, mentioned first of all, it is said to have five limbs. The second is stated thus: "Without initial thought, without sustained thought, born of concentration, with joy and happiness — one enters and abides in the second <s>dhyāna</s>."

body.text: caturṇām eṣāṃ pūrvāṃgena vicāralakṣaṇena varjitam iti. tṛtīyam apy evam ucyate. sa prīter virāgād upekṣako viharati vistareṇa yāvat sukhavihārīti. tṛtīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharatīti. prītilakṣaṇenāpareṇāṃgena varjitam iti. caturthaṃ punar evam ucyate. sa sukhasya ca prahāṇād vistareṇa yāvad aduḥkhāsukham upekṣāsmṛtipariśuddaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharatīti. sukhenāpy aṃgena varjitaṃ samādhir evātra kevalam avaśiṣyata ity ata eva sūtraṃ kṛtaṃ
body.translated_text: Of these four, it is devoid of the preceding limb characterized by sustained thought. The third too is stated thus: "Free from joy, one abides with equanimity, in detail, up to: a pleasant abider — one enters and abides in the third <s>dhyāna</s>." It is devoid of the subsequent limb characterized by joy. The fourth is stated thus: "Through the abandonment of happiness, in detail, up to: neither-painful-nor-pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness — one enters and abides in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>." It is devoid also of the limb of happiness. Only concentration remains here — therefore the <s>sūtra</s> was formulated:

children.translated_text: "Endowed with sustained thought, joy, and happiness" —

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: (VIII.2-4) eṣām api copapattaya uktā iti.
body.translated_text: (VIII.2-4) "And the rebirths of these have been stated" —

children.translated_text: "The Formless Realm is not a place; by rebirth it is fourfold" —

body.text: iti vacanāt. anuparivartakarūpābhāvad iti. dhyānānāsravasaṃvarābhāvād [Tib. 332a] ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated. "Because of the absence of accompanying form" — the meaning is: because of the absence of the <s>dhyāna</s>-uncontaminated restraint (<s>anāsravasaṃvara</s>). [Tib. 332a]

body.text: iti. vivicyate aneneti vivekaḥ. yena mārgeṇeti. ānaṃtaryamārgeṇa vimuktimārgeṇāpi vā tad ekakāryatvāt. vairāgyagamanād iti. tadvaimukhyagamanād ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. 'That by which one separates is separation (<s>viveka</s>)' — by which path. By the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) or also by the liberation path (<s>vimuktimārga</s>), because of their being directed toward the same purpose. 'Because of going toward dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>)' — the meaning is: because of going toward aversion from [the object].

children.translated_text: 'Called "those whose perception of form has perished"' —

body.text: iti. vibhūtā rūpasaṃjñāsyeti vibhūtarūpasaṃjñaḥ. vibhūtarūpasaṃjñā ity ākhyā eṣām iti vibhūtarūpasaṃjñākhyāḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. One whose perception of form has perished is a <s>vibhūtarūpasaṃjña</s>. 'Having the designation "those whose perception of form has perished"' — their designation is '<s>vibhūtarūpasaṃjñā</s>' — hence '<s>vibhūtarūpasaṃjñākhyā</s>.'

body.text: sādhyaṃ tāvad etad iti. nikāyāntarīyāḥ. yadi hi syād hi syād iti vaibhāṣikāḥ. āpiṃgalavad iti. yathā īṣat piṃgala āpiṃgalaḥ. evam īṣad rūpā ārūpyā iti. kathaṃ tadabhāve tatsaṇvarau kāyavāksaṃvarau bhaviṣyataḥ. na cāsati bhūte ārūpyāvacare saṃvarabhautikam ārūpyāvacaraṃ yujyate. anāsravasaṃvaravac cet. tatraitat syāt. yathā na saṃty anāsravāṇi bhūtāni. asti cānāsravasaṃvaro bhautikaṃ rūpam. evam ihāpi nārūpyāvacarāṇi bhūtāni syuḥ. atha vārūpyāvacarasaṃvaraḥ syāt bhautikaṃ rūpam iti. tac ca na. sāsravabhūtasadbhāvāt sāsravāṇi [Tib. 332b] bhūtāni saṃti. tāny ārūpyeṣu bhaveyuḥ. anāsravāṇi tu bhūtāni na saṃti. ato 'nāsravasaṃvaro yatra jātaḥ. tatratyāni sāsravāṇy upādāya bhavatīty akalpaneyam asāmyāt. samāpattāv api tatpratiṣedha ukta iti. anenaivopapattirūpapratiṣedhena samāpattāv api rūpapratiṣedha ukto bhavati. nātra yatnāṃtaram anuṣṭheyaṃ. kathaṃ. yadi kāyavāksaṃvaramātraṃ.
body.translated_text: 'This, however, requires proof' — [say] the non-<s>Vaibhāṣika</s> schools (<s>nikāyāntarīya</s>). 'If indeed it were so, if it were so' — [say] the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s. 'Like slightly tawny (<s>āpiṅgala</s>)' — just as what is slightly tawny is <s>āpiṅgala</s> — so too, the formless [beings] have slight form. How then, in the absence of that [form], will bodily and vocal restraint (<s>kāyavāksaṃvara</s>) exist there? For without the great elements (<s>bhūta</s>) existing in the Formless Realm, derivative matter (<s>bhautika</s>) belonging to the Formless Realm is not fitting. 'If [you say it is] like the uncontaminated restraint (<s>anāsravasaṃvara</s>)' — there, one might argue: just as there are no uncontaminated great elements, yet there is uncontaminated restraint, which is derivative matter — so too here, there would be no Formless Realm great elements, yet there would be Formless Realm restraint, which is derivative matter. But that is not [valid]. Because contaminated great elements do exist. Contaminated great elements exist — they could exist in the Formless Realms. But uncontaminated great elements do not exist. Therefore, uncontaminated restraint, wherever it arises, exists in dependence on the contaminated [great elements] of that place — this is not to be imagined [as analogous], because of the dissimilarity. 'The negation of that is stated even for the attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>)' — by this very negation of form in [formless] rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>), the negation of form in the [formless] attainment too is stated. No additional effort is needed here. How? If [form] is merely bodily and vocal restraint,

body.text: kathaṃ tadabhāve tatsaṃvaro bhaviṣyati. na cāsati bhūte bhautikaṃ yujyate. anāsravasaṃvaravac cet. na. sāsravabhūtasadbhāvād iti. sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramād iti vacanāt. samāpattāv api tatpratiṣedha ukta ity apare. tad evaṃ nārūpyasamāpattiṣu nārūpyopapattiṣu rūpam astīti darśitaṃ bhavati. parimāṇālpatvāc cet. atha mataṃ. paramāṇumātraṃ rūpam asti. atas ta īṣadrūpā iṣyanta iti. udakajaṃtukeṣv apy aṇutvād adṛśyarūpeṣu prasaṃgaḥ ārūpyaprasaṃga ity arthaḥ. acchatāc cet. tatraitad syād rūpasyācchatvād ārūpyā iti. antarābhavarūpāvacareṣv apu prasaṃgaḥ. antarābhavarūpāvacarā hi vajramayeṣv api parvateṣv acchatvād asajjamānā [Tib. 333a] gacchaṃti. teṣv ārūpyaprasaṃgaḥ. samāpattivat tadupapattiviśeṣād iti. yathaiva hy ākāśānantyādisamāpattayo viśiṣṭatamāḥ. evam upapattiviśeṣo 'pi tāsām abhyupagantavyo 'cchācchataratama iti. ataḥ samāpattivad upapattiviśeṣo 'py acchataratama iti. tad evārūpyaṃ syāt. yadi cārūpyopapattirūpasyādharabhūmikenendriyeṇācchataratvād agrahaṇam ity ārūpyā ucyaṃte. dhyānopapattirūpasyāpi ceti vistaraḥ. eṣa saṃbhavo dhyānopapattirūpasyāpi cādharabhūmikenendriyeṇāgrahaṇaṃ. kathaṃ. prathamadhyānabhūmikenendriyeṇa dvitīyabhūmikasyāgrahaṇaṃ. evaṃ yāvat tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikenendriyeṇa caturthadhyānabhūmikasya rūpasyāgrahaṇaṃ. ūrdhvabhūmikasyācchataratamatvāt. tad evaṃ dhyānopapattirūpasya cādharabhūmikenendriyeṇāgrahaṇāt kas tatra viśeṣaḥ. ārūpyadhātau yad acchataratamābhyāṃ sāmānye 'pi ta evārūpyā iṣyaṃgte na rūpāvacarāḥ. tasmān na tatra rūpaṃ. atha mataṃ dvayor dhātvor anvarthā saṃjñā. kāmaguṇaprabhāvitaḥ kāmadhātuḥ. rūpaprabhāvito rūpadhātur iti. nārūpyadhātor [Tib. 333b] anvarthā saṃjñā. kiṃ tarhi yādṛcchikī ti. kātra yuktiḥ. dvayor dhātvor anvarthā saṃjñā. nārūpyadhātor iti. yuktyā pratiṣidhya nārūpyadhātau rūpam astīti āgamaṃ parigṛhyāśaṃkitaṃ vāryate. tatra rūpaprasiddhyārtham āyurūṣmaṇor iti vistaraḥ. ārūpyeṣu rūpāstitvasiddhir iti ced ity etat padaṃ pratyekaṃ yojyaṃ. katham. āyurūṣmaṇoḥ saṃsṛṣṭavacanād rūpāstitvasiddhir iti cet. tatraitat syāt sūtra uktaṃ. yac cāyuṣman kauṣṭhila āyur yac coṣmakaṃ saṃsṛṣṭāv imau dharmau. na visaṃsṛṣṭāv iti vistaraḥ. atas tatrāyuṣi saty ūṣmaṇā bhavitavyaṃ. ūṣmā ca rūpam iti sidhyati. naḍakalāpīdvayavan nāmarūpayor
body.translated_text: how, in the absence of that [great elements], will that restraint exist? For without the great elements existing, derivative matter is not fitting. 'If [you say it is] like the uncontaminated restraint' — it is not [valid], because of the existence of contaminated great elements — thus. 'Because of the complete transcendence of all perceptions of form' — from this statement, the negation of that is stated even for the attainment — [say] others. Thus it is shown that in neither the formless attainments nor the formless rebirths does form exist. 'If [you say] because of the smallness of the measure [of form]' — if it is thought that there is a mere atom of form, and therefore they are accepted as having slight form — then even among water-creatures (<s>udakajantu</s>) with forms invisible due to their minuteness, there would be the consequence of being formless — the meaning is: the consequence of the Formless Realm [designation]. 'If [you say] because of transparency (<s>acchatā</s>)' — there, one might argue that the formless [beings] are so because of the transparency of form. [Then] there would be the consequence even for the Form Realm intermediate-existence (<s>antarābhava</s>) beings. For the Form Realm intermediate-existence beings, being transparent, pass even through diamond-hard mountains without being obstructed — for them there would be the consequence of being formless. 'Like the attainment, because of the distinction of that rebirth' — just as the attainments of the Infinity of Space and the rest are the most distinguished — so too, the distinction of rebirth should be accepted as transparent, more transparent, and most transparent. Therefore, like the attainment, the distinction of rebirth is also most transparent — that very [being] would be formless. And if the non-apprehension of the form of formless rebirth by lower-ground faculties is because of its greater transparency, and therefore they are called formless — [then] even of the form of <s>dhyāna</s>-rebirth — in detail. This possibility applies to <s>dhyāna</s>-rebirth form too — that it is not apprehended by lower-ground faculties. How? Form of the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground is not apprehended by the faculty of the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. Similarly, up to: form of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> ground is not apprehended by the faculty of the third <s>dhyāna</s> ground — because the higher-ground [form] is more and most transparent. Thus, since even <s>dhyāna</s>-rebirth form is not apprehended by lower-ground faculties, what is the distinction there? In the Formless Realm, even though there is commonality with respect to that which is most transparent of the two [rebirth and attainment], those very ones are accepted as formless, not Form Realm beings. Therefore there is no form there. And if it is thought that the designation of the two realms [Desire and Form] is etymologically derived — the Desire Realm is so-called because of being pervaded by sensual pleasures; the Form Realm because of being pervaded by form — but the designation of the Formless Realm is not etymologically derived but rather arbitrary (<s>yādṛcchikī</s>) — what is the logic here? 'The designation of the two realms is etymologically derived but not that of the Formless Realm' — having refuted by logic that there is no form in the Formless Realm, the doubt raised by recourse to scripture is dispelled. 'For the purpose of establishing the existence of form there, [the argument] from life-force (<s>āyus</s>) and warmth (<s>ūṣman</s>)' — in detail. Each phrase of 'the establishment of the existence of form in the Formless Realms' should be connected individually. How? 'From the statement of the conjunction of life-force and warmth — [you argue] the establishment of the existence of form' — if so, there, it might be argued: in the <s>sūtra</s> it is stated: 'O Venerable <s>Kauṣṭhila</s>, life-force and warmth are conjoined. These two <s>dharma</s>s are conjoined, not unconjoined' — in detail. Therefore, where there is life-force, there must be warmth. And warmth is form — thus it is established. 'From the statement of the mutual dependence of <s>nāma</s> (name) and <s>rūpa</s> (form), like two bundles of reeds'

body.text:
anyonyaniśritavacanāt. ārūpyeṣu rūpāstitvasiddhir iti cet. sūtra uktaṃ. tadyathāyuṣman śāriputra dve naḍakalāpyāv ākāśe ucchrite syātāṃ. te anyonyaniśrite anyonyaṃ niśritya tiṣṭheyātām. tatra kaścid ekām apanayet. dvitīyā nipatet. dvitīyām apanayet. ekā nipatet. evam āyuṣman śāriputra nāmaṃ ca rūpaṃ cānyonyaniśritaṃ. anyonyaṃ niśritya tiṣṭhatīti vistaraḥ. vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam iti vacanāt. tasmād ārūpyeṣu rūpāstitvasiddhir iti cet. [Tib. 334a] pratītyasamutpādasūtra uktaṃ. ārūpyaprasiddhikṣaṇe vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam iti vacanāt tasmād ārūpyeṣu rūpam astīti sidhyati. anyatra rūpād iti vistaraḥ. sūtra uktaṃ. rūpopagaṃ bhikṣavo vijñānaṃ tiṣṭhati. iti rūpālambanarūpapratiṣṭhaṃ. yaḥ kaścid bhikṣava evaṃ vadet. ahaṃ anyatra rūpād vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārebhyo vijñānasyāgatiṃ vā gatiṃ vā vadāmīti. tasya tad vāgvastv eva syād iti.
asmād api cāgamād ārūpyeṣu rūpam astīti sidhyaty evaṃ cet. tan na. saṃpradhāryatvāt.
body.translated_text: — [you argue] the establishment of the existence of form in the Formless Realms — if so. In the <s>sūtra</s> it is stated: 'Just as, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, two bundles of reeds might be set upright in space. Those two would stand leaning against each other, supported by each other. If someone were to remove one, the second would fall. If one removes the second, the first would fall. Just so, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>nāma</s> (name) and <s>rūpa</s> (form) are mutually dependent. They stand supported by each other' — in detail. 'From the statement that <s>nāmarūpa</s> is conditioned by consciousness (<s>vijñānapratyaya</s>)' — therefore, the establishment of the existence of form in the Formless Realms — if so. In the <s>sūtra</s> on dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), it is stated: conditioned by consciousness, <s>nāmarūpa</s> [arises]. From that statement, the establishment that at the moment of the Formless Realm [rebirth], form exists — therefore form exists in the Formless Realms — this is established. 'Except for form (<s>anyatra rūpāt</s>)' — in detail. In the <s>sūtra</s> it is stated: 'Consciousness, O monks, that has arrived at form, stands' — [that is:] having form as its object-domain and form as its support. 'Whoever, O monks, would say: "I shall describe the coming and going of consciousness apart from form, apart from feeling, apart from perception, apart from formations" — for that one, such a verbal claim alone would exist.' And from this scripture too, the existence of form in the Formless Realms is established — if so. That is not [valid]. Because it must be carefully examined (<s>saṃpradhārya</s>).

body.text: āhosvit sarvam iti. kāmarūpārūpyāvacaraṃ. ayam atrābhiprāyārthaḥ. kāmāvacaram evāyuḥ saṃdhāyaivam uktam iti. tathā hy uktaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Or is it all?' — [that is:] belonging to the Desire, Form, and Formless Realms. This is the intended meaning here: it is stated with reference to the Desire Realm life-force alone. For thus it is stated:

children.text:
āyur ūṣmātha vijñānaṃ yadā kāyaṃ jahaty amī.
apaviddhas tadā śete yathā kāṣṭham acetana
children.translated_text:
'When life-force, warmth, and consciousness
abandon this body —
then it lies discarded,
like a piece of wood, unconscious.'

body.text: iti. na cārūpyadhātau kāyo 'sti. kuta eva kāyanidhanaṃ. rūpadhātau tu yady api kāyo 'sti. na tu kāyanidhanaṃ prajñāyata iti. yac ca nāmarūpayor anyonyāśritatvam uktaṃ. tad api kāmarūpāvacaram eva saṃdhāyoktam iti lakṣyate. dvayasaṃbhave hy anyonyāśritatvaṃ saṃbhavati. [Tib. 334b] yac ca vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam iti. vijñānaṃ pratyayo 'syeti vijñānāpratyayaṃ nāmarūpam ity evaṃ ṣaṣṭhībahuvrīhisamāse. kim atra sarvavijñānaṃ kāmāvacarasaṃskārapratyayaṃ yāvad ārūpyāvacarasaṃskārapratyayaṃ nāmarūpasya pratyayaḥ. āhosvit sarvaṃ nāmarūpaṃ vijñānapratyayam iti. vayaṃ brūmo vijñānapratyayaṃ māmarūpam ity evaṃ sarvasya nāmarūpasya vijñānaṃ pratyaya ity avadhāryate. na tu sarvaṃ vijñānaṃ nāmarūpasya pratyaya ity avadhāryate. kiṃcid vijñānaṃ nāmna eva pratyayo yad ārūpyāvacarasaṃskārapratyayaṃ. kiṃcin nāmarūpasya yat kāmarūpāvacarasaṃskārapratyayaṃ. tad idam uktaṃ bhavati. pratyaya eva vijñānam asya nāmarūpasya. na tv asyaiva samuditasya nāmarūpasya pratyaya iti. saṃbhavaṃ praty evam ucyate. tathā hy upapādukānāṃ vijñānapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam eva bhavati. na nāmarūpam aniṣpannaṣaḍāyatanāvasthā hi paṃca skaṃdhā nāmarūpam
body.translated_text: And in the Formless Realm there is no body. How then could there be the abandonment of the body? But in the Form Realm too, although there is a body, the abandonment of the body is not recognized. And what was stated about the mutual dependence of <s>nāma</s> (name) and <s>rūpa</s> (form) — that too is perceived as stated with reference to the Desire and Form Realms alone. For mutual dependence is possible when both exist. And regarding 'conditioned by consciousness, <s>nāmarūpa</s> [arises]' — in the genitive <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound where consciousness is a condition of <s>nāmarūpa</s> — is it the case that all consciousness conditioned by all Desire Realm formations, up to all consciousness conditioned by Formless Realm formations, is the condition of <s>nāmarūpa</s>? Or is it the case that all <s>nāmarūpa</s> is conditioned by consciousness? We say: it is determined that all <s>nāmarūpa</s> is conditioned by consciousness — all <s>nāmarūpa</s> has consciousness as its condition. But it is not determined that all consciousness is the condition of <s>nāmarūpa</s>. Some consciousness is the condition of <s>nāma</s> (name) alone — that which is conditioned by Formless Realm formations. Some [consciousness is the condition] of <s>nāmarūpa</s> — that which is conditioned by Desire and Form Realm formations. What is thus stated amounts to this: consciousness alone is the condition of this <s>nāmarūpa</s>. But it is not the case that this condition is the condition of this very unified <s>nāmarūpa</s> [everywhere]. This is said with reference to origination (<s>saṃbhava</s>). For thus, for spontaneously-born beings (<s>upapāduka</s>), consciousness conditions the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>) alone, not <s>nāmarūpa</s>. For the state in which the six sense-bases are not yet fully formed — the five aggregates in that state — is <s>nāmarūpa</s>

body.text: ity ākhyāyante. sūtraṃ caitam evārthaṃ dyotayati. vijñānaṃ ced ānanda mātuḥ kukṣiṃ nāvakrāmed api tu tan nāmarūpaṃ kalalatvāya saṃmūrchet. na bhadanta. vijñānaṃ ced ānandāvakrāmya kṣipram evāpakrāmed api tu tan nāmarūpam itthavtāya prajñāyeta. [Tib. 335a] no bhadanta. vijñānaṃ ced ānanda daharasya kumārasya kumārikāyā vā ucchidyeta vinaśyen na bhaved api tu tan nāmarūpaṃ vṛddhiṃ vipulatām āpadyeta. no bhadanta. tad anenāpi paryāyeṇa veditavyaṃ. yad vijñānasya pratyayaṃ nāmarūpaṃ. nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ca vijñānam iti vistaraḥ. kim atra sarvair etai rūpādibhir vinā tatpratiṣedha āgatigatipratiṣedhaḥ. tatra pūrvasmāl lokād aṃtarābhavasaṃtatyā ihopapattir āgatiḥ. aṃtarābhavasaṃtatyā punar asmāl lokāt paraloka upapattir gatiḥ. āhosvid ekenāpi rūpādīnām anyatamam eva. vayaṃ brūmaḥ. sarvair vinā tatpratiṣedha iti. aviśeṣavacanān na saṃpradhāryam iti cet. syād eṣā buddhir aviśeṣeṇedaṃ sūtravacanaṃ. yac cāyuṣman mahākauṣṭhila āyur iti vistareṇa yāvad rūpopagaṃ vijñānaṃ tiṣṭhatīty anena sūtravacanena viśeṣitaṃ kāmāvacaraṃ rūpāvacaraṃ vāyuḥ saṃdhāyoktaṃ yāvat sarvair eva tair vinā rūpādibhis tatpratiṣedha iti. atrocyate. astiprasaṃgaḥ. bāhyasyāpi hy ūṣmaṇa āyuṣā vinābhāvo na prāpnotīty aviśeṣavacanāt. na hy evaṃ viśeṣitaṃ yac cāyuṣman kauṣṭhila āyur yac coṣmā ādhyātmika ityādi. [Tib. 335b] bāhyasyāpi ca rūpasya kāṣṭhakuḍyāder asattvasaṃkhyātasya vijñānāśritatvaṃ prāpnoty aviśeṣavacanāt. caturvijñānasthitivac ceti vistaraḥ. yathā catasṛṇāṃ vijñānasthitīnām aviśeṣavacanād ārūpyadhātau tava rūpāstitvam. evaṃ tavāhāracatuṣkavacanād rūpārūpyadhātau kavaḍīkārāhāraprasaṃgaḥ. evaṃ hi sūtraṃ paṭhyate. catvāra āhārā bhūtānāṃ sattvānāṃ sthitaye saṃbhavaiṣiṇāṃ cānugrahāye. katame catvāraḥ. kavaḍīkārāhāraḥ audārikaḥ sūkṣmaḥ. sparśo dvitīyaḥ. manaḥsaṃcetanā tṛtīyaḥ. vijñānam āhāraś caturtha iti. evam āhāracatuṣkavacanāt sattvānāṃ sthityārtham aviśeṣeṇa. kāmāvacarāṇām ity aviśeṣitatvāt tava rūpārūpyadhātvor api kavaḍīkārāhāraprasaṃgaḥ. atikramyeti vistaraḥ. tatra nikāyāntarīyasyaitat syāt. asty asyotsargasyāpavādhaḥ. atikramya devān kavaḍīkārāhārabhakṣān iti vacanāt. udāyisūtrādiṣu bhedāc ca kāyasyātikramya devān kavaḍīkārāhārabhakṣān anyatamasmin divye manomayakāya upapadyata iti. prītyāhāravacanāc ceti. bhavati bhikṣavaḥ sa samayo yad ayaṃ lokaḥ saṃvartate. saṃvartamāne loke yadbhūyasā sattvā [Tib. 336a] ābhāsvare
body.translated_text: — thus they are called. And the <s>sūtra</s> illuminates this very meaning: 'If, <s>Ānanda</s>, consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) were not to descend into the mother's womb, would that name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) coagulate into the embryonic state (<s>kalala</s>)?' 'No, Venerable One.' 'If, <s>Ānanda</s>, consciousness, having descended, were to depart quickly, would that name-and-form become manifest in such a way (<s>itthatvā</s>)?' [Tib. 335a] 'No, Venerable One.' 'If, <s>Ānanda</s>, the consciousness of a young boy or girl were to be cut off, were to perish, were to cease to exist — would that name-and-form attain growth and full development?' 'No, Venerable One.' 'By this method too it should be understood that consciousness is the condition of name-and-form, and name-and-form is the condition of consciousness' — and so forth in detail. Here, is the negation [of life] without all of these — form and the rest — a negation of coming and going? Therein, coming (<s>āgati</s>) is rebirth here from the previous world through the continuum of intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>). Going (<s>gati</s>) is rebirth in the next world from this world through the continuum of intermediate existence. Or is it without even one of form and the rest — just any one of them? We say: the negation is without all of them — without form and the rest. 'One should not deliberate because of the undifferentiated statement' — if one were to think: 'this <s>sūtra</s> statement is undifferentiated.' But [it is] qualified by this <s>sūtra</s> statement: 'Venerable <s>Mahākauṣṭhila</s>, life-span (<s>āyus</s>)' — and so forth in detail up to — 'consciousness endowed with form (<s>rūpopaga</s>) remains' — by this <s>sūtra</s> statement it is qualified — stated with reference to the Desire Realm or the Form Realm. Up to: 'without all of those — form and the rest — the negation [applies].' To this it is said: there is an undesired consequence (<s>prasaṅga</s>). For even external heat would not lack life-span — because of the undifferentiated statement. For it is not thus qualified: 'Venerable <s>Kauṣṭhila</s>, life-span and heat are internal' and so forth. [Tib. 335b] And even external form — wood, walls, and the rest, counted as non-sentient — would absurdly require dependence on consciousness, because of the undifferentiated statement. 'Like the four stations of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>)' — and so forth in detail. Just as, because of the undifferentiated statement regarding the four stations of consciousness, for you there is the existence of form in the Formless Realm — similarly, because of your statement of the four nutriments (<s>āhāra</s>), there would absurdly be mouthful-food (<s>kavaḍīkārāhāra</s>) in the Form and Formless Realms. For thus the <s>sūtra</s> is read: 'There are four nutriments for the sustenance of existing beings and for the assistance of those seeking birth. What are the four? Mouthful-food, gross and subtle; contact is the second; mental volition is the third; and consciousness is the fourth nutriment.' Thus, because of the statement of four nutriments for the sustenance of beings, without differentiation — since it is not differentiated as 'of those in the Desire Realm' — for you there would absurdly be mouthful-food in the Form and Formless Realms. 'Going beyond' — and so forth in detail. Here, one belonging to another school (<s>nikāyāntarīya</s>) might say: this general rule has an exception. Because of the statement: 'Going beyond the gods who eat mouthful-food.' And because of the division of the body in the <s>Udāyi</s>-<s>sūtra</s> and the rest: 'Going beyond the gods who eat mouthful-food, one is reborn in a certain divine mind-made body.' 'And because of the statement of the joy-nutriment' — at that time, O monks, when this world devolves, for the most part beings [Tib. 336a] are reborn in the <s>Ābhāsvara</s>

body.text:
devanikāye utpadyante. tatra bhavanti rūpiṇo manomayā avikalā ahīnendriyāḥ sarvāṃgapratyaṃgopetāḥ śubhā varṇasthāyinaḥ svayaṃprabhā vihāyasaṃgamāḥ prītibhakṣāḥ prītyahārā dīrghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhantīty evamādiṣu sūtreṣu vacanād aprasaṃgaḥ kavaḍīkārāhārasya. yady evam ārūpyeṣv api rūpasyāprasaṃgaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇam apavādāt. kathaṃ. rūpāṇāṃ niḥsaraṇam ārūpyā ity ekaṃ sūtram apavādaḥ. ye te śāntā vimokṣā atikramya rūpāṇy ārūpyā iti dvitīyam. arūpiṇaḥ santi sattvā iti tṛtīyaṃ. sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramād iti caturtham. sati hi rūpa iti. yady ārūpyasamāpattyupapattiṣu rūpaṃ syāt. sati hi rūpe svaṃ rūpam avaśyaṃ saṃjānīrann iti sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramād iti vacanaṃ noktaṃ syāt. uktaṃ tu. ato 'pi na tatra rūpam asti. audārikaṃ iti vistaraḥ. tatraitat syāt. [Tib. 336b] audārikam adhobhūmikaṃ rūpam abhisaṃdhāyoktaṃ. ye te śāntā vimokṣā iti vistareṇa.
atra brūmaḥ. kavaḍīkārāhāre 'pi tulyaṃ. kathaṃ. atikramya devān kavaḍīkārāhārabhakṣān ity audārikam adhobhūmikaṃ kavaḍīkārāhāram abhisaṃdhāyoktam na rūpāvacaraṃ kavaḍīkārāhāraṃ sūkṣmam iti. yadi cādhobhūmyaudārikarūpaniḥsaraṇād ārūpyā ity ucyante. dhyānānām api cādhobhūminiḥsaraṇatvād ārūpyatvaprasaṃgaḥ. kathaṃ. kāmāvacaraudārikarūpaniḥsaraṇaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam. evam uttarottaraudārikarūpaniḥsaraṇaṃ. yāvac caturthadhyānam ity ārūpyatvaprasaṃgaḥ. vedanādiniḥsaraṇaṃ ca kiṃ noktaṃ. yady adhobhūmikaudārikaniḥsaraṇāt saty api svabhūmikarūpe ārūpyā ity ucyante. vedanādiniḥsaraṇād ārūpyā avedanā iti kiṃ nocyante. satyām api svabhūmivedanāyāṃ. ādiśabdena yāvad avijñānā iti kiṃ nocyante. saty api svabhūmivijñāna iti. kiṃ kāraṇam. adhobhūmikavedanādiniḥsaraṇāt. adhobhūmyaudarikavedanādiniḥsaraṇāt ity arthaḥ. rūpajātiṃ tu kṛtsnām atikrāntā. [Tib. 337a] yā kācid rūpajātiḥ audārikī vā sūkṣmā vā ādhyātmikī vā bāhyā vā. tāṃ sarvām atikrāntā ārūpyāḥ samāpattyupapattau. na vedanādijātiṃ na vedanāṃ sarvām atikrāntā ārūpyāḥ samāpattyupapattau. aduḥkhāsukhavedanāstitvāt. ādiśabdena yāvad vijñānaṃ vaktavyaṃ. ato rūpāṇāṃ niḥsaraṇam uktaṃ. na vedanādiniḥsaraṇaṃ. tasmād evaṃvādinām asmākaṃ na bhavaty ayaṃ prasaṃgaḥ. adhobhūmikavedanādiniḥsaraṇāt. vedanādiniḥsaraṇaṃ ca kiṃ noktam iti.
body.translated_text:
divine assembly. There they exist as having form, mind-made, with complete [faculties], with unimpaired sense-faculties, with all limbs and minor limbs, of beautiful complexion, self-luminous, going through the sky, eating joy, nourished by joy, long-lived, abiding for a long period' — from such statements in the <s>sūtra</s>s, there is no undesired consequence of mouthful-food. If so, even in the Formless [Realms], there is no undesired consequence of form. For what reason? Because of the exception. How? 'The Formless [Realms] are the escape from forms' — this is one <s>sūtra</s> as exception. 'Those peaceful liberations that, going beyond forms, are formless' — this is the second. 'There exist formless beings' — this is the third. 'Through the complete transcendence of all perceptions of form' — this is the fourth. 'Since form exists' — if form were to exist in the Formless attainments and births, then, since form exists, [beings] would necessarily perceive their own form — and thus the statement 'through the complete transcendence of all perceptions of form' would not have been made. But it has been stated — therefore form does not exist there either. 'Gross' — and so forth in detail. Here, one might think: [Tib. 336b] 'This was said with reference to gross form belonging to the lower ground: "Those peaceful liberations" — and so forth in detail.'
Here we say: the same applies to mouthful-food. How? 'Going beyond the gods who eat mouthful-food' — this was said with reference to gross mouthful-food belonging to the lower ground — not the subtle mouthful-food of the Form Realm. And if, because the Formless [Realms] are called 'formless' due to being the escape from gross form of the lower ground, then the <s>dhyāna</s>s too, being the escape from the lower ground, would absurdly be formless. How? The first <s>dhyāna</s> is the escape from gross form of the Desire Realm. Similarly, each successive one is the escape from the gross form of each successive lower ground — up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> — and thus the absurd consequence of formlessness. 'And why is escape from feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) and the rest not stated?' If, despite the existence of form belonging to their own ground, they are called 'formless' because of the escape from gross form of the lower ground — then why are they not called 'without feeling,' since they are the escape from feeling and the rest of the lower ground? Despite the existence of feeling belonging to their own ground — because of the escape from gross feeling of the lower ground. By the word 'and the rest,' up to: why are they not called 'without consciousness'? Despite the existence of consciousness belonging to their own ground. For what reason? Because of the escape from gross feeling and the rest of the lower ground — the meaning is: because of the escape from the gross feeling and the rest of the lower ground. But they have transcended the entire class of form — [Tib. 337a] whatever class of form there is — gross or subtle, internal or external — they have transcended all of it — the Formless [Realms], in both attainment and birth. They have not transcended the entire class of feeling and the rest — they have not transcended all feeling in the Formless attainments and births — because of the existence of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. By the word 'and the rest,' up to consciousness should be stated. Therefore, the escape from forms is stated — not the escape from feeling and the rest. Therefore, for us who hold this view, this undesired consequence does not arise — [the objection] 'because of the escape from feeling and the rest of the lower ground, why is escape from feeling not stated?'

body.text: āha. yadi rūpāṇāṃ niḥsaraṇam ārūpyāḥ. yat tarhy uktaṃ sūtre nāhaṃ bhavena bhavasya niḥsaraṇaṃ vadāmīti. tat katham rūpabhavasyārūpyabhavena
body.translated_text: He says: if the Formless [Realms] are the escape from forms, then what was stated in the <s>sūtra</s> — 'I do not say, monks, that escape from existence is by existence' — how then

body.text: niḥsaraṇaṃ. bhavenabhavasyāniḥsaraṇavacanaṃ tu tenaiva tasyāniḥsaraṇāt. tenaiva bhavena tasyaiva bhavasyāniḥsaraṇāt evam uktam. asarvānatyantaniḥsaraṇāc ca. asarvaniḥsaranaṃ. na hi rūpabhavena kāmabhavasya niḥsaraṇam iti. ārūpyabhavasyāpi tena niḥsaraṇaṃ bhavati. na cātyantaniḥsaraṇaṃ kāmabhavāt tena bhavati. punar āgamanāt. tathārūpyabhavena [Tib. 337b] rūpabhavasya niḥsaraṇaṃ. na kāmabhavasya. na cātyantaniḥsaraṇaṃ rūpabhavānām ārūpyabhavena.
body.translated_text: is there escape from form-existence (<s>rūpabhava</s>) through formless-existence (<s>ārūpyabhava</s>)? But the statement that escape from existence is not through existence itself [is made] because there is no escape from that very existence through that very same existence. And because the escape is not from all [existences], and not ultimate. 'Not from all' — for the escape from Desire-existence is not through Form-existence. And yet there is escape from Formless-existence through Form-existence too. And the escape from Desire-existence through Form-existence is not ultimate — because of returning again. Similarly, through Formless-existence, [Tib. 337b] there is escape from Form-existence, but not from Desire-existence. And the escape from Form-existence through Formless-existence is not ultimate.

body.text: uktaṃ yathā vartata iti.
body.translated_text: 'It has been stated how it operates' —

children.translated_text: 'The mental continuum depends on the class, the lifespan, and here' —

body.text: ityādi. traya iti pulliṃganirdeśaḥ. ārūpyā ity abhisaṃbaṃdhanāt. tathāprayogād iti. prayogakāle ākāśādīny ālambanāni bhavanti anyadā tv anye 'pi dharmā yathāsaṃbhavam ālambanānīti darśayati.
body.translated_text: and so forth. 'Three' — the use of the masculine gender is because of the connection with 'formless' (<s>ārūpya</s>). 'Because of the practice being thus' — he shows that at the time of the preparatory practice, space and the rest are the objects, but at other times, other <s>dharma</s>s too serve as objects as applicable.

children.translated_text: 'But not having perception and not without perception, because of dullness' —

body.text: iti. caturtha ārūpyaḥ kasmān na saṃjñīty ucyate. nāpy asaṃjña iti. māṃdyāt. tuśabdena tasyākāro 'ntarnītarūpo veditavyaḥ. yena hi kāraṇena sa caturtha ārūpyo naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam ity ucyate. tad eva kāraṇam ity ucyate. māndyād iti. prayogas tv asyaivaṃ sūcito bhavati. anvarthasaṃjñākaraṇāt. ata evāha. yady api tatrāpy evaṃ prayujyata ity ādi. saṃjñā gaṇḍaḥ gaṇḍavad gaṇḍaḥ. evaṃ yāvac chalyaḥ. asaṃjñakaḥ saṃmoham iti. saṃjñāyā abhāvo hi saṃmohakāraṇaṃ. ity arthaḥ. śīyateti saṃjñāsamucchedād ity abhiprāyaḥ. etac chāntaṃ etat praṇītaṃ. kiṃ. tad ity āha. yad uta naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam iti. saṃjñāmāndyam abhiprīyate. atra praśnayitavyam. kasmāt tu tais tad evaṃ gṛhyata iti. tair iti tatsamāpattibhiḥ. tad iti naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ. [Tib. 338a] evaṃ gṛhyata iti naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñeti gṛhyata ity arthaḥ. tad evaṃ paripraśne vigṛhītasyāvaśyam idaṃ vaktavyaṃ jāyate. mṛdatvāt saṃjñānāṃ. naivasaṃjnānāsaṃjñāyatanam ucyate ity etad evoktaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. Why is the fourth Formless [Realm] not called 'having perception' (<s>saṃjñī</s>)? Nor 'without perception' (<s>asaṃjña</s>)? Because of dullness (<s>māndya</s>). By the word 'but' (<s>tu</s>), its hidden meaning should be understood — [namely] the reason for which the fourth Formless [Realm] is called the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>) — that very reason is stated: 'because of dullness.' The method, however, is indicated thus: because of making a designation true to the meaning (<s>anvarthasaṃjñā</s>). Therefore he says: 'even though therein too it is thus applied' — and so forth. 'Perception is a boil, a boil-like boil' — similarly up to: 'a thorn.' 'Without perception [means] confusion' — for the absence of perception is the cause of confusion — this is the meaning. '[Perception] decays' — the intent is: because of the total destruction of perception. 'This is peaceful, this is excellent' — what? — he says: namely the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. The dullness of perception is meant. Here one should ask: why then is it grasped thus [as neither-perception-nor-non-perception] by them? 'By them' means: by those attainments. 'That' means: the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. [Tib. 338a] 'Grasped thus' means: grasped as 'neither-perception-nor-non-perception' — this is the meaning. Thus, when this question is analyzed, this must necessarily be stated: because of the mildness of perceptions, it is called the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception — this very thing has been stated.

body.text: (VIII.5, 6) samāpattidravyāṇi maulānīti.
body.translated_text: (VIII.5, 6) 'The fundamental substances of the attainments' —

body.text: śakhās teṣāṃ nopanaśyanta ity abhiprāyaḥ. kathaṃ sapta trividhānīty āha.
body.translated_text: the intent is: their branches do not perish. How are there seven threefold? — he says:

body.text: anāsravaṃ nāstīti saṃjñamāndyāt. yad āsvādayati. tasmād vyutthita iti. śuddhakāt. yenāsvādayati. tat samāpanna iti. āsvādanāsaṃprayuktaṃ.
body.translated_text: the uncontaminated does not exist [for the fourth formless] — because of the dullness of perception. 'From which one has tasted — from that, having emerged' — from the pure [attainment]. 'By which one tastes — being attained in that' — the [attainment] associated with tasting (<s>āsvādanāsaṃprayukta</s>).

body.text: (VIII.7, 8) yathānta caturaṅgasenā nāṃgebhyo 'rthāṃtarabhūtā. evaṃ paṃcāṃgadhyānaṃ
body.translated_text: (VIII.7, 8) Just as a four-limbed army is not something different from its limbs — so a five-limbed <s>dhyāna</s>

body.text: nārthāntaram iti svamataṃ darśayati.
body.translated_text: is not something different — he shows his own view.

body.text: iti. pūrvoktāḥ prītisukhacittaikāgratāḥ.
body.translated_text: that is, the previously stated joy, bliss (<s>sukha</s>), and one-pointedness of mind (<s>cittaikāgratā</s>).

body.text: caturaṃgaṃ dvitīyam.
body.translated_text: the second [<s>dhyāna</s>] has four limbs.

body.text: saṃskāropekṣātra gṛhyate. yā prītir anābhogalakṣaṇā. smṛtir upekṣānimittasyāsaṃpramoṣaḥ. smṛtyasaṃpramoṣe saṃprajñānatā saṃprajñānaṃ. caturthe upekṣāpariśuddhiḥ. upekṣāyāḥ pariśuddhir upekṣāpariśuddhiḥ. [Tib. 338b] adhobhūmikapakṣālavigamāt. aṣṭāv apakṣālā apakṣīyante. evaṃ smṛtipariśuddhiḥ.
body.translated_text: what is grasped here is equanimity regarding formations (<s>saṃskāropekṣā</s>). The joy (<s>prīti</s>) that has the character of non-deliberateness (<s>anābhoga</s>). Mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) is the non-loss of the sign of equanimity. Clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajñāna</s>) in the non-loss of mindfulness is clear knowing. In the fourth, the purification of equanimity — the purification of equanimity is the purification of equanimity. [Tib. 338b] Because of the departure of the blemish of the lower ground. Eight blemishes are removed. Similarly, the purification of mindfulness.

body.text: (VIII.9) prathamadhyānikānīti. prathamadhyāne bhavāni. ata evocyata iti. yasmād dvitīyādiṣv adhyātmasaṃprasādādayo vardhante. kathaṃ. catuṣkoṭikaṃ. syāt prathame dhyāne na dvitīye. syād dvitīye na prathame. syād ubhayoḥ. syān nobhayoḥ. evaṃ sarvāṇi dhyānāṃgāni parasparaṃ yojyāni. kathaṃ. yāny aṃgāni prathame dhyāne. tṛtīye 'pi tāni. catuṣkoṭikaṃ. prathamā koṭiḥ vitarkavicāraprītisukhāni. dvitīyā upekṣāsmṛtisaṃprajñānasukhāni. tṛtīyā samādhiḥ. caturthī koṭir uktanirmuktā dharmāḥ. yāny aṃgāni prathame dhyāne. caturthe 'pi tāni. catuṣkoṭikam. prathamā koṭir vitarkavicāraprītisukhāni. dvitīyā aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā upekṣāpariśuddhiḥ. smṛtipariśuddhiś ca. tṛtīyā samādhiḥ. caturthī uktanirmuktā dharmāḥ [Tib. 339a] yāny aṃgāni dvitīye dhyāne. tṛtīye 'pi tāni. catuṣkoṭikaṃ. prathamā koṭir adhyātmasaṃprasādaprītisukhāni. dvitīyā upekṣāsmṛtisaṃprajñānasukhāni. tṛtīyā samādhiḥ. caturthī uktanirmuktadharmāḥ. yāny aṃgāni dvitīye dhyāne. caturthe 'pi vā tāni. catuṣkoṭikaṃ. prathamā koṭir adhyātmasaṃprasādaprītisukhāni. dvitīyā tadaṃgāni samādhiṃ hitvā. tṛtīyā samādhiḥ. caturthī uktanirmuktā dharmāḥ. yāny aṃgāni tṛtīye dhyāne caturthe 'pi tāni. catuṣkoṭikaṃ. prathamā koṭīḥ samādhivarjyāni tadaṃgāni. dvitīyāpy evaṃ. tṛtīyā samādhiḥ. caturthī uktanirmuktā dharmāḥ. etac ca tad ekāvacaraṃ nāma.
body.translated_text: (VIII.9) 'Of the first <s>dhyāna</s>' — belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s>. 'Therefore it is said' — because in the second and subsequent [<s>dhyāna</s>s], inner clarity (<s>adhyātmasaṃprasāda</s>) and the rest increase. How? A four-cornered analysis (<s>catuṣkoṭika</s>): there may be [a factor] in the first <s>dhyāna</s> but not in the second; there may be [one] in the second but not in the first; there may be [one] in both; there may be [one] in neither. Thus, all <s>dhyāna</s> limbs should be combined with each other. How? Those limbs that belong to the first <s>dhyāna</s> — those also [belong to] the third. The four-cornered analysis: the first corner is <s>vitarka</s> (initial application), <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application), <s>prīti</s> (joy), and <s>sukha</s> (pleasure). The second is <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), <s>saṃprajñāna</s> (clear comprehension), and <s>sukha</s>. The third is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). The fourth corner is the <s>dharma</s>s excluded from those stated. Those limbs that belong to the first <s>dhyāna</s> — those also [compared with] the fourth. [Tib. 339a] The four-cornered analysis: the first corner is <s>vitarka</s>, <s>vicāra</s>, <s>prīti</s>, and <s>sukha</s>. The second is <s>aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā</s> (neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling), purity of <s>upekṣā</s>, and purity of <s>smṛti</s>. The third is <s>samādhi</s>. The fourth is the <s>dharma</s>s excluded from those stated. Those limbs that belong to the second <s>dhyāna</s> — those also [compared with] the third. The four-cornered analysis: the first corner is inner clarity (<s>adhyātmasaṃprasāda</s>), <s>prīti</s>, and <s>sukha</s>. The second is <s>upekṣā</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>saṃprajñāna</s>, and <s>sukha</s>. The third is <s>samādhi</s>. The fourth is the <s>dharma</s>s excluded from those stated. Those limbs that belong to the second <s>dhyāna</s> — those also [compared with] the fourth. The four-cornered analysis: the first corner is inner clarity, <s>prīti</s>, and <s>sukha</s>. The second is the limbs of that [fourth dhyāna] excluding <s>samādhi</s>. The third is <s>samādhi</s>. The fourth is the <s>dharma</s>s excluded from those stated. Those limbs that belong to the third <s>dhyāna</s> — those also [compared with] the fourth. The four-cornered analysis: the first corner is the limbs of that [third dhyāna] excluding <s>samādhi</s>. The second is likewise. The third is <s>samādhi</s>. The fourth is the <s>dharma</s>s excluded from those stated. And this is called 'belonging to a single ground' (<s>ekāvacara</s>).

body.text: kasmāt tṛtīye dhyāne sukhaṃ dravyāntaram ucyata iti. katham ucyate. tāny etāny aṣṭādaśadhyānāṃgāni bhavantīti vistareṇoktvā punar āha. nāmata evaṃ.
body.translated_text: Why is <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) in the third <s>dhyāna</s> said to be a distinct substance (<s>dravyāntara</s>)? How is it stated? Having stated in detail 'these are the eighteen <s>dhyāna</s> limbs,' he further says: 'only in name thus' —

body.text: dravyata etāny ekādaśa bhavanti. prathamadhyānikāni paṃca. dvitīye 'dhyātmasaṃprasādo vardhate. tṛtīye upekṣāsmṛtisaṃprajñānasukhānītivacanāt. sukheṃdriyayogād iti. sukheṃdriyasaṃbhavāt. nāsty eva caitasikaṃ sukheṃdriyaṃ triṣv api hi dhyāneṣu. kiṃ tarhi. kāyikam [Tib. 339b] eva sukham aṃgavyavasthāpitaṃ. samāhitāvasthāṃtarālasamudācārāt. dārṣṭāṃtikānāṃ kilaiṣa pakṣaḥ. teṣāṃ hi na dvibhūmikam eva sukhendriyaṃ. kāmaprathamadhyānabhūmikam iti. kiṃ tarhi. caturbhūmikam api sukhendriyaṃ bhavati. kāmāvacaraṃ yāvat tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikaṃ iti. ata eva ca vibhāṣāyāṃ bhadantena sautrāntikenoktam. ābhidhārmikāṇāṃ araghaṭṭeneva cakṣurvijñānādikam adhastād ūrdhvam ākṛṣyata iti. tad evam asyeṣṭaṃ bhavati. cakṣurvijñānādikaṃ dvitīyādidhyānabhūmikam api bhavatīti.
body.translated_text: In substance, these are eleven. Five belong to the first <s>dhyāna</s>. In the second, inner clarity (<s>adhyātmasaṃprasāda</s>) increases. In the third, because of the statement '<s>upekṣā</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>saṃprajñāna</s>, and <s>sukha</s>' — 'because of the connection with <s>sukhendriya</s> (the pleasure faculty)' — because of the occurrence of <s>sukhendriya</s>. There is no mental (<s>caitasika</s>) pleasure faculty whatsoever in [any of] the three <s>dhyāna</s>s. What then? Only bodily (<s>kāyika</s>) pleasure is established as a limb [of <s>dhyāna</s>] — [Tib. 339b] because it occurs in the intervals between concentrated states (<s>samāhitāvasthāntarāla</s>). This is reportedly the position of the <s>Dārṣṭāntika</s>s. For them, the pleasure faculty does not belong to merely two grounds; it is not limited to the Desire Realm and first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. What then? The pleasure faculty extends to four grounds — from the Desire Realm up to and including the third <s>dhyāna</s> ground. And for precisely this reason, the venerable <s>Sautrāntika</s> stated in the <s>Vibhāṣā</s>: 'For the <s>Ābhidhārmika</s>s, eye-consciousness and the rest are pulled upward from below as if by a water-wheel (<s>araghaṭṭa</s>).' Thus, his accepted position becomes: eye-consciousness and the rest also belong to the ground of the second and subsequent <s>dhyāna</s>s.

body.text: adhyāropita eṣa pāṭha iti. yo 'yaṃ caitasikam iti pāṭhaḥ. sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisaṃvedayata iti svaśabdena vacanāc ceti. tṛtīyadhyānanirdeśa evam uktaṃ. sa prīter virāgād upekṣako viharati smṛtimān saṃprajānamān. sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisaṃvedayate. yat tad āryā ācakṣate upekṣakaḥ smṛtimān sukhavihārī tṛtīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharatīti. yadi hi tac caitasikaṃ syāt kathaṃ tat kāyena pratisaṃvedyet. manaḥ kāyeneti. manaḥ samudāyenaivam uktvā. ko guṇa iti. sukhaṃ ca manasā pratisaṃvedayati. sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisaṃvedayata ity evaṃ vā vaktavyaṃ syād ity abhiprāyaḥ. caturthe dhyāne praśrabdhibhūyastve 'pi sukhāvacanāc ceti. caturthe dhyāne praśrabdhisukhaṃ bhūyo bhavati bahutaraṃ bhavati. dhyānāntarebhyaś caturthasya praśrabdhataratvāt. tadbhūyastve [Tib. 340a] 'pi sukhasyāvacanaṃ. caturthe dhyāne sukhaṃ nocyate. tasya sukhasyāvacanāt. vedanāsukham eva tat tṛtīye dhyāne gamyate. na caturthe sukhā vedanāstīti tatra nocyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. sukhavedanānukūlā praśrabdhiḥ sukham iti cet. syān mataṃ. prathamadvitīyayor dhyānayoḥ. sukhavedanānukūlā praśrabdhiḥ. taddvayoḥ sukham ity uktvā caturthe dhyāne praśrabdhiḥ sukhavedanānukūlā na bhavatīti noktā. yady evaṃ tṛtīye praśrabdhisukhāvacanaṃ kasmāt. tṛtīyadhyānapraśrabdhir api sukhavedanānukūlā bhavati. tatra praśrabdhisukhaṃ kasmān noktaṃ. vedanāsukham eva hi tatra bhavadbhir vyavasthāpitaṃ. na praśrabdhiḥ sukhaṃ. dviḥsukhapāṭhāt. upekṣopahatatvād iti cet. syān mataṃ. tṛtīye dhyāna upekṣā karmaṇyatālakṣaṇā bhavati. tayopahatā praśrabdhir iti nocyate iti. na. upekṣayaiva
body.translated_text: 'This reading is interpolated' — referring to the reading 'mental' (<s>caitasika</s>). 'And because of the statement in its own words: "one experiences pleasure with the body"' — in the description of the third <s>dhyāna</s>, it is stated thus: 'Free from the fading of <s>prīti</s> (joy), one abides in <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), mindful and clearly comprehending. One experiences <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) with the body. That which the noble ones declare: "Equanimous, mindful, abiding in pleasure" — one enters and abides in the third <s>dhyāna</s>.' For if that [pleasure] were mental, how would one experience it with the body? '<s>Manaḥ</s> (mind) is meant by "body"' — meaning the aggregate (<s>samudāya</s>). Having stated this, [the objection follows:] 'What is the advantage?' — the intent is: it should be stated either 'one experiences pleasure with the mind' or 'one experiences pleasure with the body' — [but not equivocally]. 'And because in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, despite the abundance of <s>praśrabdhi</s> (tranquility), <s>sukha</s> is not mentioned' — in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>praśrabdhi</s>-<s>sukha</s> (tranquility-pleasure) is more [abundant], is greater, because the fourth is more tranquil than the other <s>dhyāna</s>s. Despite its abundance, <s>sukha</s> is not mentioned — <s>sukha</s> is not stated for the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. Because of the non-mention of that <s>sukha</s>, it is understood that it is <s>vedanā</s>-<s>sukha</s> (feeling-pleasure) alone in the third <s>dhyāna</s>. The intent is: because pleasant feeling does not exist in the fourth, it is not mentioned there. 'If <s>praśrabdhi</s> favorable to pleasant feeling is <s>sukha</s>' — suppose one thinks: in the first and second <s>dhyāna</s>s, <s>praśrabdhi</s> favorable to pleasant feeling — that is the <s>sukha</s> of those two — having stated this, [the objector continues:] in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>praśrabdhi</s> is not favorable to pleasant feeling, therefore it is not called [<s>sukha</s>]. If so, why is <s>praśrabdhi</s>-<s>sukha</s> not mentioned in the third? The <s>praśrabdhi</s> of the third <s>dhyāna</s> is also favorable to pleasant feeling. Why is <s>praśrabdhi</s>-<s>sukha</s> not stated there? For it is <s>vedanā</s>-<s>sukha</s> alone that you have established there, not <s>praśrabdhi</s> as <s>sukha</s> — because of the double occurrence of the word '<s>sukha</s>.' 'Because of being undermined by <s>upekṣā</s>' — suppose one thinks: in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>upekṣā</s> has the characteristic of workability (<s>karmaṇyatā</s>). <s>Praśrabdhi</s> undermined by that [<s>upekṣā</s>] is therefore not mentioned. No — because of the growth of that by <s>upekṣā</s> alone

body.text: tadvṛddheḥ. naitad evaṃ. upekṣayaiva tu tatra tṛtīye dhyāne praśrabdhisukhavṛddheḥ. na hy upaghātahetunaiva vṛddhir yujyata iti. katham upekṣayaiva tadvṛddhir ity ato bravīti. pūrvikābhyāṃ tadviśeṣād iti. pūrvikābhyāṃ hi prathamadvitīyadhyānapraśrabdhibhyāṃ. [Tib. 340b] tṛtīyadhyānapraśrabdhir viśiṣṭā. pūrvikābhyāṃ dhyānābhyāṃ tṛtīyasya viśiṣṭatvāt. yasmin samaya iti vistaraḥ. yasmin samaye āryaśrāvakaḥ pravivekajāṃ prītiṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharati. paṃcāsya dharmās tasmin samaye prahīyante. paṃca dharmā bhāvanāparipūriṃ gacchanti. adhyātmasaṃprasādaḥ prītiḥ praśrabdhiḥ sukhaṃ [prajñā] samādhiś ceti. praśrabdhisukhayor ananyatve katham eṣāṃ paṃcatvaṃ syāt. arthāntaratve ca sati kāyikam eva sukhaṃ triṣv api dhyāneṣv iti siddhaṃ bhavati. samāpannasya kathaṃ kāyavijñānam iti. atrocyate. samādhiviśeṣajena praśrabdhināmnā sukhavedanīyena sukhavedanānukūlena vāyunā kāyaspharaṇāt kāyadhmāpanāt. kiṃ. kāyavijñānaṃ bhavaty eveti. bahirvikṣepāt samādhibhraṃśa iti cet. yadi manyeta kāyvijñānotpattyā bahirvikṣepād bāhyaviṣayavikṣepāt samādhibhraṃśa iti. na. samādhijasyeti vistaraḥ. naitad evaṃ bhaviṣyatīti. kasmāt. samādhijasyāṃtaḥkāyasaṃbhūtasyābahirjabhūtasyety arthaḥ. kāyasukhasya kāyavijñānasaṃprayuktasya veditasukhasya samādhyanukūlatvān nāsmāt samādhibhraṃśa ity arthaḥ. na. [Tib. 341a] ata eveti. na kāyavijñānakāle vyutthitaḥ syāt. ata eva kāraṇāt samādhyanukūlatvād ity arthaḥ. tatsaṃmukhībhāvāntaraṃ hi punar upatiṣṭhate samādhir ity abhiprāyaḥ. kāmāvacareṇa kāyavijñānena rūpāvacarasya spraṣṭavyasyāgrahaṇād rūpāvacaram etat kāyavijñānaṃ na kāmāvacaram. ata eva tatsaṃprayogi sukhaṃ dhyānāṃgaṃ na sidhyati. praśrabdhijñānasyotpatter iti. rūpāvacarasyāḥ kāmāvacareṇa [kāyavijñānena] kāyendriyeṇa samadhibalādhānataḥ. tad dhi kāyendriyaṃ samāhitasya tām avasthāṃ gataṃ. yad ūrdhvabhūmikasya kāyavijñānasyāśrayo bhavatīti. anāsrave apīti. spraṣṭavyaṃ ca praśrabdhilakṣaṇaṃ tadālaṃbanaṃ ca kāyavijñānaṃ spraṣṭavyakāyavijñāne 'nāsrave api syātāṃ. kiṃ kāraṇam ity āha. mā bhūt kiṃcid aṃgaṃ sāsravaṃ kiṃcid anāsravam iti cet. yady evaṃ manyeta. kāyikapraśrabdhisaṃbodhyaṃgavacanād iṣṭe. yāpi kāyapraśrabdhiḥ. tad api praśrabdhisaṃbodhyaṃgam abhijñāyai saṃbodhaye nirvāṇāya saṃvartate. yāpi
body.translated_text: . This is not so. Rather, it is because of the growth of <s>praśrabdhi</s>-<s>sukha</s> in that very third <s>dhyāna</s> by <s>upekṣā</s> alone. For growth through the very cause of undermining is not logically possible. How then does <s>upekṣā</s> alone cause the growth of that? Therefore he says: 'Because of the distinction from the two previous ones' — for in comparison with the two previous <s>praśrabdhi</s>s belonging to the first and second <s>dhyāna</s>s, [Tib. 340b] the <s>praśrabdhi</s> of the third <s>dhyāna</s> is superior, because the third is superior to the two previous <s>dhyāna</s>s. 'At the time when' — and so forth in detail. 'At the time when a noble <s>śrāvaka</s>, having directly realized the joy born of seclusion, enters and abides [in the first <s>dhyāna</s>], five <s>dharma</s>s are abandoned in him at that time, and five <s>dharma</s>s reach the fullness of cultivation: inner clarity, <s>prīti</s>, <s>praśrabdhi</s>, <s>sukha</s>, [<s>prajñā</s>,] and <s>samādhi</s>.' If <s>praśrabdhi</s> and <s>sukha</s> were not distinct, how could these be five? And given their distinctness, it is established that in all three <s>dhyāna</s>s, <s>sukha</s> is bodily alone. 'How can there be body-consciousness (<s>kāyavijñāna</s>) for one who is concentrated?' — to this, it is replied: because of the pervading (<s>spharaṇa</s>) and suffusing (<s>dhmāpana</s>) of the body by a pleasant-to-be-felt, favorable-to-pleasant-feeling wind (<s>vāyu</s>) called <s>praśrabdhi</s>, born from the distinction of <s>samādhi</s>. What [follows]? Body-consciousness does indeed arise. 'Because of distraction outward and loss of <s>samādhi</s>' — if one thinks that through the arising of body-consciousness there is distraction outward — distraction toward external objects — and thus loss of <s>samādhi</s>: No. 'Because it is born of <s>samādhi</s>' — and so forth in detail. This will not be so. Why? Because it is born of <s>samādhi</s>, arisen within the body, not arisen externally — this is the meaning. The bodily pleasure associated with body-consciousness — the felt pleasure — because of its being favorable to <s>samādhi</s>, there is no loss of <s>samādhi</s> from this — this is the meaning. No — [Tib. 341a] 'for this very reason' — one would not be in the post-attainment state at the time of body-consciousness. For this very reason — because of its being favorable to <s>samādhi</s> — this is the meaning. The intent is: <s>samādhi</s> re-establishes itself in another moment of facing that [concentration]. Because a Desire Realm body-consciousness cannot apprehend a Form Realm tangible, this body-consciousness belongs to the Form Realm, not the Desire Realm. For this very reason, the pleasure associated with it is not established as a <s>dhyāna</s> limb. 'Because of the arising of <s>praśrabdhi</s>-knowledge' — of that Form Realm [body-consciousness], through the empowerment of <s>samādhi</s> by means of the Desire Realm body-faculty (<s>kāyendriya</s>). For that body-faculty of one who is concentrated has reached such a state that it becomes the support for body-consciousness belonging to a higher ground. 'Even in the uncontaminated [<s>dhyāna</s>]' — tangibles of the nature of <s>praśrabdhi</s> and the body-consciousness taking them as object — even if the tangible and body-consciousness were uncontaminated. For what reason? He says: 'Lest some limb be contaminated and some uncontaminated' — if one were to think so. 'Because of the statement of bodily <s>praśrabdhi</s> as a limb of awakening (<s>saṃbodhyaṅga</s>)' — it is accepted that whatever bodily <s>praśrabdhi</s> there is, that too is a <s>praśrabdhi</s> limb of awakening, conducive to <s>abhijñā</s>, to awakening, to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Whatever

body.text:
cittapraśrabdhir yāvad eva spraṣṭavyāni saṃbodhyaṃgam abhijñāyai saṃbodhaye nirvāṇāya saṃvartata iti vacanāt. bodhyaṃgavacanād iṣṭe [Tib. 341b] spraṣṭavyakāyavijñāne anāsrave iti. bodhyaṃgānukūlatvād iti cet. athaivaṃ parihriyeta. yasmāt kāyikī praśrabdhir bodhyaṃgānukūlā. tasmād bodhyaṃgam ity upacaryate na tu bodhyaṃgam iti. anāsravatvam
apy evaṃ. anāsravatvānukūlatvāt te spraṣṭavyakāyavijñāne anāsrave ity upacaryete. na tv anāsrave eveti. evam anayor anāsravatvaṃ. sāsravā dharmā iti vistaraḥ. sāsravā dharmāḥ katame. yāvad eva cakṣur yāvanti eva rūpāṇi yāvad eva cakṣurvijñānaṃ. yāvad yāvān eva kāyo yāvanty eva spraṣṭavyāni yāvad eva kāyavijñānam iti. asya sūtrasya virodha iti evaṃ cen manyeta. tan na. anyaspraṣṭavyakāyavijñānābhisaṃdhivacanāt. tat praśrabdhivyatiriktānāṃ spraṣṭavyānāṃ kāyavijñānavyatiriktānāṃ ca kayavijñānānām abhisaṃdhivacanāt. na cānāsrava iti vistaraḥ. nanv anāsrave 'nāsravavavyavasthāne kiṃcid aṃgaṃ sāsravaṃ kiṃcid anāsravaṃ syād iti. yady eṣa doṣa iti manyeta. tatspraṣṭavyakāyavijñānasya sāsravatvāt. taditarasyānāsravatvāt. atrocyate. ayaugapadyāt ko doṣa iti. [Tib. 342a] yadā sāsravam aṃgaṃ samudācarati. na tadānāsravaṃ samudācarati. yadānāsravam aṃgaṃ. na tadā sāsravam ity adoṣa eṣaḥ. sukhaprītyasamavadhānāt. sukhasya kāyikasya prīteś ca mānasyāḥ asamavadhānād ayaugapadyāt. na paṃcāṃgaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ syād iti cet. yady evaṃ manyeta. na sa doṣaḥ. kasmāt. saṃbhavaṃ praty upadeśād vitarkavicāravat. yathā savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam iti paryāyeṇa vitarkavicārau bhavataḥ. evaṃ sukhaprītī api saṃbhavaṃ praty upadeśād adoṣa eṣa iti. sādhyam iti cet. vitarkavicārau paryāyeṇa bhavata iti sādhyam iti. āha. siddhaṃ. katham ity āha. vitarkavicārayor virodhād iti. yady audārikatā cittasya. sūkṣmatā nāsti. yadi sūkṣmatā. audārikatā nāstīti. virodhād vitarkavicārayor ayaugapadyaṃ. doṣavacanāc ceti. āpekṣikī caudārikasūkṣmatā bhūmiprakārabhedād ity ā bhavāgrād vitarkavicārau syātām ity ādi. keṣāṃcit pāṭho bhavati doṣāvacanāc ceti. asmavadhānena ca na kaścid doṣa ucyata ity arthaḥ. dvitricaturaṃgāpakarṣeṇeti. dvyaṅgāpakarṣeṇa dvitīyadhyānavyavasthānaṃ. tatra vitarkavicārayor abhāvat. [Tib. 342b] tryaṃgāpakarṣeṇa tṛtīyadhyānavyavasthānaṃ. tatra prītir api nāstīti. caturaṃgāpakarṣeṇa
body.translated_text: — 'Mental tranquility (<s>cittapraśrabdhi</s>), up to tangibles, is an awakening factor that conduces to <s>abhijñā</s> (direct knowledge), to awakening, and to <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — from this statement. 'Because of the statement of "awakening factor," it is accepted that tangibles and body-consciousness are uncontaminated' — if [one argues] because of being favorable to the awakening factors. Then it could be resolved thus: since bodily tranquility (<s>kāyikī praśrabdhi</s>) is favorable to the awakening factors, therefore it is metaphorically designated as an awakening factor — but it is not [actually] an awakening factor. Similarly with uncontaminated status — because of being favorable to uncontaminated status, those tangibles and body-consciousness are metaphorically designated as uncontaminated — but they are not actually uncontaminated. Thus is the uncontaminated status of these two. 'Contaminated <s>dharma</s>s' — in detail. 'What are contaminated <s>dharma</s>s? Whatever is the eye, up to whatever are forms, up to whatever is eye-consciousness; up to whatever is the body, up to whatever are tangibles, up to whatever is body-consciousness' — if one thinks there is contradiction with this <s>sūtra</s> — that is not so. Because the statement is with reference to other tangibles and body-consciousness — that is, with reference to tangibles other than tranquility and body-consciousnesses other than [uncontaminated] body-consciousness — the statement is intended [for those]. 'And they are not uncontaminated' — in detail. 'Surely, in the establishment of an uncontaminated [awakening factor], some limb would be contaminated and some uncontaminated' — if one thinks this is a fault — because of the contaminated status of those tangibles and body-consciousness, and the uncontaminated status of the others — here it is said: 'What fault is there from non-simultaneity?' When a contaminated limb is operative, at that time an uncontaminated [limb] is not operative; when an uncontaminated limb [is operative], at that time a contaminated [limb] is not — so this is no fault. 'Because of the non-co-occurrence of pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and joy (<s>prīti</s>)' — because of the non-co-occurrence of bodily pleasure and mental joy — because of [their] non-simultaneity — 'the first <s>dhyāna</s> would not have five limbs' — if one thinks so. That is not a fault. Why? 'Because the teaching is regarding the possibility [of their occurrence], like <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>' — just as 'the first <s>dhyāna</s> has <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application)' — <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> exist alternately. Similarly, pleasure and joy too — because the teaching is regarding the possibility [of their occurrence] — this is no fault. 'If [you say] this is what needs to be proved' (<s>sādhyam</s>) — that <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> exist alternately is what needs to be proved. He says: 'It is established.' How? — he says: 'Because of the mutual incompatibility of <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>.' If there is coarseness of mind, fineness does not exist; if there is fineness, coarseness does not exist — because of the mutual incompatibility of <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, [their] non-simultaneity [is established]. 'And because of the statement of a fault' — the coarseness and fineness are relative, based on the distinction of grounds and types — and so forth, up to: <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> would exist up to the Peak of Existence. Some have the reading: 'and because of no statement of a fault' — the meaning is: no fault is stated regarding non-co-occurrence. 'Through the subtraction of two, three, and four limbs' — through the subtraction of two limbs, the second <s>dhyāna</s> is established — because <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> are absent there. Through the subtraction of three limbs, the third <s>dhyāna</s> is established — because joy too is absent there. Through the subtraction of four limbs

body.text: caturthadhyānavyavasthānaṃ. tatra sukham api nāstīti. na tu saṃjñādīnām aṃgatvam uktam iti. na hi saṃjñādīnāṃ dhyānāntareṣv apakarso 'stīti. kim arthaṃ paṃcānām evāṃgatvaṃ. yady ayam artho nābhipreta iti. yady upakaratvāt paṃcānām evāṃgatvaṃ. tan na. vitarkavicārābhyāṃ smṛtiprajñayor upakaratvāt. na hi. tathā vitarkavicārāv upakarau yathā smṛtiprajñe iṣṭe. sūpasthitasmṛter yathābhūtaṃprajānato layauddhatyādyabhāvataḥ.
body.translated_text: the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is established — because pleasure too is absent there. 'But the status of being a limb for perception and the rest is not stated' — for perception and the rest do not undergo subtraction in the different <s>dhyāna</s>s. 'For what purpose is the status of limb assigned to only five?' — if this meaning is not intended. 'If [the status of limb is] because of being beneficial, the five alone' — that is not so. Because <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> are beneficial to mindfulness and wisdom. 'Not so' — <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> are not beneficial in the same way that mindfulness and wisdom are accepted [to be]. 'Because of the absence of sinking and agitation and the rest, for one whose mindfulness is well-established and who knows as it truly is.'

body.text: tasmād vicāryam etad iti. yogācārabhūmidarśanena vicāryam etad iti tatra kautūhalaṃ pātayaty ācāryaḥ. ayaṃ cātrārthasaṃkṣepo draṣṭavyaḥ. kiṃ punar adhikṛtya vitarkādaya evāṃgatvena vyavasthāpitāḥ satsv anyeṣu dharmeṣu. tāvadbhiḥ. pratipakṣānuśaṃsatadubhayāśrayāṃgaparisamāpteḥ. ārūpyeṣv aṃgavyavasthānaṃ nāsti. śamathaikarasatām upādāya. tad uktaṃ pratipakṣāṃgam upadāya. anuśaṃsāṅgam upādāya. tadubhayasaṃniśrayāṃgaṃ copādāya. prathame tāvad dhyāne vitarko vicāraś ca pratipakṣāṃgaṃ. tabhyāṃ kāmavyāpādavihiṃsāvitarkaprahāṇāt. prītiḥ sukhaṃ cānuśaṃsāṃgaṃ. [Tib. 343a] vitarkavicārābhyāṃ pratipakṣite vipakṣe tadvivekajaprītisukhalābhāt. cittaikāgratā tadubhayasaṃniśrayāṃgaṃ. saṃniśrayabalena vitarkādipravṛtter iti. tathā dvitīye dhyāne 'dhyātmasaṃprasādaḥ pratipakṣāṃgaṃ. tena vitarkavicārapratipakṣaṇāt. prītisukhe cittaikāgratā ca śeṣe aṃge pūrvavat. tṛtīye dhyāne upekṣāsmṛtisaṃprajanyaṃ ca pratipakṣāṃgaḥ. taiḥ prītipratipakṣaṇāt. sukhaṃ cittaikāgratā ca śeṣe aṃge yathākramaṃ pūrvavat. caturthe dhyāne upekṣāpariśuddhiḥ smṛtipariśuddhiś ca pratipakṣāṃgaṃ. tābhyāṃ dhyāneṣu sukhapratipakṣaṇāt. aduḥkhasukhā vedanā anuśaṃsāṃgaṃ. cittaikāgratā tadubhayasaṃniśrayāṃgam iti.
body.translated_text: 'Therefore this should be examined' — by examining through the view of the <s>Yogācārabhūmi</s>, the <s>Ācārya</s> arouses curiosity about that [text]. And here the summary of the meaning should be understood. With reference to what, then, are <s>vitarka</s> and the rest established as limbs, when other <s>dharma</s>s exist? [They are so established] by so many [dharmas] — because of the complete enumeration of limbs that are antidote, benefit, and the basis of both.
