In the formless [attainments], there is no establishment of limbs — because of their having a single flavor of tranquility. This has been stated: taking up the antidote-limb, taking up the benefit-limb, and taking up the basis-of-both limb. In the first <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> are the antidote-limb — because by those two, the <s>vitarka</s>s of desire (<s>kāma</s>), ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), and harming (<s>vihiṃsā</s>) are abandoned. Joy (<s>prīti</s>) and pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) are the benefit-limb — because when the adversary is counteracted by <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, the joy and pleasure born of that seclusion are obtained. One-pointedness of mind (<s>cittaikāgratā</s>) is the basis-of-both limb — because <s>vitarka</s> and the rest operate by the power of that basis. Similarly, in the second <s>dhyāna</s>, inner clarity (<s>adhyātmasaṃprasāda</s>) is the antidote-limb — because by that, <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> are counteracted. Joy, pleasure, and one-pointedness — the remaining limbs — are as before. In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), and clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>) are the antidote-limb — because by those, joy is counteracted. Pleasure and one-pointedness are the remaining limbs, in order, as before. In the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, purification of equanimity (<s>upekṣāpariśuddhi</s>) and purification of mindfulness (<s>smṛtipariśuddhi</s>) are the antidote-limb — because by those two, pleasure in the <s>dhyāna</s>s is counteracted. The feeling of neither-pleasure-nor-pain (<s>aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā</s>) is the benefit-limb. One-pointedness is the basis-of-both limb.

body.text: śraddhā prasāda iti. śraddhaiva prasādaḥ śraddhāprasādaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Faith is clarity (<s>prasāda</s>)' — faith itself is clarity; hence 'faith-clarity' (<s>śraddhāprasāda</s>).

body.text: katham asati dravyāntaratve caitasikatvam iti. vitarkādīnāṃ. avasthāviśeṣo 'pi hi nāma cetasaś caitasiko bhavati. cetasi bhavatvāt. paryeṣakamanojalpāvasthā vitarkaḥ. pratyavekṣakamanojalpāvasthā vicāraḥ. vāksamutthāpikāvasthā cittasya vitarkaḥ. tadanyāvasthā vicāra iti bhagavadviśeṣaḥ. avikṣiptāvasthā samādhiḥ. [Tib. 343b] praśāntavāhitāvasthā cittasyādhyātmasaṃprasāda iti.
body.translated_text: 'How can there be the status of being a mental factor (<s>caitasika</s>) when there is no difference in substance?' — of <s>vitarka</s> and the rest. Even a particular state (<s>avasthāviśeṣa</s>) of mind can be a mental factor — because of existing in the mind. The state of investigative mental speech is <s>vitarka</s>; the state of examining mental speech is <s>vicāra</s>. The state that gives rise to vocal expression is <s>vitarka</s> of the mind; the other state is <s>vicāra</s> — [says] <s>Bhagavadviśeṣa</s>. The undistracted state is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). The state of peaceful flow of the mind is inner clarity (<s>adhyātmasaṃprasāda</s>).

body.text: na vai sukhaṃ dhyāneṣu saumanasyaṃ yujyata iti. tulyasukhavedanāsvābhāvye mānasatve 'pi sati. kasmāt saumanasyaṃ sukham iti nocyate. asti
body.translated_text: 'Indeed, pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) in the <s>dhyāna</s>s is not fitting to be called mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>)' — even though [joy and pleasure] have the same nature as pleasant feeling and are mental — why is mental pleasure not called 'pleasure' (<s>sukha</s>)? There is

body.text: kāraṇaṃ. iyaṃ hi prītir anupaśāṃtā. tayā hi tat samāhitam api cittaṃ kṣipyata ivonnamyata iva sāmodaṃ sahāsaṃ viplutam iva vyavasthāpyate. tad yadopaśāṃtaṃ bhavati. tadā bhūmyantaraprāptā tajjātīyaiva vedanā sukham ity ucyate.
body.translated_text: a reason. For this joy (<s>prīti</s>) is unquieted — by it, that concentrated mind is, as it were, tossed about, raised up, and established as though joyfully laughing and agitated. When that becomes quieted, then at the attainment of another ground, feeling of that very same type is called 'pleasure' (<s>sukha</s>).

body.text: (VIII.10) kleśāviviktatvād iti. tadbhūmikaiḥ kleśair aviviktatvād ity arthaḥ. kleśāvilatvād iti. kleśair aprasannatvād ity arthaḥ. kliṣṭasukhasambhramitatvād iti. kliṣṭena sukhena saṃbhramitatvāt. smṛtiḥ saṃprajanyaṃ ca na bhavataḥ. kleśamalinatvād iti. tadbhūmikaiḥ kleśair malinatvāt. upekṣāyāḥ smṛteś ca pariśuddhir nāsti.
body.translated_text: (VIII.10) 'Because of not being separated from afflictions' — the meaning is: because of not being separated from the afflictions belonging to that ground. 'Because of being polluted by afflictions' — the meaning is: because of not being clarified by afflictions. 'Because of being confused with afflicted pleasure' — because of being confused by afflicted pleasure. Mindfulness and clear comprehension do not exist [there] — 'because of being defiled by afflictions' — because of being defiled by the afflictions belonging to that ground. There is no purification of equanimity or of mindfulness.

body.text: kuśalamahābhūmikatvād anayor iti. praśrabdhyupekṣe kuśalamahābhūmike paṭhite.
body.translated_text: 'Because these two are wholesome <s>mahābhūmika</s>s' — tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>) and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) are read as wholesome <s>mahābhūmika</s>s.

children.text:
śraddhāpramādaḥ praśrabdhir upekṣā hrir apatrapā
mūladvayam ahiṃsā ca vīryaṃ ca kuśalaṃ sadeti
children.translated_text:
'Faith, non-negligence, tranquility, equanimity, shame, fear of wrongdoing,
the two roots [of non-greed and non-hatred], non-harming, and energy — the wholesome is always [accompanied by these]' —

body.text: vacanāt. kiṃ punar ete pūrvasmin pakṣe kliṣṭeṣv api dhyāneṣu bhavataḥ. na ca bhavata ity āha. kasmād etan noktaṃ. anuktasiddhatvāt. kuśalamahābhūmikayoḥ praśrabdhyupekṣayor aparigrahād bhavata eva te ity apare.
body.translated_text: from this statement. 'But do these exist even in afflicted <s>dhyāna</s>s, on the former position?' They do not exist — he says. 'Why is this not stated?' Because it is established without being stated. Others say: because tranquility and equanimity, [which are] wholesome <s>mahābhūmika</s>s, are not included [in afflicted dhyānas], they certainly exist [only in wholesome dhyānas].

body.text: (VIII.11) śvāse iti.
body.translated_text: (VIII.11) 'Breathing' (<s>śvāsa</s>) —

body.text: Tib. 344a
body.translated_text: inhalation and exhalation (<s>āśvāsapraśvāsa</s>). The dual number is used here for the purpose of showing the twofold nature. 'Because of being unshakable by <s>vitarka</s>, <s>vicāra</s>, joy, and pleasure' — just as the first three <s>dhyāna</s>s are shaken by <s>vitarka</s> and the rest: the first <s>dhyāna</s> is shaken by <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>; the second by joy; the third by pleasure — the fourth is not shaken by these.

body.text: āśvāsapraśvāsau. dvitvapradarśanārthaṃ cātra dvivacananirdeśaḥ. vitarkavicāraprītisukhair akaṃpanīyatvād iti. yathā pūrvakāṇi trīṇi dhyānāni vitarkādibhiḥ. kaṃpyate prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ vitarkavicārābhyāṃ kaṃpyate. dvitīyaṃ prītyā. tṛtīyaṃ sukhena. naivam ebhiś caturthaṃ kaṃpyate.
yathā nivāte dīpo na kaṃpyate vāyunā. tadvad ity uktaṃ sūtra ity apara āhuḥ. aṣṭāpakṣālamuktatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'Just as a lamp in a windless place is not shaken by the wind — similarly' — thus it is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>, say others. 'Because of being freed from eight defective aspects.'

body.text: (VIII.13)
body.translated_text: (VIII.13)

body.text: iti. ādyadhyānasaṃgṛhītaṃ. nirmāṇacittavad iti. yathādharabhūmikaṃ nirmāṇacittaṃ tadbhūmikaṃ nirmāṇaṃ nirmātukāmā nirmātāraḥ saṃmukhīkurvanti. tadvat. na kuśalaṃ hīnatvād iti. tad dhi prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ kuśalaṃ dvitīyadhyānabhūmikān nihīnaṃ nikṛṣṭam. ato na saṃmukhīkurvanti. prayojanena hi te prathamadhyānabhūmikaṃ saṃmukhīkurvanti. na bahumānena. savipākaṃ ca tat kuśalaṃ. na ca tadvipākena te 'rthina iti kuśalacittasaṃmukhīkaraṇe yatnaṃ na kurvanti.
body.translated_text: thus. Included in the first <s>dhyāna</s>. 'Like the creation-mind (<s>nirmāṇacitta</s>)' — just as those creators who wish to create a creation of a lower ground — belonging to that ground — bring it face-to-face. Similarly. 'Not the wholesome, because of its inferiority' — for that wholesome [mind] belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground is inferior, diminished compared to the second <s>dhyāna</s> ground. Therefore they do not bring it face-to-face. For they bring face-to-face what belongs to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground out of necessity, not out of high regard. And that wholesome [mind] has a retribution — but they do not desire its retribution — therefore they do not make the effort to bring face-to-face the wholesome mind.

body.text: (VIII.14)
body.translated_text: (VIII.14)

body.text: iti. vairāgyeṇopapattito veti. vāśabdo luptanirdeśaḥ. adhobhūmivairāgyād
body.translated_text: thus. 'Through dispassion or through rebirth' — the particle 'or' (<s>vā</s>) is an elided expression. 'Through dispassion from lower grounds'

body.text: vā asamanvāgatas tena śuddhakaṃ pratilabhate dhyānaṃ ārūpyaṃ vā. kāmavairāgyāt prathamaṃ śuddhakaṃ pratilabhate triprakāram anyatra nirvedhabhāgīyāt. evaṃ yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanavairāgyād [Tib. 344b] bhavāgraṃ pratilabhate. adhobhūmyupapattito vā. upariṣṭād adharāyāṃ bhūmāv upapadyamānas tal labhate. anyatra bhavāgrād iti. tasyādhobhūmivairāgyata eva lābhaḥ. prayogato nirvedhabhāgīyam iti. tasya vairāgyopapattikṛtaḥ sa lābho na bhavati. parihāṇito 'pi hānabhāgīyam iti. sthitibhāgīyāt parihīyamāṇo hānabhāgīyaṃ labhate. ata evocyata iti. yasmāt parihīṇo pi hānabhāgīyaṃ labhate. evaṃ parihāṇyā copapattyāpi ceti yojyaṃ. kathaṃ. syāc chuddhakaṃ parihāṇyā labheta parihāṇyā vijahyāt. syāc chuddhakaṃ dhyānam upapattyā labheta upapattyā vijahyād iti. āha. syāt. katham ity āha. hānabhāgīyaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam iti. brahmalokaḥ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ tribhūmikaṃ. viśeṣeṇa brahmaloke upapadyamāna iti vacanāt. brahmalokavairāgyeṇa tyajyata iti. yasmāt prathamadhyānavairāgyeṇa hānabhāgīyaṃ dhyānaṃ kleśānuguṇyāt. tadbhūmikakleśam iva tyajati. ato brahmalokavairāgyeṇa tyajyata ity ucyate. evaṃ tāvat prathamasya praśnasya vivarjanaṃ. brahmalokavairāgyaparihāṇyā labhate. yadi brahmalokavairāgyaparihāṇyā parihīyate punas tad dhānabhāgīyaṃ pratilabhate. tadbhūmikakleśavat. [Tib. 345a] kāmadhātuvairāgyaparihāṇyā tyajyate. yadā kāmadhātuvairāgyāt parihīyate. tadā śuddhakaṃ tyajyate. upariṣṭād brahmaloka upapadyamāno labhata iti. dvitīyādibhyo brahmaloka upapadyamāno hānabhāgīyaṃ tadbhūmikakleśavad eva labhate. tasmāt kāmadhātāv upapadyamāno vijahātīti. tasmād brahmalokāt kāmadhātāv upapadyamāno vijahātīti. indriyasaṃcārato 'pi śaikṣāśaikṣam iti. śraddhāvimukto dṛṣṭiprāptāyāṃ śaikṣaṃ labhate. samayavimikto 'py akopyaprativedhe aśaikṣaṃ labhate. nāvaśyam. ānupūrvikenālābhād iti. yady ānupūrviko 'nāgamyasaṃniśrayeṇa niyāmam avakrāmati na labhate.
body.translated_text: — or one not possessing that — obtains the pure (<s>śuddhaka</s>) <s>dhyāna</s> or a formless [attainment]. Through dispassion from the Desire Realm, one first obtains the pure [dhyāna], which is of three kinds — except for the penetration-conducive (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). Similarly, up to: through dispassion from the Sphere of Nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), one obtains the Peak of Existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). Or through rebirth in a lower ground — when being reborn from an upper to a lower ground, one obtains that. Except for the Peak of Existence — for that [Peak of Existence], obtaining occurs only through dispassion from the lower ground. Through application (<s>prayoga</s>), [one obtains] the penetration-conducive (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>) — for that, the obtaining does not occur through dispassion or rebirth. Through regression too, [one obtains] the decline-conducive (<s>hānabhāgīya</s>) — when regressing from the stability-conducive (<s>sthitibhāgīya</s>), one obtains the decline-conducive. For this very reason it is stated — because even one who has regressed obtains the decline-conducive. Thus, 'through regression and through rebirth too' — this should be connected. How? 'Can a pure [dhyāna] be obtained through regression and lost through regression? Can a pure <s>dhyāna</s> be obtained through rebirth and lost through rebirth?' — he says: it can. How? — he says: 'The decline-conducive first <s>dhyāna</s>' — the <s>Brahmaloka</s> is the first <s>dhyāna</s>, comprising three grounds. Specifically, because of the statement 'being reborn in the <s>Brahmaloka</s>' — 'it is lost through dispassion from the <s>Brahmaloka</s>' — because through dispassion from the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the decline-conducive <s>dhyāna</s>, being in conformity with the afflictions, is lost like the afflictions of that ground. Therefore it is said: it is lost through dispassion from the <s>Brahmaloka</s>. Thus, for the first question, the explanation is as follows: it is obtained through regression from dispassion from the <s>Brahmaloka</s>. If one regresses from the dispassion from the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, one again obtains that decline-conducive [dhyāna] — like the afflictions of that ground. It is lost through regression from dispassion from the Desire Realm — when one regresses from dispassion from the Desire Realm, then the pure [dhyāna] is lost. It is obtained when being reborn from above in the <s>Brahmaloka</s> — when being reborn from the second and other [dhyānas] in the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, one obtains the decline-conducive, just like the afflictions of that ground. Therefore it is lost when being reborn in the Desire Realm from that — when being reborn in the Desire Realm from that <s>Brahmaloka</s>, one loses it. Through faculty-transfer too, [one obtains] the learner's and non-learner's [dhyāna] — a faith-liberated (<s>śraddhāvimukta</s>) one, [upon transferring] to the view-attained (<s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s>) [state], obtains the learner's [dhyāna]. An occasionally-liberated (<s>samayavimukta</s>) one too, at the penetration of the unshakable (<s>akopya</s>) [nature], obtains the non-learner's [dhyāna]. Not necessarily — because of non-obtaining by one of sequential [practice] (<s>ānupūrvika</s>). If one of sequential practice enters the determined course (<s>niyāma</s>) relying on the preliminary stage (<s>anāgamya</s>), one does not obtain it.

body.text: (VIII.15, 16) svabhūmike śuddhānāsrave iti. vyutthānakāle pravāhe ca. dvitīyatṛtīyadhyānabhūmike ceti. miśrakāmiśrakānulomasamāpattau vyutkrāntakasamāpattau ca. sapta svabhūmike śuddhakānāsrave iti. pūrvavad vijñānākāśānaṃtyāyatanabhūmike ca. tathaiva pratilomasamāpattau. bhavāgraṃ śuddhakam evānāsravābhāvād iti. māṃdyād anāsravaṃ nāstīty uktaṃ. anulomasamāpattau tu vyutthānakāle tad bhavati. tṛtīyacaturthaprathamadhyānabhūmike ceti. amiśrakamiśrakānulomapratilomavyutkrāntasamāpattikāleṣu. [Tib. 345b]
body.translated_text: (VIII.15, 16) 'On one's own ground, the pure (<s>śuddha</s>) and uncontaminated' — at the time of emergence and in the continuation [of the stream]. 'And on the ground of the second and third <s>dhyāna</s>s' — in the attainment of mixed (<s>miśraka</s>) and unmixed forward-order attainment and in the skip-attainment (<s>vyutkrāntaka</s>). 'Seven [arise] on one's own ground: the pure and the uncontaminated' — as before, and on the ground of the Infinity of Consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>) [sphere]. Similarly, in the reverse-order attainment. 'The Peak of Existence is pure only, because of the absence of the uncontaminated' — it is stated that the uncontaminated does not exist there because of dullness (<s>māndya</s>). But in the forward-order attainment, at the time of emergence, it does occur. 'And on the grounds of the third, fourth, and first <s>dhyāna</s>s' — at the times of unmixed, mixed, forward-order, reverse-order, and skip-attainments.

body.text: ākāśānaṃtyāyatanacaturthadhyānabhūmikāni catvārīti. teṣv eva kāleṣu. trīṇīty anāsravābhāvāt. evam anyadhyānārūpyād anaṃtaraṃ daśa dravyāṇi yojyānīti. tadyathā tṛtīyadhyānād anantaraṃ daśa. svabhūmike dve śuddhakānāsrave. caturthadhyānākāśānaṃtyāyatanabhūmikāni catvāri. tathaiva ca prathamadvitīyadhyānabhūmikāni catvārīti. caturthadhyānād anantaraṃ daśa. svabhūmike dve śuddhakānāsrave. ākāśavijñānānaṃtyāyatanabhūmikāni catvāri. dvitīyatṛtīyadhyānabhūmikāni catvārīti. ākāśānaṃtyāyatanād anantaraṃ daśa. svabhūmike dve. vijñānākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmikāni catvāri. tṛtīyacaturthadhyānabhūmikāni catvāry utpadyanta ity evaṃ daśa bhavanti. anvayajñānānantaraṃ ceti vistaraḥ. idaṃ vyutpādyate. ūrdhvādharabhūmyālaṃbanatvād dhyānānam asti prasaṃga iti kṛtvā. tasyādharāśrayālambanatvād iti. yamāt tad dharmajñānam adharāśrayakāmadhātvāśrayam adharālambanaṃ kāmaduḥkhādyālambanaṃ. tasyādharāśrayālambanatvān na dharmajñānānantaram ārūpyān samāpadyante. śeṣaṃ yathaivānāsravād iti. svabhūmike ca śuddhānāsrave utpadyete. ūrdhvād adhobhūmike ca [Tib. 346a] yāvat tṛtīyād iti. praṇidhāyeti vistaraḥ. yadi kaścid evaṃ buddhim utpādyārdharātre candrodaye candrāstamaye vā mayā praboddhavyam iti svapet. sa pūrvābhiprāyānuvartanāt saṃtatateḥ tasminn eva kāle prabudhyate. yathāsyaivaṃ praṇidhāya suptaḥ. tasyābhiprete kāle prabodho bhavati. tadvad etat. sarvathā notpadyata iti. nāpi svabhūmikaṃ nāpy adharabhūmikam utpadyata ity arthaḥ. samāpattikālaṃ praty etad uktam iti. śuddhakāt kliṣṭāc ca samanantaraṃ svabhūmikam eva kliṣṭam utpadyate nānyabhūmikam iti. kathaṃ. tathā śuddhāt kliṣṭaṃ vāpi svabhūmikaṃ. kliṣṭāt svaṃ śuddhakaṃ kliṣṭam ity evaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Four on the grounds of the Infinity of Space and the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>' — at those very times. 'Three' — because of the absence of the uncontaminated. Thus, from each <s>dhyāna</s> or formless [attainment] immediately [after], ten substances should be connected. For example, immediately after the third <s>dhyāna</s>, ten [substances arise]: on one's own ground, two — the pure and the uncontaminated. On the grounds of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and the Infinity of Space, four. And similarly, on the grounds of the first and second <s>dhyāna</s>s, four. Immediately after the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, ten: on one's own ground, two — the pure and the uncontaminated. On the grounds of the Infinity of Space and the Infinity of Consciousness, four. On the grounds of the second and third <s>dhyāna</s>s, four. Immediately after the Infinity of Space, ten: on one's own ground, two. On the grounds of the Infinity of Consciousness and the Sphere of Nothingness, four. On the grounds of the third and fourth <s>dhyāna</s>s, four arise — thus there are ten. 'And immediately after the <s>anvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge)' — in detail. This is explained: because the <s>dhyāna</s>s have upper and lower grounds as their object-domain, there is a [potential] consequence. Because that [<s>dharmajñāna</s>] has a lower basis and object-domain — because that <s>dharmajñāna</s> has a lower basis, namely a Desire-Realm basis, and a lower object-domain, namely having the suffering of the Desire Realm and the rest as its object-domain — because of its lower basis and object-domain, one does not enter into a formless [attainment] immediately after <s>dharmajñāna</s>. 'The remainder, just as from the uncontaminated' — on one's own ground, the pure and uncontaminated arise. And on upper and lower grounds — up to the third [dhyāna]. 'Having resolved' — in detail. If someone, having generated the intention, 'I shall awaken at midnight, at moonrise, or at moonset,' were to fall asleep — that one, from the continuation of the mental stream following the prior intention, awakens at that very time. Just as for this one who has fallen asleep having thus resolved — his awakening occurs at the intended time — so too is this case. 'In no way does it arise' — the meaning is: neither on one's own ground nor on a lower ground does it arise. 'This is stated with reference to the time of attainment' — immediately after the pure or the afflicted, only the afflicted of one's own ground arises, not of another ground. How? 'Thus, from the pure, the afflicted too is of one's own ground. From the afflicted, one's own pure or afflicted.'

body.text: maraṇabhave. upapattilābhikāc chuddhakād iti vistaraḥ. upapattidhyāneṣu yad upapattilābhikaṃ kuśalasamāhitaṃ. tad api śuddhakaṃ dhyānam ity ucyate. ata idam ucyate.
body.translated_text: at the death-existence (<s>maraṇabhava</s>). 'From the pure that is obtained through rebirth (<s>upapattilābhika</s>)' — in detail. In the rebirth-<s>dhyāna</s>s, whatever is obtained through rebirth, wholesome and collected — that too is called a pure <s>dhyāna</s>. Therefore this is stated:

body.text: iti vistareṇa. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. asamāhitatvān maraṇabhavasya. na hi tadānīṃ śuddhakaṃ samāpattidhyānam astīti. ataḥ sarvabhūmikaṃ kliṣṭam utpadyata iti. svabhūmikādharordhvabhūmikaṃ pratisaṃdhicittaṃ kliṣṭam asamāhitam utpadyata ity arthaḥ. nordhvabhūmikaṃ. kliṣṭasadbhāve sati tatropapattyasaṃbhavāt.
body.translated_text: — in detail. What is the reason? Because the death-existence is non-collected (<s>asamāhita</s>). For at that time, there is no pure attainment-<s>dhyāna</s>. Therefore, the afflicted of all grounds arises. The meaning is: the rebirth-linking consciousness (<s>pratisaṃdhicitta</s>) — afflicted, non-collected — arises [belonging to] one's own ground, lower, or upper ground. Not an upper-ground [afflicted mind] — because, when the afflicted exists [at that ground], rebirth there is impossible.

body.text: (VIII.17, 18) anyatra viśeṣabhāgīyād [Tib. 346b] iti. ita ūrdhvabhūmyabhāvāt. tasmād anāsravam utpadyata iti nirvedhabhāgīyāt. hānasthitibhāgīye iti. hānabhāgīyaṃ pravāhakāle. sthitibhāgīyaṃ viśeṣagamanakāle. anyatra hānabhāgīyād iti. viśeṣabhāgīyād dhīyamānasya sthitibhāgīyāparityāge tasyaivotpattiyogāt. tad evaikaṃ iti. tad eva nirvedhabhāgīyaṃ pravāhayogena.
body.translated_text: (VIII.17, 18) 'Except for the distinction-conducive (<s>viśeṣabhāgīya</s>)' — because above that, no higher ground exists. Therefore, the uncontaminated arises from the penetration-conducive (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). 'The decline-conducive and stability-conducive' — the decline-conducive [arises] at the time of the stream-continuation. The stability-conducive [arises] at the time of advancing to distinction. 'Except for the decline-conducive' — because, for one declining from the distinction-conducive, if the stability-conducive is not abandoned, only that very [stability-conducive] arises — because of the fitness for the arising of that alone. 'That very one alone' — that very penetration-conducive [arises], through the continuation of the stream.

body.text: (VIII.19) ākṛṣṭā ity anukrameṇeti. anulomānukrameṇa pratilomānukrameṇa ca.
body.translated_text: (VIII.19) 'In forward order, [the attainments] are practiced' — in forward sequential order and in reverse sequential order.

body.text: (VIII.20) vidhīyata iti kriyata ity arthaḥ. sthāpyata iti vā. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. nihīnatvāt.
body.translated_text: (VIII.20) 'Is established' means 'is done' — or 'is set up.' For what reason? Because of inferiority.

children.translated_text: 'From the proximity of the noble [uncontaminated] Sphere of Nothingness' —

body.text: iti. āryam anāsravaṃ. anāsravasyākiṃcanyāyatanasya sāṃmukhyāt saṃmukhībhāvāt. bhavāgre jātasyāsravaprahāṇaṃ bhavati. tuśabdo 'pavādārthaṃ dyotayati. svasyābhāvād iti. bhāvāgrikasyānāsravasya mārgasyābhāvād ity arthaḥ. tasya cābhyāsād iti. tasyākiṃcanyāyatanasyānāsravasyābhyāsāt saṃnikṛṣṭatvāt.
body.translated_text: thus. 'Noble' means uncontaminated. From the proximity, the coming face-to-face, of the uncontaminated Sphere of Nothingness — the abandonment of outflows occurs for one born at the Peak of Existence. The particle 'tu' indicates an exception. 'Because of the absence of its own [uncontaminated path]' — the meaning is: because of the absence of the uncontaminated path belonging to the Peak of Existence. 'And because of the practice of that' — because of the practice, the proximity, of that uncontaminated Sphere of Nothingness.

body.text: (VIII.21) tṛṣṇāparicchinnatvād bhūmīnām iti. yā yasyāṃ bhūmau. tasyām eva bhūmāv anuśayanāt. tayā sā bhūmiḥ paricchinnā bhavati. anyathā hi tasyottaratvam eva na sidhyed ekabhūmisthānāntaravat. ata evauttarādharye 'pi sthānāntarāṇāṃ trayāṇāṃ trayāṇām aṣṭānāṃ [Tib. 347a] caikabhūmitā sidhyati. tṛṣṇāvyatihārayogāt. nānāsravaṃ kuśalatvaprasaṃgād iti. tatprārthanā hi kuśalo dharmacchanda iti.
body.translated_text: (VIII.21) 'Because the grounds are delimited by craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>)' — whatever [craving] exists in whatever ground, it lies dormant (<s>anuśayana</s>) in that very ground alone. By that [craving], that ground is delimited. Otherwise, its being upper [relative to another ground] would not be established — like stations within one ground. For this very reason, the oneness-of-ground of the three and three and eight stations in upper and lower [relations] is established — because of the intermixture of craving. 'Not the uncontaminated — because of the unwanted consequence of being wholesome' — for the desire for that [uncontaminated attainment] is the wholesome <s>dharmacchanda</s> (desire for <s>dharma</s>).

children.translated_text: 'The fundamental wholesome formless [attainments], being contaminated, do not have a lower [realm] as their object-domain' —

body.text: iti. maulagrahaṇaṃ sāmantakanirāsārthaṃ. ārūpyasāmantakāni hy adharāṃ sāsravāṃ bhūmim ālaṃbate. kuśalagrahaṇam āsvādanāsaṃprayuktanirāsārthaṃ. ubhayakuśalagrahaṇārthaṃ ca. yadi hy ārūpyā ity evocyeta āsvādanāsaṃprayuktā maulā ārūpyā na sāsravādharagocarā iti saṃbhāvyeran. anāsravā evārūpyā evam iti gṛhyeran. ārūpyagrahaṇaṃ dhyānanirāsārthaṃ. dhyānāni hi maulāni api sāsravādharavastvālambanāni bhavanti. samantālocanatvād dhyānānāṃ. sāsravagrahaṇam anāsravanivṛttyārtham. anāsravā hy adharā dharmā maulānāṃ kuśalānāṃ ārūpyānām ālambanāni saṃbhavanti. adharagrahaṇam ūrdhvaviśeṣaṇārthaṃ. ūrdhvabhūmikasāsravālambanasaṃbhavāt. anāsravaṃ tv ālambanam ity udgrāhya darśyati sarvānvayajñānapakṣa iti. sarva iti navabhūmika indriyagotrādibhedābhinno 'pi gṛhyate. anvayajñānapakṣa iti pakṣagrahaṇena duḥkhādyanvayajñānakṣāntayaḥ tatsahabhuvaś
body.translated_text: thus. The mention of 'fundamental' (<s>maula</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the preliminary (<s>sāmantaka</s>). For the preliminaries of the formless [attainments] do take a lower contaminated ground as their object-domain. The mention of 'wholesome' is for the purpose of excluding those associated with relishing (<s>āsvādanasaṃprayukta</s>). And for the purpose of including both [kinds of] wholesome. For if it were said only 'the formless,' it might be supposed that the relishing-associated and the fundamental formless [attainments] do not have a lower contaminated [realm] as their object-domain — and the uncontaminated formless alone would be so understood. The mention of 'formless' (<s>ārūpya</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the <s>dhyāna</s>s. For the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>s too, being contaminated, do have lower material entities as their object-domain — because the <s>dhyāna</s>s are all-surveying (<s>samantālocana</s>). The mention of 'contaminated' (<s>sāsrava</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the uncontaminated. For uncontaminated lower <s>dharma</s>s can be the object-domains of the fundamental wholesome formless [attainments]. The mention of 'lower' (<s>adhara</s>) is a qualifier for 'upper' — because of the possibility of having an upper-ground contaminated [dharma] as object-domain. 'But the uncontaminated object-domain' — having taken this up, he shows: 'the entire <s>anvayajñāna</s> class.' 'Entire' includes even that belonging to nine grounds and differentiated by faculty, lineage, and the rest. 'The <s>anvayajñāna</s> class' — by the word 'class' (<s>pakṣa</s>), the patient acceptances (<s>kṣānti</s>) of the <s>anvayajñāna</s>s of suffering and the rest, and those co-arising with them

body.text: ca gṛhyante. [Tib. 347b] na dharmajñānapakṣaḥ. kāmaduḥkhādyālambanatvena viprakṛṣṭatvāt. nādhobhūminirodhaḥ. adhobhūmigrahaṇaprasaṃgād iti. vyākhyātam etat purastāt.
body.translated_text: are included. Not the <s>dharmajñāna</s> class — because of being remote, having the suffering and the rest of the Desire Realm as its object-domain. Not the cessation of a lower ground — because of the consequence of including a lower ground. This has been explained previously.

body.text: (VIII.22)
body.translated_text: (VIII.22)

body.text: iti. dhyānārūpyāṇāṃ yo 'nāsravaḥ saṃbhavati. tena yathāsaṃbhavaṃ kleśāḥ prahīyante. katamenānāsraveṇa maulena. vakṣyate hi
body.translated_text: thus. Whatever uncontaminated [path] is possible for the <s>dhyāna</s>s and formless [attainments] — by that, afflictions are destroyed as applicable. By which fundamental uncontaminated [path]? For he will state:

body.text: apavādarūpeṇa sāmantakena śuddhakena kleśāḥ prahīyanta ity adhikṛtaṃ. kuta eva kliṣṭeneti. kliṣṭena kleśaprahāṇaṃ naiva saṃbhavatīty abhiprāyaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ śuddhakena kleśā na prahīyanta ity āha. vītarāgatvān nādha iti vistaraḥ. adharabhūmivītarāgatvān na śuddhakenādharabhūmikāḥ prahīyante. kuta eva kliṣṭena. tasyaiva tadapratipakṣatvān na svabhūmau. tasyaiva prathamadhyānasya yāvan naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasya. tadapratipakṣatvāt tasyāpratipakṣas tadapratipakṣaḥ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. tadapratipakṣatvān na svabhūmau kleśāḥ prahīyante. na hi bhavena bhavasya niḥsaraṇam asti. viśiṣṭataratvān nordhvam iti. nordhvabhūmikāḥ [Tib. 348a] kleśāḥ adharabhūmikena śuddhakena prahīyante. viśiṣṭataratvāt kleśānāṃ. na ca nyūnam āśritya viśiṣṭānāṃ prahāṇaṃ yujyate. ity anena śuddhakenāpi kleśā na prahīyante. kuta eva kliṣṭeneti siddham etat. śuddhakenāpīty apiśabdād anāsraveṇāpīti. saṃbhavatas tv etad uktaṃ. ata evocyate. adhobhūmipratipakṣatvāt iti. kāmāvacarā hi kleśāḥ prathamadhyānasāmantakena prahīyante. prathamadhyānabhūmikā dvitīyadhyānasāmantakena. evaṃ yāvad ākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmikā naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasāmantakeneti.
body.translated_text: It has been stated that afflictions are abandoned by the access concentration (<s>sāmantaka</s>), the pure (<s>śuddhaka</s>), in the form of an antidote. How then by the afflicted [concentration]? The intent is: the abandonment of afflictions by the afflicted is simply not possible. Why are afflictions not abandoned by the pure? He says: "Because of dispassion from the lower ground, not by the lower" — in detail. Because of dispassion from the lower ground, lower-ground [afflictions] are not abandoned by the pure. How then by the afflicted. "Because of being their non-antidote, not on one's own ground" — of that very first <s>dhyāna</s>, up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Because of being their non-antidote — the non-antidote of that — that is being their non-antidote; the state of being such; therefore — because of being their non-antidote, afflictions are not abandoned on one's own ground. For there is no escape from existence through existence. "Because of being more distinguished, not the higher" — higher-ground [Tib. 348a] afflictions are not abandoned by the lower-ground pure [concentration]. Because of the afflictions being more distinguished. And the abandonment of the more distinguished based on the lesser is not fitting. Thus, by this [argument], afflictions are not abandoned even by the pure. How then by the afflicted — this is established. "Even by the pure" — by the word "even" (<s>api</s>), [the meaning is:] even by the uncontaminated. But this is stated with respect to what is possible. Therefore it is said: "Because of being the antidote of the lower ground" — for afflictions of the Desire Realm are abandoned by the access concentration of the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Those of the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground are [abandoned] by the access concentration of the second <s>dhyāna</s>. Thus, up to: those of the Nothingness sphere ground [are abandoned] by the access concentration of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

body.text: (VIII.22) yena tatpraveśa iti. yena sāmantakena teṣāṃ maulānāṃ dhyānārūpyāṇāṃ praveśaḥ. kiṃ tāny api trividhānīti. āsvādanāsaṃprayuktādibhedāt. tathaiva ca teṣu vedaneti. prathamayor dhyānayoḥ prītiḥ. tṛtīye sukhaṃ. caturtha upekṣety uktaṃ. kim evaṃ sāmantakeṣu. upekṣendriyasaṃprayuktāni ca yatnavāhyatvād iti. anābhisaṃskāravāhī mārgaḥ prītisukhābhyāṃ saṃprayujyate. tāni ca sāmantakāni yatnavāhyāni sābhisaṃskāravāhyānīty ata upekṣendriyasaṃprayuktāni. [Tib. 348b] punar adhobhūmyudvegānapagamāt prītisukhayor ayoga iti. ato 'py upekṣendriyasaṃprayuktāni. vairāgyapathatvāc ca. nāsvādanāsaṃprayuktānīti. yadi hy āsvādanāsaṃprayuktāni syur vairāgyamārgo na syāt. na hi tṛṣṇāsaṃprayukto mārgaḥ kleśaprahāṇāya
body.translated_text: (VIII.22) "By which there is entry into those" — by which access concentration there is entry into those fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>s and formless [attainments]. "Are those also threefold?" — because of the distinction of relishing-associated (<s>āsvādanāsaṃprayukta</s>) and the rest. "And in those, feeling is just so" — in the first two <s>dhyāna</s>s there is joy (<s>prīti</s>); in the third, happiness (<s>sukha</s>); in the fourth, equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) — it has been stated. Is it also so in the access [concentrations]? "And they are associated with the equanimity faculty, because of being effort-driven" — the path that flows without effort is associated with joy and happiness. But those access concentrations are effort-driven, requiring deliberate effort — therefore they are associated with the equanimity faculty. [Tib. 348b] Furthermore, because of the non-removal of disturbance from the lower ground, joy and happiness are not fitting. Therefore too they are associated with the equanimity faculty. And because of being the path of dispassion. "They are not associated with relishing" — for if they were associated with relishing, there would be no path of dispassion. For a path associated with craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) does not serve the abandonment of afflictions

body.text: bhavati. atha vāyam abhisaṃbandhaḥ. upekṣeṃdriyasaṃprayuktāni ca yatnavāhyatvāt. adhobhūmyudvegānapagamād vairāgyapathatvāc ceti dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ nāsvādanāsaṃprayuktānīti. pūrvavad vaktavyaṃ śeṣaṃ. yady api sāmantakacittena saṃdhibandha iti. aṣṭāsv api dhyānārūpyeṣu yasya yat sāmantake. tasya tena sāmantakacittena kliṣṭenāsamāhitena saṃdhibandha ity eṣa siddhāntaḥ iti. ata idam ucyate. yady api sāmantakacitteneti vistaraḥ. āsvādanāsaṃprayuktam apy anāgamyam iti. anāgamyasya paṭutvāt. yathā hi tad anāsravam api saṃbhavati. tathāsvādanāsaṃprayuktam apīty abhiprāyaḥ. maulapratispardhitvād āsvādanāsamutpattisadbhāvād iti ācāryasaṃghabhadraḥ.
body.translated_text: . Alternatively, this is the connection: they are associated with the equanimity faculty, and because of being effort-driven, because of the non-removal of disturbance from the lower ground, and because of being the path of dispassion — for these two reasons they are not associated with relishing. The rest should be stated as before. "Even though the linking is by access-concentration mind" — in all eight <s>dhyāna</s>s and formless [attainments], for whichever one, the linking (<s>saṃdhibandha</s>) is by that access-concentration mind which is afflicted and non-collected — this is the established doctrine. Therefore this is stated: "Even though by access-concentration mind" — in detail. "The <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary) too can be associated with relishing" — because of the acuity of the <s>anāgamya</s>. For just as it can also be uncontaminated — so too it can be associated with relishing — this is the intent. Because of rivaling the fundamental [<s>dhyāna</s>], because of the actual existence of the arising of relishing — [says] <s>Ācārya Saṃghabhadra</s>.

body.text: (VIII.23) dhyānaviśeṣatvād iti. tad eva maulaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ vitarkāpaganmād viśiṣṭaṃ [sa] dhyānāntaram ity ucyate [Tib. 349a] ity arthaḥ. viśeṣābhāvād iti. yathā prathame dhyāne viśeṣo bhavati. kvacid vitarkavicārau. kvacid vicāra eveti. na tathā dvitīyādiṣv iti. ato dhyāneṣu na vyavasthāpyate dhyānāntaram. ata eva duḥkhā pratipad iti. ata eva hi saṃskāravāhitvāt. vitarkamātrapratiṣedhād iti.
body.translated_text: (VIII.23) "Because of being a special <s>dhyāna</s>" — that very fundamental first <s>dhyāna</s>, being distinguished by the removal of <s>vitarka</s> (initial thought), is called the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> (<s>dhyānāntara</s>) — [Tib. 349a] this is the meaning. "Because of the absence of distinction" — just as in the first <s>dhyāna</s> there is a distinction — sometimes with <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, sometimes with <s>vicāra</s> alone — there is no such [distinction] in the second and the rest. Therefore the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> is not established among the [other] <s>dhyāna</s>s. For this very reason it is a painful practice — for this very reason, because of being effort-driven, because of the mere negation of <s>vitarka</s>.

body.text: iti vacanāt.
body.translated_text: thus it is stated.

body.text: (VIII.24, 25) tadālambanaḥ samādhir ānimitta iti. animitte bhava ānimittaḥ. daśākāra iti. anityaduḥkhākārau dvau. samudayākāraś catvāro mārgākāraś catvāra ity ete daśākārāḥ. anityaduḥkhataddhetubhya udvegād iti. anityād duḥkhāt taddhetoś ca. tasya duḥkhasya hetoś ca samudayād udvegāt. kiṃ. apraṇihitaḥ. akṛtasaṃskāra ity arthaḥ. mārgasya kolopamatayāvaśyatyājyatvāt. kola ucyate uḍupaḥ. sa upamāsyeti kolopamaḥ. mārgaḥ. tadbhāvaḥ. tayā. kolopamatayā mārgasyāvaśyatyājyatvaṃ. tasmād apraṇihita ity adhikṛtaḥ. yathā hi kolam āśritya nadīm uttaran na kolaniṣṭho bhavati. tasyāvaśyatyājyatvāt. evaṃ mārgam āśritya na mārganiṣṭho bhavati. tasyāvaśyatyājyatvāt. tadākāra iti. taddaśākāro [Tib. 349b] yathoktaḥ. tadatikramābhimukhatvād iti. tasya mārgasyātikrame 'bhimukhatvāt. anenāvaśyatyājyatvam asya darśayati. anityaduḥkhataddhetvatikramābhimukha ity anuktam apy etad gamyata eva. śūnyatā-anātmatābhyāṃ tu nodvega iti. śūnyānātmākārābhyāṃ tu nodvego yogino bhavati. yady api hi duḥkhasatyaṃ śūnyānātmākārābhyām ākāryate. na tu tābhyāṃ tasmād duḥkhād udvegaḥ. kasmāt. nirvāṇasāmānyāt. nirvāṇam api śūnyānātmalakṣaṇaṃ. śūnyatā-anātmate hi sarvadharmāṇāṃ lakṣaṇam
body.translated_text: (VIII.24, 25) "The <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) having that as its object-domain is signless (<s>ānimitta</s>)" — existing in the signless, it is signless. "Of ten aspects" — impermanent and suffering — these are two; the four aspects of origination; and the four aspects of the path — these are ten aspects. "Because of disturbance from impermanence, suffering, and their cause" — from impermanence, from suffering, and from its cause — the cause of suffering, that is, origination — because of disturbance from [these]. What [follows]? It is wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>). The meaning is: one without deliberate intention. "Because of the path being like a raft that must necessarily be abandoned" — a <s>kola</s> is called a raft (<s>uḍupa</s>). That which has it as a simile is "raft-like" (<s>kolopama</s>) — the path. The state of being such — because of the path's necessarily being abandoned, like a raft. Therefore [the samādhi] is said to be wishless. For just as, having relied on a raft to cross a river, one does not remain fixed on the raft — because it must necessarily be abandoned — so too, having relied on the path, one does not remain fixed on the path — because it must necessarily be abandoned. "Of that aspect" — of those ten aspects [Tib. 349b] as stated. "Because of facing the transcendence of that" — because of facing the transcendence of that path. By this he shows its necessarily being abandoned. "Because of facing the transcendence of impermanence, suffering, and their cause" — though not stated, this is understood. "But there is no disturbance from emptiness and non-self" — by the aspects of empty (<s>śūnya</s>) and non-self (<s>anātma</s>), there is no disturbance for the yogin. For even though the truth of suffering is apprehended through the aspects of empty and non-self, there is no disturbance from that suffering through those [aspects]. Why? Because of their commonality with <s>nirvāṇa</s>. <s>Nirvāṇa</s> too has the characteristics of emptiness and non-self. For emptiness and non-selfness are the characteristics of all <s>dharma</s>s

body.text: iti. na ca tābhyāṃ tasmān nirvāṇād udvegaḥ. tasmān na tadākāro 'praṇihitasamādhir iti. laukikā ekādaśasv iti. kāmadhātāv anāgamye dhyānāntare dhyānārūpyeṣu ceti. yatra mārga iti. kāmadhātubhavāgradvitīyādisāmantakavarjitāsu bhūmiṣu. mokṣadvāratvād iti. dvārārtho mukhārtha iti darśayati.
body.translated_text: — thus. And there is no disturbance from that <s>nirvāṇa</s> through those [aspects]. Therefore the <s>samādhi</s> of those aspects is not wishless. "Mundane in eleven" — in the Desire Realm, <s>anāgamya</s>, the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, and the <s>dhyāna</s>s and formless [attainments]. "Where the path [exists]" — in the grounds excluding the Desire Realm, the Peak of Existence, and the access concentrations of the second and the rest. "Because of being the gates to liberation" — he shows that the meaning of "gate" is "entrance" (<s>mukha</s>).

body.text: (VIII.25, 26) śūnyatādyālambanatvāt tan nāmeti. śūnyatāpraṇihitānimittālambanatvāt. śūnyatāśūnyateti nāma. apraṇihitāpraṇihiteti. ānimittānimitta iti ca.
body.translated_text: (VIII.25, 26) "They are so named because of having emptiness and the rest as their object-domain" — because of having emptiness, wishlessness, and signlessness as their object-domain. Thus: <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness), <s>apraṇihitāpraṇihita</s> (wishlessness of wishlessness), and <s>ānimittānimitta</s> (signlessness of signlessness).

children.text: iti. yathāsaṃkhyena. śūnyatāśūnyatā [Tib. 350a] hi śūnyatākāreṇāśaikṣaṃ śūnyatāsamādhim ālambate nāyam ātmīyam iti. nānātmākāreṇa.
children.translated_text: in due order. <s>Śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> [Tib. 350a] (emptiness of emptiness) takes the non-learner's (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) emptiness <s>samādhi</s> as its object-domain through the aspect of emptiness — "this is not mine" — not through the aspect of non-self.

body.text: āha. kim atra kāraṇaṃ yac chūnyatāśūnyatāsamādhiḥ śūnyatākāra eva. na punar anātmākāro 'pi śūnyatāvad iti. atrocyate. śūnyatākārapravṛttaśūnyatāpṛṣṭhotpādyatvāt. āha. kim arthaṃ punaḥ śūnyatākārapravṛttaśūnyatāpṛṣṭhenotpattir na punar anātmākārapravṛttaśūnyatāpṛṣṭheneti. atrocyate. tadutpattyānukūlyāt. sa eva hi śūnyatākārapravṛttaśūnyatāsamādhis tasya śūnyatāśūnyatāsamādher utpattāv ānukūlyenāvatiṣṭhate. nānātmākāraḥ. na hy evam anātmadarśanam udvejayati yathā śūnyadarśanaṃ. dṛṣṭeṣv api hy anātmato bhaveṣv abhiratir asti saṃsāre śūnyadarśanābhāvāt. tadyathādhvagasyāsaṃbaṃdhād adhvagadarśanād api prītiḥ. ekākinas tu tacchūnyatvād aprītir iti. tadvat.
body.translated_text: He asks: what is the reason that the <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> <s>samādhi</s> has only the aspect of emptiness and not also the aspect of non-self, like [the primary] emptiness [<s>samādhi</s>]? Here it is said: because of being produced immediately after the emptiness [<s>samādhi</s>] that has functioned through the aspect of emptiness. He asks: what, then, is the reason for being produced immediately after the emptiness [<s>samādhi</s>] that functioned through the aspect of emptiness, and not immediately after [one] that functioned through the aspect of non-self? Here it is said: because of its suitability for the arising of that. For that very emptiness <s>samādhi</s> that functioned through the aspect of emptiness is favorably disposed toward the arising of that <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> <s>samādhi</s> — not the non-self aspect. For the seeing of non-self does not produce disturbance in the way that the seeing of emptiness does. For even in existences seen as non-self, there is delight in <s>saṃsāra</s> — because of the absence of the seeing of emptiness. For example, a traveler feels joy even at the sight of an unrelated fellow-traveler. But when alone, because of that being empty [of companions], there is no joy — so too.

body.text: anityākāreṇeti. daśānām ākārāṇāṃ. na duḥkhata iti vistaraḥ. na duḥkhata ākārayaṃty anāsravasyātallakṣaṇatvāt. āryapratikūlatayā hi duḥkham iṣyate. na hetusamudayaprabhavapratyayākārair anāsravasyātallakṣaṇatvād evānāsravasyāsamudayādilakṣaṇatvād ity arthaḥ. na mārgākārair [Tib. 350b] dūṣaṇīyatvād iti. so 'śaikṣaḥ samādhir dūṣayitavyo na ca mārgākārā dūṣaṇarūpā iti. ato na mārgākārais taṃ samādhim ālambate. nirodhākārais tu naiva sambandha iti. na taiś cintyate. pāriśeṣyād anityākāreṇaiva.
body.translated_text: "Through the aspect of impermanence" — of the ten aspects. "Not through the aspect of suffering" — in detail. It does not apprehend [the <s>samādhi</s>] through the aspect of suffering — because the uncontaminated does not have that characteristic. For suffering is accepted as that which is adverse to the Noble Ones. "Not through the aspects of cause, origination, arising, and condition" — because the uncontaminated does not have that characteristic — the meaning is: because the uncontaminated does not have the characteristic of origination and the rest. "Not through the aspects of the path" — [Tib. 350b] because of being something to be corrupted (<s>dūṣaṇīya</s>). That non-learner's <s>samādhi</s> is to be corrupted — but the aspects of the path are not of a corrupting nature. Therefore one does not take that <s>samādhi</s> as object-domain through the path-aspects. "But through the aspects of cessation, there is simply no connection" — it is not apprehended through those. By elimination, through the aspect of impermanence alone.

body.text: ity apratisaṃkhyānirodham ity arthaḥ. aśaikṣasyānimittasya samādher apratisaṃkhyānirodham ālambate. śāntataḥ śānto 'yam iti. kathaṃ tasyāpratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. aśaikṣād ānimittāt samādher vyutthitasya tadanantaraṃ ye sāsravāḥ kṣaṇā atikrāmanti anye cānāsravāḥ. yadi te notpannāḥ. syuḥ. aśaikṣā
body.translated_text: the meaning is: <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (cessation not through deliberation). [The <s>ānimittānimitta</s> samādhi] takes the <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> of the non-learner's signless <s>samādhi</s> as its object-domain. "Through [the aspect of] peacefulness" — "this is peaceful." How is there <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> of that? When one has emerged from the non-learner's signless <s>samādhi</s>, immediately after that, whatever contaminated moments pass by, and also other uncontaminated [moments] — if those had not arisen — [the following] would have arisen: non-learner's

body.text: ānimittakṣaṇā utpannāḥ syuḥ. teṣāṃ sāsravāṇām anyānāsravāṇāṃ cotpattikāle teṣām aśaikṣāṇāṃ ānimittakṣaṇānām apratisaṃkhyānirodho labhyate. pratyayavaikalyāt. tam apratisaṃkhyānirodham ālambate śāntākāreṇa. anāsravasya pratisaṃkhyānirodhābhāvāt. na pratisaṃkhyānirodham ālambate. kasmāt punar anāsravasya pratisaṃkhyānirodho nāsti. apratikūlatvāt. yad dhi pratikūlam āryāṇāṃ. tat saṃyogasya visaṃyogāya yatas te yatante. visaṃyogaś ca pratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ. ato 'nāsravasya na pratisaṃkhyanirodhaḥ. kiṃ cāśaikṣasyānimittasya samādheḥ pratisaṃkhyānirodhābhāvāt. [Tib. 351a] apratisaṃkhyānirodhasya ca tatpratyarthikabhūtatvāt. tatprotsāhanenaiva tadvidūṣaṇam abhilaṣaṃs tadapratisaṃkhyānirodham evālambate. śatrūpagraheṇa hi loke māryopaghātaḥ kriyamāṇo dṛśyata iti. na nirodhapraṇītaniḥsaraṇākārair iti. nirodhaḥ sādhāraṇāḥ. na nirodha iti. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. anityatānirodhasadhāraṇatvād ayam apratisaṃkhyānirodho na nirodhākāreṇākāryate. anyathā hi śāntākāreṇa tadviśiṣṭena nālambitaḥ syāt. nirodhākāreṇa hy anityatānirodhenaiva dūṣita evāsāv apratisaṃkhyānirodhaḥ syāt. taddūṣaṇena nāśaikṣa ānimittasamādhidūṣitaḥ syād ity abhiprāyaḥ. na praṇītākāreṇa. avyākṛtatvād apratisaṃkhyānirodhasya. kuśalaṃ hi praṇītaṃ nāvyākṛtam. ato na praṇītākāreṇālambate. avisaṃyogāc cāpratisaṃkhyānirodhasya. na niḥsaraṇākāreṇa tam ālambate. saṃkleśaviyogo hi saṃkleśaniḥsaraṇam iṣyate. yasmān nāpratisaṃkhyānirodhena saṃsāraniḥsaraṇaṃ bhavati. tathā hi saty apy apratisaṃkhyānirodhe keṣāṃcit kuśalākuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ taiḥ saṃprayukta eva tatprāptyavicchedāt. āryamārgadveṣitvād [Tib. 351b] iti. kathaṃ dviṣati. śūnyatādibhir ākārais tadvaimukhyāt.
body.translated_text: signless moments would have arisen. At the time of the arising of those contaminated and other uncontaminated [moments], the <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> of those non-learner's signless moments is obtained — because of the deficiency of conditions. It takes that <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> as its object-domain through the aspect of peacefulness. Because of the absence of <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (cessation through deliberation) for the uncontaminated — it does not take <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> as its object-domain. Why, then, is there no <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> for the uncontaminated? Because of its not being adverse. For that which is adverse to the Noble Ones — from the bondage (<s>saṃyoga</s>) with that, they strive for disconnection (<s>visaṃyoga</s>). And disconnection is <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>. Therefore the uncontaminated has no <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>. Moreover, because of the absence of <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> for the non-learner's signless <s>samādhi</s>, [Tib. 351a] and because the <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is an adversary to it — by the encouragement of that [enemy], desiring the corruption of that [<s>samādhi</s>], one takes that <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> alone as its object-domain. For in the world, it is seen that the injury of an enemy is accomplished through the support of the enemy's [own] enemy. "Not through the aspects of cessation, excellence, escape" — cessation is shared [with <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>]. The non-cessation-like-character — the state of being such. Therefore — because the <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> shares impermanence and cessation [with other things], this <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is not apprehended through the aspect of cessation. For otherwise it would not be taken as object-domain through the aspect of peacefulness, which is more distinguished. For through the aspect of cessation — the cessation that is shared with impermanence — that very <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> would already be corrupted. By its corruption, the non-learner's signless <s>samādhi</s> would not be corrupted — this is the intent. "Not through the aspect of excellence" — because of the indeterminate nature of <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>. For the wholesome is excellent, not the indeterminate. Therefore one does not take it as object-domain through the aspect of excellence. And because <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is not disconnection — one does not take it as object-domain through the aspect of escape. For the departure from afflictive bondage (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) is accepted as escape from affliction. Since there is no escape from <s>saṃsāra</s> through <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>. For even when <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> exists for certain wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s, one is still conjoined with them — because of the non-interruption of their acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>). "Because of being hostile to the Noble Path" — [Tib. 351b] how is it hostile? Through the aspects of emptiness and the rest, because of turning away from that [path].

body.text: akopyadharmaṇaḥ. tasya tīkṣṇendriyatvāt tadutpādane sāmarthyam asti. nānyasyārhataḥ. tebhyo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāratvād āsaṃgāspadabhūtebhyo 'śaikṣebhyaḥ śūnyatādisamādhibhyo vaimukhyārtham aparasamādhīn samāpadyante.
body.translated_text: of one with unshakable nature (<s>akopyadharman</s>). Because of that one's sharp faculties, there is the capacity to produce that. Not for another <s>Arhat</s>. From those [attainments] — from the uncontaminated [attainments] that are abodes of pleasant dwelling in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra</s>) and are beyond attachment — they enter into other <s>samādhi</s>s for the purpose of turning away from them.

body.text: (VIII.27, 28) vistara iti. asti samādhibhāvanā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārāya vartate. asti samādhibhāvanā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā divyacakṣurabhijñājñānadarśanāya saṃvartate. asti samādhibhāvanāsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā prajñāprabhedāya saṃvartate. asti samādhibhāvanā
body.translated_text: (VIII.27, 28) 'In detail' — thus. 'There is a cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> that, when practiced, developed, and made much of, conduces to pleasant dwelling in the present life. There is a cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> that, when practiced, developed, and made much of, conduces to the <s>abhijñā</s>-knowledge-and-vision of the divine eye. There is a cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> that, when practiced, developed, and made much of, conduces to the differentiation of wisdom. There is a cultivation of <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā āsravakṣayāya saṃvartata iti sūtraṃ. tatrāsevitā niṣevaṇabhāvanayā. bhāvitā vipakṣaprahāṇatayā. bahulīkṛtā vipakṣadūrīkaraṇatayā.
body.translated_text: that, when practiced, developed, and made much of, conduces to the destruction of the <s>āsrava</s>s (outflows)' — this is the <s>sūtra</s>. Therein, 'practiced' (<s>āsevitā</s>) means: through the cultivation of familiarization (<s>niṣevaṇabhāvanā</s>). 'Developed' (<s>bhāvitā</s>) means: through the abandonment of the adversary. 'Made much of' (<s>bahulīkṛtā</s>) means: through the distancing of the adversary.

body.text: āha. divyacakṣurabhijñājñānadarśanāya saṃvartata ity uktaṃ. na ca divyacakṣurabhijñāsamādhibhāvanā. atrocyate. ayaṃ phale hetūpacāraḥ. yasya hetoḥ samādhibhāvanāyā divyacakṣurabhijñāphalaṃ. tatra phale hetūpacāraḥ. jñānadarśanāya samādhibhavaneti. yeṣāṃ punar ayaṃ pakṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: He says: 'it conduces to the <s>abhijñā</s>-knowledge-and-vision of the divine eye' — this has been stated. But the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> is not itself the <s>abhijñā</s> of the divine eye. To this it is said: this is a figurative designation of the cause in terms of the effect (<s>phale hetūpacāra</s>). The effect of the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> that is the cause is the <s>abhijñā</s> of the divine eye. There, the figurative designation of the cause in terms of the effect [applies]: 'the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> for knowledge-and-vision.' But for those whose position is this —

body.text: iti dhyānasaṃgṛhītā eva mānasā vimuktimārgāḥ ṣaḍ abhijñā iti. teṣām acodyam evaitat. teṣāṃ vimuktimārgāṇāṃ samāhitatvāt. pūrvaka eva tu pakṣo abhidharmakośacintakānām ity avagantavyaṃ. divyacakṣuḥśrotravijñānayor abhijñatvenābhīṣṭatvāt. tadādikatvāt. anyonyo 'pīti. udāharaṇatvarūpoktatvāt. nāvaśyaṃ saṃparāyasukhavihārāyeti. saṃparāyo 'nāgataṃ janma. tatra sukhavihāraḥ. tasmai nāvaśyam etat bhavati. kasmād ity āha. parihīṇānāṃ prathamadhyānāt. ūrdhvopapannānāṃ dvitīyādiṣu. parinirvṛtānāṃ ca. saṃparāyasukhavihārasyābhāvāt.
body.translated_text: thus — the six <s>abhijñā</s>s are mental liberation-paths included in the <s>dhyāna</s>s — for them, this is not subject to objection at all. Because those liberation-paths are [states of] concentration (<s>samāhita</s>). But the former position should be understood as that of the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s> commentators. Because the divine eye and ear consciousnesses are accepted as <s>abhijñā</s>s. Because of being of that nature and the like. 'And each other too' — because of being stated in the manner of illustration. 'Not necessarily for pleasant dwelling in future lives (<s>saṃparāyasukhavihāra</s>)' — thus. <s>Saṃparāya</s> is future birth. Pleasant dwelling therein. For that [purpose], this does not necessarily apply. Why? — he says: for those who have regressed from the first <s>dhyāna</s>; for those reborn above in the second and higher [<s>dhyāna</s>s]; and for those who have attained final <s>nirvāṇa</s> — because of the absence of pleasant dwelling in future lives.

body.text: jñānāya darśanāya ceti samāsaḥ. tatra [Tib. 352a] jñānaṃ manovijñānasaṃprayuktā prajñā. amī bhavantaḥ sattvāḥ kāyaduścaritena samanvāgatā ity evamādivikalpād darśanaṃ cakṣurvijñānasaṃprayuktā prajñā avikalpikā. traidhātukā anāsravā iti. traidhātukā aśubhānāpānasmṛtyaraṇāpraṇidhijñānapratisaṃvidabhijñāvimokṣābhibhvāyatanādayaḥ. anāsravāḥ vimokṣasukhavyutkrāntakasamāpattyāsravakṣayābhijñādayaḥ. atra tu samādhisaṃprayogāt prāyogikānāṃ [Tib. 352b] guṇānāṃ samādhibhāvanety upacāraḥ. prajñāprabhedāyeti. prajñāviśeṣakarṣāya. ātmopanāyikā kilaiṣā bhagavato dharmopadeśaneti. ātmana upanāyikā ātmano deśikety arthaḥ bodhisattvo hi karmāntapratyavekṣaṇāya niḥkrānto jambumūle prathamaṃ dhyānam utpāditavān. bodhimūle ca devaputramāraṃ bhaṃktvā prathame yāme divyaṃ cakṣur utpāditavān. tena divyena cakṣuṣā sattvāṃś cyutyupapattisaṃkaṭasthān abhivīkṣya tatparitrāṇāya madhyame yāme dhyānavimokṣasamāpattiḥ saṃmukhīkṛtavān. te 'sya prāyogikā guṇāḥ prajñāprabhedāya jāyante. tatas tṛtīye yāme caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ niśritya niyāmam avakramya yāvad vajropamena samādhinā sarvasaṃyojanaprahāṇaṃ kṛtavān iti. yasmāc caivam ātmopanāyikā dharmadeśanā. ataś
body.translated_text: the compound means: for knowledge and for vision. Therein, [Tib. 352a] knowledge is the wisdom associated with <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness). 'These beings are endowed with bodily misconduct' — from such differentiations, vision is the non-conceptual wisdom associated with <s>cakṣurvijñāna</s> (eye-consciousness). 'Belonging to the three realms and uncontaminated' — thus. Belonging to the three realms: the meditation on the impure (<s>aśubhā</s>), <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing), <s>araṇā</s>, <s>praṇidhijñāna</s>, <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledges), <s>abhijñā</s>s (direct knowledges), <s>vimokṣa</s>s (liberations), <s>abhibhvāyatana</s>s (bases of mastery), and the like. Uncontaminated: the <s>vimokṣa</s>s, the pleasant-dwelling-transcendence-<s>samāpatti</s> (<s>sukhavyutkrāntakasamāpatti</s>), the <s>abhijñā</s> of the destruction of the outflows, and the like. Here, however, because of their association with <s>samādhi</s>, the figurative designation of the preparatory qualities as 'cultivation of <s>samādhi</s>' [is used]. 'For the differentiation of wisdom' — for the distinction and perfection of wisdom. 'This <s>dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s> is indeed personally conducive' (<s>ātmopanāyikā</s>) — personally conducive means: guiding for oneself — this is the meaning. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having gone forth for the examination of his actions, produced the first <s>dhyāna</s> at the foot of the <s>Jambu</s> tree. And at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, having defeated <s>Māra</s> the <s>Devaputra</s>, he produced the divine eye in the first watch of the night. With that divine eye, having observed beings caught in the calamity of dying and being reborn, for the purpose of rescuing them, in the middle watch he brought face-to-face the <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>vimokṣa</s>-<s>samāpatti</s>s. Those preparatory qualities of his conduce to the differentiation of wisdom. Then in the third watch, relying on the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, entering the path of certainty (<s>niyāma</s>), he accomplished the abandonment of all fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) by the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s> (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>) — thus. Since this <s>dharma</s>-teaching is indeed personally conducive, therefore

body.text: caturtha eva.
body.translated_text: the fourth alone.

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: thus.

body.text: (VIII.29-31) apramāṇasattvālambanād iti. apramāṇasaṃjñākaraṇe kāraṇam etat.
body.translated_text: (VIII.29-31) 'Because of having immeasurable (<s>apramāṇa</s>) beings as the object' — this is the reason for calling them <s>apramāṇa</s> (immeasurables).

body.text: yathāsaṃkhyam iti. vyāpādabahulānāṃ tatprahāṇāya maitrī. vihiṃsābahulānāṃ tatprahāṇāya karuṇā. aratibahulānāṃ tatprahāṇāya muditā. kāmarāgavyāpādabahulānāṃ tatprahāṇāyopekṣeti. kāmarāgapratipakṣatve ko viśeṣa iti. kāmarāgabahulāt [Tib. 353a] praticintā. matāpitṛputrajñātirāgasyopekṣeti. yathaivasaṃbaddhāḥ puruṣāḥ. evam evaite ity upekṣety abhiprāyaḥ. tasya lobhākṛṣṭatvād iti. yasmāl lobhākṛṣṭo vyāpādaḥ. tasmāl lobhapratipakṣarūpatāṃ bhajata ity abhiprāyaḥ. ubhayasvabhāvāt tv asau yujyata iti. alobhasvabhāvā cādveṣasvabhāvā ca yujyata ity arthaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇam. rāgadveṣayoḥ pratipakṣatvāt. atas tu naiko dharma ubhayasvabhāva iti grahītavyaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. alobhādveṣayor upekṣāśabdo vartata iti. sukhitā bata sattvā iti. saṃtv ity abhiprāyaḥ. duḥkhitā bata sattvā iti. duḥkhitā duḥkhād vimucyaṃtāṃ ity abhiprāyaḥ. tathā hi vyākhyāsyate. vyāpādādayaḥ kleśopakleśā dūrīkriyante. atas tatpratipakṣatvam uktaṃ. katham iti darśasyati. kāmadhātubhūmikāni anāgamyabhūmikāni ca maitryādīni trīṇi maulapramāṇasadṛśāni vidyante. prayogālambanākārasvabhāvasādṛśyāt maulaiḥ sadṛśyāni bhavanti. tair apramāṇais tribhis tān kleśān viṣkaṃbhya prahāṇamārgaiḥ. maitrī vihiṃsābahulānāṃ tatprahāṇāya. mādhyasthyād iti. apakṣapātivenāpy anunīto nāpi pratihata ity arthaḥ. aśraddhatām iti vistaraḥ. asukhavatāṃ. sukham astīty adhimokṣāt kathaṃ na viparītatvaṃ bhavati. saṃtv ity abhiprāyād iti. sukhitāḥ saṃtv ity abhiprāyāt. na viparītatvam ity abhiprāyaḥ. āśayasyāviparītatvād veti. āśayaḥ kuśalā dharmāḥ sukhitā bata sattvā ity ete cittacaittāḥ saparivārāḥ. asyāśayasyāviparītatvān na viparītatvaṃ [Tib. 353b] bhavati. kathaṃ punar āśayasyāviparītatvam ity āha. adhimuktisaṃjñānād iti. adhimukteḥ saṃjñānam adhimuktisaṃjñānaṃ. tasmāt. yasmāt tām adhimuktiṃ tathaiva saṃjānīte. ādhimokṣiko 'yaṃ manaskāra iti paricchinatti. akuśalatvam iti. viparītagrahaṇataḥ. na. kuśalatvāt. naitad evaṃ. kasmāt. kuśalamūlatvāt. kathaṃ punaḥ kuśalamūlam ity āha. vyāpādādipratipakṣatvāt. adveṣasvabhāvatvāt maitrī vyāpādapratipakṣaḥ. duḥkhāpanayanākāratvāc ca karuṇā
body.translated_text: 'In corresponding order' — thus. For those predominating in ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), for the abandonment of that — <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). For those predominating in harmfulness (<s>vihiṃsā</s>), for the abandonment of that — <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion). For those predominating in discontent (<s>arati</s>), for the abandonment of that — <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy). For those predominating in sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>) and ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), for the abandonment of those — <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity). 'What is the distinction regarding the antidote to sensual desire?' — the reflection is from one predominating in sensual desire. [Tib. 353a] The <s>upekṣā</s> is toward the attachment to mother, father, children, and relatives. Just as persons are unconnected — so too are these [beings] — thus equanimity — this is the intent. 'Because of being drawn by greed' — since ill-will is drawn by greed, therefore the intent is that it partakes of the nature of being an antidote to greed. 'But that [<s>upekṣā</s>] is fitting because of its dual nature' — it is fitting because it has the nature of both non-greed (<s>alobha</s>) and non-hatred (<s>adveṣa</s>) — this is the meaning. For what reason? Because it is the antidote to both desire and hatred. But from this, one should understand that no single <s>dharma</s> has a dual nature. Rather, the word '<s>upekṣā</s>' applies to both non-greed and non-hatred. 'May beings be happy!' — the intent is: 'may they be [happy].' 'Alas, beings are suffering!' — the intent is: 'may those who are suffering be freed from suffering.' For thus it will be explained. Ill-will and the other afflictions and secondary afflictions are distanced — therefore their status as antidotes is stated. How? — he shows. Loving-kindness and the other three [immeasurables] belonging to the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> ground and belonging to the <s>Anāgamya</s> (access) ground are found to be similar to the fundamental <s>apramāṇa</s>s (immeasurables). Because of similarity in preparatory practice, object, aspect, and own-nature, they are similar to the fundamental ones. By those three immeasurables, having suppressed those afflictions, through the paths of abandonment — [one abandons them]. '<s>Maitrī</s> [is the antidote] for those predominating in harmfulness, for the abandonment of that' — because of impartiality (<s>mādhyasthya</s>). Not partial — meaning: neither attracted nor repelled. 'Disbelief' — in detail. 'Of those who are not happy' — toward those not endowed with happiness. 'Because of the conviction that happiness exists' — from the conviction [that they are happy], how is there no distortion? 'Because the intent is "may they be [happy]"' — because the intent is 'may [beings] be happy,' there is no distortion — this is the intent. Because of the non-distortion of the intention — thus. The intention consists of the wholesome <s>dharma</s>s — 'alas, may beings be happy!' — these <s>citta</s>-<s>caitta</s>s (mind and mental factors) with their retinue. Because of the non-distortion of this intention, there is no distortion [Tib. 353b]. How then is there non-distortion of the intention? — he says: 'Because of knowing it as conviction' (<s>adhimuktisaṃjñāna</s>). Because one recognizes that very conviction as such — one discerns: 'this is a mental engagement based on conviction' (<s>ādhimokṣikamanaskāra</s>). 'Unwholesomeness' — from apprehending in a distorted manner. No. Because of wholesomeness. This is not so. Why? Because of being a wholesome root. How then is it a wholesome root? — he says: because of being the antidote to ill-will and the rest. Because of having the nature of non-hatred (<s>adveṣa</s>), <s>maitrī</s> is the antidote to ill-will. Because of the aspect of removing suffering, <s>karuṇā</s>

body.text:
duḥkhopasaṃhārākārāyā vihiṃsāyāḥ pratipakṣo bhavati. muditā carateḥ pratipakṣaḥ saumanasyārūpatvāt. upekṣā ca mādhyasthyāt kāmarāgavyāpādayoḥ pratipakṣa iti. tadālaṃbanānām iti. kāmāvacarasattvālaṃbanānām ity arthaḥ. tadbhājanena bhājanagataṃ darśitam iti. sthānena sthānīyasattvaloko darśita ity arthaḥ. samāhitāsamāhitamaulaprayogagrahaṇād iti. ṣaṭpaṃcadaśabhūmikatvāt trayāṇām api kāraṇam ucyate saṃbhavataḥ. tatrāsamāhitaḥ kāmadhātuḥ. prayogāḥ sāmantakānīti saṃbhavato yojyaṃ. ṣaṭbhūmikavyāvasthāne 'nāgamyaṃ sāmantakam apīṣyate [Tib. 354a] sāmantakāny api prayogabhūtāni gṛhyante. kiṃ maulānīti. mauladhyānabhūmikatvād iti. maulaśuddhakadhyānabhūmikatvād ity arthaḥ. na hi śuddhakair mauladhyānaiḥ kleśāḥ prahīyanta ity uktaṃ prāk. adhimuktimanaskāratvān na taiḥ kleśāḥ prahīyante. tattvamanaskāreṇa hi kleśaprahāṇaṃ. sattvālambanatvāc ca na taiḥ prahāṇaṃ. dharmasāmānyalakṣaṇamanaskāreṇa hi kleśaprahāṇam iti siddhāntaḥ. kathaṃ tarhīty āha. tatprayogeṇa tv iti vistaraḥ. maitryādiprayogeṇa vyāpādādiviṣkaṃbhaṇāt. tatpratipakṣatvam uktam iti. vyāpādādipratipakṣatvam uktaṃ. viṣkambhaṇaprahāṇāni tanīty arthaḥ. prahīṇadūrīkaraṇāc ceti. yasmād ānantaryamārgair laukikair lokottarair vā mārgair vyāpādādayaḥ kleśopakleśā dūrīkriyante. atas tatpratipakṣatvam uktaṃ. katham iti darśayati. kāmadhātubhūmikāny anāgamyabhūmikāni
ca maitryādini trīṇi [Tib. 354b] maulāpramāṇasadṛśāni saṃvidyante. prayogālambanākārasvabhāvasādṛśyān maulaiḥ sadṛśāni bhavanti. tair apramāṇais tribhis tān kleśān viṣkaṃbhya prahāṇamārgair ānantaryamārgaiḥ prajahāti. balavatpratyayalābhe 'pīti. vyāpādādipratyayalābhe 'pi balavati sati taiḥ kleśair anādhṛṣyo bhavati. saṃmukhībhāvataḥ. adhimātra iti. mitrapakṣe. paramamitre hi sukarā maitrī. spharatīti. vyāpnoti. pūrvapuṇyāphalasaṃdarśanād iti. pūrvapuṇyaphalasaṃdarśanāt samucchinnakuśalamūle 'pi pudgale śakyaṃ guṇagrāhiṇānena bhavituṃ puṇyam anena kṛtam āsīd yenāsya rūpādisaṃpad iti. pratyekabuddhe ca doṣagrāhiṇā nūnam anenāpuṇyaṃ kṛtam āsīd yenāsyaivaṃ rūpādivaikalyam iti. api eva duḥkhād vimucyerann ity adhimucyamānaḥ karuṇāyāṃ
body.translated_text: is the antidote to harmfulness (<s>vihiṃsā</s>), which has the aspect of bringing about suffering. <s>Muditā</s> (sympathetic joy) is the antidote to discontent (<s>arati</s>), because of having the nature of mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>). And <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), because of impartiality, is the antidote to both sensual desire and ill-will. 'Of those having those as their object' — meaning: of those having beings of the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (Desire Realm) as their object. 'By the container, the contained is shown' — meaning: by the ground (<s>sthāna</s>), the beings of that ground are shown. 'Because of the inclusion of concentrated and non-concentrated, fundamental and preparatory' — the reason for the three [immeasurables] being on six, five, or fifteen grounds is stated from the standpoint of possibility. Therein, the non-concentrated is the <s>Kāmadhātu</s>. The preparatory stages are the access [concentrations] (<s>sāmantaka</s>) — to be connected as applicable. In the arrangement on six grounds, the <s>Anāgamya</s> access is also accepted [Tib. 354a] — the preparatory access stages are also included. 'Are they fundamental?' — because of belonging to the ground of the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s>s. Meaning: because of belonging to the ground of the fundamental pure <s>dhyāna</s>s. For it has been previously stated that afflictions are not abandoned by the fundamental pure <s>dhyāna</s>s. Because of being mental engagements based on conviction, afflictions are not abandoned by them. For the abandonment of afflictions is through mental engagement with reality (<s>tattvamanaskāra</s>). And because of having beings as their object, there is no abandonment by them — for the established doctrine is that the abandonment of afflictions is through mental engagement with the general characteristics of <s>dharma</s>s. How then? — he says: 'But through their preparatory practice' — in detail. Through the preparatory practice of <s>maitrī</s> and the rest, because of the suppression of ill-will and the rest. 'Their status as antidotes is stated' — the status as antidotes to ill-will and the rest is stated. Those are [antidotes in the sense of] suppression-abandonment (<s>viṣkambhaṇaprahāṇa</s>) — this is the meaning. 'And because of the distancing of what has been abandoned' — since through uninterrupted paths (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>), whether mundane or supramundane, ill-will and the other afflictions and secondary afflictions are distanced, therefore their status as antidotes is stated. How? — he shows. Loving-kindness and the other three [immeasurables] belonging to the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> ground and belonging to the <s>Anāgamya</s> ground [Tib. 354b] are found to be similar to the fundamental immeasurables. Because of similarity in preparatory practice, object, aspect, and own-nature, they are similar to the fundamental ones. By those three immeasurables, having suppressed those afflictions, through the paths of abandonment — through the uninterrupted paths — one abandons [them]. 'Even upon obtaining a powerful condition' — even upon obtaining a powerful condition of ill-will and the rest, one becomes invincible by those afflictions. 'From the state of being face-to-face' — 'intense' means: toward the friendly party. For loving-kindness toward one's dearest friend is easy. 'Pervades' means: extends throughout. 'Because of showing the result of former merit' — because of showing the result of former merit, even toward one whose wholesome roots have been completely cut off, one is able to apprehend their qualities — thinking: 'this one must have performed merit, since they possess beauty of form and the like.' And toward a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> too, one who apprehends faults [may think]: 'this one must have performed demerit, since they have such deficiency of form and the like.' 'May they indeed be freed from suffering!' — cultivating this conviction, one engages in <s>karuṇā</s>

body.text: prayujyate. apy evābhipramoderann ity adhimucyamāno muditāyāṃ prayujyate. muditayā na samanvāgata iti. tṛtīyacaturthayoḥ saumanasyābhāvāt.
body.translated_text: (compassion). 'May they indeed rejoice greatly!' — cultivating this conviction, one engages in <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy). <s>Muditā</s> is not endowed [in the third and fourth dhyānas] — because of the absence of mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>) in the third and fourth [<s>dhyāna</s>s].

body.text: iti. yathāsūtraṃ. katham. aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ. katame 'ṣṭau. rūpī rūpāṇi paśyatīty ayaṃ prathamo vimokṣaḥ. adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi [Tib. 355a] paśyatīty ayaṃ dvitīyo vimokṣaḥ. śubhaṃ vimokṣaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharatīty ayaṃ tṛtīyo vimokṣaḥ. sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramāt pratighasaṃjñānām astaṃgamāt nānātvasaṃjñānām amanasikārād anantam ākāśam anantam ākāśam ity ākāśānantyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharati. tadyathā devā ākāśānantyāyatanopagāḥ. ayaṃ caturtho vimokṣaḥ. punar aparaṃ sarvaśa ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ samatikramyānaṃtaṃ vijñānam anaṃtaṃ vijñānam iti vijñānānantyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharati. tadyathā devā vijñānānaṃtyāyatanopagāḥ. ayaṃ paṃcamo vimokṣaḥ. punar aparaṃ sarvaśo vijñānānaṃtyāyatanaṃ samatikramya nāsti kiṃcid ity ākiṃcanyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharati. tadyathā devā ākiṃcanyāyatanopagāḥ. ayaṃ ṣaṣṭo vimokṣaḥ. punar aparaṃ sarvaśa ākiṃcanyāyatanaṃ samatikramya naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharati. tadyathā devā naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanopagāḥ. ayaṃ saptamo vimokṣaḥ. punar aparaṃ sarvaśo naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ samatikramya saṃjñānirodhaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya [Tib. 355b] viharati. ayam aṣṭamo vimokṣa iti. rūpī rūpāṇīti. svātmani rūpāṇi vibhāvya bahir api rūpāṇi paśyati. vinīlakādyālambanatvāt. aśubhāvan nayo veditavya iti. adhirāgasya varṇarāgādipratipakṣam ārabhya saṃbhavato vistareṇa yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: — thus, according to the <s>sūtra</s>. How? 'There are eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>). What are the eight? "One possessing form sees forms" — this is the first liberation. "Internally having the perception of formlessness, one sees forms externally" — this is the second liberation. "Having directly realized the beautiful liberation with the body, one enters and dwells" — this is the third liberation. "Through the complete transcendence of perceptions of form, the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and the non-attention to perceptions of diversity, [thinking] "space is infinite," one enters and dwells in the Infinity of Space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>). Just like the <s>deva</s>s who have attained the Infinity of Space" — this is the fourth liberation. "Furthermore, through the complete transcendence of the Infinity of Space, [thinking] "consciousness is infinite," one enters and dwells in the Infinity of Consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>). Just like the <s>deva</s>s who have attained the Infinity of Consciousness" — this is the fifth liberation. "Furthermore, through the complete transcendence of the Infinity of Consciousness, [thinking] "there is nothing," one enters and dwells in the Sphere of Nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>). Just like the <s>deva</s>s who have attained the Sphere of Nothingness" — this is the sixth liberation. "Furthermore, through the complete transcendence of the Sphere of Nothingness, one enters and dwells in the Sphere of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). Just like the <s>deva</s>s who have attained the Sphere of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception" — this is the seventh liberation. "Furthermore, through the complete transcendence of the Sphere of Neither-Perception-Nor-Non-Perception, having directly realized the cessation of perception (<s>saṃjñānirodha</s>) with the body, one enters and dwells" — this is the eighth liberation.' 'One possessing form, forms' — having cultivated forms in one's own self, one sees forms externally as well — because of having blue-colored (<s>vinīlaka</s>) and other [kasinas] as object-domain. 'The method of the impurity [meditation] (<s>aśubhā</s>) should be understood' — regarding the antidote to excessive desire (<s>adhirāga</s>) for color-attachment and the rest, it should be applied in detail where possible.

children.translated_text: 'Non-greed (<s>alobha</s>), belonging to ten grounds, having Desire Realm and visible [forms] as its domain, born of humans, impurity [meditation]' —

body.text: yathāsaṃkhyam iti. kāmāvacarasya varṇarāgasya pratipakṣeṇa prathamadhyānabhūmiko vimokṣaḥ. prathamadhyānabhūmikasyāpi varṇarāgapratipakṣeṇa dvitīyadhyānabhūmiko vimokṣaḥ. etau ca dvau punar dūrībhāvapratipakṣau veditavyau.
body.translated_text: in due order — by the antidote to color-attachment of the Desire Realm, the first liberation belongs to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground. By the antidote to color-attachment belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, the second liberation belongs to the second <s>dhyāna</s> ground. And these two should be understood as antidotes for the purpose of distancing (<s>dūrībhāvapratipakṣa</s>).

body.text: āha. dvitīyādidhyāneṣu varṇarāgo nāstīti kathaṃ gamyate. cakṣurvijñānābhāvāt. yo hi yasmād viṣayād viraktaḥ. niyatam asau tadgrāhakād api vijñānād viraktaḥ. dvitīyādiṣu ca dhyāneṣu cakṣurvijñānādi nāstīti. ato varṇavītarāgās ta iti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: He says: 'How is it understood that there is no color-attachment in the second and higher <s>dhyāna</s>s?' Because of the absence of eye-consciousness. For whoever is dispassionate from a particular sense-object is necessarily also dispassionate from the consciousness that grasps it. And in the second and higher <s>dhyāna</s>s, there is no eye-consciousness and the like — therefore it is established that they are free from color-attachment.

body.text: iti śuddhakānāsravāḥ.
body.translated_text: that is, pure (<s>śuddhaka</s>) and uncontaminated.

body.text: anyadāpy asamāhitāḥ saṃtīti. ārūpyeṣu vipākajāṃś cittacaittān abhisaṃdhāyocyate. [Tib. 356a] pūrvasmiṃs tu pakṣe maraṇabhavāvasthāyām evāsamāhitā ārūpyā iti darśayati. sāmantakavimuktamārgā api vimokṣākhyāṃ labhanta iti. kim aṃga maulā ity apiśabdārthaḥ. nānantaryamārga iti vistaraḥ. yasmād adharabhūmivaimukhyād vimokṣā ity ucyante. tasmād ānantaryamārgā na vimokṣākhyāṃ labhante. adharālambanatvāt. vimuktimārgās tu labhante. ūrdhvālambanatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'Even at other times, they exist as non-concentrated' — this is said with reference to the retribution-born (<s>vipākaja</s>) mind and mental factors in the formless [realms]. But on the former position, he shows that the formless [beings] are non-concentrated only in the state of the death-existence (<s>maraṇabhava</s>). 'The preliminary (<s>sāmantaka</s>) and liberation paths also obtain the designation "liberation" (<s>vimokṣa</s>)' — the word 'also' (<s>api</s>) implies: how much more so the fundamental ones. 'Not the uninterrupted paths' — in detail. Because liberations are so called because of turning away from a lower ground — therefore the uninterrupted paths do not obtain the designation 'liberation.' Because they have a lower [ground] as their object-domain. But the liberation paths do obtain it — because they have an upper [ground] as their object-domain.

children.translated_text: 'But the cessation [of perception and feeling] is an attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>)' —

body.text: aṣṭama iti vākyaśeṣaḥ. saṃjñāveditavaimukhyād iti. saṃjñāvaimukhyād veditavaimukhyāc ca vimokṣaḥ. sarvasaṃskṛtād vā vaimukhyād vimokṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'the eighth' — this completes the sentence. 'Because of turning away from perception and feeling' — it is a liberation because of turning away from perception and from feeling. Or it is a liberation because of turning away from all conditioned things.

body.text: samāpattyāvaraṇavimokṣaṇād vimokṣa iti. samāpattyāvaraṇavimokṣavaimukhyād vimokṣa iti. tatra samāpattyāvaraṇaṃ yasminn āvaraṇe cittākarmaṇyatā traidhātukavītarāgā api saṃtaḥ prathamam api maulaṃ dhyānaṃ notpādayanti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of liberation from the obstruction to attainment (<s>samāpattyāvaraṇa</s>), it is a liberation' — because of turning away from the liberation from the obstruction to attainment, it is a liberation.
