Therein, the obstruction to attainment is that obstruction due to which — the unworkability of mind — even those who are dispassionate from all three realms, being [thus qualified], do not initially produce even the fundamental first <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: yathāyogam iti. dvayor vinīlakādyamanojñaṃ rūpaṃ ālambanaṃ. tṛtīyasya manojñam ālambanam iti. taddhetunirodhau ceti. tasya duḥkhasya [Tib. 356b] samudayanirodhau. sarvaś cānvayajñānapakṣa iti. ūrdhvādhaḥ svabhūmika ity arthaḥ. apratisaṃkhyānirodhaś ceti. apratisaṃkhyānirodhaś cārūpyāvimokṣāṇāṃ ālambanam iti vaktavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'As applicable' — for the first two, the object-domain is unattractive form such as blue-colored (<s>vinīlaka</s>) and the rest. For the third, the object-domain is attractive [form]. 'And the cessation and origination of that [suffering]' — the origination and cessation of that suffering. 'And all belong to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class' — the meaning is: upper, lower, and belonging to one's own ground. 'And <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (non-analytical cessation)' — one should also state that <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is the object-domain of the formless liberations.

children.translated_text:
'Those formless ones
belong to the <s>anvayajñāna</s> class, having the suffering and the rest of upper and own grounds as their object' —

body.text: ity atravacanāt.
body.translated_text: because of no statement here [of apratisaṃkhyānirodha].

body.text: āha. katamaḥ punar apratisaṃkhyānirodhas teṣām ālambanam. atrocyate. aśaikṣasyānimittasya samādher apratisaṃkhyānirodham ālambante. te ca sapta sāmantakāni hitvānyāsv ekādaśasu bhūmiṣu kāmadhātāv anāgamye dhyānāntareṣu dhyanārūpyeṣu cāṣṭāsv iti. sopasaṃkhyānaṃ śāstram iti śāstralakṣaṇaṃ darśitaṃ bhavati. ākāśaṃ caikasyeti. vaktavyaṃ ākāśānaṃtyāyatanavimokṣasyālambanaṃ. dvitīyadhyānabhūmikavarṇarāgābhāvād iti. dvitīyadhyānabhūmikasya varṇarāgapratipakṣayitavyasyābhāvād ity arthaḥ. tadabhāvaḥ kāyikavijñānābhāvāt. sukhamaṇḍeñjitatvāc ca. sukhasya maṇḍaḥ. sarvasukhasyoparisthaṃ sukham ity arthaḥ. teneñjitatvāt kampitatvāt. na tṛtīye dhyāne vimokṣo vyavasthāpyate.
body.translated_text: He says: 'Which <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> is their object-domain?' Here it is said: they take as their object-domain the <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> of the non-learner's signless concentration (<s>ānimittasamādhi</s>). And those seven — excluding the seven preliminaries (<s>sāmantaka</s>) — exist in the other eleven grounds: the Desire Realm, the preliminary stage (<s>anāgamya</s>), the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>s, and the eight [grounds of] <s>dhyāna</s>s and formless [attainments]. 'The <s>śāstra</s> is with annotation (<s>sopasaṃkhyāna</s>)' — the characteristic of the <s>śāstra</s> has been shown. 'And for one [liberation], space' — one should state that space is the object-domain of the Infinity of Space liberation. 'Because of the absence of color-attachment belonging to the second <s>dhyāna</s> ground' — the meaning is: because of the absence of that which is to be counteracted as color-attachment belonging to the second <s>dhyāna</s> ground. The absence of that is because of the absence of bodily consciousness. 'And because of being shaken by the summit of pleasure (<s>sukhamaṇḍa</s>)' — the summit of pleasure is the topmost of all pleasures — this is the meaning. Because of being shaken, agitated by that — no liberation is established in the third <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: Tib. 357a
body.translated_text: 'If there is no color-attachment belonging to the third <s>dhyāna</s> ground, why does one produce the beautiful (

body.text: yadi tṛtīyadhyānabhūmiko varṇarāgo nāsti. kasmāc chubhaṃ

vimokṣam utpādayatīti. ata āha aśubhayā līnāṃ saṃtatiṃ pramodayituṃ jijñāsanārthaṃ veti. vimokṣādīnām iti. ādiśabdenābhibhvāyatanādyupagrahaḥ. kleśadūrīkaraṇārthaṃ. vimokṣādīnaṃ dūribhāvapratipakṣatvāt. samāpattivaśitvārthaṃ ca. tac ca samāpattivaśitvam araṇādiguṇābhinirhārāya bhavati. āryāyāś ca rddheḥ. kiṃ. abhinirhārāyeti prakṛtaṃ. sā punar yayā vastupariṇāmādhiṣṭhānāyurutsargādīnīti. tatra vastupariṇāmaṃ. yad vastu yathādhimucyate. tathaiva tad bhavati. yathā suvarṇasya mṛtkaraṇaṃ. tathādhimokṣād adhiṣṭhānaṃ sthirasya vastunaḥ. imaṃ tu kālam avatiṣṭhatām iti tathāyuṣā utsargaḥ. ādiśabdena sumeroḥ paramāṇau praveśa ity evam anyac ca sūtre draṣṭavyaṃ.
body.translated_text: liberation?' Therefore he says: 'In order to delight a continuum that has become sluggish through impurity [meditation], and for the purpose of investigation (<s>jijñāsana</s>).' 'Of liberations and the rest' — by the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), the overmastering bases (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>) and the rest are included. 'For the purpose of distancing afflictions' — because the liberations and the rest serve as antidotes for distancing. 'And for the purpose of mastery over attainments' — and that mastery over attainments serves for the accomplishment of qualities such as <s>araṇā</s> (non-conflict) and the rest. 'And of the Noble <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power)' — for what purpose? — 'for the accomplishment' — this continues from the main [sentence]. That [Noble ṛddhi], moreover, is that by which the empowerment of transformation of objects, life-force-relinquishment, and the rest [are accomplished]. Therein, transformation of objects means: whatever object one resolves upon, it becomes exactly that — like turning gold into clay. Similarly, empowerment means the [determination regarding] a stable object: 'Let this remain for this duration of time.' And life-force-relinquishment means: through that, with the life-force, the relinquishment [occurs]. By the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), the entry of [Mount] <s>Sumeru</s> into an atom, and other such [feats] seen in the <s>sūtra</s> [are included].

body.text: kasmāt tṛtīyāṣṭamayor eva sākṣātkaraṇam uktaṃ. nānyeṣām iti. kathaṃ tṛtīyasya sākṣātkaraṇam uktaṃ. śubhaṃ vimokṣaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharatīti. aṣṭamasyāpi. saṃjñāveditanirodhaṃ [Tib. 357b] kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharatīti. atra sākṣātkṛtveti pratyakṣīkṛtvety arthaḥ. upasaṃpadya viharatīti tāṃ samāpadya samāpattiṃ viharatīty arthaḥ. atrocyate. prathamadvitīyābhyāṃ vimokṣābhyāṃ tṛtīyasya vimokṣasya prādhānyāt. rūpivimokṣāvaraṇasākalyaprahāṇād āśrayaparivṛttitas tṛtīyasya sākṣātkaraṇam uktam. evam aṣṭamasyāpi prādhānyāt. ārūpyāvimokṣāvaraṇasākalyaprahāṇād āśrayaparivṛttitaḥ sākṣātkaraṇam uktaṃ. dhātubhūmiparyantāvasthitatvāc ceti. caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ rūpadhātubhūmiparyaṃtāvasthitaṃ. bhavāgram apy ārūpyadhātubhūmiparyantāvasthitaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Why is direct realization (<s>sākṣātkaraṇa</s>) stated only for the third and eighth [liberations] and not for the others?' How is direct realization stated for the third? 'Having directly realized the beautiful liberation with the body, one enters and dwells' — thus. And for the eighth as well: 'Having directly realized the cessation of perception and feeling with the body, one enters and dwells' — thus. Here, 'having directly realized' means 'having made [it] directly perceptible.' 'Enters and dwells' means 'having entered that attainment, one dwells.' Here it is said: because of the preeminence of the third liberation over the first and second liberations — because of the abandonment of the entire obstruction to the form-liberations, and because of the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>) — direct realization is stated for the third. Similarly, because of the preeminence of the eighth too — because of the abandonment of the entire obstruction to the formless liberations, and because of the transformation of the basis — direct realization is stated. 'And because of being situated at the limit of the realm and ground' — the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> is situated at the limit of the Form Realm ground; the Peak of Existence too is situated at the limit of the Formless Realm ground.

body.text: (VIII.35) evam adhimātrāṇīti. adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyaty adhimātrāṇi suvarṇadurvarṇānīti vistaraḥ yāvad idaṃ dvitīyam abhibhvāyatanam. adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñi evam eveti. katham. adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati parīttāni suvarṇadurvarṇānīti pūrvavad yāvad idaṃ tṛtīyam abhibhvāyatanaṃ. tathā adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśayti adhimātrāṇi suvarṇadurvarṇānīti pūrvavad yāvad idaṃ tṛtīyam abhibhvāyatanaṃ. tathā adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī paśyaty adhimātrāṇi suvarṇadurvarṇānīti pūrvavat yāvād idaṃ caturtham abhibhvāyatanam ity etāni catvārīti. arūpasaṃjñy eva punar nīlapītalohitāvadātāni [Tib. 358a] paśyatīti. katham. adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati nīlāni nīlavarṇāni nīlanidarśanāni nīlanirbhāsāni. tadyathā umakāpuṣpaṃ saṃpannaṃ vārāṇaseyaṃ vā vastraṃ nīlaṃ nīlavarṇaṃ nīlanidarśanaṃ nīlanirbhāsaṃ
body.translated_text: (VIII.35) 'Thus, extensive' — 'internally having the perception of form, one sees forms externally — extensive, beautiful and ugly in color' — in detail, up to: 'this is the second overmastering base (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>).' 'Internally having the perception of formlessness, likewise' — how? 'Internally having the perception of formlessness, one sees forms externally — small, beautiful and ugly in color' — as before, up to: 'this is the third overmastering base.' Similarly, 'internally having the perception of formlessness, one sees forms externally — extensive, beautiful and ugly in color' — as before, up to: 'this is the fourth overmastering base' — thus these are four. 'One with the perception of formlessness, moreover, sees blue, yellow, red, and white' — how? 'Internally having the perception of formlessness, one sees forms externally — blue, blue-colored, blue-appearing, blue-shining — just like a flax flower (<s>umākāpuṣpa</s>) in full bloom, or a <s>Vārāṇasī</s> cloth that is blue, blue-colored, blue-appearing, blue-shining'

body.text: tāni khalu rūpāṇy abhibhūya jānāty abhibhūya paśyati. evaṃsaṃjñī ca bhavatīdaṃ paṃcamaṃ abhibhvāyatanaṃ. adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati pītāni pītavarṇāni pītanidarśanāni pītanirbhāsāni. tadyathā karṇikārapuṣpaṃ vārāṇaseyaṃ vā vastraṃ pītam iti vistaraḥ. idaṃ ṣaṣṭham abhibhvāyatanaṃ. adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī rūpāṇi paśyati lohitāni lohitavarṇāni lohitanidarśanāni lohitanirbhāsāni. tadyathā baṃdhūkapuṣpaṃ saṃpannaṃ vārāṇaseyaṃ vā vastraṃ lohitam iti vistaraḥ. idaṃ saptamam abhibhvāyatanaṃ. adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati avadātāny avadātavarṇāni avadātanidarśanāni avadātanirbhāsāni. tadyathā uśanastārakā saṃpannaṃ vā vārāṇaseyaṃ vastram avadātam [Tib. 358b] iti vistaraḥ. idam aṣṭmam abhibhvāyatanam iti. mūrdhakāni catvārīmāni cātyārīty aṣṭau bhavanti.
body.translated_text: — 'Having overcome those forms, one knows and sees. One has such a perception. This is the fifth overmastering base.' 'Internally having the perception of formlessness, one sees forms externally — yellow, yellow-colored, yellow-appearing, yellow-shining — just like a <s>karṇikāra</s> flower, or a <s>Vārāṇasī</s> cloth that is yellow' — in detail. 'This is the sixth overmastering base.' 'Internally having the perception of formlessness, one sees forms — red, red-colored, red-appearing, red-shining — just like a <s>bandhūka</s> flower in full bloom, or a <s>Vārāṇasī</s> cloth that is red' — in detail. 'This is the seventh overmastering base.' 'Internally having the perception of formlessness, one sees forms externally — white, white-colored, white-appearing, white-shining — just like the star <s>Uśanas</s> (Venus), or a <s>Vārāṇasī</s> cloth in full bloom that is white' — in detail. 'This is the eighth overmastering base.' The four principal ones and these four — thus there are eight.

body.text: iti. yathā rūpī rūpāṇi paśyatīti prathamo vimokṣaḥ. ātmagataṃ rūpaṃ paśyan bahirgataṃ rūpaṃ paśyati. evam ādye abhibhvāyatane. tayor hy ekam ātmagataṃ rūpaṃ paśyan bahirgataṃ paśyati. tathā hy etat paṭhyate. adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati parīttānīti vistaraḥ. dvitīyam api tathaiva. ayaṃ tu viśeṣo bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyaty adhimātrāṇīti. kiṃ ca yathā prathamo vimokṣaḥ prathamadhyānabhūmikaḥ kāmāvacaravarṇarāgapratipakṣaḥ kāmāvacararūpāyatanālambanaś ca. tatheme prathame abhibhvāyatane veditavye.
body.translated_text: thus. Just as 'one possessing form sees forms' — this is the first liberation — seeing form in one's own self, one sees form externally — so too in the first [pair of] overmastering bases. For in those two, one sees form in one's own self and sees external form. For thus it is read: 'Internally having the perception of form, one sees forms externally — small' — in detail. The second too is just the same. But the distinction is: 'one sees forms externally — extensive.' Moreover, just as the first liberation belongs to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, is the antidote to Desire Realm color-attachment, and has Desire Realm form-sense-sphere as its object-domain — so these first [pair of] overmastering bases should be understood.

body.text: iti. yathādhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatīty evaṃlakṣaṇo dvitīyo vimokṣaḥ. evaṃlakṣaṇe evaṃ tṛtīyacaturthe abhibhvāyatane. te api hy evaṃ paṭhyete. adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñībahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati parīttānīti tṛtīyaḥ paṭhyate. adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyaty adhimātrāṇīti caturthaḥ paṭhyate. kiṃ ca yathā dvitīyo vimokṣaḥ dvitīyadhyānabhūmikaḥ prathamadhyānabhūmikavarṇarāgapratipakṣaḥ [Tib. 359a] kāmāvacararūpālaṃbanaś ca. tathā tṛtīyaṃ caturthaṃ cābhibhvāyatanaṃ.
body.translated_text: thus. Just as 'internally having the perception of formlessness, one sees forms externally' — this is the characteristic of the second liberation — so the third and fourth overmastering bases have the same characteristic. For those too are read thus: 'Internally having the perception of formlessness, one sees forms externally — small' — the third is read. 'Internally having the perception of formlessness, one sees forms externally — extensive' — the fourth is read. Moreover, just as the second liberation belongs to the second <s>dhyāna</s> ground, is the antidote to color-attachment belonging to the first <s>dhyāna</s> ground, and has Desire Realm form as its object-domain — so too the third and fourth overmastering bases.

children.translated_text: The others, however, are like the fair liberation (<s>śubhavimokṣa</s>)

body.text: iti. yathā śubho vimokṣaś caturthadhyānabhūmikaḥ kāmāvacaramanojñarūpāyatanālambanaś ca. tathā nīlapītalohitāvadātābhibhvāyatanāni. kevalaṃ tv iha varṇacatuṣṭayaṃ vibhajya gṛhyate. śubhasya ca vimokṣasyālobhaḥ svabhāvaḥ. evam eṣām api. yathāyaṃ śubho vimokṣaḥ saparivāragrahaṇāt paṃcaskaṃdhasvabhāvaḥ. tathaiva tāny apīty avagantavyaṃ. tair vimokṣamātram
body.translated_text: thus. Just as the fair liberation (<s>śubhavimokṣa</s>) belongs to the ground of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> and has as its object-domain the pleasant form-base (<s>rūpāyatana</s>) of the Desire Realm, so too are the overmastering bases (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>) of blue, yellow, red, and white. The only [difference] is that here the four colors are grasped by being distinguished separately. And the essential nature of the fair liberation is non-attachment (<s>alobha</s>). Similarly for these as well. Just as this fair liberation, because of being grasped together with its retinue, has the essential nature of the five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>s) — so too should those be understood. By those, it is merely liberation

body.text: iti. nālambanābhibhavanaṃ. kathaṃ cābhibhvāyatanair ālaṃbanābhibhavanam ity ata āha. yatheṣṭam adhimokṣād iti. yatheṣṭaṃ tair nīlapītādyadhimokṣāt. kṣaṇena nīlaṃ kṣaṇena pītam ityādi. amanojñasya vā vinīlakāder manojñādhimokṣāt. kleśānutpādāc ceti. śubhato 'pi ca sāṃkleśikaṃ vastv ākārayataḥ kleśānutpattes tair abhibhvāyatanair ālaṃbanābhibhavanaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: — not the overmastering of the object-domain. And how is there overmastering of the object-domain through the overmastering bases (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>)? Therefore he says: 'because of resolving as one wishes' (<s>yatheṣṭam adhimokṣāt</s>). Because of resolving as one wishes upon blue, yellow, and the rest through those [bases]. In one moment blue, in one moment yellow, and so forth. Or because of resolving the unpleasant — such as the dark blue of a corpse — as pleasant. And because of the non-arising of afflictions — because even when apprehending a defiled object from the perspective of being fair, afflictions do not arise — therefore through those overmastering bases there is overmastering of the object-domain.

body.text: (VIII.36) nirantarakṛtsnaspharaṇād iti. nirantaraṃ kṛtsnānāṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ spharaṇād vyāpanāt tasmāt kṛtsnāyatanānīty [Tib. 359b] ucyante. kāmāvacaraṃ rūpāyatanam iti.
body.translated_text: (VIII.36) 'Because of uninterrupted total pervading of the <s>kṛtsna</s>s' — because of the uninterrupted pervading, the spreading, of the <s>kṛtsna</s>s (totalities) such as earth and the rest, therefore they are called <s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>s (totality bases). 'The form-base of the Desire Realm' —

children.text:
pṛthivī varṇasaṃsthānam ucyate lokasaṃjñayā
āpas tejaś ca vāyuś ca dhātur eva tathāpi ceti
children.translated_text:
'Earth, color, and shape are spoken of in worldly convention;
water, fire, and wind — these are likewise elements' —

body.text: vacanāt.
body.translated_text: from this statement.

body.text: vāyau spraṣṭavyāyatanam ity eka iti. ye vāyau rūpāyatanaṃ necchanti. ta āhuḥ. vāyau spraṣṭavyāyatnam ālambanam iti. vimokṣaprāveśikānīti. praveśā eva prāveśikāni. iti svārthavṛddhividhānāt. praveśe bhavāni vā. uttarottaraviśiṣṭatvād iti. yasmād vimokṣebhya uttarāṇy abhibhvāyatanāni viśiṣṭāni. abhibhvāyatanebhya uttarāṇi kṛtsnāyatanāni viśiṣṭānīti. tad uktaṃ bhavati. vimokṣān utpādyābhibhvāyatanāny utpādayati. abhibhvāyatanāny utpādya kṛtsnāyatanāny utpādayatīti. sthāpayitvā nirodhavimokṣam iti. tasyaikāntenāryasaṃtānikatvāt.
body.translated_text: 'In the case of wind, the tangible-base' — this is one [view]. Those who do not accept form-base in the case of wind say: 'In the case of wind, the tangible-base is the object-domain.' 'Introductory to the liberations' (<s>vimokṣaprāveśika</s>) — the introductions themselves are the introductory [means]. This is by the rule of the affix in its own sense (<s>svārthavṛddhi</s>). Or: [those] that exist in the introduction. 'Because of being successively more distinguished' — because the overmastering bases are more distinguished than the liberations, being superior; and the totality bases are more distinguished than the overmastering bases, being superior — that is what is stated. Having produced the liberations, one produces the overmastering bases. Having produced the overmastering bases, one produces the totality bases. 'Except for the cessation-liberation' (<s>nirodhavimokṣa</s>) — because that is exclusively belonging to the stream of a noble one (<s>ārya</s>).

body.text: (VIII.37) ucitānucitatvād iti. ucitāni vairāgyalābhikāni. anucitāni prāyogikāni.
body.translated_text: (VIII.37) 'Because of being accustomed and unaccustomed' — the accustomed are those obtained through dispassion (<s>vairāgyalābhika</s>). The unaccustomed are those [obtained] through application (<s>prāyogika</s>).

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. kiṃ punaḥ śeṣaṃ. prathamās trayo vimokṣāḥ abhibhvāyatanāny aṣṭau. kṛtsnāyatanāny aṣṭau. etan manuṣyāśrayam eva. kiṃ kāraṇam. upadeśasāmarthyenotpādanāt. anyatra devādiṣūpadeśabhāvāt.
body.translated_text: — thus in detail. What then is the rest? The first three liberations, the eight overmastering bases, and the eight totality bases — these have a human support only. What is the reason? Because they are produced through the power of instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>). Because there is no instruction elsewhere, among <s>deva</s>s and such.

body.text: (VIII.38) kathaṃ [Tib. 360a] rūpārūpyadhātvor ārūpyadhyānaviśeṣotpādanam iti. ārūpyadhātau rūpadhātau vā yasyāṃ bhūmāv upapannaḥ. tadūrdhvaṃ yad ārūpyaṃ dhyānaṃ ca. tat tato viśiṣyate ity ārūpyadhyānaviśeṣāḥ. tasyārūpyadhyānaviśeṣaya katham upadeśam antareṇa bhavatīti. yataḥ śeṣaṃ manuṣyāśrayam eva. upadeśasāmarthyenotpādanād ity uktam. ato 'nena saṃbandhena pṛṣṭaṃ. kathaṃ rūpārūpyadhātvor iti vistaraḥ. hetubālāc cāsannābhīkṣṇābhyāsād iti. āsannābhyāsād abhīkṣṇābhyāsāc ca. kathaṃ kṛtvā. kaścid ārūpyasamāpattiṃ samāpadya tataś ca parihāyānantaram eva rūpadhātāv upapadyate. ārūpyasamāpattilakṣaṇasya sabhāgahetor balīyastvāt tasya rūpadhātāv ārūpyasamāpattir utpatsyate. abhīkṣṇābhyāsād api. yadi kaścid ārūpyasamāpattim
body.translated_text: (VIII.38) 'How is the production of the distinction of formless [attainments] and <s>dhyāna</s>s in the Form and Formless Realms?' — in whatever ground one is born in the Formless Realm or the Form Realm, the formless [attainment] and <s>dhyāna</s> that are above that [ground] are more distinguished than it — these are the distinctions of formless [attainments] and <s>dhyāna</s>s. How does the production of those distinctions of formless [attainments] and <s>dhyāna</s>s occur without instruction? Since the rest has a human support only, because they are produced through the power of instruction — as was stated. Therefore, by this connection, the question is asked: 'How in the Form and Formless Realms?' — thus in detail. 'Through the power of cause (<s>hetubala</s>), from proximate and repeated practice' — from proximate practice and from repeated practice. How so? Someone, having entered a formless attainment (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) and then regressing from it, is immediately reborn in the Form Realm. Because of the predominance of the homogeneous cause (<s>sabhāgahetu</s>) characterized by that formless attainment, that formless attainment will arise for that one in the Form Realm. Also from repeated practice — if someone repeatedly

body.text: abhīkṣṇaṃ samāpadya tataś ca parihāya rūpadhātāv upapadyate. tasyārūpyasamāpattilakṣaṇasya sabhāgahetor balīyastvād rūpadhātāv ārūpyasamāpattir utpadyate. evaṃ vijñānānantyāyatanasamāpatter [Tib. 360b] api parihīṇasyākāśānantyāyatanopapannasya tathaiva tatsamāpattīnām utpādanaṃ. evaṃ tadūrdhvopapannasya. karmabalāc ca. rūpadhātāv upapannasya aparaparyāyavedanīyasya karmaṇaḥ pratyupasthitavipākatvāt. tadvairāgyānukūlā saṃtatir avatiṣṭhate. na hy adhastād avītarāgeṇordhvam ārūpyadhātau śakyam upapattum iti. evam ārūpyeṣv ākāśānantyāyatanopapannasya karmabhalāt. ūrdhvabhūmikasya vijñānānantyāyatanabhūmikasyāparaparyāyavedanīyasya karmaṇaḥ pratyupasthitavipākatvāt. tadvairāgyānukūlā saṃtatir avatiṣṭhate. na hy adhastād avītarāgeṇordhvaṃ śakyam upapattum iti. etābhyāṃ ca hetukarmabalābhyāṃ. kathaṃ prathamādiṣu dhyāneṣu dvitīyādidhyānotpādanaṃ. hetubalāc cāsannābhīkṣṇābhyāsāt. karmabalāc cordhvabhūmikasyeti vistareṇa yojyaṃ. dharmatayāpi ceti. kathaṃ dharmatā nāma. kecit tāvat sautrāntikā āhuḥ. eṣām eva dharmāṇām udbhūtavṛttīnāṃ pūrvadhyānavāsanādhipatyāt tadutpattāv upadeśam antareṇa dhyānotpattāv ānuguṇyaṃ dharmatā prakṛtiḥ svabhāva ity arthaḥ. vaibhāṣikā api kecid āhuḥ. paurvajānmanikāt sabhāgahetoḥ niṣyandaphalaṃ dhyānotpādanaṃ. tadupadeśam antareṇānyato dharmateti. [Tib. 361a] kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām udbhūtavṛttitvād iti. tatra saṃvartanīkāle kuśalānāṃ karmapathānām ity arthaḥ. vṛttis teṣām eva dharmāṇāṃ yat kāritram. udbhūtā utkṛṣṭā vṛttir eṣām ity udbhūtavṛttayaḥ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. etad uktaṃ bhavati. teṣāṃ kuśalānāṃ prakarṣeṇātmalābhāt tadutpattyānuguṇyenātmalābhāt tadupadeśam antareṇānyataḥ pūrvadhyānavāsanāyāṃ satyāṃ dhyānotpattir iti.
body.translated_text: enters a formless attainment and then regresses from it and is reborn in the Form Realm, because of the predominance of the homogeneous cause characterized by that formless attainment, the formless attainment arises in the Form Realm. Similarly, for one who has regressed from the attainment of the Infinity of Consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>) and is reborn in the Infinity of Space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), the production of those attainments occurs in the same way. Similarly for one reborn above that. 'And through the power of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmabala</s>)' — for one reborn in the Form Realm, because the retribution of a <s>karma</s> to be experienced in a subsequent life (<s>aparaparyāyavedanīya</s>) has become imminent, a mental stream conducive to dispassion from that [lower ground] persists. For it is impossible to be reborn upward in the Formless Realm without being dispassioned from the lower [ground]. Similarly, in the formless [realms], for one reborn in the Infinity of Space, because of <s>karma</s>-power — because the retribution of a <s>karma</s> to be experienced in a subsequent life, belonging to a higher ground, namely the ground of the Infinity of Consciousness, has become imminent — a mental stream conducive to dispassion from that [lower ground] persists. For it is impossible to be reborn upward without being dispassioned from the lower [ground]. And through these two — the power of cause and the power of <s>karma</s> — how does the production of the second and other <s>dhyāna</s>s occur in the first and other <s>dhyāna</s>s? Through the power of cause, from proximate and repeated practice; and through the power of <s>karma</s>, of a higher ground — this should be connected in detail. 'And through natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) as well' — what is this natural law? First, certain <s>Sautrāntika</s>s say: because of the predominance of the predisposition (<s>vāsanā</s>) of prior <s>dhyāna</s> [practice] upon these very <s>dharma</s>s whose activity has become manifest, the fitness for the arising of <s>dhyāna</s> without instruction — [this] natural law, nature, essential character — that is the meaning. Certain <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s also say: the production of <s>dhyāna</s> as an outflow-result (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>) from a homogeneous cause belonging to a former birth — that, without instruction, from another [source], is natural law. 'Because of the manifest activity of wholesome <s>dharma</s>s' — there, at the time of the cosmic evolution (<s>saṃvartanī</s>), of the wholesome paths of action — that is the meaning. The activity of those very <s>dharma</s>s is their function. Manifest means excellent activity — [those dharmas] whose activity is manifest are called 'of manifest activity.' The state of that. Therefore. This is what is stated: because of the excellent self-acquisition of those wholesome [dharmas], because of the self-acquisition that is conducive to their arising, without instruction, from another [source], when the predisposition of prior <s>dhyāna</s> exists, the arising of <s>dhyāna</s> [occurs].

body.text: (VIII.39) ima īdṛśā dharmāṇāṃ prakārā iti. sāsravānāsravāṇāṃ dharmānāṃ dhātubhūmyālaṃbanākārādiprakārā yathāyogam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: (VIII.39) 'These are such categories of <s>dharma</s>s' — the categories of contaminated and uncontaminated <s>dharma</s>s such as realm, ground, object-domain, aspect, and so forth, as applicable — that is the meaning.

children.text: dhātāras tasya vaktāraḥ pratipattāra eva ceti.
children.translated_text: 'The bearers of that are its speakers and its practitioners as well' —

body.text: tasyāgamādhigamātmakasya saddharmasya yathāsaṃkhyam āgamasya ye vaktāraḥ. te 'sya dhātāraḥ. adhigamasya ca ye pratipattāraḥ. te 'sya dhātāra iti. adhigamasyaivam iti. varṣasahasram avasthānam iti. āgamasya tu bhūyāṃsaṃ kālam iti. varṣasahasrād ūrdhvam apīty arthaḥ. eṣa eva pakṣo yukta iti paśyāmaḥ.
body.translated_text: of that <s>saddharma</s> (true <s>dharma</s>) whose nature is scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and realization (<s>adhigama</s>), respectively: those who are speakers of the scripture are its bearers. And those who are practitioners of the realization are its bearers. 'Of the realization, thus' — its duration is a thousand years. 'But of the scripture, for a longer period' — meaning: even beyond a thousand years. 'We consider this very position to be correct.'

body.text: (VIII.40) yo 'yam iti vistaraḥ. yo 'yam ihābhidharmakośalakṣaṇe 'bhidharma
body.translated_text: (VIII.40) 'This which' — thus in detail. 'This which here has been taught as having the character of the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>' — the <s>Abhidharma</s>

body.text: uktaḥ. kim. eṣa eva śāstro 'bhidharmo Jñānaprasthānādilakṣaṇo deśitaḥ ata idam ucyate.
body.translated_text: has been taught. What [is the question]? Is this alone the <s>Abhidharma</s> as the treatise (<s>śāstra</s>), having the character of the <s>Jñānaprasthāna</s> and the rest, that was taught? Therefore this is stated.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. kaśmīre [Tib. 361b] bhavāḥ kāśmīrāḥ. vibhāṣayā dīvyanti vaibhāṣikā iti vyākhyātam etat. santi kāśmīrā na vaibhāṣikāḥ. ye vinayavidādayaḥ sautrāntikā bhadantādayaḥ. santi vaibhāṣikā na kāśmīrāḥ. ye bahirdeśakā vaibhāṣikā ity ubhayaviśeṣaṇaṃ. teṣāṃ nītyā yaḥ siddho 'bhidharmaḥ. sa prāyeṇeha mayā deśitaḥ. arthād uktaṃ bhavati. anyanītisiddho 'pi deśita iti
body.translated_text: — thus in detail. Those who dwell in <s>Kaśmīra</s> are <s>Kāśmīra</s>s. Those who excel in the <s>Vibhāṣā</s> are <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s — thus it has been explained. There are <s>Kāśmīra</s>s who are not <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s — those who are experts in <s>Vinaya</s> and the rest, the <s>Sautrāntika</s>s such as <s>Bhadanta</s> and others. There are <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s who are not <s>Kāśmīra</s>s — those who are <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s from outside regions. Hence the double qualification. The <s>Abhidharma</s> that is established by the method of those — that has been taught here by me for the most part. By implication, it is stated: that which is established by the method of others has also been taught.

body.text: kāśmīravaibhāṣikanayenānyanayena vā.
body.translated_text: — by the method of the <s>Kāśmīra</s> <s>Vaibhāṣika</s>s or by another method.

body.text: vacane
body.translated_text: — in this teaching,

body.text: 'smadaparādhaḥ. kiṃ kāraṇam ity āha.
body.translated_text: '— our fault.' What is the reason? He says:

children.translated_text: 'In the method of the <s>saddharma</s>, the <s>muni</s>s are the authority'

body.text: iti. saddharmasyāgamādhigamalakṣaṇasya nītau varṇane munayo buddhā bhagavanto buddhaputrāś cāryaśāradvatīputrādayaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvākārasarvadharmāvabodhe āptā ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: — in the method, the exposition, of the <s>saddharma</s> (true <s>dharma</s>) whose nature is scripture and realization, the <s>muni</s>s — the <s>Buddha</s>s, the Blessed Ones, and the sons of the <s>Buddha</s> such as the noble <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> and others — are the authority, meaning they are trustworthy (<s>āpta</s>) in the comprehension of all <s>dharma</s>s in all aspects.

body.text: (VIII.41-43) nimīlite śāstari lokacakṣuṣīti.
body.translated_text: (VIII.41-43) 'When the Teacher, the eye of the world, has closed his eyes' —

body.text: parinirvṛte bhagavati lokasya cakṣurbhūte mārgāmārgasaṃdarśake. anenāndhabhūtatāṃ lokasya darśayati.
body.translated_text: when the Blessed One, who is the eye of the world, the one who shows the path and the non-path, has attained final <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>parinirvṛta</s>). By this, he shows that the world has become blind.

children.translated_text: 'And when the witness-folk have mostly gone to destruction' —

body.text: sākṣāddraṣṭari sākṣī mārgāmārgajño bhagavān iti yo 'dhigatatattvo bhagavataḥ sākṣijanaḥ sahāyabhūtaḥ. tasmin parinirvāṇe kṣīṇe. [Tib. 362a] avidyāndhen-
body.translated_text: a witness is one who sees directly — meaning the Blessed One, the knower of path and non-path, is the one who has realized the truth. The witness-folk of the Blessed One are those who serve as his companions. When they have perished, gone to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

children.translated_text: 'By those blinded by ignorance,' 'who have not seen the truth,' 'who are unrestrained,'

body.text: niraṃkuśaiḥ
body.translated_text: 'unbridled,'

body.text: dṛṣṭikatayā
body.translated_text: '— through adherence to views,'

body.text: āpannair bhavadhir bhagavataḥ
body.translated_text: 'the teaching of the Blessed One has been'

body.text: granthataś cārthataś c'
body.translated_text: 'both in letter and in meaning'

children.translated_text: 'For when the Self-arisen One has gone to supreme peace'

body.text: ityādi pūrvaślokoktasyārthasya heturūpo 'yaṃ dvitīyaḥ śloka upanyasyate. buddhabuddhaputreṣu hi
body.translated_text: — and so forth. This second verse is presented as having the character of a reason for what was stated in the previous verse. For when the <s>Buddha</s>s and the sons of the <s>Buddha</s>

children.translated_text: in the world that is without a protector,

body.text: śāsanāntardhānahetubhiḥ. dṛṣṭyādibhir
body.translated_text: by the causes of the disappearance of the teaching — by views and the rest,

body.text: doṣair
body.translated_text: by faults,

body.text: yatheccham
body.translated_text: 'as they please,'

body.text: loke.
body.translated_text: — in the world,

body.text: saṃprati
body.translated_text: — at present,

body.text: bhāvasādhanam etat. tataś ca
body.translated_text: This is a statement of what is the case (<s>bhāvasādhana</s>). And therefore:

body.text: kaṇṭhagataprāṇam ivety arthaḥ. tad
body.translated_text: — meaning: as if with life-breath at the throat. That

children.translated_text: 'having understood the strength and the time of the defilements'

body.text: dośāṇāṃ viditvā
body.translated_text: — having understood [the strength and time] of the faults,

children.translated_text: 'those who desire liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) should not be negligent'

body.text: iti bhāvasādhanam iti.
body.translated_text: — this is a statement of what is the case (<s>bhāvasādhana</s>).

body.text: blank
body.translated_text: [blank]

body.text: IX (pudgalaviniścayaḥ)
body.translated_text: IX (<s>Pudgalaviniścaya</s> — Determination of Persons)

body.text: kiṃ khalv ato 'nyatra mokṣo nāstīti.
body.translated_text: 'Is there then no liberation elsewhere [than in this teaching]?'

children.translated_text: 'Those who desire liberation should not be negligent'

body.text: iti vacanād ayam eva mokṣopāyaḥ. nāsty ato 'nyo mokṣopāyaḥ. tad atra moktukāmaiḥ pramādo na kartavya ity arthād uktam ācāryena. codakaḥ pṛcchati. kiṃ khalv ata iti vistaraḥ. atrocyate. nāstīti. kiṃ kāraṇam ity āha. vitathātmadṛṣṭiniviṣṭatvād iti. vitathāyām ātmadṛṣṭau niviṣṭāḥ kutīrthyā vitathātma [Tib. 362b] dṛṣṭiniviṣṭāḥ. tadbhāvaḥ. tasmāt. nāsty anyatra mokṣa iti. stotrakāreṇāpy eṣo 'rtha uktaḥ.
body.translated_text: — from this statement, this alone is the means to liberation. There is no other means to liberation. Therefore, those who desire to be liberated should not be negligent in this — that is what the <s>Ācārya</s> has stated by implication. The objector asks: 'Is there then [no liberation] from this?' — thus in detail. Here it is answered: there is not. What is the reason? He says: 'Because of being attached to a false view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>).' Those non-Buddhist teachers (<s>kutīrthya</s>s) who are attached to a false view of self — attached to a false self-view, are said to be 'attached to a false self-view.' The state of that. Therefore. There is no liberation elsewhere — this [is the meaning]. The author of the hymn (<s>stotrakāra</s>) has also stated this meaning:

children.text:
sāhaṃkāre manasi na śamaṃ yāti janmaprabandho
nāhaṃkāraś calati hṛdayād ātmadṛṣṭau ca satyāṃ.
anyaḥ śāstā jagati ca yato nāsti nairātmyavādī
nānyas tasmād upaśamavidhes tvanmatād asti mārga
children.translated_text:
'In a mind that has the notion of "I" (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), the continuum of births does not come to rest;
nor does the notion of "I" depart from the heart when the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) persists.
Since there is no other teacher in the world who teaches selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>),
therefore there is no path to pacification other than your doctrine.'

body.text: iti. sādhanaṃ cātra. nāsti kapilolūkādīnāṃ mokṣaḥ. vitathātmadṛṣṭiniviṣṭatvāt. adṛṣṭatattvapuruṣavat. ātmagrāhaprabhavāś ca kleśāḥ iti yathoktaṃ. yāni vā punar ihaikatyānāṃ śramaṇabrāhmaṇānāṃ pṛthag loke dṛṣṭigatāni satkāyadṛṣṭimūlakāni tānīti vistaraḥ. ātmadṛṣṭau ca satyām ātmasnehādayaḥ kleśāḥ pravartante. skaṃdhasaṃtāna evedam ātmābhidhānam iti. ātmety abhidhānam ātmaprajñaptir ity arthaḥ. nānyasminn abhidheye skaṃdhasaṃtānavyatirikte kalpita ity arthaḥ. kasmād evam ity āha. pratyakṣānumānābhāvād iti. pratyakṣasyānumānasya cābhāvān na tasyāstitvam ity abhiprāyaḥ. āgamasyānumānāntarbhāvād apṛthagvacanaṃ. teṣāṃ pratyakṣam upalabdhir iti. [Tib. 363a] pratyakṣam ity upalabdhiviśeṣaṇaṃ. pratyakṣaṃ tadupalabdhiḥ pratyakṣata upalabdhir ity arthaḥ. atha vā pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam upalabdhir upalabhyate 'nayety upalabdhiḥ. asaty aṃtarāya iti. asaty upalabdhivighne 'tisaṃnikarṣātiviprakarṣādike teṣāṃ. ṣaṇṇāṃ viṣayāṇām iti. rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāyatanānāṃ
body.translated_text: Thus. And the proof here is: there is no liberation for <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Ulūka</s>, and the others — because of being attached to false views of self. Like a person who has not seen the truth. And afflictions arise from the grasping of self — as stated: "Whatever views of the various <s>śramaṇa</s>s and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s here in the world — those are rooted in the view of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>)" — in detail. And when the view of self exists, afflictions such as self-attachment and the rest operate. "This designation of self applies only to the continuum of aggregates" — the designation "self" (<s>ātman</s>) means the conceptual designation of self — this is the meaning. It is not fabricated with reference to any other referent distinct from the continuum of aggregates — this is the meaning. Why is this so? He says: "Because of the absence of direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>)" — the intent is: because of the absence of direct perception and inference, its existence [cannot be established]. Because scripture (<s>āgama</s>) is subsumed under inference, it is not separately mentioned. "The direct perception of those is apprehension" — [Tib. 363a] "direct" (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is a qualifier of "apprehension" (<s>upalabdhi</s>). Direct apprehension means apprehension that is direct — this is the meaning. Alternatively, "direct perception" is the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>); "apprehension" is that by which something is apprehended — hence apprehension. "In the absence of obstruction" — in the absence of obstruction to apprehension, such as excessive proximity, excessive distance, and the like. "Of the six objects" — of the sense-fields of form, sound, smell, taste, tangible [objects],

body.text: dharmāyatanasya ca vedanādilakṣaṇasya yogiviṣayasya cāgamavikalpātītasyeti. manasaś ca. kiṃ. pratyakṣam upalabdhiḥ. samanantaraniruddhaṃ hi mano 'nantarotpannena manovijñānena vijñāyate. raktaṃ vā dviṣṭaṃ vā sukhasaṃprayuktaṃ vā duḥkhasaṃprayuktaṃ vā ity evamādi svasaṃvedyatayety apare. tad etad dvividhaṃ pratyakṣaṃ grāhyagataṃ grāhakagataṃ ceti. anumānaṃ ceti vistaraḥ. yatra pratyakṣasyāpravṛttiḥ. tatrānumānatas tadupalabdhiḥ. tadyathā paṃcānām iṃdriyāṇām iti. cakṣuriṃdriyādīnāṃ. sati kāraṇe kṣetrodakādike. kāraṇāntarasya bījalakṣaṇasyābhāve kāryasyāṃkurākhyasyābhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ. bhāve ca tasya bījasya punarbhavo 'ṃkurasya dṛṣṭaḥ. tadyathāṃkurasyeti dṛṣṭāṃtopanyāsaḥ. evaṃ dṛṣṭāntam upanyasya dārṣṭāṃtikam upadarśayann āha. saty eva vābhāsaprāpta iti vistaraḥ. vidyamāna eva saṃmukhīprāpte viṣaye rūpādike manaskāre ca tajje kāraṇe. viṣayagrahaṇasya cakṣurādivijñānasyābhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ. punaś ca bhāvaḥ. keṣām iti [Tib. 363b] yathāsaṃkhyaṃ darśayati. andhabadhirādīnām abhāvaḥ. anandhabadhirādīnaṃ ca bhāva iti. ādiśabdenopahatānupahataghrāṇendriyādīnāṃ grahaṇam. atas tatrāpi kāraṇāṃtarasya kasyāpi anirbhinnarūpasyābhāvo bhāvaś ca yathāsaṃkhyam eva niścīyate. kiṃ punas tad ity āha. yac ca tat kāraṇāntaram apekṣyate. tad indriyaṃ. cakṣurādikam ity abhiprāyaḥ. sādhanaṃ cātra. kāraṇāntarasahitaḥ svakāryajanakaḥ. paṃcavijñānakāyajanakasaṃmato viṣayamanaskāralakṣaṇo bhāvaḥ. kadācid eva svakāryanirvartakatvāt. kadācid eva svakāryanirvartakaṃ. tat kāraṇāṃtarasahitasvakāryajanakaṃ. tadyathāṃkurajanakaṃ kṣetrodakaṃ. bījalakṣaṇakāraṇāntarasahitasvakāryāntarajanakaṃ hi kṣetrodakaṃ kadācid eva svakāryanirvartakaṃ. bījasadbhāvāvasthāyām aṃkuranirvartakatvāt. bījasadbhāvāvasthāyāṃ ca svakāryajanakatvāt. tathā ca sa viṣayamanaskāralakṣaṇo bhāvaḥ. sa hy anaṃdhābadhirādyāvasthāyāṃ tasya paṃcavijñānakāyalakṣaṇasya svakāryasya janako bhavati. andhabadhirādyāvasthāyāṃ cājanakaḥ. tasmād asau kāraṇāntarasahitaḥ svakāryajanaka iti. tad indriyam iti. kathaṃ tad indriyam iti paricchidyate. kāraṇāṃtaram atrāstīty etāvad eva hi paricchidyate. na tu tad indriyam iti. [Tib. 364a] siddham evaitat. maharṣipraṇidhijñānaparicchinnatvād asty eva cakṣurādikaṃ indriyaṃ cakṣurvijñānādikāraṇam iti. sarveṣām avivādāc ca. na caivam ātmato 'stīti nāsty ātmeti nigamayati. uktaṃ hy evam arthataḥ sādhanaṃ. nāsty ātmā. pramāṇenānupalabhyamānatvāt. atyantābhāvavad iti. asty anumānam. ato
body.translated_text: and also of the <s>dharmāyatana</s> (mental object sense-field) characterized by feeling and the rest, and of what is the domain of yogins and beyond ordinary conceptualization and scripture. "And of mind" — what [about it]? Direct apprehension. For the mind that has just ceased is cognized by the <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness) that arises immediately after — whether it was desirous, hateful, associated with happiness, or associated with suffering — and so forth. "Through self-awareness" — according to others. Thus, this twofold direct perception pertains to the apprehended and the apprehender. "And inference" — in detail. Where direct perception does not operate, there, through inference, the apprehension of that [object occurs]. For example, of the five faculties — the eye-faculty and the rest. When the cause — the field, water, and the rest — exists, but a different causal factor characterized by a seed is absent, the absence of the effect called a sprout is observed. And when that seed exists, the re-arising of the sprout is observed. "Just as of a sprout" — this is the introduction of the example. Having introduced the example, showing the exemplified, he says: "When the [object] is present and within the range of appearance" — in detail. When the object — form and the rest — actually exists and is within range, and when attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), the [other] causal factor, [exists] — the absence of apprehension of the object, that is, eye-consciousness and the rest, is observed. And also its [re-]arising. For whom? — [Tib. 363b] he shows in due order. The absence [is observed] for the blind, deaf, and the rest. And the arising for the non-blind, non-deaf, and the rest. By the word "and the rest" (<s>ādi</s>), those with impaired and unimpaired olfactory faculties and the rest are included. Therefore, in that case too, the absence and presence of some other causal factor of unmanifest form is ascertained in due order. What, then, is that? He says: and that other causal factor that is required — that is the faculty (<s>indriya</s>). The intent is: the eye and the rest. And the proof here is: a thing characterized by the object and attention that, together with another causal factor, produces its own effect — that is accepted as producing the five types of consciousness — and sometimes alone produces its own effect. That which sometimes alone produces its own effect — that [thing], together with another causal factor, produces its own effect. Just as the field and water that produce a sprout — for the field and water, together with another causal factor characterized by a seed, produce their own additional effect, and sometimes alone produce their own effect — in the presence of the seed they produce a sprout, and in the presence of the seed they produce their own effect. Similarly, that entity characterized by the object and attention — for in the state of non-blindness, non-deafness, and the rest, it produces its own effect characterized by the five types of consciousness. And in the state of blindness, deafness, and the rest, it does not produce [them]. Therefore, that [entity] produces its own effect together with another causal factor. That is the faculty. How is it determined that that is a faculty? "Only this much is determined: there is another causal factor here" — [Tib. 364a] but not that it is a faculty. "This is already established" — because it has been ascertained through the resolutional knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>) of the Great Sage — the eye-faculty and the rest do indeed exist as causes of eye-consciousness and the rest. "And because of the agreement of all" — and not thus regarding the self — therefore "there is no self" — he concludes. For the proof has been stated thus in substance: there is no self — because of not being apprehended by any means of valid knowledge — like what is utterly non-existent. "There is inference" — therefore

body.text: siddho hetur iti cet. na. tasyābhidheyatvāt. yadi hi tad asti. tad ucyatāṃ. na vānmātreṇāsiddho 'yaṃ hetur iti pratyavasthātavyam iti.
body.translated_text: the reason is established — if so [one objects]. No. Because that [self] is what is to be referred to. If it indeed exists, then let it be stated. One should not counter [the argument] by the mere [claim] "this reason is not established."

body.text: yat tarhi vātsīputrīyā iti vistaraḥ. vātsīputrīyā aryasāṃmatīyāḥ. anena vitathātmadṛṣṭiniviṣṭalakṣaṇo hetur anaikāṃtika iti darśayati. na hi vātsīputrīyāṇāṃ mokṣo neṣyate. bauddhatvāt. atha vā prākpakṣavirodhasāpakṣālo 'yaṃ pakṣo nāsty ātmety anena darśayati. svapakṣo hi vātsīputrīyo nikāya iti. vicāryaṃ tāvad etad iti. tannikāye prajñaptisatpudgala ity adoṣa eṣa ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: "But what about the <s>Vātsīputrīya</s>s" — in detail. The <s>Vātsīputrīya</s>s are the <s>Āryasāṃmitīya</s>s. By this he shows that the reason characterized by "being attached to false views of self" is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). For it is not the case that liberation is not accepted for the <s>Vātsīputrīya</s>s — because they are Buddhists. Alternatively, by this he shows a same-side example for the opponent's thesis "there is no self." For the <s>Vātsīputrīya</s> school is one's own school. "This should first be examined" — the intent is: in that school, the person (<s>pudgala</s>) is conceptually designated (<s>prajñaptisat</s>), and therefore there is no fault.

body.text: kiṃ vedaṃ dravyata iti kiṃ vā prajñaptita iti codita acārya āha. rūpādivad bhāvāntaraṃ ced dravyataḥ. yadi yathā rūpādiḥ śabdāder bhāvāntaram abhiprīyate. dravyataḥ pudgala ity upagato bhavati. [Tib. 364b] bhinnalakṣaṇaṃ rūpaṃ śabdād ityādi. kṣīrādivat samudāyaś cet prajñaptitaḥ. yathā kṣīragṛhasenādikaṃ rūparasagaṃdhaspraṣṭavyebhyaḥ. tṛṇakāṣṭheṣṭīkādibhyaḥ hastyaśvarathādibhyaś ca na bhāvāntaram iṣyate. kiṃ tarhi. teṣām eva samudāyamātram ity evaṃ cet. prajñaptitaḥ pudgala ity upagato bhavati. na hi rūpādibhyas ṭṛṇādibhyo hastyādibhyo vā kṣīragṛhaseneti vā kaścid bhāvo 'sti. kiṃ cātaḥ kaś cāto doṣa ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: Being challenged — "Is this [person] substantial (<s>dravyatas</s>) or conceptually designated (<s>prajñaptitas</s>)?" — the <s>Ācārya</s> says: "If it is a different entity from form and the rest, it is substantial" — if, just as form is accepted as a different entity from sound and the rest, the person (<s>pudgala</s>) is accepted as substantial — [Tib. 364b] form having a distinct characteristic from sound, and so forth. "If a composite like milk and the rest, it is conceptually designated" — just as milk, a house, an army, and the like are not accepted as entities different from form, taste, smell, tangible [objects], or from grass, wood, bricks, and the like, or from elephants, horses, chariots, and the like — rather, they are merely composites of those — if so, then the person is accepted as conceptually designated. For there is no entity whatsoever — milk, house, army — that exists apart from form and the rest, grass and the rest, or elephants and the rest. "And what of that? What fault follows from that?" — this is the meaning.

body.text: yadi tāvad dravyata iti pakṣaḥ āśrīyate. sa pudgalo bhinnasvabhāvatvāt bhinnasvalakṣaṇatvāt skaṃdhebhyo 'nyo vaktavyaḥ. na skandhasamudāyamātraḥ. itaretaraskaṃdhavat. yathā rūpādiskandhād vedanāskandho 'nyo bhinnalakṣaṇatvāt. evaṃ skaṃdhebhyaḥ pudgalaḥ syāt. arūpaskandhādilakṣaṇatvāt pudgalasya. kāraṇaṃ cāsya vaktavyaṃ. yadi saṃskṛta ity abhiprāyaḥ. asaṃskṛto vā. atas tīrthikadṛṣṭiprasaṃgaḥ. ato 'saṃkṛtatvāt vātsīputrīyāṇāṃ tīrthikadṛṣṭiḥ prasajyate. niḥprayojanatvaṃ ceti.
body.translated_text: "If, to begin with, the thesis of substantiality is adopted" — that person, because of having a different intrinsic nature, because of having a different own-characteristic, would have to be declared as other than the aggregates — not a mere composite of aggregates. Like each aggregate [being different] from another. Just as the feeling aggregate is other than the form aggregate and the rest because of having a different characteristic — so too the person would be [other] than the aggregates — because of having a characteristic different from the non-form aggregates and the rest. And its cause must be stated — the intent is: whether it is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). Or unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). Therefore, the consequence of a non-Buddhist view follows — because of being unconditioned, the <s>Vātsīputrīya</s>s' view becomes equivalent to a non-Buddhist (<s>tīrthika</s>) view. And there is purposelessness.

children.text:
varṣātapābhyāṃ kiṃ vyomnaś carmaṇy asti tayoḥ [Tib. 365a] phalaṃ.
carmopamaś cet so 'nityaḥ. khatulyaś ced asat phalam
children.translated_text:
"What can rain and sun do to space? In leather, those two have their effect.
If like leather, it is impermanent; if equal to space, the effect is non-existent" —

body.text: ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: this is the meaning.

body.text: idam andhavaṃcanam anunmīlitārtham iti. andham ivāndhaṃ. kasmāt. yasmād anunmīlitārthaṃ avyaṃjitārtham ity arthaḥ. [ity ataḥ] skaṃdhān ālaṃbyeti gṛhītvety arthaḥ. yathā rūpādīn gṛhītvāpekṣya kṣīraprajñaptiḥ. na rūpādivyatiriktaṃ kṣīram astīti. yadi tathā pudgala iti prajñaptir asatpudgalaḥ prāpnotīty arthaḥ. skaṃdhān pratītyeti. yadi skaṃdhān pratītya prāpyeti. sa eva doṣaḥ. teṣv eva skaṃdheṣu pudgalaprajñaptiḥ prāpnotīty arthaḥ atha vā
body.translated_text: "This is a deception of the blind, an unexplained meaning" — blind-like, [as if deceiving] the blind. Why? Because the meaning is unexplained, unelucidated — this is the meaning. [Therefore,] "Having grasped" — the meaning is: having taken — the aggregates. Just as, having taken — that is, in dependence on — form and the rest, the designation "milk" [is made] — there is no milk that exists apart from form and the rest. If the person is designated in the same way, then the person is non-existent — this is the meaning. "In dependence on the aggregates" — if in dependence on, that is, having obtained, the aggregates — the same fault [applies]. The designation "person" applies to those very aggregates — this is the meaning. Alternatively,

body.text: pudgalaprajñapteḥ skaṃdhāḥ pratyayo na pudgalaḥ. pudgalas tu tathaiva prajñaptisann iti. sa eva doṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: the aggregates are the condition of the person-designation, not the person [itself]. The person, however, exists as merely conceptually designated — just so. The same fault [applies].

body.text: yathendhanam upādāyāgniḥ prajñapyata iti. dravyasan pudgalaḥ.
body.translated_text: "Just as fire is designated in dependence on fuel" — therefore the person exists as a substance (<s>dravyasat</s>).

body.text: nānyo nānanya iti. svam upādānam upādāya prajñapyamānatvāt. yo hi bhāvo nānyo nānanya iti svam upādāya prajñapyamānaḥ. sa dravyasaṃs tadyathāgnir iti vātsīputrīyābhiprāyaḥ. ata eva cāha. yadi hy anyaḥ syād iti vistareṇa. lokavirodhaṃ svasiddhāntavirodhaṃ vā darśayati. śāśvataprasaṃgāt ti. asaṃskṛtavat. ucchedaprasaṃgād [Tib. 365b] iti. skaṃdhavat.
body.translated_text: "Neither the same nor different" — because of being designated in dependence on its own substratum (<s>upādāna</s>). The <s>Vātsīputrīya</s> intent is: whatever entity is designated in dependence on its own substratum as neither the same nor different — that exists as a substance, just like fire. For this very reason he says: "If it were different" — in detail. He shows the contradiction with the world or the contradiction with one's own doctrine. "Because of the consequence of eternalism" — like the unconditioned. "Because of the consequence of annihilationism" — [Tib. 365b] like the aggregates.

body.text: apradīptaṃ kāṣṭhādikam indhanam iti vistaraḥ. anenāsiddhatāṃ dṛṣṭāntasya darśayati. anyatvam eva hy agnīndhanayor iṣyate. tena hi tad idhyate dahyate ceti. tenāgninā. tad indhanam idhyate. dīpyata ity arthaḥ. dahyate bhasmīkriyate. saṃtativikārāpādanāt. bhasmatāpādanād ity arthaḥ. idhyate dahyate ceti paryāyāv ity apare. tac cobhayam aṣṭadravyakam iti. indhanaṃ cāgniś caitad ubhayam apy aṣṭadravyakaṃ. cetvāri mahābhūtāni catvāri copādāyarūpāṇi rūpaṃ yāvat spraṣṭavyam iti.
body.translated_text: "Unburning wood and the like is fuel" — in detail. By this he shows the unestablished nature of the example. For it is the otherness of fire and fuel that is accepted. By that — by that fire — that [fuel] is kindled and burned. "Kindled" means: it shines — this is the meaning. "Burned" means: it is reduced to ashes. Because of being brought to a change of continuity — the meaning is: because of being reduced to the state of ashes. "Kindled and burned are synonyms" — according to others. "And both are of eight substances" — fuel and fire — both of these are of eight substances: the four great elements and the four derivative material [properties] — form, up to tangible [objects].

children.translated_text: "In the Desire Realm, of eight substances, without sound" —

body.text: iti siddhāntāt.
body.translated_text: from this established doctrine.

body.text: bhinnakālatvād iti. pūrvam indhanaṃ paścād agniḥ. bhinnakālayoś cānyatvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bījāṃkurayoḥ. anityaś ca prāpnotīti. utpattimato rūpāder anityatvadarśanāt. tatraiva kāṣṭhādau pradīpta iti. tadubhayalakṣaṇe samudāye. tayor api siddham anyatvaṃ lakṣaṇabhedād iti. tayor apy agnīndhanayor evaṃlakṣaṇayoḥ siddham anyatvaṃ lakṣaṇabhedāt. pṛthivīdhātvādīnāṃ lakṣaṇānyatvāt. bhinnalakṣaṇānāṃ hy anyatvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ rūpavedanādīnāṃ. upādayārthas tu vaktavya iti. ananyatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. na hi tat tasya kāraṇam iti. [Tib. 366a] na hi tad indhanaṃ bhūtatrayalakṣaṇaṃ. tasyoṣṇalakṣaṇasyāgneḥ kāraṇaṃ yujyate. sahajatvāt. savyetaragoviṣāṇavat. nāpi tat prajñapter iti. agniprajñapteḥ. yady āśrayārtha iti. indhanam upādāya indhanam āśrityety arthaḥ. sahabhāvo 'rtho veti. sahotpādārthaḥ. indhanaṃ sahabhūtvenāgṛhyety arthaḥ. āśrayasahabhūtāḥ prāpnuvantīti. āśrayabhūtāḥ sahabhūtāś ca prāpnuvaṃtīty arthaḥ. skaṃdhataḥ spaṣṭam anyatvaṃ pratijñāyate vātsīputrīyaiḥ. tadabhāva iti. skaṃdhābhāve. anyabhūtasvabhāvatvād iti. pṛthivīdhātvādisvabhāvatvāt. anyad apīti na kevalam auṣṇyam uṣṇam. anyad api tatpradīptāgnisaṃbandhaṃ bhūmyādikam uṣṇaṃ sidhyati. ato yathā tasyānyatve na doṣaḥ. tathāsyapīti. tataś cāvaktavya iti. tatpakṣalopaḥ
body.translated_text: "Because of being at different times" — fuel comes first, fire after. And for things at different times, otherness is observed — like seed and sprout. "And it would be impermanent" — because of observing the impermanence of form and the rest that arise [and cease]. "In that very wood and the rest, when burning" — in the composite having the characteristics of both [fuel and fire]. "For those two also, otherness is established because of the difference of characteristics" — for those two — fire and fuel — having such characteristics, otherness is established because of the difference of characteristics. Because of the otherness of the characteristics of the earth element and the rest. For the otherness of things with different characteristics is observed — of form, feeling, and the rest. "But the meaning of "in dependence on" (<s>upādāya</s>) must be stated" — the intent is: because of non-otherness [of fire and fuel]. "For that is not its cause" — [Tib. 366a] for that fuel, characterized by the triad of elements [earth, water, wind], is not reasonably the cause of that fire, characterized by the heat element — because of being co-arisen. Like the right and left horns of a cow. "Nor is it for the designation" — of the designation of fire. "If the meaning is "basis"" — "in dependence on fuel" means "based on fuel" — this is the meaning. "Or the meaning is co-existence" — the meaning of co-arising. "Fuel is grasped as co-existent with fire" — this is the meaning. "The basis and the co-existent would follow" — the meaning is: those that are the basis and those that are co-existent would follow. "The otherness from the aggregates is clearly affirmed by the <s>Vātsīputrīya</s>s" — "in its absence" — in the absence of the aggregates. "Because of having the nature of a different entity" — because of having the nature of the earth element and the rest. "Something else too" — not only heat is hot — something else too, in contact with that burning fire — earth and the rest — becomes hot. Therefore, just as there is no fault in the otherness of that [earth etc. from fire], so too for this [person from aggregates]. "And from that, it would be indescribable" — then there would be the loss of that position

body.text: syāt. kāṣṭhādikam iti. kāṣṭhatṛṇagomayādikam.
body.translated_text: . "Wood and the rest" — wood, grass, cow-dung, and the like.

body.text: avaktavyam iti pudgalaḥ. anirbhinnatvān napuṃsakaliṃgatā. kiṃ te jātam iti yathā. na vaktavyaṃ prāpnotīti. paṃcavidhaṃ jñeyam iti kathaṃ tarhi vaktavyam ity āha. naiva hi tad atītādibhyaḥ paṃcamaṃ nāpaṃcamaṃ vaktavyam iti.
body.translated_text: 'Inexpressible' — this is the <s>pudgala</s> (person). Because of non-differentiation, it has neuter gender — like 'what was born to you?' It 'cannot be stated' — thus it follows. 'The knowable is fivefold' — then how is it to be stated? He says: 'It is neither to be stated as a fifth beyond the past and the rest, nor as a non-fifth.'

body.text: rūpasyāpīti vistaraḥ. rūpasyāpi prajñaptir vaktavyā. cakṣurādiṣu satsu tasyopalambhāt tāni cakṣurādīny upādāya rūpaṃ prajñapyata iti.
body.translated_text: 'Even of form' — in detail. The designation of form too must be stated. Because of its apprehension when the eye and the rest exist — dependent upon those [bases] such as the eye and the rest, form is designated.

body.text: prativibhāvayatīty upalakṣayati. [Tib. 366b] tadupādānatvāt. na tu vaktavyo rūpāṇi vā no veti. atallakṣaṇatvad avaktavyatvāc ca. evaṃ yāvad dharmo vā no veti.
body.translated_text: 'Discerns' means 'perceives.' [Tib. 366b] Because of being dependent on that. But one should not state whether it is forms or not — because of not having that characteristic, and because of being inexpressible. Similarly, up to: whether it is a <s>dharma</s> or not.

body.text: kṣīraṃ prativibhāvayaty udakaṃ ceti. udāharaṇadvayaṃ. tad evaṃ vaktavyaṃ. cakṣurvijñeyāni ced rūpāṇi pratītya kṣīraṃ prativibhāvayati cakṣurvijñeyaṃ kṣīraṃ vaktavyaṃ. no tu vaktavyaṃ. rūpāṇi vā no veti sarvaṃ. tathaitad api vaktavyaṃ. cakṣurvijñeyāni ced rūpāṇi pratītyodakaṃ prativibhāvayati. cakṣurvijñeyam udakaṃ vaktavyaṃ. no tu vaktavyaṃ. rūpāṇi vā no veti sarvaṃ. mā bhūt kṣīrodakayoś catuṣṭvaprasaṃga iti. rūpāṇīti yady ucyet. yāvat spraṣṭavyānīti yady ucyeta kṣīrasyodakasya vā catuṣṭvaṃ prasajyet. catuḥprakāraṃ kṣīram udakaṃ vā prāpnotīty arthaḥ. śabda āgaṃtukatvān nātrādhikṛtaḥ. ato yathā rūpādīny eva samastāni samuditāni kṣīram ity udakam iti vā prajñapyate. tathā skandhā eva samastāḥ pudgala iti prajñapyanta iti siddhaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'One discerns milk and water' — these are two examples. Thus it should be stated: if, dependent on forms cognizable by eye-consciousness, one discerns milk, then milk is to be stated as cognizable by eye-consciousness. But one should not state everything — whether it is forms or not. Likewise, this too should be stated: if, dependent on forms cognizable by eye-consciousness, one discerns water, then water is to be stated as cognizable by eye-consciousness. But one should not state everything — whether it is forms or not. 'Lest the fourfoldness of milk and water be entailed' — if one were to say 'forms,' up to: if one were to say 'tangibles' — then the fourfoldness of milk or water would be entailed. The meaning is: milk or water would become fourfold. Sound is not included here because of its adventitious nature. Therefore, just as all the forms and the rest together, combined, are designated as 'milk' or 'water' — so too the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>s) alone, together, are designated as '<s>pudgala</s>' (person) — this is established.

body.text: rūpāṇi pudgalopalabdheḥ kāraṇam iti rūpāṇy ualabhamānaḥ pudgalam upalabhata iti. ko 'nayoḥ pakṣayor viśeṣaḥ. [Tib. 367a] pūrvasmin pakṣe rūpāṇāṃ kāraṇatvam adhikriyate. dvitīye na tu kāraṇatvaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. rūpāṇy upādāya pudgalopalabdhir iti. tatra rūpāṇaṃ yadi kāraṇatvam iṣyate. sa ca pudgalas tebhyo rūpebhyo 'nyo na vaktavya iti. idaṃ tarhi vaḥ prasajyate. rūpam apīti vistaraḥ. yathā rūpāṇi pudgalopalabdheḥ kāraṇaṃ bhavanti sa ca tebhyo 'nyo na vaktavyaḥ. ālokacakṣurmanaskārā api rūpopalabdheḥ kāraṇaṃ bhavanti. tad api rūpaṃ tebhya ālokādibhyo 'nyan na vaktavyaṃ bhavadbhiḥ. teṣāṃ tadupalabdhikāraṇatvāt. teṣām ālokādīnāṃ rūpopalabdhikāraṇatvāt. rūpād abhinnasvabhāvaḥ pudgalaḥ prāpnoti. tayaivaikayopalabdhyopalabhyamānatvāt. rūpāntaravat. rūpa eva vā tatprajñaptiḥ. pudgalaprajñaptiḥ prāpnotīti
body.translated_text: 'Forms are the cause of the apprehension of the <s>pudgala</s>' — apprehending forms, one apprehends the <s>pudgala</s>. What is the difference between these two positions? [Tib. 367a] In the first position, the causal nature of forms is maintained. In the second, the causal nature is not [maintained]. What then? Dependent on forms, there is apprehension of the <s>pudgala</s>. Therein, if the causal nature of forms is accepted, and if that <s>pudgala</s> is not to be stated as other than those forms — then this consequence follows for you: 'even form' — in detail. Just as forms are the cause of the apprehension of the <s>pudgala</s>, and it is not to be stated as other than those — so too light, the eye, and attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) are the cause of the apprehension of form. That form too should not be stated by you as other than those — light and the rest — because of their being the cause of its apprehension. Because of those — light and the rest — being the cause of the apprehension of form. The <s>pudgala</s> would have an essence non-different from form — because of being apprehended by that one and the same apprehension. Like another form. Or the designation of the <s>pudgala</s> would be nothing but form itself

body.text: vartate. kutaḥ. tata eva hetoḥ. idaṃ ca rūpam iti vistaraḥ. upalabdher ekatve rūpapudgalayoḥ paricchedo na prāpnotīti. athaivaṃ na paricchidyate. idaṃ rūpam ayaṃ pudgala iti. katham ubhayaṃ pratijñāyate. rūpam eva hi pratijñātavyaṃ syāt. tadupalabdhisadbhāvāt. evaṃ yāvad dharmebhyo vaktavyam iti. kathaṃ. yac cocyate. śrotravijñeyān śabdān pratītya pudgalaṃ prativibhāvayatīti ko 'sya vākyasyārthaḥ kiṃ tāvac chabdaḥ pudgalopalabdheḥ [Tib. 367b] kāraṇaṃ bhavanti. āhosvic chabdān upalabhamānaḥ pudgalam upalabhata iti. yadi tāvac chabdāḥ pudgalopalabdheḥ kāraṇaṃ bhavanti. sa ca tebhyo 'nyo na vaktavyaḥ. evaṃ tarhi śabdo 'py ālokaśrotramanaskārebhyo 'nyo na vaktavyaḥ. teṣāṃ tadupalabdhikāraṇatvāt. atha śabdān upalabhamānaḥ pudgalam upalabhate. kiṃ tayaivopalabdhyopalabhate. āhosvid anyayā. yadi tayaiva śabdād abhinnasvabhāvaḥ pudgalaḥ prāpnoti. śabda eva vā tatprajñaptiḥ. ayaṃ ca śabdo 'yaṃ pudgala iti katham idaṃ paricchidyate. athaivaṃ na paricchidyate. katham idaṃ parijñāyate. śabdo 'py asti pudgalo 'py astīti. upalabdhivaśena hi tasyāstitvaṃ prajñāyate. anayā diśā yāvad dharmebhyo yojayitavyaṃ. nīlād iva pītam iti. yadā paricchedena nīlam upalabhyate. na tadā pītam upalabhyate. paścāt tūpalabhyata iti. anyayopalabdhyopalabhyate. tac ca nīlāt pītam anyad iti pratītaṃ. tathā ca pudgalo 'nyayopalabhyopalabhyata iti. rūpād anyaḥ prāpnoti. evaṃ kṣaṇād api kṣaṇāntaram anyad ity udāhāryam. evaṃ yāvad dharmebhyo vaktavyam iti. katham. athānyayā bhinnakālopalambhād anyaḥ śabdaḥ prāpnoti. yathā bherīśabdān mṛdāṃgaśabdaḥ. kṣaṇād iva ca kṣaṇāntaraṃ. yathāpūrvam uktaṃ. nīlād iva pītaṃ [Tib. 368a] kṣaṇād iva kṣaṇāntaram iti. bhinnalakṣaṇe viṣaye abhinnalakṣaṇe ca bhinnakālopalabdhyānyatvaṃ darśitam eva. athānyayeti vistareṇa yāvad dharmebhyo yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: — this follows. From what? From that very reason. 'And this form' — in detail. When the apprehension is one, the discrimination of form and <s>pudgala</s> is not possible. But if thus they are not discriminated — 'this is form, this is the <s>pudgala</s>' — how are both asserted? For only form should be asserted — because of the existence of its apprehension. 'Thus, up to <s>dharma</s>s it should be stated' — how? 'And what is said: "Dependent on sounds cognizable by ear-consciousness, one discerns the <s>pudgala</s>"' — what is the meaning of this statement? Are sounds, first of all, the cause of the apprehension of the <s>pudgala</s>, [Tib. 367b] or does one apprehend the <s>pudgala</s> while apprehending sounds? If, first, sounds are the cause of the apprehension of the <s>pudgala</s>, and it is not to be stated as other than those — then in that case, sound too should not be stated as other than light, the ear, and attention — because of their being the cause of its apprehension. But if one apprehends the <s>pudgala</s> while apprehending sounds — does one apprehend it by that very [same] apprehension, or by another? If by that very one, the <s>pudgala</s> would have an essence non-different from sound. Or the designation of the <s>pudgala</s> would be nothing but sound. And how is 'this is sound, this is the <s>pudgala</s>' discriminated? But if thus they are not discriminated, how is it known that 'sound exists and the <s>pudgala</s> too exists'? For its existence is known by virtue of apprehension. In this direction, one should apply [the argument] up to <s>dharma</s>s. 'Like blue from yellow' — when blue is apprehended by discrimination, yellow is not apprehended at that time. But it is apprehended afterwards — thus it is apprehended by another apprehension. And it is understood that yellow is other than blue. Similarly, the <s>pudgala</s> too is apprehended by another apprehension — thus it would be other than form. Similarly, even one moment from another moment should be cited as [being] other. 'Thus, up to <s>dharma</s>s it should be stated' — how? But if by another [apprehension] — because of apprehension at different times, sound would be other — like the sound of a drum from the sound of a <s>mṛdaṅga</s>. And one moment from another moment — as stated before. 'Like blue from yellow, [Tib. 368a] like one moment from another moment' — in the case of objects with different characteristics and objects with non-different characteristics, otherness through apprehension at different times has been shown. 'But if by another' — in detail, up to <s>dharma</s>s it should be applied.

body.text: āha rūpapudgalavad iti vistaraḥ. yathā rūpapudgalayor anyānanyatvam avaktavyam evaṃ tadupalabdhyor apy anyānanyatvam avaktavyam ity evaṃ yadi brūyāt. tena tarhi saṃskṛtam apy avaktavyaṃ bhavati tadupalabdhilakṣaṇaṃ saṃskṛtam apy etad avaktavyam iti. siddhāntabhedaḥ. yo 'yaṃ siddhāntaḥ pudgala evāvaktavya iti. ayaṃ bhidyate. saṃskṛtam apy avaktavyam iti kṛtvā. yadi cāyam iti vistaraḥ. yady evaṃ rūpāṇi no veti na vaktavyaḥ kiṃ tarhi etad bhagavatoktaṃ rūpam anātmeti. yāvad vijñānam anātmeti. evaṃ hi bruvato vaktavya eva pudgalo nāvaktavya iti darśitaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: He says: 'Like form and the <s>pudgala</s>' — in detail. Just as the otherness or non-otherness of form and the <s>pudgala</s> is inexpressible, so too the otherness or non-otherness of their apprehensions is inexpressible — if one were to say thus: then the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) too would be inexpressible — its apprehension-characteristic — even the conditioned would be inexpressible. A doctrinal breach (<s>siddhāntabheda</s>). The doctrine that 'the <s>pudgala</s> alone is inexpressible' — this is breached, by making the conditioned too inexpressible. 'But if this' — in detail. If it is not to be stated whether it is forms or not, then what about this statement of the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Form is non-self,' up to: 'Consciousness is non-self'? For by speaking thus, it is shown that the <s>pudgala</s> is indeed to be stated, not inexpressible.

body.text: śabdādivad iti. na rūpavijñānenopalabhyate pudgalaḥ. tadanālambanapratyayabhūtatvāt. śabdavat. ādiśabdenātra gandhavad rasavad ityādi yojyam. evaṃ śrotrādivijñānānupalabhyamānatvam asya [Tib. 368b] vaktavyam. eṣā hi dik. anena copanyāsena dharmiviśeṣaviparyayapratijñādoṣa udbhāvyata ity avagantavyaṃ. dvayaṃ pratītyeti. dvayaṃ pratītya na tu trayaṃ pratītyeti. ata idam utsūtram iti.
body.translated_text: 'Like sound and the rest' — the <s>pudgala</s> is not apprehended by form-consciousness (<s>rūpavijñāna</s>) — because of not being its object-condition (<s>ālambanapratyaya</s>). Like sound. By the word 'and the rest,' 'like smell, like taste' and so forth should be applied. Thus, its non-apprehension by ear-consciousness and the rest [Tib. 368b] should be stated. For this is the direction [of argument]. And by this demonstration, the fault of the thesis-contradiction regarding the specific property (<s>dharmiviśeṣaviparyayapratijñā</s>) is exposed — this should be understood. 'Dependent on two' — dependent on two, not dependent on three — therefore this contradicts the <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: cakṣur bhikṣo hetur iti vistaraḥ. hetur āsannaḥ pratyayaḥ. viprakṛṣṭas tu pratyaya eva. janako hetuḥ. pratyayas tv ālambanamātram ity apare. paryāyāv etāv ity apare.
body.translated_text: 'The eye, O <s>bhikṣu</s>, is a cause' — in detail. A cause (<s>hetu</s>) is a proximate condition. But a distant one is merely a condition (<s>pratyaya</s>). A generative one is a cause. But a condition is merely an object-support (<s>ālambana</s>) — say others. These two are synonyms — say yet others.

body.text: rūpād anyaḥ pudgala iti pakṣaprasaṃgaḥ. śrotravijñānavijñeyatvāc chabdavat. tathā śabdād anyaḥ pudgala iti pakṣaprasaṃgaḥ. cakṣurvijñānavijñeyatvād rūpavat. iti evam anyebhyo yojyam iti. rūpaśabdābhyām anyaḥ pudgala iti pakṣaprasaṃgaḥ. ghrāṇavijñeyatvāt. gandhavat. ity eṣā dig yojanaṃ pratīti. svakaṃ svakaṃ gocaraviṣayaṃ pratyanubhavantīti vacanāt pudgalena pratyanubhavantīty uktaṃ bhavati. manaś caiṣāṃ pratisaraṇam iti. anuṣaṃgenedam uktaṃ. nedam udāharaṇaṃ. tathāpi tu manaś caiṣām indriyāṇāṃ pratisaraṇam iti tadapekṣāṇīndriyāṇi vijñānotpattau [Tib. 369a] kāraṇaṃ bhavantīty arthaḥ. na vā pudgalo viṣaya iti. yadi sūtraṃ pramāṇīkriyate. tataḥ kim ity āha. na ced viṣayaḥ. yadi na kasyacid vijñānasya viṣaya na tarhi vijñeyaḥ. tataś ca paṃcavidhaṃ jñeyam iti svasiddhānto bādhyate.
body.translated_text: 'The <s>pudgala</s> is other than form' — this thesis-consequence [follows]. Because of being cognizable by ear-consciousness — like sound. Similarly, 'the <s>pudgala</s> is other than sound' — this thesis-consequence [follows]. Because of being cognizable by eye-consciousness — like form. Thus, it should be applied to the others. 'The <s>pudgala</s> is other than form and sound' — this thesis-consequence [follows]. Because of being cognizable by nose-consciousness — like smell. This is the direction; the application should follow. 'They experience their own respective object-domains' — because of the statement 'they experience their own respective object-domains,' it amounts to saying 'the <s>pudgala</s> experiences.' 'And the mind is their recourse' — this is stated by connection. This is not [meant as] an example. Nevertheless, 'the mind is the recourse of these faculties' — meaning the faculties are dependent on that, and the faculties become the cause of the arising of consciousness — this is the meaning. 'Or the <s>pudgala</s> is not [their] object' — if the <s>sūtra</s> is taken as authoritative. Then what? He says: 'If it is not an object' — if it is not the object of any consciousness, then it is not knowable. And in that case, one's own doctrine — 'the knowable is fivefold' — is contradicted.

body.text: yady evaṃ sūtre vacanān nānyad anyasya gocaraviṣayaṃ pratyanubhavatīti paṃcānāṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ pramāṇīkriyate. svaviṣayāvyabhicāraḥ. svaviṣayāvyabhicāre ca na cakṣurvijñānādibhir vijñeyaḥ pudgalaḥ. tad evaṃ sati manaindriyasyāpy avyabhicāraḥ prāpnoti. ṣaḍ imānīndriyāṇi nānāgocarāṇīti vistareṇa sūtre vacanāt. kukkurapakṣiśṛgālaśiśumārasarpamarkaṭāḥ ṣaṭprāṇakāḥ kenacid baddhā madhye granthiṃ kṛtvotsṛṣṭāḥ. te svakaṃ svakaṃ gocaraviṣayam ākāṃkṣante. grāmākāśāśmaśānodakāntavalmīkavanākāṃkṣaṇāt. evam eva ṣaḍ imānīndriyāṇi svakaṃ svakaṃ gocaraviṣayam ākāṃkṣante. ity evam upamātra kriyate. atha saty api sūtravacane manaindriyasya vyabhicāraḥ. evaṃ cakṣurādīnām apīndriyāṇāṃ vyabhicāraḥ. vyabhicāre ca cakṣurvijñānādibhir vijñeyaḥ pudgalo bhaviṣyatīti.
body.translated_text: If thus, because of the statement in the <s>sūtra</s> 'nothing other than its own object-domain does it experience,' the five [faculties] — the eye and the rest — are taken as authoritative — [meaning] their non-deviation from their own objects — and if, given the non-deviation from their own objects, the <s>pudgala</s> is not knowable by eye-consciousness and the rest, then given this, the non-deviation of the mind-faculty too would follow — because of the statement in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'These six faculties have different domains.' In detail, from the <s>sūtra</s>: 'A dog, a bird, a jackal, a <s>śiśumāra</s> (crocodile), a snake, and a monkey — six creatures bound together with a knot made in the middle and released. They each desire their own respective object-domain — desiring a village, sky, charnel-ground, water, ant-hill, and forest. Just so, these six faculties each desire their own respective object-domain.' Thus the simile is made. But if, despite the <s>sūtra</s> statement, there is deviation for the mind-faculty, then there is deviation for the eye and the rest as well. And given deviation, the <s>pudgala</s> would be knowable by eye-consciousness and the rest.

body.text: atra [Tib. 369b] brūmaḥ. na tatreti vistaraḥ. tatra ṣaṭprāṇakopame sūtre nendriyam eva cakṣurādikam indriyaṃ kṛtvoktaṃ. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. cakṣurādīnāṃ
body.translated_text: Here [Tib. 369b] we say: 'Not there' — in detail. In that <s>sūtra</s> of the six-creature simile, it is not the faculty itself — the faculty of the eye and the rest — that is taken [as subject]. For what reason? Because of the impossibility of the desire for seeing and the rest

body.text: paṃcānām indriyāṇāṃ darśanādyākāṃkṣaṇāsaṃbhavāt. yasmād eṣāṃ darśanaśravaṇādyākāṃkṣaṇaṃ na saṃbhavati rūpasvabhāvatvāt. tadvijñānānāṃ ca. cakṣurādivijñānānāṃ ca darśanādyākāṃkṣāsaṃbhavāt. kasmād eṣāṃ darśanaśravaṇādyākāṃkṣaṇaṃ na saṃbhavati. avikalpakatvāt. tadādhipatyādhyāhṛtaṃ tu manovijñānam indriyam ity uktam indriyam iveti kṛtvā. katham jñāyate tadādhipatyādhyāhṛtaṃ tad iti. yadi hi cakṣurādidvāreṇa cakṣurvijñānādi notpannaṃ syāt. katham anyathā vikalpakaṃ manovijñānam utpannaṃ syāt. ity ato jñāyate. tadādhipatyādhyāhṛtam iti. tan manovijñānaṃ cakṣurādīndriyabhūtaṃ svakaṃ svakaṃ gocaraviṣayaṃ rūpādikam ākāṃkṣatīti. yac ca tat kevalam iti vistaraḥ. naiva tadanyeṣāṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ viṣayam ākāṃkṣati yan mana-ādhipatyādhyāhṛtaṃ. kiṃ tarhi. svaviṣayam eva dharmāyatanam evālambata iti. ato nāsty eṣa doṣaḥ. yady evaṃ manaindriyasyāpy [Tib. 370a] avyabhicāraḥ prāpnotīti yad uktam iti.
body.translated_text: on the part of the five faculties of the eye and the rest — since their desire for seeing, hearing, and the rest is impossible, because of their being of the nature of form. And [also because of the impossibility] on the part of their consciousnesses — because of the impossibility of the desire for seeing and the rest on the part of eye-consciousness and the rest. Why is their desire for seeing, hearing, and the rest impossible? Because of their being non-conceptual (<s>avikalpaka</s>). Rather, it is mental consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>), introduced under the dominance of those [sense-faculties], that is called 'faculty' — as if [it were] a faculty. How is it known that it is introduced under their dominance? For if eye-consciousness and the rest had not arisen through the gateway of the eye and the rest, how otherwise would conceptual mental consciousness have arisen? Therefore it is known that it is introduced under their dominance. That mental consciousness, being in the state of being an eye-faculty and the rest, desires its own respective object-domain — form and the rest. And [the mental consciousness] that is merely [functioning as mind] — [Tib. 370a] that which is introduced under the dominance of the others — the eye and the rest — does not at all desire their objects. What then? It takes only its own object — the <s>dharmāyatana</s> (mind-object-base) — as its support. Therefore this fault does not exist — namely, what was said: 'the non-deviation of the mind-faculty too would follow.'

body.text: na pudgalaḥ. kim. abhijñeyaḥ parijñeyaś ceti. tasmād vijñeyo 'py asau pudgalo na bhavati. nanu cāsāv arthād abhijñeyaḥ parijñeyaś ca na bhavatīty uktaḥ. na tv artho vijñeyaḥ iti. ata āha. prajñāvijñānayoḥ samānaviṣayatvād iti. vijñeyam api hi cakṣurādikaṃ bhavati. na kevalam abhijñeyaṃ parijñeyaṃ ceti.
body.translated_text: The <s>pudgala</s> is not — what? — either directly knowable (<s>abhijñeya</s>) or fully knowable (<s>parijñeya</s>). Therefore that <s>pudgala</s> is not knowable (<s>vijñeya</s>) either. But is it not the case that he has effectively said that it is neither directly knowable nor fully knowable — not that it is not knowable in the sense of being an object? Therefore he says: 'Because of the sameness of object-domain between <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)' — for the eye and the rest are also knowable (<s>vijñeya</s>), not merely directly knowable and fully knowable.

body.text: anātmaneti. cakṣuṣā cakṣurvijñānenety arthaḥ. nītārthaṃ ca sūtraṃ pratisaraṇam uktam iti. catvārīmāni bhikṣavaḥ pratisaraṇāni. katamāni catvāri. dharmaḥ pratisaraṇaṃ na pudgalaḥ. arthaḥ pratisaraṇaṃ na vyaṃjanaṃ. nītārthasūtraṃ pratisaraṇaṃ na neyārthaṃ. jñānaṃ pratisaraṇaṃ na vijñānam iti.
body.translated_text: 'Non-self' (<s>anātman</s>) — the meaning is: by the eye and by eye-consciousness. And it has been stated that a <s>sūtra</s> of definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>) is the authority. 'There are, O monks, four authorities (<s>pratisaraṇa</s>). What are the four? The <s>dharma</s> is the authority, not the person (<s>pudgala</s>). The meaning is the authority, not the letter (<s>vyañjana</s>). A <s>sūtra</s> of definitive meaning is the authority, not one of interpretable meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>). Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is the authority, not [mere] consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>).'

body.text: prajñaptim anūpapatita iti. yatraiva prajñaptiḥ kṛtā ātmeti vyavahārārthaṃ tām evātmety abhiniviṣṭa ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Having followed the designation' (<s>prajñaptim anūpapatita</s>) — wherever the designation 'self' (<s>ātman</s>) has been made for the purpose of conventional usage, one who clings to that very thing as 'self' — this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: 'There is no being here, nor a self' —

body.text: idam ihodāharaṇaṃ
