body.translated_text: this is the illustration here,

body.text: ity etac ca.
body.translated_text: and this too.

children.translated_text: 'That one too does not exist at all' —

body.text: itīdaṃ vāpy udāharaṇaṃ.
body.translated_text: this also is the illustration.

children.text: yogy api nāsti yaḥ śūnyatām abhyasyātīti.
children.translated_text: 'Even a <s>yogin</s> does not exist — one who practices emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>)' — thus.

body.text: ātmadṛṣṭir bhavati yāvaj jīvadṛṣṭir iti prathamā ādinavo nirviśeṣo bhavati. tīrthikair [Tib. 370b] iti dvitīyaḥ. unmārgapratipanno bhavatīti tṛtīyaḥ. śūnyatāyām
body.translated_text: 'The view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) arises, up to the view of a life-principle (<s>jīvadṛṣṭi</s>)' — this is the first danger; it is undifferentiated. 'With the <s>tīrthika</s>s' [Tib. 370b] — this is the second. 'One follows a wrong path' — this is the third. 'In emptiness

body.text: asya cittaṃ na praskandati yāvan nādhimucyata iti caturthaḥ. āryadharmā asya na vyavadāyanta iti paṃcamaḥ.
body.translated_text: his mind does not leap forward, up to he has no conviction' — this is the fourth. 'The noble <s>dharma</s>s do not become purified for him' — this is the fifth.

body.text: na tarhi teṣāṃ buddhaḥ śāsteti. buddhavacanam eṣāṃ na pramāṇam ity abhiprāyāt.
body.translated_text: 'Then the <s>Buddha</s> is not their teacher' — because the intent is that the word of the <s>Buddha</s> is not authoritative for them.

body.text: na kilaitad buddhavacanam iti. kenāpy adhyāropitāny etāni sūtrāṇīty abhiprāyaḥ. sarvanikāyāntareṣv iti tāmraparṇīyanikāyādiṣu. na ca sūtraṃ bādhate na ca sūtrāntaraṃ bādhate. na ca sūtrāntaraṃ virodhayati. na dharmatāṃ bādhata iti pratītyasamutpādadharmatāṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Surely this is not the word of the <s>Buddha</s>' — the intent is: these <s>sūtra</s>s have been interpolated by someone. 'In all the other schools (<s>nikāyāntara</s>)' — in the <s>Tāmraparṇīya</s> school and the rest. 'It does not contradict the <s>sūtra</s>, nor does it contradict another <s>sūtra</s>. It does not conflict with another <s>sūtra</s>. It does not contradict the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>)' — that is, the <s>dharmatā</s> of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>).

body.text: sarvadharmā anātmāna iti. na caita ātmasvabhāvāḥ. na caiteṣv ātmā vidyata iti anātmānaḥ sarvadharmāḥ. dvayaṃ pratītyeti. cakṣū rūpāṇi yāvan mano dharmān iti. [na pudgalo na dharmā iti] .
body.translated_text: 'All <s>dharma</s>s are non-self' (<s>anātman</s>) — they do not have self as their own-nature, nor is a self found in them — thus all <s>dharma</s>s are non-self. 'Dependent on a pair' — that is, the eye and forms, up to the mind and <s>dharma</s>s. [Neither a person nor dharmas].

body.text: nātmā skaṃdhāyatanadhātava iti vacane yat kaścit pūrvaṃ no tu vaktavyaṃ rūpāṇi vā no vety uktam. apoḍham apāstaṃ tad bhavati ātmano 'nyatvāt.
body.translated_text: Regarding the statement 'neither self, nor aggregates, sense-bases, and elements' — what was previously stated as 'it is not to be said whether [it is] forms or not' — that is rejected, set aside, because of the otherness of self.

body.text: tasmāt sarva evānmātmany ātmagrāha iti. nāto 'nyo 'stīti darśayati.
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, all grasping of self is indeed in what is non-self' — he shows: there is no other [self] beyond this.

body.text: yady evam iti vistaraḥ. yadīmān eva paṃcopādānaskandhān samanusmarantaḥ samanvasmārṣuḥ samanusmaranti samanusmariṣyanti vā na pudgalaṃ. kasmād āha rūpavān ahaṃ [Tib. 371a] babhūvātīte 'dhvanīti. aham iti vacanāt pudgala ucyate iti darśayati. evam anekavidhaṃ ye samanusmaranti. ta evam anusmarantīti vākyādhyāhāraḥ. apāṭha eva cātra śaraṇaṃ syād iti. aham iti pāṭhe hi sati satkāyadṛṣṭiparigrahaprasaṃgaḥ syād ity arthaḥ. viṃśatikoṭikā hi satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ paṭhyate. rūpam ātmeti samanupaśyati. rūpavantam ātmānam. ātmīyaṃ rūpaṃ. rūpe ātmety evaṃ yāvad vijñānaṃ vaktavyaṃ. rāśidhārādivad iti. rāśivad dhārāvac ca. ādiśabdena pānakādigrahaṇaṃ. ekasmin kṣaṇe samavahitānāṃ bahūnāṃ rāśiḥ. bahuṣu kṣaṇeṣu samavahitānāṃ dhārā. rāśidṛṣṭāntena bahuṣu dharmeṣu pudgalaprajñaptiṃ darśayati dhārādṛṣṭāntena bahutve sati rūpavedanādīnāṃ skaṃdhānāṃ pravāhe pudgalaprajñaptiṃ darśayati.
body.translated_text: 'If so' — in detail. If those who recall, have recalled, and will recall these very five aggregates of clinging, and not a <s>pudgala</s> — why did he say: 'I had form in the past life?' [Tib. 371a] He shows that by the word 'I,' a <s>pudgala</s> is spoken of. 'Thus, those who recall in various ways — they recall in this way' — this is a supplementation of the sentence. 'Here, an alternate reading alone would be the refuge' — for if the reading 'I' (<s>aham</s>) were present, there would be the undesired consequence of grasping the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) — this is the meaning. For the view of the existing body is read as having twenty aspects: 'one regards form as self; self as possessing form; form as belonging to self; self as in form' — thus up to consciousness should be stated. 'Like a heap, a stream, and the rest' — like a heap, like a stream. By the word 'and the rest,' beverages and the like are included. A heap is of many [things] assembled at one moment. A stream is of [things] assembled over many moments. By the illustration of a heap, he shows the designation of <s>pudgala</s> with reference to many <s>dharma</s>s; by the illustration of a stream, he shows the designation of <s>pudgala</s> with reference to the continuum of aggregates such as form, feeling, and the rest, when there is multiplicity.

body.text: katham idaṃ gamyata iti. buddhākhyāyāḥ saṃtater idaṃ sāmarthyaṃ. yad ābhogamātreṇāviparītam jñānam utpadyate yatreṣṭaṃ. na punaḥ pudgalasyeti.
body.translated_text: 'How is this understood?' — this is the capacity of the continuum designated as 'Buddha.' That by mere intention (<s>ābhoga</s>), non-distorted knowledge arises wherever desired. But not of a <s>pudgala</s>.

body.text: ucyate. atītādivacanāt.
body.translated_text: It is said: because of the statement of past and the rest.

body.text: iti vistareṇokta upasaṃhāraḥ. tasmāt skaṃdhasaṃtāna eva buddhākhyā. na pudgala iti.
body.translated_text: the conclusion stated in detail. Therefore, the continuum of aggregates alone has the designation '<s>Buddha</s>' — not a <s>pudgala</s>.

body.text: bhāraṃ ca vo bhikṣavo deśayiṣyāmīti vistaraḥ. [Tib. 371b] bhāraṃ ca vo bhikṣavo deśayiṣyāmi bhārādānaṃ ca bhāranikṣepaṇaṃ ca bhārahāraṃ ca. tac chṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuruta bhāṣiṣye. bhāraḥ katamaḥ. paṃcopādānaskaṃdhāḥ. bhārādānaṃ katamat. tṛṣṇā paunarbhavikī nandīrāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī. bhāranikṣepaṇaṃ katamat. yad asyā eva tṛsṇāyāḥ paunarbhavikyā nandīrāgasahagatāyāḥ tatratatrābhinandinyāḥ aśeṣaprahāṇaṃ pratiniḥsargo vyantībhāvaḥ kṣayo virāgo nirodho vyupaśamo 'staṃgamaḥ bhārahāraḥ katamaḥ. pudgala iti syād vacanīyaṃ. yo 'sāv āyuṣmān evaṃnāmā evaṃjanya evaṃgotraḥ evamāhāraḥ evaṃsukhaduḥkhapratisaṃvedī evaṃdīrghāyur evaṃcirasthitika evamāyuṣmanta iti. bhāraṃ haratīti bhārahāraḥ. pudgala ity abhiprāyaḥ. chedam udāharaṇam. ata evāha. na hi bhāra eva bhārahāra iti.
body.translated_text: 'I shall teach you the burden, O monks' — in detail. [Tib. 371b] 'I shall teach you, O monks, the burden, the taking up of the burden, the putting down of the burden, and the burden-bearer. Listen to that well and thoroughly, pay careful attention, and I shall speak. What is the burden? The five aggregates of clinging. What is the taking up of the burden? That craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and passion, delighting here and there. What is the putting down of the burden? That which is the complete abandonment of this very craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and passion, delighting here and there — the relinquishment, the ending, the exhaustion, the dispassion, the cessation, the calming, the disappearance. What is the burden-bearer? It should be said: the <s>pudgala</s> — namely, the venerable one of such-and-such a name, such-and-such a birth, such-and-such a lineage, such-and-such a diet, experiencing such-and-such pleasure and pain, of such-and-such a lifespan, of such-and-such a length of stay, with such-and-such a span of life.' 'One who carries the burden is the burden-bearer' — the intent is: the <s>pudgala</s>. This is a concluding illustration. Therefore he says: 'for the burden itself is not the burden-bearer.'

body.text: bhārādānasyāpi yathoktalakṣaṇasya skaṃdhāsaṃgrahaprasaṃgāc ca. pudgalavad askaṃdhasaṃgrahaprasaṃgaḥ. na caivam iṣyate. tasmād bhārādānavan na skaṃdhebhyo 'rthāntarabhūtaḥ pudgalaḥ. ity artham eva ceti vistareṇa sarvam uktvā vaktavyaṃ mānyatheti. yadi dravyasan syāt pudgalaḥ bhārahāraḥ katamaḥ pudgala iti syād vacanīyam ity etāvad evoktaṃ syāt tatra sūtre. pareṇa sa na vibhaktvyaḥ syāt. yo 'sāv āyuṣmān iti vistareṇa yāvad āyuḥparyanta iti. [Tib. 372a] prajñaptisatpudgalapratipattyarthaṃ hy etat pareṇa viśeṣaṇam ity abhiprāyaḥ. sa eva tu prajñaptisan kuto vijñāyate. mānyathā vijñāyi nityo vāvaktavyo vā dravyasatpudgala iti. skaṃdhānām iti vistaraḥ. tatra ye upaghātāya saṃvartante duḥkhahetavaḥ skaṃdhāḥ. te bhāva iti kṛtvoktāḥ. uttare ye pīḍyante. te bhārahāra iti kṛtvoktā iti. upapādukatvād iti. upapadane sādhukāritvād ity arthaḥ. pudgalasya satyeṣv anantarbhāvād iti. yasmād yathāparikalpitasya pudgalasya satyeṣu duḥkhādisu nānantarbhāvaḥ. na hi pudgalo duḥkhaṃ yāvan mārga iti. ato na satyadarśanaprahātavyaiṣā pudgalāpavādika mithyādṛṣṭiḥ. yā hi dṛṣṭir yasmin satye vipratipannā. tatsatyadarśanāt tasyāḥ prahāṇaṃ bhavet. tathā duḥkhasamudayasatyayoḥ pudgalasyānantarbhāvān nāpi bhāvanāprahātavyā. bhāvanāprahātavyo hi kleśo bhāvanāprahātavyam
body.translated_text: And because the taking up of the burden, as described, would have the undesired consequence of not being included in the aggregates — like the <s>pudgala</s>, it would have the undesired consequence of not being included in the aggregates. But this is not accepted. Therefore, like the taking up of the burden, the <s>pudgala</s> is not something different from the aggregates. Thus, having stated 'the meaning alone' — in detail, everything having been stated, one should say 'do not [understand it] otherwise.' If the <s>pudgala</s> were a real entity (<s>dravyasat</s>), then in that <s>sūtra</s>, only this much would have been said — 'What is the burden-bearer? It should be said: the <s>pudgala</s>' — and it would not have been further qualified by the other party: 'namely, the venerable one' — in detail, up to 'the end of the lifespan.' [Tib. 372a] The intent is that this further qualification by the other party is for the purpose of understanding the <s>pudgala</s> as existing only as a designation (<s>prajñaptisat</s>). But that very one, existing only as a designation — from what is it known? 'Lest it be otherwise known' — lest an eternal or a substantially real <s>pudgala</s> be understood. 'Of the aggregates' — in detail. Therein, those aggregates that conduce to harm, that are the causes of suffering — they are called 'burden' (<s>bhāra</s>). The subsequent [aggregates] that are afflicted — they are called 'burden-bearer.' 'Because of being spontaneously-born (<s>upapāduka</s>)' — the meaning is: because of welcoming rebirth. 'Because of the non-inclusion of the <s>pudgala</s> in the truths' — since the <s>pudgala</s> as conceived is not included in the truths of suffering and the rest. For the <s>pudgala</s> is not suffering, up to not the path. Therefore this wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) that denies the <s>pudgala</s> is not to be abandoned by the seeing of the truths. For whatever view is mistaken regarding a particular truth — its abandonment would come from seeing that truth. Similarly, because the <s>pudgala</s> is not included in the truths of suffering and origination, it is also not to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). For the affliction to be abandoned by cultivation

body.text: eva vastu duḥkaṃ samudayaṃ vālaṃbata ity evaṃ tasyā bhāvanāprahātavyatvaṃ yujyate. na ca pudgalas tayor aṃtarbhūta ity ato bhāvanāprahātavyā sā na bhavati. atha vā na kadācid api dṛṣṭir bhāvanāprahātavyeti nāsau bhāvanāprahātavyā.
body.translated_text: takes as its object only a thing to be abandoned by cultivation — either suffering or origination — thus its status as to be abandoned by cultivation is fitting. But since the <s>pudgala</s> is not included in those two, that [view] is not to be abandoned by cultivation. Alternatively, at no time is a view to be abandoned by cultivation — therefore it is not to be abandoned by cultivation.

body.text: ekatilaikataṇḍulavad ekarāśyekavacanavac ceti. yathā [Tib. 372b] 'ṣṭadravyakatve 'py ekatila ekataṇḍula iti cocyate. tathā eko rāśir ekavacanam iti. tadvad ekaḥ pudgala iti. utpattimattvābhyupagamād iti. utpadyata iti vacanād utpattimattvam asyābhyupagataṃ bhavati. tataś ca saṃskṛta iti vaktavyo bhavadbhiḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Like a single sesame seed, a single grain of rice, like a single heap, a single word' — just as, [Tib. 372b] though there are many substances, one speaks of 'a single sesame seed,' 'a single grain of rice.' Similarly, 'a single heap,' 'a single word.' Likewise, 'a single <s>pudgala</s>.' 'Because of the admission of having origination' — because of the statement 'it originates,' it is admitted that it has origination. And from that, it should be said by you to be conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>).

body.text: skandhāntaropādānād iti. nāsya saṃskṛtatvam āpdyata iti abhiprāyaḥ. yathā hi yājñiko jāta iti vidyopādānād ucyate. na cāsau bhūtārthena jātaḥ. tadvad iti sarvaṃ yojyaṃ.
body.translated_text: 'Because of taking up another aggregate' (<s>skandhāntaropādāna</s>) — the intent is: its status as conditioned is not thereby established. For just as a Vedic sacrificer is called 'born' because of the taking up of learning — but he is not truly born [again]. Similarly, everything should be connected.

body.text: kārakas tu nopalabhyata iti vistaraḥ. karmaṇaḥ kārako nopalabhyate. kīdṛśo 'sāv iti. āha. ya imāṃś caihikāṃ skandhān nikṣipati tyajaty anyāṃś ca pāratrikān skaṃdhān pratisaṃdadhāti upasaṃgṛhṇāti. dravyasann avasthita iti. anyatra dharmasaṃketād iti pratītyasamutpādalakṣaṇāntenāha yad utāsmin satīti.
body.translated_text: 'But a doer is not found' — in detail. A doer of action is not found. Of what kind? — he says: one who puts down, discards, these aggregates of the present life and reconnects, takes up, other aggregates of the next life — as a real entity that remains. 'Other than the <s>dharma</s>-convention' (<s>dharmasaṃketa</s>) — he states by way of the characteristic of dependent origination: 'namely, when this exists...'

body.text: upādatta iti phālguna na vadāmīti. ahaṃ ced evaṃ vadeyam upādatta iti. atra te kalpaḥ syād vacanāya ko nu bhadanta upādānam upādatta iti. tasmān nāsti skandhānāṃ kaścid upādātā nāpi nikṣipteti.
body.translated_text: 'I do not say "one takes up," O <s>Phālguna</s>' — if I were to say 'one takes up,' then there would be an occasion for you to say: 'Who, Venerable One, takes up the clinging (<s>upādāna</s>)?' Therefore there is no one who takes up the aggregates, nor anyone who puts them down.

body.text: tasyāpi tatheti. pratikṣaṇam apūrvotpattir evety arthaḥ. yadi pudgalaḥ. so 'siddha ity evamādinopanyāsenāsiddhatāṃ dṛṣṭāntasya darśayati.
body.translated_text: 'Of that too, likewise' — the meaning is: there is only the arising of something new at every moment. 'If a <s>pudgala</s> [existed]' — by such arguments as 'that is unestablished,' he shows the unestablished nature of the example.

body.text: śarīravidyāliṃgavac ceti. vidyā ca liṃgaṃ ca vidyāliṃgaṃ. śarīraṃ ca vidyāliṃgaṃ ca śarīravidyāliṃgaṃ. [Tib. 373a] tayor iva śarīravidyāliṃgavat.
body.translated_text: 'Like body, learning, and marks' — learning (<s>vidyā</s>) and marks (<s>liṅga</s>) together are 'learning-and-marks.' Body and learning-and-marks together are 'body-learning-and-marks.' [Tib. 373a] Like those two — like body-learning-and-marks.

body.text: skandhapudgalayor anyatvam āpadyate. yathopādeyāyā vidyāyā liṃgāc ca śarīrasya anyatvaṃ. evam upādeyāt skandhāt pudgalasyānyatvam upādātṛtvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. jīrṇaṃ taṃ śarīrāntaram eva vyādhitaṃ ceti pratikṣaṇam anyatvam avasthānād ity abhiprāyāt. tatra yad uktaṃ jīrṇo jāto vyādhito jāta ity asiddho dṛṣṭānta iti darśayati. athāpi syād avasthitasya śarīrasyāvasthāntaranirvṛttāv avasthāntaraprādurbhāva iti. tac ca nāpratiṣiddho hi sāṃkhyeyaḥ pariṇāmavādaḥ pūrvasmin kośasthāne. katham. sa eva hi dharmī na saṃvidyate. yasyāvasthitasya dharmāntaravikalpaḥ parikalpeta. tad eva cedaṃ tathety apūrvikā vācoyuktir iti.
body.translated_text: The otherness of aggregates and <s>pudgala</s> would follow. Just as the body is other than the learning and marks that are taken up — so too the <s>pudgala</s> would be other than the aggregates that are taken up, because of being the taker-up — this is the intent. 'Aged — [one says] a different body; and diseased' — the intent is: because of otherness at every moment, due to the different states. Therein, regarding what was said — 'aged one was born, diseased one was born' — he shows this is an unestablished example. Or, if there were a transformation of state for an abiding body — the state changing while the thing remains — that too is not forbidden, for the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine of transformation has been [refuted] in the previous section of the <s>Kośa</s>. How? For that very possessor of properties (<s>dharmin</s>) is not found — for whom, while remaining, one could conceive of a change of properties. 'If that is indeed so' — this is an unprecedented way of speaking.

body.text: bhūtāni catvāri rūpaṃ caikam iti. rūpaṃ katamat. catvāri mahābhūtānīty
body.translated_text: 'Four elements and one form' — 'What is form? The four great elements' —

body.text: ādi.
body.translated_text: and so forth.

body.text: pākṣika eva doṣa iti ekasmin pakṣe ayaṃ doṣavāda ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'The fault applies only to one position (<s>pākṣika</s>)' — the meaning is: this criticism applies only to one position.

body.text: bhūtamātrikapakṣa iti sthavirabuddhadevapakṣe nāsmatpakṣa ity arthaḥ. tathāpi tv iti. bhūtamātrikapakṣe 'pi bhūtebhyo rūpaṃ nānyat. bhūtamātrikapakṣe 'pi bhūtebhyo rūpavat skandhebhyo nānyaḥ pudgala ity upagataṃ bhavatīti svasiddhāntaḥ parityāgaḥ syād ity abhiprāyaḥ. kasmād [Tib. 373b] bhagavatā sa jīvaḥ. tac charīram anyo veti na vyākṛtam iti. ayam eṣām abhiprāyaḥ. yadi skandheṣu pudgalopacāraḥ kasmāc charīram eva jīva iti noktam iti. pūrvakair eveti sthaviranāgasenādibhiḥ. bahuvollakā iti. bahupralāpā iti.
body.translated_text: 'The position of the elements being merely the basis (<s>bhūtamātrika</s>)' — in the position of elder <s>Buddhadeva</s>, not in our position — this is the meaning. 'Even so, however' — even in the position that elements are merely the basis, form is not other than the elements. [Similarly,] even in that position, like form from elements, the <s>pudgala</s> is not other than the aggregates — thus [admitting this] would be an abandonment of one's own established doctrine — this is the intent. 'Why [Tib. 373b] did the <s>Bhagavān</s> not explain: "that being is the body, or is it another?"' — their intent is this: if the <s>pudgala</s> is a figurative designation (<s>upacāra</s>) upon the aggregates, why was it not stated: 'the body itself is the being (<s>jīva</s>)?' 'By the predecessors' — by elder <s>Nāgasena</s> and the rest. 'Much talkers' (<s>bahuvollaka</s>) — meaning: much prattlers.

body.text: itarāha. yadi pudgalo nāvaktavyaḥ kasmān nokto nāsty eveti.
body.translated_text: The other party says: if the <s>pudgala</s> is not to be [positively] stated, why was it not said: 'it simply does not exist'?

body.text: sa ca taddeśanāyā akṣama iti. nairātmyadeśanāyā ayogya ity arthaḥ. pūrvam evaṃ saṃmūḍha iti. satkāyadṛṣṭisahagatena mohena. bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃmoham āpadyeteti ucchedadṛṣṭisahagataṃ dṛṣṭyantaram utpādayed ity abhiprāyaḥ. ata evāha. abhūn me ātmā sa me etarhi nāstīti. āha cātreti. bhadantakumāralātaḥ
body.translated_text: 'And he was incapable of that teaching' — meaning: unfit for the teaching of non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>). 'Already thus confused' — by delusion accompanied by the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). 'He would fall into even greater confusion' — the intent is: he would generate another wrong view accompanied by the annihilationist view (<s>ucchedadṛṣṭi</s>). Therefore he says: 'I had a self — that self of mine now does not exist.' And here he cites: the venerable <s>Kumāralāta</s> —

children.translated_text: 'The breaking of the fangs of [wrong] views' —

body.text: vistaraḥ. dṛṣṭir eva daṃṣṭrā. tayāvabhedam
body.translated_text: in detail. Views themselves are the fangs. Their breaking —

body.text: bhagavanto
body.translated_text: the <s>Bhagavān</s>s

body.text: nairātmyaṃ tatpratipakṣeṇa.
body.translated_text: non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>), by means of its antidote.

children.translated_text: And having regard to the loss of actions,

body.text: kṛtavipraṇāśam apekṣya. pudgalāstitvam iva darśayanto 'nyathā deśayanti.
body.translated_text: having regard to the non-destruction of what has been done (<s>kṛtavipraṇāśa</s>). As if showing the existence of a <s>pudgala</s> (person), they teach otherwise.

children.translated_text: Like a tigress carrying away her cub —

body.text: iti. yathā vyāghrī nātiniṣṭhureṇa dantagrahaṇena svapotam apaharati nayati. māsya daṃṣṭrayā śarīraṃ kṣataṃ bhūd iti. nāpy atiśithilena dantagrahaṇena tam apaharati māsya bhraṃśapāto 'smin visaye bhūd iti. yuktenaiva grahaṇenāpaharatīty artaḥ. apaharatīty apare [Tib. 374a] paṭhanti sthānāntarād apaharaty apanayatīty arthaḥ. tathārthadarśane kāraṇaṃ darśayann āha.
body.translated_text: thus. Just as a tigress carries away, leads, her own cub, not with an excessively harsh grip of the teeth — lest its body be wounded by the fangs — nor with an excessively loose grip of the teeth — lest it fall and drop in that area — but carries it away with just the right grip — this is the meaning. Others read 'carries away' (<s>apaharati</s>) [Tib. 374a] — meaning: carries away from another place, removes — this is the meaning. Showing the reason for seeing [things] in that way, he says:

body.text: iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: — thus in detail.

children.translated_text: If someone who has accepted the existence of a self

body.text: cet kaścid
body.translated_text: — if anyone —

body.text: satkāyadṛṣṭilakṣaṇayā
body.translated_text: characterized by the view of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>),

body.text: vineyajanaḥ syāt.
body.translated_text: trainable person would be [lost].

body.text: dharmasaṃketam ajānānaḥ.
body.translated_text: not knowing the conventions of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: kuśalakarmaṇo vyāghrīpotabhūtasya
body.translated_text: of wholesome action that is like a tigress's cub,

body.text: kuryāt. nāsti karmaṇaḥ phalam iti.
body.translated_text: would occur — 'there is no fruit of action' — thus.

body.text: iti prajñaptau bhavaḥ prājñaptikaḥ. saṃvṛtisann api pudgalo nāstīti kaścid gṛhṇīyād ity ato
body.translated_text: meaning: existing in designation (<s>prajñapti</s>), hence <s>prājñaptika</s>. Someone might grasp that the <s>pudgala</s>, even though existing conventionally (<s>saṃvṛtisat</s>), does not exist — therefore

children.translated_text: he did not say 'it does not exist.'
But why did he not say 'it does exist,' since it does exist? —

body.text: iti. yadi bhūtārthena pudgalo 'sti kim iti kṛtvā bhagavān asti pudgala iti na bravīti. na hi rūpam astīti vacane doṣo bhavati tasyāstitvāt.
body.translated_text: thus. If the <s>pudgala</s> exists in reality, why does the <s>Bhagavān</s> not say 'the <s>pudgala</s> exists'? For there is no fault in the statement 'form exists,' because of its [actual] existence.

body.text: nirgranthaśrāvakacaṭakavad iti. nirgranthaśrāvakeṇa caṭakaṃ jīvantaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavān pṛṣṭaḥ. kim ayaṃ caṭako jīvati na veti. tasyāyam abhiprāyaḥ yadi śramaṇo gautama ādiśej jīvatīti. sa tan nipīḍanena mārayitvā darśayet. yadi punar bhagavān evam ādiśen mṛta iti. sa taṃ jīvantam eva darśayet. kathaṃ nāmāyam ajña iti loko jānīyād iti tasyābhinveśaḥ. bhagavatā tu tasyāśayaṃ viditvā na vyākṛtaṃ. tvaccittapratibaddham evaitaj jīvati vā na veti cety evābhihitaṃ. tadvad [Tib. 374b] etan na vyākṛtam iti.
body.translated_text: Like the <s>Nirgrantha</s> disciple with the sparrow — thus. A disciple of the <s>Nirgrantha</s>s, having seized a living sparrow, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Does this sparrow live or not?' His intent was: if the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> were to declare 'it lives,' he would kill it by crushing and show [it dead]. But if the <s>Bhagavān</s> were to declare thus 'it is dead,' he would show it alive. 'Let the world know that this one is ignorant' — such was his obsession. But the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having understood his intention, did not answer. 'This depends on your mind — whether it lives or not' — thus he spoke. [Tib. 374b] Likewise, this was not answered.

body.text: tulyārtho hy eṣa catuṣka iti. śāśvato loko 'śāśvato loka ity anena catuṣkena antavān loko 'naṃtavān ity ayaṃ catuṣkas tulyārthaḥ. yady evaṃ kathaṃ caturdaśāvyākṛtavastūni bhavaṃti. śāśvato loka ity ekacatuṣkaḥ. antavān iti dvitīyaś catuṣkaḥ. bhavati tathāgata iti tṛtīyaś catuṣkaḥ. sa jīvas tac charīram anyo jīvo 'nyac charīram iti dvikaḥ. trayaś catuṣkāḥ ekaś ca dvika iti caturdaśāvyākṛtavastūnīti. paryāyarūpatvavyāvasthāne 'pi caturdaśatvaṃ bhavatīty adoṣaḥ. tvam evaitat pṛcchasīti. antavān iti yaṃ pṛṣṭavān. kathaṃ. kiṃ nu sarvo loko 'nena mārgeṇa niryāsyatīti anena antavān iti aśāśvata iti ca pṛṣṭaṃ bhavati. āhosvid ekadeśo lokasyety anenāntavāṃś cānantavāṃś ceti
body.translated_text: This set of four has an equivalent meaning — thus. By the set of four 'the world is eternal, the world is not eternal,' the set of four 'the world is finite, the world is infinite' has an equivalent meaning. If so, how are there fourteen unexplained matters (<s>avyākṛtavastu</s>)? 'The world is eternal' — this is one set of four. 'The world is finite' — the second set of four. 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> exists [after death]' — the third set of four. 'The life-principle is identical with the body, the life-principle is different from the body' — this is a pair. Three sets of four and one pair — thus there are fourteen unexplained matters. Even with the establishment of variant form, the number fourteen obtains — so there is no fault. 'You yourself are asking this' — thus. The one who asked 'is the world finite?' — how? 'Will the entire world escape by this path?' — by this, 'is it finite?' and 'is it non-eternal?' are both asked. Or else, 'will a portion of the world [escape]?' — by this, 'it is both finite and infinite'

body.text: śāśvataś cāśāśvataś ceti ca pṛṣṭaṃ bhavati.
body.translated_text: and 'it is both eternal and non-eternal' are both asked.

body.text: jīvantaṃ pudgalam astīti vyākarotīti. tattvānyatvenāvaktavyaṃ santam eva pudgalaṃ vyākarotīty abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: He declares the living <s>pudgala</s> as existing — thus. The intent is: he declares the <s>pudgala</s> as existing, [which is] inexpressible as either identical with or different from [the aggregates].

body.text: śāśvatadoṣaprasaṃgād iti vātsiputrīyavacanaṃ. idaṃ tarhi kasmād vyākarotīti vistareṇācāryavacanaṃ. sārvajñam ity aṇ bhāvapratyayo yauvanam iti yathā. na vaktavyaṃ paśyati vā na veti. paśyati na paśyati na vaktavyam ity arthaḥ. śanaiḥśanair avaktavyaṃ kriyatām [Tib. 375a] iti. sarvajño vā bhagavān na veti na vaktavyam iti. śanaiḥśanairgrahaṇaṃ samānaśākyaputrīyaprakopaparihārārthaṃ. satyataḥ sthitita iti. sthitirūpeṇety arthaḥ. dṛṣṭisthānam uktam iti. mithyādṛṣṭisthānam uktam ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: Because of the consequence of the fault of eternalism — this is the <s>Vātsīputrīya</s> statement. 'Why then does he declare this?' — in detail, is the <s>Ācārya</s>'s statement. '<s>Sārvajña</s>' (omniscient) — the suffix <s>aṇ</s> is a state-suffix, as in '<s>yauvana</s>' (youth). 'It should not be said whether he sees or not' — the meaning is: it should not be said 'he sees' or 'he does not see.' 'Gradually make it unspeakable' — [Tib. 375a] — thus: 'Whether the <s>Bhagavān</s> is omniscient or not should not be said.' The word 'gradually' is for the purpose of avoiding the anger of fellow <s>Śākyaputrīya</s>s. 'Being established in truth' — the meaning is: in the form of being established. 'A basis for [wrong] view has been stated' — the intent is: a basis for wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) has been stated.

body.text: ācārya āha. astīty api dṛṣṭisthānam uktam iti. satkāyadṛṣṭisthānam uktam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: The <s>Ācārya</s> says: 'A basis for [wrong] view has also been stated with regard to "it exists"' — the meaning is: a basis for the view of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) has been stated.

body.text: uktottara eṣa pakṣa iti. kathaṃ ca na. pratikṣepāt. sūtra eva hi pratikṣiptaṃ bhagavateti vistareṇa yāvad apadṛṣṭāntā eta iti. kim idam upādāyety ārabhyaitad apareṣāṃ vyākhyānaṃ. svamatena tu yathā saṃsarati. tathā darśayann āha. yathā tu kṣaṇiko 'gnir iti vistaraḥ. kṣaṇiko 'gniḥ prasiddhaḥ. sa ca deśāṃtarotpattisaṃtatyā saṃcaratīty ucyate. tathā sattvākhyaskandhasamudāyas tṛṣṇopādānaḥ. tṛṣṇā upādānam asyeti tṛṣṇopādānaḥ. kṣaṇiko 'pi saṃtatyā saṃsaratīti.
body.translated_text: This position has been answered — thus. And how is it not? Because of refutation. For it has been refuted in the <s>sūtra</s> itself by the <s>Bhagavān</s> — in detail, up to: 'these are [arguments with] defective examples.' Beginning from 'dependent on what?' — this is the explanation of the others. But according to his own position, showing how [the being] transmigrates, he says: 'Just as fire is momentary' — in detail. Fire is accepted as momentary. And it is said to 'wander' by the continuity of arising in another location. Similarly, the assemblage of aggregates called a 'being' (<s>sattvākhya</s>) has craving as its appropriation (<s>tṛṣṇopādāna</s>) — craving is the appropriation of this, hence <s>tṛṣṇopādāna</s>. Though momentary, it transmigrates by continuity.

body.text: sunetro nāma śāsteti. saptasūryodayasūtre 'yam eva bhagavān ṛṣiḥ sunetro nāma babhūveti.
body.translated_text: There was a teacher named <s>Sunetra</s> — thus. In the <s>Saptasūryodayasūtra</s> (Sūtra of the Seven Suns Rising), this very <s>Bhagavān</s> was a seer named <s>Sunetra</s> — thus it is said.

body.text: anyatvāt skaṃdhānam iti. kṣaṇikatve saty anyatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. ekasaṃtānatāṃ darśayatīti. yasmāt sunetro buddhasaṃtāna evāsīt. ataḥ sa evāham ity abhedopacāraḥ. [Tib. 375b] yathā sa evāgnir yaḥ pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭo dahann āgata iti. saṃtānavrṭtyā sa evety ucyate. tadvat. saiṣāṃ syāt satkāyadṛṣṭir iti. saiṣāṃ tathāgatānām ātmātmīyākārā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ syāt. dṛḍhatarātmātmīyasnehaparigāhitabaṃdhanānām iti. ātmadṛṣṭāv ātmīyadṛṣṭau ca satyām ātmasneha ātmīyasnehaś ca bhavati. ity ato rāgo bandhanam iti kṛtvā dṛḍhīkṛtabandhanānāṃ satāṃ mokṣo dūrībhavet. naiva bhaved ity abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: Because of the otherness of the aggregates — the intent is: given momentariness, because of otherness. He shows the unity of continuity — thus. Since <s>Sunetra</s> was indeed of the <s>Buddha</s>'s continuity, therefore the figurative expression of identity 'I myself was that one' [is used]. [Tib. 375b] Just as 'that is the very fire which was previously seen burning and has come' — by the operation of continuity, it is said 'that very one.' Likewise. This would be their view of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) — this <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s would have the aspect of self and mine. For those whose bonds are firmly grasped by strong attachment to self and mine — when the view of self exists and the view of mine exists, attachment to self and attachment to mine arise. Therefore, since attachment is bondage, for those whose bonds have been made firm, liberation would become remote. The intent is: it would never occur.

body.text: ya ekeṣāṃ pudgalagrāha iti vātsīputrīyāṇām. ekeṣāṃ sarvanāstigrāha iti. madhyamakacittānām ity abhiprāyaḥ. smṛtiviṣayasaṃjñānvayāc cittaviśeṣād
body.translated_text: The <s>pudgala</s>-grasping of some — refers to the <s>Vātsīputrīya</s>s. The grasping of total non-existence by some — the intent is: of the <s>Mādhyamika</s>s. From the connection of recognition following upon the object-domain of memory, [there arises] a mental distinction

body.text: iti. smṛter viṣayo 'nubhūto 'rthaḥ. tatra saṃjñā sānvayo hetur asyeti smṛtiviṣayasaṃjñānvayaś cittaviśeṣaḥ. kiṃcid eva cittaṃ. na sarvam ity arthaḥ. tasmāt smaraṇaṃ bhavati pratyabhijñānaṃ vā.
body.translated_text: — thus. The object-domain of memory is an experienced object. The recognition (<s>saṃjñā</s>) pertaining to that, which follows as a cause — this is the mental distinction [arising] from the connection of recognition following upon the object-domain of memory. It is only a particular mental state, not every [mental state] — this is the meaning. From that, remembrance or re-cognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) occurs.

body.text: evam ubhayaviśeṣaṇe kṛte pṛcchati kīdṛśāc cittaviśeṣād iti.
body.translated_text: Having thus qualified both, he asks: 'From what kind of mental distinction?'

body.text: āha. tadābhoga iti vistaraḥ. tasmin smartavya ābhogas tadābhogaḥ. yatra tena sadṛśāḥ saṃbaṃdhinaś ca saṃjñādayo ye te vidyante 'syeti tadābhogasadṛśasaṃbaṃdhisaṃjñādimāṃś cittaviśeṣaḥ. ādigrahaṇena praṇidhānanibandhābhyāsādigrahaṇaṃ. [Tib. 376a] āśrayaviśeṣaś ca śokataś ca vyākṣepataś cādir eṣām iti āśrayaviśeṣaśokavyākṣepādīni. tair anupahataprabhāvaś cittaviśeṣaḥ. sa evam anena darśito bhavati. tasmād īdṛśāc cittaviśeṣāt smṛtir bhavati. tad idam uktaṃ bhavati. tadābhogavataḥ yadi tatrābhogaḥ kriyate. sadṛśasaṃjñādimataḥ yatra sādṛśyāt smṛtir bhavati. sambandhisaṃjñādimataḥ yatrāntareṇāpi sādṛśyaṃ dhūmādidarśanāt smṛtir bhavati. praṇidhānanibaṃdhābhyāsādimataś ca yatra praṇidhānam atra kāle smartavyam abhyāso vāsya tatsmartavyādi. āśrayaviśeṣādibhir anupahataprabhāvatvād iti. vyādhilakṣaṇenāśrayaviśeṣeṇa śokena vyākṣepeṇānyatra kārye. ādiśabdagṛhītaiś ca karmavidyādibhiḥ. tādṛśo 'pīti vistaraḥ. tadābhogayāvatsaṃjñādimān anupahataprabhāvo 'pīty arthaḥ. atadanvaya iti. asmṛtiviṣayasaṃjñānvaya ity arthaḥ. bhāvayitum utpādayituṃ. anyādṛśa iti. atadābhogayāvatsaṃjñādimān anupahataprabhāvo vā. anyasya cittaviśeṣād anyasya.
body.translated_text: He says: 'With the engagement toward that (<s>tadābhoga</s>)' — in detail. The engagement toward that which is to be remembered is <s>tadābhoga</s>. That which possesses recognitions and the rest that are similar to and connected with that [object of memory] — this is the mental distinction possessing the engagement toward that, [along with] similar and connected recognitions and the rest. By the word 'and the rest' (<s>ādi</s>), resolution (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), binding attention (<s>nibandha</s>), repeated practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>), and the rest are included. [Tib. 376a] Particular conditions of the basis (<s>āśrayaviśeṣa</s>), grief (<s>śoka</s>), and distraction (<s>vyākṣepa</s>) — these and the rest are particular conditions of the basis, grief, distraction, and the like. The mental distinction whose power is not impaired by those [factors]. That has been shown by this. Therefore, from such a mental distinction, memory arises. Thus this has been said: for one who has the engagement toward that — if the engagement is made toward that [object]; for one who has similar recognitions and the rest — where memory arises due to similarity; for one who has connected recognitions and the rest — where, even without similarity, memory arises from seeing smoke and the like; and for one who has resolution, binding attention, repeated practice, and the rest — where there is resolution 'at this time it should be remembered,' or repeated practice of that which is to be remembered, and the like. And 'whose power is not impaired by particular conditions of the basis and the rest' — by particular conditions of the basis characterized by illness, by grief, by distraction toward other tasks, and by what is included by the word 'and the rest,' namely action (<s>karma</s>), knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), and the like. 'Even one of such a kind' — in detail. The meaning is: even one who has the engagement toward that, and so on up to recognitions and the rest, and whose power is not impaired. 'Not following that' — the meaning is: not following the recognition pertaining to the object-domain of memory. 'To produce, to generate.' 'Of another kind' — one who does not have the engagement toward that, or the recognitions and the rest, or whose power is not impaired. 'From the mental distinction of one, for another' —

body.text: na. asaṃbaṃdhād iti. devadattayajñadattacetasor akāryakāraṇabhāvenāsaṃbaṃdhād [Tib. 376b] ity arthaḥ. yathaikasāṃtānikayoś cetasoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvāt saṃbaṃdho. naivaṃ devadattayajñadattacetasoḥ saṃbandhaḥ. ity anena dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayor asāmyaṃ darśayati. tatra yadi pareṇaivaṃ sādhanam abhidhīyate. na devadattānubhavacittānubhūtam arthaṃ tatsmaraṇacittaṃ smarati. anyatvāt. yajñadattacittavad iti. tad asādhanaṃ. hetoḥ svayamaniścitatvāt pratyakṣavirodhena ca pūrvapakṣasāpakṣālatvāt. atha devadattānubhavacittānusmaraṇacittayor anyatvapratijñāyām idaṃ dūṣaṇam udgrāhyet. tad adūṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭabādhāyāṃ dūṣaṇānupapatteḥ. bhavatsiddhānte 'pi hi devadattānubhavacittānubhūtam arthaṃ tatsmaraṇacittaṃ smaratīti. na ca brūmo 'nyena cetasā dṛṣṭam anyat anyat smaratīti. na yatkiṃcid anyat
body.translated_text: No. Because of the absence of connection — the meaning is: because of the absence of connection in the manner of cause-and-effect between the minds of <s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Yajñadatta</s>. [Tib. 376b] Just as there is connection between two mental states belonging to one continuum because of the cause-and-effect relationship — there is no such connection between the minds of <s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Yajñadatta</s>. By this he shows the dissimilarity between the example and the exemplified. Therein, if the opponent states the proof thus: 'The mind of <s>Devadatta</s>'s recollection does not remember the object experienced by <s>Devadatta</s>'s experiencing mind — because of otherness — like the mind of <s>Yajñadatta</s>' — that is not a valid proof, because of the uncertainty of the reason itself and because of the contradiction with direct perception, making the prior thesis untenable. But if this objection is raised against the thesis that <s>Devadatta</s>'s experiencing mind and recollecting mind are other — that is not a valid objection, because objections do not apply when there is observed invalidation. For even in your own system, <s>Devadatta</s>'s recollecting mind remembers the object experienced by <s>Devadatta</s>'s experiencing mind. And we do not say 'what is seen by one mind, another [mind] remembers [something] altogether other'

body.text: smaratīty abhiprāyaḥ. darśanacittāt smṛticittam anyad evotpadyata iti. vidyamānakāraṇatvād vidyamānabījāṃkuravad ity arthaḥ. smaraṇād eva ca pratyabhijñānam iti. smaraṇe sati pratyabhijñānaṃ. tad evedaṃ yan mayā dṛṣṭam iti smaraṇāt.
body.translated_text: — this is the intent. 'From the seeing-mind, a memory-mind that is indeed other arises' — because of having an existing cause, like the existing seed-and-sprout — this is the meaning. And recognition is from memory itself — when memory exists, recognition arises: 'This is indeed that which was seen by me' — from that memory.

body.text: yat tarhīti. yadi cittaviśeṣa eva smarati. yat tarhi caitraḥ smaratīti tat katham iti vākyādhyāhāraḥ. sa cāpi tasyeti vistaraḥ. sa cāpi caitrābhidhānaḥ. saṃskārasamūhasaṃtānas tasya gavākhyasya deśāṃtaravikārotpattau [Tib. 377a] deśāntarotpattau vikārotpattau ca kāraṇabhāvaṃ cetasikṛtvā. kiṃ. svāmīty ucyate. na tu pudgalaṃ. kāryakāraṇabhāvāpekṣo 'yaṃ vyavahāraḥ. na pudgalāpekṣa ity abhiprāyaḥ. ata evāha. na tu kaścid iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: 'But what about this' — if it is indeed the mental distinction that remembers, then 'what about this, that <s>Caitra</s> remembers?' — how is that [to be understood]? — this is the sentence to be supplied. 'And that too, of that' — in detail. And that one too, called <s>Caitra</s> — the continuum of the assemblage of <s>saṃskāra</s>s (formations), having made a causal connection with the arising of transformation in another location [Tib. 377a] — arising in another location and arising of transformation — of that one called 'cow' [as an analogy] — what [is it called]? — 'owner' — thus it is called. Not the <s>pudgala</s>. This usage is dependent on the cause-and-effect relationship, not dependent on a <s>pudgala</s> — this is the intent. Therefore he says: 'But no one' — in detail.

body.text: evaṃ ko vijānātīti vistaraḥ. asaty ātmani ka evaṃ vijānāti. vijānātīti ko 'rthaḥ. vijñānena viṣayaṃ gṛhṇāti. kiṃ tad grahaṇam anyad vijñānat. vijñānaṃ tarhi karoti. uktaḥ saḥ. yas tat karoti. vijñānahetur indriyārthamanaskārāḥ. cittaviśeṣa iti tan na vaktavyaṃ. indriyādihetvantarayogāt. ata eva cocyate yathāyogam ity eṣa viśeṣa iti. yat tarhi caitro vijānātīty ucyate. tato hi caitrākhyāt saṃtānād bhavadṛṣṭocyate. asaty ātmani kasyedaṃ vijñānaṃ. kim arthaiṣā ṣaṣṭhī. svāmyarthā. yathā kasya kaḥ svāmīti vistareṇa yāvat kva ca punar vijñānaṃ viniyoktavyaṃ yata etasya svāmī mṛgyate. vijñātavye 'rthe. kim arthaṃ viniyoktavyaṃ. vijñānārtham. aho sūktāni sukhaidhitānāṃ. tad eva hi nāma tadarthaṃ viniyoktavyam iti. kathaṃ ca viniyoktavyaṃ. utpādanata āhosvit saṃpreṣaṇataḥ. vijñānagatyayogād utpādanataḥ. [Tib. 377b] hetur eva tarhi svāmīti vistareṇa yāvad yo hy eva heturvijñānasya tasyaivāsau. yaś cāpi sa caitrābhidhāna iti vistareṇa yāvan na tatrāpi hetubhāvaṃ vyatītyāsti svāmibhāva iti. ādiśabdena ko vedayate kasya vedanā. kaḥ saṃjānīte kasya saṃjñety evamādi. eṣā dig iti.
body.translated_text: 'Thus, who cognizes?' — in detail. In the absence of a self, who cognizes thus? What is the meaning of 'cognizes'? One apprehends an object through consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). Is that apprehension something other than consciousness? Then consciousness does the [cognizing]. He has been stated — the one who does that. The causes of consciousness are the sense faculty, object, and attention (<s>manaskāra</s>). 'A particular state of mind' — this should not be stated, because of the connection with other causal factors such as the sense faculty and the rest. For this very reason it is said: 'as applicable' — this is the distinction. But then, the statement '<s>Caitra</s> cognizes' — that is said with reference to the continuum called <s>Caitra</s>, as you [the opponent] see it. 'In the absence of a self, whose is this consciousness?' What is the purpose of this genitive case? It expresses ownership. Just as 'whose is whose owner?' — in detail, up to: 'And moreover, to what purpose should consciousness be applied, such that an owner of it is sought?' To the object to be cognized. For what purpose should it be applied? For the purpose of consciousness. 'Ah, well-spoken words of those who prosper at ease!' — for that very thing is to be applied for the purpose of that itself! And how should it be applied? Through production or through dispatching? Because of the impossibility of consciousness going — through production. [Tib. 377b] 'Then the cause itself is the owner' — in detail, up to: 'whatever is the cause of consciousness, to that alone it belongs.' 'And also whoever is called <s>Caitra</s>' — in detail, up to: 'even there, beyond the state of being a cause, there is no state of being an owner.' By the word 'and the rest': 'who feels? whose is feeling? who perceives? whose is perception?' — and so forth of this kind. This is the direction.

body.text: yo 'py āha. bhāvasya bhavitrapekṣād iti vaiyākaraṇaḥ. tena bhavitavyam iti. vijñātrā bhavitavyaṃ pudgalenety abhiprāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'He who also says: "Because of the existence [<s>bhāva</s>] requiring an existent [<s>bhavitr</s>]"' — [this is] the grammarian. By that, there must be an existent. The intent is: there must be a cognizer — a <s>pudgala</s> (person).

body.text: gacchatigamanābhidhānavad iti. yathā jvālā gacchati śabdo gacchatīti gacchatiśabdābhidhānaṃ. yathā jvālāyāḥ śabdasya vā gamanam. evaṃ devadatto gacchati devadattasya gamanam. anena dṛṣṭāntena vijānāti devadatta iti sidhyati.
body.translated_text: 'Like the expression of "goes" and "going"' — just as 'the flame goes,' 'the sound goes' — this is the expression with the word 'goes.' Just as the going of the flame or of the sound — so too '<s>Devadatta</s> goes' — the going of <s>Devadatta</s>. By this example, '<s>Devadatta</s> cognizes' is established.

body.text: sādṛśyenātmalābhād iti. kāraṇasādṛśyena kāryātmalābhāt. akurvad api kiṃcid iti. parispandam akurvad apīty arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Because of the obtaining of [its] own nature through similarity' — because of the obtaining of the nature of the effect through the similarity of the cause. 'Even without doing anything' — the meaning is: even without making any movement.

body.text: tadākārateti. nīlādiviṣayākāratety arthaḥ. vijñāne kāraṇabhāvād iti.
body.translated_text: 'Of that aspect' — the meaning is: of the aspect of the object such as blue and the rest. 'Because of being a cause with respect to consciousness'

body.text: vijñānaṃ vijñānāntarsya kāraṇam. ato vijñānāntaram utpādād vijānātīty ucyate. kāraṇe kartṛśabdaniveśād iti. kāraṇaṃ kartṛbhūtam iti kṛtvā. tadyathā nādasya kāraṇaṃ ghaṇṭeti ghaṇṭā rautīty ucyate. tadvat.
body.translated_text: — consciousness is the cause of another consciousness. Therefore, because of the production of another consciousness, it is said 'it cognizes.' 'Because of the application of the agent-word to the cause' — considering that the cause is the agent. Just as, for example, a bell is the cause of a sound, and therefore it is said 'the bell sounds' — so too.

body.text: Tib. 378a
body.translated_text: Tib. 378a

body.text: pradīpa iti. arciṣāṃ saṃtāne pradīpa iti upacaryate. eka iveti kṛtvā. sa deśāntareṣūtpadyamānaḥ saṃtānarūpaḥ pradīpadeśāntareṣūtpadyamānaḥ. taṃtaṃ deśaṃ gacchatīty ucyate. evaṃ cittānāṃ saṃtāne vijñānam ity upacaryate. ekam iveti kṛtvā. tat saṃtānarūpaṃ vijñānaṃ viṣayāntareṣūtpadyamānaṃ taṃtaṃ viṣayaṃ vijānātīty ucyate. saṃtānena vijñānotpattyā vijānātīty abhiprāyaḥ. yathā vā rūpaṃ bhavatīti vistaraḥ. yathā bhavitū rūpasya bhāvāj janitur jāteḥ sthātuḥ sthiter anarthāntaratvam. evaṃ vijñāne 'pi syāt. vijñātur vijñānasya bhāvād anarthāntaratvaṃ. vyatiriktasya bhāvasyānupalabdheḥ. vaiśeṣikasūtrānusārād vā.
body.translated_text: 'Lamp' — in the continuum of flames, the term 'lamp' is applied figuratively — as if it were one. That [lamp], arising in different locations, in the form of a continuum — a lamp arising in different locations — is said to 'go to this and that place.' Similarly, in the continuum of mental moments, the term 'consciousness' (<s>vijñāna</s>) is applied figuratively — as if it were one. That consciousness, in the form of a continuum, arising with respect to different objects, is said to 'cognize this and that object.' The intent is: through the arising of consciousness in a continuum, it cognizes. 'Or just as form exists' — in detail. Just as the existence of a thing-to-be (<s>bhavitr</s>) is non-different from the existence (<s>bhāva</s>) of form — [meaning] the existence of a generator is non-different from generation, the existence of a stander is non-different from standing — so too it should be in the case of consciousness. The existence of a cognizer is non-different from consciousness — because of the non-apprehension of anything distinct. Or, following the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: nātmana iti. yadi nātmano vijñānam utpadyate vijñānalakṣaṇasyāviśeṣāt tādṛśam eva vijñānam utpadyeta. yadi tv ātmanaḥ tasyābhiprāyaviśeṣād viśiṣṭaṃ jñānam utpadyetety abhiprāyaḥ. na ca kramaniyameneti. kasmāc ca na kramaniyamenotpadyate. aniyamenāpi hy utpadyate gobuddher anantaraṃ strībhuddhiḥ. strībuddher mahiṣabhuddhiḥ. kasmād gobuddhir evānantaraṃ notpadyate. aṃkurakāṇḍapattrādivad iti. aṃkurāt kāṇḍa evotpadyate [Tib. 378b] na pattrādi. kāṇḍāt pattram evotpadyate na puṣpādy aṃkurādi vā. tadvat.
body.translated_text: 'Not from a self' — if consciousness does not arise from a self, then because of the non-differentiation of the characteristic of consciousness, only such consciousness would arise [always the same]. But if [it arises] from a self, then because of the specific intention of that [self], differentiated knowledge would arise — this is the intent. 'And not in a fixed sequence' — and why does it not arise in a fixed sequence? Because it also arises without a fixed sequence — after a cognition of a cow, a cognition of a woman; after a cognition of a woman, a cognition of a buffalo. Why does a cow-cognition alone not arise immediately after [a cow-cognition]? 'Like a sprout, stalk, leaf, and the rest' — from a sprout, only a stalk arises, [Tib. 378b] not a leaf and the rest. From a stalk, only a leaf arises, not a flower and the rest, or a sprout and the rest. So too.

body.text: nikāmadhyānasamāhitānām iti. nikāmena paryāptena samāptena dhyānena samāhitānām. sadṛśakāyacittotpattau sadṛśasya kāyasya cittasya cotpattau. svayaṃvyutthānam iti. na paropakrameṇety abhiprāyaḥ. evam anena kasmān na nityaṃ sadṛśam evotpadyata ity yat pṛṣṭaṃ. tad visarjanaṃ. yat tu pṛṣṭaṃ na ca kramaniyameneti. tad darśayann āha. kramo 'pi hi cittānām niyatam eveti. abhīṣṭam evaitat. gotraviśeṣād iti bhāvanāviśeṣāt. strīcittād iti vistaraḥ. strīcittāt stryālambanāc cittād anantaraṃ tasyāḥ striyāḥ kāyas tatkāyaḥ. tatkāyasya vidūsāṇāyai yadi parivrājakasyānyasya vā sādhoś cittam utpannaṃ bhavati. tatpatiputrādicittaṃ vā. tasyāḥ patiputrādayaḥ. ādiśabdena duhitrādayo gṛhyante. tadālambanaṃ cittaṃ tatpatiputrādicittaṃ. tad vānyatarad yad idaṃ tasmāt strīcittād anantam utpannaṃ bhavati. punaś ca kālāntareṇa saṃtatipariṇāmena strīcittam utpadyate. tat paścād utpannaṃ strīcittaṃ
body.translated_text: 'Of those fully concentrated in deep meditation (<s>nikāmadhyāna</s>)' — of those concentrated with complete, sufficient, accomplished meditation. 'When there is the arising of a similar body and mind' — when there is the arising of a similar body and similar mind. 'Self-emergence' — the intent is: not through the intervention of another. Thus, by this, what was asked — 'why does not always only a similar [consciousness] arise?' — that is answered. But as for what was asked — 'and not in a fixed sequence' — showing that, he says: 'For the sequence of mental moments is indeed fixed' — this is exactly what is accepted. 'Because of the distinction of lineage (<s>gotra</s>)' — because of the distinction of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). 'From a woman-thought' — in detail. From a woman-thought — a thought having a woman as its object — immediately after that, [there arises a thought about] the body of that woman — her body. For the corruption of that body — if a thought arises in a wandering ascetic or in another virtuous person. Or a thought of her husband, sons, and the rest — her husbands, sons, and the rest. By the word 'and the rest,' daughters and the rest are included. A thought having them as its object — a thought of her husband, sons, and the rest. That, or another [thought] — whatever arises immediately after that woman-thought. And again, after an interval of time, through the transformation of the continuum, a woman-thought arises. That subsequently arisen woman-thought

body.text: samarthaṃ bhavati tatkāyavidūṣaṇācittotpādane tatstrīkāyavidūṣaṇācittotpādane tatpatiputrādicittotpādane vā samarthaṃ. kasmād ity [Tib. 379a] āha. tadgotratvād iti. tadkāyavidūsaṇācittaṃ tatpatiputrādicittaṃ vā gotraṃ bījam asyeti tadgotraṃ. cittaṃ tasya bhāvaḥ. tasmāt. tajjātīyatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ. anyathety atadgotraṃ. atha punaḥ paryāyeṇeti vistaraḥ. paryāyeṇāyugapat. strīcittāt tatkāyavidūṣaṇācittaṃ tatas tatpaticittaṃ tatas tatputracittaṃ tata eva ca tadduhitṛcittaṃ tata eva ca tadupakaraṇādicittaṃ utpannaṃ bhavati. tataḥ strīcittād anaṃtarotpannebhyaś cittebhyo yad bahutaraṃ pravāhataḥ paṭutaraṃ śaktitaḥ āsannataraṃ vāsyotpādyasya cittasya. tad eva cittam utpadyate. tadbhāvanāyā balīyastvāt tasya bahutarasya paṭutarasyāsannatarasya vā bhāvanāyā balavattaratvāt. anyatreti vistaraḥ. tatkālapratyupasthitas tatkālikaḥ kāyapratyayaviśeṣo bāhyapratyayaviśeṣaś ca. tasmād anyatra tasmād ṛta ity arthaḥ. tad eva hy upapadyate yasya kāyo bāhyo vā pratyayaviṣaya uptiṣṭhate.
body.translated_text: is capable of producing a thought of corrupting that [woman's] body — of corrupting that woman's body — or of producing a thought of her husband, sons, and the rest — is capable. Why? [Tib. 379a] He says: 'Because of being of that lineage (<s>gotra</s>)' — a thought of corrupting that body, or a thought of her husband, sons, and the rest — that is the lineage, the seed, of this [thought]. The state of that — because of that. The intent is: because of being of the same class. 'Otherwise' — of a different lineage. 'And then again, in succession' — in detail. In succession, not simultaneously. From a woman-thought, a thought of corrupting that body [arises]; from that, a thought of her husband; from that, a thought of her son; and from that itself, a thought of her daughter; and from that itself, a thought of her possessions and the rest — [these] arise. Then, from the thoughts arisen immediately after that woman-thought, whichever is more abundant in terms of flow, sharper in terms of power, or nearer [in terms of recency] to the consciousness to be produced — that very thought arises. Because of the greater strength of the cultivation of that — of that which is more abundant, sharper, or nearer — because of the greater strength of cultivation. 'Except for' — in detail. A particular bodily condition present at that time — an external condition particular [to that time]. Therefore, 'except for that' — means 'apart from that.' For only that [thought] arises for which the bodily or external condition-object presents itself.

body.text: saiva balīyasīti. yā bahutarasya paṭutarasya āsannatarasya vābhihitā saiva balīyasi bhāvanā. kasmān nityaṃ na phalati na hi tac cittaṃ nivartate.
body.translated_text: 'That very one is the stronger' — that which was stated as the cultivation of the more abundant, sharper, or nearer — that very one is the stronger cultivation. Why does it not always bear fruit? — for that thought does not cease [to exist].

body.text: vartata itītareṇa codita āha. sthityanyathātvalakṣaṇatvāt. [Tib. 379b] sthiter anyathātvaṃ lakṣaṇam asyeti sthityanyathātvalakṣaṇaṃ. tadbhāvāt. tasya cānyathātvasya saṃskṛtalakṣaṇasya. anyabhāvanāphalotpattau anyabhāvanāphalasya cittāntarasyotpattāv ānuguṇyān nityaṃ na phalati tad evety arthasaṃbandhaḥ.
body.translated_text: Being challenged by the other, he says: 'Because of having the characteristic of alteration of persistence.' [Tib. 379b] That whose characteristic is alteration of persistence — whose mark is the alteration of persistence — because of the existence of that — of that alteration, which is a characteristic of the conditioned. Because of the fitness for the arising of the fruit of another cultivation — because of the fitness for the arising of another mental moment that is the fruit of another cultivation — it does not always bear fruit, that very [thought] — this is the connection of meaning.

body.text: evaṃ hy āhur iti sthavirarāhulaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'For thus they say' — this is Elder <s>Rāhula</s>.

body.text: iti sarvaprakāraṃ. yāvanto
body.translated_text: meaning in every manner. 'However many' —

body.text: varṇasaṃniveśādiprakārāḥ. teṣāṃ
body.translated_text: the varieties of color-arrangement and the rest. 'Of those' —

children.text: idam asya kāraṇaṃ yenaivaṃ varṇaḥ evaṃ saṃniveśaḥ evaṃ snigdhateti. evamādibhir ākārair
children.translated_text: 'this is its cause' — by which there is such color, such arrangement, such sleekness — and so forth. By such aspects —

body.text: na jñātuṃ śakyaṃ. kaiḥ.
body.translated_text: cannot be known. By whom?

body.text: śrāvakapratyekabuddhādibhiḥ.
body.translated_text: by <s>śrāvaka</s>s, <s>pratyekabuddha</s>s, and the like.

children.translated_text: 'For that knowledge is the power of the omniscient' —

body.text: sarvavidbalaṃ hi taj jñānaṃ. yena tat kāraṇaṃ jñāyata ity abhiprāyaḥ. prāg
body.translated_text: for that knowledge is the power of the all-knowing. The intent is: by which that cause is known. 'Earlier'

body.text: evarūpiṇāṃ cittabhedānām iti. rūpakāraṇam api sarvathā jñātum aśakyaṃ kim arūpiṇām ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'of such varieties of mental moments' — if even the cause of form cannot be known in every way, how much less [can] that of the formless [be known] — this is the meaning.

body.text: ekīyas tīrthika iti vaiśeṣikaḥ. manaḥsaṃyogaviśeṣāpekṣatvād iti cet. syān mataṃ tulye 'py ātmaprabhavatve cittotpatter ātmā kadācit karhicin manaḥsaṃyogaviśeṣam apekṣate. ity ato na nityaṃ tādṛśam eva cittam utpadyate na ca kramaniyamenāṃkurakāṇḍapattrādivad iti. na. anyasaṃyogāsiddheḥ. [Tib. 380a] naitad evaṃ. kasmāt. tābhyām ātmamanobhyām anyasya saṃyogasyāsiddheḥ. na hi saṃyogo nāma bhāvaḥ kaścid asmākaṃ siddho 'sti. saṃyoginoś ceti vistaraḥ. abhyupagate 'pi saṃyoge saṃyoginoś ceti vistaraḥ. lokaprasiddhayoḥ kāṣṭhayor anyayor vā kayościt. paricchinnatvāt paricchinnadeśadṛṣṭatvād ity arthaḥ. lakṣaṇavyākhyānde ceti. vaiśeṣikataṃtre saṃyogalakṣaṇanirdeśāt. tataḥ kim ātmanaḥ paricchedaprasaṃgaḥ. paricchinnadeśatvaprasaṃgaḥ. yatrātmā. na tatra manaḥ. yatra manaḥ. na tatrātmeti. anenānumānāgamāpattito dharmiviśeṣaviparyayo 'sya pakṣasya saṃdarśito bhavati. manasā saṃyoga ātmana iti. ātmā dharmī. tasya viśeṣaḥ sarvagatvaṃ. tadviparyayo 'sarvagatatvam iti. tato manaḥsaṃcārād ātmanaḥ saṃcāraprasaṃgād iti. tato lakṣaṇād aprāptipūrvikā prāptiḥ saṃyoga iti manaḥsaṃcārād yaṃyaṃ śarīrapradeśaṃ manaḥ saṃcarati. tatastata ātmā saṃcaraty apaitīti prasajyate. tadyathā yaṃyaṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ puruṣaḥ saṃcarati. tatastata ātapo 'pasarpati. tathā ca sati niḥkriyatvam asya bādhitaṃ bhavatīti. sa eva pratijñādoṣaḥ. vināśasya vā. prasaṃga iti vartate. ātmana iti ca. yatrayatra manaḥ saṃcarati. tatratatrātmā vinaśyatīti. sa eva cātra pratijñādoṣaḥ. ātmano nityatvanivṛtteḥ. pradeśasaṃyoga [Tib. 380b] iti cet. syān matam ātmanā pradeśena saṃyogo manasaḥ. ātmano vā pradeśena manasā saha saṃyogaḥ. yasmiṃ charīrapradeśe mano 'vasthitaṃ bhavati. tadgatenātmapradeśena mano na saṃyujyate. pradeśāntareṇānyapārśvataḥ saṃyujyate. tasṃād aprāptipūrvakatve 'pi saṃyogasyāprāptenaivātmapradeśena manaḥ saṃyujyata iti. tan na. tasyaiva tatpradeśatvāyogāt. na hy ātmano 'nyapradeśa vidyaṃte. na caivātmaivātmanaḥ pradeśo yujyate. astu vā saṃyoga iti vistaraḥ. abhyupetyāpi saṃyogaṃ tathāpi nirvikāratvād aviśiṣṭe manasi kathaṃ saṃyogaviśeṣaḥ. kathaṃ viśiṣṭaḥ saṃyogo bhavati. yate evam uktaṃ manaḥsaṃyogaviśeṣāpekṣatvād iti. buddhiviśeṣāpekṣatvād iti cet. sa evopari codyate kathaṃ buddhiviśeṣa iti. kasmān na nityam īdṛśam evotpadyate cittam aviśiṣṭe ātmanīti. kāraṇaviśeṣād dhi kāryaviśeṣa
body.translated_text: "A certain non-Buddhist" — the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>. "If [one objects:] because of depending on a special conjunction of mind" — one might think: even though both arise from the self equally, the self sometimes depends on a special conjunction with mind — therefore not always the same kind of consciousness arises, and not in a fixed sequence like sprout, stalk, leaf, and the rest. No. Because of the unestablished nature of the other conjunction. [Tib. 380a] This is not so. Why? Because the conjunction other than those two — self and mind — is not established. For no entity called "conjunction" (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is established for us. "And of the two things conjoined" — in detail. Even granting conjunction — "of the two things conjoined" — in detail — of two things well-known in the world, such as two sticks or any others. Because of their being delimited — the meaning is: because of being observed as having delimited spatial extent. "And in the definition-explanation" — from the statement of the definition of conjunction in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> treatise. What follows from that? The consequence of the delimitation of the self — the consequence of having delimited spatial extent. Where the self is, there the mind is not; where the mind is, there the self is not. By this, from the inference and scripture-based objection (<s>āgamāpatti</s>), the contradiction of the specific property of the subject (<s>dharmiviśeṣaviparyaya</s>) of this thesis is shown. "The self has conjunction with mind" — the self is the subject (<s>dharmin</s>). Its specific property is omnipresence (<s>sarvagatatva</s>). The contradiction of that is non-omnipresence. "Therefore, from the movement of mind, the consequence of the movement of the self" — from that definition, conjunction is the attainment preceded by non-attainment — therefore, from the movement of mind, to whatever bodily region the mind moves, the self would move and depart from there — this is the consequence. Just as to whatever region of the earth a person moves, from there the heat retreats. And in that case, its actionlessness (<s>niḥkriyatva</s>) would be contradicted. This is the very defect of the thesis. "Or [the consequence] of destruction" — this continues. "Of the self" — also [continues]. Wherever the mind moves, there the self would be destroyed. And this too is the very defect of the thesis — because of the negation of the self's permanence. "If [one says:] conjunction of a part" — [Tib. 380b] one might think: it is a part of the self that has conjunction with mind. Or: a part of the self is in conjunction with mind. In whatever bodily region the mind is situated, the mind is not conjoined with the part of the self that has gone there — it is conjoined with another part, from another side. Therefore, even though conjunction is preceded by non-attainment, the mind is conjoined with a very part of the self that has not [yet] attained [conjunction]. That is not [valid]. Because of the impossibility of that [self] having such parts. For the self does not have other parts. Nor is it fitting that the self itself be a part of the self. "Let there be conjunction" — in detail. Even granting conjunction, still, because of the changelessness [of the self], when mind is undifferentiated, how can there be a special conjunction? How can a differentiated conjunction exist? Since it was thus stated: "because of depending on a special conjunction with mind." "If [one says:] because of depending on a special cognition (<s>buddhi</s>)" — this very [objection] is refuted above: "how is there a special cognition?" Why does not always this same kind of consciousness arise when the self is undifferentiated? For a special effect

body.text:
iṣyate śaṃkhapaṭahādiśabdavat. saṃskāraviśeṣāpekṣād ātmamanaḥsaṃyogād iti cet. syān mataṃ nityam aviśiṣṭe 'py ātmani manasi ca saṃskāraviśeṣāpekṣād ātmamanasoḥ saṃyogād buddhiviśeṣa iti. tad uktaṃ bhavati. saṃskāraviśeṣād bhāvanāviśeṣalakṣaṇād ātmamanaḥsaṃyogaviśeṣaḥ. tadviśeṣād buddhiviśeṣa iti. atra brūmaḥ. cittād evāstv iti vistaraḥ. ayam ihācāryasyābhiprāyaḥ. [sāntarbhavaś cittam astīty avivādaḥ] mama tava ca cittam astīty avivādaḥ. [Tib. 381a] saṃskāraviśeṣo 'py asti bhāvanāviśeṣalakṣaṇo yo 'sau vāsanā bījam iti vāsmābhir vyavasthāpyate. bhāvāntaraṃ na veti tuviśeṣaḥ. tasmāc cittād eva saṃskāraviśeṣāpekṣād buddhiviśeṣo 'stu. kim ātmanā tatsaṃyogena vā kalpiteneti. na hi kiṃcid iti vistaraḥ. kuhakenaikatareṇa vaidyena kasmaicit glānāyauṣadhaṃ dadānena cintitaṃ. idam auṣadhaṃ sulabhaṃ. viditaṃ cāsya saparijanasya glānasya. etena cauṣadhenāsya glānasya glānopaśamo bhavet. tad evaṃ mām avadhūyānye 'pi kariṣyanti. tataś ca mamārthalābho na bhaviṣyati. iti cintayitvā tad abhimaṃtrya phūḥ svāhā phūḥ svāheti janasya darśitam. anena mantreṇedam auṣadhaṃ sidhyatīti. tatra yathā kuhakavaidyaphūḥsvāhānām auṣadhakāryasiddhau sāmarthyaṃ nāsti. auṣadhasyaiva tu sāmarthyam. evam ātmano buddhiviśeṣopattau nāsti sāmarthyaṃ. cittasyaiva sāmarthyam iti. saty ātmani tayoḥ saṃbhava iti cet. syān mataṃ. saty ātmani tayoḥ saṃskāracittayoḥ saṃbhavaḥ. ity ato 'sty ātmeti. atra brūmo vāṅmātraṃ.
nātra kācid yuktir astīti. āśrayaḥ sa iti cet. syān matam. ātmāśrayas tayor iti. yathā kaḥ kasyāśraya iti. āśrayarūpeṇodāharaṇaṃ mṛgyate. tam asyāśrayārtham ayuktaṃ darśayann āha. na hi te [Tib. 381b] iti vistaraḥ. te saṃskāracitte. citrabadarādivat. yathā kuḍye citram ādhāryaṃ badaraṃ ca kuṇḍe. ādiśabdena bhājane bhojanam ityādi. naiva te saṃskāracitte tatrātmany ādheye. dhārye. nāpi sa kuḍyakuṇḍādivad ādhāro yuktaḥ. nāpi sa ātmā kuḍyavat kuṇḍavac cādhāro yuktaḥ. ādiśabdena bhājanādigrahaṇaṃ. kiṃ karaṇam ity āha. pratighātiyutatvadoṣād iti pratighātitvadoṣād yutatvadoṣāc ca. sapratighatvaprasaṃgāt pṛthagdaśatvaprasaṃgāc cety arthaḥ. yathā citrabadarayoḥ kuḍyakuṇḍayoś cādhāryādhārabhāve pratighātitvam yutatvaṃ ca dṛṣṭe. evam eteṣām api syāt. aniṣṭaṃ caitat. ato 'nātmāśrayaḥ.
body.translated_text: is accepted as [arising] from a special cause — like the sounds of a conch, drum, and the rest. "If [one says:] from the conjunction of self and mind that depends on a special <s>saṃskāra</s> (conditioning)" — one might think: even though the self and mind are perpetually undifferentiated, from the conjunction of self and mind that depends on a special <s>saṃskāra</s>, there is a special cognition. What has been stated amounts to this: from a special <s>saṃskāra</s>, characterized by a special cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), there is a special conjunction of self and mind; from that special [conjunction], a special cognition. Here we say: "Let it be from mind alone" — in detail. The <s>Ācārya</s>'s intent here is: [the fact that] mind exists is undisputed between us and you. [Tib. 381a] A special <s>saṃskāra</s> too exists, characterized by a special cultivation, which we establish as <s>vāsanā</s> (impression) or seed (<s>bīja</s>). Whether it is a separate entity or not is the point of difference. Therefore, let the special cognition be from mind alone, dependent on the special <s>saṃskāra</s>. What need is there for the self or for a fabricated conjunction with it? "For nothing" — in detail. Like a quack physician — one of two physicians — giving medicine to some patient, who thought: "This medicine is easily available and known to his attendants and the patient. By this medicine, the patient's illness could be relieved. If so, others will spurn me too. Then there will be no profit for me." Having thought thus, he enchanted it [saying] "phūḥ svāhā, phūḥ svāhā" and showed it to the people: "By this mantra, this medicine is efficacious." Just as the quack physician's "phūḥ svāhā" has no efficacy in accomplishing the effect of the medicine — but the medicine alone has efficacy — so too the self has no efficacy in producing a special cognition — mind alone has efficacy. "If [one says:] given the existence of the self, those two are possible" — one might think: given the existence of the self, those two — <s>saṃskāra</s> and mind — are possible, and therefore the self exists. Here we say: this is a mere verbal [claim]. There is no reasoning here at all. "If [one says:] it is the support" — one might think: the self is the support of those two. "Like what of what is the support?" — an example in the form of a support is sought. Showing that the meaning of "support" for this is not fitting, he says: "For those two [Tib. 381b]" — in detail. Those two — <s>saṃskāra</s> and mind — like a painting and <s>badara</s> fruit. Just as a painting is placed on a wall, and <s>badara</s> fruit in a vessel — by the word "and the rest," food in a dish, and so forth. Neither are those two — <s>saṃskāra</s> and mind — placeable there, in the self — they cannot be placed there. Nor is that self reasonably a container like a wall or vessel — nor is that self reasonably a container like a wall or vessel. By the word "and the rest," the inclusion of dishes and the like. What is the reason? He says: "Because of the fault of having resistance and having parts" — because of the fault of resistance and the fault of having parts. The meaning is: the consequence of having resistance (<s>sapratighatva</s>) and the consequence of being manifold (<s>pṛthagdaśatva</s>). Just as in the case of painting and <s>badara</s> as container and contained with wall and vessel — resistance and having parts are observed — so too for these. And this is undesired. Therefore the self is not the support.

body.text: yathā na gandhādhibhyo 'nyā pṛthivī. tathā buddhyādibhyo 'nya ātmeti.
body.translated_text: "Just as earth is not other than smell and the rest — so too the self [is not other] than cognition and the rest."

body.text: ko hi satpuruṣo gaṃdhādibhyo 'nyāṃ pṛthivīṃ nidhārayati. na hi pṛthivī katamety ukte rūpagandharasasparśebhyo 'nyā darśayituṃ śakyate yathā rūpaṃ gandhādibhyo 'nyad iti.
body.translated_text: For what wise person would determine earth as other than smell and the rest? For when asked "what is earth?" — it cannot be shown as other than form, smell, taste, and tangible — as form is shown to be other than smell and the rest.

body.text: yadi na gaṃdhādibhyo 'nyā pṛthivī. katham ayaṃ vyapadeśaḥ pṛthivyāṃ gandhādaya iti. anyena hy anyasya vyapadeśo dṛṣṭaḥ. caitrasya kambala iti. ata ucyate. vyapadeśas tu iti vistaraḥ.
body.translated_text: "If earth is not other than smell and the rest, how is this usage: 'smells and the rest are in earth'? For usage of one with respect to another is observed — as "<s>Caitra</s>'s blanket."" Therefore it is said: "But the usage" — in detail.

body.text: Tib. 382a
body.translated_text: Tib. 382a

body.text: viśeṣaṇārthaṃ ity abādibhyo viśeṣaṇārtham ity arthaḥ. katham iti pratipādyati. te hy eveti vistaraḥ. te hy evety evakāras tadvytiriktapṛthivīdravyanivṛttyarthaḥ. te eva gandhādayaḥ. tadākhyāḥ pṛthivyākhyāḥ. yathā vijñāyeran. tathā viśeṣaṇārthaṃ vyapadeśa ity abhisaṃbandhaḥ. nānya iti. nābādyākhyāḥ. pṛthivyākhyebhyo 'nye vijñāyerann ity arthaḥ. kāṣṭhapratimāyāḥ śarīravyapadeśavad iti. yathā kāṣṭhapratimāyāḥ śarīram iti vyapadiśyate. anyābhyo mṛnmayādiviśeṣaṇārthaṃ. na ca kāṣṭhapratimāyāḥ śarīram anyat. evam ihāpi vyapadeśaḥ syāt. na ca gandhādibhyo 'nyā pṛthivīti.
body.translated_text: "For the purpose of specification" — the meaning is: for the purpose of specification from water and the rest. How? — he explains. "For those very" — in detail. "Those very" — the word "very" (<s>eva</s>) is for the purpose of excluding an earth-substance distinct from those. Those very smells and the rest — designated by that name, by the name "earth" — so that they might be known. "For the purpose of specification" — this is connected with "usage." "Not other" — not designated by the name of water and the rest. The meaning is: they would not be known [as other than] those designated by the name of earth. "Like the designation "body" for a wooden statue" — just as a wooden statue is designated as "body" — for the purpose of specification from clay and other [statues]. And the body of a wooden statue is not something other. Similarly here too, the usage would [function] thus — earth is not other than smell and the rest.

body.text: saṃskāraviśeṣāpekṣatva ity ātmamanaḥsaṃyogasya.
body.translated_text: "The dependence on a special <s>saṃskāra</s>" — of the conjunction of self and mind.

body.text: yo hi baliṣṭha iti. saṃskāraviśeṣaḥ. tenānyeṣāṃ saṃskāraviśeṣāṇāṃ pratibandhaḥ.
body.translated_text: "That which is strongest" — the special <s>saṃskāra</s>. By that, there is the obstruction of other special <s>saṃskāra</s>s.

body.text: sa eva baliṣṭhaḥ kasmān nityaṃ na phalatīty ācāryavacanaṃ.
body.translated_text: "Why does that very strongest not always produce fruit?" — this is the <s>Ācārya</s>'s statement.

body.text: sa eva punar āha. yo 'sya nyāyo yaḥ saṃskārasya nyāyo vināśaḥ pratibandho vā.
body.translated_text: He himself again says: "Whatever is the nature of that" — whatever is the nature of the <s>saṃskāra</s> — destruction or obstruction.

body.text: so 'stu bhāvanāyā bījātmikāyāḥ. ātmā tu nirarthako niḥprayojanaḥ kalpyate. saṃskārārthā hi tatkalpanā syāt. tasya ca saṃskārasya yat kāryaṃ. tad bhāvanayaiva kriyata iti.
body.translated_text: "Let that [nature] belong to cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), which is of the nature of a seed." But the self is fabricated as purposeless, without function. For that fabrication would be for the purpose of <s>saṃskāra</s>. And whatever is the effect of that <s>saṃskāra</s> — that is accomplished by cultivation alone.

body.text: smṛtyādīnām iti vistaraḥ. syān mataṃ. smṛtisaṃskārecchādveṣādīnāṃ [Tib. 382b] guṇapadārthatvāt tasya ca guṇapadārthasyāvaśyadravyāśritatvād dravyāśrayaś ca guṇavān ity evaṃ lakṣaṇopadeśāt. na caiṣām anya āśrayaḥ pṛthvyādiko yujyate 'parapratyakṣatvādhibhiḥ. kāraṇaiḥ. ato ya eṣām āśrayaḥ. sa ātmā. tasmād asty ātmeti.
body.translated_text: "Of memory and the rest" — in detail. One might think: since memory, <s>saṃskāra</s>, desire, aversion, and the rest [Tib. 382b] are of the category of quality (<s>guṇapadārtha</s>), and since that category of quality necessarily depends on a substance (<s>dravya</s>), and since the instruction on the definition is "a substance that possesses qualities is qualified by them" — and since no other support of these, such as earth and the rest, is fitting — for reasons such as not being perceptible by another's direct perception — therefore, whatever is the support of these, that is the self. Hence the self exists.

body.text: na. asiddheḥ. naitad evaṃ. kasmāt. smṛtyādīnāṃ guṇapadārthatvāsiddheḥ. vidyamānaṃ dravyam iti. yat svalakṣaṇato vidyamānaṃ. tad dravyaṃ. ṣaṭ dravyāṇi śrāmaṇyaphalānīti. rūpaskandhādīni paṃca skandhāni śrāmaṇyaphalāny asaṃskṛtaṃ ca ṣaṣṭham iti ṣaṭ dravyāṇi bhavanti. nāpy eṣām iti. smṛtyādinaṃ. parīkṣito hy āśrayārtha iti. yathā kaḥ kasyāśrayaḥ. na hi te citrabadarādivad ādhārya iti vistareṇa.
body.translated_text: No. Because of non-establishment. This is not so. Why? Because the status of memory and the rest as the category of quality is not established. "An existing substance" — whatever exists by its own characteristic — that is a substance. "The six substances are the fruits of the ascetic life" — the five aggregates beginning with the form aggregate are the fruits of the ascetic life, and the unconditioned as the sixth — thus there are six substances. "Nor of these" — of memory and the rest. "For the meaning of 'support' has been examined" — as to what is the support of what. "For those two are not to be placed like a painting and <s>badara</s> fruit" — in detail.

body.text: ete prakārā iti. gaurādiprakārāḥ. skaṃdheṣv ayam ity ahaṃkarāḥ. na tv ahaṃkāra iti. na tv aham ity evam ākaraḥ pratyaya ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: "These modes" — modes such as cow and the rest. "The I-notion (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) regarding the aggregates." "But it is not the I-notion" — but it is not a cognition of the form "I" — this is the meaning.

body.text: idaṃ punas tad evāyātam iti. kimarthaiṣā ṣaṣṭhī. svāmyarthā. yathā kaḥ kasyo svāmī. yathā goś caitraḥ katham asau tasyāḥ svāmī. tadadhīno hi tasyāvāhadhohādiṣu [Tib. 383a] viniyogaḥ. kva ca punar ahaṃkāro viniyoktavyo yata etasya svāmi mṛgyate. ahaṃkartavye 'rthe. kimarthaṃ viniyoktayaḥ. ahaṃkārārtham. aho sūktāni sukhaidhitānāṃ. sa eva hi nāma tadarthaṃ viniyoktavya iti. kathaṃ ca viniyoktvyaḥ. utpādanataḥ āhosvit saṃpreṣaṇataḥ. ahaṃkāragatyayogād utpādanataḥ. hetur eva tarhi svāmi prāpnoti. phalam eva ca svaṃ. yasmād dhetor ādhipatyaṃ phale. phalena ca tadvān hetur iti.
body.translated_text: "But this has come to the same point" — what is the purpose of this genitive [case]? It has the meaning of ownership. "Like what of what is the owner?" — like <s>Caitra</s> of a cow. How is he the owner of that? Because the deployment of that [cow] — in drawing, milking, and the rest — [Tib. 383a] is dependent on him. But where, then, is the I-notion to be deployed, such that an owner of it is sought? In the matter that is the object of I-making. For what purpose is it to be deployed? For the purpose of I-making. Ah, how well said by the well-nourished! For that very [owner] is to be deployed for that purpose! And how is it to be deployed? Through producing, or through commanding? Because of the impossibility of the I-notion having movement — through producing. Then the cause would be the owner. And only the effect would be one's own. Because the cause has dominion over the effect. And through that [effect], the cause is possessed of it.

body.text: ya evāsya hetur ahaṃkārasya. tasyaivayam iti. puṣpito vṛkṣa iti dṛṣṭānto yatra siddhānte vṛkṣāvayavī neṣyate. vijātīyacaturmahābhūtakāyārambhānabhīṣṭe. yatra tu vṛkṣāvayavy asti. tatra dvitīyo dṛṣṭāntaḥ. phalitaṃ vanam iti. na hi vanaṃ nāma kiṃcid asti. yathā yasmin vane phalam utpannaṃ tat phalitam iti ucyate. yathā yasminn āśraye ṣaḍāyatanalakṣaṇe sukham utpannaṃ duḥkhaṃ vā. sa sukhito duḥkhito vā. tathoktam iti. yathā āśrayaḥ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ tathoktaṃ.
body.translated_text: "Whatever is the cause of this I-notion — to that alone does it belong" — "a blossoming tree" is the example, in the case where a tree as a whole (<s>avayavin</s>) is not accepted as distinct [from its parts]. When the arising of a body of dissimilar-species four great elements is not accepted. But where a tree as a whole does exist — there is a second example: "a fruitful forest." For there is no such thing as a forest. Just as a forest in which fruit has arisen is called "fruitful" — so too, in whatever support characterized by the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>), happiness or suffering has arisen — that is called happy or suffering. As stated — the support, the six sense-bases, is thus stated.

children.translated_text: "Because the support — the eye and the rest — undergoes modification of that" —

body.text: iti. atha paṃcaskandhakaṃ bhavān udāharatīty adhikṛtaṃ. sa eva karteti. sa eva paṃcaskandhalakṣaṇaḥ kartā. [Tib. 383b] nātmā. iti siddho naḥ pakṣaḥ. tatrāpi svātaṃtryaṃ nāstīti darśayann āha. trividhaṃ cedaṃ karmeti vistaraḥ. kāyasya cittaparataṃtrā vṛttiḥ cittapravartitvāt kāyakarmaṇaḥ. cittasyāpi kāye vṛttiḥ svakāraṇaprartaṃtrā. [manodharma]manaskārādiparataṃtratvāt. tasyāpy evaṃ tasya cittakāraṇasya svakāraṇaparataṃtrā vṛttir iti. nāsti kasyacid api svātaṃtryaṃ kāyasya cittasya cittakāraṇasyānyasya vā. pratyayaparataṃtrā hi sarve bhāvāḥ.
body.translated_text: thus. Now, 'You cite the five aggregates' — this is the topic. 'That very one is the agent' — that very one characterized by the five aggregates is the agent, not the self (<s>ātman</s>). Thus our thesis is established. Showing that even therein there is no independence (<s>svātantrya</s>), he says: 'And this action is threefold' — thus in detail. The activity of the body is dependent on mind (<s>cittaparatantra</s>), because bodily action is set in motion by mind. And the activity of mind in the body is dependent on its own cause — because of being dependent on mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) and the rest. And that [cause] too — that cause of mind — has its activity dependent on its own cause. Thus there is no independence for anything whatsoever — neither of the body, nor of the mind, nor of the cause of the mind, nor of anything else. For all entities are dependent on conditions (<s>pratyayaparatantra</s>).

children.text:
caturbhiś cittacaittā hi samāpattidvayaṃ tribhiḥ.
