dvābhyām anye tu jāyanta
children.translated_text:
'Mind and mental factors [arise] from four [conditions]; the two attainments from three;
others arise from two' —

body.text: iti vacanāt. ātmano 'pi ca nirapekṣasya buddhiviśeṣādyutpattāv akāraṇatvābhyupagamān na svātaṃtryaṃ sidhyati. tasmān naivaṃ lakṣaṇa iti. svataṃtraḥ karteti. evaṃ tarhi kartety āha. yat tu yasya pradhānakāraṇaṃ. tat
body.translated_text: from this statement. And even for the self, since it is non-dependent (<s>nirapekṣa</s>), because of the acceptance that it is not the cause of the arising of distinct cognitions and the rest, independence is not established. Therefore, it is not of such a character — that is, an independent agent. Then he says: 'It is indeed the agent.' How? Whatever is the principal cause (<s>pradhānakāraṇa</s>) of whatever — that

body.text: tasya kartety ucyate. prādhānye tatpratītyotpatteḥ. sa evam api kartā na yujyate. pradhānakāraṇabhāvenāpi na yujyata ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: is called the agent of that. Because of the principality [of the cause], [the effect] arises dependent on that. But even so, that agent is not tenable — the meaning is: even in the sense of being the principal cause, it is not tenable.

body.text: tasyākāraṇatvam upadarśayann āha. smṛtito hi chanda iti vistaraḥ. pūrvasmartavye 'ṛthe smṛtir utpadyate. smṛteś chandaḥ kartukāmatā. chandād vitarkaś cetanāviśeṣo 'bhisaṃskāralakṣaṇaḥ. prajñāviśeṣo vā yogācāranayena. vaibhāṣikanayena tv abhirūpaṇavikalpalakṣaṇaḥ. [Tib. 384a] vitarkāt pratyatno vīryaṃ. prayatnād vāyuḥ. tato vāyoḥ karma deśāntarotpattilakṣaṇam iti. kim atrātmā kurute.
body.translated_text: Showing its non-causality, he says: 'For from memory (<s>smṛti</s>), desire (<s>chanda</s>)' — thus in detail. Memory arises with regard to a previously remembered object. From memory, desire (<s>chanda</s>) — the wish to act. From desire, <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) — a particular volition (<s>cetanāviśeṣa</s>) characterized by mental formation (<s>abhisaṃskāra</s>). Or a particular wisdom (<s>prajñāviśeṣa</s>) — according to the <s>Yogācāra</s> method. But according to the <s>Vaibhāṣika</s> method, it is characterized by formative conceptualization (<s>abhirūpaṇavikalpa</s>). From <s>vitarka</s>, effort (<s>prayatna</s>) — that is, energy (<s>vīrya</s>). From effort, wind (<s>vāyu</s>). Then from wind, action characterized by arising in another location. What does the self do herein?

body.text: vijñāne pratiṣedhād iti. yaivopalabdhiḥ. tad eva vijñānaṃ. vijñāne cātmanaḥ sāmarthyaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ. cittād evāstu saṃskāraviśeṣāpekṣāt. na hi kiṃcid ātmana upalabhyate samarthyam. auṣadhakāryasiddhāv iva kuhakavaidyaphūḥsvāhānām iti.
body.translated_text: 'Because of its being negated with respect to consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>)' — that which is apprehension itself is consciousness. And the capacity of the self with respect to consciousness has been negated. Let it [arise] from mind itself, dependent on particular formations (<s>saṃskāraviśeṣa</s>). For no capacity whatsoever of the self is apprehended — just like the incantations 'phūḥ' and 'svāhā' of a quack physician in the accomplishment of the effect of medicine.

body.text: yathā tathoktam iti
body.translated_text: 'As it was stated' —

children.translated_text: 'Because of being modified by the modifications of that, the supports are the eye and the rest'

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: — thus.

body.text: tadāśritād ity ātmāśritāt. uktottaraiṣā vācoyuktir iti. yathā kaḥ kasyāśrayaḥ. na hi te citrabadarādivad ādhārye. nāpi sa kuḍyakuṇḍādivad ādhāro yuktaḥ. pratighātitvayuktatvādidoṣān na vai sa evam āśrayaḥ. kathaṃ tarhīti vistaraḥ. tadāhitaṃ hi tad iti. tena bījenāhitaṃ tat sāmarthyam ity arthaḥ.
body.translated_text: 'Dependent on that' — meaning: dependent on the self. 'This is a verbal expression whose answer has been given' — namely: what is the support of what? For they [the sense-faculties] are not supported like the variegated [patterns on] a <s>badara</s> (jujube) fruit and the like. Nor is that [self] reasonably a support like a wall, a vessel, and the like — because of faults such as being obstructive and the like. That is certainly not a support in that sense. How then? — thus in detail. 'For that power has been deposited by that' — meaning: the power deposited by that seed — that is the meaning.

body.text: yathoktam iti sthavirarāhulena.

children.translated_text: 'Whatever is weighty and whatever is proximate'

body.translated_text: 'As stated' — by the Elder <s>Rāhula</s>.

body.text: iti vistaraḥ. ekasmin saṃtāne catvāri karmāṇi. guru āsannam abhyastaṃ pūrvakṛtaṃ ca. eṣāṃ caturṇāṃ gurukarma pūrvakam iti tribhyas tat pūrvaṃ vipacyate. āsannābhyastapūrvakṛtānām [Tib. 384b] apy āsannaṃ pūrvam iti tat pūrvaṃ dvābhyāṃ vipacyate. abhyastapūrvakṛtayoś cābhyastaṃ pūrvam iti ekasmāt pūrvaṃ vipacyate. asatsv eteṣu pūrvajanmakṛtaṃ vipacyate aparaparyāyavedanīyaṃ. akliṣṭānām iti. kuśalānām anivṛtāvyākṛtanāṃ ca. viklittiviśeṣajād iti. bhūmyudakasambandhāt phalasya sūkṣmo vikāro viklittiḥ. tasyā viśeṣaḥ. sa evātiprakṛṣṭaḥ. tasmāj jāto vikāraviśeṣaḥ. tasmāt. phalāntaram utpadyate. kīdṛśād vikāraviśeṣād iti darśayann āha. yo hi tatra bhūtaprakāraṅkuraṃ nivartayati. sa tasya bījam iti. tasyāṃkurasya bījaṃ. nānyo bhūtaprakāraḥ. na pūrvabījāvastho bhūtaprakāra ity arthaḥ. bhavinyā tu saṃjñayeti. odanaṃ pacati saktuṃ pinaṣṭīti yathā bhāvinyā saṃjñayā vyapadeśaḥ. evaṃ pūrvako 'pi
body.translated_text: — thus in detail. In a single continuum there are four [kinds of] <s>karma</s>: weighty (<s>guru</s>), proximate (<s>āsanna</s>), habitual (<s>abhyasta</s>), and previously done (<s>pūrvakṛta</s>). Of these four, the weighty <s>karma</s> comes first — thus it ripens before the other three. Of the proximate, habitual, and previously done, the proximate comes first — thus it ripens before the other two. Of the habitual and previously done, the habitual comes first — thus it ripens before the one. In the absence of these, the <s>karma</s> done in a former birth ripens, as one to be experienced in a subsequent life (<s>aparaparyāyavedanīya</s>). 'Of the non-afflicted' — meaning: of the wholesome and of the unobstructed indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>). 'From a particular alteration of soaking' — from the connection of ground and water, a subtle change in the fruit is 'soaking' (<s>viklitti</s>). Its particular [state] — that very [alteration] in its most advanced [form]. From that arises a particular transformation. From that, another fruit arises. Showing what kind of particular transformation [it is], he says: 'That which there causes the element-type sprout to turn [into fruit] — that is the seed of that.' That is the seed of that sprout — not another element-type [entity], not the element-type that was in the state of the prior seed — that is the meaning. 'But by a future designation' — just as 'one cooks rice' or 'one grinds flour' — designations are made by a future name. Similarly, the prior

body.text: saṃtānaḥ aviklinnabījāvasthaḥ bījam ity ākhyāyate bhāvinyānayā saṃjñayeti. sādṛśyād veti. viklinnaviśeṣajena bhūtavikāraviśeṣeṇa sadṛśaḥ. sa pūrvakaḥ saṃtāna iti kṛtvā bījam ity ākhyāyate. evam ihāpīti vistaraḥ. yadi saddharmaśravaṇayoniśomanaskārapratyayaviśeṣāj jātaḥ kuśalasāsravaś cittavikāra utpadyate. asaddharmaśravaṇayoniśomanaskārapratyayaviśeṣāj jātaḥ akuśalo vā cittavikāra [Tib. 385a] utpadyate. tasmād tadvipākāntaram utpadyate. nānyatheti samānam etat. yathā na phalād eva phalāntaram utpadyate. kiṃ tarhi. vikāraviśeṣāt. evaṃ na vipākād eva vipākāntaram utpadyate. kiṃ tarhi. cittavikāraviśeṣād utpadyate iti. tulyam etat.
body.translated_text: continuum, being in the state of an un-soaked seed, is called 'seed' by this future designation. 'Or because of similarity' — the prior continuum, being similar to the particular element-type transformation produced from the particular soaking-alteration, is called 'seed' on that account. 'Similarly here too' — thus in detail. If, from a particular condition characterized by hearing the true <s>dharma</s> and proper mental attention (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>), a particular mental transformation that is wholesome and contaminated arises; or if, from a particular condition characterized by hearing the untrue <s>dharma</s> and improper mental attention, a particular mental transformation that is unwholesome arises — from that, another retribution (<s>vipāka</s>) arises. 'Not otherwise' — this is the same [as above]. Just as another fruit does not arise from [a previous] fruit alone, but rather from a particular transformation — so too another retribution does not arise from [a previous] retribution alone. Rather, it arises from a particular mental transformation — this is equivalent.

body.text: phale raktaḥ kesara iti. phalābhyantare kesaraḥ. yatra bījapūrakarasa āmlo 'vatiṣṭhate. na ca sa tasmāt punar anya iti. na rasaraktaḥ kesaras tasmād uktāt kesarāt punar upajāyate. kiṃ tarhi. prākṛta evāraktaḥ kesaras upajāyata ity arthaḥ. idam atrodāharaṇaṃ. yathā lākṣārasaraktamātuluṃgapuṣpaphalād raktakesarān na raktaṃ kesarāntaraṃ punar bhavati. evaṃ karmajād vipakān na punar vipākāntaram iti. āha cātra.
body.translated_text: 'The stamen in the fruit is dyed' — the stamen is inside the fruit, where the sour juice of the citron (<s>bījapūra</s>) resides. 'And that does not again arise from it as another' — a dye-stained stamen does not again produce [another] stamen from that stated stamen. Rather, only a natural, undyed stamen is produced — that is the meaning. Here, this is the illustration: just as from a <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron) flower or fruit whose stamen is dyed with lac-resin dye, another dyed stamen does not again come into being — so too from a retribution born of <s>karma</s>, another retribution does not again [arise]. And here he states:

children.text:
cittaṃ hy etad anantabījasahitaṃ saṃtānato vartate.
tattad bījam upaiti puṣṭim udite sve pratyaye cetasi. |
tat puṣṭaṃ drumalabdhavṛtti phaladaṃ kālena saṃpadyate.
raṃgasyeva hi mātuluṃgakusume 'nyas tasya tatkesare. ||
children.translated_text:
'This mind, accompanied by infinite seeds, proceeds in its continuum.
Each seed attains growth when its own condition arises in the mind.
That [seed], having grown, having acquired the function of a tree, in time becomes fruit-bearing.
Just as dye in the blossom of a citron — another [effect] is in its stamen.'

body.text: punar āha.
body.translated_text: Again he says:

children.translated_text: 'In the cotton seed and in the flower of the citron, dyed
with lac — the cotton stamen is produced as dyed.'

children.text:
tasminn astamite raṃge saṃtānād bhāvitakramāt. |
karmaṇy astamite caiva bhāvanātaḥ phalodaya. ||
children.translated_text:
'When that dye has disappeared, from the continuum through the process of cultivation,
and when the <s>karma</s> too has disappeared, from cultivation the fruit arises.'

body.text: iti.
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: karmabhāvanāṃ.
body.translated_text: — the cultivation of <s>karma</s>.

body.text: bhāvanāyā
body.translated_text: — of the cultivation.

body.text: tvadvṛttaṃ lābhaṃ.
body.translated_text: — the obtaining of your function.

body.text: tadvṛttilābhāt.
body.translated_text: — from the obtaining of that function.

body.text: ity etac catuṣṭayaṃ
body.translated_text: — these four

body.text: śrāvakādiḥ
body.translated_text: — a <s>śrāvaka</s> and so forth —

body.text: arthād uktaṃ bhavati. buddha eva tat sarvaṃ sarvathā prajānātīti.
body.translated_text: By implication, it is stated: only the <s>Buddha</s> fully understands all that in every way.

body.text: ity etām iti vistaraḥ. itikaraṇaḥ samāptyarthaḥ. pradarśanārtho vā. etāṃ buddhānāṃ pravacanadharmatāṃ suvihitena hetor mārgeṇa hetumārgeṇa śuddhāṃ niravadyāṃ niśāmya dṛṣṭvā. aṃdhās tīrthyāḥ. yathābhūtadarśanavaikalyāt. kutsitā dṛṣṭiḥ kudṛṣṭiḥ. tasyāś ceṣṭitāni kudṛṣṭiceṣṭitāni. vividhāni kudṛṣṭiceṣṭitān eṣām iti vividhakudṛṣṭiceṣṭitāḥ svargāpavargahetāv apratipanna mithyāpratipannāś cety arthaḥ. teṣām evaṃvidhānāṃ tīrthyānāṃ kapilolūkādīnāṃ mataṃ darśanam apavidhya tyaktvā yāṃti saṃsārān nirvāṇam iti vākyādhyāhāraḥ. ke te sattvāḥ prajñācakṣuṣmanta āryaśrāvakāḥ. atha vā tām eva pravacanadharmatāṃ yānti pratipadyanta ity arthaḥ. pravacanadharmatā punar atra nairātmyaṃ buddhānuśāsani vā. anya āhuḥ. pravacanaṃ sūtrādidvādaśāṃgavacogatam. tasya dharmatā svākhyātatā yuktyupetatvāt. nirvāṇapravaṇatā ca nirvāṇadyotanāt. yathoktaṃ sarva ime dharmā nirvāṇapravaṇāḥ nirvāṇaprāgbhārāḥ nirvāṇam evābhivadanto [Tib. 386a] 'bhivadantīti. anātmasaṃjñinaś ca nirvāṇe śāntasaṃjñāḥ saṃtiṣṭhante. ātmocchedāśaṃkāpagamād iti. tad evam anandhā eva yānti. nāndhāḥ. andhās tu bhramanty eva saṃsārārṇave nairātmyam apaśyantaḥ. tad darśayann āha imāṃ hīti vistaraḥ. iyaṃ nirātmatā. nirvāṇam eva puraṃ nirvāṇapuraṃ. tasyaikā vartinīti nirvāṇapuraikamārgo nānyo mārga ity arthaḥ. tathāgata evādityo gaṃbhīradharmābhiprakāśakatvād ādityabhūtas tathāgataḥ. tasya vacāṃsi tāny evāṃśavaḥ. tair bhāsvatī ālokavatī tathāgatādityavaco'ṃśubhāsvati. āryāṇāṃ sahasrair vāhitety āryasahasravāhitā. vivṛtām apīti. tām imāṃ nirvāṇapuraikavartinīṃ tathāgatādityavaco'ṃśubhāsvatīṃ vivṛtām api nirātmatāṃ. prajñācakṣuṣo viśadasyābhāvād avidyākośapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetratvād vā mandacakṣuḥ tīrthiko vātsīputrīyo 'pi vā nekṣate. trayaś ceha mārgaguṇa varṇyante.
body.translated_text: 'Thus this' — in detail. The word 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) has the sense of completion, or of illustration. This <s>dharmatā</s> (nature) of the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>s — having examined it, having seen it, through a pure, faultless method of reasoning, a causal method — the blind [are the] non-Buddhist teachers (<s>tīrthya</s>s), because of their deficiency in seeing things as they truly are. A base view is a wrong view (<s>kudṛṣṭi</s>). The conduct of that [wrong view] is wrong-view-conduct. Those whose manifold wrong-view-conduct [defines them] are 'of manifold wrong-view-conduct' — not having attained [the means to] heaven and liberation, or having wrongly attained [them] — that is the meaning. Having cast aside, having abandoned, the views of those non-Buddhist teachers of such kind — <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Ulūka</s>, and the rest — they go from <s>saṃsāra</s> to <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is the completion of the sentence. Who are those beings? Those with the eye of wisdom (<s>prajñācakṣus</s>) — the noble <s>śrāvaka</s>s. Alternatively, they go to, they realize, that very nature of the teaching — that is the meaning. The nature of the teaching here is selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), or the instruction of the <s>Buddha</s>. Others say: the teaching is the speech belonging to the twelve divisions of scripture — <s>sūtra</s> and the rest. Its nature is its being well-spoken (<s>svākhyātatā</s>), because of being endowed with reasoning. And its inclination toward <s>nirvāṇa</s> — because of illuminating <s>nirvāṇa</s>. As stated: 'All these <s>dharma</s>s are inclined toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, tending toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, speaking of <s>nirvāṇa</s> itself.' And those who have the perception of non-self abide in the peaceful perception of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — because of the removal of the fear of the annihilation of self. Thus indeed, the non-blind alone go [to <s>nirvāṇa</s>], not the blind. The blind, however, wander in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, not seeing selflessness. Showing that, he says: 'For this' — thus in detail. This selflessness (<s>nirātmatā</s>). <s>Nirvāṇa</s> itself is the city — the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Its single path — that is the 'single path to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>,' meaning there is no other path. The <s>Tathāgata</s> himself is the sun — because of illuminating profound <s>dharma</s>s, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is like the sun. His words are its rays. By those, it is luminous — resplendent with the rays of the words of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-sun. 'Traversed by thousands of noble ones' — traversed by thousands of noble ones (<s>ārya</s>s). 'Even though it is open' — that selflessness, though it is the single path to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, luminous with the rays of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-sun's words, and opened [by the noble ones] — because of the absence of a clear eye of wisdom, or because the eyes are covered by the veil of the shell of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) — one of dim vision, whether a non-Buddhist teacher or even a <s>Vātsīputrīya</s>, does not see it. And here three qualities of the path are described:

body.text: tadyathaikāyanatābhipretadeśaprāyaṇāt. sālokatā yato niḥśaṃko gacchati. yātānuyātatā ca parimarditasthāṇukaṇṭakāditvāt. [Tib. 386b] yena sukhaṃ gacchati. tatsādharmyeṇeyaṃ nirātmatāvartinī draṣṭavyā. caturbhiś ca kāraṇair mārgo na vidyate. satvānutamaskatayā. prakāśito 'py ādityena avāhitatayā. bahupuruṣavāhito 'py āvṛtatayā. vivṛto 'pi draṣṭur mandacakṣuṣkatayeti. teṣām ihaikam eva kāraṇam asya mārgasyādarśana uktaṃ. yato draṣṭur doṣeṇaivāyaṃ mārgo na dṛśyate. na mārgadoṣeṇeti. yata eṣa mandacakṣur etaṃ na paśyatīty avagantavyam.
body.translated_text: namely: its being a single path — because of leading to the desired destination; its luminosity — because of which one goes without doubt; and its being traversed by those who have gone before — because of the thorns, stumps, and the like being cleared away, by which one goes comfortably. By analogy with those, this path of selflessness should be seen. And for four reasons a path is not seen: because of the darkness of the place; even when illuminated by the sun, because of not being traversed; even when traversed by many, because of being concealed; even when open, because of the dim vision of the observer. Of these, only one reason is stated here for the non-seeing of this path: because it is through the fault of the observer alone that this path is not seen, not through the fault of the path. Since this one of dim vision does not see it — this should be understood.

body.text: iti. sarvam iti yathoktaṃ. dig eva diṅmātram evakārārtho mātraśabdaḥ. dik pramāṇam asyeti diṅmātram iti vā. mahato 'bhidharmaśāstrād alpam idam
body.translated_text: — thus. 'Everything' means as stated. 'Indication' itself is 'merely an indication' — the word 'merely' (<s>mātra</s>) has the force of the particle 'eva.' Or: that whose measure is an indication — that is 'merely an indication.' From the great <s>Abhidharma</s> treatise, this small [amount]

body.text: mayeti vākyaśeṣaḥ. keṣām.
body.translated_text: — by me — this is the rest of the sentence. For whom?

body.text: matimatām ity arthaḥ. tādarthye ṣaṣṭhi. kiṃvad ity āha.
body.translated_text: — meaning: for those who have understanding. The genitive is used in the sense of purpose. Like what? He says:

children.translated_text: 'Like the site of a wound for poison that spreads by its own power'

body.text: iti. yathā visaṃ svasāmarthyād vraṇadeśaṃ prāpya sarveṣv aṅgapratyaṅgeṣv atyantaṃ visarpatīti matvā kenacit tasya vraṇadeśaḥ kṛtaḥ. kathaṃ nāmedaṃ visarpatīti. evaṃ sumedhasaḥ svasāmarthyavisarpitvād viṣasthāniyāḥ. ity atas teṣāṃ sumedhasām udghaṭitajñānāṃ prājñānām idam upadiṣṭaṃ mayā. katham. alpena granthena mahad abhidharmaśāstraṃ.
body.translated_text: — thus. Just as poison, having reached the site of a wound by its own power, spreads exceedingly to all limbs and secondary limbs — and thinking thus, someone makes the wound-site for it — 'how indeed does this [poison] spread!' — so too the intelligent, being like poison in their capacity to spread by their own power — therefore, for those intelligent ones, those of ready understanding (<s>udghaṭitajñāna</s>), those who are wise — this has been taught by me. How? Through a small text, the great <s>Abhidharma</s> treatise.

body.text: arthataḥ pratipadyerann iti. apare punar vyācakṣate. iti diṅmātram evedam iti idam eva nairātmyaprativedham adhikṛtyoktam iti.
body.translated_text: — they would understand in substance. Others, however, explain: 'Thus, this is merely an indication' — this is stated with reference to the penetration of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>).

children.translated_text: 'this <s>Abhidharma</s> has been for the most part taught by me'

body.text: ity anenaivārthasyābhihitatvād iti.
body.translated_text: — because the meaning has been stated by this very [verse].

body.text: samāptaś cāṣṭamakośasthānasaṃbaddha eva pudgalaviniścayaḥ.
body.translated_text: The <s>Pudgalaviniścaya</s> (Determination of Persons), connected with the Eighth <s>Kośasthāna</s> (Treasury Chapter), is concluded.

body.text:
nānābhidharmārthakaraṃḍabhūtam
etad vivṛ .......

children.translated_text: Born from the womb of craving-produced nectar and water,
opened by the rays of the sun of my explanatory words,
may the bee-like wise ones enjoy this lotus of the <s>śāstra</s>!

body.translated_text:
'This, which is a casket of the various meanings of the <s>Abhidharma</s>,
this exposition .......'

children.translated_text: He who, having studied all <s>śāstra</s>s, [gained] the fame of the learned — <s>Yaśomitra</s>,

children.text: sa imāṃ kṛtavān vyākhyāṃ vyākhyāsv anyāsv asaṃtuṣṭaḥ. ||
children.translated_text: he composed this commentary, being unsatisfied with other commentaries.
By him, O lord of the glorious <s>Bhāratī</s> (Goddess of Speech), this commentary of ultimate meaning (<s>paramārtha</s>) and scripture (<s>āgama</s>)
was composed for the god-like one of divine appearance.

body.text: ācāryayaśomitrakṛtāyāṃ sphuṭārthāyām abhidharmakośavyākhyāyām aṣṭamaṃ kośasthānaṃ samāptam iti.
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sphuṭārthā Abhidharmakośavyākhyā</s> composed by <s>Ācārya Yaśomitra</s>, the eighth <s>kośasthāna</s> (section of the Treasury) is completed.

body.text: graṃthakārasaṃkhyā 25000.
body.translated_text: Number of verses by the author: 25,000.

body.text: śubhaṃ
body.translated_text: Auspiciousness (<s>śubham</s>).
